sig_000107cc0d6a952c8aeb.description: Capital City Partnership (CCP) intends to undertake a procurement exercise for the provision, support, maintenance and ongoing development of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Management Information System (MIS). Lot 1: . Capital City Partnership (CCP) intends to undertake a procurement exercise for the provision, support, maintenance and ongoing development of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Management Information System (MIS) covering - City of Edinburgh - East Lothian - Fife - Midlothian - Scottish Borders - West Lothian The platform supports service delivery across a wide range of organisations involved in employability, skills and related service delivery activities throughout the region. This Prior Information Notice is intended to provide advance notice of the procurement and to encourage engagement from suitably experienced suppliers. CCP currently operates an established regional CRM and Management Information System supporting service delivery across six Local Authority areas. The solution is used by approximately: - 1,000 users - 110 organisations - 115,000 client records - 2.5 million recorded activities and interventions - 14,500 employer records - 17,000 vacancy records The platform supports a range of operational and reporting requirements and provides a critical service supporting frontline delivery, partnership working and performance management. While the primary use of the system is employability and skills delivery, the platform is also used to support wider service delivery activities including Community Learning and Development, work experience and placement management, and public-facing provider directory functionality. CCP intends to procure a solution capable of supporting the current and future requirements of the partnership. The successful supplier will be expected to provide: - CRM and participant management functionality - Case management functionality - Referral management - Action planning and intervention recording - Outcome tracking and reporting - Employer engagement functionality - Vacancy management - Programme and project management functionality - Management information and reporting - Document management - Workflow and configuration tools - Hosting, support and maintenance services - Ongoing development and enhancement services - Service management and governance arrangements CCP is seeking a solution capable of supporting future growth, service development and innovation throughout the contract term of 8 years. The current solution operates in a multi-organisational environment supporting Local Authorities and a wide range of delivery partners. The platform currently supports: - Configurable forms and workflows - Multi-organisation access and permissions - Standard and customised reporting - Document management - Employer engagement and vacancy management - Data imports, exports and secure data exchange processes - Public-facing information directory functionality CCP currently operates a single core user model and is seeking a commercially sustainable and scalable approach to licensing and service provision. The successful supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with CCP throughout the contract term and support: - Continuous improvement - Product development - Service innovation - Additional reporting requirements - New business processes - Additional users and organisations - Future integration requirements - Additional service delivery models where required CCP is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers support long-term product development, customer engagement and technology innovation. CCP is seeking a transparent and scalable commercial model. The anticipated approach is based upon: - An annual service charge - Pricing predicated on active user volumes - Separation of implementation and transition costs from ongoing service costs - Transparent pricing for optional functionality and professional services

sig_000e079e9de4d5d53941.description: NATIONAL SECURITY EXCEPTION In respect of all phases of the solicitation, SSC has invoked the National Security Exception (NSE). As such, this invocation exempts all phases of the procurement processes for sovereign cloud services from the application of all of Canada’s trade agreements, including the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (Article III(1)) and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (Article 801). 1. INTRODUCTION The Government of Canada (GC) is advancing its digital infrastructure and hosting capabilities to meet evolving operational requirements and to deliver services to Canadians that are secure, reliable, and user-centric. Building on findings and industry feedback obtained through prior engagement activities, Shared Services Canada (SSC) is establishing a structured Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process as an initial step to support future procurements. The Sovereign Cloud Qualification process is intended to: • Establish a standing entry point for Canadian-owned and -controlled businesses seeking to qualify to participate in sovereign cloud procurements • Enable Canada to collect information on available and emerging offerings to support market awareness and procurement planning • Provide a consistent, transparent, and accessible mechanism for industry engagement • This Notice of Planned Procurement does not constitute a commitment by Canada to issue any solicitation or to procure any services. 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW The Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process is supported by an Invitation to Qualify (ITQ). The ITQ defines the requirements for qualification, including: • Eligibility conditions • Submission requirements • Supporting documentation • Process instructions The qualification process serves as the entry point and a mandatory step for vendors to participate in current and future sovereign cloud procurement processes. Vendors that participate in the qualification process and meet the eligibility conditions defined in the ITQ will be considered as Qualified Respondents (QR) for participation in future sovereign cloud procurement opportunities. This qualification process is not a competitive procurement process and will not result in a contract award. It is intended solely to establish a list of qualified vendors for participation in future procurement activities. 3. ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS Eligibility conditions details are defined in the ITQ (available in tab “Bidding Details” above). At a minimum, eligibility conditions include: - Confirmation of Respondent’s Canadian ownership and control, including parent companies. - Submission of a Value Proposition describing the respondent’s sovereign cloud offerings. 4. OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE 4.1 Objective The objective of the Sovereign Cloud Services procurement stream is to strengthen Canada’s cloud posture by enabling and supporting solutions that advance Canadian control over data and services, and protection from foreign legal or extraterritorial authority. The sovereign cloud procurement stream is intended to complement, and not replace, existing cloud procurement approaches. 4.2 Scope (Indicative Only) The service categories described below are indicative only and provided to inform respondents of the types of capabilities Canada may consider procuring in the future. Additional requirements, eligibility conditions, certifications, or evaluation criteria will be defined in future procurement stages once the procurement process is confirmed The scope of the Sovereign Cloud Services procurement stream may include, but is not limited to: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): This category may include sovereign fundamental computing resources such as processing, storage, and networking. These services allow departments to deploy and run their own software, including operating systems and applications. While the cloud provider manages the underlying infrastructure, Canada retains control over operating systems, storage, deployed applications, and certain network configuration. Platform as a Service (PaaS): This category may include sovereign cloud services that allow departments to deploy and run applications built using programming languages, libraries, services, and tools supported by the provider. The provider manages the underlying infrastructure, including networks, servers, operating systems, and storage, while Canada retains control over the applications it deploys and the configuration of the application hosting environment. AI enabling services: This category may include sovereign services that support the development, deployment, or operation of artificial intelligence solutions, such as machine learning platforms, model hosting, data processing environments, and AI infrastructure. Managed Service Providers of Classified Cloud Solutions: This category may include managed services for classified cloud solutions. Vendors intending to operate as infrastructure providers will be required to provide certification from a recognized classified cloud solution provider in the Five Eyes confirming their authorization and agreement to deliver classified cloud services and associated managed solutions. Recognizing that many classified and unclassified cloud solutions are operated or owned by foreign providers, Canada may also consider managed service providers that have unique access to such cloud service solutions, even where those solutions are owned by foreign entities. In such cases, the managed service provider will need to demonstrate full control over the technology and the delivery of services. Other cloud or cloud enabling capabilities that support sovereign digital service delivery. This category may include other sovereign cloud or cloud-enabling capabilities not otherwise described in the indicative scopes provided above. 5. SUBMISSION PROCEDURES To participate in the Sovereign Cloud Qualification process, respondents must complete and submit the designated submission form in accordance with the requirements set out in the ITQ. 6. PROCESS AND TIMELINES The Sovereign Cloud Qualification process is open, ongoing, and continuously available through CanadaBuys. The ITQ defines intake periods and closing dates. The first intake period closing date is set to October 19, 2026. Following the end of each intake period, or more often at SSC’s discretion, responses will be assessed and each Respondent will be notified of its qualification status within 20 working days. SSC reserves the right to update, amend, or discontinue the Sovereign Cloud Qualification process at any time. 7. INFORMATION WEBINAR Vendors are invited to attend an Informational Webinar to discuss any questions you may have on the ITQ. Interested vendors must register by contacting the Contracting Authority before October 6, 2026, 23:59 Pacific Time, at the following email address: PVRCloudServicesRCRs.DCCServicesinfonuagiquesARF@ssc-spc.gc.ca. The Information Webinars will be held on the following dates and times: The French-language webinar will be held on October 8, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. EDT The English-language webinar will be held on October 8, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. EDT 8. FUTURE COMMUNICATION Vendors are responsible for monitoring CanadaBuys for updates related to this Sovereign Cloud Qualification. SSC may communicate updates or request clarification from respondents as required. 9. PRIVACY STATEMENT All responses will be treated as confidential, subject to the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act. 10. TRADE AGREEMENTS No trade agreement applies to this requirement, as the National Security Exception has been invoked. 11. LANGUAGE Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. 12. ENQUIRIES Enquiries regarding the Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process are to be submitted to: PVRCloudServicesRCRs.DCCServicesinfonuagiquesARF@ssc-spc.gc.ca

sig_001223f1888ca3deedd7.description: Post Office Ltd (POL) is undertaking a multi-phase Identity & Access Management (IDAM) Transformation Programme, comprising multiple work packages across Customer CIAM, PAM/IGA, migration from legacy platforms, and Zero Trust alignment. The procurement will be conducted as a Further Competition under the Crown Commercial Service (CCS) Technology Services 3 (TS3) Framework Agreement (RM6100), LOT 1 - Technology Strategy & Service Design and LOT 2 - Transition & Transformation in accordance with section 20 (1) and (2)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023. The purpose of this Expression of Interest (EOI) is to: • support the discovery, validation, and mobilisation of the Identity & Access Management (IDAM) workstream under the Post Office Cyber Security Maturity Programme (CSMP) • Identify suppliers on TS3 Lots 1 and 2 with demonstrable capability to deliver outcome-based IDAM solutions. • Generate a shortlist (approx. 5-6 suppliers) to invite to the formal Initial Invitation to Tender (IIT). • Inform refinement of the IIT scope and procurement plan. The total estimated value of this contract is between £4.5 million and £5 million over the full contract term. However, at the time of issuing this tender, only £800,000 has received formal funding approval. The remaining contract value is subject to annual approval by POL's Board, and there is no guarantee that future funding will be secured. This funding dependency is disclosed as a known risk in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. Suppliers should be aware that: • POL is not obligated to commit beyond the currently approved funding. • Future contract performance may be subject to modification, suspension, or early termination if funding is not approved. Any such changes will be managed in accordance with the contract terms and applicable provisions of the Procurement Act 2023. To request to participate, bidders must respond to the Expression of Interest (EOI) and the Capability Assessment Questionnaire, register with POL's e-Sourcing platform, Web 3, complete, sign and return the non-disclosure agreement (NDA), conflict of interest form (COIF) and ethical walls agreements (EWA) (where required for incumbent suppliers) sent to the bidder. All Clarifications must be submitted by 12:00 on 27th October 2025. Responses to all Clarifications will be shared through the portal no later than 28 October 2025. Bidder's must complete the Expression of Interest Capability Assessment Questionnaire by no later than 12:00 GMT 31st October 2025. Participation in this procurement is strictly limited to bidders currently appointed to the Crown Commercial Service (CCS) Technology Services 3 Framework Agreement (RM6100) under LOT 1 - Technology Strategy & Service Design and LOT 2 - Transition & Transformation. Only bidders registered under these LOTs are eligible to participate in this procurement exercise. Bidders not registered under the RM6100 Framework (LOT 1 and LOT 2) are not permitted to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) and will not be considered. Lot 1: .

Stream C - A.3 Enterprise Resource Planning Programmer Analyst (LEVEL 3) Objective: The objective is to implement Warehouse Management in CSC’s Oracle IFMMS system in order to replace the existing two legacy systems and to have an integrated solution that will be supported from a functional and technical perspective; using the existing and internal knowledge base to best manage and support the business processes at both the Laval National Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse sites. Enhancing IFMMS with advanced warehouse management functionality, will provide industry best practices in CSC and CORCAN’s supply chain management process through efficiencies, innovation, and consolidation of three software applications into one. The solution will create efficiencies in business processes and increase accuracy in the supply chain process through tracking all inputs and outputs within one system. Functional and technical expertise are required for the implementation, configuration and delivery of the Warehouse Management functionality in IFMMS, which includes enhancements to the Inventory Management and order Management modules. Scope: The Warehouse Management solution must effectively support both the Laval Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse. By enhancing functionality within Oracle EBS to include Warehouse Management, and potentially include Oracle’s Mobile Supply Chain Applications (MSCA), and by enhancing Oracle EBS modules such as Inventory Management and Order Management this will enable users at both locations to: a) Accurately manage and process physical goods; b) Increase the accuracy of inventory counts for costing, manufacturing, and shipment of goods,; c) Properly reconcile and integrate billing, pricing, and returns related to goods sold, and d) Establish a consistent business process and source of truth for users at both locations. This transformation will provide both the Laval Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse with an integrated solution that is more automated and streamlined, thus reducing inventory reconciliation issues, and allowing for more accurate and timely processing of orders. The solution must: a. Be integrated (and not interfaced) with the existing Oracle EBS V12.2 ERP system. b. Be compatible with CSC current technology infrastructure. c. Be upgradable at regular intervals to keep current with industry standards, as well as the Government of Canada standards through Shared Services Canada (SSC). d. Adhere to Treasury Board Secretariat directives for financial systems.. e. Utilize and implement industry standard “best-practices.” f. Limit costly customizations to those that are required either by external legislation or internal Commissioner’s directives. g. Be able to easily enter orders, process shipments, and reconcile all transactions. There should be few to no inventory discrepancies. This will improve reporting capabilities and facilitate accurate and consistent responses to Access to Information and Privacy requests (ATIP). sig_001cc01bde3357fe3ac2.description: The Messe Berlin GmbH, hereinafter also referred to as Messe Berlin (MB) and the Contracting Authority (CA), is issuing a call for tenders for the following service: IP Address Management (DDI), CP1-2025-0019. The subject of this procurement is the provision, implementation and operation of a physical appliance for DHCP/DNS/IP address management. With the appliance being tendered, the Messe Berlin GmbH intends to position itself for the future in the field of network technology. The Messe Berlin GmbH is therefore seeking a dedicated IP address management solution as a complete DDI system with which the administration of DHCP ranges and DNS management can be made simpler and clearer. Due to the group's goal of further expanding its cloud architecture, it will also be necessary at a later date to introduce a central IP address management system in order to improve the overall overview of assigned IP addresses and to standardise overall management. The following service items are involved: - Hardware: Complete solution incl. maintenance - Software: DDI - Application - Maintenance (servicing, inspection, repair): Incident management (3rd level) + request + change management - Consulting service: Further development of the application at the customer's request - Implementation service: Delivery, commissioning, individual adjustments according to requirements, handover to operations incl. complete documentation (technical + user)

sig_0049340f881120d7a0b2.description: As part of the BIM@BD programme, the Building Directorate of the Canton of Zurich is introducing the Building Information Modeling (BIM) method across the ARE, TBA, HBA and IMA departments. The objective is to make construction and management processes more efficient through the digital continuity of data and documents across all lifecycle phases, and to increase data quality and completeness. As part of the phased model (Stage 1) of the programme, the procurement of a modern BIM CDE (Common Data Environment) with a focus on user acceptance and economic efficiency is planned. The BIM CDE forms the software solution for mapping digitalised processes for collaboration with structured building information. It enables the guided exchange of data during the planning and construction phases and its transfer to existing peripheral systems for property operations. The BIM CDE is designed as an interaction between two software solutions: 1. The BIM CDE PIM (Project Information Model) serves the data and information exchange of the departments with external project teams in ongoing projects. Accordingly, a large number of users with various professional backgrounds is to be expected here, which necessitates simple and intuitive user guidance. The BIM CDE PIM provides functionalities that are necessary for the implementation of BIM use cases. The BIM CDE PIM is the subject of this tender. 2. The BIM CDE DIP (Data Integration Platform) is designed as an expert system and is used exclusively by internal, trained specialists. The solution serves to retrieve project data from the BIM CDE PIM and prepare it for transfer to the Building Directorate's existing target systems. The procurement of the BIM CDE DIP is planned for the year 2026 and does not form part of this tender. Two Lots This present tender for the BIM CDE PIM is divided into two lots. - Lot 1 CDE PIM optimally usable for building construction projects - Lot 2 CDE PIM optimally usable for civil engineering projects It is desired that tenderers submit a bid for both lots respectively. The objective is to find a joint BIM CDE solution for building construction and civil engineering. The evaluation awards additional points for the resulting synergy. However, it is also possible to award contracts for two different products. Described in simplified terms, the evaluation procedure takes place in three steps. In a first step, all submitted bids are checked to see whether they meet the general participation requirements. Bids that do not meet these requirements are excluded from the further procedure. In the second step, the remaining bids are evaluated based on the defined suitability criteria and award criteria. On this basis, a provisional ranking is drawn up. In the third step, those bids are comprehensively checked and evaluated which, on the basis of the provisional evaluation, still have a realistic mathematical chance of being awarded the contract. This in-depth examination comprises a PoC (Proof of Concept) followed by a product presentation by the tenderer. The tenderers invited to the PoC receive a package of test data with which they can configure their solution and make it available to a selection of test users for live testing. In the subsequent product presentation, initial empirical values, feedback on the first impression and user-friendliness are already available and can be discussed with the tenderer in the Q&A session. This procedure is deliberately chosen, as intuitive usability is enormously important for the BIM CDE PIM. The results are combined into an overall evaluation. Option "Confidential data classification" Special attention must be paid to information security requirements. The offered solution must at least meet the requirements of the "internal" data classification. If the requirements for use with data of the "confidential" data classification are additionally met, the tenderer receives additional points. For further information, see the specifications. CDE PIM optimally usable for building construction projects For further information, see the specifications.

sig_0049e75f6b39a38e0f84.description: The purpose of this procurement is to establish a modern, scalable video streaming solution for traffic cameras, replacing the current outdated system which no longer supports further development. The new solution will enhance the Norwegian Public Roads Administration's (Norwegian Public Roads Administration's) capabilities in traffic monitoring and emergency preparedness, while also improving access to real-time video data for both internal and external stakeholders. The scope includes the delivery of a system that supports approximately 840 road cameras currently in use for traffic information, surveillance, and emergency response. Of these, 125 cameras are video-enabled to provide real-time footage to the public and traffic operators. The solution must cater to the needs of internal traffic operators as well as external users who rely on timely and accurate traffic video data.

sig_004c838b95cf7ec892b3.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This Department of War (DoW) Drone Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the DoW Drone Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the DoW will better incentivize industry innovation. DoW Drone Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional DoW acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the DoW to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The DoW has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform DoW Drone Marketplace capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The DoW is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The DoW anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled bythe DoW. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST (AOI) This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY AOIs or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Payloads Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS): Full Systems Air Vehicles Maritime Systems: Surface and Undersea Systems Maritime Reconnaissance and Domain Awareness Littoral and Amphibious Support Ground Systems: Reconnaissance and Surveillance Systems Logistics and Equipment Transport Combat and Tactical Support Platforms Counter- UAS: Mutli-Domain Sensing and Detection Command, Control and Data Fusion Defeat Mechanisms (Kinetic and Non-Kinetic) Platform & Operation Integration Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects Drone Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any AOI in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment when providing a submission to an IWS. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below and within the specific C4Ss posted. The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for, as applicable, for phase 2 and/or 3, the submission may be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the DoW and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the DoW and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. Area of Interest in Subject Line usarmy.redstone.cpe-avn.mbx.uasmarketplaceiws@army.mil C4S Brief submissions (Section D) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: USARMY Redstone Arsenal PEO AVN Mailbox DoW Drone Marketplace SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the DoW will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoW that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoW for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoW has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoW relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

sig_0067bac40918552d2706.description: SOURCES SOUGHT Nationwide Flexible Coworking Services for GSA, PBS. Sources Sought Response Date: October 20th, 2026 4pm CST The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 531120 - Lessors of nonresidential buildings (except miniwarehouses). This Sources Sought Notice is a market research tool being utilized to determine interest and capability of potential sources prior to issuing a formal solicitation, as the solicitation is not available at this time. This IS NOT a Request for Offerors or Proposals. This notice does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for planning purposes only. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are businesses with the requisite capabilities and experience to perform the required work. In addition, this market research is to determine if there are respondents that qualify under one or more socio-economic indicators, including but not limited to, small business, woman-owned business, Women Owned Small business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women Owned Small business (EDWOSB), Veteran Owned Small business, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small business, SBA Certified Small Disadvantaged business, SBA Certified 8(a) Firm, SBA Certified HUBZone Firm. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) anticipates procuring the services of multiple contractors to perform Flexible Coworking Services, either as shared co-working spaces (Standard coworking spaces where an organization shares the space with other individuals and organizations) or private co-working spaces (Coworking spaces where a certain area (floor, section, private offices with locks) is dedicated to a single organization for federal agencies looking to occupy a coworking space with other federal or private sector employees. It is the intention of GSA to award a multiple contractor, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. Description of Services: The firm shall be able to provide flexible coworking space nationwide. The firm shall have an online booking system where Government employees can quickly select a workspace from an online system and/or from a mobile phone application. In addition to having access to both private and shared offices and workstations, Government employees should be able to utilize a meeting room on an hourly or daily basis. The space should be able, if necessary, to be segregated from certain parts of the vendor’s general operations, or at times operate autonomously. The firm shall provide management for each location. Management duties include, but are not limited to providing, uninterrupted internet, office support, oversight for the online booking platform, monthly usage reports to GSA, and billing based on actual usage. Specific management services may vary per location and are subject to localized requirements and offerings. Management does not include IT support for government furnished equipment. Commercial contracting approaches from RFO Part 12 apply to these requirements. If interested in responding to this Sources Sought, please respond by completing and submitting the GSA Flexible Coworking Services Sources Sought Questionnaire no later than 4:00pm Central Standard Time on Tuesday, October 20th, 2026. NO TELEPHONE CALLS WILL BE ACCEPTED. QUESTIONS ARE NOT PERMITTED. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR SOLICITATION.

sig_008fcbd451c57a3642ec.description: In compliance with the principles of necessity, suitability and efficiency established in Article 28 of the LCSP, the nature and extent of the needs intended to be covered by the conclusion of this contract fall within the scope of the functions and powers attributed to this Management Centre, determining with precision the suitability of the object and content of the contract in the Specifications of Technical Requirements. The contract aims to respond to the need to comply with the provisions of Article 3.2.a of Royal Decree 1046/2022, of 27 December, which regulates the governance of the Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy in Spain and of the European agricultural funds EAGF and EAFRD (hereinafter, Royal Decree 1046/2022), which stipulates that the regional Management Authorities, responsible for the management and execution of the CSP in their territorial scope, shall participate in relation to the evaluation plan and ex-post evaluation, in the establishment of the CSP evaluation plan and in the monitoring and evaluation tasks corresponding to their sphere of competence, reporting on their development and outcome to the Strategic Plan Management Authority. Such an evaluation must necessarily be carried out by functionally independent experts, as required by Article 140 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 December 2021 laying down rules on support for strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States under the common agricultural policy (CAP strategic plans) and financed by the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and repealing Regulations (EU) No. 1305/2013 and (EU) No. 1307/2013. Therefore, the corresponding tender must be carried out by this Department so that a team of independent expert evaluators in the field—since the Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Rural Development currently lacks this type of human resource among its staff capable of carrying out the necessary functions to perform this type of work and with the necessary knowledge to be able to carry out thematic evaluations within the framework of the CSP Strategic Plan in the territorial scope of Castile and Leon—can carry it out. In compliance with the provisions of Article 3.2 of DECREE 23/2025, of 30 December, regulating the conditions for the extension of the General Budgets of the Community of Castile and Leon for 2024 in the 2026 financial year, it is noted that the contract proposed to be initiated is considered a continuation of the CAP Strategic Plan approved on 31 August 2022 by the European Commission.
sig_008fcbd451c57a3642ec.title: The purpose of the contract is the provision of the service to the Regional Management Authority of Castile and Leon for thematic evaluations during the years 2026 and 2027.

sig_00cb4035c1e3f4f6e4ff.description: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. Submission In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below. • Short narrative describing your overall approach to working with Innovate UK Business Connect • Checklist against the requirements • Supporting information against the essential requirements • A rate card of costs associated with services you provide • A completed copy of the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire including: o A copy of your audited accounts for the most recent two years (or alternative means of demonstrating financial status if trading for less than a year) • Legal information i.e. Your standard T&Cs Please provide the information requested above to re.support@iukbc.org.uk by 17:00 10 October 2026 at the latest. IR35 will be assessed before the awarding of a successful contract. Submissions sent without relevant documents as listed above will be automatically rejected. Innovate UK Business Connect may require successful submissions to be subject to non-disclosure agreements. Evaluation structure Submissions will be scored against the following areas: • Value for money - 20% • Technical specification - 70% o alignment to objective 10% o essential requirements 40% o desirable requirements 20% • Demonstration - 10% Lot 1: .

The contracting authority is not initiating a tender contest by publishing this information request, but a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tender contest that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of web analytics tools and related expert services. The purpose of the information request is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain the available technical solutions for web analytics that are suitable for a healthcare operating environment where sensitive personal data is processed. In addition, the purpose is to ascertain the expert services available to support the use and efficient utilisation of web analytics tools. In the solution to be procured, data processing and storage must take place within the EU area. HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and attach to their response a general description/brochure of the solutions you offer for the need described above. Please state in your response whether you are interested in offering only web analytics tools or related expert services, or both, and address in your response in particular the information security aspect of the solution you offer and the use of cookies. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, clarifying questions may be presented to the supplier and/or an opportunity offered to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the information request may receive preliminary procurement documents for comment. Please submit responses to the information request and notify of your interest no later than 28.8.2026 at 12:00 to kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must mention "HUS 135-2026 - Web analytics tools ".

sig_011055b01c4d88cc16cc.description: A national programme is being established to encourage increased levels of physical activity and sustained participation in movement across England. The programme comprises a number of complementary workstreams, including marketing and communications, partnerships and engagement, rewards and recognition, educational content, and a digital component intended to support participation, engagement and long-term habit formation. The contracting authority is considering the future procurement of a supplier to design, build, operate and support the digital elements of the programme. A digital discovery exercise is currently underway and will provide an evidence-based recommendation for the future digital service, including user needs, service design, delivery approach and implementation roadmap. Whilst the final solution has not yet been determined, the discovery is expected to narrow the scope significantly and provide sufficient detail to support rapid delivery. The digital service may comprise a digital product, web-based service, social and community capability, AI-enabled engagement service, integration with existing consumer platforms, or a combination of these approaches. The successful supplier will be expected to take the outputs of the discovery phase through detailed design, build, deployment and live operation. The appointed supplier will work alongside other specialist partners responsible for marketing, communications, partnerships, rewards and wider programme delivery. The role of the digital supplier will be to translate programme objectives into effective digital services and experiences rather than duplicate functions delivered elsewhere within the programme. The programme is operating to ambitious timescales, with an initial digital capability expected to be launched before the end of 2026 and subsequently enhanced through live operation. The authority is therefore interested in engaging with suppliers who can demonstrate experience of delivering, operating and evolving user-centred digital services at pace. Additional information: HI NENC would like to invite potential providers of Digital services to apply to our Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) DN670401 as a supplier. If your company is not registered with the Proactis (ProContract) Due North Portal, click on this link Supplier registration (due-north.com) and complete your organisation name and email address and continue your registration. If you are already registered on the portal, log in as normal. In the "search" box in upper right-hand corner, type in DN670401 (this is the HI NENC DPS reference number). This opportunity will be developed as a further competition under Lot 5 of our DPS. You should therefore ensure you apply to Lot 5 to be able to bid to provide this service. You are also welcome to apply for any other Lots on our DPS that you feel are relevant to your organisation. Should we decide to proceed to procurement, we are expecting to publish the Invitation to Quote to our Lot 5 suppliers towards the end of July 2026. This timeline is subject to change. Interested suppliers are advised to apply to the DPS promptly to ensure they have been accepted to the framework and receive the competition notification. This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal procurement process and not award a contract. The information contained in this notice, including information relating to the nature and scope of the requirements, the service classification of this requirement from the list of CPV codes, is only indicative of the HI NENC's current thinking and is neither exhaustive nor binding. HI NENC reserves the right at its absolute discretion to amend it at the time of issue of any further notices or at any other time. HI NENC will not be liable for any bid cost, expenditure, work or effort incurred by a potential supplier in acting on the basis of this PIN

sig_013c2efea15fef33f841.description: Airedale NHS Foundation Trust ("the Trust") is progressing its Securing the Future (StF) programme, a Wave 1 scheme under the national New Hospital Programme (NHP). This initiative represents a significant strategic opportunity to modernise the Trust's estate and transform clinical delivery models in line with the Hospital 2.0 design principles. As an early pathfinder site, the Trust is positioned to influence and contribute to the development of future hospital standards and digitally enabled care environments. As the programme moves into the next phase of design development, the Trust is undertaking structured early market engagement to explore how innovative digital technologies and integrated solutions can support the delivery of Hospital 2.0 objectives, notably the transition to single‐patient‐room models of care. The Trust is particularly interested in solutions that can address the following priority areas: * Enhancing staff-patient communication: enabling patients to communicate their needs effectively and enabling staff to manage and prioritise tasks efficiently and safely across single‐room environments. * Supporting staff coordination across enlarged ward footprints: facilitating real‐time collaboration, communication, and staff location to improve workflow efficiency across expanded clinical areas. * Strengthening patient and clinical safety: enabling continuous or event‐based monitoring, improving response times and reducing unnecessary alarms, while mitigating the risk of alarm fatigue. * Optimising patient flow and operational management: supporting end‐to‐end patient movement within the hospital and enabling effective coordination with community services to improve throughput and discharge efficiency. To support this engagement, the Trust will host a virtual market engagement event at 10:30am on 23 April 2026. This session will outline the Trust's objectives, provide further context regarding the StF programme, and describe the thematic areas where market insight is sought. The briefing will be delivered by the Securing the Future programme team. Kindly be advised that, owing to anticipated attendance numbers, participation may be restricted to a maximum of two representatives per organisation. Following the event, the Trust will invite participants to provide structured feedback to help inform its understanding of available technologies, market capability, potential operating models, and integration approaches. Information gathered will support the Trust's future strategic planning and may inform the development of any subsequent procurement approach. Details of how to submit feedback will be provided during the event. For the avoidance of doubt, this activity constitutes early market engagement only. It does not form part of any procurement process, does not commit the Trust to undertake a procurement exercise, and does not confer any advantage in relation to any future competition undertaken by the Trust under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 or the Procurement Act 2023. Lot 1: .

sig_013c39969725eb8ec34f.description: Modernisation and consolidation of data centre infrastructure. Budapest Public Utilities Non-Profit Private Company Limited by Shares (BKM) wishes to modernise its data centre infrastructure. The IT infrastructure of the individual divisions (former Companies) operates under differing maturity and availability models; during the consolidation of these systems, it is intended to establish a service-based IT system (Infrastructure as a Service, hereinafter IAAS) that simplifies daily operational tasks. Therefore, it is necessary both to consolidate the systems operating in the data centre and to extend the support periods for equipment currently under manufacturer support, such that during the planned migration, by shutting down equipment leaving active operation, the support coverage attributable to them can be flexibly tracked over the contract period. The systems operating in the data centres (the systems to be consolidated and those under manufacturer support combined) are built from HPE system elements to an extent of ~80%. In addition to the service-based implementation, it is also necessary to ensure manufacturer hardware and software support for any system elements that continue to operate throughout the entire contract period. The server environment for the services to be provided during the contract period must be housed in the rented data centres of 2 different data centre service providers across a total of 2 locations, and administrator access must be provided to all systems implementing the service. In the initial phase of the service, the net storage capacity to be provided must be at least 354 TB per month. By the end of the contract period, the net storage demand may reach 600 TB per month, which must be able to be provided without replacing the data storage system. The service to be established must ensure the following allocable resources at the secondary site: 128 CPU cores 3072 GB memory (2611 unit of measurement; CU). The service platform must also be provided for the primary site in addition to the existing blades: 64 CPU cores 1536 GB memory (1306 unit of measurement; CU). sig_01649132e69dc7f0b1ec.description: Title: Software solution for strategic property management towards climate neutrality for Bildungsbau Hamburg - No contract notice Description: Market sounding regarding "Software solution for strategic property management towards climate neutrality for Bildungsbau Hamburg" - Voluntary prior information - No contract notice - This publication serves as a market sounding in preparation for a planned procurement project for the introduction of a digital system for the strategic and operational management of the decarbonisation of Bildungsbau Hamburg's property portfolio. The aim of the market sounding is to probe the market for corresponding software solutions, identify technical solution approaches, implementation options, functional delimitations as well as essential cost drivers and, on this basis, to develop a feasible and economically reasonable functional description for a subsequent procurement procedure. Upon completion of the market sounding, the insights gained will be evaluated by the contracting authority and neutrally incorporated into the further procurement documents. The contracting authority attaches great importance to the feedback from market participants and expressly intends to take this into account when designing the subsequent procurement project. Bildungsbau Hamburg is responsible for the construction, development and management of educational properties. The property portfolio comprises over 3.000 school buildings at several hundred locations with around 3,5 million m2 of rental space. In addition, the portfolio includes other education-related properties, including university buildings with over 200 individual properties and around 1 million m2 of space, as well as sports and special-purpose properties. Overall, this is a highly complex, structurally and functionally heterogeneous property portfolio. Organisationally, the portfolio is divided into two legally separate areas (SBH | Schulbau Hamburg as a state-run enterprise and GMH | Gebäudemanagement Hamburg GmbH as a 100% FHH-owned company), which differ not only in terms of legal framework conditions, but also in terms of organisational structures, management processes as well as data availability and data storage. Both organisational units pursue the goal of climate neutrality by 2040 at the latest, including defined interim targets by 2030. The building stock is characterised by a high degree of heterogeneity with regard to construction age, energy condition, building condition (e.g. building condition classes), usage types and technical equipment. Relevant data is available organisation-specific in various specialist systems and data bases (e.g. CAFM systems, energy management, maintenance and investment planning). As part of the project, it is to be examined how consolidated analyses for emissions and measure control can be derived on this basis. Against this background, the contracting authority intends to introduce a digital system that enables strategic and operational management of decarbonisation. The system shall in particular support the accounting of greenhouse gas emissions, the modelling of reduction paths and scenarios, the linking of emission and cost impacts, the prioritisation of measures in the existing stock as well as transparent and audit-proof decision support for management and political committees. Specialist energy planning, construction project management or the preparation of full life-cycle analyses are not the subject of the intended system. Upon completion of the market sounding, the insights resulting from it will be evaluated and, if necessary, taken into account for the further procurement projects and the procedure directed towards them. As part of the market sounding, the contracting authority would like to contact market participants without obligation in order to obtain assessments on the feasibility of the described functions, market-standard solution approaches, dependencies between data availability and functional scope as well as typical cost and effort structures. Notes on the procedure: See further under "Description of procurement"
sig_01649132e69dc7f0b1ec.title: Market consultation regarding "Software solution for strategic real estate management for climate neutrality for Bildungsbau Hamburg"

sig_01db481eb3edb9e7b16c.description: Short description: As a particularly vulnerable target for cyber security, the contracting authority wishes to expand and enhance IT security and data backup security. For this purpose, software and hardware are required which guarantee recovery after a cyber attack. A measure is therefore to be procured that protects the contracting authority's existing system, particularly with regard to virus scanning and data backup. Accordingly, a solution is to be implemented that enables rapid and efficient reconstruction in the event of a cyber-security-relevant attack. The focus is on protecting particularly sensitive and critical data (e.g. patient data). In particular, in this context attackers must be isolated, systems cleanly restored, downtime minimised and business continuity ensured. Description of the procurement (nature and scope of the service or indication of needs and requirements): This specification concerns software and hardware - as well as a cyber security solution within the backup - which serves to expand the IT security and data backup of Mannheim University Medical Centre within the backup. The solution is a vulnerable target for cyber security and data backup within the backup. For this purpose, software and hardware are provided as a solution for data recovery after a cyber attack. In particular, attackers are kept away, systems are cleanly restored, downtime is reduced and business continuity is ensured. In its current form, the contracting authority is the result of a merger of many companies that are digitising future-proof businesses with detailed IT know-how and innovative software development and supporting their business success. The cyber security solution consists of secure hardware and innovative software and guarantees the highest level of security. The physically isolated appliance, the immutable file systems and the end-to-end encryption offer comprehensive protection against potential attacks. These security features ensured that no one has unauthorised access to the data and systems. The cyber security solution makes it possible to protect critical data in the event of a cyber attack. It has the capability to isolate the attacker and cleanly restore the systems and ensures that it does not get into serious difficulties. Through this solution, downtime can be minimised and business continuity ensured. The cyber security solution works exclusively with hardware appliances. These appliances offer protection of data in hardware. The desired retention period for backup data is (always) part of a backup job. This retention period is applied when writing the data in the appliance - data that has been written once cannot be deleted or modified for this period. Furthermore, it continuously pulls malware signatures via a BSI portal and maintains an internal database for known malware. During data backup, it is checked in real time whether the data to be backed up is infected. During use, existing hardware is not quarantined. Accordingly, existing hardware can be put back into operation promptly. 1. Cyber security in the recovery process: The subject matter of the contract enables rapid and effective reconstruction in the event of a cyber-security-relevant attack. The focus here is on the protection of sensitive information and data. In the event of a cyber attack, the attacker is isolated and clean restoration of the systems is ensured. 2. 24/7 Customer support and integrated team: The contracting authority has a highly qualified team. This team can be reached around the clock and guarantees fast and efficient data recovery in the event of a cyber attack. The seamless integration of this team guarantees fast and competent support. 3. Hardware and software security: The holistic solution consisting of secure hardware and innovative software guarantees the highest level of security. The physically isolated appliance, the immutable file systems and the end-to-end encryption offer comprehensive protection against potential attacks. These security features ensured that no one has unauthorised access to the data and systems. Bunker-in-a-box: Security-by-design, immutable file system, physically isolated appliance (hardened Linux, no shell access) with scale-out performance, end-2-end-encrypted, NTP protection, retention lock, not recognizable in the network. Ransomware monitoring: Immediate areas of impact of an encryption attack and the data affected therein - also at VM level - are detected. Threat hunting: Threats are identified and a clean recovery point in the backup is found, without startling a potential attacker, by means of hashes, patterns or YARA rules. Sensitive data discovery: The proactive reduction of the attack surface takes place through understanding which data could be of interest to attackers. Orchestrated recovery: Commissioning and testing of the required procedures is automated. Here it is determined which applications or infrastructure areas require how much time for a recovery. Commvault backup infrastructure consists of: - 4 disk libraries (total 600 TB storage) - 1 tape library (6x LT0-7, 160 slots) Backed up daily are 800 VMs (approx. 500 TB) plus Windows file services (approx. 100 TB) Scope of contract award Lot LOT-0001: Expansion: Cyber security solution in backup / IT security and data backup. SW, HW, service and provision of services
sig_01db481eb3edb9e7b16c.title: Expansion: Cyber Security solution in backup/ IT security and data backup

sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO’s and TDPs.
sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production

sig_0214ef7a73c691b97c0e.description: The HSE is issuing this Request to Participate (“RTP”) in a Dynamic Purchasing System (hereafter ‘the DPS’) for the provision of Remote Health Monitoring Technologies to support the implementation of Virtual Ward care models via a fully end to end vendor managed solution. The HSE is the Contracting Authority for this public procurement competition on its own behalf and on behalf of all organisations funded by the HSE. A Virtual Ward is a time-limited, safe, and efficient alternative to bedded care enabled by technology that aims to support people who have an acute condition, or exacerbation of a chronic condition requiring hospital-level care, to receive this high acuity care in the place they call home. This approach can provide both an alternative to hospital admission at the Emergency Department, and/or facilitate an earlier discharge from a hospital ward for medical and surgical patients. This DPS will support the implementation of Virtual Wards and associated service capabilities within adult, older persons, and paediatric services across, but not limited to, respiratory, cardiology, and endocrinology pathways. The HSE is seeking to procure an effective and successful market proven, end-to-end vendor managed solution ready for immediate deployment. A central component of the Virtual Ward Solution supported by Remote Health Monitoring Technologies service will be a comprehensive fully vendor managed (end-to-end) solution, including the provision and support of a suite of web-based application(s) and clinical measurement equipment, to facilitate acute clinical care delivered remotely by a multidisciplinary team (MDT) if clinically appropriate and with clear lines of clinical responsibility and governance. This solution will facilitate the avoidance of hospital admission and/or early hospital discharge by providing safe technology that allows suitable patients to be clinically monitored from where they call home.
sig_0214ef7a73c691b97c0e.title: DPS Qualification__Provision of Remote Health Monitoring Technologies to Support the Implementation of Virtual Ward Care Model Solutions (HSE ref. 23112)
