sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.description: Avfall Sør would like to invite the market to a dialogue on the future solution for weighing residual waste at the recycling stations. The aim is to find a system with a high degree of automation/self-service, user friendliness and effective customer flow. It must take care of HSE considerations and be adapted to both the current and future needs for effective resource utilisation and sustainable operation. Avfall Sør has three recycling stations with high availability and access control. The residue waste is collected in large containers with compression; either closed compressor containers or open containers with rolling compressors. This can be changed, but a compressor system is wanted and protection from weather and wind. Key figures are given in the annex. We would like to charge for residual waste based on the weighted amount per customer, in order to comply with the polluter-payer principle and to ensure that sorting pays off. Avfall Sør has examined known systems in the market, but not found satisfactory systems. We would therefore like to have a dialogue with a tenderer who believes that they can offer this. The system must handle weighing and payment of residue waste in an efficient and user friendly way, without a requirement for dedicated manpower. Integration to established systems is not required, but we would like to present the possibilities. Tenderers are invited to submit a solution proposal with a description of relevant systems and price estimates, as well as a reference system. Deadline: 10.12.25, 16.00.Solution proposal can be sent in communication module in Mercell. Deadline for this: 03.12.25, 16:00.
sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.title: Market dialogue - solution for weighing residual waste at recycling stations for Avfall Sør AS

sig_0232050ad191d862ee04.description: The Ministry of Justice, through His Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS), is undertaking preliminary market engagement to support consideration of a potential legacy archive recovery and digitisation requirement relating to historic index records currently held on obsolete media. HMCTS holds a substantial archive of historic index records, primarily across microfiche and cassette media. The current estimated scope includes approximately 20,000 microfiche sheets containing around 2 million records, and 658 cassette media units containing around 6.5 million records. The total estimated archive is therefore approximately 8.5 million records. There are also historic records held in books, although these are currently considered lower volume and lower priority than the microfiche and cassette records. The current arrangements rely on legacy physical and digital media, manual search activity, local operational knowledge and ageing technology. This creates challenges around retrieval speed, consistency, resilience, future access, preservation and the continued availability of the underlying information. HMCTS is therefore exploring market capability that could support the controlled recovery, digitisation, extraction, validation, indexing and searchability of these historic records. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to improve HMCTS’ understanding of market capability relating to: • inventory, cataloguing and condition assessment of microfiche and cassette media; • technical discovery of cassette formats, data structures, hardware or software dependencies and recoverability; • high-resolution microfiche digitisation; • recovery and extraction of data from cassette media; • image enhancement, OCR, intelligent data extraction and confidence scoring; • creation of a common target data model across recovered and digitised records; • validation, de-duplication, exception handling and quality assurance; • secure repository and search capability, including access controls, audit logging and reporting; • service transition, user guidance, business change and benefits tracking. Through this RFI, HMCTS is seeking to better understand: • available market capability and supplier capacity; • how relevant services are normally delivered, for example through specialist digitisation services, legacy media recovery, data extraction, repository/search solutions, managed technical services, consultancy, integration support or mixed delivery models; • indicative discovery, pilot, implementation and delivery approaches; • potential commercial models, procurement routes and phasing options; • legal, data protection, security, records management and information assurance considerations; • indicative costs, cost drivers, timescales, dependencies and delivery risks; • the extent to which existing storage, records management or archive services could support or influence a future delivery route. This RFI is deliberately focused on market capability, technical feasibility and delivery evidence. HMCTS is not asking suppliers to design the future service or make policy, legal, retention, disposal or public access decisions at this stage. Any future capability would need to operate within appropriate HMCTS governance, records management, data protection, security, information assurance, auditability and access control arrangements. This RFI is an evidence-gathering activity only. It is not a request for a quotation, proposal or tender, and it should not be treated as a commitment to any future procurement. The issuing of this RFI does not commit HMCTS or MoJ to procure any services, software, data platforms or solutions; does not indicate any supplier preference; and does not create exclusivity or advantage for suppliers who respond. Responses will be used solely to inform HMCTS’ understanding of the market, possible future delivery options, recoverability of legacy media, business case development, affordability, assurance considerations, commercial strategy and potential next-stage routes. Lot 1: . None

sig_0240706272c9855b09af.description: ***SEE ATTACHMENTS FOR FULL TEXT OF ANNOUNCEMENT*** BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) FA9451-24-S-0001 Air Force Research Laboratory Directed Energy Directorate ANNOUNCEMENT OVERVIEW Initial 22 November 2023 NAICS CODE: The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715 for Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees. FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. ANNUAL REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS: Potential offerors are notified that effective 01 Jan 2005 to be eligible for an award and in compliance with FAR 52.204-7 and DFARS 252.204-7007 Alternate A, they must submit Annual Representations and Certifications, via SAM.gov. Before submitting the electronic Annual Representations and Certifications, Contractors must be registered in the SAM Database. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. ESTIMATED PROGRAM COST: Anticipated funding for the program (not per Call, contract, or award): FY24 FY25 FY26 FY27 FY28 TOTAL $100M $100M $100M $100M $99M $499M This funding profile is an estimate only and will not be a contractual obligation for funding. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). It is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all the Offeror’s data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. POINT OF CONTACT: a) Administrative, technical, or contractual questions should be sent via e-mail to afrl.rdlb.tacticalbaa@us.af.mil. All requests must include a name, e-mail address, and phone number of an organizational point of contact. b) Each Call will include specific contracting points of contact. sig_02420d8bb1e90b05c099.description: The contract covers the delivery, operation, maintenance and support of a biometric solution that enables the capture of biometrics (facial photo, fingerprints and signature) at the contracting entity's locations in Denmark and Greenland. In connection with this, the supplier must deliver the following services: - Solution for the capture of biometrics (facial photo, fingerprints and signature) in Denmark and Greenland; - Mobile solution for both online and offline capture of biometrics (facial photo, fingerprints and signature); - Delivery and operation of a High Level Application Programming Interface (HL-API) for installation on the Customer's systems, as well as the delivery of system documentation; - Removal and disposal of the Customer's existing system; - Operation, maintenance and support of the biometric solution; - Removal of the biometric solution upon termination of the contract. The contracting entity's expected scope of biometric capture during the contract period appears from Annex 2.2, Statement and forecast for biometric capture, as well as from Annex 5, Prices. The tendered contract also includes the following options: - Option for the Danish Immigration Service's acquisition of the contract's services. When the Danish Immigration Service exercises the option, the supplier must deliver, install and implement a biometric solution at the Danish Immigration Service's locations, deliver a biometric solution for mobile online and offline capture, and deliver operation, maintenance and support of the biometric solution to the Danish Immigration Service. The option is described in further detail in Annex 12, Options, item 5, and the Danish Immigration Service's expected need for biometric capture is stated in Annex 5, Prices. - Option for the delivery of a biometric solution in the Faroe Islands, cf. Annex 12, Options, item 2. - Option for the delivery of a biometric solution for self-service, cf. Annex 12, Options, item 3. - Option for the delivery of a solution for the physical collection of residence cards (document boxes), cf. Annex 12, Options, item 4. Please note that the stated estimated contract value includes the utilisation of all options. The estimated contract value excl. options, except options for contract extensions, is estimated to be approximately DKK 6.800.000.

sig_0258ca6e43217c6877de.description: In the current model, the technical implementation of communal services is integrated into the IT organisation established by the State of Fribourg. In particular, SITel ensures contracting with technical service providers and the management of IT developments, in collaboration with the DIGI-FR team, which carries the business needs and ensures functional responsibility for communal services. With the coming to an end of the DIGI-FR program 2023–2026 and the evolution of the legal framework relating to e-government, this model is bound to evolve. From 2027, the municipalities, through the entity responsible for representing them, will take over responsibility for the development, operation and maintenance of their services on the Fribourg virtual counter. They will thus have the capacity to directly commission the necessary service providers and manage the end-to-end technical implementation of their services. This call for tenders aims to establish the capacities required for the development and maintenance of communal services in this new model. The public procurement aims to establish a contractual framework which will subsequently allow the ACF, according to its needs and on the basis of a predefined service catalogue, to award its contracts to referenced partners via single consultations (mini-tenders) in a simplified and competitive procedure.
sig_0258ca6e43217c6877de.title: Framework contract for e-government DIGI-FR

sig_02613a63542d4781b004.description: INITIAL CONTRACT The Pensionsversicherungsanstalt (PVA) carried out a negotiated procedure without prior call for competition with a single tenderer in the year 2015 following the revocation of an open procedure for the procurement of licences (Alfresco, Camunda and Vaadin) including maintenance. Licences relating to Alfresco (lot 01), Camunda (lot 02) and Vaadin Enterprise (lot 03) including maintenance and support services were to be procured for all computer workstations (approx. 7500) for the PVA. The services for the Camunda licences (lot 2) were commissioned on 28.05.2015 and those for the Alfresco licences (lot 1) and Vaadin licences (lot 3) on 19.08.2015 (costs € 1.504.160,00). 1. The previous pricing was discontinued by the manufacturer Camunda in January 2024. In order to continue to be able to access the enterprise edition of Camunda, a transition to a new licensing model was required and the term ran (instead of previously indefinite) from 01.01.2025 to 31.12.2025 (costs € 164.029,00). The existing service contract was accordingly amended in this respect pursuant to section 365 para. 3 item 5 of the BVergG [Federal Public Procurement Act] 2018. 2. NOTICE OF AMENDMENT of the Camunda licensing (lot 2), which is hereby announced: After the expiry of the term of the 1 contract amendment for lot 2 as of 31.12.2025, the existing licence agreement was extended for a further 3 years from 01.01.2026 to 31.12.2028 (costs € 492.087,00) and this contract amendment is hereby announced pursuant to section 365 para. 3 item 5 of the BVergG 2018. CALCULATION BREAKDOWN CONCERNING THE TWO ANNOUNCED CONTRACT AMENDMENTS: The original contract value of all 3 tendered lots (initial contract) amounted (extrapolated to 4 years) to € 1.504.160,00. Accordingly, a theoretical total contract status for all 3 lots of € 2.160.276,00 would currently result (however, without taking into account cost reductions and without taking into account index adjustments as well as without other contract amendments made in the past before the entry into force of the BVergG 2018). sig_0261d29e8ce4f6d85567.description: The Danish Parliament passed in 2018 the Act on trials of a social tax-free card, which entered into force on 1. January 2019, after which vulnerable citizens can be assessed for a social tax-free card. The social tax-free card has now been made permanent cf. Act 616 of 11. June 2024 with entry into force on 1. January 2025. The authority responsible for the Act is the Ministry of Social Affairs and Housing. The purpose of the Act is that citizens with special social problems have the right to receive a social tax-free card. The tax-free card must give vulnerable citizens the opportunity to earn 41.280 DKK tax-free per calendar year (2024-level) through ordinary and unsupported work for companies, public authorities, etc., without the income being deducted from welfare benefits or other income-dependent public benefits. The social tax-free card must thus give the most vulnerable citizens in society better opportunities to participate in society's communities, contribute and experience value in everyday life. The intention is also that the social tax-free card encourages companies to take social responsibility by engaging vulnerable citizens. KOMBIT has, pursuant to the Act, the responsibility to operate the system support on behalf of the municipalities. KOMBIT is therefore tendering the permanent management of the Social Tax-Free Card System for 6 + 2 years. It has been agreed between the parties (Ministry of Social Affairs, Local Government Denmark and KOMBIT) that the current solution supporting the trial scheme is made permanent with limited planned further development. KOMBIT is therefore tendering the management of the System, including application operations, support and application maintenance, further development and infrastructure operations as well as transition from the current supplier, KnowledgeCube, which has managed the trial scheme.
sig_0261d29e8ce4f6d85567.title: Socialt Frikort 2.0.

sig_0273419f3619102cfe5e.description: Link Group, the Contracting Authority, is seeking to modernise its telephony and contact management environment as part of a wider customer experience transformation. The requirement is not limited to a like-for-like telephony replacement. Link is seeking to understand how the market can support a move from fragmented channels and siloed systems towards a single, integrated and insight-led contact management platform. The primary objective is to implement a modern, scalable, cloud-based Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) solution capable of supporting seamless multi-channel customer engagement across voice, live chat, messaging, social media and future digital channels. Link is particularly interested in solutions that can provide a single view of the customer, intelligent routing based on customer intent and need, real-time operational visibility, workforce engagement capability and data-driven insight across the end-to-end customer journey. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued solely to initiate a Preliminary Market Consultation exercise. The purpose is to test market capability, understand available delivery models, inform Link’s emerging specification and procurement strategy, and explore how suppliers can support both technology replacement and service transformation outcomes, including automation, virtual assistants, AI-assisted colleague support, workforce management and customer journey-led redesign. Link’s emerging priorities include reducing repeat contact, redials, avoidable transfers and misdirected queries; improving colleague access to customer history and knowledge prompts; enabling real-time demand management and reporting; increasing digital adoption through automation and self-service; and ensuring that future technology is aligned to priority customer journeys rather than being designed around existing channel structures. Lot 1: . Link Group is a group of social enterprise companies and one of Scotland’s largest social landlords. Link Group provides affordable housing, property management, regeneration, advice, financial inclusion, employability, care and support services to a large and diverse customer base across Scotland. Link Group serves more than 20,000 customers and provides housing management services to circa 16,000 tenants in social rented accommodation, including general needs and sheltered housing. The Link Group structure includes a number of related organisations and service areas that collectively deliver housing, property, care, support and community-based services. These include Link Group Ltd, which provides core group functions; Link Group Housing Services, which delivers housing management services for social rented tenants; C~urb, which brings together development, property management, letting, factoring and property maintenance activities; Horizon Housing Association, which provides affordable housing and services that support people with impairments to live independently; Larkfield Housing Association, a community-based Registered Social Landlord in Greenock; LinkLiving, which provides person-centred care, housing support and wellbeing services, and West Highland Housing Association, which provides affordable housing, property management, and maintenance services across the Lorn area and the Inner Hebridean islands of Scotland. The proposed replacement of telephony and contact centre systems is intended to support the wider Link Group operating environment rather than a single isolated service area. The future solution may therefore need to support multiple customer-facing and colleague-facing functions across housing, repairs, property management, factoring, care and support, advice, employability, development and corporate services. The Customer Service Centre (CSC) acts as a primary customer contact function, managing enquiries across housing, repairs, income, complaints and related services. Link also operates specialist customer-facing teams, including services supporting housing applications, registrations, lettings, responsive repairs, planned maintenance, compliance activities and property-related enquiries. These teams collectively support high-volume contact across a broad range of customer journeys. For market-sizing purposes, Link currently anticipates a future licence requirement in the region of 250–500 user licences across the Group, subject to confirmation through future operating model development, service design and multi-skilling activity. Given the scale and breadth of these services, effective contact management is central to Link’s ability to provide responsive, accessible and joined-up services to tenants, owners, applicants, private rented sector customers, supported people, partners and other stakeholders. This group-wide context is important because suppliers may be required to demonstrate how their proposed solution can support different operating models, service hours, customer journeys, user groups, reporting requirements, call flows, contact channels and integration needs across Link Group. Link is therefore seeking market insight into solutions that can provide scalable, resilient and configurable contact management capability across the full breadth of the group, while enabling consistent customer experience, improved colleague access to information and better operational insight.. sig_02acb1039e53b4932dca.description: Scottish Government and NHSScotland are exploring options for a single national Infection Prevention Control eSurveillance solution that will ensure consistent application across all of NHSScotland. This will replace the existing disparate systems across Health Boards. The national solution will need to: - Integrate and be interoperable with some of the numerous NHS Scotland existing systems. - Provide efficient local and national reporting. - Provide real time data (e.g. providing alerts to flag identification of an infection, provide up to date reporting) - Be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and must have an extremely high degree of resilience in order to minimise any periods of scheduled or unscheduled downtime. Vendors of future solutions should note that this resilience should include but not be limited to Failover and Disaster Recovery of the system with limited technical intervention. This soft market test is being conducted to determine what solutions may be available, determine the scope of any future procurement to enable the delivery of a national solution, and to ascertain indicative costs. sig_02f3081ecfb6290db6c4.description: For over 25 years, the Authority has relied on its existing Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) platform to manage IT services. It has been the backbone of logging, tracking and resolving requests—everything from fixing technical issues to setting up new starters. The technology landscape has moved on: cloud platforms, automation and integrated digital services are now standard, and the Authority now wishes to explore this technology. The Authority is now moving to Enterprise Service Management (ESM). In simple terms, ESM means creating one front door for services—a single, easy‐to‐use platform where staff and customers can make requests, check progress and get help quickly, regardless of which team provides the service. Behind the scenes, it uses proven good‐practice processes (ITIL) to ensure work is handled consistently and efficiently. It will also integrate with tools we already use, enabling automation, clearer customer journeys and, over time, the use of AI to enhance the experience. The Authority’s current version of its ESM platform is hosted on‐premise, and the contract ends in March 2026. The Authority’s version of this ESM tool provides a single platform for multiple service areas, not just IT. The Authority’s ambition for this Procurement is to implement, migrate to and continue to support a cloud hosted ESM platform that provides a modern, flexible and integrated approach to organisation wide service delivery. The Authority plans to retire its I.T. Asset Management (ITAM) tool as part of this tender. This will allow the Authority to leverage greater capabilities within a single platform, providing better data for decision‐making through modern dashboards and reporting. The Contract is expected to commence on Thursday 19th February 2026 and will run for a core period of five (5) years, unless terminated or extended in accordance with the terms set out in the Contract. The estimated total value of the requirement over the Contract’s five-year core period is £935,000, which also represents the maximum budget available for Supplier Tenders and the resulting ESM Contract. Any Tender submissions exceeding this value will be rejected in accordance with the assessment criteria outlined in Stage 1: Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) and Stage 2: Tender Evaluation Criteria. The Contract will have a core period of five (5) years, subject to the termination provisions set out within the Contract. In addition, the Authority reserves the right to extend the Contract by up to five (5) additional years, through two separate extension options: • One extension of three (3) years • One extension of two (2) years If both extension options are exercised, the maximum potential duration of the Contract would be ten (10) years. The estimated contract value of £1,910,000.00, as stated in this Contract Notice, is based on the Authority awarding the contract at its maximum budget of £935,000 for the initial 5-year core term, and subsequently exercising all five optional extension years. For the extension period (years 6 to 10), an estimated annual inflation rate of 4% has been applied to reflect projected cost increases over time. The estimated value is provided in good faith to assist Suppliers in preparing their Tenders. It does not constitute a commitment by the Authority to spend the full amount. No stated value shall create a binding financial obligation unless explicitly confirmed within the Contract. Lot 1: .

sig_0300d71afe51f9879564.description: The subject of the tender is a contract for the following service: framework agreement FA SAP BW BPC SAC (Lot 1). As a promotional bank for North Rhine-Westphalia, NRW.BANK (hereinafter also referred to as the contracting authority) supports the federal state in its structural and economic policy tasks. In doing so, it acts on behalf of the public, neutrally regarding competition, and deploys the entire spectrum of credit-based promotional products - from classical credit to tailored advice. Its three promotional fields are "Economy", "Living space" as well as "Infrastructure/Municipalities". In contrast to commercial banks, the customers of NRW.BANK are primarily house banks and other promotional intermediaries. NRW.BANK strictly observes the prohibition of discrimination in relation to other credit institutions. Its cooperation with cooperative and private banks as well as savings banks follows - neutrally regarding competition - the house bank procedure. The business of NRW.BANK focuses on the canon of promotional areas defined by Understanding II. Competitive business (such as commercial property financing as well as the new issue of mortgage pfandbriefe) was no longer pursued by Landesbank NRW, the predecessor institution of NRW.BANK. To fulfil its mandate, NRW.BANK operates in the following areas: - Securing and improving the medium-sized structure of the economy, in particular financings for business start-ups and consolidations, - state social housing promotion, - provision of venture capital, - structural development of towns and municipalities, - infrastructure measures, - measures in agriculture and forestry and in rural areas, - environmental protection, technology and innovation measures, - measures of a social, cultural and scientific nature. Against this background, the subject matter of the performance is a framework agreement on the consultation and support of NRW.BANK in the area of SAP BW (HANA) and msgGillardon (BAIS and ORRP). The award of the individual contracts relating to the framework agreement takes place on the procurement platform vergabe.NRW on the basis of mini-competitions between the contractual partners to the framework agreement. The framework agreement is to be concluded with 6 framework agreement partners (Lot 1). The framework agreement has a term of three years and can be extended by one year. The maximum call-off is 5.200 person days (Lot 1). The minimum purchase across all framework agreement partners is 200 person days.

sig_0326642c9a73f5e007d5.description:
The strategic objective of the Office is the elimination of unnecessary paper-based administration. To this end, the Office aims to transition internal records management processes entirely to electronic channels and to develop electronic communication with its clients – taking into consideration the rules prescribed in Act 2023 of 2015 on the digital state and the provision of digital services (hereinafter referred to as the Digital State Act) and Government Decrees and implementing regulations on the general rules for electronic administration and trust services – striving primarily for electronic communication via the official gateway (Hivatali kapu), company gateway (Cégkapu) and client gateway (Ügyfélkapu). For the purpose of developing the Office's records management processes, a project has been established (hereinafter referred to as the IFK Project), the aim of which is to replace the Electronic Document and Records Management System currently operating in the Office (CONTENTUM – EDOK) and to introduce a records and document management software supporting digital administration. The main objective of the procurement is to procure an electronic records and document management system that: - supports paperless internal electronic operations and the intra-organisational implementation of electronic administration at a high level of operational security, - is capable of supporting the records management, document storage and case management processes of high volumes of documents with as little human intervention as possible and with built-in automations, - ensures the workflow and task management related to documents necessary for the performance of official records management duties, and ensures the establishment of the reporting capability arising in connection therewith. - The Office intends to implement a complex, predominantly electronic document management-based operation, which necessarily includes the support of uniform traditional paper-based processes. Main expectations regarding the future records management processes to be implemented: Technical Description Annex No. 2. Subject of the procurement: a) supply of electronic records and document management software (and system modules) (off-the-shelf / proprietary off-the-shelf software) certified pursuant to Ministry of Interior Decree No. 3/2018 (II.21.) and associated licences (main subject of procurement): The Contracting Authority requests the complete handover of the finished software (and system modules) licence certificates in 3 instalments according to the tasks and deadlines set out in the implementation schedule as follows: 20 licences within 11 days following contract signature, 200 licences within 179 days following contract signature, 580 licences within 326 days following contract signature. b) implementation (realisation, development) tasks: implementation tasks comprise the following tasks carried out in accordance with the requirements defined in the Technical Description: ba) establishment of the software environment (installation, parameterisation), bb) development tasks, bc) system integration tasks, bd) training, be) testing and bug fixing, bf) migration tasks. c) trial operation, support of go-live and further support services. Following the successful completion and acceptance of tests, as well as the delivery of end-user training, the Contracting Authority expects the electronic records and document management software to be put into live operation during support. The Contracting Authority stipulates that from handover for live operation until the end of the support period, support services shall be provided for at least 6 and at most 12 months in accordance with the requirements of the Technical Description. The records management activity of the Office must be established in compliance with the relevant legislation; thus, the new records and document management software must support the following along the lines of compliance with the following basic legal requirements: • The electronic records and document management system is capable of supporting the establishment of the Office's records management process in accordance with Government Decree No. 335/2005 (XII. 29.) on the general requirements for records management of bodies performing public duties, based on Section 4 of Ministry of Interior Decree No. 3/2018 (II.21.). • The electronic records and document management system complies with the expectations set out in Ministry of Interior Decree No. 3/2018 (II.21.) on the requirements applicable to records management software usable at bodies performing public duties, which it certifies with a valid certificate. • The archival transfer of electronic records from the records management system must be implemented directly in accordance with the provisions of Ministry of Human Capacities Decree No. 34/2016 (XI. 30.) on the procedures and technical requirements for the public archival acceptance of records stored in electronic form. • The electronic records and document management system must manage the records schedule set out in Ministry of Interior Decree No. 78/2012 (XII. 28.) on the issuance of the uniform records schedule of municipal offices. • The electronic records and document management system must ensure integrated operation with the secure delivery service set out in Act 2023 of 2015 on the digital state and the provision of digital services (hereinafter referred to as the Digital State Act) and in Government Decree No. 321/2024 (XI.6.), the automatic downloading, registration, filing and legible (pdf) display of consignments and electronic forms (iForm, E-paper) received using the form submission support service. The records and document management software must ensure from its interface the verification of validity associated with the electronic signature and seal usable for the provision of digital services defined in the Digital State Act and its implementing regulations. The subject of the procurement, as indicated in point 2 of the Technical Description,

the electronic records and document management system and system modules indicated in the point, as well as the related services, have been grouped according to the following requirements: - functional requirements (Technical description point 4.1), - non-functional requirements (Technical description point 4.2), - technical requirements (Technical description point 4.3). Security requirements: The records and document management system must meet the security requirements defined in the relevant legislation, with particular regard to the following legislation and future amendments to new and/or currently known legislation that have become effective during the implementation period: - The provisions of Act No. 2024. of the year on the cyber security of Hungary. - The provisions of Government Decree No. 418/2024. (XII. 23.) on the implementation of the Act on the cyber security of Hungary, and those defined in MK Decree No. 7/2024. (VI. 24.) on the requirements for security classification and the specific protection measures to be applied in the case of individual security classes. - Requirements according to § 25/I of Act No. 2011. of the year (Infotv.). - Security and protection requirements defined in the IT Security and IT regulations of the Mayor's Office, or based thereon. The tenderer must prepare a security plan in connection with the development and adaptation tasks of the records and document management system, which includes the presentation of security requirements and necessary measures. In detail according to the draft contract and the technical description.

sig_0328641f844792a58a5c.description: DMZ network for tunnels and bridges The gemeente Den Haag had a DMZ network designed, supplied and integrated in 2018-2019 in order to operate and monitor road tunnels and bridges more efficiently. A DMZ network (demilitarised zone) is a secured sub-network that provides an extra layer of protection between an internal network and external networks, such as the internet. The following objects and locations are connected to the DMZ network for tunnels and bridges of the gemeente Den Haag: Road tunnels: Victory Boogie Woogie tunnel; Hubertus tunnel; Konings tunnel; Bridges: Binckhorst bridge; Laak bridge; Trekvliet bridge. Locations: Scheveningen Control Centre; Secondary Control Centre; The Hague City Hall. During the realisation of the network, a maintenance contract was agreed by the gemeente Den Haag with the realising party for a duration of a maximum of 7 years. This maintenance contract expires in September 2026. Assignment In order to keep the DMZ network available and reliable, the gemeente Den Haag (hereinafter: Client) wishes to conclude a multi-year maintenance contract with one Contractor through this tendering procedure, with an initial term of six (6) years. The Client wants the DMZ network to continue functioning independently and securely with high availability and reliability. The maintenance must be carried out in such a way that all systems continue to function within the established failure definitions. For the multi-year maintenance, the Client wishes to enter into a performance-based maintenance contract. It is the responsibility of the Contractor to determine within the maintenance contract which activities must be performed to meet the (functional) requirements of the Client. In doing so, the Client wishes to make the contract with the Contractor as result-oriented as possible. This is reflected by including requirements in the area of availability and reliability of the network in the Programme of Requirements. The Contractor is expected to fully unburden the Client in the area of operational management and maintenance of the DMZ network. The following activities generally fall within the scope of the Assignment (non-exhaustive): Preventive and corrective maintenance; Installation responsibility; Maintenance registration; Fault registration and analysis; Inventory and warehouse management; Information management; Reporting and consultation; Continuous improvement. The scope of the maintenance concerns the network systems that belong to the DMZ network in (technical rooms of) the various objects. The objects and locations are connected in a network configuration with fibre-optic cables. These fibre-optic cables are leased lines from Ziggo and do not form part of the scope. The current maintenance contract for the DMZ network expires on 8 September 2026. In accordance with the planning (see paragraph 2.3), the contract can be awarded from 31 July 2026. There will then be a short transition period between the new Contractor and the current contractor, namely from a maximum of 31 July 2026 to 8 September 2026. For the award, a Plan of Approach is requested for the “quality” component to ensure the transition period runs as efficiently as possible. The Contractor must take over the current network from 8 September to then create a design for the upgrade of the network for both hardware and software. Optional scope Replacement of network components (including extension of multi-year maintenance) To keep the DMZ network up-to-date, periodic replacement of network components (switches, firewalls and servers) is necessary. In approximately 6 years, various components will reach/approach the end of their technical or economic life and a replacement will be necessary. The Agreement includes an option to have this replacement carried out by the Contractor, linked to an extension of the multi-year maintenance for a duration of six (6) years. Integration of new objects The DMZ network was developed to be scalable during its realisation so that new objects can be integrated in the future. The Agreement takes into account the expansion of the number of objects connected to the DMZ network, by means of an option to extend the maintenance of the network to the maximum capacity in the Control Centre, whereby a maximum of 3 road tunnels and 4 movable bridges can be connected to the network in addition to the current objects. Scope changes Renovation of 4 movable bridges (4BB) The municipality entered into an agreement in 2025 with a contractor for the renovation of 4 movable bridges (the 4BB project). The renovation of the Laak bridge and the Trekvliet bridge is part of the scope of this agreement, and the renovation of both bridges will take place within the term of the Agreement for the maintenance of the DMZ network. After completion of the renovation, the maintenance scope within the DMZ network Agreement regarding the Laak bridge and Trekvliet bridge will change/lapse. This concerns the components belonging to the local object and the Scheveningen/Secondary Control Centre. The connection to the DMZ network will remain in place. Renewal of Binckhorst bridge The gemeente Den Haag is currently preparing for the renewal of the Binckhorst bridge. The renewal is expected to take place from the year 2028 and will therefore be carried out within the term of the Agreement for the maintenance (local object components) of the DMZ network. After completion of the project, the maintenance scope within the DMZ network regarding the Binckhorst bridge will change/lapse.

Procurement of support services for the editorial maintenance of the internet and intranet pages of the State of Hesse Lot LOT-0000: Support services for the editorial maintenance of the internet and intranet pages of the State of Hesse. Editorial Profile – Online Communication The fields of activity include ongoing and project-related support in the online-appropriate preparation and uploading of content on the State's portals as well as support in the maintenance of social media channels. This profile comprises the following tasks: •Online-appropriate preparation of texts in accordance with the respective media user requirements. •Editorial maintenance of texts for our internet and intranet presences. •Support for the daily maintenance of the State's own social media channels (predominantly Facebook, Instagram or X), expansion and development of social media strategies and community management. •Analysis, design and optimisation of navigation and information structures of the various portals. •Conception and setup of new internet services. •Pre-qualification and forwarding of error and fault reports. •Quality assurance of style guides and guidelines on the portals and their functionalities from an editorial perspective. •Creation and updating of reference works and working aids for editorial teams. •Carrying out measures for search engine optimisation (SEO) and AI-supported search system optimisation (GEO). •Advising, conception and creation of statistics using the Matomo software. •Planning and implementation of workshops and training courses in the online editorial environment. •Conception and production of explainer videos. •Research and consultancy activities on new internet trends as well as best practices in digital administrative communication. Qualification At least three years of experience in the following qualifications is expected: •Editorial maintenance and further development of digital internet offerings •Working with the Drupal content management system or Portal Site Manager •Daily maintenance of portal pages and migration of content from external sources •Analysis, design and optimisation of navigation and information structures •Image research, image editing and design of information •Sound knowledge of search engine optimisation (SEO) and AI-supported search system optimisation (GEO) •In carrying out workshops and training courses on editorial topics Very good knowledge of the German language in spoken and written form is required (minimum requirement C2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages or equivalent). In addition, the following qualifications are desirable: •Experience in the editorial maintenance of an information portal for the presentation of current news, events and projects for a federal, state or municipal administration •Experience in the editorial maintenance and management of an administrative portal with a connection to the Online Gateway Portal Federation (PVOG) for a federal, state or municipal administration Editorial Profile - Accessibility When preparing content to be suitable for online use, particular care must be taken to ensure that people with disabilities and non-native speakers can also use these offerings. In order to meet these requirements, editorial teams must integrate alternative presentation forms into the website alongside the normal processing and presentation of web content. Examples: •For visually impaired people who have the text read out to them by appropriate programmes, the text structure must be conveyed via the HTML code. •In the case of video content, the content of the audio track must always be provided via subtitling and thus also be accessible to people with hearing impairments. •Standard language texts must be translated into Plain Language, thereby opening up access to information and communication for people with cognitive disabilities and non-native speakers. Tasks •PDF documents must be revised so that they meet accessibility requirements (in accordance with PDF/UA-1 & WCAG 2.1). oTag structures in PDFs must be created and checked. oDocuments checked for readability via screen reader and documents checked for conformity regarding PDF/UA •PDF documents that were created in the various departments of the State must be retroactively checked for accessibility. •WORD format templates for generating accessible PDFs must be created, as must test catalogues/guidelines and problem statistics. •Creation of texts in Plain Language. •In addition, VTT files must be provided for the subtitling of videos. •Designing and creating sign language videos. •Specialist editorial teams are to be advised and supported with regard to improving accessibility, and information materials on the subject of accessibility are to be created. •Furthermore, the planning and implementation of workshops and training courses, in close cooperation with the training area for accessible IT, is part of the range of tasks. •The planning and implementation of long-term strategies to improve accessibility are also expected. Qualification At least 3 years of experience in the following points is required: •Creation of accessible PDFs in accordance with European Standard EN 301 549 and the PDF/UA standard (ISO 14289-1) •Creation of texts in Plain Language (DIN SPEC 33429) •Subtitling of videos (creation of VTT files) Very good knowledge of the German language in spoken and written form is required (minimum requirement C2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages or equivalent).

In addition, the following experiences are desirable: •Implementation of accessibility measures in accordance with the Hessian Accessible Information Technology Ordinance (BITV HE) •Creation of sign language videos Further information can be found in the file "Leistungsbeschreibung" on the procurement platform.

sig_0339b1bcbb995a1a1447.description: The published call for tenders was based on the dynamic purchasing system ''Telecommunications equipment 2025 (00758)'' established by Hansel Oy. Rajavartiolaitos invited tenders for gateway solutions in accordance with the published call for tenders and its annexes. Significant changes to data processing environments are under way at the Border Guard, which have identified the need to implement, streamline and standardise the procurement procedures used for gateway solutions. In addition, a need has been identified to procure services that ensure the suitability of gateways for the target architecture and guarantee the efficient utilisation of the solutions during their lifecycle. The currently estimated need is for approximately 13 gateway solutions, the procurement of which will take place in the years 2025-2029. Support is estimated to be needed for the entire lifecycle of the products. Gateway solutions are needed to segregate public, restricted (TLIV), confidential (TLIII) and secret (TLII) security classification data processing environments from environments of other security classification categories. Needs range from simple data diode solutions to more complex bidirectional implementations. The majority of estimated needs are unidirectional implementations intended to bring information from a lower-level environment to a higher-level environment in compliance with the Bell-LaPadula model. The minimum requirements for the products and services subject to procurement were described in the call for tenders and its annexes. This procurement concerns the contract period 2026-2027 possibly extended by optional periods of 2 years, two (2) items in total. The estimated scope of the procurement is 13 gateway solutions, of which approximately 10 items would be data diodes, and the rest are divided between two other sub-areas. Part of the subject matter of the procurement consisted of data diode solutions with services (e.g., expert work, installation, technical support).; Part of the subject matter of the procurement consisted of integrated exchange gateway (IEG) solutions with services (e.g., expert work, installation, technical support).; Part of the subject matter of the procurement consisted of NATO CDS gateways with services (e.g., expert work, installation, technical support).
sig_0339b1bcbb995a1a1447.title: Rajavartiolaitos - Telecommunications equipment 2025 (00758) - Procurement of gateway solutions

sig_033d0f601fbcd60cea0c.description: The subject of the public contract is the selection of a contractor for specialised support and maintenance of core modules of the established "e-University" software platform at MU-Varna, in accordance with the attached Technical Specification (Appendix No 1), hereinafter referred to as the "system". In accordance with its specific needs and financial provision, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to commission the development of additional functionalities for the system or changes to existing ones, hereinafter referred to as "additional modifications". Each tenderer must submit a tender for support and maintenance for the full scope of modules included in the Technical Specification (Appendix No 1). The support and maintenance of the system must be carried out with a view to anticipating and preventing incidents before they occur at the Contracting Authority and building high reliability for the operational capability of the system, and must include a minimum of weekly reviews of system error logs, checks for potential problems related to the hardware and software infrastructure, and their remediation. The operational regime of the system must be uninterrupted, year-round. When the need arises according to the Contracting Authority's brief, the Contractor shall carry out corrections and additional modifications tailored to the current architecture and performance requirements of the system. The Contracting Authority shall commission any development of additional functionalities or modification of existing ones in the system via a written request containing a description of the objective prerequisites giving rise to the need for the additional modification, a specified reasonable time limit for the Contractor to submit information regarding the solution, date, and the name and position of the contact person on behalf of the Contracting Authority. For its part, the Contractor shall provide, within the specified time limit, the information regarding the specific execution of the brief and the hours required for the specific solutions.

sig_035001209bca881b8b6d.description: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is commencing pre‐market engagement to inform a forthcoming procurement for a replacement Clinical Document Repository, enhanced digital e‐Forms capability, and associated scanning provision. This engagement also supports advance planning as the current contract reaches expiry in December 2027, enabling a smooth transition, safe parallel‐running and a controlled implementation phase. There is no commitment from the Health Board at this stage to progress any further with this Procurement. This is a PME exercise to establish the scope of the market. This is an information gathering exercise which will help inform a future procurement procedure. However, dependent upon the responses the Health Board reserves the right not to progress the procurement. It is possible that further expressions of interest are issued after the initial responses have been considered. If you are interested in this procurement BCUHB have a number of documents that require completion. Please contact Emma Burns - emma.burns@wales.nhs.uk for access to these documents. sig_036f4eac3fd5c15f630b.description: NatureScot has a requirement to place a contract with an external service provider for the provision of Deer Vehicle Collision Data Collation and Analysis Project, 2025 – 2028. NatureScot, in conjunction with Transport Scotland (Scotland’s national transport agency) requires the collation, analysis and reporting of data relating to deer vehicle collisions (DVCs) in Scotland to help improve our knowledge of DVCs across the Scottish road network and to inform decision making regarding the implementation of DVC mitigation measures. Lot 1: . NatureScot, in partnership with Transport Scotland, has been running the Deer Vehicle Collision (DVC) Project since 2008. The previous phase incorporated data to the end of 2024. The purpose of the project is to collect and collate data, analyse that data and then provide information to NatureScot, Transport Scotland, Road Operating Companies, local authorities and local deer managers to assist them with decision-making around the allocation of resources and delivery of actions to reduce the number of DVCs and thereby reduce risks to public safety and safeguard deer welfare.. Link below to access the PIN questions https://www.cognitoforms.com/ScotlandExcel1/OnBehalfOfNatureScotDeerVehicleCollisionDataCollationAndAnalysisProject Scotland Excel is acting on behalf of NatureScot in the execution of this PIN Notice. Please respond to this PIN Notice by Friday 28th of November at 12pm noon.

sig_037f795dc96a1e7ddcea.description: ADVANCED RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT (ARA) FA9451-21-S-0001 Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research (DETER) Air Force Research Laboratory/Directed Energy Directorate NAICS Code: The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715 for Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees Federal Agency Name: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy, Phillips Research Site, Kirtland AFB NM (AFRL/RD) ARA Title: Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research Announcement (DETER) ARA Type: This is an Open ARA with Calls; initial announcement ARA Number: FA9451-21-S-0001 Program Summary: This is an Open ARA announcement pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). AFRL/RD is interested in receiving white papers and proposals through a Two-Step Process to perform research and development (R&D), modeling and simulation (M&S), design, component/subsystem, prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of directed energy source components (to include spares and alternate component technologies), and/or systems and any required accessories, materials, and supplies for laboratory research and experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged. *Note: AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. *Please see the attached DETER Industry User Guide for guidance on definitions, processes, submission requirements and evaluation criteria.* Background: AFRL/RD equips the joint warfighter with next-generation technologies, advanced concepts, and weapon system options across all operational domains to become more agile and increase the commercialization potential of directed energy investments to ensure the National defense. This solicitation intends to use acquisition authorities provided by 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). This authority applies to acquisition of items related to “...ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that are necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense.” Consequently, white papers and proposals should address how the proposed effort provides benefits to the national defense and a strategy for verifying those intended benefits. The proposed solutions should be innovative and substantially improve national defense capabilities across the domains of directed energy. While the Government describes discrete topic areas below, it also anticipates that certain comprehensive technology solutions and prototypes may require multidiscipline approaches that address two or more topic areas. The topic areas are covered under this announcement, which may be used in any combination. The Government reserves the right to add, delete or modify the topic areas as necessary. Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged throughout the life of this ARA. However, communication will be limited once full-proposals are submitted for evaluation/review. Prospective Offerors are welcome to request sit-downs and provide demonstrations of their capabilities. Discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. No guidance related to technical approach will be given. However, questions related to the objectives of the effort or prior similar efforts may be answered. Offerors are advised that only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to contractually bind or otherwise commit the Government. THIS WILL BE A HYBRID ANNOUNCEMENT: This announcement has an open request for white papers as described below. Calls may be issued under this announcement for discrete requirements. Call types can vary and may include, but are not limited to, One-Step, Two-Step, Open, Closed, Staggered, Limited Calls or any combination therein. AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. Open Announcement Request: AFRL/RD Kirtland Air Force Base is soliciting white papers on the research effort described in the below topic areas pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373), Procurement for Experimental Purposes. Open Announcement Submission: White papers must be submitted to https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signup. If it is determined that a classified white paper is required, please DO NOT DELIVER any classified portion of the white paper, but rather contact the DETER Org Mailbox for specific delivery instructions. Further instructions for white paper submission can be found in the DETER Industry User Guide attached to this announcement. Call Request: Calls, other than Limited Calls, will be issued under this announcement via the Government Point of Entry (GPE) at https://beta.sam.gov. Notification of Calls may be announced on other platforms (i.e. www.grants.gov) and will direct Offerors to the GPE for full solicitation details. Call Submission: Submission requirements for Calls will be specified in the solicitation documentation of each Call. Call Variations: Variations of the ARA Call process are available for use. The following types are commonly used, but are not considered all inclusive. One-Step: The one-step process is used to request full technical and cost proposals from each Offeror. The proposals are reviewed in accordance with the solicitation criteria and typically all of a selected proposal, part of a selected proposal, or none of the proposals may be selected for award. Two-Step: The two-step process is sometimes used when a large number of proposals are anticipated. Potential Offerors are invited to submit brief descriptive white papers in lieu of full proposals. The Call must state whether an unfavorable white paper review will bar the Offeror from further consideration. The Government may retain unselected white papers for a specific period of time, which will be identified in the solicitation. Full proposals are requested from those Offerors selected in the white paper review process. After proposals are received, they are reviewed consistent with the process for one-step ARAs. Open Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at any time within a specified period. Open calls will be updated no less frequently than annually. White papers/proposals are reviewed when received during the period that the ARA is open. Closed Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at a specified date and time as set forth in the ARA. Staggered-Closed Call: The staggered-closed Call states a specified date and time for receipt of proposals or white papers, but also allows for proposals/white papers after the date and time set for proposal receipt. All Offerors should be cautioned, however, that the likelihood of funding proposals received after the specified date and time is substantially reduced. Limited Call: This approach allows for solicitation to a limited group of potential offerors. Request for Proposals (RFP) or Requests for white papers will be issued directly to potential offerors without a requirement to publish to the GPE. The Government may issue solicitations that combine one or more of the above approaches. Open Announcement Modifications: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is subject to updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor https://beta.sam.gov to ensure they receive the latest guidance for this announcement. The Government shall provide updates to this announcement no less than annually. Updates may include changes to: topic areas, submission requirements, administrative changes, evaluation criteria, solicitation methods, etc. (not an inclusive list). Type of Contract/Instrument: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract/instrument type under the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10 U.S.C. §4021 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371) "Other Transaction for Research 10 U.S.C. §4022 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371b) "Other Transaction for Prototype" 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373) "Procurement for Experimental Purposes" 10 U.S.C. §4025 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2374) "Prize Competitions" DoD Grant and Agreement Regulation (DoDGARS) The Government anticipates that a mix of contract/instrument types will be used throughout the life of this ARA. Generally, awards under this announcement or any Calls may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, Firm Fixed Price, Other Transaction Authority, etc. NOTE: If proposing a Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) type contract, the FAR clauses will be referenced at the Call level or within the Request for Proposal. The FAR and supplement provisions and clauses are incorporated by reference. The full text of these provisions and clauses can be found at https://www.acquisition.gov. If proposing an assistance instrument (grants or cooperative agreements) then articles and guidance found under DoDGARS, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) and OMB/DoD Policy shall be used and followed as appropriate. If proposing an Other Transaction (OT) these FAR references and clauses would not apply. The terms and conditions of an OT agreement should be developed and negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Estimated Program Cost: The overarching announcement has an unrestricted ceiling. However, individual Calls may elect to provide an estimated program value or funding profile for planning purposes. Anticipated Number of Awards: The Air Force anticipates awarding multiple awards for this announcement. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more agreements, other transactions, or contracts for all, some or none of the solicited effort based on the Offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding availability. There is no limit on the number of awards that may be made to an individual Offeror. Schedule: The anticipated period of performance will be determined through dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives for each topic area and specified in each individual award. Deliverables: Hardware and software deliverables will be specified within a separately priced line items and data deliverables will be specified on individual CDRL(s) in any resultant contract or an OT article. Within Scope Award Modifications: Offerors are advised that due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to make within scope changes, to include but not limited to, modifications which increase overall contract/award ceiling amount. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Before the Government can issue an award, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). If an Offeror was previously registered in Central Contractor Registration (CCR), the information has been transferred to SAM. However, it is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all of their data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM replaced CCR, Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors that are submitting PROPOSAL RESPONSES ONLY (Not required for submission of white papers) shall submit as a part of the proposal submission 1.) a completed Standard Form (SF 424), Research and Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form (See Attachments) for all Senior/Key Personnel proposed; and, 2.) A Completed Security Program Questionnaire (See Attachments). Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. By submitting a proposal, the offeror certifies that it is in compliance with Section 223(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 which requires that: (a) the Principal Investigator (PI) and other key personnel certify that the current and pending support provided on the proposal is current, accurate and complete; (B) agree to update such disclosure at the request of the agency prior to the award of support and at any subsequent time the agency determines appropriate during the term of the award; and (c) the PI and other key personnel have been made aware of the requirements under Section 223(a)(1) of this Act.
