sig_050d9c89badfb1df000c.description: The contract relates to the execution of fixed maintenance on the movable objects in the West Netherlands South area by means of tasks and services and activities. To ensure that the objects maintain an acceptable level of maintenance, a maintenance regime is prescribed in the contract. The contractor has the opportunity to submit improvement proposals to the maintenance regime during the contract period, in order to optimise the fixed maintenance. The Agreement relates to the multi-year upkeep, monitoring and provision of information on (the condition of) the Functioning and Performance of the Area. The Contractor is expected to maintain the functionality and performance of the Area by executing the maintenance regime made available by the Client and rectifying faults, defects and deployment in the event of emergencies and, if agreed, to be improved. The Contractor is also expected to identify, optimise and execute the Work required for this purpose and to verify, analyse and improve the results thereof. sig_059a20d80c543fae06ab.description: As a result of the subject public procurement procedure, the Contracting Authority wishes to use an administrative and action-supporting IT specialist system within the framework of a contractor's agreement, which on the part of the contractor also extends to the performance of operation and maintenance tasks. The Contracting Authority would like, during the implementation of its tasks specified in legislation, for public space inspectors and parking inspectors to carry out their activity using mobile devices (PDA, mobile printer). The Contracting Authority would like the issuance and management of entry permits and the management of entry fines to take place in a unified system. The general aim and task of the Contracting Authority is to operate the Szentendre public space parking system, the established chargeable road parking spaces in the long term, in a user-friendly manner, securely and with a high degree of operational reliability, efficiently. The main technical and functional requirements set against the specialist system are 1. Devices and operational environment provided by the Contracting Authority:  The Contracting Authority provides the workstations (computers) connected to the IT system with additional peripherals.  The Contracting Authority currently uses the following additional devices, with which the offered program system must be compatible, or if not, it must also propose a device that is functionally equivalent to the following devices, compatible with the offered program system, available as new in normal commercial circulation, indicating at least the make and type number of the device 8 pcs Samsung Galaxy 8 phone 8 pcs Zebra ZQ520 printer  The Contracting Authority ensures the lawfulness of the use of the BM authentic registries.  The Contracting Authority provides the text of all those forms that it uses during street actions (information sheets, reports, fine sheets, payment notices), as well as the documents applied during the use of the administrative system (reminder letters, reports, warnings, order for payment, documents related to the initiation of enforcement).  The Contracting Authority provides the public space address directory of its area of operation, as well as the address directory of the acting authorities.  The Contracting Authority determines the access rights and levels to the mobile and central administrative systems of the specialist system. The specialist system offered by the winning Tenderer under this contract must be suitable for setting different permission levels, thus it must be possible to form permission types/groups in the system. It must be possible to assign users to the types/groups thus defined, who receive the permissions of the given group. 2. Functional requirements related to the applications running on mobile devices, provided by the winning Tenderer under this contract:  The expectation towards the specialist system is that it fully supports the work carried out by the Contracting Authority's staff in public spaces, on site.  The application running on the PDA devices must contain the designation of all offences related to the tasks defined in Act 1999 of LXIII on public space supervision and the relevant legislation, and infringements sanctionable by the imposition of an administrative fine, or by report, together with the exact amount of fines that can be imposed in the case of individual infringements, and in the case of road traffic offences, together with the number of penalty points assigned to them. The specialist system must contain the designation of rule violations defined in the local government decree, together with the amount limits of the administrative fine that can be imposed. Based on all these, the specialist system automatically prevents the recording of erroneous or unlawful actions contrary to the integrated data, the exchanging of the amount of the fine assigned to the offence or rule violation (offence, administrative, and administrative fine), and the number of points belonging to the penalty point system. The expectation towards the specialist system is that it assigns to the case type selected by the acting inspector the relevant, associated form designed on the basis of the Contracting Authority data provision and expectations. A further expectation is that from a given action, in accordance with the development of circumstances, it should be possible to switch to the execution and recording of another action type without interrupting the ongoing case management (conversion of absentee on-the-spot fine into on-the-spot fine, and then in case of non-recognition thereof into report). The information form must comply with 22/2012. (IV.13) BM decree and the relevant legislation.  The application running on the PDA devices must support parking surcharge imposition, using drop-down menus. With automatic checking of mobile parking ticket purchase and parking permit data on the basis of licence plate data.  The specialist system must possess a permission/access function that ensures that only authorised persons can log in to the specialist system. The specialist system must log data suitable for identifying users, the location of entry, its GPS coordinates, time, all data relating to the use of the specialist system, data entry, data query, data transmission, modification (what, when, who modified what to), and deletion (what/what was modified, what was deleted). The system is capable of querying vehicle data on the basis of licence plate and time and querying personal data and address registry, through the connection implemented by the ministry operating the registry and an application supporting on-site wheel clamping also operates there, furthermore it is capable of serving at least 12 simultaneous users active on the provider side. Due to character limits, further details are in the procurement documents.

sig_05c082b3f09addce3ffe.description: IT services are being awarded successively in six lots. The present case concerns solely the services for Lot 1 - Infrastructure and application operation for the Hessian agricultural subsidy scheme. Essential components are application operation and infrastructure operation. Application operation includes, among other things, land information services such as FIG and WMS services, frontend components (LaWi portal as an online application platform and the IP-Web modules as container-based subsidy routes) as well as backend functionalities with SAP - process processing (WERKBank, mbWERK) and the berichtsWERK as reporting and data warehouse. Infrastructure operation includes, among other things, the provision and operation of the complete IT infrastructure, environment provision, backup infrastructure as well as security and authorisation management. Furthermore, the provision of the LAN/WAN infrastructure and its network operation are the subject of this service. The Wirtschafts- und Infrastrukturbank Hessen (WIBank) acts as the EU-accredited paying agency for agricultural subsidies in Hessen. The WIBank is part of the Landesbank Hessen – Thüringen (Helaba). The provision and operation of the specialised IT systems necessary for agricultural subsidies is the responsibility of Helaba. Helaba has currently awarded the IT services for agricultural subsidies to a general contractor. The contract with this general contractor ends on 31.12.2026. Therefore, the IT services are being re-tendered. As part of these tenders, a change from the current general contractor model to a multi-provider model is taking place. The services previously provided centrally by the general contractor are being divided and successively tendered in competition via six technically defined lots. The IT systems for agricultural subsidies are based on a highly integrated architecture, which necessitates technical and functional dependencies between the six lots. As part of the transition from a general contractor to a multi-provider model, it is therefore mandatory that the service providers for each lot do not act in isolation, but become part of an integrated IT ecosystem. The present case concerns solely the services for Lot 1 - Infrastructure and application operation for the Hessian agricultural subsidy scheme. Essential components are application operation and infrastructure operation. Application operation includes, among other things, land information services such as FIG (Land Information System Geodata) and WMS services (Web Map Services), frontend components (LaWi portal as an online application platform and the IP-Web modules as container-based subsidy routes) as well as backend functionalities with SAP - process processing (WERKBank, mbWERK) and the berichtsWERK as reporting and data warehouse. Infrastructure operation includes, among other things, the provision and operation of the complete IT infrastructure, environment provision, backup infrastructure as well as security and authorisation management. Furthermore, the provision of the LAN/WAN infrastructure and its network operation are the subject of this service. For further details, reference is made to Annex I 02 - Annex 0_Service Description. Optional services (infrastructure): Storage expansion additional 1 TB; RAM expansion additional 8 / 16 / 32 GB (physical); processor upgrade additional 1 CPU.

sig_05d3584685e1404a4362.description: The subject of procurement is the Security Operation Center (SOC) service, responsible for monitoring, detection, and response to security incidents in real time as well as the mitigation of harmful consequences of an incident in the shortest possible time. The Security Operation Center (SOC), operating in a 24x7x365 regime, continuously monitors the security of the entire information system of Pula General Hospital in order to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive patient data, as well as the availability, authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality of the hospital's key services. The most important goal of the SOC is a fast, efficient, and reliable reaction in the event of a security incident, and it is crucial, due to the outsourcing of this function, to ensure the timeliness of activities and mutual coordination of the activities of the SOC and Pula General Hospital so that any individual incident is resolved in the shortest possible time. Additionally, following the Cybersecurity Regulation for operators of essential services and digital service providers, Pula General Hospital, as an operator of essential services, has the obligation to reduce all those risks that may arise within the framework of the outsourcing of the service to an acceptable level. The Contracting Authority has implemented an IBM QRadar SIEM system for collecting and processing data from the following sources: Aruba ClearPass Policy Manager Fortinet FortiGate Security Gateway Microsoft DHCP Server Microsoft DNS Debug Microsoft Exchange Server Microsoft IIS Microsoft Windows Security Event Log Symantec Email ATP Symantec Email Cloud Queue Symantec Email Core Symantec Endpoint Protection Servers (approx. 70 units) The Security Operation Center service must meet all technical conditions stated in the technical specification. As part of the bid, it is also necessary to offer the renewal of the manufacturer's warranty on the Contracting Authority's existing SIEM system, and the requested services in accordance with the Contracting Authority's technical specification. sig_05d79cecffd9e0fdfaee.description: Thames Valley Fire Control Service (TVFCS) is initiating a Competitive Flexible Procedure procurement for the replacement of its Command & Control (C&C) system. TVFCS is a tri-service collaboration between Oxfordshire Fire & Rescue Service, Buckinghamshire Fire & Rescue Service, and Royal Berkshire Fire & Rescue Service. Oxfordshire County Council are undertaking this procurement on behalf of the other Fires Services. Since becoming operational in 2015, TVFCS has provided a critical shared emergency control room service, handling 999 calls and mobilising resources across the Thames Valley region, serving a population of approximately 2.5 million residents. The current C&C system (NEC Vision Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) and DS3000 Integrated Communication Control System (ICCS)) is approaching end-of-life, with key infrastructure components due to become unsupported by 2029. The replacement project seeks to ensure continuity of statutory emergency response services, enhance operational resilience, and support future innovation through a modern, modular solution. The tools shall be used in mapping, reviewing, diagnosing patients in all age groups. They shall be based on recognised, standardised and normed methods. For example, cognitive ability tests, mapping executive functions, symptom mapping, function mapping, mapping of quality of life and mapping of patient satisfaction. We would like the different tools to be included in a digital platform where we as a customer can choose between different tools. As a minimum the delivery must include cognitive ability tests. The ability tests ought to include an option to also map verbal and non-verbal abilities. We are also interested in deliveries that cover parts of the needs, if one delivery does not cover all of the needs described here. Requirements for a digital system. We need a digital system that covers the needs outlined above, which ensure uniform administration, automatic scoring and reporting, which provides safe processing of sensitive data. The solution must also provide an option to use the existing paper based test set where the scoring still occurs digitally.

sig_0611fab13b4f11434e43.description: Performance recording software for Technical Operations (municipal works yard) as Software as a Service (SaaS) The Technical Operations department of the City of Bochum (4, 44793 Bochum) currently maintains and services municipal infrastructure in the areas of urban greenery, road and drainage facilities, and municipal cemeteries with approx. 600 employees. It also operates a crematorium. The department has four divisions: Central Tasks, Greenery Division, Roads and Drainage Division, and Cemeteries and Crematorium Division. Within the divisions, a total of 27 operational units are active in providing these services. In addition, there is the technical administrative department, which awards services externally to third parties. Technical Operations is subject to continuous task review and optimisation, meaning that the organisational structure and workflows must be adapted regularly. New tasks and business processes may be added. This therefore also applies to the regularly required reports and evaluations. The employees work within the scope of the collective agreement for the public service (TVöD-VKA and TVöD-NRW) and provide numerous services. Management and administrative roles are partly filled by civil servants who are subject to the regulations of the North Rhine-Westphalia State Civil Service Act (Landesbeamtenrecht NRW). In order to record the services provided and the associated costs efficiently and purposefully, Technical Operations is looking for recording software for municipal works yards / depots. All services provided ("products") must be recorded, evaluated, and analysed. These services arise from the budget structure of Technical Operations. The services are provided in the area of predefined facilities or georeferenced points. In addition, services provided in connection with vehicles are to be evaluated. In particular, the software solution must be used not only to record performance but also to record hardship allowances in accordance with TVöD. For this purpose, the current regulations from the relevant collective agreements must be observed (in particular TVöD in the area of the Association of Municipal Employers' Associations (TVöD-VKA) and the regional collective agreement for the TVöD in the area of KAV NW (TVöD-NRW)). In this context, Technical Operations is planning the introduction of a cloud solution in which the bidder provides and maintains a software solution and the associated cloud (Software as a Service (SaaS)). The bidder provides a Software as a Service (SaaS), supports the setup, provides the IT infrastructure required for this, and carries out maintenance. The provider takes care of maintenance, upgrades, support, security, and all other aspects of software administration, including the cloud required for operation. A Software as a Service (SaaS) provider undertakes several important tasks to enable customers to use the software smoothly and efficiently: - Provision and maintenance of the infrastructure: The provider provides the necessary hardware and network infrastructure and ensures its maintenance and updating. - Software updates and maintenance: Regular updates and maintenance work are carried out to keep the software up to date and close security gaps. - Security and data protection: The provider implements security measures to protect users' data and ensures that data protection regulations are complied with. - Customer support: Effective customer support is provided to help with technical problems or questions regarding the use of the software. - Scalability: The provider ensures that the software is scalable and meets the growing demands of users. - Accessibility and availability: The software is made available around the clock so that users can access it at any time. This list is not exhaustive. Rather, it is intended to ensure a common understanding of what is generally meant by SaaS. In particular, the client's requirements are specified by this specification of services, the bill of quantities, and the EVB-IT cloud contract. However, the provision of the software solution must imperatively take place as a SaaS / cloud solution. The SaaS or cloud solution must be entirely browser-based and must not require any additional local components on the part of the client for its operation. The software already exists in its basic functions and does not first need to be developed. It must be adapted to the client's requirements (customisation). A service contract will be concluded with a base term of 24 months from the award of contract. Thereafter, the contract is automatically extended by a further 12 months each time, unless the contract is terminated by either party. The offer price is to be calculated for a term of 48 months.

sig_06124ef180c6e335d1c2.description: Description of the assignment The consultants shall perform management of the region's care systems. The work involves implementing decided changes to the existing configuration and preparing and configuring new modules and functions. The work is carried out in a team together with the region's employees and includes: Ongoing case management and troubleshooting Planned changes implemented in a sprint-based manner Practical configuration tasks such as setting up new units, configuring processes, connecting integrations and setting up templates, and performing tests during system upgrades Development of processes and technical frameworks for automation, including configuration scripts, deploy pipelines and automated documentation of system configuration. Expectations The region does not require consultants to have prior knowledge of the region's care systems at the start of the contract — training is provided by the region. The region is looking for consultants who are driven, committed and take responsibility for their work. Great emphasis is placed on collaboration skills and communication, as the work takes place in close dialogue with the region's employees. Consultants are expected to work in a structured and efficient manner within the team. Purpose and description of the assignment The assignment includes work within both ongoing system management and further development of working methods, processes and technical frameworks linked to the region's care systems. The purpose is to ensure stable and quality-assured management while the degree of automation and efficiency is progressively increased. Over time, the region wishes to establish a consultant pool of up to eight to ten consultants who together form a foundation that can staff and reinforce when peaks occur. Staffing and allocation Total volume refers to 4 full-time equivalents Total volume outside the holiday period must correspond to four (4) full-time equivalents/FTE Holiday periods, mid-June to mid-August, one (1) full-time equivalent/FTE No resource below 50% in the assignment during an ongoing assignment. The assignment is initially staffed with four (4) consultants, where three (3) resources consist of junior consultants and one (1) senior consultant acts as a mentor and team leader for the team.

sig_0624bfeaf7dea114c107.description: The subject of the project is the design, supply, installation and support of a "Wireless Communication System for the Fire Service and the National Crisis Management and Risk Response Mechanism (SAEPSEMDAK)" for the more effective coverage of its operational needs throughout the territory. The system will offer combined voice and data services in network operation. The fundamental characteristics of the system will be availability, reliability, security, quality and scalability. The system consists of telecommunication equipment, hardware and software, which will provide the capability for priority voice transmission and basic data. It ensures group or individual calls in the field of operations, as well as two-way communication of users with the competent services of the Fire Service at Central (ESKSEDIK), Regional (13 Regional Centres - PEKE), and Local level (Fire Services / Stations - P.Y., P.S., P.K.). The trunked radio system will be based on a trunk network, via microwave links, the "SYZEFXIS" and "SYZEFXIS II" network or other means. It will be used to support the operations of the Fire Service and aims at seamless communications for collaborative crisis management, common situational awareness, information exchange and cooperation with all services of the Fire Service and Civil Protection and immediate decision-making. (Paragraph 1.3 and Annex I of the Tender Notice)

sig_06b3a3335a34b3149477.description: A service provider is sought who provides CMS-neutral advice, supports UMMD in the selection of a suitable CMS and is responsible for the technical implementation of the web platform – including information architecture, data/content model, templates/components, integration and migration. Lot LOT-0001: Digitalisation programme: Relaunch of www.med.ovgu.de website & intranet. The subject of the tender is the conceptual design, layout, technical implementation and introduction of a future-proof content management system (CMS) for the external web presence and the intranet of Universitätsmedizin Magdeburg, including the project, consulting, implementation, training and migration services required for this. The contract comprises in particular the functional, technical and design conception, the development and implementation of a suitable CMS-based solution approach, the creation and implementation of templates and modules, the mapping of defined content, editorial and release processes, the migration of selected content, quality assurance, training of the participating user groups, and support for commissioning and rollout. The aim is a high-performance, user-oriented, low-barrier, scalable and future-proof solution that meets both the requirements for the public internet presence and an internal intranet for information, communication and editorial processes. The contracting authority reserves the right to commission the operation and further development of the platform after go-live and the hypercare phase in a second stage (option). Furthermore, the contracting authority reserves the right to extend the service to additional interfaces beyond the interfaces already defined, in particular for person search and DWH/structural data (option). The contracting authority also reserves the right to commission change requests and workshops beyond the defined scope (option). Further information on the options will be made available by the contracting authority in the final specification of services and in the course of the negotiations. For reasons of confidentiality, the complete tender documents with the detailed specification of services will only be made available after the return of a signed confidentiality agreement.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. ANNUAL REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS: Potential offerors are notified that effective 01 Jan 2005 to be eligible for an award and in compliance with FAR 52.204-7 and DFARS 252.204-7007 Alternate A, they must submit Annual Representations and Certifications, via SAM.gov. Before submitting the electronic Annual Representations and Certifications, Contractors must be registered in the SAM Database. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). (End of Amendment) Amendment 06 – Revision to TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language and GFP Clause List (21 November 2024) The purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language included in Section I paragraph 9 (formerly included in Section I paragraph 8) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. The revised paragraph is as follows: 9) Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors are notified that subsequent Call Announcements shall include a requirement for submission of the documents identified below. Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. sig_070576f1552b42207971.description: Groupe E currently uses the ServiceNow platform as a central tool for several internal and customer-oriented processes. The instance, named "Nestor", has been progressively configured to meet the operational and organisational needs of the Group. ServiceNow is used in particular for business request management, offering a centralised portal and automated workflows to facilitate the processing and tracking of internal requests. The platform also constitutes an essential pillar of ITSM, covering incident, change, task and problem management. Beyond internal processes, ServiceNow is used for customer request management, allowing for better traceability, improved service quality and optimal management of commitments (SLAs). The solution also integrates a module dedicated to vehicle fleet management, ensuring the operational and administrative monitoring of the Group's mobility resources. The ServiceNow instance is currently maintained and evolved by an external partner, who provides application support, specific developments and technical integration, in collaboration with internal governance teams. As the ServiceNow licence contract and service contract with the integrator are expiring, Groupe E is launching this call for tenders to ensure the continuity of these services, optimise costs and guarantee consistent development of the platform for the coming years. This lot concerns the acquisition of licences necessary for the use of the ServiceNow solution; The purpose of this lot is the provision of support services related to our ServiceNow instances

sig_07c2a31972111c0e382b.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system regarding the procurement of IT consultancy services within 14 service areas with associated sub-areas, sub-categories and services. Below are the 14 service areas with associated sub-areas indicated. The actual services that can be procured in the 14 service areas are described in detail in Appendix C. Subject of the system: Service area 1: IT-related strategies Sub-area: Preparation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Implementation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Evaluation and updating as well as impact assessment of strategies Service area 2: Business needs, business case and benefit realisation Sub-area: Identification of business needs and preparation of business cases Sub-area: Realisation of business cases Sub-area: Follow-up on business cases Service area 3: IT tendering Sub-area: Preparation of tenders Sub-area: Execution of tenders Service area 4: IT security, business continuity and IT compliance Sub-area: Establishment of IT security Sub-area: Crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery Sub-area: IT compliance Service area 5: IT architecture Sub-area: Establishment of an IT architecture Sub-area: Review and adjustment of existing IT architecture Service area 6: IT governance Sub-area: Establishment of IT governance Sub-area: Organisation of system management Sub-area: Establishment of IT supplier management Service area 7: Project and programme management Sub-area: Project management – the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Management of agile projects Sub-area: Programme management Service area 8: Data processing Sub-area: Data analysis and reporting Sub-area: Use of external data Sub-area: Conversion, cleaning and archiving of data Service area 9: Advice on software licences Sub-area: Open source software vs. closed source software Sub-area: Determination of the size of specific licences, as well as the conditions associated with the use Service area 10: Infrastructure and hardware Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of networks Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of servers Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of clients Service area 11: Test Sub-area: IT testing of development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT testing Service area 12: Development of new functionality Sub-area: IT development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT development Service area 13: Adaptation of existing IT systems Sub-area: IT development with a view to adapting existing IT systems Service area 14: IT system operation Sub-area: Operation of IT systems The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase The same services can be procured in both categories, but the categories differ in that the customer in category 1 must procure one or more specific competence(s), while the customer in category 2 must have a specific task solved. The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. It is voluntary for all SKI's customers, as stated in Appendix B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure IT consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase In category 1 customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in 2 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate).; Procurement of IT consultancy services for task solution In category 2 the customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in 3 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of IT consultancy services for the solution of the described task (number x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate). 3. Remuneration form 3: Purchase of task solution at a fixed price.

sig_07c3218a70b76bdfbfb0.description: The subject of this contract is the provision of specialised advisory and technical support services to the Contracting Authority for the effective implementation, management and monitoring of the sub-projects 'Supply of materials and services for the equipment of the GRNET hub network as well as for protection equipment against cyberattacks' and 'Supply of materials and services of network, computing and storage equipment for the data centres of GRNET' of the project 'Replacement and expansion of the equipment of the data centres of GRNET S.A.' (OPS TA Code 5225560). The Technical Support Consultant (TSC) will act as the strategic and operational supporter of the Contracting Authority throughout the duration of the project's implementation, assuming the role of liaison between the involved parties, the technical and quality monitoring of the project Contractor's deliverables and ensuring compliance with schedules, requirements and quality specifications. The subject of this contract is the provision of technical assistance and support to the Contracting Authority for the correct and timely execution of the sub-projects mentioned above. Due to the complexity and size of the sub-projects, external technical assistance is required for their implementation and monitoring until their completion and final acceptance. Therefore, the subject of the technical assistance sub-project is the provision of specialised technical support consultant services, so as to ensure the effective implementation of the sub-projects in terms of timeliness, quality and results in general. The timely and correct implementation of the sub-projects requires a series of coordinated management and monitoring actions. The TSC is called upon to support these actions, providing support to the Contracting Authority on technical/financial, organisational, managerial and expertise-related matters whenever required. Specifically, the TSC will undertake the provision of Technical Support Services, under the supervision of the Contracting Authority, in the following categories: - Organisation of the Management / Quality System of the Overall Project - Monitoring – Support of the progress of the sub-projects' implementation - Support of the sub-projects' acceptance procedures. The TSC will support the management and monitoring tasks of the sub-projects' implementation by providing appropriate human resources and the necessary infrastructure and tools. The purpose of the technical assistance sub-project is broken down into the following: - Monitoring the implementation of the sub-projects, with an emphasis on adhering to time and cost constraints. - Ensuring the quality of the operation of the sub-projects' management system, while simultaneously upgrading its implementation means and communication between all involved parties. - Ensuring the quality of the deliverables and products of the sub-projects. - Ensuring the interconnection and operational and technical interoperability of the sub-projects. - Systematic utilisation of human resources during the implementation of the sub-projects. - Successful completion and securing of the results of the sub-projects and the action in general. The TSC will assist the Contracting Authority with the aim of fully and continuously informing it regarding the progress of the implementation of the main sub-project and in particular: - In adhering to the established schedule of administrative actions and tasks. - In accelerating the implementation of tasks that are experiencing time delays. - In coordinating the bodies involved in the project with the aim of maximising benefits and accelerating actions for effective implementation. - In the timely identification of prerequisites required for the smooth progress of the main sub-project. - In the timely identification of problems that may jeopardise the implementation of the main sub-project and in the timely submission of proposals for addressing them. - In the timely identification of impacts from non-adherence to pre-planned actions or implementation schedules and in the submission of proposals for managing them. - In ensuring the technical soundness of the main sub-project which will allow for the effective and efficient commissioning of the systems and infrastructure that will be developed. - In potential improvements and revisions to the implementation design of the main sub-project, with the aim of their successful completion and the maximisation of the benefit that may arise from their productive operation. The objectives of the TSC's services are: - Contributing to the preparation and ensuring the correct implementation of the sub-projects, in terms of time, financial and technical planning. - Ensuring the quality and technical soundness of the deliverables of each distinct work package of the sub-projects, and ensuring the interconnection, coordination and interoperability of the individual elements of the Overall Project/Action. - Successful implementation and ensuring the functionality of the Overall Project, as well as the effective commissioning of the software and equipment, within the pre-defined time and cost limits. - Ensuring (forecasting, formulating, shaping) the prerequisites for smooth operation after the installation and acceptance of the sub-projects, successful integration into its operational environment and the maximisation of their utilisation by the Project Owner, for the benefit of the citizen and society as a whole. - Systematic upgrading and effective utilisation of human resources, throughout the duration of the sub-projects' implementation, so as to ensure the smooth introduction and longevity of their results.

sig_07d781a90ddb7303fa04.description: This is a request for information on a system for project and portfolio management in a university context. With this RFI Aalto University is seeking information on suppliers interested in delivering the services described. Aalto University is a foundation university as provided in the Universities Act (558/2009) and started operations at the beginning of 2010. Aalto has six schools and approximately 20 000 students, 4800 staff of which over 400 are professors. Development projects support the implementation of Aalto University’s strategy. They are based on the university’s annually updated strategic plans and executed by Aalto Gate Model principles. Development projects include, for example, process development, service development and information systems development projects. Research projects are out-of-scope of the current system and managed with separate processes and tools. Aalto University carries out on average 100 development projects per year. The process involves project managers, steering group members, project group members, and management and service personnel. With the forthcoming procurement and contract our goal is to establish a long-term partnership with a supplier who can cater to our evolving project and portfolio management needs in alignment with our strategy in an agile manner. REQUIREMENT FOR THE PROJECT AND PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT SYSTEM Aalto University currently has an information system for project and portfolio management. System is used on a Software as a Service basis and maintained by a partner. Aalto University’s development projects are recorded in the system. For each project, the basic information, project lifecycle, selected internal compliance evaluations, schedule, gate approvals and status are documented in the system. The system’s reporting and analysis functions are in limited use. The main user group at the current state are project managers who update the status of their projects. Aalto University has renewed its project and portfolio management processes in recent years. Changes have been made to the project funding and prioritization model, project management guidelines and project steering processes. A project management office (PMO) will be established. More formal project resource management process is desired to be implemented. The current implementation of the system does not support the renewed processes. sig_07fe1ebe5551b495d769.description: Lincolnshire Housing Partnership (LHP) is a greater Lincolnshire based housing association created in April 2018. LHP is a charity regulated as a Community Benefit Society and a not for profit housing provider regulated by the Regulator for Social Housing. LHP’s Data and Technology Strategy 2026–2029 sets out LHP’s vision to become a digitally confident, data-driven housing association by March 2029, supported by a sequenced three-year roadmap structured around three phases: Foundations (Year 1, 2026/27), Transformation (Year 2, 2027/28), and Innovation (Year 3, 2028/29). The strategy has one overriding objective: to give LHP the technology and data foundations it needs to achieve and sustain a C1 Consumer Standard grading, with a target of March 2027. The most important implication is that LHP needs a modern, integrated housing and repairs platform, supported by a clear integration architecture and a stronger data foundation.  Core Systems — a modern, integrated core housing and repairs platform at the heart of operations, supplemented where necessary by specialist capability that is tightly integrated into the target architecture, replacing our Housing Management System alongside a fit-for-purpose finance system and consolidated service charge platform.  Data Foundation — the Data Warehouse as a single source of truth, with Power BI as the reporting and analytics layer and governance embedded through the Data Stewards.  Integration Layer — an API-first architecture with a strategic integration partner, removing manual re-keying between core systems, with the integration architecture agreed before any new system is procured.  Customer & Colleague Experience — a fully AI-enabled CXone contact centre, an enhanced customer portal integrated with the new HMS, and mobile-first field working tools. Within this roadmap, the HMS/Digital Repairs Options is a priority Year 1 initiative. The decisions taken through this appraisal will shape the future platform architecture, the integration approach, and the sequencing of wider change across the strategy period. This project is associated with the procurement of a solution for a Housing Management System, Repairs Platform and Dynamic Scheduling tool. Access to the procurement documentation can be found at the following address: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/lhp/aspx/Home Lot 1: Lot 1 – Housing Management System (HMS):. Housing Management System (HMS): tenancy, rents, lettings, arrears, income, asset management, compliance, CRM and case management. Lot 2: Lot 2 – Repairs Management System (RMS) and Dynamic Scheduler. Repairs Management System (RMS) and Dynamic Scheduler: responsive, planned and cyclical repairs, dynamic scheduling and resource optimisation across the in-house DLO and external contractors, and mobile working. Lot 3: Lot 3 Combined Lot Housing Management System and Repairs Management System. Housing Management System (HMS): tenancy, rents, lettings, arrears, income, asset management, compliance, CRM and case management and Repairs Management System (RMS) and Dynamic Scheduler: responsive, planned and cyclical repairs, dynamic scheduling and resource optimisation across the in-house DLO and external contractors, and mobile working.

Baseline Evaluation Aims -Set out current data, indicators and contextual evidence. -Identify what would likely happen without STEP to support later assessment of additionality. -Test the validity of STEP’s theory of change, assumptions and risks. -Assess data availability, quality, and feasibility for longterm evaluation. Scope -Codevelop the theory of change and logic model. -Expand the benefits library with metrics, data sources and recommendations for future monetisation. -Specify data sources, quality plans, counterfactual logic, and longterm lag assumptions. -Highlight evidence gaps and uncertainties. 2. Impact Evaluation Aims -Assess progress towards STEP’s Tranche 1 and T2a objectives. -Examine early technical advances and initial economic/social effects. -Forecast potential longerterm impacts where possible. -Identify what data and systems must be established now to enable robust T2a and future evaluations. Scope -Mixedmethods approach including early monetisation and nonmonetised impact assessment. -Develop methodologies to value fusionspecific benefits (jobs, skills, supply chain, innovation, infrastructure). -Use baseline counterfactuals to determine additionality. -Include placebased, distributional analysis and uncertainty testing. -Produce a set of highimpact case studies. 3. Process Evaluation Aims -Assess whether delivery aligns with STEP’s mission, plans and intent. -Review progress against milestones, delivery structures, partnerships, resources and governance. -Understand stakeholder engagement, risk management, dependencies and overall programme maturity. -Identify lessons learned and readiness for transition to future tranches. Scope -Review programme documentation and structures. -Conduct stakeholder interviews across UKIFS, partners and external organisations. -Use the theory of change to analyse delivery barriers and enablers. sig_08388bf3d1c7538f0a8c.description: This tender relates to Transport for Greater Manchester's (TfGM) need to procure a Cloud Public Address (PA) System and associated services to provide a secure, resilient, IP-based PA capability across TfGM Transport Service Facilities (TSFs). The PA service is intended to provide real-time passenger information, site-specific passenger safety and security (PSS) messages, and event-driven announcements, operable centrally from the Operations Control Centre (OCC) and locally by designated TSF Site Co-Ordinators. TfGM requires a cloud-hosted PA management system (with main and failover capability) integrated with an on-net estate of PA end user devices (EUDs) such as IP speakers, audio gateways, AFILs, paging stations and user clients, including the ability to interface with legacy Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems during transition and with existing third-party systems (e.g., Cisco Unified Call Manager) as required. This is an Open Tender procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. This route has been selected to ensure unrestricted market access, maximise competition, and enable engagement with the full range of capable Bidders across the services market. Lot 1: .

sig_0843e6ba64389c2b9b9f.description: The subject of the contract is the assessment of measures for compliance with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, the United Nations (hereinafter referred to as "UN") Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, gender equality, non-discrimination and accessibility for persons with disabilities, which are defined in the Partnership Agreement of the SR for the years 2021 – 2027 (hereinafter referred to as "PA") and in Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2021 laying down common provisions on the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund Plus, the Cohesion Fund, the Just Transition Fund and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund and financial rules for those and also for the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund, the Internal Security Fund and the Instrument for Financial Support for Border Management and Visa Policy (hereinafter referred to as "Regulation (EU) 2021/1060") as horizontal principles (hereinafter also referred to as "HP"). Compliance with the horizontal principles is to be evaluated within the framework of the implementation of the Slovakia Programme (hereinafter referred to as "SK P") with regard to established processes and the perception of the effectiveness of the measures by support providers and beneficiaries. The assessment will focus on the quality of the application of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in implemented projects as a consequence of measures for the application of HPs within the implementation processes of the Slovakia Programme (when issuing calls, selecting projects, monitoring and controlling projects). The assessment will also partially focus on the practical application of horizontal principles in projects within the SK P and the results achieved aimed at eliminating inequalities, discrimination and improving accessibility in accordance with evaluation questions and the required methodological procedure. Recommendations should be aimed at improving compliance with the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in implemented projects, improving cooperation between the HP manager and providers, the managing authority, or intermediate bodies (hereinafter referred to as "MA/IB") in setting up management documentation, calls, objectives and evaluation criteria. The purpose of the evaluation is to improve cooperation between MA/IBs and the HP manager with public support providers in setting up management documentation, calls, objectives and evaluation criteria with regard to good practice and the needs of target groups, as well as to ensure the high-quality implementation of SK P projects in accordance with horizontal principles in the 2021 – 2027 programme period. A detailed definition of the subject of the contract is given in Section B 1 of the tender documents.
sig_0843e6ba64389c2b9b9f.title: Assessment of the implementation of horizontal principles in the Slovakia Programme

sig_0846015502f2dfc88a0f.description: Bayerische Staatsforsten AöR operates a highly available, centrally administered IT and communications infrastructure to support business and production processes at around 600 locations, branch offices, data centre sites and home office workstations. The infrastructure comprises local area networks (LAN), cross-site wide area networks (WAN), network security solutions, WLAN infrastructures, voice communication systems as well as central management and automation platforms. To ensure secure, stable and economical operation, the network services are centrally controlled, monitored and administered. The network infrastructure connects the client's locations with the data centres and forms the basis for access to specialist applications, communication services and digital business processes. The infrastructure is continuously expanded, modernised and adapted to new technical, organisational and security-related requirements. Only network components (hardware, software, software services) from the company Cisco are used for the networks of Bayerische Staatsforsten. The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement for the supply of network components from the manufacturer Cisco, including associated software, licences, maintenance, care, support and repair services as well as, if applicable, further technical services. On the basis of the framework agreement, existing components are to be renewed, expanded or replaced as required during the contract term. The framework agreement is not intended for the complete reconstruction of an isolated infrastructure, but for the further development of an existing, productively operated network landscape during ongoing operation on the basis of network components. The services to be procured must be capable of being integrated into the existing system landscape and must meet the requirements for interoperability, information security, availability, operational stability, manageability and cost-effectiveness. Particular importance is attached to compatibility with existing network, security, management and automation processes as well as the ability to ensure the operation of the existing infrastructure without disproportionate conversion, migration or parallel operation efforts. The estimated total requirement includes the successive procurement of network components, network security solutions, software licences as well as associated maintenance, care, support and repair services over the intended contract term. The services are obtained on a demand-driven basis through individual call-offs from the framework agreement.
sig_0846015502f2dfc88a0f.title: Framework agreement for network components 2027, Cisco EA extension

sig_089d7f975758391e5039.description: THIS IS A MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE ONLY Introduction: The Buyer is delivering the GOV.UK One Login programme and system; a single, ubiquitous and secure way for users to log in and, where necessary, prove who they are to access central government services. It will replace multiple legacy systems across government, transforming the user experience and reducing duplication, improving counter-fraud protection and realising significant financial benefits. The core of the system is live. Users can create an account, log in and prove (and then reuse) their identity through either a web-based journey or smartphone app to access a growing number of government services. They can draw on recognised identity evidence like passports or Drivers Licences to prove their identity wholly online, or choose to use our in-person identity checking option (offered in partnership with the Post Office). Over 3 million people have so far proved their identity through GOV.UK One Login. Purpose: Government Digital Service (GDS) is conducting this market engagement exercise to gather information from suppliers regarding the potential procurement for the provision of email and phone validation service as well as an Identity Fraud checks service. This is to help us refine our requirements, understand the available solutions and gauge market interest. The purpose of this RFI is to: - Understand the range of solutions, services and prices available in the market. - Refine our requirements and procurement approach based on market feedback. To express your interest, please email: commissioning-digital@dsit.gov.uk with the subject line clearly stating: prj_6102 RFI - Identity Fraud Check and, Email and Phone Validation by EOP 30 October 2025. We will then send you the market engagement pack to complete. Lot 1: .
sig_089d7f975758391e5039.title: RFI - Identity Fraud Check and, Email and Phone Validation

sig_08e31437b35cbedcdc3a.description: To support the renewal of England’s women’s health strategy https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69df5d7261d2e8e9b9e42d2e/renewed-womens-health-strategy-for-england-web-accessible.pdf the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is exploring collaboration opportunities with stakeholders from the voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) and private sectors interested in supporting the improvement of women’s health outcomes. The renewed women's health strategy sets out the government’s ambitions for women’s health in the context of the 10 Year Health Plan and focus on the key themes of women being listened to and getting the care they need, women being supported to make reproductive choices, and women being empowered and supported to prevent future ill health. The renewed women's health strategy builds on the core objectives of the 2022 Women's health strategy https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/womens-health-strategy-for-england/womens-health-strategy-for-england and the 10 Year Health Plan for England https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/10-year-health-plan-for-england-fit-for-the-future and both should be used as a framework for this exercise. We are asking interested parties to complete a questionnaire detailing their proposal at this link: https://forms.office.com/e/Rxbv8jvT1t The questionnaire will close for responses at 12:00pm on 22nd of April 2026. Further guidance on how to complete the questionnaire can be found at the following link: https://atamis-1928.my.salesforce.com/sfc/p/0O000000rwim/a/Pz00000IaOZK/G0YmgVuobfYOa6XQ9fi1Az3mJA_kfBnqq7DoCPxAWL4 DHSC is specifically looking at collaborating on a “value in kind” basis and we are especially interested in hearing about planned or ongoing initiatives focusing on addressing health inequalities for women which could include: • Health literacy, • Prevention and barriers to women’s access to appropriate health provision, • Engagement and/or positive experience with the health system, and • Securing funding for these. Since the publication of this notice, we have received a number of clarification questions in relation to the Women’s Health Strategic Partnership Opportunity. To ensure transparency and equal access to information for all prospective respondents, we are publishing our responses at the following link for reference when preparing submissions: https://atamis-1928.my.salesforce.com/sfc/p/#0O000000rwim/a/Pz00000J81nB/UbSVM_btaIOdC4fVGX.cn1EKPlKsCKjZsej9VLMigtQ Lot 1: .

sig_08e3b296801d0b707233.description: The primary purpose of this preliminary market engagement exercise (“Exercise”) is for the Education Authority (EA) to explain, and seek supplier views and feedback on, potential approaches for a Configuration Management Database solution. EA requires a CMDB to provide a trusted, accurate and near-real-time view of its ICT assets, applications, services and the relationships between them. Acting as the single source of truth for the DTS estate, it will reduce manual data maintenance through automation, support Cyber Essentials accreditation and provide the foundation for EA’s ICT Service Catalogue. To deliver these outcomes, the CMDB must integrate with EA’s Change Management process and ITSM platform. This integration will ensure that trusted configuration and service data informs change assessment, approval and implementation. By mapping the relationships between services, applications and infrastructure components, the CMDB will allow proposed changes to be assessed against known dependencies and potential business impacts before implementation. This visibility will support more reliable planning, testing and communication, giving decision-makers greater confidence that changes can proceed safely. Lot 1: .

sig_091918c49ae03344e714.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) is a health authority charged with identifying, investigating and preventing fraud and other economic crime within the NHS and the wider health group. As a health authority focused entirely on counter fraud work, the NHSCFA is independent from other NHS bodies and directly accountable to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). THE NHSCFA currently operate two separate systems for the provision of an intelligence database and a case management system. The intention is to identify if there is a single solution that can replace the existing systems. If that is not possible then the aim would be to have two separate products that connect and align with each other to avoid duplication and operational inefficiencies. This market engagement exercise seeks the views and opinions of those organisations that may be interested in delivering the requirements. The scope of this market engagement covers is provided within the draft service specification. This exercise and any subsequent responses are in no way legally binding on any party. Participation in the engagement exercise is not a mandatory requirement for participating in any potential future procurement; however, responses received will assist to inform the Contracting Authority as to the level of interest from the market and will be used to evidence a decision as to whether or not to undertake a competitive procurement. The Market Engagement Questionnaire and current Service Specifications can be downloaded from SAP Ariba Portal at the below link: https://discovery.ariba.com/rfx/23496944 Please return your completed MEQ through the Portal no later than 5pm on 30 October 2025.
sig_091918c49ae03344e714.title: The Provision of a Fraud Case Management System and Intelligence Database on behalf of NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA)

sig_0928a1f0bb628f91b713.description: The joint regulation IJsselgemeenten is looking for a contractor to supply an iPaaS/SaaS ESB and SaaS data distribution facility as a multi-tenant service. Within the Client's subscription, the solution supports a logically separated setup per participating organisation. Integrations, data, subscriptions, configurations, authorisations and logging can be shielded per organisation, while authorised central administrators of the joint regulation IJsselgemeenten can manage the whole. Exchange between organisations takes place exclusively via explicitly configured and authorised connections. Thus, the platform forms the central facility for secure, reliable and structured data exchange between the applications within the ICT landscape of the IJsselgemeenten. In addition to delivery, the assignment includes the setup and configuration per organisation, the migration of existing connections, and the structural management and maintenance during the term of the agreement. The contract concerns the delivery of an ESB platform and a data distribution module as a multi-tenant SaaS/iPaaS service, including connection to national facilities via Diginetwerk and Digikoppeling, in accordance with Appendix D – Programme of Requirements. As of the reference date, approximately 75 integrations run via the current platform. These will be migrated to the new platform within an implementation period of 7 months. In addition, the assignment includes building new connections and integrations during the term of the agreement, as well as the management, maintenance and further development of the ESB platform, the data distribution module and the integrations. The services have an initial term of four years, with a maximum of three extension options of two years. Joint regulation IJsselgemeenten is looking for a single contractor for the delivery, implementation and management of an Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) platform. The assignment includes making available and setting up the ESB platform, migrating existing connections, building and making available new connections and integrations, and managing, maintaining and further developing the platform and integrations. In addition, service, support, incident handling and a structured exit and handover arrangement are part of the assignment. The assignment comprises the delivery, implementation/migration, management, maintenance and further development of an ESB platform. The current integration landscape comprises approximately 150 integrations. The services have an initial term of four years, with a maximum of three extension options of two years.
