sig_0c99e5b1c4435536da69.description: Capital City Partnership (CCP) intends to undertake a procurement exercise for the provision, support, maintenance and ongoing development of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Management Information System (MIS). Lot 1: . Capital City Partnership (CCP) intends to undertake a procurement exercise for the provision, support, maintenance and ongoing development of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Management Information System (MIS) covering - City of Edinburgh - East Lothian - Fife - Midlothian - Scottish Borders - West Lothian The platform supports service delivery across a wide range of organisations involved in employability, skills and related service delivery activities throughout the region. This Prior Information Notice is intended to provide advance notice of the procurement and to encourage engagement from suitably experienced suppliers. CCP currently operates an established regional CRM and Management Information System supporting service delivery across six Local Authority areas. The solution is used by approximately: - 1,000 users - 110 organisations - 115,000 client records - 2.5 million recorded activities and interventions - 14,500 employer records - 17,000 vacancy records The platform supports a range of operational and reporting requirements and provides a critical service supporting frontline delivery, partnership working and performance management. While the primary use of the system is employability and skills delivery, the platform is also used to support wider service delivery activities including Community Learning and Development, work experience and placement management, and public-facing provider directory functionality. CCP intends to procure a solution capable of supporting the current and future requirements of the partnership. The successful supplier will be expected to provide: - CRM and participant management functionality - Case management functionality - Referral management - Action planning and intervention recording - Outcome tracking and reporting - Employer engagement functionality - Vacancy management - Programme and project management functionality - Management information and reporting - Document management - Workflow and configuration tools - Hosting, support and maintenance services - Ongoing development and enhancement services - Service management and governance arrangements CCP is seeking a solution capable of supporting future growth, service development and innovation throughout the contract term of 8 years. The current solution operates in a multi-organisational environment supporting Local Authorities and a wide range of delivery partners. The platform currently supports: - Configurable forms and workflows - Multi-organisation access and permissions - Standard and customised reporting - Document management - Employer engagement and vacancy management - Data imports, exports and secure data exchange processes - Public-facing information directory functionality CCP currently operates a single core user model and is seeking a commercially sustainable and scalable approach to licensing and service provision. The successful supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with CCP throughout the contract term and support: - Continuous improvement - Product development - Service innovation - Additional reporting requirements - New business processes - Additional users and organisations - Future integration requirements - Additional service delivery models where required CCP is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers support long-term product development, customer engagement and technology innovation. CCP is seeking a transparent and scalable commercial model. sig_0ca369a61c17641187e5.description: 1. Purpose of the Notice This UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Notice is issued in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. The purpose of this notice is to inform the market of a MoJ Request for Information (RFI) and to engage with suppliers to obtain feedback and insights on the potential requirement for a workload, workflow and productivity solution. The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) is a major government department, at the heart of the justice system. The MoJ works to protect and advance the principles of justice; our vision is to deliver a world-class justice system that works for everyone in society. His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) is an executive agency, sponsored by the MoJ and carries out sentences given by the courts, in custody and in the community, and rehabilitates people in its care through education and employment. High workload remains a stubborn and persistent issue within Probation. A National Audit Office report https://www.nao.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/building-an-effective-and-resilient-probation-service.pdf reviewed the resilience of Probation Services in England and Wales earlier in 2025 and identified: - 10 of 12 regions were exceeding 100% average workload for Probation Officers; - 46 of 108 delivery units were operating in red or amber delivery status (set up to manage high workloads), and so were not delivering all mandated sentence management activities; and - There was a 3150 FTE shortfall in staff working within sentence management. This sets a challenging context for Probation, and the need for us to better understand and manage workload, workflow and productivity. Ahead of budget allocations for 2026/27, the MoJ is keen to obtain feedback and insights on the potential requirement for a workload, workflow and productivity solution for HMPPS. This Request for Information (RFI) is a preliminary market engagement exercise to seek information relating to this requirement, and to gain a better understanding of the types and availability of products and services, as well as the commercial terms on which to acquire them. 2. Access and Communication This RFI is being conducted through the MoJ e-Sourcing portal and all communications between MoJ and Suppliers during this RFI process must strictly be made using the MoJ e-Sourcing portal. - Suppliers must create an account on the e-sourcing portal found via the link here: https://ministryofjusticecommercial.bravosolution.co.uk/web/login.html - Suppliers can access the RFI from 4th December (the ‘RfI Opens’ date) via PQQ_545. - The PQQ will hold the following RFI documents and information which consists of: *Attachment 1 RFI Instructions *Attachment 2 RFI Background and Scope *Attachment 3 RFI Questionnaire *Clarification questions and answers document (shared using the messaging facility) -Suppliers will respond to the RFI by uploading the completed Attachment 3 RFI Questionnaire to Technical Envelope, Question 1.1 ‘RFI Questionnaire’. 3. Timescales These are our intended RFI timescales. We will inform you if and when timelines change. 1st December 2025 - UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice released and supplier e-sourcing system registration 4th December 2025 - RFI opens and Clarification period starts 16th December 2025, 17:00 - Clarification period ends 17th December 2025, 17:00 - Deadline for the publication of responses to RFI Clarification questions 19th December 2025, 17:00 - Deadline for submission of RFI Responses December to January 2025 - Confirm the next steps to Suppliers including potential opportunity for demonstrations 4. Disclaimer Nothing shall constitute a commitment to ordering or award unless the MoJ publishes an Invitation to Tender that results in the award of a Contract. The contents of the Preliminary Market Engagement are not binding and may be subject to change or cancellation. Lot 1: .

sig_0ca3fc787d91c8a6ec32.description: The Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB) is an independent scientific research centre under the umbrella of the Helmholtz Association with sites in Berlin-Adlershof and Wannsee. The BESSY II electron storage ring delivers highly brilliant synchrotron radiation from the terahertz to the X-ray range. With its focus on VUV and soft X-ray radiation, BESSY II is exceptionally well suited for the analysis of energy materials and thin-film systems. The further development of instrumentation and the preparation of a concept for a successor source (BESSY III) are among the most important tasks of the coming years. At our BESSY II electron storage ring, we record an annual average of 2.700 visits by guest researchers from 28 countries. Each year, 500 to 600 publications appear in scientific journals based on measurements at BESSY II and – until the end of 2019 – on measurements at BER II. The "BESSY II+" upgrade programme: This programme makes it possible to continue cutting-edge research at BESSY II and to test new concepts with a view to the BESSY III successor source. BESSY is to become an "operando synchrotron for the energy transition". BESSY II+ comprises new experimental possibilities, in particular for operando investigations. These make it possible, for example, to observe batteries or solar cells "in operation". In addition to the new "operando" possibilities, the BESSY II+ project also focuses on the topics of "modernisation" and "sustainability". Sustainability includes, among other things, the use of waste heat from the experimental hall of BESSY II. In addition, machine learning and artificial intelligence are increasingly being integrated into many processes. As part of the modernisation project, the HZB has received additional funding from the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF). "Invest BESSY II+" comprises the key investments for the project funded by the BMBF. This funding secures the development of new infrastructures, such as the SoTeXS (Soft-to-Tender X-ray Spectroscopy) instrument. This is a comprehensive concept for metrological, multimodal experiments that can be used in battery and materials research for energy applications. This call for tenders comprises the procurement and manufacture of two Pt/B4C coated toroidal X-ray mirrors (TO-1, TO-2) for measurement station KMC-1 at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin. The mirrors serve to focus the white beam of the storage ring. 2x 1 piece(s) of toroidal mirrors for KMC-1 (Bessy II+), in accordance with the performance description (technical specification) and tender documents.
sig_0ca3fc787d91c8a6ec32.title: V427_2026 – WI-AOS – Toroidal mirror for KMC-1 (Bessy II+)

The general objective of the contract is to support the AM PR BI programme evaluation experts in ensuring the quality of evaluation reports, creating and fostering an evaluation culture, and developing the stakeholders' programme evaluation capacity. The specific objectives of the Contract are as follows: - Assistance in drawing up the specifications for the following 3 evaluations: Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Supporting the staff of the PR BI Programme Evaluation Office (BEP) in managing the evaluation reports provided for in the Evaluation Plan (EP) and in carrying out other programme evaluation activities, monitoring the progress of evaluations, participating in meetings with the Evaluator, providing methodological guidance throughout the implementation of each evaluation, including by drawing up quality check grids for evaluation reports and validating evaluation results. The service provider shall provide views, observations and proposals for improvement, and shall methodologically and technically validate the evaluation reports (initial, interim, final, as appropriate) for the following 4 evaluations: Evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027, Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Consolidating the transfer of learning from the evaluation process in order to create and develop the capacity and evaluation culture of stakeholders by carrying out training for BEP programme evaluation experts, members of the Evaluation Coordination Committee (ECC) and other persons involved in the field of programme evaluation. Results of the contract: - 3 proposals for specifications, including evaluation factors, details of expert teams, requirements regarding the quality of evaluations and methodologies used, for the following evaluations: Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Minimum 8 – maximum 12 Quality reports on the analysis of the initial, interim and final evaluation reports for the four evaluations, 4 Checklists for initial reports and 4 Evaluation report quality check grids; the number of working versions for the quality reports may vary depending on the report versions submitted by the evaluator. The service provider shall complete an evaluation list / check grid for each version of the programme evaluation reports, and the grids for the final reports shall be presented at ECC meetings, referring to the applied methodology, the robustness of the database used, the quality of the analysis carried out by experts, including by attaching to the grid the reports on the support activity for each evaluation, the minutes of the meetings and the methodological guidance provided throughout the implementation of each evaluation, for the following evaluations: Evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027, Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - 1 Training plan, 2 training reports, which shall include course materials, participant lists, training session agendas, course photos, feedback forms and participation certificates issued by the trainer, for the training activities carried out to improve the level of professional training in the field of programme evaluation of BEP and AM PR BI members. The evaluation plan for PR BI 2021-2027 is a strategic document whose purpose is to establish how evaluations will be carried out during the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027 and to set out the resources necessary to carry out programme evaluations. The Evaluation Plan includes a series of interim evaluations deemed necessary to improve the quality of the drafting and implementation of PR BI 2021 - 2027, such as the evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021 - 2027, as well as thematic evaluations (evaluation of communication actions, evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes and evaluation of Technical Assistance actions). To ensure the quality of the evaluation process and to validate the evaluation results, the need was identified to develop the evaluation capacity of the Managing Authority by setting up the Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC1) through the procurement of consultancy and technical assistance services. The Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC1) shall be set up with the aim of providing technical expertise to ensure the quality of the evaluation process and to validate the evaluation results. ETSC1 shall analyse evaluation data needs, provide support in finalising the specifications, and contribute to improving the quality of evaluation reports. It shall also generate scientific / technical opinions on evaluation methodologies and evaluation reports, and support the development of evaluation skills for the evaluation unit and ECC. The experts for this contract shall carry out their activities in the form of an Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC) and shall contribute to ensuring the quality of reports by directly supporting BEP PR BI members (guidance/training) in analysing the evaluations carried out under the PR BI evaluation contracts 2021 – 2027. The Technical Committee shall formulate views on the various versions of evaluation reports, provide support for drawing up specifications and train personnel involved in programme evaluation activities.

The technical evaluation support committee shall consist of at least three senior experts (members of academia or senior experts at sector level or in the field of programme/policy evaluation), who shall support the MA in implementing individual evaluations. Given the novelty of the programme evaluation activity within the contract, the Service Provider shall carry out the following specific activities: 1. Activity 1 – Assistance in drawing up specifications for 3 evaluations provided for in the Evaluation Plan, including the evaluability analysis of the evaluation themes relating to the 3 evaluations; 2. Activity 2 – Support for ensuring the quality of deliverables within the 4 evaluations from the Evaluation Plan; 3. Activity 3 – Transfer and use of knowledge generated by the evaluation process to support the development of institutional and individual skills and to build an evaluation culture among stakeholders.
sig_0cf2bb1000cb6faf6b39.title: Consultancy and technical assistance services for the development of the evaluation capacity of the Management Authority of the Bucharest – Ilfov Regional Programme 2021-2027

sig_0cf9033be4e6247940fc.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of a digital application to improve the estimation procedure, utilising the existing database of its information system in combination with additional geospatial information, and interoperating with other public bodies such as the Ministry of Rural Development and Food (MinRDAF), OPEKEPE, etc. This digital application will enable the estimator to organise, carry out, and complete their estimation, having online or offline availability of all data necessary for the completion of the estimation procedure on-site in their field of action (plot of land - holding), saving time, reliability, cost reduction, and flexibility for the entire estimation procedure. (para. 1.3 and ANNEX I of the Notice). The subject of the contract is the implementation of a digital application to improve the estimation procedure, utilising the existing database of its information system in combination with additional geospatial information, and interoperating with other public bodies such as the Ministry of Rural Development and Food (MinRDAF), OPEKEPE, etc. This digital application will enable the estimator to organise, carry out, and complete their estimation, having online or offline availability of all data necessary for the completion of the estimation procedure on-site in their field of action (plot of land - holding), saving time, reliability, cost reduction, and flexibility for the entire estimation procedure. Furthermore, by adding geospatial and multimedia additional information within the framework of the estimation, a large database is expected to be created for future use of business analytics applications, which upgrade the organisation's capability for decision making and ultimately improving its services. The subject of the project is therefore the implementation of a digital application with which the estimator, using a portable device (tablet), completes the estimation procedure on-site in their field of action, having the ability to have all necessary data gathered and available online. It is clarified that the damage declaration procedure is not altered by this Project and that the damage estimation of each plot of land is carried out in accordance with the rules of agronomic science by an agronomist-estimator of ELGA – it is supported but not altered by this Project. (para. 1.3 and ANNEX I of the Notice).
sig_0cf9033be4e6247940fc.title: “Digital Application for the ELGA Estimation Procedure” with MIS Code: 5129458

General technical specification (part-level, comprehensive) The part contains equipment supporting the motor, sensory, cognitive, communication, linguistic and psychological development, as well as diagnostic and pedagogical examination, of children and pupils of various ages. The equipment can be applied in individual and group development, in an inclusive educational environment, in pedagogical and special education institutions. 1. Equipment supporting motor and physical development 1.1. tactile path, sensor floor set) Technical requirements: • Items containing various surface structures • Modularly assembled set • Safe, rounded edges • Non-slip bottom surface • Suitable for indoor use 2.2. Visual and light-based sensory devices (e.g., illuminated tray, light projector) Technical requirements: • Uniform light distribution • Adjustable brightness or colour • Safe low-voltage operation • Durable, child-safe design 3. Devices supporting time perception and behaviour regulation 3.1. Visual timers (e.g., hourglass set, visual timer) Technical requirements: • Time ranges in multiple steps (e.g., 1–60 minutes) • Display of visualised passage of time • Sound signal can be switched off • Portable design • Durable, child-safe casing 4. Communication supporting devices (AAC) 4.1. Talking and voice-recording devices (e.g., talking tile, disc, voice-recording album) Technical requirements: • Simple, push-button operation • Minimum 10–30 second recording capability/button • Replaceable or rechargeable power source • Durable, impact-resistant design • Suitable for Hungarian language use 4.2. Alternative and augmentative communication devices (e.g., multi-button communicators, picture communication sets) Technical requirements: • Multiple activatable communication fields • Interchangeable picture cards • Multi-level usage capability • Suitable for both hand-held and desktop use • Design tested in institutional environments 5. Cognitive, linguistic and mathematical development tools 5.1. Language and reading-readiness games (e.g., language tic-tac-toe, magnetic, card-based language games) Technical requirements: • Tasks developing native language competencies • Development of vocabulary, sound and syllable awareness • Suitable for individual and group use • Durable, thick cardboard or plastic elements 5.2. Mathematical and number-concept development tools (e.g., number houses, base-ten system tools) Technical requirements: • Elements supporting manipulative learning • Development of number concept and quantitative thinking • Coloured, visually well-distinguished elements • Durable design, for pedagogical use 6. Diagnostic and pedagogical examination tools 6.1. Packages serving for the examination of learning abilities (e.g., dyscalculia, screening packages for learning difficulties) Technical requirements: • Structured, age-specific task series • Usable by educators and specialists • Contains both written and manipulative tasks • With printed or digital accompanying material 7. Tools supporting psychological safety and emotional regulation 7.1. Calming and stress-relieving tools (e.g., stress ball, nook, dark tent) Technical requirements: • Soft, flexible material • Safe, non-choking design • Easy to clean • Size suitable for institutional use QUANTITY: 502 pcs, in detail: under point "II.2.14) Additional information:" due to character limit This part contains tools serving pedagogical, psychological and special needs developmental and examination purposes, for children of various ages and development levels. The subject of the procurement consists of such board games, developmental and skill-development tools that are suitable for the complex development of preschool and school-age children, particularly children struggling with special educational needs (SEN), learning, attention, communication or social difficulties. The tools must relate to several of the following development areas: • native language and communication skills (vocabulary, speech initiation, reading comprehension, phonological awareness), • logical and mathematical thinking, • attention, memory, executive functions, • social competencies, emotional intelligence, conflict management, • fine and gross motor skills, hand-eye coordination, • perception, sensation, sensory integration, • creativity, problem-solving, cooperation. Functional expectations The board games and tools may include the following types: • logical and thinking-development games (e.g.,

sequentiality, patterns, combinations), • linguistic and native language development games, picture cards, worksheet systems, • memory, attention and association games, • social-emotional development tools (recognition of emotions, self-awareness, social situations), • manipulative, construction, building-type games (wood, plastic, magnetic elements), • tools developing fine motor skills (threading, screwing, pinching), • games containing sensory and tactile elements (development of touch, sight, hearing), • sets suitable for role-play, storytelling, • board games suitable for both individual and group sessions. Usage environment The tools can be used: • in kindergarten and school group rooms, • in development and therapy rooms, • during individual and small-group developments, • in inclusive educational environments. sig_0d0a5a0caeb59743b8c5.description: The investment aims to support the process of redefining and reorganising the services provided by the Information Technology and Communications Directorate, as well as the IT&C infrastructure of the Company, so that they can support the conduct of processes under conditions of safety, efficiency, and availability. In addition, an increase in the efficiency of processes within the Company is ensured by reducing downtime in situations where data losses occur. The backup & restore system is dedicated to ensuring backups for the managerial IT domain, which is currently in the process of migrating from a silo infrastructure to a Hyper-converged Infrastructure (HCI) using VMware virtualisation software, hereinafter referred to as the "Private Cloud". The system shall be able to provide backups for the "Private Cloud" at the time it is loaded at 100%, but, until the migration is completed, to provide backups for silo-type systems for the period while they are not yet migrated. The system called "Back-up and restore system" involves the procurement of hardware and software equipment. The requested backup solution must be an appliance-type configuration and backup software supplemented with a long-term tape backup system. The system proposed by the Tenderers must perform backups in such a way as to ensure increased operational efficiency, safety, and agility through the use of new centralised backup policies. Thus, the proposed solution will ensure both the licences necessary for the management of the back-up and restore system and its scalability at the central level as well as at the 8 (eight) Transport Branches. Number of days before the deadline for submission of tenders by which clarifications may be requested: 17 The contracting entity will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information in a single stage, as follows: - on the 11-th calendar day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting entity will only respond to requests for clarifications addressed by economic operators by the established deadline. The "Back-up & Restore System" involves the procurement of hardware and software equipment to support the availability of the IT systems of CNTEE Transelectrica SA in a coherent manner, based on technological convergence, independent of the software applications or platforms required by the Company and with reduced maintenance costs. sig_0d364cceeec484708669.description: As part of urban development funding and based on the Integrated Urban Development Concept (ISEK), the Stadt Castrop-Rauxel is planning the monument- and climate-compatible further development of the ensemble in the centre of the town, which includes the buildings of the town hall, the municipal and European hall and the Forum Square. The town hall building consists of a total of five self-contained blocks (Blocks A to E) with a length of 45 m each and five storeys, and is supplemented in the inner area of the Forum Square by the council chamber, which is connected underground directly to the town hall building on the lowest floor of Block B. Lot LOT-0001: building physics and structural planning services for Town Hall CR. The aim of the renovation is, alongside the creation of open-space work and recreation areas, a sound energetic and building-physical upgrade of the building envelope. This includes services for thermal insulation and energy balancing, which encompass energy planning, verification in accordance with the GModG (Building Modernisation Act) and optimisation of the building envelope in accordance with the state of the art, insofar as this is possible under monument protection law. A central challenge is the thermal heating of the storage masses of the structure, such as the concrete columns, and requires summer thermal insulation. This is to be prevented by appropriate measures on the facade (blow-in insulation) or internally in the column area. In addition, the technical and economic feasibility of green roofs in combination with a photovoltaic system on the existing flat roof is to be investigated. The existing PV system including substructure, ballasting and fastening as well as the static and structural boundary conditions of the building must be taken into account. The existing system was built in 2007 and leased to a cooperative. It comprises 556 solar modules from the manufacturer Chaori (CRM 180Wp). The modules are erected on a raised, ballasted support structure. The total roof area of the town hall is (W x L) approx. 14,20 x 253,00 m. In the course of the renovation, a complete replacement of the window and door glazing in blocks A and B is also planned. Services for thermal insulation and energy balancing are to be carried out for the guarantee town hall. These include energetic planning, verification in accordance with the GModG and optimisation of the building envelope in accordance with the state of the art, insofar as permitted under monument protection law. For this purpose, an as-is analysis must be carried out to determine the current U-values. Following the commissioning of the architect and object planning (expected 2 quarter 2027), the required or possible renovation measures (including U-value calculations, thermal bridge analyses, summer thermal insulation) are to be determined with the contracting authority and the specialist planners. For this reason, the provision of services will take place in two commissioning stages. In principle, structural engineering measures to improve thermal insulation can only be carried out in close coordination with monument conservation. In the course of the feasibility check, additional structural planning services must be provided. These include a structural check of the roof statics with regard to the dead load of a green roof in conjunction with a PV system as well as the new structural calculation of the facade statics with regard to anchoring. In this context, endoscopic investigations are to be carried out to verify, on the one hand, the quality and number of anchorings and, on the other hand, the dimensions of the cavity for potential blow-in insulation.

sig_0d7e044234df7db60761.description: This is an invitation and request for information for a market consultation (not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders). No tenders are submitted in response to the request for information; instead, by registering for the market consultation, the supplier declares its willingness to participate in the preparation of the procurement. SUBJECT: Kela is preparing the procurement of an organisation-wide AI governance tool (AI Governance Tool), which provides a centralised solution for the registration, risk classification, lifecycle management, documentation of AI systems, and verification of compliance in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act). The subject of the procurement is an off-the-shelf software delivered as a cloud service, which brings together processes, workflows, monitoring and reporting, enabling transparent, auditable and efficient AI governance across Kela's operations. The solution supports the initial setup of the 20–50 system and will scale according to growing needs, providing comprehensive maintenance, information security and support services as well as role-based access control. MARKET CONSULTATION: Participants are requested to, inter alia: - present solutions available on the market - answer questions concerning the procurement - comment on minimum requirements, for example for the removal of conflicts of interest - provide ideas for improving the solution and the tendering process The consultation will be carried out in multiple formats: Presentation sessions may be held remotely via Microsoft Teams, and requirement definitions, for example, will be handled by email. As part of the market survey, the signing of a non-disclosure agreement may be required for the sharing of confidential material. The material and procurement documentation provided by Kela are in Finnish, and the contracting authority will not translate the material. PARTICIPATION: Interested participants are requested to declare their willingness to participate in the market survey by email to it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi 27.3.2026 by 12. Example of message content: Message subject: Company xx's participation in the market consultation for the procurement of the AI governance tool Message content: The message should ideally indicate the supplier's name, business ID and contact person through whom the consultation will be conducted. We also hope that a short presentation material on the offered solution would be attached to the participation message. The presentation material is expected to describe concisely the key features of the solution, the technical architecture, the implementation of AI Act requirements, and any experience of similar implementations. OTHER: The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to execute the procurement in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the request for information in the drafting of the invitation to tenders and contract template. Respondents to the request for information will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information. Responding to the request for information does not bind the supplier to participate in the tender contest, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tender contest later. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender contest. The information obtained through the request for information will be treated confidentially.

The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from electronic information resources (hereinafter also referred to as 'EIZ'), which serve as a source of information for the needs of implementing scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic. 1. CONTRACT TITLE: Ensuring access to the database analytical and information service STATISTA or 'equivalent' 2. SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT: The subject of the contract is to ensure access to an online database analytical and information service for a period of two years, which provides comprehensive, structured and regularly updated statistical data, analytical outputs, surveys and market analyses from the fields of economics, business, society, consumer behaviour and selected market sectors. The service must allow professional and non-professional users effective access to data, their comparison, visualisation and use for analytical, strategic, research, pedagogical and decision-making purposes. 3. SPECIFICATION OF THE SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT – MINIMUM SCOPE: A. Statistical database and analytical content The database service must contain: • an extensive collection of statistical data, indicators and time series from international and national sources of a public or professional nature, containing at least 900 thousand statistical indicators • data covering at least the areas of: o macroeconomics and public finance, o demography and social development, o education, healthcare, technologies, media, o business, industry and services, o information technology and digitalisation o social and demographic areas • geographical coverage: o global data o data for the EU and individual member states o the possibility to identify the Slovak Republic • graphic and tabular display of data with the possibility of editing, • the possibility of exporting data and visualisations at least into commonly used formats (at least XLS, CSV, PDF, PNG formats), • clear indication of data sources and methodological notes, • it must have regular content updates at least on a monthly basis. B. Consumer behaviour analyses (Consumer Insights 'or equivalent') The database service must allow access to analytical content focused on consumer behaviour and attitudes, which meets these minimum requirements: • analysis of consumer behaviour, attitudes, preferences and lifestyle, • data obtained through standardised consumer surveys, • the possibility of segmenting respondents according to selected criteria (e.g. age, gender, region, income, education), • comparison of results between countries or regions, • clear visualisations and interpretable outputs suitable for analytical and research purposes. C. Market and industry analyses (Market Insights 'or equivalent') The database service must contain analytical content focused on market and industry analyses, which meets these minimum requirements: • market and industry analyses of selected segments of the economy, especially the digital economy, finance, consumer markets, healthcare, industry, transport, media and other relevant sectors, including data on market size, forecasts and development. • information on: o market size, o development and trends, o development forecasts, o key performance indicators, • comparison of markets at national, regional and global levels, • analytical reports and overviews usable for strategic and decision-making purposes; the database must provide analytical overviews at least to the extent of: market analyses (Market Insights or equivalent), industry and country reports, consumer analyses, forecasting models (Outlook), benchmarking overviews and macroeconomic indicators, including expert commentary and comparative analyses. • the user must have the possibility to:  display data in the form of graphs and tables  export data at least in the formats: • XLS / CSV • PDF • image formats (e.g. PNG)  use outputs for: • research purposes • analytical reports • presentations D. Requirements for quality, updating and transparency • the content of the database must be regularly updated at least on a monthly basis, • for every data output, the data source and year of collection must be stated, • the methodology of data collection must be available or briefly described, • the service must ensure the consistency and comparability of data over time. 3.1 Technical and user requirements • access via a web interface without the need for local software installation, • searching within the database by keywords and thematic areas, • access for an agreed number of users within institutions • availability of the service for the duration of access ...............................................................a detailed description of the subject of the contract is part of the tender documents; 1. CONTRACT TITLE: Ensuring access to the web programming service Web of Science API EXPANDED or 'equivalent'. 2. SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT: The subject of the contract is the procurement of an Application Programming Interface (API) service to the Web of Science database (hereinafter referred to as 'API') for a period of two years, which provides authorised access to bibliographic, citation and metrically relevant data on scientific publications, authors, institutions and publication sources for academic and research purposes. The service is to be made available via an online programming interface, which allows automated access to data and their further processing and use for the purposes of research, bibliometric analyses, reporting and data aggregation from the Web of Science database. 3. SPECIFICATION OF THE SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT – MINIMUM SCOPE: A) Functional requirements of the service A.1. Interface • The service must provide REST-API access with output in JSON or XML formats. • Authentication must be carried out using an API key / registered application. A.2. Content and data The subject of the contract must allow: a) Advanced searching and filtering of bibliographic records according to various criteria (e.g. author, DOI, title, institution, year of publication).

b) Obtaining full metadata about publications, including: • title of publication, DOI, identifiers, document type, • authors, their identifiers (at least ResearcherID / ORCID if available), • title of publication source, year, ISSN/ISBN, pagination, • citation data – number of citations, cited references and citing documents. c) Connections between records – the possibility to obtain: • cited references – references that the given document cited, • citing items – which publications cite the given document, • related records – related publications. A.3. Expanding metrics and data • The API must support the obtaining of bibliometric indicators and metadata associated with publications, such as data on research funding, author organisations, subject category fields or geographical data of authors, if available. B) Technical requirements of the service B.1. Availability and performance • The API must be available 24/7, with guaranteed response for common queries up to a set number of queries per second/average per year according to the licensing plan. B.2. Usage plans The service must support various levels of load including medium to high volumes of requests for bibliographic data, with defined limits for: • number of 'requests' per second, • monthly/annual volume of returned records. B.3. Security • Authentication based on secure API keys, compliance with cryptographic standards during data transmission (HTTPS/TLS). • Compliance with personal data protection principles and GDPR when processing data about authors where relevant. 3.2 The provider must simultaneously ensure the following additional services during the access period: ..............the full description of the subject of the contract is stated in the tender documents.; 1. CONTRACT TITLE: Provision of an analytical service for research evaluation based on artificial intelligence 2. SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT: The subject of the contract is the delivery, implementation and provision of access to an electronic information resource - a comprehensive analytical service for a period of two years, intended to support strategic research management, evaluation of scientific activity innovations and analysis of the social impact of research at the level of research organisations and higher education institutions. The service must be a next-generation research-intelligence platform, which through an AI solution allows centralised processing, linking and analysis of data on research and innovation, researchers, organisational units, research funding and its impact, whereby the data must be based on verified, internationally comparable and auditable data sources. 3. SPECIFICATION OF THE SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT – Required functional and qualitative properties of the service The subject of the contract is to ensure access to an electronic information resource – Research Intelligence 'or equivalent' for a duration of 2 years. The required properties are: A. Integrated research information management The service must provide a unified analytical environment that: • covers at least the areas of: o research funding o collaboration o evaluation of scientific impact o benchmarking of research organisations and countries • allows evaluation of research impact at least in the areas of: o scientific impact (citation-based) o technological impact (e.g. linking to patents) o social and political impact • integrates bibliographic data on scientific publications, preprints and other research outputs • links data on: o researchers o organisations and their organisational units o research topics • allows consolidation of data from external and internal systems (at least CRIS, repositories or grant systems) • uses persistent identifiers (e.g. for authors, institutions and outputs) to ensure data clarity Data foundation The service must provide a linked data foundation that: • connects various types of research outputs, at least: o scientific publications o patents o data on research funding or grant projects o other relevant outputs (e.g. clinical studies or public policy documents) • integrates data from multiple internationally recognised sources of bibliographic, patent and grant data • allows research analysis based on multiple types of outputs and their mutual links Minimum scope of data The service must contain: • at least 80 million bibliographic records • at least 1 billion citation links • historical data coverage of at least 8 years • geographical coverage of at least 40 countries The service must cover at least these types of data: • scientific publications • patents • data on research funding or grant projects Minimum analytical dimensions The service must allow analysis at least in the dimensions of: • scientific impact • collaboration • research funding • social or technological contribution Advanced analytical functionalities The service must contain: • tools for modelling or simulating the development of research, research teams or grant success • tools for benchmarking organisations, countries or research areas AI functionalities The service must contain functionalities using artificial intelligence or advanced analytics, at least: • support for searching or creating queries in natural language • automated interpretation or summarisation of analytical outputs ...............................................................a detailed description of the subject of the contract is part of the tender documents

sig_0dede13dbac2a395a289.description: The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research. The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) requests applications for the NIAMS P30 Centers Program to support integrated research Centers within its mission areas of skin biology and diseases; bone, muscle, and orthopaedic research; and rheumatic diseases. The NIAMS P30 Centers Program supports Centers that provide coordinated research infrastructure, shared resources, and methodological expertise to advance basic, translational, and clinical research. These Centers are expected to integrate state-of-the-art research resources with capabilities that support clinical and translational research, including the development, testing, and dissemination of novel analytical methods, study designs, outcome measures, and data-driven approaches. The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research.

sig_0e2f07b22240fe5949d6.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_0e3446af9ad3836d3110.description: The subject matter of the procurement represents the hardware equipment and COTS products (licences/subscriptions), including for the security component, necessary to support (operationalise) the future ECRIS V case management system, currently under development, as well as other IT systems of the judicial system, including related ancillary services (e.g., delivery and installation of infrastructure at beneficiaries' premises, commissioning, configuration and training, technical support, warranty). Thus, within this procurement, the aim is to obtain the following deliverables:  Hardware products (equipment);  Software products (licences);  Training reports for end users regarding the administration and use of the delivered and installed systems (hardware and software). The IT&C infrastructure to be procured, under a framework agreement, will ensure the necessary requirements (both current and forecast for the 48 months of the framework agreement) of hardware equipment and COTS products (licences/subscriptions), including for the security component, with a view to supporting (operationalising) the IT systems used in the activity of the institutions in the judicial system (e.g., the ECRIS V electronic case management system, the National NGO Register, the automated court hearing transcription system – Speech2Text, the National Register for Movable Publicity / RNPM), which together require a hardware and software infrastructure appropriate to supporting them in the Justice private cloud, in accordance with current developments in the context of digital transformation, but also from the perspective of foreseeable organic growth (central/virtualisation servers, scalable technologies, high availability, increased security, etc.). The procurement involves the association formed between the MINISTRY OF JUSTICE, in its capacity as Designated Associated Contracting Authority, and the PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE AT THE HIGH COURT OF CASSATION AND JUSTICE, in its capacity as Associated Contracting Authority, in accordance with the provisions of Article 44, paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) of Law No. 98/2016, with subsequent amendments and completions. Any request for clarifications must be transmitted in SEAP (https://e-licitatie.ro/pub ). sig_0e352871b5e6b7d019f6.description: Jisc is establishing a Framework to enable it access to specialist consultants, with expertise in digital transformation, libraries and research & innovation in the UK non-profit organisation sector (tertiary education, charities, funding). Jisc consultancy supports a range of organisations through the development and implementation of digital leadership, digital transformation, and research and innovation initiatives. To enhance the delivery of these services to its members, Jisc requires external consultants to collaborate in providing strategic and operational expertise across all areas of business. Lot 1: Digital Transformation. Digital and organisational change across learning, teaching and assessment, student experience and support, training, research, knowledge management and digital and physical infrastructure. Consultancy work can help organisations with strategy development and review, organisational planning and review of systems, services, information and data management to inform investment priorities and future development. Jisc consultancy around digital transformation helps to explore and address factors such as organisational culture, digital leadership, digital capability and wellbeing, helping to create the conditions for sustainable change and enhanced business outcomes. This work will align with our Framework for digital transformation in higher education. Our digital transformation toolkit (https://www.jisc.ac.uk/taking-digital-transformation-forward-in-your-organisation/towards-digital-transformation) provides further details. Lot 2: Research and Innovation. Digital and data research infrastructure strategy and operational development in higher education and publicly funded research and related partnerships across sectors. Research management strategy and operational development in higher education and publicly funded research and related partnerships across sectors. Scholarly communications in higher education and publicly funded research and related partnerships across sectors.

sig_0e909dd6335ed6f4f36e.description:
The contracting authority is procuring 4 software for geological surveys, by lots, as follows: LOT 1. SOFTWARE FOR GEOLOGICAL MODELLING AND DEFORMATION ANALYSIS WITH CAPABILITIES FOR: 1. 2D KINEMATIC DEFORMATION ANALYSIS; 2. FAULT ANALYSIS; 3. PALEOSTRESS ANALYSIS LOT 2. SOFTWARE FOR PROCESSING AND VECTORISING REMOTE SENSING DATA LOT 3. SOFTWARE FOR VISUALISATION AND ANALYSIS OF LARGE VOLUMES OF REMOTE SENSING DATA LOT 4. SOFTWARE FOR ANALYSING DEEP BOREHOLE WELL LOG DATA The public procurement procedure is conducted as part of the project "Infrastructure Renewal and Instrument Procurement at the Croatian Geological Survey - Geoscientific Laboratories (GEOLAB)", NPOO.C3.2.R2-I2.04.0001. A detailed description of the subject of procurement is provided in the attached minimum technical specifications per procurement lot. The subject of procurement is a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, i.e. a software package for geological modelling and deformation analysis in 2D and 3D space. The software includes at least: 1. a basic module for the visualisation, editing and interpretation of stratigraphic and structural data collected at the surface, in boreholes or via remote sensing, 2. a module for 2D kinematic deformation analysis, 3. a module for fault zone analysis and 4. a module for Earth's crust stress analysis. Based on the foregoing, it is mandatory to have the capability to visualise, create and edit geological maps and profiles. The licence must include a permanent licence for at least one user via a USB hardware key or a network licence. The software must support standard data import and export formats (e.g. CSV, KMZ, 3D PDF, segy) and enable operation in an interface compatible with Windows operating systems (versions 7–11). The subject of procurement includes technical support as well as software maintenance and updates for 1 year(s) following delivery. Upon contract conclusion, the selected tenderer is obliged to provide the details of persons and contacts whom the contracting authority's representative may contact via telephone or email in the event of programme (re)installation, necessary technical support for all parts of the software, and necessary error and defect corrections in the software, for a minimum period of 1 year(s) following delivery. The contract shall be deemed fulfilled upon the expiry of the customer support period. The software shall be delivered in electronic form, i.e. online by sending a download link for the software package and installation key (as applicable) to the email address of the contracting authority's representative, or in physical form on an electronic medium to the address of the contracting authority: Hrvatski geološki institut, Sachsova ulica 2, 10000 Zagreb. All delivery costs (if applicable) are included in the price of the subject of procurement. The subject of procurement is delivered with the corresponding user manual and all accompanying original technical documentation from the manufacturer or authorised representative in Croatian or English and in the Latin script, containing instructions for installation, operation and handling, and maintenance. Successful handover implies that the subject of procurement has been delivered, which constitutes a condition for issuing and paying the invoice.; The subject of procurement is a permanent software licence for processing and vectorising remote sensing data (optical, multispectral, thermal, LiDAR and radar (SAR) imagery). The software must enable the processing, analysis and manipulation of data from these sources for the purposes of geological, hydrogeological and engineering-geological surveys. A permanent commercial licence is required that can be transferred without restriction among computers on the same network. The software is delivered in electronic form, i.e. online by sending a download link for the software package and installation key (as applicable) to the email address of the contracting authority's representative. The subject of procurement and unit price include delivery, installation and configuration of the software at the contracting authority's premises, as well as training for a duration of at least 5 day(s) of 8 hours for a maximum of 5 employees of the contracting authority, at the contracting authority's location, in Croatian or English, and upon completion of the training, a certificate or confirmation of completed training shall be issued to the trained employees of the contracting authority. The training shall be conducted by a person qualified to do so by the manufacturer or the manufacturer's authorised representative, which the contractor is obliged to prove upon the contracting authority's request during the term of the contract. The subject of procurement includes technical support as well as software maintenance and updates for 1 year(s) following delivery. Upon contract conclusion, the selected tenderer is obliged to provide the details of persons and contacts whom the contracting authority's representative may contact via telephone or email in the event of programme (re)installation, necessary technical support for all parts of the software, and necessary error and defect corrections in the software, for a minimum period of 1 year(s) following delivery. The contract shall be deemed fulfilled upon the expiry of the customer support period. The subject of procurement is delivered with the corresponding user manual and all accompanying original technical documentation from the manufacturer or authorised representative in Croatian or English and in the Latin script, containing instructions for installation, operation and handling, and maintenance. Successful handover implies that the subject of procurement has been delivered, installed and configured, and that training has been carried out, of which a handover minutes document is drawn up, signed by the representatives of the contracting authority and the contractor. Successful handover constitutes a condition for issuing and paying the invoice.; The subject of procurement is a permanent software licence for displaying and analysing large volumes of remote sensing data (optical, multispectral, thermal and LiDAR imagery), as well as other spatial data. The software must enable the display and analysis of data for the purposes of geological, hydrogeological and engineering-geological surveys. In this regard, the capability for simultaneous display of a large amount of data in high resolution in 2D and 3D view is required.

A permanent commercial licence is required that can be transferred without restriction among computers on the same network. The software is delivered in electronic form, i.e. online by sending a download link for the software package and installation key (as applicable) to the email address of the contracting authority's representative. The subject of procurement is delivered with the corresponding user manual and all accompanying original technical documentation from the manufacturer or authorised representative in Croatian or English and in the Latin script, containing instructions for installation, operation and handling, and maintenance. Successful handover constitutes a condition for issuing and paying the invoice. The selected tenderer undertakes to provide the contracting authority with customer support for a minimum of 1 (one) year(s) following installation. Customer support means free software upgrades, availability of customer support and educational materials. Upon contract conclusion, the selected tenderer is obliged to provide customer support contact persons and details. The contracting authority awards points for extended customer support duration within the framework of ENP criteria. The contract shall be deemed fulfilled upon the expiry of the customer support period.; The subject of procurement is a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, i.e. a software package for analysing deep borehole well log data. The software must enable the interpretation and integration of deep borehole well log data, data input in various formats (e.g. LAS). In addition, the software must enable the editing of well log diagrams, calculation of porosity, water saturation and shale/clay volume. The licence must be a network licensing system and must include a permanent licence for at least one user via a USB hardware key or a network licence. The software must be compatible with deep subsurface geological analysis software and enable operation in an interface compatible with Windows operating systems (versions 7–11). The software is delivered in electronic form, i.e. online by sending a download link for the software package and installation key (as applicable) to the email address of the contracting authority's representative. Installation must be accompanied by documentation containing a description and operating instructions in English or Croatian. The subject of procurement is delivered with the corresponding user manual and all accompanying original technical documentation from the manufacturer or authorised representative in Croatian or English and in the Latin script, containing instructions for installation, operation and handling, and maintenance. Successful delivery constitutes a condition for issuing and paying the invoice. The selected tenderer undertakes to provide the contracting authority with customer support for a minimum of 1 year(s) following delivery. Customer support means support during programme downloading and (re)installation via telephone or email, technical support for all parts of the software, and corrections of errors and defects in the software, as well as new software updates throughout the entire customer support period. Upon contract conclusion, the selected tenderer is obliged to provide customer support contact persons and details. The contracting authority awards points for extended customer support duration within the framework of ENP criteria. The contract shall be deemed fulfilled upon the expiry of the customer support period.

sig_0e9facaa130fd390f974.description: Works contract for the provision and operation of an administrative and action-supporting IT specialist system for Zuglói Önkormányzati Rendészet As a result of the procurement procedure, the Contracting Authority intends to use an administrative and action-supporting IT specialist system within the framework of a contractor's agreement, which on the part of the winning tenderer also covers the performance of operation and maintenance tasks. Tasks of the Contractor: A) Provision of an administrative and action-supporting IT specialist system (1 units): Requirement: - supporting the activities of public space supervisors taking action in public spaces during the performance of the Contracting Authority's tasks defined by law through the use of mobile devices (PDA, mobile printer) during all procedures placed within the competence of the Contracting Authority by law (initiation of misdemeanour, administrative, and rule-infringement procedures, complaints, documentation of warnings, as well as wheel-clamping); - ensuring data traffic related to the actions between the PDA device, the portable printer, and the Contracting Authority's command centre, duty service, and administrative system; - full-scale provision of the registration and processing workflow of the generated data in the administrative system in accordance with the technical specification, ensuring online individual and mass batch data traffic connections. The supplied system must handle data exchange via a closed server-server connection on the interface connection offered by the Ministry of Energy (and its potential successor bodies) in accordance with the relevant legislation. - supporting management and duty work by providing data related to the performance of duty, the number, status, and outcome of actions, imposed misdemeanour and administrative fines, complaints, rule-infringement procedures, warnings, and wheel-clamping. B) Training, instruction Requirement: provision of instruction regarding the use of the specialist system. The winning tenderer must provide training/refresher training opportunities once a month for a maximum of 4 hours per occasion by making available a suitably qualified specialist to instruct the Contracting Authority's new staff members and to present changes made in the specialist system. C) Operation Requirement: the winning tenderer must ensure the reliable operation of the specialist system throughout the entire duration of the contract, the investigation and documentation of the causes of operational disruptions, and their elimination - daily maintenance of the specialist system - provision of continuous, planned, and extraordinary fault repair and service activity - 24.00-hour help-desk function - 24-hour duty service. The main administrative and action areas affected by the support of the specialist system: • fining and workflow management; • wheel-clamping and workflow management; • vehicle towing and workflow management; • management and control of area occupancy permits; • pedestrian tracking. Quantities: • specialist system 1 units; • number of workstations (PC computers) connected to the specialist system: 40 units + 10% (the contracting authority provides the supplementary peripherals); • number of PDA devices and mobile printers integrated into the specialist system 18 units (+20%); • with the support of the specialist system, on an annual average - expectedly - the provision of on-site interventions (10.000 + 10% for the management of on-site fines, absentee on-site fines, administrative procedures, rule-infringement procedures and complaints, as well as warning documentation and wheel-clamping-related procedures) and the performance of administrative tasks related to the actions must be ensured. • with the support of the specialist system, the annual rate of processes to be ensured from the authentic registers of the Ministry of Energy (and its potential successor bodies) regarding national personal, residential address, and motor vehicle registers (number of queries, as well as data transfer into the misdemeanour registry system) - expectedly - 7.000 units + 20% queries, 5.000 units + 20% data transfer. The specialist system must provide the option for data querying from authentic registers using the KKSZB protocol. The following services must be available: 1. Query of vehicle data based on registration number and time 2. Personal Data and Address Registry personal search interface 4T (New NSZL LEK) 3. Query of parking permit data based on document number 4. Query of vehicle data based on chassis number 5. Query of temporary registration plate data based on registration number and time. 6. Pet register. The specialist system must be suitable for initiating a query from authentic registers also on the PDA device. The action-supporting and administrative specialist system must be completely closed and must ensure that unauthorised persons cannot access the data and processes stored in the system. Regarding the application of unfruitfulness pursuant to point b) of subsection (2) of Section 75 of the Public Procurement Act, the contracting authority records that the amount of financial cover available to it is not sufficient for concluding the contract with the tenderer that submitted the most favourable tender based on the evaluation if sixty times the offered monthly flat-rate price exceeds the amount of financial cover available to the contracting authority. Precise parameters and details of the expected performance are set out in the technical specification and the draft contract.
sig_0e9facaa130fd390f974.title: Operation of the ZÖR administrative IT specialist system

sig_0eae879ae512de7f35df.description: Tenderers are hereby invited to a market dialogue for the procurement of 2026/68199 for the procurement of an ID card for access and login to the health companies in Helse Vest. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out as the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from possible suppliers and other interested parties. It will be central to identify, among other things, how the supplier market can cover the need and relevant environmental considerations. At the same time, the contracting authority would like to make the market aware that Helse Vest is looking into future possibilities for acquiring a regional access administration system that shall collect identity and access management in a common platform. This is seen to have close connections with cards that shall be procured and it will be important to clarify the dependencies and important requirements against this so that it works together. We would like, in this market dialogue, to respond in writing to concrete questions in order to map the supplier market, environmental impact and relevant areas for the requirement specifications. It is also of interest to gain insight into important links and possibilities toward a future regional access management system. In order to limit the use of resources in the further dialogue after written responses, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to limit the number of participants who will be invited to one-to-one meetings.
sig_0eae879ae512de7f35df.title: Procurement of an ID card for access and login in Helse Vest

sig_0eb5ed4bdb218c247ddb.description: The Home Office seeks an experienced commercial provider to supply capable Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) to support the Border Security Command's (BSC) Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) operations. The RPAS must be capable of detecting, identifying, and tracking vessels and individuals within the defined area of operations, operating as part of a multi layered ISR framework that includes manned aviation, maritime assets, and land based infrastructure. The systems will provide enhanced situational awareness to inform operational decision making and support the effective tasking and coordination of operational assets The primary operational role of the RPAS will be to conduct routine surveillance missions in support of Search, Rescue and Recovery (SRR) activity. Lot 1: . The primary operational requirement is for RPAS' that can conduct routine surveillance flights to detect, track, and identify vessels and people to support the primary Search, Rescue and Recovery (SRR) Vessels within the area of operations. The SRR vessels will operate primarily within UK Territorial Waters (TTW) and the wider UK Area of Operations, including the English Channel. RPAS' information will be transmitted in real-time to an existing Command and Control facility to enable real-time coordination of responses to threats. RPAS' will also be required to perform targeted surveillance to record high-quality video footage to support Criminal and Financial Investigation (CFI) prosecutions. The Home Office have a requirement for one (1) Supplier to provide RPAS' for 5000 on-task sensor coverage hours per year, over three (3) separate task lines, for the purpose of supporting BSC operations. The Home Office requires availability of two (2) task lines to provide year-round coverage including weekends and public holidays. An additional third task line will be required for approximately six-months per year. Additional information: The contract will be for three (3) years fixed with a possible plus one (1) year extension, if mutually agreed at the time by both parties. There is a requirement for the service to be fully operational within four months of the contract being awarded (Contract Award will be on/or before 30th November 2026). There will be an expected mobilisation period starting on the 1st December 2026
sig_0eb5ed4bdb218c247ddb.title: Tactical Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPAS) System Managed Service
