sig_0ecc13967a879f6c7e88.description: The Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Handwerk und Tourismus Baden-Württemberg is awarding a framework agreement for project management to implement measures in the field of innovation promotion. The project manager is to be commissioned with the conception and overall handling of corresponding funding programmes. Baden-Württemberg is one of the most innovative regions in Europe. The state's export-oriented economy can only be and remain successful on world markets with technologically and qualitatively high-quality products, production processes and services. Therefore, considerable efforts are necessary in the areas of research, development and innovation, including technology transfer. A decisive factor here is the ability of companies to develop new technologies themselves or to adapt them to market requirements, and to convert research results into marketable products and services as quickly as possible in order to then market them successfully. Other decisive factors in international location competition are a high-performance research infrastructure, close networking between business and science, a qualified supply of skilled workers and suitable financing options. In Baden-Württemberg, research and innovation funding has been an essential core component of economic and medium-sized business policy for many years. In order to sustainably strengthen the innovative capacity of the Baden-Württemberg economy, and in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, various funding measures are being implemented to strengthen industry-related research and knowledge and technology transfer. Against the background of the current challenges for the economy due to increasing digitalisation and structural change in the state, the innovation and business location is to be targetedly supported in the future with various application-oriented funding measures. Against this background, the Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Handwerk und Tourismus Baden-Württemberg intends to conclude a framework agreement for project management to implement measures in the field of innovation promotion. The project manager is to be commissioned with the conception and overall handling of corresponding funding programmes. This includes in particular the following points: - Conception of new funding formats to support technology transfer and innovation ecosystems as well as to promote research and development in key technologies. Participation in the communication of activities and results. - Professional and content-related support as well as assistance in the preparation of calls for proposals and individual company funding programmes, including the corresponding funding guidelines in the field of innovation and technology. The issuing or publication of the corresponding programmes and calls for proposals is carried out by the Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Handwerk und Tourismus Baden-Württemberg, if necessary in coordination with other state ministries. - Preparation of the forms and templates required for programme processing, including the provision of a technical infrastructure required for legally secure electronic programme processing (IT procedures, databases, etc.), digital, media-consistent and accessible implementation in accordance with the requirements of budgetary law (LHO Baden-Württemberg). - Information and advice for funding prospects and applicants. - Legally secure design and high-quality implementation of assessment and selection processes in various technology areas. - Administrative implementation of project funding, including final application review and approval or rejection. - Handling of funding procedures under grant law after approval, including fund management, disbursement of funding, monitoring of use, including verification of proof of use and documentation of audit results, if necessary carrying out objection, withdrawal and revocation as well as recovery procedures, including calculation and assessment of interest, if necessary first-instance legal proceedings. - Administrative and professional support and accompaniment of funded projects, including answering queries and processing amendment applications. - Ongoing reporting to the client, including recording, processing and evaluation of programme-specific key figures and statistical data (monitoring). If necessary, conception and implementation of a scientific evaluation process. Since the project manager is to act in a sovereign capacity, the project manager is entrusted with sovereign tasks in accordance with § 44 para. 3 LHO. The contractor is bound by the guidelines and instructions of the client within the scope of the order; the technical supervision for the activity lies with the Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Handwerk und Tourismus Baden-Württemberg.

sig_0ecf3f0ae5930329bd86.description: UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. Lot 1: . University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, "UCLH", is one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom and provides first-class acute and specialist services. UCLH comprises of the following hospitals: University College Hospital, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing, MacMillan Cancer Centre, University College Hospital Grafton Way Building, University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street, Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine, and the Institute of Sport, Exercise and Health. UCLH delivers world class cancer care to patients from across the country. Cancer at UCLH spans across multiple sites and departments within the Trust and has included the opening of the Grafton Way Building one of two national Proton Beam Therapy services in December 2021. UCLH is a lead provider within the North Central London Cancer Alliance, as well as providing tertiary services for wider patient populations in specialist services, such as sarcoma for patients from across South East England. In early 2020, UCLH was selected by NHS England as the preferred tertiary cancer provider to take over management of the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre. This transition is subject to a due diligence process during which UCLH are providing transitional support to the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre team, building upon a number of years of collaborative working between the two services. Our Radiotherapy department offers cutting edge and specialised therapy to adult and paediatric patients treating over 2400 new patients a year. UCLH Radiotherapy is a national leader in complex/highly technical radiotherapy in: • Brain and was recently designated a Tessa Jowell Brain Cancer Centre of Excellence • Paediatrics, with the largest paediatric radiotherapy unit in the UK • Sarcomas - one of Europe’s largest service • Head and Neck – (ENT) third largest in the UK • Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR) • Haematological including total body radiation • Brachytherapy • Molecular Radiotherapy - National Referral centre (Paediatric, TYA and adult). The department works closely with a number of specialist hospitals to support cancer pathways which span multiple centres including Great Ormond Street, St. Mary's, Oxford, Southampton and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital. The UCH radiotherapy department contains six bunkers with four Varian TrueBeams and one Varian Halcyon. There is a large difference between the national and UCLH complexity profile, 92% of the UCH workload is classed as complex and approximately 8% of the workload is paediatric. The radiotherapy service is delivered by a team of staff including clinical oncologists, radiotherapy physics and engineers, therapeutic radiographers, healthcare play specialists, admin and clerical staff and dedicated nurses. UCLH is also one of two national Proton Beam Therapy centres, providing services to patients from the south of the UK. The departments run an integrated workforce model, with physicists, dosimetrists and radiographers rotating across Radiotherapy and PBT. In total there are around 300 WT across both services. UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. This could include but is not limited to: • Delivering Cancer Waiting Time Access standards. • Scheduling of patients. • Machine downtime. • Patient pathway and organisation of workflow. • Radiotherapy physics pathways. • Process for commissioning of new linacs. • Use of automation and AI. Expression of Interest The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to engage with potential partners to gather information and insights from the market to aid the development of the requirements and scope of opportunities for efficiencies to inform the procurement of a transformation partner. Suppliers are requested to provide expressions of interest, including responses to the below questions by e-mail to steviejay.cavanagh@nhs.net by 15:00 on 26th September 2025. 1. What innovative or new ways of working are you currently seeing in the market that may benefit the NHS, and more specifically UCLH, including those that have been included in procurements over the past 12 months? 2. Please describe how you think this contract should be best structured to deliver an efficient Radiotherapy service? 3. Is there anything you think that the Trust should consider before going out to market for these services? 4. What would be your expectations from a partnership with an NHS organisation? This notice does not constitute a formal call for competition. sig_0ed16ea9aef8b6890e36.description: The Universitätsklinikum Münster (UKM) intends to further develop its clinical capacity planning and operational capacity management. The sought-after digital solution should in particular be able to consolidate relevant capacity and patient flow data and make it usable for operational management. This includes in particular information on current and planned admissions, elective and unplanned patient flows, occupancy and available bed capacities, planned discharges, surgical and treatment capacities, as well as available staff capacities. On this basis, current situations should be presented transparently, future capacity trends forecast, and potential over- or undercapacities identified at an early stage. The information should be available in suitable, user-oriented dashboards for operational management and coordination formats. Cross-departmental consideration is of particular importance. Capacities should not be optimised exclusively within individual clinics, wards or occupational groups. Rather, the solution should map the mutual dependencies of patient volumes, surgical and treatment planning, inpatient capacities, human resources and, where applicable, further resources, and support coordinated operational management. The explicit aim is not merely to maximise utilisation, but to achieve a more reliable, predictive and, as far as possible, disruption-free use of available resources. For data provision, the interface connection to the ORBIS hospital information system used at the UKM is initially of particular relevance. Prospectively, further data sources, in particular from personnel and roster planning, should be able to be integrated. Tenderers are requested to present which standardised interfaces and integration options are supported and what data quality or data availability is required for productive use. The objective of the market sounding explicitly goes beyond the provision and technical implementation of software. The UKM regards the introduction of integrated capacity management as an organisational and change project whose technical component represents an essential, but not the sole, element. The tenderer should therefore be in a position to substantially design and accompany the change and transformation process associated with the introduction. Support is expected in particular in the analysis of existing planning and control processes, the development of a shared target vision, the definition of suitable control processes and decision-making rules, as well as the clarification of roles, responsibilities and governance structures. Relevant clinical, nursing, administrative and technical stakeholders should also be systematically involved in the development and implementation. The services should also include suitable communication, training and enablement measures, including support in day-to-day operations. The aim of this change process is in particular the development of a shared management culture with greater transparency, cross-departmental cooperation and clear shared responsibility for existing capacities. The technical solution and organisational transformation should therefore be methodically and temporally interlinked. Tenderers are sought who can provide both components from a single source or under a bindingly integrated overall responsibility. The introduction is to take place initially in selected clinical areas as part of a pilot phase. Both the technical usability and data integration and the practical effectiveness of the new planning and control processes, as well as their acceptance within the organisation, are to be evaluated. The solution must in principle be suitable for subsequent step-by-step scaling to further clinical areas and, prospectively, to the entire University Hospital. As part of the market sounding, the UKM asks interested tenderers to provide a brief presentation on the following points: 1) Description of the offered solution and the essential functions for operational and prospective capacity management, including forecasting, analysis and visualisation functions; description of the supported data sources, interfaces, hosting and operating models, as well as the technical prerequisites for integration into an existing hospital IT landscape. 2) Description of the methodological approach for implementation and piloting, including typical project phases, time required, required resources on the tenderer and client side, and possibilities for subsequent scaling to further areas or an overall hospital. 3) Presentation of the offered change management and transformation approach, in particular regarding process analysis and redesign, roles and responsibilities, governance, stakeholder involvement, communication, training, employee enablement, and sustainable organisational anchoring. 4) References from hospitals of comparable size and complexity, preferably university hospitals or maximum-care providers, where both digital capacity management and the associated organisational change have been implemented. 5) Non-binding details on potential licence, implementation, integration, consulting and ongoing operating costs, as well as common contract and licence models. Please send your expression of interest to: vvgm@ukmuenster.de

sig_0ed2d1e215db95e7dedd.description: Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue uses the Clausion Financial Performance Management (also system) financial planning system. Meidän IT ja Talous Oy (Meita) has put out to tender a financial planning system as a procurement procedure in accordance with the Act on Public Contracts and Concession Contracts (1397/2016, Procurement Act), on the basis of which insightsoftware Finland Oy has been selected as the system supplier. Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue has made significant investments in the implementation and development of the current system, which is at the beginning of its life cycle, starting from 2023, as a result of which the system has become an integral part of the operating environment, has increased supplier-specific know-how and contains interoperability requirements with other systems. Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue procured the system from Meita by a decision of the provisional preparation body of Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue based on an in-house entity position in accordance with section 18.01.2022 subsection 6 of the Procurement Act. With the reform of the Procurement Act, the in-house entity position ceases to exist. The procurement procedure is implemented as a direct procurement in accordance with section 40 of the Procurement Act, in which the contracting authority negotiates the terms of the procurement contract with the supplier of its choice without publishing a procurement notice in advance. The ground for the direct procurement is the ground in accordance with section 40 subsection 2 point 2 of the Procurement Act: for technical reasons or reasons connected with the protection of an exclusive right, only a certain supplier can implement the procurement; an additional condition is that there are no reasonable alternative or replacement solutions and the absence of competition is not due to an artificial narrowing of the procurement conditions. Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue has used a significant amount of resources to develop the current system. Through the development work, the current system supplier's know-how regarding the special needs of the wellbeing services county has been increased in order to make the system meet the required performance level. Achieving the required performance level for a new system would require the contracting authority to use a significant amount of resources, which the wellbeing services county does not have available for system development. For the aforementioned reasons, there are no reasonable alternative solutions. In accordance with section 2 subsection 2 of the Procurement Act, contracting authorities must strive to organise their procurement activities in such a way that procurements can be implemented as economically, qualitatively and systematically as possible. In addition, the section requires taking advantage of existing competitive conditions, which were taken into account in Meita's original tendering. Päijät-Hämeen hyvinvointialue has negotiated with Meita and insightsoftware Finland Oy regarding the procurement of the current system environment and the continuation of use.
sig_0ed2d1e215db95e7dedd.title: Direct procurement of financial planning system

sig_0f15f690a6a1f19f021a.description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

sig_0f53a03dbad4c54b0407.description: The purpose of this contract is the SERVICES FOR THE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEM (CoVA) APPLIED TO INTERGENERATIONAL ASSISTANCE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ASTURIAS which enables a proactive and efficient administration, covering both processes and people and the technology necessary for its proper use, security and management. This contract is part of Public Procurement of Innovative Technology (CPTI), its purpose has an innovative content and employs functional specifications, rather than technical requirements: It is aimed at the acquisition of a service that does not exist in the Principality of Asturias, but can be developed in a reasonable time, given that the technology is at a degree of development that allows it to do so. The main tasks included in this contract are the following: a. Implementation of a virtual agent coordination system based on artificial intelligence applied to intergenerational assistance for the Administration of the Principality of Asturias that allows the exploitation of the data generated and managed. b. All services necessary for the commissioning of the contracted elements, necessary subscriptions/licences, as well as their management and maintenance during the pilot demonstration phase. c. The exploitation of the potential of the data of the Administration of the Principality of Asturias (hereinafter, APA) to implement new forms of public management based on interoperability and data analytics. d. Establish the technological and procedural bases for the implementation of a proactive administration that allows the optimisation of public expenditure while maximising its performance. e. The development of techniques/rules for the automated management and classification of data, documents and files using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques. f. The incorporation of deep learning techniques since these digitalisation processes can produce immense amounts of data for training and thus be able to provide processing that increases efficiency, effectiveness and intelligence in the processing of data in the processes of Public Administrations. g. The creation of a corporate data space that includes origin data, those that may have been inferred during the scope of use of the system, as well as facilitating interoperability and administrative processing circuits. h. Creation of a proactive care and assistance environment with citizens. i. Creation of a specialised sandbox that serves as an ideation and experimentation environment. j. Integration with the APA's electronic file processing system (SITE), and other applications and systems indicated in these specifications. k. Ensuring the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain, for which measures will be implemented to guarantee the integrity and security of the artificial intelligence models at all stages, components and data used, with strict legal compliance with EU Regulation 2024/1689, and compliance with the decree 98/2025 regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the Administration of the Principality of Asturias.

sig_0f56c5668e9676b95423.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A REQUEST FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET CONSULTATION AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. The procurement entity HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also referred to as the contracting authority) is using this information request to survey the market to support the planning of a potential readiness communication and alert system procurement carried out as a joint procurement (possibly on a Uusimaa regional co-operation area scale). The purpose of the information request is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The aim is to obtain information on, among other things, various solutions, functionalities, pricing models, and the boundary conditions for a potential joint procurement. The details of the joint procurement will be specified later as the procurement preparation progresses. Preliminary objectives of the procurement: The entity under review may consist of one or more parts. Potential use cases include, among others: - critical 2-way alerting and communication as well as video conferencing - regional communication crossing organisational boundaries - workstation messaging and operational communication - situational picture collection and reporting (collection also from actors outside the organisation) - call-outs for work and resource alerts - lone worker safety - browser-based notifications. The solution must take into account multiple communication channels (mobile, SMS, workstations), the information security and operational reliability requirements of the authorities' environment, and integration with other systems. Key themes of the market consultation: - operational reliability and usability in disruption situations - scalability of user numbers - suitability of the joint procurement model - pricing models and potential add-ons - integrations and interfaces - information security, data protection, and the location of the server infrastructure - key benefits and risks (e.g. vendor lock-in). RESPONDING TO THE INFORMATION REQUEST AND MARKET DIALOGUE We kindly ask suppliers interested in the procurement to describe the solutions you offer, taking into account the procurement objectives and themes mentioned above. If you wish, you can also attach brochures or other information about your offered products and services to your response. Please submit responses to the information request by 25.3.2026 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message should state "HUS 105-2026 - Readiness communication and alert system". The contracting authority may, at its discretion, propose clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have responded to this information request. The responses provided may be utilised in the further preparation of the procurement, potential market dialogue, and requirement definition. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. INFORMATION ON THE PROCEDURE The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the information request; instead, a potential contract notice and request for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The contracting authority tentatively plans to publish the request for tenders during the year 2026.

The Customer is the Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (the ”Customer”) . In this capacity, the Customer provides the Solution to the Ministry, and the Supplier is a sub-Supplier to the Customer for this purpose. Under the terms of the Contract, the Supplier shall establish, operate and maintain the Solution and provide related auxiliary services. The Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (DMFA) comprises the Ministry in Copenhagen and a global network abroad of Embassies, Consulates-General and Trade Commissions. Denmark has 67 Embassies. An Embassy handles all aspects of Denmark’s ties with the host country and many Embassies cover several countries. The number and location of Embassies is reviewed and prioritized on an ongoing basis according to Denmark’s foreign policy interests. Denmark has Ambassadors in virtually every European country, in most large countries outside Europe, and in developing countries where we are partners in the country’s development. Denmark has 6 diplomatic missions at international organizations, for example at the EU in Brussels, at the UN in New York and Geneva, at NATO in Brussels, and at the Council of Europe in Strasbourg. Denmark has 17 Consulates-General and Trade Commissions. These provide first and foremost commercial services and are in areas where Denmark has significant commercial interests. We have, for example, Consulates-General in New York and Shanghai, and Trade Commission in Taipei. The Solution is used for administrative data traffic, including office and journal systems, electronic mail, intranet, internet, IT administration and collaboration services between the Missions and the Ministry. The Solution is an essential tool for the Ministry and its routines and working procedures, which require that all communication at all times is secret, secure, reliable and at high speed. The security requirements are continuously adjusted by the DMFA in accordance with the political and security related matters concerning Denmark. This includes the physical security and access control as well as the consideration for the high level of protection of data transmissions and information integrity, which might be important to Denmark’s image as a trustworthy international partner, and at worst national security. For more information about DMFA see https://um.dk/en and the Customer see https://statens-it.dk/english/.

sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.description: The Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for research on the impact of technology and digital media on children and adolescents. Technology and digital media (TDM) encompasses social media, applications, websites, television, motion pictures, artificial intelligence, mobile devices, computers, video games, virtual and augmented reality, and other content, networks, or platforms disseminated through the internet, broadcasted, or other media technologies, as applicable. Collectively, they have become an integral part of our children’s and families’ daily lives. Most children and adolescents now engage with TDM starting from an early age, often with high levels of exposure across multiple devices and contexts and involving a wide range of content. There is therefore an urgent need to understand how TDM use and exposure impacts children’s health and development, as well as how it alters the very nature of interactions between children and their family members, peers, and society at large. As TDM has evolved with breathtaking speed, our understanding of its impacts – whether positive, neutral, or negative – on children’s health and development has not kept pace. This initiative intends to address this expanding gap by inviting research proposals on the impact of TDM on children and adolescents, including potential broader effects on their families and communities. Please note that applications are not being solicited at this time . This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize a phased R61/R33 mechanism. Investigators with interests at the intersection of TDM and child/adolescent development are encouraged to apply. In addition, collaborative teams that combine expertise across domains such as behavioral sciences, cognition and learning, computational and statistical modeling, computer science, geographic information science, library and information sciences, neurodevelopment, pediatrics, social and affective development and social sciences will be encouraged, and these investigators should also consider applying for this opportunity.
sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.title: Notice of Intent to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Impact of Technology and Digital Media Exposure Usage on Child and Adolescent Development

sig_0f68a6f5d8c0a8a88d05.description: Asker municipality would like to invite suppliers of the geographical information system (GIS) to a dialogue. Asker municipality currently has Askerkart for executive officers and residents. Askerkart is a web-based map system, but in connection with the current system supplier having notified transition to cloud, the municipality wants to update itself on the market situation and the different possibilities that exist. The dialogue meetings will be held in Asker municipality ́s premises in the period 3.11-7. 11.2025. The GIS tool shall be able to support the municipality ́s work with knowledge based decisions. It shall be a map solution for case handling in accordance with the Planning and Building Act and other legislation, at the same time that the system should be able to give inhabitants access to relevant information from the same knowledge basis. We would like the map system to be easy to administer and it has a user friendly interface. We would like tenderers to give a general system demonstration so that we can get an understanding of whether this will fit into Asker municipality ́s ICT architecture/portfolio. We want the demo to say something about: • User administration of the system • Inhabitant services • 3D display in the system. • Analysing and reporting possibilities • data flow and possible system integrations • How the system itself is administered - what can we do ourselves Each tenderer can have up to three persons with good competence in the system. Asker municipality will provide an ICT consultant, as well as three representatives from the department Analyse og Geodata. Business sensitive information that is shared in the individual meetings will be handled confidentially. Tenderers wishing to participate can register their interest by email to elfrid.nygaard.stabellini@asker.kommune.no and at the same time state the preferred date for holding the meeting (03.11, 04.11, 05.11, 06.11 or 07.11). Any questions to the market dialogue can also be directed here and will be answered continuously. The registration deadline is 31.10.2025 Agenda for the dialogue meeting: 1. Presentation of meeting participants and cards on the municipality ́s need for a GIS tool. 2. General demo of the supplier ́s system. Documentation that shall be submitted after the dialogue meeting (deadline: 14.11.2025) 1. Presentation from the dialogue meeting. 2. Three reference customers with an equivalent system (with contact information). 3. Upper and lower price estimates for licences/subscriptions, rolling out and training per annum, including support. The estimates are not binding.

NAK – National IT network development: Supplementary network equipment, as well as related operational and installation services. The procurement includes the supply of supplementary equipment for the IT network, which operates as an integrated part of the Contracting Authority's nationwide inhomogeneous equipment fleet, the installation and commissioning of active and passive network equipment, as well as the provision of operational and support services, and the performance of on-demand network development services in the form of a framework agreement. The Contracting Authority aims to establish and operate an integrated, unified, quality-assured network infrastructure at approximately 200 sites nationwide. The list of the Contracting Authority's sites to which this procurement procedure applies is contained in point VI.). (Hereinafter: sites). The procurement includes, among other things, the supply of equipment necessary for the physical construction of the IT network at the listed sites and the construction of the physical IT network, the commissioning of active and passive network equipment and the related logistical tasks, as well as the technical documentation of the completed tasks. The Contracting Authority shall provide for the procurement of active equipment to be installed in the national IT network, outside the scope of this procurement. The product categories of the equipment procured by the Contracting Authority are contained in Table No. 3. of point II.4.3.) of the technical specification. The storage location for equipment belonging to the product categories according to Table No. 3. of point II.4.3.) is the IT warehouse located at the Contracting Authority's headquarters. It is the Contractor's task to deliver these devices from the Contracting Authority's headquarters to the site – depending on the client's requirements – (logistical task), to install and commission the devices (putting into operation), and, if required, to return unused network equipment to the Contracting Authority's headquarters. The supply of network supplementary equipment necessary for the installation and commissioning of the devices within the framework of this procurement is the Contractor's task. The supplementary network equipment – which, among other things, is the subject of this procurement – is contained in Tables No. 1. and 2 of point II.4.2.). Furthermore, it is the Contractor's task – upon order – to perform services supporting operation, which means, on the one hand, a logistical task (e.g., equipment must be relocated due to a site move), and on the other hand, configuration and troubleshooting tasks related to operation. The Contractor shall prepare technical documentation for the work performed (which is part of the task). This technical specification was prepared with reference to Keline products. The Contracting Authority also accepts offers equivalent to the products specified in the technical specification. The Contracting Authority determines equivalence by taking into account the technical and functional parameters defined in the Technical Specification. If tenderers offer an equivalent product, the data necessary for the clear identification of the product (manufacturer, part number, product name) and the description of the technical and functional properties necessary for assessing equivalence (at least a technical data sheet or its availability) must be attached to the tender. In the case of offering an equivalent product, the tenderer must possess a manufacturer qualification equivalent to Certified Keline installer and/or Certified Keline designer and/or Certified Keline distributor (https://www.keline.eu/a/24/keline-partner-program). The manufacturer shall provide a long-term manufacturer's warranty of at least 5 years for the entire built system and the components used. Following this performance, documentation issued and verified by the manufacturer must certify this. The certification must be site-specific. The Tenderer must declare in the procedure that the warranty provided by them complies with the conditions prescribed in this point. The contract must be performed throughout the country. The detailed conditions for the performance of the contract are contained in the technical specification and the draft contract. sig_100934a7d636cf3be09a.description: The Development Bank of Wales (DBW) is seeking to establish a Framework Agreement for the provision of training, coaching and development services to support the learning and development needs of its employees. The framework will provide access to suitably qualified and experienced suppliers capable of delivering a broad range of professional development services, including leadership and management development, procurement and commercial skills, finance, risk and compliance, project management, coaching and mentoring, digital and technology skills, personal effectiveness, and other specialist training requirements. Through this procurement, DBW aims to appoint a panel of providers who can deliver high-quality, flexible and value-for-money learning solutions across a range of delivery methods, including classroom-based, virtual and blended learning. Tenderers may apply for one, some or multiple disciplines within a Lot. Tenderers are not required to demonstrate capability across all disciplines contained within a Lot. Additional questions within the eTenderWales portal will require Tenderers to identify the specific discipline(s) for which they are submitting a Tender. The framework will support DBW's strategic objectives by enhancing workforce capability, supporting organisational development and ensuring employees have access to relevant and effective learning opportunities. Further details of the scope, lot structure, evaluation methodology and framework arrangements are set out within the procurement documents. The framework is expected to be divided into lots to reflect different areas of expertise. The Development Bank of Wales does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work under the framework. Contracts will be awarded in accordance with the call-off procedures set out in the procurement documents. Services may include training programmes, workshops, masterclasses, briefings, coaching, mentoring, facilitation, training needs analysis, learner diagnostics, preparation of learning materials, post-course evaluation and associated reporting. Delivery may be in person, virtual or blended, depending on the requirement, audience and relevant lot. The framework will be divided into lots covering leadership and management development; procurement, commercial and contract management; financial services, risk and regulatory training; digital, technology and AI skills; project and change management; HR, equality, diversity and inclusion; health, safety and wellbeing; Welsh language and communication skills; coaching and mentoring; and soft skills and business development. The framework will not guarantee any minimum level of spend, volume of work or number of call-off contracts. Requirements will be commissioned through the framework call-off arrangements and will be subject to business need, budget availability, approval requirements and supplier performance. The tender code for etenderwales is itt_127450 Strategic Approach to Supplier Appointment In order to maximise competition, improve resilience of supply and provide access to a diverse range of specialist providers, DBW has structured this Framework to allow Tenderers to bid for individual disciplines within each Lot. DBW's approach is intended to support participation from SMEs, micro-businesses, specialist providers and Welsh suppliers who may possess expertise in specific disciplines rather than across all service areas within a Lot. To ensure continuity of service, competitive tension and sufficient market capacity throughout the term of the Framework Agreement, DBW intends to appoint a minimum of two (2) suppliers and a maximum of four (4) suppliers per discipline within each Lot, subject to a sufficient number of Tenderers meeting the Conditions of Participation and achieving the minimum required evaluation standards. Where fewer than two compliant Tenderers are received for a particular discipline, DBW reserves the right to proceed with the available compliant Tenderer(s) or take such other action as it considers appropriate in accordance with the procurement documents. The overall maximum number of suppliers that may be appointed across all Lots and disciplines under the Framework Agreement is 314. This figure represents the total maximum framework capacity and should not be interpreted as the number of suppliers to be appointed to any individual Lot or discipline. This approach is intended to: maintain value for money through ongoing competition at call-off; reduce dependency on individual suppliers; provide flexibility to meet varying business requirements; encourage participation from specialist providers; improve resilience and continuity of service provision; and support DBW's objective of creating a broad and diverse supplier base capable of delivering high-quality training, coaching and development services. Lot 1: Leadership and Management Development. Provision of leadership and management development services, including training, workshops, programmes, coaching support, facilitated sessions and practical tools to develop current and aspiring managers, senior leaders and team leaders. Services may cover people management, performance management, strategic leadership, culture, change leadership, communication, decision-making, resilience and inclusive leadership. Lot 2: Procurement, Commercial and Contract Management. Provision of procurement, commercial and contract management training and development services. Services may include training on procurement legislation, procurement planning, tendering, evaluation, supplier management, contract management, commercial risk, negotiation, governance, transparency, social value and practical procurement processes relevant to DBW’s operating environment. Lot 3: Financial Services, Risk and Regulatory Training. Provision of financial services, risk, compliance and regulatory training. Services may include technical and practical training on financial services regulation, credit risk, investment risk, operational risk, fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, conduct, governance, assurance, financial crime, data protection, regulatory change and other specialist topics relevant to DBW’s activities. Lot 4: Digital, Technology and AI Skills. Provision of digital, technology and AI skills training to support staff confidence and capability. Services may include training on Microsoft 365 tools, digital productivity, data literacy, cyber awareness, artificial intelligence, automation, digital transformation, accessibility in digital tools and practical use of technology in a professional services environment. Lot 5: Project and Change Management. Provision of project management, programme management and change management training and development services. Services may include training on project planning, governance, delivery methods, risk and issue management, benefits realisation, stakeholder engagement, communication planning, change readiness, adoption and practical delivery of organisational change. Lot 6: HR, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion. Provision of HR-related, equality, diversity and inclusion training. Services may include training on employment-related people practices, inclusive workplaces, dignity at work, unconscious bias, equality duties, reasonable adjustments, recruitment and selection, employee relations, wellbeing conversations, policy implementation and inclusive management practices. Lot 7: Health, Safety and Wellbeing. Provision of health, safety and wellbeing training and development services. Services may include statutory or good-practice health and safety training, mental health awareness, wellbeing, resilience, stress management, workplace safety, first aid-related awareness, risk awareness, personal safety and practical support for safe and healthy working practices. Lot 8: Welsh Language and Communication Skills. Provision of Welsh language and communication skills training. Services may include Welsh language learning, confidence-building, workplace Welsh, bilingual customer or stakeholder communication, plain English, written communication, presentation skills, report writing, influencing skills and communication tailored to DBW’s internal and external audiences. Lot 9: Coaching and Mentoring Services. Provision of coaching and mentoring services for individuals, groups, managers and senior leaders. Services may include executive coaching, leadership coaching, career coaching, mentoring support, group coaching, action learning, coaching for change, coaching for performance and development-focused support linked to agreed outcomes. Lot 10: Soft Skills and Business Development. Provision of soft skills and business development training. Services may include training on communication, collaboration, confidence, negotiation, influencing, customer service, stakeholder management, time management, presentation skills, problem solving, decision-making, personal effectiveness and wider professional development skills.

sig_1020b371ff9781d06756.description: Science IT is responsible for the operation of the ScienceCloud and ScienceCluster. The Team needs professional consulting support for the opensource technology OpenStack and CephFS. The University of Zurich (UZH) invites tenders for the following reasons: Expiring support contract with current consultant Science IT already had a support contract with a provider (StackHPC) for the OpenStack platform in the past. This needs to be renewed for the next 5 years. This is a suitable opportunity to redefine the desired support services, familiarise with other providers and obtain prices in line with the market. Enlarge support to also cover CephFS Science IT has experienced two major incidents last year on CephFS with a total downtime of the whole ScienceCluster service for several weeks. Therefore, Science IT is looking for a strong partner with lots of experience in CephFS to provide 3rd level support as well as consulting service to stabilize the platform. Two long-serving employees have left the team Two experienced employees with in-depth knowledge of CephFS and OpenStack have left the Science IT team. Over the next two years, the knowledge in the team will be built up again. This will require a targeted transfer of expertise from an experienced partner to the employees of Science IT. Therefore, with this tender, Science IT is looking for experienced partners for the support of OpenStack and CephFS. The cooperation with an experienced provider should achieve the following goals: * In the event of a disaster, Science IT receives professional support for OpenStack and CephFS on the next business day at the latest. * Employees will be able to benefit from the provider's expertise in the coming years. The provider also employs staff who are actively involved in CephFS and OpenStack as contributors. Using the provider's documentation on the UZH platform, the team will be enabled to solve problems independently. * Updates or upgrades can be planned and implemented together so that the platform is always operated at the second latest technical level. * Conceptual adjustments to the platform can be discussed with an experienced partner. They challenge internal employees so that the right solution is implemented for UZH. For the operation of ScienceCloud and ScienceCluster CephFS is key technology. With lot 2 the UZH is seeking for the following services. * Third level support: Support requests should be answered on the next business day, work is carried out during business hours, support is provided by arrangement * Disaster support: Support requests should be answered on the next business day, work is carried out during business hours and at weekends, support is immediate * Annual update support: The provider plans to carry out the update together with Science IT once a year. * Know-how transfer: The provider documents the platform on an ongoing basis and discusses the adjustments with internal employees * Initial project, ramp-up: The provider and the Science IT team discuss the status of the platform and possible conceptual adjustments to optimise the platform that may be needed to enable the provider to fulfil above requirements. These are then implemented together.

sig_102cbcbe68334930801c.description: This is a Prior Information Notice (PIN) with the purpose of assisting the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) in engaging the market by gathering information. This PIN has the purpose of a fact-finding exercise and only. Background Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) are exploring options to digitalise payments out of the Agency in a bid to reduce payable orders. A specific user case includes invoice-based payments. Invoices are returned with information to support a customer’s application. These applications, information and invoices are currently paper based which are scanned and digitalised in-house. On receipt of the information and sufficient checks, a payment is made by payable order to those named on the invoice. The payable order process is also managed in-house and posted from DVLA. Volumes In this example, for the financial year 2025-26, 221,406 individual payable orders were issued, with a net value of approximately £14.8M. Considerations • The payments are made to anyone qualified to complete the supporting evidence, so there is no static list of payees. There could be around 60,000 individual payees which fluctuates. Some are repeat payees and some are one off payees. • The payees include individuals and company accounts from across the UK. • The invoices (currently paper based) include the payee bank information (account number, sort code). • The invoices are then scanned and a digital copy held. • As a Government Agency we are required to follow all HM Treasury guidance outlined in the ‘Managing Public Money’ published documentation. • This includes not being able to use intermediary bank accounts outside of the Exchequer pyramid. • DVLA do not have an existing BACs business as usual process for payments out. • DVLA has explored Open Banking for this user case and feel that due to the considerations above it doesn’t fully meet our requirements. Project aims • Digitalise movement of funds • Reduce/remove payable orders • Improve invoice management processes • Improve customer experience Information required • Potential solutions to support the project aims aligned to the considerations • Any costs associated with developing and implementing the solution including any licences or additional external costs. • Any ongoing costs associated with ongoing running of the solution. • Time taken to develop and implement the solution. • Any wider considerations, fees or any other supporting information. • Do you provide this type of service for any other large organisations? • How can DVLA procure from your organisation? e.g. Are they on a framework? If so which one? Do we need to go through any third parties to obtain their services? Please provide a response via email to the above question to Michelle Palmer - Michelle.Palmer@dvla.gov.uk by 5pm on May 13th 2026 Lot 1: . This is a Prior Information Notice (PIN) with the purpose of assisting the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) in engaging the market by gathering information. This PIN has the purpose of a fact-finding exercise and only.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. ANNUAL REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS: Potential offerors are notified that effective 01 Jan 2005 to be eligible for an award and in compliance with FAR 52.204-7 and DFARS 252.204-7007 Alternate A, they must submit Annual Representations and Certifications, via SAM.gov. Before submitting the electronic Annual Representations and Certifications, Contractors must be registered in the SAM Database. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. ESTIMATED PROGRAM COST: Anticipated funding for the program (not per Call, contract, or award): FY24 FY25 FY26 FY27 FY28 TOTAL $100M $100M $100M $100M $99M $499M This funding profile is an estimate only and will not be a contractual obligation for funding. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). It is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all the Offeror’s data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. POINT OF CONTACT: a) Administrative, technical, or contractual questions should be sent via e-mail to afrl.rdlb.tacticalbaa@us.af.mil. All requests must include a name, e-mail address, and phone number of an organizational point of contact. b) Each Call will include specific contracting points of contact. The revised paragraph is as follows: 9) Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors are notified that subsequent Call Announcements shall include a requirement for submission of the documents identified below. Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. Additionally, the purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Government Furnished Property Clause list in Section I paragraph 10 (formerly Section I paragraph 9) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. sig_1083b97d32e617e97520.description: As a federal company, Toll Collect organises toll collection in Germany and operates one of the largest satellite-based toll systems in the world, which we are also opening up to private toll service providers. Furthermore, in the interest of the Federal Government, Toll Collect undertakes a wide range of tasks for the intelligent management of traffic. These include the provision of digital platforms on which all participants can work together smoothly. In addition, Toll Collect uses its extensive technology expertise to advise its customers and, together with them, combines ideas and services into an overall solution tailored to their needs. Furthermore, Toll Collect operates and develops extensive IT systems from A to Z: agile, data protection-compliant and reliable. Toll Collect creates added value for society. We analyse data from the toll system that enables efficient and sustainable traffic management. We make the transport infrastructure more efficient and increase traffic safety. We improve publicly available map material and provide open data for third parties. We support the Federal Government in achieving its ambitious climate targets. The Toll Collect GmbH is based in Berlin and employs around 700 staff. Toll Collect operates several hundred control devices - including control gantries, control columns as well as mobile and portable systems - which automatically capture, evaluate and assess vehicle data and vehicle images. Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) plays an essential role in this: official number plates of the checked vehicles are recognised from the vehicle images and the country of origin is determined. This forms an important basis for toll and traffic safety control, particularly for data allocation from various data sources. Currently, number plate recognition is carried out decentrally on the individual control devices themselves. As part of a further development of the IT architecture, Toll Collect is considering the possibility of centralising this processing logic and operating it in its own data centre in the future. This is intended to improve, among other things, maintainability, scalability and the uniform further development of the recognition logic. As an operating platform, Toll Collect relies on OpenShift, a container-based on-premise platform that enables flexible and secure data centre operation. Since several hundred control devices can generate requests virtually simultaneously, centrally operated ANPR software must be highly available and highly scalable as well as seamlessly integrable into the existing IT infrastructure - without jeopardising real-time number plate recognition in very high quality. Toll Collect would like to find out which software with which functions and boundary conditions are available on the market for data centre operation in an OpenShift environment, which interfaces they offer and, in particular, how customisable the solutions are during ongoing operation, how optimisations could work and to what extent and in what model licensing would be necessary. In preparation for a possible procurement procedure, Toll Collect is conducting a market exploration in accordance with § 28 VgV. There is expressly no intention to negotiate or award a contract with the request as part of the market exploration.
sig_1083b97d32e617e97520.title: Market exploration - Open Shift ANPR service

sig_10909ba23813bebf6c6e.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) is the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system for the procurement of services consisting in the processing of socio-economic and similar studies and analyses in the field of immovable infrastructure, the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities, consultancy services and expert support from the founding/establishing entity for individual legal entities within the contracting authority's remit, the preparation of analyses of the Czech defence industry and analyses of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure, under the conditions set out in the tender documentation (in detail in the tender documentation). The subject matter will be in particular the acquisition of comprehensive information important for evaluating and mapping the consequences of increased expenditure and defence requirements in the medium and long-term outlook. This primarily concerns the Czech economy (for example, the labour market, support for science and research, regional development or involvement in EU funds and other financial mechanisms), society in the Czech Republic and international cooperation. Processing of the analysis of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure and requirements with regard to the commitments undertaken by the Czech Republic at the NATO summit in The Hague in June 2025; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the provision and submission to the Ministry of Defence of comprehensive information on the actual state of capabilities and capacities of the domestic industry and research organisations, focusing in particular on capabilities in the field of development, production and logistical support of military material, training of technical personnel, training and fulfilment of mobilisation supplies; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities and contributing to the increase of their profitability, the provision of consultancy services and expert support to increase the efficiency of the performance of the function of the founder or establishing entity for individual legal entities within the remit of the Ministry of Defence; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular activities consisting in the provision of studies that will deal with the evaluation of both positive and negative impacts of construction on employment, the economy, transport, social and technical infrastructure, the environment (sustainable development) and the provision of public and private services in the area. The content of the studies will also include the identification of entities responsible for the prevention of risks and the resolution of arisen risks and proposals for measures that could eliminate, resolve or prevent the arisen risks, as well as the preparation of recommendations for the amendment of relevant strategic documents. The subject matter will also in certain cases include the preparation of presentations intended for concerned public administration stakeholders; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the analysis of the process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, the preparation and submission of a proposal for a new process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, including implementation steps and the provision of consultancy services during implementation; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).
