sig_10a29ada7157abb880d7.description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Title: Biobanking, Laboratory Analytics, and Associated Informatics Services for NIH Biorepositories Agency: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Description This is a SMALL BUSINESS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses); (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition; and (4) whether commercials sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code 541714 should not submit a response to this notice. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Purpose NIH is seeking capability statements from small businesses, and subcontractors regarding their abilities to continue the work of the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. This notice also serves to determine the availability of all small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses) with the capability to perform this work. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. These repositories typically: Receive, process, store, and biosamples from a wide range of biospecimen types (e.g. blood/derivatives, fluids, DNA/RNA, hair, cell lines, iPSCs, teeth, fecal matter, birth specimens and other tissues such as brain and other organs) at various temperature and storage conditions (e.g. -80C, liquid nitrogen; fresh, frozen, paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed) at scales ranging from tens of thousands to several million specimens. Serve dozens to hundreds of research studies across the United States and abroad. Enable broad, controlled-access biomaterial sharing to meet specific research objectives that further our knowledge of health Anticipate continued growth in biospecimen and data volume over the life of the award. Scope of Work & Required Capabilities Capable vendors should provide examples from current or previous projects when responding to capabilities. A. Sample Management and Storage Maintain secure, humidity- and temperature-controlled storage and tracking for at least 3,500,000 biospecimens in accordance with Best Practices, Clinical and Laboratory Standards, and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP; 21 CFR 58) with expert quality control and assurance procedures. Document the maximum capacity that could be achieved to expand storage beyond the minimum requested. Destroy samples per regulatory and consent requirements when no longer needed. College of American Pathologists (CAP) Biorepository Accreditation preferred. Maintain positive chain of custody and resolve data/sample discrepancies (missing data, incorrect information, misdirected samples) through issue tracking and resolution, coordinating with relevant receiving/data management teams (e.g. sites, site monitors, study staff). Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data alongside biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Centrally manage and cost-effectively distribute biosamples to qualified investigators approved through established access programs. Provide studies with collection kits and supplies, including barcoded tubes with human-readable labels. Provide research staff training for ordering supplies and collecting samples. B. Data Curation and Management Develop and maintain SOPs for sample receipt, storage, processing, QC, and distribution. Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data associated with biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Maintain an internal relational database (e.g., using persistent identifiers such as RRIDs) linked to associated data and participant and sample identifiers, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample and data location. Register and track biospecimens via an internal relational database with sample IDs (RRID) linked to participant IDs and associated data in the Contractor's auditable LIMS, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample/data location. Clean, standardize, and harmonize clinical data with cross-disorder phenotypic knowledge (e.g. different diagnostic systems or criteria, such as RDOC, DSM, ICD), incorporating data from electronic health records when applicable. Transfer data and sample IDs to controlled-access repositories or Data Centers (e.g., dbGAP, NBDC Data Hub or program specific data repositories). C. Laboratory and Analytic Capabilities Demonstrate laboratory expertise appropriate to the repository's sample types, which may include molecular biology techniques (e.g., DNA/RNA extraction, cell line transformation/immortalization), rigorous quality control, and tissue/cell culture (isolation, scale-up, and banking of primary cells). Provide CLIA-certification status. Provide laboratory capabilities for, but not limited to: metabolic, hematologic, and/or clinical assays high-throughput genotyping, sequencing, and gene-expression analysis Mass spectrometry for proteomics and metabolomics Advanced genomic and cellular techniques such as short- and long-range sequencing, chromatin capture, ChIP-seq, Cut-and-Tag, HiC generation of iPSC/neural stem cell lines CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing Analysis of RNA and DNA from Formalin-Fixed Parafin-Embedded tissue Provide scientific and technical expertise to evaluate and respond to researcher-submitted requests for biospecimen availability. Demonstrate that lead investigators and support staff have relevant experience in biobanking, LIMS, and database management Store and/or process histopathological tissue samples. Isolate, scale up, and bank primary cells from diverse tissue samples. D. Informatics Requirements and Cyberinfrastructure Develop, or manage and enhance (if already existing), a biorepository web portal (front-end and back-end), supporting existing features and providing updates/improvements as requested, potentially including: Synchronizing sample availability data with a public- or investigator-facing sample explorer tool to streamline discovery of related data and biospecimens across repositories Showcase published research and provide lay summaries Advertise repository resources For existing resources, support all currently available features, with updates and improvements as requested Where in scope, develop outreach tools (e.g., an integrated chatbot or public-facing portal) to help users locate biomaterials/data and discover related resources across repositories Develop or maintain backend infrastructure (e.g., server maintenance, microservices, relational databases such as PostgreSQL) and front-end website design/UI-UX. Maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) and require security documentation to keep systems compliant with applicable FISMA-level and other NIH requirements. Maintain, update, and develop Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and cyberinfrastructure for secure, interoperable data exchange. Capabilities for homomorphic encryption and distributed learning. Demonstrate experience and technical expertise to address all aspects of informatics requirements listed above. K. Collaboration & Governance Establish a strong collaborative relationship with the NIH Data Centers, study teams, and Institutes/Centers to enable modifications as the studies evolve. Serve as a co-signatory of the Specimen/Material Transfer Agreements developed by the funding Institute/Center. Be eligible to receive a Certificate of Confidentiality, adhering to requirements for protecting sensitive participant information as set forth in 45 CFR Part 75.303(a), NIHGPS Chapter 8.3 and 15.2.1, and subsection 301(d) of the Public Health Service Act (see: https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-17-109.html). Comply with all applicable human subjects protection, ethical, privacy, and data security regulations. Submission Requirements Interested organizations must demonstrate and document in a submitted capability statement extensive experience across the technical areas above, and include specific information on: Experience — An outline of previous similar projects, specifically the techniques employed in the areas described above. Personnel — Name and professional qualifications of personnel with specific experience in the work requested and knowledge of/experience in biomedical research. Facilities — Availability and description of facilities and equipment required to conduct this type of work. The Government will assess the appropriateness of professional and technical personnel classifications and consider any other specific and relevant information that would improve evaluation of respondents. Organizations should demonstrate capability to administer and coordinate interrelated tasks effectively and in a timely manner. Supporting documentation may include contracts in which the organization performed equivalent tasks (Government and commercial), references (names, titles, phone numbers, and other identifying information), and awards or commendations. An organization that does not have all the listed expertise, may respond by listing organizations with which they intend to collaborate or have as subcontractors to fulfill the requirements. Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than October 20, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. All capability statements should include: Company name and address Point of contact SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Phone/fax/email NAICS Code(s) Business size and status Capability information responsive to the requirements and qualifications identified in this notice Type(s) of business, if any (e.g., small, Veteran-owned, service-disabled Veteran-owned, women-owned, 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone)) NAICS Code: 541714 — Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology). SBA size standard: 1,000 employees or fewer. Submission Instructions Capability statements must be submitted electronically to: Shaun Rostad, Contract Specialist Email: shaun.rostad@nih.gov Secondary Point of Contact: Joshua T. Lazarus, Contract Specialist Email: josh.lazarus@nih.gov Submissions are due NO LATER THAN 1:00 p.m. EST on October 20, 2026. The subject line must include the Small Business Sources Sought Number. NIDA will not accept paper or faxed capability statements. Disclaimer THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement, nor does it constitute a solicitation or commitment by NIDA. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses under this announcement, nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information submitted. Any proprietary information should be so marked. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Respondents should ensure their response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of information or provide feedback with respect to any information submitted. Based on the Government’s market research, it is the agency’s assessment that the services described herein do not appear to constitute commercial services as defined under RFO Subpart 2.1, and therefore, the agency does not currently intend to utilize RFO Part 12 Acquisition Procedures. However, if an interested party asserts that these services are in fact commercial in nature, it should respond to this requirement and provide supporting evidence demonstrating that the services meet the definition of commercial services as prescribed by the applicable regulations.

sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.description: Die Bäder, Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH (BSF) originated from Thermalsolbad Salzgitter GmbH and Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH. BSF is a subsidiary of the City of Salzgitter and performs numerous tasks, particularly in the field of public services of general economic interest. It operates the thermal brine baths in Salzgitter-Bad with their extensive offerings, the municipal pool in Salzgitter-Lebenstedt with attractive family offerings, and the ice sports centre at Salzgittersee with various leisure offerings. In addition, BSF is the point of contact for organised sport in Salzgitter provided by the district sports association (Kreissportbund) and its numerous sports clubs, as well as the primary contact address for all queries relating to Lake Salzgitter. The contracting authority is planning the introduction of a uniform, cloud-based point of sale and administration system for its three facilities - the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad, the Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt, and the Eissporthalle am Salzgittersee. The aim is to optimise internal working processes and create a seamless, consistent customer experience across all premises. Currently existing, disparate software systems lead to significant organisational and technical challenges. Customers cannot use products (e.g. value cards or vouchers) across different premises, and support provided by various service providers complicates administration. A uniform system with central support by a single supplier is intended to solve these challenges, standardise technical operations, and improve customer service. A solution involving multiple different systems and subsequent connection to a common back-end system is not considered expedient from a technical and economic perspective. The subject matter of the contract comprises the following partial services: a. Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Eissporthalle Salzgittersee b. Optional: Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Stadtbad - Salzgitter-Lebenstedt c. Optional: Delivery of new access hardware and point of sale hardware for the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad d. Provision and operation of the SaaS-based back-end solution. The introduction is to take place in phases: - Eissporthalle Salzgittersee: after the season 2025/2026 from the 2. quarter 2026. Completion by no later than 15.09.2026 (season opening of the ice sports centre is on the last weekend of September). - Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt: expected in the 4. quarter 2026 - Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad: expected from the 1. quarter 2027.
sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.title: Cloud-based point-of-sale and management system for the Salzgittersee ice rink, the Salzgitter-Lebenstedt municipal pool, and the Salzgitter-Bad thermal brine bath

sig_10af27fd76b5a5a53a54.description: To prepare for a potential procurement for an estimated June 2027, market research is being carried out. The objective is to determine whether the patch management service required for the existing CGM-MEDICO environment can be provided fully and equivalently by a service provider. Mission-critical core components are operated within the existing CGM-MEDICO environment, in particular Oracle RAC, Ingres, CGM MEDICO application servers (UNIX), test systems as well as risk management and high-availability environments. The operating environment is already integrated into existing service and support structures; these include in particular the Remote Information Service, xRISE / Early-Morning-Reports, Secure Link, connection to the RHEL repositories, valid RHEL subscriptions and existing service contracts for support for system technology components CGM MEDICO (40015660), SecureDB 0-2 (40015681) and SecureDB 3-4 (40015682). For operating system updates, a functional test environment matching the parameters of the production environment is also available. As part of the market research, it is to be determined whether a service provider can take over the patch management service for this existing CGM-MEDICO environment fully and equivalently. The service must cover the entire required scope, in particular continuous monitoring of system statuses, evaluation and control of updates, planning and coordination of necessary measures, and execution of the rollout process including the Basic, Firmware and DBMS modules. In doing so, the existing service and support structures and ongoing service contracts must not be impaired. Furthermore, it must be ensured that patches and updates can be technically evaluated, prepared for release and implemented without system-critical impairment of the existing environment prior to being adopted into productive operation. Further information you may require or a questionnaire provided by us can be obtained upon request by email to vergabestelle@kbo.de. Please note: This procurement-related market research is carried out for the purpose of gathering information and creating a market overview. The direct award of a contract or call for competition is not associated with the market research. The implementation of a corresponding procurement procedure is anticipated for 2027. Interested bidders are requested to send us corresponding descriptions or documentation of their system solution, if possible within 2 months from the publication of this market research.
sig_10af27fd76b5a5a53a54.title: Market exploration patch management

sig_10bc118a65412c89aed0.description: Design (DTAC+PT+CS+DE) + technical assistance during the execution of works and execution of works, related to the investment objective ” Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park”. The number of days up to which clarifications can be requested by economic operators, before the deadline for the submission of tenders : 20 days. The contracting authority shall respond to all requests for clarification and/or additional information received from economic operators, in relation to the tender documentation, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The estimated value of the procurement is 20.550.373,85 lei without VAT, of which: Stage I design + technical assistance: 130.000,00 lei without VAT Stage II execution of works: 20.420.373,85 lei without VAT. The Municipality of Bistrița has concluded financing contract no. 1063/28.05.2025 with the Ministry of Energy for the realisation of the project ” Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park ” , financed through the modernisation programme (MEFM) managed by the Ministry of Energy. Specific Objective I – ESTABLISHMENT OF A PRODUCTION UNIT FOR ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES, RESPECTIVELY SOLAR SOURCES The objective targets the acquisition of technological equipment with and without assembly, respectively works, with the aim of establishing a production unit for energy from solar sources. The specific objective envisages the execution of specific works for the operationalisation of a renewable energy production unit to be characterised by the following functional parameters: - Newly installed capacity for producing energy from renewable sources: 3.961,44 kWp / 3.900 kW AC; - Net production of primary energy of 391,16 toe/year from renewable sources; - Total net electricity production of 86.623,20 MWh over a period of 20 years; The specific objective is correlated with the indicators assumed through the Financing Application, contributing to ensuring a significant share of the electricity requirement of the Municipality of Bistrița from renewable sources, namely solar sources. Specific Objective II – REDUCTION OF CARBON FOOTPRINT AND PROMOTION OF THE USE OF ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES The specific objective envisages reducing the carbon footprint of the Municipality of Bistrița by reducing greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the production of energy necessary for carrying out its own activity. To this end, the implementation of the investment project contributes to reducing greenhouse gases by 53.004,74 tonnes of CO2 equivalent over a period of 20 years (considering a conversion factor of 0,6119 tonnes of CO2 equivalent/MWh). Also, the specific objective envisages promoting the use of energy from renewable sources, the implementation of the investment project contributing to ensuring self-consumption from renewable sources to the detriment of using energy originating from greenhouse gas emission-generating sources. The specific objective targets the use in a percentage of 100% of the electricity produced at the level of the photovoltaic power plant for the self-consumption of the Municipality of Bistrița. The project “Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park ” will be carried out on a plot of land located in the extra-muros area of the municipality of Bistrița on an area of 47.593 sqm identified with cadastral number 93614, in the pasture category.

sig_10c05a3cbc7b283bacc0.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_114a6982aba5524c4139.description: FCC currently utilizes a third-party platform to administer its Inventory Financing (IF) program as this capability does not exist in our current technical solution stack. The solution is used to store key information to help administer the program and manage over 50 dealer partners across Canada which includes financial transactions, disbursements, monitoring dealer interest rates, and credit utilization integration.     Additionally, FCC currently leverages a manual inventory audit and validation process through a separate third-party provider. Audits are an important measure in place to ensure dealers are complying with the IF guidelines which ensures FCC’s security is accurately documented and located at the appropriate site indicated by the dealer. A manual onsite audit is conducted with a data file and any associated documents being sent to FCC for review, reconciliation, and follow-up where needed. There is no integration between the third-party audit tracking solution and FCC’s IF platform. Currently the process can require significant travel time between locations which has a negative carbon footprint and increases costs to FCC.     FCC’s preference is for one Proponent to provide a software platform to administer the Inventory Financing program and offer an audit function that will allow FCC to achieve the business needs stated below. However, FCC reserves the right to award the RFP scope of service to one or multiple vendors to ensure the success of the third-party software function and the administration of the audit program with little to no manual intervention required.

sig_115d8e80d87baf0187d1.description: Processing of evaluations of projects or calls financed from the European Social Fund. Evaluations are systematic and objective assessments of ongoing or completed projects, programmes or policies, their design, implementation and results. The aim is to determine relevance and the fulfilment of objectives, and to assess developmental effectiveness, impact and sustainability. It is a process of determining the importance or significance of a certain activity, policy or programme/project. Within the framework of the dynamic purchasing system (DNS), process, impact or strategic evaluations will be carried out. Process evaluations assess the implementation process of a programme or intervention, focus on ongoing processes and their aim is recommendations for better process design. Impact evaluations assess the achievement of planned effects/impacts/results. Most frequently using counterfactual impact evaluation (CIE type) based on statistical methods or in the form of theory-based evaluation (TBIE type) using the theory of change method and case studies. Strategic evaluations assess the design, achievement of strategic objectives and the contribution to their achievement at the level of the entire operational programme. They do not focus on partial interventions, but evaluate the programme as a whole with regard to the dominant themes of the operational programme in relation to the strategic objectives.
sig_115d8e80d87baf0187d1.title: DYNAMIC PURCHASING SYSTEM FOR STANDARD EVALUATIONS AND DATA COLLECTION II (Category 1 – Evaluation)

sig_1173cc2bcae43e84bfd9.description: Holbæk Kommune invites you to a market dialogue ahead of an upcoming procurement for the purchase of safety-enhancing IT technology in connection with citizens requiring care. The upcoming procurement comprises the delivery of an integrated software and hardware solution intended to support staff at the municipality's care centres – and potentially other areas – in prioritising and making the best possible professional care decisions. Dialogue is requested regarding an IT solution that can translate data into actionable insights that strengthen the professional overview, improve the quality of care and increase safety for citizens through more targeted efforts and better use of resources. The procurement is expected to include installation and configuration of software and hardware, implementation, ongoing user training, maintenance and support, etc. The service thus comprises both the supply of software and hardware and other services intended to support Holbæk Kommune in using and optimally exploiting the IT technology. The market dialogue is conducted as individual meetings, which are expected to be held on 16 and 17 February 2026 at the Town Hall in Holbæk Kommune, Kanalstræde 2, 4300 Holbæk. Registration must be made by email to: birgn@holb.dk.

sig_119cfd32ed7161537492.description: EDC is seeking a solution to provide and operate a secure, customizable online Branded Merchandise platform. The platform must allow authorized EDC employees to order approved Branded Merchandise through a centralized online storefront. EDC’s primary objective for this requirement is to support Business Orders for approved Branded Merchandise. EDC is seeking a single vendor of record for the Branded Merchandise program, responsible for end-to-end service delivery on EDC’s behalf, including sourcing, storage, inventory management, fulfillment, and delivery. Where feasible, priority should be given to Canadian-made and Canadian-supplied products. The Preferred Proponent will manage the full lifecycle of Branded Merchandise, including product sourcing, brand compliance, warehousing, pick-and-pack services, fulfillment, and domestic and international shipping. The Proponent must also provide governance and administrative capabilities, such as approvals, budget controls, and reporting. This engagement will help EDC centralize Branded Merchandise management, improve operational efficiency, maintain brand consistency, increase access to approved items, and monitor and control costs across the organization more effectively. EDC aims to achieve the following business objectives: Centralize the management of Branded Merchandise across EDC Improve operational efficiency and cost control Ensure consistent governance and brand application across Branded Merchandise Enable self-service ordering with appropriate governance Provide greater access to all EDC and employees to purchased Branded Merchandise for Business Orders and Personal Purchases Support domestic and international delivery needs Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.
sig_119cfd32ed7161537492.title: EDC Branded Merchandise Platform

sig_119ff6256237302f0213.description: Background Trysil and Folldal municipalities shall enter into new contracts for the procurement of insurances, as the current agreements expire. The aim is to establish contracts that give the municipalities a predictable, safe and appropriate insurance scheme. The procurement shall contribute to safeguarding the municipalities ́ insurance needs in a good way, at the same time facilitating effective use of resources, a good overview of risks and injuries as well as appropriate follow-up in the contract period. The municipalities would like a system that ensures stable and available follow-up, clear contact points and good assistance with injury incidents. Tenderers shall use their expertise and competence to contribute to fulfilling the objective of the agreement. Description of the assignment The assignment is for the delivery of insurance of persons and property damage insurances for Trysil and Folldal municipalities. The procurement includes coverage of insurance within the municipalities ́needs, including i.a. insurance of employees and other relevant personal groups, property, vehicles, liability and other relevant insurance coverages. Further details on insurance objects, coverages, insurance sums and excesses are stated in the price form and other requirements in the competition. The price form is a guideline for which insurances and objects are covered by the procurement. The procurement is divided into the following two parts: Part 1: Insurance of persons Part 2: Property damage insurances Tenderers can submit tenders for one or both parts. The parts are evaluated and awarded separately. The contracting authority can enter into a contract with up to two tenderers. This means that the contracting authority can enter into a contract with one tenderer for both parts, or enter into separate contracts with different tenderers for insurance of persons and property damage insurances respectively. The delivery shall include ordinary management and follow-up of the insurance contracts in the contract period. This includes, among other things, customer service, injury management, permanent gender neutral preferred and annual status or follow-up meetings with the municipalities. Furthermore, the tenderer shall be able to assist the municipalities with advice on damage prevention measures and risk mapping in municipal entities. The delivery shall also include appropriate digital solutions, for example a customer portal or equivalent system, which gives municipalities access to relevant information about the insurance contracts, damages, documentation and follow-up. The agreements shall, in total, provide the municipalities with a clear, efficient and robust insurance system, with clear routines and stable services throughout the entire contract period.
sig_119ff6256237302f0213.title: HO-26-05 Insurances

sig_11adbf005318cf83e444.description: The purpose of this procedure is to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (hereinafter, DPS) for the procurement, through agile and flexible electronic procedures, of the supply of software licences, digital solutions, technological platforms and the provision of associated services in the field of information and communication technologies (ICT), with priority destination to the public educational centres affiliated with the Departamento de Educación del Gobierno de Navarra. This category constitutes the functional core of the system, integrating solutions designed to provide access to digital tools, applications, technological platforms and cloud services that directly support the teaching, organisational and management activities of the educational centres and of the Department itself.; This category groups solutions oriented towards the provision, management and development of digital content and educational resources intended for the teaching-learning process. It includes both access to educational materials in various formats and the platforms that allow their distribution, organisation and use in digital environments, as well as tools that facilitate their integration into existing learning environments.; The purpose of this category is the procurement of digital services of a transversal and specialised nature, aimed at ensuring the effective use, sustainability, evolution and continuous improvement of the digital services of the educational system, when these are not directly linked to a specific solution or platform.; This category comprises services aimed at the design, development, adaptation and integration of technological solutions that allow a response to specific needs of the educational system, as well as the continuous evolution of existing systems.; This category groups solutions intended for the implementation, management and operation of the digital infrastructures that support the ICT services of the Department of Education, guaranteeing their operation, availability, security and evolution. It includes the technological infrastructure systems necessary for the provision of digital services, such as operating systems, virtualisation platforms, containers, service orchestration, middleware platforms, application servers, execution environments and infrastructure management solutions in both local, cloud or hybrid environments.; The purpose of this category is to incorporate solutions based on advanced and emerging technologies into the educational system, as well as to facilitate the experimentation, development, validation and progressive adoption of new technological models in the educational, organisational and management fields. It includes artificial intelligence solutions in their various modalities, such as content generation systems, intelligent assistants, natural language processing, computer vision, recommendation systems, intelligent process automation and other similar technologies, applied both to the teaching-learning process and to the improvement of management and the optimisation of digital services.

sig_11d0564660421f761475.description: The Housing Ombudsman Service (HOS) intends to conduct preliminary market engagement to inform a forthcoming further competition under Crown Commercial Service Digital Outcomes & Specialists 7 (RM1043.9), Lot 1 (Digital Outcomes). The engagement will help refine the outcomes, delivery approach, commercial model, and procurement timetable for an outcome-based digital delivery requirement. The Housing Ombudsman Service (HOS) is considering options to recommission its patchwork of customer-facing software, introducing an integrated customer 'front door' that better supports existing and future strategic priorities, including the possibility of a major expansion of its service to the Private Rented Sector (PRS). The project directly supports the following strategic aims listed in the 26/27 business case and 2030 corporate strategy. • Provide an excellent, person-centred service • Drive positive local complaint handling cultures • Support better services through our insights, data and intelligence • Organisation Design: Systems (Strategic Enabler) To help define the requirements and understand the potential of a new suite of digital tools, HOS requires the support of a Digital Delivery Partner who can facilitate and complement our in-house knowledge and expertise. Indicative requirement (high-level outcomes) The deliverables have been split into two work packages, which are closely aligned with project stages: Discover, Design, Delivery & Transition. A. Discovery & Design (including quick wins) B. Delivery & Transition These work packages will be procured separately and sequentially so that the specification and requirements of any new system(s) delivered under Work Package B benefit from the findings of Discovery & Design. This Preliminary Market Engagement is specifically for Work Package A. To ensure momentum, positive engagement and early benefit realisation, Work Package A includes a requirement for the identification and delivery of 'quick wins'. These are likely to be delivered through existing system optimisation and the potential use of AI and automation, rather than through the wholesale replacement of existing digital infrastructure. Work Package A: Discovery & Design This work package covers the activities and artefacts required to fully understand the opportunities, risks, costs and benefits associated with a range of options for recommissioning HOS' customer-facing digital infrastructure. This is the first work package to be procured, and on delivery, HOS will be able to define its integrated customer 'front door' requirements in a way that supports a new Target Operating Model, aligns with key strategic plans, and delivers measurable benefits to the organisation. Work Package A will also provide funding for quick wins identified by the digital delivery partner and validated by the services impacted. These will be enhancements to existing systems that provide rapid returns on investment (Resource Savings) and/or measurable improvements to current ways of working (Greater Productivity; Improved User Experience; Improved Conversion Rate) and will be subject to further funding approval. Work Package A: Summary Table of Deliverables Reference Description of Deliverable A1 Validation and enhancement of Work Package B outcomes A2 Approved Scope of Works A3 Risk and Opportunity assessment A4 Benefits Profiles - baselines, measures and targets A5 Work Package B delivery resource requirements A6 Quick Wins and System Optimisations A7 Options appraisal, costs and recommendation for Work Package B Lot 1: .

sig_11e9b67bc2c57cd6c404.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the procurement of a Väylävirasto requirements database currently in preparation, which will serve as a centralised digital platform for the management of infrastructure asset information requirements. The requirements database is part of the VETO development programme (Transport Infrastructure Asset Lifecycle Information Management Development Programme). BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES In Väylävirasto, a number of studies have been carried out since 2021 examining the tools and services needed for data flows. The studies identified that current information requirements are fragmented: they are maintained in a decentralised manner in guidelines, spreadsheets and various systems. This causes inconsistencies and outdated information, and degrades data quality, timeliness and auditability. The objective of the procurement is to implement a centralised requirements database that brings together infrastructure asset information requirements into a single structured, consistent and machine-readable format. The solution will improve the quality, consistency and timeliness of information requirements and enable their efficient utilisation in various processes, such as procurement, design, construction and maintenance. The aim is also to enable controlled lifecycle maintenance of information requirements (creation, modification, approval and publication), version control and change traceability, as well as automated quality assurance. In addition, the requirements database must support integrations with other Väylävirasto systems and enable the sharing and utilisation of information requirements in a machine-readable format for various stakeholders. The solution will support Väylävirasto digitalisation objectives, data-driven management and interoperability between different systems and actors. At the same time, manual work, errors and ambiguity will be reduced, and the conditions for new, automated operating models will be created. A key benefit arises from the fact that the content of the requirements database can be shared and utilised via APIs in various systems and services. OBJECTIVE OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The objective is to obtain feedback on the procurement design, preliminary requirements and boundaries, and to ensure that the planned package is feasible and appropriate in relation to the solutions offered by the market. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for the market dialogue and the implementation of the procurement is: Technical dialogue May 2026 Publication of contract notice early summer 2026 Comparison of tenders late summer 2026 Award decision and continuation early autumn 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not constitute a request for tenders. The prior information notice includes an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its specification at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in any potential tendering procedure. The technical dialogue will be conducted through commenting on draft versions of the tender documents and answering questions drawn up by the contracting authority. Registration instructions: Suppliers must express their interest in participating in the market dialogue by sending a message to suvi.hyokkari@vayla.fi with the subject line: "Vaatimustietokannan hankinta - markkinavuoropuhelu". The contracting authority will provide interested suppliers with the materials and questions for comment. The deadline for replies and comments is 22.5.2026 at 12:00. Suppliers are requested to provide the following information in their message: - supplier contact person's email address The contracting authority reserves the right to invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions and estimated publication date of the contract notice presented in this prior information notice, as well as the draft dialogue materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information on the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.
sig_11e9b67bc2c57cd6c404.title: Call for market dialogue: Requirements database service

The Contracting Authority's 171-person organisation is launching a comprehensive, strategic IT modernisation in order to elevate operations into a cloud-centric, regulated and measurable service model. According to the target concept, the vast majority of business services will be designed/operated in a cloud environment; the role of on-premises components is intentionally minimised and restricted exclusively to basic (hygiene) functions (directory service, name resolution, IP allocation, edge connection). sig_120fa4206e6c8af5eee6.description: The subject of procurement is the Security Operation Center (SOC) service, responsible for monitoring, detection, and response to security incidents in real time as well as the mitigation of harmful consequences of an incident in the shortest possible time. The Security Operation Center (SOC), operating in a 24x7x365 regime, continuously monitors the security of the entire information system of Pula General Hospital in order to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive patient data, as well as the availability, authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality of the hospital's key services. The most important goal of the SOC is a fast, efficient, and reliable reaction in the event of a security incident, and it is crucial, due to the outsourcing of this function, to ensure the timeliness of activities and mutual coordination of the activities of the SOC and Pula General Hospital so that any individual incident is resolved in the shortest possible time. Additionally, following the Cybersecurity Regulation for operators of essential services and digital service providers, Pula General Hospital, as an operator of essential services, has the obligation to reduce all those risks that may arise within the framework of the outsourcing of the service to an acceptable level. The Contracting Authority has implemented an IBM QRadar SIEM system for collecting and processing data from the following sources: Aruba ClearPass Policy Manager Fortinet FortiGate Security Gateway Microsoft DHCP Server Microsoft DNS Debug Microsoft Exchange Server Microsoft IIS Microsoft Windows Security Event Log Symantec Email ATP Symantec Email Cloud Queue Symantec Email Core Symantec Endpoint Protection Servers (approx. 70 units) The Security Operation Center service must meet all technical conditions stated in the technical specification. As part of the bid, it is also necessary to offer the renewal of the manufacturer's warranty on the Contracting Authority's existing SIEM system, and the requested services in accordance with the Contracting Authority's technical specification. sig_12152d52da211860004a.description: Education of the Flemish Community (GO!) is official education organised and funded on behalf of the Flemish Community. GO! organises ordinary and special pre-school, primary and secondary education, adult education and part-time arts education for more than 300 000 pupils and trainees. The pedagogical project, the PPGO! and the polaris vision in the strategic plan 2030 describe the mission and vision of GO!, why and how we as GO! do what we do. The digital transformation of GO! is an important building block of the strategic plan to realise our mission and polaris vision. The GO! Digital Store project is one of the strategic projects with which we want to put digital transformation into practice in everyday life. With this project, we want to support our educational professionals in making well-considered choices for digital tools and learning resources, and offer schools tools for shaping and implementing a supported digital policy. Because this project aims for an innovative solution that is not yet readily available on the market, we can rely on support from the Innovative Procurement Programme (PIO) of the Agency for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (VLAIO). Within this programme, the project was prepared by a needs analysis in cooperation with Addestino, the report of which has been published online. Based on this report and further research within GO!, this public contract took shape. This public contract comprises the development of an online platform, the GO! Digital Store. This platform aims to support an end-to-end process whereby GO! educational professionals are advised on and guided towards high-quality digital learning resources and tools. Specifically, the functionalities that the platform must offer can be divided into two categories: on the one hand, offering clear and transparent information on the existing range of high-quality digital tools and content, and on the other hand, instruments to support school teams in shaping, implementing and monitoring a digital policy plan. The analysis that took place during the preliminary study defines various functional building blocks of which the platform must consist. These building blocks are described in the 7 TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS section. In the final tender specifications, these building blocks will be described in more detail in the form of functional descriptions. The following elements of the contract are initially distinguished: Development of the platform, including testing with end users; Support for the rollout of the platform; Support for the project management of the contract.

sig_12365f79805d82db1e72.description: The contracting authority's SOC has the primary task of monitoring the organisation's IT landscape around the clock and initiating appropriate measures in the event of security incidents. The previous contractual partner provided endpoint detection and response (EDR), analysis and incident response, vulnerability management, and security information and event management (SIEM) as key focus areas; accordingly, this tender essentially comprises the replacement of said components and services. While some tasks will now be performed by the contracting authority's SOC, internal staff resources are a limiting factor. Therefore, some tasks, including the continuous monitoring of the environment, will still need to be performed jointly with the support of an external partner. The future environment is to be based on the current internal log data platform Splunk, which will be expanded into a SIEM. This platform is to be supplemented by a managed detection and response (MDR) solution that operates using its own data lake and transmits alerts to the internal SIEM. Continuous monitoring is to take place on the basis of the MDR service, while the contracting authority's employees will in future be able to deal primarily with the internal SIEM and thus also cover internal and organisation-specific use cases. The systems are supplemented by various services to operate the SIEM platform, as well as cyber analysis services and support in the event of an incident. The future platform must also support operations in vulnerability management with suitable tools. The procurement is divided into four lots. Lot 1 is intended to ensure the fundamental cybersecurity of the contracting authority. For this purpose, an XDR solution is to be procured, which must be ensured with a suitable MDR service twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week (24x7). The MDR service is to be provided on the basis of the XDR's own data lake. Data retention must take place for at least 6 months; an option to increase this period to 2 years must be offered. The contracting authority's systems must also be scanned automatically for vulnerabilities both in the internal networks and from an external side. Therefore – integrated into the XDR or via an independent solution – a vulnerability management solution must also be offered, which carries out the scans as automatically as possible and can prioritise vulnerabilities. Both XDR and vulnerability scanning must have interfaces to the log data management tool Splunk.
sig_12365f79805d82db1e72.title: Support for the operation and further development of the Security Operations Centre (SOC)

sig_1249c09c9d0df5491ce2.description: In 2024 the National Health Service (NHS) Vaccinations Digital Services (VDS) sub-directorate (under the Digital Prevention Services Programme Directorate) determined that development of an in-house system for the capture and flow of vaccination data would assist NHS England to achieve a number of key objectives: - Ensure a rapid ability to onboard new vaccine types for data capture and flow without having to undertake the significant effort and cost of engaging multiple 3rd party suppliers to development and assurance processes. - Achieve savings on the annual national digital health spend of at least £6million, and - Improve value for money and return on investment for NHSE funding, focussing public health expenditure on NHS England digital development, through the implementation of the Provider Pays Policy. These requirements align to the Government Missions and Measures parameter for: New delivery in direct response to the new Governmental priorities for health and social care, most specifically as identified under Primary Care Recovery Programme (PCARP) and the NHSE 10-year plan which places emphasis on the delivery of local and community based health services and reduction of spend with 3rd party commercial entities. In order to realise objectives, set for NHS England in the NHSE 10-Year Plan, NHS-VDS developed the Record A Vaccination System (RAVS). This system was rolled-out within Secondary Care settings through 2024/25 and in 2025 commenced limited roll-out to the Primary Care market supporting wider section 7a vaccination campaigns. VDS has determined that further roll-out of RAVS to the Primary Care market, most specifically in community pharmacy (CP) settings, is the most robust strategy to achieve: - Greater engagement of Community Pharmacy (CP) Providers to NHS vaccination campaigns through offering a single sign-on experience, via their existing CP IT systems; - Greater engagement of CP systems suppliers, through offering integration to RAVS, removing the burden of ongoing seasonal development and assurance requirements. - Improved digital health spend through reduction in requirement on NHSE to subsidise supplier development and assurance demand and to provide ongoing support and assurance capabilities. Therefore, VDS seeks to procure CP IT suppliers to integrate RAVS (as the sole and standardised digital vaccination data capture system for CP Providers) into their CP IT systems. This procurement will award contracts for up to ten (10) qualified CP IT suppliers; where such suppliers will be offered a standard remuneration for achievement, by the defined milestone date, of development implementation of the single sign in Integration and full assured readiness to support the Autumn/Winter 2026 COVID/Flu Seasonal Vaccination Campaign. Subsequent procurement activity is expected to take the form of an Open Procedure in line with requirements identified in Procurement Act 2023. Further information regarding the requirements evaluated as part if this procedure will be shared during the market engagement period. The market engagement activity will take the form of this Preliminary Market Engagement notice, with suppliers required to express interest via NHS England's Atamis procurement portal - details can be found below. Additionally, VDS shall hold an information webinar, expected for March 2026 - the specific date for this will be announced via Atamis. Release of the Invitation to Tender documents is intended for early-April 2026, but is dependent on the market response identified through the market engagement. Lot 1: .
sig_1249c09c9d0df5491ce2.title: NHS England RAVS Integration

sig_124ce7126b3149601812.description: The Bundesministerium für Umwelt, Klimaschutz, Naturschutz und nukleare Sicherheit (BMUKN) with its locations in Bonn and Berlin pursues the objective with its public relations work of presenting the entire range of topics of the ministry to a broad public as well as the press in an up-to-date and target-group-oriented manner and making corresponding information accessible. In order to further increase the attractiveness of the internet presence and the social media channels of the agency and to utilise the diversity of communication channels in a modern way, video contributions and live streams are to be used. The video contributions and live streams are to be published primarily on the social media channels and the internet pages of the BMUKN in order to communicate current political topics in a low-threshold and clear manner and to enable the interested public to participate digitally live in events or to get into direct conversation with the house management via digital live formats. Individual recordings are also passed on to cooperation partners of the contracting authority (CA) or interested parties for free use, further processing, publication as well as for public and non-public screenings. The BMUKN intends to award a framework agreement for the creation of video contributions and live streams on current political developments and topics relevant to the department. The services to be provided are commissioned individually as required by the CA. On annual average, about 1 reportage and 2 explanatory videos, about 30 statements and about 4 live streams (via website and social media channels) are to be expected. The occasions range from e.g. press conferences, press statements to greetings, short messages, position statements up to day events and multi-day events. In addition, the creation of daily updated clips from existing or purchased image and video material in the form of collages, slideshows and GIFs for social media is required, the average here is approximately 2 clips per week. The legally compliant use of AI-based audio and moving image material is also usable in production – subject to the necessary statutory labelling obligations. The service to be provided is subdivided into several service packages: 1. Intro and outro 2. Creation of social media video 3. Supplementary social media video services as required 4. Video contribution statement 5. Video contribution interview 6. Video contribution recording 7. Video contribution reportage 8. Explanatory film/animation film 9. Mobile live stream 10. Audio-video media package as well as other optional services.

sig_12967e5c18c4f730c06a.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.
sig_12967e5c18c4f730c06a.title: 17.13 Management consultancy services (DIS)

sig_12c02ab808cda33bc30f.description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.

sig_12c6c0259211469d1719.description: The subject of the contract is the supply of new applications and technological means that will improve the management and functionality of the Municipality. The selection of the proposed actions was made from the actions marketplace of the call with the aim of serving the local needs and policies of the Municipality. These Actions are: • Interconnection of lamps to a central management computer centre • Organisation of Fleet Office and Municipal vehicle fleet management • Municipal cemetery management system and file digitisation • Electronic budget and technical programme consultation system • Electronic invoicing • Comprehensive cyber-attack protection infrastructure (Network Firewall, Endpoint security, etc.) and provision of a teleworking system. The lighting network must have the capability of remote management, control and supervision via a special system. The solution must include a central Smart Lighting platform, which can be hosted either in a Cloud infrastructure or on customer premises and can be interconnected, easily, smoothly and in seamless operation, with a central management system. These controllers must be installed in the power supply distribution board of the luminaires (switchboard or pillar) and control (on/off) as a set the group of interconnected luminaires as well as record the operating characteristics (energy, time, etc.).; -Organisation of Fleet Office and Municipal vehicle fleet management The application must monitor and manage the entire municipal vehicle fleet by installing modern telematics units and screens in at least twenty (20) vehicles of the Municipality and interconnection with their central management software. By using the platform, real-time verification of vehicle movement and routes taken, control of schedule adherence and route execution, as well as significant fuel savings, will be achieved. -Municipal cemetery management system and file digitisation This web application aims at the interoperability and digitisation of the operation of the cemetery office. The aim is to increase the efficiency of the cemetery office and improve citizen service. The system must fully cover the management of burials, exhumations, ossuaries, extensions, charges, etc. of the municipal cemetery. It must also provide spatial visualisation of information on a digital map. With this project, the Municipality will be given the opportunity to have a clear and fully up-to-date picture of the cemeteries and the competent department of the respective municipality will have a tool for daily operation. -Electronic budget and technical programme consultation system This web application must enable the Municipality to conduct consultations with citizens via the internet. Citizens, through authentication, comment, interact with the municipal authority, propose, and answer questionnaires on matters affecting the Municipality. As a result, citizens' proposals will be published based on the most popular choices. -Electronic invoicing The electronic invoicing system is a necessity in local government organisations (LGIs) in accordance with applicable legislation in the context of public procurement execution. sig_12fded181b12050c636e.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Extreme Computing BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 20 Sep 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hrs. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 20 Sep 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 4 Oct 2023 FY25 by 30 Sep 2024 FY26 by 30 Sep 2025 FY27 by 30 Sep 2026 FY28 by 30 Sep 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Broad Agency Announcement for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to support research in the focus areas computational diversity and efficient computing architectures, machine learning and artificial intelligence in embedded system and architectures, computing at the edge, nanocomputing, space computing, and robust algorithms and applications. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $497.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 36 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $3M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99.9M ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023( previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Joel Moore AFRL/RITB 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-4958 Email: joel.moore.2@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. sig_131cd555715d98425eca.description: This is a MARKET EXPLORATION. As part of the funded project to establish a nationwide research infrastructure for digital pathology, an independent scope of services for research data management is to be established and operated sustainably. The subject of the intended procurement is the conception, provision and permanent further development of services and components that enable the standardised description, quality assurance, sustainable provision, findability, citability and reusability of medical research data. In this context, the requirements of medical and digital pathological research data must be taken into account in particular. To ensure a sustainable, supra-regionally compatible and long-term usable infrastructure, a professional, technical and organisational connection to the National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI) and in particular NFDI4Health is required. The developed concepts, services and components are to be integrated with the structures, standards and services established there and designed in such a way that permanent integration into the national research data ecosystem is made possible. From the perspective of the University Hospital, the requirement can currently only be met by one market participant. This market exploration is being carried out to verify this assumption. The contracting authority reserves the right to take further steps under procurement law.
sig_131cd555715d98425eca.title: MARKET EXPLORATION in accordance with § 28 VgV - Research data management for digital pathology

The purpose of this contract notice is to define the conditions of the consultation relating to services for Multi-Application Third-Party Maintenance, development of new applications and administration of application environments.
