sig_1355dc1e570ee749b61c.description: The subject of the contract is "Procurement of HPC Research Infrastructure". More specifically, this procurement concerns technologically sound computing infrastructure complying with modern high-performance computing (HPC) system standards to cover the implementation needs of the physical scope of the MW – ATLAS Project. The contract aims to procure a technologically sound computing infrastructure, complying with modern High-Performance Computing (HPC) system standards, for scientific applications. Specifically, the infrastructure will include a comprehensive cluster of servers with the following main components: 1. High-performance servers with GPU accelerators (GPU nodes) 2. Servers for user access, system management, proper operation control and usage statistics generation (login/management/monitoring servers) 3. Server with high-speed and high-capacity storage system (storage target node) 4. High-speed and low-latency computer network between cluster nodes (high-performance network) 5. General access and management computer network 6. High-availability SAN storage data storage system 7. Server for data backup 8. Installation racks with power distribution units (PDUs) The offered sub-units are required to be fully compatible with each other. The procurement also includes the supplier's obligation to guarantee its operation for a period of at least five (5) years after its final acceptance.
sig_1355dc1e570ee749b61c.title: Procurement of HPC Research Infrastructure

sig_135ad6c6febfc4f2e5cf.description: Services for the development, updating and maintenance of a geospatial application for receiving single support requests (a new GIS platform – Geo-spatial Aid Application - GSAA -)", in order to fulfil the specific activities of the institution in the direction of managing European and national funds intended to support agriculture, taking into account also the new context of the common agricultural policy to be implemented in the period 2023-2027. The IPA-Online application currently used was developed on an old platform that no longer supports updates. This application is an IT system intended for receiving single payment applications submitted by farmers. The new application must meet the current requirements of APIA, in accordance with the specifications the subject of this procurement and of the framework agreement to be awarded, comprising four major categories of services: 1. The primary development of the GIS platform on a new technology to take over / adapt existing functionalities in the current GIS parcel digitisation application (IPA - Online), 2. The development of new functionalities according to the purchaser's requirements, after the commissioning of the platform from point 1; 3. The component for the maintenance of the applications and servers on which it runs within optimal parameters for both the production and test systems; 4. Provision of a assistance and support centre for recording and remedying incidents reported by users. Based on the framework agreement, subsequent contracts will be awarded which will constitute the legal basis for payment, depending on the needs of the contracting authority. Subsequent contracts will be concluded in compliance with the unit rates for each individual category of services provided in the framework agreement and within the allocated budget funds. The unit rates provided in the framework agreement, updated where appropriate, will govern all subsequent contracts to be awarded during the execution of the framework agreement. The framework agreement will be governed by specific unit rates for each category of services (man-day unit rates for new functionality development services, respectively monthly subscription unit rates for maintenance, assistance and support, and maintenance support), unit rates which will form the basis for the award of all subsequent contracts to be concluded during the execution of the framework agreement. The framework agreement will be concluded with a single economic operator, for a duration of 48 months. The estimated timetable for applying the framework agreement award procedure: It is estimated that the framework agreement will be applied during the period: May 2023 – May 2027. It is estimated that between 2 and 4 subsequent contracts will be awarded per year depending on the needs of APIA, whenever this need arises. The detailed description of the services requested to be performed, as well as the technical requirements of the services, are presented in the Specifications. Economic operators may request clarifications 18 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The contracting authority will draw up and post in SICAP the response to all requests for clarification submitted within the above term, on the 11th day before the deadline for submitting tenders. The estimated maximum and minimum quantities expected to be achieved during the framework agreement and during the largest subsequent contract are found in the Annex to the Specifications - Estimated minimum and maximum quantities. The estimated maximum value of the framework agreement, which was calculated based on the maximum quantities of services that could be requested over the duration of the entire framework agreement, for all categories of services, is 24.156.600 lei, excluding VAT. The estimated minimum value of the framework agreement, which was calculated based on the minimum quantities of services that could be requested over the duration of the entire framework agreement, for all categories of services, is 6.315.570,50 lei, excluding VAT. The estimated maximum total value of the largest subsequent contract is 11.207.982,5 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the maximum quantities of services to be procured during the largest subsequent contract, for all categories of services requested in the specifications. The estimated minimum total value of a subsequent contract is 6.315.570,50 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the minimum quantities of services to be procured during a subsequent contract, for all categories of services requested in the specifications.

sig_136415155d07597188bb.description: "Technical assistance, corrective and evolutionary maintenance services for the integrated IT system of the National Public Pension House" With a view to ensuring use at optimal parameters and in accordance with the standards and specifications of the CNPP integrated IT system, as well as to bringing added value to this system, it is imperative to ensure the sustainability of the system. The activities to be carried out are as follows: - Resolving application dysfunctions (Bug-fixing); - Data corrections when errors are found in the system functionality caused by data inconsistencies or corruption; - Administration of the equipment on which the IT system applications are installed (Oracle); - Administration of the equipment on which the IT system applications are installed (non-Oracle); - Administration of networking equipment; - Microsoft infrastructure administration services During the maintenance period, the winning tenderer must perform the following activities: a. Periodic meetings regarding the analysis and discussion of identified problems; b. Maintenance and proper functioning of the IT system at agreed parameters (functional, availability and data integrity) by verifying the solution. i. Database administration, ii. Process administration, Back-up and database restoration (back-up/restore): iv. Database performance monitoring: the supplier shall monitor the performance of the databases relating to the CNPP integrated IT system, with a view to analysing potential problems and identifying remediation methods. v. The provider shall monitor the security of the data stored within the databases relating to the CNPP integrated IT system and shall ensure that access to this data, as well as to the objects stored within the database, can only be carried out using the application authentication mechanisms (predefined roles). ii. Application back-up and restoration: the supplier shall maintain and monitor the back-up procedure for the application modules within the CNPP integrated IT system. iii. Installation of new application versions resulting from the remediation of software manufacturing defects. d. The Microsoft infrastructure existing within the CNPP is characterised by high complexity, comprising several types of services and systems, distributed in different locations and at various stages of technological updating. To this end, at least the following stages must be completed: i. analysis of the requirements and the impact of updates/modifications on the Orizont integrated IT system following the implementation of amendments and additions to the legislation in force; ii. development of new modules or functionalities or modification of existing ones following the implementation of the aforementioned legislative amendments and additions, in a manner that ensures compatibility with both the current system (Orizont) and the future one (Phoenix); iii. testing of the applications developed following the implementation of the requirements; iv. staff training for the new functionalities implemented; v. updating of documentation in accordance with the modifications/new functionalities implemented. 6.3.2. Implementation of other legislative modifications or specific application modification requirements To this end, at least the following stages must be completed: i. analysis of the requirements and the impact of updates/modifications on the Orizont integrated IT system following the implementation of amendments and additions to the legislation in force; ii. development of new modules or functionalities or modification of existing ones following the implementation of the aforementioned legislative amendments and additions. iii. testing of the applications developed following the implementation of the requirements; iv. staff training for the new functionalities implemented. In accordance with the descriptive document

sig_138721de2c5d110905c3.description: The RWTH Chair of Biotechnology intends to offer the teams participating in the RWTH ABBt "The Materials Lab Incubator" a structured programme comprising coaching, practical mentoring and an entrepreneurial training curriculum. For this purpose, an external mentoring programme is to be integrated which brings the teams together with experienced mentors from industry and successful founders. An external service for the structured support of the science-related deep-tech incubator Materials Lab Incubator (MerLIn) of RWTH Aachen University is to be procured. MerLIn is based at the Institute of Biology and Biotechnology and is funded under the STARK funding directive. The aim of the incubator is to support start-up teams from the university and non-university research environment in developing scientific ideas into marketable enterprises. The thematic focus is in particular on sustainable materials, biotechnology, synthetic biology, microbiology, circular economy, waste recycling and green chemistry. The subject of the procurement is the conception, organisation, implementation, coordination and documentation of a structured mentoring and entrepreneurship support offering for the start-up teams funded within the framework of MerLIn. The target group consists predominantly of deep-tech start-ups or spin-off projects with a high scientific-technological maturity level, but frequently limited entrepreneurial experience. Through the service to be procured, these teams are to be specifically supported in matters of enterprise and product development and accompanied on the path to a marketable enterprise. The service comprises in particular the planning and organisation of mentoring events within the framework of which suitable mentors are brought together with the respective start-up teams. The mentors are above all to be experienced practitioners from relevant specialist areas who can support the teams in individual 1:1 guidance regarding specific issues of enterprise development, product development, market validation, business model development, scaling, financing or comparable start-up-relevant topics. The contractor shall assume the structured allocation of mentors and teams as well as the further coordination of the resulting mentoring relationships. In addition, the procurement encompasses mentor management, including the support, coordination and organisational integration of the mentors into the MerLIn programme. This includes in particular communication with those involved, appointment and schedule coordination, ensuring targeted cooperation between teams and mentors as well as the follow-up of the agreed measures and results. The resulting mentoring pairings and their progress are to be documented continuously by the contractor. In addition to individual mentoring, an entrepreneurship curriculum in a group format is to be organised and accompanied. This curriculum is to address start-up-relevant topics from the fields of enterprise and product development and impart overarching entrepreneurial knowledge to the funded teams. In contrast to 1:1 mentoring, this offering does not take place individually, but in the form of group formats, workshops or comparable collaborative learning and exchange formats. The service to be procured must be provided as a continuous, structured and fully organised support offering. The contractor must ensure that the services are implemented as planned, target-group-orientated and in accordance with the requirements of a science-related deep-tech incubator. Professional coordination of all relevant stakeholders, comprehensible documentation of the measures carried out and close coordination with the MerLIn team of RWTH Aachen University are expected. The aim of the procurement is to support the start-up teams supervised in the incubator through external expertise, individual guidance and systematic qualification formats in developing viable business models and marketable products. In this way, a contribution is to be made to the foundation and establishment of future-proof enterprises in the structurally weak coal phase-out region of the Rhenish Mining Area and the creation of sustainable jobs is to be promoted.
sig_138721de2c5d110905c3.title: 176 - Mentoringprogramm "The Materials Lab Incubator" (2027/2028)

sig_13963b92b10f4f0728f5.description: The subject of the contract is a framework agreement for print shop services. This is understood to mean all services related to receiving and preparing data files from various sources, as well as printing, preparing for dispatch, dispatching where applicable and/or further processing of documents via various media, including associated tracking and reporting. The service provider shall perform the following services throughout the entire term of the framework agreement in accordance with agreed service levels: • Document processing: o Receiving and processing data files in various formats originating from different sources; o Printing these files on various types of paper and envelopes; o Folding and inserting into envelopes; o Sorting according to recipient and delivering to the postal operator, currently Bpost; o Full handling of registered mail. • Mail-ID; • Reporting and real-time tracking of generated documents; • Handling peaks and troughs in supplied documents, being able to process large volumes; • Quality control on outgoing letters. Fluvius expects the service provider to carry out a number of optimisations to the existing services, such as, but not limited to: • Minimising dependence on pre-printed documents (stock, replenishment, version control, etc.). • Minimising set-up costs; • Reporting and real-time tracking; • Simplified and more transparent price table and bill of quantities, which allows for more conclusive and faster approval; • Monitoring innovations in print technology and proposing new possibilities and more efficient techniques; • Introducing new templates and replacing existing templates must be possible; • More thorough document tracking. • Electronic dispatch, retrieval and processing (e-invoicing, web portal); • Structured feedback on the status and progress of individual documents.
sig_13963b92b10f4f0728f5.title: Printshop

sig_13b301f08a8c88865d6f.description: The subject of the procurement is a framework agreement for planning, implementation, maintenance and development services for road traffic technical control systems to the extent specified in more detail in the procurement documents. Detailed information on the framework agreement is described in Appendix 1 Description of the subject of the procurement. CONTRACT PERIOD The contract period begins upon the signing of the framework agreement and is valid for a fixed term until 31.1.2029. After the fixed-term contract period, the contract may continue with an option period such that the option period is one year in duration. The contract shall terminate automatically if the contract has not been terminated or the option period has not been taken into use. The estimated maximum value of sub-area 3 excluding value added tax is 12 000 000 euros, also including any possible option period. The estimated maximum value of sub-area 4 excluding value added tax is 6 000 000 euros, also including any possible option period. See in more detail Appendix 1 Description of the subject of the procurement.; Assignments for the sub-area may include the tasks of a software integrator and design during the implementation of road traffic technical systems, as well as equipment procurement. The size of the objects ranges from small monitoring points up to the implementation of tunnel technical systems. See in more detail Appendix 1 Description of the subject of the procurement.; System-specific assignments for the sub-area include system monitoring and on-call tasks during the maintenance of road traffic technical systems. See in more detail Appendix 1 Description of the subject of the procurement.; Tasks for the sub-area include architecture, software development and configuration tasks related to the development of road traffic technical systems and information systems. sig_13f9daed6ed6129e1bbd.description: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation that provides a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions designed to support public sector organisations. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders has been extended to 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 14 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

sig_13fa9d304890b65d4737.description: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS All central government departments and UK public sector bodies can access open banking related tools and services. Description Instead of relying on card payments, open banking services provide citizens and businesses with an alternative method of paying and/or receiving money from the public sector. You will be able to access a range of open banking services including: payment initiation service providers (PISPs): let you pay companies directly from your bank account rather than using your debit or credit card through a third party, such as Visa or Mastercard account information service providers (AISPs): being an authorised AISP means that a company can access an individual’s bank account data from their financial institution with their explicit consent To help you find the services and suppliers to meet your needs you will be able to use the following filters: service type total contract value hosting and delivery capabilities This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will run for 8 years. Benefits open banking will reduce customer transaction costs where card payments are the existing and only method of payment payments can be made directly from bank account to bank account without the need to repeatedly input details existing customers of the Payment Acceptance framework can transition to Open Banking includes real time bank account data to confirm payee account details reducing the risk of error payments and minimising losses due to fraud Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS Expires: 07/12/2031 How to buy You can access the Open Banking DPS through the Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace. you will need to select the ‘financial services’ section, and scroll to ‘Open Banking’ Select the ‘access as a buyer’ link. you will then be asked to either sign into your Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace account or register for one Accept the terms and conditions of the DPS as a buyer. You can then view and manage your ‘DPS category exports’ page where you will have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export (this is how you filter the suppliers to find those that can meet your needs) When creating a new category use the filtering tool to specify your needs and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘save category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From the ‘manage your category exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (the export is to an Excel spreadsheet). Close the DPS. Use your supplier shortlist to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers in your shortlist to bid against your detailed statement of requirements, evaluation criteria and contract format. Your supplier list is valid for 2 working days from the date of creation. If you do not use your list within 2 working days you will need to create a new supplier list (follow steps 6 to 10). You can use our eSourcing tool to run a competition or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. read guidance for our eSourcing tool Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your needs. You should allow enough time for suppliers to review, prepare a response and ask clarification questions. Evaluate supplier responses. Award the contract. Put a notification of the award on Contracts Finder. Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. sig_14213528728af17a1ead.description: Procurement and implementation of applicant management software for the Universität Stuttgart Lot LOT-0001: Procurement and implementation of applicant management software. The Universität Stuttgart (hereinafter referred to as the "contracting authority") pursues the objective of digitalising its staff recruitment with the exception of appointment procedures for professorships. Staff recruitment currently still runs largely manually and with media breaks. This causes additional effort, makes uniform documentation more difficult and makes the procedures less traceable. For applicants, entering the process is often cumbersome and no longer up to date. This can impair the candidate experience and the employer attractiveness of the contracting authority. A digital solution is already in use for individual target groups. However, the contracting authority pursues a uniform BMS strategy for the entire university. Therefore, an applicant management system (AMS) is to be introduced as a central solution. The objective is end-to-end digital support from the job request to recruitment preparation. At the same time, it is to ensure barrier-free, simple and transparent workflows as well as structured, timely and documentation-secure procedure execution. A uniform digital standard is planned for the central administration and central facilities. Faculties and institutes can initially use the AMS optionally
sig_14213528728af17a1ead.title: Procurement and implementation of applicant management software

The Updated Response Date is: 1 December 2026. The Inactive Policy will remain as "15 Days after Response Date." **UPDATE** 21 August 2026** The Government has made available via DoD SAFE transmissions the following documents to interested vendors (in good standing on SAM.GOV) who have contacted the Government POCs in this RFI: (CUI) MEO Epoch 3&4 Industry Day Briefing 07_22_2026 (CUI) Epoch 3&4 Market Research RFI CUI Industry Day Q&A Document 08_20_2026 (CUI) Instructions for the Release of Attachments to MEO Epoch 3&4 Market Research RFI 08_20_2026 Additionally, the Primary Point of Contact (Contracting Officer/Agreements Officer) has been updated, to Capt Kerry Kearschner, USAF. Email: kerry.kearschner@spaceforce.mil. The following companies were added to the list of entities/contractors supporting SSC/SYD 84 and its affiliated government organizations: The Tech7 Company and Galaxia If the respondent disagrees with the release of its RFI response to any of the aforementioned firms, the respondent must clearly state this restriction in the cover letter accompanying the RFI response. **END OF UPDATE** Description SSC requests industry feedback on a Resilient Missile Warning and Tracking (MWT) Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) layer Epochs 3 & 4 (E3&4) production feasibility that will support MWT Full Warfighting Capabilities (FWC). The government is seeking industry feedback to inform the MEO E3&4 acquisition strategy and technical approach. The MEO MWT architecture is being incrementally developed in capability-based deliveries called Epochs. Each Epoch is expected to include at least one competitive award and allows for insertion of new technology and innovative solutions in response to progressive or updated warfighter requirements to ultimately meet Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR) capability needs. This RFI requests industry feedback and approaches to support delivering a MEO MWT E3&4 capability. The government encourages capability providers to offer responses for individual or multiple elements of the system architecture: Epochs 3 & 4 Space Vehicles (E3&4 SVs) - delivery, integration, and operations MEO Ground - ground segment with facilities and sites to operate the entire MEO MWT constellation with respect to Command and Control (C2) Digital Engineering Integration in alignment with Government Digital Engineering vision Contract Type The government is intending to use only Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract type with an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement. Feedback on this approach is welcome. Small Business Consideration The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 - Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The small business size standard is 1,000 employees. Participation from small and small disadvantaged businesses is encouraged. SSC's Small Business points of contact can be reached at smallbus@spaceforce.mil or by phone at (310) 653-1108. Small Business Opportunities The government would like to encourage small business participation in the performance of this effort and requests insight into how your company would incentivize Small Business participation. Provide an assessment of potential subcontracting opportunities. Do you have any recommendations to increase small business participation under this effort? Is there a more appropriate NAICS code to advertise this effort to maximize competition in industry? sig_14447123245a33497af0.description: Digital workstations are essential for the efficient fulfilment of the performance mandate of a modern public administration. The currently installed devices, such as hardware, multi-function devices and peripheral devices (keyboards, mice, etc.), are to be successively replaced for ITSH customers and service recipients. Furthermore, due to mobility and digitalisation, requirements regarding new working requirements in terms of digital workstations have changed in recent years. The current client infrastructure is to be unified and standardised in order to ensure future-oriented, smooth and economical operation in the longer term. Notebooks, convertibles, tablets, monitors and peripheral devices (keyboards, mice, headsets, etc.) as well as printers and multi-function printers are to be procured via this public tender. A service provider is also being sought to take over the software packaging service for ITSH. Lot 1 involves procuring client hardware in its various configurations. For this purpose, a service provider is sought which can purchase these devices, pre-configure and deliver them in accordance with ITSH requirements, and which is capable of continuously adapting its service along the evolving service level of ITSH and the roadmap of the manufacturer or manufacturers of the devices. It should also be possible to procure unmanaged devices, namely iOS, Android and Windows tablets and non-standard Windows clients, via the service provider. sig_14477e0eda5db20a0de9.description: Ministerstvo financí (hereinafter also "MF" or "contracting authority") carried out an open procurement procedure in the past half-year for the award of the public contract "Delivery and implementation of nIISSP DWH and provision of operational support services and development services II". The contracting authority did not receive any tenders in the given procurement procedure, as a result of which it was forced to cancel the procurement procedure. The need to ensure the functionalities currently provided by the State Treasury Integrated Information System (hereinafter "IISSP") continues to exist, and for this reason the contracting authority politely asks potential tenderers for their comments as part of the preliminary market consultation. In the cancelled procurement procedure, the MF attempted to secure an optimal setting of rights and obligations in the contractual relationship with the tenderer for the Czech Republic. The contracting authority's aim was to open up competition to more qualified tenderers, enable performance to be implemented using various technological solutions, and at the same time avoid legal or factual dependence on a single tenderer. Last but not least, the MF endeavoured to ensure the future functioning of nIISSP while complying with all obligations arising from public procurement law and the principles applicable to the management of public funds. In retrospect, the MF considers the requirements in the original procurement procedure to be justified. However, in a situation where no tenderer was found under the stipulated conditions who was qualified and at the same time willing to accept the requirements, the contracting authority is proceeding to consider reassessing the configuration of the original public contract. The MF approaches this possibility very seriously and asks potential tenderers for a similar approach. However, the accommodating approach of the contracting authority, even in a new procurement procedure, cannot lead to a complete resignation from the above-mentioned objectives. Tenderers should therefore submit proposals that are realistic and at the same time as specific as possible. The preliminary market consultation will be conducted in the form of completing this questionnaire and subsequently through potential in-person meetings. The second part of the PMC will be carried out with tenderers who send their response to this questionnaire within the PMC – participation is also possible together with business partners, e.g. a representative of the software manufacturer. You can send the documents to the MF's data box or to the email: verejne.zakazky@mf.gov.cz, preferably by 1. 7. 2026. The MF will also take subsequent responses into account. It is not necessary to answer all areas. If you have any questions about this document or need further information, you can contact the Public Procurement Department of the Ministry of Finance at the stated email address.

sig_1454ce8d74395c6f923e.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 ARA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial Announcement ADVANCED RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT (ARA) TITLE: ADVANCED TRACKING ARCHITECTURE USING AI (ATA-AI) BAA or ARA NUMBER: FA8750-24-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step ARA which is open and effective until 12 July 2029. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 5pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 12 July 2029, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY25 by 30 NOV 2024 FY26 by 30 NOV 2025 FY27 by 30 NOV 2026 FY28 by 30 NOV 2027 FY29 by 30 NOV 2028 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. ARA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this ARA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $10M. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based procurement contracts or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive ARA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. sig_14adc2b679f6a8cd4621.description: The project "Vaccines for Africa: Roll out and Production in South Africa" (SAVax) is part of South Africa's strategic objective to enhance the local production of vaccines, medicines, and health technologies. Co-financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the European Union (EU), SAVax aims to strengthen local manufacturing capacity in the biopharmaceutical industry and improve access to essential health products. The initiative aligns with the goals of key South African government partners, including the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI), the Department of Health (DoH), and the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA), to create a sustainable and competitive biopharmaceutical sector. The project aims at supporting selected South African biopharmaceutical companies with "ready-for-market" products, providing targeted technical assistance to improve their manufacturing capacity, and enhancing market access at national, regional, and continental levels. These companies face challenges such as market intelligence gaps, demand forecasting difficulties, high production costs, and technology transfer obstacles, which impede their ability to meet growing health needs. Addressing these challenges requires long-term strategies, including off-take agreements, purchase guarantees, and investment in technology and skills development. Lot LOT-0001: 81322845-MAV+: Technical assistance for selected companies in the pharmaceutical sector in South Africa for the SAVax project. SAVax conducted a landscape assessment of South Africa's biopharmaceutical industry, covering the pharmaceutical, biotechnological, and biomanufacturing sectors as well as a call for applica-tions for companies to self-identify their technical assistance needs. The objective of this assignment is to engage a service provider to provide tailored technical assistance for the selected companies in the biopharmaceutical sector. This technical assistance aims at enhancing the capacities of companies to gain market access with their products. The goal is to equip these companies with the knowledge and skills necessary to advance their products to market access. The selected companies will receive targeted, non-financial support addressing the technical, regulatory, organizational, and strategic challenges they face in advancing biopharmaceutical products to market. Support areas may include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Technology Platforms and Innovation Readiness o mRNA Technology Transfer Support: Assistance in understanding, adapting, or implementing mRNA-based platforms, including guidance on formulation, delivery systems, process design, cold-chain logistics, and regulatory considerations for mRNA therapeutics or vaccines. o Digitisation of cGMP Systems: Support in planning and implementing digital systems for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance. This includes electronic batch records, quality management systems (QMS), equipment calibration tracking, and data integrity solutions aligned with international norms. 2. Regulatory and Quality Systems Strengthening o Navigating Regulatory Pathways: Tailored guidance for interacting with SAHPRA and other relevant authorities (e.g. WHO Prequalification), including dossier preparation, clinical trial applications, reliance mechanisms, and fast-track pathways. Also includes strategic regulatory planning for biosimilars and advanced therapies. o Quality Management Process Strengthening: Support in designing, upgrading, or implementing fit-for-purpose Quality Management Systems (QMS) based on ICH Q10 principles. This includes standard operating procedures (SOPs), change control, deviation management, and risk-based approaches to quality oversight. o ISO Certification Readiness: Technical support to prepare for ISO 9001, 13485 or other relevant certifications, including gap assessments, internal audits, documentation guidance, and quality culture development. o GMP Training and Compliance Advisory: Provision of technical training in GMP principles, inspection readiness, and facility hygiene requirements, adapted to different staff levels (operators, QA/QC, management). May include site-specific support for corrective/preventive actions (CAPA). 3. Intellectual Property and Commercial Strategy o Intellectual Property (IP) Strategies: Support in designing or refining IP strategies including freedom-to-operate analyses, IP landscaping, filing strategies (local and international), and licensing terms. Emphasis on protection in the context of part-nerships and technology transfer. o Optimising Commercialisation Pathways: Advisory services to develop and refine commercial strategies, including go-to-market models, pricing approaches, and health economic value propositions. May include support in understanding procurement systems (e.g. NHI, pooled African mechanisms). o Market Assessment and Market Access Support: Tailored market research to eval-uate demand, pricing, competition, and policy environments in local and regional markets. Support may include alignment with public procurement frameworks and donor-funded demand sources. 4. Organisational Resilience and Investment Readiness o Financial Restructuring and Strategy Advisory: Guidance on cost structures, business modelling, and capital allocation to improve organisational sustainability. Support may include preparing for audits, understanding grant or equity implications, or structuring financials for growth. o Managing Investor Relations: Capacity-building on investor engagement, including pitch deck refinement, term sheet review, investor reporting frameworks, and relationship management practices that align with sector expectations. o Mentorship Programmes: Pairing of companies with seasoned executives, technical experts, or entrepreneurs who can provide continuous coaching in technical, strategic, and commercial areas. Structured mentorship plans with KPIs will be encouraged. 5. Human Capital and Collaboration o Strategies for Talent Development and Retention: Development of internal work-force strategies including upskilling plans, career progression models, and organisational culture interventions to reduce talent attrition in critical areas like QC, regulatory affairs, and bioprocessing. o Managing Strategic Partnerships: Support in structuring and managing public-private partnerships, consortia, and technology transfer agreements. This includes due diligence, contractual frameworks, IP considerations, and governance models to ensure mutual value. o Facilitation of International Training Exchanges: Design and support of outbound and inbound staff exchange opportunities with regional or international centres of excellence, including identification of partner institutions, logistics coordination, and documentation of learning outcomes.
sig_14adc2b679f6a8cd4621.title: 81322845-MAV+: Technical assistance for selected companies in the pharmaceutical sector in South Africa for the SAVax project

sig_14d0247c1ab1f9aeecf8.description:
The subject of contracts awarded within the established DPS will be the purchase of cloud services corresponding to IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and other models, cloud service support services, cloud migration services, or other related services that meet the legal conditions of publicly available services. Cloud services are services provided as services in the public part of the government cloud or in the form of a private government cloud. The subject of the contract is the supply of a cloud service provided in the form of "Cloud as a Service", which will be located in the customer's data centre in the territory of the Slovak Republic as a central private cloud cloud service. The cloud service is to consist of one region and three fault domains. The exclusive customer of this service will be the Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization of the Slovak Republic (hereinafter referred to as MIRRI). The cloud service consists of / is implemented via partial cloud services, the minimum scope of which is defined below in the text, as well as in Annex No. 6 of the call for tenders. The cloud service will ensure the development, testing and operation of IT projects supported by the Recovery and Resilience Plan and other sources. This cloud service will serve as an extension of the government cloud to a hybrid form. Cloud services will allow access to management bodies (hereinafter referred to as "MB"), which will be able to effectively use cloud services for their specific needs and requirements in a dynamic environment. Cloud services support scalability and high availability. Cloud services will be provided as a centralised private cloud solution, which will ensure the development, testing and operation of IT projects supported by the recovery plan and other sources. The cloud service must allow operation without internet connection for a period of at least 30 days and provide full functionality controlled via a web portal. Cloud services must be available in an identical form in the public cloud in at least three different countries within the EU. The cloud service is to allow the management of at least two locations and their interconnectivity without the need for modifications, including full operation of disaster recovery locations (hereinafter referred to as "DR") with the possibility of using synchronous and asynchronous replication, via a central web portal. The web portal (SelfService portal) is to provide basic functions for dashboard visualisation in both the user and administrator interface in order to improve navigation and the gathering of necessary information. Overall, the web portal is to ensure important dashboard visualisation functions for users and administrators, which is to lead to better navigation and the retrieval of necessary information concerning, for example, network infrastructure and compute utilisation metrics, etc. For administrators, the web portal is to be a fully fledged tool for environment management. The cloud service must allow physical connection to the internal networks of the MBs, specifically by connecting to the GovNet and internet networks. The GovNet node is not the subject of the contract. Information necessary for connection to the GovNet network is available at https://www.nases.gov.sk/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Poziadavky_na_uzol.pdf. The GovNet node will connect at a speed of max. 10 Gbps and a contiguous address range from GovNet private IP addresses, e.g. 100.x.x.0/20, will be allocated for the node. The cloud service must support multi-tenancy with logical separation of the MB environment, which will be able to support a function that will allow the MB to create its own logical division for its subordinate organisations in their environment. Interconnection within multi-tenancy will communicate via the internal and fast network of the solution (backbone) and must not go out to the internet. The cloud service must allow the definition and enforcement of policies and audits for the multi-tenant solution, which will help ensure proper governance and control. This will ensure effective governance and control over the entire solution. The cloud service must ensure a high level of security, including network security and access management. The aim is to protect data and applications from various security threats and attacks. The solution is also to provide basic security functions such as authentication, which verifies the identity of users and services, authorisation, which sets permissions and access rights, and data encryption using the MB's private keys, which minimises the risk of leakage or compromise of sensitive information during transmission and storage. The cloud service must allow efficient cost management using recommendations and forecasts that help achieve better prices. This means it must include a clear dashboard that allows monitoring and prediction of costs for resources running in the cloud environment. In addition, it should be possible to assign budgets and set soft limit thresholds, which the system will automatically notify about when exceeded. All this will contribute to more effective cost management and better stewardship of financial resources. The cloud service must allow automatic scaling within a specified range. The cloud service must support Windows, RHEL, Suse, CentOS and Ubuntu operating systems, and at the same time must allow the use of users' own operating system images and licences. The cloud service must allow the use of processors from AMD and Intel and must be able to support the use of both processors simultaneously in the solution. At the same time, the highest over-provisioning value must not exceed 1:4. The cloud service must allow backup management, where each tenant has the option to independently manage their backups (setting retention policies, ad-hoc backups, archive backups, data recovery and others) via the web portal. From our experience, the most frequently used retention policies are operating system (OS) 15 days, for databases (DB) 35 days and for database logs (DB logs) 15 days. For archived data, it is 1 year to 3/5 years. The volumes themselves are in Annex No. 6 row 48 and 49.

The cloud service provides the option of operation in a multi-cloud environment (in cooperation with local solutions, VMware, hybrid cloud solutions, ...) The cloud service provides the option of sharing virtual resources between multiple cloud solutions in a multi-cloud environment or in a real public cloud, while also enabling central management of such a solution. The cloud service must allow the tenant to be able to move workloads from the solution to the public cloud, which are not part of this order.
sig_14d0247c1ab1f9aeecf8.title: Central dynamic purchasing system for government cloud services

sig_14d0e79bb7f7acb2c3a1.description: The Authority seeks to develop a planning tool that enables AI-augmented decision making for planning applications. The initial focus will be on householder developments (as defined in Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015) with a view to expand into further application types within the ‘other*’ category (those not classified as Major or Minor) which represent 69% of all planning applications. *“Other applications” are: advertisements, change of use, householder developments, listed building consents and relevant demolition in a conservation area. Also available at “View PS2 data” and the drop down ”Other” available at: https://app.powerbi.com/view?r=eyJrIjoiMDQ1MmRlMjEtMThlMy00MWIxLThmNTEtMzU4M2I5ODNmYTJlIiwidCI6ImJmMzQ2ODEwLTljN2QtNDNkZS1hODcyLTI0YTJlZjM5OTVhOCJ9 The objective is to dramatically reduce planning application processing times initially targeting a reduction from upwards of 8 weeks to circa 4 weeks, with a long-term vision of near-instant decisions for straightforward applications. All reduction targets do not include elements that solutions cannot be expected to affect i.e. statutory 21-day consultation periods, site visits, neighbour notifications, external consultee responses, and committee scheduling. Proposals will need to demonstrate understanding of the relevant parts of the planning process including administrative processes (e.g. policy research, citation generation, report generation) as well as analytical processes (e.g. material considerations identification, policy compliance assessment, planning balance evaluation, decision reasoning). Solutions should be designed to assist planning officers with the above processes and provide reasoned, verifiable recommendations for decisions. Solutions must be integrated with existing planning systems. As part of the Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage, bidders will be required to participate in a two-week demo build (unpaid) to each develop a working prototype which will be evaluated at "Demo Day". This will take the form of a presentation of the prototype, and this will be evaluated in accordance with the process and award criteria set out in the ITT. During the contract, the service recipients (i.e. those that will use the solution) may include: DSIT MHCLG Local Planning Authorities (317 LPAs) Planning Inspectorate Devolved Administrations Combined Authorities (mayoral authorities with planning powers) National Parks Authorities (separate planning authorities) Broads Authority (special planning authority) Lot 1: .
sig_14d0e79bb7f7acb2c3a1.title: MHCLG Augmented Planning Decisions

sig_14fcd19448edc9fd42e2.description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

sig_157a89f03a3a4cfc1836.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $499M. Individual awards will not normally exceed sixty (60) months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $500K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions and assistance instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Deputy BAA Manager TRISTEN M. CARRIG PETER J. FITZGERALD AFRL/RIGD AFRL/RITGB 525 Brooks Rd 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330- 2558 Telephone: (315) 330-2081 Email: tristen.carrig@us.af.mil Email: peter.fitzgerald.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_157da4527bb7c2c449e0.description: Horsens Municipality is preparing an upcoming tender for an electronic key system and emergency call system for elderly care and, as part of this, wishes to conduct a market dialogue with relevant suppliers. The market dialogue is targeted at suppliers of electronic key systems as well as suppliers that can provide both electronic key systems and emergency call solutions. Background: Horsens Municipality uses digital solutions that support the performance of tasks in home care and care centres and contribute to peace of mind, security and efficient workflows for both citizens and employees. The municipality currently uses an electronic key system that gives employees and partners secure digital access to citizens' homes in connection with the delivery of care and support services. The solution replaces physical keys and includes, among other things, electronic locking units, an administration system, access-granting units and associated operation and support. The solution must support secure, efficient and flexible access to citizens' homes and be simple to administer and use in daily operations. The municipality also uses emergency call solutions at care centres, in other round-the-clock staffed facilities and - to a relevant extent - with citizens who need reassurance technology. The emergency call solutions support citizens' ability to call for help and employees' handling of emergency calls, alarms and other incidents where a rapid response is needed. The solutions include emergency call units, sensors, alarm management and associated administrative functions. Both solution areas support core workflows in the elderly sector and are used by many of the same employees in daily task performance. At the same time, the solutions interact with the municipality's other welfare technology solutions and relevant IT systems. Purpose: The purpose of the market dialogue is to qualify the upcoming procurement and the overall procurement strategy as well as to obtain a better basis for preparing the tender documents. Among other things, the municipality wants the market's input on: - the market's solutions and development in the field, - functional possibilities and needs in modern electronic key systems and emergency call solutions, - implementation, operation, support and service, - integration possibilities with the municipality's other welfare technology solutions, - contractual and commercial conditions that can support an appropriate procurement - other conditions that the market considers essential to ensure a competitive and future-proof tender. As part of the market dialogue, Horsens Municipality also wishes to qualify the decision on the future procurement strategy. Among other things, the municipality is considering whether the electronic key system and emergency call solutions are most appropriately tendered together or separately. The municipality therefore wants suppliers' input on the possibilities of bidding for a combined solution and a solution solely regarding the electronic key system, as well as on how the various models are assessed to affect competition.

sig_158c26522fed5882e7d0.description: The procurement supports the wellbeing services county's own capability to respond to changes in the operating environment and ensures that operating models based on up-to-date development trends and research-based knowledge are in use. The purpose of the service is to support Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue in change and development work by providing expert services that produce concrete, documented and acceptable development outputs for the subscriber. The subject of the procurement is expert services that support the change and development work of Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue in separately definable assignments. The objective of the service is to produce written and acceptable outputs in accordance with the assignment-specific objectives defined in advance by the subscriber, within the agreed schedule and with the agreed workload. The subject of the procurement comprises several key subject areas regarding the reform of the wellbeing services county, which are used to strengthen modern and developing social and healthcare operations and to promote the continuous renewal of services and operating methods. The subject areas may require very broad-ranging expertise in change and development work. Assignments whose procurement value is less than 60 000 € are carried out through the framework system. Assignments larger than this are put out to tender outside the framework system. Each assignment is defined in writing and includes at least: - the objective and delimitation of the assignment - the estimated workload (in person-working days) - the agreed outputs - the schedule - the acceptance criteria An assignment is considered completed when the subscriber has approved the agreed outputs in writing. The subscriber procures the service according to its needs. The subscriber estimates that it will carry out approximately ten to fifteen assignments per year. The subscriber does not commit to a specific procurement volume, nor is it liable for compensation for changes in the procurement volume during the contract period. The supplier does not have exclusivity for deliveries to the subscriber. The supplier's right to offer to others is not restricted. The supplier offers the service to the subscriber within the limits of its capacity, and the supplier is not obliged to keep capacity free for the subscriber. Sub-area 1 covers expert services related to the development and support of project and programme management. Assignments in this sub-area are focused in particular on: - the preparation, guidance and monitoring of individual change and development projects - the development of project models, PMO operating methods and project management practices - project reporting, schedule and resource monitoring The sub-area does not cover the technical design of digital solutions or the strategic development of management systems, which belong to sub-areas 2 and 3.; Sub-area 2 covers expert services that support the development of digital services and processes in accordance with the subscriber's needs. The objective of the service is to strengthen Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue's capability to design, manage and implement the reform related to the development of digital services and to support concrete implementation in various development and change projects. The services that are the subject of the procurement can be used to implement, for example, preliminary studies, descriptions of overall architecture, design of development paths, deployment support, analytics-based development and trials of new innovative solutions. Assignments may also concern method and process support for development, studies related to strategic work or other expert tasks in digital development according to the subscriber's needs. The expert service may focus on, among other things, the following areas: - design, development and deployment of digital services and processes (incl. artificial intelligence development work) - collection and utilisation of customer- and user-oriented data - evaluation and conceptualisation of technical solutions - change support for operations and services - procurement support for digital services or solutions - enterprise architecture work - innovation development work; Sub-area 3 covers expert services that support the development of management, organisation and service production. The subject of the procurement is an expert service whose purpose is to strengthen the development of the subscriber's service production methods, operating models and management. The services support strategic, operational and change-related development. Expert services may include, for example: - design and implementation of strategy/strategic programmes - stakeholder engagement - management development - change management support - design, analysis and implementation of operating models related to organisation - definition of benefit mechanisms and productivity measures and implementation support - service portfolio design and conceptualisation - formation of value networks - development of financial management processes - cost and activity-based accounting - procurement support - analytics services and development of data-driven management

The government is seeking industry feedback to inform the MEO E3&4 acquisition strategy and technical approach. Each Epoch is expected to include at least one competitive award and allows for insertion of new technology and innovative solutions in response to progressive or updated warfighter requirements to ultimately meet Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR) capability needs. This RFI requests industry feedback and approaches to support delivering a MEO MWT E3&4 capability. The government encourages capability providers to offer responses for individual or multiple elements of the system architecture: Epochs 3 & 4 Space Vehicles (E3&4 SVs) - delivery, integration, and operations MEO Ground - ground segment with facilities and sites to operate the entire MEO MWT constellation with respect to Command and Control (C2) Digital Engineering Integration in alignment with Government Digital Engineering vision Contract Type The government is intending to use only Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract type with an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement.
