sig_15c36a45adf25d815a70.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. The purpose of this request for information is to survey solutions available on the market and to gather information for a procurement to be carried out later at HUS. The contracting authority is not initiating a call for competition by publishing this request for information; instead, a possible contract notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in a possible subsequent call for competition. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the request for information or for participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of cardiology US/IVUS and MRI analysis software. HUS is seeking an imaging analysis and reporting solution intended for cardiological use and a cardiological temporary archive by means of which it is possible to store, process and analyse cardiological examinations performed primarily with ultrasound devices (US). The purpose of the system or service to be procured is to store and analyse cardiological imaging performed primarily with US devices and to enable the transfer of generated 2D, 3D and 4D examination images and measurement results to HUS's centralised image management and patient information system. The system must enable the viewing, analysis, comparison and reporting of examinations as part of clinical operations. In addition, the solution must include viewing and analysis features used during fluoroscopy procedures (IVUS) and support clinical decision-making during procedures. HUS is aiming for a solution in which ultrasound and fluoroscopy functions are included in the same software package and form a unified clinical working environment. Vendor neutrality is one of the key objectives of the procurement. HUS is interested in solutions that make it possible to utilise image and measurement data produced by imaging devices from different manufacturers in the same environment and that support open standards and interfaces. In addition to ultrasound and fluoroscopy data, HUS is interested in the possibilities of performing corresponding cardiological analyses also from magnetic resonance (MR) and computed tomography (CT) images. The software to be procured is intended to analyse and store cardiac magnetic resonance examinations and enable, among other things, cardiac volumetric and flow analyses (3D/4D), tissue characterisation (T1, T2, T2*, late enhancement) and strain measurements. It must be possible to use the MR software from all HUS locations. These functionalities can be implemented either in the same software package or as a separate software solution. Suppliers can therefore offer separate MR and CT imaging analysis software even if they were not part of the offered ultrasound and fluoroscopy solution. Regarding the solutions on offer, HUS is particularly interested in the following entities: - Analysis and reporting of cardiological US examinations - Processing and analysis of 2D, 3D and 4D image data - Management and transfer of measurement results to image management and patient information systems - Viewing, analysis and decision-making support during fluoroscopy procedures - Vendor neutrality between image and measurement data of different imaging devices - Possibility to analyse also MR and CT image data and related technical solutions - Interfaces (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) and integratability into HUS's system environment - Long-term storage and re-analysis of images and analysis results - Browser-based usage possibilities and remote access - Data protection and information security - Future development paths and analysis features utilising artificial intelligence - Customer references - Supplier support in Finland - Pricing models/bases and, for example, a description of the software licence models We kindly ask suppliers to express their interest in the procurement described above and to state to what extent you would be able to offer a solution to the needs described above and to describe the technical features of the solution you offer, the supported imaging modalities, analysis capabilities, integration possibilities and the development prospects of the solution for coming years. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered the opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may possibly receive preliminary call for competition documents for comment. Please submit responses to the request for information and express your interest no later than by 21.8.2026 at 12:00 to the address: kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must mention "HUS 235-2026 - Cardiological US/IVUS and MRI analysis software".

The contracting authority intends to introduce enterprise-wide uniform, legally compliant and digital records management (e-file). The aim of this market consultation is to gain an overview of available solutions as well as established professional, technical and organisational implementation approaches. In particular, insights are to be gained into: - suitable solution architectures and implementation approaches - integration options into the existing system landscape - requirements for operation, support and governance - automation and AI functionalities - licence, operating and cost models - scalability and future-proofing of the solutions - procedural models for introduction, migration and rollout - experiences from comparable organisations, particularly in the public environment and among KRITIS operators 1. Initial situation The contracting authority currently has a heterogeneous system and information landscape with different storage locations, applications and forms of documentation. Information and documents are stored, among other things, in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint), various document management systems, SAP applications and local storage structures. As an operator of Critical Infrastructures (KRITIS), the contracting authority is subject to special requirements regarding information security, compliance, traceability and the long-term availability of information. The aim is to introduce central and standardised digital records management. 2. Target vision (functional requirements) We are looking for a solution that supports the following requirements in particular: - Central management and provision of files, documents and information - Role- and permission-based access control - Mapping of filing plans, metadata and retention rules - Audit-proof documentation and traceability - Integration of relevant enterprise applications and specialist procedures - Support for automated filing, search and research functions - Scalability for enterprise-wide deployment The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches and technological implementation options. 3. Operation and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services for the operation and further development of digital records management are expected. The future solution is to be operated as a cloud-based service (SaaS). In particular, the contracting authority shall assume the professional management, governance and user and role management. The technical operation of the solution shall be provided by the vendor. Support is expected in the following areas in particular: - Maintenance and further development of the solution - Technical support and error analysis - Implementation of updates and release changes - Support for configurations and system adjustments - Support for operations, performance and interface management - Training and qualification offers for administrators and users Solutions with an established cloud operating model, transparent support services and clearly defined service level agreements (SLAs) are sought. 4. Questions for the market The contracting authority asks interested companies for feedback on the following points: Solution & architecture - What solution approaches do you offer for the introduction of digital records management? - How are file structures, metadata, retention periods and archiving mapped in your solution? - What integration options exist with Microsoft 365, SAP and other enterprise applications? - What automation and AI functions are available? Operation & organisation - How is user, role and permission management carried out? - How are traceability, audit-proofness and audibility ensured? - What governance and compliance functions does your solution offer? - What operating and support models do you offer (e.g. SaaS, on-premises or hybrid)? - What experience do you have regarding the operational effort before and after the introduction of your solution? Scaling & costs - How does your solution scale in terms of user numbers, file volumes and organisational units? - What licence and pricing models are used? - Is the solution multi-tenant capable? - What essential cost and effort factors must be taken into account? Introduction & implementation - How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. project procedure and phased model)? - What timeframe can be expected from experience for the introduction of digital records management? - What success factors and typical challenges should be taken into account on the customer side? - What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in public sector companies or operators of critical infrastructures? The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the above-mentioned questions are answered. On the basis of the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to hold in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. Information and documents are stored, among other things, in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint), various document management systems, SAP applications and local storage structures. As an operator of Critical Infrastructures (KRITIS), the contracting authority is subject to special requirements regarding information security, compliance, traceability and the long-term availability of information. The aim is to introduce central and standardised digital records management. 2. Target vision (functional requirements) We are looking for a solution that supports the following requirements in particular: - Central management and provision of files, documents and information - Role- and permission-based access control - Mapping of filing plans, metadata and retention rules - Audit-proof documentation and traceability - Integration of relevant enterprise applications and specialist procedures - Support for automated filing, search and research functions - Scalability for enterprise-wide deployment The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches and technological implementation options. 3. Operation and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services for the operation and further development of digital records management are expected. The future solution is to be operated as a cloud-based service (SaaS). In particular, the contracting authority shall assume the professional management, governance and user and role management. The technical operation of the solution shall be provided by the vendor. Support is expected in the following areas in particular: - Maintenance and further development of the solution - Technical support and error analysis - Implementation of updates and release changes - Support for configurations and system adjustments - Support for operations, performance and interface management - Training and qualification offers for administrators and users Solutions with an established cloud operating model, transparent support services and clearly defined service level agreements (SLAs) are sought. 4. Questions for the market The contracting authority asks interested companies for feedback on the following points: Solution & architecture - What solution approaches do you offer for the introduction of digital records management? - How are file structures, metadata, retention periods and archiving mapped in your solution? - What integration options exist with Microsoft 365, SAP and other enterprise applications? - What automation and AI functions are available? Operation & organisation - How is user, role and permission management carried out? - How are traceability, audit-proofness and audibility ensured? - What governance and compliance functions does your solution offer? - What operating and support models do you offer (e.g. SaaS, on-premises or hybrid)? - What experience do you have regarding the operational effort before and after the introduction of your solution? Scaling & costs - How does your solution scale in terms of user numbers, file volumes and organisational units? - What licence and pricing models are used? - Is the solution multi-tenant capable? - What essential cost and effort factors must be taken into account? Introduction & implementation - How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. project procedure and phased model)? - What timeframe can be expected from experience for the introduction of digital records management? - What success factors and typical challenges should be taken into account on the customer side? - What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in public sector companies or operators of critical infrastructures? The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the above-mentioned questions are answered. On the basis of the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to hold in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. In this case, the signing of an NDA is necessary.
sig_15d3de0b21e21d2f3694.title: Market exploration for the introduction of digital file management (e-file) at HAMBURG WASSER

sig_166e2f7cc7cf9366a131.description: The Bank of England is reviewing its future requirements for Microsoft support services and is seeking market insight into the support models, service capabilities and commercial approaches available to support its Microsoft estate. At this stage, the Bank has not made any decisions regarding a future procurement. This preliminary market engagement is intended to inform the Bank's understanding of the market, potential service offerings, and future sourcing strategy. The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market feedback on areas including: • Support service models and delivery approaches. • Service capabilities, including proactive, reactive and advisory support services. • Commercial and pricing models. • Service levels, escalation processes and governance arrangements. • Access to specialist technical expertise and engineering resources. • Innovation, automation and emerging support capabilities. • Market trends and developments relevant to Microsoft support services. The Bank welcomes responses from suppliers with relevant Microsoft support services expertise. Feedback received will help inform the Bank's future requirements, sourcing strategy and any subsequent procurement decisions. This Preliminary Market Engagement exercise does not constitute a call for competition and will not result in the award of any contract. The Bank reserves the right to amend the scope, requirements and procurement approach of any future procurement following completion of the engagement process. Lot 1: .
sig_166e2f7cc7cf9366a131.title: Microsoft Support Services

sig_168347a08dd999cc21a1.description: Further development of the green cadastre of the City with County Rights of Pécs based on remote sensing data in the following two parts: 1. Production of GIS analyses and databases 2. Software development Creation, identification and production of a 2D vector database of green spaces located within the territory of the City with County Rights of Pécs, based on data obtained by high-resolution aerial remote sensing and mobile laser scanning methods, arranging these surveyed elements into GIS databases, carrying out particulate matter binding calculations based on the produced database, and developing a software solution for managing the databases. Part 1 (production of GIS analyses and databases) The Contracting Authority prescribes that the survey of the tree stock located within the territory of the City with County Rights of Pécs must be carried out using data produced by high-resolution aerial and mobile laser scanning remote sensing methods. The working area of the LiDAR and mobile laser scanning surveys produced by the aerial and mobile laser scanning remote sensing method covers the central inner area of the City with County Rights of Pécs measuring 62,2 km2. The task of the winning tenderer is to produce a tree cadastre relating to the inner area, which is a vector-graphic database containing point-like elements, specifies the position of individual trees found in the working area in the EOV projection system, and includes the height of each individual tree from the ground at the attribute level for each tree point. The database also contains, in the form of closed polygon shapes, the 2D ground-projected extent of the tree crowns of individual trees. The steps for producing the database are: • Preparation of 1 units of LiDAR-based individual tree databases • Production of 1 units of tree species maps based on hyperspectral data • Estimation of 1 units of foliage mass and foliage area The task of the winning tenderer is also to map the binding (deposition) capacity for airborne dust (PM10 and PM2.5) for the settlement of Pécs in individual tree-level and grid-based spatial resolution. For the tree cadastre database, the winning tenderer must perform a storm risk analysis for each identified individual tree as specified in the technical specification. In the case of storm risk analyses, the building stock of the settlement must also be taken into account, the production of which as input data for the modelling is likewise the task of the winning tenderer. The task of the winning tenderer is to produce the surface cover map in the form of a vector-graphic database built from closed polygon shapes, which contains the respective characteristic urban surface cover green categories spatially in the EOV projection system, with exact extents belonging to each category, with the technical content given in the technical specification. The task of the winning tenderer is the high-precision survey of green space objects and individual trees located in the cemeteries of Pécs with the aid of aerial remote sensing data and field geodetic measurements. In relation to the task parts of the inner-area tree cadastre and dust-binding capacity calculation, the winning tenderer must prepare and hand over the following databases to the Contracting Authority: • 1 units of individual tree-level vector databases • 1 units of grid-based dust-binding maps • 1 units of thematic maps ready for map display • 1 units of technical documentation The detailed description of the subject matter of the procurement is contained in the technical specification forming part of the procurement documents.; Part 2 (software development) The task of the winning tenderer is the further development of the currently used Green Area Cadastre GIS system of the City with County Rights of Pécs (1 units of software development) as follows: 1. Further development of the "topoXpress" application with PMxx calculation 2. Development of the topoXpress and "Biokom_0401" project for surveying with data validation 3. Development of the system with residential tree planting map support 4. Development of the system with a district filter - spatial filtering implemented across multiple layers 5. Development of dxf display 6. Development of the system with Windows proxy support 7. Review of utility protection zones 8. Further breakdown of the utility analysis layer 9. Incorporation of a maximum of 9 units of custom reports into topoXpress 10. Management of attached documents – Desktop 11. Redesign of adoption 12. Web application containerisation / Docker 13. Modernisation of the web application – Node.JS & Angular The detailed description of the subject matter of the procurement is contained in the technical specification forming part of the procurement documents.
sig_168347a08dd999cc21a1.title: LIFE Development of green space cadastre

sig_16856e52cb32edd04753.description: Wageningen University & Research (WUR) intends to procure a SaaS solution for similarity detection to support academic and scientific integrity in education and research. The solution must enable the comparison of submitted academic and scientific written work against a broad and relevant range of sources, including internet sources, previously submitted work and scientific publications, including relevant full-text paywalled scientific content. The scope of the contract includes the provision of the software as a service, implementation and configuration, integration with relevant WUR systems, including Brightspace and OSIRIS Zaak, transition and migration where applicable, maintenance, support, information security, privacy and related service provision. WUR is conducting a restricted procedure. Following the selection stage, WUR intends to invite a maximum of five suitable Candidates to participate in the contract award stage, in accordance with the Selection Guidelines. The estimated contract value is indicative and does not constitute a budget, guaranteed turnover or minimum purchase commitment. The actual contract value will depend on the Tender and the services actually provided during the term of the Agreement.
sig_16856e52cb32edd04753.title: Similarity detection software

sig_16884a1efb8ea7b001c9.description: Essex County Council (ECC) are seeking a comprehensive Enterprise Architecture Transformation Tool to support the Council's ongoing Local Government Reorganisation journey. ECC is undertaking this Preliminary market engagement notice (PME) to engage with potential suppliers to understand market capability and available solutions to help develop the Authority's requirements and inform the procurement strategy. ECC is looking to understand more about tools that can provide the following outcomes: • Help manage and simplify the complexities of our transformation, guiding robust decision-making around investment priorities. • Deliver actionable insights for Operations, Products, Cyber, and Functional Services teams, underpinned by measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that track the business maturity, resilience, user outcomes, and service performance. • Enable the enterprise architecture to clearly demonstrate value, inform and justify decisions to enhance services, reduce organisational risk, and improve the experience for users. • Integrate seamlessly with ECC's existing digital platforms and services across multiple tenancies, handle large volumes of data, and provide outputs that are accessible and useful for officers at all levels within the council. • Offer a maturity model that has proven effective in other local government authorities, to support ECC throughout this significant transformation. • Assess and map the digital and data assets across the Essex region. • Support the consolidation and rationalisation of the digital applications and contracts to achieve greater efficiency. • Provide visibility into known and unknown areas, with the ability to prioritise and rank risks, thereby strengthening decision-making. In summary, ECC require a mature, proven tool that will not only enable it to govern and improve its transformation journey, but also drive business value, mitigate risks, and deliver measurable outcomes for teams and communities. ECC is in its earliest stages of generating requirements and therefore for any future potential procurement opportunity for an Enterprise Architecture Transformation Tool, it is anticipated that requirements, scope and timelines will be refined/amended following PME. Therefore, there is no commitment or guarantee that procurement activity will go ahead. Lot 1: .
sig_16884a1efb8ea7b001c9.title: Enterprise Architecture Transformation Tool

sig_16964a072bf6f2732818.description: INVITATION TO MARKERT DIALOGUE With this RFI Yle invites interested suppliers to participate in the market dialogue held prior publishing the call for tenders (RFQ or RFP). In this RFI, Yle is looking to identify the solutions available in the market that could meet Yle’s needs. In the RFI process, Yle may schedule meetings with a few chosen suppliers. Yle is preparing a public procurement concerning a solution for media management, archiving, preservation and security. SHORT DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The planned procurement concerns a comprehensive solution for: * Long-term Preservation: Archiving and preserving media assets for the long term. * Asset Management and Security: Securely managing, storing, and enabling the retrieval of media assets. * Lifecycle and Metadata Management: Managing the content lifecycle and associated metadata. * System Integration: Seamlessly integrating with existing production and content management systems. * Data Integrity: Guaranteeing data availability, security, and compliance. You can also propose a solution that partly fits our procurement. The procurement is described in detail in the appendices of this RFI. HOW TO PARTICIPATE? Interested suppliers are invited to take part in the market dialogue by sending the response by email to tarjoukset.yle(at)yle.fi at latest by 5th of June 2026. In case you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to contact us. We look forward to your replies. We will review them as soon as they are received. Please include a description or additional appendices covering the following topics in your response: 1) Description of the solution you provide, including a description of which key features are included in your solution a. Description of the proposed solution b. Deployment models (cloud, on-premise, hybrid) c. Scalability and performance capabilities d. Metadata management and search capabilities 2) A short company presentation, including the size of the company in terms of revenue and number of employees. 3) Reference architecture view a. Integration Capabilities, APIs and integration methods 4) Experience with media production ecosystems 5) Description of your cyber security policies and continuity planning a. Data security measures (encryption, access control, auditing) b. Compliance with relevant regulations (e.g., GDPR) c. Certifications and standards 6) Delivery and Readiness a. Typical implementation timelines b. Migration approach and tooling c. Resource requirements from the customer Also we kindly ask you to answer questions in Appendix 3 Questions: Media Preservation and Processing Solution We invite an open discussion and would appreciate your vision for building a solution. Please include different alternatives, any other possibilities, or any potential risks that might interfere with our vision. Yle may invite selected suppliers to bilateral meetings during weeks 21–25/2026. We’ll thrive to send the invitations by early June 2026 at the latest. Appendices RFI, Media storage solution for archiving, preservation, and security Appendix 1 Architecture: Media Preservation and Processing Solution Appendix 2 Use cases: Media Preservation and Processing Solution Appendix 3 Questions: Media Preservation and Processing Solution
sig_16964a072bf6f2732818.title: RFI: Media Preservation and Processing Solution

sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.description: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.
sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.title: The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI

sig_16a2b40e750c13585e40.description: The workload, expectations and demands on teachers has increased. While we can pinpoint different factors contributing to increasing workloads, we don’t know enough about how these manifest themselves for teachers, nor how they vary at different career stages, in different school contexts (high school, primary etc) or across different roles (principal teacher, department head, management etc). This Challenge seeks to reduce teacher workload by developing a strong understanding of the reality of teachers’ different, varying experiences and so drive the development of products that teachers (and related professions) want to use and make a real impact on reducing workload. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-6-reducing-teaching-workload
sig_16a2b40e750c13585e40.title: CivTech 11 - Challenge 11.6 - How can technology reduce teacher workload?

To disseminate the provisional results as they are produced through the established channels and functionalities: Consultation application, Press conference system, Reports, Result files for the media, Consultation terminals, Video/multimedia and Internet. sig_16a777e75b86af434518.description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.
sig_16a777e75b86af434518.title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning

sig_16badbeade9515a7df3d.description: Software Asset Management (SAM) is a strategic business discipline focused on maximizing the value and minimizing the risk associated with an organization’s software assets. It encompasses the end-to-end lifecycle management of software covering procurement, deployment, maintenance, utilization, and retirement to ensure compliance, cost-efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The primary objectives of Software Asset Management (SAM) are to drive down IT expenditure, mitigate legal and compliance risks associated with software ownership and usage, and enhance operational agility and end-user productivity across the organization. At Kent and Essex Police we have a solution we are currently using and have been using for many years. We are now undertaking a strategic review to assess whether a more cost-effective solution is available that can deliver equivalent or enhanced functionality without compromising the capabilities currently provided by the current solution We are looking to establish communication with potential suppliers and initiate preliminary discussions regarding possible solution offerings. Please reach out to: Lovejoy.Mutizwa@beds.police.uk to discuss. Lot 1: .
sig_16badbeade9515a7df3d.title: Asset Tool Management - Kent & Essex Police

sig_16e23817260c8a02cff2.description: 1. The subject of the contract covers the performance of a service consisting in the processing of analogue materials of the central geodetic and cartographic resource (czgik) in the scope of geodetic control networks into digital form and describing them with metadata. Analogue czgik materials in the scope of geodetic control networks cover 100 running metres [lm] (approx. 2870 pieces) referred to as technical reports. Individual reports can be divided into generic groups: 1) duplicates of topographic descriptions – in the form of transparent foils collected in a report for a specific area in format a5 – approx. 430 reports (approx. 12 lm); 2) tabulograms – reports in the form of bound (with staples or thread) compilations – approx. 60 reports (approx. 8 lm); 3) explanations to card index catalogues – reports in the form of bound (with staples or thread) compilations – approx. 430 reports (approx. 8 lm); 4) metrics of card index catalogues – reports in the form of bound (with staples or thread) compilations – approx. 800 reports (approx. 13 lm); 5) coordinate lists – reports in the form of bound (with rivets, staples or thread) compilations – approx. 430 reports (approx. 7 lm); 6) card index catalogues – a collection of card indexes of horizontal geodetic control point data in the form of single double-sided cards or collections of several cards bound with staples, collected into reports for a specific area - approx. 280 reports (approx. 27 lm); 7) coordinate adjustment reports – a collection of materials in the form of single sheets, bound sheets (with staples), sketches – approx. 440 reports (approx. 25 lm). 2. A detailed Description of the Subject of the Contract constitutes Appendix No. 1 to the SWZ.

sig_17050fcae1aedbdb2830.description: The Department of Neurosurgery at Heidelberg University Hospital is one of Europe's leading neurosurgical institutions, treating the entire spectrum of neurosurgical specialisms operatively in high case numbers. To improve the quality of treatment for the overall medically highly complex patient population, the replacement procurement of a navigation system for the central operating theatre is intended, which is justified by the end of service provision for the old device (out of service). The aim of the procurement is to achieve a technical upgrade of the overall installation by replacing the existing device without compromising established surgical techniques, optimised operating theatre workflows, or the competence of already trained user groups. In addition, the improved performance parameters of a new system result in efficiency potentials for improved economic efficiency of use. Lot LOT-0001: Operating theatre navigation system. To do justice to the broad service spectrum and the medically highly complex service offering of the Neurosurgery Department at Heidelberg University Hospital, the following criteria must be unconditionally met for the award: 1. The product must be usable both cranially and spinally and must strictly fulfil the following technical requirements: a. The system must be capable of being used interdisciplinary both for interventions on the head including common image fusion and fibre tract reconstruction procedures as well as with the integration of external examinations (TMS), and must be suitable for instrumentations on the spine as well as for guided biopsies and stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). b. Integration of the existing Zeiss Kinevo microscope for cranial interventions incl. the possibility of projecting planning data of multimodal neuronavigation as semi-transparent structures into the heads-up display. c. Integration of an intraoperative MRI and data transfer with the possibility of automatic MRI-based patient registration. 2. Secure integration into the existing and proven IT and server infrastructure of Heidelberg University Hospital must be ensured for smooth and reliable data transmission and planning of surgical interventions via remote access, and must fulfil the following requirements: a. Integration into the existing, centralised server infrastructure for neurosurgery, OMFS and ENT incl. implementation of fail-safe data communication. b. Connection and compatibility of all relevant navigation systems at Heidelberg University Hospital and automatic data synchronisation. c. Flexible data access to the planning server from the navigation unit as well as from any computer in the hospital network incl. the possibility of multiple simultaneous user accesses. d. Possibility of access to advanced planning software for installation on a local server infrastructure for spinal and cranial interventions, including module for rigid as well as elastic image fusion, module for fibre tract reconstruction (probabilistic/deterministic), module for automated planning of pedicle screws based on CT data, as well as a stereotactic planning package incl. a patient-specific segmentation algorithm for the automatic generation and display of risk structures. 3. Taking into account the local personnel and spatial conditions, integration into the existing navigation infrastructure as well as a modular concept for the demand-oriented use of the individual components is required in the sense of preserving user competencies and reducing space requirements. The following requirements must be met: a. Incorporation into existing user workflows as well as the software-side user experience to preserve the existing and long-term established competencies of the users. b. Independently usable mobile navigation system for spinal and cranially navigated interventions with the modular connection option to existing robotic systems from the same manufacturer and/or imaging units. 4. The possibility of shared use of the individual components with neighbouring departments must be possible taking into account local conditions (device sharing): a. Interdisciplinary planning server for shared use for cranial, spinal, OMFS & ENT interventions. b. Interdisciplinary navigation system for cranial, spinal & ENT interventions. c. Interdisciplinary robotics solution for spinal and cranial indications (incl. biopsy & SEEG). d. Interdisciplinary 2D and 3D imaging for spinal, cranial, OMFS and ENT interventions. 5. The manufacturer must have a high-performance service network in Germany to ensure high availability of the installation for patient operations. The possibility of remote maintenance and remote access must be provided. 6. The contractor guarantees compliance with all statutory provisions applicable to the device, in particular MDR (EU) 2017/745, MPDG, occupational health and safety, hygiene, EMC, data protection and radiation protection regulations.
sig_17050fcae1aedbdb2830.title: Surgical navigation system

The dynamic purchasing system will be divided into two categories: 1) Purchase of hardware and hardware product support 2) Purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. The specific scope of the subject of the contract, detailed specification, as well as other supplementary information will be part of individual calls for tenders within the established DPS, which will be sent to all candidates included in this category via the JOSEPHINE electronic tool for CPV codes: 30200000 Computer equipment and supplies 30210000-4 Data processing machines (hardware) 30230000-0 Computer-related equipment 32400000-7 Networks 35125100-7 Sensors 48820000-2 Servers 72600000-6 Computer auxiliary services and consultancy 72700000-7 Computer network services The subject of individual contracts may also include, to the necessary extent, related services standardly provided with the relevant HW, e.g. in cases where the manufacturer requires installation/activation by the vendor (certified technician of the supplier). sig_173829bb99ce680ac230.description: Development of an innovative system which will provide important tourist information in a fast and simple way, as well as a series of useful functions such as automated tourist services, effective search for tourist attractions, provision of information regarding real distances, travel, fares, tickets. Furthermore, the system will aim at the provision of maps, accessibility to information regarding means of transport (in cooperation with OASA), the ability to submit questions / complaints, the ability to search regarding topics concerning culture, as well as the ability to inform citizens / tourists regarding severe weather phenomena, announcements, flight and route reminders (in cooperation with the airport system) as well as reminders for specific events etc. The action will include support for stakeholders (local administrations, destination management and promotion organisations, transport authorities (airports, ports), points of cultural interest (museums and archaeological sites) and businesses providing services to tourists/visitors. The purpose of the project is the promotion of Greece as a tourist destination through ICT actions that will lead to the digital transformation of the Greek National Tourism Organisation. The subject of the project is the development of an innovative system which will provide important tourist information in a fast and simple way, as well as a series of useful functions such as automated tourist services, effective search for tourist attractions, provision of information regarding real distances, travel, fares, tickets. Furthermore, the system will aim at the provision of maps, accessibility to information regarding means of transport (in cooperation with OASA), the ability to submit questions / complaints, the ability to search regarding topics concerning culture, as well as the ability to inform citizens / tourists regarding severe weather phenomena, announcements, flight and route reminders (in cooperation with the airport system) as well as reminders for specific events etc. The action will include support for stakeholders (local administrations, destination management and promotion organisations, transport authorities (airports, ports), points of cultural interest (museums and archaeological sites) and businesses providing services to tourists/visitors. The purpose of the project is the promotion of Greece as a tourist destination through ICT actions that will lead to the digital transformation of the Greek National Tourism Organisation. In the context of the project, a platform will be implemented which, as a tool, will contribute to the design and implementation of a strategy for the promotion of the sensitive and volatile tourism product. It will focus on the creation of added value for every tourist destination and its involved stakeholders, contributing to the implementation and service of the goals of integrated marketing and communication strategies and, through a customisable web platform, to the targeted provision of information for tourist products as well as points of interest, both via the internet and via mobile phone. The project will contribute gradually and among other things, to the increase of the competitiveness of every city/region, so that there is a positive impact on investments (ROI), real estate, infrastructure and the various cultural events that can take place in it, through the digital interconnection of content / information with the relevant points of interest throughout the country. Furthermore, the goal is the improvement of the quality of life of residents and the provision of a unique experience to visitors, the strengthening of entrepreneurship and the highlighting of the particular identity and attractiveness of a city / region. After the creation of the platform and the corresponding applications, training of the executives/users of the Operating Body and all stakeholders involved in this contract will take place.

With this market consultation, Omgevingsdienst IJsselland aims to gain insight into what is market-conform, feasible and future-proof, so that any potential procurement optimally aligns with the possibilities of the market, the needs of the organisation and the applicable statutory obligations. In addition, Omgevingsdienst IJsselland wants to test which contract forms, cooperation models and service elements contribute to an effective and sustainable partnership. sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-2-scaling-dynamically-service-management-capabilities
sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.title: Civtech 12 - Challenge 12.2 - How can technology enable fast-growing digital public service providers to dynamically scale their service management capabilities as demand, complexity and customer expectations increase?

sig_17a9711e715ab8f79e5c.description: The workload, expectations and demands on teachers has increased. While we can pinpoint different factors contributing to increasing workloads, we don’t know enough about how these manifest themselves for teachers, nor how they vary at different career stages, in different school contexts (high school, primary etc) or across different roles (principal teacher, department head, management etc). This Challenge seeks to reduce teacher workload by developing a strong understanding of the reality of teachers’ different, varying experiences and so drive the development of products that teachers (and related professions) want to use and make a real impact on reducing workload. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-6-reducing-teaching-workload

sig_17b52fab6d56e98718f5.description: Existing EV Charging infrastructure within Thames Water is ageing and does not meet the needs of the business in the future. Due to changes in supplier capability and to aid in reducing our carbon emissions, TW is aiming to ensure our infrastructure is capable of supporting a transition from ICE ( Internal Combustion Engine) vehicles to EVs in the future. To enable this transition of our fleet, we also need to consider the infrastructure required to keep these vehicles moving, and the systems needed to ensure our operations can continue to run smoothly with minimal impact to our customer service and downtime. Thames Water reserves the right to refine the award criteria. Please note that that deadline for asking for access to the PSQ & submitting of the PSQ is 14 January 2026, at 10 am. Lot 1a: E- Mobility Service Provider Platform. A centralised e-mobility platform to manage all existing and future electric vehicle charging infrastructure across its estate. This platform will provide a single source of truth for charger usage, billing, user access, and operational insights, enabling the organisation to maximise charger uptime and support sustainable fleet operations. Lot 1b: Site Charging Infrastructure. The requirement under Lot 1b - Site Charging Infrastructure covers the supply, installation, and ongoing maintenance of chargers at selected Thames Water sites. The successful provider will be expected to supply chargers that meet the technical requirements set out in the specification, provide a minimum three-year warranty (with preference for a five-year warranty) for all installed chargers, and deliver 24/7 support services for the duration of the warranty period to ensure operational reliability and continuity.
sig_17b52fab6d56e98718f5.title: Electric Vehicles and Charging Infrastructure

sig_17e1631a4186f5375453.description: INFORMATION REQUEST HUS is preparing a procurement concerning the laboratory production management system (LIS system) and associated operational, support and maintenance services for the use of HUS Diagnostic Centre. The purpose of the information request is to survey solutions available on the market, suppliers' capabilities, implementation and commissioning models, life-cycle cost factors, and the appropriate scoping and procurement model for the procurement. This information request is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, and responding to it does not bind HUS or the respondent. This information request does not initiate a tendering competition. HUS Diagnostic Centre is the leading producer of clinical laboratory services in Finland. The Diagnostic Centre operates in eight medical specialties and is responsible nationally for a number of highly specialised examinations as well as research and teaching pertaining to a university hospital. The Diagnostic Centre operates within primary healthcare and specialist medical care in the regions of Uusimaa, Kymenlaakso and South Karelia. The laboratory operations of HUS Diagnostic Centre and their key functionalities are described in more detail in Appendix 1, HUS Diagnostic Centre laboratory operations and key functionalities. The objective of HUS is to reform laboratory production management such that the future LIS solution or LIS solution package supports high-quality, safe and cost-efficient laboratory operations as well as the continuous development of operations in accordance with HUS's strategy. The solution must serve the common and specialty-specific needs of the various laboratory specialties of HUS Diagnostic Centre. The objectives are: • to streamline and appropriately harmonise laboratory processes • to reduce manual work and the risk of human error • to improve patient safety, traceability, usability and operational efficiency • to enable a broader utilisation of automation, reporting and artificial intelligence than at present • to provide a real-time situational picture for operational monitoring and management • to ensure secure and smooth information flow between laboratory analysers, other laboratory equipment, HUS, client organisations, national services and other systems • to enable the scalability, adaptability and cost-efficient development of the solution throughout its life cycle. HUS has not at this stage defined a single pre-selected system or architecture model to achieve the target state. The solution may be based on a single comprehensive solution serving different laboratory specialties, a package comprising multiple compatible LIS solutions potentially produced by different suppliers, specialty-specific solutions, a combination of these or another appropriate implementation model. Through the information request, HUS requests software suppliers' views on what kind of solution and service package would best support the operations of HUS Diagnostic Centre, the needs of the various specialties, the management of integrations, operational continuity, and the life-cycle development and cost-efficiency of the system package. Key benefits, limitations, dependencies, risks and life-cycle impacts of the proposed implementation model are requested to be justified. We ask interested service providers to submit their answers to the questions in Appendix 2 no later than 30.10.2026 at 16:00 (GMT+2) to the email address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The email subject line must include the marking: "HUS 439-2026 Laboratory production management system". Based on the information request, HUS may invite suppliers to separate discussions or visit reference laboratories to inspect solutions available on the market. HUS may utilise the responses received in preparing the subject of the procurement, requirements, pricing model, schedule and procurement structure. Respondents to the information request will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request. Responding to the information request does not oblige the supplier to participate in a tendering competition that may be organised later, nor is it a precondition for participating in the tendering competition. Responding or failing to respond to the information request does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tendering competition. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to execute the procurement in the manner described in the information request, and the contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drafting the call for tenders. The responses provided by suppliers will be treated confidentially.

sig_1800193b1f4f616c40fd.description: The object of this procurement is the acquisition of specialised retro-digitisation services for documents belonging to the physical archive held by the General Directorate of Local Taxes and Fees Sector 3, for an estimated volume of 10.000 linear metres of archive. The requested services aim to convert documents from physical to digital format, as well as ensuring their archival and technical compliance, with a view to implementing an efficient electronic document management system that ensures rapid, secure and legal access to the stored information. The services that are the subject of the procurement include, but are not limited to, the following activities: - collection, handling and organisation of the physical documents existing in the institution's archive; - scanning of documents at technical parameters that ensure the legibility, integrity and fidelity of the digital reproduction; - indexing and association of metadata related to each document or file, in order to facilitate the rapid identification and retrieval of information; - structured organisation of digital documents, so that they can be integrated into existing electronic document management information systems; - quality verification of images and indexing accuracy, to ensure a high level of precision and compliance; - handover of physical documents, together with the resulting digital archive. The final result of the contract will consist of: - digitised and indexed documents, organised in a logical and coherent structure; - an organised and easily accessible archival fund, which allows for the rapid retrieval of documents and their integration into the institution's electronic workflows. By carrying out this procurement, the aim is to create a structural and digitised archive, which ensures transparency, information security, operational efficiency and compliance with the applicable legal regulations in the field of archives and document management. sig_184e668f093a7ce06510.description: SRUC is seeking to implement a fully supported Software as a Service (SaaS) solution that will replace our existing Student Management System and deliver strategic and operational benefits across our undergraduate and post-graduate Teaching activities. The objectives of this procurement include but are not limited to a modernisation and enhancement of our current 1. timetabling system 2. curriculum management 3. applications and admissions systems 4. student registration 5. It is anticipated that the solution will be a modern, future-proofed and highly functional system that shall deliver measurable business efficiencies, benefits and form part of our aspirations for organisation-wide change to processes, systems, controls and employee roles. The solution may also be required to integrate in an up-stream and down-stream manner with other specialist operational systems. It should be noted that SRUC is also considering opportunities to replace its financial and procurement management system within the next 6 to 12 months. The objectives of this project include but are not limited to a modernisation and enhancement of our current 1. operational financial management processes including budgeting, accounts receivable and accounts payable, strategic financial planning and forecasting; 2. procurement and contract management; 3. financial planning and analysis; 4. statutory and management account preparation; 5. tax calculations and return preparation; 6. pre-award & post-award research management; 7. staff expenses; 8. asset and stock management; 9. credit control. The requirement for a third smaller project for a work-based learning system is currently also under review. Any resulting contract for the student management system shall be for an initial period of five years, with the option to extend, by mutual agreement, for five further periods of 12 months. In accordance with the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 the procurement process shall follow a two-stage Restricted Procedure and any subsequent contract award shall be based on the most economically advantageous tender (MEAT). Stage 1: Selection Stage - Open to all interested suppliers - Selection shall be based on capability, capacity, experience and financial standing (using the Single Procurement Document Scotland (SPD)) - The SPD shall be scored on a pass / fail basis. As part of the requirements for this tender, the SPD shall confirm that SRUC is seeking a supplier that is fully accredited under ISO27001 - Written tender submissions (See Stage 2, Part 1) must also be submitted along with the SPD. Stage 2: Tender Stage - Only suppliers that have passed Stage 1 shall proceed to Part 1 (below) and have their written submission evaluated. - Part 1 of the tender stage shall be a formal, written response to questions and submission of an initial price. The top three ranked suppliers (based on their score for the written response to questions) shall then be invited to participate in Part 2 of the tender. SRUC anticipates that one Supplier will be selected to provide this service. Further, it should be noted that SRUC reserves the right to vary the selected numbers. - Part 2 of the tender shall comprise a scored demonstration of the supplier’s system and submission of a final price. It is noted that suppliers can improve and/or vary their price between initial and final submission. It is further noted that SRUC shall not enter a price negotiation with any supplier at any stage of this tender process. - The scoring from Part 1 and Part 2 shall then be combined to provide a final total score, resulting in the identification of a preferred supplier. - Confirmation of a contract award to the preferred supplier shall be subject to approval by the Board of SRUC. It is estimated that any such approval shall be discussed at the September 2026 Board meeting. SRUC regards the implementation of this system as a high risk and complex task. Therefore, SRUC may also seek appropriate implementation consultancy services to support the configuration and implementation of the new system.

sig_18505bd007cfba2ea6ae.description: Following an analysis of existing systems that revealed functional gaps related to reporting, early warning and funding tracking, the contracting authority has determined that the complexity of the Merheim campus project and the requirements of the funding providers necessitate an effective and transparent controlling and communication system. For this purpose, the contracting authority wishes to commission the implementation of an IT-supported system for construction and project controlling for the compliant and auditable management of all projects and sub-projects of the new health campus at the Merheim site, whereby transparency, traceability and early warning in particular must be ensured on all levels via system support. It must be ensured that the integration of existing systems and the connection of relevant interfaces take place smoothly. This includes the transfer and exchange of cost and financial data, the transmission of procurement information and contract award statuses, as well as the provision of structured, role-based access to relevant project data, plans and approvals for external service providers and suppliers. Furthermore, internal audit must be enabled through read-based access rights to ensure the traceability and documentation of internal audits.

sig_185933c236bd984bfad6.description: The Urban Environment Division (KYMP) is procuring an application for infrastructure construction monitoring and situational awareness. It will support the monitoring of infrastructure projects on streets, parks and other public areas from preparation to the expiry of the warranty period, particularly the management, documentation and communication of contract execution phases in field conditions. The system will be used by the city's developers and designers, as well as contractors and design and supervision consultants. In addition, the procurement includes training, further development and expert services to be ordered separately as needed. The contract shall run until further notice. The background and subject matter of the procurement are described in more detail in the appendix Description of the Subject Matter of the Procurement.

sig_1863dee06096214d8eb0.description: Väylävirasto invites you to submit a tender for information security and data protection expert services in accordance with this invitation to tender and its appendices. The procurement is carried out as an internal competitive bidding process under the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Cyber Security and Data Protection Expert Services (2025) (00751) established by Hansel Oy. Väylävirasto has several ongoing administrative or technical projects and initiatives aimed at developing operations, reforming existing information systems or procuring new ones. What all these projects and initiatives have in common is that information security and compliance with central government information security requirements must be implemented in a manner appropriate to the organisation. The subject of the procurement is information and cybersecurity consulting and auditing services. The work will largely take place in a multi-supplier environment, but also as internal consulting for individual projects or initiatives. Information security audits are also regularly conducted in the supplier environment. In addition, an assessment will be made of, among other things, the impact of information security guidelines directed at central government on the projects and operations of Väylävirasto. In addition to the office environment, the subject of the procurement includes the infrastructures managed by the Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency, i.e. state-owned road, rail and waterway routes. Each mode of transport has its own cybersecurity development needs, which may differ significantly in certain respects. The aim of the procurement is to provide Väylävirasto with a partner with whom the development of information and cybersecurity for the organisation and the various modes of transport can be implemented. The competitive bidding concerns the contract period. The aim is that the procurement contract will enter into force on 1.5.2026 and last for five (5) years. See more about the contract period in the chapter "Contract period" of the procurement contract. Assignments will be agreed upon during the contract period. The subject matter of the procurement and the minimum requirements are described in detail in this invitation to tender and its appendices. The estimated value of the procurement during the contract period is 800 000–900 000 EUR (excl. VAT 0 %). One supplier will be selected as the service provider.
sig_1863dee06096214d8eb0.title: Väylävirasto - Expert services for cybersecurity and data protection 2025 (00751) DPS - Expert services for cybersecurity and data protection

BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded.
