Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. sig_18704aa2b30ae6cbe0de.description: The purpose of the public procurement is the acquisition, installation and related services of an electronic legal material registry system for 24 months, which ensures access to legal materials on workstations connected to the NAV internal IT network in accordance with the requirements of the procurement documents. This includes: The subject of the procurement is the legal material of the national legal system, as well as related legal documents, and European Union legal material (hereinafter: electronic legal material collection), serving workstations connected to the central server(s) with low bandwidth on the client side using a web application, providing it for the NAV internal user base of up to 18.000 (potential users), for a minimum of 5.000 concurrent users (simultaneous users) at the same time. The Service Provider must continuously update the electronic legal material collection, with the online processing of legislation published in the Hungarian Gazette taking place no later than the working day following the publication of the given legislation, but at the latest on the 4-th day following the publication. sig_1882821160452191a523.description: Introduction of a cloud-based personnel information system (HR system) The Investitions- und Strukturbank Rheinland-Pfalz (ISB) has been in a state of dynamic personnel change since the COVID-19 pandemic. Since 2021, the headcount has increased significantly and permanently. In parallel, both the requirements for recruitment and the complexity of internal HR processes have risen considerably. Natural staff turnover has additionally led to a continuous increase in the number and variety of processes to be handled. Currently, there is no central, system-supported solution for the holistic management and documentation of HR processes. Payroll accounting, time recording, and access control are handled via external providers, but without integration into a common platform. Further HR processes - including recruiting, pre-onboarding, onboarding, personnel development, target agreements, appraisals, and the administration of personnel costs - are managed manually or via disconnected individual solutions. Personnel files have so far been kept exclusively in paper form or as unstructured text files. This hinders access, causes high space requirements, and harbours risks regarding legibility, completeness, and data protection. The creation and processing of personnel documents is also inconsistent, as each HR officer relies on their own folder structures and individually designed templates. A standardised, quality-assured, and audit-proof architecture is missing. Against this background, the ISB is pursuing the goal of introducing a modern, cloud-based HR software solution that digitally maps all relevant HR processes in an integrated system. The new solution is intended to enable the HR organisational unit to perform its tasks efficiently, transparently, and in a legally compliant manner - regardless of individual working methods or personnel changes. For the HR department, this means a significant reduction in workload through automated workflows, central data storage, and uniform document templates. For managers, the solution opens up the possibility of being actively involved in HR processes via a self-service portal - for example, for approvals, target agreements, or development measures. For IT managers, the solution offers a future-proof, scalable architecture with open interfaces for the integration of existing systems such as payroll, access control, and time recording. And for the board, it creates the foundation for a strategically oriented, data-driven HR management system that supports growth, quality, and compliance in equal measure. The software must be flexibly configurable so that the ISB can design its own workflows and adapt them as required - without being dependent on external programming. A digital, audit-proof personnel file must facilitate access to information and ensure compliance with data protection requirements. Overall, the solution must contribute to making the ISB's HR work future-proof, scalable, and strategically alignable - as a foundation for a modern, service-oriented HR organisation. Service contents: - Digital personnel file and master data management - Time recording and access control - Employee Self Service (ESS) for employees and managers - Applicant and vacancy management - Talent management and personnel development - Personnel cost planning - Travel expense accounting - Appraisal and target agreement processes - Flexible process design - User-friendliness and user guidance
sig_1882821160452191a523.title: Introduction of a cloud-based personnel information system (HR system)

According to Section 9/D (__) of Act 1988 of 2 on Road Traffic, the public service aimed at providing parking for vehicles on local public roads, as well as on private roads, squares, parks and other public areas owned by the local government and not closed to public traffic, shall be provided by the local government or the service provider pursuant to Section 16/A of Act 2011 of on Local Governments of Hungary (hereinafter referred to as the Act on Local Governments). Based on this statutory authorisation, the Contracting Authority carries out parking operation activities within the administrative area of District XI of the Capital City of Budapest, based on the public service contract concluded with the Municipality of Újbuda, District XI of the Capital City of Budapest – which activities are: the operation of public surface parking spaces designated for fee-paying parking owned by the local government within a parking management system, an activity also enabling mobile payment, the operation, modernisation and, where necessary, replacement of parking ticket machines, the performance of parking inspection and surcharge activities, complaint handling and receivables management related to surcharges, and the issuance of parking permits (hereinafter referred to as „parking operation”). The task of the successful tenderer is to provide a software system supporting the public task of parking operation, system support and the provision of related services, as specified in the technical description issued as part of the tender documentation: - installation of a complex parking administration, inspection and operational system complying with the technical specifications on the Contracting Authority's equipment, - training for the Contracting Authority's staff necessary for the operation of the software system, and - provision of technical support via remote monitoring and on-site intervention to the Contracting Authority during the operation of the software system. Information regarding the introduction of the IT professional system supporting parking administration and measures and the operational period: The contract intended to be concluded shall enter into force on the day of its signature. The successful tenderer undertakes to make available, commission and offer for acceptance the IT professional system supporting parking administration and measures no later than 1 January 2026. The Contractor undertakes to train the Ordering Party's employees (20 persons) prior to the handover of the system. The Contracting Authority intends to provide adequate time for the commissioning of the system, training and handover – taking into account the above deadline – and therefore, also considering the time required for the planned public procurement procedure, the Contracting Authority plans to conclude the contract with the successful tenderer no later than 1 October 2025. The introduced system must operate from 1 January 2026 for 24 months, provided that the Contracting Authority may extend the operational period by an additional 24 months by means of its unilateral declaration sent to the successful tenderer no later than 30 days prior to the expiry of the 24-month operational period. Further information is available in the „Description of procurement” section of the notice and in the draft contract. The task of the successful tenderer currently consists of providing software services aimed at the operation/support of 24500 units (which is expected to expand by 50 %) of public fee-paying parking spaces, in which area Siemens Prisma 5 and Nort ParkSolar type parking ticket machines are operated. The software service aimed at operation/support must be provided for at least 35 users performing parking inspections on operational days. Based on the experience of recent years, the software service must ensure the imposition of at least 110.000 surcharges annually. The Successful Tenderer shall, within the scope of its duties, be obliged to: - Provide and operate an administration system supporting parking operations. - Requirement: provision of an administration system supporting the parking operation service – at least at the minimum level specified in the technical description – (transparent and continuous records of data, photographs, payments, deadlines, correspondence, complaint handling, recovery, receivables, as well as data on payment orders, litigation procedures, enforcement): 1 units. - Task: continuous maintenance of the operation and functioning of the administration system during the term, continuous provision of background capacities necessary for operation, storage and backup of data, provision of data access, background customer service and implementation of modifications resulting from legislative changes. - The number of concurrent users to be supported by the administration system on the part of the contracting authority shall be a minimum of 75 persons. Within the framework of the background customer service, the expected volume of complaint handling cases shall reach 15 000 units annually. - Provision of training on the use of the system is expected: at most twice a month and for a maximum of 15 persons per occasion. The monthly level of on-site or premises-based training shall be a maximum of 5 hours/month. - Provision and maintenance of SIM cards required for the parking operation service. - provision of the SIM card operating in the PDAs within a closed APN network at 4G network speed, provided that the mobile service provider is capable of providing this in the operating area; - Expected – based on the relevant authorisation of the contracting authority – continuous maintenance of contact at a necessary and sufficient level with external bodies, conducting matters related to the parking operation service: - OTP Bank Plc. – Electronic terminal; - Data request from the vehicle registry maintained by the Ministry of Energy (KKSZB), within the framework of which the following information is queried: • query of vehicle data based on licence plate number and time • query of personal data and address registry based on 4T (NSZL query), • query of parking card data based on document number, • query of temporary licence plate data based on licence plate number and time. - MOKK – handling of payment orders (FMH) and enforcement; - Magyar Posta Zrt.

– regulation related to official correspondence, management of PEK files; - Nemzeti Mobilfizetési Zrt. mobile parking enforcement; - Municipality of Budapest Capital City issuance/revocation of city hall entry permits; - EPC Plc / Ungarische Autobahn Inkasso Gmbh - data transfer/receipt to service providers specialising in the collection of penalty charges for vehicles with foreign registration numbers; - Reading of bank transaction items - NAV – transmission of issued invoices according to legal requirements The administrative system supporting parking operation must be capable of operating in the Contracting Authority's following already operational hardware and software environment: - unlimited number of handheld computers, of which 30 Catepillar S42H type units are currently available to the Contracting Authority, - unlimited number of mobile printer devices, of which 30 30 Zebra ZQ 521 type units are currently available to the Contracting Authority. sig_18dca3066447c65cf6d3.description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA’s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed above. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed above. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources. Update as of 10/1/26 Submission Format Requirements Use Times New Roman, 12?point font for all text. Maintain 1?inch margins on all sides of every page. The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30?page limit. Please do not paginate these two sections. Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats. Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov. In the email subject line, format the title exactly as: “Response to GSMO?4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]” Scope Guidance NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research. If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate “Limited Scope” on the Cover Page, along with a brief description of the capabilities included. Q&A Sessions The program intends to hold formal one?on?one Q&A sessions with vendors capable of delivering the full contract scope once the RFI period closes. Dates and duration for these sessions are TBD.

sig_18ee903403fc351cf9a5.description: THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer’s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO’s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include “inherently governmental functions” nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to “deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.” The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. Shortterm situations may make performance in excess of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week necessary on occasion. The Contractor must ensure that they can provide for this contingency. 1.6 Tasks. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, Modeling & Simulation (M&S), analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO’s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The Contractor shall conduct the activities and tasks outlined in the following paragraphs. 1.6.1 Multi-Disciplinary Computational Technologies. The Contractor shall develop, sustain and use current and next generation tools. 1.6.2 Software Development and Sustainment. The Contractor shall provide development and sustainment of software tools and applications to support the AFSEO mission. The Contractor shall identify and prioritize AFSEO tool requirements; provide annual strategic execution and project planning, inputs for budget estimates; and execute software development and sustainment projects. These duties include: 1.6.2.1 Providing database software development and sustainment for the AFSEO Compatibility Enterprise System (ACES) and any follow-on systems. The Contractor shall design, edit and sustain ORACLE and SQL Server relational databases; and integrate Common-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) software using Application Programming Interfaces to communicate with ACES when needed. 1.6.2.2 Providing development and sustainment of engineering tools for analysis of aircraft carriage mechanics and carriage interference characteristics to support store compatibility evaluations. This shall include modeling the aircraft store combination for computer simulation, running computer simulations, and documenting changes to existing analysis software. 1.6.3 Computer-Aided Design and Stores Integration. The Contractor shall provide M&S support to include development, testing, and debugging of 3-dimensional and animated modeling software. The Contractor shall work with advanced engineering computer hardware to produce models of, but not limited to aircraft, suspension equipment and stores. These duties shall include: 1.6.3.1 Managing engineering and technical support personnel involved in the digital modeling of aircraft, suspension equipment, and stores and associated test equipment. This includes planning and managing multiple projects and coordinating with Department of War (DoW) management. The Contractor shall also provide required M&S products, perform quality assurance, and perform configuration management of all models and programs produced by the Computerized Physical Fit (CPF) team. 1.6.3.2 Designing, creating, and/or modifying aircraft, suspension equipment, stores and associated test equipment models using engineering drawings of aircraft, suspension equipment, stores, loading equipment and other components and associated physical interfaces. The Contractor shall follow the requirements outlined in MIL-STD-1289D. The Contractor shall perform quality assurance of all models and programs. 1.6.3.3 Using approved programming languages to develop in-house fit check tools of aircraft, suspension equipment and stores that interface with Siemens UGS NX 5 software or Government directed equivalent. The Contractor shall develop user friendly Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) so personnel can perform fit checks without being fully trained in the UGS NX 5 software. 1.6.3.4 Providing support for editing, modifying, and maintaining Siemens UGS files. The Contractor shall design, modify, and maintain relational databases. 1.6.3.5 Providing configuration control for M&S data. The Contractor shall create and maintain model history sheets and develop and execute procedures for archiving all M&S data. 1.6.4 Computational Fluid Dynamics. The Contractor shall perform the evaluation of numerical solution methods, the implementation of these techniques in a production environment, and the performance of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analyses for aircraft and store configurations. The Contractor shall produce and maintain simulation algorithms, codes and pre/post-processing software tools developed specifically for CFD investigations. These duties shall include: 1.6.4.1 Creating 3-dimensional surface and volume grids necessary to generate CFD analyses. The Contractor shall use both structured and unstructured methodologies and shall apply these methods to solve complex aircraft/weapon configurations. The Contractor shall use CFD codes and associated tools supporting the dynamic, time-accurate analysis of bodies in relative motion. The Contractor shall support aerodynamic M&S related to aero-elastic effects, weapon carriage and release, and internal weapons bay physics. 1.6.4.2 Creating 3-dimensional surface and volume grids necessary to generate CFD analyses. The Contractor shall use both structured and unstructured methodologies and shall apply these methods to solve complex aircraft/weapon configurations. The Contractor shall use CFD codes and associated tools supporting the dynamic, time-accurate analysis of bodies in relative motion. The Contractor shall support aerodynamic M&S related to aero-elastic effects, weapon carriage and release, and internal weapons bay physics. 1.6.4.3 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of CFD analysis necessary to complete the store certification process. The Contractor shall document aerodynamic analyses and write justifications to support compatibility issues. 1.6.5 High Performance Computing Software Development. The Contractor shall develop software using an approved Government development process, targeted at High Performance Computing (HPC) hardware. The Contractor shall apply computer engineering principles, practices, and techniques to solve difficult and unprecedented design problems involving HPC hardware. These duties shall include: 1.6.5.1 Managing projects. The Contractor shall coordinate and direct major software development efforts to include HPC hardware optimization and Internet web-enabled applications. 1.6.5.2 Developing software. The Contractor shall develop, using approved Government processes, software implementations of complex software architectures in various computer science languages to simulate multiple physical phenomena on HPC hardware. 1.6.6 Project Management/Project Planning. The Contractor shall provide project management and project planning support using project portfolio management tools specified by the Government for compatibility recommendations to air worthiness authorities and test work requests (to include mission summaries) to test organizations. Examples of recommendations include Recommended Flight Clearances (RFCs), Risk Assessments (RAs), Engineering Letters (ELs), and Certification Recommendations (CRs). In addition, the Contractor shall provide support as described in the following paragraphs. 1.6.6.1 Pre-Project Planning/AFSEO Customer Interface. The Contractor shall ensure that aircraft technical support concerns are addressed early in the developmental phase for each project assigned. This shall include but is not limited to documentation technical reviews, participating in requirement and design reviews and Technical Interchange Meetings (TIM), providing engineering and analysis support, and providing flight and ground test support. 1.6.6.2 Project Planning. The Contractor shall generate a project strategy, to include cost, schedule and requirements for the applicable period of performance for each project assigned. The Contractor shall generate a Statement of Capability (SOC), Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) letter, Project Plan, test work requests, or other documentation as required by the Government. Financial status shall be tracked using appropriate JON and WBS codes, which will be provided by the Government. The Contractor shall begin the execution phase of the project when approved by the Government. 1.6.6.3 Project Execution. The Contractor shall manage the execution of the analysis and test activities according to the Project Plan to meet AFSEO's customer requirements for each project assigned. The Contractor shall maintain current project status (cost, schedule and performance information) in the SEMSS or equivalent database (as determined by the Government) for each project assigned. The Contractor shall use this information to brief AFSEO management on project status, as required. The Contractor shall support meetings and/or conferences that may require travel. 1.6.6.4 Project Documents. The Contractor shall coordinate, generate, track, and revise recommendation documents to airworthiness authorities for applicable aircraft and store combinations for each project assigned. 1.6.7 Compatibility Engineering and Analysis. The Contractor shall provide engineering and analysis to support the AFSEO as described in the following paragraphs. 1.6.7.1 Fit and Function. The Contractor shall provide store fit and function support to determine whether stores are physically compatible with aircraft IAW MIL-STD-1289D. These tasks shall include: 1.6.7.1.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, Memorandum for Records (MFRs), military standards, and drawings. 1.6.7.1.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required fit and function analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. 1.6.7.1.3 Performing analysis to determine if a store can be loaded and maintained while on the aircraft, assess the store functionality, and perform digital and physical fit checks if needed. 1.6.7.1.4 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound recommendations for loading, installation and functionality of stores. Additionally, the Contractor shall provide assistance with creation of loading and installation manuals. Lastly, the Contractor shall provide inputs as required to aircraft and store original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) that document engineering findings related to engineering analyses findings and conclusions. 1.6.7.2 Structural Load Engineering. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support in the area of structural loads and vibrations, acoustics, and/or thermal (as required) for stores, suspension and release equipment, and aircraft required for the store certification process. The Contractor shall support the entire aircraft store Evaluate Compatibility and certification process. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation indicated in the duties below along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.7.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data to ensure compliance with MIL-STD-8591 for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, military standards, and drawings. 1.6.7.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of conducting required loads analysis, testing and reporting necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. Analysis requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: analytical aerodynamic evaluations (e.g. CFD), loads analysis, stress analysis, and vibration analysis. Testing requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: wind tunnel tests, static loads tests, ground vibration tests, non-instrumented flight tests, and instrumented flight tests. 1.6.7.3 Conducting analysis by manual and computer methods to evaluate inertial and aerodynamic loads and stress on aircraft, stores, and suspension and release equipment. This shall include using commercial and in-house developed software. 1.6.7.4 Developing and documenting required computer software and computer analysis methods using approved Government processes to create an in-house capability to analyze loads and stresses on the aircraft. This shall include using numerical methods to determine flexible aircraft loads from rigid airframe aerodynamic data, aerodynamic influence coefficients, structural influence coefficients, mass distribution data, 6-degree of freedom simulation data, and Finite Element Models (FEM). The Contractor shall develop and document any software necessary to perform this analysis. 1.6.7.5 Preparing and supporting off-site wind tunnel tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, wind tunnel chamber conditions (e.g. Mach number, total pressure, angle of attack), and data requirements; developing a wind tunnel test plan; attending pre-test coordination meetings; making technical decisions during the test; and reducing the data. 1.6.7.6 Preparing, executing, and documenting static loads and ground vibration tests to gather store and/or aircraft load data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, worst case loading cases, and data requirements; developing a static loads and ground vibration test plan; attending pre-test coordination meetings; setting up of the test stand; controlling the test apparatus; making technical decisions during the test; reducing the data; and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.7 Preparing and supporting non-instrumented structural loads flight tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight test conditions, and tolerances; and providing risk assessments, test maneuvers, and data requirements. This also includes developing mission summaries; attending pre-test coordination, safety, and technical review meetings; reviewing flight test cards; inspecting the store and aircraft prior to flight; attending the mission pre and post briefings; inspecting the store and aircraft after flight; and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.8 Preparing and supporting instrumented structural loads flight tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight conditions and tolerances, test maneuvers, and data requirements. This shall also include developing mission summaries, attending pre-test coordination meetings, safety/technical review meetings, reviewing flight test cards, inspecting the store and aircraft prior to flight, attending the mission pre and post briefings, verifying instrumentation calibration, assisting in setting up mission control room (e.g. Central Control Facility (CCF)), monitoring safety-of-flight parameters in a control room during the flight test mission, inspecting the store and aircraft after flight, reducing the data, and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.9 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound operating limit recommendations (e.g. Mach number, airspeed, acceleration limits). 1.6.8 Electromagnetic Compatibility/Electromagnetic Interface Engineering. The Contractor shall provide support in the area of aircraft-store Electromagnetic Compatibility/Electromagnetic Interface (EMC/EMI) capability. These duties shall include: 1.6.8.1 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required for conducting EMC/EMI analysis, testing and reporting necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification recommendation. 1.6.8.2 Reviewing sources of existing technical data to substantiate compatibility recommendations. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: MIL-STD-464 (A, B, C), MIL-STD-461 (A-F), DoW Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Ordnance (HERO) reports, technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, and drawings. 1.6.8.3 Conducting analysis of aircraft-store configurations using appropriate computational methods (linear, nonlinear, and computational electromagnetic) to evaluate the EMC/EMI characteristics. Additionally, the Contractor shall develop and sustain analysis software tools and models using approved Government processes for the purpose of evaluating EMC/EMI characteristics. 1.6.8.4 Preparing and supporting EMC/EMI testing including preparing methods of test, executing the test or assisting in testing, including the use of network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, precision instrumentation, antennas and low-loss hardware, collecting and analyzing test results, and preparing test reports. Testing can occur many bases and facilities. 1.6.8.5 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound compatibility recommendations. 1.6.9 Stability and Control Engineering. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support in the area of aircraft stability and control required for the store certification process. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation indicated in the duties below along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.9.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, military standards, and drawings. 1.6.9.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of conducting the required stability and control analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft store certification process. Analysis requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: analytical aerodynamic evaluations including CFD and 6-degree of freedom simulation. Testing requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: wind tunnel tests, non-instrumented flight tests, and instrumented flight-tests. 1.6.9.3 Conducting analysis by manual and computer methods. This shall include modeling the aircraft store combination for computer simulation, running computer simulations to evaluate the aircraft stability and control characteristics, and modifying and documenting changes to existing analysis software for evaluating an aircraft's stability and control characteristics. Additionally, the Contractor shall develop and document analysis software using approved Government processes for the purpose of evaluating an aircraft's stability and control characteristics. 1.6.9.4 Preparing and supporting off-site wind tunnel tests to gather aircraft stability and control data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, wind tunnel chamber conditions (e.g. Mach number, total pressure, angle of attack), and data requirements; authoring a wind tunnel test plan; attending pre-test coordination meetings; making technical decisions during the test; and reducing the data. 1.6.9.5 Preparing and supporting non-instrumented stability and control flight tests to gather data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight test conditions, and tolerances; providing risk assessments, test maneuvers including open loop and closed loop maneuvers, and data requirements; developing mission summaries; attending pre-test coordination, safety, and technical review meetings; reviewing flight test cards; attending mission pre and post briefings; and documenting the test results. 1.6.9.6 Preparing and supporting instrumented stability and control flight tests to gather data to support aircraft store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight conditions and tolerances, test maneuvers including open loop and closed loop maneuvers, and data requirements. This shall also include developing mission summaries, attending pre-test coordination meetings, safety/technical review meetings, reviewing flight test cards, attending mission pre and post briefs, assisting in setting up mission control room (e.g. CCF), monitoring safety-of-flight parameters in a control room during the flight test mission, reducing the data, and documenting the test results. 1.6.9.7 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing aircraft state (e.g. aircraft's configuration weight, fuel burn, drag indices) and sound operating limit recommendations (e.g. Mach number, airspeed and acceleration limits). 1.6.10 Flutter Engineering. The Contractor shall support the aircraft-store certification process by providing engineering and technical support in the area of aircraft flutter. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation indicated in the duties below along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.10.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, and military standards. 1.6.10.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required flutter and vibrations analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. Testing requirements shall include ground vibration tests and instrumented flutter flight tests. 1.6.10.3 Conducting analyses by manual and computer methods to evaluate flutter characteristics for given aircraft and store configurations. This shall include using commercial and in-house developed software. If necessary, the Contractor shall modify and create computer simulation programs and document changes to existing analysis software. 1.6.10.4 Preparing and supporting instrumented flutter flight tests to gather data to support store certification efforts. This shall include providing risk assessments and determining test configurations, flight conditions, tolerances, test maneuvers, and data requirements. This shall also include developing mission summaries, attending pre-test coordination meetings, attending safety/technical review meetings, reviewing flight test cards, attending the mission pre and post briefs, verifying instrumentation calibration, assisting in setting up mission control room (e.g. CCF), monitoring safety of flight parameters in a control room during the flight test mission, reducing the data, and documenting the test results. 1.6.10.5 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound operating limit recommendations (e.g. Mach number, airspeed, acceleration limits). 1.6.11 Store Separation Engineering. The Contractor shall support the store certification process by providing engineering and technical support in the area of store separations. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.11.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, military standards, and drawings. 1.6.11.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required store separation analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. Analysis requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: analytical aerodynamic evaluations including CFD and 6-degree of freedom trajectory simulation. Testing requirements shall include but are not limited to any of the following: wind tunnel tests (e.g. freestream, grid, trajectory, free-drop, and flowfield probe), static ejection tests, and instrumented flight tests. 1.6.11.3 Conducting analysis by manual and computer methods. This shall include modeling the aircraft-store combination for computer simulation, running computer simulations to analyze store separation characteristics, and modifying and documenting changes to existing analysis software for evaluating store separation characteristics. sig_18f7a0327103b15c1297.description: The Contracting Authority is considering entering into a retainer agreement. In this context, two ongoing retainer contracts, namely those of NA and DUO, will be merged into a single retainer for the entire OCW, with the exception of ODC-N. The manner or form in which this will take place is not yet exactly known. Based on the responses and answers to this Market Consultation, a decision will be made regarding, among other things, the best follow-up steps. Furthermore, the Contracting Authority aims to obtain a good picture of the level of interest and the possibilities and impossibilities in the market through this Market Consultation. The answers provided by you will serve as one of the sources of information for the documents that will form the basis for a potential tender. The Market Consultation provides benefits for all parties involved. The Contracting Authority identifies what is possible and what is current in the market. This allows for better orientation on how, for example, the requirements in the subsequent tender can be formulated and what characteristics the requested service should have. For the market parties involved, there is the advantage of having an early picture of the Contracting Authority as an organisation and the goals set for the project. The market can, for example, influence requirements that will be included in the tender documents. In this way, the participants contribute to increasing the success rate of the potential tender. sig_191cb2037bc1fadd51e2.description: Fleet Logistics Center Puget Sound will be soliciting for the installation, maintenance and removal of a Casualty Control (CASCON) evacuation and alarm reporting system onboard a forward deployed vessel in support of the U.S. Naval SRF-JRMC Yokosuka, Japan. The Government will provide the system itself and requires only installation, maintenance and removal of the system. This acquisition will be negotiated on a full and open competitive basis. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals prior to offer due date. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted to the NECO website on or about 24 March 2016 with proposals due by 04 April 2016. A Firm-Fixed Price, Service type contract will be awarded in accordance with FAR parts 12 and 13.5, Commercial and Simplified Acquisition Procedures. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by FLCPS. This solicitation and any subsequent amendments will be posted to the NECO website: https://www.neco.navy.mil. Prospective offerors are responsible for downloading their own copy of the solicitation from this website and for frequently monitoring that site for any amendments. The Government is not responsible for any inability of the offeror to access the posted documents. No telephone or fax requests will be accepted, and no hard-copy solicitation/amendment will be mailed or faxed. Electronic submission of proposals/quotes is not available at this time. Emailing completed solicitations to the Contracting Officer, Austin Carter at austin.carter@navy.mil is acceptable and preferred.

sig_1924161ce67f4633b840.description: An Post is seeking to establish a Qualification Panel of suppliers capable of delivering the services as follows. As of 2026, An Post has an established digital presence across a range of products and services, with AnPost.com acting as its primary customer-facing digital platform. As well as being a key acquisition channel, organic search plays a critical role in enabling customers to discover, access and engage with An Post services. Aligned with An Post’s wider Digital strategy and the rapidly fragmenting search landscape, An Post is seeking to establish a panel of suppliers capable of supporting both traditional Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) and emerging AI Search and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO), ensuring sustained visibility across current and future search environments. This panel will cover strategic advisory, optimisation execution, technical deployment, and performance measurement and reporting activities related to enhancing An Post’s visibility in traditional and emerging search engines. sig_1932f4544c6abd58d9b7.description: The Municipality of Messini is willing to adopt digital applications and intelligent actions, with the aim of transforming itself into a 'smart city', through the development and use of new technological means that will improve the management and functionality of the urban environment. As a 'smart city', the Municipality will be a place where traditional services will become more efficient, through the use of digital and telecommunications technologies, for the benefit of residents, visitors and businesses. These actions include smart and disability-friendly pedestrian crossings, the provision of telemedicine systems to vulnerable groups for remote diagnosis, integrated cyber-attack protection infrastructure (Network Firewall, End point security, WAF, etc.), a central unified platform for the management and collection of smart city data, smart energy management systems for municipal and school buildings, smart lighting systems within municipal buildings, a municipal cemetery management and file digitisation system, electronic invoicing, and an electronic system for the management and organisation of the Administration and the operational capacity of Local Government Organisations. The project will constitute an 'Integrated Electronic Public Procurement Management System' to cover the requirements introduced by Law 4412/2016 'Public Works, Supply and Service Contracts'. The system incorporates the legislative framework and is a tool for the proper management of an organisation's public contracts. It is a tool that covers all cases under the Law, whether it concerns general services and supplies or technical subject matter (works, studies, technical and other related scientific services). It is the most comprehensive system on the market, with an already large client base, covering all issues related to a public contract. Its basic functions are mentioned indicatively: • Standardisation - Assistance - Guidance. Guidance for the competent officers of the Contracting Authority in every tender procedure, through defined steps and checks based on Law 4412/16 for all types of contracts (supplies, services, works, studies, social services, other services). • Monitoring. Comprehensive monitoring of the life cycle of a public contract (proposals, programming, conduct, execution). Ability to monitor physical, financial, temporal subject matter and audit trail. • Digital File. Creation and ensuring the mandatory maintenance of the integrated Digital Public Contract File. • Connectivity. Interoperability with Diavgeia, KHMDIHS, ESHDIHS as well as with other external systems (e.g. Financial Management, SHDE) for the retrieval of documents and data. Posting of documents and data to KHMDIHS and DIAVGEIA. • Creation of Registers. (Studies, Guarantees, Appeals, Suppliers, Items, etc.). • Procedure Control. Checks regarding the procedure and legislation, e.g. check of divisions, deadlines, required publications, sufficiency of amount, CPV, etc. • Reports - Notifications. Printing of reports & statistics. Creation of notifications with contract milestones. Sending notifications to those involved (competent departments, committees, etc.). Easy data search with filters so that personalised reports can be created. User Action Calendar. (Indicative reports: remaining commitments, ongoing expenses, check of divisions, progress of procedures, procedures by KAE, CPV, service, type, etc.). • Web Application. It is a web application that works with all browsers, without the requirement of installing add-ons, in an easy-to-use and friendly environment. • Ability to send data to a Mobile Application. • Ability to register all types of contracts (works, studies, supplies, services) and associate them with the involved persons and bodies.; Integrated platform for the management and collection of data for all data of the modern city. The collection and analysis of data will be carried out with the aim of extracting knowledge for combined decision-making, based on governance indicators. The platform will collect data and manage functions from individual 'smart' applications and will provide services to citizens, businesses and municipal staff. In the central unified platform for the management and collection of smart city data, it must be possible to interconnect all the 'smart' applications of the Municipality, existing ones, within the framework of this specific project, as well as future ones, with the aim of monitoring and operating all 'smart' applications through a single and integrated environment. Access to the central unified management platform must be achieved securely via a simple browser without the need to install special software. In this way, access from everywhere, performance stability, continuous availability and full control of the system's smooth operation will be provided.

sig_1951d05192e6de448c03.description: CLARIFICATION: This is ONLY a market exploration procedure to determine whether and, if so, which companies can offer the service intended for procurement. This preliminary information does not serve the purposes of Section 38 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Munich Fire Department is planning, in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany, to tender and introduce an interface management system (≠ interface modelling system, see below) named "RESQON". RESQON is intended to make it possible to network all Integrated Control Centres (ILS) nationwide with one another and exchange data amongst each other. In addition, the system is to be used to connect external services with partly proprietary protocols to the various computer-aided dispatch systems of the respective control centre. RESQON consists of local instances at the control centres, which are to be combined into a network. This network is referred to as RESQON Mesh. Participating control centres can exchange incident data via RESQON Mesh. Within the RESQON Mesh there is a central instance, the so-called RESQON Core. RESQON Core provides external connections to standardised services such as, for example, AML and the nora emergency call app. Furthermore, connections to statutory health insurance control centres, to TPS service providers for eCall and police control centres are to be possible in the future. An elementary component of RESQON is an interface modelling system which allows various protocols and data to be transformed and, if necessary, process logic to be mapped using it. The interface modelling system is a component of every local RESQON instance. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PLEASE NOTE: The purpose of this market exploration is to evaluate the availability of such interface modelling systems. This is also in particular in preparation for a possible direct award - in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany - in accordance with Section 14 Paragraph 4 No. 2 letter b) of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), since the objective absence of competition for technical reasons must be demonstrated and, if necessary, proven by the contracting authority. This market exploration is therefore an essential part of the required comprehensive market analysis at European level. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- See additionally the document "2025-11-25_Markterkundung_Schnittstellenmodellierungssystem.pdf". This can be requested from the contact point via the e-tendering system. ======================================================== PROCEDURE FOR INTERESTED COMPANIES: Interested companies that consider themselves in a position to offer a corresponding product are requested to contact the contact point by email at: info@mayburg.de (providing contact details, at least email and telephone) by no later than Thu., 08.01.2025. The LH Munich - Fire Department - will then be informed accordingly and will seek further contact for the continuation of the market exploration or the market exploration procedure.

sig_19756d764e2cdf35ad54.description: Development of a simulation model for the Paks II nuclear power plant electrical power supply system. The purpose of the procurement is to develop a simulation model of the nuclear power plant electrical power system for the new Paks II nuclear power plant units 5 and 6 (with a capacity of 2*1200 MW), with which the electrical transient processes critical to the nuclear and production safety of the nuclear power plant can be examined, and by using the results of which, measures can be taken to reduce the number of unit shutdowns occurring in connection with both external and internal grid transients to a minimum level. The fundamental focus of the computer application to be developed for solving the task is the electrical and technological modelling of the nuclear power plant unit and common-facility electrical power supply systems (both producer, grid and consumer system elements), and the modelling of secondary technology for checking the system-level coordinated operation of relay protection automatics. A secondary objective is real-time simulation, during which critical electrical control technology devices are examined via co-simulation (C-HIL). The custom-developed simulation model must be suitable for the simulation of all known electrical technological phenomena (normal operational stationary and transient states interpreted in the electromechanical range and automatic operations, operational switching processes, emergency stationary and transient states interpreted in the electromechanical range and automatic operations) and event sequences, as well as for the simulation-based examination of the operation of electrical protection and control automatics – based on a logical model. Computational functionality expected regarding the simulation software: The simulation model ('Digital Twin') of the nuclear power plant electrical power supply systems shall be suitable for performing the following examinations: - Power flow and voltage drop calculation: AC & DC LoadFlow (with symmetrical and asymmetrical load). - Short-circuit and phase loss calculation: AC & DC Short Circuit (symmetrical: 3F, 3FN; Asymmetrical: 2FN, 2F, 1FN, 1F phase-break). - Dynamic power flow calculation: normal operational and emergency electrical events in the electromechanical transient range. - Equipment-level transmission reserve (utilisation) calculation: based on typical electrical consumer distribution and load profiles. - Simulation of fault phenomena and switching scenarios for coordinated and selective automatic protection and control operation checking. (Electrical protection and automation devices are to be modelled using a 'blackbox' (deterministic, logical operation-based) modelling method, down to the low-voltage main distribution equipment level in the network, as well as producer and consumer intelligent protection and automatic control devices). Further expectations and a detailed task description are in the Technical Description forming part of the procurement documents. sig_1990f1bfa7fb40150881.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system for Specialist Systems (02.19 Specialist Systems) The system contains one procurement category: Specialist Systems, delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS). Specialist Systems are supplied as "Software as a Service" (SaaS). Users subscribe to the software and gain access to it via the internet or via the supplier's application programming interfaces. Specialist Systems must support case processing/task handling of one or more of the customers' tasks/services, within one or more of the service areas mentioned below. The customer's needs determine which service area or areas are covered by the specific procurement. A specific procurement may well cover several of the service areas listed below. Specialist Systems as SaaS are characterised by being "on-demand services" which are owned, developed, maintained, managed and operated by the supplier or by the service owner's subcontractor. Services must be fully developed. Consequently, no services can be offered in the dynamic purchasing system that are developed or further developed specifically for the customer. The content of the service must be suitable for use in the Danish public sector. In addition, a procurement of services must comprise the implementation of the service (handover upon supplier change of a service and start-up upon the new establishment of a service) as well as the termination of the service (in connection with the expiry of the delivery contract). Implementation and termination form part of the overall service. Services are thus generic, fully developed solutions that meet uniform needs across customers, although such that these can be simply and quickly scaled and configured to the specific customer's IT environment, e.g. in relation to capacity, number of users or user rights etc. Consequently, services cannot be procured in the dynamic purchasing system that are intended to be developed for the individual customer on the basis of the customer's needs. The system covers all services and performance in the procurement of specialist systems within the service areas specified below. The service areas are based on FORM services. Reference is made to Annex C for a review of the covered service areas. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the dynamic purchasing system when they are to procure specialist systems "as a Service".

The aim of establishing the DPS is to create a platform for awarding contracts within the DPS in order to enable the contracting authority to award contracts flexibly in accordance with the Public Procurement Act according to its actual needs, i.e., at a time and in a scope known to it. The dynamic purchasing system will be divided into two categories: 1) Purchase of hardware and hardware product support 2) Purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. sig_19e75823402d3ba87c6d.description: About the Office for National Statistics (ONS) ONS is the UK's largest independent producer of official statistics and is the National Statistical Institute for the UK. Formally, it is the executive office of the UK Statistics Authority, a non-Ministerial Department established by the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. It is responsible for collecting and publishing statistics related to the economy, population, and society at national, regional and local levels. ONS plays a leading role in national and international good practice in the production of official statistics. Overview The Office for National Statistics (ONS) wishes to make estimations of household vehicle expenditure, the ONS wishes to appoint a sole supplier to provide fully representative prices (RRP) for the list of sold/registered cars in the UK each quarter, inclusive of VAT. The Department for Transport (DfT) will provide the ONS with a volume list of vehicles, which is detailed by vehicle make, model detail, engine size, body type, and manufacturer month. The data set contains an average of approximately 20,000 rows of data, this will then require the successful supplier to evaluate and price each model provided. Where no exact price can be found, the supplier will be expected to find the lowest level average price available. Furthermore, the number of exact matches must be identified in order to maintain the standards of the data that is being delivered. The lowest level averages are required to maintain the quality and accuracy of the estimates that are produced by the ONS, this also ensures continuity in the data. This data will be also used for the ONS Prices Division to construct a sample frame from which to select a sample (and weights). Suppliers must also be aware that the data that is provided will be utilised to create estimations of household expenditure which will be published by the ONS. Suppliers must agree that the data can be used for these purposes and also provide assurance that the data can be held for perpetuity. Please be aware, this is an irrevocable, royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual right for the AUTHORITY to keep the data or data downloaded beyond the expiry of the contract to comply with the AUTHORITY's obligations under the UK Code of Practice for Official Statistics as prescribed within the Statistics and Registrations Service Act 2007. Furthermore Data may be shared with other government agencies to evidence household spending figures when asked. Organisations that should consider contacting us: If you believe that your company has the capability of supplying the ONS with prices data from a wide range of online and physical motor trade authorities, including private and industry leading dealerships. Trade partners that collect data on motor vehicles and their use. Data on finance and leasing details would be sought after but not essential. Data on second hand cars would be advantageous but not essential. Types of support could include: Price and volume data covering the lower level breakdowns of vehicles, new, used, financed or leased. Data should include all sales direct to the final customer. Briefings for each quarterly data delivery; commentating on any unusual price or volume movements in the data. What can a contract with ONS offer? An opportunity to work with a world class statistics organisation, to create better and more timely statistics to be used by all for the benefit of the public good. There is a possibility for this work to be funded if all requirements are met by the provider. How to register When you have expressed an interest, please submit a return to Sophie.keal@ons.gov.uk with the following information to allow ONS to have an understanding of what your company can offer. Please include as a minimum: Organisation Name Contact details Brief description of primary activity of organisation Type of data you can provide and support available It is anticipated that any resulting tenders from this engagement exercise will be conducted through ONS's 'DPS Data SaSiE'. To sign up for this in readiness to receive any future tender packs, please search here Dynamic Purchasing System for Data Sources and Services including Expertise (DPS Data SaSiE) - Contracts Finder This will take you through to the associated documentation for your organisation to apply. Additional Information This Exercise is NOT a pre-qualification or selection exercise and is NOT part of any pre-qualification or selection process that may apply to any future potential procurement. It is intended to act as an awareness and information gathering exercise offering an opportunity for suppliers to advise the extent to which they potentially can provide some or all the services that ONS may require, in order to help ONS with its future intentions. Lot 1: .
sig_19e75823402d3ba87c6d.title: Provision of Car Price Data

sig_1a1c48108e015f0ba994.description: The Bergische Universität Wuppertal (BUW) is seeking a survey institute with relevant, demonstrated expertise in the service areas outlined below to carry out the survey for the fifth survey wave of the lidA study in the year 2027. The study "lidA - living in work" (www.lida-studie.de) is a cohort study in Germany that investigates the thematic field of "Work, Age, Health and Employment Participation". The study is led by the Chair of Occupational Science at the University of Wuppertal. At intervals of three to five years, older workers in lidA were surveyed for approx. 70 minutes using Computer Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI). In survey wave 1 (2011), this involved 6.585 people nationwide from birth cohorts 1959 and 1965; the second wave took place in 2014 (N=4.244) and the third in 2018 (N=3.586). In survey wave 3 (2022/23), birth cohorts 1959 and 1965 were added to bring the total to over 3000 respondents, and nearly 3.000 people from birth cohort 1971 were surveyed for the first time. A total of 8.884 people were surveyed in this wave. Lot LOT-0001: LidA - Living in Work: Survey Wave 5. In the upcoming fifth survey wave in the year 2027, as many people as possible from the group of currently approximately 9.000 panel-ready previous lidA participants are to be surveyed in the main survey. Based on previous experience, it can be estimated that this will involve approximately 6.500 respondents. Subsequently, from October 2027 to October 2030, thirteen quarterly online follow-up surveys (with closed and open-ended questions) are to be conducted with those willing to participate. Participation of initially approx. 4.000 people and at the end approx. 2.900 people is expected here.
sig_1a1c48108e015f0ba994.title: LidA - Life at Work: Survey wave 5
