sig_1a28003f2338fffd5e56.description: The Army that fought and won World War II relied on commercial industry and civilian ingenuity for the machines and technology that enabled Allied victory. Army investments and civilian know-how set the stage for the high-tech revolution that continues to fuel global markets over seventy years later. Today, as the accelerated rate of technological change in areas like artificial intelligence, robotics and autonomy, and power and energy presages unprecedented opportunities and threats, the Army seeks to renew its commitment to the revolutionary ideas and civilian research and development partnerships that will ensure the safety and prosperity of the nation in the years to come. United States Army Futures Command (AFC) is focused on modernizing the Army and focuses on seven priorities: Long-Range Precision Fires Next Generation of Combat Vehicles Future Vertical Lift Platforms Army Network Network Command, Control, Communications, and Intelligence Assured Position Navigation and Timing Air and Missile Defense Capabilities Soldier Lethality Soldier Lethality Synthetic Training Environment Contested Logistics AFC's cross-functional teams (CFTs) are the Army’s vehicle for force modernization, ensuring capability overmatch for Army forces on future battlefields. While the Army plays a unique role in our society to deploy, fight, and win decisively against any adversary, anytime, and anywhere, many of the technologies that the Army relies on to accomplish this mission are being propelled by the civilian world. Army modernization priorities related to manned and unmanned vehicles, space systems, sensing, networks and connectivity, data visualization and gaming, space, and human performance monitoring (to name a few) all have substantial overlap with civilian sources, uses, and markets. To capitalize on opportunities for breakthrough research and development in key civil-military technology areas relevant to the Army’s modernization priorities, AFC has established the Army Applications Lab (AAL) to capitalize on the extended marketplace of ideas in government, academia, industry, and civilian innovation ecosystems and lead the research and development of disruptive innovations – i.e., technology demonstrators and early-stage products that revolutionize Army capabilities and corresponding civilian industries and create a first-mover advantage for the Army across a full spectrum of missions. The three main lines of effort associated with this BAA are discovery, acceleration, and translation of disruptive technology applications: Discovery of novel capability concepts that capitalize on emerging technologies and application insights from the widest possible range of sources. Acceleration of disruptive applications of technology that delivers a 2-4 times improvement over current or planned Army capabilities through the research, development, and validation of technology demonstrators. Translation of breakthrough innovations that create a scalable, first-mover advantage for the Army in strategic technology areas by synchronizing knowledge generated in the discovery and acceleration phases with key decision points across the Army Future Force Modernization Enterprise (FFME). Solutions consistent with these three functions and reflective of priorities, technical challenges, and problems associated with the FFME will be solicited through this BAA. AAL is seeking technologies that address a wide range of Army needs consistent with CFT capability focus areas and associated programs and lines of effort as well as potentially disruptive new capabilities that augment or enhance Army capability overmatch. A key focus for AAL is to identify and transition new technologies, methodologies, and concepts related to: Translational Research - Approaches and methodologies that accelerate the Army’s innovation cycle through the translation of emerging technologies to Army capability objectives, including the Army’s six modernization priorities and associated programs and lines of effort. Fourth Industrial Revolution Technologies - Approaches and methodologies that are characterized by a fusion of technologies in the physical, digital, and biological spheres. Specific technologies of interest include robotics; artificial intelligence; autonomy; augmented and virtual reality; nanotechnology; quantum information systems; synthetic biology and biotechnology; Internet of Things (IoT); space systems; advanced networking, communications, and command and control technology; additive manufacturing; and power and energy systems. Commercialization - Approaches and methodologies that support the research and development of dual-use solutions - i.e., solutions that support both emerging Army needs and scalable commercial markets.
sig_1a28003f2338fffd5e56.title: ARMY APPLICATIONS LABORATORY BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT FOR DISRUPTIVE TECHNOLOGIES

sig_1a2a580082fc8844ca89.description: Social Care Wales is looking for two experienced, independent suppliers to help shape and test a new programme designed to build positive, relationship centred cultures in adult social care across Wales. The programme aims to “help care providers nurture, measure and sustain positive, relationship centred cultures.” This work is funded through the Rayne Foundation’s Better Carers Better Careers initiative and will run across multiple years. The programme is split into two lots, each with a distinct focus but designed to work closely together. The contract will be divided into the following Lots, and Social Care Wales intends to appoint one provider per Lot. Suppliers may bid for one or both Lots; however, a Supplier awarded one Lot will not be eligible to be awarded the other. Lot 1 – Codesigning and Testing New Leadership Support and a Self-Assessment Tool This supplier will: - Recruit six adult social care providers to act as pilot sites. - Run co design workshops with leaders, managers, frontline workers and stakeholders. - Develop a Theory of Change and work with the supplier leading the evaluation to shape the evaluation approach. - Collect and support high-quality data throughout the programme. - Carry out baseline, midpoint and final culture assessments at each site. - Provide tailored support such as coaching or team learning. - Produce: ~ A Service Design Report explaining what was created, how it was tested and what was learned. ~ A Tool Design and Testing Report for a new bilingual digital/printable self assessment tool. Lot 2 – Evaluation and Impact Assessment This supplier will: - Design and deliver a mixed methods evaluation to understand how the programme works and what difference it makes. - Assess whether the user research, leadership support and self-assessment tool were delivered as intended. - Explore outcomes for staff, leaders, providers, people using services and the wider system. - Capture lived experience across the six pilot sites using ethical, inclusive methods. - Produce: ~ A full evaluation framework and data collection plan. ~ Regular progress and insight reports. ~ A final bilingual evaluation report with findings, case studies and recommendations. ~ A bilingual stakeholder presentation. Cross cutting Requirements Both suppliers must: - Work collaboratively with each other, Social Care Wales, Care Inspectorate Wales and the Rayne Foundation’s evaluators. - Deliver inclusive, accessible activities that reflect the diversity of the Welsh social care workforce. - Use secure digital tools for engagement and data collection. - Carry out at least 20 engagement activities (e.g., workshops, interviews, focus groups). - Meet all requirements for data protection, ethics, bilingual delivery and Social Care Wales branding. The goal is the step-by-step establishment of a modern, scalable and integrated data and reporting landscape that supports data-driven decisions, reduces manual processes and creates a uniform data basis for specialist departments and management. The contractor is to support the HMC both strategically and operationally in the further development of the data and analytics landscape, providing consulting, development, support and knowledge transfer from a single source. Lot LOT-0001: Development and further development of business intelligence and analytics services. Essential service contents: The contractor supports the HMC in the conception, development, migration and optimisation of data and analytics solutions. This includes in particular: - Integration, transformation and preparation of data from various specialist systems - Development and further development of data pipelines, data models as well as data warehouse, lakehouse and cloud storage structures - Development and optimisation of dashboards, reports and real-time reporting solutions based on Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric - User-centred data visualisation according to the principles of the International Business Communication Standards (IBCS) - Consulting on data architecture, governance, reporting standards and analytics strategy - Ensuring data quality, data security and compliance requirements - Execution of test, quality and change management measures - Error analysis, incident management as well as support in ongoing operations - Training and empowerment of the specialist departments as well as execution of a structured knowledge transfer.

sig_1a5e4858e85acc727854.description: 1.2 Purpose and scope of the procurement The purpose of the procurement is to better understand the nature-related risks and opportunities faced by enterprises in which the state has an ownership share, the steps these companies are taking to manage nature-related risks and opportunities, and what are currently considered best practices in this area. The following scope of the procurement has been identified, as further described in appendix 1: i) Screen the nature-related dependencies and impacts, risks and opportunities of 16 Norwegian state-owned enterprises (SOEs). ii) Identify best practice related to identifying, managing and reporting on nature-related dependencies and impacts, risks and opportunities, and iii) Carry out a detailed assessment of the nature-related dependencies and impacts, risks and opportunities of 4 - 8 SOEs and actions taken by these companies to identify, manage and report on these, as well as recommend next steps. The procurement consists of part i) and ii) of the scope above, while part (iii) of the scope above is an option. As explained in section 5 and appendix 5, the price offer for the Assignment should be a fixed price for encompassing both parties i) and ii), while the price offer for part iii) (the Option) should be a fixed price per enterprise assessment. The value of the total procurement (including the Option) is estimated to a range between NOK 2 million excl. VAT and NOK 4 million excl. VAT. For further information on the purpose, scope and content of the procurement, we refer to appendix 1.
sig_1a5e4858e85acc727854.title: Assessing the Nature-Related Dependencies and Impacts, Risks and Opportunities of Norwegian State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs)

sig_1a5f2afffbc00c7c70e5.description: The purpose of amendment no. 3 is to respond to the following questions. Question-9. Is MARAD primarily looking for design-stage studies in which fuel efficiency and URN are predicted through fluid dynamic modeling? Response-9. Yes. The goal is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. There is no limitation on the type of modeling - approaches should be used as needed. Question-10. Is there any room for measurements within the Challenge? Response-10. This is a design stage challenge and does not include an expectation of direct measurement. ================================================== The purpose of amendment no. 2 is to respond to the following questions. Question-4. Is MARAD open to all forms of propulsion to gain fuel efficiencies - for example, hybrid diesel-electric equipment with electric motors and batteries? Response-4. There are no limits or specific requirements for the type of propulsion or fuel. Technologies, including fuels and propulsion, should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Question-5. Under the Eligibility Information section of the subject notice, it states that the opportunity is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." In reviewing the statutory definition of a “domestic source” under 50 U.S.C. § 4555(7), “the term “domestic source” means a business concern— (A) that performs in the United States or Canada substantially all of the research and development, engineering, manufacturing, and production activities required of such business concern under a contract with the United States relating to a critical component or a critical technology item.” Based on this definition, which appears to include qualifying Canadian businesses as domestic sources for certain USG Response-5. For the purposes of this RFP a domestic applicant is considered to be a contractor organized or existing under the laws of the United States. Keep in mind that the RFP states preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag; the RFP does not exclude those with team leads or team members outside the U.S. " Question-6. Confidentiality of design information: Our understanding is that the final report and presentation will be publicly shared, while sensitive supporting information, such as calculations, design plans and drawings, modeling results, technology details, and cost information, can be provided to MARAD without being made public. The terms and conditions, however, grant MARAD broad rights to reproduce, distribute, and display project materials. Could you clarify whether sensitive design information submitted during the project can be designated and maintained as confidential, and whether MARAD’s rights to distribute it would be limited? Response-6. Confidential business information or sensitive design information will not be shared publicly without permission. Prior to publication, MARAD and the project team will discuss the extent and limits of the information that will be shared. Question-7. Subcontracting limits: Are there any restrictions on the value or proportion of work that may be subcontracted to organizations outside the named project team, such as model testing facilities or noise specialists? Response-7. The proposed project team should include all intended team members including those that would be subcontracted such as testing facilities or noise specialists. The specifics of subcontract awards are not determined by the MARAD project manager. Question-8. Work outside the United States: May project funds be used to subcontract specialized work outside the United States? If so, are there limits on the type or value of that work? Response-8. The proposed project team should include all proposed team members. Preference will be given to those team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag. There is no specific requirement for subcontractors. ========================================================= The purpose for this amendment is to respond to the following questions: Question-1. Domestic Applicant Definition: Section D.1 of the RFP states the Challenge is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." Our company is a U.S.-registered entity, though its ultimate parents are in Canada and Europe. Could you confirm whether an entity with this ownership structure qualifies as a "domestic applicant" for purposes of serving as the lead applicant/Recipient of a cooperative agreement under this RFP? Response-1. For the purposes of this project, a U.S. registered entity will be evaluated as a domestic applicant. Question-2. Citizenship-Based Funding Restriction: We understand that MARAD/META cooperative agreements may include a restriction on using award funds for "work to be done or done in a facility owned by someone other than a Citizen of the United States (as defined in 46 C.F.R. § 315.3(b))." Could you confirm whether this restriction, or an equivalent, will apply to cooperative agreements resulting from this RFP, and if so, how it would apply to a design team whose naval architecture/engineering firm is U.S.-registered and performs all work domestically, but has foreign parent ownership? Response-2. For the purposes of this project, a design team located in the U.S. working at a U.S.-registered firm and performing all work domestically would not fall under the restriction. Question-3. Team Lead Eligibility vs. Preference: Section B notes a preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag." Could you confirm whether this operates solely as an evaluative preference, or whether it functions as a disqualifying eligibility criterion for a team lead whose ultimate parent is a foreign entity? Response-3. The preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag" is an evaluative preference. A U.S. registered entity with U.S. offices and staff performing work domestically, would fall under consideration as a domestic applicant for this project. ======================================================================= U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION: MARAD will provide funding through a cooperative agreement for the execution of this Design Challenge. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit MARAD to make any award. To be considered for selection, the contractor participating in the Challenge must be able to complete it within 18 months from time of award. The final report and other summary materials will be publicly available and posted to the META webpage. Proposals in response to this RFP are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals will be screened for use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. Any use of AI tools in generating content for the proposal must be clearly identified and justified. MARAD reserves the right to fund one or none of the proposals received under this RFP. MARAD is not responsible for reimbursing the costs that applicants incur to prepare and submit their proposals in response to this RFP. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this RFP will not be returned. It is MARAD’s policy to treat all proposals submitted under this RFP as sensitive competitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. All applicants must be registered and current with SAM.gov at the time of award. ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION. 1. Eligible Applicants: Open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals. 2. MARAD is seeking to provide full funding through cooperative agreement for the proposals that provides sufficient, verifiable, and detailed data on how to reach the objective of this Design Challenge. MARAD will fund 100% of the total cost of the project. Proposals must include a detailed cost breakdown that shows how Federal funds will be used for the project. Please see Section E.2 for information on proposal format requirements. 3. Systems for Award Management (SAM) Requirements. No specific application form or other materials need to be obtained from MARAD. Content and Form of Application. Proposals are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals must provide sufficient, verifiable, and detailed information covering all elements of the “Proposal Content” described in section B.1 above. Unique Entity Identifier and System for Award Management (SAM). Each applicant is required to: (a) be registered and current in SAM before submitting its application; (b) provide a valid unique entity identifier in its applicant; and (c) continue to maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times during which it has an active Federal award or an application or plan under consideration by a Federal awarding agency. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Submission Dates and Times. The deadline for proposal submission is 12:00 PM EST on the closing date listed for this RFP on SAMS.gov Please submit proposals in PDF format attached to an email. Send proposals to Christian Onwudiegwu/Contract Specialist at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov, Office of Acquisitions. Do not send paper copies, or other media of the proposal via post office or delivery service. Proposals received by MARAD after the deadline will not be considered for award. An email will be deemed “received” by MARAD on the date and time the email was “sent” to the email address in Section E.7, below, as determined by MARAD’s servers. Intergovernmental Review. This funding opportunity is not subject to Executive Order 12372, “Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs.” l Funding Restrictions. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201 for cost principles used to determine allowable costs of work performed under Federal awards. Other Submission Requirements. Proposals must be submitted by the deadline set forth in Section E.4 above by electronic mail to Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. Please include the Funding Opportunity Number and Title in the Subject Line. APPLICATION REVIEW INFORMATION Review and Selection Process. MARAD will set up an internal review team to evaluate all proposals that are submitted under this announcement. All eligible proposals will be evaluated within four weeks after the closing date. If the review team has any questions on an individual proposal, it will notify the applicant for clarification. The proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: Well-documented and context-appropriate plan to undertake and successfully demonstrate the design integration of technology to achieve the fuel efficiency goal, URN limit, and economic analysis required by the Challenge. Clear application of methods supporting vessel design, technology integration, data collection, assessment, and analysis to include specifications for fuel efficiency and URN modeling consistent with international and class standards and reference to existing guidelines, standards, and notations. Methodologies must include descriptions of major analytical approaches being proposed for the Challenge components to meet the Design Challenge Parameters. Methodology also includes any specific models and data sources intended to be used for each component of the Challenge. The Team’s capabilities, related experience, technical knowledge, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve Challenge goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Detailed project timeline with descriptions of key decision points and areas of uncertainty. Budget and justification demonstrating appropriate and defensible cost per component, personnel, timeline, and final deliverables; including consideration of the experience and capability of key personnel involved, the number of hours budgeted for key people, and the role, value, and level of participation of any noted partners. FEDERAL AWARD ADMINISTRATION INFORMATION Federal Award Notices. The successful applicant(s) will be notified by MARAD’s Office of Acquisition via telephone; however, the telephone call is not the actual award or the authorization to begin performance. All awards will be made by a cooperative agreement signed by MARAD’s Agreement/Grants Officer. After an award has been made, a representative from the MARAD’s Office of Innovation will schedule a kick-off meeting for the project. Unsuccessful applicants will be notified via email. sig_1a6c5a92f490ff7b3e2a.description: Operation of the Bicycle Parking Information Centre. The subject of the procurement is the continuation and operation of the Bicycle Parking Information Centre. BALM has been assigned project management for the special programme "City and Country" (SP "S&L"). This also includes the operation of the information centre established in 2021, which supports municipalities and other relevant stakeholders through expert advice, knowledge transfer, information services and practice-oriented working aids in the planning and implementation of bicycle parking facilities and multi-storey bicycle parking. The current contract ends on 31.12.2027; the information centre is to be continued from 01.01.2028 and further developed in terms of expertise and content in line with demand. The further development of the field of action and the administrative agreement of the SP "S&L" existing until the year 2030 establish a considerable need for information and support extending beyond the year 2027. More recent estimates from the current contract period assume around 1,84 million additional bicycle parking spaces by the year 2040 due to the forecasted increase in passenger volumes. At the same time, planning, technical, organisational and operational requirements are increasing, particularly in the case of multi-storey bicycle parking and complex facilities at railway stations and other public transport interfaces. In addition, topics such as digitalisation and access systems, data standards and interfaces, GIS-supported planning procedures, and digital and, prospectively, AI-supported knowledge services are gaining in importance. In order to support local implementation through information and advice, and in particular to enable municipalities to independently plan and implement bicycle parking facilities at public transport stations, the existing "Bicycle Parking" information centre is to be continued from 01.01.2028 onwards and further developed in line with demand. For this purpose, previous findings and relevant knowledge bases, in particular existing studies and publications of the information centre, are to be systematically secured, updated and supplemented by newly prepared information, and actively and service-orientatedly passed on, in particular to interested municipalities and other relevant stakeholders. The information centre is also intended to take up new technical and professional developments and make them usable for municipal practice. The aforementioned services cannot be provided by the contracting authority itself, meaning there is a need to award the services to a contractor with corresponding technical expertise.
sig_1a6c5a92f490ff7b3e2a.title: Operation of the "Bicycle Parking" Information Centre

sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.description: This is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, but a request for information through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying system suppliers to register for a potential tendering procedure. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social welfare, healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 6 000 professionals from various fields. Our vision is to be a pioneering community where services are accessible, the wellbeing of our population is among the best in Finland, and the occupational wellbeing of our employees is high. Our mission is to increase the health, functional capacity and security of our residents throughout their lives. Our values are “Mie turvaan”, “Mie uskallan”, “Mie vastaan” and “Mie välitän”. Strategic priorities include investing in personnel, smooth processes and the gradation of services. The realisation of these requires efficient, safe and user-friendly digital solutions. The roster planning system plays a central role in supporting the smooth flow of everyday operations, the occupational wellbeing of the staff and cost-efficiency. The purpose of the market dialogue is to obtain a comprehensive overview of the roster planning systems and related services available on the market. The information obtained can be used to assess what kinds of solutions exist on the market, what benefits they generate and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on the market offering and various suppliers' solutions 2. Understand the functionalities and key use cases of the systems 3. Explore integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 4. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 5. Gain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 6. Survey delivery and service models 7. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer systems or services falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the concept stage is not desired on this occasion. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: • what ready-made solutions and services they offer • in what kinds of environments the solutions have been deployed (example descriptions, no mandatory references) • the key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue All participants are offered equal opportunities to obtain information regarding the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, nor are procurement decisions made on the basis of it. If there is a large number of registered suppliers, the wellbeing services county may hold both a joint information session and a limited number of individual meetings. The market dialogue focuses in particular on how solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but thematic areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: • User management and information security • Working hours and shift management • Consideration of collective agreements and local agreements • Competence, qualifications and occupational health management • Usability and multi-user support • Reporting and information-driven management • Integrations with other systems • Mobile usage and employee services • Main administration, maintenance and support services • Intelligence and automation Pricing models and lifecycle services Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions also through a demo or practical example scenarios. The wellbeing services county will provide a set of questions in advance to guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared on an equal basis. The market dialogue will be conducted as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 60 to 90 minutes. The supplier will have the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also ask pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 21.10., 22.10., 27.10., 28.10. and 29.10.2025. The exact time will be agreed with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and schedule coordination. The language of potential presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations are requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12:00. This request for information / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted nor are tenders given in response to this request for information; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participating or refraining from participating in the market survey / request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in any potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a precondition for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey have no right to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be handled as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.
sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.title: Request for Information/Market Survey: Work shift planning system and related services

sig_1a987e065f85d4806e63.description: The subject of the call for competition is the provision, implementation, migration and introduction of an integrated HR application portfolio to replace the existing personnel IT landscape, as well as consultancy on process optimisation within the framework of implementation and subsequent operational support. The contract comprises in particular the work packages described in the following sections, which will be specified in further detail by the specifications in the course of the call for competition. The Mobil Krankenkasse is aware that such a project involves cooperation obligations that must be coordinated with the contractor. Corresponding resources will be made available for the agreed project period. Depending on the solution offered, responsibilities will have to be coordinated during the project and for subsequent operation / support between the Mobil Krankenkasse, the current infrastructure service provider of the Mobil Krankenkasse (Mobil ISC GmbH) and the subsequent contractor. Currently, the company operates the SAP HCM system within the industry-specific solution oscare(R) and supplements it with several standalone solutions. An end of maintenance has been announced for 31.12.2027 for essential components of this system landscape, such as HCM ERP, employee portal (ESS/MSS) and Learning Solution (LSO). This creates a clear need for action to further develop or restructure personnel IT in good time. Against this background, the preliminary project "Personnel IT Analysis" was carried out for 2025. The aim was a holistic stocktaking and well-founded analysis of existing processes and applications in the areas of personnel and personnel IT. It was confirmed that the software landscape of the personnel department of the Mobil Krankenkasse is based on a historically grown and heterogeneous architecture. At the centre is SAP HCM On-Premise within the industry-specific solution oscare(R) (AOK Systems), via which the classic core HR functions such as master data management (PA), organisational management (OM), time management (PT) and payroll accounting (PY) are mapped. In addition, selected modules of SAP SuccessFactors are used as cloud solutions. Today's architecture presents itself as a patchwork of SAP standard components, AOK-specific solutions, other third-party tools and in-house developments. The integration landscape has also grown organically over many years and is characterised by a multitude of individual interfaces, technical dependencies as well as media breaks and many manual processes.
sig_1a987e065f85d4806e63.title: Transformation of the HR system and process landscape: Introduction of a future-proof HR system landscape

sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.description: Hereon requires external support for the migration of its SAP ERP system to S/4. The brownfield approach is to be used. This is a technical migration; potential improvements or optimisations will be carried out subsequently, decoupled from the migration. The subject matter of Lot 1 is the provision of comprehensive consultancy services for the planning, execution and documentation of the migration of the existing SAP ERP system to SAP S/4HANA. The services shall be performed in close coordination with the client's specialist departments. The contractor shall assume the following tasks: 3.1. Project planning and design - Preparation of a project schedule and content plan in close coordination with Hereon - Development of a migration concept including test design, definition of responsibilities and accompanying documentation 3.2. System analysis and process evaluation - Review of the existing SAP ERP systems with regard to the S/4HANA migration - Identification and evaluation of correction requirements in the implemented business processes - Communication of correction requirements to the specialist departments and verification of implementation 3.3. Archiving and system preparation - Archiving of FI and MM documents from completed financial years 2014-2019 - Setup of a sandbox system - Execution of necessary system copies from production to test systems 3.4. Migration and customising - Execution of the necessary customising - Execution and testing of the S/4HANA migration on sandbox, test and production systems - Review and adjustment of structural authorisations in connection with the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) - Analysis of existing roles and authorisations in the SAP ERP system as well as evaluation and application of new authorisation objects in the context of S/4HANA - Execution of the H4S4 conversion - Review and migration of the personnel cost commitment processor, ensuring functionality and data integrity in personnel cost planning - Connection of the SAP Enterprise Portal and support for the connection of the above-mentioned non-SAP products 3.5. Documentation and quality assurance - Preparation of audit-compliant final documentation of the migration - Support in the review of non-SAP software - Support during an internal security check (SAP Basis) 3.6. Training and hypercare - Preparation of (delta) training materials - Conducting training sessions for participating employees and key users - Provision of live support (hypercare) after the migration 3.7. Cooperation with the client - All services shall be provided in close coordination with the responsible specialist departments - Tasks that can sensibly be carried out by Hereon itself (e.g. non-SAP software, authorisation roles) shall be processed internally accordingly 3.8. Period and scope - The consultancy service is to be provided over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027.; As part of an ongoing SAP migration project, an external service provider is commissioned with Lot 2 to technically accompany and evaluate the project phases of concept review, test preparation and test execution as well as the final documentation. The objective is quality assurance and risk minimisation in the migration process, as well as ensuring audit-compliant documentation. The contract specifically comprises the following services: 4.1. Review of the migration concept - Analysis of the migration concept for completeness, consistency and feasibility - with a particular focus on ensuring that the planned documentation meets the requirements of an audit - Identification of potential risks and vulnerabilities, particularly with regard to the traceability and audibility of the migration steps - Preparation of an evaluation with recommended actions to ensure audit-compliant documentation 4.2. Support for test preparation and test execution - Advice on the planning and organisation of test activities (e.g. system, integration and acceptance tests) - Support in the definition of test cases and test data so that traceability and audibility for an audit are guaranteed at all times - Quality assurance during test execution with a particular focus on complete and audit-compliant logging - Evaluation of test results and derivation of measures 4.3. Review of the final documentation - Evaluation of project documentation regarding traceability, completeness and conformity with project objectives - Support in the preparation of handover documents so that all necessary evidence for a subsequent audit is available 4.4. Conditions of participation - Demonstrable experience in supporting SAP migration projects - Specialist knowledge of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA - Experience in test management and quality assurance - Knowledge of standard project management and IT service management standards (e.g. PRINCE2, ITIL) 4.5. Period and scope The consultancy service is to be provided alongside the project over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027. The exact scope will be agreed upon when the contract is awarded.

sig_1ac12aa178d8f3df5a0a.description: The purpose of the procurement consists of contracting technical assistance services for the management and supervision of the execution of works relating to: - contract no. 1182/25.10.2018, Design, Technical Assistance and Execution of Works for the investment objective "Rehabilitation of the district heating system of the Municipality of Bucharest (7 objectives totalling a route length of 31,621 km)", concluded by the Municipality of Bucharest with Compania Municipală Energetica Servicii București SA, and - the online open tender procedure "Rehabilitation of the district heating system of the Municipality of Bucharest (four objectives totalling a route length of 19,861 km)" - 3 Lots" currently being run by the contracting authority, the Municipality of Bucharest. The purpose of the technical assistance services for management and supervision/site management that the service provider must ensure for the investment objective is to provide the Contracting Authority with the guarantee that the contractors awarded the contracts for the execution of district heating network rehabilitation works will fulfil all responsibilities assumed through the contract, and will comply with legal provisions, technical regulations and the Specifications. The contracting authority aims to ensure supervision to the highest standards with specialist technical personnel qualified for the 3 lots of works, in accordance with the specifications. The duration of the provision of services shall run from the Purchaser's start order for the entire duration of the execution of the works relating to the objective, in accordance with the works contracts concluded by the Municipality of Bucharest, specifically for - Lot I: objective 1 - Main I South – CM 11’ – CP3 – CV5/4 (sector 2), Lot II: objective 3 - Main II South CM 43 – CO2 (sector 2) and objective 4 - Main II – III Grozăvești – C15/20 – CS 12 (sector 1), and Lot III: objective 5 - Main Progresu – Berceni – CB4 – CO5 (sector 4). -5.1. The duration of the provision of services is 12 months (until the issue of the certificate of works completion) from the date of transmission of the works start order for each Objective, plus the warranty period offered by the contractor of 60 months. The start orders for the technical assistance services for management and supervision of the execution of works shall be issued for each of the 7 objectives, depending on the issuance of the works start orders, in accordance with the works contracts concluded by the Municipality of Bucharest. The duration of the provision of services of 12 months does not include the period when the works are suspended. The number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for submission of tenders is 23 days. The CA shall respond to requests for clarifications 11 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The investment objective "Rehabilitation of the district heating system of the Municipality of Bucharest (7 objectives totalling a route length of 31,621 km)", approved by HCGMB no. 216/19.04.2018, has as its object the rehabilitation of 7 lots of primary thermal networks within the district heating mains belonging to the centralized heat supply system, as a result of the age of the existing pipes and the high number of failures that have occurred in these networks. The purpose of the technical assistance services for management and supervision/site management that the service provider must ensure for the above-mentioned investment objective is to provide the Contracting Authority with the guarantee that the contractors awarded the contracts for the execution of district heating network rehabilitation works will fulfil all responsibilities assumed through the contract, and will comply with legal provisions, technical regulations and the Specifications. The general objective of the Supervision Services consists in ensuring the successful implementation of the investment, by providing appropriate management and supervision services, while ensuring compliance with national and European legislative standards regarding the execution of works and environmental protection. The specific objectives of the management and supervision services are: a) Fulfilling the management and supervision role, namely the administration and management of the works execution contracts relating to the investment that form the subject of the services requested within the limits of the capacities/responsibilities delegated to the service provider by the Municipality of Bucharest, in order to ensure that the contractor complies with the associated contractual terms and conditions, the legislative framework and national legislation, as well as good practice. b) Supervising the execution works and all other related activities for the approval of materials, equipment and execution, so as to ensure that a high quality of construction is achieved within the established timeframe and budget and that all works are carried out in accordance with the designs and technical specifications, performance specifications, quality and environmental management plan, and the approved execution schedule. c) Ensuring supervision to the highest standards with qualified personnel for the works execution contracts;

sig_1b14d8b0802608b4973d.description: Helse Nord IKT HF (Northern Norway Health ICT Trust) wants to investigate whether there are solutions in the market that can support management of vulnerabilities. Rapid changes in the digital landscape, combined with a continuous more complex threat landscape, require public sector organisations to maintain clear visibility into vulnerabilities across their systems, networks, and applications. Public digital infrastructure is built on intricate systems and interconnected environments that are constantly exposed to cyber risks. A vulnerability management service enables organisations to identify and assess these environments, detect security weaknesses, optimise remediation efforts, and optimise vulnerability management workflows. sig_1b225cff828fc842c320.description: The Department of the Army is pleased to announce the availability of a cutting-edge software framework designed to enhance the capabilities of Software Defined Radio (SDR) systems. This framework enables the SDR signal chain to dynamically adjust its capabilities based on the sensed RF environment and to respond at the protocol level in real-time. The Department of the Army is releasing this software framework to foster collaboration with industry partners and encourage the integration of this technology into their SDR products. The intent is to enable greater flexibility in conducting radio frequency operations, allowing industry partners to leverage this framework to enhance their SDR systems' adaptability and operational effectiveness. By providing this framework, we aim to advance the state of SDR technology and promote innovation in the field of radio frequency operations. Key Features of the Framework: Rapid Reconfiguration: The framework allows for swift reconfiguration of the RF signal processing chain modules within the SDR’s field programmable gate array (FPGA), ensuring adaptability to varying operational requirements. FPGA-Based Physical Layer (PHY) and Media Access Control (MAC): The framework enables the rapid development and implementation of a fully-customized PHY and MAC layer that supports various signals and waveforms, providing a comprehensive solution for SDR applications. Elements Available for Industry: FPGA Top-Level Framework: This top-level hardware description language (HDL) framework resides within the SDR FPGA, facilitating seamless communication between the General-Purpose Processor (GPP) and the signal modules. Application Programming Interface (API): A user-friendly, common C-based API is provided, allowing developers to create SDR-agnostic applications that can manipulate the programmed signal FPGA modules effectively. Transport Interface (TI): The TI consists of dynamic or static C libraries utilized during application builds, enabling efficient message transport to and from user-based applications and FPGA signal modules. Exemplar Data Generation/Consumption Module: This module serves as a testing tool for hardware-specific implementations of the framework, ensuring compatibility and performance validation. Documentation: Comprehensive documentation will be made available, including development environment guides and a developer's guide, to assist industry partners in effectively utilizing the framework. The Department of the Army encourages industry partners to engage with this innovative framework, which is expected to significantly advance the capabilities of SDR technology. The Government retains all rights of modifications made to the original framework. To access this software interested parties shall complete the attached Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) (Attachment 1). Individuals identified as contractor representatives/users pursuant to signed/complete NDAs may then create an account on Test Resource Management Center (TRMC) to access the codebase. A step-by-step guide for creating a TRMC account and accessing the repository is included in Attachment 2. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETING THE NDA: An authorized representative of each contractor organization is to complete the following steps to ensure the NDA is processed correctly: Complete all fields on page 1. Complete and sign as the "Recipient’s Authorized Representative" on page 4. Complete the fields for the "Requesting Organization Authorized POC" on page 5. Sign the acknowledgement on page 5 and identify all contractor users from the company they represent. Obtain signatures from all authorized users identified on page 5. Return the completed NDA to the Warped Alloy Management Team at usarmy.meade.7-sig-cmd.mbx.warped-alloy-software@mail.mil for final completion and signature of fields on page 6. For additional information or questions, please reach out using the contact information below. For inquiries, please send an email to the Warped Alloy Management Team at usarmy.meade.7-sig-cmd.mbx.warped-alloy-software@mail.mil Thank you for your attention to this exciting opportunity.

sig_1b62b8abb1aa992552dc.description: SRUC is seeking to implement a fully supported Software as a Service (SaaS) solution that will replace our existing Student Management System and deliver strategic and operational benefits across our undergraduate and post-graduate Teaching activities. Lot 1: . The objectives of this procurement include but are not limited to a modernisation and enhancement of our current 1. timetabling system 2. curriculum management 3. applications and admissions systems 4. student registration 5. Fees and Funding 6. student support and case management 7. post-graduate student management 8. statutory and operational reporting. It is anticipated that the solution will be a modern, future-proofed and highly functional system that shall deliver measurable business efficiencies, benefits and form part of our aspirations for organisation-wide change to processes, systems, controls and employee roles. The solution may also be required to integrate in an up-stream and down-stream manner with other specialist operational systems. It should be noted that SRUC is also considering opportunities to replace its financial and procurement management system within the next 6 to 12 months. The objectives of this project include but are not limited to a modernisation and enhancement of our current 1. operational financial management processes including budgeting, accounts receivable and accounts payable, strategic financial planning and forecasting; 2. procurement and contract management; 3. financial planning and analysis; 4. statutory and management account preparation; 5. tax calculations and return preparation; 6. pre-award & post-award research management; 7. staff expenses; 8. asset and stock management; 9. credit control. The requirement for a third smaller project for a work-based learning system is currently also under review. Any resulting contract for the student management system shall be for an initial period of five years, with the option to extend, by mutual agreement, for five further periods of 12 months. In accordance with the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 the procurement process shall follow a two-stage Restricted Procedure and any subsequent contract award shall be based on the most economically advantageous tender (MEAT). Stage 1: Selection Stage - Open to all interested suppliers - Selection shall be based on capability, capacity, experience and financial standing (using the Single Procurement Document Scotland (SPD)) - The SPD shall be scored on a pass / fail basis. As part of the requirements for this tender, the SPD shall confirm that SRUC is seeking a supplier that is fully accredited under ISO27001 - Written tender submissions (See Stage 2, Part 1) must also be submitted along with the SPD. Stage 2: Tender Stage - Only suppliers that have passed Stage 1 shall proceed to Part 1 (below) and have their written submission evaluated. - Part 1 of the tender stage shall be a formal, written response to questions and submission of an initial price. The top three ranked suppliers (based on their score for the written response to questions) shall then be invited to participate in Part 2 of the tender. SRUC anticipates that one Supplier will be selected to provide this service. Further, it should be noted that SRUC reserves the right to vary the selected numbers. - Part 2 of the tender shall comprise a scored demonstration of the supplier’s system and submission of a final price. It is noted that suppliers can improve and/or vary their price between initial and final submission. It is further noted that SRUC shall not enter a price negotiation with any supplier at any stage of this tender process. - The scoring from Part 1 and Part 2 shall then be combined to provide a final total score, resulting in the identification of a preferred supplier. - Confirmation of a contract award to the preferred supplier shall be subject to approval by the Board of SRUC. It is estimated that any such approval shall be discussed at the September 2026 Board meeting. SRUC regards the implementation of this system as a high risk and complex task. Therefore, SRUC may also seek appropriate implementation consultancy services to support the configuration and implementation of the new system.
sig_1b62b8abb1aa992552dc.title: Provision of a fully supported Student Management System

The object of the contract to be awarded consists of the supply and provision of development and implementation services for an "INTEGRATED OPERATIONAL MONITORING IT SYSTEM" which will be able to ensure the company's general long-term sustainability in terms of staff availability and mobility, from the perspective of ensuring logistical support and implicitly in terms of costs, during the agreed period and in accordance with the obligations assumed under the contract, with the following main components: 1. GIS component, which will allow the management and analysis of spatial data concerning the entire water production infrastructure and water networks (catchments, adductions, transport networks, etc.) 2. SCADA component - modernisation and improvement of the system 3. IoT integrated IT system component and digitalisation of the smart metering component, consisting of a number of new flow meters equipped with an IoT-type communication module, which will create a unified system for monitoring water networks b Digital platform component for collecting data from flow meters and managing information from flow meters (MDC – Meter Data Collection) C Digital platform component for storing and analysing data from flow meters, as well as for the general management of the flow meter fleet (MDM – Meter Data Management) The general objective of the project is to optimise infrastructure operation and monitoring, and to detect losses or topology or network execution defects by: installing an efficient metering and monitoring system; implementing an integrated IT system for infrastructure and water loss management, which offers specific solutions for water supply and distribution management; a system that integrates existing systems and provides the foundation for further developments, creating the foundation of the smart water network. Achieving this objective will ensure the efficiency and sustainability of investments in the water sector and will allow for the acceleration of decisions to improve service quality, maintaining the main parameters (pressure, flow, quality) at a high level, as well as customer satisfaction regarding operability. The IT system proposed for procurement will be a completely new platform, common to the target user groups and activities, with a database core and operating systems compatible with the existing SCADA system, for integration and interoperability. It will be a unified construction, but with user rights structured on distinct personalised modules. These modules are distinct software applications, personalised by user groups, which allow both the editing of field data, as well as the addition of files such as images, PDFs or videos to the common database/storage system, and user access to all technical, telemetry, SCADA and geospatial (GIS) information. The software modules will be web-based with GPRS-GSM data transmission, but will allow editing and access to all GIS project data or without map components and in the absence of a GSM signal, in deficient areas with subsequent automatic or semi-automatic synchronisation. The applications will be secured for each device by password and username and will be able to function on the project implemented locally and offline on the installed module, as well as via WEB/online. sig_1bc16e8744033d7305a3.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET SOUNDING AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also the contracting authority) is using this request for information to survey the market to support the planning of the procurement of a virtual learning and procedure training platform. The purpose of the request for information is to find out what kind of solutions are available on the market to support specialist surgical training, what content and service models suppliers offer, and how the solutions suit the training needs of HUS. The subject of the procurement is a virtual training and learning platform intended for surgical teaching, which supports e.g. step-by-step learning of procedures, understanding of anatomy, studying of surgical techniques and monitoring of training. The potential procurement may include: - ready-made procedure and anatomy content - the ability to produce and manage the organisation's own teaching content - multimodal learning materials (text, image, video, 3D models) - analytics and user-specific learning monitoring - support, maintenance and expert services. We ask suppliers interested in the procurement to reply in writing to the following questions. Description of the platform and content: - What kind of virtual learning, procedure teaching or training environment solution does your solution offer? - What ready-made content (anatomy, procedures, surgical steps, complications, training videos, etc.) does the platform contain? - How is the content updated and how is its up-to-date status ensured? - Is it possible to produce and manage the subscriber organisation's own content (e.g. videos, images, texts, 3D models) in the solution? Suitability for Finnish training and care practices: - How does the solution support surgical care practices and training requirements used in Finland? - Does the platform have ready-made Finnish-language content or is it possible to produce them? - How does the platform support nationally defined competence objectives for specialist fields? - Is it possible to adapt the content according to local training requirements? Licensing, access rights and user management: - What kind of licensing model (e.g. user-specific, organisation-specific, fixed-term) does the platform have? - How can user licence transfers and user changes be implemented? - How is licence pricing determined in a situation where the user does not actively use the service? - What access rights are granted to content produced by the organisation? Technical implementation and information security: - With what technologies has the platform been implemented and what kind of device, browser or connection requirements does it have? - How does your service take into account information security, data protection, processing of patient and personal data, GDPR requirements and the requirements of the client data act (703/2023) and LVV? - Have external information security assessments been carried out on the platform? Commissioning, support and expert services: - What training, maintenance and support services do you offer (e.g. commissioning, technical support, trainer training)? - How quickly are support services available and in which channels? Delivery and service model: - Through what delivery or commissioning model is the solution you offer available (e.g. SaaS, cloud service, hybrid environment, local installation)? - If the solution is cloud-based, where is the data located and are there options for different geographical locations? - If the solution can be delivered as a locally installed version, what infrastructure requirements are associated with it? - Is it possible to choose between different service models? - What kind of reporting or analytics tools do you offer? - How are updates delivered and are they included in the price of the service? References: - What kind of references do you have from medical training, surgical teaching or similar learning platforms? - Is the solution in use in Finland or other Nordic countries? You may also attach brochures or other information about your products and services to your reply if you wish. Please submit replies to the request for information by 15.5.2026 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Subject of the message: "HUS 652-2024: Training and learning platform for surgical procedures". The replies given to this request for information may be used in procurement planning. The contracting authority may, at its discretion, suggest clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have replied to this request for information. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your reply confidentially. The contracting authority does not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information, but a potential contract notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a precondition for participating in a potentially organised subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue.
