sig_1be0867e4c201f640954.description: Väylävirasto is seeking, through an innovation partnership, a solution for the real-time and automated monitoring, calculation and verification of carbon emissions from infrastructure construction sites. The subject of the procurement is not a finished product, but the development, piloting and implementation of a solution in cooperation with the client. The solution must enable active and transparent monitoring of the cumulative emissions of the construction site, the allocation of emissions, total emissions in relation to the forecast, and the identification and verification of the effectiveness of the emission reduction measures implemented. The information must be based on input-based, bill of quantities and/or data model-based traceable monitoring data, which enables comparison with the calculation prepared during the design phase in accordance with the low-carbon assessment method and any targets set by the client at the construction component level. The monitoring data must be usable for monitoring the progress of the construction site and connectable to data model-based tools as well as the client's systems. The goal is to develop a reliable, transparent and scalable solution that: - improves the timeliness of emission data during construction - enables the reliable and consistent separation of measured and calculated data - supports the client's reporting and management needs The solution must enable: - monitoring and reporting of actual quantity data and CO2 emissions during the construction phase (A1–A5) as far as technically possible - overall monitoring of the construction project's emissions, including the overall management of emissions from the materials and masses of the construction components being built and site logistics (energy consumption and transport), i.e. all emissions related to the construction site. - traceability, transparency and documentation of data in emission monitoring in accordance with the standards defined by Väylävirasto as well as allocation to the construction site in a traceable manner based on the bill of quantities and/or data model. - compatibility with Väylävirasto's low-carbon assessment method and sustainable construction standards - compatibility with other agency systems, such as the project portal, situational awareness service and other systems defined by the client. The procurement is described in detail in the request for participation and its annexes. For the partner, the project offers an opportunity to participate in product development, which can open up new markets and customer relationships. The end result of the project is aimed at a product marketable to the partner, for which there is a broad market among contracting authorities in Finland and internationally. The starting point of the project is that the partner receives the intellectual property rights enabling commercialisation and further development of the solution being developed, and the client receives a broad right of use for the solution. The arrangements for intellectual property rights are described in more detail in the draft contract. The contracting authority will select one partner for the development phase. The client's budget for the development phase is approximately 150 000 euros.

sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.description: Background and Objectives of the Pathfinder Project: The Public Sector AI (PSAI) Directorate within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) exists to help the government make brilliant public services that empower people in the UK. We work at the very centre of government to drive digital transformation focused on user needs and to reimagine how government uses AI to deliver public services and initiatives. The newly established Government Efficiency Accelerator (GEA) programme is a flagship initiative aimed at driving operational efficiencies across some of the government's key enabling functions (Finance, Policy, HR) through the safe and responsible adoption of AI. The GEA is working in collaboration with the GCF Commercial Innovation Hub (CIH) to better understand the availability of AI based solutions that can be used by teams across government departments to drive efficiency and increase productivity. The goal of this Pathfinder Project is to engage with the market to understand current capabilities, initially focusing on three core business areas: Finance, HR and policy (more details on a specific problem area below). Applicants should note that this engagement is not intended to lead to the procurement of a particular solution for DSIT or any other UK Government Department. Rather, we are looking to build a catalogue of tested and "kitemarked" products that will be made available to public sector organisations to consider procuring them in the knowledge that they have been tested and will meet requirements such as security, usability, transparency etc. We are interested in hearing from all types of suppliers and would particularly encourage SMEs and VCSEs to submit proposals. Challenge Summary: As noted above, the GEA and CIH are engaging with the market to build a deeper understanding of how AI based solutions and products can help make government departments more efficient and productive. We appreciate there are a multitude of potential use cases so for this initial engagement we have chosen to focus on problems relating to budgeting and workforce forecasting. We are inviting suppliers to submit proposals outlining how their products could be used by finance teams across UK government departments in a safe, transparent and unbiased way. We are keen to explore solutions which can reduce the level of repetitive tasks required specifically when budgeting and conducting workforce forecasting. Submissions should demonstrate how the solution can streamline tasks, improve accuracy, and shorten time spent on repetitive work in order to free colleagues up to complete higher-value work. There is no fixed scope, as we aim for platform-agnostic, AI driven and innovative tools that adapt to various organisational needs. Solution should be accessible to organisations of all sizes and is not dependent on any specific ERP platform.
sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.title: GEA Pathfinder

sig_1c0ed4be1626734ebc0c.description: The structural and semantic harmonization of the OKSTRA (object catalogue for road and transport engineering) and IFC (Industry Foundation Classes) standards is becoming increasingly important for the digitalisation of road engineering. OKSTRA is a national standard with a high level of detail specific to road engineering, object-oriented modelling and integrated validation support. It forms the basis of numerous specialist processes such as INSPIRE data provision, the VEMAGS statics module and road information databases. IFC is an internationally recognised, vendor-neutral BIM standard which, with version 4.3, was comprehensively extended to infrastructure structures for the first time. However, IFC classes are uniform internationally and are not designed for specific national requirements. There is a considerable need for harmonization between the two standards: OKSTRA describes road-related facts in a finely granular and unambiguous manner, whereas IFC focuses on physical components and partly uses more generic structures. There are currently various lists of technical meanings between the federal states, which lead to inconsistent assignments of meanings. Without a clear, machine-readable assignment of OKSTRA specialist objects to IFC structures, neither automated conversion nor reliable validation is possible. Objectives The aim of this research project is the development and provision of a feature database that contains OKSTRA object classes, BIM object catalogue objects and the harmonised list of technical meanings including attributes, and unambiguously assigns these to IFC entities, property sets and classifications. In addition, the exploratory harmonization of different schemas is to be carried out. The feature database is to be provided as a machine-readable artefact via a standardised REST API interface. The mapping is to be carried out completely across all OKSTRA object classes and the harmonised list of technical meanings. Operation within the federal BIM portal is to be investigated. Benefits of the R&D project With the feature database, the R&D project creates a binding basis for automated OKSTRA/IFC conversion and thus enables lossless data exchange between OKSTRA- and BIM-based processes in road engineering. The semantically correct assignments increase planning quality and enhance efficiency in the implementation of BIM projects in road engineering. Duplicate structures and parallel data storage are avoided. In addition, the project supports the ongoing standardization of OKSTRA and buildingSMART by providing consolidated mapping rules that can be incorporated into the further development of the standards. Lot LOT-0000: Development of a feature database for the semantic linkage of OKSTRA and IFC. The structural and semantic harmonization of the OKSTRA (object catalogue for road and transport engineering) and IFC (Industry Foundation Classes) standards is becoming increasingly important for the digitalisation of road engineering. OKSTRA is a national standard with a high level of detail specific to road engineering, object-oriented modelling and integrated validation support. It forms the basis of numerous specialist processes such as INSPIRE data provision, the VEMAGS statics module and road information databases. IFC is an internationally recognised, vendor-neutral BIM standard which, with version 4.3, was comprehensively extended to infrastructure structures for the first time. However, IFC classes are uniform internationally and are not designed for specific national requirements. There is a considerable need for harmonization between the two standards: OKSTRA describes road-related facts in a finely granular and unambiguous manner, whereas IFC focuses on physical components and partly uses more generic structures. There are currently various lists of technical meanings between the federal states, which lead to inconsistent assignments of meanings. Without a clear, machine-readable assignment of OKSTRA specialist objects to IFC structures, neither automated conversion nor reliable validation is possible. Objectives The aim of this research project is the development and provision of a feature database that contains OKSTRA object classes, BIM object catalogue objects and the harmonised list of technical meanings including attributes, and unambiguously assigns these to IFC entities, property sets and classifications. In addition, the exploratory harmonization of different schemas is to be carried out. The feature database is to be provided as a machine-readable artefact via a standardised REST API interface. The mapping is to be carried out completely across all OKSTRA object classes and the harmonised list of technical meanings. Operation within the federal BIM portal is to be investigated. Benefits of the R&D project With the feature database, the R&D project creates a binding basis for automated OKSTRA/IFC conversion and thus enables lossless data exchange between OKSTRA- and BIM-based processes in road engineering. The semantically correct assignments increase planning quality and enhance efficiency in the implementation of BIM projects in road engineering. Duplicate structures and parallel data storage are avoided. In addition, the project supports the ongoing standardization of OKSTRA and buildingSMART by providing consolidated mapping rules that can be incorporated into the further development of the standards.
sig_1c0ed4be1626734ebc0c.title: Development of a feature database for the semantic linkage of OKSTRA and IFC

sig_1cc2ca142bc183305faa.description: SBB Telecom is currently undergoing a modernization process for its networks and production platform. This includes the renewal of the data and mobile network across Switzerland in the coming years. Additionally, there is a need to replace or modernize tools in the OSS/BSS area, aiming towards an integrated production platform. One important component of this procurement is the Multi Domain Service Orchestrator (MDSO). The MDSO will act as a central platform for automating and orchestrating the delivery and management of services across various network domains, including data, security, and cellular networks. Additionally, a service assurance solution will be integrated to detect any irregularities in the services and enable appropriate measures to be taken. The MDSO plays a crucial role in ensuring interoperability among various providers and technologies, thus guaranteeing smooth and efficient service delivery for SBB Telecom. This platform will not only facilitate the delivery of the anticipated 100,000 services but also monitor them using the Service Assurance component, so that, in case of any irregularities, prompt action can be taken. Furthermore, the platform is responsible for orchestrating and monitoring network resources. For future network development, SBB aims to implement the zero-touch installation approach to automatically deploy the new networks. The goal is to utilize this approach for approximately 20,000 network devices in the new data network and around 1,800 RAN (Radio Access Network) sites in the mobile communications sector. These devices and sites will need to be efficiently put into operation and monitored. The solution being sought should optionally support the implementation of this approach. The MDSO production platform must support modernization towards open interfaces, decoupling of functions, and a scalable and open architecture. SBB is seeking a provider who embraces agile collaboration and follows modern software development approaches
sig_1cc2ca142bc183305faa.title: Multi Domain Service Orchestrator (MDSO)

sig_1cd46a061ff6e7b07660.description: Solicitation Number: Notice Type: W31P4Q27RA009 Request for Information/Sources Sought Purpose & Disclaimer: This Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be considered as an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Quotations (RFQ), or Request for Proposals (RFP). Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the U.S. Government (USG) to acquire any products or services described in this RFI/SS. Your response to this notice is strictly voluntary and will be treated only as information for the USG to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI/SS, and the USG will not pay for the information submitted. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. The information provided may be used by the Army in developing its acquisition strategy. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition-sensitive information contained in their response. If a solicitation is released for the supplies or services described herein, it will be synopsized on the government-wide point of entry (SAM.gov). The response date for this RFI/SS is 25 September 2026. Background: The US Army, Search Track Acquire Radiate Eliminate (STARE) Project Office is conducting market research for Production and Engineering Services of the Lower Tier Air Missile Defense Sensor (LTAMDS). All production and engineering services must strictly conform to the U.S. Government (USG) performance specification (P-Spec), MIS-PRF-59464, and the Raytheon Prime Item Performance (PIP) specification, MIS-PRF-62863, Rev B. Effort would include all associated hardware, software, firmware, and engineering services inherent to production (e.g. inspection, systems integration, logistics support, depot maintenance, spares package development, program management, configuration management, software development, product assurance, verification of system performance, hazardous material management, obsolescence management, safety, testing and evaluation, coordination for and implementation of future training exercises etc.), interim contractor support (ICS), system integration and check out support (SICO), new equipment training (NET), and technical documentation. The USG has a requirement for follow-on production of LTAMDS following successful completion of the LTAMDS 6-lot Urgent Material Release (UMR) Prototype Development Project. This effort was previously competitively awarded on 16 October 2019 to Raytheon Company through an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), W15QKN-20-9-1002, pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022 (formerly 10 U.S.C.§ 2371b(a)). Other related awards include: • Pre-Planned Product Improvement (P3I): A 2-lot agreement awarded on 24 May 2022 to Raytheon Company through an OTA, AMTC-21-02-008, pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 4022. Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP): A four-option-year, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)-based Undefinitized Contract Action awarded on 31 July 2024 to Raytheon Company through Army Contracting Command (Contract #: W31P4Q-24-C-0024), pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. § 2304(a)(7)), as implemented in FAR 6.302-1. The LRIP contract has an anticipated production quantity of up to 48 radars. Scope of Planned Procurement: This follow-on LTAMDS requirement is anticipated to be awarded as a seven (7) year Multiyear Procurement (MYP), Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. This effort will cover a production ceiling of twenty (20) LTAMDS radars annually. The award will also include annual task orders for engineering services, alongside yearly orders for SICO, ICS, and NET support. First Article Inspection (FAI), Environmental Stress Screening (ESS), Product Acceptance, Functional Configuration Audit (FCA), Physical Configuration Audit (PCA), and Highly Accelerated Life Testing (HALT) may be required for baseline revisions and/or updates. Initial delivery of the LTAMDS radars is required no later than 33 months after contract award. This procurement will include access to classified information. The successful contractor must be a U.S. corporation with a secure manufacturing facility approved to the SECRET level by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) (formerly DSS). Additionally, the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) may conduct a pre-award survey of the contractor’s facility to evaluate technical capability, financial viability, and quality assurance processes to minimize LTAMDS program execution risks. Technical Data Package (TDP) Constraints A formal Technical Data Package (TDP) was submitted to the USG on 31 July 2026. The USG is currently executing an exhaustive technical validation and quality assurance assessment against all applicable American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) digital product definition and drafting standards (including model-based definition and data schema protocols), alongside establishing downstream 3D model generation and repository architectures. Due to the duration required to complete this verification and standardization process, the USG will not release technical data packages, native 3D models, or detailed specifications in support of this RFI/SS. Acquisition Strategy & Authority The Government will consider all capability statements received. To be deemed a viable source, interested firms must demonstrate their capability to fulfill the requirements without causing substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, and without causing unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's urgent air defense requirements. Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), OR REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ). IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE RFQ, IFB, OR RFP. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WIL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. Required Submission Information Interested firms that believe they have the capability, experience, and legal access to data necessary to fulfill the requirements detailed above are invited to submit a statement of capability. Submissions must include the following information: 1. Company name, physical address, overnight delivery address (if different from mailing address), CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Primary point of contact (POC) name, title, email address, and telephone number. 2. Business size status under the NAICS code associated with radar manufacturing (i.e. Large, Small Disadvantaged, Veteran Owned, Woman Owned, etc.) 3. Affirmation that the company is a U.S. corporation and verification of active facility clearance at the SECRET level, and confirmation of cleared personnel capable of starting work immediately upon award. 4. A description of your firm's manufacturing expertise, capacity, and facility infrastructure to meet the required LTAMDS production throughput (up to 20 radars annually) 5. Detailed explanation of how your firm would execute First Article Inspection (FAI), ESS, FCA, PCA, and HALT along with an estimated schedule and cost associated with completing these activities prior to commencing deliveries. 6. Assuming the Government will not provide a TDP, provide a detailed estimate of the schedule and cost (via a rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimate) required to reverse-engineer or independently develop and qualify a compatible alternative radar system. 7. Explain how your proposed schedule—including necessary timelines for reverse engineering, prototype development, system integration, qualification, and testing—can realistically meet the Government’s required initial delivery window of no later than 36 months after contract award. 8. Explain how your strategy prevents substantial duplication of non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs to the Government. 9. Evidence of the company's performance history and experience meeting strict contractual due dates on programs of similar scope, technical complexity, and scale. Submission Instructions All responses must be UNCLASSIFIED. All questions must be submitted to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer identified above. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought. Potential sources are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition-sensitive information. All such information must be clearly identified and marked at the paragraph level. All assumptions, including any assumed USG support, shall be clearly identified. Responses must be submitted in electronic format (compatible with MS Word or PDF) and must not exceed 15 pages total (including tables, charts, and appendices). Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged. The Government will not provide direct feedback or individual evaluations to respondents regarding their submissions. The Government reserves the right to contact respondents for clarification or additional information as necessary. All responses must be transmitted electronically no later than 21 October 2026 (or the updated date indicated on the final posting) to the following primary POCs: Primary Point of Contact: Dawn Patterson Chief, Acquisition Management Division STARE Project Office, CPE – Defensive Fires, PAE – Fires SFAE-PFD-R Email: Dawn.p.patterson2.civ@mail.mil Contracting Office Address: Army Contracting Command-Redstone (ACC-RSA) CCAM-MSA-C ACC-RSA, Bldg 4505 Huntsville, AL 35898 ACC Point of Contact: Joel Koppinger Contracting Officer CCAM-MSA-C, ACC-RSA Joel.m.koppinger.civ@mail.mil

sig_1cda1ddfd2cb87305a8b.description: Reykjavík Procurement Office, on behalf of the department of Service and Innovation, welcomes tenders for a DAM (digital asset management) system for the City of Reykjavík. sig_1ce7b698769dc61d75cf.description: The subject of the procurement is information security inspections and audits for DigiFinland Oy's projects and services, which includes technical information security testing and architecture reviews (platform services/infrastructure, system integrations). The audit uses inter alia security audit criteria PiTuKri, Katakri and GDPR, as well as applicable international frameworks and best practices, such as OWASP (e.g. OWASP Top 10) and CIS Controls. The work will be carried out in compliance with DigiFinland's internal information handling guidelines (public, internal and confidential). If necessary, the work may also process classified information (TL) in accordance with the client's instructions and applicable legislation. The audit is implemented in such a way that the information security level of the audited service or service package can be determined. The selected supplier, i.e. the auditor, performs so-called ethical hacking on the service, where the auditor programmatically searches for vulnerabilities and other information security problems in the target designated by DigiFinland or evaluates the architecture of the service from an information security perspective. The auditor draws up an information security report in which potential service vulnerabilities and other information security-related problems are specified and instructions for resolving them are provided. This report is reviewed with representatives of DigiFinland and the IT suppliers that built the service. The audits cover DigiFinland's existing services (currently Omaolo, Navigator Services and grounds for treatment) as well as potential future services. According to the contracting authority's non-binding estimate, each service will be audited once per calendar year. The estimated total value of the procurement is approximately 300 000 †.
sig_1ce7b698769dc61d75cf.title: DigiFinland Oy - IT consulting 2023-2028 (DPS) - Information Security Testing

sig_1ced1263dffe9796f2a1.description: Introduction and Background: The Gambling Commission is an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. The Commission is responsible for issuing personal gambling licences for individuals and gambling operating licences for businesses operating in Great Britain and we are responsible for ensuring all licensed gambling is conducted subject to the following licensing objectives: • preventing gambling from being a source of crime or disorder, being associated with crime or disorder or being used to support crime • ensuring that gambling is conducted in a fair and open way • protecting children and other vulnerable people from being harmed or exploited by gambling. In January 2025, we published a consultation which proposed changes to our requirements on licensees, through the Gaming Machine Technical Standards (GMTS), Gaming Machine Testing Strategy (testing strategy) and the Licence Conditions and Codes of Practice (LCCP). This was in connection with the commitment in the April 2023 Gambling Act Review White Paper (*1) that set out that: “The Gambling Commission will conduct a review of its gaming machine technical standards. The review will include an assessment of the role of session limits across category B and C machines and the role of safer gambling tools. The review will consider the effects of any legislative change following the Gambling Act Review and, where appropriate, will consolidate the progress made so far by the industry on a voluntary basis.” In January 2026, we set out our position in relation to our proposal to introduce a licence condition to more effectively address non-compliant gaming machines (*2). The new licence condition came into effect on 29 July 2026. Our September response (*3) sets out our position in relation to all other proposals within the consultation published in January 2025. In line with fulfilling our 2024-2027 corporate strategy which includes evaluating the GAR White Paper commitments we are responsible for, the Commission will be conducting an evaluation of the changes arising from the consultation. As part of this evaluation, we are looking to procure qualitative research in land-based premises to be carried out between April 2027 and January 2029. We envisage this will be delivered across 2 or 3 waves of fieldwork. The first wave of fieldwork will be a pilot study to collect baseline data after the session definition is introduced, and to test the feasibility of the methodology; this data collection must be carried out after 30 March 2027 and be completed by 29 June 2027. The pilot study will also be an opportunity to trial approaches for the full fieldwork, to be carried out post-implementation from 30 June 2027 and should be used to inform the wider project’s design. Land-based fieldwork in gambling premises presents an exciting opportunity for the Commission to explore an often-underutilised methodology within gambling research; capturing the experiences and behaviours of consumers, and staff, of the policy changes in real-time and in live environments. This kind of data collection is especially powerful as it partly mitigates limitations of other qualitative approaches, such as surveys or remote interviews, which rely on consumer recall and accurate self-report. Ethnographic, fieldwork-based approaches can utilise in-person interviews or questionnaires and also incorporate methods such as observation in order to gain a more rounded view of participant experiences. We also welcome innovative or new approaches within relevant disciplines. Please note: This project will collect data to be triangulated within the Gaming Machine evaluation, it will not be carrying out evaluation itself or producing evaluation-related outputs. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Purpose of the Engagement: • Understand market capability to provide expertise and specialist research in land-based gambling across Great Britain; with a focus on qualitative and ethnographic methods within live, public environments that engage members of the public. • Explore indicative cost models for the pilot study and full fieldwork ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Description of Requirements: Expertise and experience - Suppliers should have demonstratable experience with relevant methodologies, and past experience of delivering successful public-facing fieldwork in Great Britain in gambling, retail or hospitality premises. Especially strong bids would have experience conducting fieldwork in different contexts across multiple locations. Research requirements - Methodologies should be drawn from qualitative and ethnographic approaches and aim to capture consumer experiences and behaviour, in addition to staff experiences, relating to the policy changes; this could include interviews, questionnaires, and observational data, as examples. More innovative and original methodologies in the field are welcome; especially surrounding ethnographies, play-based research, place-based approaches, and research that has explored experiences of gaming machines. For example, methods could explore the experience of, and feelings about, limit setting functionality (Proposal 4) (*4) and its potential impact on consumer play. Depending on the chosen methodological approaches, relevant ethical approval(s) will need to be in place that follow the Commission’s Research Governance Framework (*5); including any relevant guidelines for conducting gambling research with human participants. Locations of premises included in the fieldwork should span city and rural areas; with geographical diversity in mind across England, Wales and Scotland; for example, covering city centre to costal locations. Researchers should also anticipate some fieldwork occurring outside of regular working hours, in order to capture different times of day and levels of business in relevant venues. There are four types of premises affected by the policy changes, and these should all be included in the research approach: Types of premises included in the fieldwork should include: - Casino - Adult Gaming Centre (AGC) - Bingo; this would include more traditional Bingo Clubs as well as high street Bingo premises - Betting Exact numbers of venues will vary depending on the methodological approach. We expect the pilot to cover less venues than the full fieldwork. The full fieldwork would ideally include 2 separate waves of data collection. In more detail, the approximate number of venues the pilot & full fieldwork would include: Please note this is anticipating an even split between Casino, AGC, Bingo and Betting premises. • Minimum: 16 venues • Expected: 24 venues • Ideal: 32 + venues These figures should be used to inform estimated minimum, expected and ideal costings. In addition to venue coverage, ideal, expected and minimum participant sampling numbers would be established in project set up and explored via the Pilot Study to ensure a diversity of perspectives are captured; including identities that are often under-represented in gambling research. Deliverables - Data will be shared in clear, appropriately anonymised formats. A short report accounting the methodological approach, ethics, and any lessons learned for the Commission, would also be produced for internal use and to inform the wider Gaming Machine evaluation. The vendor must comply with all relevant legislation, including data protection (GDPR) legislation. Timescale - The project will have natural periods of intensity and pause due to implementation timelines. Vendors would need to be able to deliver fieldwork in windows across 2027 to early 2029. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Links to sources: (*1) Gambling Act Review White Paper - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/high-stakes-gambling-reform-for-the-digital-age (*2) January 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-gaming-machine-consultation-part-1-response (*3) September 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-consultation-on-proposed-changes-to-the-gmts-testing-strategy-and-lccp-consultation-response/related-documents-january-2025-gaming-machine-consultation-part-2-response (*4) Proposal 4 / September 2026 Response - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/consultation-response/january-2025-consultation-on-proposed-changes-to-the-gmts-testing-strategy-and-lccp-consultation-response/proposal-4-gaming-machine-consultation-part-2-response (*5) The Commission's Research Governance Framework - https://www.gamblingcommission.gov.uk/standards/research-governance-framework/data-accessibility-and-data-sharing-information-and-data-research-governance Lot 1: .

sig_1d1e22c08aaa61bab36d.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a procurement procedure with the publication of the Request for Information; instead, any potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a precondition for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Suppliers are not paid compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. HUS is surveying solutions on the market for an AI-based customer service assistant that combines information retrieval, service guidance and a conversational user interface. The aim of the request for information is primarily to increase the contracting authority's understanding of solutions available on the market, their capabilities, product maturity and implementation methods, as well as to support the preparation of a possible future procurement. HUS is looking for a solution that can act as the user's primary interface for customer service and information retrieval and thus partly replace the traditional search function. The goal is not a separate floating widget or a traditional chatbot plugin, but an assistant naturally integrated into the website. The assistant must be available on the site continuously, but its user interface must not be dominant, intrusive or forcefully demanding the user's attention. In the target state, the assistant resembles a search bar in its role, but its capabilities are substantially broader than traditional search. The solution must operate as part of the site's core user interface so that the user encounters it in the same role as the search function, not as a separate or overlapping component. The starting point for the user interface is a conversation between the customer and artificial intelligence. From the perspective of further development, the solution takes into account the possibility of transferring customer service to a human when necessary, if required. This is not a first-stage functionality, but relates to preparedness and integration capability, where any transition to customer service is implemented by utilising a separate in-use Contact Center solution. The role of the solution is to act as a guiding user interface for customer service, not as an independent system executing transactions or a channel replacing backend systems. In the future, other customer service channels and services can be integrated into the assistant as part of the user experience, but the assistant does not actually replace these underlying services. The request for information primarily seeks off-the-shelf products available on the market, not solutions developed specifically for customers from scratch. Limited customisation on top of the ready-made product is possible to achieve the target state, but the core capabilities of the solution must already exist in the ready-made product. In addition, these core capabilities must be in use and validated by other customers in regular production use. The solution is expected to enable at least the following functionalities: Information retrieval and answering • retrieves and presents information comprehensibly • answers user questions directly, where appropriate also guiding them to sources or services • acts as the user's primary interface for information retrieval, not merely a list of search results Guidance and customer service support • guides the user to the correct service, customer service channel or next stage • structures the service architecture comprehensibly for the user • identifies when the user needs action guidance in addition to information Situational awareness • understands the user's situation and intent, not just individual search words • asks clarifying questions when necessary • limits operation so that the user is not given diagnoses or treatment instructions Explaining concepts • explains concepts, terms and service-related matters comprehensibly • adapts the response method into, for example, a clearer or simpler form • utilises terminology, contents or other manageable information sources Multilingualism • operates at least in Finnish, Swedish and English with equal quality • enables language switching even mid-transaction • produces responses in a controlled manner even when the source content is not directly available in that language Integratability and user experience • integrates naturally into the website's user interface as part of the service • is available on different pages of the site without dominating the user experience • supports the possibility of transferring customer service to a conversation with a human when necessary Reliability, controllability and security • utilises manageable information sources • supports the production of correct and up-to-date answers • enables sources to be shown to the user when appropriate • meets requirements related to information security and data protection

sig_1d284f8f0326426a5aef.description: We have kickstarted a large programme to understand the existing challenges and opportunities. The key findings of the current state assessment are:  Contract Management & Optimisation: Multiple contracts providing similar services creates several challenges including, increased costs and overheads.  Duplication of Services: Overlapping services (especially telephone payments and direct debits) lead to administrative complexity and unnecessary costs (economies of scale).  Inconsistent Customer Experience: Customers from different parts of the merged organisation face varied payment options, leading to confusion and potential dis-satisfaction.  Gap in Services: With closure of banks and post offices, local convenient options for customers to pay (pay point), alternatives to minimise handling of cash (card machines) etc.  Technical Inefficiency: Managing multiple systems creates increased complexity for our technical teams within Technology & Finance. As a result, the group have set out key justifications which revolve around implementing a single enterprise-wide solution for Payments and Collections  Offers the opportunity to reduce the technical complexity and contractual challenges resulting from several solutions across Payments & Collections.  Improves Customer Experience by centralising Collections through a single solution providing all Customers a single view.  Potential to improve collection routes available to customers in a changing banking environment.  Improves group's ability to report and track insights enabling wider recovery strategy improvements.  Simplifies internal Business Processes and business adoption activities because of a single-solution focus. Lot 1: .

sig_1d3ac604a526b988e9fa.description: By the present procurement procedure, the EIT KIC Urban Mobility S.L. hereby being referred to as “EIT UM” or the “Company” is aiming to identify a provider (hereinafter, referred to as “Provider”) to support the Digital Platform for EIT Urban Mobility community, presently known as “Mobility Innovators”. This document, along with its annexes, constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by EIT Urban Mobility for a potential procurement of services in the field of online communities. EIT Urban Mobility community is made of over 270 partners and larger ecosystem of more than 1,200 stakeholders as we work together to make the transition to more sustainable urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. This community includes industry, including large enterprises, SMEs, and startups, universities and education institutions; students and alumni; research and technology organisations; governments at local, regional, national and EU-level; and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Two years ago, EIT Urban Mobility launched its private digital community platform, Mobility Innovators, which brings together our vibrant community of innovators described above. The platform already has more than 1,500 active users and serves as the central platform for collaboration and engagement within our community. Mobility Innovators enables partners and stakeholders to access information, documents and opportunities shared by EIT Urban Mobility, register for events, and engage in discussions with peers across sectors. It connects organisations from industry, research, academia, and the public sector, fostering collaboration to advance the transition towards more sustainable and liveable urban mobility. Our goal in this next phase is to further grow and activate the community, expand platform functionalities, and enhance user experience to ensure Mobility Innovators continues to support EIT Urban Mobility’s role as Europe’s leading innovation community for urban mobility.

sig_1dc5f8b6a8d7d73ed79e.description: The delivery of Security Incident Response services for the Participants via an SLA. The scope of this procurement consists of the following core components. - Analysis: mapping the scale and cause of an incident and conducting a robust and adequate investigation/response; - Coordination: coordinating the approach to the incident at Participants. Coordination of the activities may relate to all components of the Assignment. - Defence and mitigation: containing and eradicating the "infected" components of the IT and OT Infrastructure ("fire brigade function") - Investigation: carrying out digital forensic investigation ("detective function"). - Evaluation and reporting: adequately transferring results (investigation details) to incident response partners designated by us ("reporting function"). These reports must also be able to contribute to compliancy, for instance by delivering a "second opinion". As part of these core components, the following may be delivered: - The delivery and/or deployment of hardware and software for the execution of parts of this Assignment. In doing so, the Contractor shall take into account the standards and/or installed base used by the Participant. - Trainings: Where applicable, the Participant may request the Contractor to execute or provide trainings. In addition to these core components, the following matters are also part of the scope. - Strategic and technical consultancy: Strategic and technical advice on the handling of incidents. Consider advice on paying compensation in the event of attacks/ransomware. Or strategic advice on policy regarding these topics. - Communication advice: advice on communication strategies and advice on communication during specific incidents. This may include assisting the Institution in drafting communiqués and/or translating technical matters into understandable language to support general communication towards the outside world. This may also include additional reporting activities, such as advising on how reports can be shared with the (SURF) communities and/or third parties or contributing to presentations in which results are shared. - Conducting discussions on behalf of the Institution regarding security incidents with "malicious actors". - Other ways of knowledge sharing within and outside the Institutions/community, such as contributing knowledge and expertise to exercises, red teaming and training to strengthen cooperation within the incident response process. Each incident response request may include one or more of the mentioned tasks, but does not have to include all tasks. For instance, when an incident occurs, the Institution may invoke "defence and mitigation", whilst that same Institution may arrange the coordination of activities itself. Other combinations of components of the assignment may also be assigned to the contractor by the Institution.
sig_1dc5f8b6a8d7d73ed79e.title: Security Incident Response 2.0 (2026)

sig_1dcc234e4a0c51b91703.description: The procurement concerns the purchase and delivery of the "Digital Wind Turbine" for Skive College. The learning activities must be targeted at students on the electrician training programme GF2, participants on specialised courses on electrical installations in wind turbines, AMU courses, etc. The solution must include simulation equipment and tools as well as other technologies that support practice-oriented scenarios and learning processes, including the visualisation of functions and workflows, among other things through a realistic interactive 3D simulation environment. The solution comprises equipment such as software, programming, licences and physical devices such as PCs, presentation screens and visualisation equipment used together via a hosted IT platform. The supplier is responsible for the final development and customisation of the solution in accordance with this specification for the digital wind turbine, implementation (configuration and setup, testing, training, etc.) and commissioning of the overall solution, as well as the provision of operational services. Any development services form part of the customer's procurement. The digital wind turbine is primarily financed by pool funds under the EU Recovery Fund for "Equipment investments in vocational and labour market education targeted at the green transition 2025". The contract covers the purchase and delivery of the "Digital Wind Turbine" for Skive College.

sig_1e23be12466ac686cbe7.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR INVITATION TO TENDER, BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET SURVEY AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tender contest by publishing this information request; instead, any potential contract notice and invitation to tender will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tender contest that may be held. Suppliers will not be remunerated for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this information request will be used in the preparation of the procurement and the evaluation of implementation options for remote monitoring solutions. HUS and Keusote are planning a procurement related to the research, implementation and deployment of a digital solution (eMOM) supporting the treatment of gestational diabetes (GDM). The objectives of the solution are to: • support patient self-care, • utilise data produced or measured by the patient, • provide professionals with a remote monitoring view, • function in both primary healthcare and specialised medical care contexts. The solution is provisionally examined through the following data sources: • continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), • fingertip measurements, • diet and weight, • physical activity, • physiological metrics (e.g. HRV, EDA), • audio and self-assessment data (EMA). The aim is to find an implementation model that is: • cost-effective, • scalable for use by wellbeing services counties, • enables the further development of the solution and potential broader utilisation. The purpose of the market dialogue is to: • survey solution and implementation options existing on the market, • receive feedback on the preliminary service description, • evaluate the suitability of various procurement models (e.g. ready-made solution, development project, hybrid model), • clarify perspectives related to implementation, costs, maintenance and lifecycle. The market dialogue we are planning will be implemented in two phases: Phase 1 – written commentary (summer 2026) • Suppliers will be provided with a preliminary service description. • Suppliers are asked to submit written comments. Phase 2 – company meetings (autumn 2026) • Detailed discussions will be organised with selected operators. The subject of the planned procurement is a digital solution comprising, inter alia: • an application intended for patient use or a corresponding solution, • a professional user interface, • integrations with wellbeing data (continuous glucose, diet and physical activity), • potential integrations with patient information systems. The solution must be suitable for multiple use cases and enable the remote monitoring of multiple different patient groups using the same technical solution. The solution must be implemented such that: • new data sources can be connected via interfaces, • the solution is scalable to other use cases without significant structural changes, • the solution supports use in both primary healthcare and specialised healthcare environments. The solution does not include the implementation of prediction models. Prediction models will be produced by the contracting authority (HUS and KeuSote) or a separate third party. It is the supplier's responsibility to implement the solution such that: • prediction models can be integrated and used securely, • the results produced by the models can be presented as part of the service, • the results of the models are distinguishable from other data. The solution must enable the connection of prediction models via interfaces. The contracting authority assesses that, depending on the intended use of the prediction models, they may fall within the scope of regulation concerning medical devices (MDR). If such models are utilised in the solution, the responsibility for their regulatory compliance lies with the model producer (e.g. manufacturer), not the supplier implementing the platform. The preliminary starting point is that prediction models act as decision support and do not make automatic clinical decisions without a professional's assessment. The exact content, scope and implementation model of the solution will be refined based on the market dialogue. The implementation of the solution must include operational and technical maintenance during the research phase, provisionally until the end of year 2028. The aim is to recruit approximately 400 individuals diagnosed with gestational diabetes within the KeuSote region to participate in the research. The contracting authority also assesses the possibility of procuring maintenance as an option after the research phase. Suppliers are asked to comment on maintenance models and their impacts on costs, implementation and lifecycle. Intellectual Property Rights and Further Development (Preliminary Principle) In preparing the procurement, the contracting authority will assess solutions that enable: • the further development of the solution, • the flexible arrangement of portability and maintenance, • as well as the utilisation of the solution in the operations of multiple organisations. In addition, the contracting authority will assess possibilities to agree on separate: • licensing or usage right arrangements, • as well as potential cooperation models related to commercialisation. Arrangements related to commercialisation are not part of the subject matter of the procurement, but they can be examined separately at a later stage.

sig_1e36e4da8b700c63d492.description: South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. Lot 1: . South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. The MTBIC is a new build, being built in partnership with Hub South East. Morrisons are the main contractor. The appointed supplier will need to source, provide and install all required equipment per an IT matrix that has been produced and will be issued as part of the tender documentation. They will also need to provide a managed service provision to the tenants and SOSE within the building. Key requirements will likely include but will not be limited to: - Full Wi-Fi network, both internal and external - EDUROM Network - Ability for segregation of network to tenants - Ability to link into fire alarm and CCTV systems where appropriate - Managed service provision - Ability to live stream from the building - Potential for 100 concurrent users at select times - IT security compliant with relevant statutory requirements - Managed and maintained equipment - Service desk provision SOSE will require a comprehensive service, from inception to completion. The MTBIC is a brand new building, and the contractor will provide the cable routes and CAT install but SOSE is required to undertake all other aspects. Any infrastructure required e.g. WAPs, cabinets will need to be costed and provided for as part of this tender. SOSE will not be seeking discrete components or partial delivery — the requirement is for a single, fully managed service covering all IT and network requirements for the building. The purpose of the MTBIC is to provide workshop space to companies interested in developing new and exciting technology, hot desk space and office space, events space both internal and external. This is to be a hub out of which businesses will operate.

sig_1e54a836dbecee79c03c.description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. The platform supports traceability, information exchange and risk management in the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) area. The contract will also support interoperability with local systems and relevant international platforms, as well as gradual alignment with the EU IMSOC approach, including TRACES NT, RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS-related functionalities, where relevant. Maintenance, support, further development and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is based on the TRACES NT source code provided by the European Commission’s DG SANTE to CEFTA and adapted to support SPS processes and information exchange within CEFTA. The platform supports the electronic processing, issuance and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and other SPS-related documentation and data, as well as traceability, information exchange and risk management between competent administrations. A key objective of the contract is to further develop CEFTA TRACES NT towards fully electronic, end-to-end exchange of phytosanitary and veterinary certificates within CEFTA and, progressively, with the European Union, reducing and ultimately replacing paper-based exchanges where the necessary technical conditions are in place. This will include further development of electronic certification workflows, certificate models, validation mechanisms, electronic signatures and trust services, and the interfaces required for electronic data exchange. The contract will also support the completion, further development and operationalisation of the CEFTA Notification System for plant health and food and feed safety, including notifications concerning risks, non-compliant consignments, rejections and related follow-up information. The contract will cover continuous maintenance, security, performance and reliability of the platform, as well as upgrades and new functionalities required to respond to evolving operational needs. It will also support interoperability with local SPS systems of CEFTA Parties and relevant EU and international systems, including the further development of interfaces and automated data exchange to minimise duplicate data entry. Further development will seek to maintain close technical alignment with the EU IMSOC environment and TRACES NT, as well as relevant notification and information-exchange processes linked to RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS, where applicable. The overall objective is to establish a progressively integrated SPS digital environment enabling reliable electronic exchange of certificates, notifications and other SPS information within CEFTA and between CEFTA and the EU.
sig_1e54a836dbecee79c03c.title: CEFTA TRACES NT Maintenance, Expansion and SPS Digital Systems Support

sig_1e59be5fdc9cfaa79eb0.description: Aarhus Kommune has concluded an agreement regarding licences for a new law guide system. The system must support the municipality's employees in the application of laws and regulations within all administrative areas, primarily in relation to the exercise of public authority. In addition, the system must support the handling of personnel matters and include Local Government Denmark's (KL) commentaries on collective agreements and settlements. The system must comprise the following: 1. The system must contain access to updated laws and guidance within all administrative areas as well as the integration of KL's commentaries and interpretations of collective agreements and settlements. 2. The system must provide the opportunity for tailored content with the option to upload and maintain the municipality's own procedures, rules and workflows. Content must be capable of being categorised and adapted to specific legal areas for easy access. 3. The system must contain access to a large number of guides on the administration of legal areas, which support case handlers in their exercise of public authority/administration of the legal area. 4. The system must contain an advanced search function for quick and efficient access to laws, regulations and commentaries. The system must have an intuitive interface that is easy to use in daily work. 5. The system must be continuously updated so that it always contains the newest versions of laws, guidance, etc., and automatic updating of KL's commentaries must also take place upon changes in collective agreements and settlements. 6. The system must be able to handle differentiated access rights based on the employees' roles. Prior to the dispatch of this notice, the contracting authority has published notice 612430-2025.
