sig_2279c5b9fac845732665.description: A. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. B. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) intends to award a firm fixed-price, commercial item, single award, purchase order for a new LED sign at the Woodrow Wilson Keeble Memorial Health Care Center, Sisseton, South Dakota in response to RFQ 75H70626Q00230. This acquisition will be conducted under FAR Part 12. C. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, and the FAR Overhaul. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. D. This RFQ is set aside Total Small Business with the associated NAICS Code is 339950, which has a small business standard of 500 employees. E. The quoted unit pricing must be “all inclusive” (to include but not be limited to regular hours, holidays, overtime, weeknight, weekends, call back, travel, lodging, per diem, fringe benefits, federal, state and local taxes) plus all other costs pertinent to the performance of this contract. Utilize your most competitive and reasonable pricing. LED Sign Installation – See Performance Work Statement To provide a new sign, complete with removal of old and installation per the Performance Work Statement (PWS), at the Woodrow Wilson Keeble Memorial Health Care Center Indian Health Service - Sisseton Service Unit, 100 Lake Traverse Drive, Sisseton, SD 57262. F. The period of performance will be: 120 days from the date of award. G. FAR 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Items (Deviation NOV 2025). (a) Submission of offers. Submit signed and dated offers to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified in this solicitation. As a minimum, offers shall include— (1) The solicitation number; 75H70626Q00230, Closing Date: October 23, 2026, at 1:00 pm CST (2) The name, address, telephone number of the Offeror; (3) The Offeror’s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and, if applicable, Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator; (4) Information necessary to evaluate the factors contained in the provision at 52.212-2 or as described in the solicitation; (5) Responses to provisions that require Offeror completion of information, representations, and certifications (other than those collected via the System for Award Management (SAM)); and (6) A statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments. (b) Period for acceptance of offers. The Offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation. (c) Late submissions, modifications, revisions, and withdrawals of offers. (1) Offerors are responsible for submitting offers and any modifications or revisions to the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation. (2) Any offer, modification, or revision received after the time specified for receipt of offers is “late” and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made and the Contracting Officer determines that accepting the late offer would not unduly delay the acquisition. However, a late modification of an otherwise successful offer that makes its terms more favorable to the Government will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted. (3) If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that offers cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of offers by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation or other notice of an extension of the closing date, the time specified for receipt of offers will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume. (4) Offerors may withdraw their offers by written notice to the Government received at any time before award. (d) Contract award (not applicable to Invitation for Bids). The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract without discussions with Offerors. Therefore, the Offeror’s initial offer should contain the Offeror’s best terms. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions, if necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest, accept other than the lowest offer, and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. (e) Debriefings. If a postaward debriefing is given to requesting Offerors, the Government will disclose the following information, if applicable: (1) The agency’s evaluation of the significant weak or deficient factors in the debriefed Offeror’s offer. (2) The overall evaluated cost or price and technical rating of the successful Offeror and the debriefed Offeror and past performance information on the debriefed Offeror. (3) The overall ranking of all Offerors when any ranking was developed by the agency during source selection. (4) A summary of the rationale for award. (5) For acquisitions of commercial products, the make and model of the product to be delivered by the successful Offeror. (6) Reasonable responses to relevant questions posed by the debriefed Offeror as to whether the agency followed source-selection procedures set forth in the solicitation, applicable regulations, and other applicable authorities. In addition, Contractors shall provide the following: Name and phone number of three (3) professional references Shall meet the qualifications in the PWS and provide copies of requested documents. Copy of malpractice insurance coverage. Copy of a degree from a qualified medical science program. Maintain continuing education/certification. Copy of current Basic Life Support (BLS). Current immunization record. DO NOT INCLUDE PERSONAL IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION (PII) on any documents that are being submitted. Attachments: Performance Work Statement (PWS) Provisions and Clauses incorporated by reference and full text H. Basis of Award is Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). This award selection will be conducted using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) procedures. FAR 52.217-8 extension pricing will be evaluated for protest protection. To be eligible for award, a proposal must meet all technical requirements, conform to all required terms and conditions, and include all information required. All non-price evaluation factors must be rated as "ACCEPTABLE" in order to be eligible for award. An "UNACCEPTABLE" rating in any factor will result in the proposal being rated "UNACCEPTABLE" unless corrected through discussions. A proposal rating of "UNACCEPTABLE" makes a proposal ineligible for award. Since the LPTA methodology prohibits trade-offs, all evaluation factors and sub-factors are equally important. Proposals are evaluated for acceptability but not ranked using the non-price factors. A price evaluation will be performed for all offerors and proposals will be ranked from lowest to highest price based on the Total Proposed Price (TPP) provided by the offeror on the price schedule sheet. Next, an evaluation of each factor and, subsequently, the overall proposal will be performed beginning with the lowest priced proposal. Award will be made to the lowest evaluated priced proposal meeting the acceptability standards for the non-price factors. The Government intends to award a contract without conducting discussions; therefore, the initial proposal shall conform to the solicitation requirements and should contain the best offer from a technical and price perspective. Technical Factor 1 – Past Performance (a) Solicitation Submittal Requirements: Offerors do not need to provide any information under this factor as the US Government will base the evaluation on all INTERIM and FINAL Contractor Performance Assessment Reports (CPARs) that are recent and relevant. The CPARs will be retrieved from official US Government sources, including, but not limited to, the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System and the Past Performance Information Retrieval System. (b) Basis of Evaluation: Recency: For the purposes of this solicitation, a past performance record is recent if the CPAR final date of assessment listed in the “Period of Performance Being Assessed” block is within the 24-month period preceding the proposal due date. Relevancy: For the purposes of this solicitation, a past performance record is relevant if the CPAR business sector is listed as “Services”. To receive an "acceptable" rating for this factor, an Offer's recent and relevant CPARs must NOT include one or more INTERIM and/or FINAL CPARs with a rating of "UNSATISFACTORY" in one or more categories OR one or more INTERIM and/or FINAL CPARs with a rating of "MARGINAL" in two or more categories. If an Offeror has one or more CPARs with a rating of "UNSATISFACTORY" in one or more categories OR one or more CPARs with a rating of "MARGINAL" in two or more categories, the Offeror's past performance will be evaluated as "UNACCEPTABLE". In the case of an Offeror without a record of recent and relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available or so sparse that no meaningful past performance rating can be reasonably assigned, the Offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. Therefore, the Offeror shall be determined to have unknown past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, “unknown” shall be considered “acceptable.” An “UNACCEPTABLE” rating for a single factor will result in the Offeror’s entire proposal being rated “UNACCEPTABLE”. Technical Factor 2 – Problem and Approach (a) Solicitation Submittal Requirements: Proposals, which merely offer a statement to conduct/provide services in accordance with the requirements in the Governments PWS, will not be eligible for award. The offeror must submit an explanation that meet the requirements identified under Contractor Requirements. (b) Basis of Evaluation: This factor will be evaluated as “ACCEPTABLE” if explanation meets the requirements identified under Contractor Requirements. If an explanation of one or more Requirements is not provided, and/or do not comply with the requirements, this factor will receive an “UNACCEPTABLE” rating. Technical Factor 3 – Management (a) Solicitation Submittal Requirements: Proposals, which merely offer a statement to conduct/provide services in accordance with the requirements in the Governments PWS, will not be eligible for award. The offeror must submit an explanation that identifies the offeror’s management capabilities and responsibilities to meet the requirements. (b) Basis of Evaluation: This factor will be evaluated as “ACCEPTABLE” if the explanation meets the requirement for management capabilities and responsibilities to meet the following: Tour of Duty/Schedule, Description of Services, Contractor Responsibility and Personnel Requirements, which comply with the requirements outlined above, are submitted. If an explanation of one or more of the following: Design, Installation, Warranty, disposal of old unit and/or do not comply with the requirements, this factor will receive an “UNACCEPTABLE” rating. IHS reserves the right to make multiple awards, which is most advantages to the Government. This is a competitive solicitation and the offer your firm submits will be used by IHS to determine, which of the quantities listed within are, “estimate only” and it is not the intent of IHS to be obligated to order the “quantities.” Factor 4 – Price (a) Solicitation Submittal Requirements: Completed Price Schedule Sheet (b) Basis of Evaluation: The Government will evaluate price based on the total proposed price calculated as the sum of bid item that includes Contract cost, Subcontractor cost, Overhead and Profit. Analysis will be performed by one or more of the following techniques to ensure a fair and reasonable price: (i) Comparison of proposed prices received in response to the RFQ. (ii) Comparison of proposed prices with the IGCE. (iii) Comparison of proposed prices with available historical information. Note: A price that is found to be either unreasonable high or unrealistically low in relation to the proposed work may be indicative of an inherent lack of understanding of the solicitation requirements and may result in the overall proposal being considered unacceptable. INTENT TO AWARD WITHOUT DISCUSSIONS The Government intends to evaluate proposals and award a contract without discussions with Offerors. Therefore, the Offeror's initial proposal should contain the Offeror's best terms from a price and technical standpoint. The Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if the Contracting Officer later determines them to be necessary. In the event discussions are held, a competitive range determination will be made. If the Contracting Officer determines that the number of proposals that would otherwise be in the competitive range exceeds the number at which an efficient competition can be conducted, the Contracting Officer may limit the number of proposals in the competitive range to the greatest number that will permit an efficient competition among the most highly rated proposals. However, The Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if the Contracting Officer later determines them to be necessary. I. sig_22ac4f2d5f47bf5d5a01.description: For the past decade, London Transport Museum has conducted regular onsite customer satisfaction research to understand the experiences and motivations of visitors, retail shoppers and café customers. This long running programme has provided essential insights into satisfaction, visitor demographics, operational performance and brand awareness, enabling the Museum to track trends, benchmark performance and support annual planning. The Museum is now entering a new phase. Following a recent total market survey and segmentation refresh, and with a new CRM system enabling post visit email surveys from 2027/28, we are updating our approach to ensure continued robustness while reflecting changing organisational needs. Upcoming capital developments will also require more frequent insights into visitor experiences as spaces evolve, and this piece of ongoing research will be required help test themes and ideas with audiences during this period of change. We are therefore seeking a research partner who can, for the next three to five years, deliver reliable, unbiased audience insight while embracing innovations such as AI and best practice methodologies. The supplier will help us understand motivations, expectations, experiences and profiles across Museum, Retail and Catering audiences; keep our segmentation framework active and insightful; and provide timely reporting to support internal decision making, planning and stakeholder reporting. The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to source a research partner who can contribute to developing the most effective method for delivering the research. Lot 1: .
sig_22ac4f2d5f47bf5d5a01.title: London Transport Museum Annual Visitor and Market Research

sig_22aee91e4b7cf9cd81f1.description: The geographic information system (GIS) is the central spatial data management system at Swissgrid and represents an essential resource for asset management in the network sector. Using the GIS, Swissgrid's assets are visualised in 2D and 3D and made available to users via a user-friendly web interface (WebGIS). The current GIS solution is based on technology from the provider ESRI and is supplemented by the WebOffice and GEONIS components from the company VertiGIS. These components were introduced in 2019 as part of a GATT/WTO tender. Since then, VertiGIS products have been announced as end-of-life and will only receive support in the form of essential patches and security updates until February 2028. No further development has been offered since the beginning of 2024. This situation prevents the necessary upgrades of the ESRI components used at Swissgrid, which severely restricts, or even hinders, the implementation of important digitisation projects within the framework of the strategic programme 'Asset Management 4.0'. Due to the technological superiority of the ESRI platform as well as its integration possibilities with existing Swissgrid systems such as SAP, FNT-Command, Salesforce and PLS-CADD, the continuation of this solution is strategically sound. For this reason, a direct procurement of ESRI licences, as well as the associated maintenance services, has been implemented. The objective is to replace the currently used VertiGIS components with a new structure based on ESRI components, to optimise the data model, and to ensure future development and the provision of third-level support in collaboration with a service provider that will have to provide the services tendered from the 1st of August 2026 to the 31th of July 2031.

sig_22ef79c3fb93659935ec.description: In order to protect Statens IT (Ordering Party) against current and future cyber threats, the Ordering Party uses a number of security technologies, including an Extended Detection and Response (XDR) platform. The XDR platform supports the collection, correlation and analysis of security-related incidents across the Ordering Party's IT environment in order to protect systems, services and data, as well as to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data. In view of this, the Ordering Party is tendering a contract whose purpose is to support and strengthen the Ordering Party's own operational IT security through the provision of a Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service from a Security Operations Center (SOC). The MDR service must use and supplement the Ordering Party's XDR platform with round-the-clock monitoring, analysis, detection, validation, escalation and handling of security incidents. The service must be delivered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and contribute to the rapid identification, assessment and handling of cyber threats and security incidents. The services constitute an essential element in the Ordering Party's ongoing maturation and development process in the field of cybersecurity with a focus on technology, processes, competencies and collaboration across internal and external stakeholders. Through the procurement, the Ordering Party wishes to gain access to a professional MDR service that can meet the Ordering Party's high demands for quality, robustness and efficiency, as well as a supplier that can continuously engage in dialogue with the Ordering Party on developments within cybersecurity, including the threat picture, technological opportunities, automation, competence development and ongoing improvements to the security level. The supplier must carry out a technical, organisational and procedural Transition In, which ensures that the ongoing MDR services can be delivered from the transition to the operational phase. The Ordering Party draws attention to the fact that the Ordering Party has concluded a contract with two (2) suppliers to handle the Ordering Party's existing XDR platform, with whom the supplier must cooperate in connection with Transition In. As part of this, the supplier must establish and configure the necessary integrations between the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other relevant security sources, as well as the supplier's tools and platforms used for the fulfilment of the contract. The supplier must deliver Ongoing MDR Services; including continuous monitoring, analysis, correlation, validation and detection of alarms and security incidents. The supplier must carry out triage and qualification of alarms in order to identify actual security incidents and ensure timely escalation and notification in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. These ongoing MDR services include: • Continuous SOC monitoring of security-related incidents and alarms. • Analysis, correlation and qualification of incidents across relevant data sources. • Identification, detection and validation of security incidents. • Preparation, implementation and ongoing optimisation of detection rules, use cases and analysis models. • Application of relevant Threat Intelligence to support the detection and analysis work. • Ongoing assessment of the threat picture and its relevance to the Ordering Party's environment. • Proactive identification of potential security incidents and security risks, including through Threat Hunting activities. • Escalation, notification and reporting of security incidents in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. • Maintenance of existing integrations and establishment of new integrations as needed. • Optimisation and further development of the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other security solutions. • Advice regarding the development and maturation of the Ordering Party's security organisation, security processes and governance. • Execution of targeted Threat Hunting courses and analyses of suspicious activities. • Incident Response assistance in the event of security incidents upon requisition from the Ordering Party, including analysis, delimitation, handling, remediation and recovery. • Assistance during major security incidents, cyber crises and coordination with relevant stakeholders. • Security-related advice and strategic sparring on developments within cybersecurity. The contract also includes cross-cutting services, including documentation, reporting, governance, quality assurance and information security, which are delivered throughout the contract period. Furthermore, the contract includes obligations upon contract termination (Transition Out), which must ensure a controlled, secure and documented transfer of knowledge, data, processes, integrations and other contract-related deliverables to the Ordering Party or a subsequent supplier.
sig_22ef79c3fb93659935ec.title: Managed Detection and Response (MDR)

With this rostering application, employees are rostered and staffing is managed (traffic control). sig_23103fc3ebc0597973b3.description: The project includes the supply and installation of equipment for the creation of a national electronic citizen authentication system compliant with the highest security standards and compatible with the European Regulation (eIDAS 2.0) and the European Digital Identity Regulation, which will offer an advanced set of authentication services. Additionally, it includes the creation of a central Citizen Identity Hub and the infrastructure for providing qualified electronic signature certificates to Greek citizens. Overall, the offered system must be able to successfully serve the entire production-issuance cycle (collection of supporting documents and biometric data, management of applications and data, personalisation of security documents, quality control of personalised documents) of security documents. The Contracting Authority considers the reasonable delivery deadline for the Integrated Security Documents Information System, its related implementation services, as well as the digital identity and authentication services (hereinafter “Main Project”), to be the period of 18 months. Within the framework of the Main Project, the Contractor must implement and deliver the following: Implementation Study, Delivery of Project Equipment and ready-to-use Software, Implementation services for development - operational environment and development, Integration Services, Trial migration and Acceptance Testing period, Training, Trial Operation Period. After the final delivery and acceptance of the Main Project, the operation and maintenance period of ten (10) years begins, during which the contractor will provide the following services: - Operation and maintenance of the system - On site support - Telecommunications services - Supply of other consumable materials (envelopes, barcode labels, cardboard boxes). - Supply and Personalisation of security documents. Specifically: Period A (3 years): During the first three (3) years from the final acceptance of the Main Project, the contracting authority will procure 6.420.000 security documents of type ID1 and 1.050.000 security documents of type ID3. Period B (7 years): During the remaining seven (7) years of the contract duration, the contracting authority will procure up to 32.580.000 security documents of type ID1 and up to 7.150.000 of type ID3, according to its needs. At the same time, it will be able to personalise other security documents (format ID-1, ID-3) in case it is required in the future. At any time during the operation and maintenance period, following a decision by the Contracting Authority, an option may be exercised with the object of: a) extending the provision of the operation and maintenance period services for an additional period of up to 5 years in total, from its original expiry date, and/or b) extending the duration of the supply and personalisation services for security documents until the quantities of the contract are exhausted and, in any case, not beyond five (5) years from the original expiry date of the operation and maintenance period. The option may be exercised by a unilateral declaration of the contracting authority to the contractor once or more times for a minimum period of one (1) year and a maximum of five (5) years.

sig_231749969774b9fa8440.description: Cadent currently stores asset drawing records on a shared drive solution, which has proven to be inefficient and prone to human error. This introduces risks to the quality and completeness of asset documentation. The existing manual process for managing and updating asset records creates operational inefficiencies and lacks scalability. To address these challenges, Cadent seeks to implement a scalable, fully digitised, and automated Asset Record Management System that supports future growth. The current repository lacks essential capabilities such as metadata assignment and embedded workflow processes. Cadent requires a strategic system that enables metadata tagging of asset drawings and automation of workflows to improve operational efficiency. Additionally, KPI reporting from the current system is manual and likely inaccurate. The new system should provide automated and reliable KPI reporting, enabling Cadent to focus on both the management and quality assurance of asset documentation. Lot 1: .

sig_2351a49151cd1db5a74c.description: 1 db TSM IT system operation support service under a Framework Agreement, Framework amount: 5 940 000 000 HUF. The purpose of the procurement is to involve expert operation support to ensure the continuous high availability of the TSM system's 7X24 hour operation for a period of 36 months. The TSM system currently supports transport authority inspections nationwide at a total of 89 points, 106 measuring locations, 274 lanes, based on data from approximately 1500 WIM sensors (measuring instruments). Tasks: ML 2.1. Expert support with continuous availability: Following the submission of a support service request by the Contracting Authority, the Tenderer shall commence the execution of the task specified in the request within 2 days of the date of the relevant request. The tasks expected within the scope of expert support are detailed in the technical description. ML.2.2. Incident management, bug fixing: It is the Tenderer's obligation to ensure, with continuous availability, 7X24 hours a day, that the Contracting Authority can submit incidents and bug reports to the Tenderer's notification email address and direct telephone contact, and that the Tenderer receives them continuously, registers them, and takes the necessary measures as follows. - Software bug fixing (L2): The Tenderer is obliged to fix software bugs occurring in the TSM system that cause incidents. The Tenderer shall perform the fixing of software bugs causing incidents as an expert performing second-level (L2) troubleshooting. - Provision of expert support for L3 level software bug fixing: The Tenderer is obliged to provide expert support for L3 level bug fixing of software bugs causing incidents upon the Contracting Authority's request to this effect. - Advanced troubleshooting service (incident management): The Tenderer shall act as a fourth-level (L4 - manufacturer or developer support) troubleshooting expert to resolve errors, incidents, and problems occurring in the transport authority system components listed in the TSM System Plan - which are under the operation of the Contracting Authority - in order to ensure application operation support and the further development of the entire application environment. During troubleshooting, the provision of expert capacity and the resolution of the error are the Tenderer's task. ML.2.3. Preparation of developments: In the event of a development requirement regarding modifications necessary in the TSM system based on changes in legislation, the Tenderer shall assess the change requirements, design the application modification tasks resulting from the indicated changes, and prepare the development specification, plan, and development schedule regarding the handover and introduction of the modifications for the Contracting Authority. To prepare the development specification, the Winning Tenderer is expected to possess comprehensive knowledge of the relevant transport authority legislation to ensure the full functionality of the TSM system, with particular regard to knowledge of the processes performing the evaluation of data recorded by axle load scales that are part of the system, as well as other devices performing road traffic or vehicle parameterisation that may be integrated into the system. ML.2.4. Expert consulting: Expert consulting on the planning of administrative and IT changes affecting the TSM system, which extends to the interoperability of software performing the evaluation of data recorded by axle load scales connected to the TSM system or other devices performing road traffic or vehicle parameterisation to be connected to the TSM system. Technologies and applied services used by the supported system: Network elements: LAN, SAN Running infrastructure: Oracle DBMS, Oracle Exadata (running database environment), HP infrastructure (for running productive and test environments) Server operating systems: - Red Hat Linux - Oracle Linux server Database managers: - Oracle (RAC/Grid and standalone) 10, 11, 12c Virtualisation technologies: - ASX Network services: - DHCP, - DNS, - ARP, - VPN, - RDP, - SSH. Security class of the system (according to 41/2015. (VII. 15.) Ministry of Interior Decree): 3 Tasks in detail: in the Technical description. The Contracting Authority intends to order the tasks contained in points ML.2.1. and 2.2. within the framework of a monthly flat-rate service. The Contracting Authority undertakes to call off the TSM IT system operation support service according to points ML.2.1. and 2.2 for a total of 12 months. Order quantity: 495 hours Order completion deadline (KM III.10. point b): 90 working days Order start date (KM III.10. point b): the day following the confirmation of the order.

sig_235a502906ce9de990f9.description: This notice is a prior information notice regarding a forthcoming procurement of service design expert services by the City of Tampere. The purpose of the notice is to inform the market of the upcoming procurement and to invite operators to participate in market consultation. This notice does not constitute a call for tenders. The City of Tampere has had framework arrangements for service design expert services in place during 2014–2017, 2018–2022 and 2023–2026. The city plans to establish a new framework arrangement for the years 2027–2030 upon the expiry of the current contract period on 12/2026. The City of Tampere has a need for service design expert services across many different development targets. The contract will be widely used by almost all city units. In the years 2023-2025 the combined annual value of orders has been approximately 400 000 €. We invite operators interested in the procurement to participate in market consultation, the purpose of which is to discuss the procurement object, its definition and preliminary plans. The views of potential tenderers are very important to us in preparing the procurement, and we are happy to hear new ideas regarding both the content of the procurement and its implementation method. We welcome views on, among other things: • preliminary lot division • service description • minimum requirements • quality evaluation criteria Companies registered for the market consultation will be invited to an event held via Teams on Wednesday 11.3.2026 at 13:30-14:50, where plans related to the procurement will be presented. Questions and comments concerning the procurement may also be raised at the event. Operators interested in the procurement are requested to register by Mon 9.3 at 16:00. Registration takes place via the City of Tampere Supplier Service at https://toimittaja-asiointi.tampere.fi/. Participation in the event requires registration in the service in question. There are a few questions during registration which we ask you to answer.

sig_2366bcd26f0a92db294b.description: HUS (hereinafter also referred to as the Contracting Authority or Client) requests to participate in the procurement of imaging solution and related services. The procurement will be carried out through a competitive dialogue procedure (see Annex 1 Description of the Procedure). The object of the procurement is imaging solution and related services. This procurement concerns the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), which is intended to be replaced with a new solution. The solution entity may also include functionalities of a Radiology Information System (RIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) platform designed to support the achievement of the objectives, and functionalities related to appointment booking/scheduling, as well as a speech recognition solution. The objective is to ensure that the service path between appointment booking system, the radiological information system (RIS), and the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) operates optimally. The aim is to develop customer experience based on a unified service model. The objective is to provide patients with more efficient diagnostics and good care also in the future. In addition, the objective is to reduce the manual and overlapping work. The imaging solution must enable smooth workflows for all user groups and support the development of processes to improve productivity. The deployment project may include the migration of images, image metadata, and RIS data from the Client’s current PACS system. The service includes support and maintenance activities and may also include 1 level support provided by the Supplier. The objective is also to explore solutions for scalability regarding a joint archiving solution for digital pathology and imaging. A more detailed description of the current state, the solution to be procured, and the services included in the procurement can be found in Annex 2 Current and target state description of imaging systems. Please also take into account the other annexes to the request to participate (Annexes 2.1–2.6, and 4), which provide additional information on the current and target state. These annexes are not binding on the Contracting Authority in the later stages of the procurement procedure and may be subject to change during the negotiations. If the documents have been drawn up in both Finnish and English, in the event of conflict of interpretation, the Finnish text shall prevail. The request for participation, along with all related documentation and any clarifying questions, must be submitted in Finnish or English in accordance with the instructions provided in the request to participate. sig_23c452036bac960a51c9.description: The University of Edinburgh is undertaking preliminary market engagement to improve our understanding of current and emerging supplier capabilities, products and solutions for a Student Record Platform. The University is interested in student record systems that can integrate with its existing landscape, with the potential to rationalise and simplify the complexity of its current environment. This includes supporting areas such as exceptional circumstances, scholarships and assessment and progression,with the aim of delivering a more streamlined and effective solution. The University currently has contractual arrangements in place for its existing student record system. This engagement forms part of longer-term planning and is intended to improve understanding of how the market is evolving, inform the University's business requirements and support the development of its strategic planning and any future procurement strategy. Lot 1: . Please see the attached documentation for further information and details of the documents to be returned by interested suppliers. Responses will be reviewed by the University to inform its understanding of the current market, available technologies and delivery approaches. The information provided will support longer-term planning, strategic planning and, where appropriate, any future procurement strategy. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued solely for the purpose of preliminary market engagement. It is not a call for competition and should not be interpreted as a commitment to undertake a procurement exercise or award any contract. Should a procurement be taken forward, it is anticipated that this could take place at any point within the next three to five years. The University welcome participation from all interested suppliers. Participation is voluntary, at each suppliers’ own cost and will not affect any future procurement process.. Interested suppliers should send the requested information to Suzanne Toole, Procurement Manager, suzie.toole@ed.ac.uk by 12 Noon (BST) on 04 September 2026. Suppliers should mark their email with ‘PIN Response “SUPPLIER NAME”– Student Record Platform’.

sig_23c50f29f189e02de94a.description: The purpose of the procurement is to ensure access to external expertise in the form of IT consultancy services. Kriminalvården conducts extensive IT operations regarding development, operation and support. At the same time, Kriminalvården is in a digital transformation journey that places high demands on quality improvements, efficiencies and new ways of working, while a high level of security permeates everything the authority undertakes. Increased digitalisation, improved digital maturity and the use of new technology are prerequisites for sustainable efficiency and relief for the organisation so that the core business staff can focus on client-facing work. Kriminalvården shall also work for a digitalisation that increases the conditions for optimising existing expertise, improving the work environment and contributing to increased attractiveness and relevance as an employer. A contributing part in taking advantage of opportunities and successfully meeting challenges during this transformation journey is to strengthen the organisation through external expertise in the form of IT consultancy services. The need for external expertise ranges from deep specialist expertise in strategic areas to more general expertise such as IT technicians and developers (see Appendix "Competence areas and example roles"). To ensure that winning suppliers have sufficient breadth in their IT consultancy services, the need has, for evaluation purposes, been grouped into the following competence areas: Application, Infrastructure and IT Management & Architecture. Winning suppliers are expected to be able to deliver the requested expertise within all competence areas.

sig_23c79bd926e4edd238a3.description: Business Analysis: Business Analysis at Thames Water drives successful change by analysing business situations, assessing feasibility, and defining clear requirements across people, processes, and technology. Support more experienced BAs in workshops and stakeholder meetings. Business Analyst (Gartner level 2) - Works on clearly defined tasks within projects, handles moderately complex analysis, usually within a single business area, works under direction of Senior or Lead Business Analyst; receives guidance on priorities and methods. Limited to project-level stakeholders. Senior Business Analyst (Gartner level 3) - Leads BA activities across multiple projects or programmes (including strategic analysis); often covers multiple business domains, deals with high ambiguity and complex business situations, sets BA approach and advises others. Facilitates decision-making at senior stakeholder level. Coaches and mentors other BAs. Activities as per the BA above, whilst demonstrating a higher level of responsibility, complexity, autonomy, and influence. Lead Business Analyst (Gartner level 4) - Focused on Strategic alignment and team leadership. Leads BA Activities across Enterprise-level initiatives, multiple projects, and strategic programs. Align requirements with strategic and technical roadmaps. Define BA standards, governance, and best practices. Manage and coach BA team members. Act as key liaison between business and technology leadership. A project manager is a professional responsible for planning, organizing, and overseeing the execution of a project from start to finish following the Thames Water delivery framework/methodology. They ensure the project meets its goals within the agreed scope, schedule, budget, quality standards, and resources. Key Roles: Project Support Office role (Gartner Level 1): A Project Support Office provides the administrative, logistical, and coordination backbone that keeps programmes/ projects running smoothly. It supports project managers, teams, and sometimes entire programmes by ensuring consistency, documentation control, reporting, and governance. They act as the primary point of accountability for senior stakeholders. Programme Manager (Gartner Level 5): oversees and coordinates multiple related projects to ensure they collectively deliver strategic organisational outcomes. They provide leadership, governance, and direction across a programme of work, ensuring alignment with business goals and successful delivery of benefits. Act as the primary point of accountability into senior stakeholders / Executives. The function includes taking a structured approach to managing change; ensuring awareness, willingness, capability and training to adopt change; understanding and tracking change impact; managing risks related to change implementation (including resistance and adoption barriers); delivering change interventions to office-based and field-based operational colleagues. sig_23e920630a744f4942a8.description:
SKI hereby establishes a dynamic purchasing system for standard software and related services (02.06 Standard Software). The system comprises two purchasing categories: Category 1 – Simple Solution and Category 2 – Complex Solution. The system may be used to procure the following service areas: 1) Standard Software 2) Support and maintenance agreements 3) Installation/implementation and/or configuration 4) Training 5) Consultancy Standard software is defined as software that is prefabricated and commercially available. Standard software is also referred to as COTS (Commercial Off The Shelf). A more detailed definition of the nature of the software is set out in Appendix C, which also includes a more detailed description of the 5 service areas. All 5 service areas may be procured in both categories. The difference between the two categories lies in a differentiation in the customer's need for tenders for the solution. Category 1 is used when the customer has a precisely specified purchasing need / standard purchase, where the customer has defined the solution prior to the purchase and solely wishes to receive tenders for this solution from suppliers. The customer evaluates solely on price, cf. point 14.1 of the tendering conditions. Category 2 is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions. In Category 2, evaluation is based on both price and the suppliers' offered solutions (quality), cf. point 14.2 of the tendering conditions. In both categories of the system, standard software and related services, as delimited by the 5 service areas above, may be procured within the following functional areas: 1. Applications - 1 Customer Experience and Relationship Management (CRM) - 2 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) - 3 Supply Chain Management (SCM) - 4 Project and Portfolio Management - 5 E-mail and Authoring - 6 Content Services - 7 Other Application Software 2. Application Platforms - 1 Application Infrastructure and Middleware - 2 Data Management - 3 Analytics and Business Intelligence 3. Infrastructure Software - 1 Operating Systems - 2 Storage Management - 3 Virtualization Infrastructure - 4 Other Infrastructure Software 4. Development and Operations Tools - 1 Application Development - 2 IT Operations 5. IT Security Software - 1 Security Appendix D, Overview of functional standard software areas, describes in more detail which functional areas of software and services linked to these functional standard software areas are included in the service areas 1-5. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as shown in the published customer list, to make use of the System when they are to procure standard software or related services. The customer list in Appendix B.1 specifies the customers and their organisations that are customers of SKI at the time of tender and can thus use the system. However, the dynamic purchasing system may, throughout the term of the system, be used by all contracting authorities that are customers of SKI at the time of publication of a specific purchase in the system. All parts of the Danish state, regions and municipalities – including public companies and publicly owned companies subject to the obligation to tender as a result of their public ownership – can become customers of SKI by taking out a subscription covering their organisation. When new contracting authorities become customers of SKI, SKI will update the customer list on SKI.dk and announce on SKI.dk that a change has been made to SKI's customer list, as well as which contracting authorities are new customers of SKI and from what date these can publish purchases in the system. The customer list in Appendix B.1 is not updated after the time of tender. Instead, SKI's customer list valid at any given time will be publicly available on SKI.dk. Special attention is drawn to the fact that KL and the Ministry of Finance in the "Agreement on municipal finances for 2026" have agreed that 4-5 inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be established, which are to handle various tasks and establish solutions in the IT field for the participating municipalities. It appears from the agreement: "There is [...] agreement that the municipalities will, no later than d. 1. January 2027, establish themselves in new inter-municipal partnerships in the form of 4-5 municipal IT service organisations with a geographical starting point in the four regions. The new IT service organisations will be established as municipal units and will before the end of 2027 take over the municipalities' operation of server and network infrastructure. The parties have a shared ambition that the units will subsequently also gradually take over the operation of user management and monitoring, PCs and other end-user equipment as well as service desk and support leading up to 2030 and will continuously discuss the progress of the work." These inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be considered customers of SKI from the time they are established as an independent legal entity and will thereafter be able to use the system for specific purchases published in the system after their establishment. At the time of tender, the inter-municipal IT service organisations appear in Appendix B.1 Customer List with the designations [It-Service Nord], [It-Service Midt], [It-Service Syd], [It-Service Øst] and [It-Service Hovedstaden]. These designations will be updated according to the process stated in the foregoing when the units have been established. Whether 4 or 5 IT service organisations are established does not affect the fact that the total group of participants across the IT service organisations, i.e. the municipalities, is the same. Like all the other customers in the system, the inter-municipal IT service organisations have a right – but not an obligation – to use the system. Category 2 – Complex Solution Is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions.

sig_23ea0ee3a98d4e162b34.description: The purpose of these specifications is to establish the technical conditions that will govern the contracting of the advisory and technical assistance service for the evolution towards digital comprehensive archival management in the Archives and Documentary Heritage Service. * For the purposes of this contract, „digital comprehensive archival management“ means the set of processes and techniques applied in a regulated, orderly and efficient manner to the entire archival ecosystem, through the functional and technological transformation and adaptation required in accordance with the principles established in Foral Law 9/2026, of 20 May, on Archives, Document Management and Documentary Heritage. Said ecosystem reaches both the set of information assets and the technological tools where they reside and the document and archival management processes that govern them, with the aim of optimal service provision directed at citizens from the archive centres. Likewise, the identification, treatment, management, preservation and conservation of documentary collections in their original support form part of the archival ecosystem, singularly those of a film, musical and performing arts nature that must be subjected to digitisation due to their risk of obsolescence.

sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.description: The Urban Environment Division of the City of Helsinki (hereinafter "Contracting Authority") is requesting requests to participate in a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) to be established for the procurement of digital twin platforms. The Contracting Authority uses digital twin services to make official operations and citizens' participation more efficient. Digital twin platforms are used in use-case-specific pilot projects of agile development in the Urban Environment as well as in production solutions. The platforms are intended to be able to combine and visualise data from various sources, such as e.g. city information model data, building and infrastructure information models, point cloud data and basic data of the built environment. The objective is to utilise the industry's best platforms and resources in creating services. Digital twin services are being developed for internal use in the urban environment for stakeholders, for official use, and for citizens. Some of the services will probably contain confidential official information and will only be accessible by authorities, which must be taken into account in their implementation. This contract notice establishes a dynamic purchasing system. The dynamic purchasing system is in two stages. In the first stage, service providers apply to join the purchasing system by submitting a request to participate. All candidates fulfilling the suitability requirements will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. In the second stage, the contracting authority makes procurements as procurements internal to the established dynamic purchasing system and selects, on the basis of the internal competition, the platform solution best suited to each use case. Admission to the dynamic purchasing system is not binding on the candidate. The candidate may choose which competitions organised within the system it participates in. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. The dynamic purchasing system is valid for eight (8) years. The content of the dynamic purchasing system and the implementation of procurements are described in more detail in the appendix documents. The estimated value of the dynamic purchasing system is a total of approximately 2,3 million euros.
sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.title: Dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for digital twin platforms

sig_247d9789cb28140b655d.description: The objective of this project is to design, develop, and implement a comprehensive Digital Twin solution for the National Research Council of Canada’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering (NRC OCRE) facilities, specifically the M32 Building and the Large Wave Current Flume (LWCF). The Digital Twin will create a high fidelity, data driven virtual representation of NRC OCRE’s physical assets to improve operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, lower energy and fuel consumption, and enhance forecasting capabilities for research and facility operations. The solution will deliver a high-fidelity digital representation of the targeted physical assets, integrating real-time and historical data from environmental sensors, physical modelling instrumentation, electrical load monitors, operational equipment status, weather feeds, and simulation outputs derived from both physics-based models (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics [CFD]) and AI/ML predictive models. The digital twin will support advanced analytics, physics-based modelling, and machine learning to enable predictive maintenance, scenario testing, and operational optimization. The contractor will work collaboratively with NRC-OCRE subject matter experts to define scope, use cases, and system specifications, ensuring alignment with scientific, operational, and engineering priorities. The Contractor is expected to provide the data architecture component of this project required for data storage and management infrastructure. This capability must be secure, scalable, and compliant with Government of Canada cybersecurity, data governance. The data architecture must support the acquisition, processing, harmonization, and long-term management of diverse data types — including sensor data, simulation outputs, environmental data, and multimedia content — while maintaining interoperability with NRC’s existing digital systems and infrastructure. This component must support the acquisition, processing, harmonization, and long-term management of diverse data types—sensor data, simulation outputs, environmental data, and intuitive visualization interfaces (dashboards, 2D/3D, AR/VR), while maintaining interoperability with NRC’s existing digital systems. The end result will be a sustainable, expandable digital twin platform that aligns with NRC’s long-term research, operational, and digitalization goals.
sig_247d9789cb28140b655d.title: Development and Implementation of a Digital Twin Solution

sig_24b3195e9eda23da087d.description: This public procurement covers the following activities: Analysis of system requirements for the upgraded simulation thermo-hydraulic modelling system. Supply of a new licence, or upgrade of the current one, for the existing computer simulation environment, guaranteed to meet the set requirements regarding the volume and exhaustiveness of the characteristics of the simulated object (simulation model) and the requirements for functional expansion. Provision of an operational environment for the automated platform for thermo-hydraulic modelling, monitoring and management, in particular of the heat transmission network, and generally of the heat supply system of the city of Sofia. Installation of the licence. Migration of the existing simulation model of the heat supply system into the new/upgraded computer simulation environment. Updating, unification and completion of the existing simulation model; Development of models for calculating consumers' heat loads Calibration of the simulation model in steady-state operating mode; Integration of existing SCADA systems with the new/upgraded computer simulation environment for data exchange (values of operating parameters from actual measurements). Connection to a platform for current and forecast weather data. Dynamic calibration of the simulation model. Supply and installation of a licence for conducting parametric optimisation – temperature optimisation. Execution of activities for temperature optimisation of the operating mode of the heat supply system. Supply and installation of computer equipment to secure workstations for working with the automated platform for thermo-hydraulic modelling, monitoring and management. Development of user screens for direct and graphical visualisation of the results of real-time simulation calculations. Commissioning (testing and validation of the developed models) and conducting staff training. Maintenance services for the implemented automated thermo-hydraulic modelling platform and additional consultancy services.
sig_24b3195e9eda23da087d.title: "DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF AN AUTOMATED PLATFORM FOR THERMO-HYDRAULIC MODELLING, MONITORING AND MANAGEMENT OF THE HEAT NETWORK OF ""TOPLOFIKATSIA SOFIA"" EAD"

sig_25122663a3280822109d.description: The West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) is made up of 18 local councils, working together to make the West Midlands the best place to live, work and visit. Our priorities include homes, jobs, transport and growth for everyone. As an organisation, we're focused on making life better for people in the West Midlands. To achieve this, we need to work with communities to understand their lives, explore their aspirations for the future, and collaborate on potential solutions. When individuals have power over their personal circumstances, they can shape the places they live and spend time in. Those who actively participate in shaping their communities will feel a greater sense of belonging. An online engagement platform is a crucial mechanism for enabling us to build stronger, more inclusive, and more effective governance that truly meets the needs of our community. The right platform will allow us to increase research and accessibility, enhance transparency and trust, support resident-led decision-making, and foster community collaboration. We are seeking to gain a greater understanding of suppliers within the market, who would be interested in responding to the upcoming release of the specification of requirements. We plan to use the information gathered in this exercise to inform and help develop our procurement strategy before approaching the market for a full procurement exercise in early 2026. Lot 1: .

The development of this tool must enable us to manage the operation and appearance of all our digital products (apps and sites) from a single central location. This includes, among other things, the visual configuration of swimlanes, banners, navigation, and the layout of main and landing pages. sig_25691773fadd0d99dd05.description: Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures. Six principles shape the design of the future service: 1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice. 2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification. 3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team. 4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint. 5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised. 6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment. The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation: - Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. - Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management. - End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal. - Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB. - Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites. - Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. - Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. - Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required. - DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports. - Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design. - Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service. Full details are provided in the service specification. The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled. The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements. The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_25763d59c2e214aa710d.description: Derry City and Strabane District Council plans to commence a robust, credible and transparent preliminary market engagement process to procure specialist technical services to assess the feasibility and support the design of a £2m Positive Energy District (PED) Pilot project in Strabane Town Centre. PEDs, according to JPI Urban Europe, are “energy-efficient and energy-flexible urban areas or groups of connected buildings which produce net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and actively manage an annual local or regional surplus production of renewable energy. They require integration of different systems and infrastructures and interaction between buildings, the users and the regional energy, mobility and ICT systems while securing the energy supply and a good life for all in line with social, economic, and environmental sustainability.” (Ref: JPI Urban Europe / SET Plan Action 3.2, “White Paper on Reference Framework for Positive Energy Districts and Neighbourhoods,” Austria, 2020). The purpose of this preliminary market engagement (PME) is to gather insights and feedback from the market to inform the development of the procurement strategy and specification for the PED technical consultancy requirement as well as assisting Derry City and Strabane District Council to ensure that the most efficient and effective methods of procurement are considered. The first phase of the market engagement exercise will be participation from the supply base through the attached questionnaire. Responses to these questions will help Derry City and Strabane District Council gather comprehensive information about potential suppliers and the services they offer. This will allow us to make informed decisions regarding our specification and procurement strategy before entering the market with a full procurement competition. At this stage, any information gathered through this engagement exercise will solely inform internal business planning and any possible subsequent procurement process; and will NOT be appraised in any future tender evaluation exercise. Your submission must be submitted via etendersNI, via this CFT. No other method of submissions will be accepted. Please refer to the CfT documents for further detail. Lot 1: .

sig_2579468b30cb199d5ff8.description: All entities that carry out work at construction sites, all approved cleaning companies, certified entities in vehicle care, wheel shifts and wheel storage, as well as entities that transport the goods of others by car (from 1 January 2026) and other entities that possibly be subject to the rules in the future, both Norwegian and foreign, are obliged to equip their employees with HSE cards. The users of the system are these entities as well as other public and private actors with a factual and appropriate need for access to the system (User/Users). The Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs has given the Contracting Authority responsibility for the HSE card. The Contracting Authority is in the starting point responsible for the operation and maintenance of all work connected to the HSE card, including establishment, operation, maintenance, further development of the necessary systems for the HSE card, as well as design, production, personalisation and distribution of the HSE card (the HSE card scheme) and that The HSE card scheme functions as intentional. In connection with entering into this agreement, the contracting authority will transfer the responsibility for the HSE card scheme resulting from this contract to the Tenderer as a service concession. This means that the tenderer ́s remuneration fully consists of the right to offer HSE cards and associated services as defined in the contract for payment from the Users. It also means that the operational risk connected to the service has been transferred to the Tenderer, including the risks connected to the demand for the service and (to the degree relevant) the delivery risk. Beyond that stated in the Agreement, The Tenderer cannot, therefore, demand compensation or change the prices in the Contract for changes in earnings basis or as a result of other conditions that affect the tenderer's turnover or Return. As all work and all obligations connected to the HSE card are transferred to the tenderer, there will also be a responsibility on the Tenderer to develop the HSE card in accordance with changes to the relevant regulations and adapt the delivery to future orientated systems to improve the HSE card system. The contract means that the Users shall order HSE cards from the tenderer. The tenderer, for their part, shall, as a result of the contract, relate to both the Contracting Authority and the Users. One of the purposes of the contract is therefore to facilitate a good cooperation between the Contracting Authority and the Tenderer, and between the Tenderer and the Users. Furthermore, the aim of the Contract is to ensure that the HSE card scheme is user friendly, stable and adapted in accordance with future innovative systems and that the adaptations will not, without further ado, be at the cost of the Users. The contract is for the establishment, development and maintenance of a system for the HSE card scheme, as well as delivery of services connected to the production and distribution of HSE cards, including operation, personalisation, development, design as well as management of register-postings (delivery). The scope, execution and further specification and prerequisites for the delivery are further described in the annexes that are included in the contract.

sig_257ee8e651f6a8140943.description: The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) ("the Authority") is responsible for welfare, pensions, and child maintenance policy within the UK. As the UK’s biggest public service department, it administers the State Pension and a range of working age and disability benefits to around 20 million UK citizens. The Authority is committed to doing everything it can to enhance the overall citizen experience. Citizens contact the Authority wishing to start, validate, change or query their benefit claims. Citizens calling from within the UK contact the Authority via free of charge Non-Geographic Numbers (“NGNs”) or via web chat when wishing to discuss their individual circumstances with regards to a type of service/benefit they have with the Authority. NGNs are currently answered by advisors within the Authority’s contact centre, which is the largest platform of its kind across all UK government departments and is one of the largest in Europe. The contact centre managed service ensures that all twenty-seven business groups, spread across around 200 locations, can connect with and support citizens, whilst also offering specialist services such as debt recovery and support for citizens with complex needs. Conversational AI Platform (“CaiP”) is a natural language call steering (“NLCS”) solution which allows citizens to speak naturally to the platform so it can determine why our citizens are calling. This enables the guiding of the citizen to the most effective outcome, whether that is to the right agent first time or to personalised call deflection and/or self-service offerings. This should enhance the citizen experience and produce operational efficiencies. The CaiP service will integrate with the Authority’s contact centre to help better serve millions of citizens by improving how DWP handles inbound calls, route queries intelligently, and offer self-service options. Lot 1: .

sig_257fc4947670c7dd5a1e.description: *** The purpose of this Amendment is to post Q&A see attachment Amendment #0002 to RPP W91CRB-26-AWSP *** The purpose of this update is to publish the confirmed deadline for proposal submissions is 08 October 2026 at 16:00 Eastern Time (ET). ***The purpose of this update is to publish the Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) for the Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS) Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP). Please review the attached document titled "AWS_RPP_Official_QandA" for the Government's responses to all received industry questions. As confirmed in the Q&A, the deadline for proposal submissions remains 08 October 2026 at 16:00 Eastern Time (ET). All other terms, requirements, and submission instructions in the solicitation remain unchanged. 1.0 Overview The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground, Project Manager Maneuver Medical Systems (PM M2S), is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit prototype project proposals for a modernized Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS). This RPP is issued pursuant to the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. § 4022. This is a DIRECT OTA and is NOT a solicitation for a procurement contract under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Consortium membership is not required to respond to this RPP. 2.0 Mission Need & Scope The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) anesthesia workstation system capable of supporting life-saving medical operations in austere environments at Role of Care (ROC) 3 with little to no modification. The system must overcome the capability gaps of legacy systems, specifically regarding interoperability with Army Oxygen Generation Systems, heavy logistical footprint (weight), and proprietary maintenance constraints. The Government intends to award one (1) OT Agreement for the delivery of two (2) prototype units. These units will undergo rigorous operational testing by the Medical Test and Evaluation Activity (MTEAC) and environmental testing conducted in accordance with MIL-STD-810H. Proposed solutions must be FDA-cleared for human use and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant. A high priority for this effort is organic supportability. The Government strongly prefers systems designed to be maintainable by military Biomedical Equipment Technicians (BMETs) at the Field and Depot levels without reliance on proprietary vendor service contracts. 3.0 Follow-On Production Authority In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), this OT Agreement is issued with a provision for follow-on production. Upon successful prototype completion and validation, the Government may award a follow-on production contract or OT Agreement for approximately one hundred and eighty (180) AWS units without further competitive procedures. 4.0 Proposal Submission Instructions All proposal instructions, technical specifications (CODS and APAs), and evaluation criteria are detailed in the attached Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) document. Questions: All questions must be submitted in writing via email to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialist no later than 15:00 ET on 17 September 2026. Proposals: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email no later than 16:00 ET on 08 October 2026. Communications: Unauthorized contact with program office personnel or technical end-users regarding this RPP may result in disqualification. All communications must be directed to the points of contact listed below. Attachments The Final RPP Document (which includes Appendix E) The Standalone ADRL Document Attachment A (The blank TAA Certificate) Attachment C / OTA Articles Points of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Timothy Compton Agreements Officer Email: timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil Secondary Point of Contact: Roxanne A. Dalrymple Agreements Specialist Email: roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil

sig_258de6adf437438b71b7.description: Europe-wide call for tenders for the "Introduction of a suitable software solution to support the three requirement clusters of project portfolio control, project management and resource management in the company" Lot LOT-0000: Introduction of a company-wide PPM and resource management tool. The purchasing community HAMBURG WASSER, consisting of the companies Hamburger Stadtentwässerung AöR (HSE) and Hamburger Wasserwerke GmbH (HWW), is tendering the aforementioned service under the lead management of HSE. Basic contract duration = 48 months. Maximum contract duration = 96 months. After 48 months have elapsed, the contracting authorities are entitled at any time to terminate the contract with a notice period of 6 months at the end of a calendar month. Initial situation: Currently, HAMBURG WASSER (coordinated group of the core companies HWW and HSE) does not have a central tool for project, resource management and project portfolio control. Excel and similar tools are used as aids for this in the individual areas. With the introduction of central project portfolio control at HAMBURG WASSER, the use of software is indispensable and mandatory for the success of functioning processes. The tool to be introduced must be easy to use and give users a good overview of their tasks and the current status of the respective portfolios, projects, budget utilisation and resource utilisation. The solution is intended to create transparency regarding ongoing and planned projects, enable prioritised control of the project portfolio and ensure efficient planning and utilisation of resources. Target vision: The goal is the operational setup of the software in accordance with the agreed functional requirements while making the greatest possible use of standard functions of the software to ensure maintainability, update capability and future-proofing. Expected scope of services: Setup, configuration and initial operation of the software. After provision of the software, initial setup and configuration is required to meet the professional and organisational requirements of the contracting authorities. The contracting authorities shall provide project management for this purpose, which technically represents, prioritises and approves the requirements. The contractor assumes responsibility for the technical and professional configuration of the software in close coordination with the project management of the contracting authorities.
