sig_26865d895472ce0874e9.description: Veikkaus Oy is requesting tenders for a four-year (2+1+1) framework arrangement to procure Oracle development partners. The maximum total value of the agreement is 12 000 000 € VAT 0 %. The object of the procurement with its different sections is specified in more detail in the invitation to tender, Annex 2. Service requirements, here and other attachments. During the term of agreement, the procuring entity will be ordering services specific to sections according to its needs. The procuring entity is not committed to making specific purchases for fixed amounts. The agreement does not grant the service provider an exclusive right to provide the service to the procuring entity. This section covers the procurement of Oracle Fusion Applications–related ser-vices, focusing on design, configuration, development, integration, and opera-tions on the Oracle Cloud platform. The scope includes core ERP processes such as finance, procurement, supply chain and projects, extension and customiza-tion using platform tools, release and test management for quarterly updates, and continuous improvement of the Fusion-based solution landscape. Work typically involves designing and configuring Oracle Fusion modules, im-plementing end-to-end ERP processes, integrating Fusion with surrounding sys-tems, and managing quarterly release impacts. The category focuses on solu-tion design, configuration, extensions and integrations, test and release man-agement, and the full lifecycle of Fusion-based ERP services from implementa-tion to continuous improvement. General requirements for the category · Proven experience in Oracle Fusion Cloud implementations, enhance-ments, and support ERP Financials, Procurement, Supply Chain and Pro-ject management module. · Ability to work in multi-vendor and hybrid environments (on-prem, OCI, integrations with non-Oracle systems). · Capability to support full lifecycle: requirements, solution design, con-figuration, integrations, testing, migration, cutover, hyper care, and con-tinuous improvement. · Familiarity with Oracle implementation best practices, security model, and quarterly update processes. · Experience in integrating Fusion with external systems via APIs, OIC or other integration platforms. · Custom extension design in APEX and / or VBCS. · Analytics and Reporting desing, build in Oracle Fusion Cloud environ-ment. · Ability to produce clear documentation (designs, configurations, test plans, user guides) in English. Finnish language is considered an ad-vantage. · Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section is dedicated to the procurement of services related to Oracle CX Applications, supporting customer-facing processes such as customer service, sales, and marketing. The scope includes configuration and development of CX solutions, integrations with backend and data platforms, customer data and consent management, and continuous optimization of customer experience across channels. Work typically involves designing and implementing CX solutions to support customer service, sales, and marketing processes, integrating CX with back-end and data platforms, and optimizing the use of customer data. The category fo-cuses on process and solution design, configuration and development of CX ap-plications, integrations and data flows, and the full lifecycle management of Or-acle CX–based services. General requirements for the category · Demonstrated experience implementing and supporting Oracle CX Cloud applications relevant to Veikkaus CX Service Cloud, Engagement, Marketing. · Understanding customer lifecycle, customer data, and omnichannel ser-vice concepts. · Ability to integrate CX with back-end systems, Fusion, data warehouses, and external tools. · Custom extension design in APEX and / or VBCS. · Analytics and Reporting design, built in Oracle Fusion Cloud environ-ment. · Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section covers the procurement of Oracle HCM Cloud–related services, supporting HR processes throughout the employee lifecycle. The scope includes design and configuration of HCM modules, integrations with payroll, identity and access management, and analytics solutions, as well as support for regula-tory compliance, security, and continuous enhancement of HR services. Work typically involves designing and configuring HCM modules to support HR processes, integrating HCM with payroll, identity management and analytics, and ensuring compliance with HR and data privacy regulations. The category fo-cuses on HR process digitalization, HCM solution design and configuration, inte-grations and reporting, and the full lifecycle of Oracle HCM–based services from rollout to continuous enhancement. General requirements for the category · Proven experience in Oracle HCM Cloud implementation and support Core HR, Recruiting, Talent Management, Time & Labor. · Understanding of HR processes, local (Finnish/EU) legal and regulatory requirements, and data privacy. · Custom extension design in APEX and / or VBCS. · Analytics and Reporting design, built in Oracle Fusion Cloud environ-ment. · Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section is dedicated to the procurement of Oracle EPM Cloud–related ser-vices for financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and consolidation. The scope includes model design and configuration, integrations with ERP and data plat-forms, reporting and analytics development, and ongoing optimization of EPM solutions to support Finance and business steering. Work typically involves designing and implementing planning and consolidation models, integrating EPM with ERP and data warehouses, and developing report-ing and analytics for Finance and business control. The category focuses on fi-nancial process and model design, configuration and optimization of EPM appli-cations, data integrations and reporting, and the full lifecycle of Oracle EPM–based services supporting planning, forecasting, and closing. General requirements for the category · Proven experience with Oracle EPM Cloud (e.g. Planning, Financial Con-solidation & Close, Account Reconciliation, PCM, etc.). · Understanding financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and consolida-tion processes. · Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section covers the procurement of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), secu-rity in Saas and PaaS-related Cloud services, which encompass design, imple-mentation, and operations of the underlying Veikkaus Oracle Cloud Tenancies. This includes services such as OCI infrastructure design and management, iden-tity and access management, OCI networks, Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC), cus-tom extensions (APEX, VBCS), Oracle Databases, monitoring and logging (SOC), automation/DevOps tooling, and other security and platform capabilities re-quired to run and integrate Veikkaus’ Oracle solutions securely and efficiently. Work typically involves designing and implementing cloud environments, estab-lishing governance and landing zones, securing cloud workloads, and ensuring high availability and operational reliability. The category focuses on cloud engi-neering, architecture, and the full lifecycle of OCI SaaS and PaaS based services, including custom extensions, integration platforms and security capabilities. General requirements for the category · Proven experience with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and Oracle PaaS services relevant to Veikkaus (e.g. OIC, APEX, VBCS, IDCS/OCI IAM, FDI, database services). · Strong understanding of cloud security, networking, and compliance in EU context. · Ability to collaborate closely with Veikkaus security, infrastructure, and application teams. · Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section covers the procurement of cost-efficient Oracle development and support services delivered from EU/EEA-based near-shore delivery centers. The section focuses on providing flexible and scalable resources for the develop-ment and support of Veikkaus’ Oracle solutions. Services include technical de-velopment, application support, and continuous improvement activities for Ora-cle platforms across all solution areas defined in this framework. Near-shore delivery ensures proximity, compliance with EU regulations, and en-ables efficient collaboration with Veikkaus teams, while leveraging the expertise of Oracle professionals in the delivery center. The supplier is required to maintain a permanent delivery capacity and demon-strate the ability to allocate suitable technical resources for Veikkaus’ assign-ments, ranging from project-based work to ongoing support. Typical work includes software development and integration, technical trouble-shooting, enhancements, support services, and collaboration with Veikkaus per-sonnel for secure and compliant operation of Oracle solutions. General requirements for the category • Proven experience in Oracle development, support and services deliv-ered from EU/EEA-based near-shore centers. • Ability to provide development and technical support services for a range of Oracle products and platforms relevant to Veikkaus (e.g. ERP, HCM, EPM, CX, SCM, Oracle Cloud). • Capability to allocate and scale permanent Oracle delivery capacity (min-imum 10 professionals) with demonstrable competencies. • Compliance with EU data protection and security requirements; robust processes for ensuring secure, high-quality delivery. • Effective communication and collaboration with Veikkaus teams and ability to leverage near-shore proximity. • Additional roles can also be eg. project manager, test manager and ser-vice manager; This section covers the procurement of cost-efficient Oracle development and support services delivered from off-shore delivery centers. The section focuses on providing flexible and scalable resources for the development and support of Veikkaus’ Oracle solutions. Services include technical development, application support, and continuous improvement activities for Oracle platforms across all solution areas defined in this framework. The supplier is required to maintain a permanent delivery capacity and demon-strate the ability to allocate suitable technical resources for Veikkaus’ assign-ments, ranging from project-based work to ongoing support. Typical work includes software development and integration, technical trouble-shooting, enhancements, support services, and collaboration with Veikkaus per-sonnel for secure and compliant operation of Oracle solutions. General requirements for the category • Proven experience in Oracle development, support and services deliv-ered from off-shore centers. • Ability to provide development and technical support services for a range of Oracle products and platforms relevant to Veikkaus (e.g. ERP, HCM, EPM, CX, SCM, Oracle Cloud). • Capability to allocate and scale permanent Oracle delivery capacity (min-imum 10 professionals) with demonstrable competencies. • Compliance with EU data protection and security requirements; robust processes for ensuring secure, high-quality delivery. • Effective communication and collaboration with Veikkaus teams and ability to leverage near-shore proximity.

sig_268d17cf8ca438336650.description: Development of an innovative system which will provide important tourist information in a fast and simple way, as well as a series of useful functions such as automated tourist services, effective search for tourist attractions, provision of information regarding real distances, travel, fares, tickets. Furthermore, the system will aim at the provision of maps, accessibility to information regarding means of transport (in cooperation with OASA), the ability to submit questions / complaints, the ability to search regarding topics concerning culture, as well as the ability to inform citizens / tourists regarding severe weather phenomena, announcements, flight and route reminders (in cooperation with the airport system) as well as reminders for specific events etc. The action will include support for stakeholders (local administrations, destination management and promotion organisations, transport authorities (airports, ports), points of cultural interest (museums and archaeological sites) and businesses providing services to tourists/visitors. The purpose of the project is the promotion of Greece as a tourist destination through ICT actions that will lead to the digital transformation of the Greek National Tourism Organisation. The subject of the project is the development of an innovative system which will provide important tourist information in a fast and simple way, as well as a series of useful functions such as automated tourist services, effective search for tourist attractions, provision of information regarding real distances, travel, fares, tickets. Furthermore, the system will aim at the provision of maps, accessibility to information regarding means of transport (in cooperation with OASA), the ability to submit questions / complaints, the ability to search regarding topics concerning culture, as well as the ability to inform citizens / tourists regarding severe weather phenomena, announcements, flight and route reminders (in cooperation with the airport system) as well as reminders for specific events etc. The action will include support for stakeholders (local administrations, destination management and promotion organisations, transport authorities (airports, ports), points of cultural interest (museums and archaeological sites) and businesses providing services to tourists/visitors. The purpose of the project is the promotion of Greece as a tourist destination through ICT actions that will lead to the digital transformation of the Greek National Tourism Organisation. In the context of the project, a platform will be implemented which, as a tool, will contribute to the design and implementation of a strategy for the promotion of the sensitive and volatile tourism product. It will focus on the creation of added value for every tourist destination and its involved stakeholders, contributing to the implementation and service of the goals of integrated marketing and communication strategies and, through a customisable web platform, to the targeted provision of information for tourist products as well as points of interest, both via the internet and via mobile phone. The project will contribute gradually and among other things, to the increase of the competitiveness of every city/region, so that there is a positive impact on investments (ROI), real estate, infrastructure and the various cultural events that can take place in it, through the digital interconnection of content / information with the relevant points of interest throughout the country. sig_26a98529eaa32684637e.description: The subject matter of this procurement comprises the procurement of a SaaS solution, which encompasses various functions and services. The focus is on the provision of an extensive digital communication solution based on OX 8. The MBJS is looking for an experienced contractor capable of providing a corresponding solution based on OX 8 while meeting the specific requirements and needs of a state-level solution for the State of Brandenburg regarding high security standards (BSI IT-Grundschutz), data protection compliance (GDPR), integrity, flexibility and scalability. Lot LOT-0001: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail). In the year 2019, on behalf of the Ministry for Education, Youth and Sport (hereinafter referred to as MBJS), a complex IT infrastructure was built based on the products Univention UCS and Univention UCS@School, consisting of a central identity management system, hereinafter referred to as IDM, and the groupware and email solution Open Xchange from the manufacturer of the same name, hereinafter referred to as OX. An extensive communication solution was created for 20.000 teaching staff at publicly maintained schools in the State of Brandenburg. The schools mapped in UCS and UCS@School in the form of separate school OUs form the basis for the contexts set up in OX. Each school is thus assigned to a separate context in OX. The creation, modification and deletion of accounts in the IDM are carried out via the specialist procedures developed by the MBJS. After several years of operation, due to the lifecycle of OX, it is necessary to transition to the current version 8. The transition to OX 8 requires extensive changes to the UCS OX connector and the IT infrastructure. The version OX 8 requires Docker runtime environments that are not provided by the existing IT infrastructure. It is not possible to simply update the software in the existing system. The MBJS therefore intends to have the groupware and email solution for teaching staff based on OX operated in future as a SaaS solution by a provider. In this context, the user accounts in the existing IDM shall continue to form the basis for the email mailboxes and the existing provisioning processes shall be retained. Only the mail stack of the existing IT infrastructure is to be replaced by a SaaS solution.

Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. sig_26be5d5c49421572d5b9.description: The subject of performance of the awarded public contract ("public contract") is the provision of necessary operational support for security technologies that ensure the protection of the MHMP network perimeter. This involves the provision of services according to the following Catalogue Sheets ("CS"): • Catalogue Sheet 01 – Helpdesk and Servicedesk services • Catalogue Sheet 02 – Incident resolution • Catalogue Sheet 03 – Problem management • Catalogue Sheet 04 – Execution of service interventions • Catalogue Sheet 05 – Consultations • Catalogue Sheet 06 – Monitoring and supervisory service • Catalogue Sheet 07 – Security maintenance • Catalogue Sheet 08 – Documentation management These Catalogue Sheets will be provided for individual technologies, based on the activation of a Technology Sheet ("TS") for the given unit. These are: • TS01 – External Firewall • TS02 – Internal Firewall • TS03 – Firewall Management • TS04 – Endpoint Security • TS05 – Sandbox • TS06 – DDoS protection • TS07 – Balancer & application Firewall • TS08 – External DNS and SSL certificate management • TS09 – Vulnerability management • TS10 – Municipal District Firewall Management • TS11a – Municipal District Firewall P1 – P22 • TS11b – Municipal District Firewall P23 – P57 • TS12 – Remote access management For the operation of these systems, it is necessary to ensure their comprehensive management, which includes not only their correct configuration and integration links, but also supervisory, maintenance, preventive, mitigation and investigative activities. These systems have guaranteed manufacturer licences/ M&S/RMA, but a qualified team for supervision, management and development is necessary for their configuration, operation and utilisation. The subject of the implementation of this public contract is therefore: a) transition of the existing operational management of security technologies (Handover services); b) operation and management defined by Catalogue and Technology Sheets (Services according to Catalogue Sheets); c) provision of activities of Technology Development Specialists beyond the scope of Services according to Catalogue Sheets in the estimated extent of 756 MD; d) exit services. Operational support (Services according to Catalogue Sheets) will be provided for a period of 36 months. Technology Sheets will be activated based on the operational needs of the contracting authority. The activation of TS11a and TS11b will depend on the activation and implementation of the technology for each respective municipal district separately.

sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information with which the contracting authority is conducting a market survey of potential tenderers and solutions available on the market for its procurement need. The information obtained through the market survey will be used in the preparation of the future procurement. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) has a need to procure technology to be taken home for the use of the wellbeing services county's residents, as well as an alarm system that receives the alarms produced by the aforementioned technology. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is assembling and launching as its own operation a so-called Safety Assistance Service, the goal of which is to enable and support customers' independent coping in their own homes around the clock. A central element in the Safety Assistance Service is the technology utilised in it that is taken to homes or home-like services, and the receiving system for the alarms produced by them. With this request for information, LUVN wants to survey the technology solutions available on the market that are suitable for social and health care, that ensure the customer's safety at home, and solutions suitable for receiving alarms related to these. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue estimates that the procurement entity according to its needs will consist of the following parts, but changes may occur in the entity: - Technology installed at home for the customer's safety (e.g. sensors, detectors, wristbands) as well as their maintenance and backup device services - Safety alarm centre system and mobile software possibly related to it - Service implementation project - Continuous services, support, maintenance and service of the technology and alarm centre system - Expert services related to the aforementioned technology and its utilisation and use during the contract period according to the subscriber's need. To support the specification of its procurement needs, the planning of the procurement and the preparation of the tendering documents, Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue wants to engage in a market dialogue with suppliers offering solutions corresponding to the procurement need. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county hopes to receive information generally about solutions on the market corresponding to the object of the procurement. We are interested in your solutions and services related to safety technology supporting living at home and how the solutions direct alarms to the safety alarm receiving system and what features the receiving system includes. We also want to know what kind of information your system produces to support the planning of services offered to the customer for the professional, in addition to alarm information. Suppliers are requested to register for the market dialogue by email to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi Registration is requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12. The registration should be titled as follows: “Kodin turvapalvelulaitteet ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä” (Home safety service devices and alarm receiving system). The content of the email message is sufficient to be the supplier's name and the contact details of the supplier's contact person. LUVN will be in contact with the contact persons of the suppliers who have registered to agree on the implementation of the market dialogue. According to the wellbeing services county's plans, the market dialogue should include both discussion sessions and the exchange of written material, but the exact schedule of the dialogue will be specified later. The subscriber reserves the possibility to organise one-to-one market dialogue discussions in addition to commenting on written material. The subscriber reserves the right to select a suitable number of Suppliers for one-to-one discussions based on the written responses. The times for the one-to-one discussions will be agreed separately with the Suppliers. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding by companies does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation is paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.
sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of home safety service devices and alarm receiving system

sig_273bb4b184eb906f90a8.description: Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialueis used in pharmaceutical services and materials management units as the Webmarela enterprise resource planning system. The Webmarela system is subject to indefinite procurement contracts that have been transferred to the wellbeing services county with the supplier CGI Suomi Oy [contract numbers 2022.454.1 and 2021.908.1]. During the contract period, a need has arisen to amend the contracts in the following respects: merging the databases of the pharmaceutical services and materials management systems and introducing UDI functionality. Separate operating environments in Mikkeli and Savonlinna are currently in use for the Webmarela system. Over the years, functionalities and specifications that diverge from each other to some extent have been implemented in the operating environments. Due to the operational needs of the wellbeing services county, the separate operating environments must be merged. Merging the operating environments enables uniform operating processes for the wellbeing services county, shared data structures, and consistent system maintenance. At the same time, administrative work caused by local specifications is reduced, the harmonisation of working methods is supported, and cost-efficiency is improved. In connection with the merging of the environments, the functionalities in use in both environments must be implemented in the shared production environment. Otherwise, some of the current functionalities would cease to be available as a result of the merging of the environments. The objective of the procurement is to safeguard the continuity of current operations and to enable the use of a single shared Webmarela environment across the entire wellbeing services county. In addition, a need has arisen to introduce so-called UDI tracking functionality in the system for medical devices and accessories. UDI tracking is mandatory for healthcare organisations and is based on statutory regulations (EU) 2017/745 and (EU) 2017/746 as well as the Act on Medical Devices (719/2021). A Tokio version update has been made to the system, which enables the implementation of UDI functionalities. Fimea has, in a regulation issued on 30.1.2026, obliged Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialue to bring the medical device tracking system up to date and to implement the recording of UDI identifiers for risk class III implantable medical devices to the extent required by law no later than 30.10.2026. Almost all of Eloisa's disposable medical devices and accessories pass through materials management, a significant proportion of which fall under UDI regulation. UDI requirements have expanded in phases to various risk classes, and from 2027 onwards the requirements apply practically to all medical devices. The traceability of medical devices is a key part of customer and patient safety. Eloisa already uses operating models in which the UDI identifiers of implants are recorded in the Orbit and RIS systems to enable patient traceability. UDI identifiers can be used to manage, among other things, device tracking, recalls, and adverse incident reports. Webmarela acts as the operational system for materials management, where the receipt, storage, picking, and distribution of medical devices and accessories are managed. With the help of UDI functionality, product-identifying information can be linked to the material flow starting from the receiving stage, which supports the traceability of medical devices and forms the basis for implementing traceability requirements across the entire supply chain. Negotiations have been held with CGI Suomi Oy concerning the merging of the operating environments and the UDI functionalities. The procurement contract amendment shall enter into force when both contract parties have signed the contract amendment. Procurement contract 20167-M22 Contract ID 20167-M22; Procurement contract S100423y-220 Contract ID 2021.908.1

sig_2740c3b2b4cb57a42f76.description: This Pre-Market Engagement (PME) Notice issued by Tai Tarian to encourage Data and Insights Transformation Partner suppliers to register and attend a meet the buyer session for an anticipated procurement process. Tai Tarian is a not-for-profit Registered Social Landlord (RSL) responsible for managing and maintaining more than 9,000 homes across Neath Port Talbot. Since our establishment in 2011, we have focused on delivering safe, efficient, and sustainable homes that support thriving communities. We are now delivering a multi-year transformation programme aimed at improving customer experience, colleague engagement, organisational efficiency, and our ability to make data-driven decisions. Tai Tarian’s transformation is structured around five inter-linking workstreams: 1. Customer Experience – Improving services and interactions for tenants and communities. 2. Colleague Experience – Enabling a skilled and motivated workforce through better tools and insight. 3. Organisational Excellence – Clarifying processes and strengthening governance and accountability. 4. Data and Insights – Creating integrated, trusted data foundations that support evidence-based decisions. 5. Business Systems – Modernising and connecting systems to improve accuracy, efficiency, and service quality. This Pre-Market Engagement (PME) aims to understand the capability and capacity within the market to deliver an integrated Data and Insights Transformation Partnership. Information gathered will inform the final scope and design of a formal procurement to be advertised on Sell2Wales in early 2026. The programme will replace core business systems in two stages: • Starting H1 2026: HR, Payroll, and Finance systems. • Starting H2 2026: Housing Management, Asset Management, Customer Portal, and Field Service (including works scheduling). To support these changes, Tai Tarian plans to implement a phased Data and Insights Transformation that establishes a single, governed data platform. The supplier will help transition from legacy structures to Housing standard data models, first within the analytics layer of existing systems, then through data migration and integration into the new systems as they go live. This approach ensures continuity of reporting, insight, and compliance throughout the system replacements and creates a sustainable, standardised data foundation for the future. The Data and Insights Transformation Partner will support delivery across the five phases of Tai Tarian’s Data and Insights Transformation Programme, forming a core part of our wider organisational change agenda. Phase 1 – Build Data Platform Design and implement a secure and scalable data platform to provide a single source of truth across key business domains. This phase will establish foundational datasets, governance, and data models to enable future phases. Key functions may include: • Consolidation of data into a single, governed environment. • Definition of core data entities (tenant, asset, property, finance, HR). • Implementation of structured data storage, lineage tracking, and metadata standards. • Establishment of data ownership, stewardship, and quality controls. Phase 2 – Migrations and Integrations Develop the ETL and integration capability required to move and align data between legacy and modern systems. This will ensure consistent, timely, and accurate information across organisational platforms. Key functions may include: • Data migration planning, transformation, and validation activities. • Development of automated Extract, Transform and Load (ETL) processes. • Implementation of master data management and cross-system interoperability. • Testing and assurance to confirm data accuracy and completeness post-migration. Phase 3 – AI-Powered Data Cleansing Introduce automation and rule-based validation to improve data quality, consistency, and usability across the organisation. This will underpin a shift towards self-service reporting, insight generation, and predictive analytics. Key functions may include: • Deployment of automated data-cleansing routines and dashboards. • Application of business rules to identify and resolve duplicates or anomalies. • Establishment of feedback loops for continuous data improvement. • Support for data literacy and culture development across teams. Phase 4 – Analytics Layer Buildout Develop an integrated analytics and insight capability to deliver actionable information to decision-makers, colleagues, and stakeholders. This will enable evidence-based planning, regulatory reporting, and performance management. Key functions may include: • Creation of standardised reporting datasets and dashboards. • Development of analytics models supporting operational, financial, and sustainability outcomes. • Implementation of self-service tools for managers and teams. • Support for environmental and ESG reporting, including decarbonisation progress. Phase 5 – AI Services & Co-Pilot Development Establish an insight-driven culture by embedding intelligent automation, predictive modelling, and data-driven decision-making into services. This phase will focus on long-term enablement and innovation. Key functions may include: • Development of early AI-enabled use cases that enhance efficiency and tenant experience. • Introduction of natural-language and conversational query tools for insight access. • Design of governance processes for ethical and responsible automation. • Continued capability-building for Tai Tarian’s internal Data & Analytics function. Each phase will be delivered in alignment with Tai Tarian’s Data Strategy, Information Management Framework, Sustainable Planet Strategy, and Target Operating Model, ensuring that all solutions support long-term sustainability, compliance, and operational excellence. Meet the Buyer Sessions Interested suppliers may invited to attend ‘Meet the Buyer’ sessions, held on Monday 1st December and Tuesday 2nd December 2025 at Tai Tarian’s offices. To register your interest in attending please email procurement@taitarian.co.uk. Please note that you must email procurement@taitarian.co.uk to register your interest in attending, no other method of registering will be accepted. The deadline to register is 12PM Friday 21st November 2025. The session will allow interested suppliers the opportunity to meet with Tai Tarian’s representatives to gain an understanding of our requirements. For example, we are asking interested suppliers: • How their proposal could bring benefit to Tai Tarian and our stakeholders. • What makes a contract attractive to them. • Their experience of undertaking similar contracts. • Their experience both within and outside the Housing sector. • Lessons learnt from previous contracts. • Why they want to work with Tai Tarian. • Innovative ways of working (doing things differently) Please note that ‘Meet the Buyer’ sessions will only be carried out on specified days and that slots will be reserved by Suppliers on a first come first served basis. When all slots are filled, we will be unable to extend these sessions further. However, depending on the level of market interest, Tai Tarian reserves the right to reduce the number of interested Suppliers by using a questionnaire or another mechanism before opening slots, to ensure the best use of Tai Tarian resources by meeting relevant Suppliers over the specified period for the Meet the Buyer sessions. If this mechanism is used, then Tai Tarian will ensure equal treatment of all interested Suppliers and will share any relevant findings and information (when not commercially sensitive) from the Meet the Buyer sessions to all interested Suppliers. Please note that recording an interest is voluntary and potential tenderers will not be advantaged or disadvantaged through participation in any ‘Meet the Buyer’ session and any discussions held will not form part of any formal tender process. Tai Tarian reserves the right to change its requirements prior to the Tender Notice being issued and this PME does not commit Tai Tarian to undertake any procurement process. It is anticipated that a Tender Notice will be published in the coming months. The estimated contract value and estimated contract period provided in this Notice are for indicative purposes only and the estimated contract value and estimated contract period will be confirmed in any future Tender Notice. sig_27944c4b719203d14292.description: The objective of the procurement is to enter into an agreement for the procurement of digital teaching aids and teaching resources for the Oslo School. The purchasing system has previously been announced on Doffin/TED and is being re-announced to continue the scheme in Oslo municipality ́s new KGV. See the attached qualification documentation for further information. The Oslo School has participated in a R&D project together with KS since 2017. the R&D project ends in its current form in summer 2024. In order to achieve autonomy and freedom of methodology in the choice of teaching aids, a use-based payment model is required where schools have access to all products and pay in arrears in arrears in accordance with actual use. Digital teaching aids and teaching resources consist of a market that is constantly developing. To a small degree, traditional approaches cover the schools ́need for flexible access to a wide range of teaching aids. The aim is also that an overall ecosystem shall make the procurement process of digital teaching aids and learning resources easier for school owners and more in line with the needs of the schools and pupils. The dynamic procurement scheme is for continuous delivery of digital teaching aids (freestanding or as part of teaching aids/learning universe), teaching resources, resource banks (news, pictures, movies, audio, music, etc.), teacher guides, teacher resources, assignment/trial collections and mapping tool with accompanying teacher overview, glosses, etc. that are delivered over the internet ("Software-as-a-service") for teaching purposes. The agreement also includes digital books and installed apps with Feide sign-in for teaching purposes. The diagnostic tool, which requires special competence to use, is not included. Digital services, which only have a functionality for delivering teaching aids that shall be physically implemented, are also not included. The agreement does not include the purchase of services that do not have Feide sign-in, including apps for iPads that are purchased via the App Store/Apple School Manager.
sig_27944c4b719203d14292.title: 1-UDE-2024 Dynamic procurement scheme for digital teaching aids in the Schools of Oslo (USE)

sig_27949c058751021cac24.description: The subject of the contract is the delivery and installation of equipment for the Digital Court Hearing Recording System for the courts of the Kraków appeal and in so-called friendly interview rooms, divided into two parts of the contract: Part 1: –Delivery including installation of equipment for the Digital Court Hearing Recording System for the courts of the Kraków appeal–, Part 2: –Delivery including installation of image and sound recording equipment in so-called friendly interview rooms–. 1. The subject of the contract includes in particular: a) the delivery of technical devices together with software for the purposes of digital recording of court hearings, installation, implementation, commissioning as well as warranty service and technical support in courtrooms not previously equipped with equipment for the digital recording of court hearings; b) the technical support and service service for courtrooms equipped with equipment for the digital recording of court hearings supplied to the Contracting Authority. 2. As part of the subject of the contract, the delivery of technical devices together with software for the purposes of digital recording of court hearings, installation, implementation, commissioning and warranty service of the following elements as well as the delivery of electronic signature cards is required: a) Courtroom infrastructure; b) Electronic signature infrastructure; c) Other delivery elements. 3. The equipment should ensure hardware and software level compatibility with the currently used Digital Court Hearing Recording System. 4. A necessary condition for the award of the contract is the adaptation of all elements of the Digital Court Hearing Recording System to meet standards regarding the accessibility of public utility facilities for people with disabilities and the reduction of architectural barriers, in accordance with applicable regulations.; 1. The subject of the contract is the equipment of a friendly room with an image and sound recording system integrated with the ReCourt Services system, hereinafter referred to as RCS. 2. The system enables multi-channel real-time stream recording of: a) Audio – from installed microphones and established videoconferencing sessions, b) Video – from installed cameras and established videoconferencing sessions. c) Replay of a fragment of a previously recorded recording or replay of electronic evidence. 3. The resulting recording is compatible and has the ability to be replayed in any courtroom equipped with the ReCourt system. 4. The solution consists in equipping the Technical Room and the Interview Room with all necessary technical components, the quantity of which in special cases may be adapted to user requirements and room conditions. 5. An equivalent product to the specified subject of the contract is understood as a product with parameters and minimum requirements itemised (listed) and defined in the description of the subject of the contract (Annex No. 2.2 to the SWZ).

sig_27cac4da34016922339e.description: This is not a procurement notice or an invitation to tender, but a request for information from potential tenderers. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the market and gather information as well as suppliers' comments so that a subsequent procurement procedure can be carried out in an appropriate manner. The request for information does not request, and tenders will not be submitted in response to it. The subject matter of the procurement is the provision of financial management (bookkeeping, purchase and sales ledger, reporting) and payroll management (pay payment, statutory obligations, travel and expense claims) services, which is described in more detail in this request for information and its appendices. Appendix two describes in more detail the official duties and division of responsibilities of the intermediary body. The service package includes information systems and software, and the organisation and implementation of the transition project. In addition, the procurement may include, as an option, HR services, a personnel management system and related services. The purpose of the market dialogue is to determine what kind of package could be used to implement financial and payroll management and HR services in the Regional Council of Ostrobothnia in the future. The aim of the market dialogue is to survey service providers and information systems with software suitable for the needs of the Regional Council of Ostrobothnia. The procurement package includes, AS AN OBJECTIVE, services in accordance with this call (=request for information). INFORMATION SYSTEMS AND SOFTWARE System users in the Regional Council of Ostrobothnia will be approximately 5 persons. The service package includes the tenderer's information systems and software in financial management and payroll management for the client's use. In addition, the procurement may include, as an option, HR services, a personnel management system and related services. ORGANISATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE COMMISSIONING PROJECT The service package also includes the organisation and implementation of the transition project. REQUIREMENTS AND DIVISION OF RESPONSIBILITIES TABLES CONCERNING FINANCIAL, PERSONNEL AND PAYROLL MANAGEMENT SERVICES More detailed requirements and division of responsibilities tables for the financial, personnel and payroll management service will be provided separately at a later date to those who have registered for the market dialogue. TASKS OF THE REGIONAL COUNCIL OF OSTROBOTHNIA According to the preliminary plan, the tasks of the Regional Council of Ostrobothnia will remain in particular preparatory tasks for the monitoring and reporting of the administration of its own projects, and in addition to this, in particular decisions on project disbursements belonging to state assignments and the official duties of the intermediary body (approx. 100 disbursements / year). The contract is intended to be concluded for a fixed term of two years, after which the contract will continue until further notice. A notice period of six months (6 months) shall be included in the contract.

It is a national government initiative led by Enterprise Ireland under the Action Plan for Competitiveness and Productivity, to strengthen Ireland’s capacity to create, grow, and scale indigenous businesses. Startup Ireland leads on the design, implementation, coordination and delivery of the new National Accelerator Programme with a core objective to support the creation of 1,000 new start-up businesses by 2029, alongside a wider ambition to support entrepreneurial activity nationally and regionally. A full list of requirements is outlined in the tender documents.

Program Description: Statement of Objectives (SOO)/Description of Technical Areas: Scope: The scope of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. Objective: The performance objectives of this effort are to: The Government's objective is to achieve the following capabilities and milestones across the period of performance. The contractor shall propose the specific methodology and detailed work breakdown to achieve these objectives: Phase Technical Objectives & Deliverables CLIN 0001 - Labor: Key Deliverable: esign & Integration Report Design & Build: Design and construct a space vehicle flat-sat and a corresponding space vehicle cyber range. Integration: Integrate the flat-sat with the cyber-range and verify the functionality of selected space vehicle subsystems. Software Hardening: Initiate cyber-hardening of the space vehicle flight software utilizing Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS). Key Deliverable: Design & Integration Report. CLIN 0002: ODCs Integration: Integrate the cyber-hardened flight software into the established flat-sat/cyber range environment. Functional T&E: Assess the function and performance of the cyber-hardened solution against a non-hardened baseline. Cyber-Effectiveness T&E: Develop cyber-attack scenarios and evaluate the defensive effectiveness of the hardened solution against the baseline. Key Deliverable: T&E Reports (Functional, Performance, and Cyber-Effectiveness). CLIN 0003 - Reports: Operational Procedures and Ground Demonstration CONOPs & COAs: Develop and test Concepts of Operations (CONOPs) and Courses of Action (COAs) for cyber detection, protection, and recovery. User Interface: Develop a UI for interaction, visualization, and further development of the cyber-hardened solution. Demonstration: Conduct ground-based experimentation and system demonstrations. Key Deliverable: CONOPs and COAs Report, Ground Demonstration Completion. Live Experimentation: Conduct on-orbit experimentation and a live demonstration of the developed cyber-hardened space vehicle system. Key Deliverable: Successful On-Orbit Demonstration and Final Technical Report. CLIN 0004: Contractor Acquired Property - CAP Areas from the ARA with CALLS, FA9453-21-S-0001, Full Text: Space Battle Management, Command, and Control: Enable uninterrupted delivery of tactical, operational, and strategic space services within a contested environment by providing unprecedented domain awareness; accurate and timely battle management tools; and robust command and control options. Specific areas of technology being sought include data fusion, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and related methods for rapid threat assessment and response; multi-domain (land, sea, air, and space) net-centric command and control concepts; autonomy and on-board threat assessment algorithms to enhance satellite resiliency; and integration of allied, commercial, and non-traditional capabilities. Deliverable Items: Data: DD Form 1423-CDRLs Key Deliverable Report: Design & Integration Report. T&E Reports. CONOPS and COAs Report. Ground Demonstration Completion. Final Reports: Final Scientific and Technical Report to be delivered under each award, 3 months after the end of the technical effort. Software: Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) will not need to be provided to contractor. Hardware: The government and MITLL developed CHSS and since MITLL will be performing the cyber-hardening, CHSS will not need to be provided to contractor. The government will provide CHSS interfaces and drivers in order for the flat-sat software to interface. The government will provide requirements/information for the space vehicle contractor to design the flat-sat and then build it. Other Requirements: Program Security Classification: While it is anticipated that this effort may be performed UNCLASSIFIED, CUI to Secret. Individuals must be US citizens and have a security classification level equal to or higher than the security requirement for the effort. Offerors may be required to have a level of safekeeping. DD Form 254, Department of Defense (DoD) Contract Security Classification Specification, will be attached to each CALL, as this call is anticipated to conducted work at the Secret level, therefore a draft DD254 is attached. sig_282c8cd008c1f2f752e4.description: IKOMM AS invites tenderers, on behalf of Enebakk municipality, to a competition for the procurement of a new top management system for the municipality ́s treatment facilities with the accompanying pump stations. Enebakk municipality shall procure and implement a joint, modern top system (SCADA/SD) for monitoring and management of its two sewage treatment plants and 33 pumping stations. The project shall replace the current fragmented systems and provide higher operational security, improved event management and full traceability of process data. The system shall meet strict requirements for information security and stand-by, reduce operational and energy costs and ensure that the municipality meets the current environmental and reporting requirements. Brief description of the current sewage installations and operations control system: Enebakk municipality has a municipal sewage network that comprises approx. 109 km pipeline network for wastewater and serves approx. 10,500 inhabitants. The facility consists of two treatment plants and 33 pumping stations as well as four out stations in addition. The current operational control system is based on local installation and communication via 4g, fibre and radio. The system monitors and controls pumps, level meters, alarms. Data collected for reporting and analysis functionality is limited. Enebakk has therefore adopted Gemini Water Alert to work more efficiently with the foreign water problem. The municipality has 4 operational operators as well as a manager who uses the system, with a duty scheme for 24 hour contingency. The background for the procurement is the need for a more modern, secure and scalable top system common for both treatment plants, which provide a better overview, simpler reporting and an option for future integration with other systems. The procurement only includes sewage treatment; water supply is not part of the project.
sig_282c8cd008c1f2f752e4.title: Top management system for the treatment facilities in Enebakk municipality

sig_2879105c1cffd551dfb7.description: As part of the ESF Plus-funded programme "DigWohl", the contracting authority is planning the development of a digital solution to strengthen child protection - a child protection app for Thuringia. The aim is to develop a low-threshold, age-appropriate web app that informs children and young people aged 6 to 16 years about their rights, provides guidance within the support system and facilitates access to support services. The subject of the tender is the conception, development and further development of a web-based child protection app in the period from November 2026 to April 2028. The contracting authority currently estimates a total budget of 105.000€ (gross). The web app should in particular include the following functions: - Information module: information on children's rights and child protection topics prepared in an age- and target group-appropriate manner, differentiated for children aged 6 to 11 years and young people aged 12 to 16 years - interactive content (e.g. quizzes, playful formats) - Dialogue system or chatbot function: to support information retrieval - Help module: presentation of regional and digital support and advisory services - Complaint and contact function: age-appropriate entry option for concerns and complaints with forwarding to a contact person of the carrier or the respective institution stored in the backend; prospectively expandable for further carriers - Central backend: for the administration of reported cases, the maintenance of content, support services and contact persons by the contracting authority; prospectively expandable for further carriers The web app should initially be usable by children and young people in German, English, Arabic and Ukrainian. There are also special requirements regarding low-barrier accessibility, participation of the target group and long-term expandability. sig_289a5c58119a75aa4b4d.description: ECMWF, as the Entrusted Entity for the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), invites Tenders for Co-design of GHG policy services in support of EU Member States and Copernicus Participating countries ECMWF intends to award a single Framework Agreement for a period of maximum 22 months, which shall be implemented via a single multi-annual Service Contract expected to commence in Q1 2027. The successful bidder will propose the interaction with national inventory agencies and related institutes that are responsible for national monitoring of GHG emissions and the reporting to the UNFCCC . The successful Tenderer shall carry out the following activities: • Detailed familiarisation of the successful Tenderer with the latest status of current and emerging operational CAMS products and the use of satellite Earth Observations (EO) for GHG emissions monitoring. • Facilitate collaboration between European national inventory agencies and CAMS. • Collect, document and analyse user requirements at national level for EU member states and Copernicus participating countries. • Provide recommendations for the development of policy-relevant tools, including data visualisation, at national level.

sig_28cd0a339f3d0d41da3f.description: Invitation RFQ Description: Fairhive Homes Limited is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced supplier to provide, implement, configure, support, maintain and continuously improve a Learning Management System (LMS). The LMS will support Fairhive's requirements for effective learning management, compliance training, reporting, user administration and integration with Fairhive's wider systems environment. The scope is expected to include: • Hosted Learning Management System platform. • Configuration of workflows, roles, permissions, learning pathways, dashboards, notifications and branding. • Implementation support including mobilisation, discovery, testing, user acceptance testing, go-live support and hypercare. • Data migration including mapping, cleansing, reconciliation and validation. • Microsoft Entra ID Single Sign-On and user provisioning. • Microsoft 365 integrations including Microsoft Teams and Outlook calendar integration. • Administrator, manager and end-user training. • SCORM 1.2 and SCORM 2004 content support. • Hosting, backups, disaster recovery, maintenance and support. • Reporting, dashboards and scheduled reporting. • Continuous improvement and account management. • Estimated Contract Value: £36,000 to £50,000 per annum. • Estimated Maximum Contract Value: £108,000 to £150,000 including VAT. • Procurement Above or Below Threshold: Below Threshold. • Main Procurement Category: Services • Contract Commencement: TBC - Fairhive to confirm.  Initial Term: 2 Years.  Extension Options: 1 Optional Year.  Potential Contract Expiry: TBC, dependent upon contract commencement date. NB - This procurement is being undertaken as a below-threshold Request for Quotation (RFQ) under the Procurement Act 2023. As the estimated contract value is below the applicable procurement threshold, it is not subject to the full regulated procurement procedures that apply to above-threshold procurements. The Act requires a proportionate approach to below-threshold procurement and provides contracting authorities with greater flexibility in determining an appropriate route to market. In accordance with this approach, the RFQ will be conducted on an invitation-only basis, with quotations being sought from a selected number of suppliers assessed as capable of delivering the requirement. This enables meaningful competition whilst maintaining a proportionate process aligned to the value, complexity and risk profile of the contract. Similar approaches are reflected within procurement guidance and procurement policies developed in response to the Procurement Act 2023. For completeness, the Procurement Act 2023 does not require contracting authorities to run an open tender process for below-threshold procurements. In particular: • Part 6 of the Act establishes a separate regime for below-threshold contracts, recognising that fewer obligations apply than for covered procurements. • Section 85 sets out requirements where a contracting authority chooses to invite tenders for a regulated below-threshold contract but does not mandate that the opportunity must be advertised openly to all suppliers. • The Act allows contracting authorities to take a proportionate approach to supplier selection and competition for below-threshold opportunities, provided that transparency requirements applicable to the procurement are met. sig_28e502fcb6051b981121.description: The subject of the public procurement is "Service maintenance of an information system for the management and maintenance of the register of integrated permits (IP) pursuant to Article 129, paragraph 1 of the Environmental Protection Act (EPA)". 1. In performance of the procurement, the Contractor shall provide service maintenance services for the information system for the management and maintenance of the register of integrated permits (IP) under the Environmental Protection Act (EPA) with the following scope: 1.1. Resolution of all issues that disrupt the functional operability of the information system (IS) such as: 1.1.1. Rectification of errors in the program code and software settings - if necessary, within a period not exceeding one working day; 1.1.2. Assistance with modifying software settings - if necessary; within a period not exceeding one working day; 1.1.3. Rectification of other technical malfunctions - if necessary; within a period not exceeding one working day. Note: the activities under item 1 shall be performed after receiving a notification of their occurrence and a request for their rectification from the Contracting Authority 1.2. Review of system logs for errors and issues, including attempts at unauthorised access – weekly. 1.3. Maintenance of the software application and database – monthly. 1.4. Current integration with other systems and optimisation of its functioning, with a workload of no more than 24 (twenty-four) man-hours per year; 1.5. Consultations for system users (experts of the MoEW) regarding the functionality of the information system, within working hours (from 9:00 to 17:30 hrs every working day), through an automated information system for servicing queries and problem reports from users or by servicing an email address for queries and problem reports from users, as well as via a contact telephone number during the working day for urgent issues. As part of the Tender for performance of the procurement, the participant must present its query and problem reporting system. 1.6. Restoration of the information system and data in the event of a potential crash, including from a backup created by a centralised system for backup and archiving of data, servers and systems of MoEW-HQ, no later than one working day after receiving notification of a crash and a request for system restoration from the Contracting Authority. 1.7. Updating and handover of a new version of the system documentation in case of established obvious discrepancies with the actual functionalities, as well as in cases where actions have been taken to rectify defects and errors, within the term of the contract. 1.8. Within the term of the contract and if a need arises, the Contractor may be required once to carry out a migration of the information system to another IT infrastructure, including: • Establishment of a highly resilient virtualisation platform (VMware) for normal functioning and backup of the information system in a hardware environment of the Contracting Authority, different from the current one in which the system is currently operating and its maintenance for the entire term of the contract; • Migration of the information system to the established virtualisation platform, including the modules and components implementing integration with other systems; • Testing of all system functionalities after migration; • Commissioning of the migrated system into live operation; All activities listed above in item 8 must be carried out within a period of up to 15 days after notification from the Contracting Authority of an arisen need for migration. All changes, migration and testing must be performed outside working hours without disrupting the workflow of employees working with the system. The supply of system software licences is not the subject of the subsequently concluded contract in performance of the public procurement. The performance of the procurement does not include the development of new functionalities. The scope described in items 1 - 8 also covers the currently established functionalities of the information system for the public register under the EOEPB. 2. Technological platform of the software applications within the scope of maintenance The software applications within the scope of the procurement are implemented on the following technological platform: • Internet Information Server 7.5; • .NET Framework 4.5; • ASP.NET 4.5; • ASP.NET WebApi; • Programming language C#. Database management system: • Microsoft SQL Server Standard Edition 2012. Where possible, the Contracting Authority will provide a higher version of the database, to which the database must be migrated.
sig_28e502fcb6051b981121.title: "Service maintenance of an information system for the management and maintenance of the register of integrated permits (IP) pursuant to Article 129, paragraph 1 of the Environmental Protection Act (EPA)"

More in detail, the specific objectives of this Call are as follows: - Selection of AIGF Consortia: Following a rigorous evaluation of the tenders by the EuroHPC JU with the support of independent experts, the Governing Board will make an award decision, establishing a ranked list of successful AIGF Consortia. - Procurement of Compute Access Time: To establish a framework for the joint acquisition of a guaranteed share of AI compute access time from the selected AIGF Consortia, formalised through the signature of a Framework Contract and a number of subsequent Specific Contracts with the successful AIGF Consortia. AIGF refers to state-of-the-art large-scale facility with sufficient capacity to handle the complete lifecycle, from development to large-scale inference, of very large AI models and applications, providing a supercomputing service infrastructure which is composed of AI-optimised computing capacity, a supporting data centre infrastructure including high-capacity storage and networking, dedicated secure cloud user access environments, and specialised secure AI-oriented support services for its advanced operations, all of which are supported by an environmentally sustainable infrastructure, in particular for energy and water supply systems. This lot targets the establishment of 4 awarded consortia capable of deploying a medium-scale AI Gigafactory project each. sig_2930b1e5977b5494c20e.description: The Council require a single, modular enterprise cloud platform to support all Salisbury City Council service areas and functions, not limited to any one department. The solution has to be capable of being configured and rolled out across the organisation in phases, while maintaining a consistent data model, user management, reporting and governance. The platform has to be capable of supporting end-to-end processes across all Council service areas, including but not limited to Customer Services and Contact Centre functions (such as enquiries, requests, complaints and communications), Parks, Open Spaces, Play Areas, Trees and Grounds Maintenance, Inspections, Compliance and Health & Safety activities (including vehicle and equipment checks where applicable), Asset Management, Task Management, Works Orders and Maintenance, Crematorium and Bereavement Services (including bookings, tasks, payments and record management), Allotments, Grants and Funding administration (covering applications, assessments, scoring, approvals, agreements, payments, monitoring and reporting), Markets, Street Trading and Events, Facilities and Venue Bookings (including halls, rooms, pitches and other council assets available for hire), Licensing and permission-based workflows, FOI, SAR, EIR and Complaints processes where required, Payments and Income Collection through integrated payment solutions, and Internal Service Requests where the Council chooses to operate the platform as a service desk. The platform must also provide a comprehensive audit trail across all modules and service workflows, recording as a minimum the user identity, timestamp, action or event undertaken, and the associated record or context. The audit trail must capture the full lifecycle of records, including creation, amendments, status changes, assignments, approvals, closures and controlled deletions. It must also record inspection evidence, including completed forms, photographs and attachments, outcomes, findings and any actions taken, as well as task and works order lifecycle activity, including findings recorded for monitoring purposes only. The system must maintain a complete history of enquiry and case communications, covering both inbound and outbound correspondence, and where payment functionality is utilised, record payment events and their linkage to the relevant case, service or transaction. In addition, the platform must log integration and web service events, including successful and failed transactions. All audit information must be readily reportable and exportable to support operational assurance, compliance monitoring, evidential requirements, and both internal and external audit activities. Lot 1: . None

sig_295346eb1564c99b92c5.description: This notice is published in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. It should not be interpreted as a guarantee of any future procurement opportunity, nor as confirmation of the approach outlined herein. The purpose of this Notice is: a) For MoJ to engage the market and provide an initial brief as to our future requirement and direction of travel, for the provision of High-Volume Offsite Printing. b) For MoJ to ask questions pertinent to our strategy and stage of the project and elicit useful information and answers from market experts. This will be conducted through a Request for Information (RFI) exercise. The MoJ is a diverse organisation providing services and regulation for the broader criminal justice system in the UK. As well as the core of MoJ Headquarters, it also includes His Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS), His Majesty’s Prisons and Probation Service (HMPPS), the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), the Legal Advice Agency (LAA), Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs) and others. A full list of the MoJ’s services and organisations can be found on the gov.uk website, here: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/ministry-of-justice/about In total, there are approximately 90,000+ users across the organisations, located all across the country and in approximately 1000+ different buildings. These include headquarters, HMCTS offices, courts, probation offices, prisons, and specialist print centres. All of these users require printing services in a variety of ways and against a number of use cases. The MoJ is looking to procure its next generation of print services. The Future Print Services team has refined the services it requires into two main categories: a) Office Print b) High Volume Offsite Printing (HVOP) We are separately exploring an opportunity for Office Print. This Notice relates specifically to the HVOP service. The requirement is for a Hybrid Mail solution operating out of a dedicated, secure document production centre located off-site. Files and documents will be submitted through either an integration with an MoJ line-of-business application, or via a dedicated portal provided by the supplier. The documents must then be printed, packed and dispatched directly to the intended recipient. Additionally, there is an option to validate postcodes prior to dispatch, ensuring that items with invalid postcodes are not sent. The service includes all components of the delivery including the cost of the postage to the ultimate recipient. The intended timescale for the RFI is February 2026. Further details on how to participate and access the RFI documents can be found in the Engagement section of this Notice. The procurement process is expected to commence June/July 2026 (exact timing to be confirmed). The MoJ is currently evaluating whether to utilise an existing framework agreement (under the 2015 or 2023 Procurement Act regulations) or to proceed with a new tender. This decision will follow a comprehensive review of market conditions and internal requirements. Please note that the details outlined in this notice are subject to change as the MoJ continues to develop its procurement strategy. Please also note that the estimated value of this procurement is a high level estimate at an early stage of the process, inclusive of optimism bias contingency. It should not be taken as a guarantee for actual expenditure under any future contract. Lot 1: .
sig_295346eb1564c99b92c5.title: High Volume Offsite Print (HVOP)

sig_295a6cb3fe7e96e81bd5.description: The FET College Major Capital Programme (FCMCP) is the primary focus of the Framework and Competition. It is anticipated that services drawn down from the Framework will, primarily, relate to the FET College Major Capital Programme, allowing for the provision of services from an Integrated Design Team (the IDT) with respect to the twelve (12) projects under the FET College Major Capital Programme (FCMCP). The provision of services, as required on an individual and ad-hoc basis by a Contracting Authority, which are ancillary or related to the delivery of one of the twelve (12) projects under the FCMCP (the Related Services). The Framework Owner and Framework Users may also make appointments within the remit of the Framework to support their own mandate outside of the current FCMCP. This will allow for the following: technical, design, delivery, consultancy and advisory services (the Supplementary Services) and the provision of services from an IDT with respect of Capital Project Delivery of buildings and facilities of a similar scale than those currently described as part of the FCMCP. The FCMCP involves the development of purpose-designed Further Education and Training facilities (buildings) in 12 of the 16 Education and Training Board (ETB) areas throughout the country. The FET College Major Capital Programme (FCMCP) is a major, multi-year investment initiative designed to modernise and transform the Further Education and Training (FET) sector. The programme, as part of a new operational model for FET, aims to shift towards a portfolio of consolidated, high-quality, and sustainable FET Colleges that will support an inclusive and inspiring learning environment using sustainable design and construction approaches. The Applications for this competition consist of four Principal Consultants (Architecture and Team Lead, Civil and Structural Engineer, Mechanical and Electrical Engineer, Quantity Surveyor) established as part of this Framework. Please refer to Procurement Documentation (Programme Information Memorandum) for full description of Services that are to be included within the Principal Consultants Service.

sig_295c2cc6d2cf6fcac330.description: Development of 3D Models for Nuclear Facilities. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) maintains its ability to verify the nuclear programmes of non-nuclear weapon State (NNWS), including the capability to rapidly respond to any significant changes required for the implementation of safeguards-related activities in the field. As one part of its longer-term preparedness activities to date, the Department of Safeguards has already been able to acquire and demonstrate a limited technical capability in using Virtual Reality (VR) navigation inside real-world 3D scans, including the ability to attach relevant geobased data sources to 2D optical imagery. Lessons learned from previous VR projects have already been applied in the development of the current capability. However, to be more effective in its ability to rapidly respond to potentially significant changes in the short term, there is a need for the Department of Safeguards to develop 3D models of a number of very specific critical facilities. As part of its long term preparedness activities, the Department of Safeguards needs to develop the ability to develop and use 3D and Virtual Reality (VR) models for training, analysis and knowledge management. This task will support the creation of models for a number of different nuclear facilities and sites, in close consultation with IAEA experts and inspectors. The 3D models will provide tangible benefits in terms of knowledge management and implementation of safeguards. This will include the training/familiarization of inspectors who may have limited experience of the specific processes at the selected critical nuclear facilities and implementation of safeguards therein. The activity within this task is highly specialised, requiring significant technical knowledge and capabilities with advanced state-of-the-art 3D modelling technology. The proposed contractor must have experience of developing 3D models and resources similar to the facilities of interest. In addition, models must have the capability of being integrated with relevant IAEA Safeguards IT architecture, standards, policies and procedures. The proposed contractor must demonstrable experience of working with the nuclear sector. The specific target for the research is considered sensitive and, therefore suppliers must meet the minimum security requirements to handle, OFFICIAL SENSITIVE information. Lot 1: .
sig_295c2cc6d2cf6fcac330.title: Modelling of Critical Nuclear Facilities
