sig_29714e9c55d9c6aac73c.description: The subject matter of this contract is: "Implementation of integration of the Information System for Management and Maintenance of the Public Register under the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act (ISMMPR under ELPRA), including migration of existing data, with the identified information systems of bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA" The main objective of the project is the integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with other information systems (IS), both within the Ministry of Environment and Water (MoEW) and with external systems maintained by other state bodies. Main aspects of the subject matter of the contract: Analysis of existing information systems: • The project includes validating the analysis of the designated information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA for their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA and their functionalities that can be integrated with the ISMMPR under ELPRA. This validation of the analysis aims to determine the electronic nomenclatures in these systems, as well as the possibilities for copy-pasting existing data. Integration requirements: • The contract covers the definition of architectural and functional requirements for the integration of the systems, including automated data exchange between the ISMMPR under ELPRA and other registers of administrative bodies, as well as the maintenance of compatibility with information systems outside the MoEW. • Integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16 of ELPRA, in accordance with the Ordinance on the Public Register of Operators Performing Activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act and Guidelines on the provision of information for entry in the public register of operators performing the activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of ELPRA, including: • Validating the identified information systems of the executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA and their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA for data, as well as providing new functionalities for connecting the systems. Improvement of the public register under ELPRA: • The project provides for the modernisation and upgrading of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with the aim of ensuring centralised access to data and greater interoperability with other systems, while maintaining high information security and eliminating duplicate data. Maintenance services: • Information on the maintenance services of the integrated systems will be provided, including updating and monitoring of their operation. Compliance with regulatory requirements: • The requirements of the contract are aligned with the regulatory framework of the Electronic Governance Act (EGA) and subordinate legislation, as well as with the business analysis that establishes additional requirements for the implementation of the project. The subject matter of the contract covers the development and deployment of effective integration of information systems, ensuring interoperability between registers and systems maintained by various state administration bodies, and guaranteeing the proper functioning of the ISMMPR under ELPRA, in accordance with the requirements of ELPRA. Scope: The described objectives are achieved through the implementation of the following main stages: 1. Data and requirements analysis; 2. Preparation of a system design; 3. Development of the software solution; 4. Testing; 5. Deployment; 6. Training; 7. Warranty support. Project activities: Activity 1: Design; Activity 2: Integration/Construction.

sig_299020684a6708fa9c2c.description: The Combined Authority already has in place a single supplier framework for the provision, installation and maintenance of multi modal traffic sensors across the Liverpool City Region which will come to an end in June 2026 and there is therefore a need to re-tender a suitable framework to continue to expand the sensor network across the LCR. Being able to evidence the return on investment for transport funding is a key requirement and it is now recognised that the data obtained from the sensors is now part a core dataset for multiple purposes across the LCR. The LCRCA is conducting market engagement in order to better understand what is currently available on the market in relation to providing a service for the purchase, installation, maintenance (and repair/replacement of the same if required) and data licensing and hosting requirements of AI multi modal traffic counters/sensors and a data platform to access the data from the counters/sensors. This will allow the LCRCA to improve its data which will enable us to justify, monitor and evaluate improvements we make to the transport network. Lot 1: .
sig_299020684a6708fa9c2c.title: Market Engagement - Liverpool City Region Multi Modal Traffic Sensor Framework

sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.description: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (hereinafter referred to as RED) is designed to build upon previous efforts in engineering education research. Specifically, previous and ongoing evaluations of the NSF Engineering Education and Centers Division program and its predecessors, as well as those related programs in the Directorate for STEM Education, have shown that prior investments have significantly improved the first year of engineering students’ experiences, incorporating engineering material, active learning approaches, design instruction, and a broad introduction to professional skills and a sense of professional practice – giving students an idea of what it means to become an engineer. Similarly, the senior year has seen notable change through capstone design experiences, which ask students to synthesize the technical knowledge, skills, and abilities they have gained with professional capacities, using reflective judgment to make decisions and communicate these effectively. However, this ideal of the senior year has not yet been fully realized, because many of the competencies required in capstone design, or required of professional engineers, are only partially introduced in the first year and not carried forward with significant emphasis through the sophomore and junior years. The Directorates for Engineering (ENG) and STEM Education (EDU) are funding projects as part of the RED program, in alignment with the Improving Undergraduate STEM Education (IUSE) framework and Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) initiative. These projects are designing revolutionary new approaches to engineering education, ranging from changing the canon of engineering to fundamentally altering the way courses are structured to creating new departmental structures and educational collaborations with industry. A common thread across these projects is a focus on organizational and cultural change within the departments, involving students, faculty, staff, and industry in rethinking what it means to provide an engineering program. In order to continue to catalyze revolutionary approaches, while expanding the reach of those that have proved efficacious in particular contexts, the RED program supports four tracks: RED Planning (Track 1), RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2), RED Innovation (Track 3), and RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4). Two- and four-year institutions are encouraged to submit to any track as appropriate for their goals and context. RED Planning (Track 1) projects will support capacity-building activities at institutions of special interest to NSF’s mission, including two-year engineering-centered programs building transfer partnerships, two-year or four-year institutions in EPSCoR jurisdictions, Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs), and Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) in order to create more opportunities in engineering for students in every part of the country. Planning projects should provide the support for such institutions to explore the development of a RED Projects in Tracks 2, 3, & 4. RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2) projects will adapt and implement evidence-based organizational change strategies and actions to the local context, which helps propagate this transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation (Track 3) projects will develop new, revolutionary approaches and change strategies that enable the transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4) projects will achieve the same goals as Track 3 projects across multiple institutions. Of particular interest to this track are projects partnering two-year institutions with other eligible institutions. Projects in tracks 2, 3, & 4 will include consideration of the cultural, organizational, structural, and pedagogical changes needed to transform one or more departments to ones in which students are engaged, develop their technical and professional skills, and establish identities as professional engineers or technologists. The focus of projects in these tracks should be on the department’s disciplinary courses and program. RED project initiatives are expected to be institutionalized at the end of the funding period. Proposals are especially encouraged that address areas of increased national interest including but not limited to advanced manufacturing, advanced wireless, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, microelectronics and semiconductors, net zero technologies, sustainability, systems engineering, and quantum engineering.
sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (IUSE/PFE: RED)

sig_29fab6c00fddd730cfd0.description: The subject of this public contract is the "Selection of an operator to provide redundant communication connectivity and to ensure the capability for management and security related to this provision, configuration and maintenance of the necessary communication equipment for the needs of Toplofikatsiya Sofia EAD". The main objective of awarding the contract is to provide communication connectivity and to ensure the capability for management and security related to this provision, configuration and maintenance of the necessary communication equipment in order to provide a fully functional, highly secure and manageable communication environment for data exchange with the ability to flexibly prioritise traffic types, monitor load, protect and manage events in this environment. The scope of the contract includes the execution of the following activities: - provision of redundant communication connectivity with parameters and speed according to the requirements of the technical specifications and the implementation proposal, within up to 120 working days from the date of contract signing and maintaining it in operational condition for a period of 36 months; - provision for the duration of the contract, installation and configuration of communication equipment to build a communication system to be provided as a service, ensuring the capability for flexible security management, monitoring and prioritisation by traffic type, within up to 120 working days from the date of contract signing and maintaining its operational readiness for a period of 36 months; - for the equipment provided for the duration of the contract, the Contracting Authority does not owe separate fees and does not acquire ownership of it. - provision of a service, in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications and the implementation proposal, within up to 120 working days from the date of contract signing and maintaining its operational readiness for a period of 36 months. - All provided services must be delivered with high quality, reliability and security, which must be maintained for the period of the contract along with their operational readiness and fault tolerance. The individual types of activities and implementation requirements are described in detail in the Technical Specification published in the electronic file of the contract.

(End of Amendment) Amendment 06 – Revision to TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language and GFP Clause List (21 November 2024) The purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language included in Section I paragraph 9 (formerly included in Section I paragraph 8) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. The revised paragraph is as follows: 9) Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors are notified that subsequent Call Announcements shall include a requirement for submission of the documents identified below. Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. Additionally, the purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Government Furnished Property Clause list in Section I paragraph 10 (formerly Section I paragraph 9) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. The revised paragraph is as follows: a) Government Furnished Property (GFP): To be determined for each award. In accordance with FAR 45.201(b), the contractor is responsible for all costs related to making the property available for use, such as payment of all transportation, installation, or rehabilitation costs. If GFP is requested in a proposal, the following clauses/provisions apply: (i) FAR 52.245-1 Government Property or FAR 52.245-1, Alt II if the resulting contract is with a nonprofit organization or applied research at nonprofit organizations (SEP 2021) (ii) FAR 52.245-9 Use and Charges (APR 2012) (iii) DFARS 252.245-7003, Contractor Property Management System Administration (APR 2012) (iii) DFARS 252.245-7005, Management and Reporting of Government Property (JAN 2024) (End of Amendment)

sig_2a19c6e7c46b70946e86.description: Framework agreement iBS II Lot LOT-0001: Integrated Control System (iBS). The integrated control system (iBS) is a subsystem of the integrated control and operating system (iLBS) and includes, amongst other things, the central services of the iBS (iBS-Z), integrated operator terminals (iBP) in accordance with the redundancy regulation 2, the reference image function (RBF), iBS communication (iBS-Kom) as well as the iBS-Z console. The iBS subsystem is connected to other iLBS subsystems via standardised interfaces, thereby enabling the operation of integrated sub-centres (iUZ) with electronic interlocking / digital interlocking (ESTW/DSTW). Lot LOT-0002: Transfer network router. The transfer network is a component of the iLBS system and implements communication between all transfer network participants (e.g. iBS-Z, iLBS-ZE and central directory service) in the overall iLBS system up to the network layer (OSI layer 3). This does not include: VPN LST gateway modules, all components of the transport network, the time standard receiver (e.g. DCF-77) or the middleware broker. (including all system components for redundancies). The components are thus used both at the interlocking location (TSO or existing interlocking) and at the locations of the individual iBS, the BSO. Lot LOT-0003: Broker and directory service. A component of the iLBS is a network of broker servers via which the components and subsystems communicate with each other (via Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP)). (including all system components for redundancies). The brokers are thus used at the iBS and LMC locations. A broker pair (redundant design) is always required at each location. The brokers use the AMQP protocol or Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP) as a platform. For the hardware, 2 HU per physical broker instance in the computer cabinet are provided in the 19 inch rack. The installation depth of 700 mm must not be exceeded. Cooling of the brokers must take place from the front. (see also system specifications requirements specification DiB-0454). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0004: Local routing plan management (LLPV). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0005: Operational management of the central directory service (ZVD) of the LMC and the transfer network of the iLBS . The operational management for the central directory service and the transfer network (transmission system consisting of transfer network router, broker, etc.) comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. These systems already exist in the ITU. Procurement of the components is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded. Lot LOT-0006: Operational management of the central routing plan management (LPV) for the LMC . The operational management for the central routing plan management comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. This system already exists in the ITU. Procurement of the component is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded.

sig_2a1f8f660027b868c5b8.description: This procurement covers the Population Health Management framework. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector. The framework is divided into three lots: Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these. Lot 1 is suitable for solutions with the below characteristics: • Solutions that can address large scale populations, however defined. • Multiple features and functionality, covering a wide range of Population Health Management. • Typically draws data from a range of sources of other organisations. • Horizontal integration to provide large populations to manage. • May or may not include the features and functionality of more specialist solutions. Lot 2: Consultancy &Support Services The nature of services will be to address a variety of needs through providing information, advice, direction and potential solutions to customers. Suppliers will be expected to be able to assist customers to make more informed decisions surrounding their population health programme. • Support of the delivery of population health management to the NHS and broader public sector. • Consultancy services are about helping the NHS or other public sector organisations that may use this framework to implement and deliver population support for some or all of the people who live in the areas they either commission or provide health and care services to. • Consultancy could extend across the NHS, wider health, public health, local government, broader policy areas impacting on health (such as transportation policy, housing policy, employment, environmental - other areas of policy relating to population health management and social determinants of health. • Consultancy might also be more targeted, dealing with a more limited area of healthcare, such as risk stratification, social prescribing, medicines usage, etc. Lot 3: Combined Solutions This Lot covers the provision of Population Health Management solutions that deliver bundle services or comprehensive workflows. Population Health Management provided under this Lot should ensure a seamless, integrated approach, delivering all the necessary components required for Approved Organisations. Across all lots, suppliers must provide: • Software licences or subscriptions • Implementation, configuration, and integration services • Training, onboarding, and change management support • Ongoing maintenance, updates, and technical support • Clear service level agreements and performance reporting Lot 1: .

sig_2a296527a11036b196a8.description: LapIT Oy is initiating a procurement competition for the acquisition of usage rights for VMware by Broadcom products or equivalent licences. The subject of the planned procurement competition may also include maintenance, support and distribution services for the usage rights. The future procurement competition is planned to be a 'combined procurement' (Section 7 of Chapter 1 of 1397/2026) for goods and services exceeding the EU threshold, in accordance with the Act on Public Procurement and Concession Contracts (1397/2016) applicable to mixed contracts. The aim is to launch the procurement competition in late autumn 2026. This market survey notice informs potential candidates and tenderers of the launch of the future procurement competition, possibly via an open procedure, during the autumn of 2026. This market survey notice also publishes an invitation to a market dialogue, which will be held between 4.9 at 8-16, between 10.9 at 8-16 and between 11-9 at 8-16. More detailed information on the market dialogue is described in the market survey notice. The deadline for registration for the market dialogue is 28.8 at 23:59. Registrations are made directly by responding to the request for information in the market survey notice. The market dialogue will be conducted in bilateral discussions between the registered potential candidates and tenderers and LapIT Oy. Both the market dialogue and the request for information are non-binding and are used only to assist in planning the future procurement competition and contract period. LapIT Oy will contact those who have registered for the market dialogue separately to agree on the timing of the bilateral dialogues. The market dialogues will be held entirely remotely using Teams. The market dialogues will be recorded. This market survey notice also initiates a request for information. The request for information is part of this market survey notice and the request for information must be answered electronically in the Cloudia Tender Service. The deadline for responding to the request for information is 28.8 at 23:59. The request for information survey serves as part of the preparation and planning of the procurement. This market survey notice, the invitation to the market dialogue and the request for information are not a prior information notice nor a contract notice, and they do not initiate the actual tendering process for the future procurement. The objective of this market survey notice's invitation to the market dialogue and the request for information is to survey the market and initiate an open interaction process between LapIT Oy and potential candidates and tenderers, and to review alternative views and solution proposals for the procurement competition for the requirements-compliant purchase. Participation in the market dialogue or the request for information does not bind the candidate or tenderer to participate in the tendering process, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering process later. Failure to respond to the request for information does not exclude participation in a possible actual tendering process. Responding to the request for information does not affect the position of the candidate or tenderer in the tendering process itself. Failure to attend the market dialogue does not exclude participation in a possible actual tendering process. Participation in the market dialogue also does not affect the position of the candidate or tenderer in the tendering process itself. In the market dialogue, it is possible to present comments and engage in open discussion with the persons preparing the procurement. The content of the request for information will also be reviewed during the market dialogue. The observations from the request for information and the market dialogue will be utilised in planning the future procurement competition and contract period.

sig_2a52539a7445318cd45d.description: The subject of the contract is the digitisation and electronic filing of the physical archive of the Department of Traditional Settlements and Listed Buildings (DT&LB) for approximately 7.500 "cases". The services provided include the conversion of the analogue archive into digital format by scanning high-resolution documents, drawings and photographs, while the migration of already digitised data hosted in the existing database of the DT&LB Department will also take place. For the management of the digitised documents and related data, a digital repository will be created that will allow the collection, storage, management and analysis of information, integrating digitised files such as approvals, decisions, studies, drawings and photographs. The core structure of the existing archive will be maintained, thereby ensuring the best organisation and management of the material and its correspondence with the analogue material. To improve system efficiency, new fields will be added to improve the functionality of the search engine, as well as the consolidation of existing fields in cooperation with the Contracting Authority, where required. At the same time, with the development of the digital repository, equipment will also be procured for the digitisation process. In particular, through the operation, two (2) desktop computers and one (1) NAS disk system with a minimum total capacity of 40 TB will be procured. sig_2a73dc8dc4647d227f01.description: Prior to this contract, the TPS.Plan train planning system has been supplied and operated within the framework of the contracting authority's contract with a consortium consisting of Alstom Transport Danmark A/S, Alstom Belgium S.A. and Alstom Ferroviaria S.p.A. for the supply of a signalling system for Eastern Denmark (see contract notice 2010/S 39-057711), where Hacon Ingenieurgesellschaft mbH – now part of the Siemens Mobility group – has acted as a subcontractor with direct technical responsibility for the system's development and maintenance tasks. This contract constitutes a carve-out of the TPS.Plan task from the existing contract structure. The purpose of the carve-out is to establish an independent and direct contractual relationship between the contracting authority and Siemens Mobility A/S (which is part of the Siemens Mobility group), which will henceforth bear overall responsibility for the system's operation, maintenance and modernisation directly towards the contracting authority. As part of this, the relevant parts of the existing contract relating to the TPS.Plan system will be terminated and replaced by this contract. The value of the payment made under this agreement is thus offset by a lower payment under the contract with Alstom Transport Danmark A/S, Alstom Belgium S.A. and Alstom Ferroviaria S.p.A. for the supply of a signalling system for Eastern Denmark. It is noted that Banedanmark has published a notice with a view to voluntary ex ante transparency, cf. statutory order no. 187575-2026. This contract concerns the maintenance and modernisation of the contracting authority's train planning system, TPS.Plan. The purpose of the contract is to ensure reliable and secure operation of the system, while keeping the system updated and modern as a central component of the contracting authority's overall traffic management infrastructure (TMS). The supplier shall take over responsibility for the maintenance and modernisation of the system in the contracting authority's production environment upon completion of a transition from the previous supplier. The total scope of delivery comprises the following service categories: Continuing Services: Continuing maintenance and support of the system after transition as well as cross-vendor incident management. Modernization Services: Further development and modernisation of the system, including a planned major upgrade from TPS.Plan v. 4 to TPS.Plan v. 5 ("TPS Master"), two new major releases and specific customer adaptations. Ordered Services: Services specifically ordered by the contracting authority on an ad hoc basis in accordance with the contract, including general consultancy assistance, hypercare, software development and exit services. Cross-Cutting Services: Services delivered as an integrated part of the other service categories. The value of the delivery amounts to 29.503.288 DKK. The value of maintenance for 10 years amounts to 91.700.020 DKK.
sig_2a73dc8dc4647d227f01.title: Contract for TPS.Plan System maintenance and modernization

Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is surveying suppliers' interest in a tender concerning a recruitment system. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to express their interest in the procurement by email. Expressing interest in the request for information does not bind the service provider/supplier to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. The subject of the request for information is a recruitment system package that supports all stages of Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue's recruitment process and enables the smooth execution of the process. The system must be flexible, user-friendly and easily developable according to future needs. With its help, routine tasks and the documentation of the recruitment process required by the Local Government Act can be largely automated, and it is possible to transfer data electronically between other systems from the system through integrations. The aim is to offer applicants a good applicant experience, and the system must adapt to various recruitment needs and clearly depict the progress of recruitments. Flexible functions are required for substitute recruitment, such as the automatic contacting of those registered in the substitute pool at the time of publishing the substitute need, as well as the possibility of automated applicant selection and information. 1. Functional features: - Building the organisation in the system, user rights at different levels, creating user rights ("mass" creation in the implementation phase) - Stages of the recruitment process (permit processing, notices, applications, communication and message templates (applicants, line managers, main users), video interviews, comparisons, reporting/statistics, monitoring the progress of recruitments, "desktop" views of recruitments for line managers and main users, document templates (possibility to create various document templates)) - Stages and functionalities of substitute recruitment (is it possible to transfer data electronically for drawing up the employment contract) - Publishing interfaces (e.g. Job Market Finland, other channels) - Customisability of application forms - Booking interviews via the interview calendar, anonymous recruitment, video interview, artificial intelligence utilisation possibilities, social media - Co-operation tool / module, if the supplier's solution includes the functionality, functionality means the organisation and automation of obligations related to job offering, re-placement, re-engagement obligation and lay-offs - Artificial intelligence utilisation possibilities in different stages of the recruitment process 3. Flexibility and extensibility: - Support for the further development of the system and integrations e.g. to the HR system, electronic archive and document management system. 7. References and user experiences: - Comparable implementations in the public sector - Success of implementations and customer satisfaction Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue requests that responses to the request for information be submitted no later than 23.12 at 12 to the email address marja.ahola@luvn.fi. sig_2aa409454ffbf16ff19d.description: NHS Shared Business Services Limited (NHS SBS) intends to put in place its 2nd generation Framework for the provision of Sustainable Transport and Infrastructure to be used by Approved Organisations for the following proposed Lots, which are under consideration during this preliminary market engagement (PLEASE NOTE: The proposed Framework is intended to cover the provision of Sustainable Transport and Infrastructure, together with Goods and Services that support transport-related environmental sustainability and net zero initiatives, by helping the NHS and other Approved Organisations to produce sustainable travel plans to reduce organisational carbon output, thus enabling them to build resilience to a changing climate both now and for future generations): Lot 1 - Micro-Mobility This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure expertise, planning and implementation of micro-mobility schemes, which will minimise the environmental impact of travel by offering alternative methods of transport. This includes but is not limited to electric bikes, cargo bikes, and pedal bikes. The schemes will encourage the use of alternative commuting methods by developing and implementing effective strategies, as well as through education and marketing. Lot 2a - Drone Delivery Services This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure safe, efficient, and sustainable drone delivery services that supports the transformation of healthcare logistics and contributes to net zero objectives. Suppliers will provide fully managed drone operations that facilitates the rapid, secure, and low carbon movement of medical items, including but not limited to pathology samples, pharmaceuticals, medical equipment, and urgent clinical supplies. Services included under this Lot may cover scheduled and on-demand deliveries, emergency-response missions, airspace and regulatory compliance, real-time tracking, and secure chain of custody processes. Suppliers are expected to integrate seamlessly with the Approved Organisation's operational workflows and uphold the highest standards of safety, data security, and reliability. Where required, Suppliers may also offer associated infrastructure, including but not limited to drone landing stations, automated docking and charging units, and digital monitoring platforms. This Lot supports Approved Organisations in reducing road-based transport emissions, improving delivery times, and enhancing resilience through modern, sustainable, technology enabled logistics solutions. Lot 2b - Robotic Logistics This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure safe, efficient, and sustainable robotic logistics solutions that support modern operations and contributes to the net zero agenda. Suppliers will provide fully managed robotic systems, including but not limited to autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and robotic carts, to automate the movement of essential items including medications, consumables, linen, food, and pathology materials across sites. Services under this Lot may include system design, installation, integration with existing infrastructure, fleet management, maintenance, and ongoing technical support. Suppliers are expected to adhere to high standards of safety, infection control compliance, reliability, and cybersecurity, ensuring robotic platforms operate effectively within clinical and non‐clinical environments. Supporting infrastructure may also be incorporated, including but not limited to charging stations, docking bays, lift‐integration systems, and digital platforms for mapping, scheduling, and monitoring. This Lot helps Approved Organisations to reduce internal transportation emissions, improve workflow efficiency, and free staff to focus on patient‐centred activities. Lot 2c - Traditional Courier Services This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure compliant, efficient, and sustainable traditional courier services that supports the secure movement of items across local, regional, and national networks. Services under this Lot will facilitate the reliable transportation of a wide range of medical and non‐medical goods, including but not limited to pathology samples, pharmaceuticals, medical records, confidential documents, equipment, supplies, and ad‐hoc consignments. Suppliers must provide fully managed courier operations that uphold the Approved Organisation's standards for safety, security, and chain-of-custody integrity. This may include scheduled route‐based collections, on-demand, and same‐day services, temperature‐controlled deliveries, and specialist handling where required. Suppliers must ensure robust compliance with relevant legislation, data protection requirements, and industry standards for secure transport. In support of the net zero agenda, Suppliers must demonstrate environmentally responsible delivery practices, which may involve the use of low or zero‐emission vehicles, route optimisation technologies, consolidated deliveries, and other measures that reduce carbon output compared to traditional transportation models. Where required, Suppliers may also provide supportive digital systems including but not limited to booking platforms, real‐time tracking, electronic proof of delivery, and reporting dashboards to enhance transparency, efficiency, and operational integration. This Lot enables Approved Organisations to access high‐quality, resilient courier services that meet both logistical needs and sustainability objectives. Lot 3 - Car Park Management This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure the design, build, and management of sustainable car parks with reduced carbon impact. Suppliers must deliver car park solutions that minimise carbon output compared to traditional construction, and where required by the Approved Organisation, incorporate biodiversity enhancements within the local environment. The Lot requires the adoption of modern methods of construction (MMC) and the utilisation of low or zero carbon materials, components, and processes to further support sustainability goals. The objective of this Lot is to improve the overall experience for patients, staff, and visitors by implementing car park management practices that align with the Approved Organisation's car parking principles, while also offering solutions that help lower carbon emissions. This includes the provision, installation, and maintenance of car park equipment and supporting services that help Approved Organisations meet their operational and sustainability objectives. Lot 4 - Electric Vehicle Charging and Infrastructure This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure the planning, proposal, and implementation of electric vehicle charging solutions for a diverse user base, including but not limited to fleet, grey fleet, and personal vehicles. The Lot will provide Approved Organisations with safe, reliable, robust, and secure infrastructure, that is easy to use and always available to the end user. The Lot includes the supply, installation, maintenance, and back-office systems, along with grid upgrades, induction, solar panel / PV, and battery storage. The Lot also includes the option to fund electric vehicle charging infrastructure, including hubs. Lot 5 - Cycle Parking and Infrastructure This Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure high-quality, safe, and secure cycle parking and infrastructure solutions that supports active travel, sustainability objectives, and site accessibility across the Approved Organisation's estate. It includes a complete range of cycle and micromobility storage facilities designed to encourage low carbon travel among staff, patients, and visitors, while ensuring robust security, durability, and ease of use. The Lot will deliver fully managed services that cover the end-to-end lifecycle of cycle parking provision, including design, installation, maintenance, and ongoing operational management. Innovative financing models may also be offered to support flexible and cost-effective deployment across diverse Approved Organisation settings. The Lot encompasses a comprehensive suite of infrastructure options, which includes full cycle hubs and multimodal mobility hubs that integrate multiple services at a single location, alongside individual components including but not limited to cycle stands, racks, clamps, bike boxes, and lockers. Additional protective structures may include canopies, shelters, and secure enclosures to enhance user safety and protect assets from weather and vandalism. Technology enabled access systems including but not limited to RFID tags (or equivalents) and mobile app-based access control can also be incorporated where required by the Approved Organisation. To support ongoing user convenience and promote a culture of active travel, the Lot enables Approved Organisations to procure ancillary equipment, including but not limited to fixed cycle pumps, cycle repair stations, cycle counters, and dedicated e-bike charging points. sig_2aaeb06480df2b157fe5.description: The Department of Neurosurgery at Heidelberg University Hospital is one of Europe's leading neurosurgical institutions, treating the entire spectrum of neurosurgical conditions surgically in high case numbers. To improve the quality of treatment for the overall medically highly complex patient cohort, the replacement procurement of a navigation system for the central operating theatre is intended, which is necessitated by the end of service provision for the old device (out of service). The aim of the procurement is to achieve a technical upgrade of the overall installation by replacing the existing device without compromising the established surgical techniques and optimised operating theatre workflows, as well as the expertise of already trained user groups. In addition, improved performance parameters of a new system create efficiency potential for improved economic efficiency of use. In order to meet the broad range of services and the medically highly complex service offering of the Neurosurgery department at Heidelberg University Hospital, the following criteria must be unconditionally fulfilled for the award: 1. The product must be usable both cranially and spinally and strictly fulfil the following technical requirements: a. The system must be capable of being used interdisciplinary both for interventions on the head, including common image fusion and fibre tract reconstruction methods as well as the integration of external examinations (TMS), and for instrumentations on the spine as well as for guided biopsies and stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). b. Integration of the existing Zeiss Kinevo microscope for cranial interventions incl. the possibility of projecting planning data of multimodal neuronavigation as semi-transparent structures into the heads-up display. c. Integration of an intraoperative MRI and data transfer with the possibility of automatic MRI-based patient registration. 2. Secure integration into the existing and proven IT and server infrastructure of Heidelberg University Hospital must be ensured for smooth and reliable data transmission and planning of surgical interventions via remote access and must meet the following requirements: a. Integration into the existing, centralised server infrastructure for neurosurgery, maxillofacial surgery and ENT incl. implementation of fail-safe data communication. b. Connection and compatibility of all relevant navigation systems at UKHD and automatic data synchronisation. c. Flexible data access to the planning server from the navigation unit as well as from any computer from the hospital network incl. the possibility of several simultaneous user accesses. d. Possibility of access to advanced planning software for installation on a local server infrastructure for spinal and cranial interventions, including a module for rigid and elastic image fusion, a module for fibre tract reconstruction (probabilistic/deterministic), a module for automated pedicle screw planning based on CT data, as well as a stereotactic planning package incl. a patient-specific segmentation algorithm for the automatic generation and display of risk structures. 3. Taking into account the personnel and spatial conditions on site, integration into the existing navigation infrastructure as well as a modular concept for the needs-based use of the individual components in the sense of preserving user competencies and a reduction in space requirements is required. The following requirements must be met: a. Incorporation into existing user workflows as well as the software-side user experience to preserve the existing and long-term established competencies of users. b. Independently usable mobile navigation system for spinal and cranially navigated interventions with the modular connection option to existing robotic systems of the same manufacturer and/or imaging units. 4. The possibility of shared use of the individual components with neighbouring departments must be possible taking into account local conditions (device sharing): a. Interdisciplinary planning server for shared use for cranial, spinal, maxillofacial and ENT interventions. b. Interdisciplinary navigation system for cranial, spinal and ENT interventions. c. Interdisciplinary robotics solution for spinal and cranial indications (incl. biopsy and SEEG). d. Interdisciplinary 2D and 3D imaging for spinal, cranial, maxillofacial and ENT interventions. 5. The manufacturer must have a high-performance service network in Germany in order to guarantee high availability of the installation for patient operations. The possibility of remote maintenance and remote access must be provided. 6. The contractor guarantees compliance with all statutory provisions applicable to the device, in particular MDR (EU) 2017/745, MPDG, occupational health and safety, hygiene, EMC, data protection and radiation protection regulations.

sig_2abe54df7814d724f0ff.description: The L&R licensing activities for taxi, private hire drivers, taxi proprietors and private hire operators, are currently delivered by directly employed TfL staff. As part of the licensing process, staff need to verify a DBS Check has been completed and applicants are fit and proper persons to hold the licence applied for. Public and passenger safety is a priority for TfL. Once licensed, a driver will be in day-to-day contact with members of the public, including children and vulnerable adults. It is therefore essential to ensure that applicants are of good character and are a 'fit and proper' person before they become a licensed driver. Taxi and PHV driver licences are valid for a period of three (3) years. Private hire operator licences are valid for up to five (5) years, and taxi and private hire vehicle licences are valid for one (1) year. TfL is also looking to introduce Pedicab licensing in London. This is currently undergoing review and consultation, so full requirements are in progress and anticipated to be finalised and included in the Contract prior to Contract Award. The primary aims of the service are to ensure: - All new applicants for a taxi and private hire driver's licence, have had an enhanced DBS check including checks of the Barred Lists. Pedicab drivers may also have to have these checks but this is subject to consultation; - All licensed taxi and private hire drivers have had an enhanced DBS check including checks of the Barred Lists. Pedicab drivers may also have to have these checks, but this is subject to consultation; - All private hire operators have a basic DBS check with every new and renewal application, a further basic DBS check annually on the anniversary of the licence issue. Pedicab operators may also have to have these checks, but this is subject to consultation; - Dial-a-Ride drivers and staff have DBS checks to the required standard dependant on role; - ID document checks to meet the DBS requirements; - Offer basic checks for taxi vehicle owners as required. Pedicab vehicle owners may also have to have these checks, but this is subject to consultation; - Offer an option for private hire operators who live overseas (TfL do not envisage large numbers of these), this is operators where they have lived their whole life overseas and not in UK; -Any other DBS checks that TfL may require (for example: any additional TfL employees, etc); - Provide a user-friendly DBS application with an online service and a paper version if needed; - Meet all required security and privacy standards; - Provide an API Interface into the Licensing System. The Licensing System administers the licensing of drivers, operators and vehicles; - Provide a user-friendly Web Portal that allows and encourages applicants to apply online for the appropriate level of DBS check, make an online payment for their DBS check and track the status of their application; - Provide a solution to check real time results and status of the DBS check; - Provide an administrative service to request paper disclosures where there is content and upload for TfL to access; - A DBS registered umbrella body company are required to provide the services and shall adhere to the DBS code of practice and guidance including all DBS stipulated requirements and standards. sig_2ad20d2b02e40250ad87.description: The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) intends to create a pathway to link problems identified by large organisations with solutions provided by innovative cyber small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) known as the Cyber Accelerator Programme. If you are interested in this potential opportunity, DSIT would like to engage with you. The Bidder presentation is due to take place Wednesday 23rd September 11:00 ( details at the bottom of the notice, on how to register) The Authority is seeking to engage the market to gather information, insights and feedback, while also providing an opportunity for Suppliers to better understand and discuss our requirements. This activity is not a procurement or a commitment to purchase goods or services. Its purpose is to facilitate open dialogue, improve our understanding of available solutions and supplier capabilities, and help shape the requirement and future approach, ensuring any subsequent procurement activity is informed, proportionate and delivers the best possible outcome. The principal objective of the programme is to create a credible pathway from agreed challenges facing the public sector to the commercial adoption of cyber innovation by public-sector buyers. It is intended to link problems identified by public-sector organisations with solutions provided by innovative cyber small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The programme will use structured, pro bono design partnerships between public-sector organisations with identified cyber challenges and innovative cyber SMEs capable of developing and testing solutions. Participation will not provide funding, an assurance of future work or preferential treatment in any subsequent procurement. The appointed supplier will be expected to: - identify and recruit suitable public-sector Challenge Council members; - build a broad pipeline of potential Programme Innovators and select suitable innovators against defined challenges; - support challenge development and match innovators to challenges; - establish, facilitate and oversee at least five design partnerships; - provide programme governance and a light-touch commercial, procurement, data protection and security compliance wrapper; - support routes to adoption or other lawful commercial progression; - organise one Showcase Day and other programme activity; - report on progress and produce a final report; and - create and disseminate a pattern library of repeatable approaches to support public-sector adoption of cyber innovation. Lot 1: . None

sig_2ad57a51f6fa26648b0f.description: Through this Research Announcement (RA), the Office of Pipeline Safety, at the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), an operating administration of the U.S. Department of Transportation, solicits applications for research projects awarded and funded as Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs). A comprehensive administrative and technical review will be conducted to determine the merits of the proposals and their relevance to the topic areas of focus. All proposals will be evaluated using only the materials provided in each proposal. PHMSA will reject proposals that duplicate work already planned, completed, or validated under recent initiatives. PHMSA reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the proposals submitted in response to this RA. PHMSA will not reimburse any proposal development costs. All proposals will be treated as sensitive, competitive information and their contents will be used for evaluation and award purposes only. Any questions are to be directed at the PHMSA Acquisition Services Division as listed in this solicitation. Any questions on solicitation content, issues, or procedures must be submitted via email to Stephen Jones at stephen.jones@dot.gov with a cc to Tremayne Terry at Tremayne.Terry@dot.gov no later than 5:00 p.m. EST, Friday, October 9, 2026. The research announcement number (693JK326RA001) must be included in the subject line. Responses to questions submitted on time will be posted publicly on SAM.gov within 2-3 business days after questions deadline. A full proposal package is defined as the proposal that includes Appendices A and B, and the proposal attachments. No award will be made if any of the above documents are missing from the full proposal package. Please submit the proposal and the proposal attachments in PDF format, except for Attachment #3 “Technical and Deliverable Milestone Schedule,” which should be submitted as an editable Excel document. The procedure for submitting a proposal is as follows: Prior to submitting a proposal package: All offerors must be registered in the Federal Government’s System for Award Management (SAM) (www.sam.gov). Each organization must complete an online registration form to access PHMSA’s Pipeline Safety R&D Management Information System (MIS). More information can be found at: https://primis.phmsa.dot.gov/matrix/RfpHome.rdm?rfp=109. Credentials from past registration will still be valid. To avoid account duplications and for questions or concerns with the registration or application, please submit an e-mail to rd-support@dot.gov prior to starting your submittal to ensure you don’t already have an existing account. Submit Proposal Package: Only electronic submissions, through MIS, will be accepted. Additional instructions regarding the preparation and electronic submission of proposals along with individual questions and answers are available on the website above. sig_2ad8d0ebae71d4b21900.description: The subject of the contract is the interventions for energy upgrading and energy saving, concerning the emblematic Cultural and Spiritual Centre of the Municipality of Corinthians, which is of particular cultural value. The intended results of the Action include the reduction of the building's energy consumption and the simultaneous reduction of CO2 emissions through the improvement of energy efficiency and the use of RES in its building infrastructure, by adopting energy-efficient systems for cooling and heating its spaces as well as replacing existing lighting lamps with LEDs. For the implementation of the proposed project, the Municipality will implement 5 categories of energy saving interventions and exploitation of RES systems as follows: 1. Supply and installation of an air-to-water heat pump 2. Supply and installation of LED lighting fixtures 3. Supply and installation of a Photovoltaic System 4. Supply and installation of an energy management system 5. Supply and replacement of window frames and glazing The supply includes the installation and commissioning of the equipment and includes all minor materials or automations. Also, all necessary materials that will be required and connected for the full and proper operation of the systems are included. Furthermore, prior to their final acceptance by the Municipality of Corinthians, the contractor is required to carry out a proper installation and operation check and, where specified by the technical study, issue a certificate of proper installation and operation as well as training of the personnel who will undertake the operational handling of the installed systems. The subject of this contract is the Supply and installation of an air-to-water heat pump at the Cultural and Spiritual Centre of the Municipality of Corinthians.

sig_2ae5455bf1ceb9a21bd6.description: The subject of the procurement is the design, delivery and implementation support services of an external service provider for TVET teacher training to be carried out in Ethiopia. The procurement supports the digital transformation of the country’ s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system as part of Specific Objective 2 (SO2) of the DESTA, Digital Ethiopia: Skills and TVET Action programme. The selected tenderer will be responsible for designing and delivering the first training programme within a three-tier TVET Trainers’ Digital Competence Pathway: the Foundation Programme in Digital TVET and Learner-Centred Pedagogy. The overall three-tier pathway also includes an advanced-level training programme and a Training of Trainers (ToT) programme. Programmes 2 and 3 are included in this procurement as option. The contracting authority may decide to procure these programmes during the contract period. The training programme will be delivered using blended learning modalities (face-to-face, distance and online learning) and will leverage Ethiopia’s national Moodle-based learning management system. The contracting authority will select one (1) service provider.

sig_2af5c184c2748a3998bb.description: The Maynooth University School of Business was established in 2007 and currently employs over 100 academic, administrative, and support staff as well as a student body of over 4,000 full time undergraduate and postgraduate students. The School of Business offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programmes across a wide range of business disciplines as well as offering a suite of modules within the Arts programme. The teaching and learning experience of our students involves a series of face-to-face lectures within our state-of-the-art facilities within Maynooth’s campus delivered primarily by academic faculty but can also include guest lectures from industry. The School’s collective pedagogical strategy is further enhanced by Moodle, an online learning environment whereby learning materials, supplementary readings, case studies, or other media resources facilitating additional student engagement with individual modules. sig_2af5c97b910435612743.description: The University of Sussex (Sussex) is preparing to seek a partner for the provision of Online Programme Management (OPM) Services, with the current contract set to expire on 5 October 2027 and the new contract commencing on 6 October 2027. Under the existing arrangement, Sussex has collaborated with a partner to deliver a portfolio of Masters-level degree courses accessible to students both nationally and internationally via online distance learning. The current contract encompasses a range of services across three core areas. • Marketing and Recruitment: Market Research and Strategy, Lead Generation, Inquiry Management, Admissions Support, Application Processing, Reporting and Analysis. • Course Development and Delivery Model: Course Design and Development, Content Creation, Platform Integration, Technical Support, Continuous Improvement, Compliance and Reporting. • Student Support: Induction and Orientation, Ongoing Support, Monitoring and Communication, Reporting. As the end of the current collaboration approaches, Sussex is actively reviewing its strategy for online learning. The University's strategic aims are to establish a sustainable, high-quality online provision aligned with the University's strategic priorities, enhancing our institutional reputation globally. The provision will be future-ready in terms of modularity, flexibility, and compliance with regulatory frameworks such as the Lifelong Learning Entitlement. Further details regarding this engagement are available in the Instruction Document, which can be accessed via the e-sourcing portal, Proactis: https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com/account/login While participation in this engagement is not mandatory for involvement in any future procurement process, responses received will help inform the Contracting Authority about the level of market interest. Additionally, feedback from this engagement may help shape the final service requirements and inform the design of the forthcoming procurement strategy, ensuring it reflects both institutional priorities and sector best practice. Lot 1: .

sig_2b14b5982fefbfea6495.description: ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS”) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: • Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. • Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M as defined by SBA regulations. • Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 — All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. • Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3’s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. sig_2b2d0dca8c2ef7c1a532.description: Veiligheidsregio Gelderland Zuid (VRGZ), Veiligheids- en Gezondheidsregio Gelderland Midden (VGGM) and RAV Noord- en Oost Gelderland (NOG) are jointly procuring Timelab's Seconds software. This application supports dispatchers in the emergency control room with the dispatch and positioning process of ambulances. The system advises which ambulance can be sent most optimally to an incident and proactively positions ambulances based on a predictive AI model. Several data sources are processed simultaneously here: historical run data, current traffic information, weather conditions, vehicle availability and personnel planning. Together, the three regions handle approximately 148.000 ambulance deployments annually. The software replaces manual decision-making with data-driven support, leading to shorter response times and less cognitive load for dispatchers. The initial agreement has a duration of one year, with three unilateral extension options of The contract concerns an agreement with an initial duration of one year, with the possibility of three unilateral extensions of one year each, resulting in a maximum duration of four years. The estimated annual licence costs amount to 60.500 euro for VRGZ, 77.000 euro for VGGM and 106.000 euro for RAV NOG. In addition, a one-off amount of 30.000 euro is estimated for the joint implementation of the software across the three regions. The estimated total contract value over the maximum duration amounts to 1.010.000 euro.
sig_2b2d0dca8c2ef7c1a532.title: Voluntary transparency for AI in the emergency dispatch centre RAV

sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.description: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a complex disease involving interactions among many different cell types, tissues, organs and biological processes. Genetics, the environment, and lifestyle all play a role in disease development and progression. Over the past two decades, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) has supported major T1D research consortia covering basic, translational, and clinical research. Each consortium has focused on different aspects of T1D, such as specific organs, stages of disease or clinical outcomes. Together, these consortia have collected large longitudinal and multimodal datasets using standardized protocols and coordinated studies. While individual consortia have improved our understanding of specific areas, combining their work offers a rare opportunity to see how different biological processes interact to drive T1D development and progression. This integrated view can answer fundamental questions about T1D biology that cannot be answered using individual datasets or studies alone. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now make it possible to integrate these complementary datasets and study T1D across various tissues, disease stages, and biological levels. Building on these resources, NIDDK will support a coordinated, milestone-driven research project to answer fundamental questions about T1D biology and accelerate the development of personalized medicine. The project will combine multimodal human pancreas and clinical datasets to better understand how biological processes interact as T1D develops and progresses. The research will generate new insights into T1D biology, help us understand the different forms and stages of T1D, identify biomarkers, and inform new approaches for disease prevention, intervention, and treatment. To support the research, the project will develop and test advanced multimodal AI models. It will also develop AI-enabled research workflows, new methods to integrate data, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets.
sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.title: Multimodal AI to Accelerate Precision Medicine for Type 1 Diabetes (U01- Clinical Trials Not Allowed)
