sig_2b9474414b35cda9e318.description: For governing bodies to be able to make data-driven decisions, it is necessary to have quality data. Any person, at any time or place, must have the autonomy to find answers to fundamental questions for their work, in an agile and secure manner and based on quality data that allows them to make informed decisions. In many current UIB processes, the serious problems caused by not having information or having low-quality information have become apparent. For example, with various requirements from auditors in monitoring and accreditation processes for official degrees due to not having certain key information; or also the amount of time spent manually cleansing low-quality information that a project of this nature will automate. For all these reasons, the strategic plan 2023-2027 of the University of the Balearic Islands has 3 strategic objectives related to the corporate information factory: - Teaching objective 12: To be able to make sound teaching decisions based on reliable and up-to-date data. - Transfer objective 10: To account to society for activities carried out through the publication of objective indicators. - Management objective 8: To have quality corporate information through the construction of a data factory. The benefits of this solution in efficiency and quality reach a multitude of institutional processes. Some of which are: - Monitoring and accreditation of official degrees. - Implementation of a new quality system based on ANECA's AUDIT programme. - Generation, validation and submission of SIIU files. - Monitoring the execution of the institutional Strategic Plan. - Active transparency, with the web publication of objective data. - Obtaining quality data for participation in university rankings such as CyD, THE Times, Shanghai, THE Impact and GreenMetric. - Automating the acquisition of data for the annual academic report.
sig_2b9474414b35cda9e318.title: Implementation service for an information factory for the University of the Balearic Islands

sig_2b98060f20dc271f5023.description: Naíonra Garbháin was established in 1981 as an early-immersion Irish-language based educational setting for pre-school children in Dún Garbhán and the surrounding areas. Dún Garbhán is a Baile Seirbhíse Gaeltachta (Gaeltacht Service Town). Naíonra Garbháin provides education and childcare services for people from the Gaeltacht who do not have access to housing in An Rinn or An Sean Phobal and who live in the surrounding area. Naíonra Garbháin is managed by a voluntary committee known as Croí na nÓg. As it is located immediately adjacent to the Irish-language based primary school, Scoil Gharbháin, progression from the Naíonra to the primary school is seamless and therefore the Naíonra is an important foundation and integral part of life on the Scoil Gharbháin campus. As the population of the town of Dún Garbháin, and in particular the area adjacent to the Naíonra, continues to grow, Croí na nÓg wishes to ensure that the facilities provided in the town of Dún Garbháin are sufficient to cater for the demand for Irish-language based education for pre-school children in the town. It also wishes to ensure that suitable facilities are available to cater for the demand for Irish-language based pre- and post-school services in the area. The latter is particularly important as a significant number of parents of primary school travel into Dún Garbháin on a daily basis for employment and are likely to avail of such services if they were available. Croí na nÓg have recently purchased lands immediately adjoining the Department of Education and Skills lands upon which Scoil Gharbháin is constructed and wish to ensure that the lands are utilised in the most efficient manner possible to meet the Irish-language based early education and pre/post school service demands of the area. Croí na nÓg wish to appoint a consultant to undertake a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case as envisaged in the Infrastructure Guidelines and the tender documents to improve the range of early-years educational and pre/post school services in the area.
sig_2b98060f20dc271f5023.title: Consultancy Services to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in relation to the provision of Irish-language based early-years (Naíonra) facilities in Dún Gar

sig_2bba206a99678924bef8.description: This notification is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, and its publication does not initiate a procurement procedure. This is a request for information related to market research and preliminary procurement assessment, the purpose of which is to survey solutions and suppliers available on the market to support the planning of a future procurement. Responding to the request for information or expressing interest is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent procurement, nor does it affect a supplier's position in a potential procurement. Suppliers who have expressed interest may be invited to a market dialogue, during which written and/or oral discussions regarding the subject matter of the procurement may take place and draft material related to the procurement may be commented on. The contracting authority shall decide on the implementation method and participants of the market dialogue. The request for information or market dialogue does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request for information or its appendices, and the procurement procedure may also not be carried out at all. No compensation is paid for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. OBJECTIVE AND PRELIMINARY CONTENT OF THE PROCUREMENT The objective of the procurement is to acquire Microsoft CSP licences and supporting Microsoft expert services. In addition, secure communication and backup solutions are included in the procurement. Preliminary sub-areas: - Microsoft CSP licences and backup - Microsoft expert services - Secure communication STRUCTURE AND SCHEDULE OF THE PROCUREMENT The contracting authority reserves the right to refine the scope, structure and schedule of the procurement before the publication of the actual procurement notice. The procurement will be implemented as a joint procurement. Regarding expert services, the objective is to put out to tender several packages and select multiple suppliers. Regarding licences and secure email, the objective is to select one supplier. The estimate for the publication date of the procurement notice is Q3/2026. REGISTRATION FOR MARKET DIALOGUE Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their contact details by email to the address hankinnat@velora.fi no later than 2.3.2026. The message should state at least the company name and business ID (Y-tunnus) as well as the contact person's name, job title, telephone number and email address.

sig_2bc53b8c7a8e147131d9.description: INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE Introduction Vestfold fylkeskommune invites suppliers of systems for processing applications for school transport and for the planning and execution of assisted school transport by taxi and minibus to a market dialogue. The County Municipality wants a market dialogue with suppliers who can offer case processing of applications and/or planning of assisted school transport. The County Municipality is responsible for school transport pursuant to the Education Act and is subject to the Public Procurement Act and Regulations (LOA and FOA). Purpose of the market dialogue The County Municipality is planning to procure new agreements for a system for case processing of applications for school transport. It is also planned to procure a system for the planning and execution of assisted school transport by taxi and minibus. These systems can be supplied separately or in a single delivery. The purpose of the market dialogue is to gain an overview of existing solutions and how they can meet the County Municipality's needs, expectations and requirements for the case processing of applications for school transport, and the planning and execution of school transport. Participation in the market dialogue will not commit either the supplier or the County Municipality with regard to subsequent procurements. The market dialogue is not to be considered part of upcoming procurement processes. Final decisions and choices for the procurement processes have not been made upon publication of the invitation. Practical information about the market dialogue Suppliers are invited to present their services in one-to-one meetings at Vestfold fylkeskommune's premises. The exact time for these meetings will be scheduled after the registration deadline. Execution of the market dialogue The dialogue meetings are planned to be held on 28 May and 29 May. The meetings will be held at Svend Foyns gate 9, 3126 Tønsberg or, at the request of the supplier, as an online meeting using Teams. 1,5 hour of meeting time will be allocated to each supplier meeting. Registration Deadline for registration: 13 May at 12:00. Upon registration, a meeting summons with an agenda for the market dialogue will be sent to the supplier. All suppliers will receive the same agenda. Please provide the company name, name and email address of participants in the market dialogue upon registration, as well as any request for an online meeting. Suppliers will subsequently receive a meeting invitation by email. Registration must be sent by email to: oyvind.hanssen@vestfoldfylke.no Costs The parties are responsible for their own costs associated with the market dialogue. Use of information and confidentiality Information that has emerged in the market dialogue can/will be used in the further work on drafting the requirement specifications. The County Municipality has a duty to prevent others from gaining access to or knowledge of information about technical devices, procedures or operating and business secrets that it would be of competitive importance to keep secret, cf. Section 13 of the Public Administration Act and Section 13 of the Freedom of Information Act

sig_2be3e7e320020b25aa96.description: Provision of application management, project support and further development services for the basic payment transactions component as well as support for the office on the basis of a framework agreement. E-government is a central topic for public administrations and their customers, such as users of electronic services as citizens, commercial enterprises, other authorities and public institutions. For several years, the Free State of Saxony has been providing functionalities for implementing e-government measures in the form of IT applications and IT services with the aid of technical (basic) components. To this end, the Free State uses the central and decentralised technical infrastructures of its SIDI platform and the Saxon Administrative Network (SVN), which are not to be set up multiple times within the administrations of the Free State of Saxony for cost reasons. The BaK ZV (basic payment transactions component) is responsible for the operation and management of ePayBL. This forms the central data hub between an administration's web presentation or web portal, a payment transactions provider and the administration's budget, cash office and accounting system. ePayBL offers Saxon administrations the opportunity to offer their customers (citizens, companies and institutions) electronic processing of payment transactions. ePayBL has provided a technical infrastructure and implemented organisational regulations with which these sometimes very complex payment processes can be mapped. All payment-related interactions (e.g. payment of a fee in the application procedure, payment of an item in the online shop) can be carried out. In addition, ePayBL supports payment monitoring and booking in the administrations' HKR procedure applications. The BaK ZV uses the federal government's tried-and-tested and comprehensively certified payment transactions platform, which has been adapted to Saxon conditions. The Free State of Saxony joined the nationwide developer community for this payment transactions platform. The name of the software is protected under the brand "ePayBL" (ePayment Federal States). The BaK ZV is currently operated within the developer community as ePayBL in version 2.x and 3.x. It is planned to introduce version 4.x in the current year 2026. To this end, a stronger modularisation of the functions of ePayBL into basic functions and extended functions is planned. With the aid of this call for competition, an external service provider is to be found who, on the basis of a framework agreement, provides services for external support regarding, among other things, the following topics: - Supervision and support for the further development of BaK ZV or ePayBL - Support for regularly occurring tasks in the sense of application management of BaK ZV for the SID - Project-related support or advice for the SID - Project-related support or advice in the environment of the ePayBL office or ePayBL developer community - Project-related support for compliance with legal regulations and IT standards
sig_2be3e7e320020b25aa96.title: Framework agreement for application management and project support for the BaK payment transactions component as well as support for the office

sig_2c1677eb90fb1766c40d.description: TfGM are testing the market for a new Content Management System contract to potentially take over from the current contract that they have in place for this service. TfGM has a range of websites and mobile apps whose content is managed by a single CMS. The type of content ranges from rich content pages, mixing text, images, video and downloadable content, to micro-content such as the labels on form fields, and navigation menu links. The main features of the CMS which we use are: • Headless architecture: separating content from presentation, content is delivered via APIs and consumed by our front end websites and app. • Content modelling: creating custom, composable and reusable content types. • Media management: upload and manage image, video and documents. • Content editing: user friendly interface for editing content. • Content preview: see how content will look before it goes live. • Versioning: track changes and enable content editors to revert to earlier versions of content. • Environment management: test and production environments which can be connected to our test and production front end environments. • Developer tools: to make integration and automation easy. This is likely to be a 3+1+1 contract term so a max term of 5 years in the extension is taken up. The current contract ends in March 2026 so any system that is implemented would need to be up and running before this date. Lot 1: .
sig_2c1677eb90fb1766c40d.title: TfGM Content Management System

sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.description: This program will advance scientific community datasets to enable scientific discovery and innovation using artificial intelligence (AI) and other methods. Its goal is to increase the value that can be derived from existing scientific datasets by leveraging novel methods and artificial intelligence (AI). This will unlock new AI-driven insights. It can enable interdisciplinary research. It also enables investigations outside of the original motivation for data collection and analysis. The program seeks to 1) apply AI-based capabilities to feature extraction and metadata generation, and the integration of multiple datasets. 2) Develop robust data pipelines necessary for automated analysis of existing datasets and similar use-cases by AI tools and systems. 3) Augment and/or harmonize existing datasets to better enable use by AI data pipelines and automated analysis. Proposals should address dataset security and integrity. Governance and the process for scientific communities to contribute to the datasets should also be addressed. Proposals are encouraged to leverage existing resources. These may include NSF data platforms , the NSF Integrated Data Systems and Services program , the NSF-led National AI Research Resource , the Genesis Mission platform , or other national infrastructure. NSF is open to exploring partnerships with philanthropy, private industry, or the non-profit sector to support additional proposals or collaborative opportunities that will advance AI-driven scientific discovery through unlocking the value of high-impact scientific datasets. Expanding Participation in STEM, NSF Priorities, and Gold Standard Science: NSF prioritizes cutting-edge discovery science and engineering research, advancing technology and innovation, and creating opportunities for all Americans. NSF has established priorities set forth by Congress, the administration and the NSF director to promote NSF's mission . Proposers should review the list of NSF priorities and are encouraged to align their proposals with them, where appropriate. NSF also expects the highest standards of scientific rigor, integrity and adherence tenets of Gold Standard Science in proposals, as appropriate for the field of science and research modality.
sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.title: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets)

sig_2cabce95d37d16132c9d.description: Currently, within the Personnel Department of ZOL, various HR systems are used that are not or only to a limited extent integrated with each other, which makes maintenance across different systems difficult for our target groups. The functionalities offered today no longer meet current and future HR needs. We therefore want to invest in an integrated HR system with the following characteristics:  Efficiency improvement and process optimisation  Improved employee satisfaction and experience  Strategic advantages for talent management  Data-driven decision-making  Long-term cost savings  Competitive advantage in the healthcare sector  Technologically up to date The contract is divided into 3 lots:  Lot 1 – Talent Acquisition (recruitment and selection)  Lot 2 – Personnel Management  Lot 3 – Talent Experience Platform (TXP) Investing in an integrated HR system is not a cost item, but a strategic step to support ZOL's operational efficiency, employee satisfaction and organisational goals. It not only helps to address current HR challenges, but also prepares the hospital for future growth and complexity. The contract will be described in further detail in the second phase of the award procedure, namely the award phase.  Job application request  Vacancy management  Candidate management  Application process and Workflow Management  Interview and selection management  Appointment and onboarding  Integrations and automation  Compliance and security  Reporting and analytics; This lot is considered the master of personnel data. Personnel data means data from various target groups such as employees, doctors, students, volunteers, retirees, etc. The HR department (and persons outside HR with specific rights) must be able to maintain and feed this modular input box without extensive technical knowledge.  Employee data management  Onboarding/offboarding  Contract and role management  Employee Self-Service (ESS)  Manager Self-Service (MSS)  Document management  Time and attendance management  Compensation management  Cost centres  Org chart  Portfolio;  HR Dashboard (ESS, MSS and HR SS)  Learning Management System  Talent and skills management  Performance management

sig_2cb16744c7b4fcced9e8.description: The Norwegian Institute of Marine Research, Research Station Matre, shall replace the existing programmable logical control units (PLCs) in the current control plant/operations control plant. The procurement includes the delivery and installation of the necessary PLC and hardware components, as well as programming, configuration, integration, testing, verification and commissioning of the new PLCs. The work shall be carried out gradually, without the entire plant being taken out of operation, and with the necessary cooperation between the existing and new PLSs in the transition period. The delivery shall be integrated with the existing control, alarm, history and security functions and shall ensure the continued stable and safe operation of four trial departments at the research station. The facility is used for research and trial activities where continuous regulation and monitoring of, among other things, water level, water quantity, temperature, oxygen level, salinity, alarms and safety functions are crucial for biological safety, research results and animal welfare. The contract applies from the signing of the contract to replacing, integration, testing, verification and commissioning of the new PLCs have been carried out and approved by the Norwegian Institute of Marine Research. The planned completion date is 31 December 2027. Any objections or questions are to be sent to the jannicke.bergesen.clarke@hi.no [jannicke.bergesen.clarke@hi.no] by 20.09.2026, 23.59.
sig_2cb16744c7b4fcced9e8.title: Intention notice - Replacement of existing PLCs at matre research station.

Amendment 01 _ AOI 01 AOI-2025_01 - Solicitation Request: CFC SAIO/PKO is soliciting white papers on the effort(s) identifed as Area(s) of Interest (AOIs) to this solicitation. Type of Contract: This is a Fixed-Price type contract IAW FAR Part 12 and Part 35. Limitation: This acquisition is set aside for small business. Anticipated Award: Government reserves the right to award all, some, or none of the proposed solutions. Classified Information: Offerors are encouraged to submit unclassified White Papers to simplify and expedite reviews and response by the Government. Description The United States Space Force (USSF), through the Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)to solicit innovative commercial solutions that enhance Space Domain Awareness (SDA)capabilities. This CSO is authorized under DFARS 212.70and is designed to identify and acquire innovative technologies, products, and services that support the USSF's warfighting missions. The CSO provides a flexible, enterprise-wide acquisition mechanism to address SDA mission challenges through advanced software engineering, data analytics, and other innovative approaches. Submissions will be evaluated under a multi-phase process to ensure alignment with mission needs and operational priorities. Scope of the CSO The CSO seeks solutions that address the following Space Domain Awareness (SDA)mission challenges: Detecting, characterizing, and predicting activities in the space domain. Enhancing the accuracy and timeliness of SDA data. Supporting emerging SDA missions through innovative technologies. Specific Areas of Interest (AOIs) will be issued under this CSO to define technical focus areas, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria. Each AOI will be posted as a standalone solicitation module under this CSO. Submission Process The CSO employs a three-phase submission process: Phase I – White Paper and PowerPoint Briefing Offerors must submit a PowerPoint briefing (including a Quad Chart) and a White Paper summarizing their proposed solution. Submissions must align with the specific AOI requirements. Phase II – Pitch Session (Optional) Selected Offerors may be invited to present their proposed solution in greater depth during a virtual or in-person pitch session. Phase III – Full Proposal Offerors invited to Phase III must submit a complete proposal package, including a Technical Proposal, Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Price Proposal. The Government reserves the right to proceed directly from Phase I to Phase III. Key Information Security Requirements: Phase I submissions must be unclassified. Subsequent phases may require higher classification levels, as specified in the AOI and any draft or final DD Form 254. Foreign Participation: Restricted to U.S. entities due to export control and national security considerations. Cybersecurity Compliance: Offerors must comply with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC 2.0 requirements. How to Respond Interested Offerors must monitor SAM.gov for AOI-specific postings under this CSO. Each AOI will include detailed submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and deadlines. Submissions must comply with the formats and requirements outlined in the CSO and the applicable AOI. For general inquiries, contact the SAIO CSO Contracting Officer at SAIO.SDA.CSO@spaceforce.mil. Use the subject line: "SDA CSO – General Question(s)". Disclaimer This CSO does not obligate the Government to award a contract, nor does it commit the Government to pay for any costs incurred in the preparation and submission of responses. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the proposals received under this CSO.

Stream C - A.3 Enterprise Resource Planning Programmer Analyst (LEVEL 3) Objective: The objective is to implement Warehouse Management in CSC’s Oracle IFMMS system in order to replace the existing two legacy systems and to have an integrated solution that will be supported from a functional and technical perspective; using the existing and internal knowledge base to best manage and support the business processes at both the Laval National Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse sites. Enhancing IFMMS with advanced warehouse management functionality, will provide industry best practices in CSC and CORCAN’s supply chain management process through efficiencies, innovation, and consolidation of three software applications into one. The solution will create efficiencies in business processes and increase accuracy in the supply chain process through tracking all inputs and outputs within one system. Functional and technical expertise are required for the implementation, configuration and delivery of the Warehouse Management functionality in IFMMS, which includes enhancements to the Inventory Management and order Management modules. Scope: The Warehouse Management solution must effectively support both the Laval Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse. By enhancing functionality within Oracle EBS to include Warehouse Management, and potentially include Oracle’s Mobile Supply Chain Applications (MSCA), and by enhancing Oracle EBS modules such as Inventory Management and Order Management this will enable users at both locations to: a) Accurately manage and process physical goods; b) Increase the accuracy of inventory counts for costing, manufacturing, and shipment of goods,; c) Properly reconcile and integrate billing, pricing, and returns related to goods sold, and d) Establish a consistent business process and source of truth for users at both locations. This transformation will provide both the Laval Depot and the CORCAN Warehouse with an integrated solution that is more automated and streamlined, thus reducing inventory reconciliation issues, and allowing for more accurate and timely processing of orders. The solution must: a. Be integrated (and not interfaced) with the existing Oracle EBS V12.2 ERP system. b. Be compatible with CSC current technology infrastructure. c. Be upgradable at regular intervals to keep current with industry standards, as well as the Government of Canada standards through Shared Services Canada (SSC). d. Adhere to Treasury Board Secretariat directives for financial systems.. e. Utilize and implement industry standard “best-practices.” f. Limit costly customizations to those that are required either by external legislation or internal Commissioner’s directives. g. Be able to easily enter orders, process shipments, and reconcile all transactions. There should be few to no inventory discrepancies. This will improve reporting capabilities and facilitate accurate and consistent responses to Access to Information and Privacy requests (ATIP). sig_2cd2e99a3f8a97ad3900.description: The scope of the contract includes the execution of activities related to the Cyber Incident Monitoring and Response Centre at the State Agency for National Security, where a cybersecurity management system for critical systems of strategic sites has been implemented. By holding this public procurement, its functionalities will be expanded and developed by integrating information from external sources and threat intelligence sharing platforms regarding hacker groups, attacks, threats, methods used, alerts for various events and others in order to increase analytical capabilities and support processes and decisions for the protection and prevention of critical systems in strategic sites. Licences for the established information system will be supplied. To guarantee technological and functional compatibility and the smooth operation of the implemented solutions with the available resources in the operational centre, hardware and software support for the infrastructure will be provided. In order to minimise operational risks and increase the reliability of IT systems, this public procurement also requires the provision of expert services to ensure normal operation, operational support and sustainable management of the environment. The type and quantities of software and hardware products, along with a detailed description of the activities for expanding and developing the functionalities of the cybersecurity management system for critical systems of strategic sites, are contained in the Technical Specification with a classification level of 'Secret' pursuant to item 14 of Section II of Annex No 1 to Article 25 in conjunction with Article 28, paragraph 2, item 2 and § 1, item 13, item 14 and item 15, letter 'b' of the Additional Provisions of the Classified Information Protection Act.
sig_2cd2e99a3f8a97ad3900.title: Delivery and integration of an extension to the system ensuring the cybersecurity management activities for critical systems of strategic sites

sig_2ce0aa5f2cd0462c0226.description: North Northamptonshire Council (here after referred to as the 'The Council') was formed in 2021 and is one of the largest unitary councils in the country. The council covers Corby, East Northamptonshire, Kettering, and Wellingborough districts. The Council receives a high volume of noise complaints relating to residential and commercial premises and are seeking clarity on market appetite for the provision of a cloud-based noise/nuisance reporting application and case management portal to ensure measures are in place to assist the Council to assess and investigate noise complaints. This provision would also be required to enable our residents/users to make noise recordings from 30 - 90 seconds, along with video and photographs and the Council to receive/download recordings and associated data. The Council would like to understand which suppliers are able to provide this provision based on the following overview of the Councils minimum mandatory requirements: Mobile App • User/residents download for free and record audio and video evidence. The council do not wish for any advertisement to be part of this provision. • Workload control by user invite only • User/Resident can submit evidence directly to the Council • Supports GPS validation for accurate tracking • Ability to bypass smartphone noise suppression • In-app messaging/notifications • Accessible via Apple App store and Google Play Case Portal • Evidence collected is securely stored, meeting data protection requirements • Validated tamper resistant recordings, which have been proven to be admissible as evidence in court, with a verified audit trail, exportable for legal proceedings • Supports the Council to triage complaints • Enables multi-agency collaboration • Provide analytics on data held and AI-supported safeguarding • Notifications supported by Microsoft outlook Any potential provider looking to respond to this 'expression of interest' must be able to deliver the above requirements from day one (1), at this time the Council would not be looking to work collaboratively with a potential provider or develop software. If you believe your organisation can provide this service based on the mandatory requirements, please contact the Council demonstrating how you can meet the requirements and, if applicable, identify any relevant framework solutions, compliant with the Public Contract Regulations/Procurement Act 2023, to potential support the Council's route to market. This is an information gathering exercise only to help us understand what options are available and establish a market appetite. The Authority will not commit or be influenced by this information at this stage. Lot 1: .
sig_2ce0aa5f2cd0462c0226.title: North Northamptonshire Council call for Expressions of Interest (EOI) for the Provision of a Noise App

sig_2cff661070ea07ad63d3.description: The subject of the procurement was a ready-to-use, operational AI-based analytics service package that combines data collected from existing security systems and produces real-time and predictive information based on it for security situation management. The objective is for the procured solution to enable: • A real-time situational picture of the security situation of buildings and premises • Predictive analytics for identifying security threats and anomalies • AI-based decision support and automated proposed measures that support security management and operational response See appendix: "Description of the subject of the procurement". The subject of the procurement and the requirements concerning it were described in detail in the call for tenders and its appendices. The contracting authority will select one (1) supplier with which it will enter into an agreement. The procurement contract will be used solely by Istekki Oy and the parties to the resulting contract will be solely Istekki Oy and the selected Supplier. For the avoidance of doubt, Istekki's customers are not parties to this procurement procedure or the procurement contract concluded on the basis of it. The procurement quantities presented in the call for tenders were estimates, and the contract does not constitute a volume purchase obligation for the contracting authority.
sig_2cff661070ea07ad63d3.title: AI-based situational picture and analytics service for security

sig_2d24e1899e0037659856.description: As part of a market exploration / RFI (Request for Information) for the selection of a central, bank-wide CRM standard software, Deutsche Bundesbank intends to make an initial assessment of the system compatibility of solutions available on the market with the functional, technical and regulatory requirements. The aim in particular is to identify a solution that provides a uniform, standardised data model for contacts, processes and activities as well as a central, cross-departmental customer and process file. Comprehensive standard functionalities, flexible customising options, in particular through low-code/no-code functionalities, and the possibility of integrating existing systems are expected. In addition, the solution is intended to automate processes, reduce media discontinuities and enable efficiency gains and a resource-saving IT support structure. A cloud solution is preferred. However, due to potential protection needs and sovereignty considerations, an on-premises option must also be provided. For a cloud solution, EU hosting is mandatory. In addition, all relevant data protection and compliance requirements must be met. The future viability of the system, particularly with regard to AI technologies, must also be ensured. Participation in the RFI takes place on the basis of a questionnaire. The essential points regarding the procedure are listed below: 1. Providers can contact CRM@bundesbank.de via the functional email address by 17 July and request the questionnaire. 2. The questionnaire must be answered within two weeks. 3. The answers must be returned to Deutsche Bundesbank no later than 31 July. 4. The initial assessment of system compatibility with the aforementioned requirements will be carried out on the basis of the submitted answers to the questionnaire. 5. Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to subsequently conduct clarification and concretisation discussions with the providers on the basis of the files. 6. The assessment will focus in particular on the functional and technical requirements for a central CRM standard software, the mapping of a standardised data model, the central customer and process file, integration capability, automation options, reduction of media discontinuities, customising options and low-code/no-code functionalities. 7. In addition, requirements regarding data protection, compliance, EU hosting for cloud solutions, possible on-premises provision and the future viability of the solution, particularly with regard to AI technologies, will be taken into account. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and does not constitute either an offer or an invitation to treat. The implementation of a procurement procedure, including with a different scope of services, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences for the participating company (neither preference nor disadvantage) in the context of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to obtain knowledge from the results of the market exploration.
sig_2d24e1899e0037659856.title: Market exploration: CRM tool for Deutsche Bundesbank

sig_2d2dd630c88b4e61bbc5.description: The College of Policing is seeking information from suppliers to better understand the market capabilities and potential solutions for developing a national Lessons Learned database. This initiative follows the government's announcement in October 2024 that the College will create a system to capture, integrate and share learning arising from investigations into deaths or serious injury (DSI) following police contact or pursuits. Through this RFI, the College aims to explore secure database solutions that integrate with public-facing websites. We are also seeking to understand suppliers' capabilities in evaluating and developing AI tools and models for two purposes: first, to generate accurate Incident Learning Summaries (ILS) that describe official reports into death and serious injury cases; and second, to support automated data ingestion that enables resources on specific websites (such as coroners reports) to be scraped, relevant data to be transformed, validated and imported automatically into the database, reducing the need for manual entry. These requirements are detailed further below. This RFI is an information gathering exercise, not a formal tender. Supplier responses will help refine the College's requirements and procurement approach for a future tender. Lot 1: .
sig_2d2dd630c88b4e61bbc5.title: Provision of Database for Deaths and Serious Injury

sig_2d2fe4d469eae77b6d37.description: The University is undertaking discovery work under the External Digital Experience (EDE) Programme. This RFI is intended to test the market before any formal procurement decision is made. It is not a tender and it does not commit the University to procure a solution or to follow a particular route. The purpose of this RFI is to gather supplier perspectives on a future Content Management System (CMS) and the implementation, migration, governance and operating model considerations that would support a more coherent external digital experience. The RFI is CMS-only. The University is not seeking CRM supplier proposals through this exercise. CRM should only be referenced where it relates to CMS integration, enquiry/form hand-off, campaign source tracking, consent capture, student journey data, or future interoperability. This RFI is intended to help the University: • understand credible CMS options available in the market, including traditional, headless, hybrid, composable or DXP-aligned approaches • test assumptions from CMS discovery, the EDE Strategy and the CMS Discovery Checklist • understand how suppliers would support content governance, structured content, publishing workflows, accessibility, IA, SEO, internal search, migration and editor experience • understand how a CMS could integrate with CRM and other systems without making CRM part of this RFI • obtain indicative views on delivery approach, sequencing, risks, University-side resourcing and cost drivers; • inform any subsequent CMS business case, procurement strategy, RFP/tender documentation and evaluation criteria. The University of Manchester no longer meets the criteria of a 'body governed by public law' and is therefore not considered a contracting authority for the purposes of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and/or any replacement legislation. As a result, the University of Manchester will no longer be subject to the regime contained in The Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and/or any replacement legislation with effect from 1 August 2023. However, as an institution founded for the public good, an exempt charity and an organization in receipt of public funds, the University has a duty to manage expenditure in an appropriate manner and aims to deliver value for money across its non-pay spend by adhering to good procurement practice. Information, formalities and necessary requirements to be met will be set out in the RFI document, all of which are freely available via the University's procurement portal In-Tend - https://in-tendhost.co.uk/manchesteruniversity
sig_2d2fe4d469eae77b6d37.title: Request for Information - External Digital Experience: CMS Discovery - 2026-3565-RFI-CMS Disc-DL-PST

sig_2d36f3469676bf64cc3b.description: The selection guide explains the selection phase of the contract "MAINTENANCE and UPGRADE OF THE ODOO ERP AT SPI". By means of this, the contracting authority invites interested parties to submit a request to participate in this contract. This guide aims to select the candidates who will be invited to submit a tender in the second phase of the award procedure, on the basis of the specifications which will only be sent to the selected candidates. The sole objective of the selection guide is to offer interested candidates the opportunity to submit a request to participate without an obligation of exhaustiveness. The contracting authority reserves the right to derogate from the provisions of this selection guide during the procedure to the extent that this does not undermine the principles of transparency, objectivity and equal treatment. The contracting authority will only use this right to the extent that it does not entail any distortion of competition or any discrimination against candidates. To this end, candidates will be explicitly informed of any modification whatsoever (derogation, adaptation or addition). This selection guide forms an integral part of the contract documents. "Contract documents" means the documents applicable to the contract, including all additional documents and other documents to which they refer. A detailed description of the procedure is available in these specifications. Nevertheless, for the sake of clarity, here is a diagram outlining the main steps of the procedure (4 in total). The first step (in blue) consists of the opening of the contract, the submission of applications by tenderers as well as the ON/OFF selection. The ON/OFF selection indicates that either the tenderer's application complies with the selection criteria as defined in these specifications (and in this case, they will be invited to submit their tender for the POC) or the tenderer does not comply with one or more selection criteria and in this case, their application will not be selected. The second step (in green) consists of the submission of tenders for the POC by the tenderers, the analysis by SPI of the tenders received as well as the selection of a certain number of tenderers (maximum 3) on the basis of the criteria set out in these specifications (cf. the chapter on the POC). Tenderers whose tender has been selected will be invited to develop the POC in co-construction with SPI. The co-construction as well as the selection of 2 tenderers form part of the 3th step (in orange). Following the completion of the POCs, SPI will select 2 tenderers who will be invited to submit their tender for the specifications relating to the MAINTENANCE OF THE ODOO ERP. Tenders which will also be analysed by SPI in order to select the final partner (step in red). Please note that this diagram is a summary of the procedure with the objective of outlining the main steps of this procedure. This diagram in no way replaces the procedure described in detail in these specifications, which therefore takes precedence over this summary.

sig_2d3c0ee9ffdbb46ff944.description: This request for information is intended to examine questions and price estimates related to the procurement of a dictation transcription service and speech recognition solution for use in pathology by Fimlab Laboratoriot Oy (hereinafter referred to as "Fimlab" or the "contracting authority"). This is not a contract notice or a call for competition, but rather a request for information for a market survey, the objective of which is to obtain comprehensive additional information regarding the planned procurement so that any future tendering procedure can be carried out as appropriately as possible, taking into account the latest technologies and market trends. Fimlab invites interested suppliers to participate in the market survey and requests your views regarding the planned procurement. Fimlab does not bind itself to carry out the procurement that is the subject of the request for information. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The procurement would potentially consist of the following parts: 1) Dictation transcription service 2) Speech recognition solution The contracting authority will evaluate the division of the procurement into parts based on suppliers' responses. Dictations for the dictation transcription service and the speech recognition solution are divided into three categories by length: Short: under 499 characters Medium: 500–1500 characters Long: over 1501 characters. DICTATION TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE In the dictation transcription service, a digital dictation recorded by a healthcare professional in audio file format in text format is transcribed into text format and saved in Fimlab's IT management systems using an encrypted remote connection. The dictation transcription service must include a cloud-based (SaaS) dictation management system and associated workstation and mobile applications used for recording dictation. The dictation transcription service will be integrated into Fimlab's LIS (Whitelake Software Point's LabVantage Medical Suite). The dictation transcription service must be provided in Finnish and Swedish. The dictation transcription service must recognise the medical terminology and vocabulary used in specialised medical care as well as foreign words related to the context. The dictation transcription service must be provided on weekdays (Mon-Fri) between 08:00-18:00 according to Fimlab's needs. The dictation system must be available 24/7. Users of the dictation transcription service are employees of the pathology unit, with pathology physicians as the primary users. Not all physicians may necessarily start using the service immediately at the deployment stage, but they must have the opportunity to join as users of the service later. The service must include maintenance, technical support, user support and a sufficient number of user licences related to the use of the dictation system and the provision of the transcription service. Approximately 50 000 - 60 000 reports are routed to the transcription service annually. SPEECH RECOGNITION SOLUTION The speech recognition solution is procured as a cloud service (SaaS service), and the procurement also includes deployment, user and support services. The speech recognition solution must include real-time direct speech recognition in Finnish and Swedish. The speech recognition application must produce text content that is easily transferable to the target system. The speech recognition application must have medical vocabulary capabilities. The application will not be integrated or connected to existing Fimlab IT systems. The speech recognition solution must operate as an application installed on users' desktops. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Companies interested in the procurement are requested to answer the questions attached to the request for information ("Questions for the Request for Information") and submit the completed attachment via the Tender Service Portal. You may submit your response in Finnish or English in a free-form manner (in writing). Your responses will be utilised in the preparation of the procurement and in finalising the contract notice and its attachments. All responses will be treated confidentially. Information will not be shared with other suppliers without written consent to disclose the information. Please follow the numbering of the questions. Also clearly indicate trade secrets or confidential information. The procurement parts described above are Fimlab's preliminary views. We would gladly hear if you have alternative solutions to offer. Responding to the request for information does not affect a potential tenderer's position in the actual tendering procedure. No compensation is paid to those who responded to the request for information for their participation. If the contracting authority deems it necessary, it is possible that the contracting authority will continue supplier-specific discussions with a maximum of 5 suppliers.
sig_2d3c0ee9ffdbb46ff944.title: Market consultation - Information request: Dictation transcription service and speech recognition solution

sig_2d596d7159c49c3ca004.description: Lumero Educational Trust (formerly Inicio Educational Trust) – Financial Management Software Tender There are 12 schools in the Lumero Educational Trust family – 4 secondary schools and 8 primary schools, united by a shared commitment to transforming lives through exceptional education. Our schools vary in size and have a combined student numbers of 7,429 in the school census of October 2025, with approximately 950 staff. We are committed to excellence, having great aspirations for our children and young people, and encouraging them to seek out and take hold of opportunities. Our drive for excellence is supported by our collaboration, both between our schools and with our excellent support service providers. Further information regarding the Trust can be obtained here: https://www.iniciotrust.org/ Tender information: This tender is for the provision of financial management software to the Inicio Educational Trust The contract term being tendered is for three years, 1st September 2026 – 31st August 2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31st August 2031. Key requirements are: a single contract across the thirteen entities (12 schools and the Trust), provision of the necessary software to meet our technical requirements and the provision of a user-accessible help desk, portal and remote access within agreed hours. The Trust requires a completely cloud based finance system solution compatible with both Microsoft and Google. The solution must be DFE Chart of Accounts compliant, have comprehensive financial transaction, search capability, transaction and journal capability, with seamless links between finance and budgeting modules. The Trust is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender, rather they are keen to secure ‘best value’. The trust seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver both a cutting edge solution and the highest levels of support at all times. Competitive Flexible Procedure This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 50% price, 25% technical capability and 25% support. Value of contract: The annual value of the current contract is £53,000 Therefore the value of this contract is £265,000 Additional requirements and information: •The Trust has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurances of £5 million •The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £200,000 •The services are currently provided by Access Education and Iris PS Financials. •Please note this is a growing Trust and any other schools that may join the Trust during the tenure of this new contract may, at the Trust’s discretion, be added to this contract. •The client reserves the right not to appoint in conclusion of this project. For more information about this opportunity, please visit the Delta eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Kent:-Software-package-and-information-systems./F53PW4QSGH To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/F53PW4QSGH Lot 1: .

sig_2d684752d8ef40c76e5f.description: Supply of chamber alarm devices and operating software and telecommunication devices for district heating network monitoring Lot LOT-0001: Chamber alarm devices. Approximately 900 district heating chambers are installed in the Hamburg urban area. The water level in these chambers is monitored by sensors and transmitted via a radio network to a server. The subject of this enquiry is, on the one hand, the supply of an alarm and transmission unit for connecting sensors and for transmitting messages via various telecommunication paths. The system comprises alarm device(s), transmission unit, required software as well as the interface technology necessary for operation. Furthermore, the enquiry comprises the supply and installation of a telecommunication device for continuous leakage monitoring/location of buried pre-insulated pipe (KMR). The telecommunication devices are to be offered in 3 different designs. The first variant is in an IP66 housing, the second variant is without housing and the third variant is in a housing, battery-operated. The device messages must be transmitted via the same software/retrieval platform as the alarm and transmission unit.

The scope of the contract includes the provision of the following additional licences: - Cisco Unified Communication Manager (CUCM) Enhanced Users: NU On-Premises Calling Enhanced, with product number: A-FLEX-NUPL-E - 20 numbers; - Cisco Unified Contact Center Express (UCCX) Premium Users: On-Premises UCCX Premium Concurrent Agent, with product number: A-FLEX-CCX-P-C - 10 numbers; - CARIN user licence 365 Edition 11.0 Channel licence with software maintenance, with product number: CARIN-365-110-LIC - 14 numbers; - Microsoft Dynamics user licences 365 Team Members SLng LSA OLV NL 1Y Aq Y3 AP DCAL, with product number: EMJ-00244 - 10 numbers. The additional licences provided must come with standard software support, including: • all included updates and new versions up to the latest features and functionality of the respective product for the duration of the support; • all included add-ons available for the respective product for the duration of the support; • all included fixes (Fixes & Patches, etc.) available for the respective product for the duration of the support. *** *** *** The deadline for providing the licences is up to 15 working days, starting from the date of receipt of a written notification sent by the Contracting Authority to the Contractor regarding secured financing under the contract and the submission by the Contractor of the specified performance bond, in compliance with the terms of the draft contract. The duration of the secured right of use and maintenance of the licences is up to 31.01.2027 , starting from the date of provision. *** *** *** In the event that they are not the manufacturer, the tenderer in the public procurement must be duly authorised by the manufacturer or its official representative for the right of distribution/delivery of the offered software products under item 1 and item 2 of Table No 1 from the Contracting Authority's Technical Specification on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria. The tenderer proves their compliance with the set requirement by attaching an authorisation letter or another equivalent document issued by the manufacturer or its official representative in Bulgarian or accompanied by a translation into Bulgarian in their Technical Proposal. In cases where the Tenderer submits an authorisation letter from an official representative of the manufacturer (or an equivalent document), the bid must also include an authorisation letter issued by the manufacturer (or an equivalent document in Bulgarian or accompanied by a translation into Bulgarian), which empowers the official representative of the manufacturer to grant authorisation to third parties. *** *** *** The set requirement for authorisation at the stage of submitting bids is justified by the subject matter of the contract and represents a guarantee for its timely and high-quality execution. In the event that a contractor is chosen who is refused authorisation by the manufacturer, this may lead to a delay in the execution of the public contract, as well as to its termination. According to the conclusions of the Supreme Administrative Court, "the requirement for authorisation in itself is not restrictive, insofar as it is a guarantee of the quality and reliability of the activity carried out. In standard commercial practice, authorisation takes place on the basis of a contract, which can be directly with the manufacturer or with another economic entity authorised to grant authorisation on behalf of the manufacturer" (Decision No 10859 of 27.10.2021 of the SAC on administrative case No 6546/2021 , VII Division). In the documentation, the condition for authorisation is set broadly, i.e. it is not restricted solely to the equipment manufacturer, but also to any official representative of theirs. General authorisation is required, rather than for a specific procedure, and an opportunity is provided for any interested tenderer – partner, regardless of whether they are a Bulgarian or foreign entity, to submit a bid, with the opportunity provided to prove the aforementioned circumstance both with an authorisation letter and with any other equivalent document that certifies compliance with the set requirement.

sig_2d9632169b86508efd34.description: Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) for Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust Lot 1: . Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to procure an Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) solution to support clinical documentation across a range of services and care settings. The solution should enable clinicians to capture consultations and generate structured clinical outputs including but not limited to documentation, clinical record notes, summaries, and correspondence, while integrating seamlessly into existing clinical workflows and digital systems. The aim is to reduce administrative burden and support more meaningful patient interactions, improving the overall patient experience through more engaged consultations, higher quality documentation, reduced errors, improved continuity of care, and shorter turnaround times for clinic letters and updates. It should also enable clinicians to spend more time focusing on the patient, while maintaining high standards of clinical safety, transparency, and documentation quality. The solution must support use across a range of real-world clinical environments, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, and community settings, where factors such as background noise, shared spaces, and variable connectivity may impact performance. The solution must also support consultations involving third parties (e.g. carers, family members, or interpreters), ensuring accurate capture, speaker differentiation, and appropriate inclusion within the output. The contract will be for 2 years with optional extensions for two more years. The procurement will be undertaken using the Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) RM6200. If you wish to register on this DPS you can find out how to do so here: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6200?nav=0 Please note that all bidders for this requirement must be certified under NHS England's Ambient Voice Technology Self-Certified Supplier Registry. Details can be found here: https://digital.nhs.uk/services/ambient-scribing/ambient-voice-technology-self-certified-supplier-registry. Additional information: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust intends to create a DPS supplier shortlist on 13th October 2026 with the intention of issuing a capability assessment on 14th October 2026, to be returned by 21st October 2026. The intention is for the tender documents to be issued on 10th November 2026 to those bidders who have met the capability assessment requirements. Berkshire Healthcare reserves the right to amend these dates.

sig_2dc27978aa84192b7559.description: Istekki Oy (hereinafter also the Subscriber) requested tenders for the procurement of a comprehensive risk management system and its maintenance services. The system was intended to be delivered as a SaaS service under an open-ended contract. The system to be procured was to be a solution focused on risk management that supports the company's overall risk management and its various process stages. The implementation of the system was planned to start no later than 4.1.2027. The system was to be off-the-shelf software with subscriber-specific customisation. The procurement included services related to the use of the system, such as user training, necessary customisations, and technical and content support. More detailed requirements for the subject of the procurement were found in Annex 3, Requirement Specification. The Subscriber's risk management is based on the international ISO 31000 standard. Risks refer to both threats and opportunities, and the risk management process consists of risk identification, assessment and management, as well as compliance assessment. The system was to support this whole by offering versatile functions for different purposes so that risk management can be implemented comprehensively and systematically. The subject of the procurement was a risk management system and its interfaces with other systems, a delivery project (including, among other things, migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support service, separately ordered expert services, and customer service. It was to be possible to carry out further development on the system to be procured during the contract period. The procurement was sought as a single entity, and one comprehensive supplier was sought for the system. In the procurement procedure concerning the procurement of the risk management system, one acceptable tender was received, which was too expensive in relation to the funds reserved for the procurement. The funds reserved by the contracting entity for the procurement are not sufficient for the implementation of the procurement. In addition, because the contracting entity received only one (1) acceptable tender, genuine competition did not arise in the procurement procedure, and the contracting entity has not had the opportunity to assess the market-based nature of the tender in a sufficient manner.

sig_2df78301deded8cd8c31.description: Measurement and Analysis Tool for News Visibility in the Google Ecosystem (RFI) OBJECT OF THE RFI Yleisradio Oy (later “Yle”) is preparing a public tender of measurement and analysis tool for news visibility in the Google Ecosystem. This request for information is aimed to enter discourse with interested parties, and gather information for tender purposes. The object of the procurement is an analytics tool that measures and reports news visibility in the Google ecosystem in Finland in the Finnish language in real-time (with an option additionally for the Swedish language in Finland). Yle aims to enhance the speed and relevance of its news operations and improve event planning. Google's ecosystem* and its services are widely used in Finland at a national level, and its impact on the discoverability and reach of content and services is significant. The goal of the procurement is to obtain a SaaS solution which provides clear and up-to-date picture of the news topics being searched within Google search engine ecosystem, the emerging news topics, and how our organization compares to other news outlets in terms of news visibility. *By Google news ecosystem, we mean features where news/articles can appear (Google search results, Google Top Stories, Google News, Google Discover) Please view the annexes attached to this RFI for further information: Annex 1: The objective of the procurement_DRAFT Annex2: Q&A Measurement and Analysis Tool for News Visibility in the Google Ecosystem INTERESTED? If you are interested, we kindly ask you to answer our questions in the Annex 2 and return them at the latest 26.2.2026 at 12:00 Finnish time (EET) via email to tarjoukset.yle@yle.fi. In your response, please ensure to include also the following information: 1. A short company presentation 2. Description of the solution you provide 3. General terms and conditions, including data protection agreement and service level agreement (if there is one, alternatively service levels), of your company.

The subject matter of this procurement is the signature of a Framework Agreement establishing the terms, conditions and the legal, financial, technical and administrative framework for the award of subsequent contracts, in order for tenderers to provide the services described in the specification, namely the technical and economic documentation necessary and mandatory for carrying out the investments targeted by the contracting authority. The duration of subsequent contracts concluded during the validity period of the framework agreement may exceed the duration of the framework agreement and shall extend until the complete completion of the activities forming their subject matter, taking into account any forms of extension, guarantee period, defect remediation, etc. The description of the services is detailed in the specification, which contains all the information necessary for drawing up the tender. The subject matter of this procurement is the provision of design services consisting of: technical expertise, energy audit and initial energy performance certificate, intervention works approval documentation, feasibility study, detailed urban planning scheme, documentation for obtaining the approvals required in the urbanism certificate and the technical documentation for authorising construction works, technical design and execution details, technical assistance, energy performance certificate upon completion of the works and the designer's viewpoint and consultancy. The general objective of the framework agreement is to improve living conditions for citizens through the continuation and/or implementation of large-scale investments; prior to launching the investments, the contracting authority/authorities must contract services for drawing up technical and economic documentation. The Contracting Authority intends to adopt measures that will lead to an improvement in the living standard, measures that will require extensive construction works for new facilities, interventions, rehabilitation, modernisation and development of infrastructure and buildings. The construction works for which the procurement of technical and economic documentation preparation services is intended are classified into 6 main investment directions: · Modernisation and development of basic urban infrastructure; · Environmental protection and ecological management of the territory at sector level; · Improvement of housing quality at the intervention area level; · "Smart" solutions for the benefit of the urban community; · Support for the existing business environment; · Development of urban tourism. The estimated value of the largest subsequent contract: 87.426.000 lei The number of days before the deadline for submitting tenders by which clarifications may be requested: 18 days. Clarifications requested after this deadline will no longer be taken into account. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification / additional information on the 11-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. Design services for existing buildings, extensions, demolitions and new buildings, modernisation of installation systems by using renewable energy sources. The technical and economic documentation to be produced must be such as to lead to the achievement of the investment objectives, as described in the annex to the specification. Estimates of the minimum and maximum quantities that could be requested during the entire framework agreement and of those that could form the subject of a single subsequent contract among those to be awarded during the Framework Agreement can be found in the annex to the specification. Modification of the framework agreement/public procurement contract during its validity period may be carried out under the conditions provided for in Article 221 of Law No 98/2016 and the provisions within the ANAP Instruction No 1/2021. Given that the procurement documents contain a minimum set of specific information regarding estimates of the minimum and maximum quantities that could be requested during the entire framework agreement, as well as estimates of the minimum and maximum quantities that could form the subject of a single subsequent contract among those to be awarded during the framework agreement, we emphasise that these minimum and maximum quantities that the contracting authority initially sets in the procurement documents and subsequently in the framework agreement represent estimates of quantities that could be requested during the entire framework agreement and not the exact quantities that will be procured, the latter being able to be smaller, equal, or larger compared to the estimated ones, depending on the actual needs of the contracting authority. The Promising Purchaser reserves the right/option to supplement the quantity estimated at the level of the procurement documents by up to a maximum of 50% of the maximum quantity for the framework agreement/subsequent contract, for each category of services individually. The price of items to be additionally procured based on the review clause shall be that from the financial proposal underlying the framework agreement (adjusted as appropriate, according to the adjustment formula), the period of time during which this option may be used by the Promising Purchaser: throughout the validity period of the framework agreement/subsequent contract. The low-value modification provided for in Article 221 paragraph (1), letter f) of Law No 98/2016 is treated and calculated separately from the modification based on Article 221 paragraph (1), letter a) of Law No 98/2016". During the implementation period of the framework agreement, the conclusion of subsequent contracts shall be made under the condition of the allocation of budget credits for this purpose, with signing being carried out in compliance with the provisions regarding the commitment of expenditure from budgets falling under the legislation on public finances.

Subsequent contracts may also be financed from other legally established financial sources. For the financing of the execution of works related to subsequent contracts concluded during the performance of the framework agreement, the contracting authority shall access projects and/or programmes financed from national funds and European Union funds (ROP, etc.) without this description being a limiting one. Tenderers in this procedure understand that the Contracting Authority cannot be held responsible for any damage in the event of the cancellation of the award procedure, regardless of its nature and regardless of whether the Contracting Authority was notified of the existence of such damage. Tenderers in this procedure accept the use of the above special conditions / the suspensive clause, assuming full responsibility in relation to any damage they might suffer in the described situation.

sig_2e3dc67f50f6f01eaaa3.description: Project HARMOS (Health Assessment and Risk Management Operational System) will deliver an Agentic AI‐assisted software platform that optimises production of operational medical plans and Healthcare Risk Assessments (HRAs). The initial activity is a 3 – 4 month pilot/MVP on MODCloud for ~50 med and non‐med planners, delivering validated first‐pass med plans and HRAs, demonstrable evidence of data lineage, measurable time savings for CMAs (OF3–OF5) and a pathway to scale/transition to DMS Digital. Suppliers should be prepared to build their solution on the Rapid Development and Innovation Platform (RDIP) which is an accredited AWS-based solution available via MODNET. RDIP offers platform, software, and expertise as a service with the aim of accelerating innovation projects and simplifying accreditation processes. The Joint Hub for Innovation (jHub) will be the project owners for HARMOS. jHub wishes to enhance the speed and efficiency of Medical Planning through the use of AI-supported tooling. The primary objectives include: 1. To reduce the time required for generating draft medical operations plans from the current 5 days to approximately 30 minutes for a first pass. 2. To improve the accuracy of medical risk assessments by leaning on a repository of Post Exercise Reports (PXRs), historical event data, and prior art. 3. To facilitate effective knowledge transfer between deployments, ensuring lessons learned are incorporated into future deployment planning. Through achieving these objectives, jHub will be better positioned to further support the welfare of the military personnel being deployed. The intention of the Pilot / MVP will be to deliver an AI-supported tool that can produce the first draft of a Medical Operations plan, using historical data, priorart (existing technologies, methods or systems that have been developed prior to the creation of new military innovation), and open source data. The solution will allow jHub to specify a location, number of personnel, and the type of activities being completed during deployment, and receive an automated draft Medical Operations Plan with perspectives specific to different roles, with potential risks highlighted. The system will maintain a searchable repository of previous deployments and provide real-time monitoring capabilities through visual dashboards. The output from this tool can then be reviewed, improved, and shared rapidly with colleagues across the UK MOD using a widely understood language. Route to Market: Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchase System - ref. RM6200 https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6200?nav=0 The intended route to market will be RM6200 referenced above. Please note this is subject to change should a more suitable route be identified. If you are interested in this project, we would encourage you to register on the AI DPS ahead of our intended competition timelines. The categories for filter are not yet defined but will be aligned to the requirement outlined above. Timelines: The intention is to release this project to competition via RM6200 late January/February 2026. Timelines are subject to change. Lot 1: . See above.

sig_2e4fbb5002bde7fc6653.description: Provision of Disaster Recovery Site service and associated hosting service for Budapest Főváros Főpolgármesteri Hivatal. The Winning Tenderer's task is to provide a Disaster Recovery Site service and associated hosting service for Budapest Főváros Főpolgármesteri Hivatal for a period of 24 months. Characteristics of the DR Site service to be provided: - Public internet with a minimum bandwidth of 300 Mbs VPN. 1 IP addresses are sufficient if the FPH's own Class C can be routed there in the event of a disaster. - Perimeter firewall (Firewall, NAT, IPsec, Routing, MPLS and Switching) with subscription for security functions and hardware support; - WAF - Web Application Firewall with subscription for 200 Mbit traffic capacity (virtual appliance runnable even on Hyper-V); - Provision of server infrastructure with the following minimum resources: 3 Hyper-V host servers, per server: o CPU: Intel 24 Core o RAM: 1 TB o Disk system: 2 x 480 GB SSD – RAID1 o Disk data: 35 TB SSD o LAN: 2 x 25 Gbit SFP28 o LAN: 2 x 1 Gbit RJ45 The three servers form a Hyper-V cluster and provide the shared storage for the virtual infrastructure using a storage spaces solution. - Provision of network infrastructure with the following minimum resources: o Switch 8 port 25 Gbit SFP28 o Switch 24x10Gbit SFP+ central switch o Switch 24x1Gbit T port central switch o Juniper switch preferred, with L2 operation, without redundancy o PoE not required o LACP configuration may be required o BGP - Static route BGP or full-dynamic BGP is not required if the FPH's own domain can be routed there in the event of a disaster, a static route is enough. o Performance Monitoring service and proactive troubleshooting are not required. - Veeam-compatible LTO 7 library for Veeam backup; the server is provided by the FPH. The Service Provider undertakes to establish the connection necessary for the provision of the service in accordance with the Technical Description at the place of performance specified in the contract within 15 calendar days from the entry into force of the contract, on the understanding that the execution work shall be carried out at times agreed in advance with the Ordering Party. - at least 99% availability on a monthly average (planned maintenance is not included)
