sig_2e50c7af3975443b5d7d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $499M. Individual awards will not normally exceed sixty (60) months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $500K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions and assistance instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. sig_2e67f31755959e22143f.description: The Stadt Lübben (Spreewald)/Lubin (Blota) intends the acquisition, delivery and migration of the "New System Landscape" (Server). Lot LOT-0001: Delivery and migration of the "New System Landscape". The following technical summary presents the essential key points of the intended target architecture and the scope of services to be procured in a condensed form. It serves for the clear classification of the overall project and summarises in particular the fundamental requirements for the target hardware, virtualisation/HCI platform, availability, network, VDI, backup, infrastructure components, as well as the associated operating and support services ("IT system landscape"). Renewal of the existing virtualisation environment by 3 VM cluster nodes and 2 VDI cluster nodes, supplemented by 1 separate physical witness/quorum server, 1 physical backup/repository server, 1 rackmount NAS and 1 physical control/infrastructure server. VM and VDI clusters are based on the same hypervisor/HCI product family, a uniformly supported platform stack and a common management and administration architecture. VM and VDI nodes with 2 server processors, each with at least 16 physical cores, thus at least 32 physical cores per server, as well as 1.024 GB RAM per node. Benchmark specifications serve comparability; there is no additional minimum benchmark threshold. Per productive cluster node 8 x NVMe SSD with at least o 7,68 TB, o at least 61,44 TB raw capacity per node, power loss protection, at least o 1 DWPD over five years and o MTTF/MTBF at least 2.000.000 hours.
sig_2e67f31755959e22143f.title: Delivery and migration of "New System Landscape"

The subject matter of the contract is the procurement of services necessary for the design, development, implementation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning, user training and provision of technical support relating to an integrated IT solution intended for the digitalisation of the activity of Teliu Commune. The contract entails the creation of a unitary IT platform, consisting of interconnected software components, which will enable both the digitalisation of activities carried out within the functional departments of the institution (Back-Office) and the provision of electronic public services to citizens and the business environment (Front-Office). The IT solution shall be designed so that all its components operate within a unitary architecture, use common authentication and administration mechanisms, allow the automatic exchange of information between modules, and ensure the integrity and security of the processed data. The contract shall mainly comprise the following categories of activities: • analysis of administrative processes and identification of functional requirements; • design of the IT solution architecture; • development and configuration of software components; • integration with existing applications and IT systems; • configuration of electronic workflows; • migration of data necessary for the operation of the system; • functional, technical and acceptance testing; • commissioning of the IT solution; • drafting of technical and user documentation; • training of users designated by the contracting authority; • provision of technical support and maintenance services for the period stipulated in the contract. The intended result is the implementation of an integrated, fully functional IT solution that enables the digitalisation of administrative processes, increases the efficiency of the institution's activity and improves the relationship with citizens through the provision of electronic public services. Components of the IT solution A. Back-Office Component The Back-Office component has the role of digitalising internal administrative processes and ensuring the unitary management of activities carried out within the institution. Within this component, IT modules intended for managing activities specific to local public administration will be implemented, among which: • registry and document management; • electronic archive; • management of debts and enforcement; • modules specific to fiscal activities; • urban planning module; • geographic information system (GIS); • centralisation of data concerning citizens and property; • management of performance indicators; • managerial reporting and analysis; • solutions for cybersecurity and monitoring of the IT infrastructure. All these modules will operate in an integrated environment and will use common databases, avoiding the duplication of information and repetitive data entry. B. Front-Office Component The Front-Office component is intended for the provision of electronic public services to citizens and the business environment. This will mainly include: • the electronic services portal; • the single user account; • online submission of applications; • intelligent electronic forms; • mobile application; • electronic notifications; • request status tracking system; • info-kiosk; • access to public documents and information. The subject matter of the contract is the procurement of services necessary for the design, development, implementation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning, user training and provision of technical support relating to an integrated IT solution intended for the digitalisation of the activity of Teliu Commune. The contract entails the creation of a unitary IT platform, consisting of interconnected software components, which will enable both the digitalisation of activities carried out within the functional departments of the institution (Back-Office) and the provision of electronic public services to citizens and the business environment (Front-Office). The IT solution shall be designed so that all its components operate within a unitary architecture, use common authentication and administration mechanisms, allow the automatic exchange of information between modules, and ensure the integrity and security of the processed data. The contract shall mainly comprise the following categories of activities: • analysis of administrative processes and identification of functional requirements; • design of the IT solution architecture; • development and configuration of software components; • integration with existing applications and IT systems; • configuration of electronic workflows; • migration of data necessary for the operation of the system; • functional, technical and acceptance testing; • commissioning of the IT solution; • drafting of technical and user documentation; • training of users designated by the contracting authority; • provision of technical support and maintenance services for the period stipulated in the contract. The intended result is the implementation of an integrated, fully functional IT solution that enables the digitalisation of administrative processes, increases the efficiency of the institution's activity and improves the relationship with citizens through the provision of electronic public services. Components of the IT solution A. Back-Office Component The Back-Office component has the role of digitalising internal administrative processes and ensuring the unitary management of activities carried out within the institution. Within this component, IT modules intended for managing activities specific to local public administration will be implemented, among which: • registry and document management; • electronic archive; • management of debts and enforcement;

• modules specific to fiscal activities; • urban planning module; • geographic information system (GIS); • centralisation of data concerning citizens and property; • management of performance indicators; • managerial reporting and analysis; • solutions for cybersecurity and monitoring of the IT infrastructure. All these modules will operate in an integrated environment and will use common databases, avoiding the duplication of information and repetitive data entry. B. Front-Office Component The Front-Office component is intended for the provision of electronic public services to citizens and the business environment. This will mainly include: • the electronic services portal; • the single user account; • online submission of applications; • intelligent electronic forms; • mobile application; • electronic notifications; • request status tracking system; • info-kiosk; • access to public documents and information. The implementation of these functionalities aims to reduce the number of trips to the institution's headquarters and increase the accessibility of public services. Detailed information regarding the contract activities can be found in the specifications.

sig_2f1a854bc4281772bc0a.description: The subject matter of the contract is the further development and operation of an existing business intelligence system based on the already implemented Qlik system for the Federal State of Rhineland-Palatinate and the Saarland. The existing business intelligence system is used to evaluate and analyse data from transport contracts and to check billing-relevant parameters and contractually required quality standards. The existing Qlik system is to continue to be used and further developed in future. Support is required for this. A switch to another provider is not planned. sig_2f7e22857769bacf0d6f.description: Suffolk County Council aims to gather input from the market to help develop a secure, real-time interoperability solution connecting ESNEFT’s SystmOne (S1), managed by TPP, with Suffolk County Council’s Liquidlogic Adults’ System (LAS), operated by System C. The Council is interested in solutions that enable reliable, standards-based data exchange to support integrated working across health and social care. The integration should reduce duplication, improve data quality, and ensure professionals have timely access to accurate information to support decision making across 16 Integrated Neighbourhood Teams. The solution should support the sharing of key information, including assessments, care plans, contact and demographic data, and relevant clinical details. Improved interoperability is expected to enhance safety and continuity of care, reduce delays and unnecessary referrals, and support more efficient multi agency working. For residents, the integration will enable a more joined up, person-centred experience, while supporting wider system priorities such as integrated care delivery, reduced avoidable hospital admissions, and improved outcomes. The Council is seeking a modern, secure, and scalable solution that complies with information governance requirements and NHS digital standards. This engagement will help shape a future procurement by testing market capability and delivery approaches. Lot 1: .

sig_2fd143ba14d7fab029ed.description: The subject matter of the public contract being awarded (hereinafter referred to as the "public contract") is the delivery, development, implementation, configuration, testing and commissioning of the modernised UNIS hospital information system (hereinafter referred to as the "HIS") and the modernised Orpheus LIS laboratory information system (hereinafter referred to as the "LIS"), specifically in the form of an expansion and upgrade of the information systems currently used by the contracting authority. The subject matter of performance is not a complete replacement of the existing HIS and LIS with new information systems, but their modernisation through the development, modification and addition of the required functionalities, modules, database structures, user interfaces, integration services and data interfaces. The feasibility study explicitly envisages the expansion of the existing HIS and LIS in the form of an upgrade, rather than their complete replacement. The performance includes in particular: a) analysis of the existing solution, affected modules, data structures and integration links; b) preparation of a detailed design of the technical and implementation solution; c) development, configuration and implementation of the required modifications, modules and functionalities of the HIS and LIS; d) modification of database structures, data models, user interfaces, integration services and data interfaces; e) implementation of requirements for the management, exchange, sharing and making available of priority categories of electronic health records; f) implementation of departmental identifiers for patients, healthcare professionals and healthcare service providers; g) implementation of integration links and interfaces to the extent specified by the procurement documentation; h) installation, configuration, functional and integration testing, pilot operation and commissioning of the modernised information systems into proper operation; i) preparation and handover of as-built documentation, administrator, user, operational and integration documentation; j) training of administrators, key users and other employees of the contracting authority; k) provision of a warranty for the modernised HIS and LIS; l) provision of development of the supplied software solution according to the requirements of the contracting authority up to a maximum extent of 400 person-days (MD) during the warranty period. A detailed binding definition of technical, functional, integration, implementation and operational requirements is contained in Annex No. 12 of this procurement documentation – technical specification of the HIS and LIS. The feasibility study contains a description of the initial state, subsidy, economic, schedule, organisational and administrative information. These parts are not in themselves a binding technical specification of the subject matter of the public contract. Only the requirements stated in Annex No. 12 shall be considered as binding technical requirements. The contractor is obliged to ensure the maintenance of operational continuity with the existing HIS and LIS. Part of the modernisation of the HIS is the maintenance of the current number of licenses acquired for the existing version of the HIS. The technological and infrastructural architecture, hardware, underlying operating systems, database platform, workstations and network infrastructure elements are not the subject of delivery, unless the procurement documentation explicitly states otherwise. The modernised components and interfaces will be operated on the contracting authority's existing HW/SW solution. The contracting authority states that the original supplier of the hospital information system and the laboratory information system will provide cooperation during the performance of the contract to the extent stated in its declaration, which forms Annex No. 11 of this procurement documentation. A detailed definition of the subject matter of the public contract, including technical conditions in the detail necessary for the preparation of the tender, is given in the annexes to this procurement documentation.

sig_3028d0dc07dbcafe59a0.description: GIZ has been commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to support the ECOWAS Commission in the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The main objective of the project is to strengthen the regional and national frameworks for the implementation of the AfCFTA. The project aims to achieve five major results, namely 1) The contribution of the ECOWAS Commission to the coordination of positions of its member countries in the further negotiations of the agreement on AfCFTA is strengthened. 2) The coordination among ECOWAS MS to design the technical framework for AfCFTA implementation has been strengthened. 3) The competencies of competent line ministries and the private sector in ECOWAS member countries to shape the implementation of AfCFTA provisions are strengthened. 4) Information access for member countries, private sector, and civil society on ACFTA implementation and export opportunities is improved in the ECOWAS region. 5) ECOWAS member states have expanded agreements on regional and continental climate-friendly trade in services. The contract concerns the provision and management of a pool of short-term experts (STE) to support the achievement of the project"s objectives related to the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in the ECOWAS region, with a particular focus on Trade in Services (TiS) and Trade Facilitation (TF). The experts will provide technical, strategic, and operational advisory services to the ECOWAS Commission and national institutions such as trade ministries, customs authorities, and AfCFTA committees, as well as private-sector stakeholders. The contractor will be responsible for establishing, coordinating, and managing the STE pool, including expert selection, deployment, briefing, and quality assurance. A dedicated STE Pool Coordinator will serve as the main contact point for GIZ and ensure close coordination with the project team. The services cover human capacity development, organisational development, and policy and strategy advisory in the following thematic areas: - Barriers to TiS - AfCFTA negotiations and implementation, with a focus on TiS - National and regional implementation of AfCFTA regulations - Trade facilitation and customs procedures, including transit-related instruments (e.g. SIGMAT, guarantee mechanisms, e-certificates of origin, AEO programmes) - Sustainable and green trade, including climate- and socially responsible service exports - SME export development and competitiveness - Access to trade-related information Key activities include the designing and delivering training modules, workshops, coaching, and on-the-job support; strengthening negotiation skills of AfCFTA negotiators and private-sector representatives; supporting the development of export strategies for SMEs; facilitating public-private dialogues; and supporting the development of regional and bilateral regulatory frameworks, policies and roadmaps, including mutual recognition agreements (MRAs). The scope of services is structured around the following work packages: Work Package 1 - Policy, Regulatory and Strategic Advisory: Support to public and private sector stakeholders through analyses, studies, drafting and review of regulations, guidelines, strategies, action plans and position papers related to TiS, trade facilitation, AfCFTA implementation, green trade and private-sector development. This also includes support for the development and implementation of AfCFTA communication strategies, the organisation of regional conferences, and the updating and improvement of trade information platforms to ensure wider access to reliable trade-related information. Work Package 2 - Capacity Development and Organisational Advisory: Design and delivery of trainings, workshops, study tours, coaching and knowledge-transfer measures for regional and national authorities and private-sector actors to strengthen institutional capacities and sustainable trade in the ECOWAS region. This includes targeted capacity-building on Trade in Services (TiS), AfCFTA negotiations and implementation, as well as tailored support for women- and youth-led SMEs to enhance their effective participation in AfCFTA-related processes and markets. Work Package 3 - Strategic Planning and Capacity WORKS Support: Support to the Programme"s strategic planning processes, including the review and facilitation of Capacity WORKS tools, organisational and steering structures, and the preparation and facilitation of internal and partner workshops (e.g. annual planning, technical and steering committee meetings). Deliverables will be provided in English, French, or Portuguese, depending on the concerned ECOWAS Member State. All key outputs, including training materials and methodological tools, will be made available to the ECOWAS Commission and relevant national stakeholders to support sustainable knowledge transfer and future capacity-building activities.
sig_3028d0dc07dbcafe59a0.title: 81322059 - Short-Term Expert (STE) Pool for Trade Advisory in the ECOWAS Region

sig_3050f3f173da0eebff1e.description: Update - 22 Sep 26 The purpose of this update is to revise section VIII request additional input regarding: 1. Capacity to support all requirements in the PWS (to include the potential for increased quantity of exercises) for the anticipated 7-year ordering period without subcontracting more than 50% 2. Whether a single award or multiple award IDIQ is recommended Update - 14 Sep 26 The purpose of this update is to clarify procurement history of this requirement. While this is not a follow-on acquisition, portions of this requirement are currently being satisfied under FA251824D0001 awarded to Gemini Technical Services JV, LLC. I. General Information: The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses. This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses to this Sources Sought will assist the Government in determining the potential level of interest, competition adequacy, and technical capabilities of industry respondents (specifically small businesses) to provide the required products and services. The Government may also use this information to assist in determining whether a small business set-aside (or other socioeconomic set-aside) will be appropriate or developing any subsequent small business subcontract participation and small business goal percentages. The Government does not intend to respond to questions posed in Industry responses. The Government does not guarantee any action beyond this notice. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Responses that are incomplete and/or not submitted per the Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed. Interested parties or potential contractors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) before the issuance of a potential Request for Proposals/Quotes to be eligible for contract award or payment if the Government chooses to make an award. Information on registration and annual confirmation requirements may be obtained via SAM.gov. Conflict of interest rules apply, and offerors will be required to submit mitigation plans following the release of the RFP. II. Requirement Information: This Sources Sought notice seeks to identify qualified firms capable of providing comprehensive, non-personal mission support services for the 392d Combat Training Squadron (392 CTS). Under this framework, contractor personnel will deliver core capabilities to plan, integrate, execute, and assess Modeling and Simulation (M&S)-enabled exercises (including SPACE FLAG, FLASH POINT, POLARIS HAMMER, and SPACE SKIES) in support of U.S., joint, and allied warfighters. To ensure the continuous readiness of United States Space Force (USSF), joint and coalition forces, this expertise spans a critical array of warfare domains, including Satellite Communications (SATCOM), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), Electronic Attack (EA), Orbital Warfare (OW), Space Electronic Warfare (SEW), Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Missile Warning (MW), and Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO). Furthermore, contractor personnel will drive operational execution by providing Command and Control (C2) support, intelligence product generation, operations assessments, and lessons learned (L2). This operational framework is firmly underpinned by robust technical requirements, encompassing full-scope IT and cybersecurity support, systems engineering, configuration management, orbital analysis, and sophisticated M&S for the Distributed Mission Operations Center-Space (DMOC-S) and BattleLab enclaves. Ultimately, these integrated capabilities will be leveraged to design, plan, execute, and assess USSF service-level exercises and advanced mission-focused training. Support includes programs identified as Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Required (SAR) administered under the enhanced security guidelines/procedures authorized by Department of Defense DODI 5200.01 (DoD Information Security Program and Protection of Sensitive Compartmented Information) and AFI 16-1404 (Air Force Information Security Program). Responses to this announcement are needed to help inform acquisition planning and to identify capable sources. To efficiently and effectively deliver the required supplies/services, it is anticipated that vendors will have specialized experience in large-scale space exercises, complex IT and M&S environments, and managing highly cleared personnel. III. Purpose: The Government is currently considering NAICS Code 541330 (Engineering Services) and Product Service Code (PSC) R425 (Support – Professional: Engineering/Technical) for this requirement. If your firm believes this requirement should be solicited under a different NAICS code or PSC, please include your detailed rationale and supporting market data within your response. This synopsis is encouraging responses from qualified and capable Small Businesses. Firms responding to this Sources Sought must be U.S. owned and must (1) state whether they are a small or large business based on the size standard above; (2) state if they have socioeconomic classification(s) as follows: Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB); section 8(a) small business; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Economically-Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB); a Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone small business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB);. Small Businesses that are in or are considering Joint Ventures or Mentor Protégé Agreements are encouraged to respond to the source sought. Responses from other than small businesses will be reviewed. Note: If the requirement is set aside for small business, the clause RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will be included in the contract. The data obtained from this notice will assist the Government in understanding the capabilities available in providing advanced space training, exercise execution, and mission rehearsal capabilities. IV. Scope of Anticipated Effort: The 392 CTS provides space combat training through Live, Virtual, & Constructive (LVC) environments to prepare warfighters to achieve and maintain operational dominance in the space domain. The contractor shall provide Mission Support Services, Information Technology, Communications, and Management Support (ITC&MS), and Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS). The Government anticipates this requirement will consist of an IDIQ ordering period of five years. Work will primarily take place at Schriever SFB, Suffolk, Buckley SFB, Hurlburt Field, Vandenberg SFB, and other designated facilities. V. General Submission Instructions: The responses submitted shall be in sufficient detail and clarity to provide the Government with the information it needs. Responses to this Source Sought notice shall meet the following standards: Page Limitations: Section 1 Cover Letter: 2 Pages Section 2 Capability Statement: 10 Pages Section 3 PWS Review: 3 Pages Text Size: No smaller than 10 point Text included in graphics, tables, and figures can be no smaller than 9 point No embedded documents Fully address Sections 1-3 as outlined above Responses that are incomplete and or do not follow these Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed Electronic version of your response only in Microsoft Word or PDF compatible files VI. Section 1 - Cover Letter: The cover letter shall include the following: Company information: Company name 2 points of contact and with contact information (name, address, phone number, website URL, if available, and email address) Cage Code, UEI, and DUNS Number Short description of the company (history, experience in similar service activities/supplies, etc.). Company business size with socioeconomic classification based on the designated NAICS code Information on any potential teaming arrangements, joint ventures, or significant subcontracting arrangements. VII. Section 2 – Capability Statement: Please provide detailed responses to the following questions based on the draft PWS. For each area, identify your firm's current or recent (completed within the last five years) contracts or subcontracts that match the scope, complexity, and magnitude of this PWS. Highlight prime contract experience supporting Space Force Delta-level organizations, Distributed Mission Operations Nodes, or equivalent joint distributed simulation hubs of similar financial magnitude: Plan and Execute Large-Scale Joint LVC Exercises (USSF Service Exercises). Plan, coordinate, execute, and assess large-scale (700+ participants) military exercises. Detail your proven experience managing the full Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC) across geographically distributed nodes. Provide a specific historical example of where you translated joint space doctrine into dynamic Master Scenario Events List (MSEL) injects (e.g., simulated orbital debris, electronic attack) within a LVC environment. Finally, describe your capability to conduct post-exercise analysis and deliver formal After-Action Reports (AAR). Recruit and Retain Specialized TS/SCI/SAP Personnel. Explain your relevant experience in recruiting, clearing, and retaining qualified personnel with Top Secret (TS)/Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearances and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. Include historical metrics (such as average time-to-fill rates for tactical space domains and historical retention rates exceeding 90%). DMOC-S Operations. Operate, sustain, and manage the DMOC-S and its complex M&S environment certified to Joint National Training Capability (JNTC) standards. Provide a specific example of how your team successfully operated systems involving missile warning, Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), and operational RF communications. Demonstrate your experience managing distributed simulation networks (e.g. JTEN, DMON) and utilizing standard architecture protocols (e.g., DIS, HLA) to link space simulators with joint air, land, and maritime simulators. Multi-Domain Information Technology (IT) and Cybersecurity Support. Deliver comprehensive IT, cybersecurity, and network engineering support across multiple security enclaves (e.g., AFSCI, SIPRNet, Stone Ghost/FVEY coalition networks) at both primary and distributed locations. Detail your experience maintaining system configurations, securing Assessment and Authorization (A&A) packages via eMASS under the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and performing concurrent cybersecurity auditing (such as STIG compliance). Decribe your experience rapidly-restoring network outages during high-tempo, simulated LVC exercise operations without degrading the training audience’s experience. Professional Planning and Control Force (PPCF) Support. Manage and oversee a distributed workforce of full-time, embedded M&S and exercise planners deployed to geographically separated USSF Component Commands (e.g., SPACEFOR-INDOPAC, SPACEFOREUR-AF). Describe your firm’s experience interfacing directly with senior combatant command staff. Provide examples of previous contracts your company has had that had embedded planners responding to local theater commanders’ Operational Plans. Surge Capacity and Contingency Operations. Manage, schedule, and execute approximately 15,000 hours of surge support annually, frequently requiring 24/7 operations to support exercises with little to no notice. Detail contractual experience executing large-scale, short-notice surge requirements. Specifically, how you maintained and deployed a pool of cleared, pre-screened, or cross-trained personnel to sustain 24/7 operations during massive events without causing mission failure or degrading steady-state services. VIII. Section 3 - SOW/PWS Review: Please identify areas within the draft PWS that are unclear, restrictive, or present execution obstacles, referenced by PWS paragraph number. Outline any best commercial practices, industry innovations, and recommendations for the most effective contract type and pricing structure to efficiently support the 15,000-hour annual exercise surge requirement. Capacity to support all requirements in the PWS (to include the potential for increased quantity of exercises) for the anticipated 7-year ordering period without subcontracting more than 50%. Whether a single award or multiple award IDIQ is recommended.

sig_307114be0289da1e920d.description: The subject of the project is Integrated Risk Management and is based on measures and actions concerning four different axes / stages, which are Prevention, Preparedness, Response and Recovery, using advanced information technology and telecommunications systems and applications. The objective of the project is to create the necessary infrastructure to enhance the administrative capacity of the Municipality of Chios in managing and handling incidents and emergency situations such as earthquakes, fires, etc. At the same time, the project includes citizen information and training actions, a solution for sending messages - information, supporting vulnerable groups such as disabled persons (PWDs), and finally, studies for the identification, assessment and analysis of natural hazards, enhancing the firefighting means of the Municipality of Chios by supplying three (3) firefighting vehicles suitable for the areas of the Municipality to address and suppress forest fires. It includes the following main sections: 1. Customisation and implementation of an Integrated Information System for Civil Protection, Coordination and Crisis Management. It shall consist of networked information system infrastructures, appropriate geographical data backgrounds, a resource position monitoring module, an infrastructure for managing data from early detection sensors, workstation applications for the Civil Protection Control Centre and Mobile Field Terminals, as well as integrated services and embedded tools for designing and optimising the operational planning required for crisis management from natural disasters. 2. Customisation and implementation of an early detection and forest fire management sub-system. It shall consist of fire detection software housed within the Integrated Information System for Civil Protection, Coordination and Crisis Management. Field equipment with cameras, meteorological stations, communication infrastructures linked to the control centre, and pylons - receivers for mounting materials. 3. Design and implementation of a support system for the Protection of Persons with Disabilities to ensure their survival in natural disaster / emergency situations. It concerns supporting/assisting the movement of PWDs in the urban environment of the Municipality of Chios. Available spatial data regarding urban planning schemes, data from field research, as well as general guidelines of PWD Design will be utilised to indicate alternative scenarios for proposed PWD routes on a map. 4. Training services for citizens and volunteers on Natural Hazards and Disasters. It includes training and education of various target groups (teachers, service executives, local government employees and elected officials, engineers, volunteers / volunteer groups, etc.) on matters concerning prevention - preparedness and self-protection actions, which is essential for drawing up emergency plans and organising readiness exercises. 5. Installation and operation of a direct citizen and visitor outreach system (Push Notification) to support the work of the Municipality with the aim of protecting as well as informing and serving the citizen. To determine the user's position and routes, mobile telephony antenna technologies, device GPS, and WI-FI will be used. 6. Services for the identification, assessment and analysis of natural hazards (earthquakes, landslides, extreme weather events, forest fires) and the drafting of Plans. The main objectives of this section are: To reduce the impact of natural disasters at a social, economic and environmental level in the Municipality of Chios. The assimilation and utilisation of the provided knowledge and practices by target groups. The enhancement of the corresponding operational planning and civil protection plans to be executed through the Project's Civil Protection, Coordination and Crisis Management system. The drafting - updating of all Civil Protection plans in accordance with the guidelines of the General Secretariat for Civil Protection (G.S.C.P.). Furthermore, within the framework of the project for LOT A, the following other services shall also be provided: • Implementation studies. • Supply and installation of equipment and off-the-shelf software – commissioning • Personnel training • Pilot Operation • Publicity Actions • Project Management, reports and administrative information. The project includes a 4-year warranty on equipment and applications. The installation of the equipment shall take place on the premises of the Municipality of Chios and at selected points on the island (concerning surveillance pylons). The contract duration for LOT A is set at eighteen (18) months. Tenders are accepted only for all of the supplies, services and systems described.; It includes: 1. Three (3) vehicles with Firefighting Attachment 2. Personnel Training Services 3. Warranty Services. The contract duration for LOT B is set at six (6) months.
sig_307114be0289da1e920d.title: "Specialised actions and application of intelligent technologies to enhance the protection of the Municipality of Chios against large-scale natural phenomena"

The equipment to be purchased is strictly necessary for the equipping of the Critical Cardiac Patients Advanced Monitoring and Treatment Unit (USTACC). The initiation of the tender procedure is requested given the approval of the project with CALL CODE: PS/665/PS_P3/OP4/RSO4.5/PS_P3_RSO4.5_A7-Investments of the provisioning type in the infrastructure of public health units that treat critical cardiac patients, project title: "Equipping the Satu Mare County Emergency Hospital for the treatment of critical cardiac patients" The general objective of the project consists in improving the response capacity of the Satu Mare County Emergency Hospital in the face of critical cardiovascular emergency cases, by consolidating and equipping the Critical Cardiac Patients Advanced Monitoring and Treatment Unit (USTACC) with high-performance medical equipment, in accordance with national and European standards regarding critical medical care. Through this investment, the aim is to create a modern, functional and efficient medical framework, capable of ensuring rapid, safe and precise interventions for patients with severe cardiovascular conditions, with increased vital risk. The project aligns with Specific Objective RSO4.5 of the Health Programme – "Ensuring equal access to medical care and ensuring the resilience of health systems" – contributing to: reducing avoidable mortality caused by cardiovascular diseases; reducing territorial disparities in access to advanced treatments; increasing the efficiency of intervention in medical emergency situations with a cardiac profile. At the same time, the investment supports the achievement of EU Policy Objective 4 – "A more social and inclusive Europe" – by providing modern, safe and accessible health services to all critical patients, regardless of socio-economic status or area of origin. Enterprise framework agreement – Development of an executive information and report management system 1. Purpose of the system to be delivered The aim is to establish an Executive Information System (hereinafter EIS) for the Contracting Authority consisting of a data visualisation and reporting interface based on Business Intelligence, which, by using the large amount of data generated in the Contracting Authority's various internal systems, can help support management decision-making and improve business performance. It is suitable for analysing both past and current operations, from which the future can also be inferred. It can provide support both in relation to daily operational activities and at a strategic level. The task of the new tool is to collect data from various sources and display it to managers in an understandable, easily digestible format. The aim of the tool is to effectively support the optimisation of business processes, the creation of new processes, the increase of efficiency, and the identification of trends. SAMPLE CONFIGURATION TABLE – regarding the subject of the procurement Item number Designation according to KM Quantity Quantity unit SWF01-PV Project Manager (1 hours) 1400 hours SWF01-SZF Software Developer (1 hours) 8600 hours SWF01-ÜERSZ Business Analyst/Systems Organiser (1 hours) 1700 hours SWF01-T Tester (1 hours) 2200 hours SWF01-VSZF Senior Software Developer (1 hours) 2600 hours The contracting authority requests the detailed price quotation for the above full sample configuration in accordance with the Excel table prescribed by DKÜ (tender price list template), which is Annex No. 6 of Supplement 3 of the documentation. With regard to the item numbers SWF01-PV, SWF01-SZF, SWF01-ÜERSZ, SWF01-T, SWF01-VSZF indicated in the sample configuration table, the estimated total framework quantity is: a total of 16 500 hours. The Contracting Authority undertakes to call off 70% of the estimated total framework quantity with regard to the item numbers SWF01-PV, SWF01-SZF, SWF01-ÜERSZ, SWF01-T, SWF01-VSZF indicated in the sample configuration table. 2. Basic expectations regarding the system The system to be delivered must operate within the Contracting Authority's internal network in an on-premise environment, and data must not leave the Contracting Authority's internal environment. The system to be delivered must ensure that it collects the data forming the basis of the reports from the Contracting Authority's internal systems, stores them and updates them continuously. For this purpose, it is necessary to further develop the DataWarehouse Manager (hereinafter DWM) already found among the Contracting Authority's internal systems, which is currently responsible for the data extraction processes of the Controlling Manager system. During the further development, maintaining the compatibility of the processes serving the Controlling Manager system is an expected task. 2.1. Corporate data model and data warehouse Its task is to collect, link and consolidate data originating from the Contracting Authority's various IT systems, professional fields and processes. Linking data from different sources allows for the discovery of more complex analyses and correlations. Data storage is dimensional in nature, meaning that factual data is complemented by dimension-type data. The data storage schema must support efficient reporting. Reporting functions are built upon the data warehouse's corporate data model. The data stored in the data warehouse is not real-time and does not contain the momentary value of the transactional systems serving as the source of the data, but is collected and kept up-to-date at periodic intervals, adapted to the company's business rhythm, by a data extraction process (Extract, Transformation, Load - hereinafter ETL). The collection and storage of data are, where possible and necessary from the perspective of reports, stored chronologically and historically. If earlier data is also available, it must be collected as well. 2.2. Reporting and report sharing service A module built on the data warehouse's data model that is capable of creating and generating detailed reports based on the stored data, as well as sharing these reports among different user groups. The structure of the data in the data warehouse, as well as their regular updating (ETL process), ensures that the reports contain up-to-date and consistent information. It is capable of visualising data, thereby facilitating business decision-making and analysis processes. The above objectives are achieved, on the one hand, by applying Microsoft Power BI business analysis on-premise services, within this also the elements of Power BI Desktop and Power BI Report Server, within the framework provided by them. On the other hand, an executive dashboard must be developed, which displays the most important reports for the user base. ***** Continuation: II.2.4) Description of procurement: ****** II.1.4) Continuation of description of procurement: 3. Functional expectations regarding the system 3.1. Expectations placed on the reporting service Data visualisation: Displaying data and the correlations between them with the help of graphs and charts. Interactive reports: Incorporating user interactions into reports, by means of which users can filter and examine data according to their own needs. Linking information from different professional fields and processes: Linking data originating from different sources allows for the discovery of more complex correlations. Comparing performance indicators of different organizational units and groups. Filtering out outliers or cases deviating from the statistical average or target value. Collaboration and sharing: Sharing and distributing created reports within the organisation with authorised persons, ensuring the possibility of joint analysis. Flexibility: New reports can be easily added to the system based on the data in the data warehouse. Trend monitoring: Data models must be designed in such a way that reports and statements can also be generated retroactively. 3.2.

Expectations related to permissions The user base will be the executive tier of the Contracting Authority consisting of approx. 40-50 persons. Managers and deputies of all organizational units (top management, cabinets, directorates, offices, groups) will have access to the system. However, the permission scope of these users differs. From the perspective of data security, it is important that every user can only access reports determined on the basis of their hierarchical level and professional field, organizational unit, and within those only the data rows belonging to them. The system must provide the possibility for the flexible management of organizations, organizational hierarchy and permissions. Collection of data for the following data scopes - Work-related data o work statistics collected by user activity tracker o entry and exit data originating from the access card system o data related to work order (Nexon, Provys) - Financial and economic data o plan and forecast data (Controlling Manager) o financial data (Forrás) - Contracts and their data (Oriana) o scope of data related to contract - Human resources management employee data o employee data (Nexon) o data related to rewarding (Performance Management System) o Aid disbursements - HelpDesk ticketing system (Redmine) - Resource planning interface data It is an expectation that the following external systems can be linked to the data scopes: - User activity tracking system - Access card system - Provys - Controlling Manager - Forrás - Oriana - Nexon - Performance Management System (PMS) - HelpDesk (and Redmine) - Resource planning interface / Project register Definition of expected report types (with the designation of the source system in brackets) - Work-related data (Provys, Nexon, Access system, User activity tracker) - Financial and economic data (Controlling Manager, Forrás) - Contracts and their data (Oriana) - Human resources management employee data (Nexon) - HelpDesk ticketing system, operational and administrative data (Helpdesk, Redmine) - Resource planning interface data (Project register) The connected systems and data scopes to be collected determine the report types that can be extracted. Report types do not describe concrete reports, but report groups depending on the type of data scopes. Several reports can belong to one report type. The task is the survey and definition of concrete reports, as well as the extraction of data scopes feeding the reports from the source systems operated by the Contracting Authority. If the source-side system provides a data extraction capability, it is necessary to arrange the transfer of the data required for the report to the data warehouse serving the system. Due to the operation of the DataWarehouse Manager system, validating data and maintaining them is not a task. 4. Tasks to be performed and project operation In connection with the development of the system, the following tasks must be performed: - survey of the data connection capability of connected systems, - clarification of data that can be transferred, design and implementation of system connection - survey and creation of reports defined by the Contracting Authority - joint design and creation of logical and physical architecture, system environment and planes with the Contracting Authority - installation and configuration of the system on the defined planes - provision of training support for the implementation The utilization of the framework hours for preparing the developments is done with individual orders. The content, scope and deadline of the orders are determined jointly with the Winning Tenderer. 5. Deliverables During the development – where applicable – the following documents must be produced: - logical system plan - physical system plan - architecture plan - design plans/screen images - user manual - training aid - operational manual - test plan and record - source code, parameterisations The completed documents must be kept continuously up-to-date during the developments. 6. Further expectations Prior to the go-live of the system, the Contracting Authority shall subject it to an IT security vulnerability assessment, in which the Winning Tenderer shall cooperate and rectify the errors identified therein. General requirements: • Partial tenders for individual services are not possible, considering the volume of the procurement, the short completion time, and the importance of homogeneity; the possibility of submitting partial tenders is incompatible with economic rationality. • Submitting multi-variant tenders and tenders for options is not possible. Further information in the tendering documentation.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. sig_30e3fb6e9c2c3a9709ee.description: Background: The Get Britain Working (GBW) White Paper, co-authored by the Secretaries of State for the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC), Department for Education (DfE) and His Majesty’s Treasury (HMT), sets out plans to set the country on a path to bring down economic inactivity and improve employment outcomes. A key enabler is to reform Jobcentre Plus (JCP) through the creation of a new single and universal Jobs and Careers Service (JCS). JCS will provide support for anyone who is looking for work, who wants to get on in work, or who wants to change their career or retrain. It will be a service that values employer engagement, working with employers to understand and support their current and future recruitment needs. Among the key objectives of JCS are: • Creating a digital, universal and fully inclusive service; and, • Providing high-quality personalised support to help people into work, support training and get on in work. Requirements / Contract subject-matter: DWP Digital teams are progressing digital activity which will underpin JCS and DWP is keen to explore third party solutions which could support this new digital service. The engagement will cover a wide range of requirements. DWP has defined 12 areas of employment support which we are keen to explore suitable products for, including AI solutions. JCS Employment Support categories: The JCS ‘Employment Support’ categories are listed below: • ES01 - Career advice • ES02 - Career planning • ES03 - Skills gap analysis • ES04 - Financial planning • ES05 - Career coaching • ES06 - Learning / Training / Provision • ES07 - Job discovery • ES08 - Job market insights • ES09 - CV support • ES10 - Job application support • ES11 - Application tracking • ES12 - Interview support DWP is conducting this preliminary market engagement to help develop the requirements and the strategy/approach for any future procurements for products/services that would align to the JCS Employment Support categories. Following this preliminary market engagement, DWP may decide to run multiple procurements (with each procurement covering an individual or a group of Employment Support categories), either in parallel or in a phased approach, in line with the priorities of the JCS programme. Suppliers are invited to participate even if they are only interested in specific components of the wider scope. Due to the early stage of this engagement and the fact that it could relate to numerous separate procurements, there are certain aspects of any associated procurement activities that are yet to be determined. As a result, there are some sections of this notice which cannot be completed at this time. Where this is the case, we have stated in the relevant field that the information is “To be determined.” The following points are examples of areas that still need to be determined: • Procurement procedure: will any resulting procurements be above or below the relevant threshold – to be determined. • Is a dynamic market or framework being established – to be determined. • Total Contract Value (estimated) – to be determined. • Contract start dates, end dates and extension options – to be determined (please ignore the start date of 01/01/2027 and end date of 31/12/2027 that are showing on this notice). • Publication date of the tender or transparency notice – to be determined. sig_30e99ea3204b81397bd2.description: By means of the RFP, Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) is seeking proposals from bidders for: The objective of this work is to design, develop and deploy a digital tool (calculator and dashboard) for analyzing and reporting the fuel and GHG reductions of the projects funded under the Green Freight Program. This tool will allow the Program team to systematically track, calculate and report on key metrics for each project. Key requirements include embedded calculations, a functionality for data entry for measuring future projects and reporting features. The calculator must use established formulas to estimate fuel savings (liters) and GHG reductions (tonnes of CO2e) for all eligible activities under Streams 1 and 2 of the green freight program. It must allow program staff to add new project data, generate dashboards for monitoring and decision-making.
sig_30e99ea3204b81397bd2.title: Green Freight Program Impact Data Analysis & Reporting Tool (Estimated Fuel and GHG-Reduction Calculator and Dashboard)

sig_30f5bdb315fc27770530.description: Title of Event: Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) Industry Summit – Road to improved data sharing and access in the Army data eco-system Audience: Department of War Contractors and Government Stakeholders When: 27 Oct 2026 Where: Virtual via MS Teams Army Data Operations Center will conduct an Industry Summit on 27 October 2026 via Army MS Teams in order to brief Industry on ADOC activities/capabilities and to inform ADOC Full Operational Capability. Key tasks center around an explanation of what the Army Data Operations Center is, the vision for Army Data Governance and Accessibility, outlining current capability roadmaps, and identifying gaps to Industry and Key DOW Stakeholders. **NOTICE OF SPECIAL INTEREST / INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT DISCLAIMER** **No Solicitation or Pending RFP:** This announcement is issued solely for information-sharing and market research purposes in support of the Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) Industry Summit. This engagement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). There is no pending contract, solicitation, or procurement action anticipated as a direct result of this event. **No Commitment by the Government:** Participation in the ADOC Industry Summit is completely voluntary. The U.S. Army will not pay for any information submitted, nor will it reimburse vendors for preparation, or any other costs associated with attending or responding to this notice. DOW Briefers include: Army Data Operations Center The Desired End State: ADOC receives and incorporates feedback from Industry Summit participants into the ADOC Lessons Learned Wiki and Rolodex. Industry and DOW Stakeholders have a shared understanding of the Army Data Operations Center’s mission and DOW Data governance & accessibility challenges. This Industry Summit will be held at the CUI level and will be 100% Virtual via Army MS Teams ADOC Focus Areas The Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) is hosting this Industry Summit to foster a technical exchange with industry leaders, innovators, and practitioners. The primary objective is to understand how industry-proven methodologies can be applied to modernize, secure, and scale Army enterprise data infrastructure. During the technical sessions, ADOC is specifically interested in hearing briefings, live demonstrations, and case studies addressing the following core focus areas provided by priority: # Focus Area Participation Criteria 1 Data Platform Support: Describe your current and past performance supporting Army Data platforms (legacy or new systems). What specific technical and operational environments have you actively supported? 2 "As Code" Governance: Detail your methodology and past implementation of "Documentation as Code" and "Policy as Code" within secure DoW or federal enterprise environments to automate governance. 3 Access Control Frameworks: Explain how your solutions implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) to enforce security while ensuring secure, mission-appropriate data sharing. 4 Reusability & Products: What is your proven approach to developing stable, discoverable, and reusable baseline data products to reduce duplicate engineering efforts across enterprise platforms? 5 Emerging Trends & AI: How do your solutions leverage AI/ML to optimize governance workflows, analyze request patterns, and improve operational efficiency within a regulated data ecosystem? AGENDA: This is a single day event. Each Vendor will have a 30-minute block for presentations and Q&A. ADOC reserves the right to extend/reduce time in the final agenda. Each participating vendor will have a sperate dedicated Team Meetings established for their allocated time with ADOC government civilian/military personnel. sig_3109fa3b417e21ba4302.description: The Baudirektion of the Canton of Zurich is introducing the Building Information Modelling (BIM) method across the ARE, TBA, HBA and IMA offices as part of the BIM@BD programme. The aim is to make construction and management processes more efficient through the digital continuity of data and documents across all lifecycle phases, and to increase the quality and completeness of data. As part of the phased model (Stage 1) of the programme, the procurement of a modern BIM CDE (Common Data Environment) with a focus on user acceptance and cost-effectiveness is planned. The BIM CDE forms the software solution for mapping digitalised processes for collaboration with structured building information. It enables the guided exchange of data during the planning and construction phases and their transfer into existing peripheral systems for property operations. The BIM CDE is designed as an interaction between two software solutions: 1. The BIM CDE PIM (Project Information Model) serves the exchange of data and information between the offices and external project teams in ongoing projects. Accordingly, a large number of users with various technical backgrounds is to be expected here, which necessitates simple and intuitive user guidance. The BIM CDE PIM offers functionalities that are necessary for the implementation of BIM use cases. The BIM CDE PIM is the subject of this tender. 2. The BIM CDE DIP (Data Integration Platform) is designed as an expert system and is used exclusively by internal, trained specialists. The solution serves to retrieve project data from the BIM CDE PIM and process it for transfer to the Baudirektion's existing target systems. The procurement of the BIM CDE DIP is planned for the year 2026 and is not part of this tender. Two Lots This BIM CDE PIM tender is divided into two lots. - Lot 1 CDE PIM optimally usable for building construction projects - Lot 2 CDE PIM optimally usable for civil engineering projects It is desired that tenderers submit one tender for each of the two lots. The aim is to find a common BIM CDE solution for building construction and civil engineering. Additional points are awarded in the evaluation for the resulting synergy. However, there is also the possibility of awarding contracts for two different products. The evaluation procedure takes place – described in simplified terms – in three steps. In a first step, all submitted tenders are checked to see whether they meet the general participation requirements. Tenders that do not meet these requirements are excluded from the further procedure. In the second step, the remaining tenders are evaluated based on the defined suitability criteria and award criteria. A provisional ranking is drawn up on this basis. In the third step, those tenders are comprehensively checked and evaluated which still have a realistic chance of being awarded the contract based on the provisional evaluation. This in-depth check includes a PoC (Proof of Concept) and subsequently a product presentation by the tenderer. The tenderers invited to the PoC receive a package of test data with which they can configure their solution and make it available to a selection of test users for live testing. In the subsequent product presentation, initial empirical values, feedback on the first impression and user-friendliness are already available and can be discussed with the tenderer in the Q&A part. This procedure is deliberately chosen, as intuitive usability is extremely important for the BIM CDE PIM. The results are combined into an overall evaluation. Option "Confidential data classification" Special attention must be paid to information security requirements. The offered solution must at least meet the requirements of the "internal" data classification. If the requirements for use for data of the "confidential" data classification are additionally met, the tenderer receives additional points. For further information, see the specifications. CDE PIM optimally usable for civil engineering projects. For further information, see the specifications.
sig_3109fa3b417e21ba4302.title: Common Data Environment for Project Information Model (BIM CDE PIM)

sig_311029dcf4f9e4f83cb5.description: The Industrial Logistics (IL) service centre, reporting to the Support Services Directorate (DIR2S) of Enedis, wishes to acquire a turnkey SaaS solution enabling the planning, optimisation, management and traceability of incoming delivery flows at logistics sites, in order to support the operational performance of logistics sites and the supply chain. Beyond planning functions, the solution must constitute a genuine activity management tool by incorporating advanced data analysis, reporting and valuation capabilities. It must provide a consolidated, reliable and actionable overview of supplier delivery flows, both at the level of each logistics site and at national level, in order to facilitate decision-making, load forecasting and continuous process improvement. Maximum contract amount: 869 000 EUR excluding VAT. This contract is awarded to a single contractor. A maximum of 5 candidates will be selected to participate in the consultation phase. Firm duration of the contract: 3 years. Renewal: 5 times for one year. The estimated contract start date is: 26/04/2027. The Industrial Logistics (IL) service centre, reporting to the Support Services Directorate (DIR2S) of Enedis, wishes to acquire a turnkey SaaS solution enabling the planning, optimisation, management and traceability of incoming delivery flows at logistics sites, in order to support the operational performance of logistics sites and the supply chain. Beyond planning functions, the solution must constitute a genuine activity management tool by incorporating advanced data analysis, reporting and valuation capabilities. It must provide a consolidated, reliable and actionable overview of supplier delivery flows, both at the level of each logistics site and at national level, in order to facilitate decision-making, load forecasting and continuous process improvement. In this context, the main expected functionalities are: - The ability to configure and administer logistics sites, notably via the management of appointment time slots and reception capacities (in volume or number of appointments); - Electronic appointment booking on a schedule for carriers and suppliers, based on available time slots and capacities, with verification of expected orders (interfaced with the Enedis ERP), incorporating the characteristics of expected deliveries (volumes, type of equipment, etc.); - Real-time consultation of schedules and the progress or status of appointments, as well as tracking compliance with appointments (date, arrival time, volume and number of pallets delivered, etc.); - Recording and qualification of anomalies or non-conformities, according to structured categories (failure to respect schedules, damaged equipment, etc.) enabling their analysis; - Extensive capabilities for extracting, structuring and exploiting data (reference frameworks, schedules, history, non-conformities); - Provision of dashboards, performance indicators and reporting tools, enabling operational and strategic management of the activity; - The capacity to analyse trends, identify pain points and feed into continuous improvement initiatives, both locally and nationally. The details of the expected services are described in the provisional CCTP available in the "documents" tab of the purchasing portal of the call for applications.
