sig_3149a018f5df4410ddcb.description: Cornwall Council is seeking market feedback to inform the development of a final specification for a future income management solution. The Council invites suppliers to respond to this Request for Information (RFI) to help shape a solution that meets operational, technical, and compliance needs. The Council requires a cloud-based, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) income management system that: Core Functional Requirements • Provides a central transaction database to control, reconcile, and report on income. • Re-formats and exports data to update a range of back-office financial management systems (FMS). • Is accessible via a browser and supports integration with third-party applications used by Cornwall Council. • Offers self-tailoring configurable import/export functionality to enable full system ownership and flexibility. Payment Processing Capabilities • Supports payments via telephone (call centre), face-to-face (card, cash, cheque), and opportunistic payments initiated by staff. • Integrates with a Secure Bureau Service (SBS) for PCI DSS-compliant card authorisation. • Includes a portal interface for retrieving customer and payment details during calls, with seamless access from host systems. • Includes transaction visibility through APACS reporting. Security & Compliance • Ensures cardholder data is not accessible to Council staff or stored on Council infrastructure. • Provides automated, secure card entry to simplify PCI DSS compliance and reduce SAQ scope. Staff Tools & Satellite Office Support • Enables staff to submit electronic forms with ledger codes and banking summaries, particularly for satellite offices without full receipting systems. Customer Present Transactions • Supports Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE) for chip & PIN payments. • Includes terminal management and smart client software for secure device operation. Online & E-Commerce Payments • Offers a fully hosted internet payment solution with shopping cart, miscellaneous payments, and a Digital Wallet for card reuse. • Provides tools to customise hosted payment pages. Third-Party Integration • Supports integration with external applications via SOAP and REST APIs. • Allows secure transaction handoff and return for receipting and system updates. • Accepts alternative payment methods including PayPal, Pingit, and Visa Checkout. System Compatibility • Integrates with existing systems such as Microsoft Dynamics. Automated Telephony •,Provides a fully hosted automated telephony solution for 24/7/365 payments and balance enquiries. Data Access & Refunds • Enables real-time transaction viewing, balance queries, and customer refund processing. Service Level Agreement (SLA) • The SLA will define minimum acceptable service levels, including system uptime, response times, and resolution times for incidents. • Support hours, escalation procedures, and contact channels must be clearly documented. • Regular service reviews will be conducted to ensure SLA compliance. • Penalties or service credits may apply for failure to meet agreed service levels. Performance Management • Performance will be monitored against agreed KPIs, including transaction processing speed, system availability, and customer satisfaction. • The supplier must provide regular performance reports and participate in review meetings. • Continuous improvement plans should be in place to address any performance gaps. Lot 1: .

sig_315e321e6ee6bd9019c1.description: The procedure is being conducted as an Open House procurement. An Open House procurement is a procedure in which public contracting authorities do not conclude a contract with one company, but will instead contract with all interested companies under previously clearly defined conditions. This notice serves to correct the notice with the identifier/version 65f6def5-a7a2-449a-96f8-ad5247ffa714 - 01, published on 23.11.2023. Any interested entrepreneur may submit a request to participate at any time. For the conditions of participation, see the Open House documents on the procurement portal https://schiefer.vemap.com/home/bekannt/. The subject Open House model is not subject to the Federal Public Procurement Act 2018, BGBl I No 65/2018 as amended. The Open House procedure runs for an indefinite period. The submission deadline on the procurement portal (30.11.2026, 12:00 hours) is irrelevant and is conditional for technical reasons. The indication of the Federal Administrative Court as the responsible body is irrelevant and is conditional for technical reasons. The correction concerns the collaboration agreement (Annex ./1 to the Open House document). Changes are visible in change mode. In contrast to the original procedure, the establishment of a 'carefree' configurator is not mandatory. Alternatively, a link to the collaboration partner's homepage can be provided. See the description under 2.1 of this notice

sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.description: The European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) invites Tenders for the future acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System. The ITT seeks proposals from Tenderers for licensing and support services for an advanced hierarchical data storage management system and related consultancy services. The aim is to enter into a long-term contract for the procurement of these services, include commissioning, training of ECMWF staff and supporting the solution over the lifetime of the contract. Full information is available on ECMWF’s eProcurement Portal which will is accessible via https://procurement.ecmwf.int/. Further details of the scope and overview of the procurement are provided below: ECMWF’s data archive is based on HPSS (High Performance Storage System) software and underpinned by large capacity disk and automated tape library infrastructure. Overall HPSS holds 1.5 Exabytes of data and the expectation is that by the end of 2032 they will have grown to hold well over 4 Exabytes and by the end of 2035, well over 8 Exabytes. HPSS is primarily used by two applications, both developed at ECMWF; MARS and ECFS: MARS, the Meteorological Archival and Retrieval System, provides access to a powerful abstraction engine that allows the thousands of registered users to access the meteorological data that has been collected or generated at ECMWF for more than 40 years. ECFS, the ECMWF Common File System, provides users with a logical view of a seemingly very large file system and is used for data in formats that are not suitable for storing in MARS. The archives are very busy, most of their activity is responding to read workloads from the HPC systems. However, around 620TB of new data is being added every day, and it is expected that daily growth will be close to 1.5PB following the introduction of the new HPC in 2027. Further details on activity and existing equipment will be provided in the ITT. The intention is to determine whether to remain with HPSS or to migrate to a new storage solution, whichever provides the most compelling case based on long-term growth potential, stability and pricing. ECMWF is seeking to enter a long-term relationship with a vendor to supply a license and provide 24/7 support for the software. The initial installation will be at the Centre's Bologna data centre in Italy. If there are optimisation benefits, it will be possible to supply hardware in this tender, however the main intention is for this to be predominantly a software solution, with commodity hardware being purchased elsewhere. The ITT has an estimated value exceeding 3 million EUR. Further details are available in the ITT volumes accessible via the ECMWF procurement portal. The closing date for the Tender, as indicated in Volume IA is Thursday, 05 March 2026, 15:00 (UK Local time).
sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.title: Acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System

In addition the system is integrated with a number of surrounding trade systems. The final scope for the new system has not yet been decided, and we would like input on this in the market dialogue. After the survey, we invite tenderers who confirmed their intention to participate in the tender process, preferential 3 individual supplier meetings in Drammen Town Hall for dialogues on selected topics. sig_31b430e006143bd2c907.description: We kindly request you to submit your response to this information request regarding the procurement OMNI360 AI solutions embedded in healthcare. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a potential tendering process. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that the preparers of the tendering process have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. With this information request, we wish to survey suppliers' capability and interest in acting as a development partner for AI solutions embedded in the OMNI360 system. In addition, we are exploring ready-made or near-ready-made OMNI360 embedded AI solutions available on the market. We also aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services and solutions, related products, contract terms and commercial conditions such as pricing. The procurement will be put out to tender within the dynamic purchasing system for Artificial intelligence and automation solutions and related services 2026-2033. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions and/or technical market dialogues may be organised. In the market dialogue sessions, suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement object. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the more detailed schedules and the Teams meeting link later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering process presented in this information request are merely preliminary and indicative. The final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. CONTRACTING AUTHORITIES The contracting entities acting in the procurement are likely to be Istekki Oy and the Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county. In addition, other contracting entities designated in the said dynamic purchasing system may join the procurement before the publication of the call for tenders. The contracting entities for the procurement will be confirmed as the preparation of the procurement progresses. By responding to the information request, the Tenderer accepts that Istekki shares the information request responses confidentially with the contracting entities designated in the dynamic purchasing system who participate in the preparation of the procurement or utilise its results. Representatives of the contracting entities involved in the procurement and also possibly of Istekki's End Customers may participate in the market dialogue meetings. RESPONDING TO THE INFORMATION REQUEST Attached to this notice is a preliminary description of the procurement, as well as questions which interested parties are requested to answer. We kindly ask you to submit your response in the tender service no later than 02.10.2026 at 14.00. We hope that the responses are submitted as a separate attachment in the Finnish language so that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you can also include Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your response. All responses received to the information request will be taken into account in the preparation of the call for tenders, and they are an important part of understanding the whole. It is good to note that this information request does not oblige Istekki Oy, the Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county, other contracting entities or End Customers to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its attachments. A potential tendering procedure may also not be organised. No separate compensation is paid for responding to the information request or participating in potential presentation sessions. We would like to mention again that this is an information request, not a prior information notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the information request is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the object of procurement to support the planning of the future tendering process. Responding to the information request is voluntary, and it is not a prerequisite for participation in a potential tendering procedure nor does it bind the Contracting Authorities to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us to build the future tendering process into as functional and clear a whole as possible. This notice applies to all procurement procedures concerning the procurements described in the notice. In the same procurement, it may be necessary to carry out several procurement procedures, for example if the procurement procedure has to be discontinued.

sig_31d8450c7c903c727665.description: Kantonsspital Winterthur (KSW) intends to introduce a new integrated IT service management system (ITSM) in order to sustainably optimise the efficiency, transparency and quality of IT services. The existing system is approaching its end-of-life (EoL) date and only partially meets the requirements for a modern, scalable and future-proof ITSM. In particular, the core processes implemented in the current tool are in some cases highly customised and not consistently implemented according to ITIL best practices. The new procurement is intended to introduce a standardised ITSM tool that comprehensively supports ITIL version 4 practices and enables a transparent and comprehensible mapping of ITIL processes. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of standard processes in order to increase maintainability, reduce customisation effort and ensure long-term further development. The new ITSM system is intended to map the entire lifecycle of IT services and support the specific requirements of a hospital operation with regard to availability, security, compliance and traceability. In addition, the system should be flexibly expandable in order to be able to take future organisational, technological and regulatory developments into account.
sig_31d8450c7c903c727665.title: NextServe - New IT service management system for the KSW

With a view to the objectives of the project, the procurement comprises the following performance items: Operational development of a web-based feedback, learning and analysis system that offers family carers a simple and secure way to share experiences from home care. The development and operation of the CIRS take place on the basis of an EVB-IT cloud contract. The contract begins on 01.09.2026. A minimum contract duration of one year applies. sig_31ed502ea055f66bfb63.description:
The integrated, intelligent and adaptive traffic management system (TMS) which is the subject of this procurement is an integrated assembly of hardware, software and communications that offers the possibility of prioritising public transport vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists in traffic (at intersections), to the detriment of personal cars. The detailed technical solution is presented in the Technical Project, an annex to the Specifications. The integrated, intelligent and adaptive traffic management system is an integrated assembly of hardware and software that offers the possibility of prioritising public transport vehicles and pedestrians and cyclists in traffic, to the detriment of personal cars. The proposed technical solution consists of the following elements [modules], in order to meet the needs of the project implementation, in correlation and correspondence with the technical, functional and architectural solutions detailed in the previous design stage: - Implementation of the traffic management component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and distributed (communications network); the system ensures an adaptation of signal timings based on information on traffic flows received in real time from field equipment – adaptive traffic management - Implementation of the monitoring component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and distributed (communications network): the system ensures video monitoring of signalised locations, with a view to increasing road safety for all road users: drivers, public transport passengers, cyclists, pedestrians, including video monitoring with ANPR-type systems located at the municipality's road entry points; - Implementation of the public transport vehicle prioritisation component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and mobile (in public transport vehicles); the system ensures an adaptation of signal timings based on information received in real time regarding the position of public transport vehicles, so as to ensure the fastest possible crossing of signalised intersections by these vehicles. From the point of view of the necessary works, the investment objective is composed of the following investment elements: □ Signalisation of 88 intersections; □ Electrical installation works; □ Rehabilitation of the pavement on Calea Republici street, the left side when travelling towards the city centre (section between Calea Republicii No. 190-192 (Bus line terminus) and the intersection with Strada Condorilor; □ Arrangement of raised traffic separation islands; □ Arrangement of transition zones (shared-space) in the area of intersections; □ Arrangement of green spaces; □ Repairs with asphalt mixtures of the carriageway in signalised intersections; □ Repairs of the carriageway and pavements following underground conduit works; □ Road markings and signs. For the execution of the works, the provisions of the specialist Specifications, part of the Technical Documentation attached to this Specification, shall be observed. For the optimisation of traffic and the realisation of a signalisation system compliant with European standards and which allows for the real-time identification of traffic values, communication between intersections, and the modification of signal timings according to traffic values for good traffic flow, especially for public transport vehicles, and equipment with modern and durable systems, the following types of works have been provided: □ Realisation of electrical conduits in the carriageway, pavement and green space. The connections between the traffic light support poles and the traffic controller will be made through a dedicated underground electrical conduit. □ Realisation of manholes with covers. At the points of crossing the carriageway and at changes in the direction of the route, the conduit will be provided with cement concrete manholes, 64x64 cm. □ Laying/Changing of traffic light connection cables. The electrical cables connecting the traffic lights and the traffic controller will be of the Csyy 3-19x1.5 type. □ Equipping/Replacing existing traffic lights with new traffic lights, which use LED technology, these having better visibility, lower maintenance costs and a much longer service life than conventional incandescent bulb traffic lights. □ Installing/Replacing existing traffic controllers with new traffic controllers, provided with equipment that allows communication between intersections, the introduction of multi-programmes or the possibility of adding new equipment or equipment with other characteristics (inductive loops, video detection cameras, etc.). □ Planting of new traffic light poles. The installation of simple poles and poles with brackets has been provided to double the vehicle traffic lights, thus increasing their visibility from at least 50m (according to STAS 1848/4). □ Each pedestrian crossing-type intersection will be provided with acoustic devices (for persons with disabilities) and with push-button devices (for confirming the pedestrian crossing request). □ Mounting of inductive traffic loops in the carriageway, which allow for the real and instantaneous identification of the number of vehicles entering the intersection. These data allow the traffic controllers proposed to equip the intersections to create signal timings according to traffic conditions and to optimise the operation of the intersections to the maximum.

The placement of inductive detection loops has been provided on the entry lanes to the intersection, on each direction, two for each entry lane to the intersection and one for each exit lane from the signalised intersection. After the realisation of the inductive traffic detection loops, the intersection will be able to operate in a local adaptive mode or it will be possible to correlate it with the intersections upstream and downstream. □ Each non-signalised intersection will be electrically connected to the network. □ Realisation of communication via fibre optics between intersections, thus helping to create a green wave, to correlate the intersections with each other in real time and to establish their connection with the Command and Control Centre.

The system covers IT operating services under the seven service areas listed below and elaborated in Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System. In addition, as part of its delivery of IT operating services to the customer, the supplier is responsible for making the necessary operational adjustments and configurations, as well as delivering cross-functional services and ordering services related to the IT operating services. The supplier is responsible, inter alia, for operating, maintaining and administering the IT operating services and making the necessary minor adjustments, up-/downscaling, configurations, patching, etc., and handling the service management processes, including documentation, reporting, ITIL processes and participation in the customer's governance organisation as part of the delivery of IT operating services to the customer. The supplier must also ensure that the supplier's IT operating services have a high degree of security, which the supplier must incorporate into its IT operating services and ensure the necessary monitoring and control of. In connection with specific procurements under the system, the supplier must deliver an onboarding transition service and, in connection with the total or partial termination of the Delivery Contract, also deliver an offboarding transition service. Common to both transition services is that the supplier must manage, operate and plan these phases and assist the customer, the outgoing supplier and the incoming supplier to the necessary extent to ensure a successful transition. It is possible to purchase various forms of IT operating services that all complement each other. The system has a high degree of flexibility and contains many different use scenarios that make it possible to purchase IT services such as, for example: publicly available cloud tools as well as managed cloud services and administration of cloud platforms, storage, backup, computing, physical floor space in a data centre, racks for IT equipment, office WiFi solutions, network cables for data centres, managed network solutions, VPN solutions, operation of standard and specially developed applications, database operations, middleware operations, rental of computers, tablets, PC screens, headsets and associated mobile device management, as well as service desk, Security Operations Centre (SOC), operation of modern office applications including e-mail, collaboration platforms, archiving systems, etc. Overall, the system category contains the following seven service areas, with associated underlying services, cross-functional services and ordering services that the customer can procure across: • Cloud operations • Data centre operations • Co-location • Network operations • Application operations • End-user services • Security services Under the seven service areas, it is possible to procure capacity – for example, cloud capacity and server and storage capacity. Reference is otherwise made to Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System for an elaboration of the 7 service areas that the subject matter of the system consists of.

sig_325870b72bba15601c84.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A NOTICE OF THE COMMENCEMENT OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is planning a tender process where the subject of the procurement is an HR system package for payroll, employment relationship management, personnel development, and travel and expense claim management, including an outsourced payroll service and a travel and expense claim service. The package also potentially includes a statutory archiving solution. The subject of the procurement also includes system implementation and commissioning, support and maintenance services, operational services, and further development services. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue’s payroll and travel and expense claim services are currently outsourced to Sarastia Oy. The services are managed in systems administered by the service provider, S365 HR and M2. S365 HR acts as the master data for personal information. Supervisors, employees and HR have access to the current HR system, which is currently used for employment lifecycle functions - HRD functions are not in use. The new system and service to be procured will support Länsi-Uusimaa’s desire to facilitate and lighten the administrative work of supervisors and to develop the HR system towards a more modern solution that includes HRD functions such as development discussions and the management of permits and qualifications. The goal is not only to select systems but also to build a functional and sustainable partnership with the supplier. The procurement tentatively includes, among other things, the following functionalities and features: - Outsourced payroll service, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel, excluding social benefits. The service includes customer service for supervisors and employees. - Payroll system as part of the outsourced payroll service solution. - HR system, which acts as the client’s HR master and covers employment lifecycle management as well as HRD functions such as development discussions, management of permits and qualifications, and support for on-boarding and off-boarding processes. The system must have an electronic signature capability. - Travel and expense claim system, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel. - Outsourced travel and expense claim service, which includes, among other things, customer service, weekly payments, and the handling of official reports. - Integrations with the subscriber’s other systems via interfaces. - Advanced automation technologies, which can be used to automate, for example, tasks related to supervisory work and the delivery of data to payroll. The procurement will be carried out using a competitive dialogue procedure. The preliminary procurement schedule is: - Publication of the contract notice by the end of September. - Participation applications by the end of October. - Selection of tenderers by the end of October. - Preliminary call for tenders and sending of invitations to negotiate in November. - Two rounds of negotiations, which will take place in weeks 48 and 50. - Final call for tenders in week 2-3/2026. - Procurement decision in March 2026. - Estimated start time for implementation April 2026. - Services and systems into production use 1.4.2027. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 19.9.2025 at 12.00 to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi. The registration must be titled as follows: “HR kokonaisratkaisun hankinta” (Procurement of HR overall solution). The registration must also contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding to the market survey does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.
sig_325870b72bba15601c84.title: Procurement of HR and payroll system and outsourcing of services

sig_3299f37d3ba51203b947.description: The project "Vaccines for Africa: Roll out and Production in South Africa" (SAVax) is part of South Africa's strategic objective to enhance the local production of vaccines, medicines, and health technologies. Co-financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the European Union (EU), SAVax aims to strengthen local manufacturing capacity in the biopharmaceutical industry and improve access to essential health products. The initiative aligns with the goals of key South African government partners, including the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI), the Department of Health (DoH), and the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA), to create a sustainable and competitive biopharmaceutical sector. The project aims at supporting selected South African biopharmaceutical companies with "ready-for-market" products, providing targeted technical assistance to improve their manufacturing capacity, and enhancing market access at national, regional, and continental levels. These companies face challenges such as market intelligence gaps, demand forecasting difficulties, high production costs, and technology transfer obstacles, which impede their ability to meet growing health needs. Addressing these challenges requires long-term strategies, including off-take agreements, purchase guarantees, and investment in technology and skills development. SAVax conducted a landscape assessment of South Africa's biopharmaceutical industry, covering the pharmaceutical, biotechnological, and biomanufacturing sectors as well as a call for applica-tions for companies to self-identify their technical assistance needs. The objective of this assignment is to engage a service provider to provide tailored technical assistance for the selected companies in the biopharmaceutical sector. This technical assistance aims at enhancing the capacities of companies to gain market access with their products. The goal is to equip these companies with the knowledge and skills necessary to advance their products to market access. The selected companies will receive targeted, non-financial support addressing the technical, regulatory, organizational, and strategic challenges they face in advancing biopharmaceutical products to market. Support areas may include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Technology Platforms and Innovation Readiness o mRNA Technology Transfer Support: Assistance in understanding, adapting, or implementing mRNA-based platforms, including guidance on formulation, delivery systems, process design, cold-chain logistics, and regulatory considerations for mRNA therapeutics or vaccines. o Digitisation of cGMP Systems: Support in planning and implementing digital systems for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance. This includes electronic batch records, quality management systems (QMS), equipment calibration tracking, and data integrity solutions aligned with international norms. 2. Regulatory and Quality Systems Strengthening o Navigating Regulatory Pathways: Tailored guidance for interacting with SAHPRA and other relevant authorities (e.g. WHO Prequalification), including dossier preparation, clinical trial applications, reliance mechanisms, and fast-track pathways. Also includes strategic regulatory planning for biosimilars and advanced therapies. o Quality Management Process Strengthening: Support in designing, upgrading, or implementing fit-for-purpose Quality Management Systems (QMS) based on ICH Q10 principles. This includes standard operating procedures (SOPs), change control, deviation management, and risk-based approaches to quality oversight. o ISO Certification Readiness: Technical support to prepare for ISO 9001, 13485 or other relevant certifications, including gap assessments, internal audits, documentation guidance, and quality culture development. o GMP Training and Compliance Advisory: Provision of technical training in GMP principles, inspection readiness, and facility hygiene requirements, adapted to different staff levels (operators, QA/QC, management). May include site-specific support for corrective/preventive actions (CAPA). 3. Intellectual Property and Commercial Strategy o Intellectual Property (IP) Strategies: Support in designing or refining IP strategies including freedom-to-operate analyses, IP landscaping, filing strategies (local and international), and licensing terms. Emphasis on protection in the context of part-nerships and technology transfer. o Optimising Commercialisation Pathways: Advisory services to develop and refine commercial strategies, including go-to-market models, pricing approaches, and health economic value propositions. May include support in understanding procurement systems (e.g. NHI, pooled African mechanisms). o Market Assessment and Market Access Support: Tailored market research to eval-uate demand, pricing, competition, and policy environments in local and regional markets. Support may include alignment with public procurement frameworks and donor-funded demand sources. 4. Organisational Resilience and Investment Readiness o Financial Restructuring and Strategy Advisory: Guidance on cost structures, business modelling, and capital allocation to improve organisational sustainability. Support may include preparing for audits, understanding grant or equity implications, or structuring financials for growth. o Managing Investor Relations: Capacity-building on investor engagement, including pitch deck refinement, term sheet review, investor reporting frameworks, and relationship management practices that align with sector expectations. o Mentorship Programmes: Pairing of companies with seasoned executives, technical experts, or entrepreneurs who can provide continuous coaching in technical, strategic, and commercial areas. Structured mentorship plans with KPIs will be encouraged. 5. Human Capital and Collaboration o Strategies for Talent Development and Retention: Development of internal work-force strategies including upskilling plans, career progression models, and organisational culture interventions to reduce talent attrition in critical areas like QC, regulatory affairs, and bioprocessing. o Managing Strategic Partnerships: Support in structuring and managing public-private partnerships, consortia, and technology transfer agreements. This includes due diligence, contractual frameworks, IP considerations, and governance models to ensure mutual value. o Facilitation of International Training Exchanges: Design and support of outbound and inbound staff exchange opportunities with regional or international centres of excellence, including identification of partner institutions, logistics coordination, and documentation of learning outcomes.
sig_3299f37d3ba51203b947.title: 81322845-MAV+: Technical assistance for selected companies in the pharmaceutical sector in South Africa for the SAVax project

sig_329cb1105b32be4c0b46.description: Framework contract for scientific, technical and project-management support to ECDC for a multi-year, cross-sectional point prevalence survey (PPS) of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), antimicrobial use and infection prevention and control / antimicrobial stewardship structure and process indicators in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) in EU/EEA countries. The services will build on the previous HALT/LTCF PPS approach including: preparation and organisation of the PPS; development/adaptation of training materials, case studies, feedback-report templates and data-collection questionnaires; support to national PPS preparation and training; helpdesk, methodological and technical support to national contact points; support to data collection and data-quality checks; production of validated national databases; country- and LTCF-level feedback reports; analysis plans; early and final European survey reports; presentations/minutes for meetings; and related dissemination outputs including open-access fees for manuscripts. The contract also includes validation and additional analytical work to assess whether HAIs reported in LTCFs are correctly reported according to agreed case definitions, whether infections can be assessed as associated with healthcare in the LTCF context, and the impact of potential misclassification on PPS estimates. This may include protocol development for validation sub-studies, training and standardisation of validators, review of source documentation where available, inter-rater agreement analyses, sensitivity analyses, and methodological recommendations for future European LTCF PPS. Interested economic operators are encouraged to provide their feedback by completing the market analysis survey under the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/e5c0d4bf-4900-f38e-3601-8268f775aa58
sig_329cb1105b32be4c0b46.title: OHD/260934 Support to a point prevalence survey of healthcare-associated infections and antimicrobial use in long-term care facilities, including data validation and analysis

sig_32c27288b5bfc452d0eb.description: The contracting authority intends to introduce a digital solution to support an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programme. The aim is to digitally accompany patients along the entire perioperative treatment pathway – from preoperative preparation through to the inpatient stay and postoperative follow-up care – to promote guideline-compliant treatment, patient engagement and interdisciplinary cooperation. As part of market sounding, information is to be gathered on solutions available on the market. In particular, interest lies in: • the functional scope of the solution, • support for standardised ERAS treatment pathways, • options for patient communication and patient monitoring, • documentation and evaluation functions, • interfaces to hospital information systems and other relevant IT systems, • requirements for data protection and information security, • implementation and training effort, • operating and licensing models, and • experience from previously realised reference projects. The specification serves exclusively for market sounding in accordance with Section 28 of the VgV. It does not represent a final specification for a subsequent procurement procedure. The contracting authority is expressly interested in information on all market-available solutions that meet the described functional requirements. The contracting authority is aware of, among others, the solution from 'Encure'. The naming of this solution is done exclusively as an example of a solution available on the market and is not to be understood as a pre-determination for a specific product or a specific manufacturer. The subject of the market sounding is expressly the identification of all comparable solutions corresponding to the functional requirements. Minimum requirements for alternative providers In order for an alternative provider to be considered by the UKM as an equivalent alternative to Encare, it should demonstrably fulfil all of the following requirements: 1. Official recognition by the ERAS® Society • Evidence of an official partnership or authorisation by the ERAS® Society. • Possibility for international ERAS® certification of the participating clinics. • Evidence that several university hospitals have already been successfully certified according to this standard. 2. Complete ERAS® programme portfolio • Availability of the currently eleven established specialist ERAS® programmes: o Liver surgery o Pancreatic surgery o Colorectal surgery o Breast reconstruction o Cardiac surgery o Gynaecology o Head and neck surgery o Hip and knee arthroplasty o Thoracic surgery o Urology/cystectomy o Bariatric surgery • Additionally, availability of the ERAS® Essentials programme as a standardised basis for the development and implementation of further treatment pathways. • Evidence that new treatment pathways for further specialist areas (e.g. transplant surgery, oesophageal surgery, gastric surgery or other highly specialised areas) can be developed, implemented and quality-assured jointly with the UKM via the ERAS® Essentials programme • Possibility to gradually expand the programme to almost all surgical departments of the UKM while utilising synergies between the clinics. • Availability of a standardised digital prehabilitation module as an integral component of the ERAS® programme for the structured preoperative preparation of patients 3. Evidence of successful implementations • Documented implementation of comparable programmes at several university tertiary care centres • Evidence of a sustainable improvement in ERAS compliance, treatment quality and clinical outcomes • Evidence of standardised implementation with experienced multidisciplinary teams 4. International audit and benchmarking platform • Provision of an established, digitised and web-based data platform for the standardised recording of perioperative data • Continuous audit, compliance monitoring and international benchmarking • Long-term use of the data for quality management and scientific projects • Provision of extensive filtering, analysis and visualisation functions for the systematic evaluation of the collected data • Possibility to analyse and present correlations between process quality (ERAS® compliance) and clinical treatment outcomes in a standardised manner 5. Migration of existing data • Complete takeover of the EIAS data already collected at the UKM • Preservation of historical quality data and comparability with previous benchmarks • Evidence that no loss of scientifically relevant data or quality indicators occurs 6. Scientific infrastructure • Support for multicentric scientific projects • Standardised data collection for registries, studies and publications • International comparability of the collected data • Possibility for long-term use of the data for research and quality assurance 7. Reference and training centre • Possibility to establish the UKM as an official reference and training centre • Authorisation to conduct official training courses, hospitations and implementation programmes • International visibility within the ERAS® network 8. Sustainable implementation • Structured knowledge transfer with the aim of being able to carry out future implementations at the UKM largely independently • Evidence that external consultancy services can be reduced in the long term • Use of existing implementation structures and synergies within the UKM 9. Economic equivalence • Evidence that no additional implementation, training, certification or migration costs are caused Please send your expression of interest to vvgm@ukmuenster.de.
sig_32c27288b5bfc452d0eb.title: ERAS-Softwarelösung

sig_32d329c2612c9ff67eeb.description: In accordance with Government Decision (H.G.) No. 592/2024 on the organisation and operation of the Ministry of Justice, as subsequently amended and supplemented, the MJ draws up public policies, strategies and action plans in the field of justice, the prevention and combating of corruption and serious forms of crime, including in accordance with the objectives of the governing programme, and negotiates, implements, monitors and evaluates international technical and financial assistance programmes for the prevention of crime and corruption, regardless of the beneficiary institution or the one implementing them. Currently, the Ministry of Justice provides the legislative IT application legislatie.just.ro, a website dedicated to both individuals and legal entities. The purpose of the platform is to facilitate public access to official information on normative acts issued by Romanian state institutions, thereby contributing to legislative transparency and a better understanding of the legal framework in force. The general objective consists in modernising the legislatie.just.ro legislative platform, in order to ensure legislative transparency, accessibility and a better understanding of the national normative framework by citizens and interested institutions. The modernisation of the IT platform will contribute to: – Facilitating public access to official information through an updated, secure and efficient technological infrastructure. – Increasing the quality and efficiency of digital public services by aligning with European standards and improving the end-user experience. – Optimised interconnection with European legislative portals (e.g. N-Lex), thereby supporting integration into an international legislative network. – Increasing the number of users and traffic on the legislative platform by implementing modern functionalities that meet current requirements. The impact of the modernisation is complementary to other initiatives of the institution aimed at digitising and making public services more efficient. Clarifications schedule: Requests for clarifications shall be transmitted via the SEAP portal at www.e-licitatie.ro. Deadline for receiving requests for clarifications: 21 days before the deadline for submitting tenders in SEAP. According to art. 161 of Law No. 98/2016 as subsequently amended and supplemented, to the extent that clarifications are requested in good time, the contracting authority's response to these requests shall be published in S.E.A.P on the 11 day before the deadline set for the submission of applications/tenders. Responses to requests for clarifications shall be published in S.E.A.P. by the contracting authority in a single stage, without disclosing the identity of the person who requested the clarifications. The specific objectives of the procurement target the modernisation of the legislatie.just.ro legislative platform, so that it meets current performance, accessibility and security requirements, ensuring an optimised user experience and facilitating legislative management. The implementation of the solution will follow a modular, scalable and secure architecture, complying with European interoperability and accessibility standards. In order to achieve the objectives established by the purchaser through the documentation, stages/activities have been structured in the Specifications as follows: 1. Activity No. 1 (A1)- Project management activities; 2. Activity No. 2 (A2)- Detailed analysis and design activities; 3. Activity No. 3 (A3)- Software component development and testing activities; 4. Activity No. 4 (A4) -Environment installation and configuration activities; 5. Activity No. 5 (A5)-Transition activities to the new system and migration of existing data; 6. Activity No. 6 (A6)- Warranty and support activities. The technical requirements requested by the Purchaser can be found in Section II - Specifications, part of the tender documentation.

Within the framework of a works contract, extension and software maintenance of licences (right of use) related to the "AVAYA Contact Center" system, as well as manufacturer support. Furthermore, ensuring availability and an on-call system for receiving fault reports and initiating troubleshooting for malfunctions that have occurred in the operation of the telephone switchboard and endpoint devices (AVAYA Experience Portal IVR, DSR and SBC devices), as well as remote and on-site troubleshooting. Requested support services: Mediated manufacturer product support and software maintenance for the Contact Center and related components are required with continuity of rights until 2026.08.31. Operational support from the first day of the month following the entry into force of the contract until 2026.08.31. sig_33000f3352f4e6bdda41.description: According to SURF and its members, the future of ICT and associated services for education and research lies to a significant extent in the cloud. The members (institutions) therefore wish to be able to make flexible use of the cloud and combine it with their own ICT infrastructures (hybrid infrastructure). In practice, transitioning to the cloud is not a simple step, and for many institutions, little experience has been gained with it. As a result, unexpected challenges can arise during the execution of cloud projects as well as in the subsequent management phase. The initially intended benefits are then not achieved, which can lead to a risk of failure or capital destruction. To support institutions with these challenges, it is therefore desirable to make SURFcumulus Professional Services available to them via a SURF tender. SURF has chosen to conduct this via a DPS. The delivery of SURFcumulus Professional Services is explicitly linked to the SURFcumulus service. Specifically, this concerns executive, common services intended for cloud implementation, migration, and management. Delivery takes place on the basis of a fixed price and a fixed delivery date. A further description of the service components is as follows: Setting up a cloud landing zone, integrated into an institution's existing (hybrid) architecture, at least including: Account setup: based on the administrative organisation, compliance guidelines, existing environments, and structures of the institution. Network configuration: according to guidelines, within cloud environments and between on-premise and these cloud environments. Security baseline: identity and access management based on SURFconext, availability of standardised, hardened machine images, security policies, network monitoring, and log analytics. Automation: standardised setup of security, governance, and cost optimisation. Executing/supporting cloud migrations, by means of: Lift-and-shift migration scenario: moving (part of) an ICT infrastructure from a data centre to the cloud without major changes. Re-design migration scenario: making (part of) an existing ICT infrastructure cloud-ready and/or implementing replacement, newly built solutions so that the potential of the cloud can be optimally utilised. Delivering cloud managed services in the (hybrid) cloud infrastructure, including, for example: Operations (account management, software update management, licence management, network management, backup & restore, monitoring, platform management) Application management (technical application management, functional application management, data management, application configuration management) Service support (incident, problem & change management, multi-vendor coordination, second and third-line support, escalation handling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity, cost, and continuity management) Information security and privacy protection (detection, prevention, reporting, adjustment). See further the added document "Toelatingsleidraad DAS SURFcumulus Professional Services".
sig_33000f3352f4e6bdda41.title: DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023

sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.
sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?

sig_3304045744b019976a73.description: By implementing this contract, the public contracting authority pursues the fulfilment of the objectives of the Prievidza City Data Management project, implemented on the basis of the call "Support for the development of creation, processing, utilisation and interconnection of data within public administration for intelligent decision-making, planning and management." The contract is divided into two separate parts, each of which will be subject to separate evaluation. The main objectives of the project include the collection, management and systematic, efficient storage of data acquired in the processes of the City of Prievidza, achieving efficiency and consistency of the provided and processed/presented data at the level of the City of Prievidza, and increasing the quality level and quantity of data provided in specific life situations to individual electronic services. The subject of the contract is also the establishment of a new GIS technological solution, the collection of data (spatial and descriptive) on objects from defined areas and the subsequent delivery of the data set, its referencing and provision for further processing and publication by the city's systems. The contract will also address the establishment of registration, analytical and presentation tools for spatial data. The centralisation of spatial data will enable their systematic updating, sharing and making available within the public administration and will allow easier access to them for citizens and entrepreneurs. By implementing this part of the contract, the public contracting authority aims to comprehensively resolve the collection and management of data of registration objects in its environment, while aiming for the unambiguous referencing of any data based on information on the reference nature of the source or mechanism that assesses the level of credibility as well as the temporal relevance of any data source. The objective is to create a central data repository (DATA HUB) that will contain a complete data model on the storage of data and relationships of all registration objects of the City of Prievidza's systems and will ensure centralised data management, which will take place via an integration bus ensuring the communication of individual information systems and modules operated at the level of the City of Prievidza through services. The project is intended to bring efficient, secure and standardised data integration between the city's information systems and state systems. Details of the description of the subject matter of the contract in this part of the contract are in the Tender Documents.
sig_3304045744b019976a73.title: ESTABLISHMENT OF A UNIFIED MUNICIPAL DATA MANAGEMENT FOR THE CITY OF PRIEVIDZA

sig_3326adccce916fc6eb24.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) seeks to advance its mission through the continued support of the Immune Drivers of Autoimmune Disease (IDAD) network. This network aims to understand the earliest steps and triggers leading to autoimmunity and flare in humans, with the vision of ultimately preventing autoimmune disease. Priorities include discovering pre-clinical immune mechanisms, developing autoimmunity risk and staging prediction tools and biomarkers, building preclinical cohorts, leveraging remote recruitment and sampling, and artificial intelligence (AI)/big data. This complex, sustained collaboration relies on shared infrastructure to identify common triggers, pathways, and prevention opportunities. An Infrastructure Opportunity Fund (IOF) will be included in the initiative to provide the network the opportunity to conduct collaborative research projects. An IDAD Network Coordinating Center (NCC) will be responsible for administering the IOF and supporting additional coordinating activities amongst IDAD awardees, including the organization of Steering Committee meetings, resource sharing, data harmonization, sample sharing, and administering the IOF. Grant authorities that allow NIAID to forecast this opportunity are as follows: Sections 301 and 405 of the Public Health Service Act as amended (42 USC 241 and 284) and under Federal Regulations 42 CFR Part 52 and 2 CFR Part 2.
sig_3326adccce916fc6eb24.title: Immune Drivers of Autoimmune Disease

sig_332ac9ded4e88023b8e6.description: This ex-ante notice is published in addition to a planned negotiated procedure. For the proper operation of the model medical degree programme at the Lausitz Medical University - Carl Thiem, the use of a specialised software solution for integrated timetable, room, group and lecturer planning as well as course registration is strictly necessary. The degree programme is characterised by very high planning complexity. This arises in particular from rotation- and model-based curricula, small-scale medical teaching formats, changing small and extra-small groups, the integration of clinical teaching locations, and the necessity of medical-specific course registration with mandatory attendance. Several tens of individual appointments per semester must be planned taking into account rooms, travel times, groups, teaching capacities and didactic dependencies. Manual or semi-manual planning is organisationally unachievable, non-scalable and highly prone to error. Without a suitable software solution, there is a considerable risk of overlaps, capacity errors, delays in study operations and failure to comply with organisational and legal requirements. The procurement is therefore a mandatory prerequisite for ensuring stable, transparent and rule-compliant teaching operations, for the medical-specific integration of timetabling and course registration, and for the further development of the study provision of the Lausitz Medical University - Carl Thiem.
sig_332ac9ded4e88023b8e6.title: Procurement of a software solution for integrated timetable, room, group and lecturer planning as well as course registration for the model medical degree programme

sig_33d771385e8bdf36a5a9.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) is the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system for the procurement of services consisting in the processing of socio-economic and similar studies and analyses in the field of immovable infrastructure, the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities, consultancy services and expert support from the founding/establishing entity for individual legal entities within the contracting authority's remit, the preparation of analyses of the Czech defence industry and analyses of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure, under the conditions set out in the tender documentation (in detail in the tender documentation). The subject matter will be in particular the acquisition of comprehensive information important for evaluating and mapping the consequences of increased expenditure and defence requirements in the medium and long-term outlook. This primarily concerns the Czech economy (for example, the labour market, support for science and research, regional development or involvement in EU funds and other financial mechanisms), society in the Czech Republic and international cooperation. Processing of the analysis of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure and requirements with regard to the commitments undertaken by the Czech Republic at the NATO summit in The Hague in June 2025; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the provision and submission to the Ministry of Defence of comprehensive information on the actual state of capabilities and capacities of the domestic industry and research organisations, focusing in particular on capabilities in the field of development, production and logistical support of military material, training of technical personnel, training and fulfilment of mobilisation supplies; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities and contributing to the increase of their profitability, the provision of consultancy services and expert support to increase the efficiency of the performance of the function of the founder or establishing entity for individual legal entities within the remit of the Ministry of Defence; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular activities consisting in the provision of studies that will deal with the evaluation of both positive and negative impacts of construction on employment, the economy, transport, social and technical infrastructure, the environment (sustainable development) and the provision of public and private services in the area. The content of the studies will also include the identification of entities responsible for the prevention of risks and the resolution of arisen risks and proposals for measures that could eliminate, resolve or prevent the arisen risks, as well as the preparation of recommendations for the amendment of relevant strategic documents. The subject matter will also in certain cases include the preparation of presentations intended for concerned public administration stakeholders; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the analysis of the process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, the preparation and submission of a proposal for a new process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, including implementation steps and the provision of consultancy services during implementation; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).

sig_340ee90a950351779337.description: I. Background and purpose: Rigspolitiet (contracting authority) is tendering for the operation, maintenance, support and further development of a portfolio of the contracting authority's existing IT systems. The tender includes 21 IT systems, a number of supporting runs and programmes, a common infrastructure, cross-cutting environments (collectively referred to as the 'system portfolio') and integrations between these. In addition, shared services such as an SFTP gateway and transformation service are used. The majority of the system portfolio is based on a mainframe platform and a smaller part of the system portfolio on midrange platforms. The system portfolio consists of a number of socially critical IT systems, such as POLSAS, the Criminal Register and the Passport Register, which are currently operated and maintained by the contracting authority's existing supplier. The system portfolio is of crucial importance for supporting the contracting authority's tasks and is characterised by significant complexity and volume. Some of the systems date back to the 1980s and the beginning of the 1990s — and are referred to as 'legacy systems'. It is the contracting authority's requirement that, in the delivery of the services, cf. section II, focus is placed on operational stability and system availability. This is achieved through the delivery of scalable services and a contingency plan that can ensure the maintenance of availability during operational incidents. It is also the contracting authority's requirement that the services include continuous optimisation and are operated in a resource-efficient manner. The contracting authority has implemented the tendered system portfolio for both the mainframe and midrange platforms in such a way that the individual systems have a number of technical dependencies in relation to the underlying infrastructure and software. With this tender, the contracting authority wishes to ensure up-to-date contract terms, optimal supplier management, market-compliant prices as well as predictability and transparency in services and pricing. In addition, the contracting authority requires that the contracting authority and/or a third party appointed by the contracting authority can take back all or parts of the system portfolio, and that the performance of all or parts of the services can be taken over by the contracting authority or a third party appointed by the contracting authority. II. Services: The services are described below in relation to the overall system portfolio. The tender documents will contain a more detailed description of the individual elements of the system portfolio. Main services: A) Infrastructure operation and maintenance: Infrastructure operation and maintenance includes the provision, operation and maintenance of the system portfolio's infrastructure. The service also includes, among other things, the provision of housing facilities for the contracting authority's own hardware and software. B) Application operation: Application operation includes the operation of the system portfolio's applications, as well as integration with other systems and with the underlying infrastructure. C) Application maintenance: Application maintenance includes the implementation of relevant software and security updates and continuous informing of the contracting authority about new software updates, continuous handling and remediation of errors in the system portfolio's applications as well as preventive maintenance. In addition, the service includes the optimisation of applications in the contracting authority's system portfolio. D) Support: The support service includes support for the system portfolio through, among other things, the provision of a service desk for 3rd level support. The contracting authority or a third party appointed by the contracting authority handles 1st and 2nd level support. E) Further development: Further development includes projects that change the system portfolio, for example by expanding, altering and adjusting elements and parts thereof, as well as development resulting from maturation services. As part of the further development, the supplier must assist the contracting authority with the takeover of third-party software as well as with implementing third-party software in the system portfolio. Further development must be delivered at the request of the contracting authority. F) Transition: Transition includes both transition in (takeover) and out (handover). Transition in includes, among other things, the establishment of the operating environment for the system portfolio as well as the migration of the system portfolio from the contracting authority's existing supplier. There will be no takeover of hardware from the outgoing supplier or the contracting authority as part of the transition in. Transition out includes termination assistance, among other things, with a view to full or partial shutdown and/or any handover to a third-party supplier or the contracting authority itself. The transition includes a clarification of which personal data-related adjustments are necessary in relation to the supplier's role. Other services: G) Print: Print includes printing and delivery of output on other media. H) Maturation services: Maturation services include analyses which, among other things, aim to support the extension of the lifespan of the system portfolio or parts thereof, the taking back of a part of the system portfolio, the phasing out and shutdown of parts of the system portfolio, etc. Maturation services can furthermore lead to a need for modernisation of the system portfolio, which must be delivered in the form of further development, cf. E), or time-based services, cf. I). Maturation services must be delivered at the request of the contracting authority. I) Time-based services: The supplier must continuously deliver time-based services for the resolution of tasks related to the system portfolio. Time-based services are delivered by persons with competencies equivalent to the competencies required for the resolution of the other services described under section II. The services include, for example, contributions to the preparation of strategies, implementation of recommendations, optimisation of governance and modification of systems. Time-based services must be delivered at the request of the contracting authority. J) Knowledge transfer and co-location: The supplier must provide knowledge transfer, including any side-by-side training of the contracting authority's employees, in relation to any of the services covered by the tender and the system portfolio in general. The contracting authority must also be entitled to co-location. K) Reporting and monitoring: The supplier must provide reporting linked to the services covered by the framework agreement.
sig_340ee90a950351779337.title: Framework agreement on operation, maintenance, support and further development of Rigspolitiet's system portfolio

sig_343fbd80f5144d8c73f3.description: Consulting service for needs analysis and requirements definition in continuous learning Consulting service for needs analysis and requirements definition in continuous learning; Skatteverket will accept the tender that is most economically advantageous. The tender will be evaluated on the following basis: Best price-quality ratio. To determine the most economically advantageous tender, the added value model is used. The added value model is based on the principle that the evaluation criteria other than price assessed in the evaluation are given an added value in SEK and that this value is stated in the procurement document. This establishes the basis for a deliberate and business-like trade-off between price and stated evaluation criteria. In addition, the economic value attached to the various evaluation criteria is clarified. Each evaluation requirement is valued separately and assigned an economic value in SEK. Added values obtained in the evaluation are deducted from the tender sum. Higher requirement fulfilment yields a larger deduction than lower requirement fulfilment. The result is designated the tender's comparison sum. The tender with the lowest comparison sum is the most economically advantageous tender. The tender with the lowest comparison sum is considered to be the most economically advantageous and will be accepted.
sig_343fbd80f5144d8c73f3.title: Consulting service for needs analysis and requirements definition in continuous learning

sig_34403cfd253538b761f2.description: Dynamic Purchasing System - Qualification (DPSQ) for the Provision of Compliance Management Information System (CMIS) Solution. A Compliance Management Information System (CMIS) is a comprehensive digital system which supports all aspects of an organisation’s regulatory, compliance, quality management. It is made up of a number of different modules and functionalities, each one enables the user to carry out a specific type of activity, e.g. document management, non-conformance or audit actions. Using a CMIS allows a proactive rather than reactive approach to managing processes, as a result of improved document management and communications of related tasks. A CMIS solution is required to support, at a minimum, the development, configuration, integration, migration, management, review, analysis and reporting of data relating to quality and patient safety activities.

sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) National Center for Injury Prevention and Control (NCIPC) is soliciting investigator-initiated gold standard research proposals to rigorously evaluate programs and policies for their impact on primary prevention of child sexual abuse (CSA) or problematic sexual behavior (PSB) among youth. For the purposes of this NOFO: CSA is defined as sexual victimization during childhood (younger than 18 years of age) perpetrated by an adult. PSB is defined as sexual behaviors among children (younger than 18 years of age) that are not developmentally appropriate and have the potential to cause harm to the child or children involved (including behaviors that are unintentionally harmful or inappropriate as well as behaviors intended to cause harm). Research funded under this announcement will strengthen the evidence base for primary prevention of CSA and PSB. Applicants must propose to rigorously evaluate a program or policy for primary prevention of CSA or PSB that addresses one of the following three research priorities: Programs or policies focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in digital spaces (e.g., downloading or possession of illegal images of children, nonconsensual image sharing, use of artificial intelligence to create fake explicit images of children); Programs or policies addressing the use of digital spaces for commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) or sex trafficking (e.g., online recruitment of minors for sexual content creation, online advertisements soliciting minors for commercial sex acts, using technology to facilitate in-person meetings with minors for the purpose of sex); Organizational policy approaches focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in youth-serving organizations (e.g., community centers, youth development organizations, juvenile residential care facilities, faith-based organizations, group foster care).
sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.title: Rigorously Evaluating Approaches to Prevent Child Sexual Abuse and Problematic Sexual Behavior among Youth

sig_3477bbd5b69db61314bd.description: The evolution of markets from physical trading floors to interconnected, electronic venues has introduced new speed, transparency, and efficiency, but has also created new attack surfaces and systemic risks. Modern markets, which host trading for everything from equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources, can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers. The 2010 United States Equity market "flash crash" and the 2000-2001 California energy crisis demonstrated how weaknesses in a market's public interfaces could have dramatic consequences. Similar design issues in today's complex, interacting market systems could be used to cause economic damage, which the IMR program technology seeks to prevent. The IMR program aims to develop repair methods to protect essential economic sectors against devastating attacks that exploit the public interfaces of modern markets. Current legal and regulatory protections focus on deterring profit-seeking manipulation and ensuring compliance, but they do not sufficiently protect markets from adversaries aiming simply to cause disruption. The IMR program seeks to address this gap by developing the tools to automatically model market designs, identify hidden weaknesses, and recommend and analyze repairs on the market models to make markets fundamentally more resilient to attack. IMR aims to combine Large Language Model (LLM)-based automation with rigorous modeling and analysis to identify remediations for market weaknesses. The program will develop formal notations to precisely describe how markets operate and coordinate, creating machine-analyzable models from informal descriptions like regulatory filings and technical specifications. Against these models, IMR will formulate and assess "resilience conjectures” - mathematical statements about desirable market properties, such as the inability for actors to manipulate prices without risking loss. By automatically analyzing these conjectures, the program aims to prove that a market design is resilient in specific ways or, if it is not, to generate a counterexample that illustrates a concrete weakness. These counterexamples will then be used to refine the conjectures and, ultimately, to recommend and confirm specific repairs to the market's design. This approach is intended to provide a capability to protect U.S. markets against adversaries who wish to cause chaos, ensuring the stability of both civilian and military critical resources that rely on modern market mechanisms.
sig_3477bbd5b69db61314bd.title: Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR)

sig_348050f0afa61c23c367.description: The subject matter of the call for tenders is the procurement of state-of-the-art equipment for monitoring meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters. The project will develop an extensive, diverse and modern research infrastructure providing a wealth of data. The equipment will include mobile hydrometeorological radars, a low-frequency lightning detection network, meteorological and fire-meteorological stations, a computer system for meteorological data analysis and archiving, a data collection system for the calibration of meteorological and radiometric instruments, high-precision solar radiation measurement sensors, and hydro-telemetric stations, optical instruments and portable hydrometry equipment. Pre-existing meteorological, radiometric and hydrological measuring structures will be significantly upgraded and expanded, and a new standard fire-meteorological measuring network will also be developed. Self-propelled long-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted medium-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted short-range meteorological radar; Meteorological radar towing vehicle; Lightning discharge and atmospheric electricity detection network; Integrated high-precision system for the simultaneous measurement of the electrical outputs of multiple sensors, with simultaneous provision to a computer for further processing and analysis; Integrated automatic sun tracker for recording direct, diffuse and global solar radiation in accordance with WMO standards; Programmable scanning sky-dome spectroradiometer for measuring direct and diffuse solar radiation; Integrated autonomous modular system for measuring meteorological and/or agro-meteorological parameters
sig_348050f0afa61c23c367.title: Procurement of Specialised Scientific Equipment for the monitoring of meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters
