The software to be used is fixed, does not form part of the tendered service and is based exclusively on open source components. These include in particular: • Linux operating system (currently Debian), • Mapbender 2.8 (<3), • PostgreSQL with PostGIS, • MapServer, • Django framework, • MediaWiki. sig_385fb26148b2325dfc3a.description: Open procedure, pursuant to Article 71 of Legislative Decree No 36/2023, for the award of development, maintenance and management services for the information system of Fondimpresa (FPF System). A contract concerning the following activities shall be concluded with the successful tenderer of this procedure: i) Software development and enhancement (MEV) ii) Corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) iii) Housing, operation and hardware/software maintenance iv) Helpdesk (hereinafter also referred to solely as "Service" or "Services"), as better defined, described and set out in the technical specification attached to the tender specifications. A handover period with the new successful tenderer taking over at the end of the contract must be guaranteed, lasting at least 2 (two) months. Regarding the procedures for executing the contractual relationship, please refer to the provisions in paragraph 9 of the technical specification, without prejudice to compliance with the service levels referred to in paragraph 10 of the technical specification, failing which the penalties established therein shall apply. In order to outline the background context, notwithstanding what is better established in the technical specification, it is specified that Fondimpresa has acquired an information system (named "FPF System") for managing the training plans of the Training Account and the System Account, for communication between Fondimpresa, its regional offices and the member companies, for acquiring and managing membership data and contributions transmitted by INPS, as well as monitoring information to be sent periodically to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and for registering state aid with the RNA. The development of the Fund's activities, the diversification of training financing measures made available to member companies (via public notices), the increase in financing granted and the number of training plans managed, the steady growth in memberships and the evolution of monitoring specifications required by the guidance and supervisory authority, entail the need to guarantee: • evolutionary maintenance (MEV) of the FPF system; • corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) of the FPF system; • management of housing and operation services with particular attention to system monitoring activities and security aspect verification (penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, etc.); • management of the first and second-level helpdesk service; • the development of new document flow management features with a view to continuous and progressive paperless operation of the Fund's activities; • the integration of new tools based on artificial intelligence to automate and optimise human operational workflows; • architectural developments and hardware/software infrastructure modernisation interventions to ensure appropriate levels of security, efficiency and service continuity; • application support for the disaster recovery system. The currently estimated user base is approximately 280.000 users against approximately 210.000 contributing positions affiliated with Fondimpresa. The contract shall have a duration of 60 natural and consecutive months, commencing from the start date of activities determined by the date of a specific record of commencement of activities. For all services described in the preceding article, no interfering risks are identifiable for which specific safety measures need to be adopted and, therefore, the preparation of the DUVRI is not required (pursuant to Article 26, paragraph 3-bis, of Legislative Decree No 81/2008). Consequently, there are no safety costs of an interfering nature, which are therefore quantified as € 0,00. Since the tender procedure has as its object services of an intellectual nature (as these primarily concern software development and the elaboration of customised solutions, functional analysis and governance of system evolution), tenderers are not required to indicate, pursuant to Article 108, paragraph 9, of the Code, the amount of labour costs and company costs for fulfilling provisions regarding health and safety in the workplace. Please refer to the Tender Specifications and its attached technical specification for tender particulars. The contract consists of a single lot as it is characterised by the functional unity of the service. Therefore, it is considered appropriate, both from the perspective of economic efficiency and optimal service execution, not to proceed with a division into lots. In any event, the tenderer's future bid shall be understood to refer overall to the entirety of the services forming the subject matter of the tender.

sig_38986fa46939d895c50f.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_3898ee07fae00cf03225.description: The subject of the contracts awarded under the established DNS will be the procurement of cloud services corresponding to IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and other models, cloud service support services, cloud migration services, or other related services that meet the statutory conditions of publicly available services. Cloud services are services provided as services in the public part of the government cloud or in the form of a private government cloud. A special type of service is so-called cloud service management, which will also be available through the DNS. The subject of the sub-contract awarded within the DNS is Microsoft Azure Prepayment cloud services or their equivalent, in order to cover the operational and developmental needs of the Consolidated Analytical Layer project (hereinafter referred to as the "CAL") in the public part of eSKa Cloud, as well as the needs of the environments of public authority bodies (hereinafter referred to as "PABs") that are involved in the CAL project. Within the CAL project, individual PABs are operated as separate logical environments and at the same time integrated through the common analytical and integration layer of the CAL project. The CAL project represents a central data and analytical platform intended for the integration, processing, consolidation and analysis of data across participating PABs. Currently, 5 PABs are involved in the project, with another 7 PABs planned. Credits must be provided in the form of "upfront" (pre-paid), and they are not tied to specific cloud services. This model makes it possible to pay for the use of cloud resources in advance, instead of payment based on actual consumption. The subject of the contract is also the delivery of related complementary services for the optimisation of the CAL environment, re-validation of security policies, governance rules and the introduction of best practices in a number of a maximum of 30 person-days for a period up to 31.10.2026 (hereinafter referred to as "complementary services"). The contracting authority requires that the relevant complementary services be provided by an entity included in the Microsoft "Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (Azure Expert MSP)" programme or that the tenderer demonstrate, by confirmation from Microsoft, that the entity that will provide the complementary services is capable of providing services equivalent (equal) to the services provided by entities included in the Microsoft "Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (Azure Expert MSP)" programme. In the event that the contracting authority accepts an equivalent solution or the tenderer's equivalent product to Microsoft Azure cloud services (under the conditions for the equivalent stated below), the contracting authority will require that the complementary services be provided by an entity with an equivalent level corresponding to the level of "Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (Azure Expert MSP)" within the submitted equivalent solution/product to Microsoft Azure cloud services accepted by the contracting authority. As an equivalent level corresponding to the "Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (Azure Expert MSP)" programme within the equivalent solution to Microsoft Azure cloud services, the contracting authority will consider such a level of capability that is demonstrated in an objectively verifiable manner through an independent audit, partner expert programme, specialisation or similar third-party mechanism relating to the provision of cloud managed services. The demonstrated professional competence must cover in particular the areas of: cloud governance, security and compliance, identity management, network architecture, monitoring and operations, cost optimisation and cloud architecture design. sig_3899a8330c5609c16319.description: Despite the growing use on online services, understanding how disabled and neurodiverse individuals experience harms within these digital environments remains limited. Existing research, such as Ofcom’s findings, highlights that more individuals with limiting conditions see harmful content compared to those without, but these insights are fragmented and fail to capture escalating risks across different disabilities and neurodiverse conditions. Current strategies for harm reduction are largely advisory and rely on user vigilance, leaving substantial gaps in effective, systemic protections. Thus this project will attempt to address these concerns through a literature review looking into the online experience of disabled and neurodiverse users, and optional functionality review which would look at the current state of mainly social media sites to see if features or functions present could be adversely affecting users. Ending with a selection of interviews with users or those who represent the target demographics to see understand if the lived experiences match up with what was found within the previous stages. Lot 1: .

sig_38a995d9a50f8239283c.description: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service (CFRS) is currently conducting a soft market testing exercise in preparation for a future procurement of an Asset Management System. The aim is to identify a centralised solution capable of managing CFRS's critical assets and infrastructure, including fleet, operational equipment, and hydrants. Core Functional Requirements; Any proposed Asset Management System must support the management of the following service areas: - Fleet Management (Vehicles, servicing schedules, defect reporting, cost tracking) - Operational Equipment Management (Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), Breathing Apparatus (BA) sets, radios, all operational equipment, servicing, and defect tracking) - Hydrant Management (Inspection, maintenance, water schemes, compliance monitoring, and mapping) Desirable (Non-Essential) Capabilities; - Property Asset Management - ICT Asset Management Minimum System Capabilities The system must be able to deliver, at a minimum, the following functionalities: - Centralised storage of all critical asset data - Scheduling and management of routine and ad hoc maintenance/testing - Defect reporting and escalation workflows based on urgency - Automated alerts and reminders for servicing and inspections - Integration with stock control and ordering systems - Full asset history tracking (maintenance, testing, usage) - Servicing and maintenance records - Generation of compliance-ready reports - Remote access via tablets or mobile devices with internet connectivity - Multi-user access from any location - Seamless integration with CFRS's existing Finance and Procurement systems - Standard and custom reporting across all system data - QR code compatibility for asset identification and lifecycle tracking - User-friendly interface accessible via app or browser, supporting live data and mobile use - Support for multiple stations, locations, and asset types - Role-based access control, audit trails, data encryption, and single sign-on - Cloud-based or hybrid deployment with high availability Lot 1: .

sig_38b9bfe226350afe6221.description: This contract concerns the purchase, implementation and maintenance of an Applicant Tracking System (ATS), whereby the contractor is responsible for recruiting new employees. The objective is to manage the complete recruitment and selection process within a single tool, in a cloud application, where necessary or useful via integration with other internal and external platforms in order to guarantee a maximum efficient and automated operation. City Brugge, OCMW Brugge and the associations of the OCMW Brugge operate from a legislative framework (legal status regulations), which means that there are a number of additional needs compared to a company of a similar size from the private sector. These differences are not so much substantive in nature, but rather legal and procedural. The system must support a legally robust, transparent and objective process that complies with the principles of equality, non-discrimination, duty to state reasons and openness, with fixed procedures, uniform selection criteria and the necessary reporting capabilities. At the same time, the ATS must offer sufficient flexibility and user-friendliness for both the backend user and the applicant to manage lead times, improve candidate and user experience and allow a modern selection process.
sig_38b9bfe226350afe6221.title: Purchase, implementation and maintenance of an Applicant Tracking System (ATS)

sig_38be9a2051570e0ec6b8.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. sig_38cb6fa25d4e1b599b21.description: The Transmission System Operators (TSOs) of the Central Europe Capacity Calculation Region are conducting a preliminary market consultation on development and implementation of a Common IT platform and associated business capabilities to support the Coordinated Security Analysis (CSA) process which runs load-flow calculations, contingency analysis and allows for the coordination of remedial actions among participating parties. The tool shall support this “Common CSA process” in the day-ahead (DA) and intraday (ID) timeframes; first go-live of the common CSA process in the region is targeted for 2029, preceded by a parallel run. The intent is to publish a European tender in Q1 2027 for the CSA Platform. This common CSA solution is the first implementation step towards the long-term process goal, which also includes an optimization of remedial actions, and cost sharing thereof. To support this evolution, the solution for common CSA process must be designed for scalability and long-term sustainability, leveraging open standards, modular architecture, documented interfaces, and technologies that minimize dependency on proprietary products, vendor-specific expertise, or closed ecosystems. The common CSA solution should allow to be extended with additional business capabilities and modules over time (e.g. Remedial Action Optimization module, Cost-Sharing process), to support the target processes (Regional Operational Security Coordination and Cost Sharing).
sig_38cb6fa25d4e1b599b21.title: Market consultation - Coordinated Security Analysis (CSA) Platform

sig_38cd941ec3c72ffc2adf.description: The objective of HUS is to procure, via a dynamic purchasing system, the rights of use for basic and other off-the-shelf software it requires, as well as the associated software vendor support and maintenance services (hereinafter "software products") for the HUS server, cloud and terminal environment by entering into the necessary agreements with resellers and, where applicable, the principals of the software products. This may involve licences for traditional software products as well as rights of use for services delivered over the network. The software products may already be in use by HUS, in which case the procurement need stems, for example, from licence terms, changes in usage volume, operating platform or the like, expansions required by the social and healthcare reform, or maintenance required by an up-to-date version. In such cases, the call for competition within the dynamic purchasing system may target a named software product. Selection may be made between different software products if possible. The subject of the procurement also includes reseller services, such as planning for the customer-specific utilisation of software, consulting, modification, implementation, training, support and maintenance. The subject of the procurement is defined in more detail in the calls for competition within the dynamic purchasing system. The subject of an internal call for competition may be only part of the aforementioned services, for example, mere reselling of software products or mere reseller services. All software resellers that meet the suitability requirements will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Software vendors will also be accepted if they sell their own software directly and meet the suitability requirements.
sig_38cd941ec3c72ffc2adf.title: Software resale, support services and reseller services

sig_38d0f9268d6160d11e66.description: Coventry University Group is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to deliver Hosting, Licensing, Support and Maintenance Services for its Optimizely Digital Experience Cloud (DXC). These services are integral to the Group’s digital transformation efforts, ensuring continuous high performance and secure operations for online content. This section provides a formal justification for specifying Optimizely CMS as the required platform in this tender. The justification is made in accordance with the reasons below. Coventry University invites for suppliers to submit tender returns based on this justification, within the scope of an open tender. 1. Technical Interoperability and Continuity The existing digital infrastructure, including CRM, analytics, identity management, and content delivery systems, is tightly integrated with Optimizely CMS. Optimizely’s API-first architecture and support for headless delivery are essential for maintaining seamless interoperability with legacy systems and third-party services. Replacing Optimizely would require reengineering multiple integrations, introducing significant risk and cost. 2. Operational Efficiency and User Familiarity Internal teams are trained and certified in Optimizely CMS, and workflows are built around its content management and personalization capabilities. Transitioning to a new CMS would require retraining, reauthoring content, and revalidating accessibility and compliance standards, resulting in operational disruption. 3. Cost of Change and Proportionality A platform change would incur disproportionate University costs, including rebuilding templates and components, revalidating security and GDPR compliance, rewriting content migration scripts, and reintegrating with existing APIs and services. These costs are not justified given the maturity and suitability of the current Optimizely-based architecture. 4. Strategic Alignment and Future Scalability Optimizely CMS aligns with the organisation’s digital strategy, including goals for personalization, A/B testing, and omnichannel delivery. The platform supports future scalability, including cloud-native deployment and integration with AI-driven content tools. The Estimate value below is based on the initial three year contract. The extension options are two, one year extensions. Please note that a PME notice was not completed due to the timescales of the project. To view this notice, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/delta/viewNotice.html?noticeId=1001807385 Lot 1: .

sig_38d761b269c967c9db05.description: The subject of the performance is the supply, implementation and subsequent support of a comprehensive technical and organisational solution for increasing the cybersecurity of public administration information systems managed by the participating municipal districts. The solution is focused primarily on the appropriate fulfilment of the obligations of municipal districts as administrators of public administration information systems under Section 5b of Act No. 365/2000 Coll., on public administration information systems, in relation to the new legal regulation of cybersecurity and requirements for the long-term management of public administration information systems. The project is designed as a compact unit that integrates three key functional areas: log management, technical security monitoring and methodological support for the implementation of appropriate security measures for managed public administration information systems. The aim is to replace fragmented individual approaches with a unified central multi-tenant solution that will enable efficient management, consistent security monitoring, infrastructure cost sharing and methodological support while maintaining data and access isolation for individual municipal districts.

sig_38e0b72f571555448a16.description: International Media Support (IMS) seeks to establish a pool of qualified research providers through framework agreements to deliver recurring audience segmentation studies and related audience intelligence services across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. IMS reserves the right to enter into more than one framework agreement as a result of this tender. Across the region, disinformation, information manipulation, and declining trust in information sources continue to affect public discourse and democratic resilience. To design effective responses, media organisations, civil society actors, and other stakeholders require a deeper understanding of audience behaviours, information needs, media consumption habits, levels of trust, and vulnerability to harmful narratives. Through this tender, IMS aims to identify service providers capable of designing and implementing audience segmentation studies and related research in multiple countries across Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. The findings will support IMS and its partners in developing evidence-based strategies, content, engagement approaches, and interventions that strengthen information integrity and more effectively reach priority audiences. Applications are welcome from research companies, consultancies, academic institutions, and consortia with the required expertise and capacity to deliver high-quality audience research services across the target regions.
sig_38e0b72f571555448a16.title: Audience Research and Segmentation Studies in Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans

sig_38ece6f75cc2828eb819.description: SUBJECT: TWO-STEP BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (Solicitation FA8819-24-R-B003) FreeSol Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Space Systems Command (SSC) Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power (SZ-BC) Program Executive Office (PEO) Advanced Technology Transition Branch SECTION 1 - INTRODUCTION The Space Systems Command (SSC) Advanced Technologies Branch (SSC/SZET-BCET) and Contracting Branch (SSC/SZK) invites innovative technical approach concept papers addressing space and cyber technologies, to enable capabilities to counter emerging space threats. To enable the concepts espoused in the United States Space Force (USSF) Strategic Intent, investments need to be made and the USSF needs to leverage all sources of innovation, prototyping, and experimentation. In addition, the USSF will explore pathfinders to test assumptions, validate answers, and potentially field ad-hoc solutions. This effort was designed to help the SF further partner with industry, encourage innovation, and drive down system costs. This BAA champions these initiatives, develops a better understanding of requirements while rapidly addressing the need for integrated space and cyber solutions. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Contracts awarded based on responses to this BAA are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public law 98-369, “The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984.” This is an open, two-step (concept white paper followed by proposal) BAA that will be available for 60 months, through 23 February 2029. Concept papers should be submitted as specified in “Section 3, Part A” of this BAA. The Government will evaluate concept papers against the criteria stated in this announcement. Those Offerors whose concept papers are of interest may be invited to submit a formal proposal following the specifications provided in “Section 3, Part B” of this BAA. All Offerors submitting concept papers will be contacted by the Government by either (1) notifying them of a request for a formal cost and technical proposal by a specified date, (2) a request to extend the validity of the concept paper until funding can be secured, or (3) informing them that the proposed solution is not of interest to the Government. An invitation to submit a complete technical proposal, which includes a statement of work and a cost proposal, does not assure that the submitting organization will be awarded a subsequent contract. Use of Non-Government Advisors: The Government intends to use Government personnel for the White Paper review and evaluation of proposals. The Government reserves the right to use Federally Funded Research and Development Contractors (FFRDC), Systems Engineering and Integration (SE&I), Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA), or SSC Acquisition and Financial Support (SAFS) contractors who support SSC to provide technical and acquisition advisory support for evaluations of White Papers and proposals. The current list of organizations includes: Aerospace, MITRE, the System Engineering and Integration (SE&I) contractor Science Applications International (SAIC) and other contractors (e.g. AT&T Incorporated, Booz Allen Hamilton, LinQuest, SES, Stellar Solutions) the SSC Acquisition and Financial Support (SAFS) contractor (Tecolote Research) and Security Support Contractor ManTech International. The list also includes subcontractors to any of these listed organizations that are actively supporting SSC/SZ through these organizations. If those contractors change over the life of the BAA, the Government will advise in writing. The evaluators and support personnel will be bound by appropriate Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA) to protect proprietary and sensitive information. Additional NDAs will not be required; instead, a response to this BAA will be considered an implicit acknowledgement and acceptance of the fact that non-Government advisors will be assisting the Government in this process. Should the Offeror have any objections to specific companies and/or personnel from participating in the evaluation of proposals, written notification shall be provided to the Contracting Officer within ten (10) calendar days prior to the Offeror’s submission of proposals or concept papers. If there is an objection, the specific reason(s) for the objection(s) shall be stated in the written notification, and the specific support contractor of concern shall be identified. If an Offeror suspects or is aware of a potential or actual Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) or the appearance thereof they shall document the OCI in the concept paper and proposal. If a potential OCI or appearance thereof exists, the offeror shall submit the mitigation plan in place or to be put in place upon award with the concept paper and proposal. Awardees shall mitigate OCIs and shall be in compliance with FAR 9.5 – Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of Interest. OCI documentation associated with a white paper submission is not subject to any page limitations. The Government understands that information provided in response to this BAA is presented in confidence and may contain trade secrets, commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by: 18 USC 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 USC 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 USC 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Concept papers may be submitted electronically, via the appropriate communication channels (NIPR, SIPR, JWICS, SGN, SIC, etc.), to the Security POC, contracting officer, and contract specialist listed below: Contracting Officer: Security POC: 1LT Heeyeun Joo Mr. John Stelling NIPR: heeyeun.joo.1@spaceforce.mil NIPR: john.stelling.2@spaceforce.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Mr. Robert Chernoff NIPR: robert.chernoff@spaceforce.mil Concept papers shall reference the above BAA number in the subject/title of the response. Submissions shall be either PDF files or Microsoft Word Documents. This announcement is effective for five years from date of release. Concept papers may be submitted at any time during this period. The SSC/SZET Advanced Technologies Branch acknowledges that funding constraints may severely limit contract activities but anticipates the ability to execute a limited number of projects through this timeframe. Funding Information: The anticipated ceiling available for this effort is up to $99M over the BAA’s 5-year active period. The number of contract awards have not been predetermined and will depend on the scope and quality of proposals received. The Government’s requirement for technology maturation across all focus areas will balance the investments appropriately. Any award(s) is subject to the availability of funds and is at the discretion of the Government. The Government may terminate work at any time if it no longer meets Government requirements. The Government may choose to award partial, none, or the full scope of the work proposed. The Government maintains the right to request a data call which will be published via SAM.gov at any time. All companies will be permitted to respond to the call, regardless of any previous white paper submissions. Please contact the Contracting Officer for submission of any potentially SENSITIVE or CLASSIFIED MATERIAL. They will provide an appropriate secure email address at that time. SECTION 2 - AREAS OF RESEARCH INTEREST The objective of the Space Systems Command, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power (SSC/SZ-BC) Directorate is to develop, deliver, and sustain unrivaled space control capabilities to guarantee space superiority for our nation. The Directorate champions the nation’s space and cyber capabilities, as well as develops acquisition transition paths to support requirements. Proposals utilizing technology with a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3 or higher are desired; justify TRL using DoD Technology Readiness Assessment (TRA) Guidance. Topics of interest for this BAA are listed below followed with examples from each of the five topics. Proposals need not be limited solely to those provided as examples but do need to trace to one of the overarching five topics. Resiliency technologies and techniques that increase survivability of space systems: Proliferation strategies Commercial standards and multi-domain reuse Dataflows and information sharing Redundancies Rapid reconstitution Improvements to Space Domain Awareness (SDA) that enhance the knowledge of space objects, status, activities, threats and environment to enable courses of action: Low cost and resilient ground-based SDA Low size, weight, & power space-based SDA Ground/Space space-weather sensors Optics Innovative abilities to exploit space to its advantage for defensive and offensive counterspace to protect friendly space-related capabilities from attack: Capability gap studies Cyber capabilities Phenomenology (active & passive) Satellite servicing Efficiencies that promote Battle Management Command Control and Communications (BMC3) Space data analytic tools for large data sets and networks Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation for Space operations Methods for advancing exercises, tests, and training environment: Ride share opportunities Innovative solutions across multiple domains Inter-satellite link for small satellites SECTION 3 – GUIDELINES FOR PREPARATION AND SUBMISSION OF CONCEPT PAPERS AND PROPOSALS This is an open, two-step (concept paper followed by proposal) BAA. The purpose of the concept paper is to minimize stakeholders’ effort if the proposed work is not of interest to the Government. Accordingly, Offerors are encouraged to submit concept papers following the guidelines detailed below (Section 3 Part A). Concept submissions should specifically identify the focused capabilities listed in Section 2 above stating how they are enhancing operationally focused capabilities. All Offerors will receive written response on the submitted concept paper. For concepts which funding has not yet been identified but are applicable to the Government, will receive a request to extend the validity of the submission. Offerors are encouraged to submit proposals following the guidelines detailed below (Section 3 Part B) after they have submitted a concept paper and have been notified of the Government’s interest in receiving a full proposal. The Government intends to award Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) or Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contracts. Offerors whose concept papers were not deemed to be of interest are not precluded from submitting other concept papers for consideration. An invitation to submit a complete proposal, which includes a statement of work and a cost proposal, does not assure that the submitting organization will be awarded a subsequent contract. Guidelines for All Submissions Offerors are hereby advised that the Government will not pay for any White Paper or full proposal preparation costs resulting from this BAA. The cost of preparing White Papers and full proposals is NOT an allowable direct charge to any resulting contract that may be awarded as a result of this BAA, or any other contract with the Government. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Concept papers and proposals should be created using 8.5 x 11 inch portrait format pages with single spaced Times New Roman 12 point font with 1” margins. Landscape is acceptable for charts and graphs only. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. Multiple concept papers addressing different topic areas may be submitted by the same Offeror, however each concept paper may only address one concept based on the stated Government areas of research interest (Section 2). Organizations may not submit multiple concept papers addressing the same area of research interest. Submitters may update a current concept paper or proposal at any time during the announcement period. Guidance regarding data calls supersedes restrictions in this paragraph. On the title page of the submission, identify if the Offeror or a proposed sub-contractor is a small business such as 8(a), small disadvantaged business, woman-owned business, HUBZone small business, Veteran-owned business, service disabled veteran owned business, historically black college or university, and/or minority institution. The technical and cost information will be evaluated at the same time during the concept paper evaluation process. Foreign-Owned businesses may be a submitter alone or through some form of teaming arrangement with one or more United States-owned businesses. The ability to obtain a contract may depend on whether the Government information (1) necessitates clearance of the business under a Special Security Agreement and (2) approval of a National Interest Determination (see 10 U.S.C. 2536(b)(1)(A), DoD 5220.22-M, and AFI 31-601) that release of proscribed information to the foreign-owned business shall not harm the national security interests of the United States. Failure to obtain the clearance or denial by the cognizant authority of release of the proscribed information to the foreign-owned business would preclude award of a contract. Submissions shall be shared at the appropriate classification level. Please send to the Security POC or contact via phone for transmission instructions on SIPR / JWICS, questions or additional guidance, if required. All classified material must be handled in accordance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) (DoD 5220-22-M) and Industrial Security Regulation (DoD 5220.22-R). Offerors must be able to certify that they have an appropriate facility clearance to meet the security requirements of work proposed, and key personnel must be certified as holding an appropriate security clearance. The security clearance level required for these efforts is up to TS/SCI. Facility Clearance level will be documented in the DD254 of any resultant contract and documents will be classified in accordance with the Security Classification Guides to be provided during the RFP phase, as appropriate. Identification of Partner Agency: Within the concept paper submission an Offeror may identify a Government agency that may be interested in pursuing and funding the concept presented, as long as such concept is within the scope of a BAA (FAR 35.016(a)), within scope of this BAA focus areas listed in Section 2, and not a known requirement of the partnering agency. sig_38f9167cefaca6d43aca.description: 1. Contracting Authority Joint requirement of Hamburger Wasserwerke GmbH & Hamburger Stadtentwässerung AöR The contracting authority is an operator of critical infrastructure in the field of water supply and wastewater disposal and operates a distributed IT and OT system landscape. 2. Objective of the market exploration The contracting authority intends to introduce a central solution for the secure control and execution of remote access to IT and OT systems. The goal of this market exploration is to gain an overview of solutions available on the market as well as different technical and organisational approaches. In particular, insights are to be gained regarding: • Suitable solution architectures • Technical implementation options for remote access • Operating and support models • Licence and cost structures • Scalability and volume structures • Typical procedural models for the introduction of corresponding solutions • BSI compliance and certifications The market exploration serves exclusively to prepare for a possible procurement procedure and does not constitute a call for tenders. 3. Initial situation The contracting authority currently operates a distributed infrastructure with: • Various administrative, plant or operational sites • Own data centres • Diverse IT and OT systems External service providers access various systems in the context of maintenance, troubleshooting, updates and project work, including: • IT systems (e.g. servers, applications, databases) • OT systems (e.g. technical installations) Heterogeneous solutions and procedures currently exist for remote access. 4. Target image (functional requirements) A solution is sought that supports in particular the following requirements: • Central control and management of remote access • Support for internal and external user groups • Granular role and authorisation concept • Approval-controlled and time-limited access • Logging and traceability (auditability) • Support for access to IT and OT systems • Secure connection architecture (e.g. via mediation instances / DMZ) • Scalability for a distributed infrastructure The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches. 5. Operating and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services in operation are also expected. The contracting authority generally operates the solution itself (e.g. administration and user management), but requires support in particular in the following areas: • Maintenance and updating of software components • Maintenance and, if necessary, replacement of hardware components • Technical support • Support for malfunctions and error analysis • Execution of updates and release changes Approaches for supported in-house operation as well as possible alternative operating models are sought. 6. Questions to the market The contracting authority requests interested companies to provide feedback on the following points: Solution & Architecture • What solution approaches do you offer for secure remote maintenance and access to IT and OT systems? • How is the control and approval of access implemented? • Which components are typically required (software, hardware)? • What experience do you have with the integration of your solution into Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems? Operation & Organisation • How is user and rights management carried out? • How is audit-proof logging and traceability ensured? • What operating and support models do you offer? (SaaS, On-Prem, hybrid) • What experience do you have with customer-internal operating efforts during/after the introduction of the solution? Scaling & Costs • How can your solution be scaled technically and organisationally if additional sites, systems or users are connected (e.g. regarding required components, performance, operating effort and costs)? • Which licence and price models are typically used for your solution (e.g. by users, sites, infrastructure or usage)? • What price indication is to be expected for your solution and which factors significantly influence the pricing? Introduction & Implementation • How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. reference project structure or phase model)? • What timeframe is expected for the introduction of your solution based on experience? • Which success factors and typical challenges should be considered on the customer side in order to successfully introduce your solution (e.g. roles, processes and requirements)? • What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in the environment of critical infrastructure, especially in the water sector? 7. Participation and further procedure Interested companies are requested to submit their feedback by 24.08.2026, 12:00 o'clock via ausschreibungen@hamburgwasser. The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the above-mentioned questions are answered. On the basis of the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to conduct in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. In this case, the signing of an NDA is necessary. Participation in the market exploration is voluntary and non-binding. The contracting authority reserves the right to carry out a procurement procedure based on the results.

sig_38ff39f46aa4f8f627f0.description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. The platform supports traceability, information exchange and risk management in the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) area. The contract will also support interoperability with local systems and relevant international platforms, as well as gradual alignment with the EU IMSOC approach, including TRACES NT, RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS-related functionalities, where relevant. Maintenance, support, further development and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is based on the TRACES NT source code provided by the European Commission’s DG SANTE to CEFTA and adapted to support SPS processes and information exchange within CEFTA. The platform supports the electronic processing, issuance and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and other SPS-related documentation and data, as well as traceability, information exchange and risk management between competent administrations. A key objective of the contract is to further develop CEFTA TRACES NT towards fully electronic, end-to-end exchange of phytosanitary and veterinary certificates within CEFTA and, progressively, with the European Union, reducing and ultimately replacing paper-based exchanges where the necessary technical conditions are in place. This will include further development of electronic certification workflows, certificate models, validation mechanisms, electronic signatures and trust services, and the interfaces required for electronic data exchange. The contract will also support the completion, further development and operationalisation of the CEFTA Notification System for plant health and food and feed safety, including notifications concerning risks, non-compliant consignments, rejections and related follow-up information. The contract will cover continuous maintenance, security, performance and reliability of the platform, as well as upgrades and new functionalities required to respond to evolving operational needs. It will also support interoperability with local SPS systems of CEFTA Parties and relevant EU and international systems, including the further development of interfaces and automated data exchange to minimise duplicate data entry. Further development will seek to maintain close technical alignment with the EU IMSOC environment and TRACES NT, as well as relevant notification and information-exchange processes linked to RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS, where applicable. The overall objective is to establish a progressively integrated SPS digital environment enabling reliable electronic exchange of certificates, notifications and other SPS information within CEFTA and between CEFTA and the EU.
sig_38ff39f46aa4f8f627f0.title: CEFTA TRACES NT Maintenance, Expansion and SPS Digital Systems Support

sig_392f0229956d45312cc4.description:
Framework agreement for the performance of media research (market and public opinion research) tasks for Nemzeti Média- és Hírközlési Hatóság in accordance with point II.2.4) and the procurement documents. The total framework amount of the framework agreement is 900 000 000 plus VAT. Objective of the research, research questions Through data collection, we would like to gain a comprehensive picture of the podcast listening habits of the Hungarian population. The core of the research would be a questionnaire survey, which would be supplemented by focus group research. Within the framework of the questionnaire-based research, we are primarily seeking an answer to which and how large a segment of society listens to podcasts, possibly programmes that were previously published in a radio media service. • The questions would include whether they regularly listen to podcast channels, if so which ones, and apart from these what others they know, which media channel they prefer for following talk shows? • On which platform do they listen to them? Do they use different applications, online aggregator sites? Where and in what situation do they consume podcasts? • Measurement of social involvement. The questions would include, for example, whether their political conviction is an important factor in podcast selection, whether they know which political side the given podcast belongs to (if current affairs), whether they discuss what they hear in the podcast with acquaintances, whether they feel a close relationship with those who listen to the same podcast, whether they follow the host or guests of the show on social platforms? • The criterion for participation in the focus group discussion is to listen to podcasts on a weekly basis, preferably a variety of them. We would like to conduct the sessions in at least three different settlements (Budapest, county seat, smaller settlement). We carry out the study divided into two age groups per settlement, forming a younger and an older age group. We therefore envisage a total of six groups, with approximately 8-10 persons participating on each occasion. During the focus group discussion, we hope to get answers to what they base their choice of podcast channels on, how important the "personal charm" of the content creator is, their proven track record on other media channels (host recognition). Where does podcast listening rank in comparison with other traditional media channels? Has listening to podcast channels changed their media consumption habits, and related to this: did they previously listen to radio, internet radio, do they listen now? Prescribed methodology • Conducting a CAPI population quantitative survey research with 1000 persons, the length of the interview must not exceed 30 minutes. • Conducting 8 group focus group research, executing 8 person 2 group research, the duration of which must not exceed 90 minutes. • during the research, representativeness must be maintained with regard to gender, age group, type of settlement, educational attainment among internet users older than 16 years. • during the focus group survey, care must be taken to ensure that Budapest, county seats and villages are also represented. Deliverables • Handover of database in .sav and .xlsx format (containing the results of the questionnaire research) • short study in word and pdf format • detailed study in word and pdf format • text transcript related to qualitative researches • video recording made of the focus group research; Objective of the research, research questions The main questions of the research are grouped around the following topics: • How many different bubbles do consumers inhabit? • What proportion of society lives in individual opinion bubbles and what proportion moves between them? • Which bubbles do cross-media consumers move between? • Are there bubbles completely detached from the mainstream and what are these? • What media products do people in the different bubbles consume? (The questionnaire should cover TV channels, radio stations, print media and place greater weight on online news portals, influencers and podcasts.) • Which media products are closely tied to individual bubbles and which span across multiple bubbles? • What is the membership size of each bubble? • What is the homogeneity of each bubble (cluster analysis, we would also like to see a dendrogram)? • What socio-demographic characteristics are typical of the membership of each bubble? • What is the relationship network of individual media products? (Network analysis in which the edge weights are given by respondents' joint consumption of media product pairs. We would also like to see a graph/relationship network of the media products.) • Separate examination of the online world based on the above questions. • Analysis of individual age groups based on the above questions. • Deeper analysis of individuals forming the hard core of the bubbles. • Attitude measurement with 10-15 statements, with the help of which some interesting things can be revealed about the members of each bubble (e.g., belief in democracy, happiness, trust in institutions/people, positive outlook on the future, patriotism, subjective well-being, importance of family). The media consumption habits of the population cannot be derived individually from the audience measurements of individual media types, as a complex media consumption measurement taken on an identical sample is not available that would be suitable for measuring cross-consumption and simultaneous media consumption habits. The survey would be prepared by combining offline and online methods with the questioning of five thousand people. Prescribed methodology • Conducting 5 population quantitative survey research with 1000 persons using CAWI methodology • the duration of the survey must not exceed 30 minutes Deliverables • respondent-level cleaned, formatted, labelled, missing-value-handled, weighted .sav and .txt format database related to quantitative survey data collection; • short study in word and .pdf format (10-15 pages); • detailed study in .word and .pdf format (minimum 40 pages); Further detailed requirements are contained in the Technical Specification and the Draft Contract forming part of the procurement documents.; The current legal provisions regarding the age rating of film works screened in cinemas entered into force in 2012. In Hungary, every film work screened in cinemas or published on some data carrier must be classified prior to screening for the protection of minors. Domestic age rating is not a prohibitive provision, but an informative recommendation, which primarily provides information for parents and families. Since access is not directly prevented, domestic regulation places the emphasis above all on information, thus striving to spread the age rating suggested for the given film as widely as possible. While as a general rule the recommended age category must be published on all advertisements and announcements related to the film work, the film's age rating is increasingly rarely available when advertising activity begins. Due to the recommendatory nature of the age rating, there is an important interest in ensuring that the established age category is visible on the film work, on all copies thereof, on film trailers, and in all announcements and advertisements related to the film work, otherwise it cannot fulfil its attention-grabbing, informative role. At the same time, the question arises to what extent film trailers are able to anticipate the final age rating of the film work, and to what extent age rating circles can fulfil their recommendatory nature and informative function for parents, who bear the final decision and on whom it depends whether they permit their child to view the film work based on the suggested age. The cinema has no say in the parental decision, the responsibility associated with this decision rests entirely with the parent. The guarantee for the enforcement of rules aiming at the protection of minors is if parents possess sufficient knowledge about the effects of media contents, are clear about the instruments of regulation and consciously supervise their children's media consumption. The recommendatory nature of domestic regulation presupposes a highly active parental attitude. The effectiveness of protection crucially depends on whether the parent is familiar with the signalling system, is clear about the final classification of the given film work, and based on this makes a responsible decision on whether their child is suitable for receiving the given film work. The primary objective of the research is therefore to examine whether the legislator's intention to protect minors from adverse effects is properly enforced. Guided by this interest, we would like to gain an accurate picture through the study of the effectiveness of the regulation adopted in 2012, mapping in detail the general recognition of signs serving the protection of minors, as well as their application by parents. An essential aspect during the study is the identification of potential problems, shortcomings, and uncovering the measures necessary to increase the effectiveness of the regulation. Subject of the study: Knowledge, application and perception of the regulation related to the age rating of film works screened in cinemas for the sake of minors among cinema-goers, with particular regard to those with minor children. Target group: Cinema-goers over 15 years of age who have been to the cinema at least once in the past year and watched a film. Representativeness: The sample is representative of the target group by gender, age, education, place of residence type. Method, sampling: The planned method of the study is personal questioning by interviewers in the lobbies of cinemas in the capital and provinces. The sample size must be determined such that parents with minor children (3-17 years old) from the target group of domestic cinema-goers aged 15+ are sufficiently overrepresented for evaluable results, considering that the parental situation with minor children strongly influences the attitude towards classification. Research topics: 1. Cinema-going habits: • frequency, manner of cinema-going • genre preferences, • cinema type preferences, • frequency of going to the cinema independently or together with a minor/adult. 2. Attitudes related to the protection of minors: • beliefs about the necessity of regulating moving image content in general in connection with the protection of minors, up to what age it is important for children to enjoy protection against harmful audiovisual content, • what are the elements that can be said to be most harmful, which can exert an unfavourable influence on minors in the case of film works (violence, sex, drugs, foul language, choice of topic, etc.); • the question of responsibility in establishing effective protection. 3.

From those with minor children: 4. Rock Island District is actively reviewing, identifying, and modifying current contracts which may not already include the CMP Specification. Reach out to your assigned Contracting Officer with any contract-specific questions or any potential costs you anticipate form this switch. Contact Information: Primary Point of Contact - Christopher Thennes - christopher.w.thennes@usace.army.mil Alternative Point of Contact - Bryce Iwinski - bryce.e.iwinski@usace.army.mil Specification Changes RMS Specification: Governs until the official transition date. CMP Specification: Takes over once CMP goes live. Please review the specifications and the CMA2 website below for additional information. The CMA2 site is maintained at the USACE Enterprise level and will be updated as new information and system training become available. Resources & Reference Links CMP Specification UFGS 01 45 00.25 10: https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufgs/ufgs-01-45-00-25-10 RMS Specification UFGS 01 45 00.15 10: https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufgs/ufgs-01-45-00-15-10 Training & Transition Info CMA2 - USACE CMP Information Portal: https://cm-usace.erdc.dren.mil/article/8c7d854a-cdcd-44b7-a039-e2cd393133

sig_397c989237a5bd20cbca.description: The subject of the procurement is cybersecurity assessment services for the migration of Government Digital Service Applications to IaaS/PaaS solutions within Romania's Government Private Cloud (GPC). Complete details regarding the services forming the subject of this procurement can be found in the Specifications, an integral part of the Award Documentation. The objective of the Framework Agreement to be awarded by the Contracting Authority is to establish a rapid and efficient mechanism for the conclusion of Subsequent Contracts for the provision (procurement) of cybersecurity assessment services in accordance with its needs and within the limit of the budget allocated for this purpose. Total estimated value: Between 31.555.309,10 RON excluding VAT and 123.707.500,00 RON excluding VAT. The minimum total estimated value associated with the estimated minimum quantities is 31.555.309,10 RON, excluding VAT. The maximum total value associated with the maximum quantities is 123.707.500,00 RON, excluding VAT. The estimated value of the Framework Agreement is expressed as a range. The estimated value of the largest Subsequent Contract is: 3.082.790,90 RON excluding VAT (relating to an estimated number of 13 assessment / testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a very high complexity application). The estimated minimum and maximum quantities are specified in paragraph II.2. Any interested Economic Operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the Award Documentation. The number of days before the deadline for the submission of Tenders by which Economic Operators may request clarifications is 19 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Any request for clarifications must be transmitted via SEAP (www.e-licitatie.ro), after the Economic Operator has registered for the award procedure. The Contracting Authority will respond (by means of the consolidated response) clearly and completely to all Requests for clarifications and all requests for additional information received from interested Economic Operators at the latest on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of Tenders. The subject of the procurement is cybersecurity assessment services for ensuring the security and integrity of data and the IT infrastructure pertaining to Applications belonging to the Beneficiary Institutions identified in Annex 2 to Government Decision No. 112/2023, which are to be migrated to the GPC (pre-migration, post-migration as well as during the migration period). Complete details regarding the services forming the subject of this procurement can be found in the Specifications, an integral part of the Award Documentation. The objective of signing the Framework Agreement is to establish the terms and conditions, as well as the unit prices, with a view to creating the framework that enables the Contracting Authority to contract, according to specific needs, the provision of services forming the subject of the Framework Agreement. Estimation of the minimum and maximum quantities pertaining to the Framework Agreement: – The estimated minimum quantities of the Framework Agreement are: 321 testing/assessment reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a number of 30 Applications; – The estimated maximum quantities of the Framework Agreement are: 1408 assessment / testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a number of 136 Applications; Estimation of the minimum and maximum quantities that could form the subject of a single Subsequent Contract awarded based on the Framework Agreement: – The estimated quantity of the largest Subsequent Contract is: 13 assessment/testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a very high complexity application. – The estimated quantity of the smallest Subsequent Contract is: 10 assessment/testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a low complexity application. The estimated value of the largest Subsequent Contract is: 3.082.790,90 RON excluding VAT (for an estimated number of 13 assessment / testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a very high complexity application). The estimated value of the smallest Subsequent Contract is: 460.167,16 RON excluding VAT (for an estimated number of 10 assessment / testing reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a low complexity application). ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR SECTION II.2.6 TOTAL ESTIMATED VALUE The minimum estimated value associated with the estimated minimum quantities is 31.555.309,10 RON, excluding VAT (relating to an estimated quantity of services expressed in testing/assessment reports) of 321 reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a number of 30 Applications. The maximum estimated value associated with the maximum quantities is 123.707.500.00 RON, excluding VAT (relating to an estimated quantity of services expressed in testing/assessment reports) of 1408 reports representing the provision of cybersecurity assessment services for a number of 136 Applications. The estimated value of the Framework Agreement is expressed as a range.
sig_397c989237a5bd20cbca.title: Cybersecurity assessment services for the migration of certain Applications to Romania's Government Private Cloud

The system shall enable employees to log in quickly and ensure authentication. The reason for the need is due to a long log-on time with the current system and several professional applications to deal with in the daily work. sig_39c40af2c89b03ad377e.description: Denbighshire County Council (The Authority) are looking to engage with the market in relation to cost effective and high quality payment kiosks. This pre-market engagement notice outlines the high level requirements for payment kiosks capable of accepting payments via cash, chip and PIN, contactless and mobile wallets. The kiosks are to be installed in Local Authority One Stop Shops, ensuring secure, accessible, and user-friendly transactions for a diverse range of customers. Aims of Engagement The purpose is to: - Understand supplier capabilities and the very latest technologies and solutions available in the market - Identify opportunities for innovation and best practice - Test assumptions on costs, timescales, and implementation approaches - Understand options available to the Authority Requirements • Payment Methods: The kiosk must accept major debit and credit cards (including contactless), Google and Apple Pay, as well as cash (notes and coins). • Receipts: The kiosk must provide printed and digital receipts for all transactions. • Transaction Processing: Payments must be processed in real time, with confirmation displayed to the user. • Change Dispensing: For cash payments, the kiosk must dispense change where necessary. • Multiple Services: The kiosk should support payments for various Local Authority services (e.g., council tax, parking, permits). • Ability to view analytics and run reports • The devices must be able to operate bilingually in Welsh and English • Data Protection: All card transactions must comply with PCI DSS standards. Sensitive customer information must be encrypted and not stored locally. • Physical Security: The kiosk must be robust, tamper-resistant, with lockable compartments for cash and maintenance access. • Alarm Systems: Integrated alarms for unauthorised access or tampering. • Audit Trail: The system must maintain a secure log of all transactions for audit purposes. • Cash Handling: Secure cash management system, including automatic counting and secure storage of notes and coins. • Physical Accessibility: The kiosk must comply with UK accessibility standards, including wheelchair access (height and reach requirements). • User Interface: Large, clear touchscreen interface with intuitive navigation. Option for audio guidance and multiple languages. • Assistance Features: Braille labelling, tactile buttons, and headphone jack for visually impaired users. • Clear Instructions: Step-by-step instructions displayed on screen and available in print. • Connectivity: Secure internet connection for real-time transaction processing and remote support. • Reliability: Minimum uptime of 99.5%. Automated alerts for faults or maintenance needs. • Integration: Ability to integrate with Local Authority back-office systems for reconciliation and reporting. • Maintenance: Easy access for authorised personnel, with modular components for quick replacement. • Durability: Suitable for indoor use; resistant to spills, dust, and vandalism. • Power Supply: Standard UK mains power; battery backup for short-term operation during outages. • Space: Compact footprint, suitable for installation in existing One Stop Shop locations without major modifications. • Promote energy efficiency, for example by using low-power processors and LED displays • Compliance with relevant British Standards for electrical and payment equipment. • Certification for accessibility and security as required by Local Authority regulations. • On-screen help and customer support contact information. • Routine maintenance schedule and rapid response for breakdowns. • Remote diagnostics and software updates capability. Summary The payment kiosk must deliver secure, accessible, and reliable payment solutions for Local Authority customers, supporting both card and cash transactions. The design should ensure compliance with all regulatory standards, protect customer data, and provide a seamless user experience for all visitors to One Stop Shops. Lot 1: . None
sig_39c40af2c89b03ad377e.title: The Provision of Secure Payment Kiosks

sig_39da960173e23bf82f5d.description: Statnett SF has conducted a competitive procedure with negotiation following prior publication of a notice, cf. the Regulations on Procurement Procedures in the Utilities Sector (the Utilities Regulations) Parts I and II, for the award of a framework agreement for the purchase of assistance within control room design and development. The background for the procurement is the ongoing development within digitalisation, automation and other changes affecting work processes and the design of control rooms, which creates a continuous need to engage expertise in this area. The framework agreement shall cover Statnett's need for services and advisory support within user interfaces, control room design, layout and the organisation of work processes in control rooms, including the development of prototypes and/or simulations of design solutions. The supplier shall base its deliveries on recognised methods, best practices and standards for safety-critical environments, with an emphasis on user involvement. A framework agreement is entered into with a single supplier. The agreement has a duration of 4 years, with an option for the Contracting Authority to extend by up to 2 + 2 years, for a maximum total of 8 years.
sig_39da960173e23bf82f5d.title: Framework agreement for the purchase of assistance within control room design

sig_39eb53936eb08f77c816.description: Introduction This notice is intended to open dialogue with the market and inform any potential future formal procurement process, to test market capability, supplier interest, delivery options and implementation feasibility. Progression to formal procurement is not guaranteed. Bromford Flagship LiveWest (BFL) is exploring the future provision of its Human Capital Management (HCM) technology for approx 5,600 colleagues. Following organisational integration, BFL currently operates a broad range of legacy people systems and associated processes across HR, payroll, recruitment, onboarding, learning, talent, workforce management and employee relations. This document supports early, informal engagement with potential suppliers. It is not a procurement exercise, invitation to tender or commitment to purchase any solution. The engagement will help BFL understand available market capability, delivery models, indicative costs and implementation considerations before determining the scope and route of any future procurement. BFL is testing whether its emerging ambition is achievable and appropriately framed. We want suppliers to help us understand: • Whether a single platform can meet the breadth of need or whether an integrated ecosystem would provide a stronger outcome. • Which capabilities are standard, configurable, partner-delivered or dependent on third-party integration. • Indicative commercial models and whole-life cost considerations. • Realistic implementation approaches, sequencing, dependencies and timescales. • Any material gaps, risks or emerging practice that BFL should consider before formal procurement. Strategic Vision for People Services BFL wants to create a connected, consistent and future-focused people technology environment that offers a simple experience for colleagues, managers and administrators while strengthening payroll assurance, workforce insight and organisational control. Our ambition is to reduce fragmentation and duplication, increase self-service, improve mobile and field-based accessibility, automate routine activity and establish trusted people data that can support operational and strategic decision-making. We are open to a single HCM platform, modular products within one technology family, or a well-integrated ecosystem. The preferred approach must provide a coherent user journey, clear system ownership, secure data flows and sustainable administration over the long term. Design principles • One colleague and manager experience, with single sign-on and minimal switching between applications. • A reliable single source of people data with effective-dated records, governance and auditability. • Configurable self-service and workflow that reduce manual intervention without weakening controls. • Mobile-first and accessible design for office-based, remote and field-based colleagues. • Open integration using modern REST APIs, event-based services and standard data exchange methods. • Actionable reporting through native analytics and integration with Microsoft Power BI. • Secure, compliant, vendor-managed cloud services with appropriate UK or EEA data residency. • A platform and supplier roadmap capable of supporting future organisational change, AI and skills intelligence. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is issued for information gathering purposes only. Participation in this exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any future procurement process. The contract value provided is an estimate based on current spend for a 5 year contract. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Suppliers wishing to participate should contact Kate.Metzgier@flagship-group.co.uk to receive more details about the planned procurement. The deadline for submission of information is 14 October 2026 . Lot 1: . None
