sig_3cef7ee56153a86b1893.description: The State of Hesse, represented by IT-Stelle der hessischen Justiz ("Client"), intends to equip the courtrooms of all jurisdictions in the State of Hesse with uniformly operable media and video negotiation technology. The Hessian judiciary comprises the ordinary jurisdiction, labour, financial, social and administrative jurisdictions with a total of over 70 court locations and 530 courtrooms. The Hessian judiciary is currently undergoing a comprehensive digital transformation as part of the eJustice Hesse programme. Video hearings have emerged as an established instrument for conducting proceedings and are being continuously expanded within the Hessian judiciary. The courtrooms are made available to the courts as negotiation rooms for the performance of official duties. The Client points out that the financing of the equipment for all courtrooms is not secured. The Client cannot currently reliably estimate the extent to which and how many courtrooms the Contractor must equip. The framework agreement does not provide for a minimum order quantity. The Client estimates the number of courtrooms to be equipped at 530. The maximum quantity of courtrooms to be equipped is 580. The subject of the contract is the media technology equipment of the courtrooms of all jurisdictions in the State of Hesse with uniformly operable media and video negotiation technology. The Client shall equip the courtrooms according to requirements and optionally in several stages. Probably at the beginning of 2027, modern media trolleys equipped with interactive displays on a trolley and 360-cameras will initially be set up in the courtrooms as part of a separate measure. This procurement is not the subject of the procurement procedure. The Contractor must conceptually take the components of the media trolley into account and integrate them into the stages building upon them. The partial equipment building on the media trolley is structured as follows: The operating comfort equipment (partial equipment 1) comprises in particular the following services: - Presentation screens, usually as wall mounting, - functional system control (HW/SW), located on one or more control panels to control all sources/media located in the courtroom, - active network and security components and internet access (router), - provision of a central management environment for administration, monitoring, inventorying and certificate management of all systems and components; In a further stage, the Contractor must implement the target image equipment. This stage builds either on the media trolley or optionally on the operating comfort equipment. The target image equipment (partial equipment 2) comprises in particular the following additional services: - Audio control software (incl. audio hub) with table microphones, wall speakers/soundbars, - PTZ cameras, - connection panels of all participants, - integration of monitors on the judge's bench, - media hub, - document camera. The Contractor must provide service services from the acceptance of an equipment stage, consisting in particular of a multi-stage support model (2nd/3rd level and field service by the Contractor) with SLAs, incident, problem, change and release management, spare parts provisioning and replacement. The Contractor must furthermore take the existing whiteboard into service as a component part. All applications for operating the systems for the video hearings must comply with the specifications of the Barrier-Free Information Technology Ordinance. The Contractor is responsible for the design workshops, concept creation, test phases and the step-by-step equipment and commissioning of the media equipment. The Contractor must provide the services of the respective equipment stage upon call-off by the Client. The Contractor is responsible for the secure and permanent attachment - inter alia of displays, brackets and further components. The Client points out that the building structure in the courtrooms is not conclusively known to it. The Contractor must check as part of a site visit whether interventions in the wall construction are necessary for the attachment of the components and carry these out - if necessary and after call-off by the Client. The Client provides the passive infrastructure and internet access per location for the media network. The Client currently and predominantly uses Cisco Webex as a conference platform. The Client pursues a strict "Bring Your Own Meeting" strategy in order to remain technologically independent in the future as well. The Client provides the necessary laptops and docking stations for connecting the new media technology for dial-in/control/management of the conference platform. The hardware and software to be provided by the Contractor must function independently of the platform. The Client reserves the right to specify and adapt the requirements in the course of the procedure.
sig_3cef7ee56153a86b1893.title: Equipping the courtrooms of the State of Hesse

sig_3cf298cb3b92514dc247.description: The subject matter of the call for tenders is the procurement of state-of-the-art equipment for monitoring meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters. The project will develop an extensive, diverse and modern research infrastructure providing a wealth of data. The equipment will include mobile hydrometeorological radars, a low-frequency lightning detection network, meteorological and fire-meteorological stations, a computer system for meteorological data analysis and archiving, a data collection system for the calibration of meteorological and radiometric instruments, high-precision solar radiation measurement sensors, and hydro-telemetric stations, optical instruments and portable hydrometry equipment. Pre-existing meteorological, radiometric and hydrological measuring structures will be significantly upgraded and expanded, and a new standard fire-meteorological measuring network will also be developed. Self-propelled long-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted medium-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted short-range meteorological radar; Meteorological radar towing vehicle; Lightning discharge and atmospheric electricity detection network; Integrated high-precision system for the simultaneous measurement of the electrical outputs of multiple sensors, with simultaneous provision to a computer for further processing and analysis; Integrated automatic sun tracker for recording direct, diffuse and global solar radiation in accordance with WMO standards; Programmable scanning sky-dome spectroradiometer for measuring direct and diffuse solar radiation; Integrated autonomous modular system for measuring meteorological and/or agro-meteorological parameters
sig_3cf298cb3b92514dc247.title: Procurement of Specialised Scientific Equipment for the monitoring of meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters

Includes: HR cloud, private cloud for employees, payroll, personnel cost planning, reporting, certification, payroll analysis, certification, travel expense accounting, HR management, e-learning and seminar platform, digital personnel file, BEM (company integration management), document management, onboarding and offboarding, platform for surveys and employee polls, workforce planning and organisational management, employee portal, applicant management, talent and profile management, time management and workforce scheduling, project time recording, evaluations and HR analysis, intelligent scouts, digital twin for testing, intelligent production and AI relating to the topic of HR for application supervisors and employees. The contract is to be extended by 4 years.

1. The subject of the contract is the delivery of IT equipment, software and server room equipment, as well as the provision of digital competence training for the Zamość Public Library in Zamość. 2. The scope of the contract includes: 1) implementation of a library system and software for e-services, 2) purchase of ICT equipment, 3) purchase of training on enhancing digital competences and cybersecurity. 3. A detailed description of the subject of the contract has been included in the description of the subject of the contract (hereinafter referred to as the DSC), constituting appendix no. 11 to the contract notice / terms of reference (SWZ), the book dispenser installation designs, constituting appendix no. 12 to the SWZ, the technical designs for the air conditioning installation in the server room premises, constituting appendix no. 13 to the SWZ, the execution designs for the intrusion and hold-up alarm system installation and the access control system installation, constituting appendix no. 14 to the SWZ, and in the draft agreement, constituting appendix no. 10 to the SWZ. 4. The Contractor is obliged to deliver equipment that is brand new, unused and has not been exhibited at exhibitions or trade fairs, technically sound, free from legal and physical defects, safe, complete and ready for operation, covered by the subject of the contract – in accordance with the DSC. 5. The contract also includes the granting of a warranty and the provision of warranty service by the Contractor, the granting of software licences, and the handover of documentation for the delivered equipment – in accordance with the DSC. 6. Along with the delivery of the subject of the contract, the Contractor is obliged to deliver operating instructions, attestations, certificates, warranty cards, and operating and maintenance conditions in Polish. 7. The costs of loading, transport and unloading of the devices at the destination location, as well as assembly in the event that assembly by the Contractor is a condition for obtaining a warranty for the purchased equipment, shall be borne by the Contractor as part of the price for the performance of the subject of the contract. 8. The delivery and assembly of the devices constituting the subject of the contract shall take place in designated rooms of the Main Library of the Zamość Public Library and its branches, at a time agreed with the Director of the Zamość Public Library. 9. All requirements specified in the DSC constitute minimum requirements, and their fulfilment is obligatory. Failure to meet the aforementioned minimum requirements shall result in the rejection of the tender pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 5 of the Public Procurement Law Act. 10. In the event that the DSC refers to standards, technical assessments, technical specifications and technical reference systems referred to in Article 101 paragraph 1 points 2 and 3 of the Public Procurement Law Act, the Contracting Authority permits equivalent solutions, provided that they guarantee the performance of the subject of the contract in accordance with the DSC and ensure the attainment of technical, functional and operational parameters no worse than those assumed in the standards cited above. 11. sig_3d33617a58890c8e5f38.description: EDITED (20260730): After reviewing the extract from the draft PWS, vendors interested in responding to this sources sought announcment should send a statement of interest that broadly matches their own capabilites and already-demonstrated experience to those services shown below. While links to your company's website are appreciated, your response should not simpy refer us to your website. THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer’s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO’s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include “inherently governmental functions” nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to “deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.” The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. Shortterm situations may make performance in excess of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week necessary on occasion. The Contractor must ensure that they can provide for this contingency. 1.6 Tasks. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, Modeling & Simulation (M&S), analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO’s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The Contractor shall conduct the activities and tasks outlined in the following paragraphs. 1.6.1 Multi-Disciplinary Computational Technologies. The Contractor shall develop, sustain and use current and next generation tools. 1.6.2 Software Development and Sustainment. The Contractor shall provide development and sustainment of software tools and applications to support the AFSEO mission. The Contractor shall identify and prioritize AFSEO tool requirements; provide annual strategic execution and project planning, inputs for budget estimates; and execute software development and sustainment projects. These duties include: 1.6.2.1 Providing database software development and sustainment for the AFSEO Compatibility Enterprise System (ACES) and any follow-on systems. The Contractor shall design, edit and sustain ORACLE and SQL Server relational databases; and integrate Common-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) software using Application Programming Interfaces to communicate with ACES when needed. 1.6.2.2 Providing development and sustainment of engineering tools for analysis of aircraft carriage mechanics and carriage interference characteristics to support store compatibility evaluations. This shall include modeling the aircraft store combination for computer simulation, running computer simulations, and documenting changes to existing analysis software. 1.6.3 Computer-Aided Design and Stores Integration. The Contractor shall provide M&S support to include development, testing, and debugging of 3-dimensional and animated modeling software. The Contractor shall work with advanced engineering computer hardware to produce models of, but not limited to aircraft, suspension equipment and stores. These duties shall include: 1.6.3.1 Managing engineering and technical support personnel involved in the digital modeling of aircraft, suspension equipment, and stores and associated test equipment. This includes planning and managing multiple projects and coordinating with Department of War (DoW) management. The Contractor shall also provide required M&S products, perform quality assurance, and perform configuration management of all models and programs produced by the Computerized Physical Fit (CPF) team. 1.6.3.2 Designing, creating, and/or modifying aircraft, suspension equipment, stores and associated test equipment models using engineering drawings of aircraft, suspension equipment, stores, loading equipment and other components and associated physical interfaces. The Contractor shall follow the requirements outlined in MIL-STD-1289D. The Contractor shall perform quality assurance of all models and programs. 1.6.3.3 Using approved programming languages to develop in-house fit check tools of aircraft, suspension equipment and stores that interface with Siemens UGS NX 5 software or Government directed equivalent. The Contractor shall develop user friendly Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) so personnel can perform fit checks without being fully trained in the UGS NX 5 software. 1.6.3.4 Providing support for editing, modifying, and maintaining Siemens UGS files. The Contractor shall design, modify, and maintain relational databases. 1.6.3.5 Providing configuration control for M&S data. The Contractor shall create and maintain model history sheets and develop and execute procedures for archiving all M&S data. 1.6.4 Computational Fluid Dynamics. The Contractor shall perform the evaluation of numerical solution methods, the implementation of these techniques in a production environment, and the performance of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analyses for aircraft and store configurations. The Contractor shall produce and maintain simulation algorithms, codes and pre/post-processing software tools developed specifically for CFD investigations. These duties shall include: 1.6.4.1 Creating 3-dimensional surface and volume grids necessary to generate CFD analyses. The Contractor shall use both structured and unstructured methodologies and shall apply these methods to solve complex aircraft/weapon configurations. The Contractor shall use CFD codes and associated tools supporting the dynamic, time-accurate analysis of bodies in relative motion. The Contractor shall support aerodynamic M&S related to aero-elastic effects, weapon carriage and release, and internal weapons bay physics. 1.6.4.2 Creating 3-dimensional surface and volume grids necessary to generate CFD analyses. The Contractor shall use both structured and unstructured methodologies and shall apply these methods to solve complex aircraft/weapon configurations. The Contractor shall use CFD codes and associated tools supporting the dynamic, time-accurate analysis of bodies in relative motion. The Contractor shall support aerodynamic M&S related to aero-elastic effects, weapon carriage and release, and internal weapons bay physics. 1.6.4.3 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of CFD analysis necessary to complete the store certification process. The Contractor shall document aerodynamic analyses and write justifications to support compatibility issues. 1.6.5 High Performance Computing Software Development. The Contractor shall develop software using an approved Government development process, targeted at High Performance Computing (HPC) hardware. The Contractor shall apply computer engineering principles, practices, and techniques to solve difficult and unprecedented design problems involving HPC hardware. These duties shall include: 1.6.5.1 Managing projects. The Contractor shall coordinate and direct major software development efforts to include HPC hardware optimization and Internet web-enabled applications. 1.6.5.2 Developing software. The Contractor shall develop, using approved Government processes, software implementations of complex software architectures in various computer science languages to simulate multiple physical phenomena on HPC hardware. 1.6.6 Project Management/Project Planning. The Contractor shall provide project management and project planning support using project portfolio management tools specified by the Government for compatibility recommendations to air worthiness authorities and test work requests (to include mission summaries) to test organizations. Examples of recommendations include Recommended Flight Clearances (RFCs), Risk Assessments (RAs), Engineering Letters (ELs), and Certification Recommendations (CRs). In addition, the Contractor shall provide support as described in the following paragraphs. 1.6.6.1 Pre-Project Planning/AFSEO Customer Interface. The Contractor shall ensure that aircraft technical support concerns are addressed early in the developmental phase for each project assigned. This shall include but is not limited to documentation technical reviews, participating in requirement and design reviews and Technical Interchange Meetings (TIM), providing engineering and analysis support, and providing flight and ground test support. 1.6.6.2 Project Planning. The Contractor shall generate a project strategy, to include cost, schedule and requirements for the applicable period of performance for each project assigned. The Contractor shall generate a Statement of Capability (SOC), Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) letter, Project Plan, test work requests, or other documentation as required by the Government. Financial status shall be tracked using appropriate JON and WBS codes, which will be provided by the Government. The Contractor shall begin the execution phase of the project when approved by the Government. 1.6.6.3 Project Execution. The Contractor shall manage the execution of the analysis and test activities according to the Project Plan to meet AFSEO's customer requirements for each project assigned. The Contractor shall maintain current project status (cost, schedule and performance information) in the SEMSS or equivalent database (as determined by the Government) for each project assigned. The Contractor shall use this information to brief AFSEO management on project status, as required. The Contractor shall support meetings and/or conferences that may require travel. 1.6.6.4 Project Documents. The Contractor shall coordinate, generate, track, and revise recommendation documents to airworthiness authorities for applicable aircraft and store combinations for each project assigned. 1.6.7 Compatibility Engineering and Analysis. The Contractor shall provide engineering and analysis to support the AFSEO as described in the following paragraphs. 1.6.7.1 Fit and Function. The Contractor shall provide store fit and function support to determine whether stores are physically compatible with aircraft IAW MIL-STD-1289D. These tasks shall include: 1.6.7.1.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, Memorandum for Records (MFRs), military standards, and drawings. 1.6.7.1.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required fit and function analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. 1.6.7.1.3 Performing analysis to determine if a store can be loaded and maintained while on the aircraft, assess the store functionality, and perform digital and physical fit checks if needed. 1.6.7.1.4 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound recommendations for loading, installation and functionality of stores. Additionally, the Contractor shall provide assistance with creation of loading and installation manuals. Lastly, the Contractor shall provide inputs as required to aircraft and store original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) that document engineering findings related to engineering analyses findings and conclusions. 1.6.7.2 Structural Load Engineering. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support in the area of structural loads and vibrations, acoustics, and/or thermal (as required) for stores, suspension and release equipment, and aircraft required for the store certification process. The Contractor shall support the entire aircraft store Evaluate Compatibility and certification process. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation indicated in the duties below along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.7.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data to ensure compliance with MIL-STD-8591 for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, military standards, and drawings. 1.6.7.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of conducting required loads analysis, testing and reporting necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification process. Analysis requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: analytical aerodynamic evaluations (e.g. CFD), loads analysis, stress analysis, and vibration analysis. Testing requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: wind tunnel tests, static loads tests, ground vibration tests, non-instrumented flight tests, and instrumented flight tests. 1.6.7.3 Conducting analysis by manual and computer methods to evaluate inertial and aerodynamic loads and stress on aircraft, stores, and suspension and release equipment. This shall include using commercial and in-house developed software. 1.6.7.4 Developing and documenting required computer software and computer analysis methods using approved Government processes to create an in-house capability to analyze loads and stresses on the aircraft. This shall include using numerical methods to determine flexible aircraft loads from rigid airframe aerodynamic data, aerodynamic influence coefficients, structural influence coefficients, mass distribution data, 6-degree of freedom simulation data, and Finite Element Models (FEM). The Contractor shall develop and document any software necessary to perform this analysis. 1.6.7.5 Preparing and supporting off-site wind tunnel tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, wind tunnel chamber conditions (e.g. Mach number, total pressure, angle of attack), and data requirements; developing a wind tunnel test plan; attending pre-test coordination meetings; making technical decisions during the test; and reducing the data. 1.6.7.6 Preparing, executing, and documenting static loads and ground vibration tests to gather store and/or aircraft load data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, worst case loading cases, and data requirements; developing a static loads and ground vibration test plan; attending pre-test coordination meetings; setting up of the test stand; controlling the test apparatus; making technical decisions during the test; reducing the data; and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.7 Preparing and supporting non-instrumented structural loads flight tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight test conditions, and tolerances; and providing risk assessments, test maneuvers, and data requirements. This also includes developing mission summaries; attending pre-test coordination, safety, and technical review meetings; reviewing flight test cards; inspecting the store and aircraft prior to flight; attending the mission pre and post briefings; inspecting the store and aircraft after flight; and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.8 Preparing and supporting instrumented structural loads flight tests to gather store and/or aircraft loads data to support store certification efforts. This shall include determining test configurations, flight conditions and tolerances, test maneuvers, and data requirements. This shall also include developing mission summaries, attending pre-test coordination meetings, safety/technical review meetings, reviewing flight test cards, inspecting the store and aircraft prior to flight, attending the mission pre and post briefings, verifying instrumentation calibration, assisting in setting up mission control room (e.g. Central Control Facility (CCF)), monitoring safety-of-flight parameters in a control room during the flight test mission, inspecting the store and aircraft after flight, reducing the data, and documenting the test results. 1.6.7.9 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound operating limit recommendations (e.g. Mach number, airspeed, acceleration limits). 1.6.8 Electromagnetic Compatibility/Electromagnetic Interface Engineering. The Contractor shall provide support in the area of aircraft-store Electromagnetic Compatibility/Electromagnetic Interface (EMC/EMI) capability. These duties shall include: 1.6.8.1 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of required for conducting EMC/EMI analysis, testing and reporting necessary to complete the aircraft-store certification recommendation. 1.6.8.2 Reviewing sources of existing technical data to substantiate compatibility recommendations. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: MIL-STD-464 (A, B, C), MIL-STD-461 (A-F), DoW Hazards of Electromagnetic Radiation to Ordnance (HERO) reports, technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, and drawings. 1.6.8.3 Conducting analysis of aircraft-store configurations using appropriate computational methods (linear, nonlinear, and computational electromagnetic) to evaluate the EMC/EMI characteristics. Additionally, the Contractor shall develop and sustain analysis software tools and models using approved Government processes for the purpose of evaluating EMC/EMI characteristics. 1.6.8.4 Preparing and supporting EMC/EMI testing including preparing methods of test, executing the test or assisting in testing, including the use of network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, precision instrumentation, antennas and low-loss hardware, collecting and analyzing test results, and preparing test reports. Testing can occur many bases and facilities. 1.6.8.5 Interpreting the results from all data sources and providing sound compatibility recommendations. 1.6.9 Stability and Control Engineering. The Contractor shall provide engineering and technical support in the area of aircraft stability and control required for the store certification process. The Contractor shall provide the Government with the required test plans, technical reports, computer software products, and computer documentation indicated in the duties below along with all other products required in each task. These duties shall include: 1.6.9.1 Reviewing sources of existing technical data for substantiation of recommended operating limits. Examples of data sources include but are not limited to: official USAF technical reports, contractor and in-house reports, MFRs, military standards, and drawings. 1.6.9.2 Estimating and documenting the time and cost of conducting the required stability and control analysis and testing necessary to complete the aircraft store certification process. Analysis requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: analytical aerodynamic evaluations including CFD and 6-degree of freedom simulation. Testing requirements shall include but not be limited to any of the following: wind tunnel tests, non-instrumented flight tests, and instrumented flight-tests. 1.6.9.3 Conducting analysis by manual and computer methods. This shall include modeling the aircraft store combination for computer simulation, running computer simulations to evaluate the aircraft stability and control characteristics, and modifying and documenting changes to existing analysis software for evaluating an aircraft's stability and control characteristics. sig_3d775479bbe9cbc72974.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. sig_3e0c66ce8606c3312bc7.description: The purpose of the procurement is to draw up the feasibility study for the "realisation of a multi-voltage electric (traction) transformer substation at the Făurei Railway Testing Centre, which has the possibility of varying nominal parameters and performing regenerative braking" (including studies, expert reports, documentation, permits, agreements, etc.), an integral part of the Project "Modernisation and expansion of the Făurei Railway Testing Centre in order to increase the quality and testing capacity of systems and subsystems and constructive elements of the railway transport system" Note: The contracting authority will respond to requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. In accordance with art. 160 and 161 of Law 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and additions, the obligation of the contracting authority to respond to requests for clarifications is conditional upon the transmission of requests for clarifications 14 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The objective pursued through the procurement of the service for drawing up the feasibility study is the realisation of a transformer (traction) substation with multiple voltages (25 kV AC, 15 kV AC, 3 kV DC, 1,5 kV DC, 0,75 kV DC), with the possibility of varying the nominal voltage and performing regenerative braking, which will lead to the expansion of testing capacity, will facilitate the development and testing of new technologies at the level of safety and interoperability imposed by the Technical Specifications for Interoperability approved by European Regulations, and will allow for the performance of realistic simulations of operational conditions in the railway network. By awarding the service contract, the aim is, in addition to the procurement of the feasibility study (including necessary studies, expert reports, documentation, permits, agreements), the preparation of documentation for the approval of technical-economic indicators and the promotion of the Government decision, the preparation of technical documentation for the award of design and execution contracts for the works, and for consultancy/supervision of works execution, and last but not least, the preparation of documentation and assistance for obtaining financing through access to non-reimbursable European funds. This objective is included in the Project "Modernisation and expansion of the Făurei Railway Testing Centre in order to increase the quality and testing capacity of systems and subsystems and constructive elements of the railway transport system" initiated by the contracting authority.
sig_3e0c66ce8606c3312bc7.title: Preparation of a Feasibility Study for the "realisation of a multi-voltage electric traction substation at the Făurei Railway Testing Centre, which has the possibility of varying nominal parameters and performing regenerative braking"

sig_3e0f01ef6d08383468e5.description: The subject of the contract is "Performance of an interim evaluation and preparation of an interim report on the implementation of the Integrated Territorial Development Strategies for the six level 2 planning regions with a period of operation until 2027". The main objective is to develop high-quality and substantive interim evaluation and an interim report on the implementation of the ITDS with a period of operation of 2021-2027, evaluating the progress made in achieving the set targets for regional and spatial development. The ITDS were adopted by Decisions of the Council of Ministers in November 2022. Pursuant to Article 31, paragraph 1 of the Regional Development Act, the interim evaluation must also reflect the available results from the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the municipalities' integrated development plans. Pursuant to Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on the Implementation of the Regional Development Act (OIRDA), based on the information and data related to the application of the indicator system, monitoring reports on the implementation of the integrated territorial development strategies for the level 2 planning regions are drawn up every three years until the expiry of the strategies' period of operation (The Three-Year Reports). The Three-Year Reports are drawn up by the territorial unit (TU) of the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works (MRDPW) in the respective planning region, and Article 67, paragraph 2 of the OIRDA provides for expert support from the company under Article 11, paragraph 6 of the Regional Development Act. The interim evaluation of the ITDS must use the results of the Three-Year Reports drawn up by the territorial units of the MRDPW, which will provide part of the necessary information during the performance of the service depending on the stage of preparation of the reports. The selected contractor for this service will have the task of carrying out all activities for: Performance of an interim evaluation and interim report on the implementation of the ITDS with a period of operation of 2021-2027, evaluating the progress towards achieving the set targets for regional and spatial development and reflecting the available results from the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the municipalities' integrated development plans. According to the technical specification, after the execution of the public procurement, the following results are expected to be achieved: 1 no. Introductory Report; 1 no. First Interim Report; 1 no. Second Interim Report; 1 no. Final Report, presenting the final product as follows: Developed interim evaluation for the implementation of each of the six ITDS including Reports approved by the MoEW pursuant to Article 68, paragraph 2 of the OIRDA with incorporated notes and comments from all coordination procedures. Prepared interim report on the implementation of each of the six ITDS with incorporated notes and comments from all coordination procedures. Prepared summary including brief aggregated results from the implementation of all six ITDS of the level 2 planning regions (in Bulgarian and English).
sig_3e0f01ef6d08383468e5.title: “Performance of an interim evaluation and preparation of an interim report on the implementation of the Integrated Territorial Development Strategies for the six level 2 planning regions with a period of operation until 2027.”

sig_3e15a3cc0e08c929dab2.description: Automated Distribution and Manufacturing Centre (ADMC) Procurement Early Engagement Notice Purpose This notice is to make potential contractors aware that, via the Nottinghamshire County Council (NCC) procurement team, Ashfield District Council (ADC) will commence a process to appoint a commercial operator for their Automated Distribution and Manufacturing Centre (ADMC). The publication of this notice commences the preliminary market engagement stage of the procurement process. The procurement is expected to follow a Competitive Flexible Procedure, based on the Procurement Act 2023. Background The ADMC is a flagship project for Ashfield District Council. The ADMC will work with businesses to create and implement bespoke automation strategies and solutions that improve productivity and enable prosperity and growth. The ADMC will be a 3,000m2 purpose built, multifunctional, automation centre. Its vision is based on four "pillars" of activity: • Research and Development • Prototyping and Proof of Principle • Showcasing and Demonstration • Skills and Training The ADMC will be at the centre of a cluster of automation businesses, some of which will be located on the adjacent Ashfield Innovation and Technology Park that is also in development. The ADMC building is expected to be completed by December 2027. More details can be found on the ADMC website at www.theadmc.co.uk. Proposed Governance and Operation ADC confirmed its positioning regarding governance and operation of the ADMC in January 2025. It has resolved to carry out a public procurement procedure to appoint an external organisation to run the ADMC. ADC believe that this contracted approach will allow the ADMC to be operated effectively and efficiently such that it achieves its twin goals of supporting the greater adoption of automation within local and regional businesses and achieving financial sustainability. A previous procurement process to appoint an operator for the ADMC took place in late 2025. This process was ultimately unsuccessful in appointing an operator due to a combination of factors including feedback from potential bidders about the scope of the contract as well as subsidy and compliance issues. ADC aims to have a commercial operator appointed in 2027. Preliminary Market Engagement stage of the Procurement Process The procurement is expected to follow a Competitive Flexible Procedure, following the Procurement Act 2023. This notice commences the procurement process via a preliminary market engagement stage. The preliminary market engagement stage is intended to allow potential contractors to gain a more detailed understanding of the ADMC, its progress, and the procurement process being undertaken. It will also support NCC and ADC to develop the first stage tender by helping to: • Develop the requirements and approach to the procurement. • Design the conditions of participation and award criteria. • Inform the scope of works being contracted and whether these works should be split into separate lots. • Prepare the tender notice and associated tender documents. • Identify likely contractual terms. • Building capacity in relation to the contract being awarded. NCC/ADC proposes to run initial group engagement events via Teams on two dates: • Tuesday 10th November 10:00 - 11:00 • Thursday 12th November 10:00 - 11:00 Further events may be run before the end of November 2026 as demand requires. NCC/ADC will be having individual discussions with potential contractors. Contractors will be invited to express an interest in being part of those discussions following the group engagement events. All information and material collected from these pre-market engagement activities will be documented and form part of the subsequent tender pack, respecting commercial confidentiality. Contact To express interest in being part of the Preliminary Market Engagement stage of this procurement process and to be sent the ADMC - Intent to Go to Market - Power Point Information Pack, please contact Jamie Burton - jamie.burton2@nottscc.gov.uk Please feel free to submit any clarification questions to Jamie Burton - jamie.burton2@nottscc.gov.uk NCC/ADC will respond to these promptly. Lot 1: .

sig_3e49885497ce57f13d02.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. A detailed description of the subject of the contract, including minimum requirements regarding technical, functional, and performance parameters, equipment, compatibility, integration with HIS/RIS/PACS systems, warranty, service, delivery, installation, commissioning, and training, is specified in Annex no. 1 to the SWZ – Description of the subject of the contract – required and evaluated parameters. The Contractor is obliged to ensure the completeness and mutual compatibility of all offered elements of the solution, including ECG machines, equipment, software, and required licences, and their proper interaction with the Contracting Authority's existing IT infrastructure, to the extent specified in the OPZ, without the need for the Contracting Authority to make additional purchases or investments necessary for the commissioning and proper use of the subject of the contract.; Package 2_The subject of the contract is the delivery of a brand-new defibrillator with equipment, together with delivery, installation, assembly, commissioning, and training of users in its operation. sig_3e6c53d1d6d6d778adc7.description: Renewal of the in-house printing solution The provision of 2 colour-accurate (Fogra) multifunction systems including the required control software for equipping the central in-house printing service with corresponding services is tendered (calculation basis 1,0 million b/w pages and 2,0 million colour pages p.a.). Among other things, the contractor also ensures the supply of the devices with all consumables (except paper). The contract is not explicitly tendered as a framework agreement. However, the print volumes, which cannot be precisely determined due to the nature of the matter, give the scope of the service a framework agreement character. The volumes specified in the pricing section serve merely as guide values for the calculation within the framework of the award procedure. An obligation to purchase a specific print/copy volume is not established thereby. 1 system serves as a pure production system. The second system is to be equipped with extensive post-processing connected to the system for demanding printing tasks (firmly in-line). The planned solution consists of the interaction of various software and hardware components and must cover the described requirements. The design of the solution must map an end-to-end workflow.

sig_3e73758e8dae6ea8c0b8.description: The Directorate of DigitalIsation (Digdir) invites tenderers to give input on collaboration models for issuing a digital wallet in Norway. This request for information is related to the ongoing work with a CONCEPT CHOICE assessment (KVU) for issuing a digital wallet in accordance with the eIDAS2.0 regulation. This has been efficient and given us rapid and high spreading of eID in the population, and thus contributed to the fact that public and private actors have been able to digitalise a great many services. The national eID strategy has, however, pointed to some challenges with the current model, i.a. connected to not everyone having access to eID "High" within the current market-based systems. The eIDAS2.0 Regulation requires Norway to offer inhabitants and residents a free digital wallet at a security level "High". The regulation also requires most social sectors, both public and private, to accept the wallet for log-in, identification and different areas of use. This also applies across EU/EEA countries, which means that Norway be required to accept the digital wallets of others in norway. In addition to this, we see the introduction of digital wallets in the work with the KVU in connection with the challenges and needs described in the national eID strategy. Reply This is an open invitation to market participants, and there are no special form requirements for the feedback. Each market participant is free to emphasise what they find most relevant in their responses. However, we have prepared an overview of questions that can function as a guide, which gives an indication of which areas we would like feedback on. Response to this RFI (both questions and input) is sent via the communication module in Mercell.Deadline for written responses: 18 December 2025Se attached documents for further information.
sig_3e73758e8dae6ea8c0b8.title: RFI - Collaboration models for issuing of digital wallets

sig_3e78e69baa2432207c95.description: The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2). LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer. LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels. sig_3e7c5fbcb98a1e20c99f.description: Technical University of Denmark (hereinafter DTU) wishes to enter into an agreement regarding the delivery of a Prefabricated Server Module, Products, Support and service, as well as Time-based services (the "Agreement"). DTU wishes to enter into an Agreement concerning the procurement of a server module with accessories with a total power and cooling capacity of 1MW. The server module with accessories is to be used for hosting European Spallation Source ERIC (ESS) servers in the form of, inter alia, HPC, fast and slow storage, as well as large virtualization machines. The tendered Agreement does not include the procurement of servers. ESS is the world's largest and brightest neutron scattering research facility under construction in Lund, Sweden. As a crucial part of delivering world-class science, the Data Management and Software Center (DMSC) supports ESS's tasks. DMSC is a division under ESS and has an office in Denmark - more specifically at DTU Lyngby campus. In order to be able to store and process the desired data volumes expected to be generated by ESS (approx. 10PB per year when the facility is in full operation), DMSC must host a quantity of IT equipment aimed at the field of "Scientific computing". It is estimated that DMSC will need 30 server racks, which have a total power and cooling capacity of 1MW. DTU wishes to enter into one single overall agreement regarding the tendered Delivery. The Delivery is expected to comprise a server module with accessories in the form of, inter alia, a prefabricated server module, server racks, UPS system, cabling, cooling, monitoring, power distribution, fire protection, access control, etc. In addition, the Delivery comprises consultancy services in connection with testing and delivery of the Delivery, as well as the conclusion of a support and service agreement.

sig_3ea638f44527d5fd54fb.description: The Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (BMG) is planning the establishment of AI regulatory living labs in healthcare. The aim of the procurement for AI regulatory living labs is to accelerate the transfer of innovative AI systems into healthcare provision. It comprises several projects. One of these projects is intended to support institutions that develop AI ("AI developers") in identifying and addressing regulatory requirements at an early stage and establishing correspondingly compliant development processes. This goal is to be achieved primarily by drafting and publishing reference documentation ("blueprints") for common documents required as part of a conformity assessment or certification procedure. The BMG plans to support AI developers, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), in drawing up such "blueprints" together with relevant experts. A prerequisite for funding is that the resulting "blueprints" are published in full in order to achieve added value for non-funded AI developers as well. The "blueprints" drawn up within the scope of the project are intended in their entirety to address various challenges that are highly relevant to the market and which currently make it difficult to place innovative AI systems on the market for healthcare provision.

sig_3ee3456c728b5453b90b.description: Chiltern Rail is seeking to procure supplier-hosted software solutions and associated services to replace its existing Train Planning and Rostering systems. The solution must support planning data management, timetable change management, scenario modelling, auditability, version control, reporting, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems. Lot 2 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Rostering System. The solution is required to support base, weekly and daily rostering for relevant staff groups, including traincrew, station staff and fleet/engineering staff. sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.description: The Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (KVB) intends to publish one or, where applicable, several procurement procedures for the procurement of validators including a background system and relevant software interfaces, likely from the year 2026. In order to improve KVB's level of knowledge regarding the technical and commercial aspects of such a procedure, KVB is conducting a market consultation pursuant to Section 26 of the Sectoral Procurement Ordinance (SektVO) ("industry dialogue"). As part of the industry dialogue, KVB will inform itself about, inter alia, 1. Functionalities of validators (hardware, software) and background systems 2. implementation options for KVB 3. commercial aspects (pricing models, price range, cost factors). Subject of the industry dialogue: KVB intends to replace the mobile ticket vending machines in the trains and buses with validators. These are intended to function without paper and cash based on contactless EMV transactions and to be embedded in an ABT/IDBT-capable system. Travel entitlements are to be stored as encrypted tokens in a cloud-based background system, whereby both providers and cloud storage must at least have the necessary ISO 27001 certification. The operation of the background system in a cloud environment must be subject to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The validators must make it possible to purchase a specific, independently configurable range of tickets (pre-selection) and additionally support an interoperable check-in/check-out procedure with integrated best-price calculation for the customer. All physical and virtual payment instruments that comply with the EMV standard (EC card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.) must be accepted; in addition, payment via a prepaid card (closed-loop) must be possible. KVB reserves the right to commission a financial/payment service provider with the processing of payments. Corresponding software interfaces/APIs must therefore be supported/addressed. The payment options are to be expandable in the future. The customer must be able to view and manage their travel entitlements (ABT) independently via an online portal (web portal). The web/online portal is to be provided in KVB's corporate design. In addition, further software interfaces to a central customer account, which is set up internally by KVB, are to be provided. It must be possible to use a token that is linked to another person's payment medium. The control of the issued travel entitlements must be ensured across transport associations (at least throughout NRW) and made possible by corresponding software interfaces from the provider. A control option must also be possible when the validator is offline. The regular processing of blacklists is supported. Current and future developments of VDV-KA and (((eTiCore must be taken into account. The background system must contain at least the following software interfaces: - Ticketing back office with payment gateway and connection to payment service provider - Device management - Key management - Customer management - Enterprise asset management system - Fault notification software interface The background system should promote interoperability and must be able to be integrated into an overarching system landscape. The accounting data from the validators must be able to be integrated from there into the sales accounting system PATRIS (LHIND). Participation in the industry dialogue / qualification criteria: If potential bidders are interested in participating in the industry dialogue, KVB requests notification by email by no later than 23.9.2025, 10:00 hours, to the contact point daniela.lehnert@kvb.koeln. The references must be submitted in full by this time. When expressing interest in participating in the industry dialogue, the following qualification criteria / capabilities of the bidders must be proven and submitted. sig_3f37cd62d19c8fc6374f.description: Description The United States Space Force (USSF), through the Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)to solicit innovative commercial solutions that enhance Space Domain Awareness (SDA)capabilities. This CSO is authorized under DFARS 212.70and is designed to identify and acquire innovative technologies, products, and services that support the USSF's warfighting missions. The CSO provides a flexible, enterprise-wide acquisition mechanism to address SDA mission challenges through advanced software engineering, data analytics, and other innovative approaches. Submissions will be evaluated under a multi-phase process to ensure alignment with mission needs and operational priorities. Scope of the CSO The CSO seeks solutions that address the following Space Domain Awareness (SDA)mission challenges: Detecting, characterizing, and predicting activities in the space domain. Enhancing the accuracy and timeliness of SDA data. Supporting emerging SDA missions through innovative technologies. Specific Areas of Interest (AOIs) will be issued under this CSO to define technical focus areas, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria. Each AOI will be posted as a standalone solicitation module under this CSO. Submission Process The CSO employs a three-phase submission process: Phase I – White Paper and PowerPoint Briefing Offerors must submit a PowerPoint briefing (including a Quad Chart) and a White Paper summarizing their proposed solution. Submissions must align with the specific AOI requirements. Phase II – Pitch Session (Optional) Selected Offerors may be invited to present their proposed solution in greater depth during a virtual or in-person pitch session. Phase III – Full Proposal Offerors invited to Phase III must submit a complete proposal package, including a Technical Proposal, Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Price Proposal. The Government reserves the right to proceed directly from Phase I to Phase III. Key Information Security Requirements: Phase I submissions must be unclassified. Subsequent phases may require higher classification levels, as specified in the AOI and any draft or final DD Form 254. Foreign Participation: Restricted to U.S. entities due to export control and national security considerations. Cybersecurity Compliance: Offerors must comply with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC 2.0 requirements. How to Respond Interested Offerors must monitor SAM.gov for AOI-specific postings under this CSO. Each AOI will include detailed submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and deadlines. Submissions must comply with the formats and requirements outlined in the CSO and the applicable AOI. For general inquiries, contact the SAIO CSO Contracting Officer at SAIO.SDA.CSO@spaceforce.mil. Use the subject line: "SDA CSO – General Question(s)". Disclaimer This CSO does not obligate the Government to award a contract, nor does it commit the Government to pay for any costs incurred in the preparation and submission of responses. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the proposals received under this CSO.
sig_3f37cd62d19c8fc6374f.title: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) for Space Domain Awareness (SDA) Solutions.

sig_3fb51fab90a9468c0ef8.description: Forest management planning services will be awarded in 2027 by concluding a public procurement contract for the Reghin Forestry Office. The total area of the Reghin Forestry Office is 5030,44 ha. The services entail the drafting of the forest management plan, a product of management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically founded, by which the work necessary to be executed in a production unit is established for a period of time, for the purpose of bringing and subsequently maintaining the structural characteristics of the tree stands and of the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and completions, it is necessary for the drafting of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state's public property forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The management method of the state's public property forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state public property land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of property in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarifications formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the contract notice may be made with a deadline of at least 15 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all clarification requests formulated in compliance with the above deadline, a single time, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. Services for drafting the forest management plan for the state public property forest fund administered by the Mures Forestry Directorate – Reghin Forestry Office, for the area of 5030,44 ha, in accordance with specifications no. 9926/07.09.2026. The services include preparatory work, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, drafting and development of the GIS database and management maps, drawing up the necessary environmental documentations, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Approval Commission for Forestry (TACF) and obtaining the order approving the forest management plan.
sig_3fb51fab90a9468c0ef8.title: Forest management services, Reghin Forestry Office, Mures Forestry Directorate
