sig_3fcea115f0c7c6906d0a.description: Science IT is responsible for the operation of the ScienceCloud and ScienceCluster. The Team needs professional consulting support for the opensource technology OpenStack and CephFS. The University of Zurich (UZH) invites tenders for the following reasons: Expiring support contract with current consultant Science IT already had a support contract with a provider (StackHPC) for the OpenStack platform in the past. This needs to be renewed for the next 5 years. This is a suitable opportunity to redefine the desired support services, familiarise with other providers and obtain prices in line with the market. Enlarge support to also cover CephFS Science IT has experienced two major incidents last year on CephFS with a total downtime of the whole ScienceCluster service for several weeks. Therefore, Science IT is looking for a strong partner with lots of experience in CephFS to provide 3rd level support as well as consulting service to stabilize the platform. Two long-serving employees have left the team Two experienced employees with in-depth knowledge of CephFS and OpenStack have left the Science IT team. Over the next two years, the knowledge in the team will be built up again. This will require a targeted transfer of expertise from an experienced partner to the employees of Science IT. Therefore, with this tender, Science IT is looking for experienced partners for the support of OpenStack and CephFS. The cooperation with an experienced provider should achieve the following goals: * In the event of a disaster, Science IT receives professional support for OpenStack and CephFS on the next business day at the latest. * Employees will be able to benefit from the provider's expertise in the coming years. The provider also employs staff who are actively involved in CephFS and OpenStack as contributors. Using the provider's documentation on the UZH platform, the team will be enabled to solve problems independently. * Updates or upgrades can be planned and implemented together so that the platform is always operated at the second latest technical level. * Conceptual adjustments to the platform can be discussed with an experienced partner. They challenge internal employees so that the right solution is implemented for UZH. For the operation of ScienceCloud and ScienceCluster OpenStack is key technology. With lot 1 the UZH is seeking for the following services. * Third level support: Support requests should be answered on the next business day, work is carried out during business hours, support is provided by arrangement * Disaster Support: Support requests should be answered on the next business day, work is carried out during business hours, support is immediate * Annual update support: The provider plans to carry out the update together with Science IT once a year. * Know-how transfer: The provider documents the platform on an ongoing basis and discusses the adjustments with internal employees * Initial project, ramp-up: The provider and the Science IT team discuss the status of the platform and possible conceptual adjustments to optimise the platform that may be needed to enable the provider to fulfil above requirements. These are then implemented together.
sig_3fcea115f0c7c6906d0a.title: Operations Support for ScienceCluster and ScienceCloud on OpenStack and CephFS

Furthermore, as part of the supply, technology that is already currently obsolete and does not meet current requirements will be replaced. The reason for the introduction is ZSSK's endeavour to address the situation with internet access for the travelling public. Passengers on the train must be enabled to connect to the internet using WiFi technology in trainsets. Internet connection will be free of charge. The technology must make it possible to control internet content in terms of blocking pages with hazardous content or downloading large volumes of data. Acceptance of the conditions of use of the internet connection in ZSSK trainsets must also be part of the log-in. During log-in, the passenger will confirm agreement to the provision of the service on a special page of the onboard portal. Subsequently, they will be redirected to the basic page, where there will be links to various information about the train, timetable and the like. The subject of the supply is further to supply WiFi network equipment and to transfer ownership rights to this equipment to the contracting authority, as well as to the complete documentation forming the architecture of the work (technical documentation) to the extent and under the conditions defined by the contracting authority, and to ensure the establishment of the WiFi infrastructure by installing this equipment into selected carriages in accordance with the contracting authority's requirement in line with the drawing documentation for these carriages, including cabling, installation, configuration, testing and the delivery of drawing documentation. A detailed definition of the subject of the contract is stated in Section B.1 Description of the Subject of the Contract of the tender documents.

sig_3fe2f3d1eb0aa25d598d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_3ffaa5b72586cd6c985c.description: At the end of 2022, the provincial authority of Flemish Brabant started using Kadanza, a cloud-based Digital Asset Management (DAM) solution for the central management and consultation of digital content and assets. Today, this solution is mainly used by the communication department and the tourism department for the management of photographic material. Within the provincial authority, however, other departments also manage a considerable amount of digital content, such as photos and videos. This is currently often distributed across various platforms (such as network drives, SharePoint, etc.), which complicates management, accessibility and reuse. Moreover, this content is not exclusively used for communication and publication purposes, but also forms part of internal operations and case file management. Currently, there is a lack of a uniform and structural approach for the management of image material, including the monitoring of use and retention periods. As a result, content often remains available for a long period without clear monitoring of relevance or use. The provincial authority of Flemish Brabant therefore wishes to proceed with the procurement of a Digital Asset Management solution that can be deployed across the entire organisation. The solution must support the management, accessibility and reuse of digital assets, and additionally allow lifecycle information (such as metadata, statuses and retention periods) to be managed in a structured and user-friendly manner. The solution must be suitable for various departments with divergent needs in terms of management, accessibility, rights and reuse, and must be able to deal flexibly with both intensive use and more supportive applications within the operations of the organisation.
sig_3ffaa5b72586cd6c985c.title: Framework agreement relating to the supply and ready-for-use installation of a Digital Asset Management system (DAM software) for the provincial authority of Flemish Brabant

sig_3ffeb196ed0e1227775e.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of a production planning tool for capacity-oriented planning and control. The use of the software, including maintenance and support, is to run for a total of four years. Lot LOT-0001: Implementation of planning software. The subject of the tender is the commissioning of a qualified provider to implement an advanced planning and scheduling (APS) system that enables very detailed scheduling of all required resources using finite resource planning. The primary objective of implementing the planning tool is to generate the most realistic and actionable planning possible by optimally scheduling all resources, linked with feedback from the operational units in SAP S/4HANA in almost real time. By mapping all weapon systems and equipment in the planning tool and providing a simulation capability, equipment availability is to be simulated and visualised for future scenarios alongside planned measures. The focus is on conceptual design, implementation, customising, provision of licences, support, and training and qualification of users and administrators. System provision and server operation are carried out by the contracting authority's existing system operations IT service provider.

sig_401c9b3a1aeaaeac68f3.description: This is a Prior Information Notice (PIN) with the purpose of assisting the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) in engaging the market by gathering information. This PIN has the purpose of a fact-finding exercise and only. Background Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) are exploring options to digitalise payments out of the Agency in a bid to reduce payable orders. A specific user case includes invoice-based payments. Invoices are returned with information to support a customer's application. These applications, information and invoices are currently paper based which are scanned and digitalised in-house. On receipt of the information and sufficient checks, a payment is made by payable order to those named on the invoice. The payable order process is also managed in-house and posted from DVLA. Volumes In this example, for the financial year 2025-26, 221,406 individual payable orders were issued, with a net value of approximately £14.8M. Considerations - The payments are made to anyone qualified to complete the supporting evidence, so there is no static list of payees. There could be around 60,000 individual payees which fluctuates. Some are repeat payees and some are one off payees. - The payees include individuals and company accounts from across the UK. - The invoices (currently paper based) include the payee bank information (account number, sort code). - The invoices are then scanned and a digital copy held. - As a Government Agency we are required to follow all HM Treasury guidance outlined in the 'Managing Public Money' published documentation. - This includes not being able to use intermediary bank accounts outside of the Exchequer pyramid. - DVLA do not have an existing BACs business as usual process for payments out. - DVLA has explored Open Banking for this user case and feel that due to the considerations above it doesn't fully meet our requirements. Project aims - Digitalise movement of funds - Reduce/remove payable orders - Improve invoice management processes - Improve customer experience Information required - Potential solutions to support the project aims aligned to the considerations - Any costs associated with developing and implementing the solution including any licences or additional external costs. - Any ongoing costs associated with ongoing running of the solution. - Time taken to develop and implement the solution. - Any wider considerations, fees or any other supporting information. - Do you provide this type of service for any other large organisations? - How can DVLA procure from your organisation? e.g. Are they on a framework? If so which one? Do we need to go through any third parties to obtain their services? The subject matter of the procurement consists of such table games, developmental and skill-development tools that are suitable for the complex development of preschool and school-age children, especially children with special educational needs (SEN), learning, attention, communication or social difficulties. The tools must be related to several of the following development areas: • mother-tongue and communication skills (vocabulary, speech initiation, reading comprehension, phonological awareness), • logical and mathematical thinking, • attention, memory, executive functions, • social competences, emotional intelligence, conflict management, • fine and gross motor skills, hand-eye coordination, • perception, sensation, sensory integration, • creativity, problem-solving, cooperation. Functional expectations The table games and equipment may include the following types: • logical and thinking-development games (e.g. sequencing, patterns, combinations), • language and mother-tongue development games, picture cards, worksheet systems, • memory, attention and association games, • social-emotional development equipment (recognition of emotions, self-awareness, social situations), • manipulative, construction, building-type games (wood, plastic, magnetic elements), • fine-motor-skill development tools (threading, screwing, pinching), • games containing sensory and tactile elements (development of touch, sight, hearing), • sets suitable for role-playing and storytelling, • board games suitable for both individual and group sessions. Technical and quality requirements • The equipment shall be of a child-safe design, free from sharp edges. • They shall be made of a material suitable for durable, regular institutional use (wood, plastic, textile). • The paints and coatings used shall be non-toxic, complying with the regulations concerning children's toys. • The equipment shall be easy to clean and store. • Modular construction, expandability, and usability at differing difficulty levels shall be an advantage. • The equipment shall be suitable for supporting pedagogical, special education, developmental pedagogy, speech therapy and psychological sessions. Usage environment The equipment can be used in: • kindergarten and school group rooms, • development and therapy rooms, • during individual and small-group developments, • in an inclusive educational environment. sig_40297a331e7726e2cc9f.description: The contract has been awarded! 1.1 Initial Situation The Neuruppiner Wohnungsbaugesellschaft mbH is looking for a new ERP system for the comprehensive management of around 5.000 of its own economic units. This is intended to be a standard software product for the housing industry. The rental units are all located in the spa town of Neuruppin. Our company currently has 55 employees. The company currently uses the Wowinex ERP system. 1.2 Objective of the Tender The aim is the introduction of a future-proof, integrated standard ERP software solution for the housing industry. The central ERP platform is intended to allow the integration of specialist solutions, offer a modern user interface, and enable mobile use. 1.3 Project Goals The Neuruppiner Wohnungsbaugesellschaft mbH aims to ensure future-proofing, achieve efficiency gains, and optimise process workflows with this project. Implementation is to take place by the 3 quarter of 2028.

sig_403c58c4744a84b8e20d.description: Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficom is a central government agency operating within the administrative branch of the Ministry of Transport and Communications. Traficom is a service-oriented permit, register and supervisory authority in the transport and communications sector. The agency promotes the functionality and safety of the transport system and accelerates the development of the digital society. It supports sustainable development and ensures that high-quality, safe and affordable communications connections and services are available in Finland. Liikenne- ja viestintävirastoon and its operations can be explored in more detail at www.traficom.fi. Traficom is planning the procurement of EUDI access authenticator services. The planned procurement is described in more detail in the request for information attachment 1 (Description of the subject of the procurement). With this request for information, Traficom is exploring companies capable of carrying out the study for the planned procurement. The aim is to obtain comprehensive information concerning the implementation of the procurement so that a potential tendering procedure can be carried out in an appropriate manner. All information presented in the request for information regarding the planned procurement is preliminary and may change for the actual procurement. The request for information is not a procurement notice initiating a procurement. Traficom does not commit to carrying out the procurement; instead, the decision on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market consultation. The information provided in connection with the request for information does not bind companies to participate in a potentially later procurement. Companies do not have the right to claim compensation for responding to the request for information. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information includes the following preliminary documents: 1) Draft description of the subject of the procurement 2) Draft procurement contract Traficom invites companies interested in the procurement to share their views on key issues related to the procurement by answering the questions set out in the request for information attachment 1. The response to the request for information must be in Finnish. Please send your response to the questions set out in attachment 1 by the deadline for the request for information to: hankinnat.ktk@traficom.fi From the aforementioned email address (hankinnat.ktk@traficom.fi), you may also request further information regarding the request for information if necessary. Please attach the necessary contact details to your request for information response (contact person's name, email address and telephone number) so that we can contact you if necessary. Please mark the subject field of the response email with "Tietopyyntövastaukset, EUDI-pääsyvarmentajan palveluiden hankinta". Traficom may present follow-up questions to companies that have responded to the request for information and may also hold market consultation meetings if necessary. Traficom may process request for information responses already during the deadline of the request for information. Responses to the request for information are requested to be submitted by the deadline set out below. CONFIDENTIALITY OF REQUEST FOR INFORMATION RESPONSES Companies responding to the request for information are requested to clearly mark any trade secret information in the responses in accordance with Section 24.1, Paragraph 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. Trade secret information will be processed in accordance with the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.

Due to the expiration of the extended SAP maintenance period on 31 December 2030 and the desire for a more modern and more highly automated HR landscape, München Klinik intends to replace its existing SAP HCM system and further HR systems. The subject of the planned award is the procurement and implementation of an integrated, cloud-based HR software solution covering the following core areas: organisational management, master personnel data, payroll, travel expenses, ESS/MSS, ICS and recruitment. The solution must fully map the collective bargaining agreements applicable in the hospital and municipal environment (including TVöD-K, TV-Ärzte/VKA) at system level and meet all data protection and compliance requirements. Data storage must take place on servers in a data centre within the EU – preferably in Germany – on the basis of a certified infrastructure (e.g. ISO 27001, BSI C5). In addition to software licensing, the scope of services also includes implementation, data migration, interface development, training and go-live support. In this regard, the contracting authority wishes to get in touch with market participants without obligation and exchange further information. For this purpose, further documents will be made available to the companies participating in the market consultation. Upon completion of the market consultation, the insights resulting therefrom will be evaluated and, where applicable, taken into account for further procurement projects and the procedure directed towards them. sig_40459212b30cc95de370.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the procurement is the acquisition of an architecture service, through which a centre of expertise (hereinafter ARPA centre of expertise) will be established, which will develop and maintain the services related to the area in question. The established ARPA centre of expertise will be responsible for the development, steering, management and maintenance of operating models, services, solutions and descriptions related to enterprise architecture, data management, information, system and technology architecture, as well as continuous monitoring and support of the architecture. ARPA also provides expert and consulting services for the agency's development projects, service centres and business operations, and supports the development of digital services and data management at the level of the entire agency. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The architecture centre of expertise operates as Väylävirasto's centralised steering and development capability for data management, enterprise architecture and interoperability. The centre of expertise is responsible for the tasks of the current architecture service (ARPA) and the operation and development of the centralised data management support channel (KOJE). In addition, the centre of expertise acts as a joint architecture and data management capability for Väylävirasto's other centres of expertise and service packages. The task of the centre of expertise is to ensure that the solutions of the various service centres, projects, systems and development initiatives form a controlled, interoperable entity that supports strategic objectives. One (1) supplier will be selected as the service provider. The subject of the procurement may change and/or be refined as the preparation of the procurement progresses. OBJECTIVE OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The objective of the market dialogue is to survey suppliers on the market and obtain views on alternative implementation options for the architecture service. In addition, the objective is to obtain feedback on the procurement design, preliminary requirements and delimitations, and to ensure that the planned entity is workable and appropriate in relation to the solutions offered by the market. PRETIMINARY TIMETABLE The contracting authority's target timetable for carrying out the market dialogue and procurement is: Market dialogue: summer 2026 Publication of invitation to tender: early autumn 2026 Evaluation of tenders: autumn 2026 Procurement decision and continuation: autumn 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not constitute a call for tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, giving all suppliers interested in the procurement the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The market dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the market dialogue bind the supplier to participate in any potential tendering procedure. Instructions for registering for the technical dialogue: Suppliers must register their interest in participating in the market dialogue by sending a message to the address marika.ojanen@vayla.fi with the message subject: "ARPA - market dialogue" no later than 2.7.2026 at 16.00. The contracting authority will provide interested suppliers with the materials to be commented on and preliminary questions. Suppliers are requested to state the following information in their message: - the email address of the supplier's contact person (the email address to which the materials to be commented on and preliminary questions will be sent) Those registered for the market dialogue will have a response and commenting period until 10.8.2026 at 15:00. Detailed response instructions will be provided in connection with the materials to be commented on. The contracting authority reserves the right to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. Potential bilateral discussions: Based on the responses to the preliminary questions, the contracting authority reserves the right to invite potential suppliers to bilateral discussions. The contracting authority will schedule discussion times as soon as possible. Bilateral market dialogue discussions will be conducted in accordance with the preliminary questions. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the draft dialogue materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_404a2021ff07d0103bd3.description: The subject of the procurement consists of devices related to network-attached storage (NAS) solutions, as well as their installation and support services. The contracting authority is the University of Helsinki, and in addition to the contracting authority, the procurement involves the University of Eastern Finland, the University of Oulu, Oulu University of Applied Sciences, Tampere University and the University of Turku. Based on the results of the competitive tender, each contracting authority shall procure a package suitable for its own needs, which includes one (or more) network storage systems and the software and services associated with them. Each contracting authority already uses one or more network storage systems, which are used to provide services for the research, teaching and administration needs of the higher education communities represented by the contracting authorities. The storage systems are typically owned by each contracting authority and are located in their own server rooms. Storage systems typically have a lifecycle of approximately five years, but the lifecycle of the data in the network storage service itself can be very long. The procurement has been divided into four different lots, and the evaluation criterion for the competitive tender is the most economically advantageous price. Price has been used as the sole criterion for economic advantage because quality has been taken into account in the comprehensive minimum requirements. The client shall select the most economically advantageous tenderers from lots B-D as its framework agreement suppliers, and a framework agreement shall be concluded with these tenderers for four (4) years, with the option to extend the agreement by two option years one year at a time. Each participating contracting authority shall conclude its own agreements and be responsible for them for the duration of the agreement period. The draft framework agreement is attached to the call for tenders. The subject of the procurement and the requirements concerning it are described in detail in the call for tenders and its annexes. All suppliers selected for other lots shall be automatically selected for lot A, and tenders cannot be submitted for lot A alone. A priority order shall not be applied to lot A.; The minimum requirements for the products of technology-specific lots B and C can be found in the annex to the call for tenders Technical minimum requirements.; The minimum requirements for the products of technology-specific lots B and C can be found in the annex to the call for tenders Technical minimum requirements.; It is possible to tender for lot D with products that are equivalent to, but from different equipment manufacturers than, those in lots B and C. sig_407a8750f67e36b91460.description: IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. This section provides you with information regarding the scope of this procurement and details some of the key requirements that a successful applicant MUST be able to deliver. This tender is for a new direct contract for a Continuous Testing supplier to implement and provide a fully governed continuous testing framework for IT covering penetration testing, red/purple team exercises, cyber stress testing, vulnerability discovery and remediation re-testing. The preferred supplier must support red and purple team testing that will include a multi phase continuous testing model (e.g. tag and release), where red team activity transitions into purple teaming upon detection, and findings are shared in cycle while testing continues across subsequent phases. The service must include active collaboration with Thames Water teams during purple team activities, including validation of controls, detection capability, and response processes. The solution must demonstrate clear human oversight across testing, validation, and remediation activities, with automation used to support workflows (e.g. tracking, reporting, prioritisation) but not to replace core testing, validation, or assurance activities. The supplier must support collaborative remediation and retesting, ensuring findings are handed over, validated, and retested with Thames Water teams, with end to end traceability through to closure. The following conditions would be considered as some of key requirements for a supplier to meet to be considered for this opportunity: • Availability of a yearly penetration test as a minimum • A fully functional PTaaS service that can deliver service in line with applicable cadences • A qualified, accredited and suitably vetted PTaaS support team Thames Water reserves the right to refine the award criteria. Please note that that deadline for asking for access to the PSQ & submitting of the PSQ is Tuesday, 3 November 2026, at 12 p.m. Lot 1: .

sig_40cc327336210260ae22.description: TWFRA ('the Authority') is the publicly accountable body that oversees the policy and service delivery of Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Service ('the Service') on behalf of the community. The Service successfully leads the operational delivery of fire and rescue services such as public protection, fire and other emergency prevention, operational response and resilience. Our stations, staff and appliances are strategically placed across Tyne and Wear to ensure efficient and effective response to fires and other emergencies. Appliances work across station areas and can be mobilised whilst away from their home station. We also have robust arrangements with neighbouring services to enable additional support during major emergencies. Tyne and Wear Fire and Rescue Service (TWFRS) requires ongoing, compliant training for personnel involved in Water and Flood Rescue. Since 2006, TWFRS has adopted a recognised training framework that supports both external training and the development of internal instructors. This model has proven to be cost-effective and operationally efficient, enabling the Service to deliver high-quality training while maintaining compliance with national standards. TWFRS utilises a structured training and log booking system to manage qualifications and ensure accurate, auditable records. This supports compliance with the DEFRA Concept of Operations and the NFCC Rescue Boat Code and helps safeguard the Service's reputation in the delivery of water rescue capabilities. As national operational guidance and compliance requirements have evolved, so too have the training standards. This includes enhanced prerequisites for instructors and the introduction of new modules developed in response to national incidents and debriefs. The Service continues to adapt its training provision to meet these evolving standards. With the expansion of TWFRS's Water and Flood Rescue provision under the Community Risk Management Plan (CRMP), the demand for initial training, CPD, and recertification continues to grow. Ensuring access to recognised and compliant training is essential to maintaining operational readiness and meeting service delivery expectations. As a result, TWFRS is seeking suitable training providers to deliver the courses outlined in the scope and specification Lot 1: . Lot 2: . Lot 3: .
sig_40cc327336210260ae22.title: Rescue 3 Water Rescue Courses

sig_4109de053106f368a495.description: Further to the UK1 Pipeline Notice published on 19th November 2025 by BlueLight Commercial Limited (ref: 2025/S 000-077692) in relation to a Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution which will be used by UK law enforcement agencies, this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued to inform the market of a potential future opportunity. This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise, or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy. Any future procurement will be subject to separate formal notice and the publication of full procurement documentation via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). BlueLight Commercial Limited (BLC) are conducting Preliminary Market Engagement to gain a better understanding of the market, supplier appetite, capacity, and capability, as well as perceived risks and opportunities. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre. It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process. All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: *Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service *Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner, *Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction, *Reduce Contact Management demand, *Improve force's overall Contact Management performance. Lot 1: .

sig_4136a8ac55350aca9c76.description: Northern Gas Networks (NGN) is seeking to establish a multi‐supplier IT Professional Services Framework to provide flexible, on‐demand specialist capability in support of its technology, digital, infrastructure, and cyber security programmes. The Framework will enable NGN to access appropriately skilled resources to supplement internal teams and support the delivery of projects, programmes, service operations, and specialist technical activities. Services may be required for short‐term assignments or longer engagements, depending on business need, and may be delivered on‐site, remotely, or through a hybrid model. The scope of services is structured across the following LOTs: LOT 1 - Project & Programme Management Including project management, programme management, assurance, and business analysis services. LOT 2 - Architecture Including applications, data, enterprise, solution, infrastructure, and security architecture services. LOT 3 - Software & Infrastructure Delivery Including software development, testing, DevOps, cloud engineering, infrastructure configuration, and technical analyst services. LOT 4 - Cyber Security Including cyber risk and threat assessment, penetration testing (IT and OT), red/blue/purple teaming, incident response planning and testing, and related cyber security services. Suppliers may apply for one or more LOTs and will only be considered for those LOTs where they can demonstrate the required capability. Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee any volume or value of work. Call‐offs under the Framework may be made by direct award or mini‐competition, depending on the nature and value of the requirement, in accordance with the Framework terms. The Framework will be awarded for an initial term of three (3) years, with the option to extend for up to five (5) additional one‐year periods, subject to NGN requirements and performance. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023, using the Competitive Flexible Procedure, with the Contract Notice published via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). Full details of the scope, evaluation methodology, and procurement process are provided within the procurement documentation. Lot 1: Project & Programme Management. Provision of project and programme management capability to support the delivery of IT and digital initiatives, including project managers, programme managers, assurance roles, and business analysts. Services may be required for short‐term assignments or longer engagements to supplement internal delivery teams. Lot 2: Architecture. Provision of architecture services including applications, data, enterprise, solution, infrastructure, and security architecture. Services will support technical design, governance, assurance, and alignment with NGN's technology and cyber strategies across IT and OT environments. Lot 3: Software & Infrastructure Delivery. Provision of software development, testing, DevOps, cloud engineering, infrastructure configuration, and technical analyst services to support application development, systems enhancement, platform delivery, and infrastructure change. Lot 4: Cyber Security. Provision of cyber security services including risk and threat assessment, penetration testing (IT and OT), red/blue/purple teaming, cyber resilience activities, and incident response planning and testing.
sig_4136a8ac55350aca9c76.title: IT Professional Services Framework

sig_414f96999b06b854d502.description: The Berliner Wasserbetriebe are planning the introduction of a central, overarching energy management software in order to uniformly record, manage, evaluate and provide all energy-relevant data of the company for different use cases. The solution is intended to connect the multitude of technical facilities (pumping stations, waterworks, sewage treatment plants, properties, buildings, etc.), the energy meters and sensors installed there, as well as various commercial and technical processes, and to create a consistent, fast, up-to-date and evaluable data hub. Individual solutions and the use of multiple tools are to be abolished and standardised. The software is intended to essentially combine two important areas of application: energy controlling (commercial) and energy management (technical). Through the software, energy flows, consumption, costs, measures and emissions are to be presented transparently and analysed systematically. The goal is to support continuous improvement within the framework of EMAS, through systematic key figure formation and measure controlling, the significant reduction of manual efforts through automated data imports and plausibility checks and report generation, the improvement of data quality for reports, key figures, decisions and compliance with legal requirements (proof obligations EMAS, CSRD, EnEfG).
sig_414f96999b06b854d502.title: Market exploration for an energy controlling tool

sig_41641105a1d617ea34db.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 ARA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial Announcement ADVANCED RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT (ARA) TITLE: ADVANCED TRACKING ARCHITECTURE USING AI (ATA-AI) BAA or ARA NUMBER: FA8750-24-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step ARA which is open and effective until 12 July 2029. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 5pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 12 July 2029, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY25 by 30 NOV 2024 FY26 by 30 NOV 2025 FY27 by 30 NOV 2026 FY28 by 30 NOV 2027 FY29 by 30 NOV 2028 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking research to design, develop, test, evaluate, and deliver innovative technologies and techniques for Next Generation Target Tracking architectures, which exploit a wide array of data sources and leverage the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Machine Inferencing (MI) algorithms in a High Performance Computing (HPC) enabled framework. ARA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this ARA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available ARA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based procurement contracts or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive ARA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): ARA PROGRAM MANAGER: Carolyn Sheaff AFRL/RIED 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Email: AFRL.RIEDBAA.2024@us.af.mil ARA DEPUTY PROGRAM MANAGER: Peter Rocci AFRL/RIED 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Email: AFRL.RIEDBAA.2024@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation ARA number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing through email. Communications with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. PLEASE SEE THE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL ANNOUNCEMENT DETAILS.

sig_416e00cf0a302b7fc55c.description: The subject of the procurement is an information system package intended for monitoring the use of vehicles and for fleet management (hereinafter "System") as well as the necessary positioning devices for the North Karelia wellbeing services county and the South Savo wellbeing services county. The aim is to procure as a ready-made solution a modular, user-friendly and secure comprehensive solution that meets the requirements of data protection and other legislation. The system includes both the application and the necessary positioning equipment. The system must be able to monitor the location and use of vehicles in real time, produce an electronic driving log in accordance with the Tax Administration's requirements and manage the organisation's fleet centrally. The objective is to improve the manageability and usability of driving data at the level of the entire organisation. The system collects and analyses driving data and produces reports to support management and decision-making. The system produces real-time information on the use of vehicles and forms a clear overall picture that improves occupational safety and enables the efficiency of vehicle use to be increased. The system replaces current paper driving logs and the basic vehicle information maintained in Excel spreadsheets. It combines the vehicle's positioning data with driver identification and enables the automatic maintenance of the electronic driving log. The system must support modern interface connections through which information can be received from other systems and information transferred to other systems. The procured system and service package as well as the delivery and commissioning project shall be implemented separately for each Contracting Authority. A separate Delivery Agreement and Service Agreement shall be concluded between each Contracting Authority and the Supplier. The contract period is fixed-term for 60 months and continues thereafter until further notice. This is a joint procurement by two independent contracting authorities. The implementation of the procurement requires that the contracting authority has the appropriations necessary for it at its disposal. If the tender price of the subject of the procurement exceeds the contracting-authority-specific appropriation allocated for it, the procurement will not be implemented in these respects.
sig_416e00cf0a302b7fc55c.title: Vehicle management and positioning system, North Karelia and South Savo wellbeing services counties

sig_417d15ac89dbba52fcf6.description: The City of Bielefeld is planning the comprehensive redesign of Herforder Straße along the entire route between Zimmerstraße and the city boundary. The project is the Bielefeld part of the future OWL fast cycle route 2.0 segment between Bielefeld and Herford. The OWL fast cycle route 2.0 is intended to enable a continuous, high-performance cycling connection from Rheda-Wiedenbrück via Gütersloh and Bielefeld to Herford and to connect to the RS 3 towards Minden. Herforder Straße is classified in municipal, regional and regiopolis cycling concepts as an axis of the highest network category and represents a central development route for cycling. The project is of outstanding importance for both cycling and motor vehicle traffic. Outbound from the city, the route takes over the function of federal road B 61 in sections and connects the upper centre of Bielefeld with the middle centre of Herford. At the same time, due to the future connection of the L 712n to the A 2, increasing traffic volumes are to be expected, so that accompanying traffic-model-based studies and coordination with external specialist planning are required. The implementation of the overall project is carried out in sections. The framework conditions differ significantly along Herforder Straße and shape the focal points of communication and participation. A detailed further description can be found in the document "Information on the Subject Matter of the Contract". Herforder Straße (fast cycle route) Public participation and project communication
sig_417d15ac89dbba52fcf6.title: Herforder Straße high-speed cycle route public participation and project communication

sig_417e69f5f90a57bbfe83.description: The system's product range comprises all forms of IT operating services, both traditional on-premise solutions as well as cloud-based solutions and hybrid solutions. The system covers IT operating services under the seven service areas listed below and elaborated in Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System. In addition, as part of its delivery of IT operating services to the customer, the supplier is responsible for making the necessary operational adjustments and configurations, as well as delivering cross-functional services and ordering services related to the IT operating services. The supplier is responsible, inter alia, for operating, maintaining and administering the IT operating services and making the necessary minor adjustments, up-/downscaling, configurations, patching, etc., and handling the service management processes, including documentation, reporting, ITIL processes and participation in the customer's governance organisation as part of the delivery of IT operating services to the customer. The supplier must also ensure that the supplier's IT operating services have a high degree of security, which the supplier must incorporate into its IT operating services and ensure the necessary monitoring and control of. In connection with specific procurements under the system, the supplier must deliver an onboarding transition service and, in connection with the total or partial termination of the Delivery Contract, also deliver an offboarding transition service. Common to both transition services is that the supplier must manage, operate and plan these phases and assist the customer, the outgoing supplier and the incoming supplier to the necessary extent to ensure a successful transition. It is possible to purchase various forms of IT operating services that all complement each other. The system has a high degree of flexibility and contains many different use scenarios that make it possible to purchase IT services such as, for example: publicly available cloud tools as well as managed cloud services and administration of cloud platforms, storage, backup, computing, physical floor space in a data centre, racks for IT equipment, office WiFi solutions, network cables for data centres, managed network solutions, VPN solutions, operation of standard and specially developed applications, database operations, middleware operations, rental of computers, tablets, PC screens, headsets and associated mobile device management, as well as service desk, Security Operations Centre (SOC), operation of modern office applications including e-mail, collaboration platforms, archiving systems, etc. Overall, the system category contains the following seven service areas, with associated underlying services, cross-functional services and ordering services that the customer can procure across: • Cloud operations • Data centre operations • Co-location • Network operations • Application operations • End-user services • Security services Under the seven service areas, it is possible to procure capacity – for example, cloud capacity and server and storage capacity. Reference is otherwise made to Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System for an elaboration of the 7 service areas that the subject matter of the system consists of.

sig_41960c8c62ed060b5239.description: The subject of this contract is the provision of specialised advisory and technical support services to the Contracting Authority for the effective implementation, management and monitoring of the sub-projects 'Supply of materials and services for the equipment of the GRNET hub network as well as for protection equipment against cyberattacks' and 'Supply of materials and services of network, computing and storage equipment for the data centres of GRNET' of the project 'Replacement and expansion of the equipment of the data centres of GRNET S.A.' (OPS TA Code 5225560). The Technical Support Consultant (TSC) will act as the strategic and operational supporter of the Contracting Authority throughout the duration of the project's implementation, assuming the role of liaison between the involved parties, the technical and quality monitoring of the project Contractor's deliverables and ensuring compliance with schedules, requirements and quality specifications. The subject of this contract is the provision of technical assistance and support to the Contracting Authority for the correct and timely execution of the sub-projects mentioned above. Due to the complexity and size of the sub-projects, external technical assistance is required for their implementation and monitoring until their completion and final acceptance. Therefore, the subject of the technical assistance sub-project is the provision of specialised technical support consultant services, so as to ensure the effective implementation of the sub-projects in terms of timeliness, quality and results in general. The timely and correct implementation of the sub-projects requires a series of coordinated management and monitoring actions. The TSC is called upon to support these actions, providing support to the Contracting Authority on technical/financial, organisational, managerial and expertise-related matters whenever required. Specifically, the TSC will undertake the provision of Technical Support Services, under the supervision of the Contracting Authority, in the following categories: - Organisation of the Management / Quality System of the Overall Project - Monitoring – Support of the progress of the sub-projects' implementation - Support of the sub-projects' acceptance procedures. The TSC will support the management and monitoring tasks of the sub-projects' implementation by providing appropriate human resources and the necessary infrastructure and tools. The purpose of the technical assistance sub-project is broken down into the following: - Monitoring the implementation of the sub-projects, with an emphasis on adhering to time and cost constraints. - Ensuring the quality of the operation of the sub-projects' management system, while simultaneously upgrading its implementation means and communication between all involved parties. - Ensuring the quality of the deliverables and products of the sub-projects. - Ensuring the interconnection and operational and technical interoperability of the sub-projects. - Systematic utilisation of human resources during the implementation of the sub-projects. - Successful completion and securing of the results of the sub-projects and the action in general. The TSC will assist the Contracting Authority with the aim of fully and continuously informing it regarding the progress of the implementation of the main sub-project and in particular: - In adhering to the established schedule of administrative actions and tasks. - In accelerating the implementation of tasks that are experiencing time delays. - In coordinating the bodies involved in the project with the aim of maximising benefits and accelerating actions for effective implementation. - In the timely identification of prerequisites required for the smooth progress of the main sub-project. - In the timely identification of problems that may jeopardise the implementation of the main sub-project and in the timely submission of proposals for addressing them. - In the timely identification of impacts from non-adherence to pre-planned actions or implementation schedules and in the submission of proposals for managing them. - In ensuring the technical soundness of the main sub-project which will allow for the effective and efficient commissioning of the systems and infrastructure that will be developed. - In potential improvements and revisions to the implementation design of the main sub-project, with the aim of their successful completion and the maximisation of the benefit that may arise from their productive operation. The objectives of the TSC's services are: - Contributing to the preparation and ensuring the correct implementation of the sub-projects, in terms of time, financial and technical planning. - Ensuring the quality and technical soundness of the deliverables of each distinct work package of the sub-projects, and ensuring the interconnection, coordination and interoperability of the individual elements of the Overall Project/Action. - Successful implementation and ensuring the functionality of the Overall Project, as well as the effective commissioning of the software and equipment, within the pre-defined time and cost limits. - Ensuring (forecasting, formulating, shaping) the prerequisites for smooth operation after the installation and acceptance of the sub-projects, successful integration into its operational environment and the maximisation of their utilisation by the Project Owner, for the benefit of the citizen and society as a whole. - Systematic upgrading and effective utilisation of human resources, throughout the duration of the sub-projects' implementation, so as to ensure the smooth introduction and longevity of their results.

sig_41bd88421467f362e556.description: Chelmsford College is a Further Education college offering a variety of courses, both vocational and professional courses, with c.3500 student and c400 staff members across two main campuses, providing courses to 16-19 learners, apprentices and adult day and evening courses. The College website serves a wide array of people in the community from students & parents to local businesses and so the winning design should reflect that the website needs to appeal and be accessible to multiple stakeholder groups. The website's primary purpose is learner recruitment. Its priority audiences are prospective 16 to 19 learners and their parents and carers, adult learners, and employers and apprenticeship partners. It also serves current students, staff and job seekers. The college's objectives for the new website are to increase applicant conversion from course page to submitted application, to deliver a mobile-first and fully accessible experience, to provide search and filtering across the full course offer, to allow marketing to publish and update content directly, and to meet the college's information security and data protection requirements, including for the personal data collected through the application process. Bidders are encouraged to propose approaches that meet these objectives. Our current website was built 15 years ago and with only minor cosmetic changes since then. We have 202 pages in total 72 static pages and 130 dynamic pages that contain job adverts, course information and newsletters. All of the content on the website is taken from our internal databases and intranet so any company tendering will need to be able to interface with those tables. The college has a dedicated team that can handle the daily maintenance and updating of the new website but does not have the time the develop a new website inhouse which is why this project is going out to tender. We are looking for a company that will be able to build the website and then pass it off to the college to manage the day-to-day activities. You can read more about Chelmsford College on their website: https://www.chelmsford.ac.uk/ Lot 1: .
sig_41bd88421467f362e556.title: Chelmsford College Website tender

sig_41c87f8b745600783b86.description: Grounds Maintenance System RFI Lot 1: . Fife Council is seeking to understand the market for modern Grounds Maintenance Solutions capable of supporting operational delivery, financial management, and performance monitoring. The existing system used within the Grounds Maintenance Service presents a number of challenges, including limited mobile functionality, reliance on manual processes, and constraints in reporting and system integration. The Grounds Maintenance Service has been using its current back-office system for a number of years to support key activities such as scheduling, asset management, and billing. The Council is therefore seeking input from suppliers to help inform its future requirements and shape a potential procurement approach. The Council is now seeking to explore alternative solutions available within the market that may better meet its current and future Grounds Maintenance requirements. A list of high-level requirements has been developed in collaboration with the service and the Council’s IT Service. Potential Suppliers are invited to review these requirements and provide information on solutions that may be capable of meeting the Council’s needs. The requirements identified by the Grounds Maintenance Service and IT Service are set out below. We would welcome responses from suppliers to support the Council in developing its understanding of the market and informing this Request for Information exercise.. This is a request for Information only.

sig_41e2d09608393044b872.description: NHS 24 is undertaking market engagement to inform the potential procurement of a Headless Content Management System (CMS) and Digital Experience Platform (DXP). The exercise will explore available solutions, delivery models, implementation approaches and commercial options to support the future NHS 24 digital experience and content management capability. Lot 1: . NHS 24 is undertaking a preliminary market consultation to inform the potential procurement and implementation of a modern Headless Content Management System (CMS) and wider Digital Experience Platform (DXP) capability. The objective is to understand available market solutions, delivery approaches, commercial models and routes to market capable of supporting a secure, scalable and API-driven platform for the creation, management and reuse of content across websites, mobile experiences, conversational interfaces and future digital channels. The potential requirement may include platform licensing, hosting, implementation, systems integration, content modelling, content migration, user experience design, front-end development, training, support, knowledge transfer and ongoing service management. NHS 24 has not yet determined the preferred procurement approach and is seeking supplier input on alternative delivery models, including platform-only, implementation-only, end-to-end and multi-supplier arrangements. This exercise is for market engagement purposes only and does not constitute a formal procurement competition or commitment to procure. Supplier responses will be used to inform NHS 24's future strategy, scope and procurement approach
sig_41e2d09608393044b872.title: Headless Content Management System (CMS) and Digital Experience Platform (DXP) Market Engagement

sig_41ed77dda6b30bf6824d.description: Within the Veiligheidsregio Kennemerland (VRK), an up-to-date and integral overview of paper and digital information management is currently lacking. Paper and digital information objects are scattered and sometimes stored in multiple copies across various sources, including cabinets, network drives, cloud storage, local environments, and email. A significant portion of this information consists of unstructured files that have been created over time and are used and managed by various VRK departments. The tender relates to the existing information management of VRK. The assignment includes analysing, assessing, cleaning up, structuring, plotting, and preparing existing information objects for migration in accordance with the Processing Framework established by VRK. In doing so, VRK will provide the location of the existing information objects to the Contractor. The goal is to create a demonstrably compliant, organised, and future-proof information environment. The amount mentioned below is not representative of the assignment. The amount is included here solely to make it possible to publish the assignment on TenderNed. The estimated value of the Assignment cannot be determined exactly in terms of amounts due to the nature of the Assignment. The scope in terms of the quantity of information objects is given in paragraph 2.2. It should be noted that after an initial inventory, it may appear that a portion of this quantity may not be eligible for further processing, for example due to the age of these information objects. No rights can be derived from this statement. With a view to political, economic, budgetary, organisational, and/or administrative developments and the associated growth and shrinkage of the Contracting Authority, it is possible that the Assignment may expand, shrink, or change. These developments may affect the scope of the Assignment. Tenderers must take this into account. sig_41f331a1b166ab9e1f5f.description: Sund & Bælt uses Maximo Application Suite (MAS) as its Enterprise Asset Management system. Sund & Bælt's activities include the construction, operation & maintenance of some of the world's largest bridges and tunnels, including the Great Belt Fixed Link, the Øresund Fixed Link and the upcoming Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link. In addition, Sund & Bælt owns four ferry ports north and south of the Great Belt Fixed Link, and Sund & Bælt ensures that they are maintained and operated. The ports are Odden, Ebeltoft, Spodsbjerg and Tårs ports. sig_4240997faada84ec7457.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 from a merger of the railway and postal bus services. The transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer district, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg district, the Euskirchen district and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban conurbations with sparsely populated, more rural areas. With capacity, competence and many years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region are on the move reliably and safely – and in an environmentally friendly, sustainable and innovative way. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated by the company itself and some of which operate on behalf of RVK. The transport network comprises 132 lines with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 lines are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a mileage of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. Most of the RVK buses are already equipped with TFT interior displays. However, as not all buses have TFT monitors, RVK is procuring at least 100 additional 29 inch TFT interior displays (and up to a total of 350 TFT interior displays) for use in public transport vehicles via a framework agreement. sig_4241ee1527fd0e26e35d.description: NHS Scotland intends to procure a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme to support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes. The programme will deliver a structured, evidence-based lifestyle intervention through a digital platform, including access to health coaching, peer support, and tools to support behaviour change and self-management. The procurement is expected to be undertaken via a Restricted Procedure, with a single supplier appointed to a national framework. Lot 1: . This Prior Information Notice (PIN) relates to NHS Scotland’s intention to tender for a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme. The programme will identify individuals at risk of Type 2 Diabetes based on clinical indicators (including HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose levels) or a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes. It will provide a tailored, nine-month, evidence-based lifestyle intervention aimed at reducing the risk of progression to Type 2 Diabetes. The digital service will support Service Users via an application-based platform, providing access to trained health coaches, online peer support communities, and functionality to set, track, and monitor personalised health goals. The successful bidder will be required to deliver the programme in a way that is inclusive and accessible to Service Users from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. This will include ensuring the service is culturally sensitive to local populations and flexible enough to meet the needs of users with diverse requirements, including appropriate language support. Participants will be able to access the programme through multiple referral routes, including Primary Care (e.g. GP referral) and self-referral pathways. Current funding has been allocated to support up to 15,000 users over a three-year period. The proposed framework will operate as a single-supplier arrangement and will also include provision for the delivery of a Hypertension Pathway for approximately 500 users per annum. Eligibility for the hypertension pathway will be based on a confirmed diagnosis of primary hypertension alongside a BMI ≥25 (or BMI ≥23 for minority ethnic groups). Please Note: During the term of the Framework Agreement, NHS Scotland reserves the right, should funding become available, to increase the volume of service users (current estimate of 15000 over the initial 3-years of the Framework Agreement term) who may access the Programme. For example, additional purchases may be made which exceed the level of funding currently secured as a result of clinical and service outcomes and benefits which support wider adoption of the Programme. The Authority also reserves the right to expand the scope of the service to include additional cohorts, pathways, or clinical indicators (for example, the inclusion of further at-risk populations identified through screening), which may increase overall demand under the Framework. The procurement is expected to be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising two stages: Stage 1 Selection Stage (SPD Assessment): Suppliers will be required to complete and submit a Single Procurement Document (SPD). This stage will assess bidders’ suitability to proceed and will include a combination of pass/fail criteria (e.g. mandatory and discretionary exclusion grounds, economic and financial standing) and scored evaluation. As part of the SPD, the Authority will assess technical and professional ability, including responses to scored questions and requests for relevant examples of previous experience. These responses will be weighted and scored to enable the Authority to evaluate capability and rank suppliers. A shortlist of the highest-ranking bidders will be invited to progress to Stage 2. Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender (ITT): Only suppliers shortlisted at Stage 1 will be invited to submit a full tender. Bidders will be required to respond to a Statement of Requirements (SoR), setting out how they will deliver the contract, including proposed methodology, service delivery model, and pricing. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria, based on quality and price, to determine the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT). Stage 1 is expected to commence mid to late August 2026, with Stage 2 anticipated to commence in early October 2026.. This project is derived from the Accelerated National Innovation Adoption (ANIA) Pathway. This is an initiative focused on using technology to fast-track proven innovations into the healthcare frontline on a Once for Scotland basis. See link:https://www.nhscfsd.co.uk/our-work/innovation/accelerated-national-innovation-adoption-ania-pathway/
sig_4241ee1527fd0e26e35d.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme
