sig_427152488a7d768352a5.description: Citizen is a major housing provider in the West Midlands, managing 30,000 homes across Coventry, Birmingham, and surrounding rural areas. Our customers live in a wide range of homes, from family houses to high rise apartments, supported housing, and schemes for older people. While most customers rent, we also support many shared owners and leaseholders. Our purpose is to provide homes that act as a foundation for life, and we are continuing to transform our services to better meet customer needs. Our new Business Strategy (2026-2030) sets out two key ambitions: • to deliver services shaped by customers that feel personal and exceed expectations, and; • to use data and technology to provide more proactive services and faster outcomes. Although we hold extensive information about our customers and homes, we want to strengthen how we use this insight to understand our customers more deeply and tailor communication, engagement, and service delivery. We are therefore seeking to engage with organisations that can support us in developing a customer segmentation model or approach that is right for Citizen and aligned with our strategic ambitions. We want to explore market capability, understand available methodologies, and inform a potential future procurement process. Proposals will subsequently be invited from consultancy practices who can demonstrate: • A proven track record in delivering similar segmentation projects • Extensive knowledge of social housing operations, and customer bases • Dedicated team, with the skills and experience required for the services. sig_4281cb4f53b773e6a7aa.description: Solicitation Number: Notice Type: W31P4Q27RA009 Request for Information/Sources Sought Purpose & Disclaimer: This Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be considered as an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Quotations (RFQ), or Request for Proposals (RFP). Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the U.S. Government (USG) to acquire any products or services described in this RFI/SS. Your response to this notice is strictly voluntary and will be treated only as information for the USG to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI/SS, and the USG will not pay for the information submitted. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. The information provided may be used by the Army in developing its acquisition strategy. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition-sensitive information contained in their response. If a solicitation is released for the supplies or services described herein, it will be synopsized on the government-wide point of entry (SAM.gov). The response date for this RFI/SS is 25 September 2026. Background: The US Army, Search Track Acquire Radiate Eliminate (STARE) Project Office is conducting market research for Production and Engineering Services of the Lower Tier Air Missile Defense Sensor (LTAMDS). All production and engineering services must strictly conform to the U.S. Government (USG) performance specification (P-Spec), MIS-PRF-59464, and the Raytheon Prime Item Performance (PIP) specification, MIS-PRF-62863, Rev B. Effort would include all associated hardware, software, firmware, and engineering services inherent to production (e.g. inspection, systems integration, logistics support, depot maintenance, spares package development, program management, configuration management, software development, product assurance, verification of system performance, hazardous material management, obsolescence management, safety, testing and evaluation, coordination for and implementation of future training exercises etc.), interim contractor support (ICS), system integration and check out support (SICO), new equipment training (NET), and technical documentation. The USG has a requirement for follow-on production of LTAMDS following successful completion of the LTAMDS 6-lot Urgent Material Release (UMR) Prototype Development Project. This effort was previously competitively awarded on 16 October 2019 to Raytheon Company through an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), W15QKN-20-9-1002, pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022 (formerly 10 U.S.C.§ 2371b(a)). Other related awards include: • Pre-Planned Product Improvement (P3I): A 2-lot agreement awarded on 24 May 2022 to Raytheon Company through an OTA, AMTC-21-02-008, pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 4022. Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP): A four-option-year, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)-based Undefinitized Contract Action awarded on 31 July 2024 to Raytheon Company through Army Contracting Command (Contract #: W31P4Q-24-C-0024), pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. § 2304(a)(7)), as implemented in FAR 6.302-1. The LRIP contract has an anticipated production quantity of up to 48 radars. Scope of Planned Procurement: This follow-on LTAMDS requirement is anticipated to be awarded as a seven (7) year Multiyear Procurement (MYP), Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. This effort will cover a production ceiling of twenty (20) LTAMDS radars annually. The award will also include annual task orders for engineering services, alongside yearly orders for SICO, ICS, and NET support. First Article Inspection (FAI), Environmental Stress Screening (ESS), Product Acceptance, Functional Configuration Audit (FCA), Physical Configuration Audit (PCA), and Highly Accelerated Life Testing (HALT) may be required for baseline revisions and/or updates. Initial delivery of the LTAMDS radars is required no later than 33 months after contract award. This procurement will include access to classified information. The successful contractor must be a U.S. corporation with a secure manufacturing facility approved to the SECRET level by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) (formerly DSS). Additionally, the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) may conduct a pre-award survey of the contractor’s facility to evaluate technical capability, financial viability, and quality assurance processes to minimize LTAMDS program execution risks. Technical Data Package (TDP) Constraints A formal Technical Data Package (TDP) was submitted to the USG on 31 July 2026. The USG is currently executing an exhaustive technical validation and quality assurance assessment against all applicable American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) digital product definition and drafting standards (including model-based definition and data schema protocols), alongside establishing downstream 3D model generation and repository architectures. Due to the duration required to complete this verification and standardization process, the USG will not release technical data packages, native 3D models, or detailed specifications in support of this RFI/SS. Acquisition Strategy & Authority The Government will consider all capability statements received. To be deemed a viable source, interested firms must demonstrate their capability to fulfill the requirements without causing substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, and without causing unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's urgent air defense requirements. Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), OR REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ). RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE RFQ, IFB, OR RFP. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WIL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. Required Submission Information Interested firms that believe they have the capability, experience, and legal access to data necessary to fulfill the requirements detailed above are invited to submit a statement of capability. Submissions must include the following information: 1. Company name, physical address, overnight delivery address (if different from mailing address), CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Primary point of contact (POC) name, title, email address, and telephone number. 2. Business size status under the NAICS code associated with radar manufacturing (i.e. Large, Small Disadvantaged, Veteran Owned, Woman Owned, etc.) 3. Affirmation that the company is a U.S. corporation and verification of active facility clearance at the SECRET level, and confirmation of cleared personnel capable of starting work immediately upon award. 4. A description of your firm's manufacturing expertise, capacity, and facility infrastructure to meet the required LTAMDS production throughput (up to 20 radars annually) 5. Detailed explanation of how your firm would execute First Article Inspection (FAI), ESS, FCA, PCA, and HALT along with an estimated schedule and cost associated with completing these activities prior to commencing deliveries. 6. Assuming the Government will not provide a TDP, provide a detailed estimate of the schedule and cost (via a rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimate) required to reverse-engineer or independently develop and qualify a compatible alternative radar system. 7. Explain how your proposed schedule—including necessary timelines for reverse engineering, prototype development, system integration, qualification, and testing—can realistically meet the Government’s required initial delivery window of no later than 36 months after contract award. 8. Explain how your strategy prevents substantial duplication of non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs to the Government. 9. Evidence of the company's performance history and experience meeting strict contractual due dates on programs of similar scope, technical complexity, and scale. Submission Instructions All responses must be UNCLASSIFIED. All questions must be submitted to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer identified above. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought. All such information must be clearly identified and marked at the paragraph level. All assumptions, including any assumed USG support, shall be clearly identified. Responses must be submitted in electronic format (compatible with MS Word or PDF) and must not exceed 15 pages total (including tables, charts, and appendices). Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged. The Government will not provide direct feedback or individual evaluations to respondents regarding their submissions. The Government reserves the right to contact respondents for clarification or additional information as necessary. All responses must be transmitted electronically no later than 21 October 2026 (or the updated date indicated on the final posting) to the following primary POCs: Primary Point of Contact: Dawn Patterson Chief, Acquisition Management Division STARE Project Office, CPE – Defensive Fires, PAE – Fires SFAE-PFD-R Email: Dawn.p.patterson2.civ@mail.mil Contracting Office Address: Army Contracting Command-Redstone (ACC-RSA) CCAM-MSC-B ACC-RSA, Bldg 4505 Huntsville, AL 35898 ACC Point of Contact: Joel Koppinger Contracting Officer CCAM-MSC-B, ACC-RSA Joel.m.koppinger.civ@mail.mil

sig_42a2ad5cb89a181e57ba.description: The Stadt Münster - citeq is setting up a dynamic purchasing system with a time limit until 30.12.2025 for the digitisation of paper files. This is the publication of the extension of the dynamic purchasing system (pursuant to Section 23 paragraph 2 no. 1 of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV)) initially until 30.12.2026. A dynamic purchasing system in accordance with Section 120 paragraph 1 of the German Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) is a time-limited, exclusively electronic procedure for the procurement of standard market services where the characteristics generally available on the market meet the requirements of the contracting authority. An unlimited number of contractors are publicly invited to submit non-binding declarations for the provision of services, and all suitable contractors that have submitted admissible declarations for the provision of services are admitted to participate in the system for the entire duration of the system. An application to participate is possible at any time. Companies will be informed of their admission to the dynamic purchasing system via the communication area on the procurement marketplace. Following the publication of the dynamic purchasing system, an initial time limit of 30 days must be observed before opening applications to participate. Thereafter, no further time limits apply and new applications can be opened immediately. These applications will be evaluated within ten working days of receipt. If an individual award is pending, all admitted companies will be invited to submit a tender.

sig_42c53916dcdafd18e910.description: The project entitled "Design, Implementation, Commissioning and Support of the Productive Operation of the Single Real Estate Registry" seeks the systematic recording, management and monitoring of real estate through an integrated information system, which will gather, systematise and integrate digital information maintained by different public administration and private sector bodies. The Subproject "Interoperability of the Single Real Estate Registry with Public and Private Sector Bodies" includes both the analysis and study of existing data maintained by each body, and the necessary development services for the exchange, cleansing and optimal utilisation of these data via the Single Real Estate Registry (for updating and optimising the data they maintain through the exchange of more recent data from other bodies). The bodies estimated to be interconnected with the system in the first phase include (bodies may be added or removed during the Implementation Study period): • Cadastre • Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) • Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) • Technical Chamber of Greece (TEE) • Insurance companies • Communications network providers (e.g. Cosmote, Vodafone, WIND, etc.) • Water Supply and Sewerage Providers (e.g. EYDAP, EYATH, etc.) • Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT) • Public Properties Company (ETAD) • Central Union of Municipalities of Greece (KEDE) • Ministry of Energy • Ministry of Justice • Ministry of Finance The operation of the overall project aims at the creation of a modern, fully automated electronic real estate registry, to ensure the greatest possible information, publicity and security of transactions of citizens and involved bodies. This procurement procedure will result in the Implementation - Completion - Installation - Development and Customisation of the Single Electronic Real Estate Registry, as well as the creation of operational customisation of the framework within new technological and economic data based on European and international best practices. The subject matter of the contract has as its main axis the design, implementation, installation and commissioning of an interoperability platform and training of the administrators of each body, which will be interconnected with the Single Real Estate Registry. The project aims at the development and provision of specialised web services that will allow interoperability between the information systems of Public Administration bodies and the SRER. Specifically, it includes: • Development of interfaces (APIs) for data exchange between different systems with data concerning real estate. • Enhancement of the Information System of the Single Real Estate Registry by introducing and activating additional electronic services. • Creation and provision of services of common interest for Public Administration bodies, facilitating the upgrading of their electronic services and the completion of the registries they maintain. The provided services are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: 72322000-8 - Data management services 72310000-1 - Data processing services 72262000-9 - Software development services 80533100-0 - IT education services 72000000-5 - Information technology services: consulting, software development, Internet and support Deliverables of the contract are those referred to in APPENDIX I - DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PHYSICAL AND FINANCIAL SUBJECT MATTER of this document. - According to the relevant analysis, the project will be delivered in one phase, but will have intermediate deliverables per body interconnected with the Single Real Estate Registry. - Tenders are submitted for the entire subject matter of this procurement procedure, as detailed in the contract documents, because objectively the procurement procedure is indivisible. In particular, Subproject 2, despite including interconnection with sixteen (16) different bodies (Cadastre, AADE, HEDNO, TEE, insurance companies, communications network providers, EYDAP, EYATH, ELSTAT, ETAD, KEDE, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Justice and others), is not subdivided into separate contracts for important reasons of technical and managerial efficiency. Primarily, the development of interoperability solutions requires specialised expertise in areas such as web services development, big data management, implementation of cybersecurity protocols and the execution of real-time communication systems between heterogeneous information systems. The award of all interconnections to a single contractor (vendor) ensures faster implementation times, as the time-consuming coordination process between multiple contractors and the need to harmonise different technical approaches are avoided. In addition, all interconnections will feature common characteristics regarding communication architecture, security protocols, transmitted data structure and authentication and authorisation procedures. The aforementioned homogeneity significantly facilitates the long-term maintenance of the system, its expansion to new bodies and the assurance of cybersecurity at all interconnection points, thus contributing to the achievement of the strategic objectives of the Action within the stipulated time limits.

sig_42c57b0979d7429a8c6a.description: Brief description of the procurement: "Supply of digitalised ecological islands in the Town of Cisnădie", including transport, unloading, handling, assembly, positioning, fitting, anchoring, installation, configuration, commissioning, testing, training, warranty, maintenance and digital services. The contract has as its object the supply, installation and operationalisation of 23 above-ground digitalised ecological islands, composed of a variable number of modules for each location, up to the limit of the total quantity of 92 modules, in accordance with the annexes to the Specifications. Each eco-island will include, as appropriate: protection modules/cases, mobile containers of 1.100 litres, ramp, base levelling system, waste insertion devices, drive and locking mechanisms, batteries, control units, card readers, fill-level sensors, communication equipment (router/GSM module), access cards, firmware, mobile application and software platform. The insertion devices are drums for the residual and biodegradable fractions, and flaps for the recyclable fractions respectively. The drive and locking mechanisms comprise the actuator and the electric lock. The modules are placed on the site without anchoring to the platform. The contractor shall fully carry out all operations necessary for handing over the system in working order: transport, insurance, unloading, handling, assembly, positioning, fixing, installation, cabling, configuration, card programming, commissioning, testing, training and handover of documentation. NOTE: Economic operators may request clarifications a maximum of 20 days before the deadline established for the submission of tenders, and the contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information on the 11-th day before the deadline date for the submission of tenders. Suspensive condition regarding the conclusion of the contract: (1) The conclusion of the public procurement contract is suspensively conditioned on the completion of the award procedure and the signature of the contract no later than 20.12.2026. This is the deadline until which the financing from the state budget, allocated according to the State Budget Law for the year 2026 and Annex no. 7, can be committed. (2) If, for reasons not attributable to the Contracting Authority, the contract cannot be signed by the date provided for in para. (1), the condition is considered unfulfilled and the financing is lost. Among these reasons are the duration of the settlement of appeals and the legal waiting periods. The conclusion of the contract thus becomes impossible, and the Contracting Authority shall cancel the procedure pursuant to art. 212 para. (1) lit. c) of Law no. 98/2016. (3) The Contracting Authority shall pursue the conclusion of the contract with celerity, in compliance with legal deadlines. This condition does not confer upon it the right to refuse discretionarily the signature of the contract before the date provided for in para. (1). (4) By submitting a tender, tenderers take note of this condition and accept that its non-fulfilment does not confer upon them the right to the conclusion of the contract, to damages or to the reimbursement of tender preparation costs. Exceptions are situations where the cancellation is attributable to the Contracting Authority, according to the law. (5) The period of validity of the tenders must cover at least 20.12.2026. The object of the award procedure is the supply, installation and operationalisation of 23 above-ground digitalised ecological islands. Each eco-island will consist of a variable number of individual modules, established for each location in accordance with Annex no. 2, each module including a mobile container with the nominal capacity of 1.100 litres. The total quantity is 92 modules, distributed as follows: a) 12 modules for biodegradable waste – 1,1 m3/module; b) 48 modules for residual waste – 1,1 m3/module; c) 15 modules for plastic and metal – 1,1 m3/module; d) 17 modules for paper and cardboard – 1,1 m3/module. Each eco-island will be equipped with a digital component consisting of the hardware assembly and software solution described in these specifications. The contractor shall supply and program the access cards in the quantity and according to the allocation rule provided in Annex no. 1, including the reserve stock established thereby.
sig_42c57b0979d7429a8c6a.title: SUPPLY OF DIGITALISED ECOLOGICAL ISLANDS IN THE TOWN OF CISNĂDIE

sig_42e027755c916c659253.description: This market consultation is aimed at solution providers who can offer the following service portfolio: A SaaS-based TI threat modeling solution that can map the following essential services: Comprehensive threat modeling, particularly for the future platform strategy of the TI, in order to make the criticality of threats and their impacts identifiable more quickly. Making threats that have arisen through the interaction of various products and services visible. Reusability of TI information objects, their protection requirements, standardized TI measures (AFOs) and protection modules, to create a uniform security architecture. Integration of Jira, Confluence, and Polarion to be able to integrate existing information objects and measures into the tool. Visibility of the assignment of information objects to various products and services. Uniform methodological approach. Uniform documentation form with database support. Complete product-specific threat models (supply processes). Comprehensive TI threat model (E2E consideration). AI support. Involvement of external experts as a QA measure. Further ancillary requirements in accordance with the questionnaire. The results serve as the basis for a potential procurement decision and do not constitute a binding tender. The aim of this market consultation is to gain an overview of available solutions and their performance, integration options, and pricing models. On the basis of the information gathered, suitable providers are to be identified and pre-qualified for a subsequent product demonstration. An award is planned subsequently.

sig_42e42b71e9ac6344935f.description: NICE is holding a virtual supplier event about its Access and Identity Management System (AIMS) on April 16th 2026, 11:30am to 1pm as part of procurement activities for a new 3-year contract (plus 2 x 12-month). This system provides secure authentication and authorisation for eligible NHS and wider health and social care staff seeking who want to digital knowledge resources purchased by national, regional and local health organisations. AIMS comprises two interdependent components delivered as a single, integrated service: (1) an Identity Provider (IdP) service, which isan “identify management” capability to manage user identification and authentication; and (2) a Federated Access Management service, which is a “publisher federation” capability to manage integration with publisher platforms and ensures users receive the correct access rights. Maintaining this integration is essential to guarantee continuity of access to evidence for the healthcare workforce and to uphold contractual obligations with publishers. At the event, NICE will describe the draft service requirements and hold a question-and-answer session. NICE will highlight the importance of the federation and federated access elements of the service that is used by content providers. The event will be an opportunity for NICE to gather feedback from suppliers about specific aspects of the proposed service and for suppliers to ask questions about and to better understand the service requirements. The draft timeline for the procurement is: ITT publication in June 2026, contract award in September 2026 and service start in May 2027. The provided specification is subject to change in response to feedback from the event. To express interest and participate in this supplier event, please register and apply via Atamis e-sourcing portal https://atamis-1928.my.site.com/s/Welcome To find this opportunity in the e-sourcing portal, select "Find Opportunities" and then search by project C429620 or title. Once you have found the Opportunity, press the 'Register Interest' button to register your interest. This will make the project to appear on 'My proposals and quotes'. From there you can review documents, send clarification messages, submit the response, or decline to respond, if you decide not to participate in the opportunity. Should suppliers have any queries, or having problems using the portal, please contact Atamis Helpdesk at: Phone: +448000988201 E-mail: support-health@atamis.co.uk Lot 1: .

The subject of the contract is "Purchase of equipment for the selective collection of waste at the place of its generation" for Miejski Zakład Komunalny Sp. z o.o. in Leżajsk. The contract has been divided into four parts: Part of the contract no. 1 - Modular shelters, Part of the contract no. 2 - Waste shelters, Part of the contract no. 3 - Street bins, Part of the contract no. 4 - Waste-compacting container bins. Each Contractor may submit only one tender for the entire procedure, which means that in one tender form (or by submitting one package of documents) the contractor indicates the parts for which they are submitting a tender. The subject of the contract is the execution of a freestanding shelter consisting of 8 pcs. of prefabricated modules (so-called "smart shelter") in which containers/bins for waste for selective waste collection at source will be placed, with access to the waste storage zone exclusively by authorised residents. The dimensions of a single metal module are approximately 1,8 x 1,4 x 1,7 m (width x depth x height without masts). Bearing in mind that dimensions may differ between individual Manufacturers/Suppliers, a dimension discrepancy tolerance range of ±20% is accepted. A single module is to be an assembly of container housings connected to each other (a total of 8 pcs. of modules) standing in each other's immediate vicinity. The entire waste disposal process is to be monitored and metered. Every piece of household waste generated and collected in collective bins in a housing estate or at a designated location in the municipality is to be metered. Metering is to consist of assigning information such as name, fraction type, mass, data identifying the date and time of user authorisation to an individual billing account created for each household covered by the system. User identification should take place via a QR code sticker, which must be assigned to a given fraction and a given household, and the opening of the container flap should take place only after bringing the QR code sticker close to a reader placed on the given container. All data generated during this process are to be stored in the device (local layer) and then transferred via data transmission to the central layer of the system made available to the Contracting Authority together with an indefinite licence within the tender price. Each nest should be equipped with a minimum of two CCTV system cameras, mounted on masts on the extreme modules, in order to increase the level of protection of the devices and to motivate residents to use the devices properly. The cameras should be directed towards each other and cover the area directly in front of the devices with their range. The image should be recorded on a digital storage medium inside the device. Lighting with a motion sensor should be mounted on each mast. Each of the modules that make up the entire nest should contain elements that are to fulfil the functions of metering the waste collected inside the container. The subject of the contract are mechanical devices in the form of metal modules with contactless opening and closing of flaps. Standardised plastic containers with a capacity of 1100 litres or 240 l are to be placed in the modules. Each module is to be equipped with access control via one-off QR codes for sticking onto the bag, and the measurement of waste mass is to take place in an automatic and legalised manner. The system is to enable the measurement of the filling level of waste collection containers and CCTV monitors, as well as a voice and light communication system and data transmission to the central layer of the system. The implemented solution is to allow the unambiguous assignment of the waste bag to the waste owner in accordance with the Act on maintaining cleanliness and order in municipalities. The modular shelter will be located on cadastral plot no. 5515/146, 4230/8 and will be intended for residents of the building at ul. M.C. Skłodowskiej in Leżajsk no. 5 and 9, 37-300 Leżajsk. A detailed description of the contract is included in clause 5.1. of the ToR for this procedure.; The subject of the intended project is the execution of 3 pcs. of freestanding waste shelters in which containers or bins for waste for selective waste collection at source will be placed, with access to the waste storage zone exclusively to authorised residents. The dimensions of a single shelter should be approximately 4,0 x 5,0 m. Bearing in mind that dimensions may differ between individual Manufacturers/Suppliers, a dimension discrepancy tolerance range of ±20% is accepted. Characteristic parameters: • In order to anchor the waste shelter, concrete foundation footings with dimensions of min. 30x30*110cm must be made for each load-bearing column. Surface hardening is to be made of concrete edgings of min. thickness 80 mm and paving blocks of minimum 80 mm, sand-cement sub-base layer of min. thickness 50 mm, mechanically stabilized crushed aggregate of min. thickness 250 mm. Hardening under the entire surface of the shelter + 150 mm on each side from the structure's dimension. A foundation slab over the entire surface of the shelter, reinforced with ribbed wire mesh min. Φ10mm with meshes of approximately 150x150mm, slab thickness min. 150mm, is alternatively permitted. • Total amount of hardstandings to be made for three locations (floor together with access paths) approx. 90 m2; • An appropriate hardened communication route should be provided (made) between the waste shelter and the road, e.g. paving blocks, in order to ensure the possibility of proper use by authorised residents and emptying of containers/bins of waste by cleaning services; • Embedding and installation of the structure (columns) via anchors and bolts; • Dimensions in plan view of a single shelter: 4,0 x 5,0 m ± 20%; • Load-bearing structure (columns): closed steel or aluminium profiles (protected against corrosion) min. 80 x 80 mm, wall thickness min. 2,0 mm; • Roof frame and upper transom (Horizontal structure): closed steel or aluminium profiles (protected against corrosion) min. 60 x 40 mm, wall thickness min. 2,0 mm;

• Structural infill and crossbar: steel or aluminium profiles (protected against corrosion) min. 30 x 30 mm or min. 40 x 20 mm, wall thickness min. 2,0 mm; • Roofing: coated trapezoidal sheet metal T14 / T18, thickness min. 0,5 mm; • Wall infills: coated sheet metal panels thickness 0,5–0,7 mm; • Gate/Door: single or double-leaf with a clear width of min. 1450 mm, filled with a coated sheet metal panel or mesh, opening to 180o; • Closure: lock with a cylinder insert, handle, number of keys min. 3 pcs. • Colours: main colour graphite / anthracite (e.g. RAL 7016), green inserts (e.g. RAL 6038) • Roof drainage: small gutter systems with a gutter diameter of min. 75 mm and downpipe diameter of min. 63 mm, plastic material; • A single shelter must accommodate min. 6 pcs. of containers 1100 l while maintaining a wide maneuvering alleyway in the middle with a width of approximately 1,8 m; • The offered shelters must be brand new, free from physical and legal defects. • Warranty: min. 24 months. A detailed description of the contract is located in clause 5.2. of the ToR for this procedure.; Technical parameters: • Depth: 35 cm ±10%; • Width: 150 cm ±10%; • Height: 115 cm ±10%; • Bins are to be colour-coded (light, contrasting colours) and labelled with a large, legible font; • Galvanised sheet metal, powder-coated in graphite/anthracite colour, thickness min. 1,0 mm – outdoor installation (weatherproof); • Possibility of permanent fixing to the substrate from underneath, e.g. with pins for paving blocks; • Internal metal containers with a capacity of min. 70 litres – one for each compartment; • Body (walls and top) solid – inlet openings from the front with a flap; • Door of each compartment with a key lock – universal key for all; • Number of keys min. 10 pcs.; • Structure based on closed profiles. • Four compartments for various waste adapted for selective collection at source: Compartment no. 1 – inscriptions and inlet colour - yellow "plastic and metals" Compartment no. 2 – inscriptions and inlet colour - blue "wastepaper or paper" Compartment no. 3 – inscriptions and inlet colour - green "glass" Compartment no. 4 – inscriptions and inlet colour - brown "bio" • Warranty: min. 24 months. • Delivery: ul. Podolszyny 1, 37-300 Leżajsk A detailed description of the contract is located in clause 5.3. of the ToR for this procedure.; Type of contract: delivery Quantity: 10 pcs. • Depth: 95 cm ±10%; • Width: 80 cm ±10%; • Height: 150 cm ±20%; • Chute with a width of min. 35 cm; • Waste compression up to 2 000 litres ± 20%; • Foot pedal opening the chute flap; • Module equipped with a standard two-wheeled container with a capacity of 240 litres; • Waste compaction mechanism; • Real-time fill level measurement with reporting to the system. • Real-time preview of device operation; • Solar-powered – built-in solar panels min. 45 W together with a battery min. 45 Ah; • Container made of aluminium or galvanised steel, protected against corrosion, powder-coated; • Within the tender price, the Contractor will grant a licence for access to software and/or an application for managing waste collected in the container with online access for the Contracting Authority (information on fill level, signalling the need for emptying, bin location on the map) under the terms and in accordance with the provisions of § 14 of Appendix no. 6 PPU to the ToR; • Maintenance of the System during the warranty period and free-of-charge indefinite use of it after the warranty period. The system is understood as cloud-based device operation software and an online access application; • Bins are to be colour-coded (light, contrasting colours) and labelled with a large, legible font – graphic design and inscriptions to be agreed with the Contracting Authority; • The offered device must be brand new, free from physical and legal defects and must not be a prototype. The Contracting Authority requires that the offered model comes from serial production and is available in the manufacturer's official sales channel as of the date of submission of tenders; • During the warranty period, the Contractor undertakes to provide an API in order to enable the connection/integration of the Contractor's System with software in the possession of the Contracting Authority; • Warranty min. 24 months; • Delivery: ul. Podolszyny 1, 37-300 Leżajsk; A detailed description of the subject of the contract is located in clause 5.4. of the ToR for this procedure.

sig_42fca57fd6d8e8939511.description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to negotiate and award a sole source, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC), CAGE Code 70974, of Melbourne, FL, for the procurement of supplies and services required for the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye (AHE) Block II retrofit program. This effort encompasses the procurement, storage, assembly, and delivery of up to one hundred (100) E-2D Block II retrofit kits; installation and modification services for up to eighty-three (83) fleet E-2D AHE aircraft; procurement of Long-Lead Material (LLM); non-recurring engineering (NRE) and integration support; Manufacturing Readiness Assessments (MRAs); First Article Inspections (FAIs); depot-level and in-service repair and maintenance services, including restoring Not Ready For Issue (NRFI) components to Ready For Issue (RFI) condition; Over and Above (O&A) work; sustaining engineering; and integrated logistics and supply support. Operational verification and checkouts shall be conducted utilizing U.S. Navy Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs), and post-modification Functional Check Flights (FCFs) shall be conducted in accordance with Naval Air Training and Operating Procedures Standardization (NATOPS) publications in support of the E-2/C-2 Airborne Command and Control Systems Program Office (PMA-231). A sole source acquisition will be procured under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, “Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.” Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye aircraft, including the Hawkeye Cockpit Tech Refresh (HECTR) and Theater Combat ID (TCID) Block II configurations developed under preceding development contract N00019-23-F-2625. NGSC is the only known qualified, responsible source that possesses the requisite technical expertise, manufacturing infrastructure, specialized tooling, and proprietary technical data and software source code required to fulfill these requirements without causing unacceptable operational delays to fleet Planned Maintenance Intervals (PMIs) and substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Northrop Grumman Corporation. Unless otherwise stated herein, no additional written information is available. Requests for the same will be disregarded.

sig_434af22b0a874e92ff8a.description: Cardiff University is undertaking early market engagement to inform the development of its upcoming procurement for Hard Facilities Management Services across a number of University buildings. The purpose of this engagement is to gather insights from experienced Hard FM providers regarding deliverability, cost drivers, risk allocation, supply chain capability, mobilisation requirements, and opportunities for innovation. Responses will inform the University’s final tender strategy, specification refinement, and commercial model. This stage does not formally commence a procurement process. Participation in this Pre market engagement is voluntary and will not provide any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent tender process. This requirement covers the provision of Hard Facilities Management (FM) services across five key Cardiff University buildings: the Translational Research Hub (TRH), sbarc|spark, ABACWS, the Centre for Student Life (CSL), and JOMEC at Two Central Square. Together, these facilities represent over 48,000 m2 of diverse teaching, research, innovation, and student‐facing environments. Four of the buildings are primarily academic teaching, study, and office spaces, incorporating lecture theatres, seminar rooms, social learning areas and administrative offices. The fifth building, the Translational Research Hub (TRH), is a complex scientific and industrial research environment incorporating cleanrooms, specialist gas distribution systems, abatement units, hazardous operational zones, and other highly serviced, business‐critical engineering systems. Core requirements include: • Planned Preventative Maintenance (OEM‐led, SFG20 and statutory). • Reactive Maintenance including 24/7/365 response where needed. • Remedial Maintenance addressing defects, failures or condition‐related issues identified through PPM or inspections to return assets to a safe and reliable operating condition and prevent further deterioration. • Asset management and lifecycle planning with data integration into the University’s CAFM system (QFM), • Management of access, safety, and permit‐to‐work controls • Management of specialist subcontractors supporting systems such as DI water, FFUs, gas detection, abatement, wet benches and BMS/Trend. • Delivery of Social Value outcomes will also form part of the scope. The University anticipates refining the scope, service levels, data requirements, performance metrics, and commercial structure following this Pre‐Market Engagement. Insights gained will inform the final tender documentation Lot 1: .
sig_434af22b0a874e92ff8a.title: Hard Facilities Management Services

sig_436fdff2fb7abb42e251.description: The Authority anticipates procuring a modern HR and Payroll solution, expected to be delivered as a cloud‐based Software as a Service (SaaS) platform, to replace its existing legacy system. The proposed solution will be required to support a full range of HR and Payroll functions including (but not limited to): core HR, payroll processing, recruitment and onboarding, absence management, case management, time and attendance, and comprehensive employee and manager self-service. The system must support the requirements of the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS), including CARE benefit calculations, pensionable pay rules, and LGPS‐compliant monthly and annual returns. The Authority currently delivers HR and payroll services for approximately 1,496 employees across three payrolls, generating around 1,452 payslips per month, and processes payroll for circa 400 elections staff on an intermittent basis. Of the three payrolls, two relate to limited companies, one of which currently has no employees paid through it but continues to require statutory returns. In light of forthcoming Local Government Reorganisation (LGR), future operational requirements may necessitate support for a significantly larger employee population and additional payrolls. Scalability, configurability and flexibility will therefore be key attributes of the intended solution. Lot 1: .
sig_436fdff2fb7abb42e251.title: HR&Payroll System

sig_438aaa1d5ef8fa313f2f.description: This pre-qualification concerns a tender regarding the procurement of a security management system (hereinafter SMS) for Danmarks Fængsler (hereinafter referred to as the Contracting Authority or Danmarks Fængsler). The Danish Prison and Probation Service thus wishes to procure a software-based IT system with digital integrations to existing and future security and fire-technical systems at Danmarks Fængsler's locations. Integrations must be made to, among other things, fire alarm systems (ABA), access control systems (ADK), intrusion alarm systems (AIA), lighting, cell call systems, assault alarms, perimeter surveillance, door telephony, TV surveillance (TVO), body cameras, etc. The delivery also includes all necessary services in connection with the purchases, including implementation of a new central operating model in the Agency for Danmarks Fængsler and, in extension thereof, operational support (3 level support), implementation of the SMS at the sites, and everything that a purchase entails, including, among other things, setup, programming, installations, integration of the location's security and fire-technical systems and the individual units, as well as tests. The contract period will have a duration of 8 years with the possibility of extension up to 2 times of 24 months. Any extension of the contract will be on unchanged terms. It is the Contracting Authority that decides whether the contract is to be extended or not, and this will be done with a notice of 6 months. In addition, the Supplier is obliged to provide maintenance, support, licences, operational support, etc., for up to 7 years after a site has purchased the Solution. This is to ensure that an SMS purchased, for example, in the year 10 during the contract term, similarly has the possibility of having a well-functioning SMS for the subsequent 7 years from the implementation of the SMS at the site in question. As regards licences, this will be an indefinite right of use, with the possibility of termination. K02 forms the contractual basis for the agreement. The contract concerns the purchase of SMS for all types of sites and locations at Danmarks Fængsler. Furthermore, the contract will also be used in connection with construction and civil engineering projects, e.g., the new prison in Viborg Municipality and the new remand centre in Slagelse – both with an expected capacity of approximately 400 inmates each. The locations will purchase SMS as the need arises during the contract period. The Contracting Authority expects that all prisons and remand centres will need to purchase a new SMS during the contract period, and that the rollout will primarily take place in the years 2027-2033. However, the Supplier is not guaranteed a minimum turnover during the contract period. Reference is made to Danmarks Fængsler's website for an updated overview of all sites. All employees of the future supplier who are to have access to the Contracting Authority's locations, or who are to advise the Contracting Authority either directly or by processing written materials, including drawing materials, must be security-cleared by the Contracting Authority and must sign a confidentiality agreement. The security clearance will either be a criminal record check or a declaration that they agree to information about the person in question being obtained from the Danish Security and Intelligence Service – including information in the police's registers and the intelligence service's own registers. In that case, the security clearance is expected to be at the level “secret“. The level of the security clearance will be a concrete assessment in relation to the degree of sensitive information that the person in question will gain insight into. Furthermore, it is noted that it is forbidden to bring mobile phones and PCs inside the walls when performing tasks at Danmarks Fængsler's locations. The individual locations may grant a dispensation if it is strictly necessary in relation to the performance of the task.
sig_438aaa1d5ef8fa313f2f.title: EU-udbud vedr. Security Management System

sig_438f98c98122402d78c3.description: Lapin hyvinvointialue requests tenders for an entity including: 1. safety devices provided at home for Lapin hyvinvointialueen customers 2. alarm reception service 3. alarm reception system for producing the aforementioned service as the wellbeing services county's own operations. In the procurement, safety devices refer to various safety devices provided at home that can improve the safety of a customer living at home. The safety devices to be procured are safety phones and their accessories, a positioning safety bracelet, and a solution for door monitoring in communal living. Alarm reception service refers to a service in which alarms coming through safety devices are received, an initial assessment of the need for help is made, and the request is forwarded to safety assistants. The service must operate around the clock every day of the year. Alarm reception system refers to a system by which the subscriber can receive alarms from various safety devices and forward them as tasks to safety assistants. Lapin hyvinvointialue intends to take over the alarm reception service as its own operation according to the preliminary schedule in the spring of 2028. The wellbeing services county shall procure the alarm reception service until the reception system has been commissioned, after which the procurement of the reception service will end. The subject of procurement is described in more detail in the invitation to tender and its attachments, in particular in attachment 1 "Description of the subject of procurement". One supplier is selected as the framework agreement supplier in the tendering process. Through the framework arrangement, the wellbeing services county shall procure safety devices and services from the selected supplier during the contract period as needed. The needs of the wellbeing services county may vary during the contract period, and the invitation to tender does not commit to specific procurement quantities. The contract period of the framework agreement is a fixed term of two years, after which the agreement will continue until further notice. In addition, the alarm reception system as a whole will be procured from the selected supplier, which includes the delivery of the system and its ongoing service. The agreement for the ongoing service of the system is valid until further notice. The procurement has not been divided into lots because it is a unified entity consisting of goods and services, the compatibility of all parts of which must be ensured. From the perspective of the safety of Lapin hyvinvointialueen customers, it is important that a single supplier is responsible for the functionality of the entire entity. The contract notice has been republished because the previous procurement procedure had to be suspended due to the need to amend the procurement documents.
sig_438f98c98122402d78c3.title: Safety devices provided to the home, alarm reception service and alarm reception system

sig_43911e276513362118ad.description: Innlandet county shall procure a tool for sample preparation and implementation of teaching. The introduction of artificial intelligence has created a need for tests where students' access to aids can be limited. The development has also led to a need to be able to carry out training situations without access to the internet, artificial intelligence (KI) or language models (LLM). The contracting authority is concerned about future changes in the availability of artificial intelligence. In particular, local variants on hardware without connecting to the internet (Edge AI) can create challenges for carrying out samples themselves with sample tools. It is important that the sample tool is able to meet such challenges in order to achieve the objective of the contract. We are looking for a tool that offers improved functionality compared to Forms. The tool shall be integrated with Teams and provide an option to limit the pupils ́ access to assistive aids during tests. It should also help students focus and be used to train perseverance and concentration without distractions. The tool must also be connected to the Tasks module in Teams, so that assessments can be provided in one overall location. It shall be possible to use all training in sixth form education in Innlandet county. This tool shall not be used as an exam system, as Innlandet county has another system for this. Innlandet county currently has 11,500 pupils and 2,000 participants in the adult education. All shall use the tool from a snare. We would like a service provider who fulfils the requirements for privacy and information security in a satisfactory manner and who can offer a flexible system with a user friendly interface.

sig_439150125d0b7b93c9a1.description: The Boosting Innovative GEOINT-Science and Technology (BIG-ST) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) invites proposers to submit innovative concepts to address hard GEOINT problems that align to one or more of the following technical domains: (1) Foundational GEOINT, (2) Advanced Phenomenologies, and (3) Analytic Technologies. BAA Process and Topic Call Publication: The BIG-ST BAA is a general announcement of NGA’s research interest, including criteria for selecting proposals and soliciting the participation of all offerors capable of satisfying the Government’s needs. The requests for abstracts and proposals are transmitted via Topic Calls that are published separately under the BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation at various times during the open period of the General Solicitation. Topic Calls will be published via updates to the BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation site on Sam.gov, Grants.gov, and/or the Classified IC-Acquisition Research Center (https://acq-ui.ace.proj.nro.ic.gov). For Classified Topic Calls, interested parties must have an account to log into the Classified IC-ARC to see the notice, and all associated RFP documents. For additional support with account access, please contact the Classified ACE Help Desk at 855-4ACE. Interested parties should periodically check these websites for updates. No submissions shall be accepted to the General Solicitation; abstracts and proposals will only be reviewed in response to open Topic Calls. Please refer to the Topic Calls for Abstract and Proposal due dates. The BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation, HM047623BAA0001 Revision 3 (dated 04/25/2025), is posted and applies to Topic 5 and forward. See Attachments/Links. Closed Topics: Topic 1 - Geospatial-Intelligence Foundational Model (GFM) is closed Topic 2 - Magnifying University Science Expertise (MUSE) is closed. Topic 3 - VLBI+G Signal Chain Development (VLBI+G) is closed. Topic 5 - Better Ingested GEOINT - Identifying Artificial Intelligence and Manually Manipulated Media (BIGISLAND) is closed. Canceled Topics: Topic 4 - Production of Radio Frequency (RF) Surveys from Commercial On-orbit Passive RF (RF-COP) is canceled. Active Topics: Topic 6 – Magnifying University Science Expertise 2 (MUSE 2) is open. Topic is open to Grant Applicants only. Go to Grants.gov for details.

sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.description: Provision, implementation and operation of a cloud-based, SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud) of the Stadtwerke Düsseldorf AG including affiliated companies. The aim of the procurement is to create transparency regarding data stocks, access authorizations and security-relevant activities, as well as to support measures to increase information security and comply with regulatory requirements in the KRITIS environment. In addition to the provision of the platform, the service also includes supportive services for the analysis, evaluation and prioritisation of security-relevant events as well as for the derivation of suitable measures. The processing of all data shall take place exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR. An uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations must be ensured. The aim is to conclude a contract for the provision, implementation and operation of a scalable, cloud-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud). The solution must cover the following functions and services in particular: - Analysis and evaluation of data stocks, data access and permission structures, including the identification of potential security and data protection risks, - The solution should have integrated functions for detecting anomalies in user and system behaviour (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) - Creation of transparency regarding effective accesses and permissions, - Detection and evaluation of conspicuous, risk-prone or security-relevant activities, - Provision of monitoring, reporting and verification functions to support audit, compliance and security requirements, particularly in the regulated KRITIS environment, - Support in deriving and implementing suitable measures for risk reduction (e.g. adjustment of permissions or restriction of access rights), - Integration into the client's existing hybrid system landscape (in particular identity services, file and cloud storage as well as collaboration platforms) via standardised interfaces, - Provision and operation of the solution including maintenance, ongoing development, updates and technical documentation in a SaaS model. In addition, services are to be provided that support continuous evaluation, assessment and prioritisation (managed detection and response) of security-relevant events and provide recommendations for action. If configured accordingly, these services may also include operational support services. Continued operation requirements: - Ensuring an uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations, including a suitable migration and transition concept, - Taking over existing configurations, evaluations and settings as far as technically possible, - Guaranteeing compatibility with existing system landscapes, role and permission models, - Minimising migration, integration and training efforts while taking cost-effectiveness over the entire life cycle into account, - Ensuring continuous operational capability during the transition phase. All services relating to the client's data or metadata must be provided exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR.
sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.title: Provision and operation of a SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions

sig_43f8f851007d72d560ef.description: The purpose of this procurement is to achieve the objectives established through the approved funding application of the project ROHU00097, in particular the consolidation of disaster preparedness and management capacities through the procurement and provision of specialised hardware and software applications (VR training simulators). The virtual reality training system is necessary for conducting training stages that simulate interventions in various scenarios and operational conditions, contributing to the development of techniques, tactics and procedures specific to firefighting intervention. Each set is composed of: Software component comprising a) the training software application, 1 application / set, 4 applications in total, delivered as a perpetual licence for the provided version and a package of updates and dedicated technical support for a period of 36 months from the moment of final acceptance; Hardware component, delivered in full with a minimum guarantee of 24 months, comprising b) Portable central unit – 1 pcs / set, total 4 pieces c) Network component (integrated router) - 1 pcs / set, total 4 pieces d) Standalone VR headsets – 6 pieces / set, total 24 pieces e) Firefighting training nozzle – 2 pieces / set, total 8 pieces f) High-performance mobile workstation for analysis and processing – 1 piece / set, 4 pcs in total. The virtual reality training system is necessary for conducting training stages that simulate interventions in various scenarios and operational conditions, contributing to the development of techniques, tactics and procedures specific to firefighting intervention. Through the included hardware equipment and software applications, a realistic and highly interactive simulation environment is created, which enables training in predefined scenarios such as: residential buildings, rural areas, airports, motorways, high-rise buildings, etc. These support the safe practice of specific techniques (such as the letter technique) and familiarisation with actual fire dynamics. The system will enable training in multiple scenarios for first responders. These scenarios will include the following competencies: Communication, Reconnaissance 360°, Firefighting techniques, First aid procedures and Hazardous materials (such as lithium ions and solar panels). The system must enable multidisciplinary training scenarios in which firefighters, paramedics and police officers can work together in the same scenario. The system enables the dynamic presentation of essential elements related to fire development and behaviour, as well as the impact of the firefighting tactics used. Without compromising the physical safety of participants, users can learn to recognise hazards and make operational decisions in real time. The system involves no occupational health and safety risks, eliminating the possibility of accidents, exposure to toxic gases or carcinogenic substances. Thus, firefighters can train intensively and repeatedly, without physical consequences, at any stage of their professional training. The training platform will offer the possibility of unlimited repetition of exercises, ensuring the complete acquisition of the competencies and skills required for intervention. At the same time, the training contributes to risk awareness and strategic learning, adapted to individual needs. Each set is composed of: Software component comprising a) the training software application, 1 application / set, 4 applications in total, delivered as a perpetual licence for the provided version and a package of updates and dedicated technical support for a period of 36 months from the moment of final acceptance; Hardware component, delivered in full with a minimum guarantee of 24 months, comprising b) Portable central unit – 1 pcs / set, total 4 pieces c) Network component (integrated router) - 1 pcs / set, total 4 pieces d) Standalone VR headsets – 6 pieces / set, total 24 pieces e) Firefighting training nozzle – 2 pieces / set, total 8 pieces f) High-performance mobile workstation for analysis and processing – 1 piece / set, 4 pcs in total.
sig_43f8f851007d72d560ef.title: VIRTUAL REALITY TRAINING SYSTEM ( 4 UNITS, COMPLETE SETS)

sig_44051c4bbe1dfce6f50c.description: The subject of the procurement is a social welfare client data system as an on-premise solution, including the system application, necessary usage rights, the form functionalities of the electronic social services customer portal, support for implementing user onboarding, integration implementations regarding ATJ, reporting and information management functionalities, application support and maintenance for the contract period, and other expert services. The procured social welfare client data system must also comprehensively support, among other things, the lawful processing and invoicing of client and patient data. For a social welfare professional, the client data system is one of the most important working tools, so it must be of a high standard of usability, support professionals in carrying out their work tasks, and enable smooth communication and data flow between actors. The usability, interoperability, and data utilization of social welfare and healthcare information systems has been a strategic objective of governments for several years. In electronic transactions, the Contracting Authority uses an electronic transaction platform that brings together Customers' electronic transactions in one place on a "one stop shop" principle for the Customer. The purpose of the electronic transaction portion that is the subject of this procurement is to complement the services of the contracting authority's electronic transaction platform in accordance with the requirements described in the requirements specification. The binding objective of the procurement of the social welfare client data system is that the wellbeing services county has 1.1.2027 or at the latest six months from the signing of the contract a system in use that fulfils the functional needs as described in this document and the requirements specification document. Options The procurement includes the possibility to order functional, technical, and service coverage extensions during the service usage period according to the Contracting Authority's needs. The procurement requests the following to be offered as options: • Additional training days • Archiving • Extended 24/7 support for the social welfare client data system The Supplier may also offer other options with the price attachment (attachment 8), which are not included in the price comparison of the procurement. The performance of client data conversion and migration is excluded from the procurement. The Supplier must participate in the conversion and migration, for example regarding the review and reading in of data contents, but otherwise the contracting unit is responsible for all conversion and migration work. Kanta archives of old client data as well as locally stored archiving packages remaining outside Kanta will be planned and prioritized in separate archiving projects. One comprehensive supplier will be selected for the procurement. The supplier selected from those that have met the requirements will be the tenderer that has submitted the most economically advantageous and accepted tender. The contract period is fixed-term for 48 months, continuing thereafter until further notice. The aim is to provisionally start the contract period in the autumn of 2026, as soon as the procurement decision has attained legal force.
sig_44051c4bbe1dfce6f50c.title: Customer information system implementing social services legislation

sig_44160aacf2c87da6ae79.description: United Utilities is seeking to establish a framework for the supply, storage, stock management, fulfilment and delivery of water efficiency devices and flow regulators. The framework will support United Utilities’ AMP8 and AMP9 water demand reduction commitments, including reductions in domestic Per Capita Consumption and non-household business demand. The requirement is divided into two lots: Lot 1 covers water efficiency devices, associated fulfilment services and a UU-branded customer water usage survey and ordering platform; Lot 2 covers flow regulators in agreed sizes, flow rates and specifications. Appointed supplier(s) must be able to provide compliant, reliable and scalable products and services that support planned programmes, customer campaigns, bulk orders and changes in operational demand. Suppliers must demonstrate product quality, regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, accurate reporting, effective stock management and appropriate customer support. This includes relevant approvals and assurance evidence, secure handling of customer data where applicable, and the ability to respond flexibly as programme volumes and priorities evolve. The overall objective is to secure a robust, value-for-money supply arrangement that enables United Utilities to deliver water efficiency activity at scale, maintain continuity of supply, protect customer experience and contribute to measurable reductions in water consumption across the North West. Lot LOT-0001: PRO005128-Goods-Framework-Water Saving Devices - Lot 1. Supply, storage, stock management, picking, packing, fulfilment and delivery of water efficiency devices such as flow regulators, water butts, shower regulators, tap inserts, showerheads, cistern devices, toilet leak detection strips and other approved or innovative water saving products. Lot LOT-0002: PRO005128-Goods-Framework-Water Saving Devices - Lot 2. Supply, storage, stock management, fulfilment and delivery of flow regulators in a range of sizes, flow rates and specifications suitable for UU programmes. sig_44388e2ff5289b808d9f.description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
sig_44388e2ff5289b808d9f.title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire
