Procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement 3 in parts for Visit Hungary Nemzeti Turisztikai Szervezet Közhasznú Nonprofit Zrt. for the performance of strategic media agency, digital media agency and market research tasks. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. The aim of the Contracting Authority's communication activity is to promote Hungary for tourism purposes, strengthen inbound tourism from abroad, stimulate domestic tourism, and present the Hungarian tourism offering domestically and internationally. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform the tasks specified in the Technical Specification for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of strategic media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 3.200.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different media mix and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform strategic media agency, media planning, media buying, campaign management, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to media appearances for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The exact professional content, performance deadline, quantity, technical parameters and individual expectations of the tasks are contained in the individual orders. The Contracting Authority's domestic campaigns are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 250 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 6–8 weeks. Campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 80 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–10 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation of a media strategy, integrated media mix and media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups and channels, - strategic media agency tasks on specified channels - preparation, execution and monitoring of campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - proposal for a KPI system adapted to the nature, objective, channels and target markets of the given campaign, as well as tracking, interpretation and evaluation of campaign performance, with special regard to tourism KPIs - preparation of regular, inter-campaign and campaign-closing reports according to an agreed reporting structure. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.; The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of digital media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 820.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and digital media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism digital advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different digital media mix, targeting logic, platform usage and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform digital media agency, digital media planning, digital media buying, campaign management, optimisation, measurement, analytics, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to digital media appearances for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. The Contracting Authority's domestic digital campaigns are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Digital campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - formulation of a digital campaign strategy and digital media plan, development of digital targeting, platform and channel proposals, - performance of digital media buying and campaign management tasks, continuous tracking and optimisation of campaign performance, support for measurement and analytical settings, - evaluation and reporting of digital KPIs, (with special regard to tourism relevance) - support for the compilation of performance certification documentation, - preparation of a digital campaign strategy, digital media mix and digital media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, digital media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups, digital channels and advertising platforms, - performance of media agency tasks on specified channels and platforms, - preparation of digital campaigns, - launching of digital campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of digital media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - establishment, management and operation of an agreed advertising account structure, - support for the establishment, operation and, where necessary, development of the measurement environment related to digital campaigns, - preparation of inter-campaign reports and campaign-closing evaluation. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.;

The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of market research tasks up to a net framework amount of 320.000.000 HUF. The CA undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the CA plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. Research and analysis tasks may also cover domestic and international target markets, different target groups, campaigns, brands, destinations, communication objectives, consumer motivations, media usage characteristics, tourism decisions or campaign effectiveness issues. The CA's research projects are of a mixed nature: they include quantitative research with larger sample sizes directed at Hungary and affecting target markets outside Hungary, primary research affecting multiple target markets, as well as smaller-element qualitative, motivational, service quality, mystery shopping or other decision-supporting research tasks. The Contracting Authority generally performs the implementation of a residential quantitative research of 1000 persons once a year in 10-15 countries, and in addition initiates a minimum of 2 qualitative, small-group focus group researches in Hungary (focus groups are generally implemented with 4–8 groups, with an average participation of 6 persons per group) and manages a nationwide mystery shopping annually with a minimum of 80 trial purchases. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform market research, data acquisition, analysis and decision-supporting tasks for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation, organisation, execution, analysis and documentation of research, data acquisitions, analyses and decision-supporting materials founding, supporting or evaluating marketing and communication activity. - preparation of a research plan or methodological proposal adapted to the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task, - organisation, execution, coordination and control of research data recording, fieldwork or data collection. - processing, checking, cleaning, systematisation, analysis, interpretation of data available as a result of research or data acquisition, and formulation of decision-supporting conclusions, - with the prior approval of the CA, may carry out data purchases, procure syndicated research, or utilise an external data source or study on behalf of the CA, - performing administration related to possible research modifications, data recording changes, cancellations, data purchase or syndicated research limitations, - the Winning Tenderer is obliged to present the results of the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task according to a structure agreed with the Client. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.

sig_4484f6587dadb84a0572.description: Sund & Bælt uses Maximo Application Suite (MAS) as its Enterprise Asset Management system. Sund & Bælt's activities comprise the construction, operation and maintenance of some of the world's largest bridges and tunnels, including the Great Belt Fixed Link, the Øresund Fixed Link and the upcoming Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link. In addition, Sund & Bælt owns four ferry ports north and south of the Great Belt Fixed Link, and Sund & Bælt ensures that they are maintained and operated. The ports are Odden, Ebeltoft, Spodsbjerg and Tårs ports. The supplier shall handle the operation, upgrading, development, maintenance and servicing of Sund & Bælt's MAXIMO maintenance system and associated integrations, as described in further detail in Annex 1. In addition, the supplier shall provide sparring with the Customer regarding opportunities, analyses and the commissioning of new functionality and/or optimisations in business processes; this also includes providing input into business cases and supporting the safeguarding of described benefits. The Customer has initiated initiatives to achieve a higher degree of condition-based monitoring, and continuously works to explore opportunities and commission new modules in MAS. In addition, the Customer is expanding its portfolio of infrastructure assets, where even greater focus is placed on digital twins and the digitalisation of analogue workflows, which must also be capable of being utilised and supported by MAS. MAXIMO is run in the Azure Cloud on a Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform pursuant to the design specified by IBM. The solution is based on MAXIMO standard functionality with customizations as well as integrations into a GIS system, reporting system, financial system, etc. In addition, this involves the use of the Manage, Mobile, Spatial modules and, expectedly, also 3D/BIM, Monitor and Defect Management in the near future. The framework agreement is non-exclusive, and the Customer is thus entitled – but not obliged – to use the supplier. The supplier is obliged to provide the services covered by the framework agreement. The Customer does not commit to purchasing any specific volume of the services covered by the framework agreement.
sig_4484f6587dadb84a0572.title: Framework agreement on operation and maintenance of the MAXIMO maintenance system

sig_44898e5cf5b4086cb308.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system regarding the procurement of IT consultancy services within 14 service areas with associated sub-areas, sub-categories and services. Below are the 14 service areas with associated sub-areas indicated. The actual services that can be procured in the 14 service areas are described in detail in Appendix C. Subject of the system: Service area 1: IT-related strategies Sub-area: Preparation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Implementation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Evaluation and updating as well as impact assessment of strategies Service area 2: Business needs, business case and benefit realisation Sub-area: Identification of business needs and preparation of business cases Sub-area: Realisation of business cases Sub-area: Follow-up on business cases Service area 3: IT tendering Sub-area: Preparation of tenders Sub-area: Execution of tenders Service area 4: IT security, business continuity and IT compliance Sub-area: Establishment of IT security Sub-area: Crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery Sub-area: IT compliance Service area 5: IT architecture Sub-area: Establishment of an IT architecture Sub-area: Review and adjustment of existing IT architecture Service area 6: IT governance Sub-area: Establishment of IT governance Sub-area: Organisation of system management Sub-area: Establishment of IT supplier management Service area 7: Project and programme management Sub-area: Project management – the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Management of agile projects Sub-area: Programme management Service area 8: Data processing Sub-area: Data analysis and reporting Sub-area: Use of external data Sub-area: Conversion, cleaning and archiving of data Service area 9: Advice on software licences Sub-area: Open source software vs. closed source software Sub-area: Determination of the size of specific licences, as well as the conditions associated with the use Service area 10: Infrastructure and hardware Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of networks Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of servers Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of clients Service area 11: Test Sub-area: IT testing of development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT testing Service area 12: Development of new functionality Sub-area: IT development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT development Service area 13: Adaptation of existing IT systems Sub-area: IT development with a view to adapting existing IT systems Service area 14: IT system operation Sub-area: Operation of IT systems The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase The same services can be procured in both categories, but the categories differ in that the customer in category 1 must procure one or more specific competence(s), while the customer in category 2 must have a specific task solved. The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. It is voluntary for all SKI's customers, as stated in Appendix B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure IT consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase In category 1 customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in 2 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate).; Procurement of IT consultancy services for task solution In category 2 the customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in 3 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of IT consultancy services for the solution of the described task (number x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate). 3. Remuneration form 3: Purchase of task solution at a fixed price.

sig_44927bea86389180d737.buyer_original: Hosting des ERP-Systems Schleupen.CS der Stadtwerke Hilden GmbH
sig_44927bea86389180d737.description: The tender aims to achieve and promote the stable and future-proof operation of the "Schleupen.CS" ERP system on a highly available and secure infrastructure for use by the client's employees and external service providers, including migration, SaaS operation, interfaces, administration, and support. The SWH is tendering for the provision of a highly available cloud infrastructure in the contractor's data centre. The service consists not only of providing data centre capacity but, due to the intended role as a solution provider, encompasses holistic responsibility for the stable and future-proof operation of Schleupen.CS. The services to be provided include, in particular: - the provision of the necessary hardware and data centre infrastructure, - the provision of software necessary for the operation of the systems (including current versions of Microsoft Windows Server, Microsoft SQL Server, Remote Desktop Services, and Citrix if applicable for the publication of remote apps, as approved by Schleupen SE), - the takeover or migration of the existing system (including the sub-systems necessary for operation) into the data centre environment, - the takeover of existing interfaces to third-party service providers (mandatory requirements: SMGWA, ticket system, customer portal), - the operation of the Schleupen.CS system (including sub-systems) in the data centre: production and test systems with the existing tenants, - the sufficiently performant - at least with symmetrical 200 Mbit/s - internet connection of the client to the contractor's data centre. Connection must be established via an encrypted VPN tunnel or by providing the service provider's own hardware, which is integrated into the contractor's internal network, - the takeover of support services within the scope of data centre operations, - the takeover of support services for the Schleupen.CS system, in particular holistic, independent communication with Schleupen SE in the event of application and problem cases, - the provision and maintenance of current hardware and software (operating system software, database software, application software), which are operated with active maintenance contracts / software assurance, - the monitoring of systems and applications, - immediate error detection, communication to the client in the event of an error, and error rectification, - the maintenance of highly available system operation (24 h/ 7 days a week) throughout the entire contract term. It is mandatory that strict, logical isolation from the contractor's other customers is maintained. The precise details regarding the subject matter of the contract can be found in the specifications (Annex B of the procedural letter).

sig_44a5edc90074deb6f12b.description: The Council of Europe’s Group of States against Corruption (GRECO) regularly produces statistical, analytical and visual information related to its monitoring activities, including the implementation of GRECO recommendations by its member States, trends identified through evaluation and compliance procedures and other activities falling within its mandate. In that context, the Organisation is seeking up to 8 (eight) providers for the provision of consultancy services in statistical analysis, data processing, data verification, data visualisation and institutional reporting relating to GRECO’s monitoring activities, to be requested on an as-needed basis, in compliance with the ordering procedure defined in the Framework Contract. Similar services may also be required for analysing data pertaining to cooperation activities in the area of fight against economic crime. The deadline for submission of tenders is 30 September 2026 at 23:59 (Strasbourg/CET time). Link to tender : https://www.coe.int/en/web/greco/-/call-for-tender-intellectual-services-for-the-preparation-processing-analysis-reporting-and-visualisation-of-greco-monitoring-data .

sig_44d0899b6a9c46e76e02.description: Pääkaupunkiseudun Kaupunkiliikenne Oy organised a tender procedure on behalf of RV Kalusto ja Varikko Oy for the procurement of new stop display screens for MLNRV3 (Artic X34) trams. The series size is 70 trams. A total of 385 displays were to be procured, of which 350 units were to be installed in the trams and 35 units as spare devices. The subject of the procurement was the stop display screens for MLNRV3 (Artic X34) trams. The procurement included only the delivery of stop display screens. One tram has five (5) stop displays. The estimated delivery times for the stop displays were scheduled for 2027–2028. The supplier was required to be able to deliver displays that meet the mandatory minimum requirements set in the technical appendix (Appendix 3). The contracting entity identified the following error in the invitation to tender, which could not be corrected without discontinuing the procurement and publishing a new contract notice. The invitation to tender and its appendices did not set requirements for system information security or the management of software updates. The aforementioned requirements were central from the perspective of the subject matter of the procurement, and they should have been included as minimum requirements of the procurement in the invitation to tender. The addition of the requirements would have been a substantial modification to the procurement, so the error could not be corrected with a corrigendum notice. With reference to the above, the contracting entity has a genuine and justified reason within the meaning of the legislation for discontinuing the procurement. The decision therefore does not have a discriminatory effect on tenderers. The procurement procedure will be restarted later from the beginning by publishing a new contract notice concerning it in the Hilma notification channel and in the TED service. The Helsinki Metropolitan Area Transport Company organized a tender procedure on behalf of RV Kalusto ja Varikko Oy of the procurement of the new stop display screens for MLNRV3 (Artic X34) trams. The total fleet consists of 70 trams. Total of 385 displays were to be procured, of which 350 units were to be installed in the trams and 35 units as spare devices. The subject of the procurement was the stop display screens for MLNRV3 (Artic X34) trams. The procurement included only the supply of the stop display screens. Each tram is equipped with a total of five (5) stop displays. The estimated delivery dates were between 2027-2028. The supplier was required to be capable of delivering displays that comply with the mandatory minimum requirements specified in the technical appendix (Appendix 3). The contracting entity identified the following error in the invitation to tender, which could not be corrected without discontinuing the procurement procedure and publishing a new contract notice. The invitation to tender and its appendices did not include requirements relating to system cybersecurity or software update management. These requirements were essential from the perspective of the subject matter of the procurement and should have been included as minimum requirements in the invitation to tender. Adding such requirements would have constituted a material modification to the procurement and therefore the error could not be corrected by means of a corrigendum notice. With reference to the above, the contracting authority has a justified reason within the meaning of the legislation to interrupt the procurement. The decision therefore does not have a discriminatory effect on tenderers. The procurement procedure will be restarted at a later stage from the beginning by publishing a new procurement notice concerning it in the Hilma notification channel and in the TED service.

The network will provide a wealth of data for monitoring and better understanding the geodynamic phenomena taking place in the wider area of the south-eastern Mediterranean Multi-parametric reference seismological stations and infrasound sensors; Wireless seismic array of 30 elements; Ocean Bottom Seismometers (OBS); Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) technology measurement system and Distributed Strain Sensing and Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DSS/DAS) technology strain measurement system; Local seismicity monitoring system with an array of 10 elements; Magnetic field measurement system and gravity acceleration measurement system; Geochemical measurement station for soil emissions of carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide gases; Portable biogas analyser; Tide gauges; Vertical array of accelerographs in boreholes; Heavy-duty diamond drilling system; Motor vehicle; Radon gas emission measurement systems

sig_44d830b444d6a9ed8fb8.description: The subject of the public contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of a complex interactive projection system for shooting training intended for the training of security forces and other authorised users. The system must form one functional unit enabling the implementation of shooting training using both live weapons and weapons with laser shooting simulation. The system includes, in particular, projection technology, hit detection equipment, control and evaluation software, audiovisual and communication equipment, as well as all related technical and safety elements necessary for operation in a shooting range environment. The system must allow for the projection of static and dynamic shooting scenarios, real-time hit evaluation, archiving and subsequent analysis of shooting progress, and support for the creation and editing of custom training scenarios by the user. The supply also includes complete integration into the shooting range space, including installation, calibration and commissioning of all components, the supply of necessary hardware and software equipment, the provision of safety measures and protection of technologies against the effects of shooting, as well as the supply of related accessories for the implementation of training. The supply also includes training and maintenance of the system for a period of three (5) years. sig_4509eab3492484568101.description: This project seeks to deliver a Digital Traffic Enforcement System (DTES) Replacement Solution that will support the following potential objectives. Suppliers who express interest are asked to consider the following: Objective 1: Gauge supplier knowledge on potential routes to market and possible frameworks to carry out the procurement. Objective 2: Seek feedback on how TfL can ensure continuity of Traffic Order Enforcement on the TfL Road Network (TLRN) with no loss of enforcement capability during transition or following implementation of the replacement solution. Objective 3: Seek feedback on how TfL can deliver a more efficient and cost-effective solution with lower maintenance costs compared to current delivery solution. Objective 4:Seek feedback on how TfL can deliver a solution with a more simplified architecture to future proof technology and ensure compliance with relevant regulatory authorities. Objective 5: Seek feedback on how TfL can provide a solution which continues to be satisfactory by end users and enables effective use of enforcement resources i.e. issuing PCNs effectively and efficiently. Objective 6: Seek feedback on how TfL can ensure that all internal and external systems are integrated for effective delivery. Objective 7: Seek feedback on how TfL can enhance quality of current system and bring video quality up to market standards to increase likelihood of number plate capture and consistency of evidence packs. Objective 8: Seek feedback on how TfL can successful decommissioning of current DTES solution following migration and ensuring all necessary information required for business continuity is successfully migrated and accessible within the replacement solution. Objective 9: Seek feedback on the market’s indication of cost and time implications of delivering the works. I.E OPEX Costs, Licencing, maintenance. Lot 1: .

sig_45182218dce81071619d.description: The objective of the request is to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the preliminary subject of which is the security technologies and related services required for the implementation of technical information security and compliance. The DPS to be established would enable, among other things, the procurement of the following solutions, technologies and services as needed: - Security event management, analytics and response automation. Examples include SIEM, SOAR and other similar solutions, security alert enrichment, correlation, prioritisation, workflow automation, hyperautomation and AI agent-based automation. - Analytics and artificial intelligence solutions to support security monitoring and response. Examples include AI/ML-based solutions to support SOC operations, improving analyst efficiency, automation of threat hunting, and supporting anomaly detection and investigation. - Threat intelligence management and utilisation in security monitoring and response. Examples include the management, combination, automation, analysis and utilisation of threat intelligence collected from public, open, commercial and other sources in anomaly forecasting, enrichment and decision-making, including Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) solutions. - Asset management for security monitoring needs. Examples include solutions that create and maintain up-to-date and unified visibility into environments containing IT, OT, IoT and medical devices, including devices, software, software versions, dependencies, integrations with existing asset management solutions, and the utilisation of SBOM data. - Third-party and supply chain risk management. Examples include automated solutions supporting supplier information security risk assessment, continuous monitoring and software supply chain risk management. - Network traffic security event detection and response. Examples include Network Detection and Response (NDR) and other similar solutions for analysing network traffic, identifying anomalies and supporting automated or guided response. - Safe utilisation of artificial intelligence and usage monitoring. Examples include solutions for managing, monitoring and protecting the use of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and AI agents in the organisation, as well as the risks associated with their use. - A system/solution intended for the handling of security incidents (case management), into which all data related to incident handling, such as memory dumps, log data, actions taken, evidence, etc., can be collected securely as part of the DFIR process. - SandBox tools for malware investigation and operational analysis. In addition, probable general requirements/boundary conditions concerning all potential procurement packages are: - Solutions should in principle support a multi-tenant model or otherwise be suitable for a multi-tenant environment. - Solutions should in principle be integrable with security event management and response automation solutions (e.g. SOAR) as well as log management solutions, and support the large-scale utilisation of artificial intelligence. - Procurements to be implemented may include, inter alia, the following: consulting, maintenance, development, deployment, integration and expert services. - Istekki may procure technologies for its own use, exclusively for customers' use, or for the use of both Istekki and customers. The objective is for the establishment phase of the dynamic purchasing system to commence in May-June 2026. Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereinafter referred to as the notice), and this notice does not yet constitute a request to participate. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. REGISTRATION. Companies interested in this dynamic purchasing system (DPS) are requested to register for the market dialogue by email at: hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 17.4.2026 (with the subject "Tietoturvapalveluiden DPS"). The personal data of registered persons will be used solely for contacts related to the preparation of this dynamic purchasing system. MARKET DIALOGUE. Draft material related to the dynamic purchasing system under preparation will be sent to registered companies for comments, in a so-called market dialogue, during an estimated period of 05/2026. Registered companies will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing. The market dialogue and materials will be in Finnish. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not preclude participation in a potential procurement procedure.

No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Purpose NIH is seeking information from qualified R&D firms, small businesses, and subcontractors regarding their capabilities to support the operation, consolidation, and/or recompete of one or more NIH-funded biorepositories for FY 2028, including at a minimum the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. This notice also serves to determine the availability of all small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses) with the capability to perform this work. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. These repositories typically: Receive, process, store, and biosamples from a wide range of biospecimen types (e.g. blood/derivatives, fluids, DNA/RNA, hair, cell lines, iPSCs, teeth, fecal matter, birth specimens and other tissues such as brain and other organs) at various temperature and storage conditions (e.g. -80C, liquid nitrogen; fresh, frozen, paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed) at scales ranging from tens of thousands to several million specimens. Serve dozens to hundreds of research studies across the United States and abroad. Enable broad, controlled-access biomaterial sharing to meet specific research objectives that further our knowledge of health Anticipate continued growth in biospecimen and data volume over the life of the award. Scope of Work & Required Capabilities Capable vendors should provide examples from current or previous projects when responding to capabilities. A. Sample Management and Storage Maintain secure, humidity- and temperature-controlled storage and tracking for at least 3,500,000 biospecimens in accordance with Best Practices, Clinical and Laboratory Standards, and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP; 21 CFR 58) with expert quality control and assurance procedures. Document the maximum capacity that could be achieved to expand storage beyond the minimum requested. Destroy samples per regulatory and consent requirements when no longer needed. College of American Pathologists (CAP) Biorepository Accreditation preferred. Maintain positive chain of custody and resolve data/sample discrepancies (missing data, incorrect information, misdirected samples) through issue tracking and resolution, coordinating with relevant receiving/data management teams (e.g. sites, site monitors, study staff). Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data alongside biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Centrally manage and cost-effectively distribute biosamples to qualified investigators approved through established access programs. Provide studies with collection kits and supplies, including barcoded tubes with human-readable labels. Provide research staff training for ordering supplies and collecting samples. B. Data Curation and Management Develop and maintain SOPs for sample receipt, storage, processing, QC, and distribution. Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data associated with biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Maintain an internal relational database (e.g., using persistent identifiers such as RRIDs) linked to associated data and participant and sample identifiers, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample and data location. Register and track biospecimens via an internal relational database with sample IDs (RRID) linked to participant IDs and associated data in the Contractor's auditable LIMS, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample/data location. Clean, standardize, and harmonize clinical data with cross-disorder phenotypic knowledge (e.g. different diagnostic systems or criteria, such as RDOC, DSM, ICD), incorporating data from electronic health records when applicable. Transfer data and sample IDs to controlled-access repositories or Data Centers (e.g., dbGAP, NBDC Data Hub or program specific data repositories). C. Laboratory and Analytic Capabilities Demonstrate laboratory expertise appropriate to the repository's sample types, which may include molecular biology techniques (e.g., DNA/RNA extraction, cell line transformation/immortalization), rigorous quality control, and tissue/cell culture (isolation, scale-up, and banking of primary cells). Provide CLIA-certification status. Provide laboratory capabilities for, but not limited to: metabolic, hematologic, and/or clinical assays high-throughput genotyping, sequencing, and gene-expression analysis Mass spectrometry for proteomics and metabolomics Advanced genomic and cellular techniques such as short- and long-range sequencing, chromatin capture, ChIP-seq, Cut-and-Tag, HiC generation of iPSC/neural stem cell lines CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing Analysis of RNA and DNA from Formalin-Fixed Parafin-Embedded tissue Provide scientific and technical expertise to evaluate and respond to researcher-submitted requests for biospecimen availability. Demonstrate that lead investigators and support staff have relevant experience in biobanking, LIMS, and database management Store and/or process histopathological tissue samples. Isolate, scale up, and bank primary cells from diverse tissue samples. D. Informatics Requirements and Cyberinfrastructure Develop, or manage and enhance (if already existing), a biorepository web portal (front-end and back-end), supporting existing features and providing updates/improvements as requested, potentially including: Synchronizing sample availability data with a public- or investigator-facing sample explorer tool to streamline discovery of related data and biospecimens across repositories Showcase published research and provide lay summaries Advertise repository resources For existing resources, support all currently available features, with updates and improvements as requested Where in scope, develop outreach tools (e.g., an integrated chatbot or public-facing portal) to help users locate biomaterials/data and discover related resources across repositories Develop or maintain backend infrastructure (e.g., server maintenance, microservices, relational databases such as PostgreSQL) and front-end website design/UI-UX. Maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) and require security documentation to keep systems compliant with applicable FISMA-level and other NIH requirements. Maintain, update, and develop Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and cyberinfrastructure for secure, interoperable data exchange. Capabilities for homomorphic encryption and distributed learning. Demonstrate experience and technical expertise to address all aspects of informatics requirements listed above. K. Collaboration & Governance Establish a strong collaborative relationship with the NIH Data Centers, study teams, and Institutes/Centers to enable modifications as the studies evolve. Serve as a co-signatory of the Specimen/Material Transfer Agreements developed by the funding Institute/Center. Be eligible to receive a Certificate of Confidentiality, adhering to requirements for protecting sensitive participant information as set forth in 45 CFR Part 75.303(a), NIHGPS Chapter 8.3 and 15.2.1, and subsection 301(d) of the Public Health Service Act (see: https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-17-109.html). Comply with all applicable human subjects protection, ethical, privacy, and data security regulations. Submission Requirements Interested organizations must demonstrate and document in a submitted capability statement extensive experience across the technical areas above, and include specific information on: Experience — An outline of previous similar projects, specifically the techniques employed in the areas described above. Personnel — Name and professional qualifications of personnel with specific experience in the work requested and knowledge of/experience in biomedical research. Facilities — Availability and description of facilities and equipment required to conduct this type of work. The Government will assess the appropriateness of professional and technical personnel classifications and consider any other specific and relevant information that would improve evaluation of respondents. Organizations should demonstrate capability to administer and coordinate interrelated tasks effectively and in a timely manner. Supporting documentation may include contracts in which the organization performed equivalent tasks (Government and commercial), references (names, titles, phone numbers, and other identifying information), and awards or commendations. An organization that does not have all the listed expertise, may respond by listing organizations with which they intend to collaborate or have as subcontractors to fulfill the requirements. Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than October 20, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. All capability statements should include: Company name and address Point of contact SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Phone/fax/email NAICS Code(s) Business size and status Capability information responsive to the requirements and qualifications identified in this notice Type(s) of business, if any (e.g., small, Veteran-owned, service-disabled Veteran-owned, women-owned, 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone)) NAICS Code: 541714 — Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology). SBA size standard: 1,000 employees or fewer. Submission Instructions Capability statements must be submitted electronically to: Shaun Rostad, Contract Specialist Email: shaun.rostad@nih.gov Secondary Point of Contact: Joshua T. Lazarus, Contract Specialist Email: josh.lazarus@nih.gov Submissions are due NO LATER THAN 1:00 p.m. EST on October 20, 2026. The subject line must include the Small Business Sources Sought Number. NIDA will not accept paper or faxed capability statements. Disclaimer THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement, nor does it constitute a solicitation or commitment by NIDA. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses under this announcement, nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information submitted. Any proprietary information should be so marked. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Respondents should ensure their response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of information or provide feedback with respect to any information submitted. Based on the Government’s market research, it is the agency’s assessment that the services described herein do not appear to constitute commercial services as defined under RFO Subpart 2.1, and therefore, the agency does not currently intend to utilize RFO Part 12 Acquisition Procedures. However, if an interested party asserts that these services are in fact commercial in nature, it should respond to this requirement and provide supporting evidence demonstrating that the services meet the definition of commercial services as prescribed by the applicable regulations.

sig_45234de41d9cdbfab304.description: Lot 1: Establishment of the National Central C-ITS Node The National Central C-ITS Node covers the Central C-ITS Station and the exchange node. The Central C-ITS Station forms the content of messages regarding precisely defined protocols and scenarios of C-ITS services. Through the National Node, various stakeholders will communicate with each other in a trustworthy manner. In the future, it is expected that more and more information providers will be connected to the system and will provide data for various C-ITS services and scenarios. Thus, safety messages and traffic status warnings will arrive directly in the vehicles of various car manufacturers. Lot 2: Execution of mobile laser scanning and determination of the axis along the traffic lane The goal of the task is the acquisition and digitisation of road traffic infrastructure data for the needs of autonomous driving. The task will address the geometry of traffic surfaces at the level of traffic lanes to determine the course of the digital axis along the traffic lane. The digital model of the axis along the traffic lane is part of the digital traffic infrastructure (DPI) NCUP. The results of the task will be intended to support new digital services in traffic. The digital model must provide support for navigation, provide support and be a source of information for cooperative intelligent transport systems (C-ITS) and, in the future, enable and support autonomous driving. The subject public contract includes data acquisition in the field with mobile laser scanning and spherical photography of state roads in a length of 1.937 km (in both directions; G1, G2, R1 and selected sections R2) Lot 3: Establishment of a system for the analysis of traffic flows on public roads The basic goal of the video analytics system is to improve the obtained data on the movement of free-flow traffic vehicles on public roads, which we will achieve by analysing vehicle speed data calculated from streaming footage of already existing traffic monitoring cameras. The main result of the public contract will be the creation of a software solution for the dynamic calculation of vehicle speeds from streaming footage provided by traffic monitoring cameras. The calculated data will be integrated into the client's existing platform for managing mass data of vehicle tracks in real time (FCD platform). sig_4547ed0a491926085eb6.description: The proposed investment objective consists of ensuring a direct rail link between the towns of Timișoara (RO) and Szeged (HU). The investment aims to create modern infrastructure for crossing the Romanian-Hungarian border, adapted to current cross-border mobility requirements and integrated into the regional rail network. At the same time, it seeks to ensure a direct link between the transport networks of the two EU member states, with the aim of stimulating economic, social and cultural cooperation in the border area. The designed rail infrastructure will include the following elements: o construction of the cross-border bridge over the Mureș river, between its embankments, in the event that the chosen route variant requires the construction of a cross-border bridge; o on the territory of Romania:  rehabilitation of existing rail infrastructure and/or construction of new rail infrastructure with their electrification and centralisation;  construction of engineering structures (bridges/passages, culverts, retaining walls, etc.);  rehabilitation / construction of rail installations (electric traction stations, signalling installations, etc.);  modernisation of level crossings and construction of grade-separated crossings at the intersection of the railway line with national roads. Summary of services The summary of activities, investigations, design services, analyses, evaluations, studies, etc., which the Service Provider will carry out in order to develop the technical-economic documentation for the second stage DALI with an FS component, will include (without being limited to) the following: o Analysis of legislation and regulations in force; o Obtaining the Urban Planning Certificate and the opinions/agreements according to the UC; o Preparation of the Technical Expertise of the existing rail infrastructure; o Preparation of the Rail Traffic Study; o Preparation of the Multicriteria Analysis (MCA) regarding route alternatives; o Carrying out field investigations, by preparing:  The Topographic Study;  The Geotechnical Study;  The Hydrological, Hydrogeological and Hydraulic Study;  The Pedological Study;  Documentation regarding land occupation (identification of owners, land areas affected by the work). o Ensuring the Environmental Impact Assessment procedure, by carrying out all specialist studies requested by the competent Environmental Authority, participating in public consultations and obtaining the Environmental Agreement; o Preparation of the D.A.L.I. with an F.S. component; o Preparation of the Cost-Benefit Analysis and the Financial Model; The above list regarding specialist studies is not exhaustive and may be supplemented with other specialist studies mentioned in the Urban Planning Certificate or identified as mandatory by the Service Provider. The services that the Service Provider will carry out will be in accordance with the Terms of Reference and the documentation posted in the SEAP, with compliance with the applicability of the incident legislation and technical regulations in force at the date of preparation, as well as based on the application of relevant methodologies, based on the best national and international practices in the field of transport infrastructure, within a period of 16 months from the date mentioned in the commencement order, phased, according to the provisions of the procurement documentation – Terms of Reference chap. 5. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information, on the 12-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders, provided that the requests are addressed at least 22 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. Clarifications submitted after this deadline will no longer be taken into consideration.

sig_454b95373d6444fc5445.description: The subject of the service is the cloud-based provision (Software-as-a-Service, SaaS) of the DMS, its provision, configuration and customisation, the migration of existing data, training and documentation, formal acceptance of the one-off implementation services as well as ongoing operation including maintenance, support and service. Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of a Document Management System (DMS). The contracting authority is the Gemeinde Vaterstetten in the district of Ebersberg in the administrative region of Upper Bavaria (https://vaterstetten.de). With over 25.000 inhabitants, Vaterstetten is the second largest municipality in Bavaria that is neither a town nor a market town. Due to its population size, it has been one of the so-called efficient district-affiliated municipalities since 2001. It therefore assumes district tasks such as the processing of building permits as a lower building supervisory authority, historic preservation as a lower monument protection authority and waste disposal in the municipal area. The municipal administration, together with the municipal operations and recycling yards as well as school properties, has a staff of approximately 200 employees. The administration keeps its records partly in paper form, but largely in file-based storage systems (network drives) and in the respective specialist procedures. The Bavarian Uniform File Plan is currently only partially followed. The annual increase in documents averages about 15 %. The planned introduction is a uniform, media-break-free document management system (DMS) with an electronic file (e-file) for administration-wide case processing. The subject of the service is the cloud-based provision (Software-as-a-Service, SaaS) of the DMS, its provision, configuration and customisation, the migration of existing data, training and documentation, formal acceptance of the one-off implementation services as well as ongoing operation including maintenance, support and service.
sig_454b95373d6444fc5445.title: Procurement of a document management system (DMS)

sig_456a1e3751121d05aab0.description: Procurement of development and implementation services for the Digital Public Services Platform for Agentia Nationala Anti-Doping, as well as the hardware products, software licences and cybersecurity solutions required for its operation, under project SMIS code 342867. By providing the requested services, the contracting authority aims to digitise the public services provided by ANAD to a sophistication level of 4, ensuring advanced digital interaction between ANAD and the beneficiaries of the public services it provides. The contracting authority shall clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarification / additional information on the 11-th day prior to the deadline set for the submission of tenders. The number of days before the deadline for the submission of tenders by which clarifications may be requested: 20 days. ANAD wishes to procure integrated IT solution services (complete package for the implementation of the IT solution for the digitisation of ANAD public services, hardware, licences, development services, cybersecurity, training). The procurement is planned under the project "Digital Public Services Platform for the National Anti-Doping Agency", SMIS Code 342867, funded through the Smart Growth, Digitisation and Financial Instruments Programme 2021–2027 (PoCIDIF). In the context of accelerating digital transformation at European and national level, as well as increasing operational efficiency requirements, ANAD is initiating a broad project to digitise the public services it offers, entitled "Digital Public Services Platform for the National Anti-Doping Agency". The necessity of the project is determined by the limitations of the current IT infrastructure and the absence of an integrated digital framework for interaction with anti-doping service beneficiaries. By implementing this project, ANAD aims to become a benchmark of good practice in public administration, offering efficient and modern services that meet the current and future needs of public officials and citizens. The modernisation of the IT system will enable more efficient internal management, facilitate access to digital services and ensure a high level of security and compliance. The purpose of the procurement is the design, development, implementation and commissioning of ANAD's Digital Public Services Platform, a unitary and interdependent software solution composed of modules that communicate directly with each other in real time, with a single approach including for analysis, development, testing, implementation, training and post-implementation technical support. The following specific objectives shall be pursued through this procurement: • analysis and design of the IT system, with documentation of the technical and functional architecture; • development, configuration and integration of software modules, with electronic workflows and electronic document management, including workflows for document operations (signing, approval, allocation); • development of the public portal and electronic registry, as well as a mobile application; • implementation of a virtual assistant (chatbot) and artificial intelligence / machine learning components, with support for the Romanian language, including for the automatic identification of similar cases; • supply, delivery, installation and configuration of hardware equipment (workstations, laptops, servers, network equipment, printers, scanners, UPSs) and related software licences; • configuration and operationalisation of the private/governmental cloud infrastructure in which the solution is hosted; • implementation of cybersecurity solutions and services, including MDR/SOC-type managed services provided from the European Union; • interoperability with other IT systems of institutions benefiting from ANAD services and historical data migration; • testing, training of the contracting authority's personnel, reception and commissioning of the solution; • provision of warranty, technical support and post-implementation maintenance services. The minimum mandatory requirements, technical and functional specifications, deliverables and deadlines are detailed in the Specifications, an integral part of the tender documentation.
sig_456a1e3751121d05aab0.title: Services for an integrated IT solution within the project "Digital Public Services Platform for the National Anti-Doping Agency"

sig_458037be25f5ba8cc32b.description: 1. Objective As part of this market survey, suitable software solutions for the digital management and tracking of human milk processes (mother's own milk and donated human milk) in a clinical environment are being sought. The goal is a system for the complete, audit-proof mapping of all processes, taking into account the requirements of the SoHo Regulation, with a focus on patient safety, traceability and process automation. 2. General requirements The software must ensure end-to-end digital documentation and traceability; provide interfaces to SAP and Copra 5/6; automate workflows and notifications; integrate label printing and scanning processes; and enable role-based access. 3. Mother's Own Milk The software should enable the registration of mothers on the ward with an SAP connection, assign a unique mother ID, record CMV status including information and consent, document the amount of milk expressed, allow labels to be created by staff or the mother, track the storage location and inventory, and provide automatic alerts for CMV inactivation (day 7 and 32+0 weeks of gestation). Data on the children such as name, date of birth, week of gestation and weight should be automatically transferred from SAP or Copra. 4. Processing Mother's Own Milk CMV-inactivated milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches by bottle, labelled, inactivation documented, and cooling processes and storage locations noted. Centrifuged milk should be processed analogously, including documentation of duration and revolutions, labelling as skimmed, assignment of analyses and storage. 5. Administration The software should enable the assignment of milk batches to children, offer interfaces to Copra 5/6, record partial quantities via scan and document retrievals. 6. Batch management The software must automatically generate batches based on mother ID, week of gestation, calendar week of birth, calendar week of milk collection and processing type (raw or pasteurised). Colour coding by week of gestation should be adjusted automatically, as should the documentation of the processing day. 7. Human Milk Bank Potential donors should be identified automatically (e.g. >600 ml/day), be able to fill out digital information and anamnesis forms with a signature, and receive a donor ID. Interfaces to SAP, Copra and the laboratory (e.g. ix.serv) should automatically adopt laboratory findings. The software should enable approvals by specialist staff, evaluation of findings and labelling of pasteurisation requirements. 8. Donated milk The software should record milk quantity, date, time, calendar week, temperature, microbiological samples and storage locations. 9. Processing of donated milk Raw milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches and stored until release. Pasteurised milk should be processed with documentation of pasteurisation, cooling and storage. CMV-inactivated milk should document pooling, inactivation, cooling and release. Centrifuged milk is processed analogously to mother's own milk, if necessary with additional pasteurisation. 10. Non-released milk The software should document measures such as discarding, re-pasteurisation, training of the donor and repeat samples. 11. Dispensing The software should enable the assignment of batches to wards and individual children and record partial quantities via scan. 12. Summary We are looking for an integrated software solution for the secure, automated management of human milk processes with complete traceability, high system integration and user-friendliness. 13. Participation in the market survey Interested companies are requested to submit their participation and information on the solution by email to vergabestelle@klinikum-stuttgart.de no later than 15.05.2026. The market survey serves exclusively to prepare for a possible procurement procedure. There is no entitlement to the implementation of such a procedure.
sig_458037be25f5ba8cc32b.title: Software for the management and documentation of human milk in accordance with the SoHo Regulation

sig_45aa5d107594438d760c.description: The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is undertaking a virtual market engagement exercise Wednesday 5th August 2026 @ 10am , via MS Teams, to inform the commissioning of the Online Harms Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is committed to understanding the factors that place children and young people at risk of violence, exploitation and harm, and to working collaboratively with partners to deliver long-term, sustainable solutions. We work across communities and sectors, including youth services, local government, education, health, policing and the voluntary and community sector, championing a public health approach that combines prevention, early intervention and effective support for those experiencing the greatest levels of risk and vulnerability. At the heart of our approach is the belief that violence is preventable, not inevitable. We recognise, however, that many children and young people are already navigating the impacts of trauma, exploitation, abuse and complex community dynamics. As such, our work seeks not only to prevent harm before it occurs, but also to strengthen the systems, services and trusted adults responsible for safeguarding, supporting and intervening with those most affected. Central to this approach is a commitment to partnership working, evidence-informed practice and ensuring that the voices, experiences and expertise of young people and communities shape the solutions designed to support them. The Mayor's Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a forthcoming procurement opportunity relating to the delivery of its flagship Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The programme forms part of the VRU's wider public health approach to violence reduction and sits within a London-wide model developed following extensive consultation with young people, practitioners, safeguarding professionals, academics and sector experts. Digital life brings clear benefits for many children. Ofcom found that 99% of 13–17-year-olds see at least one benefit to being online, including help with schoolwork, learning new skills and maintaining social connections. 93% of children in the UK play video games, and children report that gaming helps them socialise with friends, learn new skills and have fun, with most online interactions taking place with friends they already know offline. At the same time, the VRU is concerned that these same digital environments expose children and young people to a wide range of harms and risks. Digital safety is increasingly a public safety and public health concern. Children and young people are navigating identity, relationships, influence, exploitation and conflict across interconnected online and offline environments. However, systems, services and safeguarding responses have often struggled to keep pace with the rapidly evolving nature of digital spaces. This matters for the VRU because online harms do not sit separately from wider concerns about violence, vulnerability, exploitation and safeguarding. The VRU is seeking delivery partners to pilot innovative Digital Youth Work (DYW) approaches across London that drive new models of engagement with young people and promote safeguarding in digital spaces. The VRU is seeking approaches that: Design, deliver and test new or existing digital youth work models Extend trusted, relationship-based youth work into digital environments Strengthen early intervention, prevention and safeguarding online Generate learning, insight and practical outputs to strengthen future activity The programme aims not only to deliver effective pilot activity, but also to contribute to sector-wide innovation and the development of scalable models of digital youth work across London. Scope of delivery The programme will be structured into three complementary lots: Lot 1: Supporting High-Need and Digitally Dependent Young People Testing approaches that improve accessibility and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, including SEND. Lot 2: Early Intervention and Prevention of Online Harms Testing models that enable early identification, prevention and response to online risks, with a focus on safeguarding and preventative practice of deterring online to offline violence. Lot 3: Universal Digital Youth Work and Positive Opportunities Exploring how digital youth work can foster connection, creativity, play, participation and digital citizenship for all young people. Bidders may apply for one, two or all three lots. Applications may be submitted by individual organisations or as partnerships/consortia. Target Audience The programme will focus on delivering digital youth work to children and young people aged 11–25 across London, including but not limited to: Young people at higher risk of being impacted by online harms Those facing barriers to traditional youth provision, including SEND and young people who may be more digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded Young people experiencing vulnerability linked to violence, exploitation or disadvantage Young people with caring responsibilities Young people in the care system Young people affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) The wider youth population through universal provision Potential delivery settings and workforces may include, but are not limited to: Community-based youth organisations and youth services Detached, outreach and neighbourhood-based provision Faith and community organisations SEND and disability-focused youth provision Organisations supporting young people experiencing vulnerability, exclusion or barriers to traditional youth provision Specialist services working with young people affected by violence, exploitation or online harms Informal education, mentoring and participation-based youth provision Indicative Outcomes The programme is expected to contribute to: Increased engagement of young people in safe, supportive digital environments Improved accessibility of youth work for young people who do not traditionally engage with youth work and are digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded) Strengthened early identification and prevention of online harms in the digital space Increased use of technology to foster positive opportunities Strengthen young people’s digital citizenship Increased workforce confidence and capability in incorporating digital youth work into traditional practice and safeguarding policy Development of scalable models, guidance and practical tools A stronger London-wide evidence base on digital youth work and online safety Timeframe and Budget The maximum estimated budget for this programme is up to £650,000 excl. VAT over a full contract period from November 2026 – March 2029, subject to confirmation of funding, internal governance and relevant approvals. This comprises: £390,000 core funding across the 2026/27 and 2027/28 financial years from November 2026 to March 2028 An extension option of up to £260,000 for a further 12 months from April 2028 The VRU welcomes bids from individual organisations as well as collaborative partnerships and consortia. We recognise that expertise may be distributed across different organisations, and we encourage applications that bring together complementary skills, knowledge and experience. Providers do not need to demonstrate strength across every area independently, provided that the partnership as a whole can evidence the required expertise and capacity to deliver the programme. This may include, for example, combining specialist knowledge in DYW, supporting SEND or neurodiverse children, digital safety, contextual safeguarding, fostering positive digital opportunities, and preventative violence reduction approaches. Market Engagement / Response The VRU welcomes engagement from organisations with expertise in: Youth work and youth engagement Digital youth work Gaming, AI, technology Safeguarding and contextual safeguarding Online harms, exploitation and violence prevention Working with vulnerable and hard-to-reach young people Youth participation and co-production Learning, evaluation and evidence generation If you are interested in the opportunity and meet the core capabilities as set out above, then please join us for our early market warming event on Wednesday 5th August 2026 at 10:00AM. Attending the early market warming session does not constitute a commitment to participate in any future procurement process. The Eventbrite link for market warming session can be found here - https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/london-vru-online-harms-digital-youth-work-pilot-market-warming-session-tickets-1994744836503?aff=oddtdtcreator Please note that this exercise is in no way a call for competition and will not result in the award of a contract to any respondents to this notice. If have any further questions about this opportunity, please contact: vruprocurement@london.gov.uk For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Digital-mapping-services./5SJUMP2G3Z To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/5SJUMP2G3Z Lot 1: Supporting high-need and digitally dependent young people. Test and develop Digital Youth Work approaches that improve accessibility, inclusion and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, particularly those with SEND, neurodiverse needs or higher levels of digital dependency. Lot 2: Early intervention and prevention of online harms. Test Digital Youth Work approaches that strengthen early identification, prevention and safeguarding responses to online harms, vulnerabilities and online-to-offline risks. Lot 3: Universal digital youth work and positive opportunities. Explore how Digital Youth Work can foster connection, belonging, creativity, participation and positive opportunities for children and young people through universal and strengths-based approaches.

sig_45c985c19003ef2cd69f.description: 1. Contracting Authority The EWE Group, headquartered in Oldenburg, is one of the large regional energy supply companies in Germany. EWE is active in various business areas, including energy (gas/electricity), telecommunications, information technology, mobility and hydrogen. With over 10.000 employees and a turnover of around 8,7 billion euros in the 2024 financial year, EWE is one of the significant players in the German energy industry. EWE pursues a clear strategy towards a sustainable, innovative and future-oriented energy supply - including through projects in the field of wind energy and the hydrogen economy. The EWE Group is predominantly in municipal hands and supplies around one million households in the electricity segment alone. 2. Subject of the tender The EWE Group as the contracting authority (CA) intends to procure a software solution for Business Process Management (BPM) that meets the company's specific professional and technical requirements. The subject of the tender is the acquisition, implementation and operation of BPM software, including initial user training and the migration of existing data and process models from the legacy system to the new system. The software should enable intuitive modelling of processes - with a focus on Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN). For this purpose, user-friendly drag-and-drop editors are required for the simple creation, adaptation and maintenance of process models. In addition, the following functionalities are required: - Independently configurable workflows, e.g. for the approval of process models - Extensive commenting and collaboration options for all user groups - Versioning of process models and the possibility to manage several variants of a process - Comprehensive reporting and analysis functions Also desired are: - A flexibly configurable authorisation and role concept - Interfaces to other IT systems to support import and export processes, in particular: * Import of data from IT systems (e.g. organisational units) * Export of data to third-party systems, such as analysis platforms like SAP Datasphere, Snowflake or Azure OneLake
sig_45c985c19003ef2cd69f.title: Process modelling tool
