sig_48d05d197a1534fcd059.description: 1.Introduction The London Borough of Newham invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced organisations to partner with us on our Housing Improvement Programme. This strategic partnership will be critical to addressing the findings of the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) inspection and achieving full compliance with the Consumer Standards. We seek a delivery partner who will work collaboratively with our in house teams and advisers to deliver safe, decent homes and secure sustainable service improvement. 2.Background and Context The Social Housing (Regulation) Act 2023 introduced strengthened Consumer Standards and a proactive inspection regime. Following the RSH inspection in May 2024, Newham Council received a C4 grading, demonstrating systemic failings in: •Safety & Quality •Transparency, Influence & Accountability In response, the Council has launched a comprehensive Improvement Programme and is entering into a Voluntary Undertaking with the Regulator. This will set out required actions, milestones, governance and reporting arrangements. Our strategic ambition is to move rapidly from reactive compliance to a proactive, intelligence led asset and safety management model supported by strong data governance and organisational capability. 3.Purpose and Partnership Objectives The Council seeks a strategic delivery partner to: •Act as an extension of the in house Housing Asset Management Team. •Provide advisory, delivery and management capacity to accelerate improvement at pace. •Ensure tenants’ homes remain safe, habitable and fully compliant with regulatory requirements. •Work with the Council’s in house Asset Management Team and Savills to co design, implement and embed the Target Operating Model (TOM) for asset, safety and compliance management, including structured mobilisation, process redesign, capability transfer and cultural change. The partner will be expected to work in line with the Council’s values: excellence, openness, transparency, learning from mistakes, collaboration, and tenant centred service delivery. 4.Scope of Services It’s anticipated the strategic partner assignment will last between 18 and 24 months. The Council are looking to appoint the strategic partner by no later than April/May 2026. The appointed partner will be responsible for delivering an integrated programme across six interconnected workstreams. 4.1Compliance, Safety and Remedial Works (including Tenant Safety) •Deliver a comprehensive programme of remedial works covering all statutory and regulatory compliance actions under the following areas: oFRA Remedials oDamp & Mould oHHSRS Remedials oElectrical Safety oStock Condition Survey Remedials oTenancy Audits Repairs oGas Safety oAsbestos Safety Management oWater Hygiene (Legionella) oLifts & Lifting Equipment (LOLER) oSmoke & CO •Address and eliminate the backlog of planned and reactive repairs, stabilising business as usual delivery. •Implement robust safety measures, including fire safety, gas safety, electrical safety, water hygiene, asbestos management, structural safety, damp and mould remediation, lift safety, smoke and Carbon Monoxide detection, and resident communication. •Ensure all activity complies with relevant legislation and guidance, including the Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS), Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012, Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 and related statutory requirements. 4.2Programme and Supply Chain Management •Design and manage a comprehensive, risk based work programme aligned to the Council’s priorities. •Establish a balanced and capable supply chain, ensuring quality, compliance and resilience. •Plan and schedule works to optimise productivity and minimise disruption to residents. •Produce clear and compliant work specifications. •Work closely with Newham Procurement, to provide additional capacity where required •Understanding service and work requirements, producing specifications, supplier evaluations and selection, etc. •Oversee contract management, performance, compliance and risk. •Implement KPIs, reporting and continuous improvement processes. 4.3Asset Management and Data Governance •Establish the Council’s asset management function, including asset data management, stock condition surveys and long term lifecycle planning. Improve data quality and governance by ensuring accuracy, completeness and timeliness of asset and compliance data. •Implement data governance frameworks and conduct regular audits. •Integrate data systems with asset management and compliance platforms for real time insight. •Provide training to staff in order to strengthen existing Newham housing teams’ knowledge on data standards, quality and best practice. •Ensure compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. 4.4Capital Programme Delivery •Plan, manage and deliver the Council’s capital investment programme. •Address priority risk areas promptly. •Ensure homes meet and exceed Decent Homes standards. •Apply strong financial control, gateway assurance and whole life value principles. 4.5Target Operating Model (TOM): Implementation and Embedding •Work with the Council’s in house Asset Management Team and Savills to deliver the TOM, covering governance, roles and responsibilities, organisational structure, end to end processes, systems, data and reporting, and performance management. •Develop mobilisation plans, standard operating procedures, training materials and quality assurance frameworks. •Provide structured change support and capability transfer to ensure the TOM is embedded, sustainable and fully owned by the Council. 4.6Capability, Culture and Organisational Development •Conduct a gap analysis of organisational readiness, skills and capacity. •Support leadership development and strengthen operational competence in compliance, asset management, risk, assurance and resident engagement. •Embed a learning culture based on transparency, continuous improvement and right first time principles. •Co produce improvement activity and communication with tenants and resident groups. 5.Expected Outcomes and Performance Measures The partnership will deliver measurable improvements, including: •100% statutory compliance across all safety areas within agreed timescales. •Reduction and elimination of repairs backlogs against an agreed trajectory. Improved accuracy, completeness and governance of asset and compliance data, validated through audit. •Capital programme delivery achieved to time, quality and cost. Improvements in resident experience, including satisfaction and communication. •Successful implementation and embedding of the TOM, with evidence of capability transfer and reduced dependency on the partner over time. •Strengthened internal controls and independent assurance. 6.Partnership, Governance and Ways of Working •Operate as a single integrated team with the Council and Savills, supported by clear governance, RACI structures and escalation pathways. •Establish a joint Programme Management Office (PMO) with transparent reporting, risk management and change control. •Uphold the Council’s standards relating to health and safety, equality, diversity and inclusion, information governance and social value. •Demonstrate open book working, clear communication and evidence based decision making. 7.Indicative Commercial and Delivery Parameters •Partnership model: strategic delivery partner; consortiums welcome with a nominated lead. •Indicative duration: 18 – 24 months, with gateways, reviews and breakpoints. •Mobilisation: immediate mobilisation following award, including a 90 day mobilisation and risk burn down plan. •Estimated value: £3m - £4m per annum (inc. VAT) •Compliance with the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and Environmental Information Regulations 2004 where relevant. 8.Market Engagement - questions In order to register your expression of interest, please complete the below form: https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=4Wk2NRiX-Eab7ZWvyHdsinT36ZDEE_JBoyz6k2rSYs9UOENNWllBTFZTNUE0NVRQTDZZQzQ0VVozTi4u The link to the survey is also included in the portal (within the document titled 'EoI for Newham Housing Strategic Partner') Timelines •EOI response (survey completion) deadline: 11th February 2026 •Estimated tender exercise publication: March 2026 NOTE: dates in refence to contract start and end dates within this notice are estimated 9.Contact Information Paul Graham – Procurement Lead for Housing Paul.graham@newham.gov.uk For more information about this opportunity, please visit the Delta eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Newham:-Housing-services./8Y9EM57XJ9 To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/8Y9EM57XJ9 Lot 1: .

sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.
sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?

Framework agreement for the performance of radio audience measurement tasks. Based on the framework agreement, the individual contract for the given service(s) shall be concluded by direct order, taking into account the provisions of point a) of subsection (1) of Section 105 of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). The detailed definition of the services is contained in the technical specification issued as part of the public procurement documents. The aim of the procurement is to ensure a coherent methodology for the domestic Radio Listening Measurement (hereinafter: RHM) at national, Budapest and local levels, as well as to implement and maintain a uniform, transparent and sustainable measurement methodology in the domestic radio sector. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement pursuant to point a) of subsection (1) of Section 105 of the Kbt. up to a net ceiling amount of 1 440 000 000 Forints, with the proviso that the implementation of the given public procurements shall take place by means of direct orders according to order categories. The framework agreement shall be concluded for a duration of three years starting at the earliest from 1 January 2024 or – if it occurs at a later date – from the signing of the contract (the measurement period shall last until 31 December 2026). The radio listening measurement must be carried out divided into two measurement components/groups, on different samples, using three different methodologies (diary-based, which may take place via the web or telephone, telephone or online self-completion DAR, as well as instrumental, passive measurement – see below) (multi-component measurement). The first measurement component includes the reception areas of national and Budapest-based radios operating in county seats and cities with county rights, as well as networked radios with a reception area populated by more than 100 thousand people (all reception areas must be measured by the winner, with the proviso that in county seats, cities with county rights and the reception areas of networked radios with a reception area larger than 100 thousand people, a total of maximum 40 units must be measured in the event that their number would exceed 40 units during the term of the contract, the radios/reception areas chosen by the Contracting Authority must be measured). The reception areas shall be determined jointly by the radios cooperating with the AT for this purpose and the Contracting Authority, and they may be reviewed quarterly. The settlement lists of the reception areas shall be handed over by the Contracting Authority to the winner by 15 December each year. The currently relevant list shall be made available by the Contracting Authority as part of the procurement documents (KD). Data must be provided monthly for the national and Budapest radios belonging to this group, while quarterly data must be provided in respect of county seats, cities with county rights, and networked reception areas populated by more than 100 thousand people. The Winner undertakes that all radios operating nationally and distributed by terrestrial analogue broadcasting shall be included in the measurement in such a way that the radios operating nationally, in Budapest, as well as networked radios with a reception area larger than 100 thousand people and in the reception area of county seats and cities with county rights can also be evaluated independently (however, a maximum of 40 out of the local radios with non-national reception areas and non-Budapest local radios). In the case of the first measurement component, various methodologies may be ordered as stated in the individual combinations. These are as follows in the case of component I.A (national and Budapest radios): • a) diary-based methodology/version; • b) methodology/version of the combination of instrumental and diary data collection. In the case of instrumental measurement, continuous operation of a personal sample panel of at least 1000 people is expected, ensuring that at least 900 people provide data for the daily estimate on every day of the measurement. The technical specification of the instrumental measuring system necessary for the performance of the instrumental measurement study according to the foregoing is: a) capable of identifying the listened to (radio) channel per minute, ultimately of delivering the listening results in minute breakdowns (recording radio listening in bands of at least 1 minutes, but the start and end of listening must be recorded in the database with second-level precision); b) performs channel identification using the method called "acoustic signal comparison"; c) the "reference signal" necessary for channel identification is provided by the measuring system itself; d) capable of storing the audio samples necessary for identification for at least 3 days, and then forwarding the recorded data to the central processing unit; e) in the case of an independent meter, the battery must provide an operating time of at least 24 hours, and in the case of a mobile phone device (under average user load) at least 12 hours; f) capable of recording the user position (geolocation-georeferencing); g) it must be possible to clearly determine whether a panel member wore the meter on a given day; h) in the event of loss, it must not be possible to extract confidential data relating to the panel member from it regarding the measurement; i) it must be of portable size; j) it must operate reliably even if it cannot connect to the mobile phone network or the internet. k) It can measure the per-minute listening data of 2-2 content items/programmes selected according to the demand of the Contracting Authority from among the maximum 10-10 stream and podcast programmes/content determined by the Contracting Authority for the diary-based measurement, consolidated for two weeks. The test tool according to the above is essential for carrying out the instrumental data collection/study. In the case of group I.B (county seats, cities with county rights and reception areas of networks populated by more than 100 thousand people), the following methodologies may be ordered as stated in the individual combinations: - diary-based methodology/version. sig_4902487e176936c102c2.description: Turun Raitiotie Oy procures legal and commercial consulting services related to the procurement of tram rolling stock, as well as project support services for the contract period ending 31.12.2028, after which the contract may, by decision of the Contracting Authority, be extended by four (4) separate one (1)-year option periods. The aim of the services to be procured is to ensure the high-quality success of the procurement. The consulting services are procured in two sub-projects: • Sub-project 1: Legal consulting services • Sub-project 2: Commercial consulting services and project management support services One (1) Service Provider will be selected for each sub-project. The Contracting Authority reserves the right not to select a Service Provider if only one (1) tender is received for a part. The task descriptions for both parts are set out in Appendix 1 to the call for tenders. The task descriptions are examples of the preliminary needs of Turun Raitiotie Oy for the services to be procured, but the tasks may change as needed. Turun Raitiotie Oy is procuring tram rolling stock for the operation of the tram line between the port and Varissuo. Commercial passenger traffic is estimated to start in the autumn of 2033 as presented in the implementation plan of the Turku Tramway Alliance. The implementation planning phase of the tramway project has been completed and the Turku City Council has made a decision on the implementation of the tramway. Construction will start with the refurbishment of the Cathedral Bridge, archaeological excavations and the construction of the public transport corridor on streets connected to the Cathedral Bridge. Actual tramway construction can begin when the state's funding share for the implementation of the tramway has been secured. The implementation plan and information about the project can be found on the website www.turunraitiotie.fi. The procurement process for tram rolling stock is long and constitutes a critical phase in terms of schedule for the implementation of the tramway project. The procurement of rolling stock must be carried out in a front-loaded manner so that rolling stock is available even before the start of actual tram operations. Trams will be used for test runs and acceptance inspections of the track infrastructure as well as for driver training. The rolling stock procurement seeks the most economically advantageous rolling stock solution for the Turku tramway. The procurement emphasises the affordability of the life-cycle costs of the tram rolling stock, passenger experience, suitability for the objectives of the City of Turku, low environmental impacts, maintainability and high availability. The Service Provider will work in close cooperation with the experts of Turun Raitiotie Oy and other contractual partners of the Contracting Authority participating in the preparation of the procurement. The management of the Service Provider is the responsibility of the planning manager of Turun Raitiotie Oy. The planning manager is responsible for the execution and management of the procurement project. The Service Provider will work with Turun Raitiotie Oy on the tasks described in the call for tenders and will help ensure that the rolling stock procurement achieves the objectives set for it. The procurement is described in this call for tenders and its appendices.; The procurement is described in this call for tenders and its appendices.

sig_490358764af255e2eee1.description: The AMC Project is a joint contract of the hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland (HHR) and the Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard (HHSK). The goal is the realisation of smart, data-driven management of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) and transport pumping stations. The AMC project has one ambition: “To control the water cycle in real time as optimally as possible based on the organization's objectives. These objectives may change in nature and number over time. This should include meeting discharge requirements, maximizing energy savings, consuming energy when green energy is available, minimal nitrous oxide production, etc. in order to give substance to administrative goals such as energy-neutral, sustainable, circular and minimal greenhouse gas emissions.” The project contributes to: - More efficient energy use and reduction of operational costs; - Improvement of effluent quality; - Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions; - Increase in the reliability and transparency of treatment processes; - The rollout of AMC takes place in phases. In the first three years, eight WWTPs will be equipped with AMC functionality.

sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure with the publication of the request for information; instead, any potential procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a precondition for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or for participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of a personnel planning system. The subject of the procurement is a personnel planning system which: - supports strategic personnel planning and takes into account the qualitative (incl. staff competency structure) and quantitative planning of personnel required for organising service operations - enables the planning of personnel resources at the supervisory level - operates in accordance with processes defined by labour legislation (takes into account the starts, changes, terminations, etc., of employment relationships) - takes into account that the volume of personnel resources is guided by the level of service operations (increases / decreases / remains the same), care intensity and the budget, rather than a static, administrative vacancy system - can be integrated into HUS's other systems - scales to HUS's current personnel and organisational structure and its potential future changes - is a ready-made overall solution / service package. Personnel planning has a close connection to financial planning / the planning system (personnel costs). BACKGROUND TO THE PROCUREMENT Personnel planning is based on HUS's strategy and objectives. Personnel planning is carried out in both the short and long term. Strategic personnel planning is the organisation's long-term personnel planning. It can be used to anticipate changes in the operating environment and evaluate cost impacts. Personnel planning supports the organisation in achieving its objectives by ensuring access to the right capabilities, in the right place and at the right time. The objectives of planning are: - To identify the required number and structure of personnel as well as competence - To define the measures needed to ensure the personnel in accordance with the objective. These may include: • structural solutions related to the organisation of work and divisions of labour • development of personnel competence • renewal of processes • utilisation of digitalisation / new technologies The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: - What kind of system / service package are you offering (description of implementation) and with what functionalities does the solution meet the needs of the contracting authority described in this request for information? - What are the integration possibilities of the solution you are offering? - What is the pricing model of the solution you are offering (e.g. licences, maintenance and support)? - Is the system / service package you are offering in use in other similar organisations (wellbeing services counties, health and social services operators)? Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will process your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered an opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may be given preliminary call for tenders documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the request for information and notify us of your interest no later than 11.12.2025 by 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must state "HUS 495-2025 - Request for information: Personnel planning system".
sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.title: Request for Information: Human Resources Planning System

sig_4957eb720bbbac0fefb0.description: The Fillers Marketing Service, part of Cabinet Office Government Communication Service (GCS), requires a Radio Filler tracking service/tool to track each radio Filler that is live on commercial radio and where possible on community radio, 24-7. We need to analyse the amount of airtime achieved by each filler. The key data from the tracking of each Filler should be provided on a website portal that can be accessed at any time. "Radio fillers" are public welfare, safety and health radio content, that is similar to advert content in spec and length. The Fillers service commission and produce a pool of Fillers, these are delivered to commercial and community radio, and they are played cost free, at the discretion of UK commercial radio and community radio stations, primarily as a resource to fill empty gaps in airtime schedules. The scope of this requirement extends to the following: Tracking of each airtime transmission of all radio Fillers identified by the Authority, that have aired on (UK) commercial radio and where possible, UK community radio. A website portal tool providing the detailed airtime transmission data. The Tracking service is not required in the Channel Islands, the Shetland, Orkney or Western Isles or any other UK overseas territory The Authority requires the following: - Tracking all radio fillers airtime on UK commercial radio and where possible community radio. The Supplier will be sent a WAV file of the audio for each new radio filler. The Authority does not know exact volumes, which are subject to demand, and therefore volumes of work are not guaranteed. - The provision of the following information on a website portal, which will be downloadable onto CSV files: - The title of radio filler - The time and date the radio filler was aired; - The name of the radio station whom played the radio filler; and RAJAR audience data: the number of RAJAR impacts (if applicable) at the time for the radio station whom aired the radio filler. - The Authority requires access to this information using a website portal provided by the Supplier in order to raise reports when required. This will be available to the Authority to run bespoke reports at any time. - The Supplier must supply all data in a format that can be easily transferred to a CSV file to be uploaded into the Authority's database. sig_49677a748a77a2a2c212.description: Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the end-to-end operation, administration, monitoring, maintenance, security, backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services. This includes Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Oracle databases, WebLogic middleware components, cloud and software licences, security platforms and tools, hosting environments, and associated support arrangements. The services will ensure the stable, secure, resilient, and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT, and other related platforms and services. The contractor shall ensure the availability, confidentiality, integrity, and resilience of CEFTA’s infrastructure, systems, applications, and data, in line with industry best practices and applicable security, compliance, and governance requirements. The scope includes infrastructure and platform administration, performance monitoring and tuning, capacity planning, availability management, patch and configuration management, incident, problem, change and release management, and service request fulfilment. The contractor shall provide a combination of proactive and reactive operational support. Proactive services will include continuous monitoring, preventive maintenance, performance and capacity management, security assessments, vulnerability management, patching, security hardening, resilience improvements, cost optimisation, compliance support, and recommendations for continuous service enhancement. Reactive services will include incident response, troubleshooting, service restoration, problem resolution, emergency remediation activities, security incident handling, and support for unplanned events affecting the availability, performance, integrity, or security of CEFTA systems and services. The contract will also include security monitoring, threat detection, cybersecurity risk assessments, vulnerability remediation, backup management, disaster recovery planning and testing, business continuity planning and validation, data protection measures, recovery readiness activities, cloud cost management, infrastructure lifecycle management, operational reporting, service-level performance tracking, documentation maintenance, knowledge transfer, and technical and architectural advisory services, ensuring alignment with CEFTA’s operational, security, and strategic business objectives while maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and recoverability of CEFTA information assets and digital services. Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the operation, monitoring, security, backup, continuity and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services, including Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle databases, WebLogic components, licences, security tools and related hosting and support arrangements. The services will support the stable, secure and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT and related platforms, as well as incident and change management, security monitoring, vulnerability management, cybersecurity assessment and remediation, disaster recovery, business continuity, cost optimisation, technical advisory support and reporting.
sig_49677a748a77a2a2c212.title: CEFTA Cloud Infrastructure, Hosting, Managed Services, Security and Business Continuity

sig_49699bf79cfa029bec3b.description: West Northamptonshire Council (WNC) is a relatively new Local Authority that has inherited a wide range of electronic document systems and storage methods from predecessor councils. These legacy solutions vary in functionality, levels of automation, and overall maturity, which often results in manual processes to meet compliance, retention, and operational needs. Key services such as Housing, Revenues & Benefits, Regulatory Services, the post room and Pensions and Payroll rely heavily on electronic document and records management to process and store critical information from residents, businesses, and other stakeholders. The Council uses several inherited systems for records management, each supporting different service areas. Additionally, WNC have an archive and heritage service that require archiving for long-term retention of digital materials. The project will consider opportunities to bring these capabilities together into a more consistent and modern corporate approach; in some cases, for archive data only.
sig_49699bf79cfa029bec3b.title: Electronic Document Record Management System

The subject matter of the public contract is "Provision and maintenance of licences by lots", divided into the following lots: - Lot No 1: "Provision of SAP licences, as well as Enterprise Support type maintenance for the provided permanent licences for the needs of the Ministry of Finance (MF)"; - Lot No 2: "Provision of Adobe licences for the needs of the Administration of the Council of Ministers (ACM)" *** The total estimated value of the public contract amounts to 190 021,00 EUR excluding VAT, distributed by lots as follows: - Estimated value of Lot No 1 – 189 217,00 EUR excluding VAT; - Estimated value of Lot No 2 – 804,00 EUR excluding VAT; *** Tenders shall be submitted only for Lot No 1. Pursuant to Article 21, paragraph 6 of the Public Procurement Act (PPA), the Contracting Authority has the right to award lots under the procedure valid for the individual estimated value of each of them, provided that the value of the respective lot does not exceed 156 464 BGN for supplies and services and the total estimated value of the lots awarded in this manner does not exceed 20 per cent of the total estimated value of the contract. In such cases, regardless of the residual value of the contract, it shall be awarded under the procedure applicable to the total value of the contract. Lot No 2 shall be awarded under the procedure valid for its respective individual value in connection with Article 21, paragraph 6 of the PPA – through the method of direct award, on the grounds of Article 20, paragraph 4, item 3 of the PPA. Tenderers shall not submit tenders for Lot No 2! *** The main activities within the scope of Lot No 1 "Provision of SAP licences, as well as Enterprise Support type maintenance for the provided permanent licences for the needs of the Ministry of Finance (MF)" include the delivery and activation of the following SAP licences: SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central (3% CPI increase), core HR – 569 units; SAP SuccessFactors Learning – 569 units; SAP AI Unit – 25 units; SAP Payroll Processing for SAP S/4HANA – 569 units; SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management for Professional Use – 16 units; SAP HANA Runtime Edition for Applications & SAP BW – New/Subsequent – 15% of the total value of the permanent licences. The activation of the SAP cloud licences shall be carried out starting from the date indicated in the delivery request. For the permanent licences, Enterprise Support type maintenance shall be provided for a period of 36 months, starting from the month following the delivery month. ****** The public contract is announced without secured funding, therefore the contract for lot No1 of the public contract shall be concluded under a condition precedent, in accordance with Article 114 of the PPA. The performance of the contract shall begin after the provision of funding by the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY, certified by a written notification sent by the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY to the CONTRACTOR and the submission by the Contractor of the designated performance guarantee. **** The time limit for the performance of the activities under lot No 1 is as follows: The delivery time limit is up to 5 working days after secured funding, submission of a performance guarantee and receipt of a written request from the Contracting Authority. The validity period of the cloud licences and Enterprise Support maintenance is 36 months. The performance requirements are described in detail in the Technical Specification of the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY for lot No 1 - Annex No1.1. The main activities within the scope of Lot No 1 "Provision of SAP licences, as well as Enterprise Support type maintenance for the provided permanent licences for the needs of the Ministry of Finance (MF)" include the delivery and activation of the following SAP licences: SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central (3% CPI increase), core HR – 569 units; SAP SuccessFactors Learning – 569 units; SAP AI Unit – 25 units; SAP Payroll Processing for SAP S/4HANA – 569 units; SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management for Professional Use – 16 units; SAP HANA Runtime Edition for Applications & SAP BW – New/Subsequent – 15% of the total value of the permanent licences. The activation of the SAP cloud licences shall be carried out starting from the date indicated in the delivery request. For the permanent licences, Enterprise Support type maintenance shall be provided for a period of 36 months, starting from the month following the delivery month. ****** The public contract is announced without secured funding, therefore the contract for lot No1 of the public contract shall be concluded under a condition precedent, in accordance with Article 114 of the PPA. The performance of the contract shall begin after the provision of funding by the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY, certified by a written notification sent by the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY to the CONTRACTOR and the submission by the Contractor of the designated performance guarantee. **** The performance requirements are described in detail in the Technical Specification of the CONTRACTING AUTHORITY for lot No 1 - Annex No1.1. *** In the event that the tenderer is not the manufacturer, they shall provide an authorisation letter or other document certifying the right to provide SAP product delivery services and Enterprise Support type maintenance for SAP licensed software for the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria from the manufacturer or from the official representative of the manufacturer for the Republic of Bulgaria. *** The established requirement for authorisation at the tender submission stage is justified by the subject matter of the contract and constitutes a guarantee for its timely and high-quality performance. In the event that a contractor is selected who is refused authorisation by the manufacturer, this may lead to a delay in the performance of the public contract, as well as to its termination. According to the conclusions of the Supreme Administrative Court, "the requirement for authorisation in itself is not restrictive, insofar as it is a guarantee of the quality and reliability of the activity carried out. In standard commercial practice, authorisation takes place on the basis of a contract, which may be directly with the manufacturer or with another economic entity authorised to grant authorisation on behalf of the manufacturer." (Decision No 10859 of 27.10.2021 of the SAC on admin.

case No 6546/2021, VII Division). In the documentation, the condition for authorisation is set broadly, i.e. it is not limited solely to the manufacturer, but also to any official representative thereof. A general authorisation is required, rather than for a specific procedure, and an opportunity is provided for any interested tenderer – partner, regardless of whether it is a Bulgarian or foreign entity, to submit a tender, whereby the aforementioned circumstance can be proven both with an Authorisation Letter and with any other equivalent document that certifies compliance with the established requirement.

sig_4987792da62d9132c76d.description: ThisSources Sought results will assist the Air Force in determining whether this solicitation will be unrestricted competition or a small business set-aside for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to fulfill Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) requirements. The Government is assessing the capability of companies that may possess the expertise to competently and competitively respond to the following requirements for the JSE program: For the JSE Program, the contractor shall possess the capabilities to fulfill 1) development, integration, and testing of modeling and simulation capabilities and 2) operations and product support functions at designated JSE test and training sites. The JSE Program is planning for two major training sites: Joint Integrated Test and Training Center–Nellis AFB, NV (JITTC-N) and Joint Integrated Test and Training Center–Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, AK (JITTC-E). The Air Force is considering a third site in the European theatre. Additional sites may be included as part of this solicitation. These sites will contain most, if not all, of the following: Multiple training systems (JSE-compliant and non-JSE-compliant) developed by other airborne platform program offices and their Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) Many supporting COTS software and hardware components Server rooms hosting JSE software components along with the cockpits support racks associated with the training systems Secure audio/visual distribution systems for mission brief and debrief Secure networks supporting Secret/Collateral, TS/SCI, and SAP information System integration labs supporting JSE development, integration and testing The IDIQ contract will commence within the 4th Quarter of CY27 with a 10-year period of performance. The first task order will be awarded 1st Quarter of CY28 to support JITTC-N including up to a 6-month transition period with the incumbent contractor. The Government anticipates the contract period of performance to be a minimum of a 1-year base period with up to nine 1-year option periods. Further questions may be e-mailed to Contract Specialist Matthew Mercer, matthew.mercer.5@us.af.mil, Contract Specialist James Floyd, james.floyd.23@us.af.mil and Logistics Management Specialist, gregory.zele@us.af.mil. Responses must be submitted via email to Contract Specialist Matthew Mercer, matthew.mercer.5@us.af.mil, and Contract Specialist James Floyd, james.floyd.23@us.af.mil and are due NLT 11:59 PM EST, 15 October 2026. The Government may converse with respondents regarding this RFI. Such conversations are solely intended to clarify potential capability to perform the requirements.
sig_4987792da62d9132c76d.title: Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)

sig_498fcd0ad44752b6eab1.description: The procurement services of the central administration of the City of Turku requested requests to participate in a competitive dialogue procedure, the objective of which is to renew the basic information technology services of the City of Turku for the period 1.4.2026 (target) – 31.3.2031, after which the agreement will continue until further notice. The primary and preliminary subject of the procurement is described in the attachment to the call for requests to participate, 'Project Description'. The procurement also includes a transfer of business, which is described in the aforementioned attachment. The content of the services and functionalities subject to the competitive tendering may change during the negotiations, and some of the services and functionalities may also be put out to tender separately if the Contracting Authority considers it expedient. The Contracting Authority does not wish to limit implementation options or technologies at the beginning of the competitive dialogue procedure. The Contracting Authority wants to give all suppliers participating in the dialogue procedure the opportunity to offer the best solutions by which the Contracting Authority's objectives are achieved. The Contracting Authority is seeking a single primary responsible supplier model. sig_49b174ed1608944e41b2.description: The DigiTVET project is an initiative within the German development cooperation programme "Vocational Education and Training in Jordan" aimed at enhancing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Jordan through digital transformation. The project seeks to improve the accessibility, quality, and relevance of TVET in alignment with the demands of the modern labour market. The overarching goal is to empower the Jordanian Ministry of Education (MoE) and related stakeholders to adopt inclusive, labour market-oriented digital methods in vocational education. The project addresses critical challenges in the Jordanian TVET system, particularly the lack of structured governance and implementation capacities for high-quality digital vocational training. By leveraging insights from previous initiatives, DigiTVET aims to foster a cohesive approach to digital education, ensuring that methodologies are tailored to the needs of diverse target groups, including women and marginalized communities. Key objectives include the establishment of standardised procedures for integrating digital tools, standards and methods into the ministry, enhancing the competencies of educators and management staff, and developing inclusive digital teaching and learning offerings. By focusing on these areas, DigiTVET will contribute significantly to Jordan's 2030 Agenda, particularly in advancing sustainable economic development and inclusive education. The expected outcomes of the DigiTVET project include improved governance of digital vocational training, increased participation of disadvantaged groups, and the establishment of a robust framework for ongoing capacity development within the TVET sector. The module is structured into three outputs: Output 1 aims to develop procedures and structures that improve the use and integration of digital methods at MoE. Output 2 aims to support the development of digital competencies and skills of teachers and managers. Output 3 aims to support selected TVET providers to develop and pilot digital teaching and learning offers in cooperation with private sector and civil society partners, with a focus on disadvantaged groups and regions, including in particular BTEC graduates. Lot LOT-0001: 10009622-Short-term expert pool for technical advice in the field of digitalisation and TVET in Jordan. The contractor delivers services in the following areas of action, which contribute to the project"s outputs and indicators stated above. Service package: Set-up and management of STE pool to support the project"s objective in particular with respect to designing and implementing processes and standards with the MoE as well as learning and teaching offers with selected TVET providers. In detail: - Set-up and management of a flexible short-term-experts pool of international and local short-term experts as a backstopping function for the project and for assignments to contribute to outputs 1and 3 and to contribute to defined indicators with the respective deliverables. - Provide short-term expertise to the partner at the MoE and other relevant TVET stakeholders (incl. expertise to support the development of digital methods and processes; advisory on digital transformation of the Jordanian TVET system with strong focus on MoE, governance, structures and processes; organisational development support; advisory on the current restructuring of the MoE, with particular emphasis on digital aspects, inclusion of digital methods into the MoE system). This also includes advisory on quality assurance (QA) frameworks and accreditation-related processes, including integrating digital aspects into QA; - Provide short-term expertise to develop and introduce a concept, standards/quality criteria, guidelines and hands-on materials for the systematic use of educational technologies, in particular immersive technologies and virtual reality (VR) and AI-supported tools, in the MoE system; - Provide short-term expertise to the contextualisation and implementation of digital and AI readiness assessment frameworks and virtual reality (VR) technology strategies for TVET to the Jordanian context, adjustment where needed to fit the needs of the project and partner. - Assess interventions to establish a VR lab and enable content development at the MoE or a selected school, related procurement and implementation including pre- and post-support of the partner (incl. specific IT-support, hand-over of the user manual, capacity building for the partner, monitoring and evaluation). - Support the design and development of digital learning content for at least 2 selected pilot pathways (including multimedia modules and interactive materials and content, for instance, for immersive learning offers) tailored to TVET/BTEC curricula, ensuring accessibility and pedagogical alignment. - Advise on digitising existing processes, such as in QA and assessments frameworks, including integrating digital aspects and potentially digitising the examination and assessment and considering the existing infrastructure. - Advisory input on the appropriate use of platforms/tools/software/hardware required for piloting and scaling of teaching and learning offers - Provide short-term expertise to strengthening the monitoring and evaluation (M&E) capacities in the MoE and other key partner organisations to enable them to better measure (1) the performance of organisational units, (2) the impact of trainings and other offers and (3) the impact on employment, incl. tools to regularly collect data, monitor the progress and evaluate the achievement of all module objectives and output indicators in line with GIZ Results Based Monitoring Guidelines and the impact matrix definitions. - Assist in collecting, analysing and reporting the data of the project. - Short-term expertise to project partners to sustainably set-up knowledge management and dissemination of lessons learned of project activities and outputs. - Provide expertise through international and national short-term experts for any other identified specific needs of the project and its partners in relation to the TVET reform and digitalisation. - Advise on and supporting the strengthening of inclusion in digital TVET offers, including analysing existing inclusion-related digital initiatives in Jordan, reviewing digital training materials and learning offers for inclusivity, proposing and supporting the implementation of digital measures targeting disadvantaged groups or regions, and mainstreaming the visibility of the inclusion dimension in project implementation. - Provide short-term expertise to partner and project staff to sustainably set-up knowledge management and dissemination of lessons learned of project activities and outputs. - Provide expertise through international and national short-term experts for any other identified specific needs of the project and its partners.
sig_49b174ed1608944e41b2.title: 10009622-Short-term expert pool for technical advice in the field of digitalisation and TVET in Jordan

sig_49c63aeb36e1723ad010.description: The LUKS is looking for a reliable and competent service provider for each of the two lots that best meets the requirements and sets up the respective part of the perimeter security for the LUKS, migrates the functions of the respective existing solution to the respective new solution, and finally commissions the new solution and decommissions and recycles or disposes of the existing one. In Lot 1, the web proxy and the perimeter firewall are to be replaced jointly by a georedundant on-premise perimeter firewall with proxy functions that is capable of taking over the VPN termination at a later date. In this context, it is particularly important to take into account that the configuration of the web proxy has grown organically over years and has been tailored to the special features of the existing web proxy solution. The migration of this configuration and its harmonisation with that of the existing perimeter firewall represents a comprehensive analysis and configuration project for which the tenderers for Lot 1 must bring comprehensive knowledge and expend significant resources. Accordingly, Lot 1 contains some heavily weighted requirements that query the tenderers' understanding of the situation and capabilities. Optionally, a new, additional internal DMZ firewall from the same manufacturer as the perimeter firewall, which can be administered in the same management GUI, including the development of a simple configuration with a maximum of 50 ACLs, is also to be offered in Lot 1. This firewall is used exclusively for layer 3 to 4 access lists and serves to separate the DMZ from the internal infrastructure. In Lot 2, on the other hand, "only" the existing WAF, a BIG-IP from the company f5, is to be replaced by the successor product f5 BIG-IP r5600 "Best Bundle". The existing configuration and the existing modules in use of the existing BIG-IP are to be transferred 1:1 to the successor product with the aim of replacing the existing BIG-IP as seamlessly and quietly as possible. Accordingly, Lot 2 contains only a few requirements alongside the heavily weighted price criterion. In addition, the LUKS already has a highly qualified service provider for the necessary operational services, which is why these are only tendered as an option in Lot 2. Since the total volume of these operational services is well below the thresholds for public procurement, the LUKS reserves the right to exercise the option and commission the successful tenderer with the operational services, or not to exercise the option and continue to procure the operational services from the existing service provider via a negotiated procedure without prior publication. The LUKS aims to manage the solutions procured in both lots independently, i.e., internally within LUKS. Nevertheless, the LUKS requires expert know-how from the successful tenderers in both lots. So that the LUKS IT department can obtain further expert know-how from the service providers at a later date if required, the tenderers also submit roles at pre-defined tariffs in their bids, which they can make available to the LUKS. In addition to this expert know-how, the tenderers for Lot 1 of this tender also show the LUKS what training and, where applicable, certification options for this solution they can offer the LUKS so that the LUKS IT department can operate the solution largely independently after commissioning; this know-how is already available within the LUKS for the BIG-IP. So that the LUKS and its partner facilities can operate the offered solutions for the next 5 years at least, the tenderers submit all additional contracts required for this purpose for licences, maintenance, etc. with their bid and calculate all associated expenditure into their bid. In Lot 2, on the other hand, the existing web application firewall (WAF), a BIG-IP from the company f5, is to be replaced by the successor product f5 BIG-IP r5600 "Best Bundle". The existing configuration and the existing modules in use of the existing BIG-IP are to be transferred 1:1 to the successor product with the aim of replacing the existing BIG-IP as seamlessly and quietly as possible. Accordingly, Lot 2 contains only a few requirements alongside the heavily weighted price criterion. In addition, the LUKS already has a highly qualified service provider for the necessary operational services, which is why these are only tendered as an option in Lot 2. Since the total volume of these operational services is well below the thresholds for public procurement, the LUKS reserves the right to exercise the option and commission the successful tenderer with the operational services, or not to exercise the option and continue to procure the operational services from the existing service provider via a negotiated procedure without prior publication.

sig_4a270e1f30b203ded6d0.description: Framework Agreement for the Call-Off Provision of Associate Trainers: Digital Skills, Management Skills, Marketing including digital marketing and social media, Communication and Soft Skills, Health and Safety, Construction and Trade, Training and Assessment, Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing, HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and bid writing, Accountancy systems, Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation Lot 1: Digital Skills. Digital skills, Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills, data literacy and data management, digital transformation and innovation capability, cybersecurity skills, digital marketing and e-commerce. With the acceleration of digital, the following are also subject areas that are in high demand: Digital skills focus on strong digital communication and collaboration abilities alongside cloud and productivity fundamentals. Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills centre on understanding foundational and responsible AI principles as well as applying process automation tools. Data literacy and data management priorities include the ability to interpret and visualise data effectively and uphold good data governance and ethics. Digital transformation and innovation capability requires skills in digital strategy and change leadership, paired with service design and user centred design approaches. Cybersecurity skills focus on building strong cyber hygiene and user awareness, supported by basic risk management and incident response knowledge. Digital marketing and e commerce emphasise SEO and analytics, combined with content creation and digital advertising to drive engagement and growth. Accredited and non-accredited opportunities ranging from SCQF5 and above requested. Training in widely used, industry standard digital tools- such as Microsoft Teams, OneNote for collaborative working, and digital bookkeeping platforms - is also in high demand. Lot 2: Management Skills. Strategic leadership & future planning, workforce development & talent management, change management and digital adoption, people, leadership & wellbeing management, operational & performance management. Businesses require managers who can demonstrate strong strategic leadership and future planning, workforce development and talent management, change management and digital adoption, people focused leadership and wellbeing management, and effective operational and performance management. Building these capabilities ensures leaders can respond to rapid technological change, manage skills gaps, and support resilient, high performing teams. Training should develop practical management capabilities including project management, change management, managing through crisis situations, supervising hybrid or home based teams, leading and motivating others, and building strong supervisory skills. Programmes should also strengthen interpersonal and developmental capabilities such as assertiveness, change and recovery management, coaching skills, developing individuals, and Insights Discovery profiling to support self awareness and team effectiveness. These subject areas are designed for new supervisors, emerging managers, and those seeking to upskill for career progression. Both accredited and non accredited options should be available. Non accredited workshops can be delivered as half day or full day sessions and should be contextualised to the specific needs of the business, particularly for bespoke contracts or sector specific requirements. Lot 3: Marketing. Businesses require marketing training across a wide range of evolving subject areas, including AI enhanced marketing skills, agile and adaptive marketing capability, data driven marketing and analytics, search engine optimisation SEO, content strategy and digital advertising, customer engagement and trust building, omnichannel and customer experience design, and advanced digital platforms and mobile first technologies. Alongside these, there is growing demand for brand creation and management, communications and PR, marketing strategy development, crisis communications, and video production, as well as understanding the difference between amplification and publication as businesses seek growth, explore new markets, or reposition for new audiences. Practical creative skills such as graphic design — particularly 2D/3D animation and Photoshop/Illustrator upskilling to enhance in house capability and deliver more impactful digital content. Digital marketing and social media skills are increasingly essential, enabling businesses to build visibility, engage target audiences, and compete effectively across fast moving online platforms. Lot 4: Communication and Soft Skills. Communication & interpersonal skills, teamwork and collaboration, adaptability & resilience, emotional intelligence & people skills, leadership & soft aligned skills, customer focused skills. Strong communication and soft skill capabilities to help teams adapt to rapid technological, economic and workforce change, clear and confident workplace communication, active listening, teamwork, collaboration, resilience, adaptability and emotional intelligence, as well as core interpersonal skills such as delivering effective presentations, problem solving, assertiveness and customer service communication. Training to mitigate the widening internal skills gaps and meet the growing importance of adaptability, creativity and strong communication. Seeking non accredited, introductory to intermediate level training, typically delivered in half day or full day formats, allowing staff to quickly upskill in essential, business ready soft skills that support productivity and workforce effectiveness. Lot 5: Health and Safety. Practical, compliance focused health and safety training that ensures staff are competent, up to date and able to manage modern workplace risks. Address gaps in documentation, risk assessments and ongoing training. COSHH Awareness, Human Factors in Health and Safety, IOSH Managing Safely, IOSH Working Safely, IOSH SHECW, NEBOSH qualifications, and broader Occupational Health and Safety training, support with legal duties around safe working environments. Fire risk awareness, mental health and wellbeing, and maintaining workforce competency through regular refresher learning. Alongside accredited options, non accredited, short format courses to provide flexible, cost effective, introductory or refresher training tailored to SME’s operational needs. Lot 6: Construction and Trades. Essential electrical safety and compliance training, including the City & Guilds 18th Edition Electrical Wiring Regulations (full qualification and industry update) and PAT Testing and Inspection & Testing Upskilling for renewable energy systems, EV charging installation, battery storage safety, Lock Out–Tag Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical diagnostics. Ensuring staff remain competent, compliant and able to work safely with modern technologies. These may be delivered through accredited qualifications or short, non accredited practical courses to support flexible, cost effective workforce development. Lot 7: Training and Assessing. Workforce development training that strengthens internal capability, particularly through Assessor and Verifier qualifications, Coaching and Mentoring, and Train the Trainer programmes, enabling businesses to build in house expertise, support staff progression and maintain quality assurance across learning and development activities. Delivered as accredited or non accredited options, offering flexible, cost effective pathways that allow organisations to choose between formal qualification routes or shorter, practical sessions tailored to operational needs. Lot 8: Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing. Safeguarding, Child Protection and Adult Protection training to ensure staff can recognise, respond to and escalate concerns in line with current legislation and best practice. Autism training, including delivery aligned to D&A certificated programmes and SQA certificated courses, supporting organisations to work confidently and inclusively with neurodiverse individuals. Trauma Informed Practice, Mental Health First Aid, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) awareness, De escalation and Behaviour Support, and Professional Boundaries & Safer Working Practices, reflecting an increased emphasis on safe, ethical and inclusive service delivery. All programmes can be offered as accredited or non accredited options, providing flexible, practical learning tailored to organisational and sector requirements. Lot 9: HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and Bid Writing. HR training to strengthens effective people management, support compliance and improve workplace capability. HR focused training in areas such as employment practice, performance management and fair work aligned people processes. Procurement training to help understand and navigate Scotland’s public procurement system, the Scottish Government’s SME and Third Sector Procurement Action Plan (2024–2026), improve supplier readiness and expand SME participation in public contracts. Training for procurement rules, compliance expectations, sustainable procurement requirements and effective use of Public Contracts Scotland. Tendering and bid writing: practical support to build confidence and competence in preparing competitive bids. Training to facilitate understanding of evaluation criteria and improved tender preparation directly and to win contracts. Training in tender structure, evidence development and persuasive, compliant bid writing. Lot 10: Accountancy Systems. Cloud accounting training, including tools to report major internal and external cost savings while simplifying invoicing, reconciliation and reporting. Software including but not limited to: Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Business Cloud. Training for real time reporting & dashboard use, automated reconciliation & digital invoicing, integration of cloud accounting with payroll, inventory & CRM. Automation & Digital Bookkeeping Skills, including AI assisted bookkeeping & categorisation, Automated VAT and payroll workflows Cybersecurity in Financial Systems, including secure logins & multi factor authentication, data backup & GDPR compliant data handling, fraud prevention & financial system risk awareness Digital Taxation & Compliance, including making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT & self assessment, digital record keeping, submission of returns via cloud platforms. Data Driven Finance & Business Partnering Skills, including training for financial dashboards & data visualisation, forecasting & scenario modelling, KPI development & management reporting, business partnering & commercial analysis. Lot 11: Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation. Creative and strategic visual merchandising, high quality customer service and communication and operational retail skills for efficient and profitable store management Visual Merchandising Skills including window display design & in store presentation - creating eye catching, brand aligned displays, store layout planning & product placement - designing customer flow, optimising lighting, and using fixtures effectively to guide purchasing decisions. Understanding customer behaviour & retail psychology. Customer Service Skills for retail, including high quality customer interaction skills- effective communication, problem solving, and managing queries or complaints. Service excellence & personalisation- delivering tailored shopping experiences, a key differentiator in modern retail. Retail Optimisation Skills to improve store performance and operational efficiency, including retail operations management- record keeping, staffing, stock control and security procedures. Maximising retail profitability, including evaluating sales data, identifying improvement opportunities, and applying merchandising strategies. Marketing products effectively - basic retail marketing skills to support promotions, product visibility and brand positioning.

sig_4a6aab5d9b18119b6e22.description: The Citizens' Register Information System was established by Law 4483/2017 (Official Gazette A' 107/31.07.2017) and specifically in Part Four, articles 115 to 124. It was implemented with a view to serving the operational field of the Country's Municipal Registers and Civil Status Registers (including the Special Civil Status Register of Athens) as well as providing interoperability services (data only) to third parties when and if they were mature enough to use them. It went live in January 2018. The subject matter of the contract is broken down into the following axes: A. Reorganisation of existing operational infrastructures B. Enhancement of application functionality C. Modernisation / redesign of subsystems and architecture D. Data completeness actions [para. 1.3 and ANNEX I (para. 2) of the Call for Tenders]. The Citizens' Register Information System was established by Law 4483/2017 (Official Gazette A' 107/31.07.2017) and specifically in Part Four, articles 115 to 124. It was implemented with a view to serving the operational field of the Country's Municipal Registers and Civil Status Registers (including the Special Civil Status Register of Athens) as well as providing interoperability services (data only) to third parties when and if they were mature enough to use them. It went live in January 2018. The subject matter of the contract is broken down into the following axes: A. Reorganisation of existing operational infrastructures B. Enhancement of application functionality C. Modernisation / redesign of subsystems and architecture D. Data completeness actions The need to reorganise the existing operational infrastructures [point (A)] will arise from the provision of a new operating environment (public cloud provider) based on the plan drawn up by the General Secretariat for Information Systems of Public Administration (GSISPA) and the Ministry of Digital Governance. On this basis, IaaS services will be used following the individual terms and policies (Service Level Agreement) to be indicated. A Disaster Recovery Site in full mirroring within the G-Cloud Government Cloud environment will be provided. The full implementation approach will emerge during the Implementation Study. The Enhancement of Functionality [point (B)] includes a series of interventions aimed at enabling the existing system to achieve the maximum degree of interoperability with third-party systems. In order to achieve all of the above and to ensure the completeness of its data, provision needs to be made for the modernisation and extension of critical subsystems of the Citizens' Register in order to achieve the maximum degree of availability and to enhance its Interoperability capability with third-party systems [point (C)]. Enhancing the completeness and correctness of the data ([point (D)] of the Citizens' Register is considered critical in order to support to the maximum extent its interoperability with third-party systems. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, on the basis of the best price-quality ratio. The duration of the contract is set at twenty-four (24) months, including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables, as defined in Para. 7.2 of the Call for Tenders. A detailed description of the physical and financial subject matter of the contract is given in ANNEX I – Detailed Description of the Physical and Financial Subject Matter of the Contract or in another descriptive document of this call for tenders. The subject matter of this contract is not subdivided into lots, due to the architecture of the project and the complementarity and interdependencies, namely the high interoperability requirements that need to be ensured. The subject matter of the project constitutes a single and indivisible whole that cannot be segmented without causing insurmountable problems both in its implementation (time delays) and in the interoperability of its individual structural elements, given that it constitutes a combination of services and works resulting in joint operation in a unified central infrastructure. For this reason, tenders are accepted for all of the services described [para. 1.3 & ANNEX I (para. 2) of the Call for Tenders].
