sig_4ca3d8924629a5d470bd.description: The tender concerns the conclusion of three (3) independent contracts for the supply of IT consultancy services to support the Contracting Authority's ongoing operation, maintenance and further development of a broad portfolio of IT systems primarily for administrative use. The systems support core business areas and are used by a large and varied user group across the organisation. The Contracting Authority requires external consultancy assistance with high specialist knowledge in system development, including advisory services, design, development and further development of solutions based on modern technologies and architecture principles. The services are delivered in close cooperation with the Contracting Authority's own employees and other suppliers and require a holistic approach where security, stable operation and future development are considered together. As part of the task execution, the Contracting Authority primarily uses Microsoft-based technologies and platforms. The tasks therefore require solid experience in full-stack development within the Microsoft technology stack, including, but not limited to, web-based solutions in JavaScript frameworks (e.g. Vue.js and/or Blazor), backend development in .NET (C#) as well as work with relevant database technologies such as MS SQL and/or MongoDB. Furthermore, the use of Microsoft Azure as a cloud platform (PaaS), the use of GIT for version control and CI/CD processes, including Azure DevOps, form an integrated part of the task execution. The tender is divided into three (3) subcontracts, each resulting in the conclusion of a single independent contract. An applicant may only apply for prequalification for one (1) subcontract. The subcontracts cover the following specialist areas: Subcontract 1 – Web technologies The subcontract comprises IT consultancy services regarding the design, development and further development of web-based solutions, including advisory services on technology selection and architecture with a focus on user-friendliness, quality and built-in security. Subcontract 2 – Cloud platform (Microsoft Azure) The subcontract comprises IT consultancy services regarding the establishment, further development and use of cloud-based solutions on the Contracting Authority's cloud platform (Microsoft Azure), including advisory services on platform services, architecture, operation and security. Subcontract 3 – Integration The subcontract comprises IT consultancy services regarding integration between internal and external systems, including the design and implementation of integration solutions with a focus on secure data exchange and stable system support. For each subcontract, the Contracting Authority guarantees an average hourly consumption of 75 hours per month, calculated over a contiguous period of 12 months. The guarantee means that the awarded supplier is assured payment for this average hourly consumption, regardless of variations in the actual monthly consumption. The total expected average hourly consumption, including the guaranteed minimum service, is otherwise estimated at: • approx. 100 hours per month for Subcontract 1 – Web technologies • approx. 150 hours per month for Subcontract 2 – Cloud platform (Microsoft Azure) • approx. 100 hours per month for Subcontract 3 – Integration The stated expected hourly consumptions are indicative only and based on the Contracting Authority's current needs and historical data. The actual hourly consumption may vary significantly from month to month, including during periods of lower activity, for example during holiday periods, and does not constitute a guarantee of a specific monthly consumption. The delivery of services presupposes close and trusting cooperation with the Contracting Authority. It is required that the assigned consultant can attend physically at the Contracting Authority's location in Aarhus as the primary workplace. If the task execution requires physical attendance elsewhere, including in Copenhagen, the consultant must be able to attend according to the Contracting Authority's instructions. The work may be organised as hybrid work, but physical attendance may be required on an ongoing basis and is determined according to the Contracting Authority's needs. The work is furthermore performed on the Contracting Authority's IT equipment. The supplier must also be able to cooperate with suppliers on the other subcontracts and prioritise tasks in accordance with the Contracting Authority's needs. Further information on the content of the task, requirements for the services and the specific competences requested under the individual subcontracts appears from Contract Appendix 1 – Requirements Specification. sig_4ca4a63cb9e7ecf8b7da.description: The EU4Digital initiative supports the digital transition of the Western Balkans and accelerates their integration into the EU Digital Single Market. It focuses on developing secure digital infrastructure in compliance with eIDAS 2.0, enhancing interoperability and improved e-Governance of public services, and supporting business across the region. The Western Balkan Six (WB6) economies Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia have made significant progress in digital transformation. National interoperability platforms now connect key public services, including civil registries, tax systems, health institutions, and business registers, enabling secure, efficient, and user-friendly digital services. By agreeing to implement regionally interoperable digital identity wallets, harmonize trust services, and strengthen regulatory and technical capacities, the Western Balkans Six committed to advancing secure and seamless digital access for citizens and businesses, in line with EU eIDAS 2.0 standards. This project will develop and pilot a regional prototype to demonstrate cross-border interoperability of digital services. Depending on national readiness, the prototype will use either wallet-based solutions or mutual recognition of digital credentials among the WB6 countries. The assignment will strengthen institutional capacities, promote regional collaboration, and provide a scalable model for interoperable digital services. By improving accessibility, efficiency, and trust in cross-border public services, the project contributes to a digitally integrated Western Balkans aligned with EU standards. The project aims to demonstrate secure, cross-border digital interactions, aligned with EU standards, including eIDAS 2.0. The work is structured in three phases: Phase 1: Inception and Review - Establish a common understanding, review prior assessments, identify gaps, and prepare a detailed roadmap. This ensures all legal, technical, organizational and institutional preconditions are in place for co-development. Phase 2: Technical Design, Co-Development, and Deployment - This phase focuses on the co-creation, design, and development of the regional prototype for selected cross-border e-services, ensuring interoperability and alignment with EU frameworks such as eIDAS 2.0 and the European Digital Identity Wallet initiative. The contractor will facilitate technical collaboration in developing the prototype and test it under controlled and live conditions. Phase 3: Evaluation, Reporting, and Capacity Building - Capture lessons learned, document technical solutions, and provide training to WB6 institutions. A final evaluation and scalability roadmap will guide replication, extension to additional services, and integration into national digital strategies. The project strengthens regional cooperation, builds institutional and technical capacities, and provides a replicable model for cross-border e-services. It contributes to a digitally integrated Western Balkans, improving access to efficient, user-centered public services and fostering closer alignment with the EU Digital Single Market.
sig_4ca4a63cb9e7ecf8b7da.title: 81322924-Technical and Advisory Services for Developing and Piloting an Interoperable Digital Wallet based Cross-Border e-Service

sig_4cb3914fcd4a49fb86d9.description: Arrochar, a Scottish beauty spot at Loch Long, was designated a ‘litter sink’ by the Scottish Government in 2017. The problem of litter gathering at the head of the Loch has been getting worse over decades and has reached a point where it creates a damaging effect on the area, its environment, wildlife, visitors, and on the Local Community. Arrochar is perhaps the most publicised but far from the only ‘Litter Sink’ in Scotland. Manual mechanical methods are challenging and costly, and so this Challenge seeks to develop new, sustainable ways of tackling a national issue, starting with Arrochar. Lot 1: . About CivTech CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-6-reducing-teaching-workload

Attachments MORA_Specification_V2.4_20210301_Final_DIST_A A519 .pdf MORA_Specification_V2.4_Revision_Notice_20210301_Final_DIST_A A520.pdf MORA_V2.4_ Specification_Atlas_Rev_F_Final_DIST_A A521.xlsx mora-wsdls-and-schemas-v2.4-DistA-20210225.zip VICTORY-Spec-Doc-V1-9-Dist-A-A787.pdf VICTORY_Architecture_A_DistroA_20190402.pdf -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This Special Notice initially aims to make the Approved for Public Release, "Command, Control, Communication, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance / Electronic Warfare (C5ISR/EW) Modular Open Suite of Standards (CMOSS) Interoperability Requirements Specification" (CMOSS IRS) widely discoverable and available. The intent is to periodically modify this Special Notice to: make additional Approved for Public Release and/or Controlled Unclassified Information documentation discoverable and available (Public download, Transmittal upon Request, or link to Authoritative Sources, as appropriate); broadcast syndicated announcements for events or opportunities of interest to members of the CMOSS-enabled ecosystem The purpose of the CMOSS Interoperability Requirements Specification is to provide a common, configuration-controlled, Science, Technology, Engineering, Experimentation, Test & Evaluation and Acquisition minimum baseline technical requirements document. This allows US Army (T), and Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, Multinational (JIIM) (O), materiel developers and integrators to ensure CMOSS compliant/conformant solutions are over-the-interface(s)-interoperable with other components/systems developed to the same "shalls". The requirements within this document should be incorporated by reference in contracts, citing the document title, revision number, and effective date of publication. 'CMOSS#####' Unique Identifiers (UID) will typically be linked as 'parent requirements' from which materiel system, subsystem, component, etc. 'child requirements' are derived. This CMOSS Interoperability Requirements Specification is under the configuration control of the chartered C5ISR Center MOSA Management Office (MMO). MOSA MANAGEMENT OFFICE RESPONSIBILITIES Coordinate MOSA usage across C5ISR Center Review S&T projects and identify cross cutting opportunities to include MOSA Allocate MOSA implementation funding for labs, experimentation, and matrixed SME support Provide MOSA training for directorate SME’s Facilitate technology transition Manage and mature standards Develop and maintain the CMOSS and VICTORY specifications Develop compliance tools and support compliance verification C5ISR Center lead for standards bodies such as the SOSA(TM) Consortium Coordinate with external MOSA activities Provide MOSA support to the acquisition community Consolidate resource requests for MOSA support facilities and staff Support inclusion of MOSA in policy and programs Coordinate/represent MOSA with external partners CMOSS is a suite of standards to support the reduction of the size, weight and power of C5ISR and EW systems while increasing the flexibility and adaptability of these systems Universal A-Kit Project Managers field capabilities as cards into a common chassis Pooled radio resources such as antennas and amplifiers for Communications, Electronic Warfare (EW), and Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) systems Shared processing resources such as computers and displays Shared data services such as Position, Navigation, and Time (PNT) Foundation for enhanced interoperability and simultaneity between C5ISR systems Reduced life cycle cost through increased competition, smaller logistics tails with common sparing, and upgrading to the latest hardware as parts are replaced Rapid insertion of new technology/capability Attachments 20220310-CMOSS-IRS-v1-1-Dist-A-A518.pdf (Public) and CMOSS Overview 18Mar22 Dist A A758.pdf (Public)

sig_4cfea7ef85d8ad403f01.description: Sanctuary Group is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) with prospective suppliers and other interested organisations operating within the technology services market. This is a broad, multi-service opportunity across an enterprise technology estate currently estimated at approximately 265-300 applications, spanning SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise technologies and supporting both operational and transformational technology services. Sanctuary Group's Technology Directorate has undergone significant change across its operating model and technology estate. Sanctuary Group is therefore assessing sourcing arrangements for technology services that support the delivery, development, transformation and ongoing operation of the estate in 2027. This engagement gives participating organisations an opportunity to contribute market insight and inform potential service groupings, sourcing approaches and procurement considerations before final decisions are made. The purpose of this engagement is to: • Provide an overview of Sanctuary Group, its technology landscape and strategic objectives. • Obtain market feedback on potential service groupings and sourcing approaches. • Understand supplier capability, capacity and appetite. • Explore potential procurement structures, routes to market and commercial models. • Understand mobilisation, transition and service-delivery considerations. • Inform the development of Sanctuary Group's technology procurement strategy. Organisations interested in participating should register with Group Procurement from publication. The supplier questionnaire is intended to be issued with, or shortly after, the notice. A supplier webinar is proposed for early-mid October 2026, with questionnaire responses proposed to close in October 2026. The indicative timetable is set out below. Procurement Objectives Sanctuary Group is considering requirements across a range of technology service areas, including: • Application Managed Services (AMS) • Application Development, Product Management, Project Delivery and Programme Delivery Services • Technology Consultancy & Advisory Services • Data Services (Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Master Data Management, Data Architecture, Data Modelling, Reporting & Analytics, Data Platforms and Storage Management) • Data Integration & Ingestion Services • Cloud Services & Platform Support • Licensing & Software Asset Management • AI, Innovation & Emerging Technologies These services may apply across a range of technology platforms and business capabilities, including SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft platforms and other enterprise applications. The service areas above are indicative and are intended to support market engagement and feedback. The final service structure, grouping, boundaries, scope, sourcing model and procurement approach have not been determined and will be informed by market feedback, commercial assessment, legal advice and governance decisions. Sanctuary Group is interested in approaches that: • Encourage innovation, continuous improvement and thought leadership. • Support effective competition and system integrations. • Enable participation by SMEs, specialist providers and larger organisations where appropriate. • Provide flexibility and scalability to meet changing requirements. • Support efficient procurement and call-off arrangements. • Deliver demonstrable value for money. • Support both business-as-usual and strategic transformational requirements. • Enable access to specialist skills and capabilities when required. Areas where Market Feedback is Sought Sanctuary Group welcomes feedback on: • Service groupings and lotting structures. • Supplier appetite for individual service areas and combinations of services. • Supplier capability and partnerships across individual and multiple service groupings. • The benefits and risks of platform-specific versus platform-agnostic service models. • Suitable procurement routes, commercial frameworks and contractual arrangements. • Commercial and pricing approaches. • Information required to support supplier participation and commercial engagement. • The most appropriate treatment of Data Services and Integration Services, including whether they are best delivered separately, together, embedded within wider services or through alternative arrangements. • Transition and mobilisation considerations. • Supplier participation barriers and opportunities. • Any aspects of the proposed scope or approach that suppliers believe could be improved. • Approaches that maximise innovation, market participation and long-term value. Engagement Activities Sanctuary Group currently intends to undertake the following engagement activities: Supplier Webinar Interested organisations may be invited to attend a market engagement webinar covering: • Introduction to Sanctuary Group. • Overview of Sanctuary Group's technology environment. • Strategic objectives and priorities. • Potential service areas, sourcing considerations and procurement approaches. • Indicative timelines. • Questions and answers. Supplier Questionnaire Interested organisations may be invited to complete a structured questionnaire seeking feedback on: • Service areas and capabilities. • Supplier appetite. • Service grouping and sourcing approaches. • Procurement and commercial considerations. • Procurement vehicle and route-to-market considerations. • Transition and mobilisation considerations. • Participation barriers. • Innovation opportunities. • Comparable market experience. Supplier Discussions Sanctuary Group may invite organisations to participate in follow-up discussions to further explore market feedback or clarify responses where appropriate. sig_4d48aff9cd8685c03c1a.description: Slovenia was hit by severe storms with floods in May, July and early August 2023. Between 4 and 6 August 2023, floods and other damaging events affected all regions of the Republic of Slovenia. Consequently, many landslides were triggered. Heavy floods and rain caused catastrophic conditions in most parts of Slovenia. The number of damage cases for which the sector allocated state aid funds increased in the year 2024 compared to previous years from approx. 600 per year to more than 8000. The critical situation required measures for the rapid adaptation of certain regulations in the field of remedying the consequences of natural disasters. The Act on Intervention Measures for Remedying the Consequences of Floods and Landslides of August 2023 – ZIUOPZP (Official Gazette of the RS, Nos. 95/23 and 117/23) and the Act on Recovery, Development and Provision of Financial Resources – ZORZFS (Official Gazette of the RS, No. 131/23) were adopted. The acts bring essential changes to the method of allocating state budget funds to victims in remedying the consequences of natural disasters on property. The purpose of the geoinformation support is thus to ensure that (1) state aid funds for remedying the consequences of natural disasters and recovery after floods and landslides are paid out in a timely, correct and transparent manner, (2) effective monitoring of the progress of natural disaster consequence remediation and recovery projects will be possible. The subject of the contract is the provision of information support in the implementation of legal provisions and the implementation of programmes for remedying the consequences of direct damage due to natural disasters with the preparation and drafting of a report on the activities carried out in remedying the consequences of natural disasters. The purpose of the geoinformation support is thus to ensure that (1) state aid funds for remedying the consequences of natural disasters and recovery after floods and landslides are paid out in a timely, correct and transparent manner, (2) effective monitoring of the progress of natural disaster consequence remediation and recovery projects will be possible. sig_4dab72d2aefae56cb3fd.description: Liverpool City Council will shortly be going to market to recommission our All-Age Carers Service for Liverpool. The All-Carers Service provides a citywide offer of information, advice, assessment and practical support for unpaid carers of all ages in Liverpool, including adult carers, young carers and parent carers. The service aims to identify carers early, assess needs, promote wellbeing, improve access to services and community support, and enable carers to sustain their caring role, including support with breaks, peer support, training and signposting, in line with statutory duties and local priorities. There will be 5 Lots in this procurement as follows: Lot 1 - Digital Carer Platform, and Information, Advice and Guidance Lot 2 - Adult Carers and Parent Carers Lot 3 - Young Carers, Young Adult Carers and Sibling Carers Lot 4 - Carers Advocacy Lot 5 - Carers Opportunities Lot 1: Digital Carer Platform and Information, Advice and Guidance service. A streamlined and simplified Information, Advice and Guidance platform for carers, with onward referral routes into carers support services. The provision of a citywide, streamlined and simplified access point for carers of all ages through a digital platform, Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) service. Its core functions include: o High quality, accurate, Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) for carers o Initial triage and navigation to the right service, pathway or support - complementing and aligning with existing mechanisms such as Adults and Children's Liquid Logic Case Management System, and consistent with existing pathways and service areas. o Supporting consistent data collection, performance reporting and outcomes tracking o Improving the overall carer journey by reducing duplication and confusion o Providing opportunities for online peer support and connection Lot 2: Adult Carers Service (Including Parent Carers). Holistic support for carers aged 18+ The provision of a single, integrated adult carers offer, including parent carers. sig_4db4a0552335fc52fe83.description:
The Federal Republic of Germany must, in accordance with Article 38 paragraph 4 of the European EES Regulation, establish monitoring that makes the proper execution of border controls verifiable. National logging implementations are developed, expanded and maintained by the Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) using a broad range of XML schemas as part of three Technical Guidelines regarding border and domestic control systems respectively. The aim of the project is to subject these schemas to fundamental analysis, consolidation and optimisation. BSI TR-03156 serves to plan and further develop the overarching processes of sovereign identity management efficiently and securely. With the aid of this, the legal requirement of Article 38 paragraph 4 of the EES Regulation in conjunction with EES-DG §4 and ETIAS-DG §4 to operate specialist logging of border and domestic control processes is fulfilled, in order thereby to comply with the legal obligations of the BSI. Within TR-03156, a breakdown into the logging of event data, systemic communication data and identity data takes place. In doing so, BSI TR-03156 incorporates BSI TR-03121 and BSI TR-03135 as an essential component in the context of biometric recording and checks as well as document checks. In order to implement this logging technically, XML schemas are produced at the BSI and made available to further stakeholders as implementation specifications alongside the Federal Office of Administration and the Federal Police. In order to create a basis for the schemas both for external authorities during implementation and for the BSI for evaluation purposes, standardisation between and optimisation of the Technical Guidelines is to be driven forward. It should be noted in this connection that the Technical Guideline extends over more schema files than are uploaded on the BSI website. The project pursues a structural and holistic standardisation of the log schemas of the above-mentioned Technical Guidelines and Schematron files based upon them, in order to optimise readability and understanding. As a result, all analysis steps and results are to be compiled in elaborated documents. In order to create a consistent basis for XSD modelling, a style guide is to be developed on the basis of BSI TR-03156. Standardised specifications are to be broken down in this document in order to define how an XSD is to be produced for the future. Beyond this, the process for publishing the XSD including its documentation is subjected to quality assurance and likewise recorded in this document. The aim is to ensure a standardised and comprehensible provision of the schemas for internal and external users. A further result of this project is the improvement of Schematron use. By means of Schematron, systematic sources of error in the incoming data sets are found and minimised through semantic checks. The current implementation has been realised in a practice-oriented manner, but must be expanded significantly. A style guide produced for this purpose by the contractor as a result document records documentation of best practice. This is tailored to the existing Schematron test cases for BSI TR-03156. Beyond these clearly defined aims, a contingency of expertise is to be made available. This is intended to ensure the clarification of open questions regarding planned or newly modelled changes or expansions of the XML schemas. Alongside the revision of current models, a basic framework for upcoming logging projects should also be set. The aim is to capture requirements, check technical feasibility and coordinate implementation options. The procedure ensures that new XSDs can be integrated consistently into the existing Technical Guidelines and these can be expanded optimally. sig_4dc8e0d671288e7d8524.description: Cornwall Council is exploring options for software solutions to identify duplicate Accounts Payable transactions prior to payment. Currently, FISCAL Technologies’ NXG product is used for this purpose, however the upcoming contract renewal in June 2026 provides an opportunity to review alternative solutions. This Request for Information (RFI) aims to gather information on available products, functionality, and indicative costs to inform future procurement decisions. All details within this document are classified Confidential. It is intended that the responses supplied will enable the Council to develop a business proposal. Any such proposal would be subject to the development and approval of a business case, and, as such, this exercise implies no commercial commitment. This is not a formal tender document. Participation this soft market assessment does not imply any commercial commitment and will not affect eligibility or prejudice suppliers participating in any future procurement. We anticipate holding 60-minute sessions for suppliers to present and discuss their responses to the RFI from Wednesday 21st January to Wednesday 28th January 2026, though this may change depending on the number of responses. Suppliers should contact Charlotte Metcalfe by email at charlotte.metcalfe@cornwall.gov.uk to express their interest in attending a session and confirm their intention to submit a response. The RFI document will then be emailed on request for completion by the due deadline. All responses must be submitted via email to charlotte.metcalfe@cornwall.gov.uk. Once the response deadline has passed, session invites will be issued to those who submitted responses. These sessions are intended to give suppliers flexibility to steer the conversation and focus on the key elements of their RFI response that they believe represent the most important and value-adding aspects for the Council. Suppliers should be prepared to demonstrate the key capabilities of their system or present a comprehensive overview of their solution. The Council will also take the opportunity to ask questions and provide input during the session to clarify aspects of the response. The deadline for RFI submission will be end of day on Wednesday 14th January 2026. All responses must be submitted via email to charlotte.metcalfe@cornwall.gov.uk. Lot 1: .

Lot 1: procurement of 1 UHD/HD cross-converter(s) (with 1 channel(s) of conversion capability) for MTVA under a sales contract, with Ember+ controllability, 60 months' warranty, as well as support and first-line support as defined in the procurement documents. Lot 2: procurement of 6 UHD/HD cross-converter(s) (with 1 channel(s) of motion-compensated conversion capability per device) for MTVA under a sales contract, with 36 months' warranty, as well as support and first-line support as defined in the procurement documents. Lot 3: procurement of a compact studio video mixer for MTVA under a sales contract, with 60 months' warranty, as well as support and first-line support as defined in the procurement documents. The Media Services and Asset Management Fund (Médiaszolgáltatás-támogató és Vagyonkezelő Alap) plans to expand its equipment fleet to accommodate and integrate into broadcasts the increased and anticipated UHD on-site broadcasts (mainly sports events, Olympics, world championships, overseas feeds, etc.) by procuring 1 UHD/HD cross-converter(s), which is/are capable of performing 1 channel(s) of conversion. The offered device must be controllable under the existing Lawo VSM control system using the Ember+ protocol. It is a requirement that the new device to be procured be fully compatible with MTVA's existing equipment and systems, which are 1080 50 HD-SDI system technologies, and signals and systems compliant with currently used video standards: SD/HD/3G-SDI (HD SDI 4:2:2 SMPTE ST 292-C / SD SDI 4:2:2 SMPTE ST 259). Detailed description of the product to be procured: A total of 1 UHD/HD cross-converter(s) with 1 channel(s) of conversion capability and Ember+ controllability. The Contracting Authority only accepts new (unused, not even operated as a demonstration unit) products, and during performance, it only accepts delivery through domestic official commercial channels, which tenderers must declare their commitment to in their tender. The offered product must form a functioning system in its entirety, fulfilling all parameters and functional requirements specified in the technical description. The Tenderer must offer device(s) that can ensure continuous 7/24-hour operation. The handover of the Hungarian and/or English language installation and operating instructions required for the installation and operation of the offered product to the Contracting Authority is a special condition for the issuance of the performance certificate. The deadline for the delivery of the devices to the warehouse is 90 calendar days following the signing of the contract by both parties, with the proviso that the Contracting Authority accepts early performance. The successful tenderer is obliged to notify the Contracting Authority in writing of the date of the offer for performance (delivery) at least 2 working days in advance. The successful tenderer must provide a minimum of 60 months' warranty for the delivered product, calculated from the delivery of the devices. The successful tenderer must provide 60 months of support and first-line support for the delivered product and system components. As a special condition for the performance certificate, the document ensuring the lawful use of the support and first-line support for the relevant period in connection with the given invoice must be handed over together with the above. The procurement includes software updates, version tracking, major version upgrades, and telephone and online technical assistance. In connection with the unique products representing the reference level, having regard to the provisions of Section 46(3) of Government Decree 321/2015 (X. 30), the Contracting Authority accepts the delivery of products equivalent to the unique products, provided that they ensure the expected quality match as detailed in the procurement documents. In the case of offering a product different from the unique product defined in the procurement documents, equivalence must be proven in the manner defined in the procurement documents, from which the characteristics of equivalence can be determined. The Contracting Authority examines equivalence according to the parameters defined in the Technical Description. Further detailed requirements can be found in the procurement documents and the technical description.; The Media Services and Asset Management Fund plans to expand its equipment fleet to accommodate and integrate into broadcasts the increased and anticipated UHD on-site broadcasts (mainly sports events, Olympics, world championships, overseas feeds, etc.) by procuring 6 UHD/HD cross-converter(s), which are capable of one channel of motion compensation per device. It is a requirement that the new devices to be procured be fully compatible with MTVA's existing equipment and systems, which are 1080 50 HD-SDI system technologies, and signals and systems compliant with currently used video standards: SD/HD/3G-SDI (HD SDI 4:2:2 SMPTE ST 292-C / SD SDI 4:2:2 SMPTE ST 259). sig_4e09f8e1c907edcb8467.description: The acquisition consists of providing all services necessary for the analysis, design, development, configuration, integration, migration and data validation, testing, piloting, implementation and commissioning of an integrated, interoperable, secure software platform adapted to the processes of UAT Dobârlău Commune. The contract includes professional training of staff, handover of documentation, source code, applicable rights and artefacts, technical guarantee for defects in the developed result, and operational services necessary for the operation of the platform for a period of 60 months from the acceptance of the implementation. The contract is unitary from a technical and contractual point of view, but contains distinct financial components related to development and implementation, professional training, and post-implementation operational services. The acquisition also includes the operational services necessary for the operation of the platform for 60 months after acceptance. These services are highlighted and priced separately in the Financial Proposal, are financed from the local budget and are invoiced quarterly after provision and acceptance. Financial separation does not affect the unitary nature of the contract and the Contractor's full liability for the compatibility, security, availability and continuity of the platform. The platform shall fully cover the 65 minimum functional modules and all mandatory requirements associated with them. The minimum 15 administrative workflows are cross-cutting processes implemented via the modules and do not constitute a distinct software component. The platform shall be developed and specifically adapted for UAT Dobârlău Commune, without requiring the full development from scratch of all components and without accepting the mere supply of an unadapted standard product. Libraries, development frameworks, open-source components, COTS components, cloud services, APIs and components or services provided by third parties may be used in its creation. These elements do not diminish the Contractor's liability for the design, integration, compatibility, security, maintainability and unitary operation of the platform. sig_4e0f3a5f7e829612a581.description: The Piedmont Region, within the scope of the Electronic Health Record (EHR), manages radiological images through local and regional PACS systems, but the current architecture is fragmented and poorly standardised across the various Healthcare Authorities. This situation generates inefficiencies, difficulties with updates and suboptimal access to images, especially in clinical contexts where timeliness is crucial. Furthermore, viewing functionalities are limited and not fully integrated with regional digital services and telemedicine. To respond to the new requirements of interoperability, continuity of care and telemedicine, it is necessary to evolve towards a federated, scalable and user-centred platform capable of guaranteeing immediate, secure and integrated access to radiological images. With this market sounding, CSI-Piemonte therefore intends to verify the presence on the market of solutions that meet the aforementioned technical-functional and organisational requirements.

sig_4e16a889a2fa49339fd7.description: The subject matter of the call for tenders is the procurement of state-of-the-art equipment for monitoring meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters. The project will develop an extensive, diverse and modern research infrastructure providing a wealth of data. The equipment will include mobile hydrometeorological radars, a low-frequency lightning detection network, meteorological and fire-meteorological stations, a computer system for meteorological data analysis and archiving, a data collection system for the calibration of meteorological and radiometric instruments, high-precision solar radiation measurement sensors, and hydro-telemetric stations, optical instruments and portable hydrometry equipment. Pre-existing meteorological, radiometric and hydrological measuring structures will be significantly upgraded and expanded, and a new standard fire-meteorological measuring network will also be developed. Self-propelled long-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted medium-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted short-range meteorological radar; Meteorological radar towing vehicle; Lightning discharge and atmospheric electricity detection network; Integrated high-precision system for the simultaneous measurement of the electrical outputs of multiple sensors, with simultaneous provision to a computer for further processing and analysis; Integrated automatic sun tracker for recording direct, diffuse and global solar radiation in accordance with WMO standards; Programmable scanning sky-dome spectroradiometer for measuring direct and diffuse solar radiation; Integrated autonomous modular system for measuring meteorological and/or agro-meteorological parameters
sig_4e16a889a2fa49339fd7.title: Procurement of Specialised Scientific Equipment for the monitoring of meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters

sig_4e2424a700013985c871.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $499M. Individual awards will not normally exceed sixty (60) months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $500K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions and assistance instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Deputy BAA Manager TRISTEN M. CARRIG PETER J. FITZGERALD AFRL/RIGD AFRL/RITGB 525 Brooks Rd 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330- 2558 Telephone: (315) 330-2081 Email: tristen.carrig@us.af.mil Email: peter.fitzgerald.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_4e659c84bfa3b76d4239.description: The purpose of this request for information is to clarify questions related to the street lighting control system and control devices. The aim of the request for information is to obtain comprehensive information concerning the street lighting control system and control devices so that any competitive tendering can be implemented in the most appropriate manner possible. This document is not a contract notice or an invitation to tender, but a specifying market survey, i.e. a request for information as part of procurement preparation, in accordance with section 65 of the Public Procurement Act (1397/2016). The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement of the street lighting control system and control devices. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. Background information concerning the procurement: Based on this procurement, the contracting authority aims to procure a street lighting control system with control devices. The aim of the procurement is to implement a solution suitable for the management of the city's outdoor lighting as a whole, which is based on central-point control and a control system implemented as a service (SaaS). The number of controlled objects is in the order of several hundreds (approximately 600 units). The solution must enable reliable control, monitoring and system management of the lighting via a centralized user interface. The entity subject to the procurement includes the control system, central-point control devices and their commissioning. Field installations of the devices are principally the responsibility of the client's contractor, and the commissioning of the system will be carried out in phases in accordance with the progress of the installations. We are inquiring about your views on the following matters: 1. In your opinion, what is the best way to implement the street lighting control system procurement for approximately 600 outdoor lighting control centres? 2. What does your solution package include and what are its most important features? 3. How are similar solutions generally priced and what do the costs mainly consist of? 4. Which technical requirements are most important for the solution to be compatible and expandable in the future as well? 5. In your opinion, what are the biggest risks or challenges of the project, and how can they be taken into account in the procurement? 6. Comments on the mandatory quality requirements for the lighting control devices and control system presented in appendix 1 Companies interested in the procurement are requested to answer the questions using the Forms form via this link: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/5b4LbR2UAZ
sig_4e659c84bfa3b76d4239.title: Request for information - street lighting control system and control devices for the City of Oulu

sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.description: Aarhus Vand is a utility group that manages water and wastewater activities. In this context, Aarhus Vand owns, operates, and maintains many kilometres of water and wastewater pipes distributed across the supply area. To ensure efficient operation of the pipes, Aarhus Vand requires accurate, updated, and accessible registration of the pipe network. For this purpose, Aarhus Vand needs a pipe registration system. Aarhus Vand wishes for a collective agreement comprising both the licences for the pipe registration system itself and consultancy services for ongoing development and maintenance of the system. Aarhus Vand hereby invites to a market dialogue regarding the above. The purpose of the market dialogue includes determining which systems are on the market that can fulfil Aarhus Vand's factual and objective needs. Aarhus Vand has identified the following requirements as being important in relation to a future pipe registration system. It is important to Aarhus Vand that these requirements can already be fulfilled now. The list is not considered exhaustive: 1. Full support for DANVA's latest models, currently: Dandas 3.1.2, TV inspection and manhole report 3.1.2, Danvand 2.1.2, cables, third-party pipes, and areas 1.1, burst registration 1.1.1. For all models, this applies to all concepts, attributes, codes, relations, and interfaces as well as DANVA's guidelines and data manuals. The system is configurable so that it can be easily and quickly adapted to changes in both the models and the user interface 2. All registrations are saved / data resides in one and the same database 3. The system must support data exchange in XML format. There must be an option for direct updating via e.g. SQL. There must be direct access to data, as well as the possibility of making direct integrations with other systems. 4. Quality assurance. XSD validation, predefined validations, etc., which support pipe registration and work with data, and thus ensure and maintain good data quality. 5. Possibility to work in "jobs" in connection with the digitalisation of an area / project / subject, which can subsequently be upgraded to be the master. That is, so that one does not work in the master until changes have been upgraded to the master. 6. The language in the system must be Danish. To a minor extent, it can be in English. 7. User interface. An intuitive and user-friendly user interface. Workflows must be supported by configurable templates/flows. Must contain a tool for replacing, splitting, and merging objects, e.g. pipes. Must have various construction tools. Must have 3D support. 8. User management via AD integration. Users must be able to have different roles/rights. 9. The solution must have stable and high performance 10. There must be an auto-save feature, or recovery of unsaved work or similar. All market operators who believe they can meet the above requirements are encouraged to register for the market dialogue. FRAMEWORK AND PARTICIPATION OF THE DIALOGUE As a general rule, the market dialogue will take place physically at Aarhus Vand, Hasselager Allé 29, 8260 Viby J. The dialogue is held individually per market operator. Interest in the market dialogue must be reported to Christoffer Larsen at christoffer.larsen@aarhusvand.dk or indkob@aarhusvand.dk no later than 20.10.2025. The dialogue meetings are held in the period from 21.10.2025 to 31.10.2025.
sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding IT system for utility registration in connection with water, wastewater, etc.
