sig_51b648c9b5676cf0069b.description: The subject of this procurement is the support of the GPItiner system, the performance of tasks related to its operation and maintenance, the further development of its functions, and version, legislative and technology tracking by the Tenderer. The Contracting Authority intends to conclude a service contract with the winning Tenderer for a fixed duration of 24 months from the date of signing by both parties, providing monthly flat-rate support services and a total development framework of 444 man-days. Of the development framework, 311 man-days are a mandatory quantity to be called off, while a further 133 man-days may be utilised as an optional framework. The monthly fee services falling within the scope of the tasks forming the subject of the service contract to be concluded as a result of the public procurement procedure (services during the entire contract duration, monthly flat-rate fee in net HUF/month): System support and availability, support as follows: • Performance of help desk services • Availability for the correction of incidents • Version tracking The winning tenderer is required to provide support on working days during a 08:00-18:00-hour period (availability period) for 24 months. The daily fee-based (daily 8 hours) development services falling within the scope of the tasks will be utilised via individual orders from the Contracting Authority (net HUF/man-day). A detailed and comprehensive list of the tasks and their technical content is contained in the technical description provided as part of the Procurement Documents, as well as in the draft contract. The subject of the public procurement is the support, version tracking and further development of the GPITINER IT service management system used by the joint contracting authorities for a duration of 24 months. The GPITINER system is the Contracting Authorities' ITIL V3-based IT service management system, which supports in particular request, incident reporting, access management, approval and IT support processes, as well as the auditable decision-making and workflows related to them. The tasks to be performed within the framework of the procurement are in particular: • performance of support tasks related to the operation and maintenance of the GPITINER system, • provision of help desk service, • provision of incident management and availability services, • version tracking of the system, • technological and legislative tracking of the system, • further development of the system, • updating of documentation, • performance of bug fixing and support tasks necessary for the operation of the system. Within the framework of the support service, the Tenderer is obliged to provide availability on working days between 08:00 and 18:00 hours, and to handle incident reports, incidents and user queries related to the system. Within the framework of the version tracking service, the Tenderer is obliged to regularly make available the latest versions of the GPITINER system modules, and to ensure the technological tracking necessary for the supported operating environments, as well as the updating of the related documentation. Within the framework of the development services, the Tenderer is obliged to further develop the GPITINER system in line with business and operational needs. The developments may be aimed in particular at modifying and expanding workflow, access management, approval, inventory management, reporting, notification and integration functions. The development services will be ordered in the form of a framework amount as follows: • mandatory development framework to be called off: 311 man-days, • optional development framework: 133 man-days. The Contracting Authority is entitled, but not obliged, to call off the optional framework. The optional framework may only be used after the mandatory development framework has been exhausted. The development tasks are called off via individual orders, with content and scheduling adapted to actual business needs. The development services are settled on the basis of man-days actually used. The procurement also includes, in particular, development opportunities related to the following areas: • further development of access management and IDM processes, • modification of approval processes, • development of client-side status and process tracking functions, • development of inventory and asset registration functions, • creation of QR code-based functionalities, • development of notification and workflow functions, • development of reporting and administration functions, • creation of timing functions handling public holidays, • modification of functions related to integrated test environments. The scope of the public procurement covers exclusively support, version tracking and development services related to the GPITINER framework and its modules. The procurement does not include the creation of a new base system, the development of another system or the implementation of developments foreign to the functional framework of the GPITINER system. The detailed technical requirements, SLA conditions, development tasks and contractual provisions are contained in the procurement documents.

sig_51c132b18872eea6c753.description: This notice serves exclusively to conduct a non-binding market consultation in accordance with section 28 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV). The aim of the market consultation is to inform the market about a potential future procurement requirement of the State of Berlin and to gain insights into market availability, product maturity, functional coverage, integration capability and the reference situation of software solutions for AI-supported assistance in housing benefit processing. The subject of the market consultation is the examination of whether software solutions are available on the market that can be operated as an independent module in front of an existing housing benefit specialist procedure, in particular DiWo, and/or in front of an electronic file, without replacing or structurally modifying the specialist procedure itself. The focus is in particular on the following functions: receipt and preparation of incoming electronic housing benefit applications including attachments up to submission to the processing department or transfer/filing towards the specialist procedure or electronic file; AI-supported analysis and evaluation of submitted application documents, in particular checking for completeness and generating notes for the processing department; creation of drafts for letters to citizens, in particular for requesting missing or unclear documents. This notice is expressly neither a contract notice nor an invitation to submit tenders or requests to participate. No procurement procedure is initiated by conducting the market consultation. The State of Berlin is not obliged to carry out a procurement procedure on the basis of the market consultation and is not bound by its results. Participation does not establish any legal claims, in particular no claim to the implementation of a procurement procedure or to participation in any later procurement procedure. Interested companies are requested to complete the provided questionnaire and submit their feedback electronically to schmutzler@syncwork.de by 07.07.2026, 12:00. No binding offers, no complete solution concepts and no price sheets are expected. Short, reliable information on product availability, functional coverage, integration capability, product maturity, reference situation and the possible operating model is sufficient. Supplementary product documentation, data sheets or publicly nameable references may be attached or linked. If individual details are to be treated as confidential from the company's perspective, these must be marked accordingly. The incoming feedback will be used exclusively for evaluating the market situation in connection with the described procurement requirement and will be taken into account within the framework of procurement law documentation. If a procurement procedure should be initiated based on the results of the market consultation, the State of Berlin will take appropriate measures to safeguard equal treatment and to prevent distortion of competition.

sig_51ca053f4b00f3f35fcf.description: We are making Hämeenlinna the best public procurement entity in Finland! Consequently, we want the potential future procurement described in this market consultation to also be the best in Finland. To achieve this, we need the help of operators who value honest and open dialogue with the contracting authority, who enjoy competition and who want to represent the pinnacle of their field. This is a market consultation in accordance with Finland's new Public Procurement Act. All information in this market consultation is preliminary and therefore does not bind Hämeenlinnan kaupunki in any way. PRELIMINARY DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT This market consultation concerns the procurement of an HRD system intended for the management of the City of Hämeenlinna's competence management and development. The contracting authority is planning to renew its current system so that the new and necessary features and functions supporting competence management and development can be utilised more versatilely than before. The procurement includes the delivery of the HRD system and an implementation project with necessary training, as well as system maintenance, support and development services. The services must include, among other things, version updates and regular and continuous development of the system taking the customer's needs into account. The aim is to procure a comprehensive system solution suitable for the city's intended uses that is secure, user-friendly and broadly accommodates the needs of various user groups. The system must support the city's personnel and competence development processes and enable the efficient utilisation of digitalisation in these processes. The solution must also be cost-effective. The system will be procured as a SaaS service. The system to be procured must include and enable the management of key competence management and development processes, such as onboarding, e-learning, training management, competence management, performance reviews, and the management of various qualifications, such as permits and credentials. The procured system is also required to be integrable with the city's other enterprise resource planning systems, such as human resources and reporting systems. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain information on the availability of services and the subject of the planned procurement so that the tendering process can be carried out as appropriately as possible. This notice surveys service providers and information systems on the market and gathers additional information for the procurement. REGISTRATION Interested operators are requested to register their interest in participating in the potential procurement via the Tarjouspalvelu portal. Answering the market consultation is not a prerequisite for participating in any tender process organised later. Registrations are requested to be made by 28.10.2026 at 16.00. OTHER INFORMATION This is not a call for tenders nor a procurement notice, so the publication of this notice does not initiate a tender process, but rather constitutes a market consultation. This notice does not oblige Hämeenlinnan kaupunki to carry out the actual procurement. Failing to answer the market consultation does not prevent participation in any potential tender process, nor does answering the market consultation affect the tenderer's position in any potential tender process in any way. Hämeenlinnan kaupunki does not pay compensation for answering the market consultation or for participating in the market consultation and market dialogue.

sig_51dd928abedab57fcef9.description: The U.S. Military Academy at West Point's mission is "to educate, train, and inspire the Corps of Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned leader of character committed to the values of Duty, Honor, Country and prepared for a career of professional excellence and service to the Nation as an officer in the United States Army." The United States Military Academy is located at West Point, New York. USMA executes research to enhance the education of cadets, develop the faculty professionally, and address important issues facing the Army and the Nation. In addition, the Academy conducts research and analysis in emerging fields that may realize novel or vastly improved Army capabilities. At West Point, research is organized and administered through centers and institutes, most of which reside within academic departments. These centers and institutes, affiliated with each other through the Academy Research Council (ARC), coordinated and supported by the Academic Research Division (ARD), provide the infrastructure necessary to tackle the nation’s and the world’s most challenging problems. Our research centers and institutes bring context to the classroom, are central to our vibrant and pioneering faculty, and are one way West Point connects to the Army and to the Nation. Our students are driven, our faculty is world-class, and through our centers, scholars and scientists thrive and produce their best work. Cadets regularly win Best Paper Awards at national and international graduate-level conferences, our faculty hold fellowships and chairmanships in their discipline's national organizations and our products are deployed to the soldier. In addition to applied research, there are centers and institutes at West Point that focus on other aspects of the USMA mission. The USMA BAA identifies topics of interest to the USMA departments, directorates, and research centers and institutes. These groups focus on executing in-house research programs, with a significant emphasis on collaborative research with other organizations. The groups fund a modest amount of extramural research in certain specific areas, and those areas are described in this BAA. The USMA BAA seeks proposals from institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, state and local governments, foreign organizations, foreign public entities, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for research based on the following campaigns: Socio-Cultural; Information Technology; Ballistics, Weapons, and Protections; Energy and Sustainability; Materials, Measurements, and Facilities; Unmanned Systems and Space; Human Support Systems; and Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Quantum Technologies. Proposals are sought for cutting-edge innovative research that could produce discoveries with a significant impact to enable new and improved Army technologies and related operational capabilities and related technologies. The specific research areas and topics of interest described in this document should be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting.

sig_520da90ad868f6b495a5.description: AsynjaVisph (AV) is an electronic health record system used within primary care in Närhälsan, Regionhälsan (including private care providers within VGR) and Habilitering och Hälsa. The agreement for AV was signed on 7 March 2011 with Lorensbergs Communication AB and covered a baseline period of eight years, with the possibility of extension for a further six years. The implementation of the system took approximately five years. During a new procurement of an electronic health record system for all care within VGR, it was decided that AV would be phased out and replaced with the new system. The newly procured new care information system was prepared for implementation for six years and tested extensively. At go-live in November 2024, a multitude of problems of various characters arose in a short time, which is why a decision was made to pause the introduction of the system. The combined effect of this deployment attempt and the problems experienced by users was that trust in the system was severely damaged. A series of investigations were carried out as a result of this to see if and how the planned new care information system could be brought into operation. In autumn 2025, the result of the investigations was presented with a recommendation not to resume the introduction. In February 2026, the political leadership also made a decision to follow this recommendation. Following the failed deployment attempt of the new system in autumn 2024, the region was forced to revert to the previous system, AsynjaVisph. Following the new decision, there is also no system that will replace it in the foreseeable future. The agreement regarding the AsynjaVisph system does not have sufficient remaining contract term to be able to carry out a procurement and implement a new system. Against the background of the circumstances stated above, it is clear that VGR has not been able to foresee or should have foreseen these at the time of contract award in the procurement of the AsynjaVisph system. There is thus support in 17 chapter 12 § of the Public Procurement Act (LOU) to amend the agreement regarding its term.
sig_520da90ad868f6b495a5.title: Extension agreement AsynjaVisph

The aim of the project is the supply and commissioning of an information system for managing access to the Ministry of the Interior's network infrastructure based on the principle of network security management using centrally managed security policies, including a system for their enforcement within the infrastructure. The AMIS is a centralised tool for protecting the integrity of communication networks; it contains functional components for verifying user identity, for managing access rights, and ensures an audit trail of AAA procedures at the network infrastructure level. Part of the project is the renewal of active components, including the renewal of voice network components, network traffic segmentation, the introduction of dynamic network management in the modernised part of the network, the introduction of a process and tools for assessing network quality, and the verification of the functional architecture of AAA components (Authentication, Authorisation, Accounting) within a testing scope. Part of the project is further the expansion of the central identity management tool (IdM, AD) and its integration into the information environment of the Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic (Economic Information System, EKIS), as well as the separation of certain UIS (Unified Information System) services for selected users of the Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic into a standalone environment. Active Directory, Mail Server (on-prem) and Sharing Environment (on-prem) services for users of the Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic will be migrated to the new environment.

sig_5277a0e2729f55acd4d9.description: Ingeus is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified suppliers to participate in an upcoming procurement for a next-generation Employment Services platform. The solution will support the end-to-end management of participant journeys, from referral and onboarding through assessment, personalised support, intervention delivery, employment outcomes, sustainment and programme performance management. The opportunity encompasses a broad range of functional, technical and integration requirements, including participant engagement, advisor enablement, workflow orchestration, reporting and analytics, accessibility, AI-assisted administration, and integration with external platforms and services. Following an initial evaluation of EOI responses, a shortlist of suppliers will be selected to progress to the next stage of the procurement process. Suppliers selected to proceed beyond the EOI stage will be required to enter into a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before receiving the full tender pack. sig_529fff393d7743a12983.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT This is not a prior information notice, tender request, procurement notice or invitation to participate in a competitive dialogue, and the publication of this notice does not initiate a tendering procedure. A potential procurement notice and tender request will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. This request for information surveys the market and obtains information regarding the procurement during planning. The objective of this request for information is to obtain information on solutions, capabilities and alternative implementation methods available on the market prior to the actual potential tendering procedure. Helsingin kaupunki describes in this request for information needs for maintenance services for artificial intelligence applications. The city develops various artificial intelligence applications, some of which will end up in production and need maintenance. The platforms and technical environments of the applications vary on a case-by-case basis. The applications to be maintained may be based on machine learning or optimisation, or utilise large language models. The provider of maintenance services shall keep the applications in working order. Maintenance includes basic technical maintenance, including version updates of the libraries used. As part of the maintenance service, the Supplier shall carry out monitoring and reporting of the application's operation. Monitoring the accuracy of artificial intelligence models or other similar performance indicators, data and model drift and biases is part of maintenance. Maintenance also includes updating artificial intelligence models and other possible minor development. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the annex “H046-26 Maintenance of artificial intelligence applications”. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We kindly ask you to answer in writing to the questions set out in the annex "H046-26 Maintenance of artificial intelligence applications" as comprehensively as possible by the set deadline. Please state if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. Please specify and clearly mark this information. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to organise clarifying market dialogues with those who have responded to the request for information at its discretion. The contracting authority does not undertake to discuss with all respondents. The contracting authority will organise supplier-specific market dialogues primarily via remote connections in the autumn 2026, if they are considered necessary. Supplier-specific invitations to the market dialogue will be delivered after the deadline of the request for information. The contracting authority will deliver potentially preliminary tender documents for commenting later. The information collected through the request for information and the market dialogue will remain confidential and will be used solely for the planning of the procurement. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The contracting authority does not undertake to be bound by the information stated in this notice or its annexes, but as the preparation progresses, the subject of the procurement and the requirements may change. The answers given in the request for information are not binding on the supplier. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in a later potential tendering procedure. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual tendering procedure. No compensation is paid for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. Provisionally, the tender request is planned to be published at the beginning of the year 2027.

sig_52aff57078f04ecb1222.description: The subject matter of the call for tenders is the procurement of state-of-the-art equipment for monitoring meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters. The project will develop an extensive, diverse and modern research infrastructure providing a wealth of data. The equipment will include mobile hydrometeorological radars, a low-frequency lightning detection network, meteorological and fire-meteorological stations, a computer system for meteorological data analysis and archiving, a data collection system for the calibration of meteorological and radiometric instruments, high-precision solar radiation measurement sensors, and hydro-telemetric stations, optical instruments and portable hydrometry equipment. Pre-existing meteorological, radiometric and hydrological measuring structures will be significantly upgraded and expanded, and a new standard fire-meteorological measuring network will also be developed. Self-propelled long-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted medium-range meteorological radar; Trailer-mounted short-range meteorological radar; Meteorological radar towing vehicle; Lightning discharge and atmospheric electricity detection network; Integrated high-precision system for the simultaneous measurement of the electrical outputs of multiple sensors, with simultaneous provision to a computer for further processing and analysis; Integrated automatic sun tracker for recording direct, diffuse and global solar radiation in accordance with WMO standards; Programmable scanning sky-dome spectroradiometer for measuring direct and diffuse solar radiation; Integrated autonomous modular system for measuring meteorological and/or agro-meteorological parameters
sig_52aff57078f04ecb1222.title: Procurement of Specialised Scientific Equipment for the monitoring of meteorological, fire-meteorological, radiometric and hydrological parameters

sig_533cdd8a885d57e2470d.description: The university currently hosts an on-campus "International Study Centre" which delivers routes to degree courses for international students. The partner provider recruits students and provides options for entry that are taught by the provider and certified by Sussex. At the successful completion of the course students are invited to join their selected course and enrol as Sussex students. https://isc.sussex.ac.uk/programmes This provision is due to expire at the end of academic year 2029/30 (31 July 2030). The university is therefore engaging the market to assist in the formation of our plans for this key student recruitment route. We see this as an opportunity to challenge our assumptions across the board about how we can support potential students and encourage them to enrol at Sussex. To this end while the international student pathway is forming the core of our investigation in this project, we see this as an opportunity to reevaluate pathways across all student cohorts, locations, models and formats. We have recently conducted premarket engagement in our Online Distance Learning space (with a tender proposed for 2026) and across the University we are seeking ways to respond to the increasingly dynamic student market. As such rather than framing specific requirements we have provided objectives and needs to meet. Our hope is that by engaging with suppliers we can be innovative in our response to student demand in collaboration with the market to meet student needs while providing sustainable income and value for money for all involved. Framework agreement for the performance of general market and public opinion research tasks for Nemzeti Média- és Hírközlési Hatóság in accordance with point II.2.4) and the procurement documents. The framework amount of the framework agreement is 450 000 000 + VAT. The aim of the procurement is to understand domestic TikTok users and usage habits, motivations, with particular regard - alongside the relevant regulatory requirements - to child users through public opinion research. During the research, the spread of the application among 16-49-year-olds and the users' usage habits (frequency, time spent, uploading own content), followed channels (by topic), and their development (from earlier, known from elsewhere and followed on TikTok (too), channels followed following recommendations from friends, acquaintances, channels followed from those recommended by the algorithm, previously unknown channels) must be examined. The role of TikTok in everyday life. The use and significance of individual feeds; experiences, impressions. Useful TikTok vs. TikTok serving relaxation. Furthermore, the potential dangers of TikTok must also be examined: data abuse, attempts at illegal data collection, unpleasant situations and expectations, challenges, etc. A highlighted objective is also to examine the attitude and usage habits of 10-15-year-old users according to the above aspects. Prescribed methodology Quantitative research phase It is necessary to carry out a complete questionnaire-based quantitative research on a nationally representative sample in the 18-49 age group, which maps out the scope of users and the detailed questions of usage. - methodology: CAWI N=1000 persons - target group: nationally representative for the 18-49-year-old population of Hungary - representativeness aspects: o gender o age (3 categories) o level of education (3 categories) o type of settlement (4 categories) - sampling: quota requirements and subsequent stratification based on the KSH's latest relevant core figures (2022 Census) according to the representativeness aspects - questionnaire length: maximum 30 minutes The research tasks form part of the following: - sampling and sample design (including the acquisition and use of relevant KSH data), - questionnaire design, consultation with the Client, - questionnaire programming and checking, - preparation, conduct and checking of fieldwork, - data cleaning, - coding of open-ended questions, - weighting of the database, - charting and analysis of data. Qualitative research phase Regarding the 10-18 age group, taking into account both the regulatory difficulties of quantitative questioning and the complexity of the research questions, the application of a qualitative methodology is necessary. - methodology: personal focus groups (12 units, with the participation of 4-6 persons each + moderator) - duration: 60 minutes - participants in separate groups according to the following breakdowns: o girls / boys o 10-12-year-olds / 13-15-year-olds / 16-18-year-olds o residents of Budapest / residents of major rural cities - the research must also extend to active users (those uploading their own content); providing 1-2 persons in a separate group or per group (the Tenderer shall make a proposal in this regard) The research tasks form part of the following: - preparation, - design of screening questionnaire and guide, consultation with the Client, - contacting and organising group members, - compliance with relevant regulatory requirements (obtaining and recording, preserving parental permissions), - provision of a studio location with a two-way mirror designed for this purpose and catering - employment of a professional, experienced (also with children) moderator, - incentivising participants, - providing the opportunity for parents (upon request) to watch the conversation on the other side of the two-way mirror, - providing the Client with the opportunity for online or personal viewing, - recording of results (for internal purposes, no need to issue to the Client) and analysis. Further detailed requirements are contained in the Technical Description and the Draft Contract which form part of the procurement documents.; Objective of the research, research questions The objective of the research is to understand the social perception, reputation of sport, as well as its representation by the media. An important question is to understand in what form, on what platforms the audience seeks and consumes various sports contents. During the research, within the specified target group, it is necessary to examine the reputation of sport according to sports disciplines, the most visited sports websites, in what manner, on what platform the contents are followed. sig_536b19268a0dacc0c406.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of pilot and standardisation studies for the evaluation of a battery of tests designed to measure mathematical, linguistic and scientific research aptitudes under the project "Supporting the accessibility of education for children and young people" (project number: FERS.01.06-IP.05-0002/23). The implementation of the study by the Contractor means conducting research using innovative diagnostic tools to measure mathematical, scientific-research and linguistic aptitudes for children aged 7-17 years. The aim of the subject of the contract is a pilot study (verification of the correctness of the created tools) and a standardisation study (development of norms). The study will be conducted in a mixed format: electronic and traditional (paper-and-pencil). The participants in the study will be pupils aged 7 - 17 years. It is planned that a total of 5 650 pupils will be examined in both stages (pilot and standardisation). The study will be conducted in schools - at the pilot stage, sample selection (in accordance with the Contracting Authority's guidelines) remains the responsibility of the Contractor, while at the standardisation study stage, the drawn sample (main and reserve) will be provided by the Contracting Authority. Questionnaires will also be completed by parents and teachers. The description of the subject of the contract and the description of the method of executing the contract are contained in the Specification of Contract Terms and Annexes. sig_5384da0b14b717ff0ebc.description: Title: Canadian Macroeconomic Data 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Definition of the requirement The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada (OSFI) has a requirement for a subscription to access curated Canadian macroeconomic data covering national, provincial, and regional economies, and Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA) data, delivered via an application program interface (API). The purpose of this Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is to signal the government's intention to award a contract for these services to Haver Analytics. Before awarding a contract, however, the government would like to provide other suppliers with the opportunity to demonstrate that they are capable of satisfying the requirements set out in this Notice, by submitting a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, the government will proceed to a full tendering process on either the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the contract. If no other supplier submits, on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Ability to Provide comprehensive Canadian macroeconomic and financial data covering, at a minimum, national accounts, employment and labour market statistics, inflation and interest rates, monetary and credit aggregates, government finance statistics, business and consumer activity indicators, population and demographic statistics, other major economic indicators required for economic forecasting and financial stability assessment. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide regional and sub-national economic data covering Canadian provinces, territories and major metropolitan covering, at a minimum, employment and labour market statistics, population and migration data, housing and construction indicators, income and consumption measures, prices and inflation indicators where available, regional economic activity and business indicators, and other regional economic indicators required for regional economic analysis and forecasting. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide Canadian residential real estate market information, including home sales activity, prices and price indices, housing inventory and listings, market supply and demand indicators, and other housing market indicators relevant to real estate analysis and financial system monitoring. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and be provided at varying levels including national, provincial and metropolitan areas. • Provide access to a software platform and/or web-based interface for searching, extracting, visualizing, transforming, and downloading data while maintaining data export functionality compatible with common analytical applications • Provide enterprise-wide license available for all OSFI users • Provide Documentation, training materials and user guides, as well as offer technical support, maintenance services, product updates and software enhancements (as applicable) • Provide programmatic access to subscribed datasets through a modern application programming interface (API) that supports automated retrieval of time-series data, metadata access and search functionality, bulk data extraction capabilities, standard authentication and security protocols, integration with statistical analytical and forecasting software, and machine-readable output formats such as JSON, CML, CSV or equivalent. 4. Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement This procurement is not subject to the following trade agreement(s) • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • Revised World Trade Organization - Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) • Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) • Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement (CUFTA) 5. Justification for the Pre-Selected Supplier Haver Analytics maintains exclusive ownership of curated macroeconomic and financial data products, including its user interface and analytical tools, proprietary data structures, series identifiers, concordance tables, historical vintages, and delivery formats. These elements are unique to Haver and are not reproduced or licensed through third party distributors. 6. Government Contracts Regulations Exception(s) The following exception to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work". 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property Ownership of any Foreground Intellectual Property arising out of the proposed contract will vest in the Contractor. 8. Period of the proposed contract or delivery date The proposed contract is for a period of one (1) year, with three (3) options to extend the contract for up to a period of one (1) year. 9. Cost estimate of the proposed contract The estimated value of the contract, including the option periods, is $46,559 USD 10. Name and address of the pre-identified supplier Haver Analytics 60 E 42nd St #3310 New York, NY 10165 United States 11. Suppliers' right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to meet the specified requirements may submit a statement of capabilities in writing to the Contracting Authority identified in this Notice on or before the closing date of this Notice. The statement of capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 12. Closing date for a submission of a statement of capabilities The closing date and time for acceptance of Statements of Capabilities is October 8, 2026 at 2:00 pm (EDT). 13. Inquiries and submission of statements of capabilities Inquiries and statements of capabilities are to be directed to: Cameron Marchand Senior Contracting Officer e-mail: contracting-approvisionnement@osfi-bsif.gc.ca 255 Albert St. 12th floor Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0H2

sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.description: 2M-IT Oy (hereinafter also the "Contracting Authority" or "Client") is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for data-driven management and artificial intelligence services. Organisations providing services under the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) may submit requests to participate in the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All candidates who have submitted a request to participate and who meet the suitability requirements set for candidates will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. The internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system to be established will cover data-driven management and AI platforms, solutions and services, licences, and expert services, as well as various combinations thereof. The aforementioned are to be procured for services produced for social and healthcare organisations, which will be specified in more detail in the call for tenders for the DPS internal competition. Solutions may be procured for use in specialised medical care, primary healthcare, and social services, as well as in support activities related to these tasks. They may be implemented in the service production of 2M-IT Oy as part of the services for one or more clients. In addition, 2M-IT Oy may also procure solutions for the needs of its own business operations. The actual procurements will be made on the basis of separate calls for tenders as internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority will specify and describe its detailed procurement need. The subject of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for data-driven management or AI, software usage rights, licences, and/or an open-source software solution. The subject may also include, among other things, tools for data-driven management, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, and visualisation. The solutions and services to be procured may consist of the supplier's own services and products or services and products licensed by a subcontractor provided through the supplier. In service production, either the Client's existing own operating service and other capacity can be utilised, or this can be included in the subject of the procurement. The subject of expert services can be specified in areas such as: • Data-driven management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data management and governance projects • Concept, data, and interface modelling and architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data pipelines (ETL) and integrations • Knowledge of open interfaces and standards and integrating AI as part of applications • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • Development of AI algorithms into finished products in various technologies • Implementation expertise in various technologies (e.g. Google AI, AWS Cloud computing, Microsoft AI) • User interface and application development (Chatbot etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development • Machine training, converting original material into a processable format, and teaching artificial intelligence
sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.title: Knowledge management and artificial intelligence (AI) services

sig_5395c69466621be49f5e.description:
The subject matter of the contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of an electronic road safety enhancement system in accordance with the provisions of Law 5256/2025, featuring the operation of digital cameras for the detection of traffic offences, for the collection and visualisation of data, and for the additional recording and analysis of road network conditions and traffic flow in the Athens basin, concerning the conditions under which OSY SA vehicles operate. The subject matter of the contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of an electronic road safety enhancement system in accordance with the provisions of Law 5256/2025, featuring the operation of digital cameras for the detection of traffic offences, for the collection and visualisation of data, and for the additional recording and analysis of road network conditions and traffic flow in the Athens basin, concerning the conditions under which OSY SA vehicles operate. In this context, to facilitate decision-making by the competent authorities as well as the collection and automated transmission of traffic offences to the competent body without any intervention or analysis on the part of OSY SA, and for the analysis of traffic flow by recording data regarding traffic patterns and congestion points, the capture of images and recordings by the cameras to be supplied and installed is permitted. The system will utilise modern digital cameras and data analysis, artificial intelligence and motion-detection sensor technologies. By using technologies such as IoT sensors, real-time interconnectivity, big data collection and processing, and artificial intelligence analysis, it will constitute a crucial tool for understanding, planning and optimising the operation of OSY SA vehicles. This tender is conducted following the prior implementation of a pilot recording and offence-certification programme using the same technology and software, for which the required data protection impact assessments have been prepared, as well as impact assessments regarding fundamental rights due to the use of artificial intelligence software. Thus, OSY has already initiated the relevant procedures to secure any required additional measures regarding compliance with personal data protection legislation (for employees and third parties, citizens) and the use of artificial intelligence software. This tender looks forward to the creation of an electronic system for the purpose of establishing a modern and efficient mechanism for the immediate detection and recording of Highway Code offences (Road Traffic Code, 5209/2025, A' 100) in public traffic areas, via camera recording systems, in order to modernise the process of certifying traffic police offences using digital means and, specifically, through the creation of a unified national information system which, by utilising the necessary interoperabilities and special interfaces, accelerates the process at all stages: from the detection of the traffic offence to the final payment of the fine, in zero time in accordance with the standards of other European countries. The operation of the requested system forms part of a modern, comprehensive and digitised system which enhances road safety, makes transport operations safer, improves the safety of transported citizens, passengers and pedestrians, and additionally promotes law-abiding behaviour for the benefit of the broader social interest and road transport service providers, namely OSY. Furthermore, in an environment where increased passenger traffic demands advanced management solutions, the application of the system for recording and analysing road network conditions, traffic flow and traffic offences is expected to contribute significantly to passenger safety and to the upgrading of OSY's overall operations, ensuring faster and more organised passenger service, while offering valuable data for the continuous improvement of its routes and procedures. The purpose of the project is the implementation, installation and commissioning of a system that will enable OSY SA to collect the necessary data on road network and traffic conditions for necessary interventions by competent authorities, as well as online recording of traffic offences by OSY vehicles, analysis of the traffic of vehicles moving in front of OSY SA buses, and structural health of road infrastructures, facilitating the early detection of congestion, the prevention of delays and the optimisation of routes with the ultimate goal of safety and better service for the travelling public, leading to the optimisation of provided services and increased efficiency. The expected results from the implementation of this project are the following: • Enhancement of vehicle and passenger safety (via traffic analysis and the quality of arterial roads). • Reduction of OSY SA operating costs. • Route optimisation (via traffic analysis). • Improvement of passenger service. • Digital upgrading of procedures. • Improvement of existing lines or development of new ones based on actual data analysis. • Facilitation of the State with direct online recording of traffic offences. The system to be procured will be implemented in two hundred and fifty (250) selected buses, which will be designated by OSY SA.

Specifically, all information concerning traffic violations shall be transmitted wherever and however lawfully provided for, and the system must have the capability to cooperate and interoperate with any unified electronic system for the digital recording and management of Road Traffic Code violations and fines, of the competent camera network management body, and of the contractor required to carry out any necessary customisation.

sig_53b182da4d1b84e7fc23.description: NAWCTSD will host a Pre-solicitation Teleconference (mini-Industry Day) for the CH-53E Baseline Configuration Upgrade (BCU) focused exclusively on the Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard. This standard is referenced for the development of software as a part of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. The pre-solicitation teleconference will take place on Thursday, 06 April 2017 from 1:00 - 3:00 pm EDT. The pre-solicitation teleconference will include a dedicated question and answer period allowing contractors to ask any questions related to the FACE portion of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. Answers to the questions generated from this pre-solicitation teleconference will be provided to all potential offerors. However, it should be noted that, all questions to the stated solicitation, unrelated to FACE, shall continue to follow normal protocol, with contractors submitting a completed L-1 Question and Answer Form and emailing it to Nicole Knight at Nicole.knight@navy.mil. All interested TSC III Lot II vendors are welcome to call in to this teleconference and should request the dial-in number from NAWCTSD Contracts, Nicole Knight (nicole.knight@navy.mil) no later than 2:30 pm EDT on Wednesday, 05 April 2017. In this request, include your company name, attendeesâ€TM names, email addresses, phone numbers, and company address to confirm attendance. Subcontractor requests must be requested through the Prime Contractor. All attendeesâ€TM for each company are encouraged to use only one call-in line. The Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard is the open avionics standard for making military computing operations more robust, interoperable, portable and secure. The standard enables developers to create and deploy a wide catalog of applications for use across the entire spectrum of military aviation systems through a common operating environment, resulting in lower implementation costs, standards that support a robust architecture and enable quality software development, more capabilities reaching the warfighter faster, and innovation and competition within the avionics industry. FACE is maintained by The Open Group FACE Consortium, a government and industry partnership to define an open avionics environment for all military airborne platform types. The FACE Consortium is a vendor-neutral forum that provides standardized approaches for using open standards with avionics systems. The FACE Consortium works to develop and consolidate FACE open standards, best practices, guidance documents and business models. The Government has included a brief entitled â€œFACE 101â€? for interested contractors to review prior to the teleconference. A NAVAIR Subject Matter Expert (SME) will present this briefing and attendees are encouraged to download the briefing so that they can follow along as he presents the materials. For more information regarding FACE, including the FACE Standards, FACE Data Architecture, The Open Group Architecture Framework Technical Reference Model, and related documentation, please visit the Open Group website at: http://www.opengroup.org/face. Failure of an offeror to call-in to the conference or to submit any questions will be construed to mean that the offeror fully understands all requirements of the solicitation. Prospective offerors are advised that the teleconference will be held solely for the purpose of explaining the FACE Technical Standard as it relates to this solicitation. All prospective offerors are advised that solicitation N61340-17-R-0035 will remain unchanged at the conclusion of the teleconference, unless this solicitation is amended in writing. If an amendment is issued, normal procedures relating to the acknowledgement and receipt of any such amendment shall be applicable. In no event, will failure to attend the conference constitute grounds for a claim after award of the delivery order. Contracting Office Address: N61340 Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division 12211 Science Drive Orlando, FL Place of Performance: Teleconference Point of Contact(s): Nicole Knight Contract Specialist 407-380-8026 Nicole.Knight@navy.mil Procurement Contracting Officer Robert Orozco Robert.Orozco@navy.mil 407-380-4173

sig_53b318ade7c83473a0de.description: Stage 1 - Conceptual technical solution and design; Stage 2 – Delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of the EWNS of the population at NUTS 3 level across the territory of 16 regional cities; Stage 3 - Achieving a completed operational state of the RC Sofia and transition to TETRA radio communication between the RC and the terminal acoustic devices (TAD) within the city - 349 units of TADs; Stage 4 - Delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of the EWNS of the population in the territory of Sofia Region in 22 municipal centres, Blagoevgrad Region in 13 municipal centres, Kyustendil Region in 8 municipal centres, Kardzhali Region in 2 municipal centres, Montana Region in 4 municipal centres, Pazardzhik Region in 2 municipal centres, Pleven Region in 2 municipal centres, Plovdiv Region in 4 municipal centres, Stara Zagora Region in 4 municipal centres and integration of all newly built systems (EWNS) into the NEWNS, and training; Stage 5 - Optimising the population EWNS of the already built 11 regional cities; Stage 6 - Warranty support. ******************************************************************************************************* This procedure awards a public contract with the subject: "Expanding the scope of the Early Warning and Notification System for the population at the regional level (NUTS 3) for the territory of the country" with an estimated value of 29 398 046,10 euros excluding VAT. sig_541318902a40eec6886f.description: The market consultation serves to examine the market in preparation for a planned procurement project. Upon completion of the market consultation, the results will be evaluated by the contracting authority and incorporated in a neutralised form into the tender documents for the intended award procedure. The subject of the market consultation discussion is intended to be the procurement project "Electronic Patient Record / sectoral IdP / Framework App". KNAPPSCHAFT is a statutory health insurance fund with currently approximately 1.100.000 insured persons, which belongs to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung Knappschaft-Bahn-See association system and is subject to the statutory requirements of a nationwide health insurance fund. The subject matter of the market consultation comprises the following three service areas: 1. Sectoral Identity Provider (sIDP) / Health ID KNAPPSCHAFT is obliged pursuant to §§ 291 paragraph 8 SGB V in conjunction with 325 paragraph 1 SGB V to offer every insured person an authorised digital identity (Health ID). The contractor shall provide and operate the sectoral identity provider in accordance with gematik specifications (including IDP backend, VAU, TI authenticator module and associated systems as well as interfaces) and demonstrate authorisation in accordance with the current gematik product type and provider type versions. At least the following authentication options for insured persons are to be offered: eID with online PIN, eGK with PIN, and ePASS. 2. Electronic Patient Record (ePA) KNAPPSCHAFT is obliged pursuant to § 341 et seq. SGB V to offer every insured person an electronic patient record authorised pursuant to § 325 paragraph 1 SGB V, which must be made available as an ePA-FdV via both mobile and stationary terminal devices (desktop client). The contractor shall offer, implement, and operate the ePA in accordance with §§ 341 et seq. SGB V in conjunction with the gematik specifications – including the ePA-FdV and the ePA backend (record system, VAU, and associated systems and interfaces). The functional scope comprises in particular document management (display, upload, deletion, and download of structured and unstructured documents), permission management (granting and revocation of access rights for service providers), the administration of an electronic medication list (dgMP), as well as representative management. In addition, TI messenger functions in accordance with the gematik specification are to be provided in the ePA framework app, including the receipt and transmission of secure messages in a medical context. 3. ePA Framework App (White-label solution) The ePA framework app is intended to represent the central digital access point for KNAPPSCHAFT insured persons to the electronic patient record and to enable insured persons to manage their health data in an available and data-protection-compliant manner in accordance with gematik specifications. The app is to be developed for iOS and Android operating systems; the ePA desktop FdV is to be delivered for Windows, Mac OS, and Linux. In addition to the core ePA functionality, the framework app is to contain further health services, including the management of preventive medical check-ups and vaccinations, the management of doctor and treatment appointments, the integration of the organ and tissue donor register, as well as the native implementation of the e-prescription app functionalities, in particular the display, administration, and redemption of electronic prescriptions. In relation to this, the contracting authority wishes to contact market participants without obligation and exchange more detailed information. For this purpose, further documents will be made available to the companies participating in the market consultation. Upon completion of the market consultation, the insights resulting therefrom will be evaluated and, where applicable, taken into account for further procurement projects and the procedure directed towards them. Procedure note: See further in section 3.1

sig_5439fdf38566ca016a1f.description: The new State Parliament of the Federal State of Brandenburg is located at the site of the 1959 demolished City Palace on the Alter Markt in the city centre of Potsdam and commenced operation in the year 2014. Alongside offices for members of parliament, parliamentary group staff and the parliamentary administration, it features a large number of meeting and conference rooms. The heart of the State Parliament is the centrally located plenary chamber. The plenary chamber as well as the larger meeting and conference rooms are equipped with complex conference and multimedia systems that were implemented during the construction phase and upgraded during ongoing operations. Given their long service life, the equipment is now largely technologically obsolete and, due to wear and tear, also exhibits declining reliability and functionality, as well as reduced compatibility with current media formats. It is therefore to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps over time through the measure described here. In some cases, components have already been replaced by devices corresponding to the current state of the art. These are to continue to be used and integrated into the new systems. Overview of Equipment The scope of the envisaged measure covers the media-technology equipment of the following rooms: - Plenary chamber with control room, including speaker and interpreter booths - State press conference / visitor room (3-fold partitionable) - 3 meeting rooms on the ground floor - 3 meeting rooms on the first floor (1), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the second floor (2), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the third floor (3) - 1 meeting room (secure against eavesdropping) in the basement - Central control room in the lower ground floor - Mobile sound reinforcement including projection The multimedia systems in the plenary chamber and the other large meeting and conference rooms currently consist essentially of the following subsystems: - Video projections or displays - Cameras with controls (including video follows audio) - Conference systems with delegate units - Loudspeaker / PA systems for playback - Video conferencing systems - Vision mixers / scalers - Media control systems For recording and signal playback as well as for AV transmission, all these rooms are networked via a central control room in the lower ground floor using dedicated infrastructure (fibre optics, etc.) via a digital matrix. In addition, a digital signage system with a large number of screens in a server/player architecture is operated within the house network. The focus of the systems is on high reliability as well as ease of use for users and operators. In particular, virtually all components should be centrally operable and capable of being monitored. The aforementioned systems are to retain their fundamental function and structure, but are to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps within the scope of the measure described here. In this context, it must be noted that all affected rooms are fully utilised almost all year round and that, during the planned renewals or adaptations, only minimal operational interruptions are possible outside of times when no meetings are taking place. Scope of Services, Overview The following services are to be tendered: - Preparation of planning documentation: working and assembly planning in consultation with the client - Procurement, installation, configuration and commissioning of all media-technology components - Dismantling and disposal of old technology in consultation with the client The following additional services are to be tendered: - Cabling (local connection cables in the individual rooms, mainly CAT7) - Commissioning and user-appropriate parameterisation - Briefing / training - Documentation - SLA (service level agreement) where applicable with remote maintenance / remote monitoring / remote control - Suitable spare parts package.

sig_54645b742dc44467f03d.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_54645b742dc44467f03d.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_54875cb2025d149ee78a.description: Procurement procedure via the European open procedure in accordance with the (amended) Public Procurement Act 2012. Contracting Authority The contracting authority for this procurement is the Gemeente Breda. For more information about the Gemeente Breda, please refer to the municipality's website: www.breda.nl. Gemeente Breda uses a software solution to describe its architecture landscape. This is done at three (3) levels: 1. Enterprise architecture; 2. Domain and theme architectures; 3. Project architectures. The purpose of this is to have an up-to-date overview of the current situation and to make the impact of change assignments transparent and translate them into frameworks and advice for the implementation of these changes. Enterprise architecture consists of principles and models that describe the (architectural) design choices at an organisation-wide level that provide guidance for the design of, among other things, business processes, information flows and applications. A domain and theme architecture consists of principles and models that describe design choices related to a specific sub-area within the organisation. This can be thematic or domain-oriented. The gemeente Breda has three business domains: - Social Economic Domain (SED); - Spatial Economic Domain (RED); - Operations and Services (BVD). The domain and theme architectures conform to the enterprise architecture and further elaborate design choices from it to a level of detail that is sufficient for the relevant domain. Project architecture describes the architectural design and impact of a proposed project. In doing so, gemeente Breda follows the municipal reference architecture GEMMA (GEMeentelijke Model Architectuur) as much as possible. The main users are seven (7) architects with full editing rights. In the gemeente Breda, the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) in Topdesk is the source registration for application components, servers, databases, network components, etc. There are currently approximately 400 applications included in the CMDB. In the near future, this number will double because separate cards will be created for the acceptance environment and production environment. In addition, the municipality has the ambition to work increasingly data-driven. Assignment Gemeente Breda is looking for a supplier to provide an architecture software solution. The ideal situation is outlined below. We would like: 1. A multi-year contract that offers room for further development without expansion of the purchased functionality leading to a mandatory procurement; 2. To have an IT performance in which users can easily find their way through large numbers of objects and views; 3. An IT performance that enables users to efficiently manage large numbers of objects and views; 4. To have an efficient IT performance for publishing established architectures; 5. To be able to make a good distinction between current and future state; 6. To have an efficient and automated process to synchronise the repository with source registrations such as the CMDB; 7. To be able to update the GEMMA reference architecture without impact on the production environment; 8. To create the possibility to develop towards a more data-driven architecture function; 9. The IT performance concerns a cloud application. 10. Entering into a partnership with the supplier that goes beyond merely supplying software. Think of help with the optimal use of our software and opportunities for influence via user groups. The assignment comprises: - The supply of architecture software via Software as a Service (SaaS); - At least two (2) environments: 1) Production environment; 2) An environment for testing purposes or experimentation. - Support for user assistance; - Collaboration documentation: An agreed contract; - An agreed Service Level Agreement with additional agreements and procedures regarding service management; - A processor agreement; - An option to purchase additional consultancy at a fixed rate; - The delivery of an agreed implementation plan including a data migration plan; - The delivery of knowledge and capacity to carry out the implementation and migration of data; - Establishing an automated link with the CMDB in Topdesk, partly automated with the DSP model within I-Navigator and other possible future applications; - Training of end-users including advice for use based on best practices. The target date for the solution to be operational is 1 October 2026. Lots This assignment is not divided into lots. Mercell This procurement will be handled exclusively and entirely digitally online via the Mercell platform (www.mercell.com). Extensive instructions regarding digital procurement can be found in the Questionnaires.

sig_548bebeaa534685cdfd9.description: The contract consists of principal project management services for the construction phase of the Rochepinard junction. This project for a new Tours Rochepinard interchange on the A10 motorway is located between the existing junctions no. 21 (Tours centre) and no. 22 (Saint Avertin), around the PS 155 (PR 208+950), and includes the construction of the 4 slip roads and all the junctions and roads necessary to ensure the connection with the local network. This junction is located in an urban area and will be toll-free. It also includes the construction of a Multimodal Exchange Hub (PEM). It also includes the redevelopment and upgrading to current standards of the 2 slip roads of the 1⁄2 existing junction no. 22 of Saint Avertin. The services covered by the contract concern the principal project management services in the study phases starting from the appropriation of the AVP and the Impact Study, the PRO, the G2 PRO/DCE (excluding surveys) then the preparation of the DCE, and the DCE, ACT, G2 ACT, VISA, DET, OPC, AOR, and ITS phases. The services covered by the contract concern the principal project management services in the construction phase. The principal project management mission includes the project management missions for the PRO, G2 PRO/DCE (excluding surveys), DCE, ACT, G2 ACT, VISA, DET, OPC, AOR phases, within the meaning of the MOP law and its implementing texts. The principal project management mission also includes a phase for the appropriation of the AVP and the Impact Study File, and a phase for assistance to the project owner for the ITS (Technical and safety inspection of FCA before commissioning). The description of the works is as follows: -the creation of a complete junction (4 slip roads) but without tolls at the level of the PS155 (PR 208+950) including the construction of the 4 slip roads and all the junctions and roads necessary to ensure the connection with the local network. -the complete redevelopment of the 2 slip roads of the existing Saint Avertin half-junction -the construction of a multimodal exchange hub including 8 bus stop bays and a bus turning area. The operation also includes the following developments (the exhaustive list will be determined in the study phase and optimised or modified if necessary according to technical possibilities): -Construction of the 4 new entry and exit slip roads; -Creation of connection junctions with the secondary network of the roundabout, urban or traffic light type; with facilities for high-level service bus traffic on a dedicated site -Removal/modification of existing junctions on the secondary network; -Integration and construction of lanes reserved for certain soft modes (pedestrians, cycles); -Restoration of roads intercepted by the project (Boulevard Georges Pompidou for example); -Resumption of safety and operational equipment intercepted by the project, on existing structures, main section and existing slip roads of the A10 motorway -Resumption and additions to drainage and construction of new basins, including in the central reservation -Installation and resumption of existing and additional signage announcing the new junction; -The construction of visual and acoustic screens; -the construction of retaining walls -the re-cutting and construction of a lower structure for the restoration of a stream -the construction of an underpass for pedestrians under secondary roads -the relocation of 2 shelters with emergency call stations on the A10 motorway -soil decontamination -utility diversions in an urban environment. The contract holder will have the role of principal project manager and will, in this capacity, ensure the coordination of all additional service providers. A risk and cost management system must be put in place. The candidate must necessarily include specialists in all aspects of the operation as cited. The exhaustive detail of the missions entrusted will be specified in the tender dossier (nature and quantity of works, supplies or services, or indication of needs and requirements), transmitted only to candidates whose application is declared admissible.
