sig_569f3229b02c59376fe9.description: This is Ex-post notification for Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki The University needs one or multiple information systems to support teaching planning and facility processes. In this context, teaching planning refers to a whole which includes • Curriculum design (every four years) • Teaching programme design (every academic year) • Timetabling (including facility booking, every academic year) The system is also able to also support the design and establishment of degree programmes. The information system or systems offered must cover all of these areas and integrations within offered System entity. The University has used a timetabling and facility booking system for more than 10 years. Timetables drawn up annually include information on exact teaching schedules as well as the teachers and facilities assigned to teaching. In addition, University staff and external customers can book the University’s teaching facilities for other purposes (e.g., meetings and conferences). Timetabling is largely reliant on the automated timetable generation enabled by the current system. Currently, we schedule over 200,000 hours of teaching per academic year in our timetabling system, with over 150,000 hours of room bookings in over 400 facilities. The timetabling is carried out by over 100 timetabling officers (usually education coordinators) and a four-person admin team. Timetable planning currently relies heavily on the automatic timetable generation functionality provided by the existing system. With this acquisition, the University of Helsinki aims to implement a unified system that supports several interlinked processes and helps harmonize these processes across the institution. The procurement includes the following components • Deployment project for the Cloud Services • All necessary licenses to run the Cloud Service for four (4) years • Maintenance and Support Services, for four (4) years It must be possible to integrate the information system or systems with other University systems, such as the Sisu student information system. The results of the completed curricula, teaching programmes and timetables, are presented to students and staff in Sisu. This is Ex-post notification for Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki Background of the processes At the University of Helsinki, most degree-awarding education takes place in degree programmes. In addition to degree-awarding education, the University provides non-degree education, including professional specialisation education, specialist training for physicians and dentists, specialist training for veterinarians, non-degree studies and micro-credentials. The University also organises commissioned degree-awarding education. Curricula are drawn up for approximately 110 degree programmes, one doctoral school, the Language Centre and several professional specialisation education programmes. Currently valid curricula contain roughly 2,800 study modules and 10,000 courses. At the University, teaching programmes are drawn up for approximately 110 degree programmes, one doctoral school, the Language Centre and several professional specialisation education programmes. In the academic year 2024–2025, roughly 12,000 courses were implemented. Degree programme design There are four levels of degree programmes: bachelor’s programmes, master’s/licentiate programmes, licentiate programmes and doctoral programmes. Degree programmes may be offered in the national languages, Swedish, English or in multiple languages. Education provided in a degree programme may consist of studies in several disciplines and the programme may have several study tracks. All degree programmes have one coordinating faculty. Degrees are awarded by this faculty. Degree programmes may be shared between several faculties. Degree programmes may also be organised in national or international cooperation and based on agreements which determine programme-specific principles. Such programmes may differ from the University’s own programmes in their principles and practices. The University of Helsinki Doctoral School coordinates doctoral programmes. The director of the degree programme is responsible for the management and quality of the programme together with the steering group of the programme. The duties of the steering group include preparing the curriculum (see Desired outcome for curriculum design) and deciding on the teaching programme (see Desired outcome for teaching programme design). The following steps may be identified in degree programme design: 1. Preparation and planning 2. Decisions 3. Further preparation 4. Changes 5. Termination Curriculum design Curricula are plans detailing the arrangement of education and teaching as well as the attainment of learning outcomes at the University. Curricula are valid for four academic years. The curriculum of the University consists of the curricula of the faculties and the Language Centre. The University curriculum also comprises general University-level policies and decisions regarding studies and studying. The curriculum of the faculty consists of the curricula of the degree programmes under the faculty as well as any faculty policies and decisions which specify the curricula. The curriculum of the degree programme indicates: • The main learning outcomes of the degree pursued in the degree programme and the goal of the education • The degree structure and any study tracks • The learning outcomes, content, coordinators, scope and assessment methods of the study modules and courses as well as equivalencies with courses in the previous curriculum The level of specificity in curricula may vary in parts (including completion methods, schedules, languages of instruction and literature of courses). Curricula are used as the basis of annual teaching programmes. More than a thousand individuals representing unit management groups and similar bodies, thousands of teachers and hundreds of support services employees contribute to curriculum design. The following steps may be identified in curriculum design: 1. Preparation 2. Design 3. Decisions 4. Publication 5. Changes This process may not be linear. Instead, some of the steps may happen in parallel. Teaching programme design The teaching programme for each academic year is a plan for how to organise the studies included in the four-year curriculum to students. Teaching programmes describe and define in more detail the teachers, timing, target groups, language and other similar elements of courses. More than a thousand individuals representing unit management groups and similar bodies, thousands of teachers and hundreds of support services employees contribute to teaching programme design.; This is Ex-post notification for Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki The University has been using the timetable and facility booking software for more than 10 years. The timetable to be drawn up each academic year includes information on the exact schedules of teaching as well as the teachers and facilities attached to teaching. In addition, University staff and external customers can reserve the University’s teaching facilities for other purposes (e.g., meetings). Timetabling is heavily based on the automatic establishment of timetables enabled by the current system. Currently, we schedule over 200,000 hours of teaching per academic year in our timetabling system, with over 150,000 hours of room bookings in over 400 facilities. The timetabling is carried out by over 100 timetabling officers (usually education coordinators) and a four-person admin team. Timetables drawn up annually include information on exact teaching schedules as well as the teachers and facilities assigned to teaching. The timetabling process takes place alongside teaching programme design. The current timetabling process at the University of Helsinki is a combination of manual and automated timetabling. Especially on campuses where multiple faculties operate in the same teaching facilities, most of the timetabling is done through centralised autoscheduling, while other faculties either do their timetabling manually or combine the two approaches according to what best suits the needs of a given academic year. Manual timetabling as well as preparing the implementations and study events for centralised autoscheduling are done mainly by timetabling officers, who work in direct contact with degree programmes; centralised autoschedulings are run by a smaller team of timetabling main users. Most of the timetabling work for an academic year takes place during the preceding spring term, with the majority of timetables published to students by the end of June. Additional timetabling and changes to the timetables go on throughout the year. The following steps may be identified in the timetabling process: 1. Rollover or copying the current academic year’s data to form a basis for the planning of the next one 2. Preparation 3. Timetabling 3.1. Centralised autoscheduling 3.2. Manual timetabling 4. Teachers review the timetables 5. Publication of the timetables 6. Changes to the timetables; This is Ex-post notification for Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki For most of the teaching facilities, non-teaching booking requests are only approved after the majority of teaching has been scheduled. The facility booking system processes facilities that remain vacant once the necessary facilities for teaching have been booked. In the last few years, University of Helsinki have had around 12,000 non-teaching-related bookings per academic year in our teaching facilities, with around 2,000 of them for external customers. There are approximately 430 rooms available, divided into 10 room types. There are approximately 1,000 external customers in the customer register, and around 1,000 invoices are sent out annually. All staff of the University of Helsinki can sign on to a web-based component of the timetabling and facility booking system and view the schedules of all teaching facilities. They can also use the system to find a suitable location for, among other things, meetings. Possible search criteria include time and duration of session, possible repetitions, campus, building, type and purpose of facility, minimum and maximum size of facility, furniture and equipment, accessibility, and whether the search should include rooms belonging to, for example, a specific faculty. Search results again include links to the website with, for example, photos of the facilities. When a suitable facility has been found, users can create a booking request (for one or more facilities at a time, for a one-time booking or a recurring booking). At this point, the creator of the request will enter the title of the session and the organisational unit responsible for it, and they are shown the total cost of the booking. After the booking request has been created, it will be reviewed and approved or rejected by our facility booking admin team. As long as the request has not been processed by the admin team, the creator can cancel it in the system. Currently, students cannot sign on or create booking requests, but they can view facility schedules (with none of the details of the bookings shown). Customers from outside the University can browse and search for teaching facilities which includes links to facility schedules (with none of the details of the bookings shown). Booking requests from external customers are done via an electronic form and the information entered into the timetabling and facility booking system by the facility booking admins. Changes and cancellations must be requested via email. Our current solutions include a built-in customer register for external customers and some billing functionalities, both managed by our facility booking admins. The system must include the Facility Register, Customer Register and possibility several price lists. Solution must also cover all functions related to booking, modifying and cancelling the reservations for facilities. Through the facility booking system, the facilities booked through both timetabling and the facility booking system are invoiced. Invoicing may be targeted at the University’s internal or external customers. The system must also cover reports related to the monitoring facility use.; This is Ex-post notification for Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki Common requirements for the system and implementation project. No price is requested in this section. The requirements set apply to the delivery of the entire system and the implementation project. All general requirements are mandatory for the bid to be accepted. The quality points awarded for the preliminary implementation plan will affect the overall evaluation of the bids.
sig_569f3229b02c59376fe9.title: Ex-post notification: Software solution(s) for curriculum and teaching programme design, timetabling and facility booking for the University of Helsinki

sig_56d2a91a7a0004cf3c55.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $499M. Individual awards will not normally exceed sixty (60) months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $500K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions and assistance instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. sig_56e1c83c5546ab672e39.description: Regional traffic computer centres (rVRZ) are increasingly confronted with heterogeneous, dynamic data streams that go far beyond classic detector data. In addition to established infrastructure-side acquisition systems such as induction loops, radar detectors and video capture, digital data streams from vehicle fleets, mobility services and cooperative systems (C-ITS) are increasingly available. This development promises a significantly higher information density, spatial coverage and up-to-dateness, but presents operational decision-making with new challenges. Existing foundational work and guidelines do not adequately take into account today's variety of dynamic, user-generated data sources. The research project is developing a practical framework with which rVRZ can systematically check, evaluate and integrate heterogeneous data sources into their operational and strategic decision-making processes. At the centre is the comparable assessment of data quality from a wide variety of sources - from classic sensors to floating car data and C-ITS services and OEM data. The work includes requirements analysis using workshops with rVRZ operators, analysis of infrastructure-side and vehicle-generated data, development of a quality assurance concept with standardised metrics, and evaluation in a test area. The results enable regional VRZs to make targeted use of different data sources in operational business in the short term, create transparency for investment decisions in the medium term, and strengthen the position of rVRZs as integrative platforms in the digitalised transport system in the long term. sig_56fc20eb91bcbb6a6bed.description: The competition is for the delivery of an electronic patient journal system (EPJ) for the participants. This involves a complete system for the nursing and care sector in the respective municipalities and shall contribute to the daily operation functioning as optimally as possible. As a starting point, the competition does not include archive core and EPJ for health centres, doctor centres, emergency doctor surgeries, test and vaccine centres, ppt and child protection, but participants have an option to procure such services. The system is to be delivered as a cloud system, with no requirements for locally installed components. The contracting authority shall procure a modern, user friendly and future orientated EPJ system that provides health personnel with effective and secure support in the task system, which contributes to better decision making and increased patient safety. The system shall facilitate seamless information sharing between municipal services, inhabitants and the specialist health service, in accordance with national guidelines and joint systems. It shall support the citizens ́ opportunity to actively participate in their health management and contribute to a uniform and sustainable health and welfare service. Participating municipalities shall have free access to their own data, also when suppliers are replaced. The system must be flexible, scaleable and facilitated for further development and interaction with other actors. Participants in the procurement: - The Kongsberg region (Kongsberg, Notodden, Tinn, Hjartdal, Flesberg, Rollag, Nore og Uvdal, Sigdal, Krødsherad) - Hallingdal (Hol, Ål, Gol, Hemsedal, Nesbyen, Flå) - Øvre Eiker municipality Lier municipality. sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 through a merger of railway and postal omnibus services. Its transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, the Euskirchen district, and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brúhl, and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban population centres with sparsely populated, rural areas. With capacity, competence, and years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region travel reliably and safely – in an environmentally friendly, sustainable, and innovative manner. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated independently and some on behalf of RVK. The transport network encompasses 132 routes with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 routes are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a transport performance of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. In order to successfully drive forward the vision of sustainable, clean mobility in the service area in the future and thus sustainably reduce local pollutant emissions, Regionalverkehr Köln GmbH (RVK) is implementing extensive measures for digitalisation and networking, and thereby more attractive public transport to reduce NOx and other pollutant emissions, as part of its internal "Null Emission" project (https://www.rvk.de/projekt-null-emission). Based on successful projects in the field of sales backend systems with electronic tickets, subscription online (Abo-Online), and digital timetable information, a stable basis for central customer management has already been established. The planned measure of developing a mobility app within the framework of the "Mobility App and Platform" project builds upon these existing structures and must be seamlessly integrated into the existing sales landscape. As part of this new measure, which is particularly tailored to rural areas, a multitude of previously analogue or isolated mobility offerings are to be bundled into an integrated, intermodal mobility app. Both regional and interregional transport services will be integrated to give users seamless access to various forms of mobility. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV). The approval period is fixed until 31.12.2026 and cannot be extended. Encompasses the programming of frontend, backend, and interfaces as well as the integration of the application into the existing system landscape.; Development of a user-centred design concept including UX design, design system, wireframes, prototyping, and accessible design. The results serve as the basis for technical implementation in Lot 1. Both lots are closely related from a technical perspective and will be implemented in parallel or sequentially. The contracting authority coordinates the cooperation between the contractors of both lots to ensure a smooth exchange. In particular, regular coordination and joint review meetings are planned.
sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.title: Digitisation of municipal transport systems for sustainable mobility solutions in rural and urban areas - mobility app and platform

sig_579c4ff897e80e986138.description: Subproject 1: Backup Storage (Hardware) Provision of a highly available, high-performance, scalable, and energy-efficient storage infrastructure for redundant, efficient, and long-term data storage and backup of all relevant Bedag workloads. The platform must integrate seamlessly with the selected backup software from Subproject 2 and support features such as deduplication, compression, encryption, immutability/WORM, last-line-of-defense protection, as well as efficient data transfer to secondary and optional air-gapped locations. The solution should be designed as an economically viable scale-out system and meet the requirements for energy efficiency, operating costs, and capacity expansion over the planned lifecycle. Custom-built backup storage solutions based on generic standard hardware without clear manufacturer responsibility for the overall system are not preferred, but may be considered favorably if the overall concept is convincing. Subproject 2: Backup Software and Associated Infrastructure Implementation of a high-performance, scalable, and user-friendly central software platform for backing up and restoring all relevant Bedag systems and applications, including native integration with the backup storage to be procured from Subproject 1. In addition to the backup software, the solution includes all necessary infrastructure components (e.g., backup servers, proxies, gateways, and other logical components), which will be dimensioned, delivered, and designed by the vendor to support operation in the three environments and two data centers using the same operating model. The software must be able to back up and restore heterogeneous environments (including virtual and physical systems, databases, file services, Kubernetes clusters, and S3 workloads), meet defined RPO/RTO targets, integrate with existing operations, security, monitoring, and ITSM processes, and support modern features such as policy-based backup, role-based access control, multi-tenancy, API integration, and optionally, anomaly detection. The backup software may consist of several logically grouped software components from the same vendor. Subproject 3:AirGap Solution (Optional) Optional implementation of a physically or logically completely isolated backup layer to protect against ransomware, manipulation, and unauthorized access. The solution should enable high-performance transfer of deduplicated data from the primary backup environment to a third, physically separate airgap location and provide sufficient capacity for multiple generations in the petabyte range. It must support defined restore scenarios and be integrable into the operational target architecture (including RPO/RTO requirements, operational processes, and responsibilities). Implementation can be carried out using backup software or backup storage and is the responsibility of the provider. This sub-project will be tendered as an option; Bedag will decide on its implementation based on the tender results and the economic and technical evaluation. Framework Agreement for Support and ICT Services for the Entire Project Term: The provider agrees to conclude a framework agreement for services supporting the operation of the backup solution (all sub-projects).
sig_579c4ff897e80e986138.title: Modernization of the backup infrastructure

sig_57ee5d561469897c12b5.description: The purpose of this Notice is to invite market operators to a Market Engagement Event for the potential future exercise to procure services supporting the development of an innovative obesity pathway in North East and North Cumbria on Thursday 8th January at 10:45 via Teams Integrated Care Board (NENC ICB) is developing a new, community-first obesity pathway as part of the Obesity Pathway Innovation Programme (OPIP). The pathway will support adults with obesity who are waiting lists or at risk of economic activity due to obesity and related long-term conditions. To enable this at scale, NENC ICB is exploring options to procure a digital partner to provide an integrated platform that will act as the digital "spine" for the pathway. The intended service is expected to support the following: 1. Identification and invitation of eligible patients (for example via population-health tools and waiting-list data) 2. Digital referral, consent and triage 3. Patient-facing tools for self-assessment, remote monitoring and behavioural support (including AI meal planning) 4. Role based portals for community pharmacies, specialist teams and programme staff. The platform will need to integrate with existing NHS systems (for example NHS App, GP clinical systems and provider electronic patient records), support high standards of clinical safety, information governance and cybersecurity, and generate data and dashboards required for independent evaluation of outcomes, equity and value for money. This Market Engagement Event is intended to help NENC ICB understand the capabilities, innovations and constraints within the digital health market, and to test our emerging requirements and delivery approach. Feedback from suppliers will be used to refine any future specification and procurement strategy for these services. Additional information: To attend this event please register on Eventbrite using this link: https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/market-engagement-event-innovative-obesity-pathway-nenc-tickets-1978132080302?aff=oddtdtcreator This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal process and not award a contract. The information contained in this notice, including information relating to the nature and scope of the requirements, the service classification of this requirement from the list of CPV codes, is only indicative of the HI NENC's current thinking and is neither exhaustive nor binding. HI NENC reserves the right at its absolute discretion to amend it at the time of issue of any further notices or at any other time. sig_57ef99bd3c7967d8a58f.description: The ICT Support at LAAT is currently provided by a single outsourced support provider who provides a mix of scheduled onsite visits and remote support. This contract will end in March 2027, and so the Trust needs to run a procurement to ensure continuity of service. In addition to this, the Trust is planning a major ICT related investment and commitment to pupil learning by implementing a Trust wide 'One to One' (hereafter, 1:1) mobile device scheme for its students. The Trust has already piloted a 1:1 mobile device scheme using Apple iPads so the Trust understands its requirements clearly. Going forward, given both the scale of the requirement and the need to sustain and develop the programme over five years the point has been reached where a significant procurement exercise is needed to both be compliant with the Procurement Act and ensure best value with a capable partner going forward. Therefore, LAAT is taking the opportunity to go to the market to identify the best innovative and forward-looking partner to work with them in the support, delivery and development of their ICT provision over the next five years providing both the Managed Service Support and potentially 1:1 device procurement and support. Given the significant investment in Apple devices, and based on experience from the pilot 1:1 project, the Trust will require specific training and CPD on the use of Apple devices and education specific applications in the classroom (including, but not limited to, Showbie - which is currently used in the pilot schools) from an appropriately accredited training provider, with 'real-world' experience of Apple devices being used in a 1:1/classroom context. The Trust is open to the MSP providing this training, but the Trust has built up a strong relationship with an existing 3rd party supplier in this area, and reserves the right to continue this relationship to ensure the most effective use of the 1:1 devices and the best outcomes for the 1:1 project. This procurement includes (but may not be limited to) the items listed below. • A core managed service, management of all ICT against an agreed SLA • A Service Desk, available 52 weeks a year including out of hours access providing a 'remote fix' to issues as they are reported where possible • On-site school staffing which suppliers deem necessary to deliver the service and meet the SLA requirements • Support for the Trust's Safeguarding/Filtering solution, Securly • Support for the Trust's Barracuda email security/Anti phishing solution • Strategic advice and direction to the Trust regarding ICT • Responsibility for design, specification, installation, and management of all ICT infrastructure • Supply of goods and services based on an agreed Best Value approach • Management of 3rd parties where relevant to the ICT support • Relevant monitoring, management, patching • Responsibility for ensuring appropriate backup and anti-virus is in place • Regular performance reporting • Support for cybersecurity readiness • CPD and training - digital skills and curriculum as necessary across Microsoft and Apple devices/software • There is an expectation that the provider will support and/or drive innovation • Maintain technical documentation • Maintain operational documentation, for example inventory management and risk registers • Collective partnership targets aligned to the Trust's objectives • In Trust support for the integration and upgrade of the connectivity, communications and security infrastructure as required, including liaising with relevant third parties on behalf of the Trust • Suppliers may be required to deliver a range of technology and change management projects in addition to the providing the core managed service. • Enhanced support during OFSTED visits, Exam periods, and around results days for Exams • The potential supply of a significant amount of Apple iPad devices - currently estimated to be c.2,500 over 5 years o A comprehensive managed service for repair and replacement,  Repair and/or replacement of devices  enrol/re-enrol hardware into the management console • Provision and management of VoIP phones/telephony across the trust Lot 1: .

sig_582b3c08cc2200df1258.description: Espoon kaupunki (hereinafter also the Contracting Authority) requests tenders for an HRM and payroll system. The subject of the procurement is a system as a software service (SaaS), which includes the functionalities of the Human Resources main register (so-called HRM entity) as well as payroll functionalities. The solution must support the various working time forms concerning the City of Espoo's employees, such as office, period and general working time, different ways of organising work, i.e. fixed and flexible working time, as well as collective agreements and local agreements used in municipalities. The subject of the procurement consists of the following service entities: - System as a software service (SaaS) - Implementation and customisation of the service for Espoo - Application maintenance services - System further development and expert services A more detailed description of the content of the procurement is in the appendix of the call for tenders 1. "Description of the subject of the procurement". Based on the competitive tendering, one supplier and one substitute supplier will be selected. The agreement enters into force upon signing and is valid until further notice. The estimated start date of the agreement period is in December 2026. PREPARATION OF THE PROCUREMENT The contracting authority has prepared the procurement by evaluating the alternatives on the market and competitive conditions as well as the methods of implementing the procurement. In the market survey, industry operators have been consulted extensively in writing and through market dialogue, expert views have been utilised, and the division of the procurement into parts and different implementation models have been evaluated. PROGRESS OF MARKET DIALOGUES 2025 In the year 2025 market dialogues were held with three identified potential suppliers. 1) Demonstrating the systems During weeks 12 - 15 / 2025 suppliers were requested to present the systems they have on offer. 2) Commenting on the draft call for tenders The draft call for tenders was sent to the suppliers for comment in two parts (A1 and A2). - A1 comment round: included other documents except for key process descriptions, a summary of report needs, the information contents of the teacher data notification as well as the requirement form regarding the functional requirements of the system. The commenting time was 5.5.2025 – 14.5.2025 and the comments were gone through with the suppliers in supplier meetings during weeks 21 - A2 comment round: included the appendices of the draft call for tenders 1.3, 1.8, 1.9 as well as appendix 5, the requirement form tab Functional requirements. The commenting time was 19.5 – 2.6.2025 and the comments were gone through with the suppliers in supplier meetings during weeks 24. 3) Sent clarifying questions Suppliers were also requested to provide clarifying information regarding the systems' payroll runs, main user services and external HRM solution, the life cycle of the technologies of the systems on offer as well as estimates of the prices of user rights and licences as well as the implementation project to support the definition of the procurement value and budget. PROGRESS OF MARKET DIALOGUES 2026 At the beginning of 2026 a fourth potential supplier was also surveyed from the market, with whom a supplier meeting was held in week 7 to present the draft call for tenders. After the meeting, the same draft call for tenders was sent to the supplier for comment as had been sent to the other potential suppliers, and comments were received on this 5.3.2026. In addition, all four suppliers were requested in writing to provide comments on the updated draft call for tenders 17.3-1.4.2026. The market survey has been carried out in such a way that no individual supplier has been favoured and the survey has been conducted impartially and openly. OBSERVATIONS OF THE MARKET SURVEY The observations obtained in the survey have been utilised in defining the subject of the procurement, setting suitability requirements, and defining the comparison criteria for tenders. Key observations of the survey were also that the market is potentially limited by the requirements of the collective agreements used by the City of Espoo (such as KVTES and OVTES) for an HRM and payroll system. In addition, limiting factors may be Espoo's needs regarding continuous services for payroll runs, the system's duplicated environment as well as integrations. In the preparation of the procurement, the principles concerning market survey according to section 65 of the Procurement Act have been taken into account, and the contracting authority considers that the preparation supports the realisation of competition. DIVISION OF THE PROCUREMENT INTO PARTS The contracting authority has evaluated the division of the procurement into parts. The procurement has not been divided into parts because the system that is the subject of the procurement and the related service form a unified entity, which it is not appropriate to divide into smaller entities. In addition, dividing the procurement into parts would significantly increase the risks related to integrations, division of responsibilities, implementation and unified management of data. The contracting authority considers that not dividing it is justified, taking into account the nature of the procurement, the method of implementation and appropriate execution.

sig_5847009535d552f3195a.description: The primary objective of this procurement is to ensure the continued service provision of a Tenancy Deposit Protection (TDP) scheme or schemes from April 2028 that meet legislative requirements as set out above. The Government's policy objectives for the TDP system are that: • Deposits are fully protected so tenants are assured that their money is safe, and landlords are confident that they are abiding by the law. • Decisions on return of deposits are as quick as possible without compromising on the quality of adjudication and users' trust in the process. • Tenants who fund the TDP system benefit from its profits. • Implementing a streamlined TDP system that is easy to use for all, meaning the sector is encouraged to use the system, and users are aware of and confident in their rights and obligations. • The system maximises VfM for taxpayers and minimises the risk of Government underwriting financial losses of suppliers. The Authority also aims to maintain and improve the service available to landlords and agents, and to improve the overall tenant experience with deposits in the Private Rented Sector (PRS) with an emphasis on continuous improvement. Following previous engagement with the market and sector stakeholders, the Government is minded to simplify the existing TDP system and secure greater value for money. Subject to the necessary legislative and commercial processes, this would involve the following reforms: • Custodial model only • Delivery by a single supplier • Profit-sharing with MHCLG Further details on the proposed requirements and scope will be included in the Pre-Market Engagement (PME) document available via email request (commercialtenders@communities.gov.uk). The Department will also be providing access to a data room document which includes supplementary information alongside the PME document. Please request access via the email address above and you will be provided with a link and/or email with instructions on how to access. Lot 1: .

sig_58526469e55cf19a49f9.description: At BGE, the BIM methodology is currently applied in particular in the planning and implementation phases of construction projects. Various common data environments (CDEs) from multiple manufacturers are used there, which correspond to the individual and "historical" needs of the repository projects (so-called project CDEs; products: Autodesk Construction Cloud (Autodesk), Dalux (Dalux), Eplass (Thinkproject)). These project CDEs are infrastructure-autonomous data management units that have evolved or are evolving from everyday requirements. In the long term, the intention is to standardise and integrate the data and functional scope of the project CDEs and to take into account all structure-dependent BGE processes, so that an end-to-end overall system is created in which the BIM model data is managed and made accessible. This system is to be named BGE-CDE and be a durable and expandable BIM data platform.

sig_586461b18ef3d2dbc89b.description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is hosting an Industry Day/Pre-Solicitation Conference on Wednesday, 14 October 2026. The conference will offer a venue to provide information for an upcoming contracting opportunity, as well an opportunity for a Site Visit. This event is open to Large, Small and Socio-Economic Businesses who are registered in System for Award Management (SAM.gov) for the NAICS Code 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). The Government is planning on issuing a construction solicitation for the design and construction of the Fort McCoy Multipurpose Athletic Field using the Design-Build-to-Budget delivery method. The Project Description is provided under the "Project Information” section of this announcement. This is not a Request for Proposal, an Invitation for Bid, or a Request for Quotation. Therefore, this event is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract nor will the Government pay for information provided to the Government in a response nor pay for administrative costs incurred attending the Industry Day event. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with travel or providing information in response to this announcement. EVENT INFORMATION: Pre-Proposal Conference Time: 9:00 a.m. Central Daylight Time (CDT) - Informational Meeting followed by Site Visit The Pre-Solicitation Conference informational presentation will be conducted on Wednesday, 14 October 2026 at the following location: (Building) 2113 South J Street, Fort McCoy, WI 54656-5148 – Classroom 133 Note: An aerial map is provided for reference under the "Attachments/Links" section of this announcement. Microsoft Teams (Virtual Participation): https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993484250583?p=GyrYlw9YrMGl2gaSOU Meeting ID: 993 484 250 583 Passcode: KB25c38S Dial in by phone: +1 601-262-2433, 317074905# United States, Vicksburg Phone conference ID: 317 074 905# Base Access All interested in-person attendees must provide the following information to the Sponsor/POC below no later than (NLT) Thursday, 08 October 2026 -- First Name, Last Name, and email address. SPONSOR/POC: Kyle Burwitz | Kyle.A.Burwitz@usace.army.mil | (402) 660-6419 (NOTE: The Sponsor/POC provided is only to be contacted in reference to submitting required information for base access. He shall NOT be contacted with questions to obtain information concerning the project and the solicitation, which will be addressed at the Pre-Solicitation Conference.) Please bring a valid driver's license or valid photo ID for each person attending, vehicle registration and proof of insurance in the vehicle to gain access to the base. QUESTIONS: For questions regarding this announcement, please email Bonny.C.Dylewski@usace.army.mil with the subject line "Fort McCoy Multipurpose Athletic Field – Industry Day". Please note that two (2) days following the conclusion of the Industry Day, this posting will be updated to include the Industry Day/Pre-solicitation Conference Presentation. Please “follow” this announcement for any future updates. PROJECT INFORMATION: Multipurpose Athletic Field – Army Combat Fitness Testing This project utilizes a Design-Build-to-Budget delivery method to design and construct a new facility to contain a 54,600 SF multipurpose athletic field at Fort McCoy, Wisconsin. The facility shall consist of a 200 meter rubberized running track and an artificial turf infield (sized according to Army Techniques Publication (ATP) 7-22.01 Holistic Health and Fitness Training requirements) for completing the annual Army Fitness Testing (AFT). Supporting facilities include site development, modification to existing improvements, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, sidewalks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Consistent temperature control inside the facility shall be provided by self-contained systems. ATFP measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Antiterrorism for Buildings will be provided. A life safety analysis of the facility shall be conducted to determine compliance with UFC, IBC, and NFPA codes and standards. A new addressable fire alarm system shall be installed in the facility that is compatible with the existing base fire alarm reporting system. Comprehensive building design services shall be required. Accessibility for individuals with disabilities shall be required. The multipurpose athletic field will be periodically occupied and shall require adequate clearance and circulation for personnel, maintenance and operations. Utility connections and telecommunications system(s)shall be coordinated. The facility shall be designed to a minimum life of 40 years and in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems performance. This is not a continuously used facility, and during periods of non-use utilities will be reduced or disconnected to conserve energy. Botkyrka kommun intends to draw up a detailed development plan for the Moheden resource centre south of the existing residential area for single-family houses in Tullinge at Bertheliusvägen. The Municipality is running the planning work and is also commissioning certain investigations, including an environmental soil investigation. The purpose of the environmental soil investigation is to demonstrate what risks any existing soil contamination may pose to people or the environment, and to provide a basis for the design and cost assessment of future excavations on the site. On the property in question, the establishment of a resource centre is planned, which has created a need to investigate to what extent high concentrations of contaminated substances occur in the soil environment. Soil layer conditions and hydrogeological conditions must be reported. Ground investigation and probing must be carried out. Environmental field and laboratory investigations must be carried out.

sig_58815ae97b4c4c08fd92.description: The Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust requires a hosted and fully maintained electronic orthopaedic Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) and outcomes reporting system / software that can be integrated with the Trust’s Electronic Patient Record (EPR) system to enable seamless communication between the provider and the patients, with minimal administrative support from the Trust, which will ensure that the Trust remains compliant with its statutory reporting requirements. The system / software is to enable the effective, efficient and streamlined collection and uploading of Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMS) and National Joint Registry (NJR) data through a single, streamlined system by the supplier on behalf of the Trust to the below listed locations / registries at the base of this description. sig_58a5f3895f2c527b2cd9.description: This BAA seeks proposals for R&D projects that address the challenges of Subsistence logistics in contested environments, with a focus on Class I (Subsistence Supply Chain) support for DLA. The program solicitation is built on three acquisition and logistics pillars: 1. Agile & Predictive Acquisition: This pillar focuses on what and how DLA procures subsistence for contested environments. It moves beyond standard items to develop rapid acquisition pathways for innovative commercial solutions, such as nutritionally optimized, vacuum-sealed, freeze-dried, and/or ultra-high-temperature (UHT) processed rations with shelf lives exceeding 5-7 years. The goal is to create a diversified, pre-qualified vendor base ready to supply these specialized items on demand. 2. Smart Packaging & Strategic Pre-Positioning: This pillar concentrates on the "materiel" aspect of the solution. R&D efforts will focus on acquiring and co-developing next-generation packaging that is not only durable but also intelligent. This includes packaging with embedded real-time tracking capability, environmental sensors (temperature, humidity, shock), chemical indicators that provide real-time data on the viability, safety, and quality of the food items, and innovative solutions to prolong shelf-life. This allows DLA to confidently "push" and pre-position critical subsistence in strategic, potentially austere locations for extended periods. 3. Autonomous & Resilient Distribution: This pillar addresses the "last tactical mile" of logistics in an AD/A2 environment. The initiative will fund the development and integration of logistics systems for moving pre-positioned Class I assets from secure caches to dispersed units using autonomous platforms (e.g., unmanned ground vehicles, cargo drones). This reduces the risk to human-crewed convoys and ensures supplies can reach the Warfighter even when direct access is contested. Other areas of interest include, but are not limited to Class I (Subsistence) Supply Chain innovations in: Combat Rations: Innovations in individual or group rations, including packaged, pre-cooked, shelf-stable food items or unitized group modules (18 or 50 person). Teaming with combat rations assemblers (e.g., AmeriQual, Baxters, Sopakco) is encouraged but not required. Food Equipment: Technology-based solutions improving energy efficiency, mobility, maintainability, or usability of field feeding equipment. Field Feeding Solutions: Systems to enhance efficiencies and reduce production and transportation lead times for feeding troops in training or combat. Food Footprint/Circular Economy: Solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from food production, processing, transportation, storage, cooking, and disposal, including waste reduction, storage optimization, and lowering costs. Food Innovations: Incremental or disruptive changes to food production or products, focused on existing fielded rations. New products/technologies require collaboration with U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (CCDC) Soldier Center, Combat Feeding Directorate (CFD) as directed by the SUBNET Program Manager. Food Safety and Defense: Risk assessment, prevention, and monitoring to protect the food supply from incidental or intentional contamination. These efforts are often conducted in collaboration with entities like the U.S. Army Public Health Center and CFD to ensure robust and reliable solutions. Garrison Feeding: Improvements to food service at permanent military installations. Nutrition and Health: Advancements increasing nutritional value and accessibility of healthy food options for troops in field or garrison settings. Storage and Packaging Solutions: Improvements in materials or packaging to extend shelf life or enhance food quality. Surge and Sustainment Support: Innovations in production to increase output and support Warfighters during surge events. Water Security: Technology innovations in bottled water or hydration alternatives. Subsistence Supplies Condition Monitoring During Shipments: Solutions for monitoring conditions during transport, potentially involving participation in the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 program. Smart Packaging Technologies: Development of intelligent packaging with embedded sensors or IoT-enabled devices to monitor food quality, freshness, and safety in real-time during storage and transport, enhancing traceability and reducing spoilage. Sustainable Food Production: Research into eco-friendly production methods, such as vertical farming, plant-based protein alternatives, or lab-grown nutrients, to reduce environmental impact and ensure sustainable sourcing for military rations. Autonomous Supply Chain Logistics: Integration of autonomous vehicles, drones, or robotic systems for last-mile delivery of subsistence supplies to remote or contested areas, improving speed and reducing logistical risks. Additive Manufacturing for Food: Exploration of 3D food printing technologies to produce customized, nutrient-dense rations on-demand in field environments, reducing logistical footprints and enabling tailored nutrition. AI-Driven Supply Chain Optimization: Application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to predict demand, optimize inventory, and streamline distribution processes in the subsistence supply chain, enhancing responsiveness and efficiency. Robotics and Automation: a) Applying robotics to the complex task of assembling individual and group rations, such as MREs and Unitized Group Rations (UGRs) to enhance speed, accuracy, and safety in the ration assembly process, b) Innovating the production of military operational rations by integrating advanced automation and robotics, c) Integrating automation into both field and garrison feeding operations to improve efficiency, reduce labor intensity, and enhance safety. Circular Economy Concepts: Aims to reduce the environmental impact of the subsistence supply chain. Research is directed at solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions across the entire lifecycle of food from production and processing to disposal. This includes minimizing waste, optimizing storage to prevent spoilage, and lowering costs. Additional Topics: Emerging or innovative research efforts not listed but fulfilling SUBNET objectives, with a clear statement describing the proposed area.

sig_58c0f58debecc85172dc.description: Hampshire County Council (HCC) is seeking to replace its existing Place, Connectivity & Infrastructure Professional Services Framework (ET14110) by establishing a new four-year multi-supplier Framework for the provision of specialist technical transportation and civil engineering professional services, together with infrastructure development and support services. The Framework aims to provide HCC with continued engineering infrastructure and development consultancy services and allows for provision for specialist technical transportation and engineering services. The Framework includes but is not limited to the following technical professional services: Lot A - Multi-Disciplinary Services • Sustainable and accessible transport infrastructure planning services • Highways, Transportation, Civil and Structural engineering design services • Design and advice services under Section 278 and 38 of the Highways Act (1980) • Construction estimating, commercial and financial management services • Safety audit, engineering and management • Waste infrastructure and development design services • Flood and water management and drainage design services • Ecological and environmental services • Landscape architecture and design services • Sustainable and community integration strategic planning • Infrastructure technology strategy and design services • Intelligent traffic systems design and advice services • Building Information Modelling (BIM) services B1 - Engineering Design Specialisms • Bridge and Structural inspections including masonry, reinforced concrete, post tensioned and steel structures • Infrastructure design services covering developments, minor and specialist street and transportation design services • Inclusive and Public Realm Design, including transport design services • 3D and BIM modelling and Visualisations and animations (for engagement purposes) • Flood and water management services including hydraulic modelling • LLFAs support and design services • Highways drainage design services including SuDs • Development drainage assessment services and design checking services • Design of small scale waste water treatment plants B2 - Transport Planning Specialisms • Active Travel and healthy streets, including walking and cycling design specialisms, Pedestrian wayfinding signage strategies and Urban area cycle network strategies • Accessible infrastructure and planning services including inclusive design, low traffic neighbourhoods and school streets • Future mobility planning services (including local mobility hubs, e-mobility solutions, electric vehicle charging etc.) and Low carbon approaches • Travel Data and Modelling including Walking and cycling data, Travel and journey modelling, Car parking data, Intelligent traffic data (including queue surveys), TAG Compliant traffic modelling and Real time journey information visualisations, business engagement • Planning including school travel planning, local travel plans and support • Business case development and Scheme economic appraisal including Cost Benefit Analysis services, Sustainability appraisals • Bid application preparations including DfT Full Business Case services, Specialist business case and funding bid support • Master planning services including Land use / spatial planning services • Associated general research services B3 - Strategic Planning Specialism • Planning application support services • Planning appeals support services • Town & Country planning Act support services • Strategic & spatial planning services • Developer and stakeholder engagement services B4 - Environmental, Sustainability and Decarbonisation Specialisms • Air quality zone modelling & assessment • Air quality, health and environmental research services (in the context of transport) • Modelling and advice services • Action plan support services (in the context of transport) • Vehicle emission modelling / simulation services • Sustainable travel and transport consultancy services & decarbonisation, including Carbon offsetting advice • Health impact surveys and assessments including noise monitoring • Waste management planning • Environmental audits and Socio-economic appraisals • Environmental survey, inspection and supervision services including Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) B5 - Ecological, Landscape & Arboriculture Specialisms • Landscape design & management services • Arboriculture planting & management advice • Arboriculture surveys & assessments including TPO & felling advice • Arboriculture and landscape survey, inspection and supervision services • Ecological & habitat assessments and surveys • Ecological appraisals and Ecological Impact Assessments • Protected species surveys & assessment, for animals including but not limited to otters, bats, dormice, etc., or for birds • Ecological survey, inspection and supervision services B6 - Advice and Community Engagement for Active Travel Specialism • Community engagement services for sustainable travel, such as surveys, school streets, community events • Applying behavioural change science for sustainable travel solutions • School engagement services for active travel including cycling and walking B7 - Traffic Management, Traffic Order and Parking Consultancy • Traffic Orders - drafting, consolidation, TRO reviews, variations and amendments • Digital TRO mapping – Interface with Traffic Order management software • Signs and lining reviews – including Parking, Speed Limits, Movement Restrictions • Parking reviews including On-road and Off-road parking and resident parking schemes • Moving Traffic Enforcement – development and delivery of schemes. • Low cost Traffic Management measures B8 - Street Lighting Design Specialism • Scoping/feasibility of street lighting projects • Preliminary and detailed design of lighting schemes, including drawings and schedules, to British and EU standards • Lighting designs to meet planning consent/conditions, including minimising impact on local ecology • S278 and S38 street lighting designs with accompanying PFI Certificate of Approval • Support PFI Street Lighting accrual process The new Framework will be divided into nine separate lots. Lot A will deliver larger scale multi-disciplinary consultancy services and Lot B will be sub dividend into eight smaller-scale specialist consultancy services. sig_58ce2f3dfda25d000d07.description: The subject matter of the contract is a retrospective evaluation of the process for drawing up the Deutschlandtakt target timetable and its updating, which highlights the strengths and weaknesses of the process – also with regard to the additional infrastructure derivations as well as recommendations for action to optimise the process. The efficiency, resilience and economic viability of the planning and participation process and the results are examined in the process. As a result, optimisation potentials for the planning process for the further development of the Deutschlandtakt target timetable are to be shown and recommendations for action for process optimisation are to be given, in particular for the regular updating of the target timetable. The aim is to incorporate experience from the past regarding the creation of the Deutschlandtakt target timetable and its updating into the future design of rail infrastructure planning within the framework of the cross-modal Federal Transport Infrastructure Plan. With the findings from the evaluation, a planning logic that is balanced in terms of effectiveness and efficiency can be developed, which provides for equal planning of all modes of transport on the rail network. This makes it possible to answer the question of whether and how timetable-based infrastructure development should continue to be used in Federal Transport Infrastructure Planning for the rail sector. Details can be found in the electronically provided tender documents.
sig_58ce2f3dfda25d000d07.title: 6#0040/E21 Evaluation of the timetable-based infrastructure development procedure based on the Deutschlandtakt target timetable

sig_5938fb883ca947d81294.description: Description SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy’s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company’s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click “My Profile”, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand “E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)”, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click “Send.” For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Classified material will be dispatched via USPS Registered Mail (or Government-approved commercial express carrier authorized for Secret transport). A double-envelope system will be utilized. The outer envelope will feature no classification markings. A signed Classified Material Receipt will be enclosed in the inner envelope. The Recipient must execute and return this receipt to the Government within five (5) business days of delivery. Detailed instructions for proposal preparation and submission are specified in Section L of the solicitation document provided on the secure E-TIC portal. sig_59675e8157d563b8ba20.description:
The general objective of the contract is to support the AM PR BI programme evaluation experts in ensuring the quality of evaluation reports, creating and fostering an evaluation culture, and developing the stakeholders' programme evaluation capacity. The specific objectives of the Contract are as follows: - Assistance in drawing up the specifications for the following 3 evaluations: Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Supporting the staff of the PR BI Programme Evaluation Office (BEP) in managing the evaluation reports provided for in the Evaluation Plan (EP) and in carrying out other programme evaluation activities, monitoring the progress of evaluations, participating in meetings with the Evaluator, providing methodological guidance throughout the implementation of each evaluation, including by drawing up quality check grids for evaluation reports and validating evaluation results. The service provider shall provide views, observations and proposals for improvement, and shall methodologically and technically validate the evaluation reports (initial, interim, final, as appropriate) for the following 4 evaluations: Evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027, Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Consolidating the transfer of learning from the evaluation process in order to create and develop the capacity and evaluation culture of stakeholders by carrying out training for BEP programme evaluation experts, members of the Evaluation Coordination Committee (ECC) and other persons involved in the field of programme evaluation. Results of the contract: - 3 proposals for specifications, including evaluation factors, details of expert teams, requirements regarding the quality of evaluations and methodologies used, for the following evaluations: Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - Minimum 8 – maximum 12 Quality reports on the analysis of the initial, interim and final evaluation reports for the four evaluations, 4 Checklists for initial reports and 4 Evaluation report quality check grids; the number of working versions for the quality reports may vary depending on the report versions submitted by the evaluator. The service provider shall complete an evaluation list / check grid for each version of the programme evaluation reports, and the grids for the final reports shall be presented at ECC meetings, referring to the applied methodology, the robustness of the database used, the quality of the analysis carried out by experts, including by attaching to the grid the reports on the support activity for each evaluation, the minutes of the meetings and the methodological guidance provided throughout the implementation of each evaluation, for the following evaluations: Evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027, Evaluation of communication actions, Evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes, Evaluation of Technical Assistance actions - 1 Training plan, 2 training reports, which shall include course materials, participant lists, training session agendas, course photos, feedback forms and participation certificates issued by the trainer, for the training activities carried out to improve the level of professional training in the field of programme evaluation of BEP and AM PR BI members. The evaluation plan for PR BI 2021-2027 is a strategic document whose purpose is to establish how evaluations will be carried out during the implementation of PR BI 2021-2027 and to set out the resources necessary to carry out programme evaluations. The Evaluation Plan includes a series of interim evaluations deemed necessary to improve the quality of the drafting and implementation of PR BI 2021 - 2027, such as the evaluation of the implementation of PR BI 2021 - 2027, as well as thematic evaluations (evaluation of communication actions, evaluation of the implementation of horizontal themes and evaluation of Technical Assistance actions). To ensure the quality of the evaluation process and to validate the evaluation results, the need was identified to develop the evaluation capacity of the Managing Authority by setting up the Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC1) through the procurement of consultancy and technical assistance services. The Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC1) shall be set up with the aim of providing technical expertise to ensure the quality of the evaluation process and to validate the evaluation results. ETSC1 shall analyse evaluation data needs, provide support in finalising the specifications, and contribute to improving the quality of evaluation reports. It shall also generate scientific / technical opinions on evaluation methodologies and evaluation reports, and support the development of evaluation skills for the evaluation unit and ECC. The experts for this contract shall carry out their activities in the form of an Evaluation Technical Support Committee (ETSC) and shall contribute to ensuring the quality of reports by directly supporting BEP PR BI members (guidance/training) in analysing the evaluations carried out under the PR BI evaluation contracts 2021 – 2027. The Technical Committee shall formulate views on the various versions of evaluation reports, provide support for drawing up specifications and train personnel involved in programme evaluation activities.

The technical evaluation support committee shall consist of at least three senior experts (members of academia or senior experts at sector level or in the field of programme/policy evaluation), who shall support the MA in implementing individual evaluations. Given the novelty of the programme evaluation activity within the contract, the Service Provider shall carry out the following specific activities: 1. Activity 1 – Assistance in drawing up specifications for 3 evaluations provided for in the Evaluation Plan, including the evaluability analysis of the evaluation themes relating to the 3 evaluations; 2. Activity 2 – Support for ensuring the quality of deliverables within the 4 evaluations from the Evaluation Plan; 3. Activity 3 – Transfer and use of knowledge generated by the evaluation process to support the development of institutional and individual skills and to build an evaluation culture among stakeholders.
sig_59675e8157d563b8ba20.title: Consultancy and technical assistance services for the development of the evaluation capacity of the Management Authority of the Bucharest – Ilfov Regional Programme 2021-2027

sig_5969e08dd968e183af0a.description: Helse Sør-Øst c/o Sykehuspartner would like to gain better insight into existing and new technological systems in electronic maternity journals.
