The electronic maternity journal is used in the health service to document and follow-up information related to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The electronic maternity journal is currently in use at 8 health authorities in Helse Sør-Øst RHF. The system is closely integrated with the central electronic patient journal system (EPJ) and supports the entire patient pathway connected to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The system also meets the requirements for obligatory reports to national authorities, including the Medical Birth Register and The Norwegian Tax Administration.The current system serves approx. 3,500 users divided in 2,700 PCs and covers 8 health trusts and 18 maternity wards. Sykehusinnkjøp HF is carrying out the market survey on behalf of Sykehuspartner HF. Attention is also agreed that the market survey is non binding and does not involve an obligation to hold a competition or enter into a contract. Deadline for replying: 30 September 2025 (10:00). sig_596dcef3e816b45583b5.description: This Pre-Market Engagement (PME) process is to allow the market the opportunity to assist, recommend and input into the development of NHS LPP’s new Clinical Artificial Intelligence (CAI) Framework Agreement prior to the release of the Invitation to Tender (ITT). The CAI framework will compliantly allow for both innovation of products/solutions within the lifetime of the framework, as well as maintain a comprehensive direct award mechanism for all framework suppliers and contracting authorities, by utilising the Procurement Act 2023 (PA 2023) Section 49 – Open Frameworks. sig_597558e11d1bf792b520.description: The Health-Related Behaviour Survey (HRBS) is a well-established tool used by local authorities to gather anonymous, self-reported data from pupils on a wide range of health-related behaviours, attitudes, and experiences. CCC intends to commission a one-off HRBS for Year 8 and Year 10 pupils in participating Cambridgeshire and Peterborough secondary schools (including those not in mainstream education where feasible) during the 2025/26 academic year. The survey will cover domains such as: Healthy eating and physical activity *Emotional wellbeing and resilience (including WEMWBS) *Sleep and screen time *Smoking, vaping, alcohol and drug use *Relationships and sexual health *Bullying, harassment, and online safety *School experience and pupil voice The provider will be expected to: *Supply secure, age-appropriate survey instruments (online and/or paper). *Ensure anonymity and GDPR compliance, including privacy notices and DPIA. *Provide school-level reports and a countywide report, with analysis by year group, gender, SEN/EHCP, deprivation proxies, and locality/place. *Offer optional trend analysis against previous HRBS waves and thematic deep dives (e.g., vaping, sexual harassment). The provider would be expected to work with the Cambridgeshire PSHE Service who will lead on local administration and school engagement, and its results with local schools education settings. Lot 1: .

sig_59f1056eeef3c217a913.description: The TOPS and POIS Replacement Project is required to deliver a solution to replace in-use functionality of the existing application under the adoption of modern technologies, thus avoiding innovation limitation, technical debt, operational risk and extended support agreements for these two mission critical services. TOPS is a mainframe system procured by British Rail (BR) from Southern Pacific in the early 1970s. It is a complex, command-driven system, originally designed for the management and control of freight vehicles and trains to provide real-time information of the whereabouts, loading, consignee, condition, etc. of freight vehicles. Since the introduction of TOPS to BR, the system has been expanded to handle locomotive activities and information about loco-hauled passenger operations, via a sub-system named POIS. The average freight traffic is currently 500 trains per day but may increase going forward. Lot 1: . sig_59fd16c23a30647b6211.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a Request for Information directed at potential Suppliers. Therefore, no tenders are requested or to be submitted in response to this request for information. No comments or questions received via the request for information will be answered. One of the tasks of the Finnish National Agency for Education is the publishing of learning materials and publications. Customers include both private individuals and organisations, in particular schools and educational institutions. Products are delivered to the customer either physically (e.g. textbooks) or digitally (e.g. electronic learning materials). We request up-to-date information on a comprehensive service encompassing product logistics, licensing, and online shop services. The service to be procured includes • a SaaS online shop solution where customers can purchase non-fiction books, textbooks, publications, and licences for digital learning materials published by the Finnish National Agency for Education, as well as downloadable files, using commonly used payment methods • a logistics and distribution service for textbooks and publications, including distribution to key resellers such as Library Service, bookshops, and learning material intermediaries • a digital product licence management service, and • a sales settlement service, including inventory value reporting. Service requirements • The online shop must serve our customers in Finnish, Swedish, and English. • The service must meet the accessibility requirements of the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. • It shall be possible to integrate the service with the Finnish National Agency for Education's digital learning platform (licence management) and product register. • The online shop solution must provide the capability for the Finnish National Agency for Education to edit the layout, texts, and settings of the online shop. In addition, it must be possible to add sample pages, reading samples, and promotional videos to the online shop. We request the following information 1. Does the Supplier have a comprehensive service meeting the above description to offer? 2. What pricing model does the Supplier use? 3. Based on the above description, does the Supplier have any comments on the potential requirement specification for the procurement? 4. Optional additional question: The Finnish National Agency for Education is exploring alternatives to replace its self-developed product information system and royalty register. Is it possible to tailor a product and royalty register into the Supplier's service that includes the necessary databases and user interface? The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement it in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take account of responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders. Responding to the request for information does not bind the tenderer or affect the tenderer's position in any potential procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or for any product demonstration.

sig_5a20c8309620f684d5b2.description: There is a growing population of patients with a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED), such as pacemakers, defibrillators and loop recorders. The medical and technical follow-up of these patients and devices requires good structural data collection. The legally mandated establishment of materiovigilance contact points (Royal Decree 15/11/2017) within healthcare institutions also requires good follow-up of all incidents involving these implants. The follow-up of these devices is shifting more and more towards remote telecardiological follow-up, which requires good documentation of data traffic and medical actions. Currently, no structural data storage and workflow of this information for patients with a CIED is provided within the KWS. A project is running with NexuzHealth in which a structural CIED file is being designed within the KWS that can be used across various hospitals. Within this, we want to collect the various information flows from hospitalisation, outpatient and telecardiological care in a "patient-centred" manner and present them within a uniform dashboard. By uniformly coding the information from these various data streams, they can land in the same place. As a result, the most recent information is always available in a centralised manner. A mapping was carried out with NexuzHealth of the desired fields and the corresponding definitions in the internationally recognised IEEE standard (IEEE Std 11073‐10103) which structures the data export across various producers of CIEDs. This translation must take place on multiple platforms, both for in-house control and via web portals where home follow-up data comes in. However, a preliminary study by NexuzHealth showed that producers do not yet apply this standard uniformly. A 'translation' of the supplied data by the various producers cannot be handled by NexuzHealth and requires the engagement of a third party ('middleware vendor').
sig_5a20c8309620f684d5b2.title: Use and maintenance of CIED software

This procurement forms part of the project "Transformation of public services through digitalisation in Comuna Chetani, Mureș County", financed through the Central Regional Programme 2021–2027, within project call PRC/444/PRC_P2/OP1, and aligns with the objective of supporting the digital development of the Commune of Chetani Town Hall. It targets the development, testing and piloting of two innovative digital solutions: a front-office type solution and a back-office type solution, intended to improve the interaction between the authority and the citizen/taxpayer and to facilitate access. The project supports the transition to an intelligent and innovative economy. In the context of a decentralised software infrastructure within the town hall, where each department uses specific software, the need is highlighted for two integrated solutions that unify e-government services and document management, ensuring the traceability of the town hall's internal and external activities. Thus, the project pursues the development, testing and piloting of two complex digital solutions: 1. The front-office digital solution – an online solution that facilitates the digitalisation of public administration by offering online services by the ATU to citizens, supporting the interaction between the Town Hall and the citizen/taxpayer. The front-office solution is designed to optimise the flow of information between the Town Hall and citizens, addressing both individuals and legal entities. The platform will allow users intuitive and efficient access to relevant and personalised information. The front-office solution will include the following: Info-kiosk application (IoT); Digital solution for offering online services Tax online services, Digital solution for offering online services regarding the agricultural register, Digital solution for urban planning online services, Information publication and management portal, Local Official Gazette digital solution, Participatory budgeting mechanism, Online communication solution for data and documents with judicial executor offices, Digital solution for offering online services to citizens, Mobile device application with shared services addressed to citizens 2. The back-office digital solution – an integrated computer system intended for the automation, streamlining and securing of the institution's internal workflows and supporting collaboration between departments. Designed to centralise and manage data and administrative processes, this system includes functionalities adapted to the operational specifics of local public administration, ensuring optimised management of internal activities. The front office solution will include the following: Digital Document Management solution, Registry Module, Mobile solution for the inventory of fixed assets and inventory items, Digital solution for ROeID, Electronic archive solution, Cyber security solution of IDS type, Citizen and address data aggregator (web and mobile), prescriptive debits management module, treasury import solution, F2201/F2202 / Garnishments, Court of Accounts Module, Communication of documents and data in structured electronic format with the DRPCIV, Video surveillance solution, Information application regarding energy efficiency. sig_5a32dbec0ca34f9d4152.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of Sub-Project 2 "Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation" of the Action "Support Mechanism of the Regional Coordination Authority of Thessaly for the development of social innovation as a means to address the crisis", with MIS code 6039177. The purpose of the contract is the operational strengthening of the RAA and the creation of a functional cooperation and social innovation mechanism, with the aim of supporting employment, social inclusion, social entrepreneurship and the resilience of the affected areas of Thessaly. Sub-Project 2 "Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation" concerns the creation of a permanent COOPERATION NETWORK FOR SOCIAL INNOVATION, the strengthening of human resources and the skills development of the Regional Coordination Authority and the members of the NETWORK, the development of a culture of social entrepreneurship, the interconnection of the RAA with European social innovation networks, as well as the creation of the necessary digital applications that will contribute to the sustainability of the RAA and of the COOPERATION NETWORK FOR SOCIAL INNOVATION. It also concerns the provision of consultancy and support to affected persons for their activation in social innovation actions, the implementation of pilot social entrepreneurship actions and civil protection volunteer groups
sig_5a32dbec0ca34f9d4152.title: SUB-PROJECT 2 Strengthening of the RAA and Development of Social Innovation

sig_5a41bd480940f063ebe9.description: The scope of the contract includes the following inextricably linked activities: Activity 1: Granting the right to use an “Integrated electronic environment for the assessment of examination papers” and providing system and software support for the technical and functional operability of the system for the duration of the contract; Activity 2: Technical provision, monitoring, control and coordination of the technical processing of examination papers, including the provision of the technical resources necessary for the execution of the activity, a team for system and software support of the process of processing identification forms and declassifying examination materials; Activity 3: Summarising the results of the conducted examination sessions by subject and preparing individual, aggregated and complex reports and protocols for the examination results according to various criteria, as well as for the work of the assessors by subject and providing the possibility for visualisation of checked examination papers. Activity 4: Conducting training for assessors and operators performing the technical processing of examination papers, as well as monitoring, control and helpdesk (support centre) of their activity during the assessment process. The listed activities refer to a total of 15 (fifteen) sessions – 6 (six) sessions of State Matriculation Exams (DZI) and 9 (nine) sessions of National External Assessment (NVO), with the largest number of examination papers for one session being 130 000 units. The estimated number of assessors and technical personnel (operators) processing the examination papers for the period of the public procurement, together with the provided reserves, will be up to 4 000 people for each individual year, and they will be determined by orders of the Minister of Education and Science/heads of the regional departments of education for the respective school year and will mandatorily undergo a training course for working with the system, even if they have undergone one earlier, in order to reflect regulatory and organisational changes. The specifics and requirements for the execution of all activities falling within the scope of the public procurement are described in detail in the Technical Specification – Annex No 1 to the participation documentation.
sig_5a41bd480940f063ebe9.title: Provision of services for technical support, maintenance and training for the process of electronic distance assessment of examination papers from the National External Assessment at the end of grades IV, VII and X and from the State Matriculation Exams, and provision of the right to use an integrated electronic environment for scanning, processing, distance assessment of examination papers and taking State Matriculation Exams in informatics and IT technologies and National External Assessment in IT and ICT after grade X.

sig_5a5c845efa522410b5e7.description: Forestry and Land Scotland (FLS) have a requirement to procure Soil Surveys to meet our requirement to manage the National Forest Estate. Survey requirements under this Framework Agreement may include: - Standard Surveys including Site/Soil/Peat Depth Surveys of afforested, clear felled, open land and ex-agricultural land (please note a very large proportion will be either afforested or clear-fell); - Non-Standard Surveys including, but not limited to: * Bespoke type of soil survey e.g. peat depth probing; or * Assessment of newly acquired land including possibly reclaimed land such as old mine works. For each survey, you will be required to: - Record the site/soil patterns and associated specific data, using the FC soil classification; - Map Soil Polygons and associated linear and point data in a digital format; - Peat Depths to be recorded in the Peat Depth layer via supplied digital layer (currently via ESRI Fieldmaps). Access to which, plus any necessary training to use the app, will be provided by FLS. - Deliver all data outputs from the survey, as specific digital GIS format directly into Foresterweb (a bespoke version of GIS Forester), together with associated attribute; and - Producing written reports for each site. sig_5a68142234ad5771b06e.description: Wales and West Utilities (WWU) wish to engage with the market to seek their views on establishing a robust, value for money contract for the provision of an Asset Investment Management System. The Asset Investment Manager system (AIM) is a decision support tool used by WWU for modelling the whole-life cost of assets, scenario modelling, and future business planning. It helps in making informed decisions regarding asset management and investment strategies. Any information gathered through this market consultation exercise will inform internal business planning and any possible subsequent procurement process and will NOT be appraised in any future tender evaluation exercise. Please note that participation or non-participation in this preliminary market consultation exercise shall not prevent any supplier from participating in any potential procurement process, nor is it intended that any information supplied shall place any supplier at an advantage or disadvantage in any forthcoming procurement process. For the avoidance of doubt, this is the scoping phase of the project and is not part of a formal procurement process. Suppliers who wish to participate in the market engagement exercise should complete the pre-market engagement questionnaire. The Questionnaire must be completed and PME Document signed and returned by no later than 3pm on 23/03/2026 in accordance with the instructions detailed in the PME Questionnaire document. There are no formal tender documents to be completed other than the questionnaire. All communication, including completed PME Questionnaires must be sent to wwuprocurement@wwutilities.co.uk Lot 1: .
sig_5a68142234ad5771b06e.title: Asset Investment Management System

sig_5a79a6dc49dd5418ba49.description: DIX (Digital Export Certificates) is Fødevarestyrelsen's system for requesting and issuing export certificates. The system is mandatory for exporters of food, feed and animal by-products to third countries. DIX was put into use on 28. February 2024 with the ongoing addition of new countries/certificates. DIX is intended to streamline and digitalise the request process, which entails a transition from manual, fillable PDF certificates to a digital solution. An export certificate is an official document attesting that a specific commodity complies with the importing country's health and safety requirements for the commodity. It is used in the export of food, feed and animal by-products. The certificate documents that the products can be exported legally and is accepted at customs in the recipient country. The issuance of the certificates requires approval from relevant authorities in the exporting country and compliance with international standards. Businesses must request export certificates via DIX. The request is submitted manually or by data transfer via XML files or API integrations. The system is prepared to support the full digital exchange of certificates based on UN/CEFACT standards. The process for exchanging certificates digitally requires Fødevarestyrelsen to conclude an agreement to this effect with third-country authorities. During a transitional period, some certificates will continue to be handled through the Certificate Database and TRACES NT. From 28. February 2024, approximately 20 certificate models have been migrated from the old issuance method to the DIX system every 14. day. This transition is expected to be completed by the end of 2025, which is why multiple issuance methods exist in parallel (this is not part of the contract, but rather to give potential suppliers an idea of where we are in the process). Certificates transitioning to DIX will no longer be available as fillable PDFs, but will be locked versions for viewing and completion guidance. The certificates are necessary to be able to export, as described previously. If there is an outage in the PROD environment, it is critical for businesses. There are therefore requirements for service levels. DIX consists partly of an in-house developed part and a part based on IBM's Workflow platform, BAW (Standard Software). DIX is integrated with other FVST systems. DIX consists of two main modules - the request part, which is used by a requester, either directly through the DIX Requester Module web app, or via a REST API exposed by the solution. Here, the requester creates a request for the issuance of an export certificate and submits it to Fødevarestyrelsen for case processing. Fødevarestyrelsen's caseworkers check the submitted data and can either approve or reject the request. If the request is approved, the solution generates a series of documents which are printed, after which the caseworker can retrieve the printout from a printer, sign the certificate, and issue or send it to the requester. The system also integrates with the Agency's ESDH system, where documentation for each case is stored. Once case processing is completed, the case information is journalised in Workzone (via MTU Workzone Service), and the billing basis is generated. The tendered contract encompasses maintenance, support, licence management, customisation, further development and consultancy in connection with DIX. For further information on the use of DIX, detailed information can be found here: https://foedevarestyrelsen.dk/portaler/information-om-dix
sig_5a79a6dc49dd5418ba49.title: Tender for a contract regarding maintenance, support, further development of and consultancy on an IT system for the issuance of Digital export certificates (DIX) (1)

sig_5a88458383e121a008b8.description: The scope of this tender is to secure a new storage system for the NORDUnet I/O intensive Media Management services. The storage system is also used as general-purpose storage, but the performance driver is the Media Services. The current storage system is based on IBM ESS, installed in two data centres in the Copenhagen area. Due to performance we are looking for a system based on disc or flash storage media. Common for the media services are that they provide fine grained access control to the content, so no videos are served directly from storage to the end consumer. The media files cover a wide range of sizes, as both length and resolution vary greatly from very short clips to feature length recordings of lectures. The new system must ensure high availability, scalability, and performance to meet the demanding needs of NORDUnet's Media Management services. Additionally, it must be compliant with the latest security standards to safeguard the sensitive research and educational content stored within. The procurement will be conducted through an open procedure. Potential bidders are expected to demonstrate their capability to deliver a robust and future-proof system, highlighting their previous experience in providing similar solutions, their technical expertise, and their commitment to ongoing support and maintenance. Options • The contract will include an initial purchase of a redundant storage system and at least 2 Peta bytes of usable storage per site, including 5 years support. • There is an option for additional upgrades of the storage capacity in steps of 1 Peta byte of usable storage. The option can be executed one time per calendar year, with 3 months’ notice anytime within the initial contract period.
sig_5a88458383e121a008b8.title: NORDUnet Storage Procurement (2025)

The installation will be located in a small room (dimensions approx. 4m x 3m) within the Spanish Armada Visitor centre. There will be a requirement for the installation to be dynamic, engaging and educational, highlighting the Armada using modern audiovisual technology. As a separate part of this project, the room will be upgraded and modernised, to facilitate the installation of the audiovisual experience. In advance of the submission of a proposal, interested qualified parties are invited to visit the Spanish Armada Visitor Centre to view the premises and facilities at first hand. sig_5a9387b58d272c68c288.description: The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/ Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions. Lot 1: . None
sig_5a9387b58d272c68c288.title: UK Space Agency - Operational Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters

FEKP.02.20-IZ.00-0005/25 co-financed by the European Regional Development Fund under Priority 2. European Funds for clean energy and protection of the region's environmental resources of Measure 2.20 Efficient management of water for human consumption and improvement of its quality OPPT of Specific Objective 2 (v.) Supporting access to water and sustainable water management of the European Funds for Kujawy and Pomorze programme 2021-2027 The subject of this order is: 1) supply of hydrants, 2) installation of telemetry infrastructure, 3) supply and installation of water meters. The subject of the order is the supply, implementation, expansion, integration and maintenance of the operation of the System for stationary remote reading of water meters in the Gruta Municipality using radio technology in the 868MHz band which does not require permits, enabling the future inclusion of other SmartCity devices into the system, such as smart street lighting controllers or parking sensors. By System, the Contracting Authority means water meter overlays, overlay software, mobile devices (including smartphones and radio devices), as well as data analysis software installed on a server owned by the Contracting Authority. Readings will be taken remotely and automatically via the LoRa network to the Contracting Authority's server or by meter readers. The Contracting Authority requires that the offered devices be designed, manufactured and programmed within the European Union or the EEA, have support in Poland and meet the requirements of the NIS2 directive. sig_5ac0b52ab5966275f5e7.description: Orust kommun is procuring a framework agreement regarding the purchase and leasing of products for IT workplaces as well as associated services for the municipality's employees. The purpose is to ensure a cost-effective, sustainable and needs-adapted range of IT-related products and services that support the municipality's digital work environment. During the contract period, the appointed supplier shall actively cooperate with the municipality to develop and streamline the entire lifecycle – from ordering to decommissioning. IT workplaces refers to products within the product categories below: • Laptops and desktop computers • Tablets • Monitors • Audio and video products (AV) for remote work as well as for work and conference rooms The entire supplier's range shall be included in the agreement. The assignment also includes services such as: • Advice on the choice of equipment • Exchange of computer equipment • Handling in connection with scrapping • Theft marking • Warranty management and related services Tenders shall be submitted for the entire assignment as stated in the procurement documentation. The total estimated value of the procurement is approximately 10 000 000 kronor. No volumes or call-offs are guaranteed. The framework agreement will be valid from the signing of the agreement, however at the earliest from the 1 of September 2025, up to and including the 31 of August 2029. A framework agreement will be signed with one (1) supplier.

[1]The subject of the Contract is the execution of the following elements: preparation of executive designs and execution of construction works for: - modernisation and construction of line no. 38 as a double-track line on the section from existing km 3+591 to existing km 98+800; - reconstruction of lines 515, 516 along with the retention of single-track sections: line no. 515 on the section from existing km 1+278 to existing km 1+915, line no. 516 on the section from existing km 1+383 to existing km 1+917. BASIC SCOPE: Modernisation and construction of line no. 38 as a double-track line on the section: - from existing km 3+591 to existing km 25+204, hereinafter referred to as the Białystok – Knyszyn section, - modernisation and construction of line no. 38 as a double-track line on the section from existing km 61+061 to existing km 98+800, hereinafter referred to as the Osowiec–Ełk section, - reconstruction of lines 515, 516 along with the retention of single-track sections: line no. 515 on the section from existing km 1+278 to existing km 1+915, line no. 516 on the section from existing km 1+383 to existing km 1+917. along with accompanying infrastructure and road layouts. The basic scope includes all branches excluding the elements covered by Option Right no. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and the Interface Option. OPTION NO. 1: Modernisation and construction of line no. 38 as a double-track line on the section from existing km 25+204 to existing km 61+061, hereinafter referred to as the Knyszyn–Osowiec section in all branches, with accompanying infrastructure and road layouts. OPTION NO. 2: Preparation of Construction Documentation, Executive Documentation and obtaining the necessary arrangements and administrative decisions, as well as the construction of a railway overpass together with the road layout and necessary infrastructure in the town of Grajewo. OPTION NO. 3: Preparation of Construction Documentation, Executive Documentation and obtaining the necessary arrangements and administrative decisions, as well as the construction of an underpass beneath the tracks together with the necessary infrastructure along Wiedeńska Street in the town of Białystok. OPTION NO. 4: Preparation of Construction Documentation, Executive Documentation and obtaining the necessary arrangements and administrative decisions, as well as the construction of a two-level intersection for vehicular traffic with a pedestrian and cycle path together with the necessary infrastructure, along Wrocławska Street, in the town of Białystok.. OPTION NO. 5: Preparation of Construction Documentation, Executive Documentation and obtaining the necessary arrangements and administrative decisions, as well as the construction of an underpass beneath the tracks together with the necessary infrastructure at Osowiec station. Interface option: covers the implementation of services specified in Chapter 4.14 of VOLUME III - FUP "Anticipated changes in the scope of interfaces". The entirety of the subject of the Contract includes the execution of the following elements: 1) Design Documentation: a) in the scope of executive designs, necessary for the correct execution of all construction works and obtaining for it all required opinions, arrangements, approvals, conditions, decisions and permits necessary for the implementation of the subject of the contract in accordance with the scope of the contract on the basis of documentation prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Employer, b) preparation of as-built documentation, including geodetic as-built documentation, c) preparation of Valuation Operative Reports, if necessary. 2) all construction works in accordance with the scope of the contract on the basis of the Design Documentation prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Employer, referred to in sub-item 1), and all preparatory works necessary for the execution of the scope of the Agreement and any activities required by Law including, among others, works in the scopes of: a) track structure and subgrade, b) rail traffic control devices (srk), c) telecommunication devices and systems, d) traction network together with power supply, e) power engineering devices and systems up to 1 kV, f) engineering structures, g) platforms and cubature structures, h) crossings and level crossings, i) geology, geotechnics, j) sanitary facilities, k) felling and planting of greenery. 3) works involving the construction of environmental protection facilities and compliance with the conditions for the implementation of the undertaking indicated in the Environmental Decision. 4) conducting the conformity assessment process for structural subsystems within the scope covered by the contract at each stage (design, construction and final tests of the subsystem) and handing over the relevant EC verification declarations and EC verification certificates for the subsystems. sig_5af9c6101683d596f21a.description: With this tender, Innovationsfonden wished to enter into a contract for the organisation and operation of a sparring programme under the Innofounder programme. The Innofounder programme is a 12-month full-time programme, which aims to develop and mature promising entrepreneurial ideas by providing time, funding and structured sparring to mature problem-solving, business models and market connection, while simultaneously giving entrepreneurs the best possible foundation for creating both societal and economic impact for Denmark. The consultant must be responsible for organising and conducting a sparring programme, which is offered in connection with Innovationsfonden's Innofounder programme and, in this connection, perform the tasks described in Contract Annex 1, including services linked to communication about the programme as well as administrative services. The consultant must organise a programme that matches the programme's high quality and international level with a clear focus on lifting startups from the idea and development stage to being investment-ready companies with the potential for significant societal impact. The tendered task generally comprises the following main elements: — Implementation of customisable sparring programmes for Innofounders, including ● Developing the entrepreneurs' competencies to methodically and systematically work on clarifying and qualifying their problem and solution description and documenting the relevance, effect and value creation of their solution. ● Facilitating contact between Innofounders and relevant actors in the ecosystem. ● Ensuring synergies with Innovationsfonden's current strategy and politically adopted priorities at any given time, including socially relevant innovation and impact. ● Monitoring and reporting to Innovationsfonden on progress and results based on agreed indicators and parameters. ● Ongoing adaptation of the sparring programme based on experience as well as Innovationsfonden's changed strategy and politically adopted priorities. — Communication services — Administrative tasks and offers. The programme is nationwide (Denmark), which means that participants do not have to move to a specific place to be part of the programme, but that access is offered to, among other things, individual sparring and events at various locations spread geographically across the country and/or online. The contract was tendered as a reverse auction. Tenderers were thus to compete to offer the best quality within the contracting authority's budget of 90 000 DKK excl. VAT per admitted Innofounder team. The evaluation model is described in more detail in Appendix A of the tender material. The remuneration per Innofounder team is a flat-rate fee per admitted Innofounder team of 90.000 DKK excl. VAT, which is paid to the consultant as specified in point 9.2 of the contract. It is noted that the total value of the contract stated in this notice constitutes an estimate (excl. VAT) of the expected contract sum for the total duration of the contract, incl. any extensions. The amount is calculated in 2026 prices, and if the contract is extended, the remuneration to the consultant is adjusted as regulated in point 12.2 of the contract. The estimate of the total value of the contract is calculated on the basis that the total financial scope for the task of operating the sparring programme under the Innofounder programme at the time of tendering constitutes a minimum remuneration corresponding to 60 Innofounder teams per year and a maximum of 175 sparring programmes annually at 90.000 DKK excl. VAT over an ordinary contract period of 3 years, corresponding to a total funding framework of 16.200.000 DKK – 47.250.000 DKK excl. VAT for the 3-year contract period. In the event of a possible extension of the contract, it is expected that the funding level in the extension period will be similar, and the estimated total contract value over the entire duration of up to 6 years thus amounts to 32.400.000 DKK – 94.500.000 DKK excl. VAT. Based on the current funding for the programme and Innovationsfonden's experience from the most recently completed Innofounder programme, Innovationsfonden expects that more than 130 teams will be referred to the consultant per year. It is also the experience that virtually everyone who is admitted to the programme completes the entire programme. The number of teams referred to the consultant may, however, vary significantly in both an upward and downward direction, cf. more on this in Contract Annex 1, Task Description and Requirements Specification. Innovationsfonden reserves the right in this connection to increase or reduce the number of Innofounder teams on the programme with whom the consultant must conduct an Innofounder programme, cf. below. The consultant is thus not guaranteed a minimum number of Innofounder teams per application round or per year, and the above-mentioned expected number of Innofounder teams per year is thus not an expression of any guarantee or otherwise binding for Innovationsfonden. The consultant is, however, in all cases guaranteed a minimum remuneration corresponding to 60 Innofounder teams per year during the contract period, including in any extension period, regardless of how many teams are actually referred to the consultant. Innovationsfonden cannot furthermore refer more than 175 teams to the consultant in a single year without the consultant's prior written acceptance.

sig_5b301cb276368d0fd0c5.description: Forest management services will be awarded in the year 2026 (field phase 2027) by concluding a public procurement contract for the Sascut Forestry Office. The total area of the Sascut Forestry Office is 6725,70 ha. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, for the purpose of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole to the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Services for the development of the forest management plan for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Bacau Forestry Directorate – Sascut Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 6725,70 ha. The services include preparatory works, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.

sig_5b55f09ce5f1c2e8641e.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the preparation, launch and provision by the Contractor to the Agency for Restructuring and Modernisation of Agriculture of an IT service in a SaaS model, enabling the automatic identification of land cover classes based on geospatial data, using artificial intelligence technology, in accordance with the Service Description constituting Appendix No. 1 to the draft contract provisions (hereinafter: "dcp") constituting Appendix No. 9 to the contract notice specifications (hereinafter: "CNS") and the Tender Form (Appendix No. 1 to the CNS). Land cover classes: 1.1 Basic land cover classes (hereinafter: "basic classes") – i.e. obligatory, required by the Contracting Authority, land cover classes for which the minimum classification quality indicators amounting to at least: Overall Accuracy 0,85; Recall 0,80; Precision 0,80.: a) Transport areas – (Management Fields (hereinafter: "MF") : K) b) Forests – (MF: L, Z, ZS, O, R) c) Industrial and urbanised areas – (MF: U) d) Settlements with buildings – (MF: D). Note: For the basic classes (classes a-d), the levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) shall be binding on the Contractor in accordance with the declaration submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. 1.2 Rewarded land cover classes (hereinafter: "rewarded classes") – i.e. non-obligatory, offered additionally by the Contractor within the scope of the tender evaluation criteria (ch. IX pt. 2.2 and 2.3 of the CNS), for which the tender will receive additional points, are: e) Waters – (MF: W, OM, OW, R2, R10), f) Other non-agricultural areas – (MF: I). Note: For the rewarded classes (classes e and f), the minimum levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) have not been specified, but their levels shall be binding on the Contractor only in the event of them being offered at a level at least equal to that for the basic classes, in accordance with the declaration for individual classes submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. Rewarded classes shall be taken into account in the Contract provided they meet the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 2. The scope of the contract includes the processing of geospatial data in raster and vector formats and the generation of results in the form of vector layers presenting land cover classes, along with the assignment of a classification confidence level for each object. The generated data must be characterised by geometric correctness and topological consistency. The identification of land cover classes is carried out in accordance with the classification used in the Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) and covers the full range of required classes and their representation in the form of spatial objects. The functionality of the service includes the visualisation of spatial data, the presentation of identification results, their analysis and editing, as well as the export of result data in standard formats and integration with other spatial data services and sources. Data processing should enable the handling of large volumes using parallel processing mechanisms, while maintaining the required performance. 3. As part of the contract, the Contractor shall provide the data processing environment, software and components necessary to carry out the identification process, including artificial intelligence models and the mechanisms for their operation. 4. As part of the execution of the contract, the possibility of selecting input data sources, importing them and processing them to the extent specified by the user must be ensured, both for entire datasets and their extracted parts, taking into account the use of data supporting the identification process. The use of artificial intelligence models and the provision of metrics for evaluating their quality, in particular Overall Accuracy, Precision and Recall, along with the possibility of analysing and reporting them, is envisaged. 5. The Contracting Authority requires the provision of an adequate level of availability, security and reliability, in particular regarding user authentication and authorisation, permissions management, data encryption and business continuity. 6. The Contractor is obliged to provide technical support, deliver user and technical documentation and conduct training for users. 7. As part of the Contract, the Contractor shall provide the Contracting Authority with up to 50 man-hours of consultations regarding the provided Service, during the period referred to in & 3 para. 1 of the dcp. 8. The Contractor shall deliver to the Contracting Authority the user and technical documentation described in pt. 6.4 of Appendix No. 1 to the dcp and educational materials/instructions necessary for using the Service, by the service launch deadline referred to in & 3 para. 2 of the dcp. 9. The consultation service referred to in pt. 8 shall be provided by the Contractor in Polish, including the interface (GUI, Graphical User Interface) to the Service, as well as the documentation referred to in pt. 8 - must be prepared by the Contractor in Polish. 10. The Contractor is obliged to present the results of the land cover class identification for the set subject to evaluation, along with the result data and error matrices by saving them in a dedicated workspace, in accordance with the procedure described in ch. I.1.1 of the CNS, to confirm compliance with the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 11. The Contracting Authority requires that the execution of the subject of the contract take place under the terms and conditions specified in the draft contract provisions together with appendices (hereinafter: dcp) constituting Appendix No. 9 to the CNS.

The subject of the contract is: Delivery and implementation of an integrated system for preventing student dropout at the University (monitoring and counteracting dropout system), including the delivery of licences, integration with university systems, configuration, user training, and the provision of guarantee and maintenance support. Activity implemented within the framework of the project: "Path to a diploma - integrated activities of the University of Opole to counteract the dropout phenomenon" under the European Funds for Social Development programme 2021-2027 co-financed from the European Social Fund Plus, Contract No.: FERS.01.05-IP.08-0056/25-00. The implementation schedule (completion deadline for individual stages) and payment breakdown are detailed in point 3.2. of Chapter I of the ToR As part of proper performance, in accordance with the description of the subject of the contract (DSOC), the Contractor is obliged to: 1. Deliver licences for the software constituting the subject of the contract, 2. Draw up the pre-implementation analysis, 3. Perform works related to installation and parametrisation, 4. Commission the functionalities listed within the defined requirements, 5. Integrate with the Ordering Party's domain systems, 6. Perform functionality tests and correct any implementation errors, 7. Conduct training for users and administrators of the System, 8. Hand over documentation and user manuals, 9. Provide guarantee and maintenance support for a period of up to 24 months counting from the completion of STAGE V and the signing of the acceptance protocol. The description of the subject of the contract can be found in Appendix No. 1.A "Description of the subject of the contract / Agreement". Detailed implementation conditions are specified in Appendix No. 3 to the ToR "Draft Agreement". 10.Guarantee: The Contractor grants twenty-four [ 24 ] months of guarantee for the subject of the contract. The Ordering Party requires that the Contractor grant a guarantee and provide maintenance support for a period of twenty-four [ 24 ] months in accordance with the requirements described in the Description of the subject of the contract. The guarantee period and maintenance support are calculated from the completion of stage V and the signing of the acceptance protocol by the Ordering Party and the Contractor. 11. Deadline for the execution of the subject of the contract: The deadline for the execution of the subject of the contract is a maximum of 156 working days (STAGE I-V) from the date of conclusion of the contract and 24 months (STAGE VI) from the completion of STAGE V. The deadline referred to above is divided into stages, in accordance with point 3.2 of Chapter I of the ToR. One of the tender evaluation criteria is the shortening of the implementation deadline of STAGE IVA from a maximum of 21 working days to a minimum of 14 working days from the completion of STAGE III. In the tender, the Contractor may declare a shorter deadline for the execution of STAGE IVA of the subject of the contract, however not shorter than: 14 working days from the completion of STAGE III, Chapter I point 19.2.2. The ToR applies. 12. Tender binding period: 22.08.2026 r. 1. The subject of the contract is: Delivery and implementation of an integrated system for preventing student dropout at the University (monitoring and counteracting dropout system), including the delivery of licences, integration with university systems, configuration, user training, and the provision of guarantee and maintenance support. 2. Activity implemented within the framework of the project: "Path to a diploma - integrated activities of the University of Opole to counteract the dropout phenomenon" under the European Funds for Social Development programme 2021-2027 co-financed from the European Social Fund Plus, Contract No.: FERS.01.05-IP.08-0056/25-00. 3. Implementation schedule (completion deadline for individual stages) and payment breakdown: - Stage I covers Project Organisation: Establishment of organisational structures, Preparation and presentation of the Detailed Schedule, execution deadline up to 14 working days from the date of signing the contract, - Stage II covers the Handover of licences, execution deadline up to 14 working days from the date of signing the contract, - Stage III covers the Pre-implementation analysis, software installation, execution deadline up to 21 working days from the completion of Stage I, payment of 45% of the gross value of the tender/contract, - Stage IV A covers the Implementation of the Virtual Pre-recruitment Assistant (VPA) module, execution deadline: In accordance with Chapter I point 19 of the ToR, STAGE IV A constitutes one of the tender evaluation criteria, the Contractor declares in the tender form the completion deadline for STAGE IV A: not shorter than 14 working days from the completion of STAGE III and not longer than 21 working days from the completion of STAGE III, - Stage IV B covers the Implementation of the remaining elements of the System: parametrisation, configuration of the System, adaptation of the offered System to the requirements of the Ordering Party, acceptance tests, execution deadline up to 100 working days from the completion of Stage III, - Stage V covers Preparation for go-live together with training, go-live, execution deadline up to 21 working days from the completion of Stage IV, payment of 50% of the gross value of the tender/contract. Payment after the completion of stage IVA, IVB, V, based on the acceptance protocol signed by the Ordering Party and the Contractor, - Stage VI covers Maintenance and guarantee support, execution deadline up to 24 months from the completion of Stage V, payment of 5% of the gross value of the tender/contract. Payment after the completion of stage VI, based on the acceptance protocol signed by the Ordering Party and the Contractor. 4. The detailed description of the subject of the contract was specified in appendix no. 1A to the ToR. Detailed implementation conditions are specified in appendix no. 3 to the ToR "Draft Agreement". 5. As part of proper performance, in accordance with the description of the subject of the contract (DSOC), the Contractor is obliged to: - Deliver licences for the software constituting the subject of the contract, - Draw up the pre-implementation analysis, - Perform works related to

installation and parameterisation, - Commissioning of the functionalities listed within the defined requirements, - Integration with the Contracting Authority's domain systems, - Execution of functionality tests and rectification of any implementation errors, - Conducting training for System users and administrators, - Handing over documentation and user manuals, - Provision of guarantee and maintenance support for a period of up to 24 months counting from the completion of STAGE V and the signing of the acceptance protocol. 6. The execution of the contract is to be carried out with due diligence and in accordance with all the requirements contained in the ToR with attachments and any information from the Contracting Authority for Contractors. The description of the subject of the contract (DSC) is not subject to interpretation. If the provisions of the specification are, in the Contractor's opinion, unclear, incomplete, imprecise or incorrect, the Contractor is obliged to ask a question before submitting a tender. 7. The Contracting Authority does not provide for the option right. 8. If trademarks, patents, origin, source or a specific process that characterise products or services supplied by a specific Contractor are indicated in the Description of the Subject of the Contract, constituting Attachment No. 1A to the ToR, the Contracting Authority permits equivalent products or services. Equivalent products or services must guarantee the achievement of technical parameters no worse than those assumed in the Description of the Subject of the Contract. The obligation to demonstrate that the offered products or services meet the above requirements lies with the Contractor. The above requirements also apply to standards, insofar as standards are referred to in the Description of the Subject of the Contract. Furthermore, substitute materials/devices/solutions adopted for pricing must fulfil the function they are intended to serve; they must be compatible with the other devices/systems so that the end result produces the intended effect. 9. In cases where the subject of the contract is described by reference to standards, technical assessments, technical specifications and technical reference systems referred to in Article 101 paragraph 1 point 2 of the new PPL and Article 101 paragraph 3 of the new PPL - the Contracting Authority hereby indicates that it permits solutions equivalent to those described, and any such reference appearing in the procurement documents is accompanied by the words "or equivalent" (the words "or equivalent" must be added to the reference each time). In the event that the solutions proposed by the contractor meet the requirements specified in the description of the subject of the contract to an equivalent degree, the contractor must prove in the tender, in particular by means of evidentiary means concerning the goods, that the services offered meet the requirements, features or criteria specified by the Contracting Authority. The Contracting Authority permits the use of equivalent solutions – provided that they guarantee the execution of the contract in accordance with the ToR and allow for the achievement of parameters/functionalities no worse than those provided for in the documentation, whilst the Contractor is obliged to prove in the tender, in particular by means of evidentiary means concerning the goods referred to in Article 104–107 of the PPL Act, that the proposed solutions meet the DSC to an equivalent degree.

sig_5b80f27b2eb22d8b04e2.description: The subject of the contract is the supply of specialised cutting-edge research equipment for monitoring geodynamic phenomena (e.g. earthquakes, volcanoes) and geothermal fields related to the convergence of lithospheric plates along the Hellenic arc, in the wider region of the southeastern Mediterranean. The supply of the equipment takes place within the framework of the development of the GEO-NET network (Hellenic Arc European laboratory for the study of the subduction zone and associated seismological, volcanic and geothermal phenomena) of the NOA-AEGIS infrastructure. The network will provide a wealth of data for monitoring and better understanding geodynamic phenomena taking place in the wider area of the southeastern Mediterranean Multiparametric reference seismological stations; Ocean bottom seismographs (OBS); Reference strong ground motion stations; Vertical array of accelerographs in boreholes; Borehole tilt meters and Floor mount tilt meters; Geochemical station for measuring soil gas emissions; Portable biogas analyser; Heavy-duty core drilling system; Seismological and geophysical data analysis software; Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) devices
sig_5b80f27b2eb22d8b04e2.title: Supplementary Supply of Specialised Scientific Equipment of the Geodynamic Institute for the NOA-AEGIS Infrastructure

sig_5ba58fff158013507e9a.description: The GIZ has been operating a document management system (DMS) based on OpenText Content Server since 2005. An upgrade to version 23.3 took place most recently. The DMS manages approx. 40 million objects, and it is used by approx. 25.300 users worldwide. The DMS is used essentially for - document filing in structured project files - document filing in organisational structure folders - linking documents in the intranet (IDA) - collaboration between teams and external parties (communities of practice) The subject matter of this tender is the conclusion of a service contract for the provision of ongoing operational support services on the basis of monthly flat rates as well as a framework agreement for the provision of IT services per individual order with a single contracting party (contractor). The contractor must conceptualise and implement optimal and economical IT solutions in close coordination with the DMS team of the IT Operations department in the DIGITS area and the specialised departments of the GIZ (services per individual order). In addition, the contractor supports the DMS team in troubleshooting and incident processing at 3rd level (operational support on the basis of monthly flat rates). Lot LOT-0001: 10030912 framework agreement for operational support "Open Text Content Server and Archive Server". The services to be provided on the basis of monthly flat rates comprise the following services: - Support for Content Server - Support for OpenText Archive Server - Security patches as required - Support for scanning workstations A framework agreement is concluded for the provision of the following services per individual order: - Consulting services - Customising and programming services - System administration services
sig_5ba58fff158013507e9a.title: 10030912-Framework agreement for operational support "Open Text Content Server and Archive Server"

The number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders is 18 days. sig_5bc3b87e40f17e947cdc.description: The purpose of the consultation is to contract support services for securing, modernising and governing the Microsoft 365 environment of ASFR. ASFR has initiated the modernisation of its messaging and collaboration environment with an Exchange / Microsoft 365 migration carried out in 2025. The environment remains hybrid with on-premises Active Directory and Entra ID. Cybersecurity audits 2024 followed by the Microsoft 365 / Active Directory audit of 29/06/2026 identified significant discrepancies in identity and privilege management, Entra Connect, workstation security, messaging protection, SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams governance, monitoring and resilience. The latest audit estimates an overall compliance score of 28/100 and recommends priority remediation of critical non-conformities. The requirement concerns a single Microsoft 365 transformation programme, broken down into three complementary and coordinated lots. The successful tenderer will be required to secure and make reliable the hybridisation and identities, modernise workstation management and security, and then implement governance, monitoring and continuous improvement of Microsoft 365. The programme must also address the documented remnants of the 2025 migration, in particular the verification of the hybrid architecture and de-hybridisation, and ensure a transfer of skills to the IT team. Lot 1 - Entra Connect security & identity governance; Lot 2 - Workstation modernisation and security; Lot 3 - Governance, monitoring & continuous improvement Microsoft 365

sig_5c18f41f535852815e8d.description: Description Pre- Market Engagement Notice: Productivity, Collaboration and Automation Enablement Northumbrian Water Group (NWG) is undertaking a pre-market engagement exercise to help us understand supplier capability, delivery approaches and partnering models to support our productivity, collaboration and automation landscape. This engagement is intended to inform potential future commercial options and does not constitute a commitment to procure, nor a call for competition. Purpose of Engagement NWG want to understand what services and partner models are available in the market to potentially set up a future multi-supplier framework and help us maximize value from: 1. Microsoft 365 (productivity and collaboration) 2. Power Platform (solution and workflow enablement) 3. Intelligent automation (including UiPath and Microsoft automation capabilities such as Power Automate Cloud & Power Automate Desktop) 4. The insight and reporting layer required to measure adoption and benefits (Power BI / Microsoft Fabric where appropriate) We are interested in suppliers who can work as a trusted partner alongside our teams, helping us improve adoption, strengthen governance, and demonstrate measurable value over time (not just deliver one-off pieces of work). Strategic intent NWG wants to build a repeatable, enterprise-grade capability for modern work and automation. We are looking for partners who can help us: • Improve adoption and effective use of tools (not just deploy features). • Put in place practical governance and support models so solutions are safe, supportable and scalable. • Use the right automation approach for the right job, including: - Power Automate for workflow automation - Microsoft Copilot agents/agent extensions where appropriate (agents that use approved knowledge and can take approved actions in workflows) - UiPath where RPA is genuinely required • Move towards end-to-end automation and orchestration for complex processes, including long running workflows and human approvals where needed. • Make outcomes measurable (adoption, performance and benefits), using Power BI / Fabric where it helps. Our processes run across a wide application estate. We are interested in automation and orchestration that can work end to end across multiple enterprise platforms (for example Oracle, ServiceNow, Maximo, Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), and other business systems), as well as Microsoft 365. Where possible, we prefer API/connectors and reusable integration patterns, with UI automation where unavoidable. We are also interested in secure integration and supporting components "behind the scenes" (including Azure where needed) to keep solutions reliable at scale. Framework intent - NWG is exploring a potential multi supplier framework to provide access to a broad range of specialist skills, with the ability to call off support as needed through outcome focused work packages and/or embedded delivery models alongside NWG teams. The final scope, structure and commercial approach may be refined based on this engagement. Areas of Interest (Non-Exhaustive) Suppliers are invited to share high level information on capability and experience across the following areas (non exhaustive): 1. Microsoft 365 optimisation and governance (e.g. Teams, SharePoint, Viva) 2. Power Platform development and governance (Power Apps, Dataverse, Power Automate) 3. Workflow automation and orchestration (Power Automate and integration-led approaches) 4. RPA and intelligent automation (UiPath/Power Automate Desktop), including guidance on when RPA is justified 5. Agent based automation in the Microsoft ecosystem (Copilot agents/extensions) and how this is governed safely (NWG is not seeking unmanaged AI tools; Copilot agents must operate within approved knowledge sources, governed actions, and auditable workflows) 6. End to end process orchestration across systems, including long running processes, exceptions and human approvals 7. Adoption, change, upskilling and knowledge transfer (so NWG ownership increases over time) 8. Value realisation and measurement (dashboards/KPIs/benefits reporting using Power BI/Fabric where appropriate) Supplier Response Please submit a short capability overview (maximum 4-6 slides or 3 pages) covering: • Your relevant service offerings (aligned to the 8 capability areas above) • Examples of similar work in large and/or regulated organisations • Your typical engagement model(s) (e.g. outcome based, embedded teams, managed service, call off approach) • How you would support adoption, governance and value realisation (high level) To help us compare responses, please also answer these three short prompts (on a single page): 1. How do you decide between Power Automate, Copilot agents, API-based automation and RPA (UiPath)? 2. Provide one example of an end to end process you've supported across multiple platforms, and how you handled exceptions and approvals. 3. What does "good" look like for governance and support in production (high level)? This information will help NWG shape requirements and consider appropriate commercial models. Lot 1: .

sig_5c387f7d35c6f0c56d24.description: The government and the Conference of Courts of the Canton of St. Gallen are seeking one or more providers to replace the currently used business management software JURIS-4 (specialist application for the judiciary). The new solution for the users of the Canton of St. Gallen (including the Public Prosecutor's Office, the courts, the Office for Corrections, the Office for the Commercial Register and Notaries, as well as the Department of Security and Justice) is intended to enable the electronic management of files and be user-friendly and user-centred. In addition to the audit-proof nature of the documents, the use of digital signatures, the traceability of data changes and compliance with statutory deletion periods, a high degree of configurability is also required. Furthermore, we are looking for a user-friendly, accessible German-language interface with automated processes for intuitive use in a collaborative working style. For our goal of an end-to-end digital, media-break-free procedure with electronic file management, a seamless integration of interfaces will also be necessary. Providers from outside the industry are also expressly invited to participate in the pre-qualification. The Office for Corrections is responsible for the execution of sentences and measures as well as the administration of detention in the Canton of St. Gallen. It executes the sentences and measures ordered by the courts and the Public Prosecutor's Office. Furthermore, it is responsible for investigative and security detention. The Office for Corrections has the statutory mandate to execute the criminal sanctions imposed by the Public Prosecutor's Office and the courts, to carry out probation assistance, and to make the necessary orders and issue decrees for this purpose.

sig_5c38f1e3a2844c72c68f.description: The Fund for African-Danish Relations through mutual ExChange of Culture and the Arts (ARCH) is Denmark’s initiative to strengthen equitable, long-term cultural partnerships with countries in Africa where Denmark is represented through an Embassy or a Consulate General, or in special cases, in other African countries where projects may be considered to be of particular importance. It is a four-year program anchored in Denmark’s Development Policy Strategy “A Changing World – Partnerships in Development” and its “Africa’s Century” strategy. ARCH is implemented through a dedicated Fund Manager (FM). The FM will be responsible for day-to-day implementation and must ensure full compliance with MFA’s principles and requirements for results-based management and financial accountability, as defined in the Aid Management Guidelines (AMG) for bilateral programmes and projects and Financial Management Guidelines (FMG). The contract period runs from August 2026 to December 2030. ARCH positions culture and the arts as a development end in itself based on the intrinsic value of culture for societies, communities and individuals and its ability to foster mutual understanding and appreciation for a diversity of cultural expressions and cultural heritage. At the same time, ARCH is also a strategic tool for contributing to a wide range of sustainable development goals and Danish development priorities related to areas such as promoting innovation, social cohesion and inclusive economic growth, and fostering intercultural dialogue and strengthened diplomatic relations that can bring about mutual benefits. ARCH is implemented in countries in Africa, where Denmark is represented through an embassy. At present, these include Algeria, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Somalia and South Africa. In special cases, projects in other African countries may be considered if they demonstrate an extraordinary ability to achieve the objective of ARCH or are considered to be of particular importance. The purpose of ARCH is: To invest in matching Danish and African culture creators and producers to develop commercial, technical and institutional relationships that facilitate mutual learning and sustainable structures generating jobs and social and economic benefits. The objective of ARCH is: Advancing equal people-to-people engagements in culture and the arts that contribute to sustainable cultural development, creates jobs, and social and economic benefits in African partner countries. ARCH is divided into three tiers of support and in addition offers travel/residency grants. The project is built on three overall outcomes: Outcome 1 - Inclusive and equitable cultural partnerships: Strengthening the quality, diversity, and sustainability of collaboration through grant support and dedicated mentorship. This outcome seeks to move beyond transactional funding by fostering genuine, long-term relationships rooted in reciprocity and mutual benefit. Outcome 2 - Mutual recognition and visibility: Enhancing awareness and public diplomacy through high-profile cultural initiatives and strategic communication. This outcome aims to challenge stereotypes and create more nuanced public narratives about contemporary African and Danish societies. Outcome 3 - Learning and exchange: Learning from cultural exchange that deepen and strengthen political cooperation between African partner countries and Denmark. This outcome positions culture as a vital space for discussing complex societal issues and exploring innovative solutions. A core premise of the ARCH project is a deliberate departure from traditional donor-recipient relationships. The principle of equal partnership is the foundational philosophy that must guide every aspect of the FM's work. The FM is expected to champion a model based on reciprocity, mutual learning, co-creation, and shared ownership. This means prioritizing African voices and perspectives in project design and decision-making, ensuring that partnerships are guided by shared interests and mutual benefit, and fostering an environment of trust, transparency, and respect where all partners have an equal stake in the outcomes. The FM modality will ensure independent, arm’s-length grant administration; proactive outreach to cultural actors, including new and underrepresented actors, proactive outreach to cultural actors; and strengthened capacity and learning across the portfolio. The FM will bring in sectoral expertise, transparent grant-making systems, and agile implementation in a decentralised context. The FM is expected to mitigate fiduciary risks, promote equitable partnerships, and ensure value for money through consolidated financial, monitoring, and grant support functions. In addition to being fund administrator, the FM will also serve as a strategic partner to the Department for Africa, Development Policy and Financing (AFRPOL) of the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, providing professionalized support that aligns with ARCH’s ambition of inclusive, equitable, and co-created cultural cooperation.

sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.description: Our Workplace Innovation Leadership Academy supports the ongoing development of business leaders at all levels and stages of experience. The Leadership Academy delivers programmes under a framework agreement with multiple suppliers across the Scottish Enterprise area, the programme plays a key role in cultivating leadership capability and innovation within businesses. The current framework expires early April 2026 and we anticipate commencing a new procurement process in December 2025. To inform this process, we are seeking to engage with the market to better understand current capabilities and approaches to delivering high-impact leadership development. We welcome expressions of interest from suppliers who possess specialist knowledge, proven experience, and the capacity to deliver innovative and effective leadership programmes tailored to diverse business needs. The Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Framework will consist of a series of one-day workshops, one-to-one coaching sessions, and topic specific diagnostic tools, delivered over a period of 2 - 6 months, depending on the Lot. Delivery will follow a hybrid model, combining online and face-to-face formats to maximise accessibility and impact. The Framework will deliver programmes across the Scottish Enterprise area, responding to demand. Where appropriate, programmes may also be delivered in collaboration with other enterprise agencies across Scotland. Lot 1: Transformational Leadership Programme. A cohesive leadership programme designed for both emerging and established leaders, with consistent core themes and tailored content to reflect each group's unique needs and experiences. Lot 2: Innovating Leadership: AI, Data & Emerging Tech. To empower leaders to embed AI, data, and emerging tech into strategy, foster ethical leadership, and drive internal innovation in a tech-enabled world. Lot 3: Growth Through Risk & Ambition. To support leaders in evaluating growth strategies, embracing risk as a catalyst for innovation, and exploring strategic options like investment, mergers, and ESG-aligned finance. Encourages a culture of learning through experimentation. Lot 4: Leadership in Times of Geopolitical & Economic Volatility. Helps leaders build resilience, agility, change capability and foresight to lead through uncertainty, global disruption, and change—while staying focused on long-term sustainability and stakeholder trust.
