This involves ensuring the procurement of technologies and services from Cisco Systems or supplementing existing technologies and services of the controlling contracting authority from Cisco Systems, exclusively in cases where it is not possible to request technologies and services from a manufacturer other than Cisco Systems, particularly for the purpose of ensuring the compatibility, security and homogeneity of the controlling contracting authority's communication network and protecting investments already made, in situations where, if equipment other than Cisco Systems were supplied, the functionality and security integrity of the entire solution would not be ensured. Within the framework of individual calls for tenders for partial public contracts implemented through the DPS (partial public contracts), the contracting authority will require delivery to the place of performance (including transport) of Cisco Systems technologies, i.e. HW and SW components including their accessories, the provision of SW licences or product subscriptions, information necessary for their use, or potentially HW maintenance and/or SW maintenance and/or subscriptions. sig_5c9a2d4cac59f3ae1c3c.description: Processing of evaluations of projects or calls financed from the European Social Fund. Evaluations are systematic and objective assessments of ongoing or completed projects, programmes or policies, their design, implementation and results. The aim is to determine relevance and the fulfilment of objectives, and to assess developmental effectiveness, impact and sustainability. It is a process of determining the importance or significance of a certain activity, policy or programme/project. Within the framework of the dynamic purchasing system (DNS), process, impact or strategic evaluations will be carried out. Process evaluations assess the implementation process of a programme or intervention, focus on ongoing processes and their aim is recommendations for better process design. Impact evaluations assess the achievement of planned effects/impacts/results. Most frequently using counterfactual impact evaluation (CIE type) based on statistical methods or in the form of theory-based evaluation (TBIE type) using the theory of change method and case studies. Strategic evaluations assess the design, achievement of strategic objectives and the contribution to their achievement at the level of the entire operational programme. They do not focus on partial interventions, but evaluate the programme as a whole with regard to the dominant themes of the operational programme in relation to the strategic objectives.
sig_5c9a2d4cac59f3ae1c3c.title: DYNAMIC PURCHASING SYSTEM FOR STANDARD EVALUATIONS AND DATA COLLECTION II (Category 1 – Evaluation)

sig_5cbf4f991d468c2962fa.description: I. Background and purpose: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding the operation, maintenance, monitoring, support and further development of the network and network security of the data communication network at the Contracting Authority's locations in Eastern Denmark. The Contracting Authority owns the Network, which consists of LAN, WLAN, WAN, firewalls, VPN, DDI, ADC/load balancing and management tools. The network components currently consist of HP Aruba switches, routers, access points and controllers, as well as Palo Alto firewalls, Infoblox DDI/NTP, F5 ADC/load balancing and HP Aruba Clearpass AAA. The network must be operated at a total of approx. 100 locations belonging to the Contracting Authority, which include data centres, hospitals, corporate centres and a number of smaller locations situated in Eastern Denmark as further specified in the Contract. At the time of tendering, the network consists of approx. 25.000 components, including approx. 21.000 access points and approx. 3000 switches. The network is a prerequisite for the stable and efficient operation of 11 hospitals and a number of outpatient clinics, psychiatric centres, etc. within the Contracting Authority's area of responsibility, which are characterised by high complexity and criticality, among other things. The network therefore has a special character and significance for the delivery of health services to citizens in Region Hovedstaden and the future Region of Eastern Denmark. The implications of this are reflected in the organisation of the tender, including in the specification of the Contract's services and service targets. From the establishment of the Region of Eastern Denmark, the current Region Zealand's need for network operation, etc. must also be supportable under this Contract. In this connection, necessary transition tasks may be ordered as Ordering Services under this Contract, after which the delivery of Ongoing Services can be scaled pursuant to the Contract. II. Main services: A) Transition of network operation and other services from Region Hovedstaden's existing supplier, including taking over responsibility for the operation and maintenance of the Network, implementation of any necessary changes to the Network in connection with the transition, testing of the Network and establishment of the Supplier's organisation for the delivery of the Contract's other services. B) Ongoing services: B.1) Network operation: The Supplier must ensure efficient and stable operation of the network while complying with service targets for availability, among other things, as well as assistance with scaling the network in accordance with the Customer's needs. In this context, the Supplier must, inter alia, provide backup and restore of network components, logging, local area network segmentation, monitoring, capacity management and operational reporting. As an integrated part of the operation, the Supplier must maintain the network, including inter alia undertaking the updating of operating systems, firmware and patches, as well as replacing network components and undertaking their re-configuration. The Supplier must furthermore handle network security, including inter alia perimeter security, remote access, management of access rights to network equipment, and network auxiliary services in the Customer's LAN. B.2) Support: The Supplier must make a service desk available, which must act as a point of contact for the Customer's IT employees. The Supplier must furthermore handle incidents and problems, including identifying, recording and resolving them in accordance with documented processes and in compliance with the service targets in the Contract, as well as continuously improving incident handling, providing root cause analyses, etc. Support also includes user administration. C) Ordering services: The Supplier must deliver ordering services related to the Network. The ordering services may include simple and standardised tasks related to the network, as well as consultancy, analytical work, assistance with the implementation of security or the preparation of designs in relation to an improvement of the network, inter alia with a view to ensuring the efficiency and optimisation of the Customer's business. The ordering services may furthermore include changes to the network's functionality, design and architecture.

sig_5d330cee58ac7e43d83c.description: Leicester City Council requires a Fuel Management System (FMS) to monitor, control and report on fuel usage across its fleet of vehicles and machinery circa 800 vehicles and plant. The solution must be compatible and installed across multiple locations within the Leicester area. The system must enable secure fuel dispensing through authorised methods (e.g. RFID, vehicle tags), provide accurate, real-time tracking of fuel transactions and stock levels; and generate detailed reporting on fuel by vehicle, operator and site. It must also include configurable alerts (e.g. low fuel, anomalies) support environmental and audit reporting, and integrate seamlessly with existing council systems, including fleet management. The system must be robust, scalable and user-friendly with high availability, role-based access control, and compliance with applicable fuel storage, environmental and data security regulations. The successful tenderer will be responsible for end-to-end delivery including the supply of hardware and software, system configuration, user training, documentation and post-deployment support. The FMS must enhance operational efficiency, reduce fuel loss and provide the transparency and accountability required by the council’s governance and reporting obligations. The Council reserves the right to onboard other service areas of the Council to call-off from this contract, should they have a requirement for the same services, during the contract term (including options to extend). sig_5d393c073c1ba7e9d3f4.description: The Digital Asset Data Information (DADI) programme is a digital programme of work within the overarching Asset Management Improvement Portfolio, with a whole life focus on how the Environment Agency as an owner-operator will digitally create, maintain and operate its asset estate in the future. As part of the DADI programme, the Strategic File Management (SFM) project underpins the Agency’s ambition to be recognised as a world-class Asset Management (AM) organisation. The SFM goal is to deliver a solution for the management of the Environment Agency’s AM files which will be based on standardised and governed processes and include the supporting technological capability to carry out these processes. The desired solution will ensure that documentation relevant to an asset’s entire lifecycle is effectively managed and can be retrieved and accessed by a wide range of users in a number of formats. The business objectives of this procurement are as follows: • Implement a compliant, centralised file management system. • Create a single source of truth supporting the entire asset lifecycle. • Enable accurate, trusted Business Intelligence. • Achieve ISO19650 and ISO55000 compliance. • Improve file accessibility, storage, sharing, and user experience. • Enhanced data governance and risk mitigation (e.g., reduced security and legal risks). • Reduced inefficiencies, such as duplication and process waste. • Ensure connectivity and interoperability with other Asset Management systems to support efficient sharing and consistency of asset information. • Support carbon reduction and improved sustainability through streamlined practices. • Provide the option for other Defra Group Bodies (https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations#department-for-environment-food-rural-affairs) and other UK "Paying Agencies" to utilise the contract. The purpose of this notice is for DEFRA (on behalf of the EA) to make known that a Further Competition is being conducted via a Competitive Flexible procedure for Procurement of Enterprise Asset Management Common Data Environment (CDE). Additional Information: The budget for the initial term (five (5) years) is at a total of £3.7m (ex VAT) with the total contract value expected to be up to a total cost of £6.5m (ex VAT) during the overall maximum 10-year term (5+2+2+1), which includes the cost of implementation, delivery of the Service, and Exit and Transition. The contract value is an estimate only. The contract value estimate will be dependent upon whether an extension (in part or in whole) is enacted, whether any optional services (in part or in whole) are enacted, the extent of any contract changes, and the indices used to index prices. Suppliers can access this by visiting https://defra-family.force.com/s/Welcome – this will require signing up to the Atamis system and following the instructions within the Portal. Lot 1: .

sig_5d80673ba81c11576d3d.description: In addition to its in-house services, companies are being sought to support the ZHdK with its IT services for three years (with an option to extend once by two years or twice by one year). Specifically, the services relate to the following: * Lot 1: Digital Transformation Services: Expertise as well as advice and support for the ZHdK in digital and agile transformation and the associated cultural change Management of or support for projects or programmes in the area of digital and agile transformation * Lot 2: AI Technical Solution & Operation Services: Establishment, further development and operation of AI services as well as the necessary AI platforms, infrastructures and technical foundations Implementation, integration and governance of AI solutions as well as enabling the ZHdK to use artificial intelligence sustainably and securely The services sought are divided into two lots. Each lot consists of one or more profiles for service provision. The specific requirements and activities are described for each lot in the two lot descriptions in Chapter 2. Companies are sought whose core competencies lie in the described areas of the IT environment and who have their own qualified personnel. The contract for each lot will be awarded to up to three companies. There is no restriction on bids, i.e. bids may be submitted for both lots. However, it is desirable that companies concentrate on bids in their respective core competencies. sig_5d8a680e62cb81f8a873.description: University of Limerick request the supply of a Mobile Robot Motion Capture System for the localisation and tracking of mobile robotic platforms within an indoor laboratory environment. The purpose of the instrument is to provide high-accuracy, low-latency, real-time 3D positional and orientation data for multiple aerial, ground and surface robotic vehicles operating simultaneously within a defined capture volume. The system will support research, teaching and industrial collaboration in autonomous systems, multi-agent robotics, navigation and human–robot interaction. The supply of a Compact Autonomous Surface Vehicle (ASV) for Hydrographic Survey for inshore hydrographic and bathymetric survey applications. The purpose of the instrument is to enable autonomous and remote-controlled survey operations in shallow inshore waters, rivers and lakes, supporting multibeam sonar bathymetric mapping, water-quality profiling, and environmental data collection. The system will support research and teaching at UL CRIS and provide a versatile, compact, easily transportable survey platform for use across coastal, estuarine and inland waterbody applications. sig_5d96390e7ee3d5b132a6.description: Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) and its subordinate and associated commands seek to accelerate the development, procurement and integration of unmanned systems (UxS) capabilities in support of the Joint Force, Special Operations Forces (SOF), and allied SOF. NSWC seeks to award Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) contracts or Other Transaction Authority agreements (OT) (see 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021-23) to provide a new method of delivering UxS systems capability called “UxS as a service” and First Person View (FPV) platforms. Resultant contracts or agreements should provide systems with a broad range of capabilities that directly support mission effectiveness in terms of platforms, payloads, Processing-Exploitation-Dissemination (PED), programming (i.e., firmware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI)), communications/data transfer, Command and Control (C2) systems, components, and/or material to be acquired, developed, or already in use by NSWC, United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), the Department of War (DoW), or the U.S. Government, as well as interagency and FVEY partners. As such, under the authority of DFARS 212.70, NSWC releases this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). NSWC anticipates the award of a Firm-Fixed Price type contract in accordance with FAR Part 12. Offerors are encouraged to review FAR 52.212-4 and 52.212-5 for standard terms and conditions of a FAR Part 12 contract. In addition, NSWC may award an OT in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4022-23. Non?FAR Contracts and Agreements are anticipated with nontraditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of the SOF Operator and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or material to be acquired or developed by the NSWC, or the improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by NSWC. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102 and the procedures set forth in this announcement satisfy the competition requirements within 10 U.S.C 4022(b)(2) and 4022(f)(2)(A). Contracting Officers shall treat items, technologies, and services acquired using a CSO as commercial items. Agreement Officers may make awards in accordance with 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021-23. Awards made in accordance with 10 U.S.C. §§ 4023 are not subject to competition requirements. The full Commercial Solutions Opening Notice H9224026SC001 and information is attached to this posting. All submissions shall be in accordance with the instructions within. Submissions – Phase I Submissions should be made via Vulcan as identified below in this section. If sensitive or classified, offerors may request additional instructions by submitting an email to: NSW.CONTRACTING.CSO.SHDMBX@socom.mil. Demonstration/pitch events that fulfill the requirements of Phase II of this CSO may reference this process in their submission instructions. Submission Deadlines and location for submission: AOI 1: Submissions shall be due 25 January 2026. Submission link is: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=e93ae11d-355b-48b3-b8be-8a7b4f55ba78 AOI 2 and 3: Bi-annual Submissions for either AOI 2 or AOI 3 shall be due on 9 January 2026. Submission link is: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=a2bcad15-6b21-4640-ba26-63d172d3ca4d AOI 2&3: Bi-annual Submissions for either AOI 2 or AOI 3 shall be due on 9 July 2026, Submission link will be included in this posting by 30 June 2026. AOI 4: Bi-annual Submissions for AOI 4 shall be due no later than (NLT) 9 April 2026. AOI 4 is added per Amendment 01 of this Notice and Attachment. Submission link is: https://vulcan-sof.com/login/ng2/submission?collectionUuid=f9989d55-ade0-4b5b-933c-520d5f4663f1 AOI 4: Bi-annual Submissions for AOI 4 shall be due no later than (NLT) 9 October 2026. The procurement concerns various consultancy services focused on industrial development for smaller manufacturing companies (SMEs). The procurement is carried out as a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). This means that the procurement is divided into two phases: Phase 1 - Application phase and Phase 2 - Tender phase. In phase 1 tenderers submit their application to be qualified for the DPS within one or more areas of expertise. In phase 2 qualified suppliers are invited to submit tenders for a specific area of expertise. The procurement is divided into 10 different areas of expertise: 1. New technology 2. Sustainability 3. Production and efficiency 4. Skills development 5. Market development/sales 6. Regional industrial development 7. Communication 8. Product development 9. Follow-up research 10. Price and profitability models and analysis Registration of email address To participate in the procurement, the supplier needs to have a user account registered for the procurement tool e-Avrop. The account required to participate is free of charge. When registering an account and when participating with a tender application in phase 1 of the procurement, it is important to carefully consider that the email address registered is correct and that it will be current to use for future communication within phase1 and phase 2 of the procurement, e.g. during upcoming call-offs. sig_5dae8edf0a8a241a68aa.description: The Municipality is in need of access to qualified and needs-adapted expert support in the field of crisis preparedness and civil defence. The assignment includes support for the municipality's work on developing and strengthening the capability to prevent, withstand and manage societal disruptions, including extraordinary events and heightened preparedness. This may include support in risk and vulnerability analyses, continuity management, development of working methods and procedures for managing societal disruptions, planning documents and governing documents, training and exercises, cooperation with internal and external actors, and efforts within the framework of the municipality's responsibilities in civil defence. JLU is planning a relaunch of its website. As part of this tender, external support is to be commissioned for the areas of Technical Implementation (Block A) as well as Hosting and Operation (Block B). A tender for the area of usability and interaction design has already taken place beforehand. In the project, content (editorial concept and content) forms the third area. This is covered by the JLU project team. Domestic and international prospective students, applicants, students, internal and external scientists, employees, alumni and other external target groups use the service as a knowledge base for a wide variety of university topics and as a source of information about university events. Central focus topics of the web relaunch project are student recruitment and the excellence strategy. A duration of four years is planned for the Technical Implementation (Block A) as well as Hosting and Operation (Block B) of the web relaunch project. In the first year, 200 person-days (PT) are provided for development. In the following years 2 to 4, 120 person-days are provided for operation and further development in each case. One person-day corresponds to 8 hours. The area of usability and interaction design was tendered separately. Early coordination between the contractor and the design agency is planned to ensure the technical feasibility of the developed design. The web relaunch will be implemented according to a hybrid-agile project management approach, in particular to achieve quickly visible results. Block A: Technical implementation includes, among other things: - Implementation of Corporate Design (Web): Implementation of the Plone theme according to the design agency's draft, development of content types for central overview pages, development of templates for content maintenance by web editors, implementation of the central navigation concept, development/adaptation of a mechanism for web forms - Special core features - Automated data integration from third-party systems - Authentication and access control - Role and rights management - Multilingualism - Search engine optimisation (SEO) / Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) - Search and search optimisation - Web statistics and analysis - Adjustments to the Plone standard - Partial migration of selected content - Mechanism for maintaining URLs in hybrid operation - Documentation - Project management Technical implementation Block B: Hosting and operation includes, among other things: - Server infrastructure and cluster setup - Operational tasks and maintenance - Continuous release planning and staging processes - Service Level Agreements (SLA) - IT security Furthermore, cross-sectional topics (accessibility, data protection-compliant operation) Requirements for the contractor's project team: For the implementation of the web relaunch project, the client expects an experienced and interdisciplinary project team. For the personnel offered, the role profiles must be submitted completed. A document must be submitted fully completed for each person. Role profiles: - Project coordination - Senior software development / Technical management - Software development / Frontend & CMS - Quality assurance / Testing A final description can be found in the service description.

With its "Flagship University" concept in the Hamburg metropolitan region, it maintains innovative and cooperative connections with scientific and non-scientific partners. It produces future-oriented social goods – education, knowledge and the exchange of knowledge – for the location, but also nationally and internationally, under the guiding objective of sustainability. sig_5e10d393da3bf8ea97bd.description:
Combined transport (CT) is a key factor in shifting freight transport from road to inland waterways and rail. It thus contributes to saving greenhouse gas emissions and to complying with national and European climate targets. Its importance will increase even further in future, according to the current traffic forecast 2040. What is required is a well-developed, nationwide network of bi- and trimodal transhipment terminals for transhipment between the transport modes of road, rail and inland waterways, which also has sufficient capacity for future demand. Transhipment between transport modes generates additional costs when transporting goods in combined transport compared with unimodal goods transport. The Federal Government therefore supports combined transport. This is provided via grants to private companies for investments in combined transport transhipment terminals. Since the end of 2022, funding has been provided on the basis of the guidelines of the Federal Ministry for Transport (BMV) on the promotion of investments in combined transport transhipment terminals dated 23 November 2022 (https://www.bmv.de/SharedDocs/DE/Anlage/G/foerderrichtlinie-von-umschlaganlagen-des-kombinierten-verkehrs.pdf?__blob=publicationFile). This funding guideline is valid until 31.12.2026. An extension by one year is planned. Federal funding guidelines have been in place continuously since 1998, on the basis of which the funding of the construction and expansion of CT transhipment terminals by private companies took place. For instance, previously in the period from 01.01.2017 to 30.09.2022, funding was provided on the basis of the guidelines on the promotion of combined transport transhipment terminals of non-federal companies. The implementation of the funding (review of funding applications, approval of funding, verification of use) has been undertaken by the Federal Railway Authority (EBA) and the Directorate-General for Waterways and Shipping (GDWS). In accordance with budgetary regulations on grant law, ongoing funding must be subjected to a review of success. This review of success comprises the evaluation of the approved projects (WP 1) as well as a target achievement check, an impact assessment and an economic efficiency check of the previous funding (WP 2). In addition, an economic viability study is to be carried out for the planning of a possible new funding scheme. Within this framework, additional possibilities are to be discussed and examined as to whether and how – in compliance with the principle of economic efficiency of the Federal Budget Code (BHO) – funding for private CT transhipment terminals can be improved, supplemented with new funding items if necessary, and extended to other multimodal transhipment terminals (WP 3). In addition, it is to be examined whether and how operational funding in the sense of start-up financing for CT transport and other multimodal transport is possible (WP 4). In the case of WP 3 and 4, it must be noted in particular that extensions of funding or new funding items require clear proof of economic efficiency with regard to the objective of the CO2 savings to be achieved thereby, in view of increasingly scarce budgetary resources. Overfunding, which may also occur due to the combination of CT-specific funding with other federal support measures, is to be avoided in any case. In line with the objective of reducing bureaucracy set out in the coalition agreement, funding should also be designed in a secure manner against abuse so that it causes as little administrative burden as possible for the applying companies and the approving authorities. ***** Details can be found in the electronically provided tender documents. Lot LOT-0000: 6#0013-G14-for the award of an evaluation of the promotion of the shift of freight transport to rail and inland waterways in combined transport and other multimodal transport chains. The study is to evaluate the guidelines for the promotion of investments in combined transport transhipment terminals dated 23 November 2022 as well as the projects funded in the period since 01.01.2023 (regardless of the relevant funding guideline). Recommendations for action for a funding regime to support multimodal freight transport and the design of a future funding guideline for investment support for transhipment terminals of private companies are to be derived from the results of the evaluation. In addition, evaluation assignments from the Multimodal Freight Transport Strategy Dialogue are to be fulfilled with the study. The study comprises the following four work packages (WP): - WP 1: Evaluation of the approved projects Evaluation of the approved projects for the promotion of investments in private CT transhipment terminals, differentiated according to projects approved on the basis of the aforementioned funding guideline since 03.12.2022 and projects funded in the period since 01.01.2023 on the basis of a previous funding guideline, - WP 2: Review of success of the current funding guideline Preparation of a publishable expert report on the review of success of the applicable funding guideline for CT transhipment terminals, comprising target achievement, impact and economic efficiency checks as well as a full assessment of the funding modalities, - WP 3: Recommendations for action for a future funding guideline Preparation of a publishable expert report containing recommendations for action for the design of a future funding guideline for the promotion of CT transhipment terminals, and - WP 4: Supplementary recommendations for action Preparation of a publishable expert report containing the assessment and building upon it recommendations for action for alternative or supplementary approaches to supporting multimodal freight transport.

In a summary, the results of the individual work packages are to be brought together and recommendations are to be issued for the future design of CT funding. ***** Details can be found in the electronically provided tender documents.

Through the request for information, the contracting authority aims to form an overall picture of the market supply and to evaluate options related to the implementation of the procurement. sig_5e421ac5bf22d9557fad.description: The Parking and Markets ICT Systems Procurement is crucial for enabling the Council’s responsibilities in parking enforcement, permits, suspensions, cycle hangars, markets, and shop fronts. These systems support Hackney in helping manage kerbside space, improving air quality, and delivering revenue. The council is seeking a shift towards a digital solution across nine separate lots and requires systems that will enable a shift in major policy changes, safeguard service continuity and is able to handle high-volume transactions across various teams. This procurement will adopt the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023. A modular, multi-lot approach will be used to evaluate bids for interoperability, data migration, and deliverability throughout the lifetime of the contracts. Lot 1: Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs). Covers the end-to-end processing and management of Penalty Charge Notices, including case management from issue through to closure, customer correspondence, evidence management, representations/appeals support, and reporting. The lot includes integration requirements to support enforcement channels (including on-street and CCTV enforcement where applicable), removals interfaces where relevant, payments and reconciliation, and debt recovery processes with enforcement agents. Lot 2: Permits and vouchers. Includes end to end management of a comprehensive range of permits issued by the council, including resident, business, and all-zone permits, along with CCTV exemptions. Lot 3: Cycle hangars . Management of cycle hangars and cycle parking in the borough. Lot 4: Parking suspensions. Management of parking suspensions and relevant services. Lot 5: Parking infrastructure maintenance. System for the management of all parking infrastructure such as signs, lines, machines and other relevant items. Lot 6: Markets, shop fronts and street trading. A system for the management of market traders' licences, pitches, pavement licences, annual fees. Lot 7: Abandoned vehicle processing. A system for end-to-end processing of abandoned vehicle reports, removals and FPNs. Lot 8: Cashless parking. System for the provision and management of cashless parking payments across the borough. Lot 9: Fixed penalty notices (FPNs). End-to-end processing of FPNs across relevant Council services, including abandoned vehicles, environmental enforcement and waste services, Markets and other future service areas.

sig_5e5f354bd3fd3471f3f9.description: The University Hospital Essen AöR intends to modernise its ERP with the procurement of SAP Rise with SAP Private Cloud Edition, including licences, operations and infrastructure. The separately available documents fully describe: - the subject matter of the contract - the required tasks and duties of the potential cooperation partner - the next steps of the market consultation. The information memorandum can be requested informally by e-mail from the procurement office. For queries, please contact: vergabe@uk-essen.de. Interested companies are requested to submit a substantial expression of interest together with an initial concept in accordance with the specifications of the covering letter and the information memorandum by 21.10.2026 10 hrs. Lot PAR-0001: Procurement of SAP Rise with SAP Private Cloud Edition, including licences, operations and infrastructure. Against the background of the expiring mainstream support for SAP ECC (end: 31 December 2027; extended maintenance until 31 December 2030, exclusively against separate remuneration) as well as the strategic objective to sustainably further develop the digital infrastructure of UK Essen, the UKE intends to transform its existing ERP landscape to a modern, cloud-based target architecture based on SAP S/4HANA. With this procurement, UK Essen pursues the goal of establishing a high-performance, secure, scalable and long-term viable ERP platform. The future platform is intended to reliably support UK Essen's existing business processes, create the prerequisites for the digitalisation of further processes and at the same time provide the technical basis for future innovations in the areas of data management, analytics, automation and artificial intelligence. The target architecture is intended to promote the standardisation and harmonisation of business processes, reduce the complexity of the existing system landscape, ensure long-term manufacturer support and guarantee the economic usability of existing investments. The subject matter of the market consultation is exclusively the provision of an integrated SAP corporate platform based on RISE with SAP Private Cloud Edition and, for human resources, SAP SuccessFactors (public cloud) including the software licences, infrastructure, operation, maintenance and support services required for this. The actual ERP transformation (system design, process conception, implementation, customising and data migration) is not the subject of this procurement. Corresponding implementation services will be awarded in a separate procurement procedure. Insofar as transformation support is mentioned below, this refers exclusively to manufacturer-side onboarding and migration preparation within the framework of the RISE conversion agreement (in particular licence conversion and License Value Credit offsetting). An essential component of the procurement object is the transfer of UKE's existing SAP licence landscape into the future operating and usage model. UKE has a historically grown SAP system landscape with existing licence, maintenance and usage rights, which are to be transferred economically, technically and under licence law into the future target architecture as part of the transformation. The consideration of existing investments as well as the use of the transformation and conversion mechanisms provided for this represent a central component of the project. Thus, the existing licences must be taken into account by the contractor as part of the transition to the new SAP private cloud licence model. A double burden caused by running on-premise maintenance fees and new cloud operating costs in parallel during the migration phase is to be effectively avoided. The service requested as part of the market consultation comprises in particular: - cloud service provision (SAP Cloud ERP Private and SAP SuccessFactors) as well as the associated SAP tools (e.g. SAP Signavio, SAP LeanIX, SAP Cloud ALM, SAP Test Automation by Tricentis, SAP Build and SAP Integration Suite) - user licences - operation and maintenance - cloud application services The documents made available to you give you a precise overview of: - the subject matter of the contract - the required tasks and duties of the potential cooperation partner as well as the further procedure of the market consultation.
sig_5e5f354bd3fd3471f3f9.title: Procurement of SAP Rise with SAP Private Cloud Edition - including licences, operations and infrastructure

sig_5e60c6fabc8a8d11e8e3.description: HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has launched a competitive procurement for the delivery of an innovation-led Proof of Concept (PoC) exploring how emerging technologies, richer transaction data and integrations across banking, payment, fintech and software ecosystems could support increased simplification and accuracy within Income Tax Self Assessment (ITSA). The PoC will build, test and evaluate a working technical demonstrator. Its purpose is to generate evidence and learning, rather than develop a live service or commit HMRC to a specific future solution. This work supports HMRC's Transformation Roadmap and aligns with HMRC's Strategic Approach to Third Party Software. It explores how banking, payments, fintech and software ecosystems can help customers manage their tax affairs through the products and services they already use, reducing administrative effort, improving visibility of tax obligations and helping customers get their tax right first time, while building on a thriving and innovative market. Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax provides the digital foundations for ITSA and continues to roll out. Innovation across banking, payments, fintech and software markets presents opportunities to develop, test and better understand ecosystem approaches to support more efficient and effective tax administration that makes it simpler for customers to meet their tax responsibilities. For many ITSA customers, software and fintech products already provide valuable automation and support, helping many customers to manage their tax affairs more efficiently. However, richer data, improved standards and greater interoperability may create opportunities to further enhance transaction categorisation and apportionment, reducing customer effort, supporting customer experience and ensuring more accurate tax outcomes. HMRC wants to test and learn with the market how banks, payment providers, fintechs and software platforms can build on existing capabilities to deliver more integrated, accurate and customer-centred tax experiences, while supporting a thriving and innovative software ecosystem. The central question for the PoC is: to what extent can future enhanced data, ecosystem integrations, and interventions reduce customer effort, improve customer experience and improve accuracy across more aspects of Income Tax Self Assessment? HMRC welcomes ideas from suppliers which innovate further, building on today, and looking towards future capabilities. Suppliers are welcome to bid independently or in partnership to build, test and evaluate an end-to-end working technical demonstrator of enhanced future capabilities and integrations. sig_5e7c5967ce7ad807aabf.description: EEM is seeking to set up a framework arrangement with a single provider capable of operating a large-scale, neutral ICT procurement and supply chain management function across the full scope of this Framework Agreement. This procurement will establish a single-supplier framework, in accordance with Section 45(4)(a) of the Procurement Act 2023. EEM has concluded, based on market analysis, statutory considerations and PME feedback, that a single neutral vendor is the only proportionate and effective model capable of delivering the full scope of ICT requirements defined in this document. This approach is justified on the following grounds: A. Interoperability and Whole-ICT Lifecycle Integration ICT procurement across the public sector is currently fragmented. Complex interdependencies between hardware, licensing, cloud consumption, cybersecurity, networks and managed services require a single entity to coordinate supply, ensure compatibility, and provide end-to-end assurance. A multi-supplier framework would not achieve these outcomes, and would increase the risk of: • conflicting supplier commercial incentives • inconsistent technical standards • fragmented support arrangements B. Transparency and Spend Control Public bodies consistently reported that pricing for software licensing, cloud consumption, and associated services is often opaque and difficult to benchmark. The single-supplier Neutral Vendor model is required to: • eliminate hidden margins and bundled charges • ensure transparent, open-book pricing • provide uniform reporting and governance • support PA23 transparency duties under Sections 69–95 C. Aggregation and Economies of Scale A single supplier is required to centralise: • demand aggregation • volume discounting • supply chain optimisation • consolidated OEM negotiation These benefits cannot be achieved with a multi-provider arrangement. D. SME Enablement and Fair Access Evidence from Preliminary Market Engagement confirmed that SMEs find it difficult to engage directly with large ICT procurements. A neutral vendor enables: • structured and fair onboarding • transparent subcontracting workflows • increased SME participation • elimination of reseller-dominated routes This directly supports government objectives on SME inclusion. E. Risk Management and Compliance The Neutral Vendor model mitigates: • inconsistent supplier compliance • unmanaged subcontracting • variable licensing and cybersecurity standards By providing a single accountable entity, the model supports: • compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 • Cyber Essentials/ISO 27001 assurance Based on PME responses, market analysis and the statutory requirements of the Procurement Act 2023, a single neutral vendor framework is considered the only proportionate and effective commercial structure capable of delivering the scope of this Framework Agreement. This Framework does not establish a traditional ICT reseller or managed service delivery model. The appointed supplier must operate as a neutral procurement intermediary, with all sourcing decisions made transparently and without bias towards any proprietary or internally delivered services. The Neutral Vendor will act as the sole contracting entity for all purchases under the Framework, with all supply chain arrangements managed on a back-to-back basis. The objectives of the framework are: Objective 0: Provide an outsourced ICT procurement function delivering compliant sourcing, commercial governance, benchmarking and transparent access to the ICT supply market. Objective 1: Provide a comprehensive range of ICT products and services, including niche suppliers, enabling public sector buyers to procure the latest technology solutions. Objective 2: Ensure competitive pricing through transparent cost structures and negotiated discounts, offering value for money for public sector bodies. Objective 3: Facilitate the redistribution of vendor incentives (e.g., rebates, kickbacks) back to the Buyer in a fair, transparent, and legally compliant manner. Objective 4: Offer flexible and scalable ICT solutions, ensuring buyers can select the most appropriate technology to meet their needs. Objective 5: Ensure all products and services comply with relevant standards and regulations, including the Procurement Act 2023, NHS standards, and sector-specific compliance requirements. The scope of this procurement is for the providers of ICT goods and services. The themes, product and services are set out in the Scope and Specification section of this document. EEM considers this framework will help: • enable EEM members, whether existing or future, and the wider public sector to procure services provided by ICT providers in an efficient and compliant way. • provide access to a vetted list of suppliers, reducing the le and effort needed to conduct individual procurements. • ensure that all purchases meet legal and regulatory requirements, such as the Procurement Act 2023. • provide better value to the buyer by creating a fairer and more efficient supply chain, whilst consolidating purchasing power to negotiate better pricing and terms. • provide clear, pre-negotiated pricing structures, enabling buyers to achieve greater value for money. • provide diverse ICT needs, including hardware, software, services, and niche products, allowing buyers to source everything from a single framework. • ensure access to cutting-edge and specialised technology, such as IoT solutions and green ICT initiatives. • allows buyers to better scale their ICT purchases in line with changing requirements, from small upgrades to large-scale projects. • Encourages greater innovation and quality by providing access to innovative products and services, including from niche vendors, ensuring buyers can procure the latest technology. • promoting competition among suppliers, driving higher quality standards. • Reducing procurement risks by offering contracts with established suppliers that adhere to framework terms and conditions. sig_5ea099a88b425bb0c01d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_5ebf9142ece3131b6268.description: The project “DEEP_AI – Solutions based on artificial intelligence, empowered by high-performance computing (HPC) systems for the spatial economy” is an industrial research and experimental development project financed through the Intelligent Growth, Digitalisation and Financial Instruments Programme (PoCIDIF) 2021–2027, within Action 1.1 Support for the private sector and for collaboration between actors from the public system and the business environment in the field of RDI. This advanced data centre will specialise in the training, simulation and processing of large volumes of data and complex algorithms, especially in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). The research infrastructure will be operationalised by the project leader, the George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Science and Technology of Târgu Mureș and used by the private partners (PRO VALUE SRL, ASTRALIS SOLUTIONS SRL, ROPARDO SRL, STARTUP WORKSPACE SRL, AXTEN SRL), targeting five distinct use cases oriented towards applications in the spatial economy, monitoring and control of generative AI, and the expansion of its applications in the social and medical sectors.

sig_5ec44ba10636452c5bf2.description: The consultant agreement shall cover the provision of technical services in support of DSA ́s core functions within regulatory work. The work shall include reviewing and assessing technical documentation and support for DSA in connection with inspections. There are three nuclear plants in Norway: the research reactor facilities in Kjeller and Halden, and the combined landfill and storage facility for low and medium radioactive waste in Himdalen. In 2018 the Norwegian government established a new government organisation, Norsk Nukleærdekommisjonering (NND), which will take over all Norwegian nuclear power plants in Kjeller, Halden and Himdalen from the original operator, Institute for Energy Engineering (IFE). NND will be responsible for the operation of the nuclear installations, the production of them and the handling of radioactive waste and used core fuel. So far the nuclear power plant in Halden has been transferred from IFE to NND, and the other two installations are close to being transferred. Before the shutdown can start, there are a number of processes that must be completed so that the operator(s) shall be able to make changes in the installations in a safe and responsible manner, and for the regulation authority (DSA) to be able to approve changes in accordance with regulations and international standards. In preparation for the liquidation and during the shutdown, there will be a need to establish a new waste handling facility, including plans for a US-developed mobile melt consolidation facility (MMC). The procurement is covered by the Security Act and reflected in the contracting authority ́s requirement specifications and security requirements. Tenderers who would like to offer in this procurement are asked separately to familiarise themselves with the stated guidelines, prerequisites and requirements.
sig_5ec44ba10636452c5bf2.title: Procurement of consultancy services for nuclear security, including handling used fuel, radiation protection and risk assessment.

sig_5ec5658725ff26b37d76.description: The gemeente Leeuwarden together with the Municipality of Waadhoeke is looking for a partner for the supply, implementation, and management of a Learning Experience Platform (LXP) combined with a Learning Management System (LMS). We are looking for a platform that offers us the possibility to use a pre-filled standard library with external content and to integrate and manage our own created internal content. It is also important that the platform can be accessed by the municipalities that join and that the content can be opened/closed per municipality. The chosen solution must be scalable, adaptive, and future-proof. We expect that approximately 2.500 employees of the two municipalities will make use of the platform (in particular the LXP). In addition, we expect that 8 employees will perform back-office activities (in the LMS) and that functional management will be carried out by a team consisting of 5 persons.

sig_5ee014d4aebe9663afd1.description: Project reason TenneT requires a portfolio management system (PMS) to support electricity trading in the short-term market (day-ahead and intraday) in Germany. Objective of the tender The objective is the procurement of a high-performance PMS to support electricity trading. In accordance with TenneT's architectural guidelines, the solution is to be cloud-based, preferably operated in the tenderer's cloud. In coordination with TenneT, deployment in a third-party provider's cloud (e.g. Azure) or at TenneT is also possible. The system will be used in the electricity trading sector and must cover the following main functions: - Portfolio management - Connection to power exchanges - Trading overviews & GUI - Algo-trader / trading support in continuous intraday trading - Data management - Reporting & analysis - Settlement - Schedule management Scope of services - Provision of a COTS software solution (licences) - Support & maintenance of this solution (maintenance) - Hosting of the solution - Application management services - Consulting and training services Procedural notice A detailed specification of services as well as other procedural-relevant documents will be provided after signing a non-disclosure agreement. sig_5ee2299248e7774e26b5.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This Department of War (DoW) Drone Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the DoW Drone Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the DoW will better incentivize industry innovation. DoW Drone Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional DoW acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the DoW to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The DoW has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform DoW Drone Marketplace capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The DoW is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The DoW anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled bythe DoW. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST (AOI) This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY AOIs or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Payloads Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS): Full Systems Air Vehicles Maritime Systems: Surface and Undersea Systems Maritime Reconnaissance and Domain Awareness Littoral and Amphibious Support Ground Systems: Reconnaissance and Surveillance Systems Logistics and Equipment Transport Combat and Tactical Support Platforms Counter- UAS: Mutli-Domain Sensing and Detection Command, Control and Data Fusion Defeat Mechanisms (Kinetic and Non-Kinetic) Platform & Operation Integration Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects Drone Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any AOI in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment when providing a submission to an IWS. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below and within the specific C4Ss posted. The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined in the attachment. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for, as applicable, for phase 2 and/or 3, the submission may be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the DoW and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the DoW and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. Area of Interest in Subject Line usarmy.redstone.cpe-avn.mbx.uasmarketplaceiws@army.mil C4S Brief submissions (Section D) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: USARMY Redstone Arsenal PEO AVN Mailbox DoW Drone Marketplace SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the DoW will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoW that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoW for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoW has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoW relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

sig_5ee9a9418066f63bf95c.description: The subject of the Public Contract is the development, delivery and implementation of the National Repository Catalogue (NRC) information system ("NRC System"). The subject of the Public Contract shall consist in the delivery of the NRC System, incl. the design and implementation of the NRC System into the Contracting Authority's IT environment and the creation of integration interfaces, putting the NRC System into operation including the provision of trial operation. Part of the subject of the Public Contract is also the services of subsequent operation support, maintenance and development of the NRC System for the anticipated provision period of 48 months. The NRC is conceived as a central register intended for the registration and management of data on Czech research data repositories. Its aim is to provide trustworthy, machine-readable and long-term sustainable information on what repositories exist in the Czech Republic, who operates them, what metadata standards and ontologies they use, and to ensure connection to external services. The entire architecture of the NRC is designed to respect FAIR principles, i.e., to support interoperability, transparency and the reuse of information. The NRC will register all research data repositories that are being created or will be created within the National Repository Platform (NRP), or will be connected to this platform. These are primarily 40 data repositories arising within the NRP project (so-called pilot repositories) and the Open Science II call (other domain repositories). These are entirely new repositories (e.g. CzBio) or innovations of existing repositories (e.g. Lindat/CLARIAH). The obligation to register a repository in the NRC is in these cases established by the Rules for Creating New and Modifying Existing Domain Repositories in the National Repository Platform and stems from the relevant legal acts of the projects. The NRC System must integrate the following components into a single, well-connected functional solution: 1. Cordra (NRC knowledge base) 2. Middleware (application layer) 3. User interface (UI) 4. Skosmos + Apache Jena Fuseki (vocabulary module) 5. MSCR (Metadata Schema and Crosswalk Registry) Detailed requirements for the NRC System, its technical parameters and functionalities of the NRC System are set out in the Specification of the NRC System for Consultation Purposes ("NRC System Specification"), which the Contracting Authority shall provide to registered suppliers upon receipt of a signed non-disclosure agreement (see point 4 of the invitation). sig_5f003ea430586fe31373.description: LCRCA is preparing for the introduction of bus franchising, starting in September 2026 with the full LCR bus network being franchised by the end of 2027, the LCRCA will directly manage network design, operational performance and operator payments. A Central AVL system (CAVL) is needed to act as the single source of truth for vehicle tracking, punctuality and network performance monitoring. The system will need to be fully tested and deployed prior to the end of May 2026 CAVL will consolidate data from multiple sources - including Electronic Ticket Machines (ETMs), on-bus static AVL units and SIRI feeds - to produce consistent and accurate real-time information for passenger systems and performance analytics for both LCRCA and operators. The CAVL system will underpin the LCRCA's franchising and customer delivery framework. It must be cloud-based, secure and capable of handling data from all franchised operators, with configurable outputs for real-time information, punctuality and contractual performance. Core functions include: • Punctuality monitoring - covering both start point (PM1) and intermediate points (PM2) as part of the bus franchising customer delivery framework. • Real-time monitoring of vehicle location (including live map), speed, headway, dwell time and journey times • Acting as the authoritative AVL data source for all franchised operators. • Managing disruptions and disruption messaging • Ingesting AVL data from both ETMs and static AVL units • Ensuring consistent GPS accuracy and refresh rates across operators. • Validating schedules using TXC files to identify early, late, on-time and missed mileage • Generating punctuality, reliability and Excess Waiting Time (EWT) KPIs. • Providing operator-specific access controls so that each operator can only view and report on its own data. • Offering open APIs and data feeds for integration with real-time passenger information systems and journey planners. • Delivering configurable dashboards and reporting tools for both operators and LCRCA. • Supporting integration with the future Contract Management and Payment Calculator System Suppliers are invited to express their interest in receiving further details about this potential future procurement by opting in via the Proactis portal. As part of this engagement, suppliers should review the pre-market engagement brief and submit the requested information. In particular, we are seeking your views on how your systems could meet LCRCA's requirements, including: • Technical feasibility of your proposed solution • Deployment approach, with consideration for meeting delivery timescales • Ongoing support and maintenance arrangements Your input will help shape the specification and ensure the procurement reflects market capability. To respond to this pre market engagement please go to: https://procontract.due-north.com/ if you are registered or register at: https://procontract.due-north.com/SupplierRegistration/Register You will then be able to search for the project name: Central AVL system (CAVL) Pre Market Engagement or the project reference number: DN794680 You will then be able to follow the directions to register your interest and submit the requested. Lot 1: .
