sig_5f3aeb38e2de1d43c4a1.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) requires a solution that will be used by 450 users who work for different health and government organisations with the appropriate access and control permissions. It needs to be able to: • Increase scalability of licences should there be a business need. The Licences must include the ability to collect and then disseminate data to third parties. • Create fraud/crime allegation reports that can be developed by users and then be promoted to investigations and the ability to create investigations and add allegation report and intelligence. • Capture investigative activity undertaken as part of criminal investigations: record, retain, review, reveal activity notes, tasks, reasonable lines of enquiry, key investigative events (arrests, searches, interviews, court appearances etc) decision making, outcomes (criminal offences, internal and external disciplinary, financial outcomes), nominal data (people, subjects, addresses, telephone number, emails, bank accounts, organisations and vehicles), statements, exhibits, unused material, financial investigation and intelligence and risk assessment/checklists. • Have assessment, sanitisation and actioning functionality that allows for the management of an investigation or case from the beginning of the process, including the ability to have them endorsed at or by tasking with rationale and then transfer to operational teams with all relevant intelligence and evidence. • To manage disclosure (CPIA) and create and update prosecution bundles submitted to Crown Prosecution Service. MG9 witness list and statement bundle; MG12 exhibit list and exhibit bundle; MG6 disclosure schedules can be generated and submitted; other MG forms can form part of a prosecution file submission to Crown Prosecution Service by direct a Two Way Interface or similar integration, or export functionality. Functionality to populate other forms in the MG suite. • Information exchange with the CPS by exporting case files and exhibits to their systems, support email notifications from system disclosure. • Issue and manage task workflows, data requests, assigned lines of enquiries, updates via a local tasking and coordination process. Should have information and activity recording, to illustrate new tasking and to highlight when actions have, or indeed have not, been completed by target date. • Record, sanitise, manage, and disseminate 3x5x2 intelligence (including financial intelligence) reports to internal, external users and third-party intelligence organisations. Manage confidential sources and ability to capture pieces of information from external sources. • The solution should be able to record Financial Investigation activity in terms of Proceeds of Crime (2002) investigations and proceedings as well as manage disclosure (CPIA) and create and update prosecution bundles submitted to Crown Prosecution Service. Centrally it needs to capture Fraud Risk (Prevention) Assessments with the ability to disseminate across users to communication fraud risks across the NHS. Information management reporting needs to have capability for all record data, including time, resource, and cost management. • Different levels of configuration and customisation are required that are available to admin users within the system. It should have the ability to easily change the status of a person from subject to witness and vice versa. The solution must allow users to delete or archive data in accordance with NHSCFA internal retention schedule. The solution should facilitate marking records following the Government Security Classifications Policy. • The solution must incorporate into the design the ability to hold any forms required during managing cases, such as investigations plans, disclosure strategy and any associated documents, and allow their searchability.) • The solution should have the ability to RAG rate operational fraud risk activity as part of the ongoing review process. The system must have the ability to rapidly allocate and report upon a risk for any assessment recorded, this could for example be a person, an organisation, or a particular investigation. Lot 1: .
sig_5f3aeb38e2de1d43c4a1.title: NHS Counter Fraud Authority (CFA) - Case Management System

sig_5f42b5a5125680c56177.description: The subject of the contract is the creation of a modern digital Public Health Surveillance (PHS) Mechanism. With the implementation of the Mechanism and the utilisation of epidemiological data collection tools, the following will be achieved: integral and secure data processing, production of mathematical and stochastic surveillance analyses, analysis of the geographical and demographic dimension of the data, creation of a modern Epidemiological Surveillance Control Centre, support for Competent Committees with the ability to access documented data and reports, provision of an appropriate emergency reporting procedure by physicians, promotion, communication and publication of findings and guidelines, and forwarding of data to reference centres. The Project synthesises the framework for the digital operation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism based on the already defined procedures, standards, organisation and regulatory framework determined by the implementation study of this project and the other sub-projects of the Action. The Project briefly includes the following distinct actions: 1. Supply, development, installation, configuration and operation of a multi-channel information management and dissemination platform (Web, Mobile App, etc.). 2. Integrated platform for the collection, processing and storage of data based on the general architecture of a DataWarehouse for the purpose of producing reports. 3. Digital tools: Data Mining, Intelligent Reporting, Predictive Analytics, Statistical packages for operational decision support (STATA: MP 2-Core, Perpetual Licence, SPSS: v18, Base Subscription, Perpetual licence) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). 4. Preparation of 3 CAPTURE/RECAPTURE studies to estimate the representativeness and rate of reported data. 5. Preparation of an analysis study on the need for a national 'living' disease registry based on COVID experience and international best practices. 6. Implementation & execution study, training plan and publicity action plan. 7. Training actions and production of educational content. 8. Workshop design, for the information, awareness and participation of the involved stakeholders in the implementation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism. 9. Design of a Public Health Scientific Conference with the subject of extracting best practices regarding the operation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism, with the participation of internationally renowned experts and all involved stakeholders.
sig_5f42b5a5125680c56177.title: Development of a new integrated epidemiological surveillance mechanism

sig_5f7f7c15c9659041a9e2.description: Nexus Multi Academy Trust (“Nexus” or “the Authority”) is seeking to establish an Open Framework for the provision of ICT products, services and solutions to the education sector. The Framework is intended to provide Nexus and other eligible Contracting Authorities with a compliant and accessible route to market for the procurement of ICT requirements. The Framework is divided into three Lots: Lot 1 – ICT Support Services and Managed Services Lot 2 – Professional Services Lot 3 – Hardware Suppliers may tender for one, multiple or all Lots. There will be no limit on the number of Suppliers that may be appointed to each Lot. The Framework will operate as an Open Framework in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and is intended to be reopened periodically to allow new Suppliers to apply for appointment. The maximum duration of the Open Framework will be eight years. The estimated maximum value of the Framework is £1,000,000,000 excluding VAT over its maximum term. This represents estimated potential expenditure through the Framework and does not constitute a guarantee of expenditure, minimum spend, volume of business or exclusivity. The Framework will be established and operated by Nexus Multi Academy Trust and will be available for use by eligible Contracting Authorities in respect of publicly funded schools and colleges. Lot 1: Lot 1 – ICT Support Services and Managed Services. This Lot covers the provision of managed ICT services and associated support solutions to educational establishments. Services may include the management, maintenance, monitoring and support of ICT infrastructure, networks, cloud environments, software applications, end user devices, and associated technology services. The scope of this Lot includes, but is not limited to, remote and on-site ICT support, service desk provision, cyber security services, safeguarding technologies, connectivity solutions, backup and disaster recovery, MIS support, infrastructure management, ICT consultancy, training and strategic ICT planning. The Lot is intended to provide Customers with access to Suppliers capable of delivering the full range of end-to-end requirements across both operational ICT support and strategic technology services, enabling organisations to maintain secure, reliable and effective technology environments that support teaching, learning and organisational performance. Please see more detail in the tender documentation. Lot 2: Lot 2 – Professional Services. This Lot covers the provision of specialist ICT related professional services, consultancy, technical expertise and project delivery support to educational establishments. Services may include the planning, design, implementation, migration, optimisation and review of technology solutions, systems, services, and digital transformation programmes. The scope of this Lot includes, but is not limited to, ICT consultancy, digital transformation support, technical design services, solution architecture, project and programme management, business analysis, cyber security consultancy, cloud strategy, systems integration, data migration, change management, adoption services, training, Procurement support, independent technical advisory services, audit, due diligence, and post-implementation review activities. Suppliers may provide strategic advice, technical expertise and delivery support throughout the lifecycle of a project, from initial requirements gathering and options appraisal through to implementation, user adoption and benefits realisation. Services may be delivered on a project specific, interim or advisory basis depending on the requirements of a Customer. The Lot is intended to provide Customers with access to specialist expertise and delivery capability to support technology-enabled change, improve organisational performance, manage risk and maximise the value of technology investments. Please see more detail in the tender documents. Lot 3: Lot 3 – Hardware. This Lot covers the supply, installation, configuration, and associated services relating to ICT hardware and technology equipment for educational establishments. The Lot is designed to provide access to a broad range of hardware solutions that support teaching, learning, administration, communication, and organisational operations. The scope of this Lot includes, but is not limited to, end-user devices, servers, network equipment, storage solutions, audio visual equipment, classroom technology, peripherals and accessories. Suppliers may also provide associated services including installation, configuration, imaging, deployment, asset tagging, asset management, warranty support and technology refresh services. Suppliers may support the full lifecycle of hardware provision, from specification and supply through to installation, deployment, ongoing support and replacement planning. Services may be delivered as individual purchases, project-based deployments or wider technology refresh programmes depending on the requirements of a Customer. The Lot is intended to provide Customers with access to Suppliers capable of delivering reliable, cost-effective and scalable hardware solutions that support educational outcomes, operational efficiency and long-term technology strategies. Please see more detail in the tender documentation.

The Clinical Comprehensive Collection must provide support to students, residents, doctors and libraries, enabling them access to knowledge and including: access to more than 215 trusted Lippincott® journals, covering more than 50 activities in the medical and scientific field, access for 3 simultaneous users, 10 vouchers for APC (Article Processing Charges) for annual publication in LWW open access journals (hybrid and gold OA) in the year 2026, accompanying services as determined by the offer and the publisher's valid licence documentation.; Medical Education International Basic and Anatomical Sciences Integrated Collection and the Acland Anatomy collection. Acland Anatomy contains 330 video clips of real anatomical structures from bones to surface anatomy. The LWW Health Library – Medical Education International Basic and Anatomical Sciences Integrated Collection enables interactive online access to top-tier Lippincott textbooks on fundamental topics, videos, images, clinical case studies and quiz collections for students and researchers.

Conclusion of a centralised public procurement framework agreement for the procurement of central and client system operation services for organisations falling within the scope of Government Decree 301/2018 (XII. 27.) on the National Telecommunications and Informatics Council as well as Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség Zártkörűen Működő Részvénytársaság and the centralised public procurement system for governmental IT procurements (hereinafter referred to as the DKÜ Decree), and for organisations voluntarily joining the centralised public procurement procedure. As a result of this public procurement procedure, the Tenderers that have concluded the framework agreement shall be tasked with providing central and client system services in accordance with the provisions of the Procurement Documents, taking into account the following main product categories and quantitative data: A total of 16 service categories 1. Data transmission service 2. Data centre service 3. Data storage and backup service 4. Identification code service 5. Cloud-based service 6. Network operation service 7. HW assurance service 8. Internet service 9. IP voice service 10. ITB data processing services 11. ITB incident services 12. ITB security services 13. Optical dark fibre pair lease service 14. Expert and engineering services 15. Support service 16. WDM services The detailed product list for the 1 supply packages forming the subject of the procedure shall consist of the technical specification and 319 price list rows. The Contracting Authority wishes to procure central and client system operation services within the framework of this procedure. The task of the Successful Tenderer is to operate at least an online notification channel for ordering the listed services and receiving related notifications. With the help of the listed service categories, central and client-side services based on equipment previously procured from a DKÜ framework agreement or individually, which are necessary for carrying out daily operational tasks, can be provided without procuring separate equipment, and the IT service background that effectively ensures the appropriate standard of performance of administrative and operational processes introduced at the Affected Organisations can also be created without procuring equipment. All services must operate with an annual availability matching this, considering the relevant service time windows. According to Annex 1 of Ministry of Interior Decree 41/2015 (VII. 15.) on the technological security requirements defined in Act 2013 of on the electronic information security of state and municipal bodies, as well as on secure information equipment, products, and classification into security classes and security levels, systems can currently be classified into security class 1-5, and damage events of varying degrees per class may occur. (Ministry of Interior Decree 2025.01.01 shall lose its effect, and instead, Ministry of Cabinet Office Decree 7/2024 (VI. 24.) on "The requirements for classification into security classes and the specific protection measures to be applied in the case of individual security classes" shall govern the classification into security classes.) In the case of the systems necessary for the operation of the Affected Organisations falling within the scope of the Framework Agreement to be concluded as a result of this procedure, based on the quality of the data handled and the risk of loss of confidence, the systems concerned in this public procurement procedure are expected to belong to security class 2 or higher based on their current classification, which, based on the Contracting Authority's market knowledge, constitutes the vast majority of the systems operating at the Affected Organisations. The Successful Tenderer's task is to ensure operating conditions complying with the indicated requirements. Data security-guaranteeing solutions: In order to ensure that the protection of the electronic information systems of the Affected Organisations falling within the scope of Act 2013 of on the electronic information security of state and municipal bodies (hereinafter: Ibtv.) is also ensured in accordance with the relevant legislation, the Contracting Authority expects that, during the performance of services related to the product groups listed in this chapter, having regard to Section 3. (1) of the Ibtv., the Successful Tenderer shall handle the data managed by the Affected Organisations exclusively in electronic information systems operated and stored in the territory of Hungary. The affected product groups are as follows • ITB data processing services • ITB incident services • ITB security services • Data storage and backup services, excluding the following services o Escrow service - 30-day retention (daily Budapest) o Escrow service - 30-day retention (daily rural) o Escrow service - 30-day retention (weekly) • Identification code services • Data centre services • Network operation services The Contracting Authority records that, in accordance with the interpretive provision under point 18 of Section 3 of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.), the total quantity stipulated in the framework agreement is represented by the framework amount (calculated without options) of net 69 300 000 000 HUF (hereinafter: framework amount). The Contracting Authority records, on the basis of the provisions of paragraph (4) of Section 21 of Government Decree 321/2015 (X. 30.), that the expected magnitude (value) of separate contracts to be implemented on the basis of the framework agreement and to be performed at the same time is net 1 799 754 750 HUF. Within this, the expected magnitude of contracts relating to wired and/or wireless network operation services directly serving client devices is on average net 337 000 000 HUF, while the expected magnitude of contracts relating to data centre services is on average net 148 000 000 HUF. The Contracting Authority prepares public procurement documents (hereinafter: Other procurement documents) supplementing the call for tenders, fulfilling Section 1 of Section 57 of the Kbt.

For the sake of clarity, the Contracting Authority records that the conceptual scope of Procurement Documents means the Tender Notice and the Other Procurement Documents taken together. The Contracting Authority refers to the services to be procured generally by the term "product" during the procedure. The specific quantity and specific subject – assembled from the elements forming part of the FA – of the individual procurements to be implemented following the conclusion of the Framework Agreement shall be determined following the conclusion of the Framework Agreement, during the reopening of competition (point c) of paragraph (2) of Section 105. of the Kbt.).

sig_5faad84e0c9126476753.description: This tender seeks an integrated platform for Customer Relationship Management & Broadcast System for OOH and DOOH for Metroselskabet I/S. Metroselskabet is issuing this tender for a strategically important contract with a total duration of 12 years, with the possibility of extending the contract by three additional 12-month periods. The purpose is to establish a stable, long-term foundation for Metroselskabet’s commercial activities and to ensure continuity, consistency and sustained commercial value over time. A long-term and robust and sustainable contractual framework is considered essential to enable the successful development and implementation of commercial initiatives, while ensuring that the necessary knowledge, expertise and relationships can be maintained throughout the contract period. This tender presents an opportunity for potential tenderers to bid for the contract regarding Metroselskabets new CRM and Broadcast-solution (the solution). Metroselskabet needs an integrated platform to support the commercial and operational management of its DOOH and OOH advertising business across the Copenhagen Metro. Metroselskabet is in the process of bringing the commercial management of advertising activities across the Copenhagen Metro in-house. These activities have previously been managed externally, and the transition therefore involves establishing the necessary internal organization, processes, systems and capabilities to enable Metroselskabet to take direct responsibility for its advertising business. The procurement of the solution is a key part of this transition. The Solution is expected to provide the technological foundation for Metroselskabet’s future advertising operations and support the new organization in managing the advertising value chain efficiently and consistently from sales through campaign execution and follow-up. The Customer seeks a standard, cloud-based platform that enables Metroselskabet to manage its advertising business from end to end. The Solution is expected to provide the commercial team with the tools needed to manage customers and sales opportunities, prepare quotations, check available advertising inventory, agree on pricing and book campaigns. Once a campaign is sold, the same Solution is expected to support campaign planning, creative handling and approval, scheduling and broadcasting, followed by monitoring of campaign delivery, Proof-of-Play, invoicing-basis and reporting. The Solution is expected to provide a connected workflow between these activities, ensuring that information established during the sales process can be used directly in subsequent planning, execution and reporting without unnecessary re-entry or manual transfer of data.
sig_5faad84e0c9126476753.title: CRM & Broadcast

sig_5fb1260d8f4da49f764c.description: Excerpt from article 3 of the tender documentation as amended by Clarification of Tender Documentation No 4: 3.1 Public contracts awarded under a DPS shall be supply public contracts pursuant to Section 14 subsection 1 of the Act. Supplies under this DPS shall mean the acquisition of items, which apart from purchase shall also mean rental, usufructuary lease, leasing or operational leasing. 3.2 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS shall be the supply of office printers, photocopying machines and multi-function printing equipment (hereinafter also collectively referred to as "Printing Equipment"). 3.3 Part of the subject matter or a separate subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS may be service and material performance. 3.4 Service and material performance shall mean: a) regular inspection and comprehensive maintenance of the Printing Equipment according to the number of printed pages or the service plan of the Printing Equipment manufacturer; b) complete service and repairs of the Printing Equipment including fault clearance, adjustment and commissioning of the Printing Equipment, complete supply and replacement of all spare parts; c) supply of consumables (e.g. office paper, toners, waste containers, belt units, fixing units, heads, rollers, manufacturer-prescribed maintenance kits, developer units, imaging units, etc.) including take-back of used consumables; d) system update of the Printing Equipment; e) software tools for the management of the service and material performance of the Printing Equipment; and f) other performance required as part of the inspection, service or maintenance of the Printing Equipment. 3.5 The subject matter of the public contract may also be the supply and implementation of software for the printing solution. This shall mean software that can centrally in particular: a) determine individual persons authorised to use the Printing Equipment, including determining the scope of authority of a specific person (e.g. setting the requirement for black-and-white or duplex printing, setting quotas); b) make the use of the Printing Equipment conditional upon logging in of the authorised person via a card reader or other device of similar function; c) manage document workflows; d) ensure reporting and cost allocation of executed printing or other tasks of the Printing Equipment; e) enable printing from mobile devices; and f) protect against document theft or data loss. 3.6 Part of the supply and implementation of software for the printing solution may also be the procurement of card readers or other similar devices and, where applicable, the procurement of such cards or other similar devices. 3.7 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under this DPS may also be service and material performance or software for the printing solution whose subject matter will be only some of the items listed in subsections 3.5 and 3.6 of the TD. 3.8 Part of the service and material performance or software for the printing solution may also be other customary components thereof, even if they are not explicitly stated in this TD. 3.9 The Central Purchasing Body anticipates awarding public contracts under the DPS at pre-determined irregular intervals depending on its operational needs and the operational needs of the commissioning contracting authorities. The volumes of individual public contracts awarded under the DPS are likewise dependent on the operational needs of the Central Purchasing Body and individual Commissioning Contracting Authorities, and their number may range from units up to hundreds of units in a specific public contract. 3.10 The subject matter of public contracts awarded under the DPS and its technical conditions will always be detailed in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act. 3.11 The Central Purchasing Body is entitled, within the scope of public contracts awarded under the DPS, to require the submission of a tender in the form of an electronic catalogue pursuant to Section 215 of the Act. This shall always be set out in detail in the specific call for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act.

sig_5fce472d03558e520413.description: The Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) provides awards to federally recognized 1 Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-serving institutions, and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions to promote high quality science (including sociology, psychology, anthropology, linguistics, economics and bioeconomics, statistics, and other social and behavioral sciences; natural sciences; computer science, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and cybersecurity), technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), STEM education, research, and outreach. Support is available to TCUP-eligible institutions (see the Additional Eligibility subsection of Section IV of this solicitation) for transformative capacity-building or community engagement projects through Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) , Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) , TCUP for Secondary and Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) , TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) , Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) , and Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) . Collaborations led by TCUP institutions that involve non-TCUP institutions of higher education are supported through TCUP Partnerships , with the participation of other NSF programs to support the work of non-TCUP institutions. Finally, research studies that further the scholarly activity of individual faculty members are supported through Small Grants for Research (SGR) . Through the opportunities highlighted above, as well as collaborations with other National Science Foundation (NSF) divisions and directorates, and other organizations, TCUP aims to increase Native individuals' participation in STEM careers, improve the quality of STEM programs at TCUP-eligible institutions, and facilitate the development of a strong STEM enterprise in TCUP institutions' service areas. TCUP supports transformative capacity-building, community engagement, or research projects at TCUP-eligible institutions through the following funding tracks: Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) projects provide support to design, implement, and assess comprehensive institutional improvements in STEM education and research capacity at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education. By strengthening STEM education and STEM education research, successful projects will increase the number of STEM students and improve the quality of their preparation. ICE-TI projects create and/or adapt and assess innovative models and materials for teaching and learning in STEM, embody knowledge about how students learn most effectively in STEM teaching and learning activities, and bring STEM disciplinary advances into the undergraduate or graduate experience. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees offered by TCUP-eligible institutions or significantly enhance instructional approaches. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) support the attainment of a short-term, well-defined goal to improve the quality of STEM education at an eligible institution. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects could, for example, enhance academic infrastructure by systematically adding traditional knowledge to the scope or content of a STEM course, updating curricula, modernizing laboratory research equipment, developing and delivering professional development for K-12 STEM educators, or improving the computational infrastructure. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees or significantly enhance instructional approaches. TCUP for Secondary & Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) supports in-service professional development in STEM disciplinary or STEM education content and/or research for K-12 STEM teachers in the relevant service area. Examples of project activities include, but are not limited to, professional development involving seminar series and engagement in STEM instruction and content during the academic year, structured series of summer intensive workshops and trainings, and summer research opportunities. The objective of this strand is to broaden the instructional capacity for STEM in the K-12 workforce and thereby to the entire community, and to build the capacity for STEM disciplinary or education research among participating educational professionals. TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) coalesce the STEM and/or STEM education expertise into a team, designed to support and promote the STEM goals, needs, aspirations, or interests of the chartering reservation or tribe(s). TEA Centers may address a critical tribal or community need or focus on a realm of research or design that is beyond the scope of individual research grants or that is of interest to multiple tribes. The objective of this strand is to build on the capacity developed through prior TCUP support and apply expertise to collaborations with communities in the institution’s service area, or nationally. The Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) strand supports projects at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education to upgrade the cyberinfrastructure necessary to conduct, expand, manage and administer STEM programs of study, including research. The objective of this strand is to equip TCUP institutions to meet the demands of virtual instruction, advanced computing, and data science opportunities. Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) provides support for activities that prepare an institution for Implementation-level projects. Consequently, they are available only to TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education that have never received TCUP support, have not received TCUP support within the previous five years, or are embarking on a significantly novel STEM strategic plan. Examples of supported activities include completing an institutional assessment of its current STEM instructional capacity, or engaging in conversations necessary to formulate a shared vision of what that capacity should be and how to achieve it. Pre-TI awards can support staff and faculty release time, travel, stakeholder gatherings, and associated administrative costs. The objective of this strand is to conduct self-studies and formulate strategic plans for the development of STEM instructional programs of study. The TCUP Partnerships strand provides support for collaborations that will improve TCUP institutions' instructional and research capacity in STEM fields supported by NSF; attract, retain, and support TCUP students in internships and research endeavors deemed to be necessary for a complete curriculum offering; and engage partner universities to provide an academic grounding and a successful transition for students who wish to study or attain degrees in STEM fields supported by NSF. TCUP Partnerships broaden the number of scientific disciplines available to students at TCUP institution through collaborations with non-TCUP institutions. Active Pre-Engineering Education Collaboratives or Partnerships in Geoscience Education awards are not affected by this revision. The objective of this strand is the development, through instructional and research capacity-building, of academic and career pathways for TCUP students through supporting collaborative projects between and among TCUP and non-TCUP institutions. Interested teams of collaborators for which a TCUP institution serves as lead should contact the TCUP program directors. Support for non-TCUP partners must be obtained from other NSF programs, which follows the procedures of the prior Partnership strands. Small Grants for Research (SGR) strand support STEM or STEM Education faculty members at TCUP-eligible institutions to initiate or pursue research projects or programs that may include undergraduate or graduate student engagement. Awards are intended to help further the faculty member's research capability and effectiveness; improve research and teaching at his or her home institution and create and study new models and innovations in STEM teaching and learning. International research or collaborations are strongly encouraged. TCUP students may seek support for international research opportunities under the guidance of a TCUP STEM or STEM education faculty member and an international research collaborator. These awards are particularly appropriate as a means of recruiting and retaining highly qualified scientists, engineers, and educators at TCUP-eligible institutions. The objective of this strand is to support faculty research and professional development that build research capacity at TCUP institutions. [1] Executive Order 13021 defines Tribal Colleges and Universities ("tribal colleges") as those institutions cited in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 301 note), and other institutions that qualify for funding under the Tribally Controlled Community College Assistance Act of 1978, (25 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.), as well as Navajo Community College as authorized in the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, Public Law 95-471, Title II (25 U.S.C. 640a note). The term "Alaska Native-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 20 percent Alaska Native students. The term "Native Hawaiian-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian students. Most TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education are two-year or community colleges. See the Who May Submit Proposals section in this solicitation for further details.

sig_5fcea02b484c0f4bd326.description: Horley Town Council invites quotes from suitably qualified suppliers for website design, development, hosting and maintenance services. REQUIREMENTS: We require a comprehensive website solution meeting all statutory requirements for local government, including: - Full WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility compliance from launch - Compliance with Local Government Transparency Code 2015 - Support for Assertion 10 audit requirements for digital and data compliance - Modern, mobile-responsive design with intuitive CMS - Secure hosting with SSL, backups and disaster recovery - Multiple user licences for content management - SEO optimisation and social media integration - Events calendar and booking system - News section and photo galleries - Document library with version control - Committee and councillor information pages - Online consultation and engagement tools - Resident reporting tools for local service issues (highways, fly-tipping, etc.) - Forms for council services and applications - Venue hire booking system - Contact forms (GDPR compliant) - Newsletter subscription functionality - Mapping for local amenities - Portal links to planning authority and online meetings (Webex) - Migration of existing website content with URL redirects - Comprehensive staff training on CMS - User manuals and video tutorials ONGOING SUPPORT: - Regular software updates and security patches - Continuous performance monitoring - Technical support during business hours - Annual accessibility compliance review (included in core service) - Maintenance of WCAG 2.2 AA compliance - Regular backups - Website analytics and usage reporting - Proactive notification of legislative/regulatory changes ESSENTIAL CRITERIA: Suppliers must demonstrate: - Minimum 3 years' experience with town and parish council websites in England - Portfolio of at least 5 current websites meeting WCAG 2.2 AA standards - Detailed knowledge of Local Government Transparency Code 2015 and Assertion 10 requirements - Proven technical capability for accessible website delivery - Adequate support infrastructure - Financial stability and appropriate insurance CONTRACT: Initial 2-year period with performance monitoring through quarterly reviews. Full specification available at: https://www.horleysurrey-tc.gov.uk/news/article/1544 SUBMISSION: Quotes by email to info@horleysurrey-tc.gov.uk by Friday 27 February 2026 at 12:00 noon.

sig_5fd4c4eb1fe23425d9fe.description: The services involve the drafting of the forest management plan, a product of management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically substantiated, by which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and subsequently maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and of the forest as a whole at the values pertaining to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Article 63 paragraph (11) of Law No. 331/2024 on the Forest Code, with subsequent amendments and completions, it is necessary that the drafting of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state's public property forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The manner of managing the state's public property forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and amendments thereto are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state public property land, the plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of property in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Clarifications regarding the tender documentation may be requested before the deadline for submitting bids, as follows: at the latest on the 18 -th day before the deadline established for submitting bids in the notice of participation. The Contracting Authority will clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarifications, as follows: at the latest on the 10 -th day before the deadline established for submitting bids in the notice of participation. NOTE: The contracting authority is not obliged to respond to requests for clarifications/additional information that were not addressed within the established deadline. Forest management services for the Brad Forest District - DS Hunedoara, with an area of 18.486,87 ha, in accordance with the specifications.
sig_5fd4c4eb1fe23425d9fe.title: Forest management services - DS Hunedoara 2026

sig_5fd4dec428e1f400f7c8.description: Cabinet Office intends to procure a robust, industry-standard Software as a Service (SaaS) Learning Management System (LMS) through the Government Commercial Agency's (GCA) RM6219 Learning and Training Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS), to support the new National School of Government and Public Services Learning & Development (L&D) offering. The LMS will provide a scalable platform to support a user base of over 558,000 users and must meet mandatory security and information assurance requirements, including UK hosting of data and adherence to Secure by Design principles. Mandatory Requirements Security and information assurance requirements, specifically mandatory UK hosting of data and adherence to 'Secure by Design' requirements Scalable and accessible to support over 558,000 users Please note - The mandatory requirement must be met by all potential bidders Essential requirements Core LMS capability (i.e. learning catalogue, content tagging) Booking and administration functionality Admin controls for end-to-end of central delivery offer and repository Migration support (for catalogue of learning) Quality data, including feedback, reporting and evaluation The requirement is for the provision of the LMS platform and associated implementation/support services. L&D content supplied by the LMS provider is out of scope; the platform will be used to host internally developed learning content. Lot 1: . The procurement will be conducted through the Government Commercial Agency's (GCA) RM6219 Learning and Training Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). Please see link to the Framework Agreement - https://www.gca.gov.uk/agreements/RM6219 Only appointed suppliers on the Learning and Training DPS who meet our essential requirements, will be invited to bid for this procurement. We encourage interested suppliers to complete their application to join the RM6219 Learning and Training DPS by 30th October 2026 at the latest, with the aim of being appointed onto the DPS in time for us to start our call off procurement. We will not be able to invite suppliers to bid that are not appointed by the time we start the procurement, so we urge you to apply as soon as possible. The procurement process will be run on our own procurement portal: e-Sourcing - https://crowncommercialservice.bravosolution.co.uk/web/login.html. Suppliers must also be registered here with details that match their DPS application. Any suppliers that are not registered on this platform by the time we launch our competition will not be included in the competition. The dedicated link above is for Supplier registration, including guidance documents and Customer Service Centre details, should you require help. Note that there will be a 1% levy payable by suppliers to GCA on the payment amounts received from awarded contracts, so suppliers are encouraged to factor this in. A levy is standard across GCA agreements. It funds GCA operating costs and enables the benefits that the commercial agreements provide. For a list of supplier minimum requirements and instructions on how to apply to join the RM6219 Learning and Training DPS, download GCA's quick supplier guide.
sig_5fd4dec428e1f400f7c8.title: National School of Government and Public Services

sig_5fd589435b9533bb721f.description: The subject of this Services Contract is the preparation of the Feasibility Study for the modernisation of the DN7F sector between DN7 and the roundabout arranged within the Cornet Road Junction of Section 3 of the Sibiu - Pitesti Motorway, in order to ensure the road infrastructure for the discharge of the motorway into DN 7 of the Cornet Road Junction of the Sibiu-Pitesti motorway, Section 3, in accordance with the provisions of the Specifications and of the legislation in the field. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (1) of Law no. 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the deadline until which any economic operator interested in participating in the public procurement procedure has the right to request clarifications or additional information in connection with the awarding documentation is 18 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (2) of Law 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the Contracting Authority establishes a single deadline in which it will respond to all requests for clarification / additional information, as follows: 11 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The deadline for responding to clarifications has been established so that economic operators have an adequate period to analyse the awarding documentation and, subsequently, to prepare tenders in view of the responses provided by the Contracting Authority. In accordance with the provisions of art. 104 para. (8) of Law no. 98/2016, the Contracting Authority opts for the subsequent acquisition of new similar services from the tenderer whose tender will be declared winning within this public procurement procedure in the amount of 207.381,16 lei, excluding VAT, the value representing 20% of the estimated value of the contract (excluding Implementation reserves, "Data Room" and excluding Advertising), and the Total Estimated Value (including similar services) will be: 1.362.977,53 lei, excluding VAT. The minimum value of the range from Section II.1.5 represents the estimated value of this procedure, according to which the tender will be prepared and evaluated, and the maximum value of the range from Section II.1.5 represents the estimated value containing both the estimated value of this procedure and the value of possible new similar services in accordance with art. 104 para. (8) of Law no. 98/2016. Within the contract, the following services will be provided and the following documents will be prepared: • Technical Expertise for DN 7F related to the Project, including the bridge over the Olt river, the railway and DN 7; • Preparation of FS for the modernisation of DN 7F, taking into account the full applicability of the legislation in force (norms, regulations, standards, laws, etc.); In accordance with the provisions of art. 221 of Law 98/2016, with subsequent amendments and completions, and in compliance with article 20 of the Services Contract, any modifications that may occur during the contract execution period refer to the following, without being limited to them: 1. modifications of the contracting parties, under the conditions provided in art. 221 para. (1) let. d), point (ii); 2. changes / legislative modifications / regulations / STASs / norms / orders / instructions / etc.; 3. requests from Authorities / Entities / Institutions issuing opinions / approvals / authorisations / permits or from other entities having duties related to the project (MTIC, MFE, Central and/or Local Institutions, ARR, Beneficiary, MAI, SRI, Certified Verifiers, etc.); 4. extension of deadlines for submission of reports / deliverables (documents / documentation); 5. replacement of personnel nominated by the Provider for the fulfilment of the contract; 6. extension of the contract duration 7. replacement / introduction of subcontractors; 8. application of the law on historical monuments, performance of road safety audit, preparation of PUZ; 9. requirements regarding archaeological research and works. Modifications will be made after the signing of the contract, in accordance with contractual provisions, only under the conditions where they do not represent substantial modifications within the meaning of the provisions of art. 221 para. (7) of Law no. 98/2016. The extension of the contract duration can be made in accordance with the provisions of article 20 of the Services Contract. More information can be found in the Contract.

sig_5ff89c84bbb02b8923f8.description: Provision of support, maintenance, operational support and troubleshooting for the SIMI Measurement Controller (SIMI-MV) system (System) IT application, provision of an on-call system to receive notifications of potential malfunctions, system development, and performance of regulatory compliance, modification and related training tasks associated with the System under a works contract. The National Media and Infocommunications Authority (NMHH or Contracting Authority (CA)) intends to procure the provision of support, maintenance, operational support and troubleshooting for the SIMI Measurement Controller (SIMI-MV) system (System) IT application, provision of an on-call system to receive notifications of potential malfunctions, system development, and performance of regulatory compliance, modification and related training tasks associated with the System through an open procurement procedure conducted in accordance with the EU procurement procedure set out in Section 81 (paragraph 1) of Act 2015 on Public Procurement (hereinafter: Kbt.). The SIMI MV uses the following runtime environment components: • Linux operating system – Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, 22.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS; • Docker swarm 27.5; • Kubernetes 1.32; • Client operating system Windows 10 and 11; • Java 21 SDK LTS (64-bit), update 21.0.5 or later; • PostgreSQL database server, v16.x or later; • Embedded Apache Tomcat web server; • Embedded Apache ActiveMQ Artemis; • WebGL 2.0, OpenCL 2.0 and Vulkan 1.3 specifications for clients. 1. The flat-rate service requires the performance of the following tasks: a) Maintenance of the development environment, b) Use of the incident management system provided by NMHH, c) Correction of reported defects, d) Incorporation of component updates provided by third parties, e) Support provided via telephone, email or online conferencing tools (for a duration of 8 hours per month) f) Testing / incorporation of updates, g) Keeping documentation up to date, h) Consistent management of source code, i) Handover of the installation kit, j) Handover of development documentation and source code. The winning Tenderer (Tenderer) is obliged to provide the flat-rate services for 18 months from the entry into force of the contract. 2. When performing services based on worksheet accounting, the NMHH is entitled to call off a maximum of 32 hours of worksheet-accounted services during the 18-month duration of the service. As part of on-site and remote support, the CA requests the performance of the following tasks:  Diagnosis of errors  Diagnosis of interoperability issues  Installation of agreed patches deemed necessary jointly by the Contractor and the Client.  Re-installations required due to hardware failure or obsolescence of the equipment ensuring the operation of the supported systems.  Cooperation in the installation of new system component versions / patch sets  Testing the operability of the system against new versions of web browsers.  Integration testing  Consultation  Extractions, data cleansing and database operations that cannot be performed via the user interface. With regard to worksheet-accounted services, the CA shall designate the specific task forming the subject matter of performance, the deadline for performance and the place of performance (task to be performed at the CA or task to be performed at the winning Tenderer's registered office or premises (Remote)) in a requirement request in respect of the tasks. 3. Provision of parameterisation services: performance of development, regulatory compliance, modification tasks exceeding the flat-rate service and worksheet-accounted service, or training tasks related to the aforementioned tasks, in accordance with the individual requirements of the NMHH. When performing parameterisation tasks, the NMHH is entitled to call off a maximum of 3928 hours of worksheet-accounted services during the 18-month duration of the service. The contractor competencies required for the implementation of the Parameterisation Services are as follows: (i) project manager, (ii) system organiser / business analyst (iii) lead software developer (iv) front-end developer, (v) measuring instrument remote control developer (vi) UI/UX expert (vii) back-end developer (viii) database expert (ix) software tester (x) documentation writer. Measuring instrument remote control developer: Their task is to modify and supplement the remote control commands (SCPI or NCP protocol) of measuring instruments integrated into the system and integrate them into the measuring instrument driver. They are responsible for modifying and expanding the driver components processing binary data streams arriving from the measuring instrument. The CA has the opportunity to place individual orders in accordance with points 2 and 3 within 18 months from the entry into force of the contract, or, if earlier, until the exhaustion of the framework amount according to sub-point 5.1.b) of the draft contract in the case of the service according to point 2, and the framework amount according to sub-point 5.1.c) of the draft contract in the case of the service according to point 3, provided that the deadlines for performance specified in the individual orders thus communicated may not exceed the deadline of 25 months from the entry into force of this contract. The Contracting Authority undertakes a call-off obligation up to 70 % of the total contractor fee according to point 5.1 of the draft contract. The source code of the SIMI-MV system is not owned by the NMHH at the time of conclusion of the contract. The source code is necessary for the performance of the services described above; the source code of the system is owned by Delta Systems Kft. (1134 Budapest, Róbert Károly körút 70-74.). The winning tenderer must ensure the acquisition of the right to use the source code, provided that the Tenderer is obliged to declare in its tender that it has or will have the source code of the SIMI-MV system at the latest by the time the contract is concluded. The detailed requirements are contained in the Technical Specification and the draft contract forming part of the Tender Documentation.

sig_5fffab3c235a7e86f664.description: The contracting authority has investigated the possibility of dividing the contract into lots, but has decided not to divide the contract into lots. The software, user rights, implementation, integration with the PET/CT environment, cloud and gateway services, maintenance, updates and technical support form one technically and functionally integrated whole. The core technology, software components and associated support are offered exclusively by Nuclivision BV and are based on proprietary technology, algorithms, know-how and intellectual property rights. A division in which parts are carried out by different contractors is not technically appropriate and would lead to risks regarding compatibility, coordination, continuity and the definition of responsibilities. Execution by one contractor ensures integrated operation and unambiguous responsibility for the implementation, correct operation, security, updates, maintenance and support of the entire solution. Moreover, a division into lots would not effectively promote competition, as the technically coherent core services can only be provided by the rights holder and producer of the software.

sig_6002cabd0bbed5d9bdc6.description:
The construction site of the Turun yliopisto Botanical Garden is located at: Ruissalon puistotie 215, 20100 Turku. The building services engineering and partially the structural engineering parts of the Ruissalo Botanical Garden have reached the end of their lifecycle. The building services engineering will be renewed to the extent shown in the plans, and structural changes, demolition work and new structures will be implemented at the site. The property will remain in use throughout the construction work. The site is visited by a large number of customers as well as tourist and school groups. The movement of users within the construction site area must be taken into account already during the preliminary planning of the works. The project will be implemented as a divided contract, where the building contractor acts as the main contractor and the principal implementer as meant in YSE 1998. The building contract includes all structural engineering works, including earthworks and demolition works, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. In addition to the main and building contract, the following sub-contracts will be put out to tender: Plumbing contract The plumbing contract includes the plumbing work and refrigeration equipment work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. HVAC contract The HVAC contract includes the ventilation and building automation work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. Electrical contract The electrical contract includes the electrical work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from the other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. Greenhouse building automation contract The greenhouse building automation contract includes the greenhouse building automation work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. The sub-contracts will be carried out as sub-contracts subordinated to the main contractor in accordance with the RT 80271 subordination agreement. The contractor does not have the right to refuse the subordination of the contract without valid reasons. Commencement of the works 3.8.2026 on the condition that the application for a responsible site manager has been approved and the contract has been signed and the contracting authority has a building permit. The construction work must be fully completed no later than 30.3.2027. The content of the project is described in more detail in the appendices of the invitation to tender. The building contractor shall act as the main contractor. The building contract includes all structural engineering works, including earthworks and demolition works, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list. The renewal of the sheet metal roof shall be constructed under a fixed weather protection shelter. The timing of the installation of the weather protection shelter shall be agreed upon jointly with the contracting authority. The weather protection shelter may be removed when the construction work is fully completed and watertight. The contractor is responsible for the design and structural calculations of the weather protection shelter and shall submit them to the contracting authority for approval prior to implementation. Site management obligations and site services: The main contract includes the obligations of the contractor responsible for site services and the obligations of the principal implementer, including site management obligations. The site management obligations also apply to the sub-contracts and the contracting authority's procurements in accordance with this invitation to tender. The site services also apply to the sub-contracts and the contracting authority's procurements in accordance with this invitation to tender. The coordination of the contracting authority's procurements and separate contracts and the consideration of delivery times is the responsibility of the main contractor. The main contractor responsible for site management obligations must draw up an acceptable work schedule together with the sub-contractors and the contracting authority within three weeks of the conclusion of the contract. The schedule must mark the various work phases with sufficient breakdown so that the implementation of the schedule can be monitored at site and contractor meetings or separate schedule meetings. The schedule drawn up in this way shall be jointly approved as a binding schedule. Quality control: The main contractor must draw up moisture and dust control plans concerning the project and have them approved by the contracting authority. All building components must be weather-protected during storage and installation so that, as finished structures, they meet the moisture requirements set for them. Organisation and powers: The main contractor must appoint a responsible site manager for the site in the contract, who shall work full-time at this site. Site safety and occupational health and safety responsible persons: The safety planning for which the main contractor is responsible includes risk assessment, and the preparation of a safety and site plan before the commencement of construction work. The preparation of the safety plan takes into account the safety requirements and information concerning the site as well as those presented by the client. The safety plan provides answers to the management of the safety tasks, risks and safety requirements presented in the client's safety document, as well as general occupational safety requirements. The main contractor responsible for site management obligations shall appoint an occupational health and safety responsible person for the site and, if necessary, a deputy for them, who shall take care of the cooperation between the parties necessary for the safety and health of the site, the organisation of the flow of information, the coordination of operations, and the order and cleanliness of the construction site area. Site order: The main contractor responsible for site management obligations shall draw up a site plan for the site. The plan shall indicate the location of the site's equipment, machinery and appliances, material storage and reception areas, waste collection points and other matters that substantially affect the order, cleanliness and occupational safety of the construction site.

Demolition and construction waste: The handling, removal and landfill fees including taxes for the demolition and construction waste generated during the work shall be the responsibility of the main contractor. Personal identifiers and induction of employees: The main contractor must ensure that all of the contractor's own employees and sub-contractors' employees working on the construction site have a visible pictorial identifier identifying the person when moving around the site. The contractor is obliged to keep a list of the persons working on the site on the wall of the site office. The list must be updated weekly if new persons have arrived at the site. The main contractor shall induct the persons working on the site and the user representatives. Occupational safety and quality risks must also be taken into account in the induction. The induction and its content must be documented. In connection with the induction, the main contractor must ensure that the employees receive information on the safety instructions to be observed at the site. The induction carried out by the main contractor shall, as a rule, be carried out once per company operating on the site. Therefore, the persons working on the site of each contractor or sub-contractor are always inducted at the same time. Any deviations from the procedure presented above shall be agreed upon at a site meeting or other jointly agreed meeting, taking into account the impact of the scope of the contract and schedule factors on the possibility of induction at one time. The tasks and obligations of the main contractor are described in the appendices of the invitation to tender.; The plumbing contract includes the plumbing work and refrigeration equipment work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list.; The HVAC contract includes the ventilation and building automation work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list.; The electrical contract includes the electrical work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list.; The greenhouse building automation contract includes the greenhouse building automation work in accordance with the plans mentioned in the document list, as well as the works and obligations arising from other contracts in accordance with the tender documents and the plans mentioned in the document list.

sig_600f510c74b8a47f1f4f.description: The University of the Balearic Islands (hereafter UIB) has various security elements whose main mission is to protect its ICT infrastructure and, consequently, its data and services. The main element of this security ecosystem is firewalls, devices that are primarily responsible for controlling user access to resources available in the University's ICT infrastructure. The manufacturer of the current firewalls has already announced the end-of-support date and the current maintenance service can no longer be renewed; therefore, the replacement of these firewalls with new equipment is required. The purpose of this contract is the acquisition of new firewalls and a unified management platform for them and their logs, as well as the maintenance of all these elements for five years. The new firewalls and their management platform will offer an important set of technical improvements, including a greater capacity for processing network sessions, an intelligence layer that allows the analysis of network traffic traces, and the expansion of the bandwidth of their links with the University's network infrastructure, all resulting in better network service for the entire university community.
sig_600f510c74b8a47f1f4f.title: Acquisition of firewalls for the data communications network of the University of the Balearic Islands.

sig_60106b1aa7da1b8b3fdd.description: We ask you to submit your answers to this information request concerning the procurement of a certificate automation system. We greatly appreciate all the answers we receive, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a possible tendering procedure. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that those preparing the tendering procedure have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and the solutions on offer as possible. With this information request, we want to survey suppliers' offerings of systems that support the automatic renewal of public SSL certificates and the managed installation of certificates for systems using them. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services related to the systems, products possibly related to the use of the system, contract terms and conditions, and commercial terms such as pricing. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions may be organised, where suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement subject. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will announce more detailed schedules and a Teams meeting link to the companies participating in the sessions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this information request are still preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as the preparation progresses. We ask you to submit your answers by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 15.4.2026 at 12.00. We hope that the answers are submitted in a separate enclosure in Finnish, so that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you can also include Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your answer. Based on the answers received, Istekki will, at its discretion, select 1-5 tenderers to present their solution in a market dialogue meeting. By default, the presentation will be implemented as an approximately one (1) hour Teams meeting between Istekki and the supplier in question at one of the following preliminary times: • Time 1: 24.04.2026, at 09-10 • Time 2: 24.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 3: 29.04.2026, at 9-10 • Time 4: 29.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 5: 29.04.2026, at 13-14 All answers received to the information request will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they are an important part of understanding the entity as a whole. It is good to note that this information request does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its enclosures. A possible tendering procedure may also not be organised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the information request or participating in possible presentation sessions. We would like to mention once again that this is an information request, not a prior information notice, a procurement notice or an invitation to tender. The purpose of the information request is to familiarise ourselves with the market situation and to gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the information request is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible tendering procedure, nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us build the future tendering procedure into as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_601883fad91c3c7ec905.description: The Legal AI Workspace software to be procured must, as a specialised working environment, support legal specialist work within the KfW Group with the aid of generative artificial intelligence. The software will be used in particular for legal research, analysis and processing of legal content, as well as for the (semi-)automated creation, revision and structuring of documents and other legal work results. Users are individuals from the Legal department as well as other specialist departments and subsidiaries within the KfW Group. A Legal AI Workspace connects large language models with specialised processing layers optimised for working with legal content. It differs from general AI assistants in that it brings together specialist legal processes in a uniform working environment and deploys mechanisms that are indispensable for professional legal application. These include in particular: the traceable anchoring of generated statements in verifiable sources, the structured processing of complex documents, and the rule-based checking of contract contents. The software must provide the following core functions. Legal research: The software must be capable of answering complex legal questions on the basis of relevant legal sources. Every generated statement must be traced back to specific, verifiable sources (in particular legislation, case law, commentaries) and made transparent to users. KfW regards integrated access to curated legal databases as a quality-enhancing feature. Furthermore, the software must be able to work with documents and internal knowledge databases provided by KfW. Document analysis and contract evaluation: The software must be able to process and evaluate the content of documents, including complexly structured contracts, tabular content and scanned documents, without losing essential structural information. This includes the ability to systematically and completely reconcile contract content against specified verification standards. Text creation and drafting support: The software must support the creation and revision of legal texts, in particular draft contracts, memoranda and opinions. Proposed changes must be traceable directly within the document; merely providing generated text for manual adoption by users does not meet the requirements. The software complements general AI software already in use at KfW. The new software will be operated as a standalone tool and uses model infrastructure provided by the contractor. It is expected that the software will achieve significant efficiency and quality gains in daily legal advice, document creation and review, and recurring standard legal tasks. Without prejudice to the provision of the Software as a Service (SaaS) described in this document and the rights of use granted in connection therewith, the software must be provided in such a way that it at least meets the intended purpose. KfW is entitled to at least those rights of use required to fulfil the intended purpose for this. The contractor is therefore indebted to the following services: (a) provision of software with the functional scope, (b) execution of a project for the introduction of the software, (c) operation as SaaS, (d) provision of additional services as required, (e) termination support. Further details can be found in the "Specification of Services" and in particular the must-criteria according to the annex to the Specification of Services "Must and Can Criteria".

sig_601a72f4f336a25499da.description: The local authority of Mortsel is looking for a time-tracking system for its staff. - This time-tracking system will provide the basic functionalities that may be expected of a time-tracking system. It enables employees with and without a physical time clock to register their arrival and working hours as well as tasks and exceptional performance. - All employees have access to their personal situation and can submit leave requests. - The data is processed according to calculation rules aligned with input to the payroll engine for remuneration. The software includes: - Virtual registration; - Software that is user-friendly and simple to operate; - The software is developed in Dutch and is available as an online platform (cloud) and offers a high degree of usability and provides user-friendliness thanks to automated functions. The platform supports multiple users and workstations and operates in network mode. The number of end users is unlimited. Access to the software is via username and password or via linkage with AD for SSO. Our payroll engine will run on Lima (Cipal Schaubroek). Export to the payroll engine is automated as much as possible.
sig_601a72f4f336a25499da.title: supply of personnel time tracking software module

sig_603dd10ffcb1f2d32fb2.description: This contract constitutes Sub-project 3 of the Project "Development of the institution, infrastructure, capabilities and competencies for the data governance of the public sector, their availability for reuse and the provision of relevant services to the public and private sector, in Greece - Phase A" (OPS TA 5158667), which is implemented within the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan "Greece 2.0". The contract concerns the implementation of actions related to awareness-raising, promotion, networking, consultation, training, increasing the degree of impact of the Project, indicatively regarding its role in the creation of a Digital Transition Indicators Observatory, in the creation of a data utilisation platform, in the assessment of the efficiency of Action 16778 "Digitisation of archives and related services", as well as as an Executive Mechanism of the Bureaucracy Observatory (BO). More specifically, the requested services are included within the framework of the following Work Packages: Work Package 1 (WP1): Implementation of awareness-raising actions. It includes the design and production of printed and other promotional and informative material, as well as the design and organisation of events/workshops, consultations and other awareness-raising actions in order to inform both citizens, businesses and other bodies about the pivotal and crucial role of the Digital Transition Indicators Observatory, the assessment of the efficiency of the Digitisation of Action 16778, the Bureaucracy Observatory, but also the importance of proper governance of public data in Greece, with the ultimate goal of promoting relevant initiatives and creating a sense of trust among citizens and businesses towards the Public Administration and the role that relevant initiatives will play. Work Package 2 (WP2): Implementation of publicity actions. It includes the promotion of the materials that will be produced for the advertising campaign, from Work Package 1. Work Package 3 (WP3): Development of informative material and conduct of information sessions. It includes the implementation of training actions through the development of educational material and the conduct of the corresponding training. The training aims, on the one hand, to inform and familiarise Public Administration executives regarding the operation of the EKT Data Marketplace and, on the other hand, to inform the wider ecosystem of the Bureaucracy Observatory regarding the methodology for measuring administrative burdens.
sig_603dd10ffcb1f2d32fb2.title: Implementation of awareness-raising, promotion, networking, consultation, training and impact-increasing actions of the Project on the economy and society
