sig_63fb6a64df652179ee87.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This UAS Marketplace Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled by the U.S. Army. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the UAS Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the PMO UAS will better incentivize industry innovation. UAS Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional Department of War (DoW) acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the Army to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The PMO UAS has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform UAS capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The PMO UAS is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The PMO UAS anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled by the PMO UAS. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY DoW areas or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Uncrewed Aircraft Systems: Full Systems Air Vehicles Payloads Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects UAS Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) a. Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any Areas of Interest (AOI) in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. b. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in Section D.1 providing a submission to an IWS. c. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) a. Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. b.Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below in Section D.2. c.The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined with each call. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for immediate review, the submission will be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the Army and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: a. Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. b. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) c. Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. d. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. e. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: a. 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); b. 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); c. 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); d. Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, e. Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the Army and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D.1, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. [Area of Interest in Subject Line][ UASMarketplaceIWS@army.mil ] C4S Brief submissions (Section D.2) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: UASMarketplaceIWS@army.mil Cc: USARMY Redstone Arsenal ACC Mailbox ACC-RSA-UAS-Marketplace usarmy.redstone.acc.mbx.acc-rsa-uas-marketplace@army.mil SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the Army will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoD that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoD for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoD has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoD relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

sig_640f397b35b00652a7f4.description: Crown Commercial Service (CCS) as the Authority intends to put in place a dynamic purchasing system for the provision of Facilities Management and Workplace related Services. This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will provide FM services to the Wider Public Sector and Central Government. It offers a compliant route to market for the procurement of lower value and / or less complex hard and soft FM services. This DPS complements the Facilities Management and Workplace Services framework RM6232 which may be suitable for higher value procurements. The services available include: ● Catering Services ● Cleaning Services ● Defence Only - End User Accommodation Services ● Helpdesk Services ● Landscaping Services ● Maintenance Services ● Miscellaneous FM Services ● Security Services ● Smart FM Solutions including Computer Aided Facility Management (CAFM) Services ● Specialist Defence FM Services ● Statutory Obligations / Compliance Services ● Visitor Support Services ● Waste Services Lot 1: . Crown Commercial Service (CCS) as the Authority intends to put in place a dynamic purchasing system for the provision of Facilities Management and Workplace related Services. The DPS will offer an alternative route to market for lower value and / or less complex contracts and will look to attract SME suppliers. This DPS complements the existing Facilities Management Marketplace framework (RM6232) and provides customers with a range of procurement solutions. It offers a wide range of works and services for public sector estates, such as maintenance, response repairs, supply and installation works. This agreement will also include services such as CAFM, help-desk services, and waste. This DPS will be available to be utilised by Central Government Departments and all other UK Public Sector Bodies, including but not limited to, Local Authorities, Health, Police, Fire and Rescue, Education, Housing, Charities, Not for Profit, Nuclear and Devolved Administrations and International. sig_643cbbe6b53a218d393b.description: The successful supplier(s) will be responsible for the implementation, operation, and ongoing support of a Training Learner System to serve approximately 120,000 users, including 43,000 internal and 80,000 external users. This new platform will replace the existing learning systems and will introduce enhanced capabilities to support the organisation and the wider rail industry. The platform must deliver for both internal and external stakeholders, ensuring seamless learning experiences at scale. Additionally, the solution must support a content library accessible to 5,000 users and provide monetisation options for industry partners. Key deliverables include: • Deployment of a learning system within NR’s IT environment, ensuring security and scalability. We understand that the market has converged to some extent with respect to the distinctions between learning management systems and learning experience platforms, so we are deliberately agnostic in our terminology. • Seamless and engaging learning experiences for all users, supporting diverse learning needs. Diversity of learning needs includes different learner abilities, different learning environments, and different accessibility requirements. • Ensure that the new system can function at peak capacity with maximum number of concurrent users that the system can realistically sustain before requests per minute start to decline and response time starts to increase. • Tenancy, instances, permissions, and access for rail industry partners, offering access to standardised or bespoke training content with built-in charging mechanisms. • Access to diverse content libraries, enabling professional and personal development. This includes (but is not limited to) professional development material, soft skills development, technology, project management and leadership skills. • Existing bespoke content migration, transferring over 1,000 eLearning materials to the new system. We expect the supplier to provide a content library and complete a mapping/triage exercise against existing content. • A centralised catalogue of all Network Rail training offerings, including content libraries, bespoke digital learning, facilitated courses, innovation (e.g. digital simulations, VR). • Effective in-platform communication channels to engage and support learners. Network Rail are open to exploring different in-platform communication features, but expect the whole suite of market norms to be available for consideration (e.g. in-platform communication, between platform communication such as email/teams, push notifications to mobile devices). • Data insights, leveraging statistical and predictive modelling for decision-making. We seek a view from the market as to the ‘art of the possible’ that can be deployed out of the box and what can be developed over time. • Systematic use of permissions, automation, and workflows (which could include AI) to minimise process and content duplication, and to surface content to learners that is relevant, customised, and personalised. • Implementation and suitable change management to deploy the system within Network Rail technical, procedural and people environment. Implementation should be supported by best practice and lessons learned from other client projects to embed the system and ensure adoption. • Effective training, upskilling and handover for internal support teams so they can confidently support the business. • An intuitive and modern user interface, serving as a dynamic platform for learning content. • Personalised or customised learning pathways, tailored to individual user needs through data-driven recommendations. • The system should support the delivery, booking, administration, tracking and scheduling for inperson and virtual training events using off the shelf capabilities. This initiative will not only replace the existing technology but also introduce new capabilities to enhance learning accessibility, engagement, and efficiency across the organisation and its partners. Lot 1: .
sig_643cbbe6b53a218d393b.title: Integrated Learning Systems

The assistance shall contribute to compliance with the current rules and ensure good progress, quality and traceability in the procurement work.; The sub-area includes assistance with planning, implementing and following-up procurements where there are special requirements for safety, screening worthy values or handling security graded information. The sub-area covers both consultancy in the early phase and operative support throughout the entire procurement process. Assistance can i.a. include assessment of security requirements, choice of procurement strategy, preparation of competition documents and contract terms, supplier assessments and follow-up of safety conditions in the contract period. Competence is expected for this sub-area within relevant procurement regulations and security regulations, including handling security graded procurements, supplier and personnel requirements, as well as the establishment of the necessary security measures and control mechanisms. It is an advantage if the tenderers ́ hrs have knowledge of defence and security procurements, including relevant rules for such procurements. The assistance shall contribute to the procurements being carried out in a safe and efficient manner, in accordance with the current rules and with the necessary safeguarding of the contracting authority ́s needs.; The sub-area includes assistance with integrating climate, environment, society and human rights considerations into procurement processes and contract follow-up. The consultancy can be both strategically and operative and it can include needs and market analyses, assessment and registration of the procurement ́s expected risk profile in relation to social conditions, climate and the environment, as well as carrying out risk assessments and due diligence assessments of supply chains. Furthermore, assistance can include formulation of requirements and criteria, including requirements for suppliers within climate, environment and social responsibility, assessment of lifecycle costs, design of contract terms, follow-up of suppliers as well as support with reporting and documentation. Tenderers shall be able to assist with identifying relevant and proportional measures that promote environmental, social and economic sustainability through procurements, while safeguarding the requirements for competition and compliance with the current regulations. Tenderers shall also be able to give advice on how requirements for climate, environment, human rights and responsible supplier chains can be integrated and followed up throughout the entire procurement and contract period.; The sub-area includes consultancy and assistance that shall contribute to further developing the company ́s procurement function, management models, processes and competence. The sub-area covers work with strengthening the procurement area ́s ability to support the entity ́s aims, create value and ensure effective use of resources. Assistance can i.a. include the development of procurement strategies, management documents and methodology, analysis of procurement portfolios, category management, profit realisation, process improvement, digitalisation, competence development and the establishment of measurement and reporting mechanisms. The sub-area can also include consultancy related to organising the procurement function, role and responsibility sharing and implementation of best practice within public procurements.

sig_6472b9b8f41c1f528937.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system regarding the procurement of IT consultancy services within 14 service areas with associated sub-areas, sub-categories and services. Below are the 14 service areas with associated sub-areas indicated. The actual services that can be procured in the 14 service areas are described in detail in Appendix C. Subject of the system: Service area 1: IT-related strategies Sub-area: Preparation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Implementation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Evaluation and updating as well as impact assessment of strategies Service area 2: Business needs, business case and benefit realisation Sub-area: Identification of business needs and preparation of business cases Sub-area: Realisation of business cases Sub-area: Follow-up on business cases Service area 3: IT tendering Sub-area: Preparation of tenders Sub-area: Execution of tenders Service area 4: IT security, business continuity and IT compliance Sub-area: Establishment of IT security Sub-area: Crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery Sub-area: IT compliance Service area 5: IT architecture Sub-area: Establishment of an IT architecture Sub-area: Review and adjustment of existing IT architecture Service area 6: IT governance Sub-area: Establishment of IT governance Sub-area: Organisation of system management Sub-area: Establishment of IT supplier management Service area 7: Project and programme management Sub-area: Project management – the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Management of agile projects Sub-area: Programme management Service area 8: Data processing Sub-area: Data analysis and reporting Sub-area: Use of external data Sub-area: Conversion, cleaning and archiving of data Service area 9: Advice on software licences Sub-area: Open source software vs. closed source software Sub-area: Determination of the size of specific licences, as well as the conditions associated with the use Service area 10: Infrastructure and hardware Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of networks Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of servers Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of clients Service area 11: Test Sub-area: IT testing of development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT testing Service area 12: Development of new functionality Sub-area: IT development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT development Service area 13: Adaptation of existing IT systems Sub-area: IT development with a view to adapting existing IT systems Service area 14: IT system operation Sub-area: Operation of IT systems The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase The same services can be procured in both categories, but the categories differ in that the customer in category 1 must procure one or more specific competence(s), while the customer in category 2 must have a specific task solved. The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. It is voluntary for all SKI's customers, as stated in Appendix B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure IT consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase In category 1 customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in 2 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate).; Procurement of IT consultancy services for task solution In category 2 the customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in 3 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of IT consultancy services for the solution of the described task (number x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate). 3. Remuneration form 3: Purchase of task solution at a fixed price.

sig_64d5d01fa5ae02d6208a.description: • Brief description of the contract: The contract consists of planning, coordinating and carrying out public consultations on the update of the drought effects counteracting plan referred to in Article 185 paragraph 1 of the Act of 20 July 2017 - Water Law (Journal of Laws 2025 item 960 as amended). The Contractor will be tasked with carrying out information activities about the consultations, holding consultation meetings and conferences concerning the plan update throughout the country. The Contractor will be responsible for collecting comments, including coordinating the process of collecting and addressing them, along with preparing a public consultation report containing a table of how the comments were addressed. • Detailed description of the contract: The Contractor's duties will include: 1. Developing a form for submitting comments and instructions on submitting comments. 2. Launching and running, for the duration of the project, a website dedicated to public consultations, including developing and posting information on the aforesaid website. 3. Preparing an electronic version of the poster and banner regarding the public consultations. 4. Preparing and printing leaflets concerning the consultations. 5. Preparing and printing a roll-up concerning public consultations of planning document drafts in water management (width 100 cm, height 200 cm) – 2 pieces. 6. Publishing information about the consultations in the regional press – 32 pieces. 7. Coordinating work on drawing up the table for addressing comments and motions, including: designing the table, supplementing it with the content of submitted comments, cooperating with other entities (e.g. distributing and collecting completed tables regarding responses). 8. Organising 1 nationwide conference in a hybrid format (up to 200 in-person participants along with online transmission to 300 people with the option to submit questions) and a press conference. 9. Organising approx. 5 consultation meetings in an in-person format (up to 120 participants) along with online transmission to 300 people with the option to submit questions. 10. Preparing press materials before each event, handling press queries, requests for public information and environmental information related to the consultations. 11. Drawing up a consultation report (along with the table of addressing comments). The report will contain an account of the course of the consultations and implemented promotional activities along with statistical summaries (attendance, number of comments, how they were addressed, substantive analysis of the impact on the document). 12. Preparing monthly project implementation reports. 13. Preparing a schedule of meetings and conferences (specifying dates and locations).
sig_64d5d01fa5ae02d6208a.title: Public consultation on the update of the drought effects counteracting plan

sig_650589afe87ef8591fbb.description: The Finnish Medicines Agency Fimea (later Fimea) is preparing the procurement of a system for receiving and validation, as well as application management, document handling, archiving, and reviewing marketing authorisation applications for medicinal products and related regulatory submissions. Fimea is primarily looking for a software as a service (SaaS) off-the shelf solution that is provided from a public cloud. The system shall enable the necessary integrations with Fimea's other systems, which will be defined later. The aim of the market dialogue is to investigate the offerings of the different service providers; especially whether it is possible to acquire the planned system as a single integrated solution or is it necessary to procure separate modules instead. The procurement includes the following entities: - Marketing authorisation application management system as a software service including possibility to upscale and downscale number of users. - Implementation project, covering the delivery of the system and the deployment of the system and its continuous services, as well as user training. - Continuous services, including e.g. continuous support and maintenance services of the system to the agreed extent, to the extent that they are not included in the software service. - Complementary expert services, covering separately ordered expert work for tasks such as further development of the system, and change management including user training. - Possible options, such as AI capabilities in different functions or modules. Migration of legacy application materials, application history, and other application-related documentation will be part of the procurement. Life cycle data of the medicinal product dossiers (sequences and attributes), application history of the medicinal products, and application related documents, including metadata, must be migrated to the system. The purpose of this request for information is to identify potential tenderers and to gather information on the solutions available on the market. Following the market dialogue, a call for tenders for the procurement will be prepared. For more information about the procurement, please see the Appendix 1 "Additional information about the procurement".
sig_650589afe87ef8591fbb.title: System for management of marketing authorisation applications of medicinal products and related regulatory submissions

sig_6506f4fca09e4fdd7bf0.description: The services requested under this procurement procedure are the continuation of Software Assurance as well as the acquisition of licences incl. Software Assurance for software products from Microsoft and / or the acquisition of online products from Microsoft that Microsoft offers via the corporate programme, in accordance with the terms of the framework agreement (corporate agreement) of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) and Microsoft via a corresponding commercial partner. The services requested in the context of this procurement procedure are described in the specification of services (Section 6 of the procurement documents) including the appendices listed therein. The technical, legal and organisational framework conditions are contained in Section 5. Westdeutscher Rundfunk Köln (WDR) is advertising a framework agreement on behalf of the following broadcasting corporations and institutions of the broadcasting corporations: ARD-Hauptstadtstudio (ARD-HSB, represented by rbb), ARD ZDF Deutschlandradio Beitragsservice (ZBS), Bayerischer Rundfunk (BR), Deutschlandradio (DLR), Deutsche Welle (DW), Hessischer Rundfunk (HR), Informationsverarbeitungszentrum (IVZ, represented by rbb), Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk (MDR), Norddeutscher Rundfunk (NDR), Radio Bremen (RB), Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg (rbb), Saarländischer Rundfunk (SR), Südwestrundfunk (SWR), Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) and Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen (ZDF). Also eligible are all other companies affiliated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions, provided that these are "Authorised Institutions" within the meaning of the opening clause of the BMI contract. Affiliated and authorised companies associated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions that do not meet the minimum order quantity of 250 qualified devices or users intend, if required, to join together with the affiliated broadcasting corporations and institutions in accordance with the BMI contract, Appendix 1 Section 3, a., (iii) to form a joint accession in order to reach the minimum order quantity. The framework agreement shall enter into force upon the award of contract and shall end upon expiry of the BMI corporate agreement, which entered into force on 01.06.2025, on 31.05.2028 or, taking into account its extension option, on 31.05.2029. During the term of the framework agreement, eligible entities may make accessions to the BMI corporate agreement. In doing so, each eligible entity may, if required and where applicable, also make accessions on the basis of various enrolments (e.g. EA Enterprise, EA SCE, EA Subscription enrolment). The effective date of each accession shall mark the commencement of a separate framework agreement (see template agreement in the appendix) between the respective eligible entity as the client and the commercial partner as the contractor. These individual framework agreements have independent terms, which are presented below, and shall therefore also apply to the respective contracting parties beyond the aforementioned end of the term of the framework agreement where applicable. Each eligible entity that makes an accession / concludes a framework agreement acts under its own responsibility, places orders and pays at its own expense. Joint and several liability between the various eligible entities is excluded. Insofar as individual clients guarantee minimum purchase quantities, these result from the appendix Minimum Purchase Quantities.xlsx of these procurement documents. Purchase quantities going beyond this are not guaranteed. The respective framework agreement shall end after 36 months without the need for termination. The framework agreement partner grants the clients the right to extend the respective framework agreement once by one year under the same conditions. The respective client must declare the exercise of the option in writing to the framework agreement partner before the expiry of the contract. The subsequent further extension option shall serve in particular the purpose of ensuring the possibility of an interruption-free commissioning of Software Assurance as well as operation for the respective client if a procurement procedure for such commissioning cannot be carried out / completed in good time. The framework agreement partner therefore grants the clients the right in each case to extend the respective framework agreement once again by up to 6 further months. The conditions may change for this extension period. An adjustment of the dealer's mark-up or markdown on its purchase prices may be made by mutual agreement in this case. The dealer must explain the circumstances altering the calculation. Insofar as further adjustments to the framework agreement have to be made due to Microsoft licence programme changes, these shall likewise be coordinated by mutual agreement. If and to the extent that valid successor agreements already exist between the Federal Ministry of the Interior and Microsoft at the time the extension option for the further 6 months is exercised - where applicable also on the basis of a different Microsoft licence programme -, these may be selected as the basis. The framework agreement partner further agrees that during this extension term, any client may terminate the framework agreement at any time and without observing a notice period and carry out a change of commercial partner. The currently existing EA accessions expire for all eligible entities on 31.05.2026. It is intended to make accessions to the new BMI corporate agreement on the following dates: 01.06.2026 The clients will announce the products and quantities for their respective initial orders in good time. The contractor will then promptly provide the respective client with the prices valid for the initial order, taking into account the Microsoft price and the discount for the EA commercial partners in accordance with the BMI corporate agreement as well as the mark-up or markdown to be offered.

sig_6512f77e4da294323564.description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. Market Involvement As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers. We are looking for one or two e-commerce agency(ies) to support and optimise our digital sales strategies and measures at up to 160 locations of the Goethe-Institut in Germany and abroad. The contractor must - support the consultancy, assistance and implementation of activities in the areas of e-commerce, strategic marketing, performance marketing, search engine optimisation (SEO/AIO), technical marketing and web analytics, - collaborate on strategies for new concepts or further developments in the areas of B2B, B2C and group registrations, - take into account any difficult conditions in international trade, - consider the specific nature of selling services or educational offers with partially limited availability and/or other restrictions in online retail. It is intended to conclude a framework agreement for a duration of four years with a service provider for Lot 1 and Lot 2: Lot 1: Service and consultancy services for performance marketing as well as MarTech and web analytics Lot 2: Consultancy and support services for online marketing/ SEO/ AIO. A detailed description of the required service can be found in Annex A "Service Description" (lot-specific). Lot LOT-0001: Service and consultancy services for performance marketing as well as MarTech and web analytics. Lot 1 Service and consultancy services for performance marketing as well as MarTech and web analytics are to be provided. These include: a) SEA: Co-administration of the Google Ads MCC, support in the setup, optimisation and data-driven evaluation of SEA campaigns on Google Ads, Bing and, if applicable, Yahoo Ads, creation of scripts for the SEA accounts; support in the implementation of Smart Bidding, PMax and AIMax; conversion tracking, co-administration of GTM and Google Analytics, if applicable, setup of server-side GTM, setup of ConversionAPI. b) Social Advertising: Support in the setup, data-driven evaluation, derivation of recommendations for action and further development of international campaigns on the platforms META, LinkedIn, TikTok and YouTube; campaign optimisation and technical optimisation of the META Pixel, installation of Conversion API. c) Strategic consultancy on the overall e-commerce strategy of the Goethe-Institut (B2B and B2C), on the customer journey, on CRM and on data-driven performance marketing. d) Further services: Email and affiliate marketing as well as marketing on previously unused or less used digital platforms or market-relevant platforms abroad (e.g. TikTok, Spotify, Reddit, Pinterest and many more). e) Support services, e.g. the creation of requirement descriptions and information and, if applicable, training of the specialist department's employees on updates regarding relevant, new developments in e-commerce. f) Web analytics and MarTech: a. Administration of the Google Tag Manager b. Integration of Google Analytics, Mapp Intelligence /Webtrekk, META Pixel, LinkedIn Insight Tag, as well as other necessary analysis tags of other platforms to improve conversion tracking and optimisation c. Support with evaluations (Google DataStudio, PowerBI or comparable) d. Necessary adjustments in the course of data protection requirements, which must be managed via the Google Tag Manager in the Consent Management Platform (Usercentrics). g) Support services for data-driven work a. Project for tracking the customer journey (across channels) b. Reconciliation and, if applicable, partial transfer of e-commerce topics from Google Analytics to Mapp Intelligence. c. the creation of requirement descriptions and information and, if applicable, training of the specialist department's employees on updates regarding relevant, new developments in e-commerce. sig_65304a5679f41cb71107.description: The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) intends to undertake preliminary market engagement (PME) to consult with suppliers in relation to the MCA’s next generation procurement of its Command and Control Programme (C2P). The C2P aims to improve resilience, interoperability, situational awareness, and support for maritime incident management, pollution response and front-line search and rescue operations. The MCA’s vision is to create a modern, resilient and insight led capability that harnesses technology, improves decision making, strengthens operational performance, and delivers better outcomes for those we serve. The MCA’s objectives for the PME are: • help shape its requirements and specification; • understand available solutions and potential delivery approaches; • understand opportunities and innovation opportunities; • understand perceived risks and constraints; • alert the market of the upcoming opportunity and provide the likely role and responsibilities of the next generation C2P partner(s); • develop its approach to the procurement; • identify suppliers that may be able to deliver the C2P and understand capacity in the market; • gauge the level of market interest; • elicit feedback on the MCA’s objectives and programme to assist the MCA to refine its approach. The MCA reserves the right to amend any of the information contained within any of the PME materials and documents prior to the publication of the Tender Notice and commencement of any procurement process. Lot 1: . None

sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.
sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.title: Tender for a common Operating Platform

sig_654ef9f5f792000791d4.description: The ServiceNow licence contract currently in force with the publisher will end on 30 June 2026. The renewal of this contract is a critical necessity to guarantee the continuity of operations and digital services within EPFL. To date, ServiceNow constitutes the central "nervous system" of several departments of the institution. The platform is intensively used for: * IT Service Management (ITSM): Management of the service catalogue, incidents, requests and changes. * Document management: Support for technical documentation. * Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM): Management of the DSI project portfolio. * Digitalisation of business processes: Automation of key services for departments such as Human Resources (HR), Academic Services, the Research Office, the Safety Service or MEDIACOM. * User engagement: Centralisation of user feedback and experience. The purpose of the open call for tenders procedure is to select a ServiceNow licence reseller for the period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2031 (5 years).

sig_65530bb5d829db07f401.description: BudapestGO application development and related services The Contracting Authority, pursuant to Article 105. (1) point c) of the Public Procurement Act, defines in this invitation to tender the additions in respect of which the Tenderer needs to supplement its tender: The purpose of this procurement is to further improve the user experience of the BudapestGO application through minor fine-tuning and convenience features. I. Custom development requirements: - Standardisation of time zone management – travel-related times must always be displayed according to CET/CEST, regardless of the device system clock (affected platform(s): Android and iOS). - Address search – automatic address completion – adding a quick button (quick-fill) to the Address group results for faster completion (affected platform(s): Android and iOS). - Facebook-BPGO account issue – investigation and fixing of the Facebook connection/account problem (affected platform(s): Android and iOS). II. Bug fixes treated as requirements: - Third-party keyboards on iOS – allowing the use of keyboard extensions in the application where secure. - Decimal comma correction on iOS – in Hungarian-language apps, distance values are displayed with a ',' decimal separator. - Correction of search box overflowing on IAM on small screens – elimination of responsiveness problems of the search field on small screens (affected platform(s): Android and iOS). III. Parameterisations: - Parameterisation of push notifications for expiring passes/tickets – the timing of push notifications is changed from T-31 hours to T-12 hours, and the text of the related bottom sheet and push notification is updated. - Modification of pass crown texts + "Where can codes be found?" help update – clarification of help texts: scanning is only necessary at front-door boarding and upon inspection. The items included in the package are aimed at increasing the convenient usability of BudapestGO by handling minor yet annoying errors that arose during customer feedback and internal testing. The package does not introduce major new features, but formulates fine-tuning requirements and minor developments promoting convenient use in existing features, thereby increasing the user experience and satisfaction with the application. A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is made available as an attachment to this document.; This procurement requirement is necessary to ensure operation in compliance with the provisions of the BKK Privacy Policy. During the management of user account data, it must be ensured that data is stored exclusively for a justified period of time, as well as the enforcement of the data protection rights of the data subjects. This requirement creates the technological and process conditions for this. It is important to highlight that the following items forming the scope of this development item go beyond the Contractor's Contractual obligations defined within the framework of operation (implementation of deletion jobs): - storage of the execution results of deletion jobs in the database, - displaying these in the BO, - creation of a deletion job, deletion job's deletion job (retention period must be agreed upon), - display of the timestamp of the last user-side activity in the BO. In the first Data Deletion development package, we handle the anonymisation of accounts of inactive users without purchase transactions and users with unconfirmed registration, in accordance with statutory provisions. The development will plannedly have two more phases, where we will define the management of scheduled tasks performing the deletion of data related to purchases and log files. A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is made available as an attachment to this document.
sig_65530bb5d829db07f401.title: Operation and development of BudapestGO

sig_65b2ac17a9c77daa0371.description: The Bergische Universität Wuppertal (BUW) is seeking a survey institute with relevant demonstrated competencies in the service areas outlined below to carry out the survey for the fifth survey wave of the lidA study in the year 2027. The study "lidA - living in work" (www.lida-studie.de) is a cohort study in Germany that investigates the thematic field of "Work, age, health and gainful employment". The study is led by the Chair of Occupational Science at the University of Wuppertal. At intervals of three to five years, older working individuals in lidA were surveyed for approx. 70 minutes using Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI). In survey wave 1 (2011), this involved 6.585 individuals nationwide from the birth cohorts 1959 and 1965, the second wave took place in 2014 (N=4.244) and the third in 2018 (N=3.586). In survey wave 3 (2022/23), the birth cohorts 1959 and 1965 were scaled up to over 3000 respondents and, for the first time, nearly 3.000 individuals from birth cohort 1971 were surveyed. A total of 8.884 individuals were surveyed in this wave. In the upcoming fifth survey wave in the year 2027, as many individuals as possible from the group of currently approximately 9.000 panel-ready previous lidA participants are to be surveyed in the main survey. Based on previous experience, it can be estimated that this will amount to approximately 6.500 respondents. Following this, from October 2027 to October 2030, thirteen quarterly online post-surveys (with closed and open questions) are to be conducted with those willing to participate. Here, the participation of initially approx. 4.000 individuals and at the end still approx. 2.900 individuals is expected.
sig_65b2ac17a9c77daa0371.title: LidA - Life at Work: Survey wave 5

sig_65e6c43d9e59f65bfeb1.description: Network Rail requires a 24/7 road haulage service to manage the collection, haulage and delivery (including loading and offloading) of materials by road, including, but not limited to: sleepers, short rail, rail ancillaries, aggregates (loose or bagged), switches & crossings, troughing, manufactured materials, and large and abnormal loads, including, but not limited to: locomotives, tampers, rolling stock and specialist switches and crossings to a specified location. The requirement over the previous two years has made ~35,000 individual journeys on a yearly basis covering the entire UK and ~100 international journeys utilising vehicles ranging in size from vans to large extendable flatbeds and cranes. Network Rail also has the requirement for warehousing management. This includes but is not limited to: physical and systemic receipt of stock; physical and systemic put‐away of stock; management of stock to legislative and Network Rail defined specifications (i.e. Certificates of Conformity, COSHH, detonators); management of life‐expired stock; physical perpetual inventory checks; physical and systemic pick of required materials; physical despatch and delivery of materials to defined delivery point; physical and systemic capture of material proof of delivery records; physical and systemic receipt and processing of requests for material return; physical and systemic receipt and processing of requests for material repair; physical collection of returned media (e.g. pallets, collars and cable drums); physical distribution and collection of repair materials to and from repair agents and systemic capture and processing of such material; provision of Customer Services Helpdesk; undertaking of certified racking inspection checks; collection of materials from some of Network Rail’s Materials Suppliers and delivery to the RDCs; distribution of materials from supplier‐operated Regional Distribution Centres (RDCs). Standard Operating Practices shall be developed by the successful supplier in conjunction with Network Rail. The scope of the proposed Contract covers combined services including the provision of a transport planning team to co-ordinate and manage all transport requests covering both the Road Haulage and Warehousing distribution requirements, proactively managing all haulage requirements and providing information to support the delivery of improvements in safety, value, and sustainability. The contract will also include combined system requirements including a Transport Management System, Web-Based Order Portal and a Customer Relations Management (CRM) System. Network Rail has a requirement to operate nine (9) RDCs which also forms part of the scope of this Contract. Supporting the geographical routes and regions with the supply of maintenance materials, this more localised supply chain is intended to make critical materials more accessible to the end user by being geographically closer to Minor Stocking Points (MSPs) and providing access 24/7 on an on-call basis when outside of core working hours. MSP regular deliveries schedules are required to be managed through the RDC(s) but the operation of the MSPs is outside of the scope of this Contract. Network Rail requires a supplier to manage and deliver a vehicle trunking service delivering materials throughout the RDC network. The trunk vehicles are currently managed centrally from the Coventry RDC. There are three vehicles that work to a set schedule. Stock for each RDC is marshalled in Coventry and delivered two or three times each week to every RDC. Stock picked at the receiving RDC is then loaded onto the same vehicle and backhauled to Coventry, marshalled, and delivered back out to fulfil customer demand at the MSPs. Trunking fulfils customer expectations on the basis that each MSP has a milk run schedule. Network Rail currently lease the 9 RDCs as detailed within the associated tender documents and the scope of the Contract includes the requirement to operate the leased buildings delivering a warehousing solution. As set out in the Contract, Network Rail requires the successful supplier to be flexible, with the possibility that RDC operations may grow or be downscaled over time. Any requirements for upscaling or downscaling shall be discussed with the successful supplier on a case-by-case basis. The value of stock, as of July 2025, within these RDCs is currently ~£80m (SCO Network Rail owned), there is additional customer owned stock. From time to time, Network Rail may require additional storage locations to hold Stock which cannot be stored at existing Network Rail sites (being RDCs and any other Network Rail storage sites). The Supplier shall work with Network Rail to find such suitable additional storage locations, either at premises owned by the Supplier or another external location as required. Network Rail currently spends on average £28m per year on road haulage services, and £9m per year for warehousing services, with the expectation of this remaining broadly in line with the annual spend, with an element of flex due to demand. Further details are set out in the specification within Schedule 1 of the Contract. Lot 1: .

sig_65ea4307482e23fc5a37.description: Invitation to a supplier conference for the Norwegian Defence ́s digital transformation in Fanehallen 5 October 2026 The Norwegian Defence and Defence Material Agency invites tenderers, research and education institutions as well as other relevant actors to a supplier conference 5 October 2015 at 09.00-12.00 in Fanehallen at Akershus fortress. The Norwegian Armed Forces are facing a historic commitment to digitalisation and technological modernisation. The aim is to strengthen the Norwegian Defence ́s operative ability through a modern digital foundation, increased use of data and artificial intelligence, stronger interaction across the branches of the armed forces and better decision support in all domains. In the coming years, significant investments will be made including modernisation of the Norwegian Armed Forces' secure platforms, the development of the future digital work surface, modernisation of performance critical joint systems (ERP), establishment and modernisation of data centre, network and communication capacity, strengthened cyber security, utilisation of artificial intelligence as well as the establishment of modern platform and cloud services. The Norwegian Armed Forces cannot realise and succeed with this ambition alone. A successful digital transformation requires close cooperation between the defence sector, the supplier market, academia and other actors in the total defence. The aim of the conference is therefore to give the market insight into the Norwegian Armed Forces' strategic direction, planned commitments and future needs, at the same time as facilitating an open dialogue on possibilities, technology development and forms of cooperation. Topics that can be expected to be addressed at the supplier conference: The Defence Staff: Strategic Framework and Direction Vision, strategic guidance and relevant priorities for the development of a data-driven defence, including the status of the Norwegian Armed Forces' digital transformation and presentation of new management documents. How data, artificial intelligence and digitalisation shall contribute to increased operative effect. The Norwegian Armed Forces: The sector's need for digital capabilities and the effect Road ahead for digital capabilities: Strategic commitments, priorities, future needs and desired effects for the sector's digital development. Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency: Procurements and market dialogue Strategies for procurement and market involvement in order to realise the future of digital defence. The conference is a part of the Norwegian Defence ́s market dialogue and is being held to increase mutual understanding between the defence sector and the market. The information presented shall contribute to better predictability for suppliers and form the basis for future procurements and collaboration possibilities. Participation in the conference does not provide any competitive advantage in later procurements. Any future procurements will be made in accordance with the procurement regulations and announced in the ordinary way. Register via the link below: The supplier conference 5 October 2026 Registration deadline is 1 October, 15:00. Due to capacity and security reasons, there can be limits on the number of participants. Each company is invited to provide up to two representatives if the company has fewer than 200 employees, three representatives of 200-400 employees and four representatives if the company has more than 400 employees. There will be access and ID control by the entrance. The strategic management documents will be digitally made available right after the conference. The meeting will be held physically and the language will be Norwegian. We hope that you will participate - together we shape the digital defence of the future and make innovation operative defence ability. Well met! The Norwegian Defence Staff | The Norwegian Armed Forces | Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency

The University of Huddersfield (UoH, we/our, the University) is exploring options for a Student Case Management (SCM) system to improve and modernise our student support offer. For the purposes of the PME we invite potential partners to complete the linked questionnaire based on the primary and secondary enquiries below. Primary Enquiries We would like to focus on and gain insight into the following aspects of your product and offer: 1. Case Handling Scope - How far does your system support case management for the following areas: • Regulatory Casework: Complaints, Disciplinaries, Misconduct, Appeals, Fitness to Practise, Attendance Monitoring, OIA Case Reviews • Academic Tutoring: Academic Skills Tutoring, Personal Academic Tutoring Support • International Office: Immigration and International Student Case Management, UKVI case monitoring • Student Services: Wellbeing, Disability, Attendance and Engagement Support 2. Case and Enquiry Handling – Creating an Intelligent Front Door • How does your system manage enquiries and cases? • Does it support integration with existing enquiry management systems, specifically our existing TopDesk system? • Can workflows be customised for different case types and escalation paths? • How does it create an online intelligent front door that can triage and route enquiries, and integrate with physical and telephone service desks? 3. Integration Capabilities • An overview of your integration capabilities and existing connections to student record systems, finance systems and other university applications such as student portals • Your support for APIs or middleware for custom integrations? 4. Product Pricing and Implementation • Your pricing model for the SCM system? Please include: o Product licensing: Is it per institution, per user, or another model? o User licensing: How do you handle different user roles (e.g., staff, students)? • What are the typical implementation costs and timelines? • What is your implementation approach? o Do you offer phased rollouts or full deployment? o What support and training do you provide during implementation? Secondary Enquiries Additionally, we would like to explore how your product addresses the areas detailed below, as well as any additional benefits and functions your product offers: 1. Streamline the student case management lifecycle from initiation through to resolution. 2. Provide students with secure access to a centralised support channel for timely help and guidance. 3. Offer role-based access and control to ensure only authorised users can view or edit sensitive information. 4. Enable documents to be captured, stored, organised, and retrieved securely. 5. Support staff communication with students and stakeholders through integrated messaging tools (e.g., email, SMS, notifications). 6. Facilitate creation, assignment, updating, and closure of cases, capturing key actions and outcomes seamlessly (including appointments and events). 7. Track and report on case activity, resolution times, case types, and outcomes to support decision-making and continuous improvement. 8. Integrate with key university systems e.g., Student Records and other support systems. 9. Maintain an audit trail of all changes, actions, and users involved in each case for accountability and compliance. sig_6618018edcde3078e955.description: I. Background and purpose: Domstolsstyrelsen (DSS) is inviting tenders for a contract for IT operations etc. of a number of Domstolsstyrelsen's applications, including specialist systems, software packages and integrations. DSS serves approximately 2.500 internal users within the Danish Courts, including the Faroe Islands and Greenland, as well as many external users, e.g. lawyers, who need to use the services made available by DSS. The contract covers approx. 75 different applications, including specialist systems, software packages and integrations, cf. the tender documents, with a total storage consumption of around 600 TB and backup consumption of 1.300 TB. These are both standard and in-house developed applications, with a few business-critical applications operated on container-based platforms, cf. appendix 3 of the tender documents. Application maintenance and further development of some of the applications are supplied by a number of different application suppliers, just as DSS itself performs a number of tasks. Application maintenance for the remaining applications is supplied under this contract. All services must be supplied in close interaction with multiple suppliers and DSS, including in relation to commissioning. The supplier must also support the ongoing DevOps and DevSecOps implementation at DSS and must contribute to the continuous modernisation of operations etc. DSS's applications covered by the contract have a high degree of social criticality. Therefore, amongst other things, DSS wishes to achieve secure, stable, up-to-date and cost-effective IT operations with the flexibility to scale up and down. Therefore, there are high requirements for availability, scalability, flexibility and security. II: Main services: 1) Transition In, inter alia implementation of secure and stable takeover of operations of the applications (within a limited time), including project management, establishment of transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of environments and data, transfer of knowledge from the outgoing supplier and implementation of hypercare periods. 2) Ongoing Services - Infrastructure operations, inter alia IT operations of infrastructure, including hardware, network, storage, software, including operating systems and middleware, as well as database administration and monitoring. The supplier is responsible for efficient and stable infrastructure operations as well as e.g. configuration, patch, release and deployment management with a view to supporting high requirements for availability, continuous scaling as well as DevOps, DevSecOps and agility. - Network operations, inter alia operation, monitoring, maintenance and logging of networks in connection with the customer's many locations. - Application operations, inter alia backup, configuration, patch and release and deployment management, operation of container-based applications as well as application maintenance of some applications. - Support, inter alia responsibility for handling incidents, problems, service requests and user administration with a view to ensuring high availability for users. - Device management, inter alia support, preparation, maintenance and reinstallation of devices. 3) Ordering services, inter alia consultancy and standard ordering services. 4) Cross-cutting services, inter alia timely, clear, correct reporting and documentation. 5) Transition Out and other termination services, inter alia in connection with insourcing, upon contract termination or potential transfer to a new supplier.

Provision of development, expansion and maintenance services for APIA's IT system for managing payment claims is requested, with a view to carrying out the institution's specific activities it performs towards the management of European and national funds intended to support agriculture, through the conclusion of a framework agreement. Development services will be provided at the request of the contracting authority, by awarding subsequent contracts, depending on legislative changes, as well as application development needs identified in accordance with the business requirements identified in the processing of payment claims, established on the basis of requests from the specialized directions within APIA, and in accordance with the requirements in the specifications. The subject of this procurement and of the framework agreement to be awarded comprises, as emerges from the specifications, two major categories of services, as follows: A. Services for the development of new functionalities/modules and the updating of the existing SI-APIA IT system, in accordance with changes in European and national regulations, respectively organizational changes B. Monthly support services for the operation of the IT system, respectively Call Center services (1, 2, 3 and 4 level), corrective maintenance and administration of the IT system The specificity and technical requirements of each category of services are detailed in the specifications.
