sig_66355692e441a3cff3eb.description: Lincolnshire Fire and Rescue is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 to inform the development of a future procurement for an Asset Management Software (AMS) solution to support Fire and Rescue Service operations. The Authority seeks to understand current market capability, innovation, delivery models, and commercial approaches for digital asset management systems that can support the full lifecycle management of both operational and non‐operational assets. The intended solution is expected to provide a centralised, accurate, and fully auditable system for managing assets from acquisition through to disposal. It should support improved asset visibility and availability, condition monitoring, inspection and maintenance scheduling, and robust reporting, with appropriate access controls for operational, technical, and managerial users. The Authority is particularly interested in how modern solutions can enhance regulatory compliance, resilience, operational readiness, data quality, and integration with existing systems, enabling improved decision‐making through reliable asset data and automated processes. Through this PME, the Authority is seeking supplier feedback to help refine its requirements, procurement strategy, commercial model, and delivery approach. Engagement may cover topics such as functional capability, implementation and data migration, security and hosting options, support and training models, scalability, interoperability, and contract management. All information provided at this stage is indicative only. Requirements, scope, contract structure, and timelines are subject to change and will be informed by the outcomes of this engagement. Participation in this PME is voluntary and will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. The Authority will conduct the PME in an open, transparent, and proportionate manner to ensure fair and effective competition. Lot 1: . None

sig_668ef8d925336d997aa7.description: The aim of this project is the development of a software library that offers exploratory data analysis techniques from the field of process mining using the example of log data according to BSI TR-03156. This includes filtering the data, visual representation of the process flow, discovery of process models as well as conformity checking between model and data. In addition to the functional components, technical requirements of the existing BSI data quality instance systems (DQI) must be complied with in order to ensure subsequent integration into the client's data warehouse infrastructure. The contractor develops a software library for the client in which algorithms from process mining are implemented, which are applied to processed data. These processed data are based on the technical log data in accordance with BSI TR-03156 and are enriched with additional data from other data sources if necessary. They are provided by the client. From this data, the implemented algorithms must enable the calculation and representation of process graphs, models and conformity checks. In addition to the software library, a technical proof of concept is carried out in R Shiny. In addition to the codebase, a documentation document on the library and Shiny application is drawn up by the contractor and corresponding tests are created and carried out. The subject of the contract is thus composed of a software library, a technical proof of concept, documentation and tests.
sig_668ef8d925336d997aa7.title: Monitoring of identity management in conjunction with EU information systems based on national TR-03156 technical log data

sig_66960ecea890f8a9f994.description: Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust ("OHFT", "the Trust") wishes to undertake Preliminary Market Engagement ("PME") for a patient flow clinical information system. This system shall be used in the "Shaped for Me" Thames Valley and Wessex Adult Secure Provider Collaborative ("the Provider Collaborative") - https://tvwadultsecurepc.nhs.uk/. A Provider Collaborative is a collaboration of public, private, and voluntary sector organisations that aim to deliver unified care across one or more Integrated Care Systems (ICS) irrespective of organisational boundaries. ICSs operate at “system” level, while Provider Collaboratives are a way of organising providers at “place” or “neighbourhood” level to actually deliver services. Their purpose is to: - **Coordinate care at scale** – working across multiple trusts to reduce unwarranted variation in services and outcomes. - **Share resources and expertise** – for example, specialist clinical staff, digital systems, or estates. - **Deliver efficiency and value** – by pooling procurement, back-office functions, or clinical services. - **Improve patient pathways** – so that patients experience more consistent, timely, and equitable care. Provider collaboratives can be subdivided as follows. For the avoidance of doubt, this process is for a Mental Health Provider Collaborative: - **Acute provider collaboratives** – usually groups of hospitals working together (e.g. elective hubs, cancer pathways). - **Mental health provider collaboratives** – often formed first, managing specialised commissioning budgets (e.g. for CAMHS Tier 4 beds, forensic services). - **Community and ambulance collaboratives** – less common but emerging, focusing on joined-up out-of-hospital care and urgent response. Provider Collaboratives can meet their goals through the following activities: - Run managed clinical networks across their member trusts. - Agree joint governance and shared leadership (boards, committees). - Take on delegated budgets from NHS England/ICSs to manage specialised services. - Lead on service transformation programmes, e.g. reducing waiting lists, setting up shared digital records, or improving discharge processes. The Shaped for Me Provider Collaborative is a partnership of seven mental health service providers (NHS Trusts and independent sector providers) working across five Integrated Care Systems, with a total population of around 5.5 million people. It delivers low and medium adult secure mental health services, including: - Low and medium secure care for adult patients with forensic mental health needs. - Low and medium secure care for adult patients with forensic mental health needs and Learning Disability and/or Autistic Spectrum Condition. - Forensic Community Mental Health services. The Trust is the Lead Provider in the Provider Collaborative. It is contractually obliged to procure, manage and maintain a suitable digital clinical system to all providers within the collaborative. The Trust entered into a contract with for its incumbent solution on the 13th October 2021 to provide a patient flow solution that could be further configured to meet the Trust's needs. This was deployed in the Provider Collaborative's Forensic services but not in Adult Eating Disorders ("AED") or Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services ("CAMHS"). The solution has been classified as end-of-life in October 2026 on the expiry of the current contract. The Trust must procure and deploy a new solution (transition for Forensics and new implementation in AED and CAMHS) to replace the incumbent solution. Lot 1: .

sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.description: With this notice, Istekki announces the organisation of market dialogues for a service voucher and purchased service system. The purpose of the dialogue is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. The subject of the procurement is the service voucher and purchased service system entity and its interfaces with other systems, the delivery project (including e.g. migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support services, separately ordered expert services, as well as customer service. Further development may be carried out on the procured system during the contract period. The service voucher and purchased service system is used for granting service vouchers and payment commitments and for purchasing services from private service providers or other public actors. Through the system, it is necessary to centralise the creation and use of service vouchers and purchased service orders (payment commitment) and the settlement of accounts for rendered services to private service providers or other public actors. The service voucher and purchased service system must take into account needs from the perspectives of the service organiser, the service producer and the customer using the service. Through the system, the service organiser must have the option to manage service provider agreements, plan service provision, grant service vouchers and payment commitments, allocate payments, handle correction requests and monitor various report views. The service provider must have the option to apply to become a service provider through the system. In addition, the service provider must be able to record the service received by the customer in the system and thereby handle settlement based on approved transaction entries. The customer must receive the granted service voucher / payment commitment for use via the system. The service voucher customer must have the option to compare or view service providers, monitor the execution of the service from the system and provide feedback on the service. The contracting authority will organise the market dialogues either as remote meetings or in writing, or utilising both methods. The market dialogues will be held in Finnish. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the dialogue of more detailed schedules and instructions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are merely preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as preparation progresses. If you are interested in participating in the market dialogue, please notify us of your interest no later than 11.09.2026 at 14.00 to hankinnat@istekki.fi. If you wish, you can also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material regarding your own service. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering procedure may also be omitted. No separate remuneration is paid for responding to the dialogue or participating in any presentation events. We would like to mention again that this is not a contract notice or call for tenders. The purpose is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate suppliers' participation, as it helps us build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear an entity as possible.
sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.title: Service voucher and purchased service system, market dialogue

sig_6778f89796c0f3373a33.description: Construction Industry Day Introduction In accordance with FAR Companion (FC) 10.001(c), this notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), nor will the VA pay for information requested. Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) will host an industry day event at the James J. Peters Department of Veterans Affairs VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 for all businesses (including, but not limited to, general contractors, subcontractor trades, and material suppliers) interested in the upcoming Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects throughout VISN 2 (NY/NJ). The purpose of the Industry Day is to facilitate collaboration between the VA and general construction contractors and subcontractors of all business sizes who are interested in performing work in New York and New Jersey. This session is designed to give all interested contractors a clear understanding of the project s intent, performance expectations, and execution approach. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the Bronx EHRM project. Six EHRM Infrastructure projects were solicited and awarded in FY26. Four of the six were designated as SDVOSB set-asides, and most of these projects received limited bids or proposals. In FY27, VISN 2 anticipates three projects, Bronx, Manhattan, and Northport, that are particularly large and complex, which may pose significant challenges for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) to execute independently due to their scale and technical requirements. As a result, the VA is considering broadening the competition beyond SDVOSBs, seeking participation from both small and/or large businesses that have the project experience, capabilities, and workforce necessary to fulfill the contract demands. This approach is critical to ensuring a robust competitive environment that accurately reflects market value and supports successful project delivery. EVENT INFORMATION The industry day will be held on Thursday, November 19th, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET. The meeting location will be Room 3D-22 in Building 100, located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468. Contractors are required to pre-register for this event. See Administrative section below. Proposed Agenda: 1. Check-in (please arrive between 9 - 9:30 AM) 2. Introductions 3. Meet and Greet 4. Overview of the EHRM Program and Each Project 4. Site walk of the Bronx VAMC EHRM project 5. Lunch Break 6. Questions and answers session 7. Networking *A final agenda will most likely be posted to SAM.gov closer to the event date. PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS VISN 2 (New York/New Jersey) has five EHRM projects that are anticipated to be solicited and awarded in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and four in FY 2028. The five planned locations for FY27 are at the following VAMC s: Bronx, Canandaigua, Manhattan, Northport, and St. Albans. A description of each project is listed below. Bronx VAMC: The design modernizes the campus technology backbone and supporting building systems so the medical center can implement the VA EHRM platform while maintaining reliable clinical and facility operations. Work extends across the Main Hospital (Building 100) and multiple adjacent campus buildings and support facilities. A distinguishing feature is the construction of two new telecommunications towers. The towers expand communications capacity and require coordinated architectural, structural, civil, electrical, mechanical, and telecommunications design. The broader project also renovates and expands existing telecommunications and data center spaces and upgrades the supporting power, cooling, fiber, security, and life-safety infrastructure. Canandaigua VAMC: This project comprehensively upgrades the campus s fiber optic network and power distribution systems to meet EHRM design guide requirements, ensuring robust support for clinical and facility operations. The work encompasses fiber network enhancements with redundant routes to each IT closet and the main demarcation room, minimizing risk through parallel systems operation during transitions from legacy to new infrastructure. The project also includes expansion or relocation of telecommunications rooms, installation of 100 new IT outlets and 75 electrical outlets, and substantial improvements in power distribution and HVAC systems. Enhanced physical security is provided through secure data cabinets, protected fiber infrastructure, secured telecommunications rooms, and installation of lockable manhole covers for underground fiber pathways. In addition, hazardous material abatement activities will ensure that all upgraded spaces meet current safety and environmental standards. Manhattan VAMC: The design modernizes telecommunications and IT infrastructure throughout Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and creates resilient power and cooling systems to support continuous healthcare operations and future technology demands. The project relocates the existing data center to renovated space and upgrades 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures. The new data center functions as the campus telecommunications hub and is supported by redundant fiber pathways, dedicated year-round cooling, and 2N UPS and electrical distribution redundancy. These features distinguish the Manhattan project and increase the reliability of critical IT systems. Northport VAMC: This information will be provided in an update to this posting on SAM.gov. St. Albans VAMC: The EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Project at St. Albans VA Medical Center in Queens, NY, is a large-scale modernization effort designed to support the implementation of the VA s new EHRM system. The initiative involves major upgrades across multiple buildings, including the construction of a new data center and telecom tower, extensive electrical and mechanical improvements, and the installation of advanced technology infrastructure such as Cat 6A cabling and a fiber optic backbone, all guided by strict VA standards for compliance, safety, and scalability. Key challenges include managing hazardous materials like asbestos and lead-based paint, addressing spatial and technical constraints in existing telecom rooms, coordinating complex system upgrades within an active healthcare environment, and ensuring meticulous phasing to minimize disruptions. Additionally, the project must integrate diverse building systems, adhere to evolving standards, and provide future-proofing for anticipated growth, all of which add significant complexity to both the design and execution phases. *The following projects anticipated for award in FY28: Albany, Buffalo, Batavia and East Orange. Procurement Information The proposed projects will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either request for proposals (RFP) in accordance with FAR part 15, considering technical and price factors or Invitation for Bids (IFBs) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering price only. The full acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been developed and will be determined after the industry day and any additional market research is concluded. The targeted cost ranges of each project are listed below. Between $20 and $30 Million: Canandaigua and St. Albans Between $40 and $50 Million: Bronx and Manhattan Between $50 and $60 Million: Northport The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. This office plans to award contracts for these projects no later than the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2027. Contract duration is estimated to be 24-36 months, for each project, although this will be specifically stated in each solicitation. ADMINISTRATIVE Due to the size of the room, contractors must pre-register for this event by emailing the following information to the point of contact on page 1 no later than 2:00 PM ET on November 5th, 2026: Organization name Business size based on NAICS code 236220 and, if applicable, socioeconomic business type Name(s) of attendee(s) (up to three per company) Any questions or topics you would like addressed during the event Responses must include the notice ID number and project title in the subject line of the email. If you previously responded with your availability to the tentative dates, please respond again to confirm final attendance details. Unregistered participants may be admitted if space allows, but we reserve the right to limit participation to registered attendees only. There will be no virtual attendance option for this event. Any response to this notice will not be considered a bid or proposal. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge or provide feedback with respect to any information submitted under this notice. All business sizes and socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond to this announcement and attend the event. Additional information may be posted about this event. It is the responsibility of the attendees to check SAM.gov for any updates. Please do not submit a full capability statement at this time. Separate from this industry day, the VA will be conducting market research for this requirement via a future sources sought notice posted to SAM.gov under the same notice ID. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized in Contract Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. It is the potential offeror's responsibility to monitor this site for the release of any solicitation or synopsis. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to joseph.rossano@va.gov and Samuel.cornwell@va.gov. Phone calls will not be accepted.

Lot no. 1 - Services for the migration of Applications to the Romanian Government Private Cloud (2). Lot no. 2 - Cybersecurity assessment services. Complete details regarding the services that are the object of this procurement can be found in the Specifications for each individual lot, which are an integral part of the Award Documentation. FOR EACH INDIVIDUAL LOT: the objective of the Framework Agreement for each individual lot, which will be awarded by the Contracting Authority, is to establish a rapid and efficient mechanism for concluding Subsequent Contracts for the provision (procurement) of services for the migration of government digital service Applications to IaaS/PaaS-type solutions in the CPG, including cybersecurity assessment services according to its needs and within the limits of the budget allocated for this purpose. Total estimated value: Between 288.668.898,76 RON excluding VAT and 867.479.705,67 RON excluding VAT (total estimated value of all lots together). The total minimum estimated value associated with the minimum estimated quantities is 288.668.898,76 RON, excluding VAT. The total maximum value associated with the maximum quantities is 867.479.705,67 RON, excluding VAT. The estimated value of the Framework Agreement is expressed as a range. The maximum estimated value of the procurement represents the total maximum value of the Framework Agreement resulting from this procedure for its entire duration (the total cumulative maximum value of both lots). The minimum and maximum estimated values for each individual lot are specified in paragraph II.2. The minimum and maximum estimated quantities for each individual lot are specified in paragraph II.2. Any interested Economic Operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the Award Documentation. The number of days before the deadline for the submission of Tenders by which Economic Operators may request clarifications is 19 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Any request for clarifications must be transmitted via SEAP (www.e-licitatie.ro), after the Economic Operator has registered for the award procedure. The Contracting Authority will respond (via the consolidated response) clearly and completely to all Requests for clarifications and to all requests for additional information received from interested Economic Operators no later than the 11th day before the deadline for the submission of Tenders. The object of the procurement is represented by services for the migration of government digital service Applications to IaaS/PaaS-type solutions in the CPG. The migration of Applications involves the provision of services and, as an ancillary matter, the supply of products. The products need to be incorporated into the services, in order to prepare an application for migration and to ensure the level of cybersecurity requested by the national authorities empowered in this regard. The products may take the form of licences and/or software products necessary to be developed in order to prepare the Application for migration. Complete details regarding the services that are the object of this procurement can be found in the Specifications, an integral part of the Award Documentation, for lot no. 1. The objective of signing the Framework Agreement for lot no. 1 is to establish the terms and conditions, as well as the unit prices, in order to create the framework that allows the Contracting Authority to contract, according to concrete needs, the provision of services that are the object of the Framework Agreement for this lot. sig_67aac576245a75030485.description: Introduction This document constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) issued as part of an early market engagement exercise and does not form part of a formal tender or call for competition. The purpose of this RFI is to engage with the market to seek insight and feedback on the proposed scope of services, lotting structure, pricing mechanisms, and the draft performance management framework, including Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Cadent requires legal support services to process and manage civil claims arising from interactions with third parties. These claims relate to recovery of losses incurred by Cadent in the normal course of operations. The service provider will be responsible for efficiently progressing these matters in accordance with relevant legislation, the Civil Procedure Rules, and Cadent's internal processes. Proposed Lotting Structure • Lot 1 - Legal Support Services • Lot 2 - Damage Claims Cadent are seeking feedback from the supply chain whether this service should remain as a single contract or be split into two separate contracts. Performance Management Monthly and quarterly KPI's will be used to assess activity, financial recovery, legal progression, timeliness, compliance, reporting, and collaboration. A monthly meeting will be held with case managers and senior partners where updates on cases must be provided. Service Credits may apply when the provider fails to meet one or more KPIs. Cadent are seeking feedback from the supply chain on the KPI categories listed above and whether there are any issues or feedback to incorporate into our strategy. Proposed Commercial Model Cadent are seeking feedback from the supply chain on the optimal commercial model for this type of service to incorporate into our strategy. | 2 PR-CT-F-043 Request for Information V-001, 21.11.2024 Lot 1 - Legal Support Services: Draft Scope of Requirements The portfolio of claims to be managed under this contract includes, but is not limited to: • Recovery of contractual sums - including claims related to Connection works, alterations, diversion works, and other operational services. • Theft of Gas Claims - pursued under the Gas Act 1986 and associated license obligations. • Recovery of Sums for Plant Protection Works. • Other miscellaneous invoices covering a range of services. • Recovery from Former Employees - where permitted under employment contract terms. Cadent would require the supplier(s) support in defending claims brought by third parties, including small claims requiring urgent response and general litigation support (pre‐action engagement, pleadings, hearings, negotiation). The supplier(s) must demonstrate strong litigation and recovery experience and provide full lifecycle management including merits assessment, litigation strategy, advocacy, ADR, enforcement, and management of both defended and undefended matters. They must maintain a robust case-management system, build strong working relationships, provide strategic advice, and deliver transparent invoices. The supplier(s) must also offer informed, case‐specific advice to Cadent on how far each claim should be pursued, based on an evidence‐based assessment of the likelihood of recovery. This assessment must consider all relevant indicators, including propensity‐to‐pay (P2P) scoring, land or asset ownership checks, employment status, and any available financial intelligence. The supplier(s) must advise whether the circumstances justify progressing beyond pre‐action to litigation, or whether alternative recovery routes are more appropriate. This includes recommending suitable enforcement options such as Charging Orders where the debt or owns property, Attachment of Earnings Orders where stable employment is confirmed, or other enforcement mechanisms where appropriate. The supplier(s) must present clear recommendations outlining expected recovery prospects, and cost‐benefit considerations to support Cadent in making informed decisions regarding case escalation. Pre-Issue Processes To ensure consistency, compliance, and effective case preparation, the supplier(s) must adhere to the following Pre-Action Protocol Requirements: • A Pre-Action Protocol (PAP) Letter of Claim is required only for business-to-individual cases. • For all other cases where PAP does not apply, the supplier(s) must follow the general pre-action requirements of the Civil Procedure Rules. Case Preparation Requirements • For all Theft of Gas referrals, the supplier(s) must obtain and document a propensityto-pay score before taking legal action.| 3 PR-CT-F-043 Request for Information V-001, 21.11.2024 • Tracing Requirements - Where a debtor's address is unknown, unverified or disputed, the supplier(s) must conduct a trace and provide results prior to issuing legal proceedings. Workload Expectations Cadent anticipates the following approximate volumes: • Small Claims: Approximately 30 cases per month, generally falling below £5,000 in value. • High Value Claims: At any given time, 20-30 ongoing matters with values above the small claim's threshold. A small number of these may range between £100,000 and £1-2 million and typically involve asset damage or theft of gas under relevant statutory frameworks. Lot 2 - Damage Claims: Cadent requires legal support services to process and manage recovery of damages to its assets and, on a limited basis, the defence of claims brought against it by third parties. The services primarily relate to negligence-based damage claims, statutory claims, and construction-related disputes, and include both volume-driven lower-value work and complex, high-value matters. Damage Claims is split into two workstreams: 1. Low Value Claims (Below £10k): a. Debt Recovery b. Full Legal Action 2. High Value Claims (Over £10k) The supplier(s) would be required to manage and progress claims including, but not limited to: • Claims arising from damage to assets, predominantly founded in negligence. • Claims where third parties have failed to comply with relevant Health and Safety Executive (HSE) guidance when undertaking works. • Statutory claims against other statutory undertakers pursuant to the New Roads and Street Works Act 1991 (NRSWA). • Claims against occupiers under the Gas Act permitting works to be undertaken resulting in damage. • Limited support in defending claims brought against the contracting authority, typically within the Small Claims Track. Draft Scope of Requirements 1. Low Value Claims - Debt Recovery: • Issuing a First Letter Before Action (LBA) • Issuing a Second Letter Before Action. • Drafting and issuing a Part 36 Offer where appropriate. 2. Low Value Claims - Full Legal Action: • Issuing a First Letter Before Action (LBA) • Issuing proceedings and obtaining judgment in default where applicable. | 4 PR-CT-F-043 Request for Information V-001, 21.11.2024 • Managing defended matters through to resolution, with the contracting authority undertaking telephone mediation. • Enforcement of judgments via High Court Enforcement Officers (HCEO) where required. 3. High Value Claims: • These matters typically fall under the Pre-Action Protocol for Construction and Engineering Disputes. • For context there were 13 high value claims were instructed in the last 12 months, ranging from £10,500 to £1.5 million. 4. Defence of Third Party Claims: • The supplier(s) may be required, on a limited basis, to assist with defending claims brought against the contracting authority,including Small Claims matters. 5. Disbursements Workload Expectations Cadent anticipates the following volumes: 1. Low Value Claims (Below £10k): a. Debt Recovery = Circa 550 claims per annum. b. Full Legal Action = Circa 132 claims per annum. 2. High Value Claims (Over £10k) = Circa 10-15 per annum. Lot 1: .

sig_67ba13627482296b4dca.description: The purpose of amendment no. 2 is to respond to the following questions. Question-4. Is MARAD open to all forms of propulsion to gain fuel efficiencies - for example, hybrid diesel-electric equipment with electric motors and batteries? Response-4. There are no limits or specific requirements for the type of propulsion or fuel. Technologies, including fuels and propulsion, should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Question-5. Under the Eligibility Information section of the subject notice, it states that the opportunity is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." In reviewing the statutory definition of a “domestic source” under 50 U.S.C. § 4555(7), “the term “domestic source” means a business concern— (A) that performs in the United States or Canada substantially all of the research and development, engineering, manufacturing, and production activities required of such business concern under a contract with the United States relating to a critical component or a critical technology item.” Based on this definition, which appears to include qualifying Canadian businesses as domestic sources for certain USG Response-5. For the purposes of this RFP a domestic applicant is considered to be a contractor organized or existing under the laws of the United States. Keep in mind that the RFP states preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag; the RFP does not exclude those with team leads or team members outside the U.S. " Question-6. Confidentiality of design information: Our understanding is that the final report and presentation will be publicly shared, while sensitive supporting information, such as calculations, design plans and drawings, modeling results, technology details, and cost information, can be provided to MARAD without being made public. The terms and conditions, however, grant MARAD broad rights to reproduce, distribute, and display project materials. Could you clarify whether sensitive design information submitted during the project can be designated and maintained as confidential, and whether MARAD’s rights to distribute it would be limited? Response-6. Confidential business information or sensitive design information will not be shared publicly without permission. Prior to publication, MARAD and the project team will discuss the extent and limits of the information that will be shared. Question-7. Subcontracting limits: Are there any restrictions on the value or proportion of work that may be subcontracted to organizations outside the named project team, such as model testing facilities or noise specialists? Response-7. The proposed project team should include all intended team members including those that would be subcontracted such as testing facilities or noise specialists. The specifics of subcontract awards are not determined by the MARAD project manager. Question-8. Work outside the United States: May project funds be used to subcontract specialized work outside the United States? If so, are there limits on the type or value of that work? Response-8. The proposed project team should include all proposed team members. Preference will be given to those team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag. There is no specific requirement for subcontractors. ========================================================= The purpose for this amendment is to respond to the following questions: Question-1. Domestic Applicant Definition: Section D.1 of the RFP states the Challenge is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." Our company is a U.S.-registered entity, though its ultimate parents are in Canada and Europe. Could you confirm whether an entity with this ownership structure qualifies as a "domestic applicant" for purposes of serving as the lead applicant/Recipient of a cooperative agreement under this RFP? Response-1. For the purposes of this project, a U.S. registered entity will be evaluated as a domestic applicant. Question-2. Citizenship-Based Funding Restriction: We understand that MARAD/META cooperative agreements may include a restriction on using award funds for "work to be done or done in a facility owned by someone other than a Citizen of the United States (as defined in 46 C.F.R. § 315.3(b))." Could you confirm whether this restriction, or an equivalent, will apply to cooperative agreements resulting from this RFP, and if so, how it would apply to a design team whose naval architecture/engineering firm is U.S.-registered and performs all work domestically, but has foreign parent ownership? Response-2. For the purposes of this project, a design team located in the U.S. working at a U.S.-registered firm and performing all work domestically would not fall under the restriction. Question-3. Team Lead Eligibility vs. Preference: Section B notes a preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag." Could you confirm whether this operates solely as an evaluative preference, or whether it functions as a disqualifying eligibility criterion for a team lead whose ultimate parent is a foreign entity? Response-3. The preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag" is an evaluative preference. A U.S. registered entity with U.S. offices and staff performing work domestically, would fall under consideration as a domestic applicant for this project. ======================================================================= U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION: MARAD will provide funding through a cooperative agreement for the execution of this Design Challenge. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit MARAD to make any award. To be considered for selection, the contractor participating in the Challenge must be able to complete it within 18 months from time of award. The final report and other summary materials will be publicly available and posted to the META webpage. Proposals in response to this RFP are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals will be screened for use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. Any use of AI tools in generating content for the proposal must be clearly identified and justified. MARAD reserves the right to fund one or none of the proposals received under this RFP. MARAD is not responsible for reimbursing the costs that applicants incur to prepare and submit their proposals in response to this RFP. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this RFP will not be returned. It is MARAD’s policy to treat all proposals submitted under this RFP as sensitive competitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. All applicants must be registered and current with SAM.gov at the time of award. ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION. 1. Eligible Applicants: Open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals. 2. MARAD is seeking to provide full funding through cooperative agreement for the proposals that provides sufficient, verifiable, and detailed data on how to reach the objective of this Design Challenge. MARAD will fund 100% of the total cost of the project. Proposals must include a detailed cost breakdown that shows how Federal funds will be used for the project. Please see Section E.2 for information on proposal format requirements. 3. Systems for Award Management (SAM) Requirements. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Please see Section E.3 for information on SAM requirements. MARAD will not make an award to any applicant with an exclusion in SAM. APPLICATION AND SUBMISSION INFORMATION Address to Request Application Package. This RFP contains all the information needed to submit a proposal and be considered for award. No specific application form or other materials need to be obtained from MARAD. Content and Form of Application. Proposals are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals must provide sufficient, verifiable, and detailed information covering all elements of the “Proposal Content” described in section B.1 above. Unique Entity Identifier and System for Award Management (SAM). Each applicant is required to: (a) be registered and current in SAM before submitting its application; (b) provide a valid unique entity identifier in its applicant; and (c) continue to maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times during which it has an active Federal award or an application or plan under consideration by a Federal awarding agency. MARAD will not make an award to an applicant until the applicant has complied with all applicable unique entity identifier and SAM requirements. If an applicant has not fully complied with the requirements by the time MARAD is ready to make an award, MARAD may determine that the applicant is not qualified to receive an award and use that determination as a basis for making an award to another applicant. Submission Dates and Times. The deadline for proposal submission is 12:00 PM EST on the closing date listed for this RFP on SAMS.gov Please submit proposals in PDF format attached to an email. Send proposals to Christian Onwudiegwu/Contract Specialist at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov, Office of Acquisitions. Do not send paper copies, or other media of the proposal via post office or delivery service. Proposals received by MARAD after the deadline will not be considered for award. An email will be deemed “received” by MARAD on the date and time the email was “sent” to the email address in Section E.7, below, as determined by MARAD’s servers. Intergovernmental Review. This funding opportunity is not subject to Executive Order 12372, “Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs.” l Funding Restrictions. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201 for cost principles used to determine allowable costs of work performed under Federal awards. Other Submission Requirements. Proposals must be submitted by the deadline set forth in Section E.4 above by electronic mail to Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov and Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. Please include the Funding Opportunity Number and Title in the Subject Line. APPLICATION REVIEW INFORMATION Review and Selection Process. MARAD will set up an internal review team to evaluate all proposals that are submitted under this announcement. All eligible proposals will be evaluated within four weeks after the closing date. If the review team has any questions on an individual proposal, it will notify the applicant for clarification. The proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: Well-documented and context-appropriate plan to undertake and successfully demonstrate the design integration of technology to achieve the fuel efficiency goal, URN limit, and economic analysis required by the Challenge. Clear application of methods supporting vessel design, technology integration, data collection, assessment, and analysis to include specifications for fuel efficiency and URN modeling consistent with international and class standards and reference to existing guidelines, standards, and notations. Methodologies must include descriptions of major analytical approaches being proposed for the Challenge components to meet the Design Challenge Parameters. Methodology also includes any specific models and data sources intended to be used for each component of the Challenge. The Team’s capabilities, related experience, technical knowledge, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve Challenge goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Detailed project timeline with descriptions of key decision points and areas of uncertainty. Budget and justification demonstrating appropriate and defensible cost per component, personnel, timeline, and final deliverables; including consideration of the experience and capability of key personnel involved, the number of hours budgeted for key people, and the role, value, and level of participation of any noted partners. FEDERAL AWARD ADMINISTRATION INFORMATION Federal Award Notices. The successful applicant(s) will be notified by MARAD’s Office of Acquisition via telephone; however, the telephone call is not the actual award or the authorization to begin performance. All awards will be made by a cooperative agreement signed by MARAD’s Agreement/Grants Officer. After an award has been made, a representative from the MARAD’s Office of Innovation will schedule a kick-off meeting for the project. Unsuccessful applicants will be notified via email. Administrative and National Policy Requirements. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Costs Principles and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201, for applicable administrative and national policy requirements. For a copy of the general terms and conditions of the Federal award made under this RFP, please contact Christian Onwudiegwu at christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov. Federal awards made under RFP may include additional terms that are specific to the project, including without limitation awardee information, project description, funding details, and appropriate data rights clauses. Reporting. Applicants are advised to review 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Costs Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards, as supplemented by 2 CFR Part 1201, for applicable reporting requirements. Federal awards made under this RFP may include additional reporting requirements that are appropriate for the specific project to be funded by MARAD. FEDERAL AWARDING AGENCY CONTACT For any questions relating to the technical or programmatic aspects of this RFP, please contact Alyson Azzara at Alyson.Azzara@dot.gov. For any questions about the administration of this funding opportunity and any awards, please contact Christian Onwudiegwu at Christian.onwudiegwu@dot.gov. cc: Kelly Mitchell-Carroll at K.mitchell-carroll@dot.gov. OTHER INFORMATION Applicants must identify all proprietary information in its submission. MARAD is not obligated to make any Federal award as a result of this RFP.

sig_67bd0d7d346752857629.description: WFD wishes to establish a panel of specialist service providers to provide technical services from time to time to support WFD's capacity and capability as part of their global support. These services are expected to support WFD primarily as part of the Democratic Governance Centre of Expertise, which WFD is delivering in partnership with the FCDO. WFD have previously operated a framework for this service, which is due to expire on 31 March 2026. WFD are building on the learning from this framework to create an enhanced model of engagement with specialist expert partners who can support with WFD strategic objectives. Interested parties should note that the contractual delivery locations could be world wide, and this would be confirmed on a case-by-case basis for individual contracts, WFD are have engaged in pre-market engagement to seek interested service providers views on the establishment of a Dynamic Market (DM) which WFD may use from time to time for any opportunities that sit above a threshold value of £207,720 (this figure may change from time to time in alignment with the requirements of the Procurement Act 2023), and the establishment of a Preferred Supplier List (PSL) for any below threshold opportunities. As part of this exercise, WFD are in a position to request applications from interested service providers to be a part of a Dynamic Market, and part of a Preferred Supplier List that will run concurrently with the Dynamic Market. Service Providers will be able to elect to apply to one or both the Dynamic Market and the Preferred Supplier list. The Dynamic Market and Preferred Supplier List will operate across the following parts (lots): Lot 1 - Expertise in Political Economy Analysis and approaches Lot 2 - Expertise in Media Freedom and Media Development Lot 3 - Expertise in Rule of Law and Justice Sector Reform Lot 4 - Expertise in Public Sector Management Reform Lot 5 - Expertise in Conflict, Security and Stabilisation Lot 6 - Expertise in Environmental Democracy and Climate Governance / justice Lot 7 - Expertise in Monitoring Evaluation and Learning Lot 8 - Expertise in Facilitation, Training, Coaching, and Adult-learning Applicants should note that WFD reserve the right to amend these parts as may be required from time-to-time throughout the lifecycle of the DM/PSL. WFD are seeking initial applications from interest suppliers by close of 06 March 2026, in order to establish the DM/PSL for use from 01 April 2026, but welcome applications throughout the lifecycle of the procurement. Lot Lot 1: Expertise in Political Economy Analysis and approaches. Support WFD's programming, research and business initiatives and/or the Centre of Expertise in responding to FCDO Posts' enquiries for/on political economy / context and sectoral analyses. This may include the following: - Conduct timely and responsive political economy / context and sectoral analyses, in line with FCDO's Guidance on Understanding political economy analysis, thinking, and working politically, and/or other methodological approaches, tools and frameworks, as and when appropriate. - Provide specialist technical advice and assistance on conducting political economy / context and sectoral analyses. This may include analysis of selected democratic governance issues, specific sectors, and/or broader PEAs of countries / contexts to identify and understand the political settlement and the main existing / emerging challenges and opportunities. Analysis and any accompanying recommendations / conclusions (as required) should be well-grounded to support Posts in applying and implementing these recommendations in their work. - Review / evaluate and/or quality assure the methodology and design of programmes. Lot Lot 2: Expertise in Media Freedom and Media Development. Support WFD's programming, research and business initiatives and/or the Centre of Expertise in responding to FCDO Posts' enquiries on and/or related to media freedom and media development. This may include the following: - Conduct timely and responsive country assessments of the media landscape and/or a media development. - Provide impartial and impactful technical advice and recommendations to promote / support media freedom and media development. - Review and/or quality assure the design and/or development of media freedom and media development programmes / initiatives / activities. Lot Lot 3: Expertise in Rule of Law and Justice Sector Reform. Support WFD's programming, research and business initiatives and/or the Centre of Expertise in responding to FCDO Posts' enquiries on and/or related to the rule of law, constitutional law, and/or justice sector reform. This may include the following: - Conduct timely and responsive country assessments / analyses of the legislative landscape and/or specific bills, legislation, or Constitutions as they may relate to a specific topic/issue of interest. - Provide impartial and impactful technical advice and recommendations as they relate to the rule of law, constitutional law, and/or justice sector reform. - Review and/or quality assure the design and/or development of rule of law and justice sector reform focused/related programmes / initiatives / activities. Lot Lot 4: Expertise in Public Sector Management Reform. Support WFD's programming, research and business initiatives and/or the Centre of Expertise in responding to FCDO Posts' enquiries on and/or related to Public Sector Management Reform. This may include expertise in/on the following: - Centre of Government - Governance, accountability, ethics, and risk management - Strategy and policy reform - Organisational change management and stakeholder engagement - Process and service delivery - Government procurement - Planning - Measuring performance - Civil service reform and Human Resource Management - Public financial management and economic governance - Digitalisation and E-Government Lot Lot 5: Expertise in Conflict, Security and Stabilisation. Support WFD's programming, research and business initiatives and/or the Centre of Expertise in responding to FCDO Posts' enquiries on and/or related to Conflict, Security and Stabilisation. sig_67bdf62e1d970d047199.description: A Budapest Gyógyfürdői és Hévizei Zrt., as Contracting Authority, requests the provision of an integrated cashless payment system for the sites operated by the Contracting Authority and the commercial units operating within them, during the second tendering phase of the IT Dynamic Purchasing System established for the procurement of IT equipment, supplies, software, licences and related services. The subject of the procedure in the DPS participation phase according to the category defined with regard to Section 106 (4) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.): category 6 Categories 6. Service elements belonging to the categories: installation, operation, testing, troubleshooting, support, consulting, development; Quantity: The Contracting Authority shall conclude a framework agreement with the winning Tenderer for the operation of a 1 system for a definite period of 24 months to the net value of 180.000.000,- HUF. The aim of the procurement is to provide and operate a cashless payment system for the Contracting Authority. The Contracting Authority intends to use a payment system associated with a commercial voucher issued by the Tenderer and registered in electronic form – which does not qualify as a substitute means of payment or electronic money –, which is embodied by a voucher card or a proximity identification device appearing in another form (hereinafter collectively: "Voucher Card"), in such a way that visitors to the Bath can redeem the topped-up amount by using the card/device purchased on site and through other alternative sales channels agreed in advance by the Parties. The Tenderer's task is the establishment of the technical conditions for payment with the Voucher Card and the cashless settlement system, on-site and remote operation, and the provision of related tasks in the commercial units operating in the Contracting Authority's Baths and at its contractual mobile commercial partners in error-free and complete quality as set out in the technical specification and the draft contract. The cashless payment method used in commercial units shall simultaneously mean: - acceptance of any payment card suitable for payment issued by any commercial bank, - use of the electronic balance managed in the system using the Voucher Card, uniquely linked to the electronic identification device. Furthermore, the Tenderer's task is: - the development, manufacture and rental of the Voucher Card; - the creation and operation of a network consisting of electronic payment points (POS Terminals, as well as NFC card readers, hereinafter the "Terminals") with regard to the individual Baths; - the creation and operation of a network consisting of cash top-up points (hereinafter "Top-up point") with regard to the individual Baths; - the creation and operation of the central IT system implementing the acceptance of the Voucher Card and vouchers, managing the balance of the Voucher Cards and purchases made with them, as well as the Terminal network and cash top-up network, including a system providing traffic reports for the Contracting Authority and its partners, but not including the construction and operation of the extra-low and/or low-voltage network installed at the Bath site; - the provision of the service through a wired or mobile network established and operated by the Client; - ensuring access to a 4G-based data communication network between the Terminals, the Top-up points and the central system. The Contractor's tasks under this point are defined in detail in the Technical Specification forming Annex No. 2 to this Contract. During the operation of the DPS, based on Section 107. (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the Contracting Authority shall make the exact technical content and contract terms relating to the specific public procurements to be implemented in the system available to the economic operators participating in the DPS simultaneously with the sending of the call for tenders. Within this framework, the Contracting Authority shall determine which product category the subject of the specific procedure belongs to. The technical description of the service forming the subject of the procurement is contained in the Procurement Documentation. The contract terms are contained in the draft contract attached to the procedure. The Contracting Authority draws the attention of esteemed Tenderers that it publishes a sample task in the pricing table, the pricing of which serves evaluation, i.e. it is a calculated value. The references to makes, origins, brands, types, processes, or activities included in the public procurement technical documentation were made solely for the purpose of clearly defining the nature and quality of the goods, and the Contracting Authority shall also accept performance equivalent thereto or more favourable to the Contracting Authority than them. Proving equivalence is the task of the Tenderer.

sig_67cb5304ffb015de35a9.description: The Liverpool City Region Combined Authority (LCRCA) is looking to create a new active travel map (walking, wheeling and cycling), primarily concentrating on cycle routes and facilities across the city region. The supplier will work with the LCRCA and the six constituent authorities (Halton, Knowsley, Liverpool, Sefton, St Helens and Wirral) to develop a map that is both clear and easy to use. The result of the contract will be six maps (1 for each local authority area) of active travel facilities such as segregated cycle lanes, off road cycle networks and on road quiet routes. The mapping data that is created by the successful supplier will be owned solely by the LCRCA. This is so that when new routes and facilities are built, the maps can be easily updated by the internal personnel using a standard specification. The maps will need to include key destinations, safety information, key landmarks, bike shops, repair stations, and links to public transport hubs. These will be determined with the successful supplier. Maps must have clear legibility and at an accurate scale for urban areas and consistent, intuitive symbology for different types of cycling infrastructure. Maps must meet accessibility standards, ensuring they are usable for people with visual impairments or varying levels of experience. We would like potential suppliers to provide us with a short statement (no more than 500 words) as to how they feel they could best suit our needs and their ethos as an organisation along with (if they have them) examples of Active Travel Maps they have previously made. Lot 1: .

sig_67da10303e40f5199415.description: ARTE G.E.I.E. in Strasbourg employs 590 people on permanent contracts and 300 people on temporary contracts: fixed-term contracts, freelance workers and intermittent workers. The HRIS ensuring administrative management and payroll is SAP ECC6, with a migration to SAP S/4HANA planned. It is currently supplemented by a UKG solution to cover the functionalities of an electronic safe, electronic signature and electronic personnel file. The purpose of the contract is the supply, implementation, hosting, maintenance and support of an integrated solution for the digitisation of human resources management processes covering the following functions. The interfaces, documentation and support are provided at a minimum in French and German. • Employee digital safe. Personal space held by the employee, intended for the storage and availability of HR documents provided to them for a period of at least fifty years, from the date of their deposit or signature. It allows ARTE to satisfy the obligation to make the payslip available in electronic form as provided for in Article D. 3243-8 of the Labour Code. This space remains accessible to the employee after the end of their employment contract and beyond the term of the contract. • Electronic personnel file. Documentary archive with probative value, accessible to authorised personnel, constituting the employee's individual file for the duration of their employment contract as well as during the recruitment phase that precedes it and the legal retention period that follows it. The solution ensures classification by document type, search, guarantee of integrity and traceability of access and actions, the lifecycle, and retention periods. • Electronic signature. Signature service whose level of proof is adjustable according to the process concerned, for internal as well as external signatures, in individual or bulk mode, including automated signatures for documents issued in series. It guarantees the retention of associated evidence and their retrieval. • Employee portal. Service allowing the employee to consult their documents and initiate human resources management requests by means of standard forms and configurable validation workflows, with progress tracking. • Distribution of individual human resources management documents. Secure, individualised and traceable distribution of documents produced by ARTE to each employee, including employment contracts and amendments, letters, management decisions, certificates and end-of-contract documents, regardless of the upstream production process. This function covers in particular the distribution of payslips, carried out in five campaigns per month. The solution supports the employee's objection to the digitised delivery of their payslip. The contract includes the recovery, in the electronic personnel file, of documents and signature evidence created since 2019. It includes a commitment to service continuity, reversibility at the end of the contract, as well as the regulation of any use of artificial intelligence excluding the collection, reuse or training based on ARTE's data. The hosting, processing, administration and backup of data are carried out exclusively on the territory of the European Union or the European Economic Area, including for each subcontractor. The contract involves the processing of personal data. Selected candidates must demonstrate, during the procedure, their ability to present appropriate guarantees regarding data protection, which must be maintained throughout the execution of the contract. The procedures and documents to be produced will be specified in the consultation.
sig_67da10303e40f5199415.title: Integrated solution for the digitisation of HR processes
