sig_68be26c5ac6585fac723.description: Delivery, implementation, migration and commissioning of an integrated ERP and billing system Lot LOT-0001: Delivery, implementation, migration and commissioning of an integrated ERP and billing system. Stadtwerke Forchheim (SWF), acting as a municipal multi-utility company, operate several divisions and perform central energy market roles in the process (including supplier, grid operator and metering point operator). The energy business processes required for this, particularly within the framework of market communication, are currently operated via an existing, multi-part system landscape. Technical metering point operation is the responsibility of SWF; the smart meter gateway is provided by an external service provider. Operation currently takes place on-premises in SWF's data centre. Against the background of the strategic further development of the existing product landscape and the prospective end of support for individual systems in use, SWF are pursuing the goal of replacing the existing ERP and billing landscape with an integrated, future-proof solution. The subject matter of this tender is therefore the delivery, implementation, migration and commissioning of an integrated ERP and billing system incl. project, migration, training and support services. The future solution is intended to provide a continuous system landscape for commercial, energy-economic and technical processes and, in particular, ensure the professional requirements of SWF as well as the client- and audit-proof mapping of operational management and service structures. In addition, other business-critical functions currently provided in a separate application are also to be covered by integration, migration or solution approaches as required. The offered target architecture can be designed optionally as a cloud/SaaS or on-premises solution; the tenderer must present the long-term support of the relevant market roles and processes.
sig_68be26c5ac6585fac723.title: Delivery, implementation, migration and commissioning of an integrated ERP and billing system

sig_68bf7f8919aa7ad8e231.description: In accordance with Law no. 92/1996 on the organisation and operation of the Special Telecommunications Service, supplemented by Law no. 266/2020, STS is the specialised central body, with legal personality, which organises, directs, carries out, controls and coordinates activities in the field of special telecommunications for public authorities in Romania and for other users provided for in Annex no. 1 to the aforementioned law. In accordance with the provisions of Law no. 214/2024 on the use of the electronic signature, time stamp and the provision of trust services based thereon, STS has become a qualified trust service provider in accordance with European Regulation 910/2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions (https://eidas.ec.europa.eu/efda/tl-browser/#/screen/tl/RO/6). Respecting national and European requirements in the field, the STS Public Key Infrastructure (STS PKI) aims to offer solutions (products and services) concerning electronic identity within electronic transactions and to ensure the security of computer networks and software applications offered to its beneficiaries. In accordance with legislation and practices in the field (Law no. 214/2024 and eIDAS Regulation no. 910/2014 with subsequent amendments and completions), STS provides qualified certification services intended exclusively for beneficiaries under Law no. 92/1996. With a view to developing new services associated with the electronic signature as well as to modernising and expanding existing ones at the Special Telecommunications Service, on 10.04.2024 the financing contract was signed relating to the project "Development of the STS platform for the interoperability of the remote qualified signature service with other document management services in electronic format and the development of the electronic service for the long-term preservation and guarantee of electronic signatures applied to documents signed electronically for central public authorities", financed through the Smart Growth, Digitisation and Financial Instruments Programme - PoCIDIF, Specific Objective RSO1.2 Capitalising on the benefits of digitisation, to the benefit of citizens, companies, research organisations and public authorities (ERDF), Action 2.2. E-governance and digitisation to the benefit of citizens/2.2.1 E-gov in public administration/institutions, Measure 1 Public services intended for citizens and/or companies identified in the CSP managed by the ADR and/or in accordance with the eGuv Policy. Having regard to the provisions of the aforementioned financing contract, the acquisition by STS of software and hardware products for the development of the STS platform for the interoperability of the remote qualified signature service and for the development of the electronic service for the long-term preservation and guarantee of the electronic signature is necessary. The contracting authority shall clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarification by the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders, for clarifications received at least 18 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Acquisition of data storage equipment - 4 pcs.; Acquisition of software for compilation - 30 cpl.; Acquisition of: Virtualisation software licence type 1 - 6 pcs. Virtualisation software licence type 2 - 6 pcs. Virtualisation software licence type 3 - 10 pcs Software licence for creating backups and replicating virtual machines - 5 pcs.; Acquisition of software for database administration - 20 cpl.; Acquisition of a static and dynamic code analysis solution - 1 cpl.

sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.description: The employee survey in The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is carried out annually, usually at the end of January/February. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency has had a very high response percentage in recent years, between 82 % and 87%. In 2025, the survey was sent out to just over 2,000 respondents. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency currently uses Rambøll as its supplier and they are responsible for the entire process - from dispatching and administration to analysing the results. The results will be presented in an insight report that will be presented to the management team. With new competence in the HR department, including HR analyst competence, Forsvarsbygg is now considering taking a greater degree of ownership of the survey. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is looking at an option to administer the survey itself and get access to raw data, so that own analyses can be carried out, etc. Practical if the market dialogue: There is a form (excel sheet) that can be answered and the deadline is set at 12:00 1 December 2025.Input and form is submitted by using the communication model in Mercell.Based on received responses, the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency will make an assessment and possibly call in some suppliers for 1:1 conversations - if the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency deems it appropriate. sig_68f2a3b350aef169ff62.description: The subject of the public contract (hereinafter also "PC") is the provision of background materials for the implementation of the project "New electronic records management system for the Financial Administration of the Czech Republic" (hereinafter also "eSSL Project"), which will meet the requirement for proper certification of the electronic records management system (hereinafter also "eSSL") within the meaning of § 69b to § 69e of Act No. 499/2004 Coll., on Archiving and Records Management and on Amendments to Certain Acts, as amended (hereinafter "ZoASS"). Certification means the assessment of the compliance of the electronic records management system with the requirements of Decree No. 259/2012 Coll., on the details of the performance of records management, issued on the basis of the authorisation under § 70 paragraph 1 of the ZoASS and the National Standard for Electronic Records Management Systems (hereinafter "NSESSS"). The new electronic records management system for the Financial Administration of the Czech Republic is classified as a significant information system (hereinafter also "VIS") within the meaning of Act No. 181/2014 Coll., on Cyber Security and on Amendments to Related Acts (Cyber Security Act), as amended (hereinafter "ZoKB"). In the future, a change of this classification to a critical information infrastructure system (hereinafter also "KII") is expected in connection with the implementation of Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council (EU) 2022/2555 of 14. December 2022 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union and amending Regulation (EU) No. 910/2014 and Directive (EU) 2018/1972 and repealing Directive (EU) 2016/1148 (NIS 2 Directive) into the legal order of the Czech Republic in the form of a new cyber security act. A more detailed list of the most relevant regulations for the performance of the PC forms Annex No. 14 of the TD. The subject of the PC consists of the following parts: a) preparation of an analysis of how to implement a new electronic records management system in the environment of the Financial Administration of the Czech Republic, and a description of the current state of the existing eSSLs used; b) preparation of an architectural design of the eSSL Project and integration of the new eSSL into the information systems of the Financial Administration of the Czech Republic; c) preparation of a solution concept; d) preparation of tender documentation for the implementation of the eSSL Project. The subject of the PC further includes the provision of advisory and consultancy activities during the tender procedure initiated on the basis of the prepared tender documentation (hereinafter also "consultation"), in a total maximum scope of 30 man-days (hereinafter "MD"), where 1 MD represents 8 hours of work by one contractor employee. The contracting authority is not obliged to take the entire scope of MD if it turns out during the implementation of the subject of the PC that it can be procured with lower capacity requirements. Only the MD actually provided will be invoiced to the contracting authority, following the procedure according to Art. III paragraph 9 et seq. of the draft Contract for Work (hereinafter "draft contract" or "contract").

sig_692e2d268e5a63183834.description: The Republic of Croatia needs, in accordance with its needs, to establish its own BIM guidelines and standards to ensure consistency and quality across all projects. By developing and implementing standards and defining guidelines, interoperability is introduced, communication is simplified, and errors during project execution are reduced. Adapting these standards to the specific needs and objectives of the Republic of Croatia is crucial for the successful implementation of BIM. The guidelines should provide answers on how BIM will be integrated into existing workflows, technologies, and processes, and define standards and rules. BIM standards should specify naming conventions, data exchange protocols, and modelling rules. The implementation plan should provide a detailed timeline for introducing BIM for different types and phases of the project. A phased approach to implementation helps the gradual and systematic introduction of BIM at all necessary levels. The state of BIM implementation in EU countries depends directly on the strategic objectives of each country, readiness for digital transition, preparedness of the state, public, and private sectors, the legislative framework, and also the preparedness of the university community. The subject of procurement is the service of drawing up national guidelines for the implementation of building information modelling / construction (BIM) with the aim of introducing BIM into spatial planning and construction processes. The starting point of this project is to effectively define the implementation of BIM at the national level through comprehensive guidelines with a elaborated approach, plan, and instructions. Drawing up the guidelines will provide a quality basis for amending statutory and secondary legislation, and will provide stakeholders with easier adoption of BIM technology. The adoption of BIM technology in the AEC (Architecture, Engineering and Construction) sector has progressed significantly in recent years. Project teams use BIM 3D digital models for project collaboration, which ensures consistent and accurate project data regardless of how many times the project changes or who changes it (engineer, architect, or building/infrastructure owner). Such projects are sustainable, completed faster, and more economical. A detailed description of the procurement is defined in the project task and technical specifications from the annex.
sig_692e2d268e5a63183834.title: Preparation of national guidelines for the implementation of building information modelling / construction (BIM)

sig_69308ce8895fc5d7ae90.description: The subject of the contract is the provision of a service entitled: Purchase of high-resolution satellite scenes, which will serve the construction of the National Satellite Information System (NSIS), a system for the reception, storage, processing and sharing of satellite data together with the necessary infrastructure, the purpose of which is to provide monitoring services, information products, analytical tools and services. High-resolution satellite data allow for obtaining very detailed geospatial data enabling the analysis of areas, objects and environmental changes. Spatial resolutions below 3 metres allow for more accurate identification of the surveyed area compared to free satellite images characterised by resolutions above 10 m. High-resolution satellite data are used in many fields, including agriculture, spatial planning, crisis management and environmental monitoring.
sig_69308ce8895fc5d7ae90.title: Purchase of high-resolution satellite scenes

sig_69354adb46d65346a779.description: This tender covers the supply and maintenance of an AI system which, by collecting and analysing images of a road surface, can identify potential damage, its extent and location. The system is to replace the traditionally used main inspections regarding the registration of road surface cracks, crazing, patches and potholes. The system must be implemented on the mobile phones made available by the Contracting Authority, which are installed in the inspection vehicles that normally carry out operational inspections on the national road network. The inspection vehicles are driven by a third party, cf. section 5.4 of the contract. By implementing such an AI system, the Contracting Authority will achieve a more frequent update rate for the condition of the road than is currently the case. This enables necessary repairs to be carried out more quickly, as well as the monitoring and mapping of any development in the damage pattern on the roads. More frequent mapping of how road damage develops over time also provides a better data basis, which can be used to predict when necessary repairs and maintenance work should be carried out.
sig_69354adb46d65346a779.title: BBM.BEL.01 Tender for a contract for the supply and maintenance of an AI system for the registration of road damage

sig_695255c55ee702a2bdc3.description: Finnfund (Teollisen yhteistyön rahasto Oy) is procuring project management services to implement a payroll outsourcing project. The subject of the procurement is a project manager service, in which the Supplier is responsible for the project planning and project management of the payroll outsourcing project throughout the entire lifecycle of the project. Content of the service The subject of the procurement is a project management service for a payroll outsourcing project. In the service, the selected supplier acts as a representative of the contracting authority and is responsible for the planning, management and execution of the payroll outsourcing project throughout the entire lifecycle of the project in accordance with the responsibility distribution table attached to the call for tenders. The tasks include, among other things, current state analysis, definition of requirements, production of substantive content for the preparation of the competitive tendering, management of the transfer and implementation phase, coordination of integrations and data transfers, and guidance of the change period following implementation. The goal of the project is to ensure a controlled and secure transition of payroll services to a new service provider without service interruptions, as well as a significant reduction in manual work stages through automation. A separate external partner, PTCServices Oy, is responsible for the implementation of the public competitive tendering (procurement of the service provider) related to the project. Independence and conflict of interest The Supplier and its designated persons must act in their duties completely independently and objectively. The Supplier or its designated persons must not have any financial, operational or personal connection to the parties participating in the future service provider tender that could jeopardise impartiality in the preparation of the procurement, the selection of the winner or the supervision of the service provider. The Supplier or persons or entities connected to it cannot participate in the service provider tender. Schedule The estimated total duration of the service is approximately 16 months. The service continues after the approval of the project until the change period following implementation has lasted at least six (6) months. The project manager must be available to the Client no later than 1.6.2026, when the service is intended to begin. The project is divided into four main phases: procurement preparation (May–August 2026), competitive tendering and selection of the service provider (August–November 2026), transfer and implementation (December 2026 – April 2027), and the change period (April – October 2027). The dates presented in the schedule are target dates, and the final schedule of the project will be specified based on the project plan to be approved at the project start-up phase. The service is produced mainly as remote work using Microsoft Teams. At the beginning of the project, in workshops and in other critical phases, on-site work at the Client's premises in Helsinki may be required as necessary. The project manager must be available to the Client on average for approximately three (3) working days per week, but the workload may vary in different project phases. The use of time will be agreed upon in more detail between the parties. The procurement quantities are estimates and do not constitute a volume purchase obligation for the Client. Language and security requirements The service is produced primarily in Finnish. Finnfund's working language is English, which is why the Project Manager is required to have sufficient oral and written English language skills. A personnel security clearance will be sought for the designated persons in accordance with the Security Clearance Act (726/2014). The Supplier shall only use secure cloud services located in the EU/EEA area or systems provided by the Client for the processing of project data. The service is described in more detail in Appendix 2 "Service Description".

The procurement will possibly consist of the following areas: A. Digitisation and scanning of samples (= scanners) B. Quality assurance of scanned samples (= harmonisation module) C. Viewing of digitised samples (= viewers and image server solution) D. Ongoing IT services supporting digital pathology The procurement areas described above are Fimlab's preliminary views. The CAD solutions must enable real-time coordination, communication and situational awareness for UK SBA emergency services. It should provide a unified platform for dispatch, tracking and communication across all blue light agencies, including SBA Customs & Immigration. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS The supplier must provide a solution that meets the following capabilities: 1. The dashboard must identify which service assets are assigned to. 2. A mobile application compatible with Android and iOS, deployable across staff and mobile resources. The application must support communication, location tracking and operational commands. It should also enable audio communication and integrate with body-camera or video equipment to enhance functionality. 3. instant on-screen features, such as: - live video streaming from a caller's device without requiring an app download - location data such as GPS for missing persons - Secure management of media attachments via SMS - Real-time text chat with multi-language translation - Delivery of operational commands through messaging and through audio - Audio communication alongside body-camera or video support. 4. Simple onboarding and setup, including bulk user creation for all services and integration with Microsoft Azure Active Directory for Single Sign-On (SSO) 5. Training options for key users and administrators, delivered remotely or face-to-face/ 6. API integration through RESTful API for data exchange, analytics dashboards, and triggering CAD functionality. 7. Integration with drones and third-party devices, supporting RTMP streaming in up to 4K UHD quality, accessible via the CAD dashboard and mobile app. 8. Support and maintenance, providing at least remote assistance via telephone and email. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS The supplier's solution must provide: 1. Secure cloud storage that will be hosted in the UK, with provision of a minimum capacity of 0.5 TB and three-way replication for data protection. 2. High availability and built-in resilience to ensure continuity of critical operations, prevent data loss, and maintain service through multi-server connectivity. ADITIONAL DATA & SERVICE LIMITS The solution must include: 1. Provision for at least 250 high-priority SMS messages per month. 2. Support for one concurrent RTMP video stream per agency at any given time. 3. A minimum of 0.5 TB of secure, replicated cloud storage hosted in UK data centres. COMPLIANCE The solution must meet the following information security and data protection standards: 1. Adherence to Ministry of Defence (MOD) information assurance requirements and protective marking policies. 2. Full compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) for handling personal and sensitive data. 3. Certification or compliance with ISO 27001, the international standard for Information Security Management, covering data protection and risk management (or a demonstrably equivalent standard). sig_69843c7c2f0c33aefc7d.description: Derbyshire Constabulary (DC) and Leicestershire Police (LP) are currently exploring the market for solutions that could modernise our HR and Duty Management system. The force aims to rationalise its digital landscape by replacing legacy applications with a set of integrated systems capable of supporting end to end business processes. DC currently operates an HR Shared Service with LP covering HR and Duty Management. As part of this market engagement, suppliers are invited to respond to one of the options below: 1. Core HR and Duty Management 2. Core HR 3. Duty Management Both forces must ensure optimal value for money across its technology estate. By transitioning to streamlined and cost effective solutions, aiming to achieve operational efficiencies, reduce duplication, eliminate siloed working practices, and future proof core business functions. A consolidated platform is expected to strengthen organisational resilience and support more connected, efficient ways of working across both frontline and support functions. As part of this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME), the forces are exploring whether a solution could serve multiple enabling-services departments across different policing areas. Assessing whether the proposed solution could incorporate a partitioned platform capable of hosting HR and Duty Management services. This approach would enable both forces to benefit from shared technological advancements while maintaining operational independence, data segregation, and appropriate local governance controls. Key Systems Core HR Core HR to provide the essential systems and processes needed to manage an organisation’s workforce. It centralises employee data, supports key HR functions such as payroll, attendance, recruitment, and performance, and ensures consistent, efficient HR operations. A modern Core HR capability improves data accuracy, reduces manual administration, and gives employees and managers easy access to the information and tools they need. • Core HR / Human Resources Information System (HRIS): Maintains centralized employee records, organizational charts, personal data, and job history. • Payroll Management: Automates salary calculations, tax deductions, benefits, and pay stub generation. • Recruitment and Onboarding: Manages the hiring process, including applicant tracking, resume screening, interviewing, and onboarding new employees. • Performance Management: Tracks employee goals, conducts performance appraisals, and provides feedback. • Training and Development (Learning Management): Tracks employee training sessions, certifications, and development activities. • Benefits Administration: Manages employee benefits selections, health insurance and retirement plans. • Employee Self-Service (ESS) & Manager Self-Service (MSS): Allows employees to update personal info, annual leave, sickness reporting, and access pay stubs, while managers approve requests. • Expense Management: Tracks and manages employee expenses. • Health and Safety: Manage workplace risks, ensure legal compliance, and protect employee wellbeing by tracking policies, training, and incident reporting. Duty Management A Duty Management System (DMS) provides the essential tools needed to plan, schedule, deploy, and record the working duties of police officers and staff. It ensures that operational resources are aligned to demand, supports compliance with working time regulations, and provides real time visibility of workforce availability and skills. A modern DMS improves operational efficiency, enhances decision making, and supports the effective deployment of officers across a range of policing activities. • Resource Planning & Scheduling: Create and manages rosters, shift patterns, and duty assignments, ensuring operational coverage across all policing functions. • Real Time Availability & Deployment: Provides up to date visibility of officer and staff availability, role qualifications, and deployable skills to support operational decision making. • Overtime & Additional Duties Management: Records and manages overtime, short notice duties, and special operations requirements with integrated approval workflows. • Demand & Event Resourcing: Supports planning and allocation of resources for pre planned events, major incidents, mutual aid, and surge requirements. • Working Time Compliance: Monitors adherence to Working Time Regulations, police-specific rostering rules, rest periods, and fatigue management standards. • Skills & Accreditation Tracking: Aligns deployment decisions to individual skills, accreditations, firearms authorisations, driving qualifications, and training currency. • Integration with Payroll & HR: Sends duty, overtime, and allowance data directly to payroll, while ensuring accurate alignment with Core HR records. • Time and Attendance Tracking: Manages clock-in/out, work hours, shifts, and integration with payroll. The Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) will support DC/LP with the development of a Business Case (BC). Lot LOT-0000: . None

The Tenderer's familiarisation with the System takes place via the application, the source code and the handed-over documentation. This obligation does not extend to software whose provision is the responsibility of the Contracting Authority. The Tenderer shall continuously monitor the EoL date of the built-in/used components, about which it shall regularly inform the Contracting Authority and update the modules before they become obsolete. sig_69c61e9b92b45fac37be.description: ACAN 26-58042 Microgrid Detailed Design Coordination and System Integration Services June 4, 2026. 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. This procurement has been set-aside under the federal government's Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Only Indigenous businesses as defined under PSIB are eligible to challenge the proposed procurement strategy to award the contract to the named Indigenous business. 2. Definition of the Requirement The National Research Council Canada (NRC), through its Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre (CEI), requires specialized services to support the detailed design coordination and system integration of an application-specific microgrid system to be tested at NRC’s microgrid research facility in Vancouver, British Columbia. The objective of this work is to support the development and evaluation of microgrid technologies intended for potential application in northern and remote Canadian communities that rely on diesel-based electricity generation. The project will integrate battery energy storage and microgrid control technologies in order to better understand their performance, operational requirements, and integration considerations for remote and isolated power systems. The requirement involves the detailed engineering coordination and system integration of two key microgrid subsystems: the Microgrid Control Panel (MGCP) and the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Fabrication and assembly of these subsystems will be conducted through a separate procurement process; however, the contractor will be responsible for coordinating the detailed engineering inputs, overseeing subsystem fabrication activities, and ensuring successful integration and commissioning of the overall system. The scope of work includes technical coordination of the detailed electrical system design, oversight of subsystem fabrication, participation in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), configuration and programming of the microgrid controller platform used in the system (ComAp), and integration, commissioning and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) of the completed system at NRC’s Vancouver facility. In addition to coordinating specialized engineering and controls programming activities, the contractor will provide technical project management and system integration oversight to ensure the resulting microgrid configuration reflects operational considerations associated with remote and northern electricity systems. This includes consideration of the operational characteristics of isolated or diesel-based electricity systems commonly found in northern communities, including reliability requirements, integration with existing diesel generation assets, and logistical constraints associated with remote infrastructure. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Any interested Indigenous supplier must demonstrate by way of a Statement of Capabilities that they meet all of the following minimum essential requirements: • Demonstrated experience of the supplier acting as the prime contractor responsible for coordinating multiple technical subcontractors delivering engineering design, controls programming, and system integration services for complex energy or infrastructure projects. • Demonstrated ownership interest in, and direct operational involvement of the supplier organization with, an electrical utility serving northern or remote communities in Canada. • Demonstrated knowledge within the supplier organization of electrical generation and distribution systems used in northern or remote communities, including systems integrating diesel generation with renewable energy and battery energy storage technologies. • Demonstrated experience of the supplier managing projects involving microgrid technologies, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and renewable energy integration in remote or off-grid environments. • Demonstrated ability of the supplier to immediately engage and coordinate specialized engineering and controller programming expertise required for this project, including experience with the ComAp microgrid controller platform used in remote power system applications. 4. Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement This procurement is set aside from the international trade agreements under the provision each has for measures with respect to Aboriginal peoples or for set-asides for small and minority businesses. 5. sig_6a0ea0101631906fdc67.description: The subject of the contract is the lot-by-lot supply, installation, integration and commissioning of software solutions for radiation therapy at St. Elisabethen-Klinikum Ravensburg, a site of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH. Lot 1 comprises an SGRT system (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy) including all necessary software components for patient positioning and monitoring as well as integration into the existing IT and LINAC infrastructure. Lot 2 comprises the treatment planning software (Treatment Planning System, TPS) for irradiation planning for photons and electrons, including installation, data migration from the legacy system, training of operating personnel and maintenance/support. Both lots will be awarded under a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Tenderers may apply for one or both lots. Contract execution will take place during ongoing clinical operations. The subject of this lot is the supply, installation, integration and commissioning of a system for surface-guided radiation therapy (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy, SGRT) including all necessary software and hardware components for patient positioning and monitoring. The service includes complete connection to the hospital's existing linear accelerator and IT infrastructure, training of operating personnel as well as maintenance and support over the envisaged period.; A treatment planning system (TPS) for the radiation therapy of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH is being procured. The system is intended to enable the planning of photon-guided irradiations with the existing linear accelerators while supporting all relevant clinical workflows (3D-CRT, IMRT, VMAT). Complete integration into the existing IT and PACS environment is expected, including interfaces to the R&V system, DICOM-RT and archiving system. The service includes supply, installation, commissioning, validation, training of specialist personnel and maintenance.

sig_6a1c3dbeafff2d320ec8.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. sig_6a250006b6c3efe55538.description: The Shared Services Centre (CDU) is designed and implemented as a scalable, highly secure and energy-efficient platform that tracks the demand and supply for hosted system capacities, thereby achieving significant savings while ensuring high service quality with a fast response to new requirements. In order for the CDU platform to comply with the standards prescribed by the Regulation on organisational and technical standards for connection to the state information infrastructure and the new Cyber Security Act, it is necessary to contract the expansion and upgrade of security systems on the CDU platform. This will significantly increase the security of hosted systems and protect users of CDU services. The subject of the procurement is divided into 4 groups: - Group 1 - Upgrade of application delivery controllers - Group 2 - Solution for network traffic security monitoring - NDR - Group 3 - Solution for collection, storage and processing of log records - LMS - Group 4 - Solution for protection of electronic mail against zero-day threats - Zero-day protection The subject of the procurement is the upgrade of existing application delivery controllers and the extension of their maintenance. The upgrades contain a licence upgrade of existing devices, which will further unlock the hardware resources built into the devices, which will result in an increase in the traffic processing capacity of the devices. As part of this procurement, the maintenance of existing devices will be extended for the next 5 years.; The subject of the procurement is the delivery of a solution for network traffic security monitoring (Network Detection And Response), hereinafter referred to as the NDR solution. As part of this subject, it is necessary to offer a complete solution that includes the delivery of software, hardware, installation and commissioning services, and an extended warranty for a duration of 3 year(s) from delivery.; The subject of the procurement is the delivery of a solution for the collection, storage and processing of log records (Log management system), hereinafter referred to as the LMS solution. As part of this subject, it is necessary to offer software licences with an extended warranty for a duration of 5 years from the delivery of the licences.; The subject of the procurement is the delivery of licences for a system for the protection of electronic mail against zero-day threats (hereinafter referred to as Zero-day protection), which provides comprehensive protection for organisations against threats via electronic mail, such as malicious software, phishing attacks, spam, zero-day threats and other forms of cyber attacks. As part of the procurement, it is necessary to deliver licences for a software solution that is installed on the CDU virtualisation platform. It is necessary to offer an extended warranty for a duration of 3 year(s) for all offered components.
sig_6a250006b6c3efe55538.title: Procurement of a system for raising the level of cyber security within the CDU

The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. In the case of state-owned land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. sig_6a5b37bcf2a1ff15a11a.description: The Helsinki City Environment Division is involved in the implementation of a city-wide document management solution (M-Files) as part of the development of the City of Helsinki's information management. The Central City Office is responsible for the technical setup of the M-Files system, but the divisions are responsible for ensuring the successful deployment of the system into their own services. The City Office is also responsible for the general definitions of the system and the functionality at the core system level. The City Environment Division is responsible for how the division's services integrate M-Files into their daily operations, and needs expert assistance particularly for implementation planning and the definition of operating models to be implemented. This includes, for example, the migration of documents from current operating environments (such as network drives and project banks), planning the utilisation of metadata functionalities, modelling access rights and planning the phased progress of the implementation. The expert support (consultant) to be procured brings deep expertise in the practices of the M-Files system or similar to the project, and their task is to guide the organisation in finding the best solutions and operating models for the rollout of document management. The aim of the consultant's work is not project management - the City Environment Division already has its own project manager and organisation responsible for the implementation - but rather bringing support and expertise to back up solution-technical decisions. The description of the subject of the procurement is appendix 1 of the call for tenders.
sig_6a5b37bcf2a1ff15a11a.title: Expert support for the implementation of the M-Files document management system

sig_6aa69851b15b7735ff92.description: Extension of the patient information eConsent Pro with modules for digitization Lot LOT-0001: Digital patient information. Description of the initial situation: Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein uses the eConsent Pro solution from the provider Thieme to inform patients in a legally compliant manner about treatments, procedures and anaesthesia. The standardized information sheets provided are established in daily clinical routine. Description of the target image: The contracting authority pursues the goal of digitalizing the patient information process. The established sheets are to be reused in terms of content. In addition, patients should be enabled to access information sheets via the contracting authority's patient portal that were previously assigned to them by clinic staff. In this way, patients can deal with the treatments in advance of their hospital stay, fill out the sheets in advance and note questions. After the sheets have been discussed together in the respective information discussion, the sheets are to be signed digitally on tablets in a legally secure manner and then transferred to the hospital information system (KIS). Justification for the product-specific call for tenders: So that processes in hospitals continue to function well, the content of the information sheets should not be changed. The information process is merely to be digitalized and the sheets subsequently transmitted in digital form to the KIS. Market analysis has shown that apart from the provider Thieme, there is no other provider on the market that has information sheets available in all clinical specialist areas required at the Gemeinschaftsklinikum. The solution described in the target image, according to which the information sheets are to be sent to patients via the patient portal, is exclusively possible with the information system solutions of the company Thime on the part of the patient portal provider Dedalus.
sig_6aa69851b15b7735ff92.title: Digital patient education

sig_6ab128d59cbaa20dd61f.description: The client's SOC has the primary mission of monitoring the organisation's IT landscape around the clock and initiating appropriate measures in the event of security incidents. The previous contractual partner provided endpoint detection and response (EDR), analysis and incident response, vulnerability management, and security information and event management (SIEM) as focal topics; accordingly, this call for tenders essentially covers the replacement of these components and services. While some tasks will now be handled by the client's SOC, internal staff resources are a limiting factor. Therefore, some tasks, including the continuous monitoring of the environment, will still need to be provided jointly with the support of an external partner. The future environment is to be based on the current internal log data platform Splunk, which will be expanded into a SIEM. This platform is to be supplemented by a managed detection and response (MDR) solution that operates using its own data lake and forwards alerts to the internal SIEM. Continuous monitoring is to take place on the basis of the MDR service, while the client's employees will in future deal primarily with the internal SIEM and thus also be able to cover internal and organisation-specific use cases. The systems will be supplemented by various services to operate the SIEM platform, but also with cyber analysis services and support in the event of an incident. The future platform must also support operations in vulnerability management with suitable tools. The procurement is divided into four lots. The existing platform is to continue to be used and expanded; for this purpose, the Cantonal Police of Bern requires licences for Splunk Enterprise, Splunk Enterprise Security, and Cribl.
sig_6ab128d59cbaa20dd61f.title: Support for the operation and further development of the Security Operations Centre (SOC)

sig_6ac1409c16d6f618b18e.description: Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) and its subordinate and associated commands seek to accelerate the development, procurement and integration of unmanned systems (UxS) capabilities in support of the Joint Force, Special Operations Forces (SOF), and allied SOF. NSWC seeks to award Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) contracts or Other Transaction Authority agreements (OT) (see 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021-23) to provide a new method of delivering UxS systems capability called “UxS as a service” and First Person View (FPV) platforms. Resultant contracts or agreements should provide systems with a broad range of capabilities that directly support mission effectiveness in terms of platforms, payloads, Processing-Exploitation-Dissemination (PED), programming (i.e., firmware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI)), communications/data transfer, Command and Control (C2) systems, components, and/or material to be acquired, developed, or already in use by NSWC, United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), the Department of War (DoW), or the U.S. Government, as well as interagency and FVEY partners. As such, under the authority of DFARS 212.70, NSWC releases this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). NSWC anticipates the award of a Firm-Fixed Price type contract in accordance with FAR Part 12. Offerors are encouraged to review FAR 52.212-4 and 52.212-5 for standard terms and conditions of a FAR Part 12 contract. In addition, NSWC may award an OT in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4022-23. Non?FAR Contracts and Agreements are anticipated with nontraditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of the SOF Operator and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or material to be acquired or developed by the NSWC, or the improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by NSWC. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102 and the procedures set forth in this announcement satisfy the competition requirements within 10 U.S.C 4022(b)(2) and 4022(f)(2)(A). Contracting Officers shall treat items, technologies, and services acquired using a CSO as commercial items. Agreement Officers may make awards in accordance with 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021-23. Awards made in accordance with 10 U.S.C. §§ 4023 are not subject to competition requirements. The full Commercial Solutions Opening Notice H9224026SC001 and information is attached to this posting. All submissions shall be in accordance with the instructions within.

sig_6ad88d8bfea0634b7117.description: Die Zentrum für Digitale Souveränität der Öffentlichen Verwaltung (ZenDiS) GmbH is implementing an open admission system in the form of an open-house procedure for the admission of distributors for the openDesk ecosystem. Admitted distributors act as a link between the openDesk portfolio compiled by ZenDiS and the end-customer sales network. Based on the package configurations specified by ZenDiS, they assemble software components into bundles and time-limited subscriptions, build a network of IT partners and distribute the offerings via this partner network. The procedure is not a procurement procedure within the meaning of the GWB, the VgV or the VOB/A. There is no comparative selection, evaluation or ranking of applicants. Every applicant who fulfils all published admission requirements is admitted under uniform and non-negotiable conditions. The number of admissions is not limited. The subject of the notice is the admission of companies as distributors for the openDesk ecosystem within the framework of an open admission system. openDesk is an open-source office and collaboration suite. In a web-based environment, the suite bundles in particular functions for document editing, file and knowledge management, e-mail, calendars, contacts, chat, video conferencing, project and task management, as well as identity and access management. The openDesk portfolio is made up of software components from various component manufacturers and the openDesk integration layer. ZenDiS is responsible for the composition, further development and packaging of the portfolio and specifies quality, security and interoperability standards. The admitted distributors form the sales tier between ZenDiS or the components of the openDesk portfolio and the downstream network of IT partners. Based on the package configurations specified by ZenDiS, they assemble combinations of individual software components into bundles, create time-limited subscription offers from them and distribute these via the IT partners integrated into their partner network. According to the intended distribution model, the distributor does not act directly in relation to end customers. End-customer sales and, in particular, setup, integration, operation and support are carried out by the integrated IT partners. With the positive admission decision, the distributor agreement is concluded between ZenDiS and the applicant under the previously published, uniform and non-negotiable conditions. The distributor agreement regulates in particular admission to the openDesk ecosystem, usage and sublicensing rights to the software components and the openDesk integration layer, access to the openDesk repositories and licence keys, use of the designation "Official openDesk Distributor", and the obligations of the distributor in the design and distribution of the bundles and subscriptions. The subject of the admission is the respective applicant as a distribution partner. There is no technical testing or integration of an applicant's software product. The admission of component manufacturers to the openDesk portfolio is not the subject of this procedure. The procedure is designed as an open-house admission procedure. There is no comparative selection decision between applicants. There is no evaluation, ranking or prioritisation of suitable applicants. Every applicant who fulfils all previously published admission requirements is admitted under the same conditions. Greater capability, experience or economic resources do not establish priority. The number of admissions is not limited. ZenDiS does not grant exclusivity, territorial protection or protection against competition. The procedure is not a procurement procedure within the meaning of the Act against Restraints of Competition (Gesetz gegen Wettbewerbsbeschränkungen), the Public Procurement Ordinance (Vergabeverordnung), the Construction Contract Procedures (Vergabe- und Vertragsordnung für Bauleistungen) or other public procurement regulations. The notice serves the transparent, equal and non-discriminatory opening of the admission system. It does not award a public contract or a concession. Applications for admission are examined separately for each applicant. The examination is carried out first formally and then in terms of content exclusively on the basis of "admission requirements fulfilled" or "admission requirements not fulfilled". The admission procedure is open continuously until 31. January 2027. Applications for admission can be submitted at any time within this period in accordance with the procedural documents.
sig_6ad88d8bfea0634b7117.title: Open-house admission procedure for the admission of distributors for the openDesk ecosystem

sig_6adb225378bf9df94899.description: UKSA intends to run a competitive procurement to secure a supplier/consortium to lead on the delivery and operation of the Earth Observation Data Hub (EODH) from April 2027 – March 2030. EODH provides a national gateway and platform for Earth Observation (EO) and model datasets. It enables users to access UK and global commercial and research satellite data, processing workflows, and applications for analysing surface temperature and land-use change. Through a single point of access (https://eodatahub.org.uk), the EO Data Hub integrates commercial and open EO datasets, allowing users to search, visualise, analyse, and process data at scale. The EODH is an operational national capability, currently delivered through UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and the National Centre for Earth Observation (NCEO). The current delivery model will continue until March 2027 and will include a technical handover phase with the new delivery supplier throughout January – March 2027. Whilst final decisions on the exact scope are yet to be made our current primary aim of the competition will be to outsource operational delivery of the EODH to both EO and non-EO users subject to relevent internal approvals. The competition would invite suppliers to demonstrate capability, user reach and a vision to grow the activity. An important aspect will be to maximise the re-use of existing intellectual property and minimise any disruption to current users. The expectations will include further development of the established EODH service – broadening the user base, expanding data availability, and improving overall service functionality. The chosen supplier will also be responsible for managing a seamless transition period and uninterrupted service continuity. UPDATE 01/10/2026 NEXT STEPS FOR EARTH OBSERVATION DATA HUB PROCUREMENT Thank you to everyone who participated in our EODH market engagement and responded to the RFI. Your feedback has helped shape the next stage of this important national capability. We are pleased to confirm that a competitive procurement for the next phase of EODH will take place. The competition will operate through UKRI-STFC Procurement and will be run by CEDA (NCEO) at RAL Space, working closely with UKSA, rather than directly by UKSA through RM6235 as previously envisaged. In accordance with UK Government policy, elements of EODH delivery have been identified as well suited to an insourced approach within Government. Details on these elements will be elaborated in future communications, but the majority of EODH activities are still expected to be delivered by competitively procured suppliers. This approach provides a strong foundation for EODH’s future. It supports continuity for users, builds on the operational and technical knowledge of the existing service, provides greater flexibility to develop a sustainable operating model, and retains a substantial role for industry in operating, supporting and developing the Hub through to 2030. UKSA and CEDA (NCEO) will provide a further coordinated update shortly, setting out the procurement process, timetable and how interested organisations can participate. For planning purposes and without commitment, we anticipate an ITT being issued in autumn 2026. Lot 1: . None

Description The United States Space Force (USSF), through the Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)to solicit innovative commercial solutions that enhance Space Domain Awareness (SDA)capabilities. This CSO is authorized under DFARS 212.70and is designed to identify and acquire innovative technologies, products, and services that support the USSF's warfighting missions. The CSO provides a flexible, enterprise-wide acquisition mechanism to address SDA mission challenges through advanced software engineering, data analytics, and other innovative approaches. Submissions will be evaluated under a multi-phase process to ensure alignment with mission needs and operational priorities. Scope of the CSO The CSO seeks solutions that address the following Space Domain Awareness (SDA)mission challenges: Detecting, characterizing, and predicting activities in the space domain. Enhancing the accuracy and timeliness of SDA data. Supporting emerging SDA missions through innovative technologies. Specific Areas of Interest (AOIs) will be issued under this CSO to define technical focus areas, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria. Each AOI will be posted as a standalone solicitation module under this CSO. Submission Process The CSO employs a three-phase submission process: Phase I – White Paper and PowerPoint Briefing Offerors must submit a PowerPoint briefing (including a Quad Chart) and a White Paper summarizing their proposed solution. Submissions must align with the specific AOI requirements. Phase II – Pitch Session (Optional) Selected Offerors may be invited to present their proposed solution in greater depth during a virtual or in-person pitch session. Phase III – Full Proposal Offerors invited to Phase III must submit a complete proposal package, including a Technical Proposal, Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Price Proposal. The Government reserves the right to proceed directly from Phase I to Phase III. Key Information Security Requirements: Phase I submissions must be unclassified. Subsequent phases may require higher classification levels, as specified in the AOI and any draft or final DD Form 254. Foreign Participation: Restricted to U.S. entities due to export control and national security considerations. Cybersecurity Compliance: Offerors must comply with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC 2.0 requirements. How to Respond Interested Offerors must monitor SAM.gov for AOI-specific postings under this CSO. Each AOI will include detailed submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and deadlines. Submissions must comply with the formats and requirements outlined in the CSO and the applicable AOI. For general inquiries, contact the SAIO CSO Contracting Officer at SAIO.SDA.CSO@spaceforce.mil. Use the subject line: "SDA CSO – General Question(s)". Disclaimer This CSO does not obligate the Government to award a contract, nor does it commit the Government to pay for any costs incurred in the preparation and submission of responses. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the proposals received under this CSO.

sig_6b13c25c6ea9b6a5aa5c.description: The Waste Digital Twins will be an end-to-end digital representation of the Sewage Treatment Works, which will allow visualisation, simulation and optimisation of the treatment processes on the site. Initially the optimisation recommendations will be manually implemented, with a view to moving towards full automation at a later date. We are seeking partner(s) with demonstrable expertise in mechanistic and deterministic modelling, digital twin architectures, cloud‐based simulation systems, and operational optimisation. The successful partner(s) will help define and deliver the modelling Blueprint, establish a best‐practice modelling methodology, and work alongside our System Integrator(s) to develop a scalable, flexible and future‐proof Waste Digital Twin platform. Delivery will follow a phased and iterative approach: Phase 1 - Feasibility: Evaluate and recommend modelling pathways, either via mechanistic software or coded mechanistic model conversion. Phase 2- Deployment: Iteratively deploy, validate and refine Digital Twins across sites, embedding learnings and enhancements. Partners will be expected to provide specialist capability, flexible resourcing, and operational support while upskilling Severn Trent's internal teams in DataOps, MLOps and Digital Twin operations. This includes integrating modelling outputs within a wider systems architecture, supporting interim standalone solutions ahead of future integration with the Asset Data Programme, and ensuring all work aligns with Severn Trent's cyber and data governance guardrails. Lot 1: .
sig_6b13c25c6ea9b6a5aa5c.title: Waste Digital Twin - Modelling Delivery

sig_6b14c4780b58600513c2.description: Operation and development of the Digital Court system package 2026. The system package serving the 11.000 court users consists of five subsystems that operate in close cooperation, in an integrated manner, and support the fundamental judicial processes of the court organisation, as well as ensuring the performance of its statutory judicial tasks. Their correct and reliable operation is of paramount importance, and their continuous availability is a fundamental prerequisite for the lawful operation of the courts. These are integrated legal software applications whose importance, sensitivity and priority nature make it necessary for them to be able to operate with a properly stable operational background, thereby ensuring their continuous and correct operation. For the performance of operational and development tasks, comprehensive, practical knowledge of the legal background governing the operation of the judiciary is indispensable, within this particularly the old and the new Pp., the old and the new Be., the Kp., the Büsz., the Beisz., and furthermore the Electronic Administration Act and its implementing decree. The subject of the procurement is the provision of expertise for the operation of the system package and, to the extent of 2.000 developer framework hours, for its further development. The expected level of system availability (per month): 99,5% (7/24 availability). The expected level of test system availability during working hours, per month, is 99% (on working days, between 8.00 and 17.00 hours). On-site availability: on working days until 8:00-17:00 hours by 2 operators, outside the on-site availability time slot, continuous telephone standby duty (including rest days and public holidays) by 1 operators. Development takes place in C#, SQL, HTML, JavaScript, XAML, CSS programming languages and the Microsoft .NET Framework 4.7.2, ASP.NET MVC 5, Entity Framework 6 application platform. Database management system: MSSQL 2022 Quantity: 5 system packages, 2.000 developer framework hours -30% (quantity variance), 11 000 users. The Contracting Authority undertakes to use 1400 framework hours, and will draw down additional (but a maximum of 2000) framework hours if development is required due to legislative changes or user requirements.

sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.description: The National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) is CDC's state-based surveillance system for violent deaths and suicides. NVDRS combines information from death certificates, coroner or medical examiner reports, including toxicology reports, and law enforcement reports to provide comprehensive, incident-level data on the circumstances surrounding violent deaths. Through this Notice of Funding Opportunity, CDC will support eligible state, territorial, and local government entities, or their bona fide agents, in operating and modernizing NVDRS. Recipients will conduct statewide or territory-wide surveillance by collecting, linking, managing, analyzing, and submitting high-quality data on violent deaths and suicides. A central focus of this NOFO is timely and complete data reporting through two coordinated reporting processes: quarterly provisional data pulls and annual data closeout. Beginning in Year 1, recipients will prepare data for CDC's quarterly provisional data pulls to support earlier access to preliminary, actionable information. Recipients will progressively update case records as additional source documents and information become available. Annual data closeout is the primary process for producing the complete, finalized, and validated NVDRS dataset for each data year. Recipients must ensure that all eligible cases are fully abstracted, updated, validated, and completed using all required and available data sources by the annual closeout deadline. The finalized annual dataset supports national reporting, analysis, dissemination, and public health action. This NOFO also emphasizes modernization of data systems and workflows to increase efficiency, reduce reporting burden, improve data quality and timeliness, and enhance data usability. All recipients will complete a modernization readiness assessment within six months of award and implement at least one modernization pilot during the period of performance. Pilot activities may include automated data import and extraction, electronic data exchange and interoperability, workflow automation, data-quality tools, and enhanced data analysis and visualization. With CDC approval, recipients may also participate in optional activities that link NVDRS data with other relevant data systems to improve surveillance and expand public health insights. The intended outcome is a sustainable, modernized national surveillance system that produces timely provisional data and complete, reliable, high-quality annual data to inform violence and suicide prevention and support public health action.

sig_6b6d7819e39ab56deb8d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $499M. Individual awards will not normally exceed sixty (60) months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $500K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions and assistance instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. sig_6b717637e2d7dc2a6ac8.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the planned procurement of translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services for the needs of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto produces a wide range of official communications, expert content and stakeholder-targeted materials in multiple languages as part of its statutory duties. Translation and language editing services are a key part of the accessibility, quality, comprehensibility and consistency of official communications. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The subject of the procurement is a comprehensive service package for translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services, through which subscribers can procure translation services for various language pairs, language editing for texts written in the target language, and subtitling and transcription services for video and audio materials. Service needs are focused in particular on the Swedish and English languages. The materials to be handled are principally factual texts, presentations, documents (e.g. call for tenders, contracts), speeches, brochures, articles and web content. Subtitling and transcription services relate, inter alia, to videos, online events and audio recordings, taking accessibility requirements into account. The aim of the procurement is to ensure a high-quality, cost-effective and reliable service package that supports subscribers' communications, information accessibility and the fulfilment of official obligations. The objective is a procurement model that enables smooth ordering, consistent end results and an administratively light operating method even in situations where the volume of assignments is large and the value of individual assignments is small. By means of the market dialogue, the contracting entity seeks to obtain information on service models existing in the market, pricing structures, quality assurance practices, and the utilisation of artificial intelligence and other automation as part of the production of translation and language editing services. The dialogue will also examine various contractual and supplier models, including the suitability of single-supplier and multi-supplier models. The procurement includes a cooperation model in which the subscriber and the supplier systematically develop the service throughout the contract period. The aim of the cooperation is the continuous improvement of the service, taking into account the subscriber's guidelines and terminology, and developing the service to meet changing needs and operating environments. The subject matter, scope and technical solutions of the procurement may be refined and/or changed as the procurement preparation and market dialogue progress. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE The subscriber's target timetable for carrying out the market dialogue and procurement is: - Market dialogue (technical dialogue), February-March 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders and calculation period, March-April 2026 - Comparison of tenders and procurement decision, April-May 2026 - Contract entry into force and commencement of cooperation, May 2026 onwards ----- ADDITIONAL NOTICE DETAILS This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a possible tendering procedure. The technical dialogue will be organised through commenting on draft versions of the call for tenders material and answering the subscriber's questions relating to the subject of the procurement. Instructions for registration: The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market dialogue by 25.2.2026 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Käännöspalvelut - markkinavuoropuhelu" [Translation services - market dialogue]. The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - the email address of the supplier's contact person The subscriber reserves the right to also invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the procurement notice, as well as the draft dialogue materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information regarding the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_6ba8569a3c2224f70368.description: The Messe Berlin GmbH, hereinafter also referred to synonymously as Messe Berlin and Contracting Authority (CA), is putting out to tender the following service: Framework agreement on quality audits and support services in the field of corporate security. The subject of this procurement is the execution of quality, process and compliance audits in connection with the deployment of security and order services, the development and documentation of security-relevant processes, as well as the preparation and implementation of security concepts for the physical security of Messe Berlin. The objective is to ensure the effectiveness, regulatory compliance and continuous further development of the security organisation. The services include the review of existing security measures and processes, the creation of governance documents, as well as the development of risk-based security concepts to guarantee an appropriate level of protection for people, property and operational workflows. These specifically include: 1. Execution of quality, process and compliance audits. Audit contents: Compliance with the security concept: Verification of the conformity of the security service provider's actual deployment with the specified security and zone concept. Staff qualification: Ensuring that the security service provider exclusively deploys registered security and order service personnel approved by Messe with the required qualification. Efficiency and effectiveness: Evaluation of the efficiency and effectiveness of the security service provider. Compliance requirements: Verification of compliance with defined processes, guidelines and contractual requirements in connection with the provision of services. 2. Development of processes and creation of governance documents. Service contents: Analysis, development and optimisation of security-relevant processes using standard BPMN notation 2.0. Documentation of target processes including roles, responsibilities, interfaces and approval workflows. Creation and updating of governance documents, guidelines and procedural instructions in the field of physical security. Development of rules for controlling access and entry authorisations and other security-relevant authorisation processes. Ensuring comprehensible, audit-proof and organisation-wide uniform process documentation. 3. Creation and implementation of security concepts. Service contents: Execution of structured and reproducible risk assessments for the identification, analysis and evaluation of hazards to people, property and operational workflows. Creation, updating and continuous revision of site-, property- or event-related security concepts. Derivation of suitable organisational, personnel and technical protective measures based on the identified risks. Evaluation of existing security measures regarding their effectiveness and identification of potential for improvement. Support with the implementation of recommended measures, as well as documentation of the results and recommendations for action. In view of the envisaged requirement increases and requirement reductions, as well as prospectively possible functional expansions, the services must be adapted or aligned to current and possible new circumstances. During the contract term, further requirements may be added or cease to apply.
sig_6ba8569a3c2224f70368.title: Framework agreement on quality audits and support services in the field of corporate security
