sig_6bc39de497de24252f81.description: At the Basel Waste Incineration Plant (KVA), ABB process controllers AC450 are in use. These are no longer supported or maintained by ABB, have therefore reached the end of their service life and must be replaced. The controller replacement is awarded in 2 independent lots: - Lot 1: Necessary hardware for controllers and IO stations including interfaces. - Lot 2: Software migration of existing controllers AC450 to AC800M. The translation of the old software must take place without modification of the process engineering functions. 5 AC450 controllers with node names 22, 32, 41, 42 and 51 are being replaced. New ABB controllers of type AC800M PM866AK02 are to be used. The currently operational, non-redundant AF100 buses to the S800 peripheral clusters must be replaced by redundant Profibus DP connections, including the S800 Profibus DP head modules. Furthermore, existing connections to third-party peripherals (boiler safety, auxiliary burner control, crane system, turbine and various touch panels) are to be implemented on the AC800M. This concerns the serial interfaces with 3964(R) and RK512 stack as well as Modbus RTU. These connection types are initially to be retained with the AC800M and replaced on a case-by-case basis by Profinet at a later point in time. The Profibus DP gateways required for this are to be procured and implemented.; The existing AC450 AMPL code (Advant MasterPiece Language) is based on a slightly modified ABB APC library. For the migration, the already installed ABB APC AC800M library must be used. This is made available exclusively for this project. The AMPL code may be translated mechanically into function blocks. In doing so, the function of the old code must not be altered. The AMPL code must not be passed on to third-party companies for translation. The newly translated AC800M code must continue to use the currently existing database names, so that only the AC800M-typical signal identifiers may be appended as a suffix. Variable names in the code are to be adopted. The existing MB300 interface must remain in place and serves, as before, for cross-communication with the other controllers. In doing so, the transmission scheme 1:1 is to be adopted in such a way that no adaptation is required on the other controllers. The last migration of node 21 has shown that it works. A dedicated 800xA AC800M engineering station is available for preparation and on-site commissioning. Commissioning must mandatorily take place on site. In particular, the migration also includes the following topics: - Process graphic adaptation - Sequences - Trends - Interfaces to third-party devices For detailed information, see Appendix C1 Specification of Services.
sig_6bc39de497de24252f81.title: IWB, Migration AC450 nach AC800M Node 22, 32, 41, 42 und 51

sig_6bd53e50dea5ca9e64bb.description: West Yorkshire Police (WYP) currently utilises a Case Management and Investigation Tracking System which is due to expire on 31st March 2026. In preparation for its replacement, WYP is seeking to explore the market to identify alternative solutions that meet its operational requirements and to assess compliant procurement routes. The Authority is specifically interested in Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solutions that are readily available and can be easily configured to align with WYP's needs. Any proposed solution must comply with relevant legislation, including the Police (Complaints and Misconduct) Regulations 2020 and the Police Conduct Regulations, and must be adaptable to accommodate future legislative updates. As a minimum, the solution must offer the core functionality outlined below. 1. Overview Purpose: Case management and investigation tracking system with full auditability and workflow integration. New System Type: Transitioning from legacy desktop to a web-based platform (trial started April 2025 by WYP with the intention to use this model to roll out to other forces). There is a new Version 7.6 which is a legislative changed coming within the next 6 months. 2. User Access & Authentication - Client-based access control with configurable access levels. - User IDs: Employee number assigned; password set on enrolment and changed on first login. Administrator capabilities: - Configure search options and table contents. (configurable). - Manage users and groups. (configurable). - Grant/revoke access to specific reports. (configurable). - Login method: Web link with username/password. 3. Case Management Features - Investigations Tab: Displays assigned cases for workload management. - Search Capabilities: Case reference, type, status, IOPC reference. - Configurable sub-types linked to case type. (configurable). - All information fields searchable. (configurable). - Case Details: 7+ searchable fields including district level. (configurable). - Summary, progress, details, notes tabs. - Allegation types and sub-types (configurable). - Risk assessments driven by legislation. (should be driven by current and emerging legislation and be kept up to date by the supplier) - Sub Judice case holding. - Protected characteristics recording. sig_6bdf90904780068f720d.description: The delivery of an integration platform that connects applications and data. The platform links internal systems (such as case management systems, ERP), external registers (BRP, KvK) and the provincial data platform (Databricks). This also includes the transition and implementation from the current integration platform to the new one. As a frame of reference, the province uses an API-led architecture approach (system APIs, process APIs and experience APIs). Integrations are made accessible in layers: from source systems via business logic to consuming applications. The province subsequently develops and defines integrations independently. The platform must therefore be accessible to developers, architects and functional administrators. The contract is not divided into lots, because the integration platform and the associated services and additional assignments form a strongly cohesive entity. Development, management and further development are closely intertwined and have mutual dependencies. Splitting would lead to additional coordination, increased complexity and fragmentation of responsibilities, with risks to the continuity and performance of the platform. To guarantee unambiguous management and integral responsibility, it is not considered proportionate to divide the contract into lots.

sig_6c1033a2b9f9a13401ec.description: The Ministry of foreign Affairs, Green Diplomacy and Climate (KLIMA) has entered into a contract regarding a Management Support Consultant (Consultant) to ensure implementation and completion of all the ongoing Danida Green Business Partnerships (DGBP) activities based on sound project and financial management support. The objective of the Consultant is to assume the functions of project implementation support, financial management support and programme level monitoring and reporting. The Client will maintain oversight over the Services performed by the Consultant and the strategic leadership of DGBP. The Consultant shall perform at least the following activities and services: • Manage and implement all the DGBP activities effectively in accordance with the agreed partnership project agreements and contracts. • Provide relevant business and project management support and guidance to actors supported under the instruments. • Provide for achievement of results as defined in the Results Framework in the project document of the instrument. This includes monitoring the DGBP activities effectively. • Provide overall financial management including verification and approval of project workplans, budgets, and reports as well as disbursement requests from the partners. This should be done in accordance with the DGBP financial guidelines and sound financial management principles. • Maintaining full compliance with MFA’s Aid Management Guidelines (AMG) and Financial Management Guidelines (FMG), and ensuring high standards of financial management, procurement, anti-corruption, and risk mitigation. • On request provide relevant information on concrete projects and communication material in Danish and highlight positive lessons learned. Ensure sharing of relevant knowledge and information that generate interest and effective participation in the instruments. The DGBP is a programme that funds and supports market-based partnership projects between commercial and non-commercial partners in developing countries addressing climate and environmental challenges while contributing to inclusive growth and improved livelihoods. Each partnership project consists of at least one commercial partner and one non-commercial partner. A DGBP project has its own results framework and contributes to the overall objectives of the programme by linking to specific indicators in the overall results framework. The objective of DGBP is to enhance global green transition and private-led inclusive economic growth through innovative partnerships. DGBP aims at contributing to two outcomes: 1) Reduced vulnerability to climate change, reduced strain on natural resources and the environment and stabilization of GHG emissions, and 2) inclusive private sector growth and improved livelihoods. The climate and environmental outcomes are estimated in terms of avoided negative effects on the climate and environment compared to status quo solutions. Income and livelihood effects are assessed from the number of people engaged in the activities and the level of targeting products and services towards underserved populations. There are two funding windows in the programme: Full projects of up to DKK 15 million (minimum DKK 4 million) and maturation projects of up to DKK 1.5 million (minimum DKK 0.8 million). Maturation projects can last up to 18 months, while a full project can last up to five years. DGBP was launched in 2022 as a four-year programme (2022-2025) and was open for applications from 2022-2025, meaning that the last commitments were given in 2025 and that the programme is now closed to new applications. However, many of the funded projects will continue implementation during the coming years and the last one is expected to be closed only during 2030. The fund has been administered by an external Management Support Consultant (MSC), which has been responsible for organising annual calls for applications and undertake activities to spur interest in Denmark and in the partner countries in close coordination with the Danish embassies and other relevant stakeholders. The administrative responsibility in each partnership project rests with the non-commercial partner(s), who will also be responsible for annual progress reporting, financial reporting and audits. A programme-level progress report is prepared annually by the MSC. The MSC is providing advice and instructions to the administrative partners in relation to budgeting, reporting and audits, but the funds are disbursed directly to the administrative partners from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (“MFA” or the “Client”) in agreed instalments. Virtual annual monitoring meetings with all partners are organised by the MSC on the basis of the annual reporting. The annual meetings, which take place during March/April, are an opportunity to revise plans and targets in view of the progress achieved and the development in the context. sig_6c26611fe5b4f29c1d99.description: Delivery of components, licences and maintenance services for the upgrade and renewal of the existing core network infrastructure Lot LOT-0000: Delivery of components, licences and maintenance services for the upgrade and renewal of the existing core network infrastructure . The existing core network and fabric infrastructure is based on components and technologies from the manufacturer Extreme Networks. The existing network components are integrated into a uniform management, monitoring and security architecture. The core network infrastructure is an essential basis for the hospital's core medical and administrative processes. Due to its remit as a maximum-care provider, the highest possible level of availability in line with the state of the art is required. Avoidable additional sources of error and operational risks must therefore be limited as early as the procurement stage. Due to increased requirements regarding performance, port capacity, transmission speed, availability, fail-safety and IT security, as well as age-related replacement needs, a comprehensive renewal and upgrade of the core network infrastructure is necessary. The aim of the procurement is the delivery of the items required for the renewal and upgrade of the existing core network infrastructure: • hardware components, • interface and expansion modules, • transceivers and connection components, • software, management and functional licences, • maintenance and support entitlements, as well as • other accessories listed in the specification of requirements. The products, item numbers and quantities to be delivered are definitively set out in the specification of requirements. The subject matter of the tender is exclusively the delivery of the components, licences and maintenance services listed in the specification of requirements. The contractor is required to provide: 1. the complete and timely delivery of the advertised hardware components and accessories, 2. the provision and transfer of the advertised software and functional licences, 3. the registration and activation of the advertised maintenance and support services, 4. the assignment of all licences and maintenance entitlements to the client, as well as 5. the handover of the associated licence, support and registration proofs. All delivered hardware components must: - be brand new and unused, - be original products from the manufacturer specified in the specification of requirements, - originate from an authorised distribution channel, - be intended for the German or European market, - have a clearly traceable serial number, - be registerable with the manufacturer, and - be approved for the respective advertised maintenance and support service. The contractor must ensure that: - the delivered licences correspond to the specified products and item numbers, - the licences can be used without restriction for the intended application, - there are no temporal or functional restrictions that are not expressly stated in the specification of requirements, - the licence periods correspond to the advertised periods, and - all licence proofs, activation keys and registration information are handed over to the client. The maintenance and support services listed in the specification of requirements must be provided as regular manufacturer services. Page 5 of 7 Specification of requirements - Core network The maintenance or support period begins at the time specified in the specification of requirements or in the order. The contractor must ensure the proper registration of the maintenance and support services with the manufacturer and provide the client with suitable proofs thereof. The proofs must contain at least: - affected items or serial numbers, - type and scope of the support service, - start and end of the service period, - agreed service or response times, and - manufacturer or contract reference numbers. No unintended support gaps may occur between the delivery of the hardware and the start of the maintenance period.

sig_6c48e904f3c8b7763564.description: Public Health Wales (PHW) have an ongoing requirement for an Infection Prevention and Control Case Management and Surveillance system supplying cross-hospital electronic infection case management, immediate alerting of information relevant to infection control to ward staff and others including health protection specialists, and in depth and real-time reporting for clinical and public health action. The current system interfaces with existing hospital information systems including surgery databases, patient administration and laboratories. It builds upon the information supplied to find, link, and at once inform the IPC and wider teams to critical infection control scenarios. Immediate alerting of these scenarios ensures prompt management of the infection event, resulting in better outcomes for the patient, reduced risk of onward transmission in the hospital or community setting and early identification of critical situations such as an outbreak. The system also helps maximise clinical time by reducing the workload required to link all this information through an enabling prospective and real time information on events, as opposed to retrospective manual case review. The connection into Public Health Wales NHS Wales Trust (PHW) Enterprise Monitor function ensures that PHW, Welsh Government and local Health Boards, all benefit from sharing correct and transparent data with a national picture available of the infection position across the acute sector within Wales. The current contract for NHS Wales is with Baxter Healthcare and has been in place since August 2023. This agreement is led contractually by PHW on behalf of itself and all NHS Wales organisations. This agreement is due to expire in August 2027. Lot 1: .

Implementation of what is described in the rating policy point 2. Must be preceded by a KO criterion check for ST transactions 3. Modification of evaluation date entry 4. Copy option for objective and subjective data, rating 5. Overview plus button, as in MAR3 6. Off-balance sheet items should also be recordable 7. For exchange rates, there should be a filtering option under Master Data (date interval, currency code) 8. Establishment of import possibility from Excel SUB module: - Developments related to the integration of ISA (new insurer core system) SOV module - Creation of SOV module + developments related to ISA integration In addition to the development tasks of the MAR framework defined above, it may also be justified for the Tenderer to use system organisation, design and other undefined software development services, for which a separate resource must be provided. Undefined software development services: - Changes arise in the requirements placed on the system due to expected changes in accounting processes or business policy rule changes in the next 2-year period. - During daily operational work, several user-experience-enhancing functions and changes may arise in the Risk Management area. - Changes may also occur in MNB regulations affecting EXIM operations, which may entail functional changes to the application. sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.description: Die BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. Lot LOT-0000: Service Portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026. The BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. The future system is intended to serve as a central platform for managing customers, contracts, access media, billing and communication with customers. The planned scope of services comprises in particular the provision, setup, customisation and operation of an integrated service portal with the following components: End Customer Portal (EKP): A digital portal through which customers can independently use services provided by BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular registration, management of customer data, conclusion and management of contracts, viewing of parking operations and invoices, as well as communication with BREPARK GmbH. Employee Portal (MA Portal): A central work surface for employees of BREPARK GmbH for managing and processing customer transactions. This comprises in particular the maintenance of customer data, processing of contract enquiries, management of contracts and access media, execution of checking and approval processes, and support for internal administrative processes. Business Customer Portal (GKP): The solution must provide a business customer portal through which authorised business customers can independently manage their contract-related data and access permissions. BREPARK manages various parking facilities on behalf of third parties and manages long-term parking permissions for business customers, amongst other things. Around 7.000 access media for business customers are currently managed. The aim is to provide business customers with a digital option for independently managing their permissions and access media, thereby simplifying administrative processes. The service portal is to be integrated into the existing system landscape of BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular connection to SAP Business ByDesign as the leading ERP system and the required interfaces to existing parking management and access systems. The contractor must provide an operational overall system which fulfils the requirements of this specification of services and enables the further development of the digital customer processes of BREPARK GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, the scope of services also includes the required configuration, customising, integration into the existing system landscape, data migration, execution of tests, commissioning, and the required training, maintenance and support services for ongoing operations. Implementation takes place as an overall system. The contractor bears responsibility for the total technical and functional integration of all required components and interfaces.
sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.title: Service portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026

sig_6ca2cf074bf19752fa24.description: Iarnród Éireann is seeking to conduct a Preliminary Market Consultation to inform the potential future procurement of a Social Value Platform. The platform will support Iarnród Éireann in embedding, measuring, monitoring and verifying social value commitments across relevant contracts and procurement activities. Iarnród Éireann has already commenced the use of a social value platform through Thrive on a pilot basis, which has supported the development of Irish and EU social value proxies and enabled social value commitments to be expressed in measurable financial terms. This approach has allowed suppliers to submit clear, contract-specific commitments linked to employment, apprenticeships, skills development, community investment, SME support, social inclusion and wider environmental and social outcomes. This pilot is due to conclude in Q4 2027, and Iarnród Éireann requires a suitable solution to replace and build upon the pilot arrangement.
sig_6ca2cf074bf19752fa24.title: Social Value Management Platform

sig_6ca4347e696540da01ba.description:
The Municipality of Messini intends to adopt digital applications and intelligent actions with the aim of transforming itself into a 'smart city', through the development and use of new technological means that will improve the management and functionality of the urban environment. As a 'smart city', the Municipality will be a place where traditional services will become more efficient through the use of digital and telecommunications technologies, for the benefit of residents, visitors and businesses. These actions include smart pedestrian crossings that are friendly to people with disabilities, the provision of telemedicine systems to vulnerable groups for remote diagnosis, integrated infrastructure for protection against cyberattacks (Network Firewall, End point security, WAF, etc.), a central unified platform for the management and collection of smart city data, smart energy management systems for municipal and school buildings, smart lighting systems within municipal buildings, a municipal cemetery management system and digitisation of files, electronic invoicing, and an electronic system for the management and organisation of the Administration and the operational capacity of Local Government Organisations. The proposed solution will be an integrated solution that serves: ● Data collection from energy resources (Electricity, Oil, Natural gas, Water) ● Data processing ● Information visualisation. At the same time, the proposed solution must allow for scalability as requirements increase, so that it can cover even the most demanding implementations. The management application must be installed in the Cloud, and access to information must be achieved via any Web Browser. Finally, the management software must provide a user-friendly visualisation environment and the ability to display information in different ways, fully configurable by the user. At the same time, the user will be able to transform and correlate every form of data originating from completely heterogeneous environments or parts of different geographical areas. It must be possible to monitor both individual facilities and all of them together. The platform must have the ability to create users and user groups, while the levels and access capabilities for each section or sub-section of the platform can be defined in detail for each user or user group. Access from mobile phones or Tablets will be via Web Browser, therefore the platform must be fully responsive. The implemented system will function as a management system for the Municipality, for the control and understanding of energy resource consumption at various points of interest - buildings, with the ultimate goal of their rational use and the reduction of both costs and the carbon footprint.; The proposed solution will be an integrated solution that serves the management of the lighting of municipal buildings regardless of the geographical area and will consist of the following: ● Management platform (software) which will collect and process the data. It visualises them in a user-friendly way. It allows the management of lighting ● Automation devices with remote management capability. At the same time, the proposed solution must allow for scalability as requirements increase, so that it can cover even the most demanding implementations. The management application must be installed in the Cloud, and access to information must be achieved via any Web Browser. Through the application, absolute control and the reduction of unnecessary electricity consumption in the municipal buildings where the equipment will be installed will be achieved. Finally, the management software must provide a user-friendly visualisation environment and the ability to display information. Management concerns either remote access at random times or the creation of scenarios (scheduling) regarding the operation of the lighting. In order to make the implementation of the automations possible, the wall switches will be replaced with corresponding smart switches, which will have the capability of remote control. Additionally, special controllers will take on the role of communicating the switches with the software, transferring the information: - For the status of the device (whether it is on or off) - For sending the action command (on / off) Access from mobile phones or Tablets will be via Web Browser, therefore the platform must be fully responsive. The software architecture will be based on object-oriented design with a focus on reliability, scalability and optimal performance.; The proposed system will fully cover the management of burials, exhumations, extensions, charges, etc. of the Municipal Cemetery. The proposed system must include the burial register (management of the deceased), the management of plots, the management of the liable parties and the financial transactions carried out by the liable parties and generally every service concerning the Cemetery. The functions will be developed at the level of specific and general searches with various criteria (time period, alphabetical, etc.), adding new records, spatial mapping / presentation on a digital map and printing of lists and notices as the case may be. It will include the ability to import descriptive digital data and connect to corresponding spatial data in the Geographic Information System for the connection of the map and the database with tools that will not require the user to have GIS knowledge. The Database will cover all possible actions in accordance with the Cemetery Operation Regulation and will operate in an open-source relational database environment.

Which must also cover security functionality with the use of users, access rights and security codes, as well as an automatic backup function. The necessary Database files will be installed on the server designated by the Contracting Authority. The system to be installed must be structured in such a way that it can accept modifications (customisation) according to the requirements of the Service, the Operation Regulation and any amendments thereto. It must support: • Parameterisation of Cemetery Operation Regulation (C.O.R.) elements • Parameterisation of documents (e.g. Burial permit, annual notices, expiry notices, etc.) • Parameterisation of elements / Spatial and Descriptive Database The system to be installed must be structured in such a way as to make searching and processing data easy and functional, providing at least the following automated functions: • adding new records and archiving for each type of data • dynamic information searches with various keys either from the database or from the map • creation of lists with dynamic searches for each type of data on the screen and tools for printing lists / notices • visualised information on a map in the form of thematic maps at various levels (e.g. searches in grave categories, occupancy, etc.) • ability to display vector cartographic data with multiple layers of information, basic spatial search, as well as navigation and selection tools on the map, zoom in, zoom out, etc. • ability to parameterise the appearance / presentation of vector data (e.g. layer colours, etc.) • ability to view additional raster layers simultaneously with the vector ones.; The object of the action is the supply of software - equipment and the provision of services with the aim of implementing an integrated infrastructure for protection against cyberattacks and a teleworking system in the Municipality of Messini. The goal is the combined utilisation of specific cutting-edge technologies and especially those of Cybersecurity to prevent malicious attacks. Given the ongoing cyberattacks against the public sector, it is obvious that critical infrastructure can be affected and confidential data of services and citizens can be put at risk. The Municipality of Messini aims to increase network security. Specifically, it must be possible to connect securely to any authorised user, anywhere for any computing resource or information to which they have access rights, at any time and from any device.; The electronic invoicing system is a necessity in Local Government Organisations according to the current legislation in the context of the execution of public contracts. It is an integrated solution for keeping electronic books (myData) and the digital circulation of documents. The system must be a ready-made software package (COTS Commercial off-the-shelf) with two years of circulation in the market of Local Government Organisations and their Legal Entities, and must have at least 10 installations (relevant certificates to be submitted) in first-degree Local Government Organisations or a Legal Entity of a Local Government Organisation. On pain of exclusion, it must cover all the general and functional characteristics and interoperability as described in this paragraph and in the compliance tables. The candidate contractor must develop and describe in detail the characteristics and functions of the system.
sig_6ca4347e696540da01ba.title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF MESSINI

sig_6cba1fd98f80579abbe3.description: About the Service Operators, hauliers and drivers of Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs) must pay the HGV road user levy when they use UK roads. This applies equally to UK-registered vehicles and those registered in other countries. This promotes a level playing field between hauliers, and such road user charges are commonplace in Europe. The levy was first introduced in 2014 and reformed in 2023. The rate varies by vehicle weight and emissions class, with an exemption for zero emission HGVs. The levy can be paid daily, weekly, monthly, 6 monthly or annually. UK registered hauliers pay the levy in conjunction with the annual Vehicle Excise Duty. Foreign registered vehicles pay through an online portal, the Foreign Operator Payment System (FOPS), and must pay before using UK roads. FOPS is provided by a contractor with the contract managed by DVLA on behalf of DfT. Market Engagement Session DVLA will host a webinar on 2nd February 2026 from 11:00 to 12:00, to present a slide pack and facilitate a Q&A session about the service. If you are interested in attending, once responses have been received, further information will be provided and a set of questions to complete prior to the event, along with the appointment for the day. To register your interest and receive the questionnaire, please email Vikki.John@dvla.gov.uk by 9th January 2026. Include your organisation name and the names, job titles, and email addresses of those wishing to attend. Please note: any information you provide will be treated as background information only and shall not constitute any offer or commitment by either party. Lot 1: .
sig_6cba1fd98f80579abbe3.title: DVLA - Provision of Foreign Operator Payment Service - Pipeline Notice

sig_6cbc219f953e7b9470e2.description: The contract includes optional tranches defined in the specification. The details of the tasks entrusted to the contractor appear in the specification. The services are paid for by fixed prices. The Departmental Council of Lot-et-Garonne has decided to initiate rehabilitation and redevelopment works on the Pont de Pierre. This bridge crosses the Garonne, the riverside roads and allows the D 656 to connect the municipality of AGEN to the municipality of LE PASSAGE, in two by 3 lanes. The bridge supports sensitive networks (TIGF gas, town gas, electricity, urban heating network, etc.) and falls within the perimeter of listed historic monuments. It is located in a sensitive natural perimeter where spawning grounds have been identified, and a remarkable population of bats has been identified on the structure. A diagnosis of the bridge was established as part of a previous project management. The project manager designated during this consultation must familiarise themselves with the data from the previous diagnosis, update them and enrich them. The structure will be modelled to understand the functioning of the structures and its accessories. This modelling must make it possible to integrate data on the uses of the bridge (road traffic counting, etc.). The collection of information must make it possible to pinpoint the condition of parts of the structure, the extent of heritage, regulatory, technical, ecological and operational issues. The project manager must draw up a works programme. In addition, they must produce an environmental diagnosis around the structure, in order to draw up an impact study of the projected works (bats, spawning grounds, etc.). Accompanying and compensatory measures must be quantified if necessary
sig_6cbc219f953e7b9470e2.title: Rehabilitation and redevelopment of the Pont de Pierre over the Garonne in Agen-Le Passage (D656)

sig_6d2b297d9c88d9c9864f.description: The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) intends to issue a single-source cooperative agreement award to the University of California, Santa Cruz. The award will renew the Data Resource and Administrative Coordination Center (DRACC), a component of the Scalable and Systematic Neurobiology of Psychiatric and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Genes (SSPsyGene) Consortium. The long-term goal of SSPsyGene is to systematically study how risk genes for neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (NPDs) affect molecular, cellular, circuit, systems/organismal biology. The renewed DRACC will refine its focus on developing a sustainable knowledge base, with shared terms, definitions, and data standards that are interoperable with other knowledge platforms and will enable the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate research on brain function and NPDs. This resource will be made available for broad use by the biomedical community. Projects that propose to build on the DRACC's current role in refining methods and standards to harmonize data from the SSPsyGene Assay and Data Generation Centers and facilitate submission to data archives are encouraged. This is a forecast for a single source NOFO that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.
sig_6d2b297d9c88d9c9864f.title: Single Source: Scalable and Systematic Neurobiology of Psychiatric and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Genes: Data Resource and Administrative Coordination Center (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_6d2d06c6d16386e3cd1b.description: Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members. This Framework is making available for its Members the provision of RTPI Content Management Systems, Ticket Vending Machines, Electronic Ticket Machines, Accessible Rail Information and Support Units, and Transport and Data Managed Services. These five Lots form the focal point for any modern Ticketing & Information Scheme in managing customer information, journey planning, physical sales, revenue, and a range of customer facing managed services. Lot 1: RTPI Content Management Systems (CMS) The RTPI CMS Lot provides a supplier-agnostic Content Management System for Real Time Passenger Information, integrating with standards like GTFS, SIRI, BODS, and RSS. It will distribute real-time schedules and multimedia content to Passenger Information Displays, managed through a secure web portal with layout control, multilingual messaging, and access management. The systems are scalable, cloud hosted, GDPR-compliant, and include monitoring, fault management, and reporting. Delivery requires commissioning, testing, migration, and maintenance, with defined backup, PID interfacing, and documentation. Suppliers must follow formal project management, deliver training, and meet strict KPIs for availability, updates, and transparency. Lot 2: Ticket Vending Machines The Ticket Vending Machine (TVM) Lot focuses on providing modern, reliable, and accessible equipment aligned with operational and customer needs. The requirements highlight durability, accessibility compliance, and integration with transport systems, while ensuring wide payment options such as contactless, mobile, and cash for inclusivity. Priority has been given to cybersecurity, remote monitoring, and easy maintenance to reduce downtime and costs. The machines also support long-term goals of sustainability, scalability, and futureproofing, using energy-efficient, recyclable components and allowing upgrades for new products or payments. User experience is central, with clear interfaces, multilingual support, and accessibility for disabled passengers. Overall, the process delivers robust, user-friendly, and cost-effective TVMs that will remain a reliable backbone of the transport network. Lot 3: Electronic Ticket Machines The ETM Lot covers the supply, installation, and maintenance of Electronic Ticket Machines for public transport. Machines must support ITSO smartcards, EMV contactless, mobile ticketing (QR, barcode, NFC), and cash, while integrating with back-office systems for revenue and data exchange in line with ITSO, PCI-DSS, and BODS. They should be reliable, user-friendly, process transactions quickly, adapt to future needs, and link with Intelligent Transport Systems for real-time information and vehicle tracking. Suppliers will ensure strong project delivery from design and testing to deployment and lifecycle support, including staff training, spares, and repairs. Defined SLAs cover uptime, fault resolution, and updates. Security requires encryption, key management, and compliance with financial and data protection standards. Ongoing monitoring, reporting, and proactive updates are expected to maintain performance and meet evolving passenger needs. Lot 4: Accessible Rail Information And Support Units Accessible Rail Information and Support Units play a vital role in ensuring that all passengers, including those with disabilities or additional needs, can travel with confidence and independence. These units provide clear, consistent, and user-friendly information about train times, routes, facilities, and accessibility features both online and at stations. These units also offer facilities through which passengers can ask for assistance with practical help like boarding support, guidance through stations, and access to mobility aids. By combining reliable information with on-the-ground assistance, Accessible Rail Information and Support Units break down barriers to travel, promote inclusivity, and make public transport a safe and welcoming option for everyone. Lot 5: Transport And Data Managed Services The Transport and Data Managed Services Lot within the Framework provide public sector and operator purchasers with a range of secure, reliable, and scalable 'managed' solutions for handling the movement and management of critical transport and data information and services. By using managed services, purchasers benefit from expert monitoring, proactive issue resolution, and optimised infrastructure without the burden of managing complex systems in-house, all while maintaining compliance, security, and performance standards. This Lot has 7 Parts: Lot 5 - Part 1. Journey Planning Managed Service Lot 5 - Part 2. Consultancy Support Managed Service Lot 5 - Part 3. Operational Data Evaluation Managed Service Lot 5 - Part 4. sig_6d2d1f9ad2aefc6fc710.description: Since 1 April 2026, the new public law organisation Sanadura has been ensuring healthcare provision in the Upper Engadine. As an independent public law institution of the sponsoring municipalities of the Upper Engadine, Sanadura guarantees needs-based and economical care for the population in the region. It is responsible for regional healthcare provision and in particular for the operation and safeguarding of the retirement centres as well as the Spitex services. As part of the organisational realignment, an independent, modern and future-proof ICT infrastructure is to be established for Sanadura. The aim is to create a stable, secure and efficient technical basis for the operation of all organisational units. Further details on the initial situation can be found in the document "Part B Performance Specification - Specifications" section 2.1 Initial situation. The procurement of the new ICT infrastructure is carried out via the present public tender. It comprises an operation and support contract duration of 4 years. The exact content and scope of the procurement object can be found in section 2 of this document as well as in the document "Part B Performance Specification - Specifications" and "Part C Appendix 3: Tender Forms".

sig_6d3707439f3a5dd41c58.description: Please Note: While SAM.gov displays a specific Inactive Date, this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) is continuously open. Solution Briefs will be accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis at any point prior to the listed Inactive Date. Further, listed PSC and NAICS are placeholder only, final PSC and NAICS will be determined at time of propsal/award. Shaw AFB, South Carolina is conducting a CSO authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 and R-DFARS 212.70 and its associated class deviations. Under a CSO, the Air Force may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. Under this CSO, all items, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items. Awards will be RFO Part 12 contracts. The Air Force intends to obtain "innovative" solutions or potential new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technology advancements. Solutions may include existing technologies or procedures, not currently in use by the Air Force, that would enhance or streamline Air Force mission capabilities. “Innovative” is defined as any technology, process or method that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal. It also includes any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. The Government is not obligated to make any awards, and all awards under this CSO are explicitly subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by any vendor prior to the issuance of any awarded contract. The Government reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this CSO at its sole discretion. The Government seeks to deploy rapid, commercial off-the-shelf counter-UAS capabilities; fuse advanced intelligence and multi-source data to create a comprehensive operational picture; develop innovative kinetic and non-kinetic solutions to defeat coordinated UAS swarms; leverage agile software and rapid prototyping methodologies; implement modular open-systems approaches (MOSA) for seamless sensor integration; and establish sustainable, open-standard architectures to drive continuous competition. This enables the Department of War (DoW) to continuously field adaptable, integrated, and resilient defensive capabilities against rapidly evolving aerial and multi-domain threats. The CSO is a streamlined acquisition process that seeks to reduce acquisition timelines and acquire new, innovative solutions that vendors can bring forth to meet the stated Areas of Interest. Performers may need to demonstrate the capability to work in classified environments up to the Secret level before any award, if necessary. While this CSO is primarily designed to fulfill the requirements of the Shaw AFB Battle Lab and United States Air Forces Central (AFCENT), it may be leveraged to support broader Department of the Air Force (DAF) or Department of War (DoW) requirements under strict execution guidelines. To maintain oversight and prevent misuse, this CSO is not authorized for decentralized use by outside contracting offices. All external requirements must be validated and routed directly through AFCENT, and the 20th Contracting Squadron will retain sole procurement authority for all contract awards. Shaw AFB is focused on rapidly acquiring and deploying counter-UAS (cUAS) and defensive capabilities that form a cohesive, enterprise-wide open architecture ecosystem. The following focus areas are representative examples of the capabilities of interest; however, this is not an exhaustive list. The Government is open to, and highly encourages, innovative solutions from industry that address other technologies or approaches that align with the strategic vision outlined below. Solutions that address technologies across multiple pillars are encouraged. Teaming and Partnership for Turnkey Solutions: To mitigate the risks of disjointed systems and reduce administrative burden, the Government highly encourages industry vendors to form strategic partnerships, joint ventures, or Prime/Subcontractor teaming arrangements to submit complete, end-to-end solutions. Proposals that offer a single lead system integrator managing a suite of best-of-breed commercial technologies are strongly preferred over submissions for isolated, piecemeal components. The intent is to streamline the acquisition, delivery, and sustainment process by fielding cohesive, fully integrated systems. The Government seeks commercial capabilities that provide end-to-end defensive solutions, from immediate point defense to advanced data integration and long-term capability sustainment. Vendors may provide insight on solutions that address all or some of the capability pillars below. The desired end-state is a deployable capability that effectively counters evolving aerial threats while exploiting open architecture principles across its full lifecycle (development, integration, test, deployment, operations, and sustainment). An ideal partner has a first-party ability to directly leverage underlying commercial technologies to meet operational requirements; supporting partners would be considered enabling providers for specific aspects of the potential solution.

sig_6d5bd544b4c4ad3cf218.description: The objective of this framework is to provide Public Sector Organisations with a comprehensive range of biomedical and clinical research support solutions to contribute to strengthening their research capacity and innovation potential. The scope covers the full research lifecycle, from the design, delivery and management of biomedical and clinical trials to logistics, sample processing, storage, data, and laboratory support. sig_6d6aacc76f40311e632f.description: The purpose of the contract is the provision of the Comprehensive Service Management and Project Leadership service of the Official Credit Institute (ICO), in order to ensure the correct implementation, coordination, monitoring and continuous improvement of services and projects related to Information Systems and Corporate Technologies. The Official Credit Institute (ICO), as a business public entity with the nature of a credit institution, faces continuous growth in the number of technological services, strategic projects and regulatory requirements that must be managed by the Information Systems Directorate. This evolution, together with the new challenges arising from its activity, makes it necessary to have a specialised service that guarantees the comprehensive management of ICT services and projects, ensuring their correct planning, coordination, monitoring and continuous improvement. The contract includes the provision of Comprehensive Service Management and Project Leadership services, including the management of services, projects, incidents, changes, quality, product and vendor coordination, providing support to the broad catalogue of ICO technological services, among which are digital banking, core banking, regulatory reporting, Business Intelligence and other corporate systems. All of this with the objective of guaranteeing the quality, availability, security and evolution of the Information Systems, contributing to the digital transformation and compliance with the strategic objectives of the Institute.

sig_6d7706564aea95f33b65.description: ***SEE ATTACHMENTS FOR FULL TEXT OF ANNOUNCEMENT*** BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) FA9451-24-S-0001 Air Force Research Laboratory Directed Energy Directorate ANNOUNCEMENT OVERVIEW Initial 22 November 2023 NAICS CODE: The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715 for Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees. FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. ANNUAL REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS: Potential offerors are notified that effective 01 Jan 2005 to be eligible for an award and in compliance with FAR 52.204-7 and DFARS 252.204-7007 Alternate A, they must submit Annual Representations and Certifications, via SAM.gov. Before submitting the electronic Annual Representations and Certifications, Contractors must be registered in the SAM Database. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. ESTIMATED PROGRAM COST: Anticipated funding for the program (not per Call, contract, or award): FY24 FY25 FY26 FY27 FY28 TOTAL $100M $100M $100M $100M $99M $499M This funding profile is an estimate only and will not be a contractual obligation for funding. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). It is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all the Offeror’s data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. POINT OF CONTACT: a) Administrative, technical, or contractual questions should be sent via e-mail to afrl.rdlb.tacticalbaa@us.af.mil. All requests must include a name, e-mail address, and phone number of an organizational point of contact. b) Each Call will include specific contracting points of contact. sig_6d7c7538dc0c8cc95f71.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. sig_6d8566747ff6969a3b34.description: Framework agreement for the provision of private cloud services and operation in respect of the contracting authority's entire central IT infrastructure (SAP and MS AD environment in the form of virtual machines) and the performance of related migration tasks, as well as the provision of consultancy tasks. Framework amount: net 390 000 000,- HUF Based on the framework agreement, the contracting authority intends to procure the following services: - Migration of the contracting authority's current IT environment into the tenderer's cloud service (migration tasks): • Assessment of the current IT environment. • Planning of the migration of the current IT environment (by preparing a migration scenario) to the service provider's cloud service, including the translation of the SAP environment from IBM Power architecture to Intel X64 architecture and validation of the estimated required (Base) IT capacity. • Preparation of a schedule broken down into elementary steps with the definition of milestones, personal resources and the designation of responsible persons, which also covers the case of a negative, pessimistic scenario (worst case scenario). The scenario and the schedule shall be approved by the client, taking into account the MNB consultation if necessary. The service provider runs functional and security tests on test data in the test environment provided by it, and records the test results with particular regard to the correction of any critical errors that may have arisen. Depending on the test results, the client decides on going live or postponing it until the errors are corrected. • Live migration of the client's IT environment to the service provider's cloud service, including the translation of the SAP environment from IBM Power architecture to Intel X64 architecture. • Collaboration in the creation of a responsibility matrix to be defined by the client. • Collaboration in the creation of an exit strategy and action plan to be defined by the client in accordance with point KM 4.5. - Provision of private cloud service and operation of the migrated IT environment (operational tasks): • Full-scale operation of the migrated IT environment, including, but not limited to: o Updating individual software elements of the IT environment in a schedule agreed with the client o Operation of the Microsoft AD environment /on-prem and PaaS (Azure)/ - user administration is part of the task, but desktop and office device operation is not. o Operation of Microsoft Exchange and later Microsoft 365 Exchange Online. o Operation of Microsoft File Server. o Operation of SAP R/3 (Base and modules, applications) and associated databases (currently Oracle 11g), later possibly switching to SAP S/4 HANA (Version change is not part of the framework agreement, but taking over any new version for operation is). o Ensuring backup of the environment for operational security. o Ensuring tape backup of databases, handing over one cassette per week at a location in Budapest. o Provision of an online ticketing system to the client. - IT consultancy (consultancy tasks) The procedure aimed at concluding the framework agreement was aimed at concluding a framework agreement with a single tenderer in accordance with Section 105(1) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). As a result of the public procurement procedure aimed at concluding the framework agreement entitled "Private cloud service and software operation" (EKR identification number: EKR001511062023; number of the contract notice: 2023/S 178-557925 [KÉ-17831/2023], publication date: 2023.09.15), on the basis of the framework agreement established on 2023.12.18 between DHK Zrt. as client and Sysman Informatikai Zrt. as service provider – client identification number: DHK09/71-1/2023 – (hereinafter: FA), DHK Zrt. as contracting authority is conducting a written consultation for the performance of consultancy tasks, as a result of which it shall conclude a consultancy contract for the execution of the Microsoft Exchange mail server migration project and the implementation of the Microsoft Intune introduction. The contracting authority is concluding the consultancy contract for the performance of tasks related to the following: - Introduction of Microsoft Intune; - Migration of Microsoft Exchange mail server to Microsoft 365 Cloud environment. The maximum billable consultancy hours per task recorded in the technical specification total: 188 hours. The detailed task definition is contained in the Technical Specification forming Annex No. 1 to the draft contract, and further conditions related to performance can be found in the draft contract.

sig_6db2890226715c68798c.description: The Landkreis Ostprignitz-Ruppin intends to replace the currently used financial software Finanz+ from MACH AG (formerly DataPlan GmbH) with a new, modern, multi-client capable budget and accounting software. Particular emphasis is placed on the possibility of retaining existing and well-functioning processing procedures, but establishing improved processes using the new software where necessary. All data from the legacy system that are necessary to correctly book depreciation, special items, accruals and deferrals, write-offs, deferrals and provisions in subsequent years should be transferred. The goal is to begin the financial year 2028 with the new budget and accounting software. The new software is to be introduced by the deadline of 01.01.2028 for the following areas: - Budget planning, execution, annual financial statements including balance sheet and consolidated financial statements; - Treasury; - Electronic / digital invoice workflow; - Asset accounting; - Liquidity planning and analysis; - Financial and debt statistics; - Controlling and analysis; - Filing and archiving of electronic documents in the existing document management system "d.velop documents" from d.velop GmbH.

sig_6db8e53d7d03a428d665.description: This is to inform the market of the contract award to AIXON Digital Ltd for the contract: Provision of Cognitive RPA, Intelligent Automation & AI Cloud Platform & Virtual Workforce. The contract is required to ensure continuity of critical automated processes that underpin statutory and essential frontline Council services. These processes currently operate on the Blue Prism Cloud Platform, supported and maintained by AI‐XON, who have developed and customised several of the Council’s automation workflows. Scope of Services. The direct award will cover:- Licensing and access to the Blue Prism Cloud RPA platform- Platform support and maintenance- Business‐as‐usual (BAU) process support- Support for the Council’s bespoke automation environment Rationale for Direct Award The Council intends to use this route on the basis of continuity of service and avoidance of disproportionate duplication of costs. The Blue Prism Cloud licence and associated workflows will only be required for the next 12 months, after which the platform will be decommissioned as part of the Council’s wider automation roadmap. Procuring an alternative supplier for such a short period would result in:- Significant onboarding and transition costs- Avoidable handover effort and operational disruption- Increased risk to the continuity of statutory processes- Poor value for money due to the short duration of remaining platform use AI‐XON has provided a competitive quotation aligned with the limited remaining requirement and offers a flexible commercial model that ensures the Council pays only for support used. The proposed commercial terms offer a cost‐effective approach for a time‐limited requirement, ensuring that the Council continues to meet statutory obligations while avoiding unnecessary expenditure. sig_6dc0d44ef48e76438ccd.description: Political transitions, governance changes, insurgencies, and violent extremism continue to reshape West Africa"s peace and security landscape. The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) plays a critical role in coordinating regional responses to security challenges through its strategic frameworks for peace and development. These include conflict prevention and governance, alongside regional strategies addressing climate adaptation, resilience, and economic integration. Strengthening coordination, fostering inclusive engagement - including with civil society - and promoting adaptive and preventive approaches are cross-cutting themes. The European Union (EU) and the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)- co-financed Support to ECOWAS in Peace, Security and Governance (EPSG) project provides technical and financial support to ECOWAS for the strengthening of regional peace, security, and democratic governance. Service provision is ensured by regular joint planning processes with the partner. At the same time, the project is required to react flexibly to the political context. The project is active in five components: a. Conflict Prevention and Crisis Management EPSG enhances ECOWAS' ability to detect and respond to conflicts by strengthening National Centres for Coordination of Response Mechanisms (NCCRMs) and other National Peace Infrastructures (NPIs). It also supports the ECOWAS Early Warning Directorate (EWD) in improving data collection, analysis, and reporting within the ECOWAS Early Warning and Response Network (ECOWARN) system. The project reinforces ECOWAS' capacity to initiate timely interventions through the Early Response Mechanism (ERM). b. Security Sector Reform, Governance and Human Rights To strengthen accountable and citizen-focused security institutions, EPSG supports security sector reform through: Training and advisory services for security actors, parliamentary committees, and civil society organizations; strengthening democratic oversight to improve governance and transparency; and promoting human rights, addressing gender-based violence, and increasing the representation of women in security roles. c. Electoral Support and Democratic Transitions Amid political transitions and the risk of election-related violence, EPSG supports ECOWAS member states to conduct peaceful and credible elections by: Supporting Election Management Bodies (EMBs) to address gaps from past elections and facilitating training and peer-learning initiatives coordinated by the ECOWAS Electoral Assistance Division (EAD) and the ECOWAS Network of Electoral Commissions (ECONEC); implementing recommendations from ECOWAS election observation missions; engaging civil society and the media to counter disinformation and prevent electoral violence; and supporting transition of member states back to a constitutional order. d. Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) and Youth, Peace, and Security (YPS) Agendas Recognizing the crucial role of women and youth in peacebuilding, EPSG supports the implementation of ECOWAS" WPS and YPS agendas. EPSG: Supports women and youth networks like the Network on Peace and Security for Women in West Africa (NOPSWECO) to enhance their involvement in peace processes; provides training and advocacy to increase women and youth participation in governance and conflict mediation. e. Strengthening cooperation of the regional training infrastructure in the implementation of the ECOWAS Peace and Security Architecture Funded by BMZ, this component enhances capacities of and cooperation between regional training centres of excellence such as the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC) and the National Defense College (NDC) and the ECOWAS Commission, in particular with respect to Peace Support Operations (PSOs). Support is focused on: Developing and implementing trainings, dialogues and research; policy development; strengthening (digital) capacities of training centres. Lot LOT-0001: 81318825 EPSG Expert Pool. To be able to deliver the requested support to the political partner ECOWAS Commission, its institutions and specialized agencies, and other cooperation partners such as Training Centres of Excellence (TCEs) in time and at a high level of flexibility, quality, efficiency and reliability, the EPSG project seeks to engage a consulting firm to facilitate the engagement of experts to implement initiatives at the continental, regional and local level in the areas of: - Structural conflict prevention; - Conflict management; - Peace consolidation; - Organizational development and change management. The selected expert pool shall advise both internal project staff and external partners for the implementation of project outputs. External partners could be officials from the ECOWAS Commission, related institutions and agencies such as the regional Training Centres of Excellence (TCEs), member states and Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). The activities implemented by the expert pool must comply with the associated indicators, fulfilling the module objective and output indicators. The implementation of all outputs of the EPSG project is managed through the project"s heads of components. Required areas of support include, but are not limited to, thematic research, curriculum development, conduct of training, inputs to and facilitation of policy development processes, inputs to and facilitation of strategic planning and monitoring, conduct of human and institutional capacity development measures, facilitation and rapporteuring of events. The key experts and expert pool which are the objective of this tender is expected to deliver the following: 1) Provision of national, regional and (at times) international experts. 2) Long-term support in some thematic fields through the same (key) consultants. 3) Flexibility in responding to emerging demands by partners: Based on the specific ToR provided by the project, the selected consultancy will provide 3 suitable options for experts to support the specific assignment. 4) Delivery of work assignments which involve both travel to ECOWAS member state countries as well as remote work from the experts" respective home countries. 5) Backstopping of individual experts by international consultancy.

sig_6dc8c6f6dd6c49b21159.description: The Joint All Domain Persistent Adaptive Collaborative Technologies (JADPACT) Project seeks to develop Human-Machine Teaming (HMT) concepts that leverage AI/Automation capabilities to support Battle Managers. C2 Decision Advantage events provide support for the ABMS Transformational Model decision functions and an opportunity to learn about and explore many different AI/automation approaches for Battle Management. Furthermore, the events and R&D aim to ensure warfighter involvement in the development of AI/autonomy and further identify areas where AI augmentation would support Battle Managers. The goal is to include industry to ensure work being done to develop and adapt the latest, cutting-edge AI/automation approaches can be leveraged and adapted to the needs of Battle Managers. This will be accomplished by seeking unique and innovative solutions to accomplish the defined technical requirements. The Combined Joint All-Domain Command and Control (CJADC2) Campaign Plan 2030 defines decision advantage as the ability to consistently make better, timelier decisions than the adversary. Current DAF command and control (C2) systems and processes are optimized for low intensity conflict and do not address decision advantage over the pacing challenge. Deriving effective C2 capability development toward decision advantage requires a clear understanding of what C2 decisions are. The DAF Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS) Cross Functional Team (CFT) provides a quantitative model for the Joint Warfighting Function of C2 as the Command, Plan, and Battle Management decision domains, supported by and integrated with Battle Analysis (military intelligence and surveillance). Each of these decision domains are decomposed in the Transformational Model for Decision Advantage (TM-DA) using model-based systems engineering to bridge the gap between operational concepts and software design. The M-DASH event is tentatively scheduled for 25 January 2027 - 4 February 2027 in Las Vegas, Nevada. A virtual Ask Me Anything session is scheduled for 15 October 2026 at 1200-1300 EST (Details in paragraph 2.2 of the Call).
sig_6dc8c6f6dd6c49b21159.title: Call 03 M-DASH - Joint All Domain Persistent Adaptive Collaborative Technologies II (JADPACT II)
