All tender information MUST be submitted through the Jaggaer eSourcing Portal. Overview of Training and Mentoring Programme We are inviting bidders to set out an approach to deliver a Training and Mentoring programme for three cohorts of UKRI Policy Fellows. The programme will begin in February 2026 for the 2025 cohort of fellows. Aims and Objectives of Training and Mentoring Programme The core aims and objectives of the training and mentoring are to: • Prepare Fellows for the cultural transition into government • Advance fellows in their careers • Foster networks and cross-working • Tailor support to different disciplines and career stages • Create a lasting alumni legacy To meet the aims as set out above, bidders should address the following objectives: • Offer a series of themed and focused learning sessions spanning each individual cohort. Bidders should ensure the time commitment is manageable for fellows and provide dates and times in advance. • The sessions should be inclusive, with at least two face-to-face meetings over the cohort. Any face-to-face sessions will be based in the UK, and the successful supplier should determine location once cohort members have been recruited, taking an inclusive approach to location and venue. • Encourage cross-disciplinary collaboration, peer support and opportunities to strengthen relationship building. • Actively design opportunities for fellows to build networks, identify synergies across fellowships, and support collaboration both among fellows and between host departments • Ensure longevity of benefit to participants beyond the duration of the programme itself. • Work closely with ESRC, providing regular (minimum monthly to start with) progress reviews via email, phone, or video conferencing in advance of and after each event/deliverable. This requirement is split into 2 Lots and 1 supplier be awarded for each: Lot 1 – Training The focus areas of this training programme are likely to include the following topics, but will not be limited to: • Policy making in the UK, actors, structure, cycles, streams • Networking and building relationships in policy • Communication training for policy, including writing and briefing • Supporting evidence use in government • Knowledge Exchange (KE) and science for policy in UK and international • Equality Diversity Inclusion (EDI) in KE • Wellbeing and mental health considerations during a fellowship • Developing effective impact case studies and using impact to support career progression • Data; Access, Use, Ethics and AI Lot 2 - Mentoring In addition to complimenting the areas of focus covered by the training programme, the mentoring programme could focus on (but not be limited to) the following activities: • Identifying and building on fellows’ unique strengths and experiences • Creating and implementing individual development plans • Identifying potential career pathways • Agreeing individual outcomes and personal milestones • Supporting fellows to grow relevant contacts and networks • Develop specific plans for communicating their research effectively to policy audiences Single bidders are welcome to submit proposals to deliver both lots (Training and Mentoring), or to submit proposals for just Lot 1 (Training) or Lot 2 (Mentoring). Please ensure you review all attached information to ensure a full understanding of this requirement. sig_6e3ccb4660701a73364f.description:
Procurement procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement for the procurement of active and passive network equipment and the performance of related services (HNET25) for organisations within the scope of Government Decree 301/2018 (XII.27.) on the National Telecommunications and Informatics Council and on Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség Zártkörűen Működő Részvénytársaság and the centralised public procurement system for governmental IT procurements (hereinafter: DKÜ Decree). With regard to the delivery deadline, the Contracting Authority stipulates the following: Pursuant to Section 105. (2) (c) of the Public Procurement Act, during the re-opening of competition, the Contracting Authority (Affected Organisation) is entitled to specify a delivery deadline longer than the specified delivery deadlines, taking into account the subject matter of the specific public procurement and the individual characteristics of the procurement, i.e., the objective performability of the specific contract. For products/services where the "Product Type" column of the "Product List" worksheet in the Detailed Price Table contains the designation "GOODS", the delivery (shipping) deadline shall be as recorded in the product list, with the proviso that the delivery (shipping) deadline is not determined by the tenderers, but in all cases by the contracting authority (Affected Organisation) implementing the specific public procurement in the second part of the framework agreement procedure, taking into account the subject matter of the specific public procurement and its individual characteristics, i.e. the objective performability of the specific contract. For products/services where the "Product Type" column of the "Product List" worksheet in the Detailed Price Table contains the designation "Service", the deadline for commencing the provision of the service shall be as recorded in the product list. For the sake of clarity, the Contracting Authority records that the term Procurement Documents means the Call for Tenders and the Other Procurement Documents taken together. The framework agreement consists of the following periods: - Contracting period (24 months): during this period, individual contracts may be concluded AND performed (if the performance level of the Framework Agreement reaches the per-lot framework amount already during the contracting period, the contracting period shall close and the contract performance period shall commence); - Contract performance period (12 months): during this period, it is exclusively possible to perform individual contracts concluded during the contracting period (in the event of the closure of the contracting period of the Framework Agreement due to the occurrence of the conditions set out in the second paragraph of point IV.8. and in point IV.12. of the Framework Agreement, the contract performance period shall be extended by the period still remaining from the 24-month (in the event of an extension of the Framework Agreement, 30-month) contracting period of the Framework Agreement); - Settlement period (3 months): during this period, settlements exclusively take place between the contracting authority and the tenderers that have concluded the framework agreement, serving to completely close the framework agreement. As a result of part 1 of this public procurement procedure, the task of the tenderers that have concluded the framework agreement is the supply of homogeneous network equipment and accessory products, as well as the performance of services related thereto in accordance with the Procurement Documents, taking into account the following main product categories and quantitative data: -- 11 pieces of main product categories: IP-based equipment supporting voice transmission Network security solutions Network management solutions IP video systems LAN active equipment Passive network elements Rack cabinets Uninterruptible power supplies Wireless solutions WAN equipment Services A total of 26 product categories including subcategories. The Contracting Authority intends to procure new (unused, unrefurbished) equipment within the framework of this procedure. The purpose of concluding the framework agreement is to procure active and passive network equipment connected to the network infrastructure already existing at the affected organisations, as well as related manufacturer and non-manufacturer services, for the purpose of expanding and further developing existing capacities, as well as creating new systems connected to the already existing network infrastructure. The Contracting Authority records that, in accordance with the explanatory provision under Section 3. Point 18. of the Public Procurement Act, the total quantity stipulated in the framework agreement means the net framework amount of 260 000 000 000 HUF (excluding options) (hereinafter: framework amount). Based on the provisions of Section 21. (4) of Government Decree 321/2015. (X. 30.), the Contracting Authority records that the expected scale (value) of separate contracts to be implemented on the basis of the framework agreement and to be performed at the same time is net 8 300 000 000 HUF; As a result of public procurement part 2 of this public procurement procedure, the task of the tenderers that have concluded the framework agreement is to supply general network equipment and accessory products, and to perform services related thereto in accordance with the Procurement Documents, taking into account the following main product categories and quantitative data: — 13 pieces of main product categories: IP-based equipment supporting voice transmission Network security solutions Network management solutions IP video systems LAN active equipment Optical transmission equipment Passive network elements Rack cabinets Rack cabinets / Optional accessories Uninterruptible power supplies Wireless solutions WAN equipment Services A total of 36 product categories including subcategories. The Contracting Authority intends to procure new (unused, unrefurbished) equipment within the framework of this procedure. The purpose of concluding the framework agreement is to procure active and passive network equipment related to the network infrastructure already existing at the affected organisations, as well as related manufacturer and non-manufacturer services, with the aim of expanding and further developing existing capacities and creating new systems connected to the already existing network infrastructure. The Contracting Authority records that in accordance with Section 3. Point 18.

of the explanatory provision, the total quantity stipulated in the framework agreement is represented by the net framework amount of 130 000 000 000 HUF (calculated without options) (hereinafter: framework amount). The Contracting Authority, based on the provisions of Section 21. (4) of Government Decree 321/2015. (X. 30.), records that the expected scale (value) of separate contracts to be implemented on the basis of the framework agreement and to be performed at the same time is net 4 166 000 000 HUF.

sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Vantaan kaupunki and other municipalities are jointly planning a tender contest for a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning, so the procurement will likely be carried out as a joint procurement group of several contracting authorities. The contracting authorities are surveying suppliers' interest in participating in the market dialogue for the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning. The subject matter of the procurement is a browser-based software service delivered via the data network for assessing the climate impacts of land use plans, with which the contracting authority can assess and compare the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use plans based on the carbon footprint and carbon handprint calculated by the tool. The subject matter of the procurement includes implementation projects for the low-carbon tool, rights of use, support and maintenance services, supplementary expert services ordered separately, and additional procurement opportunities. The aim is to obtain a solution that is suitable for the Finnish land use and construction context and for the evaluation of detailed local plan level land use plans. The solution is also intended to be further developed to improve the assessment of the climate impacts of urban land use planning. Commercial use of the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning will start according to municipality-specific schedules estimated during Q2/2026-Q1/2027. The solution to be procured must preliminarily include the following key functionalities and features: - The solution is map- and GIS-based. - The evaluation method of the solution must take into account the entire life cycle of the land use plans being evaluated, including the climate impacts of the project before use, during use and after use, as well as impacts outside the life cycle and potential climate benefits. - The solution must be able to utilise national and city-specific parameters and data. - The evaluation method must comprehensively take into account the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use projects, also considering climate impacts other than those produced by buildings, such as the climate impacts of transport or energy consumption. - The solution takes into account the Finnish Green Building Council's definition of a carbon-neutral built area. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register for the market dialogue and provide answers to the preliminary questions presented in the market consultation notice by Friday 13.3.2026 by 12 to the following address: jonna.hirvonen@vantaa.fi. Registrations must be headed as follows: "Registration for market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning". Registrations must contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company - Answers to preliminary questions
sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.title: Information request and invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning

sig_6e48c2579f22a3a99ca1.description: The subject of the procurement is an electronic signature service solution (SaaS) that is in production use on the market, operates in a multi-tenant environment and whose core functionalities are available at the time of procurement without significant customer-specific product development. The solution must enable the electronic signing of documents, reliable identification of signatories, monitoring of signing processes, and the secure handling, storage and management of signed documents. The solution must support the secure authentication and electronic signing of both internal and external organisation users as described in the invitation to tender documents. The aim of the procurement is to replace paper-based and partly manual signing procedures with controlled, information-secure and integrated electronic signature processes, as well as to improve the handleability, uniformity, traceability and lifecycle management of document-related information.
sig_6e48c2579f22a3a99ca1.title: Electronic signature solution, Siun sote

sig_6e8d7451ceffcad884f2.description: David Ross Education Trust is inviting tenders for the implementation and ongoing provision of a secure, modern and user-friendly Human Resources Information System and payroll solution. The solution will support approximately 2,200 employees across the Trust's 36 academies and central functions. It must support the full employee lifecycle and the accurate, timely and compliant operation of payroll. The requirement includes: core HR and employee record management; payroll calculation, processing and statutory reporting, including Teachers' Pension Scheme and multiple Local Government Pension Scheme arrangements; employee and manager self-service; recruitment, onboarding and employee lifecycle processes; absence, leave and contractual change management; workflows, approvals, reporting and management information; integration and secure data exchange; data migration, configuration, testing, training and implementation; security, data protection, business continuity and disaster recovery; and ongoing support, maintenance, system updates and service management. The Trust will continue to operate payroll through its in-house payroll team. The contract will be for a maximum period of ten years, with break options available to the Trust at the end of years five and eight. Tenders will be evaluated on the basis of 60% quality and 40% price. The Trust may invite shortlisted bidders to participate in a supplier demonstration as part of the evaluation process. All tender documents, communications, clarification questions and submissions must be managed through the InTend portal. The deadline for tender submissions is 09:00 BST on 19 October 2026. Lot 1: .
sig_6e8d7451ceffcad884f2.title: Provision of a Human Resources Information System and Payroll Service

sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratizes access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonization, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximize the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximize the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigor across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilize the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.title: The NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS)

sig_6edf5657f27a290062c4.description: The Reception and Population department wishes to proceed with having a new software application available for managing population registers, civil status certificates, foreign national files, the polio register and related administrative processes. The contract includes the supply, implementation, maintenance and support of an integrated software solution for civil affairs. This concerns a SaaS solution that offers the contracting authority maximum relief in terms of: management, updates and security. Furthermore, we observe that files are becoming more complex and often have overlap between different domains (civil status, foreign nationals,...) where this was previously much more often separate. Consequently, it is appropriate that this concerns a total package so that work can be carried out much more flexibly across domains within the department. The administration therefore wishes for one total quotation for various modules with an unlimited number of user licences: Population including digital residence checks Foreign nationals Civil status Elections This approach guarantees that the investment is future-proof and offers maximum added value for both the employees and the citizen.

sig_6f02285e937294df1576.description: The National Business Crime Centre (NBCC) is looking for information from the market on technical solutions to bring together intellligence and information from retailers and retail partners to more precisely and efficiently allocate policing resources against retail crime. The RCFC (Retail Crime Fusion Cell) is the central intelligence hub of the Tackling Retail Crime Together strategy, ensuring a unified, data driven national response. It integrates police and industry data to create the UK’s most comprehensive picture of retail crime, accessible through a shared, self service intelligence portal. The NBCC will own the RCFC which will be hosted by Opal on behalf of national policing. The function will be to facilitate the sharing of data and creating operational packs for police forces which provides real time insight on crime trends, offender behaviour, high harm locations and organised crime links, enabling targeted operational and strategic action. The private sector will fund the platform and a police staff post. The police contribution is facilitating the collaboration platform – albeit we won’t actually ‘own’ the platform or be the Data Controller. Policing will fill the funded post with a data analyst/ scientist to produce assessments of the problem. Operating under strict security controls, the RCFC enhances collaboration across policing and retail—strengthening efforts to disrupt organised crime groups and manage prolific offenders. It does not replace existing systems; it unifies and amplifies them, acting as the intelligence layer that connects the entire retail crime ecosystem. Please note that this is not a call for competition.No response to this PME exercise will exclude any supplier from a potential procurement exercise. Lot 1: .
sig_6f02285e937294df1576.title: PME - NBCC Retail Crime Fusion Cell

sig_6f28ceac4cc46cc5c898.description: The contracting authority has tendered a contract regarding maintenance and further development of KOT admission. KOT admission is a sector-critical application that supports admission processes for higher education programmes in Denmark. Following Transition In, the supplier must, in close agile cooperation with the contracting authority, ensure efficient maintenance and further development of KOT admission. Background and purpose KOT admission is a sector-critical application that supports the annual coordinated admission to higher education programmes in Denmark. The application annually handles approx. 85.000 applicants and 229.000 applications distributed across 940 study programmes at 30 educational institutions. The coordination task is anchored in Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen (UFS) in the Coordinated Enrolment (KOT), and comprises all academy profession, professional bachelor's and bachelor's degree programmes. The overall purpose of coordination is to support an applicant being able to apply for admission to multiple study programmes in order of priority in the same admission round, while at the same time enabling institutions, based on case processing of the applications, to rank the applications so that an applicant is offered at most one study place on the highest possible priority of the applied study programmes. KOT-optagelse has just undergone modernisation in the Agency for Digitisation and IT, after which it has been handed over to UFS, which now holds overall system responsibility. KOT-optagelse consists of modules built on various technologies, including: • Backend: Java (Spring Boot) and .NET Core • Frontend: Angular • Database: PostgreSQL The contracting authority is platform owner and makes the overall operating platform, infrastructure, network, identity management and test data available. The contract comprises the following main services: Application maintenance: Ongoing preventative application maintenance. Bug fixing: Ongoing bug fixing according to defined service levels. Minor changes: Implementation of minor changes in the application. Testing and quality assurance: Implementation of relevant testing and quality assurance prior to releases and patches, including end-to-end testing or other relevant testing (performance, security, specific integration testing, etc.). Release management: Management of ongoing releases and any patches necessary outside the ordinary release cycle. The supplier must bear overall responsibility for an efficient release process and be clear regarding process, roles and responsibilities. Technical support: 2. and 3. level support. Further development: Implementation of ongoing further development and independent further development projects with participation from UFS and the supplier. Transition In: Takeover of the application from the existing supplier.
sig_6f28ceac4cc46cc5c898.title: Contract regarding maintenance and further development of KOT admission

sig_6f3488e81221fb69a7cd.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_6f6c0b92f52d18c5cddb.description: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability in Wales and affects around 7,000 people each year. While survival rates continue to improve, many people experience a significant reduction in support once they leave hospital at a stage when rehabilitation remains critical to recovery and long-term independence. Around 45% of stroke survivors report feeling abandoned following discharge because they do not receive the support they need to recover well. The impact extends far beyond the individual. Variations in access to rehabilitation, follow-up support and community services can lead to poorer outcomes, increased carer burden, avoidable demand on health and care services, and significant societal and economic costs. Stroke currently costs NHS Wales approximately £220 million per year and the wider Welsh economy approximately £1.63 billion annually. Without intervention, these costs are expected to increase significantly. The challenge has been developed following extensive investigation across Wales involving clinicians, health boards, national leaders, stroke survivors, carers and the Stroke Association. This work has helped define the challenge, identify unmet needs, understand existing service variation and explore the current market landscape. The conclusion is clear: Wales requires innovative, scalable approaches that can strengthen recovery, improve experience, reduce feelings of abandonment and support more equitable outcomes beyond hospital discharge. The challenge aligns with the Welsh Government Quality Statement for Stroke, which places renewed emphasis on rehabilitation, recovery, person-centred care and ensuring that stroke survivors do not feel abandoned during their recovery journey. The Challenge We are seeking innovative solutions that can improve rehabilitation, recovery and long-term support for stroke survivors. Access to rehabilitation and follow-up support varies across Wales. As a result, outcomes can depend too heavily on where a person lives rather than on their clinical need. This challenge seeks innovative approaches that can improve equity of access and help ensure people can receive high-quality rehabilitation and recovery support regardless of geography, including those living in rural, remote, underserved and seldom heard communities across Wales. The challenge is outcome-focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model. Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their solution could be adapted, developed or enhanced to meet the needs of NHS Wales and stroke survivors. We are not seeking to specify a single solution in advance. The purpose of this challenge is to support the development, demonstration and evaluation of innovative approaches that can improve recovery, reduce feelings of abandonment and create foundations for sustainable improvement across Wales. Particular consideration should be given to how solutions can improve access to rehabilitation and recovery support for people who may face barriers associated with geography, transport, service availability, digital exclusion, workforce capacity or being within a seldom-heard group. The challenge is not simply about providing more therapy. We are interested in approaches that enable personalised, continuous and motivating rehabilitation and self-management support across home, community and outpatient settings whilst supporting better experiences and outcomes for stroke survivors. This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 2 Contracts for Innovation competition. In contrast to a Phase 1 competition, focusing on feasibility, we are seeking organisations with existing technologies, products, platforms, services or rehabilitation approaches that require adaptation, enhancement, configuration or further development to address the identified needs of stroke survivors, carers and rehabilitation services across Wales. This challenge follows significant investigation and engagement to understand the problem, review evidence, define requirements and explore potential market solutions. We are therefore seeking solutions with an established foundation. Early-stage concepts requiring fundamental research or proof-of-concept development are unlikely to be supported Projects should support the development, adaptation and real-world demonstration of innovative approaches capable of improving rehabilitation, recovery and life after stroke. Successful projects are expected to generate practical evidence relating to: • Patient and carer outcomes. • Rehabilitation outcomes. • User experience. • Service and workforce impact. • Affordability and sustainability. • Adoption readiness. • Future scalability. Applicants should describe in-detail: • What they propose to deliver. • How it will be tested and evaluated. • How impact will be measured. • How the solution could evolve in future. • A core delivery plan to 31 March 2027, including activities, milestones, deliverables and costs. Applicants should describe in outline: • A separate proposal for a potential further stage beyond April 2027, including the additional activities, deliverables, outcomes, milestones, timescales and costs. • How the further stage would build on the evidence and learning generated during the core project. • What additional value the further stage would deliver for stroke survivors, services and the wider recovery pathway. • How the core project would remain viable and deliver meaningful outputs if further funding does not become available. Funding Allocation and Project Details Competition Type: Phase 2 Development and Real-World Demonstration Funding Available: £300,000 Total budget to support a portfolio of projects The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, i.e., should additional funding become available. Number of Projects: Current funding is available to support a portfolio of projects, dependent upon the number/quality of submissions received. Portfolio Approach Funding decisions may be made using a portfolio approach, recognising that improving recovery and reducing abandonment after stroke is a complex challenge that may benefit from multiple complementary solutions rather than a single intervention. Consideration may be given to the overall balance of projects supported, the evidence generated, opportunities for collaboration between projects and the potential for wider adoption and learning across Wales. Solutions may address different aspects of rehabilitation, self-management, recovery, service coordination, family support, accessibility, digital capability, assistive technology, data, analytics or outcomes measurement. Collectively, these may contribute towards the wider ambition of improving life after stroke across Wales. Potential further funding: Additional funding may become available to support a further stage of development or demonstration beyond April 2027. This funding is not currently confirmed and should not be assumed as part of the initial project award. Any decision to provide further funding would be subject to funding availability, project performance, evidence of value and the priorities of the challenge partners. Lot 1: . None

sig_6f6fe2304e64fbed5991.description: The subject matter of the contract is the identification and inventory of a significant number, as described as a minimum in paragraph 1.2, of unallocated properties belonging to housing rehabilitation programmes belonging to the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family, the legal establishment of their ownership (through the provision of services concerning the legal audit of properties as regards ownership of the respective property), actions for the exploitation of the properties for public-benefit purposes, the entry of property data into a digital platform / Property Management software application to be implemented within the framework of the Project and the completion of the electronic property file through services concerning the technical audit of part of the properties and evidence to be produced within the framework of the said audit [para. 1.3 & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders] The subject matter of the project is the inventory of a significant number, as described as a minimum in paragraph 1.2. of Annex I, of unallocated properties from housing rehabilitation programmes for refugees, destitute persons, disaster victims and victims of the Second World War, implemented across the country over the last 100 years, namely buildings, flats and plot areas. The inventory shall not include properties disposed of with a final Title Deed of ownership to beneficiaries, as these are now considered private properties. In greater detail, the subject matter of the Project includes the following: • the identification and inventory of a significant number, as described as a minimum in paragraph 1.2. of Annex I, of unallocated properties from housing rehabilitation programmes of the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family and the creation of a digital property file • actions for the legal establishment of the ownership of the properties to be inventoried • actions for the optimal exploitation of part of the properties for public-benefit purposes (such as costing of damage rehabilitation or costing of property demolition) • a study of the technical specifications of a digital platform / Property Management software application and its creation • the entry of data of the unallocated properties to be identified into the digital platform / Property Management software application to be implemented within the framework of the Project and the completion of the electronic property file, through services concerning the technical audit of part of the properties and evidence to be produced within the framework of the said audit. In greater detail, within the framework of the project, a Property Management platform / online Property Management software application with an integrated Geographical Information System (GIS) shall be implemented, utilising where possible and in accordance with the judgement and proposal of the candidate Contractor, the existing system of IDIKA S.A. which is described in para. 1.2.2, while documents, diagrams and other evidence concerning properties of the Ministry shall be collected and where required digitised, and data shall be recorded with the aim of creating a digital property file. In particular, actions are provided for with the aim of the as complete as possible completion of the property file, on a case-by-case basis, as well as the entry of the relevant data into the application, ensuring the possibility of electronic management of the properties through it. The application shall include the digital file of the property with, on a case-by-case basis, technical, legal and administrative data concerning each property as well as the spatial identification thereof (connection with GIS). For a very small part of the properties, the creation of new topographical diagrams, floor plans, etc. may also be required, as the said service is specified hereinafter in this call for tenders. The subject matter of the project can be grouped into the following work sections: SECTION 1 - Implementation study for the description of the implementation steps for the entire project (technical specifications, preconditions, etc.) SECTION 2 - Development of a digital platform / Property Management software application (including training, pilot and production operation support services) SECTION 3 - Inventory of a significant number, as described as a minimum in paragraph 1.2 of Annex I, of unallocated properties owned by the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family through research in archives kept both in the competent Services of the Ministry and in the Services of the Regions and Decentralised Administrations throughout the country and entry of the property data into a digital platform SECTION 4 - Services concerning the technical audit and where possible the completion of the property file SECTION 5 - Support services for the legal establishment of the ownership of the unallocated properties and ascertainment of the conditions governing the properties SECTION 6 - Actions for the exploitation of part of the properties for public-benefit purposes of the properties (such as costing of damage rehabilitation or costing of property demolition) (para. 1.3 & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders)
sig_6f6fe2304e64fbed5991.title: "Inventory, digitisation and exploitation of public real estate under the remit of the Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family" with MIS code 5201221

sig_6fa46e8965737ffb4d50.description: We kindly request your tender for the data transmission service in accordance with this call for tenders, which enables the streaming and downloading of audio publications via a mobile connection in Mainland Finland. The offered service is part of the audio publication listening service we provide with public subsidy. In our customer communications and internally, we use the name Kuuntelukaista for the service. The end-users of our service are visually impaired persons living in Mainland Finland, with an emphasis on persons aged 80 years or over. The data transmission service to be procured provides a continuous IP-based connection from the place of use to the service points defined by the Contracting Authority in the public Internet network. The service is implemented using mobile connections. The service does not include other telecommunications connection services, such as email or homepage. The service package includes mobile data connections with support and management services, as well as optional services that restrict the use of the connection solely to the target addresses in the public network defined by the contracting authority (APN, corporate network, firewall). The contracting authority separately procures operator-independent connection devices compatible with the service. The length of the contract period is 36 months. After the contract period, the contracting authority has the right to extend the contract with 1–2 option periods, the combined maximum duration of which is 24 months.
sig_6fa46e8965737ffb4d50.title: Mobile data connections and their ancillary services

sig_6faa6f10fbc743e93fae.description: This document describes the requirements for the selection and configuration of the LMS, which is in two parts. The fixed scope of this contract is the configuration of an LMS for the preparatory phase and self-study within the regular pathway (core contract). Accordingly, the current system is retained for regular operations, meaning 2 systems are in simultaneous use for the MO training courses: the LMS for the (digital) preparatory phase, and the current system for regular operations. A subsequent, optionally call-off extension to the regular (classroom-led) operations of the MO pathway (optionally call-off extension) is also taken into account. This implies that allowance must already be made in this phase for the requirements of this stage, since the same LMS initially selected for the preparatory phase will also have to be configured for regular operations. The LMS selected now must therefore be demonstrably capable of supporting this extension at a later date, so that expansion to regular operations (optionally call-off extension) can take place under the same award, if desired by the agencies. This document consists of three parts; - Part 1 groups the functional requirements: what the platform must be able to do. - Part 2 groups the non-functional requirements: the quality requirements and preconditions that the platform must meet, including information security and alignment with architecture principles. - Part 3 groups the additional requirements for the optionally call-off extension. The identification codes (A.1, B.2, etc.) enable requirements to be referred to unambiguously throughout this specification, the tenderer's bid and the subsequent contract management.
sig_6faa6f10fbc743e93fae.title: Modular offering - Learning management system for civic integration customer portal abroad

sig_6fd0deb9fef786b17858.description: Plymouth Community Homes (PCH) currently provides payment systems to customers with a well known product suite. Ahead of the full procurement process PCH wish to undertake pre-market engagement to explore supplier options and services available. Initial early engagement with suppliers may be followed by a virtual demonstration to stakeholders from the wider user group. The high-level requirements are split across 4 main areas, listed below. PCH are interested to hear of any developments within each area over the last 5 years, that could provide benefit to PCH and our customers 1) Card Payments: PCI Compliant in person, automated and agent handled payments, in person mobile payments and online payments. 2) Direct Debits: Direct debit collections over multiple collection days/periods. Direct debit payment confirmation/failure of Friday collections is required on Saturday to ensure the accurate calculation or rent balances within our Housing Management system. 3) Post Office and Paypoint Systems: Provision for customers to make payments via barcodes or payment cards. Options around provision of cards for these customers or alternatives. 4) Income Management System: Ability to centrally view and process all payments, including payments received outside of the supplier product suite. The system must provide the ability to export to PCH back-office systems, including the NEC Housing Management System and Open Accounts finance system. Innovative offerings for other complimentary services or substitute methods of delivery are welcome. The existing contract expires in November 2026 and we are looking to enter into a 4 + 2 year contract at an estimated value of £1.2 million Lot 1: .
sig_6fd0deb9fef786b17858.title: Electronic Payment and Income Systems

sig_6fe4d93d280394ca330d.description: Project objectives As part of this project, the aim is to acquire a solution making it possible to implement the intervention management process of SBB Energie, from the intervention request to execution. The tool to be acquired must make it possible to plan and coordinate interventions on high-voltage installations (generation and high-voltage grid) and to generate the documents necessary for these interventions. The final objective is to replace the solution currently in use. Subject of the contract The subject of the acquisition is a market-compliant solution enabling the efficient implementation of the intervention management process for SBB's high-voltage grid and SBB's generation units. The service comprises a proven software from the market, which can be integrated into SBB's existing IT infrastructure and operated there. With the support of SBB, the supplier adapts the software to SBB's needs. This includes both parameterisation and customisation. The supplier assists SBB in the migration from the old to the new system, with data importation for the initial population of the application. The supplier offers training support (Train the Trainer) and provides the corresponding documentation. Once the system is put into service, the supplier provides third-level support. The subject of the contract is fully described in the tender documentation.
sig_6fe4d93d280394ca330d.title: Intervention management EN 2.0

sig_700e5cae934c12a974ad.description: As part of its commitment to reducing water demand and leakage, United Utilities is seeking to engage with the market to better understand the availability and capability of suppliers able to provide specialist onsite support associated with enforcing access to customer premises for the repair of customer‐side leaks. Under Section 75 of the Water Industry Act 1991, United Utilities has a statutory duty to ensure that leakage is repaired as quickly as possible. While established processes exist to notify customers and to support eligible vulnerable customers with leak repairs, there are occasions where access is denied and unresolved leakage presents a continued risk to the environment, third‐party property, and the water network. In such circumstances, United Utilities may obtain a court‐issued warrant to gain access. United Utilities own operational teams will undertake the physical leak repair works; however, additional support is required to coordinate and manage the safe, lawful, and proportionate execution of the warrant onsite. Lot 1: .

sig_701abf3815f1a1223dcc.description:
The contribution service of ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio (hereinafter referred to as "Contribution Service" or "Client" or "AG") intends to replace the existing Db2-z/OS platform with a modern, open target platform based on PostgreSQL in on-premises operation. The subject matter is the technical migration of the existing database and application components without functional changes. The objective is the complete, high-performing and secure executability of all affected applications on PostgreSQL. The eight work packages to be performed by the contractor (AN) within the scope of the overall project are described below. The tasks are to be performed in close cooperation and coordination with the project team of the Contribution Service. 1. Migration of the Db2 database to PostgreSQL - Analysis of the database and development of a migration plan with the aim of transferring the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Migration of the database structure including all relevant database objects incl. tables, indexes, views, triggers. The management of schema changes under PostgreSQL is to be supported by a Liquibase model. Stored procedures are not part of the migration, as their replacement has already taken place. - Migration of data from the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Verification of the correctness of the migration by suitable test procedures. 2. Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements - Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements. - Support of the Client in proving the correct functionality of the applications. - If application errors occur, solution concepts must be developed, coordinated with the Client and implemented to ensure the correct functionality of the applications. In doing so, an adaptation of the application code (e.g., Java in RUBIN) should be avoided if possible. 3. Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database and sizing of the hardware required for on-premises operation - Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database through suitable tuning measures, so that the performance requirements of the Client are met. - Elaboration of a hardware sizing on the basis of which the Contribution Service can procure the hardware required for on-premises operation for the operation of the applications without further conceptual preliminary work. - Proof of compliance with the performance requirements of the Contribution Service by means of suitable test procedures on the hardware procured by the Contribution Service (this is carried out according to the sizing specifications of the AN). 4. Setup of the required system environments and infrastructure as well as design of the required operational processes - Setup of the server infrastructure and the associated system software (operating system, database) using the Ansible Automation Platform. - Setup (installation, integration, establishment of operational readiness) and operation of the required system environments (development, reference, training, test, production) for the individual applications in cooperation with the team of the Contribution Service. - Management of test environments and test data - Documentation of the corresponding procedure and operational processes. - Design and testing of the required operational processes (backup and recovery, system monitoring, etc.). - Transfer of responsibility for these tasks to the Contribution Service team by the milestone "Trial Operation". 5. Development of a tool for pseudonymisation / anonymisation and test data generation - Development or integration of a commercial tool for pseudonymisation/anonymisation of data in accordance with the functional requirements of the Contribution Service. - Development or integration of a commercial tool for the generation of consistent test data (subsets of production data) for development and test environments as well as for performance measurements 6. Qualification of users - Transfer of the necessary integration and operational know-how to the Contribution Service team. - Support and assistance of Contribution Service experts in taking over operational tasks. - Conducting training courses and other qualification measures in the areas of PostgreSQL, operational tools and others. 7. Go-live and support during the start-up phase - Preparation of the go-live of the applications. - Go-live fine planning - Conducting dress rehearsals for the go-live of the applications. - Support of the go-live, standby - hypercare for a period of nine months. 8. Project and release management - The project is organised with project and sub-project management as well as a steering committee. The AN ensures professional project planning, project control and project reporting and establishes risk management appropriate to the risk. - At the project and sub-project level, dual staffing with representatives of the Contribution Service and the AN is planned. - All necessary deadline meetings, workshops, etc. are to be prepared, moderated and documented by the AN. - All results and in particular decisions made are to be documented properly, in detail and comprehensively by the AN. - Templates and models are to be agreed between the Contribution Service and the AN. - The Confluence system or another system provided by the Client is to be used as the project repository. - The AN shall provide for the establishment of a project office (PMO) (however, an on-site establishment at the Contribution Service is not required). The description of the tendered services is continued under section 5.1 of this notice. Continuation of the description of the tendered services from section 2.1 of this notice.

- The project office supports project management on both the Contribution Service and contractor sides for administrative tasks (recording and administrative tasks, information preparation and distribution, planning tasks, report preparation, etc.). - The AN provides release management to coordinate the further development of the applications by the Contribution Service and the migration activities over the course of the approx. three-year project duration. The following services are not the subject of this tender: - Provision of the PostgreSQL database software, operating system software - Procurement of the hardware and system technology required for operation. - Procurements of tools and software tools required by the Client for the operation of the systems beyond the end of the project or permanently. It is intended, provided that a sufficient number of applications to participate by suitable tenderers is received, to limit the number of tenderers who will be invited to submit tenders in the subsequent negotiation procedure to three suitable tenderers. Unsuccessful tenderers will be informed in writing of their elimination. The restriction of the circle of tenderers is based on objective, non-discriminatory criteria (cf. this notice and Part A. Conditions of Participation of the Participation Brochure) The Contribution Service will suspend the negotiation procedure for a period of 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation over the turn of the year. The selected bidders will receive information before the suspension of the procedure that they belong to the limited circle of bidders. In addition, the Contribution Service will inform them via the communication function of the dtvp procurement marketplace about the resumption of the negotiation procedure and the provision of the tender documents as well as the invitation to submit initial tenders on the dtvp procurement marketplace. The procurement procedure will be continued with at least one negotiation round for 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the previously described suspension of the procedure. The awarding authority will only invite the three selected suitable bidders to submit an initial tender based on the detailed tender documents including a detailed description of services. In addition, for quality assurance purposes, the implementation of a 2-month pitch is planned. Bidders will receive technical documents, test data without production reference as well as selected SQLs and code snippets, carry out an exemplary trial migration, analyse risks and outline (partial) solution concepts including procedures for hardware sizing. The pitch fee is 20.000 euros net. The pitch results feed into the quality evaluation. Further details on the pitch as well as the concrete schedule for the implementation of the pitch and the parallel preparation of the initial tenders can be found in the tender documents, which will be made available to the bidders belonging to the limited circle of bidders after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the 2-month procedure suspension via the invitation to submit the initial tender on the dtvp procurement marketplace. SELECTION OF THE LIMITED CIRCLE OF BIDDERS The Contribution Service will select a maximum of 3 bidders for the negotiation procedure. If more than 3 applicants are suitable after checking the applications to participate, the selection will be made on the basis of the following objective criteria: The Contribution Service will award a maximum of 200 points for the reference list submitted by the applicant. Within the framework of awarding the maximum 100 points per specified migration reference, the Contribution Service will exclusively base its decision on the two reference contracts of the applicant that were confirmed by the reference client during the reference check, meet the specified minimum requirements and achieved the highest score during the evaluation. In the event that more than three applicants belong to the restricted circle of applicants due to an equal number of points, all these applicants with the same score will also be invited to submit a tender. In detail, the awarding of points is based on the following criteria: a) Comparability of the source system in the reference project (15 points) - Replacement of a DB2 database from a mainframe system: 15 points b) Data volume of the reference project related to structured data (max. 30 points) - > 2 TB (minimum requirement) to 5 TB: 10 points - > 5 TB to 10 TB: 20 points - > 10 TB: 30 points c) Technical complexity of the data model and application logic (max. 40 points) - High data integrity: The migration included a data model with high referential integrity with foreign keys: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using triggers: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using views: 5 points - High application binding: The migration included the adaptation of embedded SQL: 5 points - Combined technical complexity: In addition, it is evaluated whether the migration required a combination of the above-mentioned techniques. Full points will be awarded if the migration included the cumulative application of foreign keys and triggers and views: 20 points d) Scope of operational responsibility in the reference project (max. 10 points) - Operational responsibility for 3 (minimum requirement) to 6 months: 5 points - Operational responsibility for > 6 months to 12 months: 10 points e) Type of client in the reference project (max. 5 points) - Client from the private sector: 0 points - Public sector client: 5 points Further details on the competition for participation can be found in the participation brochure provided on the dtvp procurement marketplace.

sig_703bc52bb1859f6cf4fb.description: Göng&Brú is a new Icelandic State-owned infrastructure company established to finance, build, own, operate and maintain major transport infrastructure of national economic importance, constituted under the Act on Innvidafélag enacted by the Icelandic Parliament on 18 June 2026. It follows the model of comparable State-owned infrastructure companies in the Nordic region, including Sund & Bælt in Denmark and Iceland’s own experience with the Hvalfjörður tunnel. It will operate at arm’s length from the Government, on a commercial and self-sustaining basis. Göng&Brú’s initial portfolio represents a capital programme in excess of EUR 1.5 billion, encompassing the Sundabraut arterial route in Reykjavík, a second bore of the Hvalfjörður sub-sea tunnel, the forward financing of the new Ölfusárbrú bridge, and the Fljótagöng Tunnel, with further projects to follow under the 2026–2040 National Transportation Plan. Together these projects represent a multiyear capital programme of substantial scale. This notice is published as part of a Pre-Market Engagement (PME) exercise conducted prior to any formal procurement process. The PME allows Göng&Brú to refine its thinking on scope, procurement structure and market appetite, and gives interested organisations an early opportunity to help shape the approach. The PME comprises three elements. First, interested organisations may request the PME Information Document and questionnaire, which sets out background on Göng&Brú and its programme and invites structured written responses. Second, an Open Day will be held in Reykjavík on 17 September 2026, at which further information will be presented and introductory meetings with the Göng&Brú project team will be available. Third, following review of questionnaire responses, Göng&Brú may invite selected organisations to participate in individual one-to-one discussions on a confidence-protected basis. Göng&Brú is seeking to appoint a Client Side Support Team (CSST) to act as its exclusive client side advisory partner with the potential to support the full life of the programme. During the term of appointment, the CSST will be expected to work exclusively with Göng&Brú and will not hold any role with any contractor, designer, financer, or other supply chain participant on any of the projects to be delivered through the Programme. The CSST will be responsible for providing Göng&Brú with the breadth and depth of expertise necessary to act as an informed, capable, and commercially astute buyer across all stages of each project delivered through the Programme, from early development and financing through to construction, commissioning, and operations. Prior to launching a formal procurement process, Göng&Brú is inviting market input to inform and refine its thinking on project scope, delivery structures and procurement strategy. Whilst this PME is focused on the CSST Procurement (as this will be the first procurement to formally come to market), Göng&Brú would be interested to receive questionnaire responses from any organisations that might see themselves potentially competing to be involved in this wider investment programme from any perspective, whether that be as a supplier, funder or a contractor. Notwithstanding this, please note that future PME exercises, focused on other future contracts, will likely be launched in forthcoming months and years. Göng&Brú is keen to receive market views on which services should fall within the CSST scope, which should be retained in-house, and whether any services are missing or should be structured differently. Göng&Brú is at an early stage of developing its procurement strategy but its current preliminary thinking is that it would appoint a single integrated CSST partner; and use a procurement procedure that allows meaningful dialogue with bidders to refine the scope and delivery approach before contract award.
sig_703bc52bb1859f6cf4fb.title: Pre-Market Engagement regarding the appointment of a Client Side Support Team (CSST)

sig_7045af439be9eef5607e.description: The subject of the procurement is a purchasing and purchase invoice processing system. The purchasing and purchase invoice processing system must support the City of Tampere's order-to-pay process and act as a core tool in process management, contract utilisation, financial monitoring, and the generation of procurement data. The role of the system is to enable transparent, traceable, and data-driven procurement processes, as well as to streamline manual work across the various stages of purchasing and purchase invoice processing. The system must ensure that purchases are directed to the correct contracts and suppliers, and that order approval, account coding, and monitoring take place consistently. Purchase invoice processing covers the electronic receipt, matching, verification, approval, account coding, and monitoring of purchase invoices throughout the processing lifecycle. The system must support the processing of both purchase-order-based and non-order-based purchase invoices, enable the use of automation and rule-based guidance, and ensure the accuracy, timeliness, and consistency of invoice processing. Purchase invoice processing must integrate seamlessly with purchasing, contracts, and financial monitoring so that data relating to invoices can be utilised in reporting and data-driven management. The core objectives of the purchasing system are: 1. Purchasing that reinforces data-driven management, transparency, and open data: The system produces structured and comparable procurement data and enables a transparent and traceable order-to-pay process that can be utilised in city-level and national-level reporting and analytics. 2. Process streamlining and reduction of manual work: A modern purchasing system automates repetitive work steps, streamlines the processing of orders and purchase invoices, and ensures consistent operating methods, thereby reducing manual work and improving overall process efficiency. 3. Increasing the purchase order rate and contract-compliant purchasing: The system directs purchases to tendered contracts and ensures that purchase orders are used systematically in all procurements, supporting the target of raising the City's purchase order rate to 90 %. 4. Process accuracy and compliance with instructions: The system ensures compliance with procurement legislation and the City's procurement and ordering instructions, handles preliminary control of the budget and appropriations, and reinforces the consistency and accuracy of the entire process. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE The contracting authority wishes to carry out a technical dialogue regarding the procurement in two parts: 1. 22-4-8.5 functional and non-functional requirements of the system 2. 27.5.-18.6 system requirements and contract terms The contracting authority wishes to verify market solutions and its own requirements through the technical dialogue. If you are able to offer a purchasing and purchase invoice processing system solution, register for the technical dialogue by 30.4 at the email address hankinnat@tampere.fi. You may use "Registration for technical dialogue/procurement of purchasing and purchase invoice processing" as the subject line of the message. We will deliver the materials and related detailed information in a reply message.
sig_7045af439be9eef5607e.title: System solution for purchasing and purchase invoice processing

sig_70502745d6059e59ae54.description: LAAT is a strong, outward-facing multi-academy Trust that operates within Greater Lincolnshire. We are committed to transforming lives through education and believe that every child has inherent potential. We strive to ensure we have the very best colleagues in our settings, well supported by their school-based colleagues, Leaders, and wider network of schools, as well as a dedicated central team of experts. The Lincoln Anglican Academy Trust (LAAT) is a Trust of 24 Lincolnshire, North East Lincolnshire and North Lincolnshire Primary/Infant Schools and one Secondary school (William Lovell). The Trust is characterised by the fact the majority of the schools are either in market towns or more rural areas. Underpinning this for all schools are the strong family links between the members of the LAAT itself and the objectives of the Diocesan family. LAAT is dedicated to supporting school improvement and Christian distinctiveness, whilst maintaining each school as a special and unique place in the heart of its unique context. Since it was established LAAT has demonstrated its ability to provide excellent school improvement and back office support to its schools, taking the majority to Ofsted Good. OUR VISION Our Excellence, Exploration and Encouragement powered by Equity vision statement encapsulates the Trust we are today and the Trust we aspire to be in the future. It has meaningful resonance with the work we do and our commitment to overcoming the social inequality faced by our children and young people. We are passionate about improving the life chances of every child in our care, meeting them where they are. Grounded in faith, we seek to see and understand all in our diverse communities and beyond. Every pupil has the right to flourish; academically, physically, emotionally, and spiritually, through an educational experience based on Excellence, Exploration and Encouragement. Every pupil has the right to receive what they need. And every child will need different things at different times. Providing this, is Equity at work. Excellence, Exploration and Encouragement powered by Equity. The LAAT Website is https://thelaat.co.uk The Trust has an ambitious Digital Strategy Plan which includes the 1:1 provision of devices to pupils (https://thelaat.co.uk/digital-strategy/). The new connectivity solution needs to cater for the current requirements that a modern, connected Trust requires and also allow for the anticipated increase in usage that the digital strategy promotes. The Trust estimates that it may grow by another 5 small to medium size schools over the life of this contract. This procurement encompasses a full outsource of all the connectivity and associated security services, such as firewalls and protection from cyber-attacks. At a high level the key deliverables are: • A managed connectivity service to connect schools anywhere in England • A broadband service for each school that meets (as a minimum) DfE guidelines and enables the Trust to deliver on its ambitious digital strategy. • A 'failover' line • A firewalled service • Support and maintenance service • Full end to end single SLA approach • Management of any 3rd parties required to provide the service • Relevant monitoring, management, and reporting • Full installation and transition service • Value added services • A commitment to open, transparent and timely communications with both with the Trust and their IT Support provider Technical interface into the Trusts outsourced support provision. From the Trust's point of view, the successful bidder should be prepared to work directly with the Trust's ICT Managed Service Provider to resolve any issues and/or requests. To all intents and purposes, the MSP should be viewed as 'part of the Trust'. Web filtering is not required as part of this solution - this is managed by the Trust's ICT support provider. For the avoidance of doubt telephony is not included in this procurement, but the solution must support the current VoIP solution. Bidders should note the following: • The Trust will provide a standard contract as part of the ITT Pack • There will not be a requirement for TUPE from existing suppliers. Further details about the solution requirements will be provided to those bidders who are shortlisted to receive the ITT pack. Lot 1: .
