sig_73efc516cfd176ec674f.description:
This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) includes the procurement of digital services, products and technologies intended for the revitalisation, optimisation and development of capacities in the fields of digital transformation and R&D&I of the Navarre ecosystem, under the conditions established in the Regulatory Conditions, throughout the entire validity of the DPS. The system includes different themes, each constituting a different category. Microsoft 365 is considered a suite of productivity applications, a fundamental axis in the digital transformation and creation of a collaborative work culture and organisational information in the entities that adopt it. Included in this category are the services of implementation, evolution, training, consulting, parameterisation, documentation, methodologies and procedures, design and support, relating to the use in Public Administrations of the Microsoft 365 suite and all its components and applications. Likewise, the services necessary to guarantee compliance with the regulatory, data protection and information security requirements applicable to the platform and information management (including, where applicable, ENS and GDPR) are included, encompassing the definition and application of governance policies, classification and information protection (for example, sensitivity labelling, data loss prevention and retention/preservation), as well as verification and audit activities that prove necessary within the scope of the service. Advanced security services are specifically incorporated that encompass identity management, critical migrations and the guarantee of regulatory compliance in the corporate environment, as well as the execution of configurations, deployments, integrations, audits, migrations and Tenant mergers. Although the scope includes any application that forms part of the M365 suite, process automation via Power Platform is explicitly mentioned, including the development and governance of Power Apps and Power Automate solutions intended to digitise the workflows of the Administration. Likewise, technical preparation, data security and deployment of productive AI solutions are integrated, specifically Microsoft 365 Copilot, together with the implementation of standard conversational agents.; To address a digitisation or innovation process, either from an optimisation or transformational point of view, the strategic definition of the process and the definition of the processes themselves (governance, control, execution, implementation, cultural change...) become essential. Therefore, strategic and technological consulting and engineering services, process diagnosis and evaluation, organisational, coordination and platform models, as well as the drafting of Strategic Plans and Digital Agendas are included in this category. The definition of IT governance models to ensure the control and direction of resources, work planning, measurement of the impact of digitisation, definition of operating models and strategies for the implementation of optimisation, innovation and digital transformation processes are also integrated. Specifically, this category incorporates adoption, training and change management services to ensure digital culture and the use of technologies, through the design and execution of training and digital training plans. Likewise, the implementation of business solutions based on market platforms (CRM, ERP, BPM, etc.) and Low-Code solutions (non-Microsoft) that do not require custom software development is included. Services relating to the management and revitalisation of support centres, customer service and citizen service are also included. Services relating to industrial projects concerning data processing and capture and artificial intelligence are also included. Similarly, this category incorporates ad-hoc technical assistance services aimed at the revitalisation of the Navarrese and state research, development and innovation (R&D&I) ecosystem, with a special focus on boosting digital innovation, infrastructures and the use of enabling technologies for the entire territory of the Foral Community, contributing to the strengthening of the competitiveness of the economic and technological fabric of Navarre.; Data management is a fundamental topic in optimisation and digital transformation processes, as public administrations must move towards a data-driven governance model. Thus, this category includes strategic data consulting services throughout its entire lifecycle, encompassing the design of on-premise and cloud platform architecture (datalake, data warehouse, data hub), and governance, metadata and catalogue design strategies. It is now structured into areas of specialisation ranging from strategic, ethical and data office consulting, focused on maturity models and privacy-by-design compliance, to training and methodology to provide entities with the necessary understanding in AI algorithm techniques, data science and the development of analytical and predictive models. In the field of infrastructure and interoperability, the lot incorporates the deployment of data spaces, through the implementation of nodes and connectors based on international standards such as IDS or GAIA-X for the sovereign sharing of data. This allows the creation of federated data ecosystems between administrations and third parties, guaranteeing the technical and semantic interoperability necessary for modern data governance.

To ensure the success of these ecosystems, technical training services in sovereignty standards and specific adoption plans are included to facilitate the incorporation of new participants into data spaces, guaranteeing that the actors involved understand trust models and exchange mechanisms. Likewise, data-based decision systems and the ethical regulation of algorithms are envisaged, ensuring access control, privacy and security at all times. Finally, the category is oriented towards analytical exploitation and artificial intelligence (AI) to extract maximum value from available information. This includes visual analytics and BI services for the development of interactive dashboards and data storytelling on market platforms, as well as the implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) solutions based on LLMs and model fine-tuning. All of this is complemented by training workshops and data collection and processing methodologies, ensuring that Nasertic's IT services infrastructure evolves towards competitive and secure solutions.; Cloud services and products that are a way to deploy infrastructures, software and platforms quickly, scalably and efficiently. Included in this category are consulting services, including the design, deployment and implementation of SaaS (software as a service), IaaS (infrastructure as a service) and PaaS (platform as a service) cloud solutions. Also included are consulting and advisory services for procurement, support, compliance, security, ethics, regulatory compliance and standards (ENS, GDPR, etc.) as well as data location.; The data centre is the nerve centre of companies' and public administrations' IT resources. Maintaining an updated data centre and simplifying IT management is a core part of the digital transformation process. Evolving the IT infrastructure with innovative, efficient and strategic solutions is an obligation for systems to remain competitive. Included in this category are technical assistance services for planning, situation and location analysis, relocation, expansion, creation, conceptual design, detailed design and executive project, security audits, implementation, secure data centre infrastructures, maintenance, construction management, requirements study, technical project management, preparation of security plans and adaptations for regulatory compliance, management and monitoring of facilities, works management, commissioning, and any study, project or report relating to data centre facilities, as well as covering the entire lifecycle management of mission-critical technological infrastructure support.; It includes consulting, development, product acquisition and support services necessary for the evolution, maintenance and modernisation of information systems of public administration entities, within the framework of their digital transformation processes. This category covers the design, analysis, construction, implementation, integration, maintenance and continuous improvement of software solutions adapted to business needs, aimed at guaranteeing efficient, scalable, secure systems aligned with technological and organisational changes. Included are, among others, the following services: -IT consulting services for the definition of architectures, technological strategies and systems modernisation processes. -Functional and technical analysis of applications. -Corrective and evolutive maintenance of existing applications. -Design, development and implementation of new ad hoc applications. -Integration of applications and systems in heterogeneous environments. -Support, maintenance and operation of software infrastructures. -Acquisition of software products necessary for the evolution of information systems. The solutions contemplated may be based on various technologies and environments, including, among others: -Modern technologies for cross-platform application development, such as React, React Native, Node.js, TypeScript and associated technologies, which allow the creation of modular, reusable, scalable solutions adapted to constantly evolving business environments. -Microsoft technologies such as .NET, VB and VBA, both in client-server environments and in web environments, widely implemented in public administration and with a solid track record in the development and maintenance of information systems. In this context, services associated with the complete software lifecycle on these technologies are also contemplated, including consulting, analysis, development, implementation, integration and support of solutions built on them. Overall, this category comprehensively covers the needs for the evolution and modernisation of information systems, facilitating the digital transformation of public organisations through the use of consolidated and emerging technologies.; Participation in competitive funding calls for research, development and innovation (R&D&I) and digitalisation projects constitutes a key element to boost technological development, innovation and collaboration between public entities, research centres, companies and other agents of the innovation ecosystem. Included in this category is the provision of specialised technical assistance services for the identification of funding opportunities and comprehensive support in the preparation of competitive project proposals, both in regional, national and international calls.

In particular, the following services are envisaged: ✓Project proposal preparation: Support services in the preparation and drafting of project proposals led or participated in by NASERTIC for grant applications in competitive calls in the field of R&D&I and digitalisation. These services include the preparation of technical reports, the definition of the project scope, the structuring of work packages, the definition of impact indicators, as well as the preparation of the documentation necessary for the submission of the proposal. Likewise, the collection and compilation of administrative, legal and financial information required by the different calls is included, the completion of forms and submission platforms, the review of the technical and budgetary consistency of the proposal, as well as the submission of the dossier and monitoring of the evaluation process until the resolution of the call. ✓Consortium formation: Services for the identification and search of potential partners for the constitution of consortia in collaborative projects, including public entities, companies, technology centres, universities or other agents of the innovation ecosystem. These services comprise the identification of partners aligned with the project idea, the establishment of initial contacts, the dynamisation of collaboration between the different participants and the use of national and international innovation networks of the consulting entity for the formation of competitive consortia.; The execution of projects financed in competitive R&D&I and digitalisation calls requires adequate technical, administrative and financial management that guarantees the correct development of the planned activities and compliance with the requirements established by the funding entities. Included in this category is the provision of technical and administrative support services for the comprehensive management of competitive projects in which NASERTIC participates, including the coordination of activities, monitoring of technical execution, document management and compliance with justification and control requirements established in the funding calls. In particular, the following services are envisaged: ✓Comprehensive project management Support and technical assistance services throughout the project lifecycle, including support in the planning and coordination of activities, organisation and monitoring of project meetings, supervision of compliance with milestones and deliverables, as well as coordination of NASERTIC's participation in the different work packages. Likewise, tasks of support in the administrative management of the project, preparation of monitoring reports, coordination with consortium partners and liaison with funding entities when necessary are included. ✓Technical, administrative and economic justification Support services for the preparation and drawing up of the technical, administrative and economic justification processes for financed projects, including the collection of necessary information by NASERTIC, the preparation of technical reports, the preparation of justification reports and the organisation of the documentation required for its submission within established deadlines. ✓Assistance in inspection and audit processes Support services during review, inspection or audit processes associated with financed projects, including the preparation of required documentation, accompaniment during verification visits or external audits, as well as technical assistance in responding to requirements or information requests from funding entities.; NASERTIC as an instrumental entity of the Government of Navarre, whose corporate purpose is the provision of horizontal services and technology required by Public Administrations, bodies, companies or entities dependent on them, is in charge of managing telecommunications infrastructures and services. Among the technological infrastructures and platforms managed by Nasertic are telecommunication centres and Government of Navarre sites from which telecommunications services are provided to citizens. This lot includes the procurement of various technical assistance and/or training services in different technological fields related to: Telecommunication Centres and auxiliary infrastructures: Technical assistance work or training services related to improvement, evolution or innovation in the infrastructures of telecommunication centres and auxiliary elements for their operation, including processes and tools oriented towards their management and supervision, shall be considered.” Technical Assistance Technical assistance intended to provide targeted and specialised support to Nasertic's technical staff in relation to the maintenance and/or evolution of infrastructures or technological solutions linked to the management of the telecommunication centres and auxiliary infrastructures described. Technical assistance may include: • AUDIT SERVICES: Consulting services for carrying out audits on the state of conservation or operability of infrastructures and technological platforms, including aspects relating to performance analysis, lifecycle analysis or equipment obsolescence status, regulatory compliance with technical standards and norms, legislation, compliance, security and information processing, etc.

• ADVISORY SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN OF INFRASTRUCTURES, TECHNOLOGICAL SERVICES AND SOLUTIONS: Provision of technical assistance services aimed at ensuring the technological updating, evolution and continuous improvement of technological infrastructures and platforms, including specialised consultancy on evolution plans, preparation of improvement proposals, operational procedures or methods of action, analysis or implementation of new functionalities, or engineering or structural sizing tasks. • TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE SERVICES FOR PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION: Provision of technical assistance services for requirements analysis, conceptual or detailed design, deployment and implementation of infrastructures and/or technological solutions in any of the included areas, which do not form part of the standard support of infrastructures or systems in production nor are they linked to ongoing SDC incidents in digital transformation, innovation and promotion of R&D&I of the Navarrese ecosystem 17. It also includes technical assistance work related to the documentation and/or inventory of installations. It also includes technical assistance services for the preparation of plans and/or projects for regulatory compliance, legalisation of installations, and safety and health plans. They may take the form of on-site assistance ("in situ") when the intervention requires the presence of technical personnel from the successful tenderer at NASERTIC's facilities or at defined locations, or remote assistance for analysis, detailed technical diagnosis, or actions on new developments, exclusively using the connection mechanisms enabled by NASERTIC. It likewise includes the provision of technical assistance services linked to participation in innovation projects, the definition, support, testing and validation of new technological solutions, the carrying out of pilot projects, testing and validation of pre-production environments, etc. Training Includes training services related to the management of the described infrastructures, the exploration and/or adoption of new infrastructures or technological solutions applicable to their management, including regulated training, training workshops, or the design of training plans or actions upon Nasertic's request. Training may include: • Training actions aimed at Nasertic's technical personnel, necessary for the correct management of the infrastructures, described technological platforms, or functionalities introduced as part of their implementation or evolution. • Official training or manufacturer certifications, adapted to the technologies and requirements demanded by Nasertic. • Specialised training based on specific needs in each case.; NASERTIC, as an instrumental entity of the Government of Navarre, is responsible for managing infrastructures and telecommunications services based on radio waves with which certain services are provided both to the Government of Navarre and to public bodies, companies or entities dependent on them, including the provision of broadcasting services, fundamentally the DTT broadcasting service in zone II of the Foral Community of Navarre or point-to-point radio transport and connectivity services. This category includes the procurement of various technical assistance and/or training services in different technological fields related to infrastructures and radio wave communication systems, including radio and television broadcasting services and/or platforms and the auxiliary infrastructures necessary therefor, among which are: the design, calculation, implementation, legalisation and evolution of necessary infrastructures or services related to the transport and broadcasting (broadcast) of radio and/or television signals, coverage studies and video compression and coding systems and standards, modulation techniques, etc. This category includes the procurement of both technical assistance and training services. Technical Assistance Technical assistance intended to provide targeted and specialised support to Nasertic's technical personnel in relation to services, technological solutions, infrastructures, or systems supporting the management of radio and television broadcasting services and infrastructures, evolution, development of new functionalities, or implementation of new services, infrastructures, or technological platforms. Technical assistance may include: •AUDIT SERVICES: Consultancy services for carrying out audits on the state of conservation or operability of infrastructures and technological platforms, including aspects related to performance analysis, life cycle analysis or equipment obsolescence status, regulatory compliance with technical standards and norms, legislation, quality standards, compliance, security and information processing, etc. •ADVISORY SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN OF INFRASTRUCTURES, TECHNOLOGICAL SERVICES AND SOLUTIONS: Provision of technical assistance services aimed at ensuring the technological updating, evolution and continuous improvement of services, infrastructures and technological platforms, including specialised consultancy on evolution plans, technical knowledge, specific analysis or preparation of improvement proposals, configuration, sizing, operational procedures or methods of action, analysis or implementation of new functionalities, redesigns, additional developments, or engineering or structural sizing tasks.

•TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE SERVICES FOR PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION: Provision of technical assistance services for requirements analysis, conceptual or detailed design, deployment and implementation of technological solutions in any of the areas, as well as the implementation of new configurations and technical developments, carried out by the successful tenderer at the request of NASERTIC, which do not form part of the standard support of platforms or systems in production nor are they linked to ongoing incidents. It also includes technical assistance work related to the documentation and/or inventory of installations. It also includes technical assistance services

sig_741727823f1da7b2b39b.description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code § 4001, 10 U.S.C. § 4021, 10 U.S.C. § 4022, and 10 U.S.C. § 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: • Acoustic communication and sensing • Adaptability • Advanced computing • Additive manufacturing • Architecture and advanced systems engineering • Artificial intelligence • Autonomy and control algorithms • Combat identification • Command and control (C2) • Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive • Complexity management • Critical infrastructure defense • Decision aids and C2 technology • DevOps and novel software development and integration • Directed energy (DE) • Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) • Economic security • Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) • Electro-optic/infrared sensors • Electromagnetic warfare (EW) • High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing • High voltage electric power systems and architecture • Human behavior modeling • Human-machine symbiosis • Industrial engineering • Integration and reliability technologies • Interoperability • Logistics • Modeling and simulation • Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing • Novel kinetic effects • Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) • Optical technologies • Photonics • Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) • Radar and adaptive arrays • Resilient systems • Robotics • Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing • Sensors and analytics • Signal processing • Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) • Strategy analysis technology • Supply chain analytics • System of systems • Undersea and seabed technology • Tactics development technology • Testing and data collection • Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology • Very low frequency (VLF) technology
sig_741727823f1da7b2b39b.title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement

sig_74bf9e0983dde9f52d7a.description: The subject of the procurement is a self-care equipment system for the use of Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala, which is procured as a comprehensive service provided by the system supplier. Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala produces well-being, health and safety for the people of Helsinki with strong expertise and cooperation. Health and substance abuse services are one of the city's social and health service entities. It takes care of primary health care outpatient services and adult health counselling at health stations, internal medicine outpatient clinic activities, emergency services and oral health care. The service entity also produces mental health and substance abuse services for adults as well as psychiatric specialist medical care services. The City of Helsinki's self-care equipment distribution is a service produced by the health and substance abuse service entity, which distributes free-of-charge care equipment needed for personal medical care to the city's residents under section 24 of the Health Care Act. Free-of-charge care equipment is provided for the treatment of an illness when the patient has needed them for the treatment of their illness for at least three months. Exceptions are needs resulting from a permanent illness, for example diabetes, catheter and stoma patients, for whose treatment self-care equipment can be provided from the very beginning of the illness. The City of Helsinki's self-care equipment distribution customer and order volumes have grown over the years and the currently used order processing and inventory management system developed on top of SAP software has reached the end of its life cycle. Operations are currently centralised in one location, where approximately 15 employees work, from the chief physician to warehouse workers. The subject of the procurement is an information system that replaces the current order processing and inventory management system implemented with SAP software. The information system must include software suitable for the management of referrals, customer relationships and self-care equipment, which is referred to in the document as the self-care equipment system. The entity must also include both a customer portal enabling customer orders and a mobile ordering possibility for equipment for home care employees working with customers. In connection with the implementation of the information system that is the subject of the procurement, the operating model of the self-care equipment distribution will be changed so that in the future, the City of Helsinki's service company Stara's logistics centre will be responsible for inventory management and deliveries. Self-care equipment distribution professionals will in the future focus on the processing of self-care equipment referrals, customer order management and customer service. The self-care equipment system to be procured must be integrated into Stara's SAP system regarding the product catalogue and deliveries. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.
sig_74bf9e0983dde9f52d7a.title: Self-care supplies system

sig_74c799560328d6793623.description: Nest is seeking to appoint one supplier to provide, implement and support one hosted software-as-a-service solution for Nest Invest, comprising two mandatory capabilities: Asset Allocation and Total Portfolio View. The Asset Allocation capability must support Nest Invest’s multi-level fund-of-funds structure and its controlled, model-driven asset allocation process. This includes strategic and tactical asset allocation, portfolio modelling and optimisation, configurable targets, limits and tolerances, portfolio rebalancing, asset restrictions, workflow and approval controls, auditability, scenario analysis and the generation of implementation instructions or outputs for downstream parties. The Total Portfolio View capability must provide a consolidated view of Nest Invest’s portfolio across public and private assets, including positions, exposures, performance and look-through information where available. It must support aggregation and analysis across Nest Invest’s fund structure. The supplier will be required to provide software licensing or subscription services; implementation and configuration; integration with retained data sources and Nest Invest’s planned cloud data platform through appropriate data interfaces and APIs; transition and migration from the incumbent IRP solution; testing and user acceptance support; training and documentation; go-live and transition support; and ongoing hosting, maintenance, technical support and product-roadmap services. The solution must be configured for Nest Invest and supplied electronically as a hosted service. Investment and portfolio data will be received from retained sources, including the fund administrator and custodian, and the solution must generate the required information, reporting and implementation outputs for Nest Invest and its downstream processes. The contract will be awarded to one supplier for an initial term of five years. Nest may extend the contract for an additional two years and subsequently for a further one year, giving a maximum potential term of eight years. The contract does not guarantee any minimum volume of services or minimum expenditure. Lot 1: . None

sig_74e425fa6c77c71422c9.description: The subject of the contract is support services aimed at identifying the best strategy for enhancing the value of properties owned by or in the investment pipeline of the Funds. In particular, the services include carrying out the following activities: i. framing the macroeconomic scenario of the reference territory; ii. territorial framing and analysis aimed at highlighting the critical success factors and risk areas of the locations from a commercial point of view: study of the location of the properties (macro and micro-location), analysis of the local urban fabric, analysis of strategic urban and real estate transformation scenarios at a local and supra-local level; iii. demand analysis in terms of the size and socio-demographic characteristics of the population residing in the settlement context; iv. identification of the Target User; v. market and supply analysis which, depending on the urban planning situation and current regulations, the location and the market potential of each area, provides a market analysis aimed at identifying the intended uses that can determine the greatest value for the property; vi. identification of the optimal functional mix that can guarantee the maximisation of expected returns and the minimisation of commercial risk; vii. identification of tenants/investors potentially interested in the various components of the initiative; viii. definition of the Product Concept: identification of the intended use, definition of the internal layout (division of internal spaces and possible redetermination of the single, double, triple, etc. room sizes of residential buildings); proposal of materials, finishes, furnishings to be provided according to the Target User, etc.; ix. identification of the procedures and urban planning standards necessary for any procedures for changing the building and/or urban planning destination of the property and calculation of the related charges; x. definition of the best property enhancement strategy (Highest and Best Use) and analysis of the level of rents and achievable exit values and the relative timelines for achievement. sig_74f045a196a0670014b3.description: ONS are to looking explore delivery model options for the collection of local price data across the UK. We are keen to understand what data collection and technology solutions are available. We would like to speak to suppliers to discuss their ideas for delivery models, as well as the benefits and limitations of these approaches. About the Office for National Statistics (ONS) ONS is the UK's largest independent producer of official statistics and is the National Statistical Institute for the UK. Formally, it is the executive office of the UK Statistics Authority, a non-Ministerial Department established by the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. It is responsible for collecting and publishing statistics related to the economy, population, and society at national, regional, and local levels. ONS plays a leading role in national and international good practice in the production of official statistics. Introduction The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is initiating preliminary market engagement ahead of the future procurement of Local Price Collection service delivery. The local collection is vital to produce CPI, CPIH and RPI statistics. These consumer price inflation statistics are important indicators of how the UK economy is performing. They are used in many ways by individuals, government, businesses, and academics. Inflation statistics impact on everyone, as they influence interest rates, tax allowances, benefits, pensions, savings rates, maintenance contracts, and many other payments. Collection takes place across 141 UK locations through around 300 field collectors every month under the Local Price Collection's current operating model. The delivery of this service is currently outsourced to a commercial provider. ONS is seeking to establish a contract with an organisation that can provide some or all the following services to ensure continuity of service and explore opportunities for innovation, improved data quality, efficiency, continuous improvement, and resilience. 1. Delivery of data collection service involving: -Recruitment, training, and management of a geographically dispersed workforce. -Oversight of operations involving hundreds of collectors undertaking one week of collection per month. -Collection of item prices in outlets across specific locations -Maintaining adherence to collection requirements 2. Data handling, management, and security involving: -Ensuring awareness of security requirements and working alongside ONS security team to gain approval that meets expected standards of data and security governance -Secure transfer of collected data through encrypted channels and controlled devices which adhere to legal and ONS requirements -Integrate with ONS' existing cloud‐based pipelines, validation processes, and monthly schedules 3.Quality Assurance of data and ensuring service continuity involving -Compliance with key performance indicators to ensure complete and accurate data is delivered -Commitment to quality indicators aligned with The Government Data Quality Framework -Timely delivery of data to meet monthly processing schedules -Establishing and maintaining robust quality controls -Support ONS in service delivery risk management, business continuity, and delivery contingency planning -Meet parallel run requirements during transition period 4.Innovation and continuous improvement throughout the lifetime of the contract involving -Reviewing and enhancing processes to identify improvements including to data quality and operational efficiency -Remaining aware of innovative technologies and software, and collection methods to explore applications to benefit service delivery -Proactively produce plans and timelines to carry trials for future enhancements for example supporting transformation work. ONS have questions related to the above requirements that we would like to ask prospective suppliers. This will help inform tender requirements. Initially we would be interested to hear thoughts on the questions below. -ONS are to looking explore delivery model options for the collection of local price data across the UK. What delivery model would you recommend for a national field collection operation? -How would you support this recommended delivery model? -How would you ensure innovation and continuous improvement? Lot 1: .

sig_7517f8a4b1fe027a93a1.description: Business North East is a new region-wide approach to business support developed by the North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) in partnership with the seven constituent local authorities. It will provide a simplified, coordinated and accessible business support system for entrepreneurs and businesses across the North East, supporting business The model will include a regional hub, use local authority network to maintaining strong relationships with businesses. The wider Business North East programme is expected to operate through five integrated areas of activity across the business lifecycle: Inspire - increase entrepreneurial awareness and aspiration, particularly amongst younger people and underrepresented groups. Explore - improve enterprise readiness and strengthen the quality of business propositions entering the support system. Start - increase business creation and improve business survival prospects through tailored support and business development assistance. Succeed - improve productivity, innovation, technology adoption and business resilience amongst established businesses. Grow - support ambitious businesses to scale, create jobs, access finance and enter new markets. The North East MSA intends to establish a framework to provide a flexible route through which a range of specialist business support, enterprise and related services may be commissioned in support of Business North East and wider regional economic priorities. It is anticipated that the framework will encompass a broad range of services, across five separate Lots: 1. Enterprise, Entrepreneurship and Business Start-up 2. Business Growth, Productivity and Specialist Support 3. High Growth, Scale-up and Investment 4. Sector, Cluster and Supply Chain Development 5. Business Engagement, Training and Programme Support These areas reflect the anticipated breadth of Business North East, which is intended to respond to business needs including access to finance, productivity, workforce development, innovation, digital adoption, mentoring and growth support. The Framework is intended to enable the North East MSA and constituent local authorities to identify suitably qualified suppliers with the capability and experience to deliver services within one or more of these areas. The approach is intended to accommodate a diverse supplier market, including organisations capable of delivering broad business support programmes alongside specialist providers with expertise in particular sectors, business needs or forms of intervention. It will also support the development of new and emerging provision as business needs, economic conditions and regional priorities evolve. Lot 1: .

sig_753c5acb3b209079b531.description: The North West London Integrated Care Board (NWL ICB) and North Central London Integrated Care Board (NCL ICB) are looking to procure a single Complex Care Clinical Commissioning Digital end-to-end solution for the newly merged West and North London Integrated Care Board (WNL ICB), which will support the management of approximately 13,000 clients across 13 boroughs. As both organisations merge and undertake significant change in role, structure and culture, the digital system aims to ensure there is resilience within the Complex Care service through improved efficiency, integration, and patient outcomes by replacing outdated systems. The new digital end-to-end solution will reduce unwarranted variation, introduce workflows and automation, improve data accuracy and visibility, reduce overall IT spend, lower operational cost; increase productivity through efficient use of resources, improve quality and performance, stronger security, support the development of roles, which add value both for the individual member of staff as well as the organisation, support transitioning to a new operating model and transformational ways of working and empower client and stakeholder via dedicated portals improving user experience. This initiative supports the Government’s 10 Year Health Plan for England launched in July 2025 and the Model ICB AACC Good Practice Recommendations published in September 2025 highlighting the ambition of moving the NHS from Analogue to Digital. Furthermore, it is supported by the Darzi Report (2024) which identified that the NHS has not invested in platform technologies which can radically reshape how we work and live our lives. The ICBs intend to enter into a contract for five (5) years, with the option to extend for a further three (3) 12 month periods (+1+1+1). The contractual start date of the new Digital system is to commence on 1 Aug 2027, it is anticipated that mobilisation of the system will be between 1 Apr 2027 to 31 Jul 2027 (9-months) – and will also include a dual running period at the latter stage. Lot 1: .

sig_7554bd229acfbb88761e.description: Wolverhampton City Council are conducting a Preliminary Market Engagement for Telecare Services. Telecare is a preventative service designed to support independent living by providing remote monitoring and emergency response solutions. It enables individuals, particularly older adults and those with vulnerabilities to remain safely in their own homes, reducing reliance on more intensive care services. In Wolverhampton, this is primarily delivered through the provision of personal alarms and pendants connected to an Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC), complemented by a 24-hour physical response service commissioned separately. The Council is engaging with the market to understand: • The capability of providers to deliver all or part of the Telecare service. • Innovative approaches and technologies that can overcome current challenges. • Potential business models and indicative costs for market-led delivery. • Opportunities for integration with wider assistive technology ecosystems. sig_75580301d20b9cb830b9.description: The system's product range comprises all forms of IT operating services, both traditional on-premise solutions as well as cloud-based solutions and hybrid solutions. The system covers IT operating services under the seven service areas listed below and elaborated in Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System. In addition, as part of its delivery of IT operating services to the customer, the supplier is responsible for making the necessary operational adjustments and configurations, as well as delivering cross-functional services and ordering services related to the IT operating services. The supplier is responsible, inter alia, for operating, maintaining and administering the IT operating services and making the necessary minor adjustments, up-/downscaling, configurations, patching, etc., and handling the service management processes, including documentation, reporting, ITIL processes and participation in the customer's governance organisation as part of the delivery of IT operating services to the customer. The supplier must also ensure that the supplier's IT operating services have a high degree of security, which the supplier must incorporate into its IT operating services and ensure the necessary monitoring and control of. In connection with specific procurements under the system, the supplier must deliver an onboarding transition service and, in connection with the total or partial termination of the Delivery Contract, also deliver an offboarding transition service. Common to both transition services is that the supplier must manage, operate and plan these phases and assist the customer, the outgoing supplier and the incoming supplier to the necessary extent to ensure a successful transition. It is possible to purchase various forms of IT operating services that all complement each other. The system has a high degree of flexibility and contains many different use scenarios that make it possible to purchase IT services such as, for example: publicly available cloud tools as well as managed cloud services and administration of cloud platforms, storage, backup, computing, physical floor space in a data centre, racks for IT equipment, office WiFi solutions, network cables for data centres, managed network solutions, VPN solutions, operation of standard and specially developed applications, database operations, middleware operations, rental of computers, tablets, PC screens, headsets and associated mobile device management, as well as service desk, Security Operations Centre (SOC), operation of modern office applications including e-mail, collaboration platforms, archiving systems, etc. Overall, the system category contains the following seven service areas, with associated underlying services, cross-functional services and ordering services that the customer can procure across: • Cloud operations • Data centre operations • Co-location • Network operations • Application operations • End-user services • Security services Under the seven service areas, it is possible to procure capacity – for example, cloud capacity and server and storage capacity. Reference is otherwise made to Annex C, The Subject Matter of the System for an elaboration of the 7 service areas that the subject matter of the system consists of.

sig_7591de99813acd4e4c2d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. sig_75a3dfeacef639c5452e.description: ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS”) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: • Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. • Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M as defined by SBA regulations. • Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 — All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. • Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3’s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Period of Performance / Performance Locations: Total Performance Period shall not exceed 66-months: • Base Period – (15-Feb-27 to 14-Aug-27) Agile Development and Transition In • Option Period 1 – (15-Aug-27 to 14-Aug-28) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 2 – (15-Aug-28 to 14-Aug-29) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 3 – (15-Aug-29 to 14-Aug-30) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 4 – (15-Aug-30 to 14-Aug-31) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 5 – (15-Aug-31 to 14-Feb-32) – Enterprise Performance and Transition Out • Option Period 6 – (15-Feb-32 to 14-Aug-32) – Option to Extend the Term of Service under FAR 52.217-8 * Work will be performed at Government facilities, Contractor facilities, and Remote locations. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. Proposal Submission Instructions Phase I responses to this solicitation are due by 13 October 2026 / 11:59pm (Eastern). Submission due dates for all subsequent Phases will be issued via Advisory Notifications / Invitations. All submissions must be submitted via email to the designated POCs listed below: Branch Chief / Contracting Officer: Lovisa D. Parks, Lovisa.d.parks.civ@army.mil Team Lead / Contracting Officer: Troy D. Darling, troy.d.darling.civ@army.mil Contract Specialists: Constance Hastings, constance.k.hastings.civ@army.mil, and Sophia Dasilva, sophia.g.dasilva.civ@army.mil * Late Submissions: Late submissions will be handled in accordance with FAR 52.212-1(f). ** See FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors — Commercial Items; for proposal submission instructions. 7. Additional Information i. Questions: The deadline to submit questions for this RFP is September 28th, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. All questions SHALL be submitted using the following electronic form: ACCESS VIA ATTACHED LINK a. Each Business Entity is limited to no more than five (5) questions. b. Each question SHALL be submitted under a separate submission using the provided electronic form. c. Questions submitted in “batches” (multiple questions submitted on the same form submission) shall be rejected and will not receive a response. d. No “anonymous” questions shall be answered. ii. Security Clearance Requirements: See DD254 for specifics. a. Probable Facility Clearance without Storage b. Probable Secret, Top-Secret, and TS/SCI requirements for certain employees. 8. sig_75cb8027dd0a372677f1.description: The Universiteit van Amsterdam (UvA) and the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (HvA) intend to jointly procure a new Document Management System (DMS) to replace the current DMS. The aim of the procurement is to contract a future-proof, secure and user-friendly DMS solution that supports the UvA and HvA in the sustainable management, making accessible and archiving of digital documents and files. The contract includes, among other things, the supply of the DMS solution, implementation and configuration, migration of existing documents, metadata and files, integrations with the existing IT environment, training and knowledge transfer, management, maintenance, support and further development. The offered solution must connect to the existing information provision of the UvA and HvA and, among other things, provide support for document and file management, metadata, workflows, authorization, retention periods, archiving, destruction, searching, audit trail and integrations with the existing Microsoft 365 environment. In addition to the quality of the offered solution and services, the evaluation will look at the implementation and migration approach, future-proofing, security and compliance, and user experience, adoption and self-reliance. The price also forms part of the evaluation. As part of the award procedure, mandatory demonstrations will be organised in which tenderers demonstrate the offered solution on the basis of various practical situations. The contract will be awarded to the tenderer with the economically most advantageous tender based on the best price-quality ratio (BPKV).
sig_75cb8027dd0a372677f1.title: Vervanging Document Management Systeem (DMS)

sig_764be2c8baccff324587.description: - BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE OF THE MARKET CONSULTATION – The Zentrum für Safe Sport e.V. (ZfSS) is being established for the first time as an independent institution for the prevention, intervention and processing of interpersonal violence in German sport. As a nationwide facility, the ZfSS promotes safe sport and strengthens protection structures. Its task is to investigate and sanction incidents of psychological, physical and sexualised violence in elite sport – including below the criminal threshold – independently and on the basis of uniform standards. The range of services will be expanded progressively. In addition, the ZfSS consolidates tasks in prevention and processing, develops guidelines and certifications for safe sport, and strengthens cooperation between sport, science, politics and civil society. Founded by the federation and the federal states as a non-profit association, the ZfSS is currently being set up: regular operations will start in the middle of 2027, and moving into the property in Kassel will take place from the autumn of 2026. The ZfSS is doing pioneering work and developing a working culture characterised by appreciation, interdisciplinarity and co-creation. Diverse perspectives and specialist expertise form the foundation for a future-proof institution that relies on integrity and trust. To fulfil this task, the ZfSS requires a case management system that forms the technical basis for the investigation and sanctioning of cases. It is intended to map the case file over the entire lifecycle of a case – from the receipt of an initial tip-off to disciplinary proceedings – with the participation of internal staff as well as external experts, where the protection of personal data and special categories of personal data is paramount. The objective of the market consultation is to obtain a well-founded overview of already existing solutions and their functionalities prior to the actual tender. - YOUR PARTICIPATION IN THE MARKET CONSULTATION – As part of the market consultation, product demonstration sessions are planned. In these sessions, which last up to an hour and a half, you will be given the opportunity to present your product. In the course of this, a demo scenario is to be run through (cf. Annex 1_Demo Scenario). In addition, questions on further aspects will be asked during the session. - DATES - Dates for the individual discussions will be agreed with interested parties at short notice and will take place digitally (WebEx). A limited quota (maximum 7 discussions) is available. The discussions are scheduled to take place in calendar week 42 and, if applicable, calendar week 43. - REGISTRATION - Informal registration by e-mail to Dr Elisabeth Mrozik (Elisabeth.Mrozik@pd-g.de) and Nomman Pasha (Nomman.Pasha@pd-g.de) is sufficient. After receipt of your registration, you will receive an official invitation with the access data. The quota for individual discussions will be expanded if there is corresponding demand.
sig_764be2c8baccff324587.title: Market consultation in preparation for a procurement procedure for the acquisition of a case management system for the Zentrum für Safe Sport e.V. (ZfSS)

sig_76aebd873642a1517c48.description: Femern A/S is the state-owned project company entrusted with the planning, procurement and delivery of the Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link. Femern A/S is a subsidiary of Sund & Bælt Holding A/S, which is fully owned by the Danish Ministry of Transport. Femern A/S requires Quantity Surveying services in connection with the implementation the Fehmarn Belt Fixed Link – one of Europe’s largest and most technically ambitious infrastructure projects (hereinafter “the Project”). The Project comprises the construction of an 18-kilometre immersed tunnel between Rødbyhavn (Denmark) and Puttgarden (Germany) under the Fehmarn Belt. The tunnel will accommodate a four-lane motorway and a double-track electrified railway, significantly reducing travel time and strengthening transport links between Scandinavia and continental Europe. The works have been divided into a number of contract packages, including: 1. tunnel dredging and reclamation (TDR Contract); 2. cut-and-over parts, portal buildings, ramps and light attenuation structures and landside civil engineering (TPR Contract); 3. the construction of the southern part of the immersed tunnel (TUS Contract); 4. the construction of the northern part of the immersed tunnel (TUN Contract); and 5. various packages of mechanical and electrical works; track installation; communications systems; tolling systems; lighting and power systems. (mainly TEM Contract, TPS Contract and TTC Contract). The contractors engaged on the Project are large international contractors and joint ventures. A list of contractors and other counterparties is stated in Appendix 1 – Scope of Services, section 5. The contracts are based on FIDIC Silver Book 1999 with a number of amendments. To support the continued execution and governance of the project, Femern A/S seeks assistance from a highly competent and independent Quantity Surveying (QS) company. The QS will be required to support Femern A/S in in the areas of: • Professional assessment and negotiation of contractor claims, including delay, disruption and other cost claims • Structured cost and quantity management • High-volume data analysis • Verification and audit of contractor invoicing under lump sum, remeasured, and cost-plus / time-and-material contracts • Preparation of Expert Reports for use in formal dispute resolution, including arbitration under ICC rules, and in accordance with IBA Rules on the Taking of Evidence in International Arbitration • Cross-examination regarding such Export Reports Femern A/S has a strong internal project organisation and is supported by a number of Danish and international advisors within technical, legal, environmental, and financial areas. The QS must work in close collaboration with the internal team and external advisors, ensuring accurate cost control, well-founded assessments, and structured documentation. Although the specific scope and volume of tasks cannot be fully defined in advance – as it depends on the evolving nature of the Project and ongoing dialogue with contractors – a significant need for QS services is expected for the remainder of the project and beyond. The QS provider must be able to mobilise highly qualified resources on short notice. A non-exhaustive list of expected services is provided in the tender documents – see among others Appendix 1 (Scope of Services).
sig_76aebd873642a1517c48.title: Quantity Surveyor Services

sig_76bac71395eabf97414e.description:
The main objective of the procurement is to access a modern software solution, based on cloud infrastructure, which ensures the integrated analysis of online audiovisual content and supports the radio/TV programme monitoring process. The software solution must enable advanced analysis of the media and online information ecosystem, including the identification of themes, trends and relationships between information sources, in order to support the analysis and monitoring activities carried out by the CNA. The software solution will constitute an indispensable working tool for CNA staff, providing automated mechanisms for collection, classification, analysis and reporting, as well as functionalities for organising materials by case. Through this system, the CNA will be able to quickly identify content that may contravene audiovisual legislation, generate objective reports and substantiate regulatory and sanctioning decisions. Specifically, the software solution will support the Beneficiary in: - analysing content flows in the digital environment, including video-sharing platforms; - identifying and documenting illegal or harmful content, with an emphasis on the protection of minors and combating hate speech; - observing the dynamics of inauthentic or coordinated account networks and their impact on the public space; - integrating and analysing transcripts of programmes broadcast by radio and TV stations, extracting relevant themes and indicators; - generating statistics and thematic reports tailored to institutional needs and legal obligations. The need for this procurement stems from the CNA's mission to protect the public interest, guarantee pluralism and contribute to strengthening society's resilience in the face of informational risks. The solution will contribute to increasing internal efficiency, professionalising analysis and monitoring processes, and the transparency of regulatory action, strengthening the CNA's position as a guarantor of compliance with audiovisual legislation in Romania. Detailed functional and non-functional requirements are set out in Specifications No. 10358/14.09.2026, Chapters 5–8, which form an integral part of the tender documentation. Requests for clarifications or additional information shall be submitted by economic operators no later than the 20-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders, exclusively via SEAP, in the "Requests for clarifications/Questions/Communications" section within the procurement procedure. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications or additional information submitted within the aforementioned deadline, no later than the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders, observing the minimum time limit of 10 days provided for in Article 161(1) of Law No. 98/2016 and aligning the time limits required by Article 27(2) of Government Decision No. 395/2016. The consolidated response shall be published in SEAP, under the "List of clarifications, notifications and decisions" section of the contract notice. Where the response to a request for clarifications modifies a requirement of the tender documentation, the contracting authority shall not effect the modification through the response, but shall publish a corrigendum in SEAP, appropriately revise the ESPD and, where appropriate, extend the deadline for the submission of tenders. The software solution forming the subject of this procurement shall be provided as Software as a Service (SaaS), being fully accessible via certified cloud infrastructure hosted exclusively on the territory of the European Union or the European Economic Area. The solution shall be provided on the basis of annual subsequent contracts, for the entire duration of the framework agreement, of a maximum of 48 months, under the applicable contractual and budgetary conditions. The framework agreement shall be concluded with a single economic operator. The annual access fee for SaaS services includes all services necessary for the operationalisation and use of the solution: hosting, administration, security, maintenance, updates, technical support, configuration, integration, testing and user training. Configuration, integration, testing and training activities are included in the price of the service and shall not be invoiced separately, in accordance with Chapter 11.3 of the Specifications. The service delivery model must ensure both compliance with European and national regulations on security and data protection, and the flexibility required to adapt to the institution's needs. Mandatory requirements (minimum level, detailed in the Specifications, Chapters 5–8): - Secure access: the software solution shall be available via the internet, based on individual authentication, with advanced access control mechanisms (multi-factor authentication, Single Sign-On, differentiated roles such as: user, administrator, supervisor). - Volume and collection sources: automated, continuous and configurable collection of public content from YouTube, TikTok, Facebook Video, Instagram Reels and X (Twitter Video), as mandatory sources, with a monthly quota allowing the collection and analysis of at least 2.000.000 items of content (Chapters 6.1.1.1 and 7.2.2 of the Specifications). - Users and capacity: access and simultaneous use by at least 10 users (Chapter 7.2.1 of the Specifications); training of 6 persons designated by the Beneficiary (Chapter 8.2.3). - Data retention and retroactive window: retention of collected records, metadata and results for a minimum of 12 months from collection or generation respectively, and the ability to target content published in the last 30 days (Chapter 6.1.1.1). - Service level: availability of at least 99,5 % in each calendar month of service provision, calculated according to the formula set out in Chapter 7.4.1, excluding planned maintenance (Chapter 7.4.1);

for critical incidents, a response time of a maximum of 1 hour and a resolution time of a maximum of 4 hours (Chapter 7.5.3); technical support on working days, between 08:00 and 18:00, through at least two channels (Chapter 7.5.2). - Standards-compliant infrastructure: the use of cloud infrastructures or data centres certified to ISO/IEC 27001 or equivalent, with data hosting and processing exclusively within the European Union or the European Economic Area. - Updates included: all updates, upgrades and security patches shall be provided automatically, at no additional cost to the Beneficiary, ensuring permanent alignment with the latest technological and legislative standards. - Multilingual interface: the software solution must be fully available in Romanian or English, both at the interface level and in terms of documentation, user manuals and guides. - Migration assistance and reversibility: upon termination of the contract, the Contractor shall assist the Beneficiary in the complete download and transfer of data, in open and documented formats, without loss of information and at no additional cost (Chapters 7.3.3 and 7.3.4 of the Specifications). - Algorithmic traceability: the Contractor has the obligation to document the operation of automated components (artificial intelligence/machine learning) and to allow their auditing, in order to ensure transparency and compliance with the principles of technological neutrality (Chapter 5.3 of the Specifications). Specific information regarding the framework agreement (Article 20(8) of Government Decision No. 395/2016): - Number of economic operators that will be part of the framework agreement: 1 (one). The framework agreement is concluded with a single economic operator. - Competition is not reopened upon the award of subsequent contracts: since the framework agreement is concluded with a single economic operator, subsequent contracts shall be awarded in compliance with the technical and financial conditions established in the framework agreement, pursuant to Article 117(2) of Law No. 98/2016, and their clauses may not make substantial modifications to the terms and conditions initially established, pursuant to Article 116(2) of the same law. - Frequency of awarding subsequent contracts: annual — one subsequent contract for each 12-month period covered by the duration of the framework agreement. - Unit of measurement: the annual platform access fee, for 12 months of service provision, at the volume and service level provided for in the Specifications. - Estimated quantities over the entire duration of the framework agreement: a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 annual access fees. - Estimated quantities that may form the subject of a single subsequent contract: a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 1 annual access fee, corresponding to a duration of a minimum of 1 month and a maximum of 12 months of access.
