sig_79687bc2028cbffd75cd.description: ADVANCED RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT (ARA) FA9451-21-S-0001 Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research (DETER) Air Force Research Laboratory/Directed Energy Directorate NAICS Code: The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715 for Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees Federal Agency Name: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy, Phillips Research Site, Kirtland AFB NM (AFRL/RD) ARA Title: Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research Announcement (DETER) ARA Type: This is an Open ARA with Calls; initial announcement ARA Number: FA9451-21-S-0001 Program Summary: This is an Open ARA announcement pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). AFRL/RD is interested in receiving white papers and proposals through a Two-Step Process to perform research and development (R&D), modeling and simulation (M&S), design, component/subsystem, prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of directed energy source components (to include spares and alternate component technologies), and/or systems and any required accessories, materials, and supplies for laboratory research and experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged. *Note: AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. *Please see the attached DETER Industry User Guide for guidance on definitions, processes, submission requirements and evaluation criteria.* Background: AFRL/RD equips the joint warfighter with next-generation technologies, advanced concepts, and weapon system options across all operational domains to become more agile and increase the commercialization potential of directed energy investments to ensure the National defense. This solicitation intends to use acquisition authorities provided by 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). This authority applies to acquisition of items related to “...ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that are necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense.” Consequently, white papers and proposals should address how the proposed effort provides benefits to the national defense and a strategy for verifying those intended benefits. The proposed solutions should be innovative and substantially improve national defense capabilities across the domains of directed energy. While the Government describes discrete topic areas below, it also anticipates that certain comprehensive technology solutions and prototypes may require multidiscipline approaches that address two or more topic areas. The topic areas are covered under this announcement, which may be used in any combination. The Government reserves the right to add, delete or modify the topic areas as necessary. Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged throughout the life of this ARA. However, communication will be limited once full-proposals are submitted for evaluation/review. Prospective Offerors are welcome to request sit-downs and provide demonstrations of their capabilities. Discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. No guidance related to technical approach will be given. However, questions related to the objectives of the effort or prior similar efforts may be answered. Offerors are advised that only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to contractually bind or otherwise commit the Government. THIS WILL BE A HYBRID ANNOUNCEMENT: This announcement has an open request for white papers as described below. Calls may be issued under this announcement for discrete requirements. Call types can vary and may include, but are not limited to, One-Step, Two-Step, Open, Closed, Staggered, Limited Calls or any combination therein. AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. Open Announcement Request: AFRL/RD Kirtland Air Force Base is soliciting white papers on the research effort described in the below topic areas pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373), Procurement for Experimental Purposes. Open Announcement Submission: White papers must be submitted to https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signup. If it is determined that a classified white paper is required, please DO NOT DELIVER any classified portion of the white paper, but rather contact the DETER Org Mailbox for specific delivery instructions. Further instructions for white paper submission can be found in the DETER Industry User Guide attached to this announcement. Call Request: Calls, other than Limited Calls, will be issued under this announcement via the Government Point of Entry (GPE) at https://beta.sam.gov. Notification of Calls may be announced on other platforms (i.e. www.grants.gov) and will direct Offerors to the GPE for full solicitation details. Call Submission: Submission requirements for Calls will be specified in the solicitation documentation of each Call. Call Variations: Variations of the ARA Call process are available for use. The following types are commonly used, but are not considered all inclusive. One-Step: The one-step process is used to request full technical and cost proposals from each Offeror. The proposals are reviewed in accordance with the solicitation criteria and typically all of a selected proposal, part of a selected proposal, or none of the proposals may be selected for award. Two-Step: The two-step process is sometimes used when a large number of proposals are anticipated. Potential Offerors are invited to submit brief descriptive white papers in lieu of full proposals. The Call must state whether an unfavorable white paper review will bar the Offeror from further consideration. The Government may retain unselected white papers for a specific period of time, which will be identified in the solicitation. Full proposals are requested from those Offerors selected in the white paper review process. After proposals are received, they are reviewed consistent with the process for one-step ARAs. Open Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at any time within a specified period. Open calls will be updated no less frequently than annually. White papers/proposals are reviewed when received during the period that the ARA is open. Closed Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at a specified date and time as set forth in the ARA. Staggered-Closed Call: The staggered-closed Call states a specified date and time for receipt of proposals or white papers, but also allows for proposals/white papers after the date and time set for proposal receipt. All Offerors should be cautioned, however, that the likelihood of funding proposals received after the specified date and time is substantially reduced. Limited Call: This approach allows for solicitation to a limited group of potential offerors. Request for Proposals (RFP) or Requests for white papers will be issued directly to potential offerors without a requirement to publish to the GPE. The Government may issue solicitations that combine one or more of the above approaches. Open Announcement Modifications: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is subject to updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor https://beta.sam.gov to ensure they receive the latest guidance for this announcement. The Government shall provide updates to this announcement no less than annually. Updates may include changes to: topic areas, submission requirements, administrative changes, evaluation criteria, solicitation methods, etc. (not an inclusive list). Type of Contract/Instrument: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract/instrument type under the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10 U.S.C. §4021 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371) "Other Transaction for Research 10 U.S.C. §4022 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371b) "Other Transaction for Prototype" 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373) "Procurement for Experimental Purposes" 10 U.S.C. §4025 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2374) "Prize Competitions" DoD Grant and Agreement Regulation (DoDGARS) The Government anticipates that a mix of contract/instrument types will be used throughout the life of this ARA. Generally, awards under this announcement or any Calls may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, Firm Fixed Price, Other Transaction Authority, etc. NOTE: If proposing a Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) type contract, the FAR clauses will be referenced at the Call level or within the Request for Proposal. The FAR and supplement provisions and clauses are incorporated by reference. The full text of these provisions and clauses can be found at https://www.acquisition.gov. If proposing an assistance instrument (grants or cooperative agreements) then articles and guidance found under DoDGARS, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) and OMB/DoD Policy shall be used and followed as appropriate. If proposing an Other Transaction (OT) these FAR references and clauses would not apply. The terms and conditions of an OT agreement should be developed and negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Estimated Program Cost: The overarching announcement has an unrestricted ceiling. However, individual Calls may elect to provide an estimated program value or funding profile for planning purposes. Anticipated Number of Awards: The Air Force anticipates awarding multiple awards for this announcement. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more agreements, other transactions, or contracts for all, some or none of the solicited effort based on the Offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding availability. There is no limit on the number of awards that may be made to an individual Offeror. Schedule: The anticipated period of performance will be determined through dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives for each topic area and specified in each individual award. Deliverables: Hardware and software deliverables will be specified within a separately priced line items and data deliverables will be specified on individual CDRL(s) in any resultant contract or an OT article. Within Scope Award Modifications: Offerors are advised that due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to make within scope changes, to include but not limited to, modifications which increase overall contract/award ceiling amount. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Before the Government can issue an award, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). If an Offeror was previously registered in Central Contractor Registration (CCR), the information has been transferred to SAM. However, it is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all of their data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM replaced CCR, Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. The Government reserves the right to determine an offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. I am aware that any false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements or claims may subject me to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties. (U.S. code, Title 218, Section 1001). Topic Areas 1. Directed Energy (DE) Sources This category of supplies covers research, development and testing for all directed energy sources in the near-term and far-term in support of National Defense. This area covers the design, component/subsystem, prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of directed energy source components (to include spares and alternate component technologies), and/or systems and any required accessories, materials, and supplies for laboratory research and experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. This area also covers the redesign, refurbishment, modification, and/or upgrade of existing sources, if required, to support laboratory experimentation, field or flight trials, and/or demonstrations. Examples of directed energy sources include, but are not limited to: a. Laser Sources b. High Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) Sources 2. Acquisition Tracking Pointing (ATP), Beam Control (BC) and Atmospheric Compensation (AC) Systems This area covers the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of any hardware, sensors, control electronics, and software/firmware required to develop ATP, BC and AC systems to control the propagation of directed energy so as to maximize energy/irradiance on target. This area also includes any required accessories, materials, supplies, and/or services necessary to conduct laboratory experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. 3. DE Weapon Systems This area covers the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of DE weapon components and systems, diagnostics, accessories, materials, supplies, and services necessary to build/integrate complete weapon systems for laboratory research, experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. Systems engineering design/analysis and/or trade studies are relevant in regards to size, weight, and power (SWAP). Specific topics of interest include the following areas: a. Feasibility studies of innovative HPEM applications b. Integration of disparate technologies for the fielding of new HPEM systems and weapons c. Identification and quantification of useful -HPEM effects d. Development of HPEM sources that have a role in future applications e. system integration and demonstration of future HPEM capabilities f. Power subsystems g. Thermal Management subsystems h. Command and control subsystems i. Platform integration j. Detection, targeting and tracking subsystems k. DOTmLPF-P studies and experimentation l. CONOPS, CONEMPS, TTP development and experimentation m. Performance enhancement technologies for existing systems 4. DE Effects Testing Provide testing of materials, components, subsystems, and systems to determine the vulnerability, susceptibility, and accessibility of potential DE targets to DE exposure. This includes the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of unique DE components, sources, and systems and any required diagnostic and/or special test equipment/tooling and materials necessary to conduct DE-material interaction physics experimentation to establish the efficacy of DE waveforms to support the development of DE weapons system requirements and/or assessment of proposed DE weapon systems. Develop survivability requirements and recommendations for space systems and support vulnerability predictions. 5. Modeling, Simulation and Analysis (MS&A) This area covers the development/procurement, testing, maintenance, modification, upgrade/reuse, and execution of scientific modeling, simulation and analysis software and requisite IT hardware systems necessary to efficiently execute software to support DE weapon system design, development, testing, and data analysis of test results. This includes campaign-level, engagement-level, system, and component-level MS&A codes to create test scenarios, assess design reference mission compliance, provide pre-test predictions, and conduct post-test assessment of system performance. In addition, sound principles for software engineering and development must be employed for all developed software and documentation. Robust software testing, validation, and verification are critical to software development efforts. As appropriate, software must scale to large simulation sizes and be portable to massively parallel computer architecture. MS&A software may include fast running engineering codes and detailed physics modeling codes. Examples of MS&A sub-topic areas include, but are not limited to: a. DE System Performance MS&A b. DE System Effects MS&A c. DE System Target Assessment d. DE System Biosafety and Biological Effects e. DE Source and Component Virtual Design f. Satellite signatures and Radiometric/photometric assessments of space objects. g. Assess electro-optical Space Domain Awareness (SDA) systems and architectures. h. Space system functional modeling and response i. Conduct Space Domain Awareness in non-traditional orbits j. Quantify safe operating conditions for lasers operating through the atmosphere and space 6. Wargaming This area covers the development/procurement, testing, maintenance, modification, upgrade/reuse, and execution of wargaming and scientific modeling, simulation and analysis software and their requisite IT hardware systems necessary to efficiently execute this software to support DE weapon system design, development, testing, and data analysis of wargaming results. This includes campaign-level, engagement-level, system, and component-level wargaming MS&A codes to create test scenarios, assess design reference mission compliance, provide pre-test predictions, and conduct post-test assessment of system performance. In addition, sound principles for software engineering and development must be employed for all developed software and documentation. Robust software testing, validation, and verification are critical to software development efforts. As appropriate, software must scale to large wargaming and simulation sizes and be portable to massively parallel computer architecture. Wargaming MS&A software may include fast running engineering codes and detailed physics modeling codes. Additionally, the wargaming area should provide general wargaming support to include DE wargame planning, table top, MS&A, and field execution, and wargame reporting. In addition, provide required hardware, software/firmware, accessories, materials, supplies, infrastructure, diagnostics, targets, safety equipment, and services necessary to conduct wargame research, experiments, field and/or range testing of DE components, subsystems, systems and demonstrations under operationally relevant conditions. 7. Innovative Space Domain Awareness Provide basic & applied research, algorithms, software/firmware, materials, supplies, and services necessary to conduct technology maturation for ground-based surveillance of space objects. Examples include, but are not limited to: a. Closely-spaced object detection and characterization. b. Daytime detection and custody of satellites. c. Orbit determination techniques and algorithms for satellites significantly affected by lunar and solar gravity. d. Rapid, on-demand orbit determination. e. Extremely wide field-of-view image exploitation for satellite discovery and custody. f. Multi-phenomenology sensor integration (e.g. optical, radar, passive radiofrequency). g. Active optical techniques for satellite ranging and characterization (e.g. LiDAR, LADAR). h. Sharp imaging of satellites through the atmosphere at low elevation angles. i. Characterization of atmospheric deep turbulence for image restoration. j. Techniques, algorithms, architecture designs, etc. for collaborative autonomous telescope networks. k. Multispectral, hyperspectral, and polarimetric characterization of space objects. l. Techniques to improve and exploit short- and long-wave infrared characterization of space objects. m. Machine learning algorithms to advance the state-of-the-art in areas such as: • Point spread function correction. • Space object image classification using resolved or non-resolved sensor imagery. • Uncorrelated track association. • Space object feature identification, model inference, and attitude regression. • Space object detection in noisy image backgrounds. • Generation of realistic space scene imagery / discernment of real vs. synthetic. • Detection of subtle, unique image artefacts of interest in a large dataset. 8. Experiments, Testing and Demonstrations Provide general and specialized test support to include DE test planning, laboratory and field demonstration, and reporting. Provide required hardware, software/firmware, accessories, materials, supplies, infrastructure, diagnostics, targets, safety equipment, and services necessary to conduct testing of DE components, subsystems, systems, and demonstrations under operationally relevant conditions. 9. Laboratory Materials, Supplies and Services in Support of Experimentation Provide required ancillary support systems, equipment, materials, supplies, infrastructure, and services necessary to support the development, operation, maintenance, and testing required to evaluate DE through experimentation in the laboratory and field during trials or flight/range testing. Examples include, but are not limited to: a. Clean rooms, anechoic chambers and necessary equipment, materials, supplies and/or services to support all aspects of DE source development, laboratory experimentation, and field trials. b. Diagnostic and/or special test equipment/tooling required for: • Quality assurance of components used in the fabrication of DE sources • Damage assessments and root cause analysis of component, subsystem and system failures • Characterization of target physical, chemical, and electromagnetic properties • Fabrication, assembly, integration, testing, operation and maintenance of DE sources • Direct/indirect measurements of DE source performance c. Power systems required to operate the source and any required ancillary equipment or services necessary to install, operate and/or maintain these systems d. Unique chemicals to operate, clean, and/or maintain direct energy systems and/or laboratory facilities used for directed energy experimentation as well as any required materials, accessories or services required for safe storage, use, operations, and proper disposal of any hazardous materials e. Thermal management components and systems, to include system-level and facility-level systems, necessary to support safe operations of DE sources. This includes materials, supplies, accessories, services and/or any support required for safe operations and maintenance of the system as well as proper disposal of hazardous materials/waste. f. Any required safety related items necessary to fabricate, assemble, integrate, test, operate and maintain directed energy sources. g. Transportation: This area covers all transportation, to and from, various research facilities and sites to conduct field and/or flight experimentation, testing and/or trials of directed energy components, sub-systems and systems and demonstrations. This includes such items as associated support/handling equipment, special test equipment/tooling, spares, and diagnostic/testing equipment. Specialized transportation requirements may include: design, fabrication and/or purchase of specialized packaging, crating, enclosures, trailers, and/or vehicles from which the transported item(s) will be operated/maintained to conduct experimentation, testing and/or trials outside of traditional laboratory spaces. Additionally, this area covers aspects of safe transportation to and from remote field locations, Department of Defense test ranges, and installations in support of field and/or flight experimentation, testing and/or trials. ***UPDATES AS OF 09 DEC 2021*** a) DETER Industry User Guide, Amendment 02 update to Section 2.b., White Papers shall be submitted using the following link https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signuppapers update to Section 2.c.2. b) DETER White Paper Cover Sheet, Attachment 1, Amendment 1 ***UPDATES AS OF 06 JAN 2022*** Corrects the Valid Eval web address in the Open Announcement description above From: https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signuppapers To: https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signup ***UPDATES AS OF 11 AUG 2022*** a.) IT operations, support and security services for the ONTRAS Gastransport GmbH The Standard IT lot comprises the provision and operation of central IT infrastructure and platform services for the contracting authority. The services are provided as integrated operational services and form the technological basis for the operation of a large number of business IT applications and the associated infrastructure components. In particular, this lot comprises data centre infrastructure, network and communication infrastructure, application platforms and technical application operations services. The systems, platforms and applications in scope are made available to applicants during the bidding phase in the form of a detailed service catalogue and supplementary inventory and architecture documents. Different performance levels are provided for the platforms and applications in scope. These may include in particular: housing, hosting, platform operation, technical application operation, provision of operating platforms, monitoring, backup and recovery services, patch and release management, operational support, technical operational management. The specific scope of services can vary depending on the application, platform or infrastructure component. To provide the services, the contractor provides the required operating platforms, infrastructure components and management and monitoring tools and ensures their operation in accordance with the agreed service levels. The services also include the operational management of the required infrastructure domains. These include in particular: data centre, servers, virtualisation, container platforms, storage, data backup and recovery, archiving, network and connectivity, basic communication services and technical application platforms. The services are provided on the basis of defined quality levels and service level agreements. Highly available, secure and standardised operating procedures must be applied. The services are provided in accordance with the IT service management processes specified by ONTRAS and using the IT service management tool provided by ONTRAS. The contractor must design its organisation, its process workflows and its internal systems in such a way that the ONTRAS processes are adhered to throughout and all processes relevant to ONTRAS are managed completely, up to date and comprehensibly in the ONTRAS IT service management tool. The services must also be provided on the basis of the architecture, technology, integration, security and solution specifications defined by ONTRAS. The contractor shall implement these specifications within its area of responsibility and take them into account when operating, modifying and further developing the services. The contractor is not entitled to use its own standard processes, its own IT service management systems or differing architecture and solution specifications. To the extent that the contractor uses its own processes or systems for providing its internal services, this does not release it from providing the services within the processes and systems specified by ONTRAS. Additional integrations, synchronisations or organisational measures that become necessary due to the contractor's own systems or process models are the contractor's responsibility. The processes, systems and specifications specified by ONTRAS are solely decisive for the cooperation with ONTRAS and the other service providers. sig_79785a5cab6354aca01d.description: The National Transport Authority (NTA) is seeking tenders from suitably qualified and experienced ServiceNow Elite Partners for the provision of support, maintenance, development, licensing, hosting and associated professional services for the Authority’s dedicated standalone ServiceNow instances. The successful Tenderer will be required to provide a comprehensive managed service covering platform support and maintenance, system administration, configuration and development services, upgrades and releases, incident and problem management, security and governance, reporting, training, licensing management, integrations with third-party systems and transition services. The contract will support the ongoing operation, maintenance and enhancement of the NTA’s ServiceNow environment and facilitate future platform developments and service improvements. The Services may include the provision of specialist ServiceNow resources and consultancy services as required throughout the contract term. Full details of the requirements are set out in the procurement documentation. The initial contract term is two years, with the option to extend for up to three additional periods of one year each, giving a maximum contract term of five years. Interested parties are invited to tender for this contract. While the Authority estimates the total value of this contract over its maximum term to be €5,242,299, it reserves the right to spend up to €6,552,874 to accommodate additional requirements, unforeseen demand and any permissible variations during the contract term.

sig_79859348fc30fb367b2e.description: The aim of Hansel Oy is to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the preliminary subject matter of which is software and ICT expert services. Joint procurement enables the procurement of the following services as needed, among others: 1. Software: The customer's procurement subject matter may be various software. In addition to software, expert work related to software can be procured, such as tailoring software to the customer's needs, configuration, further development, as well as support and maintenance. Both open source and closed source software are included in the subject matter of the DPS. The customer's procurement subject matter may also be a licence brokerage service (for example, resale). Software can be delivered on a licence basis, installed in the customer's own environment, or on a service basis as a SaaS implementation. 2. The following ICT expert services are included in the procurement subject matter: ICT management and service management services, ICT solution design, software development and quality assurance services, support and maintenance services, as well as IT asset management. The aim is for the establishment phase of the dynamic purchasing system to start in March-April 2026. *Read more about the dynamic purchasing system: https://www.hansel.fi/hankintatietoa/dynaaminen-hankintajarjestelma-dps/ GENERAL Please note that this is a market survey notice (hereinafter notice), and this notice does not yet request applications to participate. All information presented in this notice is preliminary and indicative prior information. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. REGISTRATION Companies interested in the dynamic purchasing system in question are requested to register for market dialogue no later than 6.2.2026 via this notice in the Hilma web service. The contracting authority will not respond at this stage to questions sent via the "Questions and Answers" section. MARKET DIALOGUE Draft material related to the dynamic purchasing system under preparation will be sent to registered companies for comments during approximately February-March 2026. Registered companies will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing. The market dialogue and materials will be in Finnish. Participating or not participating in the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid to those who participated in the market dialogue for participation.
sig_79859348fc30fb367b2e.title: Software and ICT expert services 2026 (00871)

sig_79d841361027fefb4b78.description: The procedure is organised through an online open tender, with the procurement divided into lots, with a view to the separate award of components that can be executed/supplied by specialised economic operators, while maintaining the integrated nature of the project. The procurement is structured into the following lots: Lot 1 – Construction works and installations. Its object is the execution of construction, installation and fitting-out works necessary for the implementation of the core investment: site preparation, reconstruction of the carriageway area and creation of residential car parks, modernisation and extension of the pedestrian walkway network, creation of a central square with leisure spaces and children's play areas, reconstruction of utility networks on the site and routing them underground, electrical and sanitary installations, landscaping and landscape works (planting of trees and shrubs), as well as other related works necessary for the commissioning of the facility, executed in accordance with the technical design, specification, bill of quantities and drawings. Lot 2 – Equipment. Its object is the supply and assembly/placement of equipment necessary for the functional use of the public space — specific urban furniture and equipment for the children's play area — in correlation with the works executed under Lot 1. The contract has the nature of a public supply contract, including ancillary operations of transport, handling, assembly/placement, verification and handover. Lot 3 – Intangible assets. Its object is the supply of intangible assets necessary for the operation of the video surveillance system associated with the project — software licences and rights of use, compatible with the installed surveillance equipment. The object does not include software development, customisation or complex integration, with the exception of ancillary activation and handover operations for licences. Any reference to a platform, licence or trade name shall be interpreted as "or equivalent". Integrated nature of the procurement. Although the procedure is divided into lots, the project has an integrated nature: Lot 1 provides the physical and technical infrastructure, Lot 2 the equipment necessary for functional use, and Lot 3 the intangible assets for the operation of the surveillance system. The lotting is justified by the distinct nature of the components and the need for the participation of specialised operators, without affecting the unitary operation of the investment — the technical requirements, schedules and handovers being correlated. Estimated values: Lot 1 – 10.055.637,83 lei excluding VAT; Lot 2 – 941.379,02 lei excluding VAT; Lot 3 – 5.700,00 lei excluding VAT. The execution period for the works (Lot 1) is 30 months from the date of the commencement order issued by the Beneficiary. The deadline by which any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the tender documentation is 20 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications by the 11-th day inclusive, before the deadline for the submission of tenders. sig_79e0e0f37e6fa41befc5.description: The subject of the procurement is Fingrid’s purchase order and invoice management system delivered as a SaaS service. The software service is intended to support the entire procure-to-pay process in the target state, including purchase requests (free text, catalog, punchout catalog), purchase orders, order confirmations, receipt of goods, invoice receipt and processing. As part of the invoice processing functionality, the system must also include e-invoicing operator capabilities, enabling the sending and receiving of electronic invoices in accordance with applicable standards and integration requirements. Additionally, the system must include functionalities for supplier management, contract management, and mini competitions. The procured SaaS service must include user licenses for all Fingrid employees. The procurement also includes an implementation project, which is preliminarily planned to start during the first half of 2026. The implementation is intended to proceed in phases and be completed by Q4/2026. The support and advisory service included in the procurement serves as a second-level support channel (2nd line support) for Fingrid’s key users/application owners in case of incidents. In addition, during the contract period, the Client may procure development work, project work, and extensions to expand and improve the subject of the procurement. A more detailed description of the procurement is provided in Annex 1 of the procurement notice, Project Description.
sig_79e0e0f37e6fa41befc5.title: Procurement of a Purchase to Pay -system

sig_7a0e15ccd6aad2646098.description: The London Borough of Newham is undertaking a comprehensive market intelligence and engagement exercise to inform the future design and delivery of its Housing Repairs, Maintenance, Compliance and Capital Investment Programme. The Authority is currently considering a long-term programme of works and services with an indicative value of between £288 million and £416 million over a potential ten-year period, covering a broad range of specialist housing services including compliance, building safety, planned investment, major repairs, adaptations, voids and asset improvement programmes. The proposals outlined within the accompanying draft specification are intended solely to support this engagement process and should be viewed as initial concepts that will be refined through consultation with the market. The purpose of this survey is to gather intelligence from organisations operating across the housing, construction, compliance, asset management and wider property sectors. The Authority is seeking views on market capacity, capability, commercial models, lot structures, delivery approaches, innovation, digital solutions, social value, sustainability and emerging legislative requirements. Feedback received will help shape future procurement, commercial and service delivery strategies, ensuring that any subsequent procurement exercise is informed by current market expertise and is structured to maximise value, resilience, competition, innovation and positive resident outcomes. The Authority welcomes responses from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs, specialist providers, consortiums, manufacturers, consultants and principal contractors. This exercise represents a unique opportunity for the market to help influence the future direction of one of London's largest housing investment and asset management programmes, and the Authority strongly encourages all interested organisations to participate For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Solar-installation./KAD82PW44U To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/KAD82PW44U Lot 1: . We are looking for a technical partner responsible for the secure operation, maintenance and development of the technical infrastructure. This includes the management of existing websites, migration to a suitable hosting partner, as well as project management and the implementation of the “darksite”.

sig_7a45a2d78564f2f09a47.description: Region Midtjylland is planning to conduct a tender for a dose monitoring system for performing patient dosimetry within the specialties of conventional X-ray, mammography, interventional procedures, CT, fluoroscopy, DEXA and hybrid scanners in nuclear medicine, so that the region can comply with Executive Order No. 1387 of 18 November 2025 on patient dosimetry and diagnostic reference levels, which enters into force on 1 January 2026. In this context, the region wishes to conduct a market dialogue to gain insight into the market, so that a forthcoming tender best reflects the capabilities of the market in relation to the region's needs, while at the same time uncovering potential risks so they can be mitigated. The result of the market dialogue is to be used, amongst other things, to assess what is standard in the market, so that the region has the best possible basis on which to structure the tender and draw up the tender documents. Initially, the region wishes to invite potential tenderers to a dialogue meeting with the region. The region expects that the dialogue meetings will be used, partly for participants to demonstrate how their solutions support a number of cases, and partly to hear participants' views on a number of requirements, including security requirements, which the region intends to impose on the supplier. The region reserves the right to continue the market dialogue with participants after the dialogue meetings, including asking follow-up questions to participants and potentially sending parts of the tender documents out for consultation with participants. The dialogue meetings are expected to take place in week 5 in 2026 at the region's Department of Procurement and Medical Technology (Aarhus). The meetings will be held individually with each company and are expected to have a duration of a maximum of 2 hours. The meetings will be held in Danish or English at the company's request. In the event of high interest, the region reserves the right to invite only a limited number of companies. In that case, emphasis will be placed on achieving diversity in the types of products/services that the selected companies can offer. Emphasis will also be placed on the market penetration of the product/service among companies. Companies wishing to participate in the market dialogue are asked to send an email to thomas.krogh.larsen@stab.rm.dk and Laura.Brinch.Norregaard@stab.rm.dk no later than 12 January 2026, at 12 with information about their product and/or service. Once a participant has registered, the region will send the participant the material needed for the dialogue meetings as soon as possible, including the cases and requirements. However, if registration takes place after 19 December at 12, the region reserves the right to send the material to the participant only in week 2 2026. Region Midtjylland encourages potential tenderers to participate in the market dialogue.
sig_7a45a2d78564f2f09a47.title: Market dialogue regarding the tender for a dose monitoring system for Region Midtjylland

sig_7a8bd4ab8250ee5cacbd.description: INTRODUCTION Cornwall Council is planning to undertake preliminary market engagement to ensure we are receiving best value regarding our Oracle Fusion platform. Since transitioning to Oracle Fusion in 2020, we have not yet realised the full return on our cloud investment; therefore, we intend to continue with Oracle Fusion in order to fully realise the value of our investment. As part of developing our plans to meet this requirement we are issuing this Request for Information (RFI). This RFI is looking to confirm that we are receiving the best value from our licensing agreement for HCM, ERP and EPM modules and additionally gain a greater understanding of the market’s abilities. This RFI will allow the Council to review supplier responses and use the provided information and insights in future decision making for the Council’s strategic Oracle Fusion requirements. It is intended that the responses supplied will enable the Council to develop a business proposal. Any such proposal would be subject to the development and approval of a business case, and, as such, this exercise implies no commercial commitment. This is not a formal tender document. Participation of this early market engagement will not prejudice suppliers participating in any potential future procurement. Suppliers are invited to submit a response to this RFI. Please provide your response by 15:00 on 4 February 2026. Responses should be submitted via email addressed to: Alex.Kirk@cornwall.gov.uk The Council may hold virtual meetings via Microsoft Teams with suppliers that respond to the RFI. These meetings will be to discuss the suppliers’ RFI responses in further detail. The Council will decide whether to host these meetings once the RFI responses have been received and reviewed, also communicating the decision with participating suppliers at that time. CURRENT SERVICE OVERVIEW Oracle Fusion is one of Cornwall Councils core strategic IT platforms and a cornerstone system to several of our key strategic and operational functions within the Council. These include: Human Resources: • Payroll – supporting 35,000 individual staff across 31 employers, including volunteers, electoral workers, contingent workers councillors and non-core personnel. • Core HR – Employee records, goal planning, performance management, career development. • Absence & leave management – sickness, leave and other absences • Time & Labour – enabling the entry and approval of overtime and other payments through self-service • Recruitment – via Oracle Recruitment cloud • Compensation – facilitates automation of compensation such as grade ladders, additional payments and the annual Pension Increase Finance & Procurement: • EPM Accounting & budgeting – general ledger, financial reporting and compliance • Expenses & Invoice Processing – Automated invoice handling and expense claims redirected through payroll • Procurement & Purchasing – Purchase requisitions, orders, supplier portal and self-service procurement • Receivables – raising sales invoices and management of the Council’s sundry debt. • Cash Management – bank statement reconciliation. The above details of the services the Council currently provides using the Oracle Fusion platform also acts as a summary of the Council’s contract requirements. The estimated licencing volumes can be found in a separate file that can be provided upon request (email Alex.Kirk@cornwall.gov.uk). Once received, please use the licence volumes to provide the indicative costs for the related RFI question. Lot 1: .

sig_7a96131178b856d72f35.description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA’s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. sig_7ab059c45e1a1ec32076.description: 1 Background to the Medical Workforce Rota Management Review 1.1 King’s College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust (KCH) is undertaking a strategic review of its medical workforce rota management as part of its wider financial and workforce transformation programme. The Trust’s Financial Strategy highlights the need to deliver sustainable workforce efficiencies over the next five years, with a target of achieving a £37m recurrent cost improvement plan (CIP) in 2025/26 across clinical services. 1.2 Within this context, Workstream 7 – Workforce Improvement has been established to identify and deliver opportunities for workforce optimisation. A key focus is the medical workforce, where improvements in rota design, utilisation, and deployment are essential to balancing financial efficiency with patient safety, education and training, and staff work-life balance. 1.3 The Trust is therefore seeking an external partner to conduct a combination of deep dive reviews and diagnostic assessments of medical rotas. These will test whether the Trust can achieve sustainable financial efficiencies while maintaining high standards of care. The work will involve extensive engagement with clinical and managerial leaders, on-the-ground clinicians, and the use of proven analytical tools and methodologies to generate actionable insights. 1.4 This programme is expected to deliver not only cost savings (the financial value of the recurrent savings will need to be confirmed as part of this review) but also improved rota alignment with activity levels, better leave management, enhanced skill mix utilisation, and a more consistent approach to medical workforce planning across specialties – which includes a robust understanding of cost per medical WTE when benchmarked amongst peers. 2 Specification of Requirements 2.1 Objectives The Trust seeks to appoint an experienced Provider to conduct a comprehensive review of medical workforce rotas. For clarity this will involve all doctor grades. The objectives are to: 2.1.1 Identify efficiency opportunities within rota design and workforce deployment. 2.1.2 Validate internal diagnostics on medical workforce efficiency. 2.1.3 Deliver two specialty deep-dive reviews. The two specialty deep dives will need to be confirmed but please expect one of them to involve a medical care group. 2.1.4 Deliver diagnostic overviews for 10 specialties with overspend. 2.5 Produce clear, practical action plans (e.g. job-planning improvements, rota right-sizing, rostering) with benefits, risks and dependencies set out. 2.6 Provide an optional proposal for later implementation/delivery support once the diagnostic phase has been completed at week 12 (do not price unless requested). This delivery support will be required to ensure that any recommendations are implemented appropriately and, in turn, provide advice and support to the Trust’s own team on how to achieve it. 2.7 Ensure recommendations safeguard patient safety, education and training, working time and contractual commitments and staff work-life balance. 2.8 Provide evidence-based workforce planning solutions (which will include the design of new rotas) aligned with contractual, regulatory, and financial frameworks – i.e. all relevant doctor contracts. This work must link with the Trust’s existing workforce management arrangements as provided by Patchwork and Allocate and how the Trust currently rotas its nursing, midwifery and other allied health professionals. 2.9 Support delivery of the Trust’s financial strategy, aiming for recurrent pay savings from 2026/27 – the actual recurrent value will need to be determined as part of this engagement. 2.10Ensure that any new rota solutions and/or workforce planning solutions will take into account the Trust’s existing commitments to deliver its agreed levels of clinical activity and operational performance against the national waiting time targets. 2.2 Necessary Experience The selected Provider must have: 2.2.1 Demonstrated expertise in medical workforce analysis within NHS or equivalent healthcare systems. 2.2.2 Access to analytical tools. 2.2.3 Experience working collaboratively with clinical and operational leadership. 2.2.4 Understanding of NHS workforce contracts (Consultant, Resident Doctors, Agenda for Change) and EWTR compliance. 2.2.5 Ability to evidence medical workforce efficiencies. 2.3 Scope of Work The selected Provider will undertake the following: 2.3.1 Deep Dive Reviews • Two specialties (to be confirmed). • Detailed review of workforce utilisation, rota design, leave management, and skill mix optimisation / cost per WTE. • Simulation and modelling (e.g. 24/7 attendance flows, consultant presence planning, heat mapping). 2.3.2 Diagnostic Review • Light-touch reviews of 10 additional specialties where budget overspends are anticipated. • Data-driven diagnostics validated with specialty clinical directors and general managers. • To consider how/if any of the 10 specialties would benefit from a wider South East London Acute Provider collaborative approach. The collaborative is assessing what a scope of works could look like for an acute Provider-led approach to medical workforce rota management. 2.3.3 Implementation Planning • Develop a 12-week delivery programme, including milestones and resource requirements. • Provide an implementation roadmap with options for Phase 2 delivery support. 2.3.4 Capability Assessment and Knowledge Transfer • Assess the Trust’s internal capability to implement recommendations. • Provide training/knowledge transfer to build sustainable capability. 2.4 Deliverables The Provider will deliver: • Week 2: Baseline diagnostic report • Week 6: Draft deep dive findings • Week 10: Diagnostic outputs for 10 specialties • Week 12: Final consolidated report, including financial opportunity assessment, workforce plans, and implementation roadmap. • Final Presentation: Board-level presentation summarising findings, recommendations, and next steps. Lot 1: .

sig_7adc538f5fd2c51095a1.description: The contracting authority is striving for the digital modernisation of its individual agendas. One of these agendas is the parking policy of the city of Olomouc (hereinafter also referred to as the "PPMO"). Currently, the territorial scope of the parking policy applies to only two parking zones (A and B). In the planned expansion to zones C and D (including their sub-areas), it is also necessary to adjust and strengthen the existing part of the PPMO, which handles the registry of parking permits. Therefore, the contracting authority has decided to procure the acquisition of services for a new, modern system for the registry of parking permits, whereby these services will be used to optimise faster processing for citizens, ensure connection to state administration registries, and connection to other PPMO systems for more efficient processing of transferred data, and a modern graphical interface meeting current trends will also be achieved. The provision of the services of the system for the registry of parking permits must also fulfil all current legislative and security requirements. The subject matter of performance of this public contract is: a) performance of a requirements analysis, processing and implementation of the target concept, establishment and commissioning of the Portal Solution for the registry of parking permits (hereinafter referred to as the "PPMO Portal Solution"), data migration, testing, provision of training, provision of licences and provision of all other related performance necessary for the proper commissioning of the PPMO Portal Solution; b) provision of the PPMO Portal Solution as a service (in service mode), ensuring its maintenance and support, provision of the IT infrastructure necessary for the operation of the PPMO Portal Solution; c) provision of development services, analytical and methodical services, implementation of change requests and provision of other related performance based on the requirements of the contracting authority. A more detailed specification of the subject matter of performance is contained in the relevant parts of the tender documentation (hereinafter also referred to as the "TD"), in particular Appendix No. 2 and Appendix No. 3 of the TD. sig_7b09d53b26921a248462.description:
The subject matter of the procurement procedure is the provision and implementation of a software solution for workload automation including migration as well as associated services (support services, maintenance, documentation and training). The Beitragsservice (hereinafter referred to as the "contracting authority") currently uses the software IBM Workload Scheduler (hereinafter referred to as "IWS") with version V10.1 (formerly "IBM Tivoli Workload Scheduler") to automate its business processes across multiple instances. The IWS software must be supplemented by a workload automation software solution (hereinafter referred to as the "WLA software solution") as a "central scheduler" (on-premise) and installed ready for operation on all system environments (instances) in the three data centres (DCs). Implementation (implementation and migration) takes place at all three locations and must be planned conceptually for all DCs. Implementation will begin at the locations in Cologne. Subsequently, data replication of the job chains must take place for the Ismaning location. The objective is to achieve the functional interaction of the DCs. For example, functioning data replication and timely data synchronisation from the productive DC to the backup and failsafe DC must be installed. In the event of a disaster, the failsafe DC must take over the tasks of the productive DC (failover). The contractor (hereinafter referred to as the "contractor") shall deploy project management (including a project manager and deputy) to achieve the set goals. Project management encompasses initiation, planning, execution (implementation), monitoring and control until the completion of the project. The contracting authority intends to conclude a contract with the most economically advantageous tenderer for a period of 4 years. The contracting authority requires licences for the three DCs at the locations in Cologne and Ismaning in accordance with the specifications in the description of requirements. The contracting authority intends to relocate its operations to a new location in the Cologne area during the four-year term of the contract. The current location in Cologne is to be used until 2028. The objective according to current planning is to relocate the productive DC and backup DC before the relocation of the rest of the Beitragsservice. The operation of the DCs does not necessarily have to be at the new location of the contracting authority. In this context, parallel operation of the DCs at the old and new location may be necessary for a transitional period, as production operations must be maintained. Functional tests will also be required as part of the implementation of this measure. In any case, the licence offered (on-premise) must also include the relocation for the productive DC and backup DC and ensure indefinite use for this case. This licence must be part of the licence offered across all system environments (instances). The contractor must take the relocation of the Beitragsservice into account in its tender. Service part A - Provision and implementation of a WLA software solution at all locations and data centres The contractor must provide a platform-independent WLA software solution for the central workflow control, execution and technical monitoring of all process chains as well as for the automation of work processes at the locations in Cologne (productive DC and backup DC) and Ismaning (failsafe DC) of the contracting authority, ready for operation. The future contractor must implement the WLA software solution completely and fully operational at the named locations. The WLA software solution must also be implemented in the named DCs across all system environments (instances). Following the award of the contract, the future contractor must begin conceptual work and implementation at the Cologne location immediately and complete them within the previously agreed project schedule set at the kick-off meeting. Service part B - Licensing of a WLA software solution for all locations and DCs The contractor shall license the platform-independent WLA software solution for complete operation at all locations and DCs. Licensing must cover the use of at least 200.000 executable jobs per month across all locations and DCs. Licence use must be allocated and managed independently by the contracting authority. Licensing of the WLA software solution at the contracting authority's location in Cologne must include the following system environments (instances): - Production system of the contracting authority (at least 200.000 executable jobs per month) - Development, acceptance/test environments of the contracting authority - Backup DC of the contracting authority Licensing of the WLA software solution at the location of the failsafe DC in Ismaning must include the following system environments (instances): - Productive use of the licence in the event of a disaster (at least 200.000 executable jobs per month, "licence pool"). In this context, "licence pool" is understood to mean that the productive licence of the Cologne location will also be used reciprocally at the Ismaning location and utilised in the event of a disaster. Execution of tests by the contracting authority to test the functionality of the failsafe DC. Various jobs are started to check functionality. The servers on which the WLA software solution will run are located on the premises at the respective location. The failsafe DC in Ismaning is operated in cold standby and will be used exclusively in the event of a disaster involving a complete failure at the contracting authority's location. Parallel operation of the production system and the failsafe DC, and thus simultaneous use of the licence in production operations at both locations, is not intended. In the event of a disaster, it is intended to import a backup copy of the production system into the failsafe DC of the WLA software solution. However, parallel operation for testing must be covered by the licence use at both locations. Regular adjustments are made in the failsafe DC, e.g. for data replication between the productive DC and failsafe DC as well as emergency drills, which must also be covered by the scope of the licence. Continuation of the description under 5.1.

Continuation of the description in accordance with 2.1: In the event of a disaster, it can be assumed that the production system licence will not be used. In addition, the contractor shall provide the contracting authority unprompted and in a timely manner with the software updates/versions required and necessary for use and operation (e.g. software enhancements, bug fixes) including technical documentation for both locations, so that the contracting authority can keep the WLA software solution technically up to date. Service part C - Implementation of an interface between IWS and WLA software solution In order not to endanger ongoing DC operations at the contracting authority's location, parallel operation of both software products is required until the complete takeover of all IWS tasks by the WLA software solution to be procured. IWS and the WLA software solution must be operated jointly by the contracting authority during the contract term. For this purpose, it is necessary for both software products to interact via an interface and exchange data (e.g. events) in real time. The WLA software solution is the "leading system" ("meta-instance") and determines the job flow. For smooth parallel operation and migration from the existing IWS software to the WLA software solution, a reciprocally controlling technical interface between the two software solutions is required, which ensures smooth productive operation. Reciprocal control requires functions in both directions: The WLA software solution controls IWS The WLA software solution must start IWS jobs, pass on dependencies, receive status information and detect any errors. IWS controls the WLA software solution As long as jobs are still running in IWS, IWS must start the subsequent processes in the WLA software solution or wait for their completion. Service part D - Migration of IWS to the WLA software solution - Cologne location All services and tasks of the existing scheduler (IWS) across all instances must be taken over by the new WLA software solution as part of the migration. The contracting authority provides the required servers. The contractor must migrate approx. 6.000 IWS jobs to the WLA software solution in accordance with business and technical rules. The IWS jobs are currently executed an average of 110.000 times per month. The migration of the IWS jobs to the WLA software solution is to be implemented by the contractor in packages ("migration package for migration package"). The contractor ensures complete implementation and provides all support services required for this until the WLA solution is fully operational. Job networks that lie outside the z/OS environment in future must be operated entirely by the WLA software solution. Job networks that are still required in the z/OS environment must continue to be executed, controlled and operated by IWS until they are no longer required. Both schedulers must be operated with a functioning common interface until the complete migration of all IWS jobs. Following the migration of the respective packages, the Beitragsservice will carry out tests and accept the migration package upon successful testing. Acceptance will be granted if the control, processing and processing result for each job are identical in IWS and in the WLA software solution. The takeover of the migrated IWS job networks into the production environment is carried out by the contractor after acceptance of the migration packages. Takeover into the production environment requires a ready-to-operate failsafe DC. If the takeover into production should fail, the contractor must apply a fallback scenario. The future contractor must begin migration promptly after completion of the implementation and commissioning of the WLA software solution. The migration of all IWS jobs including acceptance must take place within the agreed project schedule. Ismaning location - Following implementation and commissioning of the WLA software solution as well as complete migration including acceptance at the location in Cologne, the contractor must also implement and commission the WLA software solution in the system environment(s) of the failsafe DC at the Ismaning location and establish operational readiness for "cold standby" and the execution of tests. A functional test is carried out. The contracting authority provides the required servers. Acceptance is granted if the control, processing and processing result per job are identical to the production system. Service part E - Training and documentation Upon completion of the implementation phase, the contractor shall conduct role-specific training at the contracting authority's premises in Cologne. A maximum of 5 employees of the contracting authority will be trained. Service part F - Support / SLAs for incident management - The contracting authority must be able to report faults to the contractor via a ticket system, by email or by telephone. The processing of service requests, faults or changes is carried out via a tool belonging to the bidder, to which responsible employees of the contracting authority have access rights. System operations are divided in terms of time into online and batch operations. Online operation Monday to Friday between 06:00 and 19:15 hours, on approx. 20 days p.a. Saturdays from 06:00 to 13:30 hours. Batch operations take place during the remaining time. Maintenance work and system migrations or firmware/driver updates must be carried out outside of production operations (Mon. - Fri. between 19:15 and 06:00 hours or at weekends or on public holidays). Maintenance work in the test system during service hours is accompanied by the contracting authority. The execution of the work is the responsibility of the contracting authority. The contractor must ensure service hours Monday to Friday (excluding nationwide public holidays) from 06:30 to 17:00 hours. Response times depend on the service hour and priority. Compliance with response times must be ensured through the deployment of qualified and expert personnel.

Specifically, the candidate contractor shall provide: The subject of the Contract is broken down into the following Work Packages (WPs): Work Package 1 (WP 1): Project Administrative Support Services  Provision of administrative information  Support in the organisation of project implementation, as well as in specific matters of electronic management, routing and archiving of documents  Support in the management and processing of daily tasks of the Ministry of Digital Governance and/or any entity with which it cooperates in the context of managing/executing projects concerning the Digital Transformation of the Country  Support in specific matters of management, routing and archiving of physical and electronic archives  Support to the Committees (Advisory, Objections and Verification, Monitoring and Project Acceptance) during their meetings, providing mainly secretarial support services  Ensuring regular monitoring and management of electronic correspondence  Drafting of various letters - documents that may be required during the finalisation of Administrative Controls  General administrative support of the Ministry of Digital Governance, which shall determine the framework for the performance of duties and the place of provision of each supportive administrative service in cooperation, if required, with the contracting authority Work Package 2 (WP 2): IT Services  Creation and implementation of a Communication Plan with the end users of the systems of Information Society S.A. (e.g. for handling change requests, help-desk)  Evolution/development/optimisation/customisation services for the applications of Information Society S.A.  Backing up of all data  Management and control of changes and additional requirements (change management, bug tracking) of information systems of Information Society S.A.  Updating – management of the content of the websites managed by the Ministry whenever deemed necessary and in accordance with its requirements  Support in the documentation, management and indexing of the files and information data monitored and managed by "Information Society S.A." Work Package 3 (WP 3): Project Management & Administration Mechanism (PM)  Monitoring the implementation of the Programme Agreement of the Ministry of Digital Governance with Information Society S.A. for the Digital Transformation of the Country  Supervision and monitoring of compliance with the obligations of the Ministry of Digital Governance towards the Managing Authority as well as any other external supervising body and/or partner in the context of the execution of the project for the Digital Transformation of the Country  Continuous communication with the supervised bodies of the Ministry as well as the contractors of the projects in the course of their execution regarding any issue or problem that may arise  Identification of control points, also based on the life cycle of the individual actions/projects  Systematic collection of information and data regarding the progress of individual actions/projects  Submission of periodic and ad-hoc reports Work Package 4 (WP 4): Project Financial Support Services  Extraction of statistical data in the context of contract execution  Financial monitoring and management of projects  Provision of financial data and statistics  Assistance in the design and management of financial programmes and actions, ensuring the absorption and relevant indicators Creation of periodic reports analysing the financial status of projects and planned activities [para. 1.3 & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]
sig_7b500a2d15a12453a1cd.title: «Provision of Support Services to «Information Society S.A.» in its capacity as the Main Implementation Arm in the context of the execution of projects for the Digital Transformation of the Country»
