sig_7b71a1fa4a99a6c34386.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of the necessary actions to ensure the Business Continuity of selected public administration bodies, so that the employees to be selected are able to fulfil their work obligations remotely in a secure manner. The project is expected to upgrade the operational capacity of public sector executives and will ensure for public servants seamless access by the necessary state officials to critical IT systems and infrastructure regardless of conditions. The main subjects of the project are: • the provision of laptops to a selected group of executives of public bodies, • the provision of connections for data exchange inside and outside SYZEFXIS II. The services provided are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: 30213000-5 (Personal Computers), 72000000-5 (Information technology services: consulting, software development, Internet and support) and 64212000-5 (Mobile telecommunication services). The subject of this contract is not subdivided into lots. Tenders are accepted for the whole of the subject. Following the conclusion of the initial contract, during the implementation of the project and before the expiry of the contract, the Contracting Authority may decide to exercise an option by increasing the physical scope of the project (as described herein) up to twenty per cent (20%) of the contract price. Before the expiry of the contract, the Project Owner may decide to exercise a maintenance option up to the amount of 837.684,00 € excluding VAT (budget with VAT: 1.038.728,16 €, VAT 24% 201.044,16 €), based on the Financial Tender of the Candidate Contractor, for maintenance services (as described in Appendix I). Therefore, the total maximum estimated value of the contract, including the options as mentioned above, amounts to the sum of 3.629.964,00 € excluding VAT (budget with VAT: 4.501.155,36 €, VAT 24% 871.191,36 €). The exercise of the aforementioned options is subject to the securing of their financing. The duration of the contract is set at nine (9) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables, as specified in Appendix I of this document. A detailed description of the physical and financial subject of the contract is given in APPENDIX I - Detailed Description of the Physical and Financial Subject of the Contract or in another descriptive document of this Notice. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3, APPENDIX I & II of the Notice]

sig_7b8e4d6e3e22331ca8ae.description: contracting with companies specialised in the supply of products and provision of services to optimise the management of the main waste produced at the US, including the establishment of a system for placing skips for the sorting of types of non-hazardous waste produced in buildings, all hazardous waste management operations within the Centres and Departments, as well as consolidating the organisation of a paper collection system for recycling and for treating sensitive documentation and proceeding with its destruction, in accordance with the criteria established in the applicable regulatory framework. In addition, it includes the need to have monitoring and traceability of all waste, from its production to its proper disposal. Selective paper removal The paper collection service for recycling must be a service provided upon request by the US. To this end, only requests registered in a computer application that the US will make available to the winning contractor may be met. Companies must service requests within 5 working days from the date of the request. Upon completion of the work, the winning contractor must fill out an electronic register in the aforementioned computer application, containing the following information: building where the work is carried out, date of performance of such work, approximate kilograms removed and price of the action. The contractor, together with the invoice, must present a delivery note signed by the US justifying the work carried out. Destruction of documentation Documentation collected on any medium shall be destroyed when requested by the US, in accordance with the provisions of the regulations in force on data protection. The destruction of paper information must be carried out, with a level 4, into particles smaller than 30 mm2 (5 x 5 mm), in accordance with the DIN standard 32757-1. Upon completion of the work, the winning contractor must fill out an electronic register containing the following information: building where the work is carried out, date of performance, approximate kilograms destroyed and price of the action. The US will provide the winning contractor with access to a computer application where they must record this information.
sig_7b8e4d6e3e22331ca8ae.title: Framework Agreement for waste removal at the University of Seville.

sig_7b9f8253f870f2b59f85.description: The subject of procurement is the analysis, design, development, implementation, testing, commissioning, user training, and warranty maintenance of the integrated information system for agroecological zoning of the Republic of Croatia (hereinafter: AEZ system). The system must represent the central national platform for the collection, management, analysis, modelling, visualisation, and distribution of agroecological data and the results of agroecological analyses. The aim of the system is to establish a unified digital environment that enables the identification and monitoring of agroecological zones, the assessment of suitability for individual agricultural crops, the preparation of scenario analyses, and support for expert and strategic decision-making in the field of agricultural policy, natural resource management, and adaptation to climate change. The system must enable the processing of large amounts of spatial and temporal data, the execution of complex analytical processes, and the distribution of results via web GIS interfaces and standardised service interfaces. In the document Annex I – Project of Agroecological Zoning of the Republic of Croatia 2025–2028, the services as well as the functional and non-functional requirements that the delivered application solution must include are described in detail. All of the above are necessary elements of the delivered solution. Phase 1 – Establishment of the geospatial platform and basic functionalities Phase 2 – Development of the agroecological zoning analytical system Phase 3 – Production application of agroecological zoning Upon completion of the project, a fully functional solution must be delivered to the Contracting Authority which enables: 1. calculation of the national agroecological zones of the Republic of Croatia 2. assessment of suitability for agricultural crops 3. comparison of different climate scenarios and development scenarios of individual agricultural crops based on input data and predictive models 4. centralised management of spatial and analytical data 5. web GIS review of agroecological zones 6. data exchange via standard OGC and REST services 7. long-term upgradability and sustainability of the system
sig_7b9f8253f870f2b59f85.title: Agroekološko zoniranje

sig_7bd1b1b9ea6e3dfb8af1.description: NOTE! This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice of the initiation of market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation of a local detailed planning software procurement and invites suppliers to a market dialogue. The subject of the procurement is a CAD software solution compliant with the Act on the Built Environment Information System (431/2023) and the requirements of the Ryhti system for the production of data model-based local detailed plans. The local detailed planning software solution is used for the design and drawing of local detailed plans at various stages of the planning process together with other systems in use within the Urban Environment sector of the City of Espoo. In addition to this, the software solution is used for traffic planning and making 3D models. In traffic planning, precise street geometries are drawn up and it is ensured that sufficient space is reserved for traffic arrangements and intra-block functions, such as parking and service traffic. Traffic planning carries out general planning, street maps and cross-sections, among other things, as well as the design of street grading, in connection with which longitudinal and cross-section profiles are produced. The drawing up of a local detailed plan is a long-standing process lasting an estimated 2-5 years. Fewer than 100 local detailed plans are completed in Espoo per year, and approximately 90% of them also include traffic plans. In a single local detailed planning project, there are on average approx. 100 documents related to local detailed planning and traffic planning, which are stored mainly in the document management system. The local detailed planning and traffic planning software solution has a total of approximately 65 users. Currently, local detailed planning and traffic planning at the City of Espoo is carried out mainly using Bentley design software. In addition to this, local detailed planning data is managed in the Trimble Locus municipal information system and the document management system. In the future, the permanent plan identifier will be obtained from the Ryhti system into Trimble Locus's plan register, from where it is copied into the local detailed plan drawing software. Local detailed plans are transferred as a JSON file transfer to Trimble Locus Cloud for export to the Ryhti system. Plans are transferred to the Ryhti system from Trimble Locus, where the management of plan objects and plan amendments as well as the transfer of plan attachments to the Ryhti system also take place. The management of reference data utilised in the drawing up of traffic plans will continue to take place in the document management system. The resulting street maps and other material supporting planning will be attached as part of the local detailed plan description annex material and transferred to the Ryhti system. Swept path analyses are carried out using AutoTURN software. The subject of the procurement is a system to be procured as a service, provisionally in accordance with the following: - Ready-to-use CAD software with user licenses - Local detailed plan Ryhti objects database - Service deployment and customisation for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Additional procurement opportunities related to the subject of the procurement - System further development and expert services according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the local detailed planning and traffic planning software solution are aimed to cover, among other things, the following: - Tasks related to local detailed planning design - Production of data model-based local detailed plans - Traffic planning - Making 3D models illustrating plans - Making 3D models of traffic planning streets - Ryhti objects database - File-based transfer of plan data to the Ryhti system via the Trimble Locus municipal information system - Reporting - Management of user roles and user rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation concerning the local detailed planning software procurement. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the invitation to tender. MARKET DIALOGUE SCHEDULE The market dialogue will provisionally take place in two phases: 1. Via Teams provisionally during weeks 43-44. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite a maximum of 4 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the request for information responses. The aim of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with companies and products on the market, for example, through suppliers' company and product presentations and demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who registered for the market dialogue for commenting during an estimated period between November 2026 and January 2027. The second phase of the market dialogue will take place electronically. Written material will be sent to all those registered for the market dialogue for review. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary invitation to tender, requirement specifications and contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to hold additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. The contracting authority's aim is to launch the actual procurement procedure in the spring of 2027 and the implementation project provisionally in the autumn of 2027, such that the new system can be put into use in the spring of 2028.
sig_7bd1b1b9ea6e3dfb8af1.title: Market dialogue call and request for information: Procurement of local detailed planning software

sig_7c46b119a28d97bbcbbf.description: The subject matter of the tender is the assumption of the function of external data protection officer pursuant to Art. 37 et seq. of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) for ALDB GmbH. The data protection officer advises and supports the contracting authority in all business areas on the subject of data protection law and monitors compliance with all data protection requirements. Lot LOT-0001: Provision of services of an external data protection officer. 1 Tasks of the contractor In particular, the following tasks shall be undertaken by the contractor: - Advising and monitoring compliance with data protection regulations - Observing developments in data protection law - Monitoring data processing operations and data protection controls - Record of processing activities - Data protection impact assessments - Advising on new projects and processing operations - Contracts and data protection agreements - Data subject rights - Data breaches - Contact person for employees and contractual partners - Cooperation with the supervisory authority - Documentation and reporting - Awareness-raising and training of employees - Expertise and further training - Maintenance of data protection management - Optional: Assumption of the function of AI officer 2 Availability and response time On working days between 09:00 hours and 17:00 hours, within 24 hours of contact. Enquiries are processed remotely within Germany. In the event of data protection incidents, a maximum response time of 240 minutes is required on working days within the service hours of 09:00-17:00 hours. The response must at least indicate that the content of the enquiry has been noted. A response using an automated and/or semi-automated standard email that merely confirms receipt of the enquiry is not sufficient. If the data protection officer deployed by the contractor is unavailable, e.g. due to holiday or illness etc., a deputy shall perform the duties. The deputy must be named at the start of services, including any differing contact details. 3 Requirements for the qualification of the personnel deployed - valid certification as a CIPM and/or CIPP/E or equivalent certification (equivalent certifications are those that require a minimum CPE proof within periods of 2-3 years each to maintain validity and that are accredited according to ANSI/ISO standards) - training as a data protection officer and regular participation (at least once a year) in further training on data protection within the last 4 years - activity as a data protection officer for at least 5 years - presence of an already valid extended security clearance under classified information protection pursuant to Section 9 of the Security Clearance Act (SÜG). For details, see the specification of services

sig_7c62c0c036b86dee1e2d.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Multi-Domain Force Applications and Traffic Management for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (M-FAT) BAA NUMBER: FA8750-25-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 4 AUG 2030. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 4 AUG 2030, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY26 by 05 SEP 2025 FY27 by 31 AUG 2026 FY28 by 31 AUG 2027 FY29 by 31 AUG 2028 FY30 by 31 AUG 2029 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking innovative research to enhance Counter-small Unmanned Aerial System (C-sUAS) kill chain and point defense capabilities through advancements in Electronic Warfare (EW), Cyberspace Operations (CO), Command and Control (C2) Automation and Autonomy, Low-Collateral Defeat (LCD), Low-Collateral Effect Interceptors (LCEI)/Blue Force Interceptors (BFI), and communications. One goal is to blur the line between EW and CO by developing cyberspace countermeasures that disrupt sUAS operations, particularly command and control links. This includes improving system resiliency in contested environments and prioritizing low-collateral damage solutions. C2 advancements aim to automate and optimize responses to sUAS threats, especially swarm attacks, through AI/ML, sensor fusion, and automated decision-making. Research into LCD/LCEI/BFI could lead to the development of low-cost, autonomous interceptors with integrated EW/CO capabilities and other C-sUAS payloads. Further research will focus on improving sensor technologies for enhanced detection, identification, and tracking, as well as developing a library for storing and indexing cyberspace effects. In parallel, efforts will be made to advance UAS Traffic Management (UTM) systems, integrating them with existing air traffic control, enabling safe integration of unmanned aircraft into the airspace. Finally, communication systems will be enhanced through advanced modeling and simulation, development of resilient waveforms and networking protocols for swarm operations, and integration of AI for network optimization and spectrum management. sig_7cad23f3c9662a29a582.description: In the context of this initiative, the implementation of an Action for the systematic enhancement of the financial literacy of primary and secondary education pupils will be financed, as well as the active involvement of teachers, Education Advisers and parents in the development of responsible financial knowledge, skills and attitudes. Specifically, the programme aims to enable pupils to understand basic economic and financial concepts, manage their available resources responsibly, plan needs and expenditure, evaluate alternative options and make informed decisions in their daily lives. At the same time, it seeks to strengthen their ability to recognise risks associated with digital transactions, misleading advertising, over-indebtedness, financial scams and other precarious practices. The programme also seeks to empower teachers with appropriate educational material, knowledge and methodological tools for the effective teaching of financial literacy. Education Advisers will support training/information dissemination, pedagogical guidance and the sharing of good practices, while parents will be encouraged to contribute to the cultivation of healthy financial habits within the family environment. Through the cooperation of the school community and the family, the programme aims to shape responsible, critically thinking and financially informed citizens who will be able to meet the demands of daily life and the challenges of a constantly changing economic and digital environment. The programme is developed along two interdependent axes: on the one hand, the production of evidence-based knowledge through targeted study and, on the other hand, based on the results of the relevant study, the design and implementation of educational actions for pupils, teachers, Education Advisers and parents. The implementation of the programme will be of a pilot and feedback nature. Educational tools and actions will be utilised in school units of various levels and types, evaluated for their effectiveness, usability and pedagogical suitability, and revised based on emerging data. In this way, the study and educational interventions will not operate as independent activities, but as parts of a unified cycle of investigation, design, implementation, evaluation and improvement. The programme includes studies, actions and tools. Upon completion of the programme, an evaluation of the effectiveness of the pilot interventions and the formulation of proposals for the gradual expansion of the programme will take place. The programme includes horizontal actions concerning the information, dissemination and publicity of the project. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-six (36) months from its signature. The duration of the contract may be extended in the event of an amendment to the decision incorporating the projects into the Public Investment Programme (TPA). The subdivision of the contract subject matter into lots (according to the provisions of art. 59 of law 4412/2016) is not possible, as the deliverables of the contract are judged to be inextricably linked and interdependent. The Total Project Budget – Estimated Value of the contract amounts to 3.225.806,45 € excluding VAT, i.e. 4.000.000,00 € including VAT of 24%. The services provided are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: 71241000-9: Feasibility study, advisory, analysis services 72212190-7: Educational software development services 72262000-9: Software development services 72000000-5: Information technology services: consulting, software development, Internet and support 80000000-4: Training and tuition services 80533100-0: IT training services 79340000-9: Advertising and marketing services 79950000-8: Exhibition and conference organisation services 79951000-5: Seminar organisation services The contract award criterion is the most economically advantageous tender based on the best price-quality ratio.

(11) of Law No 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and completions, it is necessary that the drafting of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. sig_7cfa598d5e3dd2a2bcda.description: The principle of open justice is crucial. His Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS) is committed to supporting greater transparency of courts and tribunals data. We are seeking to engage with potential applicants for the new courts and tribunals non-exclusive third party data licence which will grant successful licence applicants permission to undertake computational analysis of information published by the Court and Tribunal Hearings Service (CaTH) (https://www.court-tribunal-hearings.service.gov.uk/). The information available under this licence will in time encompass all hearing lists for all courts and tribunals administered by HMCTS and registers of outcomes from the criminal courts. Other information may be made available in the future. The information will be available to successful licence applicants in a standard, machine-readable form through CaTH’s application programming interface (API). The purpose of this market engagement is to understand the views of potential applicants for the licence on topics including: 1. Other information that HMCTS should seek to prioritise and publish via CaTH; 2. The implications of HMCTS’s proposed retention terms for data provided under the licence; 3. Potential data re-use purposes 4. Restrictions on the use of the data 5. Security measures that licensees will have to have in place 6. Restrictions on where globally data can be processed We are interested in hearing from a range of organisations and individuals, including, but not limited to: journalists and the accredited news media; lawtech firms and legal publishers; research institutes and compliance or data analytics firms. The findings from this market engagement will help to inform the development of the licence and its payment model. This session will not cover the detail of the application process for a licence. We are aiming to share this detail in April 2026. Event Details HMCTS invites interested organisations to attend a virtual market engagement event on 04th March 2026 which will be delivered via MS Teams and take place 10:00 – 11:30 (UK). Agenda: - Introduction and purpose of the market engagement - An overview of the licence - What data would be shared under the licence and onwards re-use - Implications of proposed retention terms - Pricing Model - Next steps for further engagement Key questions to explore: - For what purpose would you seek to computationally re-use courts and tribunals listing and registers of outcomes data? - What functionality/capability/information would you like from the CaTH service beyond what is currently available? - What barriers (barring exemptions under data protection law) would HMCTS’s proposed retention terms place in being able to perform computational analysis for your proposed use case? - Would HMCTS’s proposed and future pricing model place unreasonable barriers that would prevent you/your organisation being able to reasonably afford a licence? Interested parties are required to complete the following actions: 1. Register for an account through the MoJ Sourcing Portal at https://ministryofjusticecommercial.bravosolution.co.uk 2. Navigate to the left side menu and click on 'PQQs Open to All Suppliers' > find and click on ‘PQQ_567 - HMCTS Third Party Courts Data Licence - Market Engagement’ - for the avoidance of doubt this is not an actual PQQ but just a space on our sourcing system to coordinate market engagement activities. There are no mandatory actions to take. 3. Interested parties must express an interest by clicking 'Express interest' and will then be able to view the detail relating to market engagement in the ‘My Response’ tab. The event will be recorded and made available for the duration of the engagement activity. Legal disclaimer: this recording is for private, authorised viewing only and may not be redistributed. The session will have the opportunity for Q&A on submission, with questions answered following the session in writing, these will be published in the attachments tab on the MoJ Sourcing Portal. Following the event, HMCTS will distribute a questionnaire to attendees to gain further information and insight to the topics covered in the session. The ‘PQQ_567 - HMCTS Third Party Courts Data Licence - Market Engagement’ area will be the forum used to communicate future events or communications in relation to the market engagement activity. The Engagement deadline in this notice reflects the closing date for questionnaire submission by Suppliers following the session. Contract dates and transparency notice details are not reflective of licence dates. Lot 1: .
sig_7cfa598d5e3dd2a2bcda.title: prj_16023 - HMCTS Third Party Courts Data Licence

sig_7cfb0d0cf53077dbe97a.description: Full information is provided within the specification. DCMS are seeking to commission "what works" research into the impact and effectiveness of AI adoption interventions within DCMS sectors. We are interested in two broad sets of questions. The first is analysis of how businesses within DCMS sectors that are in the process of adopting AI achieve this, the challenges they face and the opportunities and benefits realised. We anticipate this will be explored through an ethnographic study that observes how individuals and teams actually use AI tools in their jobs. The second set of questions is what policy interventions work best to support businesses that wish to adopt AI, which we anticipate will be answered by testing hypothetical interventions through randomised control trials (RCTs). Bidders will be able to propose alternative methodologies if they think they suit these questions better; the core need for this project is to produce direct, robust evidence of what works, as opposed to what is self-reported (e.g. through interviews, focus groups, surveys, and similar) to work. Lot 1: .
sig_7cfb0d0cf53077dbe97a.title: What works in AI Adoption within DCMS Sectors

sig_7d05957c905f2206a9a2.description: SOURCING PROCEDURE: The AI Tutoring Tools Pioneer Programme contracts (a maximum of eight (8) identical contracts) will be awarded under a Procurement Act 2023 Section 3) (6) and Schedule 2, Part 2, paragraph 22, 2) (b), (c) subject-matter exemption for research and development services. The contracts to be awarded are exempt contracts and for that reason the procurement is not subject to the Procurement Act 2023. The outputs of the proposed contracts are intended for the benefit of the public and do not include the provision of AI Tutoring Tools. The latter would be procured via other sourcing procedures separate from this Pioneers Programme procurement. These contracts answer the need for research and development of a high-quality standard for AI Tutoring Tools. Although there is a wide range of Tutoring Tools available on the market, there is no established offer that meets the complete specification to a high-quality standard, encompassing all the necessary elements of an exceptional AI Tutoring Tool. Elements being for instance the digital curriculum (to be published) and multiple sources of data which require review. AI driven Tutoring Tools currently on the market are limited in quantity, scope and evidence base with few providing full tutoring capacity and with limited public access to the research and development that underpins them. The proposed contracts seek to research and co-design a high-quality, all-encompassing standard for AI Tutoring Tools and to initiate the development of innovative, effective and safe AI Tutoring Tools to that high-quality, all-encompassing standard thereby being the most transformative for educational outcomes. The aim of the Programme is to research, trial, develop and enable the future scalability and commercialisation of AI Tutoring Tools of the highest calibre which, alongside teachers, will improve the academic attainment of pupils across England, particularly the most disadvantaged. INSTRUCTIONS TO PARTICIPATE: This informal procurement process, which includes a pre-qualification and technical capability moderated evaluation, is carried upon invitation to selected suppliers, however if a supplier believes they meet the pre-qualification criteria detailed in this notice, they may express interest in participating via the eProcurement platform (Jaggaer) “AI Tutoring Tools Reading Room – DfE Content Store” by the 1st of May 2026 via link below: https://beisgroup.ukp.app.jaggaer.com/esop/toolkit/opportunity/current/list.si?resetstored=true On the 1st of May 026, all suppliers invited and which have expressed interest in participating will receive a link to access the pre-qualification and technical capability questionnaire on the eProcurement platform (Jaggaer) “AI Tutoring Tools Pioneer Programme – Subject-Matter Exemption - Research and Development” project. PRE-QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: This is an ambitious programme of work for which I.AI are looking for exceptional suppliers across EdTech and AI development, who have a proven track record of building high-calibre products and delivering them at scale (see below the note on products capability). Suppliers wishing to participate in this Pioneers Programme informal procurement process must meet the following pre-qualification conditions on:1) AI and/or EdTech expertise and scale; and 2) Existing product expertise. The pre-qualification assessment will require that suppliers participating in this informal procurement (alone or together with any consortium they may choose to form), apply in partnership with three to four partner schools in England, with above-average rates of disadvantage (25.7% FSM). To ensure that suppliers are best placed to develop truly innovative AI Tutoring Tools, DSIT/I.AI are looking for suppliers (or consortia) that combine AI innovation with strong Edtech experience and the ability to deliver successful products at scale in England. This proven scalability experience requirement is vital to inform and assist the research and development of a common standard that enables by default the scalability-readiness sought. Suppliers / consortia should either: 1. Have exceptional expertise delivering Edtech products at scale in England, and have access to (internally, or via a partnership or subcontracting) strong expertise for AI development; or 2. Have exceptional expertise delivering innovative AI products at scale, and have access to (internally, or via partnership) strong expertise for delivering Edtech within England. While scale must be evidenced for one of these capabilities, it is not a requirement for the other. We welcome proposals that include SMEs and more bespoke, smaller scale product experience, where they demonstrate the expertise needed. In addition to the above, you must be able to demonstrate strong expertise for the other capability (EdTech / AI). Where not covered by your ‘exceptional’ capability, this must include: • Experience delivering in schools in England • Strong pedagogical expertise, consistent with pedagogical approaches in England • Experience delivering products with substantive generative AI components at scale To be considered as ‘exceptional expertise’, suppliers / consortia should: · Demonstrate significant scale as an AI lab, or be an Edtech company with significant scale in secondary schools in England. · Have deep in-house expertise and talent required to lead cutting-edge, sector wide innovation. · Have a track record of delivering high quality products. Applications must include 3-4 partner schools that suppliers will work with for co-design activity. These school and multi-academy trust (MAT) partners must meet the following criteria: * Must be state-funded schools based in England * Have a minimum of 500 students across their Year 9 & Year 10 cohorts (total across all partner schools) * At least three partner schools must have above the national average (25.7%) of students that qualify for FSM * Must have an adequate Ofsted rating: ** If last inspected by Ofsted under the previous arrangement before September 2024, partner schools must have a single headline grade of Good or Outstanding ** If last inspected by Ofsted under the previous arrangement between September 2024 and November 2025, partner schools must be graded Good or Outstanding for the Leadership and Management sub-judgment ** If inspected by Ofsted under the new arrangements from November 2025, partner schools must be graded as expected standard or higher for Leadership and Governance * Must not be in a ‘category of concern’ * Must not be part of an academy trust that is subject to a notice to improve * Must have no unresolved safeguarding or compliance issues that the DfE is involved with. * A maximum of one partner school may be selective. Schools must confirm their eligibility status as part of the application. From September 2026, suppliers may be partnered with additional schools (supported by DfE) or participate in wider activity with additional schools to explore the use of their tools across wider contexts, which will include schools in areas of higher deprivation and/or schools with lower technology maturity on an ‘as needed’ basis. While there is no requirement on regional diversity for individual applications, we will be looking to ensure regional diversity across the portfolio of grants made. NOTE ON PRODUCTS CAPABILITY: Through this programme, suppliers will be rapidly iterating on existing products, to test opportunities for advanced functionality and curriculum integration. DSIT/I.AI will therefore be working with suppliers that already have a relevant base product at a good level of maturity. This product must be deployed in a relevant environment (e.g., a school or tutoring context, with secondary school age pupils), not just in a laboratory or test environment. Examples of eligible products include (but are not limited to): • An AI feedback tool that analyses pupil work and provides formative feedback, already piloted with pupils or teachers • A chatbot that can answer curriculum-aligned questions and has been used by pupils for tutoring support • A question-generation engine that produces curriculum-aligned practice questions, validated through use in a school or tutoring setting • Adaptive tutoring systems • A system for tracking and synthesising student progress • Curriculum-aligned pupil-facing edtech tools NOTE ON INFORMATION TO THE WIDER MARKET AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY: The high-quality, all-encompassing standard co-designed during these contracts and the information shared by the participants (including the schools) with the Pioneer Programme suppliers, will be owned by DSIT/I.AI and will be shared with the wider market via a dedicated Pioneers Programme Reading Room. More information on how to request access to this Reading Room is below. The foreground intellectual property (IP) created for the purposes of any possible prototype AI Tutoring Tool will be the property of the individual Pioneer Programme suppliers, and will not be widely shared. sig_7d0f9801ffe9482059e7.description: The objective of the procurement is to enter into a contract for the delivery of external professional and methodic assistance for the Coordination Project in DFØ. The coordination project shall map and analyse coordination possibilities across DFØ ́s divisions and propose a prioritised list of relevant measures. The project will be carried out in three phases. Phase 2 (The current situation, June - November 2026) is the core delivery. The contract also includes an option for phase 3 (Vision and concepts, November 2026 - February 2027) and phase 4 (Gap-analyses and action plan, March-June 2027). The coordination project is a transverse project in DFØ that shall strengthen the co-ordination across the entity. The project is anchored in DFØ ́s business strategy 2025-2030 and the activity plan 2026, and the project ́s mandate has been decided in the management group. The aim is to increase DFØ ́s strategic scope of action by exploring and assessing how the entity is organised and how the resources are utilised across the divisions.

sig_7d2ef0beefa14a095dd0.description: The provision of temporary and interim staff services to the Scottish Public Sector Lot 1: . The Scottish Procurement and Property Directorate (SPPD) is the organisation tasked with procuring requirements on behalf of Scottish Public Sector Bodies. The current Scottish Government collaborative Temporary and Interim Staff Services Frameworks are a suite of four individual multi supplier Framework Agreements which commenced on 13 April 2023 and are due to expire on 12 April 2027. They are all National Category A Frameworks which are open to all public sector organisations throughout Scotland. They are designed to provide the full range of commonly sought temporary and interim staff services required for daily business. These are national collaborative Frameworks, for commonly required, regularly sought temporary and interim staff services roles/assignments across the Scottish public sector. These Frameworks are intended solely for short term, gap filling purposes and are not intended as an alternative to permanent or fixed term appointment (FTA) recruitment. Work has commenced in developing the procurement strategy options including canvassing of stakeholders views. In order to complete and finalise the strategy, SPPD recognises the value of suppliers having the opportunity to contribute to this process on a non-competitive, non-judgemental basis. This request for information is aimed at collating those views from market participants. Framework participants will be expected to provide a range of Fair Work First measures. This information may be utilised in developing the procurement strategy to help deliver contractual arrangements for Temporary and Interim Staff Services requirements. This notice is issued for information only and does not constitute a call for competition. Scottish Government and the Scottish Ministers shall have no liability for any costs, however incurred, by those attending any information days, attendance at meetings, or involvement in the proposed procurement process. Suppliers and other interested parties should read and complete the following Request for Information Online Questionnaire using the link below. https://forms.office.com/e/cNzCefdZzU The questionnaire will be available for all interested parties until COP 3 March 2026.
sig_7d2ef0beefa14a095dd0.title: Framework for the Provision of Temporary and Interim Staff Services

sig_7d5ac05c9aa6944e22e1.description: The service concerns the development and operation (cloud-based) of a digital signage system operating in parallel and complementarily, supporting the main physical signage system that makes up the above. The digital signage system will enhance and enrich all operations performed by traditional physical signage systems (direction, location, information), while adding new ones (navigation, asset tagging, extraction of primary data, etc.). The digital signage system will perform a set of functionalities inextricably linked to the individual physical signage elements, drawing data from a rich and open database with documented content, will be able to operate with a standalone application, will have an operational connection with the destination management information system of the Region of Peloponnese and will offer access to it for existing users (Single Sign On), while a special widget will also be developed which on the one hand will allow the use of the digital signage system by any body that manages an individual local trail network and maintains a web portal, and on the other hand will allow, in the future, its use in the context of installing new physical signage systems, provided that the relevant technical specifications are met.

sig_7d71b850cff5bb5323b2.description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection. CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.
sig_7d71b850cff5bb5323b2.title: Framework service contract for the collection of meteorological and hydrological in-situ data in support to the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Flood Early Warning Systems

sig_7daf0dc13c7bde3d2cd4.description: This contract constitutes Sub-project 3 of the Project "Development of the institution, infrastructure, capabilities and competencies for the data governance of the public sector, their availability for reuse and the provision of relevant services to the public and private sector, in Greece - Phase A" (OPS TA 5158667), which is implemented within the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan "Greece 2.0". The contract concerns the implementation of actions related to awareness-raising, promotion, networking, consultation, training, increasing the degree of impact of the Project, indicatively regarding its role in the creation of a Digital Transition Indicators Observatory, in the creation of a data utilisation platform, in the assessment of the efficiency of Action 16778 "Digitisation of archives and related services", as well as as an Executive Mechanism of the Bureaucracy Observatory (BO). More specifically, the requested services are included within the framework of the following Work Packages: Work Package 1 (WP1): Implementation of awareness-raising actions. It includes the design and production of printed and other promotional and informative material, as well as the design and organisation of events/workshops, consultations and other awareness-raising actions in order to inform both citizens, businesses and other bodies about the pivotal and crucial role of the Digital Transition Indicators Observatory, the assessment of the efficiency of the Digitisation of Action 16778, the Bureaucracy Observatory, but also the importance of proper governance of public data in Greece, with the ultimate goal of promoting relevant initiatives and creating a sense of trust among citizens and businesses towards the Public Administration and the role that relevant initiatives will play. Work Package 2 (WP2): Implementation of publicity actions. It includes the promotion of the materials that will be produced for the advertising campaign, from Work Package 1. Work Package 3 (WP3): Development of informative material and conduct of information sessions. It includes the implementation of training actions through the development of educational material and the conduct of the corresponding training. The training aims, on the one hand, to inform and familiarise Public Administration executives regarding the operation of the EKT Data Marketplace and, on the other hand, to inform the wider ecosystem of the Bureaucracy Observatory regarding the methodology for measuring administrative burdens.

sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.description: The NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program aims to expand access to the compute required for AI-enabled scientific discovery and to transform the research, education, and training opportunities offered by institutions of higher education. AI Infrastructure Hubs will connect researchers to new compute infrastructure that leverages contributions from state governments, research institutions, industry, and philanthropy, accelerating AI-enabled discovery across science and engineering and developing a skilled technical workforce for AI use in the scientific enterprise. The program responds to a core tenet of Science: A New Golden Age to renew America’s research and development (R&D) for changes in today’s scientific enterprise, including the role of AI in laying the foundation for a new era of scientific discovery and the growing role of industry and philanthropy in funding R&D. In response, the Administration’s FY28 R&D Priorities Memorandum called for investing in AI for science as a national mission and expanding the scale of, and flexible access to, advanced compute and data infrastructure that researchers now require for frontier scientific discovery. Each AI Infrastructure Hub will be organized as a flexible state or regional consortium of state and local governments, research institutions, philanthropies, and the private sector. Consortia will be responsible for all funding for new or expanded computing, data, and AI resources, whether on-premises or cloud-based. NSF will fund each Hub’s consortium coordination, AI infrastructure workforce development, and faculty training and coursework development in leveraging AI for science.
sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.title: U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs:

The purpose of the public procurement is for the MLSP to conclude a contract, following the conduct of this procedure, with which to ensure the construction of a National Electronic Information System for Full Adoption (NEISPO), including an Electronic Platform for applying for the adoption of children under the conditions of full adoption, which will be an integral part of the NEISPO. The scope of the procurement also includes the provision of the necessary hardware equipment for the operation of the system. Conducting specialised training for the specialists who will work with the system. All children who can be adopted under the conditions of full adoption and all persons who wish to adopt a child under the conditions of full adoption must be entered into the system. It must contain data on: 1) the children who may be adopted under the conditions of full adoption; 2) the persons who wish to adopt a child under the conditions of full adoption and the data from the electronic platform; 3) the expressed preferences of the persons who wish to adopt a child under the conditions of full adoption; 4) all stages of the procedures related to adoption; 5) all circumstances relevant to the adoption. As part of the NEISPO, an Electronic Platform for applying for the adoption of children under the conditions of full adoption must be created and maintained. The NEISPO will be created in accordance with Ordinance No. RD-06-46 of 04.11.2024 regarding the procedure for the entry, keeping, storage, maintenance and functioning of the NEISPO, approved by the Minister of Labour and Social Policy (published in the State Gazette, issue 97 of 2024). The system itself will have a web-based interface and will be installed on MLSP servers, which will be purchased (including storage) within the framework of the project. Methodological guides for working with the NEISPO and the Electronic Platform for applying for the adoption of children under the conditions of full adoption will be developed, both for the employees of the MLSP and the ASP, and for prospective adopters. Specialised training for the specialists who will work with the system will be organised and conducted. The achievement of the general objective will be realised through the following specific objectives, corresponding to the activities planned under the project: Provision of a modern and easy-to-use information system; Electronisation of internal business processes related to the national adoption process; Realisation of internal electronic administrative services for the automated provision of data from and to the ASP and MLSP, in their capacity as primary data administrator - by connecting the relevant registers to the RegiX inter-register exchange environment and developing the necessary adapters for this purpose; Electronisation of the administrative services provided by the ASP in connection with the national adoption process up to Level 3; With the realisation of the project, the following sub-objectives will also be achieved: Rapid and accurate exchange of information between all participants in the national adoption system, which will allow for real-time monitoring of the system and on the basis of which the MLSP will be able to carry out monitoring and annually prepare an analysis regarding the implementation of state policy in the field of national adoption; Optimisation of work processes, in which automation will be as useful and effective as possible, based on the principles of the European Interoperability Framework; Introduction of user identification and access management to information resources; Secure management of the data entered into the system; Identification, standardisation and optimisation of the business processes that are carried out in the ASP and MLSP in the field of national adoption; Automation of the processes for collecting, processing, storing and using data, while guaranteeing their reliability, quality, integrity and security at all moments of the national adoption process. sig_7df747d4831f5258c4e0.description: This Request for Information (RFI) is made by the Norwegian Public Sector Cloud Marketplace (MPS). It concerns Cloud backup and Restore solutions and Cloud External Key Management solutions. As part of an effort to address increased information security requirements, MPS is investigating a concept referred to as “Hardened Cloud”. You can read more about this concept on our website: Forsterket allmenn sky - https://markedsplassen.anskaffelser.no/om-oss/prosjektomrader/prosjektomrade-cips/forsterket-allmenn-sky. As part of this program, MPS is seeking information regarding the following services: Cloud Backup and Restore: Solutions that provide secure backup of data in cloud environments and enable timely and reliable restoration. This includes capabilities for defined Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), protection against data loss and immutable backups. The aim is to ensure data integrity and availability in support of controlled recovery processes. Cloud External Key Management: Solutions that enable customer-controlled management of cryptographic keys used by cloud services, through secure external key management. This includes capabilities to control the full key lifecycle management, such as key generation, storage, usage and revocation of keys. The aim is to ensure data confidentiality and to ensure that encrypted data remains under customer control. Respondents may choose to respond to questions about both services or only one of the services.
sig_7df747d4831f5258c4e0.title: RFI Cloud Backup and Restore and RFI Cloud External Key Management

sig_7e02a1b62a299b6646a7.description: The project "Fachkräfte-Fonds Globalvorhaben Partnerschaften für entwicklungsorientierte Ausbildungs- und Arbeitsmigration" fundamentally aims at the establishment of partnerships between economic actors in Germany and in selected cooperation countries, within the framework of which innovative models for development-oriented training and labour migration are to be designed and tested. This call for tenders serves the implementation of the BMZ policy paper "WE-Fair Fachkräfteallianz von Wirtschaft und Entwicklungspolitik". The goal is to create sustainable institutional and regulatory structures for the qualification and mobility of skilled workers and trainees in the partner countries, as well as for ensuring fair, ethical and regulated skilled worker recruitment for the German labour market, through the cooperation of the German organized economy and economic actors in the partner countries. Within the framework of the present contract, the contractor is to conceive, implement and evaluate one partnership project for training and labour migration in each of three partner countries yet to be determined, building upon already existing vocational training partnerships and with the active integration and participation of economic actors (chambers, district craft associations, associations, etc. and their institutions as well as enterprises associated with them). In doing so, the contractor shall in particular ensure that the aforementioned German economic actors make significant personnel, technical and financial contributions of their own. The work packages to be performed comprise, alongside the conception and establishment of the partnership projects (WP 1) and their formalisation (WP 2), in particular also capacity building as well as the institutional development of the partner institutions (above all vocational training providers) in the cooperation countries, preparatory qualification, the selection and accompanying integration of skilled workers and trainees (WP 3), as well as the preparation and sustainable anchoring of the gained experience in the partner countries (WP 4).
sig_7e02a1b62a299b6646a7.title: 10018130 - To conceive, set up and implement projects for the recruitment of skilled workers in the framework of vocational training partnerships in partnership with the private sector

sig_7e22e6847a5ac3750690.description: DWP is intending to procure new employment support provision for out of work Universal Credit claimants. It will provide personalised and tailored support that is responsive to the needs of individuals and the local area. This will include skills, training and work experience; matching participants with employers through job trials, jobs fairs and job brokering; support with self-employment; intensive and repeated support with applications and interviewing; support in managing health conditions in the workplace; support with travel and childcare; and specialist support (e.g. ESOL, addiction). Support will be available across England and Wales and will be integrated within local labour markets. DWP is co-designing the provision with Mayoral Strategic Authorities to ensure it is tailored to the needs of local labour markets. This Pipeline notice refers to the procurement of the service in England only. Please note, that all key decisions including final programme title, budgets, contract length and dates are yet to be approved through internal governance and therefore may change. The procurement will be conducted via DWP’s new e-procurement system Atamis. Further information on registering an interest in this procurement will be provided in future notices. Lot 1: .

sig_7e7c5bbd593eb78f2961.description: With the proposed intervention "Enhancement of the digital infrastructure of the Public Central Library of Veroia in the direction of improving the digital experience of residents and visitors of the region", the following are attempted: I. on the one hand, the expansion of the PCLV Library network using RFID technology for lending systems in areas of Imathia and II. and on the other hand, the development of the Wine Thematic Library in cooperation with bodies of the Imathia region related to this specific theme. Specific items include the enrichment of the repository with digital content that further highlights the identity of the region and the work of the Cultural and Creative Sector and the promotion of collections to create a digital experience. The planned network will be based on the existing infrastructure of the PCLV (equipment, software, databases), as described above, which will be enriched with digital content and will create conditions for direct access and availability of this content to a wider audience, especially in areas that do not have direct access to the library's services. At the same time, in cooperation with wine producer bodies in the region, it will support a set of activities aiming to create within the Library of Veroia an information hub for viticulture and wine, with an emphasis on the potential for crop development and wine production in Northern Europe, and the presentation of local production through the implementation of actions oriented towards the touristic promotion of the products. Complementary to the main actions, the robust implementation of a communication plan and dissemination of the project results to the general public is also included to stimulate interest and ensure the most intensive possible use of the provided services. It includes the supply and installation of the necessary RFID equipment (and other equipment) and a series of services. These services concern: • the collection and organisation of cultural data from available historical archives. • the digitisation of cultural data recorded in traditional media, with the aim of documentation and promotion. Digitisation will be carried out following standard good practices. • the scientific documentation of the material to be digitised in accordance with international rules and standards. • the creation of digital repositories for each category of material to be digitised and their promotion via the internet (integration into the Digital Information and Promotion Portal of the PCLV). • the expansion of the PCLV's services, which will include both the applications already in operation and the services provided, as well as the new applications and services that will be developed within the framework of the project through a unified search and browsing platform.
sig_7e7c5bbd593eb78f2961.title: Extension of the Library Network of the Veria Public Central Library using RFID technology for lending systems, development of digital applications for wine & implementation of a communication programme and promotional activities

sig_7eb33cd10162ff82898a.description: The contracting authority wishes to appoint an integrated partner for legal and social services as a recognised social secretariat, including payroll and for the maintenance, optimisation and implementation of the HR and payroll system landscape. The contract comprises, on the one hand, the correct, timely and compliant execution of all statutory, social and fiscal obligations associated with wage processing and social law and, on the other hand, supporting the contracting authority in managing, maintaining, optimising and future-proofing its HR IT environment (SAP HR / Payroll and SAP SuccessFactors). In this context, the contracting authority is looking for a single contractor who will act as an integral point of contact and ultimate person responsible for both the social secretariat and the HR and payroll system landscape. This responsibility can be fulfilled by the contractor itself or by the contractor together with one or more subcontractors, whereby the contractor shall always act as the sole contractual discussion partner and ultimate person responsible. The contractor acts as a socio-legal partner and guardian of the legislative framework and is responsible for translating and correctly implementing changes in social, employment and tax regulations within the payroll processes and the supporting HR systems. In addition, the contractor acts as a maintenance and implementation partner for the HR system landscape, both for planned developments (such as the implementation and optimisation of SAP SuccessFactors, including Employee Central and the associated talent modules) and for the contracting authority's own development and optimisation requests. The contractor acts as a strategic and advisory partner by periodically analysing our existing HR and payroll processes, identifying optimisation opportunities and formulating concrete proposals for improvement, with the aim of further developing our HR and payroll system landscape sustainably in support of our HR strategy. The award of this contract does not grant the contractor any exclusivity right or right to purchase its offered products or services. During the term of this contract, the CA may have supplies, identical or analogous to those described in the specifications, carried out by third parties. Upon application of the above, the original contractor may not at any time claim any compensation of any nature whatsoever.

sig_7ecac7801f887359855f.description: The Ministry of Transport refers to the delay connected to the project Sørli-Åkersvika and any consequences for the development of Hamar station. The Ministry will, as a follow-up of this, carry out an external review with the main aim of identifying learning points. The review consists of two parts, but is delivered together. The first part shall map and evaluate decision processes and information flow connected to the delay of the project Sørli-Åkersvika and any consequences for the development of Hamar station. The review shall: • Assess whether the decision and contract process, as well as information flow have been in accordance with the current guidelines, contracts, agreed processes and management system, both internally in Bane NOR, between Bane NOR and the Norwegian Railway Directorate and internally in the Norwegian Railway Directorate. • Assess whether there is a need to adjust the guidelines and the management system and/or implement measures to ensure better compliance with Bane NOR and the Norwegian Railway Directorate. • Identifying learning points The second part shall evaluate whether Bane NOR ́s internal management systems (including a project model) are sufficient to ensure control of costs, risks and progress in major development projects. The review shall be directed towards the following three cases – the development of the Dovre Line, the Trønder Line and the Vestfold Railway. The review shall also map and assess how the recommendations from relevant reviews in recent years, including the Follobane review from 2023 and the Auditor General's report from 2024 on investment projects, have been followed up, whether the measures implemented are sufficient and whether there is a need for other/new measures to remedy the challenges of delays and increasing costs in major investment projects. The first draft of the report shall be submitted by 14 August 2026, and the final report will be submitted by 4 September 2026. The upper financial limit is NOK 4 million excluding VAT.
sig_7ecac7801f887359855f.title: Review of postponement of double track against Hamar and learning across major investment projects

sig_7ed0606618fef632765a.description: The purpose of the procurement is to draw up the feasibility study for the "realisation of a multi-voltage electric (traction) transformer substation at the Făurei Railway Testing Centre, which has the possibility of varying nominal parameters and performing regenerative braking" (including studies, expert reports, documentation, permits, agreements, etc.), an integral part of the Project "Modernisation and expansion of the Făurei Railway Testing Centre in order to increase the quality and testing capacity of systems and subsystems and constructive elements of the railway transport system" Note: The contracting authority will respond to requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. In accordance with art. 160 and 161 of Law 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and additions, the obligation of the contracting authority to respond to requests for clarifications is conditional upon the transmission of requests for clarifications 14 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The objective pursued through the procurement of the service for drawing up the feasibility study is the realisation of a transformer (traction) substation with multiple voltages (25 kV AC, 15 kV AC, 3 kV DC, 1,5 kV DC, 0,75 kV DC), with the possibility of varying the nominal voltage and performing regenerative braking, which will lead to the expansion of testing capacity, will facilitate the development and testing of new technologies at the level of safety and interoperability imposed by the Technical Specifications for Interoperability approved by European Regulations, and will allow for the performance of realistic simulations of operational conditions in the railway network. By awarding the service contract, the aim is, in addition to the procurement of the feasibility study (including necessary studies, expert reports, documentation, permits, agreements), the preparation of documentation for the approval of technical-economic indicators and the promotion of the Government decision, the preparation of technical documentation for the award of design and execution contracts for the works, and for consultancy/supervision of works execution, and last but not least, the preparation of documentation and assistance for obtaining financing through access to non-reimbursable European funds. This objective is included in the Project "Modernisation and expansion of the Făurei Railway Testing Centre in order to increase the quality and testing capacity of systems and subsystems and constructive elements of the railway transport system" initiated by the contracting authority.

sig_7eec439042bee00b5592.description: The contracting authority's SOC has the core task of monitoring the organisation's IT landscape around the clock and initiating appropriate measures in the event of security incidents. The previous contractual partner provided the core areas of Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), analysis and incident response, vulnerability management, and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM); accordingly, this tender essentially comprises the replacement of the aforementioned components and services. While some tasks will now be performed by the contracting authority's SOC, internal personnel resources are a limiting factor. Therefore, some tasks, including the continuous monitoring of the environment, will still need to be provided jointly with the support of an external partner. The future environment is to be based on the current internal log data platform Splunk, which will be expanded into a SIEM. This platform is to be supplemented by a Managed Detection and Response (MDR) solution that operates using its own data lake and transmits alerts to the internal SIEM. Continuous monitoring is to take place on the basis of the MDR service, whilst the contracting authority's employees will in future primarily deal with the internal SIEM and thus also be able to cover internal and organisation-specific use cases. The systems will be supplemented by various services to operate the SIEM platform, but also with cyber analysis services and support in the event of an incident. The future platform must also support operations in vulnerability management with suitable tools. The procurement is divided into four lots. For the operation of the log data platform, primarily consisting of Splunk Enterprise and Cribl, and later Splunk Enterprise Security, a service partner is required who supports the daily operation of the infrastructure. This partner is also to support the contracting authority regarding optimisation, further development, and updates. The operational aspect also includes a response time (cf. specifications Lot 2). The SLA comprises support on working days; a 24-hour on-call service is not required.
sig_7eec439042bee00b5592.title: Support for the operation and further development of the Security Operations Centre (SOC)

sig_7f106fefd8b70123b073.description: Supply of components, licences and maintenance services for the enhancement and renewal of the existing core network infrastructure The existing core network and fabric infrastructure is based on components and technologies from the manufacturer Extreme Networks. The existing network components are integrated into a uniform management, monitoring and security architecture. The core network infrastructure is an essential basis for the hospital's core medical and administrative processes. Due to its remit as a maximum-care provider, the highest possible availability corresponding to the state of the art is required. Avoidable additional sources of error and operational risks must therefore be limited during procurement. Due to increased requirements regarding performance, port capacity, transmission speed, availability, fail-safe reliability and IT security, as well as age-related replacement needs, a comprehensive renewal and enhancement of the core network infrastructure is required. The aim of the procurement is the supply of the items required for the renewal and enhancement of the existing core network infrastructure: • hardware components, • interface and expansion modules, • transceivers and connection components, • software, management and functional licences, • maintenance and support entitlements, as well as • other accessories listed in the specification of requirements. The products, article numbers and quantities to be supplied specifically are ultimately derived from the specification of requirements. The subject of the tender is exclusively the supply of the components, licences and maintenance services listed in the specification of requirements. The contractor is owed: 1. the complete and punctual supply of the advertised hardware components and accessories, 2. the provision and transfer of the advertised software and functional licences, 3. the registration and activation of the advertised maintenance and support services, 4. the allocation of all licences and maintenance entitlements to the contracting authority, as well as 5. the handover of the associated licence, support and registration proofs. All hardware components supplied must: - be brand new and unused, - be original products from the manufacturer specified in the specification of requirements, - originate from an authorised distribution channel, - be intended for the German or European market, - have a clearly traceable serial number, - be registerable with the manufacturer and - be approved for the respective advertised maintenance and support service. The contractor must ensure that: - the supplied licences correspond to the specified products and article numbers, - the licences can be used without restriction for the intended use, - there are no time or functional restrictions that are not expressly stated in the specification of requirements, - the licence terms correspond to the advertised periods, and - all licence proofs, activation keys and registration information are handed over to the contracting authority. The maintenance and support services listed in the specification of requirements must be provided as regular manufacturer services. Page 5 of 7 Specification of Requirements - Core Network The maintenance or support period begins at the time specified in the specification of requirements or in the order. The contractor must ensure the proper registration of the maintenance and support services with the manufacturer and hand over suitable evidence of this to the contracting authority. The evidence must contain at least: - affected articles or serial numbers, - type and scope of the support service, - start and end of the service period, - agreed service or response times, and - manufacturer or contract reference numbers. There must be no unintentional support gaps between the delivery of the hardware and the start of the maintenance period.

sig_7f21e4c80bf85a40ceee.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.
sig_7f21e4c80bf85a40ceee.title: 17.13 Management consultancy services (DIS)
