sig_83b543e7202c8fe6331b.description: Among others, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GmbH (GIZ) is currently implementing two projects in the agricultural sector in South Sudan. The bilateral project "Community-based Rural Development in South Sudan" (CDRD) is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-financed by the Directorate-General for International Cooperation (DGIS) of the Kingdom of Netherlands as well as the European Union (EU) and runs from April 2022 to March 2029. The project, "Improved Living Conditions and Psychosocial Support in the Context of Displacement and Displacement" (ILiPS), is commissioned by BMZ under the Special Initiative on Displaced Persons and Host Countries (SIGA), with a project period ranging from October 2022 to December 2026. Both projects" main components focus on agricultural development of rural smallholder households. With its additional funding received in 2025, ILiPS now supports 2,000 households within Central and Eastern Equatoria. With its EU extension from 2024, CDRD supports now a total of 27,500 smallholder households across in Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, Nothern Bar el Ghazal and Western Bahr El Ghazal. All monitoring activities of the GIZ projects in South Sudan are centrally organized and coordinated by the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Unit. To measure progress and ensure accountability, both projects use a rigorous monitoring system based on representative household surveys. Data is collected once per year, with baseline, midline and endline surveys for each cohort. In addition to quantitative surveys, the projects employ a mixed-method approach combining household interviews with Focus Group Discussions and Key Informant Interviews. This design allows the projects to generate robust longitudinal and cross-sectional data on production capacity, income levels, nutrition and resilience, while also capturing the social, cultural and gender dynamics that shape household behaviour. Particular emphasis is placed on monitoring the impact of agricultural training on farming practices and the adoption of sustainable methods. The evidence generated is used for donor reporting, project steering and strategic decision-making in the multi-donor context. By disseminating results to national and local actors, the projects also contribute to learning across the wider partner system. In this way, ILiPS and CDRD strengthen the resilience of rural households in South Sudan while providing actionable knowledge for future programming in fragile contexts. The contractor will design and implement a multi-annual mixed-methods survey and qualitative research for the ILiPS and CDRD projects in South Sudan. The services include the development, adaptation and translation of questionnaires for household surveys, including a dedicated module on women of reproductive age. The questionnaires must follow a layered design with "must-have" questions for donor reporting and project steering, "should-have" questions to ensure context-specific adaptation of core themes, and "nice-to-have" questions that can be added according to regional or cohort-specific needs. All tools are to be translated into relevant local languages and pre-tested in the field to ensure clarity and feasibility, and must be designed in a conflict-sensitive and culturally appropriate manner. Sampling must ensure representativeness at state and cohort level with a margin of error of eight percent for both state-level and displacement-strata estimates. Each beneficiary sample shall be matched by a control group of non-beneficiaries in neighbouring Payams, representing half the sample size. The contractor will apply stratified random sampling and use a digital data collection tool, preferably Survey Solutions on GIZ servers, in order to guarantee secure and efficient handling of data. Comprehensive training of enumerators, field supervision and quality assurance measures are required throughout. The contractor will carry out household surveys for each cohort at the relevant survey stage. For ILiPS, this includes midline data collection in two states in 2026. For CDRD, this includes midterm and endline data collection for the 2024 and 2025 cohorts, as well as a final endline across all states in 2028. The surveys will gather information on sustainable food production capacity, income-generating activities and diversification, household consumption patterns and nutrition, as well as the adoption of sustainable farming practices following project-supported trainings. The mixed-method approach further includes qualitative research through Focus Group Discussions and Key Informant Interviews. These serve to provide deeper insights into community perceptions of project interventions, barriers to adoption of sustainable practices, and the roles of women and youth in income generation. The qualitative findings complement the quantitative survey data by explaining why certain changes occur, identifying structural and cultural factors influencing livelihoods, and highlighting lessons for future interventions. All collected data must be cleaned, validated and analysed. The contractor is responsible for preparing analytical reports for each round of data collection, integrating both quantitative and qualitative findings. Reports shall include descriptive results, trend analyses, and clear recommendations for project management and donor decision-making. The contractor must ensure ethical data handling, compliance with the "do no harm" principle, and avoidance of structural bias. Dissemination of findings to the partner system and local stakeholders is an integral part of the assignment, ensuring that results are accessible and contribute to learning beyond project boundaries. Finally, the contractor must establish a robust operational and security plan for data collection in the fragile context of South Sudan. This includes clear timelines, staffing, coordination with GIZ and implementing partners, risk assessments, contingency planning and adherence to humanitarian security protocols. The assignment therefore requires an experienced research organisation with proven expertise in large-scale data collection in fragile contexts, strong methodological capacities, effective field presence and security systems, and experience in agricultural and food security surveys. The contractor must ensure high-quality delivery across all phases of implementation, while maintaining conflict sensitivity, context appropriateness and methodological rigour.

sig_83ba1178ab745130e1ff.description: The Programme Delivery Contractor will deliver a coordinated programme of community-based activities across six (6) Leitrim Connected Hubs, ensuring alignment with the objectives, outputs, governance and compliance requirements of the SEUPB‐approved Connexus Programme. Working closely with Leitrim County Council, local hub committees, and partner hubs in Mid and East Antrim Borough Council (MEABC) and Sligo County Council (SCC), the Contractor will support effective planning, delivery and monitoring of programme activities. The role includes programme planning and coordination through the development of annual activity plans, participation in cross‐border planning workshops, and the preparation of hub‐specific action plans responding to local needs and capacity, including advice on ICT requirements and compliant procurement. The Contractor will design and deliver a diverse programme of hub‐based activities focused on digital inclusion, health and wellbeing, social connection, enterprise development, remote working and community governance support. Activities will target older people, marginalised groups and those with low digital confidence, while promoting intergenerational and cross‐community engagement in line with PEACEPLUS values. The Contractor will support cross‐border engagement through study visits, conferences and mentoring initiatives, capture learning outcomes for reporting, and promote hub activities through agreed communications channels. Regular coordination meetings, accurate monitoring, quarterly reporting, full compliance with SEUPB and Council requirements, and a final evaluation report will form core deliverables

sig_8404aea88a3525792476.description: Project Zora is a strategic programme within the Department for Work and Pensions’ Working Age Services portfolio, focused on improving the sustainability, agility and resilience of the Universal Credit service. It addresses the constraints of a long‐standing monolithic application estate to enable more responsive delivery of policy change, user needs and future service evolution. The programme will progressively decompose elements of the Universal Credit application into more modular, loosely coupled components aligned to a modern, microservices‐based architecture. This includes re‐architecting systems and supporting capabilities to reduce interdependencies, improve deployment flexibility, and enable faster, safer change while maintaining continuity of service. Through this transformation, Project Zora aims to establish reusable platform and service capabilities that can be iterated over time and support wider Working Age Services objectives. Delivery is expected to require specialist digital, engineering and delivery expertise across analysis, design, build and transition activity, with a clear focus on managing operational risk, supporting user‐centred outcomes and delivering long‐term value for money. Estimated total contract value (inclusive of optional extension period) is between £20,000,000 and £35,000,000 Please note, that all key decisions including final programme title, budgets, contract length and dates are yet to be approved through internal governance and therefore may change. The procurement will be conducted via DWP’s e-procurement system Atamis. Further information on registering an interest in this procurement will be provided in future notices. Lot 1: .

sig_842cff36556ab3b425ae.description: The project entitled "Unified Real Estate Register (URER)" aims at the systematic recording, management and monitoring of real estate through an integrated information system, which will gather, systematise and incorporate digital information maintained by various public administration and private sector bodies. From a feasibility perspective, the information system will serve: • Citizens and Professionals seeking information on a specific property. • Public Sector Bodies (including bodies participating in the Unified Real Estate Register), in order to enrich/improve the data of their internal registers. • Private Sector Bodies, to simplify transactions with the insurance and banking markets, as well as to provide access to data for risk assessment and faster loan approval. The operation of the overall project aims to create a modern, fully automated electronic real estate register to ensure the greatest possible information, publicity and security of transactions for citizens and involved bodies. Within the framework of the project, interoperability of the Unified Real Estate Register with public and private sector bodies will be implemented, and open data utilisation services of the Unified Real Estate Register will be provided, which include both the analysis and study of existing data maintained by each body, as well as the necessary development services for the exchange, cleansing and optimal utilisation thereof through the Unified Real Estate Register (for updating and optimising the data they maintain through the exchange of more recent data from other bodies). The bodies estimated to be interconnected with the system in the first phase include: (bodies may be added or removed during the Implementation Study period) • Hellenic Cadastre • Independent Public Revenue Authority (AADE) • Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (HEDNO) • Technical Chamber of Greece (TEE) • Insurance companies • Communications network providers (e.g. Cosmote, Vodafone, WIND, etc.) • Water supply and sewerage providers (e.g. EYDAP, EYATH, etc.) • Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT) • Public Properties Company (ETAD) • Central Union of Municipalities of Greece (KEDE) or direct Municipalities • Ministry of Energy • Ministry of Justice • Ministry of Finance This procurement will result in the implementation of the Unified Real Estate Register (URER) information system and the creation of open data utilisation services. The services concerning the possibility of interconnection and data transmission from the bodies to the URER will be provided within the framework of the separate subproject "Interoperability of the Unified Real Estate Register with Public and Private Sector Bodies - Interconnection of Bodies with the Unified Real Estate Register". The provided services are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: 72262000-9 - Software development services 80533100-0 - Training software services 72000000-5 - Information technology services: consulting, software development, Internet and support A detailed description of the physical and financial subject matter of the contract is given in APPENDIX I - DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PHYSICAL AND FINANCIAL SUBJECT MATTER Deliverables of the contract are those mentioned in APPENDIX I - DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PHYSICAL AND FINANCIAL SUBJECT MATTER hereof. Tenders are submitted for the entirety of the subject matter of this procurement, as described in detail in the procurement documents, because the procurement is objectively indivisible. In particular, Subproject 1 is not subdivided into individual lots because it constitutes a single technological entity that requires a comprehensive architectural approach. The development of the URER information system presupposes the creation of a coherent database, unified user interfaces, common security protocols and compatible technological infrastructure. Fragmenting the project into individual parts would create significant risks of incompatibility between the different parts of the system, interoperability problems within the Register itself, and increased complexity in the management and coordination of the different contractors. Furthermore, unified implementation ensures data homogeneity, the efficiency of processing procedures and a unified presentation of services to end users. Estimated value of the contract The estimated value of the contract amounts to €3.493.000,00 excluding VAT 24% (estimated value including VAT: €4.331.320,00). Before the expiry of the project, the Contracting Authority may decide to exercise an option, by increasing the physical scope of the project with or without a corresponding extension of the contract duration, up to the amount of € 1.299.396,00 including VAT 24% (Budget without VAT: € 1.047.900,00 VAT € 251.496,00). The budget of the contract is broken down in the Technical Project Sheet approved by the Recovery Fund Coordination Special Service (RFCSS) contained in ref. no. 34748 EX 2025 / 25.02.2025 Award Decision (ADA: Ψ7S8H-BX2), as correctly repeated on 26.02.2025, for registration in the Public Investment Programme (SATA 063) with project code 2025TA06300003, Award Decision of the Project "Unified Real Estate Register (U.R.E.R.) - eRegistries" (MIS Code TA 5225518) under the Action "16824 - Electronic registries" in the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Duration of the contract The total duration of the contract is set at seven (7) months from the date of signature of the contract, with the possibility of extension, provided that the duration of the project "Unified Real Estate Register (U.R.E.R.) - eRegistries" is extended within the framework of its execution and financing from the Recovery and Resilience Facility. A schedule is set out in Appendix I.

Subject: Service order "Implementation of a complex infrastructure data repository and traffic management system" Magyar Közút has decided to implement a complex infrastructure data repository and traffic management system in order to follow the legal and professional changes in the transport sector, to implement corporate strategic goals, to support operational activities following organisational transformations, and to renew its systems, which have been in use for decades and are based on obsolete information technology. The system must include support for functions not yet used in the live infrastructure, such as streaming, artificial intelligence, cloud-native components and machine learning. The goal of the system development is to create a modular system that, beyond current functionalities, allows for the connection of new software modules and databases in the future, using interfaces created with well-defined standard formats. The systems must be suitable for daily 24-hour and weekly 7-day operation. A fundamental requirement is that the registered data and the functions provided by the systems being replaced must be guaranteed; there must be no loss of data or functionality. The Winning Tenderer may not use black-box solutions during development. Complex infrastructure data repository and traffic management system The professional goal of the system is to renew the National Road Data Bank (OKA) and the Bridge Registry systems. It is necessary to solve the integration of the topological, technical and condition information of the road network, bridge registry and bridge management data, as well as municipal road network and cycling infrastructure data, eliminating the difficulties and time constraints of data flow and data synchronisation between the current heterogeneous registries. Special attention must be paid to the implementation of accurate conversion between the location identification solutions used on the road. It is an essential aspect that the dual road location identification must function properly – even in time series – without accurate map geometry. The goal in the registry is to move towards lane-axis level geometric and topological registration. It is a basic expectation in the system, therefore it must be ensured for a wide range of users that data related to roads can be displayed on a unified map, and that the data and attributes of the objects displayed on the map can be queried in tabular form. The functions to be developed within the framework of traffic management requirements are built on the database structure and geoinformatics basis created in the data repository. It replaces or works together with the traffic controller and its subsystems, the dispatcher system, ÚTINFORM, the traffic light remote monitoring system, tunnel and webcam systems. The system must support tasks related to road operation, traffic organisation, traffic safety and information provision. The goal is to create a system that monitors and controls road traffic control equipment, which is capable of providing safe and efficient system design and high-level services in the field of remote monitoring of traffic control equipment, service functions and traffic management, assists the work of road operators, supports the preparation of professional reports, and provides access to real-time and historical data through an easily understandable interface. The task is to support dynamic traffic regulation, to implement such a highly automated traffic management system that is based on the principle of adaptive traffic control and can be monitored and controlled remotely. It is the task of the Winning Tenderer to explore and reverse-engineer the protocols of the electronic devices integrated into the existing Magyar Közút IT systems and to integrate them into the system to be implemented. It is an expectation that the online networked devices be accessible on one platform and that the non-homogeneous fleet of devices be controlled in a common system. Complex infrastructure data repository and traffic management system The professional goal of the system is to renew the National Road Data Bank (OKA) and the Bridge Registry systems. It is necessary to solve the integration of the topological, technical and condition information of the road network, bridge registry and bridge management data, as well as municipal road network and cycling infrastructure data, eliminating the difficulties and time constraints of data flow and data synchronisation between the current heterogeneous registries. Special attention must be paid to the implementation of accurate conversion between the location identification solutions used on the road. It is an essential aspect that the dual road location identification must function properly – even in time series – without accurate map geometry. The goal in the registry is to move towards lane-axis level geometric and topological registration. It is a basic expectation in the system, therefore it must be ensured for a wide range of users that data related to roads can be displayed on a unified map, and that the data and attributes of the objects displayed on the map can be queried in tabular form. The functions to be developed within the framework of traffic management requirements are built on the database structure and geoinformatics basis created in the data repository. It replaces or works together with the traffic controller and its subsystems, the dispatcher system, ÚTINFORM, the traffic light remote monitoring system, tunnel and webcam systems. The system must support tasks related to road operation, traffic organisation, traffic safety and information provision. The goal is to create a system that monitors and controls road traffic control equipment, which is capable of providing safe and efficient system design and high-level services in the field of remote monitoring of traffic control equipment, service functions and traffic management, assists the work of road operators, supports the preparation of professional reports, and provides access to real-time and historical data through an easily understandable interface. The task is to support dynamic traffic regulation, to implement such a highly automated traffic management system that is based on the principle of adaptive traffic control and can be monitored and controlled remotely. It is the task of the Winning Tenderer to explore and reverse-engineer the protocols of the electronic devices integrated into the existing Magyar Közút IT systems and to integrate them into the system to be implemented. It is an expectation that the online networked devices be accessible on one platform and that the non-homogeneous fleet of devices be controlled in a common system. sig_8453eb2b8e3eacbbb0c9.description: NOTE: Updated submission in below text now reflects a 9 Oct 26 date in line with the General Information submission date. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing “one-time use” items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management – Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. This includes providing analysis to the SPO to help prioritize product improvements and tracking the implementation of all approved modifications by individual tail number. Technical Publications and Documentation: Demonstrate?authorized access to, and the authority to use, all OEM proprietary technical data, drawings, maintenance manuals, and engineering dispositions necessary to perform the?1200-hour?and four-year?inspections?on the AW139/MH-139A platform.? OEM Portal and Technical Data Reach-Back: The contractor must secure and maintain direct, authorized access into Leonardo's customer portal (Wingman Portal) to download and manage the distribution of all technical publications, including Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters, manual maintenance revisions, and Flight Manuals. This includes access to Interactive Electronic Technical Publications (IETP) and a regular summary of IETP changes. The contractor must also possess a clear process to receive and propose updates to Flight Manuals based on changing military operational profiles. ?? Sustainment/Obsolescence Program: PMA Management DER/ODA Management DMSMS monitoring, surveillance, and mitigation Parts Development and Redesign Program for Obsolescence Items Obsolescence Working Group (OWG): Provide active representation to the program's OWG to assess supply chain risks, react to obsolescence challenges, and evaluate alternate part sourcing. Spares Requirements Review Board (SRRB) for the replenishment of the sustainment of spares. This excludes all initial spares. Personnel and Certifications:?Personnel should hold appropriate FAA certifications (e.g., A&P licenses) and possess at least five years of experience with this specific airframe or comparable complex, commercial-derivative rotary-wing platforms." Implement robust workforce management plan addressing recruitment, retention, and succession planning to ensure long-term program stability and minimize turnover risk.? Possess the capability to provide familiarization and over-the-shoulder training to?Government personnel, as?required, on specific maintenance procedures or contractor-managed?logistics?systems. ?? Supply Chain and Logistics:?Supply Chain and Logistics: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets, including major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) and engines. This system must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling and predictive data analysis, actively forecast failure rates, plan/schedule maintenance events, and ensure parts are prepositioned to support complex troubleshooting and repair actions. Predictive Logistics and Consumption Tracking: Demonstrate a robust supply chain management system for sourcing, stocking, and managing the repair of all assets. The contractor must utilize historical fleet data to conduct advanced supply modeling. Crucially, the contractor must track and report both component failure rates AND true consumption rates to prevent obscured sustainment costs. This data must be actively used to plan/schedule maintenance events and ensure parts are prepositioned to support complex troubleshooting and repair actions. Cybersecurity Risk Management Framework: manage all aspects of cybersecurity in accordance with DoDI 8510.01. This includes obtaining and maintaining a platform level Authority to Operate. Facility and Quality Certifications: Part 145 Repair Station: The contractor's facilities performing heavy maintenance, depot-level component repair, and major inspections shall be certified in accordance with 14 CFR Part 145. Part 142 Training Center: Contractor personnel operating and supporting simulator training devices shall follow quality and instructional standards commensurate with 14 CFR Part 142. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INTERESTED PARTIES? Interested parties are requested to provide a capability statement addressing the following items. Please limit your response to no more than ten fifteen (15) pages.? Company Information:? Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone) CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI) Financial System Capability: Confirm your organization's capability to invoice and process payments electronically via the Government's mandated Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) / Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) system. Business Size Status under NAICS 488190 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), Woman-Owned, etc.) Business Size Status under NAICS Code 336413 (Aircraft Manufacturing), with a size standard of 1,500 employees. Please self-certify for all applicable categories: Small Business (Yes/No) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) (Yes/No) HUBZone Certified (Yes/No) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) (Yes/No) Company Ownership (Domestic or Foreign-owned). Capability Narrative Technical Capability, Logistics, and Sustainment:? Provide a detailed narrative describing your company's ability to meet the requirements outlined in Section 3.0. Describe your facility, its size, location, and the specific strategic business unit of your organization that possesses the logistics support activity; please detail if any experience is on Leonardo helicopters. Explain the basis of your authority to access and use OEM proprietary engineering data, diagnostic software, and technical documentation. Describe the training, certifications, and experience level of your technical workforce as it relates to this airframe. Facility Certifications: Describe your organization's FAA certifications. Specifically, detail your status as a 14 CFR Part 145 Certified Repair Station and your experience operating in compliance with 14 CFR Part 142 Training Center standards. Describe your company's process for managing the supply chain for a major inspection event. RAM Metrics and Consumption Analytics: Describe your capability to perform FMECA and generate accurate RAM metrics (MTBF, MTTR). Specifically, how will your organization track and report true component consumption rates to the Government, distinct from standard failure rates, to ensure full transparency of sustainment costs? Past Performance and Relevant Experience: Provide a brief summary of up to three (3) relevant contracts from the past five (5) years where your company provided?depot-level maintenance or?comparable heavy inspections on complex rotary-wing?aircraft. Experience on the Leonardo AW139 is highly preferred. Include contract?numbers, customer, period of performance, and a brief description of the work performed. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Responses shall not exceed 15 pages (single-sided, 12-point font). Submit responses electronically by?5:00 PM Eastern Time on [10/09/2026]. Mark all proprietary information clearly. Unmarked information will be considered publicly releasable. Be advised that government-contracted support personnel may handle submissions under non-disclosure agreements. Prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at?https://www.sam.gov.

sig_84764dacb5bf6f034c6f.description: The BBC is conducting early market engagement to understand the capabilities, maturity and implementation requirements of modern Spend Analytics and Savings Tracking platforms. This activity is exploratory: no procurement process has yet commenced, and all information provided is for fact‐finding only. We are seeking information from vendors who offer solutions that can: Organise, cleanse and classify spend data Provide actionable insights and opportunity identification Support savings tracking from pipeline creation through to realisation Integrate with multiple internal and external data sources Enable reporting for procurement, finance, and business stakeholders The BBC aims to gain clarity on: 1. What the current market of spend analytics and savings‐management tools can deliver 2. What is considered “best‐in‐class” in terms of data connectivity, classification, analytics, and value‐tracking 3. What typical implementation timelines and resource requirements look like 4. What dependencies, risks and considerations should be factored into our planning 5. Indicative commercial models and licensing structures (non‐binding) The BBC will also be approaching organisations on an ad-hoc basis to understand Lot 1: .

sig_84a78fdf066de6ce13ba.description: As one of 18 centres of the Helmholtz Association, the Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie (HZB) employs around 1.400 staff at its Berlin-Wannsee and Berlin-Adlershof sites and has a total budget of approximately 110 million euros. HZB works closely with universities and universities of applied sciences in Berlin-Brandenburg. HZB researches solutions for a climate-neutral society. Researchers develop and optimise efficient and inexpensive materials for solar cells, batteries and catalysts. These energy materials are essential components on the path to a CO2-neutral and secure energy supply. HZB and Friedrich Schiller University Jena founded 2023 the Helmholtz Institute for Polymers in Energy Applications (HIPOLE) in Jena as a permanent facility of HZB. Leading expertise in the fields of energy storage and photovoltaics, polymeric materials, artificial intelligence and sustainable chemistry was thus pooled in order to advance accelerated knowledge-based research into sustainable polymer materials for scalable energy technologies. HIPOLE Jena is based on three research pillars: • material design and synthesis • scalability, prototypes and transfer, and • characterisation, theory, modelling and data sciences. The focus is not only on basic research, but also on the transfer of research results. HIPOLE Jena currently employs around 50 members of staff. The research work of the scientists at HIPOLE Jena, supported by seven associated members from FSU Jena and HZB, can be assigned to five research areas: 1. Polymeric redox-flow batteries, 2. Polymer-based thin-film batteries, 3. Photovoltaics, 4. Functional self-healing materials and 5. Sustainable chemistry. The Helmholtz Institute for Polymers in Energy Applications Jena (HIPOLE Jena) intends to procure an analytical ultracentrifuge (AUC) to determine structure-property relationships of polymeric and colloidal systems in solution. These investigations using hydrodynamic methods are a central component of both the physicochemical characterisation of polymers and colloidal systems within the research projects of HIPOLE Jena. sig_84b530ce5b45a3905339.description: Wilson's School (WS) is a standalone selective academy for boys in the London Borough of Sutton and converted to this status in 2011. There are 1,300 students on roll of which 360 are in the Sixth Form. The school's website is https://www.wilsons.school/ Places at WS are highly sought after and examination results achieved by its pupils are routinely amongst the highest of any school in the country. WS was founded by Edward Wilson in 1615. The school is proud of its long history and the strong reputation for quality and excellence which current leaders and their predecessors have worked hard to build. Senior leaders are focussed on maintaining and enhancing this reputation and this is an important factor when recruiting partners. WS is deeply proud of what it offers, particularly the hugely enriching experiences pupils enjoy beyond the classroom. Indeed, these rival (and often exceed) those of fee-paying schools. Teachers engage pupils with challenging and enjoyable lessons, enriched with great activities to extend pupils' interests and skills far beyond the National Curriculum and examination specifications. Teachers know the pupils very well and visitors often comment on the warmth and good humour that characterise relationships between boys and members of staff. The aims of Wilson's School are: to ensure a safe and kind environment for learning, building pupils' confidence and actively promoting their wellbeing to enable all pupils to reach the highest levels of academic enjoyment and achievement to enable our pupils to think independently and to feel secure in taking intellectual risks to give all of our pupils every opportunity to engage with the spiritual, social, moral and cultural dimensions of life to provide every pupil with opportunities for achievement and enjoyment beyond the classroom to provide our pupils with the skills and attitudes needed to thrive in Higher Education and proceed to satisfying careers and fulfilling lives WS is nationally renowned and its leaders are involved in work which supports the education system as a whole at local and national level. In 2024, WS was named as The Sunday Times Secondary School of the Year, beating off competition from the state and independent sectors. Our contractors are partners in maintaining and enhancing our reputation and are proud to work with us. Wilson's is currently supported by an external organisation which provides onsite and remote support on the basis of a fixed term contract.This will finish at the end of March 2026. The school was recently awarded Cyber Essential Plus accreditation. The ICT Support at the School is currently provided by a single outsourced support provider which provides a mix of onsite and remote support. The School is taking the opportunity to go to the market to identify the best innovative and forward-looking partner to support them in the delivery and development of their ICT provision over the next five years. This procurement includes (but may not be limited to) the items listed below: A core managed service, management of all ICT against an agreed SLA A Service Desk, available 52 weeks a year including out of hours access and emergency support Local staffing which suppliers deem necessary to deliver the service and meet the SLA requirements Strategic advice and direction to the School's leaders regarding ICT policy, procedures and best practice Responsibility for design, specification, installation, and management of all ICT infrastructure Supply of goods and services based on an agreed Best Value approach Management of 3rd parties where relevant to the ICT support Relevant monitoring, management, patching Regular performance reporting Access to the highest quality digital training materials to support in-house delivery Advice on the impact of policy updates on the ICT solution and support There is an expectation that the provider will support and/or drive innovation, particularly around AI and environmental sustainability. Maintain technical documentation Maintain operational documentation, for example inventory management and risk registers Collective partnership targets aligned to the School's objectives In School support for the integration and upgrade of the connectivity, communications and security infrastructure as required Suppliers may be required to deliver a range of technology and change management projects in addition to the providing the core managed service. The School will provide a standard contract as part of the ITT Pack There is a requirement for TUPE from existing suppliers Lot 1: .
sig_84b530ce5b45a3905339.title: Wilson's School ICT Managed Service

sig_84dae88005aece561d37.description: The contracting organisation operates a heterogeneous ICT landscape with several thousand user accounts, various specialist applications and a growing number of privileged and business-critical accesses. The previous decentralised administration of passwords and sensitive access data leads to increased administrative effort, limited traceability and risks regarding information security, compliance and operational stability. As part of the further development of the information security and IAM strategy, a central, audit-proof and secure password manager solution is being procured. The aim is to replace unsystematic procedures and create a uniform platform for the secure storage, use and administration of passwords, secrets and other sensitive information. The future solution must meet both the requirements of modern security architectures and the regulatory and operational requirements of a public-law organisation. In particular, high demands regarding access security, encryption, traceability, governance and protection against unauthorised access must be met.
sig_84dae88005aece561d37.title: Password Manager

sig_84ec8d1d2858f9b1d81d.description: THIS IS NOT A PRELIMINARY NOTICE, A PROCUREMENT NOTICE, OR A CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT RATHER REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / MARKET SURVEY. National Bureau of Investigation is seeking for solutions (not only ready-made forensic products) to support Finnish Police forensic operations. The target is to identify components and capabilities that can form one integrated service and information system ecosystem for police forensic investigation operations. Respondents are encouraged to present innovative commercial, cross-sector or emerging solutions that could be adapted with reasonable effort and integrated with third-party solutions through open interfaces. The request for infromation is issued to gather information from market participants regarding innovative solutions, technologies and services applicable to police forensic investigation operations. National Bureau of Investigation is particularly interested in solutions originating from sectors other than forensic science, including healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, defence, critical infrastructure, laboratory environments, asset management and professional services. Solutions do not need to have been originally designed for forensic investigations. Respondents are encouraged to present commercially available products, platforms or services that could be adapted to forensic operations with reasonable configuration, integration or customization effort. The long-term objective is to enable one integrated service and information system ecosystem rather than isolated point solutions. The purpose of this RFI is to: • understand the state of the market, emerging innovations and relevant technology trends; • identify technical, functional, organizational and service-related capabilities available in the market; • identify solutions that may improve operational efficiency, quality management, traceability, resource planning, interoperability and decision-making; • support future procurement planning, including possible open procedures, competitive procedures with negotiation, innovation partnerships or other suitable procurement approaches. More details are in appendix 1. RESPONDING TO REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Respondents are invited to provide clear, concise and structured responses. Responses may include descriptive text, diagrams, references to standards, product or service descriptions, and anonymized case examples. For each proposed solution, respondents should explicitly state which RFI Part or Parts the solution covers. Respondents should also describe the interface technologies, integration architecture, data exchange mechanisms and relevant standards supported by the solution. We ask suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue to respond to the request for information by submitting materials related to the solutions no later than Ocotber 21, 2026, to the following address: sopimusasiat.krp@poliisi.fi. Please use the following subject line in your message: "RFI: Innovative solutions for forensic investigation operations". If the response contains the supplier's trade secrets or other confidential information, we ask the supplier to label the documents "Trade Secret". Information received through this RFI may be used to: • refine the scope, requirements and implementation options for possible future procurements; • identify suitable procurement procedures and market capabilities; • support strategic planning, innovation roadmaps and potential piloting or proof-of-concept activities. Whether or not you respond to this RFI will not prevent you from participating in any future competitive tendering process. All responses to this RFI received from suppliers will be treated as preliminary, non-binding and confidential. The information will be used solely for the purpose of preparing the procurement. All costs associated with submitting a response are at the respondent's own expense and risk. The request for information does not oblige National Bureau of Investigation to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request and the competitive tendering process may also be waived. National Bureau of Investigation may use the responses provided if it decides to conduct a competitive tendering process for the procurement. National Bureau of Investigation will make a decision on whether to conduct a competitive tendering process and on its timeline following the market survey. All information presented in the market survey is preliminary, is not binding on National Bureau of Investigation and may still change significantly during the preparation phase.
sig_84ec8d1d2858f9b1d81d.title: RFI: Innovative Solutions for Finnish Police Forensic Investigation Operations

sig_8504c197352dd25adf51.description: The tender concerns the procurement of an AI mammography solution for the Region of Southern Denmark and the Central Denmark Region, respectively. This is an IT system. As far as the Central Denmark Region is concerned, this is an option only. The Central Denmark Region may therefore choose to exercise or refrain from exercising the option to purchase an AI mammography solution. As a result of an increased population and an increasing average age in the population, an increase in the incidence of breast cancer is being seen in Denmark. An increase is expected from approx. 4.800 in 2024 to approx. 5310 cases of breast cancer in 2028. Early detection through breast cancer screening and best-practice treatment are considered crucial elements for reducing breast cancer-related mortality and morbidity in women. The breast cancer screening programme in the Region of Southern Denmark performs approx. 70.000 screenings annually. In addition, approx. 17.000 clinical mammography examinations are carried out annually. It is expected that approx. 10% of the clinical mammography examinations will be performed as tomosynthesis. For the Central Denmark Region, approx. 65.000 screenings and approx. 15.000 clinical mammography examinations are performed annually. Each screening examination consists of 4 X-ray images, 2 standard projections per breast. In cases of previous breast cancer and breast-conserving surgery, this is supplemented with a 3. projection. Today, each individual X-ray image is examined by two independent breast radiologists. If there is disagreement, the images are reviewed by a 3. examination. There is generally an increasing demand for breast diagnostics. Among other things, an increasing number of patients are being referred for investigation in fast-track breast cancer pathways as a result of an increase in the screening population as well as new investigation and treatment options. At the same time as the increasing need for mammography examinations, there is a nationwide challenge with a shortage of breast radiologists. Artificial intelligence (AI) solutions based on deep learning technology have in recent years shown great progress within medical image analysis, particularly with regard to the detection of breast cancer on mammograms. The tendered AI solution must be implemented at the Region of Southern Denmark's four hospital units (Odense University Hospital, Hospital Lillebælt, Hospital Sønderjylland and Esbjerg/Grindsted Hospital), which perform mammography examinations. The purpose of the acquisition of an AI mammography solution is therefore • to ensure that the national requirements for breast cancer screening can be maintained in the future, and • to free up breast radiologist resources for other tasks in connection with the detection of breast cancer. The solution must thus be able to relieve the "1. examiner" in the mammography screening programme as well as provide decision support in clinical mammography. Should the Central Denmark Region exercise the option, the solution for the Central Denmark Region will need to be installed at the following hospital units: Aarhus University Hospital, Regional Hospital Viborg and Regional Hospital Randers. The tender generally includes the following sub-services: • The AI solution itself • Installation, setup, operation and calibration of the system • Training of radiologists, system management and operating personnel • Maintenance and support of the AI solution As part of the tendered Contract, the following options are also offered for the Contracting Authority: • Possibility of using the AI solution in clinical mammography • Support for tomosynthesis (3D) in mammography screening • Purchase of additional screenings cf. Annex 3 Regarding options, reference is further made to the Draft Contract, clause 8, as well as Annex 2 and 3. The contract, including the Requirements Specification cf. Annexes 1, 2 and 8, contains a detailed description of the tendered products. The acceptance test in the Region of Southern Denmark is expected to be approved in early June 2026.

sig_850ffd8a35add872c9a3.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_85303de1d2afd00dfcb8.description: FROM: AFLCMC/WISK Special Warfare Contracting Office 1895 Fifth Street Wright Patterson AFB, OH 45433-7200 SUBJECT: Request for Information (RFI) – Next Generation Operational Control System (NGOCS) NOTICE This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing the NGOCS. CAPABILITY GAP Operators currently lack a lightweight, ruggedized, modular body-worn power, data, and edge-compute architecture capable of providing distributed processing capacity beyond the End User Device (EUD) for concurrent high-demand tactical workloads. Fielded systems rely on aging architecture, proprietary cabling, and limited processing capabilities at the edge. Consequently, the EUD is forced to absorb the entirety of application processing, edge-server hosting, message routing, video data links, and peripheral management. During high-tempo combat operations, this overreliance creates latency, power depletion, and reliability bottlenecks that can jeopardize the mission. INSTRUCTION TO POTENTIAL RESPONDENTS Interested parties who desire to participate in this SSS/RFI are encouraged to submit responses that demonstrate they presently have the technology and qualifications to provide the system described above. Responses shall also include the following information: Respondent Data: Company/Institute Name Address Point of Contact (to include phone number and email address) CAGE Code Web Page URL Pursuant to NAICS Code 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, state whether the company is: Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Women-Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Economically Disadvantaged Women- Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified HUBZone Certified (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Veteran Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified 8(a) Certified (Yes / No) Self-Certified or Third Party Certified SBA Certification Date: SBA Graduation Date: State whether the company is domestically or foreign-owned (if foreign, indicate the country of ownership). State whether the respondent is interested in being a prime or subcontractor for this requirement. Rough cost estimate (i.e. rough order of magnitude (ROM)) based on an optimum or varied pricing quantities (this is for Government budget planning purposes and will not be considered a bid or binding in any manner). If development and/or integration is required to meet the system requirements, the Government also needs an estimate of the development cost based on complexity (for planning purposes only) to include PHS&T, such as warranties, portable storage, special tooling required, and training. Indicate whether the company is currently performing this type of work/whether the capability can be obtained under an existing Government contract. Provide the contract number(s) and Government points of contact accordingly. Indicate whether the company currently provides this type of work as a commercial solution. In this instance, “commercial item” means an item that is of a type customarily used by the general public or non-Governmental entities for purposes other than Governmental purposes. Please indicate if this item has been sold, leased, or licensed to the general public; or has been offered for sale, lease, or license to the general public. Indicate whether all materials used are in compliance with the Buy American Act or Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. 2533a), as applicable. Describe any risks associated with the fulfillment of this projected requirement. This can include technical or schedule risks associated with development, key performance parameters, etc. Please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, and FAR 52.219-33, Non-Manufacturer Rule, would be achieved in the event the Government sets this requirement aside for small business. Include specific details regarding teaming arrangements, etc. If subcontracts are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and whether small or large businesses, including foreign, will be used. If this effort is not set aside for small business, small business utilization will be considered. Large and small businesses should provide a reasonable expectation for small business utilization as a percent of total contract value as well as supporting rationale for the recommended percentage. Please complete Attachment 1, Next Gen OCS Questionnaire, and Attachment 2, Next Gen OCS Requirements Compliance, and submit it with your package. RESPONSES, COMMUNICATIONS, AND ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS: The Government may contact respondents to obtain additional information or clarification in order to fully understand a company's response. This may include discussions, site visits, demonstrations, etc. to further the Government's understanding of a proposed solution, as well as a company's understanding of the Government's requirements. Responses shall not exceed 35 pages (including cover page). Include technical and descriptive text and photographs/illustrations to provide sufficient detail. The submitted documentation becomes the property of the United States Government and will not be returned. Respondents shall clearly mark proprietary data with the appropriate markings. Any proprietary information received in response to this request will be properly protected from any unauthorized disclosure. Any material that is not marked will be considered publicly releasable. Government-contracted contractor support personnel may handle proprietary data submitted in response to this RFI. These support personnel will have signed the same Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) as Government personnel. Broad industry participation for this RFI is encouraged. U.S. and non-U.S. firms are permitted to respond. Please note that prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be awarded a DOD contract; the NAICS code for this requirement, if applicable to the company’s capabilities, should be included in the company’s NAICS code listing in SAM. To learn more about this SAM requirement and how to register, please visit the SAM website at: https://www.sam.gov/portal/SAM Responses are due electronically by 12:00PM Eastern time on 22 October 2026 via email to: Capt Shaun Wheldon AFLCMC/WISN Contracting Officer shaun.wheldon@us.af.mil Mr. Matt Mangen AFLCMC/WISN Program Manager matthew.mangen.1@us.af.mil Mr. Joe Durham AFLCMC/WISN Systems Engineer joseph.durham.1.ctr@us.af.mil This notice may be updated as additional information becomes available. Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by email to the Contracting Officer identified above, with the other individuals identified above copied as a courtesy. This is a Request for Information (RFI) only to identify potential sources for the solution. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Government has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as creating such a commitment or as an authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. sig_854a6c15a0daf0f32001.description: The objective of the "WissPAS" programme is the development and implementation of a digital platform that enables the structured exchange of security-relevant data and information and supports their cooperative processing into reliable cross-organisations knowledge. In doing so, a digital interaction space is to be established which can generate new findings and insights through automated pattern recognition and data-driven synthesis. Such an interaction space contributes overall to bringing state actors in the security sector into a productive exchange, gaining new insights from the synthesis of their work results and providing impetus along the value chain. The targeted benefits can only be achieved if the users classify the knowledge platform as relevant to themselves and recognise added value in it to such an extent that they are motivated to actively participate - e.g. for the continuous feeding in of their own documents, data or datasets. Therefore, it is imperative to include the perspective of the targeted user groups in the development of the platform from the outset. Against this background, the project is structured into a study and an expansion stage: In a study, the needs and requirements of the users are structuredly recorded and analysed. This also includes what type of data and content the platform is suitable for and what findings are to be expected. In the subsequent expansion phase, the knowledge platform is then to be developed, implemented and made accessible to the users. Within the scope of this procurement, exclusively the services of the study are commissioned. Lot LOT-0000: Knowledge platform for state actors in the security sector (WissPAS); here: Study. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required. Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation. Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support. Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support. Requirements include edge processing, secure communications, remote software management, monitoring and diagnostics, onboard-system integration and future expansion throughout its operational lifecycle. sig_85a5bffb1213046bc6ac.description: Delivery, implementation, operation and maintenance of a sensor-based boarding supervision (SBBS) at Frankfurt/Main Airport, Terminal 1 Lot LOT-0000: LiDAR-based Sensor-Based Boarding Supervision (SBBS) for boarding gates in Terminal 1. Delivery, implementation, commissioning, operation and maintenance of a LiDAR-based Sensor-Based Boarding Supervision (SBBS) for boarding gates in Terminal 1 of Frankfurt/Main Airport The subject of this procurement is the following services: FraAlliance GmbH intends, after a successful proof of concept at Gate Z22, to roll out a Sensor-Based Boarding Supervision (SBBS) at the relevant boarding gates of Terminal 1 at Frankfurt/Main Airport. The subject is the planning, delivery, implementation, commissioning, operation and maintenance of a LiDAR-based solution including sensor hardware, on-premises edge AI infrastructure, VPN gateway, cloud-based software platform as well as integration, support and maintenance services. In particular, the solution is intended to automatically detect unauthorised tailgating at quick boarding gates and alarm in real time, record passenger numbers per boarding event, monitor queues and occupancy in gate areas, make the boarding and de-boarding flow visible, and provide historical data including event lists and replay function for analyses. Event and KPI data must be integrable into FraAlliance's data infrastructure via documented interfaces, in particular API and MQTT. The rollout is planned for a total of up to 30 gates in pier area A and up to 26 gates in pier areas A-Plus and Z and is to take place in several independently deliverable waves. The contract also includes planning and validation of sensor positions, calibration, acceptance support (FAT/SAT), training, documentation, preventive and corrective maintenance, spare parts supply, security and software updates, and technical support. The processing of LiDAR data must be completely anonymous. Recording video or biometric data is not permitted. Backend and cloud infrastructure must be operated within the EU/EEA. sig_85ae222284e24f061f42.description: SDU, in cooperation with a third party and HPE, has entered into a strategic and exclusive partnership for the establishment, operation and ongoing development of a green, sovereign high-performance computing (HPC) and cloud infrastructure. This partnership forms the basis of a unique national initiative designed to deliver cutting-edge computing services to Danish research, public institutions and private sector actors. The project is physically anchored at a third-party state-of-the-art data centre optimised for green operations, including advanced cooling and heat-recovery technology. The third party has committed these facilities exclusively to this partnership, and under a binding agreement, only HPE equipment and HPE-certified personnel are permitted to operate and maintain the infrastructure. This exclusivity is crucial to ensure the integration of HPE's systems with the third party's proprietary and highly specialised data centre environment, particularly regarding energy efficiency and sustainability. The exclusivity agreement between the third party and HPE means that HPE is the only supplier authorised to supply, install, operate and maintain HPC hardware in this context. No other suppliers have access to or are certified to operate within the third party's facilities. Therefore, the procurement of HPC equipment from any other supplier would be incompatible with the contractual and technical constraints of the project. In short, HPE's role cannot be replaced by any other supplier's. Furthermore, the tripartite agreement between the third party, HPE and SDU ensures long-term alignment in both technological development and sustainability strategy. The agreement includes joint commitments to innovation in green data infrastructure and cloud services that no other combination of partners could deliver in the same context. The exclusive nature of this cooperation is not based on product preferences, but on the operational and strategic integration of infrastructure, personnel and sustainability systems that can only be achieved through HPE. Therefore, the choice of HPE as a supplier is determined by the unique and exclusive framework established for this project. A competitive tendering process is not applicable in this case, as no other supplier could meet the requirements under the existing contractual obligations with the third party and SDU.

sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.description: Vantaan kaupunki is planning the procurement of a new cultural heritage system to replace the current collection management system (Kirsti), which was implemented in 2014. The current system is technically obsolete, slow, and difficult to develop. The goal is a modern, easy-to-use, and efficient solution that supports museum operations, cultural heritage management, and digital transition. The system must support, among other things, object, image, AV, paper, and cultural environment archives, a reference library, actor information, and press clippings. Integrations are required for Finna, Finto, MapInfo, Matti, the Finnish Heritage Agency's spatial data, and the PAS service. Key features: efficient search, clarity, ease of use, and compliance with GDPR requirements. Users: Museum staff, consultants, authorities, collection service customers, and the public via Finna. Targeted benefits: Better availability of information, increased work efficiency, reduction of unnecessary work, and improvement of processes. Strategic importance: supports the digital transition, has a broad impact, and generates value for over 10 000 residents.
sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.title: Procurement of a cultural heritage system
