sig_8810568850dc2662a41a.description: The London Borough of Barnet (the "Council") is seeking to engage with the market in preparation for the procurement of Level 3 Oracle Cloud Fusion Support Services for its Oracle Cloud Fusion environment. This engagement is part of the Council’s strategic transition to a new support partner following the conclusion of its current post-implementation support contract. The Council is issuing this notice in accordance with Sections 16 and 17 of the Procurement Act 2023 to invite potential providers to participate in early market engagement activities. Please note: this is not a call for competition. Scope of the Requirement The Council is seeking a highly capable support partner with demonstrable experience supporting UK Local Authorities to provide Level 3 support across the following Oracle Cloud components: •Oracle SaaS (Fusion Applications): Finance, Procurement, Human Capital Management (HCM), Payroll, Time & Labour (OTL), iExpenses, and Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) •Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) •Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and Oracle Database •Custom integrations and reporting (OTBI, BI Publisher, SmartView, ADFDI) The successful partner will be expected to: •Resolve complex technical and functional issues escalated from the Council’s internal support team •Manage quarterly patching and environment refreshes •Provide strategic input into change governance and roadmap development •Deliver continuous improvement and value-added services, including automation and innovation •Support knowledge transfer and internal capability building A Market Engagement Event will be held on: Thursday 23 October 2025 Time: 11:30-12:30 Virtual (MS Teams) This session will provide an overview of the Council’s Oracle Cloud environment, support model, and procurement timeline. sig_881df73a9ad39da56278.description: As announced in Renewing Fostering: homes for 10,000 more children, the Department for Education (DfE) is exploring how digital solutions can support the successful onboarding of more prospective foster carers. This could include providing a simple and easy journey through the application process, minimising drop-off points caused by delays in communication about progress and outcomes, and enabling richer data on fostering recruitment through to approvals to support decision-making at a local and national level. The number of foster carers in England has been steadily decreasing since 2021, which is reducing the number of loving homes available for children and young people who need foster care. This is a preliminary market engagement notice to share DfE’s interest in engaging with the market to help inform the design and potential delivery approach of digital solutions for fostering recruitment. We also want to understand market interest, capability and capacity for delivery and understand new or innovative ideas for supporting fostering recruitment with digital solutions that improve the end-to-end applicant journey, thereby reducing dropout at critical points of the recruitment process. To deliver on the ambitious plan, we are seeking a digital solution that can: • allow prospective foster carers to make an application and manage it throughout the fostering application process, from initial enquiry to approval (this may include making contact with their fostering service, booking appointments and monitoring the progress of their application online) • help fostering hubs and local authorities to manage prospective foster carers through the application process through real-time insights and by engaging relevant agencies to support the onboarding process • providing appropriate and timely information to enable applicants, hubs and local authorities to make informed decisions • provide a simple customer journey that is interoperable with other key national and local fostering guidance, including potential new elements such as a national front door • enabling the gathering of rich and consistent data on the hub fostering recruitment process and pipeline, supporting effective data sharing between DfE, hubs, local authorities and other relevant agencies, and helping to better target interventions and efforts where they are most needed. • a scalable and secure solution that is interoperable with existing platforms and infrastructure, enabling improved data sharing and portability of applications across fostering services, while also strengthening the overall digital and data capability across the system • align with government data, digital and technology standards to provide a seamless digital customer experience to the applicant (including the Government Digital Service (GDS) Standards and The Technology Code of Practice), legal compliance with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 and The Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018) We are seeking to understand market capacity to deliver a private beta in late 2026 that will test and inform the potential for national scaling. Specifically, we are interested in hearing from suppliers with experience of: • providing digital solutions to support better children's social care practice (may include fostering) • designing accessible, inclusive and user-focused digital solutions that meet government standards • delivering solutions using a test-and-learn approach with a limited number of users and organisations to prepare for, and enable, a national rollout • working with local government and interoperability of complex digital systems • developing WCAG 2.2AA accessibility compliant digital solutions Feedback from the market will help shape the department’s proposed scope to ensure any offer meets sector needs. This notice is not being used as a call for competition. All information in this notice will be subject to further agreement and internal approval, including the estimated funding amount. DfE reserves the right not to progress to a formal procurement process. . sig_882cdf60038304e89037.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. sig_885f62654a70046ee804.description: Heka is extensively renewing its information systems in the coming years. The most central objectives for all system development are improving the customer experience, digitising operating methods, and improving the quality of information supporting decision-making. The subject of this procurement is accounting and internal accounting, as well as accounts payable solutions, the related implementation project, and ongoing maintenance service. In addition, a budgeting system may be added to the procurement later based on a framework agreement. The solution package will be implemented at Heka and Heka's subsidiary, Kiinteistö Oy Laivalahdentori. The goal is a so-called off-the-shelf software solution that covers Heka's needs. The primary objective is to procure the solution as a cloud or SaaS service. The solution must enable flexible integrations with systems outside the procured solution. Systems already in use and the renewing solutions must function side-by-side as a whole, relying on the existing technical environment where necessary. It must be possible to transfer the data required in the solution from source systems and to source systems via a data warehouse. Some data may be transferred directly between the source system and the procured solution. The procured solution must enable the transfer of master data with a master data system outside the procurement in both directions. With this request for information, suppliers are invited to a market dialogue regarding questions related to the procurement. The goal of the request for information is to obtain comprehensive information regarding the procurement so that a potential call for tenders can be carried out as appropriately as possible. This request for information is not a call for tenders, and it does not bind Heka to publish a call for tenders later. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the call for tenders in the described manner. All information and requirements presented in the request for information and its attached materials regarding the planned procurement are still preliminary at this stage and may change. Responding to the request for information does not bind the supplier, and responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential call for tenders to be published later. The contracting authority may use the information received through the request for information in the planning of the procurement. The information collected through the request for information will remain confidential. The goal is to launch the procurement procedure during the spring of 2026. sig_88725d78155fd6b19c48.description: The Commission is seeking to procure a fully bilingual (Welsh and English) Senedd business management system. The contract will include the supply, implementation and ongoing support of the solution. The Commission seeks a sustainable, adaptable and supportable solution that can meet its current and future business requirements while providing long-term value, service continuity and the benefits of ongoing product investment. Suppliers must demonstrate: • successful delivery and operation of solutions with relevant or comparable capabilities; • experience supporting parliamentary, legislative, democratic services, governance or similarly complex and regulated environments; • an established, supportable and adaptable solution with demonstrable capability relevant to the Commission's requirements; • a credible implementation and migration approach; and • a clear, realistic and supportable route to meeting the Commission's functional and non-functional requirements Suppliers must clearly distinguish between capabilities that are available within the proposed solution, those that will be delivered through configuration, and those that will require product development, customisation or other enhancement. Any such activity must form part of a credible, deliverable and supportable approach to meeting the Commission's requirements. The Commission's strategic direction is to adopt Software as a Service (SaaS) solutions wherever appropriate. However, recognising the specialist nature of this market, suppliers may propose alternative delivery models where they can demonstrate that the proposed solution is an established, supportable and adaptable solution with demonstrable capability relevant to the Commission's requirements. The Commission does not intend to commission the development of a wholly new solution. It is seeking approaches that maximise the reuse of existing and demonstrable capabilities, minimise bespoke development, and support long-term maintainability, interoperability, data portability, supplier competition and whole-life value. The contract will be for an initial period of five years from the Go Live date, with the option for the Commission to extend the contract for up to a further five years. Lot 1: . None

The consulting services are expected to concern: - Development and review of business models, strategies, and target images, including promotional policy, banking, and regulatory aspects. - Analysis, optimisation, and redesign of organisational structures and business processes, particularly in the context of digital transformation. - Development and evaluation of fund solutions, public-private partnerships, and models for mobilising private capital. - Consulting on strategic and process-related issues in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and generative AI (GenAI), particularly regarding governance, organisation, and best practices (no technical implementation). - Conducting market, competition, and impact analyses, including benchmarking, market trends, and best-practice comparisons. - Support in identifying and evaluating investment needs, regulatory hurdles, and other specific research questions. - Moderation of workshops, conducting interviews, and presentation of results. Lot 2 comprises specialist, division-specific, and cross-business-area specialist consulting for KfW and its subsidiaries IPEX, KfW Capital, and DEG. sig_88db234e12c255703a67.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. Q&A will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. No other changes were made form the original version.

sig_88e69d08d79e2d641112.description: Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council has received funding through the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB) to develop and deliver a PEACEPLUS Local Community Action Plan. Programme 1 entitled ‘Our Historical Borough’ will ensure the regeneration and connectivity of heritage and historical sites throughout the Borough. As part of this, Council will deliver a range of new heritage focused visitor products, including walking and driving trails, promoted through two central Heritage Hubs. This programme will provide a platform for building a strong and vibrant local historical and tourism economy, whilst protecting and supporting the growth and knowledge of our shared history for many years to come. As part of the ‘Our Historical Borough’ Programme, Council seeks to deliver the following projects: • The creation of two designated Heritage Hubs - one in Antrim and one in Newtownabbey • The creation of five themed driving trails across the Borough • The creation of ten walking trails across the Borough • A full signage and wayfinding upgrade of heritage sites across the Borough • The development of an app to accompany the trails giving additional information on secondary sites of interest and visitor information. The purpose of this questionnaire is to gain an understanding of the latest developments, technology and products in the tourism and heritage industry, in relation to the above projects and how this can inform the Council’s tender specification. Any information gathered will NOT be considered in any future tender evaluation exercise. Participation or non-participation in this pre-procurement market engagement shall not prevent any supplier participating in a potential procurement process nor is it intended that any information supplied shall place any supplier at an advantage in any upcoming procurement process. For avoidance of doubt, this stage of the project is not part of a formal procurement process. Any procurement process will be conducted in accordance with rules and regulations applicable to projects funded under the PEACEPLUS programme. Lot 1: .

Detailed requirements regarding the subject matter and quantity of the procurement are contained in the Technical Specification forming part of the Tender Documentation. Continued from the Exclusion Grounds (GR-Procedure-ExclusionGrounds) cell: - The contracting authority (CA) shall check the exclusion grounds under 129. § (1)-(4) paragraphs of the Vbt. during the procedure with the involvement of the Constitution Protection Office (hereinafter: CPO). - Under 46. § (4) paragraph of the Vbt., the tenderer (TE) must declare in writing in its application to participate that neither the TE nor the economic operator participating in the verification of suitability is subject to the exclusion grounds set out in 45. § (1) and (2) paragraphs, 128. § (1) paragraph, and 129. § (1)-(4) paragraphs. - TE shall submit its declaration under 51. § (8) paragraph of the Vbt. that it will not involve any subcontractor subject to the scope of exclusion grounds under 45. § (1)-(2) paragraph, 128. § (1) paragraph, and 129. § (1)-(4) paragraphs of the Vbt. for the performance of the contract. - Pursuant to 116. § of the Vbt., solely economic operators listed in the register maintained by the CPO may participate in the procurement procedure as an applicant to participate, tenderer, subcontractor, and key subcontractor, with the exceptions set out in 117. § (2)-(5) paragraphs. The register includes: a) economic operators holding a PCL defined in the Mavtv., b) economic operators that have passed the preliminary qualification under 118. § of the Vbt., and c) economic operators that have passed the qualification related to the procurement procedure under 119. § of the Vbt. Pursuant to 129. § (1) paragraph of the Vbt., the CA must exclude from the procedure any TE who: a) is not listed in the register and has not attached the completed data sheets and declarations according to the template specified in separate legislation in order to initiate the procurement-related qualification by the contracting authority, b) is not entered in the register as a result of the procurement-related qualification assessment, c) has not attached the data sheets and declarations filled in by the subcontractor according to the template specified in a ministerial decree issued pursuant to the authorisation of this act, in order to initiate the subcontractor's procurement-related qualification by the contracting authority in respect of a subcontractor not listed in the register whom it intends to involve, or d) in respect of whom, during its supplementary check, the national security service has established the existence of a national security risk factor or a security risk factor endangering the proper operation of the national security service. Pursuant to 117. § (2) paragraph of the Vbt., the contracting authority prescribes that the condition for sending the summary concluding the participation phase is the inclusion of the applicant to participate and its key subcontractor in the register. sig_88f2aa3b467ba46f9464.description: Organisations are invited to take part in the pre maket engagement seek input from market participants to inform and help Ofcom inform our procurement strategy for our employee voice programme. Ofcom currently relies on an annual colleague survey as the primary means of gathering measurable feedback on employee experience. This model does not provide sufficiently timely or agile insight into emerging colleague experience, culture, engagement and organisational challenges. As a result, there is a risk that feedback is gathered too infrequently to support timely action and evidence-based decision making. The opportunity is to explore how to procure a pulse survey tool that enables shorter, more frequent colleague surveys, as well as the ability to run multiple surveys in parallel across different populations and topics. This would support a more agile employee listening model, provide quicker insight into priority issues, and strengthen the link between colleague feedback and visible action. Lot 1: . None

sig_88f7f0cb272c24a53afb.description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) Counterterrorism and Emergency Planning Branch (CPD) This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and information gathering only. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, a request for proposal, or an obligation on the part of the Federal Government. Participation is voluntary and at no cost to the Government. 1. Overview & Purpose The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Counterterrorism and Emergency Planning Branch (CPD), will host an Industry Day focused on GPS?enabled monitoring devices with integrated two?way phone call capability and associated monitoring and data?management services. The purpose of this event is to obtain information from industry on current technology capabilities, operational use cases, and emerging innovations applicable to correctional environments. Input gathered will support the BOP’s efforts to enhance inmate accountability, improve institutional safety, and strengthen the management of inmate movement and monitoring. 2. Industry Day Objectives Vendor participation will assist the Government in understanding: • Capabilities and limitations of GPS?enabled monitoring devices with two?way communication • Integration potential with BOP systems and operational workflows • Data?management tools, analytics, reporting, and service models • Security features, tamper detection, and data?protection mechanisms • Deployment and support considerations • Applicability to correctional use cases 3. Event Details Dates: October 13–14, 2026 Time: 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM Location: 320 First Street NW 8th Floor Conference Room (MAP Room) Washington, DC Vendor Presentations: Each vendor will be allotted up to 60 minutes for their demonstration and discussion. Individual time slots will be scheduled following registration. 4. Suggested NAICS Codes Potentially applicable NAICS codes include (subject to Government confirmation): • 334220 – Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing • 334290 – Other Communications Equipment Manufacturing • 541690 – Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services • 561621 – Security Systems Services Vendors may propose alternatives they consider more appropriate. 5. Target Vendor Audience This Industry Day is intended for: • Device manufacturers • Monitoring/data?management service providers • Software developers and systems integrators • Security technology firms • Research and development organizations supporting law enforcement/corrections 6. Demonstration Logistics and Requirements To assist with planning, vendors should note the following: • Vendors are responsible for bringing their own equipment and connectivity unless otherwise coordinated. • Notify the Government of any wireless transmission requirements. • Bring necessary cables, adapters, chargers, or display devices. • Clearly mark any proprietary content shared during demonstrations. • Allow adequate time for building security screening; a government?issued ID is required for entry. 7. Capability Statement Requirements Vendors interested in participating must submit a brief capability statement including: • Company name, address, and point?of?contact • Description of relevant technologies and capabilities • Applicable NAICS code(s) • Past performance or operational experience (if any) • Technology readiness and deployment model • Any scheduling constraints or preferred demonstration windows Format: PDF preferred; recommended page limit: 5 pages. 8. Registration Instructions Submit capability statements and requests to participate to: Stephanie Wyatt Email: swyatt@bop.gov Subject line: Industry Day Registration – GPS Monitoring Devices Registration closes when scheduling capacity is reached or by the date specified in the final posting. 9. Questions for Industry To support productive discussion, vendors should be prepared to address: • How does your technology address operational challenges specific to correctional environments? • What differentiates your product or service from others in the market? • What infrastructure is required to implement your solution? • How does your system ensure data integrity, communications reliability, and tamper detection? • What analytics, dashboards, or reporting tools are included? • What durability and maintenance requirements apply in long?term correctional use? 10. Disclaimers • Participation in this Industry Day is voluntary; costs will not be reimbursed. • This event is not part of any source selection process. • No contract award will result from this notice or the Industry Day. • The Government will not provide individualized feedback. • Proprietary information should be clearly labeled.

sig_88fe649111a131b35915.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The aim of the tender is to provide a future-proof and demand-oriented expandable central backup solution that enables reliable backup as well as fast and reliable recovery of the business-critical and medically relevant data and IT systems arising at Magdeburg University Hospital. The solution to be procured must take into account the requirements for secure, highly available and permanently available operation in a KRITIS-relevant environment and thus make a significant contribution to the operational safety, fail-safe operation and resilience of the IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. The overall solution to be procured is to consist of four coordinated system components: • a high-performance all-flash backup appliance for processing large amounts of data and a high number of parallel backup and restore processes, • a highly available backup storage system as the primary backup target with integrated deduplication function, • a high-performance enterprise rack server as a Veeam backup server as well as • two appropriately dimensioned enterprise rack servers as Veeam backup proxies. The backup infrastructure is to be designed in such a way that it takes into account the existing and foreseeable future requirements of Magdeburg University Hospital. In addition to the delivery of the required hardware and software, including all components and licences required for intended operation, the scope of services also includes the professional installation, configuration and integration of the overall solution into the existing IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. Furthermore, the scope of services includes the commissioning of the overall solution as well as the execution of the required functional, performance and acceptance tests. The contractor must provide a fully functional and ready-for-operation overall solution that complies with the requirements laid down in the specification of services and the schedule of services. All services are to be provided in compliance with the legal, regulatory and technical requirements applicable at the time of service provision as well as the relevant norms and standards. Lot LOT-0000: Central backup system. Procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The specific functional requirements result from the schedule of services.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. ANNUAL REPRESENTATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS: Potential offerors are notified that effective 01 Jan 2005 to be eligible for an award and in compliance with FAR 52.204-7 and DFARS 252.204-7007 Alternate A, they must submit Annual Representations and Certifications, via SAM.gov. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. sig_896cbec3f767697539ac.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation and launch of an analytical platform (analytical portal) enabling the processing, analysis and visualisation of data, in particular environmental data at the disposal of the Contracting Authority. The platform will be a Business Intelligence (BI) class solution, based exclusively on open technologies (FOSS), ensuring scalability and security of data processing. The Contractor is obliged to design the solution in a way that limits the occurrence of single points of failure in components remaining within the scope of implementation. The platform is to enable effective creation, publishing and management of analytical reports, as well as data visualisation in the form of charts, tables, maps and the preparation of ready-made reports and/or dashboards, with the simultaneous possibility of defining access levels to reports - from internal access to public sharing of data with citizens and external stakeholders. The Contractor is also obliged to conduct an analysis of the data resources indicated by the Contracting Authority and to prepare analytical reports and/or dashboards based on them, in accordance with the requirements of the Contracting Authority. An important goal of the contract is also to prepare and conduct training for IT administrators and substantive users, covering both administrative and technical aspects, as well as the practical use of reports, dashboards and analytical functions of the system. The construction of the platform in the field of environmental data analysis is aimed at improving and expanding the functionality in terms of data browsing by Citizens, along with the possibility of independent analysis of this data. The tool will provide users with more effective and efficient access to GIOŚ data and will contribute to the dissemination of environmental data. Additional information in accordance with the detailed description of the subject of the contract constituting Annex no. 2 to the SWZ. The construction of the data portal in the field of environmental data analysis is aimed at improving and expanding the functionality in terms of data browsing by Citizens on their own, along with the possibility of independent analysis of this data. The functionality will use analytical tools in a transparent and user-friendly way. The tool will provide users with more effective, efficient and faster access to GIOŚ data and will contribute to the dissemination of environmental data. Access to data made available on the portal will be free of charge and open to Citizens - without the need to log in.
sig_896cbec3f767697539ac.title: Construction of an analytical portal for environmental data

The service to be procured consists of the preparation of the Feasibility Study for the project "Electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia - Țăndărei circulation section" – Regional Railway Branch Constanța and the submission of the documentation for obtaining the urbanism certificate, as well as obtaining all permits/approvals with a view to promoting the Government Decision for the approval of the technical and economic indicators and for the expropriation of properties related to the investment project "Electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia - Țăndărei circulation section" – Regional Railway Branch Constanța - Feasibility Study Phase, in accordance with the requirements of GD 907/2016 and of Specifications No 8.2/1182/02.06.2025. The preparation of the Feasibility Study shall be carried out in accordance with the legislative and regulatory framework in force, in order to present the best alternative regarding the optimal investment option from a technical, economic as well as operational point of view for increasing energy efficiency and environmental sustainability through the electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia – Țăndărei circulation section. ***GIVEN THE CHARACTER LIMITS FOR TEXT FIELDS IMPOSED BY SEAP, THE FULL TEXT CAN BE FOUND IN THE FILE "OA – FD - INSTRUCTIONS TO TENDERERS", ATTACHED WITHIN THE DOCUMENTS COMPRISING THE TENDER DOCUMENTATION.*** SUSPENSIVE CLAUSE: The award procedure is conducted under the incidence of this suspensive clause, in the sense that the conclusion of the sectoral contract is conditioned by the securing of the funding source, the signing of the contract being possible only if the provisions regarding the commitment of expenditures from budgets falling under the incidence of public finance legislation are complied with. Before concluding the contract with the economic operator who will be declared the winner following the completion of the sectoral procurement procedure for the services for the "Electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia - Țăndărei circulation section" – Regional Railway Branch Constanța - Feasibility Study Phase, approval for signing it shall be requested and obtained from the Board of Directors of CNCF „CFR” SA. Number of days by which economic operators may request clarifications before the deadline for submitting tenders: 22 days The contracting entity shall respond to requests for clarifications on the 12th day before the deadline for submitting tenders. The service to be procured consists of the preparation of the Feasibility Study for the project "Electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia - Țăndărei circulation section" – Regional Railway Branch Constanța and the submission of the documentation for obtaining the urbanism certificate, as well as obtaining all permits/approvals with a view to promoting the Government Decision for the approval of the technical and economic indicators and for the expropriation of properties related to the investment project "Electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia - Țăndărei circulation section" – Regional Railway Branch Constanța - Feasibility Study Phase, in accordance with the requirements of GD 907/2016 and of Specifications No 8.2/1182/02.06.2025. The preparation of the Feasibility Study shall be carried out in accordance with the legislative and regulatory framework in force, in order to present the best alternative regarding the optimal investment option from a technical, economic as well as operational point of view for increasing energy efficiency and environmental sustainability through the electrification of the Ciulnița – Slobozia – Țăndărei circulation section. The general objective is part of the "Railway infrastructure development strategy for the year 2021-2030" approved by GD No 985/2020, specific objective A5: "Increasing energy efficiency and reducing the pollution level" aims to increase energy efficiency and environmental sustainability through the electrification of certain circulation sections in the Romanian railway system and to increase the electrification level of the Romanian railway network. The integration of sustainable transport between Romania's regions will be facilitated, contributing to the socio-economic development of the crossed areas, improving Romania's economic competitiveness and creating the conditions for increasing the volume of goods and the number of passengers on the railway network. The specific objectives of the project "Electrification of the Ciulnița-Slobozia-Țăndărei circulation section" are the following: a) increasing the average circulation speed of trains; b) increasing the attractiveness of rail transport on the Ciulnița – Slobozia – Țăndărei section; c) minimising negative environmental effects; d) increasing transport volume by rail; e) maintaining and, where appropriate, attracting new rail transports on the territory of Romania; f) increasing productivity and reducing operating costs in traffic management by increasing the degree of centralization of signaling installations (SCB disc); g) streamlining operations in railway nodes to ensure faster connections with other railway routes in the area by integrating signaling installations into traffic management centers (SCB); h) increasing the level of rail traffic safety by modernizing mechanical installations (SCB); i) increasing the revenues of Regional Railway Branch Constanța from the infrastructure use fee. The duration of the contract is 30 months from the issuance of the Order to Commence, of which: a) The duration for the provision of services is 17 months (510 days), of which: - 12 months (360 days) effective duration for the preparation of deliverables; - 5 months (150 days) necessary for verification and approval activities and documents/deliverables by the Contracting Entity. b) The duration for the finalization of the expropriation procedure is 13 months (390 days), of which: - 12 months (360 days) necessary for the finalization of the expropriation procedure;

- 1 month (30 days) for verification and approval by the beneficiary of the Report on the finalization of the expropriation procedure.

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. Before submitting the electronic Annual Representations and Certifications, Contractors must be registered in the SAM Database. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) REGISTRATION: Before the Government can award a contract, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). It is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all the Offeror’s data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. (End of Amendment) Amendment 06 – Revision to TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language and GFP Clause List (21 November 2024) The purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection language included in Section I paragraph 9 (formerly included in Section I paragraph 8) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. The revised paragraph is as follows: 9) Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors are notified that subsequent Call Announcements shall include a requirement for submission of the documents identified below. Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. Additionally, the purpose of this amendment is to revise the TACTICAL Government Furnished Property Clause list in Section I paragraph 10 (formerly Section I paragraph 9) of the TACTICAL full text announcement included in the attachments. The revised paragraph is as follows: a) Government Furnished Property (GFP): To be determined for each award. In accordance with FAR 45.201(b), the contractor is responsible for all costs related to making the property available for use, such as payment of all transportation, installation, or rehabilitation costs. However, any entity that previously applied for a specific TAG but was NOT selected, or any entity that was removed from a specific TAG, may reapply for inclusion under this call. sig_89b4d38947588c0d2485.description: The Services du Parlement constitute the staff upon which the Federal Assembly and its organs rely. They assist the latter in the exercise of their duties and carry out the tasks set out in Article 64 of the Parliament Act of 13 December 2002 (ParlA) and Article 17 of the Parliamentary Administration Ordinance of 3 October 2003 (PAO). They ensure liaison between the Federal Assembly, on the one hand, and the Federal Council, other authorities and the public, on the other. They preserve and defend the interests and dignity of the Federal Assembly and its organs. In accordance with the separation of powers, they are attached to Parliament; they are independent of the Federal Council and the administration. The Administrative Delegation, which assumes supreme management of the Services du Parlement, is composed of the presidents of the federal chambers. In accordance with Article 12 of the Rules of Procedure of the Services du Parlement, the Services du Parlement provide information on the Federal Assembly and parliamentary work in particular and offer parliamentarians services in the fields of documentation and information technology. In this context, the Services du Parlement manage a website (parl.ch) on which comprehensive information on parliamentary work is made available to the public. The tender for which a service provider is sought aims essentially to replace the current website of the Services du Parlement, including the content management system, by the end of 2027. It covers in particular the configuration and integration of the CMS, the connection of surrounding systems and necessary web services, the implementation of a CMS-based front-end, including its redesign, with an emphasis on accessibility and mobile-friendliness. From the commissioning of the new website, support and maintenance of the new solution, which will be continuously developed, must be ensured for four to a maximum of ten years. While the CMS is to be operated in the computer centre of the Services du Parlement, a public cloud is planned for the operation of the front-end. The storage location of the data for the public cloud infrastructure used must be located in Switzerland and be protected as far as possible against any political influence, which will guarantee the digital sovereignty of the new website. The operating solution chosen is generally sensible; if, however, during subsequent conceptual work, another approach proves more appropriate, this could be examined. The operating architecture is detailed in Annex 10 (IT Architecture).

sig_89dcc387f1cb1aea4c3a.description: The Ministry of foreign Affairs, Green Diplomacy and Climate (KLIMA) has decided to cancel the tender procedure, as only irregular tenders have been received – tenders not fulfilling the minimum requirements and will in accordance with section 61(1)(2) of the Public Procurement Act apply a competitive procedure with negotiation without prior publication, cf. section 61(4). KLIMA wishes to engage a Management Support Consultant (Consultant) to ensure implementation and completion of all the ongoing Danida Green Business Partnerships (DGBP) activities based on sound project and financial management support. The objective of the Consultant is to assume the functions of project implementation support, financial management support and programme level monitoring and reporting. The Client will maintain oversight over the Services performed by the Consultant and the strategic leadership of DGBP. The Consultant shall perform at least the following activities and services: • Manage and implement all the DGBP activities effectively in accordance with the agreed partnership project agreements and contracts. • Provide relevant business and project management support and guidance to actors supported under the instruments. • Provide for achievement of results as defined in the Results Framework in the project document of the instrument. This includes monitoring the DGBP activities effectively. • Provide overall financial management including verification and approval of project workplans, budgets, and reports as well as disbursement requests from the partners. This should be done in accordance with the DGBP financial guidelines and sound financial management principles. • Maintaining full compliance with MFA’s Aid Management Guidelines (AMG) and Financial Management Guidelines (FMG), and ensuring high standards of financial management, procurement, anti-corruption, and risk mitigation. • On request provide relevant information on concrete projects and communication material in Danish and highlight positive lessons learned. Ensure sharing of relevant knowledge and information that generate interest and effective participation in the instruments. The DGBP is a programme that funds and supports market-based partnership projects between commercial and non-commercial partners in developing countries addressing climate and environmental challenges while contributing to inclusive growth and improved livelihoods. Each partnership project consists of at least one commercial partner and one non-commercial partner. A DGBP project has its own results framework and contributes to the overall objectives of the programme by linking to specific indicators in the overall results framework. The objective of DGBP is to enhance global green transition and private-led inclusive economic growth through innovative partnerships. DGBP aims at contributing to two outcomes: 1) Reduced vulnerability to climate change, reduced strain on natural resources and the environment and stabilization of GHG emissions, and 2) inclusive private sector growth and improved livelihoods. The climate and environmental outcomes are estimated in terms of avoided negative effects on the climate and environment compared to status quo solutions. Income and livelihood effects are assessed from the number of people engaged in the activities and the level of targeting products and services towards underserved populations. There are two funding windows in the programme: Full projects of up to DKK 15 million (minimum DKK 4 million) and maturation projects of up to DKK 1.5 million (minimum DKK 0.8 million). Maturation projects can last up to 18 months, while a full project can last up to five years. DGBP was launched in 2022 as a four-year programme (2022-2025) and was open for applications from 2022-2025, meaning that the last commitments were given in 2025 and that the programme is now closed to new applications. However, many of the funded projects will continue implementation during the coming years and the last one is expected to be closed only during 2030. The fund has been administered by an external Management Support Consultant (MSC), which has been responsible for organising annual calls for applications and undertake activities to spur interest in Denmark and in the partner countries in close coordination with the Danish embassies and other relevant stakeholders. The administrative responsibility in each partnership project rests with the non-commercial partner(s), who will also be responsible for annual progress reporting, financial reporting and audits. A programme-level progress report is prepared annually by the MSC. The MSC is providing advice and instructions to the administrative partners in relation to budgeting, reporting and audits, but the funds are disbursed directly to the administrative partners from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (“MFA” or the “Client”) in agreed instalments. Virtual annual monitoring meetings with all partners are organised by the MSC on the basis of the annual reporting. The annual meetings, which take place during March/April, are an opportunity to revise plans and targets in view of the progress achieved and the development in the context. The contract with the current MSC expires at the end of September 2026. Therefore, a new MSC contract for management of the ongoing DGBP projects until their completion is needed from 1st October 2026. The Services are expected to be carried out in Denmark, as regularly physical meetings with the MFA are required. It is expected that there will be 29 DGBP full projects under implementation by October 2026 and 1 DGBP full project, which has completed implementation and is in the closing phase. In addition to the one full project in the closing phase, 4-5 DGBP maturation projects are expected to be in the closing phase by October 2026.
sig_89dcc387f1cb1aea4c3a.title: Management Support for the Danida Green Business Partnership Programme

Lothian Pension Fund is seeking to engage with the market in advance of procuring a strategic managed ICT services partner. The organisation employs approximately 120 staff and delivers pension services to more than 103,000 members. Lothian Pension Fund requires a secure, resilient and modern ICT service to support its operations within a highly regulated pension administration and investment management environment. The anticipated scope includes service design and transition, service desk and end-user support, infrastructure and network management, cloud and Microsoft 365 services, storage, backup and data management, identity and access management, telephony, business continuity and disaster recovery, security management, supplier management, and strategic ICT advisory and project services. The successful supplier will be expected to deliver a highly available, secure and scalable technology environment that supports both day-to-day operations and the organisation's longer-term strategic objectives. The supplier will also be expected to deliver a smooth transition from the incumbent provider, ensuring continuity of service and minimising operational disruption. Lothian Pension Fund is seeking a mature, collaborative and forward-thinking technology partner that will work transparently alongside the organisation, contributing strategic insight, innovation and continuous improvement to support its long-term objectives. The successful supplier will be expected to provide full visibility of service performance and operational information, enabling informed decision-making and effective governance. Lothian Pension Fund places significant importance on data transparency and accessibility and expects service management tooling and reporting capabilities that enable authorised personnel to independently access, analyse and report on service data. A strong focus will be placed on continuous improvement and innovation, with the successful supplier expected to proactively identify opportunities to enhance services, improve user experience, strengthen resilience and deliver measurable business value. Lothian Pension Fund is particularly interested in suppliers that can provide scalable and adaptable services, bringing industry best practice and new ideas to support the organisation's evolving needs over the life of the contract.
