sig_8a2ff45572d92c9c256c.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject matter of the market dialogue is the expert services in information security and data protection under preparation as well as the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security for the needs of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Väylävirasto is putting out to tender the following two expert service procurements: Expert services in information security and data protection This tender procures experts to support the safeguarding and development of information and cyber security, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto has several different administrative or technical projects and undertakings underway in which operations are developed and existing information systems are renewed or new ones are ordered. What all these projects and undertakings have in common is that they must implement information security and the fulfilment of central government information security requirements in a manner suitable for the organisation. The subject matter of the procurement is information and cybersecurity consulting and auditing services. The work takes place largely in a multi-supplier environment, but also as internal consulting for individual projects or undertakings. Information security audits are also carried out regularly in the supplier environment. In addition, an assessment is made of, among other things, the impact of information security instructions directed at central government on the projects and operations of Väylävirasto. In addition to the office environment, the subject matter of the procurement is the infrastructures managed by Väylävirasto (Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency), i.e. state-owned road, rail and waterways. Each transport mode has its own cyber security development needs, which in certain respects may differ significantly from each other. The aim of the procurement is to obtain a partner for Väylävirasto with which the organisation's and the various transport modes' information and cybersecurity development can be carried out. Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security This tender procures conformity assessment body services to support the safeguarding of the information and cybersecurity, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Within the scope of this contract, conformity assessment bodies will produce assessment services in the role of an information security conformity assessment body approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom). When offering and producing assessment services, the information security conformity assessment bodies must comply with the current legislation, official regulations, recommendations, guidelines and other obligations directed at conformity assessment bodies by the authorities concerning conformity assessment body activities. Particular attention must be paid to the instruction issued to conformity assessment bodies by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency for information security conformity assessment bodies 210/2016 O. During the course of the dialogue, the contracting entity will separately assess the need for a market dialogue regarding the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security. The following dynamic purchasing systems (DPS) of Hansel Oy will be used as the procurement procedure for both tenders: Expert services in cyber security and data protection 2025 Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security 2021–2028 Hansel Oy's dynamic purchasing systems are open to all, and all companies meeting the suitability requirements may join them. Those interested in participating in the tenders are therefore requested to join the dynamic purchasing systems. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting entity's target schedule for carrying out the market dialogue and the procurement is: - Market dialogue 12/2025-1/2026 - Publication of the invitation to tender 1/2026 - Calculation period 1-2/2026 - Comparison of tenders 2/2026 - Procurement decision and continuation 2-3/2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to conduct a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to conduct a general-level dialogue on the subject matter of the procurement and its definition. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in any potential competitive tendering. The technical dialogue is organised through commenting on draft versions of the invitation to tender material and answering the contracting entity's questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. The preliminary date for submitting the draft versions of the invitation to tender material and questions is 12.12.2025. The contracting entity reserves suppliers approximately two weeks for commenting. Instructions for registration: The supplier must declare its interest in participating in the market dialogue by 10.12.2025 at 12.00 at the latest by sending a message to the addresses paul.kinnunen@vayla.fi, pirita.tuikka@vayla.fi and aino.mannikko@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Tietoturvan hankinnat- markkinavuoropuhelu" (Information security procurements - market dialogue). The supplier is requested to state in the message to which email addresses the market dialogue material will be delivered. The supplier is requested to state the following information in the message: - email address of the supplier's contact person. The contracting entity reserves the right to also invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another separately notified manner, which will be notified of later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the procurement notice, as well as the draft materials of the dialogue to be delivered later, are preliminary and indicative prior procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for answering or participating.

sig_8a4dcbb909e4cbf9f9a2.description: The NHSBSA invites you to participate in an Pre Market Engagement exercise through this Request for Information (RFI) for the provision of a File Tracking and Scanner Procurement. The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) is seeking market insight to support the potential procurement of a modern File Tracking Solution that enhances visibility, accuracy, and operational control across key environments. This Request for Information (RFI) aims to understand the range of capabilities, technologies, and approaches available in the market for file tracking. The NHSBSA currently has a contract in place for a File Tracking and Scanner Management Information (MI) software solution. This contract began in March 2020 and runs until September 2026. The current solution is used at two NHSBSA sites located at Greenfinch Way (NE15 8NX) and Bridge House (NE1 6SN) and supports 42 users in total, 29 based at Greenfinch Way and 13 based at Bridge House. The solution supports NHSBSA’s scanning operations, which process approximately 1 billion prescriptions, medical exemption applications, and dental claims each year. These activities are critical to managing confidential records securely and efficiently across multiple sites. The system enables tracking of files from receipt through scanning, storage, and eventual destruction, while providing performance statistics and management information. As part of our forward planning and market engagement under PA23 regulations, NHSBSA is seeking to understand current market capabilities and innovations that could inform future procurement decisions when the existing contract approaches its end. The NHSBSA is particularly interested in suppliers’ solutions for tagging, tracking methodologies, automation features, and security standards that could support the operational needs of the Greenfinch Warehouse and opportunities to improve traceability, efficiency, and overall assurance. Supplier’s feedback will help NHSBSA refine its understanding of available solutions and determine the most suitable direction for any future procurement activity. Overview of Requirements: The proposed solution must align with the Authority’s operational objectives by delivering a reliable, accurate, and high performance file tracking capability that supports secure and efficient handling of physical files across NHSBSA sites. The new solution must offer end to end visibility of file movements, real time status updates, and secure audit trails to ensure full traceability throughout the file lifecycle. To maintain continuity of service within the NHSBSA Warehouse and other operational areas, suppliers must provide a solution that is fully operational, resilient, and capable of supporting consistent, high volume activity without disruption. The system should minimise manual intervention, reduce the risk of misfiled or unaccounted for items, and enable staff to locate, track, and process materials quickly and confidently. The solution must be intuitive and user friendly, enabling staff to perform routine tasks, such as scanning, updating locations, allocating files, and verifying records with minimal training. Reliability, accuracy, and real time performance are essential to ensure business continuity across critical NHSBSA services reliant on timely and precise file movement and tracking. The NHSBSA has a requirement for tracking software to manage the receipt, storage and movement of departmental records, patient records and miscellaneous equipment. The software must be able to manage records at any level in the following hierarchy: site level, departmental locations level, box level and file level. It must also log a history of movements of each item, have the ability to manage records by pre-determined retention periods and allow operators to produce MI reports. A brief list of requirements are shown below, with more detailed requirements included at Appendix 1 (High-Level Requirements). High level requirements: • Track records at file, box, location and site level. • Data for records to include the following attributes at a minimum: • Client name • Department name • Date relating to the records ‘Birth Date’ • Date the record was registered with the tracker • Record type • Record ID number (for file level records) • Box ID Number (for box level records) • Description of record • Destruction date of record • Ability to flag record for extended retention period • Additional data – system needs to be flexible to accommodate data requirements for different record types and different clients • Ability to run simple reports for operators to confirm the accuracy of their inputs • Ability to load file data from imported spreadsheets • Ability to add a file using the barcode scanner if an extra file needs to be added to a box • Ability to amend any record detail via another device e.g. desktop/laptop • Maintain a full movement history for each record. • Provide reporting and MI capabilities, including destruction schedules and audit trails. • Ability to establish Users and Superusers that have different access rights • Ability to set up new users The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) is publishing this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice under Section 17 of the Procurement Act 2023, which sets out the requirement to publish a notice where preliminary market engagement has taken place or is planned. This engagement is being carried out in line with Section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023, which permits contracting authorities to engage with the market for purposes such as understanding supplier capability, shaping the requirement, and supporting the design of the procurement approach. In conducting this engagement, we will meet our overarching duties under the Act. This includes acting in a way that supports the procurement objectives, ensuring non‐discrimination between suppliers, and managing any actual or potential conflicts of interest. These duties apply to all preliminary market engagement activities and underpin how information is shared with suppliers to avoid any unfair advantage. Interested parties must access the RFI documents via https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome (search opportunities using system reference C419390 Lot 1: .

sig_8a5603f56dd5dd66eaa0.description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) currently operates and maintains a national GSM-R mobile network which provides driver to CTC communications via on-board GSM-R cab-mobile equipment provided by Siemens Mobility. Currently, GSM-R is in operation on the DART network, with national rollout expected to occur in 2026 on the rest of IE’s fleets. As part of the overall maintenance of the GSM-R mobile network, IÉ carry out monitoring and drive- testing which at present requires IÉ Telecoms personnel to perform this task. The task requires staff to travel onboard IÉ Trainsets with monitoring equipment, which can be both onerous and time consuming. IÉ require the provision of an automated drive-testing and RF monitoring solution that will negate the requirement for staff to travel. To achieve this requirement, it is therefore required to provide a GSM-R Modem and hardware (option)/software/firmware capable of interfacing with the modem and providing the end-user (IE) with a HTTP REST API. This can be integrated with the existing IÉ hosted servers which run a combination of NodeJS applications, InfluxDB and Grafana for recording and visualization of the obtained data or hosted on a supplier provided cloud-based solution that is accessible by IÉ. Further specific details will be provided to the companies who are pre-qualified to the ITT stage.
sig_8a5603f56dd5dd66eaa0.title: 9719 IM GSM-R Call Monitoring Solution

sig_8a795a1e6d040d09c483.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the supply of a computational server with GPU accelerators for artificial intelligence applications - 1 unit. 2. The server (hereinafter - Device) is intended for local (on-premise) running, fine-tuning and inference of generative artificial intelligence models, in particular generative models for image and video creation (text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video). The Device will be used for the simultaneous loading of models with significant GPU memory demand (models requiring at least 80 GB VRAM) as well as for processing training data and storing model checkpoints. 3. The detailed description of the subject of the contract, description of the Contracting Authority's requirements regarding execution and acceptance are specified by: 1) description of the subject of the contract (hereinafter "OPZ") – app. no. 1 to the SWZ, 2) drafted contract provisions (hereinafter "PPU") – app. no. 2 to the SWZ. 4. All requirements specified in the documents indicated above constitute minimum requirements, and their fulfilment is mandatory. 5. The Contracting Authority requires that: 1) the server and all computer subassemblies forming it are brand new, unused, technically sound, safe, complete, ready for operation; 2) the server is covered by its manufacturer's support from the date of signing the final protocol of execution of the contract for the implementation of the subject of the contract, at least until the expiry date of the granted warranty for the entire subject of the contract. By manufacturer support, the Contracting Authority understands services provided by the server manufacturer or an entity authorised by it, within which the Contracting Authority, throughout the entire period of its validity, will be able to download and install free of charge all security patches (fixes), as well as software updates (including firmware); 3) the supplied server is equipped with complete cabling provided by the manufacturer to ensure its correct operation; 4) the server was manufactured no earlier than 6 months before the delivery date and was not previously assigned to any user; 5) the server came from the official, authorised distribution channel of the manufacturer within the EU and was delivered in original, undamaged manufacturer packaging. 6. Regarding the ICT security of the supplied server, the Contractor is obliged to execute the subject of the contract in a manner ensuring the security, interoperability and manageability of the server in the Contracting Authority's ICT environment. The installation of the server in a rack cabinet, its connection to the Contracting Authority's network and operational commissioning are carried out independently by the Contracting Authority (cf. section III.5 point 5). The Contractor is obliged to cooperate with the Contracting Authority's representatives responsible for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity to the extent necessary to carry out the server acceptance. The Contractor's detailed obligations in this regard and sanctions for their breach are specified in §3 of the PPU. 7. WARRANTY: 1) the Contracting Authority requires that the subject of the contract – the server, is covered by a manufacturer's quality warranty together with service support provided by the manufacturer or a service partner authorised by the manufacturer carried out within the territory of the Republic of Poland, for a period not shorter than specified in the OPZ (minimum 36 months from the date of signing the Final Acceptance Protocol), 2) the manufacturer's warranty referred to in point 1 will be executed with a Next Business Day service response time, in an on-site standard and with the service of leaving damaged data media with the Contracting Authority (Keep Your Drive or equivalent), 3) detailed conditions regarding the warranty have been specified in the drafted contract provisions (§6 of the PPU). 4) if the standard manufacturer warranty period starts running before the date of final acceptance, the Contractor shall at its own expense ensure its appropriate extension or activation so that the Contracting Authority holds the full 36 months of warranty from the date of signing the Final Acceptance Protocol, 8. The Contracting Authority requires that the subject of the contract and the manner of its execution comply with the "do no significant harm" (DNSH) principle, understood as the necessity to execute the contract in a manner that does not violate environmental objectives and minimises negative environmental impact throughout the entire delivery execution cycle. 9. The Contracting Authority does not permit the participation in the procedure of Contractors conducting business activity and having their registered office or place of residence in third countries not belonging to European Union member states nor to states that are parties to the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement or other international agreements guaranteeing mutual and equal access to the public procurement market. The ban also covers jointly applying for the award of the contract with such Contractors, entrusting the execution of part of the contract to subcontractors from those countries and further subcontracting to them. 10. The Contracting Authority informs that it does not exercise the entitlement referred to in art. 16b paragraph 2 of the Public Procurement Law Act, consisting in specifying less favourable contract conditions for supplies or services originating from third countries that are not parties to international agreements referred to in paragraph 9. 11. The Contracting Authority points out that the entitlement provided for in this SWZ to use certificates issued on the basis of the Certification Act is vested "exclusively in the contractor who conducts business activity and has a registered office or place of residence in the territory of the European Union or a state that is a party to the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement or parties to other international agreements guaranteeing on the basis of reciprocity and equality access to the public procurement market to which the European Union is a party".

sig_8a8454d4020b9c52118d.description: "Extension of the spectator team sport support system licence, as well as its functional extension adapted to the operation of the Ministry of Defence State Secretariat for Sport and the National Institute for Sport Development and Methodology" Detailed in the technical description The National Institute for Sport Development and Methodology (hereinafter: Sport Institute), as a budgetary body operating under the direction of Honvédelmi Minisztérium, plays a central role in the professional-methodological coordination of sports subsidies, as well as in the conduct of subsidy management procedures. The Sport Institute and the Honvédelmi Minisztérium State Secretariat for Sport, the Ministry of Defence Sport Budgetary Department and the Ministry of Defence Legal Department currently use predominantly paper-based administrative processes, which impose a significant administrative burden on both the sports sector actors applying for subsidies and the implementing organisations, and hinder transparency and traceability. The purpose of this public procurement procedure is the long-term provision, maintenance of operation and specified functional expansion of an IT solution consisting of multiple components and licence types. The subject of the procurement is primarily the extension of the usage right (licence) of the already existing system supporting the administrative management of spectator team sport subsidies, as well as the procurement of related extended (independently valid) perpetual licences for the subsidy management, contract management and accounting processes managed by the Honvédelmi Minisztérium State Secretariat for Sport (HM SFÁT) and the Sport Institute that have not been digitised until now. The system is functional and proven to be suitable for conducting subsidy procedures; this procurement does not involve the creation of a new software system, but the functional extension and customisation of the existing solution for the specific, previously not digitally supported processes of the Sport Institute and the HM SFÁT. The use of the extended functions is also tied to a licence-based authorisation. It is important to highlight that licensing is not based on the number of registered users, but on the number of simultaneously active users. This construction allows for wide-ranging access while ensuring a sustainable cost structure and can be flexibly adapted to user needs. As part of the procurement, a comprehensive decision support and reporting module will also be developed, which, through state-of-the-art technological solutions, will support sports sector management and control processes by providing structured, searchable and statistically processable data. The goal of the development is to create a system component with an independent reporting database that is capable of handling its own data collection logic in addition to using existing data. As part of the procurement, an accounting subsystem will be created that, in the case of passed-on subsidies, allows the supporting organisation responsible for managing the subsidies to import the cost statements provided by the affected sports organisations for the sports federations, as well as for authorised Sport Institute users. This function ensures the electronic inclusion and uploading of accounting data and related accounting documents. The system is capable of checking that an accounting document can only be used up to the amount of the specified framework limit. The goal of the entire subsidy system is the digitisation of the entirety of administrative processes: from the electronic submission of applications through professional and financial assessment to approval and accounting. Digital operation places communication between the Sport Institute, the HM SFÁT and the sports federations on a unified platform, significantly reduces administrative burdens, and increases transparency and traceability. The solution aligns with the objectives of the National Digitalisation Strategy and contributes in the long term to the more efficient, transparent and controlled operation of sports subsidies. As a result of the procurement, the Ordering Party acquires a time-limited but territorially unlimited, non-transferable, exclusive right of use according to the conditions defined in the procurement documentation for the intended use of all components of the system. sig_8ac6330df96fb77b1788.description: The subject of contracts awarded within the dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter referred to as the "dynamic purchasing system" or simply "DPS") will be the purchase of hardware and hardware product support and the purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. The aim of establishing the DPS is to create a platform for awarding contracts within the DPS in order to enable the contracting authority to award contracts flexibly in accordance with the Public Procurement Act according to its actual needs, i.e., at a time and in a scope known to it. The dynamic purchasing system will be divided into two categories: 1) Purchase of hardware and hardware product support 2) Purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. Website relaunch for Justus Liebig University Giessen. External support is being tendered in two lots. • Lot 1: Usability and interaction design • Lot 2: Technical implementation (Block A), hosting and operation (Block B) JLU is planning a relaunch of its website and has launched a project for this purpose. Within the scope of this tender, external support is to be commissioned for the technical implementation and user experience (UX) areas. These two areas are being tendered as separate lots. Within the project, content (editorial concept and content) forms the third area. This is covered by the JLU project team. A duration of four years is planned for the relaunch project. The tender is conducted in two lots: • Lot 1: Usability and interaction design • Lot 2: Technical implementation (Block A), hosting and operation (Block B) Lot 1: Usability and interaction design Development of corporate design (web) • Based on the already existing corporate design concept and the available assets and artefacts • Based on layout proposals approved by JLU committees during presentations (pitch, holding JLU-internal workshops, etc. - in German in each case: language level C2 - CEFR) Elaboration of web style guides • Definition of colours, typography, image style, icons and other visual elements in consultation with the client. • Creation of a comprehensive style guide for the website. • Appendix 3 of this specification ("Corporate Design - Style Guide for Print Products") is referred to for orientation. Creation of wireframes and prototypes • Development of low-fidelity wireframes for structuring the pages. • Creation of interactive prototypes for visualising user flow and interactions. Design of page templates, building blocks, etc. Page types • Home page, • various overview page types (including for the overall university, departments, institutes, centres, departments, administrative units, degree programmes and research projects) • Content pages (also with dynamic content integration) • Date displays • News elements • Person pages • Landing page • Forms • Image galleries, optionally with download function • Error message pages • and other page types Development takes place jointly with the client within the framework of internal workshops in German corresponding to CEFR language level C2). Central design elements • Header and footer: Design of the upper and lower areas of the pages. • Navigation: Design of the main and sub-navigation in close coordination with a content concept to be drawn up by JLU. • Call-to-actions (CTAs): Creation of eye-catching and effective CTAs. • Content areas: Design of the main content areas of the pages o Flexible text-media combinations o Flexible display of media o Teaser elements o Structured and clear presentation of larger (text) content • Design of a presentation format for complex data and structures in the form of charts or diagrams (e.g. as an alternative to tables), with accessibility to be given special consideration as an overarching design aspect. Responsiveness (under the aspect of "Mobile First") Breakpoints • Definition of breakpoints for different screen sizes (for example desktop, tablet, mobile). Adaptive layouts • Creation of adaptive layouts that adapt to the different screen sizes. Touch-friendly elements • Adaptation of interactive elements for use on touchscreen devices. Interaction design Development of UX design aligned with the requirements of the university's diverse target groups. The focus here is on prospective students as well as higher education and research policy stakeholders, particularly in connection with the "Excellence Strategy of the Federal and State Governments". User flow and paths (user journey and navigation) • Content structure of the navigation and page structure (uniformity and consideration of the user perspective). • Definition of user flows and paths through the application. Development of target-group-appropriate interaction models based on concept templates from JLU Giessen • Design and modelling of access routes (among other things) using personas. Interactive elements • Design of interactive elements such as buttons, dropdowns, modals etc. Animations and transitions • Creation of animations and transitions to improve the user experience Handover to the technology agency (contractor for Lot 2) Documentation of design decisions • Creation of comprehensive documentation of design decisions and rationales. Kick-off meeting • Holding a kick-off meeting with the technology agency (Lot 2) for the handover of designs and specifications under the management of JLU. Continuous support • Provision of support and clarification of open questions during technical implementation. • Coordination and cooperation with JLU and the technology agency (Lot 2) as part of the agile project procedure. Project management Project planning • Agreement between the contractor and the client on a joint project procedure incorporating agile methods • Joint creation of an agile project plan in the form of an initial product backlog with the associated planning parameters (for example sprints, milestones and deadlines) Communication and reporting • Holding workshops at JLU for the participatory development of design and layout. • Regular communication with stakeholders and reporting on project progress. Quality management • Ensuring the quality of the delivered designs through reviews and tests by JLU Accessibility and data-protection-compliant operation Requirements for the project team For the implementation of the web relaunch project, the client expects an experienced and interdisciplinary project team.

Proofs must be submitted. A detailed description can be found in the specification.; JLU is planning a relaunch of its website and has launched a project for this purpose. Within the scope of this tender, external support is to be commissioned for the technical implementation and user experience (UX) areas. These two areas are being tendered as separate lots. Within the project, content (editorial concept and content) forms the third area. This is covered by the JLU project team. A duration of four years is planned for the relaunch project. The tender is conducted in two lots. Lot 2 - Block A: Technical implementation - Implementation of corporate design (web) - Implementation of the Plone theme in accordance with the design agency's draft (Lot 1), development of content types for central overview pages, development of templates for content maintenance by web editors, implementation of the central navigation concept, development/adaptation of a mechanism for web forms - Special core features - Automated data integration from third-party systems, development of automated displays, social media integration - Authentication and access control - Role and rights management, implementation of JLU's web user concept, implementation of the delegation of administration rights - Multilingualism: Bilingual structure, automatic translation function - Search engine optimisation (SEO) / Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) - Implementation of technical SEO and GEO measures, on-page optimisation for non-editorial/static page elements and structures, monitoring and continuous optimisation - Search and search optimisation - Web statistics and analysis - Adaptations to the Plone standard - Partial migration of selected content - Mechanism for retaining URLs in hybrid operation - Documentation - Project management Technical implementation - Project planning (agency side), communication and reporting, quality management Lot 2 - Block B: Hosting and operation - Server infrastructure and cluster setup - Operating tasks and maintenance - Continuous release planning and staging processes - Service level agreements (SLA) - IT security - Basic protection according to BSI, operational security processes - Accessibility and data-protection-compliant operation Requirements for the project team For the implementation of the web relaunch project, the client expects an experienced and interdisciplinary project team. Proofs must be submitted. A detailed description can be found in the specification.

All technical inquiries and correspondence should be directed to Mr. Dempsey at james.a.dempsey.civ@us.navy.mil. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- (PLEASE SEE LATEST BAA ANNOUNCEMENT WITHIN, POSTED 02 APRIL 2020) This is a modification to the Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) N00024-19-R-4145 to extend the date for receipt of white papers and full proposals to 6 February 2033 and correct some administrative information. Any white papers that have already been submitted do not need to be resubmitted. Included in this modification to the BAA is revision to the Power Controls section to augment the desired technology interests. Included in this modification to the BAA is the identification of an electronic mail submission address for white papers. Included in this modification to the BAA is also a change to the identified Procuring Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. The NAVSEA Points of Contact (POC) are changed as follows: the Primary Point of Contact remains Mr. William Jee, Procuring Contracting Officer, william.j.jee.civ@us.navy.mil All other information contained in the prior announcements through Apr 02, 2020 remain unchanged. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- (PLEASE SEE LATEST BAA ANNOUNCEMENT WITHIN, POSTED 04 JUNE 2019) I. ADMINISTRATIVE INFORMATION This publication constitutes a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), as contemplated in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2). A formal Request for Proposals (RFP), solicitation, and/or additional information regarding this announcement will not be issued or further announced. This announcement will remain open for approximately one year from the date of publication or until extended or replaced by a successor BAA. Initial responses to this announcement must be in the form of White Papers. Proposals shall be requested only from those offerors selected as a result of the scientific review of the White Papers made in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein. White Papers may be submitted any time during this period. Awards may take the form of contracts, cooperative agreements, or other transactions agreements. The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) will not issue paper copies of this announcement. NAVSEA reserves the right to select for proposal submission all, some, or none from among the white papers submitted in response to this announcement. For those who are requested to submit proposals, NAVSEA reserves the right to award all, some, or none of the proposals received under this BAA. NAVSEA provides no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this BAA will not be returned. It is the policy of NAVSEA to treat all white papers and proposals as competition sensitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. White papers submitted under N00024-10-R-4215 that have not resulted in a request for a proposal are hereby considered closed-out and no further action will be taken on them. Unsuccessful offerors under N00024-10-R-4215 are encouraged to review this BAA for relevance and resubmit if the technology proposed meets the criteria below. Contract awards made under N00024-10-R-4215 and under this BAA will be announced following the announcement criteria set forth in the FAR. II. GENERAL INFORMATION 1. AGENCY NAME Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) 1333 Isaac Hull Ave SE Washington, DC 20376 2. RESEARCH OPPORTUNITY TITLE Research and Development of Naval Power and Energy Systems 3. RESPONSE DATE This announcement will remain open through the response date indicated or until extended or replaced by a successor BAA. White Papers may be submitted any time during this period. 4. RESEARCH OPPORTUNITY DESCRIPTION 4.1 SUMMARY NAVSEA, on behalf of the Electric Ships Office (PMS 460, organizationally a part of the Program Executive Office Ships) is interested in White Papers for long and short term Research and Development (R&D) projects that offer potential for advancement and improvements in current and future shipboard electric power and energy systems at the major component, subsystem and system level. The mission of PMS 460 is to develop and provide smaller, simpler, more affordable, and more capable ship power systems to the Navy by defining open architectures, developing common components, and focusing Navy, industry, and academia investments. PMS 460 will provide leadership of the developments identified as part of this BAA, will direct the transition of associated technologies developed by the Office of Naval Research (ONR), and will manage the technology portfolio represented by Program Element (PE) 0603573N (Advanced Surface Machinery Systems) for transition into existing and future Navy ships. 4.2 NAVAL POWER AND ENERGY SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT ROADMAP Naval power and energy systems are described in detail in the 2019 Naval Power and Energy Systems Technology Development Roadmap (NPES TDR). The NPES TDR focuses and aligns the power system investments for the Navy, Defense Department, industry and academia to guide future research and development investments to enable the Navy to leverage these investments to meet its future needs more affordably. Included in the NPES TDR are specific recommendations and opportunities for near, mid and long term investments, with a renewed focus on energy management. These opportunities range from an energy magazine to support advanced weapons and sensors to the development of an Integrated Power and Energy System (IPES). The NPES TDR aligns electric power system developments with war fighter needs and enables capability-based budgeting. The NPES TDR is responding to the emerging needs of the Navy, and while the plan is specific in its recommendations, it is inherently flexible enough to adapt to the changing requirements and threats that may influence the 30-year ship acquisition plan. The first section of the roadmap establishes why NPES are a critical part of the kill chain based on the capabilities desired by the Navy in the near term, as well as supporting future platforms in the Navys 30-year shipbuilding plan. The second section of the roadmap presents power and energy requirements that are derived from mission systems necessary to support future warfighting needs. The third section describes required initiatives based on capabilities and the projected electrical requirements of the future ships. 4.3 FOCUS AREAS The areas of focus for this BAA include, but are not limited to, the "FYDP/NEAR-TERM" activities as described throughout the NPES TDR; the analysis, development, risk reduction and demonstration of future shipboard (both manned and unmanned) electric power systems and components, emphasizing shipboard power generation, electric propulsion, power conversion, energy storage, distribution and control; power quality, continuity, and system stability; electric power system and component level modeling and simulation; energy storage technologies; electrical system survivability; and power system simplicity, upgradeability, flexibility, and ruggedness. The Integrated Power and Energy System (IPES) architecture provides the framework for partitioning the equipment and software into modules and defines functional elements and the power/control and information relationships between them. For power generation, high power distribution, propulsion, and large loads, the architecture includes Medium Voltage AC power (with emphasis on affordability), and Medium Voltage DC power (with emphasis on power density and fault management). For ship service electrical loads, the architecture includes zonal electrical distribution which may be either AC or DC, depending upon the specific application. Also of particular interest are technologies that result in significant energy efficiency, power density improvements and/or carbon footprint improvements over existing propulsion and power system technologies. The NPES TDR partitions the power system in to functional areas that include the following. 4.3.1 ENERGY STORAGE Energy storage modules may support short duration to long duration energy storage applications, which utilize a combination of technologies to minimize power quality and continuity impacts across the system. For the short duration energy storage applications, the module should provide hold-up power to uninterruptible loads for fault clearing and transient isolation, as well as load leveling for pulse power loads. For the mid duration, the module should provide up to approximately 3MW (100 - 150 kW-hr) of standby power for pulse power loads while also providing continuity of operations for a subset of equipment between uninterruptible and full ships load (including emergency power generation starting in a dark ship condition). For long duration applications, energy storage modules should provide the required power as an emergency backup system or to provide increased stealth for specialty equipment. The required duration for this type of application may extend up to days or longer, and may be intermittent or continuous. A number of energy storage technologies for future ship applications are of interest to the Navy, including various electrochemical, capacitor-based, or rotating discussed below: a. Capacitor: Electrochemical capacitor improvements continue to focus on improving energy density while maintaining inherently high-power density. Design improvements include development and integration of higher temperature films, advanced electrolytes, advanced electrode materials, and minimizing equivalent series resistance (ESR). b. Rotating: The Navy has interest in the investment from the transportation industry in flywheel systems that can handle gyroscopic forces continues to support flywheel usage in commercial rail and ground transportation. Additional factors of interest to the Navy include safety, recharge/discharge rates, ship motion impacts, environmental impacts and control. c. Electrochemical: Factors of interest to the Navy with respect to electrochemical energy storage include the ability to maintain state of charge when not in use; change in voltage versus state of charge; charge and discharge capability; the temporary or permanent loss of capacity due to repeated shallow discharges; the ability to shallow charge and discharge or partially charge intermittently during a discharge; battery life considerations such as service-life, cycle life, and shelf-life; off-gas properties that affect the level of ventilation and associated auxiliary systems; and safety enhancements to support qualification for use onboard US Navy ships. Near term Navy interests are in the area of common and scalable hardware and software elements which enable advanced weapons and sensors and in understanding the sizing algorithms for how to optimize energy storage sizing against various competing system requirements (short duration/high power vs. long duration/low power, for example. The specific design issues to be considered include reliability, volumetric and gravimetric power and energy densities, differentiating between high levels of stored energy and high energy density. The relevant information required for characterizing technology performance include: Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of components and systems; production capability; safety evaluation and qualifications performed on relevant subsystems or components (any hazard analyses of systems designs as relevant to notional applications); other military application of the devices; energy storage management system approach; thermal characteristics, constraints, and cooling requirements; auxiliary requirements (load); device impedance (heat generation characteristics); and device efficiency (discharge/recharge). 4.3.2 POWER CONVERSION Industry continues to drive towards increased power density, increased efficiency, higher switching frequencies, and refined topologies with associated control schemes. Innovation in power conversion from the development and implementation of wide-bandgap devices, such as Silicon Carbide (SiC), promise reduction in losses many times over Silicon. The use of high frequency transformers can provide galvanic isolation with reduced size and weight compared to traditional transformers. Advances in cooling methods will be required to handle larger heat loads associated with higher power operation. A typical Navy power conversion module might consist of a solid state power converter and/or a transformer. Advanced topologies and technologies, such as the application of wide band gap devices, are of particular interest. Navy interests are in the area of innovative approaches to address converting high voltage AC/DC to 1000 VDC with power levels on the order of 3MW or larger. The specific design issues to be considered include modularity, open architecture (focusing on future power system flexibility and the ability of a conversion module within a ships power system to be replaced/ upgraded in support of lifecycle mission system upgrades), reliability, cost, and conversion efficiency. Areas of interest include more power-dense converters supporting advanced mission systems and prototyping of full scale conversion based on second generation wide-bandgap devices. 4.3.3 POWER DISTRIBUTION Power distribution typically consists of bus duct/ bus pipe, cables, connections, switchgear and fault protection equipment, load centers, and other hardware necessary to deliver power from generators to loads. Industry has used medium voltage DC (MVDC) transmission as a method to reduce losses across long distances. Complementarily, Industry is developing MVDC circuit protection for use in MVDC transmission variants of approximately 50, 100, and 150 megawatts (MW) at transmission voltages of 20 to 50 kVDC. Analysis includes modeling and simulation to determine methods for assessing the benefits of DC vs AC undersea transmission and distribution systems for offshore oil and gas. Industry and academia continue to invest resources in advanced conductors that have applications in power distribution, power generation, and propulsion. Research is focused on using carbon nanotubes. The development of a room temperature, lightweight, low resistance conductor is of great interest to the Navy. Areas of interest include development of an MVDC distribution system up to 12 kVDC to meet maximum load demands; design of an appropriate in-zone distribution system architecture; development of high speed 1 kVDC and 12 kVDC solid state circuit protection devices that are ship ready, and advanced conductors capable of supporting power distribution. 4.3.4 PRIME MOVERS (INCLUDING POWER GENERATION) Power Generation converts fuel into electrical power. A typical power generation module might consist of a gas turbine or diesel engine (prime mover), a generator (see rotating machine discussion below), a rectifier (either active or passive), auxiliary support sub-modules and module controls. Other possible power generation technologies include propulsion derived ship service (PDSS), fuel cells, or other direct energy conversion concepts. Power generation concepts include 60 Hz wound rotor synchronous generator driven directly by a marine gas turbine (up to 30 MVA rating); commercially derived or militarized design variants of the above; and higher speed, higher frequency, high power density variants of the above with high speed or geared turbine drive. NPES DC technologies permit prime movers and other electrical sources (such as energy storage) to operate at different, non-60Hz electrical frequency speeds, improving survivability, resiliency, and operational availability. Energy storage that is fully integrated with the power generation can enable uninterrupted power to high priority loads, mission systems that reduce susceptibility, and damage control systems to enable enhanced recoverability. The specific design issues to be considered include fuel efficiency, module level power density, machine insulation system characteristics, size, weight, cost, maintainability, availability, harmonic loading, voltage, power, system grounding approaches, fault protection, response to large dynamic (step) or pulse type loading originated from ship propulsion or directed energy/electromagnetic weapons, interface to main or ship service bus, autonomy, limited maintenance, and commercial availability. Navy interests are in the area of innovative approaches to power generation in the 5 to 30 MW range, utilizing gas turbines, diesel engines and other emerging power technologies that address challenges associated with achieving reduced fuel consumption, decreased life cycle and acquisition cost, support of ship integration, enable flexibility, enable power upgrades, and improved environmental compliance. Near term Navy interest includes 10-30 MW (nominally 25 MW) output power rating and the power generation source able to supply two independent electrical buses (where abnormal conditions, including pulsed/stochastic loads, on one bus do not impact the other bus) at 12 kVDC (while also considering 6kVDC, 18kVDC, and 1 kVDC). Enhanced fuel injection, higher operating temperatures and pressures, and optimized thermal management are critical for future prime movers. Advanced controls for increased efficiency, reduced maintenance, and increased reliability include implementation of digital controls; autonomous and unmanned power control; enhanced engine monitoring, diagnostics, and prognostics; and distributed controls. Advanced designs for increased efficiency include new applications of thermodynamic cycles such as Humphrey/Atkinson cycle for gas turbines and diesels and Miller cycle for diesel. The Navy is interested in developing a knowledge bank of information on potential generator sets, generator electrical interface requirements, and the impacts of those requirements on generator set performance and size, as a logical next step from the Request for Information released under announcement N00024-16-R-4205. A long-term goal for this effort is to maximize military effectiveness through design choice and configuration option flexibility when developing next-generation distribution plants. The power generation source should fit within the length of a typical engine room (46 feet, including allowances for any needed maintenance and component removal). The power generation source is expected to have the ability to: control steady-state voltage-current characteristic for its interface; to maintain stability; and to adjust control set-points from system level controllers. For any proposed design approach, initial efforts would include conceptual design trade studies that inform the performance level that can be achieved. Trade studies may address Pulsed Load Capability (generator/rectifier design to increase pulse load capability, engine speed variation limits, and impact of cyclic pulse load on component life); Power Density (cost vs. benefits of high speed or high frequency, mounting on common skid, and advanced cooling concepts); Single vs. Dual Outputs (continuous vs. pulse rating for each output, voltage regulation with shared field, and control of load sharing); Efficiency (part load vs. full load optimization, flexible speed regulation, impact of intake and exhaust duct size/pressure drop on engine efficiency); Power Quality (voltage transient, voltage modulation for step, pulse loads, impact of voltage and current ripple requirements, and common mode current); PGM Controls (prime mover speed vs. generator field vs. rectifier active phase angle control, and pulse anticipation); Stability when operating in parallel with other sources; Short Circuit Requirements; and Dark Ship start capability (self-contained support auxiliaries). Trade studies may also address how rotational energy storage can be built into the design of the generator or added to the generator and what parameters need to be defined in order to exploit this capability. Development of advanced coatings and materials that support high temperature operations of a gas turbine is also of interest. Energy harvesting to convert heat energy and specifically low quality heat energy to electricity using solid state components is also of interest to the Navy. 4.3.5 ROTATING MACHINES (INCLUDING GENERATORS AND PROPULSION MOTORS) Recent trends in electrical machines include neural networks; artificial intelligence; expert system; fiber communications and integrated electronics; new ceramic conducting and dielectric materials; and magnetic levitation. High Temperature Superconducting rotors have higher power density than their induction and synchronous rotor counterparts. Wind power generators eliminate excitation losses which can account for 30% of total generator losses. The offshore wind power industry is moving to larger power wind tower generators in the 10MW class. Advanced low resistance room temperature wire and HTS shows promise for these higher power levels because of low excitation losses and low weight due to reduction in stator and rotor iron. HTS motors may be up to 50% smaller and lighter than traditional iron-core and copper machines. They have reduced harmonic vibrations due to minimization of flux path iron and have mitigated thermal cycling failures due to precision control of temperature. Propulsion motor concepts of interest to the Navy include Permanent Magnet Motors (radial air gap, axial air gap, or transverse flux), Induction Motors (wound rotor or squirrel cage), superconducting field type (homopolar DC or synchronous AC). The drivers and issues associated with these designs include acoustic signature, noise (requirements, limitations, modeling, sources, and mitigation methods), shock, vibration, thermal management, manufacturing infrastructure, machine insulation system characteristics, commercial commonality, platform commonality, cost, torque, power, weight, diameter, length, voltage, motor configuration, and ship arrangements constraints. Motor drives that may be explored include cyclo-converter (with variations in control and power device types), pulse width modulated converter/inverter (with many variations in topology), switching (hard switched, soft switched), and matrix converter (with variations in control, topology, cooling, power device type). Technologies for drives and rotating machines which allow the ability to operate as a motor and a generator to facilitate a PDSS installation or on a fully integrated power system to leverage the inherent energy storage in the ship's motion may be explored. Integrated motor/propulsor concepts may be considered either as aft-mounted main propulsion or as a forward propulsor capable of propelling a ship at a tactically useful speed. Areas of interest for future rotating machines include increased magnetic material flux carrying or flux generation capacity; improved electrical insulation material and insulation system dielectric strength; increased mechanical strength, increased thermal conductivity, and reduced sensitivity to temperature; improved structural materials and design concepts that accept higher torsional and electromagnetically induced stress; innovative and aggressive cooling to allow improved thermal management and increased current loading; increased electrical conductor current carrying capacity and loss reduction. 4.3.6 COOLING AND THERMAL MANAGEMENT As the demand and complexity of high energy loads increases, so does the demand and complexity of thermal management solutions. Assessing and optimizing the effectiveness of a thermal management system requires the analysis of thermal energy acquisition, thermal energy transport, and thermal energy rejection, storage, and conversion. The design of the thermal management system aims to transfer the thermal energy loads at the sources to the sinks in the most efficient manner. Areas of interest to the Navy with respect to cooling and thermal management include the application of two phased cooling and other advanced cooling techniques to power electronics and other NPES components and innovative approaches to manage overall ship thermal management issues including advanced thermal architectures, thermal energy storage systems, increases in efficiency, and advanced control philosophies. 4.3.7 POWER CONTROLS Controls manage power and energy flow within the ship to ensure delivery to the right load in the right form at the right time. Supervisory power system control typically resides on an external distributed computer system and therefore does not include hardware elements unless specialized hardware is required. The challenge to implement Tactical Energy Management (TEM) is to integrate energy storage, power generation, and interfaces with advanced warfighting systems and controls. TEM is critical to enabling full utilization of the capabilities possible from technologies under development. The state complexity and combat engagement timelines for notional future warfighting scenarios are expected to exceed the cognitive capacity and response times of human operators to effectively manage the electric plant via existing control system schema in support of executing ship missions. The survivability requirements for military ships combined with the higher dynamic power characterisitics (pulse load) characteristics of some mission systems will require more sophisticated control interfaces, power management approaches, and algorithms than are commercially available. The Navy is pursuing a long term strategy to create a unified, cyber secure architecture for machinery control systems that feature a common, reusable, cyber hardened machinery control domain specific infrastructure elements; a mechanism for transitioning new technology from a variety of sources in an efficient and consistent manner; and a mechanism to provide life cycle updates and support in a cost effective and timely manner. TEM controls will be expected to maintain awareness of the electric plant operating state (real time modeling); interface with ship mission planning (external to the electric plant control systems) for energy resource prioritization, planning, and coordination towards the identification of resource allocation states that dynamically optimize mission effectiveness; identify and select optimal trajectories to achieving those optimal resource allocation states; and actuate the relevant electric plant components to move the electric plant state along those optimized trajectories towards the optimal resource allocation state. TEM controls would enable reduced power and energy system resource requirements for a given capability (or improved capability for a given set of resources); increased adaptability of the Navy’s power and energy system design to keep pace with an evolving threat environment; and maximized abilities to execute the ship’s mission. The Navy is interested in potential applications of distributed control architectures that have led to the development of intelligent agents that have some autonomous ability to reason about system state and enact appropriate control policies. A simple example of these agents in a control system is the use of autonomous software coupled with smart meters in a smart grid implementation. The agents, smart meters in this example, can temporarily shut off air conditioning but not the refrigerator in residences during grid peak power usage times when the cost per watt is highest on hot days. The agent software acts autonomously within its authority to comply with programmed customer desires. The Navy is interested in TEM controls within a modular open systems architecture framework such that they are agnostic of, but affordably customizable to, specific ship platforms and power system architectures. TEM controls may reside between (i.e. interface with) embedded layers within individual power system components, ships’ supervisory machinery control systems, and ships’ mission planning systems. Initial or further development or modification of these interfaces may be required to achieve desired performance behaviors and characteristics. TEM controls are expected to develop within a model-based system engineering and digital engineering environment and will be initially evaluated in a purely computational environment, representing Navy-developed shipboard-representative power and energy system architecture(s), but will be progressively evaluated on systems with increasing levels of physical instantiation (i.e., controller-hardware-in-loop and power-hardware-in-loop with progressive levels of representative power system components physically instantiated). When implementing a TEM based control scheme, the overall power system should increase installed power generation available to mission and auxiliary loads; reduce power system design margins; hone the installed stored energy required for mission critical capability; and allow higher power transients (ramp rates and step loads). Other areas of interest to the Navy with respect to controls include improvements to traditional machinery control and automation, advanced power management, cyber security, and advanced controls for distributed shared energy storage and maintaining electrical system stability. The Navy is also interested in non-intrusive load monitoring, power system data analytics, real time system monitoring and onboard analysis and diagnostics capabilities. 4.3.8 SYSTEM INTERPLAY, INTERFACING, AND INTEGRATION Increasingly, the Navy is recognizing the need for incorporating flexibility and adaptability into initial ship designs and recognizing that the integration of new systems and the ability to rapidly reconfigure them will be an ongoing challenge throughout a platform's life cycle in order to maintain warfighting relevancy. The ability to support advanced electrical payload warfighting technologies requires not only power and energy systems delivered with the flexibility and adaptability to accommodate them, but a NPES engineering enterprise with the capability and capacity (knowledge, labor, and capital) for continuous systems integration. The Navy can more affordably meet this challenge by shifting as much effort as possible into the computational modeling and simulation regime. An Integrated Power System (IPS) provides total ship electric power including electric propulsion, power conversion and distribution, energy storage, combat system support and ship mission load interfaces to the electric power system. Adding Energy Storage and advanced controls to IPS results in an Integrated Power and Energy System (IPES) in order to accommodate future high energy weapons and sensors. The IPES Energy Magazine is available to multiple users, and provides enhanced power continuity to the power distribution system. The flexibility of electric power transmission allows power generating modules with various power ratings to be connected to propulsion loads and ship service in any arrangement that supports the ships mission at the lowest total ownership cost (TOC). Systems engineering in IPS/IPES is focused on increasing the commonality of components used across ship types (both manned and unmanned) and in developing modules that will be integral to standardization, zonal system architectures, and generic shipbuilding strategies with standard interfaces that are Navy-controlled. Full-scale design and production of printed information material: The task of the winning Tenderer is the full-scale graphic design, copywriting, proofreading, prepress and production, as well as packaging and delivery of a business card-sized printed information material describing the necessity of the investment. The information material is prepared in relation to the 3 Project on 1-1 occasions, with 3 different contents, in printed form (3000 pieces/Project, i.e. a total of 9000 pieces). 2. Production and placement of "A2" information board The task of the winning Tenderer is the full-scale preparation, production and surface protection, transport and placement of a total of 10 pieces of "A2" type boards used for informing the public, to be placed at the main site of the investment. 3. Provision of media appearances related to the Projects The task of the winning Tenderer is to prepare a media plan related to the campaign, purchase media spaces, produce content corresponding to the purchased media space, and perform graphic design, copywriting, and, if necessary, prepress and production tasks for the appearances using the background material provided by the Client. The winning Tenderer is required to continuously monitor the appearances, optimise advertising settings during the process based on consultations with the Client, and prepare a post-buy analysis. The task of the winning Tenderer is to provide media appearances as follows: 3.1. Online appearance 3.1.1. Provision of priority PR article copywriting and appearance on the IT Business online homepage (a total of 24 PR articles, each with an appearance lasting 1 weeks) and the Magyar Nemzet online homepage (7 PR article with an appearance lasting 3 working days) Quantity (number of occasions) and number of creative material pieces: total 31 3.1.2. Provision of static banner appearance on the IT Business online site 18 times for a duration of 1 weeks. Quantity (number of occasions): total 18; Number of creative material pieces: total 10 Forwarding the ready-to-publish advertising materials, graphic elements, and print-ready files to the individual media, or submitting them to the manufacturers, is in all cases the task of the winning Tenderer. 4. Preparation of photo documentation suitable for communication purposes The task of the winning Tenderer is to prepare photo documentation suitable for communication purposes regarding the process of the implementation of the Projects, as well as to perform the necessary post-production work. (Presentation of project closing events on a total of 2 occasions, taking 50 photos per event) 5. Full-scale design and production of result communication publication The task of the winning Tenderer is the full-scale graphic design, copywriting, proofreading, prepress and production, as well as packaging and delivery of a result communication publication presenting the results of the investment. Upon completion of the Projects, it is prepared in relation to 2 Projects on 1-1 occasions, with 1-1 types of content, in printed and electronic editions (100-100 pieces). 6. Full-scale organisation of a press-public project closing event (2 times in connection with 2 Project) The task of the winning Tenderer is the full-scale organisation and execution of press-public project closing events (event organisation, event coordination, event venue, event technical equipment, professionals, contributors, props, related travel and transport tasks, permits, construction and dismantling tasks, technical supervision, etc.). Number of attendees at the event: 100 persons/occasion Venue of the event: Budapest Duration of the event: 180 minutes/occasion The task of the winning Tenderer: compiling the script, preparing the programme plan; providing and furnishing the venue; providing the necessary technical equipment and furniture; editing and graphic design of the invitation; inviting participants, compiling a press list; sending out press invitations electronically, collecting and sending press registration feedback to the Client; on-site coordination, ensuring on-site registration, maintaining the paper-based attendance sheet; providing a cloakroom; providing catering. The detailed technical description and conditions are contained in the procurement documents.; Planned tasks of the winning Tenderer: 1. Creative agency tasks 1.1. DIMOP_PLUSZ-1.1.1 brand design The task of the winning Tenderer is to design a unified brand identity expressing the goals of the Project 1, as well as the related DIMOP_PLUSZ-1.1.2 sub-project under one brand for the purpose of unified external and internal communication, and to produce the brand manual. DIMOP_PLUSZ-1.2.1. brand design The task of the winning Tenderer is to design a brand identity expressing the goals of the Project 2 for the purpose of unified external and internal communication, and to produce the brand manual.

DIMOP_PLUSZ – 3.1.1 Creative design: The winning Tenderer's task is to perform the following creative design tasks as planned, including image retouching and editing, as well as stock photos if necessary, and also copywriting: graphic design and print preparation for roll-ups; desk flag design; graphic design for E-newsletter. 2. PR agency tasks The winning Tenderer's task is to perform PR agency tasks, as planned: • preparation of a PR plan that covers the dissemination activities prescribed in the Projects, including the use of a unified brand for the DIMOP_PLUSZ Projects defined in the brand manual; • general press work: building and continuously operating press and media relations to ensure continuous "generated" PR appearances; creating and continuously updating press lists; press monitoring, handling press enquiries, performing PR tasks for press events and press conferences (handling and organising interviews, involving an external expert in the communication regarding Project 1 and Project 2, and a networking expert regarding Project 3); PR copywriting, participation in daily press communication; writing, sending and managing press releases, background materials and unique stories, etc. Producing PR articles arises as further tasks regarding all three affected projects. 3. Online agency tasks 3.1. sig_8b4bf10de5e76b471c05.description: South Lanarkshire Council seeks a Creative Consultancy to deliver a Market Assessment, Branding Strategy, Website Development, Content Library and Wayfinding Strategy for the Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism initiative within the Hagshaw Energy Cluster. 1. Market Assessment Review existing project documentation and identify implications for branding, marketing and website development. Analyse visitor data, market trends and audience segmentation, including visitor case studies. Benchmark comparable projects and destinations. Provide recommendations to inform branding, website design, content and future marketing activity. 2. Branding Development Develop and consult on three branding concepts before producing a final identity. Create brand assets including logo, name, tagline, colours, fonts and digital/print applications. Produce brand guidelines covering signage, interpretation, promotional materials and integration with existing site branding. Include recommendations for social media and future marketing activity. 3. Website Design, Build and Launch Create a branded website promoting Douglas Valley as a destination to live, work, visit and enjoy, supporting ambitions to attract up to 100,000 annual visits by 2036. Develop a scalable, content-led website with a planned lifespan of ten years. Include six core pages: Home, About, Explore, See & Stay, News and Contact. The Explore section will feature an interactive map highlighting key recreational and active travel routes, points of interest and route information including distance, elevation, difficulty and duration. Build the site on an accessible CMS suitable for community and council users. Host on a secure UK-based platform with maintenance and support arrangements. Ensure accessibility compliance and provide flexible management of route information and temporary diversions. 4. Photography and Video Library Establish a copyright-cleared library of photography and short-form video content for web, social media and print use. Source content through community engagement, youth-focused workshops and professional photography where required. Content will reflect identified visitor segments and feature strong people-focused imagery. Coverage will include renewable energy, local communities, nature, heritage and identity, local economy and outdoor recreation. Key locations include Coalburn, Douglas, Glenbuck, Glespin, Lesmahagow, Mainshill, Muirkirk, Poneil, Rigside, Douglas Water and Spireslack, alongside significant natural, heritage and recreation assets. 5. Wayfinding Strategy and Design Guidance Develop a first-phase wayfinding strategy focused on Coalburn, Douglas, Glespin, Douglasdale Community Woodland and connecting active travel routes. Establish a hierarchy of signage including gateway signs, orientation panels, interpretation boards, directional signage and waymarkers. Produce a spatial strategy identifying suitable signage locations. Develop design guidance covering dimensions, materials, specification, siting and future rollout. Prepare detailed proposals for priority installations to support future procurement. Work with Community Action Lanarkshire on implementation of information signs, directional signage and waymarkers along the NCN-Coalburn-Douglas route. Ensure all strategy, design and implementation follow inclusive design principles. Lot 1: . sig_8b6d7ddb9cd78170e9ea.description: The specialist departments of the Dietikon school currently work with a multitude of individual solutions and different software systems. This heterogeneous system landscape leads to media discontinuities, increased administrative effort, and complicates cooperation as well as data consistency. The goal is therefore to gradually replace the existing individual solutions with administrative software that is as integrated and future-proof as possible. A provider is being sought for the introduction and operation of suitable administrative software for the Dietikon school. The new administrative software will support the Dietikon school in the areas of school administration. Productivity in the cooperation between user groups is to be improved, communication simplified, and administration facilitated by the new administrative software representing an integrated overall solution in which all specialist departments work with the same current, consistent, and centrally maintained data. The new solution should enable central data storage, comply with legal requirements (particularly with regard to Digilex, data security, data protection, and archiving), and simplify administrative processes as well as make them more efficient.
sig_8b6d7ddb9cd78170e9ea.title: Procurement and operation of new administrative software for the Dietikon school

In the appendices we have added 2 documents containing more information regarding the intended procurement and actions that have been carried out in the past. This concerns a prior information notice. The exact scope of this assignment has not yet been determined. The Inspectorate of Education desires a long-term agreement of at least 4 years and thereafter 1 or 2 option years. The exact duration will be included in the future tender.

sig_8b8d31c7e923b239c899.description: The Totara platform (known within the Trust as YAS247) is a business-critical system that supports the Trust's learning, appraisal, compliance and workforce development activities. Think Learning is the Trust's incumbent supplier and, following its merger with Chambury Learning Solutions in late 2024, is now part of the Totara Group. The Trust has confirmed that it is fully satisfied with the supplier's performance and wishes to continue with the existing service. Lot 1: . The Trust requires the provision of its Totara Learn and Totara Perform Learning Management System (LMS), known within the Trust as YAS247, which is a business-critical platform supporting learning, appraisal, compliance and workforce development activities. A benchmarking exercise was undertaken through the G-Cloud 14 Framework, reviewing service offerings from six suppliers providing Totara services. The assessment considered service offering, capability, NHS experience and ability to meet the Trust’s functional requirements. Think Learning, the incumbent supplier and a Totara Platinum Partner, was identified as the Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), providing the most comprehensive solution aligned to the Trust’s requirements while maintaining continuity of the existing service. The contract will therefore be awarded to Think Learning via the CCS G-Cloud 14 Framework, providing a compliant route to market and avoiding the operational disruption, data migration, retraining and implementation risks associated with transitioning to an alternative supplier.
sig_8b8d31c7e923b239c899.title: Totara (Learn and Perform) Learning Management System
