sig_8b953cba88fa8a8ac203.description: ADVANCED RESEARCH ANNOUNCEMENT (ARA) FA9451-21-S-0001 Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research (DETER) Air Force Research Laboratory/Directed Energy Directorate NAICS Code: The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715 for Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees Federal Agency Name: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy, Phillips Research Site, Kirtland AFB NM (AFRL/RD) ARA Title: Directed Energy Technology Experimentation Research Announcement (DETER) ARA Type: This is an Open ARA with Calls; initial announcement ARA Number: FA9451-21-S-0001 Program Summary: This is an Open ARA announcement pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). AFRL/RD is interested in receiving white papers and proposals through a Two-Step Process to perform research and development (R&D), modeling and simulation (M&S), design, component/subsystem, prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of directed energy source components (to include spares and alternate component technologies), and/or systems and any required accessories, materials, and supplies for laboratory research and experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged. *Note: AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. *Please see the attached DETER Industry User Guide for guidance on definitions, processes, submission requirements and evaluation criteria.* Background: AFRL/RD equips the joint warfighter with next-generation technologies, advanced concepts, and weapon system options across all operational domains to become more agile and increase the commercialization potential of directed energy investments to ensure the National defense. This solicitation intends to use acquisition authorities provided by 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373). This authority applies to acquisition of items related to “...buy demonstrations, prototypes, products, supplies, parts, accessories, auxiliary services, and design for products or services, that the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary concerned considers necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense.” Consequently, white papers and proposals should address how the proposed effort provides benefits to the national defense and a strategy for verifying those intended benefits. The proposed solutions should be innovative and substantially improve national defense capabilities across the domains of directed energy. While the Government describes discrete topic areas below, it also anticipates that certain comprehensive technology solutions and prototypes may require multidiscipline approaches that address two or more topic areas. The topic areas are covered under this announcement, which may be used in any combination. The Government reserves the right to add, delete or modify the topic areas as necessary. Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged throughout the life of this ARA. However, communication will be limited once full-proposals are submitted for evaluation/review. Prospective Offerors are welcome to request sit-downs and provide demonstrations of their capabilities. Discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. No guidance related to technical approach will be given. However, questions related to the objectives of the effort or prior similar efforts may be answered. Offerors are advised that only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to contractually bind or otherwise commit the Government. THIS WILL BE A HYBRID ANNOUNCEMENT: This announcement has an open request for white papers as described below. Calls may be issued under this announcement for discrete requirements. Call types can vary and may include, but are not limited to, One-Step, Two-Step, Open, Closed, Staggered, Limited Calls or any combination therein. AFRL/RD reserves the right to collapse a white paper/Two-Step into a One-Step if the situation warrants the white paper contains sufficient technical detail to do full technical proposal evaluation instead of white paper evaluation. Open Announcement Request: AFRL/RD Kirtland Air Force Base is soliciting white papers on the research effort described in the below topic areas pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373), Procurement for Experimental Purposes. Open Announcement Submission: White papers must be submitted to https://usg.valideval.com/teams/DETER/signup. If it is determined that a classified white paper is required, please DO NOT DELIVER any classified portion of the white paper, but rather contact the DETER Org Mailbox for specific delivery instructions. Further instructions for white paper submission can be found in the DETER Industry User Guide attached to this announcement. Call Request: Calls, other than Limited Calls, will be issued under this announcement via the Government Point of Entry (GPE) at https://beta.sam.gov. Notification of Calls may be announced on other platforms (i.e. www.grants.gov) and will direct Offerors to the GPE for full solicitation details. Call Submission: Submission requirements for Calls will be specified in the solicitation documentation of each Call. Call Variations: Variations of the ARA Call process are available for use. The following types are commonly used, but are not considered all inclusive. One-Step: The one-step process is used to request full technical and cost proposals from each Offeror. The proposals are reviewed in accordance with the solicitation criteria and typically all of a selected proposal, part of a selected proposal, or none of the proposals may be selected for award. Two-Step: The two-step process is sometimes used when a large number of proposals are anticipated. Potential Offerors are invited to submit brief descriptive white papers in lieu of full proposals. The Call must state whether an unfavorable white paper review will bar the Offeror from further consideration. The Government may retain unselected white papers for a specific period of time, which will be identified in the solicitation. Full proposals are requested from those Offerors selected in the white paper review process. After proposals are received, they are reviewed consistent with the process for one-step ARAs. Open Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at any time within a specified period. Open calls will be updated no less frequently than annually. White papers/proposals are reviewed when received during the period that the ARA is open. Closed Call: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at a specified date and time as set forth in the ARA. Staggered-Closed Call: The staggered-closed Call states a specified date and time for receipt of proposals or white papers, but also allows for proposals/white papers after the date and time set for proposal receipt. All Offerors should be cautioned, however, that the likelihood of funding proposals received after the specified date and time is substantially reduced. Limited Call: This approach allows for solicitation to a limited group of potential offerors. Request for Proposals (RFP) or Requests for white papers will be issued directly to potential offerors without a requirement to publish to the GPE. The Government may issue solicitations that combine one or more of the above approaches. Open Announcement Modifications: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is subject to updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor https://beta.sam.gov to ensure they receive the latest guidance for this announcement. The Government shall provide updates to this announcement no less than annually. Updates may include changes to: topic areas, submission requirements, administrative changes, evaluation criteria, solicitation methods, etc. (not an inclusive list). Type of Contract/Instrument: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract/instrument type under the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10 U.S.C. §4021 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371) "Other Transaction for Research 10 U.S.C. §4022 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2371b) "Other Transaction for Prototype" 10 U.S.C. §4023 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2373) "Procurement for Experimental Purposes" 10 U.S.C. §4025 (formerly 10 U.S.C. §2374) "Prize Competitions" DoD Grant and Agreement Regulation (DoDGARS) The Government anticipates that a mix of contract/instrument types will be used throughout the life of this ARA. Generally, awards under this announcement or any Calls may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, Firm Fixed Price, Other Transaction Authority, etc. NOTE: If proposing a Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) type contract, the FAR clauses will be referenced at the Call level or within the Request for Proposal. The FAR and supplement provisions and clauses are incorporated by reference. The full text of these provisions and clauses can be found at https://www.acquisition.gov. If proposing an Other Transaction (OT) these FAR references and clauses would not apply. The terms and conditions of an OT agreement should be developed and negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Estimated Program Cost: The overarching announcement has an unrestricted ceiling. However, individual Calls may elect to provide an estimated program value or funding profile for planning purposes. Anticipated Number of Awards: The Air Force anticipates awarding multiple awards for this announcement. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more agreements, other transactions, or contracts for all, some or none of the solicited effort based on the Offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding availability. There is no limit on the number of awards that may be made to an individual Offeror. Schedule: The anticipated period of performance will be determined through dialogue between prospective Offerors and Government representatives for each topic area and specified in each individual award. Deliverables: Hardware and software deliverables will be specified within a separately priced line items and data deliverables will be specified on individual CDRL(s) in any resultant contract or an OT article. Within Scope Award Modifications: Offerors are advised that due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to make within scope changes, to include but not limited to, modifications which increase overall contract/award ceiling amount. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration: Before the Government can issue an award, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). If an Offeror was previously registered in Central Contractor Registration (CCR), the information has been transferred to SAM. However, it is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all of their data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SF424 "Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile," 2.) Security Program Questionnaire and 3.) Privacy Act Statement. The (3) template documents are attached to this announcement. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable based on an unacceptable S&T Protection risk determination. During the security review process, if it is determined that Covered Individuals are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract/agreement. Submit all questions to the DETER Org Mailbox (AFRL.DETER.ARA@us.af.mil) NOTE: Call Points of Contact will be specified at the Call level. ? TOPIC AREAS 1. Directed Energy (DE) Sources This category of supplies covers research, development and testing for all directed energy sources in the near-term and far-term in support of National Defense. This area covers the design, component/subsystem, prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of directed energy source components (to include spares and alternate component technologies), and/or systems and any required accessories, materials, and supplies for laboratory research and experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. This area also covers the redesign, refurbishment, modification, and/or upgrade of existing sources, if required, to support laboratory experimentation, field or flight trials, and/or demonstrations. Examples of directed energy sources include, but are not limited to: a. Laser Sources b. High Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) Sources 2. Acquisition Tracking Pointing (ATP), Beam Control (BC) and Atmospheric Compensation (AC) Systems This area covers the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of any hardware, sensors, control electronics, and software/firmware required to develop ATP, BC and AC systems to control the propagation of directed energy so as to maximize energy/irradiance on target. This area also includes any required accessories, materials, supplies, and/or services necessary to conduct laboratory experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. 3. DE Weapon Systems This area covers the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of DE weapon components and systems, diagnostics, accessories, materials, supplies, and services necessary to build/integrate complete weapon systems for laboratory research, experimentation and field trials in a relevant environment to demonstrate system capabilities. Systems may also be hardened to meet specific requirements imposed for operations in any domain to include ground/sea, airborne, and/or space. Systems engineering design/analysis and/or trade studies are relevant in regards to size, weight, and power (SWAP). Specific topics of interest include the following areas: a. Feasibility studies of innovative HPEM applications b. Integration of disparate technologies for the fielding of new HPEM systems and weapons c. Identification and quantification of useful -HPEM effects d. Development of HPEM sources that have a role in future applications e. system integration and demonstration of future HPEM capabilities f. Power subsystems g. Thermal Management subsystems h. Command and control subsystems i. Platform integration j. Detection, targeting and tracking subsystems k. DOTmLPF-P studies and experimentation l. CONOPS, CONEMPS, TTP development and experimentation m. Performance enhancement technologies for existing systems 4. DE Effects Testing Provide testing of materials, components, subsystems, and systems to determine the vulnerability, susceptibility, and accessibility of potential DE targets to DE exposure. This includes the design, component/subsystem prototype risk reduction, fabrication/purchase, assembly, integration, and testing of unique DE components, sources, and systems and any required diagnostic and/or special test equipment/tooling and materials necessary to conduct DE-material interaction physics experimentation to establish the efficacy of DE waveforms to support the development of DE weapons system requirements and/or assessment of proposed DE weapon systems. Develop survivability requirements and recommendations for space systems and support vulnerability predictions. 5. Modeling, Simulation and Analysis (MS&A) This area covers the development/procurement, testing, maintenance, modification, upgrade/reuse, and execution of scientific modeling, simulation and analysis software and requisite IT hardware systems necessary to efficiently execute software to support DE weapon system design, development, testing, and data analysis of test results. This includes campaign-level, engagement-level, system, and component-level MS&A codes to create test scenarios, assess design reference mission compliance, provide pre-test predictions, and conduct post-test assessment of system performance. In addition, sound principles for software engineering and development must be employed for all developed software and documentation. Robust software testing, validation, and verification are critical to software development efforts. As appropriate, software must scale to large simulation sizes and be portable to massively parallel computer architecture. MS&A software may include fast running engineering codes and detailed physics modeling codes. Examples of MS&A sub-topic areas include, but are not limited to: a. DE System Performance MS&A b. DE System Effects MS&A c. DE System Target Assessment d. DE System Biosafety and Biological Effects e. DE Source and Component Virtual Design f. Satellite signatures and Radiometric/photometric assessments of space objects. g. Assess electro-optical Space Domain Awareness (SDA) systems and architectures. h. Space system functional modeling and response i. Conduct Space Domain Awareness in non-traditional orbits j. Quantify safe operating conditions for lasers operating through the atmosphere and space 6. Wargaming This area covers the development/procurement, testing, maintenance, modification, upgrade/reuse, and execution of wargaming and scientific modeling, simulation and analysis software and their requisite IT hardware systems necessary to efficiently execute this software to support DE weapon system design, development, testing, and data analysis of wargaming results. This includes campaign-level, engagement-level, system, and component-level wargaming MS&A codes to create test scenarios, assess design reference mission compliance, provide pre-test predictions, and conduct post-test assessment of system performance. In addition, sound principles for software engineering and development must be employed for all developed software and documentation. Robust software testing, validation, and verification are critical to software development efforts. As appropriate, software must scale to large wargaming and simulation sizes and be portable to massively parallel computer architecture. Wargaming MS&A software may include fast running engineering codes and detailed physics modeling codes. Additionally, the wargaming area should provide general wargaming support to include DE wargame planning, table top, MS&A, and field execution, and wargame reporting. In addition, provide required hardware, software/firmware, accessories, materials, supplies, infrastructure, diagnostics, targets, safety equipment, and services necessary to conduct wargame research, experiments, field and/or range testing of DE components, subsystems, systems and demonstrations under operationally relevant conditions. 7. Innovative Space Domain Awareness Provide basic & applied research, algorithms, software/firmware, materials, supplies, and services necessary to conduct technology maturation for ground-based surveillance of space objects. Examples include, but are not limited to: a. Closely-spaced object detection and characterization. b. Daytime detection and custody of satellites. c. Orbit determination techniques and algorithms for satellites significantly affected by lunar and solar gravity. d. Rapid, on-demand orbit determination. e. Extremely wide field-of-view image exploitation for satellite discovery and custody. f. Multi-phenomenology sensor integration (e.g. optical, radar, passive radiofrequency). g. Active optical techniques for satellite ranging and characterization (e.g. LiDAR, LADAR). h. Sharp imaging of satellites through the atmosphere at low elevation angles. i. Characterization of atmospheric deep turbulence for image restoration. j. Techniques, algorithms, architecture designs, etc. for collaborative autonomous telescope networks. k. Multispectral, hyperspectral, and polarimetric characterization of space objects. l. Techniques to improve and exploit short- and long-wave infrared characterization of space objects. m. Machine learning algorithms to advance the state-of-the-art in areas such as: • Point spread function correction. • Space object image classification using resolved or non-resolved sensor imagery. • Uncorrelated track association. • Space object feature identification, model inference, and attitude regression. • Space object detection in noisy image backgrounds. • Generation of realistic space scene imagery / discernment of real vs. synthetic. • Detection of subtle, unique image artefacts of interest in a large dataset. 8. Experiments, Testing and Demonstrations Provide general and specialized test support to include DE test planning, laboratory and field demonstration, and reporting. Provide required hardware, software/firmware, accessories, materials, supplies, infrastructure, diagnostics, targets, safety equipment, and services necessary to conduct testing of DE components, subsystems, systems, and demonstrations under operationally relevant conditions. 9. Laboratory Materials, Supplies and Services in Support of Experimentation Provide required ancillary support systems, equipment, materials, supplies, infrastructure, and services necessary to support the development, operation, maintenance, and testing required to evaluate DE through experimentation in the laboratory and field during trials or flight/range testing. Examples include, but are not limited to: a. Clean rooms, anechoic chambers and necessary equipment, materials, supplies and/or services to support all aspects of DE source development, laboratory experimentation, and field trials. b. Diagnostic and/or special test equipment/tooling required for: • Quality assurance of components used in the fabrication of DE sources • Damage assessments and root cause analysis of component, subsystem and system failures • Characterization of target physical, chemical, and electromagnetic properties • Fabrication, assembly, integration, testing, operation and maintenance of DE sources • Direct/indirect measurements of DE source performance c. Power systems required to operate the source and any required ancillary equipment or services necessary to install, operate and/or maintain these systems d. Unique chemicals to operate, clean, and/or maintain direct energy systems and/or laboratory facilities used for directed energy experimentation as well as any required materials, accessories or services required for safe storage, use, operations, and proper disposal of any hazardous materials e. Thermal management components and systems, to include system-level and facility-level systems, necessary to support safe operations of DE sources. This includes materials, supplies, accessories, services and/or any support required for safe operations and maintenance of the system as well as proper disposal of hazardous materials/waste. f. Any required safety related items necessary to fabricate, assemble, integrate, test, operate and maintain directed energy sources. g. Transportation: This area covers all transportation, to and from, various research facilities and sites to conduct field and/or flight experimentation, testing and/or trials of directed energy components, sub-systems and systems and demonstrations. This includes such items as associated support/handling equipment, special test equipment/tooling, spares, and diagnostic/testing equipment. Specialized transportation requirements may include: design, fabrication and/or purchase of specialized packaging, crating, enclosures, trailers, and/or vehicles from which the transported item(s) will be operated/maintained to conduct experimentation, testing and/or trials outside of traditional laboratory spaces. sig_8bb2d98306a09357b555.description: ewz currently does not have a comprehensive OT monitoring solution for the systematic monitoring of the OT infrastructure at the various locations. The MoniTOR project aims to procure and implement a professional OT monitoring solution. The aim is to monitor around 90% of all OT systems, with very small locations being deliberately excluded from the scope. The new solution is intended to make a significant contribution to fulfilling the ICT minimum standard and significantly increase the cybersecurity of ewz's critical infrastructure. Through the systematic monitoring of the OT environment, threats are detected at an early stage, transparency regarding the state of the infrastructure is increased and incident response processes are efficiently supported. With the new OT monitoring system, a central management console is being introduced that makes it possible to automatically record and correlate alarms and assign them to the responsible persons. Clear dashboards and visualisations are intended to make the security and operating status of the systems recognisable at a glance. The project covers the "Systems and Networks", "Power Plants" and "District Heating" areas of ewz, while ewz Informatik and OIZ are explicitly excluded from the scope.
sig_8bb2d98306a09357b555.title: Security Monitoring OT Environment (OT Monitoring)

The project "Integrated intervention for professional development and integration into the labour market for young people aged up to 29 years" concerns the provision of an integrated, targeted and innovative range of services to 8.000 unemployed young people aged up to 29 years, graduates of secondary and post-secondary education. The provided range of services includes career counselling, theoretical training, practical placement and certification, and is directly linked to the development directions of the country's regions, according to the analysis of the Labour Market Needs Diagnosis Mechanism, at the level of the administrative region. It concerns the provision of an integrated, targeted and innovative range of services to 2.455 unemployed young people aged up to 29 years, graduates of secondary and post-secondary education. The provided range of services includes career counselling, theoretical training, practical placement and certification, and is directly linked to the development directions of the country's regions, according to the analysis of the Labour Market Needs Diagnosis Mechanism, at the level of the administrative region. In particular, it includes: 1. Provision of career counselling services. Through these services, individual career counselling sessions are provided, aiming to assist the individual in (re)designing their career path. Within this framework, the profile of the beneficiaries is analysed and their needs, capabilities and skills related to issues of (re)integration into the labour market are investigated. Part of the relevant services is also scheduled to be provided during both theoretical training and practical placement, in order to ensure the interconnection of theoretical training with the subject matter of the practical placement. 2. Provision of continuing vocational training services. These services include theoretical training and practical placement, in a mix that will result according to the outputs of the personalised career counselling. The practical placement will take place in private sector enterprises. sig_8bec36df5c07c3af445b.description: Time management is currently implemented for the contracting authority by "PAISY C/S" from ADP. "PAISY" encompasses all time values of an employee that need to be documented and reported by law. Furthermore, it includes the evaluation of working hours with the help of several hundred time types and segments. For this purpose, approximately 250 SWR-specific one-week shift schedules, approximately 60 multi-week sliding shift schedules, and various standard shift schedules are stored in "PAISY". The "primion" system supplies the times from the time recording terminals of currently approximately 3.900 employees. The system was introduced at the contracting authority in the 1990s and has been repeatedly adapted to requirements over time through extensive software adjustments and modernised as far as possible. From today's perspective, the system no longer meets the requirements for current technical standards, usability, functionality and accessibility, and has reached the end of its life cycles. For these reasons, the contracting authority has decided to newly introduce a modern time management system and to have the operation taken over by an external, appropriately qualified service provider in the form of a cloud-based "managed service". This EU-wide procurement procedure is intended to procure the provision and operation of a modern time management system in the form of a cloud-based managed service for the contracting authority in return for a monthly fee. Essential services to be provided are: • Provision and operation of a modern time management system in the form of a cloud-based managed service for a term of at least 4, optionally up to 10 years • Provision and operation of interfaces to: oPaisy oPrimion (time recording terminals) operspectively SAP HCM • Maintenance of the offered time management system over the entire provision period • Provision of support services in accordance with the agreed SLAs over the entire provision period by professionally appropriately qualified personnel • Provision services during implementation (project management, training, migration support) A detailed specification of services will be published together with the call for competition, but must only be processed by suitably qualified applicants in the second phase of the tender (service competition). For the service forming the subject of the tender, an EVB-IT Cloud contract with a term of 48 months and six renewal options of 12 months each (max. term 120 months) will be concluded. Service provision under regular operation is to take place from 01.06.2027. The necessary installation and integration services must be provided from 01.02.2027, but at the earliest upon award of the contract.
sig_8bec36df5c07c3af445b.title: Provision and operation of a time management system in the form of a cloud-based managed service

The itemised service list for the 2 supply packages that are the subject of the procedure is comprised of 13564 price list rows in part 1. and 6999 price list rows in part 2. The specific quantity and specific subject of individual procurements to be implemented following the conclusion of the FA—composed of elements forming part of the FA—shall be determined during the reopening of competition or direct ordering [Public Procurement Act (Kbt.) 105.§ (2) subsection b)]. 1. On-premise (or local) software: software that can be run on the user's own infrastructure, as well as related product support and other services. The service is not equivalent if operation can only be realised through the unauthorised modification or bypassing of the original software, or in any other unlawful manner or manner that violates IT security. Tendering is mandatory for all price list rows. The contracting authority draws attention to the fact that the consideration for the services included in the itemised price list cannot be 0 (zero) HUF for any single item, given that the public procurement contract to be concluded as a result of this public procurement procedure is a contract for consideration based on Section 3. § 24. of the Public Procurement Act. 2. sig_8bf58f0c24f150eeeda1.description: The Transport Suitability and Examination Centre Nonprofit Ltd. (KAV) has branch offices and customer services nationwide in every county to serve approximately 400 thousand customers annually. KAV wishes to continue maintaining the benefits of the current design of the centralised IT infrastructure, and therefore wishes to operate its nationwide IT systems with an active network connection whose data transmission capabilities are available to an extent that can bridge physical distances imperceptibly. It is able to meet this business requirement by providing a stable, modern, redundant data connection for the Budapest and county branch offices and customer service points that meets the high-level expectations of the age. The nationwide distribution of the branch offices is of a different nature and has different technical solutions, and can utilise data connection options based on open internet access that are adapted to local conditions in order to ensure info-communication with the Budapest headquarters. The continuous maintenance of these data connections is of fundamental interest to KAV Nonprofit Ltd., and therefore the repeated procurement of its comprehensive, nationwide data connection service is recommended for a further 24-month interval. Redundant internet access must be provided for KAV at a total of 36 locations (1 registered office + 35 branch offices) in accordance with the parameters defined in the technical specification. The technical content of the tender is to provide redundant internet access for KAV at 36 branch offices in accordance with the parameters defined below. Network topology Characteristics of the design of the network topology: • properties located at the addresses found in the KAV branch office list are the locations of the data connection endpoints based on open internet access to be established, • public internet endpoints must consist of two independent, redundant internet lines, • the branch office internet lines must be aggregated to BIX (Budapest Internet Exchange). Establishment of redundancy The expectations per branch office are as follows: • provision of one main internet line in the prescribed bandwidth in a symmetrical manner (both download and upload must be of the same bandwidth), with the exception of those branch offices where the infrastructure construction works are restricted by historic monument protection regulations; in this case, asymmetrical operation is acceptable in such a way that the upstream cannot be less than 50% of the downstream, • main line latency (avg) < 20 ms, • main line jitter (avg) < 1 ms, • main line packet loss < 0,1%, • the main internet line must be suitable for a 60%-increase in the prescribed bandwidth with a device replacement deadline of a maximum of 100 days, • provision of one internet backup line in the prescribed bandwidth in a symmetrical manner (both download and upload must be of the same bandwidth), with the exception of those branch offices where the infrastructure construction works are restricted by historic monument protection regulations; in this case, asymmetrical operation is acceptable, • backup line latency (avg) < 20 ms, • backup line jitter (avg) < 5 ms, • backup packet loss < 0,1%, • a fail-over device must be provided that combines these two lines and provides the data connection by default on the main line, and in the event of its failure, via the backup line with immediate switchover, • the output of the fail-over device is the service handover point, which must have a public IP address, • starting from the output of the fail-over device, it is necessary to create an IP tunnel, the other end of which is established aggregated per branch office on the BIX backbone, but the endpoint service is open internet access, • the main and backup lines must be constructed on different physical media per branch office. If this is not possible, in the case of identical physical media, the introduction into the building must take place along physically different routes. Identical street branches, adjacent protective conduits, and antennas with a line of sight to the same transmission tower shall not qualify as different routes, with the exception of those branch offices where the infrastructure construction works are restricted by historic monument protection regulations, or where no alternative service is available that could be constructed economically (e.g. route construction greater than 500 metres); in this case, the most prudent solution possible must be chosen. • regarding documentations, the Tenderer must provide the following documents to the Contracting Authority for the branch office constructions and the 24-month operation of the national network: o construction plans per branch office regarding both the main line and the reserve line, which the Contracting Authority shall approve as the first step of the construction process, o as-built documentation per branch office following constructions, with a detailed route illustration, o measurement logs supporting the bandwidth per line and per branch office, o following the national construction, presentation of SLA values on a monthly basis per branch office, which are the basic data of the monthly performance certificate (TIG) documents. The task of the winning tenderer is to introduce the internet lines into the property, construct the route after entering the property up to the designated RACK cabinet, and also terminate them in the RACK cabinet, and install and commission the terminal equipment. Detailed regulations and parameters are contained in the technical specification and the draft contract.

sig_8c1ebeab85a867af4cb1.description: The subject of this procurement is the preparation, implementation and follow-up of pedestrian traffic checks in 20 selected municipalities in Rhineland-Palatinate. Details of the scope of services can be found in the task description. Lot LOT-0001: Carrying out pedestrian traffic checks 2027-2028. It is an important concern of the Rhineland-Palatinate state government to sustainably increase the quality of stay in inner cities and town centres. At the same time, it is necessary to find answers to the climate changes that are now clearly noticeable. In this context, pedestrian traffic plays a crucial role. Cities that can be experienced on foot are more attractive and offer a higher quality of life. Retail and gastronomy benefit from this: those who travel on foot linger longer and perceive offers quite differently than other road users. Furthermore, walking has positive effects on health and the climate. Against this background, the Rhineland-Palatinate Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Tourismus, Energie und Klima would also like to offer ten municipalities in the state selected as part of a competition the opportunity to carry out professionally prepared and accompanied pedestrian traffic checks in each of the years 2027 and 2028. An external service provider is being sought for the comprehensive handling of this project. A pedestrian traffic check is understood here as a dialogue-oriented, participatory event format in which a city's citizens, administration and politicians jointly discuss the situation of pedestrian traffic in the municipality over several appointments. The focus of the pedestrian traffic check is two guided walks per municipality, during which the strengths and weaknesses of the pedestrian route network are recorded and analysed. Based on these findings, an action plan for rectifying the deficiencies is ultimately developed. The pedestrian traffic checks can be placed under a specific motto (e.g. quality of life, crossings). The implementation of pedestrian traffic checks as a statewide measure aims to bring pedestrian traffic and its specific requirements more strongly into the awareness of the administration, politicians and citizens in Rhineland-Palatinate and particularly in the participating municipalities. The promotion of pedestrian traffic in municipalities is to be sustainably strengthened by developing concrete content and results regarding local pedestrian traffic (e.g. status quo in pedestrian traffic, strengths-weaknesses analysis, action plan with priority and cost notes). In addition, the institutionalisation of pedestrian traffic promotion in the municipalities is to be supported. The statewide campaign is intended to arouse interest in further measures to promote pedestrian traffic and stimulate intercommunal exchange of experience on the subject. For the handling of the measure at the municipal level, the contracting authority (CA) provides a standardised project design that is identical and binding for all participating municipalities in terms of structure, time and cost framework. This basic framework can be filled with different content by the municipalities in coordination with the contractor (CO) according to local requirements. It is important that the promotion of pedestrian traffic remains the focus and that the specifications of the CA are not violated. In addition, municipalities are to be encouraged to implement further elements independently and at their own expense. The service provider to be commissioned has the following tasks: - From the date of contract award until the completion of the measure at the end of 2028, the CO shall accompany the statewide measure in a preparatory, executing and follow-up function as well as an advisor in close coordination with the CA. - In the total of 20 selected municipalities, the CO shall carry out the preparation, implementation and follow-up of the measure in close and consensual coordination with the municipal stakeholders. In particular, advisory, moderating, coordinating and documenting tasks are to be fulfilled here. The contract to be awarded is divided into the work packages described below. WP 1.1: Project management WP 1.2: In-person coordination with the contracting authority WP 1.3: Detailed project planning WP 1.4: Call for applications WP 1.5: Selection criteria and application documents WP 1.6: Execution of the application procedure WP 1.7: Selection of municipalities with the help of an expert jury WP 1.8: Creation of general text templates for the pedestrian traffic check for the municipalities WP 1.9: Support for press work at the state level WP 2.1: Preparatory work for the pedestrian traffic check in the municipality WP 2.1.1 Concretisation of the investigation design WP 2.1.2: Organisation of the overall project WP 2.1.3: Support for local press and media work WP 2.1.4: Participant acquisition WP 2.2: Kick-off workshop WP 2.3: Walks in the municipality WP 2.4: Final workshop WP 2.5: Final report for the municipality WP 2.6: Presentation of the results of the pedestrian traffic check in the municipal council WP 3.1: Final reports at the state level Details of the scope of services can be found in the task description.

Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is mapping suppliers' interest in the tendering for the coordination of resources, patient visits and space utilisation planning. The subject of the procurement is the better coordination than previously of customer and patient visits and space utilisation planning and monitoring. In the target state, space and resource planning is carried out using a scalable system entity. In the future, it can be linked to, among other things, the Numeron work shift planning system, property information system and patient and customer information system to be introduced in the wellbeing services county. Currently, health and social welfare professionals in the wellbeing services county use a single patient and customer information system from the same product family (SosiaaliLifeCare, TerveysLifeCare or both). In the target state, it would be essential that the professional would not need numerous systems to manage patient and customer work entries, appointments, arrivals and room bookings. The wellbeing services county currently does not have a master system for spatial data. The data is fragmented across different systems. Consequently, data-driven management views related to spatial efficiency are also not comprehensively available. In the future, for patients and customers, the wellbeing services county's own application Lunna will be the main transaction portal through which the customer or patient can handle their health and social welfare matters, and e.g. make appointments, register for appointments and receive (physical) customer guidance at the location. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue invites suppliers to market dialogues to discuss their solution models and present their products. The market dialogue discussions will take place in May during weeks 20 and 21 in Otaniemi, Espoo. The duration of the presentation session is preliminarily planned to be approximately two hours per supplier. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue reserves the right to invite the number of suppliers it deems necessary to the presentation session. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind suppliers to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the tendering procedure. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to declare their interest in the procurement via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind the service provider/supplier to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Interest in the procurement is requested to be submitted by 06.04.2026 at 12.00 via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. We will contact everyone who has expressed their interest.

sig_8c424b171a2b3359d9e4.description: The subject of the contract is the purchase together with delivery of Financial Trail Software intended for the standardisation and analysis of financial data and making it available in a structured form to external analytical tools. The system is equipped with an import engine that ensures the processing and retrieval of bank statements in various formats such as TXT/CSV/XLSX/PDF as well as JPK, KRS files and others, including foreign bank accounts. Imported data is stored in a built-in PostgreSQL database. The system has built-in data import control mechanisms. Import results are saved in the database in the form of import history. Imported data can be filtered and presented in tabular form, graphs or on dashboards. The system is integrated with IBM i2 software and allows the visualisation of data on IBM i2 Analysis Notebook diagrams, as well as the export of financial data to other IBM i2 tools, such as IBM i2 iBase. The aforementioned compatibility with IBM i2 software is extremely important because these tools have functioned for years as fundamental in the work of criminal analysts. The negotiated procedure without prior publication consists of conducting negotiations with only one contractor pursuant to Article 213 of the Public Procurement Law Act. The contracting authority conducted negotiations which consisted of the parties holding discussions for the purpose of jointly and mutually agreeing upon the provisions of the future contract, including the price for the delivery of 2 units of software.

sig_8c98020a43b971fe1d0a.description: This procurement is intended to implement the digital basis for carrying out the Swissnoso focus 1 “Digital Infrastructure” using the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Platform. The IPC Platform is intended to continue beyond the project period and serve to achieve the formulated goal of the Federal Office of Public Health's NOSO national strategy to achieve an HAI prevalence of 5% in the year 2030 and of 4% in the year 2035. The IPC Platform consists of two interconnected components: • the national IPC Datacenter and • the IPC Toolkits installed locally in the participating hospitals. The IPC Datacenter forms the national data infrastructure. The central data platform receives the encrypted, pseudonymised data from the hospitals, carries out national evaluations and provides the hospitals with benchmarking information for comparison and quality development. In addition, it provides the data basis for national surveillance and public health interventions. The graphical representation of the results in dashboards is a central aspect. For further information, see the specifications
sig_8c98020a43b971fe1d0a.title: IPC Platform “Surveillance and Prevention of Healthcare-Associated Infections”

sig_8ca460ccefc7522a6cb9.description: The subject of the Contract is the provision of technical support services to the Municipality of Athens in the management and monitoring of the implementation of those projects that are ongoing from the signing of this Contract and during its implementation. sig_8cab755f3e31b4ef5778.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to catalyze the translation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal CDS tools, developed as Software as a Medical Device, from training and testing of prototypes towards clinical applications that address unmet health challenges in precision medicine. These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.
sig_8cab755f3e31b4ef5778.title: Model-to-Clinic (M2C) for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (UG3/UH3, Clinical Trial Optional)

sig_8cad8135f2dd4b26faee.description: The subject of the contract is the reconstruction of the VJP manipulator – MAPP-400 used for handling spent nuclear fuel (VJP) at the Spent Fuel Interim Storage Facility nuclear facility (JZ MSVP). The MAPP-400 manipulator is classified into safety class III and, pursuant to Decree No. 431/2011 Coll. of the Nuclear Regulatory Authority of the SR (ÚJD SR) on the quality management system, it has a Quality Plan for the selected facility and a Schedule of Operational Controls drawn up and approved by the ÚJD SR. The subject of the reconstruction will be: • Drawing up of the as-built project documentation (PD) for the reconstruction, • Drawing up and updating of documentation pursuant to Annex No. 1, Letter C, points a) to g), i), q), s) for the approval of a modification at a nuclear facility (JZ) pursuant to Section 2, letter w and subsequently for the approval of the modification within the scope of the implementation of AEA (active trial operation) and commissioning of the nuclear facility in accordance with Act No. 541/2004 Coll. and on the amendment and supplementing of certain acts as amended, • Drawing up of documentation for the approval of the implementation of a modification significant from the perspective of radiation protection pursuant to Section 32, paragraph (3), letter a) and drawing up of documentation for the operating licence pursuant to Section 28 paragraph (1) letter a) of Act No. 87/2018 Coll. on radiation protection and on the amendment and supplementing of certain acts as amended, • Updating of the affected operational and process documentation and other QMS (quality management system) documentation affected by the change, • Drawing up of a detailed Work Implementation Schedule, • Drawing up of PTT (pre-complex testing) and CT (complex testing) programmes, • Manufacture, delivery and installation of switchboards and PLCs (programmable logic controllers), • Creation of visualization, delivery of operating PC (2 pcs), monitors (2 pcs), • Establishment of an ergonomic operator workstation (for 2 persons) consisting of operating desks and chairs, on which monitors with visualization and camera systems will be located, • Delivery and installation of M&C (measurement and regulation) instruments - sensors, transducers and actuators, • Delivery and installation of the relevant cabling (control and power), • Delivery and installation of camera systems (guidance and overview camera system), • Replacement of main drive units (6 pcs) and all absolute position sensors (6 pcs), • Performance of PTT, CT, AEA (active trial operation) tests and their evaluation, • Training of operating personnel, • Drawing up and delivery of As-Built Documentation (DSV) and Accompanying Technical Documentation (STD). Within the framework of the PD, it is required to draw up and hand over a separate PD for industrial cybersecurity solutions in accordance with standard IEC 62443. When drawing up the PD and the subsequent implementation of cybersecurity for MAPP-400, special security measures must be taken into account, as this information is considered classified information in accordance with the List of Classified Information under the remit of the ÚJD SR. For this reason, when fulfilling this part of the subject matter of the Work, all conditions for the protection of classified information, and the rights and obligations of legal entities and natural persons regarding this protection arising from the applicable legislation of the SR, must be complied with. The documentation shall be processed by the successful tenderer and handed over to the public buyer in the "Confidential" security classification grade.
sig_8cad8135f2dd4b26faee.title: Reconstruction of the VJP manipulator - MAPP-400

sig_8ccabcdf823bb7b6cb3b.description: Guldborgsund kommune, Denmark's southernmost rural municipality, with approximately 60.000 inhabitants in an area of approximately 90.000 hectares comprising long coastlines, forests and many villages and market towns distributed throughout the municipality. In the municipality there are several association houses, 16 halls and 3 swimming baths, as well as 5 artificial turf pitches which are used daily by our many associations, where approximately 285 popular education associations and evening schools are currently registered, as well as approximately 430 other associations. Guldborgsund Kommune invites tenders for one joint contract for the supply and operation of a digital solution for managing facilities and grants in Guldborgsund Kommune. Guldborgsund Kommune therefore needs a new digital and fully functional solution for managing the municipality's associations, grant management, and booking and management of the municipality's facilities. The new solution must ensure that the primary users, which are the associations in the municipality, have only one point of entry to the municipality regarding communication with the municipality on grants and facilities. The solution must at the same time be easy and intuitive for users to apply, including for elderly citizens, who make up a large proportion of the users. With a new solution, Guldborgsund Kommune will make it simpler for users to apply for grants pursuant to the Public Education Act, as well as apply for the use of the municipality's facilities for their activities. The solution must at the same time help to make case processing simpler for the municipality's administrative staff, for example via integrations with the municipality's financial system. In addition, the solution must also include municipal staff being able to book facilities via Outlook. The solution must also be able to handle events with registration, for example when the municipality invites people to thematic meetings, or activities are offered for Active Summer for the municipality's children. A new solution must bring together and manage all the municipality's facilities in one system, so that both internal and external registration are brought together in one place.
sig_8ccabcdf823bb7b6cb3b.title: Contract for the supply and operation of a digital solution for managing facilities and grants

sig_8cd7b85ff300eecc505c.description: Carmarthenshire County Council is undertaking an Early Market Engagement exercise to better understand the care rostering, scheduling and workforce management solutions currently available within the market. This exercise is intended to inform future planning and does not represent a commitment to undertake a procurement process. The Council is particularly interested in solutions that support: • Domiciliary Care scheduling and visit management. • Residential Care rostering and workforce management. • Workforce resource teams and shared staffing models. • Mobile working for frontline care staff. • Leave, absence and availability management. • Skills, compliance and workforce competency management. • Payroll, travel and workforce payment processes. • Reporting, operational oversight and management information. • Continuity of care and workforce utilisation. • Integration with care management, HR, payroll, finance and identity management systems. The Council intends to provide a high-level requirements document to interested suppliers and may invite suppliers to demonstrate how their solution supports the functional areas identified. Participation in this engagement is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Council to any procurement or award. All interested parties are encouraged to register their interest by 22/09/26 to participate in the demonstration sessions which we are planning to hold in October. Details of any formal tender will be provided in due course. Lot 1: . None

sig_8cdacbdc2b901768395d.description: This document is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, and its publication does not initiate a tendering procedure. This is a market consultation notice intended to identify potential suppliers operating in the market and their offerings. Participation in the market dialogue is entirely voluntary. Participating or not participating in the market dialogue will not affect a tenderer's opportunities to participate in a procurement procedure to be implemented later. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tender competition, nor does it exclude anyone from it. Rovaniemen kaupunki is preparing the procurement of a shift planning and working hours monitoring software service. The solution to be procured will be implemented as a SaaS service and must include shift planning and working hours monitoring functionalities. The entity to be procured also includes support, maintenance and further development services. The solution to be procured will be deployed in several different sectors, the largest user group being in early childhood education services. The estimated number of users of the system is approximately 1100 persons. The solution must enable shift planning and working hours calculation in accordance with the municipal general collective agreement for civil servants and employees (KVTES) and local collective agreements. MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue is intended for companies interested in tendering. The contracting authority may send questions and drafts of call for tenders materials to companies that have registered for the market discussion for a written statement round. Participants in the market dialogue will not be paid for their participation. The information provided in this notice and in the market dialogue itself is preliminary and may change as the preparation progresses. The announced schedule is also preliminary and may change as the preparation of the tender competition progresses. Please note that the market consultation does not include a question & answer phase. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register in accordance with the instructions described below. PROGRESS OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE In the first phase, written discussions will be held with potential service providers. The contracting authority will send questions related to the procurement as well as descriptions of a few use cases to the suppliers who have registered for the market dialogue. In the second phase, the aim is to organise solution demonstration sessions. According to the preliminary schedule, these sessions will be held during weeks 36-37. In the third phase, the contracting authority will send drafts of the procurement documents to the suppliers who have registered for the market dialogue for commenting. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Companies interested in the procurement are requested to notify their contact details by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi. The registration should be titled as follows: ”Työvuorosuunnittelun- ja työajanseurannan ohjelmistopalvelu – Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun”. State in the message the name of your organisation and the email address of the contact person to whom questions and draft materials of the call for tenders will be delivered. We request registrations for the market dialogue by 17.6.2026 at the latest by 12:00. Hansel Oy acts in a consulting role in the procurement.
sig_8cdacbdc2b901768395d.title: CALL FOR MARKET CONSULTATION: Procurement of a shift planning and working hours monitoring software service

sig_8d30077e689bbf059d25.description: Purpose Norsk Tipping (NT) currently uses ServiceNow, among other things, as IT Service Management and CSM tools and currently has a licence and maintenance agreement through DXC Technology. The contract expires in February 2027 and this procurement is a renewal of the maintenance contract for ServiceNow. NT is looking for a professional cooperation partner who can help maintain and further develop the current system. Tenderers must see possibilities, propose improvements and have good routines for development and support. The CSM module is used by Customer Service (Interactions/Case), Dealer service and some other small user groups (Case). Customer service is among norway's best and requires high efficiency in case handling with focus on quick access to information, getting pressure and high system degree. The system bears the mark that it has lived for almost 10 years. There are some technical debts that we need help cleaning up. Part of this is moving some internal APIs, which have been made available with MID-server, over to exposed facade services which are more responsive. The ITSM module is used to a very large degree by IT Operations, but also on customer service, dealer services (incident) and in Security. The case types in use are: incident, major incident, problem, change and request. NP's internal Service Desk and HR use Agent Workspace. ServiceDesk receives cases via the user portal, chat, telephone, attendance and e-mails that are automatically registered in ServiceNow. The case types they work with are primarily incident and request. It is a well developed Change management with a number of automated standard changes. ServiceNow is receiving more and more changes via pipeline or other integrations from internal Jira. The operational centre is the escalation point for general errors in the systems. They have monitoring and use, among other things, Splunk to receive events. Emphasis will be put on the tenderer ́s experience and competence in addition to operation and maintenance. Tenderers shall be a proactive consultant for the entire spectrum of services the contract covers. Whether there is new functionality in ServiceNow, a need for clearing in technical debts, smart choices around integrations, utilisation of functionality in the existing system based on the supplier knowing NP's business needs or the like. Requirements that shall be met. Norsk Tipping has organised development work in a product development model. The Customer Support product area is responsible for i.a. management and further development of ServiceNow, Genesys Cloud and self-service systems. Developers and consultants from the chosen supplier in this procurement will be important resources in this team together with other internal and external resources. NT has few, but good internal resources with competence in ServiceNow, and it is important to have a professional supplier that provides me good access to resources and who can contribute with expert help. As a starting point, the team consists of a system manager/owner and two system administrators, one of whom is defined as a team architect. The product development area currently consists of two multi-disciplinary teams, but which share internal resources and to a large degree work across. The product development manager has management responsibility for the teams and has, in addition, a team management role for the teams, in order to ensure progress and prioritising tasks. The product area is responsible for the management assignments being carried out and together prioritise small and large assignments based on the company principles for product development. The product development area follows the company ́s development cycle together with the other 12 areas and a joint plan is carried out at a general level, approx. 3 times per annum. The detailed planning will mainly be carried out in 2-week sprinters. Errors that occur are continually corrected as well as ongoing work in the other processes. The tenderer is expected to have competence in the following main areas. The list is not exhaustive: · ServiceNow platform · Licenses · Administration · Development · Integrations and integration security · Active and proactive consulting (ServiceNow and technology/architecture) · Coordination and planning · Work in multi-disciplinary teams · SLA and support Norsk Tipping currently has an agreement with DXC for ServiceNow. The agreement includes both consultancy services for the operation, management and further development of ServiceNow, as well as ServiceNow licences. The two parts of the existing agreement have different lengths. The agreement on consultancy services expires 27 February 2027, while the existing agreement on ServiceNow licences runs until February 2029. A new contract that will be signed as a result of this competition shall include both consultancy services and ServiceNow licences.
sig_8d30077e689bbf059d25.title: Maintenance and further development of ServiceNow

sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.description: The MSHIP Program is an initiative by TransnetBW aimed at supporting Germany's energy transition by developing a sustainable, scalable, and efficient grid management system. It focuses on modularity, automation, and simplicity to enhance operational security and reduce costs. The architecture is based on a self-hosted, cloud-native platform specifically designed for secure and data-driven operations. The MSHIP - LFC ensures continuous monitoring of the power balance and thus a stable energy supply. The controller detects deviations in the power balance or frequency and activates the appropriate secondary control power providers on a price-based basis to stabilize the balance and thus also the frequency. In addition, a controller is to be developed for special emergency situations in which no conventional control power market environment is available. The purpose of this RFI is to identify potential providers and solutions that can meet the requirements of the MSHIP - LFC. The RFI is intended to provide an initial market overview and to evaluate possible technological approaches and their ability to integrate into the existing MSHIP architecture. The aim is not to commit to a specific system, an architecture or provider in advance. Openness to different approaches remains the main guiding principle. The information gathered will serve as a basis for future decisions and possible tenders. Participation in this market exploration will not result in any advantages or disadvantages for the participants as potential bidders in a future - not yet binding - tender procedure. Please note that also responses are invited and will be considered that do not cover all listed functionalities.
sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.title: MSHIP Market Survey for LFC
