sig_8d8d596e08bcc065d2a5.description:
Public procurement procedure entitled 'Service contract for expert support for the implementation of horizontal obligations serving EU Cohesion Policy and for expert support related to strategic environmental assessment' 1. Part: EXPERT SUPPORT FOR HORIZONTAL EXPECTATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS 2. Part: EXPERT SUPPORT FOR STRATEGIC ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT (SEA) The precise and detailed task description and quantities are contained in point II.2.4. of the notice, as well as in the technical specification issued as part of the procurement documents. The purpose of the procurement is to obtain expert assistance necessary for the fulfilment of the horizontal expectations of the 2021-2027 period. The development and assurance of compliance with the following horizontal expectations is the task of the Member States, and therefore expert consultancy services are required for the effective performance of these additional tasks. Article 9. of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 of the European Parliament and of the Council (hereinafter: EU Regulation) prescribes the enforcement of horizontal principles, namely: - respect for fundamental rights and compliance with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, - ensuring gender equality, - preventing any discrimination based on sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation, - accessibility for persons with disabilities, and prescribes that - programmes must be implemented in accordance with the objective of promoting sustainable development, taking into account the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the Paris Agreement and the 'Do No Significant Harm' (hereinafter: DNSH) principle. Article 73. of the EU Regulation further prescribes that - when selecting operations, the managing authority must establish and apply criteria and procedures that are non-discriminatory, transparent, ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities and gender equality, and take into account the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, the principle of sustainable development and the Union's environmental policy in accordance with Article 11. and Article 191. (1) of the TFEU, and that - the managing authority(ies) must ensure a climate change resilience assessment for investments in infrastructure with an expected lifespan of at least five years when selecting operations. In addition to the above expert support, the winning tenderer shall also perform other closely related expert, training and presentation tasks. During performance, the tasks to be carried out include – as deliverables, in accordance with ad hoc orders – the development of environmental policy and/or sustainability documentation, as well as the development of climate protection documentation and/or climate change resilience assessments and/or climate risk assessments, as well as the development of equal opportunities and/or social inclusion documentation. NUMBER OF EXPERT DAYS ASSIGNED TO THE TASK: 550 expert days. During 275 expert days, preparation of analytical studies and/or strategies and/or evaluations and/or documentation related to professional advice concerning the preparation or implementation of development policy and/or cohesion policy and/or structural funds support policy programmes. During 275 expert days, preparation of analytical studies and/or strategies and/or evaluations and/or documentation related to professional advice concerning environmental and/or climate protection and/or sustainability aspects. One expert day consists of 8 hours. SCOPE OF TASKS TO BE PERFORMED: Due to the complexity and horizontal nature of the tasks, it is necessary for the experts to have appropriate experience in the fields of environment, climate protection and development policy, thus ensuring the practical enforcement of horizontal principles. 1. Updating the Horizontal Guide as required, supplementing it with new requirements. 2. Updating the Guide for carrying out climate change resilience assessments of infrastructure projects 2021-2027 (hereinafter: Climate Resilience Guide) as required during the 2021-2027 period, and reviewing it if necessary. 3. Expert advice on issues arising during the quality assurance of horizontal aspects of calls for proposals for operational programmes in the period between 2021-2027. 4. Preparation of studies, presentations, supporting materials and holding training sessions for the development policy institutional system and the beneficiary circle regarding all horizontal thematic areas (general horizontal principles and requirements according to Article 9. of the EU Regulation, DNSH, NEB, climate resilience). 5. Other expert tasks (regarding horizontal tasks). The precise scope and content of the tasks to be performed shall be determined within the framework of professional consultations between the Client and the Contractor during the cooperation, taking into account the specifics of the given part. Task assignment is based on individual orders. continued in point II.2.14.; To ensure the fulfilment of the environmental horizontal expectation, it is mandatory to conduct a so-called Strategic Environmental Assessment (hereinafter: SEA) for operational programmes based on the provisions of Directive 2001/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27. June 2001. on the assessment of the effects of certain plans and programmes on the environment (hereinafter: SEA Directive), as well as Government Decree 2/2005. (I. 11.) on the environmental assessment of certain plans and programmes (hereinafter: SEA Decree). During the modification of programmes, it is necessary to examine the environmental impact of the modifications in the framework of a so-called SEA pre-screening or, in the case of significant modifications, a full SEA.

The environmental and sustainability recommendations formulated as a result of SEAs must fit the content of operational programmes, calls for proposals and development policy documents, as well as the development policy planning and implementation system, therefore it is necessary to take these connections into account during the performance of SEA tasks and ensure the proper integrability of recommendations. With regard to modifications of operational programmes for the 2021-2027 period, it is necessary to use expert support in order to ensure compliance with these expectations. In addition to the above expert support, the winning tenderer also performs other expert, training and presentation tasks closely related thereto. NUMBER OF EXPERT DAYS ALLOCATED TO THE TASK: 700 expert days One expert day consists of 8 hours. In order to ensure that continuous expert assistance is available regarding horizontal tasks during programme implementation, the contract must be concluded for several years. EXPECTED SCOPE OF TASKS TO BE PERFORMED: 1. To ensure the fulfilment of the environmental horizontal expectation, it is necessary to provide expert support related to the environmental assessment of operational programmes and their modifications for the 2021–2027 period based on the SEA Directive and the SEA Decree. 2. Preparation of SEA pre-screening documentation in the case of modifications of operational programmes for the period between 2021–2027. 3. Preparation of SEA Monitoring Reports related to SEA reports of operational programmes for the period between 2021–2027. The exact scope and content of the tasks to be performed are determined by the Client and the Contractor within the framework of professional consultations during cooperation, taking into account the specifics of the given part. During the preparation of the above documents, it must be ensured that the results and recommendations of the SEA are relevantly linked to the development policy objectives, the intervention logic of the operational programmes, and the processes of preparing and modifying support calls. GENERAL PROVISIONS II.1. Task assignment - Ordering Expert tasks are issued to the Contractor by the Monitoring and Evaluation Department of Nemzeti Fejlesztési Központ in the framework of a written order. The Order contains the specific, detailed task description, the result product, and the maximum number of expert days chargeable for it. For individual orders, the Client also determines the deadline for performance concerning the result products. The Contracting Authority undertakes to exhaust the expert fee up to at least 70% of the expert fee. Based on the order, the Contractor draws up a project plan and detailed methodology, which must be approved by the Client. Thereafter, the execution of the order by the Contractor may commence. The experts offered in the Tender are obliged to participate in the performance of individual orders. II.2. Task performance The Contractor is obliged to perform the task issued in the Order according to the specified and agreed content, by the deadline, taking into consideration consultations held with stakeholders (e.g. specialists representing policy and managing authorities). Tasks entailing an expert day accounting may be accounted for exclusively on the basis of an Order issued by the Client. In addition to performing the (sub)task, the project manager's duties include ensuring project management, compiling the comprehensive report to be prepared on project progress (concerning all subtasks), organising necessary meetings and consultations, preparing minutes, compiling final documents, and ensuring the substantive and formal consistency of documents, paying special attention to correct grammar, and understandable and simple formulation. II.3. Proof of professional compliance For each individual performance, the experts producing the performance must be named. The Client confirms the compliance of the performance sent electronically (by e-mail) by issuing a certificate of performance within 15 calendar days at the latest. Tasks defined in the Order shall be deemed performed on the day when the Client issues the certificate concerning the performance of the task to the Contractor. II.4. Expert day accounting Following the Client's certification of the professional compliance of the task, the Contractor prepares an expert-day-based timesheet for the performed tasks (lists and totals the expert days actually used for individual tasks). The number of expert days intended to be accounted for against a given Order may not exceed the framework recorded in the Order. The Client has the right to dispute the submitted expert day timesheet if it finds that the professional standard of the submitted performance or the number of expert days to be accounted for does not correspond to each other. Based on the consideration of the Client's objection, the Contractor may modify the submitted expert day timesheet. The Client issues the professional certificate of performance after the certification of professional compliance and the expert day accounting. The Contracting Authority undertakes a call-off obligation for 70% of the defined framework quantities. Task assignment is based on individual orders. Detailed technical description and conditions in the proc. doc.

sig_8d90f991c93ae6d49be7.description: BACKGROUND Espoon seudun koulutuskuntayhtymä Omnia published a request for information in autumn 2025 and conducted market dialogue concerning the overhaul of financial and HR systems. At the stage when the request for information was published, the preliminary starting point was that the overall delivery would be put out to tender as a single procurement so that the implementation project could have begun as early as the beginning of year 2026. As the preparation of the procurement has progressed, the plans have been refined. According to the current estimate, the financial management and human resources management solutions will be put out to tender as two separate procurements. The solution is based on refinements made during the preparation of the procurements regarding the scope, market and implementation method of the overall deliveries. UPCOMING TENDERS The planned procurements are: - Procurement of financial management services and systems as a SaaS service - Human resources management system as a SaaS service and payroll processing as a comprehensive service The content and titles of the procurements may still change, but the plan is to implement the procurements as separate tender processes. According to the contracting authority's preliminary estimate, the estimated total values of both procurements will exceed the EU threshold, and the procurements will be implemented as an open procedure. According to the current estimate, the tender processes for both procurements will kick off in late 2026. More detailed schedules will be specified as the preparation progresses. The Act on Public Contracts and Concession Contracts (1397/2016) is complied with in the procurements. MARKET INFO AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE Before publishing the contract notices, Omnia plans to do the following around August–September 2026: - organise a market information event presenting the objectives and implementation schedules of the procurements - offer suppliers the opportunity to participate in a technical dialogue where suppliers can comment on the preliminary procurement documents The objective of the market info and technical dialogue is to ensure that the market is adequately informed about the upcoming tenders, and above all to ensure appropriate and viable requirements for both procurements. NEXT STEPS Omnia will communicate separately about the market info and dialogues with a new prior information notice in August 2026. Omnia encourages operators to actively monitor notices immediately after the summer holiday season and to allocate resources for participation during the coming autumn.

sig_8da8e0a9f3cbf3232423.description: Transport for London (TfL) is seeking to procure a replacement Central Management System (CMS) to supersede the current platform, which is being phased out due to its reliance on obsolete 2G/3G networks. The new CMS is required to support TfL's ongoing LED upgrade programme across the Transport for London Road Network (TLRN), where approximately 37,000 lighting column luminaires form part of a wider 190,000‐point lighting estate. As LED adoption increases-forecast to reach 85% of lighting column luminaires by March 2026-TfL requires a modern, interoperable CMS to control lighting assets, manage Harvard‐equipped luminaires, and provide real‐time fault monitoring essential for maintenance and operational efficiency. The upgraded estate incorporates both NEMA and ZHAGA socket standards, reflecting the transition to more flexible and future‐proof lighting technologies. TfL intends to invest to complete the lighting upgrade programme and implement a unified, modernised control solution. The procurement will cover: CMS hardware (nodes, gateways, infrastructure) CMS software and asset monitoring Support and maintenance services Installation and on-boarding Training for operational teams Technical and design consultancy Delivery as a SaaS-based solution The new CMS will enable standardisation, improved performance visibility, and long-term compatibility across TfL's lighting network Lot 1: .
sig_8da8e0a9f3cbf3232423.title: TfL Street Lighting - Control Management System (CMS)

sig_8da9325aa41095cb85f2.description: The SIDEC du JURA wishes to acquire, for its own needs and those of the local authorities of Jura, computer hardware, management software and their maintenance. In order to successfully carry out this mission, SIDEC is setting up a Dynamic Purchasing System to acquire them, authorised by deliberation No. 2328 of 5 October 2024 and a purchasing body, authorised by deliberation No. 2347 of 25 January 2025. A Dynamic Purchasing System (hereinafter referred to as the "DPS" or "System"), without being a contract as such, is a fully electronic purchasing technique which allows economic operators admitted to participate in the DPS to be put into periodic competition for the award of several public contracts called specific contracts (SCs), comparable to call-off framework agreements. In other words, throughout the validity period of the DPS, any operator may apply to be admitted. Once admitted, the operator is informed directly of upcoming specific contracts and may submit bids without having to resubmit a whole series of supporting documents. The DPS is divided into several categories according to the type of product. It is possible to be admitted to one or more categories. Consequently, any operator admitted to a given category is invited, if they so wish, to tender for each corresponding specific contract. The specific contracts are themselves divided into lots, one per product. Each operator is free to submit a tender for one or more lots. Each resulting contract will be of the call-off contract type, with a maximum for each contract Notification 1th consultation; Lot 2 covers the acquisition of office computer hardware according to the needs of SIDEC and the contracted Jura local authorities; lot 3 covers the supply of office and utility software; lot 4 corresponds to the maintenance of hardware and supply of small equipment
sig_8da9325aa41095cb85f2.title: SIDEC - DPS - IT CONSULTATION FOR HARDWARE, SOFTWARE AND MAINTENANCE - 4 lots

sig_8da989a45f6313ecb8e9.description: Background and reason The municipality wants to map out what possibilities already currently exist in the market to retrieve and process data from various sources using a source data platform, such as data from the UWV, the Tax and Customs Administration, DUO, banks, RDW and the Chamber of Commerce. This platform must improve service provision by relieving citizens of the burden of supplying data and speed up decision-making, for example by automatically or ex officio granting benefits. In this regard, data minimisation and compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) are central. Why this market consultation The purpose of this market consultation is to gain insight into the possibilities, limitations and ambitions of market parties, and to gather information regarding this subject. To this end, we are approaching a number of organisations in the sector that we deem capable of performing these services. For whom Participation is open to individual parties and partnerships (e.g. consortium). An anonymised report may be produced from the market consultation. Your input will be processed anonymously. Purpose of market consultation With this market consultation, the municipality aims to: Gain insight into the technical capabilities of source data platforms. Understand how data is retrieved, processed and supplied. Gather information on the user-friendliness and accessibility of the solutions. Understand what internal resources are required for implementation and management. Gain insight into the cost structure and potential additional costs. The information from this market consultation may potentially be used in the future to shape a tender; however, this is not yet certain. The contract value in this announcement is stated for administrative reasons. (BT-27-Procedure)
sig_8da989a45f6313ecb8e9.title: Market exploration for the retrieval and processing of data via source data platforms

sig_8dacfa2eccd12a9d7b3b.description: Klief is a rehabilitation hospital in Ostend, Belgium, which, due to the phase-out of the existing software package Obasi, is putting out to tender the public contract for the implementation and support of a replacement software package. Obasi is currently used for the following organisational processes: • Logistics and inventory management; • Accounting and financial administration; • Procurement management; • Patient management (admission, intake, discharge, scheduling); • Invoicing (VSB, health insurance fund, patients, third-party payer); • Pharmacy management (incl. Recip-e, link to eHealth platform); • Optional in scope: BI and reporting, integrations with lab and radiology. Simultaneously, we also have an implementation process underway for a new EHR (KWS, NexuzHealth) that will replace our existing EHR (Oxygen, CompuGroup). In view of the phase-out of Obasi on the one hand and the implementation of KWS on the other, a strict condition applies that the implementation of the new replacement software module(s) can be started and completed in close coordination with all stakeholders and within the shortest possible timeframe. In this regard, the contracting authority expects the new hospital information system to go live no later than 2028. In January 2027, the implementation of the new software module(s) will start so that the implementation itself is carried out in a timely, qualitative, complete and correct manner according to industry standards. In doing so, the contracting authority will take particular account of the mutual (contracting authority and contractor) required resources, manpower profiles, project steps and planning; which is subject to validation by the contracting authority and also constitutes a crucial component (award criterion) for this contract. This concerns a strategically important contract for our organisation for which the contracting authority expects a strongly integrated software package and information system that not only supports current and future activities, but is also capable of further digitising existing work processes and integrating them into the organisation's operations. In addition to the compatibility of the software product with our hospital processes and working methods, the necessary certification, expertise and experience with similar contracts, from a holistic perspective there are very many elements associated with this contract for which the contracting authority would like to gain insight into how the candidate contractor views this. This concerns, for example, but not exclusively: project methodologies that can be applied, change management, governance and communication, partnership, values and norms, training, effectiveness and efficiency in project execution, etc. We look forward to realising a new strategic collaboration with this contract.
sig_8dacfa2eccd12a9d7b3b.title: Implementation and support of a new hospital information system

sig_8db8a81842fcad2bc5a5.description: The present public procurement provides for the development and implementation of an intelligent system and integrated digital solution for improving the safety and working conditions of drivers and passengers in public transport in the city of Dobrich, including a specialised system for specific video surveillance of drivers operating public transport vehicles. It should integrate functions such as: 1. Mobile video surveillance of the driver's cabin; 2. GPS tracking and the possibility of speed control and limitation; 3. Two-way voice communication between the vehicle driver and the dispatch centre, the possibility of sending/receiving messages, which would allow dispatchers to interact with drivers in real time; 4. Various types of alarms, such as: panic alarm, speeding alarm, route deviation alarm, power failure alarm. The system should support high-resolution video recording (1080P) using H.265 encoding, which would allow the transmission of high-quality CCTV footage in real time to the dispatch centre. 5. Delivery and installation of the relevant on-board equipment. The system must provide the possibility both for integration with the Contracting Authority's existing Public Transport Management System (PTMS), and the possibility for future functional expansion and upgrading. Result of the execution of the public procurement: Development and implementation of an intelligent system and integrated digital solution for improving the safety and working conditions of drivers and passengers in public transport in the city of Dobrich, including a specialised system for specific video surveillance of drivers operating public transport vehicles with the following functions: 1. Mobile video surveillance of the driver's cabin; 2. GPS tracking and the possibility of speed control and limitation; 3. Two-way voice communication between the vehicle driver and the dispatch centre, the possibility of sending/receiving messages, which would allow dispatchers to interact with drivers in real time; 4. Various types of alarms, such as: panic alarm, speeding alarm, route deviation alarm, power failure alarm. The system should support high-resolution video recording (1080P) using H.265 encoding, which would allow the transmission of high-quality CCTV footage in real time to the dispatch centre. 5. Delivery and installation of the relevant on-board equipment; 6. Trained personnel for working and operating the system. Accordingly, a significant impact on the safety and efficiency of public transport and an increase in passenger confidence will be achieved. As an indirect result, it is expected to achieve: Prevention of road accidents through monitoring of driver behaviour – for example, detection of drowsiness, distraction or aggressive driving. Improved compliance with traffic rules, as drivers are aware that they are being monitored. Control over interactions between staff and passengers – for example, in cases of conflict, aggression or complaints. Increasing the sense of security and peace of mind for passengers and drivers – passengers will be calmer knowing that there is surveillance and control, and drivers, knowing that in the event of an incident, they can count on timely assistance. The detailed description of the requirements for the participants is written in the Technical Specification.
sig_8db8a81842fcad2bc5a5.title: "Development and implementation of an intelligent system and integrated digital solution for improving the safety and working conditions of drivers and passengers in public transport in the city of Dobrich"

sig_8dcf54fafbf8fa54d240.description: Lot 1: Establishment of the National Central C-ITS Hub. The National Central C-ITS Hub comprises the Central C-ITS Station and the exchange hub. The Central C-ITS Station shapes the content of messages regarding precisely defined C-ITS service protocols and scenarios. Via the National Hub, various stakeholders will communicate with each other in a trustworthy manner. In future, it is expected that an increasing number of information providers will be connected to the system and will provide data for various C-ITS services and scenarios. In this way, safety messages and traffic condition alerts will reach the vehicles of various car manufacturers directly. Lot 2: Execution of mobile laser scanning and determination of lane axes. The aim of the task is the capture and digitalisation of road traffic infrastructure data for autonomous driving purposes. The task will address the geometry of traffic areas at the lane level to determine the course of the digital axis per lane. The digital lane axis model forms part of the National Traffic Information Centre (NCUP) digital traffic infrastructure (DTI). The results of the task will be intended to support new digital traffic services. The digital model must provide support for navigation, provide support and act as a source of information for cooperative intelligent transport systems (C-ITS) and, in future, enable and support autonomous driving. This public contract covers data capture in the field using mobile laser scanning and spherical photography of national roads over a length of 1.937 km (in both directions; G1, G2, R1 and selected sections of R2). Lot 3: Establishment of a system for the analysis of traffic flows on public roads. The primary objective of the video analytics system is to improve the acquired data on free-flowing vehicle movement on public roads, which will be achieved by analysing vehicle speed data calculated from streaming footage from pre-existing traffic surveillance cameras. The main result of the public contract will be the development of a software solution for the dynamic calculation of vehicle speeds from streaming footage provided by traffic surveillance cameras. The calculated data will be integrated into the contracting authority's existing real-time vehicle trace big data management platform (FCD platform). The National Central C-ITS Hub comprises the Central C-ITS Station and the exchange hub. The Central C-ITS Station shapes the content of messages regarding precisely defined C-ITS service protocols and scenarios. Via the National Hub, various stakeholders will communicate with each other in a trustworthy manner. In future, it is expected that an increasing number of information providers will be connected to the system and will provide data for various C-ITS services and scenarios. In this way, safety messages and traffic condition alerts will reach the vehicles of various car manufacturers directly.

sig_8dfed59770476e947318.description: For the electric commercial vehicles, Disposal + Recycling requires power distribution cabinets in the two motor vehicle halls at the Forsthaus energy centre, each with at least 6 charging points, distribution boxes for the individual vehicles and a load management system (software). The power distribution cabinets must meet the following requirements: · Suitable for use in depots (municipal works yards) with fixed, schedulable charging times. · Suitable for 24/7 use in a frost-protected environment (hall, marquee). · Suitable for normal charging and rapid charging of individual vehicles. · Equipped with LAN, WLAN and mobile communications (at least 4G). The distribution boxes for the individual vehicles must be compatible for CCS charging cables with 5 m, 7 m and optionally 10 m. The boxes must have at least IP54 protection. Wall mounting is intended in principle. Optionally, ceiling mounting with a cable reel featuring a 7 m long cable is to be tendered. The installation (excluding electrical installation) of the power distribution cabinets and distribution boxes must be carried out by the tenderer. Commissioning is to be carried out by the supplier and must be recorded in a report. The electrical installations are tendered separately and are not part of the scope of services. However, the software for load management must be offered as well. Since Energie Wasser Bern is constructing a new building on the site of the Forsthaus energy centre from July 2027, the distribution cabinets and boxes of the North motor vehicle hall must be accommodated in a provisional structure (temperature-controlled marquee) and will only be installed in the motor vehicle hall after a construction period of approx. 3 years. The distribution cabinets and boxes for the East motor vehicle hall can be installed at the final location upon delivery. The installation of the infrastructure must take place by early June 2027 at the latest. With regard to the software, it is important that not all vehicles are charged simultaneously, but rather that the entire available time (approx. 16 hours to 06.30 hours) is utilised. In addition, the system must restart automatically in the event of a power or network failure and issue a notification. Furthermore, the following requirements are placed on the software: · Locally installed hardware/software solution, also possible web-based, which controls the charging processes locally. · Autonomous functionality of the system even in the event of an internet failure or malfunction. · Arbitrary scalability when retrofitting additional charging points. · Immediate clearance of the charging process following successful authentication. · Online access (web UI) via desktop computer and mobile end devices. · German language selection. · Display of energy consumption per vehicle live and retroactively. · Evaluations and statistics on energy consumption, charging processes and efficiency per vehicle as well as comparison options between the vehicles. · Export of consumption and charging data (e.g. CSV or Excel). · Guarantee that the software will be actively supported for at least five years after acceptance of the installation (delivery of security patches, adaptation to new versions of peripheral systems, elimination of functional errors, etc.). The detailed technical requirements can be found in the bill of quantities in the appendix. The bill of quantities must be completed in full without references to additional documents. Product, brand, design or type designations are dispensed with. If such designations are listed in exceptional cases, equivalent alternatives are permitted. Equivalence must be proven by the tenderer.

sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.description: BIM Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH (BIM) intends to procure and introduce a new document management system (DMS) for company-wide use. The aim of the project is to provide a central, secure and audit-proof platform for managing, processing and archiving documents and files. The DMS is intended to support cross-departmental collaboration, reduce existing media discontinuity and ensure compliance with statutory, data protection and organisational requirements. Operation will initially take place on-premises in the BIM data centre. In the long term, the solution is intended to technically support hybrid and cloud-based operating models respectively. The scope of services comprises in particular: - Provision, implementation and introduction of the DMS software including installation, configuration and training, - Integration into existing systems, in particular SAP S/4HANA, email and office environments, - Migration of existing documents and metadata, - Design and implementation of defined workflows, archiving and authorisation structures, - Ensuring information security, digital accessibility and GDPR compliance, - Operation, maintenance and software support (support S) including service level management. The project is part of BIM's digitalisation strategy and is closely linked to the parallel projects "BIM SAP 2028" and "BitX", in which core business processes and specialist procedures are modernised and integrated. The contract term is 48 months with the option for a one-time extension of up to 24 months. The basis for the provision of services is the EVB-IT system contract in its currently valid version.

sig_8e9f61b4506ff5c4dd2f.description: The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) is issuing a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3458 as implemented by RFO DFARS 212.7000. Under a CSO, the ERDC may competitively select proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), based on a review of proposal by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers within the ERDC and/or other federal experts. This CSO will be used to acquire innovative products, services, or technologies, and under this CSO, all products, services, and technologies shall be treated as commercial items. Products, technologies, and services do not have to be ?commercially available? to be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the DFARS regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the Contracting Officer will utilize commercial procedures to develop and execute the resultant award. This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) contains broadly defined areas of interest for ERDC?s Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) and intends to obtain ?innovative? solutions or potential new capabilities in support of integrated digital transformation, advanced computing, secure and resilient systems, and data-driven decision-making to address complex defense and civil works challenges. Solutions may include existing technologies or procedures that are not currently in use that would enhance or streamline mission capabilities.?More specific individual program requirements (IPRs) may be added in the future. The AOIs are intentionally broad in nature, generally have no known funding specifically available, and will be posted under this CSO on an open-continuous basis for one (1) year from the date of original posting. Any specific individual program requirements that are posted under the authority of this CSO will describe the desired end results, offer additional context for the needs that seek solutions, provide funding profiles, and will stipulate specific due dates for solutions. All resultant awards will be firm-fixed price. All items, technologies, and services (including research and development) procured via this CSO are treated as commercial. Applicants from universities and/or non-profit organizations should be aware that commercial clauses will be integrated into the award and should coordinate proposals with associated legal counsel prior to submission. ERDC is conducting this CSO on a full and open basis and intends to award contracts in accordance with FAR part 12 and the FAR part that is deemed most appropriate for the solution proposed (i.e., FAR part 13, 15, and/or 35); the government reserves the right to award prototype agreements (e.g. Other Transaction Agreements), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. ?2371b, if deemed appropriate and in the government?s best interest.Go to https://www.erdcwerx.org/information-technology-laboratory-cso/ for all of the CSO details and submission requirements. All solutions must be submitted through the ERDCWERX platform.
sig_8e9f61b4506ff5c4dd2f.title: Information Technology Laboratory Commercial Solutions Openings (CSO)

sig_8eb17e4064ad6095e84a.description: The purpose of this consultation is: The institutional website of the City of Asnières-sur-Seine underwent its last graphic and functional redesign in 2023. Managed by a service provider placed into compulsory liquidation on 27 March 2025, it was the subject of an urgently launched consultation which resulted in the selection of two service providers to organise the takeover of the site, its optimisation (updates, security, accessibility, bug fixes), as well as the hosting and maintenance of the TYPO3 CMS for a period of one year. During this transitional period, the IT management service provider and the TYPO3 application service provider restored a functional and fully accessible version of the site, focused on its security and compliance with the community's standards and legal obligations. The site thus has a solid foundation and does not require any urgent intervention. The local authority is also covered by an ELTS warranty extension for its current version of TYPO3 until October 2026. The purpose of this contract is the designation of two new service providers responsible, on the one hand, for the TYPO3 application maintenance of the site and, on the other hand, for the hosting and IT management of the server. Lot 1 : TYPO3 application maintenance and development service; Lot 2 : Hosting and IT management service

sig_8f144bf3cc1e2dfa5244.description: The very strong competition between modes of transport (air, private cars, carpooling, buses, etc.), the opening up of international rail transport to competition since 2010 and upcoming ecological awareness make responsiveness, agility and innovation imperative. In this context, Voyages SNCF has been offering willing airlines a rail service enabling air sector customers to be transported from a selection of French and European TGV stations to major French airports for 30 years. In view of the development of this business sector, Voyages SNCF wishes to develop this product with the help of an IT service provider taking charge of all the management stages for booking, ordering and ticketing as part of the sale of this product by airlines. This partner must be able to manage the increase and diversity of available data linked to the marketing of several SNCF offers (TGV Inoui, OUIGO) and a set of partner airlines. To date, the booking of seats in TGVs by partner airlines is based on an automated process in 2022 allowing airline customers to book an end-to-end train + air ticket using a technical component linking the various inventories. This booking process is currently based on fixed pricing, regardless of the date or time of travel. The current process allows customers to independently manage the issuance of their train ticket via an online platform. SNCF ticket counters are therefore no longer responsible for this issuance, except in disrupted cases. SNCF Voyageurs wishes to improve the Train+Air product for the following reasons: • Continue the development of the current offering, global and segmented, with a digital product present across the entire LGV network (Inter-sector and radial lines) offering different levels of service (complementarity of offering between TGV Inoui and OUIGO); • Have a competitive product to attract new airlines. • Have a tool that can easily evolve with the opportunities offered by the growth of the air market. SNCF Voyageurs wishes to have a solution that allows the various airlines to connect to the SNCF booking system. This solution must therefore: • Integrate with airline systems and manage the operational differences between air and rail; • Interface with the SNCF booking system by accessing the SNCF offers access portal, the entry point for booking all SNCF offers (specifically TGV Inoui, Ouigo). The sought-after solution has several objectives: • Ensure booking management and the staggered opening of booking periods between rail and air carriers; • Publish SNCF timetables and services to airlines and their distributors; • Ensure the issuance of rail transport tickets; • Monitor and share the management of passenger status changes (Boarded status for checked tickets) in accordance with SNCF and airline processes; • Enable the monitoring of service billing; • Transmit the customer's ticket to the airline; • Offer a simple solution so that the customer can collect their train ticket independently; • Offer a rail ticket consultation solution to SNCF agents in order to overcome operational issues. The consultation is conducted by the Purchasing and Circular Economy Directorate (DAGEC) of SNCF, acting as agent for the CRMS subsidiary which will hold the contract. Indeed, the management of the Train + Air product is ensured by CRMS as a subcontractor of SNCF Voyageurs. SNCF Voyageurs provides rail capacities purchased by airlines and CRMS manages and facilitates the arrangement for the benefit of SNCF Voyageurs.
sig_8f144bf3cc1e2dfa5244.title: Digitalisation Train + Air

IT demand sometimes grows faster than internal staff can be built up and should it decrease, reducing internal staff is sluggish. This scaling requirement is addressed by awarding services to external parties. One form of this is the external takeover of testing of software applications in a scope appropriate for each application (test concept, test management, test case definition, execution of functional and non-functional tests (e.g. L&P tests, regression tests, exploratory tests, ...), test automation). This support takes place in both traditional and agile environments. The client currently has 3 candidate groups of applications for which they wish to outsource testing. The known support effort is approx. 3 to 5 FTE. During the contract term, applications may be added, removed, or the annual effort for them may fluctuate. A framework agreement is being tendered. The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. Exceptions that require on-site service delivery are workshops and, where applicable, tests in connection with hardware that is only available on-site at the client (e.g. a ticket vending machine). Other special conditions for contract performance: Contract execution in German, written and oral; within EU GDPR

This prior information notice is not intended to shorten the tender deadline in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations §20-2 (2). NHN wants to start a procurement process for broadband access for small and medium sized locations. The accesses are used by members in the health network, service providers and entities in the central health management. The accesses represent an important part of a robust and secure infrastructure for transporting digital services for the entire health and welfare sector. Limitations: Accesses to large locations such as hospitals, computer centres etc. are not a part of this procurement. The aim is to enter into an agreement with one or several tenderers. Furthermore, we see great opportunities in further developing digital interaction systems that make NHNs and the supplier's work processes more efficient for the establishment, operation and termination of accesses. The Contracting Authority intends to sign a contract by the end of 2026, starting the agreement from January 2027. We are responsible for national e-health services such as e-prescription, helsenorge.no, core journal and basic data. We also provide services within ICT, procurements and archives for the health administration agencies. NHN operates 80 national ICT systems and has 1,000 capable employees distributed across offices in Trondheim, Oslo, Tromsø, Moss and Svalbard. Read more at the https://www.nhn.no. At the time of the prior information notice, NHN plans to conduct the procurement in accordance with the Norwegian Public Procurement Act and Regulations, based on the procedure competitive procedure with negotiation after prior publication above the EU/EEA threshold (1.49 MNOK) pursuant to FOA Parts I and III. To further strengthen the market’s ability to participate in the competition, and to facilitate a well‐executed procurement process, NHN is considering market research and supplier dialogue in accordance with FOA §§12‐1 and 12‐2. sig_8f3294994ee46c9f5598.description: UPDATE (23 September 2026): Due to the significant number of questions received, this Special Notice is amended to extend the Request for Information (RFI) submission deadline. This extension allows the Personal Property Activity (PPA) team to review the questions received and provide responses as applicable. The PPA team responses will be posted at a later date prior to the RFI submission deadline. Companies or interested stakeholders who have already submitted an RFI response may revise or update their submission prior to the new deadline. The attached RFI has been amended to reflect the new submission deadline; no other changes have been made to that attachment. UPDATE (28 August 2026): This Special Notice is amended to extend the deadline for clarifying questions and Request for Information (RFI) submissions. Please review below and the attachment for further information on updated timelines. INTRODUCTION The Personal Property Activity (PPA) is conducting market research to understand how integrating vendor systems with a government central platform via an Application Programming Interface (API) will affect household goods (HHG) moving, shipping, transportation, and storage service providers. Accordingly, the PPA invites industry partners and service providers to submit detailed information regarding integration costs, associated software development timelines, standard industry practices, and recommendations for testing and risk mitigation when connecting their internal software systems to a central Government platform. This RFI enables industry stakeholders to provide direct feedback on how this type of integration will impact their current systems and operations, helping to shape future technical requirements and acquisition decisions. This RFI is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation for proposals. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot form a binding contract. The PPA is not under any obligation to pursue any acquisition alternative based on this RFI, and the Government will not compensate respondents for any information received. All submissions will be kept confidential, will become the property of the U.S. Government, and will not be returned. RFI submissions and questions must be submitted via email to all points of contact. sig_8f6b49f9ed8ec5cf26f3.description: Public information and project visibility services include: 1) Preparatory activities aimed at information and raising visibility • Public survey • Communication strategy 2) Project promotion • Design, production and delivery of promotional and informational materials 3) Informing target audiences with the aim of boosting visibility • Implementation of the communication strategy and communication plan • Internet promotion of the project • Organisation and preparation of events 4) Strengthening the Contracting Authority's capacity for project implementation purposes with the aim of project sustainability • Employee training on public speaking • Information and visibility guidelines for post-project activities • Crisis manual for preventive purposes of the Contracting Authority • Public relations aimed at boosting visibility • Relations with all types of publics determined by the communication strategy • Arranging interviews and guest appearances • Responses to enquiries from all types of publics • Press releases 5) Evaluation of implemented activities and preparation of reports in accordance with specified EU procedures • Monitoring and collection of media coverage (press clipping) • Analysis of project media activities. Public information and project visibility activities are mandatory elements of any project financed by EU funds. The purpose of these activities is: • to present the project, project idea, objectives and results; • raising awareness among the public, media and stakeholders regarding the role of the European Union and publishing the fact that the EU is co-financing the project; • to share acquired knowledge and experience, both professional and relating to project management. The subject of procurement is not divided into lots as it represents a functional and technical whole, as determined by the Feasibility Study and the Application to EU funds, and the Tenderer is obliged to offer the subject of procurement in its entirety, meaning the tender must cover all items of the Bill of Quantities. Therefore, the subject of procurement is not divided into lots because the management service relates to a single project financed by European Union funds, which represents a single functional, technical, implementation, financial and administrative entity. Although the project encompasses multiple activities, all activities are mutually linked in terms of deadlines, financing, reporting, risk management and communication with other stakeholders. Splitting the information and visibility service into lots would lead to a division of responsibilities, difficult coordination, potential uncoordinated action by multiple contractors, an increased risk of delays and irregularities, and difficulties in achieving project objectives. Following the above, the tenderer must offer the subject of procurement in its entirety. The subject functions and tasks are interconnected and interdependent, and division into lots would render the provision of the subject services less efficient and complicate the implementation of the contract.

sig_8f6c2b07765d271d9620.description: CBI is implementing a five (5) year project in the organic fresh fruit and vegetables (FFV) sector in Egypt, aimed at strengthening the competitiveness of Egyptian SMEs and increasing sustainable exports to the EU market. To achieve this, the project will support export-ready and exporting SMEs in adopting organic, climate- and water-smart farming practices, improving post-harvest handling, strengthening transparency and traceability, and complying with EU organic standards. In parallel, the project will foster long-term trade partnerships between Egyptian exporters and EU buyers and strengthen the capacities of sector associations, service providers, certification bodies, and other ecosystem actors to create a more transparent, collaborative, and competitive organic FFV sector. CBI wants to contract experts to provide technical support to this project. Two teams of experts will be contracted through a framework agreement for the duration of five (5) years. The estimated total contract value is: €1.000.000 The maximum total contract value is: €1.300.000 For the value per lot see tenderdocument section 2.4 The three roles for this lot have distinct responsibilities, as outlined below; however, they are expected to work together closely to deliver a cohesive and integrated approach: Expert A) has knowledge off the EU organic market, buyers, import and export strategy. The focus is on EU market requirements and how to access the market. Expert B) works closely with expert A on business export coaching of the SMEs in Egypt, making sure follow up is being done. Topics include capacity building around export readiness, business management and organisational development. Focus is on how the SMEs can organise themselves to successfully export. Expert C) has all technical know-how on organic production, post-harvest and food safety. Moreover, has knowledge of Egyptian legislation related to these topics and is familiar with service providers in this field. The main focus is on supporting SMEs in producing organic products that meet EU market requirements. The Tendering Authority has estimated the total contract value for lot 1 at €600.000 (exclusive of Dutch VAT and including, if applicable, all local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees). Maximum total contract value: €750.000,- (exclusive of Dutch VAT and including, if applicable, all local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees); The two roles for this lot have distinct responsibilities, as outlined below; however, they are expected to work together closely to deliver a cohesive and integrated approach: Expert D) Senior Market Systems Development Expert is skilled in market systems development. The focus in on facilitating the development of market-based services supporting the competitiveness and an improved climate- and water smart character of the Egyptian organic FFV sector. Expert E) Local Value Chain and Stakeholder Development Expert works closely with expert D on the implementation of the market systems development approach, making sure follow-up is being done. Topics include stakeholder mapping and management as well as value chain analysis. The focus in on an improved enabling environment supporting the competitiveness and sustainability of the Egyptian organic FFV sector. The Tendering Authority has estimated the total contract value for lot 2 at €400.000 (exclusive of Dutch VAT and including, if applicable, all local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees). Maximum total contract value: €550.000,- (exclusive of Dutch VAT and including, if applicable, all local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees).

sig_8f91fa51e68b5cdac5b8.description: WeST operates 31 schools serving approximately 15,000 pupils and employing approximately 2,300 staff. The estate comprises 23 primary schools and 8 Secondary schools, the largest of which serves approximately 2,500 pupils. Buildings are mixed in age, construction and condition. The aim is to achieve a coherent service operating through one principal interface and authoritative asset hierarchy. Current thinking is that this may be through a single platform or demonstrably integrated solution covering the following requirements: • Compliance: records, recurring schedules, evidence, audit history, alerts and remediation across fire, water hygiene and legionella, asbestos, electrical condition, gas, radon, emergency lighting, lifts and playground equipment. • Assets and maintenance: hierarchical asset register, condition and lifecycle data, planned maintenance, reactive requests, work orders, mobile working and contractor workflows. • Financial and capital planning: budget and purchase-order attribution, expenditure reporting and forecasting, DfE condition-data import, replacement forecasting and structured export. • Reporting: Trust-, school- and asset-level dashboards, drill-down, configurable reports and governance-ready outputs. The solution should support demonstrable compliance assurance; complete evidence and audit retention; end-to-end maintenance and contractor workflows; expenditure traceability; maintenance and replacement forecasting; self-service reporting; mobile working; scalability; and secure data portability. WeST is considering at least 99.5% monthly availability, prioritised support targets, service credits for material failure and acceptance-based implementation payments. Feedback is invited on proportionality and market practice. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_8fb3588b8829110aea21.description: Following on from the Publication of a UK 5 and UK 6 notice the Development Bank of Wales has entered into a contract with suppliers for translation and support services. The Development Bank of Wales (DBW) is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Welsh Government. We therefore have a duty to comply with the Welsh language standards, meaning that Welsh is treated no less favourably than English. All of our English language content requires translation. Services include: Translation: The conversion of written documents into another language as text via human, computer assisted and machine translation solutions. Support Services: Additional services which include documentation formatting and file recreation. The Suppliers shall provide comprehensive Translation and Support services to enable DBW to translate and create supporting materials in Welsh. The Suppliers shall be able to facilitate a broad spectrum of requirements, for each the Suppliers shall utilise experienced individuals who can apply their skills appropriately to the specific requirements of DBW. This will include, but not be limited to: Advisory and instruction documents Correspondence, information leaflets Press releases and briefing documents Corporate publications including our annual report, documents and briefing papers Marketing collateral, subtitles and captions Technical, scientific, legal, financial or any other specialist category ProofreadingThe Suppliers shall ensure that all Visual Translations and Transcriptions shall be completed by accredited Individuals. The Suppliers must fulfil 98% of all translation within the accepted turnaround target set by the buyer. The Suppliers is permitted to use Machine Translation (MT) with the explicit permission from DBW. The Suppliers must ensure that these services are only utilised when clear efficiencies and cost savings can be demonstrated, or at the express request of DBW. Consideration should include: Type of Content Language Pairing Buyer's accuracy requirements Volume of content Turnaround Times Any use of a technological solution shall be implemented securely, ensuring that all software complies with the security standards, Data Security. The Suppliers must also ensure that all data is maintained in accordance with the Data Protection Act 2018 and the General Data Protection Act 2016.The Suppliers agrees to retain any template documents, Translation Memories, or Language Databases and will not charge for duplicate translations during the contract period. The template/Translation Memory will remain the property of the DBW and will be returned at the conclusion of the contract. Any documents and/or data stored within the Supplier's database related to the Services provided will remain the property of DBW. The service may be required at any location within Wales, including instances where Translation must be conducted at DBWs premises for security reasons. In such cases, travel costs will be reimbursed according to DBWs travel policy. The supplier shall ensure that it has a robust quality management process for all translation projects. This process must include checks to ensure that all translations are accurate and consistent with the original source material, and where necessary corrections of any errors in the translated content, such as spelling or grammar errors, formatting, punctuation, or syntax should be made at no additional cost. The Suppliers shall also ensure it has sufficient resources and capabilities to provide proofing services. This service shall be undertaken by an independent, but equally qualified translator, to undertake a final check for any errors to ensure the highest level of quality and accuracy. The Suppliers must ensure that all translators translate only into their native language. In cases where this is not possible, translations must be thoroughly revised by a native English speaker with the necessary subject matter expertise, at no additional cost to DBW. This process ensures the quality and accuracy of the translated content. The Suppliers should have dedicated project management personnel who will provide oversight of DBWs translation project(s), provide updates on the project(s) and serve as a conduit for answering any queries or requests from DBW. Translation: The range of Translator qualifications for this service include, but are not limited to, the below. The Suppliers must be able to provide all of the below upon request within the pricing submitted. Honours degree in the relevant language and/or a degree in Communications or Translation. Membership and/or professional training with Cymdeithas Cyfieithwyr Cymru / Society of Welsh Translators. Mandatory Service Requirements. The Suppliers must deliver an end-to-end service with a seamless process for the end user, utilising its own Individuals, contracted Individuals, and, if necessary, Sub Contractors. The Suppliers Subcontractors value and saving benefits into the service delivery for Buyers and more efficient and innovative ways of working must be shared with the Buyer, with any added value or savings passed onto the Buyer. The Suppliers must maintain a strong focus on continuous improvement by regularly seeking feedback on their service and using this feedback to develop strategies that drive and improve future service delivery. The Suppliers may explore the use of robotic process automation or artificial intelligence (AI) in delivering Services to the Buyer on a case-by-case basis, where it demonstrates additional benefits. If considering any AI solution, the Suppliers must align with the following, including other relevant or updated guidance for the Public Sector throughout the duration of this agreement or Call Off: Data Ethics Framework Understanding Artificial Intelligence Ethics and Safety Generative AI Framework for HMG Code of conduct: As an integral aspect of Framework delivery, Suppliers are required to establish a Code of Conduct that all Individuals engaged in the provision of Services under the Framework must agree to and comply with. Individuals registered with a Regulatory Organization may alternatively adhere to the respective Code of Conduct of that organisation. The Code of Conduct mandates that Individuals: Maintain strict confidentiality, refraining from seeking personal gain through information disclosed during their work. Accept assignments only within their competency, ensuring delivery to the standard required by the Buyer. Refrain from Individuals assigned by the Supplier to complete an assignment from passing on or subcontracting assignments to other Individuals, regardless of their ability to fulfil the requirements. Act impartially and professionally in all actions related to the provision of Language Services under this Framework Contract. Avoid discrimination for or against parties based on grounds such as race, colour, ethnic origin, age, nationality, religion, sex, sexuality, disability, or political allegiance. Disclose any information, including criminal records, that may render them unsuitable for a particular case. Immediately disclose any conflict of interest arising from the end user being known to the Individual, allowing the Buyer to determine whether to proceed with the booking. Disclose any business, financial, family, or other interest, personal or otherwise, relevant to the matter at hand. sig_8fe9987daecc83f52d3b.description: DOTLUMEN S.R.L. is organising the award procedure for the contract for the supply of a Robot Kit in order to equip the research team with the robotic platforms necessary for testing and validating pedestrian autonomous navigation algorithms (PAD AI) in real urban environments. Achieving the research and development objectives targeted in the PABLO project necessarily requires the physical availability of the robotic platforms on which the algorithms will be run, tested and validated, both in simulation environments and in real field conditions. The acquired robotic platforms will advance the technology readiness level (TRL) of the solution from TRL4 (validated in laboratory) to TRL7-8 (system demonstrated in a real operational environment), thereby constituting a necessary and irreplaceable condition for achieving the project performance indicators. The subject of this public procurement contract consists of the supply, DDP transport to the beneficiary's premises and functional verification of the following robotic platforms and associated accessories, within the PABLO project: - Bipedal (humanoid) robot – 1 pcs., with a computing module compatible with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor or equivalent and robotic hands included; - Additional battery for bipedal robot – 1 pcs.; - Quadruped robot – Unitree B2W or equivalent – 2 pcs., with LIDAR included in the standard configuration, minimum protection rating IP67 and additional replacement battery included per unit; - Robotic arm for quadruped robot – Unitree Z1 Pro or equivalent – 1 pcs., with a reach of at least 740 mm; - Technical documentation, SDK/API interfaces and technical knowledge transfer. The acquired robotic platforms will be used exclusively for testing and validation of the PAD AI (Pedestrian Autonomous Driving AI) algorithms developed by the PABLO consortium within the framework of research and development activities. The contract includes the functional verification of each platform upon delivery and the transfer of technical knowledge regarding system operation. - Financing programme: POCIDIF – Programme for Smart Growth, Digitisation and Financial Instruments - Priority: P1 – Supporting and promoting an attractive and competitive RDI ecosystem in Romania - Specific objective: RSO1.1 – Developing and enhancing research and innovation capacities and the adoption of advanced technologies - Project call no.: PCIDIF/159/PCIDIF_P1/OP1/RSO1.1/PCIDIF_A1 - Financing contract no. 390060 / 16.09.2025, SMIS Code: 333334 The robotic platforms, together with the PAD AI software infrastructure, directly contribute to achieving the specific objective of the project and fulfilling the general objective, namely the creation of an efficient, sustainable and automated system of autonomous logistics robots for the urban delivery of products in the final phase (last-mile delivery), capable of reducing operational costs, optimising delivery times and minimising environmental impact.
sig_8fe9987daecc83f52d3b.title: Supply of bipedal and quadrupedal robots, extra batteries for bipedal and quadrupedal robots and a robotic arm for a quadrupedal robot and related accessories, intended for research, development and innovation activities carried out within the project "PABLO - Urban Delivery Autonomous Robots"

sig_8fefea72088ce0135a52.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; instead, any procurement notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible later tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or participating in market dialogue. Responses given to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of expert services to support the management of software assets (licence management). Expert assistance is needed flexibly across several different areas. The main user of HUS's centralised licence management system and product responsible persons for different areas maintain information on the most important software rights in a centralised system (Matrix42, SAM tool). In addition, supplier-specific portals are in use. In the planned procurement, the licence experts of the supplier to be procured would analyse and report quarterly on the current situation regarding agreed software rights (e.g. Microsoft, Oracle, Adobe and IBM manufacturers). They would compare information from different supplier portals with information in the centralised SAM tool, observe deficiencies and provide HUS with recommendations related to optimisation and compliance. The supplier should provide SAM Manager expertise, helping to manage valid software contracts. The supplier should advise on products, contract models, software lifecycles and usage rights. In addition, the supplier is hoped to provide support in building the management model for licence management. It is planned to include as an option in the procurement the entry of licence, cost and contract information into the SAM tool by the supplier instead of HUS personnel. HUS-yhtymä is renewing its ITSM system. In connection with this, the integration of licence management as part of this entity will also be evaluated. External expertise will also be needed for this. The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers available on the market and their service range. The purpose is to clarify service solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and attach to the response a general description/brochure of the service solution you offer for the need described above. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, clarifying questions may be presented to the supplier and/or an opportunity offered to present their solutions in a manner to be notified later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may possibly receive preliminary call for competition documents for comment. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect the supplier's position in a potential tendering procedure. We ask that responses to the request for information and notifications of interest be submitted no later than 20.3.2026 at 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject of the message should state "HUS 090-2026 - Lisenssienhallinnan asiantuntijapalvelut".
