sig_90116dd5159cffb33fea.description: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. In order to provision for a retender of the agreement SLC are undertaking pre-market engagement with regards to the provision of the following: • Requirement A: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service (2026-TR-0109a) • Requirement B: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management (VM) Service (2026-TR-0109b) • Requirement C: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) Service (2026-TR-0109c) • Requirement D: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Service (2026-TR-0109d) • Requirement E: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Retainer Service (2026-TR-0109e) • Requirement F: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture and Engineering Support Services (2026-TR-0109f) SLC is considering an approach to the market to give the suppliers an option to bid for one or ALL of the contractual requirements. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services. Threat Intelligence Managed Service The Supplier shall provide: • Threat Intelligence reporting. • Integration into Microsoft Sentinel. • Indicator of Compromise feeds. • Threat actor intelligence. Operational Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat alerts. • Vulnerability intelligence. • Emerging threat notifications. • Campaign tracking. • Industry specific intelligence. Strategic Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat landscape assessments. • Quarterly threat reports. • Executive intelligence briefings. • Board level threat summaries. • Sector specific threat reporting. Security Operations Support The Supplier shall provide: • Intelligence support during incidents. • Threat hunting support. • Intelligence driven use-case creation. • Intelligence enrichment services. Requirement E Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics & Incident Response Retainer Service The Supplier shall provide a DFIR Retainer available 24x7x365. Cyber Incident Response The Supplier shall provide: • Incident investigation. • Malware analysis. • Threat containment. • Threat eradication. • Recovery support. • Crisis management support. • Regulator support. • On-site support Digital Forensics The Supplier shall provide: • Evidence acquisition. • Chain of custody management. • Endpoint forensics. • Server forensics. • Network forensics. • Cloud forensics. • Forensic reporting. Readiness Services The Supplier shall provide access to: • Tabletop exercises. • Incident simulations. • Executive workshops. • CSIRT training. • Lessons learned reviews. Retained Consultancy The Supplier shall provide specialist support including: • Security strategy input. • Audit support. • Major incident reviews. • Regulatory engagement support. • Ransomware negotiation services. Requirement F Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture & Engineering Support Services The Supplier shall provide specialist Security Architecture and Engineering services on a call-off basis. Security Architecture The Supplier shall provide: • Security architecture reviews. • Security design authority support. • Secure by Design reviews. • Solution security reviews. • Threat modelling. • Architecture governance. • Security requirements definition. • Architectural risk assessments. sig_901b7928824b1bb17f12.description: The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) invites you to participate in an RFI for a Drug Tariff Solution. The solution is required to create the Drug Tariff which the NHSBSA produces on behalf of the Department of Health and Social Care. The NHSBSA are looking to introduce a flexible solution, underpinning business activities, to enable more agility to react to an ever-changing landscape and future proof the creation and accessing of the Drug Tariff by end users (e.g. pharmacists). The NHSBSA Medicines Data Team and specifically the Drug Tariff Team within, are responsible for the processing and assessing of Part IX applications for the listing or request to change a listing of medical devices as well as the creation of the Drug Tariff on a monthly basis on behalf of the Department of Health and Social Care. The Drug Tariff outlines: - what will be paid to pharmacy contractors for NHS services provided either for reimbursement or for remuneration - rules to follow when dispensing - value of the fees and allowances to be paid - drug and appliance prices you will be paid The Drug Tariff is published on the NHSBSA website and can be viewed at Drug Tariff | NHSBSA. The Drug Tariff is supplied by the NHSBSA in an electronic format primarily to pharmacists and GP practices. The requirement is for a solution which produces the Drug Tariff from importing several data sources (from the NHSBSA CDR (Common Drug Reference) database in xml format, Microsoft Word and PDF documents (for NHS Directions) as well as Excel documents for new content). The Drug Tariff will reflect all the information from the previous edition as well as all drug and appliance changes, price changes, additions and deletions applicable in the current month edition. Further details on the Functional and Non-functional requirements and formats (The Drug Tariff Document and the Electronic Drug Tariff) are detailed in Appendix 1. The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) is publishing this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice under Section 17 of the Procurement Act 2023, which sets out the requirement to publish a notice where preliminary market engagement has taken place or is planned. This engagement is being carried out in line with Section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023, which permits contracting authorities to engage with the market for purposes such as understanding supplier capability, shaping the requirement, and supporting the design of the procurement approach. In conducting this engagement, we will meet our overarching duties under the Act. This includes acting in a way that supports the procurement objectives, ensuring non‐discrimination between suppliers, and managing any actual or potential conflicts of interest. These duties apply to all preliminary market engagement activities and underpin how information is shared with suppliers to avoid any unfair advantage. Interested parties must access the RFI documents via https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome (search opportunities using system reference C428345). Lot 1: .

Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tender procedure presented in this information request are preliminary and indicative only. The final schedules will be specified as the preparation progresses. Additional information and instructions for responding to the information request can be found in the appendix. The deadline for responding to the information request is 04.02.2026 at 14:00. The information provided will be treated confidentially. This is an information request, which does not constitute a procurement notice or an invitation to tender. No compensation will be paid to those who have responded to the information request for compiling the information request or participating in any presentation sessions related to the information request. sig_90272ec0d70d8c4bc2a3.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.

sig_9054eede2ea30eefb309.description: Thames Water intends to establish a Framework Agreement to appoint suitably qualified suppliers to deliver site investigation surveys and associated deliverables across its operational area. Thames Water reserves the right to refine the award criteria. Please note that that deadline for asking for access to the PSQ & submitting of the 5 March 2026. Lot 1: Above Ground Surveys. Lot 1 covers delivery of above ground surveys and associated outputs to support feasibility, optioneering, design development, consents and construction planning across Thames Water's operational area. sig_90a14e14039ee7844efb.description: Bournemouth University ("BU" or the "University") is exploring options for the provision of a co-managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) service to enhance and future-proof its cyber security operations capability. The University is seeking market feedback from experienced Managed Security Service Providers to better understand available service models, implementation approaches, commercial arrangements and indicative costs. BU has invested significantly in its internal cyber security capability and Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Entra ID Protection, Security Copilot and related services. The University is now considering how external specialist support could complement its in-house team through a co-managed SOC operating model. The key objectives of a future service are expected to include: - Enhancing monitoring, detection and response capabilities through either 24/7 or out-of-hours SOC coverage. - Improving threat detection, triage, false-positive reduction and incident response effectiveness. - Providing additional specialist expertise, operational resilience and surge capacity during major incidents or periods of heightened risk. - Maintaining and continuously improving detection rules, playbooks, automation and security monitoring capabilities. - Leveraging threat intelligence, sector insight, automation and AI-enabled capabilities to strengthen cyber resilience and operational effectiveness. - Establishing a robust governance, reporting and service management framework with clear responsibilities between BU and the supplier. - Maximising the value of the University's existing Microsoft security investments while minimising the need for additional tooling wherever appropriate. The University wishes to understand how the market can support these objectives, together with the costs, benefits, risks and implementation considerations associated with different service models. Supplier feedback received through this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will help inform the University's future requirements, budget planning and procurement strategy. Lot 1: .
sig_90a14e14039ee7844efb.title: Security Operation Centre

ISR activities may include support related to chemical, nuclear, biological, and radiological (CNBR) elements related to unmanned system. sig_90d54d77ce3d313e963e.description: We are seeking a tenderer for the implementation and cloud operation of an industry-specific solution (planning & workforce management) for grid operators. The software must comprise the following modules: "PLAN" for the iMSys rollout and "PL-ZÄ" for mapping the entire meter lifecycle (gas, water, electricity) including lifecycle management, workflow control and SILKE requirements. Dispatching ("DISPO") must ensure resource-optimised planning and allocation of work orders to internal technicians. For field service, a mobile solution ("MOBIL") is required that supports order processing, time/material recording, documentation and digital signatures. A service provider portal ("DL-PORTAL") must serve external partners in order processing, taking an offline mode into account. Furthermore, interfaces for the synchronisation of master data with the internal SAP S/4 HANA system and for audit-proof archiving in Enaio are mandatory. The package is rounded off by a customer portal ("KU-PORTAL") for appointment management and communication. The aim is an integrated cloud solution for the efficient control of all metering point processes. Lot LOT-0001: Workforce management system - metering. Within the scope of this EU procurement procedure, a candidate is to be found that implements a standard software solution specific to the industry for grid operators (planning tool & workforce management) with the service modules listed below and operates it in a cloud environment. - Service module planning tool ("PLAN") for the rollout of intelligent measuring systems [iMSys] - Service module metering process solution ("PL-ZÄ"), which maps the lifecycle (e.g. procurement, installation, repair, removal & disposal) of all relevant meter types (gas, water & electricity incl. iMSys). In this regard, the following functionalities are included, amongst others: o Tabular overviews of the various data objects (e.g. work orders & meters) o Status scheme for, e.g., work orders and meters o Recording of hours & their subsequent follow-up o Documents & forms along the metering processes o Standard reports o Checklists o Workflow control o Individual configuration of the following processes: - Meter installation - Expert examination - Warehouse management - Meter (dis)connection - Secure supply chain (SILKE) - Service module dispatching ("DISPO"), via which meter work orders can be planned and technicians assigned to them. In this context, the following functionalities should be mapped, amongst others: o Assignment & scheduling of work orders (metering point operation) o Availability of resources o Status, filter, display & export options o Combination of work orders o Individual periodic replacement process - Service module mobile processing ("MOBIL"), which comprises the following functionalities, amongst others: o Processing of work orders o Recording of hours o Booking of vehicles & tools o Processing of checklists, measured values & condition assessments o Documentation of individual activities o Creation of notifications (e.g. faults) o Documentation of photos o Material booking & requirement o Plausibility check & mandatory inputs o Storage & access to documents o Synchronisation with the metering process solution o Processing of digital forms with signature function o Individual metering processes requirements o Work orders & corresponding objects notifications etc. - Service module service provider portal ("DL-PORTAL"), via which assigned meter work orders can be processed by external service providers and which maps the following functionalities, amongst others: o Dispatching of technicians (external technicians by the own company) o Execution of meter work orders o Creation of notifications (e.g. faults) o Documentation of photos o Plausibility check & mandatory inputs o Storage & access to documents o Synchronisation with the metering process solution (incl. consideration of an offline mode) o Processing of digital forms with signature function - Connection to internal SAP S/4 HANA [Core & IS-U] system (service module "SAP-SCHNITT") for the synchronisation of master data (incl. meter data) - Audit-proof archiving in internal Enaio (service module "DMS-SCHNITT") system - Service module customer portal (KU-PORTAL) for e.g. the communication of a customer's requested appointment incl. email communication A decisive quality feature of the solution should be the guarantee of consistently integrated and consistent user guidance across all access levels. This comprises workplace systems (desktop, notebook), native mobile applications (apps) as well as web browser-based portal applications. The tenderer must ensure that a uniform design (look & feel), homogeneous operating logic and process-seamless user guidance are realised in order to maximise acceptance among all users and minimise training efforts. For connection to the contracting authority's existing IT landscape, the software must have open, standardised interfaces (generally REST-based). In particular, interfaces are intended to provide seamless integration into the SAP S/4HANA system (service module "SAP-SCHNITT") and the enaio document management system (Optimal Systems) (service module "DMS-SCHNITT") to guarantee data consistency and automated workflows across system boundaries. Within the scope of implementation, a transition phase with parallel operation of legacy and new systems as well as a migration of existing meter orders is planned. Existing IT systems are to be connected or replaced, provided this is technically and economically sensible. In addition to software provision and implementation, the tenderer must provide software maintenance services for the metering software solution for a further 10 years (120 months) following this.

sig_90e24f5d6d44a5320e46.description: The main objective of the project is to maintain the Roertunnel and Swalmen tunnel in a safe, available, reliable, maintainable and sustainable condition and to ensure that the tunnel technical installations comply with laws and regulations and the most recent standards (National Tunnel Standard), frameworks and guidelines after replacement and renovation. Broadly speaking, the contract comprises designing and subsequently replacing and renovating a number of tunnel technical installations, and implementing multi-year maintenance before, during and after the replacement and renovation. Rijkswaterstaat, as manager, is responsible for the daily operation and performance of the Roertunnel and the Swalmen tunnel in the A73. From 2021 a number of installations in the Roertunnel and Swalmen tunnel have reached the end of their lifespan. The Roertunnel and Swalmen tunnel are part of the Replacement and Renovation (VenR) programme. The VenR task is scheduled in 2023. Broadly speaking, the contract comprises designing and subsequently replacing and/or renovating a number of tunnel technical installations and implementing multi-year maintenance before, during and after the replacement and renovation. .

sig_90f473a48a12a0b28cd3.description: SURF is at an advanced stage in preparing the procurement of service management software (ticketing system) on behalf of the participating organisations. The tender documents and procedures themselves will take place in the short term. Please note! These will be published with TenderNed references other than this prior information notice. After publication, a reference to the actual procurement procedures will be placed in this prior information notice. In broad terms, the intended Contract consists of the delivery of a service management software solution (the System), the implementation of the System at the participating organisations and related services. A service management software solution concerns a software solution with which service-providing processes are streamlined and supported, as a rule also referred to as a “ticketing system”. The System supports the registration and handling of Tickets and reporting on them. Although the contract is broadly similar, there is a distinction in needs among the participating organisations. Some of the participating organisations need a System that can (now or in the future) be expanded to support more processes than just IT service management, for example processes in the context of facility management and HR, while other institutions do not have this need and require a System that primarily supports IT service management. With the intended procurement procedure, SURF wishes to meet the needs of both “groups” of participating organisations. The contract is therefore divided into two procurement procedures that are mutually related. A distinction is made between a System that can support multiple processes, with at least support for ITSM processes and FMIS processes (an “Enterprise Service Management solution (ESM)”) and a solution that only supports ITSM processes (an ITSM solution). Tenderers may choose whether they participate in only one procurement process or both. With regard to the ESM solution, it applies that minimum support must be offered for IT service management processes (ITSM) and facility management processes (FMIS). The support of ITSM processes concerns the minimum purchase by a participating organisation. However, the Tenderer is obliged to also offer the support of FMIS processes in accordance with the requirements and wishes in this context, but the actual support thereof is optional for a participating institution to purchase. The support of other processes, such as, for example, processes in the context of building management, HR, finance, risk management, legal affairs and student affairs, can also optionally be part of this Contract, on the understanding that it must remain service management software. This means, for example, that a participating organisation can purchase service management software to support, for example, HR processes, but that this is not the same as setting up a full HR suite. The ESM procurement procedure will lead to a number of Framework Agreements with the winning Tenderers, after which participating organisations will organise a mini-competition for their individual contract, in which the exact processes that the relevant participating organisation wishes to purchase will be further specified. Award of the Framework Agreements will take place on the basis of the best price-quality ratio. With regard to the ITSM solution, it applies that this will only support IT service management processes (ITSM) and that these contracts do not include support for FMIS processes or other processes. For this procurement need, a Dynamic Purchasing System will be set up by SURF, in which participating organisations will place a further request for their individual contract.

sig_9130e3cbeff18c7174fe.description: Under the Maritime Responsibilities Act (SeeAufgG) within the framework of the maritime surveying service, the BSH is legally obliged to carry out maritime surveying and wreck investigations in the German Baltic and North Seas. Maritime surveying is a core task of the BSH and provides information on seafloor topography and underwater obstacles located thereon through the use of ship-borne hydroacoustic methods. The collected geobasic data form the basis for the production of official nautical charts, traffic safety measures, oceanographic investigations, and coastal protection. To fulfil these tasks, 5 survey vessels and 12 survey boats are deployed at the BSH. For this purpose, the vessels are equipped with precise positioning systems, survey echosounders, sonars, and other special equipment. Surveying data are collected, stored, and evaluated on the survey vessels and boats. Surveying software (VMS) developed within the BSH is used for data acquisition and processing. The VMS previously used at the BSH is to be replaced within the scope of this call for competition. For further information: See description of the service Lot LOT-0000: Replacement procurement of surveying software for BSH ships. See description of the service
sig_9130e3cbeff18c7174fe.title: Replacement procurement of surveying software for the BSH vessels

sig_9144158514e6f36b037d.description: In the course of advancing digitalisation and for the strategic further development of its construction management processes, Netze Duisburg is planning the introduction of an integrated workforce management system for grid construction (WFM BAU). The aim is the sustainable optimisation of operational processes through an end-to-end process review, which enables comprehensive, transparent and efficient planning, control and tracking of internal and external resources across all construction processes. As part of the present EU tender, an applicant is to be found who will introduce and operate a workforce management standard software solution specific to the industry for grid operators, with the service modules listed below. - The service module service provider portal ("DL-PORTAL") comprises the complete digital order processing for external partners. This ranges from the dispositional assignment and provision of all order information through the active processing of orders, checklists and digital forms (incl. signature function) to documentation via photos and plausibility checks. Central synchronisation and access to relevant documents always ensure the current data status. The range of functions also covers the entire grid construction lifecycle and contains specific requirements for the phases of planning, construction execution, surveying, measurement/billing and final project completion. - The service module mobile processing ("MOBIL") enables field service employees to carry out work completely digitally and location-independently. At the core is the processing of orders including associated objects and messages, supplemented by the recording of checklists, measured values, condition assessments as well as individual activities - each supported by plausibility checks and mandatory input controls. The solution also includes direct documentation via photos, access to relevant documents and the processing of digital forms including electronic signature. Comprehensive booking functions cover the recording of working hours, material requirements and the reservation of materials. Reliable synchronisation ensures data consistency at all times. Special functions also support the grid construction-specific processes in the phases of construction execution, surveying as well as measurement and billing directly on site. The service module dispatch ("DISPO") serves the central control of resource-optimised deployment planning. It enables the intelligent combination and assignment of orders taking into account the current availability of personnel. Through comprehensive status, filter and display functions as well as export options, a high level of transparency is created regarding all ongoing measures. The service module also supports the management of qualifications through the planning of necessary training courses and instructions. Specific functions for grid construction ensure that all special requirements of the construction processes are automatically taken into account during scheduling. - The service module grid construction process solution ("PROZESS-BAU"), as the core piece of the solution, maps the entire lifecycle of a construction measure in a continuous, workflow-controlled process. Mapping begins with strategic preliminary planning, coordination and circulation procedures, leads via draft and approval planning and the tender to detailed implementation planning and work preparation. During construction execution, all processes from GIS map-based control via surveying and documentation to the management of checklists, orders and material reservations are integrated. The solution also includes a seamless SAP connection for project creation (WBS elements), asset accounting and the checking of reported working hours records. Finally, the service module covers project completion with measurement, billing and final documentation. Continuous status schemes, standardised reports and flexible tabular overviews ensure full transparency and controllability of all project data at all times.
sig_9144158514e6f36b037d.title: Workforcemanagementsystem - Netzbau (WFM BAU)

sig_9146bb9df139c693066c.description: Data collection for the Road and Motorway Network Information System of the Czech Republic (ISSDS ČR) is organised by the Road Databank Department and NDIC Ostrava. This involves ongoing and uninterrupted data collection for the construction activity register (RSČ), road inventory description (PPK), junction description (PK) and pavement structural layers (KV). The suppliers of this service also provide methodological assistance to individual road asset managers (ŘSD ČR Administration and Maintenance Depots, district and regional road authorities), control of data for the road inventory description, junction description, pavement structural layers and maintenance of their up-to-date status. The supply of requested data is a highly specialised activity that takes place simultaneously over time in individual regions, which is why it is not ideal to carry it out from a single centre. The activity also requires detailed knowledge of the monitored roads in the given region, systematic work, long-term training, regular training, experience in data collection and, last but not least, special equipment and modification of the measuring vehicle. The data from the aforementioned activities will be used, among other things, for the planned and gradually implemented pavement management system (SHV). The Czech Republic is divided into 7 reporting regions as follows: 1. Central Bohemia Region. 2. South Bohemia Region. 3. West Bohemia Region 4. North Bohemia Region. 5. East Bohemia Region. 6. South Moravia Region. 7. North Moravia Region. Out of these 7 reporting regions, 5 regions will be put out to tender this year, where existing contracts expire in 2023: 1. Central Bohemia Region. 2. The object of the project is the utilisation of the latest information technologies and, in order to respond with speed, security and reliability to the needs, new functionalities and services of the Directorate for the Management of the National Archive of Monuments and of the Ministry of Culture in general through the Archaeological Cadastre. The implementation of the project will follow best practices and innovative technologies, always guided by the comprehensive quantitative and qualitative delivery of the cultural reserve and its promotion on the internet, as well as the provision of electronic services to all interested citizens, investors and public and private sector bodies. Within the framework of the project, the upgrade of the logistics infrastructure and software applications of the Integrated Information System (hereinafter IIS) of the Archaeological Cadastre will be implemented. The new functionalities to be developed will extend the capacity of the Archaeological Cadastre so that it is able to meet the additional requirements in terms of capacity, speed, workload and user traffic. The upgrade will include: a. Adaptation of the database to Cloud Native architecture, b. Upgrade and enrichment of the IIS of the Archaeological Cadastre information system with new functionalities, c. Upgrade and enrichment of the Web Portal of the Archaeological Cadastre information system with new functionalities, d. Upgrade and extension of the architecture of the geospatial software (GIS) and the geospatial database. The Contractor shall, as a minimum, be required to implement within the framework of the project: • Supply of all necessary licences covering all required needs of the existing information systems of the Archaeological Cadastre. • Upgrade of existing ARCGIS licences and addition of new Geographic Information System software licences • Application development / optimisation of existing ones and new functionalities • Upgrade of the AK web portal and addition of new functions and an automatic translation tool. • Upgrade of procedures and security level, with the creation and implementation of a new Security Policy. • Implementation of new and integrated interoperability services • Training services The individual objectives of the project are: • The digital transformation and upgrading of the Archaeological Cadastre with modern and innovative information technologies resulting in the improvement of its efficiency and effectiveness, so as to provide a modern environment for the digital recording and documentation of all archaeological and architectural treasures of the country's immovable monuments. • Supporting the Directorate for the Management of the National Archive of Monuments (DDEAM) to design and reform its procedures in accordance with its priorities, taking into account the initial conditions and expected increasing requirements at the stage of maturity of the Archaeological Cadastre, its operational phase, and the continuous enrichment and expansion of its content and services. • Supporting the DDEAM so that, through a modern technological environment, it can define and apply appropriate procedures and methodologies taking into account good practices and lessons learned from its operation to date in order to address the increasing needs in the smooth design and execution of public works, as well as the development of investments in a Country. • The contribution of the Archaeological Cadastre and the Ministry of Culture and Sports to the broader effort to complete the National Cadastre, to create a Land Bank and other related management and exploitation platforms for public property. sig_91ab19fa1dda99143b0d.description: In November 2023, Network Rail brought its entire Occupational Health (OH) service in‐house. The service now operates nationally across 22 clinics, supported by remote and virtual delivery models, and provides health assessments, surveillance, management referrals and safety‐critical medicals for approximately 42,000 employees. This includes statutory obligations under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and the Transport and Works Act 1992, making the OH function central to compliance, governance and operational safety. The organisation’s Health Sustainability Strategy reinforces a shift towards evidence‐based health management, stronger governance, and better use of high‐quality data. An Occupational Health IT system is therefore fundamental to delivering a consistent, efficient and forward‐looking service. The system must not only support the day‐to‐day administration of clinical activity but also enhance the quality, governance and insight required from a national, safety‐critical operation. Network Rail require an Occupational Health system to build a detailed and accurate picture of workforce health, enabling richer understanding of demographics, emerging risks and preventive opportunities. It will generate robust management information and high‐quality OH data that supports statutory reporting, internal assurance and workforce analytics, aligning with Network Rail’s broader ambition to treat health as a core business outcome. Intelligent appointment and diary management will help reduce cancellations and no‐shows, ensuring clinics run efficiently and clinical time is maximised. Consistent national data sets will provide a clear view of health and wellbeing trends across all regions, reinforcing the need for standardisation and comparability across the organisation. In summary, the future OH IT system must: ⦁ Support a national Occupational Health service covering approximately 42,000 employees across 22 clinics, alongside remote and virtual delivery. ⦁ Accommodate a hybrid workforce of clinical and non‐clinical users involved in safety‐critical and statutory health activity. ⦁ Manage high‐volume, regulated workflows, including management referrals, health surveillance, fitness‐for‐work assessments and other statutory medicals. ⦁ Provide strong auditability, governance and management insight, enabling consistent assurance and evidence‐based decision‐making. Lot 1: .
sig_91ab19fa1dda99143b0d.title: Provision of Occupational Health IT System

sig_91cf58e13eee2fba2da8.description: The subject of the contract is the supply and integration of a functional technological unit consisting of new goods and their installation; these are analysers for monitoring ambient air pollutants, calibration and support equipment, communication interfaces, data transmission and integration into the central collection and database system in the National Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Network (hereinafter referred to as the "NMSKO"), with the expansion of the system with equipment for measuring new pollutants such as NH3, particulate matter PM1, Black Carbon particles, ultra-fine particles resulting from the requirements of the implementation of the new directive: DIRECTIVE OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL (EU) 2024/2881 of 23 October 2024 on ambient air quality and cleaner air in Europe and, at the same time, the requirements of STN EN ISO/IEC 17025 and Decree No. 250/2023 Coll. The subject of the contract was determined on the basis of a review of pollutant monitoring in the NMSKO carried out by the European Environment Agency (hereinafter referred to as the "EEA") and the implementation of the new directive requirement to ensure compliance with the requirement for pollutant monitoring, transmission and processing of measured data. The subject of the contract will integrate the technological unit into the accredited system of ambient air pollutant quality monitoring within the NMSKO using reference and alternative methods, ensure activities for improving the operation of the NMSKO, performance of metrological checks and tests, sampling for analyses of ambient air and atmospheric precipitation samples, calibration of NMSKO analysers, performance of monitoring station quality system checks, performance of comparative measurements of NMSKO monitoring stations, required data yield of measured data, informing the general public about the level of air pollution in accordance with the requirements of Act No. 146/2023 Coll. of 17 February 2023 on air protection and amending certain acts. At the same time, the measured results serve as a basis for fulfilling obligations related to the smog warning system in accordance with the requirements of valid legislation, fully respecting the established system of accredited measurements in the NMSKO in accordance with the requirements of standard STN EN ISO/IEC 17025 including the established quality system and the requirements of standard STN/EN 17255 focused on the requirements of the collection system, furthermore the requirements of Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council (EU) 2024/2881 of 23 October 2024 on ambient air quality and cleaner air in Europe transposed into Act No. 146/2023 Coll. of 17 February 2023 on air protection and amending certain acts and Decree No. 250/2023 Coll. Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council (EU) 2024/2881 of 23 October 2024 on ambient air quality and cleaner air in Europe in Annex IV defines individual reference methods for assessing ambient air concentrations by reference to the description in individual standards as follows: the reference method for measurements of nitrogen dioxide and oxides of nitrogen in ambient air is described in standard EN 14211, the reference method for measurements of sulphur dioxide in ambient air is described in standard EN 14212, the reference method for measurements of ozone in ambient air is described in standard EN 14625 and the reference method for measurements of carbon monoxide in ambient air is described in standard EN 14626. The stated legislation is legally binding for the contracting authority. The contracting authority's accreditation certificate is given in Annex No. 5 of the Tender Documents. The defined technological functional unit must ensure the automation of processes within the NMSKO and must be fully compatible with the existing system operated within the monitoring network. The newly supplied technological unit must constitute a systemic functional superstructure of the current infrastructure and be in full compliance with the requirements of standards STN EN ISO/IEC 17025, STN EN 17255 and the established NMSKO quality system, and the aforementioned related valid legislation. Operations must be governed by the requirements of binding regulations for established accredited measurements in the NMSKO. Ensuring process continuity is crucial for the acceptability and representativeness of measurement results published in hourly time slots on the contracting authority's website and to the EEA. Any incompatibility with established quality control procedures would lead to the degradation of measured data and the loss of the NMSKO's accreditation status. The subject of the contract therefore constitutes a single functional technological unit, which includes: • air quality analysers, their installation and commissioning; • calibration and support equipment, their installation and commissioning; • communication interfaces, their installation and commissioning; • data transmission and integration into the central collection and database system. Further information on individual items as well as the overall technological unit and related services of the technological functional unit is given in Chapter (B) Description and Pricing of the Subject of the Contract.

sig_923644f930e86e97f83c.description: Istekki Oy (hereinafter also the Contracting Authority) invited tenders for a risk and hazard management and service provider monitoring system in section 1 of this call for tenders, and for a risk management system in section 2 for the use of the Contracting Authority and its End Customers. The requirements for the sections were defined in more detail in the appendices to the call for tenders. The systems had to meet the requirements described in the call for tenders and its appendices. The tenderer was able to submit a tender for both sections or only one. Parallel tenders were not permitted. Istekki Oy (hereinafter also the Contracting Authority) requested tenders for the implementation of a risk and hazard management and service provider monitoring system (hereinafter the "System") and ongoing maintenance services. The objective was to obtain one comprehensive supplier to provide the service for the Contracting Authority's needs. The system had to be a user-friendly SaaS system and be commissioned within 8 months of the signing of the contract, but no later than during the year 2026. The system had to be off-the-shelf software that has been proven to be functional and reliable based on previous similar continuous customer deliveries, and it must function seamlessly as part of the operating processes of the customers implementing it.; Istekki Oy (hereinafter also the Contracting Authority) requested tenders for the procurement of a comprehensive risk management system and its maintenance services. The subject of the procurement was a risk management system and its interfaces with other systems, a delivery project (including, among other things, migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support service, separately ordered expert services, and customer service. Further development can be carried out on the system to be procured during the contract period. The procurement is carried out as one entity, and one comprehensive supplier was sought for the System. The system had to be delivered as a SaaS service. The system to be procured had to be a solution focusing on risk management that supports the company's overall risk management and its various process stages. The commissioning of the system is planned to start no later than 1.9.2026. The system had to be off-the-shelf software with client-specific customisation. The Contracting Authority's risk management is based on the international ISO 31000 standard. Risks refer to both threats and opportunities, and the risk management process consists of risk identification, assessment, and management, as well as compliance assessment. The system must support this entity by offering versatile functions for different purposes so that risk management can be implemented comprehensively and systematically. As only one tender was received for the call for tenders, which was contrary to the call for tenders, Istekki Oy had to cancel the tendering process.
sig_923644f930e86e97f83c.title: Procurement of a risk and hazard management and service provider monitoring system and a risk management system

sig_92a836a202ab5c950638.description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) is exploring tools to support employees in learning their second official language (English or French) in response to evolving operational and legislative requirements. The modernization of the Official Languages Act has reinforced the importance of maintaining and strengthening bilingual capacity across the organization to ensure compliance with the Agency's obligations to serve Canadians and support employees in the official language of their choice. Investing in effective and accessible second-language learning solutions will help the CRA maintain its bilingual capacity, support succession planning, and continue providing high-quality services in both official languages. As a result, the CRA is assessing the feasibility of implementing a scalable, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered language learning solution aligned with CRA corporate requirements and Government of Canada requirements. Responding to this Request for Information (RFI) is not a prerequisite to being eligible to bid on any subsequent solicitation. Any subsequent solicitation will be advertised on the Government Electronic Tendering Service commonly referred to as CanadaBuys. This RFI is not to be construed as a solicitation for tenders or proposals. No contract or other form of commitment will be entered into based on responses to this RFI. This RFI is not authorization by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) to undertake any work that would result in costs to the CRA. RFI Closing Date Responses must be received on or before October 22, 2026, no later than 14:00 EDT. All responses to this Request for Information must be directed in writing and submitted by email to: Contracting Authority: Charles Safarian E-mail: charles.safarian@cra-arc.gc.ca It is recommended that all electronic submissions contain a read receipt option to confirm that the email was received. Respondents are requested to provide a contact name, email address and telephone number when submitting their response. Please refer to the solicitation documents for further information and instructions regarding this opportunity.
sig_92a836a202ab5c950638.title: AI-POWERED OFFICIAL LANGUAGES LEARNING SOLUTION

sig_92b0afeeb9d68b38aa73.description: In the TSG, the Healthcare Institute, in collaboration with the parties involved, will examine for each new medicinal product based on a risk assessment whether an assessment is necessary, what kind of assessment that should be, and who will carry it out. This collaboration must be supported with the help of an information management system (IMS). By collecting information in one place to which the various parties have access, risk-based working can be carried out and communication about this can be supported, as described in the TSG. The information for risk-based working is collected from the Horizon Scan and possibly other sources. Initially, the IMS must make the new intake process according to the TSG practically feasible; this legislation comes into effect on 1 January 2028. In the further development phase, further support for the current situation of the medicinal product assessment process (organisational, procedural, data and functional context) as well as elements yet to be developed can be included in the IMS.

sig_92ba1e9aafe1f2ebf54e.description: SUBJECT OF THE CONTRACT The purpose of the contract is the drawing up of plans, studies and documents necessary for the execution of the infrastructure works for the economic activity park known as "Wérihet" in Liège, as well as the management, control and supervision of these works. The site known as "Wérihet" is a site of approximately thirty hectares located at the northern entrance to the city of Liège, directly bordering the E25 and E42 motorways, and directly accessible via the Wandre interchange. These are developable plots of land, predominantly designated as industrial zones in the sector plan. By decision of the city of Liège and AIDE in 1953, the site must be backfilled prior to any occupation, so as to avoid the need for permanent dewatering of the water. This prior backfilling stage is partially completed and also forms part of the future infrastructure works contract. The Zone Recognition file was drawn up and submitted by Spi in July 2015 to DGO6 - Directorate-General for Economy. The acknowledgement of receipt was issued in April 2016 by DEPA (Directorate for the Equipment of Activity Parks). The ministerial decree relating to the adoption of the perimeter for the Recognition of the Economic Activity Zone "Wandre Wérihet" was issued on 7 May 2019. BUDGET The infrastructure and implementation works for the economic activity park are estimated at 11 500 000 EUR including VAT. SKILLS The tenderer must propose a tender including all of the following skills: - Engineer with experience in the design of infrastructure related to roads, utility providers, drainage systems, electromechanical equipment, etc.; - Engineer with experience in the design of a district heating network; - Landscape architect; - Mobility expert; - Land surveyor; - Health and safety coordinator. The mission includes a coordination mission for the various participants listed above and any external participants necessary to successfully complete the mission entrusted to them. Details of the project author's missions (engineer, architecture, landscape architect, etc.) are given in Chapter III "Description of technical requirements". This contract comprises three (3) firm tranches and two (2) conditional tranches: Tranche 1 (firm) – Economic Activity Park Infrastructure: - Complete study and design mission for roads and technical infrastructure relating to the creation of the Economic Activity Park, including backfilling as well as the specific drainage network (in particular storm basin, pipe jacking and network for discharging runoff water into the Meuse); - The mission also includes the drawing up of permit and award files, coordination, planning, management, control, supervision and health and safety coordination (CPV 71317210-8) of the works; - The mission also includes the compilation of all project, execution and completion documents, including those originating from concessionaires and/or utility providers. Tranche 2 (firm) – District Heating Network Feasibility: - Complete feasibility study mission for a district heating network intended for future investors in the Economic Activity Park and/or located within the perimeter of the Recognition of the Economic Activity Zone. Tranche 3 (firm) – Water Infrastructure: - Complete study and design mission for the water distribution network; - The mission also includes coordination, planning, management, control and health and safety coordination (CPV 71317210-8) of the works; - The works supervision mission is carried out by the distribution company. Tranche 4 (conditional) – Infrastructure on the SPW-MI National Road: - Complete mobility study mission; - Complete study and design mission for access points and exits to the Economic Activity Park, namely the creation of a signal-controlled intersection or a roundabout on the SPW-MI National Road adjacent to the Wandre bridge interchange, as well as a direct exit connection to the E25 and E40 motorways; - Complete study and design mission for technical equipment (cf. public lighting and signage); - The mission also includes the drawing up of permit and award files, coordination, planning, management, control and health and safety coordination (CPV 71317210-8) of the works; - The works supervision mission is carried out by the SPW-MI. This tranche 4 will be ordered if the SPW-MI decides not to carry out the studies through its own design office. Tranche 5 (conditional) – District Heating Network Infrastructure: - Complete study and design mission for a district heating network; - The mission also includes the drawing up of permit and award files, coordination, planning, management, control, supervision and health and safety coordination (CPV 71317210-8) of the works. This tranche 5 will be ordered depending on the results of the study (feasibility, budget, internal decision, etc.) provided for in tranche 2 of this contract.

sig_92d4574971aba33d56ff.description: NOW IS YOUR CHANCE TO INFLUENCE THE PROCUREMENT DURING THE MARKET CONSULTATION PHASE! The main applicant and administrator of the project is the Urban Environment Division of the City of Lappeenranta. In addition to the City of Lappeenranta, the project includes the cities of Turku, Vaasa, Kouvola, Oulu, Espoo, Kokkola, Tampere, Järvenpää and Helsinki. For the planning of this AI project, the municipalities have invited the Ministry of the Environment, Senate Properties, the Association of Finnish Cities and Municipalities (AFCM), universities, and other Finnish, European and international public organisations to participate in stakeholder cooperation. The main driving force behind the need for a new AI service is the national need for the use of data analysis models arising from the reform of the Building Act and Decree. In Finland, the new Building Act was adopted by the Parliament in February 2023. With this market survey, the Municipalities AI development project is identifying markets and potential suppliers to identify an AI service for automatic inspection and building control use cases for buildings, built environment and Geographic information. For a more detailed description of the requirements of the solution sought, please refer to the 'Description of the Acquisition' section of this notice. This notice does not call for tenders or requests for participation. Company-specific interviews via teams will be held via Teams during October – November 2026. The organizer reserves the right to record the event if needed. For companies who are interested in participating in the interviews and market dialogue please provide your answers to given pre-questions by latest by October 07, 2026. The contracting entity reserves the possibility of inviting the companies that have expressed interest to present their products or solutions at company-specific events and to send a possible draft invitation to tender for comments to interested companies before the possible publication of the actual contract notice or tender. The aim is to organize possible company-specific presentation events during October 2026 (in principle remotely). The timetables and other information provided in this notice, such as the planned market dialogue, are preliminary and indicative and may change as the preparation of the notification progresses. The information provided is not binding on the contracting entity. Failure to respond to the market survey will not prevent a supplier from participating in a potential tender and will not affect the supplier's position in the actual tender. This notice does not call for tenders or requests for participation. The market survey is accompanied by an invitation to a market survey, where the contracting entity can conduct a market dialogue with the operators that have expressed an interest. The outcome of this market survey will be used by the municipalities and stakeholders in Finland, such as ministries, to prepare a separate development project and a competitive tendering process for the procurement of suitable products according to the market. We warmly invite interested companies to participate in the market dialogue!
sig_92d4574971aba33d56ff.title: Market Dialogue – AI-Based Analysis of Building Permit and Geographic information use cases

In the event that a contractor is selected who is refused authorisation by the manufacturer, this may lead to a delay in the performance of the public contract, as well as to its termination. According to the conclusions of the Supreme Administrative Court ,,the requirement for authorisation in itself is not restrictive, insofar as it is a guarantee of the quality and reliability of the activity carried out. In standard commercial practice, authorisation takes place on the basis of a contract, which may be directly with the manufacturer or with another economic entity authorised to grant authorisation on behalf of the manufacturer‘‘. (Decision No 10859 of 27.10.2021 of the Supreme Administrative Court under administrative case No 6546/2021 of the VIIth Division). In the documentation, the condition for authorisation is set out broadly, i.e., it is not restricted solely to the manufacturer, but also to any official representative thereof. General authorisation is required, rather than for a specific procedure, and an opportunity is provided for every interested tenderer – partner, regardless of whether they are a Bulgarian or foreign entity, to submit a bid, with the possibility provided to prove the above-mentioned circumstance both with an authorisation letter and with any other equivalent document that certifies compliance with the established requirement.

sig_933b0068f3175736e62a.description: This notice does not commence a competitive tendering process. For the detailed requirements and relevant documentation, please see the Call for Competition, published on OJEU ref 6868206 https://www.etenders.gov.ie/epps/cft/viewTenders.do?resourceId=6868206 EirGrid and SONI are currently developing the Future Arrangements of System Services (FASS) which includes the development and implementation of a new set of arrangements to replace the existing System Services procurement mechanism (DS3 System Services (DS3)). The existing DS3 arrangements were designed to meet the 2020 renewable targets of 40% RES-E and are not sufficient for Ireland and Northern Ireland to achieve targets of 80% renewable generation by 2030. The new set of arrangements aim to drive investment in an efficient manner to ensure the all-island power system can continue to be operated safely and securely. In April 2022 the SEM Committee (SEMC) published its High-Level Design for the SSFA as set out in SEM-22-012. EirGrid and SONI, in their respective capacities as Transmission System Operator in Ireland and Northern Ireland respectively are supporting the SEMC in the development of its High-Level Design (HLD) into an implementable solution. The Regulatory Authorities (RAs) have requested the TSOs to implement these arrangements to achieve the RES-E targets and to ensure compliance with the relevant aspects of European legislation such as the European Balancing Guidelines (EBGL) and the Clean Energy Package. On 8th December 2023, the SEMC released a decision paper on the Detailed Design and Implementation of Future Arrangements of System Services (SEM-23-103). As set out in the decision paper, the RAs have proposed to proceed with the Day Ahead System Services Auction (DASSA). The decision paper sets out a number of workstreams for the TSOs to commence, which includes a secondary market via a central platform where market participants can bilaterally trade their DASSA positions on a half hourly basis. The DASSA is scheduled to go live from May 2027. Elements of the DASSA design require collateral coverage to manage credit risk to the TSOs. These elements include but are not limited to secondary trading, any performance related payments due to the TSOs (e.g. DASSA compensation payments) and resettlement. The TSOs require a third-party provider to assume the credit risk for these FASS Collateral Arrangements and host the requirements outlined in the scope of requirements section below. The Opportunity EirGrid plc intends to establish a single supplier framework. The supplier will assume and manage credit risk for the FASS Collateral Arrangements on behalf of EirGrid plc and SONI Limited. The Framework Agreement will encompass further credit management related services agreed during negotiations. EirGrid plc is acting as lead contracting authority and its group company, SONI Limited will benefit from services under the Framework. As such and in compliance with SONI Limited’s obligations under the Procurement Act 2023 (the “Act”), this notice is published to advertise the opportunity but does not commence a competitive tendering procedure for the purposes of the Act. The procurement remains governed by Council Directive 2014/25/EU as transposed into Irish law by the European Union Award of Contracts by Utility Undertakings) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 286 of 2016) (the “Regulations”), will be run in compliance with those Regulations, pursuant to OJEU Notice ref: 6868206, but will also be managed in compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 in so far as possible, to discharge SONI Limited’s obligations under the Act. Lot 1: .
sig_933b0068f3175736e62a.title: ENQEIR983 FASS Credit Management Services

sig_93617c846247c2fd780b.description: Provision and operation of an online voting product for conducting the social security election 2029 as a hybrid primary election of Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund, in all its components (such as cloud solution, online voting software, technical system environment for operation - incl. buildings or premises -, full service, project support, etc.) Lot LOT-0000: Online voting product social security election 2029. Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund intends to procure an online voting product for conducting the social security election 2029 as a - for the first time - hybrid primary election of Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund. The online voting product must enable IT-secure, legally compliant, punctual, traceable, accessible and data protection-compliant electronic voting and its evaluation. In addition, the integration of online voting into the postal voting to be carried out additionally must be ensured. The scope of services includes the provision and operation of a full-service online voting product in all its components (such as cloud solution, online voting software, technical system environment for operation, full service, project support, etc.) that are necessary to achieve the objective. Contract start: 01.07.2027 or upon contract award Contract end: 31.03.2030, provided no election challenge action is filed If the election result is challenged, the duration of the contract may be extended monthly until the conclusion of the appeal proceedings. Note: The Retirement Provision Commission submitted a total of 33 recommendations in June 2026 to ensure long-term retirement provision in Germany. The Federal Government has announced its intention to implement the recommendations as quickly and completely as possible. Based on current knowledge, implementation could fall within the tender/service phase and lead to up to 75 million eligible voters being entitled to electronic (or postal) voting with the contracting authority. In this case, it must be ensured that the scope of services is adjusted accordingly (cf. price sheet, Appendix 3 to the EVB-IT System Contract).

sig_9371096c9f5bf40a2337.description: 4846/AMRC/ATR/JS/25 – Autonomous Tool Room Cell (Phase 1) The University of Sheffield wishes to invite tenders for an 'Autonomous Tool Room Cell' on behalf of the Advanced Manufacturing Research Centre, Castings Group at Catcliffe, South Yorkshire. Scope of Requirement The AMRC has launched an innovation challenge to develop a digital framework to explore autonomy in subtractive manufacturing process planning. This focuses on industrial software interoperability and the improvement of modelling predictions through real-time data. The innovation challenge to develop a reconfigurable tended subtractive manufacturing cell initially centres around a three-axis mill CNC. A phased investment approach is applied to the innovation challenge, within Phase One, an automation cell (herein referred to as the ‘Autonomous Tool Room (ATR) Cell’ and/or “Cell”) will be purchased. This will include a seven-axis robot with a range of part tending routes, tool management options, representing current affordable and accessible physical automation solutions. Within Phase One, the ‘Cell’ will be installed on Factory of the Future (FoF) shopfloor requiring the rerouting of services, both physical such as air and power and also data connectivity, including sustainability focused monitoring solutions. In the coming years further investment will be made around the ‘Cell’ to build capability in the autonomy space. This will provide an AMRC sandpit to physically demonstrate technologies for autonomy in tool room/job shop activities which represents a significant part of the UK supply chain. This work will focus on key strategic priority areas around workforce development, supply chains and SME support. To this end the ‘Cell’ should be designed with a fundamentally modular architecture which allows for future adaptation and expansion (see section G4). The Vision To create a secure, traceable, and interoperable end-to-end digitally connected manufacturing system. This system will integrate human knowledge, real-time process data, and advanced virtual models to optimise subtractive process planning, remove the mundane and time wasteful processes, improve machining performance, automate decision making and support certification of parts by analysis in order to reduce time-to-market and address the skills shortage in the workforce of the future. This is a cross AMRC proposal including The Machining Group (TMG), Integrated Manufacturing Group (IMG), AMRC North West, and AMRC Metrology. This is a multi-phased, multi-year project which may be procured over the coming years. General Specification Key Objectives of the ‘Autonomous Tool Room (ATR) Cell’ -Implement an end-to-end digitally connected manufacturing system from CAD to final part inspection. -Implement a cyber-secure digital infrastructure to protect sensitive manufacturing data during real-time operations and in cloud environments. -Implement cloud and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure to manage and analyse large datasets, with 5G technology ensuring fast, seamless communication between systems. -Develop an integrated and automated CAD/CAM environment which is digitally connected to the shop floor. -Utilise the latest Generative AI and Digital Twin systems for real-time process improvement, model validation and to eliminate trial-and-error on both the shop floor and in the CAM office. -Deploy multi-model machine tool connectivity to integrate supply chain data and monitor machine and process performance. -Close the loop between metrology and the machining process by integrating metrology equipment within the ‘Cell’. For the avoidance of doubt, integration of metrology equipment is outside the scope of this tender (see G4: a). This tender is for the supply, installation, commissioning, integration, and support over the product lifetime of an autonomous cell playing a key part of the Autonomous Tool Room (ATR) vision. ATR is a key initiative within the AMRC and forms one of their Subtractive Manufacturing Innovation Challenges to develop the interconnected shop floor of the future. This tender specifically addresses Phase One of the ATR vision, the machining cell (the “Cell”) which focuses on enabling physical automation and autonomy. The ‘Cell’, destined for the AMRC Factory of the Future shopfloor in Sheffield, will ultimately integrate multiple machine tools (note that within Phase One, the scope of this tender, only one machine tool is considered*), a multi-axis robot and rail for diverse functionalities such as part/vice/pallet and tool loading, AMRC owned hardware integration (Alternative vices, Dynamometers, etc.), autonomous guided vehicle (AGV) / autonomous mobile robot (AMR) integration (example system Iconsys IAM-R), safety cell, and a metrology zone, all overseen by a central controller station. *For the avoidance of doubt it is envisaged that the machine tool will be a new ‘DNM6700’ (https://www.millscnc.co.uk/product/dnm-6700/) and should be on site at the AMRC’s Factory of the Future by the end of April 2026. This will be confirmed for certain as soon as possible. Phase One will consider the integration of a single machine tool (Machine Tool 1) to be accessed from the right-hand side by the robotic arm alongside part/vice/pallet and tool loading. The ATR Cell In summary the ATR Cell will be comprised of various pieces of Equipment, and Cell Controller Software and Cell Controller Station (HMI) as detailed below:- Equipment The proposed ‘Cell’ must have the capability to move part/vice/pallet and tooling between key ‘Cell’ elements which include:- -Machine Tool 1 (DNM6700) – sourced seprately from this tender -Multi-Axis Robot on a Rail -Part Storage -Tool Storage -Pallet Storage -Pallet In/Out -Vice Storage -Gripper Storage; and -Safety Cell (including industrial safety fence, sensors, light curtains etc.) The ‘Cell’ must be designed to enable expansion in later phases to integrate an additional machine tool (Machine Tool 2), an AGV / AMR, metrology equipment, and other capabilities as the scope of the ‘Cell’ increases. To this end flexibility and adaptability are key capabilities that are required within this tender as this hardware will form the backbone of a multi-year investment / development programme. Please see section G4. Tender Process and Documentation: This procurement is an open procedure conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 The ITT can be downloaded by registering and expressing your interest on the University`s e-tendering system https://in-tendhost.co.uk/Sheffield If you have any questions or comments in relation to this tender they must be submitted via the In-tend System, this can be accessed at https://in-tendhost.co.uk/Sheffield Completed tenders must be returned through the same e-tendering system. Closing date for receipt of tenders: Monday 1st December 2025 at 12:00 noon (UK time) Lot 1: .

sig_938748fd3c788d8d56ea.description: Decree 14 2022, of 5 May, establishing the organic structure of the Ministry of Education, attributes, in its article 8 section a), to the Directorate-General for Innovation and Teacher Training, competence over the design, coordination and development of educational innovation programmes and plans. The Reading Plan of the Ministry of Education has as its main objective “to promote the reading habit among our schoolchildren and develop their reading comprehension capacity using different supports, formats and textual typologies, as well as their writing and oral communication, to favour the acquisition of media and information literacy, proper to this new knowledge society”. Among the specific objectives is “to encourage the development of innovative initiatives for the application of ICT to the world of books and reading, writing and oral communication”. Therefore, for several academic years, the Ministry of Education has offered educational centres the possibility of improving digital literacy and reading as a complement to the work carried out in the classroom, as an instrument to support curriculum development that has a very positive impact on the quality of teaching, which becomes an indicator of the quality of the educational centre, which must adapt to current needs, having the availability of a library in which books and educational materials can be consulted in various supports and formats, including those found on the network. Because the Ministry of Education lacks adequate and sufficient personal and material resources to execute the services intended to be contracted, it is necessary to open the tender for a digital literacy and reading service, through a personalised web platform in SaaS (Software as a Service) mode that allows students and teachers of public primary, secondary and high school centres to access digital content, with the purpose of jointly creating a literary work between the author and their readers (students) in order to stimulate the student's taste for reading as well as stimulate and improve written expression, all within a digital environment adapted to the variety of formats used by the current knowledge society. The digital books created through the platform will become part of a permanent network consultation library.
sig_938748fd3c788d8d56ea.title: School digital literacy and reading service for public educational centres of the Community of Castile and León via a platform (courses 2026-2027 and 2027-2028)
