sig_93a14c3114ecf7058c54.description: We kindly request you to submit your response to the request for information regarding the procurement of a pedigree tree drawing software. We aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation for services related to the systems, products potentially related to the use of the system, contract terms, and commercial terms such as pricing. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of any potential tendering process. This is a request for information intended to gather information for the planning of a future procurement. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the procurement in the form described herein. See attachment: "619264_Tietopyyntö_Sukupuunpiirto-ohjelma". The subject of the procurement is a pedigree tree drawing software solution that supports the collection, management, and visualisation of genetic data for use by social welfare and healthcare professionals. The solution is used to generate a pedigree tree based on the patient's and family's health data, which is utilised to support diagnostics, treatment planning, and genetic counselling. The objective of the solution is to enable data collection using, for example, electronic preliminary information forms, the visual creation of pedigree trees, and the up-to-date maintenance of data. Furthermore, the objective is to improve data quality, standardise data processing, and streamline the work of professionals by providing a smooth and appropriate user experience. In addition to the system itself, the procurement covers related interfaces with other systems used in healthcare, access rights and licences, and the delivery project. Maintenance and support of the system are also included, and expert services related to the development and use of the system can be included in the procurement if necessary. The purpose of the request for information is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. This request for information seeks to survey the market situation, services related to the systems, contract terms, and commercial models, such as pricing. Based on the responses to the request for information, market dialogue sessions may be organised where suppliers can present their solutions and views on the implementation of the procurement. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be held in Finnish. Istekki Oy will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the more detailed schedules and the Teams meeting link at a later date. Please submit your response by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 10.8.2026 at 9.00. Responses to the request for information should be headed as follows: "Request for information response: "Pedigree tree drawing software [Company Name]"" We hope that responses are submitted as a separate attachment in Finnish to ensure that processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you can also attach brochures or other material in Finnish that supports the content of your response.

sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.description: The Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE) program supports the translation of open-source science and engineering-focused research products into safe and sustainable ecosystems that address national and societal challenges. Open-source tools such as software, hardware, machine learning models, languages, and data platforms are designed to be shared as they are publicly-accessible and modifiable. These tools spark innovation in critical fields as varied as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, banking, healthcare, research, education, next-gen manufacturing, mobility, and National security (including cybersecurity). PESOSE supports the creation of managing organizations for these ecosystems, ensuring strong governance, distributed development, and broad user communities across academia, industry, and government. PESOSE also supports enhancements to the safety, security, and privacy of Open-Source Ecosystems (OSE) by addressing significant vulnerabilities, both technical and socio-technical, to improve the resistance of the ecosystem against threats. This solicitation seeks three types of proposals, allowing teams to propose specific activities to: 1) scope and plan the establishment of an OSE, 2) establish and expand a sustainable OSE based on a robust, promising open-source product that meets an emergent societal or national need, and 3) improve the safety, security, and privacy of an existing OSE and its products.
sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.title: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)

The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. sig_943e2ac41330811910c9.description: TfW is inviting suppliers to express interest in an upcoming tender for an advanced, future-oriented Rolling Stock Asset Management System to supersede the existing solution. The new system must accommodate both legacy and modern rolling stock, with the aim of improving maintenance efficiency, materials management, regulatory compliance, and seamless integration with TfW’s internal and third-party systems. The proposed system should support mobile usage as well as desktop and enhance all facets of maintenance planning, execution, and reporting—including both preventive and corrective tasks. Capabilities must include improved material availability, optimised inventory management, and effective warranty and cost control. Essential features comprise real-time fault and delay reporting, robust analytics for operational and financial performance, and strict adherence to railway safety and regulatory requirements. The solution should additionally enable third-party maintenance operations and offer comprehensive traceability and auditability of all assets. All maintenance activities must be documented electronically including mobile usage with complete traceability, including change logs, user activity, and audit trails, and distinguish between preventive and corrective maintenance activities, supporting dynamic scheduling based on time, date, vehicle, and component manufacturer. Integration with external platforms such as CAF GMAO, Stadler SRMS, Tracsis Enterprise, and TfW's procurement and finance systems is essential. This includes automated purchase order processing, supplier qualification oversight, and approval workflow facilitation. Master Data: The solution should incorporate templates for vehicle structures, track sub-assemblies, and serialised spare parts, ensuring full lifecycle traceability for all assets and components. It must also allow for counter readings, calibration tracking, and attachment of relevant safety documentation and drawings. Materials Management: The system must provide inventory tracking across multiple locations, technician logging, automated procurement, and stock replenishment capabilities. Support for return and scrap management, lead time monitoring, and asset/component association per maintenance cycle is required. Security and Compliance Requirements: • The solution must meet strict security and compliance standards to protect operations and sensitive data with enough flexible licensing for separate roles, location and organisational needs, with tight access controls. • Full adherence to TfW's security standards is required. Reporting & Analytics: • Real-time dashboards and reporting tools should deliver insights into performance, costs, compliance, and material usage. • Reporting capabilities must extend to profitability, productivity, utilization, effectiveness, forecasting, and inventory valuation. Planning & Scheduling: • The platform should enable dynamic scheduling creation, mass updates to maintenance plans, and long-range simulations, assisting planners in optimising vehicle deployment and workforce allocation. Interested parties are invited to express their interest in attending an online market engagement event on January 19th 2026 where a detailed scope will be presented and tender timeframes will be announced. Please register your interest in attending the above by email to supplychain@tfw.wales Lot 1: .

sig_9444aa8290c269f275f6.description: The Provincie Limburg is at the start of a major modernisation of its information management. This modernisation drive is necessary due to rapid technological developments, increasing digitalisation and partnerships, and increasingly stringent and changing laws and regulations. Examples include the new Archives Act, the Open Government Act (Woo), the Modernisation of Electronic Administrative Traffic Act (Wmebv), the Digital Government Act (Wdo), the Government Information Security Baseline (BIO), and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The current application landscape, with outdated and fragmented systems, is proving increasingly less capable of providing the organisation, administration and society with information in a secure, efficient and future-proof manner. To tackle these challenges, the Provincie Limburg has drawn up a clear vision for its information management. The starting point is that information is managed in a sustainably accessible, secure, efficient, high-quality and compliant manner. For employees, this means more overview, simplicity and uniformity; for society, optimal transparency and service delivery are central. The European tendering procedure for a new case management system is an important part of realising this vision. With the implementation of one integrated, cloud-based and user-friendly case management system, the Provincie Limburg is laying the foundation for case-oriented working, modern archive management and professional process support. The new system will serve as the central hub of the provincial information provision and enables further digitalisation, better service delivery and more control over quality, compliance and risk management. The Provincie Limburg is therefore looking for a contractor that, in close cooperation with the organisation, will be responsible for supplying, implementing, supporting the adoption of and managing a modern SaaS case management system and the associated integrations. sig_944df2b4983d009ceb7b.description: The Bank of England is considering its future approach to procuring technology products and associated services following the expiry of its current technology Value Added Reseller (VAR) framework. At this stage, the Bank has not made a final decision on the structure of any future procurement and is undertaking preliminary market engagement to help inform its thinking, procurement strategy and framework design. Whilst one option is a like-for-like replacement of the existing arrangement, the Bank's initial view is that the future model may comprise multiple frameworks rather than a single framework. In particular, the Bank is considering a dedicated framework focussed on Cyber & Emerging Technology, alongside one or more additional frameworks covering other areas of technology spend. The categories currently being considered are: Cyber & Emerging Technology Software & Platforms Hardware, End User Computing (EUC) & Connectivity Enterprise Applications, Cloud Hosting & Infrastructure The purpose of this engagement is to obtain market feedback on areas including: Framework structure and lotting strategy The advantages and disadvantages of single versus multiple framework arrangements Supplier capability and capacity across the proposed categories Commercial and pricing models Routes to market for emerging technologies Innovation and market developments Supplier onboarding, framework governance and competition models The Bank welcomes input from suppliers operating in one or more of the proposed categories and intends to use the feedback received to inform its future procurement strategy, framework design and any subsequent procurement activity. This Preliminary Market Engagement exercise does not constitute a call for competition and will not result in the award of any contract. The Bank reserves the right to amend the scope, structure, lotting approach and procurement strategy of any future procurement following completion of the engagement process. Lot 1: .

sig_94a9d4a5c9b862d58df5.description: This call for tenders is for an external independent study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and to support the contracting authority in relation to the open public consultation in preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework. The strategic framework sets out three crosscutting key objectives and a range of actions for promoting workers’ health and safety. The three objectives are: anticipating and managing change in the new world of work brought about by the green, digital and demographic transitions; improving prevention of workplace accidents and illnesses; increasing preparedness for any potential future health crises. The implementation of these three objectives is underpinned by: (i) social dialogue; (ii) strengthening of the evidence base; (iii) strengthening of enforcement; (iv) awareness raising; and (v) funding. At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. The results of this screening exercise study will inform the process of developing new EU OSH priorities in the strategic framework on health and safety at work after 2027.
sig_94a9d4a5c9b862d58df5.title: Study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and support to the preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework

sig_94b3d91a27d65a491757.description: In line with its commitment to increasing investment in the UK’s transport infrastructure, the Department for Transport (DfT) requires ongoing access to high-quality, specialist technical and commercial advisory services. This need is currently fulfilled through the STARThree Framework, which succeeded the Specialist Technical Advisory for Rail (STARTwo) Framework—both managed by the Department’s Group Commercial Directorate (GCD). The Department for Transport intends to publish the STARFour Framework, a fourth generation, closed, multi-lot framework agreement to succeed the STARThree Framework (expiring July 2027). However, this will be subject to approvals and market engagement feedback. STARFour will provide continued access to specialist technical and commercial advisory services across all transport sectors, supporting the Department, its ALBs, and other qualifying bodies. Building on the success of STARThree, the new framework will encourage SME participation, promote innovation, and deliver value for money through streamlined procurement routes including mini-competitions and direct awards. The STARFour Framework is essential to maintain a fit-for-purpose, flexible, and cost-effective route for specialist transport technical and commercial advice following the expiry of STARThree. As transport challenges grow—across net zero strategies, decarbonisation, multi-modal integration, and industry restructuring—STARFour will ensure DfT, ALBs and qualifying bodies have continued access to critical expertise across all transport sectors, not just rail. Lot 1: .
sig_94b3d91a27d65a491757.title: Specialist Technical and Commercial Advisory for Rail and Other Transport Systems Framework (STARFour)

Upon its termination, the framework agreement shall continue to apply for the duration of individual orders. The objective of the tender is the introduction of a secrets management system (SAM) with an attached privileged access management system (PAM) to be developed step by step. This system is being procured for 500 privileged users, 3 cloud environments and 60.000 technical accounts. Following the reintroduction of regular secrets and password changes, the need for a secrets management system has become apparent in many parts of kubus IT. In particular, due to the increase in infrastructure as code and the increased use of container-based infrastructure, significantly more secrets are required than in the past. To counter this challenge, the implementation of the secrets and access management system on-prem is planned. The product is tendered including implementation, since more complex settings are generally required during the initial connection of the systems in the course of implementing the product. Product training, consulting and support services are to be provided optionally. The contracting authority understands a secrets and privileged access management system to be a system for the administration and security of privileged accesses and for automatic password changes (privileged access management system (PAM) or secrets and access management system (SAM)). For reasons of protecting the confidentiality of information, the specific software solution will only be announced upon invitation to submit a tender. The contracting authority intends to procure software components under a software rental licensing model in an on-premise operational model. The contractor shall also provide consulting or support services optionally and on demand. The EVB-IT framework agreement shall apply. The maximum volume for orders under this contract is set at 2,1 million euros net. There is no entitlement to the exhaustion of this upper limit. Licences may be ordered up to the attainment of the upper limit within the four-year term of the framework agreement. The framework agreement shall enter into force upon the award of the contract. It shall end upon the expiry of 4 years following acceptance of the installation services (implementation project), without requiring notice of termination, or prematurely upon reaching the maximum volumes. The framework agreement shall continue to apply for the duration of individual orders after its termination. The basic services are ordered for 48 months. The contracting authority reserves the right to commission the subscription via a further individual call-off before the expiry of the framework agreement. Any subsequent order shall be capped in amount by the maximum volume of the framework agreement and shall not exceed a term of 12 months.

sig_94d0836410ef6a9595ae.description: The procurement concerns the XR, metaverse and web3 sub-implementations of the supra-municipal XR Museum project. The procurement will be carried out dynamically and the individual sub-projects will be tendered at a later stage among the suppliers selected in this procurement. The XR Museum is a joint project between the museums of Järvenpää, Kerava and Tuusula to build a fully virtual museum centre. In addition to the municipal museums, the private museums Ainola and Lottamuseo are also involved. The project has received funding from the European Union's Next Generation EU structural funding. The project started in spring 2023 and the new museum will open in spring 2025. The project is led by a steering group of representatives from the participating museums and municipalities. The project will be implemented by a separate project team. The XR Museum consists of different XR, metaverse and web3 implementations. Most of these are browser-based, but we also work on VR productions, for example. The aim is to create experiential and interactive ways to experience the art and culture of the region. All applications produced by the project will be designed and tested in collaboration with audiences and stakeholders, and participatory processes will be integrated into all sub-projects. So far, the project has produced 360-photo constructed remote tours and a model of the artist's home Villa Kokkonen. Work is underway to build a metaverse environment and create an event space for the museum. Future work will include the production of more modelling and browser and VR experiences using these. sig_94ed62920cd8a11c3205.description: The subject of the public contract is the complete delivery of the required HW and SW for the technology centre of the Hradec Králové Region, its installation and implementation, including the execution of the necessary migration of operated servers, information systems and data from the existing technology centre to the new one. Also included is test operation, the drawing up of corresponding project, technical and operational documentation, user training, and the subsequent provision of technical support and service. The subject matter of performance includes: a) The elaboration of the TCK implementation project, including an analysis of the current state, the implementation schedule for individual works, and the design of acceptance tests. The implementation project shall meet the requirements according to Annex No. 1 of the tendering conditions and shall contain a detailed procedure for the implementation of all parts of the public contract agreed and approved between the contracting authority and the contractor within the framework of the elaboration of the implementation project. b) The delivery and commissioning of the TCK according to the implementation project, which includes: • The delivery of hardware and software for the TCK in accordance with Annex No. 1 of the tendering conditions. • The installation and implementation of individual technological units and the commissioning of the TCK as a whole. The delivery includes the following technological units: 1) Network infrastructure 2) SAN infrastructure 3) Server infrastructure 4) Server virtualisation - VMware software product licences including the provision of Support and Subscription support in the 365x7x24 mode shall be provided by the contracting authority 5) Data storage 6) Accessories • The execution of the necessary migration of operated servers, information systems and data from the existing TCK to the new TCK. Migration (transfer) of all servers, information systems and data operated on the existing TCK to the new TCK shall be carried out, including the preservation of full functionality to the extent specified by the implementation project. • The execution of acceptance tests. c) Test operation for a duration of 1 months. d) The preparation of complete project, technical and operational documentation for the TCK in accordance with Annex No. 1 of the tendering conditions for all parts of the work in written and electronic editable form, in MS Word/Excel, MS Visio format, which shall include implementation, operational and security documentation, user and administrator manuals for the supplied parts of the work including training documentation, a description of regular maintenance of the solution, and final-as-built documentation including a detailed description of all interfaces. e) Training of designated employees of the Hradec Králové Region in basic operation and administration, within which the administrators will be acquainted with the administration and proper use of the supplied products. f) The provision of service and technical support for a specified period. g) Other services not explicitly stated, which are nevertheless inextricably linked with the implementation of the work and without which the implementation of the work is not possible. Test operation During the test operation, the fulfilment of the contracting authority's functional requirements shall be verified. The test operation period begins to run on the day of the protocol-based completion of the implementation of the work and its handover for test operation. The duration of the test operation shall be 1 month. If defects occur during the test operation that limit the functionalities of the work, the test operation period shall be extended by the same period during which the work was not fully functional. The test operation shall be terminated by the protocol-based completion of the test operation and the handover of the work to routine operation. Provision of service and technical support for a specified period Service and technical support shall be provided from the start of test operation a) for a period of 5 years from the date of handover of the work to routine operation for the parts of the work comprising the technological units SAN infrastructure, network infrastructure and server virtualisation, whereas the delivery of VMware software product licences for server virtualisation including the provision of Support and Subscription support for VMware software products in the 365x7x24 mode shall be ensured by the contracting authority outside of this public contract. b) for a period of 7 years from the date of handover of the work to routine operation for all other parts of the work. During the test operation, service and technical support shall be provided free of charge. Warranty period The warranty period for the work shall be agreed for a period of 84 months (7 years) with the exception of the technological units SAN infrastructure, network infrastructure and server virtualisation, for which a warranty period of 60 months (5 years) shall be agreed. The warranty period shall also apply to all software that is part of the supplied hardware, including the contracting authority's right to the provision of new software versions. The warranty period begins to run from the day of the protocol-based completion of the test operation and the handover of the subject matter of performance to routine operation. The contractor shall be responsible for defects in the delivery throughout the entire warranty period. The scope of the warranty provided for individual parts of the public contract is detailed in Annex No. 3 of the tendering conditions.

sig_953d35e7ecb0dc9c7a32.description: The aim of the award procedure is to commission a high-performing managed service provider (MSP) that will take over the complete planning, management, implementation and operational transfer of the brownfield transformation of the existing SAP ECC system landscape to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition, as part of "RISE with SAP". The subject of the contract is a holistic transformation and operational service. This includes in particular the technical and functional analysis of the existing system landscape, the SAP S/4HANA conversion, the transfer to the private cloud environment, test migrations and data conversion, the adaptation of custom developments, add-ons and interfaces, as well as the implementation and optimisation of the relevant commercial processes. In addition, SAP Fiori, reporting and embedded analytics, as well as the necessary integration services, in particular using the SAP Business Technology Platform and the SAP Integration Suite, must be taken into account. The contractor shall accompany the transformation including tests, cutover, go-live, hypercare, training and handover to regular operations and shall subsequently take over the agreed managed services as well as operational, support and further development services. In this context, particular account must be taken of the clean core approach, the maintenance of ongoing clinical operations, the existing dependencies on SAP IS-H, i.s.h.med, SAP HCM and other peripheral systems, as well as requirements regarding data protection, information security, compliance, availability, scalability and an orderly exit scenario. The contractual basis is intended to be the conclusion of an EVB-IT cloud contract, which covers both the transformation and implementation services up to acceptance and the managed services, operational, support and further development services to be provided thereafter.

sig_9540a13983912afbe4d1.description: The subject matter of the contract is the digital transformation of the Municipality of Egaleo through the design, supply and installation of applications and technological means that will improve the management and functionality of the municipality's urban environment, providing more efficient, innovative and high-quality services for the benefit of residents, visitors and businesses. "DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION ACTIONS EXCLUDING FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT", of an estimated value of 1.128.087,10 † plus VAT • 3.Smart accessibility assurance system for people with mobility issues • 4.Smart pedestrian crossings and systems friendly to persons with disabilities • 5.Traffic information systems • 6.Smart waste bins • 8.Organisation of the Fleet Office and Management of the Municipal vehicle fleet • 9.Smart energy management systems for municipal and school buildings • 10.Smart lighting systems within municipal buildings • 14.Digital platform for the management of vulnerable groups • 15.Management of indoor and outdoor sports, cultural and recreational areas • 21.Installation of smart air quality measurement systems within the municipality's territory • 24.Smart warning and risk management system (flood phenomena, fire, earthquake, etc.) within the boundaries of the municipality and in accordance with their responsibilities • 26.Urban green space and common areas management system • 33.Implementation of public key performance indicators in accordance with ISO 37122, adapted to Greek conditions The goods to be supplied are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: - 48600000-4 - Database and operating system software packages - 72314000-9: Data collection and collation services - 80533100-0: IT training services - 50324100-3: Systems maintenance services The above subject matter is tendered in a single lot as the undertaking of the project by a single contractor ensures better coordinated execution of the project and single responsibility for the completion of the project by the contractor. At the same time, it is ensured that specific technical and quality specifications requiring overall management and control will be complied with. Furthermore, regarding the additional benefits of this option for the Municipality, administrative burden is reduced and there is single responsibility on the part of the Municipality for the completion of the project, reducing the risk of inconsistency or incompatibility between the different departments/services of the Municipality. Tenders are submitted for all of the systems to be supplied. The subject matter of the contract includes, in addition to the supply, maintenance and support services for the Good Operation Guarantee Period which is set at a minimum of two (2) years. In addition, the Contractor is obliged to install and operate the offered Software in a Public Digital Data Centre which will be indicated by the Municipality. For this reason, the Contractor shall deliver to the Municipality the infrastructure requirements for the proper operation of the application. Until the indication by the Municipality of the Digital Data Centre where the application will ultimately be installed and hosted, the contractor undertakes to host the application in a facility under its responsibility or in a dedicated data hosting centre (host centre) at no additional cost to the Municipality. The maximum hosting period by the contractor shall be five (5) years from the date of delivery of the application. During this period, the contractor is obliged to migrate the application to the Digital Data Centre that will be indicated. Additionally, the contractor must include in the analysis and design study a data classification study for the following actions: • Action 14.Digital platform for the management of vulnerable groups • Action 15.Management of indoor and outdoor sports, cultural and recreational areas • Action 24.Smart warning and risk management system (flood phenomena, fire, earthquake, etc.) within the boundaries of the municipality and in accordance with their responsibilities • Action 26.Urban green space and common areas management system • Action 33.Implementation of public key performance indicators in accordance with ISO 37122, adapted to Greek conditions in accordance with para. 2 of article 85 of Law 4727/2020, where it is stated that ‑Each new information system of public sector bodies must be accompanied by a data classification study, which is compulsorily included in the project analysis and design studies‑. The estimated value of the contract amounts to 1.128.087,10 † excluding VAT 24 % (estimated value including VAT: † 1.398.828,00 †) and VAT 270.740,90 †. A detailed description of the physical and financial subject matter of the contract is given in APPENDIX I of this tender notice. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, using the best price-quality ratio.

Lot LOT-0001: FA roll-out/roll-in, installation and disposal of decentralised IT systems. The framework agreement includes the following services: - the roll-out of IT systems (installation services, assembly activities and logistics activities) - pure logistics activities (transport) - the roll-in of IT systems (dismantling activities, logistics activities) - the disposal of IT systems (dismantling activities, logistics activities, disposal). It is based on the following estimated order quantity in accordance with Annex 3 to the contract - price sheet during the minimum contract term. These are conservatively estimated values. The quantity specifications serve as the basis for calculation. Planned acceptance quantity for the minimum contract term are: 1. 000 units roll-out - installation services, assembly and transport 100 units roll-out - transport 100 units roll-out - assembly and transport 500 units roll-in - dismantling and transport 500 units roll-in - dismantling, transport and disposal 9900 metres - Cat7 cable 80 hours of wage labour The order volume envisaged for this framework agreement has been described as precisely as possible. However, the requirement is not binding and cannot be definitively determined. This only reflects an estimated order quantity and an anticipated period for the provision of services. It can therefore not be ruled out that the services are called off in a different volume and/or a different period. A minimum purchase is not agreed. There is no obligation to accept the estimated, optional call-off quantities. The call-off quantity may therefore decrease. Since services can be called off simultaneously at different locations of the client's customers, the contractor must ensure that in the event of submitting a tender for the required provision of services, the personnel, technical and spatial resources are available. The contractor must confirm the performance capability of its organisation with regard to a possible simultaneous provision of these quantities (cf. Chapter 3.3 - performance period of Annex 2 to the contract - description of services). The contract term begins with the award of contract but at the earliest on 09.01.2027 and is, unless terminated beforehand, initially two years (minimum contract term). The client reserves the right to extend the contract twice by one year each time (optional contract periods). The minimum contract term is extended automatically by another year unless the client terminates the contract three months before the end of the contract term. The same applies to the second optional extension period. The contract ends in any case upon reaching the maximum total order limit of 400.000,00 EUR net; 476.000,00 EUR gross (incl. optional services). The estimated acceptance quantity can be found in Annex 3 to the contract - price sheet. If the contract value is increased by a contract amendment during the contract term in accordance with Section 132 of the German Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), the contract ends upon reaching this new contract value. Unaffected by the end of the contract is the contractor's obligation to provide the services commissioned during the contract term in accordance with the contract.

sig_956f0c383c0f502bac86.description: Data collection for the Information System on the Road and Motorway Network of the Czech Republic (ISSDS ČR) is organised by the Road Data Bank Department and NDIC Ostrava. This involves continuous and uninterrupted data collection for the Construction Activity Register (RSČ), road passportisation description (PPK), junction description (PK) and road surface structural layers (KV). Suppliers of this service also provide methodological assistance to individual road asset managers (Road and Motorway Directorate of the Czech Republic Administrations and Facilities, district and regional Road Maintenance Administrations), control of road passportisation description data, junction description, road surface structural layers and the maintenance of their current status. The supply of the required data is a highly specialised activity that takes place simultaneously in different regions, which is why it is not ideal to carry it out from a single centre. The activity further requires detailed knowledge of the monitored roads in the given region, systematic work, long-term training, regular training, experience with data collection and, last but not least, special equipment and modification of the measuring vehicle. The data from the above-mentioned activities will be used, among other things, for the planned and gradually introduced Pavement Management System (SHV). West Bohemian region. It consists of the districts: Rakovník, Domažlice, Cheb, Karlovy Vary, Klatovy, Plzeň-město, Plzeň-jih, Plzeň-sever, Rokycany, Sokolov and Tachov.
sig_956f0c383c0f502bac86.title: Supply of data to the Information System on the Road and Motorway Network

sig_95c7d2ca1d81d71c517c.description: Munster Technological University is seeking tenders from competent service providers for the provision of maintenance, support, upgrades, enhancement/ancillary services, and content development for an existing Airbus mobile Cyber Range platform at MTU. Specifically, the purpose of this tender is to procure services to support the continued operation, maintenance, hosting, and enhancement of an existing Airbus Mobile Cyber Range platform. The platform is currently used to simulate cybersecurity attacks and user activities, test the resilience of IT networks for business and industry clients, provide realistic training environments for cybersecurity personnel and on-site support capabilities for cybersecurity testing of Operational Technology (OT) and Internet of Things (IoT) networks, particularly in environments such as manufacturing and process industries where assets include physical monitoring and control systems. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: • Technical maintenance and servicing of the Airbus system hardware and software • Hosting and operational support for newly developed deployments • Development and integration of new training content, attack/defence scenarios, and test cases • Ongoing upgrades to align with evolving cybersecurity threats and industry needs • Hardware and software upgrades to expand the CR8 system, including additional servers, software, etc.
sig_95c7d2ca1d81d71c517c.title: The Provision of Maintenance, Support, Upgrades, Enhancement/Ancillary Services and content development for an Airbus Mobile Cyber Range Platform to MTU

sig_95cf5ff5ad4732ed2382.description: Pursuant to Article L. 2113-2 of the Public Procurement Code, SMO Nord Pas-de-Calais Numérique acts as a central purchasing body in the sense that this buyer acquires supplies or services for other contracting authorities, public undertakings or contracting entities. The purpose of this contract is the supply of: • personal RGS** and eIDAS authentication and signature certificates, on a USB key type medium, for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments; • NFC cards on a physical medium, intended for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments, supplied according to the same ordering, delivery and handover procedures as personal certificates on a physical medium (cf. point 3.5). The Syndicat mixte Nord-Pas-de-Calais Numérique, in partnership with the Territorial Civil Service management centres of the Nord (Cdg59) and the Pas-de-Calais (Cdg62), operates a central purchasing body for the local authorities and public establishments of the Nord and Pas-de-Calais departments. This central purchasing body facilitates access to the authentication and electronic signature certificates necessary for the dematerialisation of administrative procedures and documents. It offers member entities a shared system, allowing them to benefit from negotiated rates and a simplified ordering process. At the date of launch of this consultation, 560 local authorities and public establishments belonging to the central purchasing body have access to a dematerialised platform allowing them to order their certificates directly. This contract is a continuation of the previous contract. It aims to guarantee the continuity of the service provided to the members of the central purchasing body, within an updated regulatory framework marked in particular by the evolution of the eIDAS regulation 2.0 and the strengthening of security requirements. This consultation pursues the following objectives: - To guarantee, for all members of the central purchasing body, the continuity and quality of the service for the supply of RGS** and eIDAS certificates; - To promote the consistency of digital public services open to users and facilitate their adoption, thanks to interfaces and operating modes that are similar from one local administration to another; - To promote the dematerialisation of exchanges in order to save time, eliminate time or location constraints, reduce costs related to paper and postage, and optimise the tracking and searching of documents; - To allow fully digital management of data and documents produced internally or transmitted by partners, whether they are administrations, citizens or suppliers.

sig_95d910cedef83f709841.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE SUBJECT The subject of the procurement currently being prepared is a company, credit and control information retrieval service for the use of Valtiokonttori. Valtiokonttori is an agency under the Ministry of Finance (VM), which is responsible for state debt management, investment and financial services, as well as the administration and supervision of state loans, guarantees, warranties and interest subsidies. In addition, it handles the state's central accounting and the preparation of financial statements, as well as compensation and benefit matters. Valtiokonttori maintains a financial information repository for municipalities and wellbeing services counties, produces analysis and reporting services for the state administration, manages the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility, and maintains an electronic procurement notification system. Valtiokonttori manages loans, interest subsidies and state guarantees and warranties granted by the state. Up-to-date company, credit and control information is needed daily, e.g. in making payment and grant decisions and in risk management. The goal of Valtiokonttori is to renew the currently used - company and credit information retrieval service - control service - integration into the Microsoft Dynamics CRM system The service has approximately 40 users, of which 2 users act as main users. The subject of the procurement possibly also includes a sanctions list retrieval service. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. The notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this notice is preliminary and indicative prior information. MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue is intended for companies interested in tendering and includes commenting on draft tender documentation before the publication of the final call for tenders. In addition to written comments on the draft tender documentation, the Contracting Authority reserves the possibility to meet interested companies in Teams meetings. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We ask companies interested in tendering in the competitive tendering to register for the market dialogue by providing the following information by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the subject "VK/4262/2025 Valtiokonttorin company, credit and control information retrieval service": • company name and business ID • name of the contact person • email address of the contact person. Personal data will only be stored for the duration of the preparation of the competitive tendering in question and any related tendering process.

sig_95e3e7f6217533c93aca.description: Amendment 01 dated 12 July 2021: Updated "CSO" to read "Commercial Solutions Opening" in an effort to prevent confusion with other acronyms. Federal Agency: Air Force Program Office: AFLCMC/XA “Architecture and Integration Directorate” CSO Title: JADC2 Commercial Solutions Opening CSO Type: Commercial Solutions Opening with Calls CSO Number: FA8612-21-S-C001 CSO Date: June 28, 2021 NOTE This is only an announcement; PLEASE DO NOT SUBMIT PROPOSALS IN RESPONSE. Subsequent calls will be issued under this announcement to solicit proposals for specific efforts. Please refer to the attachment section of this announcement for the calls. Publication of this announcement does not obligate the DoD to review any white papers submission beyond an initial administrative review, or to award any specific project, or to obligate any available funds. 1.0 OVERVIEW This Commercial Solutions Opening is intended to be as streamlined as possible to allow the Architecture and Integration Directorate (AFLCMC/XA), or any organization AFLCMC/XA supports, to leverage the latest technology advances from a large variety of prospective Contractors. AFLCMC/XA invites innovative technical approach proposals addressing Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) problems associated with getting the right information to the right platform/decision maker in the most efficient manner thereby reducing kill chain and Observe, Orient, Decide and Act (OODA) timelines and cycles. This Commercial Solutions Opening will focus on existing and emerging technologies and platforms across the Defense Department, the Intelligence Community, and the commercial world, to perform an integrated analysis of the capability of various options to contribute to the fight and prioritize investments over time. This solicitation is not requesting any white papers or proposals at this time. This Commercial Solutions Opening functions as the overarching umbrella solicitation from which Calls will be published. This Commercial Solutions Opening will remain open for Calls until rescinded. This Commercial Solutions Opening can result in the award of FAR Part 12 Contracts or Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) under 10 USC 2371b. Over the course of this time period, AFLCMC/XA will publish Calls via amendments to this Commercial Solutions Opening. These Calls will contain specific Areas of Interest (AoIs) related to JADC2’s Technology Focus Areas. Those specific AoIs are what prospective Contractors shall focus their solutions towards. This is a competitive solicitation that seeks to fund innovative technologies that propose new solutions to expand Air Force capabilities as it relates to JADC2 Technology Focus Areas. AFLCMC/XA is interested in receiving responses from all interested offerors to include, but not limited to, the following: traditional defense contractors, nontraditional defense contractors, large businesses, small businesses and research institutions. The Commercial Solutions Opening is a streamlined acquisition process that seeks to reduce acquisition timelines and acquire new, innovative solutions that companies can bring forth to meet the stated AoIs detailed in each Call. All details of the process shall be governed by this Commercial Solutions Opening unless otherwise noted or expanded upon in each Call. AFLCMC/XA is not obligated to make any awards as a result of this Commercial Solutions Opening and all awards are subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by the proposer prior to the issuance of any contract award. AFLCMC/XA reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this Commercial Solutions Opening and each subsequent Call. The Commercial Solutions Opening authority is Section 879 of the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2017, Public Law 114-328, and Class Deviation 2018-O0016. 2.0 Commercial Solutions Opening with Calls This Commercial Solutions Opening is a hybrid solicitation against which both Closed Calls and/or Open Period Calls can be published via amendments to the Commercial Solutions Opening. All Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening will include specific instructions including dates, AoIs, evaluation criteria and proposal instructions to potential offerors. While each offeror shall adhere to this Commercial Solutions Opening, the Calls can contain other information the Contractor shall adhere to. Each Call will be announced on the Government Point of Entry (beta.SAM.gov), which may result in the award of a FAR Part 12 contract or an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under 10 USC 2371b. 2.1 Closed Calls (One-Step or Two-Step) Over the period of this Commercial Solutions Opening, Calls may be issued to request white papers and/or proposals for specific AoIs. It will be determined on a Call-by-Call basis whether or not the announcement is for a one-step (Proposals only) or a two-step process (White Papers first, then Proposals by invite-only). The submission for white papers and proposals shall be submitted at a specific date and time as set forth in each particular Call. White papers and/or proposals will not be reviewed if submitted after the stated date and time. No exceptions will be made for late proposal submission, including technology issues encountered during submission. One-Step Calls Step 1: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Calls issued against this Commercial Solutions Opening. Two-Step Calls Step 1: White Paper due date and time will be provided in Calls issued against this Commercial Solutions Opening Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Requests for Proposals (RFPs) sent to offerors that submit White Papers who are evaluated well in accordance with the criteria stated in each Call. 2.2 Open Period Calls (Two-Step) This Commercial Solutions Opening may also have Open Period Calls. Open Period Calls will only be issued under a two-step process. After an Open Call is published, white papers may be submitted at any time during an Open Period for the AoIs detailed in the Call. It is important to note that only white papers submitted in response to the specific AoIs detailed in the Call will be considered. Step 1: White paper submission period will be provided in Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening. Step 2: Proposal due date and time will be provided in Requests for Proposals (RFPs) sent to offerors that submit White Papers who are evaluated well in accordance with the criteria stated in each Call. 3.0 TECHNOLOGY FOCUS AREAS (TFAs) Each Technology Focus Area identifies an area where prospective Contractors can bring substantial value to meet the JADC2 mission. This Commercial Solutions Opening is not limited to the following TFAs. Additional TFAs may be included via amendments to this Commercial Solutions Opening. Digital Architecture, Standards and Concepts This category consists of various activities to analyze, mature, and document the foundational aspects of the development of the overall enterprise architecture. This includes digital modeling, simulation and analysis, trade studies, government owned standard development and maintenance, and potential concept development and refinement. Development of digital engineering architecture to include appropriate toolsets, licenses, data, etc., at multiple levels of security and including services such as data management, configuration control, and security/access management. Other activities may include architecting the toolchains to support the linkage of digital engineering artifacts to modeling and simulation tools and operational analysis. Sensor Integration The development, maturation, integration, demonstration, and proliferation of sensor hardware and software. A key interest of JADC2 is the compatibility and interoperability capabilities through the use of open interfaces to enable improved control of systems and the processing of their data. Data Data incorporates the cloud based data repositories across domains that are discoverable, enabling publish subscribe approaches servicing various consumers across the DoD. These repositories contain data that consists of structured and unstructured data and where possible, this data will be meta tagged for further analytics and as well as fusion purposes. One of the key element of this approach is this ability to analyze the data to develop machine learning and further enhance the artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to provide previously unrealized military utility in decision aides. Secure Processing Secure Processing will leverage the Enterprise Information Technology as a Service (EITaaS) work at the unclassified and secret level to expand this capability to all levels of security. A key feature of secure processing will be to develop a multi-level security (MLS) technology set that enables moving up and down in security level where feasible no matter the hardware device, transportation method, or environment. Lastly secure processing encompasses providing deployment, training, and support services for all of these capabilities worldwide. Connectivity Development and fielding of networks to enable the timely processing and dissemination of data from any sensor to users at the tactical edge and/or strategic levels. Assets in any domain may be platforms-of-opportunity to serve as communications nodes enabled by omnidirectional and directional line-of-sight (LOS), and beyond-line-of-sight (BLOS) capabilities. Attributes of interest include: increased data rates, reduced latency, improved anti-jam, Low Probability of Intercept/Low Probability of Detection (LPI/LPD) characteristics, scalability of nodes/connections, improved integration of dissimilar users, etc. Applications Applications encompasses the design, development and demonstration of open interface applications and/or open interface software development kits for distributed command and control decision-makers (e.g., machine-to-human, machine-to-machine) across multi-domain operations. Additionally, this category seeks solutions which demonstrate the ability to ingest and process cross domain, multi-sourced data feeds (intelligence, information, etc.) via fusion environments and/or fusion services. Effects Integration Design, development, demonstration and integration of networked weapons engaged across complex (e.g. wide area mesh) environments. This includes, but is not limited to, smart munitions and low-cost autonomous platforms capable of supporting C2 de-confliction and synchronization of multi-domain assets. Incorporation of techniques and/or technologies are also sought to enable near-real time mission feedback loops and reduce processing time between system/mission data updates. The specific AoIs that prospective Contractors shall propose to will logically relate back to the Technology Focus Areas. Additional details and requirement specifics will be contained within the AoIs section of the Calls published under this Commercial Solutions Opening. The technology being proposed should meet the requirements of a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) assessment of at least three (3) or higher as detailed in the GAO link provided. AFLCMC/XA has the ability to adjust the TRL it requires on a per call basis and is the final decision authority for the TRL determination of any proposed technology solutions. For more information on TRL please see Figure 1 on page 11 at the following link: https://www.gao.gov/assets/710/703694.pdf 4.0 DEFINITIONS Commercial Solutions Opening with Calls: This allows for publication of an umbrella Commercial Solutions Opening solicitation that contains overarching information, but does not request white papers or proposals. The Commercial Solutions Opening functions as a framework identifying the technical areas and giving the basic terms and administrative information of the Commercial Solutions Opening. The requests for white papers and/or proposals are done by issuing Calls that are published via amendments to the Commercial Solutions Opening. Calls can be issued at any time during the open period of the Commercial Solutions Opening. Each Call will be tailored to best fit the acquisition approach identified by the Government. The Calls may also include specific terms that apply to that Call such as further technical details and any pertinent clauses. Proposals or white papers are submitted only when Calls under this Commercial Solutions Opening are published. Open Period Calls: This type of Call allows for white paper and proposal submittals at any time within a specified period as set forth in the subsequent Call. Closed Calls: This type of Call allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at a specified date and time as set forth in the subsequent Call. This process and the dates associated with it are more structured than Open Period Calls. Areas of Interest (AoIs): These are specific requests for innovative solutions that AFLCMC/XA will detail in each subsequent Call and will derive from the Technology Focus Areas. Contractors’ innovative solutions should focus on addressing a specific AoI. White Paper: A brief (usually 2-5 pages) summary of the proposed technical approach with an accompanying rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) price. Pitch Day: Pitch Day is a tool that can be used as a part of the Call process. When used, Pitch Day gives Contractors an opportunity to meet AFLCMC/XA personnel in-person and provide a Pitch of their proposed technology. If a Pitch Day is utilized, specific details explaining the process and evaluation methods will be contained in the specific Call. Other Transaction: Refers to the type of Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) that may be placed as a result of this Commercial Solutions Opening and associated Calls. This type of OT is authorized by 10 U.S.C. § 2371b for prototype projects directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the DoD, or for the improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. This type of OTA is treated by DoD as an acquisition instrument, commonly referred to as an "other transaction" for a prototype project or a Section 2371b "other transaction". Prototype Project: Can generally be described as a proof of concept, model, reverse engineering to address obsolescence, pilot, novel application of commercial technologies for defense purposes, agile development activity, creation, design, development, demonstration of technical or operational utility, or combinations of the foregoing. A process, including a business process, may also be the subject of a prototype project. Although assistance terms are generally not appropriate in OT agreements in 10 U.S.C. § 2371b, ancillary work efforts that are necessary for completion of the prototype project, such as test site training or limited logistics support, may be included in prototype projects. A prototype may be physical, virtual, or conceptual in nature. The quantity of prototypes/commercial solutions should generally be limited to that needed to prove technical or manufacturing feasibility or evaluate military utility. Innovative: This refers to any technology, process, or method, including research and development that is new as of the date of proposal submission; or any new application of an existing technology, process or method as of the proposal date. Nontraditional Defense Contractor: As defined in 10 U.S.C. § 2302(9) as an entity that is not currently performing and has not performed, for at least the one-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by the DoD for the procurement or transaction, any contract or subcontract for the DoD that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. § 1502 and the regulations implementing such section. This includes all small business concerns under the criteria and size standards in 13 C.F.R. Part 121. Small Business Concern: Defined in the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632) and 13 CFR Part 121. 5.0 CONTRACT/AGREEMENT DETAILS As stated in the Overview Section, Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening can result in the award of either a FAR Part 12 Contract or an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under 10 USC 2371b. Regardless of the Contract Instrument AFLCMC/XA chooses to purse the Contract/Agreement type for all shall be Fixed Price, which includes Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Fixed Price Incentive (FPI). This solicitation is not accepting offers for grants or cooperative agreements as the purpose of this Commercial Solutions Opening is to transfer something of value directly to the Government. The Government will be the decision authority on whether to pursue a FAR Part 12 Contract, an OTA or no award at all. The Government reserves the right to award some, all or none of the proposals from responses to each Call. The Contracting/Agreements Officer reserves the right to negotiate directly with the offeror on the terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting contract/agreement on behalf of the Government. Be advised that only a Contracting/Agreements Officer has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding contract/agreement on behalf of the United Stated Government. 5.1 Prototyping This Commercial Solutions Opening may result in the award of prototype projects, which include not only commercially available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, but also concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing government-owned capabilities, and/or concepts for broad defense and/or public application(s). The Government reserves the right to award a FAR Part 12 contract, or an Other Transaction (OT) under 10 USC 2371b agreement (including an OT for a prototype project and a follow-on OT or contract for production), or no award at all. Calls issued under this Commercial Solutions Opening constitute competitive procedures. AFLCMC/XA may competitively award OTs for prototype projects that provide for the award of a follow-on production contract or OT for production to participants in the OT for prototype projects without the use of further competitive procedures, if the participant in the OT for prototype projects successfully completes the prototype project, as permitted by 10 U.S.C. § 2371b(f). 5.1.1 Iterative Prototyping A contract or OT for a prototype awarded under this Commercial Solutions Opening shall allow for an iterative prototyping process. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in a separate prototype project rather than a modification of the original prototype contract or OT. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by AFLCMC/XA or originate within any organization that AFLCMC/XA supports. 5.1.2 Successful Completion of Prototype A prototype project is complete upon the written determination of the appropriate approving official (program manager and Contracting/Agreements Officer) for the matter in question that the efforts conducted under a prototype contract or OT: (1) met the key technical goals of a project; (2) met the metrics incorporated into the prototype contract or OT; or (3) accomplished a particularly favorable or unexpected result that justifies the transition to a production contract or OT. Furthermore, prior to successful completion of a prototype project under this Commercial Solutions Opening, the Government can transition any aspect of the prototype project determined to provide utility into production while other aspects of the prototype project have yet to be completed. 5.1.3 Follow-on Production of a Prototype After award of a prototype using OT authority, the Government and offeror may negotiate a follow-on contract or OT for production or solution integration with or without further competition. Any concept/technology/solution successfully proven through a Prototype OT can be transitioned to a production contract. The Government reserves the right to award a follow-on contract or OT before the prototype is complete, under competitive procedures as provided in 10 U.S.C. 2371b. Any Call posted by the Government under this Commercial Solutions Opening could result in the potential award of a follow on production or solution integration contract or OT. The Government reserves the right to extend performance to all, some, or none of the selected solutions and decisions will be made based on the availability of government funds. 5.2 Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) Specifics In accordance with 10 U.S.C 2371b(c), if an Agreement for a prototype is utilized and if that Agreement provides for payments in a total amount in excess of $5,000,000, the Agreement will include a mandatory clause that provides for the Comptroller General the ability to examine the records of any party to the agreement or any entity that participates in the performance of the agreement. The $5,000,000 amount includes the base agreement plus options. Additionally, to enter into an OT for a Prototype agreement under 10 U.S.C. 2371b, one of the following conditions must be met: There is at least one nontraditional defense contractor or nonprofit research institution participating to a significant extent in the prototype project. All significant participants other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors. Parties to the transaction other than the Federal Government must pay at least one third of the prototype project total cost. The senior procurement executive determines that exceptional circumstances justify the use of an OT to provide an innovative business arrangement not feasible under a contract or to expand the defense supply base in a manner not practical under a contract. Further specifics and requirements as it relates to OTs may be applicable and included in subsequent Calls published under this Commercial Solutions Opening. 6.0 CLOSED CALLS This Commercial Solutions Opening will have Closed Calls that consist of either a one-step or two-step process and will be specified in each individual Call. For a one-step Call, only proposals will be solicited. For a two-step Call, white papers will be solicited first and then subsequent Requests for Proposals may follow after the government first reviews your white paper. Any part of this process may be modified or altered by AFLCMC/XA in the Calls or through an amendment to this Commercial Solutions Opening (e.g. A Pitch Day might be utilized). It is important to note that at no stage is AFLCMC/XA obligated to make any awards and all awards are subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by the proposer prior to the issuance of any contract/agreement award. 6.1 One-Step Closed Call Process 6.1.1 Call Published AFLCMC/XA would publish a Call via an amendment to this Commercial Solutions Opening. The Call would specifically state the Commercial Solutions Opening Call type is a one-step, Closed Call. This Call would provide a required date and time for proposal submission. The Call would also detail the specific AoIs being solicited for, required proposal content, evaluation criteria and detail other requirements unique to that particular Call. 6.1.2 Proposals Received Proposals that are received on time will then be evaluated according to the evaluation criteria stated in the Call. After this technical review is complete, AFLCMC/XA will notify each prospective Contractor that has been selected to proceed to the Contract Negotiations and Fact Finding stage. 6.1.3 Contract Negotiations and Fact-Finding If a company is notified that it has been selected to proceed to the next stage, then contract negotiations and fact-finding will occur. This includes contract formation, scope, cost/price and any other terms and conditions the Contracting/Agreements Officer wishes to discuss. 6.1.4 Award Decision After Contract Negotiations and Fact-Finding is complete, AFLCMC/XA will render a decision whether or not to enter into a Contract/Agreement with the prospective Contractor. 6.2 Two-Step Closed Call Process 6.2.1 Call Published AFLCMC/XA would publish a Call via an amendment to this Commercial Solutions Opening. The Call would specifically state that the Commercial Solutions Opening Call type is a two-step, Closed Call. This Call would provide a specific date and time when prospective contractors may submit their white-papers. The Call would also detail the specific AoIs being solicited for, required white paper content, evaluation criteria and detail any other requirements unique to that particular Call. 6.2.2 White Papers Received White papers that are received on time will then be evaluated according to the evaluation criteria stated in the Call. 6.2.3 Requests for Proposals (RFPs) Sent Companies who submit white papers that are reviewed favorably by AFLCMC/XA will be sent a Request for Proposal (RFP) to notify them that they have been selected to proceed to the next step of the process and submit a proposal. Additional details will also be provided in the RFP. 6.2.4 Incorporate Sections 6.1.2 - 6.1.4 After the submission of the white papers and the RFPs are sent to the Contractors whose white papers are evaluated favorably, the rest of the process is the same as the one-step, closed Call. Therefore, Sections 6.1.2, 6.1.3 and 6.1.4 are incorporated into this Section by reference. 7.0 OPEN PERIOD CALLS This Commercial Solutions Opening will have Open Period Calls that consist only of a two-step process. For this Call type, the process would almost exactly mirror Section 6.2; however, with the important distinction that white papers will be accepted at any time during the stated time period on the Call. This is in contrast to a Closed Call where all proposals are required to be submitted at a specific date and time together and follow a standard timeline for all participants. For Open Period Calls, the timelines are usually less structured and broader in nature. Typical turn-around times that Contractors can expect are usually stated in the Call. AFLCMC/XA reserves the right to modify or alter any of these instructions in each Call. 8.0 EVALUATION CRITERIA The evaluation criteria for White Papers and Proposals will be further detailed and/or expanded upon in the Calls. Solutions will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AoI, not against other solution briefs submitted in response to the same AoI. Disclaimer: No proposals or white papers are being requested at this time. Those will be requested via Calls published under this Commercial Solutions Opening. 9.0 GENERAL PROPOSAL INFORMATION 9.1 Proposal Content Below is the typical structure and required volumes for proposal submission. AFLCMC/XA reserves the right to alter or change the structure and content it requires for each proposal submission on a per Call basis. Title Page (does not count against page limit) Company Name, CAGE Number (if applicable), Title, Offeror, Date, E-Mail Address, Phone, Fax, Organization/Office symbol, and Address. AFLCMC/XA assumes no liability for disclosure or use of unmarked data and may use or disclose such data for any purpose. If a proposer is awarded a contract as a result of or in connection with the submission of proprietary data in the proposal, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent provided in the resulting contract/agreement. Proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences in accordance with FAR 52.215-1(e)(1) and (2) on the cover page: “This proposal includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this proposal. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: “Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.” 9.3 Classified Proposals Classified whitepapers/proposals will not be accepted under this Commercial Solutions Opening unless otherwise stated in the Call. If topics require classified work, the proposing firm must have a facility clearance in order to perform the work. 9.4 Security Security Classification will be determined for each Call/Award. If classified data will be accessed or generated, a facility and storage clearance, at the required classification level, will be required and the proposal will discuss appropriate personnel and facility clearances. If a submitter has any reason to believe their concept may reference ideas or operations that require special protection, the submitter should immediately contact the Contracting/Agreements Officer for further instruction. Additionally, if a DD254 is applicable for a Call/Award, offerors must verify their Cognizant Security Office information is current with Defense Security Service (DSS). 9.5 Promotional Material Promotional and non-project related discussion is discouraged, and additional information provided via Universal Resource Locator (URL) links or on computer disks, CDs, DVDs, video tapes or any other medium will not be accepted or considered in the proposal evaluation unless otherwise directed by the Call or Contracting/Agreements Officer. sig_964f8aed2d779ba5eaed.description: As part of its activities, the CEA/CESTA wishes to award corrective, adaptive and perfective maintenance services for industrial technical IT software and their control-command systems. These services include integration, mastership, consolidation, maintenance in an operational and secure condition, as well as software and hardware development for these control-command systems. The CEA therefore plans to set up a framework agreement for the performance of IT maintenance services for industrial systems of CEA/CESTA, including those of the Outdoor Testing Ground (TEE) and the Ile Longue base (ILO), called MISI 3. This agreement will be executed under a single-award arrangement for a maximum duration of 7 years and will be remunerated on the basis of lump sums, unit price schedules, hourly rates and penalty and care coefficients. This IT maintenance service for industrial systems (MISI 3) covers the following areas of activity: 1) Service Centre including the following activities: - Ticket management, - CMDB (Configuration Management Database), - ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) type processes, - User assistance and support. 2) Activity and project management: - Team management and steering, - Activity monitoring (indicators, financial, etc.), - Meeting management, - Document management. 3) Corrective and adaptive maintenance service for industrial systems (software, hardware and control-command): - Access control, - Video surveillance, - Utilities, - Supervision of experimental installations (test and measurement means), - Cabling works. 4) Infrastructure management and supervision: - Virtual and physical, - Maintenance in operational condition (MCO) of system and network infrastructure, - Storage and backup solutions. 5) MCOS (Maintenance in Operational Condition of Security) and SOC (Security Operation Center) System operation. 6) On-call service and HNO (Non-Working Hours). Indicative volumetry: - Number of annual tickets: 1 000 which represents approximately 10 000 technical actions, - Hardware inventory: 2 000 items of equipment (Operational Technology (OT), Information Technology (IT) and networks), - Number of systems: Approximately 80 industrial systems, - Document repository: approximately 300 technical documents under management, - Current and overall breakdown of activity is approximately 35 % for automation, 45 % for IT and 20 % for specific software. All these services will take place during the following hours: time slot established from 7h to 20h according to the CEA activity schedule. However, during peak activity periods, it may be requested to punctually modify the working hours regime. The rules for handling the various regimes will be detailed in the draft contract (communicated during the "Offers" phase). The contract is concluded for a maximum duration of 7 years and 3 months broken down as follows: - Phase 1 : preparation and takeover phase with a duration of 3 months, - Phase 2 : operational phase with a duration of 7 years (84 months) comprising 4 firm years (48 months) and 3 optional years (12 months each), - Phase 3 : reversibility phase with knowledge transfer of 3 optional months. This phase is included in the last firm or firmed-up year of the operational phase.
sig_964f8aed2d779ba5eaed.title: IT maintenance for industrial systems of CEA/CESTA (MISI3)
