sig_966964fa4ce72f0599dd.description: This procurement description outlines the context and requirements for Sunderland City Council ("the Council") for the appointment of a Managing Agent to provide a range of key services at the Council's Business Centres ("the Centres") namely, Evolve Business Centre, Sunderland Software Centre, and Washington Business Centre. The Council previously procured the construction and delivery of the Centres over the period from 2006 to 2014 (drawing on resources secured through the European Regional Development Fund ("ERDF") alongside the Council's own resources) to support the economic development of the city, creating facilities for businesses to start up and grow within the city. All of the Centres have been managed throughout their lifetime directly by the Council and together, as at end July 2025, are home to 75 businesses, collectively employing a total of 363 people. It is now considered that external expertise is required from a Managing Agent to provide a combination of strategic and operational leadership and management services to work alongside the Council in order to drive optimum performance from the Centres, both in terms of securing operational efficiencies and maximising economic impact (considered to be the dual objectives). It is proposed that the Managing Agent would be required to deliver the following core services on behalf of the Council as the owner of the Centres: • Strategic management of the Centres including targeted improvement of operational practices - with responsibility for procuring and appointing all contractors and with day-to-day supervision of the Council's retained staff operations. • Marketing and letting of vacant spaces. • Integrated culture of business development / support to stimulate business growth and expansion. • ICT Managed Service Provision available to businesses on an opt in / opt out basis and • Delivery of repairs and maintenance. Lot 1: .

sig_96883c60bb74ee0b4427.description: Connected Places Catapult (CPC) is a UK innovation accelerator for cities/transport, helping public bodies use innovation for better living/working/travel, and its initiative, the Innovation Procurement Empowerment Centre (IPEC), provides practical support, expert guidance and shared learning to overcome procurement barriers and bring innovation into the public sector. Councils are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve public services through innovative solutions. This work supports broader council objectives to enhance service delivery and address anti-social behaviour, while maximising value for residents. This notification seeks to explore the potential impact of AI in the public realm for local authorities. The aim is to assess market maturity, identify available solutions, and develop a procurement strategy for trials and recommendations to councils. Purpose of Engagement IPEC are leading this pre-market engagement exercise to explore the range of solutions currently available in the market to help shape the scope and inform the design of a future procurements for Councils. This market engagement is a strategic initiative that brings together a number of authorities, aligns requirements, and optimises resources for tendering. It also facilitates knowledge sharing across councils, ensuring a more coordinated and impactful approach. We are particularly interested in technologies and approaches that could address one or more of the identified challenges within the public realm. Depending on the nature, maturity, and potential impact of the solutions identified, this may lead to a procurement structured into one or more lots or delivered through multiple tenders. The final approach will be shaped by market readiness and a balanced assessment of cost versus impact. While the Councils will consider a range of benefits and outcomes (such as environmental improvements and social value), the current economic climate necessitates that all new spending and existing programs are heavily scrutinised for cost-effectiveness and efficiency. Please note: This is an initial market engagement and discovery exercise. As engagement progresses and additional authorities choose to participate, updates will be communicated through future notifications. The estimated value is highly speculative and may increase to include pilot activities, testing, and potential scaling. The final value will be determined following pre-market engagement and through further collaboration with participating authorities. Lot 1: .
sig_96883c60bb74ee0b4427.title: AI Technology Solutions for Public Realm Challenges

sig_96984682e48b8608a275.description: Introduction and Purpose Platform Housing Group ("the Authority") is preparing to undertake a major transformation initiative, Together in Data, which aims to create a unified, cloud-first data ecosystem across the organisation. At the heart of this programme is the implementation of Microsoft Fabric as the foundation of a modern, scalable, and secure cloud data platform. The purpose of this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) is to: Inform the market of this upcoming opportunity. Gather supplier insights that will shape our procurement strategy, solution design, and implementation approach. Understand market capability across cloud data platforms, Fabric-based architectures, data engineering, governance, and AI/ML readiness. Validate our assumptions and ensure an optimal, futureproofed commercial and technical route. This notice does not initiate a formal procurement process. Background Platform's current data landscape is fragmented, with multiple systems, shadow databases, inconsistent reporting, and low confidence in data quality. Staff experience frustration with data accessibility, reliability, and responsiveness. The Together in Data initiative proposes: A cloud-first, Microsoft Fabric-based data platform incorporating Data Factory, OneLake, Power BI, Warehouse, and governance tooling. A single, trusted environment spanning raw → working → curated data layers. A unified data model enabling Customer 360, Home 360, Repairs, Assets, Finance and other critical subject areas. A data ecosystem that supports AI, ML, predictive analytics, automated insight, improved decision making, and self-service analytics. Scope of the Proposed Procurement The Authority anticipates procuring a partner (or partners) to support the design, build, testing, governance, and early life support of the new data platform. Indicative scope areas include: 3.1 Core Technical Requirements Microsoft Fabric tenant and associated Azure configuration (security, workspaces, licensing). Development of raw/working/curated data lakehouse layers. On premise and cloud data ingestion pipelines. Data modelling, transformation, and semantic layer creation for enterprise datasets. Migration from an existing limited Microsoft data lakehouse structure. Integration with 3rd party data sets. CI/CD automation and platform observability tooling. Environment strategy (Dev / Test / Prod). Integration with Dynamics 365 CRM and Finance & Operations. Integration with other line of business applications. 3.2 Governance & Operating Model Meet the requirements of a Platform's data governance framework (including Data quality, lineage, cataloguing, and access control standards). GDPR compliant data retention and observability improvements. Support the enablement and operational activities surrounding Data Use Act, SARs, STAIRS. 3.3 Business Facing Deliverables Production of trusted Power BI datasets, dashboards, and AIready data assets. Establishment of a Platform wide data Community of Practice. Training and capability uplift for business users and analysts. Support for priority use cases including Customer 360, Home 360, asset forecasting, neighbourhood intelligence, and proactive home checks. Lot 1: .
sig_96984682e48b8608a275.title: Together in Data Programme

sig_96a70b8a007195fc2317.description: The tender for ODIN2 comprises an agreement consisting of two (2) lots: the Application Contract and the Operations Contract. The Application Contract covers the development, delivery, support and maintenance of a new internet-facing reporting system for the Danish Emergency Management Agency (ODIN2) and an IDP supporting access control for the Danish Emergency Management Agency's systems, as the current reporting system (ODIN) is to be replaced. The Operations Contract covers the operation of ODIN2. Both lots will be awarded to the same tenderers. The development of ODIN2 follows an agile methodology in partial deliveries in accordance with the established milestones in the Application Contract's schedule and is divided into four partial deliveries. The takeover day for partial delivery 1 and partial delivery 2 and the transition day for operations are planned for 15 December 2026 with a view to the go-live of ODIN2 on 1 January 2027. Subsequently, partial delivery 3 and partial delivery 4 will be delivered. The Danish Emergency Management Agency's new registration and reporting system ODIN2 (Online Data Registration and Reporting) must be used by the municipal rescue services and the Danish Emergency Management Agency to report information on their capabilities and emergency response activities to the Danish Emergency Management Agency. The purpose of ODIN2 is to generate a national overview of the rescue services' capacity and operations in Denmark. ODIN2 must support both the risk-based dimensioning of the rescue services and provide input for learning in operational actions within the services. Contract regarding development, delivery, support and maintenance, as well as additional services for ODIN2; Contract regarding the operation of ODIN2
sig_96a70b8a007195fc2317.title: New registration and reporting system for the Danish Emergency Management Agency (ODIN2)

sig_96eeae5e2a219a41c119.description: The dynamic purchasing system consists of two categories. The difference between the two categories consists in a differentiation of whether the customer in the specific procurement needs to evaluate on other factors than price. Category 1 covers those cases where the customer can have their needs met solely by evaluating the prices offered by suppliers, whereas category 2 is used in those cases where the customer needs to evaluate on both price and the solutions offered by suppliers (quality). Customers have the option to include, for example, switching costs when evaluating the sub-criterion price in category 2. Both categories can be used to acquire the following service areas, as described in further detail in Appendix C, Subject matter of the system: Standard software, support and maintenance agreements for standard software, installation/implementation and configuration, as well as related services in the form of training and consultancy related to standard software. Standard software and related services can be acquired within the following functional areas: 1) Application Infrastructure and Middleware, 2) Application Development, 3) Customer Experience and Relationship Management (CRM), 4) Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), 5) Supply Chain Management (SCM), 6) Project and Portfolio Management, 7) Email and Authoring, 8) Content Services, 9) IT Operations, 10) Operating Systems, 11) Storage Management, 12) Virtualisation Infrastructure, 13) Security, 14) Data Management, 15) Analytics and Business Intelligence, 16) Other Application Software (Collaboration Services, Enterprise IM and Web Conferencing), 17) Other Infrastructure Software. The functional standard software areas are described in further detail in Appendix D of the tender conditions, Overview of functional standard software areas. Standard software can be acquired as a product or as a service, for a limited or unlimited period, to be installed locally, or to be accessed via a browser or similar, where the licensor makes the software available, typically as a cloud solution. The system cannot be used to conclude an agreement on the development of new software functionality developed specifically for the customer. Category 2 is used in those cases where the customer needs to evaluate on both price and the solutions offered by suppliers (quality).; Category 1 is used in those cases where the customer can have their need met solely by evaluating the prices offered by participants. Covers the whole of Denmark.
sig_96eeae5e2a219a41c119.title: Standard software

sig_970871ef1406bcab2954.description: Request for Information Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense Avenger Weapon System Support Synopsis: The Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense (SHIELD) Project Office is conducting market research to determine if there are potential sources with the capability to provide engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201 (e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. The Government Point of Contact will be Ms. Lillian Irby, U.S. Army Contracting Command-Redstone, and can be contacted via email: lillian.m.irby.civ@army.mil. EMAIL ONLY, NO PHONE CALLS. Administrative: In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. Per FAR 52.215-3, Request for Information (RFI) or Solicitation for Planning Purposes: a. The U.S. Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information solicited, except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the FAR. b. Although the term “proposal” may be used in this RFI, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. c. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and should not be considered as a request for proposals or as a solicitation to do business with the U.S. Government. Avenger System Overview: The Avenger mission is to provide a lightweight, highly mobile, shoot-on-the-move, day/night, short-range surface-to-air missile and gun weapon system. Mounted on an M1097A2 High Mobility Multi-Purpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV), it engages Fixed Wing, Rotary Wing, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, and Cruise Missile threats. The Avenger M47A2 derivative system, termed Slew-to-Cue, receives cues to a track from an outside source and automatically slews to and follows the target beyond the line of sight. Avenger System Description: The Avenger Weapon System is a critical component of the Army’s Short Range Air Defense System (SHORADS). The system consists of: Two Standard Vehicle Mounted Launchers mounted on a turret A .50 caliber machinegun Forward Looking Infrared Laser Range Finder Environmental Control Unit/Prime Power Unit Auto-track systems and Identification Friend or Foe system Two 12V, 100 AMP lead-acid batteries connected in series (24V system power) 360 degrees continuously rotating, gyro-stabilized turret mounted on the HMMWV The fire unit can engage targets with missiles or the machinegun while on-the-move or stationery. The gunner can operate the system in-turret or from a remote location using the Remote-Control Unit. Scope of Work and Contractor Requirements: The SHIELD Project Office is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System and all derivative systems. Note: Proposers must have the required capability at the start of the performance period and must be able to perform all required tasks. Partial solution proposals will not be considered. Core Support Areas: The contractor will be responsible for complex system engineering, manufacturing, test equipment, logistics, and sustainment support. Support includes, but is not limited to: Engineering and Integration: Providing detailed technical expertise for Avenger Weapon Systems, Line Replaceable Units (LRU) (all variants), support equipment, and system interfaces. Designing and fabricating new solutions based on the current Avenger design to meet U.S. Government requirements. Performing complex system integration tasks. Providing software engineering and development for current and future software requirements. Providing in-depth system engineering analysis to support performance improvement, failure analysis, and other engineering activities. Testing & Analysis: Supporting test activities, including the assessment of test results. Providing design and technical support for existing and future contractor- and U.S. Government-owned test equipment. Performing reliability assessments and failure analysis with corrective action identification at the system and LRU level. Quickly and effectively analyzing and resolving hardware/software failures to restore operational capability. Logistics: Performing logistics functions, including technical manual generation/modification, maintenance support, system repairs and Field Service Representative support. Training and Fielding: Redesigning, replacing, installing, and training on all LRUs. Conducting training and system deployment, including New Equipment Training. Supporting sustainment training for deployed systems. Quality Assurance and Security: Complying with all Quality Assurance requirements (configuration management). Maintaining a facility compliant with all federal, state, and local requirements. Ensuring compliance with current DoW Information Assurance and Cybersecurity requirements. Meeting all contractor security, Communications Security, Federal, and DoW requirements, including Defense Security Service accreditation for both unclassified and classified information. Personnel Requirements: The U.S. Government requires a team of Field Service Representatives with expertise in Weapon Systems operation, sustainment, mechanical/electrical maintenance, physical security, and site maintenance. Security Clearance: Contractor employees will be required to hold and maintain a Secret security clearance. Operations: The contractor is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation and maintenance of Avenger Weapon Systems and sites. Response Instructions: Respondents must provide comprehensive answers to the following sections: Part A. Business Information: Please provide the following information for your company/institution and any teaming or joint venture partners: Company/Institute Name Address Point of Contact Phone Number Email Address CAGE Code DUNS Number Web page URL State (Yes/No) whether your company qualifies as a Small Business, Woman Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) Certified, HUB Zone Certified, Veteran Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Small Business, or Central Contractor Registration. Provide a statement describing your company as domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate country of ownership). Part B. Capability Questionnaire: Capabilities Overview: Briefly describe your company’s capabilities, the nature of your goods/services, staff composition, and management structure. Past Experience: Describe up to five previous projects similar in complexity to this requirement. Include contract numbers, a brief description of work, period of performance, supported agency/organization, and individual points of contact (Contracting Officer or Program Manager). Defense Systems and Avenger Experience: What experience do you have planning and executing the deployment and sustainment of weapons/defense systems? Detail any specific experience with the Avenger Weapon System. Maintenance Support: Describe your experience providing maintenance support, particularly in foreign countries. Collaborative Operations: Describe your experience supporting military personnel and working collaboratively with another prime contractor. Security and Information Assurance: Describe your experience with Information Assurance/Cybersecurity and associated documentation, as well as your capability to generate, handle, process, and store classified material and data. Simultaneous Deployment: Describe your capabilities and experience deploying and supporting complex weapons systems at multiple locations simultaneously, including Foreign Military Sales countries. Risk Management: Identify the top five risks you foresee in executing an effort of this scope and the mitigation steps you would take. Subcontracting: If relying on subcontractors, identify who you would use, what percentage/portions they would perform, their experience, and your existing relationship with them. Personnel Staffing: Describe your approach to obtaining and retaining qualified personnel. How quickly could you secure the necessary workforce? Training Capabilities: Describe your experience in classroom and simulator instruction. What are the top five risks for your company in executing these training methods? Inventory and Logistics: Describe your process for maintaining inventory records, reporting on-hand versus in-work balances, and updating repair statuses for the customer. Part C. Financial Capability: Describe your financial capabilities to successfully perform a contract of this scope. Detail any other relevant topics, concerns, or information that will assist the Government in shaping its acquisition strategy. Additional Submission Instructions: All responses must be unclassified. Marketing material is considered an insufficient response to this RFI. Respondents should indicate which portions of their responses are proprietary and should mark them accordingly. The U.S. Government will honor appropriate proprietary claims to prevent improper disclosure. Questions pertaining to this RFI may be directed to the Army Contracting Command point of contact for up to 7 days after this RFI is published on SAM.gov. The U.S. Government must receive your RFI response no later than 15 days after this RFI is published. The U.S. Government will receive responses via email submission.

sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.description: The contracting authority is PD - Berater der Öffentlichen Hand GmbH. A client of the contracting authority has established 2021 with the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG), an umbrella brand for sustainable construction in Germany. The Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG) is intended to promote sustainable construction on a broad scale in Germany and to ensure a minimum quality for "sustainable buildings". In addition, it is intended to create a legally secure basis for the award of funding that enables grants in the construction sector to be in compliance with social objectives (sustainability objectives). Since 2022 the contracting authority has been supporting the client with the establishment and setting up of a QNG office with all associated activities, such as a hotline, operation of a website and further development of the QNG requirements with the associated publications. In order to provide up-to-date information on the seal and the processes to be observed, the QNG website https://www.qng.info/ was developed and set up in the year 2022 with an external service provider. The QNG website represents a knowledge platform that processes ongoing developments and changes, and provides users with basic procedures, interfaces and assistance. The contract is awarded in two lots: - Lot 1: Hosting, further development and support of the existing website - Lot 2: Technical support (pool of experts) for the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG). The lot-specific tasks are described in more detail below. Bids may be submitted for one or for both lots. The contractor assumes continuous support, operation, hosting, and provision of the server infrastructure for the operation of the already existing website. Services include: 1. Website support, provision of licences 2. Website hosting and optimisation 3. Hosting and further development of an AI-based, self-learning chatbot The contractor shall ensure a seamless transition from 01. January 2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 1 is an EVB-IT cloud contract.; The pool of experts is intended to provide support for consultations on enquiries resulting from the application of the QNG in practice, as well as for the further development of the QNG requirements and the introduction and implementation phase of the revised requirements. Services include: • Support for the content-related further development of the quality seal • Support for the revision and quality assurance of the associated documents with regard to comprehensibility and technical correctness • Support for the creation or revision of accompanying materials such as FAQs and quick answers • Creation of training materials for certification bodies and auditors as part of the introduction of the revised requirements • Support for the processing of complex or technically demanding enquiries, where applicable support for the ongoing quality assurance of new FAQs and quick answers The commencement of services is 01.01.2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 2 is a service contract. There is no fixed purchase quantity. The estimated volume results from the estimated quantity specified in the price sheet. The contract is limited to 280.000 euro.
sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.title: Web hosting and professional support (expertise pool) for the "Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings" (QNG)

sig_9730b9a9ef0944dc616b.description: The subject of the public contract is the renewal and expansion of Fidelis security technology in the ICT environment of the Prague City Hall (MHMP) and the Prague Municipal Police (MPP), including the provision of system operation for both entities. Operational support for MHMP also includes the operation of PacketBroker technology. Fidelis Elevate technology is a key security element of MHMP, which ensures the detection of cyber events, their investigation, mitigation and remediation. Currently, MHMP operates Fidelis Elevate to the following extent: o Fidelis Elevate Network 1Gbit - provides in-depth analysis of network traffic at L2 - L7 layers with a retention of 90 days; o Fidelis Elevate Endpoint - analyses endpoint behaviour (5 300). The subject of this public contract for MHMP is therefore: a) provision of manufacturer support for Fidelis Elevate Network (1 Gbit /retention 90 days) for a period of 36 months; b) provision of manufacturer support for Fidelis Elevate Endpoint (5 300 endpoints) for a period of 36 months; c) perpetual licences for Fidelis Elevate Network 1Gbit with a retention of 90 days, incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; d) perpetual licences for Fidelis Elevate Deception for the protection of 501 IP addresses, incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; e) provision of operational support for the system according to the Catalogue Sheets for Fidelis and PacketBroker technology for a period of 36 months; f) development work to the extent of 150 man-days (MD) for the duration of the Contract; g) exit services to the extent of 10 MD. The subject of this public contract for MPP is: a) supply of Fidelis Appliance XA4 (HW) – 2 units; b) supply of Fidelis Network Sensor (HW) – 1 Gbit; c) related licences to the extent of: o Fidelis Elevate Network 1Gbit (retention 60 days) incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; o Fidelis Elevate Endpoint (1 400 endpoints) incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; o Fidelis Elevate Deception – 501 IP addresses incl. manufacturer support for a period of 36 months; d) provision of operational support for the system according to the Catalogue Sheets for Fidelis technology for a period of 36 months; e) development work to the extent of 100 man-days (MD) for the duration of the Contract; f) exit services to the extent of 5 MD. The execution of the contract will ensure the operation of key cyber security tools for MHMP and MPP, the protection and detection of modern APT (Advanced Persistent Threat) threats, and the operation of key tools for the investigation of cyber events and incidents, response to cyber incidents, including impact mitigation and potential remediation. The implementation and operation of the aforementioned tool will be carried out fully in accordance with the requirements of Act No. 264/2025 Coll., on Cyber Security, as amended ('ZoKB'), related decrees No. 408 – No. 412/2025 Coll. ('VoKB') and the regulations and methodological guidelines of the NÚKIB.

sig_9744a64f2368fa23a4d9.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Extreme Computing BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 20 Sep 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hrs. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 20 Sep 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 4 Oct 2023 FY25 by 30 Sep 2024 FY26 by 30 Sep 2025 FY27 by 30 Sep 2026 FY28 by 30 Sep 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Broad Agency Announcement for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to support research in the focus areas computational diversity and efficient computing architectures, machine learning and artificial intelligence in embedded system and architectures, computing at the edge, nanocomputing, space computing, and robust algorithms and applications. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $497.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 36 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $3M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99.9M ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023( previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Joel Moore AFRL/RITB 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-4958 Email: joel.moore.2@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. sig_977364f183ee85d7885c.description: The 'Network for Neighbourhoods' (Network) is intended to build capacity and facilitate peer learning within MHCLG's flagship Pride in Place Programme (PiPP). PiPP is investing in 284 places across the UK to support regeneration, civic participation, and community leadership. The local delivery model for PiPP centres the power of local people and partnerships, bringing together residents, the local MP, councils, businesses, and community organisations to produce a clear vision for their area through the establishment of a Neighbourhood Board. The Neighbourhood Board is responsible for producing the 10-year vision for a place, supported by interventions which are set out in their Plan. Neighbourhoods will decide how to prioritise funding, based on extensive community engagement. The Network is being developed as part of the support offer for Neighbourhood Boards and community leaders (as the end customer/user), aiming to build lasting community capacity and support inclusive, locally-led change. This will be in addition to the support already in place from MHCLG's Communities Delivery Unit, which provides a designated 'point person' to each place who provides direct ongoing support, helps places to interpret guidance, and builds connections into government. The Network aims will be to: • Provide Neighbourhood Boards with access to bespoke advice and guidance to support community-led regeneration • Enable strong community leadership, facilitating identification of current and future leaders, and equipping them with the skills, tools and confidence to drive change through inclusive engagement and effective community organising • Support peer learning and share good practice, including through events and a new digital platform • Amplify opportunities to 'crowd in' funders to create a multiplier effect by drawing in additional funding MHCLG are considering options to work with external delivery partners to deliver the first three aims, i.e.: • bespoke advice and guidance to support community-led regeneration; • supporting strong community leadership and engagement through capacity building activities; and • facilitating a network of good practice and peer learning, including through digital solutions. Further details on the proposed requirements and scope will be included in the Pre-Market Engagement document available via email request (commercialtenders@communities.gov.uk) Lot 1: .
sig_977364f183ee85d7885c.title: Delivery of the Network for Neighbourhoods, part of the Pride in Place Programme

sig_97bbc7bfa6252a48ca78.description: Science of Learning and Augmented Intelligence (SL) supports potentially transformative research that develops basic theoretical insights and fundamental knowledge about principles, processes and mechanisms of learning, and about augmented intelligence — how human cognitive function can be augmented through interactions with others or with technology, or through variations in context. The program supports research addressing learning in individuals and in groups, across a wide range of domains at one or more levels of analysis, including molecular and cellular mechanisms; brain systems; cognitive, affective and behavioral processes; and social and cultural influences. The program also supports research on augmented intelligence that clearly articulates principled ways in which human approaches to learning and related processes, such as in design, complex decision-making and problem-solving, can be improved through interactions with others or through the use of artificial intelligence in technology. These could include ways of using knowledge about human functioning to improve the design of collaborative technologies that have the capacity to learn to adapt to humans. For both aspects of the program, there is special interest in collaborative and collective models of learning and intelligence that are supported by the unprecedented speed and scale of technological connectivity. This includes emphasis on how people and technology working together in new ways and at scale can achieve more than either can attain alone. The program also seeks explanations for how the emergent intelligence of groups, organizations and networks intersects with processes of learning, behavior and cognition in individuals. Projects that are convergent or interdisciplinary may be especially valuable in advancing basic understanding of these areas, but research within a single discipline or methodology is also appropriate. Connections between proposed research and specific technological, educational and workforce applications will be considered as valuable broader impacts but are not necessarily central to the intellectual merit of proposed research. The program supports a variety of approaches, including experiments, field studies, surveys, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence or machine learning methods. Examples of general research questions within scope of Science of Learning and Augmented Intelligence (SL) include: What are the underlying mechanisms that support transfer of learning from one context to another or from one domain to another? How is learning generalized from a small set of specific experiences? What is the basis for robust learning that is resilient against potential interference from new experiences? How is learning consolidated and reconsolidated from transient experience to stable memory? How do human interactions with technologies, imbued with artificial intelligence, provide improved human task performance? What models best describe the interplay of the individual and collaborative processes that lead to co-creation of knowledge and collective intelligence? In what ways do the capacities and constraints of human cognition inform improved methods of human-artificial intelligence collaboration? How can we integrate research findings and insights across levels of analysis, relating understanding of cellular and molecular mechanisms of learning in the neurons, to circuit and systems-level computations of learning in the brain, to cognitive, affective, social and behavioral processes of learning? What is the relationship between assembly of new networks (development) and learning new knowledge in a maturing or mature brain? What concepts, tools (including Big Data, machine learning, and other computational models) or questions will provide the most productive linkages across levels of analysis? How can insights from biological learners contribute and derive new theoretical perspectives to artificial intelligence, neuromorphic engineering, materials science and nanotechnology? How can the ability of biological systems to learn from relatively few examples improve efficiency of artificial systems? How do learning systems (biological and artificial) address complex issues of causal reasoning? How can knowledge about the ways in which humans learn help in the design of human-machine interfaces?
sig_97bbc7bfa6252a48ca78.title: Science of Learning and Augmented Intelligence (SL)

It will enable the ongoing expansion of digital self-service and workflow automation capabilities in support of the Council's digital transformation objectives and the efficient delivery of services to customers.. sig_97d8f56e17fc9249007b.description: Subject: Implementation of IT support for tasks arising in connection with the European Union information systems interoperability project. The quantity of the procurement is 1 software development(s). The operation of the automated fingerprint and palm print identification system (AFIS) operating at the Institute of Forensic Dactyloscopy of the National Centre for Expertise and Research (hereinafter: NSZKK), the exchange of stored data and its sharing are mandatory tasks through national legislation and international (EU) obligations. The automation of biometric data services currently performed manually or newly arising due to interoperability, the establishment of procedural rules for new workflows based on consultations held with relevant domestic and EU organisations, as well as the IT developments supporting them have become necessary. The NSZKK intends to implement this IT support by connecting it to the AFIS in such a way that an interface enabling the automation of data exchange processes is developed, and a new software module is introduced by means of which the NSZKK can act as a decision-support expert body in clarifying alerts given by the multiple identity detection system (MID) appearing as an interoperability component, and can manage unsolved crime scene traces in the sBMS in the case of major crimes. The detailed technical requirements are contained in the technical specification forming an annex to the Other Procurement Documents (hereinafter: OPD). The NSZKK intends to implement the development detailed above on the basis of the Call for Proposals with the code "HAVE Plusz-1.4.1-24", within the framework of the project titled "Development of an interface serving interoperability tasks and automating workflows for NSZKK" with the identification number HAVE_Plusz-1.4.1-24-00001, on the basis of a non-refundable project support contract co-financed by the European Union, in the form of supplier financing. Considering that at the launch of this procurement the project support contract referred to above has not yet been concluded, the Contracting Authority is conducting a so-called conditional procurement procedure pursuant to Section 53. (6) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). Pursuant to point a) of Subsection (2) of Section 75. of the Kbt., the Contracting Authority may declare the procedure unsuccessful if its application for support has not been accepted or is accepted for an amount smaller than requested. Pursuant to the Section of the Kbt. based on 135. (12), the Contracting Authority also makes the entry into force of the contract to be concluded as a result of the procurement procedure subject to a suspensive condition in accordance with the provisions of the draft contract forming an annex to the OPD. The subject of the procurement falls within the scope of the equipment specified in point e) subpoint 2., subsection 2., Chapter XXV (HUML25) of Annex 1. to Government Decree No. 156/2017. (VI. 16.) on the detailed rules for the licensing of military activities and the certification of undertakings (hereinafter: Government Decree No. 156/2017. (VI. 16.)), and the service related thereto specified in point b) of Chapter XXIV (HUML24.). Subject: Implementation of IT support for tasks arising in connection with the European Union information systems interoperability project. The quantity of the procurement is 1 software development(s). The main objective of the project is the development of the software tool (HUbMID tool) necessary to perform the comparative examination of dactyloscopic samples forming part of MID alerts, as well as the creation of a user interface that assists experts in managing unsolved crime scene traces in the sBMS (searching, uploading, evaluation of candidates). The second objective of the project is the creation of a platform-independent interface (INTEROP_NIST_ROUTER) that ensures data exchange, on the one hand, between the national AFIS and the specialist systems of domestic organisations authorised to request data (partner organisations), and, on the other hand, regarding unsolved crime scene traces found at the scenes of major crimes, between the national AFIS and the European Union central biometric repository (sBMS) via the ESP. The detailed technical requirements are contained in the technical specification forming an annex to the OPD.
sig_97d8f56e17fc9249007b.title: Software developments related to interoperability

sig_97d99cf28ff2bd6e97f7.description: With a maximum of three branch programmes, the objective is to achieve a total of 40 GWh of electricity savings by the end of 2029, or even 100 GWh in the event of an extension until the end of 2032. The prerequisite for the implementation of a programme is to involve at least one trade association, active throughout Switzerland, as a multiplier that supports the programme conceptually and promotes it among its members throughout its duration. The programme encourages measures relating to specific processes of a given branch, which can be standardised and implemented in a scalable manner nationwide. The programme excludes measures already encouraged in existing ProKilowatt programmes (e.g. it does not support cross-cutting technologies such as lighting, compressed air, etc.) and informs the target group of these other support possibilities. To ensure the communication of the incentive programme, individuals from the branch speak out to show good examples and recommend relevant measures. The SFOE monitors the achievement of objectives and the cost-effectiveness of the programme using semi-annual interim reports and may adapt the subsidies. The SFOE may also interrupt the programme if the milestones are not achieved. The main services for the implementation of branch programmes include: * carrying out technological and market analyses in order to develop eligible measures; * establishing partnerships with trade associations, formalised in an agreement for the implementation of the programme; * the technical monitoring of the measures implemented as well as the efficient processing of administrative processes for the disbursement of subsidies; * the management and coordination of communication; * the drafting of reports, the monitoring of the achievement of objectives, quality assurance and the strategic development of the programme.

sig_98107f4a67bc8f3d16f7.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of management consultancy services. The System includes the procurement of management consultancy services within the 6 service areas below. The content of the service areas is defined in more detail in Annex C. Subject of the System: Service area 1: Strategy and organisational development. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following five sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Strategy analysis 2. Sub-area 2: Strategy development 3. Sub-area 3: Strategy implementation 4. Sub-area 4: Organisational analysis and design as well as 5. Sub-area 5: Structural implementation. Service area 2: Business processes and efficiency. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Process analysis and process optimisation 2. Sub-area 2: Outsourcing 3. Sub-area 3: Public-private partnership (PPP). Service area 3: Analyses and evaluations. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Analyses and evaluations. Service area 4: Systems and management. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Finance and economic management 2. Sub-area 2: Quality and risk management 3. Sub-area 3: Control and optimisation of administrative processes. Service area 5: Human resources. Under this service area, services falling within one or more of the following three sub-areas may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Leadership and employee development 2. Sub-area 2: Culture and behavioural development 3. Sub-area 3: Personnel policy. Service area 6: Green services. Under this service area, services falling within the following sub-area may be purchased: 1. Sub-area 1: Green services. The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase. Both categories concern the procurement of services, where those in category 1 are procured as hours, while those in category 2 are procured as a finished result (report, analysis, etc.). The procurement of services in both categories assumes that these are commonly used and generally available on the market at the time of procurement. The system can therefore not be used to procure services that are not generally available on the market. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure management consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase. In category 1, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to meet the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate).; Procurement of management consultancy services for task resolution. In category 2, customers can procure management consultancy services within the 6 service areas described in Annex C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in the following way: Purchase of task resolution at a fixed price.

sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.description: GENERAL This is not a procurement notice or request for tenders, and the notice does not launch a procurement procedure. The aim of this information request and market sounding is to obtain additional information on options available on the market and to hear suppliers' views on the subject of the procurement so that any subsequent procurement procedure can be carried out appropriately. Answering the information request or participating in the market sounding has no effect on the position of market operators in any actual procurement procedure that may be initiated later. BACKGROUND AND SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT Digi- ja väestötietovirasto (DVV) is planning and preparing a procurement through which, on the basis of the resulting contract or contracts, DVV may procure, as needed, the printing and processing services for the right-to-vote notifications (so-called notification card) and their annexes defined in the Election Act, as well as other related printing, enveloping and folding services. The whole to be put out to tender includes - the production of paper and electronic notification cards and their delivery for sending, as well as - the distribution service for paper notification cards in accordance with the Postal Act, and the return of undelivered consignments to the sender address - in the case of electronic consignments, their transfer for sending to the Suomi.fi Messages service, and the production of the metadata required for this - expert services for preparing the graphic layout of these consignments In addition, the procurement may include other information letters for European Parliament elections as well as regional and municipal elections. The regular elections during the new contract period in the years 2027-2030 will be the following: 1. Parliamentary elections 2027 2. Regional and municipal elections 2029 3. European Parliament elections 2029 4. Presidential election 2030 In addition to regular elections, the contract covers any other elections that will be held during the contract period. Occurrence in the contract period is determined according to the date of election day (in the case of the presidential election, 1. election). Such non-regular elections may be, for example, a presidential election held mid-term due to the death or permanent incapacitation of the president, or early parliamentary elections ordered by the President of the Republic, or elections to be rerun following a court decision as a result of an appeal. In addition to elections, the contract also covers corresponding procurements in state consultative referendums. The notification card is regulated by section 21 of the Election Act. Other election-related information drawn up by the Ministry of Justice may be attached to the notification card consignment. As a rule, in all election types, in addition to the notification card sheet itself, a list of advance polling stations in the recipient's local area and an information insert about the body to be elected in the election are attached to the consignment. In addition, in the presidential election, two notification cards are sent to each person entitled to vote, one for each (possible) round of the two-round election. Other attachments are also possible; for example, during the pandemic caused by the Covid19 virus, municipal elections held featured an additional insert page about health safety in voting. The smallest composition for a notification card consignment is 3 sheets (notification card, one sheet for the list of advance polling stations, information leaflet about the body to be elected), and at most the size of the consignment could be (estimated) 7 sheets. The purpose of the notification card is to provide information on the approach of elections and the recipient's right to vote in them, and to give them the opportunity to request further information and, if necessary, rectification from the authority in good time if they consider that any information relating to their right to vote shown on the notification card is incorrect. In some rarer situations, the notification card can also be used to streamline the voting procedure, but it is never a prerequisite for voting or sufficient proof of identity and right to vote at the polling station. Notification cards are drawn up on forms according to the formula confirmed by the Ministry of Justice (VaaliL 193 §). For paper consignments of notification cards, their manufacturer produces windowed envelopes with election-specific prints and takes care of enveloping the consignments. Regarding the regular elections of the contract period put out to tender, estimates of the quantities of electronic and paper letter post are presented in the annex to this notice. The stated estimates of the distributions of the format and delivery method of notification cards have been estimated on the basis that the legislation on the priority of digital official communication will be completed and its application will begin in the spring of 2026. INFORMATION REQUEST AND MARKET SOUNDING The information request section of this notice presents questions to potential tenderer candidates interested in the procurement. The information request aims to survey market operators' views on, among other things, whether it is appropriate to put the service package out to tender in one or two parts (production and distribution separately). On the basis of the responses received to the information request, DVV may, at its discretion, also hold more detailed bilateral discussions on the specifications of the procurement and/or request comments on the preliminary tender documents from those who responded to the information request prior to the actual procurement.
sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.title: Information request and market sounding: Production and distribution services for election notification cards 2027-2030

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. sig_982976e7de8277e9a83f.description: Preliminary Market Engagement Notice London St. Pancras Highspeed's current TVM430 signalling system is reaching obsolescence, creating increasing operational, safety and resilience risks. Without intervention, system reliability and lifecycle issues are expected to significantly impact network performance from the 2030s. Stage 1 of the upgrade programme—delivered with SYSTRA—produced an Operational Context Document, a Technical Strategy with long‐ and short‐list options, and a Strategic Outline Business Case (SOBC) in WebTAG format. This completed the Rail Network Enhancements Pipeline (RNEP) Stage 1: Determine. LSPH and its stakeholders are now progressing to RNEP Stage 2: Develop, requiring specialist external consultancy support throughout 2026. Stage 2 will resolve key strategic questions, including the preferred technology solution for replacing TVM430, the funding approach within the HS1 regulatory and concession framework, the suitability of innovative commercial models, strategic opportunities, and the project delivery and scope choices that minimise whole‐life cost. Additional strategic issues may be identified collaboratively during the process. Summary of requirement Stage 2 has an estimated duration of six months, extending if an option to complete on-site surveys is executed, and aims to evaluate a range of delivery options for introducing ERTMS on High Speed 1. The assessment will include but not be limited to benefits, costs, deliverability, and operational impacts. The objective is to secure full stakeholder agreement on a single, coherent project delivery strategy for ERTMS implementation. To complete Stage 2, the appointed consultant will deliver: • Confirmation of the preferred technical option, commercial delivery model, funding route, and integrated project delivery model. • Long‐list and short‐list optioneering across technical, commercial, and funding dimensions to determine the integrated delivery model. • A whole‐life cost estimate for the integrated delivery model. • A delivery schedule through to entry into service and handover to maintenance. • A comprehensive RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies) register in the authority’s format. • All Deliverables from the Deliverables Register (to be provided). • Satisfy paragraphs A.6 to A.11 of the latest Rail Network Enhancements Pipeline guidance to enable progression to the next phase. Required Outcome All relevant stakeholders support and agree to the implementation of a single, coherent project delivery strategy for ERTMS on High Speed 1. Timescales and Procedure The Contracting Authority intends to follow a Competitive Flexible procedure in this procurement. The Contracting Authority intends to publish a tender notice in April 2026 and award a contract in September 2026. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_98313257b2c69275491a.description: ***This is not a tender exercise*** The Education Authority Northern Ireland (EANI) would like to invite participation in a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to seek the views of the market for the future provision of education technology services (referred to in this PME as the “Education Technology Managed Services”) currently included in the EN(ni) contract for all Schools in Northern Ireland including but not limited to infrastructure managed services, supplier and service integration, cyber security operations and management, user experience and schools catalogue services. The purpose of this PME exercise is for EANI to gain a better understanding of the supplier market and the feasibility of its requirements for these services, the most appropriate contracting strategy, procurement strategy and operational approach, the capacity of the market to deliver the requirements. The exercise will also provide an opportunity for the market to highlight any possible risks or issues that may not have previously been considered. This PME exercise will inform EANI’s decision as to whether the Education Technology Managed Services should be procured as a single contract or procured as separate contracts (for example an infrastructure managed services contract plus one or more contracts for cyber security operations and management, user experience, schools catalogue services and supplier and service integration if they are not incorporated in the infrastructure managed services contract). If the Education Technology Managed Services are procured as separate contracts, this PME exercise would act as the PME exercise for the Infrastructure Managed Services contract and EA may, and reserves the right to (or not), conduct separate additional PME exercises in respect of the Supplier and Service Integration Provider, Cyber Security Operations and Management Service, User Experience and Schools Catalogue contracts if and to the extent that these services are not incorporated in the Infrastructure Managed Services contract. For the avoidance of doubt, this is the scoping phase of the project and is not part of any formal procurement process and there is no commitment at this stage to carry out such a process. Any information gathered will not be considered in any future tender exercise. Please note that participation or non-participation in this PME exercise shall not prevent any supplier from participating in any future procurement process, nor is it intended that any information provided shall place any supplier at an advantage or disadvantage in any future procurement exercise. Further information including the questionnaire can be downloaded from the documents section of the CfT on eTendersNI. sig_9842a73150a2753fb421.description:
The integrated, intelligent and adaptive traffic management system (TMS) which is the subject of this procurement is an integrated assembly of hardware, software and communications that offers the possibility of prioritising public transport vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists in traffic (at intersections), to the detriment of personal cars. The detailed technical solution is presented in the Technical Project, an annex to the Specifications. The integrated, intelligent and adaptive traffic management system is an integrated assembly of hardware and software that offers the possibility of prioritising public transport vehicles and pedestrians and cyclists in traffic, to the detriment of personal cars. The proposed technical solution consists of the following elements [modules], in order to meet the needs of the project implementation, in correlation and correspondence with the technical, functional and architectural solutions detailed in the previous design stage: - Implementation of the traffic management component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and distributed (communications network); the system ensures an adaptation of signal timings based on information on traffic flows received in real time from field equipment – adaptive traffic management - Implementation of the monitoring component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and distributed (communications network): the system ensures video monitoring of signalised locations, with a view to increasing road safety for all road users: drivers, public transport passengers, cyclists, pedestrians, including video monitoring with ANPR-type systems located at the municipality's road entry points; - Implementation of the public transport vehicle prioritisation component, with all its components: local (in intersections and signalised pedestrian crossings), central (equipment and software in the Control Centre) and mobile (in public transport vehicles); the system ensures an adaptation of signal timings based on information received in real time regarding the position of public transport vehicles, so as to ensure the fastest possible crossing of signalised intersections by these vehicles. From the point of view of the necessary works, the investment objective is composed of the following investment elements: □ Signalisation of 88 intersections; □ Electrical installation works; □ Rehabilitation of the pavement on Calea Republici street, the left side when travelling towards the city centre (section between Calea Republicii No. 190-192 (Bus line terminus) and the intersection with Strada Condorilor; □ Arrangement of raised traffic separation islands; □ Arrangement of transition zones (shared-space) in the area of intersections; □ Arrangement of green spaces; □ Repairs with asphalt mixtures of the carriageway in signalised intersections; □ Repairs of the carriageway and pavements following underground conduit works; □ Road markings and signs. For the execution of the works, the provisions of the specialist Specifications, part of the Technical Documentation attached to this Specification, shall be observed. For the optimisation of traffic and the realisation of a signalisation system compliant with European standards and which allows for the real-time identification of traffic values, communication between intersections, and the modification of signal timings according to traffic values for good traffic flow, especially for public transport vehicles, and equipment with modern and durable systems, the following types of works have been provided: □ Realisation of electrical conduits in the carriageway, pavement and green space. The connections between the traffic light support poles and the traffic controller will be made through a dedicated underground electrical conduit. □ Realisation of manholes with covers. At the points of crossing the carriageway and at changes in the direction of the route, the conduit will be provided with cement concrete manholes, 64x64 cm. □ Laying/Changing of traffic light connection cables. The electrical cables connecting the traffic lights and the traffic controller will be of the Csyy 3-19x1.5 type. □ Equipping/Replacing existing traffic lights with new traffic lights, which use LED technology, these having better visibility, lower maintenance costs and a much longer service life than conventional incandescent bulb traffic lights. □ Installing/Replacing existing traffic controllers with new traffic controllers, provided with equipment that allows communication between intersections, the introduction of multi-programmes or the possibility of adding new equipment or equipment with other characteristics (inductive loops, video detection cameras, etc.). □ Planting of new traffic light poles. The installation of simple poles and poles with brackets has been provided to double the vehicle traffic lights, thus increasing their visibility from at least 50m (according to STAS 1848/4). □ Each pedestrian crossing-type intersection will be provided with acoustic devices (for persons with disabilities) and with push-button devices (for confirming the pedestrian crossing request). □ Mounting of inductive traffic loops in the carriageway, which allow for the real and instantaneous identification of the number of vehicles entering the intersection. These data allow the traffic controllers proposed to equip the intersections to create signal timings according to traffic conditions and to optimise the operation of the intersections to the maximum.

The placement of inductive detection loops has been provided on the entry lanes to the intersection, on each direction, two for each entry lane to the intersection and one for each exit lane from the signalised intersection. After the realisation of the inductive traffic detection loops, the intersection will be able to operate in a local adaptive mode or it will be possible to correlate it with the intersections upstream and downstream. □ Each non-signalised intersection will be electrically connected to the network. □ Realisation of communication via fibre optics between intersections, thus helping to create a green wave, to correlate the intersections with each other in real time and to establish their connection with the Command and Control Centre.

sig_98a87365479d2353620e.description: Update: This is a further request for information based on the previous below Pre-Market Engagement Notice. Further to the UK2 preliminary market engagement notice published on 11 July 2025 (identifier 2025/S 000-039328), the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) is looking for the market to provide further input to help guide any resulting tender process. Previously the market has responded to OPSS’ request for information on the availability of Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) packages that will enable OPSS to gather data on harmful products on the online market (Amazon, eBay, Etsy, Temu and Ali Express together with smaller webshops and social media markets selling products within the UK). This supplementary request is for the market to provide information on its tendering preferences and pricing models to enable OPSS to ensure any resulting tender is accessible to all bidders and any barriers which could deter a supplier from bidding, are considered (and removed where possible). You are requested to respond to the following questions: 1) Would a tender process involving multiple stages / multiple staggered responses be more desirable than a single stage / single response process? It is anticipated that the overall bidding timescales would be the same regardless of number of stages involved in the process. We are particularly interested in the challenges any resulting tender would place on the resources available to you and whether a multi-stage or single stage approach would enable you to manage this requirement and your other business opportunities / commitments more effectively. 2) How would you propose charging for the online market data gathering service (e.g. a flat fee, an annual subscription, price per ‘scrape’, price per page searched etc.). We do not require your specific pricing, rather the type of model you would use to calculate the charges to OPSS. 3) OPSS’ annual budget is ~£400k per annum. Currently, OPSS are searching for over 3000 products on the recall list (Product Safety Alerts, Reports and Recalls - GOV.UK). For this procurement, OPSS would look to run searches on initially 7 online marketplaces, with the potential for this to increase to 56. Currenly, OPSS has 21 individuals running manual searches on marketplaces, spending approximately 660 hours per month doing manual sweeps]. Are you able to deliver an appropriate solution to OPSS based on the expected budget, and current and future usage? Please respond by 9am (BST) Monday 26th January 2025 via email to commercialddat@businessandtrade.gov.uk . Please note, this is not a commitment from DBT / OPSS to proceed with procuring a solution. At this stage we are still gathering information to determine how we can support the market by designing a tender process that enables potential suppliers to bid for and deliver a COTS solution which meets our budget and functional requirements. There is no guarantee that any resulting tender will align exactly with proposals made by the market to this notice. We reserve the right to change and amend the budget, functional requirements and timescales as necessary to meet our financial, operational and delivery needs. This is a request for information (RfI) The Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) are looking to understand if there are existing Commercial of The Shelf (COTS) software packages that will allow them to gather data on harmful products on the online market. At a minimum, OPSS will need the ability to gather data on products on the following online marketplaces: - Amazon - eBay - Etsy - Temu - Ali Express OPSS would also like the ability to capture product information from smaller, individual webshops and social media markets, selling products within the UK. The need for OPSS to get complete, accurate and quality data is the foundation to this discovery and will enable the fulfilment of other additional requirements that OPSS can benefit from pertaining to product searching. The desired results that the requirements aim to achieve as part of this work is: • Efficiencies in product searching • Better monitoring of previously delisted products • Ability to monitor seller activity • Better insights into problematic products • Increase in number of non-compliant product found/taken down • Increase number of prosecutions These outcomes will help enable OPSS to proficiently identify harmful products in the UK market and ensure consumers and businesses can buy and sell products with confidence. We are issuing this request for information to understand if the above software is currently available at COTS software. Please contact commercialddat@businessandtrade.gov.uk to request access to the full list of current expected functional requirements. Please respond by 9am (BST) Monday 28th July 2025 via email to commercialddat@businessandtrade.gov.uk with confirmation on whether this is a piece of software that your company would be able to provide. Please note, there is not commitment from DBT to proceed with procuring a solution. Currently, we are solely gathering information on the curent market and to understand if there are is an existing solution in the market that meets our needs. There is no guarantee that any potential procurement that occurs will be like-for-like with the requirements in this notice, and the Department for Business and Trade (DBT)/OPSS reserves the right to change and amend the requirements as they see fit. Please note that the estimated contract value and contract start dates within this notice are unknown and not confirmed. At this stage, DBT/OPSS is only gathering information from the market. sig_98b769b4954780386a45.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement, implementation and operation of a central clearing and settlement system for a state-wide In/Out ticketing system (In/Out BY) in public local passenger transport (ÖPNV). The system serves in particular: • the recording, processing and validation of sales and revenue data, • transparent and audit-proof revenue settlement (clearing), • settlement between the participating actors (processing of cross-network journeys / handling of the state-wide addition tariff as well as settlement of third-party sales between sales partners (mutual sales)), • the provision of evaluations and reports, • handling of best price, capping (e.g. daily caps), • correction runs, • user and interface management. The service is being procured as a cloud-based solution in the sense of a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) model. The contract basis is the EVB-IT cloud contract and the criteria catalogue for the EVB-IT cloud contract. The detailed technical and functional requirements and mandatory criteria are described in the specifications and the annexes to the specifications. Objective: The objective is the provision and operation of a highly available, scalable and secure system that: • supports complex tariff and network structures, • enables automated clearing processes and thereby maps complex clearing and settlement rules, • supports open and standardised interfaces, • ensures high transparency and audit-proof traceability, • fully supports both the addition tariff and third-party sales in terms of settlement technology, • can be flexibly adapted to future requirements. The clearing and settlement system must be fully available by 31.03.2027 and commissioned on 01.04.2027.
sig_98b769b4954780386a45.title: Clearing and settlement system for In/Out Bavaria

The applications in lot 1 represent two distinct applications with separately defined functionalities and purposes, but integrated at user level. The notice management application aims to perform activities related to the evaluation and issuance of notices, and document circulation allows correspondence circulation flows. Both applications manage AACR documents, digitalising stages and workflows. The applications are installed in AACR's IT infrastructure, and users use a single access interface. Requests for clarifications shall be submitted 18 days before the deadline for submission of tenders specified in the simplified contract notice. The contracting authority shall respond to all requests for clarifications on the 11th day before the deadline for submission of tenders. The Document Management software and the Notice Management software represent two distinct applications with separately defined functionalities and purposes, but integrated at user level. The notice management application aims to perform activities related to the evaluation and issuance of notices for technical documentation pertaining to targets in areas with civil aeronautical servitude or in other areas where they may constitute obstacles to air navigation and/or may affect flight safety in the territory and airspace of Romania, based on the provisions of Article 87 paragraph (1) of the Romanian Air Code of 2020, approved by Law No. 21/2020, of OMTCT 1185/ 2006 and of Article 3 paragraph 1 letter a point 13 of the Organisation and Functioning Regulation, annex to Decision No. 405/1993 on the establishment of AACR, as amended and supplemented. The document circulation application allows correspondence circulation flows in accordance with internal procedure PI-GN-CIC. Both applications manage AACR documents, digitalising stages and workflows. The applications are installed in AACR's IT infrastructure, and users use a single access interface. Depending on their duties, access to the various functions of the applications is achieved. The applications allow the grouping on the registry page of all correspondence at AACR level, both that received by email and that from the online forms on AACR's website. The document management application is addressed to all AACR employees, and the notice management application is monitored by DA, to ensure compliance with legal provisions regarding AACR's duties to issue notices in areas with aeronautical servitudes.; At AACR level, the application IT system for creating the statistical data pool (URL: statistica.caa.ro) is used, developed as a result of the requirements for reporting, collection and creation of the statistical data pool in accordance with the provisions of Article 4 paragraph (1) letter u) of the Air Code (Law No. 21/2020), of OMTI No. 1089/2012 (regarding the collection, analysis, centralisation and dissemination of statistical data from the air transport field) and PAC-STA ed. 2/2024.
