sig_99261c1bd47690033773.description: The subject matter of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) consists of knowledge management and artificial intelligence platforms, licences, and expert services. Actual procurements are made on the basis of separate requests for tenders through internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority specifies and describes its detailed procurement need. The subject matter of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for knowledge management, software usage rights, licences, and/or a software solution based on open source code. The subject matter may additionally include tools intended for, among other things, knowledge management administration, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, as well as visualisation. The subject matter of the expert services can be specified in areas such as the following: • Knowledge management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data governance and management projects • Conceptual, data, and interface modelling as well as architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for extract, transform, load (ETL) chains and integrations • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, administration, and monitoring for visualisations and reporting • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • User interface and application development (Chatbot, etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development The contracting authority does not commit to procuring any minimum quantity within the DPS. A procurement contract concluded within the DPS does not grant the supplier an exclusive right to provide the service. In internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, the contracting authority requests an assurance from the tenderer that the tenderer company, or those companies or persons in whose ownership, possession, or control the tenderer company is, or its subcontractor, is not burdened by sanctions imposed by the European Union or the United Nations (UN) or by sanctions or asset freezing decisions imposed by Finnish authorities. The contracting authority shall exclude from the internal tendering procedure of the purchasing system tenderers who do not meet the aforementioned requirement. The contracting authority also has the right to terminate the procurement contract with immediate effect if the supplier is burdened by any of the above-mentioned sanctions or asset freezing decisions.
sig_99261c1bd47690033773.title: Knowledge management and artificial intelligence services

sig_9936af3fe823c1bfa3a7.description: In the autumn of 2023, the HL Center decided to work towards a new permanent exhibition on the Holocaust. The new permanent exhibition will build upon and enhance the unique national responsibility that the HL Center holds for the dissemination of the history of the Holocaust and related themes. The HL Center has prepared an exhibition brief for the new exhibition. This document defines the overarching goals, principles for the development of the concept and thematic content, as well as the framework for the organisation and implementation of the project. It is intended to serve as the cornerstone for the realisation of the main project. A prequalification process will now be carried out, followed by a tender competition in the form of a competitive dialogue to select the exhibition provider who will collaborate with the centre in realising the new permanent exhibition. The main project is planned to begin in 2026, and the new exhibition is scheduled to open to the public in the autumn of 2028.

sig_9957d5582c173ef113c4.description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE – No. 75N98026R00175 Title: Biobanking, Laboratory Analytics, and Associated Informatics Services for NIH Biorepositories Agency: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Description This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources and (2) whether commercial sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Purpose NIH is seeking capability statements from businesses, and subcontractors regarding their abilities to continue the work of the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. These repositories typically: Receive, process, store, and biosamples from a wide range of biospecimen types (e.g. blood/derivatives, fluids, DNA/RNA, hair, cell lines, iPSCs, teeth, fecal matter, birth specimens and other tissues such as brain and other organs) at various temperature and storage conditions (e.g. -80C, liquid nitrogen; fresh, frozen, paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed) at scales ranging from tens of thousands to several million specimens. Serve dozens to hundreds of research studies across the United States and abroad. Enable broad, controlled-access biomaterial sharing to meet specific research objectives that further our knowledge of health Anticipate continued growth in biospecimen and data volume over the life of the award. Scope of Work & Required Capabilities Capable vendors should provide examples from current or previous projects when responding to capabilities. A. Sample Management and Storage Maintain secure, humidity- and temperature-controlled storage and tracking for at least 3,500,000 biospecimens in accordance with Best Practices, Clinical and Laboratory Standards, and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP; 21 CFR 58) with expert quality control and assurance procedures. Document the maximum capacity that could be achieved to expand storage beyond the minimum requested. Destroy samples per regulatory and consent requirements when no longer needed. College of American Pathologists (CAP) Biorepository Accreditation preferred. Maintain positive chain of custody and resolve data/sample discrepancies (missing data, incorrect information, misdirected samples) through issue tracking and resolution, coordinating with relevant receiving/data management teams (e.g. sites, site monitors, study staff). Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data alongside biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Centrally manage and cost-effectively distribute biosamples to qualified investigators approved through established access programs. Provide studies with collection kits and supplies, including barcoded tubes with human-readable labels. Provide research staff training for ordering supplies and collecting samples. B. Data Curation and Management Develop and maintain SOPs for sample receipt, storage, processing, QC, and distribution. Receive de-identified clinical, diagnostic, environmental, and phenotypic data associated with biospecimens from funded grants/contracts. Maintain an internal relational database (e.g., using persistent identifiers such as RRIDs) linked to associated data and participant and sample identifiers, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample and data location. Register and track biospecimens via an internal relational database with sample IDs (RRID) linked to participant IDs and associated data in the Contractor's auditable LIMS, with computerized inventory management and accurate tracking of sample/data location. Clean, standardize, and harmonize clinical data with cross-disorder phenotypic knowledge (e.g. different diagnostic systems or criteria, such as RDOC, DSM, ICD), incorporating data from electronic health records when applicable. Transfer data and sample IDs to controlled-access repositories or Data Centers (e.g., dbGAP, NBDC Data Hub or program specific data repositories). C. Laboratory and Analytic Capabilities Demonstrate laboratory expertise appropriate to the repository's sample types, which may include molecular biology techniques (e.g., DNA/RNA extraction, cell line transformation/immortalization), rigorous quality control, and tissue/cell culture (isolation, scale-up, and banking of primary cells). Provide CLIA-certification status. Provide laboratory capabilities for, but not limited to: metabolic, hematologic, and/or clinical assays high-throughput genotyping, sequencing, and gene-expression analysis Mass spectrometry for proteomics and metabolomics Advanced genomic and cellular techniques such as short- and long-range sequencing, chromatin capture, ChIP-seq, Cut-and-Tag, HiC generation of iPSC/neural stem cell lines CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing Analysis of RNA and DNA from Formalin-Fixed Parafin-Embedded tissue Provide scientific and technical expertise to evaluate and respond to researcher-submitted requests for biospecimen availability. Demonstrate that lead investigators and support staff have relevant experience in biobanking, LIMS, and database management Store and/or process histopathological tissue samples. Isolate, scale up, and bank primary cells from diverse tissue samples. D. Informatics Requirements and Cyberinfrastructure Develop, or manage and enhance (if already existing), a biorepository web portal (front-end and back-end), supporting existing features and providing updates/improvements as requested, potentially including: Synchronizing sample availability data with a public- or investigator-facing sample explorer tool to streamline discovery of related data and biospecimens across repositories Showcase published research and provide lay summaries Advertise repository resources For existing resources, support all currently available features, with updates and improvements as requested Where in scope, develop outreach tools (e.g., an integrated chatbot or public-facing portal) to help users locate biomaterials/data and discover related resources across repositories Develop or maintain backend infrastructure (e.g., server maintenance, microservices, relational databases such as PostgreSQL) and front-end website design/UI-UX. Maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) and require security documentation to keep systems compliant with applicable FISMA-level and other NIH requirements. Maintain, update, and develop Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and cyberinfrastructure for secure, interoperable data exchange. Capabilities for homomorphic encryption and distributed learning. Demonstrate experience and technical expertise to address all aspects of informatics requirements listed above. K. Collaboration & Governance Establish a strong collaborative relationship with the NIH Data Centers, study teams, and Institutes/Centers to enable modifications as the studies evolve. Serve as a co-signatory of the Specimen/Material Transfer Agreements developed by the funding Institute/Center. Be eligible to receive a Certificate of Confidentiality, adhering to requirements for protecting sensitive participant information as set forth in 45 CFR Part 75.303(a), NIHGPS Chapter 8.3 and 15.2.1, and subsection 301(d) of the Public Health Service Act (see: https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-17-109.html). Comply with all applicable human subjects protection, ethical, privacy, and data security regulations. Submission Requirements Interested organizations must demonstrate and document in a submitted capability statement extensive experience across the technical areas above, and include specific information on: Experience — An outline of previous similar projects, specifically the techniques employed in the areas described above. Personnel — Name and professional qualifications of personnel with specific experience in the work requested and knowledge of/experience in biomedical research. Facilities — Availability and description of facilities and equipment required to conduct this type of work. The Government will assess the appropriateness of professional and technical personnel classifications and consider any other specific and relevant information that would improve evaluation of respondents. Organizations should demonstrate capability to administer and coordinate interrelated tasks effectively and in a timely manner. Supporting documentation may include contracts in which the organization performed equivalent tasks (Government and commercial), references (names, titles, phone numbers, and other identifying information), and awards or commendations. An organization that does not have all the listed expertise, may respond by listing organizations with which they intend to collaborate or have as subcontractors to fulfill the requirements. Based on preliminary market research, the Government has determined that the requirements described herein do not meet the definition of a commercial product or commercial service as defined in RFO 2.101, and therefore, RFO Part 12 procedures are not applicable to this requirement. However, if a capable vendor believes that these services or products qualify as commercial under FAR 2.101, the vendor may submit a written justification for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Such submissions must be provided to the Contracting Officer no later than October 20, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. All capability statements should include: Company name and address Point of contact SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Phone/fax/email NAICS Code(s) Business size and status Capability information responsive to the requirements and qualifications identified in this notice Type(s) of business, if any (e.g., small, Veteran-owned, service-disabled Veteran-owned, women-owned, 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone)) NAICS Code: 541714 — Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology). SBA size standard: 1,000 employees or fewer. Submission Instructions Capability statements must be submitted electronically to: Shaun Rostad, Contract Specialist Email: shaun.rostad@nih.gov Secondary Point of Contact: Joshua T. Lazarus, Contract Specialist Email: josh.lazarus@nih.gov Submissions are due NO LATER THAN 1:00 p.m. EST on October 20, 2026. The subject line must include the Sources Sought Number. NIDA will not accept paper or faxed capability statements. Disclaimer THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement, nor does it constitute a solicitation or commitment by NIDA. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses under this announcement, nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information submitted. Any proprietary information should be so marked. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Respondents should ensure their response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of information or provide feedback with respect to any information submitted. Based on the Government’s market research, it is the agency’s assessment that the services described herein do not appear to constitute commercial services as defined under RFO Subpart 2.1, and therefore, the agency does not currently intend to utilize RFO Part 12 Acquisition Procedures. However, if an interested party asserts that these services are in fact commercial in nature, it should respond to this requirement and provide supporting evidence demonstrating that the services meet the definition of commercial services as prescribed by the applicable regulations.

sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.description: At the BWB sewage treatment plants and sewage pumping stations, the PI System from the company AVEVA (formerly OSIsoft) is used for the long-term archiving of process data. The Berliner Wasserbetriebe currently operate 9 PI Data Archive Servers. These are supplied with data via approx. 50 OPC Interfaces. In total, the measured values, up to 40.000 - 50.000 data points, are collected and archived in the smallest possible resolution (> 1 second). They serve as a data source for the Asset Framework, PI Vision, a simulation server, as well as for external customers who need to access live and historical data. For this purpose, the API interface of the PI System is also required. The retention of historical data goes back to the year 1999. It includes all existing measured values and data points. These are permanently mapped in the PI Data Archive and are therefore available for retrieval within milliseconds at any time. The following questionnaire is intended to evaluate whether a migration to an alternative system is possible and economically viable.

sig_99ad07f1569fba5f7fd4.description: Framework agreement for temporary agency work in connection with construction projects of Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg Lot LOT-0000: Framework agreement for temporary agency work in connection with construction projects of Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg. The State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg is the central service provider for the real estate management of the State of Baden-Württemberg. It looks after approx. 8.000 buildings, some of which are listed historical monuments. Its mission is to maintain, further develop and sustainably manage the buildings, plots of land and structural facilities so that they offer long-term added value for society, the economy and the environment. In doing so, the State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg handles all building construction measures for the State of Baden-Württemberg. For various building construction measures, the State Enterprise receives federal funds under the Federal and Municipal Infrastructure Financing Act (LuKIFG). The planning, coordination and implementation of these building construction measures give rise to an additional personnel requirement, which in some cases arises at short notice. In order to cover the additional personnel requirement in a demand-driven manner, the existing personnel capacities in the State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg are to be supplemented by means of temporary agency work. The aim is to enable the offices of the State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg to have the most short-notice and flexible access possible to qualified employees of various disciplines and qualifications via suitable personnel service providers when there is a concrete personnel requirement. For this purpose, a framework agreement for temporary agency work is to be concluded with several personnel service providers. This framework agreement is intended to define the conditions for cooperation between the State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg and the personnel service provider and thus form the basis for future temporary employment contracts. This includes in particular the following profiles: Profile 1 - Technical Project Development / Heat Transition State-certified technicians or persons with a university degree, in particular in the fields of technical building services, supply engineering, energy engineering or comparable disciplines to support technical project development and the preparation of heat transition projects. Profile 2 - Project Management Heat Conversion State-certified technicians or engineers, in particular from the fields of technical building services, supply engineering, energy engineering or comparable disciplines for the planning, coordination and implementation of heat supply measures. Profile 3 - Client Representation / Project Management in Construction Execution Persons with a university degree, in particular in architecture, civil engineering, construction management, construction project management or comparable disciplines to perform operative client tasks and to support project management in larger and more complex construction measures. The specific professional and other requirements for the respective personnel profiles result from the document "Requirement Profiles" enclosed with the procurement documents. The contracting authority intends to conclude the framework agreement with a maximum of four personnel service providers. The conclusion of the framework agreement does not give the framework agreement partners any entitlement to the award of a specific number of individual contracts, to a specific contract volume or to the utilization of a specific contingent of temporary employment services. The conclusion of temporary employment contracts takes place within the framework of individual contracts. Individual contracts are awarded by the responsible office of the State Enterprise Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg when a specific personnel requirement arises by way of a renewed call for competition among all framework agreement partners.
sig_99ad07f1569fba5f7fd4.title: Framework agreement for temporary agency work in connection with construction projects of Property and Construction Baden-Württemberg

sig_99e9197fd85bbe8c8d9c.description: The Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom invites Service Providers to participate to a Procurement of accessibility monitoring tool. Traficom monitors the accessibility of approximately 240 websites annually with an automated tool. Accessibility requirements are defined in the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. Traficom currently uses the SALVIA system developed for this purpose, which is based on the open source QUALWEB testing core. When the contract period ends at the end of 2026, we will map out the solution as a tool for monitoring work to check the accessibility of websites with an automated tool. Traficom acquires Software service for simplified monitoring of website accessibility as a SaaS solution. The Software service is used to automatically check whether a website contain con-tent that does not meet the accessibility requirements of the Act. Accessibility requirements are defined in the European harmonized standard EN 301549 Accessibility requirements for information and communication technology products and services. The objective of the procurement is to facilitate the implementation of the Subscriber's accessibility checks and to free up resources for actual monitoring work instead of developing and maintaining the current monitoring system. With the procurement, the Subscriber will have access to new features for monitoring work and new reporting methods that will improve the service received by the monitoring targets. We aim for four important strategic benefits: • Reliability: The system meets the need of the supervisory authority to monitor websites in accordance with the obligations set, and the testing rules are updated when standards or other obligations are updated. • Efficiency: the Supplier is responsible for maintenance and updates, which frees up staff work for monitoring • Quality: modern features and reporting methods improve the service to the monitored objects and reduce the workload of the Subscriber • Security: servers in the EU, the system is tailored to Subscriber's needs. The subject of the procurement is a Software service for monitoring the accessibility of websites as a SaaS solution, accessible via a browser-based user interface. This simplified monitoring procedure, the selection of targets and their number are described in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1524 in point 1.3 of Annex I (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX: 32018D1524#anx_I ). Traficom acquires a Software service that enables its staff to perform automated accessibility inspections in accordance with the simplified monitoring method. The Subscriber performs monitoring evaluations throughout the year. Accessibility monitoring is aimed at websites that can be freely browsed or behind a login. Traficom defines the monitored targets and sites annually, either at one time or in several batches. Traficom selects some of the pages or the entire site to be evaluated. Evaluations are performed to complete web pages in the website. Each of the web pages selected for evaluation are identified by a unique URL or by other means e.g. in cases where the website is a single-page app or otherwise contains dynamic content that cannot been reached with a URL alone without additional events performed by the user or automated scripts. Traficom shall submit to the Website Service Provider an inspection report on the performance of the inspection and its results, which shall include, among other things, the accessibility deficiencies found on the evaluated pages. If necessary, Traficom shall provide guidance to the service provider subject to supervision on correcting the deficiencies. Traficom currently supervises approximately 240 websites annually. It is possible that the number may increase to, for example, 500 websites due to regulatory changes. However, Traficom does not commit to the number of websites to be supervised. Websites selected for supervision will generally undergo one inspection during one supervision period. The number of pages to be inspected on a website may vary, but maximum number of pages per website is 150. The website may be selected for inspection again in the next supervision period, and therefore the previous assessments with reports must be available in the system. Traficom also performs in-depth review of websites. This in-depth review procedure, the selection of targets and their number are described in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1524 in point 1.2 of Annex I (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32018D1524#anx_I) At the moment in-depth review is done manually by inspectors. If the new Software service provides in-depth review, Traficom may implement the feature during the implementation project. The whole Software service and all Traficom's material processed in the software service must be located in the European Union or the European Economic Area (EEA).
sig_99e9197fd85bbe8c8d9c.title: Procurement of accessibility monitoring tool

sig_99f2649703aba91345f5.description: The NHSBSA are undertaking an RFI in relation to an Integrated Research Delivery Solution. NHSBSA, as digital delivery partner to NIHR, is managing the Research Delivery Data and Intelligence (RDDI) project which aims to create a new digital service, to provide a real-time overview of the delivery status of health and care research nationally. This service will provide information to patients, the public and key stakeholders including industry and health research. This will provide deeper insights into research performance, capability and capacity in research host organisations to the UK Government and other stakeholders. This is expected to support activity in England and may extend to the Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland (Devolved Administrations). The requirement for an Integrated Research Delivery Solution form part of the RDDI project. The Integrated Research Delivery Solution needs to provide the a system to cover three core capabilities: • Scalable workflow capability so that research data needs and activities can be managed in a secure, user- based, real time UK wide environment. • Data integration & transformation capability to allow data to be easily integrated and de-duplicated/transformed through APIs into and out-of the Integrated Research Delivery Solution. • BI/AI capability providing a real time data reporting and analytical insight to support a wide user base across four health and care administrations within the UK with tailored reporting needs. The RFI will be seeking high-level information to enable the NHSBSA to assess the market, and to inform the design of the programme and determine the requirements for any future procurement process. Interested parties must register an interest in this RFI via https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome (search opportunities using system reference C390630). The RFI documents are available within the Health Family Portal from 18th November 2025. Suppliers are able to request a 40min 121 slot with the project team ahead of the RFI deadline. Requests can be made via the messaging function within the Health Family Portal and 121 session will be held 2nd and 3rd December 2025. The response deadlines for the RFI is the 12th of December 2025. The estimated procurement publication of UK04 Tender Notice is 1st April 2026. Lot 1: .
sig_99f2649703aba91345f5.title: C390630 Integrated Research Delivery Solution

sig_99f8bcb4ae60df74e9bb.description: The Department of Area Development, Environmental Planning and Projects (GOP) is the reliable partner for (policy) implementation in the field with a view to qualitative space use, a sustainable living environment and society. The department is a professional in area development and cooperation. From a shared vision, it works together with various actors so that projects reinforce each other from coherence. As an inspirer, initiator or facilitator, it brings about creative processes in which partners join forces, win-win situations arise and conflicts during implementation are prevented. For this, it works proactively and in an integrated manner with a high-performance toolkit that is deployed with knowledge and expertise, and where it acts as a network centre in making it available. The department carries out, among other things, integrated planning processes, including in function of the preparation of regional spatial implementation plans. In order to increase the throughput speed of procedures and the capacity for preparing documents necessary for going through planning processes, the GOP department will call on the support of an external agency with expertise in spatial planning, the preparation of spatial implementation plans (including environmental assessment / plan-MER) and the conducting of planning processes at the regional level. This concerns about five spatial implementation plans on an annual basis.

sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.description: This Expression of Interest (EOI) outlines Macmillan Cancer Support's request for agencies to collaborate on designing, testing and delivering a new cancer information and support offer(s). The project is part of Macmillan's 2025 strategy commitment to reach more people living with cancer and to improve the support we offer for people who experience inequitable access to cancer care and treatment. The design challenge for this project is "How Might We develop a scalable solution that helps people understand their rights, choices and influence in decisions about their care, irrespective of their confidence, self-advocacy skills or system knowledge?" This is an end-to-end Innovation project that we require to be delivered in its entirety by the supplier(s), with input and guidance from Macmillan. This includes insight development and analysis, solution development, prototyping and testing of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). The solution should be scalable and likely be digital or include digital elements. The supplier must have extensive experience designing with communities and individuals that are marginalised. The supplier should be an expert in approaches including designing from the margins and embed meaningful and equitable participatory approaches into every phase of the project. Given the nature of the requirements, we are open to working with 2 suppliers who can deliver different elements or phases of the project. The agency must be able to recruit participants who reflect Macmillan's priority cancer support audiences to take part in user research, co-design and testing of solutions; people who have been diagnosed with cancer in the past 5 years. This includes people who are currently undergoing anti-cancer treatment (more details in attachment). Timelines • Expression of interest response deadline by 10/03/2026. • Selected agencies will receive the full RFP pack in March / April. • The anticipated project duration is 4-6 months from kick-off. The final timeline will be agreed with Macmillan during the tender process. Supplier Response Instructions Via email, interested suppliers should provide: (1) A brief outline of their research, design and innovation approach, including how they will use design from the margin approaches (see examples here); (2) evidence of prior engagement and participatory work with marginalised communities (3) evidence of developing and delivering scalable products and/or services (especially digital) (4) identification of gaps in their ability to meet the full requirements and if there are gaps (5) willingness to partner with another agency. Responses at this stage do not need to be extensive. Responses should be sent to procurement@macmillan.org.uk with the subject line EOI - Innovation Advocacy/Empowerment.
sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.title: Expression of Interest for a Macmillan Cancer Support Innovation project

sig_99fa581350b0946367f1.description: MSB has a need of expert consulting in the field of mission critical communication services for PPDR. MSB has chosen to divide the procurement into 3 different areas: Area 1: Experts in the field of 4G and 5G Mission Critical PPDR Networks Area 2: Experts in the mobile ecosystem for Mission Critical Networks and Services Area 3: Supporting services in Mission Critical projects and programs The areas are further specified in the procurement documents. The purpose of this dynamic purchasing system is to meet MSB’s needs of expert consulting in the field of mission critical communication services for PPDR. Due to the fact that MSB has a broad need for different skills within the area, MSB has chosen to divide the procurement into 3 different areas, see below: Area 1: Experts in the field of 4G and 5G Mission Critical PPDR Networks Area 2: Experts in the mobile ecosystem for Mission Critical Networks and Services Area 3: Supporting services in Mission Critical projects and programs These areas are specified in more detail below. Specific procurement through the DPS will be carried out within these 3 different competence areas where the supplier must be able to provide competence with a relevant focus and level of competence for the current area and need. Specific procurements may refer to contracts with one of more suppliers. MSB might procure both junior and senior consultants, within each area, depending on the scope and nature of the assignment. Rakel G2 will be built as a hybrid technology based on a Multi Operator Core Network (MOCN) architecture, where a government core network is connected to a dedicated radio access network (RAN) in the 700 MHz band together with one or more Mobile Network Operator (MNO) RAN. It will use SGSI for fixed connections and WIS is one of the applications that will exist within the ecosystem The long-term goal for Rakel G2 is to provide 3GPP-standardised mission critical services in an ecosystem of multi-vendor system technologies. MSB’s intention is to make the systems interoperable during the transition period, allowing users to communicate with each other seamlessly regardless of the system used. 1. The subject of the contract is the implementation of an integrated IT and OT cybersecurity architecture together with the organisational preparation of the Contracting Authority as part of the 'Cyber-secure Waterworks' grant project. 2. Acting on the basis of the Act of 16 April 1993 on Combating Unfair Competition (Journal of Laws of 2026, item 85), the Contracting Authority excludes the transparency of part of the Technical Specification (OPZ). Technical and organisational information concerning competence and organisational gaps, the Contracting Authority's needs in the field of cybersecurity, ICT systems and applied security mechanisms, which constitute a trade secret and the disclosure of which could lead to an increased risk of a cybersecurity breach, in particular by enabling the identification of system architecture or potential vulnerabilities, or techniques and tactics for securing infrastructure, are subject to exclusion. The scope of the transparency exclusion has been limited to information necessary to protect the security of the enterprise, including ICT systems, and does not violate the principles of fair competition or equal treatment of contractors, while ensuring that contractors have access to information necessary to prepare tenders. The subject of the contract includes a coherent security model combining technical, organisational and competence-based solutions. Although individual elements may be general in nature, their combined presentation and reference to the Contracting Authority's actual environment leads to the disclosure of the overall security architecture. Disclosure of such a consolidated picture could enable unauthorised persons to identify the security architecture, incident response methods, dependencies between systems and potential weaknesses, which consequently increases the risk of a successful attack. In accordance with the approach based on MITRE ATT&CK, knowledge of protection mechanisms, organisational procedures and user behaviour can be used at various stages of the attack chain, including the preparation, reconnaissance and privilege escalation phases. The Contracting Authority emphasises that the subject of the contract concerns systems of importance for ensuring the continuity of public service provision, and its goal is to achieve a real, operational level of resilience against cyber threats. The exclusion of transparency has been applied as a proportionate measure aimed at protecting the security of the Contracting Authority, while ensuring that contractors have access to full documentation on equal terms, upon meeting confidentiality requirements. 3. The transparent part of the OPZ constitutes Annex no. 8 to the SWZ 4. The non-transparent part of the OPZ, constituting Annex no. 9 to the SWZ, will be made available to the Contractor who submits an appropriate application together with a confidentiality statement, the template of which constitutes Annex no. 10 to the SWZ, on the terms set out below 5. The deadline for submitting the application referred to in point 4 expires 7 days before the designated day for submitting tenders. The Contracting Authority may leave applications submitted after this deadline unexamined. 6. An application for access to the non-transparent part of the OPZ may be submitted only by a Contractor who demonstrates the application of organisational and technical measures ensuring the protection of confidential information. The Contracting Authority will consider the above condition to be met in particular by having an implemented information security management system compliant with the ISO/IEC 27001 standard or equivalent, confirmed by a certificate issued by an accredited certification body, or by holding a valid industrial security certificate of any level, or another document issued by independent bodies confirming the application of organisational and technical measures ensuring the protection of information for any industry, e.g., a valid TISAX certificate (minimum level AL2) or a current SOC 2 Type II audit report. The Contractor shall attach a certificate/document confirmed as a true copy of the original as an attachment to the application referred to in point 4 7. The application together with the confidentiality statement shall be signed by a person authorised to represent the Contractor or a duly authorised proxy. In the case of acting through a proxy, an appropriate power of attorney must be attached to the application. 8. The application, signed with a qualified electronic signature, must be submitted via the Open Nexsus purchasing platform no later than 7 days before the deadline for submitting tenders, with the proviso that the Contracting Authority is not responsible for the inability to prepare a tender in the event of submitting an application within a time limit that makes it impossible to review the documentation and prepare a tender before the deadline for submitting tenders. 9. The Contracting Authority will make the non-transparent part of the OPZ available after receiving a complete application submitted in accordance with the SWZ. In the event of identifying formal deficiencies in the application, the Contracting Authority may call upon the Contractor to supplement them within a specified time limit. Access to the non-transparent part of the OPZ will be granted after the effective supplementation of formal deficiencies. 10. Information contained in the non-transparent part of the OPZ may be used solely for the purpose of preparing and submitting a tender in these proceedings. It is forbidden to disclose it to third parties, with the exception of persons involved on the Contractor's side in the preparation of the tender, provided that these persons are obliged to maintain confidentiality to at least the same extent as specified in the Contractor's statement. The subject of the contract is the implementation of an integrated IT and OT cybersecurity architecture together with the organisational preparation of the Contracting Authority as part of the 'Cyber-secure Waterworks' grant project. 2.

Acting on the basis of the Act of 16 April 1993 on Combating Unfair Competition (Journal of Laws of 2026 item 85), the Contracting Authority excludes the transparency of part of the Description of the Subject of the Contract (OPZ). Excluded are technical and organisational information concerning competence and organisational gaps, the Contracting Authority's needs in the scope of cybersecurity, ICT systems and applied security mechanisms, which constitute a trade secret and the disclosure of which could lead to an increased risk of a cybersecurity breach, in particular by enabling the identification of system architecture or potential vulnerabilities, or techniques and tactics for securing infrastructure. The scope of the transparency exclusion has been limited to information necessary to protect the security of the enterprise, including ICT systems, and does not violate the principles of fair competition or equal treatment of economic operators, while ensuring that economic operators have access to information necessary to prepare tenders. The subject of the contract includes a coherent security model combining technical, organisational and competence-based solutions. Although individual elements may be of a general nature, their combined presentation and reference to the actual environment of the Contracting Authority leads to the disclosure of the overall security architecture. Disclosure of such a consolidated picture could enable unauthorised persons to identify the security architecture, methods of responding to incidents, dependencies between systems and potential weaknesses, which consequently increases the risk of a successful attack. In accordance with the approach based on MITRE ATT&CK, knowledge of protection mechanisms, organisational procedures and user behaviour can be used at various stages of the attack chain, including in the preparation, reconnaissance and privilege escalation phases. The Contracting Authority emphasises that the subject of the contract concerns systems of importance for ensuring the continuity of public service provision, and its objective is to achieve a real, operational level of resilience to cyber threats. The exclusion of transparency has been applied as a proportionate measure aimed at protecting the security of the Contracting Authority, while simultaneously ensuring that economic operators have access to full documentation on equal terms, upon meeting confidentiality requirements. 3. The Contracting Authority shall consider the above condition to be met in particular by having an implemented information security management system compliant with the ISO/IEC 27001 standard or equivalent, confirmed by a certificate issued by an accredited certification body, or by holding a valid industrial security certificate of any level or another document issued by independent bodies confirming the application of organisational and technical measures ensuring the protection of information for any industry, e.g. a valid TISAX certificate (minimum level AL2) or a current SOC 2 Type II audit report. sig_9a39d4d91f11d44edd3e.description: Environment Agency (EA) Asset Management Software System delivering an enterprise Asset Management platform. EA are looking to secure a platform provision that is sufficiently flexible to deliver those capabilities in the best way utilising current and future technologies. This is a Request for Information (RFI) and relates to Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) only, not a procurement exercise. The objective of this RFI and PME is for the Environment Agency (EA), the Authority, to obtain key information to understand the market's capability, innovation, approaches, on what it has to offer and how it may be able to meet the EA's needs both now, and in the future. Further to the previously published pipeline notice, please be aware that the Authority plans to publish the Invitation to Tender (ITT) for this via a potential Competitive Flexible Procedure by early September 2026. It should be noted that this planned procurement is subject to internal governance and approvals. The EA reserves the right to alter any aspect of this planned procurement notice before a tender notice is published, or to not proceed with the procurement in any way. This notice summarises certain aspects of the procurement but does not purport to contain complete descriptions of it, nor to be all inclusive or contain all the information that a prospective tenderer may require when determining whether to take part in any subsequent tender notice to be published. The Environment Agency (EA) are seeking to procure an Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system, which is sufficiently flexible to deliver ISO 55000 compliance and asset management capabilities, utilising current and future technologies. EA will be seeking suppliers that can potentially provide: (a) A unified system with strong standardisation and governance (b) Centralises information storage with consistent formats and locations (c) Streamlines processes to reduce inefficiencies, duplication, and costs (d) Enhances data accessibility to support informed decision-making and effective risk management (e) Complies with ISO 55000, 19650, and 9000 (f) Should provide a simple, intuitive, and partially automated user experience (g) Preference for a unified platform; integrated solutions also acceptable (h) Suppliers must support migration of existing records with metadata tagging (i) Enable file retrieval using metadata and spatial context (j) Solution must allow full export of files, metadata, and configurations to avoid vendor lock-in The objectives of EAM are: (a) Implement an asset management system that is compliant with the Institute of Asset Management's (IAM) - An Anatomy. (b) Create a single source of truth supporting the entire asset lifecycle. (c) Enable accurate, trusted Business Intelligence. (d) Achieve ISO19650 and ISO55000 compliance. (e) Improve file/data accessibility, storage, sharing, and user experience. (f) Enhanced data governance and risk mitigation (e.g., reduced security and legal risks). (g) Reduced inefficiencies, such as duplication and process waste. (h) Support carbon reduction and improved sustainability through streamlined practices Procurement Reference. Lot 1: .

sig_9a60a56c9b973ba6986c.description: YPO is developing a new national Training Solutions Framework designed to provide public sector organisations with flexible, compliant access to a broad range of training and development services. The framework is intended to support both off-the-shelf and bespoke training requirements across multiple professional and operational disciplines. YPO is the sole public sector buying organisation for this procurement. Our frameworks provide compliant routes to market enabling public sector organisations to procure services efficiently while ensuring value for money and regulatory compliance. The proposed framework aims to: • Provide access to a wide range of accredited and non-accredited training solutions • Support both digital and face-to-face delivery models • Offer flexible procurement routes including Award Without Competition and Competitive Selection Process • Enable access to innovative training methods and emerging learning technologies • Support social value delivery aligned with public sector priorities YPO is developing this framework to replace the current 999 Training DPS with a solution that is industry-leading in scope and capability. The aim is to for the new framework to feature an online platform supporting both Award Without Competition and Competitive Selection Process (PA23) routes. It will cover a broader range of training than the existing DPS, including innovative and in-demand areas not currently available, ensuring public sector organisations have access to the latest learning and development solutions. Indicative Framework Structure YPO is proposing that the new Training Solutions Framework will be structured to support a wide range of training delivery models, providing public sector organisations with access to both standardised and specialist training requirements through flexible procurement routes. The framework is currently expected to be divided into four lots, designed to offer clarity and ease of access while accommodating diverse learning needs, including digital, face-to-face, and blended approaches. This structure is indicative and may be refined following market engagement feedback to ensure it aligns with both customer requirements and the full capability of the market. The framework’s flexible lot and delivery model design will allow customers to procure training solutions efficiently and compliantly, whether accessing off-the-shelf courses via Award Without Competition or bespoke solutions through Competitive Selection Process (PA23). By structuring the framework in this way, YPO aims to ensure that public sector organisations can access a comprehensive, innovative, and responsive training offering that evolves to meet emerging industry trends and learning needs. Lot 1 – Off-the-Shelf Training Solutions This lot is intended to provide access to pre-defined, standardised training courses that can be delivered with minimal or no bespoke adaptation. Training may be delivered via classroom, virtual, or e-learning methods. YPO is exploring the use of a digital catalogue or platform to support Award Without Competition functionality, allowing customers to filter and select courses based on defined criteria such as subject area, delivery method, location, and pricing structure. YPO is considering the inclusion of defined training categories within this lot to ensure customers can easily identify providers with relevant expertise and experience for the training opportunities they require. Lot 2 – Bespoke Training Solutions (Competitive Selection Process) This lot is intended to support customers requiring tailored or customised training programmes designed to meet specific organisational or operational requirements. Services under this lot are expected to be awarded via Competitive Selection Process to allow customers to refine specifications, delivery methods, and outcomes aligned to their individual needs. YPO is considering the inclusion of defined training categories within this lot to ensure customers can easily identify providers with relevant expertise and experience for the training opportunities they require. Lot 3 – Managed Service Provision (MSP) for Training This lot is intended to provide customers with access to managed training service providers who can oversee end-to-end training requirements. This may include training needs analysis, supplier management, booking and administration services, performance monitoring, reporting, and strategic workforce development support. Lot 4 – Specialist and Regulated Training This lot is intended to support highly specialised or regulated training disciplines where suppliers are required to meet specific accreditation, legislative, or regulatory standards. This may include operational, safety-critical, or compliance-driven training areas. YPO is considering the inclusion of defined training categories within this lot to ensure customers can easily identify providers with relevant expertise and certifications. Training Categories YPO is considering incorporating defined training categories across relevant lots to support supplier specialisms and improve customer navigation of the framework. The final category structure will be informed by market engagement responses and customer demand to ensure it reflects current and emerging training requirements. If you would like to be involved in shaping the future of training provision for the public sector, we encourage you to participate in this market engagement exercise. Lot 1: .

sig_9a688150d1a2e7e4c00c.description: Data collection for the Information System on the Road and Motorway Network of the CR (ISSDS CR) is organised by the Road Databank Department and NDIC Ostrava. This involves continuous and uninterrupted collection of data for the construction activity register (RSČ), road inventory description (PPK), junction description (PK) and pavement structural layers (KV). Suppliers of this service also provide methodological assistance to individual road property managers (ŘSD CR Administration and Workshops, district and regional road authorities), quality control of data for road inventory descriptions, junction descriptions, pavement structural layers, and maintaining their up-to-date status. The delivery of the required data is a highly specialised activity that takes place concurrently in time across individual regions, which is why it is not ideal to carry it out from a single centre. The activity further requires detailed knowledge of the monitored roads in the given region, systematic activity, long-term training, regular training courses, experience in data collection, and last but not least, special equipment and modification of the measuring vehicle. Data from the aforementioned activities will be used, inter alia, for the planned and gradually implemented pavement management system (PMS). The CR is divided into 7 reporting regions as follows: 1. sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.description: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) is planning a tender for a condition monitoring system for its Kuopio office. THL is an independent state expert and research institute that promotes the well-being, health and safety of people. The institute's laboratories store millions of samples as well as reagents required for analytics in various storage conditions. The condition monitoring system must centrally collect temperature and alarm data from all measurement points. The primary objective of the system is to provide alarms when temperature limits are exceeded and to manage these alarms. The system must also be able to monitor and record condition data in both normal and alarm conditions. Monitoring and operational update tasks are intended to be performed by THL users. The intention is that the system will include all components required from measurement to alarm and data recording, with the exception of THL's existing sensors used in deep-freeze freezers (Pt100), which are intended to be used as part of the system. THL's Kuopio office deep-freeze freezers currently use approximately 20 Pt100 sensors. The deep-freeze freezers have a separate 4-conductor Pt-100 sensor, which is attached to the transmitter with a spring loaded connector. REGISTRATION INSTRUCTIONS FOR MARKET SURVEY (HEREINAFTER MARKET DIALOGUE): Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 1.10.2025 at 12:00 by email to kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the following information: - Message subject: "Olosuhdevalvontajärjestelmä Kuopion toimipisteeseen - markkinavuoropuhelu" - Message content: 1) Company name and business ID 2) Contact person's name and email address 3) Experience in supplying a condition monitoring system (in what kind of environment does the company's monitoring system operate) 4) Do you have any obstacles to using the above-described THL-owned sensors as part of your system? 5) How would the existing sensors (Pt-100) be connected to transmitters/SaaS service in your system? 6) If the information provided above is not sufficient, what information do you still need about the sensors owned by THL? 7) What is the response time for maintenance, troubleshooting, and delivery of replacement and spare equipment to Kuopio? IMPLEMENTATION OF MARKET DIALOGUE: The contracting authority will send draft materials of the tender for a written comment round as the preparation process progresses. No compensation will be paid to those who participated in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy acts in a consulting role in the market dialogue and the potential tender.

sig_9a9f35e6c361d321a591.description: The subject of contracts awarded within the framework of a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter referred to as the "dynamic purchasing system" or simply "DPS") will be the purchase of hardware and hardware product support and the purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. The purpose of establishing the DPS is to create a platform for awarding contracts within the DPS in order to enable the contracting authority to flexibly award contracts in accordance with the Public Procurement Act according to its actual needs, i.e. at a time and in a scope known to it. The dynamic purchasing system will be divided into two categories: 1) Purchase of hardware and hardware product support 2) Purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. Main CPV 30200000 Computer equipment and supplies Additional CPV codes: Category 1 Purchase of hardware and hardware product support 30200000 Computer equipment and supplies 30210000-4 Data processing machines (hardware) 30230000-0 Computer-related equipment 32400000-7 Networks 35125100-7 Sensors 48820000-2 Servers 72600000-6 Computer auxiliary services and consultancy 72700000-7 Computer network services Category 2 Purchase of licences for standard software products and support for these products. 48200000-0 Networking, internet and intranet software package 48300000-1 Document creation, drawing, painting, scheduling and productivity software package 48500000-3 Communication and multimedia software package 48600000-4 Database and operating software package 48700000-5 Software package utilities 48800000-6 Information systems and servers 48900000-7 Various software packages and computer systems 72600000-6 Computer auxiliary services and consultancy 72700000-7 Computer network services By creating this DPS for category 1, a DPS is established through which individual contracts for the purchase of hardware and hardware product support will be continuously awarded as needed by the contracting authority during 48 months after the establishment of the DPS. The specific scope of the subject of the contract, detailed specification, as well as other supplementary information will be part of individual calls for tenders within the established DPS, which will be sent to all candidates included in this category via the JOSEPHINE electronic tool for CPV codes: 30200000 Computer equipment and supplies 30210000-4 Data processing machines (hardware) 30230000-0 Computer-related equipment 32400000-7 Networks 35125100-7 Sensors 48820000-2 Servers 72600000-6 Computer auxiliary services and consultancy 72700000-7 Computer network services The subject of individual contracts may also include, to the necessary extent, related services standardly provided with the relevant HW, e.g. in cases where the manufacturer requires installation/activation by the vendor (certified technician of the supplier). The subject matter of the contract is: • the digitisation, documentation and Scientific Documentation of all the Items provided for herein o of the Library, o of the Art Gallery and o of the archival material, which constitute the cultural asset of the Society for Macedonian Studies, • the creation of a Digital Museum, including a Digital Museum Web Portal, through which the promotion and dissemination of the digitised cultural asset of the Society for Macedonian Studies will be ensured both to the public visiting its physical premises and to the general public via a web portal to be developed for this purpose, as well as • the supply of Museum equipment, off-the-shelf Software and other equipment • provision of other services (training and support of trial and productive operation of systems, publicity and dissemination of Project results services). The services provided are classified under the following Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) codes: 72000000-5, 79999100-4, 79131000-1, 80533100-0, 48000000-8, 48800000-6, 79341000-6, The subject matter of the contract is not subdivided into lots, due to the complementarity and strong interdependencies of the individual actions that compose it, so as to ensure the creation of conceptually sound digital content, the uniform operation of systems that make up the project, and to achieve the implementation of specialised digital applications to support the institutional role and responsibilities of the S.M.S.. Cohesion and a unified strategy are of critical importance for the success of the project. The creation of digital content and the development of the presentation and management system constitute interdependent parts of a single project. The integrated approach ensures consistency and cohesion in all phases of the project, from design and development to final implementation. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the likelihood of security gaps or incompatibility between the different systems and contents. Also, the non-subdivision of the contract can lead to economies of scale, since a single contractor can make better use of resources and offer more cost-effective solutions. Subdividing the project into lots often increases the overall cost due to increased expenses for Single European Document (ESED) / Standard Responsible Declaration Form (ESED) 3 lots often increases the overall cost due to increased expenses for coordination, management and contractual costs. In addition, the unified management of the project allows better coordination and flexibility in changes, reducing the chances of misunderstandings, delays, lack of coordination and conflicts that may arise when different contractors undertake different parts. This also allows faster decision-making and adaptation to the needs of the project. Offers are accepted for all the services described. The estimated value of the contract amounts to one million one hundred and eighty-four thousand two hundred and sixty-two Euros (1.184.262,00€) including VAT 24% (budget without VAT: 955.050,00€, VAT: 229.212,00€). Following the conclusion of the initial contract, during the implementation of the project and before the expiry of the contract, the Contracting Authority may decide to exercise an option by increasing the physical subject matter of the project (as described herein) up to one hundred percent (100%) of the contract price. Before the expiry of the contract, the Project Owner may decide to exercise a maintenance option up to the amount of 58.000,00€ excluding VAT (budget with VAT: 71.920,00€, VAT 24% 13.920,00€), based on the Financial Offer of the Candidate Contractor, for maintenance services (as described in Para. 7.12.1.2 of Annex I). The subject of the public contract includes the delivery, installation, implementation, training and maintenance of an integrated inventory and material asset management system based on UHF RFID technology, consisting of hardware and software components ("the equipment" and/or "the components") for the needs of the administrative bodies (specified in a Council of Ministers Decision (CMD) No. 727/05.12.2019 , with subsequent amendments and supplements, and the Bulgarian Telegraph Agency, pursuant to § 9 of the Transitional and Final Provisions of the Act on Amendment and Supplement to the Bulgarian Telegraph Agency (BTA) Act, described in detail by type, quantity and technical characteristics in the Technical Specification of the Contracting Authority - Appendix No. 1. The requirements for performance are described in detail in the Technical Specification of the Contracting Authority - Appendix No. 1. The subject of the public contract includes the delivery, installation, implementation, training and maintenance of an integrated inventory and material asset management system based on UHF RFID technology, consisting of hardware and software components ("the equipment" and/or "the components") for the needs of the administrative bodies (specified in a Council of Ministers Decision (CMD) No. 727/05.12.2019 , with subsequent amendments and supplements, and the BTA, described in detail by type, quantity and technical characteristics in the TS of the Contracting Authority - Appendix No. 1. The requirements for performance are described in detail in the TS of the Contracting Authority. ***** The scope of the contract includes the following activities: 1. Activity No. 1 - „Delivery, installation and commissioning“, including: - Component 1: „Inventory software system — delivery, installation and licensing of the latest stable version, configuration, testing and validation of functionality“ with an estimated quantity of 357 000 licences; - Component 2: „UHF RFID readers — delivery and configuration“ with an estimated quantity of 19 units; - Component 3: „Thermal transfer printers for RFID labels — delivery, configuration and template preparation“ with an estimated quantity of 15 units; - Component 4: „RFID labels — printed, encoded and sorted by the Contractor AND/OR consumables for independent printing by the respective administration (upon request)“ with an estimated quantity of 357 000 labels and thermal transfer ribbon - 39 units; - Component 5: „Integration with the administration's available ERP and other systems — jointly with the Contracting Authority“ with a total estimated quantity of up to 200 man-hours; - Component 6 including: 1. „On-site or online training for working with the system and individual components, including the handover of detailed written instructions for working with the System in the Bulgarian language“; 2. Technical instructions for action in case of problems, intended for the administration's technical experts; 2. Activity No. 2 – „Maintenance and warranty service“. *** The Contracting Authority reserves the right, during the term of the contract, not to order every type of component and/or the entire estimated quantity, or, in case of necessity, to increase it until the maximum contract value is reached, which equals the maximum estimated value of the contract. Payment for the delivered components shall be made on the basis of the unit prices indicated in the selected contractor's offer. ***** Delivery shall be made on the basis of a corresponding written order to the selected contractor. The order shall indicate the following information: - Administration for which the system and/or the labels are intended; - Type and quantity of the equipment and/or number of labels to be delivered/printed; - Delivery location of the components; - Other information at the discretion of the Contracting Authority. ***** Performance deadlines: Deadline for submitting orders for the inventory system or components thereof - 24 months, counting from the entry into force of the public contract. Deadline for the delivery of hardware and/or software - 30 calendar days, counting from the date of sending the written order by the Contracting Authority. Deadline for implementation and commissioning - up to 45 calendar days after the delivery date, certified by a handover protocol. System maintenance period - 36 months, counting from the date of signing the handover protocol for commissioning. Equipment maintenance period - 36 months, counting from the date of signing the delivery handover protocol. **** In the event that they are not the manufacturer, the tenderer must be a person duly authorised by the manufacturer or their official representative for the right to distribute/deliver the software and hardware products offered by them on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria. The tenderer shall prove their compliance with the set requirement by enclosing an authorisation letter or an equivalent document issued by the manufacturer or their official representative, in the Bulgarian language or with a translation into the Bulgarian language in their Technical Proposal. The document must be valid as of the date of submission of the tender. In cases where the tenderer in the public contract submits an authorisation letter from an official representative of the manufacturer (or an equivalent document), the tender shall also include an authorisation letter issued by the manufacturer (or an equivalent document in the Bulgarian language or accompanied by a translation into the Bulgarian language), which empowers the manufacturer's official representative to grant authorisation to third parties. *** The set requirement for authorisation at the tender submission stage is justified by the subject of the contract and represents a guarantee for its timely and high-quality performance. In the event that a contractor is selected who is refused authorisation by the manufacturer, this may lead to a delay in the performance of the public contract, as well as to its termination. According to the conclusions of the Supreme Administrative Court, "the requirement for authorisation in itself is not restrictive, insofar as it is a guarantee of the quality and reliability of the activity carried out. "

"In ordinary commercial practice, authorisation takes place on the basis of a contract, which can be directly with the manufacturer or with another economic entity authorised to grant authorisation on behalf of the manufacturer" (Decision No. 10859 of 27.10.2021 of the SAC on administrative case No. 6546/2021 , VII Division). In the documentation, the condition for authorisation is set broadly, i.e. it is not restricted solely to the manufacturer of the equipment, but also any official representative thereof. General authorisation is required, rather than for a specific procedure, and an opportunity is provided for any interested tenderer – partner, regardless of whether they are a Bulgarian or foreign entity, to submit a tender, with the opportunity provided to prove the aforementioned circumstance both with an authorisation letter and with any other equivalent document that certifies compliance with the set requirement.

sig_9aecbba6e2f5f8440b31.description: SUBJECT OF THE DYNAMIC PURCHASING SYSTEM The subject of this dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter also DPS) is communication and marketing services for the customers of Hansel Oy. The subject of the DPS includes the following services: • Communication and marketing consulting • Communication planning and implementation • Marketing planning and implementation • Communication and marketing production • Digital marketing and communication • Media planning services • Communication training services • Other additional services related to communication and marketing. The main subject of the DPS is expert work. In addition to expert work, the Customer's procurement may include software and/or operating environments closely related to communication and marketing services, including cloud services and software services, such as media monitoring, newsletter services, etc. However, the value of the aforementioned software and/or operating environments may be at most 30 % of the estimated total value of the Customer's procurement, or if the procurement is divided into parts, of the estimated value of the relevant section. The subject of the DPS is described in more detail in the request to participate and its annexes, in particular in the annex "Subject of the dynamic purchasing system". During the duration of the DPS, all interested candidates can submit an application to participate in it. The DPS is valid until the date stated in the contract notice, unless it is suspended or amended while the DPS is in force. The customers of Hansel Oy carry out procurements among the candidates accepted into the DPS through internal DPS competitions, which can take place throughout the entire procurement phase of the DPS. The procurement phase of the DPS begins after the establishment phase on 1.10.2025 and ends when the validity period of the DPS ends. Procurement contracts made by customers based on the DPS can be valid for a maximum of six (6) years. SCOPE OF THE DYNAMIC PURCHASING SYSTEM The estimated total value of the dynamic purchasing system is a maximum of 300 000 000 euros (excluding value added tax).
