This contract aims to provide the Public Local Company Asset Management and Mobility Support Hauts-de-France with Project Management Assistance (PMA) in the railway sector, concerning the provision of Intellectual Services: technical assistance, studies and consulting. This PMA will allow the PLC to ensure the operational implementation of its missions. The Hauts-de-France Region owns a fleet of Rolling Stock to enable the provision of the regional public passenger rail transport service. The SPL GAAM HDF has been granted the patrimonial management of these assets, which are furthermore made available to Railway Operators to whom the Hauts-de-France Region has awarded a public service delegation contract concerning the operation of regional passenger rail transport services falling within its scope of competence. The Railway Operator thus uses the Rolling Stock for an average duration of 10 years, according to the terms and conditions defined in the public service delegation contract binding it to the Hauts-de-France Region on the one hand, and in a provision contract (CMAD) binding it to the SPL GAAM HDF and the Region on the other hand. In its role as patrimonial manager, the SPL GAAM HDF must preserve the patrimonial and technical value of the assets entrusted to it for management and which it makes available to Railway Operators. In this respect, it has a right (and a duty) of oversight regarding the use of the assets. It also intervenes, as part of its general duty of advice and alert, in support of the Hauts-de-France Region, to define the strategy regarding the acquisition, modernization, potential restoration, and end-of-life of Rolling Stock. This lot has as its object the project management assistance of the public Buyer on the technical aspects related to the carrying out of studies concerning Rolling Stock intended for passenger transport. The services cover in particular the identification and formalization of needs, the management of the life cycle of the equipment, the definition and monitoring of major maintenance programmes (levels 4 and 5 within the meaning of standard NF X60-000), as well as the elaboration of strategies for managing the end-of-life of the equipment. Without this list being exhaustive, the Holder of lot 1 may be required to carry out interventions with the SPL GAAM HDF in order to: • Provide technical expertise in the fields of engineering, maintenance and patrimonial management of Rolling Stock; • Support the PLC in the definition and implementation of its patrimonial management strategy for Rolling Stock over their entire life cycle; • Assist the PLC in the technical, economic and operational analysis of its Rolling Stock fleet in order to optimize its availability, reliability, maintainability and total cost of ownership; • Evaluate and optimize the operating, maintenance, renovation, modernization and investment costs relating to Rolling Stock; • Assist the PLC in the procedures for transferring ownership of Rolling Stock and in the organization of associated patrimonial data; • Provide expertise relating to on-board systems (command-control, signaling, ETCS/ERTMS, KVB, ground-to-train communication, passenger information, video surveillance, on-board diagnostics, etc.) as well as the impacts of technological and regulatory developments on Rolling Stock; • Analyze the consequences of regulatory, normative and technical developments (TSI, railway safety, cybersecurity, accessibility, environment, market placement authorizations, etc.) on the patrimonial strategy and life cycle costs of Rolling Stock; • Contribute to strengthening the expertise of the SPL GAAM HDF in terms of Rolling Stock, maintenance, patrimonial management and on-board systems; • Take into account the capacities and constraints of the maintenance and stabling sites (SMR) in order to contribute to the optimization of the operation of the Rolling Stock fleet and the transport offer. Depending on the analyses carried out, the needs of the PLC in terms of Rolling Stock may evolve, both in number and in technical characteristics, expected performance or acquisition cost.; The Hauts-de-France Region owns or is in the process of acquiring a set of tertiary, technical and industrial railway buildings integrated into the Maintenance and Stabling Site (SMR) with a view to enabling the realization of the regional public passenger rail transport service. The SPL GAAM HDF has been granted the patrimonial management of these assets which it makes available to Railway Operators to whom the Hauts-de-France Region has awarded a public service delegation contract concerning the operation of regional passenger rail transport services falling within its scope of competence. The Railway Operator thus uses the buildings and maintenance sites autonomously, for an average duration of 10 years, according to the terms and conditions defined in the public service delegation contract binding it to the Hauts-de-France Region on the one hand, and in a provision contract (CMAD) binding it to the SPL GAAM HDF and the Region on the other hand. During the phase of transferring ownership of the Maintenance and Stabling Sites (SMR), prior to their being taken into patrimonial management by the PLC, inventories and audits may be commissioned in order to determine the condition of the buildings, installations and tools as well as the compliance of investments made on behalf of the Region in its capacity as project owner.

In its role as property manager, SPL GAAM HDF must also preserve the property and technical value of the entrusted assets, which it makes available to Railway Operators. In this respect, it has the right (and the duty) to oversee the use of the sites it manages. It also intervenes, as part of its general duty of advice and warning, in support of the Hauts-de-France Region, to define its investment strategy. In this context, various monitoring actions are implemented by the SPL to ensure compliance with the obligations incumbent upon the Railway Operator, through the performance of audits, technical inspections, etc., included in the SPL's multiannual monitoring plan or triggered following operational drift, incidents or investments. These actions do not fall within the scope of regulatory controls (such as: monitoring of the Railway Operator, administrative inspections, certification). However, they may lead to verifying that the Railway Operator has effectively carried out the regulatory checks and that the necessary valid administrative authorisations have indeed been issued to it. SPL GAAM HDF ensures that the Railway Operator monitors and maintains the buildings made available to it, that regulatory checks are carried out and that action plans are implemented. For the purposes of this lot, the following definitions apply: • Tertiary buildings: these are buildings used for administrative purposes. SPL GAAM HDF may thus make available, within the perimeter of a Maintenance and Storing Site, buildings incorporating executive offices, computer rooms, training rooms, archiving rooms, a Telecom room, rest rooms and sanitary facilities, • Technical buildings: these are buildings without public access that may be intended for storage, electric power distribution, operation and maintenance, • Industrial buildings: these are structures intended for the production, transformation and assembly of goods, incorporating the technical equipment necessary for operation, and which do not fall under public reception. The services expected under this lot aim to: • Identify discrepancies, risks of degradation or contractual non-conformities; • Verify the proper preservation of the real estate assets made available to a Railway Operator; • Ensure that operating uses and practices do not undermine the technical, functional and accounting value of the assets; • Formulate corrective or conservatory recommendations. The transfer of ownership of assets for the benefit of the Region, the taking over of the property management of a building, as well as its provision (sometimes simultaneous) to the Railway Operator are subject to a condition report. To this end, a contradictory visit is carried out between the Region, the Railway Operator of the site concerned, and SPL GAAM HDF, sometimes preceded by technical studies. This condition report and these studies form part of this lot. The Railway Operator of each site is also required to carry out investments or major maintenance and renewals (MMR) in execution of public service delegation contracts. The SPL may be required to monitor the execution of the investment plan contracted between the Railway Operator and the Region. In this respect, without replacing the project owner or the project manager, the SPL may check the conformity of the investments or MMR carried out with regard to the contractual commitments between the Railway Operator and the Region, as well as their entry in the physical inventory. The SPL may also, on its own behalf or on behalf of the Region, monitor the implementation of interventions allowing the repair of damage in the event of claims or the implementation of guarantees attached to the assets. The lot also covers this aspect.; The Hauts-de-France Region owns or is in the process of acquiring a set of railway sites, facilities and tools in order to enable the performance of the regional public passenger railway transport service. SPL GAAM HDF has been granted the property management of these assets, which it makes available to the Railway Operators to whom the Hauts-de-France Region has awarded a public service delegation contract concerning the operation of regional passenger railway transport services falling within its area of competence. The Railway Operator thus uses the maintenance sites, facilities and tools independently, for an average duration of 10 years, according to the terms and conditions defined in the public service delegation contract binding it to the Hauts-de-France Region on the one hand, and in a provision contract (CMAD) binding it to SPL GAAM HDF and the Region on the other hand. In its role as property manager, SPL GAAM HDF must preserve the property and technical value of the assets it makes available to Railway Operators, and in this respect, it has the right (and the duty) to oversee the use of the sites it manages. It also intervenes, as part of its general duty of advice and warning, in support of the Hauts-de-France Region, to define its investment strategy. In this context, various monitoring actions are implemented by the SPL to ensure compliance with the obligations incumbent upon the Railway Operator, through the performance of audits and technical inspections.

However, the SPL shall under no circumstances replace the responsibilities assigned to Railway Operators, administrative authorities or certification bodies provided for by the regulations. It shall ensure that the Railway Operator performs the regulatory checks incumbent upon it, and performs the maintenance of these assets in compliance with the contractual commitments placed upon it. These actions do not fall within the scope of the exercise of checks provided for by the regulations (such as: monitoring of the Railway Operator, administrative inspections, certification). However, they may lead to ensuring that the Railway Operator has effectively had the regulatory checks carried out and that the necessary valid administrative authorisations have been effectively issued to it. The SPL GAAM HDF shall ensure that the Railway Operator monitors and maintains the land, infrastructure and railway facilities and associated tools made available to it, that the regulatory checks are carried out and that the action plans are implemented. It is therefore specified that these are audits and inspections included in the SPL's multiannual monitoring plan or triggered following operational drifts, incidents or investments. The Railway Operator of each site is furthermore required to make investments in execution of public service delegation contracts, which may concern: • New constructions (maintenance and stabling sites, light maintenance and stabling sites); • Heavy maintenance and renewals (HMR); • Constructions, modernisation of facilities, infrastructure, equipment and tools; • Replacements of equipment and tools. In this context, the SPL is neither mandated nor delegated with the rights and obligations of the contracting authority. It acts in support of the Region solely within the framework of its general advisory duty. The SPL may be required to monitor the execution of the investment plan contracted between the Railway Operator and the Region. As such, without legally replacing either the contracting authority or the project manager, the SPL may be required to issue an opinion to the Region regarding the conformity of the operations carried out with regard to the commitments contracted between the Railway Operator and the Region, as well as their entry in the physical inventory. The SPL may also, for its own account or that of the Region, monitor the implementation of interventions enabling the repair of damage in the event of claims or the implementation of guarantees attached to the assets. This lot thus covers: • The phases of acceptance of railway sites, facilities and tools; • Joint site visits. Finally, any takeover in management of a site or a facility by the SPL shall be the subject of a tripartite joint inventory of fixtures carried out with between the Region and the Railway Operator concerned. These inventories of fixtures fall within the scope of this lot.; The operation of railway rolling stock, maintenance sites and railway buildings is accompanied by environmental objectives such as the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the reduction of energy consumption, the control of effluent and soiled waste discharges, as well as the control of soil and water pollution prevention. These objectives form part of compliance with the environmental regulations related to industrial sites and facilities, in particular: • The Environmental Code (Articles L511-1 A to L517-2); • The ICPE decree (Legislation: Articles L511-1 to L517-2) (Regulation: Articles R511-9 to R517-10); • The Orders on general requirements related to the IOTA nomenclature (with reference to Articles articles L.214-1 to L.214-6 and article R.214-1 of the Environmental Code); • The REACH Regulation (EU Regulation no. 1907/2006); • Tertiary decree no. 2019 771 of 23 July 2019; • The BACS decree (decree no. 2020-887 of 20 July 2020 amended by decree no. 2023-259 of 7 April 2023); • The sustainable development objectives of Agenda 2030 in France; • The SNBC3 national low-carbon strategy (Carbon neutrality of France in 2050, halving of territorial emissions (excluding carbon sink) by 2030); and • ISO standards 14001:2026 – Environmental management system, ISO 45001:2018 – Occupational health and safety management system and ISO 50001:2018 – Energy management system and their derivatives. In this context, the SPL, as asset manager, must ensure that the use of the goods entrusted to it that it has made available is compatible with the control of environmental impacts by the Railway Operator, the preservation of the asset value of the assets in compliance with the environmental regulations mentioned previously. Thus, the SPL has established a monitoring strategy for the assets it manages, which is structured around various monitoring actions such as audits and inspections. This strategy is part of a contractual framework. The monitoring exercised by the SPL is part of its multiannual monitoring plan, but may also consist of audits triggered following operational drifts. Furthermore, the operation of Rolling Stock and maintenance sites may lead to the implementation of investments or heavy maintenance and renewals (HMR) throughout the PSD Contracts. The conditions for carrying out these investments and HMR are also monitored by the SPL on behalf of the Hauts-de-France Region. In this context, the SPL is neither mandated nor delegated with the rights and obligations of the contracting authority.

It acts in support of the Region solely within the framework of its general advisory duty. The SPL shall under no circumstances replace the responsibilities assigned to Railway Operators, administrative authorities or certification bodies provided for by the regulations. It shall ensure that the Railway Operator performs the regulatory checks incumbent upon it concerning each Rolling Stock and Maintenance Site and associated building, and performs the maintenance of these assets in compliance with the contractual commitments placed upon it. Thus, these actions do not fall within the scope of the exercise of checks provided for by the regulations (such as: monitoring of the Railway Operator, administrative inspections, certification). However, they may lead to ensuring that the Railway Operator has effectively had the regulatory checks carried out and that the necessary valid administrative authorisations have been effectively issued to it. Finally, the property transfer operations and then the takeover in management of a site may be the subject of studies, and at the very least an inventory of fixtures. Joint visits between the Railway Operator, the SPL and the Organising Authority may form part of a mission integrated into this lot, as well as site studies. This present lot concerns: • The following Rolling Stock: o BIBI self-propelled trainsets of BGC type; o XGC type diesel self-propelled trainsets; o TER 2N NG type electric self-propelled trainsets; o Régiolis type BIBI self-propelled trainsets; o Régio 2N type electric self-propelled trainsets; • The following maintenance sites and facilities: o The maintenance and stabling sites located in Saint-Denis (93), Amiens (80), Calais (62), Lille (59), and planned in Tourcoing (59) and Longueau (80); o A maintenance site and in-line stabling yard planned in Laon (02); o The service facilities located in Saint-Quentin (02), Beauvais (60), Lens (62). The services aim, without being exhaustive, to support the SPL GAAM HDF in its decision-making regarding the environmental management of assets to: • Comply with environmental regulations; • Control the environmental impacts and risks related to the provision of railway assets to a Railway Operator who uses them; • Structure and make reliable environmental and asset data.; The purpose of this lot is the supply of advice concerning data structuring, in particular that related to the asset monitoring of Rolling Stock and maintenance and stabling sites (MSS) whose management has been entrusted to the SPL GAAM HDF (Rolling Stock and Maintenance Sites) in order to allow the continued implementation of its asset management system making it possible to ensure the sustainability of all Assets. The data aggregated by Railway Operators within the framework of PSD Contracts make it possible to monitor the state of Assets, their performance as well as their uses. PSD Contracts last on average 10 years and the data related thereto are intended to be transferred on the one hand to the SPL which ensures long-term asset management (40 years), and on the other hand to the next Railway Operator, without compromising the continuity of the public service. At the end of these PSDs, the data considered necessary for the Public Service will become reversionary assets that must return to the Region and, by delegation, to the SPL GAAM HDF. Structuring this data constitutes a strategic challenge for the SPL GAAM HDF, in order to optimise the monitoring of Assets (Building management, Rolling Stock usage history, production of traffic forecasts, etc.), ensure the reversibility of data and software between Railway Operators and the SPL at the end of the PSD Contract, and optimise the definition of the statement of needs in the event of a mid-life operation on the RS, purchase of new RS, and modernisation of MSS. The SPL GAAM HDF expects the contractor selected to meet the needs of this lot to advise it, among other things, concerning the subjects of "Data Governance" as well as the "Creation and structuring of its data platform(s)", which may lead where applicable to the creation of a Machine Learning system. The elements provided must be reliable, accessible and reversible. Without this list being exhaustive, the lot holder may be required to perform the following services: • Audit existing data (In particular the production of mapping, maturity analysis and identification of needs); • Organise existing data; • Advise on the data governance and management strategy to be adopted; • Carry out strategic and/or technical studies related to tools and data management to support decision-making; • Advise on the security and compliance strategy of existing information systems; • Carry out information system security audits; • Valorise the obtained data by proposing tools adapted to the company's environment (Local public company subject to public law and private law in terms of data management); • Train teams on the adopted organisation as well as on the use of the tools made available; • Perform assistance and maintenance of the tools made available to propose optimisation areas; It is specified here that existing data concerns: • Free-access and publicly accessible data; • Data belonging to the Region over which the SPL GAAM HDF holds a right of use; • Data belonging to third parties and over which the Region and/or the SPL GAAM HDF hold rights of use.

The data sources concerned include, but are not limited to: • External parties: Excel, Powerpoint, Hauts-de-France Region databases; • Databases shared with other Regions (Rolling Stock and maintenance and stabling facilities), building plans, land registries, Local Urban Plan, easement plan, ART PAN system, ERATV, RINF, DRR, path allocation, infrastructure capacities, running lines; • Asset-related systems: sensors, meters, physical readings. sig_9d264e54a5df0736900a.description: The subject matter of the tender is a contract for the following service: Framework agreement RV SAP BAIS ORRP (Lot 2) As promotional bank for North Rhine-Westphalia, NRW.BANK (hereinafter also: contracting authority) supports the federal state in its structural and economic policy tasks. It acts on a public mandate, in a competition-neutral manner and deploys the entire spectrum of credit-based promotional products - from classical credit to tailored advice. Its three promotional fields are "Economy", "Housing" as well as "Infrastructure/Municipalities". In contrast to commercial banks, NRW.BANK's customers are primarily house banks and other promotional intermediaries. NRW.BANK strictly observes the prohibition of discrimination in relation to other credit institutions. Its cooperation with cooperative and private banks as well as savings banks follows - in a competition-neutral manner - the house bank procedure. NRW.BANK's business focuses on the canon of promotional areas defined by Agreement II. Competitive business (such as commercial property financing and the new issue of mortgage Pfandbriefe) was no longer pursued by Landesbank NRW, the predecessor institution of NRW.BANK. To fulfil its mandate, NRW.BANK operates in the following areas: - Securing and improving the medium-sized structure of the economy, in particular financings for business start-ups and consolidations, - state social residential housing promotion, - provision of venture capital, - structural development of towns and municipalities, - infrastructure measures, - measures in agriculture and forestry and in rural areas, - environmental protection, technology and innovation measures, - measures of a social, cultural and scientific nature. Against this background, the subject matter of the service is a framework agreement on the consultation and support of NRW.BANK in the area of msgGillardon (BAIS and ORRP). The award of individual contracts under the framework agreement takes place on the procurement platform vergabe.NRW on the basis of mini-competitions between the contractor partners to the framework agreement. The framework agreement is to be concluded with 2 framework contractor partners (Lot 2). The framework agreement has a term of three years and can be extended by one year. The maximum call-off is 5.200 person days (Lot 1) or 800 person days (Lot 2). The minimum take-off across all framework contractor partners is 200 person days (Lot 1) or 25 person days (Lot 2).

Department of Veterans Affairs Comprehensive Legal Assistance & Integrated Management (VA CLAIM) 1. Introduction The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires a broad, flexible source of comprehensive legal assistance, alternate dispute resolution (ADR), court support, and integrated case management services to support VA's mission of serving Veterans, their families, and survivors. VA's Office of General Counsel, regional counsel offices, and program offices routinely require surge and specialized support for litigation, administrative hearings, EEO complaints, investigations, and related proceedings that cannot be fully met with in-house staff alone. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes a pre-vetted pool of qualified Contractors capable of rapidly fulfilling orders for legal support services, ADR neutrals, court reporting, transcription, and related trainings across VA facilities nationwide, ensuring continuity of legal operations, reduced procurement lead time, and consistent quality and pricing across the enterprise. 2. Scope This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirements for support of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in accomplishing VA's mission, strategic goals, priorities, and initiatives related to legal, ADR, and court support functions. Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, vehicles, certifications, supervision, and all other technologies and technical services necessary to deliver comprehensive legal assistance and integrated management services. This includes, but is not limited to: Alternate dispute resolution services Legal support services (case development, research, litigation and administrative claim support, expert witness support) Court reporting services Transcription, translation, and interpretation services Real-time reporting, Communication Access Realtime Translation (CART), and remote/video deposition support Trial and hearing exhibit or technology support Litigation-related and ADR-related training This PWS establishes the scope, terms, and general requirements of the base BPA. Specific requirements, deliverables, staffing, place of performance, and performance periods will be defined at the individual order level. Orders may be issued for any combination of the services described herein, and the task areas below are intended to be read broadly so as to encompass the full range of court support, transcription, and litigation support services VA may require over the life of the BPA. 3. General Information 3.1 Type of Agreement/Contract The Government anticipates awarding multiple Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs). BPA orders will be issued as Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and/or Labor-Hour (LH), and may include a Not-to-Exceed (NTE) CLIN for travel. The type of BPA order will be identified at the order level. 3.2 Ordering Period The BPA ordering period is a 12-month base period with up to four (4) 12-month option periods. Each order shall identify its own period of performance, which may extend up to 12 months beyond the expiration of the BPA ordering period, consistent with applicable ordering procedures in effect at time of award. 3.3 Place of Performance Place of performance will be specified at the order level and may include VA facilities, contractor facilities, and remote/virtual performance as appropriate to the service ordered. 3.4 Travel Travel requirements will be specified in each order and shall be in accordance with the Federal Travel Regulations (FTR). Local travel within a 50-mile radius of the contractor's facility or the assigned Government facility is considered the cost of doing business and will not be separately reimbursed, including subsistence and associated labor charges for travel time. Travel for personal convenience or daily commuting will not be reimbursed. Travel, subsistence, and labor charges for travel beyond a 50-mile radius may be authorized on a case-by-case basis with advance approval by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). General and Administrative (G&A) costs on travel are not allowable and will not be reimbursed. 3.5 Hours of Operation Hours of operation will be identified at the order level and shall reflect local time for the parties involved. 3.6 Government-Furnished Information/Equipment Government-Furnished Information (GFI) and/or Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE), if applicable, will be identified at the order level. 3.7 BPA Ordering Procedures BPA orders may be issued at any time during the ordering period. The order-level Contracting Officer shall award and administer orders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in this BPA and the applicable FAR Part 12 commercial item/service ordering procedures in effect at the time of ordering, including any subsequent regulatory updates to those procedures. BPA orders shall be within the scope of the BPA. Only the Contracting Officer for the BPA may modify the BPA itself. Order of Precedence: The terms and conditions of this BPA apply to all orders issued under it. In the event of inconsistency between the BPA terms and an individual order, the BPA terms and conditions take precedence. Annual Review: The Government will conduct an annual review of the BPA consistent with applicable ordering regulations, to confirm authorized procedures are being followed and to assess market conditions, sources of supply, pricing, and other factors that may warrant new agreements or modification of existing ones. Nonconformance: The Government will address nonconformance in accordance with applicable FAR subpart 8.4 procedures governing termination for cause, termination for convenience, and disputes, as in effect at time of order. At no time shall order prices exceed awarded BPA prices. The discount pricing relationship established under the BPA shall be maintained throughout its life unless modified by the BPA Contracting Officer. 4. Background 4.1 Applicable Laws, Regulations, and Guidance The Contractor shall perform all services in accordance with applicable federal law and regulation, including but not limited to: Statutory Authorities 28 U.S.C. Â§ 1346(b), Â§Â§ 2671 2680 Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) 5 U.S.C. Â§ 552 Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 5 U.S.C. Â§ 552a, as amended Privacy Act of 1974 5 U.S.C. Chapters 75, 77 Adverse actions; appeals 5 U.S.C. Â§ 504 / 28 U.S.C. Â§ 2412 Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) 38 U.S.C. Â§Â§ 5901 5905 Recognition of representatives; unauthorized practice 42 U.S.C. Â§ 2000d Title VI, Civil Rights Act of 1964 42 U.S.C. Â§ 2000e et seq. Title VII, Civil Rights Act of 1964 29 U.S.C. Â§ 794 Section 508/Rehabilitation Act (accessibility) 44 U.S.C. Â§ 3541 et seq. Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) of 2014 44 U.S.C. Chapter 31 Records Management by Federal Agencies The Administrative Dispute Resolution Act (ADRA) of 1996 Regulatory Authorities 5 CFR Part 177 Administrative claims 29 CFR Part 1614 Federal EEO complaint processing 5 CFR Parts 315, 752, 1201, 1209 Employment, adverse actions, MSPB 38 CFR Â§Â§ 14.626 14.637 VA accreditation of representatives FIPS Pub 201-3 Personal Identity Verification of Federal Employees and Contractors Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (FRCP) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and BPA ordering procedures thereunder, as in effect at time of ordering VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) and VA Acquisition Manual (VAAM), as applicable Policy/Guidance Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Management Directive 110 Model Standards of Conduct for Mediators (www.adr.gov) VA directives and handbooks governing records retention, information security, and privacy, as applicable at the order level The Contractor shall remain current with amendments to the above authorities and any additional laws, regulations, or VA policy identified at the order level. 5. Task Areas Task areas are stated broadly. Individual orders may draw on any combination of the following in any proportion, and are not limited to the specific examples listed. 5.1 Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) The Contractor shall provide ADR services related to workplace disputes, EEO complaints, and facilitation needs across VA, including assignment of neutrals (mediators, facilitators, conflict coaches, arbitrators) within the local commuting area when feasible. Adjudication is not permitted under this task area. Services include, without limitation: Arbitration Private resolution before one or more neutral arbitrators rendering a binding, court-enforceable award. Mediation Neutral-facilitated negotiation toward a voluntary, mutually acceptable resolution. Conciliation Neutral-assisted settlement process involving active proposal of settlement terms, non-binding. Record development support for all ADR matters, including gathering, organizing, and preparing supporting documentation and evidence. 5.2 Court and Hearing Support Services The Contractor shall provide the full range of services needed to capture, preserve, and produce the official record of hearings, depositions, investigations, arbitrations, and other proceedings, including: Court Reporting Certified court reporters/stenographers (or equivalent, e.g., digital/electronic reporters) to record and produce official transcripts; compiling documents and exhibits; reading back portions of the record on request; clarifying inaudible statements. Transcription Conversion of live or recorded speech into written/electronic text, including AI-assisted transcription where appropriate, with fully operational and serviceable recording/transcription equipment at all times. Proofreading/Quality Review Accurate editing of AI-generated or draft transcripts against the source recording; production and delivery of complete, accurate final transcripts within order-specified timeframes. Real-Time Reporting/CART Real-time speech-to-text captioning for proceedings requiring immediate access to the record, including accommodation needs. Read and Sign Access for deponents and legal representatives to review transcripts and errata sheets, noting page/line discrepancies for verification against the original recording. Translation and Interpretation Foreign language and sign language interpretation/translation in support of proceedings, upon request. Remote/Video Proceeding Support Technical and logistical support for remote or hybrid depositions, hearings, and other proceedings, including secure videoconferencing. Record Development Gathering, organizing, and preparing documentation and exhibits supporting the official proceeding record. All service providers shall be certified in accordance with applicable state law (e.g., NCRA, NVRA, or state-specific certification) for the jurisdiction in which services are performed, and the Contractor shall furnish proof of certification upon request. VA will provide 24-hour prior notice for expedited assignments; expedited transcripts shall be delivered overnight to VA's Ordering Representative upon request. Certification requirements, cancellation terms, and expedite procedures will be further specified at the order level. Cancellation notices provided at least 24 hours prior to a scheduled appearance shall not incur a cancellation fee, unless otherwise stated at the order level. 5.3 Legal Support Services The Contractor shall provide comprehensive legal support services spanning case development, research, litigation support, and expert witness services, organized into the following subtask areas: 5.3.1 Case Development, Research, and Analysis Preparing draft documents for attorney review; opening, organizing, and maintaining case files; gathering, sorting, classifying, and interpreting information from multiple sources; identifying gaps, inconsistencies, or issues requiring further inquiry; conducting legal and factual research; coordinating with custodians and stakeholders to obtain responsive information; documenting search and information-processing efforts; compiling authorities into organized reference materials; record development, including gathering, organizing, analyzing, and preparing documentation and evidence. 5.3.2 Litigation and Administrative Claim Support Preparing summaries, chronologies, inventories, and data analyses to support attorney decision-making; identifying and organizing exhibits; scheduling depositions and related meetings; supporting eDiscovery, litigation holds, document acquisition and preparation, data extraction from forensic images, and document analysis; supporting FOIA/Privacy Act appeals, FTCA claims, EAJA processing, and employment/labor litigation matters. All litigation and trial support work product shall be submitted through, and filed by, VA counsel; the Contractor shall not submit filings independently. 5.3.3 Administrative Investigations and Interviews Supporting administrative investigations, including scheduling and coordinating interviews, organizing investigative records, and preparing supporting materials for investigators or administrative judges. 5.3.4 Operational and Case Management Support Entering, updating, and maintaining information in electronic case management systems; scanning, copying, and organizing records; managing case intake; screening and responding to customer/stakeholder communications; monitoring case status and deadlines; closing out matters per established procedures; records retention processing; general project management support. Work shall be performed using checklists, templates, and established guidance, with issues or conflicts elevated to supervising attorneys. 5.3.5 Expert Witness and Technical Analysis Support Providing expert witness services as directed by Agency counsel, including specialized subject-matter analysis and evaluation, preparation of expert reports and opinions, consultation with Agency counsel, development of supporting exhibits, and expert testimony at depositions, hearings, mediations, or trials. Services under this task area may support, without limitation: eDiscovery; FOIA and Privacy Act appeals; FTCA cases; employment and labor litigation; contract matters; ethics program support; accreditation and fee matters; litigation hold support; document acquisition, preparation, and organization; forensic data extraction and document analysis; EAJA processing; records retention; and general project management. Contractor personnel shall be fully trained and experienced in their area of expertise commensurate with PWS requirements. 5.4 Training 5.4.1 Litigation Skills Training Training for VA attorneys who represent the Department before the EEOC, Merit Systems Protection Board, Federal Labor Relations Authority, and other legal forums, covering direct and cross-examination, opening statements, closing arguments, exhibit handling, depositions, negotiation, legal writing, and related litigation skills. 5.4.2 ADR and Mediation Training Design, development, and facilitation of customized courses, including meaningful conversations, leading up and advocacy training, group facilitation, workplace civility (including supervisory-level), conflict management, and team building. Additional or emerging training topics related to litigation, ADR, or court support functions may be added at the order level. 6. Applicable Documents Conflict of Interest disclosures/certifications, as required at the order level Additional applicable documents as identified at the order level 7. Deliverables Deliverables, formats, delivery timeframes, and acceptance criteria shall be identified within each individual order.

sig_9d4a59ecbf9895455e49.description: We kindly ask you to submit your response to the request for information regarding the procurement of expert services for personnel capacity management. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a potential tendering procedure. The subject of the procurement is an expert service for personnel capacity management, the purpose of which is to support the organisation's ability to plan, anticipate and manage the use of human resources and competence as part of business management. A more detailed description of the procurement is attached. The purpose of the request for information is to ensure that those preparing the tendering procedure have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. With this request for information, we wish to survey the market situation for personnel capacity management expert work. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of the services, contract terms and pricing. Based on the responses to the request for information, market dialogue sessions may be organised where suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement subject. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the more detailed schedules and meeting link later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this request for information are preliminary and indicative only. Final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. The document "Tietopyyntö_kapasiteetinhallinta" attached to this request for information contains a description of the subject of the procurement, instructions for responding to the request for information, and the questions of the request for information to which the contracting authority requests responses. Please submit your response by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 25.06.2026 at 16.00. We hope that the responses will be submitted as a separate attachment in the Finnish language so that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you may also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your response. Based on the responses received, Istekki will, at its discretion, select tenderers to present their services in a market dialogue meeting. By default, the presentation will be carried out as a Teams meeting of approximately 1-2 hours between Istekki and the supplier in question, provisionally in August or September. All responses received to the request for information will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they are an important part of understanding the whole. It is worth noting that this request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its attachments. A potential tendering procedure may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or for participating in possible presentation sessions. We would also like to mention that this is a request for information, not a prior information notice, procurement notice or invitation to tender. The purpose of the request for information is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and to gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us to build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_9d4ccce0bf55b49a1d73.description: The purpose of this program is to improve maternal and infant outcomes by preventing contact with harmful materials before, during, and after pregnancy. This program aims to improve maternal and infant health outcomes by preventing harmful exposures before, during, and after pregnancy. It supports a national expert-staffed call center that provides timely, evidence-based information and personalized counseling on medications, nutrition, foods, household products, and environmental exposures. By translating complex scientific evidence into clear, accessible guidance and leveraging emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), the program empowers women, families, and healthcare providers to make informed decisions that promote healthy pregnancies and improve maternal and infant outcomes.

sig_9d5282bd403bcdb3d090.description: **This notice supercedes UK3 Planned Procurement Notice reference 2026/S 000-078126, which was issued on 3rd August and modified on 17th of August.** **This contract is an Exempt Contract within the meaning of the Procurement Act 2023, in accordance with Schedule 2, paragraph 25 of the Act (national security). Accordingly, this procurement does not constitute a covered procurement and the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to covered procurements do not apply. Where any provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 are expressed to apply more generally to a “procurement”, the Authority has determined that those provisions are inapplicable in the circumstances of this procurement, having regard to the fact that the application of any such provision would be inconsistent with, or would undermine the operation of, the national security exemption. Any reference by the Authority to concepts, procedures or terminology derived from the Procurement Act 2023 is for convenience only and does not consititute an acknowledgment that the Act, or any particular provision of it, applies to this procurement or any resulting contract. ** The UK Space Agency (UKSA), as part of the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) programme, intends to commence a competitive procurement for the deployment of a sovereign, high‐power space surveillance radar in the Southern Hemisphere (final location is still to be determined but bidders should note the requirement to deploy into the Southern Hemisphere) to enhance the UK's Space Surveillance & Tracking (SST) and Space Domain Awareness (SDA) capability. It is expected that the radar system will operate as a key national asset, providing enhanced detection, tracking and custody of resident space objects, particularly small-size debris and operational satellites in Low Earth Orbit. It will deliver significant improvements to UK resilience, space safety, collision avoidance, re-entry monitoring, fragmentation detection, and wider civil-military situational awareness objectives. The budget for this hardware requirement is capped at £25,000,000 exclusive of VAT and will cover the following elements: * Radar hardware (including, but not limited to, antenna systems, signal generation/timing/processing hardware, power systems, cooling and thermal management) * Radar software (noting the Authority is likely to specify software covers both edge and cloud elements, with a 10 year licence including free security and basic maintenance updates) * Software development to integrate software with wider Government systems (including capture and implementation of user stories/change requests to better exploit the equipment provided) * Two separate training courses - one focused on tasking/sensor capabilities and one focused on hardware support and maintenance * Obtaining spectrum rights and permissions: whilst the Authority will support the appointed contractor with this, responsibility will rest with the appointed contractor * Software and hardware support and maintenance for the initial 3 year contract term * Cyber assurance * Project and contract management (including interface with the infrastructure contractor) * Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location The following is currently expected to be in scope of the infrastructure and enabling works contract, which is expected to be valued at £5,000,000 exclusive of VAT. Prospective bidders should note that at least some staff are likely to require SC or DV clearance for this requirement. To assist prospective bidders with planning, an indicative requirements list is provided below. Depending on final deployment location, some of these elements may not be required: * Planning investigation and, if required, planning consents * Site surveys and ground works (including environmental and site safety surveys) * Enabling works to prepare the site for radar deployment (e.g. construction of concrete base) * Site civils and foundations (design and build) * Power and data connectivity * Potential utilities connections as required (e.g. drainage) * Collaboration around installation and commissioning at final deployment location * Temporary or permanent access to site, as required * Site security (e.g. perimeter fencing, CCTV, gates) * Site support * Project and contract management (including interface with the radar hardware contractor) The following is expected to be in scope of neither contract: * Ongoing utilities costs * Spare components (the radar contractor will be expected to include in the pricing schedule the cost of spare components) A suitable location for deployment has been identified but discussions cannot progress further until the actual equipment specification and characteristics are known. The appointed contractor will therefore be required to work closely with the Contracting Authority and the appointed infrastructure contractor to ensure successful deployment. Bidders will be provided with details of the broad location and constraining assumptions at PSQ stage to assist with technical responses, but should note the final location is unlikely to be disclosed until tender stage. The Contracting Authority will only enter into discussions relating to deployment locations with bidders under NDA, noting that detailed discussions will not be possible at SQ stage. Please note the Contracting Authority will not respond to any further queries raised on the technical specification or conditions of participation at this point: these will need to be raised as formal clarifications via the e-tendering portal in accordance with the timetable specified in the procurement documents. sig_9d549e054b6923de2f82.description: The project put out to tender concerns the creation of a new mobile application for the University of Geneva, replacing the current application (UNIGE Mobile). The new application will retain its service-oriented purpose but will also take on a unifying role, linking the academic and extra-academic spheres to become a "Virtual Student Center" (VSC). The application will offer both academic services (student record, library) and services related to campus life (activities, events, student life, etc.). Designed primarily for students, the application will also offer services intended for UNIGE academic and administrative staff. The development of this new mobile application must be based on modern and robust technology, allowing for the provision of dynamic services and functionalities, fostering student engagement and their sense of belonging, as well as that of the entire university community.
sig_9d549e054b6923de2f82.title: AO Application mobile UNIGE VIRTUAL STUDENT CENTER 2026

External service provision is considered appropriate because specialised providers possess broader expertise, higher specialisation and better professional networking due to their work for multiple clients. Coding is carried out in the acute somatic sector in accordance with the SwissDRG system. Psychiatric and rehabilitation services are not part of the scope of services. The annual case volume is approximately 4'500 inpatient cases. The subject of this tender is the external primary coding of acute inpatient cases according to SwissDRG for the Kantonsspital Glarus (KSGL).

ORIGINAL POSTING: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) N00164-25-S-C001 Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC, Crane) The procedures outlined in this CSO apply to Areas of Interest posted under N00164-25-S-C001 OBJECTIVE: this announcement is intended to enable the rapid selection of innovative commercial solutions through a three-phased, competitive process. Including commercially-available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 1.1 Background and Authority NSWC Crane’s mission is to deliver innovative solutions and readiness to the Nation and its Warfighters through application of Technical Capabilities; advance all-domain system of systems within the Mission Areas of Expeditionary Warfare, Strategic Missions, and Electromagnetic Warfare; conduct science and technology, research, development, test and evaluation, acquisition and in-service engineering across the Defense lifecycles. To achieve these mission imperatives, NSWC Crane regularly partners with private industry using a variety of collaborative tools in order to streamline the incorporation of innovative technology into the products and services delivered to the Warfighter. To accelerate the adoption of advanced technology, curate solutions to technology gaps, and lead rapid prototyping NSWC Crane issues this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) as authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation. In this context “Innovative” means— Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. NSWC Crane is seeking innovative commercial solutions relevant to the following areas of technological exploration: • Expeditionary Warfare Guided by the National Defense Strategy, NSWC Crane recognizes the priorities and threats shifted to the Pacific. NSWC Crane’s efforts must counter the multi-domain threats and deter aggression posed in the Indo-Pacific region. This reinforces the need of a Joint Force that is even more lethal, resilient, agile and responsive. Autonomous solutions with a focus on payload and sensor integration to enhance detection, tracking, identifying, decision making, maneuver and kinetic/non-kinetic engagement capabilities for multi-domain, uncrewed and counter-crewed systems are a strategic priority. Expeditionary Warfare Development’s heritage has been and continues to focus on rapid prototyping and proven solutions supporting the evolving needs of the Expeditionary force. • Strategic Missions As the Navy’s primary organic field activity for full life cycle management including hardware, ordnance and power systems, NSWC Crane applies the distinct capabilities inherent to its people and facilities to assure 100% operational readiness of strategic missile systems. Fleet Readiness and Modernization and Hypersonics are a top priority of the Navy and DoD. These strategic priorities require collaboration between the Navy, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency to align appropriate requirements, technology development, rapid prototyping, production, sustainment and protection activities of ballistic missile systems to enable affordability, advance technology and reduce program risks to modernize the nuclear enterprise to defeat emerging threats worldwide. • Electromagnetic Warfare NSWC Crane’s Spectrum Warfare Department is the largest concentration of Electronic Warfare experts in the DoD. NSWC Crane provides non-kinetic expertise and electromagnetic spectrum dominance to all the services. Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) is a strategic priority due to the increasingly congested, contested and constrained environments. NSWC Crane supports multidomain integrated solutions through multispectral capabilities utilizing technology development, rapid prototyping, production and sustainment. Pursuant to DFARS 212.7002, NSWC Crane will only use this CSO to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements and to close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological advancements. All products and services acquired using this CSO will be treated as commercial products or commercial services, awarded on a fixed-price basis. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.10270, this announcement is a competitive selection of proposals based on a review by scientific, technological, or other subject-matter expert peers and is a competitive procedure. As a result of the competitive processes used under this CSO Announcement, multiple awards may be executed. The methods utilized to execute awards include: FARbased contract, Purchase Order, Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), and/or Bailment Agreement. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022, NSWC Crane may award an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to vendors to carry out prototype project(s) directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4023, NSWC Crane may procure (by contract or otherwise) ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, telecommunications, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary concerned considers necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense. 1.2 General Solicitation and Evaluation Procedures NSWC Crane’s CSO is soliciting Solution Briefs in response to individual Areas of Interest (AOIs). AOIs are focused topic(s) categories that will be published separately and posted on the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. All Solution Briefs submitted in response to AOIs will be governed by this CSO unless otherwise noted in the AOI. AOIs will be written in broad terms to maximize latitude in creativity when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from nontraditional defense contractors and interested parties (entities) who may be unfamiliar with submitting traditional proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post AOIs at any time. Interested parties are encouraged to frequently check the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC, Crane website for new AOI postings. Evaluation of responses will consist of the following 3 Phases: 1) Solution Brief, 2) Pitch, and 3) Full written proposal – described in more detail here: Phase 1 Solution Briefs: Solution Briefs submitted in response to an AOI shall be submitted as specified in Section 2 of this CSO. The Government will evaluate Solution Briefs against the criteria stated in this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for the costs associated with Solution Brief submissions. Phase 2 Pitch Session: Respondents whose Solution Briefs are evaluated to be of merit may be invited to provide a pitch following the instructions provided in Section 2.3 of this CSO. The Government reserves the right to limit the number of parties invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. In the event that the Government requires a demonstration, additional information will be provided in the specific AOI highlighting those procedures, otherwise Phase 2 will be comprised solely of the pitch. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with pitches, unless otherwise stipulated. Phase 3 Proposal: Those entities whose Solution Brief and Pitch are evaluated to be of merit and are selected for potential award may be invited to submit a full written proposal following the instructions provided in Section 2.4 of this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with the proposal in Phase 3, unless otherwise stipulated. SECTION 2 – GUIDELINES FOR SUBMISSION 2.1 General Guidelines Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. Companies may submit multiple Solution Briefs in response to any single AOI if each submission represents a separate and distinct concept. The period of performance for any Solution Brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24-months. Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. All Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals shall be unclassified. Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: “This [select one: Solution Brief, Pitch, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to non-Government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of -- or in connection with – the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use the information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: “Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.” Foreign-Owned businesses may independently submit a solution or do so as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more United States-Owned businesses. However, the ability to obtain an agreement based upon a submission may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-Owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain proscribed information. Submissions must be submitted electronically. Submissions sent through other channels or after the AOI period has ended will not be reviewed nor evaluated. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.2 Phase 1 Solution Brief PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF CONTENT Solution Briefs should not exceed five (5) written pages using 12-point font. Alternatively, Solution Briefs may take the form of briefing slides which should not exceed fifteen (15) slides. Briefs should include at a minimum: Title Page (does not count against page limit) Entity Name, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address. Specifically identify the AOI for which the Solution Brief is submitted. Executive Summary of the technology (one page) Describe the concept and unique aspects of the technology as it relates to the AOI. Identify whether the solution is an existing technology that has satisfied a pilot or demonstration (ie, commercially ready and viable technology), or the if the solution will require development for defense application. If development or adaptation is proposed, identify a suggested path to mature the technology. Identify aspects of the solution which may be considered proprietary or Intellectual Property (IP) Provide a brief overview of the company, including a summary of product commercialization and go-to-market strategy. PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF BASIS OF EVALUATION All solution briefs correctly submitted in response to an AOI will be evaluated against the stated criteria below. (Y/N) The proposed innovative commercial solution, technology, process, or method, is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or is an application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. Relevance of the Solution Brief in addressing the AOI. Technical Merit and feasibility of the solution to address Government AOI problem statement. A quick, reasonable, and efficient way exists for the DoD to test the innovative commercial solution, within a specified duration, whether outside or integrated within the DoD infrastructures or networks, as appropriate. Additional technical evaluation criteria specific to a particular project may be used. In these instances, the additional criteria will be posted within the AOI announcement on the SAM.Gov and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI, not against other Solution Briefs submitted in response to the same AOI. Additionally, while not overtly stated in AOIs, the Government’s evaluation will consider whether the proposal increases the likelihood of accomplishing NSWC Crane’s Mission Focus Areas. All submissions will be evaluated, however, only a select few will be invited to pitch. The government reserves the right to limit the number of entities invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.3 Phase 2 Pitch PHASE 2 PITCH CONTENT In Phase 2, entities shall provide an in-person or virtual pitch to demonstrate and provide further details on their proposed innovative commercial solution and the technical and business viability of the proposed solution. The Government may elect to use external market research during the Pitch to evaluate viability. In addition to the Pitch, the Government, at its discretion, may request for consideration an additional written submission to further supplement the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. During the Phase 2 Pitch, the Company must detail/address: Estimated Price/Schedule Rough order of magnitude (ROM) or pricing Anticipated Data Rights Assertions During the Pitch, the Government may request the additional information/detail with respect to the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. PHASE 2 PITCH BASIS OF EVALUATION Individual pitches will be evaluated against the following factors: Relevance of the pitch in addressing the AOI and the ability of the presenter to adequately address Government questions or concerns regarding the proposed application or use of the innovative commercial solution. The solution has technical merit, adequately & realistically addresses Government need and can be quickly incorporated into DOD systems. Reasonableness of the ROM The associated delivery schedule is expeditious and realistic. Individual pitches will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI and the factors above, not against any other Pitches held under the same AOI. Pitch submissions will be valid for 180 calendar days after the pitch date. Upon completion of evaluations, the Government will notify the Company that: (1) the proposed concept/technology/solution has been selected for possible award and the entity is invited to submit a full proposal; (2) the proposed concept/technology/solution is not of interest to the Government; or (3) the proposed concept/technology/solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources. If the proposed innovative commercial solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources, the Company may be contacted with a request to respond to proposal request within 180 calendar days from the pitch date. If after 180 calendar days from the pitch date (or earlier if notified by NSWC, Crane), Government resources are not identified to formally move into Phase 3, the entity will no longer be eligible for an award under that particular AOI. 2.4 Phase 3 Proposal PHASE 3 PROPOSAL CONTENT The final phase of the evaluation process is the proposal request. Based upon the evaluation process detailed in Phase 1 and 2, the Government may request a full written proposal. The entity will be invited to develop and submit a full written proposal and negotiate appropriate terms and conditions. Entities may discuss ideas and questions related to the proposal with the Government POC during the proposal writing process. Each proposal submitted shall consist of two sections: Section 1 shall consist of the technical proposal; Section 2 shall consist of the price/cost/schedule. Proposals will be assessed by NSWC Crane technical and Contracting subject matter experts. Entities may propose their own internal terms and conditions (e.g., Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA)) to be considered during negotiations with the Government. Note, there are certain terms and conditions the Government is unable to accept. Awards made under this authority will only be issued as fixed price awards in accordance with DFARS 212.7002(b). However, projects awarded through the CSO are flexible to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and where it meets the Government’s needs. At a minimum, written proposals must contain: Title Page Company Name, Point of Contact Name, Date, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address and any subcontractors or team members. Include an abstract which provides a concise description of the proposal. Description of the proposed innovative commercial solution Background and objectives of the proposed solution, deliverables, and resources needed to execute. Include the nature and extent of the anticipated results. Include ancillary and operational issues such as certifications, algorithms, and any engineering/software development methodologies to be used. If services, include a Statement of Work (SOW). Provide a detailed project schedule that outlines the various phases of work to be accomplished within the proposed period of performance. You may refer to the Solution Brief that prompted this proposal request, but do not duplicate it. Identify any Government material, equipment, data, or other items necessary. Phase 3 - Price Proposal The entity shall propose a fixed price for the item or service and provide any data or supporting information necessary for the determination of a fair and reasonable price. This can include, but is not limited to, commercial price catalog or other proprietary information to help the Government assess the proposed price. Additionally, if proposing an OT, while not required to be specifically addressed in the proposal (with the exception of the 1/3 cost-share requirement, if applicable), the Government will review the proposal to determine if the following OT statutory requirements are met: Fits the definition of a prototype Meets non-traditional participation/cost share requirement: Non-traditional defense contractor contributes to a significant extent or not; if not, 1/3 cost share implementation is addressed Defense Utility: Solution is applicable to a DoD platform, system or component SECTION 3 – AWARDS 3.1 General Guidelines Upon favorable review and available funds, the Government may choose to make an award. Only Warranted Contracting Officers or Agreements Officers may obligate the Government by entering into or modifying a binding agreement on behalf of the Government. Awards made under this CSO will be fixed price. Contract type will be determined during Phase 3. Multiple awards may be made to pursue similar or dissimilar solutions should they all meet the technical criteria, be selected for award, and if funds are available. Entities must have a DUNs and CAGE Code registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award. Companies are advised to commence SAM registration upon receipt of a proposal request. Awardees must be determined to be responsible by the Contracting or Agreements Officer and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving award. Receipt of a proposal request does not guarantee receipt of award. The Government reserves the right, at any point prior to award, to cancel the request. Upon award, awardees must register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (e.g. Wide Area Work Flow). 3.2 Comptroller General Access to Information In OT projects that provide for payments in a total amount in excess of $5,000,000, the Agreement will include a mandatory clause that provides for the Comptroller General the ability to examine the records of any party to the agreement or any entity that participates in the performance of the agreement. 3.3 Procurement Integrity Act (PIA) All awards under this CSO shall be treated as Federal Agency procurements for purpose of 41 U.S.C. Chapter 21. Accordingly, the CSO competitive solicitation process and awards made thereof must adhere to the ethical standards required by the PIA. SECTION 4 - ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING As it is the mission of NSWC Crane to enable access to commercially-derived disruptive capabilities across the entirety of the DoD enterprise, Prototype OTAs awarded against this CSO will allow for an iterative prototyping process. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the work in a prototype project to allow the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the original Government customer or originate with other organizations within the Federal Government. SECTION 5 – FOLLOW-ON PRODUCTION Upon successful completion of a prototype project under the OTA, the Government may negotiate a follow-on production contract or agreement without further competition. Any concept/technology/solution successfully proven through a Prototype OTA can be transitioned to production. AOIs posted by the Government under this CSO and Prototype OTAs awarded will include language providing for the potential award of a follow-on production contract or agreement as authorized under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 Individual AOIs and CSO prototype OTAs will explicitly identify follow-on Prototype OTAs as a potential outcome of a successful prototyping effort. SECTION 6 SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION A transaction for a prototype project is complete upon the written determination of the appropriate approving official (program manager and Agreement Officer) for the matter in question that efforts conducted under a Prototype OTA: (1) met the key technical goals of a project; (2) satisfied success metrics incorporated into the Prototype OTA; or (3) accomplished a particularly favorable or unexpected result that justifies the transition to production. Furthermore, successful completion can occur prior to the conclusion of a prototype project to allow the Government to transition any aspect of the prototype project determined to provide utility into production while other aspects of the prototype project have yet to be completed. Any Prototype OTA shall contain a provision that sets forth the conditions under which that prototype agreement must be successfully completed. SECTION 7 – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during Proposal development and negotiations. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. Companies may enter into specific NDAs directly with the Non-Government advisors or their corporate entities. Submission of an offer under this CSO will constitute a grant of authority by the submitting company to the Government to allow the use of non-Government advisors to participate in evaluations of all phases of the CSO process. The Government understands that information provided in response to this CSO is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. NSWC, Crane policy is to treat all submissions as source selection sensitive information, and to disclose their contents only for the purpose of evaluation. Restrictive notices notwithstanding, during the evaluation process, submissions may be handled by support contractors for administrative purposes and/or to assist with technical evaluation. All NSWC, Crane and DoD support contractors performing this role are expressly prohibited from performing NSWC, Crane-sponsored technical research and are bound by appropriate NDAs. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained at NSWC, Crane and all other non-required copies destroyed. A certification of destruction may be requested, provided the formal request is received at this office within 5 calendar days after notification that a proposal was not selected.
