sig_9d6f7f0318057a43b3de.description: The main object of the framework agreement consists of specialist support granted to the contracting authority for carrying out specific tasks for conducting procurement procedures initiated to cover their needs and carrying out investments within the development plan approved at the level of the administrative-territorial unit. The specific objective consists in streamlining the procurement activity process by reducing the risk of errors materialised in fines/corrections related to the manner of carrying out the procurement processes, as well as reducing the number of issues arising during the implementation of contracts – contract modifications, optimisation of the administration of the public procurement process portfolio, improvement of tender documentation likely to lead to the selection of economic operators who possess and have at their disposal the capacity to successfully complete the concluded procurement contracts. The contracting authority considers it necessary for the activity to be supplemented by the acquisition of consultancy services, hereinafter referred to as auxiliary procurement services, in order to support the activity of internal compartments specialised in the field of procurement, for the drafting of documents/documentation necessary to go through the stages of the public/sectoral procurement/concession processes and/or for the implementation of programmes for the prevention/mitigation of risks in public procurement, targeting all stages from the planning/preparation of the process, organisation/application of the award procedure up to the execution/monitoring of the implementation of the procurement contract/framework agreement, including in relation to the activity of the evaluation committee and/or the settlement of appeals. Estimated value of the largest subsequent contract: 1.497.200 lei excluding VAT 1) The contracting authority will clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarification/additional information on the 11-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders cf. sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.description: The contracting authority is tendering a contract regarding Transition In, development of the Modernised Support Systems, application operation, application maintenance, support, ordering services, including further development of the Support Systems, as well as Transition Out. The contract consists of the following 3 main services: I. Transition In, including, among other things, a secure and stable takeover of the application responsibility for the Support Systems, implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, transfer of source code and documentation, implementation of technical transition and necessary transformation, takeover of knowledge from the outgoing supplier as well as establishment of the operations organisation, including establishment of the collaboration with the operations supplier. II. Ongoing services for the Support Systems, including; a. Support, including, among other things, responsibility for Service Desk, user administration, handling of incidents, problems, service requests, early life support, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of ensuring high availability for the users; b. Application operation, including, among other things, database operation, operation of middleware, backup, restore, monitoring and logging, 2. and 3. line support, configuration, patch, and release and deployment management, cf. the operational processes, and operational reporting with high requirements for uptime and response times; c. Application maintenance, including, among other things, ongoing and preventive maintenance of the IT systems, minor changes, new versions, bug fixes, release management, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of supporting high requirements for uptime and response times; d. Governance, including close collaboration with the operations supplier, operational processes, security services, documentation and operational reporting. III. Agile development, e.g. via a design and planning phase, including proof of concept, as well as a development phase based on the supplier's product vision and advice. Development of the Modernised Support Systems takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties regarding support for the contracting authority's business goals and needs, so that the Modernised Support Systems can be implemented after a time-limited period. Development includes any new functionality as well as any re-implementation and reuse of parts of the current Support Systems. Further development of the Support Systems also takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties. It is the contracting authority's business need that all services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In Transition In, the supplier must take over the application responsibility for the Support Systems and, from the transition day, deliver ongoing services, including, among other things, application operation, application maintenance and further development, to the Support Systems. The further development will take place in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority. The supplier must also, in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority, carry out a modernisation of the Support Systems based on the contracting authority's modernisation wishes. The Support Systems are part of the overall joint municipal infrastructure, and the supplier must therefore collaborate partly with the other suppliers, including the operations supplier as well as suppliers who deliver other parts of the joint municipal infrastructure, and partly with users of the infrastructure. It is the contracting authority's business goal and need, among other things, to give parts of the current Support Systems a quality boost in the form of a modernisation that supports the Modernised Support Systems appearing attractive, reliable, future-proof and secure, so that the municipalities also in the future have a strong foundation to deliver the best digital services to the citizens in an increasingly more coherent, efficient and modern public sector.
sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.title: Tender for Support Systems

sig_9dbcee159f0cff96c1aa.description: The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) is an Arm’s Length Body (ALB) of the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). We deliver a wide range of national services for the NHS, contractors, patients and the public. NHSBSA currently undertakes benchmarking in selected areas of its business, both internally and with external support, alongside informal peer networks. This RFI is intended to explore how additional external benchmarking services could complement and broaden that activity across all NHSBSA services. NHSBSA is interested exploring alternative options for benchmarking across its diverse services. As a business services provider, our activities are potentially often comparable to private sector organisations (e.g. insurance companies, shared services providers) as well as other NHS Arm’s Length Bodies. This RFI will help us understand how external suppliers can support benchmarking that is credible, repeatable, and insightful, with clear value for money. Scope of services We are particularly interested in benchmarking services that can support: • Operational efficiency - cost per transaction, turnaround times, digital adoption • Contact centre operations • Customer experience - across digital and offline channels • Digital and technology delivery • Back-office services cost/size including Finance, Commercial and HR • Maturity assessments and performance dashboards - providing structured frameworks and visibility of progress NHSBSA is open to comparators from both public and private sectors where relevant. NHSBSA are carrying out this pre-tender market engagement exercise to understand more about the market capabilities for benchmarking our services and at this stage we are seeking high-level input to enable us to assess our options which may potentially inform any future procurement strategy ensuring compliance with The Procurement Act 2023 in respect of benchmarking services. Interested parties must register an interest in this RFI via https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome (search opportunities using system reference C387227). Suppliers can register from 25th September 2025 and the RFI documents will be made available on 25th September 2025. Registration for the event will close on 30th October 2025 12:00 BST. As part of our pre-tender market engagement process for the provision of External Benchmarking Services, Registered suppliers are invited to attend a Supplier Briefing Session which will consist of a presentation via Microsoft Teams which will be held on 20th October 2025 09:30-10:30. Suppliers may also request an optional 1-2-1 session on 20th & 22nd October 2025. Written RFI responses are requested by no later than Friday 31st October 2025 12:00 BST. The NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) invites all interested economic operators to participate in an RFI and a Supplier Webinar, followed by a number of 121 sessions in addition to a number of questions. Suppliers can answer and submit following the presentation. Following this pre-tender market engagement should a procurement follow, then depending upon the chosen route to market and value (existing framework or covered procurement) it will be governed by either the Public Contract Regulations 2015 or the Procurement Act 2023. Any subsequent invitation to tender and notices will be aligned to the relevant regulation/act. As this RFI is exploring the market capability and associated costs which are unknown at present this is reflected in the Total Contract Value set out in this notice. Once the RFI process has concluded we hope to have a greater understanding of any potential contract value. Lot 1: .

sig_9ddb8eedda1619b3ec33.description: 1. Introduction OsloBygg KF is considering to procure a digital service for condition based operational monitoring of technical installations in nurseries. The objective of the market survey is to gain better insight into the market and input from suppliers on what systems are available, what can be delivered and how such services can normally be introduced. The market survey is not a competition and the contracting authority is not requesting tenders at this point in time. Participation in the market survey gives no rights or advantages in any later procurement. 2. Provisional need The contracting authority would like input on digital systems that can monitor technical components in nurseries by using sensors, audio analysis, vibration analysis or other relevant measurement parameters. The analysis shall be carried out by KI or ML and it shall automatically alarm in the event of deviations and errors. The system is particularly relevant for: * ventilation aggregates * engines * Fans * Pumps * other relevant technical components The aim of any system is to uncover abnormal operations, errors or wear at an early stage, so that the contracting authority can carry out more targeted and preventive maintenance. The system ought to be able to contribute to better operational security, reduced energy consumption, fewer operational deviations and a better overview of the condition of the technical installations. 3. Input from the market The contracting authority would like general input from suppliers on: * what systems and technologies are available in the market * the types of technical installations and components that can be monitored * if the systems can be used on existing installations without comprehensive reconstruction * how notification, reporting and visualisation normally works * whether the systems can be integrated with MOM systems. * what gains and effects suppliers believe such solutions could provide
sig_9ddb8eedda1619b3ec33.title: Market survey - Condition based operational monitoring of technical installations in nurseries.

sig_9dde345c02b247504173.description: There is a demand for various services, which are being tendered in the form of a maintenance contract, a service contract and a framework agreement. Due to the individual specialist procedures for the Electronic Commercial and Partnership Register (EHUG), the electronic criminal message exchange (ESTA) and the use of the DOMEA document management system, the BfJ works with standard Kofax scanning software. Kofax is required for the creation of electronic documents from the paper-based incoming mail of EHUG and the judiciary recovery service. The BfJ intends to continue using the software, meaning that a new maintenance contract is required for continuous maintenance from 1 January 2027. An EVB-IT maintenance contract is to be concluded for this purpose. A connector was developed for connection to the EHUG specialist procedure. This interface (custom software) must also be placed under maintenance from 1 January 2027. This will be concluded under an EVB-IT service contract. The central scanning office of the BfJ has been upgraded in accordance with TR-RESISCAN specifications. To implement the TR-RESISCAN specifications technically, adjustments and expansions were made to Kofax by the current service provider. The scanned material passes through the Kofax-own modules Scanning, PDFGenerator and Export during the scanning process. Furthermore, they pass through modules of the current service provider (Kofax Capture Custom Modules). The maintenance of the Kofax Capture Custom Modules is also part of this tender and will likewise be required from 1 January 2027. These three service components are each to be provided and billed via an annual flat rate. In addition, there is a demand by the BfJ for creation, development and other services. A framework agreement will be concluded for this purpose. Development and further development services are to be commissioned for the existing EHUG interface as well as potentially other new specialist procedures. Configuration and development services may need to be provided for the connection of new specialist procedures. Other services may be called upon, inter alia, as consultancy services, workshops and/or as operational support, e.g. for installation/configuration work or development work on site at the contractor's premises, in the form of telephone consultation and/or as remote support. A more detailed description of the service can be found in the specification of services ( Leistungsbeschreibung - LB).

The BITMARCK Holding GmbH and BITMARCK GmbH intend to award framework agreements for the provision of various IT services for the BITMARCK corporate group. The procurement is divided into 20 lots. The services comprise in particular project coordination, security analyses, SQL support, specification services, workplace application management, SAP HCM application management, testing services, telematics services, Java backend development, SPPM governance, SAP application development, test environment management, test automation, expert consulting, migration, performance testing, TI consulting, UX and UI design, process modelling and vulnerability management. Companies may submit tenders for one lot, several lots or all lots. Examination and evaluation will be carried out separately for each lot. Framework agreements with a maximum of five companies are to be concluded per lot. Lot LOT-0001: Lot 1 - Project Coordination. The subject matter of this lot is IT services for the structuring, planning, coordination and quality assurance of IT projects in the environment of the products, solutions and services of the BITMARCK corporate group. IT project management involves the implementation of projects in accordance with the project management method of BITMARCK. This method was adapted closely based on PRINCE2 to the requirements of BITMARCK and BITMARCK customers in the statutory health insurance (GKV) environment. The aim is to obtain external specialist expertise for the methodical planning, documentation and tracking of project-related requirements and results. To this end, the contractor contributes its own specialist know-how on the application of established project management methods in IT projects and independently draws up the service results described below. The contractor shall provide needs-based support services in IT project management within the scope of customer projects and BITMARCK internal projects. Service-related coordination shall take place exclusively to the extent necessary for the proper provision of services between the client's designated single point of contact, in particular the Project Management Hub (PMH) as well as the Head of IT Project Management, and the contractor. The organisation of the service provision as well as the selection and control of the sub-contractors deployed for contract performance are the sole responsibility of the contractor. The services comprise in particular: • Project initiation and establishment of a suitable project organisation including roles and responsibilities clarification, team building and preparation of the project start. • Analysis of project requirements as well as the organisational, professional and technical framework conditions as a basis for structured project execution. • Creation, maintenance and coordination of project management concepts including project structure, schedule, resource, communication, quality, risk and documentation planning. • Planning and control of project objectives, results, work packages, milestones, dependencies and deliverables taking into account the agreed project specifications. • Identification, analysis, evaluation, documentation and tracking of stakeholders, risks, opportunities, dependencies, decisions, changes and courses of action. • Establishment and implementation of an addressee-appropriate information, communication, reporting and escalation management including the preparation and execution of project and steering committees. • Control and monitoring of project progress with regard to deadlines, resources, expenditure, costs, quality and scope of services as well as execution of project-related controlling. • Creation, maintenance and quality assurance of project information, proofs, status reports, progress reports, decision documentation as well as result and completion documentation. • Planning, coordination and monitoring of quality and test measures including the tracking of deviations as well as ensuring defined quality requirements and acceptance criteria. • Administration and maintenance of project documentation as well as execution of document, configuration and change management to ensure transparency, traceability and auditability. • Execution of project-specific analyses, reviews and evaluations as well as derivation of recommendations for action for clients and project committees. • Control of external service providers and suppliers including performance monitoring, contract and claims management as well as support of acceptances. • Orderly project handover and project closure including results preservation, knowledge transfer, final reporting and lessons-learned considerations. For cost calculation purposes, this lot is based on an annual demand for services whose provision triggers an effort of approx. 1.750 person-days (so-called estimated quantity). For the maximum duration of the framework agreement (up to 4 years including extension options), this results in an estimated order volume of up to 3960 person-days. The maximum order volume (maximum quantity) is quantified – based on the maximum duration – at 7000 person-days (= 150 % of the estimated quantity). Lot LOT-0002: Lot 2 - Execution of Security Analyses. Within the scope of this lot, IT services in the form of consultancy services and other IT services in the cybersecurity and resilience management (CSRM) area of the BITMARCK corporate group are being tendered. The aim is to obtain external specialist expertise for issues relating to incident response and IT forensics in the Cyber Defence Center. The contractor ("contractor" or

"tenderer") to provide IT services comprise in particular ensuring the operational readiness of supervised security solutions, security-related consulting in the context of projects and applications, the analysis and evaluation of security incidents, forensic evidence preservation and evaluation, the provision of defined services within the scope of the incident response process as well as the conception and further development of the security platforms and associated security solutions of the BITMARCK corporate group. The services shall be provided independently and self-organised by the contractor on the basis of the respective commissioning and the service items, requirements and results defined therein. sig_9e03d76eab069222b52f.description: Region Syddanmark puts out to tender a contract concerning a Warehouse Management System (WMS) for the new Esbjerg Hospital Storage and Logistics Centre. Esbjerg Hospital's physical framework for the Storage and Supply Service is 100% utilised and cannot support the desired growth and future-proofing that is required. The Storage and Supply Service is currently located in the basement of Esbjerg Hospital, where all goods are delivered on xsØstergade in the inner city of Esbjerg. Esbjerg Hospital's new Storage and Logistics Centre will form the framework for an increase in goods in storage which ensures the supply to Esbjerg Hospital and partners. The increase in stored goods has a positive impact on the green transition in the form of a reduction in transport to the Storage and Logistics Centre compared to the current load. Heavy and black traffic in Esbjerg inner city will be significantly reduced by the establishment of Esbjerg Hospital's new Storage and Logistics Centre. The Esbjerg Hospital Storage and Logistics Centre supplies Esbjerg & Grindsted Hospital, the Venereology Clinic in Brørup, Psychiatry on Gl. Vardevej and all local psychiatric departments. Esbjerg Hospital cooperates with the surrounding municipalities regarding, among other things, IV treatments in citizens' homes as well as the upcoming Health and Care Facilities. The cooperation includes an agreement on supplies for local depots in the cooperating municipalities. The tendered task comprises the delivery, implementation, configuration and customisation of the WMS, including the establishment of integrations, training of superusers and users, trials and testing as well as commissioning, operation, support and maintenance. At the time of entering into the tendered Contract, the storage building is under construction. The supplier's services also include project management and coordination with the contractor – KG Hansen, though primarily with the supplier of AutoStore and Conveyor systems – Element Logic. The WMS solution delivered in accordance with the tendered Contract must fulfil the requirements for function, quality, capacity, etc., which appear from the tender documentation. The Region needs up to 2 sites with 3 superusers and 12 users. One site is to be used for Esbjerg Hospital as part of the Delivery, and the other site is to be connected for Grindsted Hospital during the contract period without additional costs. Grindsted Hospital does not have a corresponding WMS, but only manual stores. The task is tendered as one single contract based on functional, market-related and economic considerations. The contract is indefinite. The Customer has a notice period of 12 months, and the Supplier has a notice period of 24 months, though at the earliest to expire 5 years after the Take-over Day.
sig_9e03d76eab069222b52f.title: Tender for WMS for new Warehouse & Logistics Centre for Esbjerg Hospital

sig_9e076abeedbb7c1835c4.description: The three Regional Assemblies are seeking to appoint suitably qualified and experienced consultants to prepare: A report for each of the three Regions to establish and allocate local authority on-shore wind energy and solar energy targets. This report will be underpinned by a comprehensive geospatial and environmental analysis to help establish viable renewable energy targets for local authorities. The consultant will engage with relevant infrastructure stakeholders (namely EirGrid and ESB Networks) to identify grid capacity, constraints and any planned infrastructure projects. The consultant will take account of energy security needs for the Regions in order to meet regional (and national) targets for constituent local authorities in each Region, achieve compliance with all statutory requirements in legislation. Each report will be a bespoke document specific to each Regional Assembly territory based on an agreed methodology (further detail in the next paragraph). sig_9e4fb05ce5604c37e9e9.description: The Contract is for the purchase, delivery and implementation of Ørsted Risk Management Platform to the Contracting Entity for the Project. The purpose of the purchase is for Ørsted to acquire a comprehensive Risk Management Platform to support our organization in effectively managing risks across our company, including wind farm operations. Ørsted operates in the renewable energy sector, manages a diverse portfolio of wind assets, both in development and in operation. The complexity of operations, along with external factors like environmental regulations and regulatory requirements, requires the continuous evolution of our risk management approach to maintain resilience, agility, and efficiency across the risk lifecycle. We aim to establish a platform where the major business risk areas will be able to manage their detailed risks in their individual access-controlled domains. Risks should be able to be aggregated at an enterprise level with integration from other risk systems. The new platform should enable us to capture risks consistently from many business areas across the organization, promote consistency in risk evaluation, and facilitate enhanced communication and decision-making at all layers of the business. The platform should support structured risk identification and assessment methodologies, allowing Ørsted to prioritize risk based on likelihood and impact, and assign clear ownership and mitigation actions.
sig_9e4fb05ce5604c37e9e9.title: Tender for ​purchase, delivery and implementation of Ørsted Risk Management Platform

sig_9e5242d7228c30d25fdc.description: Under the supervision of the contracting authority, the service provider must carry out an analytical study intended to serve as a strategic decision-making aid aimed at guiding the establishment of an early detection system for CBRN agents in the context of intentional acts. The analytical study is based on a method of literature review, technological comparison and strategic evaluation. It does not constitute an equipment acquisition phase or an operational deployment project. The service provider has complete methodological freedom, provided that the expected deliverables are produced, usable and comply with the essential requirements defined; to this end, the expected deliverables must enable: 1) an understanding of available technologies; 2) an objective comparison contextualised by the employment contexts defined in point 1.4 of document B; 3) operational and financially controlled recommendations. The analytical study must answer the following questions: • which chemical and biological agents present the most credible and serious threat in the context of an intentional act targeting Belgian critical infrastructure or population gatherings? • which detection technologies perform best for these specific agents, in the identified employment contexts? • what combination of fixed and mobile technologies makes it possible to cover the priority contexts identified by the risk analysis in an optimal manner? • what cost/efficiency/coverage balance is achievable within the framework of a realistic deployment on Belgian critical infrastructure? The analytical study does not provide for the carrying out of: • technical trials in real conditions; • experimental evaluations of equipment; • measurement or detection campaigns. The analytical study will rely primarily on: • available technical data; • existing feedback from experience; • information communicated by manufacturers or users. The service provider must guarantee a neutral and independent approach in the analytical study of the technologies studied. The recommendations formulated may under no circumstances be oriented so as to favour a particular supplier or a specific technology without objective technical justification. The analytical study must be structured into three successive and interdependent parts, each composed of one or more deliverables. These three parts are described in points 1.3. to 1.5 of document B.
sig_9e5242d7228c30d25fdc.title: Framework agreement via an open procedure for an analytical study relating to chemical and biological (CB) agent detection technologies, in the context of intentional acts targeting critical infrastructure on behalf of SPF Intérieur

sig_9e81c059856c2c12935f.description: Simulator maintenance services: Existing simulator software maintenance – software recommissioning, software repair, ensuring replacement of conventional hardware by reinstalling the software. Existing simulator specific hardware maintenance – periodic check and repair/replacement, cleaning. Existing simulator technical support – provision of all available software modifications and remediation of deficiencies contained by the installed system. The provision of simulator maintenance services shall be carried out for a period of 12 months from the date of signing of the contract by both parties. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (2) of Law no. 98/2016, with subsequent amendments and completions, the Contracting Authority shall transmit the consolidated response formulated to requests for clarifications/additional information at least 10 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders, to the extent that they are transmitted within the specified term. The contracting authority shall conclude a contract for a period of 12 calendar months with a single economic operator, following the application of the simplified procedure, for the provision of simulator maintenance services, as follows:  Existing simulator software maintenance – software recommissioning, software repair, ensuring conventional hardware replacement by reinstalling the software; In situations where conventional hardware (standard computers making up the simulator) breaks down, or must be replaced for reasons of physical or moral wear and tear, the contractor shall undertake to ensure the reinstallation of the software on this equipment (procured by the contracting authority/entity), so that the simulator as a whole maintains its functionality;  Specific maintenance of the existing simulator hardware – periodic check and repairs/replacement, cleaning; In situations where specific hardware (proprietary hardware modules or equipment dedicated to the specific operation of the simulator and making up the simulator) breaks down, the contractor shall undertake to ensure its repair or replacement (the costs of these operations being borne by the contracting authority/entity, not forming part of the object of the contract), reinstallation of the equipment so that the simulator as a whole maintains its functionality;  Existing simulator technical support - provision of all available software modifications and remediation of deficiencies contained by the installed system. During the execution of the contract, the contractor's activity shall be carried out as follows:  The contractor shall perform maintenance – computer technical assistance, taking into consideration the latest version marketed by the manufacturer, where applicable, being accompanied by manufacturer licenses;  Any subsequent version must ensure functional requirements and take into account the existing hardware configuration;  If the subsequent version requires standard hardware or software modifications (for example PCs with another configuration, operating systems), the contractor shall communicate this aspect to the contracting authority/entity, before installation, in order to be able to prevent a non-functioning state and so that the buyer can make an appropriate decision;  If required, the contractor shall perform installation and configuration activities of licenses at the buyer, as an extension of the existing system;  The contractor shall provide user, operation and administration documentation in Romanian or English, technical description of database structures, relations between modules and procedures, naming conventions used, etc.;  The contractor shall ensure, at the buyer's request, technical assistance for the installation and configuration of delivered licenses at the buyer's headquarters;  The contractor shall ensure permanent on-line computer and operational technical assistance for software, hardware and operation at the buyer's headquarters, upon request, (no later than 2 (two) working days from the date of announcing the necessity), throughout the contract period;  During the present contract, the contractor shall obligatorily include a service session at the beneficiary's headquarters, with a duration of at least 4 days x 1 man, of which one day for the installation of the new software version. Procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement 3 in parts for Visit Hungary Nemzeti Turisztikai Szervezet Közhasznú Nonprofit Zrt. for the performance of strategic media agency, digital media agency and market research tasks. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. The aim of the Contracting Authority's communication activity is to promote Hungary for tourism purposes, strengthen inbound tourism from abroad, stimulate domestic tourism, and present the Hungarian tourism offering domestically and internationally. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform the tasks specified in the Technical Specification for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of strategic media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 3.200.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different media mix and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform strategic media agency, media planning, media buying, campaign management, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to media appearances for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The exact professional content, performance deadline, quantity, technical parameters and individual expectations of the tasks are contained in the individual orders. The Contracting Authority's domestic campaigns are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 250 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 6–8 weeks. Campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 80 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–10 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation of a media strategy, integrated media mix and media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups and channels, - strategic media agency tasks on specified channels - preparation, execution and monitoring of campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - proposal for a KPI system adapted to the nature, objective, channels and target markets of the given campaign, as well as tracking, interpretation and evaluation of campaign performance, with special regard to tourism KPIs - preparation of regular, inter-campaign and campaign-closing reports according to an agreed reporting structure. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.; The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of digital media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 820.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and digital media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism digital advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different digital media mix, targeting logic, platform usage and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform digital media agency, digital media planning, digital media buying, campaign management, optimisation, measurement, analytics, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to digital media appearances for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. The Contracting Authority's domestic digital campaigns are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Digital campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - formulation of a digital campaign strategy and digital media plan, development of digital targeting, platform and channel proposals, - performance of digital media buying and campaign management tasks, continuous tracking and optimisation of campaign performance, support for measurement and analytical settings, - evaluation and reporting of digital KPIs, (with special regard to tourism relevance) - support for the compilation of performance certification documentation, - preparation of a digital campaign strategy, digital media mix and digital media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, digital media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups, digital channels and advertising platforms, - performance of media agency tasks on specified channels and platforms, - preparation of digital campaigns, - launching of digital campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of digital media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - establishment, management and operation of an agreed advertising account structure, - support for the establishment, operation and, where necessary, development of the measurement environment related to digital campaigns, - preparation of inter-campaign reports and campaign-closing evaluation. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.;

The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of market research tasks up to a net framework amount of 320.000.000 HUF. The CA undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the CA plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. Research and analysis tasks may also cover domestic and international target markets, different target groups, campaigns, brands, destinations, communication objectives, consumer motivations, media usage characteristics, tourism decisions or campaign effectiveness issues. The CA's research projects are of a mixed nature: they include quantitative research with larger sample sizes directed at Hungary and affecting target markets outside Hungary, primary research affecting multiple target markets, as well as smaller-element qualitative, motivational, service quality, mystery shopping or other decision-supporting research tasks. The Contracting Authority generally performs the implementation of a residential quantitative research of 1000 persons once a year in 10-15 countries, and in addition initiates a minimum of 2 qualitative, small-group focus group researches in Hungary (focus groups are generally implemented with 4–8 groups, with an average participation of 6 persons per group) and manages a nationwide mystery shopping annually with a minimum of 80 trial purchases. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform market research, data acquisition, analysis and decision-supporting tasks for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation, organisation, execution, analysis and documentation of research, data acquisitions, analyses and decision-supporting materials founding, supporting or evaluating marketing and communication activity. - preparation of a research plan or methodological proposal adapted to the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task, - organisation, execution, coordination and control of research data recording, fieldwork or data collection. - processing, checking, cleaning, systematisation, analysis, interpretation of data available as a result of research or data acquisition, and formulation of decision-supporting conclusions, - with the prior approval of the CA, may carry out data purchases, procure syndicated research, or utilise an external data source or study on behalf of the CA, - performing administration related to possible research modifications, data recording changes, cancellations, data purchase or syndicated research limitations, - the Winning Tenderer is obliged to present the results of the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task according to a structure agreed with the Client. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.

sig_9e95134797688f91fdae.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) relating to the procurement of IT operations and related services. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Appendix B Customer List, to make use of the System when procuring IT operations services. The customer list in Appendix B.1 specifies the customers and their organisations that are customers of SKI at the time of tender and can therefore use the System. However, throughout the term of the System, the dynamic purchasing system may be used by all contracting authorities that are customers of SKI at the time a specific procurement is published in the System. All parts of the Danish state, regions and municipalities – including public companies and publicly owned companies subject to procurement obligations as a result of their public ownership – may become customers of SKI by taking out a subscription covering their organisation. When new contracting authorities become customers of SKI, SKI will update the customer list on SKI.dk and announce on SKI.dk that a change has been made to SKI's customer list, as well as which contracting authorities are new customers of SKI and from which date they can publish procurements in the system. The customer list in Appendix B.1 is not updated after the time of tender. Instead, SKI's customer list in force at any given time will be publicly available on SKI.dk. The System will be tendered as a single combined category with a single combined subject matter for IT operations services. The category is created with a view to the customer's need to procure IT operations services across the service areas of the subject matter. The System can be used to procure the following service areas: 1. Cloud operations 2. Data centre operations 3. Co-location 4. Network operations 5. Application operations 6. End-user services 7. sig_9ea325fdd73e88495155.description: Translink are looking to engage with suppliers capable of providing a scheduling and depot allocation system to support bus operations on Ulsterbus and Metro Fleet. The system would be expected to allow Translink operations to efficiently create route diagrams, timetables and duty allocation for the full network in Northern Ireland, and some cross-border services. Translink require the system to interface with wider bus systems, including the control room interface, therefore, a cloud-based, open data architecture is necessary, to ensure that the bus systems can integrate with other client systems, enhancing data flow and ensuring regular operations continue without interruption. The supplier will be required to maintain and support upgrades to the system to ensure Translink are able to take advantage of market developments. Before embarking on a tender process, Translink wishes to engage with the marketplace to gather information which will be used to inform the sourcing strategy for this contract and thus, the procurement process. We are therefore looking to engage with providers that are experienced in scheduling and depot allocation systems, which believe they are capable of fulfilling all requirements below. It is anticipated that this contract will commence in Q1 2027. Our requirements include, but are not limited to the following: • Facilitate bus route development. • Facilitate Timetable and staff rota development. • Provide reporting on bus mileage to allow Translink to reconcile fleet mileage. • Provide a method of storing and managing fleet details. • Support integration with a wide variety of third-party bus systems that are already in place. • Facilitate a bus stop asset database which contains information including, the NaPTAN location code, stop name, locality, and facilities (shelter/pole). • Allow for daily variation outside of the regular timetables and schedules during peak periods. • Flag errors or notifications between the scheduling system and wider bus systems. • Allow for the fleets (Ulsterbus and Metro) to be managed independently of each other, to facilitate their specific requirements. • Support data exports and imports in recognised formats such as TransXChange and CIF files. • Verify that all rotas are compliant with EU regulations relating to driver rest and compensation during allocated duties. • Verify that all duties are accounted for in the driver rotas. • Allow for operational changes, such as driver pay allocations to be manually updated by schedulers. • Include a dedicated analytics package that supports manual and automated performance and management reporting. • Support integration with current, and future bus systems. To advance to the next stage, suppliers must also be able to demonstrate that they have supplied a similar solution to customers with a similar fleet size (c. 1400 vehicles) within the last 3 years. Lot 1: .
sig_9ea325fdd73e88495155.title: Bus Scheduling and Depot Allocation System

Subproject 3 "Scientific support and other supportive actions of the Operation for the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027" shall be awarded to third parties through an open tendering procedure in application of the provisions of Law 4412/2016 (sub-threshold) and comprises 3 Work Packages as follows: • WP1: Development of National Diagnostic Examination subjects for the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027. • WP2: Results of National Diagnostic Examinations for the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027. • WP3: Other supportive actions during the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 This Call for Tenders concerns the implementation of WP1, WP2 and WP3 which shall be awarded to third parties through an open tendering procedure in application of the provisions of Law 4412/2016 (sub-threshold). The Work Packages of Subproject 3 within the framework of this Call for Tenders are divided into 3 lots, namely, Lot 1 concerns WP1, Lot 2 concerns WP2 and Lot 3 concerns WP3, as follows: The purpose of WP1 is the development of theoretical and/or research-documented subjects and corresponding closed and open questions for the subject of Modern Greek Language and Mathematics for the school year 2025-26 which are designed as a core tool for evaluating the knowledge, attitudes and skills of pupils in the sixth year of primary school (St' Dimotikou) and the third year of lower secondary school (G' Gymnasiou). The main objective is to offer documented feedback, while enhancing reflective practice and the provision of evidence in a substantive and useful way for all stakeholders, as well as to help shape proposals for improving educational policy in Primary and Secondary Education. Respectively, the purpose of WP2 is the analysis of the results of closed and open questions of the National Diagnostic Examinations in the subjects of Modern Greek Language and Mathematics of pupils in the sixth year of primary school (St' Dimotikou) and the third year of lower secondary school (G' Gymnasiou) during the school years 2025-26 and 2026-27 as well as the presentation, theoretical documentation and feedback on related research questions/hypotheses. The main objective is to offer documented feedback, while enhancing reflective practice and the provision of evidence in a substantive and useful way for all stakeholders, as well as to help shape proposals for improving educational policy in Primary and Secondary Education. The subject of WP3 comprises the printing of Answer Sheets, their dispatch and collection from the sample schools in order to conduct, at a national level, during the school years 2025-26 and 2026-27 the National Diagnostic Examinations for pupils in the sixth year of primary school (St' Dimotikou) and the third year of lower secondary school (G' Gymnasiou). Subsequently, the scanning of the Answer Sheets and the updating of the existing IEP database shall support data analysis in order to provide a valid and reliable diagnosis of the knowledge, attitudes and skills of pupils in the sixth year of primary school (St' Dimotikou) and the third year of lower secondary school (G' Gymnasiou) in Modern Greek Language - reading comprehension and Mathematics, in accordance with the expected learning outcomes as described in the relevant Curricula. Based on the above, for Work Packages WP1 and WP2 of Lot 1 and 2 it is not possible for a single Contractor to undertake the preparation of both the Language and Mathematics subjects with the questions and their analysis. Respectively, WP3 concerns the printing and dispatch/collection of Answer Sheets, scanning of Answer Sheets and updating of the database which correspond to different CPVs and therefore constitutes a separate Lot. The Tendering Procedure comprises three (3) lots and interested parties (prospective Contractors) under penalty of exclusion may submit a tender for only one (1) lot of the Contract. Non-compliance with the above term entails the automatic exclusion of the prospective Contractor. Specifically: Lot 1: Development of National Diagnostic Examination subjects for the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027. Lot 2: Results of National Diagnostic Examinations for the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027. Lot 3: Other supportive actions during the school years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027. sig_9ebb58bda34827bd9a74.description: The subject of the tender is the extension of software maintenance and support services for the OpenText products Identity Manager (IDM), Open Enterprise Server (OES) and ZENworks Configuration Management (ZCM) used by the contracting authority. Furthermore, the contract includes the option of calling off additional support, consultancy and assistance services in the environment of the existing OpenText environment. The contracting authority operates a centralised OpenText environment consisting of the product areas Identity Manager (IDM), Open Enterprise Server (OES) and ZENworks Configuration Management (ZCM). The systems form essential components of access management, user administration, server infrastructure as well as client and endpoint management. The subject of the tender is the provision of the required software maintenance, servicing and manufacturer support services, including the extension of the existing usage and support permissions for the deployed OpenText products over the contract term. At the time of the tender, the environment comprises in particular: - IDM environment with approx. 3.222 user objects, - OES environment with approx. 3.193 user objects, - ZCM environment with approx. 1.474 managed end devices and approx. 2.707 users. The quantities stated serve as orientation and may change during the contract term. In addition to the renewal and support services, the contracting authority is to be given the option of calling off further assistance and consultancy services on the basis of an offered daily rate as required. These include in particular error analyses, manufacturer escalations, configuration adjustments, support with updates and upgrades, technical consultancy services as well as other services in direct connection with the existing OpenText environment. The aim of the tender is to ensure the fault-free and economical operation of the existing OpenText system landscape as well as the needs-based support of the contracting authority by qualified specialist personnel throughout the entire contract term.

sig_9ebd91955b7d03791136.description: WDR intends to sell the northern part of its site in Cologne-Bocklemünd, which covers approximately 58 ha. The site extends on both sides of Freimersdorfer Weg, is partially built upon and is currently used in part by WDR and by third parties. Against the background of declining own use, the location is to be abandoned prospectively. The complete clearance of the site is expected for the period between 2028 and 2035. A sale can in principle also take place before complete clearance. The service to be awarded comprises the conception and management of the entire transaction process by an experienced advisory firm. The contractor supports WDR in the preparation, marketing, execution and monitoring of the investor selection as well as in the commercial handling of the sales process until the selection of a preferred investor. Parallel to this call for competition, consultancy for a separate expression of interest procedure is being commissioned. The expression of interest procedure is thus accompanied by a separate contractor. The results of this procedure are to be taken into account by the contractor for the transaction advisory services and incorporated into the further transaction process. The legal advice for the transaction as well as contract drafting and negotiation are carried out by separately commissioned advisors and are not the subject of this call for competition. Note: The participation brochure and the procurement documents contain in principle all information necessary for the assessment of the overall project. However, applicants who are successful in the call for competition will receive further information which, for reasons of confidentiality, is not published on the procurement platform. These concern, for example, evaluations and already completed reviews regarding the overall project.
sig_9ebd91955b7d03791136.title: Conception and management for the transaction process for the sale of the WDR site in Cologne-Bocklemünd

sig_9eda50e380f0864410e7.description: Under the Federal Act on Maritime Responsibilities (SeeAufgG), the BSH is legally obliged as part of the marine surveying service to carry out marine surveys and wreck investigations in the German Baltic and North Seas. Marine surveying is a core task of the BSH and, through the use of ship-based hydroacoustic methods, provides information on the seabed topography and underwater obstacles located on it. The collected geobasis data form the basis for the production of official nautical charts, traffic safety measures, oceanographic investigations and coastal protection. To fulfil these tasks, the BSH uses 5 survey vessels and 12 survey boats. For this purpose, the vessels are equipped with precise positioning systems, survey echosounders, sonars and other special equipment. The survey data are collected, stored and evaluated on the survey vessels and boats. A surveying software (VMS) developed within the BSH is used for data collection and processing. The VMS previously used in the BSH is to be replaced as part of this tender. For further information: See description of services See description of services
sig_9eda50e380f0864410e7.title: Replacement procurement of surveying software for the BSH vessels

sig_9eeb0e95df78e643035a.description: This is not a procurement notice or a request for tenders, but a market survey and request for information. The National ID forum (informal forum) has decided to organize a joint RFI event. The idea is to organize a single RFI involving several national agencies and ministries, which would maximize synergy benefits and be a cost-effective model. The ID Forum is a national informal cooperation forum that focuses on comprehensive identity management, its development, and creating a situational picture. The aim is to produce national services that develop capacity in identity management, coordinate training and information events, and improve the common situational awareness and ability to combat abuse. Identity is therefore at the heart of the forum and is dealt with within the remit of each member organization. The ID Forum consists of several Finnish agencies and ministries; Immigration Service (FIS), Border Guard Force (BGF), National Bureau of Investigations (NBI), National Police Board (NPB), Police departments, Customs, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). The subject of the RFI and information about the procedure are described in more detail in Appendix 1.

sig_9ef821de6ec07dbba549.description: For multimedia processing and PDF creation as well as for the creation of web-based trainings (WBT), Adobe and Articulate products are used in the administration of the Canton of Bern. The Canton intends to re-tender the licences required for three years from June 2026. The licences are tendered in two lots. The contract for the two lots will be awarded individually or as a complete package. Lot 1 comprises Adobe Government Enterprise CC and DC licences as well as Adobe Education Enterprise CC and DC licences. Lot 2 comprises Articulate 360 licences including Articulate 360 AI Assistant licences. Where there is a corresponding demand, the licences should also be able to be used by the Bernese municipalities and other entities fulfilling public tasks of the Canton of Bern, such as educational institutions, under the conditions agreed with the Canton. Adobe CC / DC Government Enterprise Licences: The subject matter of procurement comprises, on the one hand, Adobe Creative Cloud (CC) Government for Enterprise Edition 4 licences [Creative Cloud all Apps, Creative Cloud Pro Plus, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, InCopy and Dreamweaver] and Document Cloud (DC) licences [Acrobat Pro] and credits for Adobe Stock. Adobe CC / DC Education Enterprise Licences: On the other hand, the subject matter of procurement comprises Adobe Creative Cloud (CC) for Education Enterprise licences [Creative Cloud all Apps, Creative Cloud Pro Plus, Photoshop, Illustrator & InDesign] and Document Cloud (DC) licences for teams [Acrobat Pro]
sig_9ef821de6ec07dbba549.title: Procurement of Adobe and Articulate licences

sig_9ef9d42a4f1a3b086b82.description: The U.S. Embassy in Panama requires mobile and data services, including voice and text for basic phones and unlimited data service for Smart Phones and Tablets, for official domestic and international use. The anticipated performance is for a base year, with two one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. The U.S. Government intends to award a contract to the most qualified, responsible offeror representing best value using trade-off evaluation methodology. The Embassy intends to conduct a pre-quotation conference, and all prospective quoters are invited to attend. Prospective offerors should contact Aranza Gutierrez at (507) 317-5309, or by email to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov for additional information or to arrange access to the virtual meeting. Quotations are due by 3:00p.m. on Tuesday, October 13th, 2026. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Quotations must be in English and incomplete quotations will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov . It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. In order for a quotation to be considered, you must also complete and submit the following: 1. SF-1449 2. Section 1, Pricing 3. Section 5, Representations and Certifications 4. Additional information as required in Section 3 5. The Offeror shall submit a completed IRS Form W-14, found at www.irs.gov/w14, to ensure compliance with FAR 52.229-11. 6. Proof of SAM Registration. 7. CYBERSECURITY SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT (C-SCRM) C-SCRM Questionnaire and/or State Department Secure Software Development Attestation Form Direct any questions regarding this solicitation in writing to Alex Phannestiel, Contracting Officer. Questions must be written in English and may be emailed to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov or sent to fax number (507) 317-5141 no later than COB Wednesday, September 23, 2026. Notwithstanding FAR 4.203-1(b)(5)(ii), the Contracting Officer has determined that it is in the best interest of the U.S. Government that offerors be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) database at https://www.sam.gov at the time of submitting a proposal.

sig_9efdf9e2d4b0b7e6e550.description: As Environmental Advice Coordinator for Environmental Permits, you will coordinate environmental advice for environmental permits for construction and development activities. You will ensure that applications are assessed in a timely and careful manner and that the various environmental aspects are integrally included in the final advice. In this assignment, you will work under the direction and supervision of the team leader. Permit issuers from the participating municipalities ask the ODU to test applications for environmental permits against the applicable laws and regulations on various environmental themes. In your role, you will ensure an integral assessment of these applications within the organisation. You will assess which environmental themes are relevant, issue requests for advice to the appropriate subject matter experts within the ODU, and monitor progress. You will then bundle the received advice into a clear and usable final advice for the municipal permit issuer. In doing so, you will actively coordinate with municipalities, internal specialists, and other stakeholders. You will work independently in the PowerBrowser case system, monitor statutory deadlines, and ensure complete and traceable file formation. Because you will be handling multiple applications at the same time, it is important that you set priorities, meet agreements, and signal in a timely manner when additional information or coordination is needed. The position is for an average of 24 hours per week. The work is demand-driven and requires flexible deployment. A temporary extension is possible.
sig_9efdf9e2d4b0b7e6e550.title: Environmental Advice Coordinator for Environmental Permits (flexible for an average of 24 hours per week)

sig_9f00dd95fcc7b6df24df.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL ANNOUCEMENT DETAILS.

If you are admitted, you will receive specific assignments within your selected categories during the term of the DPS. If you are rejected, you can withdraw, adjust and resubmit your registration. You can find the DPS via www.NJihuurtin.nl. For more information about KBL you can look at www.KBL.nl and for more information about NJi you can look at www.nji.nl. The number of requests via the DPS cannot be foreseen in advance. The DPS is primarily intended for the hiring of flexible staff for the Quality and Continuous Learning Network Organisation. By this we mean the categories as described in this announcement. For other flexible hiring for other initiatives housed at the Netherlands Youth Institute, the DPS is not currently being used. This may change in the future. NJi has included the categories below for this DPS. For the time being, these categories are described for external hiring at the Quality and Continuous Learning network. During the term, this can be expanded to broader hiring for the NJi. The example functions mentioned only serve as an indication to show the scope of the category and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of which assignments will be placed in the category. Category 1: Content This includes all hiring of external staff and organisations focused on working towards the substantive objectives. Example functions: - Learning coach - Content expert - Programme leader - Project employee - Project coordinator - Process supervisor - Advisor - Researcher Example organisations - Consultancy firms - Research agency Category 2: Network/community This includes all hiring of external staff and organisations focused on development, construction and support. Example functions: - Network director - Network supporter - Community manager Example organisations: - ICT organisation (regarding e.g. CRM systems / platform) - Consultancy firms - Research agency Category 3: Marketing & communication This includes all hiring of external staff and organisations focused on the (further) development and support of internal and external communication. Example functions: - Copywriter - Designer - Illustrator - Communications employee - Communications advisor - Support with organising events Example organisations: - Design agency - Event agency The number of requests via the DPS cannot be foreseen in advance. The DPS is primarily intended for the hiring of flexible staff for the Quality and Continuous Learning Network Organisation. By this we mean the categories as described above. For other flexible hiring for other initiatives housed at the Netherlands Youth Institute, the DPS is not currently being used. This may change in the future. sig_9f256e95ecb472f792e8.description: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration would like to carry out a market survey to map which tenderers offer systems for financial management in road projects. There is a need for IT system support for areas such as cost estimation, financial project management and follow-up, uncertainty management and price bank (experience prices used for estimating future projects). The objective of the survey is to gain better insight into what systems are available in the market, how these are technically and functionally designed and which delivery models are offered. It is particularly interesting to examine if there are systems that support several or all of the above mentioned areas in one and the same system. Furthermore, we would like information on whether systems that only cover one or some of the areas can be further developed or configured so that several of the areas can be delivered in one system that safeguards all or most of the value chain. The market survey shall form the basis for any new procurement, and contribute to the Norwegian Public Roads Administration designing a competition that is well adapted to the market and at the same time cover the identified needs in an efficient and future-oriented manner.
sig_9f256e95ecb472f792e8.title: System for cost estimation, financial management and uncertainty management in road projects.

sig_9f4a51a8f3aaa59ae60c.description: Verohallinto requests, with this information request, solution alternatives for a centralised communication system for companies' financial data from companies operating in the market. The content of the information request is described in more detail in the appendix "Report on the reform needs of official reporting by companies and organisations" and in appendix 4 "Solution description for centralised communication". We kindly ask for replies to the questions in appendix 3 of the information request. The aim of the information request is to obtain comprehensive information on solution alternatives and their costs so that a possible procurement can be implemented as appropriately and cost-effectively as possible. To be implemented, the reform requires legislative amendments. Verohallinto organised a public consultation round on the planned solution in February–March 2026. The impacts of the consultation feedback have not yet been taken into account in the solution description and they may substantially alter the solution. The consultation request regarding the report, which was open for comments in early 2026 (lausuntopalvelu.fi) https://www.lausuntopalvelu.fi/FI/Proposal/Participation?proposalId=2f30da4a-df3d-472c-9f0d-63536116bb5a. This document is not a call for tenders but a market consultation, i.e. an information request. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement. Decisions on initiating a possible procurement process will be made later. Answering or failing to answer the information request does not affect participation in a possible tendering procedure. Verohallinto does not pay compensation to suppliers that have replied to the information request.
sig_9f4a51a8f3aaa59ae60c.title: Information request: Procurement of a centralised communication system for companies' financial data

sig_9f6d7d315132b12b38eb.description: The Tourismus Marketing GmbH Baden-Württemberg (TMBW) is tendering for the development and implementation of a nationwide, modular dashboard solution for the central consolidation, processing and visualisation of tourism indicators from various data sources. TMBW expects the design, development, implementation and commissioning of a productively usable software solution. The subject of the tendered service is the design, development, implementation and commissioning of a productively usable software solution. This service component, referred to as the base model, comprises both the technical and visual implementation of a core set of indicators and metrics as well as the agile design and iterative further development of innovative evaluation and presentation forms carried out jointly with the client. This agile approach is to be understood as an integral part of the basic service. The dashboard subject to the contract must be modular in design. Upon award of the contract, TMBW will initially commission the development of a basic version for central tourism indicators. This basic version must already be fully operational. It is also the basis for subsequent expansions (further data sources, analysis functions and, prospectively, AI applications), the development of which is an optional subject of the tendered service. Hosting and operation of the software solution, software maintenance and data entry are also subjects of the tender as services for the duration of the NZT project funding until 31 December 2028. The software solution must be configured in such a way that it can also be supported and further developed by another service provider after the project funding expires on 31 December 2028. Following completion and acceptance of the stable base model, further qualitative or functional expansion stages can be implemented on its basis as optional extension services. The tendered contract shall come into effect upon the award of the contract. This is scheduled for spring 2027. The provision of services shall commence immediately after the award of the contract in accordance with the contractual specifications. Commissioning of the basic version of the dashboard is to be completed by autumn 2027.
sig_9f6d7d315132b12b38eb.title: Tourismus Marketing GmbH Baden-Württemberg - Contract award for the development and implementation of a tourism dashboard for Baden-Württemberg

sig_9f771e609eb8b71cf361.description: Broad Horizons Education Trust is currently exploring options for the future provision of its payroll services commencing in September 2027.
