The purpose of this Request for Information is to engage with potential suppliers prior to any formal procurement to: Inform our procurement strategy, scope, and specification. 1. The subject of the contract is the delivery, installation and maintenance of a Passenger Counting System for 284 vehicles of ZTM Operators. The contract has been divided into two tasks. The first task – delivery, installation and maintenance of a Passenger Counting System for 181 buses of ZTM Operators. The task involves retrofitting 23 BN-type buses and 23 CN-type buses of PKM Gliwice Sp. z o.o., 90 BN-type buses and 45 CN-type buses of PKM Katowice Sp. z o.o., manufactured no earlier than in 2014, providing transport services commissioned by ZTM Katowice, with 611 sensors and 181 central units, switches, GSM communication modules/at least 4G in LTE standard or newer, GPS locators and an appropriate number of batteries. The task has been divided into three parts. The first part includes implementation: a) Delivery, installation and commissioning of equipment in buses together with the necessary accessories and cabling, as well as software for this equipment, b) Obtaining a certificate from the GZM PCS contractor (specified in the integration agreement together with appendices) for the solution supplied to the buses (if the Contractor does not possess such for the supplied solution), c) Integration of the supplied equipment with the central software of the GZM Passenger Counting System (GZM PCS) regarding the transmitted data in accordance with the requirements of the Description of the Subject of the Contract, d) Preparation and delivery of as-built documentation, e) Ensuring correct operation during the implementation period on the terms specified in the second part. The second part includes maintenance of the “Vehicle PCS”: a) Warranty and service of the System, b) In the case of an indirect server-to-server connection, maintenance and service of the intermediary server and APN connectivity and VPN tunnel supplied by the Contractor, including the possibility for the Contracting Authority and persons indicated by it from ZTM and Operators to report faults for the aforementioned elements 24 hours a day / for 7 days a week / 365 days a year, c) In the case of an indirect server-to-server connection, carrying out the activities included in the Exit Procedure, intended to ensure the Contracting Authority the continued operation of the solution after the end of the contract with the Contractor, in particular the assignment to the Contracting Authority of the contract for a dedicated APN network held by the Contractor, as well as the commissioning of the intermediary server solution at the location indicated by the Contracting Authority, together with the transfer of licenses enabling the use of the software installed by the Contractor. The Contractor guarantees the correct operation of the solution for the duration of the warranty contract; d) Termination of the Contract, sending all data regarding the intermediary server to GZM cloud resources, so that the functionality of the applied solution is maintained. The third part includes the right of option: an order under the right of option, which includes the possibility of extending the maintenance period in full or limited scope for a period not exceeding 5 years. The third part will be implemented according to the contractual provisions as for the second part. The initiative aims to increase access to facilities within the Scottish space sector by identifying relevant, commercially available, non-space-specific infrastructure and capabilities in adjacent sectors. This will help create clearer pathways between Scottish space companies and facilities that already exist across sectors including energy, manufacturing, maritime, automotive, defence, advanced materials, electronics and other relevant industries. The work will build on existing infrastructure mapping and recommendations and establish a consistent methodology for identifying, assessing and engaging relevant facilities and facility operators. The appointed contractor will work closely with the Space Scotland team, the Infrastructure and Facilities Working Group and relevant stakeholders. What We Need - Experience of conducting infrastructure, capability or market intelligence exercises, particularly across multiple sectors. - Experience identifying and assessing technical facilities, equipment or capabilities against defined requirements. - Demonstrable understanding of relevant Scottish industrial and innovation ecosystems. - Experience engaging with industry clusters, facility operators, universities, research organisations, innovation centres and/or public-sector organisations. Existing relationships would be advantageous. - Ability to translate technical information into clear, structured and actionable outputs. - Knowledge of the Scottish space sector and its infrastructure requirements. Scope of Work Facility Assessment Criteria The contractor will develop a framework to assess relevant facilities and equipment, identify and prioritise adjacent sectors with relevant capabilities, and create an initial capability database with standardised information requirements to support future stakeholder engagement and expansion of the Space Scotland facilities database. Engage Priority Adjacent Sectors Undertake structured engagement with the sectors identified, using the developed standardised information requirements. Engagement will focus on the prioritised facilities and equipment that could support Scottish space-sector activities and understanding how companies can realistically access them. Expand the Space Scotland Facilities Database Relevant and validated facilities should be collated in a spreadsheet, with appropriate formatting and sector tags, so that it can be easily integrated with the existing database. Some small promotional resources, such as case studies or quotes inviting the space sector to utilise these selected facilities, should be created too. Budget The budget available for this commission is 30,000 GBP excluding VAT. Proposal Requirements Submissions should be limited to 6 pages. Submissions should include: - Company/contractor overview. - Relevant sector experience and case studies, including experience of space, infrastructure, facilities, manufacturing, technology or cross-sector engagement. - Proposed approach to delivering the scope of work, including a risk register. - Proposed deliverables and timetable. - Key personnel who would undertake the work and their relevant experience. - Fee breakdown demonstrating delivery within the 30,000 GBP budget. - Details of any relevant conflicts of interest. Evaluation Proposals will be assessed on: - Understanding and requirements of the brief. - Alignment with the qualities listed in the “What We Need from a Contractor” section. - Strength of the proposed approach to the scope of work. - Relevant experience and capability of the proposed team. - Value for money within the available budget. - Ability to deliver the work within the required timeframe. Submission Applications should be submitted to admin@spacescotland.org by 10AM 21 October 2026. Please include “Cross-Sector Facilities Access Initiative – ITT” in the subject line.

sig_a058f7fc2ffb0620a563.description: In spring 2023 the Government and QA launched a joint strategy for digital competence and infrastructure in nurseries and schools (2023-2030)[1] (hereafter; The strategy). The strategy points out that there is a need for more research and knowledge on how digital solutions are used in kindergarten and school and what educational value they provide. There is also a need for knowledge on employees ́ competence and sharing of digital practices. One of the initiatives in the strategy is "to establish a target orthopaedal research programme on the subject of and on digitalisation and digital competence in the sector". The strategy conveys a desire for the research programme to provide better and more systematic knowledge of good, reliable and appropriate use of digital systems and media in schools. One of the initiatives in the strategy is to develop research based knowledge on appropriate development of teaching and assessment practices in light of the changes that generative artificial intelligence (GenKI) brings about the education system. The assignment of establishing the research programme was given to Udir from KD in spring 2024. The research programme for digitalisation and digital competence in nurseries and schools was initiated autumn 2024.

sig_a05a3503e77e37addd6d.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to support the continued operation and expansion of the Exceptional Longevity Data Management and Coordinating Center (EL DMCC) through a single U24 cooperative agreement award. The NOFO will be open to all eligible applicants. Established in 2022, the EL DMCC serves as the central hub for NIA’s human longevity translational research portfolio, integrating data and activities across studies to maximize the value of deeply phenotyped cohorts and associated genomic and multi-omics datasets. The DMCC currently plays a critical role in enabling cross-cohort analyses, coordinating collaborative research, and advancing shared data resources. Core functions include data harmonization and integration; development and implementation of common data standards; provision of statistical, computational, and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) infrastructure and tools; coordination of cross-project collaborations; and managing shared data systems, including data storage, access, and platform operations. The DMCC also develops and maintains the ELITE (Exceptional Longevity Translational Resources) Portal, which provides secure access to harmonized datasets, analytical tools, and cloud-based computational workspaces. The DMCC supports controlled access to EL data and use of these resources by the research community and maintains ongoing efforts to ensure the Portal is interoperable with the NIA Alzheimer’s Disease Knowledge Portal and other data resources of the National Institutes of Health, consistent with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles. Through the NOFO, the Coordinating Center will be expected to build on and expand these core functions by: Enhancing integration of increasingly large and diverse datasets across cohorts and species Expanding statistical, computational, and AI/ML capabilities and associated infrastructure Developing and refining methods and standards for multi-omics data harmonization and integrative analyses Coordinating and supporting collaborative research across NIA-funded projects Developing and disseminating translational resources, including target nomination and prioritization resources, curated target knowledgebases, and inventories of candidate therapeutic targets Advancing the ELITE Portal, including improvements in data organization, search, visualization, interoperability, and cloud-based analytical environments Strengthening community engagement through training, workshops, and collaborative activities Applications are not being solicited at this time. This Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_a05a3503e77e37addd6d.title: Continuation of the Exceptional Longevity Data Management and Coordinating Center (EL DMCC) (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_a0600d2a401fca39874c.description: The Urban Solidarity and Renewal Act of 13 December 2000 created beach management plans (SAP) " in order to reduce the consequences on a beach and the natural areas close to it of nuisances or degradation linked to the presence of equipment or constructions carried out before 5 January 1986 ". In this sense, the Act provides " that in order to improve conditions of access to the public maritime domain, the management scheme may, by way of derogation, authorise the maintenance or reconstruction of part of the existing equipment or constructions within the coastal strip defined in Article L. 121-16, provided that these are such as to make it possible to reconcile the objectives of environmental preservation and the organisation of tourist visitor numbers ". From the end of the 1970s, the Municipality of Vendres stated its desire to develop the coastal strip in a lightweight manner, while also wishing to potentially draw revenue from the beach concession. Aerial photographs from 1980/1982 show the presence of constructions on the beaches. Since then, the Municipality of VENDRES has benefited from a beach concession awarded from 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2022, extended annually. Almost all of the 8 lots are located in a remarkable and characteristic coastal area, yet, in the absence of a beach management plan, beach concessions should no longer exist. Therefore, the mission relates to the drafting of the municipality's beach management plan, up to its approval by decree in the Council of State. This drafting will cover, geographically, the entirety of the perimeter defined in the pre-operational studies (which users are strongly advised to download from the CEREMA documentary portal) in order to measure the effects of the provisions of the beach management plan. The services shall be of three types: - The drafting as such of the beach management plan, including missions relating to consultation (mandatory and optional) and communication. This service will organise times for discussion with the legal assistance and the environmental assessment. - The strategic environmental assessment, which will be carried out in an iterative manner, - Legal support. The three lots relate to the entire procedure for drafting the management scheme, up to the approval of the document by the Council of State. Subsequent stages (any appeals against the document) do not form part of it. This mission aims to coordinate the study with the service providers for lots 2 and 3. It is also responsible for drafting the entire dossier for the proposed beach management scheme by incorporating the documents produced by the other service providers (in particular lot 3). It will more specifically be responsible for drafting the documents of the beach management plan, namely: - Presentation report - Operational perimeter of the Beach Management Scheme - Master plan of equipment, constructions and installations to be removed as part of the implementation of the Beach Management Scheme - Regulatory zoning and perimeter of the beach concessions - Book of architectural and landscape recommendations with regulatory value. Finally, it will run the consultation process, which will take the form of public meetings or workshops offered to the entire municipal population, aimed at regularly presenting the progress of the procedure and gathering opinions. Lot 1 is an ordinary contract.; This advisory and expert mission aims to limit the risks of appeals against the approved beach management plan document, both regarding the procedure and the substance or form of the document. It is therefore equally a matter of: - Auditing the procedure initiated and advising the municipality on conducting the rest of the procedure, with regard in particular to the provisions of the Town Planning Code, the Environmental Code and the General Code of Territorial Collectivities; - Assisting the service provider of Lot 1 in drafting the beach management plan dossier, in particular to avoid any inadequacy in the various documents that comprise it; - Advising and assisting the municipality on how to manage any subsequent appeals; - Providing the contracting authority with monitoring and a legal reading of texts relating to the subject and procedure of the beach management plan. Lots 2 and 3 are mixed contracts comprising a lump sum and unit prices for additional services.; The mission comprises several main types of services: - Proposal and implementation of a robust methodological approach aimed at successfully carrying out the environmental assessment process (including the drafting of an initial state of the environment) for the drafting of the beach management plan; - Identification, description and evaluation of the likely effects of the beach management plan on the environment. Pursuant to Article L. 122-6 of the Environmental Code, the service provider will endeavour to exploit the various available sources, in particular by analysing and making use of the results of existing studies that may be provided to it. The service provider will also work, in consultation with the contracting authority, to integrate the elements (vigilances, recommendations, etc.) that the environmental authority might raise through a possible scoping note. - Drafting of the complete environmental assessment report. This report must be a decision-support document, based on available environmental data and documents. It will cover all environmental themes. - Contribution to the written submission in response to the environmental authority, following the opinion that the latter may have formulated after the finalisation of the beach management plan. Lots 2 and 3 are mixed contracts comprising a lump sum and unit prices for additional services.
sig_a0600d2a401fca39874c.title: Drawing up a Beach Management Scheme pursuant to Article L121-28 of the Town Planning Code

sig_a07fce4b15f695ee3f33.description: Renovation of the Saidenbach Dam pressure pipeline system Lot LOT-0001: Earthworks and pipe laying, road construction, replacement of pump stations, sewer rehabilitation. Lot 1: Site installation, construct, relocate and operate 5.700 m of provisional wastewater pressure pipeline in 3 sections 49.200 m2 terrain clearance 18.000 m2 construct and dismantle site access roads 42 pcs. fell trees, grub tree stumps 25 pcs. trim clearance profile on trees, site traffic safety Lot 2: PEHD PE100 RC pipelines, SDR 11, laying in single trench alongside existing old trench, pipe cover 1,50 m - 2,00 m, trench-parallel renewal of existing pressure pipelines DN 150 – DN 250 ductile cast iron (GGG) Section A: 2.750 m 160 x 14,6, connection using electrofusion sockets Section B: 2.900 m 180 x 16,4, connection using electrofusion sockets Section C: 490 m 315 x 28,6, connection using electrofusion sockets Section C: 1.700 m 280 x 25,4, connection using electrofusion sockets 27 inspection and valve chambers of the pressure pipeline 8 water body crossings Section D1: 500 m gravity sewer PEHD, SN 16, SDR 17, welded pipes DN315, 10 chamber structures PEHD replace existing gravity pipeline along the same route 7.830 m emptying and pigging of old pipelines DN 150 – 250 ductile cast iron (GGG) 1.000 m removal and disposal of old pipelines DN 150 – 250 ductile cast iron (GGG) 500 m removal and disposal of old pipeline DN 400 reinforced concrete (StB) 14.600 m3 soil excavation, disposal of displaced excavated material, soil BM-0, BM-F0*, BM-F1, DK I, DKIII Lot 3: Conversion of pump stations, replacement new build of the pump stations in Haselbach and Niedersaida including piping, valves and electrical installation. At the Lippersdorf pump station, the scope of services is limited to individual conversion and adaptation measures. The concrete structures of the pump stations can remain unchanged. Due to the high delivery heads in Haselbach and Niedersaida, two pumps are connected in series to double the delivery head. The wastewater pump stations are designed to be fully redundant; both pump lines can convey the full discharge. Haselbach pump station: Q = 35,4 m3/h; H = 37 m Niedersaida pump station: Q = 31,4 m3/h; H = 36 m The Haselbach and Lippersdorf pump stations are each equipped with a chemical dosing station for dosing a calcium nitrate solution. The dosing stations are set up outside the pump station buildings in mobile hazardous material containers and serve to suppress H2S formation in the downstream sewer network up to the sewage treatment plant and to prevent corrosion damage. For the Niedersaida pump station, initially only the connection for a possible later retrofitting of chemical dosing is planned. The subject matter of the process automation includes in particular the renewal and adaptation of the control, measurement and telecontrol technology at the pump station locations Haselbach, Niedersaida and Lippersdorf, as well as the control technology integration via radio of the locations Haselbach, Niedersaida, Lippersdorf and Forchheim into the process control system of the Wünschendorf sewage treatment plant. The coarse quantities provided for are: extensive renewal of process automation incl. control cabinets for pump technology in two pump stations, supplementary adaptations in another pump station, control technology connection of a total of four pump station locations, renewal or supplementation of level, flow and overflow sensors, replacement of three CSO evaluation units as well as connection of chemical dosing systems and electrically driven valves. The scope of services also includes workshop and assembly planning, software creation, system integration, testing, commissioning, training and as-built documentation. The control systems are to be implemented manufacturer-independently on the basis of an open standard (preferably Profinet). For remote transmission, VPN, Ethernet and MQTT as well as the project-specific interfaces to the process control system must be taken into account. Lot 4: Sewer rehabilitation Section D2: 1.100 m trenchless pipe lining (CIPP) foul wastewater sewer DN 300 – DN 500 Chamber rehabilitation Wastewater diversion for rehabilitation work

sig_a0997e3b53056022777e.description: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ in support of Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Division is soliciting white papers/proposals for research and development support in technologies that are applicable to the following: air platforms, manned and unmanned payloads, advanced computing and processing, air platform support systems, advanced air system security and protection, and improved Naval air capabilities. Example focus areas include improved technologies, techniques or advanced applications of communications, Electro-Optical (EO), Infrared (IR), Radio Frequency (RF), acoustic and non-acoustic sensors, persistent surveillance technologies, and special sensor systems for Navy manned aircraft and Unmanned Air Systems (UAS). The NAWCAD WOLF ASI Division develops advanced air platforms, sensors (e.g., acoustics, EO/IR, radar, magnetics, and other special sensors), and systems to meet current and future Naval capability demands. The purpose of these platforms, sensors and systems is to support a variety of aviation missions including distributed maritime surveillance, Air Undersea Warfare (USW), airborne strike, air warfare, counter-air, close air support and interdiction, defense suppression, advanced communications, digital interoperability, electronic attack, naval warfare and amphibious strike, Counter Unmanned Systems (C-UxS), anti-surface warfare, and contested logistic support. Most of the air platforms will be small Group 1 to Group 4 UAS or modifications to existing larger manned and unmanned air platforms. Sensors could be air deployed (via manned or unmanned aircraft), ground, surface, or undersea deployable as driven by the mission needs. Advanced computing and processing will be focused on air vehicle, payload, edge computing, artificial intelligence and machine learning, or multi-platform collaborative solutions supporting all aspects of mission information from pre-deployment, through operations, to post deployment and sustainment. Advanced air system security and protection will be focused on securing information, transmissions, anti-tampering, and reduced probability of compromise of existing technologies or technologies in development. Improved naval capabilities will focus on key naval focus areas or capability gaps supporting improved lethality, availability, and affordability. This BAA not only includes air vehicle systems, mission systems, sensors, sensor data processing, and sensor systems, but it also includes mathematical modeling of the sensors and air platforms, communication techniques between the sensors and/or platforms, interfaces, software development, the fusion and exploitation of multi-sensor data, studies, artificial intelligence, deep learning, machine learning, advanced algorithms, and other techniques used to develop advanced capabilities and reduce the cost of transitioning sensors technologies to the fleet. Furthermore, this BAA shall cover development and analysis of related air, sea, and land detection models using relevant data.
sig_a0997e3b53056022777e.title: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Division

sig_a09d818daccb5737fb61.description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This is a notice of intent to solicit, negotiate and award a sole source contract under statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Naval Surface Warfare Center Port Hueneme Division intends to award a sole source contract to General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc. (GDMS) (CAGE 3CX85) for in-service engineering and lifecycle support of Command, Control, Computers, Communications, Combat Systems, and Intelligence (C5I) system elements of the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) equipment specific to the Independence (INDY) variant. Services include engineering; design; integration; test and evaluation; software development, testing, and load; system upgrade/replacement planning onboard and at sites; logistics product development and distribution; configuration management of the systems and logistics products; as well as training systems. Market research indicates that GDMS, as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the LCS INDY variant combat system, is the only source capable of satisfying the agency requirements. A Sources Sought Notice (N6339426R0TBD) was published to SAM.gov on 24 October 2025 to identify potential sources. The Government reviewed capability statements from 10 respondents and determined that GDMS is the only source capable of satisfying the agency requirements for this follow-on acquisition without unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of cost that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Transitioning this work to a non-OEM source without access to GDMS' proprietary design data, is estimated to result in duplicate costs of at least $26M-$34M and create an immediate, minimum five-year gap in critical engineering support. This is based on the need for a non-OEM source to design, construct, equip, and certify specialized testing and integration facilities to replicate the LCS INDY variant's unique computing environment; recruit, clear, and train a specialized nationwide workforce, and negotiate new subcontracts for proprietary OEM materials; reverse-engineer proprietary software interfaces and C5I integration nodes to perform the required lifecycle engineering; and complete rigorous land-based testing, at-sea trials, and formal Navy combat system safety certification necessary to obtain a Navy Authority to Operate. sig_a0cbd6a6a871201bd3bb.description: The gemeente Lingewaard uses GBI World from Antea Group for the management of public space. This management system supports the municipality in the preparation, planning, execution and accountability of management and maintenance activities within the public space. The gemeente Lingewaard intends to continue the contract for GBI World. This choice is based on content-related, organisational and economic considerations. Market information and practical experience show that Antea Group's solution stands out due to proven technology, broad comprehensive functionality for public space management and a stable SaaS environment that demonstrably meets the current and future needs of the municipality. In addition, Lingewaard is currently involved in several extensive change and development processes, including the further improvement of data quality, the implementation of IMBOR and GWSW, the further development of asset management and various optimisations within public space management. A procurement and migration process would currently compete with these ongoing developments, creating significant risks for the continuity of service provision, the progress of strategic tasks and available execution capacity. At the same time, in recent years the municipality has invested substantially in the setup, linkages, data quality, processes and knowledge building surrounding GBI World. A transition to an alternative solution would lead to significant divestment of public funds and place a long-term drain on scarce expertise and capacity. The municipality therefore does not consider it expedient to initiate a procurement process at this time that could lead to the loss of investments already realised, additional implementation costs and delays to ongoing improvement processes. Based on these circumstances, the municipality is of the opinion that continuation of the current solution is currently the most justifiable choice from the point of view of continuity, expediency, risk control and careful management of public funds. This assessment and the underlying reasoning are further explained in the supplier document. Intended decision • The municipality intends to conclude a contract with the current supplier for an indefinite period. • The estimated value of the contract amounts to € 200.000,- (excl. VAT). Attention! This notice is used solely to make the intended choice of procedure known in advance to the market in order to give interested parties the opportunity to express any objections. If interested parties, despite the attached justification, wish to lodge an objection to the aforementioned intention, they must submit a reasoned objection to the continuation of this procedure within a period of 20 calendar days after publication of this notice. For this purpose, you can use the e-mail address as stated in the contact details. The gemeente Lingewaard will take any objection into account in its assessment. If no objection has been made known during this period, the rights of undertakings to still oppose the intended procedure shall lapse. Appeal procedure: Precise indication of the time limit(s) for appeal procedures: 20 days

sig_a0f5854749b0abbdde6a.description: It is the intention of Aster Group (also known as ‘Aster Sales’) to establish a framework agreement with suitably qualified specialist external agencies to help us deliver our shared ownership sales & marketing strategy with support on creative development, digital marketing and marketing automation delivery services to meet needs that cannot be met in-house by its own provision, or where additional knowledge and expertise is required. The appointed agency (s) will lead on strategic creative direction and planning, campaign development, cross-platform asset creation, content optimisation and performance analysis. The requirement IS split into four lots: • Lot 1 – Digital marketing support • Lot 2 – Creative support • Lot 3 – Artworking • Lot 4 - Development marketing automation delivery Suppliers will be able to submit a response for either one or more lots. Lot 1: Digital Marketing Support. As part of the launch of our new housing developments across the UK we require digital marketing support to drive awareness, generate leads, and support occupancy targets. The aim is to drive qualified traffic and leads through digital channels and the Aster sales website, optimising for awareness, engagement and conversions across our shared ownership pages and developments pages. This lot focuses on performance-driven digital channels and content creation to reach prospective residents effectively. Successful Supplier(s) will support Aster with: •Paid Search (PPC) strategy, setup, and optimisation across platforms including Google Ads and Bing. •SEO and GEO audits, covering both on-page and off-page optimisation, including: •Creation of traffic and ranking reports across major search engines. •Content strategy and creation, including blogs, landing pages, and guides. •Paid social media advertising across Meta, TikTok, and LinkedIn. •Programmatic display and retargeting campaigns. •YouTube and video ad campaigns. •Localised SEO to improve visibility for specific developments. •Influencer and micro-influencer outreach. •Monthly performance reporting and insights. •Recommendations for emerging platforms and support with implementation. •Recommendations for AI integration within our processes and help with implementation. Lot 2: Creative Support. As part of showcasing our existing stock and the launch of our new housing developments across the UK through a mix of affordable rent, shared ownership, and outright sale, our intention is appoint a supplier to support this, our inhouse creative services team to develop and deliver a compelling visual identity and campaign assets that resonate with our target audiences and reflect our brand values. The aim is to develop compelling, engaging and bold creative that resonates with our different target audiences and supports the full marketing funnel, from awareness to conversion, while also enhancing brand presence through events and community engagement. Successful Supplier(s) will collaborate with Aster on the following: •Concept development and delivery for new marketing campaigns. •Creative direction and execution, including static, video, and motion assets. •Print production for marketing materials. •Brand storytelling and tone of voice development. •Creative design for digital, brochures, print, out-of-home (OOH), hoardings, signage, and social media platforms. •Video production and editing, including shared owner stories, virtual tours, and lifestyle content. •Interactive content creation, such as quizzes, affordability tools, and calculators. •Creative tailored for emerging platforms, including TikTok and Snapchat. •Support with brand refresh or evolution, specifically for shared ownership. •Recommendations for A/B testing and creative optimisation. •Insights into audience engagement and creative performance. •Recommendations for relevant events, awards, and community engagement opportunities. Lot 3: Artworking. To support development of creative assets for the launch of new developments and existing stock, Aster will require artworking support to adapt, resize, and amend existing creative assets and materials for use across multiple channels and formats, ensuring consistency and speed to market. This lot focuses on efficient, accurate delivery of artwork based on approved creative concepts. The intention is to appoint a supplier to support us with: •Amending and resizing existing creative assets for various formats and platforms. •Creating editable templates for internal use (e.g. Canva). •Supplying final artwork files in required formats for print and digital use. •Ensuring accessibility compliance, including alt text, font contrast, and readability. •Dynamic creative optimisation (DCO) for digital advertising. •Versioning of creative assets tailored to different developments, audiences, and platforms. Lot 4: Development sales & marketing automation delivery. To support the launch and sales process of our new housing developments and existing stock in specific locations across UK, we require marketing automation services to deliver timely, personalised communications throughout the customer journey from enquiry to reservation and completion, using marketing automation tools or via our current CRM system. This includes lead nurturing, application updates, and post-sale engagement using automated workflows and CRM integration. Successful Supplier(s) will support Aster with: •Customer journey reviews and mapping to identify opportunities for improvement and optimisation. •Email campaign creation tailored for different platforms and audience segments. •Personalised content delivery based on user behaviour and preferences. •Lead segmentation to improve targeting and conversion. •Monthly reporting on engagement and conversion metrics to inform future strategy.

sig_a12c578abb3060ae967d.description: The User requires a capability to plan, conduct, and review Dismounted Close Combat (DCC) live-fire tactical training (LFTT) activities at ranges across UK and overseas. The system must enable the creation, submission, authorisation, and secure retention of compliant digital traces, in accordance with Defence Safety Authority (DSA) Regulations 1 and Live Fire Policy 2. It must provide enhanced situational awareness for range safety staff. The system must support After-Action Review (AAR) by integrating historical activity data and allow access via Defence Gateway on both MOD and civilian devices. Live field firing represents the apex of operational preparation for land forces yet carries persistently high risks of dangerous occurrences and fratricide. Current manual live fire range design and exercise control methods are antiquated and inefficient; they do not optimise Defence Training Estate (DTE) usage or force generation opportunities. They are prone to human error, incapable of genuinely supporting the execution and review phases of training and cannot integrate with complementary technologies or digital modernisation capabilities. Safety incidents and fatalities on ranges are attributed to a combination of causal, contributory and other factors, often stemming from human error, procedural efficiencies, and limitations in equipment and training. The 17 live fire training deaths of UK military personnel and subsequent investigations from Jan 2000 to Mar 2023 are an illustration of these failings. Modernising range planning and management will enhance the UK's training, improve coherence and deconfliction while maximising DTE usage, improving safety and reducing the risk of the Armed Forces preparing for operations. A software package will apply digital parameters and technology-enabled safety interventions throughout the planning, management, execution and after-action review (AAR) phases of training. It will enable the dynamic management of the Defence range estate to maximise throughput and save lost training time and resources. Modernised range planning, management and conduct will aid in reducing the risk resulting from the Army's key risk to life activity, without the value of the training suffering. The capability will not replace, but support the already inherently Safe Persons, Safe Equipment, Safe Place and Safe Practice as detailed in live-fire SSoW policy. RSPM seeks to provide: An efficient range planning and management process: The legacy reversionary methods of planning DCC live-fire activity, whilst considered safe, can be made more efficient. Situational awareness and enhancing safety of live-fire activity: Incidents and fatalities have occurred during live-fire activity for multiple reasons, often compounding. Situational awareness of range safety staff has been cited as a Contributory Factor, especially at night. Quantification of lethality: The imperative for the DCC operative is to become more lethal and this begins with the fundamentals of marksmanship training. The aim of live-fire training is to provide a realistic tactical setting to train firers and team leaders in the skills and procedures necessary for operations. This can be shortened into the adage ‘Train how we fight’. To garner the most benefit from any live-fire exercise there needs to be feedback, formal and informal to those involved with all stages of the training. Defence Equipment and Support (DE&S) as part of the MOD, reserves the right and has no obligation to continue with the requirement following Preliminary Market Engagement (PME), and if potential suppliers choose to act on any information received during PME, it is entirely at their own risk. Lot 1: .

sig_a1601ba3832f0d5f4a9b.description: The Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) is a municipal transport company wholly (100%) owned by the City of Göttingen. It operates local public passenger transport in the city of Göttingen and adjacent regions, and uses its bus fleet to ensure the daily mobility of residents and guests. As a sector contracting entity within the meaning of Section 100 of the German Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), GöVB is responsible for procuring services and systems that secure the operation and further development of public transport. GöVB pursues the objective of gradually converting its bus fleet to alternative drives, in particular electric drives. In doing so, it makes a substantial contribution to sustainable mobility, the reduction of emissions and the achievement of the City of Göttingen's climate targets. The expansion of the e-bus fleet is accompanied by a considerable need for modern charging infrastructure that enables efficient, reliable and economical operational management. To support this transformation, GöVB is planning to introduce a charging, load and energy management system. This system is intended to enable intelligent control and monitoring of all charging processes at the depot and, from a medium-term perspective, also in scheduled line operations. The focus is on guaranteeing vehicle availability, grid and load optimisation, and the safe and economical operation of electric mobility in Göttingen's public transport. The aim is the demand-driven, secure and energy-efficient control of all charging and load processes, taking into account existing grid connections and operational requirements. The system must be able to map both short-term requirements (e.g. duty-roster relevance of individual vehicles) and medium- to long-term aspects (e.g. peak load management, integration with energy suppliers). The procedure was preceded by an EU-wide preliminary market consultation. The publication number of the notice was 628238-2025, OJ S - issue number: 184/2025, date of publication: 25/09/2025. Eight companies participated in the preliminary market consultation. The subject matter of the contract is the procurement of an integrated charging, load and energy management system (CLEMS) as Software as a Service (SaaS), including the managed cloud services required for this, operated by a managed service provider. The contractor shall assume full 24x7 operation of the overall system, including ensuring a contractually assured overall availability. The scope of services comprises in particular: - the provision, operation and maintenance of the cloud-based CLEMS, - the integration of charging points into the background system, - upon request, the time-limited transfer (rental), installation and system service of depot controllers, - support services (including hotline and ticketing system), - project management for the implementation of the solution, - training and instruction, and - complete documentation of the services rendered. The services form a factual, economic and legal unit and are to be provided as a functional overall system. The contractor bears overall responsibility for the proper provision of services and is also liable for the deployment of any subcontractors. The complete provision of the cloud service, including integration of the CLEMS, must take place within the execution period specified in the contract.
sig_a1601ba3832f0d5f4a9b.title: Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) - Introduction of a charging, load and energy management system (CLEMS) as SaaS

sig_a166664b6860ad79c464.description: The subject of the procurement is licences for an app for the improved care of insured persons with limitations in the area of cognition and language as a result of neurological diseases. The content of the app should be exercises for training the various competence areas of language, cognition, memory and attention. The decision regarding the eligibility for benefits of the affected insured persons is the responsibility of the DAK-Gesundheit in individual cases. Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of an app for training cognition and language in neurological diseases. The key to successful neurological rehabilitation in the therapeutic area is a high training intensity after the disease event in both the acute and chronic phases. The use of the app should be useful in both phases. The focus of the application should be on sustainable motivation for independent and self-responsible training and should pick up on and take into account fluctuations in the user's performance. In doing so, the development of training routines should support the user. Medical advice must not be provided in the app. Since the app is only to be made available to eligible insured persons from the 18. year of life of the DAK-Gesundheit, identification of the users is necessary. Precise coordination for implementation and/or for checking the user's eligibility for benefits takes place after consultation between the manufacturer and the DAK-Gesundheit and must be GDPR-compliant. During the transition from inpatient to outpatient care for neurologically ill insured persons, gaps in care arise due to difficulties in scheduling appointments with doctors and service providers, which hinder rapid convalescence. Independent, structured training in this transition phase is currently not systematically available. With this procurement, insured persons with limitations in cognition and language as a result of neurological diseases are to be enabled to bridge the waiting time until or in parallel with standard care with independent, evidence-based training. The app is intended to increase training intensity, promote continuous use and take individual performance fluctuations into account. In this respect, the app should address the disease-specific individual symptoms of those affected. The app for neurologically ill insured persons is intended to accompany those affected in therapy and support them in training independently, self-determinedly and regularly. The course of the disease and disease relapses should be positively influenced by this and the quality of life of those affected should increase. As a result, the DAK-Gesundheit achieves increased satisfaction among those affected as well as indirectly among their social environment. In this way, service costs in care are also to be specifically reduced through the use of the app.
sig_a166664b6860ad79c464.title: Procurement of an app for training cognition and language in neurological diseases

sig_a167084ae789385c0536.description: Northumbria University is launching a bold and innovative digital transformation programme centred on the implementation of SMART cards and advanced identity management. This initiative is designed to strengthen our identification capabilities improving the wider user experience and is to be driven by the adoption of a cutting-edge approach supported by market-leading technology. This strategic investment will replace the University’s outdated ImageBase system (introduced in 2015) and photo uploader (introduced in 2006), which no longer support the university’s operational, security or digital transformation needs. The current anticipated project approach is to deliver a modern, cloud-native identity and credential management solution to support around 7,000 staff, 77,000 student accounts and a wide range of visitors across our campuses. As a minimum, the solution must enable secure identity verification, smartcard issuance and management and integrate smoothly with the University’s established Joiners, Movers, and Leavers (JML) processes. Identified key deliverables that will form part of this requirement include (but is not limited to): •Cloud solutions replacing Smartcard system (ImageBase) and Identity application (MIM). •Mobile-friendly platform for photo capture and validation, replacing the legacy photo uploader. •Transition from Mifare Classic 1K to a secure credential card storage such as Mifare DESFire EV3. •Smooth interoperability with key business applications such as SITS, Oracle HCM, Entra, ADFS, PACOM and other student and library systems. •Architecture designed to support mobile credentials and future digital identity options and centralised dashboard for card issuance, usage tracking, and operational reporting. •Cyber secure offerings to align to National Cyber Security Centres Cyber Assessment Framework Prior to commencing formal procurement, we are engaging the market to: •Deepen and confirm our understanding of the wider opportunity, showcasing best practice in deploying new technology while meeting the key deliverables outlined above as well as any mandatory and statutory requirements, placing user experience at the core of the solution. •Define and evolve our requirements beyond key deliverables by leveraging industry best practice and supplier insight to deliver a solution that surpasses conventional approaches to identity management. •Gather insight into indicative commercial models, potential delivery timelines and the critical internal enablers necessary to ensure the programme’s success. •Draw on supplier expertise in implementing scalable technology solutions for organisations with comparable scale and complexity. •Expand our understanding on how current hardware could be retained or repurposed. •Explore potential delivery models that follow a phased approach beginning with strategic advisory and progressing through design, delivery and implementation. By engaging suppliers at this early stage, we aim to harness market insight to help inform and shape our future requirements. This approach is designed to support a fair, competitive and effective tender process, ensuring we identify the right supplier to successfully deliver the programme. Further information relating to this PME opportunity are available via our Delta eSourcing platform: https://login.bipsolutions.com/casDelta/login?service=https%3A%2F%2Fneupc.delta-esourcing.com%2Fdelta%2Fj_spring_cas_security_check Access Code: 4S99HAJH85 To access the platform, please copy and paste the URL into your browser. If you don’t yet have a Delta account, registration is quick and straightforward. As part of this process and to assist the University develop its requirements, we would appreciate responses from interested suppliers to our questionnaire. Responses to the questionnaire should be submitted by 17:00 GMT on 2nd December, 2025 via Delta eSourcing. In addition to the questionnaire process and to promote further insight into the programme, we will be holding a Microsoft Teams Town Hall on 28th November, 2025 at 14:00 GMT. The purpose of this session will be for the University to provide further insight into the programme including background, scope and indicative project timescales. Please note, Q and A will not be open for this Town Hall. Furthermore, suppliers are invited to book a virtual one-to-one Microsoft Teams session for 30 minutes which will be running over 3 days; 8th – 10th December, 2025. Each supplier may reserve a single slot on any of these dates to offer their input, expand on responses given within your Supplier Questionnaire and raise any queries or questions. Slots will be allocated on a first come, first served basis and communications regarding your preferred slot should be made via the submission of your Supplier Questionnaire within Delta. The value referenced in relation to this pre-market engagement is indicative only and does not represent a commitment to any specific level of expenditure. For more information about this opportunity, please visit the Delta eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Newcastle-upon-Tyne:-Smart-cards./4S99HAJH85 To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/4S99HAJH85 Lot 1: .

sig_a169371e66cee006b78c.description: EIFO wishes to enter into a framework agreement on communication and campaign services. The framework agreement is divided into four sub-agreements: • Sub-agreement 1: Communication consultancy • Sub-agreement 2: Advertising agency services • Sub-agreement 3: Media agency services • Sub-agreement 4: Consultancy services for website development This sub-agreement covers strategic communication consultancy in Denmark. EIFO is relevant to everyone from top to bottom in Danish business life – from startups over SMEs to large companies with multi-billion export projects. As a relatively new company, we wish to increase awareness of EIFO and our solutions among our Danish target audiences. At the same time, EIFO is an independent public enterprise that must constantly remain commercially and politically relevant for Denmark. With changing societal agendas and new political priorities, EIFO's essential agendas and strategic initiatives can change quickly. First and foremost, agencies must be able to analyse and understand EIFO's needs and deliver high-level communication consultancy. In addition, agencies must, for example, be able to do the following: • Advise on communication strategy • Deliver communication consultancy in individual cases – e.g. handling new political mandates, new important agendas, crisis communication etc. • Understand EIFO's agendas and target audiences and develop messages for the target audiences • Media-train spokespersons • Advise on and execute effective communication across various channels, e.g. press, website, social media, newsletters, webinars, events (e.g. Folkemødet and TechBBQ), oral presentations in network forums etc. • Advise on strategic management communication and internal communication to EIFO's group executive board. • Develop and execute smaller communication campaigns; This sub-agreement covers creative advertising agency services for the development of campaigns. EIFO wishes to strengthen our awareness and business in the Danish market and international markets by continuously developing and implementing both broad awareness campaigns and targeted tactical activation campaigns. We therefore need ongoing cooperation with creative and strategically strong advertising agencies. The agencies must help us develop campaign concepts that strengthen EIFO's brand and create visibility, awareness, engagement and results. The tasks include inter alia: • Having a strategic understanding of EIFO's communication landscape and target audiences • Creating creative concept development based on the strategic understanding • Activation of the concepts through the production of concrete campaign materials and communication events.; Sub-agreement 3 covers media agency services in connection with the execution of campaigns, including those developed by the advertising agencies under sub-agreement 2. EIFO wishes to ensure that campaigns are implemented effectively and reach the right target audiences through strategically planned and optimised media efforts. For this purpose, we need close and ongoing cooperation with media agencies that can deliver both strategic consultancy and practical execution. The media agencies must inter alia: • Develop and implement media strategies that maximise the reach and impact of campaigns. • Advise on target audiences, media channels, budget allocation and other factors that can affect the impact of campaigns. • Identify and analyse relevant media platforms. • Handle media planning, negotiation of media purchases, booking and optimisation of media placements. • Report on campaign performance and provide recommendations for improving future efforts.; This sub-agreement covers consultancy services for the further development and maintenance of EIFO's website. EIFO wishes to strengthen its digital presence and accessibility for customers and partners through a professional, user-friendly and visually appealing website that supports EIFO's overarching business goals and digital strategy. We therefore seek ongoing cooperation with digital agencies that can deliver full-service web development with both technical and creative competence – and which at the same time have insight into EIFO's visual identity, business complexity and core target audiences. Concrete tasks under this sub-agreement may inter alia include: • Further development of web design based on EIFO's CVI and existing design principles, • Implementation and upgrading of CMS (Umbraco), • Consultancy on and implementation of SEO and performance optimisation measures, • Ongoing technical and content-related maintenance and updating of the website, • User testing and UX optimisation based on the target audience's needs and behaviour, • Consultancy on and implementation of solutions that strengthen the website's security, stability and accessibility.
sig_a169371e66cee006b78c.title: Tendering for a framework agreement on communication and campaign services for the Denmark Export and Investment Fund (EIFO)

sig_a16a4e96938af1aa3fb6.description: This Call for Solutions is issued under the Army Open Solicitation W9128Z-25-S-A002. Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Defense Commissary Agency is seeking for solutions for Enterprise Grocery Product Content Creation, Management, and Syndication SaaS Solution The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is a component of the Department of War (DoW) that provides enterprise-wide mission support to all United States (U.S.) uniformed services, including the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, and Coast Guard, in both continental United States (CONUS) and outside of the continental United States (OCONUS) locations. DeCA’s mission is to deliver a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings to military personnel and their families. DeCA operates a global system of 235 commissaries across 45 states, 13 countries, and two U.S. territories, with approximately 3,000 checkout lanes. To support modern, multi-channel retail operations, DeCA requires a robust, centralized enterprise capability to acquire, create, validate, manage, and syndicate product images, digital assets, specifications, dimensions, metadata, and related content. This system is essential for driving digital commerce, in-store merchandising, automated planogramming, marketing, and global store operations. DeCA manages a highly diverse, worldwide grocery portfolio. Accurate, consistent, and timely product content is critical across multiple downstream business functions, including eCommerce platforms, digital marketing, category management, shelf planning, and physical store operations. DeCA is seeking an integrated Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution combining centralized Digital Asset Management (DAM) and Product Information Management (PIM) capabilities with content creation services, supplier collaboration tools, and automated system integration. The Call for Solutions document, submission requirements can be found in the Attachments section below. The deadline to submit questions for Phase I is 01 October 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT

sig_a16d45d2cf3e7923a6dc.description: The subject of performance of the (partial) public contracts awarded under the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) will be the procurement of technologies, software resources, products and services from the manufacturer Cisco Systems, Inc., 170 West Tasman Dr. San Jose, CA 95134 USA (hereinafter referred to as 'Cisco Systems'). This involves ensuring the procurement of technologies and services from Cisco Systems or supplementing existing technologies and services of the controlling contracting authority from Cisco Systems, exclusively in cases where it is not possible to request technologies and services from a manufacturer other than Cisco Systems, particularly for the purpose of ensuring the compatibility, security and homogeneity of the controlling contracting authority's communication network and protecting investments already made, in situations where, if equipment other than Cisco Systems were supplied, the functionality and security integrity of the entire solution would not be ensured. Within the framework of individual calls for tenders for partial public contracts implemented through the DPS (partial public contracts), the contracting authority will require delivery to the place of performance (including transport) of Cisco Systems technologies, i.e. HW and SW components including their accessories, the provision of SW licences or product subscriptions, information necessary for their use, or potentially HW maintenance and/or SW maintenance and/or subscriptions. HW maintenance and/or SW maintenance and/or subscriptions must be provided within the Cisco Systems service programme. The subject of performance in the established DPS may thus include, in particular: - the provision of products whose essence is licensing or firmware equipment, using original and proprietary Cisco Systems resources and original Cisco Systems accessories, including the possibility of their implementation: - routers and corresponding proprietary SW licences for software products and/or Cisco Systems subscriptions, - switches and corresponding proprietary SW licences for software products and/or Cisco Systems subscriptions, - products for wireless networks and corresponding proprietary SW licences for software products and/or Cisco Systems subscriptions, - security products and corresponding proprietary SW licences for software products and/or Cisco Systems subscriptions, - tools for team collaboration and corresponding proprietary SW licences for software products and/or Cisco Systems subscriptions, - original Cisco Systems accessories, - the provision of licences for all Cisco Systems software resources, - the provision of support for Cisco Systems products, - the provision of subscriptions for Cisco Systems products, - the provision of 'AS-Fixed' type catalogue services from Cisco Systems, - the provision of Cisco Systems catalogue training credits, - the provision of pre-sales consultancy from Cisco Systems for the controlling contracting authority, - the provision of information on Cisco Systems software changes and new features, - the provision of consultancy on how to purchase Cisco Systems licences, - the provision of information on the Cisco Systems product lifecycle. The subject of performance of individual (partial) public contracts awarded under the DPS, with the required technical specification, will be detailed in the procurement documentation for the award of the specific partial public contract under the DPS (in the call for tenders within the meaning of Section 141 of the Public Procurement Act) and in its annexes.

sig_a1af30c14efa775186fd.description: The Norwegian Coastal Administration is a transport agency under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries, with responsibility for safe and efficient transport in Norwegian farleder. The agency also has a national responsibility for stand-by against severe pollution. The Norwegian Coastal Administration is responsible for civil maritime monitoring, including monitoring shipping traffic, as well as supporting other departments ́ sector responsibility within maritime safety and contingency. The current monitoring capacity is largely based on maritime reporting systems, where the Automatic Identification System (AIS) makes up a central supporting beam. Although AIS provides comprehensive information about ship traffic, situations occur where location data is not received is insufficient or deliberately suppressed. This creates a need for complementary monitoring methods. The objective of the procurement is therefore to supplement the existing monitoring capacity with satellite based, non-cooperative sensor data. The system shall contribute to strengthening situational comprehension in Norwegian sea areas by using image forming sensors (optical and SAR – Synthetic Aperture Radar). This shall enable: verification of AIS data detection of vessels that do not send AIS (so-called "dark vessels") improved situation understanding and decision support in the operative contexts The coastal works would like to enter into an agreement for access to an already established and operative system for satellite based detection and analysis. Developments in this procurement cannot be included. The contract will be valid for one (1) year, with an option for an extension.
sig_a1af30c14efa775186fd.title: Procurement of satellite based and optical SAR.

sig_a1d31a611e6e4549cb68.description: The objective of the procurement is to acquire IT project manager and expert resources to support, among other things, the definition, programming, testing and management of the Finnish Tax Administration's new and existing systems. The expert resources will operate in projects, development tasks and ongoing service production. The purpose of the procurement is to secure specialist expertise and sufficient resources. The procurement is divided into six (6) lots, for each of which three (3) suppliers and three (3) reserve suppliers will be selected. The lots and their contents are described in more detail below. More detailed descriptions of the contents of the assignments for the procurement lots are described in the appendix Description of the subject matter of the procurement in section 3. The objective is for the contract to enter into force on 16.11.2026. The contract shall be valid for 72 months. Verohallinto develops and maintains digital services primarily as cloud-based and cloud-native solutions. The development work utilises application, integration, data and platform services provided by the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, as well as modern software development, information security and operational practices. Solutions vary in scope and criticality from mission-critical core applications to more limited services targeting specific business needs. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for cloud-based software development implemented in the Microsoft Azure environment. The lot includes in particular architecture design for cloud solutions and cloud applications, application and integration development, DevOps, the development and maintenance of cloud platforms, and the technical information security of cloud environments and applications. Key expert roles include cloud solution architect, cloud application architect, cloud software developer, integration developer, cloud DevOps specialist, cloud platform specialist and technical information security specialist.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for applications and information system solutions utilising artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and machine learning. The solutions are implemented primarily in the Microsoft Azure cloud environment, utilising the artificial intelligence capabilities offered by Microsoft Foundry and other Azure services. The solutions can be standalone AI applications or parts of broader information systems, digital services and software solutions. Expert work concerning new technologies may relate to the assessment of the possibilities, suitability, information security and risks of technologies, experiments and prototyping, software and hardware integration, the development of embedded systems, preparation for deployment, or the practical utilisation of technologies. Key expert roles for AI applications include AI application specialists, AI developers, AI solution architects, machine learning specialists and software developers participating in the implementation of AI applications.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services aimed at improving the efficiency, quality and transparency of the organisation's operational and data-driven processes through automation, hyper-automation, analytics and systematic development methods. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is primarily process automation expert services as well as process analytics and process development expert services in a cloud-based operating environment.; The Finnish Tax Administration's technological operating environment strongly includes the development of infrastructure, analytics, information security and cloud services. The Finnish Tax Administration uses the Gentax core taxation system and several smaller systems (e.g. supporting administration). The National Incomes Register and the Positive Credit Register are also the responsibility of the Finnish Tax Administration. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot includes: - project manager services for the development, creation and deployment of operating models and processes, as well as the development of related applications. The scope of impact of operational development can be internal to the organisation and/or customer-related. - technical project manager services, particularly for the areas of infrastructure and information security - Scrum master/team lead services for operational and technical development teams.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is IT service management expert services for the ServiceNow environment, as well as expert services specialised in ServiceNow development for architecture, consulting and development tasks. The tasks include ICT architecture and expert tasks in the ServiceNow modules used by the Finnish Tax Administration, including (* supplemented 4.9.2026): • ITSM (IT Service Management) • ITOM (IT Operations Management) • ITBM / SPM (Strategic Portfolio and Demand Management) • SecOps / SIR* (Security Operations) • IRM (Risk Management)* • CMDB (Configuration Management)* • IAM / AM (Access Management, Identity Management)* Expert tasks may include system development, configuration, maintenance, testing and training tasks for the modules in question, as well as related functional and technical architecture design.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is user-driven development expert services. By expert service, we mean working under the direction of the Finnish Tax Administration as part of the Finnish Tax Administration's development teams or in close cooperation with them, consulting, business sparring and/s or the implementation of various assignments. Verohallinto can also order fixed-price assignments for e.g. system accessibility audits.

sig_a23eb38604499b0b0ebf.description: The subject of the contract is the development and implementation of a digital mechanism for gathering and analysing data, as well as the provision of corresponding services to comprehensively determine the statutory minimum wage. Replacing the current country procedure for the statutory minimum wage with an automated data processing and weighting mechanism will bolster public trust in the state, restoring a sense of security regarding the new procedure, which will stand as a pinnacle of transparency and the simplification of convoluted procedures. Through the use of advanced technology, the new digital tool will provide the framework for decision-making procedures concerning the statutory minimum wage and the validity consistent with the overall objective of the state's strategic digital transformation. A new system for defining the statutory minimum wage and statutory minimum daily wage was introduced in Greece by Article 103 of Law 4172/ 2013 (Government Gazette A ́ 167), following extensive consultation. Said article empowers the Minister of Labour to issue a decision determining it, with the concurring opinion of the Cabinet. This procedure was initiated for the first time in September 2018 and was completed with the issuance of Ministerial Decision No. 4241/ 127/ 30.1.2019 (Government Gazette B ́ 173), on the basis of which the lawful minimum wage and lawful minimum daily wage for full-time employment for employees and manual workers throughout the country, without age discrimination, were determined as of 1.2.2019. Circular No. 7613/ 395/ 18.2.2019 issued instructions for the application of the above decision. The procedure for defining the statutory minimum wage and statutory minimum daily wage begins with consultations between the social partners and the Government. The consultation is coordinated by a tripartite committee consisting of the President of O.ME.D., a person of standing as a representative of the Minister of Finance, and a person of standing as a representative of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs. The consultation coordination committee invites specialised scientific, research and other bodies to draw up a report evaluating the current statutory minimum wage with estimates for their adaptation to current economic conditions. A file containing the above reports is then compiled and sent to the representatives of the social partners to express their opinion, by submitting a memorandum and documentation at their discretion for the readjustment of the current statutory minimum wage. The transmission of all memoranda as well as the report of the specialised scientific and research bodies is sent to the Centre for Planning and Economic Research (KEPE), for it to draft the Consultation Conclusions Draft in cooperation with a committee consisting of independent experts on economic matters, primarily labour economics, social policy and industrial relations, appointed by the Ministers of Labour and Social Affairs, Development, and Finance. The Consultation Conclusions Draft is submitted to the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, who proposes the minimum wage to the Cabinet and issues a decision determining the minimum wage for employees and the minimum daily wage for manual workers, following the concurring opinion of the Cabinet. Based on the above, the importance of adopting a scientifically sound methodology to support relevant decisions on adjusting the minimum wage in the country based on comprehensive data ("evidence-based policy making") is highlighted, the development of which methodology will rely on a suitably designed "data processing and weighting mechanism" for the scientific support and ultimately the upgrading of the current procedure for defining the statutory minimum wage. By harnessing digital technologies, the new Digital Tool will provide the framework for decision-making documentation procedures for the statutory minimum wage as well as compatibility with the broader objective of the state's strategic digital transformation. The new Digital Tool will strengthen citizens' trust in the state, cultivating a sense of security given that the new procedure will constitute a catalytic step towards safeguarding transparency through the simplification of procedures.
sig_a23eb38604499b0b0ebf.title: Digital Mechanism for data collection and calculation of the Statutory Minimum Wage
