sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.description: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Specific research goals include: establishing a fundamental mathematical understanding of the factors determining the capabilities and limitations of current and emerging generation s of AI systems, including, but not limited to, foundation models, generative models, deep learning, statistical learning, federated learning, and other evolving paradigms; the development of mathematically grounded design and analysis principles for the current and next generations of AI systems; rigorous approaches for characterizing and validating machine learning algorithms and their predictions; research enabling provably reliable, translational, general-purpose AI systems and algorithms; e ncouragement of new collaborations in this interdisciplinary research community and between institution s. The overall goal is to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology using creative yet theoretically grounded mathematical and statistical frameworks, yielding explainable and interpretable models that can enable sustainable, socially responsible, and trustworthy AI.

sig_a6751a53b2a5f548d6e5.description: The purpose of this contract is the provision of consultancy services in communication and digital marketing for the Campus Rural Programme, as well as the ancillary supply of promotional material and merchandising linked to its implementation. The provision of services shall comprise the planning, coordination, operational execution and monitoring of communication and promotion activities linked to the programme. In particular, they shall include the drafting and application of communication criteria, the creation of dissemination materials and media, the basic planning and coordination of contents and messages, as well as the promotion and support of participants in the programme through activities such as welcome sessions, thematic webinars, monitoring actions and visits to students carrying out work placements in rural areas. Likewise, as part of the development of the planned communication and promotion activities, the contract shall comprise the supply of promotional material and merchandising directly linked to the Campus Rural Programme. Said supply shall be of an ancillary and instrumental nature with respect to the provision of services and shall be aimed at supporting the promotion, dissemination and identification actions of the programme, without constituting an autonomous or independent purpose. The provision of services and supply are directly linked to each other and are complementary for the achievement of the communication, positioning and community promotion objectives of the Campus Rural Programme, forming a single functional unit.

sig_a68428bbecf07464a8ef.description: Workforce shortages and uncertainties have derailed nuclear projects worldwide—causing delays, cost overruns and lost investor confidence. The specialized talent nuclear needs to succeed requires years to develop. The ReactorCast platform answers human capital questions, coupled to strategic decisions and financial considerations, before the issues become crises. ReactorCast is a custom system dynamics platform that models and ties strategic decisions and investment considerations with workforce requirements across the entire lifecycle of nuclear programs—from initial planning through decades of operation to eventual decommissioning. The platform provides real-time analytics and visual dashboards that track workforce flows from identified populations to education and training programs through employment across utilities, developers, contractors, regulators and support organizations. ReactorCast also models the impact of policy, regulatory and investment decisions on workforce development trajectories. Unlike individual HR management systems, ReactorCast operates at the strategic level—modeling the workforce potential to answer questions that matter most to executives, investors and leaders: Can this organization or region supply the talent we need? What does workforce availability mean for our site selection? How do different technology choices impact long-term staffing costs? These aren’t HR questions—they’re business strategy questions. The underlying modeling methodology— developed at Los Alamos and licensed to the IAEA as the basis for their national nuclear workforce planning workshops and tools—has been applied internationally across numerous nuclear programs LA-UR-26-23908 Technical Specifications Custom developed software for system dynamics modeling Modular, extensible design for evolving analysis needs Local deployment (secure, non-cloud infrastructure framework) Interfaces with external data sources and planning tools Outputs include: regional, statewide or national mapping, workforce opportunities and competency projections, gap analyses and scenario-based deployment comparisons For those realizing new nuclear deployments, ReactorCast models workforce requirements across different reactor technologies and sites. Compare the human capital implications of a large light-water reactor versus multiple small modular reactors. Assess whether different reactor technologies affect your ability to recruit and retain talent in specific regions. Understand how workforce costs—which can exceed capital costs over a plant’s lifetime—vary based on technology and location decisions made today. ReactorCast separates serious strategic planning from optimistic assumptions, giving stakeholders the intelligence to make informed decisions about workforce-related project risk. Advantages Reactor Technology Differentiation: Different reactor technologies may potentially require fundamentally different workforce profiles. ReactorCast can model the varying implications and makes the trade-offs and considerations visible. This platform helps identify strategies for closing any gaps before commitments are made. With access to Los Alamos’s unique technical domain and expertise, the technical nuances between these designs can be quantized, incorporated and analyzed. Strategic Site Selection and Regional Assessment: Site selection for nuclear projects traditionally focuses on technical factors including: cooling water availability, seismic stability, grid connection and emergency planning zones. ReactorCast adds the workforce dimension that determines whether a technically perfect site can support successful project execution, and if it can’t, models strategic approaches for how to mitigate this risk. Location decisions made for workforce reasons create competitive advantages. A site chosen because it has workforce capacity that competitors overlooked becomes a strategic asset. Cost control, schedule discipline, regulatory strategy, stakeholder engagement and workforce planning are equally essential for nuclear’s success. Strategic Modeling Capability Points / Market Applications Real-time analytics and visual dashboards derived from custom developed stock-and-flow workforce dynamics software Multi-reactor technology comparison Lifecycle cost modeling (planning through decommissioning) Scenario planning and risk assessment tools Customizable for regional, statewide or multi-site contexts LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL’s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. Note: This is not a call for external services for the development of this technology. https://www.lanl.gov/engage/collaboration/feynman-center/partner-with-us/licensing-technology m.lanl.gov/tech-search

sig_a6a2116e8d4379fe2232.description: Defence Equipment and Support (DE&S) on behalf of the Ministry of Defence (MOD), is looking to secure a support solution to provide maintenance and technical support for an Authority owned Ground Station Terminal. The requirement is for a period of three (3) years, with the potential to extend to an additional two (2) years via costed options. This procurement shall be procured through the Crown Commercial Service (CCS), Space Technology Solutions (RM6370) Dynamic Market. The DM contains a list of qualified suppliers who meet specific membership conditions and are eligible to participate in procurements. Should Suppliers wish to recieve the PSQ are not yet on the DM, please engage with the Authority, who may be able to assit with expediting your application. Interested suppliers are required to be registered on the DM, and Defence Sourcing Portal (DSP) to engage and complete the Procurement Selective Questionnaire (PSQ). Should Tenderers be Invited to Negotiate (ITN), the Authority will evaluate the Tenderers capacity and capability against the evaluation criteria. For more details please refer to the official guidance, and the Space Technology Solutions DM. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-dynamic-markets-html / Space Technology Solutions - CCS It is the Authority's intention to down-select approximately 5 highest scoring Tenderers, who will then be ITN providing they meet the overall score of a pass within the PSQ. The Authority reserve the right to a fail a tenderer should they not meet the minimum pass criteria at the Evaluation Stage, and subsequently not be ITN. Overview: PRIMUS is a UK-located Ground Terminal designed to provide an interface between the Authority’s operations centre (Or the Authority’s authorised operation centres) and the space segment (SSeg). PRIMUS, is based on a 7.3-Meter S and X-band solution, sited within a Radome. It has been scoped to send and receive data from a MOD-owned satellite, whilst the Authority views PRIMUS as an enduring capability, intended to support numerous future Operational Concept Demonstrators (OCDs) that currently exist in various stages of development. The duration of the Authority’s In-Service Support (ISS) requirements covers a three-year core contract for the maintenance and operational readiness of the asset. Background: PRIMUS has been conceived under the auspices of the Authority’s ISTARI programme as its foremost conceptual demonstrator through which ground segment hardware, software and architecture associated with current and future missions has been, and will continue to be, procured, developed and integrated. The objective of PRIMUS is to develop an operational demonstration of the required hardware architecture that both informs and qualifies the MoD’s ground control segment concept, as well as integrating into the wider ISTARI architecture, enabling MoD execution of the Tasking, Collection, Processing, Exploitation, and Dissemination (TCPED) cycle. A core objective is to realise a solution which is applicable to supporting imminent missions, whilst also ensuring enduring capability through compatibility with future MoD activities where required. Requirement: PRIMUS is part of the UK Government’s broader efforts to maintain, secure and update its satellite communications capabilities, ensuring remote data links for Defence purposes. The Authority requires provision of maintenance and support, which will include both hardware and software elements. The requirements span numerous considerations ranging from routine preventative maintenance to training and management of critical spares, commensurate with Line-3 support. Miscellanous: PRIMUS has been designed with future capability in mind, allowing for – thanks to the terminal’s modular design and line replaceable units – potential upgrades. The Modular design preferred on the basis of achieving relatively easy swap-out of small RF components such as feeds/waveguides/Low Noise amplifiers etc., by supplier-trained engineers. The Cyber Risk Profile for this procurement identified by the Cyber Risk Assessment is: Reference: Level 2 PRIMUS is equipped with the OEM’s licensed software and, as such, the terms governing the use of this proprietary software are prescribed within an existing and enduring licensing agreement between the OEM and the Authority. Suppliers are advised they are not explicitly covered under the agreement, and may be required to establish a relationship with the OEM in relation to licence software. Tenderers are to be advised that this contract shall have a rolling start date, due to on-going dependencies associated with the terminal. Lot 1: .

sig_a6a4fbe2e1f8f46b3c6b.description: Iarnród Éireann – Irish Rail (IÉ) is seeking to establish a contract for the design, supply, configuration, integration, commissioning, support and maintenance of a Station Services Mediation System (SSMS). The SSMS will provide the central processing, integration and management platform for real-time passenger information services across the Iarnród Éireann railway network. The system will interface with existing and future IÉ operational systems, including timetable systems, signalling systems, Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS), Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems and external passenger information platforms. The solution will support the phased migration from IÉ's existing Customer Information Systems to the future Centralised Traffic Control and Communications Based Interlocking (CBI) environment while maintaining continuity of passenger information services throughout the transition. The scope includes all necessary software, licences, configuration and integration services, testing, commissioning, migration, documentation, training, maintenance, technical support, cybersecurity updates, lifecycle and obsolescence management required to provide a fully operational and supported SSMS solution. The proposed contract will be for an initial period of eight (8) years, with an option for IÉ to extend the contract for a further three (3) years at its discretion.

sig_a6a7c2fba9edcda32bee.description: The EU Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR) provides for mandatory pollinator monitoring. The first reporting cycle covers 4, the following 6 years, and the first reporting year is 2030. With the 1. delegated act (1. DA), the Commission specifies a concrete concept with uniform methods that are to be implemented by the Member States. This is intended to ensure that the data collected can be compared and evaluated at EU level. The aim of this project is to develop an implementation concept for Germany. As far as possible, the pollinator monitoring is to be integrated into the nationwide insect monitoring (IM). The basis for the German implementation concept is formed by the delegated acts issued by the European Commission (EC), which contain the methodology for the implementation of Article 10 of the NRR. The publication of the 1. DA establishing the scientifically sound method for monitoring the diversity of pollinators and pollinator populations is expected for autumn 2025. The technical basis for the 1. DA is the concept for EU pollinator monitoring developed on behalf of the EC (Potts et al. 2024, Potts et al. 2021). The 1. DA formulates the methodological specifications for pollinator monitoring. These specifications are to be translated into an operable implementation concept, and the content-related, structural and organisational requirements for pollinator monitoring are to be worked out in detail. The 1. DA formulates the rules for the selection of the sample areas to be monitored. It defines the animal groups to be recorded and the methodology with which these taxa are observed. Accordingly, the project comprises the following objectives: i) development and definition of the sample population to be sampled in accordance with the specifications of the 1. DA, ii) implementation-ready preparation of the recording methodology for all modules required and described in the 1. DA, as well as iii) development of an IT specialist concept for the modules designed here. sig_a6a82e16a4eedf106be5.description: The subject and purpose of the performance of the public contract is the design, manufacture, delivery and subsequent installation of electronic intelligent public transport stop poles in the statutory city of Chomutov, all under the Design and Build regime, where the contractor will also be the author of the project and the technical solution. The aim is the installation of 45 intelligent stop poles at bus and trolleybus stops and significant transport hubs. The subject-matter of performance also includes the design and integration of a software system for the management and monitoring of the stop poles (dispatching and monitoring system), including the provision of connection to the API of the Ústí Region Transport (DÚK). Furthermore, the subject-matter of performance includes all structural alterations and earthworks necessary for the installation of the stop poles and related infrastructure, including the securing of all necessary permits including the building permit (intent permit) and necessary statements from authorities. As part of ensuring the long-term functionality and sustainability of the subject-matter of performance, the public contract is combined with operational and maintenance support for a period of five years, which the contractor undertakes to provide to the contracting authority on the basis of a separate service contract concluded simultaneously with the works contract.
sig_a6a82e16a4eedf106be5.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF CHOMUTOV PUBLIC TRANSPORT ELECTRONIC STOP POLES USING THE DESIGN & BUILD METHOD

The subject of the Contract is the execution of the following elements: The subject of the Contract is the execution of the following elements: Design and execution of works for the task entitled: “Construction of a building structure entitled: railway line no. 622 Gdów – Szczyrzyc on section G from km 17+487 to km 32+854 together with technical infrastructure along railway line no. 622 on the section from km 17+036 to km 32+973 and railway line no. 623 junction Fornale – Szczyrzyc on section G from km 9+668 to km 10+105 together with technical infrastructure along the railway connecting track no. 623 on the section from km 9+668 to km 10+105”. The entire subject of the Contract includes the execution of the following elements: 1) Design documentation, including: a) development of the executive design, b) development of as-built documentation, including geodetic as-built documentation, 2) and works in the scopes described in the Description of the Subject of the Contract (OPZ) and the Functional-Utility Programme (PFU): a) track surface and substructure, b) drainage and hydrotechnical works, c) external networks, d) roads, e) railway traffic control (srk) devices, f) telecommunication devices and systems, g) overhead contact line and power supply and control system, h) non-traction power supply line (LPN); i) electrical power engineering devices and systems up to 1 kV, j) engineering structures together with accompanying works, including railway tunnels, k) platforms, passenger service facilities and cubature facilities, l) crossings and level crossings, m) geological and geotechnical works, n) works related to the execution of small architecture elements, o) cutting of trees and shrubs and environmental industry works, p) all others necessary for the implementation of the task in accordance with applicable regulations. 3) works consisting of the construction of facilities serving environmental protection. 4) conducting the process of conformity assessment of structural subsystems in the scope covered by the contract at every stage (design, construction and final tests of the subsystem) and submission of appropriate EC verification declarations and EC verification certificates for the subsystems. The option for the interface includes the implementation of cooperation with other contractors carrying out construction works or supplies for the Contracting Authority, which require connection with railway traffic control devices installed as part of this task. Cooperation will take place through the Contracting Authority and/or the Engineer. The Contracting Authority anticipates that the scope of works carried out under other Contracts affects the necessity of making, among others, changes in the scope of interfaces (i.e. implementation of the Option for the Interface as part of this task). The detailed scope of the Option for the Interface has been defined in Chapter no. 5 of VOLUME IV — PFU entitled: “Anticipated changes in the scope of interfaces”, which concern the srk devices intended for installation as part of this contract. 2. A detailed Description of the Subject of the Contract has been presented in the Description of the Subject of the Contract constituting Volume III of this SWZ and the Functional-Utility Programme (PFU) constituting Volume IV of this SWZ. 3. The Contracting Authority anticipates awarding contracts referred to in Art. 388 point 2) letter c) of the Act. The scope of contracts referred to in Art. 388 point 2) letter c) of the Act and the conditions under which they will be awarded are defined by the OPZ and PFU. A similar contract may be awarded in the single-source procurement mode, after prior negotiations with the Contractor, in particular regarding the terms of the contract including price, completion date, warranty period/statutory warranty period and will consist of repeating similar executive designs for the srk industry and complex construction works consistent with the subject of the contract, in particular in the scopes: a) dismantling and liquidation of railway infrastructure in poor technical condition, devastated, unused cubature facilities as well as elements conflicting with design solutions, b) execution of construction works covering the track industry with drainage, engineering structures industry (including tunnels) together with the execution of hydrotechnical works in their vicinity, road industry, electrical power industry, overhead contact line industry, overhead contact line power supply industry, telecommunication industry, passenger service facilities and cubature facilities together with surface drainage of the area, sanitary industry, srk industry, c) removal of collisions with networks of various utility owners.

sig_a6d72838cab06fca093c.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. Part II covers the implementation of a GIS system, conducting a measurement campaign, and the creation and calibration of a hydraulic model of the water supply network. The contract also includes the provision of SIM cards and data transmission for a period of 10 years. A mandatory site visit is required to verify the coverage and availability of the network in the area of contract implementation, on the terms specified in the SWZ.; The subject of Part 2 of the contract is the implementation of a GIS system, conducting a measurement campaign, and the creation and calibration of a hydraulic model of the Lipno Municipality water supply network, together with the commissioning of the system, documentation, training, and support.; Part III covers work on the active water supply network in 141 locations, including 70 complete hydrant nodes DN80 together with the replacement of the gate valve DN80, 10 complete hydrant nodes DN80 without replacing the existing gate valve DN80 and 61 complete replacements of gate valves DN100. The total material scope includes 80 hydrants DN80, 70 gate valves DN80 and 61 gate valves DN100. The contract also includes all earthworks, assembly and restoration works, and other activities required by the OPZ

sig_a6f71bc460a7855ca54f.description: To support current and future road infrastructure schemes aligned with the Mayor's Transport Strategy for London, TfL plans to award a contract to a single service provider to deliver the Detection and Enforcement Infrastructure (D&EI) Services. The primary function of the D&EI Services is to operate and maintain detection and enforcement infrastructure and technology that provides the required evidence for charging and enforcement of all Road User Charging (RUC) schemes. At the date of this Tender Notice, these schemes are: • Congestion Charge (CC); • Low Emission Zone (LEZ); • Ultra-Low Emission Zone (ULEZ); • Tunnel User Charging (TUC) (Silvertown and Blackwall Tunnels); and • Direct Vision Standards (DVS). The D&EI Services provide high-quality images and data for vehicles passing any of the approximate 4,400 ANPR cameras stationed at locations in Greater London (the "Outstations"). Vehicle records from the roadside are processed to produce accurate and secure evidential records which are then transferred to TfL's Business Operations system and to TfL and other Connected Parties (being other parties with whom TfL shares another form of evidential records or data), which use these records to initiate payment and enforcement processes and analyse vehicle journey times. TfL anticipates the D&EI Services will cover the following: Outstation Systems and Services - The primary function of the Outstation System is to detect moving vehicles in the Greater London area, capture images of the vehicles, read the vehicles registration plates and to send this data to the Instation and to Connected Parties for processing. The Outstation System comprises of a network of approximately 4,400 ANPR cameras and associated equipment, including mounting brackets, poles, cabinets, cabling and, at tunnel sites, radar detection units. The scope of the D&EI Services includes the management, support, maintenance and repair of the Outstation Systems. The scope will include the provision of new ANPR cameras where required to replace existing units that are vandalised, stolen, beyond economic repair or end of life, and for the installation of new Outstations. At the expiry of the current D&EI contract, there will be c.4,400 Outstation assets throughout the TfL RUC estate. TfL is not intending to replace all of these assets as part of transition to the new D&EI Services contract. Instead, to support the new service provider's delivery of the D&EI Services, TfL will put in place a standalone contract with the current D&EI service provider to cover certain OEM-level maintenance and support services for those elements of the existing Outstation assets which are proprietary in nature to that service provider. This will include: • firmware/software updates to maintain outstation performance and security;​​ • ongoing access to a repair facility for legacy outstation hardware;​ • access to bespoke spare parts not available on the open market.​ Instation Systems and Services - The primary function of the Instation System is to process data collected by the Outstations, including some validation and filtering functions. This scope of services will include the design, supply, build and installation of an Instation System. The D&EI service provider will be required to support, maintain and operate the Instation System. The Instation System is also used for centralised management, configuration and monitoring of Outstations, as well as installing required Outstation firmware/software updates. Camera replacement programme - During the life of the contract, existing camera assets will need to be replaced from time to time. This may be carried out on an ad hoc basis or, at TfL's discretion, in accordance with a structured replacement programme. The D&EI contract will include camera replacement pricing. Given the likelihood of policy changes and developments, evolutions and other changes to the RUC schemes over the life of the D&EI contract, TfL may require additional services which are similar to the D&EI Services to be provided, including: • amendments to the D&EI service and systems to support any changes, extensions or reductions to the operation of the charging schemes; • amendments to the D&EI service and systems to support new charging methods; • incorporating additional traffic monitoring or detection functionality into Outstation Systems; • provision of data to TfL approved third parties; • provision and maintenance of a separate power supply to power additional communications equipment located at fixed line Outstation Sites; • other relevant charging schemes, including: - interoperability with other road pricing schemes; - different scheme charging options; and/or - any other UK-based road user charging scheme, including infrastructure charging, congestion charging and clean air zones. Exclusion on national security grounds Under the Procurement Act 2023, contracting authorities must assess the national security threat posed by suppliers, their associated persons and (intended) sub-contractors. Given the nature and distribution of Outstations around London and the interfaces between the D&EI system and other systems, TfL considers that the D&EI procurement is a higher sensitivity procurement. TfL will, in accordance with its obligations under the Procurement Act 2023, assess Participants (including their associated persons and intended sub-contractors) for potential national security threats to determine whether a Participant may be an excluded or excludable supplier on national security grounds. In carrying out this assessment and making any related decisions, TfL will consult with the National Security Unit for Procurement and only take action where necessary to address a relevant risk, and in a targeted and proportionate manner. Reservation of Right. TfL reserves the right without prior notice to change the procurement process or to amend the information provided, including, but not limited to, changing the timeline, the scope and nature of the procurement and the procurement process, and to cancel the procurement process at any stage without awarding any contract. In particular, TfL reserves the right to issue circulars to Participants providing further information or supplementing and/or amending the procurement process. In no circumstances shall TfL incur any liability in respect of any changes. This will be subject to the requirements of public law and UK procurement rules. Lot 1: .

sig_a705234c9346f4b6b8ef.description: The procurement is carried out in the context of implementing digitalisation infrastructure at the Mehedinți County Council through the project titled "Digitalisation of processes at the South-West Oltenia region level - Mehedinți County", SMIS code 327303, financed within the project call PRSVO/224/PRSVO_P2/OP1/RSO1.2/PRSVO_A9, Priority 2 - "Digitalisation for the benefit of citizens and businesses", of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021-2027. Through the acquisition and implementation of digitalisation services, the Contracting Authority anticipates a profound transformation of its activity, aiming for a significant increase in the quality of administrative acts and operational efficiency. The results of the services will influence institutional activity through the standardisation of processes, ensuring legal compliance and radically improving interaction with public service beneficiaries. The general objective of the project aims to achieve digitalisation for the benefit of citizens and businesses, by providing the inhabitants of Mehedinți County with a centralised access point to all services under the institution's remit. To this end, the aim is to implement a mature IT solution and create a digital governance system for the structured collection, standardisation and efficient management of data at the Mehedinți County level, through secure bidirectional transfer both internally and in relation to third parties and other institutions, parameterisation (customisation) of process digitalisation, creation of new functionalities for electronic public services, and staff training. The number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders/applications is 18 days. The Contracting Authority will respond to requests for clarification once on the 11th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. In order to streamline the activity of Mehedinți County, an inter-institutional, interconnected and interoperable IT solution will be implemented, a commercial product available to the provider at the time of tender submission, understanding by this a distributed architecture of different instances based on a common core, each instance being capable of ensuring governance specific to the particular functional context and acting in an interconnected and interoperable manner with all others, benefiting from its own tools and work interfaces. The implementation of an ERDP (Electronic Registered Delivery Platform) type IT solution is requested, which includes (1) a subscription/licensing services component for access to a SAAS cloud solution for the digitalisation of processes and the relationship with third parties, a commercial product available to the provider at the time of tender submission which natively includes hosting infrastructure, security and functional updates, as well as standard technical support; (2) a component for parameterisation (customisation) services of the SAAS solution to the needs of Mehedinți County and its subordinates in relation to administrative processes and specific electronic services (including installation and commissioning); (3) a component for staff training services, including for cybersecurity, including for cybersecurity. The solution will include a secure collaborative work environment that will allow and facilitate: • digitalisation of specific and institutional internal workflows (support) / digitalisation of processes; • digitalisation of interaction with third parties (by third party is meant various entities with which Mehedinți County comes into contact: citizens, commercial companies, institutions etc); • preparation of the system for interoperability with other institutions/units (integration/consolidation and data replication). The duration of the contract is 9 months, representing the duration for the contractor to carry out all activities in the object of the contract, as these are summarised in the Specifications, in the chapter "Results to be obtained following the provision of services".

sig_a717790af332f4a06ce5.description: Background: Harstad municipality shall, on behalf of the participating collaboration municipalities, enter into a new framework agreement for advertising services. The need is a more general, efficient and predictable ad process. The municipalities need a system that combines a high degree of self-service with access to professional consultancy as needed. This particularly applies to recruitment advertisements, but the municipalities can also use the system for more complex or statutory announcements, where correct channel choices, targeting and documentation are important. Harstad municipality is the contracting authority for the procurement on behalf of the municipalities included in the contract. Each participating municipality will be responsible for its own obligations under the framework agreement. Other municipal entities, including public law bodies and organisations established by Harstad municipality, shall have the right, but are not obliged, to join the contract. Description of the assignment: Framework agreement for the procurement, production and publication of job advertisements, announcements and equivalent announcements on relevant channels. The contract ́s system shall facilitate simple and effective orders, follow-up and documentation of announcements. A service with self-service functionality is requested, combined with access to consultancy and assistance in the cases required by the municipalities. The contract shall contribute to better traceability and internal control throughout the entire process, from ordering and production to publication, reporting and archivable documentation. It is also a central objective that the system shall support the municipality ́s work flow and interact with the recruitment and HR systems that are used. The delivery shall cover publication in relevant digital and printed channels, including, among other things, newspapers, trade and trade media, job portals, social media and public registers where publication is required. Furthermore, the tenderer ́s system shall allow advertisements prepared in the municipalities ́ own recruitment and HR systems to be imported or uploaded to the tenderer ́s platform in an easy and appropriate manner. System integrations or automated data exchange are not required. The assignment also includes the necessary reporting and documentation for each advertisement or campaign.

sig_a71b20277db6da2c6586.description: The tender process comprises the conclusion of one (1) contract regarding the Contracting Authority's procurement of the development of an AI-based simulation tool for training child interviews. Based on this tender, one (1) joint contract will be concluded between the supplier and the Responsible Contracting Authority, cf. point 1.2 of the tender conditions, which acts on behalf of all participating contracting authorities. The Responsible Contracting Authority is Professionshøjskolen Absalon, which is authorised to manage all rights and obligations under the contract and acts as the contracting party towards the supplier. The supplier may therefore only direct claims against the Responsible Contracting Authority. Other participating contracting authorities are not direct contracting parties and are not liable either individually or jointly for the performance of the contract. Professionshøjskolen Absalon, in collaboration with the other university colleges, Red Barnet, Barndom Uden Vold and Ole Kirk’s Fond, is offering a contract for the development of an AI-based simulation tool, which is referred to in the tender documentation as the Solution. The purpose is to strengthen the competencies of social workers and social work students to conduct interviews with children in vulnerable situations, including children who may have been exposed to violence or abuse. The Solution must create a realistic, safe and learning-oriented training environment where users can prepare for child interviews, conduct interviews with digital avatars, receive guidance and feedback from a Tutor and subsequently analyse their interviews for the purpose of learning and reflection. It must be capable of being used in social work education, in continuing and further education programmes and in municipal practice. The first version, which this tender covers, must provide the possibility for speech- and text-based interaction with four avatars aged 9–11 years, representing different backgrounds and case types. In addition, there is a Tutor who supports the user before, during and after the interview through preparatory information, ongoing professional hints and subsequent debriefing. The Solution must accommodate both full interview processes and shorter modules where individual interview techniques can be trained in isolation. In the long term, the ambition is to expand the solution with more advanced modalities such as facial expressions and body language as well as real-time analysis of non-verbal communication. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to attract suppliers who can not only deliver the tendered solution but can also think visionarily in terms of creating a future-proof and innovative platform. The Responsible Contracting Authority provides an extensive knowledge base in the form of practice-oriented cases, anonymised child interviews and the expertise of professionals, and will also contribute actively with professional sparring during development. The tenders will be evaluated on feasibility and risk assessment, functionality and security, the realism of the avatars, the professional quality of the tutor as well as the overall user experience and technical robustness. The Responsible Contracting Authority is entitled to terminate the contract at Partial Delivery Day 1 (POC), solely for the purpose of bringing the project to an end, if it turns out during Partial Delivery 1 - POC that there are technical challenges which make it impossible to develop a suitable and usable Solution for the purpose that the contract supports, cf. point 31.2.1 of the Contract. However, it is the clear intention of the Responsible Contracting Authority to complete the development of a complete Solution that functions according to its purpose. Due to the established budget, the Contracting Authority has set a price ceiling for the Delivery Consideration. The Delivery Consideration, including the price for the Clarification Phase and the Delivery, cf. Contract Annex 01 – Schedule, must thus be a maximum of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT. Within the established price ceiling of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT, the Contracting Authority wishes to promote solutions that combine high technical quality and a high level of innovation. With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to support a competition that is not only based on price, but also on the Tenderers' ability to think long-term and visionarily. The Contracting Authority therefore explains the strategic and technological ambitions for the Solution in order to encourage tenderers to present proposals that reflect a future-proof and technologically advanced approach. At the same time, it is important for the Contracting Authority that the Solution can be operated sustainably within the financial frameworks that apply to the joint operations of the university colleges. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to enter into a contract with a Supplier who can ensure creativity and technical ingenuity in relation to developing a Solution that meets the desired needs, but which can at the same time be operated by the university colleges jointly - where interview flow is weighted higher than visualisation of the child's non-verbal language.
sig_a71b20277db6da2c6586.title: Tender with negotiation regarding the development of an AI-based simulation tool for training in child interviews

sig_a736a7b98d9c7ba008af.description: This PMEN is for the Business and Enforcement Operations (BEOps) Service in support of TfL's Road User Charging (RUC) programme. The new BEOps Contract will support all current RUC Schemes, any associated volumetric changes and may also need to make provision for future enhancements or developments that may be associated with RUC schemes, subject to due governance process. The scope includes the detailed design, development, configuration, integration, testing, and implementation of scalable IT systems and services for both Business Operations and Enforcement Operations. It encompasses ongoing continuous operation, support and maintenance of the systems and services, alongside data quality analysis and collaboration with other RUC and third-party suppliers. The service provider will be responsible for the operation of the end-to-end BEOps Service including: - Receive Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) data for processing. - Customer account management. - Discount processing. - Digital services. - Payment processing, reimbursement services and billing. - Event processing. - Provision of an enquiry and complaints service via various channels including telephone, webchat and digital. - Financial accounting. - Validating contraventions. - Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) issuing and processing. - Representations and appeals. - Debt registration and enforcement. - Claims and applications. - Service management. sig_a737d568f912d506e0a5.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) is IT specialist services for Energiavirasto. The subject of the dynamic purchasing system thus includes the following services, which are divided into two categories (sub-areas): 1) Development and maintenance work for Energiavirasto systems 2) Development and maintenance services for the Energiavirasto data processing environment Energiavirasto has case management systems for external customer service and internal work. In system development, Energiavirasto uses its own software development model and architecture (Energiavirasto Framework for Application Development, 'EFAD'). The systems are built in Microsoft Azure and M365 environments, for which we require experience from suppliers. The tasks include, for example, system definition, development, system modification work, continuous service maintenance tasks, security development, data migrations and interface service development. System developers, administrators and architects monitor and utilise public cloud services in the provision of services, with the main emphasis on the Microsoft Azure environment, but not necessarily limited to it. The goal of Energiavirasto is to acquire efficient, productive and high-quality competence and expertise for system development and maintenance work as well as other project-related tasks related to the subject of the procurement. The development work takes place in accordance with the delivery model of Energiavirasto, which Energiavirasto will specify in connection with each internal competition. As a general rule, the delivery model means that Energiavirasto is responsible for project management and the experts work under the management of Energiavirasto. Suppliers are required to have versatile evidence of competence in application development on the Microsoft Azure platform and maintenance of the environment in question. The systems of Energiavirasto are developed entirely in a serverless (PaaS) environment. A more detailed description of the required competence is provided in connection with each internal competition, and the areas of competence and their weightings may vary in internal competitions on a project-by-project basis. During the duration of the DPS, all interested candidates can submit an application to participate in it. There is no limit to the number of candidates that can be accepted into the DPS. This DPS is valid until the date stated in the contract notice. Energiavirasto has the right to suspend the dynamic purchasing system during its validity, close it temporarily or change its validity. Energiavirasto carries out procurements through internal competitions of the DPS. It is possible to conduct internal competitions throughout the duration of the DPS, starting, however, after the establishment phase. Internal procurements are put out to tender among the suppliers accepted into the DPS. Internal competitions may include one or more items. The items are defined in more detail in the calls for tenders. For one project or procurement of a service, expert services can be acquired from one or more suppliers according to the needs of Energiavirasto. Procurement contracts made on the basis of the DPS can in principle be valid for the duration of the DPS or for a shorter period. However, it is possible to agree on an option of up to 2 years in the contracts. Energiavirasto has estimated that the total estimated value of the procurement during the duration of the DPS is approximately 5 200 000 euros. Energiavirasto carries out procurements according to its needs. Energiavirasto is not committed to specific procurement volumes. The value of the procurement may also change. The development and maintenance work of the systems of Energiavirasto includes the maintenance and development of the individual systems, system development model and architecture of Energiavirasto.; The development and maintenance work of the data processing environment of Energiavirasto includes development and maintenance work on the IT platform used by Energiavirasto, which may relate, for example, to data security, technical solutions and the utilisation of services offered by the platform.
sig_a737d568f912d506e0a5.title: Maintenance and development work for the systems and data processing environment of Energiavirasto

sig_a742b435065b73a224b9.description: Kessel Run (KR) is responsible for developing, fielding, and operating mission critical warfighting applications in support of the U.S. Air Force. These applications need to be operationally available and mission capable 24/7/365 in highly contested environments. The Air Operations Center (AOC) Weapon System (WS) is a complex Command and Control system-of-systems comprised of diverse hardware, software, third-party applications, and web services, which require a comprehensive platform, infrastructure, and application integrations strategy. This strategy must address the complexities of maintaining, upgrading, and securing a heterogeneous environment while ensuring interoperability with other Department of War (DoW) systems. Leveraging Government Off-the-Shelf (GOTS) and Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions is a key tenet of the program to expedite integration and deployment. The AOC WS program office relies heavily on third-party providers for mission application development and sustainment. See attached files for additional information. Response Submittal: Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. Submit either by e-mail to rachel.sullivan.3@us.af.mil and tracey.toombs@us.af.mil or through the DoD Secure Access File Exchange (SAFE) website (https://safe.apps.mil/) to the same email addresses. White papers are due on the response date stated on this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the expense of the interested party. Format: White papers must be submitted in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) format, compatible with Adobe Acrobat Pro, and in 12-point font (smaller font may be used for figures and tables). White papers shall be limited to 8 pages including all figures, tables, and charts.

sig_a7617693f13f9726c07a.description: Climate change is impacting society already today and will have further consequences in the future. It is the objective of the European System of Central Banks to ensure stable prices, safe payments and financial stability within the European Union. To address any material impact on these objectives, that could arise from Environmental, Social and Governance factors, having quality data on ESG related variables is key. The scope of this EPCO Joint Procurement is the establishment of a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of Environmental, Social and Governance data to allow Danmarks Nationalbank, as well as the Eligible EPCO Members entitled to participate in it, to accomplish their daily business activities, regulatory and statutory tasks. The public procurement procedure will be carried out by Danmarks Nationalbank, as contracting entity and lead central bank, with the support of the Eurosystem Procurement Coordination Office (EPCO). The scope of this joint procurement includes the following scope of data (for further information see “Requirements” files part of the tender documentation): • Environmental data, including climate data, biodiversity data, water data, resources and circular economy, etc. • Social data, including diversity data, remuneration data, workers rights data, etc. • Governance data, including anti-competition data, company policies, board data, controversies data, etc. • Supranational data sets on EU Taxonomy, DNSH Principles data, SFDR PAIs data, UN SDG data, etc. • Generic data, including ESG Scores or ESG Derivatives data. • Provision of transparent methodology and sources. • Enablement of multiple parallel access point such as SFTPs, APIs, web platform, third party redistributors and Excel add-ins. • Appropriate usage rights for central banking activities and statutory tasks, as well as tasks for the Eligible EPCO Members. Furthermore, the central banks of the European Union manage large foreign exchange reserves and need a screening tool to easily screen its portfolios for compliance with ESG guidelines. The framework agreement will be non-exclusive, which means that the Eligible EPCO Members will have the option – but not the obligation – to order data from the future contractor(s).
sig_a7617693f13f9726c07a.title: Framework Agreement on the delivery of ESG data

sig_a771389125a44086a875.buyer_name: State Capital Potsdam, Procurement Management Division
sig_a771389125a44086a875.description:
The State Capital of Potsdam operates a central communications infrastructure based on the Alcatel-Lucent OmniPCX Enterprise (OXE) communication platform. It is pursuing the objective of modernising the existing communications infrastructure step-by-step and expanding it with contemporary unified communications and collaboration functionalities. The Rainbow platform from the manufacturer Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise (ALE) has been identified as the target platform. The subject of this procurement is the complete introduction, integration, migration, commissioning, documentation and maintenance of this target platform. In this context, the State Capital of Potsdam already has - 1.200 licences for Open Touch Conversation (OTC), which were discontinued by the manufacturer Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise on 31.12.2026. The existing OTC licences are to be factored in from OTC to Rainbow in accordance with the currently applicable migration conditions of Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise. The conversion of the existing system to ALE Purple on Demand using Cloud Connect is planned even before the expiry of the deadline for the submission of tenders. For this purpose, the State Capital of Potsdam already has 4.515 Voice Enterprise Users. In addition, the procurement provides for the connection of Rainbow via the remote extension. The current licence end date is 31.12.2027. The aim of the procurement is the introduction of a future-proof unified communications and collaboration platform (abbreviated as UCC) based on ALE Rainbow Hybrid. In particular, the following objectives are to be achieved: - Modernisation of the existing communications environment - Ensuring the investment security of existing OXE components - Improvement of cross-location collaboration - Support for hybrid working methods - Integration of mobile end devices - Provision of modern presence, chat and collaboration functions - Ensuring high availability - Compliance with information security and data protection requirements - Enabling a step-by-step migration without impairing ongoing operations The contracting authority intends to pay for the licences at the start of the term for the entire licence period (prepaid). Lot LOT-0001: Introduction of a Unified Communications & Collaboration platform based on Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise Rainbow. 2.1 Brief Overview The contractor must provide all services required for the complete introduction and operation of the target platform for a period of 48 months. These include: - Project management - Architecture and detailed planning - Delivery of required licences - Delivery of required system components - Installation and configuration - Integration into existing systems - Migration of existing users and services - Conducting tests - Training - Documentation - Commissioning - Manufacturer support - Maintenance and operational services 2.2 Integration into the Existing OXE Infrastructure The offered solution must be fully integrated into the existing Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise OXE infrastructure. This includes in particular: - Call control - Numbering plans - User management - Presence information - CTI functions - Switchboard functions - Contact centre functions - Mobile clients 2.3 Target State Upon takeover into regular operation, at least the following must be provided: - Rainbow user platform - Desktop clients - Mobile clients - Integration of the existing OXE infrastructure - Full administerability by the client - Integration of existing directory services 2.4 Demarcation Not subject to the contract are the provision, operation and maintenance of the telephone system operated by the client including the associated hardware, the local network infrastructure, the internet connection as well as the end devices. 3 Provision of the Rainbow Cloud Platform and Licences The contractor must provide all Rainbow licences required to implement the target architecture including all necessary system, administration and integration components. 3.1 Licences Licensing must enable the complete operation of the solution for the contract term. The offered licences must be suitable for operation within a Rainbow hybrid architecture. 3.1.1 Licences from Pilot Operation Licence type: Rainbow Enterprise Named User Planned quantity: 100 Licence period: 48 months 3.1.2 Licences from Production Start Licence type: Rainbow Enterprise Named User Planned quantity: 2.600 Licence period: 46 months 3.2 Optional Licence Increase The client reserves the right to optionally increase the licences during the contract term: 300 Rainbow Enterprise Named User licences. 3.3 Cloud Operation and Data Protection Requirements The Rainbow cloud platform is to be provided and operated in such a way that the processing of personal data within the scope of the procured services takes place in compliance with the applicable data protection requirements. The contractor must provide the client prior to commissioning and during the contract term with all information required for the data protection assessment and secure operation of the cloud components. 4 Project Services 4.1 Project Phases The contractor must carry out the following project phases jointly with the client for the introduction of the Rainbow platform: Project phases 1) Project initialisation 2) Architecture and detailed planning 3) Implementation and system integration 4) Test and validation 5) Pilot operation 6) Training 7) Rollout and production start 8) Hypercare 9) Regular operation 4.4 Takeover of the Results of the Proof of Concept The basic installation of ALE Rainbow as well as the delivery and provision of a WebRTC gateway has already been implemented by the client as part of a Proof of Concept (PoC). The results of the PoC must be taken into account as binding.

The technical decisions made within the framework of the PoC must be adopted by the contractor into the implementation planning. 5 Implementation and System Integration 5.1 Scaling WebRTC Gateway 5.2 User Management and Integration of Existing Directory Services and Identity Management 5.3 Mobile Clients and Flexible Workplaces 6 Training 6.2 Administrator Training 6.3 Key User Training 6.4 Training Documents 7 Transition to Regular Operation 7.1 Test and Validation 7.2 Pilot Operation 7.3 Production Start 7.4 Hypercare 8 Documentation 8.2 System Documentation 8.3 Final Documentation 9 Operating and Service Services 9.2 Maintenance Services 9.3 Incident Management 9.4 Service Desk 9.5 Service Level Agreement 9.6 Manufacturer Support 10 Services on Demand 10.2 Integration Contact Centre 10.3 Integration CTI Solution 10.4 SBC and Carrier Integration 10.5 Mobile Device Management 11 Suitability Requirements for Tenderers 11.1 Manufacturer Authorisation At the time of submitting the tender and during the contract term, the tenderer must be an authorised business partner of Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise and be listed under the following link: https://www.al-enterprise.com/de-de/partner-locator 11.2 Personnel Qualification The designated project manager must have at least three years of project experience in the field of UCC systems. At least one deployed specialist must have demonstrable Rainbow certification (ACFE OXO Connect). The corresponding certificate is to be submitted after the award of contract. A detailed description of the aforementioned service components is not possible due to limited display options. Therefore, the relevant contents are to be taken from the service description.

sig_a7785a91c8d10c18b5d8.description: The Universitätsklinikum Münster intends to procure a web-based software solution for the digital instruction management of medical devices. The objective is the fully digital recording, administration and evaluation of device instructions including legally compliant and audit-proof verification in accordance with the Medical Devices Operator Ordinance (MPBetriebV). The solution is to map the instruction processes of the UKM without custom programming, provide a matrix view of personnel, device types and instruction status (including recording and management of requirements) and enable the mobile recording of instruction proofs including the digital submission of signatures. Requirements for integration: Personnel master data is transferred daily from the SAP system of the UKM into the new system; the interface is unidirectional, no data flows back into the SAP system. From the CAFM system waveware, the master data of the medical devices including the dates of the next metrological and safety-related inspections (MTK/STK) must be available in real time. Authentication takes place via a central directory service, authorisation within the application. Documented standard interfaces (REST API) are expected. Operation can take place as a cloud solution or as a solution within the corporate network of the UKM. If a cloud solution is offered, an exit strategy with regular data export, a data protection concept and a security concept must be presented; data storage must take place within the EU. As part of the market sounding, a solution is to be identified that fulfils the requirements, particularly with regard to functional scope, integration capability, security level and cost-effectiveness. Interested providers will receive the detailed requirement documents upon request. Please send your expression of interest to the following address: vvgm@ukmuenster.de
sig_a7785a91c8d10c18b5d8.title: Market sounding for the introduction of software for digital instruction management of medical devices

sig_a77be16deeba86dbfbd4.description: Background Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council's Commissioning Team is exploring the potential development of an Independent Living Skills App for young people living in supported accommodation and those preparing to move into independent living. The concept has evolved from previous work undertaken to develop an Independent Living Skills Workbook. Feedback gathered through engagement with stakeholders indicated a preference for a digital solution, with an app being viewed as a more engaging, accessible and interactive way of supporting young people to develop essential life skills. The proposed app could include content relating to daily living skills, health and wellbeing and tenancy rights and responsibilities and is intended to be a mixed model of engagement through guidance, learning and self-development. The Council is currently undertaking soft market testing to understand the opportunities, constraints and indicative costs associated with developing such a solution before determining any future procurement approach. Purpose of Market Engagement:- The Council wishes to engage with organisations that have experience in app design, development and implementation, particularly those with experience in: • Youth and children's services • Housing and supported accommodation services • Educational and skills development applications • Public sector and local authority projects • User-centred and co-produced digital solutions Feedback gathered through these engagement sessions will help inform future decision-making and procurement considerations. The Council has identified a potential funding opportunity to support this work and is undertaking market engagement activity to better understand the feasibility, costs, technical requirements and delivery timescales associated with developing such a solution. Supplier feedback will help inform the Council's assessment of what may be achievable within the funding and implementation timeframe available. Areas for Discussion:- A discussion paper containing further information and specific questions will be circulated to organisations in advance of the engagement sessions, however the Council is seeking feedback in the following areas: • Potential approaches to app development and delivery • User engagement and accessibility considerations • Data protection, cyber security and information governance considerations • Hosting and technical requirements • Ongoing maintenance and support arrangements • Indicative development and implementation timescales • Licensing options and commercial models • Indicative costs and budget considerations • Key risks, dependencies and lessons learned from similar projects Market Engagement Sessions:- Individual engagement sessions will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams. Sessions will last up to one hour and will be allocated on a first come, first served basis.
