sig_a95342db16dd8aa49d8e.description: WM5G Ltd is seeking to procure a configurable Digital Discharge Service (DDS) Workflow solution to support the coordination of hospital discharge-to-home pathways across NHS partner organisations. The solution will provide a single operational platform through which WM5G Ltd staff can manage referrals, patient workflows, consent, tasks, communications and service performance, replacing fragmented processes that currently rely on multiple supplier systems and manual administration. The procurement covers the software platform, implementation, integration, hosting, training, support and maintenance required throughout the contract term. The solution will act as the operational orchestration layer for the wider DDS service, providing a unified view of patient journeys while integrating with existing Home Readiness, Remote Monitoring and Asset Management services. It is intended to improve the efficiency, scalability and governance of discharge services while maintaining clear accountability and visibility across multiple organisations and care settings. The platform must support the complete discharge workflow, from patient identification and referral through triage, enrolment, discharge preparation, discharge, monitoring and completion. Core capability areas include referral and onward-care management, workflow and task management, consent management, reporting and analytics, administration and role-based access control, standards-based integration, and data quality management. WM5G Ltd has defined a mandatory high-level architecture that suppliers must conform to. The solution must support API-first integration, HL7 FHIR interoperability standards, UK cloud hosting, strong identity management and secure integration with external systems. The architecture is designed to support rapid onboarding of new customers and providers while minimising operational complexity and vendor lock-in. The authority's desired outcomes are improved patient flow, reduced discharge delays, better patient and carer experience, reduced administrative burden, improved operational oversight, higher data quality and a platform capable of scaling across multiple regions and thousands of patients. Compliance with NHS and regulatory standards, including DCB0129, DCB0160, DTAC, DSPT, Cyber Essentials Plus and UK GDPR, is mandatory. Contract award will be based on the Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), assessing suppliers' ability to meet both the mandatory architectural requirements and the operational outcomes defined within the Requirements Compliance Matrix. For this plant, an AVEVA PI System of a maximum of 1.000 measurement signals (tags) and 10 users will need to be set up during the pilot project. sig_a9656848e995cc6fb6d9.description: The HUS Group requests tenders for family pedigree software solution mainly for the Clinical Genetics Unit. The procured software must be an on-premises, ready-to-use solution installed and operated within HUS-managed infrastructure and environment. The scope of the procurement includes software licences, implementation services, and related maintenance and support services required for the operational use of the software. The software will be used on a daily basis by approximately 20 to 30 users mainly within the Clinical Genetics Unit, including both physicians and nurses. In addition, a small number of users from the cardiology specialty will use the system. The family pedigree software is a critical tool in the Clinical Genetics Unit's daily operations. Information concerning almost all patients and families treated by the unit is recorded in the software. The Clinical Genetics Unit receives approximately 150 to 200 patient visits per week. The information stored in the software is of long-term clinical significance. When new patients from previously recorded families contact the Clinical Genetics Unit, often after several years, access to historical family data is essential. Therefore, reliable data preservation, availability, and retrievability are key requirements of the procurement. Laboratory system integration may be procured as an optional service and implemented as separately ordered expert work at the hourly expert rates specified in the Pricing Appendix. The subject matter and requirements of the procurement are described in detail in the call for tenders and its appendices.
sig_a9656848e995cc6fb6d9.title: Family Pedigree Software Solution

sig_a9965518a1e3593529c8.description: Identification of a service provider to carry out the functional design and technical implementation of an AI-based care solution for non-communicable diseases for the project "EVIGAIN 2025". 3.1 Type of service The subject of this procedure is the award of a contract for the functional design and technical implementation of an AI-based care solution for non-communicable diseases to improve patient care in the field of non-communicable diseases. Details can be found in the contractual documents. In preparation for this procurement procedure, the contracting authority (CA) has already created the content components and an MVP. These components form the basis for the technical implementation by the contractor (CO). For the functional design and technical implementation, a standalone backend must be provided as an API service (container-based), which handles authentication/authorisation, multi-tenancy, audit logging, data access, and the orchestration of AI functions (in particular RAG). The interfaces must be documented as a versioned REST API including OpenAPI/Swagger specification. Secrets must not reside in the frontend at any time. The source code must be provided via GitHub and operated using CI/CD (build, tests, security scans, deployment). During implementation, current requirements for applicable data protection regulations must additionally be taken into account, in particular those of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Data Protection Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (DSG NRW), and the Act on Data Protection and the Protection of Privacy in Telecommunications and Telemedia (TTDSG). The contractor must also observe these requirements when processing personal data in connection with the solution. This also includes, in particular, the conclusion of a data processing agreement with the contracting authority in accordance with Article 28 GDPR, insofar as this is legally required. The accessibility requirements in accordance with BITV 2.0 as well as the Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue - C5 (basic criteria) current at the time of contract conclusion must also be observed and implemented. It is intended to conclude an EVB-IT (IT Contracting Terms) creation contract and an EVB-IT cloud contract with the future contractor, on the basis of which the services are to be implemented. 3.2 Scope of service 3.2.1 Scope of service The scope of the service comprises in particular the partial services and tasks listed below: (a) Agile project management (sprint organisation, maintenance of product and sprint backlogs), (b) Further development and creation of software, (c) Documentation and handover, (d) Care and maintenance services, (e) Operational and support services, (f) Provision of specialised personnel, (g) Services in connection with the end of the contract

sig_a9b4b7d8e8d7f2cbb89a.description: Provision of a parking register system - The subject of the public procurement is the provision of an IT system related to the operation/support of public fee-paying parking spaces (parking spaces) within the Contracting Authority's area of jurisdiction under a works contract, and its operation for the duration of the contract; and the provision of other related services, as well as the provision of equipment necessary for the performance of the parking operation service. Provision of a parking register system - The subject of the public procurement is the provision of an IT system related to the operation/support of public fee-paying parking spaces (parking spaces) within the Contracting Authority's area of jurisdiction under a works contract, and its operation for the duration of the contract; and the provision of other related services, as well as the provision of equipment necessary for the performance of the parking operation service. SUBJECT OF PUBLIC PROCUREMENT: 1. On the one hand, the task of the successful Tenderer is to provide the "Parking Register System" IT system providing the parking operation service (transparent and continuous record of individual parking, parking control events, related data, photographs, payments, deadlines, correspondence, complaint handling, collections, receivables portfolio, as well as data on payment orders, court proceedings, enforcement proceedings), and its operation for the duration of the contract. 2. On the other hand, the task of the successful Tenderer is to provide the IT equipment and background capacities necessary for operations (servers, routers, communication channels). 3. Furthermore, the expected task of the successful Tenderer is the further development (enhancement) of the developed/set up IT system according to the Contracting Authority's ad hoc requirements, for which service the Contracting Authority determines a framework amount of net 15.000.000 HUF for the entire duration of the contract. The Contracting Authority undertakes a call-off obligation for 75 % of the further development framework amount. MAIN QUANTITATIVE DATA OF THE PUBLIC PROCUREMENT: - The maximum number of concurrent users to be supported by the business system on the part of the Contracting Authority is 30 (thirty) persons. Within the framework of the background customer service, the expected volume of complaint handling cases is 30.000 (thirty thousand) per year. - As a related service, provision of training on the use of the IT system provided by the successful tenderer for a maximum of 2 occasions per month and for a maximum of 15 persons per occasion. The monthly level of on-site or premises training is a maximum of 10 hours/month. - As a related service, provision of remote desktop access service for at least 15 persons. The Technical Requirements document found among the procurement documents details the contracting authority's technical expectations regarding the IT system. In order to ensure equal opportunities for tendering, the Contracting Authority does not require tenderers to possess the software according to the Technical Requirements at the start of the procurement. The Contracting Authority has determined the time limit for performance taking this into account, providing the opportunity for economic operators who do not yet possess the software according to the Technical Requirements at the start of the procurement to submit tenders, but who are capable of developing it.

sig_a9c400aa1d1ef48a090b.description: The NZa wishes to replace the current on-premise environment with a modern, cloud-based and modular information supply based on Software as a Service (SaaS). The continuity of the technical management of the current environment is no longer guaranteed after the expiry of the existing management agreement, making timely go-live of the new Solution necessary for the continuity of the business-critical, primary processes of the NZa. The desired Solution consists of three coherent yet separate lots: a Case System, a Document Management System (DMS) with records management functionality, and an omnichannel solution for consolidating customer contact. With this, the NZa aims to support case-oriented working, file formation, archiving and customer contact via multiple channels in an unambiguous and structured manner, with a sustainably accessible and reliable information management system tailored to the processing of sensitive personal data. The core of this tender is the new case system, with which the NZa works case-orientated. See documents; When handling cases, the NZa processes many documents. This includes both documents sent by e-mail, for example, and physical documents arriving via the scanning facility. A DMS is required for keeping and managing information in a proper, orderly and accessible state.; The NZa has customer contact via multiple channels: e-mail, telephony, online forms and chat. In order to ensure that we can serve our customers optimally, it is important to consolidate information from these various channels. An omnichannel solution should provide a solution here.
sig_a9c400aa1d1ef48a090b.title: Case System, DMS and Omnichannel Solution

sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.description: The subject of the procurement is the development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, evaluation and monitoring of funded projects. Hrvatska zaklada za znanost (HRZZ) as the Contracting Authority, is the central national organisation for the funding of scientific, higher education and technological programmes and projects in Croatia. Every year, HRZZ announces a series of calls for proposals to support scientific research, thereby ensuring stable funding for research groups engaged in internationally and/or nationally significant scientific issues that create new knowledge and improve existing knowledge through basic, applied or development research. In order to ensure the selection and funding of the best projects, HRZZ has developed a project proposal evaluation procedure based on the internationally accepted practice of peer review, in which scientists from Croatia and abroad participate. The procedure for applying to HRZZ calls for proposals, the evaluation and selection of project proposals, and the monitoring of the implementation of contracted projects takes place via the Electronic System for Project Submission and Monitoring (hereinafter: EPP system). In this regard, the existing EPP system was developed in 2011. and has been upgraded several times over the years. The total server space it currently occupies is ~720 GB. The total number of active registered users in the system is 21.875, while on an annual basis about 7.000 users in various roles and 30 HRZZ employees work with the system. However, following the above, it is necessary to build a new modular system that the Contracting Authority can independently adapt to the type of call for proposals, the type of evaluation procedure and the involved users. The system must allow the Contracting Authority to select from predefined elements those that will be used in a specific call period (e.g. criteria for checking applicant eligibility, cards or forms that the user fills out, mandatory fields, documentation for uploading, etc.). Following the above, a detailed description of the subject of procurement is contained in the Technical Specifications document, which forms Appendix I to this Procurement Documentation.
sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.title: Development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, management and monitoring of funded projects

sig_a9d09892f266587515a3.description: In accordance with Government Decision (H.G.) No. 592/2024 on the organisation and operation of the Ministry of Justice, as subsequently amended and supplemented, the MJ draws up public policies, strategies and action plans in the field of justice, the prevention and combating of corruption and serious forms of crime, including in accordance with the objectives of the governing programme, and negotiates, implements, monitors and evaluates international technical and financial assistance programmes for the prevention of crime and corruption, regardless of the beneficiary institution or the one implementing them. Currently, the Ministry of Justice provides the legislative IT application legislatie.just.ro, a website dedicated to both individuals and legal entities. The purpose of the platform is to facilitate public access to official information on normative acts issued by Romanian state institutions, thereby contributing to legislative transparency and a better understanding of the legal framework in force. The general objective consists in modernising the legislatie.just.ro legislative platform, in order to ensure legislative transparency, accessibility and a better understanding of the national normative framework by citizens and interested institutions. The modernisation of the IT platform will contribute to: – Facilitating public access to official information through an updated, secure and efficient technological infrastructure. – Increasing the quality and efficiency of digital public services by aligning with European standards and improving the end-user experience. – Optimised interconnection with European legislative portals (e.g. N-Lex), thereby supporting integration into an international legislative network. – Increasing the number of users and traffic on the legislative platform by implementing modern functionalities that meet current requirements. The impact of the modernisation is complementary to other initiatives of the institution aimed at digitising and making public services more efficient. Clarifications schedule: Requests for clarifications shall be transmitted via the SEAP portal at www.e-licitatie.ro. Deadline for receiving requests for clarifications: 21 days before the deadline for submitting tenders in SEAP. According to art. 161 of Law No. 98/2016 as subsequently amended and supplemented, to the extent that clarifications are requested in good time, the contracting authority's response to these requests shall be published in S.E.A.P on the 11 day before the deadline set for the submission of applications/tenders. Responses to requests for clarifications shall be published in S.E.A.P. by the contracting authority in a single stage, without disclosing the identity of the person who requested the clarifications. The specific objectives of the procurement target the modernisation of the legislatie.just.ro legislative platform, so that it meets current performance, accessibility and security requirements, ensuring an optimised user experience and facilitating legislative management. The implementation of the solution will follow a modular, scalable and secure architecture, complying with European interoperability and accessibility standards. In order to achieve the objectives established by the purchaser through the documentation, stages/activities have been structured in the Specifications as follows: 1. Activity No. 1 (A1)- Project management activities; 2. Activity No. 2 (A2)- Detailed analysis and design activities; 3. Activity No. 3 (A3)- Software component development and testing activities; 4. Activity No. 4 (A4) -Environment installation and configuration activities; 5. Activity No. 5 (A5)-Transition activities to the new system and migration of existing data; 6. Activity No. 6 (A6)- Warranty and support activities. The technical requirements requested by the Purchaser can be found in Section II - Specifications, part of the tender documentation.

sig_aa2ac4620658140f3853.description: Data collection for the Information System on the Road and Motorway Network of the CR (ISSDS CR) is organised by the Road Databank Department and NDIC Ostrava. This involves continuous and uninterrupted collection of data for the construction activity register (RSČ), road inventory description (PPK), junction description (PK) and pavement structural layers (KV). Suppliers of this service also provide methodological assistance to individual road property managers (ŘSD CR Administration and Workshops, district and regional road authorities), quality control of data for road inventory descriptions, junction descriptions, pavement structural layers, and maintaining their up-to-date status. The delivery of the required data is a highly specialised activity that takes place concurrently in time across individual regions, which is why it is not ideal to carry it out from a single centre. The activity further requires detailed knowledge of the monitored roads in the given region, systematic activity, long-term training, regular training courses, experience in data collection, and last but not least, special equipment and modification of the measuring vehicle. Data from the aforementioned activities will be used, inter alia, for the planned and gradually implemented pavement management system (PMS). The CR is divided into 7 reporting regions as follows: 1. Central Bohemia Region. 2. South Bohemia Region. 3. West Bohemia Region 4. North Bohemia Region. 5. East Bohemia Region. 6. South Moravia Region. 7. North Moravia Region. Out of these 7 reporting regions, 5 regions will be tendered this year, in which existing contracts expire in the year 2023: 1. Central Bohemia Region. 2. North Bohemia Region. 3. East Bohemia Region. 4. South Moravia Region. 5. North Moravia Region. North Bohemia Region. It consists of the districts of: Mladá Boleslav, Česká Lípa, Děčín, Chomutov, Jablonec n/N, Liberec, Litoměřice, Louny, Most, Teplice, Ústí n/L and Semily;

The network will provide a wealth of data for monitoring and better understanding geodynamic phenomena taking place in the wider area of the southeastern Mediterranean Multiparametric reference seismological stations; Ocean bottom seismographs (OBS); Reference strong ground motion stations; Vertical array of accelerographs in boreholes; Borehole tilt meters and Floor mount tilt meters; Geochemical station for measuring soil gas emissions; Portable biogas analyser; Heavy-duty core drilling system; Seismological and geophysical data analysis software; Uninterruptible power supply (UPS) devices

sig_aa474e4a12a2a9f8d1ee.description: Define a single integrated system to manage risks, audit actions, controls and assurance activities aligned to UKSBS governance, ISO27001, CAF and Government Standards. UK Shared Business Services (UKSBS) is seeking to understand the market for a Risk Management and Assurance system that can support enterprise-wide governance and compliance aligned to ISO27001, CAF and wider Government standards. The intended solution should provide a single, integrated platform to manage risks, controls, audit actions and assurance activities, supporting a Three Lines of Defence model and enabling a clear, consistent view across team, directorate and corporate levels. The system should facilitate risk identification, scoring, escalation and linkage to strategic objectives, alongside the ability to define and monitor risk appetite, including automated identification of breaches. The solution is also expected to support end-to-end assurance processes, including audit and action tracking, control management, compliance mapping, and evidence handling, with robust reporting and dashboards to support both operational management and Board-level governance. Key considerations include configurability, usability, integration with existing tools, and strong security and access controls. Overall, UKSBS is seeking a scalable and user-friendly solution that reduces manual effort, improves visibility of risks and controls, and strengthens organisational assurance and decision-making Lot 1: .

sig_aa7ec166aa9f05539ff0.description: The Arts Data Bank is a gross financed department under the Ministry of Climate and Environment. Artsdatabanken is considering announcing a tender for an external review of the IT portfolio. We would like to discuss with the market whether the descriptions of the assignment seem recognisable in the market and how costly such an assignment is. The market dialogue will be held through a digital meeting Wednesday 14 May 0900-1000. The draft for the notice will be sent as registered at the latest on Monday 11 May. After the meeting, five 30 minute meetings have been set aside with individual tenderers. Registration for an individual meeting can take place at the same time as register for the market dialogue. Individual meetings will be awarded on a first come, first served principle. Registration shall be sent by sending an email to the postmottak@artsdatabanken.no. The Arts Data Bank has, via the Digitalisation Council, received a recommendation to carry out an external review of the IT portfolio. • What does it cost to manage and further develop the different systems? • Where can you have internal operational advantages by thinking about consolidation and reuse? We would like an as-ice mapping of the technical solutions, with a focus on cost picture in money and personal resources, and technology/architectural choices. Are there changes we can make to be better rigged for the future? The majority of the systems in the portfolio are developed by the Arts Data Bank. We envisage that the following deliveries from an external supplier can be useful: • Mapping the services in the cloud infrastructure. I.a. visual overview of our services, with connections and dependencies between them. • An assessment of technical choices for infrastructure and cloud systems. • An assessment of infrastructure costs and what we can possibly do to reduce costs • A calculation of the development costs? • An assessment of resource use for managing the portfolio we have • Plan for liquidation of services that have been decided to discontinue or have been assessed for liquidation. • Assess vulnerability connected to the choice of cloud suppliers connected to security problems. The Arts Data Bank invites potential suppliers to a dialogue on how the procurement can best be arranged. Central themes we would like dialogue around include — o If the notice is sufficiently detailed in order to submit a tender. o Whether the frame of the notice is realistic. o If the evaluation criteria facilitate fair competition.
sig_aa7ec166aa9f05539ff0.title: Market dialogue - Review IT portfolio

sig_aa84add878faeca1f0f9.description: Short description The contracting authority wishes to expand and enhance IT security and data backup as a particularly vulnerable target for cybersecurity. For this purpose, software and hardware are required that guarantee recovery following a cyberattack. A measure is therefore to be procured that protects the contracting authority's existing system, particularly with regard to virus scanning and data backup. In this respect, a solution is to be implemented that enables rapid and efficient reconstruction in the event of a cybersecurity-relevant attack. The focus is on the protection of particularly sensitive and critical data (e.g. patient data). In this context, it is essential to isolate attackers, restore systems cleanly, minimise downtime and ensure business continuity. Description of the procurement (nature and scope of the service or indication of needs and requirements) This specification concerns software and hardware, as well as a cybersecurity solution for backup, which serves to expand the IT security and data backup of the University Hospital Mannheim. The solution is a vulnerable target for cybersecurity and data backup. For this purpose, software and hardware are provided as a solution for data recovery after a cyberattack. In particular, attackers are kept at bay, systems are restored cleanly, downtime is reduced and business continuity is guaranteed. The contracting authority in its current form is the result of a merger of many companies that digitise future-proof enterprises and support their business success with detailed IT know-how and innovative software development. The cybersecurity solution consists of secure hardware and innovative software and guarantees the highest level of security. The physically isolated appliance, the immutable file systems and the end-to-end encryption offer comprehensive protection against potential attacks. These security features ensure that no one has unauthorised access to the data or systems. The cybersecurity solution makes it possible to protect critical data in the event of a cyberattack. It has the ability to isolate the attacker and restore the systems cleanly, ensuring that no serious difficulties are encountered. Through this solution, downtime can be minimised and business continuity ensured. The cybersecurity solution works exclusively with hardware appliances. These appliances offer protection of data in hardware. The desired retention period for backup data is (always) part of a backup job. This retention period is adopted when writing the data to the appliance - data that has been written once cannot be deleted or changed for this period. Furthermore, it permanently pulls signatures of malicious software via a BSI portal and maintains an internal database for known malicious software. During data backup, it is checked in real time whether the data to be backed up is infected. When used, existing hardware is not quarantined. Accordingly, existing hardware can be put back into operation promptly. 1. Cyber security in the recovery process: The subject of the contract enables rapid and effective reconstruction in the event of a cybersecurity-relevant attack. The focus here is on the protection of sensitive information and data. In the event of a cyberattack, the attacker is isolated and a clean recovery of the systems is guaranteed. 2. 24/7 Customer support and integrated team: The contracting authority has a highly qualified team. This team is available around the clock and guarantees rapid and efficient data recovery in the event of a cyberattack. The seamless integration of this team ensures rapid and competent support. 3. Hardware and software security: The holistic solution consists of secure hardware and innovative software and guarantees the highest level of security. The physically isolated appliance, the immutable file systems and the end-to-end encryption offer comprehensive protection against potential attacks. These security features ensure that no one has unauthorised access to the data or systems. Bunker-in-a-Box: Security-by-Design, immutable file system, physically isolated appliance (hardened Linux, no shell access) with scale-out performance, end-2-to-end encrypted, NTP protection, retention lock, not detectable on the network. Ransomware monitoring: Immediate areas of impact of an encryption attack and the data affected therein - also at VM level - are detected. Threat hunting: Threats are identified and a clean recovery point in the backup is found without alerting a potential attacker, using hashes, patterns or YARA rules. Sensitive data discovery: The proactive reduction of the attack surface is achieved by understanding which data might be of interest to attackers. Orchestrated recovery: The commissioning and testing of the required processes is automated. This determines which applications or infrastructure areas require how long for a recovery. Commvault backup infrastructure consists of: - 4 disk libraries (total 600 TB storage) - 1 tape library (6x LT0-7, 160 slots) Daily backups are made of 800 VMs (approx. 500 TB) plus Windows File Services (approx. 100 TB scope of the contract award SW, HW, service and provision of services
sig_aa84add878faeca1f0f9.title: Expansion: Cyber Security solution in backup/ IT security and data backup

sig_aa9b4c97623d5777369b.description: The UK Global Screen Fund (UKGSF) is designed to boost international development, production, distribution, and promotional opportunities for the UK’s independent screen sector. It targets support across the screen sector, including film, TV, documentary, animation and interactive narrative games content. It is aimed at boosting the international competitiveness of UK screen content whilst growing the revenues, reach and partnerships of domestic independent businesses. The UK Global Screen Fund Framework for Promoting UK Screen Services consolidates all screen sector promotional activities under one combined ScreenUK umbrella. It encompasses the current ScreenUK Industry physical UK screen sector presence at international festivals and markets such as Cannes Marche du Film, Berlin European Film Market (EFM), Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) and Annecy International Animation Festival, as well as the digital presence of both ScreenUK Industry activity and the ScreenUK consumer promotional campaign. The BFI requires Service Provider(s) to deliver the UK Global Screen Fund Framework for Promoting UK Screen Services in the following Lots: Lot 1 – Events and Logistics Services (£1,616,100) Lot 2 – Creative Assets Services (£460,500) Lot 3 – Media Agency Services (£854,451) Lot 4 – Digital Promotion and Production Services (£705,000) Total value of Framework = £3,636,051 across all Lots Framework Duration – 3 years. Any option to extend this Framework for an additional year will be subject to additional funding being secured prior to the expiry of this Framework. The Framework Award(s) will be subject to the final approval from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sports (DCMS) Lot 1: Lot 1 – Events and Logistics Services. Project management and delivery of the physical ScreenUK Industry presence (in the form of a stand/booth/pavilion) at up to four key international festivals and markets such as eg Cannes Marche du Film and Berlin EFM. This includes fit-out, build, décor, staffing, technical delivery, freight and logistics. Additionally, full management and delivery of ScreenUK consumer events, to be further scoped but likely to include the continued delivery of the ScreenUK Studio at the British Independent Film Awards. Lot 2: Lot 2 – Creative Assets Services. Project management and delivery of creative assets, executing the ScreenUK brand strategy across both physical and digital channels and across both B2C and B2B activity. This includes the design of UK stand/booth/pavilions at key international festivals and markets as well as year-round digital campaign assets plus ongoing design, development and hosting of the ScreenUK and ScreenUK Industry platforms. Lot 3: Lot 3 – Media Agency Services. Project management and delivery of ScreenUK paid media planning, buying and campaign delivery and optimisation, with a focus on digital channels. sig_aa9bf871720f9c6c88a4.description: The Assignment comprises the supply, implementation and support of a new Energy Management System (EnMS) for the Universiteit Leiden. A well-functioning Energy Registration and Monitoring System (EBS) forms an integral part of the EnMS solution. An EBS is legally required for the majority of buildings. The EnMS solution must therefore comply with the applicable guidelines as established by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO). With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to have a scalable, future-proof and securely configured SaaS solution that unlocks reliable energy information and provides support for legal obligations, financial processes and sustainability objectives. The EnMS acts as the primary system for long-term storage, management and analysis of the Contracting Authority's energy data. The EnMS must integrate in a robust and traceable manner with existing systems and data sources of the Universiteit Leiden and be suitable for data exchange within the existing information provision. The Assignment consists of the following components: the supply, implementation and support of an EnMS as a SaaS solution, the supply of monitoring services focused on data quality and continuity, the supply of additional functionality modules and dashboards (optional). There is no purchase obligation for component 3. The Contracting Authority wishes to be able to purchase modules and dashboards optionally and separately from each other according to use during the term of the Agreement. Whether or not the full offering of component 3 is provided does not constitute grounds for exclusion. The extent to which the functionality of the requested modules and/or dashboards is offered will, however, be taken into account in the quality assessment of the tender.

Kick-off meeting • Conducting a kick-off meeting with the technical agency (Lot 2) for the handover of designs and specifications under the leadership of the JLU. Continuous support • Provision of support and clarification of open questions during technical implementation. • Coordination and cooperation with the JLU and the technical agency (Lot 2) within the framework of the agile project procedure. Project management Project planning • Agreement between contractor and client on a joint project procedure involving agile methods • Joint creation of an agile project plan in the form of an initial product backlog with the associated planning parameters (for example sprints, milestones and deadlines) Communication and reporting • Conducting workshops at the JLU for the participatory development of design and layout. • Regular communication with stakeholders and reporting on project progress.

Quality management • Ensuring the quality of the delivered designs through reviews and tests of the JLU Accessibility and data protection-compliant operation Requirements for the project team For the implementation of the web relaunch project, the client expects an experienced and interdisciplinary project team. sig_aac4251745c9d32957be.description: Please note: this is not a call for tenders, a contract notice or a prior information notice, but a notice of the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. The City of Helsinki Urban Environment Division (hereinafter KYMP) has initiated the preparation of the 4/26 procurement and invites service providers to participate in a market dialogue. KYMP is surveying solutions available on the market based on Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) for mobile parking enforcement. The subject of the procurement is an ALPR camera system, which consists of: • ALPR cameras to be installed in a vehicle and related peripheral equipment • a back-end system for the cameras (e.g. analytics, management and reporting user interfaces, interfaces) • possible cloud services and/or local system components The system must be capable of: • automatically reading vehicle registration numbers in urban traffic • identifying vehicles that are in violation of parking regulations (e.g. unpaid parking, incorrect parking, exceeding time limits) • producing information in real time or near real time to support parking enforcement The primary intended use of the system is to improve the efficiency of: • paid parking enforcement • incorrect parking enforcement Possible other uses may include: • supporting the enforcement of vehicle removal operations • producing situational and monitoring information related to parking and traffic flows • collecting guidance and analytics data concerning parking behaviour The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement, the solution alternatives available on the market, and various implementation, licence and service models. Through the market dialogue, KYMP wishes to obtain insights from service providers to support the preparation of the future competitive tendering, including the definition of the subject of the procurement, potential procurement models and the key content of the contract. Written material will be sent to those registering for the market dialogue for comment. The written material will be sent to those who have registered for preliminary review during the spring of 2026. In addition, KYMP reserves the possibility to discuss the details of the tender competition to be organised with the service providers registering for the market dialogue. We request service providers interested in participating in the market dialogue to register by 31.5.2026 to the address kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi. Please head your registration message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu -ALPR-kamerajärjestelmä". At the same time, please provide the name and contact details of your contact person whom we can contact. The market dialogue and the information provided therein do not bind any participating party, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tender competition later. If the procurement is proceeded with, the official call for tenders will be published no earlier than during the year 2027. No compensation will be paid to the participating companies for responding or participating. Responses will be treated confidentially.
sig_aac4251745c9d32957be.title: Invitation to market dialogue: ALPR camera system

sig_aac8b06940b4b8525bad.description: Background Region Värmland (Regionservice) has a need for system support for cleaning time calculations, resource scheduling, cleaning area optimisation, follow-up and statistics, receiving extra orders and visual support for employees to be able to see the day's work area based on a coloured drawing on their mobile or tablet in real time. Need Regionservice has a need to utilise drawing documentation within the framework of facilities management. The region is now facing a procurement of a new digital planning, quality and follow-up system for facilities management (cleaning system) where access to drawing documentation is a prerequisite. Drawings may contain sensitive information and therefore guidelines are needed to ensure that the information does not end up in the wrong hands. Many so-called A-drawings are not assessed individually as sensitive information, but taken together, all drawings result in the sensitivity increasing. The information security classification for drawing documentation is therefore assessed as sensitive information corresponding to K3. Purpose The purpose of introducing system support is to achieve consolidated management and to coordinate and streamline processes within facilities management. This includes calculation of cleaning time, resource scheduling, optimisation of cleaning areas, follow-up and statistics, receiving extra orders, up to the employee physically being able to see the day's work area and extra orders based on a coloured drawing on their mobile or tablet in real time. The system support must have a user-friendly interface and management both in the administrative parts carried out via computer and also in the app. The system must also offer visual support for employees by showing the day's work area on a coloured drawing in real time via mobile/tablet, contain instructions and governing documents, report deviations in delivery and receive extra orders.
sig_aac8b06940b4b8525bad.title: Digital planning, quality and follow-up system for facilities management

The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary for the development of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Number of days before which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for submission of tenders/applications 18 days. The contracting authority will clearly respond to requests for clarification on the 11-th day before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. NOTE: The contracting authority is not obliged to respond to requests for clarification/additional information that have not been addressed within the established deadline. Forest management services for the Lunca Timisului Forestry Office - DS Timis, with an area of 9.388,78 ha; Forest management services for the Timisoara Forestry Office - DS Timis, with an area of 10.921,49 ha

sig_aafec3bc82d1f24961f9.description: The subject of the procurement is an electronic resident appointment booking software service (hereinafter Software Service). The Software Service enables service users to book, cancel, reschedule and confirm appointments in accordance with national development, as well as to view booked appointments (including proxy services). The comprehensive services of the appointment booking system will be expanded Itä-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue to primary health care, oral health care and social services. Itä-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue electronic appointment booking has been in use in limited services, but now that the region has moved to using only one supplier's customer and patient information system entity (Tieto / Lifecare), the service is intended to be expanded. Appointment booking functionalities are intended to be introduced in primary health care, oral health care and social services. Electronic appointment booking is intended to free up professionals' time from the telephone, as well as to streamline the customer's service experience, as appointments can be booked regardless of time and place. The estimated value of the procurement, excluding VAT, calculated in accordance with the Public Procurement Act for the contract period, including the software service, implementation, expert services and options, is 600 000,00 euros (€). The contract period is fixed for two (2) years, after which it will continue until further notice.
sig_aafec3bc82d1f24961f9.title: Procurement of an electronic appointment booking system for social and health services

sig_ab668499e223ace79d4b.description: As a producer of the highest-quality food and drink, the vast majority of which is exported around the world, Ireland has developed robust and integrated systems governing its agriculture (including aquaculture) and food. In areas like food safety, traceability, animal health and welfare, productivity and breeding, sustainability and innovation, Ireland’s government-sponsored services are world-class. Sustainable Food Systems Ireland (SFSI) is a consortium of public bodies that are responsible for the agriculture (including aquaculture) and food sectors in Ireland. Covering diverse technical and skills domains, SFSI is charged with developing long-term relationships internationally based on the transfer of Irish knowledge, expertise and technologies, in support of the development of safe, secure and sustainable value chains in agri-food. The SFSI consortium members are: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine Teagasc - The Agriculture and Food Development Authority Food Safety Authority of Ireland Bord Bia - The Irish Food Board Enterprise Ireland SFSI consortium members can co-operate internationally using a variety of inputs: • expertise in project and programme design • government-to-government advice • delivery of technical assistance • organisation of training and study tours • project and programme monitoring, reviews and evaluation • impact evaluation • creation of financing models for industry support. SFSI consortium membership provides expertise to support partner governments and organizations globally in the following areas: • formulating agricultural (including aquaculture), food and marine sectoral policy, strategies and programmes • building regulatory systems and institutional capability • strengthening food safety at all stages of the supply chain • protecting standards of animal health and welfare and expertise in veterinary services • systems for animal identification, registration and movement control • traceability in the food chain • establishing and improving research and innovation in agriculture (including aquaculture) and food • knowledge transfer, agricultural education and extension services and systems • establishment of producer groups and co-operatives • developing and embedding sustainability programmes at primary and processor levels • SME development and company funding support systems • export promotion in food or commodity sectors • creation and marketing of national or regional brands The Executive Team of SFSI undertakes business development, project preparation and delivery, project management and administration and coordination activities on behalf of the Consortium Members and is the point of contact for overseas clients - governments, agencies and other organisations. The Team can negotiate participation in international food, agriculture (including aquaculture) and rural development projects through direct business development activities and through engaging in open and restricted tenders on behalf of the Consortium members. The SFSI Executive team is a Unit of the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine and oversees the administration of this DPS including External Expert appointments on behalf of the Consortium Members. The consortium members will use existing/internal staff resources to provide services. However, they require external experts to supplement the existing resources where necessary. sig_ab73eda5d0f43a62657a.description: Subscription licence for cyber attack recognition and advanced defence system The subject of procurement is the procurement of a cyber attack recognition and advanced defence system. The system must have the capability to actively monitor a minimum of 2500 IP addresses (users, servers and devices) and enable automated detection and protection against malicious activities on the network, system and user infrastructure. The system should enable manual, semi-automated and automated levels of protection. The system should accept a capture of all network traffic and, using supervised and unsupervised deep learning (DL) methods, enable the recognition of not only external but also internal threats originating from the organisation by monitoring lateral communication that does not pass through the firewall. The system should be sized for monitoring network traffic for a minimum of 2500 unique IP addresses. The tenderer shall install hardware components (physical devices) at locations according to the contracting authority's instructions, depending on the type of traffic the device must collect. The hardware components will be located in the IT network (business network) and will inspect and analyse all network traffic at the primary and secondary locations. The hardware component will be installed at the contracting authority's primary (Prisavlje 14, Zagreb) and secondary locations (Krležin Gvozd 1a, Zagreb). The supplied services include hardware warranty, new software versions, security patches and the like, as well as manufacturer support for error analysis on the system. Upon expiry of the service, the hardware and software shall be returned to the supplier.
sig_ab73eda5d0f43a62657a.title: Subscription licence for cyber attack recognition and advanced defence system

sig_ab7ac730170057b7a5e5.description: The purpose of this update is to publish the Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) for the Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS) Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP). Please review the attached document titled "AWS_RPP_Official_QandA" for the Government's responses to all received industry questions. As confirmed in the Q&A, the deadline for proposal submissions remains 01 October 2026 at 16:00 Eastern Time (ET). All other terms, requirements, and submission instructions in the solicitation remain unchanged. 1.0 Overview The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC), on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground, Project Manager Maneuver Medical Systems (PM M2S), is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit prototype project proposals for a modernized Anesthesia Workstation System (AWS). This RPP is issued pursuant to the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. § 4022. This is a DIRECT OTA and is NOT a solicitation for a procurement contract under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Consortium membership is not required to respond to this RPP. 2.0 Mission Need & Scope The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) anesthesia workstation system capable of supporting life-saving medical operations in austere environments at Role of Care (ROC) 3 with little to no modification. The system must overcome the capability gaps of legacy systems, specifically regarding interoperability with Army Oxygen Generation Systems, heavy logistical footprint (weight), and proprietary maintenance constraints. The Government intends to award one (1) OT Agreement for the delivery of two (2) prototype units. These units will undergo rigorous operational testing by the Medical Test and Evaluation Activity (MTEAC) and environmental testing conducted in accordance with MIL-STD-810H. Proposed solutions must be FDA-cleared for human use and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant. A high priority for this effort is organic supportability. The Government strongly prefers systems designed to be maintainable by military Biomedical Equipment Technicians (BMETs) at the Field and Depot levels without reliance on proprietary vendor service contracts. 3.0 Follow-On Production Authority In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), this OT Agreement is issued with a provision for follow-on production. Upon successful prototype completion and validation, the Government may award a follow-on production contract or OT Agreement for approximately one hundred and eighty (180) AWS units without further competitive procedures. 4.0 Proposal Submission Instructions All proposal instructions, technical specifications (CODS and APAs), and evaluation criteria are detailed in the attached Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) document. Questions: All questions must be submitted in writing via email to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialist no later than 15:00 ET on 17 September 2026. Proposals: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email no later than 16:00 ET on 01 October 2026. Communications: Unauthorized contact with program office personnel or technical end-users regarding this RPP may result in disqualification. All communications must be directed to the points of contact listed below. Attachments The Final RPP Document (which includes Appendix E) The Standalone ADRL Document Attachment A (The blank TAA Certificate) Attachment C / OTA Articles Points of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Timothy Compton Agreements Officer Email: timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil Secondary Point of Contact: Roxanne A. Dalrymple Agreements Specialist Email: roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil

sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.description: The objective of the Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI) program is to advance scientific discovery and innovation by enhancing the security and privacy of cyberinfrastructure. CICI supports efforts to develop, deploy and integrate cybersecurity that will benefit the broader scientific community by securing science data, computation, collaborations workflows, and infrastructure. CICI recognizes the unique nature of modern, complex, data-driven, distributed, rapid, and collaborative science and the breadth of infrastructure and requirements across scientific disciplines, practitioners, researchers, and projects. CICI seeks proposals in four program areas: 1. Usable and Collaborative Security for Science (UCSS): Projects in this program area should support novel and/or applied security and usability research that facilitates scientific collaboration, encourages the adoption of security into the scientific workflow, and helps create a holistic, integrated security environment that spans the entire scientific cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. 2. Reference Scientific Security Datasets (RSSD): Projects in this program area should leverage instrumented cyberinfrastructure to capture metadata from scientific workflows and workloads as reference data artifacts that can help support reproducible security research, testing and evaluation. 3. Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience (TCR): Projects in this program area should improve the robustness, trustworthiness, integrity, and/or resilience of scientific cyberinfrastructure through testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and technology transition of novel cybersecurity research. The TCR area further encourages transition activities that advance the deployment and use of reproducibility in CI, workflows, and data. 4. Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data (IPAAI): Projects in this program area should enhance confidence and reproducibility in AI produced scientific results by improving the integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific datasets used by Artificial Intelligence systems.
sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.title: Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI)

sig_ab833bc159e77ba9fab6.description: Open Source Software: MOOSE: The Multiphysics Simulation Powerhouse The demand for versatile, powerful simulation tools in scientific computing and engineering has never increased. Enter the Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment (MOOSE), a state-of-the-art finite-element framework that promises to revolutionize how researchers and engineers approach multiphysics problems. Developed by the prestigious Idaho National Laboratory, MOOSE emerged from a need to tackle complex, real-world scientific challenges with precision and efficiency. Traditional simulation tools struggled with the nonlinear complexities inherent in multiphysics problems, leading to the development of MOOSE, which leverages advanced nonlinear solver technology to offer unmatched computational capabilities. MOOSE provides a high-level interface that simplifies the complexity of multiphysics simulations. Its core features include a fully-coupled, fully-implicit multiphysics solver, dimension-independent physics, automatic parallelization for large-scale simulations, and modular development for code reuse. With built-in mesh adaptivity and Continuous and Discontinuous Galerkin methods, MOOSE is designed to be both powerful and intuitive, ensuring researchers can focus on their work without getting bogged down by the intricacies of the simulation software. Advantages: Streamlined Multiphysics Simulation: Tackle complex problems with a fully coupled, implicit solver. Scalability: Effortlessly scales to over 100,000 CPU cores for large-scale computations. Flexibility: Dimension-independent physics and ~30 pluggable interfaces cater to various scientific disciplines. User-Friendly: An intuitive API and flexible GUI simplify the user experience from setup to execution. Advanced Features: Continuous and Discontinuous Galerkin methods, mesh adaptivity, and parallel multiscale solves. Applications: Engineering Analysis: Design and validate engineering solutions across various disciplines. Scientific Research: Conduct sophisticated physics, materials science, and beyond research. Energy Sector: Optimize renewable energy integration and nuclear reactor simulations. Environmental Studies: Model ecological impact and sustainability measures. Embark on a journey of discovery and innovation with MOOSE. sig_ab8ccc5bcfcfb00ac105.description: Oulun kaupunki, the Corporate Management invites you to submit a tender for IBM Planning Analytics on Cloud (PA) support, maintenance and development services (IT expert services), (hereinafter also referred to as "Subscribers") in accordance with this call for tenders and its annexes. IBM Planning Analytics on Cloud (PA) is a financial planning system procured as a cloud service from IBM, which is used to produce, among other things, the City of Oulu rolling forecast and budget. Financial planning utilises planning models built into the system, such as HR planning, investments and depreciation, as well as the financial planning of early childhood education, basic education and upper secondary schools. In addition, the system is used to produce financial data reporting for the State Treasury's financial data service for municipalities and wellbeing services counties. Data on finances and operations transferred from various source systems is used in the calculations. The system is widely used throughout the city organisation, with approximately 180 users in 2025. Technical expertise required for support, maintenance and development services: - IBM Planning Analytics on Cloud - IBM Planning Analytics Workspace / Workbench - IBM Planning Analytics for Microsoft Excel - IBM Cognos Command Center - IBM Satellite Connector - SQL Server databases Support and maintenance services mean the advice, orientation, problem-solving, implementation of service requests and other similar activities (including necessary documentation) relating to the IBM Planning Analytics on Cloud (PA) financial planning system provided by the Supplier to the Subscriber's designated persons and the Subscriber's IT system team. The Supplier shall provide expert services regarding subject areas related to PA technology, the operating environment and end-user tools, as well as bug fixing and updates for the system and the implementation of update requirements arising from the technical platform in cooperation with the Subscriber's main users and the IT system team, either performed by the Supplier or, in respect of PA, in such a way that the Supplier acts towards the holder of the PA rights (IBM) by forwarding and coordinating service requests and the like and delivering the service. The service also includes analysing the impact of version and patch updates on the Subscriber's environment and informing the Subscriber. The Supplier shall monitor and supervise the functionality of the system and report problems to the Subscriber. Development services mean development and expert services related to PA technology, the operating environment and the system, separately ordered by the Subscriber and provided by the Supplier, directed at existing models. In addition, for example, the planning of development pathways and the planning, specification and implementation of new functionalities and features. Before the approval of the deliverables of the Development Service, the object of delivery shall be tested and it shall be ensured that it meets the requirements. The object of the delivery must be completed on the agreed schedule. The Supplier must test the functionality in accordance with the requirements before delivery for the Subscriber's acceptance test. The Supplier's delivery must include, if required by the Subscriber, a test plan, test records/results, design documentation, software presentation/demo and user instructions, as well as the Software itself (executable and professionally commented source code). Actual development work shall be carried out on the basis of separate assignments within the contract. In the implementation of support and maintenance services and development services, the Supplier shall take into account the entire existing implementation and the impact of changes on other existing implementations. The Subscriber undertakes no commitment to procure any minimum quantity of services that are separately ordered and invoiced.
sig_ab8ccc5bcfcfb00ac105.title: IBM Planning Analytics on Cloud (PA) support, maintenance and development services (IT expert services)

If such a change proves mandatory during the term of the contract, it shall be carried out at the contractor's expense under the contract, and this shall not affect the SCADA/EMS software of the control system. All other activities that are the subject of the contract shall be carried out seven days a week, between 08:00 and 22:00, following the submission of a request by the Contracting Authority to the email address, fax number or telephone number specified in the bid. sig_abfaec7577f8533b5648.description: The TechFirst Women’s Programme is a UK Government workforce‐development intervention designed to increase the participation, retention and progression of women in high‐growth digital and frontier‐technology sectors. Evidence shows that women remain structurally under‐represented across the UK tech workforce, facing systemic barriers including biased recruitment practices, limited access routes, inflexible working patterns, and poor workplace cultures. At the same time, employers—particularly SMEs—are experiencing severe digital skills shortages across key frontier‐technology roles, including AI, cyber security, advanced connectivity, semiconductors, quantum technologies and engineering biology. These labour‐market failures are constraining innovation, productivity and regional growth, and disproportionately impact businesses unable to access or train technical talent. The programme will procure a women‐focused training and deployment model delivering employer‐aligned technical instruction, workplace‐readiness training, wraparound pastoral support, and structured mentoring. This will enable a target of 300 women to progress into meaningful entry and mid‐level roles in frontier‐tech sectors. Training will be co‐designed with employers to ensure alignment with real occupational needs in areas such as software engineering, cyber security, data engineering, cloud/DevOps, AI/ML operations and telecoms/network engineering. The programme should reduce the cost burden on SMEs, helping them to participate in the digital economy and adopt emerging technologies that would otherwise be inaccessible due to recruitment and training costs. The programme sets a target of 80% demployment into mid-career roles, and 20% deployment into early-career roles. The deployment phase will match participants to paid, high‐quality technical roles, with pathway support throughout onboarding and early retention. Delivery partners may deploy a contingent‐workforce approach, ensuring employment decisions into permanent roles remain open, merit‐based and compliant with the Equality Act 2010. The programme sets a target for 80% of deployments to SMEs, with flexibility where regional or sector‐specific SME demand is insufficient. This SME‐first approach strengthens regional innovation ecosystems and ensures benefits flow to the parts of the economy facing the most acute hiring barriers. The expected benefits of the programme include increased representation of women in frontier‐tech roles; improved retention through structured mentoring and culture‐focused employer support; expanded domestic early‐career pipelines; enhanced SME digital adoption; and reduced reliance on international recruitment for mid‐career tech roles. By addressing systemic inequality and market failure, the TechFirst Women’s Programme delivers a targeted, evidence‐based intervention that strengthens the UK’s technology workforce, boosts regional economic resilience, and supports long‐term productivity growth. Lot 3: Creative Engagement. Providing services that focuses on engaging pupils and learning through creative activities. Services may include but are not limited to, music, art, drama and dance. Lot 4: External Tutors - Additional Support. Providing services where external personnel offer additional support to pupils on a group or one to one basis. Services may include but are not limited to; resilience coaching, speech and language therapy, literacy and maths champions and Nurture support. Lot 5: Pupil workshops. Providing services that engages pupils on a particular subject, activity or project through discussion, performance or participation in class(s)dedicated to the project or activity. Services may include but are not limited to mindfulness, yoga, confidence building, nutrition, diversity, health and wellbeing (physical and mental). Lot 6: Parental Support & Family Learning. Providing services that engage with parents and families to provide support to increase involvement in the pupil’s learning. Services may include, but are not limited to, parental engagement workshops, leadership training, one to one sessions. Lot 7: Community Engagement. Providing services that focuses on engaging pupils, parents/carers and the wider community in learning and will build and develop local capacity. Services provided should draw on existing interventions and community programmes to build a stronger local community based on local needs and aspirations. Lot 8: Mentoring. Providing a service that focuses on the support and encouragement of pupils to manage their own learning in order that they may develop their learning skills, improve their academic performance and maximise their potential. Services may include, but are not limited to, additional support with academic studies, coaching, youth work and support and mentoring programs Lot 9: Leadership for Pupils. Provide services that will develop leadership and team working skills in pupils of all ages and abilities across the local authority. Lot 10: Educational leadership. Providing support and assessment materials primarily in the areas of Literacy, Numeracy and Health and Wellbeing. Services may include, but are not limited to, standardised and diagnostic assessment and screening tools. Lot 11: Educational Assessments. Providing support and assessment materials primarily in the areas of Literacy, Numeracy and Health and Wellbeing. Services may include, but are not limited to, standardised and diagnostic assessment and screening tools. Lot 12: Developing the Young Workforce. Providing services that will assist schools in developing skills for learning, life and work in children and young people in the broad general education, particularly for those young people with barriers to learning and at risk of disengaging from education early. Services may include but are not limited to work-related learning experiences and involvement with families or employers. Lot 13: Out of School Clubs. Providing services that provides a regulated club that offers a safe environment for children outside of school hours. Clubs often include the provision of food and some activities or social element. These may include but are not limited to breakfast, after school and holiday clubs. Lot 15: Miscellaneous Services. This lot will provide for any service that does not easily fall into any of the categories above e.g., Pet Therapy, Bee Keeping, Massage-in-Schools

sig_ac0e10b74e0ba72d034f.description: This notice is a request for information and an invitation to market dialogue, not a procurement notice or a call for tenders. Suppliers are not expected to submit tenders in response to this notice. Provincia Oy is a service centre owned by municipalities and wellbeing services counties, which produces high-quality and cost-effective HR and financial management services for its owner-customers. Together with our system partners, we offer our customers the most modern and efficient financial and HR management system solutions on the market. We are preparing the procurement of a modern comprehensive financial planning system produced as a SaaS service, with which our customers can handle, in addition to versatile budgeting and forecasting operations, also e.g. the planning of their projects and investment ventures. We are not looking for a mere data entry form, but a system that integrates into our operating environment, streamlines our customers' entire financial planning process and minimises manual work as much as possible. In addition, our hope is to be able to utilise artificial intelligence to support financial planning. With this notice, we invite suppliers to participate in market dialogue, the purpose of which is to clarify the details related to the subject of procurement and the requirements. In this way, we are able to carry out the procurement in the most appropriate manner possible. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The financial planning system to be procured must support the entire budget and financial planning process all the way from basic data definition to budget drawing up, changes, forecasting and monitoring. The planning process proceeds in stages and continues throughout the budget period. The system must enable the management of the budget and operating plan, supplementary budgets and budget changes, as well as the drawing up of forecasts and alternative scenarios in such a way that the integrity of the official budget is maintained. Planning must enable monthly budgeting that can be updated flexibly and regularly during the budget year based on outturn and forecasting. In addition, budgeting must be possible on a rolling basis. Budget data must be comparable with outturn and the system must also support data transfer and validation in accordance with existing accounting structures. As a whole, the objective of the system is to enable continuous, controlled and comparable financial planning throughout the budget period, while taking into account the individual roles and needs of our customer organisations of various sizes. In addition to the system itself, the procurement will include implementation projects, system maintenance services, integration development and testing work, and support services intended for the service centre's technical superusers, such as incident and change management services and necessary training. A more detailed description of the requirements related to the system can be found in the request for information's appendix 1 "Preliminary requirements". These requirements are intended as an opening for discussion and they will evolve during the dialogue. The contracting authority reserves the right to use or not to use the requirements, pricing models, procedures, contract terms, schedules or other similar details related to the procurement raised during the request for information and market dialogue. SCHEDULE AND PROGRESS OF THE PROCUREMENT The plan for progress and scheduling is presented in appendix 2 "Estimated procurement schedule". The market dialogue will be held during May-June in such a way that written material will be circulated for comment to all suppliers who have registered to participate, and in addition the contracting authority may, at its own discretion, invite suppliers to hold separate general-level demo sessions via Teams. The publication of the actual procurement notice and call for tenders will settle for August according to the estimated schedule. According to current information, the procedure to be used will be an open procedure. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Please declare your interest in participating in the dialogue by 18.05.2026 at 15:00 at the latest with a free-form email to the address hankinnat@provincia.fi and attach to your email the document "Questions to suppliers" which is appendix 3 of this request for information, filled in. You may also, if you wish, attach a general presentation of your company and your product to the email. Title your message "Market dialogue: financial planning system". APPENDICES Appendix 1 – Preliminary requirements Appendix 2 – Estimated procurement schedule Appendix 3 – Questions to suppliers
sig_ac0e10b74e0ba72d034f.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Financial planning system as a SaaS service

Lot 1: Dental Consumables & Appliances. This Lot provides dental consumables and appliance-based solutions designed to support the delivery of routine and specialist dental care across primary, community, and secondary care settings. These products include single use and repeat use materials, small appliances, and consumable items required for preventive dentistry, restorative procedures, orthodontics, minor oral surgery, anaesthesia, and infection control. The scope includes consumables and all associated accessories, where applicable, required to support safe, effective, and compliant dental treatment. Lot 2: Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. This Lot covers specialist clinical systems, implantology and orthodontic products, as well as bespoke dental laboratory appliances and restorations manufactured to individual patient requirements. It covers powered systems, procedure kits and software enabled treatment solutions that support diagnosis, planning and delivery of specialist dental care. The scope includes devices and all associated equipment, accessories, consumables (where part of a system), maintenance, software, technical support and training. Additionally, it covers the provision of patient specific and bespoke restorations. Lot 3: Operatory Equipment. This Lot provides dental operatory equipment used for routine chairside patient care within dental treatment environments. It includes dental treatment units, delivery systems, operating lights, handpieces, micromotors, ultrasonic scaling systems, mobile treatment carts and associated operatory infrastructure, including suction systems and compressors. This Lot excludes specialist clinical systems used within defined endodontic, implantology, orthodontic and oral surgery workflows, which fall within the scope of Lot 2 – Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. Lot 4: Dental Laboratory & Digital Solutions. This Lot provides digital dentistry and laboratory solutions spanning the design, manufacture and finishing of dental restorations and appliances, and supports associated digital workflows. It includes CAD/CAM systems, scanners, milling units, 3D printers, sintering furnaces, laboratory equipment and materials. The scope includes equipment and all associated accessories, installation, maintenance, software, technical support, training and, where applicable, validated workflows. Lot 5: Dental Imaging & Diagnostics. This Lot includes both ionising imaging systems (e.g. X-ray, CBCT) and non-ionising diagnostic imaging devices (e.g. intraoral cameras and scanners). It includes intraoral x-ray units, OPG/cephalometric systems, CBCT, digital sensors/PSP systems, intraoral cameras and diagnostic imaging software. The scope includes devices and all associated equipment, accessories, installation, acceptance testing, maintenance, software, technical support, integration and training. Lot 6: Dental Environment, Decontamination & Practice Building. This Lot provides environmental, furniture and fit-out solutions for dental surgeries and decontamination areas. It includes clinical cabinetry and furniture, ergonomic surgery design/refurbishment, decontamination room furniture and workflow systems, and supporting clinical infrastructure components associated with dental environments. The scope includes supply, installation, and, where applicable, design support, project services, maintenance and training. Lot 7: Mobile Dental Clinics & Equipment. This Lot provides mobile dental treatment environments and portable operatory solutions designed to deliver care outside fixed clinical premises. It includes mobile dental vans, trailers and self-contained pods, as well as portable dental chairs/units and field dentistry kits. The scope includes units and associated equipment, installation/commissioning (where applicable), accessories, maintenance, technical support, training and documentation.
