sig_ac75bcf93de2fa4af4b2.description: North Hertfordshire District Council (NHDC) is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement to inform a future procurement for the replacement of its existing Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC) platform supporting the Herts Careline service. The ARC forms a critical component of the Council’s telecare infrastructure, providing 24/7 monitoring and response capability for vulnerable residents and partner organisations. The current platform is approaching technical and contractual end of life and requires replacement with a modern, secure and resilient solution capable of supporting both legacy analogue alarm traffic and the transition to digital telecare technologies. The purpose of this Preliminary Market Engagement is to obtain market insight and supplier feedback to support the development of a proportionate, transparent and competition-friendly procurement strategy in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. The engagement will explore supplier capability across a range of areas including: - Availability of ARC platforms capable of supporting hybrid analogue and digital alarm protocols - Migration approaches from a live operational ARC environment with minimal service disruption - Alternative delivery models including on-premise, private cloud and fully managed platform solutions - Integration capability with telephony, CRM, field service and related operational systems - Platform resilience, disaster recovery and cybersecurity capability - Commercial models, lifecycle cost drivers and approaches to managing supplier lock-in - Scalability and interoperability to support future shared service arrangements and Local Government Reorganisation - Opportunities for innovation, automation and operational efficiency improvements - Sustainability and social value considerations within platform delivery and hosting models. NHDC uses an E-Tendering system (In-Tend) for all procurement activities, including Preliminary Market Engagement (PME). Suppliers must submit their responses via the Supply Hertfordshire Portal at: Supply Hertfordshire Electronic Tendering Site https://in-tendhost.co.uk/supplyhertfordshire/aspx/Home - You must be registered on the portal to submit a response. - If already registered, use your existing username and password. - A password reminder link is available on the homepage if required. For technical difficulties, please contact the In-Tend Helpdesk at 0845 557 8079 or support@in-tend.com This engagement is strictly for information gathering purposes and does not constitute a call for competition or commitment to procure. Insights obtained will be used to refine the specification, procurement approach, contract structure and evaluation methodology while ensuring equal treatment of suppliers and avoidance of any unfair competitive advantage. DESCRIPTION The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) intends to issue a Full and Open Competitive Solicitation (N00024-26-R-5246) for the development, production, integration, testing, fielding, and lifecycle sustainment of the U.S. Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System (ECDIS) Hardware and Software. This procurement supports PEO IWS 6.0 Navigation Program requirements for both surface and subsurface platforms. The resultant contract will provide continued production and sustainment of Navy ECDIS Hardware and Software. Hardware Scope: Includes production, sustainment, integration, assembly, and testing. Software Scope: Includes maintenance, modification, upgrades, integration, testing, and delivery of ECDIS software products. These software scope activities will be provided as level-of-effort tasks under Government oversight, with technical support from the Navy ECDIS Systems Engineering and Integration Agent, NSWC Philadelphia, PA. Award is anticipated in Q4 FY27 and will be made to the Offeror whose proposal represents the Best Value to the Government in accordance with FAR 15.101?1. The planned contract structure includes one base year with four one?year option periods, beginning in FY27. Deliveries are anticipated to be FOB Destination. 2. BACKGROUND The Navy ECDIS is fielded on all U.S. Navy ships and submarines as the Navy’s primary navigation plotting system. It integrates inputs from multiple sensors to provide accurate ship positioning and ensure safe navigation. Historically, these requirements were fulfilled under two separate contracts: Software development: N00024?18?C?5216 Hardware production: N64498?21?G?4003 This solicitation consolidates both into a single competitive procurement. 3. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) will be made available on Sam.gov no later than 31 July 2026 and will be provided to all interested parties who request access per the instructions in the attached “ECDIS DRAFT Solicitation Document Access” form. Industry feedback is strongly encouraged and will be considered during preparation of the final RFP. The Government intends to require electronic proposal submission exclusively through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module at https://piee.eb.mil. Offerors are strongly encouraged to ensure their organization has an active PIEE account and that the Proposal Manager role is approved prior to the Final RFP release. A vendor registration guide for obtaining access to the PIEE Solicitation Module is posted at: https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/solicitation-module. 4. Access Control Notice While the Draft RFP and the Final RFP will be posted publicly and be available to all interested parties on SAM.gov, access to the controlled Final RFP attachments and the Government’s Offeror’s Library will be restricted. Only those business entities formally identifying and bidding as a Prime Contractor will be granted access to these controlled RFP attachments and the Government’s Offeror’s Library. Subcontractors and lower-tier vendors must obtain any controlled Final RFP attachments or access to the library directly through their respective prospective Prime Contractor. 5. DISCLAMER This Pre?Solicitation Notice is issued for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as an invitation for bid, request for quotation, or Request for Proposal. It does not obligate the Government to award a contract or authorize negotiations. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs will arise from responses to this announcement. All industry comments and questions submitted in response to this notice may be treated as public information and may be posted on SAM.gov. The Government does not commit to responding to comments or questions. Any revisions to RFP documents based on industry feedback remain solely at the Government’s discretion. No inquiries shall be made to any Government personnel other than the points of contact identified in this synopsis.

sig_acf1a9a17d273256b03e.description: The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is undertaking an additional round of market engagement activities in order to inform the market of the revised timeline and route to market for the Consular Core Platform Delivery Partner requirement. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) leads the UK’s diplomatic, development and consular work around the world, working in over 250 Posts across the globe. The objective of the Consular & Crisis Directorate is to support British people overseas who find themselves in need or distress, and to help people avoid the need for our assistance in the first place. The Core Platform refers to FCDO’s Salesforce platform which hosts Consular’s case management and appointments booking systems. The new contract is likely to start in September 2026 and is anticipated to be for a duration of three (3) years, with an option to extend for additional two periods of 12 months, based on satisfactory performance provided by the selected service provider and continued business requirement by the FCDO. The intention is to call for competition under Lot 5 (Applications and Data Management) of the new Technology Services 4 (TS4) Framework Agreement (RM6190) that is due to go live in January 2026. We anticipate the call for competition commencing February 2026. Early Market Engagement invitations will be restricted to Suppliers who have been offered a conditional place on Lot 5 of CCS TS4. The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be restricted to Suppliers who have been confirmed as accepted onto Lot 5 of CCS TS4. Lot 1: .

sig_ad0260b8a808b1d30c29.description: The subject of the public procurement is delivery, commissioning, maintenance and payment processing of validators for validating journeys with payment cards, control devices, and software for the needs of „Trolleybus Transport“ EOOD - city of Pleven. The purpose of the public procurement is Delivery of Validators for validating journeys with payment cards and software for validating payments with payment cards and application programming interfaces for integration with a payment institution, fiscal system, and ticketing system. Delivery of control devices and software for control devices. Installation of equipment and software; implementation, provision of technical support and communication connectivity for the duration of the contract, assistance with integration with the systems of the Contracting Authority and third parties through the interfaces that are the subject of this procurement, as well as staff training – system administrators, inspectors, drivers and service personnel. Processing of cashless payments for the purchase of transport documents. The execution of the activities under the public procurement aims to improve public transport in the city of Pleven by realizing the possibility of using payment cards for travel in the vehicles of „Trolleybus Transport“ EOOD without the need for prior registration and purchase of a transport document. The control devices delivered in execution of the activities will be able to check payment cards in order to establish the regularity of passengers using payment cards for travel.

sig_ad104b7185757690110c.description: The subject matter of the public contract is the delivery, installation, configuration and commissioning of a multi-user virtual reality training system intended for the training of security forces. The system must enable the simultaneous engagement of five users within a single training scenario and must contain a central operator workstation. The entire solution, particularly in terms of hardware architecture, network infrastructure and licensing model, must be designed so as to enable its future expansion to ten simultaneously connected users without the need to replace basic system elements. The supplied solution must be conceived as a fully integrated functional unit, encompassing all hardware, software and network components necessary for its proper operation. The installation must be implemented in the form of a turn-key delivery, so that it is not necessary to carry out interventions in the contracting authority's existing infrastructure beyond the scope of pre-defined premises readiness. Further binding specifications of the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority's requirements and the conditions for its delivery are stated in Annex No. 1 - Technical Specification and in Annex No. 3 - Draft Purchase Agreement.

sig_ad14cbe4b5442a11acb6.description: This tender concerns the establishment of an agreement for the provision of Managed Detection and Response (MDR) services to DSB, aimed at supporting, strengthening, and further developing the contracting authority's overall cybersecurity capacity across the organization's IT and relevant OT environments. The purpose of the tender is to identify and contract with a supplier capable of delivering a cohesive, scalable, and mature service that integrates with DSB’s existing security organization, including the Security Operations Center (SOC), and complements it with advanced competencies, methods, and technological capabilities in monitoring, detection, analysis, response, and proactive security activities. The tender encompasses a comprehensive service delivery, which includes controlled and continuous monitoring of security incidents, structured and efficient handling of security incidents, access to dedicated resources for managing critical incidents, provision of qualified and contextualized threat intelligence, and execution of proactive analyses such as threat hunting. The delivery must comply with the requirements, service objectives, and other terms specified in the contract and its annexes.

sig_ad46cb92db7ae81b3329.description: The company operates a multitude of transport technology systems that interact constantly in a complex network. The functionality and availability of this system network is essential for the smooth operation of daily light rail and bus services. Against the background of increasing digitalisation, technical innovations, functional enhancements of software products and adjustments to IT infrastructure, as well as heightened IT security requirements, demands are growing for careful coordination, monitoring and tracking of measures and tasks within IT in transport technology. In order to meet these diverse challenges and ensure the secure operation of transport technology systems, the Dynatrace observability platform has been introduced, which safeguards the operational running of the transport technology systems. To ensure efficient integration into existing operational processes, the integration is to be accompanied by external specialist expertise. The primary objective is not to have the software operated by third parties, but to empower internal staff through targeted training and consulting and to build up competencies systematically. Internal system administrators should be able to deploy Dynatrace confidently and purposefully for monitoring critical services. sig_ad649a9b13f8e072d6ea.description: The Indian Health Service, Gallup Service Unit is issuing this sources-sought notice (SSN) to identify capable Indian-owned, economic enterprises – large (IEE) or small (ISBEE) – that can provide an around-the-clock interfacility transfer coordination service to identify placement options and coordinate transfers for acutely and critically ill patients to facilities with needed specialty care. The requirement covers services such as a transfer documentation platform, protocol design, reporting, and case management follow-up support. Other capable firms are also invited to respond to this SSN. The Contracting Officer will consider responses for Buy Indian Act (25 U.S.C. 47) opportunities first, then for set aside programs under the Small Business Act (41 U.S.C. 3104). The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this requirement is 621999, All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services with a small business size standard of $20.5 million. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. Information collected from this notice is purely for market research only and will be used to determine the contracting office’s acquisition strategy including competition, set asides, and locating Indian-owned economic enterprises. Submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary. The government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred in response to this request for information. In accordance with FAR 4.203-1(b), offerors and quoters must be registered in System for Award Management at SAM.gov, at the time an offer or quotation is submitted and at time of award. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this notice by October 8, 2026 at 3:00 pm MDT to Misty Billy at Misty.Billy@ihs.gov with the subject line “SSNGSU-001-2027”. Your submission must include the following information, at a minimum: Company Profile that includes: UEI, Name and Address, Primary POC information, business size and type of ownership, socio-economic status/participation such as 8(a), WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB and HUBZone, identification of Native American ownership, SAM.gov representations and certifications, and other related documentation. A brief statement of the company’s capability that relates to the described government requirement. Additional demonstration of capability may include current and past performance history for the same or similar requirement, established contracts such as GSA or VA Schedule, etc. Indian-owned Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) and Indian-owned Economic Enterprises (IEEs) must also submit a completed IHS IEE Representation Form (attached) in accordance with HHSAR 326.606-1(b). Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.
sig_ad649a9b13f8e072d6ea.title: Interfacility Transfer Coordination Services

sig_ad707603805a60059200.description: The Environment Agency (EA) is developing a new Waste Site Intervention Framework (WSIF) to ensure we can respond quickly and safely when high‐risk waste or landfill sites pose serious environmental or public‐health risks. These situations may involve illegal waste activity, abandoned sites, or unmanaged waste that could lead to pollution, fires, or other harm. The EA’s approach remains firmly grounded in the polluter pays principle. Responsibility for preventing pollution and managing waste rests with the operator, landowner, or depositor, and the EA will continue to pursue all reasonable steps to ensure responsible parties undertake or fund any necessary works. EA intervention is expected to occur only in exceptional circumstances where significant risks remain unresolved and the potential environmental or public‐health impacts justify EA involvement. To help shape a flexible and effective commercial model, we are seeking supplier feedback. The proposed Framework will provide rapid access to specialist services across England. The Framework is expected to cover three broad areas of work: Lot 1: Abandoned Landfill Management Lot 2: Waste Removal from Unpermitted or Abandoned Waste Sites (UAWS) Lot 3: Waste‐Related Technical Advisory Services Suppliers with relevant experience in any of these areas are encouraged to take part in this engagement to help shape the final commercial approach. Information on how to participate is set out below. Lot 1: .
sig_ad707603805a60059200.title: Waste Site Intervention Framework (WSIF)

Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government will not provide feedback. c. The US Geological Survey Acquisition Team (GSAT) is not, at the time, seeking proposals or quotes and will not accept unsolicited proposals or quotes. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurements. II. PURPOSE The DOI, USGS, Earthquake Science Center (ESC) is seeking a qualified firm to conduct a focused, independent code review of the ShakeAlert® Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Production System. The purpose of this RFI is to identify potential vendors capable of providing services required in the attached Statement of Work. The objective of this contract is to improve the reliability, maintainability, and long-term sustainability of the ShakeAlert production code base through two complementary activities: - A rigorous, module-by-module review of source code quality, correctness, and maintainability. - An assessment of current software development and deployment practices, with concrete recommendations for modernizing the CI/CD pipeline and GitLab workflow. In support of this effort, GSAT is conducting market research to further refine requirements and establish the best acquisition approach. Please note that requirements defined to date may change before issuance of a final RFP/RFQ. III. REQUIREMENTS See Statement of Work, 9 pages, attached. Task 1 - Production Code Review Task 2 - Software Development Practices and CI/CD Pipeline Interested parties shall include the following in their submission: 1. Applicable socioeconomic designation. 2. Business size standard. 3. SAM UEI number. 4. GSA contract number, if applicable. 5. Ability to execute all tasks listed. IV. RESPONSES Responses are requested by October 16, 2026 at 12:00pm PST. Any response received after these dates will also be considered but may not be included in initial reporting or assessments. All responses should be submitted electronically in PDF format and emailed to the points of contact: Charlan Fejarang at charlan_fejarang@ios.doi.gov. The subject line of the email should read as follows, ¿RFI: 140G0326Q0223 - ShakeAlert Production System Code Review.¿ Respondents must submit capability statements and information describing the general approach/solution to addressing the listed requirements. General marketing information or reference to vendor web sites will not be considered responsive to this notice. No telephone, mail, or fax responses will be accepted.

sig_ad7df07d41fda8c64aa9.description: The purpose of the contract is the provision of technical assistance and management services for the Technical Support Office for European Projects (OATPE) of the Provincial Council of Valencia. These services include specialised technical assistance and consultancy for the municipalities of the province, the Provincial Council of Valencia itself, as well as any public law entity in which a municipality participates where its role is relevant (hereinafter "key agents"). The projected contract is a service contract for the management and execution of a technical office dependent on the Provincial Council of Valencia, which will cover its need to assist and advise on the search, acquisition, and management of EU funds for local entities, promote the transfer of knowledge linked to European projects among technicians and elected officials of the province of Valencia, enable the submission of European projects in which the Provincial Council of Valencia is a partner or associate partner to the European Union, and bring Europe and funding programmes closer to and disseminate them to the local administration. The specialised technical assistance and consultancy service that is the subject of this contract will be carried out by the contractor from its own offices/facilities (by telephone, electronically, by email, and/or through the website of the Provincial Council of Valencia), and any member of the assigned technical team must also travel to the municipalities and territories that so require, as well as to the premises of the Provincial Council of Valencia.

sig_ad99b2d46431eabe0358.description: Flughafen Zürich AG, ICT division (“FZAG ICT”), is conducting the procurement of a centralised Endpoint Protection Platform (EPP) as part of an open tender procedure. The goal is the selection and implementation of a high-performance, scalable and requirement-compliant IT security solution for the comprehensive protection of all end devices within all network zones of FZAG ICT. This procurement is aimed at qualified providers (manufacturers and/or integrators) who possess demonstrable professional and organisational competencies to provide and implement an EPP solution that meets the IT security standards and operational requirements of FZAG ICT. Scope of end devices to be protected: - Windows clients and servers - Linux clients and servers - Windows IoT clients as well as selected OT systems - Mobile end devices (optional) Requirements for the EPP solution: - Provision in the Software as a Service (SaaS) operating model to minimise internal operational effort - Centralised management and monitoring of all end devices - High scalability and integration capability into existing FZAG ICT infrastructure - Fulfilment of defined technical, security and compliance specifications
sig_ad99b2d46431eabe0358.title: Endpoint Protection Platform (EPP)

sig_adc60af63ba1f8fe91e8.description: Maintenance, support and upgrade of Customs SEED+ and related customs digital systems. Customs SEED+ is a digital platform supporting the systematic electronic exchange of customs data and pre-arrival information between CEFTA customs administrations, and between CEFTA and participating EU Member States through the Green Lanes initiative. The platform supports data exchange, risk management, trade facilitation, monitoring of crossing point performance, and the implementation of common customs cooperation tools. The contract will also support interoperability with local customs systems and related CEFTA systems, gradual alignment with the new Union Customs Code framework and related EU customs data exchange requirements, as well as further development of customs risk management functionalities and support for the recognition of customs controls, including common risk profiles, rapid customs alerts, inspection report data exchange, AEO-related functionalities, statistics and reporting, where relevant.
sig_adc60af63ba1f8fe91e8.title: Customs SEED+ Maintenance, Upgrade and Risk Management Support

sig_adc69c18cd3d0c3473ac.description: As part of this procurement subject, the delivery of licence renewals and maintenance services for the analytical database (hereinafter referred to as CDUDB) is expected. The analytical database (CDUDB) is a platform intended for data storage within the data platform and data lake project and forms the main backbone for the storage of structured data and its processing. The CDUDB platform is installed in an 'as a service' format as a 'multi-tenant' platform intended for users of the CDU platform for building business decision-making systems. CDUDB is a solution that enables massively parallel processing (MPP) databases with an architecture specifically designed for managing large analytical data warehouses and business intelligence workloads. CDUDB is installed on a hardware platform that is part of the CDU infrastructure, and this procurement subject does not contain hardware equipment. As part of the licence delivery, it is necessary to offer an appropriate quantity of licences based on processor cores for all used software components of the solution and their activation. As part of the maintenance services, it is necessary to offer corrective and preventive maintenance of the system with included system upgrades in accordance with the recommendations of the system component manufacturers. Extended warranty must be provided for a period of 3 years. The subject of procurement is licences for a software solution for analytical databases that supports 816 physical cores on existing hardware and existing technology based on GreenPlum 7. Existing licences are valid until 30.06.2026. Licences that are the subject of procurement must be valid until 30.06.2029. The total estimated value of the entire procurement subject amounts to 3.000.000,00 EUR excluding VAT. The contracting authority is currently conducting a procurement procedure for the 1 group of the procurement subject (Procurement of licences for MPP database) with a total estimated procurement value of 2.000.000,00 EUR. The procurement procedure for the second group will be conducted subsequently.
sig_adc69c18cd3d0c3473ac.title: Procurement of licenses for the MPP database and software solution for data cataloguing within the CDU data platform: Lot 1-Procurement of licenses for the MPP database

The subject of the contract is the supply of a high-performance computer central unit with a monitor and operating system and a NAS server, hereinafter referred to as the "equipment", for the Department of Plant Taxonomy and Nature Conservation of the University of Gdańsk. 2. Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) classification code: 30211000-1 (high-performance computers), 30231300-0 (computer monitors), 48822000-6 (computer servers). 3. A detailed description of the subject of the contract has been specified in Appendix No 6 to the SWZ – description of the subject of the contract. 4. Place of delivery of the equipment: Uniwersytet Gdański, Department of Plant Taxonomy and Nature Conservation, Faculty of Biology, ul. Wita Stwosza 59, 80-308 Gdańsk. 5. Details concerning the warranty are contained in § 7 of the draft contract – Appendix No 5 to the SWZ. 6. In the description of the subject of the contract, constituting Appendix No 6 to the SWZ, the Contracting Authority has described the requirements concerning management systems relating to the production process of the offered equipment by reference to the standards indicated in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract. In each case where these standards have been indicated in the content of the SWZ, including in the appendices to the SWZ, it shall be understood that such indication is accompanied by the words "or equivalent". Accordingly, the Contracting Authority permits equivalent solutions with regard to the standards indicated in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract, in accordance with Article 101 paragraph 4 and 5 of the Public Procurement Law. The concept of equivalence shall mean that the offered equipment comes from production covered by an implemented and current management system which to an equivalent degree meets the requirements specified in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract. The applied equivalent solutions must correspond in their type and scope to the purposes served by the standards cited in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract. 7. Due to the fact that the possibility of various equivalent proposals is permitted, the Contractor is required to verify and treat all solutions as interrelated. Demonstrating equivalence, i.e., meeting to an equivalent degree the requirements specified by the Contracting Authority in the description of the subject of the contract, lies with the Contractor. In the event of offering equipment originating from production covered by a management system compliant with an equivalent standard or another equivalent solution with respect to the standards indicated in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract, the Contractor is obliged to indicate this solution in point 5 of the tender form, constituting Appendix No 1 to the SWZ, present information on the offered equivalent solution, the justification for its equivalence, and evidence confirming equivalence. The Contracting Authority will not reject the Contractor's tender solely because the offered equipment does not come from production covered by management systems compliant with the standards indicated in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract, provided that the Contractor proves in the tender, in particular by means of the means of proof regarding the subject matter referred to in Article 104 – 107 of the Public Procurement Law, that the proposed solutions meet to an equivalent degree the requirements specified by the Contracting Authority in item 9 of table 1 of the description of the subject of the contract (Article 101 paragraph 5 of the Public Procurement Law). 8. The Contracting Authority, after signing the contract, anticipates applying for the 0% VAT tax rate on the basis of Article 83 paragraph 14 point 1 of the Act of 11 March 2004 on tax on goods and services (consolidated text: Journal of Laws of 2025 item 775 as amended).

sig_add465c5a2eb03875c78.description: OneCRM NL is TenneT’s consolidated Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform for relationship and stake holder management in the Netherlands. The platform supports multiple business units, including CMN (Customer and Markets), SOM (Strategisch Omgevingsmanagement), REM (Real Estate Manage ment), SOP, PPN, LON and PCN, all operating within a single, integrated and governed Dynamics 365 environment. The solution serves as a shared platform for storing, maintaining and managing customer and stake holder information. It supports business unit- specific processes through configuration and role based access enabling both standardization and flexibility. OneCRM NL enables a centralized and con sistent view of stakeholders, interactions and related data, while allowing tailored usage aligned with the needs of individual departments. The platform is operated as part of the Microsoft Power Platform and follows standardized govern ance, data models and Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) practices. This ensures data qual ity, scalability and controlled extensibility across all participating business units.
sig_add465c5a2eb03875c78.title: Market consultation CRM

sig_add805c2fd31b2ef079d.description: The purpose of this contract is the renewal and functional extension of the Personal Space, the digital platform for the digitisation of citizen administrative procedures for the Municipal Administration of Schaerbeek. It follows the contract awarded in 2021 (reference: scha/equip/2021/034), which has reached its expiry date, and aims to ensure service continuity while addressing the functional gaps identified during the operational period. The analysis of the existing system highlighted the following functional gaps in the current platform, which this contract addresses: ► Absence of strong authentication via Itsme® or eID for procedures requiring certain identification of the citizen. ► Absence of a citizen file 360° centralising the complete history of procedures, exchanges and documents for the same citizen. ► Absence of CRM integration allowing the automatic linking of citizen files with the municipality's customer relationship management tools. This contract covers all of the following components, whether they are renewed, improved or newly introduced functionalities: ► A citizen personal space (front-end) accessible via strong authentication (Itsme®/eID/CSAM) ► A back-office for collaborative file management for municipal agents ► A no-code/low-code form creator with condition and validation management ► A workflow and process modelling engine compliant with the BPMN 2.0 standard ► SSO authentication via Azure Active Directory for agents ► Granular management of rights, roles and access by department and by type of procedure ► CRM integration and interoperability connectors (REST API, webhooks) The contract includes: the platform user licence, initial configuration and parameterisation, migration of existing data where applicable, training of agents and administrators, complete documentation, and corrective and evolutionary maintenance for the duration of the contract. The solution currently in production at the Municipality of Schaerbeek is based on a set of technical components described in detail in section D.0 — Technical context of the existing system.
sig_add805c2fd31b2ef079d.title: Renewal and functional extension of the Personal Space – Solution for the digitisation of citizen administrative procedures for the municipality of Schaerbeek

sig_adf666c1cf048a4d7b1b.description: 12 microscopes shall be procured and a total solution for scanners with the accompanying KI-analysis software for the Life Science Building (LVB) in Oslo. The microscopes are procured on behalf of the Department for Pharmacology (FAR), the Department of Medical Genetics (AMG) and the Department for Microbiology (MIK) at Oslo University Hospital. The procurement is divided into 4 sub competitions. Tenders can be submitted individually or in several sub-competitions. The procurement also includes options as described in the Competition Description, point 1.5 Options. Six microscopes shall be procured of the correct standard of the variant. The microscopes shall be used for direct microscopy of different sample materials for septic, microscopy of positive blood cultures, and microscopy of bacteria/soppisolates from different cultivation media (as a part of identifying microbes), as well as for quality assurance of chromosomal preparations, at the Department of Medical Genetics (AMG) and the Department of Microbiology (MIK). The procurement includes an option for a suitable camera with any software, which can be used together with the microscope, as well as an option for a system so that several users can simultaneously assess a preparation. In addition we would like an option for 5 microscopes equivalent to the main delivery.; 4 microscopes shall be procured from the variant straight-facing fluorescent. The microscopes shall be used for direct fluorescent microscopy of different sample materials in connection with exhaust, microscopy of positive blood cultures, and microscopy of culture of mycobacterias from liquid medium, by the Department of Microbiology (MIK). The procurement includes an option for a suitable camera with any software, which can be used together with the microscope, as well as an option for a system so that several users can simultaneously assess a preparation. In addition we would like an option for 5 microscopes equivalent to the main delivery.; 2 microscopes shall be procured of the variant inverse standard. sig_adf9d3b9ac5ece4d6055.description: This document is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a market survey in accordance with section 65 of the Public Procurement Act, which the contracting authority is carrying out as set out in this request for information. The purpose of this request for information is to examine issues related to the procurement referred to in the title. The objective of the market survey is to obtain comprehensive information regarding the subject of the procurement to support the preparation of the procurement so that any potential tendering competition can be carried out as appropriately as possible. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. SUMMARY OF THE PROCUREMENT DESCRIPTION The subject of the procurement is the modernisation of the financial management system package for the City of Rauma. Due to upcoming changes in the in-house entity regulation of the Public Procurement Act, it is necessary for the city to prepare the competitive tendering for the financial management system. The city's preliminary objective is for the new solution to be in production use starting from 1.1.2028. The current operating model includes numerous manual work stages, particularly regarding checks, controls and corrections. This undermines process efficiency, increases the risk of errors and makes transparent documentation of operations difficult. The objective of the procurement is to find a SaaS-based solution primarily supporting the financial management package that improves process reliability, usability, efficiency, manageability and information security, as well as reduces the need for manual work. The target solution must support key financial management processes of the municipal organisation, such as accounting, purchase invoice processing, sales invoicing, payment transactions, reporting, financial planning, internal accounting and authority reporting. The solution must be integrable with the city's other system environment, support reliable data transfer from existing systems, and enable controlled and, if necessary, phased implementation. The subject of the procurement may also include a payroll management system as part of the package. The customer is investigating this possibility in the market survey. At this stage, inclusion is only under preliminary consideration, which is why only general-purpose questions regarding payroll management have been presented in the request for information's material and questions. Their purpose is to assess suppliers' general capability to supply a payroll management system in addition to the financial management system, as well as to survey what benefits acquiring a payroll management system together with the financial management system could bring to the customer. The final content, scope, execution model and schedule of the procurement will be refined based on the procurement preparation and market survey. The market survey will examine, among other things, solution alternatives available on the market, execution models, integrations, migration, implementation schedule, cost structure, and automation and reporting capabilities utilised in the solutions. A more detailed description of the preliminary content of the procurement, objectives and themes to be examined in the market survey is presented in the appendix to the procurement notice.
sig_adf9d3b9ac5ece4d6055.title: MARKET SURVEY: Financial management system procurement for the City of Rauma

sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.description: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE INFORMATION REQUEST Helsingin kaupunki, kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (hereinafter referred to as "KYMP") is preparing a procurement procedure regarding the "Procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness". Before initiating the actual procurement procedure, KYMP is surveying the market supply, willingness and interest to tender for the procurement in question, and is seeking answers to questions related to the planned procurement. The information request is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a market dialogue. The publication of the information request does not initiate a procurement procedure. The contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Market operators will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. Information obtained through the information request may be used in the preparation of procurement documents. BACKGROUND AND OBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The Urban Environment Division (KYMP) is implementing the procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness. The City of Helsinki has not previously used a system intended for infrastructure construction contract management. In the current situation, information related to an individual contract is scattered across the systems of the Client and contractors, a large part of communication takes place solely via email, operating models in different contracts and among contractors vary, and up-to-date information is not easily accessible to all parties to the contract or in cover situations. In the current situation, contract management processes such as reporting, site diaries and defect repairs lack modern tools that can be smoothly utilised in fieldwork; instead, a large part of the entries are first made on paper and recorded digitally afterwards. Tools intended for the management of infrastructure site contracts have been piloted and test-used in the sector, and it has been observed that the use of a contract management system can speed up and streamline, among other things, the preparation of inspection reports and the sharing of reports between the parties. The key objective of the procurement is the procurement and implementation of a system suitable for monitoring infrastructure construction projects from project preparation to the end of the warranty period, and particularly for management, tasks, communication and field conditions during the contract implementation phase. The background and object of the procurement are described in more detail in the appendix to the information request, Description of the object of the procurement. INFORMATION REQUEST KYMP requests informal answers to the questions in the document "Change proposal table_for technical market dialogue_TENDERER_FILLS IN" attached to the information request, and to mark any proposed changes. Please submit your answers by email to kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi no later than 17.4.2026 at 16.15. KYMP will treat the answers confidentially. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE AND SCHEDULE Preliminary schedule of the procurement: March 2026 Information request May 2026 Publication of the call for tenders June 2026 Procurement decision and conclusion of the procurement contract

The project includes the design, production, delivery, installation, programming, testing and commissioning, including the handover of a fully functional work and 24-month warranty service. All activities must be carried out in accordance with valid STN standards and project documentation, with maximum regard for the status of the NKP. Further details are provided in the tender documents and other annexes.

sig_ae7eb8d554010b10ca22.description: Following a competitive procurement undertaken in 2019, a contract was awarded for the provision of the Apperta Foundation's OpenEyes Electronic Patient Record (EPR) solution for the management of ophthalmology services across NHS Wales. Digital Health and Care Wales (DHCW) is now undertaking an informal Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to better understand current market conditions and supplier capabilities in advance of any potential future procurement activity. This engagement relates solely to the hosting, support, maintenance, and ongoing development of the OpenEyes solution across NHS Wales. The scope includes support for implementations within secondary care ophthalmology departments and community optometric practices. Interested suppliers are invited to complete a Request for Information (RFI) questionnaire, available via the eTenderWales portal: https://etenderwales.bravosolution.co.uk/home.html Completed RFI responses must be submitted through the eTenderWales portal no later than 12:00 noon on 1 October 2026. This exercise is being undertaken for market research purposes only and does not constitute a procurement process, commitment to procure, or invitation to tender. DHCW has not yet determined whether a future procurement will be undertaken. Information gathered through this engagement will be used to inform future decision-making and procurement strategy development. Following review of the RFI responses, DHCW reserves the right to engage with respondents on an individual basis to clarify, verify, or supplement information provided. Lot 1: . None

sig_ae8ad84891f4a6a2b53b.description: A service provider is sought who provides CMS-neutral advice, supports UMMD in selecting a suitable CMS and is responsible for the technical implementation of the web platform – including information architecture, data/content model, templates/components, integration and migration. The subject of the tender is the conception, design, technical implementation and introduction of a future-proof content management system (CMS) for the external web presence and the intranet of the Magdeburg University Medicine including the project, consulting, implementation, training and migration services required for this. The contract comprises in particular the specialist, technical and design conception, the development or implementation of a suitable CMS-based solution approach, the creation and implementation of templates and modules, the mapping of defined content, editorial and approval processes, the migration of selected content, quality assurance, training of the participating user groups as well as the support of commissioning and rollout. The goal is a high-performance, user-oriented, low-barrier, scalable and future-proof solution that fulfils both the requirements for the public internet presence and for an internal intranet for information, communication and editorial processes. The contracting authority reserves the right to commission the operation and further development of the platform after go-live and the hypercare phase in a second stage (option). The contracting authority reserves the right to extend the service to additional adjacent buildings (option). The contracting authority furthermore reserves the right to extend the service beyond the interfaces already defined to further interfaces, in particular for staff search as well as DWH/structural data (option). The contracting authority also reserves the right to commission change requests and workshops beyond the defined scope (option). Further information on the options will be provided by the contracting authority in the final specification of services and in the context of the negotiation talks. For reasons of confidentiality, the complete tender documents with the detailed specification of services will only be made available after the return of a signed confidentiality agreement.

sig_ae9618fd2e1cfeda3803.description: Services are being procured to be provided within the framework of the bilateral cooperation project "German-Argentine Agricultural Policy Dialogue". The services include the implementation and coordination of the dialogue project, in particular the organisation of seminars, delegation trips and other events, as well as the promotion of entrepreneurial and scientific-technological cooperation. To this end, several long-term experts are to work in Argentina, who will be supplemented by the deployment of short-term experts and supported by qualified backstopping. The project aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Germany and Argentina in the agricultural, food and forestry sectors through a deepened and institutionally anchored agricultural policy dialogue as well as through increased entrepreneurial and scientific-technological cooperation and to translate this into concrete joint initiatives for innovation, competitiveness and market access. Result area 1: Strategic agricultural policy dialogue (Addressing priority agricultural policy topics, including regulatory frameworks, trade standards and market access issues.) Result area 2: Market and innovation bridge (Strengthening entrepreneurial cooperation and promoting innovation along agricultural and food industry value chains through B2B formats, innovation platforms and pilot projects.) Result area 3: Scientific-technological cooperation (Selective, cross-result-area cooperation between research institutions, universities and technology centres of both countries as an interface between science and politics.) Result area 4: Regulatory frameworks and cooperation in the forestry and timber sector (forestry component) (Addressing regulatory requirements, including in connection with the EUDR and the sustainability chapter of the Mercosur agreement, strengthening networking between actors in the forestry and timber industry as well as developing concrete approaches for knowledge, trade and technology transfer.) Result area 2: Market and innovation bridge (Strengthening entrepreneurial cooperation and promoting innovation along agricultural and food industry value chains through B2B formats, innovation platforms and pilot projects.) Result area 3: Scientific-technological cooperation (Selective, cross-result-area cooperation between research institutions, universities and technology centres of both countries as an interface between science and politics.) Result area 4: Regulatory frameworks and cooperation in the forestry and timber sector (forestry component) (Addressing regulatory requirements, including in connection with the EUDR and the sustainability chapter of the Mercosur agreement, strengthening networking between actors in the forestry and timber industry as well as developing concrete approaches for knowledge, trade and technology transfer.) This structure flexibly combines political, economic and regional cooperation

sig_aeb283490452bb8b4a94.description: AZ Groeninge is a large regional hospital in Kortrijk that offers a wide range of medical care and specialised treatments. The hospital works with various medical and support services in this regard. Currently, there is a very close partnership between AZ Groeninge and Sint Jozefskliniek Izegem. Presently, each of the two hospitals has its own warehouse. The scope of this tender is a new WMS software for the warehouse in AZ Groeninge. This warehouse currently uses SAP WM to manage its warehouse operations. Given that the support situation for this is changing and coming to an end at the end of 2028, AZ Groeninge is looking for a new IT solution. This new solution must cover the same scope as the current SAP WM. In addition to the warehouses in the hospitals, there are also 2 external warehouses (managed by 3 third parties) where pallet overflow is stored. The new WMS must also be able to handle operations with these external warehouses via a stock transfer function. This function may be approached pragmatically at a general location level, not at a detailed location level, from which certain pallets will be requested based on requirements. The warehouse in AZ Groeninge consists of classical standard storage components (pallets and shelving) as well as 3 vertical lift modules from supplier Kardex. The scope of the requested software will range from the delivery of goods at the loading bays, to storage, up to and including delivery into an “empty/full” storage facility in the departments (management of the empty/full storage facility is also in scope). The control of the vertical lift modules in machine language is part of the scope of the requested software.
sig_aeb283490452bb8b4a94.title: Purchase, implementation and maintenance of WMS software package for AZ Groeninge warehouse

sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.description: The progressive digitalisation of core business processes, geopolitical developments and rising European requirements for data sovereignty and compliance require a future-proof and resilient IT infrastructure. As the independent central bank of the Federal Republic of Germany and part of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB), the Deutsche Bundesbank establishes the highest requirements for the autonomy, sovereignty and performance of its IT portfolio. To achieve the combination of these ambitious goals, the Deutsche Bundesbank requires reliable partners also for sovereign cloud services. With the strategic decision to use sovereign cloud services in addition to other public cloud services, the Deutsche Bundesbank pursues the goal of strengthening the digital sovereignty and security of its IT infrastructure without having to dispense with the innovative strength and scalability of modern public cloud offerings. In the course of this strategic orientation, the Deutsche Bundesbank is therefore initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the sovereign cloud services available on the market. In doing so, it is to be examined in particular to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security-related requirements of the Deutsche Bundesbank. This market exploration therefore focuses on cloud computing offerings that fulfil the European Commission's understanding of full digital sovereignty ("Technology and operations under complete EU control, subject only to EU law, with no critical non-EU dependencies", cf. EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework). The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to define the concept of digital sovereignty more broadly and deviating from the aforementioned scope. Further details on the Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for sovereign cloud services can be obtained exclusively upon request from the email address provided in the contact details. This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially pending EU-wide procurement procedure by the Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of cloud services and forms, among other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and does not constitute either an offer or an invitation to conclude a contract. The implementation of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences (neither preferential treatment nor disadvantage) for the participating company within the framework of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration.
sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.title: Market exploration: Sovereign cloud services for the Deutsche Bundesbank

sig_aebe9d81b32297fdc8ec.description: Oikeusrekisterikeskus (in this notice also “ORK” and “contracting authority”) has procured an application performance and availability monitoring service (APM/Dynatrace) from the State ICT Centre Valtori, whose service provider in the procurement is Vivicta Oy. Valtori has informed ORK on 12.6.2026 that it will cease offering the service in question to its customers on 31.12.2026. Upon receiving the notice, ORK has immediately begun preparing the procurement of a replacement service. However, the new service is not automatically deployable, but requires a system-specific implementation project to configure the service and carry out the migrations. The subject of the procurement is the acquisition of an application performance and availability monitoring service for a transition period until the migrations of the systems dependent on the service have been completed and the new replacement service has been deployed gradually. The procurement is an interim solution that enables a controlled transition towards a new service solution. The procurement is a service package that covers both the service and the necessary licences. A one-year fixed-term contract has been concluded for the procurement (1.8.2026-31.7.2027). The procurement also includes two options, which are described in more detail in the notice sections “Description of additional procurement opportunities” and “Description of the contract option periods”. The contracting authority states that the duration of the transition arrangement is essentially affected by the fact that this is not a single piece of software but a broad service and system entity, where change management, continuity, information security, and operational transition must be carried out in a controlled manner. The contracting authority estimates that the deployment of the replacement service in its systems will be possible at the earliest during the year 2027. However, the contracting authority states that the overall schedule for system migrations and the deployment of the new service inevitably involves uncertainties. However, the procurement will not be continued longer than is necessary to secure the migration of the systems and to deploy the replacement service. The direct procurement is thus limited to the necessary transition period and arranged in such a way that the system migrations and the new service can be deployed in a controlled manner without interruption of services, which would cause serious harm to the service production of the contracting authority's customers. A notice concerning voluntary ex-ante transparency has been published for the procurement.
sig_aebe9d81b32297fdc8ec.title: Ex-post notice on the procurement of an application performance and availability monitoring service as a direct procurement

sig_aec7d6a03ec72425f0dd.description: The complexity of the projects, the large number of parallel projects and the high safety and operational requirements lead to an increased need for specialist and expert support in various disciplines, which cannot be fully covered with internal resources. sig_aef4f63cccfb7bb7913a.description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL/QUOTE. This synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract nor does the Government intend to directly pay for any information or responses submitted as a result of this solicitation. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis; there is no solicitation available at this time. This Sources Sought Synopsis is published for market research purposes only. Companies may be contacted if further information is needed. This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Synopsis to seek a contractor for future work pertaining to the B-52H engineering services starting 01 January 2028. The Boeing B-52H Stratofortress is an American long-range subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber. The B-52 was designed and built by Boeing, which has continued to provide support and upgrades. It has been operated by the United States Air Force (USAF) since 1955 and was flown by NASA from 1959 to 2007. The bomber can carry up to 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of weapons and has a typical combat range of around 8,800 miles (14,200 km) without aerial refueling. The sustainment of the B-52H currently includes the delivery of engineering design, engineering support, and technical support services crucial for the ongoing maintenance and operational readiness of the B-52H aircraft, including its components and associated support and test equipment. The original estimated minimum/maximum amount for the B-52H sustainment contracts was $1.15B over ten (10) years (2019-2028) for engineering services Contract efforts are subject to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.232-18 availability of funds. The sustainment contracts currently contain multiple contract types at the contract line-item level (e.g. firm fixed price, cost plus incentive fee, cost plus fixed fee, etc.) This Sources Sought Synopsis only addresses the B-52H engineering services requirements starting 01 January 2029. The contractor will be required to provide engineering support services that provide technical information and logistics resources to enable maintenance and operational readiness of 76 B-52H aircraft. Engineering services will be required at the following USAF operational bases: Tinker AFB, Oklahoma; Edwards AFB, California; Minot AFB, North Dakota, and Barksdale AFB, Louisiana. Additionally, the contractor shall provide engineering support at the Boeing facility Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, to reflect field service representative (FSR) support. The contractor will be required to perform the following recurring engineering services: - Program Management and Integration - Principal Point of Contact - Platform Website - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Structures Working Group - Government Property and Material Management - Unique Identifier (UID) Requirements - Configuration Management - Data management, automation and Contract data Requirements Delivery (CDRL) and CDRL Quality - Engineering Data/Documents Files - Quality Assurance Program - Engineering Support - Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP) - Specialized Engineering Support - System Integration Lab (SIL) - Ground and Flight Test Engineering Support - Drawing Cleanup and Procurement Ready Drawing - Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) Repair Development - Voluntary Protection Program - Field Services Representative (FSR) The contractor will be required to perform the following Non-recurring Engineering (NRE) services support: - Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Statement of Work (SOW) - Expedited Acquisitioin Process (EAP) and Engineering Projects (EP) - Interim Contractor Support (ICS) - Over & Above (O&A) - Travel - Material - Data Requirements - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Associate Contractors and Proprietary Information Agreements (PIA) - Quality Assurance and Quality Management System - Safety - System Engineering - Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) - Earned Value management (EVM)s - Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) It is critical that respondents include the degree to which they will require access to B-52H rights and the degree to which they have or are able to obtain B-52H rights from Boeing. The capabilities package should be brief and concise yet clearly demonstrate an ability to meet the stated requirements. Recent, relevant experience should be provided for each area. If a company is capable of some, but not all of the consolidated requirements stated in this Sources Sought Synopsis, please provide a response that explains the requirements for which you are capable. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this action is 541330, size standard is $25.5 million. Firms responding to this announcement should indicate whether they are a large business, other than small business, small business, small disadvantaged business (SDB), woman-owned small business (WOSB), economically disadvantaged women-owned small business (EDWOSB), 8(a)-certified business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), or Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business (HUBZone). All prospective contractors shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be awarded a DoD contract. Note that the NAICS code for this requirement, if applicable to the company's capabilities, should be included in the company's NAICS code listing in SAM (www.sam.gov). The acquisition strategy has not yet been determined. Market research results will assist the Air Force in determining whether this requirement will be a full and open, a small business (or other socioeconomic) set aside, or a sole source acquisition. Note that, if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small business contractors, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a Small Business Set-Aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting. If it is determined that a small business set-aside is appropriate and your company anticipates submitting a proposal as the prime contractor for a small business set-aside, please provide specific details and rationale as to how compliance with FAR clause 52.219-14 would be achieved, including specific details regarding teaming arrangements, etc. If subcontracts are to be used, provide anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and whether small or large businesses will be used. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. It is anticipated that appropriate security classifications for personnel and facilities will be required up to the Secret level in satisfying these performance requirements. It is also anticipated that the contractor will require access to special access information, receive and generate classified material and fabricate, modify or store classified hardware. Appropriate security requirements will be required before contract award. Companies may be contacted for further information as required to assess their capabilities. The B-52 Contracting Branch is surveying the market to determine if any sources are qualified to fulfil any or all the above-mentioned requirements. Interested firms should submit sufficient information (limit to 20 pages – 12-point font, single-spaced, 1" margins) which will permit assessment of technical capabilities in writing or electronically to Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, AFLCMC/WBK, Attn. Mr. Kurt McKay, 3001 Staff Drive, Tinker AFB, OK 73145. If there are any questions with regard to the contract please contact Kurt McKay, Contract Negotiator, AFLCMC/WBK, (405) 736-4121, e-mail kurt.mckay@us.af.mil or Ms. Shelby Mancello, Contracting Officer, AFLCMC/WBK, (405) 336-5553, e-mail shelby.mancello@us.af.mil. RESPONSES ARE DUE NO LATER THAN 6 Nov 2026.

sig_af225a8291df25ef0109.description: The Police and Crime Commissioner for West Midlands as the Contracting Authority for West Midlands Police is seeking information to inform the procurement strategy for a future tender for a Forensic Case Management System (FCMS) to support the delivery of forensic science activities. There is a possibility that this may lead to a collaborative opportunity with other contracting authorities. The supplier market engagement is being held to explore if there are solutions, systems or innovations within the market place which may be able to provide the below and inform the future procurement strategy and/or specification: Support all forensic science activities, including digital forensics, enabling the end-to-end management of forensic cases from submission through examination, reporting, review, and finalisation. Support evidential integrity, continuity, and full auditability across multiple forensic disciplines. Capable of integration with existing force systems, including Command and Control, Records Management and Property Management systems, to enable secure and efficient data exchange, reduce duplication, and support operational policing requirements. Provide the capability to securely store, manage, and retrieve forensic imagery and documentation, including photographs, reports, exhibits, and associated materials, with appropriate access controls, versioning, and audit trails. Functionality to support quality management, including compliance with applicable forensic standards and regulatory requirements, audit processes, non-conformance management, and continuous improvement. An integrated asset register is required to record, manage, and track forensic assets, tools, and equipment, including calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle information. Comprehensive management information and reporting, including configurable dashboards and reporting tools to support operational, performance, and strategic oversight. Ability to support automation, including workflow management, task allocation, alerts, and automated retention and disposal of records and digital material in line with legislative, regulatory, and force retention policies. The future engagement may also test feasibility, potential commercials and delivery models.
