sig_b42b0023e25ccfd1beed.description:
The Data Governance project involves the implementation of measures to improve data management at NBank. As part of the pilot scheme for the Finance (FIN) & Controlling (CON) divisions, key building blocks have already been implemented with the establishment of the Finance & Risk Data Management (FRD) team and the decision to establish DG processes. In order to be able to adequately perform corresponding tasks in the future, the use of tools and instruments is essential. As part of the project, an analysis of the requirement coverage and expandability of existing tools with a focus on data quality management and metadata management was carried out in coordination with IT. The implementation of self-service data quality management is taking place in the Business Warehouse environment. To support metadata management, a new software is to be introduced via this procurement procedure. The aim is to leverage significant optimisation potential for NBank through the further development of future-oriented metadata management. The following core objectives are to be realised with the implementation: - Transparency regarding existing data, its content, context and properties - Basis for systematic data administration and cataloguing - Creation of a uniform understanding of data - Further development of the IT architecture and value contribution to digitalisation through data transparency - Strengthening of regulatory compliance - Multiplier for data-driven issues of other projects in the bank. The Data Governance implementation project will carry out the conception and realisation of structures and measures in metadata management. A central component is the introduction of metadata management software that supports the three components of the business data model, data dictionary and data lineage and associated processes: - Business data model: Mapping and administration of data clusters (data and sub-domains, data object/entity and data fields) as well as linking these with guidelines, systems, interest groups, including roles and responsibilities - Data dictionary: Directory of metadata, as well as registers of professional knowledge regarding terms, business objects, reports and key figures (business glossary) but also technical aspects (technical glossary) - Data lineage (data flow tracking): Recording and modelling of data flows to identify dependencies and impacts in the Run the Bank and Change the Bank environment. For the start, metadata management is to be set up with a focus on the NBank Business Warehouse (NBW). The NBW is the Single Point of Truth (SPOT) of NBank. The SPOT pursues the goal of providing all evaluation-relevant data of the bank in a complete and transparent data layer in the dispositive system and supplying all target systems with the required data via flexible access options. Furthermore, the NBW ensures the technical and professional consistency of all data, the supplied interfaces and all evaluations, reports or statements generated as a result, which is an essential aspect of the tasks in the Data Governance environment. The NBW is a contract development based on an Oracle Datenbank. Data is integrated, condensed and prepared for the requested purposes by the NBW from SAP (modules such as FI, CO, CML, CFM), the ABAKUS (development bank add-on), as well as other external sources (such as EUCTFSL, market data, address data, rating, various upstream systems). Key target systems are THINC and BAIS, which in turn partially feed their result data back to the NBW. Prospectively, metadata management is to be extended to further areas and thus further systems beyond the NBW. The NBW and the ReportServer based on it are the central reporting system of NBank and will also be used for DQ reporting in the future. These reports are enriched with metadata such as domains and data lineage, which originate from the metadata management software. For further information, see: Service description, requirements specification and functional scope questionnaire. The implementation plan provides for the introduction of the metadata management software from 04.03.2026; the installation of the software and its tests are to be completed by 28.09.2026. In parallel, the initial collection of metadata via use cases in the FIN & CON areas is taking place in the Data Governance project. In Q4 2026, this information will be transferred to the target solution and initial data lineage use cases will be set up. In 2027, the expansion will take place as a further development stage beyond the initial scope of application. In this procurement procedure, we are looking for standard software for the metadata management of NBank. The requirements for the metadata management software are divided into functional and non-functional requirements, which are specified in more detail in the following sections. Each requirement has a priority that indicates its urgency: Priority 1: Must criterion (minimum requirement) Priority 2: Should criterion Priority 3: Can criterion 3.1. Functional requirements The functional requirements are divided into the three components of metadata management. The requirements for the data model and the data dictionary overlap strongly and are closely related. Therefore, their requirements are summarised; data lineage follows separately. The requirements are formulated in the style of user stories. For the acting users, there are three hierarchy levels: Master, User and Reader. Readers only have read functions, the User additionally has write rights for their configurable area, and the Master has all functions. In the user stories, only the lowest hierarchy level is mentioned, which means that all higher-level users have the same functionality. 3.1.1.

Business data model & Data dictionary In the business data model, the data is structured in the domain model, which recognises four levels. A data domain comprises a data area that covers central functions and processes at NBank. It contains a collection of sub-domains, data objects and data fields contained therein, which are functionally or logically connected to one another. A sub-domain further divides a data domain into specific functional blocks that represent more granular categories or subsets of data within the domain. They help to classify and organise the entities based on their content and context. An entity is a structured set of data (fields) as an image of the objects and facts represented by this data, about which NBank collects information. This can also be thought of as a table. It serves to represent the relationship between the data and, if necessary, to further subdivide a sub-domain. A data field is a business data element that characterises or describes one or more technical attributes. This can also be thought of as a column in a table. The data field is the most granular element in a business data model. Entries can be recorded in the business data model, the business glossary and the technical glossary. In this process, structures are entered in the data model, business information such as field descriptions in the business glossary, and technical information such as data type in the technical glossary. A template is a form with predefined mandatory fields and optional fields for recording entries in a structured and standardised manner. 3.1.2. Data lineage The central structure in the data lineage component is data trees, which illustrate the data flow and the relationships between different data fields in a hierarchical representation in a dependency graph in order to make the origin and the course of the data at NBank comprehensible. 3.2. Non-functional requirements New software solutions should integrate seamlessly into the existing application landscape of NBank as a cloud solution. In this process, the new software will not be granted direct data access to the systems of NBank (pull); instead, the data will be supplied from NBank (push). The NBW is based on an interlocking sequence of SQL statements, some of which are generated at runtime. A complete metadata path from the source to the graphical report already exists. For objects from SAP, for example, the stored business designations and descriptions are available in addition to their technical designations. Furthermore, the data objects (tables, fields, reports) are already divided into areas of responsibility and assigned to so-called application managers. It is explicitly required that this data be used directly (e.g. transfer of tables, no direct coupling of systems) from the DWH for the construction of the data model and the dictionary. From the perspective of NBank, interfaces should be as simple and flexible as possible. The provider is expected to have a documented procedure for how the data can be translated into a format that can be processed for the MDM. We assume <10 PT having to put into the construction of interfaces on our side. In addition, the expectation is that providers follow the following four principles to enable a successful introduction of new software: - Architecture: The application architecture is designed to support changing and growing requirements while remaining in a maintainable and operational state. - Technology: Configuration via application functions is preferred over modifications with specific code / development. - Business: Use of industry standards and best practices to ensure efficient processes for conception and delivery - Future-proofing: The solution is supported by the provider's roadmap and offers continuous support and suitable technologies

sig_b4709a8e5a81e54fe159.description: Contract aimed at designing, creating and deploying an educational and fun video game experience dedicated to aeronautical trades and technologies. The device must be usable in three contexts: in class (learning environment), at a trade fair/event (demonstration mode) and at home (free access on browser and/or app). General objective: to design, develop and operate a modular game experience, usable in class, at a trade fair and at home, with usage tracking and GDPR compliance. In line with the educational objectives and the list of modules, the scope of the service consists of choosing the game mechanics (mini-challenges, quizzes, badges, nominative certificate), designing a simple and accessible interface, providing for the translation into English of the basic French version (with the support of the holder of lot 2) and drafting the functional, technical and narrative architecture. The candidate will propose a solution mixing 3D and 2D in order to optimise the price/quality ratio without deteriorating the user experience. The reception area must be in 3D in third-person view. A meeting to define the requests will be held at the start of the project where the holder will present various solutions, functionalities and ideas. See Specifications, Special Administrative Clauses, Special Technical Clauses and Consultation Regulations.; General objective: to design and produce all the educational content of the game, for a wide audience (from middle school (4th grade) to adults in retraining), while guaranteeing clarity, accuracy and consistency with the game mechanics of Lot 1. See Specifications, Special Administrative Clauses, Special Technical Clauses and Consultation Regulations.; Before the launch, the priority is to make the project known to the various audiences. The key indicators will be the number of video views and qualified traffic to the site. In parallel, we will aim for conversion: registrations and active users over the long term. See Specifications, Special Administrative Clauses, Special Technical Clauses and Consultation Regulations.
sig_b4709a8e5a81e54fe159.title: Creation of an educational video game "serious game"

sig_b48220f71872ddd8d52f.description: The contracting authorities intend with this procedure to award separate contracts for consultancy services on knowledge and technology transfer for local SMEs. Lot LOT-0001: Consultancy services on knowledge and technology transfer in the districts of Diepholz and Osnabrück as well as in the independent cities of Oldenburg and Osnabrück in the years 2027-2029. In view of rapid technological change and shortening innovation cycles, the contracting authorities consider it necessary to actively promote knowledge and technology transfer in the specialisation fields of the Lower Saxony "Regional Innovation Strategy for Smart Specialisation (RIS3)" within their territorial authorities through the qualified advice of small and medium-sized enterprises (hereinafter referred to as "SMEs", these are enterprises within the meaning of Annex 1 of Regulation (EU) 651/2014) as well as associated preliminary and follow-up work. To increase their competitiveness, SMEs established in the territory of the relevant territorial authorities are to be supported through enhanced advice and assistance with innovations. Securing existing jobs and creating new ones is of particular importance here. The aim is for SMEs in the affected territorial authorities to be advised by the contractor regarding their innovation orientation and to initiate concrete innovation projects for implementation in the SMEs. The content of the service is the provision of qualified advice to SMEs in the participating territorial authorities by the contractor and the preliminary and follow-up tasks associated with the qualified advice. These comprise preliminary exploratory talks as well as accompanying measures in public relations and the administration of the overall project.
sig_b48220f71872ddd8d52f.title: Consultancy services for knowledge and technology transfer in the Diepholz and Osnabrück districts as well as in the cities of Oldenburg and Osnabrück that do not belong to a district in the years 2027-2029

sig_b492b1bf98cac3c7b384.description: Description & Purpose of Request 1.1 Objective The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) and Non-Developmental Item (NDI) core maritime navigation software solutions that have the capability of being enhanced to meet USCG requirements (e.g. EAIS IDD). The primary objective is to survey industry capabilities to inform the prospective modernization and eventual replacement of the legacy USCG “Vega” navigation software suite (currently derived from commercial core navigation architectures) across the cutter and boat fleet. 1.2 Purpose & Scope of Market Inquiry The Coast Guard seeks insight into the current commercial and naval navigation software, including cutting-edge display engines, autonomous voyage planning, sensor fusion, resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), and modern software architectures (e.g., modular open systems, containerized microservices, cross-platform runtimes). The Government intends to assess software suites that can match or exceed the complete operational baseline of current USCG E-NAV capabilities while remaining flexible, open, and capable of integrating seamlessly into existing USCG shipboard hardware configurations without requiring complete bridge refits. 1.3 Disclaimer This is a Request for Information (RFI) and is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes. This is not a Request for Proposals or a Request for Quotations, and it is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract/order nor is the Government responsible for any costs incurred in furnishing information provided under this RFI. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this RFI or Government use of any information provided. Further, the Government is not seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals at this time. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this RFI. Proprietary information must be clearly marked if included. The Government reserves the right to use any information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate, including using technical information provided by respondents in any resultant solicitation. Responses will assist the Government in determining the availability of potential solutions and commercial products in the market. At this time, no solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. The information and requirements in this RFI, and any attachments, is subject to change at the sole discretion of the Government. 2. Operational Environment & Hardware Baseline Constraints To ensure candidate software solutions can integrate into active cutter classes without widespread structural or electrical bridge overhauls, respondents must demonstrate compatibility with the following operational constraints: 2.1 Installed Hardware Baseline (E-NAV) The USCG fleet operates on a variety of IEC 60945 compliant hardware baselines consisting of: rack mounted industrial computers, rack mounted servers, ruggedized small factor computers, marine-grade All-in-One (AIO) Computer/Displays, system displays ranging from 15-19 inches, KVM matrix, ruggedized mouse and keyboard. 2.2 Operating System (OS) Gatekeeper Requirements Software architecture must natively support modern enterprise operating system standards: Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise (including Long-Term Servicing Channel [LTSC] builds). Enterprise Linux Distributions (e.g., Latest version of Red Hat Enterprise Linux [RHEL]). Vendors must state whether their software executes natively on Windows 11, Linux, or maintains a dual-OS cross-platform compiled codebase. 2.3 System Availability and Deterministic State Recovery Deterministic State Recovery: In the event of ungraceful bridge power interruption or system reset, the software must reboot and restore its previous operational state, active route, safety parameters, and sensor assignments without manual database rebuilding. 3. Core Functional Capability Matrix See Attachment. 3.1 Sensor Ingestion & Data Distribution Protocol Support: Native ingestion, parsing, translation, and broadcast of NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 (IEC 61162-3), NMEA OneNet, and Lightweight Ethernet (LWE)(IEC 61162-450) protocols. Sensor Interfacing: Interfacing with gyrocompasses, Doppler velocity logs (DVL), magnetic compasses, wind sensors, depth sounders, GPS/DGPS/Galileo receivers, Inertial Navigation Systems (INS), and radar targets (ARPA). Integrity & Checksum: Cryptographic and checksum integrity verification for all data streams; automated detection and notification of malformed or invalid sentences. Decoupled Time Distribution: Network time distribution via UDP/TCP; ability to assign an authoritative UTC time source independent of the primary positioning source. 3.2 Data Recording, Playback, and Forensics Comprehensive Logging: Continuous background recording of ownship dynamics, sensor inputs, target tracking data, alert histories, and operator interactions. Storage Flexibility: Ability to write logs and telemetry to internal storage, external mission media (USB/NAS), or enterprise shipboard repositories. Visual Playback: Integrated forensic playback mode providing time-synchronized replay of chart presentation, radar overlay, and sensor states for accident investigation and tactical debrief. 3.3 Chart Management & Next-Gen Hydrographic Standards Legacy Format Support: Seamless handling of S-57 ENC, S-63 encrypted charts, and DNC (Digital Nautical Chart) formats. S-100 Transition Framework: Implementation roadmap and readiness for the IHO S-100 Universal Hydrographic Data Model, specifically: S-101 Electronic Navigational Charts (ENC) S-102 High-Resolution Bathymetric Surfaces S-104 Water Level Information S-111 Surface Currents S-124 Navigational Warnings Manual Corrections: Ability to create, save, import, and visually verify manual notice-to-mariners chart corrections and local marine hazards. 3.4 Operational Display Area (ODA) & Ownship Dynamics Ownship Dynamics: Multi-source position fixing utilizing GNSS (GGA/GNS), INS, Radar Chart Matching, manual visual/radar Lines of Position (LOPs), and Dead Reckoning (DR). Dynamic Calculations: Automated computation of real-time Set and Drift, Course Over Ground (COG), Speed Over Ground (SOG), Speed Through Water (STW), and Rate of Turn (ROT). Tactical Plotting: Rapid generation of Danger Bearings/Ranges, Clearing Lines, Variable Range Markers (VRM), Electronic Bearing Lines (EBL), and instant Man Overboard (MOB) emergency markers. RADAR Overlay: Software must be compatible with Furuno SDK and SSR COMRIC for RADAR overlay capability. 3.5 Human-System Interface (HSI) & Publications Visual Standards: Full conformance with IHO S-52 Presentation Library colors, symbology, and display modes (Day, Dusk, Night). Coordinate Precision: Coordinate calculation and display capabilities resolving latitude and longitude to one thousandth of a second (0.001”). Nautical Nomenclature: Standardization using Pub. 9 (Bowditch) and Chart No. 1 nautical symbology and abbreviations. Electronic Publications: Native viewer for hydrographic reference materials, Standard Bearing Books, and Adobe PDF navigation documentation. 3.6 Cybersecurity, Information Assurance & System Management DoD/DHS Compliance: Architecture capable of being hardened to DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), meeting NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 security controls, and aligning with Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) parameters. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Distinct cryptographic user/administrator profiles, group policies, and role permissions preserved across software patches and upgrades. Configuration Auditing: Secure text-searchable configuration repositories, system event logging, and controlled patch deployment. 4. Specialized Coast Guard Mission Functions The legacy Vega suite incorporates specialized operational modules tailored to unique USCG mission sets. Prospective solutions must identify whether these capabilities exist natively, can be integrated via plug-in/APIs, or require custom development. 4.1 Western Rivers (WR) Navigation & ATON Management The software must provide the capability to: Database Management: Dedicated database maintaining Western Rivers Aids to Navigation (WR ATON) and dynamic river segments. Buoy Tending Workflow: Specialized user interface designed for USCG river tenders to track, position, edit, drop, and inspect buoys directly within the ODA. Depth Survey Mode: Ingestion and visualization of single-beam and multi-beam bathymetric survey depth data in real-time. Enterprise Synchronization: Capability to export, import, archive, and synchronize ATON position reports, worklists, and discrepancy logs with Coast Guard enterprise ashore systems. 4.2 STEDS / Sensitive Tactical Asset Tracking & Encrypted AIS The software must provide the capability to: Encrypted AIS (EAIS) Interfacing: Two-way transactional command, status, and messaging interface between the navigation engine and EAIS transponders. Software must have a transactional process between an EAIS transponder and be able to act as a Presentation Interface with a STEDS capable transponder. Blue Force Tracking (BFT): Ingestion and presentation of Sensitive but Unclassified (SBU) tactical data, Situation Reports (SITREPs), and friendly force positions. Tactical Target of Interest (TOI): Management of specialized tactical identifiers, target classification, and Intercept / Closest Point of Approach (CPA) calculations. SAR Integration: Automated generation, overlay, and management of standard Search and Rescue (SAR) patterns (e.g., Expanding Square, Parallel Search, Sector Search, Creeping Line) and tracklines. Tactical Messaging: Transmission and reception of Geographic Notice messages, tactical text bulletins, and Linkage ID route information. 5. Vendor Survey & Technology Discovery Questions 5.1 Architecture, Operating Systems & Hardware Modularity Describe your software's underlying architecture. Is it built upon a monolithic codebase, modular libraries, or containerized microservices? Detail your native OS support across Windows 11 Enterprise (64-bit) and Enterprise Linux [RHEL] 8/9/10 etc.). Do you maintain parity across both operating systems with a single unified codebase? What are the minimum and recommended compute specifications (CPU, RAM, GPU, storage throughput) to operate your software efficiently on Marine AIO panel computers? What are some unique features or characteristics that your software provides? In the event of an uncontrolled system shutdown or power loss, what failover, fallback, or rapid-reboot behaviors does your software execute to minimize Time to First Fix and restore safety to navigation displays? Can your software be manipulated to include a widget within the ODA to remotely control KVM switch if provided the KVM’s SDK? Is your software capable of allowing pre-loaded, programmed configurations, as well as selecting individualized configurations using a graphical user interface matrix? 5.2 Next-Generation Hydrographic Standards (IHO S-100) What is the current maturity and operational status of your software regarding the IHO S-100 framework? Specifically, what is your production timeline or current support for S-101 (ENC), S-102 (Bathymetry), and S-111 (Surface Currents)? How does your display engine handle dynamic layering and visual priority when multi-source datasets (e.g., bathymetry + vector chart + radar overlay) are active simultaneously? 5.3 Resilient PNT, Sensor Fusion & EW Mitigation How does your navigation engine detect, alert, and mitigate Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) anomalies, such as jamming, spoofing, or multipath drift? Does your system support automated sensor fusion and Kalman filtering across heterogeneous inputs (e.g., GPS, INS, Doppler Log, Compass, Radar Matching)? What is the system's failover behavior when primary PNT data is lost or declared untrusted? 5.4 Specialized Mission Module Adaptation (Western Rivers & STEDS) Does your platform currently possess native capabilities comparable to the Western Rivers ATON and STEDS/EAIS requirements detailed in Section 4? If not natively present, what mechanism does your software offer for government or third-party developers to integrate custom mission logic (e.g., Open APIs, Software Development Kits [SDKs], gRPC/REST endpoints, C++ / Python plugins)? What is the intellectual property (IP) and licensing model for custom plugins developed on your platform? 5.5 Modern Human-System Interface (HSI) & Usability How is your graphical user interface optimized for high-stress bridge operations, night-vision adaptation (red/low-light), and rapid touch/trackball interaction? 5.6 Cybersecurity, Patching & Lifecycle Support What is your experience in deploying software that meets DISA STIG requirements and undergoes DoD/DHS Risk Management Framework (RMF) assessment? How are vulnerability security patches delivered, validated, and applied without disrupting marine type approvals or custom operational configurations? What is your commercial licensing structure (e.g., perpetual node license, enterprise subscription, per-seat maintenance)? How does your company provide/handle continued product support and warranty contracts? 5.7 Core Navigation Engine and Data Lifecycle Describe how your software ingests, validates (via checksums/cryptography), and processes raw sensor data (e.g., GPS, INS, Gyro, DVL) Explain your system’s internal and networked data distribution architecture for sharing telemetry across bridge workstations. Detail your chart management workflow, including how the system updates, overlays, and prioritizes multi-format charts (ENC, DNC, S-100) Explain the technical architecture of your data logging system and how the forensic visual playback mode is executed without impacting active navigation performance. 6. Response Submission Instructions 6.1 Content & Format Guidelines Executive Summary: Maximum 2 pages highlighting corporate overview, maritime navigation experience, and core product offerings. Vendors are encouraged to provide links to publicly available marketing materials, spec sheets, or other applicable materials. Technical Capability Statement: Maximum 15 pages addressing the Functional Baseline (Section 3), Mission Modules (Section 4), and Vendor Discovery Questions (Section 5). Format: Submissions must be delivered electronically in Adobe PDF format (searchable, 11-point font minimum). 6.2 Company Information Cover Sheet All submissions must include a cover sheet detailing: Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone Number) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Business Size Standard under NAICS 513210 Existing Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWAC), GSA Multiple Award Schedules (MAS), or DoD Enterprise Software Initiative (ESI) vehicles held. 6.3 Submission Logistics Submission Deadline: October 23rd, 2026, no later than 5:00pm Eastern Time. Submission Delivery: Responses must be submitted via email to the USCG Contracting Personnel Listed Below: Contract Specialist: Roberta.F.Pluim@uscg.mil Contract Specialist: Eric.R.St.Pierre@uscg.mil Contracting Officer: Jessica.L.Coltz@uscg.mil Proprietary Data: If a respondent wishes to submit proprietary information, it must be clearly marked on each page containing proprietary data. The Government will handle proprietary material in accordance with applicable Federal statutes and FAR requirements.

sig_b498b4f3a2517da9153d.description: The subject of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration, commissioning and provision of support for software solutions based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support at St. Anne's University Hospital in Brno. The performance of the public contract is designed as the provision of software in the form of a cloud solution (SaaS). The supplier shall provide software operated in a cloud infrastructure, whereby: - installation of a full-fledged on-premise solution is not required, - data processing and storage will take place within the EU/EEA, unless another regime is expressly approved in writing by the contracting authority while simultaneously meeting all legal and security conditions), - integration into the contracting authority's systems (PACS, NIS) will be ensured via standard interfaces. The scope of performance therefore includes: - a time-limited usage right (licence/subscription) for the duration of the contract, - provision of operation, availability, updates and technical support as part of the service. The performance includes in particular: • delivery of medical devices in the form of software meeting the requirements of MDR (EU) 2017/745, • their integration into the contracting authority's information systems (PACS, NIS), • commissioning into live operation, • provision of service, technical support and updates for the duration of the contract. The supplier shall be insured for the entire duration of the contract against liability for damage caused in connection with the performance of the contract, with a minimum limit of indemnity in the amount of 5 000 000 CZK per one insurance event for each part of the public contract. The public contract (PC) is divided into 2 separate parts: Part 1 PC - AI Software for prostate cancer screening using artificial intelligence algorithms Part 2 PC - Software using artificial intelligence algorithms in chest X-ray diagnostics. The subject of this part of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration and support of a software solution based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support in the evaluation of prostate magnetic resonance (MR). The offered software must be a medical device within the meaning of Art. 2 para. 1 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council on medical devices (MDR) and must be duly placed on the market in the European Union. The system must be intended as a clinical decision-support tool for the detection, localisation and assessment of lesions suspicious for clinically significant prostate cancer. The aim of the system implementation is in particular: • increasing the quality and standardisation of prostate MR evaluation, • support for the early detection of clinically significant findings, • reduction of variability between evaluators, • streamlining the workflow of the radiology department, • support for multidisciplinary cooperation (radiology – urology). The system must not serve as a substitute for a doctor's clinical judgement; the final diagnostic decision is always made by an authorised healthcare professional.; The subject of this part of the public contract is the delivery, implementation, integration and operation of a software solution based on artificial intelligence intended for clinical decision support in the evaluation of chest X-ray images. The offered software must be a medical device within the meaning of Art. 2 para. 1 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and must be duly placed on the market in the European Union. The system is intended as a clinical decision-support tool for the detection and evaluation of pathological findings on chest X-rays. The system will be operated primarily at the Department of Imaging Methods and the Emergency Department of St. Anne's University Hospital in Brno and possibly at other workplaces of the contracting authority. The final clinical decision is always made by a healthcare professional.

sig_b49c5a65f5582fbb683f.description: Statnett’s mission is to ensure a secure electricity supply by building, operating and maintaining the Norwegian power system. We maintain emergency preparedness around the clock. Statnett is a state-owned enterprise under the Ministry of Energy. We also facilitate electrification and value creation for our customers and society. Statnett is establishing a modern security architecture based on Gartner’s Cybersecurity Mesh Architecture (CSMA) framework. A core component of CSMA is privileged access management, with identity serving as the perimeter for both humans and machines. Through this request for information, Statnett seeks to identify which solutions on the market manage privileged access in accordance with the CSMA framework. The solution Statnett seeks must support a hybrid infrastructure comprising both legacy and modern services. Please refer to the document “RFI Zero Trust platform” for further information.

sig_b4a36845e72980286d3a.description: 1.Legacy Data Viewer The Mental Health and Community Information System (MHCS) Programme within CAV UHB Digital and Health Intelligence is seeking to commission a legacy data viewer solution for circa 176 clinical services within Mental Health, community Health and Therapies services ahead of the approaching end of contract with the current EPR supplier. Due to the volume of clinical information and the bespoke nature of structured data within the current EPR, migrating the entirety of this data to a new EPR is not viable. Legacy data will need to be stored in a ‘Legacy Data Viewer’ solution accessible to services in an in-context launch. This solution entails the need to commission a dedicated team to deliver planning and designing, developing and testing a legacy data viewer solution within the current 2025/26 financial year. 2. Business Analysis: Service Mapping & Transformation Readiness The Mental Health and Community Information System (MHCS) Programme within CAV UHB Digital and Health Intelligence is seeking to commission Business Analysis expertise to apply best practices in preparing service readiness for an upcoming digital transformation project, including effectively documenting the ‘As Is’ business process/patient journey of 176 clinical services through service mapping templates and transferring this this BA toolkit to the team. Outputs will include requirements specification for service readiness documentation, service mapping plan, a bespoke process map template to apply to all MHCS services and ensure BA standardisation with comprehensive information to capture workflows and processes and a system integration map to ensure the network of integrations between the EPR in use and other systems is suitably captured. 3. Clinical Safety The Mental Health and Community Information System (MHCS) Programme within CAV UHB Digital and Health Intelligence is seeking to commission clinical safety expertise to apply DCB0129 and DCB0160 clinical safety standards to assess and inform the design and build of a data archive/viewer for accessing a legacy EPR. Requirements also include the transfer of clinical safety knowledge and best practices to the project team. This will entail working closely with the team involved in planning and deploying this solution, as well as the project team for knowledge transfer and training. Lot 1: .

Team Submarines, Australia, United Kingdom, and United States (AUKUS), International & Systems (AI&S), Submarine Electromagnetic Systems Program Office (PMS 435) is pleased to release a competitive Area of Interest (AOI) announcement for the Low Profile Mast (LPM) and Rotational Module (RM) component to address several key operational needs. The LPM/RM programs seek innovative technologies that accelerate the prototyping of capabilities that address these key operational needs. To accelerate the design, development and demonstration of LPM/RM capabilities, the Navy will be utilizing the Other Transaction Authority pathway outlined in Title 10 U.S.C. § 4022. It is intended that this solicitation may result in the award of one or more prototype projects. There are nine (9) attachments to this AOI, some of which contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): LPM/RM Terms of Use Agreement AOI AOI Guidance CUI LPM Type 24 Mod 1Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI LPM Verification Guide (VG) [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Verification Guide [RESTRICTED] LPM/RM AOI Questions Form CUI LPM/RM Placemat Template [RESTRICTED] Companies are advised to proceed with the following steps to respond to this notice: STEP 1 – Terms of Use Agreement (TOU) Several key documents related to the LPM Type 24 Mod 1 and RM are only releasable to eligible businesses with ownership in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Non-Australia, United Kingdom, or United States foreign-owned businesses may submit a technical solution as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more Australia, United Kingdom, or United States-owned businesses. The ability to be awarded an Agreement may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain access to restricted information. Companies interested in submitting a technical solution in response to the AOI shall complete Attachment 1: TOU Agreement and return it via e-mail to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialists listed in this notice. sig_b4c9ccfe6d612bf648f1.description: *** 14 July 2022- This Update makes an additional Approved for Public Release document, an Interface Description Document for C5ISR Systems Integration into Army Ground Vehicles, discoverable and available. *** 22 April 2022- This Update makes additional Approved for Public Release documentation, referenced by the CMOSS Interoperability Requirements Specification v1.1, discoverable and available. Additionally, referenced SOSA(TM) downloads are currently available at https://www.opengroup.org/library/c212 . Attachments MORA_Specification_V2.4_20210301_Final_DIST_A A519 .pdf MORA_Specification_V2.4_Revision_Notice_20210301_Final_DIST_A A520.pdf MORA_V2.4_ Specification_Atlas_Rev_F_Final_DIST_A A521.xlsx mora-wsdls-and-schemas-v2.4-DistA-20210225.zip VICTORY-Spec-Doc-V1-9-Dist-A-A787.pdf VICTORY_Architecture_A_DistroA_20190402.pdf -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This Special Notice initially aims to make the Approved for Public Release, "Command, Control, Communication, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance / Electronic Warfare (C5ISR/EW) Modular Open Suite of Standards (CMOSS) Interoperability Requirements Specification" (CMOSS IRS) widely discoverable and available. The intent is to periodically modify this Special Notice to: make additional Approved for Public Release and/or Controlled Unclassified Information documentation discoverable and available (Public download, Transmittal upon Request, or link to Authoritative Sources, as appropriate); broadcast syndicated announcements for events or opportunities of interest to members of the CMOSS-enabled ecosystem The purpose of the CMOSS Interoperability Requirements Specification is to provide a common, configuration-controlled, Science, Technology, Engineering, Experimentation, Test & Evaluation and Acquisition minimum baseline technical requirements document. This allows US Army (T), and Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, Multinational (JIIM) (O), materiel developers and integrators to ensure CMOSS compliant/conformant solutions are over-the-interface(s)-interoperable with other components/systems developed to the same "shalls". The requirements within this document should be incorporated by reference in contracts, citing the document title, revision number, and effective date of publication. 'CMOSS#####' Unique Identifiers (UID) will typically be linked as 'parent requirements' from which materiel system, subsystem, component, etc. 'child requirements' are derived. This CMOSS Interoperability Requirements Specification is under the configuration control of the chartered C5ISR Center MOSA Management Office (MMO). MOSA MANAGEMENT OFFICE RESPONSIBILITIES Coordinate MOSA usage across C5ISR Center Review S&T projects and identify cross cutting opportunities to include MOSA Allocate MOSA implementation funding for labs, experimentation, and matrixed SME support Provide MOSA training for directorate SME’s Facilitate technology transition Manage and mature standards Develop and maintain the CMOSS and VICTORY specifications Develop compliance tools and support compliance verification C5ISR Center lead for standards bodies such as the SOSA(TM) Consortium Coordinate with external MOSA activities Provide MOSA support to the acquisition community Consolidate resource requests for MOSA support facilities and staff Support inclusion of MOSA in policy and programs Coordinate/represent MOSA with external partners CMOSS is a suite of standards to support the reduction of the size, weight and power of C5ISR and EW systems while increasing the flexibility and adaptability of these systems Universal A-Kit Project Managers field capabilities as cards into a common chassis Pooled radio resources such as antennas and amplifiers for Communications, Electronic Warfare (EW), and Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) systems Shared processing resources such as computers and displays Shared data services such as Position, Navigation, and Time (PNT) Foundation for enhanced interoperability and simultaneity between C5ISR systems Reduced life cycle cost through increased competition, smaller logistics tails with common sparing, and upgrading to the latest hardware as parts are replaced Rapid insertion of new technology/capability Attachments 20220310-CMOSS-IRS-v1-1-Dist-A-A518.pdf (Public) and CMOSS Overview 18Mar22 Dist A A758.pdf (Public)

sig_b4cb85529a2d918a2c26.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. sig_b4d9cfe26155ca11b906.description: The City aims to partner with a software provider to support management of utility spend and consumption, with the ultimate aim of reducing cost and carbon. This will support Climate Action Strategy (CAS) goals and objectives of Net Zero in our own operations by 2027. The following represent essential requirements which must be met by the supplier, who must be able to provide and manage both software solutions and invoice validation services. 1. Provide invoice validation services. This includes utilities on the City's corporate contracts and ad-hoc supplies. All invoices must be loaded by the contractor into the software. 2. Provide easily accessible and customizable dashboards for cost, consumption and carbon based on portfolio, site, utility, meter level and Fund. 3. Provide high consumption notifications for any utility/site/meter, based on invoice or HH data. 4. Ensure customer satisfaction by allocating a dedicated account manager and accountability for KPI performance. 5. Invoices to Accounts payable are provided in a file format requested by the City in order to upload to the City's payment system (SAP). This must be completed for all utilities including electricity, gas, district heating/cooling and water. The City is seeking a software that will leverage recent advances in technology to support energy and cost reduction, along with improved access of resources. To support energy reduction, alerts must be configured to notify the user of high or low consumption. To minimise costs, reports must be generated based on elements of supplier invoices (i.e, standing charges, CCL, water and sewerage). To improve City resource use, the City wishes to use the software for tenant recharging for the first time. This must be completed by, at a minimum, subtracting submeters from the main fiscal meter. The City wishes to form a strong partnership with a provider who is eager to support the City's ambitious climate goals by freeing up City's resources to pursue energy opportunities, rather than day-to-day administrative tasks such as updating meter serial numbers in the database and chasing suppliers for costs. This tendering exercise is being undertaken using the electronic tendering system ‘City of London Corporation Sourcing & Contracts Portal’ (https://cityoflondon.ukp.app.jaggaer.com/) Suppliers will need to register an interest on the system in order to participate and registration is free. The estimated contract value given at sections 31 and 32 is for the full duration of the contract including the maximum possible extensions. The estimated annual contract value is therefore £112500 exc. VAT Lot 1: .

sig_b4e68a7c53995cdd762c.description: The subject of the service is the licensing, further development and technical operation of a campaign planning tool for all AOK regional companies and the AOK Federal Association, which facilitates joint processes. Campaign planning currently takes place in each AOK for its own campaigns, and in the AOK-BV for joint campaigns separately and using different tools. sig_b4f74a117c513861457f.description: Description NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy’s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company’s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click “My Profile”, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand “E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)”, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click “Send.” For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Classified material will be dispatched via USPS Registered Mail (or Government-approved commercial express carrier authorized for Secret transport). A double-envelope system will be utilized. The outer envelope will feature no classification markings. A signed Classified Material Receipt will be enclosed in the inner envelope. The Recipient must execute and return this receipt to the Government within five (5) business days of delivery. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION Proposals in response to this solicitation must be submitted electronically via the PIEE Solicitation Module no later than October 19, 2026, at 1600 (4:00 PM) Eastern Daylight Time. Detailed instructions for proposal preparation and submission are specified in Section L of the solicitation document provided on the secure E-TIC portal. SUBMISSION OF QUESTIONS AND COMMENTS All questions and comments regarding this solicitation must be submitted using the Offeror’s Question Submittal Form in its original Excel format. Unclassified Questions Submission Deadline: Questions must be received no later than 1600 (4:00 PM) Eastern Time on the twenty-fifth (25th) calendar day following the formal issuance of this solicitation. Weekend/Holiday Rule: If the twenty-fifth (25th) calendar day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal Holiday, the deadline is automatically extended to 1600 (4:00 PM) Eastern Time on the next consecutive business day. Questions received after this designated deadline will not be considered or answered. How to Submit: Submit the completed Offeror’s Question Submittal Form via email to the Points of Contact listed below. Email Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Question from [Insert Offeror Name]. Classified Questions Questions concerning classified matters shall be handled in strict accordance with the DD Form 254 and 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Offerors must contact the Points of Contact listed below via unclassified email for specific delivery and transmission instructions. Do not send classified questions or classified information directly to the unclassified email addresses listed below. POINTS OF CONTACT Matthew C. Hedrick Procuring Contracting Officer matthew.c.hedrick.civ@us.navy.mil (202) 781-4265 Michael J. Ravnitzky Contract Specialist michael.j.ravnitzky.civ@us.navy.mil (202) 781-3192

Within the investment objective "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact" – Procurement 1, the following contract objects have been defined: • Object 1 - Sub-object 1.1: Electrical Substation; - Sub-object 1.2: Related Systems (Digital Twin, Augmented Reality, Robotic Assistance/inspection and drones); • Object 5 – The electronic security system (ESS) of the objective and the fire security system (FSS); • Object 6 – The photovoltaic system. The detailed description can be found in the tender documentation. Number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders: 22 The contracting entity shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification / additional information in two stages, as follows: - on the 17th calendar day from the publication of the contract notice and - on the 11th calendar day before the time limit for the submission of tenders. The contracting entity shall respond only to requests for clarifications addressed by economic operators by the established time limit. 1.1 Object 1 – Retrofitting of the Mostiștea substation This object consists in turn of two sub-objects and the corresponding Specifications: 1.1.1 Mostiștea electrical substation The 220 kV substation shall be of outdoor type, with air insulation, implemented with conventional equipment, located on the decommissioned surface of the current 220 kV substation. The 110 kV substation shall be of indoor type, equipped with enclosed switchgear panels, with air/technical gas insulation, in three-phase construction. The 20 kV substation shall be located in the building of the current medium voltage substation. In this project, two new, independent auxiliary services units have been provided, namely a direct current (d.c.) unit and an alternating current (a.c.) unit respectively, as follows: • a d.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the d.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV, 20 kV substation, autotransformers AT1, AT2 and transformer units T1 and T2 110/20 kV; • an a.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the a.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV and 20 kV substation Within the work "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact", the technical condition module will be implemented in accordance with the Smart Grid reference architecture, for asset management at the level of the Mostiștea substation, called "Condition Monitoring System (CMS)". In the telecommunications field, within this project the following shall be performed: • ensuring the technical equipment for data and/or voice transmissions (HW&SW) necessary for: o carrying out the traffic required by the EMS/SCADA System; o remote control of the substation from the CTSI/DET level; o monitoring and parameterisation of protection systems from the level of the SSCPA of the Bucharest Branch and the DEN headquarters; o data-voice transmissions for operation and maintenance needs; o ensuring telecommunication facilities for the control of the substation; o the interzonal oscillation monitoring system (synchrophasors); o ensuring the transmission channels for metering data, local metering and power quality data. o ensuring hardware redundancy for interfaces that receive/transmit data and/or voice, which require this. o creation of telecommunication facilities to ensure the voice and/or data traffic requirements due to the emergence of a new Integrated IT/Information System, provided, at this stage, to be composed, in principle, of the following Systems:  Components/Sub-systems of the Asset Management System in Procurement 1 of the project:  AR, Digital Twin and PIA  BMS (also receives information from SIS - Integrated (Physical) Security)  Integrated (Physical) Security; • provision of technical equipment for cybersecurity (HW&SW); • provision of transmission equipment for teleprotection (HW&SW) Construction and installation works related to the performance of retrofitting works in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact: The new control block building will be a ground floor + 1 storey construction, designed according to the nZEB concept and as an intelligent building. Within this project, a dedicated building management system (BMS) architecture will be provided at the level of the Bucharest Branch, capable of integrating both the local BMS from the Mostiștea substation and the future BMS systems belonging to the other electrical substations under the management of the Bucharest Branch. The BMS system to be implemented in the Mostiștea substation will have the following integrated: • The control block; • The 110 kV GIS building; • Old medium voltage building; • Relay containers and photovoltaic installation container; • Perimeter lighting in the substation. 1.1.2 Related systems: I. Digital Twin and Augmented Reality – consisting mainly of: • equipment (hardware and/or software), (re)configurations, services, tests/measurements and works in:  The 220/110 kV Mostiștea Substation;  Bucharest Branch;  CNTEE Transelectrica SA Head Office. • integration/interfacing with the telecommunications infrastructure; • integration/interfacing with the systems in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea electrical substation from which it retrieves data/information, mainly:  Condition Monitoring System;  BMS; • integration into the Beneficiary's existing and new installations. II.• Substation robotic inspection assistance (Intervention and Assistance Platform - PIA). In the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation, advanced monitoring solutions will be implemented by developing inspection and analysis platforms that include both physical robots, such as drones and hardware robots, and software robots, capable of improving monitoring, maintenance and intervention processes.

1.5 Object 5 – "Electronic Security System (ESS) of the site and Fire Security System (FSS)" The 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation shall be provided with the ESS+FSS Integrated Security System. 1.6 Object 6 – Photovoltaic System Within the investment project "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept and with low environmental impact", considering the nZEB building and energy efficiency requirements as well as the transition to GIS technology of the 110 kV substation, on the surface of the current 110 kV substation cleared following the retrofitting, a ground-mounted photovoltaic system shall be implemented, with photovoltaic panels mounted on a metal structure, and with the related equipment mounted in a dedicated metal container. Estimated contract execution duration - 40 months according to the execution schedule in the specifications.
sig_b5285b4fbd447a5b1d37.title: "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation into a digital substation concept with low environmental impact" – Procurement 1

sig_b54bebbbfa32e48eae56.description: Full-line dispensing system for the hospital pharmacy Lot LOT-0001: Full-line dispensing system for the hospital pharmacy. For the corporate group Klinikum St. Georg, an automated full-line dispensing system for the hospital pharmacy is to be procured, including delivery, installation, commissioning, maintenance, conveyor technology, control software, interface integration, training, as well as a service and maintenance contract. The installation and integration into the existing pharmacy premises are of crucial importance. The available space must not be exceeded by the dispensing system and must optimally support the process workflow. The feeding and output of the medications must be able to take place in an automated manner. The fully automatic dispensing machine must be dimensioned in such a way as to enable optimal use and maximisation of the storage space given a limited amount of space on site. The conveyor technology and control software must be designed so that storing and retrieving take place with the greatest possible flexibility and speed. Due to their functional and technical dependencies, the described services are to be regarded as an indivisible economic entity. Splitting them into individual lots or awarding partial services would considerably impair coordination, quality assurance and economical service provision. For this reason, only a complete tender is permitted.

During the duration of the dynamic purchasing system, all interested candidates may submit a request for participation. The operation and scope of the dynamic purchasing system are described in more detail in the invitation to participate and its attachments. According to the preliminary estimate, dozens of procurements will be carried out within the dynamic purchasing system over the coming years. The total value of the procurements is estimated to be 65 000 000 EUR during the entire duration of the DPS for comprehensive service procurements. The dynamic purchasing system is designed to address procurement needs in the coming years, with a sufficient amount to achieve the objectives. This is an estimate, and the contracting authority is not committed to any specific procurement quantities. The number of procurements may be significantly lower than estimated if the objectives of the snow management system are met through other means. sig_b5de943dc0f871c7823f.description: The contracting authority invites you to submit a tender for expert services in accordance with this invitation to tender and its appendices. The project is implemented jointly by Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences (HHUAS), Tampere University (TAU) and the University of Helsinki (HY). The administration of the project package is the responsibility of Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences, which, inter alia, procures through a competitive tender process the IT services required in the RDI project and external additional experts for the research team as needed. Haaga-Helia and Tampere University are responsible for the legality of the procurement procedure. The University of Helsinki is involved in the procurement solely as a separate participant in the research project. SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is the consultancy service of two IT experts for the publicly funded GAIK project (Generative AI-Enhanced Knowledge Management in Business) implemented by Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences (HHUAS). The procurement involves the implementation of a connector framework for the GAIK toolkit, which enables the connection of solutions based on generative artificial intelligence to organisations' data sources in a uniform and reusable manner. The assignment includes the design and implementation of a generic connector engine and connection interface, the development of connectors for Microsoft 365 (OneDrive and SharePoint), Google Drive and file shares, the implementation of a connector configuration user interface, and the integration of synchronisation, error handling and security functionalities as part of the GAIK toolkit. The solution to be implemented will be released as open-source software at the end of the project. The contracting authority estimates that the expert workload required for the GAIK Toolkit development sub-package now being put out to tender is a total of approximately 70 person working days. The assignment requires two experts, which corresponds to approximately 35 person working days per expert. The working language of the project is English. All project materials and documents to be drawn up shall be in English. A language proficiency requirement in the English language has therefore been set for the experts appointed by the tenderer. The description of the subject of the procurement and the minimum requirements are described in this invitation to tender and its appendices. SCHEDULE AND CONTRACT PERIOD The development work is expected to begin after the signing of the agreement. The contracting authority assumes that work can begin on 17.10.2026. The final results of the assignment must be delivered no later than 31.12.2026. The client has the right to request corrections or clarifications to the final results before granting permission for invoicing. The requested corrections and clarifications must be delivered by the beginning of January 2027. The assignment must be invoiced no later than 15.1.2027. The contracting parties shall agree on a more detailed work schedule. The work will progress in phases, and interim targets will be set for the work on a monthly basis, unless more frequently. At the beginning of the work, a more detailed progress plan shall be drawn up, which shall be approved by the client. The agreement shall enter into force when both contracting parties have signed it. The contract period ends when the implementation and follow-up work have been successfully completed. The termination of the agreement shall not affect the validity of terms that are intended to remain in force after the termination of the agreement, such as terms concerning confidentiality, limitations of liability and warranty. The customer has the right to extend the contract period by one (1) optional period of a maximum of one (1) year. The customer must notify in writing of the exercise of the option period no later than one (1) month before the estimated completion date of the implementation.
sig_b5de943dc0f871c7823f.title: Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences - WP3 Connectors - IT Consulting 2023-2028 (DPS) - Application and Software Development Services

sig_b5f8d7e1036070077b97.description: The Norwegian Maritime Directorate's vision for the strategy period 2025-2028 is to be "The Preferred Maritime Administration". The strategy emphasises user orientation, effective use of resources and further development of digital services and work processes. The aim is to deliver modern and available systems that support both internal needs and interaction with the industry and other collaboration partners. To support this work, the Norwegian Maritime Directorate has over time established a service orientated platform - the total architecture - which is central for efficient case handling and digital services. The joint management team is responsible for the further development, operation and error recovery of the case handling systems, the customer surfaces and the subsystems included in this platform. A large part of the team ́s portfolio shall, in the long term, be discontinued, whilst other parts shall be further developed and lifted to a cloud. The work includes i.a. needs analysis, estimation, development, testing, production and close dialogue and cooperation with product owners, professional environments and external cooperation partners (DigDir, Sikri etc.). At the same time, the Norwegian Maritime Directorate is in a transitional phase where the organisation is gradually moving from project based development to a more product orientated organisation. This means that the current team structure can, over time, be organised into different product areas with clearer responsibilities and ownership. The ambition is that this shall contribute to more general priorities, better interaction and a more efficient and professional management and further development of the systems.
sig_b5f8d7e1036070077b97.title: Shared Product Management Team 2026

sig_b6057fa9f62ce2c7a89c.description: Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue has decided to cancel the procurement of personal safety solutions. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue has checked the conformity of the tenders received by the deadline and ascertained the fulfilment of the suitability requirements. In connection with checking the suitability requirements, the contracting entity has evaluated the content of the call for tenders and its annexes, as well as the answers to supplementary questions regarding the call for tenders given during the procurement procedure. In the evaluation, it was established that the reference requirement set in the call for tenders concerning a positioning accuracy of 5 metres has remained ambiguous, in particular as regards whether the reference delivery should have included portable alarms whose alarm event location information is located with an accuracy of at least 5 metres. Consequently, the contracting entity considers that the call for tenders has been unclear regarding an essential requirement in the manner referred to in Section 67 of the Public Procurement Act. The ambiguity may have affected the comparability of the tenders and prevented the realisation of equal and non-discriminatory treatment of tenderers. Consequently, the contracting entity considers that there is a genuine and justified reason referred to in Section 125 of the Public Procurement Act for cancelling the procurement procedure. The procurement will be cancelled and prepared anew.
