sig_b7fcaeb2cd1f08b33f2a.description: Section 47 of the 1999 Act, which refers to section 45 of the Electricity Supply Act 1927, gives the Contracting Authority legal powers to decide to grant or refuse to grant a special order on the application of ESB, or of a holder of an authorisation to construct or reconstruct a generating station for the purpose of supply to final customers, or to construct an interconnector, or of a person who has applied for such an authorisation, in certain circumstances. Section 45 of the Electricity Supply Act sets out the legal basis for the compulsory acquisition of any land, easement, or other right over land, or to acquire or use compulsorily any right over land by special order. Section 45 also establishes a procedure for exercising that compulsory acquisition power. In considering whether or not to grant a special order the Contracting Authority may hold a public inquiry. This legislation can be found on www.irishstatutebook.ie and the revised acts, administrative consolidations of the legislation, can be found on www.lawreform.ie. The Contracting Authority expects that one or more applications for a special order may be received and is seeking (by this Competition) to appoint a framework of Inspectors. The Contracting Authority is seeking an Inspector to review, chair a public inquiry (if required), prepare a written reasoned report, assess the relevant information and make a recommendation to the Commissioners on an application for a special order(s). The Contracting Authority is proposing that a panel of Inspectors be procured. The Inspector will work closely with a secretariat, who will provide all administrative, logistical, technical and environmental supports, where required, to complete the review. The Contracting Authority will separately appoint a service provider to provide Secretariat services to support the Contracting Authority and any appointed Inspector.
sig_b7fcaeb2cd1f08b33f2a.title: Framework Agreement for the Provision of Inspector Services [544A]

sig_b85395b18665e1d0c71b.description: The West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) is made up of 18 local councils, working together to make the West Midlands the best place to live, work and visit. Our priorities include homes, jobs, transport and growth for everyone. As an organisation, we're focused on making life better for people in the West Midlands. To achieve this, WMCA, working with partners as part of the West Midlands Investment Zone, is developing a specification to assess the capacity and capability of local skills and education providers to deliver high level skills and qualifications across several identified sectors and clusters. The WMCA is seeking to commission an evaluation of the current Skills Delivery Capacity with a focus on its Investment Zones during 2026. The purpose of the commission will be to understand and assess what the current skills capacity is to deliver high level skills that will support Investment Zone (IZ) aims and objectives as well as wider aspirations within the WMCA Growth Plan. Furthermore, it is intended that when WMCA do approach the market, the successful supplier will: • Assess and identify how the current skills ecosystem and training delivery capacity can be strengthened. • Outline how WMCA can enhance collaboration among Further Education (FE), Higher Education (HE), and private providers to meet industry needs reducing fragmentation and inefficient engagement. • Assess the current higher-level skills offer in the region at Level 4 and Level 5 training providers and with particular reference to the identified WM clusters. • Design and produce a mechanism for providing ongoing periodic assessment of this landscape to understand where gaps are reducing, being maintained or increasing and make recommendations accordingly. Lot 1: .
sig_b85395b18665e1d0c71b.title: Investment Zone Scoping – Higher Skills Capacity Evaluation

sig_b87b4b06a62abd218402.description: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is undertaking this procurement in its own name and on behalf of the other participating trusts within the South 4 Pathology Network, namely Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust, Milton Keynes University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The Authority intends to procure a Pathology Managed Equipment Service (MES) to support high-quality, resilient and standardised pathology services across participating sites. The service is expected to cover the provision, installation, commissioning and lifecycle management of pathology laboratory equipment, together with maintenance, servicing, repair, upgrades, replacement planning, training and performance support. The scope of testing is expected to focus primarily on blood sciences and related hospital laboratory services, including biochemistry, haematology, coagulation, serology, immunology, automation and pre-pre-analytics such as specimen tracking and auto receipting. The service model is expected to include equipment supply through capital and/or leased models, asset management, consumables and reagents where required, inventory and logistics management, interoperability with existing and future LIMS, digital enablement, automation, data and reporting capability, technical support, training and continuous service improvement. The procurement project is aligned to NHS pathology transformation priorities. It is also expected to contribute to sustainability and social value objectives. The service will be delivered across multiple NHS sites within the South 4 Pathology Network geography, with flexibility for future changes to network configuration. The Authority anticipates awarding either a single supplier or multi-lot contract, with the final structure and contract term to reflect equipment lifecycle and long-term service delivery requirements. The information provided is indicative only and does not constitute a call for competition or commitment to procure. This Pre Market Engagement notice is issued in accordance with the requirements of the Procurement Act 2023. Lot 1: .

sig_b883c73f6fb0cf397736.description: We are making Hämeenlinna the best public procurer in Finland! Consequently, we want any potential future procurement described in this market consultation also to be the best in Finland. For that, we need the help of operators who appreciate honest and open dialogue with the contracting authority, who enjoy competition and who want to represent the pinnacle of their field. This is a market consultation in accordance with Finland's new Public Procurement Act. All information contained in this market consultation is preliminary and therefore does not bind Hämeenlinnan kaupunki in any way. PRELIMINARY DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT Hämeenlinnan kaupunki is surveying solutions available on the market as a platform for substitute management in early childhood education. Approximately 490 people work in the city's early childhood education and activities are organised in 19 day-care centres. The estimated average volume of short-term substitutes is approximately 110–140 people. The city is seeking a solution that streamlines the overall substitute management process, reduces manual work and enables the efficient and economical use of personnel resources. The substitute management platform aims for a comprehensive solution that can be used to manage the recruitment of short-term substitutes as well as the offering and booking of shifts, and to enable the smooth transfer of necessary data to payroll. In addition, the platform is intended to manage the allocation of the permanent early childhood education staff pool to units. Through the market consultation, we are seeking information on solutions available on the market and their potential to meet the city's operational needs. From interested suppliers, we also appreciate information on what kind of integrations into payroll systems have been implemented for your solution and whether an integration from the solution has been implemented into Visma's Personec F system, which is in use by the City of Hämeenlinna. In addition, we request an estimate of the duration of a typical deployment project. REGISTRATION Interested operators are requested to register their interest in participating in the potential procurement via the Tarjouspalvelu portal. Answering the market consultation is not a prerequisite for participating in any potential tendering procedure organised later. Registrations are requested to be made by 23.10.2026 at 16.00. OTHER INFORMATION This is not a call for tenders or a procurement notice, so the publication of this notice does not initiate a tendering procedure; rather, this is a market consultation. This notice does not oblige Hämeenlinnan kaupunki to carry out the actual procurement. Failing to answer the market consultation does not prevent participation in a potential tendering procedure, nor does answering the market consultation affect the tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure in any way. Hämeenlinnan kaupunki will not pay compensation for answering the market consultation or for participating in the market consultation and market dialogue.

sig_b893295fcb04d926edf8.description: Identification of a service provider to carry out the functional design and technical implementation of an AI-based care solution for non-communicable diseases for the project "EVIGAIN 2025". Lot LOT-0001: EVIGAIN 2025 - Functional design and technical implementation of an AI-based care solution for non-communicable diseases. 3.1 Type of service The subject of this procedure is the awarding of a contract for the functional design and technical implementation of an AI-based care solution for non-communicable diseases to improve patient care in the field of non-communicable illnesses. Details can be found in the contractual documents. In preparation for this procurement procedure, the contracting authority (CA) has already drawn up the content components and an MVP. These components form the basis for the technical implementation by the contractor (CO). For the functional design and technical implementation, an independent backend must be provided as an API service (container-based), which handles authentication/authorisation, multi-tenancy, audit logging, data access and the orchestration of AI functions (in particular RAG). The interfaces must be documented as a versioned REST API including OpenAPI/Swagger specification. Secrets must not reside in the frontend at any time. The source code must be provided via GitHub and operated using CI/CD (build, tests, security scans, deployment). Lot 2 Maintenance of the NCM Compliance System • Ensure the SBEM calculation engine, iSBEM interface and all associated documentation remains valid, secure, and accessible. • Ensure integration with external systems such as the EPC register and 3rd party software tools is maintained • Provide user support and technical guidance Estimated initial duration 36 months - this is likely to be a recurring requirement. sig_b8ddfed44fc145fd8df5.description: Award Notice Award Notice Page 3 of 8 Award Notice *= Required FieldAward Notice Page 1 of 8 DESCRIPTION Competition: Sole Source This order was awarded on a sole source basis under the authority of the contractor s existing Federal Supply Schedule contract. The Justification & Approval (J&A) supporting this determination is attached to this award notice in accordance with FAR 6.305 and FAR 13.501 requirements. Description of Requirement: The VA Boston Healthcare System requires replacement and upgrade of ScriptPro automated prescription dispensing systems and related equipment at the West Roxbury, Brockton, and Jamaica Plain campuses. Work includes delivery, installation, Workflow Management System 2.0 upgrades, workstation replacement, robotic components, and associated support. All items are ordered under FSS Contract 36F79719D0135. Place of Performance: VA Boston Healthcare System West Roxbury, Brockton, Jamaica Plain DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b) Sole Source Justifications Exceeding Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) Page 1 of Acquisition ID: 36C241-26-AP-3255 Page 8 of 8 Page 8 of 8 Page 1 of This justification aligns with the deviation outlined in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) for Part 8.4 - Ordering under the Federal Supply Schedule and GSAM/R 538.71, as required by Executive Order (E.O.) 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement, signed April 15, 2025. Deviation effective date: November 3, 2025. Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C241-26-AP-3255 ScriptPro Prescription Medication Filling Robot Replacement. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 01, located at 555 Willard Avenue, Newington, CT, In support of VISN 01_VA Health Care Systems. Brockton VAMC, 940 Belmont St., Brockton, MA 02301-5596 Jamaica Plain VAMC, 150 South Huntington Ave., Boston, MA 02132-4924 West Roxbury VAMC, 1400 VFW Parkway, West Roxbury, MA 02132-4927 2237: 523-26-3-1484-0036 Description of Action: This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Multiple-Award Schedule Program (41 U.S.C. 152(3) and 40 U.S.C. 501). The VA Boston Health Care System (VABHS) is requesting replacement of the existing ScriptPro Equipment at all three campus locations. This is a new firm-fixed price order to replace the existing equipment that is at the end of its useful life (>15 years), and replacement will mitigate future degradation of services. Order against: FSS Contract Number: 36F79719D0135 Name of Proposed Contractor: ScriptPro USA, Inc. Street Address: 5828 Reeds Road City, State, Zip: Shawnee Mission, KS 66202 Phone: 800-606-7628 Description of Supplies or Services: The estimated value of the proposed action is $1,171,788.09 The VA Boston Healthcare System (VABHS) utilizes the ScriptPro prescription dispensing system to automate the repetitive, manual dispensing tasks most subject to human error and automatically collates all prescriptions for each patient for pickup or mail. ScriptPro interfaces with VistA to fill, label, and collate up to 150 prescription vials per hour. The system holds 200 frequently used medications to improve operational efficiency. The system enforces barcode scanning throughout the process for accuracy, safety, and quality control. The system provides real-time inventory tracking, order generation, electronic transmission to the prime-vendor, and inventory receiving for the outpatient pharmacies. This order includes 124-line items and 42 equipment uninstalls. [Reference] Item BR JP WR Total ScriptPro 200/CCC (6 Slot) 1 1 1 3 Workflow Management System Software 2.0 (WMS 2.0) 1 1 1 3 Pharmacy Workstation 10 13 10 33 Notice Board 40 1 1 1 3 Remote Access Server for WMS 1 1 1 3 Robot Cell Multiplexor 3 3 3 9 Robotic Inspection Camera 1 1 1 3 Platform to Expanded Platform Conversion 2 1 1 4 Full Disk Encryption (per server computer/HCI VM) 1 2 2 5 Customer Hard Drive Retention HCL 1000 / HCL 2000 / Workflow Platform Server 1 1 1 3 Customer Hard Drive Retention Robotic Systems 1 1 1 3 Endpoint Security Management (per pharmacy) 1 1 1 3 Endpoint Security (per server/client computer) 15 18 15 48 SPCE On-Site Upgrade, Gen 9, Server OS 2019, SQL 2019 1 0 0 1 Totals 40 45 39 124 ScriptPro retains exclusive rights to perform system upgrades, major hardware updates, software enhancements, and configuration changes. These OEM exclusive services include Platform to Expanded Server upgrades, GEN9 upgrades, and WMS 1.0 to 2.0 transitions functions that authorized distributors, such as Veterans Healthcare Supply Solutions (VHSS), are not permitted or qualified to perform under ScriptPro s commercial business model. This structure aligns with typical industry practices where distributors may sell new equipment but are not authorized to execute proprietary installation, modification, or upgrade work. ScriptPro holds active patents covering: Prescription storage and retrieval systems with proprietary robotics and transport mechanisms (U.S. Patent 10,346,590). Its CRS/CRS-150 robots include features such as direct-to-vial dispensing, cross-contamination safeguards, integrated labeling and barcode verification, and workflow interface not offered by other manufacturers. The VA Boston Pharmacy has utilized ScriptPro equipment, technology, and support services for over 20 years. The equipment has been reliable and has a proven history of success and switching to another system would require: Full replacement of hardware/software modules. Switching systems mid-operation would disrupt direct patient care including inability to process prescriptions if systems fail or are replaced. Extensive retraining Revalidation of workflows and integrations (e.g., with RPMS, Cerner). ScriptPro s uptime (>99%) and accuracy (~99.7%) are integral to maintaining reliable dispensing operations Increased downtime and cost risk. Identify the Authority and Supporting Rationale (see below and if applicable, a demonstration of the proposed contractor s unique qualifications to provide the required supply or service. GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(i): An urgent and compelling need exists and following the ordering procedures would result in unacceptable delays: GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii): Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized; GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii): In the interest of economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-on to an original Federal Supply Schedule order provided that the original order was placed in accordance with the applicable Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures. The original order must not have been previously issued under sole source or limited source procedures. GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iv): It is necessary to place the order with a particular FSS contractor to satisfy a minimum guarantee established in the FSS BPA; or GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(v): A law expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified source. GSAM/R 538.7104-4: Items peculiar to one manufacturer. The required replacement equipment, system upgrades, and software enhancements for the VA Boston Healthcare System s automated prescription dispensing systems are peculiar to ScriptPro as the sole manufacturer. ScriptPro maintains exclusive proprietary rights over the system architecture, hardware components, software platforms, and all major configuration and upgrade processes necessary for continued safe and effective operation of the pharmacy automation systems currently in use. ScriptPro retains ownership of all patents associated with its robotic dispensing, storage, and vial-handling technologies, including features such as direct-to-vial dispensing, integrated labeling, barcode verification, and contamination-prevention mechanisms. These patented capabilities are not offered by any other manufacturer, and no alternate vendor can provide equipment compatible with ScriptPro s proprietary system design. Describe Why You Believe the Order Represents the Best Value consistent with GSAM/R 538.7102-2(b)(4) to aid the contracting officer in making this best value determination: The proposed order represents the best value to the Government in accordance with GSAM/R 538.7102-2(b)(4) because it ensures continuity of operations, system compatibility, and compliance with OEM exclusive technical requirements essential to maintaining safe, accurate, and efficient pharmacy services. ScriptPro systems currently in use at all three VA Boston campuses have been fully integrated with VistA and pharmacy workflows for more than 20 years, and the equipment performs critical dispensing, labeling, barcoding, inventory, and workflow management functions that directly affect patient safety and service delivery. Replacement of these end of life systems with the OEM s upgraded hardware and software ensures seamless compatibility with existing interfaces, preserves patient safety driven automation features, and prevents service disruptions that would occur if alternative systems were introduced. Price reasonableness was validated through comparison with ScriptPro s current VA Federal Supply Schedule pricing, and market research confirmed that quoted prices align exactly with the established FSS price list. However, IAW GSAM/R 538.7102-2(c)(2), further price discounts or other concessions should be sought before placing an order or establishing an FSS BPA. Only ScriptPro can perform the required OEM exclusive upgrades, including Platform to Expanded Server upgrades, GEN9 upgrades, and the WMS 2.0 transition. These upgrades are proprietary and cannot be performed by authorized distributors such as VHSS, nor by any alternative source. Selecting any vendor other than the OEM would create substantial risks of operational downtime, invalid warranty coverage, cybersecurity noncompliance, and failure of critical patient care systems. Describe the Market Research Conducted among schedule holders and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. Market research was conducted in accordance with RFO Part 10 and VAAR 810.001 70, as required for acquisitions under the Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures referenced in GSAM/R 538.7104 3(b). The Contract Specialist performed extensive research to determine whether any sources other than ScriptPro could fulfill the VA Boston Healthcare System s requirement for replacement pharmacy automation systems and OEM exclusive system upgrades. This research included a review of historical VA acquisitions for ScriptPro equipment across multiple VISN 1 facilities, analysis of prior contract vehicles, and verification of available vendors in SAM.gov and SBA s SBS database under NAICS 339112. The search identified 983 SDVOSB/VOSB entities under the NAICS code; however, no verified firms were found that manufacture ScriptPro compatible systems or possess authorization to perform the proprietary upgrades required for continued pharmacy operations. Further review of schedule holders confirmed that ScriptPro remains the only FSS contractor capable of meeting the VABHS requirement under FSS Contract 36F79719D0135, consistent with MAS ordering authorities under 41 U.S.C. 152(3) and 40 U.S.C. 501. Direct engagement with ScriptPro representatives validated that all required upgrades including the Platform to Expanded Server upgrade, GEN9 upgrade, and Workflow Management System (WMS) 1.0 to 2.0 transition are OEM exclusive, proprietary services. ScriptPro maintains the sole rights to its system architecture, software code, firmware, robotic mechanisms, and configuration utilities, and no third party distributor (including VHSS) is authorized or qualified to perform these tasks. This proprietary limitation is reinforced by ScriptPro s active U.S. patents covering vial handling robotics, direct to vial dispensing, integrated barcode verification, and contamination prevention features capabilities not offered by any other domestic manufacturer. Because the required upgrades involve access to source controlled elements of ScriptPro s system, only the OEM can legally and technically perform the effort, meeting the criteria for limited source justification under GSAM/R 538.7104 3(b)(1)(ii) and GSAM/R 538.7104 4. Market research further demonstrated that replacing ScriptPro with an alternate automation platform would require a full divestiture of existing hardware, software, and workflow interfaces. Such a conversion would entail months of operational downtime, extensive staff retraining, revalidation of inventory workflows, reintegration with VistA and VA pharmacy systems, and acceptance testing of a new robotic dispensing architecture all of which would severely disrupt outpatient pharmacy operations. The risk is especially unacceptable given the essential nature of reliable, high volume prescription dispensing in support of direct patient care. ScriptPro s systems have been used successfully by VA Boston for over 20 years with demonstrated uptime exceeding 99% and accuracy above 99.7%, and replacing this mature ecosystem with unfamiliar technology presents significant patient safety, cyber security, warranty, and operational reliability hazards. Pricing provided by ScriptPro aligns exactly with its published VA Federal Supply Schedule price list, supporting price reasonableness under GSAM/R 538.7102 2(b)(4). The requirement was also evaluated in accordance with the hierarchy of preferences established under the Veterans First Contracting Program (VAAR 819.70), but no SDVOSB or VOSB exists that can perform the OEM exclusive upgrades or provide compatible equipment. Based on all available evidence, the results of market research conclusively demonstrate that ScriptPro is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Government s minimum needs without introducing unacceptable mission critical risk. Accordingly, the market research fully supports a sole source action to ScriptPro under FSS Contract 36F79719D0135. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification: Additional supporting facts reinforce the need to limit consideration to ScriptPro. The existing pharmacy automation systems at the VA Boston Healthcare System have reached end of life after more than 15 years of continuous use, and failure to replace or upgrade these systems would result in significant degradation of outpatient prescription services, workflow disruptions, and increased risk to patient safety. ScriptPro equipment is fully integrated with VistA and existing pharmacy operations, and the VA Boston pharmacies rely on ScriptPro s established automation capabilities including barcode verified dispensing, real time inventory tracking, and automated vial filling and collating to maintain accuracy, efficiency, and uninterrupted prescription processing. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services is made: To reduce barriers to competition in future acquisitions, the agency will continue to monitor the automated pharmacy systems marketplace to identify whether alternative manufacturers develop solutions that are interoperable with VA pharmacy platforms or capable of meeting VA Boston s high volume, high accuracy dispensing needs. The agency will also reassess the market during future technology refresh cycles to determine whether proprietary constraints have changed or whether third party vendors gain authorization to perform upgrades, maintenance, or system modifications.

sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.description: UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre. This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce. This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to: 1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment. 2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce. 3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery. This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties. UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes. Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties. To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.

The Finance and HR systems may be provided as separate products/solutions however seamless integration must be demonstrated. whg anticipated key dates in relation to the Contract are detailed in the tender documentation and split between Mobilisation / Build, License Minimum term with the option to extend at whg’s sole discretion. An outline is provided below: • HR System o Mobilisation / Build Period: February 2027 o Go Live: January 2028 o Minimum term: 7 years and 3 months with the option to extend for further periods of up to 5 (five) years at whg’s sole discretion. • Finance System o Mobilisation / Build Period: February 2027 o Go Live: April 2028 o Minimum term: 7 years with the option to extend for further periods of up to 5 (five) years at whg’s sole discretion. whg and Aspire Housing are in early talks around a potential merger of the two organisations to create a new housing association with over 32,000 homes across their Midlands heartlands. The merger would see the creation of a new housing association, building on an existing footprint across the West Midlands and Staffordshire. Under the proposals, whg and Aspire aim to bring together the best from both organisations to provide excellent housing services, create more regional growth opportunities and build more affordable homes for people in local communities. The estimated contract value includes an allowance for the merger proportion (35%) of licenses and additional costs associated with implementation/build phase over the term including the extension options. Please see the tender documentation for the full description and requirements. Lot 1: .

sig_b8f1a4a9df7c21ddf35a.description: Stad Hasselt works on diverse themes that influence the physical and social living environment. Files concerning urban development, mobility, infrastructure, roadworks, public space, climate, energy and sustainability require clear communication, an appropriate participation approach and good coordination with residents, users and other stakeholders. With this framework agreement, Stad Hasselt wishes to have specialised and flexibly deployable expertise to support such files strategically, creatively and operationally. The framework agreement is therefore divided into two complementary lots. Both lots relate to environmental communication on urban files. The distinction lies in the level of service Stad Hasselt is looking for an experienced communication partner for the strategic guidance of urban files that have an impact on the physical and social living environment. These include files regarding urban development, mobility, infrastructure, roadworks, public space, climate, energy and sustainability and other related policy domains. Environmental communication in this lot comprises strategic communication on developments and changes in the living environment. The focus is on informing, creating understanding, involvement and support among residents, users, stakeholders and other target groups involved. The contractor analyses the social, policy-related, spatial and communicative context and advises Stad Hasselt on the most appropriate communication, participation, awareness-raising and stakeholder approach. The contractor thereby possesses demonstrable experience with environmental communication and with the specific communication issues that go hand in hand with developments and changes in the urban and social living environment. The service provision may relate to a specific sub-assignment or to the strategic guidance and management of a complete process. For files with increased sensitivity or social impact, the contractor maps out target groups, stakeholders, interests, sensitivities and potential resistance and develops an appropriate strategy. In doing so, they monitor the coherence between communication, participation and stakeholder management and support Stad Hasselt in creating support, positioning and, where relevant, behavioural change. The contractor acts as a strategic adviser and process manager and ensures a cohesive approach throughout all phases of the process. Delimitation: this lot focuses exclusively on strategy, advice, strategic concept development and process management. The concrete creative elaboration, production and operational execution of communication means, campaigns and participation activities fall under Lot 2.; Stad Hasselt is looking for a creative and execution-oriented communication partner with demonstrable experience in environmental communication for the concrete elaboration and execution of environmental communication surrounding urban files. This concerns communication about developments and changes in the physical and social living environment, inter alia regarding urban development, mobility, infrastructure, roadworks, public space, climate, energy, sustainability and other related policy domains. The contractor understands the specific context of environmental communication and is able to translate information about urban files and developments in the living environment into understandable, accessible and activating communication for residents, users, stakeholders and other target groups involved. The contractor translates strategies, concepts and briefings into concrete communication and communication activities that align with the specific context, target groups and dynamics of urban environmental files. This can range from the elaboration of an individual communication tool to the development and execution of a complete campaign. The services may include the creative elaboration of concepts, content creation, graphic and audiovisual production, digital communication, campaign execution and practical support for participation and awareness-raising trajectories. The contractor can be deployed both independently and in cooperation with the contractor of Lot 1 or on the basis of a strategy, concept or briefing provided by Stad Hasselt. Delimitation: this lot focuses on the creative elaboration, production and operational execution of environmental communication. Strategic analysis, strategy formulation, strategic concept development, strategic stakeholder analysis and strategic process management fall under Lot 1.

sig_b900bd9b691a1b4fb043.description: The board wishes to purchase a new software package for the Leisure department. The purpose of this process is to manage the entire process surrounding hall and room rental in a digital, user-friendly and efficient manner. This process includes: - Application and reservation by citizens, associations, schools or internal staff - Confirmation, follow-up and communication regarding applications - Automatic allocation of work stations or notifications (cleaning, technical, hall attendant, access control) - Price calculation, allocation of correct rates or exemptions - Linkage with access, planning and accounting - Invoicing or direct payment, with follow-up of cancellations or exceptions - User-friendly reporting and policy monitoring. The process strives for minimal manual intervention, unless the department or the board explicitly chooses to deliberately keep certain steps manual. Furthermore, it is aimed at a clear division of roles and maximum reuse of data (such as profiles, availability or reservation history), so that both the citizen and internal operations are optimally supported.; The purpose of the "Registrations and participation management" process is to digitally manage registrations for activities, courses, trips or events organised by the leisure services. This includes both paid and free activities and applies to various target groups (citizens, associations, schools...). The system must: - enable users to register easily, possibly for multiple participants or sessions; - make participation trackable per activity or participant; - allow administration and payments to proceed automatically; - enable reporting on registrations, participation rates and target group reach.; The "Cash register and sales process" process regulates the registration, payment and follow-up of all direct sales that take place at the counter, via a kiosk or via a cash register system. This includes, among other things, the sale of drinks, meals, products (such as local products), UiTPAS cards, multi-visit cards and entrance tickets for infrastructure such as a swimming pool, sports hall or meeting room. The goal is to guarantee correct and user-friendly operation for citizens and staff with the necessary legal, financial and access-related follow-up. Webshop sales are a digital extension of this same process, with an adapted user interface. The "Webshop interface and digital processing" process is a channel extension of the cash register and sales process, with which citizens can independently and fully digitally make use of the leisure services' offer via a user-friendly and integrated webshop environment. This includes, among other things, the online sale of multi-visit cards, entrance tickets, equipment rental, meal reservations and registrations for activities. The webshop retrieves its product configuration, prices and processing entirely from the cash register system and follows the same rules for validation, access and payment. As a result, transactions via the webshop are substantively identical to purchases via the counter or kiosk. The goal is to offer customer-oriented digital access without the intervention of staff, thereby reducing administrative workload and decreasing error sensitivity.; The purpose of this process is to offer, load, use, transfer and monitor digital and physical gift cards in a secure, user-friendly and financially sound manner within the urban leisure services. This process supports: - Sale of digital and physical gift cards to citizens, organisations or companies - Loading of balances onto cards (online or at physical counters) - Use as a means of payment within the webshop, cash register or registration modules - Allocation of balance, expiry date and unique code (QR or numeric) - Transfer of cards to third parties (for example as a gift) - Secure processing of transactions and balance adjustments - Administrative and financial processing (such as payments to merchants, balance management, accounting) - Linkage with financial systems such as Alfa - Reporting on usage, balances and annual rollover of credits - Governance on rights structure, logging and access management. The process avoids manual actions where possible and supports policy-based management of incentives, promotions or compensations. It is aimed at future-oriented operation with functionality and user experience comparable to modern gift voucher platforms such as bol.com, with an emphasis on transparency, flexibility and auditability.

sig_b900df91d30c81b95590.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Lt Col Sean Carlson AFRL/RIS 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)-330-2936 Email: sean.carlson.1@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_b901c8042d6d2634044a.description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

sig_b904a406b43c7b76b692.description: The objective of the DISM project is to support the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in exploiting international demand for responsibly extracted raw materials to create and strengthen high-potential local added value. The project contributes to significantly reducing poverty and diversifying the economy, particularly in areas around mining sites and the Lobito corridor, to reduce dependence on mining sector revenues and develop local value chains. The project is based on environmental, social, and governance standards in the mining sector in the DRC. It strengthens governance and economic development around mining exploitation in existing intervention regions, and mainly around the Lobito corridor. It also actively contributes to strengthening the capacity of civil society to promote transparency and accountability in the mining sector and increasing the mobilization of revenues from the mining sector. Under its component 2 on Economic Development in the Lobito Corridor Area, the project supports the structuring and organizational development of the Federation of Congolese Enterprises (FEC) in Lualaba, as well as the promotion of training programs, especially for SMEs. The project aims to strengthen the FEC's position as a government interlocutor at national and provincial levels, as well as in its role as an interface for economic actors in the DRC, contributing to improving the business climate and increasing opportunities for added value creation through access to subcontracting markets for Congolese SMEs. Furthermore, through the establishment of a multi-stakeholder consultation framework, the project creates a dedicated space for dialogue, fostering synergies and the co-construction of initiatives that promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth. Co-led by the Federation of Congolese Enterprises (FEC) and the Ministry of Industry and SMEs, this framework will bring together public institutions, the private sector, and civil society from the provinces of Haut-Katanga and Lualaba. The tender intends to recruit a pool of international and national experts (see personnel concept) who will provide short- and long-term technical advisory services contributing towards the improvement of the business climate and integrated economic development along the corridor, primarily in Lualaba province. Specifically, the contractor is expected to contribute to the following objectives through targeted measures in organizational development and capacity development of the FEC Lualaba: - Strengthening the FEC's institutional triple role as (i) a trade association that brings together stakeholders to develop solutions to improve the business environment; (ii) a chamber of commerce that establishes contacts with international and national economic players; and (iii) a trade union that defends the rights of its members. - Enhancing the FEC's position as a credible interlocutor with the State at national and provincial level, and its role as an interface for economic players in the DRC. This aims to improve the number and quality of its members. - Diversifying the FEC's training programs for large companies, small and medium-sized enterprises, and entrepreneurs in semi-urban areas along the Lobito corridor.

sig_b91f7e893afe066c1749.description: Creation of the Budapestiana portal commissioned by Budapest Főváros Levéltára Budapest Főváros Levéltára intends to create the Budapestiana portal application. The source base of Budapestiana is the databases and digital files handed over by the contracting authority to the tenderer/developer. The main objectives of the project: - creation of 1 own, cloud-based database system and portal (Budapestiana), - migration of the files handed over by Budapest Főváros Levéltára to the Budapestiana portal and its database to be created (approx. 2.867.313 records, approx. 3.578.831 digital recordings and files, a total of approx. 8,2 terabytes), the data stored in the existing SQL database must be migrated to the relational database(s) built in the new cloud-based infrastructure, - creation of a modern, fast search engine for the data set of the Budapestiana portal to be created, - creation of a data maintenance interface for the BFL data set of the Budapestiana portal to be created, which allows data and image file uploading by BFL staff. The details and estimated quantities of the Hungaricana export files to be migrated to the Budapestiana portal are contained in Annex No 3. The expected functionality of the portal is contained in Annexes No 1. and 2. The system to be developed must provide at least the functionality, service level and solutions of the current Hungaricana database and the Budapest Time Machine equivalently, and all its software components must be based on open source products. The contracting authority expects a cloud service and software system to be developed that is scalable, securely operable and reliable according to the tenderer's needs. The tenderer should address the technical solutions for this in their tender. The contracting authority expects the tenderer to hand over the source code of the created software system upon completion of the project. The contracting authority stipulates that it acquires unlimited usage and further development rights regarding the created software system as a result of the contract, which it may – following prior notification of the winning tenderer – transfer to others. The deadline for the implementation of the system is a maximum of 12 months following the conclusion of the contract. The winning tenderer is entitled to early performance. The winning tenderer undertakes a minimum of 12 months' warranty for the created system. The contracting authority expects that any operational, data maintenance, operational safety or any other problem affecting the operation of the system as a whole or any of its components arising within the warranty period will be resolved under warranty. The contracting authority expects the tenderer to operate the system for 12 months following the handover, during which time they must perform the necessary updates. The tenderer may not charge any additional costs beyond their tender for the 12 months of operation and warranty repairs. The contracting authority expects the tenderer to submit an itemised tender for an additional 24 months of operation beyond the 12 months of operation (as an optional item, see the field in BT-54). The details of the task are contained in the attached requirements list and the list of data (documents) to be migrated.

sig_b9238efb05ba0be8c731.description: The contracting of the service has the objective of ensuring the maintenance, support and evolution of the ATM Projects Tool platform, guaranteeing that its architecture and functionality continue to be aligned with ENAIRE's project management needs. The service will provide methodological support to drive the continuous improvement of the processes defined in the current corporate documentation – including requirement sheets, procedures and manuals – in order to optimise the planning, execution, monitoring and reporting of DSNA projects, increasing the utilisation of the tool and its adaptation to new needs. In addition, support will be provided to reinforce the management of project teams and ensure that the organisation's requirements are aligned with ENAIRE's strategic objectives. Technical maintenance and functional evolution of the ATM Projects Tool will also be guaranteed, which includes the adaptation and updating of existing developments, the implementation of new evolutions to respond to regulatory changes, version updates, maintenance of licences and integration with other corporate systems. These activities contemplate a periodic analysis of improvements and the exploitation of standard functionalities, together with training and dissemination actions within ENAIRE. sig_b94b226bb2c0f7073105.description: Service description for the operational management of the PVCRM environment: The aim of this tender is to find a qualified external partner who operates and further develops the ÖBB-Personenverkehr CRM (PVCRM) environment efficiently and effectively in order to continuously improve customer satisfaction and the quality of ÖBB customer data. Application operational management comprises the comprehensive administration and operation of the PVCRM systems. This includes the following technologies and tasks: Dynamics 365: Administration and operation of the CRM platform, including ensuring the availability and performance of the application. Carrying out regular maintenance work and updates to ensure system stability and security. Customer Insights (Data & Journey): Analysis and management of customer data to gain valuable insights into customer behaviour. Implementation and management of customer journey processes to create personalised customer experiences. Synapse: Provision of analytical services for processing and analysing large amounts of data. Ensuring data integrity and security throughout the entire analysis process. Power APP: Development and management of user-defined apps to support specific business requirements. Integration of the apps into the existing PVCRM environment to ensure seamless workflows. Power BI: Data visualisation and analysis for creating meaningful reports and dashboards. Supporting users in interpreting the data and deriving sound decisions. Azure platform: Provision of cloud computing services to support the PVCRM environment. Management of the infrastructure, including scaling and monitoring of cloud resources. Monitoring: Monitoring of systems for early detection and elimination of faults. Implementation of alerting mechanisms to ensure prompt fault clearance. In addition to application operational management, the scope of services also includes the further development (customisation) of the technologies mentioned above. This includes adjustments and extensions, including individual development with a connection to the Dynamics/Power platform. All further developments must be seamlessly transferred to operational management and, if necessary, the takeover of third-party code must also be ensured Further development (customisation): The external partner ensures that adjustments and extensions are carried out continuously in the technologies mentioned above. This includes: Individual development: Development of tailor-made solutions in connection with the Dynamics/Power platform. Transfer of further developments to operational management: Ensuring that all further developments are seamlessly integrated into ongoing operations. Takeover of third-party code: Review and integration of third-party code into the existing environment. Support and fault clearance service: The external partner provides a fault clearance service with 24/7 availability, including public holidays, and guarantees continuous monitoring and prompt rectification of faults. The PVCRM environment comprises several important areas that work together to provide an efficient and effective customer relationship management platform. Here is a detailed description consisting of, among other things, the following sub-areas. Customer Service – Dynamics 365: This area focuses on managing and improving interactions with customers. It includes functions such as ticketing systems, customer queries and complaints as well as the provision of support services Marketing automation - Customer Insights Journeys: This involves the automation of marketing processes to create and carry out targeted campaigns. This includes customer segmentation, sending personalised emails and analysing campaign results Bonus programme: The bonus programme offers customers incentives and rewards for their loyalty. It includes functions such as point promotions, prize draws and the management of bonus points Central data management (Dataverse): Dataverse serves as a central database for all customer data. It enables the storage, management and analysis of data from various sources to ensure a unified view of the customer Customer Insights: Customer Insights offers advanced analysis options to gain deeper insights into customer behaviour. It includes functions such as customer lifecycle analysis, the RFM model (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) and the creation of detailed reports and dashboards

sig_b9559fbfdf1f9deba63a.description: NOIS is a system which is a joint Nordic Operational Information System and has been in operation since 2009. The system was put out to joint tender in 2006, where Arriva (later Alstom and GE) won the contract as supplier. Energinet, together with the other 4 Nordic TSOs, needs to purchase support and maintenance as well as adaptation of the NOIS system until the migration of the various processes supported in NOIS is completed in 2028. The purchase of the services is strictly necessary for the maintenance of the Nordic market, which is business-critical. Since a joint Nordic NOIS system had to be found, it was not possible to acquire a standard product on the market that could meet the Nordic TSOs' needs for this system, as such a system did not exist. The NOIS system was therefore developed as a proprietary system to meet the necessary needs for the system. The source code for the system is owned by GE Digital Services Europe. Energinet does not have access to changes herein without this being done through GE Digital Services Europe. It is planned that most services (functionality) will be taken over by other systems from 2025 and during 2027-28 there will only be approx. 10 % of the current services left in NOIS, which must be replaced either by in-house development or through a tender. The specific scope of services that must be re-procured is not known until other new systems have been fully developed. Energinet assesses that it is objectively excluded that another supplier can provide the necessary services. Based on the above, the purchase is assessed to be covered by the exemption provision in EU Directive 2014/25/EU art. 50, letter c – there is only one specific supplier that will apply in connection with the purchase of support and maintenance of NOIS.
sig_b9559fbfdf1f9deba63a.title: Support and maintenance of the NOIS system

sig_b97f03653fdc562326a3.description: Preliminary Market Engagement Notice Reference & Title: prj_15796 MoJ/HMPPS AI-enhanced Digital Reading Education Cloud-based Software Solution – Request for Information Procurement Unique Identifier: PDNN-2773-HVYN Date of Issue: 10/11/2025 Contracting Authority: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) Contact Details: Shannon Wood, Commercial Lead for Emerging Technology – shannon.wood1@justice.gov.uk 1. Purpose of the Notice This UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Notice is issued in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023. The purpose of this notice is to inform the market of a MoJ Request for Information (RFI) and to engage with suppliers to obtain feedback and insights on the potential requirement for an AI-enhanced Digital Reading Education Cloud-Based Software Solution. The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) is a major government department, at the heart of the justice system. The MoJ works to protect and advance the principles of justice; our vision is to deliver a world-class justice system that works for everyone in society. His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) is an executive agency, sponsored by the MoJ and carries out sentences given by the courts, in custody and in the community, and rehabilitates people in its care through education and employment. For at least the past three years, there have been over 80,000 prisoners held in custody at any given time. In 2015/16 the estimated total cost of crime in England and Wales is more than £58 billion. Rehabilitative services, including reading education, have proven to reduce recidivism, changing lives. Over 60% of prisoners have literacy levels below those expected at the end of primary education. Traditional reading interventions can fail to engage adult learners in custody, especially those with neurodiverse needs or disrupted educational histories. This contributes to poor mental health, behavioural issues, and reduced rehabilitation prospects. The MoJ is keen to obtain feedback and insights on the potential requirement for an AI-enhanced Digital Reading Education Cloud-Based Software Solution. This Request for Information (RFI) is a preliminary market engagement exercise to seek information relating to this requirement, and to gain a better understanding of the types and availability of products and services, as well as the commercial terms on which to acquire them. 2. Access and Communication This RFI is being conducted through the MoJ e-Sourcing portal and all communications between MoJ and Suppliers during this RFI process must strictly be made using the MoJ e-Sourcing portal. Suppliers must create an account on the e-sourcing portal found via the link here: https://ministryofjusticecommercial.bravosolution.co.uk/web/login.html Suppliers can access the RFI via PQQ_541 ‘MoJ/HMPPS AI-enhanced Digital Reading Education Cloud-based Software Solution’. sig_b987e19ce4f169d8d6d8.description: This procurement is to establish a framework to procure transport and environmental consultancy services for Transport for London (TfL), the Greater London Authority (GLA), the GLA Group, and London Boroughs. The framework will be part of TfL Professional Services Frameworks 3. The name of this framework will be: Transport Planning & Impact Monitoring and Environmental Services. Lot A1: ROAD SAFETY (INC USING ROAD CASUALTY DATA). Provide road safety research, policy reviews, audit and engineering input, speed management, vehicle technology and behavioural interventions. Analyse STATS19 (police-reported road collision and casualty data collection system) and related casualty datasets, addressing data quality and limitations, identifying trends and mitigating measures. Deliver robust statistical evaluation and recommendations supporting Vision Zero objectives for Transport for London decisions and reporting. Lot A2: Statistical Modelling & Bespoke Analysis. Provide statistical modelling and bespoke analysis of travel behaviour outside Transport for London strategic models. Design specialist surveys, including stated-preference surveys, and develop forecasting tools using open-source programming. Apply data science methods such as regression, classification, choice modelling and machine learning. Deliver clear reports, presentations and expert advice in accessible language promptly. Lot A3: Strategic Transport Modelling. Provide strategic transport modelling, including: demand, public transport, land-use interaction and highway modelling. Build, adapt, calibrate, validate and run models using software and open-source tools. Integrate traditional and big-data sources, undertake quality assurance and auditing, and interpret outputs for appraisal, environmental impacts, societal impacts and decision making aligned with Transport Analysis Guidance (TAG). Lot A4: Strategic Transport Studies, Scheme Planning & Design. Provide feasibility, optioneering and scheme-planning studies for transport improvements and development support. Deliver surveys, multi-modal forecasting, public-transport and highway modelling, pedestrian-flow modelling and design development. Evaluate environmental, economic and social factors using multi-criteria appraisal, and prepare proportionate business cases. Where required, undertake early-stage environmental appraisal outputs. Lot A5: Strategic Transport Planning and Policy. Provide strategic transport planning and policy analysis supporting the Mayor's Transport Strategy and London Plan. Develop and appraise options, area plans and investment priorities, integrating transport and land use and Healthy Streets. Lead research on emerging issues, manage stakeholder engagement and consultation, and provide impartial, evidence-based advice with programme management. Lot A6: Economic Appraisal and Advice. Provide economic appraisal, evaluation and advisory services for Transport for London schemes and policies. Prepare business-case appraisals and value-for-money assessments aligned with Department for Transport (DfT) Transport Analysis Guidance (TAG) and HM Treasury guidance. Develop bespoke appraisal frameworks, cost-benefit and multi-criteria analyses, wider economic and revenue impacts, and land-use and regeneration appraisal. Produce clear narratives for decision making. Lot A7: Transport Surveys (inc travel research behaviour). Provide end-to-end transport surveys and travel-behaviour research. Design and manage programmes; deliver fieldwork, sampling, quality assurance and processing including geocoding, weighting and analysis. Cover counts, origin-destination and number-plate studies, plus quantitative and qualitative social research. Supply robust reports and visual outputs, compliant with the United Kingdom General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and Transport for London information governance. Lot A8: Public Consultation. Provide specialist support for Transport for London public consultation and stakeholder engagement. Analyse consultation responses using qualitative and quantitative methods, including manual coding of open-text data. Advise on questionnaire design and deliver engagement such as focus groups and workshops. Produce reports and cross-tabulated outputs, ensuring traceability and data management to Transport for London standards. Lot B1: Data Analysis, Modelling and Monitoring. Provide environmental data analysis, modelling and monitoring for air quality and greenhouse-gas management. Develop and apply emissions inventories and dispersion modelling, including baseline and future-year assessments. Support ambient monitoring for validation and fleet composition forecasting. Integrate environmental and socio-economic datasets to assess exposure inequalities and health impacts for policy assessment. Lot B2: Ecology Surveys and Monitoring. Provide ecological, arboricultural and landscape surveys and monitoring for Transport for London and the Greater London Authority activities. Deliver Preliminary Ecological Appraisals (PEAs), habitat and species surveys, protected and invasive species advice, arboricultural assessments, and monitoring supporting Biodiversity Net Gain. Provide mitigation recommendations and reporting, and return geospatial outputs in Geographic Information System (GIS) format to Transport for London and Greenspace Information for Greater London (GiGL) agreed standards. Lot B3: Green Infrastructure and Biodiversity Research, Policy, Data Analysis and Innovation. Provide research, policy, analytical and advisory services for green infrastructure, biodiversity and natural capital. Deliver natural-capital accounting, ecosystem-service valuation, Geographic Information System (GIS) and remote-sensing analysis, and monitoring of green cover and biodiversity units. Provide feasibility advice for habitat banks and offsetting, and develop innovative tools and methods balancing enhancement with operational safety. Lot B4: Health, Equalities and Socio-Economic Assessment. Provide research, analysis and technical assessment of health, equality and socio-economic impacts of Transport for London policies and schemes. Deliver Health Impact Assessments (HIAs), socio-economic assessments and Equality Impact Assessments (EqIAs), including quantification, modelling and appraisal of determinants such as activity, air and noise pollution, safety and accessibility. Integrate assessments, recommend mitigation, engage stakeholders, and support statutory duties. Lot B5: Environmental Assessments. Provide environmental assessment and advisory services to secure consents and manage impacts for Transport for London projects and plans. Lead Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and Strategic Environmental Assessments (SEAs), including screening, scoping, baseline studies, topic assessments, carbon and Biodiversity Net Gain evaluation, mitigation and enhancement design, stakeholder engagement, and Environmental Statements. Provide independent expert-witness support and post-consent monitoring. Lot B6: Noise and Vibration. Provide specialist noise and vibration monitoring, modelling, assessment and mitigation for transport projects, operations and policies. Deliver baseline measurement and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) inputs using recognised methodologies, and develop mitigation strategies for design, operations and construction. Support policy development and research, including emerging technologies. Provide clear technical reporting and defensible expert-witness evidence. Lot B7: Climate Modelling, Mapping and Data Analysis. Provide climate modelling, mapping and data analysis to assess climate risks to Transport for London assets. Deliver hazard modelling for heat and flooding, exposure and vulnerability assessments, and scenario testing. Develop climate design parameters, undertake site-based resilience audits, and present outputs through Geographic Information System (GIS) and reports, ensuring data governance, traceability and accessible recommendations. Lot B8: Adaptation Measure Research, Policy, Innovation and Technology. Provide research, analytical support, policy insight and innovation for climate-change adaptation measures. Research, design, test and evaluate nature-based and engineered interventions; monitor performance and quantify outcomes; benchmark against other authorities; and develop tools to track resilience. Deliver pilots and cost-benefit analysis with uncertainty testing, plus practical implementation guidance and playbooks. Lot B9: Climate Risk and Adaptation Planning Advice. Provide technical advice and planning support to integrate climate-risk management and adaptation into Transport for London schemes. Assess heat, flood, drought, subsidence and extreme-weather risks; develop proportionate design options; and prepare planning documentation including Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) inputs, Flood Risk Assessments, drainage strategies and climate adaptation reports. Coordinate multidisciplinary inputs and produce clear outputs. Lot B10: Energy and Climate Change Mitigation. Provide expertise, analysis and policy support for decarbonisation, energy management and climate-change mitigation. Apply whole-life carbon methods consistent with British Standards Institution Publicly Available Specification PAS 2080:2023 (carbon management in buildings and infrastructure), including baselining, forecasting and tracking. Model energy demand and emissions, interface with Transport for London tools and frameworks, and develop Energy Statements. Identify and evaluate mitigation measures using the Avoid-Switch-Improve hierarchy.
