The NISC IV contract will also be transitioned to NISC V contract during the award period, which will require a new system to support the NISC V contract, while maintaining the NIMS system to close out the NISC IV contract. This work requires a support contractor that will provide Operations and Maintenance services for the NIMS systems that is used to manage the current NISC IV contract using the existing technology stack and will provide quality assurance and quality control to ensure uninterrupted system availability. In addition, the vendor should maintain and run reports if required from CMIS system that was used to support the NISC III contract and is currently not active. The work also requires the vendor to serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) capable of providing design, development, testing, deployment and documentation of the new software that will be required to support the NISC V contract when required. This includes, but is not limited to, making recommendations regarding the selection of software architecture and software development tools that will be required to develop the new system. The Contractor must provide operations and maintenance support for the NIMS/CMIS system, provide quality assurance and quality control, provide security compliance and ensure uninterrupted system availability. This effort also requires the vendor to serve as a SME and provide support with system architecture, software recommendations, system design, development, testing, deployment, and documentation for a new system to support NISC V contract requirements when required. Contractor will maintain NIMS/CMIS security certifications required to operate the software and its associated server hardware. The Contractor must also provide transition support to any potential new vendor at the contract’s end. ***THIS OPPORTUNITY IS SET-ASIDE FOR WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) CONCERNS*** **A LIVE NIMS DEMONSTRATION WILL OCCUR 09 SEP 2026, SEE L.8 FOR DETAILS**

sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.description: Open-quantity framework agreements are concluded for development services required by DB Systemtechnik. DB Systemtechnik works on extremely demanding digitalisation projects in the field of rail vehicle technology. The project portfolio thus encompasses challenges of the entire railway system, i.e. rail vehicles, their components, the infrastructure and the corresponding interfaces. For the initiation, definition, planning, control and successful completion of these technically demanding projects, DB Systemtechnik is looking for experienced partners with broad methodological expertise and industry know-how for consulting and project management services.; DB Systemtechnik uses various sensors, measurement and data loggers to acquire, process, transmit to the land side and evaluate process, diagnostic and operating data from rail vehicles and railway assets. For the development of customer-specific and standard assemblies based on embedded technology and railway-compatible measurement and sensor modules, DB Systemtechnik is looking for development partners and suppliers. The services cover all steps, from conception to the approval-ready hardware product that can be implemented in the vehicle by the client, including the necessary basic software. The suppliers are experienced in the development of railway-approved embedded hardware and software and have established certified development and production processes. They master documented series-delivery and quality processes and are experienced in supply chain and obsolescence management in the railway sector.; Within the scope of digitalisation projects in the railway sector, DB Systemtechnik develops customer-specific products which, among other things, require the development, modification and operation of specific applications. For this purpose, suppliers and development partners are sought who can efficiently develop reliable, robust and secure software solutions and use structured and proven development methods and certifiable development processes for this purpose. The suppliers have comprehensive knowledge and experience in the field of architecture, software development, CI/CD, software testing and quality assurance for embedded systems in critical environments. All software solutions must comply with the standards for approval in rail vehicles and operation in the railway sector.

sig_b9c3a15f0e771dca38e3.description: Hertfordshire County Council (HCC) is a large user of postal services. It uses printed communications and physical letters to communicate with residents / individuals / businesses within the county and produced approximately 545,000 mail items in 2024/25 necessitating the need for a flexible and forward-thinking approach with the HCC postal system. The current Hybrid Mail system used by HCC enables the electronic submission of documents for remote printing, enveloping, and posting. In the current year approximately 50% of our outbound mail has been sent via our Hybrid Mail system. The current system was adopted in 2020 and is widely utilised across HCC Services and teams, supporting essential communications such as general mailings, invoices, legal notices, and reminders, and aligns with GDPR and legal compliance standards. The current contract has reached the end of its initial 5-year term, and we have extended the maintenance contract. Hertfordshire County Council (HCC) seeks to procure a modern, flexible, and scalable Hybrid Mail solution to support its evolving communication needs. The system must enable secure, efficient, and compliant electronic submission of documents for remote printing, enveloping, and posting. Please refer to the PME document for full details. The Council is carrying out PME in relation to this project. The Council will consider the feedback received to help inform the Council’s options, requirements and further decision making. For the avoidance of doubt, this stage of the project is not part of a formal procurement process and the Council is not committing, at this stage, to carrying out such a process. Participation or non-participation in the PME shall not prevent any supplier participating in a potential future procurement, nor is it intended that any information supplied as part of the PME shall place any supplier at an advantage in a potential procurement process. Please make sure that you have submitted your Supplier Questionnaire following the instructions within the PME documentation and e-tendering system. The Council will not be held accountable for any errors made by an organisation in submitting their Supplier Questionnaire. sig_b9d9e685de270c259292.description: Skatteforvaltningen is an authority under the Ministry of Taxation and Growth group that handles tasks such as debt collection for the public sector, public property and land valuations, and the settlement and control of taxes and duties in the personal, commercial and corporate sectors. Skatteforvaltningen consists of seven specialised agencies, each of which performs tasks within its core area. UFST develops, ensures the operation of and maintains new and existing IT systems so that they are stable, secure and cost-effective. This is to support the correct and timely payment of taxes and duties. Further information about UFST can be found at: Udviklings- og Forenklingsstyrelsen | ufst.dk Skatteforvaltningen's current Corporate Data Warehouse (KDW) was established in 1996 and has since moved from merely exhibiting data from a few specialist systems to housing over 200 billion rows and 35 thousand tables today. It has been decided to replace the previous platform in favour of a modern and up-to-date platform, and it is therefore necessary to migrate data products from KDW to a new and modern platform that will support a combined cross-cutting data need. KDW uses a number of older, different technology components which do not necessarily need to be carried over to the new and modern platform that has already been established. It is therefore likely that a high degree of re-establishment of solutions will need to take place in close cooperation with the business. This is therefore a migration from an on-premise legacy data warehouse based on, among other things, Informatica and SAP Sybase to a modern cloud platform based on Microsoft Azure and Synapse. Front-end solutions and reports are thus expected to be migrated from SAP BO and Qlik Sense to Power BI. The current platform contains over 200 billion rows, 35.000 tables, 79.000 self-developed reports and 1.000 standard reports with data from more than 230 sources/IT systems. UFST is therefore looking into various possibilities, solutions and scenarios in connection with the migration task itself and needs to know what the market offers to support such a task. UFST thus seeks insight into; - how potential suppliers intend to approach migration, including "lift and shift", new/re-establishment, etc., as well as which factors may influence the size and scope of the migration. - considerations regarding the "cut" for migration – e.g. prioritisation of repatriation and standardisation of data. - possibilities for accelerating the migration – e.g. through automation of parts of the migration task. - the supplier's experience with comparable migration tasks. - clarifying the approach to user involvement in connection with the migration, including experience with the role and responsibility distribution between IT and users. - possible delivery model, change management, testing and experiences.
sig_b9d9e685de270c259292.title: Markedsdialog til Migrering af KDW

sig_b9e44041454269a4f2c0.description: Digipolis is looking, for the City of Antwerp among others, for a partner responsible for the supply, installation and maintenance of: • Sensors and reading out the current fill level of small-volume waste systems such as paper bins and other (waste) systems; • Software to monitor the current fill level of (waste) systems, predict the fill-level evolution based on historical measurement data and then plan the complete and most optimal route for collection vehicles to carry out emptying. In doing so, the available vehicles must be deployed optimally in the field depending on the required capacity for emptyings. This software is used for both existing, already installed sensors and sensors to be installed in the future. It is not the intention to replace all existing sensors. However, all sensors, existing and new, must be consultable in a single software system. The software must also be able to include unique, self-chosen collection points, e.g. for collecting illegal dumping, in the route calculation. The purpose of this contract is to achieve optimal emptying taking into account personnel, working time, vehicles, weight, volume, consumption, CO2 emissions, costs and traffic situations. The contract is divided into two lots: • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data. • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above. • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data.; • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above.

sig_ba484ec231515826cc38.description: The State Office for Finance (LfF) - Regensburg branch awards services for a full-stack developer under a temporary employment framework for the BayBAS procedure used in medical assistance benefits. The BayBAS procedure used for medical assistance benefits was developed approximately 20 years ago using the then common Visual Basic 6 technology (VB6) and has been continuously adapted to technical and functional requirements. The dwindling support for VB6 applications, as well as the increasingly difficult personnel situation for VB6 developers, make a new development absolutely necessary. Lot LOT-0001: Temporary employment full-stack developer. The State Office for Finance (LfF) - Regensburg branch is awarding services for a full-stack developer under a temporary employment arrangement for a duration of 18 months with an option to renew twice by 18 months each, in compliance with the cooling-off period required under the Temporary Employment Act (AÜG). The provision of services must commence two weeks after the award of contract. The BayBAS procedure used for medical assistance benefits was developed approximately 20 years ago using the then common Visual Basic 6 technology (VB6) and has been continuously adapted to technical and functional requirements. The dwindling support for VB6 applications, as well as the increasingly difficult personnel situation for VB6 developers, make a new development absolutely necessary. In order to make the procedure viable for the future once again, the new development has already been started. The aim is to continue to support caseworkers with a legally compliant and efficient software solution in the form of a modern web application. Common technologies such as C# in the backend and React in the frontend are used here. The full-stack developer works as part of the software development team in procedure development. They are to independently implement requirements and change orders of a technical and functional nature, as well as act in an advisory capacity and, where applicable, take the lead in technical design work. Necessary documentation is also part of the scope of duties. In addition, the task includes providing technical support to the sub-project management and monitoring compliance with technical standards. The requirements are listed again below. The developer must be named and must give basic consent to the performance of a basic security clearance check under the Bavarian Security Clearance Act (BaySÜG). Existing evidence of current security clearances must be submitted upon a potential award of contract. The developer deployed must also sign a declaration of commitment pursuant to the Act on Formal Obligations (Verpflichtungsgesetz) prior to deployment. The services can be provided largely remotely (on the contractor's premises or in a home office). Depending on the course of the project, however, a time-limited on-site presence of 10-20 % of the respective person days may be required for the fulfilment of the contract. The willingness of the proposed employee to attend these on-site appointments is assumed. The provision of services during on-site presence must generally take place at the place of work in Regensburg at the State Office for Finance – FinanzIT Bayern, Bahnhofstr. 7, 93047 Regensburg. On-site presence will be agreed upon with the contractor in good time.

sig_ba8c6865600a695d388f.description: UKROEd is undertaking a tender to procure a delivery partner for implementation of its MApp Phase 2 requirements. UKROEd has worked hard to establish its role as trusted governor of the National Driver Offender Retraining Scheme and while stakeholder feedback is consistently positive, we also know that accessing our systems and services, and our communications, can sometimes feel disjointed. 'Behind the scenes' some of our systems and processes are not as efficient and effective as we would wish. UKROEd has expanded rapidly since its creation in 2016. The company has recently developed its first Digital Strategy and within this, identified several areas of activity that would benefit from some digital investment. To address the challenges, UKROEd has commissioned Project MApp (Management Application), which will deliver an integrated business management solution that seeks to improve organisational and staff efficiency, ensure high data quality and accuracy to support timely decision making, and provide an exceptional user experience for our staff and external stakeholders. It will deliver the consolidation (and where possible automation) of critical business processes around an integrated solution. This holistic solution will not be a single logical product or technology platform and will at least comprise of a Learning Management Solution (LMS) and a Customer Relationship Management System (CRM), to be sourced separately but branded and acting (where required) cohesively as an integrated system. MApp in totality will facilitate much of UKROEd's core business including stakeholder engagement, trainer and provider licence management, training interventions (face-to-face and e-learning) and live events / conferences. Acknowledging the fact that an LMS has a simpler set of requirements and to start realising benefits as quickly as possible, these requirements were "frontloaded", with the procurement of an LMS being authorised as part of MApp 'Phase 1'. Phase 1 implementation is underway, with Open eLMS as the chosen technology platform. This tender exercise for 'Phase 2', will address the wider requirement set. UKROEd is seeking a delivery partner for implementation of its MApp Phase 2 requirements, centred around the deployment of an integrated, low/no-code CRM. Given the organisation's existing Microsoft 365 platform/application base, current technology strategy and internal skillset, it is anticipated the core CRM solution will likely comprise of Microsoft Dynamics 365, integrating with the Power Platform ecosystem for customer portal and full workflow capabilities. However, alternatives will also be considered. While the wider support model for MApp is to be determined, we would anticipate that the contracted delivery partner thereafter provides platform and application support for the implemented solution as part of a managed service. A budget envelope of GBP 500,000 has been established, within which prospective tenderers will be invited to submit capped implementation pricing (during invitation to submit a final tender - i.e. after dialogue) for delivery of all core components. As a small organisation with a limited budget, robust control over costs will be imperative. Lot 1: .
sig_ba8c6865600a695d388f.title: Tender for UKROEd Project MApp (Management Application) CRM Phase 2

sig_ba933b0b8bddc88d6e42.description:
Provision and operation of licences for an integrated, complex, Hungarian-language IT system supporting the (sub)tasks of parking operations management based on a service contract. Summary of the legal and factual background of the parking system: It is the task of the Municipality of Budapest District VI Terézváros (hereinafter: Municipality) to provide for the parking of motor vehicles and parking operations based on Section 13. (1) point 2. and Section 23. (5) point 3. of Act CLXXXIX of 2011. on Local Governments of Hungary (hereinafter: Mötv.). Within the framework of the relevant legislation, the Municipality has transferred the operation of the public parking spaces owned by it and located within its administrative area, but owned by the Municipality of Budapest (hereinafter: Metropolitan Municipality), to the non-profit business association owned 100% by the Contracting Authority, taking into account the provisions of Section 16/A of the Mötv. In accordance with the provisions recorded in Annex 6. of the municipal decree 30/2010. (VI.4.) of the General Assembly of Budapest on the uniform establishment of the order of parking with vehicles, the parking fee and the rules for the storage of inoperable vehicles in the administrative area of Budapest, a legal condition for the parking operation activity is that the Contracting Authority, as the parking operator organisation, is obliged to issue surcharge payment notices with the help of a portable computer and printer, which are entered into an office computer system in a traceable and verifiable manner. Provision and operation of licences for an integrated, complex, Hungarian-language IT system supporting the (sub)tasks of parking operations management based on a service contract. Tasks of the winning tenderer (for information purposes): Subject of the Contract: 1. the Contractor provides the usage rights for the management software or software supporting the operation of the parking system owned by it (charged to the monthly fee) by the partial performance deadline undertaken according to the evaluation criteria. The Software must minimally ensure the performance of the following tasks: - on-site inspection; - video-based licence plate and vehicle recognition service (with at least 90% accuracy); - central inspection; - complaint handling; - parking permits; - cash management; - debt management. Master data to be managed: User (group)-; User authorisation-; Portable devices-; User workstation-; Customers-; Surcharge, inspection-; Vehicles-; Complaint, and Bank master data. Expected authorisation levels (User groups): parking inspector, clerk, operator, dispatcher, area inspector, administrator (super user) authorisations. Ensuring that photographs taken during on-site inspection (including the photograph taken of the surcharge payment notice) are provided with an electronic timestamp. In connection with the introduction of the system, the winning Tenderer is obliged to provide one-off introductory training with the following content and scope: – a total of at most 3 training days, – in a duration of 2–4 hours per group, – for the user groups defined in the call. The above introductory training is part of the monthly fee. Training held for repeat or new entrant staff requested after the introduction shall be settled based on a separate order at the same hourly rate as the net hourly rate for Program modification. 2. performance of IT support Services related to the Software continuously after the performance of the tasks according to point 1., - Within the framework of operation (charged to the monthly fee), the winning Tenderer is obliged to provide all conditions for the Contracting Authority and is obliged to perform all tasks for the continuous, full-scale and error-free operation of the Software; the operation tasks include software tracking, preparation of installation packages, remote monitoring, troubleshooting and maintenance, availability tasks, support for the operation of interfaces established with other systems, within the framework of which, among others, the performance of the following tasks o daily maintenance o provision of continuous, planned and extraordinary error correction and service activity o continuous availability during the operating days established by the parking operation legislation (30/2010. (VI. 4.) municipal decree of Budapest), daily between 7.00 o'clock in the morning and 22.00 o'clock in the evening (hereinafter: Operating Time), within the framework of which, depending on the nature of the problem, it is obliged to start troubleshooting the error via remote connection within at most 1 hours from the potential error report, or to start on-site troubleshooting of the error within at most 3 hours. - Within the framework of program modification and review, the winning Tenderer is obliged to adapt the existing software to the needs of the Contracting Authority (thus in particular establishing communication between programs, creating new functions within the functional framework of the existing system), of which a total of at most 20 working hours per month is part of the flat-rate fee according to the conditions recorded in the draft contract, while additional modifications can be settled at the hourly rate provided by the winning Tenderer up to the net 15 000 000 HUF framework amount according to the draft contract. Based on the above, the monthly flat-rate fee includes the following: Licence fee per month (for at most 150 users) Support fee per month (which includes at most 20 hours of rollable program modification per month) The software must be capable of managing the following: - number of workstations (PC computers) connected to the specialised system: 40 pcs + 10% (the Contracting Authority provides with additional peripherals); - 20 pcs of PDA and 20 pcs of mobile printer devices integrated into the specialised system (+10%-+10%) (the Contracting Authority provides the devices);

sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.description: The Bundesbank manages four staff canteens under its own management. The management of a further eight Bundesbank canteens is carried out by external caterers under contract management. For the canteens under its own management, the Bundesbank uses an inventory management system and a checkout/payment system on its own infrastructure (cash or direct debit for internal employees; cash for external employees and guests). The checkout/payment system is integrated into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape. Orders to suppliers are placed by PDF/email; a B2B connection is not available. In daily operations, many steps are currently carried out manually or twice due to a lack of integrations. The same checkout/payment system is used in the contract-managed canteens (including integration into SAP), but inventory management is carried out independently by the caterers outside the Bundesbank's IT landscape. The inventory management system and checkout/payment system are outdated, meaning that the Bundesbank has initiated a project to replace these systems with a SaaS solution. With this new SaaS solution, which is then to be introduced in the following one to two years, modern payment methods (cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) are to be introduced alongside cash and direct debit. In addition, the solution is to be B2B-capable in order to enable a B2B connection of suppliers. Further focus is placed on automation and digitalisation in order to significantly reduce manual effort, e.g. during stocktaking, and the associated sources of error. In the course of this strategic alignment, Deutsche Bundesbank is initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the SaaS-based gastro-system platforms available on the market (inventory management with checkout and payment system). In particular, it is to be examined to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security requirements of Deutsche Bundesbank. A key focus is inter alia on: - Support for modern payment methods (cash, direct debit, cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) - B2B capability including connection of suppliers - Integration capability into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape - Functions for automation and digitalisation (e.g. for stocktaking) - Operation as SaaS in a BSI C5-certified cloud - Use both in canteens under own management and contract management - German-language project management, support and documentation This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially upcoming EU-wide procurement procedure by Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of the described services and forms, amongst other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and constitutes neither an offer nor an invitation to conclude a contract. The execution of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences for the participating company (neither preference nor disadvantage) in the context of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration. Further details on Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for the SaaS solution described above are available exclusively upon request to the stored e-mail address: Projekt-GastroSys@bundesbank.de
sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.title: Market exploration: GastroSys - SaaS solution for gastronomy systems of Deutsche Bundesbank

Green space certificate diagnostic service: The purpose of the green space certificate is to objectively measure and verify the green infrastructure supply and ecological performance capacity of plots of land and properties. The diagnostic service is therefore essential for an objective and authentic assessment of the current condition, which forms the basis for issuing the certificate. Applied technical standards and requirements: - GNSS RTK accuracy (2-5 cm): ensuring on-site georeferencing; - Photogrammetric and LiDAR accuracy: 2-5 cm (drone-based), 2-5 mm (laser scanner); - Digital processing: point cloud (.las/.e57), orthophoto (.tiff), 3D model (.obj/.stl), contour-line relief (.dwg/.shp); - Geographic information system analysis in QGIS, GlobalMapper, ArcMap environment; - Biological activity value (BAV) and green volume calculation in accordance with the decree parameters; Quality expectations: - Comprehensive data collection: ground-connected green spaces, tree stock, biodiversity, invasive species, green volume, green asset value; - On-site inspection with photo documentation; - Certificate meeting the content and formal requirements stipulated by legislation; Environmental and safety regulations: - Operational and flight permits (NMHH, aviation authority, military remote sensing permit); - Constitution Protection Office risk-free expert opinion; The process of the diagnostic service: (1)Preparation: - Recording of basic data, topographical lot number, and client requirements of the area to be examined; sig_bb14f49cc23d4493455a.description: This is not a procurement procedure! It is a non-binding information request intended solely for market consultation in accordance with Section 28 of the Ordinance on Public Procurement (VgV). Description of the task: The Deutsche Raumfahrtagentur im Deutschen Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e.V., Space Situation division, is probing the procurement of turn-key satellite-based observation systems for optical observations (detection and tracking) of space objects in near-Earth orbit as well as the use of commercially available data from existing space infrastructures. Additional detection technologies for monitoring space objects from comparable distances may also be proposed. This concerns fully integrated satellites with sensor units including control software, control systems and software for automated processing of observation data as well as, where applicable, subsequent maintenance and support of the systems in orbit. The aim of this project is to integrate new or existing satellite-based sensors into the existing space surveillance network of the German Space Situation Centre (WRLageZ) and to put them into operational service. The satellites are intended to be capable of detecting and tracking objects in various Earth orbits - in particular in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) and Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO). In this context, space objects should be able to be recorded with high accuracy at the highest possible repetition rate. In the final expansion stage, recording is to take place in almost real time. The sensors must be designed for operation in orbit and must be able to carry out the observation tasks centrally controlled by the WRLageZ independently, taking into account environmental conditions (e.g. radiation, thermal fluctuations) and system integrity. The recorded observation data - in particular angular coordinates and apparent brightness - must be processed in a fully automated manner within a time window of less than 60 minutes and made available to the WRLageZ in a standardized format (e.g. TDM format). A specific technical specification is not currently prescribed in order to initially obtain a comprehensive overview of market-relevant systems already existing or under development for space-based space surveillance (SBSS). The obtained orbit data is to be entered into the central orbit data catalogue of the WRLageZ and shared with selected national and international partners. These data form the basis for the further development of national capabilities for operational space surveillance in the field of optical observations from space. Specifically, the following activities are planned: (a) Provision of already available pre-processed data from existing space infrastructures, (b) Establishment of a satellite-based observation system for the optical detection and tracking of space objects, (c) Launch, commissioning and validation of the system in orbit, including connection to the WRLageZ, (d) Training of the supervising personnel for operation and data analysis. According to current planning, a period of 24 to 36 months, expected from April 2027, is scheduled for the implementation of the project. This can be extended if necessary to achieve the final expansion stage. If you are able to offer the service described above, please send meaningful documents and references (preferably to the email address stated below) by no later than 31.05.2026, 23:59:59 hrs to the following contact and information office: German Space Agency at the German Aerospace Center (DLR e. V.) Department AR-ZF Attn. Ms Martina Böhm-Braun, Königswinterer Str. 522 – 524 53227 Bonn
sig_bb14f49cc23d4493455a.title: Information gathering as part of a MARKET CONSULTATION - For the procurement of systems for "space-based optical detection and tracking of objects in Earth orbit".

sig_bb18efef9c8e67f879bd.description: The Stadt Burgdorf is centrally located in the north-eastern area of the Hanover Region, right in the middle of the Hanover - Celle - Braunschweig - Hildesheim city square with very good connections to the supra-regional road and rail network. Burgdorf has 31.156 inhabitants and is economically characterised by small and medium-sized enterprises. The Stadt Burgdorf has been in the funded "Living Centres" urban development funding programme with the redevelopment area "Innerstadt Burgdorf" since 2022. As a component of this multi-year redevelopment measure, the establishment of so-called "city management" is planned for the year 2026. Inner city development is increasingly understood as a joint task that requires active, steering management for this purpose. The Burgdorf City Marketing Association (SMB) has been firmly anchored in urban society for decades (2.700 members). It works closely with the Burgdorf Traffic and Beautification Association (VVV) and is already implementing a diverse range of projects. However, there is no strongly developed quarter or neighbourhood life in the inner city itself. This is where city management comes in: it is intended to close a gap between existing city marketing activities and actor activation focused on the inner city. City management assumes this role as a coordinating and networking interface between the municipality, citizens, businesses and other actors. The aim of this project is to drive the inner city forward in the direction of a more attractive, active place of social, economic and cultural togetherness. In its role as a networking point, city management is intended to bundle activities, initiate projects and steer processes. City management does not compete with existing actors, but rather complements their work with a coordination and activation function focused on the redevelopment area. It does not work within the city administration, but rather as an external contractor that cooperates closely with the economic development, urban planning and environment, culture, and youth welfare departments. City management comprises the core tasks described below. The list is not exhaustive. By its very nature, the activity of city management requires flexible responses to changing framework conditions, needs and local opportunities in order to achieve the overarching task objectives. Further individual activities may therefore arise within the framework of the annual target agreement (cf. section 5 paragraph 2 of the consultant agreement), insofar as they correspond to the subject and purpose of the city management. - Contact person in the redevelopment area - Support and communication in the redevelopment process - Acquisition of funding - Establishment and management of the allocation fund - Development and increase in the attractiveness of the Inner City business location - Public relations and press work - Communication and reporting The individual services can be found in the specification of services (Part B of the tender documents) and the consultant agreement (Part C of the tender documents).
sig_bb18efef9c8e67f879bd.title: Ex Post: Stadt Burgdorf: City management for the Innerstadt Burgdorf redevelopment area

sig_bb542182ed1d19838b54.description: The activity provides for the delivery and implementation of a system for electronic passenger ticketing in public transport and a system for automatic passenger counting, which represents an integrated digital solution to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of public transport. Full information regarding the technical requirements for the performance of the public contract is described and regulated in the Technical Specifications for the relevant lot, an integral part of the participation documentation. Lot 2 includes Delivery and implementation of a system for automatic passenger counting. The public transport provision service must meet people's mobility needs and follow their travel behaviour. Preparation of a digital register of the stock of trees on the green spaces within the area affected by the service (in the area of tree alignments, parks, institutional properties). The number of currently registered trees is 49 600, the aim of the survey is also to refine this: based on the Contracting Authority's estimate, the survey of approximately 60 000 trees is required. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to establish a digital tree cadastre serving basic municipal operational and other requirements, which must be suitable for registering the data of the surveyed trees, tracking changes occurring in the data, recording tree care work, as well as for displaying data indicating the effects of climate change in relation to the tree stock. The digital tree cadastre must be created by preparing a green space cadastre – digital tree register – based on a survey performed using mobile LIDAR technology and panoramic images, which must include the 2D map representation of the green space, as well as one 3D digital copy per individual tree. The digital tree register must be prepared based on LIDAR point clouds and panoramic images produced by a mobile terrestrial laser scanner MLS (Mobile Laser Scanning). The register must be prepared for municipally owned public space trees and partially private/institutional area trees identifiable by the MLS from the road in the required data content. In order to fulfil the required accuracy and detail requirements, the MLS must be capable of recording at least three million LIDAR points per second. This ensures that trees located further away from the survey point – even 20–30 metres away – are documented with appropriate detail. In the case of trees, the expected minimum data content of the cadastre: • precise data of the tree location (by indicating the street, house number, by providing EOV coordinates); map representation with cm accuracy • designation of tree species/variety • metric data: trunk diameter (at 1,0 metres height), trunk height, crown height, crown ellipse, crown centre of gravity, tree height, tree species, tree location, height of living wood part • age (calculated/estimated) • safety analysis and tree condition data: root collar, trunk, crown condition data, visible damage, pathological alterations based on visual inspection. A safety analysis must be prepared based on the surveyed data, on the basis of which the treatments to be performed (felling, rejuvenation, pruning) must be determined. • i-Tree Eco model, or equivalent data content: percentage of crown missing (percent crown missing) • branch structure model: for precise static and safety analysis of individual trees, with at least the leafless display of the branch system. • economic value and regulatory ecosystem services (general thermal sensation index; evapotranspiration capacity; 2, 3, 2, CO, particulate matter binding; oxygen production; transpiration; carbon sequestration, carbon storage; water uptake) • data suitable for presenting microclimatic effects: illustration of the micro-scale pattern of shading, based on canopy cover • foliage mass The database to be prepared during the survey shall be handed over to the Contracting Authority. The availability of the on-line application usable for displaying the data, for analytics, as well as for the allocation of tree care work is 2 years (which must be included in the lump sum price), during which period the data must be made available with at least the following display modes: Overview 2D map display with at least the following content: - Base map with the road network and major green areas - Point-like and canopy cover-illustrating representation of trees. Display of individual trees with at least 3, with the image containing the tree and as a 3D digital copy of the trees, where the foliage and branch system of the trees are depicted separately, and their metric and other data listed above also appear. - The evaluated data of the trees must also be handed over (transferred) in SHP file format. The user accesses and the associated database required for the application created by the winning Tenderer must be handed over via a cloud-based solution. Access must be provided for 15 users to the application, which must be included in the lump sum price. In detail in the technical specification.
sig_bb6706c236c8ccc29134.title: Preparation of a tree cadastre in the administrative area of Budapest District XI

sig_bb9148db9afc1d6e5d58.description: This contract award notice informs interested operators about the outcome of a tender. On 26/12/2023, a contract notice was published as part of the EU project CircularPSP to purchase R&D services from a number of R&D providers in parallel (PCP procurement). The procurement is open on equal terms to all types of operators that are established in EU Member States and Horizon Europe associated countries and that fulfil the requirements set out in section 3 of the Call for Tenders which defines the eligibility of tenderers, exclusion and selection criteria. The procurement aims to trigger new solutions to be developed and tested to address the following challenge: accelerating a digital transition towards a Circular Economy (CE). The procurers are willing to invest €5.64 million in Research and Development to address this challenge in their regions. This PCP is a joint procurement by different procurers across Europe that are all facing the same common challenge and are thus looking for similar solutions (‘Buyers Group’). The procurement will take the form of a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) under which R&D service contracts will be awarded to a number of R&D providers in parallel in a phased approach. This will make it possible to compare competing alternative solutions. Each selected operator will be awarded a framework agreement that covers 3 R&D phases. Each selected R&D provider will be awarded a framework agreement that covers the following R&D phases and a specific contract per phase. The 3 phases are: solution design (phase 1),prototyping and pilot testing (phase 2), original development, installation, validation and field testing of a limited set of first products or services (phase 3). After each phase, intermediate evaluations will be carried out to progressively select the best of the competing solutions. The contractors with the best-value-for-money solutions will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. A total budget of € 5.640.000,- was earmarked for awarding the contracts to a minimum of: - 5 contractors for phase 1 - 3 contractors for phase 2 and - 2 contractors for phase 3. Testing is expected to take place in Istanbul (TR), Berlin (DE), Dublin (IE), Maribor (SI), Guimarães (PT), Stockholm (SE), London (UK), Helsinki (FIN). This testing may also serve as a first customer test reference for the contractors. The procurement has started in 15/05/2024 and is expected to end in 31/07/2026. The selected operators will retain ownership of the intellectual property rights (IPRs) that they generate during the PCP and will be able to use them to exploit the full market potential of the developed solutions i.e. beyond the procurers. sig_bbd093a697d5c6c981fe.description: The subject of this contract is the conclusion of a framework agreement (FA) with a potential contractor for the awarding of contracts regarding the PROVISION OF COMMUNICATION CONNECTIVITY FOR REAL-TIME DATA TRANSMISSION, MAINTENANCE AND UPGRADING OF THE ELECTRONIC MONITORING SYSTEM OF ОБЩИНА БУРГАС Scope and territorial scope: Община Бургас currently operates an electronic monitoring system colocated in the CVUT. Through the team of the Municipal Enterprise "Transport" of Община Бургас, the data received from all terminal monitoring devices located on the territory of Община Бургас are processed. The processing of data streams is organisationally divided into several subsystems - for electronic monitoring of public spaces, for road transport infrastructure, for buses and public transport stops, and others, for individual administration sites. Through the established communication and logical infrastructure, the transmission of real-time data from other smart terminal devices collecting metadata for the city is also ensured. The purpose of this public procurement is to ensure communication connectivity for real-time data transmission, maintenance and development of the systems, while ensuring continuity, quality of services and information security in accordance with the relevant legislation and the specific technical requirements described below. The activities must be carried out through the delivery, installation, commissioning and maintenance in working order of new hardware and software components for the system, maintenance of existing equipment and video signal processing subsystems, as well as the provision of communication connectivity for the real-time transmission of video streams and metadata, separated into separate virtual segments, to the existing CVUT (Video Surveillance and Traffic Management Centre) of Община Бургас, located at: Burgas, Stefan Stambolov St. 19; to ensure their further processing through the elements of the City's Integrated Information Systems. The activities included in the subject of the public procurement are: Activity 1 Upgrading and expanding the scope of the electronic monitoring system with new end locations Activity 2 Maintenance of the elements of the existing electronic monitoring subsystems so as to ensure continuous and full operability and operation of the municipal electronic monitoring system. Activity 3 Provision of communication connectivity for existing and newly constructed electronic monitoring subsystems Activity 4 Provision of planned preventive activities to ensure the operability of Burgas's electronic monitoring system
sig_bbd093a697d5c6c981fe.title: Framework agreement for the selection of a contractor to provide communication connectivity for real-time data transmission, maintenance and upgrading of the electronic monitoring system of Община Бургас

sig_bbfa6b69883d2147ec73.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Extreme Computing BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7004 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 20 Sep 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hrs. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 20 Sep 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 4 Oct 2023 FY25 by 30 Sep 2024 FY26 by 30 Sep 2025 FY27 by 30 Sep 2026 FY28 by 30 Sep 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Broad Agency Announcement for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to support research in the focus areas computational diversity and efficient computing architectures, machine learning and artificial intelligence in embedded system and architectures, computing at the edge, nanocomputing, space computing, and robust algorithms and applications. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $497.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 36 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $3M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $99.9M ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023( previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Joel Moore AFRL/RITB 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-4958 Email: joel.moore.2@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL ANNOUNCEMENT DETAILS. sig_bbfeb61d00d77672cf0a.description: Comuna Sanmartin is implementing the project PRNV/2024/723/1 „CONSTRUCTION OF LEISURE COMPLEX - AQUAPARK SANMARTIN” SMIS code: 325406 The general objective of the project is promoting the integrated and inclusive development of tourism and natural heritage, increasing the quality of life in Sânmartin commune. The objective of the project will be achieved by developing the leisure infrastructure, namely the Sânmartin Aquapark Leisure Complex, with a total built-up area of 6653.82 sq m, respectively 6332.72 sq m (excluding terraces), and respectively by increasing the number of visitors > 21%. The deadline by which economic operators may request clarifications, in accordance with the provisions of art. 160 paragraph (1) of Law 98/2016 is 10 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The contracting authority will clearly and completely respond to all requests for additional clarifications (if they were received on time), in accordance with the provisions of art. 161 of Law 98/2016 6 days before the date set for submitting tenders. The objective of the contract to be awarded consists in the procurement of consultancy services related to the project management of PRNV/2024/723/1 „CONSTRUCTION OF LEISURE COMPLEX - AQUAPARK SANMARTIN”, with an implementation period of 31.08.2029, a project financed within the North-West Regional Programme 2021-2027, Call Title: PRNV/2024/723/1 - Development of infrastructure for spa and balneoclimatic tourism, including the improvement of access to resources and tourist objectives (RURAL), Specific Objective: RSO5.2_Promotion of integrated and inclusive local development in the social, economic and environmental fields, as well as culture, natural heritage, sustainable tourism and security in areas other than urban areas, State aid scheme: Development of infrastructure for spa and balneoclimatic tourism, including the improvement of access to resources and tourist objectives; EU Fund: ERDF - European Regional Development Fund. The duration of the services is from the date of signing the public procurement contract for the entire implementation period thereof until the full completion of the project activities. The project completion deadline is 31.08.2029. The consultant's role in this case is to identify the best ways to achieve the project objective, while complying with the provisions of the financing contract. The activity of a consultant in the implementation of projects financed from non-reimbursable funds consists in carrying out all managerial activities necessary to achieve the objectives proposed within the projects and their successful implementation. The success of the entire project can only be ensured through professional project management. Professional project management, including project-related reporting, requires the existence of qualified personnel in terms of methodology, professional expertise and communication. The project implementation management consultant fully assimilates the information from the project documentation and carries out its activity in accordance with legislative provisions and guidelines, instructions, rules and amendments issued by the programme management authority. The objective of the contract to be awarded consists in the procurement of project management consultancy services for Comuna Sanmartin as beneficiary. The duration of the services is from the date of signing the public procurement contract for the entire implementation period thereof in accordance with the financing contract and subsequent amendments approved by addendum. For the initiation, preparation/organisation and supervision under the conditions established by the project of all its activities, it is necessary to procure project management services. According to the budget of Sanmartin commune within the Financing Contract, outsourced general project management services are provided, covering the entire implementation period, for the purpose of preparing and organising payment/reimbursement claims, progress reports, notifications, as well as for monitoring and reporting.
sig_bbfeb61d00d77672cf0a.title: Consultancy services for project management PRNV/2024/723/1 „Construction of leisure complex - Aquapark Sanmartin” SMIS code: 325406

sig_bc36d4f46e434011d441.description: It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act: - Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner - Mitigate and adapt to climate change - Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide - Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use. Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities: 1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities. 2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’. 3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero. 4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest. SCOPE: Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy. Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme. We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management. The project "Integrated intervention for professional development and integration into the labour market for young people aged up to 29 years" concerns the provision of an integrated, targeted and innovative range of services to 8.000 unemployed young people aged up to 29 years, graduates of secondary and post-secondary education. The provided range of services includes career counselling, theoretical training, practical placement and certification, and is directly linked to the development directions of the country's regions, according to the analysis of the Labour Market Needs Diagnosis Mechanism, at the level of the administrative region. It concerns the provision of an integrated, targeted and innovative range of services to 2.455 unemployed young people aged up to 29 years, graduates of secondary and post-secondary education. The provided range of services includes career counselling, theoretical training, practical placement and certification, and is directly linked to the development directions of the country's regions, according to the analysis of the Labour Market Needs Diagnosis Mechanism, at the level of the administrative region. In particular, it includes: 1. Provision of career counselling services. Through these services, individual career counselling sessions are provided, aiming to assist the individual in (re)designing their career path. Within this framework, the profile of the beneficiaries is analysed and their needs, capabilities and skills related to issues of (re)integration into the labour market are investigated. Part of the relevant services is also scheduled to be provided during both theoretical training and practical placement, in order to ensure the interconnection of theoretical training with the subject matter of the practical placement. 2. Provision of continuing vocational training services. These services include theoretical training and practical placement, in a mix that will result according to the outputs of the personalised career counselling. The practical placement will take place in private sector enterprises. The placement of beneficiaries in practical placement positions will be carried out through specialised matching actions and tools that will be fed back from the counselling process and theoretical training. 3. Provision of certification services. Following the successful completion of the training, beneficiaries shall compulsorily participate in certification procedures for their acquired qualifications / skills, through the evaluation of their knowledge and abilities by accredited personnel certification bodies, in accordance with the international standard ISO/IEC 17024 or EOPPEP. The certification will concern the specialised training subjects attended by the beneficiary trainees and will be provided based on standardised procedures, which will be audited by the competent accreditation bodies or EOPPEP. The certification exams shall be mandatorily repeated once (re-examination) in case of failure or inability of the beneficiaries to participate during the first exam.; It concerns the provision of an integrated, targeted and innovative range of services to 2.410 unemployed young people aged up to 29 years, graduates of secondary and post-secondary education. sig_bc43c7ea3be5d5c68c37.description: Long term health conditions can have a significant impact on the lives of people that live with them. Musculoskeletal conditions are one of the most common conditions with impacts for sufferers ranging from management of pain and limits on mobility to problems sleeping and social isolation. We know these conditions can both impact long term health outcomes and make people with them more likely to experience poverty as a result of difficulties engaging with work. Being economically inactive due to these conditions can further impact health outcomes even life expectancy. So how can innovation and technology improve the situation for people with these conditions? Lot 1: . About CivTech CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved: https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-4-help-prevent-detect-and-support-musco-skeletal-conditions

sig_bc43f21f7f16f9a15723.description: The purpose of the contract is structured into three main services and two transversal management services to guarantee support for the Hospital Information System (GIS/HIS) of the La Plana Health Department: 1) Maintenance and Operational Support: Preventive, corrective and adaptive maintenance of care systems (xHIS, xGPC, eHC, PATWIN) and the web and mobility application environment (UHD, Emergency2, Opera2, Intranet, among others), tier 2/tier 3 incident management, and the server and workstation exploitation plan. 2) ECR Development and Migration: Evolution projects, programming of new functionalities and execution of the Extraction, Transformation and Load (ETL) process for the migration of xHIS to the Electronic Clinical Record (ECR). 3) Governance, Quality and Service Transition: Transversal services comprising project management and monitoring through a single point of contact, execution of deliverable quality control plans, user training and security (ENS/GDPR), as well as management of initial deployment and final service return/reversion plans.

sig_bc57d560f7416ee6bfda.description: D. 4. February, the contracting authority published, via contract notice no. 80265-2026, a tender for a framework agreement concerning development, maintenance, application operation and consultancy in connection with Arbejdstilsynet's specialist systems with the description below: I. Background and purpose Arbejdstilsynet is the Danish authority in the field of working environment. Arbejdstilsynet's goal is to promote a safe and healthy working life for everyone and to move the working environment in the right direction. Arbejdstilsynet has a number of specialist systems which Arbejdstilsynet uses in its daily work. The systems support the inspection in terms of preparation, implementation and reporting of inspections as well as secure data in Arbejdstilsynet's registers, data warehouse, etc. The systems are self-developed and are primarily based on Microsoft products. Arbejdstilsynet is tendering with this notice a framework agreement for development, maintenance, application operation and consultancy regarding the inspection's specialist systems. The services must – with the exception of the main service "Projects", cf. below – be delivered by a consultant team offered by the supplier consisting of approx. 40 consultants. The consultants must work in close cooperation with Arbejdstilsynet's own employees in Arbejdstilsynet's agile teams. The consultant team works directly in Arbejdstilsynet's systems. Several of Arbejdstilsynet's specialist systems have an interface to the ESDH system "F2" and have integration points to other public authorities. Arbejdstilsynet uses the State IT (SIT) as an operations supplier and mainly uses SIT's operating model 3a. II. Main services The tendered framework agreement includes the following main services: A) Development and adaptation B) Projects based on a waterfall-based approach C) Maintenance D) Application operation E) Consultancy Re main service A): The supplier must provide development and adaptation of the specialist systems using an agile approach (cf. the SAFE framework), including changes and/or extensions to the systems' functionality, user interface, reports and integrations. Development and adaptation must be delivered in accordance with the frameworks and technologies specified above, cf. section I. Re main service B): The supplier must provide "Projects" based on a waterfall-based approach. The delivery covered by the "Project" must be handed over to Arbejdstilsynet's agile teams (technically and process-wise). Projects must be delivered in accordance with the frameworks and technologies specified above, cf. section I. Re main service C): The supplier must provide maintenance, including technical support, troubleshooting and emergency response. Maintenance must be delivered in accordance with the frameworks and technologies specified above, cf. section I. Re main service D): The supplier must provide application operation on selected specialist systems, which are based on Microsoft products and Sitecore (which is being phased out). The supplier must allocate resources to carry out ongoing application operation. The customer handles the role of release manager itself. Pipelines are executed in Azure DevOps and application monitoring via Grafana. Re main service E): The supplier must provide consultancy in relation to the specialist systems, for example business intelligence, user interfaces and user experience, analysis tasks, development of architecture and technological platform, integrations, security and compliance, performance and monitoring, self-service solutions as well as AI. Consultancy must be delivered in accordance with the frameworks and technologies specified above, cf. section I.
sig_bc57d560f7416ee6bfda.title: Framework agreement on development, maintenance, application operation and consultancy regarding Arbejdstilsynet's professional systems

sig_bc588ca4e4a648c112af.description: This territorial study aims to deliver territorial evidence on development opportunities in Norway’s rural and peripheral regions, with a particular focus on the role of small places as active agents of change and consider the "right to stay" as a potential guiding principle for territorial cohesion. The project will develop a conceptual framework integrating agency, connectivity, and resilience to reconsider what constitutes "success" for small places; provide a territorial typology of small and peripheral places based on identified key drivers of success and systemic barriers in the Norwegian context; present a series of showcases illustrating diverse development pathways; and deliver a set of actionable policy recommendations on governance models, capacity building and financing approaches that can enable change agency in local communities.
sig_bc588ca4e4a648c112af.title: Small Places Matter and the Right to Stay: New Perspectives

sig_bc898841023e647054d4.description: The subject of the procurement is support, maintenance and development services for the emergency care report software as well as other expert services. The emergency care report (EHK) is a form used to record patient data during emergency medical care. The EHK contains information relating to patient health and treatment. In addition to emergency medical services, authorities using the emergency care report include other authorities operating as first responders with official duties. The EHK software is classified as a Class IIa medical device under the Medical Device Regulation (2017/745). The EHK enables real-time processing of patient data directly in the field and at treatment facilities by emergency medical personnel. The estimated value of the procurement calculated in accordance with the Act on Public Defence and Security Procurement (1531/2011) for four (4) years is 2–3,5 million euros (VAT 0 %). The volume of future procurements depends on the system development needs of the security authorities and available funding. The volume may vary significantly in accordance with further development needs and available funding. The estimates are provided without commitment.

Explanation: The award of the procurement of passenger counting sensors and the necessary adjustments to the MOBILEguide software can only be carried out by INIT GmbH, as there is no competition for technical reasons in accordance with § 13 paragraph 2 no. 3 b) SektVO. The defined requirements in their extensive abundance and combination cannot be met by any other potential tenderers. In this case, only INIT GmbH is able to fulfil the listed requirements. The on-board computers used on Rheinbahn vehicles originate from the company INIT GmbH. Only the company INIT GmbH possesses the necessary technical knowledge to carry out any system additions to the on-board computer software in order to be able to connect these to the central component of the ITCS of the Rheinbahn AG. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, the software of the central component of an ITCS and the software of the on-board computers used on vehicles in public transport only possess the same processes if they are procured from the same system manufacturer. The processes are manufacturer-specific standards and as such are subject to trade secrets; they are therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, a bidirectional interface between the central ITCS and the on-board computers used on the vehicles as a mobile component of an ITCS is only fully functional if the participating interface partners are procured from the same system manufacturer. The interface is a manufacturer-specific standard and as such is subject to trade secrets; it is therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. As a result of the examination for the procurement of the central components of the ITCS, it must be determined that the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point regarding mandatory requirements to be fulfilled for the services to be procured. Consequently, a public call for competition would be misleading and the associated effort would be temporally and economically inappropriate for all market participants. The procurement law limits of the public contracting authority's freedom to define the scope of services are adhered to, provided that the definition is objectively justified by the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority has provided comprehensible objective, contract-related and actually existing reasons for this, and the definition does not discriminate against other economic operators. An artificial and therefore impermissible restriction of competition does not exist. The date of the conclusion of the contract with INIT GmbH cannot be entered, as this day is only possible 10 calendar days after the publication of this notice. The procurement office cannot determine exactly at the time of entry when the period of 10 calendar days begins, as the publication is carried out by the Official Journal and generally takes several days that cannot be precisely determined. The procurement office therefore points out that the conclusion of the contract between the Rheinbahn AG and INIT GmbH will take place 10 days after the publication of this notice. Precise information on the deadlines for lodging appeals: §160 para. 3 GWB reads: The application is inadmissible insofar as 1. the applicant has identified the asserted infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the review application and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of ten calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2. infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3. infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4. more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract according to § 135 paragraph 1 number 2. § 134 paragraph 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. sig_bccecd7f79e7b40e8e36.description: Transport for London ("TfL") on behalf of the Greater London Authority ("GLA") is seeking to appoint a supplier to deliver an electronic vote counting system and associated services to be awarded via a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023. TfL is seeking proposals for the supply of an electronic vote counting system ("E-Counting System") and associated services (together "E-Counting Solution Services") for its delivery of the GLA's Mayor of London and London Assembly Elections in 2028 (with an option for the GLA's Mayor of London and London Assembly Elections due to take place in 2032). The E-Counting System technology solution for scanning, counting and calculating results from physical ballot papers will be deployed to a central Count Centre in London and the results for the Mayor of London and the London Assembly Elections contests consolidated, calculated and declared at the Count Centre or a second site, City Hall in London. The GLA expects the successful bidder (Supplier) to provide, tailor and thoroughly test a technology system, in close co-operation with the GLA. The GLA's requirement includes the supply of all scanners, networking and associated technology systems, display equipment, technology / digital systems for capturing information from all London Local Authorities, ballot papers and ballot boxes, as well as distribution to the nominated destinations in each London Local Authority. The Supplier will need to design and provide full training on using the E-Counting System. The GLA will reserve the right to consider the successful technology solution for the 2032 Elections also.
