sig_bcee08648f0238e5763a.description: The Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) deals with societal issues such as the coexistence of Swiss nationals and foreign nationals, asylum issues, internal security, and the fight against crime. Civil status and political rights issues are also part of the FDJP's field of activity, as is the supervision of gambling or the development of foundations and resources for international judicial and police cooperation. In this context, it is natural to work with forms in various formats (paper, PDF and online forms). For this reason, two offices of the FDJP, namely the Federal Office of Police (fedpol) and the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), have joined forces for this acquisition, with the aim of jointly introducing an online solution aimed at harmonising and professionalising the operation of the existing collection of forms from the points of view of development, administration and publication. The forms used in the two offices are aimed at internal users (fedpol / SEM staff) or external users (authorities / population) depending on the case. This collection of forms, most of which were created for a specific use and then made available, has grown over time, so that it presents great heterogeneity regarding administration, formats and other aspects. Furthermore, many forms are obsolete or no longer active. In view of this situation, it is necessary to harmonise, modernise and continue to digitise these forms and their management.

sig_bd0b65fdb3d886df9635.description: Amendment 0001 - (01 OCT 26) This amendment corrects the NAICS code in the text below to 541715 and corrects a typo in section 5.3 adding "Top" to the required FCL clearance. A spreadsheet of the questions and answers to date has also been added to the attachments section. Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Closed Two-Step BAA: SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) The Two-Step Process reduces acquisition resources for both the Government and industry. It may be considered when a large number of proposals are anticipated or to determine if further Government interest is warranted. If further interest is not warranted, industry saves unnecessary bid and proposal costs and the Government saves review time. Broad Agency Announcement Number FA7014-26-S-CS02 Announcement Title SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) Federal Agency Name Secretary of the Air Force Financial Management (SAF/FM) Announcement Type & Acquisition Set-Aside Initial Announcement | 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code & Size Standard 541715 (Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees) Estimated Program Ceiling $24,000,000 (Anticipated Awards: 1 single award) White Paper Submission Deadline October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time Questions Due October 1, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time 1. Overview Information & Two-Step Solicitation Structure SAF/FM is soliciting white papers on the research effort described herein. White papers must be addressed to the Contracting Points of Contact (POCs). This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 541745. White papers and resultant proposals submitted shall strictly comply with this announcement. There will be no separate formal solicitation issued regarding this requirement. This BAA will be republished at yearly intervals for administrative updates and ease of reference. 1.1 Two-Step Acquisition Sequence Step 1 — White Paper Due Date & Submission: White papers may be electronically submitted upon issuance of this BAA until October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time. Only white papers are accepted at this stage. Submissions must be delivered electronically to AFDW/PK at eric.moss.3@us.af.mil and joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil. Step 2 — Formal Proposal Due Date & Time: Formal technical and cost proposals will be requested solely from offerors whose submitted white papers are evaluated as successfully meeting the operational and research needs of the Air Force. Late Receipt Provisions: White paper and proposal receipts after the specified cutoff date and time shall be governed strictly by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). 1.2 Instrument Types and Contracting Guidance The Air Force reserves the right to award the contractual instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype authority, Grant, Cooperative Agreement, OT for Research, or an applicable technology transfer mechanism. Awards under this BAA are generally anticipated to be cost-reimbursement. Offerors are specifically advised that cost-reimbursement contracts require an accounting system determined adequate by the Government for tracking allocable contract costs. 1.3 Communications & Contracting Points of Contact Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged prior to proposal submission. Technical discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to fund or award any proposed effort. Only warranted Contracting Officers possess the legal authority to commit the Government. Inquiries regarding this solicitation should be directed to the Contracting POCs: Primary Contracting Officer: Eric Moss — eric.moss.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Joseph Spear — joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil 2. Section I — Program Description & Strategic Objectives The Department of the Air Force (DAF) has identified critical operational gaps in the enterprise databases, analytical methods, and predictive tools regularly employed for weapon system cost estimating and analysis. DAF is actively committed to modernizing the efficiency, fidelity, and throughput of its cost estimating capabilities. This requirement invests in strengthening, accelerating, and elevating cost data and analytic capabilities using modern data science and cloud engineering technologies to enable faster, higher-quality, and higher-volume analytic decision support across the DAF cost community. The CEMDAR research initiative executes four fundamental architectural shifts across enterprise cost operations: Platform Modernization: Transitioning from legacy desktop-based analytical tools to secure enterprise cloud platforms (e.g., DAF Data Fabric, VAULT, Envision). Relational Data Integration: Moving from isolated, commodity-specific datasets to integrated, relational architectures linking programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule parameters. Pipeline Automation: Replacing static spreadsheets and recurring manual reporting with dynamic, automated data engineering pipelines. Scalable Predictive Modeling: Advancing from low-volume static cost modeling to highly scalable data collection, curation, machine learning, and empirical analytics. 2.1 Strategic Research Objectives Elevating Data Fidelity: Improving the verifiable quality, authenticity, granularity, and volume of empirical data collected and accessible to DAF cost analysts. Relational Enterprise Databases: Engineering centralized, enterprise-level relational cost, schedule, and technical databases adhering to rigorous data science principles and MIL-STD-881 standards. Analytical Workflow Optimization: Constructing capabilities and streamlined workflows that empower analysts to rapidly synthesize large-scale multi-commodity datasets. Predictive Modeling & Decision Support: Establishing authoritative enterprise datasets and generating dynamic Cost Estimating Relationships (CERs), Schedule Estimating Relationships (SERs), Technical Estimating Relationships (TERs), benchmark metrics, interactive dashboards, and cloud-native cost models. The overarching vision is not only to elevate the timeliness and accuracy of program Life-Cycle Cost Estimates (LCCEs) for budgeting, programming, and acquisition milestone decisions, but also to build an agile capability for rapid high-level force design, alternative architecture trades, and component-level engineering trade-off evaluations. 3. Section II — Technical Description & Core Competencies The Department of the Air Force Cost Analysis Agency (AFCAA) is soliciting white papers (and subsequently formal technical and cost proposals from qualified respondents) addressing innovative synchronization of research related to technical, cost and schedule for DoW/DAF programs across the following five Core Competencies. Submitted white papers must move beyond generic capability statements and clearly articulate the offeror's specific technical approach, proposed system architectures and analytical methodologies. Offerors should include concrete examples of relevant past work, demonstrating proven experience in designing data pipelines, executing predictive cost modeling, and conducting targeted cost specific research within defense or similarly regulated enterprise environments. To ensure holistic technical execution, white papers must also address the following staffing and expertise qualifications: Key Personnel Competencies & Experience: Offerors must explicitly summarize the core technical competencies, relevant project experience, and security clearance/access readiness of proposed Key Personnel—specifically the Contractor Program Manager (PM), the Chief Cost Data Scientist (governing Task 2 Level 1 architectural decisions and CADOM pipelines), and any designated Technical / Data Science Task Leads—substantiating the leadership team's qualification to direct contract activities from Day 1. On-Demand Cost & Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Offerors must demonstrate an established, agile capability to deploy specialized Cost and Technical Domain SMEs on an as-required basis. These experts must possess deep commodity and engineering expertise to support targeted cost studies, schedule analyses, and novel data pipeline mapping across diverse defense domains—including Aircraft, Space and Launch Systems, Missiles and Munitions, C4ISR, Cyber and Software Systems, and Operations and Support (O&S) Sustainment. 3.1 Core Competency 1: Enterprise Data Governance, Access, and Research Lifecycle Planning (envisioned PWS Tasks 1 & 2) Task 1 — Data Access Permissions, Proprietary Information Protection, and OCI Governance: Establishes the administrative, legal, and multi-tier security foundation required to ingest proprietary defense data. Offerors must structure and manage Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) across AFCAA, OSD CAPE (for the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise [CADE] repository), Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and prime/subcontractor tiers. Because weapon system cost repositories contain business-sensitive Proprietary Information (PROPIN), tasks require rigorous OEM engagement protocols, proactive OCI screening, and monitoring to eliminate conflicts resulting from corporate reorganizations or contractor commercial affiliations. Task 2 — Integrated Research Planning, POA&M Execution, and Agile Governance: This area establishes a centralized, contractor-maintained Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) serving as the operational roadmap governing all contract activities. The integrated POA&M must establish element-level execution schedules, critical path milestones, risk mitigation triggers, and formal go/no-go evaluation gates integrating all technical efforts: foundational data governance and ingestion, automated Medallion pipeline curation (Task 3), empirical studies and predictive model building (Task 4), acquisition database modernization (Task 5), and surge research directives. To ensure seamless technical integration without compromising Government oversight, offerors must establish a disciplined governance framework that strictly delineates contractor operational management from inherently governmental authority: Contractor Operational Governance: Led by the Chief Cost Data Scientist and Contractor PM, the contractor manages internal agile execution, sprint velocity, data quality gates, and Level 1 Architectural Decisions (internal pipeline scripting, routine algorithms, and code refactoring). The contractor must maintain an Integration and Dependency Matrix linking Task 4 analytical use cases directly to underlying Task 3 data pipelines. Government Technical Oversight: The Government retains all approval and baseline acceptance authority. The AFCAA Technical Lead / COR approves Level 2 Decisions (changes to enterprise data schemas, cloud infrastructure, or CADOM standards), while Level 3 Decisions (cross-agency data sharing and multi-service standards) require stakeholder consensus (AFCAA, OSD CAPE, and Service Cost Centers). 3.2 Core Competency 2: Automated Data Pipeline Engineering & Enterprise Architecture (envisioned PWS Task 3) Cost Analysis Data Operating Model (CADOM) & Medallion Pipeline Architecture: Focuses on architecting, testing, and operationalizing scalable ETL/ELT pipelines unifying disparate programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule data streams into an enterprise CADOM schema. Utilizing modern technologies (Apache Spark, Databricks, Python, SQL, cloud data warehouses), pipelines implement a multi-stage medallion architecture: Bronze (raw ingestion), Silver (cleansed, schema-validated, normalized records), and Gold (curated, high-performance analytical views). Work mandates automated quality gates, comprehensive error-handling and telemetry logging, and full audit lineage tracing Gold metrics back to source records. Target feeds include Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR/FlexFile), Selected Acquisition Reports (SAR/MSAR), Earned Value Management (EVM/IPMDAR), Air Force Total Ownership Cost (AFTOC), and defense budget exhibits. Enterprise Metadata Schema, Data Lineage, and Catalog Services: Maintains and enriches centralized metadata models, embedding automated tagging routines during ingestion to tag program identifiers, commodity domains, and MIL-STD-881 Work Breakdown Structures (WBS). Develops searchable data catalog services (e.g., Unity Catalog, Foundry), implements Data Fidelity Scorecards measuring authenticity and normalization readiness, and enforces granular role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC) across proprietary and classified boundaries. Enterprise Analytical Applications & AI/ML Data Infrastructure: Builds cross-cutting analytic applications and ML pipelines, such as cross-commodity benchmarking engines, automated NLP-driven WBS mapping from historical CSDR submissions, and Silver-layer anomaly detection routines. Manages version-controlled infrastructure-as-code and reproducible deployment scripts inside government-controlled Git repositories. 3.3 Core Competency 3: Data-Driven Analytics, Predictive Modeling, and Application Deployment (envisioned PWS Task 4) This technical area encompasses research, predictive modeling, and application deployment executed through approved subtasks in the POA&M. Depending on operational objectives, subtasks will combine data analysis, dynamic model development, custom tool engineering, and targeted empirical studies: Dynamic Analysis, Predictive Modeling & Empirical Studies: Applies regression, econometrics, machine learning, and Bayesian methods to develop dynamic models, empirical CERs, SERs, TERs, and cost growth benchmarks. Research covers core weapon system commodities—Aircraft (Fixed/Rotary/Unmanned), Space & Launch, Missiles, Cyber/Software, and Operations & Support (O&S) sustainment. Focus areas include, for example, expenditure time-phasing, flight test benchmarks, commercial space cost adjustments, agile software metrics, and AI-generated code productivity/defects. Custom Analytical Applications & CADOM Deployment: Designs, packages, and deploys user-facing tools, calculation workbooks, and interactive dashboards connected directly to CADOM pipelines. Automates repetitive estimating workflows (e.g., inflation/escalation, price normalization, trade-off analysis). In alignment with the Integration and Dependency Matrix, models and containerized applications must comply with CADOM standards and include reproducible code and technical documentation. 3.4 Core Competency 4: Specialized Acquisition Databases and Statutory Cost Reporting Administration (envisioned PWS Task 5) Task 5 (Option CLIN) — AFCAA Contracts Database (KDB) Modernization and Analysis: Modernizes and hosts the enterprise AFCAA Contracts Database within cloud platforms (e.g., VAULT). Fuses procurement data from SAM.gov, FPDS, EDA, and USA Spending with internal metadata models (CSDR, SAR, EVM). Constructs BI pipelines, refines contract growth classification buckets, conducts Engineering Change Order (ECO) analyses to isolate cost drivers, issues quarterly database releases to CADE users, and delivers hybrid user training. 3.5 Core Competency 5: Mission Augmentation and Surge Analytical Capabilities (envisioned PWS Task 6) Task 6 (Option CLIN) — RDT&E Surge Research and Rapid Prototyping Support: Pre-negotiated surge mechanism to rapidly deploy specialized cost estimators, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and technical SMEs for high-priority emergent research, algorithm development, and novel methodology prototyping requiring RDT&E funding. 4. Section III — Contractual, Security, and Administrative Requirements Within Scope Modifications: Due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to execute within-scope adjustments, including modifications to increase contract ceiling. 4.1 Period of Performance and Deliverable Schedule The anticipated period of performance spans 12 to 60 months for the technical effort, tailored to individual award determinations. Hardware and specialized software items shall be determined per contract award. Deliverable Category Contractual Requirement Governing Standard / Delivery Frequency Period of Performance 12 to 60 months total duration Tailored to contract award and CLIN structure Data Items (CDRLs) Research reports, POA&Ms, schemas Specified in resultant Contract Work Statement Software / Codebase Data pipelines, containerized tools Delivered to government repositories; Open/Gov Rights Quarterly Releases AFCAA KDB and CADOM deployments Quarterly release cycles into VAULT/CADE environments 4.2 Security, OPSEC, and Export Control Compliance Facility & Personnel Clearance: Program classification requirements span up to and including Top Secret (refer to RFP DD Form 254). Offerors must maintain an active Facility Clearance and ensure current Cognizant Security Office records are registered with DCSA (www.dcsa.mil). All proposed Key Personnel must hold and maintain an active SECRET security clearance at contract award, and offerors must demonstrate that they have immediate access to personnel that possess the access capability to utilize TOP SECRET / SCI clearances and facilities as required for classified studies and task directives. All non-key contractor and subcontractor personnel assigned to this contract must possess, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher) on Day 1 of contract performance to support Moderate-Risk Public Trust (MRPT) and Common Access Card (CAC) / system access requirements. ). TS/SCI work is anticipated to be a small fraction of the overall work in year 1 but could vary each year as requirements evolve. Operations Security (OPSEC): Contractors and subcontractors must implement Industrial Security, Information Security, Personnel Security, and OPSEC measures to protect critical program data from adversary exploitation and export breaches. Export Control & ITAR: Technical information generated or utilized may be subject to ITAR (22 CFR 120-131) and EAR (15 CFR 710-774). Where applicable, a Certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) must accompany formal proposals. DFARS 252.225-7048 applies to all resulting awards. Contractor Performance Assessment (CPARS): Interim annual evaluations and a final evaluation will be conducted. Contractors are provided 14 calendar days to review and submit rebuttals before final determinations by the authority one level above the Contracting Officer. 4.3 Logistics, Base Support, and Intellectual Property Rights Government-Furnished Property (GFP) / Equipment (GFE): In accordance with Section VI of the PWS, the Government will furnish standard encrypted laptops, required application software licenses, and cloud platform tenant environments (e.g., DAF VAULT / Data Fabric) for authorized contractor personnel performing work under resulting awards. Provisioning will occur within 10–15 business days following security badge issuance. No additional GFP/GFE is anticipated; any extra equipment requested in an offeror's proposal must be pre-approved by the Contracting Officer. Primary contract performance will occur at contractor facilities. However, the Government will provide on-site base access, workspace, and local network connectivity for contractor personnel designated to work on-site or attend recurring program reviews at government locations in the National Capital Region (NCR), and other AFCAA Operating locations as necessary. 4.4 Data Rights and Commercial Software Licensing The Government desires the following data rights determinations: Noncommercial Technical Data: Unlimited Rights. Noncommercial Computer Software (NCS) & Documentation: Unlimited Rights. Commercial Computer Software: Customary Commercial License consistent with Federal procurement statutes. Final data rights will be determined during contract negotiations in accordance with RFO and R-DFARs. Third-party commercial and noncommercial software not reasonably identifiable at proposal submission must be formally approved by the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) prior to incorporation. Software licenses transferred to the Government must not disclaim all warranties via ‘as is’ provisions, must permit use across Air Force and support contractor facilities, and must allow code embedding/derivative works. Licensors must agree to incorporate standard federal preemption terms nullifying any provisions inconsistent with Federal law. 5. Section IV — Proposal Preparation and Evaluation Review This solicitation executes a Two-Step selection process. White papers and proposals must adhere strictly to the guidelines outlined below. The Government reserves the right to review white papers and fund some, all, or none of the proposals received. ONLY WHITE PAPERS ARE BEING SOLICIATED AT THIS TIME. 5.1 Eligibility Information Eligible Offeror: This is a 100% Small Business Set-aside. Cost Sharing or Matching: Cost Sharing is not required. Government Agencies: If a Government agency is interested in performing work, contact the Contracting Officer identified in the BAA. If those discussions result in a mutual interest to pursue your agency's participation, the effort will be pursued independent of this announcement. Other: Foreign Participation: SAF/FM is authorized to exclude all foreign participation at the prime contractor level for the subject procurement. Foreign participation will be addressed for each white paper that have the potential to best meet the Air Force’s needs based on the white paper evaluation information in Section V. Notice to Foreign-Owned Firms: Such firms are asked to immediately notify the Contracting Officer before deciding to respond to this announcement. Foreign contractors should be aware that restrictions might apply which could preclude their participation in this acquisition. There are no limits on the number of white papers/proposals an offeror may submit. You may be ineligible for award if all requirements of this solicitation are not met on the white paper (and later proposal) due date as identified above. 5.2 Step 1: White Paper Submission Format White papers must be structured into four distinct, concise sections. Total of all sections combined should be no more than 30 pages: Offerors must format white paper submissions in accordance with the standard guidelines below. Requirements are kept intentionally streamlined to minimize proposal preparation burden while ensuring equitable technical evaluation. Page Format & Margins: All pages must be formatted for standard 8.5" x 11" paper with a minimum of one-inch (1.0") margins on all four borders. Page orientation must be portrait. Typography & Line Spacing: Narrative text must be single-spaced using Times New Roman (minimum 12-point), Arial (minimum 10-point), or Calibri (minimum 11-point). Text within tables, figures, charts, and diagrams may be reduced to a minimum of 8-point font, provided all content remains legible at 100% zoom. Electronic File Formats: White papers must be submitted electronically via email as a single, searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (pdf) file. The Cost Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) may also include an optional, unlocked Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) workbook showing active formulas and calculations. Do not submit .zip compressed archives or password-protected files. Header/Footer Information: Headers and footers may fall within margin boundaries and must include the BAA number (FA7014-26-S-CS02), company name, CAGE code, and sequential page numbering ("Page X of Y"). Page Limitations: Pages shall be numbered starting with the cover page being Page 1, and the last page being no greater than Page 30. The Government may remove and not evaluate any pages that exceed the established limitations. Section A — Administrative & Corporate Metadata: BAA Number, Title of Research Effort, Company Name, Business Size, CAGE code, DUNS/UEI number, and Company Technical & Contracting POCs (with direct telephone numbers and email addresses). Section B — Technical Approach & Capability Summary: Statement of task objectives; detailed technical methodology demonstrating alignment with Core Competencies 1 through 5; concrete examples of past work demonstrating automated pipeline engineering and predictive cost modeling; and a concise staffing summary detailing: The qualifications, core competencies, relevant experience, and clearance status of proposed Key Personnel; and The offeror's established approach for providing on-demand Cost and Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across weapon system domains as task assignments require. Section C — Cost & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM): Comprehensive ROM cost estimate reflecting labor, data infrastructure, and travel necessary to execute the proposed research. Section D — Associate Contractor Agreements (ACAs): Identification of anticipated ACA frameworks required to exchange proprietary technical data, software code, and research assets among multiple defense contractors. 5.3 Step 1: White Paper Review Criteria MANDATORY EVALUATION GATE: Only white papers submitted by respondents possessing an active and verifiable Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the TOP SECRET level (issued and recorded in the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency [DCSA] National Industrial Security System [NISS] at the time of white paper submission will be reviewed by the Government. Submissions lacking verification of an active Top Secret FCL at the time of submission will be rejected without consideration. Teaming Arrangements and Joint Ventures: In any contractor teaming arrangement or Joint Venture (JV), the Prime Contractor must independently hold an active Top Secret FCL at submission. Cleared entities within the proposed teaming arrangement possessing the requisite FCL must perform at least fifty percent (50%) of the direct labor/technical effort. A cleared subcontractor may not on its own fulfill this requirement on behalf of an uncleared prime contractor. Day-1 Vetting Readiness Attestation: Offerors must certify in Section A of their white paper that: All proposed Key Personnel hold active SECRET security clearances at contract award; All labor planned for Day-1 contract performance possesses, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher); and The offeror possesses verified access capability to deploy appropriately cleared TOP SECRET / SCI analysts as required for classified projects and studies (e.g., representative efforts identified in PWS Appendix A or subsequent POA&M task directives). Technical Relevance: Is the proposed technical approach rigorously consistent with the research domains and technologies listed in this BAA? Government Interest: Does the proposed technical methodology address urgent analytical gaps and provide high-value decision support to SAF/FM and AFCAA? Fiscal Viability: Is appropriate research and operational funding available to support the proposed scope and period of performance? 5.4 Step 2: Full Proposal Preparation & Evaluation Offerors receiving favorable white paper evaluations will receive an official Request for Proposal (RFP) detailing Step 2 technical and cost submission instructions, review criteria, and formal deliverable requirements. Offerors will be notified regarding recommendation for full proposal submission on or about 30 calendar days following white paper receipt. 5.5 Statutory and Administrative Disclosures Acquisition of Commercial Items: The Government is not utilizing FAR Part 12 policies for this solicitation. Interested firms may submit commercial capability statements within 15 calendar days of notice issuance. Support Contractor Participation: Government employees will conduct all evaluations. Commercial contractor personnel providing administrative support to AFDW/PK are bound by non-disclosure agreements protecting proprietary data. Debriefing & Feedback Sessions: Offerors may request a debriefing session consistent with governing BAA and FAR acquisition procedures. Responsibility Matters (FAR 52.209-9): Applies to awards exceeding $600,000 where affirmative responsibility matters are checked under FAR 52.209-7. Proposal Adequacy Checklist: Pursuant to DFARS 215.408, proposals requiring certified cost or pricing data must include the completed DFARS 252.215-7009 Proposal Adequacy Checklist.

sig_bd82489f9e2f602380d8.description: The subject of the procurement is a system that supports the management of the procurement lifecycle by enabling the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of procurements. The system promotes the assessment of overall economic efficiency, responsibility and effectiveness, as well as the transition from decentralised and manual processes to a centralised, digital and transparent operating model. The procurement lifecycle system forms an essential part of the organisation's procurement management and development. The system strengthens overall economic efficiency, supports contract management and enables the systematic utilisation of lifecycle thinking and responsibility criteria. It allows existing data and processes to be utilised seamlessly. The procurement supports the organisation's strategic goals by strengthening, in particular, the effectiveness, transparency and responsibility of procurements. The system enables the strategic management of procurements and improves the efficiency of data-driven management and reporting. Functional and technical requirements for the procurement lifecycle system 1. Functional requirements The system must support the management of the entire procurement lifecycle as a single entity so that all stages can be carried out in the system from start to finish. The system must enable at least the following functionalities: • planning, preparation and scheduling of procurements, tendering and implementation of procurements using various procedures in accordance with the Procurement Act • receipt, comparison and evaluation of tenders • documentation of procurement decisions and justifications • contract management, monitoring and management of options • checking of contractor liability information • supplier management, monitoring and cooperation • reporting, monitoring and analytics of procurements. The system must enable the implementation of all procurement procedures in accordance with the Procurement Act (1397/2016), in addition to making procurements below the national threshold, including: • open procedure • restricted procedure • negotiated procedure • competitive dialogue • direct procurement • procurements based on framework agreements • dynamic purchasing system. The system must also support internal procurement processes so that the system forms a coherent whole in which the different stages of procurement are integrated with each other. 2. Documentation and structure The system must include structured document templates that guide the uniformity of procurement processes and documents. The requirement is that: • editable document templates (e.g. requests for tenders, draft contracts) can be built within the system. • documents consist of structured data (not just free-form text). • the system guides the user to correct and lawful documentation according to the stages of the procurement procedure. • version control and approval history of documents are traceable. • the system supports uniform terminology, structure and content throughout the organisation. • the system enables the use of free-form attachments and documents alongside structured data, which supports different procurement situations and the organisation's needs. The goal is to ensure the uniformity, lawfulness and high-quality and comparable documentation of procurement processes. 3. Technical implementation and integrations The system must meet the following technical requirements: • browser-based user interface without separate installations on user devices. • support for user roles and access rights management. • secure authentication (e.g. strong authentication, SSO possibility). • logging and audit trail of all actions. • high availability and trouble-free operation. The system must be integrable with key background systems such as the case management system and it must be integrable with the procurement lifecycle system of Kuopio city's in-house company Sansia Oy, so that synergy benefits are achieved taking into account the entire procurement entity, as Sansia Oy carries out procurements exceeding the threshold for Kuopio city and manages the procurement contracts concerning them. Procurement contracts carried out by Sansia Oy and the information concerning them must be made visible more seamlessly in the Kuopio city system and they must be connectable to the city's procurement data. Integrations must support automatic data transfer and reduce manual entry. A uniform data model and interface solutions support automatic data transfer and reduce manual entry when integrations are defined and implemented as part of the overall architecture.
sig_bd82489f9e2f602380d8.title: Procurement of a procurement lifecycle system

sig_bd89e58073bcdb90ec3a.description: The purpose of the tender is to re-establish the SUF's existing dynamic purchasing system regarding IT consultancy services in the health sector, as the dynamic purchasing system is undergoing a renewed tender with minor adjustments compared to the old dynamic purchasing system due to a platform change. The tender for the dynamic purchasing system for IT consultants in the health sector is divided into the following 11 categories: Category 1 IT architecture in relation to the healthcare system and associated security components. Category 2 BI, management information, data analysis on health data. Category 3 Project management in relation to the procurement and implementation of health systems. Category 4 Advice and assistance for process and implementation in connection with health systems in a cross-sectoral perspective. Category 5 Advice within infrastructure, mobility, MDM and related strategy in the healthcare system. Category 6 Test management. Category 7 Data warehouse development, expansion and maintenance. Category 8 Development, expansion and maintenance of auxiliary programmes. Category 9 Advice and assistance for operation, system administration and maintenance of health systems. Category 10 Project Contract Management for IT contracts within the health and care sector. Category 11 Compliance regarding IT systems, processes and data within the health and care sector. Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice on IT architecture specifically in relation to the healthcare system, including special IT architecture and security issues regarding the handling and exchange of personal sensitive data in care systems. In addition, for example, advice within IT security issues in relation to national security components and cross-sectoral cooperation within the health sector.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and data analysis specifically within the health sector and based on health data. The advice includes, among other things, qualification and delivery of management information based on data analysis as well as more general Business Intelligence on health data.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, project management for the procurement and implementation of health systems, including planning and management of user training for health staff, management of the relationship with, and deliveries from, internal and external technical suppliers.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and assistance for processes in connection with the implementation of new health and care systems. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on the implementation of new health systems in a cross-sectoral perspective, where experience from sectors other than the municipal one (regional, general practitioners, etc.) can be utilised.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, strategic advice on the procurement, use and implementation of mobile devices in a health perspective as well as infrastructure such as WAN, LAN and WiFi. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on contractual and commercial conditions, including operation, SLA and market standards within the public agreement infrastructure (SKI and state agreements) in relation to procurements within the area.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice on and handling of test management in connection with the procurement and implementation of welfare technologies and health-related IT systems. In addition, the advice includes, among other things, test management specifically in relation to municipal use and interfaces to other sectors in the healthcare system.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, further development of existing data warehouse solutions in SUF as well as maintenance of the same, primarily based on, but not limited to, Microsoft SQL and SSIS. Development and maintenance also include, among other things, presentation of data analyses from health-related information in various welfare technologies and IT systems via dashboards and similar automated consolidated views of complex data.; Includes services within, for example, but not limited to, new or further development of existing or new auxiliary programmes in SUF as well as maintenance of the same. Development and maintenance include all auxiliary programmes that can help SUF in various contexts. This may cover programmes that take over sub-functions of previous systems or it may include full or partial new development of new programmes to cover special functions for the City of Copenhagen, Health and Care Administration.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice and assistance for operation, system administration and maintenance in connection with the implementation of new and old health and care systems. The advice also includes, among other things, advice on operation, system administration and maintenance of new and old health systems, where experience from other similar systems can be utilised.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, Project Contract Management for IT contracts within the health and care sector, including, for example, assistance with the optimisation of contract management of the covered contracts, help with the capitalisation of the contracts' potential, assistance with projects regarding IT procurements by, for example, EU tenders or mini-tenders on existing framework agreements or dynamic purchasing systems.; Includes services such as, but not limited to, advice, project management and executing tasks in connection with MDR, GDPR and NIS2, as well as other legislation in relation to IT compliance, including, for example, implementation of EU regulations and other legislation regarding IT compliance, assessment and interpretation of the legislation in question, executing tasks regarding compliance, project management in relation to the implementation of compliance.

sig_bdf52152e7f5e8c97b2b.description:
The services forming the subject of the contract consist of the recognition, identification, information completion and reporting of Musical Works and related sound recording carriers used in Rai radio and television programmes and broadcasts, through the use of automatic recognition systems, specialist databases, and validation and control activities, in order to enable the correct fulfilment of obligations laid down by applicable regulations and licence agreements with Collecting Societies. As part of the service, the Supplier shall, inter alia: • acquire and monitor the audio/video streams and data necessary for reporting; • recognise and identify Musical Works and related Carriers using automatic recognition systems and the further methodologies provided for in the Technical Specification; • complete, verify and update the metadata necessary for reporting; • prepare, transmit and rectify Cue Sheets according to the prescribed layout; • manage the Black List, Waste Files and remediation and correction activities; • produce the reports and evidence requested by Rai for the purposes of checks and audits. The services also include start-up, commissioning, operational support and exit transition activities necessary to ensure the continuity and correct execution of the reporting process. Rai reserves the right to request, in whole or in part, the following "on-request" services: a) reporting of Musical Works and Carriers relating to the programming of channels currently branded with the "Rai Italia" trademark; b) recognition and reporting of Musical Works and Carriers relating to content available on the "RaiPlay" platform; c) recognition and reporting of Musical Works and Carriers relating to content available on the "RaiPlay Sound" platform; d) recognition and reporting of Musical Works and Carriers relating to programmes already broadcast in periods prior to the contract duration on general television and radio channels. In such cases, Rai shall make available to the Supplier the opportunity to listen to and/or view the relevant recordings; e) recognition and reporting of Musical Works and Carriers relating to programmes already broadcast in periods prior to the contract duration on thematic, regional and linguistic minority television and radio channels. In such cases, Rai shall make available to the Supplier the opportunity to listen to and/or view the relevant recordings; f) processing and analyses relating to the representativeness of Collecting Societies with reference to specific channels, schedules and/or time periods; g) segmentation of television programming for the purpose of identifying the actual broadcast time of programmes; h) segmentation of radio programming for the purpose of identifying the actual broadcast time of programmes; i) completion and integration of Rai data relating to Programme Content Declarations (DCP); j) integration and reconciliation of the data collected by the Supplier with the information regarding musical uses contained in the Programme Content Declarations (DCP) prepared by Rai. For a detailed description of the technical and functional characteristics of the services in question, as well as the methods for their execution, please refer to the Technical Tender Specification. - pursuant to Article 58 of the Code and in application of the relevant principles, the procedure is divided into a single lot for the following reasons: (i) the services forming the subject of the contract constitute a unitary and strongly integrated process of recognition, identification, information completion and reporting of Musical Works and related phonographic data, which requires the unitary and homogeneous management of the same Database in order to ensure consistency, uniqueness and uniformity of the reporting results; (ii) the execution of the services presupposes the use of a single operational methodology, a single recognition system and a single application integration between the Supplier's systems and those of the Client, as well as the coordinated management of Cue Sheets, the Black List, Rejections and Rectifications, activities which exhibit a high degree of technical and operational interdependence; (iii) any subdivision into lots would entail the need to coordinate different economic operators, potentially equipped with different databases, recognition systems, classification criteria and updating processes, with the consequent risk of information misalignment, duplication of activities, operational inefficiencies and an increase in coordination and control costs; (iv) unitary management of the service also makes it possible to pursue objectives of organisational efficiency and economic advantage in the contractual action, avoiding the fragmentation of responsibilities and ensuring homogeneous oversight of the entire reporting process. The overall value of the contract has been indicated as EUR 2.495.386,00, excluding VAT, for a period of 48 months, broken down as follows: o EUR 1.963.195,00 net of VAT for the base period of 36 months, broken down as follows:  EUR 1.402.430,00 net of VAT as the amount, subject to discount, for continuous "fee-based" services and inclusive of EUR 20.000 for the start-up of activities;  EUR 560.765,00 net of VAT as the total overall amount not subject to discount, for specialist "on-request" services; o EUR 532.191,00 net of VAT for the optional period of 12 months, broken down as follows:  460.810,00 net of VAT subject to discount, in the event of the exercise of the extension option referred to in Article 120 paragraph 10 of the Code for a further year, relating to continuous "fee-based" services;

 EUR 71.381,00 net of VAT as the total overall amount not subject to discount, for specialist "on-request" services. The overall amount for specialist "on-request" services represents a maximum expenditure ceiling that is not binding on Rai, up to which contractual services may be activated exclusively on the basis of actual business requirements and upon specific request by RAI. The relative economic valuation of the individual specialist "on-request" services shall take place by applying the single discount offered to the unit prices indicated in the "discounted" unit price table included in the tender documentation.

sig_be09ebe17efbbe17b102.description: The municipalities in Rogaland, organised through the Digi Rogaland cooperation, inform that a joint procurement of health technology is planned for the municipalities in Rogaland. Stavanger municipality is managing the procurement. The contracting authority intends to get a total agreement on health technological equipment, response services and user interface. The aim of this notice is to give the market early information on the coming competition and create predictability. The procurement is expected to include both user orientated and employee orientated technology, in addition to software that collects all data in one user interface. Seamless and secure data flow is expected between equipment, user interface and EPJ. The scope of the procurement leads to a high complexity and many needs that shall be covered. The volume, number of users and technologies can vary between the municipalities, and the system must be able to scale up over time. This will be clarified in the tender documentation. See the attached document for further information on the procurement.
sig_be09ebe17efbbe17b102.title: Pending joint procurement of health technology in Rogaland.

sig_be0d69b6e6a40f7dfbca.description: The University of Geneva wishes to implement an integrated software platform allowing the unified management of all functions related to real estate assets: asset repository, space management, equipment maintenance, occupant services and energy management. The objective is to have a structuring tool to support the evolution of the campus (~70 buildings, ~220 000 m2, 8 sites), optimise resource use and support environmental sustainability. This call for tenders comprises two lots conducted simultaneously: Acquisition of a facility management software solution (licences and implementation services), deployed in three successive phases over the period 2026–2029. The solution covers five functional domains: real estate assets, maintenance, spaces and booking, finance, energy and sustainability. It is intended for DiBAT employees, all UNIGE employees and, for certain modules, students.; Acquisition of licences for a SaaS software solution forming the structured digital foundation of building data and documents of UNIGE and OCBA. This contract relates exclusively to licences and publisher maintenance/support; integration, migration and parameterisation are carried out internally by UNIGE. The two lots are subject to separate procedures. Tenderers may bid for both lots.
sig_be0d69b6e6a40f7dfbca.title: AO SI FM BATIMENTS 2026

Division into lots of the object of the contract is not envisaged pursuant to the exception provided for in article 99.3.b) of the LCSP 2017. Each and every one of the different tasks required in the specifications of technical requirements corresponds to an integrated technical solution. The tasks relating to the software must be perfectly integrated and prove perfectly compatible. Independent performance of the various services comprised in the object of the contract makes the correct execution thereof difficult from a technical point of view (it would prove excessively difficult or burdensome) given that, as all of them are closely linked and interrelated, they could present serious compatibility and security/confidentiality problems if they are not offered, supplied, implemented and provided in a completely integrated manner. The estimated value of the supply is established at 56,26% whereas the services associated with the service amount to 43,74%. Therefore, the rules governing this file shall be those specific to the supply contract.

sig_be38b275ca2dede2385f.description: This tender concerns the establishment of an agreement for the provision of Managed Detection and Response (MDR) services to DSB, aimed at supporting, strengthening, and further developing the contracting authority's overall cybersecurity capacity across the organization's IT and relevant OT environments. The purpose of the tender is to identify and contract with a supplier capable of delivering a cohesive, scalable, and mature service that integrates with DSB’s existing security organization, including the Security Operations Center (SOC), and complements it with advanced competencies, methods, and technological capabilities in monitoring, detection, analysis, response, and proactive security activities. The tender encompasses a comprehensive service delivery, which includes controlled and continuous monitoring of security incidents, structured and efficient handling of security incidents, access to dedicated resources for managing critical incidents, provision of qualified and contextualized threat intelligence, and execution of proactive analyses such as threat hunting. The delivery must comply with the requirements, service objectives, and other terms specified in the contract and its annexes.

We are now seeking a development partner to provide a new system that delivers improved functionality, efficiency, and user experience. sig_be572afeabc2c3630b54.description: The general objective pursued by the project is to streamline the judicial system by providing it with a modern IT system adapted to current needs, which supports its specific activity. The specific objective to which the provision of services contributes consists of the modernisation and adaptation of the ECRIS electronic case management system to meet the current needs of the judicial system. The new ECRIS V System includes a multitude of specific technical and functional objectives, related to the development/customisation and implementation of software and hardware products, objectives organised and structured around the software components essential to its operation. Among the expected advantages of the future system, we mention:  the electronic file, which will allow beneficiaries to fully manage documents in files electronically (at the level of courts and prosecutor's offices), without, however, excluding the use of paper, so as not to restrict access to justice for people who do not have the possibility of using technology;  interconnection with other existing IT systems;  an indispensable tool made available to the management of the judicial system, offering, through the information provided, both an overview and a picture of specific situations, in order to make decisions regarding its operation under optimal conditions. Procurement of IT consultancy/expertise services for the development, testing and commissioning of the new ECRIS V case management system, including staff training services, in accordance with the award documentation.
sig_be572afeabc2c3630b54.title: Procurement of IT consultancy/expertise services for the development, testing and commissioning of the new ECRIS V case management system, including staff training services

sig_be6cd6cda274f4daf34d.description: Naval Special Warfare Command (NSWC) and its subordinate and associated commands seek to accelerate the development, procurement and integration of unmanned systems (UxS) capabilities in support of the Joint Force, Special Operations Forces (SOF), and allied SOF. NSWC seeks to award Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) contracts or Other Transaction Authority agreements (OT) (see 10 U.S.C. §§ 4021-23) to provide a new method of delivering UxS systems capability called “UxS as a service” and First Person View (FPV) platforms. Resultant contracts or agreements should provide systems with a broad range of capabilities that directly support mission effectiveness in terms of platforms, payloads, Processing-Exploitation-Dissemination (PED), programming (i.e., firmware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI)), communications/data transfer, Command and Control (C2) systems, components, and/or material to be acquired, developed, or already in use by NSWC, United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), the Department of War (DoW), or the U.S. Government, as well as interagency and FVEY partners. sig_beabb305fda4354a4b1e.description: Among others, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GmbH (GIZ) is currently implementing two projects in the agricultural sector in South Sudan. The bilateral project "Community-based Rural Development in South Sudan" (CDRD) is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-financed by the Directorate-General for International Cooperation (DGIS) of the Kingdom of Netherlands as well as the European Union (EU) and runs from April 2022 to March 2029. The project, "Improved Living Conditions and Psychosocial Support in the Context of Displacement and Displacement" (ILiPS), is commissioned by BMZ under the Special Initiative on Displaced Persons and Host Countries (SIGA), with a project period ranging from October 2022 to December 2026. Both projects" main components focus on agricultural development of rural smallholder households. With its additional funding received in 2025, ILiPS now supports 2,000 households within Central and Eastern Equatoria. With its EU extension from 2024, CDRD supports now a total of 27,500 smallholder households across in Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, Nothern Bar el Ghazal and Western Bahr El Ghazal. All monitoring activities of the GIZ projects in South Sudan are centrally organized and coordinated by the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Unit. To measure progress and ensure accountability, both projects use a rigorous monitoring system based on representative household surveys. Data is collected once per year, with baseline, midline and endline surveys for each cohort. In addition to quantitative surveys, the projects employ a mixed-method approach combining household interviews with Focus Group Discussions and Key Informant Interviews. This design allows the projects to generate robust longitudinal and cross-sectional data on production capacity, income levels, nutrition and resilience, while also capturing the social, cultural and gender dynamics that shape household behaviour. Particular emphasis is placed on monitoring the impact of agricultural training on farming practices and the adoption of sustainable methods. The evidence generated is used for donor reporting, project steering and strategic decision-making in the multi-donor context. By disseminating results to national and local actors, the projects also contribute to learning across the wider partner system. In this way, ILiPS and CDRD strengthen the resilience of rural households in South Sudan while providing actionable knowledge for future programming in fragile contexts. Lot LOT-0001: 81321664-Annual Impact Surveys of target groups. The contractor will design and implement a multi-annual mixed-methods survey and qualitative research for the ILiPS and CDRD projects in South Sudan. The services include the development, adaptation and translation of questionnaires for household surveys, including a dedicated module on women of reproductive age. The questionnaires must follow a layered design with "must-have" questions for donor reporting and project steering, "should-have" questions to ensure context-specific adaptation of core themes, and "nice-to-have" questions that can be added according to regional or cohort-specific needs. All tools are to be translated into relevant local languages and pre-tested in the field to ensure clarity and feasibility, and must be designed in a conflict-sensitive and culturally appropriate manner. Sampling must ensure representativeness at state and cohort level with a margin of error of eight percent for both state-level and displacement-strata estimates. Each beneficiary sample shall be matched by a control group of non-beneficiaries in neighbouring Payams, representing half the sample size. The contractor will apply stratified random sampling and use a digital data collection tool, preferably Survey Solutions on GIZ servers, in order to guarantee secure and efficient handling of data. Comprehensive training of enumerators, field supervision and quality assurance measures are required throughout. The contractor will carry out household surveys for each cohort at the relevant survey stage. For ILiPS, this includes midline data collection in two states in 2026. For CDRD, this includes midterm and endline data collection for the 2024 and 2025 cohorts, as well as a final endline across all states in 2028. The surveys will gather information on sustainable food production capacity, income-generating activities and diversification, household consumption patterns and nutrition, as well as the adoption of sustainable farming practices following project-supported trainings. The mixed-method approach further includes qualitative research through Focus Group Discussions and Key Informant Interviews. These serve to provide deeper insights into community perceptions of project interventions, barriers to adoption of sustainable practices, and the roles of women and youth in income generation. The qualitative findings complement the quantitative survey data by explaining why certain changes occur, identifying structural and cultural factors influencing livelihoods, and highlighting lessons for future interventions. All collected data must be cleaned, validated and analysed. The contractor is responsible for preparing analytical reports for each round of data collection, integrating both quantitative and qualitative findings. Reports shall include descriptive results, trend analyses, and clear recommendations for project management and donor decision-making. The contractor must ensure ethical data handling, compliance with the "do no harm" principle, and avoidance of structural bias. Dissemination of findings to the partner system and local stakeholders is an integral part of the assignment, ensuring that results are accessible and contribute to learning beyond project boundaries. Finally, the contractor must establish a robust operational and security plan for data collection in the fragile context of South Sudan. This includes clear timelines, staffing, coordination with GIZ and implementing partners, risk assessments, contingency planning and adherence to humanitarian security protocols. The assignment therefore requires an experienced research organisation with proven expertise in large-scale data collection in fragile contexts, strong methodological capacities, effective field presence and security systems, and experience in agricultural and food security surveys. The contractor must ensure high-quality delivery across all phases of implementation, while maintaining conflict sensitivity, context appropriateness and methodological rigour.
sig_beabb305fda4354a4b1e.title: 81321664-Annual Impact Surveys of target groups

sig_becd34ff8606e3c8f432.description: Social Service Time (MDT) is a programme of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, in collaboration with young people, social organisations, schools, municipalities and other ministries. In this way, the involvement of young people in society is increased. The nature of the assignment concerns all aspects of data handling required for carrying out the ongoing monitoring research. In addition to data collection, the data must also be managed and made accessible, monitored and managed, via multiple tools/files/dashboards/databases. The collected data is used to gain insight into the effects and impact of MDT. Maximum €3.303.000,- excl. VAT for an assignment with a duration of 2 years and the option to extend 2x by 1 years. sig_bf0aaeecfc82c0124c16.description: The Sussex Police Safer Roads Team are committed to protecting the road users of Sussex, as part of Operation Crackdown we work with members of the public, volunteers and officers to gather intelligence and investigate occurrences of poor driving within our communities. As part of our commitment, Sussex Police is looking to work with suppliers to deliver three requirements related to anti-social driving and community speed watch. • A front-end product that offers the public the ability to report anti-social driving (inc. video submissions/journey cam) in a streamlined manner. (Anti-Social Driving) • A product that offers Community Speed Watch volunteers the ability to record speed results. (Community Speed Watch) Both of the above must feed into: • An effective back-office function for the case management and investigation of anti-social driving and community speed watch, allowing interoperability between teams and clear reporting mechanisms. This solution must also be able to provide the following functionality as a minimum: o Batch print educational letters – These are sent to drivers following a report or investigation. o Produce performance reporting data which will enable governance and oversight o Allow for customer facing messaging o Integrate with government databases including DVLA and PNC to automatically carry out DVLA checks to obtain registered keeper details and allowing Officers to carry out Policing National Computer checks. o Assignment of casework to officers Objectives: Where possible, we are eager to explore single solutions that can meet the requirements above, or as a minimum have the operability to connect between systems to ensure information is accessible and remove the need for double handling of information. The solution(s) will need to be hosted either in the Sussex Polices cloud environment or within a vendor hosted cloud infrastructure. The solution must be modern, future-proof, fully supported, and accessible across multiple devices (including mobile platforms). Lot 1: .
sig_bf0aaeecfc82c0124c16.title: Antisocial Driving (ASD) and Community Speed Watch (CSW) Replacement and Modernization

sig_bf18767f6cc839b68645.description: Kirkon keskusrahasto is initiating a market dialogue with this notice regarding the potential procurement of a document management system. PURPOSE OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The aim of the market survey is to survey alternative solutions on the market and build an overall picture of the technical, functional and economic benefits of the various alternatives, as well as to help evaluate them objectively before launching a potential procurement. This request does not request or submit tenders, but invites interested tenderers to participate in the market survey. The information that emerges during the market survey will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for the planning of a potential procurement. Neither the invitation nor the market survey itself obliges the contracting authority to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request for information or in any other way. No compensation will be paid for registering for the market survey, responding to it or participating in the meeting, nor is participation a prerequisite for participation in a potential tender process. DESCRIPTION OF THE CURRENT STATE The current document management system is Tweb by Triplan Oy, and it is currently used by 9 diocesan chapters, nearly sixty parish economies and the Church Office, each of which forms its own registry within the system (multi-registry model). Parishes have been able to adopt the document management system if they wish. There are a total of 207 parish economies. In addition to case and document management, the system includes official decisions, meeting management, a publication portal and trustee portals for the General Synod and parishes. A speech review section for the General Synod has been customised for the General Synod portal, from which representatives' speeches can be imported into the document management system and published online. Documents produced by the General Synod are published in the General Synod portal during the meeting, and it serves as a data bank for General Synod representatives and committee secretaries. The system features a customised registry-specific mass deletion functionality. The system does not contain a separate archiving feature, nor have electronic transfers been made from it to any other system. In addition to producing meeting management, the Church Office and some diocesan chapters have retrospectively imported digitised and born-digital diary material into the system; other organisations use it solely as a document management system. Operations in accordance with the description of the current state, as well as the aforementioned functions customised for the current system, are central to the church's operating environment, which the document management system must support. At present, a particular shortcoming is an electronic long-term archiving solution integrated as part of the document management system package. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Suppliers can declare their interest in participating in the market dialogue by submitting a declaration of interest and a brief presentation of the document management system they offer, including reference projects, in Finnish by email to hankinnat.kirkkohallitus@evl.fi at the latest by 15.5.2026. CONTACT AND SELECTION OF SUPPLIERS FOR THE DIALOGUE Kirkon keskusrahasto will contact all operators who have expressed their interest after the deadline has passed. As a rule, 6 suppliers will be invited to the dialogue, selected by comparing the submitted system presentations and reference projects against the needs described above. According to the preliminary schedule estimate, the market dialogues are scheduled to take place in August-September in weeks 34-37 via Teams. The market dialogues will be conducted in Finnish.
sig_bf18767f6cc839b68645.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Document management system

sig_bf3ae200ba572e488c45.description: Within the GCA Energy Category, we operate a managed service on behalf of the public sector, aggregating their energy demand and purchasing on the wholesale market under a number of risk strategies. In order to support these activities, we require a cloud-based energy portfolio management solution, suitable for managing the GCA Energy portfolio frameworks, which includes; c.1,200 customers, c.108,000 power / gas meters, c. 80,000 sites There is currently no system in place to meet these requirements. This requirement will run on a 3 month trial period. If after the trial period concludes successfully, the supplier will be awarded the subsequent contract term and value. The value included in this notice is for the trial period only. Any subsequent contract term is subject to further budgetary approval which, will be confirmed at the future procurement stage. The proposed system must be able to accurately record the customer portfolio data for both gas and power, including site and meter information and assigned trading strategy. Each of the meters is assigned to a customer and a site. Each meter is attached to current and future Gas / Power buying strategies with varying buying lengths. The system must support the ability for nominated energy suppliers to access the meter data for their assigned customers. We also require the ability for customers to complete a self-serve audit of their portfolio and buying strategy, including the ability to request changes and additions to their portfolio. The system should have the The ability to extract data via API (REST) to integrate with the rest of our data infrastructure The successful supplier will be expected to provide ongoing management maintenance of the solution throughout the duration of the contract to ensure its effective running and optimisation. The dates included in this notice are indicative and subject to change. GCA intend to run this procurement opportunity via commercial agreement Demand Management & Renewables DPS RM6313. Should you intend to bid, you will need to onboard onto the agreement. Please follow the below link and click "access as a supplier": https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6313?nav=0
sig_bf3ae200ba572e488c45.title: The Provision of an Energy Portfolio Management System

sig_bf426dc0b07780c89cee.description: I: Background and purpose: Domstolsstyrelsen (DSS) is tendering a contract for application maintenance, further development and support of the DSI Applications, which consist of several underlying IT systems and associated support systems. The DSI Applications handle case processing for the criminal, probate and civil types. The support systems ensure integration with the courts' other systems and external stakeholders. DSS services approximately 2.500 users internally within the Danish Courts, including the Faroe Islands and Greenland, as well as many external users, e.g. lawyers and similar, who need to access legal information via the services made available by DSS. The contract covers approx. 40 applications, including specialist systems, integrations, software packages and support systems etc., and involves both standard and in-house developed systems, cf. Appendix 3 of the tender documents. The applications covered by the contract have a high degree of social criticality. Among other things, DSS therefore wishes to achieve a secure, stable, up-to-date and cost-effective delivery of the services. sig_bf5e743f13ae39e7a39c.description: IKOMM AS invites tenderers, on behalf of Enebakk municipality, to a market survey for the procurement of a new map and management system for water and sewage. Enebakk municipality shall procure a new map and management system for water and sewage in autumn 2026 in the municipality. The municipality needs a future orientated, comprehensive and user-friendly system for managing the water and sewage network. The system shall support both administrative and operative activities and facilitate efficient interaction between employees in offices and personnel in the field. The system must be available via modern web technology and function on different devices (PCs, tablets and mobile), so that registration, updating and posting can be carried out where the work actually takes place. The system shall support efficient registration and management of the pipeline network, manholes and the accompanying technical installations, including the use of GNSS/GPS equipment for precise surveying. The system shall meet strict requirements for information security and stand-by, reduce operational and maintenance costs and ensure that the municipality meets the current environmental and reporting requirements. >: We would like to carry out a market survey (RFI) in order to gain insight into relevant systems, technology and suppliers. Furthermore, we would like to invite up to 3 tenderers to public dialogue meetings to take a closer look at the options that can offer to ensure a good future orientated procurement. Other municipalities in the region will also be invited to participate in this market survey in order to possibly participate in a future competition. > > > > The dialogue meetings are planned to be held in early April as physical meetings in IKOMM ́s premises in Vinterbro, but with an option for participation in Teams. Relevant tenderers will be selected based on relevance, experience and references from equivalent and comparable municipal systems. The objective of the market survey is to: * Gain insight into what systems and suppliers are available in the market * Examine how the tenderers handle technical requirements, integration, security and stand-by * Using the knowledge to improve the requirement specifications and choice of procurement strategy. > This market dialogue will be carried out as a voluntary and non-binding request for information (Request for Information – RFI), cf. FOA § 9-3 and § 12-2, which allow contracting authorities to obtain information about the market before any competition. > > This is not part of a competition and does not involve any obligations for Enebakk municipality or for the tenderers who choose to provide answers. > > Tenderers who participate in the market dialogue will not be given any kind of competition, and participation (or lack of participation) will not lead to exclusion from a later competition. Any future procurements will be implemented in accordance with public procurement regulations, and all tenderers will be able to compete on equal terms. > We therefore invite interested suppliers to provide written input and possibly participate in dialogue meetings. Participation is voluntary and the market dialogue is not binding for the municipality or suppliers. Good if suppliers can give feedback on the possibility of participation in the dialogue meetings that are planned. > attached a disposition/questionnaire for the market survey. > All dialogue will take place in the KDV tool Artifik for traceability. Please use Artifik support if this tool is unknown to suppliers.

sig_bf870a7435c72027bc7a.description: The aim of the submission is the procurement of customisable support services for a large number of public authorities with heterogeneous needs. The support services are to ensure that citizens and administrative staff are supported continuously when using eGov applications and in particular with authentication (e.g. via AGOV). Procurement model and scope The submission is designed as a framework agreement tender with up to four successful tenderers in order to be able to take into account the considerable organisational and operational heterogeneity of the various demand locations. The specific services (e.g. language, media, use cases and the like) and their scope per demand location are determined on a demand-specific basis within the framework of mini-tender procedures, based on the framework agreements concluded with the successful tenderers. The specification of services used for the submission (Appendix 01) represents the maximum ("most complex") manifestation of the possible services. The services are divided into three main areas: * ID 1: Onboarding: Conception and introduction of the support services. * ID 2: Support services & Reporting: Provision of 1st-level support (by telephone, email and/or ticketing system) in German, French, Italian and/or English as well as extensive monthly reporting and management of steering committees. * ID 3: 24/7 Support: Provision of 1st-level support in accordance with ID 2 around the clock. Quality standards and billing The quality of the service is measured using key performance indicators (KPIs) and controlled via a bonus-malus system. The billing of the service takes place monthly and is made up of fixed "base services", customisable "base packages" and variable costs for the support cases. The scope and the manifestation of the quality standards and billing modalities can be regulated individually per demand location. The information contained in the submission represents the maximum ("strictest") manifestation.
