sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.description: The Public Affairs Section (PAS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia, highlight shared values, and promote bilateral cooperation in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Please see Section C. Program Description for more information. This Annual Program Statement (APS) outlines our funding priorities and the strategic themes we will focus on in FY2025, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Based on availability of funding, PAS Tunis will award grants, fixed amount awards, or cooperative agreements between a minimum of $10,000 and up to a maximum of $200,000 (U.S. dollars) each for projects that advance the priorities outlined in this APS. Please carefully follow all instructions in the full announcement. Proposals that fail to conform to the requirements outlined in this APS will not be considered. All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. PAS Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen cultural, educational, professional, scientific, and business ties between the United States and Tunisia through programming that highlights shared values, strengthens people-to-people ties and institutional linkages, and promotes bilateral cooperation, and makes America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Competitive proposals must focus on at least one grant priority area outlined below. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: · Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. · Programs that strengthen relationships and linkages between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and cultural institutions. · Educational, artistic, and cultural programs, including programs that strengthen English language teaching and learning, music, musical theater, dance workshops, master classes, and performances, live theatre performances, art exhibitions, and sports and culinary diplomacy initiatives that increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and Tunisia. · Programs, including podcasts, that promote economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or that share U.S. experiences related to addressing community challenges, including the management of water or energy resources, waste management, urban design and planning, and preparing for and mitigating natural or human-caused disasters. · Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programming, including through the use new and immersive technologies, such as VR technology. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must address at least one of the six priority areas outlined below: · Economic Prosperity and Entrepreneurship: Initiatives that prioritize mutual prosperity, expand economic and commercial links between the United States and Tunisia, promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices, and that share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of increasing economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. · INNOVATION and Collaboration in science and technology: Initiatives that promote collaboration and academic partnerships in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) between U.S. and Tunisian academic and research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and private companies, as well as programs that promote interest in STEM education among young people. · EDUCATIONAL LINKAGES AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE : Initiatives that expand collaboration and partnerships between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and research institutions through programs and professional and academic exchanges; programs to strengthen English language instruction in Tunisian universities and colleges; programs to expand the teaching of English in sign language and braille; and other programs that support and promote English language learning among Tunisian youth. · LEADERSHIP: Initiatives that provide leadership training inspired by U.S. experiences, models, and best practices to Tunisian young people (high school and university students and young professionals) to help them become effective leaders in their communities and professional field of choice. Such training may include English language, public speaking and interpersonal communication, emotional intelligence, critical thinking and problem solving, financial literacy, goal-setting, and mental health management strategies. · MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Programs that leverage the “Mega-Decade in Sports” in North America (2023-2034) when the United States will host the 2025 FIFA World Club Cup, the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles, and the 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values and demonstrate American excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. · Celebrating American Excellence AND U.S.-Tunisian Enduring Partnership: Programs that 1) celebrate U.S. scientific or sport prowess, innovation, economic dynamism, agricultural strength, and national parks and tourism during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence; 2) leverage people-to-people ties and promote the establishment of U.S-Tunisian institutional linkages through cultural diplomacy, including artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities that celebrate American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, cultural heritage protection, and film during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence and the 228th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia; AND/OR 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase awareness and understanding among broad elements of Tunisian society of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation.
sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.title: Annual Program Statement (APS) for Fiscal Year 2025

sig_bfc4d3297b4bbb37bd17.description: UK Biobank ("UKB") has extended its contract with DNAnexus for the ongoing management and support of its the Research Analysis Platform (as described in section II.2.4) for a period of two years to allow UKB to conduct i) a procurement exercise in relation to the development of an Output Checking System, ii) preliminary market engagement and a procurement exercise for the provision of cloud infrastructure services to securely store and handle the UKB data once a new cloud-based Research Analysis Platform is established and iii) preliminary market engagement and a procurement exercise for the development of that new Research Analysis Platform. The extension of the Research Analysis Platform contract was not the subject of a competitive procurement pursuant to the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 as amended or otherwise for the reasons set out in the voluntary ex ante transparency notice (reference 2026/S 000-000312) published on 5th January 2026 and in this notice. Lot 1: . UKB currently hosts a cloud-based Research Analysis Platform which makes UKB data accessible to registered researchers within designated areas of the Research Analysis Platform, such that they can conduct their approved research project. The current Research Analysis Platform was procured by UKB in 2020. It was developed by DNAnexus, in collaboration with, and cloud infrastructure provided by, Amazon Web Services. At the end of Q2 2024 UKB adopted a Research Analysis Platform by default approach (with very limited exemptions), such that all UKB researchers were obliged to conduct their research on the Research Analysis Platform. The rationale behind this change is that the health record linkage data - both secondary and in due course primary - is now only permissible through a cloud-based environment (within the EEA). This significantly raised the level of adoption and usage of the Research Analysis Platform and required substantive improvements in functionality and scale to the Research Analysis Platform. As a consequence, the volume of researchers accessing the Research Analysis Platform has increased very significantly since it was first launched by UKB, with the number of researchers accessing data via the platform increasing from less than 50 in February 2021 to circa 16,500 in 2025. UKB has extended its contract with DNAnexus for the ongoing management and support of the Research Analysis Platform for a period of two years to allow UKB to progress discrete but linked competitive procurement exercises in relation to the implementation of a secure data environment strategy which encompasses: (i) the development of an Output Checking System (OCS) to improve the functionality and security of the UKB data and to facilitate the necessary certification by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and National Health Service (NHS) for the purposes of facilitating access to linked health record data and in particular the provision of the future primary care data; (ii) the provision of cloud infrastructure for the storage and handling of growing volumes of UKB data and support proposed enhancements to the new Research Analysis Platform (see below); and (iii) the development of a new Research Analysis Platform to provide a stable platform for research activities taking account of technology advancements over the past 5/6 years and incorporate new datasets to be accessed by researchers and make improvements to meta data storage and researcher tools. On 23 April 2025, UKB issued Preliminary Market Engagement Notices in respect of the proposed procurements for the Output Checking System, cloud infrastructure and the new Research Analysis Platform. These Preliminary Market Engagement Notices were updated on 10 December 2025. These noted the inter-related nature of the three procurements and the intention to carry out the procurements for the Output Checking System and cloud infrastructure in advance of (and in order to inform) the procurement for the development of the new cloud infrastructure and Research Analysis Platform. As such, UKB intends to conduct the procurement of the Output Checking System first, in the first half of 2026, followed (in the second half of 2026 or early 2027) by the procurement of cloud infrastructure services that will apply once the new Research Analysis Platform is in operation and finally the conduct of the procurement for the new Research Analysis Platform in 2027. UKB intends to undertake preliminary market engagement in relation to the cloud infrastructure (to understand how storage capacity and compute optimisation can enhance the functionality and security of UKB's data) and in relation to the new Research Analysis Platform (to understand the needs of its researchers and the solutions which may be available on the market) before launch of the respective procurement exercises. This strategy and sequencing of the procurement exercises will facilitate a smooth transition - for UKB's many thousands of researchers - to an enhanced secure environment for the access and use of the critical UKB data and research projects. The need for the Output Checking System was only made explicit in 2024 when the DHSC and NHS communicated the need for UKB to have certification in order to continue to receive and make available linked health record data and to be able to incorporate primary care data into UKB datasets. It is necessary and appropriate for the procurement exercises for both the Output Checking System and for the cloud infrastructure which will host the data once the new platform is established to be completed before preliminary market engagement can take place with suppliers and users regarding the requirements and strategic approach to the new Research Analysis Platform. The Output Checking System and cloud infrastructure procurement exercises need to be completed before the competitive procurement exercise for the development of the new platform, on the basis that the outputs and associated infrastructure will inform the technology solution for the new platform. The Output Checking System will be delivered first to meet both UKB and government need to increase the security of data and subsequently allow for new datasets to be accessed securely by researchers. The delivery of the OCS will also allow UKB to further develop data storage and usage requirements that will inform the cloud infrastructure procurement as well as the future Research Analysis Platform. In light of the above, to facilitate the procurement of the new platform and ensure an orderly transition to that new platform, an extension to the contract with DNAnexus was required. There is no practical prospect of another contractor operating the current Research Analysis Platform due to the proprietary DNAnexus intellectual property rights in the platform software and UKB's licence to such rights only being available during the life of the DNAnexus contract. UKB considered that the extension to the contract was permitted without a new procurement procedure in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCR) as amended, on the basis that the extension was not substantial within the meaning of regulation 72(1)(e) and (8) of the PCR. UKB considered that the extension: - did not render the contract materially different in character; - would not have impacted the suppliers interested in, or the outcome of, the previous procurement of the current managed Research Analysis Platform; - did not change the economic balance of the contract in favour of DNAnexus; and - did not extend the scope of the contract (which is for services of a kind already provided for in the contract) considerably, albeit that the number of researchers accessing UKB data via the current platform is significantly greater than envisaged in 2020. It is appropriate for the various procurement exercises to be undertaken in sequence. UKB needs to develop a secure approach to researchers being able to securely egress data from the current Research Analysis Platform. The Output Checking System procurement therefore needs to be completed as a priority, in order to secure the approval of the DHSC and NHS to researchers accessing linked health record data and, in the future, primary care data. The procurement for cloud infrastructure should be completed before the initiation of the procurement of the new Research Analysis Platform, as the technology of the Output Checking System and selected cloud solution, as well as data storage and compute requirements, will impact the technology underlying the new platform which will be hosted and accessed via the cloud. In any event, even if the extension to the contract with DNAnexus were not permitted within Regulation 72 of the PCR, for the reasons set out above UKB considered that the award of a further contract to support and manage the current Research Analysis Platform without prior publication of a tender notice would have been permitted under section 41 and paragraphs 5 and/or 6 and/or 7 of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023. In particular:- (i) only DNAnexus can provide the services on the current platform until the completion of a new competitive procurement exercise for the provision of a new platform because DNAnexus and its licensors retain the proprietary intellectual property rights in the platform software and UKB's licence to such rights come to an end when the contract with DNAnexus ends, such that there is no reasonable alternatives to DNAnexus continuing to provide those services; and/or (ii) the extension concerns the supply of the same services by DNAnexus and a change to another contractor - bearing in mind there are many thousands of registered researchers with over 4000 active research projects - would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance of the current platform. Additional information: Section V indicates that a contract has been awarded. However, for the avoidance of doubt, this notice (and the estimated value of £6.2m comprising £4.8m for an extension to the existing services and £1.4m for related system development) relates to an extension of the existing contract. The date at Section V.2.1) is the date that UKB extended the contract with DNAnexus.

sig_bffb8616956ad0a0e374.description: The subject of this public contract is to ensure the cooperation of the provider (spa facility) within the framework of a clinical study in patients with prescribed complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care (hereinafter referred to as "KLP") who simultaneously have been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus type 2 falling into the indication group IV/1. This diagnosis can be stated as the main indication for the stay, or as a secondary diagnosis (comorbidity). Patients admitted to spa treatment primarily for another indication, but with an associated disease of diabetes mellitus type 2, can thus also be included in the clinical study. The aim of the conducted clinical study is the objectification of the effect of complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care ("KLP") on diseases and chronic complications of diabetes mellitus type 2 ("DMT2"), prevention and progression of hepatic steatosis in Karlovy Vary. For the purposes of this tender documentation, a spa facility is understood to be a registered provider of complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care covered by public health insurance in the territory of Karlovy Vary, who has a valid permit for the use of natural healing resources and at the same time holds the consent of the Ministry of Health to provide spa treatment and rehabilitation care. This is a spa facility providing complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care according to the above requirements and according to the selected indication criteria of the clinical study "Objectification of the effect of complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care on diseases and chronic complications of diabetes mellitus type 2, prevention and progression of liver steatosis". The transfer of pseudonymised data will take place according to a mutually agreed schedule of the Institute of Spa Management and Balneology, v. v. i. (hereinafter referred to as "ILaB"), at set intervals, every two months. All data will be structured, provided only with the "ID codes" of individual patients. The ID codes must be handed over to the selected laboratory facility, which will be responsible for carrying out laboratory diagnostics for all collections. The spa facility is responsible for the correct use of the patient ID codes and it is its responsibility that no confusion occurs. Only patients admitted for a stay in the form of complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care (KLP), which corresponds to the contractual relationship between the provider and the health insurance company, will be included in the clinical study. The subject of this public contract is not the drawing up of the "clinical study" itself, but the provision of related activities including the collection of data and patient information, without their evaluation, and the handover of this data and information to the contracting authority for the purpose of their further processing. The collected data will be handed over at set intervals (every two months) to ILaB, which will process the resulting clinical study on their basis. Furthermore, the provider must ensure: • a sufficient number of patients meeting the criteria for inclusion (see Annex No. 3 of the Tender Documentation), • obtaining their informed consent, • patient education, • performance of diagnostic procedures, examinations and questionnaire surveys (for details see Annex No. 3 of the Tender Documentation), • cooperation with the laboratory within the framework of sample transfer, • creation and handover of the pseudonymised research set to ILaB. A detailed description of the subject of performance of this public contract is contained in Annex No. 3 of this tender documentation.
sig_bffb8616956ad0a0e374.title: Objectification of the effect of complex spa treatment and rehabilitation care on diseases and chronic complications of diabetes mellitus type 2, prevention and progression of liver steatosis - repeated announcement

sig_bfff285a2ec26050a28d.description: Stuttgarter Straßenbahnen AG (SSB) is conducting a non-binding market sounding for the digitalisation of ordering, administrative and logistics processes for service and work clothing. The aim is to gain market knowledge of available shop and platform solutions, possible operating models, interfaces and integration options of clothing manufacturers and suppliers. The market sounding serves exclusively to prepare possible future procurement procedures. It does not constitute a call for competition, a call for tenders or an invitation to submit a tender. No claims to a later award of contract can be derived from participation. Interested companies are requested to communicate their interest in participating in the market sounding by 14.08.2026, 11:00 hours at the latest, by e-mail to einkauf@ssb-ag.de. Further information and documents regarding the market sounding will be made available thereafter. Stuttgarter Straßenbahnen AG (SSB) is conducting a non-binding market sounding for the digitalisation of procurement and administrative processes for service and work clothing. The aim is to obtain information on solutions, functionalities, operating models and interfaces available on the market. SSB currently supports around 3.000 employees and would like to create a digital ordering process in future that enables employees to independently order service and work clothing while simultaneously reducing the administrative workload of the clothing store. As part of the market sounding, the following is to be investigated in particular: which B2B shop and platform solutions are available on the market, which functionalities are offered for ordering, budget, stock and approval processes, what interfaces are available, in particular to SAP HCM/SuccessFactors and SAP S/4HANA, how suppliers and clothing manufacturers can be connected, whether several manufacturers can be integrated via a central platform, which operating models (e.g. cloud, on-premises or software-as-a-service) are offered, what requirements regarding data protection, information security and support are met. SSB is currently open to different solution approaches. The subject of the market sounding is both a manufacturer-independent shop solution with the connection of various clothing manufacturers and integrated overall solutions from clothing manufacturers including their own shop and ordering platform. Note: This market sounding serves exclusively to prepare possible future procurement procedures. It does not constitute a call for competition, a call for tenders or an invitation to submit a tender. No claims to a later award of contract can be derived from participation. The results of the market sounding serve to evaluate possible procurement strategies and to determine the scope of a subsequent procurement. Interested parties will gladly be considered in the event of a later price enquiry.

sig_c0125f9c3820a7af4bd6.description: Odense Kommune has concluded a framework agreement on a multimodal traffic model with COWI A/S. Odense Kommune has a multimodal traffic model prepared by COWI. The traffic model differs from traditional traffic models in VISUM as it consists of 3 parallel models. Odense Kommune's traffic model contains a car, bicycle and public transport model as well as a modal shift module, so that the model takes into account the modal shift potential towards green mobility types. COWI has a large organisation in Denmark within the traffic model field with extensive expertise in multimodal traffic models. COWI has just completed an update of the traffic model for Odense Kommune. In the update, both data, structure, algorithms and the user interface have been updated in relation to previous versions of the traffic model for Odense. This means that COWI is the only company that has in-depth knowledge of what the traffic model contains and how it works. COWI is therefore the only company that can change the calculation method and user interface, which will be necessary in order to use the model to a relevant extent, cf. also section 80, subsection 3 of the Danish Public Procurement Act. The subject of this procurement consists of: a) 350 hours of adaptive upgrading which will be used according to the needs and requirements of the contracting authority; b) lump-sum maintenance of the DAIS system (user support and maintenance for a duration of 12 months); c) delivery of IBM Filenet licences with one-year maintenance. Essential conditions and requirements in accordance with professional rules - The tenderer is required to adapt to the equipment, operating environment and software and infrastructure found at the time of signing the public procurement contract for the adaptive maintenance and upgrading of the DAIS system. - The user interface design must remain existing or, in the event of modification, approved by the contracting authority. - Connection to all existing systems of the contracting authority must be achieved via existing services. - For each upgrade, the tenderer is obliged to prepare a functional specification which must pass validation by the contracting authority, carry out data analysis in existing databases, code programs and, if necessary, new databases, prepare test scenarios for software validation which are approved by the contracting authority and form part of the project documentation upon completion of the project. - The tenderer is obliged to produce and deliver program documentation in accordance with the requirements stated in the attached technical specification. - The tenderer is obliged, if requested by the contracting authority, to ensure the presence of the tenderer's expert personnel at the contracting authority's location for up to 8 hours per month. - The tenderer is obliged to test the upgrade after development, draw up a testing scenario before testing and, after testing, hand over the testing documentation to the Contracting Authority - Upon performance of all contractual obligations, the contracting authority acquires, without time and spatial limitation, all copyright over the upgraded information system which is the subject of this public procurement (including documentation and application source code) except for moral rights of copyright, which are non-transferable. - The tenderer is obliged to write program code in accordance with good programming practice which includes, but is not limited to, clear and detailed commenting of the program code and code optimisation. - All communication between the tenderer and the contracting authority during the performance of the public procurement contract shall take place in the Croatian language and all documentation requested in this technical specification must be produced in the Croatian language and Latin script. The number of adaptive upgrade hours stated in point a) of the subject of procurement represents estimated (indicative) quantities. The actual quantity of adaptive upgrade hours shall be executed in accordance with the needs of the contracting authority.

sig_c06c9c25fd348c090399.description:
APIA is launching a procurement procedure for the award of a framework agreement for 36 months of "Preventive and corrective maintenance services (software and database maintenance and administration, maintenance and resolution of incidents that may arise) for the IPA-ONLINE application". The IPA Online application is an essential IT element within the system for collecting, digitising and verifying data submitted by farmers in payment campaigns run by APIA up to the year 2025. Although the application is no longer used for operational processes relating to current campaigns, it remains indispensable for consulting, analysing and exploiting the data history relating to periods prior to the year 2025. In this context, maintaining the functionality of the IPA Online application is necessary to comply with institutional obligations regarding access to historical data, carrying out administrative checks on past campaigns, providing information to APIA's internal structures, as well as ensuring the traceability and auditability of data managed in the system. Since the application remains operational and accessible to APIA staff, it is mandatory to ensure a minimum level of technical support for: • corrective maintenance, necessary for rectifying errors arising in the operation of application components, including GIS components and those involving access to historical data; • preventive maintenance, necessary for maintaining the technical stability of the application, preventing performance degradation, monitoring software services and avoiding incidents that could affect the integrity or accessibility of historical information; A framework agreement for services will be concluded for a period of 36 months, with a single economic operator. Based on the framework agreement, subsequent contracts will be awarded which will constitute the legal basis for payment, depending on the needs of the contracting authority. Subsequent contracts will be concluded in compliance with the unit rates for the category of services provided in the framework agreement and within the allocated budget funds. The unit rates provided in the framework agreement, updated where applicable, shall govern all subsequent contracts to be awarded during the course of the framework agreement. Under these conditions, the framework agreement shall be governed by specific unit rates for the category of services to be provided within this framework agreement, namely: monthly unit rates for the category of preventive and corrective maintenance services, rates which will form the basis for the award of all subsequent contracts to be concluded during the course of the framework agreement. If the contracting authority submits a request for the conclusion of a subsequent contract to the economic operator who signed the framework agreement and the operator replies that it does not have the capacity to resolve this requirement through its own fault, then it shall suffer the consequences provided for in the framework agreement for non-fulfilment of its obligations. Duration of the framework agreement: Duration in months: 36 months. The framework agreement will be concluded with a single economic operator. Estimated timetable for applying the framework agreement award procedure: It is estimated that the framework agreement will be applied during the period: 2026 –2029. • It is estimated that a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 subsequent contracts will be awarded, depending on APIA's needs, whenever this need arises. For preventive maintenance, monthly support shall be ensured across all working environments for the entire duration of the Framework Agreement. During the Framework Agreement, depending on the needs identified by the beneficiary, service provision subsequent contracts for preventive and corrective maintenance will be concluded. Economic operators may request clarifications 18 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The contracting authority shall draw up and post in SICAP the response to all clarification requests submitted within the above deadline, on the 11 day before the deadline for submitting tenders. The estimated maximum and minimum quantities of services expected to be carried out during the duration of the framework agreement, respectively during the duration of a subsequent contract, in accordance with the requirements of the specifications are: • The estimated maximum quantity of services to be procured over the entire duration of the framework agreement can be found in the table below • The estimated minimum quantity of services to be procured over the entire duration of the framework agreement can be found in the table below Minimum quantity Framework agreement, months Maximum quantity Framework agreement, months Preventive and corrective maintenance 1 36 • The maximum quantity of services expected to be procured during the duration of the largest subsequent contract to be awarded during the duration of the framework agreement can be found in the table below, • The minimum quantity of services expected to be procured during the duration of a subsequent contract to be awarded during the duration of the framework agreement can be found in the table below, No. of months Maximum quantities No. of months Maximum quantities, no. of months Smallest subsequent contract Largest subsequent contract Preventive and corrective maintenance 1 1 12 Estimated maximum and minimum values of the framework agreement and of a subsequent contract: The estimated maximum value of the framework agreement for preventive and corrective maintenance services is 736.560 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the maximum quantities of services of this type to be procured for a period of 36 months, in accordance with the details above. The estimated minimum value of the framework agreement for corrective maintenance services of the framework agreement is 20.460 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the minimum quantities of services of this type to be procured for a period of 1 month, in accordance with the details above.

The estimated maximum value of the largest subsequent contract for preventive and corrective maintenance services is 245.520 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the maximum quantities of services to be procured over the duration of the largest subsequent contract, for a period of 12 months, in accordance with the details above. The estimated minimum value of a subsequent contract for preventive and corrective maintenance services is 20.460 lei excluding VAT and corresponds to the minimum quantities of services to be procured over the duration of a subsequent contract, for a period of 1 month, in accordance with the details above. - Note: The contracting authority is not obliged to perform services for the entire estimated value of the framework agreement.

sig_c07527328d69dfb2bba0.description: In the field of road safety, the Safe System approach, recognised internationally and included in the European Union Road Safety Policy 2021 2030 and the European Commission's strategic action plan on road safety, suggests acquiring greater knowledge about the different variables that influence road accidents, beyond standard indicators, such as the number of accidents, fatalities and seriously injured persons, recommending obtaining other indicators, called Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), directly related to the prevention of deaths and injuries in traffic accidents. Among these indicators are the use of seat belts and child restraint systems, the use of helmets, vehicles travelling within the speed limit, drivers driving within the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, distractions at the wheel and vehicle safety. These indicators constitute the subject-matter of this tendering procedure. The subject-matter of this lot is the design of a sampling plan for lots 2 and 3 and for the alcohol indicator and EDAP Study, obtaining the KPIs (except for KPI 6, whose calculation work falls within the scope of lot 4), and the preparation of the dashboard.

sig_c0c184bb112e6d033038.description: The system supports ATP’s business in relation to six overarching schemes that are administered: State Pension (Folkepension), Early Retirement Pension (Førtidspension) granted before and after 1 January 2003, Early Pension (Tidlig pension), Senior Pension (Seniorpension), Senior Premium (Seniorpræmie) as well as collection and disbursement of Flexible Pension (Fleksydelse). In connection with this, several benefits are administered, including Heating Supplement (Varmetillæg) granted before and after 1988, Elderly Check (Ældrecheck), and waiting supplement after deferred pension. A total of 20 benefits are administered. Furthermore, annual post-adjustments are made on the basis of incomes, and decisions are made regarding the basis for municipal grants of health cards. Pension is disbursed to pensioners abroad, and assistance is provided to obtain disbursements from abroad. Annually, approximately 100.000 applications and approximately 250.000 other enquiries are received, and approximately 7,5 million letters are sent, distributed among approximately 1,5 million recipients. The system uses, manually or automatically, a good 100 processes approximately 12 million times annually. The benefit area is regulated by pension legislation (the Social Pension Act, the Old Early Retirement Pension Act and associated executive orders, etc.), the flexible pension act and the senior premium act. In addition, benefits for foreign nationals and Danish nationals abroad are regulated by a number of conventions and regulations. The system was developed by Netcompany A/S, which currently provides operation, maintenance, support and further development, etc. ATP entered into the contract with Netcompany A/S in 2017, cf. notice of concluded contracts no. 3132432017. The professional system consists partly of the standard software Amplio (formerly Modulus Ydelse), which is supplied by Netcompany A/S, and partly of ATP-specific software. Both the Amplio software and the ATP-specific part of the application are developed in Java and use the Spring Framework. Amplio constitutes 25 % of the total number of lines of code. Maintenance and further development of Amplio are procured separately by ATP. ATP-specific legislation is supported by the ATP-specific code. The system runs on an Oracle/Linux platform and currently consists of local development environments (on the developers' PCs), as well as development environments, test environments, training/demo environments, pre-production environments and a production environment. For major further development tasks, additional test and pre-production environments are added during the development period. Approximately 50 integrations have been established for the production environment. Vastly most integrations, including to common public components such as the Benefit Index (Ydelsesindeks) and SKAT eIncome (Skat eIndkomst), are supported by Amplio. The system is under continuous further development and improvement, including in connection with legislative and practice changes, automation, efficiency enhancement and ongoing improvement of the customer experience

sig_c0f7471166943ec601b9.description: The term intends to enter into a contract for licences for the KI based tool Claude from the supplier Anthropic. Justification for the choice: The term needs an advanced, general KI-tool that can be used by employees across disciplines, including developers, designers and other roles. The aim is to support analysis, development and interaction assignments in line with Sikt's strategic targets for the use of artificial intelligence. After completed needs and market assessments, Visibility ́s assessment is that Claude currently appears to be the best suitable solution for the purpose, particularly in light of: *support for secure and final user-controlled access to data and integrations based on open standards, **good interaction between different user groups, including close collaboration between developers and other professional environments, technical prerequisites for integration with Sikt's existing platform services and architecture. Visibility has assessed alternative systems in the market, including, among other things, Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor, but they are not currently assessed to cover the need to a sufficient degree, especially in terms of the combination of access management, integration options and use across roles. The market for KI tools is developing quickly. The choice of Claude is therefore based on an assessment of available systems at the time of the procurement and is not intended to establish any type of long-term standardisation or supplier binding. Procurement form: The term has examined the possibility of acquiring Claude through the existing framework agreement for software licenses, but has been confirmed that the product cannot be delivered through it. Direct procurements from Anthropic are thus the only available procurement route. Extent and value of the procurement: The procurement concerns licences for Claude, with a staged and needs managed employee disclosure. The estimated total contract value is NOK 3,500,000. The actual cost will depend on the number of users and actual use over time. Options: No options.
sig_c0f7471166943ec601b9.title: Intention notice: Procurement of ki-tool Claude

sig_c1114644e365759a47be.description: The present notice is not intended to initiate a procurement procedure nor to prepare one. It serves solely for market consultation. The Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) is conducting a market consultation in preparation for a procurement in the area of BayernCloud Schule (hereinafter: ByCS), which provides digital applications and services for the Bavarian school community. The contracting authority is examining the future provision, further development, integration and operation of a digital board application for the ByCS. The existing application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software. The subject of the market consultation is the question of whether suitable market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing ByCS board or its code base, or to replace the existing ByCS board with another functionally and technically suitable board application. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain reliable information on solutions available on the market and fundamentally suitable for the described requirement. In particular, it is to be investigated whether an already available or adaptable board application can meet the functional, technical, data protection and operational requirements of the contracting authority and can be integrated, operated, maintained and further developed into the ByCS environment. Within the scope of the market consultation, insights are to be gained in particular as to whether and, if applicable, by whom the described services can be provided. Lot PAR-0001: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services. The existing digital ByCS board application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software for use in in-person and remote phases of teaching. The application was developed on behalf of the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs as a component of BayernCloud Schule and is continuously developed further. In doing so, the application is to fulfil the following criteria in particular: - Platform-independent (device types, operating system) - Browser-based - Responsive design - Offline app / PWA - GDPR-compliant design - Accessible according to WCAG - Collaboration - Very good writing feel / high quality of pen input with palm rejection - Suitable for primary schools -> Simplicity - Special school scripts integrable with individual menus - WOPI connection - Files can be saved offline - Sharing mechanism / permissions between teachers and pupils - Import/export of PDF files and images - Integration of websites and videos - Customisations to ByCS possible (design, repositories, CSP, ...) - Set square and compass - Import of GGS files (previous format) possible Within the scope of the market consultation, insights should be provided in particular on - the extent to which market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing board application; - whether other board applications suitable for school use are already available on the market; - whether such applications can meet the functional and technical requirements of the contracting authority; - whether and under what conditions an alternative application can be integrated into the ByCS environment; - what technical, operational and economic risks are associated with the different solution variants. Please contact markterkundung@abante.de by 20 September 2026, 23.59 hrs at the latest if you are interested in participating in the local market consultation. Your participation will not be remunerated. There is also no entitlement to participate in any procurement procedure that may subsequently follow. The decision as to whether a procurement procedure must be carried out is precisely what is to be brought about by the local market consultation. In your initial enquiry, please state as detailed as possible what qualifies you and what capacities you have to provide the envisaged services if the contracting authority decides on a procurement on the market. This is necessary in order to be able to assess the seriousness of the enquiry.
sig_c1114644e365759a47be.title: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services

sig_c131aae4482a201c8f3c.description: The Court Funds Office (CFO) provides a banking and investment service for the civil courts in England and Wales, including the Court of Protection. The CFO exists to discharge the legal responsibilities of the Accountant General (AG). It is the AG’s responsibility to safeguard funds in court. The Administration of Justice Act 1982 (Primary) and Court Funds Rules 2011 (Secondary Legislation) provide for CFO’s statutory requirements. The Office of the Accountant General (OAG), part of the MoJ, provides oversight over the services provided by the CFO. The CFO service, under the instructions of the Court, allows for deposits to be lodged, paid out and to interact with the Lord Chancellor’s equity Investment product (Tracker Fund) provided by Legal & General for court clients {mainly Children and Court of Protection Clients (CoP)}. CFO also provides operational and back-office services for all said activities. Given the specific rules and regulations, the current service provided includes bespoke and manual requirements not ordinarily provided by a banking service provider. This procurement aims to deliver a solution that enables the complete digital transformation of the CFO service, providing clients with secure, web-based access to account information and processing, while removing legacy barriers to efficiency. Lot 1: .
sig_c131aae4482a201c8f3c.title: Court Funds Office Service - Preliminary Market Engagement Series

sig_c132829e01dd34c84937.description: The subject of the overall project is the conceptual, technical and operational implementation of the "SH-Navi" project as an open, modular and, as far as possible, open-source-based mobility platform for the intermodal, multimodal and data-based linking of various mobility services. The goal of the overall project is the step-by-step development, integration and provision of a future-proof digital mobility solution that brings together different modes of transport, routing, data, information and, in the future, other supplementary mobility functions in a common system architecture. For the proper structuring of the overall project and for the clear separation of different service areas, the project is divided into two technically and functionally interconnected, but procurement-wise separate, lots: 1. Lot 1 - Development, adaptation, integration and technical further development of the application and system landscape - Lot 1 includes in particular the conceptual, technical and operational development, adaptation, integration, configuration, customising, development and expansion services in connection with the web application, optional additional modules (e.g. app), technical interfaces, routing, data and system logic as well as the implementation of the development services covered by the contract in the intended project model. 2. Lot 2 - Provision, operation, hosting, production-related infrastructure and operational management responsibility - Lot 2 includes in particular the production-related provision, operation, hosting, deployment, infrastructure, system environment, operational management as well as, where applicable, other operation-related services for the permanent operational use of the overall product. Both lots are in a functional overall context, but pursue different service objects, areas of responsibility and contractual priorities. The specific design of the interfaces, participation and handover obligations between the lots results from the respective procurement and contract documents. This procedure relates exclusively to Lot 2. Lot LOT-0001: Digitalagentur Smarte Grenzregion GmbH, KielRegion GmbH - SH-Navi - Lot 2 - DevOps and Operations. The present procurement documents, service descriptions, requirements and evaluation criteria relate exclusively to Lot 2 - Provision, operation as well as deployment and technical operational support services for the cloud and operating environment. The subject of Lot 2 is in particular: - the provision and operation of the cloud and operating environment covered by the contract, - the managed cloud services required for this, - the execution of deployment, release, monitoring and incident processes, - as well as the associated technical operational, support and operational support services. Conversely, services of Lot 1 are not the subject of these documents, in particular no original development, adaptation, further development or software-side error correction services for the software solution covered by the contract, unless expressly regulated otherwise in the documents or required across lots. Insofar as there are requirements for deployment, integration, handover, test, monitoring, incident or support processes within the scope of Lot 2, these serve exclusively the contractually compliant implementation of the operation, cloud and deployment services of Lot 2 and do not in themselves constitute an assumption of the original service objects of Lot 1. A maximum budget of 80.000 EUR (gross) is available for the services of this Lot 2. The budget specification does not refer to services that are invoiced according to expenditure. Tenders that exceed this budget are to be excluded from the procedure.
sig_c132829e01dd34c84937.title: Digitalagentur Smarte Grenzregion GmbH, KielRegion GmbH - SH-Navi - Lot 2 - DevOps and Operations

sig_c1471e7c1c89ae3900a9.description: The subject of the contract is the delivery and commissioning of workstations for the distribution of official time or time compliant with official time using the NTP or PTP protocol, along with a system for monitoring the correctness of their operation and collecting statistics of implemented services, which is necessary to: - create an official time distribution workstation using the NTP and PTP protocol in the backup official time maintenance centre at the Świętokrzyskie Laboratory Campus of the Central Office of Measures in Kielces (part 1), - create a system of distributed workstations for official time distribution using the NTP method, increasing the number of reliable time servers in the national pool of servers registered at ntppool.org and, by dispersing the location of workstations in various cities of Poland, increasing availability and enabling faster synchronisation to official time for local users (part 2), - create systems for the distribution of time compliant with official time using the NTP protocol in laboratories having independently operating atomic time and frequency standards compared continuously against UTC(PL) and ensuring the required accuracy against UTC(PL) (part 3), and to: - ensure continuity of monitoring the correctness of operation and collecting statistics of services implemented by NTP servers in the aforementioned official time distribution workstations using the NTP protocol in mini NTP server clusters (part 4), which is necessary to expand the number of possible locations, availability and synchronisation capabilities to official time or time compliant with official time using the NTP protocol, ensure availability of official time servers in the backup official time maintenance centre, increase the number and availability of reliable NTP servers in the national pool of servers registered at ntppool.org and enhance the security of using this pool of servers by domestic users, as well as to ensure proper supervision over the functioning of the aforementioned workstations and the collection of statistics of services implemented by them.

sig_c14ad9e9077087aecbda.description: The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to solicit UG3/UH3 phased, cooperative agreement research applications to evaluate, implement, and/or test population-based interventions to policies, programs, and/or practices for promoting integration of services, systems, and/or values by leveraging cross-sector partnerships in communities. Such interventions must address social and chronic disease common risk factors and/or barriers driving oral disease burden in communities. sig_c188f28e57e919e2ed80.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA), represented by the Royal Danish Embassy (RDE) in Accra, Ghana (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”), has entered into a fund management contract concerning Grant management for Y/WPS project under the Peace and Stabilization Programme for West Africa (PSP WA). The Consultant will serve as grants manager for “Call for Proposals for Youth & Women, Peace and Security” (Y/WPS) (hereinafter ‘the Y/WPS call for proposals’) under Pillar 1 in the period 2026-2028 under the overall guidance of the Client and full compliance with the MFAs Aid Management Guidelines and the Ministry’s Financial Management Guidelines. The Y/WPS project will entail management of grant funds totaling DKK 67 million (the total allocation of DKK 74 million also includes the management fee to the Consultant) for projects with an implementation timeline of 12-24 months implemented in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Mali, Niger and Nigeria across the following modalities: 1. Grass-roots grants (approximately DKK 500.000 – 1 million) expected up to 40 grants 2. INGO grants (approximately DKK 1 - 3 million) expected up to 10 grants 3. Regional initiatives (approximately DKK 3 – 5 million) up to 3 grants 4. Executive leadership programme on Y/WPS (approximately DKK 3 million) – 1 grantee. The purpose of having an external Consultant to serve as FUND Manager (Grants Management Unit) is to 1) Administratively manage the call for proposals process; 2) Facilitate the Steering Committees identification of grants receiving partners; 3) Contractually and administratively manage the grant allocation to and associated performance by identified partners; 4) Ensure quality controlled including MEAL of the grant receiving partners activities in line with PSP WA ToC and results framework; 5) Support grants receiving partners’ joint communication of results and advocacy messages in line with the PSP WA communication plan; 6) Organize annual partners conventions (with participation of grants receiving partners, RDE and other relevant stakeholders) in the years 2027 and 2028 respectively. The objective of the Agreement is to support the Client to deliver the ‘Call for Proposals for Youth & Women, Peace and Security-component of the Peace and Stabilization Programme for West Africa’ to contribute to stabilisation and peacebuilding in targeted border areas and geographies by strengthening capacities of youth and women via support to YPS and WPS-focused civil society projects. The role of the Consultant: • The Consultant will ensure independent grant administration; and proactive outreach and information dissemination to prospective grant recipients, including new and underrepresented actors. • The Consultant is expected to mitigate fiduciary risks, promote equitable partnerships, and ensure value for money through consolidated financial, monitoring, and grant support functions. • The Consultant will bring in sectoral expertise and transparent grant-making systems. • The Consultant will facilitate and strengthen capacity and learning across the portfolio via the annual partners’ convention events. • The Consultant facilitates the oversight of the Client of implementation of awarded grants and monitoring and reporting on results and outcomes. • The Consultant ensures and facilitates external communication of project results achieved, hereunder via formulation and implementation of a communication plan and production and dissemination of audio-visual products. • The Consultant facilitates the operations and decision-making processes by the SC (by organizing and ensuring necessary logistics for meetings and delivering timely and tailored information to support the decision-making processes). In performing the below tasks, the Consultant will deliver on the outcomes and associated detailed tasks outlined in section 5: • Manage the full grant cycles based on the project documents, including the application/call processes, with focus on efficient management, effectiveness, and accountability for funds and results. • Provide all administration of the funds including overall financial management and verification and approval of project workplans, budgets, and reports as well as disbursements to the actors which, depending on the case, is the sole grantee, or in case of partnerships, the appointed administrative partner. • Monitor achievement of results as defined in the Results Framework in the project documents, hereunder field based project monitoring and timely consolidated results reporting based on individual grantee reporting. • Provide outreach and communication to relevant actors, highlight positive lessons learned, and ensure sharing of relevant knowledge and information that generate interest and effective participation. • Provide relevant project and financial management support and guidance to actors/partners supported. • Provide overall quality assurance of projects supported. • Maintain full compliance with MFA AMG and FMG, ensuring high standards of financial management, procurement, anti-corruption, and risk mitigation. • Provide relevant information and data to the Client on concrete projects and overall status based on request and through half annual and yearly reporting and meetings.
sig_c188f28e57e919e2ed80.title: Grant management for Y/WPS project under the Peace and Stabilization Programme for West Africa (PSP WA)

sig_c18c574df88e52eea3b9.description: The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. The purpose of this third round of Preliminary Market Engagement is to share information relating to the Authority's vision for the LitUK service and the procurement approach. At this stage, no final decisions have been made regarding the preferred solution. Please Note: the content of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice may be subject to change. Lot 1: . None
sig_c18c574df88e52eea3b9.title: Preliminary Market Engagement Round 3 for the Life in the UK (LITUK) Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service

sig_c19ac454b9b9881ff913.description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-4-improving-efficiency-and-patient-experience-in-nhs-transport

sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.description: The Bars of Admission (RAKs) in Germany are corporations under public law and currently represent over 160.000 admitted lawyers. Their legal basis is formed by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). There are a total of 27 Bars of Admission in Germany. The 11 Bars of Admission issuing the tender here are actively involved in the project and contribute their professional, organisational and technical requirements to the design. The participating chambers exhibit varying organisational structures, member numbers and IT landscapes, which underlines the need for a flexible and scalable solution. However, the various Bars of Admission are essentially subject to the same legal requirements, which are primarily dictated by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). In total, the eleven participating chambers currently look after around 132.000 members, who are administered and supported by approximately 370 employees. To support their tasks, 22 chambers currently use a software solution from DATEV eG. This solution covers core administrative processes, particularly in the areas of personnel administration, billing and complaint or case management. DATEV eG has terminated the existing software solution effective 31.12.2027. This decision makes timely planning and procurement of a suitable successor solution necessary. Against this background, the eleven local Bars of Admission have joined forces with the objective of replacing the currently used software solution, procuring a suitable successor solution and successfully introducing it. The project group is led and coordinated by five Bars of Admission (Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Munich and Stuttgart). The aim is to procure a modern, high-performance and future-proof software solution that meets the specific requirements of the chambers and completely or with enhancements maps the previous functionalities of the DATEV software. In advance, a structured survey of the technical and functional requirements was conducted. This forms the basis for the drawn-up requirements catalogue. The DATEV software currently in use and to be replaced is utilised in the chambers for the following task areas: (1) Personnel administration: Administration of master data of natural and legal persons, admissions, status changes, specialist lawyer designations, training systems, resignations and reactivations. (2) Billing: Administration and billing of membership fees, charges, credit notes, etc. (3) Complaint management: Administration of professional law procedures, in particular complaints (4) Archiving and deletion: Archiving and deletion of data records from personnel and complaint management The software is deeply integrated into the work processes of users and forms a central basis for daily administrative work. Currently, the eleven participating Bars of Admission each operate independent instances of the DATEV software. While the basic functionalities are comparable in all chambers, differences exist in the specific configuration, particularly with regard to individually defined data fields, differing data structures and chamber-individual usage concepts. The project pursues the overarching objective of identifying a suitable successor solution for the discontinued DATEV software and procuring it within the framework of a structured, voluntary tender procedure.
sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.title: Procurement procedure for a Chamber of Lawyers administration system

sig_c1bd567ef6b192706741.description: SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is the municipality's outsourced financial and payroll administration services, including both service production and the necessary information systems. The selected service provider is responsible for the municipality's overall financial management, which includes bookkeeping, participation in the preparation of the financial statements and budget, statutory financial reporting including municipal data reporting, VAT reporting and tax returns, financial planning, purchase and sales ledgers, payment transactions, and entering memorandum vouchers into bookkeeping. Personnel and payroll administration services cover payroll calculation for the municipality's various collective agreement sectors (KVTES, OVTES, TS), maintenance of personnel data, service period calculation, reporting of absences and income to the incomes register and Kela, as well as the payment of travel and expense claims and trustee allowances. The municipality has approximately 250 employees whose payroll calculation must be handled monthly. The procurement package covers only the municipality's services, not, for example, the municipality's subsidiaries. The currently used systems are FPM for financial planning, Sarastia365 BI for financial reporting, Dooap for purchase invoices, Sarastia365 TalousApp for sales invoicing, and Sarastia365 MuistioApp for memorandum vouchers, as well as Populus 25.2.0 for personnel administration. The service provider must also have the capability for system integration, including sales invoicing from billing systems commonly used in various sectors, such as early childhood education, the water utility, and construction and permit supervision. In connection with the procurement, the possibility of replacing the current financial planning and HR systems with more appropriate solutions will be surveyed. The procurement may include options, such as the electronic archiving of permanently retained financial and personnel administration documents in the contracting authority's own archive, and HR system interface solutions with third-party systems, such as occupational healthcare or employee benefit services. CONTRACT PERIOD The contract period is five (5) years. The contracting authority has the right to extend the validity of the contract by an option period of two (2) years. SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT Based on previous outcomes, the annual value of the procurement has been approximately 280 000–330 000 euros (VAT 0 %). REGISTRATION FOR MARKET CONSULTATION Interested tenderers are requested to register for the market consultation by filling out the forms survey 20.4.2026 by 12.00 at https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/2wSrXSgP2e. Tenderers are requested to note that registration for the market consultation cannot be done via Tarjouspalvelu.

sig_c1be924ef93254fb39c8.description: Agency: Department of the Army Office: Army Contracting Command, Edgewood Contracting Division Fort Detrick Branch Location: Frederick, MD Solicitation Number: W911SR-22-S-NGIA Notice Type: Sources Sought Synopsis: This is a solicitation for parties interested in participating in projects sought by the United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), Program Manager Special Programs (PMSP) for state of the art technologies and capabilities for the Next Generation Identification and Awareness Initiative (NGIA). NGIA is established to meet requirements in the following focus areas: Focus Area 1: TAGGING, TRACKING AND LOCATING (TTL): Having knowledge of when, where and what the enemy is doing is crucial to mission planning and eventual success. USASOC is looking to fill technology gaps in special technical capabilities for Tagging, Tracking, and Locating of High Value Individuals and Targets (HVI&T). Tailored solutions should provide Over The Horizon (OTH) and Line of Sight (LOS) day and night target tracking capabilities for extended periods, in all terrain/weather conditions, using ground based, airborne, or satellite receive methods. Specific desired characteristics include LPI/LPD communications, non-traditional means of exfiltration, and ability to survive in austere, near/peer operational environments. Focus Area 2: RECONNAISSANCE & SURVEILLANCE (R&S): USASOC must provide operators with the ability to gain intelligence in areas that are not easily accessible due to terrain/weather restrictions, political sensitivities, and hostile forces. Special, unattended ground base sensors will provide, “orbits without orbits”, giving commanders situational awareness where traditional ISR systems are either non-existent or units are operating in unfamiliar environments where traditional collection may fail. Specific efforts that include OTH Audio/Video sensors, novel sensor modalities, and passive audio, machine vision object recognition sensors and can bypass adversarial countermeasures are highly desirable. Focus Area 3: UNMANNED SYSTEMS (UMS): Remotely controlled ground and aerial based systems have become a significant contested technology focus area for USASOC. Multiple solutions are required for the US military to win in the next fight. The solutions include the creation of denied/degraded GPS, anti-RF C2 link jamming capabilities that are manufactured by US companies using parts, and able to be integrated on group 1 and/or group 2 UAS. Additionally, we require the ability to manage and reduce the RF control link signature in order to protect the UAS from opposition EW exploitation. Autonomy is increasingly important and will allow operators to keep focus on mission tasks and decrease the amount of “eyes on screen” time required to operate remotely controlled drones, reducing troop to task requirements. With the increased proliferation of commercial and enemy drone platforms, the ability to deny, control, exploit and counter those platforms is required to survive in the current and future operating environment. Focus Area #4: Integrated Information and Electromagnetic Operations (I2EO): The Integrated Information and Electromagnetic Operations (I2EO) focus area for USASOC is centered on the development and integration of advanced capabilities in Cyber, Electronic Warfare (EW), Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Space Operations, and Communications. I2EO aims to provide USASOC with the ability to operate in a contested and dynamic environment, leveraging the electromagnetic spectrum to gain a decisive advantage over adversaries. The I2EO focus area combines the capabilities of cyber, EW, SIGINT, space operations, and communications to enable USASOC to disrupt, degrade, and destroy enemy command and control systems, while also protecting friendly forces from similar threats and maintaining secure and reliable communications in support of special operations missions. This is achieved through the development and fielding of advanced technologies, such as cyber tools, EW systems, SIGINT sensors, space-based assets, and tactical communication networks, which are integrated into a unified framework to provide real-time situational awareness, precision targeting, and effects-based operations. I2EO also emphasizes the importance of advanced analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to support the planning, execution, and assessment of special operations missions, ensuring that USASOC can operate at the speed and scale required to succeed in today's complex and rapidly evolving operational environment. I2EO will enhance the effectiveness of USASOC, improve the security of SOF, and maintain a strategic advantage over adversaries in the electromagnetic spectrum, while also ensuring seamless and secure communication between USASOC elements, coalition partners, and other stakeholders. The NGIA's purpose is to form a sphere of technological excellence made up of participants from industry, non-profit organizations, and not-for-profit entities able to rapidly and efficiently propose and carry out, the development of prototype solutions that sustain and expand strategic superiority within broadly stated special operations focus areas of interest. It is intended that participants will perform a strategically important role in developing systems focused on the development, demonstration and transition of resilient and dynamic technological capabilities critically necessary for the Nation's special operation forces. Prototype projects awarded as a result of this announcement may result in follow-on production Other Transaction Agreements or Contracts in the quantities specified within any particular project announcement released within the NGIA competitive environment. Other Transaction Authority in accordance with 10 USC 4022 (formerly 10 USC 2371b) will be used in support of NGIA. The resultant award of any OT agreement will NOT be made or issued under the provisions of the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 (P.L. 98-369), FAR Part 6 or any other FAR based regulation. The NGIA will be carried out under the terms of a Participant Basic Agreement (PBA). The PBA is available for qualified entities interested in participating in the NGIA. Entities wishing to participate shall submit an email to the Primary Point of Contact identified below demonstrating technical relevancy/recency in the desired "Focus Areas of Interest." Material that is only advertisement or marketing material in nature is not desired. The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Edgewood Contracting Division is supporting USSOCOM in the execution of NGIA. Primary Point of Contact: Elizabeth Nordell Email Address: elizabeth.m.nordell.civ@army.mil Please send technical and administrative questions and inquiries to the Primary Point of Contact to facilitate communication on all matters relating to this Announcement. The Government is prohibited from soliciting and awarding actions to contractors that have engaged or are suspected to have engaged in criminal, fraudulent, or seriously improper conduct. Prospective vendors shall complete electronic annual representations and certifications at SAM. By submission of an offer, the Offeror acknowledges the requirement that prospective awardees MUST be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to submitting an invoice and through final payment of any agreement resulting from NGIA. Vendors that are not registered should consider applying for registration immediately. To remain registered in the SAM database after the initial registration, the Vendors is required to review and update on an annual basis from the date of initial registration (or subsequent updates) its information in the SAM database to ensure it is current, accurate and complete. This notification is for planning purposes only. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for the information solicited.
