sig_c2fd482315cec4293609.description: This is a request for information of a system that includes tools for both curriculum and schedule planning work in a university context. With this RFI Aalto University is seeking information on suppliers interested in delivering the services described. Aalto University is a foundation university as provided in the Universities Act (558/2009) and started operations at the beginning of 2010. Aalto has six schools and approximately 20 000 students, 4800 staff of which over 400 are professors. Aalto’s curriculum planning process involves our 3,100 academic staff members including 120 programme directors, supported by 100 curriculum planners in the learning services. The work covers over 80 degree programmes, 700 study modules and 3500 study units. Curriculum data is updated based on the length of the curriculum period, which is currently two academic years. Aalto’s scheduling process involves the aforementioned 3,100 academic staff members, 66 timetable planners, and 3 room booking system admins. The planning encompasses classes for 16 184 students in 250 spaces. With the forthcoming procurement and contract our goal is to establish a long-term partnership with a supplier who can cater to our evolving curriculum and schedule planning needs in alignment with our strategy in an agile manner. REQUIREMENT FOR THE SYSTEM CONTAINING CURRICULUM AND SCHEDULE PLANNING TOOLS Aalto University needs a system primarily for schedule planners, curriculum planners, and teachers to efficiently draft and publish curricula and timetables collaboratively. The desired system should also provide comprehensive analytics and reporting tools to support management with strategic activities on all levels of the university, such as programme directors and department heads for degree programme -level planning, deans for school-level planning, and various members of steering groups for Aalto-level planning. The system should provide advanced contemporary solutions for curriculum mapping and automatic scheduling. The system should be a finished product that has been in active use for several years in the higher education sector. Please see attached Appendix 1 for providing a general description about the procurement and our aims towards the procured service. TERMS OF THIS RFI Contracting authority may use the information it receives during the RFI process for the planning and preparation of the actual invitation to tender. Note! This is NOT a prior information notice, a procurement notice, a contract notice nor an invitation to tender. This notification and/or answering to it do not create any obligations for the contracting authority or for those who choose to answer it. The contracting authority does not pay any compensation for taking answers to this RFI. The information provided by the contracting authority is preliminary at this point and it is subject to change. Taking or not taking part in the RFI does not change the standing or status of a supplier in the procurement process. INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS RFI With this RFI Aalto is requesting system suppliers to announce their interest in participating in a market dialogue. We request you to inform us about your interest to participate in this RFI by 28 April 2026 at 2 pm CET / 3 pm EEST via email to anna-liisa.auramo@aalto.fi, riikka.rissanen@aalto.fi and heli.jarvela@aalto.fi (please use all names as recipients). Mark "Request for information: Curriculum and Schedule planning system" as the subject of the message. Please send the following information in your response: • Appendix 1. General presentation of your company and the system you could provide • Appendix 2. Q&A template filled in with your responses - Supplier information - Answers to the “Questions from Aalto” - Comments on how you could provide solutions to our user stories - References - Investment planning - Questions from the Supplier, if you wish to pose any NOTE! In case your answers contain trade secrets or other classified information, please mark the sensitive information clearly into the materials provided. NEXT STEPS Upon receiving answers, Aalto University may contact the interested participants. Aalto University reserves the right to invite suppliers for further discussions regarding this RFI to obtain information to the necessary extent on market and suppliers providing relevant services, give out information regarding the needs of Aalto University and to clarify any issues related to the object of the procurement. Discussions may also be held with suppliers other than those who responded to the request for information. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION APPENDICES Appendix 1. Object of procurement Appendix 2. Q&A template
sig_c2fd482315cec4293609.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION – Software solution containing tools for curriculum planning and schedule planning for Aalto University

sig_c2feb53d681d6332cbb5.description: Hampshire County Council (HCC) is seeking to replace its existing Place, Connectivity & Infrastructure Professional Services Framework (ET14110) by establishing a new four-year multi-supplier Framework for the provision of specialist technical transportation and civil engineering professional services, together with infrastructure development and support services. The Framework aims to provide HCC with continued engineering infrastructure and development consultancy services and allows for provision for specialist technical transportation and engineering services. The Framework includes but is not limited to the following technical professional services: Lot A - Multi-Disciplinary Services • Sustainable and accessible transport infrastructure planning services • Highways, Transportation, Civil and Structural engineering design services • Design and advice services under Section 278 and 38 of the Highways Act (1980) • Construction estimating, commercial and financial management services • Safety audit, engineering and management • Waste infrastructure and development design services • Flood and water management and drainage design services • Ecological and environmental services • Landscape architecture and design services • Sustainable and community integration strategic planning • Infrastructure technology strategy and design services • Intelligent traffic systems design and advice services • Building Information Modelling (BIM) services B1 - Engineering Design Specialisms • Bridge and Structural inspections including masonry, reinforced concrete, post tensioned and steel structures • Infrastructure design services covering developments, minor and specialist street and transportation design services • Inclusive and Public Realm Design, including transport design services • 3D and BIM modelling and Visualisations and animations (for engagement purposes) • Flood and water management services including hydraulic modelling • LLFAs support and design services • Highways drainage design services including SuDs • Development drainage assessment services and design checking services • Design of small scale waste water treatment plants B2 - Transport Planning Specialisms • Active Travel and healthy streets, including walking and cycling design specialisms, Pedestrian wayfinding signage strategies and Urban area cycle network strategies • Accessible infrastructure and planning services including inclusive design, low traffic neighbourhoods and school streets • Future mobility planning services (including local mobility hubs, e-mobility solutions, electric vehicle charging etc.) and Low carbon approaches • Travel Data and Modelling including Walking and cycling data, Travel and journey modelling, Car parking data, Intelligent traffic data (including queue surveys), TAG Compliant traffic modelling and Real time journey information visualisations, business engagement • Planning including school travel planning, local travel plans and support • Business case development and Scheme economic appraisal including Cost Benefit Analysis services, Sustainability appraisals • Bid application preparations including DfT Full Business Case services, Specialist business case and funding bid support • Master planning services including Land use / spatial planning services • Associated general research services B3 - Strategic Planning Specialism • Planning application support services • Planning appeals support services • Town & Country planning Act support services • Strategic & spatial planning services • Developer and stakeholder engagement services B4 - Environmental, Sustainability and Decarbonisation Specialisms • Air quality zone modelling & assessment • Air quality, health and environmental research services (in the context of transport) • Modelling and advice services • Action plan support services (in the context of transport) • Vehicle emission modelling / simulation services • Sustainable travel and transport consultancy services & decarbonisation, including Carbon offsetting advice • Health impact surveys and assessments including noise monitoring • Waste management planning • Environmental audits and Socio-economic appraisals • Environmental survey, inspection and supervision services including Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) B5 - Ecological, Landscape & Arboriculture Specialisms • Landscape design & management services • Arboriculture planting & management advice • Arboriculture surveys & assessments including TPO & felling advice • Arboriculture and landscape survey, inspection and supervision services • Ecological & habitat assessments and surveys • Ecological appraisals and Ecological Impact Assessments • Protected species surveys & assessment, for animals including but not limited to otters, bats, dormice, etc., or for birds • Ecological survey, inspection and supervision services B6 - Advice and Community Engagement for Active Travel Specialism • Community engagement services for sustainable travel, such as surveys, school streets, community events • Applying behavioural change science for sustainable travel solutions • School engagement services for active travel including cycling and walking B7 - Traffic Management, Traffic Order and Parking Consultancy • Traffic Orders - drafting, consolidation, TRO reviews, variations and amendments • Digital TRO mapping – Interface with Traffic Order management software • Signs and lining reviews – including Parking, Speed Limits, Movement Restrictions • Parking reviews including On-road and Off-road parking and resident parking schemes • Moving Traffic Enforcement – development and delivery of schemes. • Low cost Traffic Management measures B8 - Street Lighting Design Specialism • Scoping/feasibility of street lighting projects • Preliminary and detailed design of lighting schemes, including drawings and schedules, to British and EU standards • Lighting designs to meet planning consent/conditions, including minimising impact on local ecology • S278 and S38 street lighting designs with accompanying PFI Certificate of Approval • Support PFI Street Lighting accrual process The new Framework will be divided into nine separate lots. Lot A will deliver larger scale multi-disciplinary consultancy services and Lot B will be sub dividend into eight smaller-scale specialist consultancy services. The Framework will be available to all Public Bodies within the geographical area of England (e.g. Local Authorities, NHS, Fire, Police, schools etc.), but predominantly those within the South East and South West regions. These public bodies shall be named as ‘Participating Authorities’ for the purposes of this Framework but Hampshire County Council shall remain the named lead ‘Contracting Authority’ for the purposes of this procurement and will retain overall control and ownership of the Framework. This Framework will be an NEC4 Framework Contract, with call-offs through the Framework using the NEC4 Professional Service Contract (PSC) and Professional Service Short Contract (PSSC). Lot 7: .

sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.description: The contracting authorities are conducting a competitive dialogue for the development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter as well as for the administrations of the three contracting authorities in accordance with the provisions of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The tender aims to develop a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter and the three contracting authorities, which is to be used to execute or perform, among other things, both the services of the Bergisches ServiceCenter and the services of the administrations of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal at the level of information provision to the public and interaction regarding the administrative services of the three cities. In the future, the chatbot is to be further developed in line with the current state of the art, particularly at the interaction and transaction level as well as for internal administrative support. The contracting authorities shall be entitled, both jointly for the Bergisches Servicecenter and individually, to call off services from the contractor regarding the developed chatbot (cf. draft contract, Annex C to the 2. Letter of Procedure). The subject of the contract is the development of a chatbot system to fulfil service tasks or services of the Bergisches Servicecenter at the level of information provision to the population of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal. Regarding the functional scope of the chatbot, the solution concepts must take into account the future further development of the interaction and transaction level as well as the possibility of internal administrative support. Furthermore, the subject of the contract also includes the maintenance, further development and adaptation of the chatbot system. On the one hand, the chatbot system should be able to implement, within the framework of providing information to citizens, companies and other information seekers, in particular direct information on available services, forwarding to corresponding services and information, and prospectively, at the interaction and transaction level, among other things, advice on services. On the other hand, with regard to internal administration, the chatbot system is prospectively intended to support, among other things, text management, research assistants and an internal service bot. The chatbot is to be implemented in particular as a multilingual, AI-supported large language model, with transparent, consistent and friendly or citizen-oriented language, with constant citation of sources, and in compliance with data protection and IT security law.
sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.title: Development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter

sig_c36adab60f849b6a0d90.description: According to primary request no. 23313 EX 2025 24.06.2026 (ADAM: 26REQ019331309) of the competent service (of the Directorate for the Support of the Operation of Public Administration Systems), the Ministry of Digital Governance developed and operates the Central Electronic Document Interchange System (CEDIS) through which documents are interchanged between public sector bodies, as defined in article 18 of law 4727/2020 (A ́184), and specified by ministerial decision no. 21145 EX 2022 (B ́2764) with the subject "Operation of the Central Electronic Document Interchange System (CEDIS)". The CEDIS was implemented within the framework of the project "Implementation of a Central Document Flow, Routing and Interoperability System with remote signatures as well as its Support Mechanism" under contract no. 2/2019 (ADAM: 19SYMV004990460), as amended. The CEDIS includes: • the central hub for the interconnection of the Electronic Document Interchange (EDI) systems of Public Bodies, • a single-step protocol and workflow service addressed to bodies that do not possess a local Electronic Document Interchange System (EDI-B service), • the application for the provision of approved digital certificates to public officials, • remote digital document signature applications in Greek and English versions, • a service for the generation of a unique QR Code / Unique Identifier and a Validity Check Service, • a specific subsystem to cover Government needs for signing documents with digital signatures, • a mechanism for automating the process of onboarding new bodies into the system, • a subsystem for the exchange of documents with foreign bodies via the CEDIS • a support portal, • a support request management application Today, 308 public bodies are interconnected with the CEDIS, of which 153 bodies have a local EDI and 155 use the EDI-B service. During the operation of the CEDIS, approved digital certificates with remote digital signature were provided to public officials: • 102.318 with a validity period from 1-10-2021 to 31-12-2023 • 52.958 with a validity period from 1-1-2024 to 31-12-2026 • 28.577 with a validity period of 3 years from the date of their provision, which is after 2-1-2024. In particular, the CEDIS project, as a horizontal application, fully covers the organisation of correspondence between bodies, providing public sector bodies with the ability to circulate, organise, archive and securely and confidentially store electronic documents exchanged in files. Furthermore, pursuant to para. 4 of article 18 of law 4727/2020, the interconnection of Electronic Document Interchange (EDI) Systems via the central hub and the transmission of documents of public bodies through it is mandatory. Consequently, it constitutes the central solution for the interconnection and interoperability of Public Bodies. In the context of new requirements and operational needs for the modernisation of the CEDIS pursuant to the provisions of article 18 of Law 4727/2020 as in force, for the enhancement of the secure and easier circulation of documents between public sector bodies excluding public enterprises and organisations of Chapter A’ of law 3429/2005, the physical subject matter of this contract is the provision of maintenance, optimisation and upgrade services, as well as user support for the system developed within the framework of the project "Implementation of a Central Document Flow, Routing and Interoperability System with remote digital signatures as well as its Support Mechanism (help desk)" (hereinafter referred to as "the project"). In particular, the subject matter of this contract includes: Phase A': Provision of maintenance services for the subsystems of the CEDIS project Phase B': Provision of optimisation and upgrade services Phase C': Provision of user support services In the context of the above PHASES of the contract, the services to be provided are summarised as follows: • Maintenance of CEDIS Crypto-devices – Procurement of Digital Certificates • Maintenance of off-the-shelf software licences • Maintenance of subsystems • Maintenance of the Monitoring Mechanism • Preventive maintenance • Maintenance of the ticket tracking and user support system • Upgrade and optimisation of services • Interconnection of the “IRIDA” Electronic Document Interchange System with the CEDIS • User support The subject matter of this contract is the provision of maintenance, optimisation and upgrade services, as well as user support for the system developed within the framework of the project "Implementation of a Central Document Flow, Routing and Interoperability System with remote digital signatures as well as its Support Mechanism (help desk)". In particular, the subject matter of this contract includes: Phase A': Provision of maintenance services for the subsystems of the CEDIS project. Phase B': Provision of optimisation and upgrade services. Phase C': Provision of user support services.

sig_c3808ae8c24d6ecf5756.description: South Lanarkshire Council are looking to notify the market of a potential future contract opportunity to deliver Sign In/Sign Out facilities for Operatives within Grounds Services and Waste Services, although it is possible that this may be extended to other Services within the Council in the future. This facility would initially be required for approximately 900 employees across 10 separate locations. Given the nature of the duties which these Operatives carry out, the use of cards, fobs, and lanyards is not practical for Health & Safety reasons. The preference would be to use fingerprint reader technology, although the facility to manually sign in or sign out using alternative methods, such as a username/password or PIN, would be required for both onsite and offsite use. As South Lanarkshire Council has recently implemented Oracle Fusion Cloud and uses the Oracle Time and Labour (OTL) module of that system within some Service Areas, it is a requirement that any Sign In/Sign Out System operates or integrates directly with the OTL module. The link between the two systems would allow for the transfer of sign in/sign out details, working patterns, annual leave, sickness absence, public holidays, season shutdowns, new starts, departures, etc. Grounds Services and Waste Services are looking to go out to tender in April 2026, with an award date of June 2026, and an implementation start date of September 2026. Please complete and return market engagement questionnaire to Georgie.Howley@southlanarkshire.gov.uk to register your interest. Lot 1: . The subject of the procurement is the upgrade of the existing analytics and visualisation system within the CDU Data Lake platform, which includes the procurement of core-based licences and the extension of the duration of existing licences, as well as upgrade services with an extended warranty for a duration of 3 years. A detailed description of the subject of the procurement can be found in the Technical Specifications, which are an annex to this Procurement Documentation, and in the quantities stated in the Bill of Quantities. The CDU Data Lake platform is conceived as a comprehensive solution for realising additional value from TDU and TJV data through integrated tools and software capable of monitoring the entire end-to-end data lifecycle. This solution is a state service that enables ministries and related institutions to store their own data, apply defined data lifecycle processes, and integrate with applications used to process, analyse, visualise, and share their data. The goal is to simplify the data processing procedure for institutions and to standardise the tools and processes used. Additionally, storing data in one place brings synergy resulting from easier data sharing among user institutions. This upgrade increases the capacity of the existing platform while maintaining full technological compatibility of all components. In the event that the tenderer offers equivalent technology, the use thereof must not cause additional costs for the Contracting Authority.

sig_c39f86df4825ae0041a6.description: SPECIAL NOTICE — INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services (OAGS) Acquisition Title: FY26–FY30 precisionFDA Platform Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Acquisition Identification Number: ODT-2026-132021 NAICS Code: 541714 PSC Code: D319 (Cloud Computing) Set-Aside: Small Business (DNAnexus confirmed SB under NAICS 541714) Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price IDIQ Period of Performance: 08/10/2026 – 08/09/2030 Estimated Value: $33,000,000 Notice: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Digital Transformation (ODT), Office of Data Analytics and Research (ODAR), Health Informatics Staff (HIS), intends to award a sole-source Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to: DNAnexus, Inc. 1975 West El Camino Real, Suite 204 Mountain View, CA 94040 This action is being conducted under the authority of FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements), pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1). Description of Requirement: The FDA requires continued operations, sustainment, modernization, and cloud support for the precisionFDA platform — a FISMA-authorized, secure, cloud-based collaborative research environment for next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay evaluation, genomics and multi-omics research, and regulatory science applications. The platform supports collaboration between FDA researchers and reviewers, as well as external collaborators and sponsors across multiple FDA centers, including CDER, CBER, CDRH, CVM, and CFSAN. Services to be acquired include: Platform access licenses, cloud computing resources (compute, storage, data transfer on AWS), operations and maintenance, security patching, and technical support Continuation of all current precisionFDA capabilities, including immutable files with chain of provenance, file locking, Government-only spaces, Protected spaces, Review spaces, FHIR Stations, Scientific Challenge Framework, and custom data portal development capability Development and maintenance of the precisionFDA High (FISMA High) platform on FDA GovCloud FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) and FISMA High compliance maintenance per NIST SP 800-53 Rev5 Integration support for FDA enterprise systems including the Global Substance Registration System (GSRS) Training, user support, disaster recovery, and business continuity services Place of Performance: Contractor facility and FDA White Oak Campus, 10903 New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20993 Basis for Sole Source Determination: Comprehensive market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10, evaluating 20 vendors with a detailed assessment of 8 shortlisted vendors against 33 critical capability requirements. The research conclusively determined that DNAnexus is the only vendor capable of meeting FDA's requirements for Day-1 continuity of the precisionFDA mission on the date of contract award, for the following reasons: Only vendor with zero capability gaps: DNAnexus is the only vendor that scored fully across all 33 assessed capabilities. No alternative vendor can replicate on Day 1 the precisionFDA capabilities of immutable files with chain of provenance, file locking, Government-only spaces, Protected spaces, Review spaces, FHIR Stations, the Scientific Challenge Framework, or custom data portal development capability. Unique secure external collaboration capability: DNAnexus is the only platform provider able to facilitate secure FDA-sponsored scientific challenges and controlled communication with industry sponsors, vendors, academic researchers, and international regulatory partners while maintaining regulatory-grade confidentiality controls, data segregation, audit trails, and compliance features. Institutional knowledge and validated workflows: FDA has invested over seven years in developing, validating, and documenting bioinformatics workflows on the precisionFDA platform. Over 300 FDA scientific reviewers, bioinformaticians, and research scientists have been trained on the platform. The application library includes 100+ versioned apps. Migration to an alternative platform would require complete revalidation and an estimated $14.7M full rebuild. FedRAMP and FISMA compliance: DNAnexus holds FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) authorization (Cert ID FR1814557199, confirmed June 18, 2026) and FISMA Moderate ATO (FDA-sponsored). DNAnexus is actively enrolled in the PRISM High-Impact Platform Pilot (March 2026) providing a structured pathway to FedRAMP High authorization, with a parallel FISMA High ATO track to support the precisionFDA High platform. Small Business: DNAnexus is confirmed as a Small Business under NAICS 541714 (~277 employees; 1,000-employee size standard). Response Instructions: This notice is not a solicitation and does not commit the Government to award a contract. No award will be made solely on the basis of responses to this notice. Interested parties who believe they are capable of meeting the Government's requirements in their entirety may submit a written capability statement to the Contracting Officer no later than 15 calendar days from the date of this notice. Capability statements will be evaluated to determine whether full and open competition should be conducted in lieu of a sole-source award. Capability statements must address, at a minimum, the vendor's ability to provide Day-1 continuity of all current precisionFDA capabilities, FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) authorization status, and a demonstrated pathway to FISMA High authorization. Responses must be submitted electronically to: Steven Gagnon, Contracting Officer Email: Steven.Gagnon@fda.hhs.gov Allison Meads, Contract Specialist Email: Allison.Meads@fda.hhs.gov Subject Line: Capability Statement — precisionFDA IDIQ Sole Source Notice, ODT-2026-132021 Telephone responses will not be accepted. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice. Point of Contact: Steven Gagnon, Contracting Officer Food and Drug Administration, Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services Email: Steven.Gagnon@fda.hhs.gov Allison Meads, Contract Specialist Email: Allison.Meads@fda.hhs.gov

sig_c3f73ce8284f2e4ade1a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.
sig_c3f73ce8284f2e4ade1a.title: Tender for a common Operating Platform

sig_c3fcbe94339e1d28c6ea.description: The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2). LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer. LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels. sig_c4364e6b37f22060198b.description: Universiteit Maastricht (UM) intends to conclude an agreement for the supply of approximately 15.400 licences of AvePoint Control Suite Plus for Microsoft 365 and Power Platform, including the associated licence-related services. UM currently already uses AvePoint solutions within its Microsoft 365 and Power Platform environment. These solutions are integrated into UM's existing technical and functional environment and form part of the existing management processes and working methods. For this procurement, UM has deliberately chosen to continue the use of the existing AvePoint solution. Replacement by an alternative solution would entail substantial migration, implementation, configuration, testing and transition work. In addition, this would require adjustments to existing management processes and working methods and lead to considerable switching costs, implementation risks and risks to service continuity. UM considers that these consequences, especially given the subject matter and scale of this contract, are not proportionate. For these reasons, this procurement relates specifically to the supply of AvePoint Control Suite Plus for Microsoft 365 and Power Platform. This procurement is therefore not intended for the selection or implementation of an alternative software solution. The reference to AvePoint expressly does not mean that the contract is reserved for AvePoint as the manufacturer. The requested AvePoint licences can be offered by multiple resellers/partners. This enables actual competition at the level of the supplier/reseller. The term of the agreement is 2 years with the option of extension 2 times 1 year (maximum 4 years). The quantities may be adjusted during the term.

sig_c447dffcae6a7a3e1937.description: INTRODUCTION The Centre for Emergency Communication (CFB) of the Danish Emergency Management Agency is preparing a procurement procedure for a contract concerning the 112 solution. The contract will cover the operation, maintenance, support and further development of the existing 112 application. The existing 112 solution is described in the attached background note Annex A. Against this background, CFB is conducting a market dialogue with potential tenderers in two phases. In the first phase, CFB is asking tenderers to answer the questions set out in Annex B. In the second phase, CFB will invite up to five tenderers to a follow-up meeting in order to elaborate on the information. First of all, we therefore ask tenderers to answer the questions in the questionnaire and upload it in the ETHICS procurement system. TIMETABLE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue has been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in a prior information notice dispatched on 15 December 2025. We will receive answers to the questions no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00, after which we will select tenderers for follow-up meetings, which we expect to hold on 27 and 28 January 2026. We expect the meetings to have a duration of 11⁄2-2 hours. If a tenderer is invited to market dialogue, the tenderer will be notified no later than 21 January 2026. The agenda for the meetings will be sent out with the invitation, and the agenda will be based on an elaboration of the questions that the tenderer has answered. We will select tenderers based on the submitted answers. The selection will be made based on, inter alia, an assessment of tenderers' relevant experience with similar tasks, tenderers' relevant considerations regarding the task's deliverables, including transition-in, as well as tenderer's answers regarding matters that the tenderer considers to be essential for tendering for the task. THE TENDER We expect to publish the tender in the second quarter of 2026. The procurement procedure will be a negotiated procedure in accordance with the provisions of the Defence and Security Directive. The tender documents will be drawn up in Danish, and answers in Danish will be required with the exception of system documentation and similar. ANSWERING THE QUESTIONS The questions appear in Annex B, and the answer must appear exclusively in the form and not in separate annexes. The questions can be answered in Danish or English. The completed form must be uploaded via the ETHICS procurement system no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00. CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATION It is voluntary for tenderers to participate in the market dialogue, and it is without significance for the subsequent tender whether a tenderer has participated. We will treat the information received as confidential, subject to the limitations arising from the right of public access to documents, cf. the Public Administration Act. QUESTIONS Questions concerning the market dialogue can be asked in the ETHICS procurement system.

sig_c451523cb9297580cca1.description:
The subject of the contract concerns the conclusion of a framework agreement for flexible and scalable services to support AG Digipolis Antwerpen and the beneficiary contracting authorities. With this framework agreement, Digipolis aims to: • respond quickly and proportionally to temporary, structural or difficult-to-predict capacity needs; • gain access to specialised knowledge and competences that are not, insufficiently or not timely available internally; • scale tasks flexibly up and down without loss of quality, continuity or knowledge; • have complete results, services or trajectories included end-to-end when this is more efficient than deploying separate profiles; • ensure continuity, substitutability and back-up capacity; • structurally embed knowledge transfer and collaboration with internal teams; • avoid unwanted technical, organisational or contractual dependency on a single supplier; • maintain effective competition in the award of subsequent contracts; • align services with the architecture, governance, security, privacy, quality and compliance frameworks of Digipolis and the using party. The specific nature, scope, results, services and requirements are further described per lot. The framework agreement does not entail any purchase obligation or exclusivity. The actual purchase depends on the needs, available budgets, priorities and concrete subsequent contracts of Digipolis and the beneficiary contracting authorities. The contract is a service contract, in accordance with art. 2, 21° of the law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement. This lot comprises the analysis, design, development, implementation, integration, maintenance, lifecycle management and further development of custom applications, software components and business APIs. This concerns both low-code solutions on Ometa or Microsoft Power Platform/Power Apps and pro-code solutions, tailored to the functional needs and the application and integration landscape of Digipolis and the using parties. Services may relate to, among other things, requirement capture, functional and technical analysis, architecture, software and API development, integrations, testing, DevOps, deployment, production support, documentation and knowledge transfer. The contractor must be able to execute tasks independently and result-oriented and, when requested, assume responsibility for the entire realisation cycle and the agreed service levels. Lifecycle management includes, inter alia, proactively detecting, analysing, classifying and remediating outdated, vulnerable or no longer supported software components and dependencies, including with the aid of automated development and repository tools. This also includes version management, upgrades, patches, technical adaptations, documentation and knowledge transfer. The contractor must also be able to perform these activities for existing solutions that they have not developed themselves. The solutions must be secure, scalable, maintainable, documented and transferable and be realised in accordance with the current guidelines for custom applications of Digipolis. In this context, the Technical Biotope applies unless motivated otherwise, separation of responsibilities, secure by design, everything as code, automated quality gates, hybrid by design and operations by design. Digipolis or the using party retains control over architecture, governance, priorities, quality and acceptance.; This lot comprises the end-to-end realisation and services for content-driven digital channels, websites, web applications, mobile applications, front-ends and content management solutions. Within each subsequent contract, the contractor assumes operational responsibility for the entire agreed trajectory: from strategy, analysis and design to realisation, implementation, commissioning, management, maintenance, lifecycle management and further development. The services are aimed at the delivery and sustainable operation of accessible, user-friendly, secure and scalable digital solutions for citizens, employees, entrepreneurs and other target groups. Services may relate to, among other things, an overarching content strategy, consolidation and optimisation of the CMS landscape, development of content-driven or citizen-oriented WCAG-compliant front-ends, construction and maintenance of coupled websites, multisite and headless CMS solutions, integration with custom applications and other digital platforms, UX/UI, business and functional analysis, testing, quality assurance, version management, lifecycle management and support according to agreed service levels. UX and business analysis are included when they form an integral part of the implementation. The front-end technologies used must comply with the Technical biotope, with in particular the React/React Native framework being put forward as the preferred technology. Pure web hosting without additional services does not fall under this lot. Hosting that forms an integral part of a delivered solution can be included when this is necessary for the end-to-end responsibility. When multiple contractors contribute to a single solution, the contractor must actively cooperate in the overarching coordination, quality assurance, integration and knowledge transfer.; This lot comprises specialised services for the assessment, design, implementation, migration, optimisation, security, automation and support of cloud, on-premises and network-related infrastructure.

The services are restricted to clearly defined assignments within the areas of expertise named in this lot and do not constitute a general outsourcing of infrastructure or operational management. The lot comprises four areas of expertise: (1) database platforms, including MS SQL Server, Azure SQL Managed Instance, PostgreSQL and MongoDB; (2) cloud and platform automation with HPE VM Essentials, HPE Morpheus, Terraform and API integrations; (3) backup and recovery with Commvault and Commvault Cloud; and (4) Azure Cloud Networking, including virtual networks, routing, DNS, hybrid connectivity, network security and Infrastructure as Code. Subsequent assignments may relate to the temporary deployment of specialised profiles or to defined results-oriented trajectories. Each assignment is explicitly linked to one or more areas of expertise and contains concrete requirements regarding technology, results, documentation and knowledge transfer. Application development, generic application management, licence sales as a separate purpose and the structural takeover of all daily infrastructure management do not fall under this lot.; This lot comprises the flexible and scalable deployment of specialised IT security profiles in support of Digipolis's entire Security product line and the using parties. The intended result is timely access to sufficient qualified capacity for operational, project-based and compliance-oriented security needs, with shorter lead times for staffing, continuity during peaks or outages, demonstrable quality, uniform working methods and usable technical, operational, project and governance deliverables. The services are organised according to a hybrid capacity model with individual medior, senior and expert profiles and, where appropriate, temporarily assembled multidisciplinary security teams. The contractor is responsible for sourcing, screening, quality monitoring, replacement, backup and scaling. Deployment may relate to, amongst other things, security architecture and project management, network security, SOC, SIEM and SOAR engineering, security engineering, IAM, IGA and PAM, cloud security, application security and DevSecOps, vulnerability management, incident response, cryptography, PKI, data security, DLP, GRC, ISMS, NIS2/CyFun and security risk management. The services include analysis, reporting, design, engineering, implementation, configuration, integration, testing, monitoring, documentation, knowledge transfer, temporary operational reinforcement and management support within clearly defined subsequent assignments. Digipolis or the using party shall at all times retain control over priorities, scope, security policy, architecture principles, risk acceptance, project governance and acceptance of results. Out of scope are, amongst other things, structural line responsibility, personnel management, transfer of legal accountability or risk acceptance, a fully managed 24/7 SOC service without separate SLAs and the supply of software licences, hardware or cloud consumption outside the relevant assignment.; This lot comprises the temporary, part-time and flexibly scalable deployment of specialised financial expertise in support of the financial processes, continuity, transformation and knowledge building of Digipolis and the using parties. sig_c458251ec268696db888.description: The regions wish to conduct a market dialogue regarding the procurement of a new system to ensure improved IT support for the processes of handling and dispensing free-of-charge medicine (VFM). The lack of IT support complicates the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine generally and particularly in relation to the transparency that clinicians, patients and other healthcare actors are accustomed to from pharmacies in the primary sector. At the same time, the risk of errors increases, partly because data is transferred manually between multiple systems. Effective IT support will facilitate the procedure and ensure an automated and patient-safe solution that enables standardised data collection and settlement between the regions as well as close management and monitoring of medicine consumption. In addition, there is a desire to support dispensing in the patient's region of residence regardless of the place of treatment/region of treatment. The core functionality is based on existing, new and adapted functionality in FMK as well as the procurement of a new VFM Client, whose main purpose is to be the hospital pharmacy staff's portal for order receipt, processing, accounting and documentation for the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine. This VFM client is the subject of a potential upcoming procurement, which this market dialogue concerns. On this basis, the regions desire a dialogue with a number of suppliers regarding how a VFM client could be designed and developed. The regions primarily desire discussions with suppliers who have experience with health IT solutions and domain knowledge within medicine management and FMK. For the use of the market dialogue, the regions have drawn up the document "Proposal for market dialogue - IT support for the dispensing of free-of-charge medicine" as well as Annex 1 and Annex 2, which are respectively the preliminary functional requirements for the VFM client and an architecture annex. Interested suppliers must send their expression of interest to Christoffer Hejle Madsen, christoffer.madsen@rn.dk, no later than Friday 15 May 2026 at 23:59. The regions expect to hold individual dialogue meetings with up to six companies. The meetings are expected to be held as physical meetings in Aalborg on 9 and 10 June respectively. If there are more than six interested companies, the regions reserve the right to select six that are assessed to have, inter alia, domain knowledge within medicine management and FMK, company size and experience with similar development projects. Interested suppliers therefore also have the opportunity, together with their expression of interest, to submit a brief description of the company and experience in relation to the tasks described in the material. The description may occupy a maximum of 1 page.
sig_c458251ec268696db888.title: Procurement of an IT system to support the dispensing of medicinal products free of charge (VFM)

sig_c4678d4f24a49ee0fc98.description: BLS operates a railway power supply management system that makes it possible to monitor and remotely control the entire railway power grid. The BLS railway power grid comprises the 15 kV/16,7 Hz grid which supplies the electric motor vehicles of railway traffic and the 16 kV/50 Hz grid which supplies the Lötschberg Base Tunnel (LBT). In addition, the BLS railway power supply management system also monitors and controls SBB railway power supply network installations. In the railway power supply switching stations, decentralised controls record the measured values, switching states and events, and then transmit them via the control levels to the network control centre in Spiez. In the reverse direction, operators send commands to the switching stations. The network management system in Spiez is therefore considered the central instrument for operating the railway power grid of BLS and SBB in the Aare Valley and the Upper Valais. The hardware of the network management system is located in the operations centre in Spiez and a redundant system is installed separately in the switching station in Spiez. The installations are monitored and remotely controlled 24 hours a 24 by operators from three control stations. The current Siemens Power5 system was purchased in 2012, its hardware and software were replaced in 2019 and it will reach the end of its technical life in 2027.
sig_c4678d4f24a49ee0fc98.title: Renewal of the railway power grid control system

sig_c4ecb070cc0c29085f2e.description: This PCP (Pre-Commercial Procurement) is a cross-border joint procurement of R&D services to reinforce public demand-driven innovation in end-user services in the area of Climate Change Adaptation through data-driven water management. The to-be-developed solutions are expected to achieve TRL 7-8. The PCP should deliver successful, innovative and fully tested product(s) and/or service(s) that meet the common needs of the Public Buyer Group (PBG) to procure research services, develop innovative marketable solutions, speed up the time-to-market and provide best value for money. More concretely, the common needs of the public buyer group are as follows. PCP WISE aims to develop smart, sustainable solutions to improve water management and climate resiliency by monitoring the ‘Soil-Water-Vegetation (SWV) System’. Market entities are challenged to design and develop a solution that achieves this by using and combining earth observation data and environmental data on the SWV-system. This to-be-developed integrated water intelligence information product/service aims to help decision-makers manage major challenges resulting from climate change, such as floods, droughts, wildfires, heat stress and infrastructure risks in both urban and rural areas. The PCP WISE project includes 5 use cases that serve as practical testing scenarios where innovative solutions must demonstrate their effectiveness in real-world conditions. They represent the diverse geographic and climatic contexts of the European continent that provide the reference framework against which the innovations are validated for relevance, resilience and impact. PCP WISE contractors are challenged by designing and developing a solution that is applicable and scalable to tackle all 5 use cases. Following the completion of the evaluation of the tenders received, the PCP has entered its implementation phase by means of awarding a Framework Agreement where contractors are developing the solution in competition. It includes call-offs for Specific Contracts for Phase 1: Solution Design, Phase 2: Prototype Development, and Phase 3: Validation and demonstration of the solutions. This project receives funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under grant agreement number No. 101182917 and selected under the HORIZONCL62024 GOVERNANCE015, topic: Customisation/preoperationalisation of prototypes enduser services in the area Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, with a budget of around €12 million earmarked for the R&D phases during the implementation of the PCP instrument. However, the European Union does not participate as a contracting authority in the procurement. This PCP is a cross-border joint procurement of R&D services to reinforce public demand driven innovation in enduser services in the area of Climate Change Adaptation. Solutions are expected to achieve TRL 7-8. The PCP should deliver successful innovative and fully tested product(s) and/or service(s) that meet the common needs of the PBG to procure research, develop innovative marketable solutions, speed up the time to market and provide best value for money. More concretely, PCP WISE aims to customise/preoperationalise water management innovations from space for European climate resilience through PCP. It addresses waterrelated crises (floods, droughts, fires, infrastructure impacts) using space and EO data. The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement with call-offs for Specific Contracts for Phase 1: Solution Design, Phase 2: Prototype Development and Phase 3:Validation and demonstration of the solutions.
sig_c4ecb070cc0c29085f2e.title: PreCommercial Procurement for the Customisation/Preoperationalisation of Water management Innovations from Space for European Climate Resilience

sig_c52e69950b02c3452729.description: The purpose of this consultation was the award of a public contract relating to the performance of property appraisals concerning the real estate portfolio of the Caisse de Prévoyance et de Retraite des Notaires. The purpose of this lot is to carry out a five-yearly appraisal of all CPRN real estate. This appraisal must be updated every year. This lot takes the form of a composite contract comprising, on the one hand, a part for the execution of recurring property appraisal services and, on the other hand, a part for the execution of occasional property appraisal services. Treated as a global and lump-sum price, the part for the execution of recurring property appraisal services functions as an ordinary contract. Treated at unit prices, the part for the execution of occasional property appraisal services functions as a single-supplier call-off framework agreement with no minimum amount and with a maximum amount of 100.000,00 excluding VAT. This lot has been concluded for a duration of 60 months. This duration is explained by the cyclical nature of the mission, which is part of a five-year property valuation horizon, in accordance with best practice and the accounting and prudential requirements applicable to certain organisations. It guarantees methodological continuity and data comparability across the entire cycle, while ensuring the profitability of the initial investment represented by the detailed portfolio valuation, which is essential for the structuring and relevance of the mission.; The purpose of this lot is to carry out property appraisals with a visit in the event of a purchase or sale. This lot takes the form of a multi-supplier call-off framework agreement concluded with 4 suppliers (subject to a sufficient number of compliant bids) and this without a minimum amount and for a maximum amount of 150.000,00 excluding VAT. sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.description: The Municipality intends to procure a modern, future-proof and comprehensive operational system that strengthens the quality, legal certainty and efficiency of social services. The system must enable digital, cohesive and automated work processes that provide case handlers and service providers with: • increased overview and transparency, • improved decision support, • reduced administrative burden. The procured system is to constitute a central digital platform for the work of social services and be fully integrable through open APIs and standardised information flows, enabling the Municipality to create a cohesive end-to-end solution across system boundaries. The system must be configurable, scalable and adaptable to changing operational needs, new legislation and technical developments. The Municipality's information must be retainable, transferable and reusable without technical or financial obstacles, while maintaining information quality and supporting long-term sustainable information management. Digitalisation and automation are to replace manual tasks, duplicate documentation and parallel support systems to the greatest extent possible. The system shall thus contribute to: • legally secure and uniform case handling, • a good working environment, • high and traceable information quality. Full traceability must exist throughout the information chain – from decisions, interventions and execution to follow-up, changes in system configurations and integrations. The Municipality must at all times be able to track how information has been handled, by whom and on what grounds.
sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.title: Social Services operational system

sig_c54e1bb11792c92a389d.description: UK Biobank ("UKB") currently hosts a cloud-based health Research Analysis Platform which makes research projects and data accessible to researchers ("RAP"). The current RAP was procured by UKB in 2020 and was developed by DNAnexus, in collaboration with, and cloud infrastructure provided by, Amazon Web Services. As part of a series of changes to implement UKB's strategy to create a more secure data environment, UKB intends to initiate a procurement exercise in 2027 for the development of a new RAP ("RAP2.0") to take account of advances in technology over the past 5 years and its future requirements. The RAP2.0 is anticipated to be the default way that most researchers will access and analyse UKB's biomedical database and it is anticipated to comprise one or more software platforms or data analysis services that work together to meet the diverse functional needs to the research community. UKB currently intends to undertake separate procurements in relation to (i) the RAP2.0, (ii) cloud infrastructure which will host data on RAP2.0, and (iii) the development of an Output Checking System (formerly badged as Airlock Software) to control the extraction of data held by UKB for research purposes, whilst ensuring the ongoing security and confidentiality of the data and confidentiality of the data ("OCS"). UKB has established an informatics working group consisting of senior experts who will provide guidance to help develop the requirements for the technology listed at (i) - (iii) above. It is necessary for the procurement exercises for cloud infrastructure services to be completed before preliminary market engagement can take place with suppliers and users regarding the requirements and strategic approach to the new RAP2.0. The identity of the cloud services infrastructure will inform the approach to the RAP2.0 procurement to ensure the compatibility of the technology underlying the platform or platforms. It is currently intended that such preliminary market engagement for RAP2.0 will take place in 2027, followed by the competitive procurement exercise for the new RAP2.0. The current contract for the enablement of the RAP with DNAnexus expires in June 2026. It is intended that this contract will be amended in January 2026 to extend the services through to June 2028. It is currently envisaged that the first procurement to be undertaken will relate to the OCS (in the first half of 2026), followed by a procurement for cloud infrastructure (in the second half of 2026), followed by the procurement of the RAP2.0 in 2027. This Preliminary Market Engagement Notice relates to the development of the RAP2.0. Separate Preliminary Market Engagement Notices were published for cloud infrastructure and OCS in April 2025 and are being updated. Further updates regarding preliminary market engagement activities will be included in an update to this notice, as appropriate. Lot 1: .
sig_c54e1bb11792c92a389d.title: Research Analysis Platform 2.0

sig_c54ed33ef2f79324a0cc.description: The Universitätsklinikum Münster (UKM) requires a suitable solution for speech recognition and speech-supported documentation to support medical staff in the creation of medical documentation. A corresponding solution is intended to support and simplify, in particular, the creation of medical letters, findings reports and other medical documents, as well as the associated workflows. To this end, an overview of the currently available technical solutions and approaches for speech-supported medical documentation is to be obtained first. The subject matter is solutions for speech recognition and speech-supported documentation that are suitable for use in a medical or clinical environment. Of particular interest are the possibilities for capturing and processing spoken content as well as for creating and editing medical texts. The solutions should be able to take into account medical specialist language and the terminology of different medical disciplines. In addition to classic speech recognition solutions, further technological approaches are also of interest, in which spoken content is, for example, structured, summarised or used to support the creation of medical documents. Furthermore, the possibilities for integrating the respective solutions into existing clinical IT systems and workflows are of importance. These include, in particular, existing interfaces, technical requirements as well as possible operating and provision models. Also of interest are the respective concepts regarding data protection and information security as well as information on licensing, implementation, operation, maintenance and support. For this reason, a market exploration is to be carried out in order to view and evaluate potential solution systems. Please send your expression of interest to vvgm@ukmuenster.de
sig_c54ed33ef2f79324a0cc.title: Speech recognition for medical and nursing staff

sig_c5955efb6d9215bde498.description: Background Region Värmland is facing the need to replace its current integration platform (Microsoft BizTalk Server) which reaches end-of-life 2028. The platform is currently socially critical and is used within all operational areas as well as for central support functions. The region has carried out a Request for Information (RFI) with associated supplier dialogues in order to gather knowledge about possible integration platforms, technical alternatives and working methods. The result of this work will form the basis for the upcoming procurement. The project manager assignment takes over in the transition between RFI and procurement. The assignment aims to ensure a well-founded and long-term sustainable choice of path for the region's integration platform, rather than quickly carrying out a technical replacement. The assignment does not include the role of purchaser; this is handled by the region's purchaser. Description of the assignment The purpose of the assignment is to provide project management for a strategic change process where: technical path choice and target architecture are not yet established focus is on structuring decision-making, requirement-setting and procurement the region's long-term needs for robustness, continuity and maintainability must be ensured The project manager will support the operations and purchasers in the transition from RFI to procurement, and an implementation when the procurement is completed and a contract has been signed. The project manager shall contribute to the preparation of decision support for technical direction together with the operations. The documentation shall form the basis for upcoming procurement and create the conditions for a controlled and long-term migration from the existing integration platform. The assignment will be approx. 60 - 100 % allocation. Initially, the assignment will be approx. 60% and the consultant must be able to scale up to 100% when the need arises.

Two critical areas of improvement have been identified: - Care Scheduling/Planning – modernising currently paper-based processes, ensuring person-centred care and real-time updates. Although a full eMAR system is not required, medication management is a large area requiring support. - Rota Management – replacing fragmented manual scheduling with a centralised, digital platform. Through this forthcoming procurement, Hanover aims to secure a solution that will: - Improve service quality and tenant engagement through modern, digital care planning. - Increase operational efficiency and staff satisfaction via streamlined rota management. - Enhance safety, compliance, and oversight of medication management. - Provide integrated reporting, dashboards, and mobile accessibility. - Support compliance with relevant regulatory frameworks. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.

sig_c5a615a74cdb9a73d4b7.description: Istekki is currently developing the procure-to-pay process. The key objectives of the development project are: • to ensure the functionality and consistency of the entire procure-to-pay process and operating methods • to define the system architecture and tender or select the necessary systems so that their use becomes more efficient and they support the operating models and set objectives • to ensure that Istekki's contracted suppliers perform in accordance with their contracts, that cooperation develops, and that operating models generate added value for both parties • to continuously improve and develop supplier cooperation, particularly with strategic and important suppliers • to provide visibility and manageability through data and reporting • to enable system controls throughout the entire process. In developing the procure-to-pay process, we are focusing in particular on developing ordering practices and supplier management, while at the same time examining the operating methods of the entire process broadly and the following tools: • the tendering system, • the contract management system, • the SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) system, • the purchase order system, • the warehouse management system, and • the purchase invoice processing system . We want to understand what kinds of packages each company has to offer so that the data flow of the entire procure-to-pay process is seamless and efficient. It is equally important for us to figure out in what parts it is advisable to make the tenders so that, on the one hand, the system package supports our operations efficiently, and, on the other hand, many companies are able to submit a tender. The purpose of the request for information is to collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for the upcoming tender process. Answering the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tender process. However, to ensure the success of the upcoming tender process, it would be important for tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. The request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement as described in the request for information or its appendices, and the tender competition may also not be carried out. Those who have answered the request for information will not be paid compensation for making the request for information or for participating in any presentation events related to the request for information. The request for information must be answered no later than 17.12.2025 by 12.00. A response form with advance questions is attached to the request for information in Tarjouspalvelu. Responses must be sent at the same time as registering as willing to participate in the market dialogue. Answering takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. The information provided will be treated confidentially. Information session We are organising a Teams session where we will present our needs and objectives to interested tenderers on Monday 15.12.2025 at 9-10. At the same time, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Register for the information session using the accompanying link (by copying the link below into your browser): https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=ewb-5OsjeUaP1ZOOp9lZERdEXEuHF6JJgdbtjascEOxUMjhGWVVFRzZBUlo5OFZBSThBQldBRVhJOS4u The registration link for the information session can also be found in Tarjouspalvelu in attachment 2 of the request for information. Any additional information questions should in principle be asked as part of the request for information responses. The contracting authority will not publish additional information questions submitted during the request for information phase.

sig_c5a9cb636e669cfdfd15.description: By contract notice 774691-2023, the contracting authority tendered framework agreement 50.40 regarding computers and IT accessories in accordance with Section II of the Danish Public Procurement Act. The framework agreement was tendered on behalf of the contracting authority's subscribers (the contracting authority is a central purchasing body for its subscribers). The framework agreement comprises two sub-agreements: one concerning the supply of computers and IT accessories for administrative use (sub-agreement 1 Administrative computers) and one sub-agreement concerning computers for school use, basic computers for non-administrative staff, and associated IT accessories (sub-agreement 2 Basic and school computers). A framework agreement was concluded with Comm2IG A/S for Sub-agreement 2 cf. notice 413770-2024. With this notice, the contracting authority states that it has entered into an agreement with Comm2IG A/S to regulate the framework agreement's prices extraordinarily, pursuant to Section 183 of the Danish Public Procurement Act. The contracting authority finds that the regulation can take place pursuant to Section 183 of the Public Procurement Act, cf. the justification in this notice. Temporary price regulation under Framework Agreement 50.40 (Sub-agreement 2) for selected products (SKI IDs) as a result of a market-wide, unforeseen increase in product-related cost prices for central semiconductor components (CPU/GPU) and memory (DRAM/NAND). For affected SKI IDs, the regulated price is set as the applicable SKI price as of the base month of January 2026 plus the difference between the supplier's documented cost price at the time of regulation and the cost price in the base month. Regulation takes place monthly on expected cost prices with subsequent adjustment/repayment in the event of overcharging. The price adjustment mechanism (USD exchange rate) is suspended for Affected Products during the period. The scheme terminates automatically when the conditions no longer exist, when the framework agreement's price rules can be applied again, or no later than 31. May 2026; prices thereafter revert to levels according to the framework agreement's mechanics. Ongoing reconciliation is carried out against the 50 % ceiling.

sig_c5d0d8720d76c1577119.description: NHS England (NHSE) plans to re-procure a clinical terminology server solution to replace the current NHS England Terminology Server. A clinical terminology server is a centralised platform that stores, manages, and provides access to standard clinical terminologies and classifications. Its primary purpose is to ensure consistency and accuracy when recording and exchanging healthcare data. The NHS England Terminology Server is a FHIR® compliant solution that holds and disseminates assured international terminologies and classifications (such as SNOMED CT and ICD-10) and terminologies mandated for use in England, such as the NHS dictionary of medicines and devices (dm+d). You can find more details about the current NHS England Terminology Server on the following website: https://digital.nhs.uk/services/terminology-server Lot 1: .
sig_c5d0d8720d76c1577119.title: Clinical Terminology Server Solution

sig_c5dd603289a67dbf574a.description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.
