sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council intend to commission an organisation to develop and implement the creation of a local Poverty dashboard, designed to provide a clear, accessible view of child poverty across Dumfries and Galloway. The dashboard should be accessible to partner organisations and any other interested party. Dumfries and Galloway Council serve a region of around 148,000 people across the South West of Scotland, stretching from Stranraer in the West, to Moffat and Annan in the East. We are the 3rd largest local authority by area in Scotland. The latest published statistics show that the rate of child poverty in Dumfries and Galloway is 22.7%. This equates to 5,672 children and young people living in poverty in the region. For example, there are some real challenges around improving health outcomes for those experiencing poverty in the early years and to ensure that all families eligible for free school meals are reached. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway have received funding through the Scottish Governments Fairer Futures initiative. The project is early in its inception but has the long-term goal to deliver systematic change in the way public services support parents and families out of poverty. Our approach is to use existing principles and approaches to put families first, focusing on prevention rather than cure. To help achieve this, accurately measuring poverty and low income is crucial, and the availability of real-time data is vital for effective policy-making. The dashboard would have geographic layers, allowing users to explore poverty data at varying levels of granularity, offering insights into where support is most needed, with a particular focus on priority groups identified by the Scottish Government. These include lone-parent households, families with a disabled member, large families, and households with a mother under the age of 25. It is hoped that data can be gathered that will make meaningful impact to household income, targeting those who are not currently accessing all the additional help and support they can. In addition it’s important that we understand the landscape of our household in poverty, not in our dense areas of deprivation. It would be sage if this could also include pertinent health related data around missed appointments, or additional useful information which might allow for a targeted approach to reduce health inequality. The dashboard should; -Filter data by employment status, housing tenure, and age group, enabling a nuanced understanding of the different dimensions of poverty. -Be a dynamic platform with regularly updated data, that can be continually used to inform decision making. -Be publicly accessible, this openness is essential for building trust and ensuring that anti-poverty efforts are responsive to the lived experiences of families across the region. The purpose of the Poverty Dashboard is to make it easier for the Council and its partners, working with our families in poverty, to easily identify the areas of greatest need to support an evidence based and targeted approach when tackling poverty and inequality in the region.. It is anticipated that this procurement requirement will be conducted through Quick Quote portal as a non-regulated procedure, interested organisations are encouraged to express an interest to be added to the quick quote where this goes as planned.
sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.title: Poverty Dashboard for Dumfries and Galloway

As part of extended funding by the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), the SoilRob project from the programme area 2 of the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) in Müncheberg is planning the expansion of existing measuring instruments and the purchase of new ones for field work. The SoilRob project is working on an integrated understanding of the effects of autonomous small and light agricultural machinery on soils in diversified cropping systems compared to conventional large-scale agricultural machinery. For this purpose, approx. 30 different soil parameters are being investigated for their significance for soil health. In order to continue to investigate existing and new trials in detail, new measuring instruments are required. Lot LOT-0001: 1 device Fully automatic soil sampling device. Computer-aided system for the automated execution of penetration resistance measurements in soils. The system is used for the mechanical insertion of a penetrometer for high-resolution recording of soil resistance and for the generation of reproducible and largely operator-independent measurement data - Measurement & control technology: System with constant, predetermined pressure during the penetration process via hydraulic control - integrated penetration resistance monitoring for quality assurance and protection of the sensor technology - Recording of sensor data (pressure (=penetration resistance), soil moisture, optional: electrical conductivity, optical reflection (see below)) in high-resolution steps of every 1 cm penetration depth, maximum penetration depth of the probe of 80 cm - Recording of further sensor data: penetration speed (as continuous as possible) - Data acquisition: data interface and memory for the field values; system must have a sufficiently dimensioned internal data memory (min. 5-10 GB), which enables the storage of at least 500 complete measurement profiles including georeferencing - Power supply: autonomous operation via a system-integrated e-power pack; independent of the carrier vehicle's on-board hydraulics. - Assembly & integration: installation on a carrier vehicle (tractor attachment to three-point hydraulics (category 1 or 2)) or pick-up (such as VW Amarok) - Performance: enables more precise control of the penetration speed compared to manual operation; minimises human error factors during data acquisition. Parallel measurement of soil moisture and optionally other soil parameters such as electrical conductivity (EC) or optical reflection (red & infrared), - Overspeed control - Technical requirements: pressure: at least 135 bar; volume flow: 20 Planning basis: MP-3.90 device Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0002: 2 devices Infiltrometer. Expansion of the existing SATURO device pool for the comparable continuation of existing measurement series: portable, computer-aided and fully automated field infiltrometer for determining the field-saturated hydraulic conductivity of soils under field conditions; designed for soil science, hydrological and soil physics field measurements with high repeatability and minimised manual operating effort. - Measurement & control technology: automated ring infiltrometer system with measurement of infiltration at at least two different hydrostatic pressure heads - automatic regulation and maintenance of a constant water level above the soil surface - automatic recording of the infiltration rate and calculation of the field-saturated hydraulic conductivity directly in the system - Consideration or correction of three-dimensional flows through multi-pressure head/dual-head measurement methods, so that no manual estimation of soil-specific correction factors is required. - Data acquisition: integrated control unit with display and storage of measured values in the field - automatic documentation of infiltration rate, pressure head, water level, measurement duration and calculated field-saturated hydraulic conductivity - Export of measurement data via USB or equivalent interface to a computer - Raw data export in a common, further-processable format, e.g. CSV and/or XLSX - Software or equivalent solution for downloading, viewing and archiving the measurement data must be included in the scope of delivery or be available free of charge. - Power supply: autonomous field operation via a rechargeable control unit or system-integrated power supply; mains charger included in the scope of delivery - Charging/supply range at least 18-24 V DC or equivalent - Operation independent of external field power supply during measurement Planning basis: Dual-Head Infiltrometer SATURO Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0003: 1 device Hood infiltrometer. Field infiltrometer for determining the hydraulic conductivity of soils in the near-saturated range under natural field conditions; designed for low-destruction infiltration measurements directly on the soil surface - Measurement & control technology: measuring system with a closed, downward-open and water-filled hood, which is placed directly on the soil surface; the circular soil surface covered by the water forms the source area for the infiltration flow. An additional contact layer, e.g. sand layer or membrane, as well as preparation of the measurement surface must not be required for standard measurement operation. - The control of the hydraulic pressure head must take place via a Mariotte water supply or an equivalent pressure-stable method - the effective hydraulic pressure head at the soil surface must be freely adjustable between zero and a negative pressure up to the air entry point of the respective soil. - The display of the hydraulic pressure head must take place via a manometer or an equivalent precise pressure display.

- The calculation of hydraulic conductivity must be possible from the steady-state flow rates determined in the test according to Wooding or an equivalent recognised evaluation method. - Data acquisition: It must be possible to record the flow rate either electronically via pressure sensors with a handheld device and associated evaluation software or via an equivalent documentable measurement method. In the case of electronic execution, it must be possible to save measurement data for the flow rate or water consumption, the set hydraulic pressure head, the measurement time and the measurement point identifier and to transfer them to a computer. Software-supported evaluation and documentation of the measurement data must be possible. - export in a common, further-processable data format is desirable. - Data acquisition: Integrated control unit with display and storage of measured values in the field - automatic documentation of infiltration rate, pressure head, water level, measurement duration and calculated field-saturated hydraulic conductivity - Export of measurement data via USB or equivalent interface to a computer; raw data export in a common, further-processable format, e.g. CSV and/or XLSX - Software or an equivalent solution for downloading, viewing and archiving the measurement data must be included in the scope of delivery or be available free of charge. Further technical data: - Infiltration vessel with Mariotte pressure control, filling volume 5 l - U-tube manometer: +25 cm ... 0 ... -25 cm - Infiltration hood small: max Ø 16 cm - Infiltration hood large: max Ø 24 cm - electronic pressure transducer - Handheld device and logger: at least 2.000 measured values, measurement interval 1 s, sampling rate 0 - 100 s (freely selectable) Planning basis: Field measuring device IL 2700 Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0004: 1 Device Portable canopy analysis system for crops. Extension of the existing SunScan device pool for the comparable continuation of existing measurement series: Mobile, scientific complete system for the non-destructive determination of the leaf area index (LAI) and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) within plant stands. - Measurement components: Set consisting of a probe unit with an integrated radio module and a high-precision, external sunshine sensor (at least class BF5) with a separate radio module for reference measurement. - Data transmission: Wireless communication via RadioLink on the frequency 434 MHz or equivalent - Range: Radio transmission between the modules over distances of at least 100 to 200 m (depending on vegetation density). - Energy supply: Completely mains-independent operation; the modules are powered by standard AA batteries. - Operation & IT: Data acquisition via a dedicated handheld computer (RPDA) with the operating system - Mechanical accessories: Including a 3-leg tripod for stable positioning of the reference sensor in the field or equivalent - Mobility & protection: Delivery in a robust transport case Planning basis: SS1-COM-R4 SunScan complete system Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0005: 10 Devices Single-board computer. sig_c603fa54adc2d7637a77.description: Tenders are sought for the Supply, Delivery, Installation and Support of an enterprise-grade Campus Occupancy Sensing Solution for Trinity College Dublin. A Campus Occupancy Sensing Solution captures and reports how spaces are used across the estate. It is intended to provide Trinity with accurate, anonymous occupancy and space-utilisation data across the timetabled teaching estate to inform space management, timetabling, energy and HVAC optimisation, and capital planning. The requirement is to be delivered in phases over the term of the framework, with an initial call-off, and the solution must integrate with Trinity’s existing enterprise network and information systems. Tenderers are asked to provide detailed responses to the requirements set out in Appendix 1 below. This procurement establishes a framework agreement for the supply, installation and support of a range of campus sensing solutions over its four-year term. The first call-off under the framework is for occupancy sensing in timetabled teaching spaces, as specified in Appendix 1. Subsequent call-offs may, at the Contracting Authority’s sole discretion and subject to available budget, extend to other categories of campus sensing, including but not limited to building-occupancy sensing, environmental sensing (for example temperature, humidity and CO2 / air quality) and energy and sub-metering sensing. The Contracting Authority gives no commitment or guarantee as to the volume, value or timing of any call-off, including in respect of these additional categories. Detailed technical requirements for sensor categories beyond the first call-off occupancy requirement will be defined at the relevant call-off stage.
sig_c603fa54adc2d7637a77.title: BE3917F - RFT to establish a Single Supplier Framework for the Supply, Delivery, Installation and Support of a Campus Occupancy Sensing Solution for Trinity College Dublin (TCD)

sig_c60989034fe39fd4f571.description: The National Information System in Sport (hereinafter: NISuS) is prescribed by articles 64 and 65 of the Sports Act ("Narodne novine", number: 141/22). The project holder is the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport. NISuS is designed as an application system for supporting business processes in the specific scope of work and activities of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport. NISuS must be fully integrated with other information systems of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport that support other, standard business processes: office operations, finance, document management, etc. NISuS consists of multiple subsystems, applications and modules for establishing a set of registers and records with corresponding code lists and support for corresponding business processes, as well as additional modules to support the business processes of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport. The system can be accessed in three ways: as a system user, anonymously in the public data section, and via the e-Citizens system in the personal data section. The source code and database of the application system are available for inspection at the Contracting Authority upon prior signing of a statement on the acceptance of data confidentiality by the Tenderer.

sig_c61fe9debf926dbae75b.description: We invite your tender to support data-driven management based on a data warehouse. A reporting package has been implemented at Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences, utilising a centralised data warehouse as the basis for reports. Data is transferred to the data warehouse from source systems in finance, student administration and human resources using interfaces, file transfers and, in part, files manually maintained on a network drive. Data transferred to the data warehouse is processed and transferred as Azure Data Factory transfers into tables, on the basis of which multiple data models designed for various purposes are formed and loaded into the Power BI service for use in reports. The need for support will be twofold. On the one hand, we need a partner who continuously monitors the operation of the data warehouse and reacts swiftly to any disruptions. On the other hand, it is foreseen that data sources will be added to the data warehouse, so support and expertise will be needed when the required workload in this respect is planned as a project. A framework agreement valid until further notice will be concluded with the selected supplier. The terms and conditions for termination of the agreement are defined in the draft agreement. The procurement has not been divided into lots because the services forming the subject matter of the procurement constitute a single technical and functional entity, the implementation of which requires a unified division of responsibilities and seamless cooperation. Based on market dialogue, there are sufficient suppliers on the market capable of implementing the entire entity, so failing to divide it into lots does not restrict competition. A more detailed description of the procurement is set out in Appendix Liite5-Hankinnan_kuvaus_Jamk_DW_ylläpito_ja_jatkokehitys

sig_c66cdda09f01679c83a5.description: Title: Software as a Service (SaaS) – Ombuds Office Case Management System Solicitation Number: 5000085894 GSIN: 81162000 Description: 1. Summary THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT #EN578-191593 ONLY. Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has a requirement for a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform and associated services (via the issuance of Task Authorizations) to securely capture (Protected A) visitor journey data through case management files, while enabling robust reporting and data analysis. This system should allow the Organizational Ombuds Case Management System (OOCMS) to capture, manage, and analyze information provided by visitors who contact the office as well as facilitate the tracking of activities and follow-ups. The case management solution must be bilingual, respect Government of Canada accessibility and security requirements, be user friendly, have a data entry interface that will avoid the possibility of overwriting information from one case to another, and have an efficient search engine. ECCC intends to award one contract for this solution for two years with the option to extend for an additional three periods of one year each under the same terms and conditions. 2. Security There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult Part 6 - Security, Financial and Other Requirements, and Part 7 - Resulting Contract Clauses. For more information on personnel and organization security screening or security clauses, Bidders should refer to the Contract Security Program of Public Works and Government Services Canada (http://www.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca/esc-src/introduction-eng.html) website. 3. Integrity Provisions Bidders must provide a list of names, or other related information as needed, pursuant to section 01 Integrity Provisions of Standard Instructions 2003. 4. Service Requirements For services requirements, bidders in receipt of a pension or a lump sum payment must provide the required information as detailed in article 3 of Part 2 of the bid solicitation. 5. Trade Agreements The requirement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada–Chile Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement, the Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive Economic Free Trade Agreement [CETA], the World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement [WTO-AGP], the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership [CPTPP] and the Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement. 6. Social Procurement Environment and Climate Change Canada supports the Government of Canada’s social and economic objectives, including increasing the participation of businesses from under-represented groups in government procurement opportunities. As such, bidders owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities are encouraged to submit a bid to this opportunity. 7. Debriefings Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 8. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Bidders may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 9. Additional Information For additional information, interested suppliers must contact the Contracting Officer named in this Notice.

sig_c6a39ce90ff3abddc5d0.description: The Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Universität Hannover is procuring GPU and CPU computing power for the "Soofi project" for the training of a large language model (LLM). The procurement is divided into two lots corresponding to two technically distinct system classes. As part of a publicly funded European project on open large language models, the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Universität Hannover (LUH) is publishing this Europe-wide call for tenders for GPU and CPU computing capacities for the pre-training and post-training of large language models (LLMs). The procurement is divided into two lots corresponding to two technically distinct system classes: Lot 1 concerns GPU nodes in accordance with the NVIDIA DGX/HGX-B200 or B300 reference architecture (8 GPU modules per node) or newer. The subject matter is the completion and post-training of mixture-of-experts (MoE) models with more than 100 billion parameters, evaluation, the generation of synthetic data using generator models of approximately 400 billion parameters, and the distillation of smaller model variants. - Reference GPU NVIDIA B200 in nodes of the DGX/HGX-B200 reference architecture (2,25 × 1015 FLOPs/s BF16 Dense per GPU); DGX/HGX B300 or newer NVIDIA reference architectures of the same class (e.g. DGX Rubin NVL8) are permissible. - Binding minimum computing power 1,5 × 1025 FLOPs ≈ 1,85 million B200 GPU hours - Reference configuration 1.024 GPUs (128 nodes) during the first 65 days, thereafter 128 GPUs (16 nodes) until the end of the term (155 days) = 1.873.920 GPU hours = 1,52 × 1025 FLOPs - Minimum number of simultaneously available GPUs ≥ 1.024 (128 nodes) during the first 65 days; thereafter ≥ 128 (16 nodes) - Start / end of the service period Start offered by the tenderer, no earlier than 1 December 2026 and no later than 15 January 2027; term 155 days (reference: 1 December 2026 to 4 May 2027), with a preceding two-week test phase - Option Up to three months after the base term, 128 GPUs - Price ceiling 16.400.000 EUR (including 19 % VAT) - CPU ≥ 15 million core hours; partition with ≥ 4.096 physical cores - Storage ≥ 1 PB parallel file system plus ≥ 1 PB S3-compatible object storage - Location EU/EEA or a country with an adequacy decision by the EU Please refer to the specification of services for further information.; As part of a publicly funded European project on open large language models, the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Universität Hannover (LUH) is publishing this Europe-wide call for tenders for GPU and CPU computing capacities for the pre-training and post-training of large language models (LLMs). The procurement is divided into two lots corresponding to two technically distinct system classes: Lot 2 concerns rack-scale systems in accordance with the NVIDIA GB200 or GB300-NVL72 reference architecture or newer. The subject matter is the pre-training and post-training of an MoE model with more than 350 billion parameters, for example via reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. sig_c6babfeec6557dda0115.description: Upgrade of the virtual environment, all in accordance with the Technical Specification for the upgrade of the virtual environment (hereinafter: Technical Specification) and the Bill of Quantities for the upgrade of the virtual environment (hereinafter: Bill of Quantities). Description of the subject of procurement: Upgrade of the virtual environment, all in accordance with the Technical Specification for the upgrade of the virtual environment (hereinafter: Technical Specification) and the Bill of Quantities for the upgrade of the virtual environment (hereinafter: Bill of Quantities). In order to enable the contracting authority's end users to have mobility, independence from the type of user platforms and a better user experience when working with business-critical services, and to increase the performance, security, availability, scalability and manageability of the business-critical services themselves, the existing data infrastructure is being expanded. The expansion of the data infrastructure includes an increase in performance, capacity, security, scalability and the possibility of future additional performance increases of the existing data infrastructure in the primary and secondary data centre according to future business needs and regulations. The implementation of the new high-availability disk system increases robustness against catastrophic events, reduces the time required to restore the business level to the pre-outage level, and automates the process of activating the disaster recovery plan for business-critical services for the purpose of optimising operational activities and complying with regulations. The contracting authority's existing data infrastructure in the primary and secondary data centre that is being expanded is implemented with equipment from the manufacturer Dell Technologies. The offered data equipment must be fully compliant with the contracting authority's existing system in all functionalities it supports. The offered data equipment must have the capability of synchronous and asynchronous replication with the existing Dell Technologies PowerMax 2000 and PowerMax 2500 high-availability disk systems without using additional devices. All offered data equipment must be new, unused and from a single manufacturer. The subject of procurement entails the following services: • Project management • Integration of the offered hardware into the contracting authority's environment • Implementation of replication and testing of the disaster recovery environment
sig_c6babfeec6557dda0115.title: Improvement of the virtual environment

sig_c6c455b74199950b4633.description: LUKS operates high-performance network connections on a fibre-optic (FO) basis between its sites and the two data centres, via which clients, servers and applications exchange large amounts of data with each other. Currently, the Sursee and Wolhusen sites are connected to the LUKS data centres via rented, redundant 10-Gbps fibre-optic cables. The capacities of these connections are increasingly exhausted, and the transmission speed is no longer sufficient for an increasing number of use cases. In addition, the equipment for data transmission over the fibre optics, the transceivers, will soon reach end-of-life status. LUKS now wants to increase the bi-directional transmission speed from the Sursee/Wolhusen sites to the LUKS data centres and, furthermore, keep open the possibility for further network expansions. To this end, technology from the WDM family ("xWDM") is to be used. This call for tenders seeks providers who can build, measure/test, introduce and hand over the new solution for the fibre-optic (FO) data transmission solution for LUKS, based on a works contract for the construction and a maintenance and support contract during the operating period. The latter has a term of 5 years, including the option for annual extension up to a maximum term of 8 years, and it regulates the provision of an SPoC for LUKS, through which all inquiries and concerns of LUKS relating to the topics regulated therein are handled, as well as next-business-day restoration by repair or replacement in the event of a transmission device failure.
sig_c6c455b74199950b4633.title: Call for tenders "xWDM Multiplexer"

sig_c6e096a2396a4ea0cf12.description: Plymouth requires a Community Equipment Service (CES) for adults and children within the Plymouth City Council area or those on the outskirts if registered with a GP in Plymouth. This service provides equipment relating to a prescribed, clinical need to support a person in their own home. This includes equipment such as beds, mattresses and mobility aids. Equipment may be provided to support someone with a short term need, while they recover from illness, or longer term or permanent ill health. Referrals to the service are made by prescribing organisations such as Livewell Southwest, University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust, St Luke's Hospice and Practice Plus Group Hospitals. CES includes the provision of a range of Core Stock equipment which is most frequently used, more specialist Non-Stock equipment ordered on an ad-hoc basis and Minor Adaptations. It is a requirement that the service is supported by a comprehensive web based IT platform for the provider and those referring to the service. A team of Plymouth City Council and Livewell staff have been working together across children's and adult services to enact a contingency plan for the contract. This has included liaison with key partners who rely on the service, including University Hospitals Plymouth and St Lukes'. sig_c6f470efe37cb0aae868.description: Development of a connector for linking operational management information systems, which will ensure data exchange of information between operational and information centres of the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic, specifically between regional operational centres and the national operational centre with the operational and information centres of neighbouring states. The connector will be used for the automated transmission of information about the type and location of an incident, requests for cooperation of Integrated Rescue System components, the status of equipment and its GPS position, and about the intervening units of the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic and neighbouring states. The connector's information will also include a map section of border areas up to a distance of approximately 50 km from the state border on the territory of the Czech Republic and the neighbouring state. The implementation of this public contract consists of three interconnected parts. The first part is the development of the Connector, which includes the development and delivery of software, implementation and commissioning of the system within the Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic. The second part is ensuring the connection of the Connector with neighbouring states. The third part is the delivery of map materials. A separate part is the provision of SLA, operation, support and development of the Connector.

sig_c71817910edd025ebdd0.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. sig_c71db71e2a6b18f6037a.description: Derbyshire Constabulary (DC) is currently looking into the available options for the Provision of an Enterprise Service Management (ESM) tool. The force aims to reduce system costs by consolidating multiple platforms into a single, unified solution. There are a variety of contract end dates for the systems being looked at so this would be a phased integration. In the current financial climate, it is paramount that Derbyshire Constabulary maximise value for money through our digital estate. DC plan to deliver a streamlined, cost-effective, and future-ready centralised solution by consolidating business systems into an integrated Enterprise Service Management solution. This will provide financial savings to supplement the Force Service Review, enhance operational efficiency, reduce siloed processes, and empower frontline and support teams through smarter, connected technologies. DC are keen to understand advancements in technology since the previous market exercise and assess whether a single solution could support multiple enabling services departments. As part of this Request for Information (RFI) DC is exploring the replacement of the below systems with an ESM: Please note this list is not exhaustive Digital Data and Technology Department (DDaT) Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) – An ITIL-aligned ITSM tool that automates workflows and elevates IT service delivery across the organisation. The current system is provided by Alemba Limited. IT Asset Management - A unified platform for IT Asset Management, Software Licensing throughout the entire lifecycle. The current system is provided by Certero. Joint Strategic Assets Asset Management System (AMS) and Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) - A system used collaboratively by Derbyshire Constabulary and Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS). The software is designed to help manage the physical assets -such as buildings, equipment, and infrastructure -of both organisations throughout their entire lifecycle. Its primary purpose is to consolidate all relevant property and asset information into a single, centralised platform where data can be stored, accessed, and analysed efficiently. The current system is provided by Concerto Support Services Limited. The system has the following modules and features: Helpdesk – defect reporting by users, job allocation and tracking from inception to completion Condition surveys Building occupancy management Estates Management e.g. deeds, lease and licences Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM)/Compliance management Asbestos management Fire Risk Assessments Reporting, Analytics and Dashboards – User configurable Project management Equipment management e.g. plant and machinery tagging e.g. plant and machinery tagging Mobile data capture CAD File viewer Health and Safety management These are interdependent, for example the system can raise a flag that asbestos hazards exist in a location which a user has reported a defect for. This will then be automatically highlighted to the allocated contractor. People Services HR Case Management – a system that enables handling of all HR related cases from initiation to resolution. Ability to create, assign, and track HR cases from initiation to resolution Support for multiple case types (e.g. absence, performance, grievance) Configurable workflows aligned with HR policies Automated escalation rules based on timelines or case status Secure document storage Full audit trail for all actions and documents Ability to record case notes and communications Option to send and log email correspondence within the system Standard and custom reporting capabilities (e.g., case volumes, case types, resolution times, trends) Fleet Fleet Management System – A system which is used collaboratively by Derbyshire Constabulary (DC) and Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS), which stores the below information: Vehicle allocation and department information Vehicle maintenance history Vehicle life cycle Vehicle check and defect history Surveillance vehicle files / Ghost plates / department information – EM-CTP / EMSOU & TSU, Section 22 agreement (Gov) Accident information including 3rd party details MOT & tax information Fuel accounts Procurement and Contract Management Records Management System – A system which provides a centralised and secure platform for holding contract information, generating reports, and tracking procurement activity across the full lifecycle of a procurement lifecycle. The system allows the department to manage key procurement records in a consistent, auditable, and efficient way. Contract details - including contract owners, values, durations, and supplier information are stored within the system to support effective contract management and organisational oversight. The current system is provided by Keto Limited. Corporate Services Risk Management System - A database for multiple risk registers, which includes strategic risks and departmental/BCU level risks. The system allows authorised users to submit corporate risks which can be fully managed within the system. It maintains a record over the lifetime of the risk enabling a risk owner to track it over time, including the use of a risk matrix adopted by the East Midlands region. Each risk has an identified responsible officer. Risk controls may be allocated to individuals, enabling a level of tasking and reporting. The system also enables the production of reports with the ability to export data for custom reporting. It is available to any authorised user on the force network. The current system is provided by Keto Limited. Please note, this system is also used by Leicestershire Police. Injury on Duty Reporting System – A system used to report all accidents, assaults and near misses. The system should have the ability to be populated with drop down menu options to ensure consistency of data and allow for changes to these lists to be administered internally. The system should allow notifications to be sent to supervising officers for investigations to be completed as well as allow for reports to be produced and a comprehensive search facility. The current system is provided by NEC Software Solutions. Finance and Business Services Ticket Booking System – A system used for employees to book out corporate tickets. The system allows ‘members only’ of the Corporate Pass Scheme to be able to book days out tickets. The system should have the ability to add and delete attractions and staff members and the ability to produce detailed reporting information such as date attended, usage of venue, who booked the ticket, how many times they have booked out the ticket etc. The current Ticket Booking System is provided by Keto Limited. The Pre-Liminary Market Engagement (PME) will support DC with the development of a Business Case (BC). To formally engage with the market, this Request for Information (RFI) to the market to conduct a comprehensive review of existing ESM solutions. Lot LOT-0000: .

The subject matter of the procurement is the migration services of government digital service applications to IaaS/PaaS solutions in Romania's Government Private Cloud (GPC) as follows: (1). Lot no. 1 - Application migration services into Romania's Government Private Cloud (2). Lot no. 2 - Cyber security assessment services Complete details regarding the services forming the subject matter of this procurement can be found in the Specifications document corresponding to each individual lot, which is an integral part of the Tender Documentation. FOR EACH INDIVIDUAL LOT: the objective of the Framework Agreement corresponding to each individual lot, to be awarded by the Contracting Authority, is to establish a rapid and efficient mechanism for the conclusion of Subsequent Contracts for the provision (procurement) of migration services for government digital service applications to IaaS/PaaS solutions in the GPC, including cyber security assessment services according to its needs and within the limit of the budget allocated for this purpose. Total estimated value: Between 288.668.898,76 RON excluding VAT and 867.479.705,67 RON excluding VAT (total estimated value of all lots combined). The total minimum estimated value associated with the minimum estimated quantities is 288.668.898,76 RON, excluding VAT. The total maximum value associated with the maximum quantities is 867.479.705,67 RON, excluding VAT. The estimated value of the Framework Agreement is expressed as a range. The maximum estimated value of the procurement represents the total maximum value of the Framework Agreement resulting from this procedure for its entire duration (the total cumulative maximum value of both lots). The minimum and maximum estimated values corresponding to each individual lot are specified in paragraph II.2. The minimum and maximum estimated quantities corresponding to each individual lot are specified in paragraph II.2. Any interested Economic Operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the Tender Documentation. The number of days before the deadline for the submission of Tenders by which Economic Operators may request clarifications is 19 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Any request for clarifications must be transmitted via SEAP (www.e-licitatie.ro), after the Economic Operator registers for the award procedure. The Contracting Authority shall respond (via the consolidated response) clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications and all requests for additional information received from interested Economic Operators at the latest on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of Tenders. The subject matter of the procurement is represented by migration services of government digital service applications to IaaS/PaaS solutions in the GPC. The migration of Applications entails the provision of services and, on an ancillary basis, the supply of products. The products need to be incorporated into the services, with a view to preparing an application for migration and ensuring the level of cyber security requested by the national authorities empowered in this regard. The products may take the form of licences and/or software products that need to be developed in order to prepare the Application for migration. Complete details regarding the services forming the subject matter of this procurement can be found in the Specifications, an integral part of the Tender Documentation, for lot no. 1. The objective of signing the Framework Agreement corresponding to lot no. 1 is to establish the terms and conditions, as well as the unit prices, in order to create the framework allowing the Contracting Authority to contract, depending on specific needs, the provision of services forming the subject matter of the Framework Agreement corresponding to this lot. The estimated value of the largest Subsequent Contract is: 77.466.241,28 RON excluding VAT (of which 6.169.302,92 RON relating to the estimated effort of 1.918 person-days for the provision of migration services and 71.296.938,36 RON representing the lump sum allocated to licences). The estimated value of the smallest Subsequent Contract is: 1.218.436,24 RON excluding VAT (of which 682.865,40 RON relating to the estimated effort of 200 person-days for the provision of migration services and 535.570,84 RON representing the lump sum allocated to licences). sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_c771b6d9c7a0b9958f38.description: This contract constitutes a single-award framework agreement within the meaning of the regulations relating to public procurement. It sets the conditions applicable to recurring services as well as to additional services and developments that may be ordered as the contracting authority's needs arise during its term. The purpose of the framework agreement is the supply, implementation, maintenance, support and development of an integrated human resources management system, covering in particular: • complete payroll management for contract, statutory, authorised, volunteer and pensioner staff (including management of bonuses, absences, career breaks, attendance fees, tax and social security declarations, etc.); • time and attendance management, including clocking in/out, leave validation, encoding and validation of teleworking, mission management, planning, as well as agent access via web portal and mobile application. The contract aims to guarantee complete functional and technical consistency between these two areas, in a single and integrated approach. It does not include the supply of physical clocking terminals. The contracting authority already has these. Tenderers must ensure the compatibility of their solution with the use of current time clocks (see Annex E). The contract will be concluded for a maximum duration of 10 years. The duration of this contract is explained by the investments and developments necessary for the provision of a solution meeting the needs and constraints of HYGEA.

Framework agreement based on the "Operation, major refurbishment of the TVM network, procurement of new vending machines" in the net amount of 12.260.426.222 HUF + VAT, which is the estimated maximum total value (framework amount) of the contracts to be concluded during the term of the framework agreement to be concluded as a result of this procedure, in accordance with Section 18. (1) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). The quantity of the public procurement (framework quantity) is determined by the definition of the above framework amount for the entire service package (for all tasks together). Within the framework of the operation service, the Contracting Authority (CA) plans to operate at least the following quantity of vending machines from the 320 machines at its disposal: within 1 years from the start of the operation of the first TVM machine, 280 units, in the following years: 280 units, then 240 units, 200 units, and 160 units. From these quantities, the CA undertakes a purchase obligation only within 1 years from the start of the operation of the first TVM machine regarding the operation of 280 units, with the proviso that the purchase obligation for the entire service package covers a total net framework amount share of 3.500.000.000 HUF during the term of the framework agreement. Basic conditions: By TVM network, the CA means the public transport ticket and pass vending machine network, which consists of TVM devices (vending machines), the TVM Central Control System, the application software of the TVM Central Control System, data connections, spare parts, reserve equipment, and the entirety of hardware and software elements. (see Technical Specification point 1.1) The Contracting Authority currently has a ticket and pass vending machine network consisting of 320 devices. It is the Tenderer's task to provide the CA with the right to use the CA-specific TVM Central Control System application software – which complies with the requirements contained in the Technical Specification (TS) – as part of the operation service, starting from its commencement for the duration of the FA (for the right of use provided with basic conditions, see FA point 11.3) and, in addition to this – if the CA orders it – it must also provide an enhanced level right of use (see FA point 11.4), within the framework of which it grants the CA, and any third party to whom the CA grants such a derived right, a non-exclusive right of use that is unlimited in time, subject matter, and territory, and which also extends to further development and further development by a third party. Accordingly, the right of use can be transferred to a third party. The provision of this right does not restrict the Tenderer in the performance of its tasks until the expiry of the framework agreement. Within the framework of providing the enhanced level right of use, the Tenderer is obliged to hand over the source code to the CA. The relevant detailed rules are contained in the FA and the TS. The Tenderer must incorporate the consideration for the right of use provided with basic conditions into the monthly fee for the right of use of the Central Control System (see Price Table item number 6), while a separate fee must be provided for the provision of the enhanced level right of use, which does not form part of the operation fee. (see Price Table item number 1) The Tenderer is obliged to make the TVM Central Control System application software, as well as all software or applications necessary for its development and operation that constitute a condition for the full operation of the TVM network, available to the CA within 6 months following the effective date of the direct order 1 issued simultaneously with the entry into force of the framework agreement to be concluded based on this public procurement procedure, in such a way that it is functional as a system in live operation – at the time of service commencement – and successfully meets the conditions, tests, and parameters prescribed by the CA. (hereinafter: Software Integration) To this end, the Tenderer is obliged, following the entry into force of the framework agreement, based on the CA's direct order 1, to commence software development – if this is necessary with regard to the software to be provided – and preparation for service commencement. The earliest date for service commencement in the case of operation and operation-related services is 2025. September 1., with the proviso that this date shall be determined in the direct order taking into account and ensuring the 6-month period provided to the Tenderer for Software Integration. The consideration for the software provision and integration task must be incorporated into the row with item number 5 of the Price Table. The Tenderer's task is to prepare for the takeover of the existing entire TVM network from the current operator, to cooperate in the execution of the takeover, and to take over the 320 TVM machines of the existing TVM network put into operation by the CA, while taking into account the aspect of business continuity. The Tenderer must incorporate the fee for this task into the operation fee of the TVM machines. (see Price Table item numbers 7-11) The commencement of the takeover is only possible if the CA has ordered the operation service for the given TVM device from the Tenderer. The machines must be integrated with the new central software that the Tenderer intends to provide, and then operated in accordance with the order. The detailed task content of the preparation for the takeover of operation and the cooperation in the execution of the takeover, as well as the takeover process, with the relevant conditions and requirements, are contained in the TS. As an organisation providing a public service, a fundamental expectation of the CA towards the Tenderer is the assurance of business continuity; within this framework, following the physical handover-takeover of the machines (in connection with the software replacement), the machines may be out of operation for a maximum of 2 hours. It is the Tenderer's task to perform tasks related to contact protection and/or electrical safety inspection. Continued in section BT-24 (point II.2.4.) Contracting Authority, pursuant to Section 105. of the Kbt.

sig_c7953e22fa55f94c22eb.description: The subject matter of the tender is the planning, implementation, integration and commissioning of a highly available Microsoft Exchange on-premise environment to replace the existing Tobit David mail system for approx. 600 users. Lot LOT-0001: Replacement of Tobit David by Microsoft Exchange On-Premise. The service comprises in particular the detailed technical planning, the setup of a highly available Exchange environment with two DAG nodes, the integration into the existing infrastructure including Active Directory, VMware, Citrix, Proxmox Mail Gateway, archiving, monitoring and backup, as well as the setup of user, functional and resource mailboxes. Furthermore, extensive functional and high-availability tests, the productive cutover, the stabilization of operations, as well as documentation, knowledge transfer and handover are owed. Historical email data is transferred separately by the contracting authority into the existing archive system and is not migrated to Exchange. Personal contacts and appointments are transferred by the users themselves. The implementation takes place in specified project phases. The specific schedule and duration of the individual phases are the responsibility of the contractor. The overall project including commissioning, documentation, handover and acceptance must be completed by 31.01.2027 at the latest.

sig_c7ae57afa624c3022150.description: As part of the "C-Roads" project (CRG-3), a replacement for the analogue-radio-based public transport priority system for motor omnibuses is to be tested. Unlike the predecessor project "LOGIN" (Optimal traffic signal control in local public transport), in which a proof of concept for C-ITS-based public transport priority could be provided with the participation of various research partners, C-Roads relies on production-ready hardware available on the market. In addition, integration into the existing ITCS/control system of IVU Traffic Technologies AG (IVU) is to take place, for example for the visualisation of signal timing forecasts. sig_c7be3752fd29945dbf59.description: NS&I is currently going through a transformation programme, with new key suppliers working to significantly update our operating model, including customer-facing services like our websites and apps, and our call centre, as well as critical systems like our core banking engine. As part of our transformation programme, we have identified a requirement for our key suppliers to have in place (or put in place) an Enterprise Data Management (EDM) or similar cataloguing tooling solution. NS&I has been considering the use of Enterprise Data Management at a strategic enterprise-wide level, and has determined that there may be significant benefit to adopting a single common EDM tool, and asking all of our strategic suppliers to utilise this platform. At present, NS&I does not have a singular view of which of the EDM tools on the market it may have a preference for. Therefore this RFI process is being conducted, to help NS&I understand the solutions that may be available. The RFI will be conducted during November, with a view to NS&I being able to express a preference for an EDM tool before the end of the year. For the avoidance of doubt, this is not a formal public tender process and will not result in the award of a contract (or contracts) by NS&I. This process is an RFI for information purposes only, intended to help NS&I understand, and form a view on, the solutions available on the market. The requirement to sub-contract / license an appropriate tool, based on the preference NS&I may indicate following this process, would remain with our key suppliers. Lot 1: .

NISuS is designed as an application system for supporting business processes in the specific scope of work and activities of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport. NISuS must be fully integrated with other information systems of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport that support other, standard business processes: office operations, finance, document management, etc. NISuS consists of multiple subsystems, applications and modules for establishing a set of registers and records with corresponding code lists and support for corresponding business processes, as well as additional modules to support the business processes of the Directorate for Sport of the Ministry of Tourism and Sport. sig_c7cd19cca4b765a55ec2.description:
The German Space Agency at DLR operates the CODE-DE-Lab data platform on behalf of the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport and the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space, which enables users in Germany to search for, obtain and process Earth observation (EO) data. Free processing quotas are available to official and scientific institutions for the latter. CODE-DE-Lab provides access to data from the Copernicus programme, various national and commercial missions and other data products. The data can be processed using various tools of varying complexity. CODE-DE-Lab is an important foundation for the official and scientific use of EO data in Germany. Over the coming years, various aspects of the provision and processing of EO data will be subject to significant changes. Data volumes will increase significantly, particularly due to the expansion of the Copernicus programme, which will also result in changes to the corresponding data modalities and relevant frameworks for data provision. Increasing data volumes will correspondingly create additional demand for required hardware. The further increasing use of AI methods also places additional requirements on the scope and design of the hardware required for the provision and processing of EO infrastructures. At the same role, the needs of EO data users are also dynamic; increased use of data on the one hand and a diversification of users can be observed. The use of EO data is required for an increasing number of administrative tasks; at the same time, EO data remains an important basis for environmental research. The data volumes required for this are constantly increasing. In addition to large scientific institutions and federal authorities, an increasing number of state and municipal institutions as well as smaller research projects are also using EO data. CODE-DE-Lab, as the central national platform for the use of EO data, is currently financed by two federal ministries, but other operating and financing concepts are also conceivable. For an early, targeted design of future EO data infrastructures in Germany, the German Space Agency at DLR requires comprehensive and detailed information due to the dynamics described. The aim of the EODATA30+ project is therefore the development of scenarios for the provision and processing of Earth observation data from 2030 onwards in Germany. The project is divided into six investigative aspects: (1) Analysis of the current CODE-DE-Lab platform and the current operating concept, (2) Stakeholder analysis and requirements gathering, (3) Gathering, analysis and evaluation of further development requirements, (4) Market sounding, (5) Derivation of scenarios and operating models, (6) Final evaluation and derivation of recommendations for action. Together with the coordination and management of the project and cooperation with the client, the six investigative aspects represent the eight work packages of the EO DATA30+ project. To carry out the project, potential contractors must have knowledge and experience in working with EO data as well as the design and provision of infrastructures for data provision and processing. An understanding of the requirements and needs of authorities and scientific institutions is also required. Within EODATA30+, close and regular cooperation with the client is required. sig_c7cdaf57dcae79fcbf7c.description: The Department for Education (DfE) requires further specialist technical services from an existing supplier to support the final phase of the Older Building Research (OBR) project. The OBR project has already been procured and a consortium bid was successful; of which the supplier was a party, fulfilling the Engineering Expert role as a subcontractor to the prime supplier. This supplier is Useful Simple Group Limited. Through the OBR project, the DfE is investigating, cataloguing and extrapolating the condition of the post-war education estate, including through onsite intrusive investigations. This research project will enable the DfE to improve its understanding of the post-war education estate. This work is underpinned by a bespoke risk model, designed using research and investigations conducted to date and based on the technical assumptions and interpretative approach applied by the Engineering Expert Advice role. The project requires a further final phase not originally included in the contract with the prime supplier successful in the original procurement. This final phase involves interpreting and enhancing fieldwork inputs for model development, support on Large Language Model (LLM) workflows to support LLM development, providing engineering-led interpretation of fieldwork findings to enhance model relevance and insight, and applying the already established fieldwork approach across up to six additional schools, developing proposals for alternative methodologies to enhance data quality and fieldwork insights. To ensure continuity and compatibility with the research and model developed to date, the services under this additional appointment must be delivered by the supplier who fulfilled the Engineering Expert Advice role in the original procurement and using the same technical assumptions and interpretative approach previously developed by them and applied. This consistency is essential; the model and supporting analysis have been built incrementally as a single coherent system. Introducing outputs based on different assumptions and knowledge base would require significant re-engineering and re-validation of existing work, creating disproportionate technical complexity and undermining the integrity of the model. The appointed supplier will provide engineering-led interpretation of the above scope to integrate new data into the current risk model without compromising its structure or functionality. These services will enable the DfE to maintain a consistent technical approach, ensuring that new findings complement and strengthen the existing evidence. Lot 1: .
sig_c7cdaf57dcae79fcbf7c.title: Older Buildings Research (OBR) Professional Engineering Expert Advice Role

UKSA will require the successful supplier to utilise the existing hardware manufacturer provided software interfaces and to use existing commercially available/open-source plate-solving software packages. This is to preserve hardware warranties and minimise assurance activities. Lot 1: . Provision of commercial off-the-shelf software solution and software development as per the description outlined above. UKSA anticipates launching this procedure in mid-March, with a planned deadline for bid submission of 24th April 2026. Contract award is planned for mid-late May with a targeted kick-off of 1st June. **UKSA intends to place this requirement via the Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services Dynamic Purchasing System (RM6235). UKSA will NOT be able to issue tender documentation to bidders who do not meet the filter requirements set. UKSA will also require Cyber Essentials Plus accreditation is in place at point of bid submission for this tender. Any bidders without Cyber Essentials Plus accreditation will be rejected. Owing to the security requirements relating to access to BOREALIS, this tender will be restricted to Uk-registered companies where all strategic decisions are undertaken in the UK by UK nationals on grounds of security. International subcontractors and project consortia partners will be permitted, though UKSA reserves the right to require changes to project consortia and/or subcontracting arrangements where a proposed structure represents a security risk.**

sig_c7f0b7c8993ae6e8b586.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request/market survey with which Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto (hereinafter the contracting authorities) are surveying the market for the procurement of capacity services. The purpose is to survey the operators in the market and to gather comments from suppliers. The objective is to obtain comprehensive information to support the implementation of the future procurement. Both the Municipality of Kaarina and the Municipality of Lieto aim to tender server capacity services as an open procedure due to an expiring agreement. The estimated commencement date of the agreements is September-October 2026. Description of the information request and invitation to market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto are organising a joint market survey for the procurement of scalable and modern capacity services that meet certified security requirements (physical and information security): Katakri, ISO27001 or equivalent. Suppliers are requested to respond in writing to the questions concerning the procurement and to state their interest in participating in the market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto produce their own basic IT services and also maintain their own servers. REGISTRATION Suppliers must respond to the questions in the information request and state their interest in participating in the market dialogue by Fri 6.2.2026 at 12.00 in the supplier service at https://kaarina.toimittajapalvelu.fi/. The contracting authorities will treat the responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, the contracting authorities will continue the market survey with separate market dialogues. The market dialogues will be implemented as Teams discussion sessions between the Municipality of Kaarina, the Municipality of Lieto, and the supplier. The discussion sessions will be held with a maximum of six (6) suppliers. If there are more than six (6) companies registered for the market dialogue, the contracting authorities will select the most suitable suppliers for the dialogue based on their own criteria. The dialogues are intended to be implemented during February 2026. Any additional information concerning the discussions will be provided to the operators heard after registration. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE NOTICE This notice is an information request for a market survey and dialogues. This notice does not request tenders. The descriptions presented in this notice are preliminary and indicative advance information on the procurement. The information request does not oblige the implementation of the procurement in the manner described in the information request. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drawing up the call for tenders. Please note that all material is intended solely for the information request and the conduct of market dialogues. The market dialogues do not bind the contracting authorities to implement the procurement, nor do they bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating. Responding or failing to respond to the information request does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tendering procedure. SCHEDULE The preliminary schedule plan aiming for the commissioning of the solution is as follows: - Invitation to participate in the market survey, January 2026 - Submission of market survey responses, February 2026 - Selection of suppliers for the market survey discussion, February 2026 - Market survey discussions, February 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders, March 2026 - Submission of tenders, March-April 2026 - Selection of solution, April 2026 - Contract negotiations, April-May 2026 - Service transfer and start-up project May-September 2026 - Production readiness September-October 2026
