Please note that this Framework will remain open to applicants for the full life time of this Framework. Call off competitions will commence in 2027. Lot 1: Health & Social Care. This lot covers apprenticeships that develop skills for roles across health, clinical support, adult social care, children’s care, and community wellbeing. It includes, but is not limited to, standards supporting public health, social work support, and wider care services. Lot 2: Education, Early Years & Community Support. This lot includes apprenticeships for professionals working in schools, early years settings, and wider community learning and support environments. It covers teaching assistants, early years practitioners, youth work, learning mentors, SEND support, and careers guidance. It also includes community-focused roles that support wellbeing, education engagement, family support, outreach, coaching, and local community development activities. Lot 3: Business, Administration & Management. This lot covers apprenticeships supporting core business operations and organisational effectiveness. It includes, but is not limited to, business administration, human resources, project and programme management, leadership and management, and business improvement roles. This lot focuses on developing strong operational, organisational, and managerial capability. Lot 4: Digital, Technology & Data. This lot includes digital and IT apprenticeships that strengthen organisational technology capability. It covers, but is not limited to, software development, cyber security, data and AI roles, digital support, cloud and infrastructure operations, and digital transformation functions. Lot 5: Creative, Cultural, Media, Marketing & Design. This lot covers apprenticeships across the creative industries, cultural sectors, marketing, media and communications, and design professions. It includes, but is not limited to, content and creative production, digital and graphic design, cultural heritage, marketing and digital marketing, communications, and design led roles. This lot supports creative, promotional, and content driven capability across sectors. Lot 6: Engineering, Construction, Transport, Environment Built & Sustainability. This lot covers technical and professional apprenticeships across engineering disciplines, the built environment, transport operations, and environmental or sustainability focused roles. It includes, but is not limited to, engineering; construction and building services; and surveying roles. It also incorporates transport focused pathways such as transport planning and infrastructure support, alongside roles related to environmental management and sustainability practices. Lot 7: Public Services, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Protective Services, CommunityS. sig_ca481643ca5c09fa8804.description: The contracting authority intends to procure a comprehensive, digital system for the management of property taxes and municipal fees. The procurement is for the systems Comtek eSkatt and Komtek eGebyr. Komtek eSkatt is a trade system that supports the entire process for property taxes, including valuation, case handling, committee processing, publication of decisions and communication with residents. The system automates central work processes and updates the ongoing valuation basis based on, among other things, changes in the land register and retrieval of the wealth basis from the Norwegian Tax Administration. Komtek eGebyr is a joint fee module that connects property, owner, trade data and fee regulates. The system automatically calculates and updates fees based on changes in the trade data, and produces the completed invoice basis for the municipality ́s finance system. This ensures correct fee calculations, better control and reduced need for post-inspections. The systems are closely integrated and together constitute a complete platform for handling property taxes and municipal property fees. Comtek eSkatt presupposes the use of Comtek eGebyr and the systems are designed to function together as one connected system for case handling, fee calculations and invoicing. If no objections are received within 10 days from the publication of this notice, the Contracting Authority will enter into a contract with the above mentioned tenderer, at the earliest, from 24.04.2026. Any objections to signing the contract without a competition must be submitted in writing and the contracting authority will be available within 10 days from publication.

sig_cab2d49ab25aa0ff2c9d.description: The subject of the procurement is the delivery, further development and maintenance of the police situation management tool (Pivo). The Police Board (hereinafter also the Subscriber) acts as the contracting entity in the procurement. The background to the procurement is the need to develop a nearly real-time and prioritised view of open matters under investigation for the police. The goal is to develop a scalable, modern tool equipped with an easy-to-use user interface for national police use to support the management of open matters in the Police Information System (Patja). The tool displays role-specific work queue views, where open investigation matters are in prioritised order. The police situation management tool (Pivo) is owned by the Police Board, which is also responsible for its maintenance. The actual users of Pivo are investigators, investigation secretaries, and team and investigation leaders at police departments. The subject of the procurement is the implementation of the MVP (Minimum Viable Product) version of Pivo as a target-priced delivery project. The system's MVP version will be available for production use during the year 2026. The procurement also includes, as a mandatory option, the system's maintenance and development services, should the Police Board decide to take these services into use.
sig_cab2d49ab25aa0ff2c9d.title: Police Board - IT consultancy 2023-2028 (DPS) - Delivery of the Police situation management tool and related maintenance and development services

sig_cb3f0a7409f3c50e390a.description: Resource Innovations Inc (RI), previously known as Nexant Inc, provide ongoing support and maintenance services for the Voltage Trajectory Tool (VTT), which RI developed for EirGrid for its use in the National Control Centre. The VTT supports secure operation of the transmission system at higher renewable and System Non Synchronous Penetration levels by assessing how changes in reactive power affect voltage conditions across the transmission network. The VTT services were originally procured via the ENQEIR639 tender. In order to meet evolving complex business requirements, certain enhancements were required on the VTT that RI developed. Due to the proprietary and custom nature of such enhancements, swift transition to a different supplier would have posed significant technical and operational challenges, and potential service disruption. To ensure continuity of support and maintenance for this critical tool, EirGrid must therefore enter into an extension agreement with RI. Entry into this extension agreement is being actioned in accordance with the Article 50.F of the Utilities Directive (2014/25/EU). In the present circumstances, the extension facilitates completion of similar support, maintenance and enhancement services that conform to the basic project under the original tender. EirGrid has expressly provided notice of its intention to rely on this provision in the ENQEIR639 tender documents, and this was further communicated in the contract award notice #45282 which outlined certain conditions for any such award to take place.
sig_cb3f0a7409f3c50e390a.title: ENQEIR639 - Resource Innovations Contract Extension 2026

sig_cb62666f7a0004e2b800.description: Purpose Norsk Tipping would like mobile partners who shall contribute with the necessary competence and capacity to develop attractive and responsible user journeys in a quality good way. The mobile partners shall also contribute to building the competence Norsk Tipping needs for the future. Mobile is the company's most important customer channel. Norsk Tipping has approx. 2.4 million customers, of which nearly 90 percent use mobile, mainly via apps distributed in the App Store and Google Play. They are, thus, a central prerequisite for Norsk Tipping being able to fulfil his social mission: "... facilitating responsible gambling offers and preventing negative consequences of gambling. Efficient operations shall ensure that as much of the revenues go to good causes". Norsk Tipping's partners must therefore contribute to the company developing in a sustainable direction, through active competence transfer and by strengthening the product model from a mobile perspective. Strengthen the ability to deliver within the product development model Norsk Tipping works smoothly to reduce risk through early learning, continual feedback from users and operations, and the possibility to adjust courses before major investments are made. The work is organised through product development areas with a multi-disciplinary product team who are responsible for both value and risk connected to defined products and user journeys. The product development areas shall have competence and responsibility to define systems for problems, develop them and further develop them so that they deliver value for companies and customers. In order to achieve this, Norsk Tipping has a mix of product development areas consisting of what can be defined as a "value stream team" (e.g. the product development area for sports), and areas with "platform" and "enablement-team" (for example Platform: Whole and Frontend). Multi-disciplinary skills in the areas shall be sufficient to define problems/possibilities and solutions, develop and further develop them, in order to raise the value and quality of their product. In order to strengthen the disciplines, practice partnerships are used, and challenges and solutions are encouraged to share trade related questions with others within their profession. This is how Norsk Tipping creates value through cross-discipline and professional competence, and contributes to the professional environment developing over time. In order to ensure a necessary minimum of coordination and coordination between product development areas and other environments, we have common rituals such as; · Joint planning for tertial. It takes place over five days, where the product development areas analysis and understanding of the effects products and services create are connected by the company ́s direction and needs. · Lot and leather. A monthly showcase, where different product development areas share things they've learned in the period. · Target demo. A tertial demo where the product development areas describe goal achievement, sharing knowledge and a selection of the things they have created. · Practice partnerships for different disciplines. · Synchronisation for product development areas. Product development managers share block to goal achievement and clarify who they need to talk to in order to move forward · Rituals on product development area/team level: Sprint planning, sync (standup), retrospective and demo/Friday wins. Different frequency in areas based on need The model shall strengthen the areas ́ autonomy to create effects, which are made possible by clear direction, necessary frames and transparency for coordination. Norsk Tipping currently has a strong internal professional environment for mobile development, with competence in development for iOS and Android, with an emphasis on iOS. Experience in the environment spans from one to over 15 years. The contracting authority also has a strong internal UX environment with competence on both web and mobile, of which the web is prominent. In addition the company has testers and test developers. The quality in Norsk Tipping shall be integrated in the work and applies for all phases of product development. The contracting authority must deliver in accordance with different standards. In Platform: Hele og Frontend (P:HF) has Norsk Tipping strategic app competence through the area management, with product development manager, tech lead/team architects. Several product development areas have permanent native developers. Areas that do not have their own native developers will receive assistance from P:HF. The contracting authority will over time develop a balanced division of responsibility between the platform and the different product development areas, in line with increased maturity and greater internal ownership. Areas with separate native user journeys will gradually be able to work more independently, but for the foreseeable future there will be common need connected to testing, release and further development of the platform. Professional development and practice partnerships shall support this across. The following product development areas currently have native user journeys: · Platform: Whole and Frontend (App platform, front page, app framework) * Accountability * Value-added services (some joint services, e.g. Grassroots, notifications) * Customer, ID and payment * Lottery * Sports * Playing together
sig_cb62666f7a0004e2b800.title: Mobile development partner

sig_cb7978fbabd6d82fcf38.description: Update - 14 Sep 26 The purpose of this update is to clarify procurement history of this requirement. While this is not a follow-on acquisition, portions of this requirement are currently being satisfied under FA251824D0001 awarded to Gemini Technical Services JV, LLC. I. General Information: The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses. This Sources Sought is issued solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this notice marked "Proprietary" will be handled accordingly. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses to this Sources Sought will assist the Government in determining the potential level of interest, competition adequacy, and technical capabilities of industry respondents (specifically small businesses) to provide the required products and services. The Government may also use this information to assist in determining whether a small business set-aside (or other socioeconomic set-aside) will be appropriate or developing any subsequent small business subcontract participation and small business goal percentages. The Government does not intend to respond to questions posed in Industry responses. The Government does not guarantee any action beyond this notice. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Responses that are incomplete and/or not submitted per the Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed. Interested parties or potential contractors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) before the issuance of a potential Request for Proposals/Quotes to be eligible for contract award or payment if the Government chooses to make an award. Information on registration and annual confirmation requirements may be obtained via SAM.gov. Conflict of interest rules apply, and offerors will be required to submit mitigation plans following the release of the RFP. II. Requirement Information: This Sources Sought notice seeks to identify qualified firms capable of providing comprehensive, non-personal mission support services for the 392d Combat Training Squadron (392 CTS). Under this framework, contractor personnel will deliver core capabilities to plan, integrate, execute, and assess Modeling and Simulation (M&S)-enabled exercises (including SPACE FLAG, FLASH POINT, POLARIS HAMMER, and SPACE SKIES) in support of U.S., joint, and allied warfighters. To ensure the continuous readiness of United States Space Force (USSF), joint and coalition forces, this expertise spans a critical array of warfare domains, including Satellite Communications (SATCOM), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), Electronic Attack (EA), Orbital Warfare (OW), Space Electronic Warfare (SEW), Space Domain Awareness (SDA), Missile Warning (MW), and Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO). Furthermore, contractor personnel will drive operational execution by providing Command and Control (C2) support, intelligence product generation, operations assessments, and lessons learned (L2). This operational framework is firmly underpinned by robust technical requirements, encompassing full-scope IT and cybersecurity support, systems engineering, configuration management, orbital analysis, and sophisticated M&S for the Distributed Mission Operations Center-Space (DMOC-S) and BattleLab enclaves. Ultimately, these integrated capabilities will be leveraged to design, plan, execute, and assess USSF service-level exercises and advanced mission-focused training. Support includes programs identified as Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Required (SAR) administered under the enhanced security guidelines/procedures authorized by Department of Defense DODI 5200.01 (DoD Information Security Program and Protection of Sensitive Compartmented Information) and AFI 16-1404 (Air Force Information Security Program). Responses to this announcement are needed to help inform acquisition planning and to identify capable sources. To efficiently and effectively deliver the required supplies/services, it is anticipated that vendors will have specialized experience in large-scale space exercises, complex IT and M&S environments, and managing highly cleared personnel. III. Purpose: The Government is currently considering NAICS Code 541330 (Engineering Services) and Product Service Code (PSC) R425 (Support – Professional: Engineering/Technical) for this requirement. If your firm believes this requirement should be solicited under a different NAICS code or PSC, please include your detailed rationale and supporting market data within your response. This synopsis is encouraging responses from qualified and capable Small Businesses. Firms responding to this Sources Sought must be U.S. owned and must (1) state whether they are a small or large business based on the size standard above; (2) state if they have socioeconomic classification(s) as follows: Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB); section 8(a) small business; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Economically-Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB); a Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone small business; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB);. Small Businesses that are in or are considering Joint Ventures or Mentor Protégé Agreements are encouraged to respond to the source sought. Responses from other than small businesses will be reviewed. Note: If the requirement is set aside for small business, the clause RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will be included in the contract. The data obtained from this notice will assist the Government in understanding the capabilities available in providing advanced space training, exercise execution, and mission rehearsal capabilities. IV. Scope of Anticipated Effort: The 392 CTS provides space combat training through Live, Virtual, & Constructive (LVC) environments to prepare warfighters to achieve and maintain operational dominance in the space domain. The contractor shall provide Mission Support Services, Information Technology, Communications, and Management Support (ITC&MS), and Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS). The Government anticipates this requirement will consist of an IDIQ ordering period of five years. Work will primarily take place at Schriever SFB, Suffolk, Buckley SFB, Hurlburt Field, Vandenberg SFB, and other designated facilities. V. General Submission Instructions: The responses submitted shall be in sufficient detail and clarity to provide the Government with the information it needs. Responses to this Source Sought notice shall meet the following standards: Page Limitations: Section 1 Cover Letter: 2 Pages Section 2 Capability Statement: 10 Pages Section 3 PWS Review: 3 Pages Text Size: No smaller than 10 point Text included in graphics, tables, and figures can be no smaller than 9 point No embedded documents Fully address Sections 1-3 as outlined above Responses that are incomplete and or do not follow these Response Submission Instructions may not be reviewed Electronic version of your response only in Microsoft Word or PDF compatible files VI. Section 1 - Cover Letter: The cover letter shall include the following: Company information: Company name 2 points of contact and with contact information (name, address, phone number, website URL, if available, and email address) Cage Code, UEI, and DUNS Number Short description of the company (history, experience in similar service activities/supplies, etc.). Company business size with socioeconomic classification based on the designated NAICS code Information on any potential teaming arrangements, joint ventures, or significant subcontracting arrangements. VII. Section 2 – Capability Statement: Please provide detailed responses to the following questions based on the draft PWS. For each area, identify your firm's current or recent (completed within the last five years) contracts or subcontracts that match the scope, complexity, and magnitude of this PWS. Highlight prime contract experience supporting Space Force Delta-level organizations, Distributed Mission Operations Nodes, or equivalent joint distributed simulation hubs of similar financial magnitude: Plan and Execute Large-Scale Joint LVC Exercises (USSF Service Exercises). Plan, coordinate, execute, and assess large-scale (700+ participants) military exercises. Detail your proven experience managing the full Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC) across geographically distributed nodes. Provide a specific historical example of where you translated joint space doctrine into dynamic Master Scenario Events List (MSEL) injects (e.g., simulated orbital debris, electronic attack) within a LVC environment. Finally, describe your capability to conduct post-exercise analysis and deliver formal After-Action Reports (AAR). Recruit and Retain Specialized TS/SCI/SAP Personnel. Explain your relevant experience in recruiting, clearing, and retaining qualified personnel with Top Secret (TS)/Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearances and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. Include historical metrics (such as average time-to-fill rates for tactical space domains and historical retention rates exceeding 90%). DMOC-S Operations. Operate, sustain, and manage the DMOC-S and its complex M&S environment certified to Joint National Training Capability (JNTC) standards. Provide a specific example of how your team successfully operated systems involving missile warning, Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), and operational RF communications. Demonstrate your experience managing distributed simulation networks (e.g. JTEN, DMON) and utilizing standard architecture protocols (e.g., DIS, HLA) to link space simulators with joint air, land, and maritime simulators. Multi-Domain Information Technology (IT) and Cybersecurity Support. Deliver comprehensive IT, cybersecurity, and network engineering support across multiple security enclaves (e.g., AFSCI, SIPRNet, Stone Ghost/FVEY coalition networks) at both primary and distributed locations. Detail your experience maintaining system configurations, securing Assessment and Authorization (A&A) packages via eMASS under the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and performing concurrent cybersecurity auditing (such as STIG compliance). Decribe your experience rapidly-restoring network outages during high-tempo, simulated LVC exercise operations without degrading the training audience’s experience. Professional Planning and Control Force (PPCF) Support. Manage and oversee a distributed workforce of full-time, embedded M&S and exercise planners deployed to geographically separated USSF Component Commands (e.g., SPACEFOR-INDOPAC, SPACEFOREUR-AF). Describe your firm’s experience interfacing directly with senior combatant command staff. Provide examples of previous contracts your company has had that had embedded planners responding to local theater commanders’ Operational Plans. Surge Capacity and Contingency Operations. Manage, schedule, and execute approximately 15,000 hours of surge support annually, frequently requiring 24/7 operations to support exercises with little to no notice. Detail contractual experience executing large-scale, short-notice surge requirements. Specifically, how you maintained and deployed a pool of cleared, pre-screened, or cross-trained personnel to sustain 24/7 operations during massive events without causing mission failure or degrading steady-state services. VIII. Section 3 - SOW/PWS Review: Please identify areas within the draft PWS that are unclear, restrictive, or present execution obstacles, referenced by PWS paragraph number. Additionally, outline any best commercial practices, industry innovations, and recommendations for the most effective contract type and pricing structure to efficiently support the 15,000-hour annual exercise surge requirement.

sig_cba675c782880b739811.description: The object of the contract is the rational utilisation of modern technology and its integration into various aspects and operations of the Municipality, with the aim of its successful social and economic development, the upgrading of the quality and quantity of the services provided, the enhancement of its operation and administrative capacity, the development of social well-being and local entrepreneurship, the enhancement of the knowledge and skills of citizens, as well as effective environmental protection. The ultimate purpose of the Digital Strategy of the Municipality of Oropos is to improve the quality of life of its residents and citizens, as well as its visitors. In particular, within the framework of developing actions and applications for the digital transformation of the Municipality of Oropos, the following Lots will be implemented: 1) Supply and installation of smart pedestrian crossings accessible to persons with disabilities. 2) Organisation of a transport office and management of the municipal vehicle fleet. 3) Smart city / municipality guide with recording of local businesses. 4) Municipal cemeteries management system and file digitalisation. 5) Cultural – Sports events – Electronic ticket management. 6) Smart early warning and risk management system within the boundaries of the municipality. 7) Electronic management and organisation system for the Administration and operational capacity of local government authorities. 8) Implementation of public key performance indicators in accordance with ISO 37122, adapted to Greek conditions. Tenders shall be submitted separately for each lot of this document and submission of a tender for more than one or for all Lots is permitted. The maximum number of lots that can be awarded to a single tenderer is set at eight (8). The proposed system will ensure the safe crossing of pedestrians and persons with disabilities through the automatic recognition of pedestrian presence and automatic luminous signalling of the crossing where feasible. The proposed system is planned to be implemented at seven () crossings; This action concerns the development of a platform for monitoring and managing the entire vehicle fleet of the municipality, with the installation of a modern telematics unit and screen within each vehicle and connection to a central management software; The proposed action concerns the creation of a platform - a point of central information and communication of local businesses with the Municipality where the profile of all businesses in the services of the Municipality will be recorded, at the same time that businesses present either summarily or in detail their products and services with periodic updates.; The proposed application concerns the development of a platform that aims at the interoperability and digitalisation of the operation of the department of the Municipality of Lavreotiki responsible for managing the municipal cemetery. The aim is to increase the efficiency of this department and improve citizen service.; With the Cultural – Sports Events management system and electronic ticket management, the Municipality will have the ability to create the events it desires (e.g. theatre, cultural event, concerts, etc.) and through this to carry out the complete management and sale of tickets; It concerns a central Unified System for the early warning of citizens – users (civil protection, fire service, police, etc.) for risk management primarily from fires. The proposed system in the Municipality of Oropos will constitute a comprehensive action to address any kind of crisis after a fire, but primarily a system for warning and safety of a location of increased risk regarding the danger of fires within the administrative boundaries of the Municipality; The proposed platform aims to gather all the necessary information of the Municipality that allows the highest administrative and political personnel to monitor the current status of the Municipality, the projects and the works it performs. The application will provide the capability for scheduling works, projects and actions.; The proposed application concerns the recording and extraction of performance metrics from predefined sources with specific periodicity. Data entry will be performed either manually by the operator of the , or (preferably) by interconnection with a relevant information system. This specific system will support input-output indicators, have the capability to connect with funded programmes and generate result reports in relation to the corresponding indicators.

Multiple contract awards are anticipated, with a performance of five years, with four negotiated rate escalations each year after the initial first year. The total MATOC shared pool capacity shall not exceed $90,000,000 or five-year duration, whichever comes first. The minimum guarantee throughout the five-year contract is $1,000. Responding firms must address each evaluation criteria in the appropriate sections of the SF 330 for the prime contractor as well as all subcontractors and consultants. If subcontracted, clearly indicate what part of the scope they will be performing. To be eligible for the contract award, the firm must be registered in the Department of Defense (DoD) System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM Internet site at https://www.sam.gov. For contractors requiring Common Access Cards (CAC) or contractors requiring unescorted access to USACE controlled property for greater than six (6) months the Centralized Suitability Service Center (CSSC) requires a T1 Background Investigation to be completed. Should a task order require a T1 Background Investigation it will be specified. The primary purpose of the proposed contract is to provide A-E General Design and other related Services anywhere within the boundaries or assignments of Mississippi Valley Division. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: A-E and related services are to be accomplished through individual Task Orders, which shall consist of the following comprehensive scope tasks and requirements: (a) Core Engineering, Design, and Project Documentation: The work will involve investigations, comparisons, data evaluations, analyses, designs, water quality analyses, technical writing, and drafting for: Engineering Documents: Preparing Design Documentation Reports (DDRs) geotechnical reports, feasibility studies, plans and specifications, Operation, Maintenance, Repair, Replacement, and Rehabilitation (OMRR&R) manuals, value engineering, or other technical engineering documents. Design, Modeling & Drafting: Civil design, hydraulic design, hydrologicanalysis, sediment transport, coastal engineering, structural design, geotechnical design, mechanical design, electrical design, architectural design, naval architecture, project management, building and civil information modeling (BIM/CIM), and CAD drafting. Engineering Support During Advertisement (EDA): Preparing amendments to the advertised plans and specifications and updating the BIM/CIM as warranted by comments received from prospective bidders. Engineering Support During Construction (EDC): Attending pre-construction conferences; responding to contractor requests for information (RFIs) and clarifications; reviewing submittals from the construction contractor; and performing monthly or bi-weekly site visits (or visits at critical times) to witness construction practices, observe site conditions, and document implementation of the design from the designer's perspective. Levee Safety & Structural Periodic Inspections: Performing detailed, systematic technical inspections and evaluations of the safety, stability, and operational adequacy of levees and civil works structures. Support Services: Surveying and the use of aerial mapping are required to support this work. (b) Required Disciplines & Professional Qualifications: The assembled team must demonstrate professional qualifications, education, training, licensing, certification, professional registration, overall relevant experience, and longevity within their disciplines and firm. Key design personnel must include: Engineering: Structural, Civil, Hydraulic (including hydrologic analysis, sediment transport, and coastal engineering), Geotechnical, Mechanical, Electrical, Corrosion, Environmental, and Cost Engineering. Scientific & Applied Fields: Hydrologists, Geologists, Architects, Naval Architects, and Surveyors. Geospatial & Technology Specialties: Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) Mapping and Analysis, Drafting via Computer-Aided Design (Autodesk), 3D Modeling CAD consisting of Building Information Modeling (BIM), and Civil Information Modeling (CIM), and professional Project Management. (c) Types of Features & Project Scopes The work may involve existing and new projects at any design stage, involving new or existing structures, including: Hydraulic Structures: Locks, floodgates, floodwalls, levees, navigation structures, drainage canals and structures, pumping stations, and prestressed/post-tensioned concrete structures. Marine Structures: Bulkheads, dolphins, fenders, guide walls, jetties, or shoreline protection. Highway & Infrastructure Work: Roads, ramps, bridges, utility relocations, and buildings (such as warehouses, pump houses, or offices related to the structures above). Risk Reduction & Environmental Projects: Flood risk management, hurricane and storm damage risk reduction projects, non-structural techniques (including elevation), freshwater and sediment diversion projects, environmental infrastructure projects, and other multi-purpose projects. (d) Specialized Civil, Structural, Geotechnical, & Surveying Tasks: The work may involve the following detailed types of related analysis, modeling, and field work: Modeling & Structural Analysis: 3D modeling of buildings, structures, sites, and horizontal construction features; civil/site work design; structural design; planning; program and project management; finite element modeling; frame analysis; pile group analysis; and drainage analysis. Contract Package Development: Development of plans and specifications, Design-Build Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and real estate rights-of-way (ROW) drawings. Field Investigations & Testing: Hazard Toxic Radioactive Waste (HTRW) investigations; architectural treatments; landscaping; performing soil borings and soil testing to determine soil properties; and providing boring logs in accordance with USACE New Orleans District geotechnical criteria. Analytical Calculations & Engineering Evaluations: Developing pile capacity curves; bearing capacity analysis; cantilever retaining or floodwall analysis; temporary retaining structure design; time-settlement projections with lift schedules; soil pressures; seepage and dewatering analysis; stability analysis for levees using Spencer's Method and/or Janbu’s Method (including reinforced embankments, dikes, and other earthen structures); bank stability analysis; slope stability analysis for revetments, channels, and excavations; stability analysis of floodwalls (T-walls, I-walls, L-walls); downdrag and settlement analysis; numerical modeling; settlement-induced bending moments in piles; and wave equation analysis. Analysis & Monitoring: Water quality analysis; anchored and multi-braced retaining wall analysis; piping analysis; uplift analysis; heave analysis; filter design; relief well design; pile load test monitoring; noise and vibration monitoring; operation and interpretation of data obtained from A-E provided pile driver analyzer (PDA) or static pile load testing; and surveys/aerial photographic coverage to locate features and develop 3D survey information models, instrumentation for stream gaging activities, topographic maps, contour maps, profiles, and sections. (e) Instrumentation & Evaluation: Field and office instrumentation activities will involve: Surveying & Field Data Gathering: Surveying and instrumentation data gathering for specific features of existing civil works structures (e.g., survey cross-sections and profiles, settlement mark readings, joint movement readings, joint alignment readings, and piezometer readings). Surveys may include overbank, horizontal distances, and control data produced and submitted in compliance with New Orleans District survey standards and USACE Engineering Manuals (EMs). Firms must indicate their capability to utilize Global Positioning Systems (GPS), total stations, terrestrial scanners, and digital levels. Data Compilation: Compiling field data into appropriate digital formats for use in various software packages (e.g., Government-provided data collector programs, Government-provided cross-section plotting programs, and Excel spreadsheets with graphics). Drafting & Plotting: Producing CAD and Excel plots and plates from the compiled data. Analysis & Technical Reporting: Analyzing field data and preparing instrumentation evaluation reports containing site photographs and thorough site visit documentation compiled by professional engineers. Device Installation: Installing instrumentation devices such as piezometers, inclinometers, stream gages, and corrosion meters. (f) Levee Safety & Structural Periodic Inspections: Comprehensive planning, mobilization, execution, and reporting for critical infrastructure evaluations, consisting of: Levee Safety Inspections: Detailed systematic technical inspections and evaluations of the safety, stability, and operational adequacy of levees and earthen flood structures. Responsibilities include evaluating original design criteria against lifetime operational changes, compiling pre-inspection brochures, generating comprehensive Inspection Reports, and inputting final inspection data directly into the USACE Levee Inspection System (LIS). Structural Periodic Inspections: Technical evaluations of structural integrity and operational capacity across civil works assets including Navigation Locks, Pumping Stations, Floodgates, Control Structures, Drainage Structures, Floodwalls, Seawalls, Freshwater Diversion Structures, and specialized complex facilities such as the S.A. Murray Hydroelectric Power Station. 3. SELECTION CRITERIA: The selection criteria are listed below in descending order of importance. Criteria (a) through (d) are primary. Criteria (e) and (f) is secondary and will be used only as tiebreakers among technically equal firms. PRIMARY CRITERIA: (a) Specialized Experience and Technical Competence of the prime firm, joint venture partners, consultants, subcontractors and/or free-lance associates in the type of services specifically indicated in paragraph 2 Project Information above. (b) Professional Qualifications of the key design personnel, including professional registration in engineering, architecture and surveying, available to work on this contract in the following disciplines: Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, Hydraulic Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Corrosion Engineering, Environmental Engineering and Cost Engineering; Hydrologists, Geologists, Architecture, Naval Architecture, Surveying, Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) (Mapping and Analysis), Drafting via Computer Aided Design (Autodesk), 3-D Modeling CAD consisting of Building Information Modeling (BIM), and Civil Information Modeling (CIM) and Project Management. Demonstrate professional qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance of required services. The evaluation will consider the education, training, licensing, certification, professional registration, overall relevant experience, and longevity in the discipline and the firm. The A-E should indicate adequate project management personnel with required qualifications and experience to assure prompt response to all assignments. (c) Capacity to Accomplish the Work (personnel and equipment) Submittal must demonstrate the ability to perform numerous projects, at the same time, and complete work in a timely manner, regardless of unexpected equipment breakdowns, and/or personnel problems. Using all of the latest versions of commercial and software packages utilized by the Corps; produce geo-referenced CAD drawings in Autodesk format according to USACE CAD Standards; produce GIS products according to USACE GIS Standards; produce specifications; produce cost estimates in Micro-Computer Aided Cost Estimating System (MCACES) (MIl); perform soil borings and soil testing and analysis in accordance with the New Orleans District geotechnical criteria; perform land based surveys in accordance with New Orleans District Survey Standards; and provide the following minimum personnel: three structural engineers, three civil engineers, two geotechnical engineers, one hydraulic engineer, one cost engineer, one electrical engineer, two mechanical engineers, one corrosion engineer, one environmental engineer, one architect, one naval architect, one project manager, one registered land surveyor (to include State of Louisiana licensing) and one Autodesk CAD technician, one building information modeler, one civil information modeler, one hydrologist, one geologist, one GIS Analyst, two 3-person topographic survey crews, and one 2-person Global Positioning System (GPS) crew capable of performing various types of GPS Surveys. The prime must be capable of performing more than 50% of the task order work. (d) Past Performance of the A-E, joint venture partners, and key subcontractors with Government agencies, including Department of Defense and private industry with respect to cost control, quality of work, and compliance with performance schedules will be considered. And as determined by the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS). SECONDARY CRITERIA: (e) Knowledge of Locality: Refers to geological features, climatic conditions or local methods that are unusual or unique. Submittals must demonstrate knowledge of the locality within the limits of the New Orleans District and the boundaries or assignments of Mississippi Valley Division and demonstrate prior field data collection experience within Louisiana. (f) Small Business Commitment: Submittals must identify and commit to small businesses (SB) including small disadvantaged businesses (SDB) and historically black colleges and universities (HBCU) and minority institutions (MI) in the contract team. Commitment will be measured as a percentage of the total anticipated contract effort, regardless of whether the SB, SDB, HBCU or MI is a prime contractor, subcontractor, or joint venture partner. The greater the commitment the greater the consideration. 4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested firms that have the capability to perform the services described in this announcement are invited to submit one electronic copy (in PDF format) and five printed copies of the Standard Form 330 (SF 330) for the proposed team. The PDF shall be emailed to Veronica Garner-Flint Veronica.Garner-Flint@usace.army.mil and Cori A. Caimi Cori.A.Caimi@usace.army.mil. The five printed copies shall be mailed to the address below no later than 1400 hours central standard time on the closing date of this announcement. All firms responding to this solicitation MUST identify in which category they are submitting. Firms should state the words LARGE or SMALL BUSINESS after the solicitation number in Part 1, Block A.3 of the SF 330. Firms will be evaluated based on which category they are responding to in this solicitation. If a firm identifies as a Small Business (SB), it must specify a Small Business category or categories apply to it. Firms which do not specify a category applicable to their firm will be considered UNRESTRICTED for evaluation purposes. Include the firm’s Unique Entity Identifier in Block 5 of the SF 330, next to the name of the firm. If an A-E firm is currently registered in SAM, its SF 330 submitted in response to this announcement should include the applicable Commercial and Government Entity Code (CAGE). The SF 330 Part 1 must not exceed 100 pages (8.5 x 11-inch sheets), including no more than 50 pages for Section H. Each side of a sheet of paper is a page. Use font type no smaller than point size 11. Any pages greater than 100 pages will not be evaluated. Firms responding to this announcement after the closing date and time will NOT be considered. Required forms may be obtained on the Internet at: http://www.gsa.gov/portal/forms/type/TOP. Overnight or courier type of mail should be sent to the following address: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New Orleans District, Attn: Veronica Garner-Flint and Cori Caimi, Room 172, 7400 Leake Avenue, New Orleans, La 70118-3651. sig_cbb9280876598968a99b.description: This notice serves exclusively to conduct a non-binding market consultation in accordance with section 28 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on Public Procurement (VgV). The aim of the market consultation is to inform the market at an early stage about a potential future procurement requirement and to gather insights on technical, economic and organisational solution approaches, current market conditions, the competitive situation and the fundamental feasibility of the planned project. In particular, the market consultation serves to identify advantages and disadvantages of potential performance components, to record existing market experience and to examine whether and to what extent multiple companies can offer comparable services. In this way, a well-founded overview of market interest and the current competitive situation is to be obtained. The present notice is expressly neither a contract notice nor an invitation to submit tenders or requests to participate. No procurement procedure is initiated by conducting the market consultation. The contracting authority is not obliged to conduct a procurement procedure on the basis of the market consultation and is not bound by its results. Participation does not establish any legal claims whatsoever, in particular no claim to the conduct of a procurement procedure or to consideration in any potential subsequent procurement procedure. Participation in the market consultation is voluntary and free of charge. Participating companies will not be reimbursed for any costs incurred by them in connection with participation, the preparation of statements, concepts or the submission of documents. Participation in the market consultation is not a prerequisite for later participation in a procurement procedure and has no influence on a company's chances of being awarded the contract. The contracting authority requests interested market participants to provide meaningful, comprehensible and advanced feedback. In particular, comments on possible implementation variants, economic framework conditions, opportunities and risks, potential problems or obstacles in implementing the intended concept, as well as own ideas and suggestions for improvement are requested. Where possible, feedback should be provided in a structured format. Interested companies are requested to express their interest immediately and informally by email to ta-vergabestellevol@hu-berlin.de and to submit their statements, ideas, proposals for implementation and economic assessments. Following the evaluation of the submitted documents, selected interested parties may be invited to explain their concepts in more detail as part of a structured dialogue. This deepening can take place in the form of an on-site appointment or alternatively via video or telephone conference and serves to clarify open questions and to evaluate the impact of the proposed solution approaches on the requirements of the contracting authority. All documents submitted as part of the market consultation shall become the property of the contracting authority. By participating, interested parties agree that their submitted concepts, evaluations, proposals and other findings may be used to prepare a potential procurement and to develop implementation proposals and, to the extent necessary, may be passed on to the contracting authority, unless this is expressly objected to. Ideas and suggestions from market participants may, where applicable in anonymised form, become part of a later specification of requirements. The contracting authority guarantees the protection of business and trade secrets. Information obtained as part of the market consultation will not be passed on to third parties, with the exception of the contracting authority itself and, where applicable, consulting firms commissioned by it. The market consultation is to be carried out promptly and is expected to be concluded by February 2026. All submitted feedback will be evaluated and made available to the contracting authority in a consolidated form. Should the contracting authority initiate a procurement procedure based on the results of the market consultation, it will take appropriate measures to exclude any distortion of competition. These include in particular the equal treatment of all interested companies, the provision of relevant information to all applicants and tenderers, and the setting of appropriate deadlines. Anticipated schedule • Expression of interest to participate: immediately • Submission of initial concept: 30.01.2026 at 12.00 hours • Presentations and interviews: February 2026

FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). Lot LOT-0000: Procurement of a Hierarchical Storage Management System (HSM). The following service was put out to tender: The HSM system to be procured is intended to replace the hardware and software of the existing HSM system. Part of the procurement is also maintenance and support over a term of 5 years, with an optional extension by a further 2 years. The HSM system to be procured is intended to replace the hardware and software of the existing Crystalonyx Stronglink type HSM system in version 3.2. The existing data of currently approx. 230 PB (1 PB=10 to the power of 15 bytes), are distributed across approx. 56 million files, and are currently stored by the contracting authority in two hierarchy levels: in the first level in a hard disk cache with a storage capacity of 2,6 PB and in the second level on around 70.000 magnetic tape cartridges, which are distributed across several tape libraries stored at two locations. The existing tape library system is to continue to be used in the future. The contracting authority plans to procure a Hierarchical Storage Management System (HSM system) with a storage capacity of at least 1 EB (1000 PB), a throughput of at least 10 GB/s to 20 GB/s and an annual growth of approx. 40 PB. Operational readiness of the HSM system, including the migrated existing data, is to be established no later than 6 months after conclusion of the contract. The contractor shall in particular provide the following services: - Delivery and installation of a Hierarchical Storage Management System (HSM system) including the hardware for the operation of the HSM software and the storage of metadata as well as options for connecting the contracting authority's magnetic tape drives in the provided tape library system. The delivery of the first storage hierarchy level (cache for the tape archive) is included. In addition, storage capacity extensions should optionally be possible during the contract term. - Migration of the existing metadata from the existing Stronglink system and the previous HPSS system. It must be ensured that the data transfer process takes place without significant restriction of data availability. In any case, it must be ruled out that this restriction lasts longer than 7 days. The readability of the existing data in HPSS and LTFS tape formats must be guaranteed after migration. - Integration of the provided tape library systems of type SpectraLogic Tfinity/Cube and Oracle SL8500 into the HSM system, - Integration of the HSM system into the provided storage infrastructure (NFS and S3 interfaces) - Support, operational support and maintenance services over a period of 5 years with an option to extend by 2 further years. The following extensions, which were not previously provided for in the original tender documents, have been commissioned: The extension of the primary cache memory to initially 840 TB and subsequently through two additional primary cache memories with 120 TB each to a total of 1.080 TB. In this context, the extension also includes two additional FC switches. The subject matter of procurement as such remains unchanged; the scope of services to be delivered has been expanded.
sig_cc18ce18a8b80c32cf5d.title: Procurement of a Hierarchical Storage Management System (HSM) - Extension

sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.
sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'

sig_cc4a847712178a213cc1.description: Tipperary County Council intend to appoint technical consultants to conserve the Westgate building and review all options available for its reuse. The brief is to explore options for the future use of the building and to apply for funding for its restoration through any available funding channels. We are looking for a design team with experience in conservation works on protected structures. The proposed works relate to the conservation of the building fabric and the identification of its end use. Tipperary County Council have been monitoring the condition of the buildings and actively engaging in maintenance over the past two decades. The most recent significant works were completed in 2002-07 which focussed on the roof and (primary) dressed sandstone east and west facades. Tipperary County Council wishes to appoint a design team which includes a RIAI Grade 1 or 2 Conservation Architect/Conservation Engineer to guide the project through the development phases. Tipperary County Council intends to explore all viable redevelopment opportunities for the Westgate area in order to enhance its functionality, attractiveness, and contribution to the public realm. As part of this study, the Council is considering the potential acquisition of one of the adjoining properties—6 O’Connell Street or Grubbs Court—to enable the creation of a more cohesive and impactful design solution. The purpose of this commission is to assess the existing built context, identify redevelopment potential, and prepare a range of integrated layout options for the future use of Westgate and its adjoining properties.
sig_cc4a847712178a213cc1.title: Tipperary County Council Provision of Design Team Services by Tipperary County Council for the Westgate Refurbishment Plan in Clonmel

sig_cc552eda53f70b2c7526.description: Performance of IT software operation and support services for the Criminal Statistics System for a duration of 24 months. Performance of IT software operation and support services for the Criminal Statistics System (hereinafter: BSR) used for processing the data sets of the unified investigative authority and prosecution criminal statistics (hereinafter: ENyÜBS) for a duration of 24 months. The BSR is primarily aimed at data acquisition, monitoring, data processing necessary for the performance of statistical activities, as well as supporting the publication obligation. The current system is able to handle statistical data generated under both the old Criminal Code and the Criminal Code, since the old Criminal Code is applicable in cases where a milder sanction is established against the perpetrator. The data providers of the BSR are currently the police, the prosecution service, and the National Tax and Customs Administration. The BSR must be able to handle the return of TXTs to the submitting bodies. The BSR must be suitable for enabling the potential future integration of bodies not connected to the system in the current period. The data collections of the court and penal enforcement bodies joining at a later stage will also form the basis of the data scopes of the ENyÜBS system, but if data that needs to be collected also arises beyond these at the joining body, the system must also be able to handle them. • In alignment with the BSR base system, the successful tenderer must perform the following service: Support service with the following content for a duration of 24 months. • Part of the support comprises the code dictionaries of the BSR base system and software modifications resulting from changes to the legal environment, the handling and execution of data refinements necessary for authentic data provision in the files recorded previously, change testing and tasks related to the training on changes, with special regard to following the changes in the legislation serving as the basis of the system (Criminal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure). • The system must comply with the conditions defined in Act 2018 of LXXV on the accessibility of websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies, and Act 2022 of XVII on the general rules for compliance with accessibility requirements relating to products and services, and Interior Ministerial Order No 14/2024. following tasks: • ensuring the availability of the data set found in the current system (ENyÜBS) complying with Act 1978 of IV on the Criminal Code (old Criminal Code) and Act 2012 of C on the Criminal Code (Criminal Code), • on the basis of the code dictionaries and completion guidelines defined by the Criminal Statistics Working Group – which the Contracting Authority shall hand over to the Contractor upon the signing of this contract – IT operation support, minor modification and continuous IT monitoring of the relevant changes in the legal environment of the new BSR system in accordance with the conditions to be determined by the Contracting Authority, • operation support of the BSR system, • repair of errors not belonging to the scope of the warranty, developer modification of the existing system, • review of the relevant documentation or the service operation documentation and modification as necessary in the event of all changes affecting the BSR to be developed, • preparation of a monthly status report on announcements made by the Contracting Authority and on the work performed for the Contracting Authority (performance report), • repair of errors Procedures for awarding call-off orders The framework agreement will be awarded to the three best-ranked candidates, subject to a sufficient number of acceptable, regular and appropriate tenders. Call-off orders will be awarded according to the so-called cascade method without negotiation and without re-opening competition between the Awardees, after having communicated the expression of requirements. The expression of requirement is sent to the Awardee ranked in first position during the award of the framework agreement. If the first awardee cannot respond in accordance with the request or refuses to respond to it, the contracting authority turns to the second awardee, and so on until an awardee accepts the request. If, however, no Awardee can respond to the expression of requirement issued by the Client, the Client reserves the right to turn to another contract known as a “freelance contract” to respond to it. A complex solution is understood as a solution where the Customer has a need for the supplier's input to prepare the specific most suitable solution to meet the Customer's needs, and where the Customer has a need to be able to procure competencies in the form of advice, technical consultancy assistance to establish the solution, or assistance in the form of emergency cover in the event that faults occur in a network switch or similar. The procurement may, for example, be an acquisition of products for a new network, or telephony products for a new location. For these types of procurement, the Customer has a need for the supplier's assistance to identify the most suitable solution model, as well as a need for subsequent ongoing advice and/or other assistance in connection with a specific solution. sig_cc6a83c06ab3bffc7ac9.description: The tender concerns the procurement of a solution for the storage, searching and analysis of logging events. The contracting authority is tendering a contract for a solution for storage, searching and analysis in logging events. The log will contain events from vital systems such as firewalls, servers, systems and applications located both on-premise and in the cloud. The contracting authority's log sources send log events, primarily in Syslog format, to a central, physical log server located in one of AU's data centres near Aarhus. The local log server forwards to the solution and archives the incoming events in “flat”, compressed files for one year. The local log server is not part of the tendered solution. The purpose of this tender is to offer the contracting authority's existing on-premise logging system as a Software-as-a-Service solution, without physical installation at the contracting authority due to security considerations. A solution is desired where one can search freely in all stored events (‘find-the-needle-in-the-haystack’), rather than a SIEM solution that filters and condenses data (‘condense-the-haystack-to-the-needle’).
sig_cc6a83c06ab3bffc7ac9.title: Logging system

sig_cc90159df7fe88ce5be6.description: On the 7th of July 2025, the government published Giving every child the best start in life. ‘Giving every child the best start in life’ outlines how the government will improve child development and ensure that all children have the chance to achieve and thrive. To achieve the government’s overall mission objective of closing the opportunity gap, a milestone of a record proportion of children starting school ready to learn has been set. Progress will be measured through 75% of five-year-olds reaching a good level of development (GLD) in the early years foundation stage assessment by 2028. This assessment looks at children’s development across areas like language, personal, social and emotional development, and maths and literacy. This strategy pledges to deliver a “new evidenced-informed core offer for parents” of which a “digital parenting offer” will form one part. Requirement In line with this, the Department for Education (DfE) is seeking to engage with potential suppliers to share its early thinking, gain insight into the current market landscape for delivering an online parenting intervention and gather feedback to help shape the future delivery approach and inform potential procurement. The Department for Education is seeking a national, evidence-informed online parenting intervention to support families with children aged 0–5 across England, aiming to improve early childhood development and school readiness. The intervention should be accessible, inclusive, and scalable, offering high-quality digital support which can demonstrate positive impact on 3-4 year-old children’s socio-emotional / behavioural and/or communication outcomes, helping to achieve the 75% GLD milestone by 2028. For more information search for: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/giving-every-child-the-best-start-in-life https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/early-years-foundation-stage-framework--2 Important: This is a zero-value notice for early market engagement purposes only. It is not a call for competition and does not commit the Department to procuring, or procuring services in any specific way. Any future opportunities will be subject to budgetary decisions and the availability of funding. The DfE is keen to maximise opportunities to participate in procurement for Small to Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and Voluntary, Community and Social Enterprises (VCSEs). Consideration will also be given to consortia and collaborative bids from all forms of organisations. Lot 1: .
