sig_cc91da8dc7a256b11ed4.description:
The Defence Innovation Research Institute is seeking expert, developer, IT, mechanical engineer, and systems engineer capacities for the implementation of its R&D, innovation, and bespoke projects. The Contracting Authority has defined the expected tasks divided into five parts as follows: 1.) Further development of packaged engineering software 2.) Development of software according to bespoke requirements 3.) Complex project service for R&D or innovation development 4.) Design and/or manufacture of bespoke products and components 5.) Acoustic data collection and data analysis 1.) The task of the contractor for the further development of packaged engineering software part is to select and provide, from commercially available so-called 'packaged' software, the software or software suite most suitable for the given project in the form specified by the Contracting Authority. The contractor's task is to provide the version approved by the CA in various structures (e.g., software leasing / licence purchase / sale / partial ownership). Due to its typically R&D&I-related scope of activities, the CA typically needs engineering software and bespoke task-solving software (e.g. design, simulation, and development programmes). 2.) The task of the tenderer for the development of software according to bespoke requirements part is the complex development of software tailored to bespoke requirements. Due to the CA's R&D scope of activities, the Contracting Authority typically requires the development of engineering software in continuous cooperation with the Contracting Authority. (Contractor's task e.g. creation and development of hardware-controlling programmes based on XR - extended reality) 3.) The task of the contractor for the R&D or innovation development project service part is the provision of services related to innovation or technological development projects, such as prototype development, technological consultancy, as well as technical design, system integration, technical inspection (e.g. validation, certification), testing, and laboratory testing services. 4.) The task of the contractor for the design and/or manufacture of bespoke products and components part is the performance of design and project preparation services aimed at the production of bespoke products, including, for example, component manufacturing, assembly, construction, and integration. 5.) The task of the contractor for the acoustic data collection and data analysis part encompasses all those activities and technical solutions whose purpose is the recording, processing, mixing, amplification, and playback of sound, as well as the provision of the optimal solution related to sound in various projects that align with the VIKI R&D scope of activities and project objectives. Main elements: acoustic design and consultancy, provision of equipment park, commissioning and installation, sound engineering services, post-production, maintenance, and servicing. The contractor's task is to provide a specialist who is experienced in performing acoustic data collection and data analysis tasks. Information extending to all parts: As a result of this participation phase, the CA intends to set up the DPSs by category (part) for a duration of 36 months. The technical professional task descriptions issued in the individual tender stages may, in certain cases, implement investment, maintenance, upkeep, or R&D&I tasks in part (category) 5. As a result of this participation phase, the CA intends to establish the DPS for a duration of 36 months. In the individual tender stages, the subject of the procurement relates fundamentally to the ordering of services, but may in certain cases also contain goods procurement or construction (prototype construction) tasks. The bespoke tasks and works must in all cases be performed on the basis of the plans, summarised expectations, and other documentation, which may even be in a non-Hungarian language, issued as part of the tender stages following the conclusion of the participation phase. Pursuant to Section 107. (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the CA shall make the documentation necessary for performance, any determination of technical, specific, or special requirements, technological instructions, and the draft contract available (accessible) to the economic operators admitted to the DPS simultaneously with the sending of the invitation to tender. In appropriate cases, the IT may form part of professional protocols, usability instructions, or technical descriptions relevant to the given project compiled by the CA, which must be complied with during performance and its preparation. The CA emphasises that all working copies, partial data, and partial calculations generated during performance may constitute the business secret of the CA, and their disclosure or familiarisation to a third party is prohibited. As specified in Section 107. (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the CA shall make main contractual terms available to interested economic operators as part of the IT. Pursuant to Section 107. (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the CA shall subsequently make available (accessible) any plans, technical, specific, or special requirements, and the draft contract necessary for performance to the economic operators admitted to the DPS simultaneously with the sending of the IT. The CA reserves the right to issue an IT for the performance of multiple projects simultaneously. Procurement process: 1. Establishment of the DPS (participation phase): The CA establishes the DPS as a result of the participation phase. No tender may be submitted in the participation phase! 2. Following the establishment of the DPS, the CA shall send the invitation to tender to every economic operator admitted to the DPS and invite them to submit a tender. Pursuant to Section 106. (3) of the Public Procurement Act, any such economic operator may join the DPS during its validity period of 36 months. Pursuant to Section 106. (4) of the Public Procurement Act, Section 61. (4)-(6) shall not apply in the participation phase of the DPS. Pursuant to Section 107. (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the CA reserves the possibility to provide the option of submitting partial tenders during the implementation of the DPS in the tender stage. The CA reserves the possibility to utilise EU/domestic/other funding for the subject DPS.

Subject of procurement: Development of XR Hadik Skill training simulators covering the 3 area Technical content of the deliverable to be developed: Development of XR Hadik Skill training simulators covering the 3 area 1.) Knife defence training simulator (VR/MR-based training platform) 2.) Sniper testing training simulator running on an educational platform 3.) Combat Medic testing training simulator running on an educational platform Quantity of procurement: Software package consisting of 3 simulators as follows 1.) Knife defence training simulator (VR/MR-based training platform) VR/MR tactical knife defence simulator: The software is a standalone training platform that enables the practice of tactical knife defence in augmented reality (MR) and fully virtual (VR) environments. The purpose of the software is to develop realistic forms of movement, cutting arcs and reaction times for research and training purposes. The requirement is for the software to be optimised for the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. Within the scope of the procurement, the Tenderer is obliged to deliver: - 1 custom-developed VR/MR simulator software ensuring the practice of knife defence for fulfilling XR research objectives. - The software must include the dummy system capable of dynamic movement, the cut guidance support system, as well as the detailed telemetry and evaluation module. - The software must be delivered in files runnable on the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. 2.) Sniper testing training simulator running on an educational platform VR sniper simulator: The software is a standalone training platform that enables the acquisition and practice of the basics of long-range precision shooting in a virtual reality environment. The focus of the simulator is on ballistic calculations (vertical and horizontal corrections), the management of environmental factors (wind, distance), and the monitoring of the shooter's physiological state (heart rate). The requirement is for the software to be optimised for the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. Within the scope of the procurement, the Tenderer is obliged to deliver: - 1 custom-developed VR sniper simulator software ensuring the practice of tasks specifically for testing purposes in the environment specified by the Contracting Authority, for fulfilling basic XR research objectives. - The software must include ballistic training and practice modules. - The software must be delivered in files runnable on the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. 3.) Combat Medic testing training simulator running on an educational platform VR/MR battlefield first aid and equipment familiarity simulator: The software is a standalone training platform that enables the practice of basic battlefield casualty care techniques and the proficiency-level recognition of individual first aid kit (IFAK) equipment in a virtual reality environment. The purpose of the simulator is to teach casualty care protocols and equipment familiarity for research and training purposes. The requirement is for the software to be optimised for the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. Within the scope of the procurement, the Tenderer is obliged to deliver: - 1 custom-developed VR Combat Medic simulator software containing casualty care and equipment recognition tasks. - The software must include the battlefield casualty care and individual first aid kit equipment familiarity module. - The software must be delivered in files runnable on the Meta Quest 3/3S headset. Further requirements regarding the software are contained in the procurement documentation. With regard to the software, the Contracting Authority acquires an exclusive, restriction-free right of use for the territory of Hungary. The Contracting Authority is entitled to adapt the software and dispose of it. The Contracting Authority acquires a perpetual licence for the software. The given deliverable to be handed over must comply with the requirements relating to the environments, tasks, functionalities and other related elements defined in the given software specification. Solutions equivalent in technical content to that set out in the software specification shall be deemed acceptable provided that the following conditions are met: - implementation of the functional requirements, - fulfilment of requirements relating to performance, compatibility and user experience, - maintenance of system security, reliability and integrity. In determining equivalence, the Contracting Authority is entitled to decide on acceptability based on the developer's justification and documented proof. Time limit for performance: 60 calendar days from contract signature. Early performance is possible according to the contract. Further details are contained in the other procurement documents (technical and professional description).

sig_ccd8096515e55cfa43c4.description: Title: AI and Data Science Specialist Support – Health and Extreme Weather Project Agency: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Sub-Agency: National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC) Department: Critical Care Medicine Department (CCMD), Clinical Epidemiology Section NAICS Code: 541715 – Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) PSC: R425 – Support–Professional: Engineering/Technical Intended Source: University of Maryland, College Park (UMD), Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering Place of Performance: University of Maryland, College Park, Maryland Period of Performance: Period 1: October 15, 2026 – October 14, 2027 Period 2: October 15, 2027 – October 14, 2028 Response Deadline: October 8, 2026, at 6:00AM Eastern Time (ET) DESCRIPTION The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Critical Care Medicine Department (CCMD), Clinical Epidemiology Section intends to procure specialized Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science Specialist support for the NIH Health and Extreme Weather Intramural study. The Health and Extreme Weather study is a two-year project examining whether emergency department and hospital overcrowding worsens during extreme heat and how these conditions affect mortality. The project also seeks to apply artificial intelligence, including large language models (LLMs), to Emergency Medical Services (EMS) free-text narratives to identify patients with heat exposure that may not be captured through structured coding. The requirement involves specialized technical support in artificial intelligence, machine learning, large language models, data science, and analysis of large and heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Required support may include, but is not limited to: • Technical consultation and study support related to research questions, data feasibility, analytical approaches, and study/evaluation design; • Data preparation, exploratory analysis, information extraction, and development or adaptation of AI, machine-learning, and LLM methods; • AI/LLM prototyping, prompting, fine-tuning, workflow development, and comparison of alternative modeling approaches; • Evaluation design, reference-data development, performance assessment, error analysis, and generalizability and robustness testing; • Development and evaluation of scalable machine-learning pipelines and model-evaluation frameworks; and • Preparation of technical summaries, analyses, methods descriptions, figures, reports, presentations, and manuscripts as required by the project. INTENDED SOURCE The Government intends to procure these services from the University of Maryland, College Park (UMD), Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The Government's market research indicates that UMD possesses the specialized technical expertise required to support this effort. The proposed technical specialist possesses Ph.D.-level expertise in Electrical and Computer Engineering/Computer Science, with demonstrated experience in large-scale AI and foundation/language-model development and evaluation, scalable machine-learning pipelines, information extraction from unstructured text, and rigorous model-validation methodologies. The NIH Clinical Center's Critical Care Medicine Department also has an ongoing machine-learning/AI effort with the same UMD contractor. The Government intends to leverage the iterative learning, technical knowledge, and core algorithms already developed through that effort in support of this new AI requirement. This continuity is expected to reduce duplication of effort, conserve Government resources, and facilitate timely execution of the Health and Extreme Weather study. UMD's proximity to NIH also facilitates in-person technical collaboration and integration between the NIH Clinical Center's Clinical Epidemiology Section and UMD's AI/ML expertise. NOTICE OF INTENT This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations. The Government intends to procure the required services from the University of Maryland, College Park. However, all responsible sources that believe they possess the specialized technical capabilities necessary to satisfy the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement for consideration. Interested parties must provide sufficient information demonstrating their ability to perform the complete requirement. At a minimum, capability statements should address: Company/organization name, address, Unique Entity ID (UEI), and point of contact; Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 541715; Demonstrated Ph.D.-level expertise in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related discipline; Demonstrated experience developing and evaluating large-scale AI, machine-learning, foundation-model, and/or large-language-model technologies; Demonstrated experience developing scalable machine-learning pipelines and rigorous model-evaluation frameworks; Experience applying AI/ML methods to healthcare, clinical, EMS, or other large heterogeneous datasets; Experience performing information extraction from unstructured text and evaluating model generalizability and robustness; and Sufficient information demonstrating the ability to satisfy the requirement within the required period of performance. Capability statements must be received no later than October 8, 2026, at 6:00 AM Eastern Time (ET) and emailed to shasheshe.goolsby@nih.gov. Telephone calls are not acceptable. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether conducting a competitive procurement is appropriate. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. .

sig_ccde6c4e8da0ef3e6e74.description: This notice is not a contract notice nor a request for tenders, but a prior information notice and a notice of the implementation of a dialogue as part of the preparation of the procurement. This may mean dialogue meetings, commenting on written material and answering questions from the contracting authority. This prior information notice and invitation to dialogue does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual tendering procedure. The description presented in the prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice are preliminary and indicative prior information. Answering or failing to answer the request for information does not prevent participation in a potential tendering procedure. The information provided in the dialogue does not bind either party. The names or other details of the companies participating in the dialogue will not be published. The contracting authority is preparing the procurement of a payroll service package. The subject of the procurement is primarily a service, but the system package required to produce the service can also alternatively be considered in the procurement. Currently, the service is produced using the Populus system, for which the contracting authority has a separate, own contract. For the sake of clarity, it is stated that Sipoo produces HR services as its own operation, with the exception of payroll and system superuser duties, and the aforementioned system is also in use in the provision of these services. The aim of the dialogue is to survey various production method alternatives under the following boundary conditions: 1. The service is produced utilising the client's system (Populus) and taking responsibility for its superuser role, i.e., the service provider is responsible for producing the overall service, but the system environment is based on the client's current solution. 2. The service is produced using an overall solution offered by the supplier, i.e., the service is produced using a system offered by the supplier, including the necessary software and service package, including the implementation project for the solution, rights of use, and ongoing services directed at the solution. The contracting authority currently considers option 1 as the primary implementation method, taking into account costs and the scale of use of the current system.

sig_ccece535a5eee65bcbc2.description: DHSC will be hosting two virtual roundtable events, led by the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Health Innovation, on the “Living with Cancer” agenda to discuss how employers and other organisations can better support people to remain in or return to work following a cancer diagnosis and treatment, with a particular focus on the challenges faced by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and spreading best practice across sectors of the economy. The roundtables will take place on: • Tuesday, 27th October 2026, 09:30-10:30 GMT • Tuesday, 3rd November 2026, 09:30-10:30 GMT To register your organisation’s interest in one of these events, please complete the following registration form by Tuesday, 20th October 2026 at 11:59 pm: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=MIwnYaiRMUyMH-9N6Jc6HHkA63U0d81Ht4WY0oa7NW1UNFZKVktHMU9ZWVhIT01GNDRKMU0zTE9aVS4u Attendance is restricted to one person per organisation. The National Cancer Plan for England recognises the impact that cancer can have on people’s working lives and sets out an ambition to work with employers and impact economy investors to raise awareness of effective interventions, scale good practice and make support more accessible. Too many people are forced to stop working due to cancer. Around 830,000 working age people are living with cancer in England. Cancer can have a significant impact on people’s finances and ability to remain in work: people hospitalised with cancer face nearly £5,000 in lost income, while patients lose an average of 75 days of work across their pathway. People living with cancer are not always able to access interventions that are known to be useful. Through engagement on the National Cancer Plan, we have heard charities, larger companies and practitioners already know which interventions can help people living with cancer to remain in and return to work. However, some sectors of the economy still find it difficult to proactively offer support due to a lack of awareness or easily accessible tools. These challenges are often faced by sectors of the economy which account for a large share of employment, including SMEs. DHSC is therefore seeking to work with purpose-driven businesses, charities and the impact economy to help raise awareness, scale effective interventions and make them more accessible. The Ministerial roundtables will provide an opportunity to hear from organisations about existing approaches, the challenges they face and where collaboration between different organisations could help scale effective support. Lot 1: .

sig_cd03c6b8b3a4d1756370.description: NIFRS currently have Mobile Data Terminals (MDTs) installed on-board frontline fire appliances. These are ruggedised computer terminals with touchscreen capabilities used by NIFRS to provide information to enhance Firefighter safety and deliver real-time GPS location, incorporating status updates in terms of appliance availability. They have become an integral part of how information supports operational decision making on the incident ground. MDTs are a vital piece of equipment to access risk critical information associated with site specific surveys carried out by NIFRS personnel. They are linked to the NIFRS Regional Control Centre (RCC) via the PSNI 'Barracuda' secure radio network and updated whilst on-station via the secure Wi-Fi network. Mobile data software is currently used by Firefighters on board fire appliances and by RCC personnel to deliver Firefighter safety critical information and situational awareness to support decision making and more effective communication. The solution is integrated with various other NIFRS systems which include Fire & Rescue Service databases and Risk Critical Information. Using the MDTs, precise and relevant situational intelligence is available to operational personnel at the touch of a button via a range of intelligence databases on route to incident and at the incident ground. NIFRS are seeking to replace their Mobile Data Solution to include an update on all hardware, software, support and maintenance components for up to approximately 160-310 terminals. NIFRS hope to approach the market with a formal PME questionnaire by March 2026, please note this will not be used to pre qualify the market. It will used to help formulate the specification and business case. If your orgasantion would be interested in taking part in a PME please email Dawn Bradley on NIFRSprocurement@nifrs.org by 5pm 20th Feb 2026. Lot 1: .

sig_cd1fb3436de8a923c95c.description: The subject of the specifications is the development of the existing GIS database by introducing the collected technical data and Stereo 70 geographical coordinates surveyed for the overhead and underground electrical networks related to investment works and introducing them into the existing GIS system, in order to constitute the GIS database belonging to SC Distributie Energie Oltenia SA. The purpose of the procurement is the development of the database by collecting in the field the objects and attributes (from Annex 5 of the Specifications) and introducing them into the existing GIS system for the distribution networks in Dolj, Gorj, Arges, Mehedinti, Olt, Teleorman and Valcea counties following investment works. The developments of the existing GIS database to be procured in accordance with the provisions of the Specifications and the related Annexes consist of: a) Collection from the field of Stereo 70 geographical coordinates and the related technical attributes for all objects in Specifications - Annex 5 related to the new overhead and underground networks as well as the related modifications to existing electrical networks resulting from investment works; b) Labelling of investment works in accordance with the specifications mentioned in Annex 2 of the Specifications; c) Processing of the collected data in order to introduce them into the existing GIS system; d) Introduction into the existing ArcGIS 10.8.1 application of the collected data (Stereo 70 geographical coordinates, objects, technical attributes) following investment works, into the data model used by Distributie Energie Oltenia SA, a model composed of objects with attributes, in accordance with Annex 5, attached to the Specifications; e) Introduction into the existing ArcGIS 10.8.1 application of the data made available by DEO (Stereo 70 geographical coordinates, objects, technical attributes), data which can be found in the CLOUD application, for investment works; f) Drawing up of documentation for the approval of the service in accordance with the methodology in Specifications - Annex 4 Methodology for topo GIS data surveying and in accordance with the specifications from point 4.3 of the Specifications. In order to fulfil the activities mentioned in section II.1.4 of this documentation, the Contracting entity estimates within the Specifications under ch. 3.1 Minimum Quantity and Maximum Quantity / framework agreement as well as Minimum Quantity and Maximum Quantity / subsequent contract. The duration of the framework agreement is 36 months. Subsequent contracts are projected to be concluded with a biannual frequency.
sig_cd1fb3436de8a923c95c.title: Development of existing GIS database for distribution networks in Dolj, Gorj, Arges, Olt, Teleorman, Mehedinti and Valcea counties as a result of investment works

sig_cd484e5965c26067c89e.description: OBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The object of the procurement is support services for railway data management, which includes, among other things, the following tasks: - The supplier coordinates and develops the services required for quality management of railway infrastructure data in support of the contracting authority and railway data maintenance operators, and prepares analyses on the quality of railway data. - The supplier participates in supporting the contracting authority in the development of railway data analytics reporting. - The supplier supports the contracting authority in the creation, contacting and activation of a network of railway data maintainers and users. - The supplier supports the contracting authority in the planning, preparation and implementation of training for new versions of railway data systems and other railway data services. - The supplier supports the contracting authority in communication related to railway data management in accordance with the communication plan agreed with the contracting authority. - The supplier supports the contracting authority in the management and production of official instructions and other guidelines related to railway data maintenance. GENERAL Please note that this is an invitation to a market survey (hereinafter the notice), and this notice does not yet request tenders. All information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as the preparation progresses. Hansel Oy acts in a consultative role in the tendering process. REGISTRATION You can register for the market survey by filling in the form in the "Other information" section of this notice in the Tender Service and sending it to the contracting authority by the deadline of 27.11.2026 at 12.00. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the possibility to send draft material of the tender to the registered tenderers for written comment in a so-called market dialogue during November-December 2025.

sig_cd4fea7587bda4826502.description: 1 db TSM IT system operation support service under a framework agreement. Framework amount: 5.940.000.000 HUF Contracting Authority is proceeding in accordance with point a) of subsection 105 (1) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.). 1 pc TSM IT system operation support service under a framework agreement, Framework amount: 5.940.000.000 HUF. The aim of the procurement is to involve expert operation support for 36 months in order to continuously ensure the high-priority availability of 7X24 hour operation of the TSM system. The TSM system currently supports transport authority inspections based on data from a total of 89 points nationwide, 106 measurement locations, in 274 bands, via approximately 1500 WIM sensors (measuring instruments). Tasks: ML 2.1. Expert support ensuring continuous availability: Following the submission of a support service request by the Contracting Authority, the Tenderer shall commence the execution of the task specified in the request within 2 days following the day of the relevant request. The tasks expected within the scope of expert support are detailed in the technical specification. ML.2.2. Incident management, bug fixing: It is the Tenderer's obligation to ensure for the Contracting Authority with continuous availability, in 7X24 hours, that incident and bug reports sent to the Tenderer's notification email address and direct telephone contact are continuously received, registered, and necessary measures are taken as follows. - Software bug fixing (L2): The Tenderer is obliged to fix software bugs arising in the TSM system that cause an incident. The Tenderer shall perform the fixing of incident-causing software bugs as an expert performing second-level (L2) troubleshooting. - Provision of expert support for L3 level software bug fixing: The Tenderer is obliged to provide expert support for the L3 level bug fixing of incident-causing software bugs in the event of a request to this effect by the Contracting Authority. - Enhanced troubleshooting service (incident management): The Tenderer acts as a fourth-level (L4 – manufacturer or developer support) troubleshooting expert in order to troubleshoot bugs, incidents, and problems arising in the system components of the transport authority system - operated by the Contracting Authority - listed in the TSM System Plan, to support application operations, and to ensure the further development of the entire application environment. During troubleshooting, the provision of expert capacity and the troubleshooting of the bug are the tasks of the Tenderer. ML.2.3. Preparation of developments: In the event of a development request concerning modifications necessary in the TSM system based on legislative changes, the Tenderer assesses the change requests, plans the application modification tasks resulting from the indicated changes, prepares the development specification, and draws up a development schedule regarding the handover or introduction of modifications towards the Contracting Authority. For the preparation of the development specification, the Winning Tenderer is expected to possess comprehensive knowledge of the relevant transport authority legislation in order to ensure the full-scale functionality of the TSM system, with particular regard to the necessity of knowing the processes evaluating data recorded by axle load scales forming part of the system, as well as other road traffic or vehicle parameterisation devices possibly to be integrated into the system. ML.2.4. Expert consultancy: Consultancy on the planning of administrative and IT changes affecting the TSM system, which covers the interoperability of software evaluating data recorded by axle load scales connected to the TSM system or other road traffic or vehicle parameterisation devices to be interfaced with the TSM system. Technologies and services used by the supported system: Network elements: LAN, SAN Execution infrastructure: Oracle DBMS, Oracle Exadata (running database environment), HP infrastructure (running productive and test environments) Server operating systems: • Red Hat Linux • Oracle Linux server Database managers: • Oracle (RAC/Grid and standalone) 10, 11, 12c Virtualisation technologies: • ASX Network services: - DHCP, - DNS, - ARP, - VPN, - RDP, - SSH. Security class of the system (according to 41/2015. (VII. 15.) BM Decree): 3-as Tasks in detail: in the Technical Specification. The Contracting Authority intends to order the tasks set out in points ML.2.1. and 2.2. within the framework of a monthly flat-rate service. The Contracting Authority undertakes to call off the TSM IT system operation support service pursuant to points ML.2.1. and 2.2 for a total of 12 months.
sig_cd4fea7587bda4826502.title: TSM operation support

(SAP ECC 6.0 as well as SAP S/4HANA)" Lot LOT-0001: Software for test data management. The aim of this call for competition is the procurement and introduction of forward-looking, general software for the test data management of VBL. In the coming years, changes will occur within the SAP system landscape at VBL due to the planned introduction of SAP S/4HANA, which require new software for test data management. Training measures as well as additional days of services for support are an essential component of the contract to be awarded for the introduction of the advertised software.

sig_cd77cd1a49240d1fc5a5.description: The procedure has as its object the procurement of CONNECTIVITY COMMUNICATIONS services - CPV code 72318000-7, which will materialise through the conclusion of three framework agreements relating to the lots below, for a period of 48 months. The procurement procedure is divided into the following 3 lots: - Lot no. 1 – Level 2 connections – primary and secondary - Lot no. 2 – Interurban connections - Lot no. 3 – Standard G.652, G.657, G.655 "dark fiber" type connections The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification by the 11-th day before the deadline for submitting tenders, for clarifications received at least 18 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The minimum and maximum quantities of Level 2 primary and secondary connections (LOT 1) estimated to be procured during the framework agreement are a minimum of 3.000 connections - a maximum of 16.000 connections. The procurement will materialise through the conclusion of a framework agreement for a period of 48 months, with all economic operators declared admitted following the application of the award criterion. The minimum and maximum quantities of national interurban connections (LOT 2) estimated to be procured during the framework agreement are a minimum of 1 connection - a maximum of 50 connections. The minimum and maximum quantities of national interurban connections (LOT 2) to be procured under a single subsequent contract are a minimum of 1 connection - a maximum of 13 connections. The estimated value of the largest subsequent contract, determined on the basis of the maximum quantities estimated to be procured under a single subsequent contract, specified above, is 78.000,00 euros excluding VAT for LOT 2. During the performance of the framework agreement, it is estimated that subsequent contracts will be awarded as follows: 1 subsequent contract in the year 2024, 1 subsequent contract in the year 2025, 1 subsequent contract in the year 2026 and 1 subsequent contract in the year 2027.; Standard G.652, G.657, G.655 “dark fiber” type connections (LOT 3) will be procured - CPV code 72318000-7, necessary for connecting user terminal points to the points of presence of the Special Telecommunications Service. The procurement will materialise through the conclusion of a framework agreement for a period of 48 months, with all economic operators declared admitted following the application of the award criterion. The minimum and maximum quantities of standard G.652, G.657, G.655 “dark fiber” type connections (LOT 3) estimated to be procured during the framework agreement are a minimum of 1 connection - a maximum of 150 connections. The minimum and maximum quantities of standard G.652, G.657, G.655 “dark fiber” type connections (LOT 3) to be procured under a single subsequent contract are a minimum of 1 connection - a maximum of 38 connections. The contract is co-financed from the FENIKS Programme 20212027. Project objective: prevention, mitigation and reduction of the impact of threats related to forest fires. The subject of the contract is the delivery, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system, equipment co-financed under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change prevention, mitigation and reduction of the impact of threats related to forest fires (PPOŻ2). sig_cdccf3cfbb832c88f7fb.description: The Artificial Intelligence Security Institute (AISI), a directorate of the former Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), is seeking information from the market to help test the feasibility, deliverability, and commercial attractiveness of a proposed requirement for the AISI Grants Portfolio. The AISI funds external research through competitively awarded grant programmes. Awards are made to universities, research institutes and non-profit organisations. The Authority currently administers grants in-house and is considering whether a specialist delivery partner could provide all or part of the post-award administration function for future grant programmes. This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to inform the Authority's understanding of market capability and delivery models. This engagement does not constitute a procurement process and places no obligation on either the Authority or participating suppliers. The Authority's current portfolio comprises approximately: • £20m of live grant funding; • around 100 active grants; • individual grants ranging between £100,000 and £1,000,000; • typical grant durations of 6 to 24 months. Future programmes are expected to be broadly similar in nature, although scope, scale and delivery models may change. The grants are primarily research-focused and commonly involve: • UK universities; • overseas universities; • research organisations; • non-profit entities; • collaborative research projects. The Authority is seeking information on supplier capability to deliver post-award grant administration services. For the purposes of this engagement, "post-award" includes all activities following the Authority's funding decision, including due diligence activities conducted prior to execution of grant agreements. The assessment of applications, evaluation of proposals and selection of grant recipients will remain the responsibility of the Authority and its expert reviewers and are not within scope. Accountability for each grant remains with the Authority under GovS 015: Grants. Any operating model will retain the Authority's grant manager in a decision-making role, with defined thresholds for what a delivery partner may decide and what must be escalated. Potential activities may include, but are not limited to: • issuing and executing grant agreements using Authority-provided templates; • managing amendments, variations, novations and extensions; • managing monitoring and reporting processes; • validating claims and expenditure submissions; • administering payment schedules and disbursements; • administering grants to overseas recipients; • managing underspend, reprofiling and no-cost extensions; • supporting suspension, recovery and clawback activity; • operating assurance, audit and counter-fraud controls; • maintaining grant records and management information; • undertaking grant closure activities and record retention. The Authority is keen to receive feedback from established grant-administration providers, specialist organisations, SMEs, new entrants and other organisations with relevant delivery experience. The Authority currently anticipates that, should it decide to proceed with a procurement following this preliminary market engagement, the opportunity would be conducted through the Fund Administration & Disbursement Services Dynamic Purchasing System, RM6322 (“FAADS”). You do not need to be an existing supplier on the Fund Administration & Disbursement Services DPS, RM6322 (“FAADS”), to respond to this market engagement. Suppliers that are not currently appointed to RM6322 are encouraged to consider applying to join the DPS if they may be interested in participating in any future procurement. Further information about RM6322 and the supplier application process is available through the Crown Commercial Service Supplier Registration Service: Fund Administration & Disbursement Services DPS (FAADS) - GCA The RM6322 application process and this RFI are independent: • completing the RFI does not result in appointment to the DPS; • applying to the DPS does not constitute an RFI response; and • neither activity guarantees that a procurement will proceed or that an organisation will receive work. RFI responses are requested solely to help the Authority understand market capability, delivery models, commercial viability, risks and implementation considerations. Responses will not be scored and participation will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in a future procurement. The Authority does not guarantee that a procurement will take place or that RM6322 will ultimately be used. Lot 1: . None
sig_cdccf3cfbb832c88f7fb.title: RFI: AISI - Post-Award Research Grant Administration

sig_cde1f904743a2e1a716f.description: The ministries currently have different ICT platforms for providing digital services. A decision has been made to establish a joint ICT platform, hereafter called the New System, and phase out the four existing unclassified platforms (DSS, the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Services, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Defence). A new system shall be delivered to the customers that have always been decided that DIO shall provide services for. The current ICT platforms handle a total of approx. 7,000 users, of which approx. 1,800 users are at approx. 100 international foreign stations. Much of the application portfolio is based on standard tools, such as MS SharePoint, MS Exchange, MS Office, SakArkiv (P360 and WebSak), etc., but there are also some heavier ministry specific applications. More than 300 applications have been identified, of which the size of one quarter includes a central server component. The operation and maintenance of the current ICT platforms mostly occurs internally, but parts of the applications and platforms in the last couple of years have been moved to public cloud services. The establishment and implementation of the New System will be gradually and is expected to be carried out over a transitional period of 2-3 years before the existing platforms are phased out. The new system shall be based on a hybrid system design that can offer services from a dedicated/private infrastructure and from public/public cloud services. A new system shall be able to offer services that fulfil the requirements for screened, unclassified information systems and other unclassified information systems. DIO would like to enter into a framework agreement with one tenderer to carry out a zero point measurement and the possibility for subsequent measurements of the safety condition. The measurement shall be based on a recognised method and a standardised framework. Using a framework allows for comparable results across measurement periods so that the maturity of security measures can be evaluated over time. The measurements and recommended measures shall be used for DIO's work with continual improvement.
sig_cde1f904743a2e1a716f.title: Procurement of measuring the safety condition.

sig_ce0671a3764c02cb0c88.description: This procurement is being conducted by the Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) on behalf of the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC) who are the Contracting Authority as defined in Section 2 of the Procurement Act 2023. This Invitation to Participate has been issued by MOPAC who are seeking to award a Contract for the provision and maintenance of a Progressive Web Application for ProtectUK, a website and digital learning platform that provides advice, guidance and information on protective security for venues and public spaces across the United Kingdom. ProtectUK is a national counter terrorism and protective security platform delivered by Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP). It provides authoritative guidance, learning, threat awareness, preparedness support to those responsible for venues and public spaces, businesses, and organisations in the private and public sector. The platform enables users to strengthen their protective security and operational resilience, prepare for and respond to terrorist incidents, access online learning and best-practice guidance, and maintain awareness of the current UK terrorism threat level. This invitation to tender presents a strategic opportunity to shift from a period of technical stabilisation to one focused on enhanced user experience, innovative content design, and improved technical resilience, working closely with the National Counter Terrorism Security Office (NaCTSO) and key counter terrorism specialists. Over the next four years, development of the ProtectUK platform will focus on: - Increasing overall user engagement and site traffic. - Diversifying content to reflect legislative developments and new target audiences. - Improving technical infrastructure to support performance, integrations, scalability, security and future digital capabilities. - Strengthening ProtectUK/NaCTSO branding and national visibility. - Enhancing analytics and insights to measure the impact of ProtectUK on user learning and protective security knowledge. - Ensure WCAG, GDPR compliance requirements are met. Bidders must be UK based - all services and support under this Agreement must be supplied from a permanent place of business located within the UK. Personnel must hold BPSS and developers with system access must hold NPPV3/SC vetting. This must already be in place or be in place by contract award. Lot 1: .

sig_ce2aa5ec0d7f3197d0f9.description: The Department of Health and Social Care is seeking to commission an external partner to produce an independent written report on the impact that a childhood diagnosis of critical illness has on families. This work supports the government’s wider commitment to expanding mental health and wellbeing provision under the 10 Year Health Plan, where identifying and supporting groups at risk is a key part of effective early intervention. The report (Hugh’s Report) will generate a robust evidence base to inform policy decisions on how best to strengthen support for affected families. It will examine the mental health needs of parents, guardians and siblings, assess the availability and effectiveness of current support, and highlight where gaps or barriers exist so that future interventions can be better targeted. Key Deliverables Identify evidence on the mental health impact of a critical illness diagnosis of a child on their families. Determine what forms of emotional and psychological support affected families need. Assess whether the needs and barriers for families of critically ill children differ from other groups with mental health needs. Examine the cost, accessibility and effectiveness of existing interventions supporting these families. Provide recommendations for: Further research areas, data sources or data collection needed. Practical, actionable next steps based on what works. Improvements to existing support. This is not a call for competition, but an opportunity to gather feedback to better understand market capabilities, refine final specifications, decide the procurement strategy, and encourage supplier engagement. Lot 1: .
sig_ce2aa5ec0d7f3197d0f9.title: DHSC: Mental Health Impact on Families with Critically Ill Children Report 2026

sig_ce46f7484795154d639f.description: Grid Research Integration and Deployment Center Technology Collaborations for US Power Electronics Industries Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is seeking industry partners to participate in short-term, collaborative projects within the Grid Research Integration and Deployment Center (GRID-C) to accelerate development and deployment of grid integrated power electronics technologies. This opportunity will provide selected participants access to ORNL's experienced staff and unique equipment and capabilities to demonstrate advanced concepts with intent to develop and deploy innovative and energy efficient power electronics for electrified grid integration and modernization. Description UT-Battelle, LLC, acting under its Prime Contract No. DE-AC05-00OR22725 with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) for the management and operation of the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, conducts research and development in support of the DOE Transformer Resilience and Advanced Components (TRAC) Program of the Office of Electricity (OE). The DOE TRAC program partners with industry, small business, universities, and other stakeholders to identify and invest in innovative technologies with the potential to accelerate the integration of grid systems and clean energy resources through power electronics technologies, as well to enhance the global competitiveness of the United States. ORNL is requesting cost-shared proposals from industry to develop next generation technologies for grid modernization to support the mission of OE and TRAC for reliable, resilient, and secure electricity delivery systems. As part of the proposals submitted under this announcement, the proposers are expected to describe the enabling technologies as well as potential energy savings and novel non-energy impacts that may be realized by the targeted project. Technology areas of interest Materials & Components: for grid devices, power electronics systems, grid storage devices Embedded Controllers: integrated advance analog and digital electronics, sensing devices Subsystems Devices and Interfaces: Converter, Inverter, controls and protection, prototypes, solid state components protection, transformers Resource Integration & Management Systems: Mutli-stage converters, Software Platforms, Algorithms Grid systems Architecture: real time systems modelling and evaluation Grid Modelling and Transient Analysis Projects will be conducted during a short-time period. At least 20% cost share, which can be funds-in to ORNL or in-kind contributions (e.g., facilities, services, and staff time), is required on the part of the industrial participant. Participant cost-share cannot be met using funds from U.S. Government sources. Funds will not be provided to the industrial participant by ORNL. The intent is to increase the in-kind cost share from 20% to 50% in the future, that timing to be determined and approved by the TRAC program. Note: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT REQUEST. Eligibility Eligibility is limited to industries that currently manufacture in the U.S. for commercial applications in the residential or commercial grid hardware and power electronics market, or to industries that will be able to do so as a direct result of these collaborative efforts. There is no restriction based on the component or grid technology area, but should align with facilities, expertise, and capabilities of ORNL’s GRID-C. Background The Grid Research Integration and Deployment Center (GRID-C) at ORNL offers access to distinctive world-leading capabilities bringing together electrification for utilities, buildings, and transportation sectors to support integration of grid systems and clean energy resources as well as leveraging advanced manufacturing capabilities at ORNL’s Manufacturing Demonstration Facility (MDF). GRID-C embodies this combination with research and development in power and energy system, power electronics, components, controls, real-time platforms, simulation, modeling, and cybersecurity to provide a vertical integration to support demonstration of modernization, security, and resiliency for grid systems integration and clean energy resources. ORNL’s expertise in power electronics and controls, materials, and hardware/software integration will assist the power electronics industries in accelerating the improvement existing and developing new innovative technologies. More information about the ORNL Grid-C can be found at: https://www.ornl.gov/content/grid-c-labs From concept to commercialization, ORNL's world-leading facilities and expertise enable research focused on reducing the energy intensity of U.S. industry, supporting development of new products, and strengthening our nation's clean energy economy to meet the commercial and national security needs of tomorrow. Objective The objective of these GRID-C Technical Collaborations is to collaborate with industry to investigate, improve, develop, and deploy innovative integrated and resilient grid resources for further intelligent electrification at the grid interfaces. In so doing, creating and preserving domestic jobs is a goal of this solicitation. The primary focus of this announcement is to target projects that will impact the following technical areas: Materials & Components: for grid devices, power electronics systems, grid storage devices Embedded Controllers: integrated advance analog and digital electronics, sensing devices Subsystems Devices and Interfaces: Converter, Inverter, controls and protection, prototypes, solid state components protection, transformers Resource Integration & Management Systems: Mutli-stage converters, Software Platforms, Algorithms Grid systems Architecture: real time systems modelling and evaluation Grid Modelling and Transient Analysis Within these technical areas, the target projects could be related to hardware or software design, application or use case development, modeling and simulation for impact of system integration, test and evaluation of proposed technology, controls, or solutions, or small-scale prototyping in a relevant environment. Laboratory Support It is anticipated that industrial partners will work collaboratively with members of the ORNL staff to conduct project activities across the various areas of expertise within GRID-C. Intellectual Property and Proprietary Data Projects will be performed with a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) as the contract instrument. See the announcement package for a sample CRADA agreement. DOE and ORNL respect the importance of industry's intellectual property and data security while balancing the need to document the benefits of public expenditures. Provisions relating to proprietary information and intellectual property are set forth in the CRADA. A Non-Disclosure agreement (NDA), if required, can be put into place during development of the project to facilitate discussions while protecting the partner's proprietary information. It is preferred that proprietary information NOT be included in the proposal. If company proprietary information is included in the proposal, the specific information should be marked as such, and UT- Battelle/ORNL will treat that information as business confidential. Proposal Guidelines Proposals should be completed using the attached template in the announcement package. Proposers are encouraged to consult with ORNL technical staff to develop a work scope that is technically feasible and compatible with ORNL facilities and capabilities. Proposal Deadline and Submission This announcement will remain open subject to availability of funding from the DOE Transformer Resilience and Advanced Components Program. Completed proposals must be submitted in PDF file format by email to GRIDCcollaborations@ornl.gov. The subject line should include: ORNL GRID-C Technology Collaborations. Receipt of proposals will be confirmed within one week of submission. Proposal Evaluation and Timeline This is an open announcement. Selection of winning proposals will be at the discretion of the DOE TRAC. Proposal evaluation criteria will include compatibility with ORNL facilities and capabilities, technical feasibility and merit, the potential to commercialize new products and create US jobs, and the potential for improvement to grid components, electrification, and integration. TRAC reserves the right to select all, a portion, or none of the submissions. Point of Contact All questions relating to this announcement should be directed to Dr. Madhu Chinthavali by email, chinthavalim@ornl.gov, or by phone, (865) 341-1411. Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) Information Awardees are required to enter into a short-form CRADA with UT-Battelle. Because of the need for accelerated placement and execution of the projects, the most favorable terms allowable within DOE guidelines have been established and will not be subject to negotiation. Failure to enter into a CRADA in a timely manner will result in termination of further project consideration. CRADAs have provisions that address the protection of the partners' existing proprietary information and intellectual property, as well as the information and intellectual property generated and made during the collaboration. More specifically, each party owns its own inventions while jointly developed inventions will be jointly owned. In all cases, U.S. Government will retain government use rights. CRADA durations are expected to be at least one year. For more specific terms and conditions, please review the model short-form CRADA attached to this announcement.

sig_ce63b02c843152f0cfc1.description: Extension of the eConsent Pro patient information software by modules for digitalisation Description of the initial situation: Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein uses the eConsent Pro solution from the provider Thieme to inform patients in a legally compliant manner about treatments, procedures and anaesthesia. The standard provided information sheets are established in everyday clinical practice. Description of the target vision: The contracting authority is pursuing the objective of digitising the patient information process. The established sheets are to be reused in terms of content. In addition, patients are to be enabled to access information sheets via the contracting authority's patient portal that have been previously assigned to them by clinical staff. In this way, patients are to be able to deal with treatments in advance of their hospital stay, fill out the sheets in advance and note questions. After the sheets have been discussed together in the respective information discussion, the sheets are to be signed in a legally secure manner digitally on tablets and then transferred to the hospital information system (KIS). Justification for the product-specific procurement: So that the procedures in the hospitals continue to function well, the content of the information sheets is not to be changed. The information process is merely to be digitised and the sheets subsequently transmitted in digital form to the KIS. Market analysis has shown that apart from the provider Thieme, there is no other provider on the market that holds information sheets in all clinical departments required at Gemeinschaftsklinikum. The solution described in the target vision, according to which the information sheets are to be sent to patients via the patient portal, is exclusively possible on the part of the patient portal provider Dedalus with the information system solutions from the company Thieme.
sig_ce63b02c843152f0cfc1.title: Digital patient education

The objective of the procurement is to create a unified, user-oriented information system supporting the quality and supervision of service production, which serves practical workers, supervisors and management, as well as support and maintenance services serving the operations. The background to the need and objective is the need to develop a unified system that gathers scattered supervision data together and supports its systematic utilisation in management and decision-making. Changed legislation, particularly the Act on Social and Health Care Supervision (741/2023), requires the improvement of the quality, uniformity and reporting of supervision data. The system package that is the subject of the procurement contains the following architectural, functional and supportable modules: -Quality and supervision package (Supervision tool) -Reporting sections, including shortcomings, adverse and hazard events, and the serious hazard events package -Package related to the activities of social and client/patient ombudsmen -Management of medicinal treatment licences. The subject of the procurement and requirements are described in more detail in the appendices of the invitation to tender.

sig_ceb95e39925eaffa288d.description: The Contracting Authority is setting up a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the subject of which is the procurement of expert software. The Contracting Authority sets out in point BT-24 (II.2.4.) of the notice, and in the procurement documents, the product category or categories and their characteristics for the procurement of which it wishes to set up a DPS. Pursuant to Section 107.§ (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the Contracting Authority shall make available the exact technical specification and contractual terms relating to the specific public contract to be implemented in the DPS simultaneously with the sending of the invitation to tender. The establishment of a dynamic purchasing system covers the following category: -- procurement of IT expert software (this includes in particular, but not exclusively, - procurement of software suitable for the backup, in-depth analysis and examination of mobile devices (such as smartphones, tablets) and cloud-based services; - procurement of software suitable for the reading out, in-depth analysis and examination of desktop and laptop computers, servers, mobile devices, and various data storage media; - procurement of software suitable for the reading out and analysis of data stored on mobile devices (Android, iOS, other); procurement of software suitable for the backup and analysis of mobile devices and other data storage media based on forensic technologies; - procurement of software suitable for the forensic-style analysis and quality improvement of image and video files; - procurement of software suitable for the reading out, analysis, searching and sorting of data stored on IT equipment manufactured by Apple and running the Windows operating system, etc.) The quantity planned to be procured over 36 months: 78 units Please note that the main categories have been listed solely for information purposes in order to assess the subject matter of the procurement. The subjects of the procurement are detailed further in the information note on the subjects of the procurement. Within the individual categories, the Contracting Authority shall make available to those participating in the DPS the exact technical specification and contractual terms of the product(s) to be procured in accordance with the arising needs, during the tender stages of the DPS, simultaneously with the sending of the invitation to tender, pursuant to Section 107.§ (2) of the Public Procurement Act. Pursuant to Section 107. § (2) of the Public Procurement Act, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to determine, during the implementation of the DPS, simultaneously with the sending of the invitation to tender, in relation to the specific procurement need contained therein - depending on the subject matter and nature of the specific public contracts - the possibility of submitting partial tenders in the invitation to tender. The Contracting Authority intends to set up the DPS for 36 months, the total estimated value of the procurements planned for this period being net 200 000 000 HUF. The CA wishes to indicate that it assumes no call-off obligation with regard to the estimated total value set out in the descriptive technical specification or in the contract notice, since in the case of the application of this specific procurement method (setting up a DPS), the Contracting Authority does not incur an actual procurement obligation. The Contracting Authority plans, according to its arising needs, to launch one or more tender stages quarterly, while reserving the right to send an invitation to tender more frequently than this. The expected maximum scale of individual contracts to be awarded under the DPS is net 8 000 000 HUF. In accordance with Section 107. § (4) of the Public Procurement Act, the Contracting Authority shall admit to the DPS any applicant satisfying the suitability criteria, and shall not limit the number of applicants to be invited to tender. The Contracting Authority informs applicants (tenderers in the later stage of the procedure) that if a reference to a make, origin, type was included in the procurement documentation in order to define the subject of the procurement clearly and intelligibly, then pursuant to the provisions of Section 46.§ (3) of Government Decree No. 321/2015. (X. 30.), the designation was made solely in order to define the nature of the subject matter clearly, and the Contracting Authority will also accept products of a make, origin, type equivalent to those prescribed. The assessment of equivalence shall take place on the basis of the fulfilment of the conditions prescribed for the product in question. Proving equivalence is the task of the tenderer.
sig_ceb95e39925eaffa288d.title: Procurement of IT expert software under a DPS

sig_cef5f71f644c84e946c9.description: YOU CAN STILL INFLUENCE DURING THE MARKET SURVEY PHASE! At the City of Turku, we want to make high-quality procurements and cooperate with companies. We are therefore conducting a market survey before the publication of the actual contract notice. The goal is to inform about the upcoming tendering process, survey the markets for the subject of the procurement, and obtain comprehensive information on the availability of the service, implementation possibilities, and potential suppliers. We will also ask suppliers participating in the market dialogue for comments on the minimum requirements and quality criteria in the procurement documents. The goal of the market dialogue is also to go through the scheduling and implementation of the upcoming tendering process. This is an invitation to a market dialogue concerning the energy consumption monitoring service planned by the City of Turku. Turun kaupunki monitors energy consumption in approx. 600 buildings, of which over 200 have district heating. A measurement hub, which provides more accurate consumption data, can be found in approx. 70 buildings. The goal is to create a digital service that produces energy consumption monitoring, which performs the expert's manual work steps, producing as highly refined information as possible on consumption changes with easy views, explanations, and follow-up measures. The goal is to make consumption monitoring as automatic as possible by reducing manual work steps, such as determining the start time, occurrence, and overall effects of increased consumption. The user should automatically receive the most important prioritised key observations and easily see the analysis of the observation. The market dialogue will be held as a webinar on Teams on 2.10. at 9 -11. Event programme: 9:00-10:00 Presentation of the tendering process 10:00-11:00 Questions, answers, and discussion A warm welcome! REGISTRATION: Registration via the Tarjouspalvelu portal by 25.9.2026 at 16:00 or by email to sari.holmberg@turku.fi. State the persons from your company participating and their email addresses. This notice is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but an invitation to a market dialogue, which aims to survey the market and develop the procurement's tendering documents. The invitation does not bind those who have responded to it. Not participating in the market dialogue event does not prevent participation in a possible tender competition, and participation in the event does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender competition. The contracting entity does not commit to carrying out the procurement based on the market survey, and the presented descriptions/specifications do not bind the client. We announce our upcoming procurements in the Hilma planning tool, where it is possible to set search alerts. Hilma planning tool You can find more information about us at www.turku.fi/hankinnat and we publish current matters on our LinkedIn page “Turun kaupungin hankintapalvelut”.

Context and requirements Terms and acronyms DfT – Department for Transport DfT(c) – Central Department for Transport and associated central business areas referenced in this requirement DIS – Digital, Information and Security, the DfT group leading this requirement DDAT – Digital, Data and Technology DOS 7 – Digital Outcomes and Specialists 7, the Crown Commercial Service framework proposed for this procurement Lot 2 – Digital Capability and Delivery Partners, the DOS 7 lot proposed for this requirement Target Operating Model (TOM) – DIS’s planned future operating model, including how services and capability will be delivered over time SbD – Secure by Design ATE Active Travel England BODS Bus Open Data Service CCAV Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles DTAC Digital & Technology Assurance Committee DTRO Digital Traffic Regulation Orders DVLA Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency GBR Great British Railways GCS Government Car Service GGMS Government Grants Managed Service GIS Geographical Information System GLD Government Legal Department NaPTAN National Public Transport Access Nodes (dataset) NTAP National Transport Analysis Platform NTCW National Transport Casework NTEM National Trip End Model NTM National Transport Model OZEV Office of Zero Emissions Vehicles RDM Rail Data Marketplace RPCD Rail Passenger Count Database RIS3 Road Investment Strategy 3 RSIC Road Safety Investigation Capability SHAPE Shared High-Performance Architecture for Prediction Environment TASM Transport Appraisal and Strategic Modelling (division) TOCs Train Operating Companies T-TRIG Transport Technology Research Innovation Grant VCA Vehicle Certification Agency VETS Vehicle Emission Trading Scheme ZEV Zero Emission Vehicles Overview Summary of the work DfT DIS seeks a strategic delivery partner to provide flexible, outcome-based DDAT capability across DIS and wider DfT areas through statements of work. The supplier will deliver at scale and pace, support multidisciplinary teams, provide advisory input, and help maintain digital delivery resilience while building DfT capability. Pricing model Capped time and materials Pricing model Other Provide further information The majority of the Statements of Works will be priced as Capped Time and Materials. There may be exceptional circumstances where Fixed Price or other pricing models are required. This will be subject to agreement by both parties. Confirm if you require a contracted out service or supply of resource Contracted out service: the off-payroll rules do not apply Organisation the work is for The Department for Transport (DfT) may make the Services available to its Executive Agencies, including DVSA, VCA, MCA and DVLA, as well as Arms Length Bodies (ALBs) and other organisations operating within the transport sector. Latest start date 2027-01-18 Expected contract length 5-00-00 Expected contract structure Initial contract term of 3 years, with options to extend by a further 2 years in 12 month increments. Estimated contract value (excl VAT) 20000000 Budget details Call Off value of up to £20m excluding VAT over the full proposed contract term, including all extension options. About the work Why the work is being done The Digital Information and Security Division (DIS) is responsible for digital and project delivery alongside cybersecurity, IT Service Operations and Architecture. This division provides the Department with digital, information and security expertise. Our vision is to deliver the most secure and inclusive digital tools, platforms and services that meet our users’ needs and surpass their expectations. DfTc is a Microsoft technology “house”, with a big part of our offering to staff being based on Windows devices, SharePoint, Teams and Office365 with E5 licences. The majority of the IT estate is cloud workloads mainly using Google Cloud Platform (GCP), but the estate also has MS Azure and Apple technologies. DfT requires a partner to deliver outcome-based Statements of Work (SoWs) aligned to GDS Agile principles, providing specialist DDaT capability at scale and pace. Under DOS7 Lot 2, digital projects, programmes and transformation activities will be commissioned through approved SoWs, each defining the required outcomes, deliverables, acceptance criteria, timescales, responsibilities and commercial arrangements. The model enables DfT to commission work progressively as priorities change, access multidisciplinary capability at scale and pace, and remain focused on measurable business outcomes rather than the supply of individual resources. The supplier must mobilise appropriately skilled teams quickly, apply GDS agile delivery principles, operate effectively in complex environments, collaborate with departmental stakeholders, and provide delivery leadership, specialist expertise, advisory support, demand shaping and knowledge transfer. The contract will maintain digital delivery resilience during implementation of the Target Operating Model and support transfer of knowledge to permanent DfT staff, particularly in scarce DDaT disciplines such as cyber security, cloud and architecture. Problem to be solved DfT Digital, Information and Security (DIS) needs a strategic delivery partner to maintain continuity of critical digital delivery and specialist DDAT support when the current arrangement expires at the end of February 2027. The strategic delivery partner will assist in the delivery of priority digital services, live service improvement, technical assurance and wider transformation activity across DIS and other DfT central business areas. The requirement is to provide flexible specialist capability and delivery support but also offer innovative digital solutions to customers problem statements and user needs. A detailed list of potential requirements that this contract may need to cover in the next 5 years is attached. DfT requires a supplier that can contribute earlier through advisory support, product management capability, triage and planning input, to help shape strategic demand solutions before work is formally commissioned. We require the supplier to bring innovation into the contract and keep up to date with developments in the emerging technology space. Suppliers will need to maintain delivery resilience from day one, provide flexible specialist capability across a varied and evolving portfolio, support stronger governance and oversight, and work within clearer service boundaries and accountabilities across Digital, Policy, PMO and other suppliers. The solution must combine continuity, scalability, strategic engagement and effective handover. Key risks include the fixed timetable for award and mobilisation, maintaining service quality across multiple work types, securing value for money in a demand-led environment, and ensuring the future model delivers strategic improvements. DfT is therefore seeking a resilient, commercially robust and outcome-focused service through defined statements of work, supported by capped time and materials at statement of work level. Who the users are and what they need to do The users of this contract will be:  Digital Portfolio Management Hub – where the contract will sit and where demand will be raised and the commission of specialist DDAT capability and outcome-based delivery support. This will enable priority digital services, transformation activity and live service improvements delivery.  Differing DfT business areas, these could be policy, Arm’s Length Bodies or Executive Agencies who require digital support. The areas will need access to flexible multidisciplinary delivery teams and specialist expertise so they can progress change, improvement and assurance activity when internal capability is insufficient or unavailable at pace.  Service Owners or Delivery /Project teams who will need access to specialist roles, technical assurance and delivery support so they can develop digital services maintaining service quality, manage delivery risk and achieve agreed outcomes.  DIS Leaders who are implementing the Target Operating Model, may require interim delivery capacity and specialist capability so that delivery resilience can be maintained while strengthening and upskilling permanent in-house capability over time.  Commissioning area or contract management lead, need suppliers to mobilise quickly, deliver against agreed statements of work and provide transparent performance information against SOW outcomes, so that work can be controlled effectively and value for money demonstrated.  DfT teams transitioning from external support to stronger internal capability, need suppliers to provide knowledge transfer and structured handover so that capability is retained within the department and dependency on suppliers reduces over time.  Public facing citizens of DfT digital services, need continuous improvements delivered through this contract so that services are more reliable, accessible and effective. Preliminary market engagement Market engagement was undertaken on 27th August 2026. Outputs from the session are included within the addition attachments. Following market engagement, there were no material changes to DfT’s requirements. Work done so far Existing team The supplier will work with DfT Digital, Information and Security (DIS), led by the Contract Owner reporting into the Senior Responsible Owner (SRO). Day to day engagement is expected to involve a cross-functional internal team drawn from commercial, digital, finance, legal, security, PMO, policy and operational colleagues, supporting requirement definition, triage, approvals, governance, mobilisation and ongoing contract management.
