sig_cf25a92abf9c64d34775.description: Caerphilly County Borough Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement to gather information and insight from suppliers regarding Electronic Committee Management Systems. The Council is exploring options for a modern, bilingual (English and Welsh) digital solution to support the efficient management, publication and governance of committee agendas, reports, minutes and Member information. This engagement aims to understand current market capabilities, potential delivery models, indicative costs, and future innovation within this area. The Council’s current system contract is due for renewal, and no final specification has yet been defined. The purpose of this market engagement is therefore to inform the development of a future procurement strategy and to help shape the Council’s requirements ahead of any formal tender process. Suppliers of relevant software solutions are invited to review the outline functional areas provided and respond to a series of structured questions regarding system capabilities, technical features, bilingual support, system security, public‐facing functionality, Member services, integration options and implementation considerations. This is not a call for competition and does not form part of a formal procurement process. No supplier selection or award will result from this exercise. The Council may use the information gathered to refine its approach, assess market readiness and inform potential future tender documentation. All responses received through this engagement will be treated transparently and used solely for market research and planning purposes. Lot 1: .

sig_cf3058980967ce5d0eaf.description: The purpose of this consultation is to carry out an exhaustive inventory of hedgerows and banks and an inventory of wetlands across the 27 municipalities of Villedieu Intercom. The work to be carried out comprises: - An exhaustive inventory of hedgerows and banks, excluding urban areas, across the 27 municipalities of Villedieu Intercom with a view to their preservation, restoration and enhancement. The survey must make it possible to categorise all hedgerows and banks in the territory (excluding urban areas). It will be carried out in 3 phases: pre-localisation, field inventory, action programmes (prioritisation and action programme); - An exhaustive inventory of wetlands across the 27 municipalities of Villedieu Intercom with a view to their preservation, restoration and enhancement. It will be carried out in 3 phases: pre-localisation (locations with a high probability of wetland presence), field inventory (precise mapping based on botanical criteria and pedology), action programmes (prioritisation and action programme). This action programme must be drawn up in alignment with the SAGE Côtier Ouest Cotentin (West Cotentin Coastal Water Management and Development Plan). The purpose of this contract is to carry out an exhaustive inventory of hedgerows and banks and an inventory of wetlands across the 27 municipalities of Villedieu Intercom.
sig_cf3058980967ce5d0eaf.title: Production of an inventory, diagnosis of hedgerows and wetlands, and development of an action plan in the territory of Villedieu Intercom

Proposers to this program element are strongly encouraged to use the optional Earth Science Division template for the required summary table of work effort of the proposal; templates are available at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/templates-for-earth-science-division-appendix-a-roses-proposals. NOTICE: Research security training required starting August 5, 2026. All PIs and any Co-Is that would spend ≥ 10% time on a proposed grants or cooperative agreements must certify they have taken research security training. NASA will be satisfied with the four online research security training modules on the National Science Foundation's (NSF) Research Security Training website at https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training or the SECURE Center condensed version of the four modules at https://www.secure-center.org/ctm This synopsis is a generic summary that is posted for each of the many individual "program elements" in NASA’s Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 solicitation. For specific information on this particular program element download and read the PDF of the text of this program element by going to Tables 2 or 3 of ROSES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table2 and https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table3 , respectively, click the title of the program element of interest, a hypertext link will take you to a page for that particular program element. On that page, on the right side under "Announcement Documents" the link on the bottom will be to the PDF of the text of the call for proposals. For example, if one were interested in the Solar System Science program (NNH25ZDA001N-SCUBED) one would follow the link to the NSPIRES page for that program element and then to read the text of the call one would click on “C.2 Solar System Science (.pdf)” to download the text of the call. While the letters and numbers are different for each element within ROSES (A.10, B.3, etc.) the basic configuration is always the same, e.g., the letter indicates the Science Division (A is Earth Science, B is Heliophysics etc.) and whatever the letter, #1 is always the division overview. In 2025, most program elements will be set up for application via Grants.gov only if requested at least 30 days in advance of the due date. For more on Grants.gov submissions see Section IV(b)v of the ROSES Summary of Solicitation, that may be found at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Science Mission Directorate (SMD) released its annual omnibus Research Announcement (NRA), Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 (OMB Approval Number 2700-0092, CFDA Number 43.001) on February 21, 2025. In this case "omnibus" means that this NRA has many individual program elements, each with its own due dates and topics. All together these cover the wide range of basic and applied supporting research and technology supported by SMD. Awards will be made as grants, cooperative agreements, or contracts depending on the nature of the work proposed. However, most extramural research awards deriving from ROSES will be grants, and many program elements of ROSES specifically exclude contracts, because contracts would not be appropriate for the nature of the work solicited. Funded Co-Is at government labs will receive inter- or intra-agency transfers . The typical period of performance for an award is three years, but some programs may allow up to five years and others specify shorter periods. In most cases, organizations of every type, Government and private, for profit and not-for-profit, domestic and foreign (with some caveats), may submit proposals without restriction on teaming arrangements. Tables listing the program elements and due dates (Tables 2 and 3 ), a table that provides a very top level summary of proposal contents ( Table 1 ), and the full text of the ROSES-2025 "Summary of Solicitation", may all be found NSPIRES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . Frequently asked questions for ROSES are posted at http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/faqs . Questions concerning specific program elements should be directed to the point(s) of contact for that particular element, who may be found either at the end of the individual program element in the summary table of key information or on the web list of topics and points of contact at: http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/program-officers-list . General questions concerning ROSES-2025 may be directed to the office of the SMD Deputy Associate Administrator for Research at sara@nasa.gov . Not all program elements are known at the time of the release of ROSES. To be informed of new program elements or amendments to this NRA, proposers may subscribe to: (1) The SMD mailing lists (by logging in at http://nspires.nasaprs.com and checking the appropriate boxes under "Account Management" and "Email Subscriptions"), (2) The ROSES-2025 blog feed for amendments, clarifications, and corrections to at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/solicitations/roses-2025/ , and (3) The ROSES-2025 due date Google calendars (one for each science division). Instructions are at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/library-and-useful-links (link from the words due date calendar).

sig_cf9e2be504d6c07be868.description:
Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO procurement system (hereinafter procurement system) forms a central part of the contracting authority's research, development, innovation and competence development activities and procurement platform. It forms the structure of a cooperation model regulated by an agreement between the subscriber and the research, development and innovation partners. The purpose of the services to be competed in the procurement system is to produce research data, development services and innovations as a basis for the subscriber's development activities and management. The procurement system is divided into categories as follows: Category 1 Innovation services Category 2 Development of service systems Category 3 Project services Category 4 Strategic development Category 5 Scientific communities In addition, the subject matter of the procurement includes piloting and experimentation services as well as continuous development and management services for the subscriber's use. The subject matter of the procurement and the operation of the procurement system are described in more detail in the appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system". The minimum requirements for each category and the competence requirements for applicants at the establishment stage are described in more detail in this call for participation. The subscriber shall define the subject matter and requirements of the assignments to be competed in the procurement system in more detail in each internal call for tenders of the procurement system. The procurement system shall be valid until 31.10.2029, during which time the internal call for tenders of the procurement system shall be carried out. The subscriber may extend the validity of the procurement system with a new contract notice. Suppliers may apply to join the procurement system at the establishment stage and later during its validity by submitting a request to participate in accordance with the call for participation. The procurement procedure is two-stage. To be able to submit tenders, a supplier must first submit a request to participate and be admitted to the procurement system. After this, the supplier may submit tenders by responding to the call for tenders sent by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall carry out internal competitions within the procurement system in the future as needed. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All applicants meeting the suitability requirements shall be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Actual procurements shall be made through internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. Participation in the internal competitions of the DPS is not possible unless the supplier has been admitted to the procurement system. The submission of a request to participate and admission to the procurement system does not oblige the supplier to submit a tender, but suppliers may submit tenders at their discretion. The contracting authority estimates that the value excluding value added tax of the planned procurements covered by the dynamic purchasing system at the time of publication of the call for participation is 5,6 million euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made within the system. The estimate is preliminary and based on the procurement need known at this time. The contracting authority does not commit to any procurement quantities or minimum purchase obligations with this notice. Category 1 Innovation services includes the generation of innovations and futures research. The purpose of innovation services is to produce innovative solutions and new methods for the organisation and production of services in an impactful way. Innovation can also aim, for example, at anticipating the demand for services and substantive change needs. Innovations include, for example, digital operating models, solutions related to the innovative utilisation of technology, or the utilisation of robotics and artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare services. Central to innovations is the consideration of customer experience, quality, impact and cost perspectives. Innovations may also relate to operational monitoring models, measurement of results or strategic work. The result of an innovation may also be a commercialised product or service. Category 1 Innovation services additionally includes Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.; Category 2 Development of service systems is expert service, the purpose of which is the development of services, service processes, service networks and service systems. The development of service systems includes the collection and analysis of data on the current state, needs and impact of services. The data is utilised in development activities. The development of service systems may include the production of various methods and tools for the subscriber's needs to support the implementation of changes. The service may include the implementation of stakeholder involvement, for example through service design or equivalent means. The development of service systems may also include coaching service, the purpose of which is to support the subscriber in development activities and the consolidation of results. Category 2 Development of service systems additionally includes - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.;

Category 3 Project Services includes the entire project process management for the subscriber's research, development and innovation activities. Project services include project planning services, project management services and project services. Category 3 Project Services also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 4 Strategic development consulting is an expert service intended to provide the subscriber with comprehensive support for development activities and change management, from the perspectives of organiser management and service production. Strategic development consulting produces versatile and comprehensive information, expertise and insights into the development of social and health services and specialised medical care, as well as large-scale integration projects. The consulting offers expert knowledge for promoting the effectiveness, customer-orientation and quality of innovation and development activities in social welfare, health services and specialised medical care, as well as for the design, analysis and implementation of new operating models and process complexes. The strategic development consulting expert service includes versatile expertise in improving the effectiveness and productivity of social and health services, financing systems, improving service accessibility, designing service systems and networks, developing data-driven management capabilities and future forecasting. Strategic development can also include service production management services, which can be used to achieve significant cost savings when service production and the producer field in accordance with procurement contracts can be managed more systematically and purposefully. The service production management service can also help the contracting authority to find consistent and replicable operating processes for managing service providers, with which better service effectiveness, customer satisfaction, quality and cost-efficiency can be achieved. Category 4 Strategic development also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 5 For the scientific community, the procurement system acts as a cooperation platform and procurement channel towards the scientific community, such as universities, higher education institutions, educational institutions, centres of expertise and research institutes. Services procured from the scientific community in the procurement system may include services considered to be scientific activities, which in their content complement projects implemented within the framework of TKIO cooperation. Scientific activity may include any research activity and services in accordance with the subject of the procurement system, but a scientific and research perspective is always emphasised in these services. Services and research activities may be such that the benefit obtained accrues for use in operations other than those of the contracting authority. Services procured from the scientific community may also be research and development services where the benefit obtained accrues exclusively for use in the contracting authority's operations and the contracting authority compensates for the service performed in full. The nature of the service is specified in each call for tenders within the procurement system. Services can also be ordered from the scientific community directly without a call for tenders within the procurement system, if the conditions for the procurement act's scope exemption concerning research and development services (9 section 1 subsection 13 point) are met. Category 5 Scientific community also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.
sig_cf9e2be504d6c07be868.title: TKIO expert services Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueelle DPS

sig_cfa2eb6bd1e690f2b8cf.description: The full title of the contract is: Construction and operation of a stationary water meter reading system in the towns of Ruda Śląska and Świętochłowice, using Narrowband technology (NB-IoT or LTE.CAT.M) operating in licensed radio bands. Due to the limited number of characters in the www.ezamowienia.gov.pl form, the Contracting Authority was forced to limit the number of characters in the title of the notice. The subject of the contract is the construction and operation of a stationary water meter reading system (hereinafter: System) in the town of Ruda Śląska and Świętochłowice, using Narrowband technology (NB-IoT or LTE.CAT.M) operating in licensed radio bands. The aim of the planned contract is the ongoing acquisition of readings from water meters, monitoring and automatic analysis of the received data, direct transfer to the integrated systems of the Contracting Authority and the possibility of making them available to service recipients. The Contractor shall ensure the construction of a stationary water meter reading system allowing for data reception at least once a day. sig_cfa968a4351ab860ab79.description: The subject of the contract is the creation of a comprehensive digital system to support spatial planning for Košický samosprávny kraj (hereinafter referred to as "KSK"). Amendment 01 _ AOI 01 AOI-2025_01 - Solicitation Request: CFC SAIO/PKO is soliciting white papers on the effort(s) identifed as Area(s) of Interest (AOIs) to this solicitation. Type of Contract: This is a Fixed-Price type contract IAW FAR Part 12 and Part 35. Limitation: This acquisition is set aside for small business. Anticipated Award: Government reserves the right to award all, some, or none of the proposed solutions. Classified Information: Offerors are encouraged to submit unclassified White Papers to simplify and expedite reviews and response by the Government. Description The United States Space Force (USSF), through the Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)to solicit innovative commercial solutions that enhance Space Domain Awareness (SDA)capabilities. This CSO is authorized under DFARS 212.70and is designed to identify and acquire innovative technologies, products, and services that support the USSF's warfighting missions. The CSO provides a flexible, enterprise-wide acquisition mechanism to address SDA mission challenges through advanced software engineering, data analytics, and other innovative approaches. Submissions will be evaluated under a multi-phase process to ensure alignment with mission needs and operational priorities. Scope of the CSO The CSO seeks solutions that address the following Space Domain Awareness (SDA)mission challenges: Detecting, characterizing, and predicting activities in the space domain. Enhancing the accuracy and timeliness of SDA data. Supporting emerging SDA missions through innovative technologies. Specific Areas of Interest (AOIs) will be issued under this CSO to define technical focus areas, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria. Each AOI will be posted as a standalone solicitation module under this CSO. Submission Process The CSO employs a three-phase submission process: Phase I – White Paper and PowerPoint Briefing Offerors must submit a PowerPoint briefing (including a Quad Chart) and a White Paper summarizing their proposed solution. Submissions must align with the specific AOI requirements. Phase II – Pitch Session (Optional) Selected Offerors may be invited to present their proposed solution in greater depth during a virtual or in-person pitch session. Phase III – Full Proposal Offerors invited to Phase III must submit a complete proposal package, including a Technical Proposal, Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Price Proposal. The Government reserves the right to proceed directly from Phase I to Phase III. Key Information Security Requirements: Phase I submissions must be unclassified. Subsequent phases may require higher classification levels, as specified in the AOI and any draft or final DD Form 254. Foreign Participation: Restricted to U.S. entities due to export control and national security considerations. Cybersecurity Compliance: Offerors must comply with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC 2.0 requirements. How to Respond Interested Offerors must monitor SAM.gov for AOI-specific postings under this CSO. Each AOI will include detailed submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and deadlines. Submissions must comply with the formats and requirements outlined in the CSO and the applicable AOI. For general inquiries, contact the SAIO CSO Contracting Officer at SAIO.SDA.CSO@spaceforce.mil. Use the subject line: "SDA CSO – General Question(s)". Disclaimer This CSO does not obligate the Government to award a contract, nor does it commit the Government to pay for any costs incurred in the preparation and submission of responses. sig_d02a65bb916331c079c1.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) is the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system for the procurement of services consisting in the processing of socio-economic and similar studies and analyses in the field of immovable infrastructure, the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities, consultancy services and expert support from the founding/establishing entity for individual legal entities within the contracting authority's remit, the preparation of analyses of the Czech defence industry and analyses of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure, under the conditions set out in the tender documentation (in detail in the tender documentation). The subject matter will be in particular the acquisition of comprehensive information important for evaluating and mapping the consequences of increased expenditure and defence requirements in the medium and long-term outlook. This primarily concerns the Czech economy (for example, the labour market, support for science and research, regional development or involvement in EU funds and other financial mechanisms), society in the Czech Republic and international cooperation. Processing of the analysis of the impacts of increased defence and security expenditure and requirements with regard to the commitments undertaken by the Czech Republic at the NATO summit in The Hague in June 2025; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the provision and submission to the Ministry of Defence of comprehensive information on the actual state of capabilities and capacities of the domestic industry and research organisations, focusing in particular on capabilities in the field of development, production and logistical support of military material, training of technical personnel, training and fulfilment of mobilisation supplies; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the preparation of analyses of the operational efficiency of subordinate legal entities and contributing to the increase of their profitability, the provision of consultancy services and expert support to increase the efficiency of the performance of the function of the founder or establishing entity for individual legal entities within the remit of the Ministry of Defence; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular activities consisting in the provision of studies that will deal with the evaluation of both positive and negative impacts of construction on employment, the economy, transport, social and technical infrastructure, the environment (sustainable development) and the provision of public and private services in the area. The content of the studies will also include the identification of entities responsible for the prevention of risks and the resolution of arisen risks and proposals for measures that could eliminate, resolve or prevent the arisen risks, as well as the preparation of recommendations for the amendment of relevant strategic documents. The subject matter will also in certain cases include the preparation of presentations intended for concerned public administration stakeholders; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).; The subject matter will be in particular the analysis of the process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, the preparation and submission of a proposal for a new process model of the Ministry of Defence department in the field of development and care of immovable infrastructure, including implementation steps and the provision of consultancy services during implementation; under the conditions specified in individual calls for tenders pursuant to Section 141 of the Act (in more detail in the TD).

sig_d039b4efab11b19e1cc6.description: The government and the conference of courts of the Canton of St. Gallen are seeking one or more tenderers to replace the currently used business management software JURIS-4 (specialist application for the judiciary). The new solution for users in the Canton of St. Gallen (including the public prosecutor's office, the courts, the Office of Corrections, the Office of the Commercial Register and Notariats, and the Department of Security and Justice) must enable the electronic management of case files while being user-friendly and user-centric. Alongside audit-proof archiving of documents, the use of digital signatures, the traceability of data changes and compliance with statutory retention periods, a high degree of configurability is also required. Furthermore, we are seeking a user-friendly, accessible German-language interface with automated processes for intuitive use in a collaborative manner. To achieve our goal of an end-to-end digital, media-break-free procedure with electronic file management, the seamless integration of interfaces will also be necessary. Non-industry tenderers are also expressly invited to take part in the pre-qualification. Lot 2a, public prosecutor's office and courts, criminal proceedings Under the title "Criminal proceedings", the business of the public prosecutor's office and those judicial authorities responsible for adjudicating criminal proceedings under the Swiss Criminal Procedure Code (CrimPC) and the Swiss Juvenile Criminal Procedure Code (J CrimPC) is grouped together. In the Canton of St. Gallen, these are the public prosecutor's office, the juvenile prosecutor's office, the Cantonal Court (incl. indictment chamber), the district courts (St. Gallen, Rorschach, Rheintal, Werdenberg-Sarganserland, See-Gaster, Toggenburg, Wil) and the cantonal compulsory measures court. Criminal proceedings are governed by federal law (CrimPC) and cantonal law (EG-CrimPC, CrimPR). Procedural workflows and steps may vary depending on the competent authority. Lot 2b, courts, civil proceedings Under the title "Civil proceedings", the business of those judicial authorities responsible for adjudicating civil law disputes as well as debt enforcement and bankruptcy disputes under the Swiss Civil Procedure Code (CPC), the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act (DEBA) and cantonal introductory acts is grouped together. In the Canton of St. Gallen, these are the Cantonal Court, the Commercial Court and the district courts (St. Gallen, Rorschach, Rheintal, Werdenberg-Sarganserland, See-Gaster, Toggenburg, Wil). Civil proceedings are governed mainly by federal law (CPC, DEBA) and cantonal law. Procedural workflows and steps may vary depending on the competent authority and the respective legal area. Lot 2b, courts, administrative proceedings Under the title "Administrative proceedings", the business of the Administrative Appeals Commission (VRKO), the Administrative Court (VWGR) and the Insurance Court (VSGR) is grouped together. Administrative proceedings are largely governed by cantonal law. Procedural workflows and steps vary depending on the authority and legal area concerned, but are fundamentally similar to appeal proceedings in civil proceedings. As a rule, business is preceded by proceedings before an authority/institution that is not connected to the NGV_SG.
sig_d039b4efab11b19e1cc6.title: New business management software for St. Gallen (NGV_SG)

sig_d051994587c2323e2f5c.description: The Welsh Government launched its Disabled People's Rights Plan on the 15th of December 2025. The Disabled People’s Rights Plan sets out a 10-year cross-government framework to advance the rights and opportunities of disabled people in Wales, removing societal barriers, and challenging the prejudice and discrimination they face. In line with the Public Sector Equality Duty to address the inequalities experienced by those with protected characteristics, the Disabled People’s Rights Plan directly targets the 670,000 disabled people in Wales who continue to experience inequalities and barriers across a range of areas, including in employment, education, healthcare, access to services, transport, housing, community participation and justice. The Plan was published alongside a supporting document that outlined the short-term actions to be delivered within the first two years up to the end of 2027. The Welsh Government has committed to delivering 67 short-term actions, which are aligned to achieving the outcomes that are set out in the Plan. These actions uphold the principles of the articles outlined in the UNCRPD and Welsh Government’s National Equality Objectives. The Client wishes to commission an evaluation of the Disabled People’s Rights Plan, comprised broadly of the following: - A Process Evaluation to understand the Plan’s implementation and suggest improvements for future work in this area - Baselining work towards an Impact Evaluation to begin to understand whether the Plan has had an impact on the lives of disabled people in Wales Lot 1: . None

For the development and support of the SMCS and Gas Reporting System of Magyar Földgáztároló Zrt., and the provision of software upgrades for a period of 3 years from the conclusion of the contract - 2023 System support, software upgrade Software support for the Contracting Authority's SMCS system, SMCS Dispatcher application, SMCS XL system, Auction application, Touch&Store application and GRS system (hereinafter: Systems) covers the following system elements: Configuration of factory unmodified system components of the NGinx web server and JBoss application server commissioned in connection with the development of the systems; Configuration of factory unmodified system components of the PostgreSQL database management system (RDBMS) commissioned in connection with the development of the systems; Taninframe UI framework, Spring framework, Spring Cloud Gateway framework, AngularJS and Angular 2+ frameworks Code of the systems written in Java, Javascript, TypeScript, HTML and GWT languages Commissioned in connection with the development of the systems: SAP BusinessObjects (v3.1) user reports, Microsoft Power BI user reports, Mule ESB system, Google Web Toolkit framework, Highsoft HighCharts library, Handsontable library, Bootstrap library, iOS Mobile application Interface modules implemented in connection with SMCS development, such as: SMCS-side interface module managing laboratory data, SMCS-side interface module managing FGSZ data, Interface module performing REMIT data reporting, Interface module performing MEKH data reporting Service period for the SMCS system, the SMCS Dispatcher application and the SMCS XL system: The service period runs on working days between 09:30-22:30h, and on public holidays: from 16:00 to 22:30h. Support service (including critical bug fixes) takes place within the service period. The service also includes on-site support at the MFGT site for a duration of 8 hours on working days. Tasks to be performed within the framework of on-site support: System support: Support for MFGT's SMCS system, SMCS Dispatcher application, SMCS XL system, Auction application, Touch&Store application and Gas Reporting System, as well as applications used by MFGT and installed by MVMI. Receiving, fixing, administering requests and bugs reported by external clients and internal users, and forwarding them to neighbouring system operators (NNOs). Development and system support of software/applications having high availability and covering the complete allocation process for the licensee, featuring a function running daily allocation and re-allocation procedures for the quantity of natural gas fed in on the supplier side. IT and gas industry consulting: General professional consultation regarding systems created by MFGT and to be created in the future. Consulting provided for the elaboration of operational and development requirements of the SMCS system and subsystems, coordination with the Client and system-using users. Participation in operational internal meetings and holding training sessions for key users of the system. Performing business analyst tasks: Preparing ad-hoc reports, analysing and visualising extracted data in accordance with user requirements. Performing BI (Business Intelligence) tasks: Integration with existing databases, creation and management of data marts, as well as creation and management of data models necessary for creating BI reports, and assisting users participating in the process. Use and management of applications serving BI tasks (MS Power BI, SSIS, SSAS, SSRS, SSMS). Liaison: with MFGT users, development companies involved in developments, and external users (clients) using MFGT's systems, MVMI, and neighbouring system operators, domestic and European regulatory bodies of the gas industry, and participation in meetings and events. Testing: Participation in testing new versions and developments of the systems, in testing processes, and in documenting these. On-site presence: working 8 hours per day at the MFGT site. Standby: System monitoring availability seven days a week according to the durations included in the tender specifications. Service period for the Auction application, the Touch&Store application and the GRS system: The service period is the period between 09:30 and 17:30h on working days. The Client provides remote access for the support of the SMCS system. It is the Contractor's task to provide the following activities regarding the live and test operating environments of the Systems in accordance with what is described in MFGT's Information Security Policy. Receiving bug reports and troubleshooting: receiving and fixing bugs related to the System and providing feedback to the Client within the SLA frameworks laid down in the business contract. Configuration of system components. Handling of storage operational state changes (injection, withdrawal). Tracking custom requirements related to capacity management. Ad-hoc reporting of data extractable from the system according to custom requirements. Server-side and client-side management of SAP BusinessObjects and Microsoft PowerBI data visualisation applications. Delimiting application bugs, network bugs, external bugs. Supporting system elements, handling problems, bugs, requests related to them. Performing administration, version updating, bug detection and fault clearance tasks related to the system. Configuration of IT system components, application servers, database management systems of the system. Management of SSL certificates. Performing migration works. Handling other information-request announcements: based on any question, complaint or other remark of the Client related to the System. System development Continuous ensuring of compliance with amendments to industry-level Get, Get vhr, MEKH decrees, ÜKSZ provisions during the term of the contract, by individual order and itemised accounting. Magyar Földgáztároló Zrt.

sig_d07971ca64f4479df958.description: This territorial study addresses the future policy needs, linked to the inclusion of the cross-border dimension in the Czechia’s Regional Development Strategy 2028+; for this purpose, it is important to understand whether and where Czech cross-border functional areas regions are present, and how their development dynamics and challenges differ. Through new granular territorial evidence and tailored recommendations, it will produce a comprehensive overview of the Czech cross-border functional areas, also alleviating the absence of a a standardised approach to the monitoring of these areas through a cross-border monitoring toolkit enabling long-term observation.
sig_d07971ca64f4479df958.title: ESPON - New perspectives on Functional Cross-Border Areas in the Czech Republic (CROSS-CZ)

sig_d07d7961da661f3618a2.description: This market consultation aims to obtain information on available software solutions and complementary services that support the secure operation and implementation of an application in a high-security environment. The subject matter of the request includes, in particular, services for supporting on-premise implementation, the technical and organisational migration of a complex Oracle database, the provision and execution of training courses, ensuring maintenance and support services in accordance with SLAs, and the implementation of release requirements. In addition, solutions for data imports and exports as well as generic interfaces for mass data processing are considered. Further details can be found in the documents at www.bdbos.de/markterkundung and / or in section 5 "Lot" of this notice. Interested bidders may ask questions (F3@bdbos.bund.de). These will be collated, answered, and published in a question-and-answer catalogue for all participants. This can also be found at www.bdbos.de/markterkundung. The document is updated regularly. 1. Procedure Should you wish to offer a product that covers our requirements, we invite you to present your software solution through meaningful documents as well as your service portfolio. A breakdown of costs into individual items is additionally helpful when examining cost-effectiveness. Please describe your offered services in a detailed and comprehensible manner. Merely sending a manual is not sufficient. When submitting your response, please use the enclosed appendix _2 - Response. Link: https://www.bdbos.bund.de/DE/Service/markterkundung/_dateien/anlage_2.html Please send your response by 03.07.2026 to: F3@bdbos.bund.de We thank you in advance for your efforts and look forward to receiving your response. 2. Contracting Authority The Bundesanstalt für den Digitalfunk der Behörden und Organisationen mit Sicherheitsaufgaben (BDBOS) operates the federal networks, the high-secure communication network of the federal administration, and the BOS digital radio for security authorities and rescue and relief organisations. We enable participants from government, administration, and operational, security, and rescue forces at the federal, state, and municipal levels to communicate securely and reliably at all times. For this purpose, alongside other database-related procedures, we also operate a complex database application for the management and evaluation of site data and network components of the digital radio (Network Lifecycle Management). BDBOS intends to comprehensively modernise the existing database application. In preparation for a possible procurement procedure, we are conducting a non-binding market consultation in accordance with Section 28 VgV / Section 20 UVgO. This is a non-binding determination of market conditions and not a procurement procedure that concludes with the award of a contract. 3. Subject Matter of the Contract Please refer to the enclosed appendix _1 - Requirements, link: https://www.bdbos.bund.de/DE/Service/markterkundung/_dateien/anlage_1.html, or the "Additional Information" field of this notice for the minimum requirements regarding the performance characteristics of the sought-after site database. In addition to the software solution, a complementary service portfolio should be provided that includes the following services: • Support for the implementation of the software solution on-premise in a high-security environment • Implementation of the technical and organisational migration of existing data from a complex Oracle database • Execution of user training for the application in a training environment to be provided • Ensuring maintenance services in accordance with an agreed SLA including customer and administration support also on-site • Readiness to implement release requirements • Exports and imports of data and provision of generic interfaces for mass data processing 4. Notes on Procurement Classification We explicitly point out that: • Participation in the market consultation is voluntary and free of charge. • The market consultation serves exclusively to prepare a potential tender. • No entitlement to participate in a subsequent procurement procedure arises. • All incoming information will be reviewed, documented, and taken into account within the procurement file. • A subsequent specification of requirements for a potential tender will be structured neutrally and openly to competition. 5. Confidentiality Information transmitted by you to us will be treated confidentially.
sig_d07d7961da661f3618a2.title: Market sounding for the procurement of a software solution / mobile communications site database

sig_d08c4b0dcdd6f24d4f77.description: Tuomi Logistiikka Oy is requesting tenders on behalf of Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialue (contracting authority) for a development portfolio package solution. The subject of the procurement is a development portfolio package solution that acts as a core tool for the contracting authority organisation for the management, monitoring and control of projects, project portfolios and the strategy portfolio. The system must support the entire lifecycle of projects from ideation, prioritisation, resourcing and decision-making to implementation, monitoring and reporting. The solution must include at least the following management packages: - a project portfolio, and - a strategy portfolio, by means of which the implementation of the strategy and related projects can be managed as a unified whole. The procurement is implemented as a SaaS-based software service (System). The system is used to manage, inter alia, project basic information, schedules, resourcing, financial and funding data, approval processes, and the situational picture of projects, project portfolios and the strategy portfolio for use by management and other stakeholders. The system must support both operational project management and portfolio- and management-level decision-making, including reporting, analytics and visual dashboard views. The procurement includes the System and its access rights, the necessary implementation and configuration services, and maintenance and support services during the contract period as described in more detail in the procurement documents. Possible additional and expert services, integrations and further development will be implemented in accordance with the invitation to tender and the terms of the contract. The solution must be user-centric, and its functionalities must be easily and intuitively absorbable. The solution must be configurable to the needs of the contracting authority, and the contracting authority's main users must have the opportunity to maintain and develop the system as extensively as possible using the management tools it provides. The solution must include versatile reporting and output functionalities and support the presentation of data in various dashboard views. A more detailed description of the content and requirements of the procurement is set out in the appendices to the invitation to tender. The contract will be concluded for an indefinite period. The estimated total value of the procurement is approximately 250 000 euros calculated over a four (4) year period. The value is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority. The procurement has not been divided into lots because the entity forming the subject of the procurement constitutes a functionally and technically unified service package that it is not expedient to divide into smaller parts.
sig_d08c4b0dcdd6f24d4f77.title: Procurement of a development portfolio solution

sig_d09c113be36ac2312b5a.description: The subject of the contract is the implementation of the "Smart System for Predictive Staffing of School Units & Educational Policy – EDUPLAN.AI". This is a national artificial intelligence (AI) information system aimed at the strategic planning and rational staffing of Primary and Secondary Education school units. Specifically, the contract concerns the design, development, pilot and productive operation of a comprehensive digital platform that will allow the evaluation of Primary and Secondary Education school units by multiple stakeholder groups: parents, teachers and students. The system will allow the monitoring, prediction and automatic simulation of permanent and substitute staff needs, based on demographic, housing, educational and specific data per region. The objective is the transition from the traditional management model to a strategic planning system that ensures optimal resource allocation and transparency in placements. The duration of the contract is twelve months (12) from its signing with the possibility of extension. The subdivision of the contract subject into lots (according to the provisions of article 59 of law 4412/2016) is not possible, as the deliverables of the contract are deemed inextricably linked and interdependent. The services of the contract are organically connected to each other and constitute a single and unique project. Effectiveness, adherence to schedules, handling of implementation risks, and immediate adaptation to needs arising during implementation are mutually dependent actions. In the event of proclaiming the contract in lots, adequate time coordination between actions would not be feasible. The sequence of individual tasks is what dictates the proposed method of conducting the tender so as to best serve the purpose of the action to be implemented in a qualitative, manageable and efficient manner. The Total Project Budget – Estimated Value of the contract amounts to the sum of 3.000.000 † excluding VAT 24%, i.e., 3.720.000,00† including VAT. sig_d0f4b503e08c5f569ed5.description: Short description of the project: Just and Climate Resilient Urban Development and Decentralisation (CitiZen+D) CitiZen+D is a technical cooperation project financed by the Federal Ministry of Economic Development and Cooperation of Germany and implemented by GIZ in Zambia. The objective of the project is to support urban development in selected cities in Zambia with an emphasise on climate resilience, social inclusion, and sustainable financing, setting best practice for the whole country. Context In Zambia, increasing numbers of people are moving to cities, posing a major challenge for these urban centres. Tight budgets, complicated regulations and unclear responsibilities in planning and development result in a lack of adequate urban planning. This particularly affects temporary, poor settlements in and around cities. The population here has only limited access to public services such as waste disposal, fresh water and sanitation, and safe road planning. Disadvantaged groups such as women, children, people with disabilities and people living in poverty are especially hard hit. Environmental pollution and social problems also result. Approach The project advises selected cities on planning, coordinationng and implementationing of socially just and climate-friendly urban development. This allows the cities to realise development plans created in the earlier project phase and incorporate specific financing and operating arrangements into these plans. The project promotes cooperation between civil society, governmental institutions, organised interest groups and business to enable broad-based, socially just and future-oriented development in cities. The project aims for the population to have a say in planning and design, bolstering promoting trust in democratic institutions. Traditional authorities are also involved in the project. Locally successful approaches provide an example for other cities and feed into national aspects such as laws and guidelines. This should also result in administrative decentralisation. The project is part of the "Responsible Governance in Zambia" German development cooperation programme. Objective of the assignment: The project "Just and Climate Resilient Urban Development and Decentralisation in Zambia" (CitiZen+D), implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), supports urban development and decentralisation in Zambia in four output areas: Output 1: The coordination, planning, and implementation capacities of selected cities for equitable and climate-resilient urban development have been improved. Output 2: The financial capacities of selected cities for equitable and climate-resilient urban development have improved. Output 3: The participation of civil society actors, especially women, in the implementation of equitable and climate-resilient urban development has improved. Output 4: The professional exchange between government and civil society actors on successful approaches to equitable, climate-resilient urban development has improved. Under Output 1, the programme supports the development of 1 Planning Agreement and 5 Local Area Plans (LAPs) in the cities of Choma, Mazabuka, and Livingstone in Southern Province and Mansa and Samfya in Luapula. In 2025 the programme was focusing on the selection of informal settlements in the respective cities and on developing a planning and implementation framework for the development of the LAPs. Based on this the LAP process was initiated in Mansa and Livingstone. To progress with the remaining cities CitiZen+D is looking for a contractor supporting the preparation of three LAPs and one Planning Agreement in Choma (LAP), Samfya (LAP), and Mazabuka (LAP). The location of the Planning Agreement is yet to be determined. The local area plans are meant to: - Guide sustainable land use and development, for example safeguard natural sensitive areas, such as for water catchment and wildlife - Improve infrastructure and service delivery - Support climate change adaptation - Align with national and regional planning strategies The contractor will assist local authorities in designing a participatory planning approach that integrates climate resilience while including the views and opinions of residents, including women, elderly, youth and other marginalized groups. To achieve active inclusion and consideration of communities and marginalized groups, the contractor will sub-contract civil society organizations for the LAP in Choma and Mazabuka through a financing instrument (local subsidy). In order to strengthen planning capacities and use of Geographic Information Systems the contractor is expected to implement and coordinate a local subsidy with the University of Zambia (UNZA). Once the Local Area Plans are approved the contractor shall support local authorities in developing a comprehensive and context-sensitive implementation concept for the LAPs targeting the selected settlements. This concept will outline actionable strategies, institutional frameworks, and phased interventions to formalize land tenure, improve access to basic services (water, sanitation, waste management, and mobility), and enhance housing conditions while preserving community livelihoods. The concept needs to explicitly emphasis on identifying, structuring, and accessing viable financing options to ensure real-world execution. The output will empower local authorities and partners to move beyond planning into funded, scalable, and accountable implementation that delivers tangible improvements in housing, infrastructure, and livelihoods for informal settlement residents. This includes strengthening of resource mobilisation in local authorities. The assignment is structured in the following work packages to be implemented by the contractor: Work Package Title Work Package 1 Climate resilient local area planning and planning agreements Work Package 2 CSO support for inclusive Local Area Plans (LAPs) Work Package 3 GIS capacities for local authorities Work Package 4 Financing models for LAP implementation Work Package 5 Strengthening national dialogue Work Package 6 Strengthening resource mobilisation Work Package 7 Support processes (Expert Pool)
sig_d0f4b503e08c5f569ed5.title: 10044493 - Climate resilient urban development and financing in selected municipalities in Zambia

sig_d1a84a44e828de901d26.description: The Boosting Innovative GEOINT-Science and Technology (BIG-ST) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) invites proposers to submit innovative concepts to address hard GEOINT problems that align to one or more of the following technical domains: (1) Foundational GEOINT, (2) Advanced Phenomenologies, and (3) Analytic Technologies. BAA Process and Topic Call Publication: The BIG-ST BAA is a general announcement of NGA’s research interest, including criteria for selecting proposals and soliciting the participation of all offerors capable of satisfying the Government’s needs. The requests for abstracts and proposals are transmitted via Topic Calls that are published separately under the BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation at various times during the open period of the General Solicitation. Topic Calls will be published via updates to the BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation site on Sam.gov, Grants.gov, and/or the Classified IC-Acquisition Research Center (https://acq-ui.ace.proj.nro.ic.gov). For Classified Topic Calls, interested parties must have an account to log into the Classified IC-ARC to see the notice, and all associated RFP documents. For additional support with account access, please contact the Classified ACE Help Desk at 855-4ACE. Interested parties should periodically check these websites for updates. No submissions shall be accepted to the General Solicitation; abstracts and proposals will only be reviewed in response to open Topic Calls. Please refer to the Topic Calls for Abstract and Proposal due dates. The BIG-ST BAA General Solicitation, HM047623BAA0001 Revision 4 (dated 07/30/2026), is posted and applies to Topic 7 and forward. See Attachments/Links. Closed Topics: Topic 1 - Geospatial-Intelligence Foundational Model (GFM) is closed Topic 2 - Magnifying University Science Expertise (MUSE) is closed. Topic 3 - VLBI+G Signal Chain Development (VLBI+G) is closed. Topic 5 - Better Ingested GEOINT - Identifying Artificial Intelligence and Manually Manipulated Media (BIGISLAND) is closed. As part of extended funding by the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), the SoilRob project from the programme area 2 of the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) in Müncheberg is planning the expansion of existing measuring instruments and the purchase of new ones for field work. The SoilRob project is working on an integrated understanding of the effects of autonomous small and light agricultural machinery on soils in diversified cropping systems compared to conventional large-scale agricultural machinery. For this purpose, approx. 30 different soil parameters are being investigated for their significance for soil health. In order to continue to investigate existing and new trials in detail, new measuring instruments are required. Lot LOT-0001: 1 device Fully automatic soil sampling device. Computer-aided system for the automated execution of penetration resistance measurements in soils. The system is used for the mechanical insertion of a penetrometer for high-resolution recording of soil resistance and for the generation of reproducible and largely operator-independent measurement data - Measurement & control technology: System with constant, predetermined pressure during the penetration process via hydraulic control - integrated penetration resistance monitoring for quality assurance and protection of the sensor technology - Recording of sensor data (pressure (=penetration resistance), soil moisture, optional: electrical conductivity, optical reflection (see below)) in high-resolution steps of every 1 cm penetration depth, maximum penetration depth of the probe of 80 cm - Recording of further sensor data: penetration speed (as continuous as possible) - Data acquisition: data interface and memory for the field values; system must have a sufficiently dimensioned internal data memory (min. 5-10 GB), which enables the storage of at least 500 complete measurement profiles including georeferencing - Power supply: autonomous operation via a system-integrated e-power pack; independent of the carrier vehicle's on-board hydraulics. - Assembly & integration: installation on a carrier vehicle (tractor attachment to three-point hydraulics (category 1 or 2)) or pick-up (such as VW Amarok) - Performance: enables more precise control of the penetration speed compared to manual operation; minimises human error factors during data acquisition. Parallel measurement of soil moisture and optionally other soil parameters such as electrical conductivity (EC) or optical reflection (red & infrared), - Overspeed control - Technical requirements: pressure: at least 135 bar; volume flow: 20 Planning basis: MP-3.90 device Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0002: 2 devices Infiltrometer. Expansion of the existing SATURO device pool for the comparable continuation of existing measurement series: portable, computer-aided and fully automated field infiltrometer for determining the field-saturated hydraulic conductivity of soils under field conditions; designed for soil science, hydrological and soil physics field measurements with high repeatability and minimised manual operating effort. - Measurement & control technology: automated ring infiltrometer system with measurement of infiltration at at least two different hydrostatic pressure heads - automatic regulation and maintenance of a constant water level above the soil surface - automatic recording of the infiltration rate and calculation of the field-saturated hydraulic conductivity directly in the system - Consideration or correction of three-dimensional flows through multi-pressure head/dual-head measurement methods, so that no manual estimation of soil-specific correction factors is required. - Data acquisition: integrated control unit with display and storage of measured values in the field - automatic documentation of infiltration rate, pressure head, water level, measurement duration and calculated field-saturated hydraulic conductivity - Export of measurement data via USB or equivalent interface to a computer - Raw data export in a common, further-processable format, e.g. CSV and/or XLSX - Software or equivalent solution for downloading, viewing and archiving the measurement data must be included in the scope of delivery or be available free of charge. - Power supply: autonomous field operation via a rechargeable control unit or system-integrated power supply; mains charger included in the scope of delivery - Charging/supply range at least 18-24 V DC or equivalent - Operation independent of external field power supply during measurement Planning basis: Dual-Head Infiltrometer SATURO Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0003: 1 device Hood infiltrometer. Field infiltrometer for determining the hydraulic conductivity of soils in the near-saturated range under natural field conditions; designed for low-destruction infiltration measurements directly on the soil surface - Measurement & control technology: measuring system with a closed, downward-open and water-filled hood, which is placed directly on the soil surface; the circular soil surface covered by the water forms the source area for the infiltration flow. An additional contact layer, e.g. sand layer or membrane, as well as preparation of the measurement surface must not be required for standard measurement operation. - The control of the hydraulic pressure head must take place via a Mariotte water supply or an equivalent pressure-stable method - the effective hydraulic pressure head at the soil surface must be freely adjustable between zero and a negative pressure up to the air entry point of the respective soil. - The display of the hydraulic pressure head must take place via a manometer or an equivalent precise pressure display.

- The calculation of hydraulic conductivity must be possible from the steady-state flow rates determined in the test according to Wooding or an equivalent recognised evaluation method. - Data acquisition: It must be possible to record the flow rate either electronically via pressure sensors with a handheld device and associated evaluation software or via an equivalent documentable measurement method. In the case of electronic execution, it must be possible to save measurement data for the flow rate or water consumption, the set hydraulic pressure head, the measurement time and the measurement point identifier and to transfer them to a computer. Software-supported evaluation and documentation of the measurement data must be possible. - export in a common, further-processable data format is desirable. - Data acquisition: Integrated control unit with display and storage of measured values in the field - automatic documentation of infiltration rate, pressure head, water level, measurement duration and calculated field-saturated hydraulic conductivity - Export of measurement data via USB or equivalent interface to a computer; raw data export in a common, further-processable format, e.g. CSV and/or XLSX - Software or an equivalent solution for downloading, viewing and archiving the measurement data must be included in the scope of delivery or be available free of charge. Further technical data: - Infiltration vessel with Mariotte pressure control, filling volume 5 l - U-tube manometer: +25 cm ... 0 ... -25 cm - Infiltration hood small: max Ø 16 cm - Infiltration hood large: max Ø 24 cm - electronic pressure transducer - Handheld device and logger: at least 2.000 measured values, measurement interval 1 s, sampling rate 0 - 100 s (freely selectable) Planning basis: Field measuring device IL 2700 Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0004: 1 Device Portable canopy analysis system for crops. Extension of the existing SunScan device pool for the comparable continuation of existing measurement series: Mobile, scientific complete system for the non-destructive determination of the leaf area index (LAI) and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) within plant stands. - Measurement components: Set consisting of a probe unit with an integrated radio module and a high-precision, external sunshine sensor (at least class BF5) with a separate radio module for reference measurement. - Data transmission: Wireless communication via RadioLink on the frequency 434 MHz or equivalent - Range: Radio transmission between the modules over distances of at least 100 to 200 m (depending on vegetation density). - Energy supply: Completely mains-independent operation; the modules are powered by standard AA batteries. - Operation & IT: Data acquisition via a dedicated handheld computer (RPDA) with the operating system - Mechanical accessories: Including a 3-leg tripod for stable positioning of the reference sensor in the field or equivalent - Mobility & protection: Delivery in a robust transport case Planning basis: SS1-COM-R4 SunScan complete system Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0005: 10 Devices Single-board computer. Single-board computer that serves as an onboard acquisition and control unit for the sensors mounted on the robot (SWIR hyperspectral, LWIR thermal sensors and supporting sensors). Handles sensor triggering, data acquisition, time-stamping and georeferencing, local data storage as well as initial onboard data processing during field trials. Optionally also suitable for laboratory use for sensor development and data processing. - Broadcom BCM2712 Quad-Core 64-bit Arm Cortex-A76 CPU with 2,4 GHz and cryptography extensions, 512 KB L2-cache per core as well as 2 MB shared L3-cache - VideoCore VII GPU - 16 GB LPDDR4X-4267 SDRAM for processing large hyperspectral data streams and parallel sensor acquisition. - Interfaces & data processing: 2 × USB 3.0 (simultaneously 5 Gbit/s) and 2 × USB 2.0 ports - Gigabit Ethernet (PoE+ capable with separate HAT) - two 4-lane MIPI CSI/DSI connectors for camera and display - PCIe 2.0 x1 interface (16 Gbit/s via M.2 adapter) for NVMe SSDs or accelerator cards - Dual-4Kp60-HDMI output - standard 40-pin GPIO header with UART, SPI, I2C, I2S and PWM for sensor and peripheral control - integrated RP1 I/O controller - Real-time clock with external battery for reliable time-stamping in field use - integrated on/off switch. - Connectivity: Dual-band (2,4 / 5 GHz) 802.11ac WLAN and Bluetooth 5.0 / BLE for wireless configuration and data transmission - wired Gigabit Ethernet for high-bandwidth data transfer. - Power supply: Operation with 5 V DC via USB-C with Power Delivery support - for full peripheral operation, a 5 V / 5 A (27 W) power supply is required; restricted operation is possible at 5 V / 3 A. Suitable for supply via the power rails of the robot platform using a regulated voltage source. - Storage: microSD card slot (high-speed SDR104) for boot and data storage, optional NVMe SSD via the PCIe interface for faster system startup and large data recordings - Standard Linux file systems for direct further processing. - Integration into the robot system: Compact board (approx. 85 × 56 mm), mounted on the quadruped robot together with hyperspectral, thermal and LiDAR sensors - acts as a central acquisition unit for synchronised and georeferenced data acquisition. Active cooling recommended for continuous field use. - supports Python-based acquisition and processing pipelines for integration into existing sensor toolchains - low cost and broad community support facilitate maintenance and expansion.

Planning basis: Raspberry Pi 5-16 GB RAM Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0006: 1 Device Hyperspectral camera, thermal camera + robot mounting equipment. Hyperspectral camera: Pushbroom (line scan) SWIR hyperspectral imaging system for in-situ mapping of soils. Primarily intended for mounting on a quadruped field robot, with optional use in the laboratory on soil samples. Extends the existing BlackBullet V2 (500-1000 nm) by the SWIR range for mapping organic soil carbon and soil indicators - Sensor & imaging specification: spectral range of at least 950-1730 nm - spatial resolution at least 1280 pixels - InGaAs detector with holographic transmission grating - Input optics f/8 mm, 15 μm slit, LP950 filter - Line scan rate up to approx. 450 Hz at full resolution and up to 1300 Hz at ROI - Scan principle: Line scan hyperspectral sensor. - Illumination: 2 × Fast Medium Wave IR line radiator Minimum values: 900-1800 nm, 500 mm length, protective grille, 3000 mm cable for controlled SWIR illumination, as solar SWIR radiation in the field can be insufficient or unstable. - Integration into the robot system: Mounting bracket/adapter plate for camera and illumination on robots via tripod or gimbal as well as engineering and commissioning support. - Calibration: SWIR white reference panel for reflection calibration in field use. - Data acquisition: Acquisition and control via the manufacturer's software Thermal camera: Uncooled long-wave infrared (LWIR) thermal imaging camera core for robot-based in-situ mapping of soil and plant surface temperatures; serves as a proxy for evaporative cooling / soil moisture as well as drought stress of plants in field trials. Designed for integration on small robot systems - Sensor & imaging specification: 2 uncooled VOx microbolometer - Resolution at least 640 × 512 (or 336 × 256), pixel size 17 μm, spectral range at least 7,5-13,5 μm - thermal sensitivity (NEdT) below 30 mK (Industrial), 40 mK (Performance) and 50 mK (Commercial); radiometric output with temperature value per pixel (TLinear) - selectable lenses / fields of view (e.g. 19 mm, 32° horizontal for the 640 format). - Data acquisition: Digital video output (8- or 14-bit LVDS, parallel CMOS or BT.656) as well as analogue video signal - integrated image processing (DDE, AGC) and telemetry - Frame rate 30/60 Hz with optional <9 Hz export-compliant variant or equivalent - Integration into the robot acquisition system for georeferenced thermal data acquisition. - Power supply: Energy-efficient OEM camera core, suitable for battery or robot operation via the platform's power rails using an interface board. - Mounting & integration: Lightweight camera core (max 75 g with lens), mounted using a tripod or gimbal on the quadruped robot platform together with hyperspectral and LiDAR sensors - common electrical, mechanical and optical interfaces - Special features: Co-registration with SWIR hyperspectral and RGB data for combined mapping of soil moisture, carbon and plant stress; compact and robust for use in field robotics Planning basis: HAIP BlackIndustry SWIR 1.7 Max and HAIP BlackBright Fast Medium Wave IR as well as AIP BlackIndustry Station Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0007: 1 Device Highly mobile handheld measuring device for spectral or sensor-based soil analysis. Highly mobile handheld measuring device for spectral or sensor-based soil analysis in real time in the field; (measurement principle: (e.g. NIR spectroscopy / hyperspectral analysis; calibration requirements: regional / soil-type-dependent models) - Measured variables: Detection of organic carbon and relevant nutrients directly on site via NIR spectroscopy/hyperspectral analysis: - Spectrum: approx. 1400-2500 nm - Resolution of wavelengths: 1% of wavelengths - Speed: at least 1-3 s - Cooldown after measurement: max. 3 s - System components: The set includes the measuring probe (scanner unit), a USB charging cable/data cable as well as a custom-fit, robust protective case for safe transport in the field. - Service & protection: The configuration includes an optional warranty extension to a total of two years, provision of software updates during the service life of the cloud platform - IT & evaluation: Cloud-based data processing for the immediate provision of analysis data on mobile devices, export options for the data in common formats (e.g. CSV, API interface, GIS-compatible) are to be provided - USB interfaces, WLAN interface Planning basis: AgroCares Scanner F Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0008: 117 Devices Soil sensor technology. Extension of the existing soil sensor system for the comparable continuation of existing measurement series: 93x soil moisture sensor technology Field-ready sensor system for the continuous recording of soil moisture and soil temperature in agricultural or soil science field trials; designed for fully buryable installation in the soil and for long-term, autonomous measurement operation under outdoor conditions. Please refer to the technical requirements in the document 1.1 Performance specifications. Planning basis: TOMST TMS datalogger Execution as described or technically equivalent 4x soil tensiometer Field-ready tensiometer system for the continuous recording of soil water potential or soil suction tension in agricultural or soil science field trials; designed for fully or largely buryable installation in the soil and for long-term, autonomous measurement operation under outdoor conditions. Please refer to the technical requirements in the document 1.1 Performance specifications.

Planning basis: Tensiomark 0-7 (ecotech) Execution as described or technically equivalent 1x Acclima SDI-12-Sensor Reader-Kit Mobile field device for displaying and saving measured values from digital SDI-12 sensors; specialised for on-site inspection and mobile data acquisition. Please refer to the technical requirements in document 1.1 Specifications. Planning basis: Acclima SDI-12-Sensor Reader-Kit Execution as described or technically equivalent 5x LoRa soil sensor system Professional outdoor set for wireless networking and data transmission of soil sensors via LoRaWAN; connection to IP networks optionally via WLAN, Ethernet, 3G or 4G. Please refer to the technical requirements in document 1.1 Specifications. Planning basis: LoRaWAN gateway Execution as described or technically equivalent 14x Eco-acoustic sensor systems (bioacoustic logger with contact microphones) Cost-effective, autonomous eco-acoustic recording system for continuous, non-invasive recording of soil fauna activity as well as the acoustic surface backdrop during field trials; designed for distributed, replicated deployment under the Agri-PV areas as a biological indicator for soil health. Please refer to the technical requirements in document 1.1 Specifications. Planning basis: AudioMoth Execution as described or technically equivalent Lot LOT-0009: 1 Device Field measuring device for air permeability. Portable, computer-aided field measuring device for the automatic determination of air conductivity or air permeability of soils; designed for soil-physical field measurements for the characterisation of the air-filled pore space, soil aeration as well as the soil-structural and hydrological properties of soils. - Measurement & control technology: Measuring system for generating a defined air flow in the examined soil volume via a measuring chamber - Determination of the flow rate via the pressure drop at a calibrated measuring restrictor or an equivalent method - Recording of the pressure difference across the flow-through soil volume by means of pressure sensors for determining the pressure gradient - automatic calculation of the pneumatic conductivity according to the Darcy equation or an equivalent physically recognised method. Measuring range of the pneumatic conductivity at least 0,03-30 cm/s - Measuring pressure at least in the range 1-3 hPa - The system must be suitable for different measurement situations, in particular for measurements with a measuring chamber for homogeneous flow, surface measuring chamber for inhomogeneous flow in the undisturbed soil volume as well as adapter solution for measurements on core samples or equivalent measuring chamber/adapter concepts. - Data acquisition: Integrated microprocessor-controlled acquisition, display, storage (min. 128 KB) and management of the measurement data in the device - automatic storage of the data from the connected sensors as well as the calibration data of the measuring chambers - Possibility for labelling or assignment of the respective measuring point in the data set - Recording of at least pneumatic conductivity, pressure difference or pressure gradient, flow rate or measurement variables calculated therefrom, measuring point identification, measuring chamber/calibration data. Data transmission to a computer via interface cable, USB or equivalent interface - Data export in a common, further-processable format must be possible. Planning basis: PL-300 Field measuring device Execution as described or technically equivalent
