sig_d8d1e6875ec91fd9f2e7.description: 1. The subject of the contract is the preparation, launch and provision by the Contractor to the Agency for Restructuring and Modernisation of Agriculture of an IT service in a SaaS model, enabling the automatic identification of land cover classes based on geospatial data, using artificial intelligence technology, in accordance with the Service Description constituting Appendix No. 1 to the draft contract provisions (hereinafter: "dcp") constituting Appendix No. 9 to the contract notice specifications (hereinafter: "CNS") and the Tender Form (Appendix No. 1 to the CNS). Land cover classes: 1.1 Basic land cover classes (hereinafter: "basic classes") – i.e. obligatory, required by the Contracting Authority, land cover classes for which the minimum classification quality indicators amounting to at least: Overall Accuracy 0,85; Recall 0,80; Precision 0,80.: a) Transport areas – (Management Fields (hereinafter: "MF") : K) b) Forests – (MF: L, Z, ZS, O, R) c) Industrial and urbanised areas – (MF: U) d) Settlements with buildings – (MF: D). Note: For the basic classes (classes a-d), the levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) shall be binding on the Contractor in accordance with the declaration submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. 1.2 Rewarded land cover classes (hereinafter: "rewarded classes") – i.e. non-obligatory, offered additionally by the Contractor within the scope of the tender evaluation criteria (ch. IX pt. 2.2 and 2.3 of the CNS), for which the tender will receive additional points, are: e) Waters – (MF: W, OM, OW, R2, R10), f) Other non-agricultural areas – (MF: I). Note: For the rewarded classes (classes e and f), the minimum levels of the classification quality indicators (Overall Accuracy; Recall; Precision) have not been specified, but their levels shall be binding on the Contractor only in the event of them being offered at a level at least equal to that for the basic classes, in accordance with the declaration for individual classes submitted by the Contractor in the Tender Form. Rewarded classes shall be taken into account in the Contract provided they meet the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 2. The scope of the contract includes the processing of geospatial data in raster and vector formats and the generation of results in the form of vector layers presenting land cover classes, along with the assignment of a classification confidence level for each object. The generated data must be characterised by geometric correctness and topological consistency. The identification of land cover classes is carried out in accordance with the classification used in the Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) and covers the full range of required classes and their representation in the form of spatial objects. The functionality of the service includes the visualisation of spatial data, the presentation of identification results, their analysis and editing, as well as the export of result data in standard formats and integration with other spatial data services and sources. Data processing should enable the handling of large volumes using parallel processing mechanisms, while maintaining the required performance. 3. As part of the contract, the Contractor shall provide the data processing environment, software and components necessary to carry out the identification process, including artificial intelligence models and the mechanisms for their operation. 4. As part of the execution of the contract, the possibility of selecting input data sources, importing them and processing them to the extent specified by the user must be ensured, both for entire datasets and their extracted parts, taking into account the use of data supporting the identification process. The use of artificial intelligence models and the provision of metrics for evaluating their quality, in particular Overall Accuracy, Precision and Recall, along with the possibility of analysing and reporting them, is envisaged. 5. The Contracting Authority requires the provision of an adequate level of availability, security and reliability, in particular regarding user authentication and authorisation, permissions management, data encryption and business continuity. 6. The Contractor is obliged to provide technical support, deliver user and technical documentation and conduct training for users. 7. As part of the Contract, the Contractor shall provide the Contracting Authority with up to 50 man-hours of consultations regarding the provided Service, during the period referred to in & 3 para. 1 of the dcp. 8. The Contractor shall deliver to the Contracting Authority the user and technical documentation described in pt. 6.4 of Appendix No. 1 to the dcp and educational materials/instructions necessary for using the Service, by the service launch deadline referred to in & 3 para. 2 of the dcp. 9. The consultation service referred to in pt. 8 shall be provided by the Contractor in Polish, including the interface (GUI, Graphical User Interface) to the Service, as well as the documentation referred to in pt. 8 - must be prepared by the Contractor in Polish. 10. The Contractor is obliged to present the results of the land cover class identification for the set subject to evaluation, along with the result data and error matrices by saving them in a dedicated workspace, in accordance with the procedure described in ch. I.1.1 of the CNS, to confirm compliance with the minimum classification quality indicators specified for the basic classes. 11. The Contracting Authority requires that the execution of the subject of the contract take place under the terms and conditions specified in the draft contract provisions together with appendices (hereinafter: dcp) constituting Appendix No. 9 to the CNS.
sig_d8d1e6875ec91fd9f2e7.title: Land cover class identification service using artificial intelligence (AI) methods for the purpose of updating the Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS)

sig_d95773dc2017b2df2a9e.description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor/Hickam, Hawaii intends to award Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Multiple Award Contract (MAC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity(IDIQ) to provide marine resource technical services throughout the Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC) Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas worldwide as needed. This solicitation will be issued as an unrestricted procurement with a partial small business set-aside that will result in the award of multiple award contracts that are comprised of two major divisions. The resulting multiple award contracts will be comprised of two major divisions: An Unrestricted Division and a partial Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division. The work shall be located primarily in Hawaii, Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). The Government may also require marine resource technical services throughout the NAVFAC Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas in the NAVFAC AOR worldwide as needed. All Marine Resource Technical Services conducted under the resultant contracts shall conform to the statutes, regulations, instructions and guidelines in compliance with the Request for Proposal (RFP). The resulting contract will include requirements that include but are not limited to, the following: (1) Coordination of Monitoring Projects and Subject Matter Experts, (2) Data Management, (3) Analysis and Reporting, (4) Visual Surveys, (5) Diving and Marine Resource Surveys, (6) Marine Species Observers, (7) Passive Acoustic Monitoring, (8) Marine Species Tagging and Tracking, (9) Photo Identification, (10) Behavioral Studies, (11) Habitat Restoration, (12) Coral Translocation, (13) Anomaly Avoidance Surveys, (14) Event Reconstruction and Environmental Data Integration, (15) Ecological Analysis, (16) Outreach, (17) Miscellaneous Marine Biological Resource Services, (18) Biomonitoring, (19) Biosecurity and Aquatic Invasive Species Management, (20) Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMPs), (21) NEPA, Environmental Planning and Supporting Studies, (22) GIS Mapping, (23) Endangered Species Act (ESA) Biological Opinions, (24) Magnuson Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) Assessments, and (25) Marine Mammal Protection Act. Work will be performed in accordance with the requirements of the Performance Work Statement, and may involve regulatory compliance, planning, analyzing, and various related services on any one or a combination of more than one task order. Exact location of each effort will be designated on individual Task Orders. The entire term of the contract is a maximum of $99 million or 90 months (consisting of a 12-month base period, six (6) 12-month option periods and one (1) 6-month extension of services period), whichever occurs first. Task orders will typically range between $3,500 and $10,000,000. Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. The Government makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, during the term of the contract, a minimum of $5,000 is guaranteed for each awardee under the contract. As task orders are awarded that exceed the $5,000, the $5,000 minimum guarantee will be deobligated and the Government’s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Projects competed to the unrestricted division will require a minimum of 18% of the work to be subcontracted to small businesses. Approximately $68.5M will be work performed in the NAVFAC Pacific Area of Responsibility (AOR), $15M in the NAVFAC Hawaii AOR and $15.5M in the NAVFAC Marianas AOR. These amounts may fluctuate with the potential need for the different types of specific services listed above and whether adequate competition exists within the SBSA Division and those contractors are capable of successfully executing those services. If one or no SBSA Division contractors submit a proposal in response to a task order request for proposal (RFP), the Contracting Officer may compete the task order amongst the Unrestricted Division contractors. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services and the corresponding small business size standard is $19.5 million (which will determine eligibility for awards under the Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division). A MAC is a contract awarded from a single solicitation and may result in award to multiple contractors. This procurement consists of one solicitation with the intent to award no more than six (6) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type service contracts to the offerors whose proposals, conforming to the solicitation, represents the most advantageous offers to the Government resulting in the best value, price and non-price factors considered. The Government reserves the right to award more than six (6) contracts if it is determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Successful awardees will compete for future work during the term of the contract. This is a best value, trade off procurement. The Government intends to evaluate proposals without conducting discussions with any Offeror, except for clarifications as described in FAR 15.306(a). However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions with Offerors, if required. The non-price evaluation factors will be 1) Experience; 2) Sample Project; 3) Safety; 4) Small Business Utilization and Participation; and 5) Past Performance. Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are considered of equal importance to each other, and when combined, are equal in importance to the past performance evaluation Factor 5. When the proposal is evaluated as a whole, the technical factors and past performance factor combined are significantly more important than price. The evaluation of the Price Factor will be based on the sample project attached to the solicitation. The sample project is for evaluation purposes only and will not be awarded on the contract. The solicitation will be available on or about 22 October 2026 for viewing and downloading at the Contract Opportunities website at https://sam.gov/. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Requests for additional information may be addressed to the attention of Ms. Rachel Gerakas via e-mail at rachel.m.gerakas.civ@us.navy.mil, Danika Kamikawa via email at danika.m.kamikawa.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Casey Sugihara via e-mail at casey.c.sugihara.civ@us.navy.mil. Amendments will be posted to the website https://sam.gov/. It is the Offeror’s responsibility to periodically check the Contract Opportunities website for any amendments or notices to the solicitation. Offeror(s) must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov/ to participate in this procurement.

sig_d962a34f9120eab68dbd.description: Published by the Canton of Geneva, acting as the project owner, but monitored/co-piloted by the French and Swiss partners of the Cross-Border Water Community, this call for tenders is aimed at firms or groups of representatives specialising in: - The transformation of data into information and knowledge to support the decision-making process (technical and political) related to environmental issues. - The design and maintenance of data platforms to support territorial environmental public policies. - The popularisation of scientific data to enable public communication and citizen interaction. Why an observatory? - A space for dialogue to support political decision-making, answer questions, and connect public policies - Understanding the functioning of water bodies (at the cross-border scale of Greater Geneva) to analyse the ecosystem services provided; - Understanding natural and anthropogenic pressures on resources (surface and groundwater); - Analysing tensions between uses (current and future), facilitating arbitration; - Finding innovative and sustainable solutions (without taking more, can we redistribute more equitably); - Monitoring the impact of the future cross-border strategy and its actions; - Managing crises (contingency plan) Project co-financed within the framework of the INTERREG cross-border cooperation programme. The mission entrusted to the AMO aims to: - Support the definition of the objectives, scope, indicators, and operating procedures of the observatory. - Identify needs, resources, and data available and to be mobilised. - Co-construct, with stakeholders, a sustainable mechanism for governance, financing, and coordination of the observatory. - Propose an operational action plan and a phasing of implementation. The pilot's mission is to demonstrate the feasibility of building a shared cross-border vision of water issues.
sig_d962a34f9120eab68dbd.title: PROJECT MANAGEMENT ASSISTANCE (AMO) FOR THE CREATION OF A CROSS-BORDER OBSERVATORY FOR WATER AND ITS USES IN THE GREATER GENEVA AREA

sig_d972734870eb32fd0eef.description: The purpose of this contract is the maintenance and execution of various minor adaptation works on the installations of the Operations Support Unit, upper part, of the Synoptic equipment, and of the fire safety system resetting systems of terminals T2ABCD, Terminal 1, Terminal 3, MN Modules, Terminals 2F, 2E, 2G, S3 and S4 at PARIS-CHARLES DE GAULLE Airport. The contractor's missions will be to guarantee optimum availability of the functionalities of the Operations Support Unit, the durability of the hardware and the assurance of being able to restore the application at any time, and to implement quality maintenance based on a methodology respecting professional standards, the maintenance of its agents' skills and the speed of its interventions. The operations delegated to the contractor are Firstly, maintenance operations comprising: • IT backups, • Preventive maintenance of hardware, • Corrective maintenance (repairs or replacement of defective hardware and corrections of software anomalies), • Software publisher contracts, • Software updates, • Any on-call services and technical assistance. • The drafting of intervention reports • The drafting of annual maintenance reports Secondly, various minor works known as adaptation works such as: • Work on hardware and software, • Migrations or major version upgrades, • Supplies of hardware, • Study days on specific applications. The Contractor shall constantly maintain an advisory role with respect to the awarding authority in order to inform the latter of adaptations making it possible to keep the system in a perfect state of evolutivity. sig_d986ff37b1335689accf.description: The Agency for Real Estate and Urban Renewal (the Customer) signs many contracts with suppliers in different branches. The contracting authority needs to follow-up the service providers ́ seriousness for the purpose of preventing work-life crime and breach of contract. The Agency thus needs a system that collates and makes relevant information available for uncovering risks at the department's suppliers. The system is planned to be used for background checks by suppliers before signing the contract and for following-up risk conditions during the contract ́s lifetime. See the attached document for a more detailed description of the Contracting Authority ́s needs. Market Feedback This time we would like to check if there are suppliers in the market that we are unfamiliar with. sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.description: NOTE! This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation for the procurement of a shared vehicle monitoring tool and is inviting suppliers to a market dialogue. The objective of the procurement of the shared vehicle management tool is to implement monitoring in accordance with the micro-mobility permit (18 section) referred to in the Act on Transport Services (3030/2025) within the area of the City of Espoo. The management tool is used to collect and monitor shared vehicle movement data and to set operating rules and restrictions for them. The tool aims to improve urban safety and facilitate urban planning based on shared vehicle usage and regulatory data. The subject of the procurement is a shared vehicle monitoring tool procured as a service as follows: - System as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) - Commissioning and customisation of the service for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Further development and expert services of the system according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the shared vehicle monitoring tool are aimed to cover the following: - Basic functions of the management tool, i.e. collecting and displaying usage data of approximately 6000 shared vehicles to the user. - Real-time and visual user interface for monitoring shared vehicles, i.e. displaying map-based information regarding shared vehicles and traffic operators based on the location data of the shared vehicles to the user. - Setting area- and shared-vehicle-operator-specific rules and restrictions for shared vehicles, as well as providing the user with notifications based on the rules and restrictions. - Analysis functions of the collected data as well as scenario analyses (proposals) on rules and measures to be set based on the collected data. - Reporting and statistical functionalities. - Management of user roles and access rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement of the shared vehicle monitoring tool. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the call for tenders. SCHEDULE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue will tentatively be conducted in two phases: 1. Via Teams tentatively during week 51. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite 3-5 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the responses to the request for information. The objective of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with the products on the market, for example through supplier demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue for comments approximately during weeks 51-2. The second phase of the market dialogue will be conducted electronically. Written material will be sent to all those who have registered for the market dialogue for review approximately during weeks 51-2. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary call for tenders, the requirement specification and the contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. The contracting authority's objective is to launch the actual procurement procedure in the spring of 2026 and the implementation project by May 2026 at the latest, so that the new system can be taken into use in the summer of 2026. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND REGISTERING FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We kindly ask suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue to register in writing by 10.12.2025 at 16.00 to the address hankinta@espoo.fi. Clearly title your registration message, e.g. "Market dialogue: Procurement of shared vehicle monitoring tool - registration [Company name]". Please provide the name of your contact person at the same time. The market dialogue and the information provided therein shall not bind any participating party, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the subsequent actual tender contest. The official call for tenders will only be published after the market dialogues have ended. Responses will be handled confidentially.
sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.title: Market dialogue invitation and request for information: Procurement of a tracking tool for shared vehicles

The checks carried out to ensure the lawful implementation of programmes serve the effective execution of Financial Instrument Programmes. By correcting errors identified during integrated checks in good time, programme risks can be mitigated by ensuring that projects coming within the purview of organisations conducting external audits (e.g. the State Audit Office, EUTAF, EU SAO) comply with legal requirements and that disbursed support is not recovered. Since the EDOP MA is responsible for the successful implementation of the programme, checking the work of the Fund of Funds Implementing Organisation (FFIO) is among its most prominent tasks during its activities. This task shall be performed in accordance with the provisions of the Audit Plan for the given year, approved by the Director-General of the EDOP MA. The subject of this call for tenders is the provision of economic consultancy during a total of 1 checks carried out by the EDOP MA based on the Audit Plan for the given year (2025.). The detailed technical description and conditions are set out in the procurement documents.

sig_da733f462fe04eea8224.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Polkka - Pohjois-Karjalan tukipalvelut oy is a publicly owned service company that produces high-quality catering, cleaning and logistics services for its owners. The company's owners are the Wellbeing Services County of North Karelia, the towns of Joensuu, Kitee and Nurmes, and the municipalities of Heinävesi, Ilomantsi, Tohmajärvi and Liperi. Polkka operates throughout the region of North Karelia, and its administration is located in Joensuu. The company employs a total of approximately 800 staff. Through its operations, Polkka supports the daily lives and well-being of the region's residents by providing reliable and efficient support services. Polkka is planning a procurement procedure where the subject of the procurement is financial and personnel management services and the associated system package. The subject of the procurement includes financial and personnel management services as well as the implementation project for the system package, user rights, support and maintenance services, separately ordered supplementary expert services, and options for additional procurements. Polkka's financial and personnel management services are currently outsourced to Meidän IT ja Talous Oy. The services are managed in the systems administered by the service provider, the key components of which are Raindance, MRDP, Rondo and UDP in financial management and Populus, Titania, Timecon and RegWeb in personnel management. The procurement provisionally includes the following functions and high-level functionalities: Financial management - Superuser service - Basic data - Purchase invoices and purchase ledger - Sales invoicing and sales ledger - Accounting and financial statements - Payment traffic - Reporting and statistics - Financial planning and budgeting - Cash management - Treasury management - Internal accounting - Fixed assets - Electronic archiving Personnel management - Superuser service - Personnel and employment lifecycle management, HRM - Payroll, remuneration and rewarding - Rostering - Working time management - Travel management - Work ability and well-being as well as occupational health - Advanced reporting - Personnel performance and skills development, HRD - Recruitment - Electronic signature - Electronic archiving The procurement will be implemented through an open procedure. The preliminary schedule for the procurement is as follows: - Market dialogue rounds 3-5/2026 - Procurement 5-8/2026 - Implementation project 8-12/2026 Operators who have registered for the market dialogue and are interested in the procurement have the opportunity to answer preliminary questions raised by the contracting authority, participate in upcoming market dialogue sessions and comment on preliminary tender documents in technical dialogue. In the next phase of the market dialogue, five separate market dialogue sessions will be held via Teams. The market dialogue sessions will be held at the following times: - on Monday 13.4. between 8-15 - on Tuesday 14.4. between 12-16 - on Friday 17.4. between 10-16 If more than five operators interested in the procurement register for the market dialogue, the operators will be selected for the market dialogue sessions based on their answers to the preliminary questions. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register, provide answers to the preliminary questions and submit the requested additional information by 7.4.2026 at 12 to the address: tuomas.vepsa@joensuu.fi. Registrations must be given the following subject line: "Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun: Tahe-hankinta". Registrations must include the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Answers to preliminary questions - Names of the offered system or systems - Solution descriptions of the offered system or systems The sessions will be held via Microsoft Teams. We will send a separate invitation to the Teams meeting to everyone selected for the session. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out an actual tendering procedure. The information presented in the market survey notice is preliminary, non-binding and indicative prior information. Answering or failing to answer the invitation to the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible tendering procedure. Information provided in the market dialogue does not bind the parties. No compensation is paid for participation in the market dialogue. Information provided by operators participating in the market dialogue will be treated confidentially, and the names or other information of the operators participating in the market dialogue will not be published.
sig_da733f462fe04eea8224.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of comprehensive financial and personnel management services for Polkka - Pohjois-Karjalan tukipalvelut oy

sig_da8c7ba6d98c16118d02.description: Met Éireann provides 24/7/365 operational forecast and warning services to the public. These services are provided digitally through a web portal (met.ie) and native mobile apps for Android and iOS operating systems. There is also a web portal providing access to observations from private weather stations (wow.met.ie). Met Éireann will be looking to procure hosting, maintenance and support and development services for these applications.. We are looking to work with organisations who can: 1) Configure and maintain a hosting solution to meet our challenging technical needs. The system will be expected to provide high availability and georesilience across multiple regions with contingency and disaster recovery applications to ensure continuity of service. Any infrastructure solution will be expected to meet the highest security standards assessed by penetration testing. 2) Develop the web portals and mobile applications based on the requirements provided. The web portal and mobile apps provide the following key services to the public and stakeholders: a. Communication and dissemination of weather and marine warnings, plus weather and environmental advisories. b. Communication of weather, marine and tailored forecasts eg farming commentary c. Presentation of radar and satellite imagery d. Presentation of analysis charts and data from Met Éireann’s observations network e. Presentation of data from private weather stations (wow.met.ie) f. Dissemination of climate services g. Interactive access to climate datasets h. Access to education and outreach materials, including the Met Éireann podcast i. Access to Met Éireann publications j. Access to information on Met Éireann’s scientific activities k. General information on Met Éireann including news articles and vacancies l. Contact helpdesk for various support channels, for example digital queries, climate enquiries m. Access to data, either through web page download or hosting links accessed from data.gov.ie The bulk of these pages have Irish language equivalents in line with Met Éireann’s obligations under the Irish Language Act. All web and mobile applications are subject to accessibility standards, which are routinely tested using an automated scan provisioned by the National Disability Authority (NDA). The anticipated development projects over the contract term are likely to include some or all of the following, but this list is not exhaustive: • Modernisation of mobile application code • Improvements to Content Management System (CMS) capability to enhance usability for Met Éireann staff. • Set up an archive to reduce operational load • Extension of Product Services (shared server) • Consolidation of Data Services – including extended use of APIs • Failover / DR solutions and processes for critical components • Enhancements to the 10 day location based forecast (Meteogram) • Ongoing enhancement of existing functionality as specified by Met Éireann stakeholders The application components will be expected to meet security and accessibility standards with support for Irish language content and responsive design. There should also be the ability to track analytics for each system component, with dashboards, notifications and alarms for Met Éireann operational staff. 3) Support and maintain the infrastructure and applications. Maintenance will be expected to be an ongoing activity for the infrastructure and applications, ensuring that components are kept up to date and overall system health is sustained. Support for the infrastructure and essential applications will be provided on a 24/7/365 basis to ensure continuity of critical services to the public and stakeholders. Our services are subject to intense scrutiny not just from the general public and stakeholders, but also through traditional and social media, hence short support response times will be set to minimise any loss of service time. This is necessary to ensure that Met Éireann’s operational teams have visibility that any issue is being investigated. The support team will not be working in isolation, there should be a close, collaborative relationship with Met Éireann’s operational IT, third party application support and forecast office teams. Further, well defined processes for management of critical scenarios would be established, with easily deployed failover/contingency solutions if the underlying issue will require significant time to resolve. Some of these failover and contingency solutions are already partially available, and further enhancement is included in the proposed development activities presented earlier. Lower priority issues should still be acknowledged outside of business hours, with resolution provided during normal business hours. All of the applications mentioned above are fully public and freely accessible and so potential tenderers are encouraged to review the functionality while assessing a response.
sig_da8c7ba6d98c16118d02.title: Met Éireann Public Web Services

sig_daab666837f29f6498a0.description: BlueLight Commercial (BLC) are looking to establish an agreement that police forces and other interested agencies can use to provide a quick, cost effective, reliable and compliant contracting solution for ANPR services. This Preliminary Market Engagement notice and link to a survey document provides the opportunity to: 1. seek input from suppliers on the procurement approach and; 2. identify suppliers that may be able to supply the services; 3. ensure capacity among suppliers in relation to any contract awarded; 4. identify contractual terms and particularly those that may prove problematic; 5. help to confirm the procurement procedure, set any conditions required to participate and confirm award criteria; 6. prepare an appropriate tender notice and tender documents for issue to the market at large. develop our requirements and approach to its procurement; Presently, working with ANPR specialists a framework solution has been drafted consisting of the following lots: Lot 1 – ANPR SYSTEMS PURCHASE to include all items used to provide a fit for purpose, functioning ANPR operational set up. This includes camera systems, cabling and mounting brackets telecommunication capability to transmit appropriate information to operation and analytical bases, ANPR servers and other Back Office Facility (BOF) equipment to aid smooth ANPR operation. Lot 2 – INSTALLATION & REMOVAL OF EQUIPMENT to include redeployment where organisations do not have this capability. Lot 3 - CONSULTANCY SERVICES that includes surveying, system design, modification, proof of concept and integration with existing networks. Lot 4 - SERVICING & MAINTENANCE of the existing ANPR systems identified in Lot 1. Lot 5 - ANPR RELATED CIVILS WORK to prepare a site for the installation of ANPR systems. The work will include ground preparation for install of cabling to provide electrical power, installation of poles or other furniture on which to mount ANPR systems, cabinet purchase and installation, approvals to work safely at the site and access services, using appropriately qualified personnel. BLC is looking for respondents to comment on the lotting structure, capacity to provide the service across the UK, the best way to price services to provide fair comparison, observations on contractual terms with particular regard to sub contracting. The current proposed approach may be modified or changed following receipt of the pre-market engagement feedback. To provide BLC with feedback on the proposals please complete the survey at the following link:- https://www.smartsurvey.co.uk/s/BLC0254_ANPR_Dec2025/ Lot 1: .

sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.description: DSB wishes to gain a better understanding of SAP RISE, and therefore an invitation to a market dialogue concerning this is extended. Background: DSB currently uses an SAP S/4HANA solution, which supports a large number of administrative business processes in the company. S/4HANA runs on-premises via an infrastructure and operations agreement with TCS. This agreement expires in the summer of 2028, which is why DSB must carry out an EU tender presumably in 2027. Against this background, DSB is considering whether the tender should comprise either: - Infrastructure and operation services regarding SAP S/4HANA based on on-premises or, - migration of DSB’s SAP S/4HANA solution to a SaaS solution in a private cloud – which is currently marketed under the name SAP RISE. Therefore, DSB wishes via market dialogue to gain insight into what suppliers in the market offer related to SAP RISE. DSB expects the individual supplier to provide a total overview of deliverables and commercial terms. DSB wishes, among other things, answers to: 1) Description of the current market. 2) Description of the supplier's footprint in the market. Generally and regarding SAP RISE. 3) Contract setup including interfaces to SAP SE. 4) Listing of services linked to the service: 4.1) Which services are delivered as standard? 4.2) Which services can be purchased additionally? 4.3) How are these services designed with regard to SLAs? 5) Description of cooperation model. 6) How and according to which structure does settlement of ongoing operations take place? 7) Description of model for transition and settlement of this. Preferably with TCO assessments. 8) Description of hardware, data centres, and geography used. 9) Description of IT security model and IT security management. DSB expects to conduct interviews with a selection of suppliers in December 2025 and January 2026. The purpose of the interviews is to gather information on which solutions and services are offered in the market. DSB plans to conduct market dialogue meetings with a maximum of six suppliers. If more than the six suppliers apply, DSB will make a representative selection among the expressions of interest received.
sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding SAP RISE

sig_dac5acb6f8f545e13f46.description: This is a MARKET EXPLORATION. The scope of services includes the development, provision and further development of interoperable software components and standardised data exchange procedures for medical image and health data within a nationwide research infrastructure for digital pathology. For the establishment and sustainable operation of the research infrastructure, an independent scope of services is required that ensures the standardised and interoperable exchange of medical image, report and metadata between different primary systems, research platforms and clinical information systems. The objective of the services to be procured is the provision of interoperable basic components which enable the use of internationally established standards and support their sustainable further development within a nationwide research infrastructure. From the perspective of the University Hospital, the requirement can currently only be met by one market participant. This market exploration is being carried out to verify this assumption. The contracting authority reserves the right to take further steps under procurement law.
sig_dac5acb6f8f545e13f46.title: MARKET EXPLORATION in accordance with § 28 VgV - Development, provision and further development of interoperable software components and standardised data exchange

sig_dacbe47d4f288288e62d.description: The subject of the public contract is supplies, services and necessary related construction works required for the implementation of the Development of the Olomouc Transport Information Centre project. The scope of performance includes in particular the modernisation of the server and communication infrastructure, the implementation of cooperative intelligent transport systems (C-ITS) and the expansion of the equipment of light-controlled intersections including vehicle-to-infrastructure communication units. The public contract is implemented in the form of performance or function requirements (also referred to as the Design & Build method). The selected tenderer shall ensure within the performance of the public contract: - the completion or preparation of all background documentation, in particular production, implementation, workshop or project documentation, necessary for the implementation of the project, - engineering activities for the purpose of procuring all necessary decisions, permits, opinions and other acts of concerned state administration or self-government bodies necessary for the implementation of the project, - the provision of supplies of all products, equipment, technologies, applications, software and other elements necessary for the implementation of the project, - the provision of all services, works and activities necessary for the implementation of the project, - the execution of all necessary related construction works required for the implementation of the project, - all other works and activities necessary for the implementation of the project, - the commissioning of the system, - the operation of the system (including servicing and maintenance) for a specified period. Further details shall be determined by the contracting authority's technical specification, the bill of quantities and the required schedule.

sig_daf824c9a8d5bdfdae63.description: DWP Estates is embarking on the delivery of the Estates 2030 Strategy and Vision, which will incorporate a new Estates 2030 Strategic Pipeline Optimisation Programme (SPOP). The Estates 2030 Strategic Pipeline Optimisation Programme is a DWP Estates led strategic transformation programme that will support a series of future re-procurements and ensure alignment with the design and development of a new and evolving Target Operating Model, incorporating a review of the internal DWP Estates organisation and ways of working. This programme will undertake a comprehensive review of the significant and complex Estates strategic pipeline to ensure the supply chain is best organised and strategically placed to support the delivery of the DWP Estates 2030 strategy. This programme will help to identify opportunities for improvements and efficiencies in future service delivery across the Estates portfolio. Using Industry Best Practice and Market Insight, SPOP will incorporate an Estates internal operating model review, capability mapping, assessment and future structure (post insource/outsource analysis), mobilising new services that are insourced to DWP as required. Consideration will be given for the Data, System and Reporting requirements of DWP Estates and an optimal delivery model based on market insight and optimal strategic delivery. At the heart of this programme, a key objective will be to design, deliver, transition and stabilise the movement from the second iteration of the DWP Estates Integrator Model services to the future service design, based on the most effective use of technology, data and innovation through market analysis. This will include supporting a Delivery Model Assessment (DMA) (a "Make or Buy" decision) for the current contract. Due to the varied, specialist nature and scope of services required for this Programme, the Authority is seeking external strategic advice and support across a number of areas including but not limited: - Real Estate and Property expertise - End to end Target Operating Model Design in the context of a Real Estate, Property & Workplace Management Environment - Data, Data Management, Business Intelligence and Insights in the context of Real Estate, Property & Workplace Management Environment - Technology and Systems Design and Integration, inclusive of, but not limited to overall CAFM design, Integration and overall Real Estate systems landscape - Market Insight and Analysis - Change Management - Organisational Design and Development - Contract Transition Support (Mobilisation, Exit & Demobilisation, Transition and Stabilisation) - Programme Assurance The supplier will be required to have a flexible approach to the delivery of this contract, and the Authority may, at its sole discretion, choose to call upon any of the service lines listed above, at any time during the Contract Term. The Authority shall not be required to maintain a minimum level of usage or commitment across any Service Line. Charges shall only apply to Service Lines that are actively engaged. Please refer to the specification and associated tender documents for further details. Lot 1: .
sig_daf824c9a8d5bdfdae63.title: DWP Estates 2030 Strategic Pipeline Optimisation Programme (SPOP)

Request for Information (RFI) The U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) is seeking information and sources capable of providing the services described below. The purpose of this notice is to gather capabilities and market information pertinent to acquisition planning. The responses to this Request for Information / Market Research notice will contribute to determining the method of procurement and identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This notice does not constitute a request for quotes or proposals. Submission of any information in response to this notice is purely voluntary. The Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. This RFI does not obligate the Government to any specific course of action or guarantee a future solicitation or contract for services described in this notice. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. Respondents are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or sensitive information contained in their response. DESCRIPTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires comprehensive legal assistance, including alternate dispute resolution (ADR), court support, and litigation support services to support VA's mission. VA's Office of General Counsel, and program offices routinely require surge and specialized support for litigation, administrative hearings, EEO complaints, investigations, and related proceedings that cannot be fully met with in-house staff alone. Contractors shall provide support services, for ADR neutrals, court reporting, transcription, training, and other related legal services across VA facilities nationwide, ensuring continuity of legal operations, reduced procurement lead time, and consistent quality and pricing across the enterprise. Please see the attached DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS). SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS If your organization is interested and capable of providing these services please provide your response to this notice by e-mail to Jennifer.Swift2@va.gov and Justin.Sawicki@va.gov no later than 1:00 PM ET on October 13, 2026 with a Subject line of RFI # 36C10X26Q0244 VA CLAIM. If your company has the potential capability to perform these contract services, please respond to this Request for Information by providing a capability statement. The number of pages is limited to a total of 10 pages; size shall be no greater than 8 1/2" x 11". The top, bottom, left and right margins shall be a minimum of one inch each. Font size shall be no smaller than 12-point. Times New Roman fonts are required. The capabilities statement must include the following information: INFORMATION REQUEST Does the Draft Performance Work Statement provide you with enough detail to propose labor categories for each objective? If not, what information can the VA provide to enable you to build teams and properly price the work? Please note, the number of hours are not determined at the BPA level. Are the objectives sufficiently clear to enable you to draft a Technical Approach for the work? If not, which objectives are unclear? Is the PWS broad enough to account for industry changes over the next five years? Are there any industry standards not adequately addressed or missing in the PWS? VA is seeking contractors that can provide these services requiring the assistance throughout the various office locations across the United States. Do you have the capability to provide support services on a national scale for all tasks? If not, which tasks can you provide support? This procurement will serve as a VA wide, BPA and may result in services performed in all US states and territories. Is this feasible for a small pool of vendors, or is locality/region-based vendors more appropriate? What is your firm’s approach to fulfilling these tasks? What contract type or pricing structure does your firm expect to see for this acquisition based on the PWS (Firm-Fixed-Price, Cost, T&M/LH)? Please explain your rationale. Does your firm have the ability to adequately staff and maintain personnel to support tasks and deliverables within the PWS on short notice (24-48 hours)? What are the challenges to hiring/maintaining these personnel? Which labor categories would you use? What are your firm’s thoughts regarding the proposed NAICS Code and PSC? If your firm believes there are more accurate NAICS/PSC Codes to consider, please provide the number and rationale. Is your firm an SDVOSB, VOSB, SB, or Large Business? What additional information if any do you have to share with the technical and procurement teams? It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided. No basis for a claim against the Government shall arise from a response to this Request for Information or Government use of any information provided. Failure to submit information in sufficient detail may result in considering a company as not a viable source and may influence competition and set-aside decisions. Regardless of the information obtained from this Request for Information, the Government reserves the right to consider any arrangement as deemed appropriated for this requirement. Respondents are advised, the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response to this Request for Information. Department of Veterans Affairs Comprehensive Legal Assistance & Integrated Management (VA CLAIM) 1. Introduction The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires a broad, flexible source of comprehensive legal assistance, alternate dispute resolution (ADR), court support, and integrated case management services to support VA's mission of serving Veterans, their families, and survivors. VA's Office of General Counsel, regional counsel offices, and program offices routinely require surge and specialized support for litigation, administrative hearings, EEO complaints, investigations, and related proceedings that cannot be fully met with in-house staff alone. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) establishes a pre-vetted pool of qualified Contractors capable of rapidly fulfilling orders for legal support services, ADR neutrals, court reporting, transcription, and related trainings across VA facilities nationwide, ensuring continuity of legal operations, reduced procurement lead time, and consistent quality and pricing across the enterprise. 2. Scope This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirements for support of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in accomplishing VA's mission, strategic goals, priorities, and initiatives related to legal, ADR, and court support functions. Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, vehicles, certifications, supervision, and all other technologies and technical services necessary to deliver comprehensive legal assistance and integrated management services. This includes, but is not limited to: Alternate dispute resolution services Legal support services (case development, research, litigation and administrative claim support, expert witness support) Court reporting services Transcription, translation, and interpretation services Real-time reporting, Communication Access Realtime Translation (CART), and remote/video deposition support Trial and hearing exhibit or technology support Litigation-related and ADR-related training This PWS establishes the scope, terms, and general requirements of the base BPA. Specific requirements, deliverables, staffing, place of performance, and performance periods will be defined at the individual order level. Orders may be issued for any combination of the services described herein, and the task areas below are intended to be read broadly so as to encompass the full range of court support, transcription, and litigation support services VA may require over the life of the BPA. 3. General Information 3.1 Type of Agreement/Contract The Government anticipates awarding multiple Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs). BPA orders will be issued as Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and/or Labor-Hour (LH), and may include a Not-to-Exceed (NTE) CLIN for travel. The type of BPA order will be identified at the order level. 3.2 Ordering Period The BPA ordering period is a 12-month base period with up to four (4) 12-month option periods. Each order shall identify its own period of performance, which may extend up to 12 months beyond the expiration of the BPA ordering period, consistent with applicable ordering procedures in effect at time of award. 3.3 Place of Performance Place of performance will be specified at the order level and may include VA facilities, contractor facilities, and remote/virtual performance as appropriate to the service ordered. 3.4 Travel Travel requirements will be specified in each order and shall be in accordance with the Federal Travel Regulations (FTR). Local travel within a 50-mile radius of the contractor's facility or the assigned Government facility is considered the cost of doing business and will not be separately reimbursed, including subsistence and associated labor charges for travel time. Travel for personal convenience or daily commuting will not be reimbursed. Travel, subsistence, and labor charges for travel beyond a 50-mile radius may be authorized on a case-by-case basis with advance approval by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). General and Administrative (G&A) costs on travel are not allowable and will not be reimbursed. 3.5 Hours of Operation Hours of operation will be identified at the order level and shall reflect local time for the parties involved. 3.6 Government-Furnished Information/Equipment Government-Furnished Information (GFI) and/or Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE), if applicable, will be identified at the order level. 3.7 BPA Ordering Procedures BPA orders may be issued at any time during the ordering period. The order-level Contracting Officer shall award and administer orders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in this BPA and the applicable FAR Part 12 commercial item/service ordering procedures in effect at the time of ordering, including any subsequent regulatory updates to those procedures. BPA orders shall be within the scope of the BPA. Only the Contracting Officer for the BPA may modify the BPA itself. Order of Precedence: The terms and conditions of this BPA apply to all orders issued under it. In the event of inconsistency between the BPA terms and an individual order, the BPA terms and conditions take precedence. Annual Review: The Government will conduct an annual review of the BPA consistent with applicable ordering regulations, to confirm authorized procedures are being followed and to assess market conditions, sources of supply, pricing, and other factors that may warrant new agreements or modification of existing ones. Nonconformance: The Government will address nonconformance in accordance with applicable FAR subpart 8.4 procedures governing termination for cause, termination for convenience, and disputes, as in effect at time of order. At no time shall order prices exceed awarded BPA prices. The discount pricing relationship established under the BPA shall be maintained throughout its life unless modified by the BPA Contracting Officer. 4. Background 4.1 Applicable Laws, Regulations, and Guidance The Contractor shall perform all services in accordance with applicable federal law and regulation, including but not limited to: Statutory Authorities 28 U.S.C. § 1346(b), §§ 2671–2680 — Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) 5 U.S.C. § 552 — Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 5 U.S.C. § 552a, as amended — Privacy Act of 1974 5 U.S.C. Chapters 75, 77 — Adverse actions; appeals 5 U.S.C. § 504 / 28 U.S.C. § 2412 — Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) 38 U.S.C. §§ 5901–5905 — Recognition of representatives; unauthorized practice 42 U.S.C. § 2000d — Title VI, Civil Rights Act of 1964 42 U.S.C. § 2000e et seq. — Title VII, Civil Rights Act of 1964 29 U.S.C. § 794 — Section 508/Rehabilitation Act (accessibility) 44 U.S.C. § 3541 et seq. — Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) of 2014 44 U.S.C. Chapter 31 — Records Management by Federal Agencies The Administrative Dispute Resolution Act (ADRA) of 1996 Regulatory Authorities 5 CFR Part 177 — Administrative claims 29 CFR Part 1614 — Federal EEO complaint processing 5 CFR Parts 315, 752, 1201, 1209 — Employment, adverse actions, MSPB 38 CFR §§ 14.626–14.637 — VA accreditation of representatives FIPS Pub 201-3 — Personal Identity Verification of Federal Employees and Contractors Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (FRCP) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 — Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, and BPA ordering procedures thereunder, as in effect at time of ordering VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) and VA Acquisition Manual (VAAM), as applicable Policy/Guidance Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Management Directive 110 Model Standards of Conduct for Mediators (www.adr.gov) VA directives and handbooks governing records retention, information security, and privacy, as applicable at the order level The Contractor shall remain current with amendments to the above authorities and any additional laws, regulations, or VA policy identified at the order level. 5. Task Areas Task areas are stated broadly. Individual orders may draw on any combination of the following in any proportion, and are not limited to the specific examples listed. 5.1 Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) The Contractor shall provide ADR services related to workplace disputes, EEO complaints, and facilitation needs across VA, including assignment of neutrals (mediators, facilitators, conflict coaches, arbitrators) within the local commuting area when feasible. Adjudication is not permitted under this task area. Services include, without limitation: Arbitration — Private resolution before one or more neutral arbitrators rendering a binding, court-enforceable award. Mediation — Neutral-facilitated negotiation toward a voluntary, mutually acceptable resolution. Conciliation — Neutral-assisted settlement process involving active proposal of settlement terms, non-binding. Record development support for all ADR matters, including gathering, organizing, and preparing supporting documentation and evidence. 5.2 Court and Hearing Support Services The Contractor shall provide the full range of services needed to capture, preserve, and produce the official record of hearings, depositions, investigations, arbitrations, and other proceedings, including: Court Reporting — Certified court reporters/stenographers (or equivalent, e.g., digital/electronic reporters) to record and produce official transcripts; compiling documents and exhibits; reading back portions of the record on request; clarifying inaudible statements. Transcription — Conversion of live or recorded speech into written/electronic text, including AI-assisted transcription where appropriate, with fully operational and serviceable recording/transcription equipment at all times. Proofreading/Quality Review — Accurate editing of AI-generated or draft transcripts against the source recording; production and delivery of complete, accurate final transcripts within order-specified timeframes. Real-Time Reporting/CART — Real-time speech-to-text captioning for proceedings requiring immediate access to the record, including accommodation needs. Read and Sign — Access for deponents and legal representatives to review transcripts and errata sheets, noting page/line discrepancies for verification against the original recording. Translation and Interpretation — Foreign language and sign language interpretation/translation in support of proceedings, upon request. Remote/Video Proceeding Support — Technical and logistical support for remote or hybrid depositions, hearings, and other proceedings, including secure videoconferencing. Record Development — Gathering, organizing, and preparing documentation and exhibits supporting the official proceeding record. All service providers shall be certified in accordance with applicable state law (e.g., NCRA, NVRA, or state-specific certification) for the jurisdiction in which services are performed, and the Contractor shall furnish proof of certification upon request. VA will provide 24-hour prior notice for expedited assignments; expedited transcripts shall be delivered overnight to VA's Ordering Representative upon request. Certification requirements, cancellation terms, and expedite procedures will be further specified at the order level. Cancellation notices provided at least 24 hours prior to a scheduled appearance shall not incur a cancellation fee, unless otherwise stated at the order level. 5.3 Legal Support Services The Contractor shall provide comprehensive legal support services spanning case development, research, litigation support, and expert witness services, organized into the following subtask areas: 5.3.1 Case Development, Research, and Analysis Preparing draft documents for attorney review; opening, organizing, and maintaining case files; gathering, sorting, classifying, and interpreting information from multiple sources; identifying gaps, inconsistencies, or issues requiring further inquiry; conducting legal and factual research; coordinating with custodians and stakeholders to obtain responsive information; documenting search and information-processing efforts; compiling authorities into organized reference materials; record development, including gathering, organizing, analyzing, and preparing documentation and evidence. 5.3.2 Litigation and Administrative Claim Support Preparing summaries, chronologies, inventories, and data analyses to support attorney decision-making; identifying and organizing exhibits; scheduling depositions and related meetings; supporting eDiscovery, litigation holds, document acquisition and preparation, data extraction from forensic images, and document analysis; supporting FOIA/Privacy Act appeals, FTCA claims, EAJA processing, and employment/labor litigation matters. All litigation and trial support work product shall be submitted through, and filed by, VA counsel; the Contractor shall not submit filings independently. 5.3.3 Administrative Investigations and Interviews Supporting administrative investigations, including scheduling and coordinating interviews, organizing investigative records, and preparing supporting materials for investigators or administrative judges. 5.3.4 Operational and Case Management Support Entering, updating, and maintaining information in electronic case management systems; scanning, copying, and organizing records; managing case intake; screening and responding to customer/stakeholder communications; monitoring case status and deadlines; closing out matters per established procedures; records retention processing; general project management support. Work shall be performed using checklists, templates, and established guidance, with issues or conflicts elevated to supervising attorneys. 5.3.5 Expert Witness and Technical Analysis Support Providing expert witness services as directed by Agency counsel, including specialized subject-matter analysis and evaluation, preparation of expert reports and opinions, consultation with Agency counsel, development of supporting exhibits, and expert testimony at depositions, hearings, mediations, or trials. Services under this task area may support, without limitation: eDiscovery; FOIA and Privacy Act appeals; FTCA cases; employment and labor litigation; contract matters; ethics program support; accreditation and fee matters; litigation hold support; document acquisition, preparation, and organization; forensic data extraction and document analysis; EAJA processing; records retention; and general project management. Contractor personnel shall be fully trained and experienced in their area of expertise commensurate with PWS requirements. 5.4 Training 5.4.1 Litigation Skills Training Training for VA attorneys who represent the Department before the EEOC, Merit Systems Protection Board, Federal Labor Relations Authority, and other legal forums, covering direct and cross-examination, opening statements, closing arguments, exhibit handling, depositions, negotiation, legal writing, and related litigation skills. 5.4.2 ADR and Mediation Training Design, development, and facilitation of customized courses, including meaningful conversations, leading up and advocacy training, group facilitation, workplace civility (including supervisory-level), conflict management, and team building. Additional or emerging training topics related to litigation, ADR, or court support functions may be added at the order level. 6. Applicable Documents Conflict of Interest disclosures/certifications, as required at the order level Additional applicable documents as identified at the order level 7. Deliverables Deliverables, formats, delivery timeframes, and acceptance criteria shall be identified within each individual order.

sig_db02fd9a7a4e80ce59f8.description: Design, installation, integration and development of technical protection systems in the area of Semmelweis Egyetem. In this context, the performance of tasks arising from various organisational units becomes necessary in the following areas: - establishment of an access control system; - establishment of an intrusion detection system; - installation of a video surveillance system; - installation of an intercom system. The implementation of the public procurement shall take place by means of direct ordering in the second part of the framework agreement procedure pursuant to Section 105. (1) paragraph (a) of the Public Procurement Act. The exact description of the tasks of the winning tenderer and their planned quantities are contained in the public procurement technical specification, pricing table and draft framework agreement forming part of the Procurement Documentation. The task of the winning tenderer (briefly: WT) for the contracting authority (briefly: CA) is the design, installation, integration and development of technical protection systems in the area of Semmelweis Egyetem. In this context, the performance of tasks arising from the various organisational units becomes necessary in the following areas: 1. Installation of an access control system, the task of which is to regulate and restrict movements within the building. The system must be capable of identifying persons, vehicles and objects, and of authorising or restricting entry and passage. When building the systems, in addition to security engineering aspects, medical professional recommendations and regulations must also be taken into account. To achieve the above objectives, the access control system can be broken down into units as follows: - identification of persons, vehicles and objects (proximity card, fingerprint reader, special wireless identification, etc.) - logical control unit, which performs the authorisation or denial of entry and passage (door control unit) - actuator part (door locks, turnstiles, speed gates, barriers) - control software, which provides the system operator with system parameterisation, issuing, modifying and revoking permissions, querying events and generating statistics. 2. Installation of an intrusion detection system, which serves for the supplementary protection of rooms located inside the buildings that are more vulnerable from a property protection point of view, and also cooperates with the access control and video surveillance systems. In this context, opening detectors, glass break detectors, passive infrared motion detectors and infrared barriers shall be installed. 3. Installation of a video surveillance system, which records and transmits images of events occurring inside the building and in the immediate surroundings of the buildings to the building supervision centre and the remote monitoring centre. 4. Installation of an intercom system, the purpose of which is to enable operating personnel to identify the entering person without having to go to the entry point. Within this, the establishment of digital audio and/or video systems ensuring the accessibility of multiple institutions becomes necessary, which should preferably be directly connected to the inputs of the access control system. Throughout the entire duration of the framework agreement, the planned quantitative characteristics of the systems intended for installation by CA are as follows: - in the case of access control systems: a total of 500 entry points; - in the case of intrusion detection systems: a total of 100 detection points; - in the case of video surveillance systems: a total of 500 observation points (cameras). The framework agreement is concluded until the framework amount is exhausted, but for a maximum duration of 3 years; the total quantity is constituted accordingly by the amount of the framework sum, which is a net of 374 066 770,- HUF. A detailed description of the tasks to be performed is contained in the public procurement technical specification forming part of the Procurement Documentation.
sig_db02fd9a7a4e80ce59f8.title: Design and installation of technical protection systems

sig_db0c678dc105aa361164.description: The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is issuing a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) pursuant to DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under a CSO, the ERDC may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation, similar to a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), to acquire innovative commercial products, technologies, or services based on a review of solutions by scientific, technological, or other subject matter expert peers within the ERDC. “Innovative,” for CSO purposes, means any new technology, process, or method, including research and development (R&D), or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. Under this CSO, all products, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items; products, technologies, and services do not have to be “commercially available” to be submitted in response to this solicitation. If the solution meets the requirements of the regulation, the solution is treated as commercial whereby the Contracting Officer will utilize commercial procedures to develop and execute the resultant award. The DoW High Performance Computing Modernization Program (HPCMP) is seeking innovative solutions to establish a new high-performance computing (HPC) system acquisition and support services model that leverages industry best practices to transform how the HPCMP procures, operates, and maintains its newest HPC systems for 2027. The HPC systems being considered are a combination of compute-intensive architectures and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. The systems would be geographically distributed at up to three of the five HPCMP DoW Supercomputing Resource Centers (DSRCs). Since the systems will reside on-premises in the DSRCs, the services model must also conform to DoW and local Service policies, especially regarding security (physical, personnel, and cyber). To navigate the current market conditions and meet mission objectives, a new strategy is needed to design, manufacture, deliver, install, operate and maintain one or more HPC systems at one to three different HPC centers. The anticipated systems will be a combination of compute-intensive architectures (mostly CPU-based) and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) platforms (mostly GPU-based) operating in either unclassified or classified (secret and above-secret) environments. Go to https://www.erdcwerx.org/innovative-technology-insertion-of-advanced-hpc-systems/ for all of the CSO details and submission requirements. All solutions must be submitted through the ERDCWERX platform. The ERDC may award a FAR-based contract or an Other Transaction under this announcement. All resultant FAR-based contracts will be firm-fixed price. All items, technologies, and services (including research and development) procured via this CSO are treated as commercial. Applicants from universities and/or non-profit organizations should be aware that commercial clauses will be integrated into the award and should coordinate proposals with associated legal counsel prior to submission.

sig_db2c6ce81a06d146931e.description: Maintenance, support and upgrade of Customs SEED+ and related customs digital systems. Customs SEED+ is a digital platform supporting the systematic electronic exchange of customs data and pre-arrival information between CEFTA customs administrations, and between CEFTA and participating EU Member States through the Green Lanes initiative. The platform supports data exchange, risk management, trade facilitation, monitoring of crossing point performance, and the implementation of common customs cooperation tools. The contract will also support interoperability with local customs systems and related CEFTA systems, gradual alignment with the new Union Customs Code framework and related EU customs data exchange requirements, as well as further development of customs risk management functionalities and support for the recognition of customs controls, including common risk profiles, rapid customs alerts, inspection report data exchange, AEO-related functionalities, statistics and reporting, where relevant. Maintenance, support, upgrade and further development of Customs SEED+ and related customs digital systems. Customs SEED+ has evolved from a platform primarily supporting the electronic exchange of advance customs information into the principal CEFTA digital platform for customs cooperation, advanced customs data processing and the digital implementation of customs-related CEFTA commitments. The platform supports the systematic electronic exchange and processing of customs data and pre-arrival information between CEFTA Customs Administrations and, through the Green Lanes initiative, with participating EU Member States. Its functionalities support the monitoring and matching of customs data and goods movements, customs risk management, trade facilitation, monitoring of crossing point performance, statistics and reporting, and the implementation of common customs cooperation tools. The contract will support the continued operation and further technical development of the Green Lanes, as well as the further development of digital functionalities related to coordinated customs risk management, including, where relevant, the exchange of risk information, common risk profiles, rapid customs alerts, inspection and control results, truck weighing and scanner information, improved waiting-time measurement, and advanced data analysis and targeting functionalities. Further developments may also include AEO cooperation and prioritisation, priority treatment of consignments containing perishable goods, and other customs cooperation measures agreed by the CEFTA Parties. Interoperability between Customs SEED+, local customs systems and other relevant systems will be further strengthened through APIs, web services and other technical solutions enabling structured and automated data exchange, reducing duplicate data entry and improving data quality. The contract will also support the progressive technical adaptation of Customs SEED+ to the evolving Union Customs Code (UCC) framework and related EU customs digital systems and data-exchange requirements, with a view to strengthening interoperability with relevant EU customs systems and supporting closer customs cooperation between CEFTA and the EU.

Lot LOT-0001: Maintenance and further development of "Portal LaWi" for Hessian agricultural funding (Lot 4). Wirtschafts- und Infrastrukturbank Hessen (WIBank) acts as an EU-accredited paying agency for agricultural funding in Hesse. WIBank is part of Landesbank Hessen – Thüringen (Helaba). The provision and operation of the specialised IT systems necessary for agricultural funding is the responsibility of Helaba. Helaba has currently awarded the IT services for agricultural funding to a general contractor. The contract with this general contractor ends on 31.12.2026. Therefore, the IT services are being re-tendered. As part of these tenders, there will be a transition from the current general contractor model to a multi-provider model. The services previously provided centrally by the general contractor will be divided up and put out to tender successively in competition via six technically delimited lots. The agricultural funding IT systems are based on a highly integrated architecture that necessitates technical and functional dependencies between the six lots. As part of the transition from a general contractor to a multi-provider model, it is therefore imperative that the service providers for each lot do not act in isolation, but rather become part of an integrated IT ecosystem. The services affected here solely relate to Lot 4 – Maintenance and further development of the "Portal LaWi" for Hessian agricultural funding. An essential component is the maintenance and further development of the central online portal for the submission of applications by farmers. The portal provides a user-friendly interface for recording, validating and tracking the status of applications. All services are to be provided on the basis of a framework agreement and therefore only upon separate call-off/individual order. For further details, reference is made to Appendix I 02 - Appendix 0_Specification of Services as well as Appendix I 03 – Annex 1 to Appendix 0_Functional Specification.
