sig_dcb19b25c435f839b478.description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA’s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources.

sig_dcc46098575b55940870.description: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.
sig_dcc46098575b55940870.title: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover

sig_dcf061ca5a09e48dfc90.description: Framework conditions * Start: from 01.09.2026 * Time horizon: 5 years * Allocation rate: 4–5 days per week (approx. 80–100 %) * Place of work: Flughafen Zürich AG, Circle, 8058 Zurich Airport; on-site presence 2/3 of working time, working from home 1/3 * Client and line manager: Teamlead ICT Windows Platforms Subject of the service We are looking for an experienced external Senior System Engineer to provide technical support and advice to our ICT Windows Platforms Engineering team. The service provider will independently take on defined work packages in the areas of design, engineering and continuous development of the hybrid Microsoft infrastructure (Windows Server from 2016, Entra ID, Microsoft 365) at 3rd level. The mandate focuses on the interface between Infrastructure Security and Cloud-Native Automation: as an established Windows Server specialist, the service provider implements strict security architectures (Active Directory Tier Model, Privileged Access Workstation (PAW), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)) and advances the complete automation of complex identity and patching processes. Tailored solutions are also developed via Azure Functions, PowerShell and API integrations (REST/OData) to smoothly orchestrate systems such as Adaxes, Omada and Entra ID. The clear focus is on engineering services such as architecture, design, transformation and hardening of platforms — and explicitly not on operational execution or classic system administration. Tasks * Identity Platforms: Implementation, ongoing maintenance and development of Active Directory and its associated infrastructure, including the tiering model, Privileged Access Workstations and hardening measures. Engineering, operation and optimisation of ADFS, Okta and Microsoft Entra ID. * OS Engineering: Performance of engineering tasks in the Microsoft OS Stack (incl. Windows Server 2025) with a focus on the technical implementation and evolution of OS hardening measures. Development, maintenance and optimisation of build and deployment standards as well as Task Sequences in Microsoft MEMCM/SCCM for standardised provisioning and hardening. Analysis and evaluation of monthly patch cycles in terms of security, compatibility and deployment strategy. * Security & EPP Platform: Autonomous management and development of the EPP platform (Palo Alto Networks) in the context of Server Engineering and the Active Directory tiering model, in collaboration with the Cyber Defense Center (CDC). Guaranteeing correct integration into the existing security architecture and support in the identification, evaluation and resolution of vulnerabilities. * Automation: Design, implementation and optimisation of Windows Server automation (MEMCM) and Identity Lifecycle processes (Adaxes) via PowerShell and Ansible. Integration and connection of surrounding systems, in particular IAM (Omada). * Public Key Infrastructure (PKI): Operation and engineering of the PKI infrastructure, including configuration of Hardware Security Modules (HSM) and lifecycle process management. Service focus * Platform & Security: Guaranteeing and continuously optimising the security architecture, particularly in Active Directory and Windows Server environments. * Consulting: Close collaboration and technical advice to teams at the IdP, security and architecture interfaces, with a focus on identity security and the Enterprise Access Model, including Azure tenant management in this context. * Audit Support: Technical preparation and provision of data and logs for IT audits, as well as implementation of the resulting technical requirements. * Application Operations: Technical management, configuration and regular updating of backend and management tools. sig_dcf525e5eba1357b1e5a.description: A framework agreement with several companies is to be awarded for advising TSG Tourismus Salzburg GmbH on the design and further development of the tourism route guidance concept (Lot 1), advice on the design and implementation of the Salzburg Local Card (Lot 2), and the technical execution and implementation of the concept for expanding the digital Salzburg Card (Lot 3). The City of Salzburg has an existing visitor guidance system to orient guests along central arterial routes and to tourist-relevant facilities. The aim is to develop a modern tourist visitor guidance system that enables guests to navigate intuitively, directs visitor flows purposefully, and makes tourist offerings more visible outside the historic old town as well. In particular, the Nonntal, Schallmoos, Elisabeth-Vorstadt and Lehen districts are to be taken into account. Furthermore, the concept is to be developed in such a way that a gradual expansion to other districts is possible and includes digital additions.; The subject of the services is consultancy on the development of a strategic concept for a Salzburg Local Card. The objective is to produce a robust decision-making model by means of which it can be assessed whether and in what form a local card can be introduced economically, organisationally and strategically in a sensible manner. In particular, potential business, service, partner and operator models as well as economic viability and organisational feasibility are to be examined and evaluated.; The starting point is an existing concept for the further development of the Salzburg Card, including a mobile Salzburg Card app. As part of the consultancy, the existing concept for expanding the digital card and the resulting requirements for the project, their economic and technical feasibility, and possible solution variants in particular are to be analysed and evaluated, and corresponding recommendations for action derived from them. The existing system architecture as well as the economic efficiency, maintainability and future-proofing of possible solutions must be taken into account. Consultancy on the technical and economic evaluation and design of the project. In particular, an assessment should be made as to whether and in what form a merger into a common mobile application or a modular overall architecture is appropriate.

Phase 2: - The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $500,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. - The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is up to 15 months (excluding submission of the final report). - Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 5 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 2 awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Travel: Travel to Suffield, Alberta for prototype demonstration. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The challenge is to provide the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) a software solution to provide an airspace common operating picture so that it can plan, deconflict, and control uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) traffic, including their use of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum, in order to ensure the safe and efficient management of UAS to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Details: Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be Windows-based. 2. Allow a user to create and store flight plans, including radio frequency requirements. 3. Have a flight plan repository (database) that stores the 4D (3D + time) trajectories and spectrum requirements of all accepted flight plans. 4. Enable integration of supplemental data services such as crewed aircraft flight plans and weather. 5. Generate an optimal 4D flight path for UAS based on specific mission goals and physical limits. 6. Be able to check new flight requests against existing flight plans, airspace constraints (no-fly zones) and RF spectrum requests to detect conflicts and resolve them (via set priorities or a human decision). 7. Generate 4D blocks of deconflicted airspace (a "tunnel" or a "box") where a UAS is permitted to fly. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Analyze real-time data from UASs to prevent collisions and automatically adjust flight paths for UASs in controlled airspace. 2. Check in real-time whether a UAS is following its pre-approved, deconflicted trajectory. 3. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies. To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined below: Critical components: 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3. On-board computer 4. Any software Requested information: i. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Name of the original equipment manufacturer of the product being sourced ii. OEM URL: Provide the URL of the OEM iii. Software: Confirm if developed by Offeror or outsourced iv. Product name: Provide the OEM's product name v. Model number: Provide the OEM's model and/or version number of the product vi. Product URL: Provide the URL of the OEM product, model, and version vii. Country of origin IMPORTANT NOTE: For this challenge, kindly disregard the Attachment requirements detailed at Section D in the Web-Portal, and instead adhere to the following: - The attachment measures 8.5" by 11" with a maximum size of 10Mb. - Only the following formats will be accepted: JPG, GIF, TIF, PDF or PNG. - The attachment must be clear and legible. Note: Including an attachment is not mandatory, but forms part of the Additional Outcomes, which is scored up to 10 points. The Applicant (Offeror) acknowledges that it is within Canada's sole discretion to determine whether the attachment is removed or included in the Offer. Background & Context The CA is undergoing a generational modernization effort to address the evolving nature of technology, the changing character of conflict, and the unravelling of the geopolitical system. The transformative changes being made are conceptually described in the CA publication Inflection Point 2025. This document provides the broad context for modernization and directs the development and acquisition of key systems; in particular, it states: Key to this transformation is the integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, autonomous and uncrewed systems. These capabilities will support a wide range of functions, from intelligence analysis and predictive modeling to targeting and operational execution. The CA, in recognizing this need, has purchased foreign robotics and autonomous systems of varying quality and has identified challenges purchasing systems that meet operational requirements, in particular related to cold-weather operations, and that have stable supply chains. Further, purchases have, in the past, been constrained by limited manufacturing capacity of industry partners. To address this, the Government of Canada's recently released policy Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, emphasizes the need to develop a strong domestic industrial capacity to produce defence materiel. This policy directs the CA to seek solutions to operational problems through Canadian industry, which will both improve the CA's capability while providing the foundation of a strong defence industrial base able to scale production of quality defence material. To date, engagements with Canadian industry have revealed a wide variety of small/medium companies that have commercial technologies that could, with support, be tailored to military requirements.

sig_dd3f36ccba348ef16bfb.description: Over time, EPFL has built up a complex network of data exchanges between systems, based on multiple applications developed internally. Although functional, the current processing within these areas presents several limitations. The objectives: • Governance: security, quality, strict data confidentiality: Ensure governance, security, compliance and trust in the use of data throughout its lifecycle • Unified data ecosystem: Create a unified, consistent and secure environment, eliminating silos to improve collaboration and unlock valuable cross-domain insights • Stimulate innovation: by enabling the development of new data-driven products and services such as AI • Improve operational efficiency: by automating data-related tasks and reducing manual interventions. • Empower users with data access: Provide the EPFL community with tools to easily access, analyse and use quality real-time data, facilitating decision-making • Modern ingestion of data sources: Be able to rapidly catalog, ingest, connect, transform and publish new data sources in a governed manner for all types of consumption, analytics, data science, operational, artificial intelligence. • Modern integration between applications: Deploy an efficient integration platform ensuring data flows, smooth workflows, guaranteeing consistency between applications and business processes. These objectives will be achieved by: • Deploying modern, easy-to-use tools. • Supporting the transformation with change management. • Decommissioning obsolete tools and systems. The main technical components expected in the long term within the programme are: • An orchestrator (ORC) to schedule the various processes transversally. • A data exchange platform (EIP): API-oriented for inter-application data exchange (API Management, Enterprise Service Bus). An orchestrator (ORC) to schedule the various processes transversally. We wish to have an ergonomic, integrated tool, transversal to several teams, enabling simple or complex processing to be scheduled in various applications in a simple and intuitive way. It plays a central role in the automation, supervision and reliability of data flows processed within the programme. It is essential that the solution is sufficiently standard (few specific developments). It is necessary for EPFL to call upon external resources in order to successfully complete this project within the allotted time and with the required level of technical expertise.

sig_dd405a6df47dca000f10.description: The tender procedure is carried out by the contracting authorities as a joint procurement procedure, cf. section 123, subsection 5. The tender procedure is covered by the Danish Public Procurement Act (Act No. 1564 of 15 December 2015 as amended), which implements the Public Procurement Directive (Directive 2014/24/EU). The tender procedure concerns the procurement of diabetes technology by Region Midtjylland, Region Syddanmark, Region Nordjylland and Region Østdanmark (current Region Sjælland and Region Hovedstaden), divided into two subcontracts concerning respectively (1) AID insulin pump systems and (2) continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGM). As an integral part of the delivery, the suppliers must also make the associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training for patients and healthcare professionals as well as technical support for patients. This means that each region concludes separate contracts/framework agreements with the winning tenderers. The subcontract concerns the procurement of AID insulin pumps in the form of either insulin pumps for infusion sets or patch pumps. The subcontract also covers the system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered AID insulin pump system into operation and using it as intended, including, depending on the offered system, for example pods, pump bases, PDM/control units, infusion sets and reservoirs. sig_dd63d81539ef030f5acf.description: Market Intelligence Notice – Hangar Construction (Hybrid Conventional and Tension Fabric Structures) Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.0 Objective The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District (SAS) is seeking market intelligence to identify and assess industry capabilities relevant to Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) and hybrid industrialized construction solutions for hangar facilities and similar large-span mission support applications. The Government is pursuing modern industrialized construction approaches intended to improve schedule, cost, and lifecycle outcomes for this facility type. Information provided by respondents will be used to help the Government understand available market participants, solution types, and industry interest, and will inform future industry engagements, acquisition planning, and assessment of potential use of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. 2.0 Forecasted Projects - Overview The following projects are currently projected for potential TFS or hybrid industrialized construction applications. USACE, SAS requires a highly resilient, energy-efficient operational hangar facility that can be rapidly constructed, scaled, and reconfigured as a tension-fabric structure. Solutions may be scaled for additional hangar facilities identified later. Maintenance Hangar, Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF), GA (approximately 193,513 square footage (SF)). Construction of a Large (10 Module) Standard Design Aircraft Maintenance Hangar Complex with integrated aviation maintenance operations, maintenance support, company operations, flight planning, flight operations spaces, Ground Support Equipment (GSE) covered storage, Associated Support Items of Equipment (ASIOE) covered storage, Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) and Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) storage, hangar access and wash aprons. Project also includes fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, exterior lighting, paving, POV parking, walks, storm drainage, information systems, landscaping and signage. Heating and air conditioning will be provided by self-contained system. Moody Air Force Base, GA (approximately 105,000 SF). Construction of an adequately sized six-bay hangar and squadron operations facility. The squadron operations section of the facility shall incorporate mission planning, life support, and squadron admin space. The aircraft maintenance section shall be designed to optimize maintenance administration for the squadron. The hangar bays will provide space to support aircraft repair and inspection, engine changes, and other activities that must be accomplished in a secure, climate-controlled environment. The hangar space must be sized to accommodate movement and placement of maintenance equipment around the aircraft and systems supporting the aircraft. 3.0 Requested Information & Market Intelligence Questionnaire Section - General Information Provide responses to the survey linked herein. https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Section - Capabilities Respondents are asked to structure Capability Statements to include the following elements: Corporate Overview - A brief summary of your firm's core capabilities, relevant experience, and capacity to perform the type of work contemplated under this RFI. Commercial Best Practices. To the extent available, provide information regarding commercial best practices applicable to the contemplated construction delivery method, including: Typical pricing/payment structures Geographic coverage Typical project schedule timelines, long lead items, and key decision points Key considerations and risk associated with permitting, logistics, staffing/labor availability, and construction execution. Specialized Systems Integration: Describe your experience integrating specialized hangar systems, such as high-capacity cranes, fall protection systems, and high-expansion foam fire suppression systems, within a tension fabric structure. Supply Chain and Logistics: Describe your supply chain for key components of the tension fabric structure. What are your typical lead times for material and fabrication? Materials and Durability: What specific materials, coatings, and structural frame materials do you typically use for facilities of this type and in a coastal environment? What is the expected design life and warranty period for these components? 3. Survey Responses – Please provide detailed responses to Survey Questions 10 through 12 (listed below and on the survey form). Respondents are asked to integrate these responses directly into their capability statements; separate or stand-alone survey responses are not required. Additional Information – Respondents may include other information that demonstrates their relevant capabilities, experience, and capacity. Examples include: Photos of TFS projects ; Smart Building Technologies (e.g., automated controls, sensors, energy management systems, fire protection and alarm systems, information systems, Intrusion Detection System (IDS) installation, closed circuit television connection, cybersecurity measures, and Energy Monitoring Control Systems (EMCS) connection.) Advanced HVAC Systems (e.g., high-efficiency climate control, specialized filtration) Survey Questions 10-12 10. Describe your experience or capability in designing and constructing tension-fabric structures that could innovate and accelerate construction. 11. Describe your firm’s practical experience with collaborative delivery models, such as Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build or Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), where your team was integrated into the design phase. What specific pre-construction services did you provide? 12. For the projects listed in response to Q11, identify the major subcontractor(s) used and describe their qualifications. Detail the teaming relationship and contract structure between the construction contractor, the owner, and the Designer of Record. Explain how your team's involvement improved the final design quality, accelerated the delivery schedule, and reduced overall project cost. 4.0 Response Submission Instructions Format: Responses to the survey must be submitted via the link provided. The capability statement must be submitted in PDF format, single-spaced, using 11-point font or larger. Submission Deadline: October 23, 2026 – 5:00 PM Submission Channel: Complete the survey at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/8B5GPKqrMh Submit capability statement via email to the Agreement Officer (AO) at Jennifer.L.Murphy@usace.army.mil and copy Sabrina.Bastine@usace.army.mil with the subject line: "USACE OTA Market Intelligence Response TFS - [Company Name]". Proprietary Information: Any proprietary, sensitive, or business-confidential information must be clearly marked as such on each page to ensure proper handling by USACE SAS.

sig_dd7cfe0f900fc45162cc.description: For the purposes of managing the operational cadastre of infrastructure facilities for municipal general economic services for the supply of drinking water and the discharge and treatment of urban waste water and storm water, the contracting authority has established a digital cadastre, which it has been supplementing by establishing the rental of various modules since year 2004. The digital cadastre comprises the installation of software on its own server, including a spatially located database, which enables it to keep records of municipal general economic services in electronic form and comprises both graphic and data records. Based on the records, the contracting authority performs analyses and produces reports and printouts on the infrastructure for various needs: reporting to owners – municipalities, reporting to state institutions, issuing project conditions, opinions and consents, etc. Modules that are the subject of the contract: General modules:  Viewer.  Longitudinal profile.  Digital terrain model.  Export of spatial data.  Address register.  Web elementary viewer. Modules for managing the digital cadastre of municipal infrastructure:  Basic (geodetic module) – water supply.  Register of faults – water supply.  Valve manipulation.  Additional hydraulic description of facilities.  Loss control.  Connection to the SCADA supervisory control and data acquisition system.  Hydrants.  Report generation service: Ministry of Environment report on achieved equipment standards for municipalities – water supply.  Report generation service: Public Health Institute report on the performance of public service – water supply.  GJI reporting* – water supply.  Basic (geodetic module) – sewerage.  Register of sewerage cleaning.  GJI reporting* – sewerage.  Register of faults/problems in sewerage.  Report generation service: Ministry of Environment report on achieved equipment standards for municipalities – sewerage.  Report generation service: Public Health Institute report on the performance of public service – sewerage.  Register of septic tanks/sewerage connections. In addition to the rental of licences "GJI reporting – water supply" and "GJI reporting – sewerage", the contracting authority orders a statement by a chartered engineer in the field of geodesy upon each submission of deliverables for the registration of facilities in the consolidated cadastre of public economic infrastructure and the actual submission of applications for registration in the consolidated cadastre of public economic infrastructure. The contract also includes software (modules) whose rental price depends on the size of the municipal infrastructure and the number of addresses (1000 km of water supply / 400 km / 15.000 addresses):  Connection to the enterprise resource planning system.  Consents.  Property register with a link to fixed assets. The subject of the contract is also the additional establishment or rental of mobile applications for 40 – 60 users:  Water supply: register of faults (licence size: 1000 km).  Water supply: water quality register (licence size: 1000 km).  Water supply: hydrants (licence size: 1000 km).  Sewerage: reporting of problems and hydraulic deficiencies (licence size: 400 km). And additional establishment or rental of modules:  Water supply: hydraulic export (licence size: 1000 km).  Sewerage: hydraulic export (licence size: 400 km).  Sewerage: additional hydraulic description of facilities, with web publication (licence size: 400 km).  Sewerage: CCTV inspection (licence size: 400 km).  Sewerage: connection to the SCADA supervisory control and data acquisition system, with web publication (licence size: 400 km). In addition to the rental of software, the contract includes all costs related to software maintenance.
sig_dd7cfe0f900fc45162cc.title: Rental of software licences for Protok for managing the leased digital infrastructure cadastre and rental of mobile applications

sig_ddba19de93540d392ee7.description: The assignment is for a general evaluation of existing initiatives within the inclusion and diversity work in the state that shall contribute to more people being in or coming into work, especially persons who are currently out of work. The government tariff area consists of around 200 entities with over 166,000 employees, and the measures range from statutory measures to voluntary schemes such as the trainee programme, placement of practice and positive special treatment. The evaluation shall map the effects of the current means and identify measures that work well, less well or do not give the desired effect. The work involves reviewing the existing research, document studies and comprehensive data acquisition, including in-depth interviews in a selection of government entities. The contracting authority shall, in conclusion, propose improvements, any new initiatives and areas where more knowledge is needed. The final delivery deadline for the contract is 31 December 2026. NOK 2,000,000 excluding VAT has been set aside for the project. Nok 100,000 excluding VAT has been set aside as an option. The description of the option is in annex 1 of the contract. See annex 1 of the contract for further details on the delivery.

sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: AI & Data Factory - Expert Services for AI and Data Development, Governance and Continuous Operations

sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.description: Gol municipality plans, on behalf of the municipalities in Hallingdal, to carry out a market survey on general documentation management in the region. 1.1.1 Background and purpose of the market survey The six municipalities in Hallingdal have started a preliminary study to look at a more comprehensive and future orientated documentation management, at the same time that we must continually deal with archival documentation in new trade systems. Our ongoing procurement of a new electronic patient journal (EPJ) has clarified the need for a total assessment of how archival documentation is handled across trade systems. The current systems are fragmented, with many archive cores and complex set-ups, and present challenges, among other things, for structure, work flow, quality and resource use. The six municipalities have joint ICT operations and cooperate on digitalisation projects and procurements of new digital systems with the accompanying joint contract management. In order to gain insight that can enable us to make good road choices further, we would like to carry out a market survey with potential suppliers. The main focus is the safeguarding of archival information generated in trade systems in accordance with laws and regulations, and it is especially important for us to see this in the light of changed laws, regulations and standards in the archive area, new technology and possibilities for a more comprehensive approach further.
sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.title: Market Survey/RFI - Archive Core

GENERAL INFORMATION The current contract for the operation, development, further development, management and support of the MitID solution was entered into with Nets DanID A/S (now IN Groupe Denmark A/S) in 2019 and runs until June 2031 (with the possibility of extension). The MitID solution is the Danish national electronic identification scheme, which is notified as an electronic identification scheme in accordance with the eIDAS Regulation (Directive 1999/93/EC). A citizen can use MitID to perform secure authentication on digital self-service solutions. MitID can be used as an authentication method in both the public and private sectors by service providers that use the MitID solution. The Contracting Authority has, in Annex 1 – description of the existing MitID solution, prepared an overall description of the existing solution. Further information about the MitID solution is available on Digitaliseringsstyrelsen's website: https://digst.dk/it-loesninger/mitid/ The Contracting Authority will conduct a tender for the continuation of the MitID solution. The tender is expected to be conducted as a tender with negotiation. The Contracting Authority wishes, among other things, to use the market survey to explore whether a possible division of the contract into several contracts would be appropriate. A division of the contract could, for example, be a structure with two contracts divided into operation and development, respectively. The Contracting Authority has not finally decided on a possible division of the contract and thus wishes for input on which options the market sees an advantage in. All information in this prior information notice about the upcoming tender must therefore also be considered preliminary.

sig_ddfd5a877d9b7d3a72e9.description: The subject of the contract is the provision of technical consultant services to the contracting authority and to the project owner in view of and during the acceptance of the project "Digital upgrade of the Integrated Judicial Case Management System for Civil and Penal Cases" (subproject 1, hereinafter referred to as the "Main Project"). These services mainly include Project Management, the certification of the physical deliverables of the Main Project, assistance to the Acceptance Committees of the Main Project, monitoring and control - verification of the proper operation of the applications of the Main Project, monitoring and verification of the correct and complete data migration to the new Integrated Judicial Case Management System for Civil and Penal Cases, and the drafting of the final report on the proper operation of the Main Project. The Contractor shall provide the contracting authority and the project owner with Project Management services during the implementation phase of the Main Project, technical advice and support during and in view of the acceptance of the Main Project. To this end, among other things and in addition to matters relating to the certification of the physical deliverables, they shall monitor the implementation progress of the Main Project and ensure the timely receipt of the various work packages. These latter responsibilities shall be exercised under the instructions and general supervision of the Contracting Authority, through the Project Management Team, and of the Council of State, as the owner and operating body of the main project. Advisory support must be provided during the following stages: (a) implementation period of Subproject 1, (b) pilot operation, (c) training - transfer of know-how, (d) installation and test operation in the production environment, and (e) provisional and final acceptance of the Parts of the Main Project. Given that the Main Project also concerns a large number of regional courts, the Acceptance Committees must be assisted by a technical consultant, who shall carry out the required on-site inspections and draw up technical expert opinions. Certification inspections shall be regular and/or extraordinary and shall include, inter alia, system tests, deliverable evaluations, etc., regarding all obligations of the contractors of the parts/contracts of the Main Project. Specifically, the Contractor shall provide the following services, which are categorised into 4 Work Units (WUs): ▪ WU1: Project Management Services of the Main Project ▪ WU2: Technical support and implementation monitoring of the Main Project. ▪ WU3: Support for the acceptance of deliverables of the Main Project. ▪ WU4: Management and monitoring of the implementation of this Project

The project 'DEVELOPMENT OF ICT INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE TOWN OF VALEA LUI MIHAI, BIHOR COUNTY' is financed through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, Component 10 Local Fund, Investment I.1.2 - Ensuring infrastructure for green transport – ITS/other ICT infrastructures (intelligent urban/local management systems), financing contract no. 1772 of 06.01.2023. The execution of the contract involves the supply of software applications, ICT equipment (server, desktop computers, laptops, printers, computer terminals, drone, licences) and related services, namely software installation and program interconnection services regardless of whether they are those subject to the contract or those already installed, namely the integration of new applications with existing applications, creating a functional online services platform within the Project financed through the PNRR. The successful implementation of the project depends to a very large extent on the quality of the products supplied, on compliance with the delivery schedule and also on compliance with the financing conditions. The total estimated value of the procurement is 1.969.080,00 lei excluding VAT. The general objective consists of the continuous improvement of the quality of life for present and future generations, for the creation of sustainable communities, capable of managing and using resources efficiently and capitalising on the ecological and social innovation potential of the economy, with a view to ensuring prosperity, environmental protection and social cohesion. The investment allows for the purchase of ICT (Information and Communications Technology) systems that contribute to the improvement of local management. Through the development of ICT infrastructure, within the Administrative Territorial Unit (UAT) of the Town of Valea lui Mihai, the debureaucratisation of the administrative system will be achieved, which will implicitly lead to rapid access to information, a streamlined communication process, and, not least, reduced waiting times. Through the project, the Town of Valea lui Mihai aims to achieve the following objectives: - personalised services for the creation of integrated information systems at community level, - provision of hardware equipment for the efficiency of the information systems that will be implemented, - debureaucratisation of the administrative system which will implicitly lead to rapid access to information, to a streamlined communication process, and, not least, to the reduction of waiting time. The deadline by which any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information in relation to the award documentation, in accordance with the provisions of Art. 160 of Law no. 98/2016 on public procurement, with subsequent amendments and additions, is 20 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification 11 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders, in accordance with the provisions of Art. 161 para. (1) of Law no. 98/2016 on public procurement, with subsequent amendments and additions. The procurement aims to supply software applications, ICT equipment (server, desktop computers, laptops, printers, computer terminals, drone, licences) and related services, namely software installation and program interconnection services regardless of whether they are those subject to the contract or those already installed, namely the integration of new applications with existing applications, creating a functional online services platform, in the UAT Town of Valea lui Mihai, namely at the headquarters of the Town Hall of Valea lui Mihai. The description and technical specifications of these can be found in the specifications attached to the award documentation. The duration of project implementation is 1 (one) month. sig_de34928b02f47282b555.description: AHDB require retail analysis for campaign results from top level categories for total beef and lamb, and total pig meat down to specific cuts or products, such as pork mince or beef mince. sig_de56f1338375649ad584.description: A self-contained nature finance game that allows players to virtually develop nature recovery projects funded using private and blended finance. Using the GFI Investment Readiness Toolkit as a framework the game will start by presenting players with options such as whether they want to play a seller or buyer, followed by various seller or buyer scenarios. Once a player has picked a role they will be taken through the process of developing a nature recovery project using private and blended finance from the start through to signing legal documents and the work starting on the ground. They will do this by working through a series of scenarios. They will have to complete every scenario satisfactorily to be able to move onto the next scenario. Reasons for not completing a scenario properly will be given, as will explanations of why they have completed a scenario correctly. Where possible there will be more than one correct way to complete a scenario. The game will be for Natural England so will focus on the roles that NE staff are likely to play at each stage of a projects development but will also be able to be used by Environment Agency and Forestry Commission staff carrying out nature finance related roles. Lot 1: .
sig_de56f1338375649ad584.title: Develop and Supply an Interactive online Nature Finance Project Development game

sig_de73ec9fd90e3f510da8.description: TfGM is looking to engage the market to find and contact, specialist suppliers in the area of connected vehicle data. TfGM on behalf of Safer Roads Greater Manchester (SRGM) Partnership is seeking a connected vehicle data provider to collaborate with TfGM's internal teams and partner authorities. SRGM is a multi-agency partnership dedicated to reducing fatalities and serious injuries on Greater Manchester's (GM ) roads by influencing attitudes and behaviours. The Safer Roads Partnership is responsible for countywide functions, as agreed with Greater Manchester partners, including casualty data and analysis, performance monitoring, and safety camera operations. The SRGM Partnership is committed to Vision Zero. Vision Zero represents Greater Manchester's ambition for zero fatalities and life changing injuries (FLCI) on our roads by 2040, whilst increasing safe, healthy and equitable mobility for all. It includes a challenging interim target of 50% reduction in FLCI casualty numbers by 2030, from 2022 levels. The Vision Zero Strategy adopts the Safe System, whereby people, vehicles and the road infrastructure interact in a way that secures a high level of safety. The objective is to deliver a comprehensive suite of analytical services aimed at deepening our understanding of road user behaviour and collision risk. In addition, several further benefits and use cases for connected vehicle data have been identified within TfGM and its partner network. TfGM is therefore looking for a partner who can provide a multi-use source of connected vehicle data. sig_de81748ebb64ecc0bb6b.description: The contracting authority aims, in cooperation with suppliers on two subcontracts, to roll out a complete solution comprising a modern, cloud-based call system, GPS equipment, staff alarms and an integrated digital observation and inspection solution. The purpose of the procurement is therefore to enter into contracts to establish a future-proof, reliable and cohesive platform that supports both safety for citizens and efficient workflows for employees in care centres and home care. The contracting authority is facing an extensive modernisation where approx. 1.400 call systems, 700 sensors and 160 GPS devices are to be replaced and implemented anew. In addition, the contracting authority has planned the setup and commissioning of up to 250 digital observation units for use in anonymised inspection, event detection and support for night and safety visits – with a particular focus on shielded units and temporary round-the-clock accommodation places (MDO). The solution must be delivered as a whole, where the call system, staff alarm and digital observation are integrated with one another. User-friendliness and simple operation are central requirements, just as full integration between the services in the two subcontracts carries high weight. The contracting authority requests solutions that are intuitive and stable in operation, and which clearly demonstrate how both citizens' need for security and employees' need for an overview and agency are met in practice. Tenderers must therefore be able to document how the offered systems live up to legal requirements, data security and operational uptime – and at the same time offer a platform that can be scaled and expanded in step with future needs. This procurement therefore represents an investment in improving and optimising the contracting authority's call solution while at the same time the contracting authority will improve care for citizens through Digital Observation. Subcontract 1 Callidus encompasses the implementation, operation and maintenance of a cloud-based call solution supported by an app and an administration system for all the contracting authority's call systems. The contract entails that the supplier must dismantle 1.400 systems and set up, program and insert SIM cards in 1.400 new systems. At the same time, up to 700 sensors and approx. 120 GPS devices must be changed to new units. The supplier must deliver SIM cards for all call systems and ensure that they are functional throughout the entire contract period. Following commissioning, the contracting authority's technical staff will handle future setups and deployments of the installed call systems. Requirements for the operation of the call solution and delivery of call systems appear in Annex 1 Requirements Specification for Subcontract 1 Callidus. The call solution must be integrable with a digital observation solution comprising digital inspections that meet the requirements in Annex 1 Requirements Specification for Subcontract 2 Digital Observation. Subcontract 1 Callidus must ensure a reliable and scalable call solution that gives citizens increased security and employees efficient workflows.; Subcontract 2 Digital Observation encompasses the implementation, operation and maintenance of a complete cloud-based solution for digital observation and digital inspection at the contracting authority's care centres, with the possibility of use in home care. The solution must be delivered with all necessary new equipment, software, SIM cards, technical infrastructure and administration system. The supplier must set up and commission up to 250 units distributed across shielded places, MDO places and homes in home care and at care centres. The solution must ensure anonymised digital inspections with image display, two-way communication and detection of events such as falls, presence and movement. The solution must be integrable with the call solution, which meets the requirements in Annex 1 Requirements Specification for Subcontract 1 Callidus. Requirements for the solution's functionality, technical specifications, operation and support appear in Annex 1 Requirements Specification for Subcontract 2 Digital Observation.; The contracting authority in cooperation with suppliers on two subcontracts rolls out a complete solution comprising a modern, cloud-based call system, GPS equipment, staff alarms and an integrated digital observation and inspection solution. The purpose of the procurement is to establish a future-proof, reliable and cohesive platform that supports both safety for citizens and efficient workflows for employees in care centres and home care.
sig_de81748ebb64ecc0bb6b.title: Contract for Safety Alarms, Subcontract 1 Callidus and Subcontract 2 Digital Observation

sig_de97bd4fc2b6f976b303.description: Statens vegvesen is conducting this market research as part of the planning for a potential procurement of a common data catalogue for the agency. The purpose is to establish a better understanding of the supplier market, available solutions, and possible approaches to realising a comprehensive capability for a data catalogue and associated data governance. The market research shall provide a better basis for assessing alternative solution directions and further developing the conceptual approach that has been established. It shall also contribute to concretising needs and clarifying which prerequisites must be in place to succeed with a solution in practice, both technically and organisationally. Statens vegvesen particularly seeks insight into how solutions for data catalogues and data governance function in complex organisations over time. This includes experiences related to the introduction, use, maintenance, and further development of such solutions, as well as which challenges, limitations, and conditions often prove to be more demanding than expected. Statens vegvesen manages large amounts of data that are used for planning, operations, analysis, management, and further digitalisation. These data represent a significant value, but the overview, documentation, and management of data are currently fragmented across the organisation. Information about datasets, concepts, responsibilities, and use is spread across several systems, local solutions, and manual overviews, and there is no unified and authoritative overview of which data the agency manages, what the data means, or which conditions apply to their use.
sig_de97bd4fc2b6f976b303.title: Market research (RFI) for the procurement of a common data catalogue in Statens vegvesen

The contracting authority acts in its own name, but in the interest of the steering and coordination group of the project "Digitisation of Vocational Training Management in Rural Areas" (AZUBIdigital). The contracting authority is Landwirtschaftskammer Nordrhein-Westfalen, represented by the Director of the Chamber of Agriculture, hereinafter referred to as the contracting authority. sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.
sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.

sig_dedcea8e15eaf386376c.description: The Highway Network Management Team at Durham County Council (DCC) is responsible for overseeing and managing the county's road network, supporting both operational delivery and strategic network planning. The Council is seeking to procure a single, modern Digital Road Management Platform to improve efficiency, data visibility, and service delivery. The proposed system will need to support both office-based and field-based operations. sig_deeec15c87a7b4c333d1.description: A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is a fully electronic procurement procedure that enables suppliers to apply for admission on an ongoing basis and to compete for specific contracts (mini-tenders) within a defined scope. Energinet will use the Comdia platform to support the digital management and operation of the DPS. Energinet is currently conducting a market assessment and preparing procurement materials for the establishment of a Dynamic Purchasing System to be used for the execution of mini-tenders concerning the acquisition of standard software and related services supporting control center operations. Energinet expects to publish the DPS with a set of overarching framework conditions. Following publication, suppliers that meet the defined admission requirements will be able to apply for inclusion in the system. The specific requirements for admission will be made available upon publication of the DPS. Submission of input is voluntary and intended to support Energinet in ensuring that the requirement specifications are aligned with market standards. In this context, suppliers are encouraged to: •Challenge specified requirements •Ask clarifying questions •Add propose adjustments, clarifications, or rewordings •Any ambiguities identified in the material are also requested to be highlighted in the feedback. Energinet reserves the right to freely assess the extent to which received input will be incorporated into the final procurement documents. The content of the draft material may be amended in whole or in part prior to publication. If market participants wish to submit input and/or express their interest in participating in the system, this must be submitted via Comdia no later than 18 May 2026 at 10:00. If a supplier does not express interest in participating in the system at this stage, it will still be possible to apply for admission to the system once it is published.
sig_deeec15c87a7b4c333d1.title: Hearing - Energinet Market involvement regarding Dynamic Purchasing System of standard software for operations technology and control center solutions - 26/07722
