The revised paragraph is as follows: 9) Science & Technology (S&T) Program Protection: Offerors are notified that subsequent Call Announcements shall include a requirement for submission of the documents identified below. Offerors may be asked to provide a mitigation plan for any identified S&T Protection risks. The Government reserves the right to determine an Offeror unawardable on the grounds of unacceptable S&T Protection risk based on its review of the SF 424 and Security Program Questionnaire. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. Implementation of electronic public services at Călimănești Town Hall, within the project "DIGITALISATION FOR THE BENEFIT OF CITIZENS AND COMPANIES", financed through the financing contract no. 60/12.07.2024, signed between the South-West Oltenia Regional Development Agency, acting as the Managing Authority for the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021-2027 (AM PR SV Oltenia) and the Administrative-Territorial Unit of Călimănești Town. The provisions of this section are supplemented by the provisions of the Specifications. The number of days before the deadline for submitting tenders by which clarifications may be requested is 20 days. The contracting authority shall clearly and fully respond to all requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for submitting tenders. Estimated total value: 2.217.410,08 lei, excluding VAT Contract duration: 6 months Warranty period: 36 months. Implementation of electronic public services at Călimănești Town Hall, within the project "DIGITALISATION FOR THE BENEFIT OF CITIZENS AND COMPANIES", financed through the financing contract no. 60/12.07.2024, signed between the South-West Oltenia Regional Development Agency, acting as the Managing Authority for the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021-2027 (AM PR SV Oltenia) and the Administrative-Territorial Unit of Călimănești Town. In accordance with the attached Specifications. The infrastructure components of the IT system in this procedure refer to the following: 1. Registry and Document Management Module Creation of a Document Management System (DMS) that manages documents in a centralised and organised manner for better efficiency and control within the local administration. This system will be used to monitor the document workflow, creation and editing of documents, storage, archiving, indexing and searching of documents, electronic signature. 2. GIS IT System – Creation of a GIS Portal which shall have the responsibility of ensuring: § availability of geospatial resources; facilitating their discovery and use; creation of a collaborative environment between all departments within a town hall; § facilitation of analytical and decision-making activities, based on geospatial information. The geospatial portal will implement specific digital workflows and an open data platform. To this end, the procurement and implementation of an integrated geospatial IT system is envisaged that will cover all the institution's needs, namely: urban planning, cadastre, street nomenclature, green spaces register. The IT component to be procured targets both the front-office and back-office areas; interoperability with the other IT systems of the Administrative-Territorial Unit shall be ensured. Functions: - Shall allow the creation of interactive web mapping maps. - Shall allow obtaining new perspectives and enhanced details as one interacts with the data. - Shall allow the use of smart, data-driven mapping styles and intuitive analysis tools to obtain location insights. - Shall allow sharing GIS maps with the public or using maps in collaboration. - Shall allow the creation of interactive maps that map local GIS databases and encourage the public to explore. - Shall allow sharing maps based on GIS data with specific groups or with everyone. - The public shall benefit from secure and simple access to the data, maps and applications they need 3. WEB Public Platform for Citizens (Citizen Module) The platform must ensure integration with the rest of the components requested in this procedure, so as to provide an integrated experience for the end user. The portal will allow citizens to track and monitor the status of their requests and provide feedback, as well as provide access to online services. The platform will be designed to facilitate the interaction of the Public Administration with citizens. It is a module that allows the citizen to interact with the town hall in digital form, and which will ensure real-time answers to questions, various processes managed by the platform can be initiated or information associated with geospatial objects can be attached/imported. The platform will allow: - Creation of special accounts through which specific datasets can be viewed, various processes managed by the platform can be initiated or information associated with geospatial objects can be attached/imported. - Communication between the citizen and the representatives of the Authority - Allows the creation of accounts for citizens or other third parties and the initiation of various processes - The application allows the creation of a schedule visible to the citizen with the time slots available for audience meetings. - Local announcements regarding certain public works, street closures, etc. - Local administration development programmes, their status and completion outlook - The possibility to access other public services (e.g. waste collection, educational unit information, local medical service information, information on existing European funds, Agency for Payments and Intervention in Agriculture information, etc.) - Submission of applications and complaints - The application allows the creation of a schedule visible to the citizen with the time slots available for audience meetings with the mayor/deputy mayor/secretary - Online scheduling of citizens for audience meetings with the mayor/deputy mayor/secretary - Online scheduling system – website that allows the online scheduling of citizens at various Public Local Administration counters; - To have an API through which interoperability with the local taxes and duties application is ensured so as to allow the payment of taxes and duties via the ghişeul.ro system into the town hall's account. 4.

Administration Module The module shall include content, website backend platform structure for the administrator: § Administration of groups, roles and users § Management of tourist attractions, event calendar, announcements, press releases. § Administration and generation of lists and reports 5. "Cloud" services – dedicated cloud services for use by the public administration (configuration and testing on server): • Secure access and automatic back-up infrastructure; • A system availability rate of 99%; • Unlimited storage space that can be expanded without requiring system downtime; 6. Development of the knowledge and skills of the staff within the Administrative-Territorial Unit, in order to support the measures targeted by the project. Training/instruction, evaluation/testing and certification of the acquired competencies/knowledge are envisaged for 20 persons regarding the use of the IT solutions and equipment supplied and implemented within this project.

sig_e2a9c39ed2c16071adfa.description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Product Service Code: DA01 – IT and Telecom – BUSINESS APPLICATION/APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT SERVICES (LABOR) NAICS Code: 541519 – Other Computer Related Services Solicitation Number: W50NH9-26-R-A019 Notice Type: Pre-Solicitation Procuring Agency: U.S. Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) Requiring Activity: U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM) Anticipated Award Type: Time and Materials (T&M), 5-Year Long-Term Contract (LTC) The United States Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA), on behalf of the U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (INSCOM), intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) W50NH9-26-R-A019 for Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Architecture Information Technology (IT) Contractor Manpower Equivalent (CME) Support (formerly known as Integrated Geospatial Intelligence Enterprise Architecture - IGEA). This action involved holistic IT services and related logistic, programmatic, training, and management support for GEOINT operations. The planned level of effort is 30 Full-time Equivalents (FTEs), plus up to an additional three surge FTEs, distributed across various Contiguous United States (CONUS) and Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS). Most of the performance is expected to occur at Fort Gordon, Georgia, but other locations include Honolulu, Hawaii; Wiesbaden, Germany; Vicenza, Italy; Republic of Korea; San Antonio, Texas; and Colorado Springs, Colorado. Notes: We expect to post the solicitation in 2 to 4 weeks. Use of Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) – Solicitation Module. sig_e2ae3a98021df988e49f.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines, which includes a selection of publications and a user interface for accessing, browsing, searching and reading the publications, as well as related support services. The Subscriber is able to obtain various usage statistics on the use of the service and the publications it contains. Access to the digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines must be available to the entire Government (ministries, the Office of the Chancellor of Justice and the Office of the President of the Republic). Access to the service is enabled via IP authentication or SSO single sign-on, which ensure that only the Subscriber's authorised users can access the service. The Subscriber's personnel have access to the service platform maintained by the Supplier as a SaaS service, which contains the domestic newspapers and magazines selected and procured by the Subscriber. The Subscriber's personnel can browse the collection, perform searches on the titles in the collection and select a publication title to read. The features and functionalities of the service platform are presented in Appendix 1 "Minimum requirements". The link or links to individual publication titles in the service will be published on the Subscriber's intranet as well as on other internal sites where information resources procured for the use of the Government are presented to Government personnel. There must be remote access to the service and the publications subscribed to by the Subscriber. Remote access means that, when working remotely, the Subscriber's personnel use the service on devices provided by the employer within the Government network. The procurement includes the possibility of additional procurement during the contract period for individual new newspaper and magazine titles. One magazine can be read simultaneously by a number of users defined in advance for each publication. The newspaper selection can be read by six users simultaneously. The service is available to the Subscriber's personnel around the clock, every day of the year. The Tenderer must attach to its tender a description of the digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines. Based on the tender competition, the Subscriber will select one supplier with whom it will enter into a contract. IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT The implementation of the service must begin upon the signing of the contract and the implementation must be complete 1 months after the signing of the contract. The content of the implementation project is the establishment and commissioning of the service. During implementation, the compliance of the service with the requirements is verified. During the implementation project, the supplier's task is: - To implement all those features to which the supplier has committed in its tender. - To open access for the Subscriber to the newspaper and magazine selection defined in the Price Form in Appendix 2 of the call for tenders. - To assist the Subscriber if necessary during acceptance testing. Implementation ends when all tasks have been completed and the Subscriber has tested the delivered system and found the system's features to be acceptable. If deficiencies are discovered during testing, the Supplier shall correct the deficiencies and the Subscriber shall test them again. Testing continues until the Subscriber declares the phase acceptable, unless the Subscriber considers the system to be so deficient that implementation cannot continue.
sig_e2ae3a98021df988e49f.title: Procurement of a digital service for domestic newspapers and magazines

sig_e2b719e2f1ab79718bd7.description: Consulting services to support corporate development / strategy and transformation processes Division into 2 lots Lot 1: Standard consulting services Lot 2: Special consulting services Standard consulting services The subject of the framework agreement is consulting, moderation and support services to accompany Nordwasser GmbH in its further corporate development and in strategic, organisational, commercial and technical issues. The services are provided on a demand-driven basis in the form of individual call-offs. The respective scope of services is concretely defined by the contracting authority on an occasion- and project-specific basis. The respective scope of services is determined by the contracting authority. The services require in-depth professional and methodological expertise, particularly in the context of water and wastewater infrastructure. There is no entitlement to specific call-offs. The assumption of line functions by the contractor is excluded. The services may in particular include the following areas: In the area of strategy and corporate development, strategies are developed, updated and reviewed. Strategic goals, programmes and measure portfolios are derived and decision-making bases are created. In addition, management systems are established and strategy communication is supported. In the area of governance and committee support, steering committees and control circles are prepared, moderated and followed up. Decision proposals are prepared and governance and coordination processes are designed and supported. Conflict and escalation situations can be moderated. In the area of organisational development, change and culture, organisational analyses are carried out and target structures are developed. Change processes are conceived and supported. Workshops are prepared and moderated, and communication and participation formats are designed. In the area of process management, processes are analysed, standardised and optimised. Key figure systems are developed and the implementation of improvement measures is supported. In the area of cost-effectiveness and management, cost-effectiveness and risk analyses are carried out. Budget, planning and management processes are supported. In addition, procurement strategies are prepared and reporting and controlling approaches are developed. In the area of technical topics, innovations and energy, concepts, technologies and technical options are evaluated. Pilot projects are supported and coordination between technical, economic and strategic requirements is supported. In the area of project management, projects are planned, managed and monitored. Project management structures are established, progress is monitored and project teams are moderated. The service areas mentioned are not exhaustive. The respective provision of services shall be governed exclusively by the contents defined in the individual call-offs.; Special consulting services: The subject of this lot is specialised consulting and support services, in particular in the area of asset management for technical concepts and innovations of Nordwasser GmbH. The services are provided on a demand-driven and project-specific basis within the framework of individual call-offs. The respective scope of services is determined by the contracting authority. The services require in-depth professional and methodological expertise, particularly in the context of water and wastewater infrastructure. There is no entitlement to specific call-offs. The assumption of line functions by the contractor is excluded. The services may in particular include the analysis, evaluation and further development of existing approaches and methods for condition monitoring and assessment of assets. This also includes examining transferability to different asset classes and identifying potential optimisation. Furthermore, services for the analysis and further development of asset strategies can be provided. This includes in particular the structured evaluation of existing strategic approaches, the introduction of external professional perspectives and support in deriving optimisation and action options. Another possible service component is methodological support in the development and further development of criteria and approaches for assessing the importance and criticality of assets. The aim here can be in particular to improve decision-making bases for planning, prioritisation and investment. The services may include analytical, conceptual and moderative elements and take place in close coordination with the contracting authority. The service areas mentioned are not exhaustive. The respective provision of services shall be governed exclusively by the contents defined in the respective individual call-off.

sig_e2c77480559669cc79f8.description: This preliminary market engagement notice has been issued by Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Combined Fire Authority also known as Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service (LFRS). The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is for LFRS to connect with suppliers of Occupational Health systems that are currently available on the market. We invite interest from suppliers to provide product information and engage in demonstrations of how their existing solutions will meet our present and future requirements. Overview of Requirement Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service has around 700 employees, including 490 operational staff. The Occupational Health department helps Leicestershire and Rescue Service ensure that its working practices do not have a negative impact on its employees' health, and that an employee's health does not impact their ability to perform their roles. This includes looking at both the mental and physical health of our workforce through different activities, including: - Health screening for potential new employees - Health surveillance of existing employees in line with relevant HSE legislation and requirements - Periodic physical fitness testing for all operational personnel - Management referrals in relation to sickness absence - Self referrals for employee support including counselling and physiotherapy - Immunisations where required The Occupational Health department employs six full time members of staff and procures the services of healthcare professionals including doctors and nurses. Further information can be obtained from the website https://www.leics-fire.gov.uk Requirement Details The Occupational Health department requires an Occupational Health system to conduct the following tasks and activities: - Diary management for the Scheduling of in-house appointments including automated reminders by e-mail/text messaging - Recording and monitoring of health surveillance data - Interface with spirometry (currently MIR Spirolab A23) and audiometry devices (currently Amplivox CA850) - Management of referrals and generation of management referral reports - Generate reports on activities for the service - The system must comply with UK legislation and good practice for data protection - Existing occupational health records from the existing OH system particularly relating to health surveillance will need to be migrated to the new system - It would be desirable for the system to have the capability of an electronic questionnaire for recording fitness data - It would be desirable for the system to have the ability for scheduled reports or APIs to enable automated reporting of statistics to the organisation's data warehouse (PowerBI) - It would be desirable for the system to have the ability to integrate with either the organisation's HR system (FireWatch by Infographics) or Azure Entra (Active Directory) to enable the OH system to automatically update to reflect the organisation's employee changes to establishment - starters, changes of role, and leavers Volumes Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service requires a total of seven licenses for the Occupational Health team. Access for fit forms and management reports may be required by managers. Lot 1: .

sig_e2d39239f3a2a8152a75.description: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration needs to procure a cloud based switchboard and call centre system. The system shall first and foremost cover the Norwegian Public Roads Administration ́s need for handling enquiries by using telephony as well as a channel, as well as SMS for outgoing enquiries to customers. The system shall, however, also allow for other channels such as chat, email and social media to be in use during the agreement period. The aim is to procure a system that contributes to a better user experience for the Norwegian Public Roads Administration ́s customers. Customers should be able to use their most preferred channel when they contact and they shall find that the Norwegian Public Roads Administration has a good overview and is available so that they can quickly get answers to their enquiries. At the same time, customers should feel confident that their privacy is safeguarded. In order to deliver good user experiences for the Norwegian Public Roads Administration ́s customers, the system shall also facilitate efficient work processes that make it easy and quick to help and guide customers. The system shall be used by a large number of agents. It is therefore important that the solution is experienced as intuitive as possible, including that screen images and number of clicks are reduced to a minimum. The system shall also provide good work support to the Norwegian Public Roads Administration ́s administrators. It shall be easy to share relevant information to customers and they shall have a tool for simpler administration and allocation of resources/agents as well as a tool for reporting and analysing customer enquiries.
sig_e2d39239f3a2a8152a75.title: Procurement of a system for telephone exchanges and call centres.

sig_e2ed645a61e73361342a.description: The Stadt Burgdorf is centrally located in the north-eastern area of the Hannover Region, in the middle of the Hannover - Celle - Braunschweig - Hildesheim urban quadrangle with very good connections to the supra-regional road and rail network. Burgdorf has 31.156 inhabitants and its economy is characterised by small and medium-sized enterprises. The Stadt Burgdorf has been included in the subsidized urban development funding programme "Lebendige Zentren" (Vibrant Centres) with the redevelopment area "Innenstadt Burgdorf" since 2022. As part of this multi-year redevelopment measure, the establishment of so-called "city management" is planned for the year 2026. Inner-city development is increasingly understood as a joint task that requires active, steering management. The city marketing association Stadtmarketingverein Burgdorf e.V. (SMB) has been firmly anchored in urban society for decades (2.700 members). It works closely with the Verkehrs- und Verschönerungsverein Burgdorf (VVV) and is already implementing a diverse range of projects. However, there is no strongly developed district or neighbourhood life within the city centre itself. This is where city management comes in: it is intended to close a gap between existing city marketing activities and stakeholder activation focused on the city centre. City management assumes this role as a coordinating and networking interface between the municipality, citizens, business owners and other stakeholders. The aim of this project is to drive the city centre forward into a more attractive, active place of social, economic and cultural coexistence. In its role as a networking body, city management is intended to bundle activities, initiate projects and steer processes. City management does not compete with existing stakeholders, but rather supplements their work with a coordination and activation function focused on the redevelopment area. It does not work within the city administration, but rather as an external contractor that cooperates closely with the departments for economic development, urban planning and environment, culture, and youth welfare. Lot LOT-0001: Ex Post: Stadt Burgdorf: City management for the redevelopment area Innenstadt Burgdorf. City management encompasses the core tasks described below. The list is not exhaustive. By its nature, the activity of city management requires flexible reaction to changing framework conditions, requirements and local opportunities in order to achieve the overarching task objectives. Further individual activities may therefore arise within the framework of the annual target agreement (cf. section 5 paragraph 2 of the advisory contract), provided they correspond to the subject and purpose of the city management. - Contact person in the redevelopment area - Support and communication in the redevelopment process - Acquisition of funding - Establishment and management of the allocation fund - Development and increase in the attractiveness of the inner-city business location - Public relations and press work - Communication and reporting The individual services can be found in the specification of services (Part B of the tender documents) and the advisory contract (Part C of the tender documents).

sig_e2f7b6987ab95d8d27ea.description: DOTLUMEN S.R.L. is organising the award procedure for the contract for the supply of a Robot Kit in order to equip the research team with the robotic platforms necessary for testing and validating pedestrian autonomous navigation algorithms (PAD AI) in real urban environments. Achieving the research and development objectives targeted in the PABLO project necessarily requires the physical availability of the robotic platforms on which the algorithms will be run, tested and validated, both in simulation environments and in real field conditions. The acquired robotic platforms will advance the technology readiness level (TRL) of the solution from TRL4 (validated in laboratory) to TRL7-8 (system demonstrated in a real operational environment), thereby constituting a necessary and irreplaceable condition for achieving the project performance indicators. The subject of this public procurement contract consists of the supply, DDP transport to the beneficiary's premises and functional verification of the following robotic platforms and associated accessories, within the PABLO project: - Bipedal (humanoid) robot – 1 pcs., with a computing module compatible with NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor or equivalent and robotic hands included; - Additional battery for bipedal robot – 1 pcs.; - Quadruped robot – Unitree B2W or equivalent – 2 pcs., with LIDAR included in the standard configuration, minimum protection rating IP67 and additional replacement battery included per unit; - Robotic arm for quadruped robot – Unitree Z1 Pro or equivalent – 1 pcs., with a reach of at least 740 mm; - Technical documentation, SDK/API interfaces and technical knowledge transfer. The acquired robotic platforms will be used exclusively for testing and validation of the PAD AI (Pedestrian Autonomous Driving AI) algorithms developed by the PABLO consortium within the framework of research and development activities. The contract includes the functional verification of each platform upon delivery and the transfer of technical knowledge regarding system operation. - Financing programme: POCIDIF – Programme for Smart Growth, Digitisation and Financial Instruments - Priority: P1 – Supporting and promoting an attractive and competitive RDI ecosystem in Romania - Specific objective: RSO1.1 – Developing and enhancing research and innovation capacities and the adoption of advanced technologies - Project call no.: PCIDIF/159/PCIDIF_P1/OP1/RSO1.1/PCIDIF_A1 - Financing contract no. 390060 / 16.09.2025, SMIS Code: 333334 The robotic platforms, together with the PAD AI software infrastructure, directly contribute to achieving the specific objective of the project and fulfilling the general objective, namely the creation of an efficient, sustainable and automated system of autonomous logistics robots for the urban delivery of products in the final phase (last-mile delivery), capable of reducing operational costs, optimising delivery times and minimising environmental impact.

sig_e33d02c87a48a62f6599.description: The aim of the project is the implementation of the new Diavgeia taking into account modern institutional, operational and technological developments, the more correct implementation of the institutional framework with emphasis on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the optimal utilisation of Diavgeia information with a data-based architecture and secondarily document-based. The project seeks to increase the efficiency and productivity of public services by enriching the applications of the Diavgeia Programme, supplementing functionality for the collaborative drafting and management of documents to be published based on standardised documents and data structures, and also to add value to the Programme by utilising and enriching the information gathered within it through the use of other information sources with the aim of creating a system of complex reports and other complementary application subsystems and solutions. The new system will allow the monitoring of the operation and organisational structure of public administration in combination with information related to the competences of bodies in the context of multi-level governance and also of personnel as recorded in the Human Resources Register of the Hellenic Republic. The aim is to provide objective evidence for the implementation of the National Administrative Procedures Policy and the prioritisation of the actions of the National Programme for Administrative Simplification. To this end, care has been taken to significantly enhance its interoperability with third-party public sector systems for the dissemination of information without necessarily requiring intervention from the end user. Additionally, through the expansion of information kept in a structured manner (metadata set), it will be possible to capture data groups with special characteristics that enhance transparency at the level of monitoring/evaluation by the general public of indicators related to, for example, the operation and structure of public administration and/or financial figures (public spending). For this purpose, data from other sources and publicly available data will also be utilised to support the monitoring of the operation and action of bodies and to support decision-making. The solution will include the creation of a system for the correct (and as complete as possible per sector) structured collection and processing of data from various public data sources and subsequently making them available to the general public. Illustrative examples of sources are data from systems under development for GOV ERP, HRMS, the Civil Society Organisations Register, ESIDIS, KHMDIS. A distinct subsystem will be developed for further utilisation and extraction of specialised reports with the aim of monitoring the structure, operation and action of public administration as well as monitoring expenditure and procurement and supporting the decision-making process. The system will be scalable for the addition of new sources arising from other actions. Also, within the framework of the action, improvements will be made in relation to identified problems associated with the management of the very large volume of documents collected by Diavgeia at a sharply increasing rate, which also led to the necessary migration of the infrastructure to public cloud services. In this context, advanced services provided by public clouds will be better utilised in order to ensure the uninterrupted provision of services and the monitoring of their provision at the lowest possible cost. The action, taking into account the life cycle of the administrative documents that are published, will address challenges such as the cleaning of multiple copies of the same documents, the extraction of all information in data format and the optimisation of the quality of Diavgeia metadata as well as the automatic publication of important data sets in the central open public data repository www.data.gov.gr. The project also aims to adopt a new architecture that will allow a drastic reduction, by at least 65%, of the required storage space and computational resources while ensuring the proper functioning of the system. To achieve the above goal, both emerging artificial intelligence and language model technologies and techniques for the correct entry of metadata into relevant information will be utilised to facilitate their search, categorisation and utilisation. This contract concerns a single subject matter and is not subdivided into lots due to the project's architecture, the strong interdependencies and complementarity of the individual services that compose it, as well as the high interoperability requirements that must be ensured on the one hand between the functional units (subsystems) to be developed within the framework of this project and on the other hand with third-party systems of Hellenic Republic bodies. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the chances of security gaps or incompatibilities appearing between the different systems and facilitates the coordination of its implementation. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-two (32) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3. & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]
sig_e33d02c87a48a62f6599.title: «Restructuring of the DIAYGEIA Programme - DIAYGEIA III»

sig_e33de6871b06fb91aa7d.description: Over time, EPFL has built up a complex network of data exchanges between systems, based on multiple in-house developed applications. Although functional, current processing within these perimeters presents several limitations. The objectives: • Governance: security, quality, rigorous data confidentiality: Ensure governance, security, compliance and trust in the use of data throughout its lifecycle • Unified data ecosystem: Create a coherent and secure unified environment, eliminating silos to improve collaboration and unlock valuable cross-domain insights • Stimulate innovation: by enabling the development of new data-driven products and services such as AI • Improve operational efficiency: by automating data-related tasks and reducing manual interventions. • Empower users with data access: Provide the EPFL community with tools to easily access, analyse and use quality real-time data, facilitating decision-making • Modern data source ingestion: Be able to quickly and governedly catalogue/ingest/connect/transform/publish new data sources for all types of consumption, analytics, data science, operational, artificial intelligence. • Modern integration between applications: Deploy an efficient integration platform ensuring data flows, smooth workflows, guaranteeing consistency between applications and business processes. These objectives will be achieved by: • Deploying modern and easy-to-use tools. • Supporting the transformation with change management. • Decommissioning obsolete tools and systems. The main technical components expected in the long term within the programme are: • An orchestrator (ORC) to schedule the various processes cross-functionally. • A data exchange platform (EIP): API-oriented for inter-application data exchange (API Management, Enterprise Service Bus). Data exchange platform (EIP): A solution that enables the connection and integration of different applications, systems and services, to ensure smooth communication and automated inter-application exchanges: * Ensure the various types of inter-application exchanges in a secure, intuitive and innovative manner, limiting redundant and point-to-point connections * Quickly set up modern, shared, interconnected and scalable APIs and services * Offer an open, integrated, centralised and secure administration interface allowing the management of the complete API lifecycle * Promote and establish a common approach to the development and provision of data within the various IT department teams.

sig_e352ed2bab4fb194f4cb.description: "Support for the seamless, secure and efficient operation of the Central IT Infrastructure of the Municipality of Thessaloniki for a period of twenty-four (24) months", with the award criterion being the most economically advantageous tender based on price, with a budget of 312.480,00€ (including VAT of 24%). The Municipality of Thessaloniki maintains and develops a complex and extensive Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure network, which consists of a Data Center at the City Hall that covers the City Hall and approximately 120 buildings throughout the city. This network includes high-performance Cisco devices, which ensure the secure, uninterrupted and efficient operation of the Municipality's services. Infrastructure Structure and Description The network of the Municipality of Thessaloniki is based on a hierarchical architecture, which includes three main levels: 1. Core Layer: The core network is located in the Data Center of the City Hall and constitutes the core of the infrastructure. Here are the main servers, data storage devices, and Cisco devices that manage data traffic and VoIP telephony. The main devices in the Core Layer are: o Cisco Nexus 56128P switches: Used for high-performance interconnection between servers and storage devices. o Cisco firewall firepower 2110, CISCO firewall firepower 1120, ASA-5545-X firewalls: Provide protection against threats and ensure network security. o CISCO UCS 5108 Blade Server: Used for virtualisation and application hosting. o Data storage devices: NETAPP FAS2650, NETAPP AFF-C190. 2. Distribution Layer: This level connects the Core Layer with the peripheral buildings and the internal points of the city hall and manages data traffic between them. The main devices in the Distribution Layer are: o Cisco Nexus 56128P switches, C1000-48T-4X-L switches: Used for managing data traffic between devices in the Data Center. 3. Access Layer: This level provides network access for users in peripheral buildings. The main devices in the Access Layer are: o Cisco ISR 1101 routers: Manage WAN connections and ensure communication between buildings. o Cisco WS-C2960-48TC-L switches: Used for connecting computers, printers and IP phones in the buildings. o Cisco IP phones (7962, 7906, 3905, etc.): Provide VoIP telephone services throughout the network. 4. Cloud Services: The Municipality of Thessaloniki also uses Cloud services through the G-Cloud (Government Cloud) of the General Secretariat of Information Systems & Digital Governance. These services include application hosting and data storage with the possibility of expansion and flexibility. To ensure and maintain the secure, uninterrupted and effective operation of the aforementioned, as well as to achieve continuous expansions and changes to them, the Directorate of E-Government, Information Technology & Communications (ICT) has specialised and experienced scientific and technical personnel. This personnel undertakes the daily supervision, development, maintenance and improvement of these infrastructures. However, due to the rapid evolution of technology and continuous upgrades, as well as the constant emergence of new services, it is obvious that the Municipality of Thessaloniki cannot manage and support these infrastructures alone. Even companies or organisations much larger than the Municipality of Thessaloniki, which have much larger Information and Communication Technology departments, encounter problems with the human resources required for the operation and management of similar infrastructures and services. Therefore, it is necessary for the Municipality of Thessaloniki to seek and cooperate with experienced, reliable and certified companies in the field of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT). These companies must provide specialised and integrated operation-management and support services in order to ensure the uninterrupted, secure and efficient operation of the aforementioned systems. The management of this infrastructure requires specialised personnel with CCIE, VCP-DCV, Microsoft Certified certifications. Consequently, the Municipality of Thessaloniki must conduct a tender for the purpose of assigning the said support services through a contract, which in this study will be referred to as a maintenance contract. The said maintenance contract will be valid for twenty-four (24) months and the contractor will be selected through the procedures of an Electronic Open Tender Above Thresholds. The support will include the aforementioned services and infrastructures, i.e. the integrated data and telephony network at the City Hall, the data and telephony networks in the peripheral buildings of the Municipality of Thessaloniki, the servers and services that form the central computing and storage infrastructures, as well as any other service described in the technical specifications of the contract. The services that the selected contractor will provide include, among others: • System restoration and installation services. • Scheduled system installation and configuration services. • Software and server support services. • VoIP telephony support services. • Off-site backup services. • Component and equipment replacement services. • Other specialised services described herein. Monthly Support for the seamless, secure and efficient operation of the Central IT Infrastructure of the Municipality of Thessaloniki

sig_e364ce2b3d3779bb5633.description:
BudapestGO application development and related services The Contracting Authority, based on point c) of paragraph 1 of Section 105 of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.), specifies in this call for tenders the additions in respect of which the Tenderer must supplement their tender: The winning tenderer's task is to create the capability to send extraordinary traffic disruption alerts, direct marketing messages, maintenance notifications and other messages, such that the filtering and segmentation of users based on various criteria (e.g. previously purchased fare products, application language, time of last login, etc.) is resolved. In addition, the development provides new deep-linking options for push messages and in-app messages, with which we can direct the user to different parts of the application, and creates the possibility for BudapestGO to send different notification sounds. The purpose of the push message development is to enable more effective and personalised communication with BudapestGO users. One of the most important functions of the application is the immediate communication of information, for example in the event of traffic changes, service notifications or promotional campaigns. With the push development, customers can receive more relevant, informative and even timed messages, which increases the customer experience. From a business perspective, the goal of the development is to expand BudapestGO's communication capabilities and improve the efficiency, segmentability and measurability of messaging, which supports the long-term plans of BudapestGO and BKK. A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is provided as an annex to this document.; The Contracting Authority, based on point c) of paragraph 1 of Section 105 of the Kbt., specifies in this call for tenders the additions in respect of which the Tenderer must supplement their tender: In 2026, Budapest's public bicycle system, MOL Bubi, will be renewed. The third generation of the system operated by BKK will serve Budapest commuters with a fleet at least twice as large as the current one (including at least 1000 electric bicycles) and a larger service area. Within the framework of the system, on a pilot basis - expectedly after the summer of 2027 - 20 cargo (electrically assisted) and ~600 child-seat (mechanical) bicycles will also be available. Our goal for the launch of the new generation is for BudapestGO to be able to display the new Bubi better than it currently does, thereby supporting the awareness and popularity of sustainable modes of transport. The Bubi 3.0 integration is a project implemented in several phases. The goal of the development is to achieve the level of integration (display and route planning) of the new, 3.0 generation of Bubi that already exists for the current generation. The high-level scope of the phase is as follows: ASIS operation with minor fine-tuning and additions • Display of new equipment: receiving and processing API data • Implementing changes related to the POI type of Bubi collection stations and Mobi points • Displaying point capacity and occupancy data (on the bottom sheet component) • Design systemisation (or updating) of POI popovers and other new/modified components involved in the development. During the design phase, the final, complete API description was not available. Consequently, if changes appear later in the final API documentation - for example, structural modifications or previously undefined value sets - we can undertake to handle these within the framework of a request. A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is provided as an annex to this document.; The Contracting Authority, based on point c) of paragraph 1 of Section 105 of the Kbt., specifies in this call for tenders the additions in respect of which the Tenderer must supplement their tender: BKK plans to introduce products that can be purchased primarily during B2B sales, typically, but not exclusively - offered to BudapestGO by the NMFR system via an exclusive interface, the purchase of which it wishes to restrict, i.e. there should be no possibility to purchase them from the app according to the current normal process. They intend to ensure the purchase (availability and usability) of these products for their partners and their partners' customers with the coupon functionality to be launched in the 2025R5 release. However, these redeemed products must currently appear on mobile front-ends. Within the framework of the development, fare product hiding on mobile front-ends will be implemented, as well as the associated Customer Service Back Office and the display development for the last 10 purchased product, in order to ensure that certain products are only available under limited circumstances. A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is provided as an annex to this document.; The Contracting Authority, based on point c) of paragraph 1 of Section 105 of the Kbt., specifies in this call for tenders the additions in respect of which the Tenderer must supplement their tender: The goal of the development is to increase the comfortable usability of BudapestGO (as well as its compliance with other aspects) by handling minor but annoying errors and deficiencies that arose during customer feedback and testing. The package does not introduce new major features, but formulates minor fine-tuning requirements for existing functions, thereby increasing user satisfaction with existing functions and reducing potential misunderstandings and inconveniences resulting from operation. Unless otherwise indicated for an item, its implementation will be carried out for both platforms (iOS and Android). The package contains 5 minor, well-defined tasks, which can be divided into 3 larger groups: I. Individual development requirements 1. Home screen shortcuts 2. Relocation of the information button in the My Tickets menu 3.

Display of route-bound custom informative texts (in bottom sheet component) II. Bug fixes handled as requirements 4. BPGO-2033: Completely overlapping UI III. Parameterisations 5. Harmonisation of validity period displayed in case of corporate annual passes The operation expected during the individual sub-items is elaborated in the following chapter. Refactoring of iOS screens: In case of data loaded from multiple different sources (e.g. BKK Info), flickering may occur in the BPGO application; refactoring the screens is necessary to resolve this. Screen flickering occurring mainly on screens related to BKK Info is annoying for users; our goal with the development is to ensure that this does not happen in the future. Display of stop identifiers: In Budapest transport, several multimodal capital transport hubs have developed where the display of stop identifiers is essential for passenger information. The purpose of the development is to display BKK stop data (hub identifiers) on the relevant screens of the application. Through the newly displayed information, the efficiency of passenger information and the popularity of the application can be increased. Coupon 2.0 With the development, we implement fine-tunes that optimise the usability of the previously introduced coupon function. Through the introduction of searchability, filtering functions and the display of extra information, the internal management process becomes simpler. On the other hand, we can provide the redemption deadline more accurately for the customer (display of hour/minute), and thirdly, from an auditing perspective, we can ensure traceability (by providing the justification for inactivation). A detailed description of the Tenderer's tasks is contained in the Technical Specification, which is made available as an annex to this document.

sig_e3add8c1b4cc747eb462.description: Project "Air Quality Monitoring in the Area of the Port Authority of Dubrovnik" - Procurement and installation of measuring and auxiliary equipment Project "Air Quality Monitoring in the Area of the Port Authority of Dubrovnik" - Procurement and installation of measuring and auxiliary equipment The subject of this tender is the procurement of goods and their installation, all in accordance with the technical specifications, drawings and bill of quantities, which indicate the name, quantity and other conditions necessary for completing the bid. The subject of procurement is not divided into lots and the estimated procurement value relates to the entire subject of procurement, and the Contracting Authority intends to conclude a single public procurement contract with the selected economic operator for the entire subject of procurement. The project includes the construction and equipping of a container-type reference measuring station for continuous air quality monitoring in the area of the Port Authority of Dubrovnik Through the implementation of modern technologies, the project will enable the monitoring of pollutants whose concentrations need to be continuously measured at the selected location of the Ploče Port Authority, namely: gaseous pollutants nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and particulate matter PM10 and PM2,5. At the location, it is necessary to continuously measure meteorological parameters (temperature, relative humidity, wind direction and speed). Also, the analyser must have the capability to check particle concentrations at the station using a reference material. The subject of the contract includes A Supply, construction and installation of one automatic air quality monitoring station in container design B Supply and installation of auxiliary equipment - three sensor stations for air quality measurement C Calibration of gaseous pollutant analysers in an accredited calibration laboratory in accordance with the HRN EN ISO/IEC 17025 standard or equivalent before delivery and after one year of station operation D Installation of an information system for the collection, storage, transmission and processing/validation of measurement results E Maintenance/servicing of equipment during two years of station operation in accordance with the equipment manufacturer's recommendations F Data validation during two years of station operation G Conducting the PM10/PM2.5 equivalence procedure during the first year of operation Criteria for assessing the equivalence of the subject of procurement: The Contracting Authority does not use descriptions citing a specific brand or source, or a specific process with characteristics of products or services provided by a specific economic operator, or trademarks, patents, types or a specific origin or production if this would have the effect of favouring or excluding certain economic operators or certain products, unless justified by the subject of procurement. If the contracting authority cannot describe the subject of procurement or any part thereof with sufficient precision and clarity, it shall include the term "or equivalent" alongside the designation, as well as the technical specification, i.e., elements which are criteria for assessing equivalence. Provisions on standards If technical rules describing the subject of procurement using Croatian, European or international standards are stated in the procurement documents, the tenderer must offer the subject of procurement in accordance with the standards from the procurement documents or an equivalent solution. For each standard listed under the respective standardisation system, it is permitted to offer an equivalent solution, technical approval or instruction from the corresponding Croatian, European or international nomenclature, and in this case, every such instruction shall be deemed to be accompanied by the term "or equivalent" and tenderers shall be free to offer equivalent solutions. The Contracting Authority shall not reject a tender on the grounds that the offered works do not comply with the technical specifications referred to, if the tenderer proves in the tender, in a manner satisfactory to the public contracting authority, by any appropriate means, including the means of proof from Article 213 of the Public Procurement Act (2016), that the solutions proposed by them satisfy the requirements defined by the technical specifications in an equivalent manner.

sig_e3da182eb1226d833c73.description:
The HZD provides - specifically the Police Application Management division - technical operations for all centralised procedures of the Hessian Police. Various services are being put out to tender for this purpose. Lot LOT-0001: POLAS. The currently approx. 65.000 PC workstations are equipped with hardware from various companies and in most cases with operating systems and office communication software from Microsoft. In addition, centrally provided applications and services are used, such as a central email platform, portals based on SAP Netweaver, an information portal implemented with Drupal and a document management system. Applications are partly operated on the basis of Windows Terminal Servers. With a few exceptions, products from Oracle and Microsoft are used as databases. The workstations are embedded in a uniform directory and integrated into a central Exchange system. The published state standards and the HZD-side standards in their respective valid versions are bindingly applicable to work processes. These include in particular the IT Service Management operational processes standardized based on ITIL. The focus regarding the tendered services is on service delivery processes, namely incident, problem, change and release management. Embedded in this framework, the HZD - and specifically the Police Application Management division here - provides technical operations for all centralised procedures of the Hessian Police. Due to the high degree of centralization, high availability of the police applications centrally operated by the HZD is of the utmost importance for the deployment of police officers. A large proportion of the procedures serves the police to guarantee public safety and order and helps to avoid harm to the life and limb of citizens and police officers. Experience from recent years has shown that the introduction of new procedures (from planning to full operational rollout) and the implementation of major procedure updates or upgrades are most effectively carried out with a team that has up-to-date software know-how and many years of experience. This demand is also expected for the coming years in a correspondingly adapted form. In addition, state-political as well as federal-political demands must be increasingly implemented or integrated. Since the required personnel needs cannot always be covered in a timely manner in sufficient capacity and quality by internal employees, the contracting authority, the State of Hesse, represented by the HZD, intends to conclude a framework agreement with a company in accordance with Section 21 Paragraph 3 of the VgV, through which services up to the complete operational rollout of new procedures in the environment of police application management and associated cooperations and departments can be commissioned. The so-called "POLAS application family" contains on the one hand the state data management system for police-relevant data and is made available as a browser-based online web application in 24-hour operation. On the other hand, the state data management system is supplemented by more than 50 sub-procedures. The POLAS application family essentially serves the preventive combat and prosecution of criminal offences, sentence enforcement, hazard prevention and administrative assistance. Specifically, it enables the maintenance and querying of police-relevant personal data, wanted persons, arrest, alias and criminal records data, criminal records references, personal notes, case, property tracing and property damage data. The POLAS sub-procedure INPOL-Land is a cooperation product of the states of Hesse, Hamburg, Baden-Württemberg and Brandenburg and is used in part or in full in many other federal states (so-called "participating states"). The participating states have only a very limited right of co-determination and do not participate in the maintenance and further development of the software. The application is highly available and is operated on a hyperconverged virtualization platform in a 2-room concept. A distinction is made between productive, reference and development environments. In total, more than 18.000 users are connected to the system and access the data present in 21 Oracle databases with approx. 6 TB of data volume. The application is highly available and is operated on the Verfahrenscloud-Hessen with a total of around 80 VMs. A distinction is made between productive, reference, development and training environments. In total, more than 18.000 users are connected to the system and access the data present in approx. 45 Oracle databases with approx. 42 TB of data volume. In the POLAS specialist area, the contractor performs activities in connection with the administration of the specialist procedures of the POLAS family. Two role profiles are put out to tender ("POLAS Procedure Specialist" according to item 4.3.1 of the specification of services and "Senior POLAS Procedure Specialist" according to item 4.3.3 of the specification of services). The minimum qualification requirements can be found in items 4.3.2.1 and 4.3.4.1 of the specification of services. sig_e3dd8273c87801ca4ae9.description: The Electronic Public Procurement Classifieds of the Republic of Croatia (EOJN RH) is a national information system for electronic public procurement intended for contracting authorities, tenderers and other interested economic operators for the implementation of and participation in public procurement procedures in accordance with the applicable regulations of the Republic of Croatia and the European Union, with the aim of concluding public procurement contracts or framework agreements for goods, works or services, conducting design contests and awarding concessions. The EOJN RH portal is available at: https://eojn.hr. sig_e40ffaa8e885507d045c.description: The BBC produces and publishes content across a broad range of broadcast and digital platforms, encompassing short form, long form and social formats. Source media originates from diverse inputs including professional camera crews, self-shot devices, user generated content, graphics and archive materials. To support this, production teams require reliable ingest workflows, rich and consistent metadata, strong identity and access controls, collaborative editing capabilities, efficient review and approval processes, and appropriate automation across hybrid on premises and cloud environments. The BBC has well established and strategically aligned solutions that support News and craft editing workflows, and these remain the core platforms for those areas. This RFI is not intended to identify alternatives or replacements for those established workflows. Instead, the BBC is exploring opportunities to enhance media production capabilities in parts of the wider production landscape that are not currently served by dedicated, organisation wide tooling. As part of this forward-looking assessment, we are seeking to understand market capabilities that could help strengthen consistency, governance and interoperability across these broader production needs. Through this RFI, the BBC is seeking insight into vendor capabilities that could inform a unified ‘Production Library’ concept, a well governed platform supporting a broad range of functional requirements and able to integrate effectively with existing BBC workflows. Market input will help shape future policy and technology decisions and ensure alignment with industry best practice. Lot 1: .
sig_e40ffaa8e885507d045c.title: Production Library - Request for Information

The present tender focuses primarily on TenneT’s German operations. As beneficiaries under the SaaS Agreement, Dutch TenneT operations may optionally draw from the services that are subject hereof. With the re-tendering of the current Content Collaboration Platform, TenneT is aiming to continue achieving a single source of information for all documents generated in infrastructure projects and managing the supplier collaboration (external collaboration) regarding the exchange and management of documents and additional data. The targeted system is facilitating and capturing the complete project lifecycle in addition to providing auditable documentation and information throughout the organization. The tender procedure is divided into two lots, which will be tendered in sequence in two different tenders: Tender 1 [Lot 1] "CDE - Collaboration-Platform for Document and Data Exchange": includes the platform provisioning, development, deployment (Implementation), initial customization and configuration, platform interfaces as well as maintenance and support of the platform and – as a proof of concept and for purposes of a successful transition – the migration of TenneT metadata as well as existing construction projects from the current to the new platform. This tender has been completed. The awarded solution is provided by ThinkProject. Tender 2 [Lot 2]: "CDE – Multi-Contractor Integration": includes intergration and implementation services associated with the platform and comprises subsequent configuration, customization and consulting services in relation to the Content Collaboration Platform. The Lot 1 Provider must always collaborate pro-actively and in a constructive manner with any Lot 2 Contractor(s), e.g. providing access, support and knowledge transfer regarding the platform and implementing technically necessary changes within Lot 1 where mutually agreed with or commissioned by TenneT. Lot 2 will be tendered subsequent to the award of Lot 1. Performance Scope Lot 2 The Lot 2 providers selected during the selection phase must be qualified for the following service areas within the framework of the mini competitions and be able to obtain contracts in these areas: Business Support for CDE Initiatives and Projects The contractor shall provide advisory and operational support for departments and project teams in the context of CDE utilization, in particular: Advising on methodological and operational use of CDE platforms in project environments Supporting data migration processes (e.g., from legacy systems) Assisting with platform configuration and workflow optimization Developing and maintaining structured knowledge management tools (e.g., CDE user guides, training materials, FAQs) Facilitating workshops to gather and refine user requirements Design, Development, and Implementation of Non-Standard Changes This service domain includes support in extending the functional scope of the CDE platform beyond its standard features: Designing and specifying customized solutions (e.g., plug-ins, tailored workflows) Developing enhancements, interfaces, and automation features Supporting innovation initiatives, e.g., through prototyping of new digital tools Providing comprehensive technical and user documentation Performing quality assurance and testing of developed components Integration support for non-standard changes The contractor will provide technical and conceptual support for integrating enhancements into the existing CDE ecosystem: Designing and executing system integration concepts (e.g., CDE ↔ third-party systems) Developing and maintaining interfaces (e.g., REST, SOAP, file-based) Conducting system, integration, and regression testing Monitoring and issue resolution during and after go-live Preparing technical operations documentation (e.g., monitoring and handover guides) Project execution The contractor shall support the delivery of CDE-related (sub-)projects, including: Providing project management services (e.g., project office, timeline planning, reporting, risk management) Conducting requirement analysis and scope definition with business stakeholders Coordinating internal and external implementation partners Reporting to project leadership or steering committees Supporting change and rollout management measures For more details please see "L2 - C11 - Summary of Requirements" and "L2 – N01 – Annex 01 – Service Description" (will be sent after signing the NDA). Both tenders/lots are evaluated and awarded independently of each other. This publication refers only to Tender 2 [Lot 2]. Procedural note A detailed service description and other documents relevant to the procedure will be provided after signing an NDA. You will find the NDA in question 1.15. Please send it to us signed via the Mercell messaging function. The tender is being conducted in accordance with SektVO in a negotiated procedure with competitive participation.

sig_e4688950228b26e31367.description: TV 2 Kosmopol S/I (hereafter TV 2 Kosmopol) has assessed that the contract is covered by Section 80, subsection 3, no. 2 of the Public Procurement Act, and that the contract can therefore be concluded following a negotiated procedure without prior publication of a contract notice. The background to this is that Adobe is the sole supplier of a comprehensive package of image editing and graphics software, etc., that meets the needs of the TV 2 regions. The TV 2 regions place emphasis on the fact that files can be opened and processed across different software without barriers, and it is therefore essential that the various types of software are supplied by the same manufacturer. There are thus no actors other than Adobe that can supply a software package meeting the needs of the TV 2 regions. The agreement includes direct support from Adobe's development department, which is important for fulfilling special technical requirements in connection with the production method and other systems of the TV 2 regions. Furthermore, it is of crucial importance for the TV 2 regions to obtain the best possible price. The contract entails a fixed-price structure that simultaneously provides the TV 2 regions with flexibility regarding the possibility of extra licences during periods without extra payment. The agreement relates to all eight TV 2 regions' use of the software.
sig_e4688950228b26e31367.title: Prophylaxis Executive Order regarding Adobe for TV 2 regions

sig_e47d7bba309d0937d878.description: The subject of the procurement is a simulation system (AV system) located in the premises being completed in 2027 for the Jyväskylä Hippos Competence Centre for the use of the Welfare Unit of Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences, primarily for teaching use. The simulation system must cover all equipment and software listed in the invitation to tender. In addition to the actual simulation premises, the simulation environment covers all learning premises on two (2) floors and control rooms from which simulation situations and connections to various teaching premises are controlled. The simulation system will be used to create versatile simulation exercises for educational purposes that resemble genuine interaction and customer situations in the social and health care sector. The purpose of the simulation system is to enable the recording, storage and real-time guidance of teaching situations. The new Hippos Centre being built in Jyväskylä, the capital of sport, will offer a unique complex for movement, hobbies and sports. The Hippos area will further strengthen Jyväskylä's position as a leading research and education city for physical activity and elite sports. The Hippos Centre consists of four (4) complexes: a sports centre, a competence centre, an ice sports centre and the Hippos-Park multi-storey car park. Construction is being carried out in phases, and the project as a whole will be completed by the end of 2027. The Welfare Unit of Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences will relocate to the premises of the Hippos Competence Centre on the fifth (5.) and sixth (6.) floors. The contracting authority has previously published a prior information notice relating to the procurement (585563 / Jamk - Simulation system prior information request) and an invitation to tender (603116 / Jamk - Hippos Competence Centre simulation system). The tender procedure / procurement was discontinued on 9.6.2026 due to essential errors in the invitation to tender. The procurement has not been divided into lots because the different areas of the procurement form a functional and technical whole, the implementation of which among several suppliers would cause a significant risk regarding compatibility, division of responsibilities and schedule management. Splitting the procurement would substantially increase the need for coordination and could jeopardise the proper execution of the contract. In addition, the overall solution enables the procurement to be implemented in a technically manageable and cost-effective manner.
sig_e47d7bba309d0937d878.title: Jamk – Hippos Competence Centre simulation system
