The indicative scope of the works is as outlined below: • tie-in to existing DLR East Route, grade separated junction and viaduct, dropping down to grade level approaching Beckton Riverside station • new station at centre of Beckton Riverside development • cross river tunnel, twin bore tunnel circa 1.5 km • new station at Thamesmead • new turnback siding to the west of the extension to facilitate a future uplift in services on Thamesmead branch and east route. The contracting entity for this procurement is expected to be Docklands Light Railway Limited, which is a 100% owned subsidiary of Transport for London (TfL). TfL is in the process of defining the scope of requirements for the goods, services and construction works under the proposed TEX programme. The following outlines the indicative scope at this stage. Scope of services includes: • civil and building design; • mechanical, electrical, sanitary and security design; • ground investigations; and • design lead and co-ordination. Scope of construction works includes: • enabling works; • general building and civil engineering works; • mechanical, electrical, security and sanitary installations; • train traction power system; • telecommunication systems; • permanent ways and tracks; • station buildings; and • landscaping. Scope of goods includes: • associated mechanical, electrical/electronic equipment; and • associated construction materials. It is expected that the works may be phased and currently planned to commence 2028 and planned completion by 2033. Lot 1: .

sig_e4b50e33dabdd399444a.description: Espoon kaupunki (hereinafter also the Contracting Authority) invites tenders for an electronic maintenance logbook system. The subject of the procurement is an electronic maintenance logbook system as a SaaS software service, the deployment and customer-specific customisation of the service, application support and maintenance services, and further development and consulting services for the system subject to the procurement. Based on the competitive tendering, one (1) supplier and one (1) backup supplier will be selected. The functional entities of the system to be procured are: • Making and execution of service requests • Drawing up and maintenance of maintenance plans for maintenance targets and execution of maintenance measures • Maintenance logbook • Property data management • Energy management of maintenance targets • Self-monitoring • Long-term plans (LTP) for some of the maintenance targets • Reporting and statistical functionalities A more detailed description of the content of the procurement is in appendix 1 of the invitation to tender, "Description of the subject of the procurement". The estimated total value of the procurement for a calculated four years (VAT 0 %) is 2 500 000 euros. Note! For budgetary reasons, a maximum price has been set for ongoing costs (SaaS service fees, support and maintenance costs, and integration maintenance costs). The annual price of ongoing costs (appendix 6, Price form tab 1-Comparison price cell O60) must not exceed 200 000 euros / year. Exceeding the maximum price will likely lead to the rejection of the tender. PREPARATION OF THE PROCUREMENT The contracting authority has prepared the procurement by evaluating the alternatives and competitive conditions on the market as well as the methods for implementing the procurement. In the market survey, industry operators were widely consulted in writing and through market dialogue, and various implementation models were evaluated. The market survey was carried out in such a way that no individual supplier was favored and the survey was conducted impartially and transparently. The market survey notice was published in HILMA on 26.2.2026. 14 suppliers registered for the market dialogue. Those who registered were sent a preliminary task in March 2026 to survey the functionalities implemented in the systems on the market. Market dialogues were subsequently continued with four suppliers. In March-April 2026, discussion sessions were held with three suppliers, during which the suppliers demonstrated their systems. In addition, one supplier demonstrated its system via videos supplied separately. In May 2026, written further clarifications were requested from the suppliers, and in June 2026, the entire draft invitation to tender with its appendices was sent to them for comments, after which further clarifying clarifications were requested from those who commented. The survey found that there are several electronic maintenance logbook systems on the market. Based on the market survey, it could be stated that, in particular, the City of Espoo's need for an energy management entity as part of the maintenance logbook narrows the market. The observations obtained in the survey have been utilised in defining the subject of the procurement, setting suitability requirements, and defining the criteria for evaluating tenders. The preparation of the procurement has taken into account the principles concerning the market survey in accordance with Section 65 of the Public Procurement Act, and the contracting authority considers that the preparation supports the realisation of competition. DIVISION OF THE PROCUREMENT INTO LOTS The contracting authority has evaluated the division of the procurement into lots. The procurement has not been divided into lots because the system subject to the procurement and the service related to it form a cohesive entity that is not expedient to divide into smaller entities. In addition, division would significantly increase the risks related to integrations, division of responsibilities, deployment, and uniform data management. The contracting authority considers that not dividing the lot is justified considering the nature of the procurement, the implementation method, and expedient implementation.
sig_e4b50e33dabdd399444a.title: Procurement of an electronic maintenance logbook system

sig_e4c25f0fcd9af53b8053.description: LADAR Innovative Development and Research (LIDR) STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVE/NEEDS: The objective of this effort is to conduct innovative research and development (R&D) of electro-optical components and technology, furthering advanced warfighting capabilities and supporting the existing and emerging needs of the Air Force and DoD. It is expected that these will be accomplished through laboratory experimentation, component fabrication and analysis, system integration, modeling and simulation (M&S), field and flight testing, signal analysis, target fabrication, and evaluation. The primary goal of this effort is to develop advanced sensor technologies and techniques successfully operable in contested and denied environments meeting Air Force air superiority, global precision attack, rapid global mobility, special operations, and global integrated Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) service core function needs. LADAR Innovative Development and Research (LIDR) will continue to advance state-of-the-art active and associated passive electro-optical and infrared (EO/IR) technologies, seek synergies with active and passive radio frequency (RF) technologies, and define and test the integrability of these technologies in support of the Air Force and Department of Defense (DoD) warfighter. The primary focus of current Air Force needs is enhanced combat identification and high resolution wide area three-dimensional imaging (WATI). This research is organized across four primary technology areas: Synthetic Aperture Laser Radar (LADAR), Vibration Sensing, Direct Detection 3 Dimensional (3D) LADAR, and multiple modalities in a single LADAR sensor. Asynchronous Geiger Mode LADAR Receiver Development (A-GMLRD) STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVE/NEEDS: The objective of this effort is to develop asynchronous Geiger mode LiDAR receivers and Geiger mode laser communications (lasercom) receivers for military use, supporting AF research efforts. The Asynchronous Geiger Mode LADAR Receiver Development (A-GMLRD) project will develop a packaged light detection and ranging (LiDAR) receiver system for laser detection and ranging (LADAR) imaging systems and lasercom applications. The result will yield a photon sensitive receiver capable of providing high precision timing measurements to objects within the sensor field of view (FOV), supporting AF sensor development programs and lasercom programs.
sig_e4c25f0fcd9af53b8053.title: LADAR Innovative Development and Research (LIDAR)

sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.description: Dear Sir or Madam, Heidelberg University Hospital (UKHD) currently uses a self-developed ABAP-based add-on called BISI for electronic demand notification. As part of the SAP S/4 migration, this demand notification system is to be replaced by a long-term future-proof and modern solution. From a prospective perspective, the demand notification system is intended to support the entire Heidelberg-Mannheim hospital network with all subsidiaries and holdings. UKHD manages 2589 beds. With 87.441 inpatient patients and 1.275.241 outpatient treatment cases, it is the largest employer in the region. 14544 employees from 133 nations are employed at UKHD. The Faculty of Medicine trains 4.750 students. The Corporate Purchasing and Logistics Management division and the pharmacy supply the entire UKHD corporate group including subsidiaries and holdings and also supply external hospitals in the surrounding area. The newly procured tool for demand requests must be intuitive and easy for end users to operate and be based on the look and feel of modern, future-proof, efficient request platforms. This requires that end customers can record and request any demands during demand requests regardless of the product group, article group, purchasing organisation or financing type in the sense of a mixed shopping basket. The tool takes over the routing of requirements into the correct demand channels and controls the follow-on documents. The tool to be procured must be able to be connected to both SAP ECC and S/4 HANA. In this market exploration, UKHD therefore wishes to examine what options the relevant market currently offers for this contract subject, what empirical values can be contributed and what price range these services fall within.
sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.title: Market exploration regarding a demand notification tool for Heidelberg University Hospital

sig_e52407d9eebda11441be.description: Stichting 113 Zelfmoordpreventie intends to publish a European procurement for the selection of a full-service digital partner. This partner will be responsible for implementing, hosting, managing, maintaining, further developing and keeping up-to-date a flexible Content Management System (CMS), suitable for centrally managing multiple websites (multi-site). The assignment also includes the functional and visual design realisation (UX/UI) of the (main) websites. This design must be developed by the partner based on the central corporate identity and guidelines provided by an external marketing agency. In addition, it may happen that this same marketing agency provides ready-made designs for specific campaign sites; in that case, the partner to be selected is responsible exclusively for the technical implementation thereof within the existing OTAP structure (Development, Test, Acceptance and Production). Furthermore, the integration and further development of innovative AI applications within the platform will form part of the scope. In preparation for the procurement, Stichting 113 Zelfmoordpreventie has a number of questions for the market which it wishes to ask by means of this market consultation. The contracting authority strives for one central platform for developing, managing and hosting multiple websites, based on one central content management system (CMS). To guarantee maximum flexibility in the presentation layer, the platform must be set up based on a modern headless (API-driven) architecture. Within this platform, separate websites (subsites and campaign sites) must be able to be set up flexibly, independently and with a unique visual identity, while at the same time there is central control over architecture, data, management and further development. The solution supports the modular construction of websites based on a standardised set of reusable functional components (data and content models). Thanks to the headless architecture, the content layer is completely decoupled from the design layer, allowing campaign sites to have a completely different appearance and unique user experience, without affecting the central integrity of the CMS. The envisaged architecture facilitates a clear separation and cohesion between different components, where management, security, performance and further development are organised in a consistent, future-proof and manageable manner. sig_e54b00c84f083e26af3b.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_e5d09b83114e2643ea18.description: The subject of the public contract is the preparation of a comprehensive impact study for the Strategic Business Park (SPP) Lazy project, focused on evaluating its expected socio-economic, fiscal and broader development impacts on the affected territory and public budgets. The preparation of the study will be based on a scenario and parametric approach to evaluating strategic investments. The performance will also include the preparation of a zero variant (i.e. development of the territory without the implementation of the project) and at least three variant development scenarios for the project (realistic, optimistic and pessimistic scenarios). The study must contain clearly defined input parameters, assumptions of calculation models and transparent documentation of the data sources and methodological procedures used. The study will in particular include: • Quantification of direct, indirect and induced impacts of the project (especially in the areas of employment, value added creation and impacts on supply chains), • Evaluation of fiscal benefits and costs for public budgets (state, regions, municipalities), • Analysis of impacts on the regional economy and labour market, including structural changes and the absorption capacity of the territory, • Assessment of broader development effects, including influences on the business environment, innovation potential and the attractiveness of the territory for investors, • Scenario modelling of development (including variant investor parameters, project scope and time horizon), • Identification of risks and assumptions for project implementation and their influence on the resulting impacts, • Preparation of outputs in accordance with the current impact assessment methodology used by the contracting authority (SIRS), with an emphasis on transparency, replicability and data-based evidence. • Analysis of the project's impacts on housing, the housing stock and the residential market in the affected territory, • Analysis of impacts on civic amenities and public services, especially education, healthcare, social services and leisure infrastructure, • Definition and analysis of catchment areas, the absorption capacity of the territory and commuting relationships, • GIS and spatial analyses related to the location of the project, the availability of labour and links to the surrounding settlement structure, • Proposal of mitigating measures and recommendations for the public sector leading to the mitigation of identified negative impacts of the project, • Evaluation of model sensitivity and working with uncertainty through interval estimates and a scenario approach. The performance also includes: • Structured processing of data inputs and their documentation, • Presentation of results for the needs of the contracting authority and key stakeholders, • Ongoing consultation with the contracting authority during the preparation of the study.
sig_e5d09b83114e2643ea18.title: Impact study for the SPP Lazy project

sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.description: In the current model, the technical implementation of communal services is integrated into the IT organisation established by the State of Fribourg. In particular, SITel ensures contracting with technical service providers and the management of IT developments, in collaboration with the DIGI-FR team, which carries the business needs and ensures functional responsibility for communal services. With the coming to an end of the DIGI-FR program 2023–2026 and the evolution of the legal framework relating to e-government, this model is bound to evolve. From 2027, the municipalities, through the entity responsible for representing them, will take over responsibility for the development, operation and maintenance of their services on the Fribourg virtual counter. They will thus have the capacity to directly commission the necessary service providers and manage the end-to-end technical implementation of their services. This call for tenders aims to establish the capacities required for the development and maintenance of communal services in this new model. The public procurement aims to establish a contractual framework which will subsequently allow the ACF, according to its needs and on the basis of a predefined service catalogue, to award its contracts to referenced partners via single consultations (mini-tenders) in a simplified and competitive procedure.
sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.title: Framework contract for e-government DIGI-FR

sig_e5e80490344e15455288.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.
sig_e5e80490344e15455288.title: Competitive procedure with negotiation regarding a contract for the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for Kredsløb A/S

sig_e619085881b1bd1b028c.description: Maritime security is a key enabler to UK, Crown Dependency, and British Overseas Territories Security. Border Security Command (BSC) is seeking to procure a maritime situational awareness system that meets the requirements of the Joint Maritime Security Centre (JMSC) and the Border Security Command Maritime - Channel Operations team. The maritime environment is important both internationally and domestically, impacting the resilience of the UK and our global influence. It is a critical sector for prosperity and security. To deliver maritime security, the UK needs full persistent surveillance capability with the ability to detect non-cooperative-reporting vessels throughout the UK Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), including British Overseas Territories (BOT). Please note, two separate market engagement events have been held for this requirement previously. Please refer to the engagment section for links to the previous notices. A decision has been made to join the two requirements Land-Based ISR and Common Operating Picture and JMSC Mobile Maritime Domain Awareness Service into one single procurement (Coastal Maritime ISR Service). This procurement will strengthen the UK’s response to clandestine entry and wider maritime security by delivering a scalable, managed service that provides enhanced domain awareness and supports operational decision-making. The solution will autonomously detect, track, and identify small boats and non-cooperative vessels at range, fusing data from land-based and Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) sources with existing platforms. It will integrate AIS, radar, and EO/IR sensors to deliver Tracks as a Service (TKaaS) in near real-time via API to the Royal Navy Maritime Domain Awareness Programme (MDAP) and connect to the Home Office TAK server for a common operating picture accessible to key decision-makers and first responders. A supplier portal will provide camera feeds, alternative track displays, and alerts, ensuring flexibility to meet short-notice operational requirements across the UK, Crown Dependencies, and British Overseas Territories. Suppliers will be responsible for owning, siting, installing, securing, and operating any hardware in the UK or overseas to provide maritime tracks from selected areas to Border Security Command. The current operational tempo assumes a requirement for 24/7/365 service availability. Suppliers will need to ensure the system is supported with sufficient personnel and process to resolve any issues promptly. The Supplier solution must : Respond to asking and provide persistent maritime surveillance of an Area of Interest (AOI) within the UK marine area (and UK Overseas/Dependent Territories). Provide active surveillance feeds across multiple concurrent AOIs around the UK coast delivering tracks as a service. Provide services that will enable/assist in the detection of both cooperative and non‐cooperative‐reporting vessels typically within UK Territorial Waters (TTWs). The solution primarily covers the UK, territorial waters, and BOTs when required. This solution will need to respond to any emerging areas of interest both in the UK and BOT. Additionally, the service is to provide autonomous domain awareness in a designated high‐priority maritime corridor within UK waters, as directed, to Border Security Command. The solution must achieve full operational capability within six months of contract award. An interim capability may be acceptable, provided it delivers a minimum viable product agreed with the Home Office, with additional functionality introduced incrementally. The system will utilise a network of existing and additional sensors to autonomously detect, track, classify, and identify small boats at range. Sensor data must be fused with information from existing platforms and presented to end‐users via a web interface and integrated with the Home Office TAK server to provide a common operating picture. Fusion nodes should enable near real‐time decision‐making, creating a cohesive and interoperable system that enhances situational awareness and operational flexibility. The expected duration of this contract is between three and five years, including any extension periods, with an estimated total value of up to approximately £100 million for the full five‐year term. The value of the contract includes flexibility to allow for any known areas of interest during the contract term that wasn't known at the start of the contract. Lot 1: .

sig_e626575762f0c95a0498.description: Background This preliminary market engagement exercise is being conducted by DfT Operator Limited (DFTO) on the basis described in this notice and in the accompanying documents. The Fares, Ticketing and Retail (FTR) Programme brings together teams from across the rail industry to transform how passengers purchase and use tickets. By modernising outdated fares, enhancing the passenger experience and unlocking retail innovation, the FTR Programme will improve passenger journeys, drive commercial growth and achieve greater cost efficiency across the rail network. We intend to make retail, easy, reliable and smart for passengers using modern technology to bring excellence to the experience. The retail experience will be built on a tech stack containing future-facing technology allowing us to take advantage of retail technical advances as these appear. Through bringing together cross-sector expertise, the FTR Programme is delivering impactful changes for passengers now, ahead of the transition to Great British Railways (GBR). These modernisations will help bring decades of fragmentation and inefficiency to an end through a simpler, more unified railway owned by the public, for the public under GBR. The FTR Programme is actively steering a series of transformational, cross-industry initiatives re-shaping fares, ticketing and retail. They include trials of easier to understand fares, introduction of tap-in, tap-out payments, and the introduction of smart ticketing. The Government released the Railways Bill on 5 November, sharing its policy position on GBR Online Retail in the related information and consultation-see Railways Bill: tickets and retail - GOV.UK. The FTR Programme is a collaboration between the Department for Transport (DfT), DFTO, Rail Delivery Group, Devolved and Regional Transport Bodies, and train operators. It is governed by DfT. The FTR Programme regularly engages with other industry stakeholders and delivery partners including ticketing retailers and campaign groups. Project Description The GBR Online Retail project will deliver the passenger-facing channel for GBR, GBR Online (website and app), at launch. The aim is to provide a high-quality national retail and journey information service, aligned with broader GBR branding and transition. This preliminary market engagement exercise will set out the current direction and seek supplier insight ahead of procurement. We will create a unified GBR Online digital experience that: • Simplifies customer experience and opportunity to increase revenue as a result • Realises cost efficiencies from reduction in duplication of websites and apps across DfT operator brands and nationalrail.co.uk • Enables improved service information authority and aligned post journey support • Supports wider FTR initiatives (e.g., fares reform, delay repay, railcards). GBR Online Retail will operate within a fair and open retail market, designed to foster real improvements for passengers and taxpayers, including innovation in customer service, wider ticketing availability and diverse options to support digital journeys. Emerging Scope It is currently envisaged that there would be two phases of work under the GBR Online Retail project: Phase 1 launch scope (non-exhaustive) • Ticket retailing and associated services (purchase, fulfilment across paper/Barcode/ITSO, seat & cycle reservations, Passenger Assist). • Journey planning with clear pricing, comparison and best fare guidance. • Live service information including disruption and future travel advice. • Post-sale customer support (changes, refunds, Delay Repay). Phase Two : TOC integration - over up to 12-months post-launch to integrate capabilities, across all Department for Transport (DfT) publicly owned operators. Beyond the Phase 1, GBR may expect the solution to be continually developed and enhanced based on a roadmap that is agreed with GBR and regularly updated based on customer and market needs. It is anticipated that this may see the phase-out of some services delivered in place of new capabilities. A significant outcome to GBR of any procurement would be the delivery of an end-to-end accredited online national rail ticket retailing solution, associated payment gateway service and CRM platform, which provides flexibility with regards to future scope and access to APIs for ongoing development opportunities. Project Objectives GBR Online Retail will serve as the direct digital sales channel for GBR, supporting the FTR Programme's objectives by delivering a streamlined, accessible, and inclusive ticketing experience. Passengers will benefit from clear fare choices, simplified ticketing across digital and physical formats, and personalized journey information. The platform is designed to integrate railcards, concessions, and support services, ensuring inclusivity from launch. GBR's ticketing website will combine the existing 14 rail operator websites and apps into one - with the previous websites ceasing to function. The solution will integrate with industry initiatives such as Fares Reform and Delay Repay, accelerate new product development, and support innovative customer propositions. Key outcomes include a trusted one-stop shop for tickets, best price guarantees, seamless support, and a unified customer experience. For the rail industry, benefits include lower operational costs, increased brand impact, and a platform that drives innovation and competitiveness. The approach emphasises continuous improvement, data-driven customer insights, and rapid response to market opportunities. Hooks will be built in to enable the use of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. Lot 1: .

sig_e65b3b1c01dca77388d9.description: Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Lot 1: . Our vision is to create a fully branded, inclusive, and functional workwear and PPE solution that unites every colleague across our organisation reflecting who we are, what we stand for, and the pride we take in serving our communities. We will deliver a modern, high‐quality uniform range designed from the ground up to support the unique needs of our operational, maritime, port, and shore‐based teams. Rooted in the heritage of Caledonian MacBrayne and our communities, our workwear will combine safety, comfort, durability, and unmistakable brand identity in every garment. Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Through clear uniform standards, easy maintenance guidance, and from warehouse to home/work distribution processes, we will set and uphold a new standard for how our brand is worn and represented. Powered by digital self-service ordering tools, our workwear transformation will enhance operational efficiency, improve stock management, and allow us to scale sustainably. Cross-functional collaboration at the early stages will ensure that every voice is heard and every role is understood, creating a sense of ownership, pride, and confidence in the final solution. By learning from industry-leading transformations and working with expert partners, we will introduce a workwear range that not only serves practical needs but also strengthens culture, improves staff experience, and supports our organisation’s evolution. This is more than new uniform, it's an opportunity to reinforce our brand, celebrate our heritage, empower our people, and deliver a workwear experience that is fit for the future.

sig_e67b305c52bf05e2e7e6.description: Supply of a High Performance Computing (HPC) infrastructure including integration with the existing HPC environment. The Leibniz computing cluster (2017) is being decommissioned. In addition, there is also the Vaughan computing cluster (2020-2021), consisting of 192 CPU nodes (zen2 and zen3 architecture) and three GPU computing nodes (one node with four NVIDIA A100 and two computing nodes with two AMD MI100). The high-performance interconnect is Infiniband HDR100. Vaughan has a scratch file system based on BeeGFS and a NetApp solution for the other file systems (home directories, application software and permanent data). The home directories and permanent data are also exported via NFS to the other VSC sites (Flemish Supercomputer Centre, www.vscentrum.be). Three chillers have been installed for cooling the machines. In-row coolers are used. This contract consists of the replacement of the Leibniz cluster. Since Leibniz is part of a hot aisle concept, this may have to be partially dismantled. The new cluster will consist of computing nodes connected by a high-speed interconnect, associated login nodes and management nodes, storage system, and possibly some nodes for experimenting with visualisation and/or accelerators. The supply includes the installation of the machine (“turnkey” solution), including cooling compatible with the current chillers. The tenderer possesses the necessary expertise not only to supply and install the hardware, but also to provide the necessary support during the machine's service life, e.g. for updates and configuration changes or other problems with the system software and hardware, and is also able to integrate future expansions purchased within the framework of this agreement into the solution. “Computing cluster” or “HPC infrastructure” refers to a computing infrastructure with very high computing power provided by a large number of computing nodes connected via a high-performance network that allows the use of applications that deploy the computing power of many computing nodes to perform a single simulation or solve other large problems. Individual sub-tasks on the computing nodes can communicate with high bandwidth and low latency over the network via, for example, MPI. Furthermore, there are multiple shared file systems (each with its own profile: home directories, applications, permanent data or scratch) that are available on all computing nodes and on the infrastructure for access and management of the whole. This tender will lead to a non-exclusive framework agreement within which further expansions of the infrastructure can be purchased during the three-year period, which may be extended by one year, including a replacement of the current BeeGFS and NetApp solution. However, further purchase is not guaranteed and depends on the evolution of the funding for this project.
sig_e67b305c52bf05e2e7e6.title: Framework agreement for the supply of HPC infrastructure

sig_e68ba558657f1e4f0aa4.description: The contracting authority is Suomen kansallisooppera ja -baletti sr (hereinafter also "SKOB"). The subject of the procurement is procurement tendering services as a single-supplier framework arrangement. The purpose of SKOB is to procure procurement consultancy services to support its own procurement operations. SKOB procures goods and services and combinations thereof as a public procurement, but concession contracts may also be procured, for example. Procurement procedures are decided based on the needs of each procurement; the most typical procedures are open and restricted procedures, but all procedures are possible. The range of procurements is broad, and each tender competition must be analysed and the best procedure and working method selected for it. Procurements to be tendered are carried out on a varying basis, estimated at approximately 10-15 per year. SKOB organises some of the tender competitions itself as in-house work, and the portion for which its own resources are insufficient or where special expertise is required is procured from the selected service provider. The contracting authority may also need consultancy in assessing the grounds for direct procurement. Based on its purchase history, SKOB procures public procurement consultancy and tendering services for an estimated amount of 60 000 euros per year. The amount may vary in different years. The tendering process may require a certain degree of familiarisation with the required products and services and/or a market survey. Smooth cooperation with SKOB's subject-matter experts is also key. Technology-related procurements may include IT equipment, systems and services, which is why ICT procurement expertise is important. Procurements may also have to be conducted in English. The subject of the procurement is the planning of public tender competitions, drafting of procurement documents and execution in accordance with the Procurement Act (1397/2016) from the preparation stage to the signing of contracts. In addition, the contracting authority may procure investigation, development and advisory services related to the Procurement Act and public procurement operations as needed. The procurement includes an optional extra for handling litigation related to the procurements. The tenderer is not obliged to tender for the optional extra.

The government is seeking industry feedback to inform the MEO E3&4 acquisition strategy and technical approach. The MEO MWT architecture is being incrementally developed in capability-based deliveries called Epochs. Each Epoch is expected to include at least one competitive award and allows for insertion of new technology and innovative solutions in response to progressive or updated warfighter requirements to ultimately meet Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR) capability needs. This RFI requests industry feedback and approaches to support delivering a MEO MWT E3&4 capability. Feedback on this approach is welcome. Small Business Consideration The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 - Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The small business size standard is 1,000 employees. Participation from small and small disadvantaged businesses is encouraged. SSC's Small Business points of contact can be reached at smallbus@spaceforce.mil or by phone at (310) 653-1108. sig_e70d429007afe6c2430a.description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. sig_e738a342e42ee6209d9c.description: Arrochar, a Scottish beauty spot at Loch Long, was designated a ‘litter sink’ by the Scottish Government in 2017. The problem of litter gathering at the head of the Loch has been getting worse over decades and has reached a point where it creates a damaging effect on the area, its environment, wildlife, visitors, and on the Local Community. Arrochar is perhaps the most publicised but far from the only ‘Litter Sink’ in Scotland. Manual mechanical methods are challenging and costly, and so this Challenge seeks to develop new, sustainable ways of tackling a national issue, starting with Arrochar. Lot 1: . About CivTech CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-6-reducing-teaching-workload

sig_e73ad6b2a29669a5ef2f.description: Background Troms County shall upgrade the navigation simulators at Nord-Troms sixth form college, skjervøy school and Senja sixth form college, Department Gibostad. The procurement will be carried out to ensure modern, stable and future orientated simulator systems that support maritime training in accordance with the current requirements and needs of teaching. The current simulator park consists of equipment from different generations, with parts of the system being from 2014-2015. This leads to challenges connected to compatibility, operation, maintenance and support. The county therefore needs a more comprehensive system with more favourable functionality, simple administration and better interaction between the systems at the two school places. The simulators shall be used in training within navigation, vessel manoeuvring, radio communication, interaction and situation comprehension. The system shall support both the continuation of existing courses and the development of new training offers, and it shall be able to be used in teaching several certificate courses as well as by external users. It is therefore important that the system provides realistic training possibilities, high educational value and good user friendliness for both pupils, teachers and instructors. Description of the assignment The contract is for the delivery, installation and commissioning of complete navigation simulators for both school places. The delivery shall include simulator stations for pupils and instructors, the necessary hardware and software, the accompanying licences, cabling, integration with relevant existing equipment and adapted furnishing. The delivery shall be complete and ready for use when taking over. The system shall facilitate realistic training in navigation, manoeuvring, GMDSS communication, interaction between vessels and exercises across disciplines. The simulators shall be able to be controlled together from the instructor station, support joint scenarios and give good possibilities for real time management, recording, documentation and evaluation of exercises. Flexibility is also wanted for future expansions and integrations, including an option for a fishing module. The assignment includes further training in use and operation, documentation, proposals for a room system and any infrastructure requirements, as well as a service and maintenance agreement with support and access to spare parts. The system shall contribute to safe and efficient operation over time, with emphasis on user friendliness, central administration, upgradability and interaction between the simulator installations at the two schools.
sig_e73ad6b2a29669a5ef2f.title: Navigation simulators for Nord-Troms and Senja sixth form colleges

sig_e77669d70c46e3406882.description: This framework agreement for the integration of ICT solutions and systems is characterised by the following activity groups: 1. Carrying out an audit that includes a critical analysis of existing ICT hardware platforms. 2. The study and (requirements) analysis for the implementation of new ICT hardware platforms or major modifications to existing ICT hardware platforms. 3. Designing the architecture to realise a development project (roadmap) in order to meet the desired ICT requirements via an integrated solution. 4. The supply, installation, maintenance and/or management (including contract management) of a full range of sector-related ICT hardware, associated operating software and standard administrative applications, tailored to specific needs and taking into account technological developments in general (e.g. solution for operating theatre, ...). 5. Building solutions up to and including the testing and implementation of new ICT hardware platforms or adjustments to existing ICT hardware platforms according to recognised methodologies (e.g. unified communication solutions, ...). 6. Providing maintenance and support as well as keeping ICT costs manageable through optimal management of already existing ICT hardware platforms and taking into account the specific business plan. 7. Fulfilling the role of a Managed Service Provider in the field of workplace support, incl. helpdesk. 8. Offering Managed Services in the field of (existing and future) ICT hardware (e.g. servers, data rooms, ...).
sig_e77669d70c46e3406882.title: Framework agreement for the integration of ICT solutions and systems

sig_e778d4c4281ef3fef99c.description: The National Library of Medicine (NLM) seeks applications for research projects that drive groundbreaking innovation and advanced development in the fields of bioinformatics, translational bioinformatics, and computational biology. The primary goal of this initiative is to support the creation and implementation of cutting-edge methods, tools, and approaches that can transform the landscape of biomedical data science. This NOFO aims to address the growing need to leverage transformative technologies — such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and large-scale computational platforms — to extract actionable knowledge from vast, diverse, and complex biological datasets. By enabling more effective interpretation and integration of multi-dimensional biological and biomedical data, this research will ultimately contribute to improving individual and population health outcomes.

Support for the operation of JKA (1-2-3-4-5-6-7-TVM) type ticket vending machines at level L3, and warranty repairs for JKA 4-5-6-7. The successful Tenderer's task, depending on the number of JKAs covered by the contract to be concluded as a result of the public procurement procedure, is to operate them as follows: 1. performance of operational service tasks, the consideration for which is the monthly operational fee offered in the public procurement procedure (HUF/JKA in operation/month), and, 2. other service tasks, which are ordered based on individual orders according to the Contracting Authority's requirements. Further information can be found in the technical description which is part of the public procurement documentation and published simultaneously with it! Documents to be attached at the time of contract conclusion: - The successful tenderer must possess, no later than the time of contract conclusion and during performance, a valid certificate for the repair and servicing of machines according to ISO 9001, ISO 45001, ISO 14001 standards or an equivalent, issued by an organisation registered in any Member State of the European Union. - The successful Tenderer must have general and service liability insurance to cover damages related to or arising from its activities, the amount of which is at least 100 million HUF/year and at least 50 million HUF/claim. The successful Tenderer is obliged to maintain the liability insurance for the entire duration of the contract. The insurance must be concluded or extended no later than the time of contract conclusion. - The successful Tenderer is required to submit manufacturer declarations at the time of contract conclusion: - With a manufacturer's declaration of spare parts supply issued to the Tenderer regarding the current main sub-assemblies required for operation (banknote handler; coin handler; printer; POS terminal, cabinet controller) and this procurement procedure, in which the device manufacturer (or its representative) declares that, in the event of the Tenderer being successful, it will ensure the Tenderer's continuous spare parts supply for the devices for at least the duration of the contract, as well as support required for hardware and software troubleshooting, and development and integration services. - The successful Tenderer is obliged to submit the following documents at the time of contract conclusion: a support declaration issued by the device manufacturer (or its official representative), in which the manufacturer (or its representative) undertakes to support the Tenderer in performing (or commencing) the maintenance, troubleshooting and other operational tasks required for operation, and to provide the necessary information, documentation, software and hardware support. If the given device(s) are within the 48-month manufacturer's warranty period, the Tenderer must submit the prior written authorisation of the manufacturer (or the previous supplier who provided the manufacturer's warranty) for this period, based on which the Tenderer may perform the operational tasks and the manufacturer's support extends to these devices as well, and which authorisation explicitly states that the maintenance, troubleshooting or other operational activities performed by the Tenderer – in possession of the manufacturer's declaration – do not constitute a breach of the warranty conditions and do not result in loss of warranty. The Tenderer must possess a manufacturer (or official representative) support declaration issued to the Tenderer regarding the current main software components and modules required for the operation of the back-office system software connected to the TVM machine, in which the software manufacturer (or its representative) declares that, in the event of the Tenderer being successful, it will ensure continuous support for the software for at least the duration of the contract. The Tenderer must further possess a manufacturer's declaration of spare parts supply issued to the Tenderer regarding the current main sub-assemblies required for operation (banknote handler; coin handler; printer; POS terminal, cabinet controller) and this procurement procedure, in which the device manufacturer (or its representative) declares that, in the event of the Tenderer being successful, it will ensure the Tenderer's continuous spare parts supply for the devices for at least the duration of the contract, as well as support required for hardware and software troubleshooting, and development and integration services. The Contracting Authority does not require a support declaration from the manufacturer of those machines whose manufacturer has ceased to exist without a legal successor and whose manufacturer support activity has been permanently closed. - We draw the attention of the esteemed Economic Operators to the fact that if the documents listed above are not available at the time of signing the contract, this shall mean withdrawal from the contract conclusion based on Section 131 (4) of the Public Procurement Act (Kbt.), and in this case, the contracting authority shall conclude a contract with the second most favourable tenderer. - Furthermore, we draw the attention of the esteemed Economic Operators to the fact that it is necessary to submit a declaration in the tender regarding the availability of the documents listed above at the time of contract conclusion. The Tenderer is required to submit the following documents in its tender: - Declaration of authorisation for instrumental testing, - Declaration of knowledge of the MSZ HD 60364 standard. Any specific make, origin, or type mentioned in the call for tenders and the public procurement documents was included solely for the purpose of clearly defining the nature of the subject matter. According to Section 46 (3)-(4) of Government Decree 321/2015. (X. 30.), the expression "or equivalent" must be added in every case alongside the designation. Regarding the verification of compliance, the Contracting Authority further draws attention to the provisions of Section 46 (4) of Government Decree 321/2015. (X. 30.).

sig_e7840b0ad4e7e51c3d9e.description: The subject of the framework agreement is the recording, collection and transmission of data representing water consumption in relation to a maximum number of 8.800 monitoring points, using as devices meters pre-equipped with radio transmission modules and a LoRaWAN communications network, and the reading and processing of the collected data. The duration of the framework agreement is 84 months, starting from the date of signing the framework agreement. Number of days by which clarifications may be requested before the deadline for submission of tenders: The time limit by which economic operators have the right to request clarifications or additional information in connection with the award documentation is: 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting entity will respond to all requests for clarification up to the 11-th day before the time limit set in the contract notice for the submission of tenders. The contracting entity will respond only to requests for clarification addressed by economic operators up to the established time limit, respectively 15 days before the deadline for submitting tenders. The estimated value of the framework agreement is 1.352.824,00 EURO, excluding VAT. The service entails ensuring the following elements: a) Consumption measurement service: To ensure the water consumption measurement service and data transmission, meters pre-equipped with radio modules and a LoraWAN communications network, suitable for daily reading of the consumption index, shall be used. Although the LoRaWAN network is an integral part of the data reading service, the making available of the network to the beneficiary shall be carried out in accordance with the schedule for the performance of the water consumption measurement service, given that the meters are dependent on the LoRaWAN network for transmitting data to the data reading service and, implicitly, to the meter data management application. The water consumption measurement and data transmission service shall be ensured in the peri-urban areas of the Municipality of Timișoara (respectively: UAT Moșnița, UAT Ghiroda). This service shall be implemented progressively over the course of 36 months, in the sense that quarterly, through the conclusion of subsequent contracts, the service shall be commenced in accordance with the implementation schedule presented at point 5 and shall be carried out for 36 months for each implemented monitoring point. The corresponding communications network shall be available and functional in normal parameters before the start of the installation of meters pre-equipped with radio modules, intended for each monitoring point, which meters shall be made available by the service provider. The meters shall be pre-equipped with radio modules using the LoRaWAN protocol, mounted and pre-programmed with meter data (index, serial number, etc.). The service provider having the obligation to implement the components that make up the system "WATER METER READING EQUIPMENT VIA RADIO SYSTEM", so that these components function as a unitary system and meet the formulated requirements. The moment of effective commencement of this service in relation to each monitoring point shall be represented by the date of conclusion of a report signed by both parties by which the implementation of the service in relation to the respective point shall be established, after the mounting, commissioning and testing of the devices. b) Data reading service: The service of reading, collecting, collating and supplying data is composed of the LoRaWAN network and the meter data management application. The data reading service shall also be commenced progressively, as it will be commenced concurrently with the water consumption measurement service, for each monitoring point. This reading service shall not be provided for a time duration limited to the 36 months during which the water consumption measurement and data transmission service is provided. It shall be ensured for each monitoring point for the entire period of time comprised between: - the moment of its commencement, which is concurrent with the moment of commencement of the water consumption measurement and data transmission service; - and the moment of finalisation of the provision of the water consumption measurement and data transmission service, for the last monitoring point implemented during the performance of the framework agreement. Therefore, the commencement of this service for each monitoring point is influenced by the moment of implementation of these points for the purpose of providing the water consumption measurement and data transmission service, but its performance for the implemented points shall extend over the entire period of time necessary for the implementation of all monitoring points that form the object of the framework agreement and the performance of the water consumption measurement and data transmission service in relation to all these points. Reception of this service shall be carried out by confirming the reading of the indices. Estimated value of the framework agreement 1.352.824,00 Euro excluding VAT. Estimated value of the smallest subsequent contract: 2.200 Euro excluding VAT. Estimated value of the largest subsequent contract: 83.952 Euro excluding VAT.
sig_e7840b0ad4e7e51c3d9e.title: Radio transmission and reception services for water meter indices using the LoRaWAN communication protocol

sig_e78b219c20680f6680a1.description: By this notice, an annulment is announced of Trafikselskabet Movia's procurement of a contract for the supply of services and related ancillary services for a new EDRM solution in Movia. The services and related ancillary services to be supplied are governed in more detail by the contract with appendices and include, inter alia, the supply, implementation, operation and maintenance of a new EDRM solution based on a Software as a Service (SaaS). The EDRM solution must meet a number of general and functional requirements as well as customised functionality to support Movia's customer enquiries and web forms (hereinafter referred to as "the Solution"), cf. Appendix 2 (Requirement Specification). Movia wishes the Solution to be based on standard functionality (cloud) to the greatest possible extent and for maintenance to be as simple as possible. These are services that specifically place stringent requirements on the supplier with regard to data integrity, confidentiality and availability. It is thus expected that the supplier shall at all times test and warrant the integrity and completeness of the data processed in the Solution. Movia wishes to create independence from suppliers and products in order to optimise the utilisation of its resources both financially and commercially. As part of the performance of the contract, the supplier must therefore actively and independently contribute to the realisation of this objective, including ensuring Movia's ability to re-tender and transfer the tasks continuously undertaken by the supplier after the Solution has been delivered, including maintenance.
sig_e78b219c20680f6680a1.title: Cancellation of ESDH procurement

sig_e7936b95f4b5b19647e0.description: As part of its open-source strategy, the State of Schleswig-Holstein has commissioned Dataport to convert the end devices of state authorities to a Linux-based operating system. Dataport (contracting authority of this procurement procedure) operates an end-device management platform for this purpose, administers physical and virtual clients with hardware architecture x86-64 (amd64) and supports users. The volume of clients is growing from a scheduled 750 clients as of 31.12.2026 to up to 19.000 clients as of 31.12.2029. The contracting authority is purposely designing the tender to be open with regard to distribution; a specific Linux distribution for which the services are to be provided is therefore not specified. Since the Linux distribution will be part of the product currently being developed by the contracting authority, "+1.Linux Workplace", the services to be provided for the Linux distribution must be rendered for a Linux distribution that fulfils the requirements described in the "Distribution Requirements Catalogue" annex. If services are offered for multiple distributions, the contracting authority reserves the right to choose one of these distributions. The subject of the procedure is the award of a framework agreement for services relating to support, further development and consulting in the area of the +1.Linux Workplace Distribution to a contractor. Individual parts of the service (hotline, support) are to be provided continuously by the contractor during the term of the contract. The remaining services will be called off by the contracting authority as required. The contractual basis for the various services is the EVB-IT service terms and conditions. The minimum contract term of the framework agreement is two years. It can be extended by the contracting authority twice by one year each to a maximum term of four years. For details, reference is made to the procurement documents and in particular the EVB-IT service contract with its annexes.
sig_e7936b95f4b5b19647e0.title: FW 3rd-Level Support, further development and consulting +1.Linux Workplace Distribution

The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Joint Cyber Command and Control (JCC2) (AFLCMC/HNCK), Joint Base San Antonio, Lackland AFB, TX. The Government has participated in several engagements with industry on these programs through Request for Information and conferences. Tasks may include but are not limited to new software development, sustainment, cradle to grave engineering analysis, software modification, maintenance, and enhancement, along with maturing of existing architecture and infrastructure. Expected Acquisition Method: Competitive Acquisition using GSA Alliant 2 Estimated Solicitation Release: Jan-Feb 2025 Enterprise Service Center Summary of Requirement: Provide Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud system administration and help desk support for all HNCJ cloud hosting environments and associated applications. Furthermore, the ESC will provide support to HNCJ applications with evolving and transitioning of existing applications into new technology directions as well as assist efforts to satisfy associated cyber security requirements. This services contract will provide capabilities to the operational community in support of deploying and maintaining daily updates to production, staging, testing, exercise, and training instances as directed by the PMO. The effort will additionally assist with Cybersecurity Risk Management Framework (RMF) technical tasks and Cyber Security Service Provider (CSSP) requirements. Tasks may include but are not limited to new software development, sustainment, cradle to grave engineering analysis, software modification, maintenance, and enhancement, maturing of existing architecture and infrastructure. Along with providing support for interoperability with other systems, system integration services, various operational deployment, and model of current application and interdependencies. Acquisition Method: Awarded through Cyber ANTX Commercial Solutions Opening Awarded: 11 Dec 2024 Any questions related to these acquisitions need to be directed to the Contracting Officer, Kevin Grant at kevin.grant.10@us.af.mil.

sig_e7d5d6310a2da1c26cbb.description: GENERAL This document is not a procurement announcement, not an Call for tenders, nor will its publication start a Tender Procurement Process. The purpose of this Pre-market consultation notice is to identify potential suppliers operating in the market and their offerings. Responding or not responding to this Pre-market consultation notice does not prevent participation in a possible future tender. This Pre-market consultation notice does not obligate the contracting authority to carry out an actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this Pre-market consultation notice is preliminary and indicative. Laurea University of Applied Sciences operates in five locations in the Uusimaa region in Finland. Laurea offers both bachelor’s and master’s degree studies but also open university studies, specialisation education and continuing education. The fields of study are Business Management, Information technology, Service business, Social Services, Nursing, Health Care and Hospitality Management. Laurea has approximately 9,900-degree students and approximately 13,000 Open UAS students per year as well as about 670 employees. The system must integrate with Laurea's learning platform (Canvas) and provide video and audio-based proctoring recorded and stored by the system. The procurement does not include a personal live monitoring service by the supplier or the use of artificial intelligence to monitor/check and identify suspected fraud. The procurement includes the deployment of the software service and support and maintenance services separately for each higher education institution. Any potential market dialogue will be conducted in English, and all related materials will be provided only in English. No compensation will be paid for participation in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy will act in a consultative role in the procurement process. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Potential service providers interested in participating in the dialogue are kindly asked to register via email as soon as possible and at the latest by 6 February 2026. Use a reference "TD for an Online exam proctoring system" and the company name as the subject of the email. The service providers may register in Finnish or English.

sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that builds upon its investment in data-driven approaches for the purpose of defining molecular mechanisms of resilience in the presence of various types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) risk. The goal of this NOFO is to build a robust program that integrates epidemiologic, genomic, and mechanistic research through the use of data driven, systems-based approaches (including the use of artificial intelligence and/or machine learning methods) to discover the molecular/cellular determinants of resilience to AD/ADRD risk across representative populations. The initiative will support the generation of high-dimensional molecular data from brain and peripheral tissues, including longitudinal data, to enable dynamic modeling of resilience mechanisms and to discover molecular predictors of resilience. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO intends to utilize the U01 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.
