sig_e7ece7826066941a8bf4.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT VR-Group Plc (“VR” or the “Contracting Entity”) is procuring a modern, SaaS-based HR solution to replace its current HRM systems in Finland and Sweden. The solution must provide a secure, reliable, and scalable platform for more than 10 000 employees globally, support country-specific requirements, and enable expansion into additional countries if needed, without major customization. VR is seeking a robust, scalable, and future-ready HR solution delivered as a single, integrated product. The solution will serve as VR’s central employment management platform and provide a reliable, secure, and consistent source of personnel and employment information throughout the employee lifecycle. The solution must enable VR to standardize and streamline core HR processes, reduce fragmented systems and manual work, improve data quality, and support efficient collaboration between HR, payroll, managers, employees, and other relevant stakeholders. The scope of this procurement is limited to the acquisition of the technology, including the HR SaaS solution and the necessary user licences. The implementation of the solution and the related support and maintenance services will be subject to a separate procurement procedure to be conducted after the technology provider has been selected. Thus, the selected HR technology must have a strong partner ecosystem in Finland and Sweden to enable competitive procurement. The new SaaS-based HR solution must include secure, enterprise-grade AI capabilities with appropriate governance and human oversight. The provider must also demonstrate continuous and substantial annual investment in product development. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE VR is conducting a market dialogue to obtain specific, substantiated, and commercially relevant input on the planned procurement scope, requirements and delivery model. VR also seeks verifiable evidence of the solution’s impact on employee experience and customer satisfaction, supported by clearly defined metrics, comparable customer results, and independent research or third-party assessments. Participants must provide concrete, evidence-based responses and clearly distinguish between: - Standard, generally available product capabilities - Configurable functionality - AI capabilities currently in production - AI capabilities planned on the committed product roadmap - Partner-delivered services - Functionality requiring customization The purpose is to ensure that the procurement reflects proven market capabilities, supports VR’s strategic objectives, and enables genuine and effective competition. VR may use the results to refine the procurement scope, mandatory requirements, evaluation criteria, contractual framework, and subsequent tendering process. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE - Market dialogue in September-October 2026 - Publication of the invitation to tender in November-December 2026 - Evaluation of the tenders and contract award in December 2026 - February 2027 - Contract period starts in November 2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a request for information. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The request for information includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Discussion are held mainly as a written market dialogue rounds. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize also joint market dialogue sessions and individual meetings with interested suppliers. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest via the link:https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ZSEbHcb4b6 no later than 30th of September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Non-participation in the market dialogue does not prohibit supplier to submit a tender in the subsequent tendering procedure. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, schedule and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.

sig_e806f5c831977d15dfb4.description: West Lothian Council has awarded a contract to Softcat plc for the provision, implementation and support of the ALVAO IT Service Management (ITSM) and IT Asset Management (ITAM) solution. The solution will replace the Council's existing unsupported IT service desk and ticketing system and provide modern service management, asset management, self-service, workflow automation, reporting, project management and integration capabilities. The contract includes software licences, implementation services, configuration, data migration, training and ongoing support and maintenance. Lot 1: . West Lothian Council has awarded a contract to Softcat plc for the provision, implementation and ongoing support of the ALVAO IT Service Management (ITSM) and IT Asset Management (ITAM) solution. The Council's existing IT service desk and ticketing system has reached end of vendor support and no longer receives security updates, patches or product enhancements. A replacement solution is required to provide a fully supported, secure and modern platform that aligns with the Council's IT service management requirements and digital strategy. The scope of the contract includes software licences, implementation, configuration, data migration, integration with corporate systems, service desk and ticket management functionality, asset management capabilities, self-service functionality, workflow automation, knowledge management, reporting and dashboard capabilities, training, support and maintenance. The solution will support key processes including incident management, service request fulfilment, problem management, change management, asset lifecycle management, project and work management, workflow orchestration, approval processes, time recording and performance reporting.. Following market engagement and evaluation of functional, technical and commercial requirements, the ALVAO ITSM and ITAM solution was identified as the preferred option. A direct award to Softcat under the HealthTrust Europe ICT Solutions 3 Framework represented the most economically advantageous framework route and met the Council's operational and technical requirements.
sig_e806f5c831977d15dfb4.title: IT Desk, Asset Management and Ticketing System

sig_e809128f7b9e58c68678.description: The University of Cologne is a higher education institution founded in 1919 in Cologne with the range of subjects of a comprehensive university and, with over 43.000 students, is one of the largest campus universities by student numbers in Germany. In the course of carrying out its research activities, the contracting authority as a public contracting authority is regularly dependent on the procurement of so-called C-materials (low-value materials with a high procurement volume), in particular medical laboratory materials, other laboratory consumables, office materials, IT consumables, tools, cleaning materials and consumables for building services engineering. To facilitate the procurement of its requirements for these C-materials, the contracting authority has decided to conclude an agreement with an online platform operator for an e-marketplace solution for such materials. A contract duration of three years is envisaged here. For this e-platform solution, certain technical requirements have been defined that the contracting authority considers to be strictly necessary and that online platforms for an e-marketplace solution must fulfil in order to be suitable for the contract purpose intended by the contracting authority: Firstly, an e-marketplace must be able to offer the product range required by the UzK for medical laboratory supplies, other laboratory consumables, office materials, IT consumables, tools, cleaning materials and consumables for building services engineering. In addition, an e-marketplace solution must fulfil the following technical requirements: - Compatibility with the contracting authority's IT infrastructure as well as an interface to the "easyBanf" catalogue management system of the company GISA GmbH, which is currently being introduced for the state's higher education institutions as part of the so-called SAP.NRW initiative of the government of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia; - Functions for the automatic documentation and archiving of order details relevant under procurement law and the option to generate a request from at least three suppliers for a product to be procured; - Functions for the automated checking of suppliers against embargoes/sanctions lists and transparent supplier selection. These defined requirements are justified by comprehensible, objective and contract-related reasons. On the basis of these requirements, market exploration was carried out in the period from early September to late November 2025. According to the contracting authority's knowledge resulting therefrom, the technical requirements can only be met by the e-marketplace platform solution of Unite Procurement Deutschland AG. Therefore, a negotiated procedure without prior call for competition was conducted exclusively with Unite Procurement Deutschland AG pursuant to Section 14 Paragraph 4 No. 2 lit. b VgV and the contract was awarded to them. The decision on the choice of procurement procedure was preceded by a careful examination of the factual and legal situation and comprehensive market exploration.
sig_e809128f7b9e58c68678.title: University of Cologne - Unite E-Marketplace

sig_e82f0d8a1133025c62c1.description: The Department for Education is seeking market feedback on the re-procurement of a national Advocacy Helpline and Safety Net Service for looked after children, care leavers, children in need, and other eligible children and young people in England. The service will provide clear, child-friendly information on advocacy rights; a national multi-channel information, advice and signposting service; and a Safety Net advocacy function where local advocacy provision is unavailable, unreasonably delayed, inaccessible or denied. In addition, the Department is exploring the inclusion of a pilot to test an opt-out advocacy model for children living in residential care. Under this model, advocacy would be routinely offered to children unless they choose to decline participation. The Department intends to use this market engagement to gather feedback on the feasibility, affordability and practical delivery considerations associated with incorporating such a pilot within the future contract. The scope, scale and final design of the pilot are therefore subject to further development and market testing. The provider will also be expected to: • maintain accurate information on advocacy provision across England and support children and young people to access appropriate local services; • provide national intelligence to the Department on advocacy demand, access, waiting times, barriers to provision and emerging themes; • maintain appropriate digital, telephony, case management and reporting systems; • comply with safeguarding, information governance, cyber security and data protection requirements; • ensure appropriate workforce capacity, skills, training and quality assurance arrangements; • support performance monitoring, evaluation and continuous improvement; and • ensure continuity of service throughout the contract period. The Department is particularly interested in market views on the delivery model, affordability, workforce implications and implementation requirements associated with integrating an opt-out advocacy pilot within the wider Advocacy Helpline and Safety Net Service. Lot 1: . None

sig_e843e4aa2fa7cc9363bd.description: The procurement concerns the award of three framework agreements / lots regarding consultancy services for the ATMP Denmark programme (Advanced Therapy Medicinal Product). Lot 1 has previously been cancelled (by notice no. 630687-2025) and subsequently re-tendered (by notice no. 633104-2025). This notice therefore only relates to lot 2 and lot 3. Lot 2 is a framework agreement concerning consultancy assistance for the development, construction and evaluation of communicative tools. Lot 3 is a framework agreement concerning consultancy assistance for mapping Real-World Data opportunities for follow-up on the efficacy of ATMP. The purpose of the framework agreements is to procure and disseminate knowledge that can help strengthen the development, testing and commissioning of commercial and academic advanced therapies in Denmark. The consultants will be part of a working group together with Amgros and carry out the tasks as well as coordinate in close cooperation with Amgros, which is responsible for overall project management. The consultants must contribute their knowledge and act as implementers where there is a need for knowledge gathering and development of deliverables. When mapping and analyses under lot 1 have been completed, the conclusions from them must be communicated under lot 2. Part of the work on lot 2 must therefore await a certain completion of lot 1, but it is expected that work will also take place in parallel on the two framework agreements. The execution of tasks under lot 3 is furthermore expected to take place partly concurrently with the other framework agreements. Each framework agreement / lot has been awarded to one (1) supplier. The lot concerns the development, construction and evaluation of communicative tools that communicate the concrete products resulting from the programme's analyses (in lot 1), in a user-friendly concept. The lot includes, among other things, task execution regarding the design of various products and proposals for solutions that can be piloted. Task execution may, among other things, include the development and setup of guides for the development of clinical ATMPs, application procedures and authority permits primarily aimed at clinical environments, ecosystem illustrations, visualisation of a map of ATMP expertise and competencies primarily in a Danish context, as well as the translation and adaptation of foreign tools to a Danish context. It is expected that several of the developed communicative tools will be pilot-tested, and user testing and evaluation of presentation and content in connection with the development of the concrete product will need to be carried out to the relevant extent. In continuation of this, a possible adaptation of the product may become relevant.; The lot concerns systematic mapping of existing and planned initiatives for Real-World Data (RWD) and Real-World Evidence (RWE) with relevance for Danish ATMP implementation and development. The lot includes, among other things, task execution regarding the mapping of existing RWD data, initiatives and existing data sources with relevance to the ATMP area as well as the scoping and analysis of potential application possibilities regarding the development and implementation of ATMPs. It is expected that this will take place based on Danish infrastructure and existing Danish data, including national and regional databases and registers as well as electronic health records, incl. planned and upcoming initiatives. The lot also includes task execution regarding the identification of unmet needs for RWD for ATMP implementation and ultimately concrete solutions based on the identified needs and available data sources. The task execution also entails input for strategies and proposals for solution models for the use of Real-World Data (RWD) for efficacy and safety monitoring of both academic and commercial ATMPs.
sig_e843e4aa2fa7cc9363bd.title: Framework agreements regarding consultancy services for the ATMP Denmark programme

sig_e8a77b6bb8b092156346.description: The purpose of this procurement is to establish a fully integrated Catering Management System that leverages digital technology to support and optimise every aspect of the catering operation, from menu design through to meal service and post-service analysis. Tenderers must include clear, system-generated infographics or visual workflow diagrams within their submission to demonstrate how the proposed solution delivers end-to-end functionality across menu and recipe planning, nutritional and dietary compliance (including allergens, calories and hydration), patient meal ordering, food production and stock control. The system must incorporate a core module for menu and recipe planning with full allergen, calorie, nutritional, hydration and dietary compliance, integrated with patient meal ordering, food production and stock control. Comprehensive stock management must be supported through the recording of supplier details, ideal stock levels, costs and stock movements, while production planning must utilise menu cycles, production days and historical data to optimise staffing, resource allocation and demand forecasting. Nutritional analysis ensures all meals meet policy guidelines, and data recording supports accurate forecasting and performance review. HACCP management is fully digitised to eliminate paperwork and ensure food safety compliance across central production units and ward pantries. In-patient meal ordering is modernised through bedside tablets, QR codes and menu leaflets, replacing paper-based systems while maintaining patient anonymity. Full end-to-end traceability is provided from primary production to consumption, enabling rapid identification of meals by ward and bed number in the event of a food safety incident, without storing any patient-identifiable information

sig_e8c9c3ee2a3adc21b527.description: The subject of the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) consists of cloud services and related expert services for the customers of Hansel Oy. Cloud services mean capacity or software services delivered via a data network and produced by the supplier. Customers receive cloud capacity for their use as a service. Customers using the cloud service are not directly responsible for or managing the cloud infrastructure, but can manage, for example, operating systems, middleware and databases. Customers may also potentially manage network components, such as firewalls, via a management console or similar. The supplier provides the necessary server capacity, computing time and/or disk capacity dynamically according to the customer's needs. The required capacity scales rapidly according to current needs. Such services include, among others: - Infrastructure services (Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)), where the customer acquires infrastructure services for their organisation's use and is themselves responsible for the management and configuration of the platform. These include, for example, server, storage, computing, memory, backup and data communication service capacity. - Container services (Containers as a Service (CaaS)), where the customer acquires container space from servers and is themselves responsible only for the contents of the container and to some extent for the management of the container. - Platform services (Platform as a Service (PaaS)), where the customer acquires a platform for their applications and is themselves responsible only for the applications. - Serverless services (Serverless, Functions as a Service (FaaS)), where the customer acquires certain functions, for example a scheduled event such as once a day/week/month. Cloud services include, among other things: - Monitoring and management services - Dedicated solutions - Hybrid environment monitoring and management services - Production environment, data communications, data protection and backup - Event, service request and access rights management - Version, configuration and change management - Asset management - Service reporting - Service operation development and management Software as a Service (SaaS) services can also be acquired to a limited extent through the DPS's internal competitions as specified below. SaaS services complementing IaaS and PaaS services can be acquired if their use is closely linked to the utilisation of IaaS and PaaS services which are the main subject of procurement. The aforementioned complementary SaaS services and other services complementing IaaS and PaaS services can be acquired from cloud service providers' services and marketplaces (Marketplace). Other SaaS services cannot be acquired on the basis of this DPS. For example, ready-made end-user software, such as CRM or financial management software, cannot be acquired as SaaS services on the basis of this DPS.
sig_e8c9c3ee2a3adc21b527.title: Cloud services 2026

sig_e8ee7eef535b3fa71066.description: GENERAL THL has commenced the preparation of the procurement process for the maintenance and publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology. As part of the preparation of the tendering process, the contracting authority is conducting a market dialogue. Please note that this is a market consultation notice, not a request for tenders. This market consultation notice does not yet invite the submission of tenders. Participation in the market dialogue is entirely voluntary. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue will not affect a supplier’s opportunities to take part in the procurement procedure to be conducted at a later stage. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tendering process, nor does it exclude anyone from it. Details of the market dialogue are below. The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) is an independent state-owned expert and research institute that promotes the welfare, health and safety of the population. PRELIMINARY SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a SNOMED CT terminology management tool and related services, which will be used for producing, maintaining, and distributing Finland’s national SNOMED CT extension, reference sets (refsets), translations, and national releases. The objective is to procure a comprehensive solution that enables the following functional areas: 1) Terminology maintenance and authoring - Creation of new national concepts when the SNOMED CT International Edition does not cover national requirements. - Management of concept descriptions, synonyms, and relationships between concepts. - Logical and technical validation in accordance with SNOMED CT rules. 2) Design and management of reference sets (refsets, subsets) - Creation and maintenance of both extensional and intentional reference sets. - Version control and metadata definition for reference sets. 3) Production and management of SNOMED CT translations - Production of Finnish and Swedish terms using the translation tool. - Quality assurance and approval workflows for translations, including optional computer-assisted translation. 4) Compilation and validation of national SNOMED CT release - Assembling the national extension and all included components into a single release package. - Validation of the release according to SNOMED CT rules. - Production of publication and distribution packages in RF2 format. 5) Workflows, project management and collaboration - Task assignment, role management, approval processes, and workflow coordination. - Support for customized workflows (e.g., integration with Jira). 6) Search functions and terminology browsing - Efficient search across both the SNOMED CT International Edition and the Finnish national extension. 7) Distribution, licensing, and reporting - Distribution of the national release to various stakeholders. - Management of licensing and access control requirements. - Production of quality, translation, and validation reports. 8) Technical implementation and nonfunctional requirements - The solution shall primarily be delivered as a SaaS service, with the service provider responsible for maintenance, versioning, and technical reliability. - Browser-based user interface, APIs (API/FHIR/REST), high-level information security, usability, and scalability. - Support for multiple languages (at minimum English, Finnish and Swedish). - Integration capabilities with national code server infrastructures. The procurement is for a ready-made software-based solution that can be implemented quickly. The contracting authority has the right to propose customization of the solution as described in the tender Please note, that the details given above are preliminary MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue sessions will be held via Microsoft Teams during weeks 18 and 19 (28 April – 8 May 2026). Each participant will be invited to an individual session with the contracting authority to ensure confidentiality. Details of the meeting, including the agenda and duration, will be sent to the participant via email. As part of the market dialogue, the contracting authority will provide an opportunity to submit written comments on the preliminary tender materials. Separate information about this will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue. Interested parties are kindly requested to register their interest by 23.4.2026, 3.00 PM by contacting kilpailutus@hansel.fi via email. Use: “MARKET DIALOGUE: maintenance and publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology” in the subject line, and provide the participant's name and contact details in the message. Upon registration, participants will receive a scheduled meeting time and a Teams meeting link. The sessions will be conducted on a one-to-one basis between the contracting authority and each participant.
sig_e8ee7eef535b3fa71066.title: INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE: Maintenance and Publication of the Finnish-Language Subset of the SNOMED CT Terminology

sig_e900dfbc64330f69da92.description: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board, (the Contracting Authority), are conducting a market engagement exercise in order to gain a better understanding of the capacity and appetite of the market to provide an end to end All Age Continuing Care (AACC) Client Record System. To support AACC in meeting its long term goals and objectives a solution to manage the full adult CHC, FNC, children's continuing care, joint funding and S117/Mental Health workflows, which can provide real-time, accurate client records, can have configurable workflows aligned to the NHS National Framework and allows multirole access for AACC staff, case managers, finance teams, brokerage, governance and wider partners is required. It is important to note that this exercise is not a call for competition and as such potential providers will need to express an interest in any future tender opportunity once a Tender Notice is published on Find and Tender on the Central Digital Platform (CDP). This market engagement invites individuals and organisations to express an interest in providing a demonstration of their AACC Client Record System. This it is NOT part of any pre-qualification or selection process. It is intended as an awareness, communication, and information gathering exercise. An expression of interest is no indication of a commitment to participate in the demonstrations, nor does it infer any preferential or special status on those individuals and organisations who express an interest. To register an interest in providing a demonstration of your solution and for information please go to the e-tender portal: https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome. Please note that the deadline for registering your interest in providing a demonstration of your solutions 17:00 on the 24th February 2026. Any organisations who express an interest to deliver a demo to the NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board must confirm that their solution can meet all of the following criteria: • Single unified workflow across NENC for Complex Care, CHC, FNC, CCC, s117. Mental Health and joint-funded cases with configurable steps per pathway. •Digital Referral Portal or equivalent for external referrers •Provider Portal or equivalent for all communication flows •Integrated Finance Capacity Following this market engagement exercise, all providers will be able to express an interest to deliver this contract following publication of a Tender Notice, regardless if they have attended a demonstration or not. Whilst registering your interest on Atamis please complete the criteria questions. Please note that all communications will be conducted via the Atamis e-tender portal only. It is free to register on the portal, and it can be accessed at any time of day providing you have a working internet connection. Should bidders have any queries, or are having problems registering on the portal; they should contact the Atamis helpdesk via Phone number 02922 809277 and by email at support-health@atamis.co.uk The helpdesk is open Monday - Friday between 9am - 5.30pm Lot 1: .

sig_e9039a62fd42901a3bf2.description: RENTAL SERVICE OF THE USE OF MICROSOFT SOFTWARE PRODUCTS FOR PUBLIC HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS AND PUBLIC SCIENTIFIC INSTITUTES Rental service of the rights to use Microsoft software products based on appropriate volume licensing models by concluding a framework agreement with a single economic operator for a period of three years, for public higher education institutions and public scientific institutes in the Republic of Croatia. The rental of Microsoft software licences for requirements must be implemented according to a three-year volume licensing model from the Enrollment for Education programme. In this public procurement procedure, a framework agreement will be concluded with a single economic operator for a period of three years. Explanation: The contracting authority intends to conclude a framework agreement with a single economic operator for three years for the following reasons: - end-user institutions for the purposes of performing their own activity to the most significant extent use the Windows operating system and other appropriate Microsoft software, in accordance with the specification, which is the most widely used software of the largest global software manufacturer - Microsoft, - in order for the daily performance of the activities of the end-user institutions as well as the management of administrative data via information services related to the higher education and science system to take place smoothly and successfully in the future, the Contracting Authority is proceeding with the procurement of the rental service of Microsoft software licences according to the volume licensing models and Enrollment for Education programme, stated in the Technical Specifications and Bill of Quantities which are an attachment to this Procurement Documentation, - the selected volume licensing models from the Microsoft Enrollment for Education programme provide for the conclusion of a framework agreement and contract exclusively for a period of three years and thereby ensure particularly favourable licence rental unit prices adapted to the three-year period and unchanging throughout the entire duration. The tenderer is obliged, as part of the subject of procurement, to also ensure the following services: - availability of the latest current versions of Microsoft software in accordance with the specification, via the tenderer's protected Internet portals, - continuous notification of the potential availability and publication of new versions of software for which the rental of licences from the subject of procurement is planned, in accordance with the specification, via the tenderer's protected Internet portals, - cooperation with the referral centre for the purpose of technical and user support for the licensed Microsoft software, especially when upgrading existing software to new software versions, in accordance with the specification, in a manner that is secure for the network environment of the referral centre and end-user institutions, as well as when using the tenderer's protected Internet portals and this without additional charge for the Contracting Authority, except for the prices stated in the Bill of Quantities.

sig_e905a57ff43c16d75a51.description: This contract relates to the conclusion of a framework agreement for the purchase, renewal and management of Atlassian software licences for VRT. Within VRT operations, Atlassian software forms a central and strategic platform for collaboration, project tracking, documentation, code management and service desk processes. The suite includes Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Jira Service Management and various specialised apps, among others. Today, more than 900 employees use one or more applications within this environment, and further structural growth is expected in both the number of users and the number of deployed applications. With a view to guaranteeing the continuity, performance and further development of this platform, VRT wishes to put out to tender a framework agreement with a recognised integrator for the delivery and management of the required Atlassian licences. This agreement must allow VRT to respond flexibly and efficiently to evolving needs within the organisation. This contract relates to the conclusion of a framework agreement for the purchase, renewal and management of Atlassian software licences for VRT.

sig_e91309dbbb2c402cefa9.description: Velindre University NHS Trust (the Authority) wishes to alert suppliers to its intention to hold preliminary market engagement with regards to the potential procurement of an Enterprise Risk Solution to assist in the recording and management of risks across the Authority, ranging from corporate, clinical and project risks. The Authority intends to procure an enterprise-wide software solution to support strategic and operational risk management. The contract will cover the provision of the platform, configuration, implementation, training, ongoing support, and maintenance. The solution must comply with NHS information governance, cyber security, and data-protection requirements and support integration with the Authorities existing technology landscape. The contract duration is expected to be: Initial term: 5 years Optional extensions: 2+2 years The Authority seeks an ERM solution that provides: - Comprehensive risk register functionality - Incident and issue reporting - Real-time dashboards & analytics - Workflow, approvals & audit trail - User-role and permission management - NHS-compliant information governance and security controls - Integration with existing Authorities systems (where applicable) - Training and support for end-users and administrators - Secure hosting and business continuity capabilities - Project management tools such as schedule risk analysis (Monte Carlo Simulation) or equivalent - Open architecture and integration into other systems All suppliers must comply with relevant NHS and statutory requirements, including data-protection legislation and cyber-security standards. Lot 1: .

sig_e943135f233a03f9eb30.description: The Commission is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider for the design, management and delivery of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content. The successful Tenderer will be required to design, manage and deliver a structured programme of talent development and content development activities that strengthen professional capability within the audiovisual sector, facilitate collaboration between practitioners across the island of Ireland and support the development of high-quality audiovisual projects aligned with the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund. The services to be provided include, but are not limited to: • designing and delivering a structured programme of workshops, masterclasses, mentoring, networking events and audiovisual content development activities; • developing and implementing a fair, open and transparent recruitment and selection process for programme participants; • facilitating collaboration between audiovisual practitioners from across the island of Ireland, including participants from different jurisdictions, backgrounds and communities; • providing experienced facilitators, mentors and industry specialists to support participant learning and project development; • supporting participants in the development of audiovisual projects that demonstrate potential to progress to production and reflect the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund; • managing all aspects of programme delivery, stakeholder engagement, administration and communications; • monitoring programme delivery and performance against agreed milestones; and • providing progress reports, financial reporting and a final programme evaluation report in accordance with the requirements set out in Appendix 1 – Specification of Services.
sig_e943135f233a03f9eb30.title: Request for Tender for the Provision of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content

sig_e9507d2c77fcbafaa474.description: Essex County Council (ECC) is seeking information from suppliers who can provide an existing, fully developed, cloud based DBS processing platform to support its HR Shared Services Team. The team delivers recruitment and vetting services for ECC and external public sector customers. ECC is an established DBS Registered Body, Umbrella Organisation, & a Responsible Organisation and will continue operating in these capacities throughout the contract. All DBS applications must be submitted under ECC's Registered Body identity, with counter signatory duties remaining with ECC. The supplier will act solely as a processor and platform provider. The platform must support Basic, Standard and Enhanced DBS checks, provide comprehensive reporting to support invoicing and financial processes, offer customer self service capability, and operate with minimal impact on ECC's infrastructure. Suppliers must demonstrate appropriate business continuity arrangements (excluding any DBS initiated eBulk suspension) and provide training and knowledge transfer at mobilisation to enable ECC to train system users. ECC's current contract ends on 30 September 2026, and this early market engagement is being undertaken in preparation for that expiry. We aim to understand market capability, implementation timescales, indicative costs, and interest ahead of issuing our formal Request for Quotation (RFQ). We are keen to identify suppliers who wish to be included in the RFQ process. We look forward to hearing from interested suppliers as part of this early engagement exercise.

sig_e96cd6c890a9e105dffe.description: Service quota to support a 24x7 Managed Security Operations Center (SOC) solution for security monitoring of various clouds (multiclouds) The Federal Employment Agency (BA) has created the commercial prerequisites for the use of public cloud services, i.e., AWS, Google, Microsoft Azure, IONOS, STACKIT, OVH, CloudFerro and others, via the cloud broker framework agreement. Initially, the use of AWS, Microsoft Azure and STACKIT is intended. Which specific applications will run on which cloud is not currently fixed and will develop over the next 12 to 24 months. The parallel operation of applications in the BA's own data centres and applications in third-party clouds requires a performance expansion in the IT security architecture and in IT security operations in order to maintain the previous level of IT security. To this end, the BA intends to introduce a 24x7 Managed Security Operations Center (SOC) solution for security monitoring of the various clouds (multiclouds). The BA's previous on-site SOC will remain in place and will perform 3rd level security analysis, incident response and digital forensics tasks in the multicloud context. Due to the multicloud focus and the cooperation between the Managed SOC and the BA SOC, the tendered service is also referred to as a "Hybrid SOC for Multicloud". In a Managed SOC (service area 1), threats and anomalies are to be detected in a central solution provided by the provider (threat and anomaly detection system). As a result of this measure, all incoming IT security information and security warnings are to be reconciled and evaluated via data analysis, data correlation, analysis and threat databases, for example. The SOC analysts provided by the Managed Security Service Provider support the BA's security team within the scope of qualifying these incidents and provide recommendations for the response to fend off threats and cyber attacks. The client is given read-only access to their log data and alarms in the contractor's system. Log data fed into the central system must also be capable of being fed from the source system or from the central analysis system into the client's own solution. In service area 2, support services for a multicloud IT security architecture and its implementation are to be provided. "Experts for multi-tier applications" and "Experts for cloud" are required to carry out these activities.
sig_e96cd6c890a9e105dffe.title: 3.RV-P - Mini-competition - Hybrid SOC - Managed Service - Lot 3

Proposal submissions are due by August 13, 2025 @ 5pm. AMENDMENT 0001: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the closing date to July 3, 2025 and add an Area of Interest N0016425SCA001 Miniature Aiming System (MAS) Machine Gun Optic (MGO) attachment. ORIGINAL POSTING: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) N00164-25-S-C001 Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC, Crane) The procedures outlined in this CSO apply to Areas of Interest posted under N00164-25-S-C001 OBJECTIVE: this announcement is intended to enable the rapid selection of innovative commercial solutions through a three-phased, competitive process. Including commercially-available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 1.1 Background and Authority NSWC Crane’s mission is to deliver innovative solutions and readiness to the Nation and its Warfighters through application of Technical Capabilities; advance all-domain system of systems within the Mission Areas of Expeditionary Warfare, Strategic Missions, and Electromagnetic Warfare; conduct science and technology, research, development, test and evaluation, acquisition and in-service engineering across the Defense lifecycles. To achieve these mission imperatives, NSWC Crane regularly partners with private industry using a variety of collaborative tools in order to streamline the incorporation of innovative technology into the products and services delivered to the Warfighter. To accelerate the adoption of advanced technology, curate solutions to technology gaps, and lead rapid prototyping NSWC Crane issues this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) as authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation. In this context “Innovative” means— Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. NSWC Crane is seeking innovative commercial solutions relevant to the following areas of technological exploration: • Expeditionary Warfare Guided by the National Defense Strategy, NSWC Crane recognizes the priorities and threats shifted to the Pacific. NSWC Crane’s efforts must counter the multi-domain threats and deter aggression posed in the Indo-Pacific region. This reinforces the need of a Joint Force that is even more lethal, resilient, agile and responsive. Autonomous solutions with a focus on payload and sensor integration to enhance detection, tracking, identifying, decision making, maneuver and kinetic/non-kinetic engagement capabilities for multi-domain, uncrewed and counter-crewed systems are a strategic priority. Expeditionary Warfare Development’s heritage has been and continues to focus on rapid prototyping and proven solutions supporting the evolving needs of the Expeditionary force. • Strategic Missions As the Navy’s primary organic field activity for full life cycle management including hardware, ordnance and power systems, NSWC Crane applies the distinct capabilities inherent to its people and facilities to assure 100% operational readiness of strategic missile systems. Fleet Readiness and Modernization and Hypersonics are a top priority of the Navy and DoD. These strategic priorities require collaboration between the Navy, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency to align appropriate requirements, technology development, rapid prototyping, production, sustainment and protection activities of ballistic missile systems to enable affordability, advance technology and reduce program risks to modernize the nuclear enterprise to defeat emerging threats worldwide. • Electromagnetic Warfare NSWC Crane’s Spectrum Warfare Department is the largest concentration of Electronic Warfare experts in the DoD. NSWC Crane provides non-kinetic expertise and electromagnetic spectrum dominance to all the services. Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) is a strategic priority due to the increasingly congested, contested and constrained environments. NSWC Crane supports multidomain integrated solutions through multispectral capabilities utilizing technology development, rapid prototyping, production and sustainment. Pursuant to DFARS 212.7002, NSWC Crane will only use this CSO to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements and to close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological advancements. All products and services acquired using this CSO will be treated as commercial products or commercial services, awarded on a fixed-price basis. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.10270, this announcement is a competitive selection of proposals based on a review by scientific, technological, or other subject-matter expert peers and is a competitive procedure. As a result of the competitive processes used under this CSO Announcement, multiple awards may be executed. The methods utilized to execute awards include: FARbased contract, Purchase Order, Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), and/or Bailment Agreement. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022, NSWC Crane may award an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to vendors to carry out prototype project(s) directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4023, NSWC Crane may procure (by contract or otherwise) ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, telecommunications, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary concerned considers necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense. 1.2 General Solicitation and Evaluation Procedures NSWC Crane’s CSO is soliciting Solution Briefs in response to individual Areas of Interest (AOIs). AOIs are focused topic(s) categories that will be published separately and posted on the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. All Solution Briefs submitted in response to AOIs will be governed by this CSO unless otherwise noted in the AOI. AOIs will be written in broad terms to maximize latitude in creativity when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from nontraditional defense contractors and interested parties (entities) who may be unfamiliar with submitting traditional proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post AOIs at any time. Interested parties are encouraged to frequently check the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC, Crane website for new AOI postings. Evaluation of responses will consist of the following 3 Phases: 1) Solution Brief, 2) Pitch, and 3) Full written proposal – described in more detail here: Phase 1 Solution Briefs: Solution Briefs submitted in response to an AOI shall be submitted as specified in Section 2 of this CSO. The Government will evaluate Solution Briefs against the criteria stated in this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for the costs associated with Solution Brief submissions. Phase 2 Pitch Session: Respondents whose Solution Briefs are evaluated to be of merit may be invited to provide a pitch following the instructions provided in Section 2.3 of this CSO. The Government reserves the right to limit the number of parties invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. In the event that the Government requires a demonstration, additional information will be provided in the specific AOI highlighting those procedures, otherwise Phase 2 will be comprised solely of the pitch. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with pitches, unless otherwise stipulated. Phase 3 Proposal: Those entities whose Solution Brief and Pitch are evaluated to be of merit and are selected for potential award may be invited to submit a full written proposal following the instructions provided in Section 2.4 of this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with the proposal in Phase 3, unless otherwise stipulated. SECTION 2 – GUIDELINES FOR SUBMISSION 2.1 General Guidelines Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. Companies may submit multiple Solution Briefs in response to any single AOI if each submission represents a separate and distinct concept. The period of performance for any Solution Brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24-months. Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. All Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals shall be unclassified. Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: “This [select one: Solution Brief, Pitch, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to non-Government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of -- or in connection with – the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use the information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: “Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.” Foreign-Owned businesses may independently submit a solution or do so as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more United States-Owned businesses. However, the ability to obtain an agreement based upon a submission may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-Owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain proscribed information. Submissions must be submitted electronically. Submissions sent through other channels or after the AOI period has ended will not be reviewed nor evaluated. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.2 Phase 1 Solution Brief PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF CONTENT Solution Briefs should not exceed five (5) written pages using 12-point font. Alternatively, Solution Briefs may take the form of briefing slides which should not exceed fifteen (15) slides. Briefs should include at a minimum: Title Page (does not count against page limit) Entity Name, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address. Specifically identify the AOI for which the Solution Brief is submitted. Executive Summary of the technology (one page) Describe the concept and unique aspects of the technology as it relates to the AOI. Identify whether the solution is an existing technology that has satisfied a pilot or demonstration (ie, commercially ready and viable technology), or the if the solution will require development for defense application. If development or adaptation is proposed, identify a suggested path to mature the technology. Identify aspects of the solution which may be considered proprietary or Intellectual Property (IP) Provide a brief overview of the company, including a summary of product commercialization and go-to-market strategy. PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF BASIS OF EVALUATION All solution briefs correctly submitted in response to an AOI will be evaluated against the stated criteria below. (Y/N) The proposed innovative commercial solution, technology, process, or method, is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or is an application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. Relevance of the Solution Brief in addressing the AOI. Technical Merit and feasibility of the solution to address Government AOI problem statement. A quick, reasonable, and efficient way exists for the DoD to test the innovative commercial solution, within a specified duration, whether outside or integrated within the DoD infrastructures or networks, as appropriate. Additional technical evaluation criteria specific to a particular project may be used. In these instances, the additional criteria will be posted within the AOI announcement on the SAM.Gov and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI, not against other Solution Briefs submitted in response to the same AOI. Additionally, while not overtly stated in AOIs, the Government’s evaluation will consider whether the proposal increases the likelihood of accomplishing NSWC Crane’s Mission Focus Areas. All submissions will be evaluated, however, only a select few will be invited to pitch. The government reserves the right to limit the number of entities invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.3 Phase 2 Pitch PHASE 2 PITCH CONTENT In Phase 2, entities shall provide an in-person or virtual pitch to demonstrate and provide further details on their proposed innovative commercial solution and the technical and business viability of the proposed solution. The Government may elect to use external market research during the Pitch to evaluate viability. In addition to the Pitch, the Government, at its discretion, may request for consideration an additional written submission to further supplement the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. During the Phase 2 Pitch, the Company must detail/address: Estimated Price/Schedule Rough order of magnitude (ROM) or pricing Anticipated Data Rights Assertions During the Pitch, the Government may request the additional information/detail with respect to the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. PHASE 2 PITCH BASIS OF EVALUATION Individual pitches will be evaluated against the following factors: Relevance of the pitch in addressing the AOI and the ability of the presenter to adequately address Government questions or concerns regarding the proposed application or use of the innovative commercial solution. The solution has technical merit, adequately & realistically addresses Government need and can be quickly incorporated into DOD systems. Reasonableness of the ROM The associated delivery schedule is expeditious and realistic. Individual pitches will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI and the factors above, not against any other Pitches held under the same AOI. Pitch submissions will be valid for 180 calendar days after the pitch date. Upon completion of evaluations, the Government will notify the Company that: (1) the proposed concept/technology/solution has been selected for possible award and the entity is invited to submit a full proposal; (2) the proposed concept/technology/solution is not of interest to the Government; or (3) the proposed concept/technology/solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources. If the proposed innovative commercial solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources, the Company may be contacted with a request to respond to proposal request within 180 calendar days from the pitch date. If after 180 calendar days from the pitch date (or earlier if notified by NSWC, Crane), Government resources are not identified to formally move into Phase 3, the entity will no longer be eligible for an award under that particular AOI. 2.4 Phase 3 Proposal PHASE 3 PROPOSAL CONTENT The final phase of the evaluation process is the proposal request. Based upon the evaluation process detailed in Phase 1 and 2, the Government may request a full written proposal. The entity will be invited to develop and submit a full written proposal and negotiate appropriate terms and conditions. Entities may discuss ideas and questions related to the proposal with the Government POC during the proposal writing process. Each proposal submitted shall consist of two sections: Section 1 shall consist of the technical proposal; Section 2 shall consist of the price/cost/schedule. Proposals will be assessed by NSWC Crane technical and Contracting subject matter experts. Entities may propose their own internal terms and conditions (e.g., Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA)) to be considered during negotiations with the Government. Note, there are certain terms and conditions the Government is unable to accept. Awards made under this authority will only be issued as fixed price awards in accordance with DFARS 212.7002(b). However, projects awarded through the CSO are flexible to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and where it meets the Government’s needs. At a minimum, written proposals must contain: Title Page Company Name, Point of Contact Name, Date, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address and any subcontractors or team members. Include an abstract which provides a concise description of the proposal. Description of the proposed innovative commercial solution Background and objectives of the proposed solution, deliverables, and resources needed to execute. Include the nature and extent of the anticipated results. Include ancillary and operational issues such as certifications, algorithms, and any engineering/software development methodologies to be used. If services, include a Statement of Work (SOW). Provide a detailed project schedule that outlines the various phases of work to be accomplished within the proposed period of performance. You may refer to the Solution Brief that prompted this proposal request, but do not duplicate it. Identify any Government material, equipment, data, or other items necessary. Phase 3 - Price Proposal The entity shall propose a fixed price for the item or service and provide any data or supporting information necessary for the determination of a fair and reasonable price. This can include, but is not limited to, commercial price catalog or other proprietary information to help the Government assess the proposed price. Additionally, if proposing an OT, while not required to be specifically addressed in the proposal (with the exception of the 1/3 cost-share requirement, if applicable), the Government will review the proposal to determine if the following OT statutory requirements are met: Fits the definition of a prototype Meets non-traditional participation/cost share requirement: Non-traditional defense contractor contributes to a significant extent or not; if not, 1/3 cost share implementation is addressed Defense Utility: Solution is applicable to a DoD platform, system or component SECTION 3 – AWARDS 3.1 General Guidelines Upon favorable review and available funds, the Government may choose to make an award. Only Warranted Contracting Officers or Agreements Officers may obligate the Government by entering into or modifying a binding agreement on behalf of the Government. Awards made under this CSO will be fixed price. Contract type will be determined during Phase 3. Multiple awards may be made to pursue similar or dissimilar solutions should they all meet the technical criteria, be selected for award, and if funds are available. Entities must have a DUNs and CAGE Code registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award. Companies are advised to commence SAM registration upon receipt of a proposal request. Awardees must be determined to be responsible by the Contracting or Agreements Officer and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving award. Receipt of a proposal request does not guarantee receipt of award. The Government reserves the right, at any point prior to award, to cancel the request. Upon award, awardees must register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (e.g. Wide Area Work Flow). 3.2 Comptroller General Access to Information In OT projects that provide for payments in a total amount in excess of $5,000,000, the Agreement will include a mandatory clause that provides for the Comptroller General the ability to examine the records of any party to the agreement or any entity that participates in the performance of the agreement. 3.3 Procurement Integrity Act (PIA) All awards under this CSO shall be treated as Federal Agency procurements for purpose of 41 U.S.C. Chapter 21. Accordingly, the CSO competitive solicitation process and awards made thereof must adhere to the ethical standards required by the PIA. SECTION 4 - ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING As it is the mission of NSWC Crane to enable access to commercially-derived disruptive capabilities across the entirety of the DoD enterprise, Prototype OTAs awarded against this CSO will allow for an iterative prototyping process. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the work in a prototype project to allow the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the original Government customer or originate with other organizations within the Federal Government. SECTION 5 – FOLLOW-ON PRODUCTION Upon successful completion of a prototype project under the OTA, the Government may negotiate a follow-on production contract or agreement without further competition. Any concept/technology/solution successfully proven through a Prototype OTA can be transitioned to production. AOIs posted by the Government under this CSO and Prototype OTAs awarded will include language providing for the potential award of a follow-on production contract or agreement as authorized under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 Individual AOIs and CSO prototype OTAs will explicitly identify follow-on Prototype OTAs as a potential outcome of a successful prototyping effort. SECTION 6 SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION A transaction for a prototype project is complete upon the written determination of the appropriate approving official (program manager and Agreement Officer) for the matter in question that efforts conducted under a Prototype OTA: (1) met the key technical goals of a project; (2) satisfied success metrics incorporated into the Prototype OTA; or (3) accomplished a particularly favorable or unexpected result that justifies the transition to production. Furthermore, successful completion can occur prior to the conclusion of a prototype project to allow the Government to transition any aspect of the prototype project determined to provide utility into production while other aspects of the prototype project have yet to be completed. Any Prototype OTA shall contain a provision that sets forth the conditions under which that prototype agreement must be successfully completed. SECTION 7 – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during Proposal development and negotiations. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. Companies may enter into specific NDAs directly with the Non-Government advisors or their corporate entities. Submission of an offer under this CSO will constitute a grant of authority by the submitting company to the Government to allow the use of non-Government advisors to participate in evaluations of all phases of the CSO process. The Government understands that information provided in response to this CSO is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. NSWC, Crane policy is to treat all submissions as source selection sensitive information, and to disclose their contents only for the purpose of evaluation. Restrictive notices notwithstanding, during the evaluation process, submissions may be handled by support contractors for administrative purposes and/or to assist with technical evaluation. All NSWC, Crane and DoD support contractors performing this role are expressly prohibited from performing NSWC, Crane-sponsored technical research and are bound by appropriate NDAs. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained at NSWC, Crane and all other non-required copies destroyed. A certification of destruction may be requested, provided the formal request is received at this office within 5 calendar days after notification that a proposal was not selected.

Development and implementation of a system for comprehensive management and debt recovery services for MZK. The delivered system is to provide a complete solution in the field of civil law debt collection, including an amicable, judicial and enforcement (bailiff) debt recovery module. 3. Development and implementation of a system managing Control Devices and Inspectors. 4. Granting an indefinite licence to the Contracting Authority for the Platform. 5. Delivery of 11 Inspector Devices together with an application for ticket inspection and generation of additional charges (with the option of printing with payment method designation (bank transfer) and making payments using payment cards, BLIK and other payment instruments. SIM cards will be provided by the Contracting Authority. At the System Design stage, the parties will agree on target solutions: based on a dedicated APN or a set-up VPN tunnel. 6. Provision by the Contractor, during the implementation period and during the period of providing payment services (on Inspector Devices, in the scope of collecting the additional charge for lack of a ticket/entitlement) and service services (maintenance period), of full cloud computing infrastructure and licences necessary to use cloud services to operate the Platform. 7. Operation of the system during the maintenance period (including warranty reviews, maintenance costs of a dedicated SMS gateway, costs resulting from the agreement with the acquiring bank) in a set number of months. 8. The obligation to transfer (migrate) passenger data from the currently operating debt collection service system to the new system. The migration should be carried out in a manner ensuring the completeness of the transferred data, ensuring the possibility of making (in the migration process and after its completion) corrections, changes to data or deletion of data, e.g. outdated lines, streets, etc., while performing this process. The final migration process should be preceded by test migration(s) in order to verify the correctness and completeness of the execution of this process. Currently, the Contracting Authority uses Municom software from PZI TARAN sp. z o.o. (R&G PLUS Sp. z o.o. Group). The database environment is based on the DB2 engine and is located on the Contracting Authority's local server. All accesses to the environment will be granted to the Contractor after signing the contract. 9. Provision by the Contractor of access to a fully functional System, enabling the Contracting Authority to carry out verification and acceptance in an environment reflecting production conditions (training and test environment). 10. Training of System users indicated by the Contracting Authority. [System maintenance and warranty conditions] 11. Provision by the Contractor for a period from 36 to 60 months (according to the bid evaluation criterion) of services in relation to the software and all components delivered as part of: 11.1. maintenance of the Debt Collection System during the warranty period, 11.2. provision of warranty and technical support for the System, 11.3. provision of service services and removal of defects, faults and errors of the System during the warranty period, 11.4. bearing the costs of maintaining a dedicated SMS gateway for sending messages from Inspector Devices (calls for payment), 11.5. Provision of programming support services during the term of the contract in a set number of man-hours, 12. Bearing by the Contractor of the costs of system operation during the maintenance period (including warranty reviews, communication costs in a set number of months. II. The scope of the OPTION RIGHT includes: delivery of additional Inspector Devices in a number not greater than 10 units, which will be identical in terms of all features and functionalities as the Inspector Devices delivered in the basic scope of the contract. Detailed provisions concerning the activation of the option right are contained in the drafted contract provisions, i.e., Appendix No. 1 to the SWZ.

sig_e9a3ae3849e00d353295.description: The subject of the public contract is the conclusion of a framework agreement (hereinafter referred to as "FA4") with one or more participants, on the basis of which the contracting authority will, in the form of partial public contracts (mini-tenders), request professional activities aimed at the completion and further development of the Shared Information System of the TA CR (SISTA) and functionalities in the SISTA Ecosystem. SISTA is an open, modular and scalable platform that the contracting authority is building as a successor to the existing information systems ISTA and IS BETA for the administration of targeted research and development support. The SISTA Ecosystem is designed so that individual services, components and technological knowledge can also be shared with other public administration entities and used in various application contexts. The performance consists of providing professional activities across the development life cycle: analytical and documentation activities, process analyses and scenario proposals, UX/UI design and user validation, design and implementation of testing, architectural design and prototyping, programming and implementation of functionalities to production quality, integration and data activities, deployment and operational preparation (CI/CD), security and compliance, and operation and maintenance of services in experimental operation. Individual performances will be awarded in the form of mini-tenders, both with the reopening of competition between participants (§ 135 ZZVZ) and without the reopening of competition (§ 134 ZZVZ). Development takes place in a DevOps model and in a multi-vendor environment. The operational and infrastructure layer (OPS / Internal Developer Platform) is provided by the contracting authority using its own resources; participants implement the development (DEV) layer. The technological framework is based on Cloud Native and Infrastructure as Code principles: the infrastructure currently runs in Google Cloud, applications are containerised (Docker) and orchestrated in Kubernetes (GKE), code and configuration versioning takes place in the GitLab environment operated by the contracting authority, and CI/CD (GitLab Pipelines, ArgoCD, GitOps) is used for deployment. The participant hands over the complete and functional source code to the contracting authority and provides an exclusive unlimited licence for the work. The remuneration for performance is based on a fixed hourly rate of 1 800 CZK excluding VAT, uniform for all performances under the framework agreement; the bid price in individual mini-tenders is formed by the product of this rate and the number of hours. The framework agreement is concluded for a period of 6 years. The total estimated value of all mini-tenders awarded on the basis of FA4 amounts to 40 000 000 CZK excluding VAT and represents the final financial limit of the framework agreement.
