The subject matter of the Contract is the improvement and upgrading of the overall taxpayer service experience and the upgrading of all related information systems and tools of the Taxpayer Service Centre (TSC) of the Independent Authority for Public Revenue. The improvement and upgrading of the overall taxpayer service experience will be achieved through a single omni-channel service system which will act as a hub for collecting and transferring information from and to the individual service channels (web portal, digital assistant, mobile application, telephone service, etc.). Through this comprehensive, multifaceted and omni-channel service via the omni-channel approach, the taxpayer will have the opportunity to utilise one or more communication channels with IAPR and the individual tax offices (DOY) and customs offices. At the same time, all technological infrastructure related to the service of taxpayers of the TSC will be upgraded through the improvement of all information systems and tools to upgrade the services provided by the existing Taxpayer Service Centre (TSC).The expenditure for the Project will be charged to the Public Investment Programme, under ΣΑΤΑ 051 (Project Code: 2022TA05100013). This contract is funded by the European Union – NextGeneration EU, under the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan "Greece 2.0" (SUB13, Action code: 16291 / Axis 4.1) and from national resources through the PIP, based on the Inclusion Decision with ref. no. 144844/EX-2022/06-10-2022 (With ADA: 9TW8H-15S)), as amended by decision ref. no. 109336 EX 2024/25-07-2024 (ADA: PS96XI-ALK) and has been assigned MIS TA code: 5149138. The procurement for this project will be charged to the PIP Budget of the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (Special Entity 1024-703-0000000).The budget for the physical scope of the project amounts to 22.000.000,00 € including VAT 24% (budget without VAT: 17.741.935,48 €, plus VAT: 4.258.064,52 €). This expenditure concerns the funded part of the project and will be charged to ΣΑΤΑ 051. Provision is made for the possibility of activating an option in the event that it is justified by the needs of the contracting authority. The activation of the option may amount up to 4.860.800,00 € including VAT (estimated option value 3.920.000,00 € excluding VAT + 940.800,00 € VAT 24%), as follows: Before the expiry of the minimum two-year warranty of good operation of the contract, the Contracting Authority may decide to exercise the option for maintenance services, software updates and licences for up to five (5) years after the expiry of the warranty period, the maximum expenditure of which cannot exceed annually ten percent (10%) of Work Packages 2 and 3 of the Initial Contract:  Maximum Annual Cost of maintenance services, software updates and licences: 784.000,00 € excluding VAT 24% (972.160,00 € including VAT).  Total Maximum Cost of maintenance services, software updates and licences for the five (5) years: 3.920.000,00 € excluding VAT 24% (4.860.800,00 € including VAT). The resulting expenditure for the provision of option services will be charged to ALE 2420389001 "Other remuneration and maintenance and repair expenses" of the Ordinary Budget of IAPR (SE 1024-801-0000000) of the financial years 2029-2033 within the framework of the MTEF in force at the time. The subject matter of the Contract is the improvement and upgrading of the overall taxpayer service experience and of all related information systems and tools of both the Taxpayer Service Centre (TSC) and the individual tax offices (DOY) and customs offices. The improvement and upgrading of the overall taxpayer service experience will be achieved through a single service system which will act as a hub for collecting, managing and transferring information from and to the individual service channels. Through this comprehensive, multifaceted and omni-channel service (omni-channel approach), the taxpayer will have the opportunity to utilise one or more communication channels with IAPR and the individual tax offices and customs offices. At the same time, all technological infrastructure related to the service of taxpayers of the TSC will be upgraded through the improvement of all information systems and tools to upgrade the services provided by the existing Taxpayer Service Centre (TSC). To achieve the required new degree of parameterisation and flexibility, the new advanced system should not be based on a specific static structure; instead, this should be definable based on the needs of each period of its development. The new system must have the capability of defining and incorporating dynamic workflows that will be newly created or modified by the System Administrator depending on the respective current service procedure of any new Service to be integrated. The new advanced system must support all functionalities provided by the existing TSC and incorporate new ones for more efficient service of transaction parties. The upgrading of the information provided in content and media, support, and the provision of new complementary and support services will concern both external users, i.e. citizens and businesses, and internal users of the Independent Authority for Public Revenue and bodies. The architectural solution ultimately adopted will enable the modelling of the new TSC information system

as a single central core computer infrastructure (omni-channel approach) which can be easily enriched with any distinct necessary functionality as a separate information entity, which can be directly attached to it (e.g. microservices technology). This will result in a clear separation of the subsystems and distinct functional parts of the TSC information system, making their modification and replacement as well as the attachment of new ones (e.g. access and role management subsystem, statistics/reports export subsystem, etc.) easy and immediate. For the effective implementation of the project, the contract is broken down into the following work packages:  Work Package 1: Project Coordination and Management  Work Package 2: Technical Infrastructure of Omni Channel System and subsystems  Work Package 3: Business Process Automation - Interconnection  Work Package 4: Promotion and Publicity Actions  Work Package 5: Taxpayer Service Services

sig_e9f1fdb30ea9598bd4f7.description: The core of the delivery is FoUI guidance as described below. Oslo municipality also requests an option for other services. The objective of the procurement is to enter into a contract with 4-7 FoUI guides for selected input areas. The FoUI guideline shall strengthen research supported innovation in the region ́s businesses and the municipality ́s own activities. The effort shall strengthen capacity for innovation in business and shall also contribute to strengthening Oslo municipality ́s own capacity for research-supported innovation, in line with the approved strategy for knowledge based development, innovation and digital technology for Oslo municipality (KID). Business orientated efforts will be prioritised, among other things, in accordance with the regional plan for competitiveness and value creation in Oslo and Akershus, which is at a hearing in autumn 2026. Special emphasis will be placed on competence for business, the public sector and research within: · Sustainable restructuring and systems for the green shift. · Public Health, Health and Life Sciences · Digitalisation and artificial intelligence · Stand-by, Security and Civil Protection It is an advantage to refer to in-depth knowledge of industries that are strategically important for Oslo, such as maritime, digitalisation, health, dual-use and circular economy. Artificial intelligence and digitalisation are in the process of taking in all parts of business and society. Knowledge on digitalisation and artificial intelligence is therefore not limited to one priority area, and it will be advantageous to be able to use digitalisation and AI within the individual commitment areas. The R&D guides have the main assignment of mobilising businesses and Oslo ́s own entities for more research-supported R&D. The R&D guides discuss project ideas and possibilities with companies or the public sector and can connect R&D needs with relevant researchers. The FoUI guideline mobilises to regional, national and international schemes, as well as for preliminary projects and the subsidy scheme SmartOslo. New this time is that we want the FoUI guidelines to also be able to contribute to mobilising to EU support schemes for businesses, including EIC.
sig_e9f1fdb30ea9598bd4f7.title: Competence brokering (FoUI guideline) Oslo

sig_e9f495077391c779d5d7.description: Waterschap Scheldestromen intends to award a contract to Haskoning Nederland B.V. for the operational support of the Nereda installation at the Breskens wastewater treatment plant. The contract comprises: -maintenance; -support; -software updates and further development of the Aquasuite Nereda Controller software; -as well as monitoring of the controller; -helpdesk support; -access to and support for a digital portal and specialist process support aimed at guaranteeing and optimising the operation of the installation. The water authority intends to award this contract directly, given that exclusively Haskoning Nederland B.V. possesses the intellectual property rights, the source code and the specialist technical knowledge that are necessary for carrying out these activities. The source code is not made available to third parties and third parties are not entitled to independently maintain, adapt or further develop the software. The requested services are inextricably linked to the Nereda Controller software, the underlying Nereda technology and the associated specialist know-how. In addition, deploying an alternative supplier would lead to the replacement or redevelopment of the existing control environment, whilst the required intellectual property rights, source code and specialist knowledge are not available to third parties. Such a transition would entail disproportionately high implementation, development and migration costs and is therefore technically, operationally and economically inefficient. Other market operators do not possess the required intellectual property rights, source code, software environment and specialist knowledge to carry out the requested services lawfully and technically equivalently. In view of the exclusive rights of Haskoning Nederland B.V. and the absence of a reasonable alternative, waterschap Scheldestromen considers that only one (1) economic operator can carry out the contract. The intended commencement date of the agreement is 1 January 2027. The agreement is entered into for an indefinite period and remains in force as long as the Nereda installation at the Breskens wastewater treatment plant within waterschap Scheldestromen is in use and no alternative market operator is available that demonstrably possesses the necessary intellectual property rights, source code, specialist knowledge and technical capabilities to carry out the aforementioned activities lawfully and in an equivalent manner.
sig_e9f495077391c779d5d7.title: Operational support, maintenance and further development of the process control of RWZI Breskens

sig_ea03035166d131d90f80.description: The Finnish Tax Administration is preparing a procurement of an online database of international company information, including a set of tools for analyzing the data. The solution shall include a global database for international companies and entities. Customer shall retrieve information, data and reports with common web-browsers (Chrome, Edge). The usage of the solution does not require installing any application software. The database must be a Software as a Service (SaaS). The service is for 35 concurrent users. All departments of the Customer can use the products listed for different purposes ranging from anti money laundering and know your customer (AML/KYC), transfer pricing, audit, tax fraud and investigation. The database must include financial and ownership data of at least 100 000 000 enterprises and detailed financial and ownership data of at least 10 000 000 enterprises on all continents. The database includes general financial and ownership information, such as name, address, company identifiers, turnover, net income and shareholders on at least 100 000 000 enterprises worldwide. The database includes detailed financial and ownership information on at least 10 000 000 enterprises worldwide. The solution shall be available 24/7. Usability for an office time (Helsinki (UTC + 2:00) 08.00-16.00) is at least 99% and at least 96% out of office time. The solution includes a global database for international companies and entities including ownership and financial data. The data must be up to date and updated frequently. It must have possibility to conduct and build precise single and mass searches. It must have MS Excel integration and possibility to export data into Excel. The tool shall provide comparability analysis for Transfer Pricing purposes, including loans, royalties and commodities information. Also peer comparison (key figures compared to peer group's figures) are needed. The offered price shall include all mandatory requirements, support and training by the supplier. Travel expenses shall not be paid separately. The Contract shall remain in effect for four (4) years as a fixed-term contract after which the Contract will automatically remain in effect until further notice.

sig_ea27b4ae3896bfc29f39.description: To procure Technology Enabled Care (TEC) Services covering Hard-Wired and Digital Alarm Unit (DAU) Maintenance of Call Monitoring Systems (Lot 1) and Monitoring & Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC) Services (Lot 2) across Aster Group's housing stock. These services will form an end-to-end TEC operating model that ensures residents receive a safe, reliable and digitally resilient service. Aster is seeking partners who can support this transformation, safeguard service continuity through the digital migration period and deliver a high-quality resident experience. Lot 1: Hard-Wired and Digital Alarm Unit (DAU) Maintenance of Call Monitoring Systems. Lot 1 covers the maintenance, servicing, repair and future upgrade of Aster’s Hard-Wired alarm systems, DAUs,smoke detection and fire panels within dwellings. The Contractor will support Aster in ensuring equipment reliability, minimising downtime, maintaining accurate asset data and enabling a smooth transition from analogue to digital-ready systems. These services play a critical role in ensuring that residents can raise alerts safely and consistently Lot 2: Monitoring & Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC) Services. Lot 2 covers Monitoring and Alarm Receiving Centre (ARC) Services. The ARC is responsible for receiving alarm activations, responding to calls, triggering appropriate actions and supporting residents in emergency and welfare situations. The ARC provider will also be responsible for onboarding new TEC users, including configuring monitoring profiles, ensuring alarms route correctly and maintaining up-to-date service user information. In addition, the ARC provider will be required to deliver a suite of performance and operational reports that enable Aster to review service outcomes, monitor compliance, identify trends and assure resident safety. Tenderers must therefore clearly outline the reports they propose to provide as part of their response. The ARC must provide key industry updates from the TSA
sig_ea27b4ae3896bfc29f39.title: CAS-01240-W3D2X3 Technology Enabled Care Services at Aster Group

sig_ea2de2486cdd4300e792.description: Oak National Academy is exploring the replacement of BeApplied, its current Applicant Tracking System (ATS), which is expected to become unavailable at the end of March 2027. Oak is also considering whether to procure a linked HR information system (HRIS) at the same time, procure the systems as separate lots, or address its HRIS needs through a later procurement. The immediate priority is an ATS that can be implemented in time to maintain recruitment services. Oak is undertaking this engagement to understand the market, test its developing requirements, assess realistic implementation times and decide how best to package the ATS and HRIS requirements. No decision has yet been made to include an HRIS in the resulting tender. Oak invites input from suppliers of ATS products, HRIS products, integrated ATS and HRIS platforms, and suppliers able to deliver either system with a reliable integration to the other. Suppliers do not need to offer both systems to participate. Oak’s current ATS needs are described in the accompanying working requirements guide. They include structured and blind sifting, independent reviewer scoring, separation of diversity monitoring data from hiring decisions, accessible candidate and staff journeys, recruitment administration, reporting and export of records. Oak also wishes to explore HRIS needs and the transfer of new-starter information between systems. These are working needs, not final tender requirements or evaluation criteria. Oak welcomes different ways of achieving the outcomes. Suppliers are invited to respond by 20th October 2026 by email to procurement@thenational.academy. Please state: Whether you offer an ATS, an HRIS, or both, and whether each is an established product or requires development. Indicative three-year costs for the ATS and HRIS separately, including implementation, migration, integrations, licences, support and optional modules. These figures are for planning and will not be scored. Availability for demonstrations to our team Oak expects to hold live demonstrations or discussions during October 2026 with potential suppliers. It may use separate ATS and HRIS scenarios so suppliers offering only one system can participate meaningfully. All interested suppliers may submit written input regardless of whether they receive a live session. The engagement will not be scored or used to select a preferred supplier. Participation is not required to bid for any subsequent contract and gives no supplier an advantage in that competition. Oak will record the engagement and make information relevant to preparing a bid available to the wider market, while protecting genuinely confidential supplier information. Oak currently expects to publish an ATS tender in late October/mid November 2026, but the timing, scope, procurement route and contract value will be reviewed following this engagement. This notice is not an invitation to tender and does not commit Oak to any particular procurement or award. Lot 1: .

sig_ea514f98d47fe9c1a57a.description:
The subject of the contract is the provision of service support for an economic information system. The support will include the following parts: 1. Microsoft Dynamics NAV (hereinafter “MD NAV”) updates within the Microsoft Enhancement Plan. 2. Service and updates for the economic information system, including all its add-ons. Helpdesk service provided via a web portal and development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements. The Contracting Authority has a valid MS BREP "Business Ready Enhancement Plan" (hereinafter “maintenance”) for MD NAV Acct number: 6100645 valid until 29.10.2026. The Contractor shall conclude a contract with the Contracting Authority for the further continuation of maintenance – Microsoft Enhancement Plan for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. The provision of the maintenance service shall include the right to use all higher versions, entitlement to service packs and updates, entitlement to support and a guarantee of compatibility with other Microsoft products released by Microsoft for use in the Czech Republic for Microsoft Dynamics NAV. The Contracting Authority requires that the price of this service be fixed for the entire duration of the contract. The contract will be concluded for a fixed term of 3 years from the date it becomes effective. The Contracting Authority requires the commencement of performance under the contract from 30. 10. 2026. Provided that the contractor commences performance according to the Contracting Authority's requirement by 30. 10. 2026, the contract will be concluded for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. In the event that the contract becomes effective after 30. 10. 2026, the contractor shall commence the provision of performance under the contract on the date the contract becomes effective, with performance being provided for a period of 3 years. All software solutions (within part 1) will be supplied and implemented in the On-Premise version.; and: Updates to extension modules The Contracting Authority uses extension modules supplied by Konica Minolta IT Solutions Czech a.s. The service includes: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions and updates of these modules for the duration of the contractual relationship. - ensuring such updates and modifications to the EIS that allow for the processing of financial, asset and other necessary data in the EIS in accordance with the legislative requirements of the Czech Republic that are binding on the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall carry out the necessary updates and modifications to the EIS in sufficient time so that they are implemented without serious acceptance reservations no later than 10 working days before the date on which the relevant legislative requirements enter into force and become binding on the Contracting Authority. In the event that the period between the publication of a legal regulation and the date of its entry into force is less than 30 days, and the contractor is unable to ensure the update and modification in advance, the deadline for delivery of the update shall be 30 days from the publication of this regulation. The contractor guarantees the flawless functionality of the reflected changes and simultaneously guarantees the flawless functionality of other system modules that were not affected by the changes made. In the event of identified defects and errors, the contractor undertakes to remove the discrepancies under the conditions stated in point b: Helpdesk Service. The contractor is obliged, when performing the public contract, to take such measures and act in such a way as to prevent the occurrence of damage. If the contractor causes damage to the Contracting Authority or other entities, the contractor is obliged to remove the damage without undue delay and, if this is not possible, to compensate for it financially. All costs associated with this shall be borne by the contractor. The choice of the method of compensation for damage belongs to the Contracting Authority if it is affected by the damage. The service does not include: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions of the Travel Orders module and updates to the Travel Orders module for the duration of the contractual relationship. b: Helpdesk Service The service consists of resolving service requests, complaints about products and services supplied as part of previous performance reported using the web portal. The web portal for reporting service requests must be available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The service response to service requests must be ensured according to the priorities listed below. In the event of technical difficulties, there must be an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The following priorities are set for submitting service requests: 1. Emergency – The EIS is unusable in its basic functions. This state may threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of five working days. 2. High – Some EIS functions work in a limited manner, but this limitation cannot be considered as one that could threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of two weeks. 3. Standard – There is no danger of direct threat to the operational activity of the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall contractually undertake to commence the resolution of a service request with a given priority and resolve it as follows: 1. Emergency – within 5 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request with an expected resolution date as soon as possible, no later than 24 hours from the notification of the service request. The contractor shall ensure the resolution of the request even during non-working days (i.e. Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays). 2. High – within 24 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than the next working day, and resolve within 5 working days from the notification of the operational problem 3. Standard – within 48 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than within 1 week, and resolve within 2 weeks from the notification of the operational problem. Resolution of a request means: - resolution of the reported (recorded) request or - provision of another acceptable solution or - proposal of an acceptable alternative solution or - provision of instructions for an alternative solution, which, however, does not have to be accepted by the Contracting Authority as a sufficient solution - forwarding the problem for resolution to a third party (e.g. Microsoft, HW supplier, etc.) in the event of a problem caused by the incorrect behaviour of a component supplied or supported by a third party c: Development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensuring compliance with legislation The service consists of drawing on a guaranteed range of hours at a set hourly rate excluding VAT.

The minimum required guaranteed range is set at 10 hours per month. The basis for invoicing will be the hours actually realised and not the guaranteed capacity. The contractor must guarantee the availability of the above-mentioned service in the range of at least 10 hours per month (with the understanding that this indicative range is also set for the purposes of evaluating tenders). However, the Contracting Authority will draw according to its current needs and does not have to use up all the guaranteed hours. At the same time, it may also exceed the number of hours. The contractor will invoice the service based on the actual number of hours consumed, based on the set hourly rate. Requests are submitted via the web portal, where all communication takes place – proposal of the request solution, schedule, determination of labour intensity, price and ordering, or rejection. At the same time, the web portal will send confirmation emails to selected email addresses of the Contracting Authority regarding the entry and status of the request resolution upon every saved change. In the event of technical difficulties, there is an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The service can also be used for consultation visits by a contractor's employee with the aim of providing expert consultations for resolving requests at the Contracting Authority's workplace. It can also be used for the implementation of new versions of updates, upgrades or builds of Microsoft Dynamics NAV application equipment and extension modules with regard to legislative changes. All software solutions (within part 2 of the public contract) will be supplied and implemented in the on-premises version.

sig_ea971947a93b5580d449.description: MARKET CONSULTATION The subject of the market consultation is the procurement of a maintenance operations management system for the tracks of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The most central task of the operations management system is to support day-to-day maintenance management by offering various functionalities for equipment and work management ranging from work planning to work reporting, as well as enabling various tracking functions, for example with regard to accumulated work and costs. Another key factor for the system is to support information-driven management, i.e., to provide, inter alia, up-to-date information on maintenance activities carried out on assets and the resulting costs, as well as potential consequential effects over the entire lifecycle of the equipment. The system's functionalities should offer the target organisation the opportunity to implement maintenance operations characteristic of its operations in a process-driven manner, such that the system supports the execution of the process at different stages of the process, in accordance with the functionalities required of it. The efficient implementation of maintenance processes, ensuring both personnel and information security, requires strong support from the operations management system with which operations are managed and monitored. The operations management system should provide an open interface for the target organisation to monitor and manage maintenance operations between different stakeholders, such as in situations where maintenance is procured either partially or entirely as a service. In addition to the primary functionalities of maintenance management, the operations management system should cover a wide range of various functionalities supporting operations. The functionalities of the system can be roughly classified as follows: - Equipment management - Work management - Reports and analysis - Mobile application - User management - Cost tracking - Contract management - Inventory management - Procurement The task of the operations management system is to act in connection with day-to-day maintenance management as part of the broader system architecture of Väylävirasto. For this reason, various integrations with other operational and administrative systems of Väylävirasto will also be necessary. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for carrying out the market consultation and procurement is: - Market consultation, technical dialogue (commenting on material) September-October 2025 - Market consultation, bilateral negotiations (approx. 3-6 companies) October-early November 2025 - Year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market consultation, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure, nor does it prevent participation if the supplier has not participated in the dialogue. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE AND BILATERAL DISCUSSIONS The market consultation is organised in two phases: 1. As a technical dialogue, where potential suppliers are asked to familiarise themselves with the service description and requirement specification and to answer the contracting authority's preliminary questions (carried out in September-October by email in accordance with registrations) 2. As bilateral discussions, where the contracting authority invites 3-6 suppliers to discussions. The contracting authority will send invitations to the discussions to the selected suppliers as soon as possible. The discussions will take place during October-November 2025 (the following times are preliminarily reserved, participants are requested to reserve the times in their calendars where possible): - Mon 27.10 at 9.30-11 - Mon 27.10 at 14-15.30 - Wed 29.10 at 14.30-16 - Fri 31.10 at 12-13.30 - Mon 3.11 at 14-15.30 - Wed 5.11 at 12-13.30 The times will be confirmed to the suppliers selected for the bilateral negotiations approximately two weeks before the time. In addition to the above, the contracting authority reserves the right for a later scheduled commenting period on draft versions of the final tender documentation and for answering the contracting authority's new questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. sig_eaa77f55c684bb03b0d6.description: ThisSources Sought results will assist the Air Force in determining whether this solicitation will be unrestricted competition or a small business set-aside for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to fulfill Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) requirements. The Government is assessing the capability of companies that may possess the expertise to competently and competitively respond to the following requirements for the JSE program: For the JSE Program, the contractor shall possess the capabilities to fulfill 1) development, integration, and testing of modeling and simulation capabilities and 2) operations and product support functions at designated JSE test and training sites. The JSE Program is planning for two major training sites: Joint Integrated Test and Training Center–Nellis AFB, NV (JITTC-N) and Joint Integrated Test and Training Center–Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, AK (JITTC-E). The Air Force is considering a third site in the European theatre. Additional sites may be included as part of this solicitation. These sites will contain most, if not all, of the following: Multiple training systems (JSE-compliant and non-JSE-compliant) developed by other airborne platform program offices and their Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) Many supporting COTS software and hardware components Server rooms hosting JSE software components along with the cockpits support racks associated with the training systems Secure audio/visual distribution systems for mission brief and debrief Secure networks supporting Secret/Collateral, TS/SCI, and SAP information System integration labs supporting JSE development, integration and testing The IDIQ contract will commence within the 4th Quarter of CY27 with a 10-year period of performance. The first task order will be awarded 1st Quarter of CY28 to support JITTC-N including up to a 6-month transition period with the incumbent contractor. The Government anticipates the contract period of performance to be a minimum of a 1-year base period with up to nine 1-year option periods. Further questions may be e-mailed to Contract Specialist Matthew Mercer, matthew.mercer.5@us.af.mil, Contract Specialist James Floyd, james.floyd.23@us.af.mil and Logistics Management Specialist, gregory.zele@us.af.mil. Responses must be submitted via email to Contract Specialist Matthew Mercer, matthew.mercer.5@us.af.mil, and Contract Specialist James Floyd, james.floyd.23@us.af.mil and are due NLT 11:59 PM EST, 15 October 2026. The Government may converse with respondents regarding this RFI. Such conversations are solely intended to clarify potential capability to perform the requirements.

sig_eacfc6b17d3a95346823.description: Processing of evaluations of projects or calls financed from the European Social Fund. Evaluations are systematic and objective assessments of ongoing or completed projects, programmes or policies, their design, implementation and results. The aim is to determine relevance and the fulfilment of objectives, and to assess developmental effectiveness, impact and sustainability. It is a process of determining the importance or significance of a certain activity, policy or programme/project. Within the framework of the dynamic purchasing system (DNS), process, impact or strategic evaluations will be carried out. Process evaluations assess the implementation process of a programme or intervention, focus on ongoing processes and their aim is recommendations for better process design. Impact evaluations assess the achievement of planned effects/impacts/results. Most frequently using counterfactual impact evaluation (CIE type) based on statistical methods or in the form of theory-based evaluation (TBIE type) using the theory of change method and case studies. Strategic evaluations assess the design, achievement of strategic objectives and the contribution to their achievement at the level of the entire operational programme. They do not focus on partial interventions, but evaluate the programme as a whole with regard to the dominant themes of the operational programme in relation to the strategic objectives.
sig_eacfc6b17d3a95346823.title: DYNAMIC PURCHASING SYSTEM FOR STANDARD EVALUATIONS AND DATA COLLECTION II (Category 1 – Evaluation)

sig_eae491b0e106c8546621.description: We invite you to submit your response to this market dialogue concerning the procurement of expert services in human capacity management. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a potential competitive tendering procedure. The purpose of the market dialogue is to ensure that the preparers of the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. Through this market dialogue, we wish to survey tenderers' views on the subject of the procurement, the requirements concerning experts, and the contract terms. Istekki Oy is procuring expert services in human capacity management to complement its own expertise in the development of human capacity planning, forecasting, resourcing, competence management, and related operating models and system solutions. The objective of human capacity management is to ensure that the competence and resources available to the organisation are allocated to the right tasks at the right time in accordance with both current and future customer needs. The expert services will support the operations of the Service Delivery Unit, the development of operating models, proactive capacity management, and the efficient and transparent utilisation of resources across the entire organisation. The subject of the procurement is a human capacity management expert service, which covers tasks related to the development, implementation, and operational and tactical support of capacity management. The service will be delivered as expert work and will be implemented primarily as assignment-specific work orders within the framework of a framework agreement. The service may include both development-oriented consultancy and practical operational support. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING. The market dialogue will be conducted in writing as the commenting of draft materials. Attached to this notice are the draft tender documents as well as detailed instructions for responding to the dialogue. Tenderers are requested to submit their comments on the dialogue notice by uploading their response in accordance with the instructions given in the notice by the deadline. Responses will be treated confidentially. Please submit your response by the deadline. We hope that responses will be submitted in accordance with the instructions with an attachment in Finnish to ensure that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you may also enclose Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your response. All responses received will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they form an important part of understanding the whole. Please note that the information, content descriptions, and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are preliminary and indicative only. Final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: If the Contracting Authority deems it necessary, it may, following the technical market dialogue, hold market dialogue sessions held via remote connection with the responding tenderers. If market dialogue sessions are held, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the sessions of the more detailed schedules and the Teams meeting link at a later date. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tender contest may also be left unorganised. No separate remuneration will be paid for responding or for participating in possible presentation sessions. We would like to mention once again that this concerns a notice of a market dialogue, not a prior information notice, a contract notice, or an invitation to tender. The purpose is to familiarise ourselves with the market situation and to gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the future tendering procedure. Responding is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a potential tender contest nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tender contest. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us to build the future tender contest into as functional and clear a whole as possible. The notice of dialogue concerns all procurement procedures relating to the procurements described in the notice. In the same procurement, it may be necessary to carry out several procurement procedures, for example if the procurement procedure has to be discontinued.
sig_eae491b0e106c8546621.title: Market dialogue for the procurement of expert work in human capacity management

sig_eaf4d9d6a3452b1f0a3d.description: The CITT, supported by the ATSSC, is seeking information from vendors regarding commercially available solutions that could support the administration of questionnaires used by the Trade Remedies Investigations Branch (TRIB). TRIB's questionnaire process is a critical component of trade remedy investigations and includes the development, publication, distribution, collection, validation, management, analysis, and reporting of questionnaire data. The process involves collecting information from Canadian and international stakeholders and requires the secure handling of sensitive information (Protected B) throughout its lifecycle. Protected B is the federal level of security that applies to information and assets that, if compromised, could cause serious injury to an individual, organization, or government. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information on available solutions that can provide a secure, web-based platform for questionnaire management and respondent engagement. The ATSSC is interested in understanding the capabilities, functionality, implementation considerations, security controls, and hosting models available in the marketplace. The desired Online Platform would support the design and management of complex questionnaires, secure respondent access, data collection and storage, reporting and analytics, workflow automation, and e-mail management. The Online Platform must support both internal and external users and provide functionality that promotes efficiency, usability, accessibility, and data integrity. Given the sensitive nature of the information collected by the CITT, the solution must be capable of meeting Government of Canada security requirements, including the protection of Protected B information, data residency within Canada, robust access controls, audit logging, and compliance with applicable Government of Canada cloud and security standards.
sig_eaf4d9d6a3452b1f0a3d.title: Online Questionnaire Management Platform

sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.description: The Integrated Rhine Programme (IRP) is a project of the State of Baden-Württemberg (BW) which comprises a total of 13 flood retention basins (FRBs) in various planning and implementation stages on former floodplains between Basel and Mannheim. The IRP specialist information system (FIS IRP) is to be developed as a central repository of the IRP for the safeguarding of relevant data. The project management and consultancy for the client (CA) for this IT project are being commissioned. The services to be provided in this context include the division of the IT project into realistic, economical implementation stages, cost estimates, the preparation of tender documents, in particular the specification of requirements and the acceptance catalogue, for the programming or development of the FIS IRP, the professional and technical support of the CA in procurement processes, and project management during implementation and programming. An optional contract is to be awarded: as a mandatory service, the contractor (CO) is to support the first implementation stage in the development of the FIS IRP; support for further implementation stages is aimed for (options). Table 1 within the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents) provides an overview of the services to be provided by the contractor with the timeframe envisaged by the CA. Included services mainly comprise, but are not limited to, the preparation of the tender for the programming of the FIS IRP for the 1 implementation stage (with a focus on the creation of the specification of requirements, in which requirements from later implementation stages or the overall project must also be taken into account), the professional and technical support of the CA in the procurement process, and project management during implementation and programming. In the further course of the project, the commissioning of comparable services for the support of further implementation stages is aimed for (optional contract). More detailed provisions on the provision of services can be found in the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents). The final specification of requirements will be submitted to the successful applicants with the invitation to submit a tender. The FIS IRP is planned as a modular specialist information system with the modules "Operating Data", "Ecology", "Groundwater and Surface Water Models", "Groundwater and Surface Water Data", and "Structures". The FIS IRP is intended to secure the data long-term, make it available for display (including viewing in a geospatial data viewer) and enable cross-cutting evaluation of the data across the entire IRP. The CA has described the FIS IRP with its modules in technical concepts in which the precise contents, functionalities and general technical requirements for the FIS are formulated without specifying particular software or a development environment. The procurement documents contain a brief description of the technical concept (Annex 2). For individual modules, local database applications or data repositories in the form of medium-term implementation solutions have already been created. The applications must be further developed, also for integration into the specialist information system. In the phased development of the FIS IRP planned for the future, the initial focus is on the integration of dynamic factual data, i.e. operating and monitoring data, as well as the development of the geospatial data viewer.
sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.title: IT consultancy and project management in the development of the Integrated Rhine Programme specialist information system (FIS IRP)

sig_eb00a26b898ea1e792a0.description: The Neue Wege Kreis Bergstraße Job Centre is an internal municipal enterprise of the Bergstraße district. It runs the municipal funding project KI_Hub Kommunal for the district, which is funded with state funds under the Starke Heimat Hessen funding programme. KI_Hub Kommunal is a collaborative project involving municipal job centres and K4K eG as the implementation partner. Within the framework of the "KI_Hub Kommunal" project, an inter-municipal community of municipal organisations, in particular municipal job centres, is supported in the systematic development of competencies in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The project community comprises several municipal sponsors who, under the lead management of the Neue Wege municipal job centre, jointly establish standards, structures and qualification offers for dealing with AI. With the increasing spread of AI applications in administrative and advisory work, there is a significant need for qualifications across the board for staff. At the same time, Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ("EU AI Regulation" or "EU AI Act") gives rise to specific obligations for the participating organisations to ensure an appropriate level of AI competence among their employees. The aim of the procurement is to build a sustainable, jointly usable qualification architecture consisting of a central AI competence platform as well as basic and advanced qualification courses based on it. The solution must be scalable, compliant with data protection laws and sustainable beyond the project duration, and make an effective contribution to fulfilling the AI competence obligation pursuant to Art. 4 of the EU AI Regulation. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an AI competence platform as well as implementation of basic AI and advanced AI qualifications. The subject matter of the contract is the provision and operation of an AI competence platform as well as the implementation of qualification offers based on it over an operational period of 6,5 months. The service comprises the following three coordinated components: 1.AI competence platform: Provision of a multi-tenant SaaS learning platform as the technical basis for the qualification offers 2. Basic AI qualification: On-demand learning programme to build broad basic AI competencies, including the mandatory part pursuant to Art. 4 of the EU AI Regulation 3. Advanced AI qualification: Moderated online workshops for in-depth competence development with a knowledge database and community approach. The three components are to be provided as an overall service ("from a single source"). The AI competence platform provides the technical basis on which both the basic and advanced qualifications are provided, used and administered.
sig_eb00a26b898ea1e792a0.title: Provision of an AI competence platform and implementation of basic and advanced AI qualifications

sig_eb0c64af8591e624f4b1.description: IT services are being awarded successively in six lots. This case concerns only the services for Lot 2 - Maintenance and further development of the central GEO specialist applications for Hessian agricultural support. Essential components are the area administration (FIG) as a legally binding reference system, the satellite-based area monitoring (AMS) for the automated control of grant applications, as well as mobile applications for farmers (HeLaWi-App) and inspection services (HeKTAR). The service provider is responsible for the integration of geodata, the analysis of satellite images, and ensuring the EU conformity and technical future-proofing of the systems. All services are to be provided on the basis of a framework agreement and therefore only upon separate call-off/individual order. The Wirtschafts- und Infrastrukturbank Hessen (WIBank) acts as the EU-accredited paying agency for agricultural support in Hesse. The WIBank is part of the Landesbank Hessen – Thüringen (Helaba). The provision and operation of the specialised IT systems necessary for agricultural support are the responsibility of Helaba. Helaba has currently awarded the IT services for agricultural support to a general contractor. The contract with this general contractor ends on 31.12.2026. Therefore, the IT services are being re-tendered. As part of these tenders, there is a change from the current general contractor model to a multi-provider model. The services previously provided centrally by the general contractor are being divided and tendered competitively in succession via six technically defined lots. The IT systems for agricultural support are based on a highly integrated architecture, which necessitates technical and functional dependencies between the six lots. As part of the transition from a general contractor to a multi-provider model, it is therefore mandatory that the service providers for each lot do not act in isolation, but become part of an integrated IT ecosystem. This case concerns only the services for Lot 2 - Maintenance and further development of the central GEO specialist applications for Hessian agricultural support. Essential components are the area administration (FIG) as a legally binding reference system, the satellite-based area monitoring (AMS) for the automated control of grant applications, as well as mobile applications for farmers (HeLaWi-App) and inspection services (HeKTAR). The service provider is responsible for the integration of geodata, the analysis of satellite images, and ensuring the EU conformity and technical future-proofing of the systems. All services are to be provided on the basis of a framework agreement and therefore only upon separate call-off/individual order. For further details, please refer to Appendix I 02 - Appendix 0_Service Description.

sig_eb4026cf7a780823f3e4.description: Pre-Market Engagement (PME) Background Thames valley Police (TVP) is the largest non-metropolitan police force in the country and polices the counties of Oxfordshire, Berkshire and Buckinghamshire. It also provides services to a number of other forces under collaborative arrangements. The force employs nearly 10,000 officers and staff. TVP, like so many organisations, is looking to improve the quality and efficiency of the services that the People and Financial Directorates and the Tasking & Resilience department (our Enabling Services) provide to the Force and their wider stakeholder requirements. The Enabling Services are therefore looking to transform the quality of the services it provides in terms of ensuring an excellent customer experience whilst also creating much greater insights to allow the Force to make better decisions. This is all against the backdrop of needing to reduce non-value-added costs and so deliver cashable savings to the Force. The Force are looking to appoint by competitive process a strategic partner who can ensure we use our current systems to deliver on our ambitions. Work to date has identified 3 essential first stage requirements. • the implementation of a Transactional service centre • Experience in building change programmes alongside the implementation of an integrated IT solution incorporating ITSM, CRM (incl CMDM) and Agentic AI and a single customer front end portal. • The ability for improved decision making by ensuring that there is appropriate and accurate data/information available at the time required in a format to support decision makers. • We are looking to appoint a strategic partner capable of delivering not just short-term change but to change the capabilities and culture of the organisation to ensure that continuous improvement becomes a core skill. This will mean that the Force's Enabling Services can manage change as an evolutionary internal process and not need to engage external consultancy support in the future. This will include a set of clear and achievable recommendations as to changes in the structure and delivery mechanisms for change management process and management within the Force. Customer focus and Data maturity sit alongside efficiency. Followed by a Stage 2 Data Integration (this will be based upon the CMDB integration system. Budget for the entire project across all phases will be in the region of £4m-£5m. Lot 1: .

sig_eb564d5b5041d9e3dbef.description: The Authority is procuring a TCN Supplier in each regional Lot to deliver the Theory Test Centre Network (TCN) Service, providing secure and accessible front end test delivery for all theory test types across Great Britain and Northern Ireland. DVSA are procuring, and contracting for, the service on behalf of the Driver and Vehicle Agency (DVA) in Northern Ireland. The Service must deliver a fully compliant Test Centre estate that meets the Authority’s 40/40 accessibility requirement, ensuring all Candidates are located within 40 minutes (urban) or 40 miles (rural) of a test centre in each region. In Northern Ireland, mandatory test centre provision is required in Ballymena, Belfast, Londonderry, Omagh, Portadown and Newry. All proposed sites will require Authority approval during implementation. The TCN Supplier will be responsible for providing a responsive scheduling system offering a real time, six month forward view of test availability to the Authority’s booking systems, reflecting test duration, demand and test type requirements. The Service includes delivery of on-site invigilation to maintain test integrity; detection and deterrence of fraud; and support for incident reporting and investigative activity integrating with Authority systems. The TCN Supplier must provide all necessary infrastructure and technology within each test centre, including secure hardware and software, on premises server capability, resilient network connectivity, CCTV, and sufficient equipment to deliver all standard and non-standard test adjustments for candidates with additional needs. The Service must support Welsh language options, voiceovers, British Sign Language (BSL), and—where applicable—additional language voiceovers in Northern Ireland. TCN Suppliers must also deliver approved Non Standard Adjustments including extra time, separate testing rooms, adapted equipment, signers, interpreters, language modifiers, readers, recorders, audio requirements (NI only), and home testing (not remote proctoring) where authorised. Multi client test sites are permitted provided they do not impede delivery of the Authority’s requirements and only with Authority approval. The TCN Service excludes delivery of tests in In House Theory Test Centres (IHTTCs). Further details of the scope are contained in the procurement documents (which include the draft contract), which are available on the Jaggaer portal. Lotting: The TCN Service is packaged into three regional Lots of broadly equivalent historic and forecast test volumes based on Government Office Region geographies: • Region 1: includes the Government Office Regions of Scotland, North East, North West, Yorkshire and the Humber and Northern Ireland. • Region 2: includes the Government Office Regions of Wales, West Midlands, South East and South West. • Region 3: includes the Government Office Regions of East Midlands, East of England and London. The Authority is seeking to appoint a different TCN Supplier in each regional Lot at contract award stage to develop a more diversified supply base. However, there is no limit on the number of Lots that a supplier can bid for. In certain circumstances, where defined objective eligibility and value for money criteria are met, a supplier may be awarded a maximum of two regional Lots, while a one-Lot cap applies where such criteria are not met. The detail of this is set out in the contract award mechanism in the procurement documents. Additional Services: The Authority has identified several potential future developments that may be explored through the regional contracts and in the delivery of the TCN Service. These Additional Services fall within the overall scope of the contract and may, where required, be implemented through the contract’s change control procedure. The Authority is therefore clearly signalling these areas to the market at this stage, and further detail is available in the procurement documents. The Additional Services are: • Exploring remote testing/proctoring technology in the delivery of the Service. • Exploring the use of end‐to‐end cloud architecture in the delivery of the Service. • Adding other Authority or Department for Transport tests into Service delivery. • Adding wider government tests into Service delivery. • Enabling validation of Digital Driving Licences. • Enhanced identification checking. sig_eb61ca0ca61928edf1ab.description: The subject of this public service contract is the provision of specialised expert activities related to the implementation of the project "IoT MeterNet: Advanced Metering Infrastructure I", financed by the Technology and Applications for Competitiveness Operational Programme (TAC OP), Call Applications - Call III - DEEP TECH. The contract is divided into parts. The subjects of the individual parts of the public contract are defined below. The subject of performance of part 1 of the public contract is the provision of expert services in the field of IoT applications and cloud solutions within the project "IoT MeterNet: Advanced Metering Infrastructure I". Performance includes in particular technical cooperation in the design, configuration, integration and verification of an IoT solution based on a cloud platform for the management and data handling of end devices. The supplier will provide expert activities in the hardware, communication and integration layers of the system, including the implementation of IoT communication, connectivity and data interfaces. Part of the performance is participation in the development and testing of functional samples, prototypes and their verification in actual operation, including the provision of technical documentation and cooperation during the implementation of the project. Services will be provided in the form of long-term capacity cooperation during the implementation of the project.; The subject of performance of part 3 of the public contract is the provision of expert services in the field of support for the IoT network platform and IoT application superstructure within the project "IoT MeterNet: Advanced Metering Infrastructure I". Performance includes in particular technical support, configuration and administration of the communication infrastructure, data flows and secure data exchange between individual system components. It further includes the administration of the application layer for data analysis, historisation and visualisation, configuration of the user environment and development of scripts for process automation. Part of the performance is also the design, implementation and maintenance of API interfaces, ensuring secure communication (e.g. MQTT, TLS), high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR), including system performance monitoring and optimisation. Services will be provided in the form of long-term capacity cooperation during the implementation of the project.; The subject of performance of part 2 of the public contract is the provision of expert services in the field of administration of MQTT communication protocols, design and operation of API interfaces and provision of the cloud infrastructure of the project "IoT MeterNet: Advanced Metering Infrastructure I". Performance includes in particular the design, implementation and administration of MQTT brokers, securing data communication, optimisation of data transfer and access management. It further includes architectural supervision of API interfaces, their documentation in the OpenAPI standard, automation of development and deployment of application layers and integration with external systems. Part of the performance is likewise support for the operation of the cloud infrastructure, ensuring high availability (HA), disaster recovery (DR) solutions, monitoring and system scaling. Services will be provided in the form of long-term capacity cooperation during the implementation of the project.

sig_eb7acd20aebf08c95f72.description: It is the intention to award a contract using the Most Suitable Provider (MSP) process under the Provider Selection Regime for the provision of NHS Talking Therapies British Sign Language (BSL). If you wish to be considered as a potential provider and can meet the mandatory requirements with the ability to deliver the required services stated in Section II.2.4, please email hertsjct@nhs.net by no later than 12pm on Monday 23rd March 2026 Lot 1: . Service Overview: To support up to 21 Deaf Hertfordshire residents for 2025/26, and expected to support 16 Deaf Hertfordshire residents for 26/27 with British Sign Language (BSL) NHS Talking Therapies. These figures are based on the expectation that the 25/26 funding can be accrued at year-end. If the accrual is not possible, the stated numbers may require a minor adjustment. The Provider must deliver both face‐to‐face and online sessions based on Service User need, ensuring confidential clinical space and suitably trained practitioners. Quality and KPIs: The Service must comply with the NHS Talking Therapies Manual and NICE guidance, including stepped-care delivery, appropriate session dosage, accredited clinicians, and provision of BSL-accessible digital self‐help tools to support post‐discharge recovery. Monthly KPI monitoring by IHCCT will require: - At least 48% reliable improvement - At least 67% reliable recovery - 75% starting treatment within 6 weeks - 95% starting treatment within 18 weeks NICE and NHS TT Compliance: The Service must fully align with NICE Depression in Adults Guideline NG222, ensuring accessible and culturally competent assessment and treatment for Deaf BSL users. This includes comprehensive assessments, adapted outcome measures, equitable access and delivery of Counselling for Depression, CBT‐based guided self‐help, behavioural activation and relapse‐prevention in BSL. Treatment must involve shared decision‐making and meet the same quality standards as for hearing populations. The Service must also comply with the NHS Talking Therapies Manual (v7, 2024) requirements for evidence‐based interventions, accredited practitioners, appropriate supervision and mandatory session‐by‐session outcomes. Digital tools must be secure, clinically appropriate and fully BSL-accessible. Therapeutic Interventions: The Provider must offer: facilitated cCBT, Step 2 PWP interventions, High‐Intensity CBT, Counselling for Depression, EMDR, IPT and Counselling for Couples. Expected delivery includes an average of 6 sessions at Step 2 and 12 sessions at Step 3, with caseload split approximately 65-70% Step 2 and 30-35% Step 3. Workforce Requirements: The workforce must be accredited, have full safeguarding governance, be able to deliver BSL Talking Therapies and accept both self‐referrals and professional referrals. Therapists must be fluent BSL users (minimum CACDP Level 6). Required professional registrations include BACP, UKCP, BPC, BABCP, PWP accreditation, postgraduate Low‐Intensity CBT qualifications or Master's‐level CBT training. Staffing must include approximately 4 FTE Step 2 and 4 FTE Step 3 practitioners, plus a designated Contract Lead and senior clinical oversight. Experience and Compliance: Providers must demonstrate experience delivering NICE‐concordant BSL Talking Therapies, stepped care, use of accredited workforce, NHS Digital dataset submissions, pathway integration and provision of BSL digital self‐help tools. Additional evidence may be requested. Data Requirements: The Provider must complete monthly NHS Talking Therapies dataset submissions to NHS Digital, maintain secure IT systems for outcomes reporting and ensure routine outcomes inform clinical supervision and quality improvement. Required data includes referral numbers, waiting times, numbers entering/completing treatment, recovery and improvement outcomes, DNAs, incidents, complaints, demographic information, PEQ feedback, session totals and all clinical outcome measures. Monthly local reporting to commissioners is mandatory. Governance and Safety: The Provider must maintain safe‐recruitment processes including enhanced DBS checks, registration and qualification verification and right‐to‐work checks. Clinical supervision must comply with the NHS Talking Therapies Manual, UCL Supervision Standards and the Supervision Competency Framework. All therapists must be fluent BSL users (minimum CACDP Level 6 or equivalent). Economic & Financial Standing: Capacity to deliver block funded activity . Monthly payments tied to delivery evidence. Ability to notify commissioners if demand exceeds capacity. Turnover (or income) of at least two times the annual contact value (£34,013) which is £68,026. Where the Tenderer is a profit-making organisation, that the Tenderer has gross profit / turnover ratio of at least 10%.Where the Tenderer is a non-profit making/charitable organisation, that the Tenderer has an operating surplus greater than 0%, and where this is not the case, that any reported deficit is either a planned deficit, or fully explained in the accounts. The Tenderer has a minimum liquidity ratio of 1.00. Where the Tenderer is a non-profit making/charitable organisation, that the Tenderer has unrestricted reserves equivalent to six (6) months' operating costs for the Service, which is £22,321. There should be an unqualified audit opinion. Dun & Bradstreet risk of low, low-moderate or moderate Technical & Professional Ability - Must Have Experience Providing NICE concordant Talking Therapies in BSL, stepped care delivery, accredited clinicians, dataset submission to NHS Digital, strong interdependencies across pathways, provision of digital BSL self help tools. Assessment will be based on the following Key Criteria: Quality and innovation - 35% Value - 15% Integration, collaboration and service sustainability - 20% Improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice - 20% Social value - 10% We may ask for further information from the provider to support any of the above requirements.

sig_ebb35b40775cd223c4c1.description:
The Leibniz Institute for Analytical Sciences -ISAS- e.V. intends to procure an automated, modularly expandable and flexible liquid handling system (pipetting robot) in order to reduce pre-analytical variability, standardise the processing of clinical samples and enable scalable, traceable processing of larger sample numbers. Lot PAR-0001: Automated, modularly expandable and flexible liquid handling system (pipetting robot). The quality of the resulting data depends significantly on standardised pre-analytical processing of the plasma samples. Even minor differences in pipetting volumes, mixing, incubation times, temperature control, order of processing or sample mix-ups can cause systematic distortions. This applies in particular to highly sensitive mass spectrometric methods such as LC-MS/MS-based lipidomics and metabolomics as well as to proteomic workflows. The liquid handling system to be procured is intended to be used both for research and development of new or adapted methods for sample preparation and analysis and for the standardised execution of already established procedures. While established workflows require high process reliability, reproducibility, parallelisability and reliable scalability, method development requires flexible adaptation of sample formats, volumes, reagents, pipetting parameters, incubation conditions and process steps. The liquid handling system to be used must therefore possess increased technical and workflow-related flexibility in order to map different requirements within one platform and to be able to transfer newly developed procedures directly into robust routine processes after successful validation. An automated, modularly expandable and flexible liquid handling system is therefore required to reduce pre-analytical variability, standardise the processing of clinical samples and enable scalable, traceable processing of larger sample numbers. A. Sustainability and system architecture The system must be designed as a highly integrated automation platform and have the smallest possible footprint, which cannot be expanded after the initial installation. At the same time, the platform must be designed in such a way that future technical expansions and the integration of additional functional units can be realised as far as possible within the existing system area. This is intended to ensure long-term use of the investment, flexible adaptation to future applications and efficient use of the available laboratory space. For the initial development of applications on the liquid handling system, the primary pipetting unit should enable air displacement pipetting with disposable tips in order to safely exclude sample-related carry-over and cross-contamination. At the same time, such a unit has low ongoing maintenance requirements. Furthermore, the platform should possess an additional pipetting unit with liquid displacement and washable fixed needles. This pipetting unit is intended to be able to process even demanding liquids precisely and reproducibly. At the same time, this should create the possibility of dispensing with disposable consumables for suitable applications and thus sustainably reduce consumption and operating costs. In conclusion, the combination of both pipetting units will enable cost-effective and sustainable operation of routine applications for widely developed applications. The automation platform must also have a sufficiently large work surface to be able to operate at least two sample preparation workflows simultaneously on the platform and to parallelise them independently of each other. For this, the highest possible capacity of usable work positions is required. In order to be able to efficiently parallelise different process steps and future multi-omics workflows and thereby increase sample throughput while simultaneously enabling cost-efficient work, the possibility of parallel operation of several independently controllable transport, pipetting and gripping operations is particularly required. A multi-arm architecture enables more efficient use of the platform, reduces waiting times between individual process steps and ultimately ensures better economic efficiency. B. Requirements for sample preparation and operation The system must support the use of common laboratory vessels and standardised microtitre plate formats and be able to manage these on the system side for the automated execution of the methods. Furthermore, the platform must be modularly configurable and retrofittable so that existing workflows can be adapted and future applications with changed requirements can be realised without a fundamental exchange of system components. For the planned multi-omics sample preparation procedures, the system must support both automated filtration and elution steps using overpressure (positive pressure filtration) and corresponding procedures for volume reduction under vacuum (evaporator). In particular, the processing of 96-well filter and SPE plates must be possible in an automated manner. These functions are required in order to be able to map different procedures for the purification, fractionation and enrichment of analytes in a common automation platform. To minimise sample-related carry-over and cross-contamination, the primary pipetting unit must be able to work with air displacement and disposable tips.

Furthermore, the system must possess suitable technical measures for the avoidance or early detection of unintentional contamination of the pipetting unit and other system components. This is particularly important when processing clinical samples, as a transfer of sample components between individual samples can influence the analytical results of subsequent multi-omics measurements. The platform must enable the integration of third-party devices (...)
sig_ebb35b40775cd223c4c1.title: Automated, modularly expandable and flexible liquid handling system (pipetting robot)

Respondents to the market survey will not be paid compensation for responding or for participating in potential presentation sessions. If a supplier's responses contain trade secrets during the market dialogue, the respondent must clearly mark the confidential documents with the marking TRADE SECRET both in the file title/name and in the document itself. Background In Finland, the development of artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare has been promoted within the national social and healthcare AI ecosystem, where DigiFinland acts as a key coordinating actor. Based on the artificial intelligence trials of wellbeing services counties carried out within the ecosystem, the most impactful use cases have been identified and experiences on their utilisation in practical customer and patient work have been gathered. Based on these results, use cases that are assessed to have good conditions for large-scale implementation have been prioritised. Real-time AI-assisted interpretation has been identified as one of these. DigiFinland, in cooperation with Sitra, is now launching a new implementation phase in which the deployment of solutions developed in the trials will be extended to wellbeing services counties. This market dialogue is part of this rollout work, and its aim is to survey AI-based interpretation solutions on the market and to form a comprehensive picture of the suitability of the solutions for use in social welfare and healthcare in Finland.
