sig_f045a19fc14bb5dea42a.description: Great Places seeks to develop a Customer mobile application to complement and extend the capabilities of the existing Customer Portal. This application will serve as a new digital channel for customers. It will enable customers to manage their housing-related services more conveniently from their mobile devices, including rent payments, repair requests and accessing documents. The eventual contract will cover the delivery of core self-service functionalities including: secure customer authentication; ability to view and update personal details and preferences; access to rent statements and arrears; raising, tracking and managing repair requests with appointment booking; submitting and updating Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) data; accessing documents from the document management system; secure two-way messaging and reminders; reporting anti-social behaviour and environmental issues; and providing feedback and survey responses. The solution must integrate in real-time with our existing systems, comply with accessibility standards (e.g. WCAG), and meet security and data protection requirements. The partner will be expected to provide implementation, integration, testing, training, and post go-live support services, with a roadmap for future enhancements to extend functionality beyond the MVP. sig_f062266fd021eb89e7f6.description: Tuomi Logistiikka Oy invites suppliers to a market survey on the procurement of a passenger transport group transport system. Attached to this market survey notice is a preliminary description of the procurement in which the Client has sought to highlight its needs and describe passenger transport processes and operations. Based on the responses received to the market survey, the Client will invite suppliers to follow-up discussions, market dialogues, to further refine the Client's needs and where the supplier can present its solution in more detail. The Client will decide at its own discretion which suppliers it will invite to the market dialogue. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the potential market, discuss the object of the procurement and its components, the criteria, procurement models, the upcoming contract period and the definition of the procurement, as well as other terms related to the tendering process. The Client emphasises that all documentation is preliminary and its requirements will be discussed as part of the market dialogue. The duration of the market dialogue is 120 min/supplier. The procurement schedule is tight, so market dialogues may be held already during the validity period of this notice. Attached is a planned schedule form showing the times reserved for the dialogues. Registrations are requested to be sent by lauri.tiainen@tuomi.fi. Answers are not to be submitted through the Tarjouspalvelu portal. The actual tendering process will likely be carried out as a competitive dialogue procedure in accordance with section 36 of the Public Procurement Act. Planned schedule Market dialogues: weeks 17-19 Publication of request to participate: June 2026 Negotiations: Autumn 2026 Final invitation to tender: November 2026 Procurement decision: December 2026 Implementation project: January 2027 First functions in production use: 1.4.2027 Actual production use: 1.6.2027 This is a notice of a market survey. This is not a prior information notice, procurement notice or invitation to tender. The actual invitation to tender for the procurement will be published later. Participation in the market survey does not bind either party. The contracting entity is not bound to carry out the procurement based on the market survey, and the descriptions or specifications presented in the market survey do not bind the client. No compensation is paid for participation in the market survey.

sig_f082bc94966f38f6acc5.description: 1. Introduction OsloBygg KF is considering to procure a digital service for condition based operational monitoring of technical installations in nurseries. The objective of the market survey is to gain better insight into the market and input from suppliers on what systems are available, what can be delivered and how such services can normally be introduced. The market survey is not a competition and the contracting authority is not requesting tenders at this point in time. Participation in the market survey gives no rights or advantages in any later procurement. 2. Provisional need The contracting authority would like input on digital systems that can monitor technical components in nurseries by using sensors, audio analysis, vibration analysis or other relevant measurement parameters. The analysis shall be carried out by KI or ML and it shall automatically alarm in the event of deviations and errors. The system is particularly relevant for: * ventilation aggregates * engines * Fans * Pumps * other relevant technical components The aim of any system is to uncover abnormal operations, errors or wear at an early stage, so that the contracting authority can carry out more targeted and preventive maintenance. The system ought to be able to contribute to better operational security, reduced energy consumption, fewer operational deviations and a better overview of the condition of the technical installations. 3. Input from the market The contracting authority would like general input from suppliers on: * what systems and technologies are available in the market * the types of technical installations and components that can be monitored * if the systems can be used on existing installations without comprehensive reconstruction * how notification, reporting and visualisation normally works * whether the systems can be integrated with MOM systems. * what gains and effects suppliers believe such solutions could provide
sig_f082bc94966f38f6acc5.title: Market survey (second call) - Condition based operational monitoring of technical installations in nurseries.

sig_f0892eef464b7e861342.description: Milton Keynes City Council (MKCC) ('The Council') is seeking to engage with suppliers in advance of a future procurement exercise for a cloud-based Regulatory and Operational Case Management Platform. The Council currently utilises a legacy case management solution across a range of services and is exploring replacement options that will support future service delivery, digital transformation, mobile working, data management and reporting requirements. The Council is seeking a modern Software as a Service (SaaS) solution capable of supporting multiple service areas through a shared platform and data model. Services anticipated to be within scope include: • Environmental Health • Environmental Crime • Trading Standards • Licensing • Private Sector Housing • Emergency Planning • Other related operational and regulatory functions The Council's preferred approach is a single corporate platform, although modular solutions from a single supplier may also be considered where they provide integrated functionality and a seamless user experience. The platform is expected to provide functionality including: • Case management • Inspection management • Investigation management • Licensing management • Enforcement management • Document and evidence management • Workflow and task management • Mobile working capability • Reporting and dashboard functionality • Information governance and retention management • Officer safety alerting • Integration with existing corporate systems • Data migration from an existing legacy system The Council is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers can support: • Cross-service working • Shared premises and entity records • Mobile and field-based operations • Cloud-first delivery models • Integration with GIS, LLPG and other corporate systems • Future use of automation and artificial intelligence • Flexible configuration without supplier dependency The Council intends to hold a supplier engagement session via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the event will be to: • Share the Council's objectives • Present high-level requirements • Understand market capability • Explore implementation approaches • Gather supplier feedback on proposed procurement routes and contract structures This market engagement exercise is intended solely to gather information and understand market capabilities. Milton Keynes City Council may, at its discretion, use or choose not to use any information received during this exercise when shaping future procurement requirements. This engagement is not an invitation to tender, a call for competition, or a commitment by the Council to undertake any procurement or award any contract. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately and conducted through an appropriate procurement process. Interested suppliers are invited to participate in a market engagement event where the Council will present its current position, emerging requirements and procurement approach. Date 21 October 2026 10am - 11am Via Microsoft Teams For any suppliers interested in this opportunity please visit our e-Tendering portal - https://in-tendhost.co.uk/milton-keynes/aspx/Home for booking form Lot 1: . None

sig_f0a1c6e22577e4434842.description: The subject of the public contract is the supplementation and expansion of the personnel and payroll information system software used by the contracting authority, named VEMA, manufactured by the company Seyfor, a. s., ID No.: 01572377, with its registered office at Drobného 555/49, Ponava, 602 00 Brno (hereinafter referred to as the "manufacturer"), with additional licences. The contracting authority currently has permanent licences purchased for VEMA software applications covering 700 processed personal numbers. The list and scope of the already supplied VEMA applications are set out in Annex No. 1 of the draft contract – Existing VEMA applications, which forms Annex C of this tender documentation. Specifically, the subject of the public contract is: 1) provision of regular annual (12-month) support for already operated (existing) VEMA applications, 2) provision of flexible licences allowing for the dynamic increase or decrease in the number of existing licences beyond the already purchased permanent VEMA application licences according to the current requirements of the contracting authority, - the number of currently used flexible licences can be changed every month, - the maximum monthly number of flexible licences is in the volume of 400 units, 3) provision of annual processing of remuneration in the MZDY application for the performance of public functions by members of advisory bodies (Expert Panels and Expert Body of Evaluators), who are granted remuneration based on a government decision, the amount of which is determined by the Chair of the Research, Development and Innovation Council. The proposal for remuneration for individual members of the Expert Panels is based on the active participation of members in the work of the given advisory body. According to § 35 paragraph 8 of Act No. 130/2002 Coll., on the support of research, experimental development and innovation from public funds and on the amendment of certain related acts (Act on the support of research, experimental development and innovation), as amended, membership in the expert and advisory bodies of the Council does not establish an employment relationship with the Czech Republic. Processing will take place for evaluators once a year in the scope of a maximum of 1200 processed personal numbers. 4) delivery, implementation, licences and support of new applications for the personnel and payroll information system VEMA already used by the contracting authority (The list of required new VEMA applications is set out in Annex No. 2 of the draft contract – Newly provided VEMA applications, which forms Annex C of this tender documentation), for each new application the following will be supplied: a)700 units of permanent licences for these new VEMA applications including support, b)a maximum of 400 units of flexible licences allowing for the dynamic increase or decrease in the number of currently used licences beyond the already purchased permanent VEMA application licences. - the provided licences (both permanent and monthly flexible licences) include the authorisation to exercise the right to use VEMA applications by the contracting authority to the same extent as existing licences, 5) provision of operational consultations - technical support for VEMA applications within a guaranteed response time to suggestions or requests from the user in order to ensure the normal functioning of VEMA applications (hereinafter referred to as "requests") related to the use of the applications, - within the scope of support, consultations are provided in the scope of 16 hours per month (unused hours are carried over to the next month), - application and system services provided to the user when resolving user requests for the operation of VEMA applications can be provided via remote access, 6) ongoing training for employees of the Personnel Department based on changes in legislation and the VEMA applications used, and any induction (introductory) training for new employees of the Personnel Department. 7) services outside the scope of service support provision: - proposals for product functions, development of the system at the user's site (e.g. connection to the contracting authority's used IS), products outside the scope of service support provision, writing or revision of own code, - delivery of integration of the VEMA IS to the Office of the Government's management dashboard including the provision of all described functions, testing and subsequent support after deployment into production operation (specification in Annex G of the TD). A detailed definition of the subject of the public contract, including technical conditions in the detail necessary for the preparation of the tender, is set out in the annexes to this tender documentation.

sig_f0ac37022977fd61c718.description:
The State of North Rhine-Westphalia, represented by the Ministerium für Heimat, Kommunales, Bau und Digitalisierung des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (MHKBD), wishes to procure an electronic records management system (E-Akte) and the associated change management for electronic administrative work. Looking ahead, approx. 250 authorities with approx. 90.000 users are to work productively with the E-Akte in the target state. The aim of this call for competition is a future-proof and efficient E-Akte that meets the current and future requirements of the North Rhine-Westphalia state administration. The E-Akte must help to optimise workflows, improve collaboration and ensure compliance with statutory regulations on digital records management. The State of North Rhine-Westphalia currently uses the nscale E-Akte system with the nscale eGov module from Ceyoniq Technology GmbH. The call for competition covers the provision and further development of the necessary software, implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure, as well as support services (third-level support). The call for competition also covers product-related services for knowledge transfer, training and introduction support for the E-Akte. The subject matter of this call for competition is the procurement, maintenance and further development of an E-Akte product, including its implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure and the associated support services. In connection with this, the contracting authority is tendering product-related services for knowledge transfer, training and introduction support for the E-Akte. The contracting authority understands an E-Akte to be a digital system that makes it possible to save, manage and archive documents digitally and centrally within files and cases. The software is installed in the infrastructure of the North Rhine-Westphalia state administration (e.g. IT.NRW, North Rhine-Westphalia Police). The contracting authority operates the E-Akte with the assistance of the contractor. The E-Akte must guarantee pure on-premises operation without an internet connection and without restriction of the core functionality, as well as operation across multiple fire compartments (failover) and remote data centres (geo-redundancy over min. 100 km) in the backend. The E-Akte must guarantee uninterrupted operation (24/7, except for maintenance windows) and availability of at least 99,9 % per calendar year. The system must run with high performance as a multi-tenant system with at least 25 tenants and at least 25.000 users per system, and must be horizontally scalable, load-balancing and - with BSI-compliant tenant separation - clusterable. In addition to classical operation in a virtual machine, looking ahead the E-Akte must also be capable of being operated in a "container" (Kubernetes) using an orchestration tool. In addition, no later than 3 years after the award of the contract, the E-Akte must be capable of being operated cloud-agnostically in a private cloud infrastructure. Cloud capability is to be understood here as a fundamental architectural objective. Looking ahead, the E-Akte must be capable of being integrated into an OSS-based workplace of the North Rhine-Westphalia state administration. To this end, the contractor must support the necessary integration and customisation work, in particular on clients and interfaces, in coordination with the contracting authority and provide appropriate resources for this. The E-Akte must be structured according to a multi-tier architecture - user layer / specialist procedures, processing layer, data layer - and must be capable of being operated on approved enterprise operating systems (Windows Server and Linux in accordance with the IT.NRW architecture guidelines). All user functions must be usable via a responsive, browser-based web client, access to which is also possible via mobile end devices (e.g. iPad). The web client as the main client must be supplemented by a Windows Explorer integration or client that provides the core functions of the E-Akte. All user interfaces must comply with the North Rhine-Westphalia Ordinance on Barrier-Free Information Technology (BITV NRW) in its currently valid version: The contractor must continuously ensure and prove accessibility even with further developments (releases). The E-Akte must support the import and export of files, cases and documents in accordance with the specifications of the XÖV standards XDOMEA and XJUSTIZ, as well as in original and PDF format. Authorised users must also be able to export files together with all cases, documents and metadata as an overall PDF. The contractor must ensure audit-proof records management through complete versioning and comprehensive history entries traceable up to long-term storage, as well as logging of all changes. For communication with connected specialist procedures and third-party systems, the E-Akte must fully provide at least the following technologies: - WebDAV - CMIS - REST API based on .NET - SAP ArchiveLink for the exchange of documents - OData - RFC connection for the bidirectional exchange of metadata between SAP and the DMS. As exchange and messaging standards, XDOMEA and XJUSTIZ must be integrated in the respective current XÖV standards. In addition, the system must provide AD and ADFS coupling (including SAML 2.0, OAuth) with single sign-on (SSO) for user management. Furthermore, the contractor must connect the E-Akte to the state's own workflow system (E-Laufmappe). Synchronisation between the E-Akte and the E-Laufmappe takes place via the CMIS interface, which the contractor must adapt accordingly. The contractor must provide performance counters or measurement points in the E-Akte that can be integrated into a central monitoring tool and used to monitor performance and availability, as well as for reporting. The E-Akte must comprise a role-based authorisation concept with configurable function rights (e.g.

reading, writing, deleting) and organisation-bound object rights. The E-Akte must remain capable of further development over the term of the contract. The contractor must provide at least one major release per year as a long-term support version (LTS version) with at least 24 months of support. For the operation of the E-Akte, the contractor must provide support services (third-level support) and advisory support services. The contractor must migrate the existing data from the existing nscale eGov E-Akte system - files, cases and documents including metadata, history entries, and user, organisation and authorisation structures - completely, with integrity and authentically, and create migration concepts, automated scripts, test cases and documentation for this purpose. As part of the introduction support, the contractor will advise on authorisation structures, accompany the rollout and commissioning, and provide suitable training and knowledge transfer services (including classroom training, web training, e-learnings). The contracting authority reserves the right to specify and adjust the requirements in the course of the procedure.

sig_f0bdda562324ecd0d5c8.description: The Department of the Army is pleased to announce the availability of a cutting-edge software framework designed to enhance the capabilities of Software Defined Radio (SDR) systems. This framework enables the SDR signal chain to dynamically adjust its capabilities based on the sensed RF environment and to respond at the protocol level in real-time. The Department of the Army is releasing this software framework to foster collaboration with industry partners and encourage the integration of this technology into their SDR products. The intent is to enable greater flexibility in conducting radio frequency operations, allowing industry partners to leverage this framework to enhance their SDR systems' adaptability and operational effectiveness. By providing this framework, we aim to advance the state of SDR technology and promote innovation in the field of radio frequency operations. Key Features of the Framework: Rapid Reconfiguration: The framework allows for swift reconfiguration of the RF signal processing chain modules within the SDR’s field programmable gate array (FPGA), ensuring adaptability to varying operational requirements. FPGA-Based Physical Layer (PHY) and Media Access Control (MAC): The framework enables the rapid development and implementation of a fully-customized PHY and MAC layer that supports various signals and waveforms, providing a comprehensive solution for SDR applications. Elements Available for Industry: FPGA Top-Level Framework: This top-level hardware description language (HDL) framework resides within the SDR FPGA, facilitating seamless communication between the General-Purpose Processor (GPP) and the signal modules. Application Programming Interface (API): A user-friendly, common C-based API is provided, allowing developers to create SDR-agnostic applications that can manipulate the programmed signal FPGA modules effectively. Transport Interface (TI): The TI consists of dynamic or static C libraries utilized during application builds, enabling efficient message transport to and from user-based applications and FPGA signal modules. Exemplar Data Generation/Consumption Module: This module serves as a testing tool for hardware-specific implementations of the framework, ensuring compatibility and performance validation. Documentation: Comprehensive documentation will be made available, including development environment guides and a developer's guide, to assist industry partners in effectively utilizing the framework. The Department of the Army encourages industry partners to engage with this innovative framework, which is expected to significantly advance the capabilities of SDR technology. The Government retains all rights of modifications made to the original framework. To access this software interested parties shall complete the attached Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) (Attachment 1). Individuals identified as contractor representatives/users pursuant to signed/complete NDAs may then create an account on Test Resource Management Center (TRMC) to access the codebase. A step-by-step guide for creating a TRMC account and accessing the repository is included in Attachment 2. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETING THE NDA: An authorized representative of each contractor organization is to complete the following steps to ensure the NDA is processed correctly: Complete all fields on page 1. Complete and sign as the "Recipient’s Authorized Representative" on page 4. Complete the fields for the "Requesting Organization Authorized POC" on page 5. Sign the acknowledgement on page 5 and identify all contractor users from the company they represent. Obtain signatures from all authorized users identified on page 5. Return the completed NDA to the Warped Alloy Management Team at usarmy.meade.7-sig-cmd.mbx.warped-alloy-software@army.mil for final completion and signature of fields on page 6. For additional information or questions, please reach out using the contact information below. For inquiries, please send an email to the Warped Alloy Management Team at usarmy.meade.7-sig-cmd.mbx.warped-alloy-software@army.mil Thank you for your attention to this exciting opportunity.

sig_f0c289458d8979cc723a.description: The Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP) is seeking information from suppliers regarding the future of the Benelux Patent Platform (BPP 3.0). The current BPP platform, BPP 2.0, is used by the National Offices of Intellectual Property of Belgium, The Netherlands and Luxembourg to manage their patent grant process in their respective countries. It has been initially built and implemented across 3 countries in 2014-2017, and has been evolving since this time through regular releases for all 3 countries, implementing functional and technological improvements. The vision for the BPP 3.0 platform is an evolution or a re-build of the platform, making improvements to functionality where necessary (e.g. user centricity), but also taking advantage of new technologies, such as making it cloud-ready; if appropriate, taking advantage of AI and other new approaches to software development (e.g. low code package solutions), where impact to users is limited but could create large improvements to the platform and make its maintenance and support more cost-effective. The scope of the services could include: Part 1 – An evolution of the current Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of: · An industry-leading, long-term solution that will need to be configured in such a way to provide as a minimum functionality of the current platform, including specific processes and functionality of the patent industry for National Patent Offices; · It could be a newly build platform, bespoke or off-the-shelf system configured to the needs of the National Offices, which will enable carefully orchestrated business change from a user perspective, making potential transition and data migration as smooth as possible, whilst keeping the business operations uninterrupted. Alternatively, it could be an upgrade and improvement of the current platform, ensuring that future platform is technologically up to date and cloud ready, replacing or upgrading the software stack to the latest versions; · If appropriate, the solution should include services for data migration from the current Platform, including extraction, transformation and loading of the data from the current platform. Part 2 – A managed service for the current and future Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of: · A service desk for internal users of all three Offices to handle incident and problem management; · Consistent releases for all three Offices for new functionality introduced as part of a change management process and maintenance and support of all software components of the Platform; · If appropriate, this should include transition of the managed services from the incumbent Supplier, ensuring uninterrupted operation of the platform and services to its users. Part 3 – Hosting infrastructure for the Benelux Patent Platform that is likely to consist of · The provision of the shared hosting platform for the users of the three National Patent Offices of the Benelux countries and for external users (e.g. patent applicants) of the system, compliant with the ISO27001 requirements. This could be either based on dedicated hardware and infrastructure, or high-assurance cloud environments (public or private) with strict compliance guarantees, taking into consideration data privacy restrictions and EU data residency, GDPR compliance, high availability and a low cost but highly secure infrastructure; · If appropriate, this should include transition of the hosting services from the incumbent Supplier, ensuring uninterrupted operation of the platform and services to its users.
sig_f0c289458d8979cc723a.title: New generation of the Benelux Patent Platform (BPP 3.0)

sig_f0d700d42a053bd9ec40.description: This agreement, let under the Procurement Act 2023 includes consultancy, covering specialisms such as business, strategy and policy, finance, HR, procurement, health or social care and community, infrastructure and environment. As well as restructuring and insolvency. Lot 1: Multidisciplinary. Customers can use this Lot to commission identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 3: Transformation. Services encompass the entire transformation lifecycle, providing strategic direction, identifying options, as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 4: Finance. This Lot provides comprehensive consultancy and professional services encompassing the full spectrum of services relating to finance, financial management and statutory compliance and governance. This may include identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 5: HR. This Lot provides comprehensive consultancy and professional services relating to HR to support the strategic alignment, operational delivery, and cultural development of an organisation's workforce. The Lot covers the full employee lifecycle and includes identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 6: Procurement. This Lot provides comprehensive consultancy and professional services covering the entire commercial lifecycle including procurement and supply chain management. This may include identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 7: Health and social care. This Lot provides comprehensive consultancy and professional services to support the strategic planning and operational improvement of health, social care, and/or community services. This may include identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery. The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 8: Infrastructure and public services. This Lot provides comprehensive consultancy and professional services to support the strategic planning, development, and optimisation of national infrastructure, transport networks, and civic spaces. This may include identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery (excluding construction). The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 9: Environment and sustainability. This lot provides consultancy and professional services relating to environment and/or sustainability. This may include identification of options with recommendations as well as implementation and delivery (excluding construction). The full scope is set out in the Framework Schedule 1 (Specification) Lot 10: Restructuring and insolvency. This lot provides objective advice in relation to corporate restructuring and insolvency. Although the exact nature of this advice will vary by case, Suppliers must be able to demonstrate the required expertise in relation to distressed corporate situations. In the information session, the contracting authority will talk about the objectives and content of the dynamic purchasing system to be established, as well as the procurement plan for procurements within the purchasing system. The information session is open to all interested operators. The session will not be recorded. The language of the session is Finnish. The presentation material for the information session will be published openly available after the session at a web address to be announced separately. A summary of the content of the information session will also be published in English after the session. The contracting authority reserves the right to conduct a bilateral market dialogue with selected operators after the information session. sig_f171b70efb97b0b9eef4.description: The aim of this project is to provide tools in the form of a guideline and a tool for public administration, industry, and security research that make it possible to increase the resilience of cloud applications in particular against microarchitectural attacks such as Spectre and Meltdown and newer variants. The focus is to be on defensive programming countermeasures at the application level. In this way, the security of the software used is to be made more independent of the cloud provider's countermeasures. To reach as large a target group as possible, the results are to be written in English. The guideline is to describe concrete, practical, and easily applicable measures, and the developed tool is to automatically identify vulnerabilities and mitigate them if necessary. sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.description: The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050. The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain. JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets. The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3. All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.
sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.title: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

sig_f1ab2c8952d3b2279e4f.description: The Region of Attica manages a particularly complex portfolio of projects with varying degrees of maturity, from different funding sources, which are tendered and implemented both by the Region of Attica and by other bodies. As is reasonable, the large number of projects and their geographical dispersion throughout the Region, as well as the large number of Beneficiaries – and by extension the different approaches to project management (methodology and tools used) – pose significant challenges in project monitoring. Also, the different typology of the projects, the different funding sources (with different management and monitoring requirements), as well as the existence of multiple supporting information systems (NSRF MIS, EPAM MIS, Beneficiaries IS, etc.) for entering information, are additional challenges in project monitoring. Given the above challenges, the need arises to support the Region of Attica with an integrated project monitoring mechanism, which will ensure continuous and valid information, both internally, within the Region, and towards citizens and businesses. The new project monitoring mechanism is called upon to cover a series of needs of the Region of Attica, such as indicatively: (a) implementation of a unified project monitoring and management system, at project portfolio management level, adapted to the needs of the Region, (b) creation of an information application for managing information regarding the progress of projects, which will interoperate with the other systems of the Region and exchange data, (c) identification of synergies between projects implemented in the Region to ensure the strategic alignment of projects with the objectives of the Region, (d) monitoring of project progress, based on the agreed physical deliverable and schedule, (e) identification of systemic risks and problems arising in the projects of the Region's portfolio and ensuring a unified and effective approach in taking corrective measures, (f) measurement and evaluation of the results and benefits of the projects, based on targets (KPIs), for the social and economic life of citizens and businesses, (g) communication and information of citizens and businesses regarding the progress of the projects, their results and the benefits arising from them, so that they can actively participate and become sharers in developments in their area, (h) feeding the Observatories operating in the Region with information on the projects (e.g. Entrepreneurship Observatory), so as to facilitate the planning of targeted actions towards citizens and businesses. Creation of a Project Monitoring Control Centre and Integrated Information System in the Region of Attica
sig_f1ab2c8952d3b2279e4f.title: Creation of a Project Monitoring Control Centre and Integrated Information System in the Region of Attica

sig_f1cdfe45e91beb444607.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The system will complement existing corporate and client-side systems, including Civica, by providing enhanced resource planning, capacity forecasting, workload visibility, timesheet reporting and management information. The objective is to improve service efficiency, strengthen forward planning, support evidence-based resource decisions and provide greater assurance over programme delivery, capacity utilisation and value for money. Lot 1: . Dundee City Council is undertaking this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and market engagement exercise to better understand the solutions currently available within the market for construction consultant resource and project management software. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire. The information provided will be used solely for market engagement purposes and to assist the Council in identifying suppliers whose solutions appear capable of meeting the Council's requirements. Completed questionnaires should be submitted by 12 Noon on 25 September 2026 to trina.forbes@dundeecity.gov.uk. Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.
sig_f1cdfe45e91beb444607.title: Procurement of Construction Consultant Management Software

sig_f1dc10784c91ef4df9fd.description: The client's SOC has the primary mission of monitoring the organisation's IT landscape around the clock and initiating appropriate measures in the event of security incidents. The main focus areas obtained from the previous contracting partner were Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), analysis and incident response, vulnerability management, and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM). Accordingly, the present procurement essentially comprises the replacement of said components and services. While some tasks will now be handled by the client's SOC, internal personnel resources are a limiting factor. Therefore, some tasks, including the ongoing monitoring of the environment, will still need to be provided jointly with the support of an external partner. The future environment is intended to be based on the current internal log data platform Splunk, which will be expanded into a SIEM. This platform is to be supplemented by a Managed Detection and Response (MDR) solution that operates using its own data lake and transmits alerts to the internal SIEM. Ongoing monitoring is to take place on the basis of the MDR service, while the client's employees will in future deal primarily with the internal SIEM and thus also be able to cover internal and organisation-specific use cases. The systems will be supplemented by various services to operate the SIEM platform, as well as by cyber analysis services and support in the event of an incident. The future platform must also support operations in vulnerability management with suitable tools. The procurement is divided into four lots. As described, the client is transitioning from an SOC outsourcing model with internal support to a predominantly internally operated SOC with supplementary services provided by external partners. Within this framework, the existing internal infrastructure will be expanded or, where necessary, newly established. The same applies to the use cases and processes. Consulting and development services for this project as well as for subsequent operations are sought in this lot. Furthermore, the client desires support with cyber security incidents from the same partner. Specifically, this concerns the following services: * Incident Response Retainer: Support in cyber emergencies and security incidents with potentially large scale damage based on predefined action plans and SLAs * Support with analysis: Support in the analysis of events and incidents, linked to specific response times, threat hunting * Consulting, specialist support and know-how transfer in the entire cybersecurity environment: Use case development and consulting, threat modelling, optimisation of the SIEM, creation and refinement of playbooks, optimisation of SOC processes and triage, assistance in projects, evaluation of new systems and other specialised consulting services
sig_f1dc10784c91ef4df9fd.title: Support for the operation and further development of the Security Operations Centre (SOC)

sig_f1e0fb59e59372b00dce.description: The subject of the contract is the creation of a modern digital Public Health Surveillance (PHS) Mechanism. With the implementation of the Mechanism and the utilisation of epidemiological data collection tools, the following will be achieved: integral and secure data processing, production of mathematical and stochastic surveillance analyses, analysis of the geographical and demographic dimension of the data, creation of a modern Epidemiological Surveillance Control Centre, support for Competent Committees with the ability to access documented data and reports, provision of an appropriate emergency reporting procedure by physicians, promotion, communication and publication of findings and guidelines, and forwarding of data to reference centres. The Project synthesises the framework for the digital operation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism based on the already defined procedures, standards, organisation and regulatory framework determined by the implementation study of this project and the other sub-projects of the Action. The Project briefly includes the following distinct actions: 1. Supply, development, installation, configuration and operation of a multi-channel information management and dissemination platform (Web, Mobile App, etc.). 2. Integrated platform for the collection, processing and storage of data based on the general architecture of a DataWarehouse for the purpose of producing reports. 3. Digital tools: Data Mining, Intelligent Reporting, Predictive Analytics, Statistical packages for operational decision support (STATA: MP 2-Core, Perpetual Licence, SPSS: v18, Base Subscription, Perpetual licence) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). 4. Preparation of 3 CAPTURE/RECAPTURE studies to estimate the representativeness and rate of reported data. 5. Preparation of an analysis study on the need for a national 'living' disease registry based on COVID experience and international best practices. 6. Implementation & execution study, training plan and publicity action plan. 7. Training actions and production of educational content. 8. Workshop design, for the information, awareness and participation of the involved stakeholders in the implementation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism. 9. Design of a Public Health Scientific Conference with the subject of extracting best practices regarding the operation of the Epidemiological Surveillance Mechanism, with the participation of internationally renowned experts and all involved stakeholders.
sig_f1e0fb59e59372b00dce.title: Development of a new integrated epidemiological surveillance mechanism

sig_f1ff1a84db1ec5d89195.description: This is not a prior information notice, call for tenders, procurement notice or invitation to negotiate, nor does the publication of the notice initiate a competitive tendering procedure. A possible procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. This request for information surveys the market and obtains information regarding the procurement when planning the procurement of the Helsinki City artificial intelligence management system. The objective of this request for information is to obtain information on solutions, capabilities and alternative implementation methods available on the market before the actual potential tendering process. Helsingin kaupunki is preparing a procurement for an artificial intelligence management system, the purpose of which is to enable the management and documentation of obligations in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) and to support the lifecycle management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems. The artificial intelligence management system enables the management, demonstration and reporting of the obligations of the provider and deployer of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act with regard to high-risk artificial intelligence systems, and supports the management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems, the identification and management of artificial intelligence risks, and communication about artificial intelligence. The artificial intelligence management system will produce information for the city's management, artificial intelligence developers, and the city's services and websites utilizing artificial intelligence. The system will act as a central tool in identifying and managing risks, documentation, preparing communications and supporting deployment processes. Further information on the subject matter of the procurement is described in the appendix "Description of the subject matter of the procurement". INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We kindly ask you to answer in writing to the questions presented in the appendices "Questions for the request for information" and "Environmental criteria" as comprehensively as possible by the set deadline. We ask you to state if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. We ask you to specify and clearly mark this information. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to arrange clarifying market dialogues with those who have responded to the request for information at its discretion. The contracting authority is not obliged to discuss with all respondents. The contracting authority will arrange supplier-specific market dialogues primarily via remote connections in March-April 2026, if they are considered necessary. Supplier-specific invitations to the market dialogue will be delivered after the deadline of the request for information. The contracting authority will deliver potentially preliminary tender documents for commenting later. The information collected through the request for information and market dialogue will remain confidential and will be used solely for procurement planning. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The contracting authority is not bound by the information stated in this notice or its appendices, but as the preparation progresses, the subject matter and requirements of the procurement may change. The responses given in the request for information are not binding on the supplier. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent procurement that may be organized. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual tendering process. No compensation is paid for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. Preliminarily, the call for tenders is planned to be published during June 2026.

sig_f284276d43baddf6d6ee.description: The forest management services will be awarded by concluding a contract for each lot. The cumulative area of the lots is 29092,29 ha. The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. The services involve the development of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 paragraph (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The management method of the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. Forest management services for the Dobrovat Forestry Office - DS Iasi, with an area of 7.522,20 ha; Forest management services for the Lunca Cetatuii Forestry Office - DS Iasi, with an area of 12.032,61 ha; Forest management services for the Podu Iloaiei Forestry Office - DS Iasi, with an area of 9.537,48 ha
sig_f284276d43baddf6d6ee.title: Forest management services - DS Iasi

sig_f2888fa063bad3bed661.description: Concluding a contract for the integration and provision of a platform with or for various applications intended for the evaluation of radiological image data using modern algorithms (machine learning or AI) (AI applications). The services covered by the awarded contract comprise in particular: a) the integration of the platform for AI applications for the evaluation of radiological image data into the contracting authority's existing IT system landscape, featuring highly automated processing of the corresponding image data and a modern, user-centred display of the results within the existing tool landscape; b) the ongoing provision of the platform for AI applications; c) the integration and ongoing provision of AI applications for fracture detection on the one hand and for the diagnosis of pulmonary embolisms on the other via the platform ("initial AI applications") in the pilot project (see below) as well as further AI applications going beyond the initial applications via the platform in the course of the contractual partnership, in each case after thorough examination of the AI applications and additional quality-assurance measures such as long-term testing, blind testing, etc., prior to the integration and provision of AI applications by the contractor; d) ongoing maintenance, quality assurance and support of the platform, including the provided AI applications; e) training for medical users and technical personnel; f) all service and support services associated with the provision of the platform including AI applications in the form of a central contractual partnership ("single point of contact"), in particular the secondary validation of AI applications with expert guidance to ensure their intended use in medical processes, as well as advice on the selection of suitable AI applications. In a first step, as part of a pilot project, the platform and the two aforementioned initial AI applications will be established in everyday medical practice in two WIGEV radiology institutes (one initial AI application in each radiology institute), during which the processes will be developed, tested and evaluated. Following successful piloting, further AI applications are to be provided as needed in all WIGEV radiology institutes via the platform as part of the contractual partnership.
sig_f2888fa063bad3bed661.title: City of Vienna – Vienna Healthcare Group / AI in Radiology

sig_f28e9efa6c54ac2a97de.description: Municipalities must submit construction and spatial data to the national Built Environment Information System (Ryhti) by 1.1.2029 at the latest. The submission of data requires the development of software used by municipalities, for which the Ministry of the Environment grants subsidies to municipalities for partner testing projects. In Jyväskylä, construction and spatial data are produced and managed in the Trimble Locus system. Jyväskylän kaupunki has decided to participate in the "Ryhti development for Trimble Locus system in local master plan and local detailed plan operations" project by decision of the Urban Engineering Services Sector Director §10/2025. The Ministry of the Environment decided on 22.10.2025 to grant the project a subsidy of 325 000 €. The project is implemented as a cooperation project between four cities. In addition to Jyväskylä, the City of Lahti, the City of Oulu and the City of Iisalmi are involved. Jyväskylä acts as the main applicant in the project, i.e. the so-called technical administrator, and is responsible for procuring the purchased service included in the project. The cooperation partner and system/software developer is Trimble Finland Oy. The Ministry of the Environment may reimburse the project costs in full up to the granted subsidy amount. The information system and software development work carried out in the project is shared free of charge with other user municipalities. The software development work carried out in the project is procured from Trimble Finland Oy as a direct procurement. The development work is divided into three work packages, the combined cost of which is approximately 274 000 € (VAT 0). In addition, the functionalities to be developed will cause an annual maintenance cost of 4000 € (VAT 0), which will enter into force when the functionality has been put into use. According to section 40, subsection 2, paragraph 2 of the Public Procurement Act, the contracting authority may choose direct procurement if, for a technical reason or a reason related to the protection of an exclusive right, only a certain supplier can implement the procurement. An additional condition is that there are no reasonable alternative or replacement solutions and the absence of competition is not due to an artificial narrowing of the procurement conditions. The project develops the Ryhti capability of the Trimble Locus system used by the participating cities to meet statutory obligations. As the owner of the intellectual property rights of the Trimble Locus system, only Trimble Finland Oy is able to carry out the system development work. Trimble Finland Oy has an exclusive right to the system solutions, technology and source code used in the Trimble Locus system.
sig_f28e9efa6c54ac2a97de.title: Ryhti software development for the Trimble Locus system as a direct procurement
