Proposal submissions are due by January 9, 2026 @5pm. For submission of questions or white papers please contact : Bradly McLaughlin bradly.k.mclaughlin.civ@us.navy.mil AMENDMENT 0002: The purpose of this amendment is to attach an Area of Interest. N0016425SCA002 Q&C are due by August 6, 2025 @ 5pm. Proposal submissions are due by August 13, 2025 @ 5pm. AMENDMENT 0001: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the closing date to July 3, 2025 and add an Area of Interest N0016425SCA001 Miniature Aiming System (MAS) Machine Gun Optic (MGO) attachment. ORIGINAL POSTING: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) N00164-25-S-C001 Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC, Crane) The procedures outlined in this CSO apply to Areas of Interest posted under N00164-25-S-C001 OBJECTIVE: this announcement is intended to enable the rapid selection of innovative commercial solutions through a three-phased, competitive process. Including commercially-available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 1.1 Background and Authority NSWC Crane’s mission is to deliver innovative solutions and readiness to the Nation and its Warfighters through application of Technical Capabilities; advance all-domain system of systems within the Mission Areas of Expeditionary Warfare, Strategic Missions, and Electromagnetic Warfare; conduct science and technology, research, development, test and evaluation, acquisition and in-service engineering across the Defense lifecycles. To achieve these mission imperatives, NSWC Crane regularly partners with private industry using a variety of collaborative tools in order to streamline the incorporation of innovative technology into the products and services delivered to the Warfighter. To accelerate the adoption of advanced technology, curate solutions to technology gaps, and lead rapid prototyping NSWC Crane issues this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) as authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation. In this context “Innovative” means— Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. NSWC Crane is seeking innovative commercial solutions relevant to the following areas of technological exploration: • Expeditionary Warfare Guided by the National Defense Strategy, NSWC Crane recognizes the priorities and threats shifted to the Pacific. NSWC Crane’s efforts must counter the multi-domain threats and deter aggression posed in the Indo-Pacific region. This reinforces the need of a Joint Force that is even more lethal, resilient, agile and responsive. Autonomous solutions with a focus on payload and sensor integration to enhance detection, tracking, identifying, decision making, maneuver and kinetic/non-kinetic engagement capabilities for multi-domain, uncrewed and counter-crewed systems are a strategic priority. Expeditionary Warfare Development’s heritage has been and continues to focus on rapid prototyping and proven solutions supporting the evolving needs of the Expeditionary force. • Strategic Missions As the Navy’s primary organic field activity for full life cycle management including hardware, ordnance and power systems, NSWC Crane applies the distinct capabilities inherent to its people and facilities to assure 100% operational readiness of strategic missile systems. Fleet Readiness and Modernization and Hypersonics are a top priority of the Navy and DoD. These strategic priorities require collaboration between the Navy, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency to align appropriate requirements, technology development, rapid prototyping, production, sustainment and protection activities of ballistic missile systems to enable affordability, advance technology and reduce program risks to modernize the nuclear enterprise to defeat emerging threats worldwide. • Electromagnetic Warfare NSWC Crane’s Spectrum Warfare Department is the largest concentration of Electronic Warfare experts in the DoD. NSWC Crane provides non-kinetic expertise and electromagnetic spectrum dominance to all the services. Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) is a strategic priority due to the increasingly congested, contested and constrained environments. NSWC Crane supports multidomain integrated solutions through multispectral capabilities utilizing technology development, rapid prototyping, production and sustainment. Pursuant to DFARS 212.7002, NSWC Crane will only use this CSO to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements and to close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological advancements. All products and services acquired using this CSO will be treated as commercial products or commercial services, awarded on a fixed-price basis. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.10270, this announcement is a competitive selection of proposals based on a review by scientific, technological, or other subject-matter expert peers and is a competitive procedure. As a result of the competitive processes used under this CSO Announcement, multiple awards may be executed. The methods utilized to execute awards include: FARbased contract, Purchase Order, Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), and/or Bailment Agreement. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022, NSWC Crane may award an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to vendors to carry out prototype project(s) directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4023, NSWC Crane may procure (by contract or otherwise) ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, telecommunications, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary concerned considers necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense. 1.2 General Solicitation and Evaluation Procedures NSWC Crane’s CSO is soliciting Solution Briefs in response to individual Areas of Interest (AOIs). AOIs are focused topic(s) categories that will be published separately and posted on the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. All Solution Briefs submitted in response to AOIs will be governed by this CSO unless otherwise noted in the AOI. AOIs will be written in broad terms to maximize latitude in creativity when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from nontraditional defense contractors and interested parties (entities) who may be unfamiliar with submitting traditional proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post AOIs at any time. Interested parties are encouraged to frequently check the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC, Crane website for new AOI postings. Evaluation of responses will consist of the following 3 Phases: 1) Solution Brief, 2) Pitch, and 3) Full written proposal – described in more detail here: Phase 1 Solution Briefs: Solution Briefs submitted in response to an AOI shall be submitted as specified in Section 2 of this CSO. The Government will evaluate Solution Briefs against the criteria stated in this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for the costs associated with Solution Brief submissions. Phase 2 Pitch Session: Respondents whose Solution Briefs are evaluated to be of merit may be invited to provide a pitch following the instructions provided in Section 2.3 of this CSO. The Government reserves the right to limit the number of parties invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. In the event that the Government requires a demonstration, additional information will be provided in the specific AOI highlighting those procedures, otherwise Phase 2 will be comprised solely of the pitch. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with pitches, unless otherwise stipulated. Phase 3 Proposal: Those entities whose Solution Brief and Pitch are evaluated to be of merit and are selected for potential award may be invited to submit a full written proposal following the instructions provided in Section 2.4 of this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with the proposal in Phase 3, unless otherwise stipulated. SECTION 2 – GUIDELINES FOR SUBMISSION 2.1 General Guidelines Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. Companies may submit multiple Solution Briefs in response to any single AOI if each submission represents a separate and distinct concept. The period of performance for any Solution Brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24-months. Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. All Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals shall be unclassified. Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: “This [select one: Solution Brief, Pitch, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to non-Government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of -- or in connection with – the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use the information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: “Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.” Foreign-Owned businesses may independently submit a solution or do so as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more United States-Owned businesses. However, the ability to obtain an agreement based upon a submission may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-Owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain proscribed information. Submissions must be submitted electronically. Submissions sent through other channels or after the AOI period has ended will not be reviewed nor evaluated. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.2 Phase 1 Solution Brief PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF CONTENT Solution Briefs should not exceed five (5) written pages using 12-point font. Alternatively, Solution Briefs may take the form of briefing slides which should not exceed fifteen (15) slides. Briefs should include at a minimum: Title Page (does not count against page limit) Entity Name, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address. Specifically identify the AOI for which the Solution Brief is submitted. Executive Summary of the technology (one page) Describe the concept and unique aspects of the technology as it relates to the AOI. Identify whether the solution is an existing technology that has satisfied a pilot or demonstration (ie, commercially ready and viable technology), or the if the solution will require development for defense application. If development or adaptation is proposed, identify a suggested path to mature the technology. Identify aspects of the solution which may be considered proprietary or Intellectual Property (IP) Provide a brief overview of the company, including a summary of product commercialization and go-to-market strategy. PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF BASIS OF EVALUATION All solution briefs correctly submitted in response to an AOI will be evaluated against the stated criteria below. (Y/N) The proposed innovative commercial solution, technology, process, or method, is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or is an application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. Relevance of the Solution Brief in addressing the AOI. Technical Merit and feasibility of the solution to address Government AOI problem statement. A quick, reasonable, and efficient way exists for the DoD to test the innovative commercial solution, within a specified duration, whether outside or integrated within the DoD infrastructures or networks, as appropriate. Additional technical evaluation criteria specific to a particular project may be used. In these instances, the additional criteria will be posted within the AOI announcement on the SAM.Gov and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI, not against other Solution Briefs submitted in response to the same AOI. Additionally, while not overtly stated in AOIs, the Government’s evaluation will consider whether the proposal increases the likelihood of accomplishing NSWC Crane’s Mission Focus Areas. All submissions will be evaluated, however, only a select few will be invited to pitch. The government reserves the right to limit the number of entities invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.3 Phase 2 Pitch PHASE 2 PITCH CONTENT In Phase 2, entities shall provide an in-person or virtual pitch to demonstrate and provide further details on their proposed innovative commercial solution and the technical and business viability of the proposed solution. The Government may elect to use external market research during the Pitch to evaluate viability. In addition to the Pitch, the Government, at its discretion, may request for consideration an additional written submission to further supplement the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. During the Phase 2 Pitch, the Company must detail/address: Estimated Price/Schedule Rough order of magnitude (ROM) or pricing Anticipated Data Rights Assertions During the Pitch, the Government may request the additional information/detail with respect to the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. PHASE 2 PITCH BASIS OF EVALUATION Individual pitches will be evaluated against the following factors: Relevance of the pitch in addressing the AOI and the ability of the presenter to adequately address Government questions or concerns regarding the proposed application or use of the innovative commercial solution. The solution has technical merit, adequately & realistically addresses Government need and can be quickly incorporated into DOD systems. Reasonableness of the ROM The associated delivery schedule is expeditious and realistic. Individual pitches will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI and the factors above, not against any other Pitches held under the same AOI. Pitch submissions will be valid for 180 calendar days after the pitch date. Upon completion of evaluations, the Government will notify the Company that: (1) the proposed concept/technology/solution has been selected for possible award and the entity is invited to submit a full proposal; (2) the proposed concept/technology/solution is not of interest to the Government; or (3) the proposed concept/technology/solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources. If the proposed innovative commercial solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources, the Company may be contacted with a request to respond to proposal request within 180 calendar days from the pitch date. If after 180 calendar days from the pitch date (or earlier if notified by NSWC, Crane), Government resources are not identified to formally move into Phase 3, the entity will no longer be eligible for an award under that particular AOI. 2.4 Phase 3 Proposal PHASE 3 PROPOSAL CONTENT The final phase of the evaluation process is the proposal request. Based upon the evaluation process detailed in Phase 1 and 2, the Government may request a full written proposal. The entity will be invited to develop and submit a full written proposal and negotiate appropriate terms and conditions. Entities may discuss ideas and questions related to the proposal with the Government POC during the proposal writing process. Each proposal submitted shall consist of two sections: Section 1 shall consist of the technical proposal; Section 2 shall consist of the price/cost/schedule. Proposals will be assessed by NSWC Crane technical and Contracting subject matter experts. Entities may propose their own internal terms and conditions (e.g., Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA)) to be considered during negotiations with the Government. Note, there are certain terms and conditions the Government is unable to accept. Awards made under this authority will only be issued as fixed price awards in accordance with DFARS 212.7002(b). However, projects awarded through the CSO are flexible to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and where it meets the Government’s needs. At a minimum, written proposals must contain: Title Page Company Name, Point of Contact Name, Date, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address and any subcontractors or team members. Include an abstract which provides a concise description of the proposal. Description of the proposed innovative commercial solution Background and objectives of the proposed solution, deliverables, and resources needed to execute. Include the nature and extent of the anticipated results. Include ancillary and operational issues such as certifications, algorithms, and any engineering/software development methodologies to be used. If services, include a Statement of Work (SOW). Provide a detailed project schedule that outlines the various phases of work to be accomplished within the proposed period of performance. You may refer to the Solution Brief that prompted this proposal request, but do not duplicate it. Identify any Government material, equipment, data, or other items necessary. Phase 3 - Price Proposal The entity shall propose a fixed price for the item or service and provide any data or supporting information necessary for the determination of a fair and reasonable price. This can include, but is not limited to, commercial price catalog or other proprietary information to help the Government assess the proposed price. Additionally, if proposing an OT, while not required to be specifically addressed in the proposal (with the exception of the 1/3 cost-share requirement, if applicable), the Government will review the proposal to determine if the following OT statutory requirements are met: Fits the definition of a prototype Meets non-traditional participation/cost share requirement: Non-traditional defense contractor contributes to a significant extent or not; if not, 1/3 cost share implementation is addressed Defense Utility: Solution is applicable to a DoD platform, system or component SECTION 3 – AWARDS 3.1 General Guidelines Upon favorable review and available funds, the Government may choose to make an award. Only Warranted Contracting Officers or Agreements Officers may obligate the Government by entering into or modifying a binding agreement on behalf of the Government. Awards made under this CSO will be fixed price. Contract type will be determined during Phase 3. Multiple awards may be made to pursue similar or dissimilar solutions should they all meet the technical criteria, be selected for award, and if funds are available. Entities must have a DUNs and CAGE Code registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award. Companies are advised to commence SAM registration upon receipt of a proposal request. Awardees must be determined to be responsible by the Contracting or Agreements Officer and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving award. Receipt of a proposal request does not guarantee receipt of award. The Government reserves the right, at any point prior to award, to cancel the request. Upon award, awardees must register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (e.g. Wide Area Work Flow). 3.2 Comptroller General Access to Information In OT projects that provide for payments in a total amount in excess of $5,000,000, the Agreement will include a mandatory clause that provides for the Comptroller General the ability to examine the records of any party to the agreement or any entity that participates in the performance of the agreement. 3.3 Procurement Integrity Act (PIA) All awards under this CSO shall be treated as Federal Agency procurements for purpose of 41 U.S.C. Chapter 21. Accordingly, the CSO competitive solicitation process and awards made thereof must adhere to the ethical standards required by the PIA. SECTION 4 - ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING As it is the mission of NSWC Crane to enable access to commercially-derived disruptive capabilities across the entirety of the DoD enterprise, Prototype OTAs awarded against this CSO will allow for an iterative prototyping process. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the work in a prototype project to allow the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the original Government customer or originate with other organizations within the Federal Government. SECTION 5 – FOLLOW-ON PRODUCTION Upon successful completion of a prototype project under the OTA, the Government may negotiate a follow-on production contract or agreement without further competition. Any concept/technology/solution successfully proven through a Prototype OTA can be transitioned to production. AOIs posted by the Government under this CSO and Prototype OTAs awarded will include language providing for the potential award of a follow-on production contract or agreement as authorized under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 Individual AOIs and CSO prototype OTAs will explicitly identify follow-on Prototype OTAs as a potential outcome of a successful prototyping effort. SECTION 6 SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION A transaction for a prototype project is complete upon the written determination of the appropriate approving official (program manager and Agreement Officer) for the matter in question that efforts conducted under a Prototype OTA: (1) met the key technical goals of a project; (2) satisfied success metrics incorporated into the Prototype OTA; or (3) accomplished a particularly favorable or unexpected result that justifies the transition to production. Furthermore, successful completion can occur prior to the conclusion of a prototype project to allow the Government to transition any aspect of the prototype project determined to provide utility into production while other aspects of the prototype project have yet to be completed. Any Prototype OTA shall contain a provision that sets forth the conditions under which that prototype agreement must be successfully completed. SECTION 7 – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during Proposal development and negotiations. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. Companies may enter into specific NDAs directly with the Non-Government advisors or their corporate entities. Submission of an offer under this CSO will constitute a grant of authority by the submitting company to the Government to allow the use of non-Government advisors to participate in evaluations of all phases of the CSO process. The Government understands that information provided in response to this CSO is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. NSWC, Crane policy is to treat all submissions as source selection sensitive information, and to disclose their contents only for the purpose of evaluation. Restrictive notices notwithstanding, during the evaluation process, submissions may be handled by support contractors for administrative purposes and/or to assist with technical evaluation. All NSWC, Crane and DoD support contractors performing this role are expressly prohibited from performing NSWC, Crane-sponsored technical research and are bound by appropriate NDAs. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained at NSWC, Crane and all other non-required copies destroyed. A certification of destruction may be requested, provided the formal request is received at this office within 5 calendar days after notification that a proposal was not selected.

sig_f2e06a9cc17348e07a69.description: The subject of the procurement is the acquisition of infrastructure and community engineering design software and infrastructure project cost calculation software for the City of Lappeenranta, Streets and Environment sector. The design software must include design tools for implementing at least roads, bridges, water supply, and landscape and regional planning. It must be possible to carry out specialised planning of traffic needs using the design software. It must be at least possible to perform turning path checks for different vehicle classes and to draw up detailed traffic control plans with quantity lists. Files obtained from the Trimble Locus Cloud software must be compatible with the design software. Lappeenrannan kaupunki uses the Trimble Locus Cloud software for, among other things, the processing and management of measurement data, map imagery and aerial photographs. Files obtained from the design software must be compatible with the Trimble Locus Cloud software in use by the City of Lappeenranta. The cost calculation software can be used to make accurate cost estimates for at least road, railway and waterway projects, as well as street and municipal engineering projects in all design phases (project component and construction component). The classification and numerical values (metric system) used in cost calculation must be directly compatible with the design software's classification (InfraBIM classification) and numerical values. The cost calculation software must also include emission calculation tools for calculating the carbon footprint of infrastructure projects. sig_f3269264b960a2e789a5.description: Organisational, professional and technical consultancy services for an omnichannel transformation project. The Audi BKK is planning to implement a future-proof omnichannel platform for customer advice in order to ensure consistent, seamless and personalised support across all relevant communication channels. In addition to connecting to existing systems of the Audi BKK, new digital contact channels for customer communication are to be provided, networked with one another and further optimised or automated. To prepare for the implementation of an omnichannel platform and to create the necessary organisational, professional and technical prerequisites, the contracting authority is hereby tendering for advisory support services to accompany and implement measures in the omnichannel context. Based on a completed as-is analysis and determination of the status quo, organisational, professional and technical measures and objectives have been derived. The results are documented in an omnichannel roadmap and are divided into a conception phase and a transformation phase (see attached annex). The concepts and optimisations developed (and potentially still emerging) during the conception phase are to be consolidated and driven forward by the contractor in their implementation and execution. The contractor shall effectively manage, methodically implement and document the omnichannel transformation process. The contractor shall support the technical and functional requirements for a suitable omnichannel platform during the derivation and survey phase in order to ensure a robust catalogue of requirements for the subsequent tendering and procurement of an omnichannel platform. The objective of this tender is to conclude a contract with a contractor for a period of two years, with planned contractual extension options. The contracting authority estimates the scope of the contract at approximately 800 consultant days.

sig_f34031d767ff90ebeb33.description: The subject of the Public Contract is the development, supply and implementation of the National Repository Catalogue (NRC) information system ("NRC System"). The subject of the Public Contract shall consist of the supply of the NRC System, including the design and implementation of the NRC System into the Contracting Authority's IT environment and the realisation of integration links, commissioning of the NRC System including the provision of trial operation. The subject of the Public Contract also includes subsequent operation support, maintenance and development services for the NRC System for an estimated provision period of 48 months. The NRC is designed as a central register intended for the registration and management of data regarding Czech research data repositories. Its aim is to provide reliable, machine-readable and long-term sustainable information on what repositories exist in the Czech Republic, who operates them, what metadata standards and ontologies they use, and to ensure connection to external services. The entire NRC architecture is designed to respect FAIR principles, thereby supporting interoperability, transparency and the re-use of information. The NRC will register all research data repositories that are or will be created within the National Repository Platform (NRP), or that will be connected to this platform. These are primarily 40 data repositories created within the NRP project (so-called pilot repositories) and the Open Science II call (other thematic repositories). These are entirely new repositories (e.g. CzBio) or innovations of existing repositories (e.g. Lindat/CLARIAH). The obligation to register a repository in the NRC is in these cases stipulated by the Rules for Creating New and Modifying Existing Thematic Repositories in the National Repository Platform and arises from the relevant legal acts of the projects. The NRC System must integrate the following components into a single, well-connected functional solution (deployed and customised in-house at NTK): 1. Cordra (NRC knowledge base) 2. Skosmos + Apache Jena Fuseki (vocabulary module) 3. MSCR (Metadata Schema and Crosswalk Registry) For this purpose, two components that are the subject of this public contract shall be developed by the supplier: 1. Middleware (application layer) 2. User interface (UI) Detailed requirements for the NRC System, its technical parameters and the functionalities of the NRC System are given in the NRC System Specification for Consultation Purposes ("NRC System Specification"), which the Contracting Authority shall provide to registered suppliers upon receipt of a signed non-disclosure agreement (see point 4 of the invitation).
sig_f34031d767ff90ebeb33.title: PTK_Pational Repository Catalogue

sig_f3443c6cc669dd343f7c.description: ESB intends to establish a multi-party Framework Agreement for the provision of Leadership, Culture and Organisational Capability Services to support the delivery of ESB's Culture and Capability Strategy. The Framework Agreement will provide access to expert service providers to support the co-design, development, deployment and ongoing evolution of Culture and Capability initiatives across ESB. The proposed scope includes the following service areas: Employee and Manager Capability Development; Leadership Development; Strategic Workforce Planning and Talent Management; Digital, Data and AI; and Organisation Development, Change Management, Culture and Future of Work.. Applicants are not required to demonstrate expertise across all service areas. Applicants may demonstrate relevant experience and capability within one or more areas of the overall Framework scope. The Framework Agreement will have an initial term of three years. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to extend the Framework Agreement for further period or periods, up to a maximum total Framework Agreement duration of eight years. sig_f35ba0be4dfa333639ef.description: The LUKS is seeking a reliable and competent service provider for both lots respectively, which fulfils the requirements to the best possible extent and sets up the respective part of the perimeter security for the LUKS, migrates the functions of the respective existing solution to the respective new solution, and finally commissions the new solution and decommissions and recycles or disposes of the existing one. In Lot 1, the web proxy and the perimeter firewall are to be jointly replaced by a geo-redundant on-premise perimeter firewall with proxy functions, which is capable of taking over the VPN termination at a later date. In this context, it is particularly important to take into account that the configuration of the web proxy has grown organically over years and has been tailored to the specific features of the existing web proxy solution. The migration of this configuration and its standardisation with that of the existing perimeter firewall represents a comprehensive analysis and configuration project for which the tenderers for Lot 1 must bring comprehensive knowledge and expend significant resources. Accordingly, Lot 1 includes some highly weighted requirements that assess the understanding of the situation and the capabilities of the tenderers. Optionally, in Lot 1, a new, additional internal DMZ firewall from the same manufacturer as the perimeter firewall should also be offered, which can be administered in the same management GUI, incl. the development of a simple configuration with a max. of 50 ACLs. This firewall is used exclusively for layer 3 to 4 access lists and serves to separate the DMZ from the internal infrastructure. In Lot 2, on the other hand, "only" the existing WAF, a BIG-IP from the company f5, is to be replaced by the successor product f5 BIG-IP r5600 "Best Bundle". The existing configuration and the existing modules in use of the existing BIG-IP are to be 1:1 transferred to the successor product, with the aim of replacing the existing BIG-IP as seamlessly and quietly as possible. Accordingly, Lot 2 contains only a few requirements alongside the highly weighted price criterion. In addition, the LUKS already has a highly qualified service provider for the necessary operational services, which is why these are only tendered as an option in Lot 2. Since the total volume of these operational services is well below the thresholds for public procurement, the LUKS reserves the right to exercise the option and award the operational services to the successful tenderer, or not to exercise the option and continue to procure the operational services from the existing service provider via a freehand award. The LUKS aims to manage the solutions procured in both lots independently, i.e., internally within LUKS. Nevertheless, the LUKS requires expert know-how from the successful tenderers in both lots. So that the LUKS IT can procure further expert know-how from the service providers at a later date if required, the tenderers shall also submit roles at predefined tariffs in their bids, which they can make available to the LUKS. In addition to this expert know-how, the tenderers for Lot 1 of this procurement procedure shall also show the LUKS which training and, where applicable, certification options for this solution they can offer the LUKS, so that the LUKS IT can operate the solution largely independently after commissioning; this know-how is already available within the LUKS for the BIG-IP. So that the LUKS and its partner operations can operate the offered solutions for the next at least 5 years, the tenderers shall submit with their bid all required additional contracts for licences, maintenance, etc. and include all related expenses in their bid. sig_f36503dab38bb9b7cef2.description: The Contracting Authority and the Client, the ministerie van Algemene Zaken, more specifically the Public and Communication Service (hereinafter: DPC), wishes to conclude framework agreements for the hiring of communication professionals, (web) editorial professionals and spokespersons. The Assignment is divided in a logical and proportionate manner into three lots, based on the type of service provision. These involve the following lots: 1) lot 1: Communication professionals; 2) lot 2: (Web) editorial professionals; 3) lot 3: Spokespersons and press officers. For each lot, a framework agreement (hereinafter also: Agreement) will be concluded in the field of the hiring of communication capacity. The intention is that the Agreements for lot 1 - Communication professionals, and lot 2 - (Web) editorial professionals, will enter into force on 9 February 2026. The Agreement for lot 3 - Spokespersons and press officers is expected to enter into force on 1 October 2026. Maximum contract value over four years (excluding VAT): Lot 1 – Communication professionals: € 396.000.000,-; Lot 2 – (Web) Editorial professionals: € 79.200.000,-; Lot 3 – Spokespersons and press officers: € 13.050.000,-. This lot comprises the provision of temporary communication capacity at junior, medior and senior level to participating organisations within central government (see Appendix E of the Descriptive Document). To this end, the Client shall enter into an Agreement with a maximum of four (4) (secondment) agencies specialised in communication. Estimated value of the assignment: € 264.000.000,- Maximum value of the framework agreement: € 396.000.000,-; This lot comprises the provision of temporary (web) editorial capacity at junior, medior and senior level to participating organisations within central government. To this end, the Client shall enter into an Agreement with a maximum of four (4) (secondment) agencies that are specialised (inter alia) in (web) editing and in social media editing. Estimated value of the assignment: € 52.800.000,- Maximum value of the framework agreement: € 79.200.000,-; This lot comprises the provision of temporary capacity in the field of spokesperson duties and press information at junior, medior and senior level to participating organisations within central government. sig_f3663306ddc60b242105.description: Revenue Scotland is seeking information from the market in relation to the next version of / replacement for its existing tax administration platform, SETS. The current platform supports the collection and operational management of devolved Scottish taxes. It enables taxpayers and their agents to submit tax returns and make payments to Revenue Scotland, and enables staff to process returns, manage taxpayer records through a number of statutory processes, reconcile inbound & outbound payments with tax declared, and undertake tax compliance activity and operational casework. Lot 1: . Revenue Scotland is seeking a strategic partner to help it deliver and support a cloud-hosted tax administration and case management platform for the collection and operational management of devolved taxes in Scotland. The system will manage tax data, support staff in administering tax returns and taxpayer records, and enable efficient case management of statutory tax management processes, workflow automation, and integration with external systems. Additionally, the solution needs to provide reporting capabilities in terms of management information and data export to our own analytics platform. We anticipate additional taxes and legislative change being introduced over the lifetime of the contract, and so the solution should be flexible enough to easily accommodate new functionality. Through this Prior Information Notice, Revenue Scotland wishes to consider the fullest range of modern, UK-based cloud-based solutions which support: - A portal for taxpayers and agents to view, edit and submit tax information - case management - workflow automation - operational processing - integration with other corporate systems such as our finance (general ledger) systems, contact management (telephony), and third-party print and post solutions. The next version of SETS will support at least five taxes and must provide a highly configurable and scalable platform capable of supporting evolving tax policy and operational requirements. Currently up to 80 back-office staff users across a range of different functional teams use the platform. Revenue Scotland welcomes engagement from suppliers with experience of delivering platforms capable of supporting complex administration and case management. Additional information: This contract may be split into lots, where market intelligence has suggested this to be viable and beneficial
sig_f3663306ddc60b242105.title: Scottish Electronic Tax System (SETS)

Failure to meet the minimum requirements will result in the rejection of the tender as incompatible with the terms of the contract pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 5 of the Public Procurement Law Act. The Contracting Authority requires that the product be brand new, grade I, not ex-display, free from technical and legal defects, authorised for marketing, and meet the quality and utility standards indicated by the Contracting Authority in Appendix No 3 to the SWZ. The Contracting Authority may, pursuant to Article 257, annul the procurement procedure if the funds which the Contracting Authority intended to allocate to finance the contract have not been granted to it. The Contracting Authority requires that the offered ICT products, ICT services and ICT processes used for the execution of the contract, both as main elements and components, elements of the service provision environment or accompanying solutions, do not include: ICT products, ICT services or ICT processes indicated in the recommendation referred to in Article 33 paragraph 4 of the Act of 5 July 2018 on the national cybersecurity system, stating their negative impact on the essential interests of state security, or an ICT product whose type has been specified in a decision concerning the recognition of a supplier as a high-risk supplier referred to in Article 67b paragraph 15 of the Act of 5 July 2018 on the national cybersecurity system, nor ICT services or ICT processes specified in that decision. Failure to meet the above requirements shall result in the rejection of the tender pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 17 or point 19 of the Public Procurement Law Act, respectively. The Contracting Authority agrees to change the delivered product to one other than that offered in the tender form in cases where the Contractor demonstrates that the offered product has been withdrawn from sale or its production has ceased, and it is not available on the Polish market (confirmed by the manufacturer or a commercial representative on the Polish market). The Contracting Authority permits the possibility of delivering another product provided that the requirements indicated in paragraph 3 section IV of the SWZ are met, and its functionality is not inferior to that of the offered product, it meets the requirements specified in the procurement documents at least to an equivalent degree, and the unit price is not higher than that offered in the tender form. In the case referred to above, the Contractor must obtain the consent of the Contracting Authority to change the offered product. If the Contractor does not justify the necessity of the change, the Contracting Authority has the right to refuse consent to change the offered product. In such a case, the Contractor will be obliged to deliver the offered product in accordance with the content of the tender. The Contracting Authority shall communicate its consent or refusal in writing to the Contractor. The tender price must include the purchase together with delivery to the Contracting Authority, i.e., 40-038 Katowice, ul. J. Lompy 19 block "E". The Contracting Authority requires that the product be brand new, grade I, not ex-display, free from technical and legal defects, authorised for marketing, and meet the quality and utility standards indicated by the Contracting Authority in Appendix No 3.1 to the SWZ. Failure to enter the manufacturer, name, version or other additional data enabling the unambiguous identification of the offered product in the tender form will result in the rejection of the tender pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 5 of the Public Procurement Law Act as incompatible with the terms of the contract. The Contracting Authority demands the submission, together with the tender, of objective evidence in the event of offering an equivalent product in the form of a detailed description of the offered product along with a comparative analysis with the described functionality of the programme in Appendix No 3 to the SWZ.

The detailed description of the offered product along with a comparative analysis may be drawn up in the form of a statement and is to confirm that the offered products are fully equivalent to the products indicated by the contracting authority in Appendix No 3 to the SWZ. The burden of proving that the offered product is equivalent and meets all the requirements specified by the contracting authority in the description of the subject of the contract, Appendix No 3 to the SWZ, rests with the Contractor. Subjective evidence drawn up in a foreign language shall be submitted together with a translation into Polish. A document drawn up in a foreign language together with a translation into Polish constitutes a complete set. In the absence of one of the documents forming part of the complete set, Article 107 paragraph 2 shall apply. The contracting authority does not grant consent in the cases referred to in Article 20 paragraph 3 of the Act (section 5 of the regulation on the manner of drawing up and transmitting information and technical requirements for electronic documents and electronic communication means in a public procurement procedure or competition, Journal of Laws of 2020 item 2452). If the Contractor has not submitted the objective evidence or the submitted objective evidence is incomplete, the Contracting Authority shall, pursuant to Article 107 paragraph 2, call for them to be submitted or completed within a designated time limit, subject to Article 107 paragraph 3 of the Act. In the event of failure to submit the objective evidence upon the call referred to in point 2.3, the tender shall be subject to rejection pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 2 letter c of the Public Procurement Law Act. In the event of failure to submit the objective evidence in Polish upon the call referred to in point 2.2, the tender shall be subject to rejection pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 2 letter c of the Public Procurement Law Act. The contracting authority's call to complete the objective evidence shall serve to establish that the offered products are fully equivalent to those indicated by the contracting authority in Appendix No 3 to the SWZ. The contracting authority's call to complete the objective evidence is a single call within the scope of the same objective evidence.

sig_f37045548e9ce75b2298.description: Contract name: "Arrangement and execution of tourist routes in the undergrounds of the Queen Luiza Adit" Basic information: The contract concerns the arrangement and execution of tourist routes in the undergrounds of the Queen Luiza Adit. As part of a single complex of underground workings, it is planned to commission two tourist routes. The route dedicated to the theme of elements will be fully enhanced and modernised, whereas the route dedicated to history will be a new product. As part of the contract, the Contractor is obliged to execute two complete tourist routes consisting of arrangement elements (scenography, structures, etc.), AV equipment, lighting, multimedia contents and multimedia installations, Ethernet and power supply networks, and electrical power installations. Descriptions of the subject-matter of the contract are contained in 4 design documents: 1. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition dedicated to elements, created on the basis of the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit together with appendices. Note: Appendix No. 2 to the concept and design contains an update of the specification of minimum technical parameters - it replaces the content of project pages 33 – 46 (point 4.3.6. Specifications of minimum parameters). 2. Concept and design of the new underground exhibition on historical themes created on the basis of the tourist routes in the Queen Luiza Adit together with appendices. Note: Appendix No. 2 to the concept and design contains an update of the specification of minimum technical parameters - it replaces the content of project pages 41- 49, regarding the specification of minimum parameters. 3. Execution of the installation design within the newly designed tourist routes located in the Queen Luiza Adit in Muzeum Górnictwa Węglowego w Zabrzu (appendices: 3a and 3b to the Description of the Subject-Matter of the Contract), 4. Execution of the installation within the newly designed tourist routes located in the Queen Luiza Adit in Muzeum Górnictwa Węglowego w Zabrzu (electrical sector) – Appendix No. 4 to the Description of the Subject-Matter of the Contract – in the part covering: a. purchase and delivery of outgoing cables between switchboards RTN-11, 12, 21, 22, 31 31.1, 31.2, 32, 33, 33.1, 41, 41.1 and TN-31, 32, 34, 35 and apparatus boxes at exhibition stations in accordance with the table (6. Cable list) placed on page 14-16 of project no. EP7-23-09/E1 (appendix no. 4 to the Description of the Subject-Matter of the Contract), b. laying of cables in workings and exhibition chambers, c. connection of cables to TN-S network switchboards, d. execution of required tests, measurements and handovers enabling their commissioning. Note: The remaining part (apart from the elements included in points a-d above constituting the subject-matter of the contract) of the scope included in the documentation referred to in point 4 has been implemented under a separate contract. With regard to the WiFi wireless network, the Contractor is obliged to select the qualitative and quantitative components of the indicated scope based on the following requirements: - Signal continuity: Full radio coverage without gaps in range along the entire length of the routes, - Seamless roaming: Ensuring an uninterrupted connection while moving with a VoIP device (switching between access points must take place imperceptibly to the user, without dropping the ongoing voice call, - Signal level (RSSI): The signal level anywhere on the route must not be worse than - 65 dBm, - Signal quality (SNR): The signal-to-noise ratio must be at least 25 dB, - Solution standard: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) or Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax), - Radio standard and band support: Full support for IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax or 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7) standards, - Multi-band operation (parallel band support: 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, 6 GHz), - Ensuring full backward compatibility for wireless devices and VoIP phones operating on older Wi-Fi standards. - Security and encryption: Support for the latest security standards: WPA3-Personal, WPA3-Enterprise and support for mixed mode (WPA2/WPA3 Mixed Mode), - Support for Management Frame Protection (PMF / IEEE 802.11w) protecting VoIP voice connections against Deauthentication/Disassociation attacks. - Support for QoS voice traffic prioritization, ensuring the supremacy of VoIP packets over other network traffic. - Construction and environmental resistance: - Dedicated casing adapted to difficult conditions prevailing underground, characterised by an IP rating of min. IP67 (full dust tightness and moisture/flooding resistance). - Power supply of devices implemented in PoE or PoE+ standard (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt). - Management and configuration: - Ability to centrally manage the operation of all access points (via a physical, virtual controller or central management system). - Built-in mechanisms for automatic optimisation of radio channels and transmission power depending on propagation conditions in the workings. Verification of the compliance of the implementation of the subject scope with contract requirements will be made on the basis of network parameter measurements carried out by the Contractor and the technical documentation of the installed devices. In connection with the above, the functional property description indicated above becomes binding for Contractors - which replaces the current description of the subject-matter of the contract for the wireless network - included in app. 3a and app. 3b. The scope of the contract does not include: AD.1.1 Station 15 Embankment is excluded from the procedure AD.1.2 The implementation of content for Stations 17 and 18 is excluded from the procedure. The complete musical work will be handed over for the implementation of the stations after signing the contract with the Contractor. AD.2.1 From Station 5 Belt ride – Audio play, the transport device is excluded AD.2.2 Station 23 In the Karlik train (content) is excluded from the procedure Both Station 15 Embankment and the delivery together with the assembly of the transport device will be covered by separate procedures. A detailed description of the subject-matter of the contract is contained in appendix 2 to the Tender Specification.

sig_f39e1119fdcfe02fd7c1.description: Short Description This Notice signals BIST's intention to go to market for the provision of Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services in support of the National Digital Twin Programme (NDTP) and is for Market Engagement purposes only. The National Digital Twin Programme is a BIST led programme developing trusted, secure and reusable digital twin capabilities across government and wider public sector partners. The programme develops open source technologies, interoperability mechanisms, data sharing capabilities and application-layer services to support improved decision-making through data and digital technologies. Description of the Scope NDTP is seeking to engage with suppliers capable of providing specialist Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services. The requirement will support the design, development, testing, deployment and continuous improvement of data-driven applications, analytics products, visualisation tools and supporting data pipelines across the NDTP portfolio. The scope may include the development of new applications and analytical capabilities, enhancement and extension of existing NDTP applications, creation of data ingestion and transformation pipelines, integration with nodes, node nets, APIs and data services, and the delivery of user-facing dashboards, maps, visualisations, analytical tools and decision-support capabilities. Suppliers may also be required to support geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, application deployment, technical documentation and transition to operational environments. The successful supplier will be expected to work within NDTP's open source delivery model, contributing code and associated artefacts through NDTP GitHub environments and supporting collaboration with government departments, public sector organisations, technical partners and other suppliers. To aid BIST in developing the specification, we are interested in furthering our understanding of the market and available capabilities. In particular, we would like to hear from suppliers with experience in application development, data engineering, analytics, visualisation, open source delivery, cloud-native technologies and integration of complex data services. Additional information: Additional Information Please note that should we proceed to market we will use the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) Spark DPS RM6094 to undertake this procurement. Only suppliers who are registered on the Spark DPS will be eligible to participate. If this opportunity is of interest, suppliers are strongly encouraged to register as soon as possible, as applications to join the DPS are assessed independently by GCA and processing times may vary. BIST intends to undertake the initial Spark DPS supplier filtering exercise during the week commencing 24th August. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this opportunity should ensure they are successfully registered on the Spark DPS and that their category selections align with the filters set out in Annex A before this date. Following the filtering exercise, BIST will issue a capability assessment questionnaire to the shortlisted suppliers. Completion of the capability assessment will be a mandatory requirement in order to be considered for invitation to tender. It is anticipated that the ITT will be published in September 2026. The contract is expected to have a value of up to £10.5 million and run until October 2029, with the option to extend for up to one additional year. This advance notice is intended to provide suppliers with sufficient time to complete Spark DPS registration and review their selected categories before the procurement is launched. Details can be found at https://www.gca.gov.uk/agreements/RM6094. Any queries relating to registering on the Spark DPS should be directed to GCA as BIST does not have any control over the process or requirements. Annex A - Spark DPS Filters Delivery Method AI & Automation Natural Language Processing Predicted Analytics Prescriptive Analysis Engineering / Materials Science Spatial Computing Data Data Presentation Location UK Security Above Official

sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.
sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?

sig_f3a77ce61c4837cba610.description: Oslo municipality would like to map whether there are market participants who have systems that can or are able to meet the municipality's needs, which are summarised below and described in the attached document. The requested system shall as a starting point not be a pure development project for the municipality, and ought to as far as possible be based on adaptations to the existing system(s). Oslo municipality currently has an agreement for the area that expires in the first quarter of 2027 and the system ought to be in operation immediately after the contract expires. Interested tenderers are asked to register their interest through the KGV system by submitting a short presentation of their system as well as a short description of any adaptation needs that are necessary to meet the municipality's needs. Based on the interest, Oslo municipality can select suppliers for further market dialogue (expected week 41/42). SUMMARY OF THE CONTRACTING AUTHORITY'S NEEDS Oslo municipality needs a cloud-based (SaaS) system that can, to the greatest possible degree, contribute to complying with the legal and regulatory requirements related to the Norwegian model, including the requirements for an electronic crew list in the Construction Client Regulation § 15, as well as follow-up of the Oslo model's seriousness requirements, and other needs closely related to this type of follow-up. The system ought, for this reason, to be able to facilitate (the list is not exhaustive): 1) Overview of ongoing projects and assignments within, among other things, building, construction and cleaning contracts with information on suppliers and sub-suppliers. 2) Overview of crews who have signed in and out in ongoing projects and assignments in the municipality. 3) Analysis and compilation of relevant information for identifying risks connected to contractual relationships. 4) Control, follow-up and reporting of contractual relationships.

sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.description: The purpose of this above-threshold Public contract for services awarded in an open procedure pursuant to Section 56 et seq. of the Public Procurement Act is the conclusion of (i) a contract for the implementation of an application / applications focused on supporting financial risk management for the needs of Risk Tools, HBK System – Rating Calculator (“HBK System – Rating Calculator”; “Implementation Contract”) and (ii) a subsequent contract for the maintenance, support and development of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (“Service Contract”; the Implementation Contract and the Service Contract collectively the “Contracts” or “Contractual Documentation”). The subject of the Public contract is the supply and implementation of a new application or applications focused on supporting risk management tools, and the provision of related services, specifically: - supply and implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator; - development of Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements; - independent validation of the developed Rating models; - services leading to the successful implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator in the Contracting Authority's environment; - provision of long-term support and maintenance and minor development for a period of 10 years from the implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator. Based on the Contracts, the subject of the Public contract will be realised with one supplier, whose tender will be evaluated as the most economically advantageous based on the evaluation of tenders. Rating calculator A rating calculator is a technological solution, i.e. a system / application or functional component that uses a Rating model to systematically evaluate entities. Rating model A rating model is a systematic tool used to evaluate a client's creditworthiness. The goal of the Public contract implementation is the simplification of processes, the use of modern technologies and approaches, and the flexibility of the HBK System – Rating Calculator fulfilling the Contracting Authority's premises. The Contracting Authority points out that through this Public contract it is seeking a supplier that will provide it with a complete solution, i.e. it will both supply and implement the HBK System – Rating Calculator (and ensure its support and maintenance), and create individual Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensure their independent validation. Rating models will be newly created in the HBK System – Rating Calculator with limited use of the Bank's historical client data. The Contracting Authority does not possess the know-how for the creation and implementation of Rating models and the selected supplier therefore cannot expect above-standard cooperation from the Contracting Authority in this area. The Contracting Authority is able to provide the selected supplier with a limited range of data, but is not able to provide the scope of data on which it would be possible to calibrate a Rating model. The subject of the Public contract is the supply, implementation, maintenance, development and support of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (including the development and validation of Rating models), the detailed specification and components of which are set out in detail in the annexes to the Contracts. The performance will be divided into two Contracts, i.e. into (i) the Implementation Contract and (ii) the Service Contract. Based on the Service Contract, the service, maintenance, support and minor development of the System will take place. A closer specification of the subject of the Public contract is regulated in other parts of the Tender documentation, especially in the binding drafts of the Contractual Documentation – Annex No. 6 and 7 of the Tender documentation, and the Technical specification of the Public contract – Annex No. 8. For more, see the TD.
sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.title: HBK System – Rating calculator

sig_f407665173fc522d220b.description: Ballerup Kommune wishes to purchase a system that can handle the municipal salary negotiation process for all stakeholders. In a municipality, salary negotiations take place with the involvement of both employees, managers, and trade unions and employee representatives, which makes the task complex. The salary negotiation process involves data from several systems and many different stakeholders: HR, managers both centrally and locally, employee representatives and trade unions, as well as all employees in Ballerup Kommune. Today, the task is handled through manual updating and circulation of Excel sheets with a high risk of errors and GDPR breaches. The purpose of the purchase is to ensure a quality boost of data in salary negotiations, make it more person-independent and transparent for the stakeholders. There is also a desire to reduce the time spent by HR, employee representatives and managers in connection with the salary negotiation process. Ballerup Kommune has prepared a requirements specification and would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue based on this requirements specification and, naturally, a demonstration of the supplier's solution. It is important to note that a development project is not desired, but rather a standard solution that supports our requirements. The market dialogue will be held at the following times: d. 6. October 2025 10.00-15.30 d. 7. October 2025 12.00- 15.30 d. 9. October 2025 11.30- 15.30 2 hours are allocated per supplier. Suppliers who may be interested in participating in a market dialogue are requested to show their interest by writing to Ballerup Kommune via Mercell no later than 1. October 2025, stating which date and time among the three possible ones above. Ballerup Kommune reserves the right to reject any interested companies if there are too many interested parties or if the company has a solution that is currently only on the drawing board.
sig_f407665173fc522d220b.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding intended procurement of salary negotiation system

sig_f42aadd4d4ff049f50f4.description: The Home Office Enterprise Networks & Infrastructure function is preparing an award with competition to procure a Hosting Capability Supplier. The successful supplier will provide a comprehensive 24x7x365 operational support capability, alongside outcome-based engineering, transformation, and service delivery services across the Home Office technology estate. The objective is to establish a simplified and integrated operating model that delivers improved service resilience, enhanced automation, accelerated technology transformation, and a single point of accountability for hosting-related services. The scope of the requirement is expected to include: • Platform services spanning on-premise, cloud and hybrid environments. • Hosting, cloud, network and infrastructure operational support and engineering services. • Legacy infrastructure and application support, including the transformation and modernisation of services to align with future-state technology strategies. • Technology services covering datacentre, platform, storage, backup, virtualisation, operating systems, network infrastructure, cloud services and associated management tooling. The Hosting Capability Supplier will absorb service elements currently delivered through the Home Office's Network Capability Services (NCS) and Private IaaS contracts that are not provided by internal Networks & Infrastructure engineering teams. This includes integrating operational support capabilities into a single commercial construct, simplifying supplier engagement, reducing contractual complexity, and removing longstanding interdependencies across the hosting, platform, cloud, network, and infrastructure landscape. The successful supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with internal engineering teams, strategic technology partners, and other service providers to support an integrated service management model and deliver continuous service improvement. The supplier will also support the transition from legacy technologies and applications, driving resilience, automation, transformation, and operational excellence whilst maintaining businesscritical services throughout the contract lifecycle. Lot 1: . None

sig_f42dfbd119f70092f405.description: INTRODUCTION Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender. BACKGROUND INFORMATION The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise. STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide: • licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route; • licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting; • Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise; • support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice; The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services. Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value. 5.0 PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME 7.0 Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027. Lot 1: .
