sig_f4ba51b9d7725d6de9a8.description: Domestic abuse remains one of the most significant public protection challenges facing South Wales. For people assessed as being at highest risk of serious harm or homicide, timely safeguarding interventions and effective multi-agency coordination can be critical in reducing harm and improving safety outcomes. South Wales Police and its partners currently deliver safeguarding through the Multi-Agency Risk Assessment Conference (MARAC) process. MARAC is a long-established mechanism that brings organisations together to share information, assess risk and coordinate actions for victims experiencing high-risk domestic abuse. It remains one of the most important safeguarding arrangements available to public services and plays a vital role in protecting some of the most vulnerable people in society. However, the current model is under increasing pressure. Across South Wales, more than 5,000 high-risk domestic abuse cases are managed annually through seven separate MARAC arrangements operating across Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan, Rhondda Cynon Taf, Merthyr Tydfil, Bridgend, Neath Port Talbot and Swansea. Together, these arrangements account for approximately 44% of MARAC demand across Wales. Different governance structures, processes and operating approaches have evolved over time, resulting in variation in delivery, increasing administrative burden and challenges in maintaining consistency across the region. Demand continues to increase whilst cases become more complex. In some areas, approximately 70 cases may be discussed during a single weekly MARAC process, and concerns have been raised regarding delays between referral, discussion and action. National reviews, safeguarding investigations and wider research have highlighted issues relating to fragmented information sharing, inconsistent processes and delays in identifying and responding to escalating risk. South Wales Police, working alongside regional MARAC governance groups, the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner and wider safeguarding partners, has identified an opportunity to explore whether a different approach could deliver faster, more consistent and more effective safeguarding outcomes. The challenge has been developed following significant stakeholder engagement and reflects a shared recognition that future approaches may need to move beyond the traditional meeting-based MARAC model. ________________________________________ The Challenge We are seeking innovative organisations to help South Wales Police and its partners explore how high-risk domestic abuse safeguarding could operate differently in the future. This challenge is intentionally outcome-focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model. Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their expertise could help develop a more responsive, coordinated and sustainable safeguarding model for South Wales. The challenge is not simply about introducing new technology or digitising existing MARAC meetings. Whilst technology, data and artificial intelligence may form part of the solution, partners have identified the need to explore wider service, governance and operating model redesign. We are interested in organisations capable of helping answer questions such as: • How can risk be identified, prioritised and escalated more effectively? • How can organisations work together more dynamically and efficiently? • How can safeguarding actions be coordinated more effectively across agencies? • How can professionals spend less time managing administration and more time safeguarding vulnerable people? • How can information be shared more effectively whilst maintaining appropriate governance and accountability? • How can future models remain practical, affordable and sustainable? • How can innovation support improved safeguarding outcomes without creating additional complexity? Applicants should not assume that technology alone is the answer. We welcome proposals that combine service design, systems thinking, operational redesign, governance innovation, behavioural approaches, digital innovation, data, analytics and artificial intelligence to explore how multi-agency safeguarding could evolve. ________________________________________ Desired Outcomes We are interested in approaches that can contribute towards measurable improvements in one or more of the following areas. Safeguarding Outcomes • Earlier identification of escalating risk. • Faster safeguarding interventions. • Improved protection for people at highest risk of harm. • Reduced repeat victimisation. • Improved management of complex and repeat cases. • Better safeguarding outcomes for victims and families. Victim Experience • More consistent safeguarding support regardless of location. • Improved coordination between agencies. • Reduced delays in accessing support. • More responsive safeguarding interventions. • Improved confidence in safeguarding processes. • More person-centred approaches to safety planning. Professional Practice • Reduced administrative burden. • Better access to relevant information. • Improved coordination and communication between organisations. • Better visibility of decisions and actions. • Improved accountability and action tracking. • More professional time focused on safeguarding activity. Service Delivery and Equity • Reduced variation between different MARAC arrangements. • More consistent safeguarding approaches across South Wales. • Improved information sharing. • Better visibility of risk. • More equitable safeguarding outcomes regardless of geography. • Improved partnership working. System Outcomes • Better use of public resources. • Reduced duplication of activity. • Improved operational intelligence. • Improved governance and oversight. • Stronger evidence for future service transformation. • Improved understanding and measurement of safeguarding outcomes. Sustainability • Affordable and scalable approaches. • Long-term sustainability beyond the funded project period. • A realistic route to implementation. • Approaches capable of supporting future adoption in other regions where appropriate. • Creation of capability that can support future safeguarding transformation. Applicants should clearly identify which outcomes their project is expected to influence and explain how impact will be assessed. Phase 1: Discovery and Concept Development This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 1 Contracts for Innovation Cymru competition. South Wales Police and partners recognise that this is a complex system challenge. Whilst the need for change has been identified, there is not yet a single agreed solution or future model. This competition is therefore focused on discovery, exploration, evidence generation and concept development. We are seeking organisations capable of helping define what a future safeguarding model might look like, which has the potential for scalability across other MARAC areas and what practical steps may be required to implement it. Funding Allocation and Project Details Competition Type: Phase 1 Discovery and Concept Development Funding Available: Up to £60k per project Number of Projects: Up to 6 projects The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, i.e., should additional funding become available Lot 1: . None

sig_f4c779028a33c8757ac6.description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. § 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America’s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team’s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only “lead” one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating “leads” will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Underwater Radiated Noise Source Level: Underwater radiated noise source level is defined using the radiated noise level (RNL). RNL is the source level that has been calculated assuming sound pressure decays geometrically with distance from the source, with no influence of the sea-surface or seabed and is often used to quantify source levels of vessels. Below are the equations for URN limits for self-propelled commercial vessels. The limits are stated in decidecade band RNL (dB re 1 ?Pa2·m2). Frequency range / Hz Transit / dB re 1 μPa2·m2 10-100 169.5+1.5log10(f) 100-1000 191-9.5log10(f) 1000-50000 199-12log10(f) Operational Conditions: Vessels designs should be able to meet or exceed the specifications under what would be considered normal operational parameters for that vessel. The intent is not for these vessels to need to employ special operations or change their normal patterns, routes, or timetables to achieve the reductions. Normal operations should be considered: Typical transit/operating conditions Transit non-working; and working for under-tow/station keeping 85% maximum continuous rating Measurement Standard: ANSI/ISO standards or an appropriate and defensible adaptation of these to suit the needs and conditions of the operational state should be described. Fuel efficiency estimation methods should be described based on industry and/or international reporting requirements (e.g. Class society, IMO) Deliverables The main deliverable is a preliminary vessel design that includes some technical details including the hull form for hydrodynamics and fuel efficiency and the selection of propulsion and power systems (engines, propellers, and other machinery) based on the ship’s operational requirements and sufficient to meet the design specifications of the Challenge. Designs should also be validated for general stability and load analyses for the ship’s safety under various conditions. Design analysis should include the technology combinations, design adjustments, machinery and propulsion arrangements that achieve desired efficiency and URN specifications. Designs should note the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Each design must include a full breakdown of the anticipated costs compared to a conventional design, including an anticipated ROI timeline and total ROI for the anticipated lifetime of the vessel. This should include a description of the additional costs for each technology element and the design and anticipated construction costs. There is no preferred technology or fuel/engine approach, but final reports should describe in reasonable detail those arrangements and technology combinations used to achieve the specifications. Since this is a concept demonstration for feasibility and economic achievability, challenges and barriers to meeting design specifications should be explicitly described. This should include findings regarding cost differences in achieving partial reductions; for example, the difference in cost between reducing fuel consumption increased rapidly after a certain point or the achievability of URN reduction became exponentially more expensive after a specific dB reduction. It should also include barriers to technology sourcing or availability and the realities of potentially building these vessels in the shipyard, i.e. does the experience exist at U.S. yards to integrate the design technologies and arrangements? These design components, technology and cost evaluations, and lessons learned should be included in a final report that can be made publicly available. Any intellectual property or business sensitive information, to include design plans and/or drawings, results of modeling, or technology or cost specifics will remain internal to the project team and Maritime Administration as not to undermine any competitive advantage. The final deliverable is participation in a debrief with MARAD to share results and lessons learned. There may be opportunities to debrief with other Challenge teams, pending willingness and interest to do so. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION: MARAD will provide funding through a cooperative agreement for the execution of this Design Challenge. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit MARAD to make any award. To be considered for selection, the contractor participating in the Challenge must be able to complete it within 18 months from time of award. The final report and other summary materials will be publicly available and posted to the META webpage. Proposals in response to this RFP are limited to 20 pages and must be received within 120 days of the publication of this notice. Proposals will be screened for use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools. Any use of AI tools in generating content for the proposal must be clearly identified and justified. MARAD is not responsible for reimbursing the costs that applicants incur to prepare and submit their proposals in response to this RFP. sig_f510cbfdc0ade476dc58.description: The subject of the procurement was an information system intended for the management of parking enforcement, which is procured as a SaaS service. The City of Pori’s existing parking enforcement system, Helga supplied by Fujitsu, does not meet all the city's needs. Updating the system to meet current requirements is necessary. Data from the existing system will be transferred to the new system in connection with the system replacement. Currently, the parking enforcement system is used by 2 officers and 7 parking inspectors. Parking penalty notices are entered into the system annually at approximately 20 000 units. Payment demands are issued at 500-800 units/month. Decisions on requests for administrative review are posted at approximately 1000 units/year. The new system must be able to handle all stages from the entry of a parking penalty notice up to statistics. A parking inspector's duties include: writing the penalty notice, photographing the situation, saving the images to the relevant penalty notice item, and printing the penalty notice. The parking inspector must also identify the vehicle based on the registration plate and the vehicle's location on the map. The parking inspector's tools are a smartphone and a penalty notice printing device. Customers must be able to check the details of the penalty notice they received, including images, electronically. Requests for administrative review must be able to be made electronically within this system. Material from the parking inspectors accumulates in the parking enforcement system and is held in the system for processing by the officer. Reports and statistics are obtained from the system. Provision must be made for a change in the number of users in the system. As an option, police users may be introduced to the system, whose use corresponds to that of a parking inspector. Content and objectives of the procurement The contents and objectives are guided by the laws governing parking enforcement and personal registers. Personal data is processed within the service. One of the objectives of the procurement is to increase work efficiency, in particular by reducing manual work, thereby allowing focus on substantive expertise. The procured system is sought to provide operational reliability and modern system usability. The system is also sought to automate manual work steps, thereby achieving efficiency in work performance and working time savings. The system must be a ready, tested entity and the required features must be deployable at the start of the contract period. The deployment of the system includes multiple interfaces. As the system provider develops the system such that, as the SaaS service evolves, new work-facilitating and speed-enhancing functions are added to it, the Contracting Authority has the right, on the basis of this tendering procedure, to also deploy new functionalities. The procured system must have interfaces to other systems and services required by the Contracting Authority, such as enforcement, payment demands and other mailings mentioned in the requirements specification, mobile payment operators, and Traficom's vehicle systems, among others. In addition, the Contracting Authority has identified that in the following entity, some of the matters related to the service or operational chain will be implemented in cooperation with third parties: Implementation of the vehicle removal function, OPTION.

sig_f5358920149b178e1a2b.description: London Underground (LU) is seeking to procure train gauging measurement systems to measure the following aspects of it's Rolling Stock: • Thermal imaging - to identify issues with overheating components including but not limited to; brake resistors, bearings, traction equipment, HVAC, brake blocks, wheel pans, bearings, traction motors, gearboxes etc. • Video imaging - to identify issues with out of gauge elements on the rolling stock including but not limited to; graffiti, broken windows, missing / misaligned equipment cover panels, missing / damaged collector shoes (both 3rd and 4th rail shoe gear), damage to under frame equipment e.g. from ballast strike or striking from foreign objects etc. The imaging capability should cover both sides of the vehicle, under frame and roof, and identify the individual vehicle by unit number(s). It is expected to trial the equipment at 2 locations for a period of between 6 - 12 months and the equipment shall work for multiple unit and single unit train configurations. The solution shall capture and store images with included data quality flags (e.g. time/date stamp etc.). Images shall then be processed using Machine Learning / Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) to identify defects for the attention of maintenance staff. For the duration of the trial, the post capture images shall be made available to view via a web based portal, accessible from the TfL Corporate network and TfL computers (laptop, desktop, thin client, tablet and mobile devices). All data captured during the trial shall remain the property of TfL and not be available to suppliers to further develop their system(s) without prior consent. Upon completion of the trial, TfL may proceed to full procurement of the successful product. Lot 1: .

The resulting contract will play a key role in enabling person-centred, digitally enabled integrated care, improving information sharing, reducing administrative burden and supporting better outcomes for citizens across Wales. FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Air Force Research Laboratory, Directed Energy Directorate (AFRL/RD) BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TITLE: TACTICAL BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: This is the Initial Announcement of BAA FA9451-24-S-0001, BAA With Closed Calls BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT NUMBER: FA9451-24-S-0001 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) NUMBER(S): Not Applicable (N/A). No assistance instrument or CFDA opportunities exist under this announcement. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a five (5) year Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) describing the research areas of interest for the Directed Energy Directorate. This BAA approach allows for proposal submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of Calls at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://sam.gov). Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. This annual review and subsequent amendment to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016 to publish the BAA no less frequently than annually. As technical requirements are identified, Calls may be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent Calls will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information peculiar to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the Call. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS OVERARCHING BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each Call announcement. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call shall be governed by the provisions of the FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the due date and time specified in the Call because of security delays will be considered late”. Furthermore, note that if offerors utilize commercial carriers in the delivery of proposals, they may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition is unrestricted. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition In Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM in the event this announcement is amended, and for the posting of Calls. ANNOUNCEMENT MODIFICATIONS: Due to the dynamically evolving nature of US warfighter directed energy needs, this announcement is potentially subject to include updates, revisions, or additional topic areas. Therefore, Offerors are highly encouraged to continually monitor SAM to ensure they receive latest guidance to this announcement. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this announcement may be Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, or Firm Fixed Price. There are no opportunities for Other Transactions, Grants, Cooperative Agreements, or other types of non-FAR instruments under this announcement. Cost-type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a cost-type contract cannot be awarded. Online registration instructions can be accessed from the SAM at https://sam.gov. These FAR and DFAR level representations and certifications are required in addition to the representations and certifications that may be attached to each Call. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. All potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific Call. However, the Air Force reserves the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a Call. There is no limit on the number of contracts that may be awarded to an individual Offeror. It is in the Offeror’s interest to visit SAM and ensure that all the Offeror’s data is up to date from SAM and other databases to avoid delay in award. SAM allows firms interested in conducting business with the federal government to provide basic information on business capabilities and financial information. To register, visit https://www.sam.gov. During the security review process, if it is determined that personnel listed to perform work are identified as potentially having a conflict of interest/commitment, the Government will not award the contract. a) Security Risk Review. Each proposal submission will be subject to a Security Risk Review prior to selection for award. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management. b) Security risk review for these subject proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews. c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023 t. The potential security risk factors are set forth below: Potential security risk factors: (see TACTICAL BAA Announcement_20241112 update in Attachments for image) Actions Required by Applicants at proposal or white paper submission: a. In accordance with AFRLI 61-113, S&T Protection, Applicants/Recipients are required to submit the following documentation with their proposal: (i) Standard Form 424, “Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile (Expanded) AND (ii) Security Program Questionnaire AND (iii) “Privacy Act Statement” consent form for each Covered Individual that is also signed by the Applicant as that Individual’s Sponsor. In the event a security risk is identified, and the Government has determined the security risk exceeds the acceptable threshold, the Applicant/Recipient will be notified and informed of the termination/decline of award. The Government will only provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. By submission of the Research and Related Senior Key Person Profile and Security Program Questionnaire, the Applicant agrees to comply with the following: a. To certify that each covered individual who is listed on the application has been made aware: (1) of all relevant disclosure requirements, including the requirements of 42 U.S.C. § 6605; and (2) that false representations may be subject to prosecution and liability pursuant to, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §§287, 1001, 1031 and 31 U.S.C. §§ 3729-3733 and 3802. See National Science and Technology Council Guidance for Implementing National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) on National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development (January 2022). b. To establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity. c. To exercise due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Senior/Key Personnel in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. Actions Required by Covered Individuals: a. Covered Individual. An individual who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the scientific development or execution of a research and development project proposed to be carried out with a research and development award from a Federal research agency; and is designated as a covered individual by the Federal research agency concerned. See 42 U.S.C. § 6605, Definitions. (For purposes of this BAA, “covered individuals” are all Senior/Key Personnel.) b. Federal law requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by 42 U.S.C. §6605, must be disclosed at the time of proposal submission, for all covered individuals. The Government may require an updated disclosure during the performance of any research project selected for funding. The Government will require an updated disclosure whenever covered individuals are added or identified as performing under the funded project. c. Covered Individuals are also required to sign the “Privacy Act Statement” and provide such signed statement to the applicant for submission with the proposal. d. Any decision to accept a proposal for funding under this announcement will include full reliance on the individual’s statements. Failure to report fully and completely all sources of project support and outside positions and affiliations may be considered a material statement within the meaning of the False Claims Act, 31 U.S.C. 3729, and constitute a violation of Federal law. Actions required by Performers during period of performance: a. Applicant/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile as an annual requirement. In addition, whenever a new covered individual(s) is to be added or identified as performing under the funded project, a new Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile will be required prior to continued performance. b. If, at any time, during performance of this award, the Applicant/Recipient learns that its Senior/Key Research Personnel (including any sub awardee personnel who receive this designation) are or are believed to be participants in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have Foreign Components with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer, the Applicant/recipient will notify the Contracting/Grants Officer within 5 business days of awareness. c. This disclosure must include specific information as to the personnel involved and the nature of the situation and relationship. The Government will review this information and conduct any necessary fact-finding or discussion with the Applicant/Recipient. The Government’s determination on disclosure may include acceptance, mitigation, or termination of the award. d. Failure of the Applicant/Recipient to reasonably exercise due diligence to discover or ensure that neither it nor any of its Senior/Key Research Personnel involved in the subject award are participating in a Foreign Government Talent Program or have a Foreign Component with a strategic competitor or country with a history of targeting U.S. technology for unauthorized transfer may result in the Government exercising remedies in accordance with federal law and regulation. e. The provisions concerning this disclosure will be included in each award. f. The Applicant/Recipient will be required to flow down this provision to all sub awardees who have personnel designated as Senior/Key Research Personnel as a result of their involvement in the performance of the research. sig_f596b3eab26c355dea2e.description: This is a post-contract notice for procurement 603797 / Istekki Oy - DPS 566026 - Sisäinen kilpailutus - tervo.fi ja tuusniemi.fi verkkosivu-uudistus. In this internal call-off competition under Istekki Oy's dynamic purchasing system "566026 / Digitaaliset asiointipalvelut: Teknologia,- kehitys-, toimitus-, tukipalvelu-, asiantuntijapalvelu-, konsultointi- ja valmisratkaisut sekä alusta- ja lisenssipalvelut 2025 - 2032 (DPS)", Istekki is running a tender process for WordPress websites implemented as a SaaS service for two municipalities. The website is implemented as a multisite entity. The sites can be made with the same theme, but fonts, colours, etc. according to the customer. Not all elements will necessarily be used by both customers. The publication of the websites will be done in a single phase. The supplier must offer the cost of the whole, including the deployment project and ongoing maintenance, where ongoing maintenance means technical maintenance of the website, security updates, etc. Istekki offers the user organisation of the website 1 and 2 level support, the supplier's 3 level support is implemented on an as-demand basis. The publication of the websites must take place as a multisite entity at the latest during Q3/2026, a more precise schedule will be agreed at the start of the project. The contracting authority shall supply the user interface designs and text content, on the basis of which the supplier shall implement the development of the website in cooperation with the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall draw up a wireframe version of the user interface for the tender process, which gives direction and an indication of the future website. The contracting authority is also responsible for drawing up the final user interface design. The supplier is responsible for the technical implementation of the website based on the user interface materials supplied by the contracting authority, and the user interface design will be refined and supplemented during the implementation phase in cooperation with the contracting authority and the supplier. Further development can be purchased for the procured solution during the contract period. The procurement aims at solutions already in production in the first phase. The procurement includes at least two separate identical environments from the supplier: production and testing/training environment. Development is carried out in the supplier's separate environment. Persons defined by the contracting authority (can be personnel of the contracting authority or the customer) must have the opportunity to test the web service in the testing/training environment. The call-off competition is carried out in DPS basket 3. WordPress technology and licences as well as platform services and ready-made solutions. The subject matter of the procurement and the requirements concerning it are described in detail in this invitation to tender and other procurement documents. The contracting authority shall select one (1) supplier with which it will enter into a contract. The procurement contract shall be used solely by Istekki Oy and the parties to the resulting contract shall be solely Istekki Oy and the selected supplier. For the sake of clarity, it is noted that Istekki's customers are not parties to this call-off competition or the procurement contract concluded on the basis of it. The procurement quantities presented in the invitation to tender are estimates, and the contract does not constitute a volume purchase obligation for the contracting authority.

Explanatory note: The Beerse municipal spatial structure plan was approved in 2007. Although the spatial principles and vision from this structure plan are still relevant to a certain extent, a revision of our vision of space is necessary. This revision serves to integrate current social and climate challenges and to tackle the further growth and development of the municipality in a sustainable and smart manner. The spatial policy plan will become a new framework that will guide the spatial development of the municipality for the coming years. The desired long-term spatial development is laid down in a strategic vision. Spatially, Beerse is characterised by a strong interaction between open space, housing and economic development. The municipality has extensive agricultural, natural and forest areas that have significant landscape, ecological and recreational value. The residential centres of Beerse and Vlimmeren offer an attractive residential environment and fulfil an important role within the regional housing structure, partly due to their location near Turnhout. In addition, Beerse forms an economic engine within the Noorderkempen thanks to the presence of important companies and business parks, whilst the canal zone along the Dessel-Turnhout-Schoten Canal acts as an important spatial and economic structural backbone. The challenge for the future consists of balancing quality residential developments, economic growth and the safeguarding of open space with each other in a sustainable manner. For three themes to be determined in more detail, this vision will subsequently be translated into policy frameworks in which the spatial choices for the medium term are named more concretely. The spatial policy plan constitutes a growing policy plan. Policy frameworks must be capable of being added to or adjusted in a simple manner at a later stage. It is very important to the municipality that the policy frameworks are concrete and achievable. Together with the spatial policy plan, a strategic plan-EIA is drawn up which maps out the potential environmental effects of the spatial policy plan and ensures that the overall integral impact is positive and negative effects are avoided or minimised through mitigating measures. The assignment is methodological, procedural and substantive. We also explicitly request support in mapping out a communication and participation process. Place of service delivery: De Loods, Dennenlaan 1, 2340 Beerse
sig_f59e28a7f7290791848d.title: Drawing up of a Beerse municipal spatial policy plan incl. plan-EIA

sig_f5a857846228214bb7db.description: This is a request for information and part of a market survey. The objective is to gather information from suppliers for the planning of the procurement of a workshop operation and production management system. The aim of the request for information is to obtain information from the market on the comprehensiveness of solutions, pricing models and implementation methods. In addition, the aim is to understand suppliers' capability to implement integrations and automation, and to utilise artificial intelligence. The request for information will also ascertain suppliers' references, particularly in workshop operations of a corresponding scale. Furthermore, suppliers' responsibility will be evaluated, for example with regard to energy efficiency and compliance with the ISO 14001 standard. KLOY needs a system to support track infrastructure maintenance that facilitates production planning, management and reporting. Approximately 30 people work in the workshop operations, and there are 28 workstations. Four computers and a few mobile devices are in use. KLOY is responsible for procuring the users' terminal equipment. Responses to the request for information questions shall be provided using the Forms form. A link to the form can be found in the links for this request for information. The information received through the request for information will be treated confidentially.
sig_f5a857846228214bb7db.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / Workshop operation and production management system

sig_f5cd10f3a75e2c5335f4.description: Description: The scope of this procurement is to provide specialized organizational, server-based documentary, and logistic support services in the context of very strategic testing-campaigns that will be carried out by the JRC. Specifically, these campaigns concern pre-normative testing of bidirectional charging technology, involving bidirectional charging column prototypes, electro-technical and ICT-analysis devices, and bidirectionally charging EV-prototypes, and thus require a high degree of specialists’, technological competence of the service provider in this field. sig_f5ded182d0ba99023e55.description: 1. Purpose Vico Homes Limited (Vico) is undertaking early market engagement to understand the capability of the supplier market to deliver either: • A single, fully integrated Finance, Procurement, HR, Payroll, and Talent Management solution, or • A modular, best-of-breed ecosystem (standalone Finance inclusive of procurement or stand-alone HR system inclusive of payroll), combining multiple interoperable platforms that collectively meet the organisation's requirements. This Premarket Engagement (PME) does not form part of any formal procurement process. Information gathered will inform the development of a Strategic Business Case, procurement strategy, and potential future tender. Suppliers responding to this PME are not advantaged or disadvantaged in any future process. 2. Background & Context Vico Homes Limited (Vico) was established on 1st April 2025 when Wakefield District Housing (WDH) rebranded to deliver our vision 'to build better futures and vibrant communities'. We are one of the UK's largest social housing providers, with over 33,000 homes across Yorkshire and our wider operating area across the North of England. We offer much more than bricks and mortar; our support goes far beyond the front door. We go the extra mile to deliver excellent customer services and provide a home to be proud of. To find out more about us please visit the link below: Welcome to Vico Homes | Vico Homes Vico currently operates its core HR, Finance and Procurement functions using Microsoft Dynamics Finance and Operations, which was implemented as an enterprise platform to support these corporate functions across the organisation. The solution is integrated with a small number of adjacent systems (Housing Management, LMS, Payroll Products) and supported by third‐party partners, with additional functionality delivered through bespoke power platform extensions and integrations. Vico currently delivers its payroll capability through a dedicated third‐party payroll solution (MHR I-Trent), which operates alongside the wider HR and Finance landscape. The payroll service has been implemented to meet statutory requirements and support accurate and timely payment for colleagues, with interfaces in place to exchange data with core HR and Finance processes. Learning and development is currently supported through a separate Learning Management System (LMS) via Learning Pool, which operates independently of the core HR platform and is used to manage learning records, compliance training, course administration and colleague development. While the LMS supports essential learning and development activities, it relies on integration points with Dynamics 365 to maintain accurate colleague data and reporting. This pre‐market engagement is intended to help the organisation better understand current market products, capabilities, deployment models, and approaches that could inform future procurement options. 3. Scope Overview The organisation is reviewing replacement options for its core Finance, Procurement, HR, Payroll, Learning, Talent, Time & Attendance, and Case Management systems. Operational requirements, compliance obligations, and strategic drivers (including digital transformation) mean that a new platform (or set of platforms) need to be procured and implemented within defined timeframes. A full list of requirements is included in Section 4 to assist suppliers in identifying alignment with their solution offering. Suppliers may respond based on their ability to offer: • (A) One unified cloud-based platform • (B) Multiple modules ecosystem (standalone Finance inclusive of procurement or HR system inclusive of payroll), from the same vendor ecosystem • (C) One of the products with proven integrations (standalone Finance inclusive of procurement or HR system inclusive of payroll) Through this exercise, Vico seeks to: • Understand the maturity and availability of market solutions. • Identify whether requirements are best met by a single platform or a modular architecture. • Assess typical cost models, implementation durations, and licensing approaches. • Explore integration capabilities, including open APIs and data exchange approaches. • Gauge suppliers' experience with UK public sector, housing associations, and charitable organisations. • Identify risks, constraints, and dependencies relevant to the implementation timeline. Please contact Vico for the full Pre-Market engagement document including System Requirements and Supplier Questionnaire Lot 1: .

We are cancelling the procurement. The contracting authority requested your tender for the Healthcare supplies and equipment 2024-2028 dynamic purchasing system (DPS) internal competition in accordance with this invitation to tender and its annexes. The subject of the procurement was medical machines and equipment for use by the Defence Forces: Monitors, Respiratory and monitoring equipment, Fluid warmer, Suction device, Syringe pump, Blood gas analyser, Ultrasound device, Multifunction device and Suction device for operating theatre. Intended use: The medical machines and equipment are intended for minor procedures and major surgeries. Place of use: The products to be procured will be used at all levels of care (e.g. tent, container, building, etc.). They will be used in all seasons, in all weather conditions domestically and in crisis management tasks abroad, as well as with NATO countries in various exercises. The products subject to the procurement and the services related to the products are presented in the invitation to tender, in the section "criteria for the subject of the procurement" and its annexes. See also the invitation to tender annex 1 contract chapter 4 "Subject of the procurement contract". Estimated scope of the procurement: the total value during the entire contract period was approximately 10M€, VAT 0%. The estimated scope was a non-binding estimate. The monitoring and anaesthesia monitor is intended for patient use when performing surgical procedures or monitoring the patient's condition before and after surgery (pre- and postoperative care). It operates independently as a medical device. The device must be capable of monitoring the patient independently. The device must be suitable for use in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises or operations. A portable monitoring monitor intended for patient work, which operates as an independent monitoring monitor in the monitoring of patients during transfers and monitoring of procedures. It operates independently as a medical device. The device must be capable of monitoring the patient independently. The device must be suitable for use in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises and operations.; A turbine or compressor-driven ventilator that operates as an independent ventilator with pressure or low-flow oxygen or without oxygen / other pressure gas source. When using supplemental oxygen, the ventilator must be able to use medical oxygen (100% O2) or oxygen produced by an oxygen generator (produced by an oxygen concentrator 93% O2). Must be capable of non-invasive and invasive ventilation of an adult patient in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises and operations.; The fluid warmer is intended for patient use when administering cold fluids (such as crystalloids or blood products). It operates independently as a medical device. The device must be capable of rapid and efficient heating and administration of fluids. The device must be suitable for use in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises.; An electric suction device intended for keeping the patient's airways open in the emergency or field medical chain using electric suction as an aid. The task of the suction is to be able to remove secretions from the airways by suction to secure the patient's breathing. The suction device is used at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises or operations.; A portable syringe pump intended for patient work. Operates as a single pump or infusion system. The device must be suitable for use in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises and operations.; A blood gas analyser used in point-of-care testing in the field, the task of which is to determine a separately defined blood count from a blood sample (fingertip, venous or arterial sample) as a rapid test. The analyser must be able to operate independently without being connected to the internet or an analysis centre via a WIFI or Bluetooth /etc. connection. Updating the device can take place via a Wifi / Bluetooth connection in connection with service and maintenance. The equipment must be able to provide an image of blood values as part of the diagnosis or monitoring of the patient's condition. The equipment is used at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises.; A portable and easily movable ultrasound device, which operates as an independent product in field conditions and provides information to support decision-making in medical examination. The device must be able to provide reliable information on the state of the abdominal and thoracic area. In addition, it must be possible to use the device as an aid for anaesthesia.

It must be possible to use the device for ultrasound examination of an adult patient in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises or operations.; The item to be procured is a multifunction device intended for patient monitoring, defibrillation and external pacing, which is delivered in a soft carrying case. Used in the Defence Forces' ambulances, aircraft, helicopters and Navy vessels in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises and operations.; An electric suction device intended for the suction of secretions (blood, fluids, faeces, etc.) in abdominal and thoracic surgeries of surgical patients in the field medical chain. The task of the suction is to be able to remove secretions from the surgical area to ensure the success of the surgery. The suction device is used at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises.; A turbine or compressor-driven intensive care ventilator with a screen, which operates as an independent ventilator with pressure or low-flow oxygen or without oxygen / other pressure gas source. When using supplemental oxygen, the ventilator must be able to use medical oxygen (100% O2) or oxygen produced by an oxygen concentrator (produced by an oxygen concentrator 93% O2). Must be capable of non-invasive and invasive ventilation of an adult patient in field conditions at the Defence Forces' field medical care sites and possibly during patient transport in ambulances, helicopters or aircraft in all seasons and in all weather conditions domestically, as well as in crisis management tasks and international exercises and operations.

sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.description: The City of Helsinki's Culture and Leisure Division is developing data-driven management and, in connection with this, visitor counting for its locations and related solutions. Visitor data is one of the most important key performance indicators for operations: visitor data is used, among other things, for resource allocation, operational planning and development, and for assessing the impact of operations. The goal of the visitor counting service is to collect comparable and accurate visitor data from the division's locations as automatically as possible for analysis and reporting needs. The SaaS (Software as a Service) provided by the supplier includes at least: • production of visitor data from the counting target according to the needs defined by the division • transmission of visitor data by providing an interface (interface service) for transferring data to the division's data warehouse • transmission of visitor data by providing a user interface (user interface service) for viewing the data • collection of visitor data from devices, as well as monitoring and reporting of data accuracy and coverage (incl. verification counts for measurement at defined intervals) • devices used for visitor data collection as a lifecycle service (HaaS service, Hardware as a Service): - installation, commissioning, maintenance, servicing, functionality testing and calibration of devices - monitoring of device operation - removal and recycling of device installations. The contracting authority is currently surveying the procurement of a new data platform and will put it out to tender in approximately late 2026. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to assist with integrations and to provide an interface from the visitor counting service to the data platform. The estimated total value of the procurement excluding VAT is 1 680 000,00 euros. The estimated value includes the actual contract period of two (2) years and, in addition, one (1) two-year (2) option period. The procurement is divided into three (3) different lots: - lot 1: indoor locations - lot 2: outdoor locations - lot 3: multi-purpose outdoor locations. The tenderer may submit a tender for as many lots as they wish. Tenderers will be selected for the framework agreement based on the most economically advantageous tender. Qualitative requirements (quality criteria) have been set as minimum requirements for the devices and services to be procured, which the offered devices and services must meet. In addition, the price comparison will compare the maximum prices per lot (hereinafter ceiling price) from cheapest to most expensive. The supplier provides a ceiling price according to the most demanding example location of the lot defined by the contracting authority. Based on the tender competition, a framework agreement will be concluded for the subject of the procurement, to which five (5) contract suppliers who have submitted the lowest ceiling price per lot will be selected, unless there are fewer tenderers meeting the requirements. The suppliers selected for the framework agreement do not have exclusive rights to the procurements covered by the framework agreement, but the contracting authority has the right to procure the same subject of procurement also from outside this framework agreement. The contracting authority also does not commit to specific procurement volumes during the framework agreement. A more detailed description of the subject of the procurement is described in this invitation to tender and its appendices. The locations in the lot have one or more entrances to the site. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different indoor locations. Such locations include, for example, libraries, youth centres, cultural centres and sports halls. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 80 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have one or more restricted or unrestricted entrances. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different outdoor locations. Such locations include, for example, fenced tennis courts, skate parks, events in urban space, beaches, outdoor islands and trails. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 82 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have several restricted or unrestricted entrances to the space and it includes several service points or spaces. Breakdown of visitor data is essential. Such locations include, for example, sports parks. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 38 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.

sig_f65cb197fb4b014a93db.description: 1 INTRODUCTION We kindly ask you to submit your response to this Request for Information concerning the planning of the procurement for a questionnaire and event management system. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of any potential tendering process. With this Request for Information, we aim to map supplier offerings regarding systems that support and provide a smooth and appropriate user experience for the end user. More detailed information on the subject of the procurement can be found in appendix 1 "Request for Information Questions" of this Request for Information. The end user of the procurement is Istekki and its owner-customers. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation, products potentially related to the use of the system, and contractual and commercial terms, such as pricing. 2 ORGANISING MARKET DIALOGUE Based on the responses to the Request for Information, market dialogue sessions will be organised where suppliers can present their own services, products and options for implementing the subject of the procurement. Based on the responses to this Request for Information, Istekki will select an estimated approximately 3–5 tenderers for the market dialogue. Any market dialogue sessions will be organised at a time specified by 24.3.2025 the contracting authority. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. sig_f6759cef6f60d4d38117.description: Market consultation for the purpose of preparing an award procedure for the development, provision, operation and maintenance of an AI platform with an AI service layer in the context of BARMER eCare. This AI service platform is to be operated in accordance with gematik standards within a trustworthy execution environment (TEE) that complies with the data protection and security requirements of the electronic patient record (ePR). Lot PAR-0000: eCareAI market consultation. The AI platform comprises a layer (AI service layer) in which various AI applications (= AI services) are operated. The various AI services process, structure and analyse individual health data and other relevant information of BARMER insured persons. Potential use cases include, for example, AI-supported chatbots, intelligent document organisation or process control. Medical evaluation, diagnosis or therapy recommendation is explicitly not the subject of the AI platform. The AI platform is to be developed step by step and continuously expanded. To this end, selected use cases with low complexity are initially to be implemented via an iterative approach. Building on this, the platform is to be successively supplemented with additional, increasingly complex AI services and functionalities. The AI platform is to be integrated into the newly emerging modular eCare app architecture, in which both the ePR and value-added services are present in the form of modules. The ePR and all other modules of the eCare app must be clearly demarcated from the AI platform so that the AI services do not have direct, uncontrolled access to the insured persons' data. In order to create a standardised and solid foundation for the use of AI technologies in the eCare app, a service provider for the development of an AI platform at the highest data protection level (ePR protection level, TEE environment) is to be procured in a first step. This includes classic development, operational, testing, monitoring and support activities as well as comprehensive documentation. As part of this market consultation, BARMER intends to determine the range of suppliers for commissioning external IT service providers to develop and operate an AI service layer for the eCare app. Furthermore, BARMER wishes to gain knowledge about the offered pricing models, price-relevant factors and the expected contract volume. The results of the market consultation are intended to form a solid basis for drawing up potential tender documents, such as the specification of services, price sheet and contract, for the subsequently planned award procedure.

sig_f68a23d04d9742df6e5e.description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code § 4001, 10 U.S.C. § 4021, 10 U.S.C. § 4022, and 10 U.S.C. § 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: • Acoustic communication and sensing • Adaptability • Advanced computing • Additive manufacturing • Architecture and advanced systems engineering • Artificial intelligence • Autonomy and control algorithms • Combat identification • Command and control (C2) • Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive • Complexity management • Critical infrastructure defense • Decision aids and C2 technology • DevOps and novel software development and integration • Directed energy (DE) • Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) • Economic security • Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) • Electro-optic/infrared sensors • Electromagnetic warfare (EW) • High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing • High voltage electric power systems and architecture • Human behavior modeling • Human-machine symbiosis • Industrial engineering • Integration and reliability technologies • Interoperability • Logistics • Modeling and simulation • Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing • Novel kinetic effects • Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) • Optical technologies • Photonics • Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) • Radar and adaptive arrays • Resilient systems • Robotics • Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing • Sensors and analytics • Signal processing • Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) • Strategy analysis technology • Supply chain analytics • System of systems • Undersea and seabed technology • Tactics development technology • Testing and data collection • Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology • Very low frequency (VLF) technology
