The subject of the procurement of Istekki Oy is various experts for development tasks, e.g. expert work related to the implementation of the Information Management Act, information architecture, development and analysis of customer experience, accessibility and non-discrimination, service design, business design, UX/UI design and innovation process, agile methods and impact. In total, the subject of the procurement is 20 different expert needs. The subject of the procurement and the requirements concerning it are described in detail in this invitation to tender and its annexes. This is a framework arrangement. The contracting authority will select a maximum of five (5) suppliers for each sub-area, with whom it will conclude sub-area-specific framework agreements. Based on the agreement concluded on the basis of this tender, Istekki may also offer experts and consulting as a service to its own customers. The procurement contract will be used only by Istekki Oy and the parties to the resulting agreement will only be Istekki Oy and the selected Supplier. For the sake of clarity, it is stated that Istekki's customers are not parties to this tender or the procurement contract concluded on the basis of it, nor are they parties, nor will they otherwise join the procurement. The estimated value of the procurement for four (4) years is 29 700 000 € (VAT 0 %). The estimated value is divided between the sub-areas as follows: - Expert role 1: Supervisor 1 650 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 2: Expert work related to the implementation of the Information Management Act 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 3: Information architecture expert 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 4: Enterprise architecture expert 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 5: Business architecture expert 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 6: ICT architect 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 7: Accessibility and non-discrimination 1 320 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 8: Disturbance demand analytics 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 9: Service design, business design, UX/UI design 1 980 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 10: Innovation process 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 11: Agile methods 3 300 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 12: Impact 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 13: Development of medication processes 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 14: Research work and information as support for development 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 15: Change management consulting 825 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 16: Change management training 7 425 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 17: Preliminary studies and analyses of operational development, management consulting 495 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 18: Service planning 1 650 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 19: Assisting tasks in service planning 330 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years - Expert role 20: Customer interface work tasks 1 650 000 € (VAT 0 %) / 4 years The procurement quantities presented in the invitation to tender are estimates, and the agreement does not constitute a quantity purchase obligation for the contracting authority. Expert work consists of tasks related to the implementation of the Information Management Act (Tihl) for customers. These may include mapping the current state of Tihl implementation, compiling the descriptions and specifications required by Tihl. In assignments, we may need either extra hands or leading experts to guide and consult the work.; Assignments consist of customer projects focusing on different aspects of information architecture. For example, defining and describing the information architecture aspects required by the Information Management Act, preparing an information architecture plan and developing an information architecture entity, supporting integration projects, preparing an information architecture model. In assignments, we may need either extra hands or leading experts to guide and consult the work.; In assignments, an enterprise architecture management model and its implementation plan that takes into account the entire organisation, legislation and guiding reference architectures are typically prepared. Some assignments may also relate to updating or implementing an enterprise architecture management model. In assignments, we may need either extra hands or leading experts to guide and consult the work.; Assignments focus on developing the customer's operations by clarifying and describing its operations and operating environment. Key descriptions of operations are, for example • Principle-level descriptions, e.g. strategy map • Current and target states • Actors • Services • Processes • Interaction • Information flows • Layer diagrams The business architect also participates in the preparation of information system procurements according to their role. Documents to be prepared are, for example: • Requirement specifications, especially functional requirements • Service stories • Use case descriptions and usability assessments; The content of the work is technology-oriented architecture design in our customer organisations, producing architecture descriptions and documentation. Assignments focus on developing the customer's ICT architecture, but experts can also act as technical experts in information system procurement projects in support of other experts. The focus is on assignments related to technology architecture. In assignments, we may need either extra hands or leading experts to guide and consult the work.; Need for accessibility assessments and reports, consulting (e.g. sparring on the interpretation of the law), improving cognitive accessibility (linguistically and visually), technical consulting, and holding training sessions.; We have a need for data collection and analysis, visualisation of problems (to make them easier to understand). In the work, one must be able to utilise industry models and trends as well as modern technology.

Creating plans and systemic thinking (what is the cause, what do the corrections affect) are part of the work. Assignments may relate to the development of Istekki's internal processes or to the investigation of demand for troubleshooting occurring at the customer interface. This may involve a multi-vendor environment.; We need extra hands for service design and UX/UI design to participate in various projects under Istekki's guidance. Regarding business design, the person must be more senior – they will act in a consultant-like manner under Istekki's guidance, strongly bringing their own expertise to the assignment. Tasks may include identifying and mapping needs, ideation and conceptualisation, designing and testing prototypes, measuring and evaluating, developing service processes, identifying and mapping stakeholders, UX/UI design, visual design, creating style guides, and building design systems. The expert must be able to work independently within the framework of the instructions received. Regarding the development of customer experience, the work may involve, for example, conducting interviews, observing usage and service, performing root cause analysis, drafting surveys, preparing and facilitating workshops, performing analyses (automation from feedback, etc.) and/or developing solution alternatives. The work may also involve coaching for staff and matters related to improving the quality of customer service, where a set of criteria is built against which we can reflect success in customer encounters and find essential areas for development. Assignments can be internal or external, involving the development of (digital) services and processes in projects. The operating environment may very well be a multi-vendor model. Some of the work is one-off and Istekki is always guiding the work.; Istekki's Innovation and Development Operations group is responsible for the development, coordination and maintenance of Istekki's innovation and development operations and the process intended for its management. Central to this work is providing suitable operating models, support (roles) and tools for the needs of Istekki and its RDI stakeholders. Support for the evaluation of the innovation process and operations Istekki's innovation and development operations are planned to be evaluated regularly, e.g., from the perspectives of their impact and risk management. Experts specialising in risk management and impact assessment can support Istekki in this work, both in designing the evaluation model and in implementing the evaluations. Support for the design and facilitation of innovation and co-development processes The design and implementation of an innovation and co-development process is, especially when involving several organisations or stakeholders, a multi-stage, demanding work package. In managing the processes, special expertise and active work input are needed for engaging and informing the participating parties, as well as for organising and facilitating innovation and co-development activities. By utilising expertise and additional work input in service design, development facilitation, participation and communication, the activities can be implemented with high quality and efficiency. Communication supporting innovation activities and their visualisation Communication is at the heart of innovation activities and its quality often affects success in innovation activities and their management. Istekki needs additional expertise and work input for producing communication solutions (e.g., an “instruction site” for innovation and development operations or an application describing the progress of operations) and materials (e.g., visualisation of processes and a written presentation style that meets the needs of stakeholders) that guide its internal and external stakeholders. The expertise required for these tasks relates to both technology development and communication skills. Market mapping of solutions and assessment of scalability To prevent overlapping and piecemeal development and innovation, it is important to assess the novelty and scalability of development proposals and solutions being developed. Additional expertise and work input for these actions can streamline and improve the quality of Istekki's innovation and development processes. Legal expertise required in the management of innovation activities Legal expertise is needed in the implementation of innovation processes, e.g., in the implementation of innovative procurements and co-development and testing processes, as well as in agreeing on the IP rights of process parties. Istekki's goal is also to develop a process for handling inventive ideas that accelerates employee inventions. Legal special expertise is needed for these tasks, e.g., regarding knowledge of procurement and invention legislation as well as contract law.; Istekki has defined agile operating models, their implementation, and is in the process of adopting Atlassian product family solutions in various functions (e.g., roadmaps, agile task management, etc.). The change in operations is supported by the company's agile coach experts. Istekki's operating model is evolving and the company is scaling agile methods and tools for wider use. The goal is also to support customers in adopting and utilising agile methods. We need extra hands for the development and implementation of Istekki's agile methods to participate in various assignments under Istekki's guidance. Assignments can be internal or external to Istekki. The operating environment is a multi-vendor environment. Development of Istekki's agile methods We need expertise to support the development of agile methods to suit Istekki's operating models. We need experts to train and support the further development of Istekki's agile methods. The required expert will help, together with Istekki's experts, to develop Istekki's agile development model. In addition, the expert will train key personnel in Istekki's agile methods. A few examples of training supporting agile methods are mentioned here (disc, wol, presentation skills, communication, self-leadership).

Implementation and training of Istekki's agile methods In addition, to assist Istekki's own Agile Coaches, we need experts to support the implementation of Istekki's agile methods by supporting Istekki's personnel and customers to act in accordance with agile methods. The work includes the implementation and training of Istekki's agile methods for experts and/or Istekki's external customers. The work includes the need to support experts and/or Istekki's external customers in their problem situations with agile methods. Agile transformation support Istekki's agile methods have been implemented in operational work, but we need expertise to help us better support other layers of the organisation in adopting agile operating models. In this point, we especially value previous experience in organisational operational change, where a transition has been made to using more agile methods. Atlassian expertise We need various support related to Atlassian products. The need for support relates to main user support and we also need support for the adoption of new Atlassian products. Istekki has Atlassian products (Cloud) in use, but we need support for their further development and more efficient utilisation.; Digital solutions are widely utilised in reforming and developing the operations of Istekki and its customers. Istekki has developed impact assessment methods, metrics and tools, which are intended to demonstrate the benefits/impact of the development measures or digital solutions being carried out to support decision-making and the evaluation of operations. This entity requires consultation both for the further development of methods and tools and for the implementation of demanding impact assessments. In addition to expert services, impact assessment may involve solutions or technologies utilised in measuring impact, with the help of which impact assessment data is produced. Impact method development: Consultation is needed for the entity of developing impact methods, operating models and metrics. As work, this means developing, implementing and adopting operating models, including e.g., creating and developing tools (e.g., a cost-effectiveness tool), describing work instructions from the perspective of roles, responsibilities and tasks, and creating templates (e.g., for marketing material and reporting on service impact). Method development aims for the following: -Aiming to identify hypothetical impacts for different target groups to support decision-making -Aiming to support the organisation's impactful management, e.g., identifying and considering impact factors in the procurement process, in the implementation of projects, in Istekki's data-driven management and in the customer organisation's data-driven management -Aiming to demonstrate the benefit of projects and continuous services. Development of impact metrics: Developing impact metrics for Istekki, the customer and national needs. From a national perspective, consultation would relate to, e.g., defining the data needs of ICT systems, collecting data from several different data sources and registers, which enables the ability to refine data into knowledge, changing social and healthcare operations in a cost-effective direction. Impact training: Developing the staff's impact expertise. A training package, e.g., for the entire staff (electronic training material/environment), training for key roles for different target groups (hybrid/in-person), training according to the impact operating model for roles and developers involved in the operating model (deepening expertise). Implementation of impact assessment projects (3-6kk): Implementation of impact assessments for ICMT services and others (e.g., operating models). The implementation of impact assessment projects includes collecting impact data according to metrics (e.g., from the customer's operations and systems), analysing and reporting development measures and supporting data-driven management/presenting recommendations to increase impact.; The uninterrupted medication process cuts across the operations of wellbeing services counties and Istekki's business operations. The goal is to support the development of both Istekki's business operations and new services, as well as customers' processes. Developing this sub-area requires solid expertise and long experience in developing medication and pharmaceutical service processes.; Istekki is profiling itself as an active development partner. Istekki has built various cooperation networks, e.g., with higher education institutions and special responsibility units. One goal is to develop understanding and collect new intellectual capital through various pilot and research projects. In the preparation of projects, there is a need for knowledge of various funding channels and instruments.; We are looking for change management experts for development projects and services delivered to Istekki's customers and to support the development of Istekki's internal change management and change capability. With systematic and human-centric change management, we help our customers adopt new operating models and ways of working to realise technology reforms and the benefits sought by them. Enabling our customers' operational change in connection with a technical system project is a prerequisite for the success of the implementation and the achievement of goals. We also support our customers in change management and organisational reform outside of system projects by creating and implementing, for example, new operating models. Change management experts are needed for customer assignments and projects.; When business or the operating environment changes, a need often arises for a neutral and quick creation of a situational picture, mapping of solutions and the formation of recommendations or development proposals.

The situation utilises expertise that is not available within the client's own organisation for the current need. Various preliminary studies, mapping of change requirements, proposals for resolving a difficult situation or project, and the creation of development plans are the core activities of management consulting. In assignments, it is often necessary to challenge prevailing ways of thinking, clarify the essential, and offer a path to sustainable change. A small team of Istekki employees and the provider's consultants typically work side-by-side with the client's representatives. In addition to general management experts, the team may include expertise related to, for example, architecture, service design, or digitalisation. Assignments may be linked to Istekki's current or later offered and delivered technical projects or services. Management consulting can also be utilised to support Istekki's internal or the client's project management in a challenging situation. Assignments are one-off, and Istekki is always directing the work and sets the objective for each assignment. The work takes place in cooperation with the client organisation's representatives and other experts.; Solution and service designers are involved in creating functional solutions and new Istekki services for our clients to streamline their everyday lives. The designers are involved in solving challenges arising from the client's needs by designing solution proposals together with other Istekki experts. A solution designer designs solutions for our clients that consist of services already in Istekki's service catalogue, for example, expert services, capacity services, various information systems and their implementation, as well as continuous services. The designer clarifies the client's needs together with the account manager, product owner, and solution architect, involving the client if necessary, and is responsible for coordinating the solution design phase and assembling the necessary experts to support the design. The designer participates in the procurement process if necessary, under the guidance of our procurement experts. The designer estimates the workloads of the solution with experts from different areas of Istekki and calculates a cost estimate for the solution and takes care of the preliminary booking of expert resources for the needs of the solution. The designer is responsible for the progress of the design phase and ultimately supports the account manager in reviewing the solution proposal and shaping it into a tender, typically for some kind of project. A service designer designs new services as part of Istekki's service catalogue to be utilised in future solutions. The designer clarifies the needs of the customer base more broadly together with stakeholders and defines the requirements and service description for the new service. The designer coordinates the progress of the service design phase. If necessary, the designer participates in organising the procurement by bringing the service requirements to the attention of the procurement organisation so that the end result of the procurement meets the needs of the service. The designer calculates the costs of the different areas of the service and designs the service's pricing model together with the product owner and business manager. The designer participates in the actual implementation and procurement phase of the service and the commissioning of the service. A central part of solution and service design is our enterprise resource planning system and the description of the solution in the system.; The key responsibilities in the supervisor role are as follows: • Responsible for the outputs and compliance of their group, in accordance with agreed processes • Acts as the supervisor of the expert group, responsible for competence development, sufficient expert capacity (incl. partners), and guidance • Responsible for planning and managing the group's operations • Participates in supplier management at an operational level • Responsible for the investigation and reporting of service deviations for their own group to account management and produces reports before service meetings • Participates in procurements for their own area of responsibility • Participates in the handling of customer feedback and complaints from the perspective of their own area of responsibility • Responsible for the implementation of information security and data protection in their own area of responsibility.; Istekki's account management has diverse work tasks that can be performed with the help of external resources. Sales support – expert work Sales support tasks are mainly administrative tasks that promote the time management of key account managers and account managers and ensure the possibility to focus on customer work. Sales support tasks can be diverse, such as preparing tenders or contracts, investigations related to invoicing, managing and coordinating internal cooperation, analysing sales success, or operating the different stages of the sales pipeline in the enterprise resource planning system. Preparing materials visually in accordance with the corporate image for operational, tactical, or strategic meetings is a sales support task. The person always acts as support for the designated account team. Development work and training services – expert work Assignments can be directed at Istekki's internal development work (e.g., development of systems, operational change, or processes). Development work can be various preliminary studies, specification work, or project expert work in different areas of sales. Assignments can also be various training services for those working at the customer interface, for example, related to sales psychology, closing a deal, managing customer experience, or sales analysis.; We are looking for a partner to implement internal change management training and coaching for Istekki. Training services can be offered to Istekki's personnel, but also to Istekki's clients.; The assisting tasks of service and solution designers are intended to be such that they can be taken on with a very low threshold.

sig_f6ab740da5a4a7ef18de.description: Trøndelag fylkeskommune (hereafter called the Contracting Authority or TRFK) shall procure a new energy follow-up system (EOS). The current system is Optima, owned by EG Norway and delivered by Entro AS. The annual combined energy use for the properties is in the range of 35 GWh electricity and 25 GWh thermal energy. Any measurements of street lights and or charging installations will come in addition, to the degree that these will be relevant for using this service/delivery. A well-functioning energy follow-up system is decisive for obtaining an overview and control of energy use, optimising operation and uncovering deviations, comparing status and development, as well as for exercising good energy management in the form of economic and environmental operations. Likewise, it is decisive to effectively report energy use to management at different levels in the organisation or to political leadership. Equivalently, it is desirable that EOS shall contribute to an overview of the use of water on the property, waste and any manual reporting of passenger transport. As Trøndelag county is already reporting through, among other things, Miljøfyrtårn and performs complete environmental reporting, it is requested that the new product has options as described in:Automatic report energy use in each building/facility, with an option for manual input where automatic meters are missing. Automatically report water consumption in each building/facility, with an option for manual input where automatic meters are missing. Automatically report waste amounts by type/fraction, with an option for manual entry where automatic meters are missing. Show climate gas emissions in CO2 equivalents connected to the operation of each building and for the entity in total. As far as possible report passenger transport to and from each unit and entity together. Where possible it is possible to integrate with the Contracting Authority's tool for property management and be able to read/write with this system. Where possible, the Contracting Authority can extract data from EOS to its own time series server in order to use data learning/artificial intelligence on the data basis. See annex 1 with sub-annex for a more detailed description of the extent.
sig_f6ab740da5a4a7ef18de.title: Energy follow-up system (EOS) - contract award notice

sig_f6b07aaffbe4935bdab7.description: See scope document market consultation further defined in paragraph 1.2: To define the scope for this market consultation, we have adopted a functional, solution‐agnostic perspective. Instead of prescribing specific tools or technologies, we describe what our business units must be able to achieve in the domain of automated parametric design. We refer to these as functional demands, which we define as follows: “A solution-agnostic definition of the functionalities required by the business, outlining what is needed from technology without specifying how they must be implemented”. This approach ensures that business needs remain central while allowing the market to propose the most suitable combination of technologies, methodologies, and consultancy services, including support for improving our internal processes, workflows, and procurement approach. Automated parametric design consists of three such functional demands: • Automated parametric design • Design automation • Automated generation of drawings, parts lists and BoM. The scope of this Market Consultation is primarily focused on automated parametric design and the implementation of a new operating model for insulator strings. The objective is to gain insight into market capabilities to automate and optimize the design process, with the aim of significantly reducing lead times from design to realization. Insulator strings have been identified as the initial focus area due to their potential to deliver the highest and fastest return on investment through automation. Following the successful implementation for insulator strings, the organization intends to progressively extend automated parametric design to additional asset components, including but not limited to mechanical tower components, civil works, and foundations. Respondents to this Market Consultation are therefore requested to: • Primarily address their proposed solutions and capabilities related to automated parametric design for insulator strings; • Provide a high-level future roadmap describing how their solution could be scaled or extended to support automated parametric design for other components; and • Provide a high-level implementation strategy.
sig_f6b07aaffbe4935bdab7.title: Market consultation CRM

The procurement includes consultancy services within the following service areas: · Agency management and governance · Organisational method and process development · Data protection and information security · General administrative legal advice (e.g. advice on public access and confidentiality and other administrative law) · Legal advice in connection with the Client's mandate at both national and EU level in connection with the new EU legal framework regarding the joint assessment by member states of the relative efficacy and safety of new medicinal products and medical devices. C16 - compressor station, C23 - generator set, C27 - silo, C28 - shed, C29 - archive, secondary access to existing building C2, C40 - greenhouse ; -Connection of the new medical complex to the existing underground tunnel C33 ; -Relocation of underground district heating, gas, water, sewerage and electricity networks for site clearance ; -Development of new access from Șoseaua Fundeni, roads, car parks and site green spaces. By awarding this contract, the Beneficiary aims to ensure the services for the supervision of the design and works execution activities in accordance with: 1.Law No 10/1995 on quality in construction, regarding: i. ensuring the verification of the correct execution of construction works through specialist site inspectors or specialized consultancy economic operators, throughout the works; ii.acting to resolve non-conformities, defects arising during the execution of the works, as well as design deficiencies, iii.carrying out the reception upon completion of construction works, as well as the final reception upon the expiry of the warranty period, under the conditions of the Law, iv. drawing up the technical book of the construction. 2.Annex No 2 to Government Decision No 1/2018, which regulates the general and specific conditions applicable in the case of the design and works execution contract. 3.The financing contract concluded with the Managing Authority for SOP, in order to implement the project. Likewise, through the contracting of Supervision services, the aim is to obtain the necessary specialist support also to: -Assist the Beneficiary in the relationship with bodies with verification and control powers (from MA, AA, ECA, ANAP, CC, to ITM, UAT, Local Police, Environmental Guard, etc.); - Verify how the investment objective behaves during the warranty period granted by the Contractor;- Increase administrative capacity regarding the management and administration process of a design and works execution contract. - Facilitate the making of informed decisions regarding changes brought to the works contract, as well as the scope/objectives associated with the investment, and the acceptance, or, where applicable, the issuance of Contractual Claims. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (1) of Law No 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the deadline by which any economic operator interested in participating in the public procurement procedure has the right to request clarifications or additional information in connection with the tender documentation is [20] days before the deadline for submitting bids. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (2) of Law 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the Contracting Authority shall respond to requests for clarifications addressed by economic operators by the established deadline. In accordance with the provisions of art. 160 para. (2) of Law 98/2016 with subsequent amendments and completions, the Contracting Authority establishes two deadlines within which it shall respond to all requests for clarification/additional information, as follows: I – 30 days before the deadline date for submitting bids II – 12 days before the deadline date for submitting bids.The deadlines for responding to clarifications have been established so that economic operators have an adequate period to analyse the tender documentation and subsequently, to draw up the bids in view of the answers provided by the CA. The services provided shall be in accordance with the obligations provided at the level of the contract model, the specifications, as well as in accordance with the provisions of Law No 10/1995 on quality in construction, Annex No 2 to Government Decision No 1/2018, which regulates the general and specific conditions applicable in the case of the design and works execution contract and of the Financing Contract concluded with the Managing Authority for the Health Programme, in order to implement the project. In accordance with contractual provisions, but also with the provisions of art. 221 – 222 of Law 98/2016, any potential modifications that may intervene during the contract implementation period refer to the situations identified within the contract, without being limited to them. The identified modifications shall be made after the signing of the contract, in accordance with the contractual provisions, only under the conditions in which these do not represent substantial modifications within the meaning of the provisions of art. 221 para. (7) of Law No 98/2016. More information can be found in the Contract.

sig_f6c9346338376d0586d2.description: The subject of the procurement is a comprehensive city bike service for the use of the City of Tampere and the Municipality of Pirkkala. The city bike service, which is the subject of the procurement, includes the delivery and maintenance of the comprehensive service for the contract period. In addition to the delivery of city bikes and station structures, the service to be procured includes their servicing and maintenance, the relocation of bikes from one station to another, the transfer of bikes and any station structures to storage and storage during the months when the city bike service is not in use, the IT system and customer service for the entire contract period. The service to be procured must be delivered to the Customer tested and ready for use. This is a framework agreement concluded with a single Supplier, which is valid for four (4) years. The City of Tampere decides on and concludes the contract concerning the framework agreement on behalf of the Municipality of Pirkkala with the selected supplier. During the term of the framework agreement, the City of Tampere and the Municipality of Pirkkala may decide and conclude their own procurement contracts for the introduction of the city bike service with the selected supplier in accordance with the terms and conditions presented in connection with this call for tenders. If the City of Tampere does not make a procurement decision on the introduction of the city bike service, the Municipality of Pirkkala cannot make use of the framework agreement in question either. The objective of the contracting entities involved in the procurement (Tampere and Pirkkala) is for the city bike service to start simultaneously in the spring of 2028. However, the municipalities may introduce the city bike service at different times. The objective of the city bike service is to normalise bicycle traffic and sustainable mobility, as well as to enable a sustainable, affordable, easy and fun way to travel. The city bike service is part of the public transport offering: it makes journey chains easier by providing a good feeder connection to public transport backbone routes, while at the same time acting as an independent service with which a journey can be made from start to finish. It is particularly important that the service is one and the same for the user, even if the service is available in the territory of two municipalities. This means that a user can use city bikes in all municipalities where city bikes are in use with a single purchase of access rights, and that the technology and operating logic of the city bikes are the same everywhere. Users can make trips crossing municipal borders. Of the municipalities involved in the procurement, only Tampere currently uses a city bike service. The Tampere city bike service was introduced in 2021, and currently includes 700 mechanical bikes. The bikes have smart locks, and the use of the service is based on the city bike application provided by the Supplier, by means of which users register as service users, purchase the desired access right, and can start and end journeys. The stations of the current city bike service are so-called virtual stations, meaning they are based on geofencing. Some of the stations have fixed infrastructure, e.g. a bike rack and/or an information board. The current city bike service will be withdrawn from use by residents at the end of 2027 and the contract period ends on 28.2.2028. Tenderers can familiarise themselves with the scope and realised quantities of the city bike service currently used by the City of Tampere in the annex to the tender request "Annex 14 Data from current bikeshare".
sig_f6c9346338376d0586d2.title: Procurement of a regional city bike system

sig_f6dd3ffa227c0290d188.description: JLU is planning a relaunch of its website. As part of this tender, external support is to be commissioned for the areas of technical implementation (Block A) as well as hosting and operation (Block B). Lot LOT-0000: Web relaunch Justus-Liebig-University Giessen - Technical implementation, hosting and operation. JLU is planning a relaunch of its website. As part of this tender, external support is to be commissioned for the areas of technical implementation (Block A) as well as hosting and operation (Block B). A tender for the area of usability and interaction design has already taken place beforehand. In the project, content (editorial concept and content) forms the third area. This is covered by the JLU project team. Domestic and foreign prospective students, applicants, students, internal and external scientists, employees, alumni and other external target groups use the service as a knowledge base for a wide variety of university topics and as a source of information about university events. Central focus topics of the web relaunch project are student recruitment and the excellence strategy. A duration of four years is planned for the technical implementation (Block A) and hosting and operation (Block B) of the web relaunch project. In the first year, 200 person-days (PD) are provided for development. In the following years 2 to 4, 120 person-days are provided for operation and further development in each case. One person-day corresponds to 8 hours. The area of usability and interaction design was tendered separately. Early coordination between the contractor and the design agency is intended to ensure the technical feasibility of the developed design. The web relaunch will be implemented according to a hybrid-agile project management approach, in particular to achieve quickly visible results. Block A: Technical implementation includes, among other things: - Implementation of Corporate Design (Web): Implementation of the Plone theme according to the design agency's draft, development of content types for central overview pages, development of templates for content maintenance by web editors, implementation of the central navigation concept, development/adaptation of a mechanism for web forms - Special core features - Automated data integration from third-party systems - Authentication and access control - Role and rights management - Multilingualism - Search engine optimisation (SEO) / Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) - Search and search optimisation - Web statistics and analysis - Adjustments to the Plone standard - Partial migration of selected content - Mechanism for maintaining URLs in hybrid operation - Documentation - Project management Technical implementation Block B: Hosting and operation includes, among other things: - Server infrastructure and cluster setup - Operational tasks and maintenance - Continuous release planning and staging processes - Service Level Agreements (SLA) - IT security Furthermore, cross-sectional topics (accessibility, data protection-compliant operation) Requirements for the contractor's project team: For the implementation of the web relaunch project, the contracting authority expects an experienced and interdisciplinary project team. For the personnel offered, the role profiles must be submitted completed. A document must be submitted fully completed for each person. Role profiles: - Project coordination - Senior software development / Technical management - Software development / Frontend & CMS - Quality assurance / Testing A final description can be found in the service description.
sig_f6dd3ffa227c0290d188.title: Web relaunch of Justus Liebig University Giessen - Technical implementation, hosting and operation

sig_f6f41ed7c5fdd73a92ec.description: The contracting authority requests your tender for the procurement of an expert resource. The expert's task is to support the overall development of the Employment Fund's IT system architecture and to ensure the consistency, continuity and quality of the architecture during the transition period. The expert is responsible for hands-on IT architecture work, overall architecture management, architectural assessment of development projects and technological solutions, as well as supporting and implementing architectural principles and the governance model, and acts as a sparring partner for management and development teams at the interface of business and technology. The expert to be procured is required to have strong and extensive experience in overall architecture and IT architecture tasks in large and complex system environments, as well as the ability to perceive entities and translate them into clear and feasible architectural guidelines. The expert must have experience in architectural design of large-scale system development entities, public procurement and tendering from an architectural perspective, as well as the readiness to act at the interface of business and technology, supporting management in decision-making and sparring development teams in solution design. In the initial phase of the assignment, the workload is estimated to be 50-100 %. The workloads for other phases of the project will be determined based on the overall plan to be drawn up. DURATION OF THE TASK According to the preliminary schedule, the task is scheduled for the period Q3/2026 - Q4/2026. If the project lasts longer than estimated, the need for the expert may continue if the project or the client so requires. The estimated total value of the procurement exceeds the EU threshold.

sig_f707e63974866f737adb.description: The University of Jyväskylä (JYU) is procuring IT expert services for programming and system development work related to its operations, project activities, and to act as part of the university's own strong personal identification process/team. The objective of the procurement is to ensure sufficient expert resources for the Subscriber at the desired skill level. The Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences (Jamk) has the right to procure services based on this tender under the same terms. The selected tenderer is required to have the capability to provide all necessary services to the Subscriber in accordance with the University of Jyväskylä's operating model and the selected technologies and systems in use. This is a single-supplier framework arrangement in which the supplier must provide experts named to an expert pool for the Subscriber's use. In addition to hourly work, fixed-price assignments such as consulting, integration construction and service maintenance can be procured under the framework arrangement if necessary. Assignments will be agreed upon in more detail separately during the contract period. The pricing of assignments must be based on the prices stated in the tender. In principle, future assignments will always be directed to experts named in the call for tenders or later approved for the expert pool. Further information on the content of the procurement can be found in the appendix "Description of the object of the procurement". The Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences participates in the tender by deciding on the ordering of the service according to its needs and does not commit to a specific order volume in advance. Jamk will enter into its own procurement contract with the supplier if necessary. The estimated value of the framework arrangement is a maximum of 800 000 €, which includes Jamk's possible share (VAT 0 %).

ORIGINAL POSTING: Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) N00164-25-S-C001 Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC, Crane) The procedures outlined in this CSO apply to Areas of Interest posted under N00164-25-S-C001 OBJECTIVE: this announcement is intended to enable the rapid selection of innovative commercial solutions through a three-phased, competitive process. Including commercially-available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for defense application. SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 1.1 Background and Authority NSWC Crane’s mission is to deliver innovative solutions and readiness to the Nation and its Warfighters through application of Technical Capabilities; advance all-domain system of systems within the Mission Areas of Expeditionary Warfare, Strategic Missions, and Electromagnetic Warfare; conduct science and technology, research, development, test and evaluation, acquisition and in-service engineering across the Defense lifecycles. To achieve these mission imperatives, NSWC Crane regularly partners with private industry using a variety of collaborative tools in order to streamline the incorporation of innovative technology into the products and services delivered to the Warfighter. To accelerate the adoption of advanced technology, curate solutions to technology gaps, and lead rapid prototyping NSWC Crane issues this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) as authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation. In this context “Innovative” means— Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. NSWC Crane is seeking innovative commercial solutions relevant to the following areas of technological exploration: • Expeditionary Warfare Guided by the National Defense Strategy, NSWC Crane recognizes the priorities and threats shifted to the Pacific. NSWC Crane’s efforts must counter the multi-domain threats and deter aggression posed in the Indo-Pacific region. This reinforces the need of a Joint Force that is even more lethal, resilient, agile and responsive. Autonomous solutions with a focus on payload and sensor integration to enhance detection, tracking, identifying, decision making, maneuver and kinetic/non-kinetic engagement capabilities for multi-domain, uncrewed and counter-crewed systems are a strategic priority. Expeditionary Warfare Development’s heritage has been and continues to focus on rapid prototyping and proven solutions supporting the evolving needs of the Expeditionary force. • Strategic Missions As the Navy’s primary organic field activity for full life cycle management including hardware, ordnance and power systems, NSWC Crane applies the distinct capabilities inherent to its people and facilities to assure 100% operational readiness of strategic missile systems. Fleet Readiness and Modernization and Hypersonics are a top priority of the Navy and DoD. These strategic priorities require collaboration between the Navy, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency to align appropriate requirements, technology development, rapid prototyping, production, sustainment and protection activities of ballistic missile systems to enable affordability, advance technology and reduce program risks to modernize the nuclear enterprise to defeat emerging threats worldwide. • Electromagnetic Warfare NSWC Crane’s Spectrum Warfare Department is the largest concentration of Electronic Warfare experts in the DoD. NSWC Crane provides non-kinetic expertise and electromagnetic spectrum dominance to all the services. Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) is a strategic priority due to the increasingly congested, contested and constrained environments. NSWC Crane supports multidomain integrated solutions through multispectral capabilities utilizing technology development, rapid prototyping, production and sustainment. Pursuant to DFARS 212.7002, NSWC Crane will only use this CSO to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements and to close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological advancements. All products and services acquired using this CSO will be treated as commercial products or commercial services, awarded on a fixed-price basis. In accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.10270, this announcement is a competitive selection of proposals based on a review by scientific, technological, or other subject-matter expert peers and is a competitive procedure. As a result of the competitive processes used under this CSO Announcement, multiple awards may be executed. The methods utilized to execute awards include: FARbased contract, Purchase Order, Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), and/or Bailment Agreement. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022, NSWC Crane may award an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to vendors to carry out prototype project(s) directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. Under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4023, NSWC Crane may procure (by contract or otherwise) ordnance, signal, chemical activity, transportation, energy, medical, space-flight, telecommunications, and aeronautical supplies, including parts and accessories, and designs thereof, that the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary concerned considers necessary for experimental or test purposes in the development of the best supplies that are needed for the national defense. 1.2 General Solicitation and Evaluation Procedures NSWC Crane’s CSO is soliciting Solution Briefs in response to individual Areas of Interest (AOIs). AOIs are focused topic(s) categories that will be published separately and posted on the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. All Solution Briefs submitted in response to AOIs will be governed by this CSO unless otherwise noted in the AOI. AOIs will be written in broad terms to maximize latitude in creativity when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from nontraditional defense contractors and interested parties (entities) who may be unfamiliar with submitting traditional proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post AOIs at any time. Interested parties are encouraged to frequently check the SAM.Gov website and the NSWC, Crane website for new AOI postings. Evaluation of responses will consist of the following 3 Phases: 1) Solution Brief, 2) Pitch, and 3) Full written proposal – described in more detail here: Phase 1 Solution Briefs: Solution Briefs submitted in response to an AOI shall be submitted as specified in Section 2 of this CSO. The Government will evaluate Solution Briefs against the criteria stated in this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for the costs associated with Solution Brief submissions. Phase 2 Pitch Session: Respondents whose Solution Briefs are evaluated to be of merit may be invited to provide a pitch following the instructions provided in Section 2.3 of this CSO. The Government reserves the right to limit the number of parties invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. In the event that the Government requires a demonstration, additional information will be provided in the specific AOI highlighting those procedures, otherwise Phase 2 will be comprised solely of the pitch. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with pitches, unless otherwise stipulated. Phase 3 Proposal: Those entities whose Solution Brief and Pitch are evaluated to be of merit and are selected for potential award may be invited to submit a full written proposal following the instructions provided in Section 2.4 of this CSO. The Government will not pay entities for costs associated with the proposal in Phase 3, unless otherwise stipulated. SECTION 2 – GUIDELINES FOR SUBMISSION 2.1 General Guidelines Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly encouraged. Companies may submit multiple Solution Briefs in response to any single AOI if each submission represents a separate and distinct concept. The period of performance for any Solution Brief or proposal submitted under this CSO should generally be no greater than 24-months. Technical data with military application may require appropriate approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation. All Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals shall be unclassified. Solution Briefs, Pitches, and Proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or used by the Government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following sentences on the cover page: “This [select one: Solution Brief, Pitch, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government, except to non-Government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed -- in whole or in part -- for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this Company as a result of -- or in connection with – the submission of this data, the Government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the Government's right to use the information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” Each restricted data sheet should be marked as follows: “Use or disclosure of data contained on this sheet is subject to the restriction on the title page of this proposal.” Foreign-Owned businesses may independently submit a solution or do so as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more United States-Owned businesses. However, the ability to obtain an agreement based upon a submission may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-Owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain proscribed information. Submissions must be submitted electronically. Submissions sent through other channels or after the AOI period has ended will not be reviewed nor evaluated. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.2 Phase 1 Solution Brief PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF CONTENT Solution Briefs should not exceed five (5) written pages using 12-point font. Alternatively, Solution Briefs may take the form of briefing slides which should not exceed fifteen (15) slides. Briefs should include at a minimum: Title Page (does not count against page limit) Entity Name, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address. Specifically identify the AOI for which the Solution Brief is submitted. Executive Summary of the technology (one page) Describe the concept and unique aspects of the technology as it relates to the AOI. Identify whether the solution is an existing technology that has satisfied a pilot or demonstration (ie, commercially ready and viable technology), or the if the solution will require development for defense application. If development or adaptation is proposed, identify a suggested path to mature the technology. Identify aspects of the solution which may be considered proprietary or Intellectual Property (IP) Provide a brief overview of the company, including a summary of product commercialization and go-to-market strategy. PHASE 1 SOLUTION BRIEF BASIS OF EVALUATION All solution briefs correctly submitted in response to an AOI will be evaluated against the stated criteria below. (Y/N) The proposed innovative commercial solution, technology, process, or method, is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or is an application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. Relevance of the Solution Brief in addressing the AOI. Technical Merit and feasibility of the solution to address Government AOI problem statement. A quick, reasonable, and efficient way exists for the DoD to test the innovative commercial solution, within a specified duration, whether outside or integrated within the DoD infrastructures or networks, as appropriate. Additional technical evaluation criteria specific to a particular project may be used. In these instances, the additional criteria will be posted within the AOI announcement on the SAM.Gov and the NSWC Crane public-facing website. Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI, not against other Solution Briefs submitted in response to the same AOI. Additionally, while not overtly stated in AOIs, the Government’s evaluation will consider whether the proposal increases the likelihood of accomplishing NSWC Crane’s Mission Focus Areas. All submissions will be evaluated, however, only a select few will be invited to pitch. The government reserves the right to limit the number of entities invited to pitch. As such, a company’s solution may be evaluated to be of merit, but not invited to pitch. Solution Briefs that are chosen for the Phase 2 Pitch will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. 2.3 Phase 2 Pitch PHASE 2 PITCH CONTENT In Phase 2, entities shall provide an in-person or virtual pitch to demonstrate and provide further details on their proposed innovative commercial solution and the technical and business viability of the proposed solution. The Government may elect to use external market research during the Pitch to evaluate viability. In addition to the Pitch, the Government, at its discretion, may request for consideration an additional written submission to further supplement the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. During the Phase 2 Pitch, the Company must detail/address: Estimated Price/Schedule Rough order of magnitude (ROM) or pricing Anticipated Data Rights Assertions During the Pitch, the Government may request the additional information/detail with respect to the information provided in the Phase 1 Solution Brief. PHASE 2 PITCH BASIS OF EVALUATION Individual pitches will be evaluated against the following factors: Relevance of the pitch in addressing the AOI and the ability of the presenter to adequately address Government questions or concerns regarding the proposed application or use of the innovative commercial solution. The solution has technical merit, adequately & realistically addresses Government need and can be quickly incorporated into DOD systems. Reasonableness of the ROM The associated delivery schedule is expeditious and realistic. Individual pitches will be evaluated on the basis of the merit of the proposed concept in addressing the AOI and the factors above, not against any other Pitches held under the same AOI. Pitch submissions will be valid for 180 calendar days after the pitch date. Upon completion of evaluations, the Government will notify the Company that: (1) the proposed concept/technology/solution has been selected for possible award and the entity is invited to submit a full proposal; (2) the proposed concept/technology/solution is not of interest to the Government; or (3) the proposed concept/technology/solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources. If the proposed innovative commercial solution is of interest, but not eligible for a proposal due to availability of Government resources, the Company may be contacted with a request to respond to proposal request within 180 calendar days from the pitch date. If after 180 calendar days from the pitch date (or earlier if notified by NSWC, Crane), Government resources are not identified to formally move into Phase 3, the entity will no longer be eligible for an award under that particular AOI. 2.4 Phase 3 Proposal PHASE 3 PROPOSAL CONTENT The final phase of the evaluation process is the proposal request. Based upon the evaluation process detailed in Phase 1 and 2, the Government may request a full written proposal. The entity will be invited to develop and submit a full written proposal and negotiate appropriate terms and conditions. Entities may discuss ideas and questions related to the proposal with the Government POC during the proposal writing process. Each proposal submitted shall consist of two sections: Section 1 shall consist of the technical proposal; Section 2 shall consist of the price/cost/schedule. Proposals will be assessed by NSWC Crane technical and Contracting subject matter experts. Entities may propose their own internal terms and conditions (e.g., Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA)) to be considered during negotiations with the Government. Note, there are certain terms and conditions the Government is unable to accept. Awards made under this authority will only be issued as fixed price awards in accordance with DFARS 212.7002(b). However, projects awarded through the CSO are flexible to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and where it meets the Government’s needs. At a minimum, written proposals must contain: Title Page Company Name, Point of Contact Name, Date, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address and any subcontractors or team members. Include an abstract which provides a concise description of the proposal. Description of the proposed innovative commercial solution Background and objectives of the proposed solution, deliverables, and resources needed to execute. Include the nature and extent of the anticipated results. Include ancillary and operational issues such as certifications, algorithms, and any engineering/software development methodologies to be used. If services, include a Statement of Work (SOW). Provide a detailed project schedule that outlines the various phases of work to be accomplished within the proposed period of performance. You may refer to the Solution Brief that prompted this proposal request, but do not duplicate it. Identify any Government material, equipment, data, or other items necessary. Phase 3 - Price Proposal The entity shall propose a fixed price for the item or service and provide any data or supporting information necessary for the determination of a fair and reasonable price. This can include, but is not limited to, commercial price catalog or other proprietary information to help the Government assess the proposed price. Additionally, if proposing an OT, while not required to be specifically addressed in the proposal (with the exception of the 1/3 cost-share requirement, if applicable), the Government will review the proposal to determine if the following OT statutory requirements are met: Fits the definition of a prototype Meets non-traditional participation/cost share requirement: Non-traditional defense contractor contributes to a significant extent or not; if not, 1/3 cost share implementation is addressed Defense Utility: Solution is applicable to a DoD platform, system or component SECTION 3 – AWARDS 3.1 General Guidelines Upon favorable review and available funds, the Government may choose to make an award. Only Warranted Contracting Officers or Agreements Officers may obligate the Government by entering into or modifying a binding agreement on behalf of the Government. Awards made under this CSO will be fixed price. Contract type will be determined during Phase 3. Multiple awards may be made to pursue similar or dissimilar solutions should they all meet the technical criteria, be selected for award, and if funds are available. Entities must have a DUNs and CAGE Code registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award. Companies are advised to commence SAM registration upon receipt of a proposal request. Awardees must be determined to be responsible by the Contracting or Agreements Officer and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving award. Receipt of a proposal request does not guarantee receipt of award. The Government reserves the right, at any point prior to award, to cancel the request. Upon award, awardees must register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (e.g. Wide Area Work Flow). 3.2 Comptroller General Access to Information In OT projects that provide for payments in a total amount in excess of $5,000,000, the Agreement will include a mandatory clause that provides for the Comptroller General the ability to examine the records of any party to the agreement or any entity that participates in the performance of the agreement. 3.3 Procurement Integrity Act (PIA) All awards under this CSO shall be treated as Federal Agency procurements for purpose of 41 U.S.C. Chapter 21. Accordingly, the CSO competitive solicitation process and awards made thereof must adhere to the ethical standards required by the PIA. SECTION 4 - ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING As it is the mission of NSWC Crane to enable access to commercially-derived disruptive capabilities across the entirety of the DoD enterprise, Prototype OTAs awarded against this CSO will allow for an iterative prototyping process. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the work in a prototype project to allow the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the original Government customer or originate with other organizations within the Federal Government. SECTION 5 – FOLLOW-ON PRODUCTION Upon successful completion of a prototype project under the OTA, the Government may negotiate a follow-on production contract or agreement without further competition. Any concept/technology/solution successfully proven through a Prototype OTA can be transitioned to production. AOIs posted by the Government under this CSO and Prototype OTAs awarded will include language providing for the potential award of a follow-on production contract or agreement as authorized under 10 U.S.C. § 4022 Individual AOIs and CSO prototype OTAs will explicitly identify follow-on Prototype OTAs as a potential outcome of a successful prototyping effort. SECTION 6 SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION A transaction for a prototype project is complete upon the written determination of the appropriate approving official (program manager and Agreement Officer) for the matter in question that efforts conducted under a Prototype OTA: (1) met the key technical goals of a project; (2) satisfied success metrics incorporated into the Prototype OTA; or (3) accomplished a particularly favorable or unexpected result that justifies the transition to production. Furthermore, successful completion can occur prior to the conclusion of a prototype project to allow the Government to transition any aspect of the prototype project determined to provide utility into production while other aspects of the prototype project have yet to be completed. Any Prototype OTA shall contain a provision that sets forth the conditions under which that prototype agreement must be successfully completed. SECTION 7 – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during Proposal development and negotiations. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. Companies may enter into specific NDAs directly with the Non-Government advisors or their corporate entities. Submission of an offer under this CSO will constitute a grant of authority by the submitting company to the Government to allow the use of non-Government advisors to participate in evaluations of all phases of the CSO process. The Government understands that information provided in response to this CSO is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. sig_f713ce13dab56897af30.description: Request for Information (RFI) for Advancing Critical and Emerging Microelectronics Technologies I. Background Information The United States is in a battle for global leadership in the critical and emerging technologies that will drive decades of national and economic security and prosperity. To ensure U.S. global dominance in the industries of the future, we seek to advance the nation’s stated agenda to secure the U.S. position as the unrivaled world leader in emerging technology. As the nation’s premier laboratory with a mission to promote U.S. innovation and industrial competitiveness, Sandia National Laboratories (SNL) is poised to work with industry at every step to support U.S. manufacturing and technological capacity in critical and emerging microelectronics technologies. The basis for this RFI is aligned with the goal of advancing technology leadership in the United States and strengthening the supply chain for domestic semiconductor manufacturing. II. Opportunity Description and Areas of Interest The following are general topic areas that have been identified as priority areas for proposals under this RFI: 1. Semiconductors. Proposed projects may include conducting research and prototyping of advanced semiconductor technologies to strengthen the economic competitiveness and security of the domestic supply chain, overcome R&D ecosystem gaps, and develop innovative advanced technologies, including but not limited to: Microelectronic/Semiconductor Devices: Analog and Digital Signal Processing and Computing Technologies Includes neuromorphic, energy efficient artificial intelligence hardware, analog, digital and mixed signal processing, next generation memory technologies Power Electronics GaN/AlGaN/AlN, Diamond, SiC, and Ga2O3 Magnetic and dielectric materials (including integrated magnetics and dielectrics), Advanced Sensing and Timing Materials, devices, architectures, detectors, systems, read out integrated circuits, and atomic clocks Communications Technologies Radio frequency, optoelectronic/photonic, quantum Miroelectronics fabrication and characterization capability: Advanced test, assembly, and packaging capability in the domestic ecosystem. Heterogeneous integration and 3D packaging, chiplets, 3D stacking, novel memory architectures, 2.5D packaging, integrated photonic packages, ultrahigh density interposers, and next generation assembly and systems packaging. Materials characterization, instrumentation, and testing for next generation microelectronics. Virtualization and automation of maintenance of semiconductor machinery. Metrology for security and supply chain verification. Next generation design: design and system level co-optimization, AI-enabled devices through system designs, advanced design automation. Accelerating domestic manufacturing fabs: robotics, automation, digital twins, AI-enabled manufacturing, national security manufacturing, and securing critical supply chains. Advanced Packaging: high-power packaging and power modules (related to HI for high voltage/power. 2. Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for advanced microelectronics research and development. Proposed projects may include the development and adoption of AI-driven autonomous agents, AI-based agents for cybersecurity, and consistency in AI system performance measurement. General applications of AI technologies not directly related to advanced microelectronics research and development are not within the scope of this RFI. Example technical areas of interest for the demonstration of AI using semiconductors include, but are not limited to: Compute efficiency. Novel memory stacks. Cryogenic operations. AI at edge. Stacked machine health monitoring. AI devices for extreme environments. Using AI to accelerate domestic manufacturing fabs to secure critical supply chains. 3. Application of quantum technology for advanced microelectronics research and development. Proposed projects may include research and prototyping of advanced semiconductor technology for quantum technology, manufacturing of quantum sensors, scalable high-performance quantum components, and development of quantum networks. Example technical areas of interest for the demonstration of quantum technology using semiconductors include, but are not limited to: Scalable quantum computing. Quantum networks and communications. Quantum sensing and metrology. Accelerating domestic manufacturing fabs: scale domestic production of quantum hardware, domestic buildout of cryogenic, optical, and ultra-high vacuum manufacturing lines, national security manufacturing, secure critical supply chains. Photonics for quantum 4. Commercialization of innovations. Proposed projects may include the adoption and commercialization of federally funded scientific discoveries and technology advancements. Examples within commercialization of innovation using semiconductors include but are not limited to: Advanced testing Assembly Packaging capability that involve eligible participants, that may include Manufacturing USA Institute or other consortiums to adopt and commercialize innovations. III. Submission Guidelines and Points of Contact Response Format: Please submit your responses in a PDF or Word document format (5 page maximum.) Deadline for Submission: Applications will be accepted until September 30, 2029. Contact Information: For any questions or clarifications regarding this RFI, please contact Ken Dean (kadean@sandia.gov) and Lauren Kemme (lakemme@sandia.gov). IV. Evaluation Criteria Responses will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Relevance and completeness of the information provided Clarity and organization of the response Demonstrated understanding of the technical purpose and background Experience and qualifications of the respondent V. Additional Information Respondents are encouraged to provide any additional information that may be relevant to this RFI. This may include case studies, examples of previous work, or any other materials that demonstrate your capabilities and expertise.
