sig_f746a32a76272f07d169.description: A platform that predicts the right signal peptide for a specific protein Many medicines, vaccines, and biotechnology products rely on proteins reaching the right cellular compartment or secretion outside a cell. Whether a protein gets there in enough quantities depends on its signal peptide or leader sequence. Scientists can identify many existing signal peptides, but predicting which one will work best for a specific protein remains difficult. SignalGen uses generative AI to predict the signal peptide most likely to guide a protein to the right location. To make that prediction, it considers the protein, where it needs to go, and the organism it comes from. This approach gives researchers a new way to improve protein expression for medicines, vaccines, and biotechnology products. Overview: Proteins carry out many of the body's essential functions, but they can only do their job if they reach the right place inside or outside a cell. Many proteins rely on signal peptides to get there. Typically, a signal peptide is a short sequence segment at the beginning of a protein that acts like a built-in address label, helping direct the protein to the location where it is needed. Predicting the right signal peptide for a specific protein remains challenging. Existing software can identify known signal peptides or determine whether a protein already contains one, but it cannot predict which signal peptide is best suited to produce the desired protein expression and cellular location. Researchers provide the protein they want to study, where they want it to go to a specific compartment in a cell, and the organism. SignalGen predicts the signal peptide best suited for those conditions, giving researchers a stronger starting point before laboratory testing. SignalGen is even critical for AI designed de novo proteins as it would require a signal peptide. Advantages: Predicts signal peptides for specific proteins instead of only identifying known ones Considers the protein, where it needs to go, and the organism in a single prediction Works with both human and non-human proteins Natural-language interface reduces the need for programming or scripting Demonstrated approximately 90% prediction accuracy using the all-organism model Technology Description: At the core of SignalGen is a protein language model trained on thousands of proteins and their associated signal peptides. By learning the relationships between proteins, signal peptides, where proteins are located inside the cell, and the organisms they come from, the model predicts the signal peptide best suited for a specific protein. The model combines information about the protein, where it needs to go inside or outside the cell, and the organism it comes from to generate its prediction. It was initially trained using human proteins and later expanded to include proteins from many different organisms, improving its versatility and achieving approximately 90% prediction accuracy. SignalGen also includes an AI agent that makes the platform easier to use. Researchers interact with the system using natural language rather than programming or scripting. The AI agent gathers the required information, runs the prediction, and returns the recommended signal peptide through a guided workflow. Market Applications: Therapeutic protein development Vaccine research and development Drug discovery Biomanufacturing Protein engineering Synthetic biology Industrial biotechnology Molecular biology research TRL: 3 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-27860 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL’s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. sig_f75214932dc650000c29.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.

Market exploration - voluntary prior information - No contract notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to obtain information on services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" as part of a market exploration in accordance with Section 28 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The subject of this market exploration is to gain knowledge about IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub" regarding the takeover of the existing codebase, for ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers can contact the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by 14.10.2026 with a brief description of their services and their suitability for fulfilling the stated requirements, stating the subject "Markterkundung - IT-Dienstleistungen Research-Hub", in order to participate in this market exploration. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration for the preparation of a procurement procedure. Market Exploration - Voluntary pre-notice - No Contract Notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to gather information, as part of a market exploration pursuant to Section 28 of the Regulation on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV), regarding services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub." The purpose of this market exploration is to gather information on IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub," specifically regarding the adoption of the existing codebase, ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers may participate in this market exploration by sending a brief description of their services and their suitability for meeting the stated requirements-with the subject line "Market Exploration - IT Services Research Hub" - to the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by October 14, 2026. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration to prepare a procurement process. Lot PAR-0001: Market exploration in accordance with Section 28 VgV for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" - Market Exploration Section 28 VgV for an IT Maintenance Contract for the "Research Hub". This market exploration serves exclusively for information gathering and the preparation of a potential procurement procedure. It does not constitute a call for tenders or prior information within the meaning of procurement law. A procurement procedure will be initiated at a later date if necessary. The web-based research information system "Research Hub" supports, among other things, the management and processing of research projects, publications and associated workflows. The aim of the market exploration is to gain a general overview of the market as well as potentially suitable service providers and their service profiles. The focus is in particular on experience with the takeover, support and further development of existing software systems as well as with comparable applications in the scientific or public environment. At the present time, neither concrete service requirements nor a specific contract model have been defined. The subject of a possible later commission could - depending on further findings and the concrete demand situation - in particular be support services in connection with the ongoing operation, technical support, maintenance and further development of the system. A possible later tender may include content that deviates from or goes beyond this. In this early phase, the Bundesbank would particularly like to know: - whether there is a fundamental interest in potential support in this environment; - what general experience the company has with comparable web-based software systems; - in which areas of software development, system support or technical consulting there are special competencies; - whether there is experience with science-related applications, publication processes, repositories or comparable technical systems; - how the takeover and further support of an existing software solution could be structured in principle; - whether there is a fundamental interest in a non-binding information meeting. sig_f76d0c844dda42681c86.description: We invite forward leaning tenderers to register for our market dialogue for a future procurement of a tender implementation tool (KGV), with the accompanying options, the County Municipalities would like a modern and user friendly tool that helps both the contracting authority and the tenderer with implementation competitions in a flexible way. Simple process and user support should be available by phone and email. The tool shall contribute to increased efficiency in the procurement work and reduce complexity, so that several parts of the entities can use the tool in line with the organisations' maturity. The contracting authorities are looking for a tool that offers efficient work flow and automated processes. The use ought to contribute to reduced the organisation's use of resources in procurement processes and contract follow-up and that the company can more easily comply with the regulations. The contracting authorities want a robust, modern and cloud based system that uses new technology to enable efficient data processing, automation of work processes and seamless integration with the existing infrastructure in the counties. The solution is expected to be maintained, upgraded and developed to support legislative changes, adopt new technology, improve the user experience, and provide continual value during the contract period. It is important that the procured system is developed in line with the market and contributes to strengthening the digitalisation work for the procurement discipline. The system shall assist with the transition to data driven everyday life for procurement consultants. In the future, it may be necessary to integrate artificial intelligence into your infrastructure, such as with Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure, to improve employee efficiency and provide access to verified information from trusted data sources, while maintaining security and data quality. The contracting authority wants a tool that, in the long term, can connect artificial intelligence to data in KGV/KAV and other parts of the system, so that employees can reliable information through interaction with artificial intelligence, independent of client. The main goals are: Streamlining of the procurement work, repaired complexity in the processes. Automation and improved work flow. Better compliance with the rules. Support for digitalisation and transition to data driven processes. Future integration of artificial intelligence, especially with Microsoft 365 and Azure.Need for integration with archive system FINT (Joint County InTegraions)What is GOOD? FINT Arkiv – Novari IKSFINT is a common digital platform that is used by Norwegian counties to standardise and make information available through open APIs. This contributes to increased efficiency, better data quality and reduced costs by enabling real time reuse of data. FINT Arkiv-integration shall be used by county entities included in this competition. Other affiliated entities may require integration in other ways, adapted to their system landscape. As the Contracting Authority consists of several entities, different archive systems are currently used. With FINT Arkiv, however, the underlying archive system does not function as the interface for the integration - FINT provides a common interface regardless of which archive system is used. Fint Arkiv is used by all of the counties in the country, byantikvaren and Bymiljøetaten in Oslo kommune as well as Sametinget.With FINT Arkiv the counties get an API with a joint information model for standardised exchange of archive information. The counties that currently participate in this competition use three different archive systems: Tieto Evry - Public 360Sikri - ElementsAcos - WebSak+Overall Requirement - Integration friendly and data driven system The contracting authority shall use systems with open and documented APIs that enable safe and efficient integration. With limited internal resources for development, the contracting authority needs assistance to extract more value from the existing data. The tenderer shall develop integrations that are easy to implement, maintain and reuse - and that can be shared with other public entities when relevant. The system shall be based on open standards and it shall provide sufficient documentation for both technical and functional understanding. The Contracting Authority strives to procure systems that shall offer an open and documented API with sufficient functionality for safe and efficient integration with other systems and data sources. The API shall support standardised protocols and formats and be available for integration without a need for comprehensive adaptations. The integrations shall be designed with modular architecture that enables reuse and sharing with other public entities. All the necessary documentation connected to the API, data flow and process design shall be provided and suitable for both technical and functional understanding. The tenderer shall assist in implementing value from existing data and contribute to a more data driven and coherent public sector.

sig_f7990335845620158c37.description: The Harghita Public Health Directorate is a deconcentrated institution within the Ministry of Health. It serves Harghita County and plays an essential role in the implementation of national public health policies, in preventive medicine and in sanitary inspections at county level. This document aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the digital capabilities needed by the Harghita Public Health Directorate. This initiative seeks to align with national objectives of advancing healthcare through the digitisation of health systems, optimisation of data governance and improvement of communication between healthcare providers and beneficiaries. At county level, DSP Harghita is responsible for coordinating health status monitoring and the organisation of health statistics, as well as for the supervision, planning and running of investments financed from the state budget for the healthcare sector. It coordinates anti-epidemic activity at county level, methodologically coordinates and supervises primary, emergency, specialised and hospital medical activity to optimise population access and territorial coverage with quality preventive and curative health services. It is responsible for the implementation at county level of the national public health strategy and guides the drafting of the county and local strategic health plan. The proposed investment falls under NRRP Investment I.1 – Component 7 – "Digital transformation", within the project call NRRP/2023/C7 - I.3.2 - MoH IT systems and healthcare institutions. This investment meets the mandatory condition of aligning the investment with the National Health Strategy 2023-2030, this strategy representing the commitment of the Ministry of Health, as the central authority for drafting and coordinating health policies at national level, towards the citizens of Romania, with a view to improving their healthy life expectancy and quality of life. sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.description: The far-reaching impact and rate of innovation in the computer and information science and engineering fields has been remarkable, generating economic prosperity and enhancing the quality of life for people throughout the world. More than a decade ago, the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE) established the Expeditions in Computing (Expeditions) program to build on past successes and provide the CISE research and education community with the opportunity to pursue ambitious, fundamental research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information. In planning Expeditions projects, investigators are strongly encouraged to come together within or across departments or institutions to combine their creative talents in the identification of compelling, transformative research agendas that look ahead by at least a decade and promise disruptive innovations in computer and information science and engineering for many years to come. Now funded at levels up to $15,000,000 for seven years, Expeditions projects represent some of the largest single investments currently made by the CISE directorate. Together with the Science and Technology Centers and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes that CISE supports, Expeditions projects form the centerpiece of the directorate's center-scale award portfolio. With awards funded at levels that promote the formation of large research teams, CISE recognizes that concurrent research advances in multiple fields or sub-fields are often necessary to stimulate deep and enduring outcomes. The awards made in this program will complement research areas supported by other CISE programs, which target particular computer and information science and engineering fields. Additionally, CISE offers Innovation Transition (InTrans) awards for teams nearing the end of their Expeditions as well as Secure and Trustworthy Cyberspace (SaTC) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Frontier projects. The goal of InTransis to continue the long-term vision and objectives of CISE’s center-scale projects. Through InTrans awards, CISE will provide limited funds to match industry support.
sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.title: Expeditions in Computing

sig_f7a193808f0a2e48e369.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET SURVEY AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also referred to as the contracting entity) is using this request for information to survey the market to support the planning of the renewal of the care item logistics enterprise resource planning system. The purpose of the request for information is primarily to survey the market's capability regarding the core system for supply chain management (material control, order processing and master data management) as well as the e-commerce service integrated into it. Regarding reporting, warehouse management (WMS), integration solutions and other complementary areas, the objective is to examine compatibility, integration possibilities and potential additional capabilities as part of the target architecture. The examination of these areas does not mean that they are the subject of procurement as such or that the current solutions would be replaced. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to familiarise themselves with the description attached to the request for information and to answer the questions presented in the attachment. The processes and functionalities described in the attachment are partly preliminary and indicative at this stage, and they will be refined as the project progresses. Please submit your responses to kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi by 10.8.2026. The subject line of the message must mention "HUS 051-2026 / Response to request for information / [Company]". Based on the responses provided, the contracting entity may, at its discretion, propose clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have responded to this request for information. The contracting entity may also ask suppliers that have responded to the request for information to comment on preliminary call for tenders documents. The responses given to this request for information may be used in the planning of the procurement. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting entity will treat your response confidentially. The contracting entity will not initiate a tendering process with the publication of the request for information; any possible contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting entity to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any later tendering process that may be organised. Suppliers will not be compensated for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue.

sig_f7b0e99a8a39411ebdd4.description: The NMA operate several specialised media platforms that were designed in collaboration with external service providers. These media platforms serve as digital distribution and information spaces. They make files (containing photos, videos, graphics, 3D objects as well as information about events, processes and projects) available to the organisational units of the federal administration and the interested public. As the contract with the current supplier expires at the end of 2026, this call for tenders aims to find a suitable supplier anew. The objective is to ensure the continuous operation, technical support, software maintenance, upkeep and further development (and, if necessary, complete redevelopment) of the following media platforms of the NMA: * Application "DDPS Media Library" (www.mediathek.admin.ch ) * Web application "DigiMedia" for 3D and 2D objects * Web application LogVision (www.log-vision.ch ) * Web application MilSport (www.mil-sport.ch ) This call for tenders covers the acquisition of services (some of which have the character of a work) for support, software maintenance, upkeep, further development and redevelopment of web platforms of the NMA. The following roles/functions are required for this purpose: Basic mandate: * Software development and system architecture service (BM): 684 hours * IT project management service (BM): 342 hours * Design / layout service (BM): 342 hours * Software testing service (BM): 69 hours * Basic availability, i.e. continuous support, software maintenance, technical upkeep (BM): 41 hours

sig_f7b493df20383bf0b66e.description: The procedure is organised with a view to concluding a forest management services contract for the area of 22.550,91 ha, the management plan of the Viseu Forestry Office within the Maramureș Forestry Directorate expiring on 31.12.2027, it being necessary to initiate the procurement procedure in good time to comply with legal deadlines. The services involve the development of the forest management plan and, where appropriate, the additional study for modifying the provisions of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model, defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary for the development of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of goods in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the contract notice may be made with a deadline of at most 18 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 11 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Forest management plan development services for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Maramureș Forestry Directorate – Viseu Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 22.550,91 ha. The services include preparatory work, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.
sig_f7b493df20383bf0b66e.title: Forest management services Viseu Forestry Office Maramures Forestry Directorate

sig_f7d5bfc6c5bdd1737ad5.description: Framework agreement for procurement consultancy and procurement services for vehicles and equipment for disaster control in Baden-Württemberg. The services are being tendered as a framework agreement. Lot LOT-0001: Framework agreement for procurement consultancy and procurement services for vehicles and equipment for disaster control of the State of Baden-Württemberg. The contracting authority is seeking a service provider to support it in the procurement of vehicles and equipment for disaster control. The contractor must provide the following primarily technical services, although the legal assessment and decision remain with the contracting authority: - Conducting market research on the vehicles and equipment to be procured for disaster control, particularly with regard to the current state of the art and technical possibilities - Drawing up service descriptions taking into account technical specifications and the specific needs of disaster control - Developing proposals for suitability and award criteria, including technical evaluation criteria - Processing technical applicant/bidder queries - Processing complaints, in particular drafting responses to complaints - Evaluating applications to participate or tenders and developing award recommendations for the contract award - Drafting prior information notices - Drafting procurement records - Providing advice in review procedures. Furthermore, the contractor must optionally support and accompany the contracting authority upon request after the respective award in the procurement process, for example during construction meetings, prototype inspections, quality checks and acceptances and, if necessary, also with regard to the warranty phase after acceptance. Legal advice services are not included in the contract. The services are being tendered in the form of a framework agreement. The specific services to be provided and their deadlines are determined by the contracting authority individually in each individual order. The contractor has no claim to the calling off of services from the framework agreement. There is no entitlement to further commissioning. The type and scope of the individual commissioning can vary depending on the individual project. The contracting authority has a right of ordinary termination at any time for every individual order placed on the basis of the framework agreement. The contracting authority reserves the right to commission any further special services. The framework agreement has a maximum duration of four years from the start of the services with regard to the non-optional services in accordance with § 21 Para. 6 VgV. Insofar as the contracting authority calls off the optional services, the conditions of the framework agreement shall continue to apply to the individual orders placed until the maximum duration is reached until their final processing by the contractor, even after the termination of this framework agreement. The maximum quantity of services expected under the framework agreement amounts to a total of up to 500 vehicles and equipment, which the contracting authority can call off bundled in the context of individual orders for each individual order.

sig_f7f5814507fd51db3b0a.description: PURPOSE AND SCOPE The Health Agency is Oslo municipality ́s agency for health. The dental health service - which is part of the Health Agency - offers dental services to different groups of the population, including children and adolescents, young adults, elderly people, long-term sick, people with mental disabilities and users of drugs. The Health Agency needs media conversion of the dental health service's patient records. There are approx. 102,000 patient journals from Oslo's public dental health service. There can be deviations from this estimate. The material is currently stored in temporary premises in Storgata in Oslo. Part of the archive is arranged and packed in archive boxes/moving boxes that are placed on large pallets. Some of the material is together with castings in plaster stored in archive cabinets. The aim of the media conversion is to replace paper based journals with fully fledged digital copies. After digitalisation and completed quality control, it shall be possible to make references in the material so that the originals on paper can be shredded. The digitalised journals shall be deposited at Oslo Byarkiv in accordance with the requirements set by the City Archive for digital archive material.
sig_f7f5814507fd51db3b0a.title: Media conversion of dental health journals.

sig_f8084aa2b56bdece448d.description: The subject of the public contract is the development of digitalisation, standardisation and interoperability in all hospitals of the Plzeň Region Hospital Group (NPK). The subject of the supplies for individual entities according to their specialisations is a hospital information system (NIS), the supply and implementation of an integration platform (ESB) for eHealth, which will ensure the sharing of medical documentation between NPK hospitals, the connection of hospital information systems to exchange networks, and central digital electronic health services (IDRR). The goal of the modernisation and consolidation of NPK hospital systems is uniform standardisation of electronic medical documentation, uniform implementation of electronic health identifiers and the use of reference data from master registries, uniform connection to central electronic health services and exchange network services for the exchange and sharing of electronic health records of medical documentation with authorised recipients via information systems and technologies. Part of the supplies of the integration platform (ESB) are interfaces and services for connection to the infrastructure of systems and services of the Accredited Affinity Domain (AAfD), the National Contact Point for eHealth (NCPeH) and the Integrated Data Interface for Electronic Health (IDRR), or to other central services. The performance of the public contract further includes service services for a period of 48 months for the modernised information systems, application software, related technologies and equipment.
sig_f8084aa2b56bdece448d.title: EHEALTH IN HOSPITALS OF THE PLZEŇ REGION HOSPITAL GROUP – DELIVERY OF NIS, ESB AND INTEGRATIONS

sig_f83b47f961afe05fd8cb.description: *** REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY **** INTRODUCTION West Mercia Police (the Authority) wishes to inform you of an upcoming requirement to replace our current finance system. The new solution must replicate existing functionality while also providing enhanced capabilities that will enable us to meet the objectives outlined below. This exercise is being undertaken to assess the capabilities available within the market and to understand how potential solutions align with the needs of West Mercia Police. The purpose of the RFI is to gain a formal understanding of the possible capabilities, indicative pricing and proposed timescales, with a view to inform West Mercia Police of options and next steps. OBJECTIVES The objective of this RFI is to: • identify how the market meets the capabilities/functionality sought by the authority and enable future capture & refinement of our requirements • identify providers with advantageous solutions from commercial and technical standpoints including future expansions of the system • identify providers with a successful track-record for delivering within the UK Police force or wider public sector • confirm technical considerations such as hosting (on-premise versus cloud), integration opportunities and security assurances. Should your organisation wish to be included in this exercise you are encouraged to register to InTend and West Mercia Police to participate in this RFI exercise. Sell2 (in-tend.co.uk) - https://sell2.in-tend.co.uk/blpd/publictender-details?tid=b9146c65-a50a-42e0-8ca4-dc42b25cf271- deadline for responses by no later than 16:00 hrs on 6th March 2026. Lot 1: .

sig_f840fdff9e7e5d4ebdf3.description: The implementation of the cantonal data strategy provides for the cantonal administration to introduce a metadata catalogue. This will systematise and streamline the handling of structured data within the administration, and enhance data-related efficiency, security and transparency. With the help of the catalogue, important administrative data will be described in a standardised manner, made easily searchable and prepared for reuse and – where legally permissible – for publication as open administrative data. This tender covers the procurement of: the cantonal metadata catalogue itself, the necessary implementation services and subsequent operation, including support. The tender comprises three service groups: the system (licence for the metadata catalogue) and ongoing operation with support, as well as one-off services for commissioning. Commissioning will take place using an agile approach with iterative implementation steps. Once the contract has been awarded, the project contract will be signed; following successful final acceptance of the entire system, a licence and maintenance contract with a term of 5 years will be signed. Translated with DeepL.com (free version)
sig_f840fdff9e7e5d4ebdf3.title: Metadata Catalogue of the Cantonal Administration of Aargau

sig_f8416d31a4f813aaa89d.description: The subject matter of the overall project is the conceptual, technical and operational implementation of the "SH-Navi" project as an open, modular and preferably open-source-based mobility platform for the intermodal, multimodal and data-based linking of various mobility services. The aim of the overall project is the gradual development, integration and provision of a future-proof digital mobility solution that brings together different modes of transport, routing, data, information and, in the future, further complementary mobility functions in a common system architecture. For the appropriate structuring of the overall project and for the clear separation of different service areas, the project is divided into two technically and functionally connected, but procurement-side separate lots: 1. Lot 1 - Development, adaptation, integration and technical further development of the application and system landscape - Lot 1 comprises in particular the conceptual, technical and operational development, adaptation, integration, configuration, customising, development and extension services in connection with the web application, optional additional modules (e.g. app), technical interfaces, routing, data and system logic as well as the implementation of the development services forming the subject matter of the contract in the envisaged project model. 2. Lot 2 - Provision, operation, hosting, production-near infrastructure and operational responsibility for operations - Lot 2 comprises in particular the production-near provision, operation, hosting, deployment, infrastructure, system environment, operational management and, where applicable, further operation-related services for the permanent operational use of the overall product. Both lots are in a functional overall context, but pursue different service subjects, areas of responsibility and contractual priorities. The concrete design of the interfaces, cooperation and handover obligations between the lots results from the respective procurement and contract documents. This procedure relates exclusively to lot 2. The present procurement documents, specifications, requirements and evaluation criteria relate exclusively to lot 2 - Provision, operation as well as deployment and technical operational support services of the cloud and operating environment. The subject matter of lot 2 is in particular: - the provision and operation of the cloud and operating environment forming the subject matter of the contract, - the managed cloud services required for this, - the execution of deployment, release, monitoring and incident processes, - as well as the technical operational, support and operational support services associated therewith. By contrast, the subject matter of these documents does not include services of lot 1, in particular no original development, adaptation, further development or software-side troubleshooting services for the software solution forming the subject matter of the contract, unless expressly stipulated otherwise in the documents or required across lots. Insofar as there are requirements for deployment, integration, handover, test, monitoring, incident or support processes within the framework of lot 2, these serve exclusively for the contractually compliant implementation of the operation, cloud and deployment services of lot 2 and do not in themselves constitute an assumption of the original service subjects of lot 1. A maximum budget of 80.000 EUR (gross) is available for the services of this lot 2. The budget specification does not refer to services that are billed on a time and materials basis. Tenders that exceed this budget are to be excluded from the procedure.
sig_f8416d31a4f813aaa89d.title: Digitalagentur Smarte Grenzregion GmbH, KielRegion GmbH - SH-Navi - Lot 2 - DevOps and Operations

sig_f8b577b664dca4200f17.description: Innovative solutions to improve participant assessment, triage support and progression following a positive FIT result Introduction Bowel cancer is one of the most common cancers in Wales, with over 2,200 new cases diagnosed each year , and early diagnosis remains one of the most important factors in improving patient outcomes. It is more common as people get older, with most cases diagnosed in those over 50. Bowel Screening Wales plays a vital role in identifying people aged 50-74 who might be at increased risk of bowel cancer, through the routine use of an at home stool sample kit, known as Faecal Immunochemical Testing (FIT) . Each year, more than 500,000 people are invited to participate in bowel screening, with around 12,000 participants receiving a positive FIT result and requiring further assessment and investigation. Following a positive FIT result, screening participants are informed to contact the national bowel screening administration team to make a mutually convenient appointment for a nurse-led pre-colonoscopy assessment. This assessment is predominantly undertaken by telephone and uses a standardised assessment form with questions designed to determine an individual's suitability for colonoscopy, identify clinical risks and ensure participants receive the support they need before further investigation. The assessment lasts between 30 and 60 minutes, depending on the level of complexity. Appointments are available Monday to Friday, 9am to 4pm, and this is currently the only option available to screening participants. The current process was established when the Bowel Screening Wales programme launched in 2008 and has remained largely unchanged since that time. Whilst the pathway continues to provide a safe and effective means of assessment, the environment in which it operates has changed considerably. Bowel Screening participation has increased, eligibility has expanded, workforce pressures have intensified and public expectations around digital access, communication and convenience have evolved. Bowel Screening Wales is therefore seeking innovative approaches that can support service modernisation, improve participant experience, improve the timeliness of pre-colonoscopy assessments and strengthen the ability of NHS Wales to meet future demand. ________________________________________ The Challenge Current pre-colonoscopy assessment processes remain heavily reliant on manual and telephone-based activity during routine office hours (Mon-Fri. 9-4pm). This can limit access for screening participants (especially those of working age), create pressure on specialist nursing teams, contribute to variation in waiting times and participant experience, and limit opportunities to make better use of participant information resources (i.e. current inability to signpost participants to digital resources and video content). We are seeking innovative solutions that can improve access to timely assessments, provide increased flexibility for participants to undertake an assessment, enables participants to have more control over their engagement with the service, including the possibility of them booking their own appointment slots following assessment. In addition, the innovation should have the ability to enable the screening programme to triage participants for appropriate investigations and stratify individuals for timely interventions based on clinical need following a positive FIT result. The challenge is outcome focused and does not prescribe a specific technology, product type or delivery model. Applicants are encouraged to propose the approach they believe will best address the challenge and demonstrate how their solution could be adapted, developed or enhanced to meet the needs of Bowel Screening Wales. We are not seeking to specify a single solution in advance. The purpose of this challenge is to support the development and demonstration of solutions that can address the underlying service need as described above whilst creating foundations for future improvement. Phase 2: Development and Real-World Demonstration This challenge is being delivered as a Phase 2 Contracts for Innovation competition. We are seeking organisations with existing technologies, products, platforms, or solutions that require adaptation, enhancement, or development to meet the needs of Bowel Screening Wales. Projects should support the development, refinement, and real-world demonstration of innovative approaches capable of improving participant assessment, triage and pathway management following a positive FIT result. The expectation is that solutions will be deployed and evaluated in a real-world setting where appropriate, enabling learning from practical implementation to inform ongoing refinement and future development throughout the project. Funding Allocation and Project Details Competition Type: Phase 2 Development and Real-World Demonstration Total Funding Available: £ 300,000 Number of Projects Anticipated: Current funding of £300,000, excluding VAT, is available to fund 4-5 projects which may be subject to change. The total funding available for the competition can change and the funders reserve the right to adjust the provisional funding allocations, I.e., should additional funding become available. Portfolio Approach This challenge is open to applications that deliver a Phase 2 development and real-world demonstration project. Current funding of up to £300,000 is available to support up to 4-5 projects which may be subject to change, dependent upon the number/quality of submissions received. All costs must be clearly justified and value for money demonstrated with willingness for appropriate contributions from the provider to help deliver the project. We reserve the right to consider an increased budget for exceptional applications if the scale of the delivery across Wales warrants it. Please note any adoption and implementation of a solution from this competition would be subject of a separate, possible competitive, procurement exercise. This competition does not cover the purchase of any solution although we may choose to investigate and explore innovative procurement routes as part of this challenge. Lot 1: . None
sig_f8b577b664dca4200f17.title: Contracts for Innovation Cymru - Modernising the Bowel Screening Pathway in Wales

sig_f9086df6359c515fd148.description: Issuing Agency: Project Management Office (PMO) Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) Capability Program Executive, Aviation SFAE-AVN-U Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: Army Contracting Command - Redstone Period of Availability: This UAS Marketplace Commercial Solutions Opening, open solicitation, will remain open in perpetuity until canceled by the U.S. Army. Call for Solutions will specify individual response times and requirements. Description of Program: In accordance with Executive Order 14307, the UAS Marketplace is the strategy to scale the industrial base and accelerate production deliveries while empowering Soldiers with freedom of choice to meet mission needs. As part of this approach, the PMO UAS will better incentivize industry innovation. UAS Marketplace marks a significant pivot from traditional Department of War (DoW) acquisition business models to a free-market approach founded on the concept of continuous competition that drives innovation, where Soldiers’ demands are directly linked to industry provided capabilities. This CSO will enable the Army to rapidly acquire and deliver innovative solutions to the Warfighter using commercial technology. SECTION A – INTRODUCTION AND AUTHORITY The PMO UAS has identified the following needs: (1) to accelerate the adoption of advanced commercial technology; (2) to transform UAS capabilities; and (3) to grow the industrial base to appropriately support the DoW. This solicitation aims to provide the DoW with access to innovative solutions enabling the DoW to evolve quickly and maintain a competitive edge over adversaries. Industry is at the forefront of innovation, developing cutting-edge capabilities that will enhance the DoW capabilities and protect the Warfighter. The DoW will select vendors whose solutions demonstrate the greatest potential to achieve the DoW's missions. The PMO UAS is maximizing existing authorities by publishing this CSO, open solicitation, combining any single authority or a combination of the authorities below: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) – Other Competitive Procedures 10 U.S.C. §3458 – Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures / DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening SECTION B - GENERAL INFORMATION The PMO UAS anticipates that the CSO will be updated frequently to improve processes and to keep pace with evolving threats, needs and innovations. The CSO will be open in perpetuity until canceled by the PMO UAS. Companies are informed that ONLY a warranted Government Contracting/Agreements Officer (KO/AO) (not a Contracting Officer Representative or other personnel) may contractually bind the Government. The Government shall not be liable to pay for work performed by a company unless a warranted KO/AO has signed an agreement in writing stating that the Government shall pay. The Government shall not fund preparation of solution briefs/proposals, or support work efforts or tasks that are inferred from discussions with technical project officers. SECTION C – AREAS OF INTEREST This CSO, open solicitation, covers any of the following example areas. These example areas shall be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting, and are not reflective of the ONLY DoW areas or in any priority of order. Intelligence, Electronic, Warfare, and Sensors Tactical Communications Soldier Equipment Ancillary Items Simulation and Stimulation Training and Instrumentation Uncrewed Aircraft Systems: Full Systems Air Vehicles Payloads Supply Chain and Logistics Installation Support and Innovation Additive Manufacturing Autonomous Vehicles Software Autonomous Behaviors Command & Control Launched Effects UAS Production (build at scale) SECTION D – COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO) PROCEDURES There are two methods for responding under this CSO: (1) Innovative Warfighter Solutions submissions and (2) Call for Solution submissions. Method 1 - Innovative Warfighter Solutions (IWS) a. Provides a flexible and open-ended opportunity for industry partners to submit solution briefs to any Areas of Interest (AOI) in Section C. This aspect of the CSO is designed to identify and bridge gaps in mission-critical capabilities by inviting innovative solutions from the private sector. The purpose is to encourage a wide range of responses that can enhance and support the example AOIs, foster collaboration and leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to meet evolving operational needs. b. Companies shall follow the procedures outlined in Section D.1 providing a submission to an IWS. c. The submission mailbox for AOI is identified in Section J. Method 2 - Call for Solutions (C4S) a. Provides an opportunity for industry partners to submit innovative solutions in response to Government issued C4S under any AOI in Section C. C4S aim to pinpoint and address critical gaps in essential capabilities by welcoming creative proposals from private sector entities. b.Companies shall follow the procedures outlined below in Section D.2. c.The individual C4S will identify how responses are to be submitted. Method 1 - IWS Overview Companies submitting an IWS in response to the AOIs shall follow the procedures outlined with each call. If the Government does not select a company’s submission for immediate review, the submission will be retained in the Solution Basket. This allows the Government to reconsider the submission for future needs and funding opportunities, maximizing its value to both the vendor and the DoW. The IWS award procedures will utilize up to three (3) phases, as appliable: Solution Brief Live Demonstration and/or Pitch (optional) Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP) Method 2 - C4S Overview CS4 (referred to as “Calls”) will be released and posted via SAM.gov as an amendment under this CSO. The Call will include all relevant submission requirements and evaluation procedures and shall govern the process for evaluations and award. Submission requirements may vary in phases and may take the form of solution briefs, white papers, demonstrations, live pitches, etc. C4S are independent from the IWS procedures discussed above in Section D.1 IWS procedures do not apply to individual Calls. Calls may be written in a broad manner to maximize efficiency, innovation and application when approaching a problem and to allow for maximum participation from vendors who may not be familiar with submitting proposals to Government solicitations. The Government may post Calls at any time. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for updates to this solicitation and posted C4S. SECTION E - AWARDS The Government may choose to issue an award(s) in accordance with IWSs or C4S procedures and subject to the availability of funds. The KO/AO reserves the right to negotiate directly with the company on terms and conditions prior to execution of the resulting award instrument, including payment terms, and will execute the instrument on behalf of the Government. All payment obligations of the Government shall be subject to receipt of appropriations from Congress for the purpose, time, and amount of the obligation. Be advised, only a KO/AO has the authority to enter into, or modify, a binding instrument on behalf of the United States Government. Awards issued under this CSO may include, but are not limited to the following award instruments: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12 Commercial Procedures; any fixed price, or fixed price incentive contract type specified under FAR Part 16; and non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C. 4022 and 10 U.S.C. 4023; for the Army and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of the AOI identified in Section J. In order to receive an award, the following must be met: a. Companies shall have a Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number and must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to receiving an instrument. If a company does not possess a valid and active SAM registration, companies are advised to commence SAM registration before responding to a Call or IWS. Companies are required to maintain registration in SAM throughout the period of performance of the instrument and during any subsequent follow-on award. b. Companies shall also register in the prescribed Government invoicing system (Wide Area Work Flow: https://wawf.eb.mil/xhtml/unauth/registration/notice.xhtml.) c. Companies shall represent their small business size and status as required in this solicitation. d. Companies shall be determined to be responsible by the KO/AO and must not be suspended or debarred from award by the Federal Government nor be prohibited by Presidential Executive Order and/or law from receiving an award. e. Any actual or potential OCIs shall be identified to KO/AO prior to award. SECTION F – ITERATIVE PROTOTYPING Iterative prototyping is a development methodology where a prototype is created, tested, and refined through multiple cycles, incorporating user feedback and improvements in each iteration, to ensure the final product meets user requirements and expectations effectively. An Other Transaction (OT) for a prototype awarded or an award using 10 U.S.C. 4023 against this open solicitation shall allow for an iterative prototyping process and will be delineated in the award document. An iterative prototyping process will allow the Government to modify, by mutual agreement, the scope of a prototype contract or OT to allow for the adaptation and modification of the technology being prototyped to meet additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets. The sequential prototype iterations may result in separate phased prototype awards rather than a modification of the original prototype award. These additional unique and discrete purposes/mission sets can be generated by the Government. SECTION I – NON-GOVERNMENT ADVISORS Non-Government advisors may be used in the evaluation of Solution Briefs, Pitches and during the Commercial Solution Proposal phase and negotiations under the IWS procedures or in C4S. Non-Government advisors will have signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with the Government. The company understands that the Government may share proprietary company information with non-Government personnel for evaluation and administrative purposes only. The Government understands that information provided in response to this open solicitation is presented in confidence and may contain trade secret or commercial or financial information, and it agrees to protect such information from unauthorized disclosure to the maximum extent permitted or required by Law, to include: a. 18 U.S.C. 1905 (Trade Secrets Act); b. 18 U.S.C. 1831 et seq. (Economic Espionage Act); c. 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (Freedom of Information Act); d. Executive Order 12600 (Pre-disclosure Notification Procedures for Confidential Commercial Information); and, e. Any other statute, regulation, or requirement applicable to Government employees. Companies shall label any information they want protected as confidential. Submissions will not be returned. The original copy of each submission received will be retained by the Army and all other non-required copies destroyed. SECTION J - CONTACT INFORMATION IWS Solution Brief submissions as detailed in Section D.1, shall be submitted to the email address listed below and shall include the associated AOI in the subject line of the e-mail. If the respondent does not include the AOI in the subject line of the e-mail, the submission will NOT be reviewed. [Area of Interest in Subject Line][UASMarketplaceIWS@peo.avn.mil] C4S Brief submissions (Section D.2) shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions and points of contact provided in the Call. General questions surrounding this open solicitation shall be submitted to: Email address: USARMY Redstone Arsenal PEO AVN Mailbox UAS Marketplace usarmy.redstone.peo-avn.mbx.uas-marketplace@army.mil Cc: USARMY Redstone Arsenal ACC Mailbox ACC-RSA-UAS-Marketplace usarmy.redstone.acc.mbx.acc-rsa-uas-marketplace@army.mil SECTION K - DEFINITIONS "Call for Solution" (C4S) an announcement posted on SAM.gov, which may result in a contract or OT and includes submission instructions, evaluation criteria, timelines, how the Army will treat late submissions, points of contact, and other specific information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. “Commercial Solutions Opening” (CSO) is a competitive procedure KO/AO may use to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, or services. “Innovative” means any item that is (1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or (2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a technology, process, or method existing as of such date. “Innovative Warfighter Solutions” (IWS) is a competitive procedure for submitting an Innovative Warfighter Solution in response to a posted Area of Interest (AOI) under this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). These procedures create a pathway we call the Solution Basket. The IWS gives industry the opportunity to approach the Government with their innovative solutions. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined by DFARS 202.101 as an “entity that is not currently performing and has not performed any contract or subcontract for DoD that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards prescribed pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1502 and the regulations implementing such section, for at least the 1-year period preceding the solicitation of sources by DoD for the procurement (10 U.S.C. 3014).” “Nonprofit Institution” is defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3703 an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which insures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual. "Other Transaction" refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoD has the authority to enter into OTs for Research Projects (10 USC 4021), OT for Prototype Projects (10 USC 4022), and DoD relevant OT that support research (10 U.S.C. 4021). “Commercial Solution Proposal” (CSP): is a proposal that is submitted in response to a Call that is governed by a CSO or a response to an unsolicited proposal that is invited to Phase III. CSPs may be requested as a result of Solution Briefs and/or presentations/pitches. “Small Business” is defined under Section 3 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 632).

Lot 1: . The Council requires a hub where users can access the system and have the ability to find any needed legislation or regulation to help ensure that whatever project they are working on is compliant with government law and standards. A portal is currently used for this requirement that has 2 parts. The first part is the Construction Information Service legislation and technical information management solution. This service ensures that Fife Council will have access to the correct, current and complaint business critical information year-round. This service provides the Council access to 27,000 full-text PDFs with the ability to save, view, print, download, copy and paste any of these documents. There are over 350 publishers that add documents to this service. Fife Council require something equal in quality and quantity to this. The second part of the portal is Occupational Health & Safety Information Service. This single source library holds more than 90,000 documents from more than 400 publishers. The focus of this service is Health, Safety, Environmental and Fire. This service relates to risk management, hazardous substances and operations, control principles, movement of people and vehicles. Fife Council also require something that is equal in quality and quantity to this part of the portal. Overall, the current solution allows access to over 2.3 million industry standards, over 10 thousand engineering manuals, handbooks, reference books, over 76 million technical articles, journals and books, over 107 million patents, patent applications, unity models and abstracts and over 39 million industry-to-industry reference links across all hosted content

sig_f91c7ae44f3ba8052dc5.description: The subject matter of the tender is the provision, implementation and operation of an integrated, cloud-based procurement suite to support procurement and supplier management processes within the corporate group of Technische Werke Dresden GmbH (TWD). The solution is to be provided as a standardised SaaS application from a single manufacturer and is to create a unified platform for the digitalisation, standardisation and efficient control of procurement processes. As part of the initial rollout wave, the scope of services encompasses the functions of supplier relationship management (SRM) as well as catalogue management and the processing of catalogue orders. The solution is to enable end-to-end support for processes ranging from supplier registration, qualification, evaluation and risk assessment through to ordering from approved catalogues. In addition, the offered suite is to form the basis for the subsequent expansion of further procurement functions. These include in particular source-to-contract (S2C) functions, further procure-to-pay (P2P) processes, and guided buying. The objective is the long-term establishment of an integrated, future-proof and largely standard-compliant procurement platform featuring a shared database, a unified user interface, and a consistent role and authorisation concept. In doing so, the contracting authority expressly pursues the principle of "standard before customisation". Individual developments are to be restricted to the technically and operationally necessary minimum in order to ensure high release capability, low operating costs, and the sustainable further development of the solution. sig_f9225328e9325df89ddb.description: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of remote qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring a Remote Qualified Signature Creation Device (rQSCD) — a certified combination of Hardware and Standard Software — to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centers (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to upgrade the throughput capacity of the rQSCD and an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of the certified rQSCD, comprising certified HSM devices (Hardware) and the associated Signature Activation Module software (Standard Software), certified as a composite in accordance with eIDAS2. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the rQSCD as part of its qualified remote signing service. The rQSCD must integrate with the Agency's existing signing infrastructure, including the Agency's certificate authority, authorisation server, and signing components. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of Hardware and Standard Software, sized and configured for operation across two data centres in an active/active configuration with a minimum throughput of 16 signatures per second, together with deployment in the Agency's production, staging, and test environments; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Standard Software and Hardware, security patching, and up to two replacements of Hardware during the contract term to maintain valid certifications; and (c) Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract. The contract term is 120 months. The service supports the national qualified signing volume — estimated at 5,100,000 signatures per year across two data centres — and the procured capacity is dimensioned to provide headroom above current demand for growth, peak load, and resilience.
sig_f9225328e9325df89ddb.title: Remote Qualified Signature Creation Device (rQSCD)

sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.description: The Technische Universität Darmstadt is among the leading technical universities in Germany and is characterised by innovative research and an international orientation. The university is structured into 13 departments and over 120 institutes. This structure is supplemented by eight directorates, which handle central administrative tasks such as student services, financial and personnel affairs, construction management and international affairs, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the university. In total, the TU Darmstadt comprises around 24.300 students and about 5.200 employees. A special role is played here by Directorates IV (Real Estate Management) and V (Construction Management and Technical Operations), which are responsible for the administration and management of a total of 210 buildings on the campus. In the course of these demanding tasks, the directorates have relied on SAP ERP software with various modules since 2000. Since 2004, the SAP RE-FX (Real Estate Management) and SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) modules have been used in the aforementioned areas. For construction management, 2019 SAP PS (Project System) including the construction add-on from PROMOS was implemented. Currently, however, many internal processes in the field of building management and maintenance are mapped outside of SAP, as only a small part of the technical requirements can be implemented in SAP. Digital plan data (CAD) and digital spatial data (SAP RE-FX spatial database) are not linked. Data is reconciled manually. Documents are only partially available in digitised form, without reference to other systems. The diverse tasks and processes of the directorates are to be supported in future step-by-step by a uniform solution in the form of a CAFM system. The professional support requirement primarily consists of creating a uniform database in order to better link and evaluate information. Further requirements arise from the specialist tasks with regard to property and facility management and facility operations.
sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.title: IMMO4TU

sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.description: The subject of the procurement is the nurse call, fall detection, and movement monitoring systems to be introduced in Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social, health, and rescue sectors in hospitals, senior centres, care homes, enhanced assisted living units, health centre inpatient wards, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring round-the-clock care and supervision. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients may have a sudden need for assistance that requires a response. Nurse call systems are a core part of daily care and nursing work, as well as client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for assistance are forwarded without delay to the right personnel and that nursing staff are able to prioritise their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support the occupational safety of staff, for example in threatening and hazardous situations, and enable the monitoring, reporting, and development of operations. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity is impaired, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.

sig_f9bf3950c8116db92fee.description: Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), supported by the North West Regional Flood and Coastal Committee (RFCC), is seeking market insight to shape a future procurement for a regional service aimed at increasing community resilience to flooding and coastal change. The service provider will act as a neutral, independent intermediary, supporting both communities and flood risk management authorities (RMAs) across the North West. Flooding remains one of the most significant climate-related risks facing the region. Traditional engineering approaches are increasingly costly, complex, and insufficient on their own. Communities must therefore be better informed, prepared, and supported to understand their flood risk, plan for emergencies, build resilience, and recover effectively when flooding occurs. We can help communities to become more resilient to better protect themselves and enable quicker recovery, but only by successfully engaging with them on their terms, at the right time, and through the channels they use. Across the North West there are hundreds of communities which are at risk from flooding from rivers and the sea. Combined with surface water flooding, the number of residents and businesses at risk is significantly higher. Climate change will continue to increase rainfall and flooding. The procurement will establish a multi-strand community engagement and resilience-building service, spanning direct community engagement, digital communications, educational materials, and the development and maintenance of The Flood Hub website as a central public information platform. GMCA will lead the procurement and enter into contractual arrangements with the selected supplier. The service will be funded predominantly by the North West RFCC, with contributions from the Environment Agency and other partners as required. The supplier will support North West flood RMAs including 36 local authorities, the Environment Agency, and United Utilities, as the primary water company. The service provider will act as a neutral intermediary organisation operating in the space between communities who have flooded, or who are at risk of flooding, and RMAs, across the North West of England, supporting those authorities to increase the resilience of those communities to flooding and coastal change. The communities to be supported include residents (homeowners and tenants) and businesses, including agricultural. Key Objectives The service aims to achieve the following outcomes: • Increased community resilience to flooding and coastal change through adapted engagement approaches to improve their understanding of flood risk, including where and why flooding may occur. • Improved preparedness at individual and community levels, including awareness of emergency actions, insurance, and property resilience measures. • Greater community contribution to community-level flood risk management interventions (e.g. sustainable drainage, rain gardens, natural flood management). • Strengthened community capability to develop and maintain community flood groups, action plans, and mutual aid structures. • Enhanced recovery outcomes, enabling households and businesses to recover more quickly following flooding. • Greater awareness and uptake of national and local support mechanisms, including property flood resilience, flood warnings, and online resources such as The Flood Hub. The Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) (TUPE) Regulations are expected to apply to this commission, requiring the team of five FTEs who have resourced the service through the previous contract, to transfer across to a new supplier organisation if selected Lot 1: .
sig_f9bf3950c8116db92fee.title: GMCA 1134 North West Community Flood Resilience Engagement Support Services
